soil-water-293.a: Flow leaving a confined channel spreads out and loses the capacity to carry its sediment.

soil-water-120.q: How does the National Technical Committee for Hydric Soils define a hydric soil?
soil-water-120.a: As soil formed under saturation, flooding or ponding long enough to turn its upper part anaerobic.

soil-agri-150.q: Why does burning the slash raise soil fertility for a time?
soil-agri-150.a: It leaves a nutrient-rich ash layer and temporarily removes weeds and pests.

soil-agri-145.q: How does expanded clay aggregate help a heavy soil?
soil-agri-145.a: Mixed in, its pellets improve aeration and drainage.

soil-agri-124.q: Why does keyline cultivation give water more time to infiltrate?
soil-agri-124.a: Cultivating parallel to the keyline drifts runoff away from the valley centre, delaying runoff concentration.

soil-agri-063.q: How do reduced-tillage and no-till systems protect soil?
soil-agri-063.a: They keep residues on the surface for erosion protection and water retention.

soil-agri-068.q: What does a catch crop do with nitrogen left from the previous crop?
soil-agri-068.a: It takes up the surplus, keeping it from loss by leaching, denitrification or volatilization, and returns it to the soil when worked in as green manure or decomposed.

soil-agri-094.q: Why can a single poor rating make a Storie index zero?
soil-agri-094.a: The index multiplies its ratings, so a zero in any one makes the whole result zero.

soil-meth-018.q: In the WRB, what does the whole soil include besides the fine earth?
soil-meth-018.a: Coarse fragments, artefacts, cemented parts and dead plant residues of any size.

soil-meth-002.q: What are the nugget, sill and range of a variogram?
soil-meth-002.a: The nugget is a jump at the origin, the sill its limit at large distances, and the range the distance where it nears the sill.

soil-env-275.q: What mainly decides the net methane flux from a wetland?
soil-env-275.a: How much methane made by methanogens reaches the surface before methanotrophs oxidize it.

soil-env-100.q: What sets the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification apart from other agreements on land?
soil-env-100.a: It is the only internationally legally binding framework on desertification, and the only convention stemming directly from the Rio Conference's Agenda 21.

soil-env-080.q: What happens to people when desertified rural land can no longer support them?
soil-env-080.a: They migrate to cities, particularly in Africa, creating unemployment and slums.

soil-env-311.q: What caused the spoil tip at Aberfan, Wales, to collapse in 1966?
soil-env-311.a: It was built over a spring and saturated by heavy rain; it collapsed onto a school, killing 144 people.

soil-env-200.q: How does PFAS in soil reach people?
soil-env-200.a: Crops take it up: soil contamination raises PFAS in foods such as white rice, coffee and animals reared on the land.

soil-env-017.q: Why are coliform bacteria in runoff measured if they do not cause disease?
soil-env-017.a: They are a common indicator of water pollution.

soil-env-050.q: What makes a plant a hyperaccumulator?
soil-env-050.a: It concentrates metals to levels toxic to related species not adapted to metalliferous soils, for example over 1000 mg/kg of dry weight for nickel, copper, cobalt, chromium or lead.

soil-env-247.q: How does bioslurping recover oil from above the water table?
soil-env-247.a: A slurp tube reaching into the free-product layer draws up liquid and soil gas together, lifting oil off the water table and capillary fringe.

soil-env-298.q: How did cadmium from upstream mines reach the people who developed itai-itai disease?
soil-env-298.a: Residents irrigated rice with the Jinzū River water, so the highly soluble cadmium contaminated paddies and rice and raised body burdens.

soil-hist-119.q: How do absolute and relative ages differ in the methods that produce them?
soil-hist-119.a: Absolute ages come from radioactive isotopes, while relative ages come from tools such as paleomagnetism and stable isotope ratios.

soil-hist-088.q: Into which two stages does taphonomy divide its processes?
soil-hist-088.a: Biostratinomy, between death and burial, and diagenesis, after burial.

soil-hist-077.q: What does agricultural chemistry often aim to do for soil?
soil-hist-077.a: Preserve or raise soil fertility so as to keep or improve crop yields and crop quality.

soil-hist-001.q: Besides parent material, what did Dokuchaev show explains how soil types vary from place to place?
soil-hist-001.a: Climate, topography and the length of soil formation.

soil-hist-076.q: What did a failed royal commission on truffle cultivation lead Albert Bernhard Frank to discover?
soil-hist-076.a: The nature and development of mycorrhizae, which he named in an 1885 paper.

soil-hist-069.q: What level of perchlorate in Martian regolith is considered toxic to humans?
soil-hist-069.a: Around 0.5%, and even trace amounts interfere with human thyroid function.

soil-env-174.q: Under what conditions need inorganic fertilizers not harm soil health?
soil-env-174.a: When they are not used in excess and they boost plant growth that returns more carbon-containing residues.

soil-found-092.q: What is the familiar vernacular distinction between soils, and what makes light soils easier to cultivate?
soil-found-092.a: Heavy (clayey) versus light (sandy) soils. Light soils are easier to cultivate and resist compaction by trampling cattle, but they erode more easily.

soil-found-088.q: Why do tropical soils turn rusty red and lack marked layer contrasts?
soil-found-088.a: Fast decomposition leaves little fulvic acid to leach metals, so mobile magnesium, iron and aluminium precipitate as oxide minerals that colour the soil rusty red.

soil-found-079.q: Why is soil water more accurately called the soil solution?
soil-found-079.a: Because it is never pure: it carries hundreds of dissolved organic and mineral substances.

soil-found-042.q: How are clay minerals most easily identified?
soil-found-042.a: By X-ray diffraction rather than by chemical or physical tests.

soil-form-136.q: What is the minimum share of silt- and clay-sized particles in a mudrock?

soil-form-111.q: How do luminescence methods date loess?
soil-form-111.a: They date when the grains were last exposed to daylight.

soil-form-152.q: What happens when volcanic ash is washed into the soil, and when is heavy ashfall harmful?
soil-form-152.a: Its minerals form a nutrient-rich andisol layer that is very good for farming. Heavy ashfalls can bury pasture and sterilize the soil by oxygen deprivation.

soil-form-154.q: What is rock varnish made of, and how does its clay arrive?
soil-form-154.a: It is made mainly of clay with iron and manganese oxides, and the clay can only arrive by wind.

soil-form-022.q: Does the United States have a legal definition of topsoil sold in commerce?
soil-form-022.a: No, it has no federal legal definition.

soil-form-026.q: Why can a perched water table form on top of a claypan?
soil-form-026.a: Its dense structure restricts roots and water infiltration.

soil-form-040.q: Why does caliche form in the B horizon under a thin A horizon?
soil-form-040.a: Calcite and other soluble minerals that water would normally remove build up there as a cemented layer.

soil-form-035.q: Why are tepetates a problem for farming at the surface?
soil-form-035.a: They are hard, poorly drained and infertile.

soil-form-123.q: What kind of soils show this wetting-drying mixing, and what does it require?
soil-form-123.a: It is specific to vertisolic soils, driven by wetting-drying cycles, and needs at least 30% clay.

soil-form-158.q: How does humus change as a soil ages from young to old?
soil-form-158.a: In a young soil humus accumulates; in a mature soil it peaks; in an old soil it declines.

soil-form-156.q: Which part of a hillslope is steepest, and what shapes it?
soil-form-156.a: The backslope, shaped mainly by mass wasting and running water.

soil-form-167.q: What made the St. Lawrence Lowlands clays unstable after glaciation?
soil-form-167.a: The Champlain Sea left salt-rich clay there, and leaching of the salt plus river incision made it unstable, causing landslides and flows of the wet clay.

soil-form-164.q: What separates the great groups of the order of dark prairie soils?
soil-form-164.a: The colour of the A horizon, which shows how much organic carbon the grasses added.

soil-phys-186.q: How did agrophysics develop from soil physics?
soil-phys-186.a: It first studied relations within the soil, then widened to crop properties and the quality and safety of food and raw farm produce.

soil-phys-167.q: What did Coulomb contribute to soil design in 1773?
soil-phys-167.a: He applied mechanics to earth pressures on ramparts, taking shear strength on a slip plane as cohesion plus friction.

soil-phys-067.q: How do IUPAC pore size limits relate to how gases adsorb on rigid solids?
soil-phys-067.a: Micropores fill cooperatively, mesopores show capillary condensation, and in macropores confinement effects vanish.

soil-phys-066.q: What is the difference between primary and secondary porosity?
soil-phys-066.a: Primary porosity is the original pore system of a rock or alluvial deposit; secondary porosity forms later, through leaching of minerals or fracturing.

soil-phys-087.q: Why are wet, clay-rich soils more susceptible to compaction?
soil-phys-087.a: Water films shield particle contacts, and fine-textured clay-rich soils are more susceptible than coarse ones, wet more than dry.

soil-phys-229.q: Why can freshly plowed soil falsely look uncompacted?

soil-phys-232.q: Why does a field headland usually yield less?
soil-phys-232.a: It gets more traffic per unit area than the rest of the field, so its soil is more compacted.

soil-phys-235.q: Why may switching compacted soil to no-till at once fail?
soil-phys-235.a: Compacted soils become addicted to tillage, and no-till benefits usually take 2 to 5 years, faster with cover crops.

soil-water-198.q: How is horizontal saturated hydraulic conductivity measured with the auger hole method?
soil-water-198.a: A hole is augered to below the water table, water is bailed out, and the rate at which the level rises again is recorded.

soil-phys-130.q: What does a root do when it senses dry soil?
soil-phys-130.a: It makes the hormone ABA, which closes stomata, cutting transpiration and photosynthesis, and loosens root cell walls so roots grow in search of water.

soil-water-167.q: How is gravimetric water content found by oven drying?
soil-water-167.a: The sample is dried and weighed until drying is complete; the mass lost is the water, divided by the wet or the dry mass.

soil-water-242.q: What turns plinthite irreversibly into ironstone hardpan?
soil-water-242.a: Repeated wetting and drying, especially with heat from the sun; a single cycle does not.

soil-water-190.a: The ratio of actual path length to the straight distance between two points; the more sinuous the path, the higher it is.

soil-phys-255.q: What is the premise of pedotransfer functions?
soil-phys-255.a: That a soil's basic properties are enough to infer all its other physical and chemical properties.

soil-phys-262.q: Between which two points is plant available water held?
soil-phys-262.a: Between field capacity and the permanent wilting point, in mesopores.

soil-water-211.q: Why does ponded water reach groundwater more readily than evenly spread rain?
soil-water-211.a: Rain spread evenly within field capacity barely percolates, but pooled in low spots the same volume can exceed field capacity and drain down to groundwater.

soil-phys-208.q: Which equation is the basic constitutive law for groundwater discharge, and who derived it?
soil-phys-208.a: Darcy's law, derived by Henry Darcy in 1856.

soil-water-158.q: How is fingering in the unsaturated zone described?
soil-water-158.a: As a Saffman-Taylor instability, arising mostly during drainage and leaving an unstable boundary between saturated and unsaturated soil.

soil-water-165.q: At what suction is field capacity defined, and what moisture does it represent?
soil-water-165.a: At -33 kPa; it is the moisture 2-3 days after rain or irrigation.

soil-water-162.q: What does a general basin water balance say?
soil-water-162.a: P = Q + ET + change in storage: precipitation equals streamflow plus evapotranspiration plus change in storage in soil or groundwater.

soil-phys-211.q: What reservoirs does this water balance model divide the soil profile into?
soil-phys-211.a: The surface, the unsaturated root zone with mainly vertical flow, a transition zone, and the aquifer with mainly horizontal flow.

soil-phys-219.q: What does the eddy covariance flux measure, and what is it the covariance of?
soil-phys-219.a: It is the covariance between fluctuations of vertical wind speed and of gas concentration, times mean air density.

soil-phys-213.q: How much of the water roots take up is lost by transpiration and guttation?
soil-phys-213.a: 97-99.5%; only a small part is used for growth.

soil-phys-146.q: Why does soil air hold less oxygen and more CO2 than the air above?
soil-phys-146.a: Microbes and roots consume oxygen and release carbon dioxide.

soil-phys-150.q: What commonly causes poor soil aeration?
soil-phys-150.a: Soil compaction, and a pore network blocked when water fills the pores.

soil-phys-163.q: What drives the formation of patterned ground?
soil-phys-163.a: Frost heaving of wet, fine-grained, porous soils: repeated freezing and thawing push larger stones up, and lateral forces pile them into clusters and stripes.

soil-phys-161.q: What do low-albedo and high-albedo surfaces do with radiation?
soil-phys-161.a: Low-albedo surfaces look dark and absorb most radiation; high-albedo surfaces such as snow look bright and reflect most of it.

soil-phys-244.q: What does Dalton's law say about a gas mixture?
soil-phys-244.a: The total pressure of an ideal gas mixture is the sum of the partial pressures of its gases.

soil-phys-245.a: Without convection, gases are good insulators, so they trap many gas-filled pockets that block conduction.

soil-phys-179.q: What conditions does ice segregation need?
soil-phys-179.a: A permeable soil or porous rock, temperatures at which ice and premelted water coexist, and a temperature gradient across the zone.

soil-phys-164.q: What is the formula for thermal diffusivity, and what does high diffusivity mean?
soil-phys-164.a: alpha = k/(rho cp). Heat moves rapidly through a material of high diffusivity because it conducts heat quickly relative to how much energy it stores.

soil-phys-183.q: What does the heat equation say about how a point heats or cools?
soil-phys-183.a: A point heats or cools at a rate proportional to how much hotter or cooler its surroundings are.

soil-chem-231.q: Why does anatase often form first even though rutile is more stable?
soil-chem-231.a: Anatase has a lower surface energy, though rutile is the most common and stable TiO2 polymorph.

soil-chem-232.q: Why does each element give its own X-ray emission peaks?
soil-chem-232.a: An incident beam ejects an inner-shell electron, and the X-ray released when an outer electron fills the hole has an energy characteristic of the element.

soil-chem-188.q: What does Bragg's law link together?
soil-chem-188.a: The wavelength, the lattice spacing and the glancing angle.

soil-chem-233.q: What gives this phosphate mineral its green colour?

soil-chem-242.q: What happens when pyrite is exposed to air?
soil-chem-242.a: It oxidizes to iron and sulfuric acid, and oxidation of sulfides can push soil pH below 2.0.

soil-chem-227.q: How does the van der Waals force change with distance?
soil-chem-227.a: It is repulsive at very short range, zero at an equilibrium distance, and attractive beyond it.

soil-chem-109.q: Where does green rust occur as a mineral?
soil-chem-109.a: As the mineral fougerite in Gleysols.

soil-chem-089.q: What alternating conditions helped kaolinite form on basalt in Kivu?
soil-chem-089.a: Alternating wet and dry seasons; it did not form in perennially swampy ground.

soil-chem-148.q: How many milliequivalents is 1 mmol of Ca2+?
soil-chem-148.a: 2, because the equivalents of an ion equal its moles multiplied by its valence (1 mmol of Na+ is 1).

soil-chem-054.q: Does base-richness predict nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium availability?
soil-chem-054.a: No: base-richness shows no correlation with their availability.

soil-chem-115.q: What is the main source of electrons in soil?

soil-chem-229.q: Why do particles sometimes stay suspended as a colloid instead of settling?
soil-chem-229.a: There is not enough attractive force to aggregate them.

soil-chem-173.q: What role does manganese play in plants?
soil-chem-173.a: It is a key micronutrient, acting as a catalyst in the oxygen-evolving complex of photosystem II.

soil-chem-041.q: Why can both over-irrigation and under-irrigation cause salinity?
soil-chem-041.a: Over-irrigation raises water tables; under-irrigation fails to flush out salts.

soil-chem-040.q: Which equation does this model numerically solve to compute groundwater levels and flows between polygons?

soil-chem-042.q: How does framboidal pyrite form in acid sulfate soils?
soil-chem-042.a: Bacteria such as Desulfovibrio desulfuricans reduce sulfate to hydrogen sulfide, which reacts with ferrous iron.

soil-chem-220.q: What is the only way to remove salt from soil, rather than just tolerate it?
soil-chem-220.a: Washing salt below the root zone.

soil-bio-008.q: What is the primary role of soil biota?
soil-bio-008.a: To recycle organic matter that comes from the above-ground, plant-based food web.

soil-bio-271.q: Why does the hyphal form suit fungi?
soil-bio-271.a: Its high surface-to-volume ratio suits nutrient extraction and invading substrates.

soil-bio-056.q: What do lithotrophs get their name from?
soil-bio-056.a: The Greek lithos (rock) and troph (consumer): they are 'eaters of rock'.

soil-bio-017.q: Why are slime molds not found far below the surface?
soil-bio-017.a: They need light, so they are spread wherever sunlight and moderate moisture reach.

soil-bio-274.q: How are protozoa classified by how they move?

soil-bio-083.q: How do entomopathogenic nematodes kill an insect?
soil-bio-083.a: An infective juvenile enters it and releases gut bacteria, Xenorhabdus or Photorhabdus, that kill it within 24-48 hours.

soil-bio-064.q: What distinguishes biologically controlled mineralization from induced mineralization?
soil-bio-064.a: In controlled mineralization the cells of one organism fully control the crystals' shape, growth, composition and location; in induced mineralization microbial metabolism merely creates conditions that favour mineral growth.

soil-bio-211.q: Why are millipedes called soil ecosystem engineers?
soil-bio-211.a: Their burrowing mixes organic with mineral matter, especially where earthworms are absent or scarce.

soil-bio-006.q: What are root tips hotspots of?

soil-bio-031.q: How does a Baermann funnel collect nematodes?
soil-bio-031.a: Nematodes sink into the collecting vial because they cannot swim.

soil-bio-221.q: How does metagenomics differ from amplicon sequencing?
soil-bio-221.a: Amplicon sequencing of marker genes such as 16S rRNA shows which taxa are present; metagenomics sequences all DNA and also recovers enzymes and pathways.

soil-bio-273.a: Organisms that parasitise fungi are called mycoparasitic.

soil-bio-276.q: What share of humus do arable soils typically hold?
soil-bio-276.a: On average 2 to 3%, within a range from under 1% to over 12%.

soil-bio-210.q: After a disturbance such as agriculture, how quickly do soil mites recolonise?
soil-bio-210.a: Most recolonise within a few months, but Oribatida take several years.

soil-hist-015.q: In a Winogradsky column, which bacteria use sulfide for photosynthesis, and which tolerate more of it?
soil-hist-015.a: Purple and green sulfur bacteria use it, and green sulfur bacteria tolerate higher sulfide than purple.

soil-bio-223.q: Which fatty acid indicates fungi in a PLFA analysis?

soil-bio-162.q: What happens to plants in sterile soils unless mycorrhizal spores or hyphae are added?
soil-bio-162.a: They often do poorly, because there are no fungi to colonise their roots.

soil-bio-239.q: Who first isolated a microbe from legume nodules, and when?
soil-bio-239.a: Martinus Beijerinck, in 1888, naming it Bacillus radicicola; it is now placed in Rhizobium.

soil-bio-321.q: Do epiphytes draw nourishment from their host?
soil-bio-321.a: No. They use the host only for support and draw no nourishment from it, and they are not rooted in soil.

soil-bio-089.q: What carbon-to-nitrogen ratio is typical of humus?
soil-bio-089.a: Commonly between 8:1 and 15:1, with a median of about 12:1.

soil-bio-090.q: Which organic materials decompose first and quickly, and which persist longest?
soil-bio-090.a: Sugars, starches, simple proteins and organic acids go first and quickly; fats, waxes and resins persist longest.

soil-bio-126.q: Which layers does the term mean in Canada, and what do specialists disagree about?
soil-bio-126.a: In Canada it means the L, F and H horizons; specialists disagree on whether it equals the O horizon or leaves out the litter.

soil-bio-284.q: Why is cellulose hard for most organisms to use, and who manages it?
soil-bio-284.a: Few organisms can metabolize it; some bacteria and protists can, and ruminants and termites use microorganisms to process it.

soil-bio-300.q: What are living and active organic matter?
soil-bio-300.a: Living matter is roots and organisms in the spaces between and inside aggregates; active matter is fresh or partly decomposed residue in the same spaces.

soil-bio-304.q: What happens to extra organic matter once a soil is saturated for its management?
soil-bio-304.a: It stays as lightly protected free particles.

soil-bio-127.q: Why does mor litter decompose slowly?
soil-bio-127.a: Low pH, low nutrients and high lignin, tannin or terpene contents make needle and heath litter slow to decompose.

soil-bio-295.q: How does the rate of organic matter loss change after cropping begins?
soil-bio-295.a: It is rapid in early years, while active organic matter is plentiful, then slows as mainly stable material remains.

soil-bio-303.q: How did water-stable aggregates vary with organic matter and tillage in the New York study?
soil-bio-303.a: The share rose with organic matter and no tillage, from 27% in conventional vegetable soils to 70% in no-till pasture.

soil-bio-298.q: How much wet dairy manure did a Vermont study say was needed yearly under continuous silage corn?

soil-bio-291.q: Why does organic matter pile up at the surface of acid soils?
soil-bio-291.a: Acidity inhibits earthworms, so organic matter is not mixed through the soil layers.

soil-bio-317.q: Which is harder to break down, cellulose or lignin, and why?
soil-bio-317.a: Lignin: it is a network of aromatic components, mainly degraded by fungi, while cellulose breaks into simple sugars that are readily degraded.

soil-bio-288.q: How does organic matter content vary with soil texture?
soil-bio-288.a: Under 1% in sands, 2-3% in loams and 4% to over 5% in clays.

soil-bio-263.q: Which isotope is used most often in stable isotope probing, and why is 15N weaker?
soil-bio-263.a: 13C; 15N gives a weaker DNA density shift because DNA holds fewer nitrogen atoms.

soil-class-011.q: At which level do moisture regime names modify USDA soil names, and what defines aquic soils?
soil-class-011.a: At the suborder level; aquic soils are saturated and almost free of oxygen long enough to show gleying and mottling.

soil-class-020.q: Which soil groups open the WRB key?
soil-class-020.a: Histosols, with thick organic layers, then soils under strong human influence: Anthrosols and Technosols.

soil-class-008.q: How do typic, intergrade and extragrade subgroups differ?
soil-class-008.a: Typic carries the basic concept of its great group; intergrade grades toward another class without being strong enough to place there; extragrade has aberrant properties that keep it out of any other class.

soil-found-101.q: What defines udic soils in USDA soil taxonomy?
soil-found-101.a: They are moist enough year-round in most years to meet plant needs.

soil-class-045.q: How does clay accumulate in an argillic horizon?
soil-class-045.a: Mainly by illuviation, the downward washing of existing clay, with some clay formed in place.

soil-class-042.q: Is the term pedalfer still used in U.S. soil classification?
soil-class-042.a: No, but it survives in college geology texts, and its 'alf' lives on in the name Alfisol.

soil-class-028.q: What happens when flooding comes with soil warmer than about 5 °C?
soil-class-028.a: Microbes use up the oxygen within days and nitrate and ferric oxide are reduced.

soil-class-047.q: How many FAO groups were there originally, and how many in 1988, for Greyzems?
soil-class-047.a: One of the original 26 FAO groups, it remained among the 28 of the 1988 revision.

soil-class-084.q: Why should fill be as free of organic matter as possible?
soil-class-084.a: Decomposing organic matter leaves voids that make the fill settle and can damage structures on it.

soil-class-157.q: Why are constructed soils preferred to imported topsoil?
soil-class-157.a: Harvesting topsoil degrades a second site and usually costs more.

soil-class-167.q: When was this quicksand without water first created in the laboratory?
soil-class-167.a: In 2004, after long being doubted as folklore.

soil-fert-190.q: Who should avoid soil with estimated total lead above 300 ppm?

soil-fert-164.q: At what concentration in soil water is boron toxic to most plants?

soil-fert-186.q: What carbon-to-nitrogen ratios point to marine sources, and what to land plants?
soil-fert-186.a: Ratios of 4-10:1 usually mean marine sources, while land vascular plants tend to exceed 20.

soil-fert-229.q: How does manganese deficiency show on leaves, and which leaves first?
soil-fert-229.a: Leaves yellow between the veins in a chequered pattern; young leaves show it first because manganese is immobile.

soil-fert-291.q: Which rotations leach less nitrogen than annual row crops?
soil-fert-291.a: Rotations with cover crops, perennial grasses and legumes.

soil-fert-284.q: How does copper deficiency show in plants?
soil-fert-284.a: As browning of leaf tips and chlorosis.

soil-fert-292.q: What do slow-release nitrogen forms and inhibitors do?
soil-fert-292.a: They better match nitrogen supply to crop needs.

soil-found-066.q: In which three oxidation states does mercury occur?

soil-fert-128.q: What limits how much phosphorus an ecosystem has?
soil-fert-128.a: The rate at which weathering releases phosphorus; apatite dissolution is a key control on productivity.

soil-fert-117.q: Who first suggested, and when, that oxidizing ammonia to nitrate is biological?

soil-fert-224.q: How does urea hydrolysis change the pH around it?
soil-fert-224.a: It raises it, because the basic ammonia released is produced in two stages through carbamic acid.

soil-fert-221.q: What view did Nitrospira inopinata overturn?
soil-fert-221.a: That the two steps of nitrification need two organisms; it carries out complete nitrification (comammox).

soil-fert-279.q: What is a farm with a negative nutrient balance doing?
soil-fert-279.a: Living off capital, drawing down mineral and organic-matter nutrients until yields fall.

soil-fert-225.q: Which organisms can turn N2O into N2?
soil-fert-225.a: Only denitrifying prokaryotes, though some denitrifiers lack the step and stop at N2O.

soil-fert-277.q: What is the optimum nitrogen balance, and what do values below 0 and above 50 mean?
soil-fert-277.a: Generally between 0 and +50 pounds per acre; below 0 the soil is being mined of nitrogen, and above 50 the excess causes environmental damage.

soil-fert-035.q: How is compost tea usually made?
soil-fert-035.a: By adding compost to water at 1:4-1:10 and stirring occasionally to release microbes, with or without aeration.

soil-fert-033.q: Why does stabilized compost pose very little risk?
soil-fert-033.a: It has reached 50-70 °C, which kills pathogens and makes even oocysts unviable.

soil-fert-081.q: Which seaweeds are used most, and in what forms?
soil-fert-081.a: Brown seaweeds; laid as mulch, composted, dried and powdered, or made into liquid extracts.

soil-fert-077.q: What did a 2013 study find about a single compost application on grassland?
soil-fert-077.a: It significantly and durably raised carbon storage by 25-70%.

soil-fert-083.q: Which has the highest salt index: potassium chloride, urea or diammonium phosphate?
soil-fert-083.a: Potassium chloride, at 116.2, against 74.4 for urea and 29.2 for diammonium phosphate.

soil-fert-262.q: By how much does a compost pile shrink?
soil-fert-262.a: By 30-60 percent as carbon dioxide and water escape.

soil-fert-205.q: As of 2016, did any country have a specific regulatory framework for biostimulants?
soil-fert-205.a: No; with no agreed definition, some treat them under fertilizer law.

soil-fert-274.q: What should be cut first when phosphorus surpluses build up on livestock farms?
soil-fert-274.a: P in animal diets; a survey found US dairy herds fed about 25% more P than NRC advice.

soil-fert-216.q: What factor converts P2O5 to elemental phosphorus, and K2O to potassium?
soil-fert-216.a: P2O5 is 43.6% phosphorus, so multiply by 0.436; K2O is 83% potassium, so multiply by 0.83.

soil-fert-240.q: What are the two types of integrated crop-livestock farm?
soil-fert-240.a: One mainly sells animal products and matches animal numbers to carrying capacity; the other is a diversified farm that raises all its feed but sells a range of crops and animal products.

soil-fert-268.q: What is the late-spring nitrate test especially good at identifying?
soil-fert-268.a: Sites that need no more N fertilizer, since it implicitly captures early-season weather.

soil-fert-249.q: What should be done where soil P is far above optimum?
soil-fert-249.a: Apply manure by crop P need and export part of it.

soil-fert-244.q: Why do dairy and beef manures influence organic matter more than poultry or swine manure?
soil-fert-244.a: They hold undigested forage and bedding rich in lignin.

soil-fert-251.q: What happens to fall-applied manure in humid climates?
soil-fert-251.a: Ammonium converts to nitrate that leaches or denitrifies; a New York study found about twice the N leaching from fall as from spring application.

soil-water-022.q: What does impervious surface do to groundwater and flooding?
soil-water-022.a: Less water reaches groundwater, so the water table falls and droughts worsen, while more water left on the surface causes flooding.

soil-water-103.q: Why can gelifluction occur on slopes of less than half a degree?
soil-water-103.a: The waterlogged topsoil flows like a liquid.

soil-water-251.q: Which particles are held up by turbulence and travel in suspension?
soil-water-251.a: Particles of about 70 micrometres or less in air.

soil-water-067.q: In which four main ways do plants act on slopes?
soil-water-067.a: Wind throw, removal of water, the added mass of the vegetation (surcharge) and mechanical reinforcement by roots.

soil-water-300.q: What happens to quick clays when saturated?
soil-water-300.a: They liquefy and flow, causing mass wasting.

soil-agri-001.q: Before pedology arose in the 19th century, what was the only branch of soil science?

soil-agri-044.q: What does fallowing do for land and for pests?
soil-agri-044.a: It lets land recover and store organic matter while keeping moisture, and breaks pest and soil-borne pathogen cycles by removing their hosts.

soil-agri-042.q: What did a 2020 review of 229 articles find about the definition of regenerative agriculture?
soil-agri-042.a: No legal or widely accepted definition: some stress practices, others outcomes.

soil-agri-133.q: Why is crop rotation not intercropping?
soil-agri-133.a: Its crops grow in separate seasons.

soil-agri-034.q: What temperature must soil reach in solarization, and to what depth do pathogens die?
soil-agri-034.a: 35-60 °C, which kills pathogens in the top 30 cm.

soil-agri-138.q: Who is called the father of the Green Revolution, and what prize did he receive?
soil-agri-138.a: Norman Borlaug, who received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1970.

soil-agri-139.q: How much does 1 kg of dry coco peat expand to when moist?
soil-agri-139.a: 15 litres, with a pH of 5.5 to 6.5.

soil-agri-012.q: What do permanent indicators and point indicators describe?
soil-agri-012.a: Permanent indicators, chiefly soil properties, describe a field's main constants; point indicators track crop status such as disease, water stress or nitrogen stress.

soil-agri-039.q: How long can rock powder supply nutrients?
soil-agri-039.a: Up to 5 years: plants take what they need and the rest stays crystallized.

soil-agri-045.q: What should susceptible crops such as corn follow, rather than a fallow?
soil-agri-045.a: A cover crop that hosts the fungi, such as oats or another small grain.

soil-agri-148.a: No tillage, no fertilizer, no pesticides or herbicides, no weeding and no pruning.

soil-agri-179.a: By blowing air or steam through molten rock at about 1600 C, giving fine intertwined fibres 2 to 6 micrometres across.

soil-agri-182.q: Why do grass cover crops scavenge nitrogen and reduce erosion?
soil-agri-182.a: Their fibrous root systems scavenge leftover nutrients, especially nitrogen, and some establish rapidly.

soil-agri-198.q: What should follow a legume forage in rotation?
soil-agri-198.a: A high-nitrogen crop such as corn.

soil-agri-190.q: How do cover crops raise infiltration and water-holding capacity?
soil-agri-190.a: Infiltration through macropores, and water-holding capacity through organic matter; residue also slows runoff.

soil-agri-191.q: Are grain crops hosts of root-knot nematode?
soil-agri-191.a: No, they are nonhosts, so growing grains reduces numbers; very bad infestations may need two full grain seasons.

soil-agri-197.q: How long a break do diseases need from their host crops?
soil-agri-197.a: Some need only a one-year break; others need several years of nonhost crops to cut inoculum.

soil-agri-203.q: What is considered the foundation of modern agroecology?

soil-agri-223.q: What did centuries of tillage cause, especially around the Mediterranean?
soil-agri-223.a: Excessive erosion, organic matter loss and nutrient depletion.

soil-agri-061.q: What is the difference between shelterbelts and woodlots?
soil-agri-061.a: Shelterbelts are rows of trees set perpendicular to the prevailing wind, while woodlots are more extensive areas of woodland.

soil-agri-070.q: What is the smother effect of a flattened cover crop?
soil-agri-070.a: It forms a nearly impenetrable mat that blocks light, cutting weed germination.

soil-agri-079.q: What did the act passed after the Supreme Court struck down the Agricultural Adjustment Act do?
soil-agri-079.a: It amended and renamed the Soil Conservation Act of 1935 to preserve soil fertility and reduce exploitation and unprofitable use of national soil resources.

soil-agri-078.q: In what climate does this road dust suppressant work best, and what is its chief benefit?
soil-agri-078.a: It works better in humid than in arid climates, and its chief benefit is lower maintenance costs for gravel roads.

soil-agri-208.q: Why does keeping soil covered reduce erosion?
soil-agri-208.a: Water and wind erosion occur almost exclusively on exposed soil, and live plants protect it best.

soil-agri-206.q: When is erosion worst, and what does tillage do to runoff?
soil-agri-206.a: It is worst when soil has no living plants, roots or residue mulch; tillage that breaks aggregates lowers infiltration and worsens runoff.

soil-agri-213.q: How does more soil organic matter reduce runoff?
soil-agri-213.a: It gives better aggregation and less surface sealing, so more water infiltrates instead of running off and carrying soil away.

soil-agri-163.q: When is a remote sensor called active, and when passive?
soil-agri-163.a: It is active when it emits a signal and detects its reflection, and passive when it detects reflected sunlight.

soil-agri-166.q: Into which four categories of decreasing generality is this land suitability classification divided?
soil-agri-166.a: Orders (kinds of suitability), classes (degrees), subclasses (kinds of limitation) and units (minor management differences).

soil-agri-218.q: Why are large expanses of poor land mapped by reconnaissance survey?
soil-agri-218.a: They have little agricultural or forest value and are often too poor to justify a detailed survey, so they are mapped at small scale, showing soil associations.

soil-meth-023.q: How does atomic absorption measure a metal?
soil-meth-023.a: The metal is vaporized in a flame and absorbs at its own wavelengths; the absorbed radiation is proportional to the density of its atoms.

soil-meth-059.q: Which extractants suit acidic and alkaline soils in Washington and Oregon?
soil-meth-059.a: Bray 1 is used for acidic soils and Olsen for alkaline soils.

soil-meth-061.q: What can very high phosphorus in a soil test point to?
soil-meth-061.a: Years of heavy poultry or other manure.

soil-meth-027.q: What does the voltage of an ion-selective electrode depend on?
soil-meth-027.a: It depends on the logarithm of the ion's activity, following the Nernst equation, and is read against a reference electrode.

soil-meth-066.q: Why is human vision still needed in image analysis despite computers?
soil-meth-066.a: Computers are indispensable for large data and quantitative extraction, but human vision cannot be replaced in many applications.

soil-meth-045.q: Name two spatial autocorrelation statistics covered by spatial analysis.

soil-agri-090.q: What two factors does the scorpan model add to the classical five?
soil-agri-090.a: s, intrinsic soil properties captured by remote and proximal sensors, and n, spatial coordinates or position.

soil-meth-053.q: What does Cohen's kappa add to overall accuracy?
soil-meth-053.a: It corrects for chance agreement; both measures range from 0 to 1.

soil-meth-001.q: What was geostatistics first developed to predict?
soil-meth-001.a: The distribution of ore grades in mines.

soil-meth-004.q: What does regression kriging model separately?
soil-meth-004.a: The deterministic and stochastic parts of variation, following Matheron's 1969 universal model.

soil-meth-048.q: What must stratified sampling strata satisfy?
soil-meth-048.a: They must be collectively exhaustive and mutually exclusive, so every element falls in exactly one.

soil-meth-052.q: What does conditioned Latin hypercube sampling do?
soil-meth-052.a: It samples all covariates with one sample per stratum.

soil-meth-016.q: How does gamma-ray spectroscopy of soil identify elements?
soil-meth-016.a: Cosmic rays make nuclei emit gamma rays; each emission line's energy identifies an element and its intensity gives the concentration.

soil-meth-033.q: Who coined the term chemometrics, and when?
soil-meth-033.a: Svante Wold, in a 1971 grant application.

soil-env-106.q: How much carbon do soils hold compared with the atmosphere?
soil-env-106.a: About 2,700 Gt, roughly three times the carbon in the atmosphere.

soil-env-110.q: What does plant uptake do to carbon in soil?
soil-env-110.a: It fixes carbon dioxide in soil, building a pool of around 1500 Pg in the first few metres, 20-40% of it lasting more than 100 years.

soil-env-103.q: What does the fast carbon cycle include?
soil-env-103.a: It runs through living things, with annual cycles driven by photosynthesis and decadal cycles of vegetation growth and decomposition.

soil-env-105.q: Why does replacing forest with cropland leave more carbon in the atmosphere?
soil-env-105.a: Cropland and urban land store comparatively little carbon.

soil-env-141.q: What visible sign shows permafrost thaw weakening soil structure?
soil-env-141.a: Trees tilting at random, so-called drunken trees.

soil-env-147.q: What is active layer thickness, and what is its main control?
soil-env-147.a: It is the maximum thaw depth over two years; maximum air temperature is the main control.

soil-env-149.q: What does the Russian word behind this term mean?
soil-env-149.a: That which survives over the summer.

soil-env-127.q: What slows weathering as the soil solution saturates?
soil-env-127.a: Weathering slows as the soil solution saturates, so some argue low rainfall limits it.

soil-env-121.q: Why is glomalin's role in soil carbon thought overestimated?
soil-env-121.a: Most glomalin-extracted proteins proved not to be mycorrhizal, and arbuscular fungi were found to cause net soil carbon losses.

soil-env-058.q: How does degradation differ from retrogression?
soil-env-058.a: Degradation is directly tied to human activity, whereas retrogression is driven mainly by soil erosion.

soil-env-063.q: How much faster than soil forms does erosion from farm fields run?
soil-env-063.a: 11 to 20 times faster under no-tillage and more than 100 times faster under conventional tillage.

soil-env-059.q: Why does secondary succession run faster than primary succession?

soil-env-078.q: Why are Middle Eastern dust storms becoming more frequent and intense?
soil-env-078.a: Long-term rainfall decline lowers soil moisture and plant cover.

soil-env-069.q: How much of human-induced land degradation is due to unsustainable farming?
soil-env-069.a: Over 60%: it had degraded 996 Mha of agricultural land by 2025.

soil-env-321.q: Why do roots need pores wider than about 0.1 mm?
soil-env-321.a: It is the size of most root tips; without such pores roots stay short and thick with few fine roots or root hairs, poor at taking up water and nutrients.

soil-env-210.q: How do denser woody canopies affect soil moisture?
soil-env-210.a: They raise transpiration and evaporation of soil moisture, and enhanced soil porosity can speed soil drought.

soil-env-099.q: How can lightly degraded land be restored?
soil-env-099.a: It can be fenced from grazing, fertilized or weeded; grazing may continue at lower, monitored intensity, for example by rotating fields seasonally.

soil-env-308.q: How do deep roots help soil handle urban runoff?
soil-env-308.a: They open extra channels for infiltration, maintain soil permeability and sustain the microbes that break down pollutants and remove nitrogen.

soil-env-375.q: When is scraping the surface and replacing it with good topsoil feasible?
soil-env-375.a: When contamination is modest or shallow, since excavating contaminated soil is expensive and regulated.

soil-env-377.q: What two demands must a rooftop soil mix meet?
soil-env-377.a: It must be light enough not to overload the roof yet heavy enough to anchor plants against wind and water.

soil-env-195.q: What makes up a septic system?
soil-env-195.a: The drain field, septic tank and piping together, where a microbial ecosystem breaks down the organic materials in the liquid.

soil-agri-169.q: What remains the main disposal mechanism in conventional septic systems?
soil-agri-169.a: Decomposition by natural organisms, so minimum retention times and distances to surface water and wells are set.

soil-env-350.q: Why sample at least 10 spots when assessing soil health in the field?
soil-env-350.a: Measurements vary with moisture and season, so a single spot may mislead.

soil-env-365.q: Why do perennials give more carbon input than annuals?
soil-env-365.a: Because of larger root systems and a longer photosynthesis period.

soil-env-341.q: Why can routine soil fumigation or broad-spectrum herbicides backfire?
soil-env-341.a: They create dependency on purchased inputs, weaken resilience and promote resistance.

soil-env-193.q: How do industry and construction damage urban soil?
soil-env-193.a: Industry alters soil chemistry with heavy metals and effluents, while construction and landfills compact and excavate soil, disturbing water purification and storage.

soil-env-344.q: How do damaged plants call in help against caterpillars?
soil-env-344.a: They produce extra-floral nectar that feeds beneficials and airborne volatiles that guide small wasps to the caterpillar, in which the wasp lays eggs that kill it.

soil-env-360.q: Which soils suit no-till, and which suit strip-till or zone-till?
soil-env-360.a: Well-drained coarse soils suit no-till; finer-textured soils do well with strip-till or zone-till.

soil-env-327.q: Which soil properties change little, and which can management change?
soil-env-327.a: Inherent properties such as drainage and depth change little; management can change dynamic ones such as organic matter, structure, and water and nutrient holding capacity.

soil-env-367.q: How can compaction be avoided on larger farms?
soil-env-367.a: By monitoring axle loads and tire inflation and avoiding field work on wet soil.

soil-env-343.q: How does East African push-pull protect corn?
soil-env-343.a: Desmodium within corn rows repels stem borers (push) and perimeter grasses attract adult moths (pull).

soil-env-346.q: Why does optimal soil health underpin pest management?
soil-env-346.a: Healthy, thriving plants defend themselves better, while stressed plants signal weakness to pests.

soil-env-009.q: Why can wiping out part of the base of the food chain matter?
soil-env-009.a: It can have major consequences for predators and other consumers.

soil-env-005.q: When did use of this pesticide peak, and why did it fall?
soil-env-005.a: Use peaked at 72,000 tonnes in 1970 and then fell as its harm became clear.

soil-env-249.q: What governs action on contaminated land where no standards exist?

soil-env-008.q: Which metals and compounds are linked to cancer or birth defects after long exposure?
soil-env-008.a: Chromium, lead and other metals, petroleum, solvents and many pesticides.

soil-env-242.q: What does a groundwater pollutant often form, and where can it reach?
soil-env-242.a: A plume that spreads through the aquifer and can reach wells, seeps and springs.

soil-env-032.q: Why do bioaugmentation attempts often fail?
soil-env-032.a: Failures come from the wrong organism, predation, competition with native bacteria and too-small doses.

soil-env-049.q: What do the seven letters-factors of the DRASTIC index describe, and what does a lower index mean?
soil-env-049.a: They cover depth to water, net recharge, aquifer media, soil media, topography, vadose zone impact and hydraulic conductivity; a lower index means lower risk of aquifer contamination.

soil-env-314.a: Sewage sludges treated to lower pathogen risk, widely used as soil amendments.

soil-env-043.q: How does rhizofiltration differ from phytoextraction?
soil-env-043.a: It traps contaminants, mainly heavy metals, in harvestable biomass but treats water, while phytoextraction treats soil.

soil-env-232.q: What is bioavailability, and why does it matter for biodegradation?
soil-env-232.a: It is the amount of a pollutant physically accessible to microbes, and it is a key factor in efficient biodegradation.

soil-env-317.q: Why does removing fines reduce the soil to treat?
soil-env-317.a: Contaminants cling to the fines, so removing them reduces total mass and volume.

soil-env-288.q: In which groups is eating soil documented?
soil-env-288.a: In over 100 primate species and, in humans, most often in children and pregnant women, classed as a form of pica.

soil-env-295.q: Where is iodine deficiency common, and what does it cause?
soil-env-295.a: In remote inland and mountainous areas with iodine-poor soil and no marine foods; it causes goitre and developmental delay.

soil-env-305.q: How are prions transmitted to grazing animals through soil?
soil-env-305.a: By eating grass growing in contaminated soil; they stay infectious for years and bind tightly to soil particles.

soil-hist-147.q: What does photosynthesis usually mean, and what does it release?
soil-hist-147.a: Oxygenic photosynthesis, which splits water and releases oxygen.

soil-hist-124.q: What builds up trapped charge in buried quartz or feldspar grains?
soil-hist-124.a: Natural radiation from cosmic rays and traces of potassium, uranium, thorium and rubidium.

soil-hist-149.q: Why is glycolate a problem for photosynthesis?
soil-hist-149.a: It is toxic at high concentration and inhibits photosynthesis.

soil-hist-125.q: Why must luminescence grains be extracted without exposure to light?
soil-hist-125.a: Light frees the trapped electrons, so exposure would release the signal.

soil-hist-122.q: Which fraction of peat gives the most reliable radiocarbon date?
soil-hist-122.a: The humins, because they are insoluble in alkali and less contaminated.

soil-hist-130.q: Where does excess lead-210 in surface soils come from?
soil-hist-130.a: Atmospheric fallout of radon-222 decay products.

soil-hist-036.q: What did Josiah Wedgwood suggest caused the buried lime and cinders at Maer Hall?

soil-hist-143.q: Where did this soil salinity research begin?
soil-hist-143.a: At Hisar in 1969, moving to Karnal that year.

soil-hist-032.q: What did soil surveys mainly serve before 1950?

soil-hist-106.q: What did this man experiment with in his twenties, and why?
soil-hist-106.a: Marl, to rejuvenate land worn out by more than a century of tobacco monoculture.

soil-hist-110.q: What did he show about where plants get their carbon?
soil-hist-110.a: Plants take their carbon from atmospheric carbon dioxide, not from soil humus.

soil-hist-017.q: Who invented the enrichment culture, and why was it hard to isolate nitrifiers?
soil-hist-017.a: Martinus Beijerinck invented it; early nitrification researchers could at first only enrich cultures of nitrifiers rather than isolate them pure.

soil-hist-047.q: What is the purpose of this international soil science union?
soil-hist-047.a: To promote all branches of soil science and their applications, foster contacts among soil scientists, and stimulate research and its use.

soil-hist-052.q: When did Milton Whitney begin field work?

soil-hist-056.q: What was the main contribution of this NRCS committee?
soil-hist-056.a: Improving technical standards for describing anthropogenic soils and defining the taxa to classify them.

b43af3d6220c.title: Soil
b43af3d6220c.sentence: Soil, also commonly referred to as earth, is a mixture of organic matter, minerals, gases, water, and organisms that together support the life of plants and soil organisms.

e546a20304c0.title: Soil
e546a20304c0.sentence: Collectively, the Earth's body of soil is called the pedosphere.

518a2de1bdd9.title: Soil
518a2de1bdd9.sentence: Soil consists of a solid collection of minerals and organic matter (the soil matrix), as well as a porous phase (Pore space) that holds gases (the soil atmosphere) and a liquid phase that holds water and dissolved substances both organic and inorganic, in ionic or in molecular form (the soil solution).

37fc265244c8.title: Soil
37fc265244c8.sentence: Accordingly, soil is a complex three-state system of solids, liquids, and gases.

f03e5621af1c.title: Soil
f03e5621af1c.sentence: Soil is a product of several factors: the influence of climate, relief (elevation, orientation, and slope of terrain), organisms, and the soil's parent materials (original minerals) interacting over time.

74ae34ff6fe8.title: Soil
74ae34ff6fe8.sentence: It continually undergoes development through numerous physical, chemical, and biological processes, which include weathering with associated erosion.

f6565a664abf.title: Soil
f6565a664abf.sentence: Most soils have a dry bulk density (density of soil taking into account voids when dry) between 1.1 and 1.6 g/cm3, though the soil particle density is much higher, in the range of 2.6 to 2.7 g/cm3.

ee3b790f0b2e.title: Soil
ee3b790f0b2e.sentence: Little of the soil of planet Earth is older than the Pleistocene and none is older than the Cenozoic, although fossilized soils are preserved from as far back as the Archean.

0b14e20f880a.title: Soil
0b14e20f880a.sentence: - as a medium for plant growth

97f76a060896.title: Soil
97f76a060896.sentence: - as a means of water storage, water supply, and water purification

335276d7a08f.title: Soil
335276d7a08f.sentence: - as a modifier of Earth's atmosphere

03c44eaab2e2.title: Soil
03c44eaab2e2.sentence: - as a habitat for soil organisms

f0e60dd4d27b.title: Soil
f0e60dd4d27b.sentence: A gram of soil can contain billions of organisms, belonging to thousands of species, mostly microbial and largely still unexplored.

d89b8513d4b5.title: Soil
d89b8513d4b5.sentence: Given its complexity and strong internal connectedness, soil ecologists regard soil as an ecosystem.

9facbe8c9005.title: Soil
9facbe8c9005.sentence: With respect to Earth's carbon cycle, soil acts as an important carbon reservoir, and it is potentially one of the most reactive to human disturbance and climate change.

6e5e244998f4.title: Soil
6e5e244998f4.sentence: Some scientific definitions distinguish dirt from soil by restricting the former term specifically to displaced soil.

bee518f26ab3.title: Soil science
bee518f26ab3.sentence: Soil science is the study of soil as a natural resource on the surface of the Earth including soil formation, classification and mapping; physical, chemical, biological, and fertility properties of soils; and these properties in relation to the use and management of soils.

03e8d020acfc.title: Soil science
03e8d020acfc.sentence: This is the conceptual perspective of pedology and edaphology, the two main historical branches of soil science.

5c6f67d59379.title: Soil science
5c6f67d59379.sentence: Pedology is the study of soil in its natural setting.

014e50bc4546.title: Soil science
014e50bc4546.sentence: Edaphology is the study of soil in relation to soil-dependent uses.

234c604c71bf.title: Soil science
234c604c71bf.sentence: Both branches apply a combination of soil physics, soil chemistry, and soil biology.

811a8a6c694d.title: Soil science
811a8a6c694d.sentence: Academically, soil scientists tend to be drawn to one of five areas of specialization: soil biology, pedology, edaphology, physics, or chemistry.

eea01fba7825.title: Soil science
eea01fba7825.sentence: Indeed, engineers, agronomists, chemists, geologists, physical geographers, ecologists, biologists, microbiologists, silviculturists, sanitarians, archaeologists, landscape architects and specialists in regional planning, all contribute to further knowledge of soils and the advancement of the soil sciences.

c5019097c9d7.title: Soil science
c5019097c9d7.sentence: Soil occupies the pedosphere, one of Earth's spheres that the geosciences use to organize the Earth conceptually.

dfcda523decc.title: Soil science
dfcda523decc.sentence: New areas of soil research are driven by the need to understand soil in the context of climate change, greenhouse gases, and carbon sequestration.

86282a535e4c.title: Soil science
86282a535e4c.sentence: Interest in maintaining biodiversity and in exploring past cultures has also created renewed interest in achieving a better understanding of soil.

07916ede0f74.title: Soil science
07916ede0f74.sentence: Soil scientists have raised concerns about how to preserve soil and arable land in a world with a growing population, possible future water crisis, increasing per-capita food consumption, and land degradation.

71fe1007958d.title: Soil science
71fe1007958d.sentence: In 1998, the World Reference Base for Soil Resources (WRB) replaced the FAO soil classification as the international soil classification system.

84cbf9631b07.title: Soil science
84cbf9631b07.sentence: The currently valid version of WRB is the 4th edition, 2022.

e6ee6265386b.title: Soil science
e6ee6265386b.sentence: Soil mapping is the process of classifying soil types and properties in a given area and geo-encoding the information.

fb442423e04d.title: Soil science
fb442423e04d.sentence: More recently digital soil mapping approaches have been developed in various countries for quantifying soils in space and time using remote sensing data.

f5e64472d139.title: Pedosphere
f5e64472d139.sentence: The pedosphere (from Ancient Greek πέδον (pédon) 'ground, earth' and σφαῖρα (sphaîra) 'sphere') is the outermost layer of the Earth's crust that is composed of soil and subject to soil formation and erosion processes.

3f238b12032e.title: Pedosphere
3f238b12032e.sentence: It exists at the interface of the lithosphere, atmosphere, hydrosphere and biosphere.

fbd5285c4a43.title: Pedosphere
fbd5285c4a43.sentence: The pedosphere is the "stratum corneum" of the Earth's surface and only develops when there is a dynamic interaction between the atmosphere (air in and above the soil), biosphere (living organisms and associated organic matters), lithosphere (unconsolidated regolith and consolidated bedrock) and the hydrosphere (water in, on and below the soil).

a8d55a73d8de.title: Pedosphere
a8d55a73d8de.sentence: The pedosphere is the foundation of terrestrial ecosystems on Earth.

6b8052512278.title: Pedosphere
6b8052512278.sentence: The pedosphere acts as the mediator of chemical and biogeochemical flux into and out of these respective systems and is made up of gaseous, mineralic, fluid and biologic components.

9d77f888cab8.title: Pedosphere
9d77f888cab8.sentence: The pedosphere lies within the Critical Zone, a broader interface that includes vegetation, pedosphere, aquifer systems, regolith and finally ends at some depth in the bedrock where the biosphere and hydrosphere cease to make significant changes to the chemistry at depth.

cef6339379f8.title: Pedosphere
cef6339379f8.sentence: Soil formation begins with the chemical and/or physical breakdown of minerals to form the initial material that overlies the bedrock substrate.

95b23c859c66.title: Pedosphere
95b23c859c66.sentence: The soil forming process (pedogenesis) can begin without the aid of biology but is significantly quickened in the presence of biologic reactions, where it forms a soil carbon sponge.

a52f6bab111d.title: Pedosphere
a52f6bab111d.sentence: As time progresses, the bulk geochemistry of the soil layer will deviate away from the initial composition of the bedrock and will evolve to a chemistry that reflects the type of reactions that take place in the soil.

61b92043e6b8.title: Pedosphere
61b92043e6b8.sentence: The primary conditions for soil development are controlled by the chemical composition of the rock on which the soil will be.

c6ab6c7c5cec.title: Pedosphere
c6ab6c7c5cec.sentence: There are few rock types that lead to localized enrichment of some of the biologically limiting elements like phosphorus (P) and nitrogen (N).

2ad7fb159ea8.title: Pedosphere
2ad7fb159ea8.sentence: The process of soil formation is dominated by chemical weathering of silicate minerals, aided by acidic products of pioneering plants and organisms as well as carbonic acid inputs from the atmosphere.

55454abc5536.title: Pedology
55454abc5536.sentence: Pedology (from Greek: πέδον, pedon, "soil"; and λόγος, logos, "study") is a discipline within soil science which focuses on understanding and characterizing soil formation, evolution, and the theoretical frameworks for modeling soil bodies, often in the context of the natural environment.

f4c509059130.title: Pedology
f4c509059130.sentence: Pedology is often seen as one of two main branches of soil inquiry, the other being edaphology which is traditionally more agronomically oriented and focuses on how soil properties influence plant communities (natural or cultivated).

652ee67b7558.title: Pedology
652ee67b7558.sentence: In studying the fundamental phenomenology of soils, e.g., soil formation (aka pedogenesis), pedologists pay particular attention to observing soil morphology, the geographic distributions of soils, and the placement of soil bodies within larger temporal and spatial contexts.

6758930cb2a0.title: Pedology
6758930cb2a0.sentence: In so doing, pedologists develop systems of soil classification, soil maps, and theories for characterizing temporal and spatial interrelations among soils.

f23b39eb3d46.title: Pedology
f23b39eb3d46.sentence: There are a few noteworthy sub-disciplines of pedology; namely pedometrics and soil geomorphology.

8d21a2d0e05b.title: Pedology
8d21a2d0e05b.sentence: Pedometrics focuses on the development of techniques for quantitative characterization of soils, especially for the purposes of mapping soil properties whereas soil geomorphology studies the interrelationships between geomorphic processes and soil formation.

04e131f03e6d.title: Pedology
04e131f03e6d.sentence: Soil users (such as agronomists) showed initially little concern in the dynamics of soil.

313130020b1c.title: Pedology
313130020b1c.sentence: They saw it as a medium whose chemical, physical and biological properties were useful for the services of agronomic productivity.

5cc6552ec31c.title: Pedology
5cc6552ec31c.sentence: On the other hand, pedologists and geologists did not initially focus on the agronomic applications of the soil characteristics (edaphic properties) but upon its relation to the nature and history of landscapes.

1654f8b187fb.title: Pedology
1654f8b187fb.sentence: Today, there is an integration of the two disciplinary approaches as part of landscape and environmental sciences.

475935059213.title: Pedology
475935059213.sentence: During its formation and genesis, the soil profile slowly deepens and develops characteristic layers, called 'horizons', while a steady state balance is approached.

70d905d3ea83.title: Edaphology
70d905d3ea83.sentence: Friedrich Albert Fallou originally conceived pedology in the 19th century as a fundamental science separate from the applied science of agrology, a predecessor term for edaphology, a distinction retained in the current understanding of edaphology.

5ad214ab1530.title: Edaphology
5ad214ab1530.sentence: Edaphology (from Greek ἔδαφος, edaphos 'ground' + -λογία, -logia) is concerned with the influence of soils on living beings, particularly plants.

cdc0d8120867.title: Edaphology
cdc0d8120867.sentence: It is one of two main divisions of soil science, the other being pedology.

1c3d4c6e01f6.title: Edaphology
1c3d4c6e01f6.sentence: Edaphology includes the study of how soil influences humankind's use of land for plant growth as well as people's overall use of the land.

35e3e0d0d420.title: Edaphology
35e3e0d0d420.sentence: General subfields within edaphology are agricultural soil science (known by the term agrology in some regions) and environmental soil science.

2b114f16041f.title: Edaphology
2b114f16041f.sentence: The history of edaphology is not simple, as the two main alternative terms for soil science—pedology and edaphology—were initially poorly distinguished.

4ad4841570a8.title: Edaphology
4ad4841570a8.sentence: In the case of Russian soil scientists, edaphology was used as an equivalent term to pedology, and in Spain, soil scientists adopted edaphology in preference to the term pedology.

55f9c5b11489.title: Edaphology
55f9c5b11489.sentence: During the 20th century, the term edaphology was "driven out of [pedology-centric] soil science" but remained in use to address edaphic problems in other disciplines.

cfd6b844b6b8.title: Edaphology
cfd6b844b6b8.sentence: In the 21st century, edaphology is recognized by soil scientists as a branch of soil science necessary and complementary to the pedology branch.

99cb54c232b4.title: Edaphology
99cb54c232b4.sentence: Xenophon (431—355 BC), and Cato (234—149 BC), were early edaphologists.

c6c07b4e1ede.title: Edaphology
c6c07b4e1ede.sentence: Cato wrote De Agri Cultura ("On Farming"), which recommended tillage, crop rotation, and the use of legumes in the rotation to build soil nitrogen.

cc3856fc467f.title: Edaphology
cc3856fc467f.sentence: He also devised the first soil capability classification for specific crops.

6f27b3a3b143.title: Edaphology
6f27b3a3b143.section: Areas of study > Environmental soil science
6f27b3a3b143.sentence: Fundamental and applied aspects of the field address vadose zone functions, septic drain field site assessment and function, land treatment of wastewater, stormwater, erosion control, soil contamination with metals and pesticides, remediation of contaminated soils, restoration of wetlands, soil degradation, and environmental nutrient management.

a3ccab778f94.title: Soil
a3ccab778f94.sentence: A typical soil is about 50% solids (45% mineral and 5% organic matter), and 50% voids (or pores) of which half is occupied by water and half by gas.

410c959f9ddd.title: Soil
410c959f9ddd.sentence: The percent soil mineral and organic content can be treated as a constant (in the short term), while the percent soil water and gas content is considered highly variable whereby a rise in one is simultaneously balanced by a reduction in the other.

83ac810871f1.title: Soil
83ac810871f1.sentence: The pore space allows for the infiltration and movement of air and water, both of which are critical for life existing in soil.

e7a164a9f49a.title: Soil
e7a164a9f49a.sentence: Compaction, a common problem with soils, in particular under heavy machinery traffic, reduces this space, preventing air and water from reaching plant roots and soil organisms.

05609e2734ea.title: Soil
05609e2734ea.sentence: The interaction of the individual mineral particles with organic matter, water, gases via biotic and abiotic processes causes those particles to flocculate (stick together) to form aggregates or peds.

1a2739156111.title: Soil
1a2739156111.sentence: Where these aggregates can be identified, a soil can be said to be developed, and can be described further in terms of color, porosity, consistency, reaction (acidity), etc.

91ceac918e85.title: Soil
91ceac918e85.sentence: Soils supply plants with nutrients, most of which are held in place by particles of clay and organic matter (colloids) The nutrients may be adsorbed on clay mineral surfaces, bound within clay minerals (absorbed), or bound within organic compounds as part of the living organisms or dead soil organic matter (humus).

73de321e24dd.title: Soil
73de321e24dd.sentence: Most plant nutrients, with the exception of nitrogen, fixed from the atmosphere, originate from the minerals that make up the soil parent material.

b9b554210db9.title: Soil
b9b554210db9.sentence: The biological influences on soil properties (e.g. bioturbation) are strongest near the surface, while the geochemical influences on soil properties increase with depth.

767d3b24c14e.title: Soil
767d3b24c14e.sentence: Soil is used in agriculture, where it serves as the anchor and primary nutrient base for plants.

8844267d548e.title: Soil
8844267d548e.sentence: Soil material is also a critical component in mining, construction and landscape development (also called landscape architecture) industries.

7f6093f547d4.title: Soil
7f6093f547d4.sentence: The types of soil and available moisture determine the species of plants that can be cultivated.

771fb3a8f767.title: Soil
771fb3a8f767.sentence: Soil resources are critical to the environment, as well as to food and fibre production, producing 98.8% of food consumed by humans.

b8da2b964d9a.title: Soil
b8da2b964d9a.sentence: Soil serves as a foundation for most construction projects.

dae1af7831c3.title: Soil
dae1af7831c3.sentence: Many building materials are soil based.

2c546ffe0d8f.title: Soil
2c546ffe0d8f.sentence: The movement of massive volumes of soil can be involved in surface mining, road building and dam construction.

3f3f8dfe8ca3.title: Soil
3f3f8dfe8ca3.sentence: Waste management often has a soil component.

d92c6a458cce.title: Soil
d92c6a458cce.sentence: Septic drain fields treat septic tank effluent using aerobic soil processes.

bdda7fcf6863.title: Soil
bdda7fcf6863.sentence: Land application of waste water relies on soil biology to aerobically treat BOD.

70790cca8062.title: Soil
70790cca8062.sentence: Alternatively, landfills use soil for daily cover, isolating waste deposits from the atmosphere and preventing unpleasant smells.

2dcd2c2c6cd0.title: Soil
2dcd2c2c6cd0.sentence: Rain water and pooled water from ponds, lakes and rivers percolate through the soil horizons and the upper rock strata, thus becoming groundwater.

7eb2a063083e.title: Soil
7eb2a063083e.sentence: Pests (viruses) and pollutants, such as persistent organic pollutants (chlorinated pesticides, polychlorinated biphenyls), oils (hydrocarbons), heavy metals (lead, zinc, cadmium), and excess nutrients (nitrates, sulfates, phosphates) are filtered out by the soil.

2e38ae34deff.title: Soil
2e38ae34deff.sentence: Organic soils, especially peat, serve as a significant fuel and horticultural resource.

21f44926d13b.title: Soil
21f44926d13b.sentence: Peat soils are also commonly used for the sake of agriculture in Nordic countries, because peatland sites, when drained, provide fertile soils for food production.

58c2f57607d1.title: Soil
58c2f57607d1.sentence: Geophagy is the practice of eating soil-like substances.

df1fe713ee0a.title: Soil
df1fe713ee0a.sentence: Both animals and humans occasionally consume soil for medicinal, recreational, or religious purposes.

c96d66d657c3.title: Soil
c96d66d657c3.sentence: It has been shown that some monkeys consume soil, together with their preferred food (tree foliage and fruits), in order to alleviate tannin toxicity.

7398db348711.title: Soil
7398db348711.sentence: However, as demonstrated by aeroponics, aquaponics and hydroponics, soil material is not an absolute essential for agriculture, and soilless cropping systems have been claimed as the future of agriculture for an endless growing mankind.

810898cf756a.title: Soil science
810898cf756a.sentence: Dokuchaev considers the soil as a natural body having its own genesis and its own history of development, a body with complex and multiform processes taking place within it.

61d65d7a0016.title: Soil science
61d65d7a0016.sentence: The soil is considered as different from bedrock.

2c1f0e6c47ae.title: Soil science
2c1f0e6c47ae.sentence: Contemporaries Friedrich Albert Fallou (the German founder of modern soil science) and Vasily Dokuchaev (the Russian founder of modern soil science) are both credited with being among the first to identify soil as a resource whose distinctness and complexity deserved to be separated conceptually from geology and crop production and treated as a whole.

a2dc3e880cbc.title: Soil science
a2dc3e880cbc.sentence: As a founding father of soil science, Fallou has primacy in time, working on the origins of soil before Dokuchaev was born.

e0866ac09016.title: Soil science
e0866ac09016.sentence: However, Dokuchaev's work was more extensive and is considered to be more significant to modern soil theory than Fallou's.

cb8b100a651a.title: Soil science
cb8b100a651a.sentence: Previously, soil had been considered a product of chemical transformations of rocks, a dead substrate from which plants derive nutritious elements.

195bc2eca764.title: Soil science
195bc2eca764.sentence: The latter becomes soil under the influence of a series of soil-forming factors (climate, vegetation, country, relief and age).

78a3d090368c.title: Soil science
78a3d090368c.sentence: A 1914 encyclopedic definition: "the different forms of earth on the surface of the rocks, formed by the breaking down or weathering of rocks". serves to illustrate the historic view of soil which persisted from the 19th century.

5790e5fae0d2.title: Soil science
5790e5fae0d2.sentence: Dokuchaev's late 19th century soil concept developed in the 20th century to one of soil as earthy material that has been altered by living processes.

a410c5f6ac37.title: Soil science
a410c5f6ac37.sentence: Further refinement of the soil concept is occurring in view of an appreciation of energy transport and transformation within soil.

c680f5587238.title: Soil science
c680f5587238.sentence: Accurate to this modern understanding of soil is Nikiforoff's 1959 definition of soil as the "excited skin of the sub aerial part of the Earth's crust".

ec067fd42752.title: Soil functions
ec067fd42752.sentence: Soil functions are general capabilities of soils that are important for various agricultural, environmental, nature protection, landscape architecture and urban applications.

d44aa6a24d96.title: Soil functions
d44aa6a24d96.sentence: Soil can perform many functions and these include functions related to the natural ecosystems, agricultural productivity, environmental quality, source of raw material, and as base for buildings.

e88c3d3943a2.title: Soil functions
e88c3d3943a2.sentence: It provides a hospitable place for a plant to live in while storing and supplying nutrients to plants.

c304067145d7.title: Soil functions
c304067145d7.sentence: Soil also functions by maintaining the quantity and quality of air by allowing CO 2 to escape and fresh O 2 to enter the root zone.

8eee529cd29e.title: Soil functions
8eee529cd29e.sentence: Pore spaces within soil can also absorb water and hold it until plant roots need it.

a65a0d029047.title: Soil functions
a65a0d029047.sentence: The soil also moderates temperature fluctuation, providing a suitable temperature for the roots to function normally.

5a3f322cf559.title: Soil functions
5a3f322cf559.sentence: The combination of these activities supports plant growth for providing food and other biomass production.

e53eb2560a4e.title: Soil functions
e53eb2560a4e.sentence: Soils also acts as a biological habitat and a gene reserve for a large variety of organisms.

77949e93d976.title: Soil functions
77949e93d976.sentence: The assistance of soil in the decomposition of dead plants, animals, and organism by transforming their remains into simpler mineral forms, can be utilized by other living things.

e7ab6f4ba7c9.title: Soil functions
e7ab6f4ba7c9.sentence: Soil provides raw materials for human use and impacts human health directly.

32fd778a216b.title: Soil functions
32fd778a216b.sentence: The composition of human food reflects the nature of the soil in which it was grown.

174e160cebb8.title: Soil functions
174e160cebb8.sentence: An example of soil as a source of raw material can be found in ancient ceramic production.

896ad80cc6e1.title: Soil functions
896ad80cc6e1.sentence: The Maya ceramics showed traits inherited from soils and sediments used as raw material.

b40e109b4037.title: Soil functions
b40e109b4037.sentence: However, the natural area of productive soils is limited and due to increasing pressure of cropping, forestry, and urbanization, extracting soil as a raw material needs to be controlled for.

1ac04bf598b6.title: Soil functions
1ac04bf598b6.sentence: Soil also has more general culture functions as they act as a part of the cultural landscape of our minds as well as the physical world around us.

c33993798b1c.title: Soil functions
c33993798b1c.sentence: An attachment to home soils or a sense of place is a cultural attribute developed mores strongly in certain people.

c581feb32594.title: Soil functions
c581feb32594.sentence: Soil also act as an earth cover that protects and preserve the physical artifacts of the past that can allow us to better understand cultural heritage.

ede6c6ef3e7d.title: Soil functions
ede6c6ef3e7d.sentence: Moreover, soil has been an important indication to where people settle as they are an essential resource for human productivity.

6c3aa3784b8a.title: Soil functions
6c3aa3784b8a.sentence: Approximately 50% of the people on the planet live in houses constructed from soil.

599bd34d10dd.title: Soil functions
599bd34d10dd.sentence: Additionally, since these structures rest on the soil, factors such as its bearing strength, compressibility, stability, and shear strength all need to be considered.

7dda45d7fb03.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.01%3A_Introduction
7dda45d7fb03.sentence: Soils govern whether rainfall runs off the field or enters the ground and eventually helps recharge underground aquifers.

b1abce41ad1c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.01%3A_Introduction
b1abce41ad1c.sentence: For example, they help to purify wastes flowing from the septic system drain fields in your backyard.

fc555ee461ca.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.01%3A_Introduction
fc555ee461ca.sentence: Soils also provide habitats for a diverse group of organisms, many of which are very important, such as those bacteria that produce antibiotics and fungi that help plants obtain nutrients and water and improve soil structure.

b01b1ef4e64e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.01%3A_Introduction
b01b1ef4e64e.sentence: Soil organic matter stores a huge amount of atmospheric carbon.

19fd2a90c24d.title: Soil health
19fd2a90c24d.sentence: Soil health is a state of a soil meeting its range of ecosystem functions as appropriate to its environment.

7adc1a933763.title: Soil health
7adc1a933763.sentence: In more colloquial terms, the health of soil arises from favorable interactions of all soil components (living and non-living) that belong together, as in microbiota, plants and animals.

fb032c2f61c4.title: Soil health
fb032c2f61c4.sentence: Soil health depends on soil biodiversity (with a robust soil biota), and it can be improved via soil management, especially by care to keep protective living covers on the soil and by natural (carbon-containing) soil amendments.

466878b62d20.title: Soil health
466878b62d20.sentence: Inorganic fertilizers do not necessarily damage soil health if they are not used in excess, and if they bring about a general improvement of overall plant growth which contributes more carbon-containing residues to the soil.

b5a9ebbc4f11.title: Soil health
b5a9ebbc4f11.sentence: The term soil health is used to describe the state of a soil in:

abe28b96d007.title: Soil health
abe28b96d007.sentence: - Sustaining plant and animal productivity (agronomic focus);

8bc472d76b57.title: Soil health
8bc472d76b57.sentence: - Maintaining or enhancing water and air quality (environmental/climate focus);

17edda54c967.title: Soil health
17edda54c967.sentence: The underlying principle in the use of the term "soil health" is that soil is not just an inert, lifeless growing medium, which modern intensive farming tends to represent, rather it is a living, dynamic and ever-so-subtly changing whole environment.

99c468bd33d5.title: Soil health
99c468bd33d5.sentence: It turns out that soils highly fertile from the point of view of crop productivity are also lively from a biological point of view.

7f008c228e6d.title: Soil health
7f008c228e6d.sentence: It is now commonly recognized that soil microbial biomass is large: in temperate grassland soil the bacterial and fungal biomass have been documented to be 1–2 t (2.0 long tons; 2.2 short tons)/hectare and 2–5 t (4.9 long tons; 5.5 short tons)/ha, respectively.

992d93f3e520.title: Soil health
992d93f3e520.sentence: Some microbiologists now believe that 80% of soil nutrient functions are essentially controlled by microbes.

631cbf77a9ca.title: Soil health
631cbf77a9ca.sentence: Using the human health analogy, a healthy soil can be categorized as one:

a36e0c4ca467.title: Soil health
a36e0c4ca467.sentence: - In a state of composite well-being in terms of biological, chemical and physical properties;

01d06d172478.title: Soil health
