01d06d172478.sentence: - Not diseased or infirmed (i.e. not degraded, nor degrading), nor causing negative off-site impacts;

37f306800ac8.title: Soil health
37f306800ac8.sentence: - With each of its qualities cooperatively functioning such that the soil reaches its full potential and resists degradation;

3931aa5d04de.title: Soil health
3931aa5d04de.sentence: - Providing a full range of functions (especially nutrient, carbon and water cycling) and in such a way that it maintains this capacity into the future.

66f223a4d219.title: Soil quality
66f223a4d219.sentence: Soil quality refers to the condition of soil based on its capacity to perform ecosystem services that meet the needs of human and non-human life.

03fed520bde7.title: Soil quality
03fed520bde7.sentence: Soil quality reflects how well a soil performs the functions of maintaining biodiversity and productivity, partitioning water and solute flow, filtering and buffering, nutrient cycling, and providing support for plants and other structures.

9c82a2b6fc5b.title: Soil quality
9c82a2b6fc5b.sentence: Unlike water or air, for which established standards have been set, soil quality is difficult to define or quantify.

c71dbbd5e1f4.title: Soil quality
c71dbbd5e1f4.sentence: Soil management has a major impact on soil quality.

0aff7db720f5.title: Cover crop
0aff7db720f5.sentence: Cover crops can also improve soil quality by increasing soil organic matter levels through the input of cover crop biomass over time.

8c0028b57d05.title: Agricultural soil science
8c0028b57d05.section: Kinds of soil and their variables
8c0028b57d05.sentence: - Biota and soil biota: Soil organisms interact with the soil and contribute to its quality in innumerable ways.

d06b5e01a19a.title: Agricultural soil science
d06b5e01a19a.section: Kinds of soil and their variables
d06b5e01a19a.sentence: Sometimes the nature of the interaction may be unclear, in particular in the frame of global changes, yet a rule is becoming evident: the amount and diversity of the biota is "proportional" to the quality of the soil.

efeee9276c8a.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
efeee9276c8a.sentence: It has enabled host plants to establish themselves on degraded soil and improve soil quality and health.

35c600003b8d.title: Pedology
35c600003b8d.sentence: - Complexity in soil genesis is more common than simplicity.

e035afc10c98.title: Pedology
e035afc10c98.sentence: - Five major, external factors of formation (climate, organisms, relief, parent material and time), and several smaller, less identifiable ones, drive pedogenic processes and create soil patterns.

a0f70bfd0ebb.title: Pedology
a0f70bfd0ebb.sentence: - Contemporary soils carry imprints of pedogenic processes that were active in the past, although in many cases these imprints are difficult to observe or quantify.

d2301293bbe0.title: Pedology
d2301293bbe0.sentence: - Pedogenic (soil-forming) processes act to both create and destroy order (anisotropy) within soils; these processes can proceed simultaneously.

0f618d779a8e.title: Pedology
0f618d779a8e.sentence: The resulting soil profile reflects the balance of these processes, present and past.

b4bd66275703.title: Pedology
b4bd66275703.sentence: - The geological Principle of Uniformitarianism applies to soils, i.e., pedogenic processes active in soils today have been operating for long periods of time, back to the time of appearance of organisms on the land surface.

7dbe96d8d1d3.title: Pedology
7dbe96d8d1d3.sentence: These processes do, however, have varying degrees of expression and intensity over space and time.

89911cd78d97.title: Pedology
89911cd78d97.sentence: - There are very few old soils (in a geological sense) because they can be destroyed or buried by geological events, or modified by shifts in climate by virtue of their vulnerable position at the surface of the earth.

2e9f79089c1b.title: Pedology
2e9f79089c1b.sentence: Little of the soil continuum dates back beyond the Tertiary period and most soils and land surfaces are no older than the Pleistocene Epoch.

0b07e1f29181.title: Pedology
0b07e1f29181.sentence: However, preserved/lithified soils (paleosols) are an almost ubiquitous feature in terrestrial (land-based) environments throughout most of geologic time.

effca7d83427.title: Pedology
effca7d83427.sentence: - Soils are natural clay factories (clay includes both clay mineral structures and particles less than 2 μm in diameter).

86431ae83e3c.title: Pedology
86431ae83e3c.sentence: Shales worldwide are, to a considerable extent, simply soil clays that have been formed in the pedosphere and eroded and deposited in the ocean basins, to become lithified at a later date.

7d8946e3a744.title: Pedology
7d8946e3a744.sentence: - Knowledge and understanding of the genesis of a soil is important in its classification and mapping.

7e3ae6b95017.title: Pedology
7e3ae6b95017.sentence: - Soil classification systems cannot be based entirely on perceptions of genesis, however, because genetic processes are seldom observed and because pedogenic processes change over time.

d64d67538293.title: Pedology
d64d67538293.sentence: - Knowledge of soil genesis is imperative and basic to soil use and management.

473b55f99c4b.title: Soil science
473b55f99c4b.sentence: A more traditional role for soil scientists has been to map soils.

4e9adfd912c5.title: Soil science
4e9adfd912c5.sentence: Yet the work specifics are very much dictated by the challenges facing our civilization's desire to sustain the land that supports it, and the distinctions between the sub-disciplines of soil science often blur in the process, with The Critical Zone concept providing a natural framework for cross-disciplinary fundamental research on soil, rock, air, water, and biotic resources at the Earth's surface.

25d95943a15e.title: Soil science
25d95943a15e.sentence: Almost every area in the United States now has a published soil survey, including interpretive tables on how soil properties support or limit activities and uses.

461977e57f56.title: Soil science
461977e57f56.sentence: The landscape functions that soil scientists are called upon to address in the field seem to fall roughly into six areas:

74c65d044c02.title: Soil science
74c65d044c02.sentence: - Identification and protection of environmentally critical areas

32e0e763a8eb.title: Soil science
32e0e763a8eb.sentence: - Unique soil situations that support valuable habitat and ecosystem diversity

4eece35a349e.title: Soil science
4eece35a349e.sentence: - Remediation and restoration of damaged lands

72f9d5156eba.title: Soil science
72f9d5156eba.sentence: - Radiometric dating: specifically a knowledge of local pedology is used to date prior activity at the site

5b5ba4230f0f.title: Soil science
5b5ba4230f0f.sentence: - Stratification (archeology) where soil formation processes and preservative qualities can inform the study of archaeological sites

c3f27f78e647.title: Soil science
c3f27f78e647.sentence: - Enhancing soil microbial capabilities in degrading contaminants (bioremediation).

6b44f87d6cb3.title: Soil science
6b44f87d6cb3.sentence: Many other classification schemes exist, including vernacular systems.

9b15cf986280.title: Soil science
9b15cf986280.sentence: The structure in vernacular systems is either nominal (giving unique names to soils or landscapes) or descriptive (naming soils by their characteristics such as red, hot, fat, or sandy).

a142fc590008.title: Soil science
a142fc590008.sentence: Soils are distinguished by obvious characteristics, such as physical appearance (e.g., color, texture, landscape position), performance (e.g., production capability, flooding), and accompanying vegetation.

c3df6dddd3a1.title: Soil science
c3df6dddd3a1.sentence: A vernacular distinction familiar to many is classifying texture as heavy (clayish) or light (sandy).

8444f1a8a53e.title: Soil science
8444f1a8a53e.sentence: Light soils with higher sand content and better structure take less effort to turn and cultivate than finer-textured soils but are more susceptible to erosion and thus to losses of production capacity.

18e6e8bda2ca.title: Soil science
18e6e8bda2ca.sentence: Light (sandy) soils do not necessarily weigh less than heavy (clay) soils on an air dry basis (i.e. they have similar bulk density), nor do they have more porosity, but they are less sensitive to cattle trampling because they are more resistant to compaction.

b6bb084a24a2.title: Soil science
b6bb084a24a2.sentence: The earliest known soil classification system comes from China, appearing in the book Yu Gong (5th century BCE), where the soil was divided into three categories and nine classes, depending on its color, texture and hydrology.

2dfa06c6ec72.title: Pedosphere
2dfa06c6ec72.sentence: The main inputs from the atmosphere are aeolian sedimentation, rainfall and gas diffusion.

9a9556ec03ff.title: Pedosphere
9a9556ec03ff.sentence: Eolian sedimentation includes anything that can be entrained by wind or that stays suspended in air and includes a wide variety of aerosol particles, biological particles like pollen, and dust particles.

689c83e93f04.title: Pedosphere
689c83e93f04.sentence: Nitrogen is the most abundant constituent in rain (after water), as water vapor utilizes aerosol particles to nucleate rain droplets.

2581663c7061.title: Pedosphere
2581663c7061.sentence: Because plant roots and soil microbes release CO2 to the soil, the concentration of bicarbonate (HCO− 3) in soil waters is much greater than that in equilibrium with the atmosphere, the high concentration of CO2 and the occurrence of metals in soil solutions results in lower pH levels in the soil.

a9bbde638fcf.title: Pedosphere
a9bbde638fcf.sentence: Gases that escape from the pedosphere to the atmosphere include the gaseous byproducts of carbonate dissolution, decomposition, redox reactions and microbial photosynthesis.

28b73d567510.title: Pedosphere
28b73d567510.sentence: Soil is well developed in the forest as suggested by the thick humus layers, rich diversity of large trees and animals that live there.

a5de7cba9a28.title: Pedosphere
a5de7cba9a28.sentence: In forests, precipitation exceeds evapotranspiration which results in an excess of water that percolates downward through the soil layers.

36338564ca5b.title: Pedosphere
36338564ca5b.sentence: Slow rates of decomposition leads to large amounts of fulvic acid, greatly enhancing chemical weathering.

e549d145e026.title: Pedosphere
e549d145e026.sentence: The downward percolation, in conjunction with chemical weathering leaches Mg, Fe, and aluminium (Al) from the soil and transports them downward, a process known as podzolization.

35b92cd68e48.title: Pedosphere
35b92cd68e48.sentence: This process leads to marked contrasts in the appearance and chemistry of the soil layers.

bd677b478826.title: Pedosphere
bd677b478826.sentence: Forest soils can form a thick soil carbon sponge.

e150c2a5f950.title: Pedosphere
e150c2a5f950.sentence: Precipitation in grasslands is equal to or less than evapotranspiration and causes soil development to operate in relative drought.

f1c602513f62.title: Pedosphere
f1c602513f62.sentence: Deserts behave similarly to grasslands but operate in constant drought as precipitation is less than evapotranspiration.

083900707cfb.title: Pedosphere
083900707cfb.sentence: Leaching and migration of weathering products is therefore decreased.

4a652295ffd6.title: Pedosphere
4a652295ffd6.sentence: Low amounts of precipitation and high levels of evapotranspiration limit the downward percolation of water and organic acids, reducing chemical weathering and soil development.

381a4545e364.title: Pedosphere
381a4545e364.sentence: Large amounts of evaporation cause a buildup of calcium (Ca), and other large cations flocculate clay minerals and fulvic acids in the upper soil profile.

6050ea622721.title: Pedosphere
6050ea622721.sentence: When leaching is decreased, the calcium precipitates as calcite (CaCO3) in the lower soil levels, a layer known as caliche.

46b2920018b7.title: Pedosphere
46b2920018b7.sentence: Chemical weathering proceeds more slowly than in grasslands and beneath the caliche layer may be a layer of gypsum and halite.

a7bf085c9a52.title: Pedosphere
a7bf085c9a52.sentence: The depth to the maximum concentration of clay increases in areas of increased precipitation and leaching.

5f6805e6f041.title: Pedosphere
5f6805e6f041.sentence: Inputs from the biosphere may begin with lichen and other microorganisms that secrete oxalic acid.

e13d0da8e02d.title: Pedosphere
e13d0da8e02d.sentence: > The initial conversion of rock into soil is carried on by the pioneer lichens and their successors, the mosses, in which the hair-like rhizoids assume the role of roots in breaking down the surface into fine dust.

5361921ffb45.title: Pedosphere
5361921ffb45.sentence: These microorganisms, associated with the lichen community or independently inhabiting rocks, include blue-green algae, green algae, various fungi, and numerous bacteria.

961a4d42ffed.title: Pedosphere
961a4d42ffed.sentence: Lichen has long been viewed as the pioneers of soil development as the following 1997 Isozaki statement suggests:

efece79c9c33.title: Pedosphere
efece79c9c33.sentence: However, lichens are not necessarily the only pioneering organisms nor the earliest form of soil formation as it has been documented that seed-bearing plants may occupy an area and colonize quicker than lichen.

47e243238faa.title: Pedosphere
47e243238faa.sentence: Nonetheless, lichen can certainly withstand harsher conditions than most vascular plants, and although they have slower colonization rates, they do form the dominant group in alpine regions.

7a73fd6af36c.title: Pedosphere
7a73fd6af36c.sentence: Organic acids released from plant roots include acetic acid and citric acid.

8592db6442e0.title: Pedosphere
8592db6442e0.sentence: During the decay of organic matter phenolic acids are released from plant matter and humic acid and fulvic acid are released by soil microbes.

0065c488fdd3.title: Pedosphere
0065c488fdd3.sentence: These organic acids speed up chemical weathering by combining with some of the weathering products in a process known as chelation.

f13bf889e7af.title: Pedosphere
f13bf889e7af.sentence: As the soil column develops further into thicker accumulations, larger animals come to inhabit the soil and continue to alter the chemical evolution of their respective niche.

c1687b1b9d81.title: Pedosphere
c1687b1b9d81.sentence: Earthworms aerate the soil and convert large amounts of organic matter into rich humus, improving soil fertility.

8d7bc8faf675.title: Pedosphere
8d7bc8faf675.sentence: Small burrowing mammals store food, grow young and may hibernate in the pedosphere altering the course of soil evolution.

337d628f1214.title: Pedosphere
337d628f1214.sentence: Large mammalian herbivores above ground transport nutrients in form of nitrogen-rich waste and phosphorus-rich antlers, while predators leave phosphorus-rich piles of bones on the soil surface, leading to localized enrichment of the soil.

ed2580fe7dc8.title: Pedosphere
ed2580fe7dc8.sentence: Tropical forests receive more insolation and rainfall over longer growing seasons than any other environment on earth.

869540e69d0a.title: Pedosphere
869540e69d0a.sentence: With these elevated temperatures, insolation and rainfall, biomass is extremely productive leading to the production of as much as 800 grams of carbon per square meter per year (8 tons of C/hectare/year).

db1f8fc14aac.title: Pedosphere
db1f8fc14aac.sentence: Higher temperatures and larger amounts of water contribute to higher rates of chemical weathering.

d68e18f44064.title: Pedosphere
d68e18f44064.sentence: Increased rates of decomposition cause smaller amounts of fulvic acid to percolate and leach metals from the zone of active weathering.

ed4af707de12.title: Pedosphere
ed4af707de12.sentence: Thus, in stark contrast to soil in temperate forests, tropical forests have little to no podzolization and therefore do not have marked visual and chemical contrasts with the soil layers.

d3efce54c90b.title: Pedosphere
d3efce54c90b.sentence: Instead, the mobile metals Mg, Fe and Al are precipitated as oxide minerals giving the soil a rusty red color.

c7bc2c06ab69.title: Edaphology
c7bc2c06ab69.sentence: Industrialization has impacted the way that soil interacts with plants in various ways.

ded6f481df7a.title: Edaphology
ded6f481df7a.sentence: Increased mechanical production has led to higher amount of heavy metals within soils.

0b30c7024485.title: Edaphology
0b30c7024485.sentence: These heavy metals have also been found in crops.

462a952d00a1.title: Edaphology
462a952d00a1.sentence: While, the increased use of synthetic fertilizer and pesticides has decreased the nutrient availability of soils.

80bb79638d58.title: Edaphology
80bb79638d58.sentence: Monocropping techniques are efficient for harvesting and business strategies but lead to a decrease in biodiversity.

a187d3449413.title: Edaphology
a187d3449413.sentence: Decreased biodiversity is shown to decrease the nutrients available in soils.

56bacd8d337c.title: Edaphology
56bacd8d337c.sentence: Furthermore, monocropping leads to an increased dependency on chemical fertilizer.

efe7c367bcc4.title: Edaphology
efe7c367bcc4.sentence: While intensive tilling disturbs the community of microorganism that live with in soil.

479ab430a167.title: Edaphology
479ab430a167.sentence: These microorganisms help maintain soil moisture and air circulation which are critical to plant growth.

f7b3eb23c08e.title: Edaphology
f7b3eb23c08e.sentence: Jan Baptist van Helmont (1577—1644) performed a famous experiment, growing a willow tree in a pot of soil and supplying only rainwater for five years.

87203705f134.title: Edaphology
87203705f134.sentence: The weight gained by the tree exceeded the weight loss of the soil.

e771443fb720.title: Edaphology
e771443fb720.sentence: He concluded that the willow was made of water.

4bdac0c41351.title: Edaphology
4bdac0c41351.sentence: Although only partly correct, his experiment reignited interest in edaphology.

dccf37ae646f.title: Biological soil crust
dccf37ae646f.sentence: Biological soil crusts are most often composed of fungi, lichens, cyanobacteria, bryophytes, and algae in varying proportions.

e3859472791f.title: Biological soil crust
e3859472791f.sentence: Biological soil crusts are formed in open spaces between vascular plants.

6d2a6e55892a.title: Biological soil crust
6d2a6e55892a.sentence: Biological soil crusts cover about 12% of the earth's landmass.

d7e2c57e7f31.title: Biological soil crust
d7e2c57e7f31.sentence: The species composition and physical appearance of biological soil crusts vary depending on the climate, soil, and disturbance conditions.

564bcdddafb7.title: Biological soil crust
564bcdddafb7.section: Ecology > Ecosystem function and services > Biogeochemical cycling > Nitrogen cycling
564bcdddafb7.sentence: Biological soil crust contributions to the nitrogen cycle varies by crust composition because only cyanobacteria and cyanolichens fix nitrogen.

92715d9be290.title: Biological soil crust
92715d9be290.section: Ecology > Ecosystem function and services > Biogeochemical cycling > Carbon cycling
92715d9be290.sentence: Biological soil crusts contribute to the carbon cycle through respiration and photosynthesis of crust microorganisms which are active only when wet.

eae16fccc1b6.title: Biological soil crust
eae16fccc1b6.section: Ecology > Ecosystem function and services > Geophysical and geomorphological properties > Albedo
eae16fccc1b6.sentence: The darkened surfaces of biological soil crusts decreases soil albedo (a measure of the amount of light reflected off of the surface) compared to nearby soils, which increases the energy absorbed by the soil surface.

504301a3ea47.title: Biological soil crust
504301a3ea47.section: Ecology > Ecosystem function and services > Geophysical and geomorphological properties > Dust-trapping
504301a3ea47.sentence: The increased surface roughness associated with biological soil crusts increase the capture of dust.

3520035fe9a1.title: Biological soil crust
3520035fe9a1.section: Human impacts and management > Conservation and management
3520035fe9a1.sentence: Removing stressors such as grazing or protecting them from disturbance are the easiest ways to maintain and improve biological soil crusts.

b430403020f9.title: Earth's critical zone
b430403020f9.sentence: Earth's critical zone is the “heterogeneous, near surface environment in which complex interactions involving rock, soil, water, air, and living organisms regulate the natural habitat and determine the availability of life-sustaining resources” (National Research Council, 2001).

2a6307fe8ced.title: Earth's critical zone
2a6307fe8ced.sentence: The Critical Zone, surface and near-surface environment, sustains nearly all terrestrial life.

7bd135c6348e.title: Earth's critical zone
7bd135c6348e.sentence: The critical zone is an interdisciplinary field of research exploring the interactions among the land surface, vegetation, and water bodies, and extends through the pedosphere, unsaturated vadose zone, and saturated groundwater zone.

8eee88ba037d.title: Earth's critical zone
8eee88ba037d.sentence: Critical Zone science is the integration of Earth surface processes (such as landscape evolution, weathering, hydrology, geochemistry, and ecology) at multiple spatial and temporal scales and across anthropogenic gradients.

4f0a41f2de02.title: Earth's critical zone
4f0a41f2de02.sentence: These processes impact mass and energy exchange necessary for biomass productivity, chemical cycling, and water storage.

2ab8430dc0e3.title: Earth's critical zone
2ab8430dc0e3.sentence: Dimitrios Tsakalotos first introduced the term critical zone in chemistry literature in 1909 to describe the binary mixture of two fluids, but has since been adopted to refer to the "connection of vegetation to soil and weathered materials" by Gail Ashley in 1998.

ba5120431693.title: Earth's critical zone
ba5120431693.sentence: The critical zone is studied at Critical Zone Observatories, where multiple scientific communities study various aspects of the critical zone that can lead to synthesized understanding of complex systems.

6e1bfea1a129.title: Earth's critical zone
6e1bfea1a129.sentence: On July 24, 2006 NSF posted a solicitation for proposals for Critical Zone Observatories (CZO) within the Division of Earth Sciences.

8377367797d8.title: Soil biomantle
8377367797d8.sentence: In practice and theory, the critical zone essentially equates to the pedosphere, whereas the 'biomantle' deals with the uppermost critical zone, or pedosphere, encompassing its epidermal layer (where most biota live).

7e6074e2ef18.title: Soil
7e6074e2ef18.sentence: The mixture of water and dissolved or suspended materials that occupy the soil pore space is called the soil solution.

d84032a4f405.title: Soil
d84032a4f405.sentence: Since soil water is never pure water, but contains hundreds of dissolved organic and mineral substances, it may be more accurately called the soil solution.

8830469bfc39.title: Soil
8830469bfc39.sentence: Water is a critical agent in soil development due to its involvement in the dissolution, precipitation, erosion, transport, and deposition of the materials of which a soil is composed.

0b4bfae5d212.title: Soil
0b4bfae5d212.sentence: Water is central to the dissolution, precipitation and leaching of minerals from the soil profile.

0ec3106c369f.title: Soil
0ec3106c369f.sentence: These bound nutrients interact with soil water to buffer the soil solution composition (attenuate changes in the soil solution) as soils wet up or dry out, as plants take up nutrients, as salts are leached, or as acids or alkalis are added.

d49afdc83303.title: Soil
d49afdc83303.sentence: Plant nutrient availability is affected by soil pH, which is a measure of the hydrogen ion activity in the soil solution.

1775f1940834.title: Soil science
1775f1940834.sentence: A corollary concept is that soil without a living component is simply a part of Earth's outer layer, a regolith.

bcb9f59832ef.title: Soil
bcb9f59832ef.sentence: However, more recent definitions of soil embrace soils without any organic matter, such as those regoliths that formed on Mars and analogous conditions in planet Earth deserts.

acb176818ed9.title: Soil
acb176818ed9.sentence: Soil is said to be formed when organic matter has accumulated and colloids are washed downward, leaving deposits of clay, humus, iron oxide, carbonate, and gypsum, producing a distinct layer called the B horizon.

d558b24f8fa1.title: Soil
d558b24f8fa1.sentence: This is a somewhat arbitrary definition as mixtures of sand, silt, clay and humus will support biological and agricultural activity before that time.

0ade4a055091.title: Soil science
0ade4a055091.sentence: The term is popularly applied to the material on the surface of the Earth's moon and Mars, a usage acceptable within only a portion of the scientific community.

3163052efc8b.title: Soil
3163052efc8b.sentence: In engineering terms, soil is included in the broader concept of regolith, which also includes other loose material that lies above the bedrock, as can be found on the Moon and other celestial objects.

c66b570b388a.title: Mineral
c66b570b388a.sentence: In geology and mineralogy, a mineral or mineral species is, broadly speaking, a solid substance with a fairly well-defined chemical composition and a specific crystal structure that occurs naturally in pure form.

745ebb23b330.title: Mineral
745ebb23b330.sentence: The concept of mineral is distinct from rock, which is any bulk solid geologic material that is relatively homogeneous at a large enough scale.

978ca2793a4c.title: Mineral
978ca2793a4c.sentence: A rock may consist of one type of mineral or may be an aggregate of two or more different types of minerals, spacially segregated into distinct phases.

7a7970565bfb.title: Mineral
7a7970565bfb.sentence: Some natural solid substances without a definite crystalline structure, such as opal or obsidian, are more properly called mineraloids.

d28b672f308c.title: Mineral
d28b672f308c.sentence: If a chemical compound occurs naturally with different crystal structures, each structure is considered a different mineral species.

9281e2f7ac94.title: Mineral
9281e2f7ac94.sentence: Thus, for example, quartz and stishovite are two different minerals consisting of the same compound, silicon dioxide.

26674c7683d7.title: Mineral
26674c7683d7.sentence: The International Mineralogical Association (IMA) is the generally recognized standard body for the definition and nomenclature of mineral species.

1d3558563ccd.title: Mineral
1d3558563ccd.sentence: As of August 2026, the IMA recognizes 6,228 official mineral species.

4599dce9c58a.title: Mineral
4599dce9c58a.sentence: - It must be a naturally occurring substance formed by natural geological processes, on Earth or other extraterrestrial bodies.

5d9f701e450b.title: Mineral
5d9f701e450b.sentence: This excludes compounds directly and exclusively generated by human activities (anthropogenic) or in living beings (biogenic), such as tungsten carbide, urinary calculi, calcium oxalate crystals in plant tissues, and seashells.

4570662d5083.title: Mineral
4570662d5083.sentence: Silicate minerals comprise approximately 90% of the Earth's crust.

743d0f4f7912.title: Mineral
743d0f4f7912.sentence: Minerals are classified by key chemical constituents; the two dominant systems are the Dana classification and the Strunz classification.

cf2bda13d49a.title: Earth structure
cf2bda13d49a.sentence: Both sand and silt are mostly inert rock particles, including quartz, calcite, feldspar and mica.

4a1e39486475.title: Weathering
4a1e39486475.sentence: Weathering is the deterioration of rocks, soils and minerals (as well as wood and artificial materials) through contact with water, atmospheric gases, sunlight, and biological organisms.

802231efdc41.title: Weathering
802231efdc41.sentence: It occurs in situ (on-site, with little or no movement), and so is distinct from erosion, which involves the transport of rocks and minerals by agents such as water, ice, snow, wind, waves and gravity.

164b7a512241.title: Weathering
164b7a512241.sentence: Weathering processes are either physical or chemical.

afcf97e609b0.title: Weathering
afcf97e609b0.sentence: The former involves the breakdown of rocks and soils through such mechanical effects as heat, water, ice, and wind.

eab3b1ca4eb6.title: Weathering
eab3b1ca4eb6.sentence: The latter covers reactions to water, atmospheric gases and biologically produced chemicals with rocks and soils.

5f067b9e729a.title: Weathering
5f067b9e729a.sentence: Water is the principal agent behind both kinds, though atmospheric oxygen and carbon dioxide and the activities of biological organisms are also important.

d808a03f0f40.title: Weathering
d808a03f0f40.sentence: The materials left after the rock breaks down combine with organic material to create soil.

a3797f08d1cb.title: Weathering
a3797f08d1cb.sentence: Furthermore, chemical and physical weathering often go hand in hand.

ccb92b72fadd.title: Weathering
ccb92b72fadd.sentence: For example, cracks extended by physical weathering will increase the surface area exposed to chemical action, thus amplifying the rate of disintegration.

b92297ac5675.title: Weathering
b92297ac5675.sentence: Weathering is a crucial part of the rock cycle; sedimentary rock, the product of weathered rock, covers 66% of the Earth's continents and much of the ocean floor.

0775da434515.title: Weathering
0775da434515.sentence: Chemical weathering takes place when water, oxygen, carbon dioxide, and other chemical substances react with rock to change its composition.

8519e2833cbe.title: Weathering
8519e2833cbe.sentence: Most rock forms at elevated temperature and pressure, and the minerals making up the rock are often chemically unstable in the relatively cool, wet, and oxidizing conditions typical of the Earth's surface.

7041fb0b7828.title: Weathering
7041fb0b7828.sentence: These reactions convert some of the original primary minerals in the rock to secondary minerals, remove other substances as solutes, and leave the most stable minerals as a chemically unchanged resistate.

75d46dd09e22.title: Weathering
75d46dd09e22.sentence: In effect, chemical weathering changes the original set of minerals in the rock into a new set of minerals that is in closer equilibrium with surface conditions.

a144ad394de6.title: Weathering
a144ad394de6.sentence: True equilibrium is rarely reached, because weathering is a slow process, and leaching carries away solutes produced by weathering reactions before they can accumulate to equilibrium levels.

cee15bb5ba41.title: Weathering
cee15bb5ba41.sentence: Water is the principal agent of chemical weathering, converting many primary minerals to clay minerals or hydrated oxides via reactions collectively described as hydrolysis.

55855f1d3622.title: Weathering
55855f1d3622.sentence: Oxygen is also important, acting to oxidize many minerals, as is carbon dioxide, whose weathering reactions are described as carbonation.

f7d62cc6d389.title: Weathering
f7d62cc6d389.sentence: It is usually much less important than chemical weathering, but can be significant in subarctic or alpine environments.

340a734cbeb3.title: Weathering
340a734cbeb3.sentence: The process of mountain block uplift is important in exposing new rock strata to the atmosphere and moisture, enabling important chemical weathering to occur; significant release occurs of Ca2+ and other ions into surface waters.

7daf55ca76f7.title: Weathering
7daf55ca76f7.sentence: Mineral weathering can also be initiated or accelerated by soil microorganisms.

361d8b9fcbc8.title: Weathering
361d8b9fcbc8.sentence: Biological chemical weathering is also called biological weathering.

89bfbcd3865a.title: Weathering
89bfbcd3865a.sentence: Living organisms may contribute to mechanical weathering, as well as chemical weathering (see § Biological weathering below).

31121e70d1fb.title: Weathering
31121e70d1fb.sentence: Soil organisms make up about 10 mg/cm3 of typical soils, and laboratory experiments have demonstrated that albite and muscovite weather twice as fast in live versus sterile soil.

ec1e10600a04.title: Weathering
ec1e10600a04.sentence: Lichens on rocks are among the most effective biological agents of chemical weathering.

75fb52be3e93.title: Weathering
75fb52be3e93.sentence: For example, an experimental study on hornblende granite in New Jersey, US, demonstrated a 3x – 4x increase in weathering rate under lichen covered surfaces compared to recently exposed bare rock surfaces.

05e9eccfaa2f.title: Weathering
05e9eccfaa2f.sentence: The most common forms of biological weathering result from the release of chelating compounds (such as certain organic acids and siderophores) and of carbon dioxide and organic acids by plants.

668dc2e0f17f.title: Weathering
668dc2e0f17f.sentence: Roots can build up the carbon dioxide level to 30% of all soil gases, aided by adsorption of CO2 on clay minerals and the very slow diffusion rate of CO2 out of the soil.

554166f3f2fc.title: Weathering
554166f3f2fc.sentence: Chelating compounds, mostly low molecular weight organic acids, are capable of removing metal ions from bare rock surfaces, with aluminium and silicon being particularly susceptible.

616359d41bfc.title: Weathering
616359d41bfc.sentence: The accumulation of chelating compounds can easily affect surrounding rocks and soils, and may lead to podsolisation of soils.

5b82ba37b140.title: Weathering
5b82ba37b140.sentence: The symbiotic mycorrhizal fungi associated with tree root systems can release inorganic nutrients from minerals such as apatite or biotite and transfer these nutrients to the trees, thus contributing to tree nutrition.

5d2d362cfdf0.title: Weathering
5d2d362cfdf0.sentence: A large range of bacterial strains or communities from diverse genera have been reported to be able to colonize mineral surfaces or to weather minerals, and for some of them a plant growth promoting effect has been demonstrated.

5c6088d3a61d.title: Weathering
5c6088d3a61d.sentence: On a larger scale, seedlings sprouting in a crevice and plant roots exert physical pressure as well as providing a pathway for water and chemical infiltration.

52e7ffadb425.title: Weathering
52e7ffadb425.sentence: Lichens have been observed to pry mineral grains loose from bare shale with their hyphae (rootlike attachment structures), a process described as plucking, and to pull the fragments into their body, where the fragments then undergo a process of chemical weathering not unlike digestion.

3b3a63ecbe93.title: Weathering
3b3a63ecbe93.sentence: Dissolution (also called simple solution or congruent dissolution) is the process in which a mineral dissolves completely without producing any new solid substance.

8220a5530005.title: Weathering
8220a5530005.sentence: Rainwater easily dissolves soluble minerals, such as halite or gypsum, but can also dissolve highly resistant minerals such as quartz, given sufficient time.

a216e122cafe.title: Weathering
a216e122cafe.sentence: The dissolved quartz takes the form of silicic acid.

fd93e88c2913.title: Weathering
fd93e88c2913.sentence: A particularly important form of dissolution is carbonate dissolution, in which atmospheric carbon dioxide enhances solution weathering.

424558facc9e.title: Weathering
424558facc9e.sentence: It takes place when rainwater combines with carbon dioxide to form carbonic acid, a weak acid, which dissolves calcium carbonate (limestone) and forms soluble calcium bicarbonate.

1903edba79c9.title: Weathering
1903edba79c9.sentence: Despite a slower reaction kinetics, this process is thermodynamically favored at low temperature, because colder water holds more dissolved carbon dioxide gas (due to the retrograde solubility of gases).

bad4225a2920.title: Weathering
bad4225a2920.sentence: Carbonate dissolution is therefore an important feature of glacial weathering.

b58a86036328.title: Weathering
b58a86036328.sentence: In unpolluted environments, the pH of rainwater due to dissolved carbon dioxide is around 5.6.

9d8e06b87974.title: Weathering
9d8e06b87974.sentence: Acid rain occurs when gases such as sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides are present in the atmosphere.

2855b7ede897.title: Weathering
2855b7ede897.sentence: These oxides react in the rain water to produce stronger acids and can lower the pH to 4.5 or even 3.0.

6218e5b39102.title: Weathering
6218e5b39102.sentence: Within the weathering environment, chemical oxidation of a variety of metals occurs.

759688bddf66.title: Weathering
759688bddf66.sentence: The most commonly observed is the oxidation of Fe2+ (iron) by oxygen and water to form Fe3+ oxides and hydroxides such as goethite, limonite, and hematite.

6df8deebb518.title: Weathering
6df8deebb518.sentence: This gives the affected rocks a reddish-brown coloration on the surface which crumbles easily and weakens the rock.

5fe23dc19630.title: Weathering
5fe23dc19630.sentence: Many other metallic ores and minerals oxidize and hydrate to produce colored deposits, as does sulfur during the weathering of sulfide minerals such as chalcopyrites or CuFeS2 oxidizing to copper hydroxide and iron oxides.

df9559aa41a6.title: Soil pH
df9559aa41a6.section: Factors affecting soil pH > Sources of acidity
df9559aa41a6.sentence: - Oxidative weathering: Oxidation of some primary minerals, especially sulfides and those containing Fe2+, generate acidity.

70f16019b392.title: Weathering
70f16019b392.sentence: Physical weathering, also called mechanical weathering or disaggregation, is the class of processes that causes the disintegration of rocks without chemical change.

cbbe70f105ff.title: Weathering
cbbe70f105ff.sentence: Physical weathering involves the breakdown of rocks into smaller fragments through processes such as expansion and contraction, mainly due to temperature changes.

e6c53cae8e45.title: Weathering
e6c53cae8e45.sentence: Two types of physical breakdown are freeze-thaw weathering and thermal fracturing.

a4ccdc6b54c2.title: Weathering
a4ccdc6b54c2.sentence: Pressure release can also cause weathering without temperature change.

519a190f0d5f.title: Weathering
519a190f0d5f.sentence: Frost weathering is the most important form of physical weathering.

747b9d9cf1cb.title: Weathering
747b9d9cf1cb.sentence: Next in importance is wedging by plant roots, which sometimes enter cracks in rocks and pry them apart.

4d61312ab288.title: Weathering
4d61312ab288.sentence: The burrowing of worms or other animals may also help disintegrate rock, as can "plucking" by lichens.

375967c8cd4d.title: Soil organic matter
375967c8cd4d.sentence: The water content of most vegetal detritus ranges from 60% to 90%.

6e520e93243c.title: Soil organic matter
6e520e93243c.sentence: Organic compounds in vegetal detritus include:

ac8f6b0de4ae.title: Soil organic matter
ac8f6b0de4ae.sentence: The dry matter consists mainly of carbon, oxygen, and hydrogen.

38702fe47345.title: Soil organic matter
38702fe47345.sentence: Although these three elements make up about 92% of the dry weight of the organic matter in the soil, other elements present are essential for the nutrition of plants, including nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, sulfur, calcium, magnesium, and many micronutrients.

14945866f30f.title: Soil organic matter
14945866f30f.sentence: - Carbohydrates that are composed of carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen and range in complexity from relatively simple sugars to large molecules of cellulose.

438d345912a3.title: Soil organic matter
438d345912a3.sentence: - Fats that are composed of glycerids of fatty acids, like butyric, stearic, and oleic.

06795385cdf5.title: Soil organic matter
06795385cdf5.sentence: - Lignins that are complex compounds from the older wood parts.

716a91de6a4c.title: Soil organic matter
716a91de6a4c.sentence: - Proteins that are composed of nitrogen, carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen; and small amounts of sulfur, iron, and phosphorus.

85364fcfb316.title: Soil organic matter
85364fcfb316.sentence: - Charcoal that is elemental carbon derived from incomplete combustion of organic matter.

ef96972a14ad.title: Soil organic matter
ef96972a14ad.sentence: It is highly resistant to decomposition.

1385def36465.title: Soil organic matter
1385def36465.sentence: Within the soil profile, soil organic matter is distributed differently between the surface layer (~20 cm depth) and the deeper, mineral soil (below 20–30 cm).

f7d0d4903836.title: Soil organic matter
f7d0d4903836.sentence: About 70% of global soil organic carbon occurs at depths below 20 cm.

bba9949c0c6f.title: Soil organic matter
bba9949c0c6f.sentence: While the surface soil typically has higher concentrations of SOC, ranging from 29%-50% SOC depending on the ecosystem, the deeper soils actually accumulate more SOC due to their increased mass.

4bc521720d67.title: Soil organic matter
4bc521720d67.sentence: An increase in SOC age (found from radiocarbon dates) between surface soil and deeper soil demonstrates how deep soil may be accumulating and storing C for longer periods of time, also contributing to why there is more SOC stored at depth.

8d90000cdfe3.title: Soil organic matter
8d90000cdfe3.sentence: Additionally, the composition of the SOC changes with depth, with more biotic influences in the surface soil and more mineral influences dominating SOC at depth.

21914b399ea8.title: Soil organic matter
21914b399ea8.sentence: This domination of mineral influences at depth, and also higher amount of SOC found in deeper soil has to do with mineral associated organic matter (MAOM or MAOC for mineral associated organic C) which is typically thought to be resistant to microbial degradation in comparison to particulate organic matter (POM or POC for organic C).

2f1bbe93595b.title: Weathering
2f1bbe93595b.sentence: Frost weathering is the collective name for those forms of physical weathering that are caused by the formation of ice within rock outcrops.

2459c827036d.title: Frost weathering
2459c827036d.sentence: Frost weathering is a collective term for several mechanical weathering processes induced by stresses created by the freezing of water into ice.

fe5cf5118a07.title: Frost weathering
fe5cf5118a07.sentence: The term serves as an umbrella term for a variety of processes, such as frost shattering, frost wedging, and cryofracturing.

a0febfcfe28f.title: Weathering
a0febfcfe28f.sentence: When water freezes the volume increases by 9.2%.

1fe17664f08f.title: Weathering
1fe17664f08f.sentence: This expansion can theoretically generate pressures greater than 200 megapascals (29,000 psi), though a more realistic upper limit is 14 megapascals (2,000 psi).

7a98f2604b8d.title: Weathering
7a98f2604b8d.sentence: This is still much greater than the tensile strength of granite, which is about 4 megapascals (580 psi).

b277173f9b57.title: Weathering
b277173f9b57.sentence: It was long believed that the most important of these is frost wedging, which is the widening of cracks or joints in rocks resulting from the expansion of porewater when it freezes.

86f4f7a09f0b.title: Weathering
86f4f7a09f0b.sentence: Thus, frost wedging can only take place in small tortuous fractures.

a5f90acaf580.title: Weathering
a5f90acaf580.sentence: The rock must also be almost completely saturated with water, or the ice will simply expand into the air spaces in the unsaturated rock without generating much pressure.

26d1fc3430ce.title: Weathering
26d1fc3430ce.sentence: These conditions are unusual enough that frost wedging is unlikely to be the dominant process of frost weathering.

89581bf6646f.title: Weathering
89581bf6646f.sentence: A growing body of theoretical and experimental work suggests that ice segregation, whereby supercooled water migrates to lenses of ice forming within the rock, is the more important mechanism.

da4db1e9c8ae.title: Weathering
da4db1e9c8ae.sentence: This results in growth of the ice grain that puts considerable pressure on the surrounding rock, up to ten times greater than is likely with frost wedging.

78837b067d4f.title: Weathering
78837b067d4f.sentence: This mechanism is most effective in rock whose temperature averages just below the freezing point, −4 to −15 °C (25 to 5 °F).

57e7b0f368e2.title: Frost weathering
57e7b0f368e2.sentence: It is most pronounced in high-altitude and high-latitude areas and is especially associated with alpine, periglacial, subpolar maritime, and polar climates, but may occur anywhere at sub-freezing temperatures (between −3 and −8 °C (27 and 18 °F)) if water is present.

645ad22d1eae.title: Weathering
645ad22d1eae.sentence: Mineral hydration is a form of chemical weathering that involves the rigid attachment of water molecules or H+ and OH- ions to the atoms and molecules of a mineral.

b3ce1c0314d4.title: Mineral hydration
b3ce1c0314d4.sentence: In inorganic chemistry, mineral hydration is a reaction which adds water to the crystal structure of a mineral, usually creating a new mineral, commonly called a hydrate.

a2dc7702e864.title: Weathering
a2dc7702e864.sentence: For example, iron oxides are converted to iron hydroxides and the hydration of anhydrite forms gypsum.

b1715a3e0a3c.title: Weathering
b1715a3e0a3c.sentence: Bulk hydration of minerals is secondary in importance to dissolution, hydrolysis, and oxidation, but hydration of the crystal surface is the crucial first step in hydrolysis.

99d0290e11ad.title: Weathering
99d0290e11ad.sentence: Some of these molecules break into H+ that bonds to exposed anions (usually oxygen) and OH- that bonds to exposed cations.

11bbcb9f8d29.title: Weathering
11bbcb9f8d29.sentence: Additional protons replace cations exposed on the surface, freeing the cations as solutes.

4db2d7eadf7e.title: Weathering
4db2d7eadf7e.sentence: As cations are removed, silicon-oxygen and silicon-aluminium bonds become more susceptible to hydrolysis, freeing silicic acid and aluminium hydroxides to be leached away or to form clay minerals.

5b1d2a31b1c7.title: Mineral hydration
5b1d2a31b1c7.sentence: Mineral hydration is also a process in the regolith that results in conversion of silicate minerals into clay minerals.

eed01029f02e.title: Mineral hydration
eed01029f02e.sentence: The other is with the incorporation of water molecules directly into the crystalline structure of a new mineral, as with the hydration of feldspars to clay minerals, garnet to chlorite, or kyanite to muscovite.

d31392e237cb.title: Mineral hydration
d31392e237cb.sentence: Some mineral structures, for example, montmorillonite, are capable of including a variable amount of water without significant change to the mineral structure.

f016f91a7be4.title: Weathering
f016f91a7be4.sentence: Pressure release or unloading is a form of physical weathering seen when deeply buried rock is exhumed.

d21d7e37da19.title: Weathering
d21d7e37da19.sentence: Intrusive igneous rocks, such as granite, are formed deep beneath the Earth's surface.

dcc7f6db0600.title: Weathering
dcc7f6db0600.sentence: They are under tremendous pressure because of the overlying rock material.

0573481b2839.title: Weathering
0573481b2839.sentence: When erosion removes the overlying rock material, these intrusive rocks are exposed and the pressure on them is released.

bc09e815ffbe.title: Weathering
bc09e815ffbe.sentence: The outer parts of the rocks then tend to expand.

a3207a6e7df2.title: Weathering
a3207a6e7df2.sentence: The expansion sets up stresses which cause fractures parallel to the rock surface to form.

356ad09e6a41.title: Weathering
356ad09e6a41.sentence: Over time, sheets of rock break away from the exposed rocks along the fractures, a process known as exfoliation.

9ba62a21116e.title: Weathering
9ba62a21116e.sentence: Exfoliation due to pressure release is also known as sheeting.

7b721213800d.title: Weathering
7b721213800d.sentence: As with thermal weathering, pressure release is most effective in buttressed rock.

40132f9e623e.title: Weathering
40132f9e623e.sentence: Here the differential stress directed toward the unbuttressed surface can be as high as 35 megapascals (5,100 psi), easily enough to shatter rock.

6afb05b8226a.title: Weathering
6afb05b8226a.sentence: Retreat of an overlying glacier can also lead to exfoliation due to pressure release.

b737aa25ec2d.title: Weathering
b737aa25ec2d.sentence: Salt crystallization (also known as salt weathering, salt wedging or haloclasty) causes disintegration of rocks when saline solutions seep into cracks and joints in the rocks and evaporate, leaving salt crystals behind.

3a3e6c654938.title: Weathering
3a3e6c654938.sentence: As with ice segregation, the surfaces of the salt grains draw in additional dissolved salts through capillary action, causing the growth of salt lenses that exert high pressure on the surrounding rock.

63c99e1b2bdd.title: Weathering
63c99e1b2bdd.sentence: Sodium and magnesium salts are the most effective at producing salt weathering.

a2479ad437f8.title: Weathering
a2479ad437f8.sentence: Salt crystallization can take place wherever salts are concentrated by evaporation.

03db614f8b19.title: Weathering
03db614f8b19.sentence: It is thus most common in arid climates where strong heating causes strong evaporation and along coasts.

c5ed7f599e42.title: Weathering
c5ed7f599e42.sentence: Salt weathering can also take place when pyrite in sedimentary rock is chemically weathered to iron(II) sulfate and gypsum, which then crystallize as salt lenses.

772c06bc077a.title: Weathering
772c06bc077a.sentence: Thermal stress weathering results from the expansion and contraction of rock due to temperature changes.

6efd484c8314.title: Weathering
6efd484c8314.sentence: Thermal stress weathering comprises two main types, thermal shock and thermal fatigue.

494234e1e8e9.title: Weathering
494234e1e8e9.sentence: Thermal shock takes place when the stresses are so great that the rock cracks immediately, but this is uncommon.

ade0f313505a.title: Weathering
ade0f313505a.sentence: More typical is thermal fatigue, in which the stresses are not great enough to cause immediate rock failure, but repeated cycles of stress and release gradually weaken the rocks.

3faed84455a6.title: Weathering
3faed84455a6.sentence: Thermal stress weathering is an important mechanism in deserts, where there is a large diurnal temperature range, hot in the day and cold at night.

df4b68497229.title: Weathering
df4b68497229.sentence: Thermal stress weathering can be caused by any large change of temperature, and not just intense solar heating.

f67526196313.title: Weathering
f67526196313.sentence: It is likely as important in cold climates as in hot, arid climates.

4b2d7c499b23.title: Weathering
4b2d7c499b23.sentence: Wildfires can also be a significant cause of rapid thermal stress weathering.

42a1431b337e.title: Weathering
42a1431b337e.sentence: Thermal stress weathering is most effective when the heated portion of the rock is buttressed by surrounding rock, so that it is free to expand in only one direction.

31ee6ce112e2.title: Weathering
31ee6ce112e2.sentence: The importance of thermal stress weathering has long been discounted by geologists, based on experiments in the early 20th century that seemed to show that its effects were unimportant.

711654ef8c8d.title: Weathering
711654ef8c8d.sentence: These experiments have since been criticized as unrealistic, since the rock samples were small, were polished (which reduces nucleation of fractures), and were not buttressed.

f06000eec2ba.title: Weathering
f06000eec2ba.sentence: Geomorphologists have begun to reemphasize the importance of thermal stress weathering, particularly in cold climates.

9ac6ccdf2f60.title: Mineral
9ac6ccdf2f60.sentence: The abundance and diversity of minerals is controlled directly by their chemistry, in turn dependent on elemental abundances in the Earth.

6b25191f9c53.title: Mineral
6b25191f9c53.sentence: As a result, it is possible for one element to be substituted for another.

7a13a8dc34ed.title: Mineral
7a13a8dc34ed.sentence: These eight elements, summing to over 98% of the crust by weight, are, in order of decreasing abundance: oxygen, silicon, aluminium, iron, magnesium, calcium, sodium and potassium.

85f24ed2da41.title: Mineral
85f24ed2da41.sentence: Oxygen and silicon are by far the two most important – oxygen composes 47% of the crust by weight, and silicon accounts for 28%.

1305ced99cd7.title: Mineral
1305ced99cd7.sentence: The minerals that form are those that are most stable at the temperature and pressure of formation, within the limits imposed by the bulk chemistry of the parent body.

7df222a6c400.title: Mineral
7df222a6c400.sentence: Chemical substitution will occur between ions of a similar size and charge; for example, K+ will not substitute for Si4+ because of chemical and structural incompatibilities caused by a big difference in size and charge.

03bab192c82b.title: Mineral
03bab192c82b.sentence: A common example of chemical substitution is that of Si4+ by Al3+, which are close in charge, size, and abundance in the crust.

313491af8711.title: Mineral
313491af8711.sentence: In the case of silicate materials, the substitution of Si4+ by Al3+ allows for a variety of minerals because of the need to balance charges.

253002d7fa1e.title: Mineral
253002d7fa1e.sentence: Changes in composition can be caused by processes such as weathering or metasomatism (hydrothermal alteration).

d2417e9858dd.title: Mineral
d2417e9858dd.sentence: Changes in temperature and pressure and composition alter the mineralogy of a rock sample.

738734a3a631.title: Mineral
738734a3a631.sentence: Oxide minerals are divided into three categories: simple oxides, hydroxides, and multiple oxides.

36e76b2c58f1.title: Mineral
36e76b2c58f1.sentence: Simple oxides are characterized by O2− as the main anion and primarily ionic bonding.

bb1e16b188ec.title: Mineral
bb1e16b188ec.sentence: In hydroxides, the dominant anion is the hydroxyl ion, OH−.

05a82cdc6425.title: Mineral
05a82cdc6425.sentence: Corundum group minerals have a 2:3 ratio, and includes minerals such as corundum (Al2O3), and hematite (Fe2O3).

8958a88fff3e.title: Mineral
8958a88fff3e.sentence: Bauxites are the chief aluminium ore, and are a heterogeneous mixture of the hydroxide minerals diaspore, gibbsite, and bohmite; they form in areas with a very high rate of chemical weathering (mainly tropical conditions).

9b1f8fb37115.title: Mineral
9b1f8fb37115.sentence: The latter is readily distinguishable by its strong magnetism, which occurs as it has iron in two oxidation states (Fe2+Fe3+2O4), which makes it a multiple oxide instead of a single oxide.

f4a1fc2b5f8f.title: Mineral
f4a1fc2b5f8f.sentence: In rocks, some mineral species and groups are much more abundant than others; these are termed the rock-forming minerals.

72f26f6c9223.title: Mineral
72f26f6c9223.sentence: A rock is an aggregate of one or more minerals or mineraloids.

750d899d8b5c.title: Mineral
750d899d8b5c.sentence: The major examples of these are quartz, the feldspars, the micas, the amphiboles, the pyroxenes, the olivines, and calcite; except for the last one, all of these minerals are silicates.

b2b9dcd6eb6e.title: Mineral
b2b9dcd6eb6e.sentence: Some rocks, such as limestone or quartzite, are composed primarily of one mineral – calcite or aragonite in the case of limestone, and quartz in the latter case.

d55cb27839c3.title: Mineral
d55cb27839c3.sentence: Other rocks can be defined by relative abundances of key (essential) minerals; a granite is defined by proportions of quartz, alkali feldspar, and plagioclase feldspar.

cddfa9802895.title: Mineral
cddfa9802895.sentence: Rocks can also be composed entirely of non-mineral material; coal is a sedimentary rock composed primarily of organically derived carbon.

d158015cf9ef.title: Mineral
d158015cf9ef.sentence: The base unit of a silicate mineral is the [SiO4]4− tetrahedron.

fdda18c0aa88.title: Mineral
fdda18c0aa88.sentence: These silica tetrahedra are then polymerized to some degree to create various structures, such as one-dimensional chains, two-dimensional sheets, and three-dimensional frameworks.

0239eeb5752c.title: Silicate mineral
0239eeb5752c.sentence: Silicate minerals are rock-forming minerals made up of silicate groups.

35fc55ec298a.title: Mineral
35fc55ec298a.sentence: In the vast majority of cases, silicon is in four-fold or tetrahedral coordination with oxygen.

82222bb34ff6.title: Mineral
82222bb34ff6.sentence: Have no linking of polyhedra, thus tetrahedra share no corners.

c1180466b559.title: Mineral
c1180466b559.sentence: Have two tetrahedra sharing one oxygen atom.

784cefb16e8f.title: Mineral
784cefb16e8f.sentence: Only need tetrahedra to share two corners to form the cyclical structure.

4b0ef7539256.title: Mineral
4b0ef7539256.sentence: Single-chain silicates have two shared corners, whereas double-chain silicates have two or three shared corners.

2259dd5a7b01.title: Mineral
2259dd5a7b01.sentence: Have a sheet structure which requires three shared oxygens; in the case of double-chain silicates, some tetrahedra must share two corners instead of three as otherwise a sheet structure would result.

134e96ea3ead.title: Mineral
134e96ea3ead.sentence: Have tetrahedra that share all four corners.

c52cf9f3ad7b.title: Mineral
c52cf9f3ad7b.sentence: It is common for the Si4+ to be substituted by Al3+ because of similarity in ionic radius and charge; in those cases, the [AlO4]5− tetrahedra form the same structures as do the unsubstituted tetrahedra, but their charge-balancing requirements are different.

c73087c35d9d.title: Mineral
c73087c35d9d.sentence: Inosilicates contain two important rock-forming mineral groups; single-chain silicates are most commonly pyroxenes, while double-chain silicates are often amphiboles.

14af56a0eb9f.title: Mineral
14af56a0eb9f.sentence: Pyroxenes are common in the Earth's crust (about 10%) and are a key constituent of mafic igneous rocks.

2e83cda62c65.title: Silicate mineral
2e83cda62c65.sentence: They are the largest and most important class of minerals and make up approximately 90 percent of Earth's crust.

4b63355f426f.title: Silicate mineral
4b63355f426f.sentence: On Earth, a wide variety of silicate minerals occur in an even wider range of combinations as a result of the processes that have been forming and re-working the crust for billions of years.

9b7bc5bf418c.title: Silicate mineral
9b7bc5bf418c.sentence: These processes include partial melting, crystallization, fractionation, metamorphism, weathering, and diagenesis.

51efc8744300.title: Silicate mineral
51efc8744300.sentence: Living organisms also contribute to this geologic cycle.

54fb0bed12e3.title: Silicate mineral
54fb0bed12e3.sentence: For example, a type of plankton known as diatoms construct their exoskeletons ("frustules") from silica extracted from seawater.

46f1350ba6f8.title: Mineral
46f1350ba6f8.sentence: Tectosilicates, also known as framework silicates, have the highest degree of polymerization.

0bff8f7374e2.title: Mineral
0bff8f7374e2.sentence: Examples are quartz, the feldspars, feldspathoids, and the zeolites.

55ef30ca5da8.title: Mineral
55ef30ca5da8.sentence: Framework silicates tend to be particularly chemically stable as a result of strong covalent bonds.

acd56875df76.title: Mineral
acd56875df76.sentence: Forming 12% of the Earth's crust, quartz (SiO2) is the most abundant mineral species.

e496fddd39e8.title: Mineral
e496fddd39e8.sentence: It is characterized by its high chemical and physical resistivity.

fd7a4a972432.title: Quartz
fd7a4a972432.sentence: Generally a high presence of quartz suggests a "mature" rock, since it indicates the rock has been heavily reworked and quartz was the primary mineral that endured heavy weathering.

e1e4d91ec5bb.title: Mineral
e1e4d91ec5bb.sentence: Feldspars are the most abundant group in the Earth's crust, at about 50%.

86d6803f3850.title: Mineral
86d6803f3850.sentence: In the feldspars, Al3+ substitutes for Si4+, which creates a charge imbalance that must be accounted for by the addition of cations.

966e74269bc5.title: Mineral
966e74269bc5.sentence: The alkali feldspars are most commonly in a series between potassium-rich orthoclase and sodium-rich albite; in the case of plagioclase, the most common series ranges from albite to calcium-rich anorthite.

c01769829dd6.title: Clay mineral
c01769829dd6.sentence: Clay minerals are common weathering products (including weathering of feldspar) and low-temperature hydrothermal alteration products.

b29fa6e8f1c2.title: Mineral
b29fa6e8f1c2.sentence: Phyllosilicates consist of sheets of polymerized tetrahedra.

e2a8e57e61d3.title: Mineral
e2a8e57e61d3.sentence: Important examples include the mica, chlorite, and the kaolinite-serpentine groups.

255f4bef4181.title: Mineral
255f4bef4181.sentence: They are bound at three oxygen sites, which gives a characteristic silicon:oxygen ratio of 2:5.

7491fb1f1d2f.title: Mineral
7491fb1f1d2f.sentence: In addition to the tetrahedra, phyllosilicates have a sheet of octahedra (elements in six-fold coordination by oxygen) that balance out the basic tetrahedra, which have a negative charge (e.g. [Si4O10]4−) These tetrahedra (T) and octahedra (O) sheets are stacked in a variety of combinations to create phyllosilicate layers.

7e45065361e6.title: Mineral
7e45065361e6.sentence: The kaolinite-serpentine group consists of T-O stacks (the 1:1 clay minerals); their hardness ranges from 2 to 4, as the sheets are held by hydrogen bonds.

2bd5bf36cb53.title: Mineral
2bd5bf36cb53.sentence: The 2:1 clay minerals (pyrophyllite-talc) consist of T-O-T stacks, but they are softer (hardness from 1 to 2), as they are instead held together by van der Waals forces.

180f53c3ed39.title: Mineral
180f53c3ed39.sentence: Micas are also T-O-T-stacked phyllosilicates, but differ from the other T-O-T and T-O-stacked subclass members in that they incorporate aluminium into the tetrahedral sheets (clay minerals have Al3+ in octahedral sites).

9f8b84a0d971.title: Mineral
9f8b84a0d971.sentence: Mica T-O-T layers are bonded together by metal ions, giving them a greater hardness than other phyllosilicate minerals, though they retain perfect basal cleavage.

c8ba30579c24.title: Mineral
c8ba30579c24.sentence: The layers are weakly bound by van der Waals forces, hydrogen bonds, or sparse ionic bonds, which causes a crystallographic weakness, in turn leading to a prominent basal cleavage among the phyllosilicates.

5aac3fc30958.title: Mineral
5aac3fc30958.sentence: Because of their chemical structure, phyllosilicates typically have flexible, elastic, transparent layers that are electrical insulators and can be split into very thin flakes.

8ebf91528b23.title: Mineral
8ebf91528b23.sentence: Within an octahedral sheet, there are three octahedral sites in a unit structure; however, not all of the sites may be occupied.

7e493abed634.title: Mineral
7e493abed634.sentence: In that case, the mineral is termed dioctahedral, whereas in other case it is termed trioctahedral.

5a842e8cd07f.title: Mineral
5a842e8cd07f.sentence: These two groups of minerals are subgrouped by octahedral occupation; specifically, kaolinite and pyrophyllite are dioctahedral whereas serpentine and talc trioctahedral.

68440b213478.title: Clay
68440b213478.sentence: Clay is a type of fine-grained natural soil material containing clay minerals (hydrous aluminium phyllosilicates, e.g. kaolinite, Al2Si2O5(OH)4).

8b41bcd5c353.title: Clay
8b41bcd5c353.sentence: Most pure clay minerals are white or light-coloured, but natural clays show a variety of colours from impurities, such as a reddish or brownish colour from small amounts of iron oxide.

01ca84c4ef84.title: Clay
01ca84c4ef84.sentence: Clays develop plasticity when wet but can be hardened through firing.

f000fb5e22b2.title: Clay
f000fb5e22b2.sentence: Clay soils are generally less suitable for crops due to poor natural drainage; however, clay soils are more fertile, due to higher cation-exchange capacity.

5b6008c0fb56.title: Clay
5b6008c0fb56.sentence: Mixtures of sand, silt and less than 40% clay are called loam.

aecdafb1f3dd.title: Clay
aecdafb1f3dd.sentence: Soils high in swelling clays (expansive clay), which are clay minerals that readily expand in volume when they absorb water, are a major challenge in civil engineering.

266bdea90d72.title: Clay
266bdea90d72.sentence: Shale, formed largely from clay, is the most common sedimentary rock.

5adc36c9bdec.title: Clay
5adc36c9bdec.sentence: Clay is the longest-known ceramic raw material.

0650a30dccdb.title: Clay
0650a30dccdb.sentence: Some of the earliest pottery shards have been dated to around 14,000 BCE, and clay tablets were the first known writing medium.

b091960bb6e4.title: Soil texture
b091960bb6e4.sentence: Soil texture is the identifying quality of the upper layer of earth, which is composed of sand, silt and clay.

221d8e75f851.title: Soil texture
221d8e75f851.sentence: These classifications are based on the percentages of sand, silt, and clay in the soil.

8624def84aaa.title: Soil texture
8624def84aaa.sentence: Soil texture focuses on the particles that are less than two millimeters in diameter which include sand, silt, and clay.

8c49f293a340.title: Soil texture
8c49f293a340.sentence: The USDA soil taxonomy and WRB soil classification systems use 12 textural classes whereas the UK-ADAS system uses 11.

36655f376d58.title: Soil texture
36655f376d58.sentence: Soil texture can be determined using qualitative methods such as texture by feel, and quantitative methods such as the hydrometer method based on Stokes' law.

078bf2918101.title: Physical properties of soil
078bf2918101.sentence: While texture is defined by the mineral component of a soil and is an innate property of the soil that does not change with agricultural activities, soil structure can be improved or destroyed by the choice and timing of farming practices.

9aae09544e66.title: Agricultural soil science
9aae09544e66.section: Kinds of soil and their variables
9aae09544e66.sentence: Field capacity, the water content retained in the soil at −33 kPa (or −0.33 bar) water potential, when air is in the macropores, and water is in the micropores, is the optimal condition for plant growth and microbial activity.

9b5cc72b4b68.title: Agricultural soil science
9b5cc72b4b68.section: Kinds of soil and their variables
9b5cc72b4b68.sentence: It varies with soil texture, increasing with decreasing size of soil particles (i.e. from sand to clay).

a83f334329a4.title: Soil texture
a83f334329a4.sentence: Soil texture has agricultural applications such as determining crop suitability and to predict the response of the soil to environmental and management conditions such as drought or calcium (lime) requirements.

00c32551ae66.title: Soil texture
00c32551ae66.sentence: The first classification, the international system, was first proposed by Albert Atterberg in 1905 and was based on his studies in southern Sweden.

05201a6c1b99.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Soils_Laboratory_Manual_(Moorberg_and_Crouse)/03%3A_Soil_Physics/03.1%3A_Soil_Texture_and_Structure
05201a6c1b99.sentence: Soil texture and structure are considered “master variables”, meaning that texture and structure directly influence a large number of other soil properties.

70bb364ce0a4.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Soils_Laboratory_Manual_(Moorberg_and_Crouse)/03%3A_Soil_Physics/03.1%3A_Soil_Texture_and_Structure
70bb364ce0a4.sentence: For example, in comparing a clayey soil and a sandy soil, one would expect the clayey soil to have larger specific surface area, more cation exchange capacity, more total porosity, less macroporosity, and more organic matter than the sandy soil.

97df112f06fc.title: Clay
97df112f06fc.sentence: Clay minerals most commonly form by prolonged chemical weathering of silicate-bearing rocks.

355904f9d648.title: Clay
355904f9d648.sentence: There are two types of clay deposits: primary and secondary.

d7b68f94fd99.title: Clay
d7b68f94fd99.sentence: Chemical weathering takes place largely by acid hydrolysis due to low concentrations of carbonic acid, dissolved in rainwater or released by plant roots.

4d09fa3ea458.title: Clay
4d09fa3ea458.sentence: The acid breaks bonds between aluminium and oxygen, releasing other metal ions and silica (as a gel of orthosilicic acid).

34301014927f.title: Mineral
34301014927f.sentence: Orthoclase feldspar (KAlSi3O8) is a mineral commonly found in granite, a plutonic igneous rock.

4734b4f98f2f.title: Mineral
4734b4f98f2f.sentence: When exposed to weathering, it reacts to form kaolinite (Al2Si2O5(OH)4, a sedimentary mineral, and silicic acid):

a1f11f36c3eb.title: Mineral
a1f11f36c3eb.sentence: 2 KAlSi3O8 + 5 H2O + 2 H+ → Al2Si2O5(OH)4 + 4 H2SiO3 + 2 K+

f8af5441c894.title: Clay
f8af5441c894.sentence: The clay minerals formed depend on the composition of the source rock and the climate.

60a051148c31.title: Clay
60a051148c31.sentence: Acid weathering of feldspar-rich rock, such as granite, in warm climates tends to produce kaolin.

ac5db9c89208.title: Clay
ac5db9c89208.sentence: Weathering of the same kind of rock under alkaline conditions produces illite.

abfd5eb9357d.title: Clay
abfd5eb9357d.sentence: Smectite forms by weathering of igneous rock under alkaline conditions, while gibbsite forms by intense weathering of other clay minerals.

516d665b172f.title: Clay
516d665b172f.sentence: They can also form locally from hydrothermal activity.

c0cfdf9e38e3.title: Clay
c0cfdf9e38e3.sentence: Primary clays form as residual deposits in soil and remain at the site of formation.

27607356f5c3.title: Clay
27607356f5c3.sentence: Secondary clays are clays that have been transported from their original location by water erosion and deposited in a new sedimentary deposit.

d2ace4223071.title: Clay
d2ace4223071.sentence: Secondary clay deposits are typically associated with very low energy depositional environments such as large lakes and marine basins.

43a66f6412ae.title: Weathering
43a66f6412ae.sentence: Hydrolysis (also called incongruent dissolution) is a form of chemical weathering in which only part of a mineral is taken into solution.

7b7fa438a4f6.title: Weathering
7b7fa438a4f6.sentence: The rest of the mineral is transformed into a new solid material, such as a clay mineral.

4ab673a6b032.title: Weathering
4ab673a6b032.sentence: Acid hydrolysis from dissolved carbon dioxide is sometimes described as carbonation, and can result in weathering of the primary minerals to secondary carbonate minerals.

a914b0d353a2.title: Weathering
a914b0d353a2.sentence: Most hydrolysis during weathering of minerals is acid hydrolysis, in which protons (hydrogen ions), which are present in acidic water, attack chemical bonds in mineral crystals.

60b003386832.title: Weathering
60b003386832.sentence: Carbon dioxide that dissolves in water to form carbonic acid is the most important source of protons, but organic acids are also important natural sources of acidity.

2a1162d633f4.title: Weathering
2a1162d633f4.sentence: The bonds between different cations and oxygen ions in minerals differ in strength, and the weakest will be attacked first.

fff377163c14.title: Weathering
fff377163c14.sentence: The result is that minerals in igneous rock weather in roughly the same order in which they were originally formed (Bowen's Reaction Series).

2a2630df0402.title: Weathering
2a2630df0402.sentence: Some minerals, such as illite, are unusually stable, while silica is unusually unstable given the strength of the silicon–oxygen bond.

d809fdc68389.title: Weathering
d809fdc68389.sentence: Aluminosilicates containing highly soluble cations, such as sodium or potassium ions, will release the cations as dissolved bicarbonates during acid hydrolysis:

49174380fa86.title: Weathering
49174380fa86.sentence: orthoclase (aluminosilicate feldspar) + carbonic acid + water ⇌ kaolinite (a clay mineral) + silicic acid in solution + potassium and bicarbonate ions in solution

e7f4a7b4e1fb.title: Weathering
e7f4a7b4e1fb.sentence: For example, weathering of forsterite can produce magnesite instead of brucite via the reaction:

493c243e726e.title: Weathering
493c243e726e.sentence: Carbonic acid is consumed by silicate weathering, resulting in more alkaline solutions because of the bicarbonate.

dc1ea0bdb4ed.title: Weathering
dc1ea0bdb4ed.sentence: This is an important reaction in controlling the amount of CO2 in the atmosphere and can affect climate.

3f85ade2eb8e.title: Weathering
3f85ade2eb8e.sentence: All are converted into a mixture of clay minerals and iron oxides.

e457854a79a0.title: Weathering
e457854a79a0.sentence: Granitic rock, the most abundant crystalline rock exposed at the Earth's surface, begins weathering with the destruction of hornblende.

9b8fbca2af12.title: Weathering
9b8fbca2af12.sentence: Biotite then weathers to vermiculite, and finally oligoclase and microcline are destroyed.

436e6f373006.title: Weathering
436e6f373006.sentence: The resulting soil is depleted in calcium, sodium, and ferrous iron compared with the bedrock, and magnesium is reduced by 40% and silicon by 15%.

74adc1be76c4.title: Weathering
74adc1be76c4.sentence: At the same time, the soil is enriched in aluminium and potassium by at least 50%; by titanium, whose abundance triples, and ferric iron, whose abundance increases by an order of magnitude compared with the bedrock.

b91f2476249e.title: Weathering
b91f2476249e.sentence: Basaltic rock is more easily weathered than granitic rock due to its formation at higher temperatures and drier conditions.

8f0b85ada2a4.title: Weathering
8f0b85ada2a4.sentence: The fine grain size and presence of volcanic glass also hasten weathering.

d121551fab9d.title: Weathering
d121551fab9d.sentence: Because most basalt is relatively poor in potassium, the basalt weathers directly to potassium-poor montmorillonite, then to kaolinite.

a76a0bce2ba9.title: Weathering
a76a0bce2ba9.sentence: Where leaching is continuous and intense, as in rain forests, the final weathering product is bauxite, the principal ore of aluminium.

a44a275f91cb.title: Weathering
a44a275f91cb.sentence: Where rainfall is intense but seasonal, as in monsoon climates, the final weathering product is iron- and titanium-rich laterite.

0653f6251ac0.title: Weathering
0653f6251ac0.sentence: Soil formation requires between 100 and 1,000 years, a brief interval in geologic time.

8f273560c84e.title: Weathering
8f273560c84e.sentence: The degree of weathering of soil can be expressed as the chemical index of alteration, defined as 100 Al2O3/(Al2O3 + CaO + Na2O + K2O).

bb2a162dcad8.title: Weathering
bb2a162dcad8.sentence: This varies from 47 for unweathered upper crust rock to 100 for fully weathered material.

d0a552be9a74.title: Clay
d0a552be9a74.sentence: Clay as the defining ingredient of loam is one of the oldest building materials on Earth, among other ancient, naturally occurring geologic materials such as stone and organic materials like wood.

04e6115907eb.title: Clay
04e6115907eb.sentence: Between one-half and two-thirds of the world's population, in both traditional societies as well as developed countries, still live or work in buildings made with clay, often baked into brick, as an essential part of their load-bearing structure.

6c499e779856.title: Clay
6c499e779856.sentence: Clay, relatively impermeable to water, is also used where natural seals are needed, such as in pond linings, the cores of dams, or as a barrier in landfills against toxic seepage (lining the landfill, preferably in combination with geotextiles).

313d1c55d065.title: Clay
313d1c55d065.sentence: Clay was used as a mortar in brick chimneys and stone walls where protected from water.

88adb91140d8.title: Clay
88adb91140d8.sentence: Studies in the early 21st century have investigated clay's absorption capacities in various applications, such as the removal of heavy metals from waste water and air purification.

0aed47e3b116.title: Clay
0aed47e3b116.sentence: The main groups of clays include kaolinite, montmorillonite-smectite, and illite.

00809a013b3d.title: Clay
00809a013b3d.sentence: Chlorite, vermiculite, talc, and pyrophyllite are sometimes also classified as clay minerals.

7facec6f13e4.title: Clay
7facec6f13e4.sentence: There are approximately 30 different types of "pure" clays in these categories, but most "natural" clay deposits are mixtures of these different types, along with other weathered minerals.

f8db435d343a.title: Clay
f8db435d343a.sentence: Clay minerals in clays are most easily identified using X-ray diffraction rather than chemical or physical tests.

f3f8cd552148.title: Clay
f3f8cd552148.sentence: Varve (or varved clay) is clay with visible annual layers that are formed by seasonal deposition of those layers and are marked by differences in erosion and organic content.

a88a8f9565e8.title: Clay
a88a8f9565e8.sentence: This type of deposit is common in former glacial lakes.

4896f2fa1d2d.title: Clay
4896f2fa1d2d.sentence: Clays are used for making pottery, both utilitarian and decorative, and construction products, such as bricks, walls, and floor tiles.

e913ed490282.title: Clay
e913ed490282.sentence: Clay is used in many industrial processes, such as paper making, cement production, and chemical filtering.

2ca70f908cbc.title: Clay
2ca70f908cbc.sentence: Some of the earliest pottery shards recovered are from central Honshu, Japan.

5359200e1a5d.title: Clay
5359200e1a5d.sentence: They are associated with the Jōmon culture, and recovered deposits have been dated to around 14,000 BCE.

0326511841a1.title: Clay
0326511841a1.sentence: Ancient peoples in Mesopotamia adopted clay tablets as the first known writing medium.

a02314e6938d.title: Clay
a02314e6938d.sentence: Scribes wrote on the tablets by inscribing them with a script known as cuneiform, using a blunt reed called a stylus, which effectively produced the wedge shaped markings of their writing.

73a02e578f15.title: Clay
73a02e578f15.sentence: Different types of clay, when used with different minerals and firing conditions, are used to produce earthenware, stoneware, and porcelain.

c895b38db689.title: Clay
c895b38db689.sentence: Nowadays, clay is added as a filler to graphite, in pencil lead, to change the hardness and blackness of the pencil.

c46452e5ed98.title: Mineralogy
c46452e5ed98.sentence: Mineralogy is a subject of geology specializing in the scientific study of the chemistry, crystal structure, and physical (including optical) properties of minerals and mineralized artifacts.

bad1f526aeec.title: Mineralogy
bad1f526aeec.sentence: Specific studies within mineralogy include the processes of mineral origin and formation, classification of minerals, their geographical distribution, and their utilization.

f5d7d17f084e.title: Mineralogy
f5d7d17f084e.sentence: The environments of mineral formation and growth are highly varied, ranging from slow crystallization at the high temperatures and pressures of igneous melts deep within the Earth's crust to the low temperature precipitation from a saline brine at the Earth's surface.

97ba294c2a0d.title: Mineralogy
97ba294c2a0d.sentence: - formation by oxidation and weathering of rocks exposed to the atmosphere or within the soil environment.

5863fd7e7ee9.title: Mineralogy
5863fd7e7ee9.sentence: An initial step in identifying a mineral is to examine its physical properties, many of which can be measured on a hand sample.

148804516eaf.title: Mineralogy
148804516eaf.sentence: In the Mohs scale, a standard set of minerals is numbered in order of increasing hardness from 1 (talc) to 10 (diamond).
