f8dcb43d2934.title: Mineralogy
f8dcb43d2934.sentence: X-ray diffraction was demonstrated by Max von Laue in 1912, and developed into a tool for analyzing the crystal structure of minerals by the father/son team of William Henry Bragg and William Lawrence Bragg.

062713c55408.title: Mineral
062713c55408.sentence: A topic of contention among geologists and mineralogists has been the IMA's decision to exclude biogenic crystalline substances.

2f0bab8fffe6.title: Mineral
2f0bab8fffe6.sentence: For example, Lowenstam (1981) stated that "organisms are capable of forming a diverse array of minerals, some of which cannot be formed inorganically in the biosphere."

b2ec668cfc81.title: Mineral
b2ec668cfc81.sentence: Skinner (2005) views all solids as potential minerals and includes biominerals in the mineral kingdom, which are those that are created by the metabolic activities of organisms.

c279c63b8db1.title: Mineral
c279c63b8db1.sentence: Skinner's (2005) definition of a mineral takes this matter into account by stating that a mineral can be crystalline or amorphous.

9a42eb080c98.title: Mineral
9a42eb080c98.sentence: Prior to the International Mineralogical Association's listing, over 60 biominerals had been discovered, named, and published.

58309c1b523c.title: Mineral
58309c1b523c.sentence: These biominerals are not listed in the International Mineral Association official list of mineral names; however, many of these biomineral representatives are distributed amongst the 78 mineral classes listed in the Dana classification scheme.

79e2612eb6a2.title: Mineral
79e2612eb6a2.sentence: The group's scope includes mineral-forming microorganisms, which exist on nearly every rock, soil, and particle surface spanning the globe to depths of at least 1600 metres below the sea floor and 70 kilometres into the stratosphere (possibly entering the mesosphere).

5855cdc6c6f1.title: Mineral
5855cdc6c6f1.sentence: Microorganisms can precipitate metals from solution, contributing to the formation of ore deposits.

31631210097c.title: Mineral
31631210097c.sentence: They can also catalyze the dissolution of minerals.

c26f7c66ec52.title: Mineral
c26f7c66ec52.sentence: The carbonate minerals are those in which the main anionic group is carbonate, [CO3]2−.

4bc5e4c75d4b.title: Mineral
4bc5e4c75d4b.sentence: The most common carbonate mineral is calcite, which is the primary constituent of sedimentary limestone and metamorphic marble.

0ed7799c7620.title: Mineral
0ed7799c7620.sentence: Carbonates tend to be brittle, many have rhombohedral cleavage, and all react with acid.

7385aad0b48d.title: Mineral
7385aad0b48d.sentence: Due to the last characteristic, field geologists often carry dilute hydrochloric acid to distinguish carbonates from non-carbonates.

31ce726158e7.title: Mineral
31ce726158e7.sentence: Dolomite is a double carbonate, with the formula CaMg(CO3)2.

356f159ffcd8.title: Mineral
356f159ffcd8.sentence: Carbonates are most often formed as biogenic or chemical sediments in marine environments.

d412514eb4b4.title: Calcite
d412514eb4b4.sentence: Calcite (English: /ˈkælˌsaɪt/) is a carbonate mineral and the most stable polymorph of calcium carbonate (CaCO3).

b33d50989716.title: Calcite
b33d50989716.sentence: It is a very common mineral, particularly as a component of limestone.

89458edcd268.title: Calcite
89458edcd268.sentence: Calcite defines hardness 3 on the Mohs scale of mineral hardness, based on scratch hardness comparison.

567e1ceaebc7.title: Calcite
567e1ceaebc7.sentence: Calcite, like most carbonates, dissolves in acids by the following reaction:

3d6b3afad90f.title: Calcite
3d6b3afad90f.sentence: The carbon dioxide released by this reaction produces a characteristic effervescence when a calcite sample is treated with an acid.

af0610573c01.title: Calcite
af0610573c01.sentence: As a result, calcite can be either dissolved by groundwater or precipitated by groundwater, depending on such factors as the water temperature, pH, and dissolved ion concentrations.

3e7da80d8e03.title: Calcite
3e7da80d8e03.sentence: If the amount of dissolved carbon dioxide drops, the reaction reverses to precipitate calcite.

22656067126e.title: Calcite
22656067126e.sentence: Calcite exhibits an unusual characteristic called retrograde solubility: it is less soluble in water as the temperature increases.

e31de40ca3c3.title: Mineral
e31de40ca3c3.sentence: A mineral can be identified by several physical properties, some of them being sufficient for full identification without equivocation.

6383fe2566f5.title: Mineral
6383fe2566f5.sentence: Physical properties applied for classification include crystal structure and habit, hardness, lustre, diaphaneity, colour, streak, cleavage and fracture, and specific gravity.

3a0c82262cbe.title: Mineral
3a0c82262cbe.sentence: In other cases, minerals can only be classified by more complex optical, chemical or X-ray diffraction analysis; these methods, however, can be costly and time-consuming.

38bfb84951a9.title: Mineral
38bfb84951a9.sentence: The most commonly used scale of measurement is the ordinal Mohs hardness scale, which measures resistance to scratching.

bb26568a14a1.title: Mineral
bb26568a14a1.sentence: Defined by ten indicators, a mineral with a higher index scratches those below it.

0cbe77245e1d.title: Mineral
0cbe77245e1d.sentence: The scale ranges from talc, a phyllosilicate, to diamond, a carbon polymorph that is the hardest natural material.

a2e283e46f6e.title: Mineral
a2e283e46f6e.sentence: Colour is the most obvious property of a mineral, but it is often non-diagnostic.

42015fb2d105.title: Mineral
42015fb2d105.sentence: The streak of a mineral refers to the colour of a mineral in powdered form, which may or may not be identical to its body colour.

d3dab8b6f50b.title: Mineral
d3dab8b6f50b.sentence: The streak of a mineral is independent of trace elements or any weathering surface.

648a4700b88d.title: Mineral
648a4700b88d.section: Physical properties > Crystal structure and habit
648a4700b88d.sentence: Even when the mineral grains are too small to see or are irregularly shaped, the underlying crystal structure is always periodic and can be determined by X-ray diffraction.

631e4b193be3.title: Mineral
631e4b193be3.sentence: The sulfate minerals all contain the sulfate anion, [SO4]2−.

4b590f0ecd4a.title: Mineral
4b590f0ecd4a.sentence: The most common hydrous sulfate by far is gypsum, CaSO4⋅2H2O.

5b86b0b6a0f1.title: Mineral
5b86b0b6a0f1.sentence: Sulfate minerals commonly form as evaporites, where they precipitate out of evaporating saline waters.

3548b82cf170.title: Mineral
3548b82cf170.sentence: Sulfates can also be found in hydrothermal vein systems associated with sulfides, or as oxidation products of sulfides.

03c1ae9687ba.title: Mineral
03c1ae9687ba.sentence: It forms as an evaporite, and is associated with other evaporites such as calcite and halite; if it incorporates sand grains as it crystallizes, gypsum can form desert roses.

4282e58a3de1.title: Mineral
4282e58a3de1.sentence: The anhydrous equivalent of gypsum is anhydrite; it can form directly from seawater in highly arid conditions.

8bcab90e7a30.title: Phytolith
8bcab90e7a30.sentence: Phytoliths (from Greek, "plant stone") are rigid, microscopic mineral deposits found in some plant tissues, often persisting after the decay of the plant.

1c9f9f3d5341.title: Phytolith
1c9f9f3d5341.sentence: Although some use "phytolith" to refer to all mineral secretions by plants, it more commonly refers to siliceous plant remains.

fac8c0094816.title: Phytolith
fac8c0094816.sentence: Soluble silica, also called monosilicic or orthosilicic acid with a chemical formula of (Si(OH)4), is taken up from the soil when plant roots absorb groundwater.

5d296be961c7.title: Phytolith
5d296be961c7.sentence: The silica is absorbed in the form of monosilicic acid (Si(OH)4), and is carried by the plant's vascular system to the cell walls, cell lumen, and intercellular spaces.

d1e905cb43bd.title: Phytolith
d1e905cb43bd.sentence: Depending on the plant taxa and soil condition, absorbed silica can range from 0.1% to 10% of the plant's total dry weight.

1da602316198.title: Phytolith
1da602316198.sentence: While researchers had previously known that phytoliths could persist in some soils for thousands of years and that there was carbon occluded within phytoliths that could be used for radiocarbon dating, research into the capacity of phytoliths as a method of storing carbon in soils was pioneered by Parr and Sullivan who suggested that there was a real opportunity to sequester carbon securely in soils for the long term, in the form of carbon inclusions in durable silica phytoliths.

cfa3d236d13b.title: Phytolith
cfa3d236d13b.sentence: Phytoliths occur abundantly in the fossil record, and have been reported from the Late Devonian onwards.

044ee4b6094d.title: Phytolith
044ee4b6094d.sentence: In addition to reconstructing human-plant interactions since the Pleistocene, phytoliths can be used to identify palaeoenvironments and to track vegetational change.

63f3c992b6cd.title: Phytolith
63f3c992b6cd.sentence: Research, particularly since 2005 has shown that carbon in phytoliths can be resistant to decomposition for millennia and can accumulate in soils.

a778639fbeaa.title: Phytolith
a778639fbeaa.sentence: During the mineralization process which creates the phytolith, many different nutrients are absorbed from the soil including carbon which forms Phytolith Occluded Carbon (PhytOC).

346a3597f2cf.title: Phytolith
346a3597f2cf.sentence: Therefore, total PhytOC sequester largely depends on the condition of the biome such as grassland, forest, or cropland, and is influenced by climate and soil conditions.

58356ff47c53.title: Soil carbon
58356ff47c53.section: Forms of Carbon in Soil > Organic carbon
58356ff47c53.sentence: Chemically stabilized organic matter is known as mineral-associated organic matter (MAOM).

58d34dd379be.title: Soil carbon
58d34dd379be.section: Forms of Carbon in Soil > Organic carbon
58d34dd379be.sentence: MAOM is formed when organic compounds adhere to clay, iron oxide, or other mineral surfaces in the soil, making them more resistant to microbial degradation and loss from the soil carbon pool.

c794ccd5ad7e.title: Soil organic matter
c794ccd5ad7e.sentence: MAOM is thought to be low molecular weight compounds of plant and microbial origin that are associated with minerals through chemical bonds between SOM and charged mineral surfaces as well as occlusion in aggregates.

ec20f2c32cc2.title: Soil organic matter
ec20f2c32cc2.sentence: This mineral association acts as a protection for the SOM, as it is less accessible for decomposers.

16f27cf00697.title: Soil organic matter
16f27cf00697.sentence: MAOM is typically more persistent in the soil, staying there for centuries, compared to POM, which remains for only a few years to decades before being decomposed.

8f83ac7b8f68.title: Soil organic matter
8f83ac7b8f68.sentence: POM is thought to be made predominantly of fungal-colonized plant remains that have not experienced much decomposition.

a5a8ae2237eb.title: Weathering rind
a5a8ae2237eb.sentence: A weathering rind is a discolored, chemically altered, outer zone or layer of a discrete rock fragment formed by the processes of weathering.

b1ee15e195a0.title: Weathering rind
b1ee15e195a0.sentence: Rock fragments with weathering rinds normally are discrete clasts, ranging in size from pebbles to cobbles or boulders.

4a89a6702d6b.title: Weathering rind
4a89a6702d6b.sentence: They typically occur either lying on the surface of the ground or buried within sediments such as alluvium, colluvium, or glacial till.

d4db70bb50b5.title: Weathering rind
d4db70bb50b5.sentence: A weathering rind represents the alteration of the outer portion of a rock by exposure to air or near surface groundwater over a period of time.

546099078d18.title: Weathering rind
546099078d18.sentence: Typically, a weathering rind may be enriched with either iron or manganese (or both), and silica, and oxidized to a yellowish red to reddish color.

a3b9b439935f.title: Weathering rind
a3b9b439935f.sentence: Weathering rinds have a long history of being used to determine the relative age of either Quaternary sediments or landforms.

2b2047c6236c.title: Weathering rind
2b2047c6236c.sentence: This is done by comparing the thickness of weathering rinds of gravel composed of similar rock types.

0854143e2ceb.title: Weathering rind
0854143e2ceb.sentence: Deposits containing gravel with thicker weathering rinds are interpreted to be older than deposits containing rocks with thinner weathering rinds.

80a1cd46fa28.title: Weathering rind
80a1cd46fa28.sentence: This is done by determining the absolute age of sedimentary deposits containing either gravel-size rocks or artifacts using absolute dating methods such as C14 and measuring the weathering-rind thickness of rocks of similar lithology.

79c679c10599.title: Weathering rind
79c679c10599.sentence: The dates obtained from absolute dating techniques and measurements of weathering rind thicknesses are then used to construct an age versus thickness curve for dating rocks in other sedimentary deposits.

ed74bdd14c8a.title: Weathering rind
ed74bdd14c8a.sentence: This technique was proposed by Cernohouz and Solc who first argued that the relationship between the thickness of a weathering-rind thickness and the time it took to form is expressed by a logarithmic function.

23536327feba.title: Soil pH
23536327feba.sentence: Soil pH is a measure of the acidity or basicity (alkalinity) of a soil.

50193f725e23.title: Soil
50193f725e23.sentence: Soil reactivity is expressed in terms of pH and is a measure of the acidity or alkalinity of the soil.

6bd9e75a6713.title: Soil pH
6bd9e75a6713.sentence: Soil pH is a key characteristic that can be used to make informative analysis both qualitative and quantitatively regarding soil characteristics. pH is defined as the negative logarithm (base 10) of the activity of hydronium ions (H+ or, more precisely, H 3O+ aq) in a solution.

4b237497ea1f.title: Soil pH
4b237497ea1f.sentence: In soils, it is measured in a slurry of soil mixed with water (or a salt solution, such as 0.01 M CaCl 2), and normally falls between 3 and 10, with 7 being neutral.

1d6b6639bbe1.title: Soil pH
1d6b6639bbe1.sentence: Ultra-acidic soils (pH < 3.5) and very strongly alkaline soils (pH > 9) are rare.

91a06a70719d.title: Soil
91a06a70719d.sentence: A pH of 3.5 has one million times more hydronium ions per litre than a solution with pH of 9.5 (9.5 − 3.5 = 6 or 10^6) and is thus more acidic.

87b4262c5134.title: Soil pH
87b4262c5134.sentence: Soil pH is considered a master variable in soils as it affects many chemical processes.

c3bc62da4d93.title: Soil pH
c3bc62da4d93.sentence: It specifically affects plant nutrient availability by controlling the chemical forms of the different nutrients and influencing the chemical reactions they undergo.

179d029b663f.title: Soil pH
179d029b663f.sentence: The optimum pH range for most plants is between 5.5 and 7.5.

8a6ae4c74b1f.title: Soil pH
8a6ae4c74b1f.sentence: However, many plants have adapted to thrive at pH values outside this range.

0e52fdc7945a.title: Soil
0e52fdc7945a.sentence: Soil organisms are hindered by high acidity, and most agricultural crops do best with mineral soils of pH 6.5 and organic soils of pH 5.5.

c9cc4827640d.title: Soil
c9cc4827640d.sentence: Soils with high acidity tend to have toxic amounts of aluminium and manganese.

877d267cb12b.title: Soil
877d267cb12b.sentence: In high rainfall areas, soils tend to acidify as the basic cations are forced off the soil colloids by the mass action of hydronium ions from usual or unusual rain acidity against those attached to the colloids.

1b36c427ca8d.title: Soil
1b36c427ca8d.sentence: In low rainfall areas, unleached calcium pushes pH to 8.5 and with the addition of exchangeable sodium, soils may reach pH 10.

7cc9682e15bd.title: Soil
7cc9682e15bd.sentence: Soil pH is a function of many soil forming factors, and is generally lower (more acidic) where weathering is more advanced.

5955472d03bc.title: Soil horizon
5955472d03bc.sentence: A soil horizon is a layer parallel to the soil surface whose physical, chemical and biological characteristics differ from the layers above and beneath.

bcd69a3f6e38.title: Soil horizon
bcd69a3f6e38.sentence: A soil horizon is a result of soil-forming processes (pedogenesis).

94d2d81ffefd.title: Soil horizon
94d2d81ffefd.sentence: Layers that have not undergone such processes may be simply called "layers".

07245565d00f.title: Soil horizon
07245565d00f.sentence: Horizons are defined in many cases by obvious physical features, mainly colour and texture.

c2a777311913.title: Soil horizon
c2a777311913.sentence: These may be described both in absolute terms (particle size distribution for texture, for instance) and in terms relative to the surrounding material, i.e. "coarser" or "sandier" or "darker" than the horizons above and below.

fd2d3c3a7d05.title: Soil
fd2d3c3a7d05.sentence: Given sufficient time, an undifferentiated soil will evolve a soil profile that consists of two or more layers, referred to as soil horizons.

60c2553ee32d.title: Soil
60c2553ee32d.sentence: The horizons differ greatly in thickness and generally lack sharp boundaries; their development is dependent on the type of parent material, the processes that modify those parent materials (e.g. mineral weathering), and the soil-forming factors that influence those processes.

e0429f420b92.title: Soil
e0429f420b92.sentence: No soil profile has all the major horizons.

6ca93687650b.title: Soil
6ca93687650b.sentence: Some, called entisols, may have only one horizon or are currently considered as having no horizon, in particular incipient soils from unreclaimed mining waste deposits, moraines, volcanic cones sand dunes or alluvial terraces.

005226605176.title: Soil
005226605176.sentence: Upper soil horizons may be lacking in truncated soils following wind or water ablation, with concomitant downslope burying of soil horizons, a natural process aggravated by agricultural practices such as tillage.

9c48cbe21574.title: Soil
9c48cbe21574.sentence: The growth of trees is another source of disturbance, creating a micro-scale heterogeneity which is still visible in soil horizons once trees have died.

8db689af8eff.title: Soil horizon
8db689af8eff.sentence: Soils with a history of human interference, for instance through major earthworks or regular deep ploughing, may lack distinct horizons almost completely.

40a32251c0f5.title: Soil
40a32251c0f5.sentence: By passing from a horizon to another, from the top to the bottom of the soil profile, one goes back in time, with past events registered in soil horizons like in sediment layers.

21f17015b37a.title: Soil
21f17015b37a.sentence: Sampling pollen, testate amoebae and plant remains in soil horizons may help to reveal environmental changes (e.g. climate change, land use change) which occurred in the course of soil formation.

36e9eac9fa45.title: Soil
36e9eac9fa45.sentence: Soil horizons can be dated by several methods such as radiocarbon, using pieces of charcoal provided they are of enough size to escape pedoturbation by earthworm activity and other mechanical disturbances.

b4cfbb2db46e.title: Soil horizon
b4cfbb2db46e.sentence: In most soil classification systems, horizons are used to define soil types.

c362a235216a.title: Soil horizon
c362a235216a.sentence: The German system uses entire horizon sequences for definition.

2d4364438a0e.title: Soil horizon
2d4364438a0e.sentence: Other systems pick out certain horizons, the "diagnostic horizons", for the definition; examples are the World Reference Base for Soil Resources (WRB), the USDA soil taxonomy and the Australian Soil Classification.

0d309aa0c44c.title: Soil
0d309aa0c44c.sentence: They are labelled using a shorthand notation of letters and numbers which describe the horizon in terms of its colour, size, texture, structure, consistency, root quantity, pH, voids, boundary characteristics and presence of nodules or concretions.

b0a84907909e.title: Soil
b0a84907909e.sentence: The resistance of soil to change in pH, as a result of the addition of acid or basic material, is a measure of the buffering capacity of a soil and (for a particular soil type) increases as the CEC increases.

5b3ec31ff024.title: Soil
5b3ec31ff024.sentence: Hence, pure sand has almost no buffering ability, though soils high in colloids (whether mineral or organic) have high buffering capacity.

d52621a50ebf.title: Soil
d52621a50ebf.sentence: Buffering occurs by cation exchange and neutralisation.

eb7423b8c332.title: Soil
eb7423b8c332.sentence: The role of carbonates should be underlined, too.

2be7668995ed.title: Soil
2be7668995ed.sentence: More generally, according to pH levels, several buffer systems take precedence over each other, from calcium carbonate buffer range to iron buffer range.

8fa329cb9977.title: Soil pH
8fa329cb9977.section: Changing soil pH > Increasing pH of acidic soil
8fa329cb9977.sentence: The buffering capacity of a soil depends on the clay content of the soil, the type of clay, and the amount of organic matter present, and may be related to the soil cation exchange capacity.

ca860d3dbd7c.title: Soil pH
ca860d3dbd7c.section: Changing soil pH > Increasing pH of acidic soil
ca860d3dbd7c.sentence: Soils with high clay content will have a higher buffering capacity than soils with little clay, and soils with high organic matter will have a higher buffering capacity than those with low organic matter.

1a2556cbf2ac.title: Soil pH
1a2556cbf2ac.section: Changing soil pH > Increasing pH of acidic soil
1a2556cbf2ac.sentence: Soils with higher buffering capacity require a greater amount of lime to achieve an equivalent change in pH.

d26e8bfc0d8b.title: Soil
d26e8bfc0d8b.sentence: The amount of lime needed to neutralize a soil must take account of the amount of acid forming ions on the colloids (exchangeable acidity), not just those in the soil water solution (free acidity).

255ef6020434.title: Soil
255ef6020434.sentence: The addition of enough lime to neutralize the soil water solution will be insufficient to change the pH, as the acid forming cations stored on the soil colloids will tend to restore the original pH condition as they are pushed off those colloids by the calcium of the added lime.

bbbd951770ee.title: Soil
bbbd951770ee.sentence: Once the colloids are saturated with H3O+, the addition of any more hydronium ions or aluminum hydroxyl cations drives the pH even lower (more acidic) as the soil has been left with no buffering capacity.

7faa1ab9ecf2.title: Soil
7faa1ab9ecf2.sentence: In areas of extreme rainfall and high temperatures, clay and humus may be washed out, further reducing the buffering capacity of the soil.

a70f2cf6ff21.title: Soil pH
a70f2cf6ff21.section: Changing soil pH > Increasing pH of acidic soil
a70f2cf6ff21.sentence: The amount of limestone or chalk needed to change pH is determined by the mesh size of the lime (how finely it is ground) and the buffering capacity of the soil.

47c451d7bc15.title: Soil pH
47c451d7bc15.section: Changing soil pH > Increasing pH of acidic soil
47c451d7bc15.sentence: The buffering of soil pH is often directly related to the quantity of aluminium in soil solution and taking up exchange sites as part of the cation exchange capacity.

b81dc6f70f05.title: Soil pH
b81dc6f70f05.section: Changing soil pH > Increasing pH of acidic soil
b81dc6f70f05.sentence: Then, using the initial soil pH and the aluminium content, the amount of lime needed to raise the pH to a desired level can be calculated.

bdf2305e5a88.title: Soil color
bdf2305e5a88.sentence: Soil color is often the most visually apparent property of soil.

450ae7cecf10.title: Soil color
450ae7cecf10.sentence: While color itself does not influence the behavior or practical use of soils, it does indicate important information about soil organic matter content, mineralogy, moisture, and leaching.

f68d18275bac.title: Soil color
f68d18275bac.sentence: Soil can display a wide range of colors including brown, red, yellow, black, gray, white, and even blue or green, and vary dramatically across landscapes, between the various horizons of a soil profile, and even within a single clod of soil.

a0165479423f.title: Soil color
a0165479423f.sentence: The development and distribution of color in soil results from chemical and biological weathering, especially redox reactions.

2dc18eaba259.title: Soil color
2dc18eaba259.sentence: As the primary minerals in soil parent material weather, the elements combine into new and colorful compounds.

26205e9a3fb6.title: Soil color
26205e9a3fb6.sentence: Soil conditions produce uniform or gradual color changes, while reducing environments result in disrupted color flow with complex, mottled patterns and points of color concentration.

fc755e6698b5.title: Physical properties of soil
fc755e6698b5.sentence: Soil color is primarily influenced by soil mineralogy.

ca0afa36d12e.title: Physical properties of soil
ca0afa36d12e.sentence: Soil colour is often the first impression one has when viewing soil.

bd610bfc28b1.title: Soil color
bd610bfc28b1.sentence: Because soil color (specifically the value) varies with moisture, it may be described at both its moist and dry state.

50722300e6eb.title: Soil pH
50722300e6eb.section: Effect of soil pH on plant growth > Acid soils
50722300e6eb.sentence: Aluminium toxicity is the most widespread problem in acid soils.

a51ce7e9bb12.title: Soil pH
a51ce7e9bb12.section: Effect of soil pH on plant growth > Acid soils
a51ce7e9bb12.sentence: Aluminium is present in all soils to varying degrees, but dissolved Al3+ is toxic to plants; Al3+ is most soluble at low pH; above pH 5.0, there is little Al in soluble form in most soils.

2ee90bdaaf53.title: Soil pH
2ee90bdaaf53.section: Effect of soil pH on plant growth > Acid soils

485435665cc1.title: Soil pH
485435665cc1.section: Effect of soil pH on plant growth > Acid soils
485435665cc1.sentence: Lateral roots and root tips become thickened, roots lack fine branching, and root tips may turn brown.

a46d4270c3bd.title: Soil pH
a46d4270c3bd.section: Effect of soil pH on plant growth > Acid soils
a46d4270c3bd.sentence: Thereafter aluminium is known to interfere with many physiological processes including the uptake and transport of calcium and other essential nutrients, cell division, cell wall formation, and enzyme activity.

25e1ec4c5995.title: Soil pH
25e1ec4c5995.section: Effect of soil pH on plant growth > Acid soils
25e1ec4c5995.sentence: Plants grown in acid soils can experience a variety of stresses including aluminium (Al), hydrogen (H), and/or manganese (Mn) toxicity, as well as nutrient deficiencies of calcium (Ca) and magnesium (Mg).

9ee675330c92.title: Soil pH
9ee675330c92.section: Effect of soil pH on plant growth > Acid soils
9ee675330c92.sentence: Manganese, like aluminium, becomes increasingly soluble as pH drops, and Mn toxicity symptoms can be seen at pH levels below 5.6.

cf2d90ea7fc8.title: Soil pH
cf2d90ea7fc8.section: Effect of soil pH on plant growth > Acid soils
cf2d90ea7fc8.sentence: Acid rain is the main factor to mobilize aluminium from natural sources and the main reason for the environmental effects of aluminium.

b15834c40f8b.title: Soil pH
b15834c40f8b.sentence: The shift from toxic to non-toxic forms of aluminium around pH 5 marks the passage from acid-tolerance to acid-intolerance, with few changes in the species composition of soil communities above this threshold, even in calcareous soils.

7541eabb7f16.title: Soil pH
7541eabb7f16.sentence: The pH of a natural soil depends on the mineral composition of the parent material of the soil, and the weathering reactions undergone by that parent material.

c01512cf54b8.title: Soil pH
c01512cf54b8.sentence: In warm, humid environments, soil acidification occurs over time as the products of weathering are leached by water moving laterally or downwards through the soil.

6b94ddd8c3d0.title: Soil pH
6b94ddd8c3d0.sentence: In dry climates, however, soil weathering and leaching are less intense and soil pH is often neutral or alkaline.

2f6da4ec0e0b.title: Soil pH
2f6da4ec0e0b.section: Factors affecting soil pH > Sources of acidity
2f6da4ec0e0b.sentence: - Rainfall: Average rainfall has a pH of 5.6 and is moderately acidic due to dissolved atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO 2) that combines with water to form carbonic acid (H 2CO 3).

bd7332bd1ba1.title: Soil pH
bd7332bd1ba1.section: Factors affecting soil pH > Sources of acidity
bd7332bd1ba1.sentence: When this water flows through the soil it results in the leaching of basic cations such as bicarbonates; this increases the percentage of Al3+ and H+ relative to other cations.

5836339a5ea7.title: Soil pH
5836339a5ea7.section: Factors affecting soil pH > Sources of acidity
5836339a5ea7.sentence: - Root respiration and decomposition of organic matter by microorganisms release CO 2 which increases the carbonic acid (H 2CO 3) concentration and subsequent leaching.

f7ecc028e559.title: Soil pH
f7ecc028e559.section: Factors affecting soil pH > Sources of acidity
f7ecc028e559.sentence: - Plant growth: Plants take up nutrients in the form of ions (e.g. NO− 3, NH+ 4, Ca2+, H 2PO− 4), and they often take up more cations than anions, in particular in legumes.

883e819fca02.title: Soil pH
883e819fca02.section: Factors affecting soil pH > Sources of acidity
883e819fca02.sentence: In order to compensate for the extra positive charge, they will release H+ ions from the root.

c5dab05392ba.title: Soil pH
c5dab05392ba.section: Factors affecting soil pH > Sources of acidity
c5dab05392ba.sentence: - Fertilizer use: Ammonium (NH+ 4) fertilizers react in the soil by the process of nitrification to form nitrate (NO− 3), and in the process release H+ ions.

230428725adf.title: Soil pH
230428725adf.section: Factors affecting soil pH > Sources of acidity
230428725adf.sentence: - Acid rain: The burning of fossil fuels releases oxides of sulfur and nitrogen into the atmosphere.

87c85bebe881.title: Soil pH
87c85bebe881.section: Factors affecting soil pH > Sources of acidity
87c85bebe881.sentence: - Mine spoil: Severely acidic conditions can form in soils near some mine spoils due to the oxidation of pyrite.

3984b671b55a.title: Soil pH
3984b671b55a.section: Factors affecting soil pH > Sources of acidity
3984b671b55a.sentence: - Acid sulfate soils formed naturally in waterlogged coastal and estuarine environments can become highly acidic when drained or excavated.

1464bb373383.title: Soil pH
1464bb373383.section: Factors affecting soil pH > Sources of alkalinity
1464bb373383.sentence: - Weathering of silicate, aluminosilicate and carbonate minerals containing Na+, Ca2+, Mg2+ and K+

72ae23b0dc2c.title: Soil pH
72ae23b0dc2c.section: Factors affecting soil pH > Sources of alkalinity
72ae23b0dc2c.sentence: - Addition of silicate, aluminosilicate and carbonate minerals to soils; this may happen by deposition of material eroded elsewhere by wind or water, or by mixing of the soil with less weathered material (such as the addition of limestone to acid soils)

cf6a2616c7ca.title: Soil pH
cf6a2616c7ca.section: Factors affecting soil pH > Sources of alkalinity
cf6a2616c7ca.sentence: - Addition of water containing dissolved bicarbonates (as occurs when irrigating with high-bicarbonate waters)

0bf3497ca2fa.title: Soil pH
0bf3497ca2fa.section: Factors affecting soil pH > Sources of alkalinity
0bf3497ca2fa.sentence: The accumulation of alkalinity in a soil (as carbonates and bicarbonates of Na, K, Ca and Mg) occurs when there is insufficient water flowing through the soils to leach soluble salts.

61ad1760a0b6.title: Soil pH
61ad1760a0b6.section: Factors affecting soil pH > Sources of alkalinity
61ad1760a0b6.sentence: This may be due to arid conditions, or poor internal soil drainage; in these situations most of the water that enters the soil is transpired (taken up by plants) or evaporates, rather than flowing through the soil.

ab03f897aae6.sentence: Calcareous soils may vary in pH from 7.0 to 9.5, depending on the degree to which Ca2+ or Na+ dominate the soluble cations.

ccbb7dce3f52.title: Soil pH

881d13d62041.title: Soil pH

9dc27b22c71c.title: Soil pH

8299792cc3b2.title: Soil pH
8299792cc3b2.sentence: Calcifuge plants (those that prefer an acidic soil) include Erica, Rhododendron and nearly all other Ericaceae species, many birch (Betula), foxglove (Digitalis), gorse (Ulex spp.), and Scots pine (Pinus sylvestris).

68946dcafb43.title: Soil pH
68946dcafb43.sentence: Calcicole (lime loving) plants include ash trees (Fraxinus spp.), honeysuckle (Lonicera), Buddleja, dogwoods (Cornus spp.), lilac (Syringa) and Clematis species.

f9aa32c539f7.title: Soil pH

32f25b6ed788.title: Soil pH

5586c5ad4dbe.title: Soil pH

9d0ef759eab8.title: Soil pH

496ea9875693.title: Soil pH

1e5ffca1e167.title: Soil pH

ae5a0d5a58fb.sentence: Because roots are damaged, nutrient uptake is reduced, and deficiencies of the macronutrients (nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, calcium and magnesium) are frequently encountered in very strongly acidic to ultra-acidic soils (pH<5.0).

d85ea37d162a.title: Soil pH
d85ea37d162a.section: Effect of soil pH on plant growth > Nutrient availability in relation to soil pH
d85ea37d162a.sentence: Molybdenum availability is increased at higher pH.

b44853c3f9b8.title: Soil pH

b44853c3f9b8.sentence: Zinc, iron, copper and manganese show decreased availability at higher pH (increased sorption at higher pH).

1f36cf7f690c.title: Soil
1f36cf7f690c.sentence: High pH results in low micro-nutrient mobility, but water-soluble chelates of those nutrients can correct the deficit.

88446d32bb46.title: Soil pH
88446d32bb46.section: Effect of soil pH on plant growth > Nutrient availability in relation to soil pH
88446d32bb46.sentence: The prevailing view in the 1940s and 1950s was that P availability was maximized near neutrality (soil pH 6.5–7.5), and decreased at higher and lower pH.

a494204e07f9.title: Soil pH
a494204e07f9.section: Effect of soil pH on plant growth > Nutrient availability in relation to soil pH
a494204e07f9.sentence: Interactions of phosphorus with pH in the moderately to slightly acidic range (pH 5.5–6.5) are, however, far more complex than is suggested by this view.

71cc1189e263.title: Soil pH
71cc1189e263.section: Effect of soil pH on plant growth > Nutrient availability in relation to soil pH
71cc1189e263.sentence: Laboratory tests, glasshouse trials and field trials have indicated that increases in pH within this range may increase, decrease, or have no effect on P availability to plants.

2c358e10c9a9.title: Soil pH
2c358e10c9a9.section: Changing soil pH > Decreasing the pH of alkaline soil
2c358e10c9a9.sentence: However, in high-pH soils with a high calcium carbonate content (more than 2%), attempting to reduce the pH with acids can be very costly and ineffective.

62b2b023832b.title: Soil pH
62b2b023832b.section: Changing soil pH > Decreasing the pH of alkaline soil
62b2b023832b.sentence: In such cases, it is often more efficient to add phosphorus, iron, manganese, copper, or zinc instead because deficiencies of these nutrients are the most common reasons for poor plant growth in calcareous soils.

6a1769875a2b.title: Soil horizon
6a1769875a2b.sentence: Master horizons (main horizons) are indicated by capital letters.

f4a8c0a7a32e.title: Soil horizon
f4a8c0a7a32e.sentence: Hard bedrock is mostly denominated R. Most individual systems defined more horizons and layers than just these five.

39a8daad4cc9.title: Soil horizon
39a8daad4cc9.sentence: Many soils have an organic surface layer, which is denominated with a capital letter "O" (letters may differ depending on the system).

c745d613770e.title: Soil horizon

fb959ee8ead4.title: Soil horizon
fb959ee8ead4.sentence: A) Surface soil: Layer of mineral soil with most organic matter accumulation and soil life.

5e6214dc7e7d.title: Soil horizon
5e6214dc7e7d.sentence: There is also an "E" horizon the leaching layer of soil.

3e5591529e44.title: Soil horizon
3e5591529e44.sentence: If a well-developed subsoil horizon as a result of soil formation exists, it is generally called a B horizon.

12f68f8177ec.title: Soil horizon

d5838f12b7fc.title: Soil horizon

edd1a224dedf.title: Soil horizon
edd1a224dedf.sentence: Unlike the above layers, R horizons consist largely of continuous masses (as opposed to boulders) of hard rock that cannot be excavated by hand.

271e78e566b6.title: Soil
271e78e566b6.sentence: Mature soil profiles typically include three basic master horizons: A, B, and C. The solum normally includes the A and B horizons.

abd6a9b6d7db.title: Soil horizon

ed62334d0c41.sentence: The pH of an alkaline soil can be reduced by adding acidifying agents or acidic organic materials.

f1e03c9b8754.section: Changing soil pH > Decreasing the pH of alkaline soil
f1e03c9b8754.sentence: Elemental sulfur (90–99% S) has been used at application rates of 300–500 kg/ha (270–450 lb/acre): it slowly oxidises in the soil to form sulfuric acid.

436dc5a0d4b9.title: Soil pH
436dc5a0d4b9.section: Changing soil pH > Decreasing the pH of alkaline soil
436dc5a0d4b9.sentence: Acidifying fertilizers, such as ammonium sulfate, ammonium nitrate and urea, can help to reduce the pH of soil because ammonium oxidises to form nitric acid.

67f3abc1e4fb.section: Changing soil pH > Decreasing the pH of alkaline soil
67f3abc1e4fb.sentence: Acidifying organic materials include peat or sphagnum peat moss.

c2fe7f2e260b.title: Soil pH
c2fe7f2e260b.sentence: In general terms, different plant species are adapted to soils of different pH ranges.

9cf18dc113cd.title: Soil pH
9cf18dc113cd.sentence: While both very low and very high pH values are detrimental to plant growth, there is an increasing trend of plant biodiversity along the range from extremely acidic (pH 3.5) to strongly alkaline (pH 9) soils, i.e. there are more calcicole than calcifuge species, at least in terrestrial environments.

b5e0149db386.title: Soil pH
b5e0149db386.sentence: Some species (like Pinus radiata and Opuntia ficus-indica) tolerate only a narrow range in soil pH, whereas others (such as Vetiveria zizanioides) tolerate a very wide pH range.

236557cdc7b8.title: Soil pH
236557cdc7b8.sentence: However, a plant may be intolerant of a particular pH in some soils as a result of a particular mechanism, and that mechanism may not apply in other soils.

c4215da14d33.title: Soil pH
c4215da14d33.sentence: For example, a soil low in molybdenum may not be suitable for soybean plants at pH 5.5, but soils with sufficient molybdenum allow optimal growth at that pH.

dd2a128b469d.title: Soil pH
dd2a128b469d.sentence: Another confounding factor is that different varieties of the same species often have different suitable soil pH ranges.

e3be8a4337da.title: Soil pH
e3be8a4337da.sentence: Plant breeders can use this to breed varieties that can tolerate conditions that are otherwise considered unsuitable for that species: examples are projects to breed aluminium-tolerant and manganese-tolerant varieties of cereal crops for food production in strongly acidic soils.

d590a1b4f67d.title: Soil pH
d590a1b4f67d.sentence: Soil biota (soil microflora, soil animals) are sensitive to soil pH, either directly upon contact or after soil ingestion or indirectly through the various soil properties to which pH contributes (e.g. nutrient status, metal toxicity, humus form).

b10ece945216.title: Soil pH
b10ece945216.section: Effects of soil biota on soil pH
b10ece945216.sentence: Soil biota affect soil pH directly through excretion, and indirectly by acting on the physical environment.

99468f7458a0.title: Soil pH
99468f7458a0.sentence: According to the various physiological and behavioural adaptations of soil biota, the species composition of soil microbial and animal communities varies with soil pH.

3573558c0b12.title: Soil pH
3573558c0b12.sentence: At low pH, the oxidative stress induced by aluminium (Al3+) affects soil animals the body of which is not protected by the thick chitinous exoskeleton of arthropods, and thus are in more direct contact with the soil solution, e.g. protists, nematodes, rotifers (microfauna), enchytraeids (mesofauna) and earthworms (macrofauna).

7121ad39c618.title: Soil pH
7121ad39c618.section: Effects of soil biota on soil pH
7121ad39c618.sentence: Many soil fungi, although not all of them, acidify the soil by excreting oxalic acid, which precipitates calcium, forming insoluble crystals of calcium oxalate and thus depriving the soil solution from this necessary element.

a18b2f3b21e3.title: Soil pH
a18b2f3b21e3.section: Effects of soil biota on soil pH
a18b2f3b21e3.sentence: On the opposite side, earthworms exert a buffering effect on soil pH through their excretion of mucus, endowed with amphoteric properties and exhibiting weak alkalinity (7.5 < pH < 8).

73ea9bd7743c.title: Soil pH
73ea9bd7743c.section: Effects of soil biota on soil pH
73ea9bd7743c.sentence: By mixing organic matter with mineral matter, in particular clay particles, and by adding mucus as a glue for some of them, burrowing soil animals, e.g. fossorial rodents, moles, earthworms, termites, some millipedes and fly larvae, contribute to decrease the natural acidity of raw organic matter, as observed in the formation of mull humus.

a9ed2702354d.title: Soil pH
a9ed2702354d.section: Water availability in relation to soil pH
a9ed2702354d.sentence: The higher the pH in the soil, the less water available to be distributed to the plants and organisms that depend on it.

98f489160d57.title: Soil pH
98f489160d57.section: Water availability in relation to soil pH
98f489160d57.sentence: Strongly alkaline soils are sodic and dispersive, with slow infiltration, low hydraulic conductivity and poor available water capacity.

b65ace59ad43.title: Soil pH
b65ace59ad43.section: Water availability in relation to soil pH
b65ace59ad43.sentence: Plant growth is severely restricted because aeration is poor when the soil is wet, while in dry conditions, plant-available water is rapidly depleted and the soils become hard and cloddy (high soil strength).

165aa4bca62d.title: Soil pH
165aa4bca62d.section: Water availability in relation to soil pH
165aa4bca62d.sentence: In strongly acidic soils, aluminium toxicity severely limits root growth, and moisture stress can occur even when the soil is relatively moist.

340911ab7885.sentence: As with the A horizon, the B horizon may be divided into B1, B2, and B3 types under the Australian system.

3c0426a76b10.sentence: These horizons are also heavily organic but are distinct from O horizons in that they form under waterlogged conditions.

581de7c531f4.sentence: While this can add necessary depth to a field description, workers should bear in mind that excessive division of a soil profile into narrow sub-horizons should be avoided.

0af7c8dfd037.sentence: - Organic layers consist of organic material: Have ≥ 20% organic carbon, not consisting of artefacts (related to the fine earth plus the dead plant residues of any length and a diameter ≤ 5 mm) and do not form part of a litter layer.

5736421935c1.sentence: - Organotechnic layers consist of organotechnic material: Have ≥ 35% (by volume, related to the whole soil) artefacts containing ≥ 20% organic carbon; and < 20% organic carbon, not consisting of artefacts (related to the fine earth plus the dead plant residues of any length and a diameter ≤ 5 mm).

65f8ab6afb2d.sentence: - Mineral layers are all other layers.

0fd37dc21785.title: Soil horizon

d394c8115b9a.title: Soil horizon

d394c8115b9a.sentence: The soil surface (0 cm) is by convention the surface of the soil after removing, if present, the litter layer and, if present, below a layer of living plants (e.g. living mosses).

3925236cc0c1.title: Soil horizon
3925236cc0c1.section: Horizons and layers according to the World Reference Base for Soil Resources
3925236cc0c1.sentence: A litter layer is a loose layer that contains > 90% (by volume, related to the fine earth plus all dead plant residues) recognizable dead plant tissues (e.g. undecomposed leaves).

c93711e78b38.title: Soil horizon
c93711e78b38.section: Horizons and layers according to the World Reference Base for Soil Resources
c93711e78b38.sentence: The designation consists of a capital letter (master symbol), which in most cases is followed by one or more lowercase letters (suffixes).

05a501b1388d.title: Soil horizon
05a501b1388d.section: Horizons and layers according to the World Reference Base for Soil Resources > Master symbols
05a501b1388d.sentence: H: Organic or organotechnic layer, not forming part of a litter layer; water saturation > 30 consecutive days in most years or drained; generally regarded as peat layer or organic limnic layer.

6dddbe345015.title: Soil horizon
6dddbe345015.section: Horizons and layers according to the World Reference Base for Soil Resources > Master symbols
6dddbe345015.sentence: O: Organic horizon or organotechnic layer, not forming part of a litter layer; water saturation ≤ 30 consecutive days in most years and not drained; generally regarded as non-peat and non-limnic horizon.

370044ea18b8.title: Soil horizon
