370044ea18b8.sentence: A: Mineral horizon at the mineral soil surface or buried; contains organic matter that has at least partly been modified in-situ; soil structure and/or structural elements created by cultivation in ≥ 50% (by volume, related to the fine earth), i.e. rock structure, if present, in < 50% (by volume).

7f03e0dbb5ec.title: Soil horizon
7f03e0dbb5ec.section: Horizons and layers according to the World Reference Base for Soil Resources > Master symbols
7f03e0dbb5ec.sentence: E: Mineral horizon; has lost by downward movement within the soil (vertically or laterally) one or more of the following: Fe, Al, and/or Mn species; clay minerals; organic matter.

d16ad5b0e64e.title: Soil horizon
d16ad5b0e64e.section: Horizons and layers according to the World Reference Base for Soil Resources > Master symbols
d16ad5b0e64e.sentence: B: Mineral horizon that has (at least originally) formed below an A or E horizon; rock structure, if present, in < 50% (by volume, related to the fine earth); one or more of the following processes of soil formation:

3406eb423925.title: Soil horizon
3406eb423925.section: Horizons and layers according to the World Reference Base for Soil Resources > Master symbols
3406eb423925.sentence: C: Mineral layer; unconsolidated (can be cut with a spade when moist), or consolidated and more fractured than the R layer; no soil formation, or soil formation that does not meet the criteria of the A, E, and B horizon.

f87cb3859c20.title: Soil horizon
f87cb3859c20.section: Horizons and layers according to the World Reference Base for Soil Resources > Master symbols
f87cb3859c20.sentence: R: Consolidated rock; air-dry or drier specimens, when placed in water, will not slake within 24 hours; fractures, if present, occupy < 10% (by volume, related to the whole soil); not resulting from the cementation of a soil horizon.

095342c8590b.title: Soil horizon
095342c8590b.section: Horizons and layers according to the World Reference Base for Soil Resources > Master symbols
095342c8590b.sentence: I: ≥ 75% ice (by volume, related to the whole soil), permanent, below an H, O, A, E, B or C layer.

2ee624a20606.title: Soil horizon
2ee624a20606.section: Horizons and layers according to the World Reference Base for Soil Resources > Master symbols
2ee624a20606.sentence: W: Permanent water above the soil surface or between layers, may be seasonally frozen.

33bab993d40a.title: Soil color
33bab993d40a.sentence: Most soil survey organizations utilize the Munsell color system to decrease the subjectivity in evaluating color.

efcba9da45d1.title: Munsell color system
efcba9da45d1.sentence: The Munsell color system is a color space that specifies colors based on three properties of color: hue (basic color), value (lightness), and chroma (color intensity).

080244de1ba5.title: Munsell color system
080244de1ba5.sentence: It was created by Albert H. Munsell in the first decade of the 20th century and adopted by the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) as the official color system for soil research in the 1930s.

c11bdb32df7f.title: Soil color
c11bdb32df7f.sentence: This system was developed by Albert Munsell, a painter in the early 20th century, to describe the full-color spectrum, though the specially adapted Munsell soil color charts commonly used by soil scientists only include the most relevant colors for soil.

2e82649c89f8.title: Soil color
2e82649c89f8.sentence: - Hue: indicates the dominant spectral (i.e., rainbow) color, which in the soil is generally yellow or red.

6bc82e6ad4e2.title: Soil color
6bc82e6ad4e2.sentence: Each page of the Munsell soil color book displays a different hue.

8af8028cc738.title: Munsell color system
8af8028cc738.sentence: Since the first rendition of the Munsell color system, each horizontal circle is divided into five principal hues: Red, Yellow, Green, Blue, and Purple, along with 5 intermediate hues between adjacent principal hues: YR, GY, BG, PB, and RP.

3c0fbc5ce4ee.title: Munsell color system
3c0fbc5ce4ee.sentence: In later renditions, these 10 principal and intermediate colors were further subdivided into 10 steps each, so that at least 100 hues are definable.

812eda2b91c4.title: Munsell color system
812eda2b91c4.sentence: In practice, color charts conventionally specify 40 hues, in increments of 2.5, progressing as for example 10R to 2.5YR.

fefd4f8783ff.title: Soil color
fefd4f8783ff.sentence: The value increases from the bottom of each page to the top, with lower numbers representing darker colors.

9626a5f67df7.title: Soil color
9626a5f67df7.sentence: Chroma increases from left to right on each page, with higher numbers representing more vivid or saturated colors.

6628bd2617e1.title: Soil color
6628bd2617e1.sentence: Color with a chroma of 0 would be neutral gray.

3f4cdde030c2.title: Soil color
3f4cdde030c2.sentence: A general color name, such as yellowish brown or light gray, often accompanies the Munsell notation for soil samples.

e804b20764ad.title: Soil color
e804b20764ad.sentence: These qualitative descriptors correspond to one or more color chips in the Munsell soil color books; however, they are not formally part of the broader Munsell color system.

84332afa9976.title: Soil color
84332afa9976.sentence: Soil is considered moist when adding water no longer changes the soil color or as "dry" when the soil is air dried.

b3c75b4bfb3a.title: Munsell color system
b3c75b4bfb3a.sentence: A color is fully specified by listing the three numbers for hue, value, and chroma in that order.

6afec23c53d0.title: Cecil (soil)
6afec23c53d0.sentence: Bt2—26 to 42 inches (1,100 mm); red (10R 4/8) clay; few fine prominent yellowish red (5YR 5/8) mottles; moderate medium subangular blocky structure; firm; sticky, plastic; common clay films on faces of peds; few fine flakes of mica; very strongly acid; gradual wavy boundary.

b4a16e482bf2.title: Munsell color system
b4a16e482bf2.sentence: An achromatic color is specified by the syntax N V/.

cbf16797feb7.title: Munsell color system
cbf16797feb7.sentence: For example, a medium grey is specified by "N 5/".

b8953884096f.title: Soil color
b8953884096f.sentence: Red colors often indicate iron accumulation or oxidation in oxygen-rich, well-aerated soils.

6d0927a63703.title: Soil color
6d0927a63703.sentence: Dark brown or black colors typically indicate that the soil has a high organic matter content.

f60ad28397cd.title: Soil color
f60ad28397cd.sentence: Organic matter coats mineral soil particles, which masks or darkens the natural mineral colors.

e62e2146b3f2.title: Soil color
e62e2146b3f2.sentence: Additionally, soils which accumulate charcoal exhibit a black color.

e4827735de8b.title: Soil color
e4827735de8b.sentence: Yellow soils may indicate iron accumulation as well, though in less oxygen-rich environments than red soils.

a6a06b9fa68d.title: Soil color
a6a06b9fa68d.sentence: Soil in anaerobic, saturated environments may appear gray or blue in color due to redox reduction and/or depletion of iron.

710bd889e3dc.title: Soil color
710bd889e3dc.sentence: Iron reduction may impart greenish gray colors, though certain minerals including glauconite, melanterite, and celadonite can also give soil a green color.

45dc7af4d3d9.title: Soil color
45dc7af4d3d9.sentence: White colors are common in soils with salt, carbonate, or calcite accumulations, which often occur in arid environments.

36c21a79b1ef.title: Soil color
36c21a79b1ef.sentence: Jarosite accumulation can also create yellow soil color and may be found in salt marshes, sulfide ore deposits, acid mine tailings, and other acidic soils.

e2588fe131a3.title: Soil color
e2588fe131a3.sentence: Sodium content also influences the depth of organic matter and therefore the soil color.

111bf69f282c.title: Soil color
111bf69f282c.sentence: Sodium causes organic matter particles such as humus to disperse more readily and reach more minerals.

8d51abb68c0c.title: Soil horizon
8d51abb68c0c.sentence: B) Subsoil: This layer normally has less organic matter than the A horizon, so its colour is mainly derived from iron oxides.

5539999aa430.title: Soil horizon
5539999aa430.section: Horizons according to the Australian Soil and Land Survey Field Handbook (2009) > Horizons
5539999aa430.sentence: It is usually brownish or reddish due to the iron oxides, which increases the chroma of the subsoil to a degree that it can be distinguished from the other horizons.

a9ffefa2cc46.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/02%3A_What_Is_Organic_Matter_and_Why_Is_It_So_Important/2.03%3A_Organic_Matter_And_Natural_Cycles
a9ffefa2cc46.section: The Carbon Cycle > Color and Organic Matter
a9ffefa2cc46.sentence: In Illinois, a handheld chart has been developed to allow people to estimate percent of soil organic matter.

1d6444daddb8.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/02%3A_What_Is_Organic_Matter_and_Why_Is_It_So_Important/2.03%3A_Organic_Matter_And_Natural_Cycles
1d6444daddb8.section: The Carbon Cycle > Color and Organic Matter
1d6444daddb8.sentence: Their darkest soils, almost black, indicate 3.5–7% organic matter.

ec34c16209ce.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/02%3A_What_Is_Organic_Matter_and_Why_Is_It_So_Important/2.03%3A_Organic_Matter_And_Natural_Cycles
ec34c16209ce.section: The Carbon Cycle > Color and Organic Matter
ec34c16209ce.sentence: A dark brown soil indicates 2–3%, and a yellowish brown soil indicates 1.5–2.5% organic matter.

1e687a62e8c2.title: Soil color
1e687a62e8c2.sentence: This often exposes the light gray colors of bare silicate minerals, and soils with a low chroma from iron reduction or depletion are said to be gleyed.

0664fc11c9ab.title: Soil morphology
0664fc11c9ab.sentence: When iron reduction and/or depletion makes gray the dominant matrix color, the soil is said to be gleyed.

f2b5092334fd.title: Soil color
f2b5092334fd.sentence: In anaerobic soils, microbes reduce iron from the ferric (Fe3+) to the ferrous (Fe2+) form.

68c9d8bcd67e.title: Soil color
68c9d8bcd67e.sentence: Manganese may also be reduced from the manganic (Mn4+) to the manganous (Mn2+) form, though iron reduction is more common in soil.

43dd90043c87.title: Soil color
43dd90043c87.sentence: The reduced iron compounds cause poorly drained soil to appear gray or blue, and because reduced iron is soluble in water, it may be removed from the soil during prolonged saturation.

6142557dccfc.title: Canadian system of soil classification
6142557dccfc.sentence: As the soil dries and oxygen re-enters, the reduced iron may be oxidized locally to bright yellow-brown spots (mottles).

0ebefc7ee3c2.title: Gleysol
0ebefc7ee3c2.sentence: The presence of reddish or orange mottles indicates localised re-oxidation of ferrous salts in the soil matrix, and is often associated with root channels, animal burrows, or cracking of the soil material during dry spells.

54b74e2d5a87.title: Solum
54b74e2d5a87.sentence: Gleyed soil material begins in some soils a few centimeters below the surface and continues practically unchanged to a depth of many meters.

a3d4323c6f8c.title: Gleysol
a3d4323c6f8c.sentence: The term gley, or glei, is derived from Ukrainian: глей, romanized: hlei, and was introduced into scientific terminology in 1905 by the Ukrainian scientist Georgy Vysotsky.

4e3a91ad3bcc.title: Core sample
4e3a91ad3bcc.sentence: A core sample is a cylindrical section of (usually) a naturally occurring substance.

058caf6f0720.title: Core sample
058caf6f0720.sentence: Most core samples are obtained by drilling with special drills into the substance, such as sediment or rock, with a hollow steel tube, called a core drill.

3e89a43a3e63.title: Core sample
3e89a43a3e63.sentence: In the coring process, the sample is pushed more or less intact into the tube.

fd1b449930f7.title: Core sample
fd1b449930f7.sentence: Removed from the tube in the laboratory, it is inspected and analyzed by different techniques and equipment depending on the type of data desired.

3e50fc8cfa13.title: Core sample
3e50fc8cfa13.sentence: - Coring by hand can be done with a variety of instruments, such as a Russian Peat Corer, a handheld piston corer or simply a hollow tube.

d7245b642e98.title: Core sample
d7245b642e98.sentence: The advantages of coring by hand are low costs and quick operation, but a handheld corer will only reach limited depths, ranging from a few decimeters in clay soils to a few meters in soft lake sediments.

cbbc803fd808.title: Core sample
cbbc803fd808.sentence: The mechanical forces imposed on the core sample by the tool frequently lead to fracture of the core and loss of less-competent intervals, which can greatly complicate the interpretation of the core.

589154ca5c19.title: Core sample
589154ca5c19.sentence: The method may be faster and use less water than core drilling, but does not produce cores of relatively undisturbed material, so less information on the rock structure can be derived from analysis.

cad221d44ce1.title: Core sample
cad221d44ce1.sentence: Once dated, it gives valuable information about changes of climate and terrain.

d6dff6af3c31.title: Core sample
d6dff6af3c31.sentence: For example, cores in the ocean floor, soil and ice have altered the view of the geologic history of the Pleistocene entirely.

3c2f6030cc8f.title: Trial pit
3c2f6030cc8f.sentence: A trial pit (or test pit) is an excavation of ground in order to study or sample the composition and structure of the subsurface, usually dug during a site investigation, a soil survey or a geological survey.

11658ada590d.title: Trial pit
11658ada590d.sentence: Trial pits are dug before the construction.

06fa65e652f8.title: Trial pit
06fa65e652f8.sentence: They are dug to determine the geology and the water table of that site.

edf8b8d98715.title: Trial pit
edf8b8d98715.sentence: Trial pits are usually between 1 and 4 metres deep, and are dug either by hand or using a mechanical digger.

c9dcd9c8760b.title: Trial pit
c9dcd9c8760b.sentence: Building and construction regulations clearly state that any trial pits that concede deeper than 1.2 metres should be secured against structural collapse, if they are to be entered by people.

04e054e69201.title: Bedrock
04e054e69201.sentence: In geology, bedrock is the solid rock that lies under weathered rock and unconsolidated or loose superficial deposits (together known as regolith) in the near surface part of Earth's crust or the crust of another terrestrial planet.

18b2fe0189e3.title: Bedrock
18b2fe0189e3.sentence: An exposed portion of bedrock is often called an outcrop.

7c35d5e0af91.title: Bedrock
7c35d5e0af91.sentence: The top of the bedrock is known as rockhead.

66f7a7b2abdb.title: Bedrock
66f7a7b2abdb.sentence: The area where bedrock and these overlying materials meet is called rockhead.

49e7aeb97365.title: Bedrock
49e7aeb97365.sentence: The surface of the bedrock beneath the soil cover (regolith) is also known as rockhead in engineering geology, and its identification by digging, drilling or geophysical methods is an important task in most civil engineering projects.

97a25489dd0e.title: Bedrock
97a25489dd0e.sentence: Superficial deposits can be very thick, such that the bedrock lies hundreds of meters below the surface.

abc377ed2a54.title: Bedrock
abc377ed2a54.sentence: Exposed bedrock experiences weathering, which may be physical or chemical, and which alters the structure of the rock to leave it susceptible to erosion.

b690e6d6e807.title: Bedrock
b690e6d6e807.sentence: Bedrock may also experience subsurface weathering at its upper boundary, forming saprolite.

a4ba15ad0560.title: Bedrock
a4ba15ad0560.sentence: Rock fragments can disconnect from the underlying bedrock, where they are found within a weathering or soil profile as floaters.

1e34f979db28.title: Bedrock
1e34f979db28.sentence: A geological map of an area will usually show the distribution of differing bedrock types, rock that would be exposed at the surface if all soil or other superficial deposits were removed.

051264edfde6.title: Bedrock
051264edfde6.sentence: Where superficial deposits are so thick that the underlying bedrock cannot be reliably mapped, the superficial deposits will be mapped instead (for example, as alluvium).

55d5a80e0393.title: Superficial deposits
55d5a80e0393.sentence: All pre-Quaternary deposits are referred to as bedrock.

20d092d3d166.title: Regolith
20d092d3d166.sentence: Regolith (/ˈrɛɡəlɪθ/) is a blanket of unconsolidated, loose, heterogeneous superficial deposits covering solid rock.

2e2c2cdcbb92.title: Regolith
2e2c2cdcbb92.sentence: It includes dust, broken rocks, and other related materials and is present on Earth, the Moon, Mars, some asteroids, and other terrestrial planets and moons.

da306c584156.title: Regolith
da306c584156.sentence: The American geologist George P. Merrill first defined the term in 1897, writing:

b926ccdddcf4.title: Regolith
b926ccdddcf4.sentence: The term regolith combines two Greek words: rhegos (ῥῆγος), 'blanket', and lithos (λίθος), 'rock'.

cb8d69b4ad96.title: Regolith
cb8d69b4ad96.sentence: This entire mantle of unconsolidated material, whatever its nature or origin, it is proposed to call the regolith.

1e822a27a273.title: Regolith
1e822a27a273.sentence: Regolith on Earth originates from weathering and biological processes.

b7f1a056011e.title: Regolith
b7f1a056011e.sentence: Regolith can vary from being essentially absent to hundreds of metres in thickness.

cc651d1bfc69.title: Regolith
cc651d1bfc69.sentence: Its age can vary from instantaneous (for an ash fall or alluvium just deposited) to hundreds of millions of years old (regolith of Precambrian age occurs in parts of Australia, though this may have been buried and subsequently exhumed.)

7a07061beea7.title: Regolith
7a07061beea7.sentence: The uppermost part of the regolith, which typically contains significant organic matter, is more conventionally referred to as soil.

493a4d23fb5f.title: Regolith
493a4d23fb5f.sentence: - alluvium and other transported cover, including that transported by aeolian, glacial, marine, and gravity flow processes.

99ded1b11a13.title: Regolith
99ded1b11a13.sentence: - volcanic ash and lava flows that are interbedded with unconsolidated material

98d4badd2b8f.title: Regolith
98d4badd2b8f.sentence: - duricrust, formed by cementation of soils, saprolith and transported material like clays, silicates, iron oxides, oxyhydroxides, carbonates, sulfates and less common agents, into indurated layers resistant to weathering and erosion.

3232fa0dacbf.title: Regolith
3232fa0dacbf.sentence: - biota and organic components derived from it.

9258d338a4c5.title: Regolith
9258d338a4c5.sentence: The presence of regolith is one of the important factors for most life, since few plants can grow on or within solid rock and animals would be unable to burrow or build shelter without loose material.

d1d1d68cbe56.title: Regolith
d1d1d68cbe56.sentence: Regolith is also important to engineers constructing buildings, roads and other civil works.

cfe0a920a5ff.title: Regolith
cfe0a920a5ff.sentence: Regolith may host mineral deposits, such as mineral sands, calcrete uranium, and lateritic nickel deposits.

9bd97230a9a9.title: Regolith
9bd97230a9a9.sentence: The regolith is also an important source of construction material, including sand, gravel, crushed stone, lime, and gypsum.

70f4ef262a86.title: Regolith
70f4ef262a86.sentence: The regolith is the zone through which aquifers are recharged and through which aquifer discharge occurs.

275035229ad0.title: Saprolite
275035229ad0.sentence: Saprolite (from Greek σαπρος (sapros) = putrid + λιθος (lithos) = rock) is a chemically weathered rock (literally, it means "rotten rock").

df85552d355c.title: Saprolite
df85552d355c.sentence: Saprolites form in the lower zones of soil profiles and represent deep weathering of the bedrock surface.

864d81b95437.title: Residuum (geology)
864d81b95437.sentence: Saprolite is commonly referring to weathered material retaining details or structural features of the bedrock.

b3133fe61aa6.title: Soil formation
b3133fe61aa6.sentence: The texture, pH and mineral constituents of saprolite are inherited from its parent material.

15f6445654f0.title: Soil formation
15f6445654f0.sentence: Saprolite is a particular example of a residual soil formed from the transformation of granite, metamorphic and other types of bedrock into clay minerals.

b6e05acd1901.title: Soil formation
b6e05acd1901.sentence: Often called weathered granite, saprolite is the result of weathering processes that include: hydrolysis, chelation from organic compounds, hydration and physical processes that include freezing and thawing.

c0374d356873.title: Soil formation
c0374d356873.sentence: This process is also called arenization, resulting in the formation of sandy soils, thanks to the much higher resistance of quartz compared to other mineral components of granite (e.g., mica, amphibole, feldspar).

1bcf624da695.title: Regolith
1bcf624da695.sentence: - lower saprolite: chemically reduced partially weathered rocks

04a5c815c317.title: Regolith
04a5c815c317.sentence: - saprock: fractured bedrock with weathering restricted to fracture margins

517b5d495c58.title: Saprolite
517b5d495c58.sentence: Iron compounds are the primary coloring agents in saprolites.

223638d1b02f.title: Saprolite
223638d1b02f.sentence: Submicron-sized goethite [FeO(OH)] is yellow; coarse goethite is brown.

48a35fc0b348.title: Saprolite
48a35fc0b348.sentence: Sub-micron-sized hematite [Fe2O3] is red; coarse hematite is gray to black.

974226d35b79.title: Saprolite
974226d35b79.sentence: More intense weathering results in a continuous transition from saprolite to laterite.

2a76489592e3.title: Laterite
2a76489592e3.sentence: The initial products of weathering are essentially kaolinized rocks called saprolites.

bb44fdf6111c.title: Saprolite
bb44fdf6111c.sentence: In some localities it is possible to relatively date saprolite by considering that the saprolite must be younger than the parent material and older than any thick cover unit such a lava or sedimentary rock.

ae77946617bc.title: Bioturbation
ae77946617bc.sentence: Plants and animals utilize soil for food and shelter, disturbing the upper soil layers and transporting chemically weathered rock called saprolite from the lower soil depths to the surface.

164dbfe1527f.title: Saprolite
164dbfe1527f.sentence: Aquifers in Western Australia are of saprolite grit.

dacc08165b03.title: Saprolite
dacc08165b03.sentence: Poorly weathered saprolite grit aquifers are capable of producing groundwater, often suitable for livestock.

1506871433d6.title: Rock (geology)
1506871433d6.sentence: In geology, a rock (also called a stone) is any naturally occurring solid mass or aggregate of minerals or mineraloid matter.

3251ee726dd7.title: Rock (geology)
3251ee726dd7.sentence: It is categorized by the minerals included, its chemical composition, and the way in which it is formed.

fe4003d52774.title: Rock (geology)
fe4003d52774.sentence: Rocks form the Earth's outer solid layer, the crust, and most of its interior, except for the liquid outer core and pockets of magma in the asthenosphere.

35384e4d84ef.title: Rock (geology)
35384e4d84ef.sentence: Rocks are usually grouped into three main groups: igneous rocks, sedimentary rocks and metamorphic rocks.

fd4e90b8b367.title: Rock (geology)
fd4e90b8b367.sentence: Sedimentary rocks are formed by diagenesis and lithification of sediments, which in turn are formed by the weathering, transport, and deposition of existing rocks.

d7167af6ebba.title: Rock (geology)
d7167af6ebba.sentence: Before being deposited, sediments are formed by weathering of earlier rocks by erosion in a source area and then transported to the place of deposition by water, wind, ice, mass movement or glaciers (agents of denudation).

fd2ccb20d66c.title: Rock (geology)
fd2ccb20d66c.sentence: The smallest sediments are clay, followed by silt, sand, and gravel.

4694786b55c4.title: Hydrolysis
4694786b55c4.sentence: Hydrolysis (/haɪˈdrɒlɪsɪs/; from Ancient Greek hydro- 'water' and lysis 'to unbind') is any chemical reaction in which a molecule of water breaks one or more chemical bonds.

1aa109c08341.title: Hydrolysis
1aa109c08341.sentence: Hydrolysis is a chemical process in which a molecule of water is added to a substance, causing both the substance and water molecule to split into two parts.

3e9de292ed87.title: Hydrolysis
3e9de292ed87.sentence: In such reactions, a chemical bond is broken, with one fragment of the target molecule (or parent molecule) gaining a hydrogen ion, and the other gaining a hydroxide.

cf0e4f75a663.title: Hydrolysis
cf0e4f75a663.sentence: Thus hydrolysis adds water to break down molecules, whereas condensation joins molecules through the removal of water.

f998ed38732a.title: Hydrolysis
f998ed38732a.sentence: Metal ions are Lewis acids, and in aqueous solution they form metal aquo complexes of the general formula M(H2O)nm+.

51a84c8673e2.title: Hydrolysis
51a84c8673e2.sentence: Thus the aqua cations behave as acids in terms of Brønsted–Lowry acid–base theory.

b7b60ec7388e.title: Hydrolysis
b7b60ec7388e.sentence: Trivalent ions like Al3+ and Fe3+ are weak acids whose pKa is comparable to that of acetic acid.

db864cda74d3.title: Hydrolysis
db864cda74d3.sentence: Ions with low charges, such as Na+ are very weak acids with almost imperceptible hydrolysis.

bcbda2623822.title: Acid sulfate soil
bcbda2623822.sentence: Titratable Actual Acidity (TAA) is a measure of soluble and exchangeable acidity associated with organic acids and loosely bound Al3+ and Fe3+ ions – which react with water to produce H+ (i.e., hydrolysis).

d178a20b1636.title: Acid sulfate soil
d178a20b1636.sentence: Retained Acidity (RA) is a measure of sparingly soluble sulfates such as jarosite and schwertmannite, which slowly generate acidity via the release and hydrolysis of Al3+ and Fe3+.

1e626876457b.title: Alkali soil
1e626876457b.sentence: The carbonate anion, CO2− 3, is a weak base accepting a proton, so it hydrolyses in water to give the bicarbonate ion and a hydroxyl ion:

3fd52086c9f3.title: Alkali soil
3fd52086c9f3.sentence: This in turn is susceptible to further hydrolysis, giving carbonic acid and another hydroxyl ion:

5ef07a6fe2db.title: Ammonia volatilization from urea
5ef07a6fe2db.sentence: Urease is a naturally occurring enzyme that catalyzes the hydrolysis of urea to unstable carbamic acid.

3162a035e511.title: Ammonia volatilization from urea
3162a035e511.sentence: Specifically, highly alkaline soils (pH~8.2 or higher) have proven to increase urea hydrolysis.

9486b0d99393.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/02%3A_Parent_Materials_and_Mineralogy/2.01%3A_Introduction
9486b0d99393.sentence: Hydrolysis is the primary reaction resulting in the release of most plant nutrient elements from minerals.

a1d93396c1ef.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/02%3A_Parent_Materials_and_Mineralogy/2.01%3A_Introduction
a1d93396c1ef.sentence: Orthoclase + Water \(\rightarrow\) Al-silicate mineral + Potassium ion + Hydroxide ion

3f937c827b5f.title: Sedimentary rock
3f937c827b5f.sentence: Sedimentary rocks are types of rock formed by the cementation of sediments—i.e. particles made of minerals (geological detritus) or organic matter (biological detritus)—that have been accumulated or deposited at Earth's surface.

da9585bf05ec.title: Sedimentary rock
da9585bf05ec.sentence: Geological detritus originates from weathering and erosion of existing rocks, or from the solidification of molten lava blobs erupted by volcanoes.

88930efaee2e.title: Sedimentary rock
88930efaee2e.sentence: The geological detritus is transported to the place of deposition by water, wind, ice or mass movement, which are called agents of denudation.

7ed40214d91b.title: Sedimentary rock
7ed40214d91b.sentence: The sedimentary rock cover of the continents of the Earth's crust is extensive (73% of the Earth's current land surface), but sedimentary rock is estimated to be only 8% of the volume of the crust.

aaa3c8f93f3d.title: Sedimentary rock
aaa3c8f93f3d.section: Classification based on origin > Clastic sedimentary rocks
aaa3c8f93f3d.sentence: Clastic sedimentary rocks are composed of rock fragments (clasts) that have been cemented together.

027bd0400939.title: Sedimentary rock
027bd0400939.section: Classification based on origin > Clastic sedimentary rocks
027bd0400939.sentence: The clasts are commonly individual grains of quartz, feldspar, clay minerals, or mica.

250313fe520c.title: Sedimentary rock
250313fe520c.section: Classification based on origin > Clastic sedimentary rocks
250313fe520c.sentence: Clastic sedimentary rocks are subdivided according to the dominant particle size.

c8ee59c25ef0.title: Sedimentary rock
c8ee59c25ef0.section: Classification based on origin > Clastic sedimentary rocks > Mudrocks
c8ee59c25ef0.sentence: Mudrocks are sedimentary rocks composed of at least 50% silt- and clay-sized particles.

e2867f5cc2f7.title: Limestone
e2867f5cc2f7.sentence: Limestone is a type of carbonate sedimentary rock which is the main source of the material lime.

e9963d517dfe.title: Limestone
e9963d517dfe.sentence: It is composed mostly of the minerals calcite and aragonite, which are different crystal forms of calcium carbonate CaCO3.

b9e921d004b9.title: Limestone
b9e921d004b9.sentence: About 20% to 25% of sedimentary rock is carbonate rock, and most of this is limestone.

6e3cb888baa5.title: Limestone
6e3cb888baa5.sentence: The remaining carbonate rock is mostly dolomite, a closely related rock, which contains a high percentage of the mineral dolomite, CaMg(CO3)2.

820a621afc4d.title: Limestone
820a621afc4d.sentence: Limestone is partially soluble, especially in acid, and therefore forms many erosional landforms.

18b79f795b5c.title: Limestone
18b79f795b5c.sentence: These include limestone pavements, pot holes, cenotes, caves and gorges.

c038969968c8.title: Limestone
c038969968c8.sentence: Such erosion landscapes are known as karsts.

14925032188d.title: Limestone
14925032188d.sentence: While draining, water and organic acid from the soil slowly (over thousands or millions of years) enlarges these cracks, dissolving the calcium carbonate and carrying it away in solution.

a30e05b5bba6.title: Limestone
a30e05b5bba6.sentence: - Pulverized limestone is used as a soil conditioner to neutralize acidic soils (agricultural lime).

587f1677808f.title: Regolith
587f1677808f.sentence: Asteroids commonly have regoliths produced by impact and other surface-altering processes.

73906d86cb13.title: Regolith
73906d86cb13.sentence: Spacecraft observations have shown that asteroids' regolith can range from fine-grained deposits to coarse, boulder-rich debris.

9032ac690695.title: Regolith
9032ac690695.sentence: Samples returned from Itokawa by the Hayabusa mission provided the first direct asteroid regolith grains for laboratory study and revealed evidence of processes such as space weathering and solar-wind implantation.

3f103adc0c5e.title: Regolith
3f103adc0c5e.sentence: Hayabusa 2 returned samples from Ryugu in 2020, and early analysis showed that the material is primitive and rich in water and organic matter.

152b23cbb056.title: Regolith
152b23cbb056.sentence: NASA's OSIRIS-REx mission returned rocks and dust from Bennu to Earth in 2023; initial studies found carbon-rich material and evidence of water, while spacecraft observations showed that Bennu's surface is unexpectedly rugged and dominated by boulders rather than broad, smooth deposits.

7b8d5b76f108.title: Regolith
7b8d5b76f108.sentence: Scientists are beginning to call this loose icy material regolith because of the mechanical similarity with regolith on other bodies.

22027b5641dd.title: Regolith
22027b5641dd.sentence: However, traditionally (and etymologically), the term had been applied only when the loose layer was composed of mineral grains like quartz or plagioclase or rock fragments that were in turn composed of such minerals.

a3f237579b3f.title: Regolith
a3f237579b3f.sentence: Loose blankets of ice grains were not considered regolith because when they appear on Earth in the form of snow, they behave differently from regolith, the grains melting and fusing with only slight changes in pressure or temperature.

e81c6660a2e8.title: Regolith
e81c6660a2e8.sentence: However, Titan is so cold that ice behaves like rock.

0bdcbae8dd49.title: Regolith
0bdcbae8dd49.sentence: Thus, there is an ice-regolith complete with erosion and aeolian and/or sedimentary processes.

772c54b15618.title: Regolith
772c54b15618.sentence: The Huygens probe used a penetrometer on landing to characterize the mechanical properties of the local regolith.

11275e29b55f.title: Regolith
11275e29b55f.sentence: The surface itself was reported to be a clay-like "material which might have a thin crust followed by a region of relative uniform consistency." Subsequent data analysis suggests that surface consistency readings were likely caused by Huygens displacing a large pebble as it landed and that the surface is better described as a 'sand' made of ice grains.

38280a1e1843.title: Regolith
38280a1e1843.sentence: The images taken after the probe's landing show a flat plain covered in pebbles.

02810f765c90.title: Regolith
02810f765c90.sentence: The pebbles, which may be made of water ice, are somewhat rounded, which may indicate the action of fluids on them.

86fe647301f7.title: Igneous rock
86fe647301f7.sentence: Igneous rock (igneous from Latin igneus 'fiery'), or magmatic rock, is one of the three main rock types, the others being sedimentary and metamorphic.

a43ee7eb5682.title: Igneous rock
a43ee7eb5682.sentence: Igneous rocks are formed through the cooling and solidification of magma or lava.

8267a617ea2a.title: Igneous rock
8267a617ea2a.sentence: Solidification into rock occurs either below the surface as intrusive rocks or on the surface as extrusive rocks.

3b52a336faa5.title: Lithology
3b52a336faa5.sentence: Igneous rocks that have visible mineral grains (phaneritic rocks) are classified as intrusive, while those that are glassy or very fine-grained (aphanitic) are classified as extrusive rock.

2eceab4c9e92.title: Igneous rock
2eceab4c9e92.sentence: Two important variables used for the classification of igneous rocks are particle size, which largely depends on the cooling history, and the mineral composition of the rock.

bd0453d3fd8c.title: Rock cycle
bd0453d3fd8c.section: Forces that drive the rock cycle > The role of water
bd0453d3fd8c.sentence: Most prominently, water mediates the processes of weathering and erosion, whereby precipitation, acidic soil water, and groundwater dissolve minerals and mechanically break down rocks, particularly igneous and metamorphic lithologies that are unstable under near-surface conditions.

7ad477154d6c.title: Metamorphic rock
7ad477154d6c.sentence: Metamorphic rocks arise from the transformation of existing rock to new types of rock in a process called metamorphism.

e825cde3b2ea.title: Metamorphic rock
e825cde3b2ea.sentence: The original rock (protolith) is subjected to temperatures greater than 150 to 200 °C (300 to 400 °F) and, often, elevated pressure of 100 megapascals (1,000 bar) or more, causing profound physical or chemical changes.

79006a947944.title: Metamorphic rock
79006a947944.sentence: During this process, the rock remains mostly in the solid state, but gradually recrystallizes to a new texture or mineral composition.

794e3ed0dc16.title: Metamorphic rock
794e3ed0dc16.sentence: The protolith may be an igneous, sedimentary, or existing metamorphic rock.

07954bf47019.title: Metamorphic rock
07954bf47019.sentence: Metamorphic rocks make up a large part of the Earth's crust and form 12% of the Earth's land surface.

b1c8a105bc68.title: Metamorphic rock
b1c8a105bc68.sentence: Some examples of metamorphic rocks are gneiss, slate, marble, schist, and quartzite.

09a7eb5d2767.title: Grus (geology)
09a7eb5d2767.sentence: Grus is an accumulation of angular, coarse-grained fragments (particles of sand and gravel) resulting from the granular disintegration by the processes of chemical and mechanical weathering of crystalline rocks (most notably granitoids), generally in an arid or semiarid region.

e90e8b4cbfc1.title: Grus (geology)
e90e8b4cbfc1.sentence: Grus sand, when cemented into a sandstone, will form an arkose.

c00fe249a72b.title: Grus (geology)
c00fe249a72b.sentence: Within a European context most of the saprolite mantles of Late Cenozoic age are made up of grus, contrasting with Mesozoic and Early Cenozoic saprolites made up of kaolinitic and ferrallitic material.

453eaae351cd.title: Saprolite
453eaae351cd.sentence: The regolith of a region is the product of its long weathering history; leaching and dispersion are dominant during the initial phase of weathering under humid conditions.

c9d442375f84.title: Saprolite
c9d442375f84.sentence: Conditions for the formation of deeply weathered regolith include a topographically moderate relief flat enough to allow leaching of the products of chemical weathering.

656e14116684.title: Saprolite
656e14116684.sentence: A second condition is long periods of tectonic stability; tectonic activity and climate change partially erode the regolith.

5bee87088834.title: Saprolite
5bee87088834.sentence: The third condition is a humid tropical to temperate climate; higher temperatures enable reactions to occur more rapidly.

771b62d42f9d.title: Saprolite
771b62d42f9d.sentence: Weathering rates of 20 m (66 ft) per million years suggest that deep regoliths require several million years to develop.

e6389f9c1a62.title: Saprolite
e6389f9c1a62.sentence: Deep weathering can occur in cooler climates but over longer periods.

b527544b9da5.title: Saprolite
b527544b9da5.sentence: Deeply weathered regoliths are widespread in the inter-tropical belt, particularly on the continental landmasses between latitudes 35°N and 35°S.

7597d26d0077.title: Saprolite
7597d26d0077.sentence: In parts of Africa, India, South America, Australia and southeast Asia, regolith has been forming continuously for over 100 million years.

960da5768d32.title: Saprolite
960da5768d32.sentence: Regoliths vary from a few meters to over 150 m (490 ft) thick, depending on the age of the land surface, tectonic activity, climate, climate history and the composition of the bedrock.

fd0b81ad2af2.title: Saprolite
fd0b81ad2af2.sentence: Sulfides are some of the most unstable minerals in humid, oxidizing environments; many cadmium, cobalt, copper, molybdenum, nickel and zinc sulfides are easily leached to deep in the profile.

d1a8d49d27b7.title: Saprolite
d1a8d49d27b7.sentence: Carbonates are highly soluble, especially in acidic environments; the elements hosted by them – calcium, magnesium, manganese and strontium – are strongly leached.

73a7d01f2320.title: Saprolite
73a7d01f2320.sentence: Ferromagnesian minerals are the principal hosts for nickel, cobalt, copper, and zinc in sulfide-poor mafic and ultramafic rocks and are retained higher in the profile than sulfide-hosted metals.

2da4659b41b6.title: Saprolite
2da4659b41b6.sentence: They are leached from the upper horizons and reprecipitate with secondary iron-manganese oxides in the mid- to lower saprolite.

bc6ff6f8b262.title: Saprolite
bc6ff6f8b262.sentence: Deep weathering causes the formation of many secondary and supergene ores: bauxite, iron ores, saprolitic gold, supergene copper, uranium, and heavy minerals in residual accumulations.

0e0518962c1e.title: Saprolite
0e0518962c1e.sentence: Supergene enrichment occurs near the surface and involves water circulation with its resulting oxidation and chemical weathering.

4022b30f45d7.title: Saprolite
4022b30f45d7.sentence: Weathering formed thin kaolinitic [Al2Si2O5(OH)4] saprolites 1,000 to 500 million years ago; thick kaolinitic saprolites 200 to 66 million years ago; and medium-thick immature saprolites 5 million years ago in Sweden.

11f34f52d37c.title: Lithology
11f34f52d37c.sentence: The lithology of a rock unit is a description of its physical characteristics visible at outcrop, in hand or core samples, or with low magnification microscopy.

cf2efdb67fbf.title: Lithology
cf2efdb67fbf.sentence: Physical characteristics include colour, texture, grain size, and composition.

37f884be8405.title: Lithology
37f884be8405.sentence: Lithology may refer to either a detailed description of these characteristics, or a summary of the gross physical character of a rock.

a4e38b88c786.title: Lithology
a4e38b88c786.sentence: Examples of lithologies in the second sense include sandstone, slate, basalt, or limestone.

89463ce7322d.title: Lithology
89463ce7322d.sentence: Lithology is the basis of subdividing rock sequences into individual lithostratigraphic units for the purposes of mapping and correlation between areas.

de4a0e0de891.title: Lithology
de4a0e0de891.sentence: In certain applications, such as site investigations, lithology is described using a standard terminology such as in the European geotechnical standard Eurocode 7.

1f82b38366d7.title: Primary mineral
1f82b38366d7.sentence: A primary mineral is any mineral formed during the original crystallization of the host igneous primary rock and includes the essential mineral(s) used to classify the rock along with any accessory minerals.

a2d5dd49f4e6.title: Primary mineral
a2d5dd49f4e6.sentence: "A primary mineral has not been altered chemically since its crystallization from a cooling magma." Additionally, a primary mineral is defined as a mineral that is found in soil but not formed in soil, whereas secondary minerals are formed during weathering of primary minerals.

ca0606492903.title: Primary mineral
ca0606492903.sentence: Minerals in soils are found in two types; primary and secondary.

6a96377c1a0f.title: Primary mineral
6a96377c1a0f.sentence: The latter is further defined by Dr. Broome of North Carolina State: the particle size of primary minerals is primarily larger than 2μm, which includes; silt, sand, and gravel.

754d970b98af.title: Primary mineral
754d970b98af.sentence: Extrusive rocks (such as basalt, rhyolite, andesite and obsidian) and intrusive rocks (such as granite, granodiorite, gabbro and peridotite) contain primary minerals including quartz, feldspar, plagioclase, muscovite, biotite, amphibole, pyroxene and olivine in varying concentrations.

101cb8a8c1ee.title: Primary mineral
101cb8a8c1ee.sentence: The most dominant primary minerals in soil are the silicate minerals.

3dd36bbe3231.title: Primary mineral
3dd36bbe3231.sentence: Tectosilicates such as quartz, and cristobalite are common in soils.

98136b5e8b34.title: Primary mineral
98136b5e8b34.sentence: The following elements are components of primary minerals, whereas primary minerals are components of parent rocks.

dd801ca82833.title: Primary mineral
dd801ca82833.sentence: Primary rocks are the source of primary minerals and primary water.

e915fc066c0a.title: Feldspar
e915fc066c0a.sentence: Feldspar (/ˈfɛl(d).ˌspɑːr/ FEL(D)-spar; sometimes spelled felspar) is a group of rock-forming aluminium tectosilicate minerals, also containing other cations such as sodium, calcium, potassium, or barium.

0a1cdcc6e7dd.title: Feldspar
0a1cdcc6e7dd.sentence: Feldspars make up about 60% of the Earth's crust and 41% of the Earth's continental crust by weight.

56c51440e4ac.title: Feldspar
56c51440e4ac.sentence: The most common members of the feldspar group are the plagioclase (sodium-calcium) feldspars and the alkali (potassium-sodium) feldspars.

fab73d883d14.title: Feldspar
fab73d883d14.sentence: Chemical weathering of feldspars happens by hydrolysis and produces clay minerals, including illite, smectite, and kaolinite.

005474ce59c1.title: Feldspar
005474ce59c1.sentence: Hydrolysis of feldspars begins with the feldspar dissolving in water, which happens best in acidic or basic solutions and less well in neutral ones.

4ace87105e4c.title: Feldspar
4ace87105e4c.sentence: The speed at which feldspars are weathered is controlled by how quickly they are dissolved.

8db321a11d11.title: Feldspar
8db321a11d11.sentence: The abundance of feldspars in the Earth's crust means that clays are very abundant weathering products.

ca8baee3ef20.title: Feldspar
ca8baee3ef20.sentence: They are also an important component of soils.

0a258af10cd2.title: Feldspar
0a258af10cd2.sentence: Feldspars, especially plagioclase feldspars, are not very stable at the Earth's surface due to their high formation temperature.

8ab81432a927.title: Feldspar
8ab81432a927.sentence: This lack of stability is why feldspars are easily weathered to clays.

92fc048194ea.title: Feldspar
92fc048194ea.sentence: Feldspar that has been replaced by clay looks chalky compared to more crystalline and glassy unweathered feldspar grains.

195c3095842a.title: Feldspar
195c3095842a.sentence: Sedimentary rocks that contain large amounts of feldspar indicate that the sediment did not undergo much chemical weathering before being buried.

757e207d6706.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
757e207d6706.section: MINERALS OF THE SAND-SIZE (2 mm – 0.05 mm) FRACTION > Feldspars
757e207d6706.sentence: Orthoclase and microcline are the mineral names given to feldspars with the same chemical composition dominated by potassium (KAlSi3O8) with minor amounts (up to about 25%) of Na substituting for K in the structure (Figure 14.7B).

33772d54b42e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
33772d54b42e.section: MINERALS OF THE SAND-SIZE (2 mm – 0.05 mm) FRACTION > Feldspars
33772d54b42e.sentence: Orthoclase and microcline are polymorphs, which means they have the same chemical composition but different crystal forms.

444d3f070353.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
444d3f070353.section: MINERALS OF THE SAND-SIZE (2 mm – 0.05 mm) FRACTION > Feldspars
444d3f070353.sentence: Orthoclase has a monoclinic crystal form while microcline is triclinic.

09c20c6b7d1e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
09c20c6b7d1e.section: MINERALS OF THE SAND-SIZE (2 mm – 0.05 mm) FRACTION > Feldspars
09c20c6b7d1e.sentence: Feldspars within the full range of K and Na compositions (orthoclase/microcline, sanidine to albite) are generally referred to as the alkali feldspars (Figure 14.7B).

8bbe572be85e.title: Olivine
8bbe572be85e.sentence: The mineral olivine (/ˈɒl.ɪˌviːn/) is a magnesium iron silicate with the chemical formula (Mg,Fe)2SiO4.

c228648de6e7.title: Olivine
c228648de6e7.sentence: It is a type of nesosilicate or orthosilicate.

a637e8aa6c66.title: Olivine
a637e8aa6c66.sentence: The primary component of the Earth's upper mantle, it is a common mineral in Earth's subsurface, but weathers quickly on the surface.

2dd59fdab7d7.title: Olivine
2dd59fdab7d7.sentence: Olivine is one of the less stable common minerals on the surface according to the Goldich dissolution series.

fd13168059e0.title: Olivine
fd13168059e0.sentence: Because of its rapid weathering, olivine is rarely found in sedimentary rock.

70d9b48291ad.title: Olivine
70d9b48291ad.sentence: It alters into iddingsite (a combination of clay minerals, iron oxides and ferrihydrite) readily in the presence of water.

1953796e26e5.title: Olivine
1953796e26e5.sentence: Artificially increasing the weathering rate of olivine, e.g. by dispersing fine-grained olivine on beaches, has been proposed as a cheap way to sequester CO2.

9df774918a63.title: Plagioclase
9df774918a63.sentence: Plagioclase (/ˈplædʒ(i)əˌkleɪs, ˈpleɪdʒ-, -ˌkleɪz/ PLAJ-(ee)-ə-klayss, PLAYJ-, -⁠klayz) is a series of tectosilicate (framework silicate) minerals within the feldspar group.

f685095f536f.title: Plagioclase
f685095f536f.sentence: Rather than referring to a particular mineral with a specific chemical composition, plagioclase is a continuous solid solution series, more properly known as the plagioclase feldspar series.

90531a027338.title: Plagioclase
90531a027338.sentence: The series ranges from albite to anorthite endmembers (with respective compositions NaAlSi3O8 to CaAl2Si2O8), where sodium and calcium atoms can substitute for each other in the mineral's crystal lattice structure.

d80b4a779160.title: Plagioclase
d80b4a779160.sentence: Part of the feldspar family of minerals, it is abundant in igneous and metamorphic rock, and it is also common as a detrital mineral in sedimentary rock.

c37c44e24f94.title: Plagioclase
c37c44e24f94.sentence: Plagioclase weathers relatively rapidly to clay minerals such as smectite.

ad819277a358.title: Plagioclase
ad819277a358.sentence: Alkali feldspar is usually more abundant than plagioclase in sandstone because Alkali feldspars are more resistant to chemical weathering and more stable, but sandstone derived from volcanic rock contains more plagioclase.

0820a397cf8b.title: Plagioclase
0820a397cf8b.sentence: Plagioclase in hand samples is often identified by its polysynthetic crystal twinning or "record-groove" effect (a band system of fine, parallel striations).

58be3f0e6d18.title: Biotite
58be3f0e6d18.sentence: Biotite is a common group of phyllosilicate minerals within the mica group, with the approximate chemical formula K(Mg,Fe)3AlSi3O10(OH,F)2.

d65c181895b7.title: Biotite
d65c181895b7.sentence: Biotite is also sometimes called "black mica" as opposed to "white mica" (muscovite) – both may form in the same rocks, and in some instances side by side.

beed178f04d0.title: Biotite
beed178f04d0.sentence: Iron, magnesium, aluminium, silicon, oxygen, and hydrogen form sheets that are weakly bound together by potassium ions.

f4d90c074768.title: Biotite
f4d90c074768.sentence: Members of the biotite group are found in a wide variety of igneous and metamorphic rocks.

b4a5960003fb.title: Biotite
b4a5960003fb.sentence: It has been estimated that biotite comprises up to 7% of the exposed continental crust.

92c73986f0be.title: Biotite
92c73986f0be.sentence: It appears greenish to brown or black, and even yellow when weathered.

7feb22a2f479.title: Mafic
7feb22a2f479.sentence: Mafic is a term used in geology to describe silicate minerals, magmas, and igneous rocks that are rich in magnesium and iron, while being relatively low in silica content.

2702ee7b7c69.title: Mafic
2702ee7b7c69.sentence: Common rock-forming mafic minerals include olivine, pyroxene, amphibole, and biotite.

a2cad81458bc.title: Mafic
a2cad81458bc.sentence: Common mafic rocks include basalt, diabase and gabbro.

518567c2200d.title: Mafic
518567c2200d.sentence: Mafic rocks and minerals occupy one end of a spectrum of chemical composition, with felsic rocks and minerals at the opposite end.

696391a0452f.title: Mafic
696391a0452f.sentence: In general, mafic rocks tend to be dark in color, dense, and found primarily in oceanic crust, while felsic rocks tend to be light in color, less dense, and found primarily in continental crust.

1e041bfa2160.title: Mafic
1e041bfa2160.sentence: Chemically, mafic rocks are sometimes defined as rocks with a silica content between 45 and 55 wt%, corresponding to the silica content of basalt in the TAS classification.

15d2c2eb659f.title: Mafic
15d2c2eb659f.sentence: Such rocks are enriched in iron, magnesium, and calcium and typically dark in color.

87dc523eb84f.title: Mafic
87dc523eb84f.sentence: In contrast, the felsic rocks are typically light in color and enriched in aluminium and silicon along with potassium and sodium.

64b1cc16b5eb.title: Mafic
64b1cc16b5eb.sentence: The term mafic is a portmanteau of "magnesium" and "ferric" and was coined by Charles Whitman Cross, Joseph P. Iddings, Louis V. Pirsson, and Henry Stephens Washington in 1912.

2d949b82299d.title: Stone stripe
2d949b82299d.sentence: A stone stripe, also called a lava stringer, is an elongated concentration of mostly talus-like basalt rock found along a hillside or the base of a cliff.

12c4c861847f.title: Stone stripe
12c4c861847f.sentence: A stone stripe is identified by its lack of vegetative cover.

7a753d8cb68f.title: Stone stripe
7a753d8cb68f.sentence: They typically occur in north central Oregon and develop at 900 to 1,100 meter elevations.

6e457e8024fb.title: Stone stripe
6e457e8024fb.sentence: Lengths can range from only a few meters to over 150 meters, and widths measure from.3 to 3 meters.

bdbca53438d4.title: Stone stripe

66cfe1b39343.title: Stone stripe
66cfe1b39343.sentence: Stone stripes are thought to have been originally created by periglacial conditions of the Quaternary period during an Ice age.

3c1e77a6a519.title: Stone stripe
3c1e77a6a519.sentence: It is likely their formation originates from multiple processes including frost action, surface erosion, eluviation, and mass wasting.

172039b043f4.title: Stone stripe

f875f54948be.title: Stone stripe
f875f54948be.sentence: Stone stripes are also found surrounding soil mounds of central Oregon which also owe their formation to freeze and thaw cycles.

719314294763.title: Stone stripe
719314294763.sentence: They are called stone rings and form on more level terrain.

b5b4b1e1b183.title: Stone stripe
b5b4b1e1b183.sentence: As the terrain increases in slope, stone rings transition into stone stripes.

54656f58812e.title: Orthoclase
54656f58812e.sentence: Orthoclase, or orthoclase feldspar (endmember formula KAlSi3O8), is an important tectosilicate mineral which forms igneous rock.

46df85088ad2.title: Orthoclase
46df85088ad2.sentence: It is a type of alkali feldspar, also known as potassium feldspar or K-spar.

6144135e12e7.title: Orthoclase
6144135e12e7.sentence: Orthoclase is a common constituent of most granites and other felsic igneous rocks and often forms huge crystals and masses in pegmatite.

0691e98c9c34.title: Rock cycle
0691e98c9c34.sentence: The rock cycle is a basic concept in geology that describes transitions through geologic time among the three main rock types: sedimentary, metamorphic, and igneous.

3195d2f4c492.title: Rock cycle
3195d2f4c492.sentence: Each rock type is altered when it is forced out of its equilibrium conditions.

4f1f5579c768.title: Rock cycle
4f1f5579c768.sentence: For example, an igneous rock such as basalt may break down and dissolve when exposed to the atmosphere, or melt as it is subducted under a continent.

72ca6ca8ee50.title: Rock cycle
72ca6ca8ee50.sentence: Due to the driving forces of the rock cycle, plate tectonics and the water cycle, rocks do not remain in equilibrium and change as they encounter new environments.

6fd706e07af7.title: Rock cycle
6fd706e07af7.sentence: Rocks exposed to the atmosphere are variably unstable and subject to the processes of weathering and erosion.

d36d3d9f7774.title: Rock cycle
d36d3d9f7774.sentence: Weathering and erosion break the original rock down into smaller fragments and carry away dissolved material.

48eded8d11d9.title: Rock cycle
48eded8d11d9.sentence: This cyclical aspect makes rock change a geologic cycle and, on planets containing life, a biogeochemical cycle.

b47aa002b911.title: Superficial deposits
b47aa002b911.sentence: Superficial deposits (or surficial deposits) refer to geological deposits typically of Quaternary age (less than 2.6 million years old) for the Earth.

76ef513c06fa.title: Superficial deposits
76ef513c06fa.sentence: These geologically recent unconsolidated sediments may include stream channel and floodplain deposits, beach sands, talus gravels and glacial drift and moraine.

fa0f1dc6929d.title: Superficial deposits
fa0f1dc6929d.sentence: There are several types of superficial deposit, including raised beaches and brickearth.

cef9b2acdeb4.title: Superficial deposits
cef9b2acdeb4.sentence: Most of these superficial deposits are unconsolidated sediments such as gravel, sand, silt and clay, and onshore they form relatively thin, often discontinuous patches.

edeed5bf16f5.title: Superficial deposits
edeed5bf16f5.sentence: Geology databases contain information on the properties of superficial deposits.

d1a93cb270af.title: Superficial deposits
d1a93cb270af.sentence: Geological survey houses these Geology databases.

7e73d368c244.title: Superficial deposits
7e73d368c244.sentence: This information can be used for a number of different purposes in farming and forestry, including avoiding erosion, assessing growing conditions, gauging risks in terms of nutrient leaching and release of toxic substances, planning site preparation, road construction, felling and extraction operations, judging accessibility etc.

1f53396202c4.title: Parent material
1f53396202c4.sentence: Parent material is the underlying geological material (generally bedrock or a superficial or drift deposit) in which soil horizons form.

8e6842625b21.title: Parent rock
8e6842625b21.sentence: In the Earth sciences, parent rock, or parent material is the original geologic material from which soil develops.

3afa71614a51.title: Parent material
3afa71614a51.sentence: Soils typically inherit a great deal of structure and minerals from their parent material, and, as such, are often classified based upon their contents of consolidated or unconsolidated mineral material that has undergone some degree of physical or chemical weathering and the mode by which the materials were most recently transported.

9f03b197278f.title: Parent rock
9f03b197278f.sentence: It may consist of bedrock (such as sedimentary, igneous, or metamorphic rock) or unconsolidated deposits such as glacial, fluvial, or volcanic sediments.

28b07d136df7.title: Parent rock
28b07d136df7.sentence: In the context of metamorphic rocks, the original rock from which a metamorphism forms is called the protolith.

cd0b15eb82a8.title: Soil formation
cd0b15eb82a8.sentence: Rock, whether its origin is igneous, sedimentary, or metamorphic, is the source of all soil mineral materials and the origin of all plant nutrients with the exceptions of nitrogen, hydrogen and carbon.

2b60e4f42c5a.title: Parent rock
2b60e4f42c5a.sentence: The nature of the parent material strongly influences the physical and chemical characteristics of the resulting soil, for example, clay-rich soils may develop from mudstone or shale, while sandy soils often develop from the weathering of sandstone.

26e9b9c75374.title: Soil formation
26e9b9c75374.sentence: Parent materials are classified according to how they came to be deposited.

56bc5638a548.title: Soil formation
56bc5638a548.sentence: Residual materials are mineral materials that have weathered in place from primary bedrock.

c6bb212df69e.title: Soil formation
c6bb212df69e.sentence: Transported materials are those that have been deposited by water, wind, ice or gravity.

bf15e0e839bc.title: Soil formation
bf15e0e839bc.sentence: Cumulose material is organic matter that has grown and accumulates in place.

5fb5db4ac369.title: Humus form
5fb5db4ac369.sentence: Mull is linked to favorable environmental conditions, more particularly good litter quality, mild climate and availability of weatherable minerals in the parent rock.

1cf065032de7.title: Humus form
1cf065032de7.sentence: Moder is generally associated with environments where nutrient cycles are slowed down, either due to cold climate (high altitude or latitude), low availability of weatherable minerals in the parent rock, or because of acidifying vegetation (e.g. conifers).

3394a57d019b.title: Base-richness
3394a57d019b.sentence: Soils parent material greatly influence the presence of basic ions in soil as well.

08d0dcb540ab.title: Parent material
08d0dcb540ab.sentence: This parent material is loosely arranged, particles are not cemented together, and not stratified.

b09a62774405.title: Parent material
b09a62774405.sentence: This parent material is classified by its last means of transport.

860ee515ffc4.title: Soil formation
860ee515ffc4.sentence: Most soils derive from transported materials that have been moved many miles by wind, water, ice and gravity:

6a93accdc90a.title: Parent material
6a93accdc90a.sentence: For example, material that was transported to a location by glacier, then deposited elsewhere by streams, is classified as stream-transported parent material, or glacial fluvial parent material.

190424f9ec1a.title: Residuum (geology)
190424f9ec1a.sentence: These modes of transport are by wind (aeolian), water, gravity (colluvial), ice (glacial till), lakes (lacustrine), oceans (marine) or in place (non transported).

afc1c8c5c47e.title: Soil formation
afc1c8c5c47e.sentence: - Aeolian processes (movement by wind) are capable of moving silt and fine sand many hundreds of miles, forming loess soils (60–90 percent silt), common in the Midwestern United States and Canada, north-western Europe, Argentina and Central Asia.

d14297ce9799.title: Parent material
d14297ce9799.sentence: The most common parent material coming from volcanoes is volcanic ash carried away by the wind and settling at various distances from the volcano.

e0bb3ba13f97.title: Loess
e0bb3ba13f97.sentence: Loess (US: /ˈlɛs, ˈlʌs, ˈloʊ.əs/, UK: /ˈloʊ.əs, ˈlɜːs/; from German: Löss [lœs]) is a clastic, predominantly silt-sized sediment that is formed by the accumulation of wind-blown dust.

c0eff7540654.title: Loess
c0eff7540654.sentence: Ten percent of Earth's land area is covered by loesses or similar deposits.

1069164ea07f.title: Loess
1069164ea07f.sentence: Loess is a periglacial or aeolian (windborne) sediment, defined as an accumulation of 20% or less of clay with a balance of roughly equal parts sand and silt (with a typical grain size from 20 to 50 micrometers), often loosely cemented by calcium carbonate.

b5b08ecfbf6d.title: Loess
b5b08ecfbf6d.sentence: Loesses are homogeneous, erosive, porous, friable, pale yellow or buff, slightly coherent, typically non-stratified, and often calcareous.

bc13e43b8d41.title: Loess
bc13e43b8d41.sentence: Loess grains are angular, with little polishing or rounding, and composed of quartz, feldspar, mica, or other mineral crystals.

c0444aca8a8a.title: Loess
c0444aca8a8a.sentence: Because the grains are angular, loesses will often stand in banks for many years without slumping.

3b0214caab04.title: Loess
3b0214caab04.sentence: Loess deposits may become very thick: at more than a hundred meters in areas of Northwestern China and tens of meters in parts of the Midwestern United States.

b38041d1397c.title: Aeolian processes
b38041d1397c.sentence: The thickest known deposit of loess, up to 350 meters (1,150 ft), is on the Loess Plateau in China.

9372fe752013.title: Loess
9372fe752013.sentence: According to Pye (1995), four fundamental requirements are necessary for the formation of loess: a dust source, adequate wind energy to transport the dust, a suitable accumulation area, and a sufficient amount of time.

16013eac4a3d.title: Loess
16013eac4a3d.sentence: The term "Löß" was first described in Central Europe by Karl Cäsar von Leonhard (1823–1824), who had reported yellowish brown, silty deposits along the Rhine valley near Heidelberg.

20fc7aff45e8.title: Loess
20fc7aff45e8.sentence: Charles Lyell (1834) brought the term into widespread usage, observing similarities between "loess" and its derivatives along the loess bluffs in the Rhine and in Mississippi.

42decfd7de8b.title: Loess
42decfd7de8b.sentence: The aeolian origin of the loesses was recognized later (Virlet D'Aoust 1857), particularly due to the convincing observations of loesses in China by Ferdinand von Richthofen (1878).

4fa13fdd8813.title: Loess
4fa13fdd8813.sentence: This type of soil has "vertical cleavage", and thus, it can be easily excavated to form cave dwellings, which is a popular method of making human habitations in some parts of China.

5ef44024e4b5.title: Alluvium
5ef44024e4b5.sentence: Alluvium (from Latin alluvius, from alluere 'to wash against') is loose clay, silt, sand, or gravel that has been deposited by running water in a stream bed, on a floodplain, in an alluvial fan or beach, or in similar settings.

bbb6744173fd.title: Alluvium
bbb6744173fd.sentence: Alluvium is typically geologically young and is not consolidated into solid rock.

ae94218cbea3.title: Alluvium
ae94218cbea3.sentence: Sediments deposited underwater, in seas, estuaries, lakes, or ponds, are not described as alluvium.

2e32ed2523b6.title: Alluvium
2e32ed2523b6.sentence: Floodplain alluvium can be highly fertile, and supported some of the earliest human civilizations.

90d46bfba36d.title: Parent material
90d46bfba36d.sentence: Floodplains are the parts of river valleys that are covered with water during floods.

3fc9089bb071.title: Parent material
3fc9089bb071.sentence: Due to their seasonal nature, floods create stratified layers in which larger particles tend to settle nearer the channel and smaller particles settle nearer the edges of A macro photo of marine parent material showcasing deposition of manganese.

554a4d3e78a7.title: Parent material
554a4d3e78a7.sentence: Alluvial fans are sedimentary areas formed by narrow valley streams that suddenly drop to lowlands and widen dramatically.

6c8e9c691472.title: Parent material
6c8e9c691472.sentence: Sedimentary in these types of deposits tend to be larger closer to the uplands and finer near the edges of the fan.

8a8386f44207.title: Parent material
8a8386f44207.sentence: Delta deposits, the third of type of alluvium, are finer sediments that are discharged from streams into lakes and eventually settle near the mouth of the river.

81e4dfba2b88.sentence: However, the meaning of the term has varied considerably since it was first defined in the French dictionary of Antoine Furetière, posthumously published in 1690.

04800a009b71.title: Alluvium
04800a009b71.sentence: Drawing upon concepts from Roman law, Furetière defined alluvion (the French term for alluvium) as new land formed by deposition of sediments along rivers and seas.

5c4de48187bd.title: Alluvium
5c4de48187bd.sentence: By the 19th century, the term had come to mean recent sediments deposited by rivers on top of older diluvium, which was similar in character but interpreted as sediments deposited by Noah's flood.

948609e1d218.title: Alluvium
948609e1d218.sentence: With the rejection by geologists of the concept of a primordial universal flood, the term "diluvium" fell into disfavor and was replaced with "older alluvium".

61401e5da25e.title: Colluvium
61401e5da25e.sentence: Alluvium specifically refers to the geomorphic processes involved with flowing water and so alluvium is generally fine-grained clay and silt material that has the capacity to be entrained in water currents and eventually deposited.

1722c1c4e86f.title: Colluvium
1722c1c4e86f.sentence: For these same reasons, alluvium is also generally well sorted material while colluvium is not.

243d363f3ebb.title: Colluvium
243d363f3ebb.sentence: Colluvium (also colluvial material or colluvial soil; from the Latin colluvio, 'jumbled') is a general name for loose, unconsolidated terrigenous sediments (diamicton) that have been deposited at the base of hillslopes by either rainwash, sheetwash, slow continuous downslope creep, or a variable combination of these processes.

b19e94d2e33a.title: Colluvium
b19e94d2e33a.sentence: Colluvium is typically composed of a heterogeneous range of rock types and sediments ranging from silt to rock fragments of various sizes.

0851c29bd940.title: Colluvium
0851c29bd940.sentence: Colluvium is typically loosely consolidated angular material located at the base of a steep hill slope or cliff.

6286fa8f050e.title: Colluvium
6286fa8f050e.sentence: Colluvium accumulates as gently sloping aprons or fans, either at the base of or within gullies and hollows within hillslopes.

ed2eea4aa28f.title: Colluvium
ed2eea4aa28f.sentence: These accumulations of colluvium can be several meters in thickness and often contain buried soils (paleosols), crude bedding, and cut and fill sequences.

d95e8e4051ff.title: Soil formation
d95e8e4051ff.sentence: - Parent material moved by gravity is obvious at the base of steep slopes as talus cones and is called colluvial material.

d6ba801e484b.title: Colluvium
d6ba801e484b.sentence: Thick accumulations of colluvium may preserve a rich record of long term paleoclimatic change based on the paleosols and the remains of plants and animals, invertebrate and vertebrates that they often contain.

a7f1d7b9dae6.title: Colluvium
a7f1d7b9dae6.sentence: Thick accumulations of colluvium often contain well-preserved and sometimes deeply buried archaeological deposits as excavated at the Cherokee Sewer Site, Cherokee County, Iowa, and the Koster Site, Greene County, Illinois.

bd04229cdee5.title: Colluvium
bd04229cdee5.sentence: The distinction between colluvium and alluvium relates to the involvement of running water.

dd4e85531810.title: Colluvium

542f2d352dbd.title: Calcisol

03c7aa6f36f1.title: Cambisol

30e95b68d0a4.title: Durisol

66e79eb7d38f.title: Till
66e79eb7d38f.sentence: Till, or glacial till, is unsorted glacial sediment.

7d87a6513dc3.title: Till
7d87a6513dc3.sentence: Till is derived from the erosion and entrainment of material by the moving ice of a glacier.

29a84b1fe3bb.title: Till
29a84b1fe3bb.sentence: It is distinguished from other forms of drift in that it is deposited directly by glaciers without being reworked by meltwater.

566826a4a535.title: Parent material
566826a4a535.sentence: Because it is not transported with liquid water, the material is not sorted by size.

3576c6c81a97.title: Till
3576c6c81a97.sentence: Till is characteristically unsorted and unstratified, and is not usually consolidated.

f4ced49c3429.title: Till
f4ced49c3429.sentence: Most till consists predominantly of clay, silt, and sand, but with pebbles, cobbles, and boulders scattered through the till.

d4ba22c89c6b.title: Till
d4ba22c89c6b.sentence: Typically, the distribution of particle sizes shows two peaks (it is bimodal) with pebbles predominating in the coarser peak.

4e90257d0f7d.title: Parent material
4e90257d0f7d.sentence: - Basal till – carried at the base of the glacier and laid underneath it.

187f7dd106ce.title: Parent material
187f7dd106ce.sentence: This till is typically very compacted and does not allow for quick water infiltration.

c6341b5645e3.title: Parent material
c6341b5645e3.sentence: - Ablation till – carried on or in the glacier and is laid down as the glacier melts.

3ffa18762df9.title: Parent material
3ffa18762df9.sentence: This till is typically less compacted than basal till.

6a61398847ad.title: Till
6a61398847ad.sentence: It is deposited some distance down-ice to form terminal, lateral, medial and ground moraines.

1c83fdcb8ce6.title: Till
1c83fdcb8ce6.sentence: Till is deposited as the terminal moraine, along the lateral and medial moraines and in the ground moraine of a glacier, and moraine is often conflated with till in older writings.

0dacc432b1f6.title: Till
0dacc432b1f6.sentence: Till may also be deposited as drumlins and flutes, though some drumlins consist of a core of stratified sediments with only a cover of till.

d45cc3878262.title: Till
d45cc3878262.sentence: The larger clasts (rock fragments) in till typically show a diverse composition, often including rock types from outcrops hundreds of kilometers away.

85ffc981b3f2.title: Till
85ffc981b3f2.sentence: Many of the clasts are faceted, striated, or polished, all signs of glacial abrasion.

91cbe63adba1.title: Till

f0ebc23eea7c.title: Till

79f0776cffb2.sentence: The glacial erosion of sandstones often produces loose and sandy boulder clays.

959a2f86e8d7.sentence: The glacial erosion of granites, gneisses and quartzose schists often results in the formation of stony, coarse and gravelly boulder clay that, in some instances, can be hardly distinguishable from in situ decayed rock.

8755173b4af4.title: Boulder clay

a05aa0b9b973.title: Loess
