(1994) and Frechen et al. (1997) for the Austrian and Hungarian loess stratigraphy, respectively.

5cf35d0a016b.title: Loess
5cf35d0a016b.sentence: Since the 1980s, thermoluminescence (TL), optically stimulated luminescence (OSL), and infrared stimulated luminescence (IRSL) dating have been available, providing the possibility for dating the time of loess (dust) depositions, i.e., the time elapsed since the last exposure of the mineral grains to daylight.

bd26c4f51430.title: Loess
bd26c4f51430.sentence: During the past decade, luminescence dating has significantly improved by new methodological improvements, especially the development of single aliquot regenerative (SAR) protocols (Murray & Wintle 2000) resulting in reliable ages (or age estimates) with an accuracy of up to 5 and 10% for the last glacial record.

a9522990fd56.title: Loess
a9522990fd56.sentence: Advances in methods of analyses, instrumentation, and refinements to the radiocarbon calibration curve have made it possible to obtain reliable ages from loess deposits for the last 40–45 ka.

aa7077c516c0.title: Loess
aa7077c516c0.sentence: However, the use of this method relies on finding suitable in situ organic material in deposits such as charcoal, seeds, earthworm granules, or snail shells.

53b487a6a3e0.title: Loess
53b487a6a3e0.sentence: Non-glacial loess can originate from deserts, dune fields, playa lakes, and volcanic ash.

87f2efaa9c9e.title: Loess
87f2efaa9c9e.sentence: - Desert loess produced by aeolian attrition of quartz grains;

c606b852f99b.title: Loess
c606b852f99b.sentence: - Volcanic loess in Ecuador and Argentina;

2298acfad2dd.title: Loess
2298acfad2dd.sentence: - Tropical loess in Argentina, Brazil and Uruguay;

8177ce743360.title: Loess
8177ce743360.sentence: - Trade wind loess in Venezuela and Brazil;

d5e849d9519d.title: Loess
d5e849d9519d.sentence: The thick Chinese loess deposits are non-glacial loess having been blown in from deserts in northern China.

c31ba5365184.title: Loess
c31ba5365184.sentence: The loess covering the Great Plains of Nebraska, Kansas, and Colorado is considered to be non-glacial desert loess.

db77ef72a33f.title: Loess
db77ef72a33f.sentence: Non-glacial desert loess is also found in Australia and Africa.

21b58132e880.title: Residuum (geology)
21b58132e880.sentence: Residuum is weathered rock that is not transported by erosion, contributing in time to the formation of soil.

f32a68d8328a.title: Residuum (geology)
f32a68d8328a.sentence: It is distinguished from other types of parent material in that it is composed solely of mineral, not organic, material, and it remains in place rather than being moved by the action of wind, water, or gravity.

448f43b9e5e0.title: Residuum (geology)
448f43b9e5e0.sentence: Soils derived from residuum are called residual soils.

b9a275157c4f.title: Residuum (geology)
b9a275157c4f.sentence: These soils are expected to be mineralogically similar to their underlying bedrock.

f2dfbf91f6c2.title: Soil formation
f2dfbf91f6c2.sentence: Residual soils are soils that develop from their underlying parent rocks and have the same general chemistry as those rocks.

ca54d7d9aaa0.title: Residuum (geology)
ca54d7d9aaa0.sentence: While residuum is similar to the term regolith, it is more specific.

9090d6fbaf0a.title: Residuum (geology)
9090d6fbaf0a.sentence: While regolith refers to all unconsolidated earth materials above the solid bed rock, including transported sediments such as sand or alluvium, residuum is strictly a non transported parent material.

abc5ed723288.title: Residuum (geology)
abc5ed723288.sentence: Residuum differs from saprolite through its structure and degree of weathering.

58145d9bc4e2.title: Residuum (geology)
58145d9bc4e2.sentence: The distinguishing feature between these is that residuum no longer retains the structural features or details of its bed rock.

01b4f719704f.title: Residuum (geology)
01b4f719704f.sentence: It has undergone greater transformation and experienced a decrease in volume from its origins as saprolite and bedrock.

80f7604e8c54.title: Residuum (geology)
80f7604e8c54.sentence: Residuum and their associated residual soils are a produced primarily through chemical weathering of their bedrock.

aa010089355f.title: Residuum (geology)
aa010089355f.sentence: Residuum occurs in all temperature regimes and locations.

b24176f2bcd6.title: Residuum (geology)
b24176f2bcd6.sentence: In temperate climate its presence is in relatively lower amounts occurring as a "thin blanket of loose material above the bedrock.

48fdaec93ae9.title: Residuum (geology)
48fdaec93ae9.sentence: In tropical climates it can be much thicker".

e622f768cd2b.title: Residuum (geology)
e622f768cd2b.sentence: A certain degree of landscape stability is inferred for residual soils.

626fb08f733d.title: Soil formation
626fb08f733d.sentence: In the United States as little as three percent of the soils are residual.

443b9bd8be4c.title: Residuum (geology)
443b9bd8be4c.sentence: In limestone terrains the boundary between bedrock and residuum is commonly very sharp, but may be highly irregular, defining pinnacles and even isolated blocks of fresh bedrock surrounded by reddish residual silts and clays derived from its decomposition.

8947eb67698a.title: Residuum (geology)
8947eb67698a.sentence: Resistant materials such as chert, silicified fossils, or beds of sandstone remain and may concentrate on the surface as float.

f8dc36e63411.title: Eluvium
f8dc36e63411.sentence: In geology, eluvium or eluvial deposits are geological deposits and soils that are derived by in situ weathering or weathering plus gravitational movement or accumulation.

610a61507fbd.title: Eluvium
610a61507fbd.sentence: In geology, the removed material is irrelevant, and the deposit (eluvial deposit) is the remaining material.

cb45c770ccb0.title: Eluvium
cb45c770ccb0.sentence: Eluvial ore deposits are those such as tungsten and gold placer deposits formed by settling and enriched by the winnowing or removal of lower density materials.

c190ca075e63.title: Eluvium
c190ca075e63.sentence: Diamonds within yellow ground (weathered portions of kimberlites) may be considered to be eluvial deposits.

9e473d756455.title: Eluvium
9e473d756455.sentence: The Pitinga tin deposit in Brazil, an eluvial deposit, is one of the largest tin mines in the world.

086660ed420a.title: Eluvium
086660ed420a.sentence: Weathering supergene enrichment of an apatite rich carbonatite in Ontario has produced a significant eluvial phosphate ore deposit.

effafd87cd33.title: River channel migration
effafd87cd33.sentence: River channel migration is the geomorphological process that involves the lateral migration of an alluvial river channel across its floodplain.

1c23b1938a54.title: River channel migration
1c23b1938a54.sentence: This process is mainly driven by the combination of bank erosion and point bar deposition over time.

bc8baf5d4466.title: River channel migration
bc8baf5d4466.sentence: The sediment taken from the bank during the process of bank erosion is deposited on the opposing side of the channel fueling the process called point bar deposition.

876e62caf71f.title: River channel migration
876e62caf71f.sentence: As flow enters the bank of an alluvial river, the centrifugal force created by the bend instigates helicoidal flow, a corkscrew like pattern of flow, which drives the hydraulic action acting on the opposing bank.

2db2de47aa61.title: River channel migration
2db2de47aa61.sentence: Often the bank is undercut, another result of the helicoidal flow, which leads to the creation of cut banks.

061cf457a88f.title: River channel migration
061cf457a88f.sentence: The helicoidal flow also plays a role in this process by acting as a cross channel component that moves the sediment to the other side.

d43e107e9948.title: River channel migration
d43e107e9948.sentence: The processes of point bar deposition and bank erosion are intertwined and in most cases the erosion rate of cut banks is equal to the deposition rate of point bars.

f8a9ee81a37c.title: River channel migration
f8a9ee81a37c.sentence: In addition, point bars act as topographic obstructions once formed that further drive flow into the opposite bank, creating a positive feedback loop.

afa1253e1039.title: River channel migration
afa1253e1039.sentence: This leads to the meanders of an alluvial river becoming more well defined over time.

5d0e3ad90100.title: River channel migration
5d0e3ad90100.sentence: Typical features found in river channel migration are point bars, cut banks, meanders, floodplains, and oxbow lakes.

c2a97542a497.title: Volcanic ash
c2a97542a497.sentence: Volcanic ash consists of fragments of rock, mineral crystals, and volcanic glass, produced during volcanic eruptions and measuring less than 2 mm (0.079 in) in diameter.

fa06f9fac66e.title: Volcanic ash
fa06f9fac66e.sentence: The term volcanic ash is also often loosely used to refer to all explosive eruption products (correctly referred to as tephra), including particles larger than 2 mm.

dc01a3233ee2.title: Tephra
dc01a3233ee2.sentence: Tephra is fragmental material produced by a volcanic eruption regardless of composition, fragment size, or emplacement mechanism.

8b5fcefd249b.title: Volcanic ash
8b5fcefd249b.sentence: Once in the air, ash is transported by wind up to thousands of kilometres away.

6e5f8849e932.title: Volcanic ash
6e5f8849e932.sentence: Once the minerals in ash are washed into the soil by rain or other natural processes, it mixes with the soil and forms an andisol layer.

5ffdffa3877e.title: Volcanic ash
5ffdffa3877e.sentence: This layer is highly rich in nutrients and is very good for agricultural use; the presence of lush forests on volcanic islands is often as a result of trees growing and flourishing in the phosphorus and nitrogen-rich andisol.

3dad53b92a3a.title: Volcanic ash
3dad53b92a3a.sentence: Heavier falls will completely bury pastures and soil leading to death of pasture and sterilization of the soil due to oxygen deprivation.

88b85ef6c181.title: Volcanic ash
88b85ef6c181.sentence: Rehabilitation treatment may include: direct seeding of deposit; mixing of deposit with buried soil; scraping of ash deposit from land surface; and application of new topsoil over the ash deposit.

883086336840.title: Parent material
883086336840.sentence: Organic deposits (or cumulose deposits) are developed in place from plant residue (for example sphagnum moss) that has typically been preserved by a high water table, or potentially due to another factor that slows decomposition.

a3b06670eeff.title: Soil formation
a3b06670eeff.sentence: This includes peat and muck soils and results from preservation of plant residues by the low oxygen content of a high water table.

44223035a18b.title: Soil formation
44223035a18b.sentence: While peat may form sterile soils, muck soils may be very fertile.

2182c86319bc.title: Soil formation
2182c86319bc.sentence: Cumulose parent material is not moved but originates from deposited organic material.

a656988b4be4.title: Parent material
a656988b4be4.sentence: Consist of boulders, gravel, sand, silt and clay from ice sheets or glaciers.

021e29e34346.title: Parent material
021e29e34346.sentence: They are transported, sorted and deposited by streams of water.

10a494d30a71.title: Parent material
10a494d30a71.sentence: The deposits are formed beside, below or downstream from the ice.

a65f10c2b0a4.title: Soil formation
a65f10c2b0a4.sentence: Retreating glaciers leave smoother ground moraines, and in all cases outwash plains are left as alluvial deposits are moved downstream from the glacier.

f51a985963e4.title: Aeolian processes
f51a985963e4.sentence: Much of North America and Europe are underlain by sand and loess of Pleistocene age originating from glacial outwash.

b5a7d2da7303.title: Loess
b5a7d2da7303.sentence: Periglacial (glacial) loess is derived from the floodplains of glacial braided rivers that carried large volumes of glacial meltwater and sediments from the annual melting of continental ice sheets and mountain ice caps during the spring and summer.

00fdf037bbd4.title: Loess
00fdf037bbd4.sentence: During the autumn and winter, when the melting of the ice sheets and ice caps ceased, the flow of meltwater down these rivers either ceased or was greatly reduced.

8a5219b40cb8.title: Loess
8a5219b40cb8.sentence: As a consequence, large parts of the formerly submerged and unvegetated floodplains of these braided rivers dried out and were exposed to the wind.

55587b1a684e.title: Loess
55587b1a684e.sentence: Because the floodplains consist of sediment containing a high content of glacially ground flour-like silt and clay, they were highly susceptible to winnowing of their silts and clays by the wind.

273d853b24df.title: Loess
273d853b24df.sentence: Once entrained by the wind, particles were then deposited downwind.

faab17b22461.title: Loess
faab17b22461.sentence: The loess deposits found along both sides of the Mississippi River alluvial valley are a classic example of periglacial loess.

aa5ed0e61bb1.title: Loess
aa5ed0e61bb1.section: Large areas of loess deposits and soils > Europe
aa5ed0e61bb1.sentence: The northern European loess belt stretches from southern England and northern France to Germany, Poland and the southern Ukraine and deposits are characterized by strong influences of periglacial conditions.

b557e5085651.title: Loess
b557e5085651.sentence: In England, periglacial loess is also known as brickearth.

56b31a860b60.title: Loess
56b31a860b60.sentence: In several areas of the world, loess ridges have formed that had been aligned with the prevailing winds during the last glacial maximum; these are called "paha ridges" in America and "greda ridges" in Europe.

af00c8620ff0.title: Soil formation
af00c8620ff0.sentence: Sedimentary deposits settled in lakes are called lacustrine.

b4b48252de49.title: Parent material
b4b48252de49.sentence: Lacustrine material is well sorted and fine-textured, having finer silts and clays.

045a257456f1.title: Parent material
045a257456f1.sentence: Soils formed from lacustrine parent material have low permeability in part because of this high clay content.

23d464fac9e0.title: Parent material
23d464fac9e0.sentence: Beach ridges may be present where ancient lakes once washed up sand.

8d5a5477a886.title: Soil formation
8d5a5477a886.sentence: Lake Bonneville and many soils around the Great Lakes are examples.

35a1109239e2.title: Parent material
35a1109239e2.sentence: Parent material that is created from the sediments coming into lakes that come from glaciers.

6798bf717336.title: Parent material
6798bf717336.sentence: The lakes are typically ice margin lakes or other types formed from glacial erosion or deposition.

805974a1c342.title: Parent material
805974a1c342.sentence: The bedload of the rivers, containing the larger rocks and stones is deposited near the lake edge, while the suspended sediments are settle out all over the lake bed.

eab219474b40.title: Parent material
eab219474b40.sentence: A macro photo of glacio-lacustrine parent material with clear varves from annual deposition of material.

babbb86c477e.title: Parent material
babbb86c477e.sentence: Ocean deposited parent materials, called marine sediments, are collections of material that have been carried by rivers and streams to the ocean and eventually sink to the bottom.

50fadbe07170.title: Soil formation
50fadbe07170.sentence: Marine deposits, such as soils along the Gulf Coast and in the Imperial Valley of California are the beds of ancient seas that have been revealed as the land uplifted.

4186e4501250.title: Parent material
4186e4501250.sentence: These sediments are created when sediments have been transported to the oceans by glaciers or icebergs.

7af39bb08c05.title: Parent material
7af39bb08c05.sentence: They may contain large boulders, transported by and dropped from icebergs, in the midst of fine-grained sediments.

b9312cc6751d.title: Paleosol
b9312cc6751d.section: Identification > Soil types > Andisol (volcanic ash soil)
b9312cc6751d.sentence: These are soils of volcanic ash of siliceous nature, consisting of bubbles or shards of volcanic glass with a high internal surface area.

56395f2cf46c.title: Paleosol
56395f2cf46c.section: Identification > Soil types > Andisol (volcanic ash soil)
56395f2cf46c.sentence: This soil weathers rapidly to imogolite and smectite.

bdd85428e65e.title: Paleosol
bdd85428e65e.section: Identification > Soil types > Andisol (volcanic ash soil)
bdd85428e65e.sentence: Thus they are highly fertile, rich in organic matter, and have particularly low bulk density.

722cabb710d1.title: Lichen
722cabb710d1.sentence: A lichen (/ˈlaɪkən/ LY-kən, UK also /ˈlɪtʃən/ LITCH-ən) is a hybrid colony of algae or cyanobacteria living symbiotically among filaments of multiple fungus species, along with bacteria embedded in the cortex, or "skin", in a mutualistic relationship.

ea591c8dce41.title: Lichen
ea591c8dce41.section: Ecology and interactions with environment > Substrates and habitats
ea591c8dce41.sentence: When growing on mineral surfaces, some lichens slowly decompose their substrate by chemically degrading and physically disrupting the minerals, contributing to the process of weathering by which rocks are gradually turned into soil.

473ea3ea02b6.title: Lichen
473ea3ea02b6.section: Ecology and interactions with environment > Lichens and soils
473ea3ea02b6.sentence: In addition to distinct physical mechanisms by which lichens break down raw stone, studies indicate lichens attack stone chemically, entering newly chelated minerals into the ecology.

a776c7417490.title: Lichen
a776c7417490.section: Ecology and interactions with environment > Lichens and soils
a776c7417490.sentence: The substances exuded by lichens, known for their strong ability to bind and sequester metals, along with the common formation of new minerals, especially metal oxalates, and the traits of the substrates they alter, all highlight the important role lichens play in the process of chemical weathering.

f021167817f3.title: Lichen
f021167817f3.section: Ecology and interactions with environment > Lichens and soils
f021167817f3.sentence: Over time, this activity creates new fertile soil from stone.

dc3b99914eb3.title: Lichen
dc3b99914eb3.section: Ecology and interactions with environment > Ecological interactions
dc3b99914eb3.sentence: Lichens are often the first to settle in places lacking soil, constituting the sole vegetation in some extreme environments such as those found at high mountain elevations and at high latitudes.

4ed17c618650.title: Lichen
4ed17c618650.section: Ecology and interactions with environment > Lichens and soils
4ed17c618650.sentence: In deserts and semi-arid areas, lichens are part of extensive, living biological soil crusts, essential for maintaining the soil structure.

d9e2746be2a1.title: Lichen
d9e2746be2a1.section: Ecology and interactions with environment > Ecological interactions
d9e2746be2a1.sentence: In these latter cases, lichens are often an important part of soil stabilization; indeed, in some desert ecosystems, vascular (higher) plant seeds cannot become established except in places where lichen crusts stabilize the sand and help retain water.

4334beb8b5fa.title: Desert varnish
4334beb8b5fa.sentence: Desert varnish or rock varnish is an orange-yellow to black coating found on exposed rock surfaces in arid environments.

cea6667df8f8.title: Desert varnish
cea6667df8f8.sentence: Desert varnish is approximately one micrometer thick and exhibits nanometer-scale layering.

995420bfb1a6.title: Desert varnish
995420bfb1a6.sentence: Desert varnish forms only on physically stable rock surfaces that are no longer subject to frequent precipitation, fracturing or wind abrasion.

01ef9a372a04.title: Desert varnish
01ef9a372a04.sentence: The varnish is primarily composed of particles of clay along with oxides of iron and manganese.

4cad0d3f9aa3.title: Desert varnish
4cad0d3f9aa3.sentence: Microscopic and microchemical observations, however, show that a major part of varnish is clay, which could only arrive by wind.

5294342c58f3.title: Desert varnish
5294342c58f3.sentence: Clay, then, acts as a substrate to catch additional substances that chemically react together when the rock reaches high temperatures in the desert sun.

fd758b230864.title: Desert varnish
fd758b230864.sentence: Wetting by dew is also important in the process.

5ef943750b32.title: Desert varnish
5ef943750b32.sentence: An important characteristic of black desert varnish is that it has an unusually high concentration of manganese.

eb8e61d71bbb.title: Desert varnish
eb8e61d71bbb.sentence: Manganese is relatively rare in the Earth's crust, making up only 0.12% of its weight.

9d349a12a334.title: Desert varnish
9d349a12a334.sentence: In black desert varnish, however, manganese is 50 to 60 times more abundant.

6867ed80ee36.title: Desert varnish
6867ed80ee36.sentence: One proposal for a mechanism of desert varnish formation is that it is caused by manganese-oxidizing microbes (mixotrophs) which are common in environments poor in organic nutrients.

333a8213f04a.title: Desert varnish
333a8213f04a.sentence: A micro-environment pH above 7.5 is inhospitable for manganese-concentrating microbes.

117b780373d1.title: Desert varnish
117b780373d1.sentence: In such conditions, orange varnishes develop, poor in manganese (Mn) but rich in iron (Fe).

1c52728ed7b9.title: Drift (geology)
1c52728ed7b9.sentence: In geology, drift is a name for all sediment (clay, silt, sand, gravel, boulders) transported by a glacier and deposited directly by or from the ice, or by glacial meltwater.

e3e893ca8b26.title: Drift (geology)
e3e893ca8b26.sentence: Drift is often subdivided into unstratified (unsorted) drift (glacial till) that forms moraines and stratified drift (glaciolacustrine and fluvioglacial sediments) that accumulates as stratified and sorted sediments in the form of outwash plains, eskers, kames, varves, and so forth.

2e7fbf3707fc.title: Drift (geology)
2e7fbf3707fc.sentence: In the United Kingdom, drift is also applied as a general term for all surficial, unconsolidated, rock debris and sediment that is moved from one place to accumulate in another and mapped separately or otherwise differentiated from underlying bedrock.

ff3eaf6f0c31.title: Drift (geology)
ff3eaf6f0c31.sentence: In this usage, drift includes a wide variety of deposits, e.g. loess, glacial till, river deposits, colluvium, and so forth, of Quaternary age.

8c252f5d976b.title: Drift (geology)
8c252f5d976b.sentence: In 1839, geologist Roderick Murchison introduced the term drift to describe unconsolidated surficial sediments previously called diluvium.

237df5a9513d.title: Drift (geology)
237df5a9513d.sentence: The term drift refers to the drift hypothesis proposed by Charles Lyell, as influenced by contemporary polar research, that these sediments had been transported by sea ice and icebergs drifting in marine currents.

1837d8d5c0a2.title: Drift (geology)
1837d8d5c0a2.sentence: This term continued to be used long after the drift hypothesis had been abandoned in favor of the glacial theory.

cffc2ec726c0.title: Moraine
cffc2ec726c0.sentence: A moraine is any accumulation of unconsolidated debris (regolith and rock), sometimes referred to as glacial till, that occurs in both currently and formerly glaciated regions and that has been previously carried along by a glacier or ice sheet.

57f756498076.title: Moraine
57f756498076.sentence: Moraines are landforms composed of glacial till deposited primarily by glacial ice.

ba0a32d1bf73.title: Moraine
ba0a32d1bf73.sentence: It may consist of partly rounded particles ranging in size from boulders (in which case it is often referred to as boulder clay) down to gravel and sand, in a groundmass of finely divided clayey material sometimes called glacial flour.

213de80a080c.title: Moraine
213de80a080c.sentence: Lateral moraines are those formed at the side of the ice flow, and terminal moraines are those formed at the foot, marking the maximum advance of the glacier.

03c3dd29ce81.title: Moraine
03c3dd29ce81.sentence: Ground moraines are till-covered areas with irregular topography and no ridges, often forming gently rolling hills or plains, with relief of less than 10 meters (33 ft).

0e733dcb54eb.title: Moraine
0e733dcb54eb.sentence: Ground moraine is accumulated at the base of the ice as lodgment till with a thin and discontinuous upper layer of supraglacial till deposited as the glacier retreats.

f3096e5a0304.title: Moraine
f3096e5a0304.sentence: Recessional moraines are small ridges left as a glacier pauses during its retreat.

d42beb638b7b.title: Outwash plain
d42beb638b7b.sentence: An outwash plain, also called a sandur (plural: sandurs), sandr or sandar, is a plain formed of glaciofluvial deposits due to meltwater outwash at the terminus of a glacier.

743d38641410.title: Outwash plain
743d38641410.sentence: The meltwater at the snout of the glacier deposits its load of sediment over the outwash plain, with larger boulders being deposited near the terminal moraine, and smaller particles travelling further before being deposited.

0a9a3c993d57.title: Outwash plain
0a9a3c993d57.sentence: The material in the outwash plain is often size-sorted by the water runoff of the melting glacier with the finest materials, like silt, being the most distantly re-deposited, whereas larger boulders are the closest to the original terminus of the glacier.

87d1af42dbe1.title: Outwash plain
87d1af42dbe1.sentence: An outwash plain might contain surficial braided stream complexes that rework the original deposits.

3da87a841872.title: Outwash plain
3da87a841872.sentence: They may also contain kettle lakes, locations where blocks of ice have melted, leaving a depression that fills with water.

e5456c01f63d.title: Outwash plain
e5456c01f63d.sentence: Fossil sandar (i.e. no longer active) are found in areas which were formerly glaciated.

8bfd1783520e.title: Spheroidal weathering
8bfd1783520e.sentence: Spheroidal weathering is a form of chemical weathering that affects jointed bedrock and results in the formation of concentric or spherical layers of highly decayed rock within weathered bedrock that is known as saprolite.

6a2e71c0d8b8.title: Spheroidal weathering
6a2e71c0d8b8.sentence: Spheroidal weathering is also called onion skin weathering, concentric weathering, spherical weathering, or woolsack weathering.

1de23a8cbd69.title: Spheroidal weathering
1de23a8cbd69.sentence: Because water can penetrate the bedrock along these joints, the near-surface bedrock will be altered by weathering progressively inward along the faces of these blocks.

113cf20307de.title: Spheroidal weathering
113cf20307de.sentence: The alteration by weathering of the bedrock will be greatest along the corners of each block, followed by the edges, and finally the faces of the cube.

5f691eac506d.title: Spheroidal weathering
5f691eac506d.sentence: The differences in weathering rates between the corners, edges, and faces of a bedrock block will result in the formation of spheroidal layers of altered rock that surround an unaltered rounded boulder-size core of relatively unaltered rock known as a corestone or woolsack.

1f1170b53ad4.title: Spheroidal weathering
1f1170b53ad4.sentence: Within saprolite, spheroidal weathering often creates rounded boulders, known as corestones or woolsack, of relatively unweathered rock.

99e4785286a6.title: Spheroidal weathering
99e4785286a6.sentence: Frequently, erosion has removed the layers of altered rock and other saprolite surrounding corestones that were produced by spheroidal weathering.

55bc476e72ec.title: Spheroidal weathering
55bc476e72ec.sentence: This leaves many corestones as freestanding boulders on the ground's surface.

029d7ab35edb.title: Spheroidal weathering
029d7ab35edb.sentence: The chemical alteration of the rock results in the formation of abundant secondary minerals such as kaolinite, sericite, serpentine, montmorillonite, and chlorite and a corresponding increase in the volume of the altered rock.

60f1c2399669.title: Spheroidal weathering
60f1c2399669.sentence: Spheroidal weathering has often been incorrectly attributed solely to various types of physical weathering.

a5e47a11bc73.title: Spheroidal weathering
a5e47a11bc73.sentence: Often the spheroidal weathering, which created these corestones and the enclosing saprolite occurred in the prehistoric past during periods of humid, even tropical climates.

337d6615b4de.title: Topsoil
337d6615b4de.sentence: Topsoil is the upper layer of soil.

831148d27cfd.title: Topsoil
831148d27cfd.sentence: It has the highest concentration of organic matter and microorganisms and is where most of the Earth's biological soil activity occurs.

9769d068a739.title: Topsoil
9769d068a739.sentence: Topsoil is composed of mineral particles and organic matter and usually extends to a depth of 5-10 inches (13–25 cm).

0be5f2f58085.title: Topsoil
0be5f2f58085.sentence: Together these make a substrate capable of holding water and air which encourages biological activity.

a56e2e065f2c.title: Topsoil
a56e2e065f2c.sentence: There is generally a high concentration of roots in topsoil since this is where plants obtain most of their vital nutrients.

1fd376086874.title: Topsoil
1fd376086874.sentence: Bacteria and fungi can be essential in facilitating nutrient exchange with plants and in breaking down organic matter into a form that roots can absorb.

e6c115007288.title: Topsoil
e6c115007288.sentence: Insects also play important roles in breaking down material and aerating and rotating the soil.

c5def9fa5888.title: Topsoil
c5def9fa5888.sentence: The depth of the topsoil layer is measured as the depth of the surface to the first densely packed soil layer, known as subsoil.

6ed9d26ca075.title: Topsoil
6ed9d26ca075.sentence: In soil classification systems, topsoil is known as the O Horizon or A Horizon.

bd213757f966.title: Topsoil
bd213757f966.sentence: Organic matter provides nutrition for living organisms and varies in quantity between different soils; more organic matter increases the strength of the soil structure.

3c9b49207d09.title: Topsoil
3c9b49207d09.sentence: Dehydrated topsoil volume substantially decreases and is more prone to wind erosion.

7f9fe21c59bb.title: Topsoil
7f9fe21c59bb.sentence: An optimum figure for topsoil in the UK is a C:N ratio of less than 20:1.

82d8ca0212ab.title: Topsoil
82d8ca0212ab.sentence: 1 inch (2.5 cm) of topsoil can take between 500 and 1,000 years to form naturally, making the rate of topsoil erosion a serious ecological concern.

3336822af334.title: Topsoil
3336822af334.sentence: The current rate of use and erosion outpaces soil generation.

67a69106fc76.title: Topsoil
67a69106fc76.sentence: The United States loses almost 3 tons of topsoil per acre per year.

211175fe4f4b.title: Topsoil
211175fe4f4b.sentence: Sustainable techniques attempt to slow erosion through the use of cover crops in order to build organic matter in the soil.

042ee8cddee3.title: Topsoil
042ee8cddee3.sentence: Techniques for improved soil conservation include crop rotation, cover crops, conservation tillage and planted windbreaks, affect both erosion and fertility.

08036a5c845b.title: Subsoil
08036a5c845b.sentence: Subsoil is the layer of soil under the topsoil on the surface of the ground.

9d185832f501.title: Subsoil
9d185832f501.sentence: Like topsoil, it is composed of a variable mixture of small particles such as sand, silt and clay, but with a much lower percentage of organic matter and humus.

ac9bbbe804e2.title: Subsoil
ac9bbbe804e2.sentence: The subsoil is labeled the B Horizon in most soil mapping systems.

f81f6a86cbb5.title: Subsoil
f81f6a86cbb5.sentence: Below the subsoil is the soil substratum (or C horizon).

6206816043dc.title: Subsoil
6206816043dc.sentence: Because it has less organic matter than topsoil, subsoil soil colour is mainly derived from iron oxides.

28c0bbd340f8.title: Subsoil
28c0bbd340f8.sentence: Iron oxides and clay minerals form due to weathering.

f0b72ac09105.title: Subsoil
f0b72ac09105.sentence: Rainfall moves these weathering products downward as solutes and colloids by rainfall.

33a7d4bb1742.title: Subsoil
33a7d4bb1742.sentence: The subsoil is the depth where these weathering products accumulate.

46b9554afc6d.title: Subsoil
46b9554afc6d.sentence: Whereas the topsoil tends to be the depth of greatest physical, chemical, and biological activity, the subsoil is the depth of most deposition.

4e4b70c46786.title: Subsoil
4e4b70c46786.sentence: Due to physical, chemical, and biological activity, the subsoil generally has a soil structure.

e8f41e3c22a4.title: Subsoil
e8f41e3c22a4.sentence: The presence of structure distinguishes the subsoil from the underlying substratum.

686badb46a16.title: Subsoil
686badb46a16.sentence: Although not sterile, subsoil is relatively barren in terms of soil organisms compared to humus-rich topsoil.

01bfd478c4a1.title: Subsoil
01bfd478c4a1.sentence: Due to human activity, the topsoil and subsoil in many environments have been mixed.

65fc5c992033.title: Subsoil
65fc5c992033.sentence: Clay-based subsoil has been the primary source of material for adobe, cob, rammed earth, wattle and daub, and other earthen construction methods for millennia.

958e566ea141.title: Soil morphology
958e566ea141.sentence: Soil morphology is the branch of soil science dedicated to the technical description of soil, particularly physical properties including texture, color, structure, and consistence.

ff265737684e.title: Soil morphology
ff265737684e.sentence: Morphological evaluations of soil are typically performed in the field on a soil profile containing multiple horizons.

ab4e3a401434.title: Soil morphology
ab4e3a401434.sentence: Observations of soil morphology are typically performed in the field on soil profiles exposed by excavating a pit or extracting a core with a push tube (handheld or hydraulic) or auger.

8ef614af4b4f.title: Soil morphology
8ef614af4b4f.sentence: Along with soil formation and soil classification, soil morphology is considered part of pedology, one of the central disciplines of soil science.

9214b27069d3.title: Soil morphology
9214b27069d3.sentence: However, soil science did not become its own scientific discipline until the 19th century, and even then early soil scientists were broadly grouped as either "agro-chemists" or "agro-geologists" due to the enduring strong ties of soil to agriculture.

22084eb16f3e.title: Soil morphology
22084eb16f3e.sentence: These agro-geologists examined soils in natural settings and were the first to scientifically study soil morphology.

8b56c7693182.title: Soil morphology
8b56c7693182.sentence: A team of Russian early soil scientists led by V.V. Dokuchaev observed soil profiles with similar horizons in areas with similar climate and vegetation, despite being hundreds of kilometers apart.

d11b77054393.title: Soil morphology
d11b77054393.sentence: Dokuchaev's work, along with later contributions from K.D. Glinka, C.F. Marbut, and Hans Jenny, established soils as independent, natural bodies with unique properties caused by their equally unique combinations of climate, biological activity, relief, parent material, and time.

1fcf8deeb64c.title: Soil morphology
1fcf8deeb64c.sentence: Soil properties had previously been inferred from geological or environmental conditions alone, but with this new understanding, soil morphological properties were now used to evaluate the integrated influence of these factors.

880ffe10bc06.title: Soil morphology
880ffe10bc06.sentence: To standardize morphological descriptions, official guidelines and handbooks for describing soil were first published in the 1930s by Charles Kellogg and the United States Department of Agriculture-Soil Conservation Service for the United States and by G.R. Clarke for the United Kingdom.

a4034e619827.title: Soil morphology
a4034e619827.sentence: In addition to location, landscape, vegetation, topographic, and other site information, soil morphology descriptions generally include the following properties:

5013630dc3ec.title: Soil morphology
5013630dc3ec.sentence: Many soil scientists in the United States document soil morphological descriptions using the standard Pedon Description field sheet published by the USDA-NRCS.

f33156e95037.title: Soil morphology
f33156e95037.sentence: Morphological descriptions of soil structure contain assessments of shape, size, and grade.

a4ff350513cf.title: Soil morphology
a4ff350513cf.sentence: Structure is often best evaluated while the soil is relatively dry, as peds may swell with moisture, press together and reduce the definition between each ped.

83ea28c0c39c.title: Soil horizon
83ea28c0c39c.sentence: A diagnostic horizon is a horizon used to define soil taxonomic units (e.g., to define soil types).

8071b4300f32.title: Soil horizon
8071b4300f32.sentence: A taxonomic unit is determined by the presence or absence of one or more diagnostic horizons in a required depth.

10e063296d34.title: Soil horizon
10e063296d34.sentence: Diagnostic horizons are usually indicated with names, e.g. the "cambic horizon" or the "spodic horizon".

acc36b4c44f7.title: Soil horizon
acc36b4c44f7.sentence: When allocating soil (a pedon, a soil profile) to a taxonomic unit, one has to check every horizon of this soil and decide whether or not the horizon fulfills the criteria of a diagnostic horizon.

93eef28c4127.title: Soil horizon
93eef28c4127.sentence: Based on the identified diagnostic horizons, one can proceed with the allocation of the soil to a taxonomic unit.

e5637ed4867d.title: Soil horizon
e5637ed4867d.section: Diagnostic soil horizons > Diagnostic horizons in the USDA soil taxonomy (ST)

bdaf8ece5952.title: Soil horizon
bdaf8ece5952.section: Diagnostic soil horizons > Diagnostic horizons in the USDA soil taxonomy (ST)

111937dd0c87.title: Soil horizon
111937dd0c87.section: Diagnostic soil horizons > Diagnostic horizons in the USDA soil taxonomy (ST)

946a94d01fd9.title: Soil horizon
946a94d01fd9.section: Diagnostic soil horizons > Diagnostic horizons in the World Reference Base for Soil Resources (WRB)

6070196b77ff.title: Soil horizon
6070196b77ff.section: Diagnostic soil horizons > Diagnostic horizons in the World Reference Base for Soil Resources (WRB)

65f1820f83c0.title: Soil horizon
65f1820f83c0.section: Diagnostic soil horizons > Diagnostic horizons in the USDA soil taxonomy (ST)

f023004f0a24.title: Soil horizon
f023004f0a24.sentence: In addition, most classification systems use other soil characteristics to define taxonomic units.

12d8e23bf9db.title: Soil horizon
12d8e23bf9db.sentence: In addition to these diagnostic horizons, some other soil characteristics may be needed to define a soil type.

20bcdb8e10fe.title: Soil horizon
20bcdb8e10fe.section: Horizons and layers according to the FAO Guidelines for Soil Description (2006) > Master horizons and layers
20bcdb8e10fe.sentence: O horizons or layers: These are layers of organic material.

dcec07d3047a.title: Soil horizon
dcec07d3047a.section: Horizons and layers according to the FAO Guidelines for Soil Description (2006) > Master horizons and layers
dcec07d3047a.sentence: The O horizon is formed from organic residues that are not incorporated into the mineral soil.

f5f7526e13e4.title: Soil horizon
f5f7526e13e4.section: Horizons and layers according to the FAO Guidelines for Soil Description (2006) > Master horizons and layers
f5f7526e13e4.sentence: Contrary to the H horizons, the O horizons are not saturated with water for prolonged periods and not drained artificially.

af4063bfa7b2.title: Soil horizon
af4063bfa7b2.section: Horizons and layers according to the FAO Guidelines for Soil Description (2006) > Master horizons and layers
af4063bfa7b2.sentence: Organic material is defined by having a certain minimum content of soil organic carbon.

ef0902ec7c1e.title: Soil horizon
ef0902ec7c1e.section: Horizons and layers according to the FAO Guidelines for Soil Description (2006) > Master horizons and layers
ef0902ec7c1e.sentence: In the WRB, this is 20% (by weight).

dfe88ddc51ad.title: Soil horizon
dfe88ddc51ad.section: Horizons and layers according to the FAO Guidelines for Soil Description (2006) > Master horizons and layers
dfe88ddc51ad.sentence: In many O horizons, the residues are leaves, coniferous needles, twigs, mosses, and lichens.

fb6a08c54b89.title: Soil horizon
fb6a08c54b89.section: Horizons and layers according to the FAO Guidelines for Soil Description (2006) > Master horizons and layers
fb6a08c54b89.sentence: The residues may be partially altered by decomposition.

9af4164edf05.title: Soil horizon
9af4164edf05.sentence: O) Organic surface layer: Plant litter layer—the upper part is often relatively undecomposed, but the lower part may be strongly humified.

bcefcc804175.title: Soil horizon
bcefcc804175.section: Horizons according to the Australian Soil and Land Survey Field Handbook (2009) > Horizons
bcefcc804175.sentence: O horizons may be divided into O1 and O2 categories, whereby O1 horizons contain undecomposed matter whose origin can be spotted on sight (for instance, fragments of leaves), and O2 horizons contain organic debris in various stages of decomposition, the origin of which is not readily visible.

a1ec6c6b4109.title: Soil horizon
a1ec6c6b4109.section: Horizons according to the Australian Soil and Land Survey Field Handbook (2009) > Horizons
a1ec6c6b4109.sentence: In the Australian system, the O horizon should be considered distinct from the layer of leaf litter covering many heavily vegetated areas, which contains no weathered mineral particles and is not part of the soil itself.

b9b187ea6de0.title: Soil
b9b187ea6de0.sentence: The remaining surficial organic layer, called the O horizon, produces a more active soil due to the effect of the organisms that live within it.

bc3dff29554c.title: Soil
bc3dff29554c.sentence: Organisms colonise and break down organic materials, making available nutrients upon which other plants and animals can live.

86a1391dda82.title: Soil
86a1391dda82.sentence: This natural process does not go to completion in the presence of conditions detrimental to soil life such as strong acidity, cold climate or pollution, stemming in the accumulation of undecomposed organic matter within a single organic horizon overlying the mineral soil and in the juxtaposition of humified organic matter and mineral particles, without intimate mixing, in the underlying mineral horizons.

01665153060f.title: Soil horizon
01665153060f.section: Horizons and layers according to the FAO Guidelines for Soil Description (2006) > Master horizons and layers
01665153060f.sentence: Although these horizons form above the mineral soil surface, they may be buried by redeposited mineral soil (e.g. after landslide, flooding, aeolian dust deposition) and therefore be found at greater depth.

2d9e65668166.title: Soil horizon
2d9e65668166.section: Horizons and layers according to the FAO Guidelines for Soil Description (2006) > Master horizons and layers
2d9e65668166.sentence: A horizons: These are mineral horizons that formed at the surface or below an O horizon.

b99b1e355d8d.title: Soil horizon
b99b1e355d8d.section: Horizons and layers according to the FAO Guidelines for Soil Description (2006) > Master horizons and layers
b99b1e355d8d.sentence: - an accumulation of humified organic matter, intimately mixed with the mineral fraction, and not displaying properties characteristic of E or B horizons (see below);

98aa260f0202.title: Soil horizon
98aa260f0202.section: Horizons according to the Australian Soil and Land Survey Field Handbook (2009) > Horizons
98aa260f0202.sentence: The A horizon is the top layer of the mineral soil horizons, often referred to as 'topsoil'.

a239f60e5b09.title: Soil horizon
a239f60e5b09.section: Horizons according to the Australian Soil and Land Survey Field Handbook (2009) > Horizons
a239f60e5b09.sentence: This layer contains dark decomposed organic matter, which is called "humus".

8cd9f8827f03.title: Soil
8cd9f8827f03.sentence: After sufficient time, humus moves downward (leaching, eluviation) and is deposited (illuviation) in a distinctive organic-mineral surface layer called the A horizon, in which organic matter is mixed with mineral matter through the activity of burrowing animals, a process called bioturbation.

51102378c0d9.title: Soil horizon
51102378c0d9.section: Horizons according to the Australian Soil and Land Survey Field Handbook (2009) > Horizons
51102378c0d9.sentence: The A is a surface horizon, and as such is also known as the zone in which most biological activity occurs.

15281ceb7a08.title: Soil horizon
15281ceb7a08.section: Horizons according to the Australian Soil and Land Survey Field Handbook (2009) > Horizons
15281ceb7a08.sentence: Soil organisms such as earthworms, potworms (enchytraeids), arthropods, nematodes, fungi, and many species of bacteria and archaea are concentrated here, often in close association with plant roots.

7dbfe8285ce0.title: Soil horizon
7dbfe8285ce0.section: Horizons according to the Australian Soil and Land Survey Field Handbook (2009) > Horizons
7dbfe8285ce0.sentence: Thus, the A horizon may be referred to as the biomantle.

7a11a11ff32f.title: Soil horizon
7a11a11ff32f.section: Horizons according to the Australian Soil and Land Survey Field Handbook (2009) > Horizons
7a11a11ff32f.sentence: However, since biological activity extends far deeper into the soil, it cannot be used as a chief distinguishing feature of an A horizon.

ad685c27ad41.title: Soil horizon
ad685c27ad41.section: Horizons according to the Australian Soil and Land Survey Field Handbook (2009) > Horizons
ad685c27ad41.sentence: The technical definition of an A horizon may vary between the systems, but it is most commonly described in terms relative to deeper layers.

59b6b5d23cc0.title: Soil horizon
59b6b5d23cc0.section: Horizons and layers according to the FAO Guidelines for Soil Description (2006) > Master horizons and layers
59b6b5d23cc0.sentence: All or much of the original rock structure has been obliterated.

fc0fc7106fec.title: Soil horizon
fc0fc7106fec.section: Horizons and layers according to the FAO Guidelines for Soil Description (2006) > Master horizons and layers
fc0fc7106fec.sentence: - properties resulting from cultivation, pasturing, or similar kinds of disturbance;

c5adb486ac01.title: Soil horizon
c5adb486ac01.section: Horizons and layers according to the World Reference Base for Soil Resources > Suffixes
c5adb486ac01.sentence: - p: Modification by cultivation (e.g. ploughing); mineral layers are designated A, even if they belonged to another layer before cultivation [p like plough] (H, O, A).

df956f0e294a.title: Illuvium
df956f0e294a.sentence: The removal of material from a soil layer is called eluviation.

dd49277e0070.title: Eluvium
dd49277e0070.sentence: In soil science, eluviation is the transport of soil material from upper layers of soil to lower levels by downward percolation of water across soil horizons, and accumulation of this material (illuvial deposit) in lower levels is called illuviation.

dc6389054e5e.title: Eluvium
dc6389054e5e.sentence: Eluviation occurs when precipitation exceeds evaporation.

f36c7510a39e.title: Eluvium
f36c7510a39e.sentence: A soil horizon formed due to eluviation is an eluvial zone or eluvial horizon.

a01bdac1e512.title: Eluvium
a01bdac1e512.sentence: Yet some sources consider the eluvial zone to be the A horizon plus the (distinct) E horizon, as eluviation technically occurs in both.

ab880751572b.title: Leaching (pedology)
ab880751572b.sentence: It is a mechanism of soil formation distinct from the soil forming process of eluviation, which is the loss of mineral and organic colloids.

e3e4bcfe3018.title: Catena (soil)
e3e4bcfe3018.sentence: In addition, the top facets lose materials such as mineral salts when these are washed out by rain (eluviation), while the bottom facets gain materials when these are washed in (illuviation).

5a564559de49.title: Cheluviation
5a564559de49.sentence: Organic acids produced under acidic conditions can increase the solubility of metal elements such as iron and aluminum, thereby enhancing soil eluviation.

6b17d0776bfc.title: Podsolisation
6b17d0776bfc.sentence: Podsolisation is an extreme form of leaching which causes the eluviation of iron and aluminium sesquioxides.

8ebd489f179c.title: Eluvium
8ebd489f179c.sentence: In a typical soil profile, the eluvial horizon refers to a light-colored zone located (depending on context and literature) either at the lower part of the A horizon (symbol: Ae) or within a distinct horizon (E horizon) below the A, where the process is most intense and rapid.

948089fa21da.title: Soil horizon
948089fa21da.section: Horizons and layers according to the FAO Guidelines for Soil Description (2006) > Master horizons and layers
948089fa21da.sentence: E horizons: These are mineral horizons in which the main feature is loss of clay minerals, iron, aluminium, organic matter or some combination of these, leaving a concentration of sand and silt particles, mostly of quartz.

c019f7f77967.title: Soil horizon
c019f7f77967.section: Horizons according to the Australian Soil and Land Survey Field Handbook (2009) > Horizons
c019f7f77967.sentence: "E", being short for eluviated, is most commonly used to label a horizon that has been significantly leached of its mineral and/or organic content, leaving a pale layer largely composed of silicates or silica.

d8090e5c9301.title: Soil horizon
d8090e5c9301.section: Horizons and layers according to the FAO Guidelines for Soil Description (2006) > Master horizons and layers
d8090e5c9301.sentence: An E horizon is commonly near to the surface, below an O or A horizon, and above a B horizon.

11d07b383c60.title: Soil horizon
11d07b383c60.section: Horizons and layers according to the FAO Guidelines for Soil Description (2006) > Master horizons and layers
11d07b383c60.sentence: An E horizon is most commonly differentiated from an underlying B horizon: by colour of higher value or lower chroma, or both; by coarser texture; or by a combination of these properties.

2def05dc4bc1.title: Soil horizon
2def05dc4bc1.section: Horizons according to the Australian Soil and Land Survey Field Handbook (2009) > Horizons
2def05dc4bc1.sentence: These are present only in older, well-developed soils, and generally occur between the A and B horizons.

c3dcdcdd9863.title: Soil horizon
c3dcdcdd9863.section: Horizons and layers according to the FAO Guidelines for Soil Description (2006) > Master horizons and layers
c3dcdcdd9863.sentence: However, pedogenesis is advanced, because the lost substances first have been formed or accumulated there.

03197e449cd7.title: Soil horizon
03197e449cd7.section: Horizons according to the Australian Soil and Land Survey Field Handbook (2009) > Horizons
03197e449cd7.sentence: In soils that contain gravels, due to animal bioturbation, a stonelayer commonly forms near or at the base of the E horizon.

4ee7e152096e.title: Soil horizon
4ee7e152096e.sentence: When this eluviation is pronounced, a lighter coloured E subsurface soil horizon is apparent below the A horizon.

306ddf569cb7.title: Soil horizon
306ddf569cb7.section: Horizons and layers according to the FAO Guidelines for Soil Description (2006) > Master horizons and layers
306ddf569cb7.sentence: An E horizon is usually, but not necessarily, lighter in colour than an underlying B horizon.

4b3db8aba35d.title: Soil horizon
4b3db8aba35d.section: Horizons and layers according to the FAO Guidelines for Soil Description (2006) > Master horizons and layers
4b3db8aba35d.sentence: In some soils, the colour is that of the sand and silt particles.

7ff2779ffdc6.title: Hardpan
7ff2779ffdc6.sentence: In soil science, agriculture and gardening, hardpan or soil pan is a dense layer of soil, usually found below the uppermost topsoil layer.

8b58d6dc04aa.title: Hardpan
8b58d6dc04aa.sentence: There are different types of hardpan, all sharing the general characteristic of being a distinct soil layer that is largely impervious to water.

0945365ede3e.title: Hardpan
0945365ede3e.sentence: Some hardpans are formed by deposits in the soil that fuse and bind the soil particles.

cf8520f455e7.title: Hardpan
cf8520f455e7.sentence: These deposits can range from dissolved silica to matrices formed from iron oxides and calcium carbonate.

8461b2ff3f32.title: Hardpan
8461b2ff3f32.sentence: Others are man-made, such as hardpan formed by compaction from repeated plowing, particularly with moldboard plows, or by heavy traffic or pollution.

aaabdcafa8f0.title: Hardpan
aaabdcafa8f0.sentence: Acidic soils are most often affected due to the propensity of certain mineral salts, most notably iron and calcium, to form hard complexes with soil particles under acidic conditions.

689f5bfcabcc.title: Hardpan
689f5bfcabcc.sentence: Soils with a high clay content are also easily compacted and affected by man-made discharges.

09017e8eaebc.title: Hardpan
09017e8eaebc.sentence: Common salts such as sodium ions contained in wastewater can fulfil this role and lead to a localized hardpan in some soil types.

1087100f2224.title: Hardpan
1087100f2224.sentence: This is a common cause of septic system failure due to the prevention of proper drainage in field.

92aed150020e.title: Hardpan
92aed150020e.sentence: Hardpan can be a problem in farming and gardening by impeding drainage of water and restricting the growth of plant roots.

50f4c0cdb580.title: Hardpan
50f4c0cdb580.sentence: In these situations, the hardpan can be broken up by either mechanical means such as digging or plowing, or through the use of soil amendments.

498e1efec240.title: Hardpan
498e1efec240.sentence: The broadfork is a manual tool specifically designed for this task; a digging fork or a spade might also be used.

5743c71dcff3.title: Hardpan
5743c71dcff3.sentence: The chisel plow does a similar job with the help of a tractor.

495642558b11.title: Hardpan
495642558b11.sentence: It has been observed that increasing the amount of soil organic matter through the working-in of manure, compost or peat can both improve local drainage and promote the proliferation of earth worms that can, over time, break hardpan layers.

46c6fa957205.title: Hardpan
46c6fa957205.sentence: More difficult hardpans may be further improved through the action of both adjusting the soil pH with lime if the soil is acidic, and with the addition of gypsum.

2fd0985576ce.title: Hardpan
2fd0985576ce.sentence: However, unlike when employing mechanical means, breaking a hardpan through the use of amendments may require action over the course of years, and even then one is by no means assured success.

c555a0e19389.title: Plinthite
c555a0e19389.sentence: Plinthite changes irreversibly to an ironstone hardpan or to irregular soil aggregates on exposure to repeated wetting and drying, especially if it is also exposed to heat from the sun.

8fe210caf5bd.title: Cryoturbation
8fe210caf5bd.sentence: In gelisols (permafrost soils), cryoturbation (frost churning) refers to the mixing of materials from various horizons of the soil down to the bedrock due to freezing and thawing.

28be6ba36b35.title: Cryoturbation
28be6ba36b35.sentence: Cryoturbation occurs to varying degrees in most gelisols.

53776e9006e5.title: Gelisol
53776e9006e5.sentence: The word "gelisol" comes from the Latin gelare meaning "to freeze", a reference to the process of cryoturbation that occurs from the alternating thawing and freezing characteristic of gelisols.

667e3bd6a1f0.title: Cryoturbation
667e3bd6a1f0.sentence: The cause of cryoturbation lies in the way in which the repeated freezing of the soil during autumn causes the formation of ice wedges at the most easily erodible parts of the parent rock.

0b86fc1681c9.title: Cryoturbation
0b86fc1681c9.sentence: As this process continues, during the summer when an active layer forms in the soil this eroded material can easily move both from the soil surface downward and from the permafrost table upward.

b0a516555e2e.title: Cryoturbation
b0a516555e2e.sentence: As this process occurs, the upper soil material gradually dries out (because the soil moisture moves from the warm surface layer to the colder layer at the top of the permafrost) so that it forms a granular structure with many very distinctive crystalline shapes (such as ice lenses).

763cacf0b296.title: Cryoturbation
763cacf0b296.sentence: Separation of coarse from fine soil materials produces distinctive patterned ground with different types of soil.

a9c6a031676e.title: Cryoturbation
a9c6a031676e.sentence: The extent of cryoturbation in gelisols varies considerably: it occurs much more on exposed sites (where turbels dominate everywhere) than in sheltered sites such as valleys (where orthels are not significantly affected by cryoturbation form).

e30ee501a3e1.title: Gelisol
e30ee501a3e1.sentence: - Turbels: soils that show marked influence of cryoturbation (more than one-third of the depth of the active layer) such as irregular, broken, or distorted horizon boundaries and involutions and areas with patterned ground.

c9ec2aa1b4a6.title: Gelisol
c9ec2aa1b4a6.sentence: - Orthels: soils that show little or no cryoturbation (less than one-third of the depth of the active layer).

9f5911f764dd.title: Active layer
9f5911f764dd.section: Soil formation in the active layer
9f5911f764dd.sentence: Cryoturbation is the dominant force operating in the active layer, and tends to make it generally uniform in composition throughout.

782eaded014c.title: Frost boil
782eaded014c.sentence: Cryoturbation within active frost boils may allow water containing basic salts to permeate from depth to the surface, neutralizing soil acidity and replenishing the supply of nutrients.

a298c1c52131.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/01%3A_Digging_In/1.02%3A_Soil_Genesis
a298c1c52131.section: MAJOR SOIL FORMATION PATHWAYS IN CANADA > Tundra and Arctic Cordillera Soils
a298c1c52131.sentence: When ice forms in the soil it draws unfrozen soil water along a thermal gradient to the ice front.

ac4a851b12f1.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/01%3A_Digging_In/1.02%3A_Soil_Genesis
ac4a851b12f1.section: MAJOR SOIL FORMATION PATHWAYS IN CANADA > Tundra and Arctic Cordillera Soils
ac4a851b12f1.sentence: This causes the lens of ice to grow and displace mineral and organic soil material, mixing together the soil at the ice-water interface (Figure 2.20).

817d23ca9834.title: Illuvium
817d23ca9834.sentence: Illuvium is material displaced across a soil profile, from one layer to another one, by the action of rainwater.

adc691970e00.title: Illuvium
adc691970e00.sentence: The process of deposition of illuvium is termed illuviation.

365b71eec71f.title: Illuvium
365b71eec71f.sentence: Illuvium includes organic matter, silicate clay, and hydrous oxides of iron and aluminum.

0b3a5e153bc0.title: Illuvium
0b3a5e153bc0.sentence: Illuvial deposits of clays, oxides, and organics accumulate in subsoil as distinctive soil horizons classified as "B horizons" or "zones of illuviation".

e938ef19d804.title: Illuvium
e938ef19d804.sentence: It is a water-assisted transport in a basically vertical direction, as compared to alluviation, the horizontal running water transfer.

aaf16a9b4a2f.title: Illuvium
aaf16a9b4a2f.sentence: When percolating rain water reaches a drier soil horizon, water from the suspension is removed by capillary action of microchannels, leaving fine deposits (cutans) oriented along percolation macrochannels.

fa88be3b2de9.title: Illuvium
fa88be3b2de9.sentence: Transport of soil solutes is termed leaching.

fc891ef3d1a4.title: Illuvium
fc891ef3d1a4.sentence: Soluble constituents are deposited due to differences in soil chemistry, especially soil pH and redox potential.

de9a44f2f3b5.title: Cutans
de9a44f2f3b5.sentence: Clay skins are also called argillans, and soil horizons with sufficient clay illuviation are termed argillic horizons.

25bcddc24b12.title: Physical properties of soil
25bcddc24b12.sentence: In medium-textured soils, clay is often washed downward through the soil profile (a process called eluviation) and accumulates in the subsoil (a process called illuviation).

9e5c49acb189.title: Soil horizon

9e5c49acb189.sentence: B horizons: These are horizons that formed below an A, E, H, or O horizon, and in which the dominant features are the obliteration of all or much of the original rock structure, together with one or a combination of the following:

febb1b4da45b.title: Soil horizon

febb1b4da45b.sentence: The B horizon is commonly referred to as "subsoil" and consists of mineral layers which are significantly altered by pedogenesis, mostly with the formation of iron oxides and clay minerals.

f7418cb125fe.title: Soil horizon
f7418cb125fe.section: Horizons and layers according to the FAO Guidelines for Soil Description (2006) > Master horizons and layers
f7418cb125fe.sentence: - residual concentration of oxides (especially iron oxides) and/or clay minerals;

5c6a0c888ba8.sentence: - evidence of removal of carbonates or gypsum;

e3813258a26d.section: Horizons and layers according to the FAO Guidelines for Soil Description (2006) > Master horizons and layers
e3813258a26d.sentence: - illuvial concentration, alone or in combination, of clay minerals, iron, aluminium, organic matter, carbonates, gypsum or silica;

112934515d54.title: Soil horizon
112934515d54.section: Horizons according to the Australian Soil and Land Survey Field Handbook (2009) > Horizons
112934515d54.sentence: The B horizon can also accumulate minerals and organic matter that are migrating downwards from the A and E horizons.

71d1fba24cab.title: Soil horizon
71d1fba24cab.section: Horizons according to the Australian Soil and Land Survey Field Handbook (2009) > Horizons
71d1fba24cab.sentence: If so, this layer is also known as the illuviated or illuvial horizon.

11284ff0a57f.title: Soil horizon
11284ff0a57f.sentence: The B horizon generally has a soil structure.

10b8b521946c.section: Horizons according to the Australian Soil and Land Survey Field Handbook (2009) > Horizons
10b8b521946c.sentence: In addition, the B horizon is defined as having a distinctly different structure or consistency than the horizon(s) above and the horizon(s) below.

7140b256f600.title: Soil horizon
7140b256f600.section: Horizons and layers according to the FAO Guidelines for Soil Description (2006) > Master horizons and layers
7140b256f600.sentence: Examples of layers that are not B horizons are: layers in which clay films either coat rock fragments or are found on finely stratified unconsolidated sediments, whether the films were formed in place or by illuviation; layers into which carbonates have been illuviated but that are not contiguous to an overlying genetic horizon; and layers with gleying but no other pedogenic changes.

2b57f4f07bf8.title: Soil horizon
2b57f4f07bf8.section: Horizons according to the Australian Soil and Land Survey Field Handbook (2009) > Horizons
2b57f4f07bf8.sentence: B1 is a transitional horizon of the opposite nature to an A3 – dominated by the properties of the B horizons below it, but containing some A-horizon characteristics.

ffbc20dbefec.title: Soil horizon
ffbc20dbefec.section: Horizons according to the Australian Soil and Land Survey Field Handbook (2009) > Horizons
ffbc20dbefec.sentence: B2 horizons have a high concentration of clay minerals or oxides.

76b54dbeca2e.title: Soil horizon
76b54dbeca2e.section: Horizons according to the Australian Soil and Land Survey Field Handbook (2009) > Horizons
76b54dbeca2e.sentence: B3 horizons are transitional between the overlying B layers and the material beneath it, whether C or D horizon.

cfd235264369.title: Soil horizon
cfd235264369.section: Horizons and layers according to the FAO Guidelines for Soil Description (2006) > Master horizons and layers
cfd235264369.sentence: C horizons or layers: These are horizons or layers, excluding hard bedrock, that are little affected by pedogenic processes and lack properties of H, O, A, E or B horizons.

fa78f07f3a47.title: Soil horizon
fa78f07f3a47.section: Horizons and layers according to the FAO Guidelines for Soil Description (2006) > Master horizons and layers
fa78f07f3a47.sentence: Included as C layers are sediments, saprolite, non-indurated bedrock, and other geological materials that commonly slake within 24 hours when air-dry or drier chunks are placed in water, and that, when moist, can be dug with a spade.

035a218a7b32.title: Soil horizon
035a218a7b32.section: Horizons according to the Australian Soil and Land Survey Field Handbook (2009) > Horizons
035a218a7b32.sentence: The C horizon forms either in deposits (e.g., loess, flood deposits, landslides) or it formed from in situ weathering of residual bedrock.

f8a1874aab9e.title: Soil horizon
f8a1874aab9e.section: Horizons according to the Australian Soil and Land Survey Field Handbook (2009) > Horizons
f8a1874aab9e.sentence: If there is no lithologic discontinuity between the solum and the C horizon and no underlying bedrock present, the C horizon resembles the parent material of the solum.

8e595f8aca14.title: Soil horizon
8e595f8aca14.section: Horizons and layers according to the FAO Guidelines for Soil Description (2006) > Master horizons and layers
8e595f8aca14.sentence: The material of C layers may be either like or unlike that from which the overlying solum presumably formed.

f8d58905dfff.title: Soil horizon
f8d58905dfff.section: Horizons and layers according to the FAO Guidelines for Soil Description (2006) > Master horizons and layers
f8d58905dfff.sentence: Plant roots can penetrate C horizons, which provide an important growing medium.

bc9e3f2fbffa.title: Soil horizon
bc9e3f2fbffa.section: Horizons according to the Australian Soil and Land Survey Field Handbook (2009) > Horizons
bc9e3f2fbffa.sentence: The C horizon may be enriched with carbonates carried below the solum by leaching.

7577ffaefb7a.title: Soil horizon
7577ffaefb7a.sentence: This layer may accumulate more potentially soluble compounds like CaCO 3.

6dfbfc845049.title: Soil horizon
6dfbfc845049.section: Horizons and layers according to the FAO Guidelines for Soil Description (2006) > Master horizons and layers
6dfbfc845049.sentence: Layers having accumulations of silica, carbonates, or gypsum, even if indurated, may be included in C horizons, unless the layer is obviously affected by pedogenic processes; then it is a B horizon.

693a23f8a01c.title: Soil morphology
693a23f8a01c.sentence: A soil profile is one face of a pedon, or an imaginary three-dimensional unit of soil that would display the full range of properties characteristic of a particular soil.

efc6da504aa1.title: Soil morphology
efc6da504aa1.sentence: Soil profiles contain multiple layers, known as horizons, that are generally parallel to the soil surface.

859ed650959b.title: Solum
859ed650959b.sentence: The solum (plural, sola) in soil science consists of the surface and subsoil layers that have undergone the same soil forming conditions.

937fd1388fbd.title: Solum
937fd1388fbd.sentence: In terms of soil horizon designations, a solum consists of A, E, and B horizons and their transitional horizons and some O horizons.

d8af247fc9fd.title: Solum
d8af247fc9fd.sentence: The base of the solum is the relatively unweathered parent material.

70d4cf28656a.title: Solum
70d4cf28656a.sentence: Included are horizons with an accumulation of carbonates or more soluble salts if they are either within, or contiguous, to other genetic horizons and are at least partly produced in the same period of soil formation.

cc4d66bdacb4.title: Solum
cc4d66bdacb4.sentence: A solum does not have a maximum or a minimum thickness.

4fe7e79319ce.title: Solum
4fe7e79319ce.sentence: A surface layer that is 10 cm thick overlying bedrock can be by itself the solum.

f711d16ba8f1.title: Solum
f711d16ba8f1.sentence: A soil that consists only of recently deposited alluvium or recently exposed soft sediment does not have a solum.

68d8862fec4d.title: Solum
68d8862fec4d.sentence: The lower limit should relate to the depth of rooting to be expected for perennial plants assuming that soil moisture conditions and soil chemistry are not limiting.

0ce77d3acc12.title: Solum
0ce77d3acc12.sentence: In some soils the lower limit of the solum can be set only arbitrarily and needs to be defined in relation to the particular soil.

c5455ec54442.title: Solum
c5455ec54442.sentence: To conceive of hardened carbonate accumulations extending for 5 meters or more below the B horizon as part of the solum is more difficult.

5ab7a3908716.title: Solum
5ab7a3908716.sentence: At great depth, gleying is likely to be relict or related to processes that are more geological than pedological.

ef89720453d6.title: Soil
ef89720453d6.sentence: The living component of the soil is largely confined to the solum, and is generally more prominent in the A horizon.

a5080a4c987c.title: Soil horizon
a5080a4c987c.section: Horizons and layers according to the FAO Guidelines for Soil Description (2006) > Master horizons and layers
a5080a4c987c.sentence: H horizons or layers: These are layers of organic material.

17d3ea49b653.title: Soil horizon
17d3ea49b653.section: Horizons and layers according to the FAO Guidelines for Soil Description (2006) > Master horizons and layers
17d3ea49b653.sentence: Contrary to the O horizons, the H horizons are saturated with water for prolonged periods, or were once saturated but are now drained artificially.

62e370857228.title: Soil horizon
62e370857228.section: Horizons and layers according to the FAO Guidelines for Soil Description (2006) > Master horizons and layers
62e370857228.sentence: In many H horizons, the residues are predominantly sphagnum mosses (peat mosses).

692a63a1036a.title: Soil horizon
692a63a1036a.section: Horizons and layers according to the FAO Guidelines for Soil Description (2006) > Master horizons and layers
692a63a1036a.sentence: H horizons may be overlain by O horizons that especially form after drainage.

0064a10d7080.sentence: R layers: These consist of hard bedrock underlying the soil.

36175933ee4c.title: Soil horizon
36175933ee4c.section: Horizons and layers according to the FAO Guidelines for Soil Description (2006) > Master horizons and layers
36175933ee4c.sentence: Granite, basalt, quartzite, and indurated limestone or sandstone are examples of bedrock that are designated R. Air-dry or drier chunks of an R layer, when placed in water, will not slake within 24 hours.

f79910eb566e.title: Soil horizon
f79910eb566e.section: Horizons and layers according to the FAO Guidelines for Soil Description (2006) > Master horizons and layers

216ad95a206e.sentence: If there is no lithologic discontinuity between the solum and the R horizon, the R horizon resembles the parent material of the solum.

d44f9963eb83.title: Soil morphology

6498b5c0cd90.title: Soil morphology
6498b5c0cd90.sentence: If there are layers distinct enough to be separate horizons, but similar enough to receive the same master and suffix letters, sequential numbers are added to the end of the designation to distinguish the horizons (such as A, Bt1, Bt2, Bt3, C).

3b68e2632182.title: Soil morphology
