cb806f3059e4.sentence: Example: A/B and B/A. The master horizon symbols may be followed by the lowercase letters indicating subordinate characteristics (see below).

6040cde74489.title: Soil horizon
6040cde74489.section: Horizons and layers according to the World Reference Base for Soil Resources > Transitional layers
6040cde74489.sentence: If the characteristics of two or more master layers are superimposed to each other, the master symbols are combined without anything in between, the dominant one first, each one followed by its suffixes.

6929e0f17dfd.title: Soil horizon
6929e0f17dfd.section: Horizons and layers according to the World Reference Base for Soil Resources > Transitional layers
6929e0f17dfd.sentence: Examples: AhBw, BwAh, AhE, EAh, EBg, BgE, BwC, CBw, BsC, CBs.

fa5eb317a7aa.title: Soil horizon
fa5eb317a7aa.section: Horizons and layers according to the World Reference Base for Soil Resources > Transitional layers
fa5eb317a7aa.sentence: Examples: Bt/E (interfingering of E material into a Bt horizon), C/Bt (Bt horizon forming lamellae within a C layer).

976297922ca9.title: Soil horizon
976297922ca9.section: Horizons according to the Australian Soil and Land Survey Field Handbook (2009) > Horizons
976297922ca9.sentence: The A3, B1, and B3 horizons are not tightly defined, and their use is generally at the discretion of the individual worker.

09ebcf3e1a71.title: Soil horizon
09ebcf3e1a71.section: Horizons and layers according to the FAO Guidelines for Soil Description (2006) > Transitional horizons and layers
09ebcf3e1a71.sentence: The I, L and W symbols are not used in transitional horizon designations.

f303ad7b330d.title: Fragipan
f303ad7b330d.sentence: A fragipan is a diagnostic horizon in USDA soil taxonomy.

5c3e4a931f3d.title: Fragipan
5c3e4a931f3d.sentence: They are altered subsurface soil layers that restrict water flow and root penetration.

23f067496a87.title: Fragipan
23f067496a87.sentence: In soil descriptions, they are commonly denoted by a Bx or Btx symbol.

56368077f281.title: Fragipan
56368077f281.sentence: Fragipans are similar to a duripan in how they affect land-use limitations.

1e20e4c31dd3.title: Soil horizon
1e20e4c31dd3.section: Diagnostic soil horizons > Diagnostic horizons in the World Reference Base for Soil Resources (WRB)

7ac517937c35.title: Fragipan
7ac517937c35.sentence: - The layer has, in 60 percent or more of the volume, a firm or firmer rupture-resistance class, a brittle manner of failure at or near field capacity, and virtually no roots; and

80240a6d2d54.title: Fragipan
80240a6d2d54.sentence: - Air-dry fragments of the natural soil fabric, 5 to 10 cm in diameter, from more than 50 percent of the layer slake when they are submerged in water; and

fc1783793e52.title: Fragipan
fc1783793e52.sentence: - The requirement that a fragipan can slake in water separates it from a petrocalcic horizon and a duripan.

afcd69485b8f.title: Fragipan
afcd69485b8f.sentence: - A fragipan does not contain calcium carbonate or magnesium carbonate, which would make it a petrocalcic horizon.

335c77ca47a9.title: Fragipan
335c77ca47a9.sentence: - The layer is not effervescent in dilute HCl.

5fdce42d9f2e.title: Fragipan
5fdce42d9f2e.sentence: Their formation can be attributed to compacting of soils by glaciers during the last ice age, physical ripening, permafrost processes, or other events that occurred in the pleistocene age.

4f8980b7da8b.title: Fragipan
4f8980b7da8b.sentence: Some fragipans inherit their properties from buried soils called paleosols.

567deb26592b.title: Fragipan
567deb26592b.sentence: It has been proposed that fragipans form by hydroconsolidation, that is the collapse of the soil structure due to loading and wetting.

e899c0c568d2.title: Fragipan
e899c0c568d2.sentence: The first record of fragipans is probably that by John Hardcastle in New Zealand in the 1880s.

7c66dfb999ec.title: Topsoil
7c66dfb999ec.sentence: A variety of soil mixtures are sold commercially as topsoil.

622caf4f3303.title: Topsoil
622caf4f3303.sentence: Natural topsoil which has been mined and conditioned for human use and makes up the bulk of commercial topsoil available.

0cb878a935c6.title: Topsoil
0cb878a935c6.sentence: Manufactured topsoil based on minerals, biosolids, compost and/or paper mill sludge is available commercially.

56b9fb787d4c.title: Topsoil
56b9fb787d4c.sentence: Typical uses for this product are improving gardens and lawns or for use in container gardens.

452e5ce05fa5.title: Topsoil
452e5ce05fa5.sentence: Topsoil is also used for proper surface grading near residential buildings.

979a289c8203.title: Topsoil
979a289c8203.sentence: Topsoil products typically are not as suitable for potting plants or growing fruit and veg as potting soil or compost.

c66157a2a601.title: Topsoil
c66157a2a601.sentence: Commercially available topsoil (manufactured or naturally occurring) in the United Kingdom must be classified to British Standard BS 3882, with the current version dated 2015.

91f5af2e3da9.title: Topsoil
91f5af2e3da9.sentence: The standard has several classifications of topsoil with the final classification requiring material to meet certain threshold criteria such as nutrient content, extractable phytotoxic elements, particle size distribution, organic matter content, carbon:nitrogen ratio, electrical conductivity, loss on ignition, pH, chemical and physical contamination.

68c65d26a7dd.title: Topsoil
68c65d26a7dd.sentence: In the United States, there is no federal, legal definition of the word topsoil when used in commerce.

d3e2b0ef7b0b.title: Topsoil
d3e2b0ef7b0b.sentence: More traditional examples of artificial plant-growth media include terra preta and potting mix.

a1473cb8809d.title: Topsoil
a1473cb8809d.sentence: An open-cut coal mine in Victoria, Australia, was rehabilitated with low-quality artificial topsoil made from local materials.

e957a93ab3f8.title: Ice wedge
e957a93ab3f8.sentence: An ice wedge is a crack in the ground formed by a narrow or thin piece of ice that measures up to 3–4 meters in length at ground level and extends downwards into the ground up to several meters.

f5f46af7a16c.title: Ice wedge
f5f46af7a16c.sentence: There are many theories that attempt to explain the origin of ice wedges but only one has been consistently supported by most prominent scientists: the thermal contraction theory.

f33baff0903c.title: Ice wedge
f33baff0903c.sentence: The thermal contraction theory posits that during the winter months, thermal contraction cracks form only a few cm wide and a couple of metres deep because of the extreme cold weather.

05da87fcf765.title: Ice wedge
05da87fcf765.sentence: Over the next few months, the snow melts and the remaining water fills the cracks and the permafrost below the surface freezes it.

0b65aa63f2ce.title: Ice wedge
0b65aa63f2ce.sentence: The next winter the cold refreezes and cracks the already forming ice wedge, opening a way for the melting snow of spring to fill the empty crack.

0164306bfeab.title: Ice wedge
0164306bfeab.sentence: The mean annual air temperature thought needed to form ice wedges is −6° to −8 °C or colder.

1aae93230b12.title: Ice wedge
1aae93230b12.sentence: Ice wedges usually appear in a polygonal pattern known as ice wedge polygons.

6da440c51433.title: Ice wedge
6da440c51433.sentence: In relation to ice wedges, this means that epigenetic ice wedges are found to form in preexisting permafrost, and are not formed at the same time as the permafrost meaning they are much younger than the surrounding material.

81a7f04e726c.title: Ice wedge
81a7f04e726c.sentence: This means that epigenetic ice wedges can grow to at most 3–5 meters in width, but stay roughly the same depth/height as when they had formed.

2e074d994967.title: Ice wedge
2e074d994967.sentence: This is because syngenetic ice wedges grow as the upper permafrost surface rises in response to the addition of material on the ground surface.

492c327f945b.title: Ice wedge
492c327f945b.sentence: If this is the case, the ice wedge can reach depths of 25 meters, but the average is much less.

feb2ecf440f1.title: Ice wedge
feb2ecf440f1.sentence: In areas of past permafrost, ice wedges have melted and are no longer filled with ice.

74ca63d387e3.title: Ice wedge
74ca63d387e3.sentence: The wedge, which is now empty, is filled with sediment and dirt from the surrounding walls.

59b47cb3e286.title: Ice wedge
59b47cb3e286.sentence: These are called ice wedge casts and can be used to estimate the climate of hundreds of thousands of years ago.

5d46cb3d720c.title: Ice wedge
5d46cb3d720c.sentence: Anti-syngenetic ice wedge were first observed in 1990 during the fieldwork of J. Ross Mackay.

0662f646cae1.title: Soil morphology
0662f646cae1.sentence: In addition to the horizon name, the distinctness and topography of each horizon's lower boundary are described.

386cf9c39330.title: Soil morphology
386cf9c39330.sentence: Boundary distinctness is determined by how accurately the border between horizons can be identified and may be very abrupt, abrupt, clear, gradual, or diffuse.

3888cdf4f91b.title: Soil morphology
3888cdf4f91b.sentence: Boundary topography refers to the horizontal variation of the border, which is often not parallel to the soil surface and may even be discontinuous.

a9b19aff2d7e.title: Soil morphology
a9b19aff2d7e.sentence: Topography categories include smooth, wavy, irregular, and broken.

0da098275156.title: Cecil (soil)
0da098275156.sentence: Ap—0 to 8 inches (200 mm); dark yellowish brown (10YR 4/4) sandy loam; weak medium granular structure; very friable; slightly acid; abrupt smooth boundary.

7b621ffa37e2.title: Cecil (soil)
7b621ffa37e2.sentence: Bt1—8 to 26 inches (660 mm); red (10R 4/8) clay; moderate medium subangular blocky structure; firm; sticky, plastic; common clay films on faces of peds; few fine flakes of mica; strongly acid; gradual wavy boundary.

3622eb11e80b.title: Duripan
3622eb11e80b.sentence: A duripan is a diagnostic soil horizon of the USDA soil taxonomy that is cemented by illuvial silica into a subsurface hardpan.

52f8d70938a5.title: Duripan
52f8d70938a5.sentence: In soil descriptions, they are most often denoted by the symbol Bqm.

1867133c75e1.title: Duripan
1867133c75e1.sentence: The closest equivalent in the Canadian system of soil classification is called a duric horizon, although it does not mean exactly the same thing as a duripan in the United States.

6567f460a8b2.title: Petrocalcic horizon
6567f460a8b2.sentence: Petrocalcic horizons are similar to a duripan (ST – WRB: petroduric horizon) and a petrogypsic horizon (WRB) in how they affect land-use limitations.

e1b2170da6a2.title: Duripan
e1b2170da6a2.sentence: They form almost exclusively in arid or Mediterranean climates, and can be as hard as concrete, which makes plowing very difficult or impossible.

bbe682e8cb27.title: Duripan
bbe682e8cb27.sentence: Soils that include duripans are generally used for grazing or wildlife habitat, and are seldom cultivated.

08546ad32727.title: Duripan
08546ad32727.sentence: Volcanic glass weathers rapidly, providing an ample supply of soluble silica to cement the underlying soil.

703b11cf4436.title: Duripan
703b11cf4436.sentence: Other common sources of the silica cementing agent are iron-magnesium minerals and feldspars.

95f35b7022c6.title: Duripan
95f35b7022c6.sentence: The weathered silica is mostly transported by water into the subsoil, where it precipitates and forms microaggregates that gradually grow into a full-fledged duripan.

17b7292d695e.title: Duripan
17b7292d695e.sentence: - The pan is cemented or indurated in more than 50 percent of the volume of some horizon; and

7a7d928c1f2d.title: Duripan
7a7d928c1f2d.sentence: - Because of lateral continuity, roots can penetrate the pan only along vertical fractures with a horizontal spacing of 10 cm or more.

c946532fcfee.title: Duripan
c946532fcfee.sentence: - Less than fifty percent of the volume of air-dry fragments slakes in 1 N HCl even during prolonged soaking, but more than 50 percent slakes in concentrated KOH or NaOH or in alternating acid and alkali; and

2094b4fb902c.title: Duripan
2094b4fb902c.sentence: - The purpose of the water, HCl, and KOH tests is to separate a duripan from a Petrocalcic Horizon or fragipan.

d14517e2e370.title: Petrocalcic horizon
d14517e2e370.sentence: A petrocalcic horizon is a diagnostic horizon in the USDA soil taxonomy (ST) and in the World Reference Base for Soil Resources (WRB).

ad2440205a09.title: Petrocalcic horizon
ad2440205a09.sentence: They are formed when secondary calcium carbonate or other carbonates accumulate in the subsoil to the extent that the soil becomes cemented into a hardpan.

208c40472184.title: Petrocalcic horizon
208c40472184.sentence: - The horizon is cemented or indurated by carbonates, with or without silica or other cementing agents; and

66d877877587.title: Petrocalcic horizon
66d877877587.sentence: - Because of lateral continuity, roots can penetrate only along vertical fractures with a horizontal spacing of 10 cm or more; and

c4982d903a95.title: Petrocalcic horizon
c4982d903a95.sentence: They form in soil parent material that contains calcium carbonate or receive regular inputs of carbonates through dust.

39a06a9cacff.title: Petrocalcic horizon
39a06a9cacff.sentence: Carbonates are transported into the subsoil by water that precipitates the carbonates in the subsoil upon evaporation, eventually forming a massive, continuous layer of cemented carbonates.

cc710f6e4b99.title: Petrocalcic horizon
cc710f6e4b99.sentence: Petrocalcic horizons are typically found in older soils and are considered a mark of advanced soil evolution.

0cd17a6fadbb.title: Petrocalcic horizon
0cd17a6fadbb.sentence: Most petrocalcic formed before the Holocene age.

84481276b3f6.title: Petrocalcic horizon
84481276b3f6.sentence: Calcium carbonates are found in alkaline soils, which are typical of arid and semiarid climates.

d57c6ace0b88.title: Petrocalcic horizon
d57c6ace0b88.sentence: A common field test for the presence of carbonates is application of hydrochloric acid to the soil, which indicates by fizzing and bubbling the presence of calcium carbonates.

f6c2e09c1823.title: Claypan
f6c2e09c1823.sentence: Claypan is a dense, compact, slowly permeable layer in the subsoil.

20c3bf73a11d.title: Claypan
20c3bf73a11d.sentence: It has a much higher clay content than the overlying material, from which it is separated by a sharply defined boundary.

00782d362472.title: Claypan
00782d362472.sentence: The dense structure restricts root growth and water infiltration.

f7959cc482c7.title: Claypan
f7959cc482c7.sentence: Therefore, a perched water table might form on top of the claypan.

b908adb9533d.title: Claypan
b908adb9533d.sentence: In the Canadian classification system, claypan is defined as a clay-enriched illuvial B (Bt) horizon.

c8eca8a3ea6d.title: Claypan
c8eca8a3ea6d.sentence: Claypan is present in a wide area of the central United States (about 4 million ha) across multiple states such as Kansas, Oklahoma, and Illinois.

a53cbff39c8e.title: Claypan
a53cbff39c8e.sentence: It can also be found in Australia throughout the south-west Queensland.

a020fc849f68.title: Claypan
a020fc849f68.sentence: The formation of the claypan relates to a lack of vegetation coverage, soil particle size distribution, and high rainfall.

e220a9d4065b.title: Claypan
e220a9d4065b.sentence: When the raindrops hit on bare soil with high energy, the fine sand, silt, and clay particles are re-arranged to plug all the pore spaces.

cf896ab6e272.title: Claypan
cf896ab6e272.sentence: When all the pores are filled, a packed layer is formed to limit the water infiltration.

0518ef99c170.title: Claypan
0518ef99c170.sentence: The dominant material is the montmorillonite clay material which has a high swell and shrinks characteristics depending on the soil water content.

5e142633756e.title: Claypan
5e142633756e.sentence: The water removal results in shrinkage of clay, and the soil becomes dry and hard.

c80ee7af9dd8.title: Claypan
c80ee7af9dd8.sentence: The high moisture content results in wet and sticky clay texture.

c850be016117.title: Claypan
c850be016117.sentence: The water permeability is restricted in the claypan layer resulting in low soil aeration.

dfaed29f4285.title: Claypan
dfaed29f4285.sentence: The water-holding capability of the claypan is high.

2aaa7bda2139.title: Claypan
2aaa7bda2139.sentence: However, most of the stored water is not available for the plant since water evaporates frequently and soil pore size is tiny.

264808174579.title: Claypan
264808174579.sentence: The acidic, clay-rich characteristics of the claypan lead to phosphorus (P) sorption to clay minerals.

c8de0854986e.title: Claypan
c8de0854986e.sentence: Even though the total P content in the claypan is relatively high, they are strongly attracted by the clay particles that are not available for plant use.

85384d62065e.title: Claypan
85384d62065e.sentence: Therefore, a high amount of P fertilizer is required to increase the available P for plant absorption.

7c7feac0e9fd.title: Claypan
7c7feac0e9fd.sentence: Different from P, the high content of potassium (K) in the claypan is available for plant use which reduces the application of potassium fertilizer.

9467d2975171.title: Claypan
9467d2975171.sentence: Soil with a claypan layer is highly vulnerable to soil erosion.

994c39cfa7c1.title: Claypan
994c39cfa7c1.sentence: The low water infiltration rate and the perched water table form on top of the claypan layer largely increase the surface runoff during precipitation with a long duration or high intensity.

5e69570c0cf0.title: Claypan
5e69570c0cf0.sentence: The runoff water can remove the topsoil with mostly organic matter.

55bb6605ccf4.title: Silcrete
55bb6605ccf4.sentence: Silcrete is an indurated (resists crumbling or powdering) soil duricrust formed when surface soil, sand, and gravel are cemented by dissolved silica.

90846ea53b36.title: Silcrete
90846ea53b36.sentence: The formation of silcrete is similar to that of calcrete, formed by calcium carbonate, and ferricrete, formed by iron oxide.

a5186b95e331.title: Silcrete
a5186b95e331.sentence: It is a hard and resistant material, and though different in origin and nature, appears similar to quartzite.

01881046f070.title: Silcrete
01881046f070.sentence: There are two types of silcrete that form in nature microcrystalline quartz and lacustrine silcretes.

e236e349ab9a.title: Silcrete
e236e349ab9a.sentence: The microcrystalline forms in arid environments with increased levels of pH and are characterized by alterations of silicate cappings.

a2b0722eed92.title: Silcrete
a2b0722eed92.sentence: Lacustrine silcretes form in environments that have decreases in pH.

47465fdc8d5a.title: Silcrete
47465fdc8d5a.sentence: Silcrete is common in the arid regions of Australia and Africa often forming the resistant cap rock on features such as the breakaways of the Stuart Range of South Australia.

ee2ffe90cdd8.title: Silcrete
ee2ffe90cdd8.sentence: In Australia, silcrete was widely used by Aboriginal people for stone tool manufacture, and as such, it was a tradeable commodity, and silcrete tools can be found in areas that have no silcrete groundmass at all, similar to the European use of flint.

07db74a9bc0b.title: Silcrete
07db74a9bc0b.sentence: Heating changes the stone structure making it more easily flaked.

1b1cd422943e.title: Silcrete
1b1cd422943e.sentence: This process may have been the first use of so-called pyrotechnology by early mankind.

5d5aec555f85.title: Silcrete
5d5aec555f85.sentence: The peoples of the African Middle Stone Age (MSA) showed a preference for silcrete tools, sourcing the material from up to 200 km to use in place of more accessible quartz and quartzite.

594f7d043aa6.title: Silcrete
594f7d043aa6.sentence: In South Africa at Pinnacle Point researchers have determined that two types of silcrete tools were developed between 60,000 and 80,000 years ago and used the heat treatment technique.

e0da53db3d8d.title: Umbric horizon
e0da53db3d8d.sentence: The umbric horizon (Latin: umbra, shade) is a thick, dark coloured, surface soil horizon rich in organic matter.

e8ad02487f1b.title: Umbric horizon
e8ad02487f1b.sentence: Normally it has a pH of less than 5.5 representing a base saturation of less than 50 percent.

0a09714ba281.title: Umbric horizon
0a09714ba281.sentence: - Munsell colours with a chroma and value ≤ 3 when moist and a value ≤ 5 when dry, both on slightly crushed samples.

c5ba6c685bd2.title: Umbric horizon
c5ba6c685bd2.sentence: - Soil organic carbon content of ≥ 0.6% throughout the thickness of mixed horizon; and

c3979586cb4e.title: Umbric horizon
c3979586cb4e.sentence: - A thickness of ≥ 100 mm if resting directly on hard rock; ≥ 200 mm else.

201f2724529d.title: Umbric horizon
201f2724529d.sentence: An indication for soil acidity is a rooting pattern whereby the roots tend to be horizontal.

fdecf77f61e8.title: Umbric horizon
fdecf77f61e8.sentence: Similar thick, dark coloured, organic-rich, base-desaturated surface horizons occur in anthropedogenic horizons from human activities such as deep cultivation, kitchen middens and the addition of organic manures etc. These horizons can usually be differentiated by the presence of artifacts, spade marks or by checking the agricultural history of the area.

0d88db4f71fb.title: Ferricrete
0d88db4f71fb.sentence: Ferricrete is a hard, erosion-resistant layer of sedimentary rock, usually conglomerate or breccia, that has been cemented into a duricrust by iron oxides.

7918d1f490cd.title: Ferricrete
7918d1f490cd.sentence: The iron oxide cements are derived from the oxidation of percolating solutions of iron salts.

e41f0bb5c293.title: Ferricrete
e41f0bb5c293.sentence: The name is a combination of ferruginous and concrete.

920b02f38df6.title: Ferricrete
920b02f38df6.sentence: Ferricretes form at or near the land surface and may contain non-local sediments that have been transported from outside the immediate area of the deposit.

d7d6d649513d.title: Ferricrete
d7d6d649513d.sentence: Synonyms include ferruginous duricrust, hardpan and ironpan.

16af91b0cf3c.title: Laterite
16af91b0cf3c.sentence: In some places laterites contain pisolites and ferricrete, and they may be found in elevated positions as result of relief inversion.

310c9635b68b.title: Laterite
310c9635b68b.sentence: To the contrary, in the wetter parts of laterites subject to leaching ferricretes have been suggested to form.

dc5ecc091f80.title: Ferricrete
dc5ecc091f80.sentence: Ferricrete is used widely in South Africa to create roads in rural areas.

e53756816596.title: Ferricrete
e53756816596.sentence: It is better known in these regions by its Afrikaans name "Koffieklip" (coffee stone).

8aec98e9b5a2.title: Cutans
8aec98e9b5a2.sentence: Cutans are the modification of the soil texture, or soil structure, at natural surfaces (particle, pore, or ped) in soil materials due to illuviation.

9de412ae203b.title: Cutans
9de412ae203b.sentence: Cutans are oriented deposits which can be composed of any of the component substances of the soil material.

f29595703995.title: Cutans
f29595703995.sentence: Cutans may include clay skins or coatings of silica, sesquioxide, manganese, ferromanganese, soil organic matter or carbonate.

fe958dca2f23.title: Cutans
fe958dca2f23.sentence: Cutans provide physical evidence, observable in the field, as to the degree and nature of pedogenesis.

5cf841bcf908.title: Cutans
5cf841bcf908.sentence: The ability to assess cutans is a core skill in soil morphology and paleopedology.

e3912ebd791f.title: Clay cutan
e3912ebd791f.sentence: Clay Cutans are most easily recognized under cross polarized light where they anisotropic.

d2a5ffc680a3.title: Clay cutan
d2a5ffc680a3.sentence: Cutans usually show lineations caused by the preferred orientation of clay minerals.

15e7c376cb97.title: Clay cutan
15e7c376cb97.sentence: While the originally openings are commonly lost through geologic time and diagenesis, the cutanic fabric remains as evidence.

7b9fd1a16f35.title: Clay cutan
7b9fd1a16f35.sentence: They are one of the most diagnostic features of paleosols.

d24591878c17.title: Pedocal
d24591878c17.sentence: Pedocal is a subdivision of the zonal soil order.

ea0d9c8b5ff5.title: Pedocal
ea0d9c8b5ff5.sentence: It is a class of soil which forms in semiarid and arid regions.

a5224185e1fc.title: Pedocal
a5224185e1fc.sentence: It is rich in calcium carbonate and has low soil organic matter.

289ecf02cf39.title: Pedocal
289ecf02cf39.sentence: With only a thin A horizon (topsoil), and intermittent precipitation calcite, other soluble minerals ordinarily removed by water may build up in the B horizon (subsoil) forming a cemented layer known as caliche.

c52e7c5fe38d.title: Curtis F. Marbut
c52e7c5fe38d.sentence: At the highest level of classification the soils were divided into pedocals and pedalfers.

bb2780087b9c.title: Curtis F. Marbut
bb2780087b9c.sentence: The pedalfers began about at the udic border and referred to soils rich in aluminium (alumen) and iron (ferrous).

72c689ba1f78.title: Pedocal
72c689ba1f78.sentence: It is not used in the current United States system of soil classification but the term commonly shows up in college geology texts.

b65e3de6ad7f.title: Paralithic
b65e3de6ad7f.sentence: A paralithic horizon is a weathered layer of bedrock.

01513596d703.title: Paralithic
01513596d703.sentence: The term comes from the Greek words para, meaning "akin to", and lithic, meaning "stony".

bc0f3cb797c5.title: Gelisol
bc0f3cb797c5.sentence: They have 80% or more organic materials from the soil surface to a depth of 50 cm (20 in) or to a glacic layer or densic, lithic, or paralithic contact, whichever is shallowest.

d7a7ba27e6c9.title: Slickenside
d7a7ba27e6c9.section: Other types of slickensides > Slickensides in soils
d7a7ba27e6c9.sentence: In pedology, the study of soils in their natural environments, a slickenside is a surface of the cracks produced in soils containing a high proportion of swelling clays.

f66800180d57.title: Slickenside
f66800180d57.section: Other types of slickensides > Slickensides in soils
f66800180d57.sentence: Slickensides are a type of cutan.

1e978625661b.title: Slickenside
1e978625661b.section: Other types of slickensides > Slickensides in soils
1e978625661b.sentence: In the Australian Soil Classification, slickensides, along with lenticular structural aggregates, are an indicator of a vertisol.

32bd2ed6611b.title: Slickenside
32bd2ed6611b.sentence: In geology, a slickenside is a smoothly polished surface caused by frictional movement between rocks along a fault.

e2df799763c8.title: Slickenside
e2df799763c8.sentence: This surface is typically striated with linear features, called slickenlines, in the direction of movement.

fcaf84a8bb8a.title: Cambic horizon
fcaf84a8bb8a.sentence: Cambic horizon (Latin: Cambiare, to change) is a diagnostic sub-surface horizon of a soil experiencing pedogenic change.

4f1a23f7b4fe.title: Cambic horizon
4f1a23f7b4fe.sentence: Development is minimal and it is cambic if it does not meet the Taxonomic requirements to classify in another horizon.

1496f37c075e.title: Cambic horizon
1496f37c075e.sentence: Cambic horizons do not consist of appreciable illuviated material such as clay, organic carbon, iron, and aluminum oxyhydroxides, carbonate, gypsum, or soluble salts.

6e462a056079.title: Cambic horizon
6e462a056079.sentence: The particles size must be as finer or finer than loamy fine sand or very fine sand.

3017b0789a07.title: Cambic horizon
3017b0789a07.sentence: Cambic horizons are found most in Mollisols and Inceptisols, but can also be found in Andisols where its designation is Bw or Bg in all three.

ed47c2b40d61.title: Cambic horizon
ed47c2b40d61.sentence: It has less clay content than an argillic horizon but is still a visible layer.

b30ffac57d2b.title: Cambic horizon
b30ffac57d2b.sentence: In the pedogenesis process under a chronosequence, once the soil develops into an alfisol, the Cambic horizon will develop into an argillic (Bt) horizon.

4e4da9d166d1.title: Tepetate
4e4da9d166d1.sentence: Tepetate (Spanish tepetate; Nahuatl tepetlatl) is a Mexican term for a geological horizon, hardened by compaction or cementation, found in Mexican volcanic regions.

15a732e8756e.title: Tepetate
15a732e8756e.sentence: Tepetates at the surface are problematic for agriculture, because of their hardness, poor drainage, and poor fertility.

5d76da7f7882.title: Tepetate
5d76da7f7882.sentence: When tepetates lie under the soil, they present a risk for erosion and landslides, because water runs off laterally, rather than being absorbed.

d6b5d9a52a05.title: Albeluvisols
d6b5d9a52a05.sentence: An Albeluvisol is a soil with a thin, dark surface horizon on a bleached subsurface horizon (an albic horizon) that tongues into a clay illuviation (Bt) horizon.

118f6a742607.title: World Reference Base for Soil Resources
118f6a742607.section: Examples > Example for naming a soil with the WRB
118f6a742607.sentence: - albic horizon (the claric material is the result of a soil-forming process, here: downward migration of clay minerals and oxides)
118f6a742607.key: World Reference Base for Soil Resources

35fbe7560fee.title: World Reference Base for Soil Resources
35fbe7560fee.section: Examples > Example for naming a soil with the WRB
35fbe7560fee.sentence: From the list of the principal qualifiers, Stagnic (stagnic properties and reducing conditions) and Albic (light colours resulting from a soil-forming process) apply.
35fbe7560fee.key: World Reference Base for Soil Resources

45d3e917292f.title: Soil horizon
45d3e917292f.section: Diagnostic soil horizons > Diagnostic horizons in the World Reference Base for Soil Resources (WRB)

0f66a8f2e0a2.title: USDA soil taxonomy
0f66a8f2e0a2.sentence: - Spodosols: Must have spodic horizon within 2 m of soil surface and without andic properties; Usually have albic horizon; high in Fe, Al oxides and humus accumulation; acidic soils; common in coniferous or boreal forests; 2.6% of global and 3.3% of U.S. ice-free land.

b555150499e1.title: Stagnosol
b555150499e1.sentence: The topsoil can also be completely bleached (albic horizon).

443f416562db.title: Plinthosol
443f416562db.sentence: These soils often show signs of eluviation, including an albic horizon beneath an umbric surface layer.

180b77f5bb90.title: Calcareous
180b77f5bb90.sentence: Additionally, these soils may have a calcic horizon, a layer of secondary accumulation of carbonates (usually calciumcarbonate or magnesiumcarbonate) in excess of 15% calcium carbonate equivalent and at least 5% more carbonate than an underlying layer.

0264bc35a381.title: Calcid
0264bc35a381.sentence: Calcids have a calcic, hypercalcic, or petrocalcic horizon with its/their upper boundary within 1.0 m of the soil surface.

083af01bba78.title: Calciorthid
083af01bba78.sentence: In the U.S. Soil Taxonomy, they fall under the Aridisols (dry soils) and are distinguished by a calcic horizon where calcium carbonate has accumulated.

1de58ab23fdd.title: Ustic
1de58ab23fdd.section: Geography and Climate of Ustic Soils
1de58ab23fdd.sentence: Most Ustolls display an accumulation of calcium carbonate in the soil profile - a calcic horizon.

123cc8a9f0ec.title: Paleopedology
123cc8a9f0ec.sentence: For example, aridisols have been redefined as soils that possess a calcic horizon of less than 1 meter in depth.

97994362d8fb.title: Argillic
97994362d8fb.sentence: In USDA soil taxonomy, the argillic is considered a diagnostic subsurface horizon, meaning that is not part of the epipedon (the upper part of the soil) and is used to describe higher soil taxonomy categories.

4f86615ff1ee.title: Soil horizon
4f86615ff1ee.section: Diagnostic soil horizons > Diagnostic horizons in the USDA soil taxonomy (ST)

3e0c3efb015e.title: Soil horizon
3e0c3efb015e.section: Diagnostic soil horizons > Diagnostic horizons in the USDA soil taxonomy (ST)

e62b9cd9797d.title: Soil horizon
e62b9cd9797d.section: Diagnostic soil horizons > Diagnostic horizons in the USDA soil taxonomy (ST)

9a7530d40b14.title: Soil horizon
9a7530d40b14.section: Diagnostic soil horizons > Diagnostic horizons in the USDA soil taxonomy (ST)

455581459120.title: Soil horizon
455581459120.section: Diagnostic soil horizons > Diagnostic horizons in the USDA soil taxonomy (ST)

3f363b635579.title: Mollisol
3f363b635579.sentence: This fertile surface horizon, called a mollic epipedon, is the defining diagnostic feature of Mollisols.

60037e0501fa.title: Mollisol
60037e0501fa.sentence: Mollic epipedons are created by long-term addition of organic materials derived from plant roots and typically have soft, granular soil structure.

56f037743a9e.title: USDA soil taxonomy
56f037743a9e.sentence: - Histosols: Must have histic epipedon; usually aquic soil moisture regime; no diagnostic subsurface horizons; rapid decomposition when aerated; peat or bog; >20% organic matter; organic soil materials extending down to an impermeable layer or with an organic layer that is more than 40 cm thick and without andic properties; commonly in wetlands (swamps, marshes, etc.); 1.2% of global and 1.3% of U.S. ice-free land.

4fe0f587ba75.title: USDA soil taxonomy
4fe0f587ba75.sentence: - Entisols: Least soil profile development; ochric epipedon is common; no B horizons; most common order by surface area (16.3% of global and 12.2% of U.S. ice-free land).

e699c6876eae.title: USDA soil taxonomy
e699c6876eae.sentence: - Aridisols: Dry soil (i.e., must have aridic moisture regime); ochric epipedon is common; Sometimes argillic or natric horizon; must have some diagnostic subsurface horizon; commonly in deserts; 12.7% of global and 8.8% of U.S. ice-free land.

f05cf5c62e8a.title: Inceptisol
f05cf5c62e8a.sentence: Inceptisol profiles can vary greatly in their epipedons, horizons, and subsoil horizons, but usually have an ochric or umbric epipedon with a cambic subsoil horizon.

186a4d459d57.title: Inceptisol
186a4d459d57.sentence: - Anthrepts – Has a plaggen or anthropic epipedon, a sign of intense and prolonged human activity

a1975a221fe2.title: Argillic
a1975a221fe2.sentence: The kandic is a argillic horizon in which the clays are primarily 1:1 silicate clays causing the soil to have a low cation exchange capacity, meaning the soil does not store nutrients as well.

7dc135f4af9e.title: USDA soil taxonomy
7dc135f4af9e.sentence: - Alfisols: Must have argillic, natric, or kandic horizon; high-to-medium base saturation; moderately weathered; commonly form under boreal or broadleaf forests; rich in iron and aluminum; common in humid areas, semi-tropics, and mediterranean climates; 9.6% of global and 14.5% of U.S. ice-free land.

e1af8a56e172.title: USDA soil taxonomy
e1af8a56e172.sentence: - Ultisols: Must have argillic or kandic horizon; Low base saturation of <35% at 2 m depth or 75 cm below a fragipan; common in subtropical regions; often known as red clay soils; 8.5% of global & 9.6% of U.S. ice-free land.

6b75ba8e7d99.title: Nitisol
6b75ba8e7d99.sentence: Nitisols correlate with the kandic alfisols, ultisols and inceptisols of the USDA soil taxonomy.

1402cfb15a90.title: Acrisol
1402cfb15a90.sentence: In the USDA soil taxonomy, Acrisols correspond to the Humult, Udult, and Ustult suborders of the Ultisols and also to Oxisols with a kandic horizon and to some Alfisols.

f530a17f8cde.title: USDA soil taxonomy
f530a17f8cde.sentence: - Mollisols: Must have mollic epipedon; high base saturation of >50%; dark soils; some with argillic or natric horizons; common in grasslands; 6.9% of global and 22.4% of U.S. ice-free land.

639e2f2c8440.title: Mollisol
639e2f2c8440.sentence: Other soils which have a mollic epipedon are classified as Vertisols because high shrink swell characteristics and relatively high clay contents dominate over the mollic epipedon.

11c2e365429d.title: Mollisol
11c2e365429d.sentence: Mollic epipedons also occur in some Andisols but the andic properties take precedence.

7eb9ef0e924c.title: Greyzem
7eb9ef0e924c.sentence: These soils are all characterized by a mollic horizon and vegetation of dry forests and ephemeral grasses where accumulation of organic matter dominates over leaching processes.

92df43be9a88.title: Argillic
92df43be9a88.sentence: The natric is an argillic horizon in which high amounts of exchangeable sodium have accumulated.

2325c3f8227c.title: Solonetz
2325c3f8227c.sentence: They have, within the upper 100 cm of the soil profile, a so-called "natric horizon" ("natrium" is the Latin term for sodium).

c627be0e74f0.title: Alfisol
c627be0e74f0.sentence: Alfisols with a natric horizon are mainly Solonetz.

0ef94cda2871.title: Mollisol
0ef94cda2871.sentence: Mollisols with a natric horizon belong to the Solonetz.

edc81f52cff6.title: Argillic
edc81f52cff6.sentence: The argillic horizon is also important as starting point from which the kandic and natric horizons form, as well as commonly from which fragipans develop.

5b5fb1572a70.title: Soil horizon
5b5fb1572a70.section: Diagnostic soil horizons > Diagnostic horizons in the World Reference Base for Soil Resources (WRB)

7bb7f4250da5.title: Soil morphology
7bb7f4250da5.sentence: Pedons generally occupy between 1 and 10 m2 of surface land area and are the fundamental unit of field-based soil study.

a70825a06cf7.title: Canadian system of soil classification
a70825a06cf7.sentence: This unit of measurement is called the pedon, defined as a 3-dimensional body, commonly with lateral dimensions of 1 metre and depth of 1 to 2 metres.

0ee5900fe8ce.title: Soil
0ee5900fe8ce.sentence: It has been suggested that the pedon, a column of soil extending vertically from the surface to the underlying parent material and large enough to show the characteristics of all its horizons, could be subdivided in the humipedon (the living part, where most soil organisms are dwelling, corresponding to the humus form), the copedon (in intermediary position, where most weathering of minerals takes place) and the lithopedon (in contact with the subsoil).

b01ea2bbedff.title: Kerala Soil Museum
b01ea2bbedff.sentence: Each monolith was dug from the ground without disturbing its elements and was processed for one month or longer before being mounted for museum display.

23f760466509.title: Lysimeter
23f760466509.sentence: The soil contained in the field lysimeter can either be collected as a monolith (i.e., in one piece) or be reconstructed from the different layers present at the sampling site.

457edd799637.title: World Soil Museum
457edd799637.sentence: Some 80 soil monoliths are on display in the WSM, with a much larger collection (some 1000 from over 70 countries) stored and maintained in the repository.

b99d13fd866b.title: World Soil Museum
b99d13fd866b.sentence: For each soil monolith, there is supplemental information about the site of sampling (e.g. landscape, land use, parent material and climate), a detailed profile description for each soil horizon or layer, and data on chemical compositions and physical features.

ad539ad8c0d3.title: V.V. Dokuchaev Central Museum of Soil
ad539ad8c0d3.sentence: There are about 330 soil monoliths representing the global diversity of soils, with scientists' embarking on various expeditions to bring new monoliths every year.
ad539ad8c0d3.key: V.V. Dokuchaev Central Museum of Soil

a292a14da3a0.title: Brown podzolic
a292a14da3a0.sentence: Although classed with podzols because they have an iron-rich, or spodic horizon, they are, in fact intermediate between podzols and Brown earths.

4d547e14f8de.title: Polish Soil Classification
4d547e14f8de.sentence: That order groups all soils where main soil developing process was podzolisation, spodic horizon is diagnostic for that group.

99c8c1fa4b59.title: Soil formation
99c8c1fa4b59.sentence: Soil formation, also known as pedogenesis, is the process of soil genesis as regulated by the effects of place, environment, and history.

dd865a62602d.title: Soil formation
dd865a62602d.sentence: The starting point is weathering of freshly accumulated parent material.

1a35b729bd41.title: Soil formation
1a35b729bd41.sentence: New soils increase in depth by a combination of weathering and further deposition.

18c5dec74e12.title: Soil formation
18c5dec74e12.sentence: New soils can also deepen from dust deposition.

f09c1f37d82a.title: Soil formation
f09c1f37d82a.sentence: A variety of soil microbes (bacteria, archaea, fungi) feed on simple compounds (nutrients) released by weathering and produce organic acids and specialized proteins which contribute in turn to mineral weathering.

5259f12aec9c.title: Soil formation
5259f12aec9c.sentence: They also leave behind organic residues which contribute to humus formation.

0ea980ac3259.title: Soil formation
0ea980ac3259.sentence: In Sicily under Mediterranean climate the soil production rate due to weathering is approximately 1/10 mm per year.

393369d84bc4.title: Soil formation
393369d84bc4.sentence: Gradually soil is able to support higher forms of plants and animals, starting with pioneer species and proceeding along ecological succession to more complex plant and animal communities.

416f4144a974.title: Soil formation
416f4144a974.sentence: Topsoils deepen with the accumulation of humus originating from dead remains of higher plants and soil microbes.

6178e07ddb83.title: Soil formation
6178e07ddb83.sentence: They also deepen through mixing of organic matter with weathered minerals.

1542faa02026.title: Soil formation
1542faa02026.sentence: As soils mature, they develop soil horizons as organic matter accumulates and mineral weathering and leaching take place.

eb5a99aa3a48.title: Soil formation
eb5a99aa3a48.sentence: These alterations lead to the development of layers, termed soil horizons, distinguished by differences in color, structure, texture, and chemistry.

455f5d3c4465.title: Soil formation
455f5d3c4465.sentence: Biogeochemical processes act to both create and destroy order (anisotropy) within soils.

cb462e2be296.title: Soil formation
cb462e2be296.sentence: These features occur in patterns of soil type distribution, forming in response to differences in soil forming factors.

7212a1d9a0d1.title: Soil formation
7212a1d9a0d1.sentence: Pedogenesis is studied as a branch of pedology, the study of soil in its natural environment.

c1253e2c908d.title: Soil formation
c1253e2c908d.sentence: The study of pedogenesis is important to understanding soil distribution patterns in current (soil geography) and past (paleopedology) geologic periods.

78f142c057a0.title: Leaching (pedology)
78f142c057a0.sentence: In pedology, leaching is the removal of soluble materials from one zone in soil to another via water movement in the profile.

fc2aebb92437.title: Leaching (pedology)
fc2aebb92437.sentence: Leached and eluviated materials tend to be lost from topsoil and deposited in subsoil.

f4898317cc64.title: Leaching (pedology)
f4898317cc64.sentence: A soil horizon accumulating leached and eluviated materials is referred to as a zone of illuviation.

8f389033640d.title: Leaching (pedology)
8f389033640d.sentence: Laterite soil, which develops in regions with high temperature and heavy rainfall, is an example of this process in action.

211dd7ba3a55.title: Brown podzolic
211dd7ba3a55.sentence: The result is that leaching of the soil profile occurs; in which mobile chemicals are washed out of the topsoil, or A horizon, and accumulate lower down, in the B horizon.

f233c6f49271.title: Brown podzolic
f233c6f49271.sentence: This means that fresh supplies of iron and aluminium oxides (sesquioxides) are constantly being provided, and leaching ensures a net accumulation of these compounds in the B horizon, giving an orange-brown "rusty" colour which is very distinctive.

21b0e6930ad8.title: Canadian system of soil classification
21b0e6930ad8.sentence: An eluvial Ae (light grey, strongly leached) horizon usually is prominent above the Podzolic B horizon, but may be inconspicuous or absent.

d3da090e73b8.title: Canadian system of soil classification
d3da090e73b8.sentence: As leaching progresses, the salts and sodium ions are translocated downward.

0a1f9084bd28.title: Soil formation
0a1f9084bd28.sentence: Climate directly affects the rate of weathering and leaching.

cdd9056b963f.title: Soil formation
cdd9056b963f.sentence: - Very intense chemical weathering, leaching, and erosion in warm and humid regions where soil does not freeze

83f84e87a5e9.title: Laterite
83f84e87a5e9.sentence: Due to intensive leaching, laterite soils lack in fertility in comparison to other soils, however they respond readily to manuring and irrigation.

68d9de5b9915.title: Acid sulfate soil
68d9de5b9915.sentence: Reclaimed acid sulfate soils have a well-developed soil structure thanks to the abundance of trivalent cations (mainly Al+3) which have a very strong flocculating effect; they are well permeable, but infertile due to the leaching that has occurred.

5fb7846400fd.title: Leaching (chemistry)
5fb7846400fd.section: Leaching processes > Leaching processes in soil
5fb7846400fd.sentence: Most leaching comes from infiltration of water, a washing effect much like that described for the leaching process of biological substances.

00517dceedcf.title: Leaching (chemistry)
00517dceedcf.section: Leaching processes > Leaching processes in soil
00517dceedcf.sentence: Leaching is controlled largely by the hydraulic conductivity of the soil, which is dependent on particle size and relative density that the soil has been consolidated to via stress.

f716f3a707f6.title: Leaching (chemistry)
f716f3a707f6.section: Leaching processes > Leaching processes in soil
f716f3a707f6.sentence: The leaching is typically described by solute transport models, such as Darcy's Law, mass flow expressions, and diffusion-dispersion understandings.

28e22591a7e5.title: Soil formation
28e22591a7e5.sentence: Soil formation is influenced by at least five classic factors that are intertwined in the evolution of a soil.

cd46349c4d3e.title: Soil formation
cd46349c4d3e.sentence: They are: parent material, climate, topography (relief), soil organisms, and time.

13d006c8c23d.title: Soil formation
13d006c8c23d.sentence: When reordered to climate, organisms, relief, parent material, and time, they form the acronym CLORPT.

1f8fcad11108.title: Soil formation
1f8fcad11108.sentence: The mineral material from which a soil forms is called parent material.

97c913fd2af8.title: Soil formation
97c913fd2af8.sentence: As the parent rock is chemically and physically weathered, transported, deposited and precipitated, it is transformed into a soil.

638bc4dcc703.title: Soil formation
638bc4dcc703.sentence: Climate is the dominant factor in soil formation, and soils show the distinctive characteristics of the climate zones in which they form, with a feedback to climate through transfer of carbon stocked in soil horizons back to the atmosphere.

1e3dd410f4cc.title: Soil formation
1e3dd410f4cc.sentence: The topographical setting may either hasten or retard the work of climatic forces.

6e6f81e6183d.title: Soil formation
6e6f81e6183d.sentence: Each soil has a unique combination of microbial, plant, animal and human influences acting upon it.

cadf2e4026d7.title: Soil formation
cadf2e4026d7.sentence: Time is a factor in the interactions of all the above.

b9e84d51786b.title: Soil formation
b9e84d51786b.sentence: That time period depends strongly on climate, parent material, relief, and biotic activity.

aa92ce787fd6.title: 1938 USDA soil taxonomy
aa92ce787fd6.sentence: The 1938 soil taxonomy divided soils into three orders dependent on dominant soil forming factors.

41b927fc9be2.title: 1938 USDA soil taxonomy
41b927fc9be2.sentence: Intrazonal soils have more or less well-defined soil profile characteristics that reflect the dominant influence of some resident factor of relief or parent material over the classic zonal effects of climate and vegetation.

89caa2ee7210.title: Paleosol
89caa2ee7210.sentence: In geoscience, paleosol (palaeosol in Great Britain and Australia) is an ancient soil that formed in the past.

7d54943d0cae.title: Paleosol
7d54943d0cae.sentence: In geology and paleontology, a paleosol is a former soil preserved by burial underneath either sediments (alluvium or loess) or volcanic deposits (lava flows or volcanic ash), which in the case of older deposits have lithified into rock.

43fadd1833de.title: Paleosol
43fadd1833de.sentence: In soil science the definition differs slightly: paleosols are soils formed long ago that have no relationship in their chemical and physical characteristics to the present-day climate or vegetation.

284438c66e87.title: Paleosol
284438c66e87.sentence: Such soils are found within extremely old continental cratons, or in small scattered locations in outliers of other ancient rock domains.

7c29d08c9c85.title: Paleosol
7c29d08c9c85.sentence: The record of paleosols extends into the Precambrian in Earth's history, with rare paleosols older than 2.5 billion years.

518978a2b595.title: Paleosol
518978a2b595.sentence: Because of the changes in the Earth's climate over the last 50 million years, soils formed under tropical rainforest (or even savanna) have become exposed to increasingly arid climates which cause former oxisols, ultisols or even alfisols to dry out in such a manner that a very hard crust is formed.

42fc20b3ebc5.title: Paleosol
42fc20b3ebc5.sentence: This process has occurred so extensively in most parts of Australia as to restrict soil development—the former soil is effectively the parent material for a new soil, but it is so unweatherable that only a very poorly developed soil can exist in present dry climates, especially when they have become much drier during glacial periods in the Quaternary.

b8a7f79ab39b.title: Paleosol
b8a7f79ab39b.sentence: Paleosols in this sense are always exceedingly infertile soils, containing available phosphorus levels orders of magnitude lower than in temperate regions with younger soils.

3b44da1c95a4.title: Paleosol
3b44da1c95a4.sentence: However, paleosols often contain the most exceptional biodiversity due to the absence of competition.

4365a151d05e.title: Paleosol
4365a151d05e.sentence: Paleosols often contain ancient plant materials such as pollen grains and phytoliths, a biomineralized form of silica produced by many plants such as grasses.

844080b46181.title: Paleosol
844080b46181.sentence: The ratio of different carbon isotopes in organic matter in paleosols reflects the proportions of plants using C3 photosynthesis, which grow in cooler and wetter climates, versus plants using C4 photosynthesis, which are better adapted to hotter and drier conditions.

0907750ace09.title: Paleosol
0907750ace09.sentence: Other methods for detecting past plant life in paleosols are based on identifying the remains of leaf waxes, which are slow to break down in soils over time.

6277f84b6747.title: Paleosol
6277f84b6747.sentence: As records of previous Earth surfaces that can be stacked on one another, paleosol sequences are also valuable for paleoseismology.

730c8d16612f.title: Soil formation
730c8d16612f.sentence: The principal climatic variables influencing soil formation are effective precipitation (i.e., precipitation minus evapotranspiration) and temperature, both of which affect the rates of chemical, physical, and biological processes.

4fbe07640818.title: Soil formation
4fbe07640818.sentence: If warm temperatures and abundant water are present in the profile at the same time, the processes of weathering, leaching, and plant growth will be maximized.

01496be4f2c1.title: Soil formation
01496be4f2c1.sentence: Surplus water percolating through the soil profile transports soluble and suspended materials from the upper layers (eluviation) to the lower layers (illuviation), including clay particles and dissolved organic matter.

a4722c1bd0ad.title: Soil formation
a4722c1bd0ad.sentence: Thus, percolating water stimulates weathering reactions and helps differentiate soil horizons.

533f4af25a67.title: Soil formation
533f4af25a67.sentence: To be effective in soil formation, water must penetrate the regolith.

fac867513c10.title: Soil formation
fac867513c10.sentence: The greater the depth of water penetration, the greater the depth of weathering of the soil and its development.

738a9afa9262.title: Soil formation
738a9afa9262.sentence: Likewise, a deficiency of water is a major factor in determining the characteristics of soils of dry regions.

e8e25a9187da.title: Soil formation
e8e25a9187da.sentence: Soluble salts are not leached from these soils, and in some cases they build up to levels that curtail plant and microbial growth.

f2ac5a99c9db.title: Soil formation
f2ac5a99c9db.sentence: Soil profiles in arid and semi-arid regions are also apt to accumulate carbonates and certain types of expansive clays (calcrete or caliche horizons).

f80d4fa282ca.title: Soil formation
f80d4fa282ca.sentence: Temperature and moisture both influence the organic matter content of soil through their effects on the balance between primary production and decomposition: the colder or drier the climate the lesser atmospheric carbon is fixed as organic matter while the lesser organic matter is decomposed.

0ad8bc2ab479.title: Soil formation
0ad8bc2ab479.sentence: Soil profiles are more distinct in wet and cool climates, where organic materials may accumulate, than in wet and warm climates, where organic materials are rapidly consumed.

560fa79ba2bb.title: Soil formation
560fa79ba2bb.sentence: Climate also indirectly influences soil formation through the effects of vegetation cover and biological activity, which modify the rates of chemical reactions in the soil.

4674c07cce02.title: Soil formation
4674c07cce02.sentence: According to the climatic determination of biomes, humid climates favor the growth of trees.

8ab7d990f9a2.title: Soil formation
8ab7d990f9a2.sentence: In contrast, grasses are the dominant native vegetation in subhumid and semiarid regions, while shrubs and brush of various kinds dominate in arid areas.

eb2804fdd0e0.title: Soil formation
eb2804fdd0e0.sentence: In tropical soils, when the soil has been deprived of vegetation (e.g. by deforestation) and thereby is submitted to intense evaporation, the upward capillary movement of water, which has dissolved iron and aluminium salts, is responsible for the formation of a superficial hardpan of laterite or bauxite, respectively, which is improper for cultivation, a known case of irreversible soil degradation.

daead8e61488.title: Soil formation
daead8e61488.sentence: Plants, animals, fungi, bacteria and humans affect soil formation (see soil biomantle and stonelayer).

b58108aeddf4.title: Soil formation
b58108aeddf4.sentence: Microorganisms are particularly influential in the mineral transformations critical to the soil forming process.

2df89b40d4f5.title: Soil formation
2df89b40d4f5.sentence: Additionally, some bacteria can fix atmospheric nitrogen, and some fungi are efficient at extracting deep soil phosphorus and increasing soil carbon levels in the form of glomalin.

39b4b22cd004.title: Soil formation
39b4b22cd004.sentence: Plants hold soil against erosion, and accumulated plant material build soil humus levels.

1a33a9210f1b.title: Soil formation
1a33a9210f1b.sentence: Plants can form new chemicals that can break down minerals, both directly and indirectly through mycorrhizal fungi and rhizosphere bacteria, and improve the soil structure.

3e111a2daa83.title: Soil formation
3e111a2daa83.sentence: Soil animals, including soil macrofauna (e.g. earthworms, termites, tenebrionids, gophers, moles) and mesofauna (e.g. enchytraeids, springtails, mites), mix soils as they form burrows and pores, allowing moisture and gases to move about, a process called bioturbation.

9805a689ee64.title: Soil formation
9805a689ee64.sentence: In general, the mixing of the soil by the activities of animals, sometimes called pedoturbation, tends to undo or counteract the tendency of other soil-forming processes that create distinct horizons.

1d032c7229ee.title: Soil formation
1d032c7229ee.sentence: Old animal burrows in the lower horizons often become filled with soil material from the overlying A horizon, creating profile features known as crotovinas or krotovinas.

2f6f50680a2e.title: Soil formation
2f6f50680a2e.sentence: The influence of humans, and by association, fire, are state factors placed within the organisms state factor.

ab7a39c97b99.title: Soil formation
ab7a39c97b99.sentence: In more recent times, human destruction of natural vegetation and subsequent tillage of the soil for crop production has abruptly modified soil formation.

1b2317a993b3.title: Soil formation
1b2317a993b3.sentence: Likewise, irrigating soil in an arid region drastically influences soil-forming factors, as does adding fertilizer and lime to soils of low fertility.

9f3e099ae96a.title: Soil formation
9f3e099ae96a.sentence: For example, three species of land snails in the genus Euchondrus in the Negev desert are noted for eating lichens growing under the surface limestone rocks and slabs (endolithic lichens).

2c18f144f3f9.title: Soil formation
2c18f144f3f9.sentence: The grazing activity of these ecosystem engineers disrupts the limestone, resulting in the weathering and the subsequent formation of soil.

72cefc3e5ac2.title: Soil formation
72cefc3e5ac2.sentence: They have a significant effect on the region: the population of snails is estimated to process between 0.7 and 1.1 metric ton per hectare per year of limestone in the Negev desert.

69855bc41147.title: Soil formation
69855bc41147.sentence: For example, the chernozems of the North American tallgrass prairie have a humus fraction nearly half of which is charcoal.

5943081b91ed.title: Soil formation
5943081b91ed.sentence: It is now accepted that Neolithic human-caused wildfires enriched soils in charcoal (also called black carbon) and played a prominent role in the formation of the fertile chernozems and terra preta, actively used for the sake of agriculture.

f359f0ff35cc.title: Soil formation
f359f0ff35cc.sentence: With time, soils will evolve features that depend on the interplay of the prior listed soil-forming factors.

50de7b836002.title: Soil formation
50de7b836002.sentence: While a mixture of sand, silt and clay constitute the texture of a soil and the aggregation of those components produces peds, the development of a distinct B horizon marks the development of a soil or pedogenesis.

d4da131c96a9.title: Soil formation
d4da131c96a9.sentence: It takes decades to several thousand years for a soil to develop a profile, although the notion of soil development has been criticized, soil being in a constant state-of-change under the influence of fluctuating soil-forming factors.

6edbc158e1ef.title: Soil formation
6edbc158e1ef.sentence: For example, recently deposited material from a flood exhibits no soil development as there has not been enough time for the material to form a structure that further defines soil.

44beb8291b9a.title: Soil formation
44beb8291b9a.sentence: The original soil surface is buried, and the formation process must begin anew for this deposit.

fa6d140f5cb8.title: Soil formation
fa6d140f5cb8.sentence: Soil-forming factors continue to affect soils during their existence, even on stable landscapes that are long-enduring, some for millions of years.

9cc7478f6af3.title: Soil formation
9cc7478f6af3.sentence: With additions, removals and alterations, soils are always subject to new conditions.

53fb6f859228.title: Soil formation
53fb6f859228.sentence: While a soil can achieve relative stability of its properties for extended periods, the soil life cycle ultimately ends in soil conditions that leave it vulnerable to erosion.

18a903b63c8d.title: Soil formation
18a903b63c8d.sentence: Despite the inevitability of soil retrogression and degradation, most soil cycles are long.

071f2a8f8f7f.title: Soil formation
071f2a8f8f7f.sentence: Time as a soil-forming factor may be investigated by studying soil chronosequences, in which soils of different ages but with minor differences in other soil-forming factors can be compared.

df08d508f40c.title: Soil formation
df08d508f40c.sentence: Paleosols are soils formed during previous soil-forming conditions which can be deduced from comparisons with present-day soil development.

be8ff006071a.title: Soil formation
be8ff006071a.sentence: The topography, or relief, is characterized by the inclination (slope), elevation, and orientation of the terrain (aspect).

d5ecf72533b1.title: Soil formation
d5ecf72533b1.sentence: Topography determines the rate of precipitation or runoff and the rate of formation or erosion of the surface soil profile.

db81ae67921d.title: Soil formation
db81ae67921d.sentence: Steep slopes encourage rapid soil loss by erosion and allow less rainfall to enter the soil before running off and hence, little mineral deposition in lower profiles (illuviation).

e2805e40971a.title: Soil formation
e2805e40971a.sentence: For all of these reasons, steep slopes prevent the formation of soil from getting very far ahead of soil destruction.

22da4bb26fe7.title: Soil formation
22da4bb26fe7.sentence: Therefore, soils on steep terrain tend to have rather shallow, poorly developed profiles in comparison to soils on nearby, more level sites.

36439e5d5b0a.title: Soil formation
36439e5d5b0a.sentence: Soils at the bottom of a hill will get more water than soils on the slopes, and soils on the slopes that face the sun's path (south aspect) will be drier than soils on slopes that do not.

3c5708ddede0.title: Soil formation
3c5708ddede0.sentence: In swales and depressions where runoff water tends to concentrate, the regolith is usually more deeply weathered, and soil profile development is more advanced.

0d37b89c9e1d.title: Soil formation
0d37b89c9e1d.sentence: However, in the lowest landscape positions, water may saturate the regolith to such a degree that drainage and aeration are restricted.

4da1e76fe787.title: Soil formation
4da1e76fe787.sentence: Here, the weathering of some minerals and the decomposition of organic matter are retarded, while the loss of iron and manganese is accelerated.

9ddffe9bdc97.title: Soil formation
9ddffe9bdc97.sentence: In such low-lying topography, special profile features characteristic of wetland soils may develop.

9995c4b0a13f.title: Soil formation
9995c4b0a13f.sentence: Depressions allow the accumulation of water, minerals and organic matter, and in the extreme, the resulting soils will be saline marshes or peat bogs.

eb677cfadafe.title: Soil formation
eb677cfadafe.sentence: Recurring patterns of topography result in toposequences or soil catenas.

33abbbde561e.title: Soil formation
33abbbde561e.sentence: These patterns emerge from topographic differences in erosion, deposition, fertility, soil moisture, plant cover, soil biology, fire history, and exposure to the elements.

897a369ea7ad.title: Soil formation
897a369ea7ad.sentence: Gravity transports water downslope, together with mineral and organic solutes and colloids, increasing particulate and base content at the foot of hills and mountains.

12451cfe71cd.title: Soil formation
12451cfe71cd.sentence: He demonstrated this in 1898 using the soil forming equation:

2f216d622edc.title: Soil formation
2f216d622edc.sentence: (where cl or c = climate, o = biological processes, p = parent material) tr = relative time (young, mature, old)

43898becbc13.title: Soil formation
43898becbc13.sentence: Russian geologist Vasily Dokuchaev, commonly regarded as the father of pedology, determined in 1883 that soil formation occurs over time under the influence of climate, vegetation, topography, and parent material.

c0eac27a0cab.title: Soil formation
c0eac27a0cab.section: History of research > Hans Jenny's state equation
c0eac27a0cab.sentence: Jenny's state equation in Factors of Soil Formation differs from Vasily Dokuchaev's equation, treating time (t) as a factor, adding topographic relief (r), and pointedly leaving the ellipsis open for more factors (state variables) to be added as our understanding becomes more refined.

3455a2d45ecd.title: Soil formation
3455a2d45ecd.section: History of research > Hans Jenny's state equation
3455a2d45ecd.sentence: American soil scientist Hans Jenny published in 1941 a state equation for the factors influencing soil formation:

c7d96c718648.title: Soil formation
c7d96c718648.section: History of research > Hans Jenny's state equation
c7d96c718648.sentence: S = f(cl, o, r, p, t,...)

4e6c3dcf97bb.title: Soil formation
4e6c3dcf97bb.section: History of research > Hans Jenny's state equation
4e6c3dcf97bb.sentence: This is often remembered with the mnemonic Clorpt.

e35ca97eb6b4.title: Soil formation
e35ca97eb6b4.section: History of research > Hans Jenny's state equation
e35ca97eb6b4.sentence: There are two principal methods by which the state equation may be solved: first in a theoretical or conceptual manner by logical deductions from certain premises, and second empirically by experimentation or field observation.

d80e798fedef.title: Soil formation
d80e798fedef.section: History of research > Hans Jenny's state equation
d80e798fedef.sentence: The empirical method is still mostly employed today, and soil formation can be defined by varying a single factor and keeping the other factors constant.

8e2ebfdd131a.title: Soil formation
8e2ebfdd131a.section: History of research > Hans Jenny's state equation
8e2ebfdd131a.sentence: This had led to the development of empirical models to describe pedogenesis, such as climofunctions, biofunctions, topofunctions, lithofunctions, and chronofunctions.

271ddae48874.title: Soil formation
271ddae48874.section: History of research > Hans Jenny's state equation
271ddae48874.sentence: Since Jenny published his formulation in 1941, it has been used by innumerable soil surveyors all over the world as a qualitative list for understanding the factors that may be important for producing the soil pattern within a region.

7d4922dca0bc.title: Stonelayer
7d4922dca0bc.sentence: According to this view, explanatory pedology has operated under a predominantly soil science utilitarian-conceptual approach, or model—the five factors (‘clorpt’) model—to map, classify, valuate, and “explain” soils (Jenny 1941; Soil Survey personnel 1951, 1975, 1991, 1993).

2aab4ad40210.title: Stonelayer
2aab4ad40210.sentence: While the model has greatly aided soil science, and spatially explains generalized soil-environmental relationships on landscapes, the device—supremely attractive in its parsimony—has constrained pedologic interpretation because its genetic-interpretive domain is constrained by its broad factorial (landscape context) tenets.

aa2273828f67.title: Stonelayer
aa2273828f67.sentence: The model allows for a wide-ranging generalized assessment of soilscapes, and is useful in soil chronosequence work (Birkeland 1974, 1984) but the biodynamic soil processes that are largely responsible in producing stonelayers are absent at a highest theoretical (five factors) level.

05448f20adfa.title: Catena (soil)
05448f20adfa.sentence: A catena in soil science (pedology) is a series of distinct but co-evolving soils arrayed down a slope.

338740cf8873.title: Catena (soil)
338740cf8873.sentence: Each soil type or "facet" differs somewhat from its neighbours, but all occur in the same climate and on the same underlying parent material.

e63fda8f7109.title: Catena (soil)
e63fda8f7109.sentence: The catena concept originated in central Uganda by chemist W.S. Martin to describe a hill slope sequence at the Bukalasa research station.

be4d0d8d03ed.title: Catena (soil)
be4d0d8d03ed.sentence: The term catena (Latin: chain) was first coined by scientist Geoffrey Milne to describe these soil-topography units.

5e6fffd97ae0.title: Catena (soil)
5e6fffd97ae0.sentence: A slope can be broken into sections known as a ridge, crest, midslope, and toeslope.

57f41a37a752.title: Catena (soil)
57f41a37a752.sentence: Steeper slope or crest sections tend to be freely drained, while at the bottom of slopes or toeslopes there is usually higher in moisture content and poor drainage.

eda37cfd8aae.title: Catena (soil)
eda37cfd8aae.sentence: Toeslope soils are also known to be richer in clay and organic matter.

49d2c15db3e7.title: Catena (soil)
49d2c15db3e7.sentence: A catena forms when the climate, including precipitation and evaporation, is the same for the whole slope, and when sufficient time has passed for equilibrium to be reached between the processes that bring materials in to a facet and the processes that take materials away.

127a260e1e36.title: Catena (soil)
127a260e1e36.sentence: The result is a predictable sequence of soil facets.

ae8f3799451b.title: Catena (soil)
ae8f3799451b.sentence: A catena is thus an open system which has continuous input and output processes.

14d0620b101e.title: Catena (soil)
14d0620b101e.sentence: On a steeper slope in the middle of a catena, erosion (surface runoff) is faster, so facets are typically thinner and drier.

1c5d5dded42c.title: Catena (soil)
1c5d5dded42c.sentence: Conversely, on a shallower slope at the top or bottom of a catena, soils are thicker and deeper.

32eeb3eb04d5.title: Catena (soil)
32eeb3eb04d5.sentence: Lithology and relief can be the primary controls on the development of certain catenas with easily disaggregated parent rock and high relief favoring particle redistribution and therefore the formation of distinct soils in particle-source and particle-deposition zones along a slope.

5f2b1e776c2d.title: Catena (soil)
5f2b1e776c2d.sentence: Catenas can also develop on low relief hillslopes, but because less potential energy is available, the redistribution of mass can be dominated by subsurface flow of plasma, a combination of dissolved and suspended solids in soil water.

c5f27addf326.title: Catena (soil)
c5f27addf326.sentence: On impermeable acid rocks such as metamorphic schists in a high rainfall climate like that of western Scotland, the catena consists of thick acidic peat-forming wet bog on the flatter facets, and thinner, drier, somewhat less acidic peaty podsols on the steeper facets.

cba8dc6f73b5.title: Catena (soil)
cba8dc6f73b5.sentence: On a permeable basic rock such as chalk, the catena may consist of thick brown earths on the flatter facets, with thin rendzinas on the steeper slopes, while the valley bottom may include alkaline fen peat or river alluvium.

4831c171b488.title: Catena (soil)
4831c171b488.sentence: A mature catena is in equilibrium as the processes of deposition and erosion are in balance.

d601269fce6c.title: Leaching model (soil)
d601269fce6c.sentence: A leaching model is a hydrological model by which the leaching with irrigation water of dissolved substances, notably salt, in the soil is described depending on the hydrological regime and the soil's properties.

138db5941497.title: Leaching model (soil)
138db5941497.sentence: The model may describe the process (1) in time and (2) as a function of amount of water applied.

35f93795f1b2.title: Leaching model (soil)
35f93795f1b2.sentence: Leaching is often done to reclaim saline soil or to conserve a favorable salt content of the soil of irrigated land as all irrigation water contains salts.

995a2b31ded8.title: Leaching model (soil)
995a2b31ded8.sentence: The leaching process in a salty soil to be reclaimed is illustrated in the leaching curves of figure 1, derived from data of the Chacupe pilot area, Peru.

1be38f77c0d2.title: Leaching model (soil)
1be38f77c0d2.sentence: It shows the soil salinity in terms of electrical conductivity (EC) of the soil solution with respect its initial value (ECi) as a function of amount of water percolating through the soil.

bd4d9271d321.title: Leaching model (soil)
bd4d9271d321.sentence: The salinity of the deeper soil first increases due to the salts leached from the top-soil, but later it also decreases.

8e666e011c03.title: Drainage research
8e666e011c03.sentence: Agro-hydro-salinity and leaching models like SaltMod may be helpful to determine the drainage requirement.

c867882785db.title: Leaching model (soil)
c867882785db.sentence: In figure 3, leaching curves are shown for different leaching efficiencies, as assumed in the leaching model SaltMod with data from the Mashtul pilot area.

d89b06430c81.title: Perturbation (geology)
d89b06430c81.sentence: Pedoturbation (from Greek: πέδον (pédon), "soil") involves mixing between soil horizons and is an important factor in soil formation.

451d19089512.title: Perturbation (geology)
451d19089512.sentence: Pedoturbation includes churning clays, cryoturbation, and bioturbation.

559d72c61c92.title: Perturbation (geology)
559d72c61c92.sentence: Pedoturbation transforms soils through destratification, mixing, and sorting, as well as creating preferential flow paths for soil gas and infiltrating water.

e6f2cbf4100e.title: Perturbation (geology)
e6f2cbf4100e.sentence: Precipitation of surface salts also causes localized disruption of soils.

beb753d419ec.title: Perturbation (geology)
beb753d419ec.sentence: Because it does not result in mixing between soil horizons, it is not considered pedoturbation.

f27f54206e30.title: Oxisol
f27f54206e30.sentence: The main processes of soil formation of oxisols are weathering, humification and pedoturbation due to animals.

8b50f3f18042.title: Perturbation (geology)
8b50f3f18042.sentence: Perturbation (from Latin: perturbare "to confuse, disorder, disturb", from per- "through" + turbare "disturb, confuse," from turba "turmoil, crowd") is a set of pedology (soil study) and sedimentary geology processes relating to changes in the nature of water-borne alluvial sediments and in situ soil deposits over time.

d16a1d694307.title: Soil biomantle
d16a1d694307.sentence: Most simply, the soil biomantle is the organic-rich bioturbated upper part of the soil, including the topsoil where most biota live, reproduce, die, and become assimilated.

0da270876e75.title: Soil biomantle
0da270876e75.sentence: The biomantle is thus the upper zone of soil that is predominantly a product of organic activity and the area where bioturbation is a dominant process.

89d754d64444.title: Soil biomantle
89d754d64444.sentence: Soil bioturbation consists predominantly of three subsets: faunalturbation (animal burrowings), floralturbation (root growth, tree-uprootings), and fungiturbation (mycelia growth).

10b524d8d86d.title: Soil biomantle
10b524d8d86d.sentence: All three processes promote soil parent material destratification, mixing, and often particle size sorting, leading with other processes to the formation of soil and its horizons.

0f3b9be6f7bc.title: Soil biomantle
0f3b9be6f7bc.section: One- and two-layered biomantles, soil stonelayers (stone lines)
0f3b9be6f7bc.sentence: The biomantle includes the topsoil, or A horizon of soils, and also, any underlying lighter-colored (E) horizon that may be present.

a00eccbcee6c.title: Soil biomantle
a00eccbcee6c.section: One- and two-layered biomantles, soil stonelayers (stone lines)
a00eccbcee6c.sentence: For midlatitude and subtropical soils that have typical A-E-B-C horizons and profiles, the biomantle is normally that part above the B horizon.

c90de01d2743.title: Soil biomantle
c90de01d2743.section: One- and two-layered biomantles, soil stonelayers (stone lines)
c90de01d2743.sentence: Biomantles with basal stonelayers are two-layered biomantles that form in parent materials with heterogeneous particle sizes (mixtures of fines and gravels); those lacking stonelayers are one-layered biomantles that form in homogeneous materials (either sands, loess, or gravels of approximately uniform size).

4d4c4d378065.title: Soil biomantle
4d4c4d378065.sentence: In midlatitude soils where most bioturbation is relatively shallow, seasonal, and without many bioturbators, the biomantle is relatively thin, often less than 1–2 m thick.

40a4edc1526b.title: Soil biomantle
40a4edc1526b.sentence: However, in humid tropical and subtropical erosionally stable regions where both greater volumes of soil are biotransfered and deeper bioturbations occur—and bioturbation is year-round and performed by more invertebrate animals (termites, ants, worms, etc.), the biomantle is often thicker, sometimes 5–6 m or more thick.

45bbd9f09274.title: Soil biomantle
45bbd9f09274.sentence: Because the soil biomantle is the main zone of bioturbation, it is invariably permeable and of low density.

6c07223c3318.title: Soil biomantle
6c07223c3318.sentence: For example, it promotes the downward percolation of rainwater and snowmelt through often-abundant biochannels and interconnected biopores.

4d8e751050fd.title: Soil biomantle
4d8e751050fd.sentence: The biomantle also promotes downslope soil-water (throughflow, interflow) movements if it is formed above a clay-enriched Bt (argillic) horizon, or above some other dense subsoil horizon (e.g., duripan, fragipan, etc.) or bedrock – all of which generally function as aquitards or aquicludes to vertical soil water flow.

0d19deda14ab.title: Soil biomantle
0d19deda14ab.sentence: As originally defined, a biomantle must exhibit at least 50% biofabric.

e81a43755d6f.title: Soil biomantle
e81a43755d6f.sentence: This criterion denotes small, often pelletized microbiofabric and mesobiofabric produced by invertebrates (ants, worms, termites), usually observed under hand lens or higher magnification (soil thin sections).

ca79829e4d7f.title: Soil biomantle
ca79829e4d7f.sentence: In some desert soils, in many mountain soils with moderate to steep slopes, in many recently eroded bedrock soils, and in various other soils, the biomantle constitutes the entire soil.

0dbd1dfe782b.title: Soil biomantle
0dbd1dfe782b.sentence: That is, neither soil horizons nor weathering zones underlie the biomantle.

8be3f41c81cb.title: Soil horizon
8be3f41c81cb.sentence: In this case, the A horizon is regarded as a " biomantle ".

d7dc4261bb5d.title: Chronosequence
d7dc4261bb5d.sentence: A chronosequence describes a set of ecological sites that share similar attributes but represent different ages.

8182863676f4.title: Chronosequence
8182863676f4.sentence: Chronosequences used in soil studies consist of sites that have developed over different periods of time with relatively small differences in other soil-forming factors.

03d89a489728.title: Chronosequence
03d89a489728.sentence: Such groups of sites are used to assess the influence of time as a factor in pedogenesis.

7a36fff71102.title: Chronosequence
7a36fff71102.sentence: A common assumption in establishing chronosequences is that no other variable besides age (such as various abiotic components and biotic components) has changed between sites of interest.

0217302428ae.title: Chronosequence
0217302428ae.sentence: Because this assumption cannot always be tested for environmental study sites, the use of chronosequences in field successional studies has recently been debated.

b6e16718f763.title: Chronosequence
b6e16718f763.sentence: Since many processes in forest ecology take a long time (decades or centuries) to develop, chronosequence methods are used to represent and study the time-dependent development of a forest.

fba7162d4435.title: Chronosequence
fba7162d4435.sentence: Field data from a forest chronosequence can be collected in a short period of several months.

9e56c0cd379a.title: Chronosequence
9e56c0cd379a.sentence: A classic example of using chronosequences to study ecological succession is in the study of plant and microbial succession in recently deglaciated zones.

82e1f33e82a1.title: Chronosequence
82e1f33e82a1.sentence: For example, a study from 2005 used the distance from the nose of a glacier as a proxy for site age.
