f2d83c520239.title: Sesquioxide
f2d83c520239.sentence: A sesquioxide is an oxide of an element (or radical), where the ratio between the number of atoms of that element and the number of atoms of oxygen is 2:3.

b568e844d8fc.title: Sesquioxide
b568e844d8fc.sentence: Many sesquioxides contain a metal in the +3 oxidation state and the oxide ion O2−, e.g., aluminium oxide Al2O3, lanthanum(III) oxide La2O3 and iron(III) oxide Fe2O3.

e93694b16383.title: Sesquioxide
e93694b16383.sentence: Sesquioxides of iron and aluminium are found in soil.

6aa08bc400ea.title: Podsolisation
6aa08bc400ea.sentence: The sesquioxides are translocated from the A Horizon, a zone of out-washing, to the B Horizon, a zone of illuviation.

7a313a4dfe1c.title: Podsolisation
7a313a4dfe1c.sentence: Below this is a red/orange layer of iron and aluminium sesquioxides deposit.

6185a92700fa.title: Ferrallitisation
6185a92700fa.sentence: The silica is removed by leaching and the sesquioxides of iron and aluminium remain, giving the characteristic red colour of many tropical soils.

d0aacfa2f73c.title: Laterite
d0aacfa2f73c.sentence: The word laterite has been used for variably cemented, sesquioxide-rich soil horizons.

91211703570b.title: Soil horizon
91211703570b.section: Horizons and layers according to the FAO Guidelines for Soil Description (2006) > Subordinate characteristics
91211703570b.sentence: - s: Illuvial accumulation of sesquioxides—B horizons.

ad05349a9f59.title: Soil horizon
ad05349a9f59.section: Horizons and layers according to the FAO Guidelines for Soil Description (2006) > Subordinate characteristics
ad05349a9f59.sentence: - o: Residual accumulation of sesquioxides (pedogenic)—no restriction.

94c43ca59071.title: Laterite
94c43ca59071.sentence: Laterite is a soil type rich in iron and aluminum that often forms in hot, wet areas; most such soil is found in the tropics.

dd6a4e7773d1.title: Laterite
dd6a4e7773d1.sentence: Nearly all laterites are of rusty-red coloration due to high iron oxide content.

72a7b92c1635.title: Laterite
72a7b92c1635.sentence: Francis Buchanan-Hamilton first described and named a laterite formation in southern India in 1807.

4fa41a90a7b7.title: Laterite
4fa41a90a7b7.sentence: He named it laterite from the Latin word later, which means a brick; this highly compacted and cemented soil can easily be cut into brick-shaped blocks for building.

361e56aebe21.title: Laterite
361e56aebe21.sentence: Yves Tardy, from the French Institut National Polytechnique de Toulouse and the Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique, calculated that laterites cover about one-third of the Earth's continental land area.

5cdf4333f751.title: Laterite
5cdf4333f751.sentence: They cover most of the land area between the tropics of Cancer and Capricorn; areas not covered within these latitudes include the extreme western portion of South America, the southwestern portion of Africa, the desert regions of north-central Africa, the Arabian peninsula and the interior of Australia.

703b47d8e8f4.title: Laterite
703b47d8e8f4.sentence: Laterite covers are thick in the stable areas of the Western Ethiopian Shield, on cratons of the South American Plate, and on the Australian Shield.

564677de69bc.title: Laterite
564677de69bc.sentence: In Madhya Pradesh, India, the laterite which caps the plateau is 30 m (100 ft) thick.

5e152f7c9665.title: Laterite
5e152f7c9665.sentence: Laterites reflect past weathering conditions; laterites which are found in present-day non-tropical areas are products of former geological epochs, when that area was near the equator.

81a8519efaee.title: Laterite
81a8519efaee.sentence: Present-day laterite occurring outside the humid tropics are considered to be indicators of climatic change, continental drift or a combination of both.

b063d8214b2b.title: Laterite
b063d8214b2b.sentence: It has also been used for any reddish soil at or near the Earth's surface.

00f28d312e2d.title: Laterite
00f28d312e2d.sentence: Aside from this variety, laterite has commonly been considered a rock type as well as a soil type.

7b34828d0b50.title: Laterite
7b34828d0b50.sentence: These facts, and further ways of conceiving the nature of laterite (e.g. as a complete weathering profile or even a theory about weathering), have led to calls for the term to be abandoned altogether.

2fa2fd125267.title: Podsolisation
2fa2fd125267.sentence: The process generally occurs in areas where precipitation is greater than evapotranspiration.

d43d5c71bd2d.title: Podsolisation
d43d5c71bd2d.sentence: When organic material is broken down nutrients are released, but at the same time organic acids are released.

7f4f4dddafbb.title: Podsolisation
7f4f4dddafbb.sentence: These organic acids are known as chelating agents.

3a6e5dd23b81.title: Podsolisation
3a6e5dd23b81.sentence: Many podsol soils form underneath coniferous forests, the fact that pine trees are evergreen causes a very thin litter layer inhibiting the production of humus.

39a7ce9e1aaa.title: Podsolisation
39a7ce9e1aaa.sentence: As a result, an acidic (pH 4.5) mor humus is produced which provides a greater amount of chelating agents.

5ebd42943add.title: Podsolisation
5ebd42943add.sentence: In podsolisation, chelating agents break down clay and release minerals such as iron and aluminium.

7f946dfbdcb6.title: Podsolisation
7f946dfbdcb6.sentence: When iron and aluminium are hydrated they become sesquioxides.

da7c06d402f9.title: Podsolisation
da7c06d402f9.sentence: Many bases such as calcium and potassium are also leached from the zone along with organic matter and silica.

9ecc236b3d27.title: Podsolisation
9ecc236b3d27.sentence: Often minerals like quartz and silica are left behind in the A horizon.

70a03db4d026.title: Podsolisation
70a03db4d026.sentence: What is significantly different about podsols in comparison to other soils is that the bottom of A horizon is known as the AE horizon, which is an eluviated area which has lost sesquioxides.

105672c5be01.title: Podsolisation
105672c5be01.sentence: The B Horizon has dark layer where minerals, organic matter and bases are being illuviated (washed in/accumulated).

0c021822b409.title: Podsolisation
0c021822b409.sentence: This can cause water logging which may then saturate the A horizon leading to mottling or a gleyed podsol.

27ab1a794907.title: Plant litter
27ab1a794907.sentence: This process is known as podzolization and is particularly intense in boreal and cool temperate forests that are mainly constituted by coniferous pines whose litterfall is rich in phenolic compounds and fulvic acid.

15dd47957e79.title: Laterite
15dd47957e79.sentence: Tropical weathering (laterization) is a prolonged process of chemical weathering which produces a wide variety in the thickness, grade, chemistry and ore mineralogy of the resulting soils.

0930f48e8ef3.title: Laterite
0930f48e8ef3.sentence: Laterite soils develop by intensive and prolonged weathering of the underlying parent rock, usually under conditions of high temperatures and heavy rainfall alternating with dry periods, in a process called laterization.

5a0d499118ef.title: Laterite
5a0d499118ef.sentence: An essential feature for the formation of laterite is the repetition of wet and dry seasons.

08d3ca744981.title: Laterite
08d3ca744981.sentence: Rocks are leached by percolating rain water during the wet season; the resulting solution containing the leached ions is brought to the surface by capillary action during the dry season.

9175101a6fda.title: Laterite
9175101a6fda.sentence: The mechanism of leaching involves acid dissolving the host mineral lattice, followed by hydrolysis and precipitation of insoluble oxides and sulfates of iron, aluminum and silica under the high temperature conditions of a humid sub-tropical monsoon climate.

6dda032f2ab7.title: Laterite
6dda032f2ab7.sentence: The reaction zone where rocks are in contact with water—from the lowest to highest water table levels—is progressively depleted of the easily leached ions of sodium, potassium, calcium and magnesium.

dd248dd98b1f.title: Laterite
dd248dd98b1f.sentence: A solution of these ions can have the correct pH to preferentially dissolve silicon oxide rather than the aluminum oxides and iron oxides.

428a037842af.title: Laterite
428a037842af.sentence: Laterites are formed from the leaching of parent sedimentary rocks (sandstones, clays, limestones); metamorphic rocks (schists, gneisses, migmatites); igneous rocks (granites, basalts, gabbros, peridotites); and mineralized proto-ores; which leaves the more insoluble ions, predominantly iron and aluminum.

13cc0802659d.title: Laterite
13cc0802659d.sentence: Quartz is the most abundant relic mineral from the parent rock.

a88ab5e7db5c.title: Laterite
a88ab5e7db5c.sentence: Laterite formation is favored in low topographical reliefs of gentle crests and plateaus which prevents erosion of the surface cover.

cab1cc6973b1.title: Laterite
cab1cc6973b1.sentence: A period of active laterization extended from about the mid-Tertiary to the mid-Quaternary periods (35 to 1.5 million years ago).

ee285b674cb4.title: Laterite
ee285b674cb4.sentence: The rate of laterization would have decreased with the abrupt cooling of the earth.

74072701cffd.title: Laterite
74072701cffd.sentence: Weathering in tropical climates continues to this day, at a reduced rate.

c336630d13fa.title: Laterite
c336630d13fa.sentence: Iron oxides are derived from mafic igneous rocks and other iron-rich rocks; bauxites are derived from granitic igneous rock and other iron-poor rocks.

6da21f66e159.title: Laterite
6da21f66e159.sentence: Nickel laterites occur in zones of the earth which experienced prolonged tropical weathering of ultramafic rocks containing the ferro-magnesian minerals olivine, pyroxene, and amphibole.

c31092afa800.title: Stonelayer
c31092afa800.sentence: A stonelayer, or soil stonelayer, or stone line, is a three-dimensional subsurface layer, or soil horizon, dominated by coarse particles (>2mm), that generally follows (mimics) the surface topography (Sharpe 1938).

1bf31e1c579f.title: Stone line
1bf31e1c579f.sentence: A stone line (see also Stonelayer) is a three-dimensional subsurface layer, or ‘carpet,’ of stones evident as a ‘line of stones’ in natural exposures such as soils, road cuts, and trenches.

3983456049a8.title: Stonelayer
3983456049a8.sentence: A stonelayer occupies the basal horizon of two-layered soil biomantles (Paton et al. 1995; Schaetzl and Anderson 2005; Fey 2009; Wilkinson et al. 2009).

d4b59dce69af.title: Stonelayer
d4b59dce69af.sentence: A stonelayer may be one stone thick, and thus appear in a trench or pit as a "stone line," or it may be several stones thick and appear as a "stone zone" (Johnson 1989).

d2c16ba64b71.title: Stone line
d2c16ba64b71.sentence: Stone lines that are more than one stone thick have been called ‘stone zones’.

63038f2d3e23.title: Stonelayer
63038f2d3e23.sentence: The gravel components of stonelayers may be compositionally variable, and while many are lithic clasts, often of quartzose composition, others may be metallic nodules and concretions of iron and manganese oxides, human artifacts, snail and clam shells (in highly calcareous soils), precious and semi-precious stones, or some combination thereof (Aleva 1983, 1987; Johnson 2002).

dda5cf1ef2fa.title: Soil biomantle
dda5cf1ef2fa.section: One- and two-layered biomantles, soil stonelayers (stone lines)
dda5cf1ef2fa.sentence: Where present they often function as subsurface "French drains" for soil-water movements and storage.

9eabae116e24.title: Soil biomantle
9eabae116e24.sentence: In such cases the stonelayer, if present, can actually function as an aquifer for free water flow.

9aa390f5566a.title: Stone line
9aa390f5566a.sentence: On the other hand, a stone line that is present in a soil or a paleosol is invariable non-imbricated and follows (mimics) the surface topography of the soil, or the paleosurface of a paleosol.

5a0e86d5a087.title: Stone line
5a0e86d5a087.sentence: This is strong evidence that such stone lines are pedogenic, and produced by soil forming processes.

63d5cbf5775f.title: Stone line
63d5cbf5775f.sentence: Where present in stratigraphic sequences, if the units were deposited by running water, the stones are usually imbricated (individual stones are lapped, or leaning, upon one another in the direction of water flow).

0f025f91f0b6.title: Stone line
0f025f91f0b6.sentence: This is strong evidence that such stone lines are geogenic.

84793a5d0b95.title: Biorhexistasy
84793a5d0b95.sentence: The theory of biorhexistasy describes climatic conditions necessary for periods of soil formation (pedogenesis) separated by periods of soil erosion.

895a14a0d0e6.title: Biorhexistasy
895a14a0d0e6.sentence: Proposed by pedologist Henry Erhart in 1951, the theory defines two climatic phases: biostasy and rhexistasy.

fa4472262cb2.title: Biorhexistasy
fa4472262cb2.sentence: During biostasy, abundant and regular precipitation induces strong pedogenesis characterized by chemical alteration of parent material and intensified eluviation and illuviation of soil minerals within the surface soil and subsoil layers (the solum).

6be260653114.title: Biorhexistasy
6be260653114.sentence: These processes contribute to the formation of eluvial and argillic horizons and an increased concentration of iron oxides, aluminum oxides, and other sesquioxides in the subsoil.

f4fd2a9b4cc7.title: Biorhexistasy
f4fd2a9b4cc7.sentence: Climatic conditions favor a vegetative cover which protects the soil from physical erosion but abundant rainfall results in the loss of mineral ions and increased concentration of those minerals in receiving bodies of water.

9983b143a971.title: Biorhexistasy
9983b143a971.sentence: During rhexistasy (from rhexein, to break) the protective vegetative cover is reduced or eliminated as a result of a drier climate.

e024ddd2d3bf.title: Biorhexistasy
e024ddd2d3bf.sentence: The drier climate slows pedogenesis and soils no longer contribute the limestone building mineral components that characterize biostasy.

ebfc62dbeade.title: Biorhexistasy
ebfc62dbeade.sentence: During rhexistasy, the dominance of chemical weathering that characterizes biostasy is replaced by the dominance of physical weathering.

23b64758dee1.title: Biorhexistasy
23b64758dee1.sentence: The intensity of punctuating rainfall events during rhexistasy results in erosion, and the accumulation of sand and silt as sedimentary layers.

a9513b2c9d88.title: Biorhexistasy
a9513b2c9d88.sentence: During the Pleistocene epoch, the periods of glaciation are considered to be periods of rhexistasy and the interglacial are considered periods of biostasy.

670119708208.title: Paleosol
670119708208.sentence: Soils form in near-constant contact with the atmosphere, so their chemical composition is affected by the composition of the atmosphere through both direct and indirect pathways.

e7b5e84055c7.title: Paleosol
e7b5e84055c7.sentence: The oxidation of paleosols has been used as an indicator of atmospheric oxygen, which has risen over Earth's history.

c022258f5c18.title: Paleosol
c022258f5c18.sentence: Paleosols have also been used to reconstruct atmospheric carbon dioxide levels, based on modern studies of soil carbon gas exchange, carbon isotopes in pedogenic carbonate nodules, and mass-balance approaches taking multiple atmospheric gases (typically carbon dioxide, oxygen, and methane) into account.

535e0a258d7f.title: Paleosol
535e0a258d7f.sentence: These methods are being actively developed in the field of early Earth research.

e945d5f29522.title: Paleosol
e945d5f29522.sentence: Palaeosols are frequently used as palaeoclimatological tools for gauging the climate in which they formed.

429c25ff1e82.title: Paleosol
429c25ff1e82.sentence: Because rates and styles of weathering are dependent on climatic factors, paleosols can be used to reconstruct variables of past climate.

8e08f0e397f4.title: Paleosol
8e08f0e397f4.sentence: Mean annual precipitation (MAP) and air temperature (MAAT) are two commonly-reconstructed variables which, along with seasonality and in conjunction with other paleoenvironmental tools, can be used to describe past terrestrial climates.

601d873b7b9a.title: Paleosol
601d873b7b9a.sentence: A suite of paleoclimatic proxies exist and while they vary in focus, many rely on changes in chemical composition throughout a soil profile that occur during weathering, burial, and post-burial processes.

9d46509fb667.title: Paleosol
9d46509fb667.sentence: Their use depends on factors such as post-burial alteration, parent material, and soil order; not every proxy is applicable to every paleosol.

348242769046.title: Paleosol
348242769046.sentence: Most proxies are applicable to Phanerozoic paleosols (not older), as landscape processes changed dramatically after the rise of land plants.

d7ade814ccae.title: Paleosol
d7ade814ccae.sentence: Proposed seasonality proxies primarily rely on a soil wetting/drying process, during which pedogenic carbonate can form; like other proxies, this tool is continually being tested and refined.

6dc3db1ab34d.title: Paleosol
6dc3db1ab34d.sentence: Consequently, our modern soil classification system cannot be readily applied to paleosols.

20159b02ae3e.title: Paleosol
20159b02ae3e.sentence: Until a paleosol-specific naming scheme is fully adopted, many paleo-pedologists have stuck to using the taxonomic classification of soils provided by the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA).

5fa14d5b891e.title: Paleosol
5fa14d5b891e.sentence: Geology, biology, and the atmosphere all changed significantly over that time, with dramatic shifts at the Great Oxidation Event (2.42 billion years ago) and during the Paleozoic, when complex animals and land plants proliferated.

80a2498c8d0c.title: Paleosol
80a2498c8d0c.sentence: For example, a modern alfisol—broadly defined as a forest soil—would not have existed prior to the evolution of trees.

45fdc442fafe.title: Paleosol
45fdc442fafe.sentence: More problematically, it is specifically defined by chemical properties that would not be preserved in the rock record.

c3f57382c7dc.title: Paleosol
c3f57382c7dc.sentence: While modern soil orders are often used to describe paleosols in a qualitative sense, a paleosol-specific naming scheme has been proposed, although it is only used sporadically in the literature.

cd5470483b9b.title: Paleosol
cd5470483b9b.sentence: The hierarchical structure cannot be applied more deeply than the order level regarding paleosols.

1945c92f3108.title: Paleosol
1945c92f3108.sentence: Rye & Holland (1998) laid out five criteria for identifying a paleosol.

0c8e80502521.title: Paleosol
0c8e80502521.sentence: - up-profile changes in chemistry, texture, and mineralogy consistent with terrestrial weathering processes.

2d3103a3d9da.title: Paleosol
2d3103a3d9da.sentence: While this was prompted by the need for more stringent identification of Precambrian paleosols, it is applicable to paleosols of any age.

239eebb64d25.title: Paleosol
239eebb64d25.sentence: - soft-sediment deformation at the top of the profile, and

c920685df4d5.title: Paleosol
c920685df4d5.sentence: In the field, physical signs of a paleosol include evidence of horizonation (e.g., color and textural changes), bedrock incorporated into a finer overlying lithology (corestones), and evidence of surface processes (e.g., root traces, organic matter, burrows, redox alteration).

3472484c825a.title: Paleosol
3472484c825a.sentence: To distinguish and identify paleosols from one another, certain diagnostic horizons and features need to be taken into account.

ecc79f1eba6f.title: Paleosol
ecc79f1eba6f.sentence: For instance, all paleosols have an A horizon, but histosols have an O horizon above the A horizon.

fd699da2df30.title: Pedodiversity
fd699da2df30.sentence: Pedodiversity is the variation of soil properties (usually characterised by soil classes) within an area.

96ac481ceb78.title: Pedodiversity
96ac481ceb78.sentence: Pedodiversity studies were first started by analyzing soil series–area relationships (Beckett and Bie, 1978).

23c30d86dddf.title: Pedodiversity
23c30d86dddf.sentence: According to Guo et al. (2003) the term pedodiversity was developed by McBratney (1992) who discussed landscape preservation strategies based on pedodiversity.

ab0aa47f64ba.title: Pedodiversity
ab0aa47f64ba.sentence: Ibáñez et al. (1995) first introduced ecological diversity indices as measures of pedodiversity.

dff708305dd8.title: Pedodiversity
dff708305dd8.sentence: They include species richness, relative species abundance, and Shannon index.

a13f9e7bba83.title: Pedodiversity
a13f9e7bba83.sentence: Richness is the number of different soil types, which is the number of soil classes at particular level in a taxonomic system.

69e8b760359e.title: Pedodiversity
69e8b760359e.sentence: Pedodiversity is a measure of soil variation, and pedodiversity is a function of soil formation.

1eb62fb099bf.title: Pedodiversity
1eb62fb099bf.sentence: Pedodiversity is introduced to pedology to analyze soil spatial patterns, soil geography, and test the pedogenetic theories.

165b5b5bcf45.title: Pedodiversity
165b5b5bcf45.sentence: Jonathan Phillips showed that in eastern North Carolina intrinsic variability within homogeneous landscape units is more important in determining the total pedodiversity of the study area than is the extrinsic variability associated with measurable differences in topography, parent material, and vegetation/land use.

f9a8648ca1d5.title: Pedodiversity
f9a8648ca1d5.sentence: In another study, they found that soils in Ouachita Mountains of Arkansas vary considerably within small more-or-less homogeneous areas, and richness–area analysis shows that the overall pattern of pedodiversity is dominated by local, intrinsic (within-plot) variability as opposed to between-plot variability.

2a4df56b7475.title: Pedodiversity
2a4df56b7475.sentence: This is consistent with variation controlled mainly by individual trees and local lithological variations.

5147146db992.title: Pedodiversity
5147146db992.sentence: In 2003, Guo et al. used the State Soil Geographic database (STATSGO) to explored quantitative aspects of pedodiversity for the US.

8d3792533c07.title: Pedodiversity
8d3792533c07.sentence: They found that the West USDA-NRCS geographical region has the highest soil taxa richness, followed by the Northern Plains.

1ea3a1c236b5.title: Pedodiversity
1ea3a1c236b5.sentence: One of the key findings of this research is that at lower levels of soil taxonomic divisions (especially the series level), soil taxa increase continuously with increasing area, indicating considerable soil endemism in the US (and likely around the world), a key consideration in conservation and preservation planning.

6061927aa6fe.title: Pedodiversity
6061927aa6fe.sentence: However conventional diversity measures, only measure the relative natural abundance of soil classes, and there is no information on the taxonomic similarity or differences between soil classes.

d01a3109389f.title: Pedodiversity
d01a3109389f.sentence: New measures of pedodiversity, such as the mean soil taxonomic distance, which considers both information on the relative abundance and the taxonomic differences between soil classes have been developed and shown to be a better measure.

e29e2e593459.title: Pedodiversity
e29e2e593459.sentence: Pedodiversity can be thought as a way to preserve, or even reconstruct, the soil cover.

071ab555d4db.title: Pedodiversity
071ab555d4db.sentence: In areas which have been degraded it will become important to reconstruct the variation.

94ff19026c71.title: Pedodiversity
94ff19026c71.sentence: A quantitative knowledge of natural pedodiversity will ease the task of the person who attempts to rebuild quasi-natural soil systems.

809f3d18d3b6.title: Soil production function
809f3d18d3b6.sentence: Soil production function refers to the rate of bedrock weathering into soil as a function of soil thickness.

8d84f5e7600b.title: Soil production function
8d84f5e7600b.sentence: A general model suggests that the rate of physical weathering of bedrock (de/dt) can be represented as an exponential decline with soil thickness:

eca934250eba.title: Soil production function
eca934250eba.sentence: where h is soil thickness [m], P0 [mm/year] is the potential (or maximum) weathering rate of bedrock and k [m−1] is an empirical constant.

5a0ac2d439f1.title: Soil production function
5a0ac2d439f1.sentence: The reduction of weathering rate with thickening of soil is related to the exponential decrease of temperature amplitude with increasing depth below the soil surface, and also the exponential decrease in average water penetration (for freely-drained soils).

d541fe51d4bc.title: Soil production function
d541fe51d4bc.sentence: The value of P0 was found to range from 0.08 to 2.0 mm/yr for sites in northern California, and 0.05–0.14 mm/yr for sites in southeastern Australia.

76fdd61b9115.title: Soil production function
76fdd61b9115.sentence: Meanwhile values of k do not vary significantly, ranging from 2 to 4 m−1.

f1acd44a2487.title: Soil production function
f1acd44a2487.sentence: Parameters P0 and k are related to the climate and type of parent material.

32df65b55be3.title: Soil production function
32df65b55be3.sentence: This model dates back to G.K. Gilbert's Report on the Geology of the Henry Mountains (1877).

7fb4459069db.title: Soil production function
7fb4459069db.sentence: Gilbert reasoned that the weathering of bedrock was fastest under an intermediate thickness of soil and slower under exposed bedrock or under thick mantled soil.

50924b357565.title: Soil production function
50924b357565.sentence: This is because chemical weathering requires the presence of water.

56379eac54f1.title: Soil production function
56379eac54f1.sentence: Under thin soil or exposed bedrock water tends to run off, reducing the chance of the decomposition of bedrock.

65ae945dcbd4.title: Laterite
65ae945dcbd4.sentence: Thick laterite layers are porous and slightly permeable, so the layers can function as aquifers in rural areas.

6419ef8ed1ac.title: Laterite
6419ef8ed1ac.sentence: Bedrock in tropical zones is often impermeable granite, gneiss, schist or sandstone; the thick laterite layer is porous and slightly permeable so the layer can function as an aquifer in rural areas.

4799e9624648.title: Laterite
4799e9624648.sentence: One example is the Southwestern Laterite (Cabook) Aquifer in Sri Lanka.

a560215b3c9a.title: Laterite
a560215b3c9a.sentence: The aquifer in this laterite recharges rapidly with the rains of April–May which follow the dry season of February–March, and continues to fill with the monsoon rains.

6642978cddad.title: Laterite
6642978cddad.sentence: The Cabook Aquifer laterites support relatively shallow aquifers that are accessible to dug wells.

bcda8092495e.title: Laterite
bcda8092495e.sentence: In some high-density suburban areas the water table could recede to 15 m (50 ft) below ground level during a prolonged dry period of more than 65 days.

33458b29da30.title: Laterite
33458b29da30.sentence: When moist, laterites can easily be cut with a spade into regular-sized blocks.

072c7ab58162.title: Laterite
072c7ab58162.sentence: Upon exposure to air it gradually hardens as the moisture between the flat clay particles evaporates and the larger iron salts lock into a rigid lattice structure and become resistant to atmospheric conditions.

cc9ee29f37ed.title: Laterite
cc9ee29f37ed.sentence: Laterite is mined while it is below the water table, so it is wet and soft.

4ff0b11950df.title: Laterite
4ff0b11950df.sentence: The stone materials used were sandstone and laterite; brick had been used in monuments constructed in the 9th and 10th centuries.

f62620153e21.title: Laterite
f62620153e21.sentence: The foundations and internal parts of the temple contain laterite blocks behind the sandstone surface.

b9208a1c6409.title: Laterite
b9208a1c6409.sentence: After 1000 AD Angkorian construction changed from circular or irregular earthen walls to rectangular temple enclosures of laterite, brick and stone structures.

9dc18a4bfcd8.title: Laterite
9dc18a4bfcd8.sentence: Since the mid-1970s, some trial sections of bituminous-surfaced, low-volume roads have used laterite in place of stone as a base course.

983c43b12b6f.title: Laterite
983c43b12b6f.sentence: In 1984 US$40,000 per 1 km (0.62 mi) was saved in Malawi by using laterite in this way.

b3df06c9bf96.title: Laterite
b3df06c9bf96.sentence: Locally available laterites have also been used to treat sewage, for example in an acid solution followed by precipitation to remove phosphorus and heavy metals.

4f710d99bb43.title: Laterite
4f710d99bb43.sentence: Locally available laterite—a low-grade bauxite rich in iron and aluminum—is used in acid solution, followed by precipitation to remove phosphorus and heavy metals at several sewage treatment facilities.

b7f603cdcc62.title: Laterite
b7f603cdcc62.sentence: In Northern Ireland, phosphorus enrichment of lakes due to agriculture is a significant problem.

26f54de043b5.title: Laterite
26f54de043b5.sentence: Initial laboratory studies show that laterite is capable of 99% removal of phosphorus from solution.

e07a6fbea8c5.title: Laterite
e07a6fbea8c5.sentence: A pilot-scale experimental facility containing laterite achieved 96% removal of phosphorus.

fe0c76039fdc.title: Laterite
fe0c76039fdc.sentence: Percolating columns of laterite removed enough cadmium, chromium and lead to undetectable concentrations.

fa46aceae35b.title: Laterite
fa46aceae35b.sentence: Laterite soils have a high clay content, which means they have higher cation exchange capacity, low permeability, high plasticity and high water-holding capacity than sandy soils.

55c708bfc30f.title: Laterite
55c708bfc30f.sentence: After the rain, the water moves into the soil slowly.

610563af8d38.title: Laterite
610563af8d38.sentence: These soils are most suitable for plantation crops.

d3372f6adac0.title: Laterite
d3372f6adac0.sentence: They are good for oil palm, tea, coffee and cashew cultivation.

4268ee821ce3.title: Laterite
4268ee821ce3.sentence: However, if the structure of lateritic soils becomes degraded, a hard crust can form on the surface, which hinders water infiltration, the emergence of seedlings, and leads to increased runoff.

fb694e9010f3.title: Laterite
fb694e9010f3.sentence: It is possible to rehabilitate such soils, using a system called the 'bio-reclamation of degraded lands'.

2994a88c4469.title: Laterite
2994a88c4469.sentence: This involves using indigenous water-harvesting methods (such as planting pits and trenches), applying animal and plant residues, and planting high-value fruit trees and indigenous vegetable crops that are tolerant of drought conditions.

bf7306e875b7.title: Laterite
bf7306e875b7.sentence: The International Crops Research Institute for the Semi-Arid Tropics (ICRISAT) has employed this system to rehabilitate degraded laterite soils in Niger and increase smallholder farmers' incomes.

5c77fdae971a.title: Laterite
5c77fdae971a.sentence: Ores are concentrated in metalliferous laterites; aluminum is found in bauxites, iron and manganese are found in iron-rich hard crusts, nickel and copper are found in disintegrated rocks, and gold is found in mottled clays.

28ab78a40339.title: Laterite
28ab78a40339.sentence: Bauxite ore is the main source of aluminum.

2ee5908289c7.title: Laterite
2ee5908289c7.sentence: It is a variety of laterite (residual sedimentary rock), so it has no precise chemical formula.

f792871a1d61.title: Laterite
f792871a1d61.sentence: The average chemical composition of bauxite, by weight, is 45 to 60% Al2O3 and 20 to 30% Fe2O3.

852d737fc6a0.title: Laterite
852d737fc6a0.sentence: It is composed mainly of hydrated alumina minerals such as gibbsite [Al(OH)3 or Al2O3.

39843177db10.title: Laterite
39843177db10.sentence: About 70% of the Earth's land-based nickel resources are contained in laterites; they currently account for about 40% of the world nickel production.

5247287733bd.title: Laterite
5247287733bd.sentence: The basaltic laterites of Northern Ireland were formed by extensive chemical weathering of basalts during a period of volcanic activity.

4d82350a8a11.title: Laterite
4d82350a8a11.sentence: They reach a maximum thickness of 30 m (100 ft) and once provided a major source of iron and aluminum ore.

5bb610018114.title: Periglaciation
5bb610018114.sentence: Periglaciation (adjective: "periglacial", referring to places at the edges of glacial areas) describes geomorphic processes that result from seasonal thawing and freezing, very often in areas of permafrost.

7de3345ada63.title: Periglaciation
7de3345ada63.sentence: However, freeze and thaw cycles influence landscapes also outside areas of past glaciation.

5a598d11854f.title: Periglaciation
5a598d11854f.sentence: Therefore, periglacial environments are anywhere when freezing and thawing modify the landscape in a significant manner.

45eccecf3def.title: Periglaciation
45eccecf3def.sentence: The definition of what a periglacial zone is not clear-cut but a conservative estimate is that a quarter of Earth's land surface has periglacial conditions.

456918fafd6f.title: Periglaciation
456918fafd6f.sentence: Beyond this quarter an additional quarter or fifth of Earth's land surface had periglacial conditions at some time during the Pleistocene.

151be3102197.title: Periglaciation
151be3102197.section: Periglacial zones and climates > Factors affecting location
151be3102197.sentence: These conditions favor processes like frost heaving, solifluction, and ice wedge formation, which are hallmarks of periglacial environments.

4a4ab55e7926.title: Periglaciation
4a4ab55e7926.sentence: Periglaciation became a distinct subject within the study of geology after Walery Łoziński, a Polish geologist, introduced the term in 1909. Łoziński drew upon the early work of Johan Gunnar Andersson.

0820f7ad54ba.title: Ecological succession
0820f7ad54ba.sentence: Ecological succession is the process of how species compositions change in an ecological community over time.

d734178b9d06.title: Ecological succession
d734178b9d06.sentence: Primary succession occurs after the initial colonization of a newly created habitat with no living organisms.

e8ef66e08e1d.title: Ecological succession
e8ef66e08e1d.sentence: This includes newly exposed rock or sand surfaces, lava flows, and newly exposed glacial tills.

5edf7af86c97.title: Ecological succession
5edf7af86c97.sentence: Secondary succession occurs after a disturbance such as fire, habitat destruction, or a natural disaster destroys a pre-existing community.

5e53d958b979.title: Ecological succession
5e53d958b979.sentence: The stages of primary succession include pioneer species such as microorganisms, plants (lichens and mosses), grasses, smaller shrubs, and trees.

72be586d1659.title: Ecological succession
72be586d1659.section: Types of succession > Causes of plant succession
72be586d1659.sentence: These changes include accumulation of organic matter in litter or humic layer, alteration of soil nutrients, or change in the pH of soil due to the plants growing there.

b117e306aa8e.title: Ecological succession
b117e306aa8e.sentence: Plants may facilitate the establishment of other plants by creating suitable conditions for them to grow, for example by providing shade or allowing for soil formation.

20859f5064e6.title: Ecological succession
20859f5064e6.sentence: The development of some ecosystem attributes, such as soil properties and nutrient cycles, are both influenced by community properties, and, in turn, influence further successional development.

df44e1e30887.title: Lessivage
df44e1e30887.sentence: Lessivage, or argilluviation, refers to the movement of fine clay minerals from the upper part of a soil to the lower part of a soil, via the downward movement of water through the soil matrix.

ffb006aa68a7.title: Lessivage
ffb006aa68a7.sentence: Lessivage is the primary mechanism in the formation of the diagnostic, clay-enriched argic, or Bt horizon (Canadian System of Soil Classification) of Luvisolic soils.

960d2e82a8a6.title: Lessivage
960d2e82a8a6.sentence: Lessivage occurs when water that infiltrates the soil picks up negatively charged clay particles, creating a colloid suspension, and carries them downward until changes in the soil physical or chemical environment cause the clay to settle out by flocculation.

57a411b185c8.title: Lessivage
57a411b185c8.sentence: Clay particles settle out of the water if the water remains stagnant for a long period of time, or the clay interacts with positively charged ions deeper in the soil.

5510f6173170.title: Lessivage
5510f6173170.sentence: As the clay and clay complexes accumulate lower in the soil, soil pore-sizes become finer at the zone of accumulation, referred to as the illuvial horizon, further promoting the deposition of clay.

b5b92f7ed609.title: Lessivage
b5b92f7ed609.sentence: Lessivage is most common in medium-textured soils within regions that have moderate to high precipitation.

edfc4f727828.title: Lessivage
edfc4f727828.sentence: It occurs mostly in loams due to their sufficient level of clay and medium-texture which allows them to hold water but still drain well.

6a77762bd54e.title: Lessivage
6a77762bd54e.sentence: It is often associated with deciduous and mixed forested environments where organic acids enhance clay dispersion in the upper soil horizons.

1373b6046bd6.title: Lessivage
1373b6046bd6.sentence: In contrast, very sandy soils drain rapidly and lack sufficient clay, while clay-rich soils drain very slowly, if at all, reducing the depth that the clay migrates.

a7d56e229849.title: Lessivage
a7d56e229849.sentence: Lessivage is widespread in regions such as central and eastern Canada, parts of Europe, and temperate zones of Asia.

6ef75f6ac929.title: Lessivage
6ef75f6ac929.sentence: The deposition of negatively charged clay particles in the lower soil enhances a soil's fertility by increasing its ability to retain positively charged plant nutrients, referred to as the cation exchange capacity (CEC).

ae66c22dd89e.title: Lessivage
ae66c22dd89e.sentence: Lessivage doesn't normally impede soil function, however depending on the depth and amount of clay in the illuvial horizon, soils influenced by lessivage may be more susceptible to compaction from foot, animal or machine traffic.

2d72199af3ee.title: Lessivage
2d72199af3ee.sentence: Overly compacted soils can experience ponding at the surface and may severely limit plant root growth.

641a971dc817.title: Lessivage
641a971dc817.sentence: Land management practices that avoid compaction and improve drainage such as limiting traffic (especially while the soil is wet), tillage by subsoiling and the installation of drain-tile may be needed if the clay-enriched lower horizon becomes too compacted.

4af3402b76c5.title: Ferrallitisation
4af3402b76c5.sentence: Ferrallitisation is the process in which rock is changed into a soil consisting of clay (kaolinite) and sesquioxides, in the form of hydrated oxides of iron and aluminium.

6d9701e20171.title: Ferrallitisation
6d9701e20171.sentence: In humid tropical areas, with consistently high temperatures and rainfall for all or most of the year, chemical weathering rapidly breaks down the rock.

f2020d70f882.title: Ferrallitisation
f2020d70f882.sentence: This at first produces clays which later also break down to form silica.

017f2ba86683.title: Ferrallitisation
017f2ba86683.sentence: Ferrallitisation is the reverse of podsolisation, where silica remains and the iron and aluminum are removed.

84b5de674aa6.title: Ferrallitisation
84b5de674aa6.sentence: In tropical rain forests with rain throughout the year, ferrallitic soils develop.

69866d5b2fdb.title: Ferrallitisation
69866d5b2fdb.sentence: In savanna areas, with altering dry and wet climates, ferruginous soils occur.

2677265ed82f.title: Leaching model (soil)
2677265ed82f.sentence: Owing to irregular distribution of salt in the soil or to irregularity of the soil structure (figure 2), the leaching efficiency (EL) can be different from unity.

a2f6e81f95b6.title: Leaching model (soil)
a2f6e81f95b6.sentence: Soils with a low leaching efficiency are difficult to reclaim.

e8c476f63a2a.title: Leaching model (soil)
e8c476f63a2a.sentence: In the Tagus delta, Portugal, the leaching efficiency of the dense clay soil was found as low as 0.10 to 0.15.

f5cfce4a2552.title: Leaching model (soil)
f5cfce4a2552.sentence: The soil could not be developed for intensive agriculture and was used for rearing of bulls in coarse natural pasture.

1395cc3b8bc8.title: Leaching model (soil)
1395cc3b8bc8.sentence: The clay soil in the Nile delta, Egypt, on the other hand has a much better leaching efficiency of 0.7 to 0.8.

3398e910fff6.title: Leaching model (soil)
3398e910fff6.sentence: The figure illustrates the calibration process of leaching efficiency, which parameter is difficult to measure directly.

c79f539a7311.title: Leaching model (soil)
c79f539a7311.sentence: The observed values of soil salinity correspond best to a leaching efficiency of about 0.75.

6cc3882cb464.title: Tree throw
6cc3882cb464.sentence: A tree throw or tree hole is a bowl-shaped cavity or depression created in the subsoil by a tree.

7eb2a820e20d.title: Tree throw
7eb2a820e20d.sentence: They are formed either by the long-term presence and growth of tree roots or when a large tree is blown over (as a windthrow) or has its stump pulled out which tears out a quantity of soil along with the roots.

d280f4231638.title: Tree throw
d280f4231638.sentence: The pit left in the ground after a rootwad is removed can be several meters across and 1–2 metres (3.3–6.6 ft) deep.

2b96291fa238.title: Tree throw
2b96291fa238.sentence: Tree throws expose humus-poor, mineral-rich soil.

4acf6e283f71.title: Tree throw
4acf6e283f71.sentence: Tree throws contribute to bedrock weathering and soil formation, and why it is fastest in soils of intermediate thickness.

288abaf73374.title: Tree throw
288abaf73374.sentence: In thin soils, fresh bedrock fragments are a large proportion of the upturned rootwad, but trees are sparse; in deeper soils less rock is upturned, but trees are more common, and in soils deeper than the depth of roots, no bedrock is upturned.

a1ebe42bc615.title: Tree throw
a1ebe42bc615.sentence: The advent of trees roughly 370 million years ago led to dramatic ecosystem changes, as before then bedrock weathering was too slow to maintain thick soils in hilly terrain.

616cd2e613a4.title: Tree throw
616cd2e613a4.sentence: Pits from tree throws, together with mounds from decaying fallen trees, are part of the characteristic pit-and-mound topography of old-growth forest.

162c8951bc5a.title: Argillipedoturbation
162c8951bc5a.sentence: Argillipedoturbation, sometimes referred to as self-mulching, is a process of soil mixing caused by the shrinking and swelling of the smectite clays contained in soil.

ae1c78a1ce65.title: Argillipedoturbation
ae1c78a1ce65.sentence: It is an effect specific to soils of the vertisolic variety, and is triggered by the constant cycles of wetting and drying.

eacc5bcdbb9f.title: Argillipedoturbation
eacc5bcdbb9f.sentence: In order for argillipedoturbation to occur, the soil must be at least 30% clay content.

118ddc7571ee.title: Argillipedoturbation
118ddc7571ee.sentence: It is characterized by wide (up to 2 centimetres (0.79 in)), deep (50 centimetres (20 in) or more) vertical cracks in the solum that contain differing materials from the rest of the soil layer they are found in, as well as sloughed-in surface materials.

838353e0f23c.title: Argillipedoturbation
838353e0f23c.sentence: Argillipedoturbation can be strong enough that it can affect the soil horizons by combining the different horizons, making them difficult to distinguish.

f68bd5d36393.title: Argillipedoturbation
f68bd5d36393.sentence: It can also result in a gently-rolling surface referred to as gilgai topography and in the dramatic soil inclusions known as slickensides.

9ec77e71ff66.title: Argillipedoturbation
9ec77e71ff66.sentence: The effects of this process are useful in agriculture, as the organic surface materials fertilize the soil and cause them to become very productive when irrigated.

1426bf89f14e.title: Argillipedoturbation
1426bf89f14e.sentence: However, they are very difficult to plow and manage due to the high, thoroughly mixed clay content.

e756f942b57d.title: Stonelayer
e756f942b57d.sentence: Few topics in the annals of Earth science have generated more controversy and genetic uncertainty than have stonelayers (stone-lines) in soils and sediments.

e13969250397.title: Stone line
e13969250397.sentence: How stone lines form, whether geogenically by geologic processes or pedogenically by soil forming processes is invariably a matter of interpretation (see Soil Biomantle).

d9108bd04984.title: Stonelayer
d9108bd04984.sentence: The controversy has involved the fields of archaeology, geography, geology, geomorphology, ecology, pedology, and soil science, has encompassed all continents except Antarctica, and occupies an extensive literature.

7fa568849211.title: Stonelayer
7fa568849211.sentence: The term ‘stone-line’ was coined and defined in 1938 by Sharpe based on observations in South Carolina, and interpreted as a product of abiotic, more or less geogenic mass transfer on slopes.

7eaff8915478.title: Stonelayer
7eaff8915478.sentence: Sharpe was apparently unaware that predecessor names had been coined in the 19th and early 20th Centuries, involving such terms as “pebble line," “gravel sheet," “cascalho," and others, usually depending on the language employed and the countries where the observations were made.

0a97025f9624.title: Stonelayer
0a97025f9624.sentence: Nor, apparently, was Sharpe aware that such features earlier had been illustrated graphically—in England by Darwin (in 1840 and 1881), in Brazil by Hartt in 1870, in North America by Webster and Shaler (in 1888 and 1891 respectively), and by others.

2026d68c8248.title: Stonelayer
2026d68c8248.sentence: In tropical and subtropical Brazil in the 1870s, Agassiz and Hartt viewed the stonelayer and material above it as evidence for glaciation, a view resurrected by others as recently as the 1960s.

5501c4069bcb.title: Stonelayer
5501c4069bcb.sentence: This two-layered unit was alternatively interpreted as an erosional pavement buried under tropical loess in the 1890s, a view re-adopted by others recently (1980s-2000s) for northern Argentina, Paraguay and southern Brazil.

6af43f12ca1d.title: Stonelayer
6af43f12ca1d.sentence: However, Morrás and colleagues (2009) have argued that stonelayers in these soils are basal components of [[soil biomantles]].

f7926ae851f7.title: Stone line
f7926ae851f7.sentence: And whether the interpretation is geogenic or pedogenic often reflects the background and training of the interpreter.

554620a5d796.title: Soil biomantle
554620a5d796.sentence: Apart from a few stratified cave sites—and those rare open-air sites where archaeological materials were deposited so rapidly that bioturbation and resultant destratifications failed to keep pace with deposition, most prehistoric cultural materials of the world reside in the soil biomantle.

744de0f41ada.title: Soil biomantle
744de0f41ada.sentence: Such materials are thus mixed, and technically and theoretically out of its original context.

1b61646c78e0.title: Soil biomantle
1b61646c78e0.sentence: Since many cultural materials (cleavers, choppers' core-stones, metates, manos, pestles, etc.) are invariably larger than burrow diameters of most key bioturbators at such sites (small rodents, ants, termites, worms), they settle downward and form a stonelayer, and thus become part of a two-layered biomantle.

ec29fc68c5bf.title: Soil biomantle
ec29fc68c5bf.sentence: Smaller artifacts (flakes, debitage) often are homogenized throughout the upper biomantle, and commonly observed in recent bioturbational spoil heaps, like those produced by pocket gophers, moles, and mole-rats.

6c81e4e3edd1.title: Soil biomantle
6c81e4e3edd1.sentence: Beginning with Darwin, the earthworm has been recognized as a key bioturbator of soil biomantles and human artifacts on many continents and islands.

ce218ad4d667.title: Soil biomantle
ce218ad4d667.section: Three notable bioturbation sub-processes and associated particle comminutions
ce218ad4d667.sentence: Soil bioturbations consist of three upper soil disorganizing and organizing sub-processes that can overlap, and that collectively promote particle abrasions and size reductions, termed "particle comminution".

37736a3bb3ff.title: Soil biomantle
37736a3bb3ff.section: Three notable bioturbation sub-processes and associated particle comminutions
37736a3bb3ff.sentence: The three bioturbation sub-processes are biomixing, biotransfers, and biosorting.

417d2e9fe478.title: Soil biomantle
417d2e9fe478.section: Three notable bioturbation sub-processes and associated particle comminutions
417d2e9fe478.sentence: Biomixing refers to the kind of soil bioturbations typically caused by surface-, shallow-, and intermediate-burrowing vertebrates, such as rodents (pocket gophers, tuco-tucos, mole-rats), insectivores (moles), mustelids (badgers), canids (wolves, coyotes, foxes), marsupials (marsupial moles, wombats), aardvarks, armadillos, pigs, and other similar organisms.

0fc697d1615b.title: Soil biomantle
0fc697d1615b.section: Three notable bioturbation sub-processes and associated particle comminutions
0fc697d1615b.sentence: Though animal bioturbations are dominant, tree uprooting is still an important process.

6c3116064e86.title: Soil biomantle
6c3116064e86.section: Three notable bioturbation sub-processes and associated particle comminutions
6c3116064e86.sentence: Biotransfers refers to transfers of soil by animals, vertebrates or invertebrates, either to the surface, within the biomantle, or from lower levels.

f4744f74bcad.title: Soil biomantle
f4744f74bcad.section: Three notable bioturbation sub-processes and associated particle comminutions
f4744f74bcad.sentence: Biotransfers can be effected by any burrowing animal, but the term is most applicable to deep burrowing, so-called conveyor-belt animals, such as ants, termites, and worms.

484679e6f343.title: Soil biomantle
484679e6f343.section: Three notable bioturbation sub-processes and associated particle comminutions
484679e6f343.sentence: Termites, for example, may burrow downward many meters into weathered and unweathered parent material to collect moist soil for constructing their surface mounds (termitaria).

f5769c12ba67.title: Soil biomantle
f5769c12ba67.section: Three notable bioturbation sub-processes and associated particle comminutions
f5769c12ba67.sentence: Biosorting refers to particle sorting, typically in gravelly (mixed particle) soils, that leads to the formation of a stonelayer (SL) horizon at the base of the biomantle, which results in a two-layered biomantle.

92084a175bc7.title: Soil biomantle
92084a175bc7.section: Three notable bioturbation sub-processes and associated particle comminutions
92084a175bc7.sentence: The process begins as animals burrow and only soil particles smaller than their burrow diameters are moved; larger particles settle downward as smaller particles are moved upward from below them.

8cc60be3a276.title: Soil biomantle
8cc60be3a276.section: Three notable bioturbation sub-processes and associated particle comminutions
8cc60be3a276.sentence: Conveyor-belt soil invertebrates (ants, termites, worms, etc.) are the primary biosorters in most tropical, subtropical, and some midlatitude soils, and thus often produce deep, two-layered biomantles if the soils contain gravels, as many do.

061347561f12.title: Soil biomantle
061347561f12.section: Three notable bioturbation sub-processes and associated particle comminutions
061347561f12.sentence: Small fossorial vertebrates (pocket gophers, moles, tuco tucos, etc.), on the other hand, tend to be dominant biosorters in many midlatitude soils, especially deserts, prairies, and steppes.

6b99d6c4633c.title: Soil biomantle
6b99d6c4633c.section: Dynamic denudation, bioturbation and soil biomantle formation
6b99d6c4633c.sentence: The expression dynamic denudation is the sum of all these processes, with bioturbation and organic impacts commonly dominant.

a2fcf26316a2.title: Soil biomantle
a2fcf26316a2.section: Dynamic denudation, bioturbation and soil biomantle formation
a2fcf26316a2.sentence: The biomantle is an organic-rich near-surface layer in which bioturbation is a dominant process, with all other biological and more traditional soil processes normally being subsidiary (e.g., organic matter productions, eluviations-illuviations, weathering-biochemical transformations, wind and water erosions-depositions, freeze-thaw, dilations-contractions, shrink-swell, gravity movements, geochemical-capillary surface-wickings and precipitations, etc.).

76b2fff5020b.title: Soil biomantle
76b2fff5020b.section: Dynamic denudation, bioturbation and soil biomantle formation
76b2fff5020b.sentence: Plants play a key role in soil formation, both agronomically and silviculturally, and this role is reasonably well understood by geomorphologists, pedologists, soil scientists, farmers, gardeners, and others.

ef8f50cc22c2.title: Soil biomantle
ef8f50cc22c2.section: Dynamic denudation, bioturbation and soil biomantle formation
ef8f50cc22c2.sentence: However, the role of animals in soil formation, and in creating soil and soil horizons, and creating various soil-landscape entities (biomantles, Mima mounds, stone lines, etc.), has been poorly understood until recently.

ce2ed6af3b46.title: Soil biomantle
ce2ed6af3b46.section: Dynamic denudation, bioturbation and soil biomantle formation
ce2ed6af3b46.sentence: Wilkinson and Humphreys offer evidence that "bioturbation appears to be the most active pedogenic process operating in many soils." While probably close to the mark, research over multiple decades strongly indicates that bioturbation is the dominant process in the upper part of most soils, notable exceptions possibly being vertisols and cryosols, where shrink-swell and freeze-thaw processes, respectively, appear dominant.

eef9189e8968.sentence: Crop productivity | Low to moderate | Good | Maximum | Low

7aba77b908d6.sentence: Nitrogen was added to soil from rainfall and the nitrogen-fixing activity of lichens, algae and legumes.

bf1364b27342.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/09%3A_Field_Lab/9.04%3A_Time
bf1364b27342.sentence: Soil organic matter began to accumulate, and the soils developed a distinct dark-colored A horizon.

a4864170e33a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/09%3A_Field_Lab/9.04%3A_Time
a4864170e33a.sentence: Rain water began to dissolve and leach the calcium and magnesium carbonates.

621fa398e6c5.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/09%3A_Field_Lab/9.04%3A_Time
621fa398e6c5.sentence: Generally, the lime inhibits further soil profile development by reducing downward leaching of clay particles.

b46bb5a98670.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/09%3A_Field_Lab/9.04%3A_Time
b46bb5a98670.sentence: On the more permeable materials, the rain water has had sufficient time to translocate silicate clay minerals from the A into the B horizon.

43745864b902.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/09%3A_Field_Lab/9.04%3A_Time
43745864b902.sentence: This zone of illuvial clay accumulation is defined as an argillic horizon.

2a5cc1823a9a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/01%3A_Fundamentals/1.01%3A_Introduction
2a5cc1823a9a.sentence: These five soil forming factors also work through four important soil forming processes (Table 2), considered in the following four groups: 1) Additions; 2) Losses; 3) Transformations; And, 4) Translocations.

cf545313fb14.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/01%3A_Fundamentals/1.01%3A_Introduction
cf545313fb14.sentence: Additions | Organic matter, fertilizers, dust deposition, other mineral soil

1a0521b51211.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/01%3A_Fundamentals/1.01%3A_Introduction
1a0521b51211.sentence: Losses | Movement of soil via wind or water, OR chemical compounds leached, eroded, or harvested from the soil

b6204b3496ce.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/01%3A_Fundamentals/1.01%3A_Introduction
b6204b3496ce.sentence: Transformations | Chemical or physical weathering of soil particles or components

2fda77edc8cc.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/01%3A_Fundamentals/1.01%3A_Introduction
2fda77edc8cc.sentence: Translocations | Movement of soil components (organic or mineral) between horizons within a soil profile

3a8d59e52f5a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/01%3A_Fundamentals/1.01%3A_Introduction
3a8d59e52f5a.sentence: These four processes aid in distinguishing soils from layers of materials deposited by geologic processes.

b75176685b88.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/01%3A_Fundamentals/1.01%3A_Introduction
b75176685b88.sentence: The extent to which these four basic processes occur help differentiate soils.

7517bfddc2ca.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/01%3A_Digging_In/1.02%3A_Soil_Genesis
7517bfddc2ca.sentence: In soil genesis we distinguish between transfer processes that remove material from a horizon (termed eluviation processes) and those that lead to gain of material in a horizon via deposition (termed illuviation processes).

e041e87ecb2d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/01%3A_Digging_In/1.02%3A_Soil_Genesis
e041e87ecb2d.sentence: Very fine clay particles can be removed from upper soil layers and deposited deeper in the soil.

22d1ef2d83d4.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/01%3A_Digging_In/1.02%3A_Soil_Genesis
22d1ef2d83d4.sentence: In some soils, complexes between iron and aluminum and OM form and are also transported vertically within the soil and deposited at depth.

1d40746e1237.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/01%3A_Digging_In/1.02%3A_Soil_Genesis
1d40746e1237.sentence: Mixing (also called turbation) between layers of the soil is another type of transfer and occurs due to both organic and physical agents.

2240c756d726.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/01%3A_Digging_In/1.02%3A_Soil_Genesis
2240c756d726.sentence: Mixing also occurs through physical processes such as the shrinking and swelling of certain clay minerals and the freezing and thawing that occurs in almost all Canadian soils.

14246b119ed7.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/01%3A_Digging_In/1.02%3A_Soil_Genesis
14246b119ed7.sentence: The release of ions from minerals or the complete transformation of mineral particles from their initial form to new, secondary minerals is generally called weathering.

707d460636c2.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/01%3A_Digging_In/1.02%3A_Soil_Genesis
707d460636c2.sentence: In some cases, these ions are completely lost from the soil (in the process of leaching) but in others reformation of new minerals (called secondary soil minerals) occurs deeper in the soil.

8f9f4381c770.title: Cheluviation
8f9f4381c770.sentence: Cheluviation is the process in which the metal ions in the upper layer of the soil are combined with organic ligands to form coordination complexes or chelates, moving downwards through eluviation and then depositing.

355b6d7361a4.title: Cheluviation
355b6d7361a4.sentence: Metal ions that can participate in chelation include Fe, Al, Mn, Ca, Mg and trace elements in soil, while the organic ligands combined with these metal ions come mainly from the soil organic matter.

a44b97faabaf.title: Cheluviation
a44b97faabaf.sentence: The chelates produced by fulvic acid and metal ions in soil humus have strong leaching and deposition effects, and therefore are an important manifestation of soil cheluviation, which is generally resulting in the formation of gray-white leaching layers and dark brown/red deposited layer.

ce719bfa05c8.title: Cheluviation
ce719bfa05c8.sentence: Iron and aluminum are easily leached at low pH.

88cce3c31587.title: Cheluviation
88cce3c31587.sentence: As the pH increases, ferric hydroxide and aluminum hydroxide compounds precipitate.

75337f5829b5.title: Cheluviation
75337f5829b5.section: Dissolution and chelation of metal elements
75337f5829b5.sentence: Conversely, at high pH (e.g. 7–8), dissolved metal ions, such as Fe(III), will precipitate out of the solution as insoluble complexes.

a07ac1a01ce4.title: Cheluviation
a07ac1a01ce4.sentence: Under reducing conditions, more organic acids are produced and metal ions are reduced to soluble metal complexes that migrate into the soil.

95d8bdd3e94f.title: Cheluviation
95d8bdd3e94f.sentence: Under oxidative conditions, metal ions are easily precipitated, and the chelate is easily polymerized, thereby separating the chelate from the metal ions.

d6e552decea4.title: Cheluviation
d6e552decea4.sentence: Clay has a certain adsorption capacity for chelates, which weakens the leaching of complexes.

953865aa3eec.title: Cheluviation
953865aa3eec.sentence: On the other hand, soils with a coarse texture and water-saturated soils will likely enhance the leaching effect of chelates.

0b80a116f760.title: Soil memory
0b80a116f760.sentence: Soil memory describes soil as retaining a record of past natural changes, environmental conditions, and human activity.

10b9822789b3.title: Soil memory
10b9822789b3.sentence: The term was coined by Nikiforoff in 1953 and echoes the earlier dictum of Vasily Dokuchaev that soil is "a mirror of the landscape".

8111c93c7b83.title: Soil memory
8111c93c7b83.sentence: In the "palimpsest-wise" mode, characteristic of soils proper (pedomemory), successive pedogenic features are superimposed within the same soil body, so that traces of the present, recent and remote past coexist and partly overprint one another, much like a palimpsest, a reused manuscript on which earlier text has been scraped away and overwritten.

78c569f3853b.title: Soil memory
78c569f3853b.sentence: In the "book-wise" mode, characteristic of stratified sedimentary deposits (lithomemory), records are stored in discrete layers stacked in chronological order, yielding higher and more exact temporal resolution.

6394288067a0.title: Soil memory
6394288067a0.sentence: The soil memory concept has been applied to investigate both natural environmental changes, such as climate evolution, and the interactions between human land use and soil development, as well as to analyze and interpret archaeological evidence preserved in prehistoric soils.

aa7e5d602d17.title: Soil memory
aa7e5d602d17.sentence: The persistence of environmental DNA in cultivated soils has likewise been interpreted as a "memory effect" usable for reconstructing the dynamics of past land use and land cover.

ede036ded341.title: Soil memory
ede036ded341.sentence: Because most soils are polygenetic, a younger pedogenic signal may overprint, mask, or erase an older one, so that the preserved record is partial and "censored" rather than complete.

289ac9e0b8bc.title: Soil memory
289ac9e0b8bc.sentence: Interpretation is further complicated by equifinality a problem common to the historical sciences.

f9261be539a9.title: Soil memory
f9261be539a9.sentence: In paleopedology the soil memory concept has accordingly been framed not as a definitive explanatory device but as an open, exploratory tool based on analogical reasoning, used to link incomplete and sometimes unrelated evidence to testable hypotheses.

7b338ec90fcd.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/09%3A_Field_Lab/9.07%3A_Slope_and_Runoff
7b338ec90fcd.sentence: The following table can be used to estimate the surface runoff rate using soil texture and the percentage of slope.

ea937c2644a1.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/09%3A_Field_Lab/9.07%3A_Slope_and_Runoff
ea937c2644a1.sentence: The steepness of slope is determined in percent (%) calculated as [(rise/run) x 100] using an Abney level or clinometer.

f32d7e41824d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/09%3A_Field_Lab/9.07%3A_Slope_and_Runoff
f32d7e41824d.sentence: The Abney level or clinometer is held at eye level and parallel to the slope.

aec55cbcf609.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/09%3A_Field_Lab/9.07%3A_Slope_and_Runoff
aec55cbcf609.sentence: The level is adjusted allowing the % slope to be read directly.

0e1654bf99bc.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/09%3A_Field_Lab/9.07%3A_Slope_and_Runoff
0e1654bf99bc.sentence: The amount of soil erosion is directly related to the amount of surface water runoff, which depends on the water infiltration rate and the % slope.

973adfaacdc5.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/09%3A_Field_Lab/9.07%3A_Slope_and_Runoff
973adfaacdc5.sentence: The steeper the slope and the less rapid the water infiltration rate, the more rapid the water runoff rate for a given soil.

a922fd6b0021.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/09%3A_Field_Lab/9.07%3A_Slope_and_Runoff
a922fd6b0021.sentence: Generally, as surface water runoff increases, soil erosion increases.

f1e477fa1ae2.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/09%3A_Field_Lab/9.07%3A_Slope_and_Runoff
f1e477fa1ae2.sentence: Soils having granular structure and high porosity have slower water runoff rates than do soils with massive structure and low porosity.

b35bf90e24a9.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/09%3A_Field_Lab/9.07%3A_Slope_and_Runoff
b35bf90e24a9.sentence: This occurs because more water infiltrates into granular soils with less total water being available for over the surface water runoff when compared to massive soils.

c101a9a335d4.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/09%3A_Field_Lab/9.07%3A_Slope_and_Runoff
c101a9a335d4.sentence: The greater the extent of plant vegetation covering the soil, the less soil erosion because the plant tissue intercepts the falling rain drops and greatly dissipates the energy of the falling water mass from directly hitting the soil.

03a5fb4166cf.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/09%3A_Field_Lab/9.07%3A_Slope_and_Runoff
03a5fb4166cf.sentence: If a soil is moister, it requires less rainfall to reach the point where the soil becomes saturated (all pores filled) and water runoff occurs.

db8e78b1872c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/09%3A_Field_Lab/9.07%3A_Slope_and_Runoff
db8e78b1872c.sentence: 6-12 | Sandy loams, sandy clay loams, loams, clay loams, silt loams, silty clay loams | Rapid

ace0a5882f10.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/09%3A_Field_Lab/9.07%3A_Slope_and_Runoff
ace0a5882f10.sentence: 6-12 | Silty clay, clay, sandy clay | Very rapid

4127a7a938b2.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/09%3A_Field_Lab/9.03%3A_Relief
4127a7a938b2.sentence: Summit | The top or highest level of an upland feature such as a hill or mountain. Usually, the summit is relatively level.

3e41c2e5179d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/09%3A_Field_Lab/9.03%3A_Relief
3e41c2e5179d.sentence: Footslope | The inner, gently inclined surface at the base of a hill slope. The surface is dominantly concave in profile. It is a transition zone between the backslope and toeslope where colluvium and alluvium accumulate.

5526a3aff5e0.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/09%3A_Field_Lab/9.03%3A_Relief
5526a3aff5e0.sentence: Shoulder | Forms the uppermost inclined surface at the top of a hill slope. It is the transition zone from the summit to the backslope of an upland. The surface is dominantly convex in profile and erosional in origin.

0fc4ab40968c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/09%3A_Field_Lab/9.03%3A_Relief
0fc4ab40968c.sentence: Backslope | The steepest inclined surface of the hill slope. Backslopes in profile are commonly steep and linear, or steep and convex-concave. Backslopes are erosional forms produced mainly by mass wasting (direct gravitational action) and running water action.

45d060fc5557.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/09%3A_Field_Lab/9.03%3A_Relief
45d060fc5557.sentence: Toeslope | The outermost, gently inclined surface at the base of a hill slope. Toeslopes are constructional surfaces forming the outermost point of a hill slope where alluvium tends to accumulate.

8c46b3deee90.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/09%3A_Field_Lab/9.03%3A_Relief
8c46b3deee90.sentence: Stream terrace | A natural level strip of land in a stream valley, parallel to the stream channel, originally formed near the level of the stream, and representing the dissected remnants of an abandoned flood plain or stream bed.

de2149808cec.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/09%3A_Field_Lab/9.03%3A_Relief
de2149808cec.sentence: Flood plain | The nearly level fluvial (river) plain bordering a stream and subjected to periodic inundation and sediment accumulation under flood stage conditions. It is a constructional landform built of sediment deposited during overflow and lateral migration of the stream.

da1c6416fc49.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/09%3A_Field_Lab/9.02%3A_Climate
da1c6416fc49.sentence: The important components of climate influencing soil formation include precipitation and temperature.

6b1320f968a5.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/09%3A_Field_Lab/9.02%3A_Climate
6b1320f968a5.sentence: As precipitation increases from one locale to another, more water is available to move downward through the soil profile.

c0ae69583d96.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/09%3A_Field_Lab/9.02%3A_Climate
c0ae69583d96.sentence: As water percolates downward (called leaching), water-soluble soil constituents such as soluble salts (bicarbonates, chlorides, nitrates) are translocated from upper soil horizons and are moved deeper into the soil profile.

6f8a1c8ff89c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/09%3A_Field_Lab/9.02%3A_Climate
6f8a1c8ff89c.sentence: Other materials including clay minerals do not dissolve in water, but the clay particles can be suspended in the soil solution and may leach into subsoil horizons.

20f8383fbc6a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/09%3A_Field_Lab/9.02%3A_Climate
20f8383fbc6a.sentence: The greater the amount of precipitation, the deeper these dissolved and suspended materials are leached.

5dd18210d282.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/09%3A_Field_Lab/9.02%3A_Climate
5dd18210d282.sentence: The consequences of leaching include a lower pH (greater acidity), fewer basic cations (Ca2+, Mg2+, K+, Na+), and a lower nutrient content.

d2500b3d90f1.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/09%3A_Field_Lab/9.02%3A_Climate
d2500b3d90f1.sentence: As a result of variations in rainfall, little leaching occurs in desert soils while extensive leaching occurs in humid forest soils.

611f2c235923.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/09%3A_Field_Lab/9.02%3A_Climate
611f2c235923.sentence: The higher the temperature, the greater the amount of evapotranspiration.

76914dd09a7c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/09%3A_Field_Lab/9.02%3A_Climate
76914dd09a7c.sentence: If two regions have the same amount of precipitation, the region having the lower soil temperatures will have more "effective" precipitation and soils will be more highly leached in the cooler region.

ea42fb20009c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/09%3A_Field_Lab/9.02%3A_Climate
ea42fb20009c.sentence: The soils on the north-facing slopes receive less direct solar radiation (lower temperatures, less evaporation).

1ea72930be8c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/09%3A_Field_Lab/9.02%3A_Climate
1ea72930be8c.sentence: These soils on north-facing slopes are more highly weathered, deeper, and subject to greater leaching than are the soils on the south-facing slopes where the microclimate is warmer and drier.

f1f0ca4a78ae.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/01%3A_Digging_In/1.02%3A_Soil_Genesis
f1f0ca4a78ae.section: MAJOR SOIL FORMATION PATHWAYS IN CANADA > Human Activity as a Soil Forming Factor
f1f0ca4a78ae.sentence: So far in this chapter we have only considered soil formation under natural conditions but in many parts of Canada soils have also been transformed by human use.

6fee236f8f88.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/01%3A_Digging_In/1.02%3A_Soil_Genesis
6fee236f8f88.section: MAJOR SOIL FORMATION PATHWAYS IN CANADA > Human Activity as a Soil Forming Factor
6fee236f8f88.sentence: Initially this impact was largely through conversion of land to agriculture and exploitation of forests but in the 19th and 20th Centuries the impact of mining and petroleum exploitation also became important.

37140c2e6e78.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/01%3A_Digging_In/1.02%3A_Soil_Genesis
37140c2e6e78.section: MAJOR SOIL FORMATION PATHWAYS IN CANADA > Human Activity as a Soil Forming Factor
37140c2e6e78.sentence: In terms of soil genesis the almost universal impact of agricultural conversion is a loss of SOM due to the combined effects of the breakup of aggregates and exposure of SOM to microbial decomposition and accelerated microbial decomposition and soil erosion (discussed below).

74dc82cbf5d4.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/01%3A_Digging_In/1.02%3A_Soil_Genesis
74dc82cbf5d4.section: MAJOR SOIL FORMATION PATHWAYS IN CANADA > Human Activity as a Soil Forming Factor
74dc82cbf5d4.sentence: Globally studies have shown that an average about 30% of the original soil organic carbon is lost when conversion from forest or grassland to cropland occurs (FAO, 2019).

64f4c7301fdd.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/01%3A_Digging_In/1.02%3A_Soil_Genesis
64f4c7301fdd.section: MAJOR SOIL FORMATION PATHWAYS IN CANADA > Human Activity as a Soil Forming Factor
64f4c7301fdd.sentence: In terms of soil formation the main effect of soil erosion is to remove part of the organically enriched surface soil.

80bf422c0e6d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/01%3A_Digging_In/1.02%3A_Soil_Genesis
80bf422c0e6d.section: MAJOR SOIL FORMATION PATHWAYS IN CANADA > Human Activity as a Soil Forming Factor
80bf422c0e6d.sentence: This loss (or truncation) of the surface layer leads to a loss of the most fertile part of the soil for plant production.

9f77ad80c574.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/01%3A_Digging_In/1.02%3A_Soil_Genesis
9f77ad80c574.section: MAJOR SOIL FORMATION PATHWAYS IN CANADA > Human Activity as a Soil Forming Factor
9f77ad80c574.sentence: It may also bring a growth-limiting lower soil layer (for example, with high sodium levels) closer to the surface, further reducing plant growth.

5f1fbd06a12a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/01%3A_Digging_In/1.02%3A_Soil_Genesis
5f1fbd06a12a.section: MAJOR SOIL FORMATION PATHWAYS IN CANADA > Human Activity as a Soil Forming Factor
5f1fbd06a12a.sentence: Where deposition of eroded soil occurs in lower slope positions, the upper soil layer becomes unnaturally over-thickened.

6baf309c8684.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/01%3A_Digging_In/1.02%3A_Soil_Genesis
6baf309c8684.section: MAJOR SOIL FORMATION PATHWAYS IN CANADA > Human Activity as a Soil Forming Factor
