6baf309c8684.sentence: Cumulic soil formed by deposition of water-eroded soil at the base of a slope.

c70430d1124f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/01%3A_Digging_In/1.02%3A_Soil_Genesis
c70430d1124f.section: MAJOR SOIL FORMATION PATHWAYS IN CANADA > Human Activity as a Soil Forming Factor
c70430d1124f.sentence: The original topsoil from upslope has been buried under less fertile subsoil.

4db4e93c3b32.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/01%3A_Digging_In/1.02%3A_Soil_Genesis
4db4e93c3b32.section: MAJOR SOIL FORMATION PATHWAYS IN CANADA > Human Activity as a Soil Forming Factor
4db4e93c3b32.sentence: Resource extraction and transport activities such as mining for minerals or for bitumen or pipeline development also fundamentally alter the soil, in some cases by completely excavating the soil and underlying sediment.

e35f64d837cb.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/01%3A_Digging_In/1.02%3A_Soil_Genesis
e35f64d837cb.section: MAJOR SOIL FORMATION PATHWAYS IN CANADA > Human Activity as a Soil Forming Factor
e35f64d837cb.sentence: Currently, regulations are placed to require some level of reconstruction of a soil but inevitably the constructed soil will differ from the original soil profile.

d0244e1e40fa.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/01%3A_Digging_In/1.02%3A_Soil_Genesis
d0244e1e40fa.section: MAJOR SOIL FORMATION PATHWAYS IN CANADA > Human Activity as a Soil Forming Factor
d0244e1e40fa.sentence: Soils resulting with major disruption from human activities are termed anthropogenic (i.e., formed by humans).

600ceabd2ca4.title: Soil memory
600ceabd2ca4.sentence: The concept of a specifically biological (microbial) soil memory has been formalized as the ability of soil microbiota to alter their structure, functional diversity, and activity in response to natural or anthropogenic factors and to preserve those changes over time.

a5c3a14eae7f.title: Soil memory
a5c3a14eae7f.sentence: At the same time, many microorganisms, particularly bacteria, are capable of surviving in dormant states for extended periods, allowing them to persist in soils despite substantial environmental changes.

cb7add5983d9.title: Soil memory
cb7add5983d9.sentence: Advances in molecular biological techniques, such as the polymerase chain reaction (PCR) and next-generation sequencing (NGS), now enable detailed characterization of microbial communities based on their DNA.

84b546ba8730.title: Soil memory
84b546ba8730.sentence: Owing to the high abundance of bacteria in soils and the extraordinary diversity of soil bacterial communities, NGS-based profiling of soil bacteria is particularly well suited for characterizing present soil conditions and for identifying traces of past environmental influences.

a287dfc516db.title: Soil memory
a287dfc516db.sentence: The microbiological dimension of soil memory has been demonstrated at an Iron Age settlement site in Sicily, and in Iron Age cremation burials, where distinctive bacterial communities reflect former human activity.

58663064dbbb.title: Soil memory
58663064dbbb.sentence: Similarly, the diversity and composition of soil bacterial communities have been shown to preserve signatures of medieval and early modern activity areas.

bdac5df0ac54.title: Soil memory
bdac5df0ac54.sentence: Changes in the intensity of agricultural practices have been reconstructed from cyanobacteria communities in lake sediments, while characteristic bacterial communities have also been found to distinguish the infill of Neolithic enclosure ditches from the surrounding soil.

a154950bd738.title: Argillic
a154950bd738.sentence: When a paleosol shows evidence of some continued soil development (pedogenesis) it is termed a "polygenetic" soil.

5346103c2beb.title: Argillic
5346103c2beb.sentence: A variety of paleosols and polygenetic soils are recognized as containing paleo-argillic horizons including the Wounded Moose paleosol of the Yukon in Canada and the Berino Paleosol of New Mexico in the United States.

17db78b955a7.title: Terra rossa (soil)
17db78b955a7.sentence: Instead they propose that terra rossa is polygenetic in origin and that, depending on their geographic location, their parent material, which has been altered by pedogenesis, contains exotic sediments from volcanic ash; non-limestone and non-dolomite; and aeolian sources.

dfd427d2d487.title: Physical geography
dfd427d2d487.sentence: - Soil geography deals with the distribution of soils across the terrain.

a8da22b38297.title: Physical geography
a8da22b38297.sentence: Soil geography studies the spatial distribution of soils as it relates to topography, climate (water, air, temperature), soil life (micro-organisms, plants, animals), and mineral materials within soils (biogeochemical cycles).

7c1332c2d123.title: Natural science
7c1332c2d123.section: Branches of natural science > Earth science > Physical geography
7c1332c2d123.sentence: The field covers the geomorphology, climatology, hydrology, soil geography and biogeography of the Earth’s surface, including mountain building, erosion and desertification.

016444084ab1.title: Konstantin Glinka
016444084ab1.sentence: - - Russian Geographical Society awarded the Lütke Gold Medal to Glinka for his work on soil geography.

04f9f8481b9a.title: Tropical rainforest
04f9f8481b9a.sentence: Most tropical soils are characterized by significant leaching and poor nutrients, however there are some areas that contain fertile soils.

4d47195dde89.title: Tropical rainforest
4d47195dde89.sentence: On younger substrates, especially of volcanic origin, tropical soils may be quite fertile.

57c608d6961d.title: Soil
57c608d6961d.section: Chemistry > Cation and anion exchange > Cation exchange capacity (CEC)
57c608d6961d.sentence: Most of the soil's CEC occurs on clay and humus colloids, and the lack of those in hot, humid, wet climates (such as tropical rainforests), due to fast leaching and decomposition, respectively, explains the apparent lack of fertility of tropical soils.

d367da9aa250.title: Plant nutrients in soil
d367da9aa250.sentence: After nitrogen, phosphorus is probably the element most likely to be deficient in soils, although it often turns to be the most deficient in tropical soils where the mineral pool is depleted under intense leaching and mineral weathering while, contrary to nitrogen, phosphorus reserves cannot be replenished from atmospheric sources.

7e72da5b1c80.title: Soil fertility
7e72da5b1c80.sentence: Bioavailable phosphorus (available to soil life) is the element in soil that is most often lacking, in particular in humid tropical soils.

02acbac741cb.title: Soil matrix
02acbac741cb.section: Mineral colloids: soil clays > Sesquioxide clays
02acbac741cb.sentence: Sesquioxide clays or sesquioxides are a product of heavy rainfall that has leached most of the silica from alumino-silica clay, leaving the less soluble oxides iron hematite (Fe2O3), iron hydroxide (Fe(OH)3), aluminium hydroxide gibbsite (Al(OH)3), hydrated manganese birnessite (MnO2), as can be observed in most lateritic weathering profiles of tropical soils.

a84dd0ff55c5.title: Soil organic matter
a84dd0ff55c5.sentence: Although the structure of humus has in itself few nutrients (with the exception of constitutive metals such as calcium, iron and aluminium) it is able to attract and link, by weak chemical bonds, cation and anion nutrients that can further be released into the soil solution in response to selective root uptake and changes in soil pH, a process of paramount importance for the maintenance of fertility in tropical soils.

de3c125c52a3.title: Soil biomantle
de3c125c52a3.section: One- and two-layered biomantles, soil stonelayers (stone lines)
de3c125c52a3.sentence: Since midlatitude type Bt (argillic) horizons are often lacking in tropical soils owing to an abundance of active and deep bioturbators that move large volumes of soil to the surface (ants, termites, worms, etc.), horizon notations are: M-SL-W, where M is the mineral soil (extended topsoil), SL is stonelayer, and W is the underlying weathered or saprolite zone.

7580c51b2dd0.title: Soil biomantle
7580c51b2dd0.section: One- and two-layered biomantles, soil stonelayers (stone lines)
7580c51b2dd0.sentence: Stonelayers occupy the base of biomantles in many, if not most, tropical soils and in many midlatitude soils.

1d9eb61e5e85.title: Soil
1d9eb61e5e85.sentence: Special mention must be made of the use of charcoal, and more generally biochar to improve nutrient-poor tropical soils, a process based on the higher fertility of anthropogenic pre-Columbian Amazonian Dark Earths, also called Terra Preta de Índio, due to interesting physical and chemical properties of soil black carbon as a source of stable humus.

cb78839eeb3c.title: Biochar
cb78839eeb3c.sentence: Biochar offers multiple soil health benefits in degraded tropical soils but is less beneficial in temperate regions.

f341758dcd5a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.01%3A_Soils_of_British_Columbia_and_Yukon-_The_Western_Cordillera
f341758dcd5a.sentence: This diversity in environmental conditions in turn results in the greatest diversity of soils in Canada.

a9487979afd3.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.01%3A_Soils_of_British_Columbia_and_Yukon-_The_Western_Cordillera
a9487979afd3.sentence: British Columbia and Yukon are the most diverse areas of Canada in terms of geologic history, physiography, climate, biologic species and land use (Valentine et al., 1978).

7ad9dda45804.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.01%3A_Soils_of_British_Columbia_and_Yukon-_The_Western_Cordillera
7ad9dda45804.sentence: The diversity in environmental conditions is the result of the geologic history of the region and the complex pattern of mountain chains and valleys that resulted from the Earth-building forces (Figure 9.1).

9c0d0a3eaf52.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.01%3A_Soils_of_British_Columbia_and_Yukon-_The_Western_Cordillera
9c0d0a3eaf52.sentence: The soils of British Columbia and Yukon include all ten of the soil orders recognized by the System of Soil Classification for Canada (Figure 9.4).

08efd62458d3.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.01%3A_Soils_of_British_Columbia_and_Yukon-_The_Western_Cordillera
08efd62458d3.sentence: This remarkable diversity reflects the wide range of soil forming factors (time, parent material, climate, biota, topography and human activity) contributing to soil formation.

c645afd51a62.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.01%3A_Soils_of_British_Columbia_and_Yukon-_The_Western_Cordillera
c645afd51a62.section: UNIQUE FEATURES OF MAJOR SOIL TYPES > Podzols
c645afd51a62.sentence: The most common soil (i.e., largest geographical extent) in British Columbia is the Podzol.

37b0bd7c64d2.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.01%3A_Soils_of_British_Columbia_and_Yukon-_The_Western_Cordillera
37b0bd7c64d2.section: UNIQUE FEATURES OF MAJOR SOIL TYPES > Podzols
37b0bd7c64d2.sentence: Podzols are predominant in regions with cool soil temperatures and humid climates.

272cecd00157.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.01%3A_Soils_of_British_Columbia_and_Yukon-_The_Western_Cordillera
272cecd00157.section: UNIQUE FEATURES OF MAJOR SOIL TYPES > Podzols
272cecd00157.sentence: Podzolic soils are the true forested soils, found on acidic parent materials of Canada.

2fb03ca8b5e5.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.01%3A_Soils_of_British_Columbia_and_Yukon-_The_Western_Cordillera
2fb03ca8b5e5.section: UNIQUE FEATURES OF MAJOR SOIL TYPES > Luvisols
2fb03ca8b5e5.sentence: Luvisolic soils are one of the two dominant soil orders in British Columbia and are less common in the Yukon.

aab0ffe7275c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.01%3A_Soils_of_British_Columbia_and_Yukon-_The_Western_Cordillera
aab0ffe7275c.section: UNIQUE FEATURES OF MAJOR SOIL TYPES > Luvisols
aab0ffe7275c.sentence: The soils are found in the Interior plateaus and are common in the Boreal forest.

986f38090948.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.01%3A_Soils_of_British_Columbia_and_Yukon-_The_Western_Cordillera
986f38090948.section: UNIQUE FEATURES OF MAJOR SOIL TYPES > Luvisols
986f38090948.sentence: Luvisolic soils are dominant in forested landscapes commonly on loamy glacial tills or glacio-lacustrine deposits.

d5b0299358a9.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.01%3A_Soils_of_British_Columbia_and_Yukon-_The_Western_Cordillera
d5b0299358a9.section: UNIQUE FEATURES OF MAJOR SOIL TYPES > Cryosols
d5b0299358a9.sentence: Cryosolic soils are geographically limited to the northern Yukon in the areas of permafrost and in the Boreal and few locations on the higher mountain peaks in the Alpine regions.

083bfeada815.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.01%3A_Soils_of_British_Columbia_and_Yukon-_The_Western_Cordillera
083bfeada815.section: UNIQUE FEATURES OF MAJOR SOIL TYPES > Chernozems
083bfeada815.sentence: Soils of the Chernozemic order are limited in British Columbia and the Yukon, and they only occur in the Central Interior regions.

603dd44c729d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.01%3A_Soils_of_British_Columbia_and_Yukon-_The_Western_Cordillera
603dd44c729d.section: UNIQUE FEATURES OF MAJOR SOIL TYPES > Chernozems
603dd44c729d.sentence: They are found in the relatively more arid regions of the Cordillera.

21fa599a4f3f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.01%3A_Soils_of_British_Columbia_and_Yukon-_The_Western_Cordillera
21fa599a4f3f.section: UNIQUE FEATURES OF MAJOR SOIL TYPES > Chernozems
21fa599a4f3f.sentence: In British Columbia, beginning at the Canada – USA border in the south, which is almost a true desert, and moving north, the climate becomes more humid, which results in a sequence of Brown Chernozems that gradually transitions to Dark Brown and Black Chernozems.

2be94b17f612.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.01%3A_Soils_of_British_Columbia_and_Yukon-_The_Western_Cordillera
2be94b17f612.section: UNIQUE FEATURES OF MAJOR SOIL TYPES
2be94b17f612.sentence: For example, some landscapes are prone to landslides and avalanches, on which weakly developed soils, the Regosols, can be found.

f3b8352f23f2.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.01%3A_Soils_of_British_Columbia_and_Yukon-_The_Western_Cordillera
f3b8352f23f2.section: UNIQUE FEATURES OF MAJOR SOIL TYPES > Regosols
f3b8352f23f2.sentence: In addition, Regosolic soils are common along the broad Fraser River Delta and on the mountainous landscapes.

2facf9953427.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.01%3A_Soils_of_British_Columbia_and_Yukon-_The_Western_Cordillera
2facf9953427.section: UNIQUE FEATURES OF MAJOR SOIL TYPES
2facf9953427.sentence: Gleysols are most common in coastal regions.

9e73491e1fe8.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.01%3A_Soils_of_British_Columbia_and_Yukon-_The_Western_Cordillera
9e73491e1fe8.section: UNIQUE FEATURES OF MAJOR SOIL TYPES > Gleysols
9e73491e1fe8.sentence: In low lying areas throughout the region and notably in the Lower Fraser Valley, Gleysols are common.

3146d4103e96.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.01%3A_Soils_of_British_Columbia_and_Yukon-_The_Western_Cordillera
3146d4103e96.section: UNIQUE FEATURES OF MAJOR SOIL TYPES > Gleysols
3146d4103e96.sentence: The artificially drained Gleysols are some of the most productive agricultural soils in British Columbia.

238e167ef9f3.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.01%3A_Soils_of_British_Columbia_and_Yukon-_The_Western_Cordillera
238e167ef9f3.section: UNIQUE FEATURES OF MAJOR SOIL TYPES > Anthroposols
238e167ef9f3.sentence: Anthroposols occur throughout British Columbia and Yukon, as the entire region is known for metal, coal, oil and gas extraction and aggregate mining.

cdffd89802fe.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.01%3A_Soils_of_British_Columbia_and_Yukon-_The_Western_Cordillera
cdffd89802fe.section: UNIQUE FEATURES OF MAJOR SOIL TYPES > Anthroposols
cdffd89802fe.sentence: These activities have resulted in local areas of mine “spoil.” In areas of metal mining, the primary concern is acid rock (mine) drainage.

42a8786cea68.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.01%3A_Soils_of_British_Columbia_and_Yukon-_The_Western_Cordillera
42a8786cea68.section: UNIQUE FEATURES OF MAJOR SOIL TYPES > Anthroposols
42a8786cea68.sentence: Most metal mines contain sulphide minerals, such as pyrite and pyrrhotite, which rapidly weather to form sulfuric acid when exposed to water and the oxidizing atmosphere.

e77332a007a7.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.03%3A_Soils_of_Ontario
e77332a007a7.sentence: All of Ontario was once covered by the Laurentide Ice sheet of the Wisconsinan glaciation, with ice thicknesses exceeding one kilometre; this glacial event is responsible for the deposition of almost all the parent materials from which Ontario soils have developed.

d8db226efbe5.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.03%3A_Soils_of_Ontario
d8db226efbe5.sentence: Upon retreat, the continental glacier left behind the varied glacial landscapes we see today.

c5995503f052.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.03%3A_Soils_of_Ontario
c5995503f052.sentence: The ice sheet retreated towards the northeast over millennia, slowly exposing parts of southern Ontario as much as 13,000 years ago, and finally the northernmost portions of the province approximately 8,500 – 6,500 years ago (Crins et al. 2009; Chapman and Putnam 1984).

2abd82e4a000.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.03%3A_Soils_of_Ontario
2abd82e4a000.section: ECOZONES OF ONTARIO > Hudson Plains Ecozone
2abd82e4a000.sentence: This ecozone comprises approximately 25% of the land area of Ontario, and has its southern limit marked by the boundary between mostly Paleozoic (541 to 252 million years ago [mya]) and Mesozoic (252 to 66 mya) limestones of the Phanerozoic Eon, which underlie the ecozone, and the Precambrian Shield (Figure 11.2, Crins et al. 2009).

09ae0ae56cc4.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.03%3A_Soils_of_Ontario
09ae0ae56cc4.section: ECOZONES OF ONTARIO > Hudson Plains Ecozone
09ae0ae56cc4.sentence: These rocks are softer than those of the Precambrian Shield and are neutral to alkaline in reaction (refer to Chapter 5: Soil pH for more information).

be86ecd1a0e2.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.03%3A_Soils_of_Ontario
be86ecd1a0e2.section: DISTRIBUTION OF SOILS IN ONTARIO > Soil distribution in the Hudson Plains Ecozone
be86ecd1a0e2.sentence: The cold, semi-arid climate is the single most important factor.

a4a0b162b943.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.03%3A_Soils_of_Ontario
a4a0b162b943.section: DISTRIBUTION OF SOILS IN ONTARIO > Soil distribution in the Hudson Plains Ecozone
a4a0b162b943.sentence: Despite the relatively small amount of annual precipitation, the cold annual temperature and short growing season do not allow for high rates of evapotranspiration, leaving much of the moisture in the soil.

41f523f3aa09.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.03%3A_Soils_of_Ontario
41f523f3aa09.section: DISTRIBUTION OF SOILS IN ONTARIO > Soil distribution in the Hudson Plains Ecozone
41f523f3aa09.sentence: This is exacerbated by the dominantly clayey and silty textured glacio-marine parent materials which have high water holding capacities.

389e664f37cd.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.03%3A_Soils_of_Ontario
389e664f37cd.section: ECOZONES OF ONTARIO > Boreal Shield Ecozone
389e664f37cd.sentence: The Boreal Shield Ecozone occupies a central band of the province, extending from the Manitoba border in the west, to the Quebec border in the east, and occupies approximately 66% of the province (Figure 11.1).

94c21b932d0c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.03%3A_Soils_of_Ontario
94c21b932d0c.section: ECOZONES OF ONTARIO > Boreal Shield Ecozone
94c21b932d0c.sentence: Bedrock is Precambrian, more specifically from the Archean Eon (formed 4000 to 2,500 mya) and is dominated by gneisses and granites.

58aef1c60d72.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.03%3A_Soils_of_Ontario
58aef1c60d72.section: ECOZONES OF ONTARIO > Boreal Shield Ecozone
58aef1c60d72.sentence: These rocks are resistant to weathering, significantly more so than the neighboring limestones, and their reaction is typically acidic.

ed3c9a8bf456.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.03%3A_Soils_of_Ontario
ed3c9a8bf456.section: DISTRIBUTION OF SOILS IN ONTARIO > Soil distribution in the Hudson Plains Ecozone > Soil distribution in the Boreal Shield Ecozone
ed3c9a8bf456.sentence: Whereas the Hudson Plains Ecozone is dominated by one soil forming factor, climate, the distribution of Soil Orders across the Boreal Shield Ecozone is governed by climate, parent material, topography and vegetation.

2846a26fcba7.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.03%3A_Soils_of_Ontario
2846a26fcba7.section: DISTRIBUTION OF SOILS IN ONTARIO > Soil distribution in the Hudson Plains Ecozone > Soil distribution in the Boreal Shield Ecozone
2846a26fcba7.sentence: In the west, generally from Thunder Bay and Lake Nipigon to the Manitoba border, soils of the Dystric Brunisol Great Group dominate (Figure 11.6).

8f45abb74847.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.03%3A_Soils_of_Ontario
8f45abb74847.section: ECOZONES OF ONTARIO > Mixedwood Plains Ecozone
8f45abb74847.sentence: It occupies the smallest area of the three ecoregions in Ontario; approximately 9% of the land surface.

1cd5789240b7.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.03%3A_Soils_of_Ontario
1cd5789240b7.section: DISTRIBUTION OF SOILS IN ONTARIO > Soil distribution in the Mixedwood Plains Ecozone
1cd5789240b7.sentence: The Mixedwood Plains Ecozone is primarily underlain by Paleozoic limestones, and as such, the parent materials are carbonate rich and typically neutral to alkaline in reaction.

af7f46787338.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.03%3A_Soils_of_Ontario
af7f46787338.section: DISTRIBUTION OF SOILS IN ONTARIO > Soil distribution in the Mixedwood Plains Ecozone
af7f46787338.sentence: Unlike the precipitation gradient that results in separation of the Brunisolic from Podzolic soils in the Boreal Shield, soil development in the Mixedwood Plains is more reliant on the distribution of parent materials, or surficial deposits.

9c562773b416.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.03%3A_Soils_of_Ontario
9c562773b416.section: ECOZONES OF ONTARIO > Mixedwood Plains Ecozone
9c562773b416.sentence: Despite the small footprint, this ecozone is the most extensively studied and managed area in Ontario, primarily because the major population centers are all located within this ecozone, and the most productive agricultural lands in Ontario (and Canada) are located here.

8af4ac3c4e72.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.03%3A_Soils_of_Ontario
8af4ac3c4e72.sentence: In Ontario, the provincial soil is the Guelph soil series, and it was officially named the provincial soil on November 30th, 2015.

253a8df43877.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.03%3A_Soils_of_Ontario
253a8df43877.sentence: The Guelph soil is classified as a Brunisolic Gray-Brown Luvisol and is found on rolling hills and drumlins in Wellington County and surrounding areas, covering over 70,000 hectares.

e5f92c71d81f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.03%3A_Soils_of_Ontario
e5f92c71d81f.sentence: In addition, the Guelph series is an agriculturally important soil, considered prime agricultural soil when not limited by slope, developed in loam to silt loam textured morainal materials, often with a loess cap that is free of stones.

22bb59559d1b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.04%3A_Soils_of_Quebec
22bb59559d1b.sentence: A consequence of that diversity is the broad range of soils found in Quebec, spanning seven soil orders, ranging from fertile Brunisols and Gleysols in the south, to Podzols of the boreal forest, Brunisols in the subarctic and Cryosols in the north.

a2c0ae056ad4.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.04%3A_Soils_of_Quebec
a2c0ae056ad4.sentence: The soils of Quebec follow a classic ‘zonal’ distribution, from south to north (Figure 12.1), reflecting the dominating influence of climate and vegetation, but also the time for soil formation and the differences in parent material from south to north.

f2b225e956cb.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.04%3A_Soils_of_Quebec
f2b225e956cb.sentence: Thus, Quebec soils have formed over the last 6,000 to 10,000 years, during which the climate has warmed and vegetation has moved northwards to occupy the glacial sediments.

6ac33579eb8c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.04%3A_Soils_of_Quebec
6ac33579eb8c.sentence: The soil parent materials partially follow the underlying geology, varying from igneous and metamorphic rocks in the Canadian Shield to the metamorphic rocks in the Appalachian region to softer sedimentary rocks underlying the St. Lawrence valley (Bird 1980).

872c88154469.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.04%3A_Soils_of_Quebec
872c88154469.sentence: Quebec was covered by the Laurentide Ice Sheet until about 12,000 years ago when the southernmost part started to be freed by the ice sheet retreating northwards (Bird 1980; Richard and Occhietti 2005).

e4c59a1c1b1f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.04%3A_Soils_of_Quebec
e4c59a1c1b1f.sentence: With the land surface depressed by the mass of the ice, the sea rushed in to create the Champlain Sea in the St. Lawrence lowlands, depositing clay-rich marine sediments with a high initial salt content.

cbb66a3ba70f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.04%3A_Soils_of_Quebec
cbb66a3ba70f.sentence: The clay sediments laid down in the Champlain Sea were initially salt-rich and leaching of the salt and incision by rivers has created instability.

96d361dfc43b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.04%3A_Soils_of_Quebec
96d361dfc43b.sentence: This has resulted in over 700 landslides and earthflows in the St. Lawrence Lowlands, from Ottawa to Lac Saint-Jean, and some of which destroyed farmland and homes and killed people, such as at Nicolet in 1955 and at St. Jean Vianney in 1971 (Bird 1980; Carson 1978)

591c621c4a6e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.04%3A_Soils_of_Quebec
591c621c4a6e.sentence: The dominant soil order in Quebec is Podzol, covering 39%, comprising mainly the Humo-Ferric great group and concentrated on the Boreal Shield and Taiga Shield terrestrial ecozones (Table 12.1).

8a39f13872d8.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.04%3A_Soils_of_Quebec
8a39f13872d8.section: SOIL DISTRIBUTION IN QUEBEC > Table 12.1. Coverage of soil Great Groups and Orders in Quebec
8a39f13872d8.sentence: Second in coverage is the Brunisol order, covering 17% dominated by the Dystric great group, mainly in the Taiga and Boreal Shield Ecozones, where profile development is not strong enough for soils to fall into the Podzol order.

492ebd89a0d4.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.04%3A_Soils_of_Quebec
492ebd89a0d4.section: SOIL DISTRIBUTION IN QUEBEC > Table 12.1. Coverage of soil Great Groups and Orders in Quebec
492ebd89a0d4.sentence: Organic soils, defined by an accumulation of organic matter over 40 cm thick, cover 8%, The Organic soils are dominantly Mesisols, in which most of the soil profile shows an intermediate degree of decomposition of the original plant tissues, whereas Fibrisols and Humisols show less and greater decomposition, respectively (see Chapter 8; Kroetsch et al. 2011).

53e253933c63.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.04%3A_Soils_of_Quebec
53e253933c63.section: SOIL DISTRIBUTION IN QUEBEC > Table 12.1. Coverage of soil Great Groups and Orders in Quebec
53e253933c63.sentence: Dystric Brunisols can transform into Podzols over several thousand years of soil formation, as occurs in sandy deposits exposed by relative sea level fall along the Quebec North Shore, resulting in the Bm horizon being replaced by sesquioxide-cemented Bfc horizons (Moore 1976).

78295fbae8bd.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.04%3A_Soils_of_Quebec
78295fbae8bd.sentence: Capability Class 1 to 3 soils are very restricted in area, and give an average of 0.28 ha (equivalent to a quarter of a football field) for each Quebecer, the smallest in any province in Canada and half the value in Ontario.

70d712ad3f5a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.04%3A_Soils_of_Quebec
70d712ad3f5a.sentence: Moreover, about 80% of the good quality soils (Classes 1 to 3) are covered by cropland, and this rises to 88% when pasture is included, a large percentage when compared to other parts of Canada.

395186af4553.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.04%3A_Soils_of_Quebec
395186af4553.sentence: Thus, conservation of this limited area of good quality soils is important.

4ede06a94bdc.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.05%3A_Soils_of_the_Atlantic_Provinces
4ede06a94bdc.sentence: Seven of Canada’s ten soil orders can be found in Atlantic Canada, but high annual precipitation rates and a preponderance of relatively coarse, acidic glacial till parent material has led to Podzols being the dominant soil in the region.

b4fa5810c0fb.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.05%3A_Soils_of_the_Atlantic_Provinces
b4fa5810c0fb.sentence: In many cases, these soils are also very stony and/or shallow to bedrock, which further limits their agricultural potential.

e53139c451a9.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.05%3A_Soils_of_the_Atlantic_Provinces
e53139c451a9.sentence: As a result, the Atlantic provinces (New Brunswick, Nova Scotia, Prince Edward Island, and Newfoundland and Labrador) account for only about 1.5% of Canada’s agricultural land base (Statistics Canada, 2016), with forests covering the majority of land in the region.

0afa3d1876b3.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.05%3A_Soils_of_the_Atlantic_Provinces
0afa3d1876b3.sentence: Although each province has locally important agricultural areas, only in Prince Edward Island does agricultural land dominate over forest land.

180545fef007.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.05%3A_Soils_of_the_Atlantic_Provinces
180545fef007.section: FACTORS CONTROLLING THE DISTRIBUTION OF SOILS IN THE ATLANTIC PROVINCES
180545fef007.sentence: Using the National Ecological Framework for Canada, the Atlantic provinces can be divided into four ecozones (Ecological Stratification Working Group, 1996; Figure 13.1), which describe regions that share similar geology, vegetation, soil, and climate.

34a9de45804d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.05%3A_Soils_of_the_Atlantic_Provinces
34a9de45804d.section: FACTORS CONTROLLING THE DISTRIBUTION OF SOILS IN THE ATLANTIC PROVINCES
34a9de45804d.sentence: New Brunswick, Nova Scotia, and Prince Edward Island are all situated within the southern-most Atlantic Maritime ecozone, with the island of Newfoundland fully covered by the Boreal Shield ecozone and Labrador primarily in the Taiga Shield ecozone (with inclusions of the Boreal Shield ecozone in the southeast and the Arctic Cordillera ecozone in the north).

264f91bf2170.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.05%3A_Soils_of_the_Atlantic_Provinces
264f91bf2170.section: FACTORS CONTROLLING THE DISTRIBUTION OF SOILS IN THE ATLANTIC PROVINCES > Atlantic Maritime Ecozone
264f91bf2170.sentence: This ecozone receives an average 1250 mm of precipitation annually (range 970 to 1840 mm) and is the warmest in the region with an average annual temperature of 7°C (range 1 to 8°C) (Fick and Hijmans, 2017).

587fd1d9e1d0.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.05%3A_Soils_of_the_Atlantic_Provinces
587fd1d9e1d0.section: FACTORS CONTROLLING THE DISTRIBUTION OF SOILS IN THE ATLANTIC PROVINCES > Atlantic Maritime Ecozone
587fd1d9e1d0.sentence: Bedrock geology is largely comprised of Paleozoic era formations (Figure 13.3) and are primarily sedimentary in nature; however, inclusions of volcanic and intrusive igneous rock are also common (Wheeler et al., 1997).

65e9e6854f65.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.05%3A_Soils_of_the_Atlantic_Provinces
65e9e6854f65.section: FACTORS CONTROLLING THE DISTRIBUTION OF SOILS IN THE ATLANTIC PROVINCES > Taiga Shield and Arctic Cordillera Ecozones
65e9e6854f65.sentence: The mean annual temperature is highest (1.5°C) along the eastern coast and decreases inland to -7°C. Average annual precipitation is 910 mm and ranges from 650 to 1250 mm.

63b68e4d3d0a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.05%3A_Soils_of_the_Atlantic_Provinces
63b68e4d3d0a.section: FACTORS CONTROLLING THE DISTRIBUTION OF SOILS IN THE ATLANTIC PROVINCES > Taiga Shield and Arctic Cordillera Ecozones
63b68e4d3d0a.sentence: In addition to being the coldest ecozone in the region, the Arctic Cordillera is the driest with an average annual precipitation of only 680 mm (range 560 to 910 mm).

10dcfa241c76.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.05%3A_Soils_of_the_Atlantic_Provinces
10dcfa241c76.section: FACTORS CONTROLLING THE DISTRIBUTION OF SOILS IN THE ATLANTIC PROVINCES > Taiga Shield and Arctic Cordillera Ecozones
10dcfa241c76.sentence: Both these ecozones are mainly underlain by Precambrian metamorphic and intrusive igneous rocks (gneiss and granite).

326a6616e6b9.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.05%3A_Soils_of_the_Atlantic_Provinces
326a6616e6b9.section: FACTORS CONTROLLING THE DISTRIBUTION OF SOILS IN THE ATLANTIC PROVINCES > Taiga Shield and Arctic Cordillera Ecozones
326a6616e6b9.sentence: Surficial geology is comprised of glacial till deposits of variable thickness, but with a large proportion of thin veneer tills and exposed rock in eastern and northern areas (Figure 13.3).

599c372d48f3.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.05%3A_Soils_of_the_Atlantic_Provinces
599c372d48f3.section: FACTORS CONTROLLING THE DISTRIBUTION OF SOILS IN THE ATLANTIC PROVINCES > Atlantic Maritime Ecozone
599c372d48f3.sentence: Surficial geology is dominated by a variety of glacial till deposits, with glacio-fluvial deposits and rocky areas locally important (Figure 13.3).

05cd444d6a69.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.05%3A_Soils_of_the_Atlantic_Provinces
05cd444d6a69.section: FACTORS CONTROLLING THE DISTRIBUTION OF SOILS IN THE ATLANTIC PROVINCES > Boreal Shield Ecozone
05cd444d6a69.sentence: As with other ecozones, surficial geology is mainly comprised of glacial till deposits of variable thickness, but with a larger proportion of thin veneer tills and exposed rock (Figure 13.3).

a33c69393906.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.05%3A_Soils_of_the_Atlantic_Provinces
a33c69393906.sentence: Within this region, there are no Class 1 lands (no significant limitations); furthermore, the distribution of Class 2 lands is limited to Prince Edward Island, northwestern New Brunswick, and the Annapolis Valley of Nova Scotia (Figure 13.7).

a3dcd99e5754.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.05%3A_Soils_of_the_Atlantic_Provinces
a3dcd99e5754.sentence: Class 2 lands occupy approximately 588,000 ha of Atlantic Canada while Class 3 and Class 4 lands occupy approximately 2,275,000 ha and 2,507,000 ha, respectively.

28219c7ab47f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.05%3A_Soils_of_the_Atlantic_Provinces
28219c7ab47f.sentence: The majority of land in Nova Scotia and Newfoundland are Class 7 and are therefore not capable for arable culture or permanent pasture.

3f841da0daa4.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.02%3A_Soils_of_the_Prairie_Provinces
3f841da0daa4.sentence: The soils of the three Prairie Provinces have experienced the greatest conversion to agricultural land uses of any region of Canada.

85ced59ac202.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.02%3A_Soils_of_the_Prairie_Provinces
85ced59ac202.section: FACTORS CONTROLLING THE DISTRIBUTION OF SOILS IN THE PRAIRIE PROVINCES
85ced59ac202.sentence: The regional pattern of soil distribution (Figure 10.1) is determined by the bedrock geology and the effect of the Western Cordillera on the regional climate.

a2aecd5030ec.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.02%3A_Soils_of_the_Prairie_Provinces
a2aecd5030ec.sentence: In most of the southern portion of this region more than 80% of the land is agricultural (Prairie Farm Rehabilitation Administration, 2000).

1ba74125c52b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.02%3A_Soils_of_the_Prairie_Provinces
1ba74125c52b.sentence: Throughout this region the specific type of agriculture is closely linked to the capability of the soil, and hence the pattern of agricultural land use is largely determined by the pattern of the soils themselves.

e02d9b6ce630.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.02%3A_Soils_of_the_Prairie_Provinces
e02d9b6ce630.sentence: Although we typically refer to Alberta, Saskatchewan and Manitoba as the Prairie Provinces, it is important recognize that the true prairies generally occupy only the southern portion of these provinces.

a03a770fdef0.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.02%3A_Soils_of_the_Prairie_Provinces
a03a770fdef0.section: FACTORS CONTROLLING THE DISTRIBUTION OF SOILS IN THE PRAIRIE PROVINCES
a03a770fdef0.sentence: The Prairie Provinces are underlain by approximately ⅓ igneous and metamorphic rocks of the Canadian Shield and ⅔ sedimentary rocks (Figure 10.2).

b8e2d29b9cad.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.02%3A_Soils_of_the_Prairie_Provinces
b8e2d29b9cad.section: FACTORS CONTROLLING THE DISTRIBUTION OF SOILS IN THE PRAIRIE PROVINCES
b8e2d29b9cad.sentence: As discussed in Chapters 2 and 8, the glacial sediments that form the parent materials of soils closely reflect the nature of the bedrock that underlies them; igneous rocks yield acidic, sandy and gravelly parent materials and sedimentary rocks produce neutral, alkaline, loamy parent materials.

8670e89ff093.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.02%3A_Soils_of_the_Prairie_Provinces
8670e89ff093.section: MAJOR SOILS OF THE PRAIRIE PROVINCES
8670e89ff093.sentence: The dominant soil order in the southern part of this region is the Chernozemic order, which formed in the grasslands that were found in this area prior to European settlement.

d7b81ae0fbde.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.02%3A_Soils_of_the_Prairie_Provinces
d7b81ae0fbde.section: MAJOR SOILS OF THE PRAIRIE PROVINCES
d7b81ae0fbde.sentence: Throughout most of the region, the Chernozemic soils are bounded by soils of the Luvisolic order, which are associated with the mixed deciduous-coniferous forest characteristic of the northern part of this region.

72e9d3ba71bc.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.02%3A_Soils_of_the_Prairie_Provinces
72e9d3ba71bc.section: MAJOR SOILS OF THE PRAIRIE PROVINCES
72e9d3ba71bc.sentence: Brunisolic soils are the dominant soil order on the Canadian Shield and consists of acidic forest soils develop on the sand and gravelly parent materials characteristic of this area.

2b0f8390c7a4.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.02%3A_Soils_of_the_Prairie_Provinces
2b0f8390c7a4.section: MAJOR SOILS OF THE PRAIRIE PROVINCES
2b0f8390c7a4.sentence: The cold temperatures and permanent water saturation has led to the development of thick layers of peat and formation of permanently frozen layers within the peats.

24edec2421df.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.02%3A_Soils_of_the_Prairie_Provinces
24edec2421df.section: MAJOR SOILS OF THE PRAIRIE PROVINCES
24edec2421df.sentence: These soils are classified as Organic Cryosols in the CSSC (Figure 10.1).

164da0e1a08b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.02%3A_Soils_of_the_Prairie_Provinces
164da0e1a08b.sentence: At that time the dominant crop was spring wheat and summerfallow (i.e., a year of fallow with tillage of the soil to suppress weed growth following a year of wheat) was the dominant tillage practice.

ad457e5a072f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.02%3A_Soils_of_the_Prairie_Provinces
ad457e5a072f.sentence: Currently, a much wider range of crops (e.g., canola, pulse crops, flax) is grown, and the great majority of producers practice continuous cultivation with high amounts of crop residue left on the soil surface (i.e., conservation tillage or no-till).

35aa585c6fa3.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.02%3A_Soils_of_the_Prairie_Provinces
35aa585c6fa3.sentence: In the CLI rankings, classes 1 through 4 are considered to be capable of sustained use for cultivated field crops.

e7fd79d91362.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.02%3A_Soils_of_the_Prairie_Provinces
e7fd79d91362.sentence: Classes 5 and 6 are only suitable for forage production and are most commonly used for grazing of livestock.

b6b8ffc01aa8.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.02%3A_Soils_of_the_Prairie_Provinces
b6b8ffc01aa8.sentence: The major soil property that determines agricultural capability in the CLI system is soil texture due primarily to its effect on water availability.

e04cfc81839a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.02%3A_Soils_of_the_Prairie_Provinces
e04cfc81839a.sentence: At the northern boundary of the Chernozemic soils the grasslands become increasingly interspersed with clumps of trees and shrubs and ultimately the forest forms an almost continuous cover over the soil.

c2a76eb60c2e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.02%3A_Soils_of_the_Prairie_Provinces
c2a76eb60c2e.sentence: The transitional grassland-forest zone is referred to as the Parkland zone, and the continuous forest cover as the Mixedwood forest, reflecting the forest cover of deciduous and coniferous species.

a7805cfe10ad.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.02%3A_Soils_of_the_Prairie_Provinces
a7805cfe10ad.sentence: In the Parkland, the inputs of organic carbon from grasses decrease and leaf litter from trees builds up on the soil surface as a LFH layer.

0e396b0f8918.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.02%3A_Soils_of_the_Prairie_Provinces
0e396b0f8918.sentence: The colour of the Ah horizon grows lighter, and bleaching of the horizon also begins to occur, forming a surface A horizon with both humus inputs (given an ‘h’ suffix) and bleaching (an ‘e’ suffix) – the Ahe horizon.

8e9e683622b7.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.02%3A_Soils_of_the_Prairie_Provinces
8e9e683622b7.sentence: These soils are classified into the Dark Gray Chernozemic great group.

183b6006b9e9.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.02%3A_Soils_of_the_Prairie_Provinces
183b6006b9e9.sentence: North of the forest-grassland transition zone, organic inputs form a discrete layer laying on top of the mineral soil (the LFH layer) and the soils have a well-developed bleached layer (Ae horizon) overlying a B horizon with higher clay levels (Bt horizon).

bdcbb9be0b73.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.02%3A_Soils_of_the_Prairie_Provinces
bdcbb9be0b73.sentence: The Bt horizon is underlain by a C horizon with secondary (Cca) or primary (Ck) carbonates.

dad3ab624150.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.02%3A_Soils_of_the_Prairie_Provinces
dad3ab624150.sentence: These soils are classified into the Gray Luvisolic great group (Figure 10.9), which dominates the forested landscapes underlain by neutral-alkaline tills (Pettapiece et al., 2010; Lavkulich and Arocena, 2011).

5788aae92851.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.02%3A_Soils_of_the_Prairie_Provinces
5788aae92851.sentence: Gray Luvisols also occur in the large area of glacio-lacustrine parent materials in north-central Manitoba.

6fd6b3ba946d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.02%3A_Soils_of_the_Prairie_Provinces
6fd6b3ba946d.sentence: The zonal pattern of great groups of the Chernozemic order reflects the different types of grasslands that once occupied the area (and the regional climates responsible for the zonation of grasses) (Fuller, 2010; Pennock et al., 2011).

69235f4bc98a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.02%3A_Soils_of_the_Prairie_Provinces
69235f4bc98a.sentence: The major climate attribute that varies across the region is the mean annual water deficit (Pennock et al., 2011, Table 10.2).

0873c8bbcf48.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.02%3A_Soils_of_the_Prairie_Provinces
0873c8bbcf48.sentence: These grasses were responsible for organic carbon inputs into the soil, and the colour of the diagnostic Ah horizons reflects differences in the amount of organic carbon additions from the various grass communities.

4b7e0daad75e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.02%3A_Soils_of_the_Prairie_Provinces
4b7e0daad75e.sentence: The great groups of the Chernozemic order are based on the colour differences of the A horizons.

ff82b22f5f35.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.02%3A_Soils_of_the_Prairie_Provinces
ff82b22f5f35.sentence: The driest portions of the region have annual water deficits of approximately 200 mm and the native grasses of this region were low grasses with limited above- and below-ground biomass.

3fbb56766ba7.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.02%3A_Soils_of_the_Prairie_Provinces
3fbb56766ba7.sentence: The lower organic carbon inputs lead to the development of soils of the Brown Chernozemic great group (Figure 10.4).

b04e8a41e85f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.02%3A_Soils_of_the_Prairie_Provinces
b04e8a41e85f.sentence: The water deficit decreases west and north of this dry region, and greater organic carbon inputs lead to formation of Dark Brown Chernozemic soils and Black Chernozemic soils.

fc251433ac4a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.02%3A_Soils_of_the_Prairie_Provinces
fc251433ac4a.sentence: The highest organic carbon levels occur in southern Manitoba where the annual water deficit is only approximately 70 mm.

c2b55ea9071f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/02%3A_Digging_Across_Canada/2.02%3A_Soils_of_the_Prairie_Provinces
c2b55ea9071f.sentence: Soils of the Chernozemic order have organically enriched A horizons (Ah) overlying decalcified and slightly reddened Bm horizons.

a058e2a08c51.title: Paleopedology
a058e2a08c51.sentence: The role of parent material is best understood from studies of soils that formed under similar conditions on different parent materials or lithosequences (differing soil profile characteristics because of differing parent materials).

3fcea8a56a97.title: Goldich dissolution series
3fcea8a56a97.sentence: The Goldich dissolution series can be applied to Lithosequences, which are a way of characterizing a soil profile based on its parent material.

000040a975e7.title: Goldich dissolution series
000040a975e7.sentence: Lithosequences include soils that have undergone relatively similar weathering conditions, so variations in composition are based on the relative weathering rates of parent minerals.

c36ce36aceef.title: Surface runoff
c36ce36aceef.sentence: On the extremely ancient soils of Australia and Southern Africa, proteoid roots with their extremely dense networks of root hairs can absorb so much rainwater as to prevent runoff even with substantial amounts of rainfall.

6cff9b3083b6.title: Cluster root
6cff9b3083b6.sentence: As a result, plants with proteoid roots can grow in soil that is very low in nutrients, such as the phosphorus-deficient native soils of Australia.

a0e35d73ce6d.title: Australian Soil Classification
a0e35d73ce6d.sentence: The Australian Soil Classification supersedes other classification systems previously developed for Australian soils, including the Factual Key (1960) and the Handbook of Australian Soils (1968).

8ec1b1c22413.title: Handbook of Australian Soils
8ec1b1c22413.sentence: The Handbook of Australian Soils is a soil classification system developed for Australian soils.

7f867f0d7616.title: James Arthur Prescott
7f867f0d7616.sentence: He published in CSIR bulletin 52 "The Soils of Australia in Relation to Vegetation and Climate".

ecd3bd943735.title: Grain size
ecd3bd943735.sentence: Grain size (or particle size) is the diameter of individual grains of sediment, or the lithified particles in clastic rocks.

fe5ea7125ca6.title: Grain size
fe5ea7125ca6.sentence: This is different from the crystallite size, which refers to the size of a single crystal inside a particle or grain.

7b0f31d858d4.title: Grain size
7b0f31d858d4.sentence: A single grain can be composed of several crystals.

411f3ee2b97e.title: Grain size
411f3ee2b97e.sentence: Granular material can range from very small colloidal particles, through clay, silt, sand, gravel, and cobbles, to boulders.

5df5fd78551e.title: Grain size
5df5fd78551e.sentence: Size ranges define limits of classes that are given names in the Wentworth scale (or Udden–Wentworth scale named after geologists Chester K. Wentworth and Johan A. Udden) used in the United States.

a373bfe49607.title: Grain size
a373bfe49607.sentence: ISO 14688-1:2017 establishes the basic principles for identifying and classifying soils based on those material and mass characteristics most commonly used for soils for engineering purposes.
