2411a8fad56e.title: Sand
2411a8fad56e.sentence: Sand is a granular material composed of finely divided mineral particles.

ae23eecbfc7c.title: Sand
ae23eecbfc7c.sentence: Sand has various compositions but is usually defined by its grain size.

ea6d415e40f1.title: Sand
ea6d415e40f1.sentence: Sand grains are smaller than gravel and coarser than silt.

0148565ea21c.title: Sand
0148565ea21c.sentence: By another definition, in terms of particle size as used by geologists, sand particles range in diameter from 0.0625 mm (or 1⁄16 mm) a volume of approximately 0.00012 cubic millimetres, to 2 mm, a volume of approximately 4.2 cubic millimetres, the difference in volumes being 34,688 measures difference.

e2ad7e724482.title: Sand
e2ad7e724482.sentence: Sand can also refer to a textural class of soil or soil type; i.e., a soil containing more than 85 percent sand-sized particles by mass.

f4a39fccd396.title: Sand
f4a39fccd396.sentence: In the United States, sand is commonly divided into five sub-categories based on size: very fine sand (1⁄16 – 1⁄8 mm diameter), fine sand (1⁄8 mm – 1⁄4 mm), medium sand (1⁄4 mm – 1⁄2 mm), coarse sand (1⁄2 mm – 1 mm), and very coarse sand (1 mm – 2 mm).

ffb08e77144e.title: Sand
ffb08e77144e.sentence: These sizes are based on the Krumbein phi scale, where size is Φ = -log2D; D being the particle size in mm.

d63588038572.title: Sand
d63588038572.sentence: The most common constituent of sand, in inland continental settings and non-tropical coastal settings, is silica (silicon dioxide, or SiO2), usually in the form of quartz, which, because of its chemical inertness and considerable hardness, is the most common mineral resistant to weathering.

d5a4852920cb.title: Sand
d5a4852920cb.sentence: Calcium carbonate is the second most common type of sand.

fab2cef1abbf.title: Sand
fab2cef1abbf.sentence: One such example of this is aragonite, which has been created over the past 500 million years by various forms of life, such as coral and shellfish.

ac91567b5229.title: Sand
ac91567b5229.sentence: Somewhat more rarely, sand may be composed of calcium sulfate, such as gypsum and selenite, as is found in places such as White Sands National Park and Salt Plains National Wildlife Refuge in the U.S.

ea51eee74856.title: Sand
ea51eee74856.sentence: Sand feels gritty when rubbed between the fingers.

904c1545b4b4.title: Sand
904c1545b4b4.sentence: Quartz sand that is recently weathered from granite or gneiss quartz crystals will be angular.

e57ca47fdecd.title: Sand
e57ca47fdecd.sentence: Sand that is transported long distances by water or wind will be rounded, with characteristic abrasion patterns on the grain surface.

44eb2cc54600.title: Sand
44eb2cc54600.sentence: The study of individual grains can reveal much historical information as to the origin and kind of transport of the grain.

bda5814f752a.title: Sand
bda5814f752a.sentence: - Agriculture: Sandy soils are ideal for crops such as watermelons, peaches, and peanuts, and their excellent drainage characteristics make them suitable for intensive dairy farming.

b30c79089ec2.title: Sand
b30c79089ec2.sentence: It is called grus in geology or sharp sand in the building trade where it is preferred for concrete, and in gardening where it is used as a soil amendment to loosen clay soils.

b0b915067f88.title: Silt
b0b915067f88.sentence: Silt is granular material of a size between sand and clay and composed mostly of broken grains of quartz.

d6946ae65800.title: Silt
d6946ae65800.sentence: A more precise definition of silt used by geologists is that it is detrital particles with sizes between 1/256 and 1/16 mm (about 4 to 63 microns).

bc2d5423e6c3.title: Silt
bc2d5423e6c3.sentence: USDA United States Department of Agriculture 0.05–0.002 mm.

c6952c6b3c60.title: Silt
c6952c6b3c60.sentence: The upper size limit of 1/16 mm or 63 microns corresponds to the smallest particles that can be discerned with the unaided eye.

b0ef2049bb4d.title: Silt
b0ef2049bb4d.sentence: As noted above, the lower limit of 2 to 4 microns corresponds to the transition from particles that are predominantly broken quartz grains to particles that are predominantly clay mineral particles.

7d0409e77031.title: Silt
7d0409e77031.sentence: Silt usually has a floury feel when dry, and lacks plasticity when wet.

9fe87cbc72cd.title: Silt
9fe87cbc72cd.sentence: Silt can be distinguished from clay in the field by its lack of plasticity or cohesiveness and by its grain size.

f2e96ce9eb7e.title: Silt
f2e96ce9eb7e.sentence: Silt grains are large enough to give silt a gritty feel, particularly if a sample is placed between the teeth.

acb3366cc208.title: Silt
acb3366cc208.sentence: Clay-size particles feel smooth between the teeth.

751d64a6fef4.title: Silt
751d64a6fef4.sentence: It is produced in both very hot climates (through such processes as collisions of quartz grains in dust storms) and very cold climates (through such processes as glacial grinding of quartz grains.)

d721371b3eb0.title: Silt
d721371b3eb0.sentence: Loess is soil rich in silt, which makes up some of the most fertile agricultural land on Earth.

cc73ccb226b6.title: Aeolian processes
cc73ccb226b6.sentence: Deposits of this windblown silt are known as loess.

c1df1f7fd47b.title: Silt
c1df1f7fd47b.sentence: The quartz particles in silt do not themselves provide nutrients, but they promote excellent soil structure, and silt-sized particles of other minerals, present in smaller amounts, provide the necessary nutrients.

62185160a302.title: Silt
62185160a302.sentence: However, silt is very vulnerable to erosion, and it has poor mechanical properties, making construction on silty soil problematic.

62335ba712f5.title: Silt
62335ba712f5.sentence: Silt is susceptible to liquefaction during strong earthquakes due to its lack of plasticity.

1aa2a92457aa.title: Silt
1aa2a92457aa.sentence: When silt appears as a pollutant in water the phenomenon is known as siltation.

e4554337c5bf.title: Silt
e4554337c5bf.sentence: The proportions of coarse and fine silt in a sediment sample are determined more precisely in the laboratory using the pipette method, which is based on settling rate via Stokes' law and gives the particle size distribution accordingly.

9b46d16c715b.title: Silt
9b46d16c715b.sentence: While the coarsest silt particles (60 micron) settle out of a meter of still water in just five minutes, the finest silt grains (2 microns) can take several days to settle out of still water.

e95b5e0cc528.title: Soil texture
e95b5e0cc528.sentence: Soil separates are specific ranges of particle sizes.

79ffcab60a2e.title: Physical properties of soil
79ffcab60a2e.sentence: Soil texture is determined by the relative proportion of the three kinds of soil mineral particles, called soil separates: sand, silt, and clay.

4f7ec7789fd5.title: Soil texture
4f7ec7789fd5.sentence: The smallest particles are clay particles and are classified as having diameters of less than 0.002 mm.

ca9faca2d585.title: Soil texture
ca9faca2d585.sentence: The next smallest particles are silt particles and have diameters between 0.002 mm and 0.05 mm (in USDA Soil Taxonomy).

318f60744cef.title: Soil texture
318f60744cef.sentence: The largest particles are sand particles and are larger than 0.05 mm in diameter.

faa3b5ae6db5.title: Soil texture
faa3b5ae6db5.sentence: Furthermore, large sand particles can be described as coarse, intermediate as medium, and the smaller as fine.

c7fca0f430a5.title: Soil texture
c7fca0f430a5.sentence: Other countries have their own particle size classifications.

f335481626b6.title: Soil texture
f335481626b6.sentence: Clay particles are plate-shaped instead of spherical, allowing for an increased specific surface area.

75ebcbd71b5a.title: Physical properties of soil
75ebcbd71b5a.sentence: Sand is least active, having the least specific surface area, followed by silt; clay is the most active.

5ca7809c2e9c.title: Physical properties of soil
5ca7809c2e9c.sentence: Water-holding capacity | Low | Medium to high | High

c5af6b2b3634.title: Physical properties of soil
c5af6b2b3634.sentence: Drainage rate | High | Slow to medium | Very slow

704739a2389c.title: Clay
704739a2389c.sentence: Clay-size particles and clay minerals are not the same, despite a degree of overlap in their respective definitions.

1867f53f9e64.title: Clay
1867f53f9e64.sentence: Although many naturally occurring deposits include both silts and clay, clays are distinguished from other fine-grained soils by differences in size and mineralogy.

4d210476708a.title: Clay
4d210476708a.sentence: Clays are distinguished from other fine-grained soils by differences in size and mineralogy.

f2d7cb8fce8b.title: Clay
f2d7cb8fce8b.sentence: Silts, which are fine-grained soils that do not include clay minerals, tend to have larger particle sizes than clays.

787fcec23e0c.title: Clay
787fcec23e0c.sentence: Geologists and soil scientists usually consider the separation to occur at a particle size of 2 μm (clays being finer than silts), sedimentologists often use 4–5 μm, and colloid chemists use 1 μm.

7a79918ded9e.title: Clay
7a79918ded9e.sentence: ISO 14688 grades clay particles as being smaller than 2 μm and silt particles as being larger.

6e062603c4ef.title: Clay
6e062603c4ef.sentence: Geotechnical engineers distinguish between silts and clays based on the plasticity properties of the soil, as measured by the soils' Atterberg limits.

bba619a77675.title: Physical properties of soil
bba619a77675.sentence: There is no clear relationship between the size of soil mineral components and their mineralogical nature: sand and silt particles can be calcareous as well as siliceous, while textural clay (0.002 mm (7.9×10^−5 in)) can be made of very fine quartz particles as well as of multi-layered secondary minerals.

51ef158d4f8a.title: Physical properties of soil
51ef158d4f8a.sentence: Soil mineral components belonging to a given textural class may thus share properties linked to their specific surface area (e.g. moisture retention) but not those linked to their chemical composition (e.g. cation exchange capacity).

92d7225570bf.title: Clay
92d7225570bf.sentence: The defining mechanical property of clay is its plasticity when wet and its ability to harden when dried or fired.

2ac1986dccec.title: Clay
2ac1986dccec.sentence: Clay has a high content of clay minerals that give it its plasticity.

0170f6cdb6b6.title: Clay
0170f6cdb6b6.sentence: These plates are tough but flexible, and in moist clay, they adhere to each other.

15713cbfe0b6.title: Clay
15713cbfe0b6.sentence: The resulting aggregates give clay the cohesion that makes it plastic.

aa252a19eea2.title: Clay
aa252a19eea2.sentence: In kaolinite clay, the bonding between plates is provided by a film of water molecules that hydrogen bond the plates together.

58b5d727fc81.title: Clay
58b5d727fc81.sentence: The bonds are weak enough to allow the plates to slip past each other when the clay is being moulded, but strong enough to hold the plates in place and allow the moulded clay to retain its shape after it is moulded.

62a539072aa6.title: Clay
62a539072aa6.sentence: When the clay is dried, most of the water molecules are removed, and the plates form direct hydrogen bonds with each other, making the dried clay rigid but still fragile.

c88fa7684d6c.title: Clay
c88fa7684d6c.sentence: If the clay is moistened again, it will once more become plastic.

0e491611a86b.title: Clay
0e491611a86b.sentence: Clays show a broad range of water content within which they are highly plastic, from a minimum water content (called the plastic limit) where the clay is just moist enough to mould, to a maximum water content (called the liquid limit) where the moulded clay is just dry enough to hold its shape.

970ea8da37d2.title: Clay
970ea8da37d2.sentence: The plastic limit of kaolinite clay ranges from about 36% to 40% and its liquid limit ranges from about 58% to 72%.

11b6666b2e28.title: Plasticity (physics)
11b6666b2e28.sentence: Soils, particularly clays, display a significant amount of inelasticity under load.

a311fd30dfc1.title: Plasticity (physics)
a311fd30dfc1.sentence: Plastic behavior in soils is caused primarily by the rearrangement of clusters of adjacent grains.

2d1fc5eed173.title: Plasticity (physics)
2d1fc5eed173.sentence: The causes of plasticity in soils can be quite complex and are strongly dependent on the microstructure, chemical composition, and water content.

16a8ffd4154e.title: Clay
16a8ffd4154e.sentence: Clay is generally considered undesirable for agriculture, although some amount of clay is a necessary component of good soil.

2655f3adeda8.title: Clay
2655f3adeda8.sentence: Compared to other soils, clay soils are less suitable for crops due to their tendency to retain water, and require artificial drainage and tillage to make suitable for planting.

a0ada381116d.title: Clay
a0ada381116d.sentence: However, clay soils are often more fertile and can hold onto nutrients better due to their higher cation-exchange capacity, allowing more land to remain in production rather than being left fallow.

fc123e233318.title: Physical properties of soil
fc123e233318.sentence: Clay soils also resist wind and water erosion better than silty and sandy soils, as the particles bond tightly to each other, and that with a strong mitigation effect of organic matter.

f10dd1045381.title: Soil texture
f10dd1045381.sentence: In the United States, twelve major soil texture classifications are defined by the United States Department of Agriculture.

e09b5e3f77be.title: Soil texture
e09b5e3f77be.sentence: The twelve classifications are sand, loamy sand, sandy loam, loam, silt loam, silt, sandy clay loam, clay loam, silty clay loam, sandy clay, silty clay, and clay.

5b22a9b97c71.title: Soil texture
5b22a9b97c71.sentence: Classifications are typically named for the primary constituent particle size or a combination of the most abundant particles sizes, e.g. "sandy clay" or "silty clay".

0b8433d569ff.title: Soil texture
0b8433d569ff.sentence: A fourth term, loam, is used to describe equal properties of sand, silt, and clay in a soil sample, and lends to the naming of even more classifications, e.g. "clay loam" or "silt loam".

9adb6d46c474.title: Loam
9adb6d46c474.sentence: Loam (in geology and soil science) is soil composed mostly of sand (particle size > 63 μm), silt (particle size > 2 μm), and a smaller amount of clay (particle size < 2 μm).

090fb7e7235f.title: Loam
090fb7e7235f.sentence: By weight, its mineral composition is about 40–40–20% concentration of sand, silt and clay, respectively.

4b44ec671d36.title: Loam
4b44ec671d36.sentence: These proportions can vary to a degree, however, and result in different types of loam soils: sandy loam, silty loam, clay loam, sandy clay loam, silty clay loam, and loam.

02b682a18779.title: Loam
02b682a18779.sentence: In the United States Department of Agriculture, textural classification triangle, the only soil that is not predominantly sand, silt, or clay is called "loam".

165babd49492.title: Loam
165babd49492.sentence: The different types of loam soils each have slightly different characteristics, with some draining liquids more efficiently than others.

4b107a435af9.title: Loam
4b107a435af9.sentence: Loam soils generally contain more nutrients, moisture, and humus than sandy soils, have better drainage and infiltration of water and air than silt- and clay-rich soils, and are easier to till than clay soils.

4f3d7b2356a4.title: Loam
4f3d7b2356a4.sentence: Loam is considered ideal for gardening and agricultural uses because it retains nutrients well and retains water while still allowing excess water to drain away.

64b8b6d8163b.title: Loam
64b8b6d8163b.sentence: Loam soil is suitable for growing most plant varieties.

2f5d362512b9.title: Loam
2f5d362512b9.sentence: A soil dominated by one or two of the three particle size groups can behave like loam if it has a strong granular structure, promoted by a high content of organic matter.

ef1825b40653.title: Loam
ef1825b40653.sentence: However, a soil that meets the textural (geological) definition of loam can lose its characteristic desirable qualities when it is compacted, depleted of organic matter, or has clay dispersed throughout its fine-earth fraction.

a904b22ae005.title: Loam
a904b22ae005.sentence: In fact, the primary definition of loam in most dictionaries is soils containing humus (organic content) with no mention of particle size or texture, and this definition is used by many gardeners.

5a45274d6e97.title: Soil texture
5a45274d6e97.sentence: Determining soil texture is often aided with the use of a soil texture triangle plot.

9301325badf8.title: Soil texture
9301325badf8.sentence: One side of the triangle represents percent sand, the second side represents percent clay, and the third side represents percent silt.

11febe875c66.title: Soil texture
11febe875c66.sentence: If the percentages of sand, clay, and silt in the soil sample are known, then the triangle can be used to classify the soil texture.

1ce34f5498eb.title: Soil texture
1ce34f5498eb.sentence: The same method can be used starting on any side of the soil triangle.

7ae1a7340727.title: Soil texture
7ae1a7340727.sentence: For example, if a soil is 70 percent sand and 10 percent clay then the soil is classified as a sandy loam.

d903008da6d2.title: Physical properties of soil
d903008da6d2.sentence: In the illustrated USDA textural classification triangle, the only soil in which neither sand, silt nor clay predominates is called loam.

81f1aebc0285.title: Soil texture
81f1aebc0285.sentence: If the texture by feel method was used to determine the soil type, the triangle can also provide a rough estimate on the percentages of sand, silt, and clay in the soil.

77bf55f93da7.title: Ternary plot
77bf55f93da7.sentence: A ternary plot, ternary graph, triangle plot, simplex plot, or Gibbs triangle is a barycentric plot on three variables which sum to a constant.

6a9f7bb2b332.title: Ternary plot
6a9f7bb2b332.sentence: In a ternary plot, the values of the three variables a, b, and c must sum to some constant, K. Usually, this constant is represented as 1.0 or 100%.

7690ae99b07c.title: Ternary plot
7690ae99b07c.sentence: Because a + b + c = K for all substances being graphed, any one variable is not independent of the others, so only two variables must be known to find a sample's point on the graph: for instance, c must be equal to K − a − b.

c6a2d65cdda8.title: Ternary plot
c6a2d65cdda8.sentence: Because the three numerical values cannot vary independently—there are only two degrees of freedom—it is possible to graph the combinations of all three variables in only two dimensions.

8a3af19335f1.title: Ternary plot
8a3af19335f1.section: Reading values on a ternary plot
8a3af19335f1.sentence: Each component is 100% in a corner of the triangle and 0% at the edge opposite it, decreasing linearly with increasing distance (perpendicular to the opposite edge) from this corner.

b95b55ecc426.title: Ternary plot
b95b55ecc426.section: Reading values on a ternary plot
b95b55ecc426.sentence: The first method is to use a diagram grid consisting of lines parallel to the triangle edges.

59f874a6392d.title: Ternary plot
59f874a6392d.sentence: Sample Clay Silt Sand Notes Sample 1 50% 20% 30% Because clay and silt together make up 70% of this sample, the proportion of sand must be 30% for the components to sum to 100%.

4f8502959cd1.title: Soil texture
4f8502959cd1.sentence: Hand analysis is a simple and effective means to rapidly assess and classify a soil's physical condition.

423cd3203ddb.title: Soil texture
423cd3203ddb.sentence: The texture by feel method involves taking a small sample of soil and making a ribbon.

b4712cf4ef1d.title: Soil texture
b4712cf4ef1d.sentence: A ribbon can be made by taking a ball of soil and pushing the soil between the thumb and forefinger and squeezing it upward into a ribbon.

75ad7cb24fa3.title: Soil texture
75ad7cb24fa3.sentence: Allow the ribbon to emerge and extend over the forefinger, breaking from its own weight.

73c2a53f2ed4.title: Soil texture
73c2a53f2ed4.sentence: Measuring the unbroken length of the ribbon can help determine the amount of clay in the sample.

1c1d0c1ac03b.title: Soil texture
1c1d0c1ac03b.sentence: After making a ribbon, excessively wet a small pinch of soil in the palm of the hand and rub in with the forefinger to determine the amount of sand in the sample.

0be3ac41fb6e.title: Soil texture
0be3ac41fb6e.sentence: Soils that have a high percentage of sand, such as sandy loam or sandy clay, have a gritty texture.

e043c409caef.title: Soil texture
e043c409caef.sentence: Soils that have a high percentage of silt, such as silty loam or silty clay, feel smooth.

0ef02d431ecf.title: Soil texture
0ef02d431ecf.sentence: Soils that have a high percentage of clay, such as clay loam, have a sticky feel.

aebbd0d60a05.title: Soil texture
aebbd0d60a05.sentence: Texture by feel is a qualitative method, as it does not provide exact values of sand, silt, and clay.

a4d480e1c71c.title: Soil texture
a4d480e1c71c.sentence: Although qualitative, the texture by feel flowchart can be an accurate way for a scientist or interested (and trained) individual to analyze the relative proportions of sand, silt, and clay.

35424b9bca1c.title: Soil texture
35424b9bca1c.sentence: Correctly executed, the procedure allows for rapid and frequent assessment of soil characteristics with little or no equipment.

3328954ff9e7.title: Soil texture
3328954ff9e7.sentence: It is thus a useful tool for identifying spatial variation both within and between fields as well as identifying progressive changes and boundaries between soil map units (soil series).

bdb2f26d6f00.title: Soil texture
bdb2f26d6f00.sentence: Although the texture by feel method takes practice, it is a useful way to determine soil texture, especially in the field.

3d77bdc38490.title: Soil texture
3d77bdc38490.sentence: The international soil classification system World Reference Base for Soil Resources (WRB) uses an alternative method to determine texture by feel, offering another flow chart.

c211cd7085fd.title: Shrink–swell capacity
c211cd7085fd.sentence: The shrink–swell capacity of soils refers to the extent certain clay minerals will expand when wet and retract when dry.

d3c57355363b.title: Shrink–swell capacity
d3c57355363b.sentence: The presence of these clay minerals is what allows soils to have the capacity to shrink and swell.

c8751d6b06bf.title: Shrink–swell capacity
c8751d6b06bf.sentence: Some of these clay minerals are: smectite, nontronite, bentonite, chlorite, montmorillonite, beidellite, attapulgite, illite and vermiculite.

b91b5b36f7b2.title: Shrink–swell capacity
b91b5b36f7b2.sentence: The amount of certain clay minerals that are present, such as montmorillonite and smectite, directly affects the shrink-swell capacity of soil.

4d3294b19b8d.title: Shrink–swell capacity
4d3294b19b8d.sentence: The amount of these minerals in a particular soil will also determine the severity of the shrink-swell capacity.

7b14da966795.title: Shrink–swell capacity
7b14da966795.sentence: If a soil is composed of at least 5 percent of these clay minerals by weight, it could have the ability to shrink and swell.

ba2b6afcbf63.title: Shrink–swell capacity
ba2b6afcbf63.sentence: This property is measured using coefficient of linear extensibility (COLE) values.

de90c041973f.title: Shrink–swell capacity
de90c041973f.sentence: If a soil has a COLE value greater than 0.06, then it can cause structural damage.

997f8f6521e5.title: Shrink–swell capacity
997f8f6521e5.sentence: A COLE value of 0.06 means that 100 inches of soil will expand by 6 inches when wet.

38af96df1625.title: Physical properties of soil
38af96df1625.sentence: Shrink/Swell Potential | Very Low | Low | Moderate to very high

1417d192e7b9.title: Shrink–swell capacity
1417d192e7b9.sentence: Soils with this shrink-swell capacity fall under the soil order of Vertisols.

68a174a0c95d.title: Shrink–swell capacity
68a174a0c95d.sentence: As these soils dry, deep cracks can form on the surface, which then allows water to penetrate to deeper levels of the soil.

e27fd6a723c4.title: Shrink–swell capacity
e27fd6a723c4.sentence: This can cause the swelling of these soils to become cyclical, with periods of both shrinking and swelling.

ec3ca0ac722e.title: Shrink–swell capacity
ec3ca0ac722e.sentence: Clay groups with a high shrink–swell capacity tend to damage crops during dry spells, as the soil contracts, by pulling roots apart.

73df7e582fd8.title: Soil compaction
73df7e582fd8.sentence: Soils with high shrink–swell capacity, such as vertisols, recover quickly from compaction where moisture conditions are variable (dry spells shrink the soil, causing it to crack).

29977b8a752d.title: Shrink–swell capacity
29977b8a752d.sentence: The swelling can cause structures to heave or lift, and the shrinking can uneven settling of sediment underneath foundations, potentially causing the structure to fail.

19ab60b07cb5.title: Shrink–swell capacity
19ab60b07cb5.sentence: Annually, there is an estimated $7 billion in damage caused by clay shrink-swell soils.

cf61950b0c9a.title: Shrink–swell capacity
cf61950b0c9a.sentence: Expansive soils are the most problematic in regions with very defined wet and dry periods, as opposed to areas that maintain a certain level of moisture throughout the year, as this annual cycle causes the soils to expand and swell every year.

bf3fb26b3c71.title: Shrink–swell capacity
bf3fb26b3c71.sentence: Damage is quite often caused by differential swelling which is caused by pockets of wet soil situated right next to dry soil.

e1305eee7ca2.title: Gravel
e1305eee7ca2.sentence: Gravel (/ˈɡrævəl/) is a loose aggregation of rock fragments.

0b9ae26d47b3.title: Gravel
0b9ae26d47b3.sentence: The technical definition of gravel varies by region and by area of application.

fb8af1ecaf84.title: Gravel
fb8af1ecaf84.sentence: Many geologists define gravel simply as loose rounded rock particles over 2 mm (0.079 in) in diameter, without specifying an upper size limit.

74f6b27ec443.title: Gravel
74f6b27ec443.sentence: The U.S. Department of Agriculture and the Soil Science Society of America define gravel as particles from 2 to 80 mm (0.079 to 3.150 in) in size, while the German scale (Atterburg) defines gravel as particles from 2 to 200 mm (0.079 to 7.874 in) in size.

fb46d44e6071.title: Gravel
fb46d44e6071.sentence: The Udden-Wentworth scale, widely used by geologists in the US, defines granular gravel as particles with a size from 2 to 4 mm (0.079 to 0.157 in) and pebble gravel as particles with a size from 4 to 64 mm (0.16 to 2.52 in).

9106d0373918.title: Physical properties of soil
9106d0373918.sentence: Soil components larger than 2.0 mm (0.079 in) are classed as rock and gravel and are removed before determining the percentages of the remaining components and the textural class of the soil, but are included in the name.

15fc02ea509d.title: Physical properties of soil
15fc02ea509d.sentence: For example, a sandy loam soil with 20% gravel would be called gravelly sandy loam.

06a9d175cb3a.title: Gravel
06a9d175cb3a.sentence: Most gravel is derived from disintegration of bedrock as it weathers.

c5c7c11ef876.title: Gravel
c5c7c11ef876.sentence: Quartz is the most common mineral found in gravel, as it is hard, chemically inert, and lacks cleavage planes along which the rock easily splits.

2793c2a797b4.title: Gravel
2793c2a797b4.sentence: The rock fragments are rapidly rounded as they are transported by rivers, often within a few tens of kilometers of their source outcrops.

007d1f42df6b.title: Gravel
007d1f42df6b.sentence: Natural gravel has a high hydraulic conductivity, sometimes reaching above 1 cm/s.

048648e9695f.title: Gravel
048648e9695f.sentence: Much of the rest is used for road construction, either in the road base or as the road surface (with or without asphalt or other binders.) Naturally occurring porous gravel deposits have a high hydraulic conductivity, making them important aquifers.

c7b53a0b041b.title: Gravel
c7b53a0b041b.sentence: In locales where gravelly soil is predominant, plant life is generally more sparse.

a489802073e8.title: Gravel
a489802073e8.sentence: This is due to the inferior ability of gravels to retain moisture, as well as the corresponding paucity of mineral nutrients, since finer soils that contain such minerals are present in smaller amounts.

ce39837531dc.title: Physical properties of soil
ce39837531dc.sentence: The physical properties of soil, in order of decreasing importance for ecosystem services such as crop production, are texture, structure, bulk density, porosity, consistency, temperature, colour and resistivity.

e6353405cfcb.title: Physical properties of soil
e6353405cfcb.sentence: These properties vary through the depth of a soil profile, i.e. through soil horizons.

fec10dc95633.title: Physical properties of soil
fec10dc95633.sentence: Most of these properties determine the aeration of the soil and the ability of water to infiltrate and to be held within the soil.

555670070b28.title: Physical properties of soil
555670070b28.sentence: At the next larger scale, soil structures called peds or more commonly soil aggregates are created from the soil separates when iron oxides, carbonates, clay, silica and humus, coat particles and cause them to adhere into larger, relatively stable secondary structures.

96232f789d05.title: Physical properties of soil
96232f789d05.sentence: Soil bulk density, when determined at standardized moisture conditions, is an estimate of soil compaction.

cc2a00adab0b.title: Physical properties of soil
cc2a00adab0b.sentence: Soil porosity consists of the void part of the soil volume and is occupied by gases or water.

5b19e8dfe019.title: Physical properties of soil
5b19e8dfe019.sentence: Ability to store plant nutrients | Poor | Medium to High | High

347e3d157943.title: Physical properties of soil
347e3d157943.sentence: Resistance to pH change | Low | Medium | High

fe5d424927c5.title: Physical properties of soil
fe5d424927c5.sentence: Pollutant leaching potential | High | Medium | Low (unless cracked)

63f403be653d.title: Physical properties of soil
63f403be653d.sentence: Warm-up in spring | Rapid | Moderate | Slow

fe0fd304a81c.title: Physical properties of soil
fe0fd304a81c.sentence: Susceptibility to wind erosion | Moderate (High if fine sand) | High | Low

f4544f1c37f2.title: Physical properties of soil
f4544f1c37f2.sentence: Susceptibility to water erosion | Low (unless fine sand) | High | Low if aggregated, otherwise high

85a94d8b08d0.title: Soil structure
85a94d8b08d0.sentence: Soil structure describes the arrangement of the solid parts of the soil and of the pore spaces located between them.

99509125296f.title: Soil structure
99509125296f.sentence: In geotechnical engineering, soil structure describes the arrangement of the solid parts of the soil and of the pore space located between them.

f0109415efe2.title: Soil structure
f0109415efe2.sentence: It is determined by how individual soil granules clump, bind together, and aggregate, resulting in the arrangement of soil pores between them.

d5e9bf60c7be.title: Soil structure
d5e9bf60c7be.sentence: Soil has a major influence on water and air movement, biological activity, root growth and seedling emergence.

7522a3d2993c.title: Physical properties of soil
7522a3d2993c.sentence: Soil structure affects aeration, water movement, conduction of heat, plant root growth and resistance to erosion.

2db6d262c26d.title: Soil structure
2db6d262c26d.sentence: Soil structure is inherently a dynamic and complex system that is affected by different factors such as tillage, wheel traffic, root, microbial and faunal activities in soil, rainfall events, wind erosion, wetting and drying, freezing and thawing.

dd8893c5640a.title: Soil structure
dd8893c5640a.sentence: It is inherently a dynamic and complex system that is affected by different biotic and abiotic factors.

092cb982cb79.title: Soil structure
092cb982cb79.sentence: The quality of soil structure will decline under most forms of cultivation; the associated mechanical mixing of the soil compacts and shears aggregates and fills pore spaces; it also exposes organic matter to a greater rate of decay and oxidation.

db83bf80283c.title: Soil structure
db83bf80283c.sentence: A further consequence of continued cultivation and traffic is the development of compacted, impermeable layers or hardpans within the soil profile.

da71ef9946d4.title: Soil structure
da71ef9946d4.sentence: The decline of soil structure under irrigation is usually related to the breakdown of aggregates and dispersion of clay material as a result of rapid wetting.

066bc7859183.title: Soil structure
066bc7859183.sentence: This is particularly so if soils are sodic; that is, having a high exchangeable sodium percentage (ESP) of the cations attached to the clays.

22f6957cbb58.title: Soil structure
22f6957cbb58.sentence: High sodium levels (compared to high calcium levels) cause particles to repel one another when wet, and the associated aggregates to disaggregate and disperse.

c2181c22041f.title: Physical properties of soil
c2181c22041f.sentence: Soil structure often gives clues to its texture, organic matter content, biological activity, past soil evolution, human use, and the chemical and mineralogical conditions under which the soil formed.

1d2e3db29464.title: Ped
1d2e3db29464.sentence: In soil science, peds are aggregates of soil particles formed naturally as a result of pedogenic processes; this natural organization of particles forms discrete units separated by pores or voids.

054bc488acb6.title: Ped
054bc488acb6.sentence: The term is generally used for macroscopic (visible; i.e. greater than 1 mm in size) structural units when soils are observed in the field.

f9f4e5e59ef3.title: Ped
f9f4e5e59ef3.sentence: An artificially formed aggregate of soil particles can be called a clod.

70bf5c5c9e70.title: Physical properties of soil
70bf5c5c9e70.sentence: A soil clod, however, is not a ped but rather a mass of soil that results from mechanical disturbance of the soil such as cultivation.

23c7230b9001.title: Aggregate (geology)
23c7230b9001.sentence: If it has formed naturally, it can be called a ped; if formed artificially, it can be called a clod.

ebf9810d45d8.title: Physical properties of soil
ebf9810d45d8.sentence: The clumping of the soil textural components of sand, silt and clay causes aggregates to form and the further association of those aggregates into larger units creates soil structures called peds (a contraction of the word pedolith).

f2f99748e139.title: Soil
f2f99748e139.sentence: At the next larger scale, soil structures called peds or more commonly soil aggregates are created from the soil separates when iron oxides, carbonates, clay, silica and humus, coat particles and cause them to adhere into larger, relatively stable secondary structures.

560eaaa68b26.title: Ped
560eaaa68b26.sentence: Soil peds should be described when the soil is dry or slightly moist, as they can be difficult to distinguish when wet.

946832c08125.title: Ped
946832c08125.sentence: Some soils have simple structure, each unit being an entity without component smaller units.

75dbb2201933.title: Ped
75dbb2201933.sentence: Others have compound structure, in which large units are composed of smaller units separated by persistent planes of weakness.

9fbfac05718f.title: Macropore
9fbfac05718f.sentence: In soil, macropores are created by plant roots, soil cracks, soil fauna, and by aggregation of soil particles into peds.

622b64b9d9d9.title: Physical properties of soil
622b64b9d9d9.sentence: - Types: Shape and arrangement of peds

c4069e298a4f.title: Ped
c4069e298a4f.sentence: There are five major classes of macrostructure seen in soils: platy, prismatic, columnar, granular, and blocky.

9aff444487c2.title: Soil structure
9aff444487c2.sentence: In platy structure, the units are flat and platelike.

9e1d535038be.title: Soil structure
9e1d535038be.sentence: Platy structure is usually found in subsurface soils that have been subject to compaction by animal trampling or machinery traffic, but platy structures may also result from wetting-drying and freeze-thaw cycles where they are of the lenticular type.

3743e13e4208.title: Soil structure
3743e13e4208.sentence: Platy structure tends to impede the downward movement of water and plant roots through the soil.

3fe96e5bca5e.title: Soil structure
3fe96e5bca5e.sentence: In the prismatic structure, the individual units are bounded by flat to rounded vertical faces.

577d7424b13f.title: Soil structure
577d7424b13f.sentence: Units are distinctly longer vertically, and the faces are typically casts or molds of adjoining units.

a500ae68d0cf.title: Soil structure
a500ae68d0cf.sentence: Vertices are angular or subrounded; the tops of the prisms are somewhat indistinct and normally flat.

146b25520c0f.title: Soil structure
146b25520c0f.sentence: Prismatic structures are characteristic of clay- illuviated B horizons or subsoils.

f84d10feaa37.title: Soil structure
f84d10feaa37.sentence: The vertical cracks result from freeze-thaw and wetting-drying cycles.

d8b289727294.title: Soil structure
d8b289727294.sentence: In the columnar structure, the units are similar to prisms and are bounded by flat or slightly rounded vertical faces.

19471e6e451a.title: Soil structure
19471e6e451a.sentence: The tops of columns, in contrast to those of prisms, are very distinct and normally rounded.

9517d4645fe1.title: Soil structure
9517d4645fe1.sentence: Columnar structure is common in the subsoil of sodium affected soils and soils rich in swelling clays such as the smectites and the kandite Halloysite.

97fe8fe3e34c.title: Soil structure
97fe8fe3e34c.sentence: Columnar structure is very dense and it is very difficult for plant roots to penetrate these layers.

1d60b530d85d.title: Soil structure
1d60b530d85d.sentence: In blocky structure, the structural units are blocklike or polyhedral.

235aa2ed3543.title: Soil structure
235aa2ed3543.sentence: Typically, blocky structural units are nearly equidimensional but grade to prisms and to plates.

1552ab334b0b.title: Soil structure
1552ab334b0b.sentence: The structure is described as angular blocky if the faces intersect at relatively sharp angles; as subangular blocky if the faces are a mixture of rounded and plane faces and the corners are mostly rounded.

9a67aff4b63d.title: Soil structure
9a67aff4b63d.sentence: Blocky structures are common in subsoil but also occur in surface soils that have a high clay content.

8f52bb7b681a.title: Soil structure
8f52bb7b681a.sentence: In the granular structure, also called crumby or crumb structure, the structural units are approximately spherical or polyhedral and are bounded by curved or very irregular faces that are not casts of adjoining peds.

da49ce24255f.title: Soil structure
da49ce24255f.sentence: Granular structure is common in the surface soils of rich grasslands and highly amended garden soils with high organic matter content.

3969d42f159a.title: Soil structure
3969d42f159a.sentence: This structure allows for good porosity and easy movement of air and water.

22e19a9f3c79.title: Soil structure
22e19a9f3c79.sentence: - Wedge – The units are approximately elliptical with interlocking lenses that terminate in acute angles.

ccf804f1b2b8.title: Soil structure
ccf804f1b2b8.sentence: They are commonly bounded by small slickensides.

a22b8ce9927d.title: Soil structure
a22b8ce9927d.sentence: - Lenticular —The units are overlapping lenses parallel to the soil surface.

aad530d73780.title: Soil structure
aad530d73780.sentence: Lenticular structure is commonly associated with moist soils, texture classes high in silt or very fine sand (e.g., silt loam), and high potential for frost action.

cb000d666af2.title: Physical properties of soil
cb000d666af2.sentence: - Classes: Size of peds whose ranges depend upon the above type

42d094f8dc7c.title: Physical properties of soil
42d094f8dc7c.sentence: - Very coarse or very thick: >10 mm platy, granular; >50 mm blocky; >100 mm prismlike.

038993b5444c.title: Particle-size distribution
038993b5444c.sentence: In granulometry, the particle-size distribution (PSD) of a powder, or granular material, or particles dispersed in fluid, is a list of values or a mathematical function that defines the relative amount, typically by mass, of particles present according to size.

e2f430eed7e7.title: Soil
e2f430eed7e7.sentence: The particle size distribution of a soil, its texture, determines many of the properties of that soil, in particular hydraulic conductivity and water potential, but the mineralogy of those particles can strongly modify those properties.

c76ff96416e5.title: Particle-size distribution
c76ff96416e5.sentence: It affects the strength and load-bearing properties of rocks and soils.

e1289fd11456.title: Particle-size distribution
e1289fd11456.sentence: Significant energy is usually required to disintegrate soil, etc. particles into the PSD that is then called a grain size distribution.

0f27eb044964.title: Particle-size distribution
0f27eb044964.sentence: PSD is usually defined by the method by which it is determined.

833fd0809a1e.title: Particle-size distribution
833fd0809a1e.sentence: The most easily understood method of determination is sieve analysis, where powder is separated on sieves of different sizes.

558f20ac2fc7.title: Particle-size distribution
558f20ac2fc7.sentence: Thus, the PSD is defined in terms of discrete size ranges: e.g. "% of sample between 45 μm and 53 μm", when sieves of these sizes are used.

e01d0938c839.title: Particle-size distribution
e01d0938c839.sentence: The PSD may be expressed as a "range" analysis, in which the amount in each size range is listed in order.

69f15d871d2e.title: Particle-size distribution
69f15d871d2e.sentence: It may also be presented in "cumulative" form, in which the total of all sizes "retained" or "passed" by a single notional "sieve" is given for a range of sizes.

256a3d758cbe.title: Particle-size distribution
256a3d758cbe.sentence: In practice, particles are irregular – often extremely so, for example in the case of fibrous materials – and the way in which such particles are characterized during analysis is very dependent on the method of measurement used.

afe3966ed01f.title: Particle-size distribution
afe3966ed01f.sentence: The way in which "size" is expressed is open to a wide range of interpretations.

00954ce58291.title: Particle-size distribution
00954ce58291.sentence: These are based upon study of the terminal velocity acquired by particles suspended in a viscous liquid.

817c1c951263.title: Particle-size distribution
817c1c951263.sentence: Advantages: this technique determines particle size as a function of settling velocity.

6f6ab8728865.title: Particle-size distribution
6f6ab8728865.sentence: Sedimentation time is longest for the finest particles, so this technique is useful for sizes below 10 μm, but sub-micrometer particles cannot be reliably measured due to the effects of Brownian motion.

ee74e24b97d4.title: Particle-size distribution
ee74e24b97d4.sentence: These depend upon analysis of the "halo" of diffracted light produced when a laser beam passes through a dispersion of particles in air or in a liquid.

49b48cb78c2b.title: Particle-size distribution
49b48cb78c2b.sentence: The angle of diffraction increases as particle size decreases, so that this method is particularly good for measuring sizes between 0.1 and 3,000 μm.

fb45c3013b0f.title: Particle-size distribution
fb45c3013b0f.sentence: Advances in sophisticated data processing and automation have allowed this to become the dominant method used in industrial PSD determination.

ab72612949b9.title: Sieve analysis
ab72612949b9.sentence: A sieve analysis (or gradation test) is a practice or procedure used in geology, civil engineering, and chemical engineering to assess the particle size distribution (also called gradation) of a granular material by allowing the material to pass through a series of sieves of progressively smaller mesh size and weighing the amount of material that is stopped by each sieve as a fraction of the whole mass.

660276d386b3.title: Sieve analysis
660276d386b3.sentence: A sieve analysis can be performed on any type of non-organic or organic granular materials including sand, crushed rock, clay, granite, feldspar, coal, soil, a wide range of manufactured powder, grain and seeds, down to a minimum size depending on the exact method.

aa9da30877cd.title: Sieve analysis
aa9da30877cd.sentence: Being such a simple technique of particle sizing, it is probably the most common.

a0586e8baeb2.title: Sieve analysis
a0586e8baeb2.sentence: A representative weighed sample is poured into the top sieve which has the largest screen openings.

cb5210c5e6b5.title: Sieve analysis
cb5210c5e6b5.sentence: Each lower sieve in the column has smaller openings than the one above.

9443a644a70b.title: Sieve analysis
9443a644a70b.sentence: At the base is a pan, called the receiver.

baac239a6918.title: Sieve analysis
baac239a6918.sentence: The column is typically placed in a mechanical shaker, which shakes the column, usually for a set period, to facilitate exposing all of the material to the screen openings so that particles small enough to fit through the holes can fall through to the next layer.

3f6bdfe62ce7.title: Sieve analysis
3f6bdfe62ce7.sentence: After the shaking is complete the material on each sieve is weighed.

6572d4b98d2a.title: Sieve analysis
6572d4b98d2a.sentence: The mass of the sample of each sieve is then divided by the total mass to give a percentage retained on each sieve.

135eba2335c8.title: Sieve analysis
135eba2335c8.sentence: For coarse material, sizes that range down to #100 mesh (150 μm), a sieve analysis and particle size distribution is accurate and consistent.

28dad1bf5b47.title: Sieve analysis
28dad1bf5b47.sentence: However, for material that is finer than 100 mesh, dry sieving can be significantly less accurate.

943d9d8ab382.title: Sieve analysis
943d9d8ab382.sentence: This is because the mechanical energy required to make particles pass through an opening and the surface attraction effects between the particles themselves and between particles and the screen increase as the particle size decreases.

29bb6c3324ae.title: Sieve analysis
29bb6c3324ae.sentence: This is the case when the sample which has to be analysed is e.g. a suspension which must not be dried; or when the sample is a very fine powder which tends to agglomerate (mostly < 45 μm) – in a dry sieving process this tendency would lead to a clogging of the sieve meshes and this would make a further sieving process impossible.

1de4017bd1c2.title: Sieve analysis
1de4017bd1c2.sentence: Above the top sieve a water-spray nozzle is placed which supports the sieving process additionally to the sieving motion.

833a13b60168.title: Sieve analysis
833a13b60168.sentence: The rinsing is carried out until the liquid which is discharged through the receiver is clear.

62d86db6f02f.title: Sieve analysis
62d86db6f02f.sentence: Sieve analysis assumes that all particle will be round (spherical) or nearly so and will pass through the square openings when the particle diameter is less than the size of the square opening in the screen.

bea7c5d24477.title: Sieve analysis
bea7c5d24477.sentence: For elongated and flat particles a sieve analysis will not yield reliable mass-based results, as the particle size reported will assume that the particles are spherical, where in fact an elongated particle might pass through the screen end-on, but would be prevented from doing so if it presented itself side-on.

150965ff2165.title: Soil texture
150965ff2165.sentence: In order to measure silt and clay (with a particle size below 60 μm), a second, independent sizing method (most often hydrometer or pipette technique) is used on the sample taken from the bottom sieve.

4cfa82487d87.title: Sieve analysis
4cfa82487d87.sentence: Sieve analysis determines the particle size distribution of a given soil sample and hence helps in easy identification of a soil's mechanical properties.

0623d64199c8.title: Sieve analysis
0623d64199c8.sentence: These mechanical properties determine whether a given soil can support the proposed engineering structure.

1e9cc9e3a36b.title: Soil texture
1e9cc9e3a36b.sentence: The hydrometer method of determining soil texture is a quantitative measurement providing estimates of the percent sand, clay, and silt in the soil based on Stokes' law, which expresses the relationship between the settling velocity and particle size.

ab6e74d6514d.title: Soil texture
ab6e74d6514d.sentence: The soil particles separate based on size and sink to the bottom.

21f0bb798569.title: Hydrometer
21f0bb798569.sentence: The basis for this test is Stokes' Law for falling spheres in a viscous fluid in which the terminal velocity of fall depends on the grain diameter and the densities of the grain in suspension and of the fluid.

5339a2b5f4b0.title: Hydrometer
5339a2b5f4b0.sentence: The grain diameter thus can be calculated from a knowledge of the distance and time of fall.

ed6cbec816a0.title: Soil texture
ed6cbec816a0.sentence: The hydrometer method requires the use of sodium hexametaphosphate, which acts as a dispersing agent to separate soil aggregates.

94d1cf8610dd.title: Soil texture
94d1cf8610dd.sentence: The soil is mixed with the sodium hexametaphosphate solution on an orbital shaker overnight.

46eb74b25d21.title: Soil texture
46eb74b25d21.sentence: The solution is transferred to one liter graduated cylinders and filled with water.

19b844cecff5.title: Soil texture
19b844cecff5.sentence: Sand particles (> 50 microns) sink to the bottom of the cylinder first.

5862d1130df7.title: Soil texture
5862d1130df7.sentence: Silt particles sink to the bottom of the cylinder after the sand.

86f0b8b73a18.title: Soil texture
86f0b8b73a18.sentence: Clay particles (2 microns or finer) separate out above the silt layer.

fbf5a60b9a15.title: Soil texture
fbf5a60b9a15.sentence: Measurements are taken using a hydrometer, (type ASTM 152H) which measures grams of dissolved and suspended material per liter of suspension.

c831f070b717.title: Soil texture
c831f070b717.sentence: The hydrometer is lowered into the cylinder containing the soil mixture and a reading made at two different times following mixing; after forty seconds to measure grams per liter of suspended silt and clay (hence giving sand content), and 6-8 hours (depending on settling cylinder dimensions and concentration of the dispersing agent used) to measure grams / L of clay still remaining above the effective settling depth.

8bcc1055c942.title: Soil texture
8bcc1055c942.sentence: A blank reading (made in a solution of dispersing agent kept at the same temperature as the soil suspension) is subtracted from each suspension reading, thus avoiding any need for temperature correction.[31] The calculations are as follows:

7c11675e127f.title: Soil texture
7c11675e127f.sentence: The hydrometer method, introduced in 1927, is still widely used today.

ea710f8c0798.title: Soil texture
ea710f8c0798.sentence: However, problems with the empirical 1927 protocol have been identified[30],[31] and the original procedure and type of settling cylinder should not be used.

bdeb87ca8904.title: Soil texture
bdeb87ca8904.sentence: The stable position during settling of particles with such shapes is with the maximum cross-sectional area being perpendicular to the direction of motion.

df30c6abff5a.title: Soil texture
df30c6abff5a.sentence: For this reason, the drag resistance of particles increases and the settling velocity decreases.

6b2cb706fc37.title: Soil texture
6b2cb706fc37.sentence: Therefore, with lower velocity, the calculated diameter also decreases determining an overestimation of the fine size fraction.

238d202ac797.title: Soil texture
238d202ac797.sentence: Sedimentation analysis shows limits for particles smaller than 0.2 micron because such small particles undergo Brownian motion in the suspension and do not settle according to Stokes' law.

f93978f60520.title: Soil texture
f93978f60520.sentence: The particle size distribution of soil containing a significant number of finer particles (silt and clay) cannot be performed by sieve analysis solely, therefore sedimentation analysis is used to determine the lower range of the particle size distribution.

27277c4df51c.title: Soil texture
27277c4df51c.sentence: Sedimentation analysis (e.g. pipette method, hydrometer) is commonly used in soil engineering or in geology to classify sediments.

27641c07dd2a.title: Hydrometer
27641c07dd2a.sentence: Hydrometer analysis is performed if the grain sizes are too small for sieve analysis.

8f454930ef22.title: Hydrometer
8f454930ef22.sentence: A hydrometer analysis is the process by which fine-grained soils, silts and clays, are graded.

d1dabfb78fa2.title: Expansive clay
d1dabfb78fa2.sentence: Expansive clay, also called expansive soil, is a clay soil prone to large volume changes (swelling and shrinking) directly related to changes in water content.

784cda02a2d4.title: Expansive clay
784cda02a2d4.sentence: All clays consist of mineral sheets packaged into layers, and can be classified as either 1:1 or 2:1.

10f73f6e3402.title: Expansive clay
10f73f6e3402.sentence: These ratios refer to the proportion of tetrahedral sheets to octahedral sheets.

296a8d21bb8e.title: Expansive clay
296a8d21bb8e.sentence: Expansive clays have an expanding crystal lattice in a 2:1 ratio; however, there are 2:1 non-expansive clays.

7a7b77290630.title: Expansive clay
7a7b77290630.sentence: Atterberg limits measure the plasticity index (PI) and liquid limit (LL) to determine soil behavior, where PI over 35 indicates high expansion potential, and LL over 50 suggests significant swelling characteristics.

649c5cd2d066.title: Expansive clay
649c5cd2d066.sentence: A free swell test measures the free swell index (FSI) by comparing the volume of dry soil in water to its volume in kerosene.

5f3184db4542.title: Expansive clay
5f3184db4542.sentence: A mineralogical analysis is an X-ray diffraction (XRD) test that can identify specific clay minerals, such as montmorillonite, which would indicate shrink-swell qualities of the soil.

d9bc1114c8ac.title: Expansive clay
d9bc1114c8ac.sentence: Field assessment for expansive soil may also be conducted, including a visual inspection to identify surface characteristics such as gilgai topography (alternating mounds and depressions) and deep shrinkage cracks.

e126267821a5.title: Expansive clay
e126267821a5.sentence: Another field assessment is a simple hand test that involves rolling moistened soil into a thread.

a2d14cc919be.title: Expansive clay
a2d14cc919be.sentence: If the thread can be rolled to a diameter of 3 mm without crumbling, the soil likely contains a measurable amount of clay content, indicating some expansiveness.

4abb2abdffa8.title: Expansive clay
4abb2abdffa8.sentence: These include designs that call for digging deep foundations or installing pile systems extending beyond affected soil depths and reinforced slab-on-grade construction with underlying crossbeams.

c47aadf40075.title: Expansive clay
c47aadf40075.sentence: Void spaces beneath foundations, created with void forms, provide empty spaces for swelling soil to move into, insulating the foundation from the impact caused by this pressure.

5d956311f296.title: Expansive clay
5d956311f296.sentence: Common chemical expansive clay treatments include lime, portland cement, fly ash, and polymer-based additives.

aa578c8f27ca.title: Expansive clay
aa578c8f27ca.sentence: Moisture control manages the swelling potential of expansive soils through preventative measures designed to redirect environmental water sources and maintain a consistent moisture equilibrium beneath and around structures.

59e0b1b6471c.title: Soil texture
59e0b1b6471c.sentence: Atterberg chose 20 μm for the upper limit of silt fraction because particles smaller than that size were not visible to the naked eye, the suspension could be coagulated by salts, capillary rise within 24 hours was most rapid in this fraction, and the pores between compacted particles were so small as to prevent the entry of root hairs.

8dea75ca52ee.title: Soil texture
8dea75ca52ee.sentence: Commission One of the International Society of Soil Science (ISSS) recommended its use at the First International Congress of Soil Science held in Washington in 1927.

618081354144.title: Soil texture
618081354144.sentence: Australia adopted this system, and its equal logarithmic intervals are an attractive feature worth maintaining.

589b54d34497.title: Soil texture
589b54d34497.sentence: The United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) adopted its own system in 1938, and the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) used the USDA system in the FAO-UNESCO world soil map and recommended its use.

5056ddc8873f.title: Soil texture
5056ddc8873f.sentence: The X-ray sedimentation technique is a hybrid technique which combines sedimentation and X-ray absorption.

b4f26e65084e.title: Soil texture
b4f26e65084e.sentence: The particle size is calculated from the terminal settling velocities of particles by applying Stokes' law.

3bef7b484819.sentence: Some examples of these methods are the pipette method, the X-ray sedimentation, the particulate organic matter (POM) method, the rapid method.

96a5d4ab6be9.title: Soil gradation
96a5d4ab6be9.sentence: In soil science, soil gradation is a classification of a coarse-grained soil that ranks the soil based on the different particle sizes contained in the soil.

f77e0e329155.title: Soil gradation
f77e0e329155.sentence: Soil gradation is a classification of the particle size distribution of a soil.

5291091df35e.title: Soil gradation
5291091df35e.sentence: Coarse-grained soils, mainly gravels or sands, are graded as either well graded or poorly graded.

5c50677c4d23.title: Soil gradation
5c50677c4d23.sentence: A well-graded soil is a soil that contains particles of a wide range of sizes and has a good representation of all sizes from the No. 4 to No. 200 sieves.

57afb7d1e1bc.title: Soil gradation
57afb7d1e1bc.sentence: Poorly graded soils are further divided into uniformly-graded or gap-graded soils.

b2097d8b0a1e.title: Soil gradation
b2097d8b0a1e.sentence: Fine-grained soils, mainly silts and clays, are classified according to their Atterberg limits.

c41cd8710b87.title: Soil gradation
c41cd8710b87.sentence: Gradation of a soil is determined by reading the grain size distribution curve produced from the results of laboratory tests on the soil.

4b197a837c7e.title: Soil gradation
4b197a837c7e.sentence: Soil gradation is determined by analyzing the results of a sieve analysis or a hydrometer analysis.

a01dbfcfba1a.title: Soil gradation
a01dbfcfba1a.sentence: The process for grading a soil is in accordance with either the Unified Soil Classification System or the AASHTO Soil Classification System.

a3a05f3b5690.title: Soil gradation
a3a05f3b5690.sentence: Soil gradation is an important aspect of soil mechanics and geotechnical engineering because it is an indicator of other engineering properties such as compressibility, shear strength, and hydraulic conductivity.

28dc50cd845e.title: Soil gradation
28dc50cd845e.sentence: A poorly graded soil will have better drainage than a well graded soil because there are more void spaces in a poorly graded soil.

8993e073ecde.title: Soil gradation
8993e073ecde.sentence: Poorly-graded soils are more susceptible to soil liquefaction than well-graded soils.

08b74dea85f4.title: Soil gradation
08b74dea85f4.sentence: A well graded soil is able to be compacted more than a poorly graded soil.

b2038d0a5e35.title: Soil aggregate stability
b2038d0a5e35.sentence: The formation of soil aggregates (or so-called secondary soil particles or peds) occurs due to interactions of primary soil particles (i.e., clay) through rearrangement, flocculation and cementation.

13f7802a5f5a.title: Soil structure
13f7802a5f5a.sentence: Aggregation is the result of the interaction of soil particles through rearrangement, flocculation and cementation.

bf471f651d39.title: Soil aggregate stability
bf471f651d39.sentence: Microscopic floccules, will become aggregates once they are stabilized through cementation by one or several cementing agents such as carbonates, gypsum, sesquioxides, clay particles, and organic matter.

59c6884e3f9a.title: Soil structure
59c6884e3f9a.sentence: It is enhanced by: the precipitation of oxides, hydroxides, carbonates and silicates; the products of biological activity (such as biofilms, fungal hyphae and glycoproteins); ionic bridging between negatively charged particles (both clay minerals and organic compounds) by multivalent cations; and interactions between organic compounds (hydrogen bonding and hydrophobic bonding).

77203916044c.title: Soil aggregate stability
77203916044c.section: Factors Affecting Aggregate Formation > Cementation > Carbonates and Gypsum
77203916044c.sentence: The calcium ion (Ca2+), through its cationic bridging effect on flocculation of clay and organic matter compounds, has a crucial role in the formation and stability of soil aggregates.

d4555d7b00fb.title: Soil aggregate stability
d4555d7b00fb.section: Factors Affecting Aggregate Formation > Cementation > Carbonates and Gypsum
d4555d7b00fb.sentence: Calcium can exchange with sodium on exchange sites.

b8447bc33f58.title: Soil aggregate stability

b8447bc33f58.sentence: This, in turn, reduces soil particle dispersion, surface crusting, and aggregate slaking associated with sodic soils and indirectly increase aggregate stability.

30f41e19cfba.title: Soil aggregate stability

30f41e19cfba.sentence: Iron and aluminum hydrous oxides (or sesquioxides) can act as a cementing agents to form aggregates >100 μm, this effect becomes more pronounced in soil containing >10% sesquioxides.

c5c6881ff7bc.title: Soil aggregate stability
c5c6881ff7bc.section: Factors Affecting Aggregate Formation > Cementation > Clay Particles
