d5fd8dee5a30.title: Soil aggregate stability
d5fd8dee5a30.section: Factors Affecting Aggregate Formation > Cementation > Clay Particles
d5fd8dee5a30.sentence: Soil organic matter is therefore the main binding agent in these soils.

dac7dc0dd183.title: Soil aggregate stability
dac7dc0dd183.section: Factors Affecting Aggregate Formation > Cementation > Clay Particles
dac7dc0dd183.sentence: On the other hand, in soils with oxides and 1:1 type of phyllosiliacte clay minerals (e.g., kaolinite), soil organic matter is not the only binding agent and aggregate formation is also due to electrostatic charges between and among oxides and kaolinite particles.

a085ebb923e5.title: Soil aggregate stability
a085ebb923e5.section: Factors Affecting Aggregate Formation > Cementation > Clay Particles
a085ebb923e5.sentence: Therefore, in these soils, aggregation is less pronounced.

269ecc8ec090.title: Soil aggregate stability
269ecc8ec090.section: Factors Affecting Aggregate Formation > Physical Processes > Wetting and Drying
269ecc8ec090.sentence: Soil wetting and drying cycles can have both a beneficial effect on soil aggregation, and a negative effect on soil aggregation.

e71dcef1b8ac.title: Soil aggregate stability
e71dcef1b8ac.section: Factors Affecting Aggregate Formation > Physical Processes > Shrinking and Swelling
e71dcef1b8ac.sentence: Through repeated shrinking and swelling action, soil aggregation occurs because of the rearrangement of soil particles due to the stress of increasing soil-water suction (Kay, 1990).

435f24e3e708.title: Soil aggregate stability
435f24e3e708.section: Factors Affecting Aggregate Formation > Physical Processes > Freezing and Thawing
435f24e3e708.sentence: It was found that with higher water content in the soil at the time of freezing had a reducing effect on aggregate stability overall.

f832161fcd13.title: Soil aggregate stability
f832161fcd13.section: Factors Affecting Aggregate Formation > Physical Processes > Freezing and Thawing
f832161fcd13.sentence: The water expands in these soils and breaks apart the aggregates into smaller aggregates, while pores created by the freezing collapse once soils thaw.

b6c6de1da245.title: Soil aggregate stability
b6c6de1da245.section: Factors Affecting Aggregate Formation > Physical Processes > Shrinking and Swelling
b6c6de1da245.sentence: Some soils even have the ability to “self-mulch”, meaning a desirable granular structure is formed at the surface of the soil due to the shrinking and swelling nature of the soil particles.

d9c33d12789c.title: Soil aggregate stability
d9c33d12789c.section: Factors Affecting Aggregate Formation > Soil Biological Factors > Soil Fauna
d9c33d12789c.sentence: When earthworms ingest soil mineral and organic components, they can increase the structural stability of that soil through increased carbon-mineral associations and formation of casts, which increase aggregate stability.

b1be03de8d7d.title: Soil aggregate stability
b1be03de8d7d.section: Factors Affecting Aggregate Formation > Soil Biological Factors > Soil Fauna
b1be03de8d7d.sentence: Their production of fecal pellets can improve soil structure.

752702480716.title: Soil aggregate stability
752702480716.section: Factors Affecting Aggregate Formation > Soil Biological Factors > Fungi and Plant Roots
752702480716.sentence: Roots and fungal hyphae are important factors in aggregate formation.

0aa69832f768.title: Soil aggregate stability
0aa69832f768.section: Factors Affecting Aggregate Formation > Soil Biological Factors
0aa69832f768.sentence: Soil biological processes are most important in soils that do not have 2:1 phyllosilicate clay minerals, and are therefore lacking in shrinking and swelling properties that can aid in structural formation.

0ddde40d96ab.title: Soil aggregate stability
0ddde40d96ab.sentence: Soil aggregate stability is a measure of the ability of soil aggregates—soil particles that bind together—to resist breaking apart when exposed to external forces such as water erosion and wind erosion, shrinking and swelling processes, and tillage.

764daa2c10c8.title: Soil aggregate stability
764daa2c10c8.sentence: Soil aggregate stability is a measure of soil structure and can be affected by soil management.

020d4d53280c.title: Soil aggregate stability
020d4d53280c.sentence: Aggregate stability is one of indicators of soil quality, as it combines soil physical, chemical, and biological properties.

0560482b1a7c.title: Soil aggregate stability
0560482b1a7c.sentence: Aggregate stability has a direct impact on soil pore size distribution, which affects soil water retention and water movement in soil, therefore affecting air movement.

92452d4b3e18.title: Soil aggregate stability
92452d4b3e18.sentence: A soil with good soil structure typically has a mix of micro-, meso-, and macropores.

96cd8a9af373.title: Soil aggregate stability
96cd8a9af373.sentence: Micropores are important for water retention and storage in soils, while macro- and mesopores allow for the movement of water and air into the soil.

df1a6f6d4b3d.title: Soil aggregate stability
df1a6f6d4b3d.sentence: Soils with good aggregate stability typically have a higher water infiltration rate, allowing more water into the soil profile faster, and are not susceptible to water ponding.

9457ff8644bc.title: Soil aggregate stability
9457ff8644bc.sentence: In a compacted soil with few aggregates and limited pore spaces, roots have difficulty growing and may be excluded from nutrients and water stored in different parts of the soil.

05e69ca2b4ea.title: Soil aggregate stability
05e69ca2b4ea.section: Factors Affecting Aggregate Formation > Other Factors Affecting Aggregate Stability > Agricultural Management
05e69ca2b4ea.sentence: The main disruptors of aggregate stability are: tillage, traffic from equipment, and traffic from livestock.

7177c78b7e07.title: Soil aggregate stability
7177c78b7e07.section: Factors Affecting Aggregate Formation > Other Factors Affecting Aggregate Stability > Agricultural Management
7177c78b7e07.sentence: Using reduced tillage or zero tillage practices have been shown to improve soil aggregation compared to conventional tillage methods.

7f39df99de00.title: Soil aggregate stability
7f39df99de00.section: Factors Affecting Aggregate Formation > Other Factors Affecting Aggregate Stability > Agricultural Management
7f39df99de00.sentence: The use of cover crops has been shown to increase soil aggregation, due to the increase of soil organic matter and soil cover that they provide.

937417e2ae1e.title: Soil aggregate stability
937417e2ae1e.section: Factors Affecting Aggregate Formation > Other Factors Affecting Aggregate Stability > Agricultural Management
937417e2ae1e.sentence: Perennial crops typically require a halt in tillage, which prevents aggregate disruption, and allows plant to develop an extensive root system which can promote aggregate stability.

8e8833a41ada.title: Soil aggregate stability
8e8833a41ada.section: Factors Affecting Aggregate Formation > Other Factors Affecting Aggregate Stability > Agricultural Management
8e8833a41ada.sentence: Additionally, inputs of organic matter in the form of mulch or manure application can increase aggregation by adding carbon to the soil matrix and increasing rates of biological activity in the soil.

5e4a77240a73.title: Soil aggregate stability
5e4a77240a73.section: Factors Affecting Aggregate Formation > Other Factors Affecting Aggregate Stability > Climate
5e4a77240a73.sentence: Higher amounts of precipitation and irregular rainfall events can decrease aggregate stability and increase erosion.

b0be058ba09b.title: Soil aggregate stability
b0be058ba09b.section: Factors Affecting Aggregate Formation > Other Factors Affecting Aggregate Stability > Climate
b0be058ba09b.sentence: Also, higher temperatures can increase the rates of decomposition in soil, which reduces the amount of carbon on the site, which can reduce aggregate stability.

8d087cce2798.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/08%3A_Soil_Health/8.01%3A_Introduction_to_Soil_Health
8d087cce2798.sentence: Soil particles form aggregates as a product of cementing agents in the soil including clay content, adsorbed cations such as calcium and magnesium, and iron oxide content.

fc42e53607d4.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/08%3A_Soil_Health/8.01%3A_Introduction_to_Soil_Health
fc42e53607d4.sentence: In contrast, aggregate stability decreases with increasing amounts of exchangeable sodium: dispersion is promoted when too many sodium ions accumulate between soil particles.

116fa253afa5.title: Tilth
116fa253afa5.sentence: Tilth is a physical condition of soil, especially in relation to its suitability for planting or growing a crop.

9dee935fc479.title: Tilth
9dee935fc479.sentence: Factors that determine tilth include the formation and stability of aggregated soil particles, moisture content, degree of aeration, soil biota, rate of water infiltration and drainage.

0a5d7b3fefa3.title: Tilth
0a5d7b3fefa3.sentence: Tilth can change rapidly, depending on environmental factors, such as changes in moisture, tillage and soil amendments.

626fce32a3a3.title: Tilth
626fce32a3a3.sentence: Soil with good tilth is spongy with large pore spaces for air infiltration and water movement.

d8aa079d1add.title: Tilth
d8aa079d1add.sentence: Roots grow only where the soil tilth allows for adequate levels of soil oxygen.

dcc2a0770859.title: Tilth
dcc2a0770859.sentence: Such soil also holds a reasonable supply of water and nutrients.

2228c8741b73.title: Tilth
2228c8741b73.sentence: Good tilth shares a balanced relation between soil-aggregate tensile strength and friability, in which it has a stable mixture of aggregate soil particles that can be readily broken up by shallow, non-abrasive tilling.

6632ebce85af.title: Tilth
6632ebce85af.sentence: A high tensile strength will result in large cemented clods of compacted soil with low friability.

fff7c81a9520.title: Tilth
fff7c81a9520.sentence: Soil that is well aggregated has a range of pore sizes.

73fe83ace5ea.title: Tilth
73fe83ace5ea.sentence: Large pores drain rapidly and are needed for good air exchange during wet periods, preventing oxygen deficiency that can drown plants and increase pest problems.

03876826cbfc.title: Tilth
03876826cbfc.sentence: Small pores are critical for water retention and help a crop endure dry periods with minimal yield loss.

ba3f061f37b5.title: Tilth
ba3f061f37b5.sentence: The objective of tillage (mechanical manipulation of the soil) is to improve tilth, thereby increasing crop production; in the long term, however, conventional tillage, especially plowing, often has the opposite effect, causing the soil carbon sponge to oxidize, break down and become compacted.

05fb0367fd05.title: Tilth
05fb0367fd05.sentence: The tilth created by tillage, however, tends to be unstable, because the aggregation is obtained through the physical manipulation of the soil, which is short lived, especially after years of intensive tillage.

2387778bd93f.title: Tilth
2387778bd93f.sentence: In 2021, the globally tilled soil volume was estimated at 1840 km3/yr.

db3d3c3dc01f.title: Tilth
db3d3c3dc01f.sentence: For comparison globally, the natural process of soil bioturbation by plant roots and earthworms, was estimated at 960 km3/yr.

322b7f19b6bb.title: Tilth
322b7f19b6bb.sentence: The preferred scenario for good tilth is as the result of natural soil-building processes, provided by the activity of plant roots, microorganisms, earthworms and other beneficial organisms.

13bd44d3d58a.title: Tilth
13bd44d3d58a.sentence: Plant root exudates feed bacteria that emit extracellular polysaccharides (EPS), and feed the growth of fungal hyphae, to form a soil carbon sponge with the dispersed clay particles.

85ba14d75a90.title: Tilth
85ba14d75a90.sentence: Crop rotation can help restore tilth in compacted soils.

3dbe7d9059b5.title: Tilth
3dbe7d9059b5.sentence: Second, grass and legume sods develop extensive root systems that continually grow and die off.

b41fe069c34e.title: Tilth
b41fe069c34e.sentence: Perennial crops, such as alfalfa, have strong, deep, penetrating tap roots that can push through hard layers, especially during wet periods when the soil is soft.

038fc41d8f00.title: Tilth
038fc41d8f00.sentence: Crop rotation and cover crops can rebuild the soil carbon sponge and positively affect tilth.

9505f9a887e7.title: Dispersion (geology)
9505f9a887e7.sentence: Dispersion is a process that occurs in soils that are particularly vulnerable to erosion by water.

fbce712b4f36.title: Dispersion (geology)
fbce712b4f36.sentence: In soil layers where clays are saturated with sodium ions ("sodic soils"), soil can break down very easily into fine particles and wash away.

dc804175d14b.title: Soil biodiversity
dc804175d14b.sentence: In high levels, sodium ions break apart clay platelets and cause swelling and dispersion in soil.

2afa083e1a91.title: Sodium adsorption ratio
2afa083e1a91.sentence: Sodium and potassium ions facilitate the dispersion of clay particles while calcium and magnesium promote their flocculation.

4fa32b4dda57.title: Soil aggregate stability
4fa32b4dda57.sentence: This is the opposite of dispersion, which occurs when individual primary soil particles are held apart.

c74edbabf00f.title: Soil aggregate stability
c74edbabf00f.sentence: Soil particle dispersion and flocculation are mainly controlled by the soil pH, electrical conductivity (EC), and sodium content.

d7e335fbc8d1.title: Dispersion (geology)
d7e335fbc8d1.sentence: This can lead to a variety of soil and water quality problems, including:

f17622321995.title: Dispersion (geology)
f17622321995.sentence: - large soil losses by gully erosion and tunnel erosion

d7cf65f569f3.title: Dispersion (geology)
d7cf65f569f3.sentence: - Soil structural degradation, clogging and sealing where dispersed particles settle

7a2b1b3a5bfa.title: Dispersion (geology)
7a2b1b3a5bfa.sentence: - Suspended soil causing turbidity in water and transporting nutrients off the land.

ce4579b7052b.title: Dispersion (geology)
ce4579b7052b.sentence: The dispersive portion of a soil profile is generally confined to the subsoil, where soil-forming processes concentrate clay minerals and sodium.

246f05afa86a.title: Dispersion (geology)
246f05afa86a.sentence: This means that dispersive soils may not be identified until they are disturbed in a way that exposes the subsoil to running water.

f9d6d216d1c6.title: Dispersion (geology)
f9d6d216d1c6.sentence: Dispersive soils are more common in older landscapes where leaching and illuviation processes have had more time to work.

a1265f40e649.title: Dispersion (geology)
a1265f40e649.sentence: Sodium ions are highly mobile in the soil solution and so they accumulate in the lower parts of the landscape.

b9837e898b82.title: Dispersion (geology)
b9837e898b82.sentence: When observed in situ, dispersive soil textures may feel 'soapy', and in many cases the physical structure of subsoil layers will be prismatic or columnar.

e7386f267784.title: Dispersion (geology)
e7386f267784.sentence: The exchangeable sodium percentage ("ESP", (sodium / (total cations)) * 100) is a key indicator derived from these measurements.

68a50304bc25.title: Dispersion (geology)
68a50304bc25.sentence: Where ESP exceeds 5%, dispersive behaviour becomes possible, and is highly likely where ESP exceeds 15%.

dc06454ec70c.title: Dispersion (geology)
dc06454ec70c.sentence: The best management approach to these soils is simply to avoid their disturbance.

e96ae04f7df5.title: Dispersion (geology)
e96ae04f7df5.sentence: Maintaining vegetation cover of the soil is also important to minimize soil dispersion.

9a3d779d5b67.title: Dispersion (geology)
9a3d779d5b67.sentence: Landscape-scale management of excess salt is also important, as secondary salinisation can induce dispersive behaviour in soil.

6a38a19bf6bc.title: Dispersion (geology)
6a38a19bf6bc.sentence: In places where disturbance has occurred, amelioration with gypsum can be helpful.

5f49941dde51.title: Soil crust
5f49941dde51.sentence: Soil crusts are soil surface layers that are distinct from the rest of the bulk soil, often hardened with a platy surface.

11dcd47cfc98.title: Soil crust
11dcd47cfc98.sentence: Depending on the manner of formation, soil crusts can be biological or physical.

d0d08ec98d69.title: Soil crust
d0d08ec98d69.sentence: Biological soil crusts are formed by communities of microorganisms that live on the soil surface whereas physical crusts are formed by physical impact such as that of raindrops.

8dd236d079ca.title: Soil crust
8dd236d079ca.sentence: Physical (as opposed to biological) soil crusts results from raindrop or trampling impacts.

96f2178816ba.title: Soil crust
96f2178816ba.sentence: They are often hardened relative to uncrusted soil due to the accumulation of salts and silica.

c6122948ea06.title: Soil crust
c6122948ea06.sentence: Physical soil crusts often reduce water infiltration, can inhibit plant establishment, and when disrupted can be eroded rapidly.

5f5dfb5a7ea9.title: Infiltration (hydrology)
5f5dfb5a7ea9.section: Factors that affect infiltration > Land cover
5f5dfb5a7ea9.sentence: The low rate of infiltration in bare areas is due mostly to the presence of a soil crust or surface seal.

30b4c4367e5c.title: Surface runoff
30b4c4367e5c.sentence: This more commonly occurs in arid and semi-arid regions, where rainfall intensities are high and the soil infiltration capacity is reduced because of surface sealing, or in urban areas where pavements prevent water from infiltrating.

fd9ec37fc7b6.title: Soil structure
fd9ec37fc7b6.sentence: The benefits of improving soil structure (i.e. tending to granular structure) for the growth of plants, particularly in an agricultural setting, include: reduced erosion due to greater soil aggregate strength and decreased overland flow; improved root penetration and access to soil moisture and nutrients; improved emergence of seedlings due to reduced crusting of the surface; and greater water infiltration, retention and water availability due to improved porosity.

7c011a80e1c2.title: Soil moisture
7c011a80e1c2.sentence: Coarse matter is best and if on the surface helps prevent the destruction of soil structure and the creation of soil crusts.

c3120368006c.title: Soil structure
c3120368006c.sentence: Several techniques exist or have been suggested to improve soil structure, all of them tending to increase either porosity, organic matter content and/or soil microbial and faunal activity, i.e. all features associated with good granular/crumb structure.

c467330252e6.title: Soil structure
c467330252e6.sentence: The New South Wales Department of Land and Water Conservation suggests that in cropping systems, wheat yields can be increased by 10 kg/ha for every extra millimetre of rain that is able to infiltrate due to soil structure.

6482f6f8493c.title: Soil structure
6482f6f8493c.sentence: Incorporating or depositing organic matter (e.g. mulch, manure, compost) has been practiced since the beginning of sedentary agriculture, favouring aggregation through the formation of stable bridges between mineral particles.

8711a5ca70a8.title: Soil structure
8711a5ca70a8.sentence: In tropical areas, the fast rate of organic matter mineralization under warm/moist climate prevents using manure, mulch or compost for improving soil structure.

1deeebe43db1.title: Soil structure
1deeebe43db1.sentence: Organic matter was favourably replaced by charcoal, a source of black carbon, known for its longevity and stable links with clay minerals.

46ba2d006b6b.title: Soil structure
46ba2d006b6b.sentence: Charcoal addition has been practiced by Amerindians during Pre-Columbian times in the so-called Terra preta areas, also known as Amazonian Dark Earths.

838172c5e5f7.title: Soil structure
838172c5e5f7.sentence: Biochar is a present-day application of this ancestral technique.

d41c37c46918.title: Soil structure
d41c37c46918.sentence: Liming, either practised alone or in association with organic matter, increases soil porosity and aggregation thanks to the bridging capacity of the divalent calcium cation towards negatively charged clay particles and organic molecules.

32fc6c4662cc.title: Soil structure
32fc6c4662cc.sentence: Calcium also protects organic matter from mineralization, stabilizing it within aggregates.

33f3e336c4f3.title: Soil structure
33f3e336c4f3.sentence: For example, the New South Wales Department of Land and Water Conservation advocates: increasing organic content by incorporating pasture phases into cropping rotations; reducing or eliminating tillage in cropping and pasture activities; avoiding soil disturbance during periods of excessive dry or wet when soils may accordingly tend to shatter or smear; and ensuring sufficient ground cover to protect the soil from raindrop impact and subsequent slaking.

e801734ef6a6.title: Soil structure
e801734ef6a6.sentence: In irrigated agriculture, it may be recommended to: apply gypsum (calcium sulfate) to displace sodium cations with calcium and so reduce ESP or sodicity, avoid rapid wetting, and avoid disturbing soils when too wet or dry.

06384642dce8.title: Soil structure
06384642dce8.sentence: Productivity from irrigated no-tillage or minimum tillage soil management in horticulture usually decreases over time due to degradation of the soil structure, inhibiting root growth and water retention.

cb6811dda509.title: Soil structure
cb6811dda509.sentence: There are a few exceptions, why such exceptional fields retain structure is unknown, but it is associated with high organic matter.

1928c260b091.title: Soil structure
1928c260b091.sentence: Hardsetting soils lose their structure when wet and then set hard as they dry out to form a structureless mass that is very difficult to cultivate.

b550dad224b9.title: Soil structure
b550dad224b9.sentence: Hardsetting has been defined this way: "A hardsetting horizon is one that sets to an almost homogeneous mass on drying.

3045d8a35aa3.title: Soil structure
3045d8a35aa3.sentence: It may have occasional cracks, typically at a spacing of >0.1 m.

5fee2180ef03.title: Soil structure
5fee2180ef03.sentence: Air dry hardset soil is hard and brittle, and it is not possible to push a forefinger into the profile face.

2820d8cbdc42.title: Soil structure
2820d8cbdc42.sentence: (In cultivated soils the thickness of the hardsetting horizon is frequently equal to or greater than that of the cultivated layer.) Hardsetting soil is not permanently cemented and is soft when wet.

62cbaf49378e.title: Soil structure
62cbaf49378e.sentence: If the soil has been sufficiently wetted, it will revert to its hardset state on drying.

c37319858b16.title: Soil structure
c37319858b16.sentence: This can happen after flood irrigation or a single intense rainfall event."

3f7f5f818f22.title: Soil structure
3f7f5f818f22.sentence: They can only be tilled when their moisture content is within a limited range.

5eba770906ed.title: Soil structure
5eba770906ed.sentence: When they are tilled the result is often a very cloddy surface (poor tilth).

9e09c5d53dbe.title: Soil structure
9e09c5d53dbe.sentence: As they dry out the high soil strength often restricts seedling and root growth.

447adc0f02fd.title: Soil structure
447adc0f02fd.sentence: Infiltration rates are low and runoff of rain and irrigation limits the productivity of many hardsetting soils.

a8f5dfdc6b9d.title: Soil structure
a8f5dfdc6b9d.sentence: Soils that crust are not necessarily hardsetting since a hardsetting horizon is thicker than a crust.

ced30da3ce9d.title: Stokes's law
ced30da3ce9d.sentence: In fluid dynamics, Stokes's law gives the frictional force – also called drag force – exerted on spherical objects moving at very small Reynolds numbers in a viscous fluid.

7a2afaa44050.title: Stokes's law
7a2afaa44050.sentence: It was derived by George Gabriel Stokes in 1851 by solving the Stokes flow limit for small Reynolds numbers of the Navier–Stokes equations.

55074d991266.title: Stokes's law
55074d991266.sentence: Stokes's law makes the following assumptions for the behavior of a particle in a fluid:

2192bf791fd8.title: Stokes's law
2192bf791fd8.sentence: - Particles do not interfere with each other.

dd09405a1a33.title: Stokes's law
dd09405a1a33.sentence: To 10% error, for instance, velocities need be limited to those giving Re < 1.

397df83b78bc.title: Stokes's law
397df83b78bc.section: Applications > Terminal velocity of sphere falling in a fluid
397df83b78bc.sentence: If a particle only experiences its own weight while falling in a viscous fluid, then a terminal velocity is reached when the sum of the frictional and the buoyant forces on the particle due to the fluid exactly balances the gravitational force.

61216b2e3b9e.title: Stokes's law
61216b2e3b9e.section: Applications > Terminal velocity of sphere falling in a fluid
61216b2e3b9e.sentence: This velocity v [m/s] is given by:

b9e5fa304f5b.title: Stokes's law
b9e5fa304f5b.section: Applications > Terminal velocity of sphere falling in a fluid

e9a1f7011c2d.title: Stokes's law
e9a1f7011c2d.section: Applications > Terminal velocity of sphere falling in a fluid
e9a1f7011c2d.sentence: Requiring the force balance Fd = Fe and solving for the velocity v gives the terminal velocity vs. Note that since the excess force increases as R3 and Stokes's drag increases as R, the terminal velocity increases as R2 and thus varies greatly with particle size as shown below.

af83ba36dfe1.title: Stokes's law
af83ba36dfe1.sentence: Stokes's law is important for understanding the swimming of microorganisms and sperm; also, the sedimentation of small particles and organisms in water, under the force of gravity.

51339532066d.title: Stokes's law
51339532066d.sentence: In air, the same theory can be used to explain why small water droplets (or ice crystals) can remain suspended in air (as clouds) until they grow to a critical size and start falling as rain (or snow and hail).

c31fcc5a9944.title: Hydrophobic soil
c31fcc5a9944.sentence: Hydrophobic soil is a soil whose particles repel water.

1fcb5dbbdea0.title: Hydrophobic soil
1fcb5dbbdea0.sentence: Hydrophobic soil is most familiarly formed when a fire or hot air disperses waxy compounds found in the uppermost litter layer consisting of organic matter.

46861c570767.title: Hydrophobic soil
46861c570767.sentence: After the compounds disperse, they mainly coat sandy soil particles near the surface in the upper layers of soil, making the soil hydrophobic.

30a91cea9176.title: Hydrophobic soil
30a91cea9176.sentence: This layer can vary in thickness and abundance and is typically covered by a layer of ash or burned soil.

aacae3a0edc3.title: Hydrophobic soil
aacae3a0edc3.sentence: Soil texture plays a large role in predicting whether a soil could be water repelling as larger grained particles in the soil such as sand have smaller surface areas, making them more prone to being fully coated by hydrophobic compounds.

0b91d60dc63c.title: Hydrophobic soil
0b91d60dc63c.sentence: It is much more difficult to entirely coat a silt or clay particle with more surface area, but when it does happen, the resulting water repellency of the soil is severe.

d66fe8db807b.title: Hydrophobic soil
d66fe8db807b.section: Locations and appearance of hydrophobic soils
d66fe8db807b.sentence: Hydrophobic soils have been found on all continents except for Antarctica.

813db6820c17.title: Hydrophobic soil
813db6820c17.sentence: By reducing the infiltration rate, runoff generation time is reduced and leads to an increase in the land flow of water during precipitation or irrigation events.

f5acb47d3ddd.title: Hydrophobic soil
f5acb47d3ddd.sentence: Greater runoff increases erosion, causes uneven wetting patterns in soil, accelerates nutrient leaching reducing soil fertility, develops different flow paths in the region, and increases the risk of contamination in soils.

a3438f1ab0c7.title: Hydrophobic soil
a3438f1ab0c7.sentence: Because the water cannot drain into the stronger areas of hydrophobicity, the water finds pathways of preferential flow where it can infiltrate deeper into the soil profile.

a607ecb4b3e7.title: Hydrophobic soil
a607ecb4b3e7.sentence: If irrigation or precipitation events are large, the water could potentially flow below the root zone, making it unavailable to any plant life and oftentimes taking fertilizers and nutrients with it.

0899fcfe6f3f.title: Hydrophobic soil
0899fcfe6f3f.sentence: For example, in Australia, there have been documented reports of up to 80% loss in production due to soil water repellency.

4d8550967fce.title: Hydrophobic soil
4d8550967fce.sentence: One method of managing sandy water-repellent soil is claying.

a022ede505a4.title: Hydrophobic soil
a022ede505a4.sentence: This is done by adding select clay materials, such as calcium-bentonite, to give the soil more surface area per unit volume and improve soil mineralogy supporting aggregation.

3836459c54d6.title: Hydrophobic soil
3836459c54d6.sentence: A hydrophobic barley field increased crop yield from 1.7 to 3.4 t/ha, and a field of lupins increased the yield by 1 t/ha within 2 years of claying.

b7a3546d3dfc.title: Hydrophobic soil
b7a3546d3dfc.sentence: Liming is a method to reduce soil water repellency in acidic soils.

c34aa7259d6c.title: Hydrophobic soil
c34aa7259d6c.sentence: The liming process consists of adding calcium carbonate, which increases the pH of the soil towards neutral.

ec5b9fdc3cb6.title: Physical properties of soil
ec5b9fdc3cb6.sentence: Consistency is the ability of soil to stick to itself or to other objects (cohesion and adhesion, respectively) and its ability to resist deformation and rupture.

6f2091cc5e68.title: Physical properties of soil
6f2091cc5e68.sentence: Soil consistency is the ability of soil materials to stick together.

e43ac0140db0.title: Physical properties of soil
e43ac0140db0.sentence: Consistency is measured at three moisture conditions: air-dry, moist, and wet.

2f608f1afbf6.title: Physical properties of soil
2f608f1afbf6.sentence: In those conditions the consistency quality depends upon the clay content.

56f753647ca2.title: Physical properties of soil
56f753647ca2.sentence: A soil's resistance to fragmentation and crumbling is assessed in the dry state by rubbing the sample.

b4e2fa928e0e.title: Physical properties of soil
b4e2fa928e0e.sentence: Its resistance to shearing forces is assessed in the moist state by thumb and finger pressure.

9d899d97faa7.title: Physical properties of soil
9d899d97faa7.sentence: In the wet state, the two qualities of stickiness and plasticity are assessed.

b98f4e0ec509.title: Physical properties of soil
b98f4e0ec509.sentence: - Consistency of Dry Soil: loose, soft, slightly hard, hard, very hard, extremely hard

36dbea5cc917.title: Physical properties of soil
36dbea5cc917.sentence: - Consistency of Moist Soil: loose, very friable, friable, firm, very firm, extremely firm

4d7cf21f2b8e.title: Physical properties of soil
4d7cf21f2b8e.sentence: - Consistency of Wet Soil: nonsticky, slightly sticky, sticky, very sticky; nonplastic, slightly plastic, plastic, very plastic

d7925f11681c.title: Physical properties of soil
d7925f11681c.sentence: Additionally, the cemented consistency depends on cementation by substances other than clay, such as calcium carbonate, silica, oxides and salts; moisture content has little effect on its assessment.

0625c120b905.title: Physical properties of soil
0625c120b905.sentence: - Consistency of Cemented Soil: weakly cemented, strongly cemented, indurated (requires hammer blows to break up)

891c6878ae3c.title: Physical properties of soil
891c6878ae3c.sentence: The measures of consistency border on subjective compared to other measures such as pH, since they employ the apparent feel of the soil in those states.

2be867c1f945.title: Physical properties of soil
2be867c1f945.sentence: It is of approximate use in predicting cultivation problems and the engineering of foundations.

af902eea8078.title: Physical properties of soil
af902eea8078.sentence: Soil consistency is useful in estimating the ability of soil to support buildings and roads.

773dbc6bba6b.title: Physical properties of soil
773dbc6bba6b.sentence: More precise measures of soil strength are often made prior to construction.

2bee0ebf3cec.title: Soil series
2bee0ebf3cec.sentence: More specifically, each series consists of pedons having soil horizons that are similar in soil color, soil texture, soil structure, soil pH, consistency, mineral and chemical composition, and arrangement in the soil profile.

0347b18fc876.title: USDA soil taxonomy
0347b18fc876.sentence: The principal characteristics used to differentiate soil families include texture, mineralogy, pH, permeability, structure, consistency, the locale's precipitation pattern, and soil temperature.

a1a9a349ecb2.title: Atterberg limits
a1a9a349ecb2.sentence: The Atterberg limits are a basic measure of the critical water contents of a fine-grained soil: its shrinkage limit, plastic limit, and liquid limit.

670a65951ff0.title: Atterberg limits
670a65951ff0.sentence: The water content at which soil changes from one state to the other is known as consistency limits, or Atterberg's limit.

f7cb22c9896a.title: Atterberg limits
f7cb22c9896a.sentence: Depending on its water content, soil may appear in one of four states: solid, semi-solid, plastic and liquid.

a1120987b334.title: Atterberg limits
a1120987b334.sentence: In each state, the consistency and behavior of soil are different, and consequently so are its engineering properties.

05d220028085.title: Atterberg limits
05d220028085.sentence: Thus, the boundary between each state can be defined based on a change in the soil's behavior.

3eedb4df2069.title: Soil mechanics
3eedb4df2069.section: Soil classification > Classification of soil grains > Atterberg limits
3eedb4df2069.sentence: The consistency of a fine grained soil varies in proportion to its water content.

d1aa3e8b1892.title: Soil mechanics
d1aa3e8b1892.section: Soil classification > Classification of soil grains > Atterberg limits
d1aa3e8b1892.sentence: As the transitions from one state to another are gradual, the tests have adopted arbitrary definitions to determine the boundaries of the states.

39be1d833863.title: Atterberg limits
39be1d833863.sentence: These limits were created by Albert Atterberg, a Swedish chemist and agronomist, in 1911.

847aceda7b25.title: Atterberg limits
847aceda7b25.sentence: They were later refined by Arthur Casagrande, an Austrian geotechnical engineer and a close collaborator of Karl Terzaghi (both pioneers of soil mechanics).

62b05f0f5891.title: Atterberg limits
62b05f0f5891.sentence: The Atterberg limits can be used to distinguish between silt and clay and to distinguish between different types of silts and clays.

d0f6c10dbef8.title: Soil mechanics
d0f6c10dbef8.section: Genesis and composition of soils > Soil composition > Grain size distribution > Hydrometer analysis
d0f6c10dbef8.sentence: The classification of fine-grained soils, i.e., soils that are finer than sand, is determined primarily by their Atterberg limits, not by their grain size.

2357aa97ef8a.title: Atterberg limits
2357aa97ef8a.sentence: These tests are mainly used on clayey or silty soils since these are the soils which expand and shrink when the moisture content varies.

a3fd8bc03d65.title: Atterberg limits
a3fd8bc03d65.sentence: Clays and silts interact with water and thus change sizes and have varying shear strengths.

19b1e61ef608.title: Atterberg limits
19b1e61ef608.sentence: There is also a close relationship between the limits and properties of soil, such as compressibility, permeability, and strength.

82ea3b1ff1c5.title: Atterberg limits
82ea3b1ff1c5.sentence: This is thought to be very useful because as limit determination is relatively simple, it is more difficult to determine these other properties.

31293f201e7b.title: Atterberg limits
31293f201e7b.sentence: Thus, the Atterberg limits are used to identify the soil's classification and allow for empirical correlations for some other engineering properties.

6afc18240798.title: Atterberg limits
6afc18240798.sentence: Thus these tests are used widely in the preliminary stages of designing any structure to ensure that the soil will have the correct amount of shear strength and not too much change in volume as it expands and shrinks with different moisture contents.

a50bb1ca86ef.title: Unified Soil Classification System
a50bb1ca86ef.sentence: The Unified Soil Classification System (USCS) is a soil classification system used in engineering and geology to describe the texture and grain size of a soil.

a4b27a543e70.title: Unified Soil Classification System
a4b27a543e70.sentence: The classification system can be applied to most unconsolidated materials, and is represented by a two-letter symbol.

84173b4d8416.title: Soil classification
84173b4d8416.sentence: The most common engineering classification system for soils in North America is the Unified Soil Classification System (USCS).

2e297db491ef.title: Unified Soil Classification System
2e297db491ef.sentence: Letter Definition G gravel S sand M silt C clay O organic PT peat | Letter Definition P poorly graded (many different particle sizes ) W well-graded (many particle of about the same size ) H high liquid limit L low liquid limit

c6c7506c5c22.title: Soil classification
c6c7506c5c22.sentence: The USCS has three major classification groups: (1) coarse-grained soils (e.g. sands and gravels); (2) fine-grained soils (e.g. silts and clays); and (3) highly organic soils (referred to as "peat").

74cf6d6515e1.title: Unified Soil Classification System
74cf6d6515e1.sentence: Coarse grained soils more than 50% retained on or above No.200 (0.075 mm) sieve | gravel > 50% of coarse fraction retained on No.4 (4.75 mm) sieve | clean gravel <5% smaller than No.200 Sieve | GW | well-graded gravel, fine to coarse gravel

3c1bb18164c5.title: Soil mechanics
3c1bb18164c5.section: Genesis and composition of soils > Soil composition > Grain size distribution > Sieve analysis
3c1bb18164c5.sentence: According to the Unified Soil Classification System, a #4 sieve (4 openings per inch) having 4.75 mm opening size separates sand from gravel and a #200 sieve with an 0.075 mm opening separates sand from silt and clay.

678a769991d1.title: Soil classification
678a769991d1.sentence: It distinguishes sands from gravels by grain size, classifying some as "well-graded" and the rest as "poorly-graded".

a177209db34e.title: Soil classification
a177209db34e.sentence: Silts and clays are distinguished by the soils' Atterberg limits, and thus the soils are separated into "high-plasticity" and "low-plasticity" soils.

2c5809b8cdd7.title: Unified Soil Classification System
2c5809b8cdd7.sentence: If the soil has 5–12% by weight of fines passing a #200 sieve (5% < P#200 < 12%), both grain size distribution and plasticity have a significant effect on the engineering properties of the soil, and dual notation may be used for the group symbol.

26837cc43ade.title: Unified Soil Classification System
26837cc43ade.sentence: For example, GW-GM corresponds to "well-graded gravel with silt."

217abd72cb3e.title: Soil mechanics
217abd72cb3e.section: Genesis and composition of soils > Genesis
217abd72cb3e.sentence: According to the Unified Soil Classification System, silt particle sizes are in the range of 0.002 mm to 0.075 mm and sand particles have sizes in the range of 0.075 mm to 4.75 mm.

1da041e666e9.title: Soil classification
1da041e666e9.sentence: The European soil classification system (ISO 14688) is very similar, differing primarily in coding and in adding an "intermediate-plasticity" classification for silts and clays, and in minor details.

c441379e2c89.title: Soil mechanics
c441379e2c89.section: Soil classification > Classification of soil grains > Classification of sands and gravels
c441379e2c89.sentence: In the USCS, gravels (given the symbol G) and sands (given the symbol S) are classified according to their grain size distribution.

58175657184d.sentence: Coarse grained soils more than 50% retained on or above No.200 (0.075 mm) sieve | sand ≥ 50% of coarse fraction passes No.4 (4.75 mm) sieve | clean sand | SW | well-graded sand, fine to coarse sand

98c6dcbeb594.title: Unified Soil Classification System
98c6dcbeb594.sentence: COARSE-GRAINED SOILS More than 50% retained on No.200 Sieve | Sands 50% or more of coarse fraction passes No.4 sieve | Sands with Fines More than 12% fines | Fines classify as ML or MH | SM | Silty sand

fca37b340d4b.title: Unified Soil Classification System
fca37b340d4b.sentence: COARSE-GRAINED SOILS More than 50% retained on No.200 Sieve | Sands 50% or more of coarse fraction passes No.4 sieve | Sands with Fines More than 12% fines | Fines classify as CL or CH | SC | Clayey sand

d265c35fedc0.sentence: Sands and gravels with a small but non-negligible amount of fines (5–12%) may be given a dual classification such as SW-SC.

2c7b55e5234b.sentence: The results are presented in a graph of percent passing versus the sieve size.

1d2fbae05c2b.title: Sieve analysis

e80a81412722.title: Sieve analysis
e80a81412722.sentence: To find the percent of aggregate passing through each sieve, first find the percent retained in each sieve.

f4b59a8b2c0b.title: Sieve analysis
f4b59a8b2c0b.sentence: The next step is to find the cumulative percent of aggregate retained in each sieve.

7d727c7e9ef2.title: Sieve analysis

30d7e3397dd5.title: Sieve analysis

e7cab9e00668.title: Sieve analysis
e7cab9e00668.sentence: The results of this test are provided in graphical form to identify the type of gradation of the aggregate.

e0cc586cedc7.title: Sieve analysis
e0cc586cedc7.sentence: A dense gradation will result in an even curve on the gradation graph.

76274bafba44.title: Sieve analysis
76274bafba44.sentence: Also known as uniform gradation, a narrow gradation is a sample that has aggregate of approximately the same size.

23c3c8a2c21a.title: Sieve analysis
23c3c8a2c21a.sentence: The curve on the gradation graph is very steep, and occupies a small range of the aggregate.

a82a4f11dd02.title: Sieve analysis

0ba900c474d1.title: Sieve analysis

34ac3e297183.title: Friability
34ac3e297183.sentence: In materials science, friability (/ˌfraɪ.əˈbɪləti/ FRY-ə-BIL-ə-tee), the condition of being friable, is the tendency of a solid substance to break into smaller pieces under stress or contact, especially by rubbing.

3ff1a482207a.title: Friability
3ff1a482207a.sentence: The opposite of friable is indurate.

75b7c754ebf1.title: Friability
75b7c754ebf1.sentence: Friable and indurated are terms used commonly in soft-rock geology, especially with sandstones, mudstones, and shales to describe how well the component rock fragments are held together.

cee9c00b14a8.title: Digging
cee9c00b14a8.section: Digging by humans > Reasons > Borrow pit
cee9c00b14a8.sentence: Borrow pits are common archaeological features in Waikato, where sand and gravel were dug to mix with clay topsoils to improve their drainage and friability, to suit growth of kūmara and taro, brought by Māori from tropical islands.

c84b13681361.title: Atterberg limits
c84b13681361.sentence: The liquid limit (LL) is conceptually defined as the water content at which the behavior of a clayey soil changes from the plastic state to the liquid state.

f216e5363fc5.title: Soil mechanics
f216e5363fc5.section: Soil classification > Classification of soil grains > Atterberg limits
f216e5363fc5.sentence: The liquid limit is the water content at which the soil behavior transitions from a plastic solid to a liquid.

e4b74bf329ca.title: Atterberg limits
e4b74bf329ca.sentence: However, the transition from plastic to liquid behavior is gradual over a range of water contents, and the shear strength of the soil is not actually zero at the liquid limit.

0cac93eb62e3.title: Soil mechanics
0cac93eb62e3.section: Soil classification > Classification of soil grains > Atterberg limits
0cac93eb62e3.sentence: The undrained shear strength of remolded soil at the liquid limit is approximately 2 kPa.

8209e7973093.title: Atterberg limits

8209e7973093.sentence: Soil is placed into the metal cup (Casagrande cup) portion of the device and a groove is made down at its center with a standardized tool of 2 millimetres (0.079 in) width.

5aada79d8cac.title: Atterberg limits
5aada79d8cac.section: Laboratory tests > Liquid limit > Casagrande's method
5aada79d8cac.sentence: The moisture content at which it takes 25 drops of the cup to cause the groove to close over a distance of 12.7 millimetres (0.50 in) is defined as the liquid limit.

f9fada9b0260.title: Atterberg limits
f9fada9b0260.section: Laboratory tests > Liquid limit > Fall cone test
f9fada9b0260.sentence: Another method for measuring the liquid limit is the fall cone test, also called the cone penetrometer test.

fcab96cce515.title: Atterberg limits
fcab96cce515.section: Laboratory tests > Liquid limit > Fall cone test
fcab96cce515.sentence: It is based on the measurement of penetration into the soil of a standardized stainless steel cone of specific apex angle, length and mass.

8b19b516bd0f.title: Atterberg limits
8b19b516bd0f.section: Laboratory tests > Liquid limit > Fall cone test
8b19b516bd0f.sentence: Although the Casagrande test is widely used across North America, the fall cone test is much more prevalent in Europe and elsewhere due to being less dependent on the operator in determining the liquid limit.

80b70cd2d744.title: Soil mechanics

80b70cd2d744.sentence: LL=50% separates high plasticity soils (given the modifier symbol H) from low plasticity soils (given the modifier symbol L).

6609afea098b.title: Soil mechanics
6609afea098b.section: Soil classification > Classification of soil grains > Atterberg limits
6609afea098b.sentence: The plastic limit is the water content at which the soil behavior transitions from that of a plastic solid to a brittle solid.

f4f2d4693f51.title: Atterberg limits
f4f2d4693f51.sentence: The plastic limit is defined as the gravimetric moisture content where the thread breaks apart at a diameter of 3.2 mm (about 1/8 inch).

cd65c1e416c1.title: Atterberg limits
cd65c1e416c1.sentence: The plastic limit (PL) is determined by rolling out a thread of the fine portion of a soil on a flat, non-porous surface.

c66941c42d4b.title: Atterberg limits
c66941c42d4b.sentence: As the moisture content falls due to evaporation, the thread will begin to break apart at larger diameters.

ffd77c240455.title: Atterberg limits
ffd77c240455.sentence: A soil is considered non-plastic if a thread cannot be rolled out down to 3.2 mm at any moisture possible.

e24b0acca5a6.title: Soil mechanics
e24b0acca5a6.section: Soil classification > Classification of soil grains > Atterberg limits
e24b0acca5a6.sentence: Remolded soil at the plastic limit is quite stiff, having an undrained shear strength of the order of about 200 kPa.

fa22b3d2d6e7.title: Soil mechanics

fa22b3d2d6e7.sentence: When the soil is at the plastic limit, the LI is 0 and the undrained shear strength is about 200 kPa.

6e73dfb4d915.title: Atterberg limits
6e73dfb4d915.sentence: The liquidity index (LI) is used to scale the natural water content of a soil sample to the limit.

34a94e3051f8.title: Atterberg limits

44dd4ed9fe68.sentence: When the LI is 1, remolded soil is at the liquid limit and it has an undrained shear strength of about 2 kPa.

c173537aa08b.title: Atterberg limits

c9a0b7637f5c.sentence: The PI is the difference between the liquid and plastic limits (PI = LL-PL).

6b2c3b5007e3.title: Soil mechanics
6b2c3b5007e3.section: Soil classification > Classification of soil grains > Atterberg limits
6b2c3b5007e3.sentence: The plasticity index of a particular soil specimen is defined as the difference between the liquid limit and the plastic limit of the specimen; it is an indicator of how much water the soil particles in the specimen can absorb, and correlates with many engineering properties like permeability, compressibility, shear strength and others.

036a9480b0b1.title: Soil mechanics
036a9480b0b1.section: Soil classification > Classification of soil grains > Atterberg limits
036a9480b0b1.sentence: Generally, the clay having high plasticity have lower permeability and also they are also difficult to be compacted.

d689b08cc724.sentence: According to the Unified Soil Classification System (USCS), silts and clays are classified by plotting the values of their plasticity index and liquid limit on a plasticity chart.

72aae56f8d51.title: Soil texture
72aae56f8d51.sentence: This diffraction pattern is then detected and analyzed by means of Mie and Fraunhofer diffraction models.

bf1e71da2dca.title: Soil texture
bf1e71da2dca.sentence: Because these parameters are often difficult to retrieve, especially the light absorption coefficients for various particles and soil grains, Fraunhofer theory, which only takes into account the light diffraction phenomena at the edge of the particles, is often recommended for natural soils.

1e636fe1a1f9.title: Laser diffraction analysis
1e636fe1a1f9.sentence: Fraunhofer theory only takes into account the diffraction phenomena occurring at the contour of the particle.

b6ddc50f40c3.title: Laser diffraction analysis
b6ddc50f40c3.sentence: Its main advantage is that it does not require any knowledge of the optical properties (complex refractive index) of the particle’s material.

038b1396ae21.title: Laser diffraction analysis
038b1396ae21.sentence: Hence, it is taking into account not only the diffraction at the particle’s contour, but also the refraction, reflection and absorption phenomena within the particle and at its surface.

df4708a78480.title: Laser diffraction analysis
df4708a78480.sentence: The model’s main limitation is that it requires precise knowledge of the complex refractive index (including the absorption coefficient) of the particle’s material.

28ae1f08b5c8.title: Laser diffraction analysis
28ae1f08b5c8.sentence: The angle of the laser beam and particle size have an inversely proportional relationship, where the laser beam angle increases as particle size decreases and vice versa.

9ef244e2129d.title: Laser diffraction analysis
9ef244e2129d.sentence: The lower theoretical detection limit of laser diffraction, using the Mie theory, is generally thought to lie around 10 nm.

9d0b939494b3.title: Laser diffraction analysis
9d0b939494b3.sentence: Because the light energy recorded by the detector array is proportional to the volume of the particles, laser diffraction results are intrinsically volume-weighted.

786e216e2c9c.title: Laser diffraction analysis
786e216e2c9c.sentence: That the diffracted light is proportional to the particle’s volume also implies that results are assuming particle sphericity, i.e. that the particle size result is an equivalent spherical diameter.

a7da0655d5d6.title: Laser diffraction analysis

f2efd5b57269.title: Laser diffraction analysis

765d9175b173.title: Laser diffraction analysis
765d9175b173.sentence: - The span, which gives a measure of the width of the particle size distribution, and is calculated as span = [D90 – D10]/D50.

617abbb7c3f3.title: Soil texture
617abbb7c3f3.sentence: Compared to other techniques laser diffraction is a fast and cost-effective method to measure particle size and quickly analyze soil samples, even very small samples as those used in forensic science.

0ec20c3abdf2.title: Soil texture
0ec20c3abdf2.sentence: A big advantage is the built-in dispersion (e.g. dispersion by air pressure or ultrasound dispersion) unit of laser diffraction instruments.

209808763d6c.title: Soil texture
209808763d6c.sentence: Therefore, dry samples can be measured without external sample preparation steps, which are required for sieving and sedimentation analysis.

a267dc42304b.title: Soil texture
a267dc42304b.sentence: Moreover, since the sample can be dispersed properly, there is no need to combine two different measurement techniques to obtain the full range of the particle size distribution, including the silt and clay content.

e482118522d5.title: Soil texture
e482118522d5.sentence: Both Fraunhofer and Mie laser diffraction theories assume that particles are spherically shaped.

82338b11b0b6.title: Soil texture
82338b11b0b6.sentence: The volume of clay particles is the diameter of the plate’s cross-section, which is treated in the calculations as the diameter of the (virtual) sphere.

a58e57f5ae85.title: Soil texture
a58e57f5ae85.sentence: Therefore, their dimensions are usually overestimated in comparison to those measured via sedimentation analysis.

557095fee5c8.title: Laser diffraction analysis
557095fee5c8.sentence: Since laser diffraction analysis is not the sole way of measuring particles it has been compared to the sieve-pipette method, which is a traditional technique for grain size analysis.

48a085e7bbcc.title: Laser diffraction analysis
48a085e7bbcc.sentence: When compared, results showed that laser diffraction analysis made fast calculations that were easy to recreate after a one-time analysis, did not need large sample sizes, and produced large amounts of data.

64fdd6df36e5.title: Laser diffraction analysis
64fdd6df36e5.sentence: Both the sieve-pipette method and laser diffraction analysis are able to analyze minuscule objects, but laser diffraction analysis resulted in having better precision than its counterpart method of particle measurement.

9cd40c1e4ad8.sentence: Slaking is the process in which earth materials disintegrate and crumble when exposed to moisture.

4648c8337b5b.title: Slaking (geology)

897c58773266.title: Soil moisture

d15110ed107c.title: Physical properties of soil

6fbae2ee0409.title: Slaking (geology)

7acf24fb0892.title: Slaking (geology)

cc31749c9fd6.title: Slaking (geology)

1b04dd7e769b.title: Soil physics

7b5f75a719cc.title: Soil physics

453fd6d4cd55.title: Soil physics

6cfbb3e256cb.title: Soil physics

1e8befd5325f.title: Soil physics

3d1e6cfb8ee3.sentence: Most attention was given to soil physics, for example, water-holding capacities of soils, moisture requirements of plants, aeration, movement of water in soils, movement of groundwater, the drafts of plows, and the lifting power of windmills; he also began studies of soil fertility.

a3d59e17bf29.title: Soil physics

8f44fd0b5159.title: Soil mechanics
8f44fd0b5159.sentence: Soil mechanics is a branch of soil physics and applied mechanics that describes the behavior of soils.

7847c2d73e04.title: Soil mechanics
7847c2d73e04.sentence: It differs from fluid mechanics and solid mechanics in the sense that soils consist of a heterogeneous mixture of fluids (usually air and water) and particles (usually clay, silt, sand, and gravel) but soil also contains organic solids and other matter.

7cdcf7e08842.title: Soil mechanics
7cdcf7e08842.sentence: Along with rock mechanics, soil mechanics provides the theoretical basis for analysis in geotechnical engineering, a subdiscipline of civil engineering, and engineering geology, a subdiscipline of geology.

bfaa23ba9e25.title: Soil mechanics
bfaa23ba9e25.sentence: Soil mechanics is used to analyze the deformations of and flow of fluids within natural and man-made structures that are supported on or made of soil, or structures that are buried in soils.

adf55194cfd6.title: Soil mechanics
adf55194cfd6.sentence: Example applications are building and bridge foundations, retaining walls, dams, and buried pipeline systems.

2c80812e1670.title: Soil mechanics
2c80812e1670.sentence: Principles of soil mechanics are also used in related disciplines such as geophysical engineering, coastal engineering, agricultural engineering, and hydrology.

788a99fbafa1.title: Soil mechanics

788a99fbafa1.sentence: The normal stresses, on the other hand, are shared by the fluid and the particles.

b949cbf1bb0b.title: Soil mechanics

b949cbf1bb0b.sentence: Neither gas nor liquid provide significant resistance to shear stress.

aac2c413631a.title: Soil mechanics
aac2c413631a.section: Effective stress and capillarity: hydrostatic conditions
aac2c413631a.sentence: The shear resistance of soil is provided by friction and interlocking of the particles.

a7aa35d46216.title: Soil mechanics
a7aa35d46216.sentence: Geotechnical engineers classify the soil particle types by performing tests on disturbed (dried, passed through sieves, and remolded) samples of the soil.

0ff63fb583e9.title: Soil mechanics

afb09ff92dc9.title: Bulk density
afb09ff92dc9.sentence: In materials science, bulk density, also called apparent density, is a material property defined as the mass of the many particles of the material divided by the bulk volume.

5bcaf47677a0.title: Bulk density
5bcaf47677a0.sentence: Bulk volume is defined as the total volume the particles occupy, including particle's own volume, inter-particle void volume, and the particles' internal pore volume.

7f38e6e406c4.title: Bulk density
7f38e6e406c4.sentence: Bulk density is not the same as the particle density, which is an intrinsic property of the solid and does not include the volume for voids between particles (see: density of non-compact materials).

a795dfe22355.title: Bulk density
a795dfe22355.sentence: Bulk density is an extrinsic property of a material; it can change depending on how the material is handled.

fae8fd6d4cee.title: Bulk density
fae8fd6d4cee.sentence: For example, a powder poured into a cylinder will have a particular bulk density; if the cylinder is disturbed, the powder particles will move and usually settle closer together, resulting in a higher bulk density.

a82198aff39f.title: Bulk density
a82198aff39f.sentence: The bulk density of soil depends greatly on the mineral make up of soil and the degree of compaction.

b0ea2daf5037.title: Bulk density
b0ea2daf5037.sentence: The density of quartz is around 2.65 g/cm3 but the (dry) bulk density of a mineral soil is normally about half that density, between 1.0 and 1.6 g/cm3.

e256838f9e58.title: Bulk density
e256838f9e58.sentence: In contrast, soils rich in soil organic carbon and some friable clays tend to have lower bulk densities (<1.0 g/cm3) due to a combination of the low-density of the organic materials themselves and increased porosity.

587b51129207.title: Bulk density
587b51129207.sentence: For instance, peat soils have bulk densities from 0.02 to 0.98 g/cm3.

2cd6371589fc.title: Bulk density
2cd6371589fc.sentence: The dry bulk density of a soil is inversely related to the porosity of the same soil: the more pore space in a soil the lower the value for bulk density.

82f705d2b46c.title: Pore space in soil
82f705d2b46c.sentence: The more pore space in a soil, the lower its dry bulk density.

1a20dca695a9.title: Bulk density

57e1d36cf7d6.title: Bulk density

ea827c1a2904.title: Physical properties of soil
ea827c1a2904.sentence: A high bulk density is indicative of either soil compaction or a mixture of soil textural classes in which small particles fill the voids among coarser particles.

38fb17d020f7.title: Humus

9da83d6a74ce.sentence: There are many different PTF methods, however, they all attempt to determine soil properties, such as hydraulic conductivity, given several measured soil properties, such as soil particle size, and bulk density.

8bf38ec945f0.title: Soil matrix
8bf38ec945f0.sentence: The soil matrix is the solid phase of soils, and comprise the solid particles that make up soils.

862bc67ba35f.title: Agricultural soil science
862bc67ba35f.sentence: The solid frames of soil (the soil matrix) consist of minerals derived from rocks and organic matter originated from the dead bodies and organs and excreta of various soil organisms.

6e1acdefb34e.title: Soil matrix
6e1acdefb34e.sentence: Soil particles can be classified by their chemical composition (mineralogy) as well as their size.

8b7f02c4502d.title: Soil matrix
8b7f02c4502d.sentence: The particle-size distribution of a soil, its texture, determines many of the properties of that soil, in particular hydraulic conductivity and water potential, but the mineralogy of those particles can strongly modify those properties.

dfde612b98dc.title: Soil matrix
dfde612b98dc.sentence: Gravel, sand and silt are the larger soil particles, and their mineralogy is often inherited from the parent material of the soil, but may include products of weathering (such as concretions of calcium carbonate or iron oxide), or residues of plant and animal life (such as silica phytoliths).

609070a1e357.title: Soil matrix
609070a1e357.sentence: Quartz is the most common mineral in the sand or silt fraction as it is resistant to chemical weathering, except under hot climate; other common minerals are feldspars, micas and ferromagnesian minerals such as pyroxenes, amphiboles and olivines, which are dissolved or transformed in clay under the combined influence of physico-chemical and biological processes.

90a1a2f82774.title: Soil matrix
90a1a2f82774.sentence: Due to its high specific surface area and its unbalanced negative electric charges, clay is the most active mineral component of soil.

79c2caa33d80.title: Soil matrix
79c2caa33d80.sentence: The mineralogy of the finest soil particles, clay, is especially important.

7df206354bab.title: Soil matrix
7df206354bab.sentence: Before the advent of X-ray diffraction clay was thought to be very small particles of quartz, feldspar, mica, hornblende or augite, but it is now known to be (with the exception of mica-based clays) a precipitate with a mineralogical composition that is dependent on but different from its parent materials and is classed as a secondary mineral.

a9a9536cd753.title: Soil matrix
a9a9536cd753.sentence: Clay minerals continue to be formed as long as the soil exists, whether by inheritance, neoformation, or transformation of pre-existing minerals.

fb2c4fa2189e.title: Soil matrix
fb2c4fa2189e.sentence: It remains in the soil as the organic component of the soil matrix while the other stage, carbon dioxide, issuing from the mineralization of carbonaceous compounds, is freely liberated in the atmosphere or reacts with calcium to form the soluble calcium bicarbonate or precipitates as calcium carbonate according to pH.

989219f44fb6.title: Soil matrix
989219f44fb6.sentence: On a dry weight basis, the CEC of humus is many times greater than that of clay.

e0dd5a3e2f8a.title: Plant nutrients in soil
e0dd5a3e2f8a.sentence: The nutrients adsorbed in an exchangeable form onto the surfaces of clay colloids and soil organic matter (the soil matrix) provide a more accessible reservoir of many plant nutrients (e.g. K, Ca, Mg, P, Zn).

7de618671f19.title: Pore space in soil
7de618671f19.sentence: The pore space of soil contains the liquid and gas phases of soil, i.e., everything but the solid phase that contains mainly minerals of varying sizes as well as organic compounds.

6c2f1f637024.title: Pore space in soil

9152bfad2a5c.title: Pore space in soil
9152bfad2a5c.sentence: The amount of porosity in a soil depends on the minerals that make up the soil and on the amount of sorting occurring within the soil structure.

5223f412a65a.title: Pore space in soil
5223f412a65a.sentence: For example, a sandy soil will have a larger porosity than a silty sand, because the silt will fill the gaps in between the sand particles, and the more in clay-silt-sand mixtures.

98a6cbd240da.title: Physical properties of soil
98a6cbd240da.sentence: Sand's greatest benefit to soil is that it resists compaction and increases soil porosity, although this property stands only for pure sand, not for sand mixed with smaller minerals which fill the voids among sand grains.

768cd31f0879.title: Pore space in soil
768cd31f0879.sentence: Macropores or fractures play a major role in infiltration rates in many soils as well as preferential flow patterns, hydraulic conductivity and evapotranspiration.

5000c062f13b.title: Pore space in soil
5000c062f13b.sentence: Cracks are also very influential in gas exchange, influencing respiration within soils.

2bd082e09352.title: Pore space in soil
2bd082e09352.sentence: The largest cracks and pores offer a great reservoir for the initial flush of water.

a04981629850.title: Pore space in soil
a04981629850.sentence: This allows a rapid infiltration mostly by gravity.

cf10bf1df579.title: Pore space in soil
cf10bf1df579.sentence: The smaller pores take longer to fill and rely on capillary forces as well as gravity.

af1a4f1f54dd.title: Pore space in soil
af1a4f1f54dd.sentence: The smaller pores have a slower infiltration as the soil becomes more saturated, as well as when air is entrapped within small pores.

7c7e020752e3.title: Pore space in soil
7c7e020752e3.sentence: Hydraulic conductivity (K) is a property of soil that describes the ease with which water can move through pore spaces.

6ad5bb66d350.title: Pore space in soil

e10a11d8f97a.title: Pore space in soil
e10a11d8f97a.sentence: The pore space of soil is the habitat of plant roots (rhizosphere), soil fauna and microorganisms, and in turn growing plant roots and burrowing soil animals affect it by creating networks of interconnected pores.

55270e6ea0b0.title: Bioclogging
55270e6ea0b0.sentence: Bioclogging or biological clogging refers to the blockage of pore space in soil by microbial biomass, including active cells and their byproducts such as extracellular polymeric substance (EPS).

c23160005af4.title: Soil compaction
c23160005af4.sentence: In geotechnical engineering, soil compaction is the process in which stress applied to a soil causes densification as air is displaced from the pores between the soil grains.

ff33d11c1aa5.title: Soil compaction
ff33d11c1aa5.sentence: When stress is applied that causes densification due to water (or other liquid) being displaced from between the soil grains, then consolidation, not compaction, has occurred.

abf375585d07.title: Soil compaction
abf375585d07.sentence: In soil science and agronomy, soil compaction is usually a combination of both engineering compaction and consolidation, so may occur due to a lack of water in the soil, the applied stress being internal suction due to water evaporation as well as due to passage of animal feet.

ffd788a4948c.title: Soil compaction
ffd788a4948c.sentence: Normally, compaction is the result of heavy machinery compressing the soil, but it can also occur due to the passage of, for example, animal feet.

7ba6f666d124.title: Soil compaction
7ba6f666d124.sentence: Affected soils become less able to absorb rainfall, thus increasing runoff and erosion.

beef852aebcf.title: Soil compaction
beef852aebcf.sentence: Plants have difficulty in compacted soil because the mineral grains are pressed together, leaving little space for air and water, which are essential for root growth.

0dcb7c53f053.title: Soil compaction
0dcb7c53f053.sentence: Burrowing animals also find it a hostile environment, because the denser soil is more difficult to penetrate.

835650b27617.sentence: Like other well-drained Ultisols, it is ideal for urban development; however, in common with other kaolinite-dominated clays, it has little ability to recover from soil compaction.

ce1655a43b7e.title: Soil compaction (agriculture)
ce1655a43b7e.sentence: Soil compaction, also known as soil structure degradation, is the increase of bulk density or decrease in porosity of soil due to externally or internally applied loads.

d3141a5f4447.title: Soil compaction (agriculture)
d3141a5f4447.sentence: Compaction can adversely affect nearly all physical, chemical and biological properties and functions of soil.

eef2df1f2cf8.title: Soil compaction (agriculture)
eef2df1f2cf8.sentence: Together with soil erosion, it is regarded as the "costliest and most serious environmental problem caused by conventional agriculture."

914b6a00e0a0.title: Soil compaction (agriculture)
914b6a00e0a0.sentence: External pressure due to the use of heavy machinery and inappropriate soil management can lead to the compaction of subsoil, creating impermeable layers within the soil that restrict water and nutrient cycles.

65c1904c456c.title: Soil compaction (agriculture)
65c1904c456c.sentence: Unlike salinization or erosion, soil compaction is principally a sub-surface problem and therefore an invisible phenomenon.

481441e90556.title: Soil compaction (agriculture)
481441e90556.sentence: Special identification methods are necessary to locate, monitor and manage the problem appropriately.

e0a368db7dd7.title: Soil compaction (agriculture)
e0a368db7dd7.sentence: This process can cause on-site effects such as reduced crop growth, yield and quality as well as off-site effects such as increased surface water run-off, soil erosion, greenhouse gas emissions, eutrophication, reduced groundwater recharge and a loss of biodiversity.

ff49261ea6dc.title: Soil compaction (agriculture)

25674387ad0f.title: Soil compaction (agriculture)

00849410a9f7.sentence: 33 million ha affected), Africa (18 million ha), Asia (10 million ha), Australia (4 million ha), and some areas of North America.

fd52a504cdea.sentence: More specifically, in Europe approximately 32% and 18% of the subsoils are highly and moderately vulnerable to compaction respectively.

7ef26a1c295d.sentence: Pore water pressure (sometimes abbreviated to pwp) refers to the pressure of groundwater held within a soil or rock, in gaps between particles (pores).

71de46b71086.sentence: Pore water pressures below the phreatic level of the groundwater are measured with piezometers.

cdde808c10fe.title: Void ratio

cdde808c10fe.sentence: Under loading, voids in the soil skeleton tend to decrease (shrinkage), increasing the contact between adjacent particles and modifying the soil effective stress.

e6ba3da6b7b9.title: Void ratio
e6ba3da6b7b9.section: Applications in soil sciences and geomechanics
e6ba3da6b7b9.sentence: The opposite situation, i. e. when the void ratio is relatively small (dense soils), indicates that the volume of the soil is vulnerable to increase (swelling) under unloading – the smectite (montmorillonite, bentonite) partially dry clay particles present in an unsaturated soil can swell due to their hydration after contact with water (when the saturated/unsaturated conditions fluctuate in a soil).

f92358ca8743.title: Void ratio

f92358ca8743.sentence: Loose soils show a high hydraulic conductivity, while dense soils are less permeable.

9b8aa8316e3e.sentence: In contrast, in dense soil, finer particles cannot freely pass the smaller pores, which leads to the clogging of the porosity.

42cd8fc48cbf.sentence: For a given soil, the greater the void ratio, the higher the value of the coefficient of permeability.

15c6fd86d568.title: Effective stress
15c6fd86d568.sentence: Effective stress is a fundamental concept in soil mechanics and geotechnical engineering that describes the portion of total stress in a soil mass that is carried by the solid soil skeleton, rather than the pore water.

52b079da572a.title: Effective stress
52b079da572a.sentence: The effective stress (σ′) acting on a soil is calculated from the total normal stress (σ) and pore water pressure (u) according to:

8ef8ecd04d72.title: Effective stress
8ef8ecd04d72.sentence: Karl von Terzaghi first proposed the relationship for effective stress in 1925.

97532c3aba2d.title: Soil mechanics
97532c3aba2d.section: Effective stress and capillarity: hydrostatic conditions
97532c3aba2d.sentence: The principle of effective stress, introduced by Karl Terzaghi, states that the effective stress σ' (i.e., the average intergranular stress between solid particles) may be calculated by a simple subtraction of the pore pressure from the total stress:

1f98a2b0017e.title: Effective stress
1f98a2b0017e.sentence: It is crucial for understanding the mechanical behaviour of porous media, as effective stress governs both their strength and volume change (deformation).

fc131c17edad.title: Effective stress
fc131c17edad.sentence: This concept applies broadly to granular media like sand, silt, and clay, as well as to porous materials such as rock, concrete, metal powders and biological tissues.

4c52457d7547.title: Effective stress
4c52457d7547.sentence: This is because soil strength is due primarily to interparticle friction, which - similar to the concept of a block sliding on a table - is proportional to the normal stress.

3df15f81187d.title: Effective stress
3df15f81187d.sentence: The pore water pressure reduces the normal stress and thus reduces the soil strength.

0f2a07fd67c7.title: Soil mechanics
0f2a07fd67c7.section: Effective stress and capillarity: hydrostatic conditions
0f2a07fd67c7.sentence: Although the pore air is relatively compressible, and hence takes little normal stress in most geotechnical problems, liquid water is relatively incompressible and if the voids are saturated with water, the pore water must be squeezed out in order to pack the particles closer together.

a33700f8ca68.title: Soil mechanics
a33700f8ca68.section: Effective stress and capillarity: hydrostatic conditions > Total stress
a33700f8ca68.sentence: For level ground conditions, the total vertical stress at a point, σv, on average, is the weight of everything above that point per unit area.

8eb1abdff4c5.title: Soil mechanics

8eb1abdff4c5.sentence: Total stress increases with increasing depth in proportion to the density of the overlying soil.

2b1ba607d7b4.title: Effective stress

c8d19d0d9712.title: Effective stress
