c7e32875e2d9.title: Effective stress
c7e32875e2d9.sentence: Two extremes of this effect are quicksand, where the groundwater gradient and seepage force act against gravity; and the "sandcastle effect", where the water drainage and capillary action act to strengthen the sand.

2b81a8ec5303.title: Effective stress
2b81a8ec5303.sentence: As well, effective stress plays an important role in slope stability, and other geotechnical engineering and engineering geology problems, such as groundwater-related subsidence.

cdc7c32524b3.title: Effective stress
cdc7c32524b3.sentence: In 1962, work by Jeremiah Jennings and John Burland examined the applicability of Terzaghi’s effective stress principle to partly saturated soils.

e113cb8b6a74.title: Effective stress
e113cb8b6a74.sentence: Through a series of experiments undertaken at the University of the Witwatersrand, including oedometer and compression tests on various soil types, they showed that behaviours such as volume changes and shear strength in partly saturated soils do not align with predictions based on effective stress changes alone.

a716a5e825a5.title: Seepage
a716a5e825a5.sentence: In soil mechanics, seepage is the movement of water through soil.

a6bd31fbf2df.title: Seepage
a6bd31fbf2df.sentence: If fluid pressures in a soil deposit are uniformly increasing with depth according to u=ρwgzw, where zw is the depth below the water table, then hydrostatic conditions will prevail and the fluids will not be flowing through the soil.

7c035215c66b.title: Seepage
7c035215c66b.sentence: However, if the water table is sloping or there is a perched water table as indicated in the accompanying sketch, then seepage will occur.

c80ca470d9cb.title: Seepage
c80ca470d9cb.sentence: Darcy's law states that the volume of flow of the pore fluid through a porous medium per unit time is proportional to the rate of change of excess fluid pressure with distance.

e0a18f379c4b.title: Seepage
e0a18f379c4b.sentence: The constant of proportionality includes the viscosity of the fluid and the intrinsic permeability of the soil.

2b472b470276.title: Seepage
2b472b470276.sentence: Values of hydraulic conductivity, k, can vary by many orders of magnitude depending on the soil type.

92fcd30a989f.title: Seepage
92fcd30a989f.sentence: Clays may have hydraulic conductivity as small as about 10−12ms, gravels may have hydraulic conductivity up to about 10−1ms.

adff96d5ee8d.title: Seepage
adff96d5ee8d.sentence: For steady state seepage, the seepage velocities are not varying with time.

0134d79470cb.title: Seepage
0134d79470cb.sentence: If the water tables are changing levels with time, or if the soil is in the process of consolidation, then steady state conditions do not apply.

dc31cc781b18.title: Seepage
dc31cc781b18.sentence: Seepage in an upward direction reduces the effective stress within the soil.

5c3f815dd617.title: Seepage
5c3f815dd617.sentence: For a surface layer, the vertical effective stress becomes zero within the layer when the upward hydraulic gradient is equal to the critical gradient.

e272c176988c.title: Seepage
e272c176988c.sentence: At zero effective stress soil has very little strength and layers of relatively impermeable soil may heave up due to the underlying water pressures.

9995d442c574.title: Seepage
9995d442c574.sentence: The condition of zero effective stress associated with upward seepage is also called liquefaction, quicksand, or a boiling condition.

3232249bae88.title: Seepage
3232249bae88.sentence: The loss in strength due to upward seepage is a common contributor to levee failures.

ba02db51dc09.title: Seepage
ba02db51dc09.sentence: When the seepage velocity is great enough, erosion can occur because of the frictional drag exerted on the soil particles.

49ef5f5dd13c.title: Seepage
49ef5f5dd13c.sentence: Seeping water removes soil, starting from the exit point of the seepage, and erosion advances upgradient.

1421000188a6.title: Seepage
1421000188a6.sentence: Erosion of the soil, known as "soil piping", can lead to failure of the structure and to sinkhole formation.

c9f144ec150a.title: Alkali soil
c9f144ec150a.sentence: Note: Certain clay minerals with almost 100% 'exchangeable sodium percentage' (ESP) (i.e. almost fully sodium saturated) are called bentonite, which is used in civil engineering to place impermeable curtains in the soil, e.g. below dams, to prevent seepage of water.

cc0ea7add6de.title: Shear strength (soil)
cc0ea7add6de.sentence: Shear strength is a term used in soil mechanics to describe the magnitude of the shear stress that a soil can sustain.

ecce607037fc.title: Shear strength (soil)
ecce607037fc.sentence: The shear resistance of soil is a result of friction and interlocking of particles, and possibly cementation or bonding of particle contacts.

d03e06b0d760.title: Soil mechanics
d03e06b0d760.section: Shear behavior: stiffness and strength > Friction, interlocking and dilation
d03e06b0d760.sentence: The shear strength of soil is primarily due to interparticle friction and therefore, the shear resistance on a plane is approximately proportional to the effective normal stress on that plane.

453f31a55f7b.title: Soil mechanics
453f31a55f7b.section: Shear behavior: stiffness and strength > Friction, interlocking and dilation
453f31a55f7b.sentence: The angle of internal friction is thus closely related to the maximum stable slope angle, often called the angle of repose.

e2b7e5c24a32.title: Shear strength (soil)
e2b7e5c24a32.sentence: The shear strength of soil depends on the effective stress, the drainage conditions, the density of the particles, the rate of strain, and the direction of the strain.

6d2d69d9dd55.title: Shear strength (soil)
6d2d69d9dd55.sentence: Due to interlocking, particulate material may expand or contract in volume as it is subject to shear strains.

8056ddddae82.title: Shear strength (soil)
8056ddddae82.sentence: If soil expands its volume, the density of particles will decrease and the strength will decrease; in this case, the peak strength would be followed by a reduction of shear stress.

67e0e63b567f.title: Shear strength (soil)
67e0e63b567f.sentence: The theoretical state at which the shear stress and density remain constant while the shear strain increases may be called the critical state, steady state, or residual strength.

2f078e718b3f.title: Shear strength (soil)
2f078e718b3f.sentence: If water is not allowed to flow in or out of the soil, the stress path is called an undrained stress path.

e2420ccc725c.title: Shear strength (soil)
e2420ccc725c.sentence: During undrained shear, if the particles are surrounded by a nearly incompressible fluid such as water, then the density of the particles cannot change without drainage, but the water pressure and effective stress will change.

37640708ea5e.title: Shear strength (soil)
37640708ea5e.sentence: In reality, soil is partially drained, somewhere between the perfectly undrained and drained idealized conditions.

c200fb934799.title: Soil mechanics
c200fb934799.sentence: Knowledge of the strength is necessary to determine if a slope will be stable, if a building or bridge might settle too far into the ground, and the limiting pressures on a retaining wall.

755673e60049.title: Shear strength (soil)
755673e60049.sentence: For undrained, constant volume shearing, the Tresca theory may be used to predict the shear strength, but for drained conditions, the Mohr–Coulomb theory may be used.

26b280f96543.title: Shear strength (soil)
26b280f96543.sentence: Two important theories of soil shear are the critical state theory and the steady state theory.

6f200656c5b6.title: Soil liquefaction
6f200656c5b6.sentence: Soil liquefaction occurs when a cohesionless saturated or partially saturated soil substantially loses strength and stiffness in response to an applied stress such as shaking during an earthquake or other sudden change in stress condition, in which material that is ordinarily a solid behaves like a liquid, a sudden physical change termed thixotropy.

9e2fcd1cc9a2.title: Soil liquefaction
9e2fcd1cc9a2.sentence: This is because a loose sand has a tendency to compress when a load is applied.

53d463df094c.title: Soil liquefaction
53d463df094c.sentence: In response to soil compressing, the pore water pressure increases and the water attempts to flow out from the soil to zones of low pressure (usually upward towards the ground surface).

e445632b078c.title: Soil liquefaction
e445632b078c.sentence: However, if the loading is rapidly applied and large enough, or is repeated many times (e.g., earthquake shaking, storm wave loading) such that the water does not flow out before the next cycle of load is applied, the water pressures may build to the extent that it exceeds the force (contact stresses) between the grains of soil that keep them in contact.

a83262ad3764.title: Soil liquefaction
a83262ad3764.sentence: Soil liquefaction occurs when the effective stress (shear strength) of soil is reduced to essentially zero.

5ff2f0a9f9f5.title: Soil liquefaction
5ff2f0a9f9f5.sentence: Dense sands, by contrast, tend to expand in volume or 'dilate'.

23de445078dc.title: Soil liquefaction
23de445078dc.sentence: Liquefaction is more likely to occur in sandy or non-plastic silty soils but may in rare cases occur in gravels and clays (see quick clay).

c105c07ab434.title: Soil liquefaction
c105c07ab434.sentence: Liquefaction is more likely to occur in loose to moderately saturated granular soils with poor drainage, such as silty sands or sands and gravels containing impermeable sediments.

116b0fb1f7e3.title: Soil liquefaction
116b0fb1f7e3.sentence: Deposits most susceptible to liquefaction are young (Holocene-age, deposited within the last 10,000 years) sands and silts of similar grain size (well-sorted), in beds at least metres thick, and saturated with water.

02cfd63f2586.title: Soil liquefaction
02cfd63f2586.sentence: Such deposits are often found along stream beds, beaches, dunes, and areas where windblown silt (loess) and sand have accumulated.

b622398d2732.title: Soil liquefaction
b622398d2732.sentence: In soil mechanics, the term "liquefied" was first used by Allen Hazen in reference to the 1918 failure of the Calaveras Dam in California.

6a9ee1ed86b0.title: Soil liquefaction
6a9ee1ed86b0.sentence: Although the effects of soil liquefaction have been long understood, engineers took more notice after the 1964 Alaska earthquake and 1964 Niigata earthquake.

c03ef0db8b7b.title: Soil liquefaction
c03ef0db8b7b.sentence: Pressures generated during large earthquakes can force underground water and liquefied sand to the surface.

7683ed615b27.title: Soil liquefaction
7683ed615b27.sentence: This can be observed at the surface as effects known alternatively as "sand boils", "sand blows" or "sand volcanoes".

39947954acd9.title: Soil liquefaction
39947954acd9.sentence: The failure of ground in this manner is called 'lateral spreading' and may occur on very shallow slopes with angles only 1 or 2 degrees from the horizontal.

5365aa5b4701.title: Soil liquefaction
5365aa5b4701.sentence: Buildings whose foundations bear directly on sand which liquefies will experience a sudden loss of support, which will result in drastic and irregular settlement of the building causing structural damage, including cracking of foundations and damage to the building structure, or leaving the structure unserviceable, even without structural damage.

8c96814edde4.title: Soil liquefaction
8c96814edde4.sentence: Sloping ground and ground next to rivers and lakes may slide on a liquefied soil layer (termed 'lateral spreading'), opening large ground fissures, and can cause significant damage to buildings, bridges, roads and services such as water, natural gas, sewerage, electric power and telecommunications installed in the affected ground.

0b75b14b6b17.title: Soil liquefaction
0b75b14b6b17.sentence: Earth embankments such as flood levees and earth dams may lose stability or collapse if the material comprising the embankment or its foundation liquefies.

a2ab1a8e3b7e.title: Soil liquefaction
a2ab1a8e3b7e.sentence: Resulting soil liquefaction buried the suburb of Balaroa and Petobo village 3 metres (9.8 ft) deep in mud during the 2018 Palu earthquake.

817d6eed19b4.title: Soil liquefaction
817d6eed19b4.sentence: Over geological time, liquefaction of soil material due to earthquakes could provide a dense parent material in which the fragipan may develop through pedogenesis.

dee7eda407e4.title: Soil liquefaction
dee7eda407e4.sentence: Mitigation methods have been devised by earthquake engineers and include various soil compaction techniques such as vibro compaction (compaction of the soil by depth vibrators), dynamic compaction, and vibro stone columns.

9021454170e3.title: Soil liquefaction
9021454170e3.sentence: These methods densify soil and enable buildings to avoid soil liquefaction.

0c6e0e2a2fe1.title: Soil liquefaction
0c6e0e2a2fe1.sentence: Existing buildings can be mitigated by injecting grout into the soil to stabilize the layer of soil that is subject to liquefaction.

3fbda8a9ab7c.title: Microbiologically induced calcite precipitation
3fbda8a9ab7c.sentence: Microbial induced calcium carbonate precipitation has been proposed as an alternative cementation technique to improve the properties of potentially liquefiable sand.

5233502683f0.title: Soil liquefaction
5233502683f0.sentence: On 28 September 2018, an earthquake of 7.5 magnitude hit the Central Sulawesi province of Indonesia.

c50b0d779891.title: Cohesion (geology)
c50b0d779891.sentence: Cohesion is the component of shear strength of a rock or soil that is independent of interparticle friction.

c593a718db27.title: Cohesion (geology)
c593a718db27.sentence: In soils, true cohesion is caused by following:

d30e6110f80a.title: Cohesion (geology)
d30e6110f80a.sentence: - Electrostatic forces in stiff overconsolidated clays (which may be lost through weathering)

f759c7aa7883.title: Cohesion (geology)
f759c7aa7883.sentence: - Cementing by Fe2O3, Ca CO3, Na Cl, etc.

62e8a1476115.title: Cohesion (geology)
62e8a1476115.sentence: - Negative capillary pressure (which is lost upon wetting)

5de35179fd3b.title: Cohesion (geology)
5de35179fd3b.sentence: - Pore pressure response during undrained loading (which is lost through time)

c7572d17a2a4.title: Cohesion (geology)
c7572d17a2a4.sentence: - Root cohesion (which may be lost through logging or fire of the contributing plants, or through solution)

dbbca36dabc6.title: Cohesion (geology)
dbbca36dabc6.sentence: Cohesion (alternatively called the cohesive strength) is typically measured on the basis of Mohr–Coulomb theory.

30e91d0934c7.title: Soil sloughing
30e91d0934c7.sentence: According to the Mohr-Coulomb equation, the cohesion of a soil is defined as the shear strength at zero normal pressure on the surface of failure.

6b377316eed2.sentence: Table: Cohesive strength (c) for some materials

c397ee441968.title: Soil sloughing
c397ee441968.sentence: Soil sloughing is soil falling off banks and slopes due to a loss in cohesion.

430370706ee3.title: Quicksand
430370706ee3.sentence: Quicksand, also known as sinking sand, is a colloid consisting of fine granular material (such as sand, silt or clay) and water.

87aedb02c45f.title: Quicksand
87aedb02c45f.sentence: It forms in saturated loose sand when the sand is suddenly agitated.

98b39835fc21.title: Quicksand
98b39835fc21.sentence: When water in the sand cannot escape, it creates a liquefied soil that loses strength and cannot support weight.

5583c037a2c5.title: Quicksand
5583c037a2c5.sentence: Quicksand can form in standing water or in upward flowing water (as from an artesian spring).

323a1655c2bd.title: Quicksand
323a1655c2bd.sentence: In the case of upward-flowing water, forces oppose the force of gravity and suspend the soil particle.

ac4a1ff06c1a.title: Quicksand
ac4a1ff06c1a.sentence: Quicksand is a shear thinning non-Newtonian fluid: when undisturbed, it often appears to be solid ("gel" form), but a less than 1% change in the stress on the quicksand will cause a sudden decrease in its viscosity ("sol" form).

abdc2ff41050.title: Quicksand
abdc2ff41050.sentence: Quicksand has a density of about 2 grams per cubic centimeter, whereas the density of the human body is only about 1 gram per cubic centimeter.

dc1d67b3c907.title: Quicksand
dc1d67b3c907.sentence: At that level of density, sinking beyond about waist height in quicksand is impossible.

13e65bf2ee6f.title: Quicksand
13e65bf2ee6f.sentence: It is impossible for a human to sink entirely into quicksand, due to the higher density of the fluid.

ededdd671385.title: Quicksand
ededdd671385.sentence: The forces required to do this are quite large: to remove a foot from quicksand at a speed of 1 cm/s would require the same amount of force as that needed to lift a car.

a7835b35c1ec.title: Quicksand
a7835b35c1ec.sentence: Quicksand may be escaped by slow movement of the legs in order to increase viscosity of the fluid, and rotation of the body so as to float in the supine position (lying horizontally with the face and torso facing up).

cb1dfef3e82c.title: Soil consolidation
cb1dfef3e82c.sentence: Soil consolidation refers to the mechanical process by which soil changes volume gradually in response to a change in pressure.

dc4fa880d57f.title: Soil consolidation
dc4fa880d57f.sentence: Consolidation is the process in which reduction in volume takes place by the gradual expulsion or absorption of water under long-term static loads.

6980791321b1.title: Soil consolidation
6980791321b1.sentence: When soil saturated with water is subjected to an increase in pressure, the high volumetric stiffness of water compared to the soil matrix means that the water initially absorbs all the change in pressure without changing volume, creating excess pore water pressure.

718f99d5d695.title: Soil consolidation
718f99d5d695.sentence: As water diffuses away from regions of high pressure due to seepage, the soil matrix gradually takes up the pressure change and shrinks in volume.

8d4cac469439.title: Soil consolidation
8d4cac469439.sentence: The process of consolidation is often explained with an idealized system composed of a spring, a container with a hole in its cover, and water.

ce631c525c1f.title: Soil consolidation
ce631c525c1f.sentence: In this system, the spring represents the compressibility or the structure of the soil itself, and the water which fills the container represents the pore water in the soil.

577427496d5c.title: Soil consolidation
577427496d5c.sentence: At this stage, only the water resists the applied load.

d5afa15f79d1.title: Soil consolidation
d5afa15f79d1.sentence: - As soon as the hole is opened, water starts to drain out through the hole and the spring shortens.

986c3737b184.title: Soil consolidation
986c3737b184.sentence: Now, the spring alone resists the applied load.

c13053d456a0.sentence: This is especially true in saturated clays because their hydraulic conductivity is extremely low, and this causes the water to take an exceptionally long time to drain out of the soil.

9ff57abfac7f.title: Soil consolidation
9ff57abfac7f.sentence: Coarse-grained soils do not undergo consolidation settlement due to relatively high hydraulic conductivity compared to clays.

ba13b7d42950.title: Soil consolidation
ba13b7d42950.sentence: Instead, coarse-grained soils undergo the immediate settlement.

19e78d61f84e.title: Soil consolidation
19e78d61f84e.sentence: Clays undergo consolidation settlement not only by the action of external loads (surcharge loads) but also under its own weight or weight of soils that exist above the clay.

e0c2fe97c29d.title: Soil consolidation
e0c2fe97c29d.sentence: Clays also undergo settlement when dewatered (groundwater pumping) because the effective stress on the clay increases.

49a04a8e0224.title: Soil consolidation
49a04a8e0224.sentence: The effects of consolidation are most conspicuous where a building sits over a layer of soil with low stiffness and low permeability, such as marine clay, leading to large settlement over many years.

fe613d9c21b1.title: Soil consolidation
fe613d9c21b1.sentence: In the narrow sense, "consolidation" refers strictly to this delayed volumetric response to pressure change due to gradual movement of water.

33b1cf23e50e.title: Soil consolidation
33b1cf23e50e.sentence: Some publications also use "consolidation" in the broad sense, to refer to any process by which soil changes volume due to a change in applied pressure.

ed2fd39a78ad.title: Soil consolidation
ed2fd39a78ad.sentence: This broader definition encompasses the overall concept of soil compaction, subsidence, and heave.

8af292ee20ab.title: Soil consolidation
8af292ee20ab.sentence: More generally, consolidation refers to the process by which soils change volume in response to a change in pressure, encompassing both compaction and swelling.

f9516bd5d2ef.title: Soil consolidation
f9516bd5d2ef.sentence: According to the "father of soil mechanics", Karl von Terzaghi, consolidation is "any process which involves a decrease in water content of saturated soil without replacement of water by air".

30b329f41507.title: Soil consolidation
30b329f41507.sentence: In an oedometer test, a series of known pressures are applied to a thin disc of soil sample, and the change of sample thickness with time is recorded.

c91a649a5c89.title: Soil consolidation
c91a649a5c89.sentence: This allows the consolidation characteristics of the soil to be quantified in terms of the coefficient of consolidation (Cv) and hydraulic conductivity (K).

eeb2a5b6d718.title: Angle of repose
eeb2a5b6d718.sentence: The angle of repose, or critical angle of repose, of a granular material is the steepest angle of descent or dip relative to the horizontal plane on which the material can be piled without slumping.

d14affc63f0f.title: Angle of repose
d14affc63f0f.sentence: At this angle, the material on the slope face is on the verge of sliding.

e9add2340196.title: Angle of repose
e9add2340196.sentence: The morphology of the material affects the angle of repose; smooth, rounded sand grains cannot be piled as steeply as can rough, interlocking sands.

f09ffcd932a6.title: Angle of repose
f09ffcd932a6.sentence: As the roundness of materials increases, the angle of repose decreases since there is less friction between the soil grains.

b2317e0fc3d0.title: Angle of repose
b2317e0fc3d0.sentence: If a small amount of water is able to bridge the gaps between particles, electrostatic attraction of the water to mineral surfaces increases the angle of repose and related quantities such as the soil strength.

47e8e33bef2c.title: Slope stability
47e8e33bef2c.sentence: However, water saturation can result in a decrease in the slope's stability since it acts as a lubricant and creates a detachment where mass wasting can occur.

87dcadff0024.title: Aeolian processes
87dcadff0024.section: Deposition > Ripples and other small-scale features
87dcadff0024.sentence: Here the sand builds up to the angle of repose (the maximum stable slope angle), about 34 degrees, then begins sliding down the slip face of the patch.

3551c3e2a61d.title: Geotechnical engineering
3551c3e2a61d.sentence: Henri Gautier, a French royal engineer, recognized the "natural slope" of different soils in 1717, an idea later known as the soil's angle of repose.

fba04b237615.title: Angle of repose
fba04b237615.sentence: When the angle of repose is exceeded, mass wasting and rockfall can occur.

91552b0cf8d4.title: Retaining wall
91552b0cf8d4.sentence: The structure is constructed to resist the lateral pressure of soil when there is a desired change in ground elevation that exceeds the angle of repose of the soil.

49c2a63fc8a6.title: Soil mechanics

49c2a63fc8a6.sentence: Due to surface tension, water will rise up in a small capillary tube above a free surface of water.

175245ae57bb.title: Soil mechanics
175245ae57bb.section: Effective stress and capillarity: hydrostatic conditions > Pore water pressure > Capillary action
175245ae57bb.sentence: Likewise, water will rise up above the water table into the small pore spaces around the soil particles.

23c2205e3d53.title: Soil mechanics
23c2205e3d53.section: Effective stress and capillarity: hydrostatic conditions > Pore water pressure > Capillary action
23c2205e3d53.sentence: Hence, hydrostatic water pressures are negative above the water table.

6128fa48aab3.title: Soil mechanics
6128fa48aab3.section: Effective stress and capillarity: hydrostatic conditions > Pore water pressure > Capillary action
6128fa48aab3.sentence: In fact the soil may be completely saturated for some distance above the water table.

b4cb5d58e300.title: Soil mechanics
b4cb5d58e300.section: Effective stress and capillarity: hydrostatic conditions > Pore water pressure > Capillary action
b4cb5d58e300.sentence: Above the height of capillary saturation, the soil may be wet but the water content will decrease with elevation.

831605ae13d6.title: Soil mechanics
831605ae13d6.section: Effective stress and capillarity: hydrostatic conditions > Pore water pressure > Capillary action
831605ae13d6.sentence: The thickness of the zone of capillary saturation depends on the pore size, but typically, the heights vary between a centimeter or so for coarse sand to tens of meters for a silt or clay.

e7d8577b294a.title: Soil mechanics
e7d8577b294a.section: Effective stress and capillarity: hydrostatic conditions > Pore water pressure > Capillary action
e7d8577b294a.sentence: Considering the effective stress equation, σ′=σ−u, if the water pressure is negative, the effective stress may be positive, even on a free surface (a surface where the total normal stress is zero).

31513dfa9d6e.title: Soil mechanics
31513dfa9d6e.section: Effective stress and capillarity: hydrostatic conditions > Pore water pressure > Capillary action
31513dfa9d6e.sentence: The negative pore pressure pulls the particles together and causes compressive particle to particle contact forces.

e49f21a8bec9.title: Soil mechanics
e49f21a8bec9.section: Effective stress and capillarity: hydrostatic conditions > Pore water pressure > Capillary action
e49f21a8bec9.sentence: The surface tension of water explains why the water does not drain out of a wet sand castle or a moist ball of clay.

1b1410a61187.title: Soil mechanics
1b1410a61187.section: Effective stress and capillarity: hydrostatic conditions > Pore water pressure > Capillary action
1b1410a61187.sentence: Negative water pressures make the water stick to the particles and pull the particles to each other, friction at the particle contacts make a sand castle stable.

fcb430017dc6.title: Soil mechanics
fcb430017dc6.section: Effective stress and capillarity: hydrostatic conditions > Pore water pressure > Capillary action
fcb430017dc6.sentence: But as soon as a wet sand castle is submerged below a free water surface, the negative pressures are lost and the castle collapses.

4623439af811.title: Soil mechanics
4623439af811.section: Effective stress and capillarity: hydrostatic conditions > Pore water pressure > Capillary action
4623439af811.sentence: Negative pore pressures in clayey soil can be much more powerful than those in sand.

56d4509e5feb.title: Soil mechanics
56d4509e5feb.section: Effective stress and capillarity: hydrostatic conditions > Pore water pressure > Capillary action
56d4509e5feb.sentence: Negative pore pressures explain why clay soils shrink when they dry and swell as they are wetted.

74e0d980ef17.title: Soil mechanics
74e0d980ef17.section: Effective stress and capillarity: hydrostatic conditions > Pore water pressure > Capillary action
74e0d980ef17.sentence: The swelling and shrinkage can cause major distress, especially to light structures and roads.

27f3a27d61fc.title: Geotechnical engineering
27f3a27d61fc.sentence: Geotechnical engineering, also known as geotechnics, is the branch of civil engineering concerned with the engineering behavior of earth materials.

11d5785d5b0e.title: Geotechnical engineering
11d5785d5b0e.sentence: It uses the principles of soil mechanics and rock mechanics to solve its engineering problems.

2390c3fea65b.title: Geotechnical engineering
2390c3fea65b.sentence: It also relies on knowledge of geology, hydrology, geophysics, and other related sciences.

3105de70b3de.title: Geotechnical engineering
3105de70b3de.sentence: The fields of geotechnical engineering and engineering geology have overlapping knowledge areas.

03ab81ecca95.title: Geotechnical engineering
03ab81ecca95.sentence: However, while geotechnical engineering is a specialty of civil engineering, engineering geology is a specialty of geology.

5cef3b57d33e.title: Geotechnical engineering
5cef3b57d33e.sentence: Until the 18th century, however, no theoretical basis for soil design had been developed, and the discipline was more of an art than a science, relying on experience.

e3e11f80bab1.title: Geotechnical engineering
e3e11f80bab1.sentence: Several foundation-related engineering problems, such as the Leaning Tower of Pisa, prompted scientists to begin taking a more scientific approach to examining the subsurface.

6a4bb42aeec0.title: Geotechnical engineering
6a4bb42aeec0.sentence: The application of the principles of mechanics to soils was documented as early as 1773 when Charles Coulomb, a physicist and engineer, developed improved methods to determine the earth pressures against military ramparts.

44251f333f4a.title: Geotechnical engineering
44251f333f4a.sentence: Coulomb observed that, at failure, a distinct slip plane would form behind a sliding retaining wall and suggested that the maximum shear stress on the slip plane, for design purposes, was the sum of the soil cohesion, c, and friction σ tan⁡(ϕ), where σ is the normal stress on the slip plane and ϕ is the friction angle of the soil.

1f91ad1d9b66.title: Geotechnical engineering
1f91ad1d9b66.sentence: In the 19th century, Henry Darcy developed what is now known as Darcy's law, describing the flow of fluids in a porous media.

60af6d6862d0.title: Geotechnical engineering
60af6d6862d0.sentence: Albert Atterberg developed the clay consistency indices that are still used today for soil classification.

e01b83375bbd.title: Geotechnical engineering
e01b83375bbd.sentence: In 1885, Osborne Reynolds recognized that shearing causes volumetric dilation of dense materials and contraction of loose granular materials.

ca4c34db54d7.title: Geotechnical engineering
ca4c34db54d7.sentence: Modern geotechnical engineering is said to have begun in 1925 with the publication of Erdbaumechanik by Karl von Terzaghi, a mechanical engineer and geologist.

b1839ce1a6db.title: Geotechnical engineering
b1839ce1a6db.sentence: Considered by many to be the father of modern soil mechanics and geotechnical engineering, Terzaghi developed the principle of effective stress, and demonstrated that the shear strength of soil is controlled by effective stress.

dee99fcd313b.title: Geotechnical engineering
dee99fcd313b.sentence: Terzaghi also developed the framework for theories of bearing capacity of foundations, and the theory for prediction of the rate of settlement of clay layers due to consolidation.

9ef98ab83fff.title: Geotechnical engineering
9ef98ab83fff.sentence: Roscoe, Schofield, and Wroth, with the publication of On the Yielding of Soils in 1958, established the interrelationships between the volume change behavior (dilation, contraction, and consolidation) and shearing behavior with the theory of plasticity using critical state soil mechanics.

ddd1d1653dbe.title: Geotechnical engineering
ddd1d1653dbe.sentence: Critical state soil mechanics is the basis for many contemporary advanced constitutive models describing the behavior of soil.

97905c73efe5.title: Geotechnical engineering
97905c73efe5.sentence: The primary considerations for a geotechnical engineer in foundation design are bearing capacity, settlement, and ground movement beneath the foundations.

e9219664a235.title: Geotechnical engineering
e9219664a235.sentence: Geotechnical engineers design foundations based on the load characteristics of the structure and the properties of the soils and bedrock at the site.

afad8ef25824.title: Overburden pressure
afad8ef25824.sentence: Overburden pressure is a geology term that denotes the pressure caused by the weight of the overlying layers of material at a specific depth under the earth's surface.

91cfdc1b6b11.title: Overburden pressure
91cfdc1b6b11.sentence: Overburden pressure is also called lithostatic pressure, or vertical stress.

1b8976a9901c.title: Overburden pressure

f2631e647f22.sentence: - ρ(z) is the density of the material above the depth z.

767ce2d8e8e4.title: Overburden pressure
767ce2d8e8e4.sentence: The average geobaric gradient corresponds to about 270 bar/km in the crust and 330 bar/km in the mantle.

b280367988f4.title: Overburden pressure
b280367988f4.sentence: Lithostatic pressure increases with depth and produces reduction of rock porosity.

72fc069ba821.title: Overburden pressure
72fc069ba821.sentence: It causes a reduction in volume without differential deformation, whereas directional pressures favour deformation of materials.

39e0d4d13001.title: Overburden pressure
39e0d4d13001.sentence: Lithostatic pressure is important in metamorphic and diagenetic processes.

1efc6b10287d.title: Overburden pressure
1efc6b10287d.sentence: By contrast, it is not easy to experimentally determine and estimate the value of horizontal stresses at a depth z.

8e3ebab631da.title: River bank failure
8e3ebab631da.sentence: Popout failure is when small to medium-sized blocks are forced out at or near the base of the river bank due to excessive pore water pressure and overburden.

3c4ad9e5c9fd.title: Oedometer test
3c4ad9e5c9fd.sentence: An oedometer test is a kind of geotechnical investigation performed in geotechnical engineering that measures a soil's consolidation properties.

8aecfda81024.title: Oedometer test
8aecfda81024.sentence: Oedometer tests are performed by applying different loads to a soil sample and measuring the deformation response.

a294ad4548b4.title: Oedometer test
a294ad4548b4.sentence: Oedometer tests are designed to simulate the one-dimensional deformation and drainage conditions that soils experience in the field.

25348efcd050.title: Oedometer test
25348efcd050.sentence: The results from these tests are used to predict how a soil in the field will deform in response to a change in effective stress.

803b2e8d1ccd.title: Oedometer test
803b2e8d1ccd.sentence: The soil sample in an oedometer test is typically a circular disc of diameter-to-height ratio of about 3:1.

c506b5cb45ab.title: Oedometer test
c506b5cb45ab.sentence: The sample is held in a rigid confining ring, which prevents lateral displacement of the soil sample, but allows the sample to swell or compress vertically in response to changes in applied load.

3da792294fa6.title: Oedometer test
3da792294fa6.sentence: For samples that are saturated with water, porous stones are placed on the top and bottom of the sample to allow drainage in the vertical direction, and the entire sample is submerged in water to prevent drying.

3388e84ea660.title: Oedometer test
3388e84ea660.sentence: Saturated soil samples exhibit the phenomenon of consolidation, whereby the soil's volume changes gradually to give a delayed response to the change in applied confining stresses.

d36add994dfd.title: Oedometer test
d36add994dfd.sentence: This typically takes minutes or hours to complete in an oedometer and the change of sample thickness with time is recorded, providing measurements of the coefficient of consolidation and the permeability of the soil.

8a5327704ec7.title: Oedometer test
8a5327704ec7.sentence: The most common type is the incremental loading (IL) test.

78be76011c32.title: Oedometer test
78be76011c32.sentence: By observing the deflection value over time data, it can be determined when the sample has reached the end of primary consolidation.

aa7b091d5731.title: Oedometer test
aa7b091d5731.sentence: Another load is then immediately placed on the soil and this process is repeated.

0d049c983fbf.title: Oedometer test
0d049c983fbf.sentence: Using a load increment ratio of 1/2 provides a sufficient number of data points to describe the relationship between void ratio and effective stress for a soil.

618b7b5a270f.title: Oedometer test
618b7b5a270f.sentence: - The effective stress that marks the boundary between stiff and soft deformation response of a soil to loading

c887b180e286.title: Oedometer test
c887b180e286.sentence: - Usually indicative of high loadings in the past from glaciers or eroded layers

a55587601f08.title: Oedometer test
a55587601f08.sentence: - How the soil will change volume (settle) under loads greater than the preconsolidation pressure

7223237b0fdb.title: Oedometer test
7223237b0fdb.sentence: - How the soil will change volume (settle) under loads less than the preconsolidation pressure

ba69353cb601.title: Oedometer test
ba69353cb601.sentence: - How the soil will change volume (settle) under a constant loading

0028bc7b6f23.title: Oedometer test
0028bc7b6f23.sentence: Consolidation experiments were first carried out in 1910 by Frontard.

197867dff64b.title: Oedometer test
197867dff64b.sentence: Karl von Terzaghi started his consolidation research in 1919 at Robert College in Istanbul.

27e1da40778f.title: Oedometer test
27e1da40778f.sentence: Through these experiments, Terzaghi started to develop his theory of consolidation which was eventually published in 1923.

a1a39484ff8b.title: Oedometer test
a1a39484ff8b.sentence: Casagrande's contributions to the technique of oedometer testing includes the "Casagrande method" to estimate the pre-consolidation pressure of a natural soil sample.

89f90ace917c.title: Oedometer test
89f90ace917c.sentence: ASTM D2435 / D2435M - 11 covers oedometer testing by incremental loading.

555bb42ea0a4.title: Oedometer test
555bb42ea0a4.sentence: BS 1377-5:1990 is the relevant British Standard for oedometer testing; the wider BS 1377 series also provides background information and best-practice advice on sample preparation for various geotechnical investigations.

664ec30b3dec.title: Oedometer test
664ec30b3dec.sentence: There are also two ISO standards on oedometer testing: ISO 17892-5:2017 on incremental loading oedometer tests; and BS EN ISO 17892-11:2019 covers various methods of soil permeability testing, including oedometer tests on saturated samples.

758c36b7f869.title: Specific storage
758c36b7f869.sentence: According to Groundwater, by Freeze and Cherry (1979), specific storage, Ss [m−1], of a saturated aquifer is defined as the volume of water that a unit volume of the aquifer releases from storage under a unit decline in hydraulic head.

2998443099d9.title: Specific storage
2998443099d9.sentence: Specific storage is the volume of water released from one unit volume of the aquifer under one unit decline in head.

4f87eb18001d.title: Specific storage
4f87eb18001d.sentence: Storativity or the storage coefficient is the volume of water released from storage per unit decline in hydraulic head in the aquifer, per unit area of the aquifer.

cfdd4aae9f95.title: Specific storage
cfdd4aae9f95.sentence: Storativity is a dimensionless quantity, and is always greater than 0.

8cbc172e30e0.title: Specific storage
8cbc172e30e0.sentence: For a confined aquifer or aquitard, storativity is the vertically integrated specific storage value.

aecc77b8f40a.title: Specific storage
aecc77b8f40a.sentence: This is related to both the compressibility of the aquifer and the compressibility of the water itself.

6338ead75a7e.title: Specific storage
6338ead75a7e.sentence: For an unconfined aquifer, storativity is approximately equal to the specific yield (Sy) since the release from specific storage (Ss) is typically orders of magnitude less (Ssb≪ Sy).

a8a6d763f35f.title: Specific storage
a8a6d763f35f.section: Storativity > Determination of the storage coefficient of aquifer systems > Laboratory consolidation tests
a8a6d763f35f.sentence: Laboratory consolidation tests yield measurements of the coefficient of consolidation within the inelastic range and provide estimates of vertical hydraulic conductivity.

18b569e5a718.title: Specific storage
18b569e5a718.section: Storativity > Determination of the storage coefficient of aquifer systems > Laboratory consolidation tests
18b569e5a718.sentence: The inelastic skeletal specific storage of the sample can be determined by calculating the ratio of vertical hydraulic conductivity to the coefficient of consolidation.

39cb2f28e5ea.title: Specific storage
39cb2f28e5ea.section: Storativity > Determination of the storage coefficient of aquifer systems > Model simulations and calibration
39cb2f28e5ea.sentence: Simulations of land subsidence incorporate data on aquifer-system storage and hydraulic conductivity.

6cf816cce4a1.sentence: where: emax is the "maximum void ratio" corresponding to a very loose state, emin is the "minimum void ratio" corresponding to a very dense state and e is the in situ void ratio.

9d33036106d1.sentence: Thus if Dr=100% the sand or gravel is very dense, and if Dr=0% the soil is extremely loose and unstable.

36f3a853d8be.section: Soil classification > Indices related to soil strength > Relative density
36f3a853d8be.sentence: Methods used to calculate relative density are defined in ASTM D4254-00(2016).

80a9f2f95a5e.section: Measurement > Relative density in soil mechanics
80a9f2f95a5e.sentence: Relative density is defined by DR=emax−eemax−emin×100% in which emax,emin, and e are the maximum, minimum and actual void ratios.

e59b85578791.title: Relative density
e59b85578791.section: Measurement > Relative density in soil mechanics
e59b85578791.sentence: Relative density DR a measure of the current void ratio in relation to the maximum and minimum void ratios, and applied effective stress control the mechanical behavior of cohesionless soil.

4bf150e33392.title: Specific weight
4bf150e33392.sentence: The specific weight, also known as the unit weight (symbol γ, the Greek letter gamma), is a volume-specific quantity defined as the weight W divided by the volume V of a material: γ=WV.

8c80920e1214.title: Specific weight
8c80920e1214.sentence: Equivalently, it may also be formulated as the product of density, ρ, and gravity acceleration, g: γ=ρg.

6e13f84befed.title: Specific weight
6e13f84befed.sentence: Its unit of measurement in the International System of Units (SI) is the newton per cubic metre (N/m3), expressed in terms of base units as kg⋅m−2⋅s−2.

25f0ee0e2b32.title: Specific weight
25f0ee0e2b32.sentence: A commonly used value is the specific weight of water on Earth at 4 °C (39 °F), which is 9.807 kilonewtons per cubic metre or 62.43 pounds-force per cubic foot.

0909ac08f0da.title: Specific weight
0909ac08f0da.sentence: Unlike density, specific weight is not a fixed property of a material, as it depends on the value of the gravitational acceleration, which varies with location (e.g., Earth's gravity).

dd197b0e21f4.title: Specific weight
dd197b0e21f4.sentence: Specific weight is often used as a property of soil to solve earthwork problems.

4fa555660d5a.title: Specific weight
4fa555660d5a.sentence: The unit weight of a soil when void spaces of the soil contain both water and air. γ=(1+w)Gsγw1+e where γ is the moist unit weight of the material γw is the unit weight of water w is the moisture content of the material Gs is the specific gravity of the solid e is the void ratio

d72452d2273d.title: Specific weight
d72452d2273d.sentence: The unit weight of a soil when all void spaces of the soil are completely filled with air, with no water.

fe6b1ee2849e.title: Specific weight
fe6b1ee2849e.sentence: The unit weight of a soil when all void spaces of the soil are completely filled with water, with no air.

3556b3387991.title: Specific weight
3556b3387991.sentence: The formula for dry unit weight is: γd=Gsγw1+e=γ1+w where γ is the moist unit weight of the material γd is the dry unit weight of the material γw is the unit weight of water w is the moisture content of the material Gs is the specific gravity of the solid e is the void ratio

bcdee5fb3e0b.title: Specific weight
bcdee5fb3e0b.sentence: The formula for saturated unit weight is: γs=(Gs+e)γw1+e where γs is the saturated unit weight of the material γw is the unit weight of water Gs is the specific gravity of the solid e is the void ratio

01f0f056f131.sentence: The pores that are too large to have any significant capillary force.

cd8a2c2a1c1d.sentence: Macropores can be caused by cracking, division of peds and aggregates, as well as plant roots and zoological exploration.

ba1b4d9f5d56.title: Soil compaction (agriculture)
ba1b4d9f5d56.sentence: Loosening of already compacted soil layers by deep ripping may be beneficial for plant growth and soil condition.

345ac46fd4fd.title: Soil compaction (agriculture)
345ac46fd4fd.sentence: For an integrated management, computer-based modelling of crop yard for vulnerability to compaction is recommended in order to avoid driving over vulnerable soil.

b0b57b087345.title: Soil compaction (agriculture)

b0b57b087345.sentence: The European Union addresses soil compaction by means of the Seventh EU Environment Action Programme, which entered into force in 2014.

be5d9eac118b.title: Soil compaction (agriculture)
be5d9eac118b.section: Avoidance and mitigation > Public policy responses
be5d9eac118b.sentence: For instance, in Germany farmers operate under the Federal Soil Conservation Law.

9b177c4f83a5.title: Soil compaction (agriculture)
9b177c4f83a5.section: Avoidance and mitigation > Public policy responses
9b177c4f83a5.sentence: The law states that farmers have the obligation of precaution towards soil compaction according to acknowledged good practices.

d10ba2d0043b.title: Soil compaction (agriculture)
d10ba2d0043b.sentence: Mechanic pressure applied to the soil is counterbalanced by an increase of soil particle interactions.

2075a2441cde.title: Soil compaction (agriculture)
2075a2441cde.sentence: This implies a reduction in soil volume by reducing the voids in between soil particles.

4184b06bcbad.title: Soil compaction (agriculture)
4184b06bcbad.sentence: As a consequence water and air is displaced and soil bulk density increases, resulting in a reduced permeability for water and air.

c7771accac2f.title: Soil compaction (agriculture)
c7771accac2f.sentence: Susceptibility of soil to compaction depends on several factors, which influence soil particle interactions:

eaa556cde5a9.title: Soil compaction (agriculture)
eaa556cde5a9.sentence: In healthy, well-structured soils, particles interact with each other forming soil aggregates.

188ca4f68a28.title: Soil compaction (agriculture)
188ca4f68a28.sentence: The resulting soil structure increases in stability with the number of interactions between soil particles.

689b6692e151.title: Soil compaction (agriculture)
689b6692e151.sentence: Water and air fills the voids between soil particles, where water interacts with soil particles forming a thin layer around them.

9423bb937970.title: Soil compaction (agriculture)
9423bb937970.sentence: This layer can shield particle–particle interaction thus reducing the stability of soil structure.

50c6dd4eb22f.title: Soil compaction (agriculture)
50c6dd4eb22f.sentence: - Soil texture, with fine textured soils (high clay content) being more susceptible to compaction than coarse textured soils.

717fcbe9ef43.title: Soil compaction (agriculture)
717fcbe9ef43.sentence: - Soil water content, a high water content increases susceptibility to compaction as the layer of water on the surface of soil particles shields interactions between soil particles

643074fe14c6.title: Soil compaction (agriculture)
643074fe14c6.sentence: - Soil structure, with angular, heterogeneous structures being more stable.

b78042f807e7.title: Soil compaction (agriculture)
b78042f807e7.sentence: - Initial bulk density, dense soils are more resistant to compaction as the number of particle interactions is higher.

99b1ed407271.title: Soil compaction (agriculture)

f35e3569aa68.title: Soil compaction (agriculture)
f35e3569aa68.sentence: - pH, affects net charges of molecules

8de7396fc032.title: Dilatancy (granular material)
8de7396fc032.sentence: In soil mechanics, dilatancy or shear dilatancy is the volume change observed in granular materials when they are subjected to shear deformations.

02f071b2191b.title: Dilatancy (granular material)
02f071b2191b.sentence: Unlike most other solid materials, the tendency of a compacted dense granular material is to dilate (expand in volume) as it is sheared.

7852265745e0.title: Dilatancy (granular material)
7852265745e0.sentence: This effect was first described scientifically by Osborne Reynolds in 1885/1886 and is also known as Reynolds dilatancy.

f416e6b36391.title: Dilatancy (granular material)
f416e6b36391.sentence: It was brought into the field of geotechnical engineering by Peter Walter Rowe [de].

efc810df7e6b.title: Dilatancy (granular material)
efc810df7e6b.sentence: This occurs because the grains in a compacted state are interlocking and therefore do not have the freedom to move around one another.

d742222319e2.title: Dilatancy (granular material)
d742222319e2.sentence: When stressed, a lever motion occurs between neighboring grains, which produces a bulk expansion of the material.

acaf0c0835b1.title: Dilatancy (granular material)
acaf0c0835b1.sentence: On the other hand, when a granular material starts in a very loose state it may continuously compact instead of dilating under shear.

b6e82ac79ae4.title: Dilatancy (granular material)
b6e82ac79ae4.sentence: Its effect can be seen when the wet sand around the foot of a person walking on beach appears to dry up.

6af0cf69899e.title: Dilatancy (granular material)
6af0cf69899e.sentence: The deformation caused by the foot expands the sand under it and the water in the sand moves to fill the new space between the grains.

3628e965b8eb.title: Dilatancy (granular material)
3628e965b8eb.sentence: In general, the denser the soil, the greater the amount of volume expansion under shear.

ae7e59934b44.title: Dilatancy (granular material)
ae7e59934b44.sentence: After the peak strength of the soil is mobilized the angle of friction abruptly decreases.

8e06e783d804.title: Dilatancy (granular material)
8e06e783d804.sentence: As a result, geotechnical engineering of slopes, footings, tunnels, and piles in such soils have to consider the potential decrease in strength after the soil strength reaches this peak value.

d2d1af3dcafd.title: Thixotropy
d2d1af3dcafd.sentence: Thixotropy is a time-dependent shear thinning property.

67fe0b0897c9.title: Thixotropy
67fe0b0897c9.sentence: Certain gels or fluids that are thick or viscous under static conditions will flow (become thinner, less viscous) over time when shaken, agitated, shear-stressed, or otherwise stressed (time-dependent viscosity).

b4ff3bab7bee.title: Thixotropy
b4ff3bab7bee.sentence: They then take a fixed time to return to a more viscous state.

4729f6b3bf76.title: Thixotropy
4729f6b3bf76.sentence: Thixotropy arises because particles or structured solutes require time to organize.

113ea586d09f.title: Thixotropy
113ea586d09f.sentence: Many gels and colloids are thixotropic materials, exhibiting a stable form at rest but becoming fluid when agitated.

1c445e8863c6.title: Thixotropy
1c445e8863c6.sentence: Some clays are thixotropic, influenced by thermochemical treatment, and their behaviour is of great importance in structural and geotechnical engineering.

59f7f4c4eb48.title: Bentonite
59f7f4c4eb48.sentence: Most often, bentonite suspensions are also thixotropic, although rare cases of rheopectic behavior have also been reported.

c0c0681c3d95.title: Fuller's earth
c0c0681c3d95.sentence: Hills, cliffs, and slopes that contain fuller's earth can be unstable, since this material can be thixotropic when saturated by heavy rainfall.

6299d6bb8799.title: Soil liquefaction
6299d6bb8799.sentence: This clay has a tendency to change from a relatively stiff condition to a liquid mass when it is disturbed.

7e97270cda16.title: Soil liquefaction
7e97270cda16.sentence: This gradual (but sometimes rapid) change in appearance from solid to liquid is a process known as spontaneous liquefaction or thixotropy.

db1214a9f372.title: Thixotropy
db1214a9f372.sentence: Landslides, such as those common in the cliffs around Lyme Regis, Dorset and in the Aberfan spoil tip disaster in Wales are evidence of this phenomenon.

8b0c83e2dc38.title: Thixotropy
8b0c83e2dc38.sentence: It was invented by Herbert Freundlich originally for a sol-gel transformation.

9960cbc1e8e6.title: Thixotropy
9960cbc1e8e6.sentence: The word comes from Ancient Greek θίξις thixis 'touch' (from thinganein 'to touch') and -tropy, -tropous, from Ancient Greek -τρόπος -tropos 'of turning', from τρόπος tropos 'a turn', from τρέπειν trepein, 'to turn, change'.

9101a6c18770.title: Thixotropy
9101a6c18770.sentence: Hence, it can be translated as something that turns (or changes) when touched.

9312b28ac8f2.title: Critical state soil mechanics
9312b28ac8f2.sentence: Critical state soil mechanics is the area of soil mechanics that encompasses the conceptual models representing the mechanical behavior of saturated remoulded soils based on the critical state concept.

654aa85879f1.title: Critical state soil mechanics
654aa85879f1.sentence: At the critical state, the relationship between forces applied in the soil (stress), and the resulting deformation resulting from this stress (strain) becomes constant.

3014af48d1ff.title: Critical state soil mechanics
3014af48d1ff.sentence: The soil will continue to deform, but the stress will no longer increase.

017ab1cd8574.title: Critical state soil mechanics
017ab1cd8574.section: Theories of Critical State Soil Mechanics
017ab1cd8574.sentence: It states that soils and other granular materials, if continuously distorted (sheared) until they flow as a frictional fluid, will come into a well-defined critical state.

267c6732c71d.title: Critical state soil mechanics
267c6732c71d.sentence: In an attempt to advance soil testing techniques, Kenneth Harry Roscoe of Cambridge University, in the late forties and early fifties, developed a simple shear apparatus in which his successive students attempted to study the changes in conditions in the shear zone both in sand and in clay soils.

7fa47dc5a6ba.title: Critical state soil mechanics
7fa47dc5a6ba.sentence: In 1958 a study of the yielding of soil based on some Cambridge data of the simple shear apparatus tests, and on much more extensive data of triaxial tests at Imperial College London from research led by Professor Sir Alec Skempton at Imperial College, led to the publication of the critical state concept (Roscoe, Schofield & Wroth 1958).

b837b81d3d2a.title: Critical state soil mechanics
b837b81d3d2a.sentence: The Original Cam-Clay model is based on the assumption that the soil is isotropic, elasto-plastic, deforms as a continuum, and it is not affected by creep.

73338a954767.title: Critical state soil mechanics
73338a954767.sentence: Professor John Burland of Imperial College who worked with Professor Roscoe is credited with the development of the modified version of the original model.

db358131fe89.title: Critical state soil mechanics
db358131fe89.sentence: The difference between the Cam Clay and the Modified Cam Clay (MCC) is that the yield surface of the MCC is described by an ellipse and therefore the plastic strain increment vector (which is perpendicular to the yield surface) for the largest value of the mean effective stress is horizontal, and hence no incremental deviatoric plastic strain takes place for a change in mean effective stress (for purely hydrostatic states of stress).

100e1b4ecdf5.title: Water content
100e1b4ecdf5.section: Classification and uses > Earth and agricultural sciences > Groundwater
100e1b4ecdf5.sentence: Most soils have a water content less than porosity, which is the definition of unsaturated conditions, and they make up the subject of vadose zone hydrogeology.

eeef4712e02f.sentence: Above a capillary fringe, pore spaces have air in them too.

bf997c30e11c.title: Water content
bf997c30e11c.section: Classification and uses > Earth and agricultural sciences > Groundwater
bf997c30e11c.sentence: In saturated groundwater aquifers, all available pore spaces are filled with water (volumetric water content = porosity).

028721a5910f.sentence: Water content in the capillary fringe decreases with increasing distance above the phreatic surface.

f1c314052ad2.section: Classification and uses > Earth and agricultural sciences > Groundwater
f1c314052ad2.sentence: One of the main complications which arises in studying the vadose zone, is the fact that the unsaturated hydraulic conductivity is a function of the water content of the material.

34bbecd9dce4.title: Water content
34bbecd9dce4.section: Classification and uses > Earth and agricultural sciences > Groundwater
34bbecd9dce4.sentence: As a material dries out, the connected wet pathways through the media become smaller, the hydraulic conductivity decreasing with lower water content in a very non-linear fashion.

12fecbdccb77.title: Water content

12fecbdccb77.sentence: The flow of water through and unsaturated zone in soils often involves a process of fingering, resulting from Saffman–Taylor instability.

9e912bd813ab.section: Classification and uses > Earth and agricultural sciences > Groundwater
9e912bd813ab.sentence: This results mostly through drainage processes and produces and unstable interface between saturated and unsaturated regions.

c7a449b806e2.title: Pore water pressure
c7a449b806e2.sentence: - Matric suction: the defining trait of unsaturated soil, this term corresponds to the pressure dry soil exerts on the surrounding material to equalise the moisture content in the overall block of soil and is defined as the difference between pore air pressure,(ua), and pore water pressure, (uw).

e9b79ff87452.title: Pore water pressure
e9b79ff87452.sentence: This is primarily due to the surface tension of pore water in voids throughout the vadose zone causing a suction effect on surrounding particles, i.e. matric suction.

8b14ea0e4e10.title: Pore water pressure
8b14ea0e4e10.sentence: At any point above the water table, in the vadose zone, the effective stress is approximately equal to the total stress, as proven by Terzaghi's principle.

a21164ea969e.title: Pore water pressure
a21164ea969e.sentence: Realistically, the effective stress is greater than the total stress, as the pore water pressure in these partially saturated soils is actually negative.

9546c0809600.title: Pore water pressure
9546c0809600.sentence: Increased water infiltration, such as that caused by heavy rainfall, brings about a reduction in matric suction, following the relationship described by the soil water characteristic curve (SWCC), resulting in a reduction of the soil's shear strength, and reduced slope stability.

4913cbe293dd.title: Pore water pressure
4913cbe293dd.sentence: The height of capillary rise is inversely proportional to the diameter of void space in contact with water.

7430eb9ed044.title: Pore water pressure
7430eb9ed044.sentence: Therefore, the smaller the void space, the higher water will rise due to tension forces.

3128f3149baf.title: Pore water pressure
3128f3149baf.sentence: Sandy soils consist of more coarse material with more room for voids, and therefore tend to have a much shallower capillary zone than do more cohesive soils, such as clays and silts.

72fa7d55f7a8.sentence: A tensiometer is an instrument used to determine the matric water potential (Ψm) (soil moisture tension) in the vadose zone.

7d67ccd96b7f.title: Bulk density
7d67ccd96b7f.sentence: Bulk density of soil is usually determined from a core sample which is taken by driving a metal corer into the soil at the desired depth and horizon.

2f10efa525c3.title: Bulk density
2f10efa525c3.sentence: For the wet bulk density (total bulk density) this sample is weighed, giving the mass Mt. For the dry bulk density, the sample is oven dried and weighed, giving the mass of soil solids, Ms.

da69873c5074.title: Bulk density
da69873c5074.sentence: This gives a soil sample of known total volume, Vt.

193036cd7630.title: Porous medium
193036cd7630.sentence: In materials science, a porous medium or a porous material is a material containing pores (voids).

b1001fca03a4.title: Porous medium
b1001fca03a4.sentence: The skeletal portion of the material is often called the "matrix" or "frame".

ecb881f66b02.title: Porous medium
ecb881f66b02.sentence: The pores are typically filled with a fluid (liquid or gas).

ca245aafe0f4.title: Porous medium
ca245aafe0f4.sentence: Many natural substances such as rocks and soil (e.g. aquifers, petroleum reservoirs), zeolites, biological tissues (e.g. bones, wood, cork), and man made materials such as cements and ceramics can be considered as porous media.

7cc3d97d21e2.title: Porous medium
7cc3d97d21e2.sentence: The concept of porous media is used in many areas of applied science and engineering: filtration, mechanics (acoustics, geomechanics, soil mechanics, rock mechanics), engineering (petroleum engineering, bioremediation, construction engineering), geosciences (hydrogeology, petroleum geology, geophysics), biology and biophysics, material science.

1de63bdb32b6.title: Porous medium
1de63bdb32b6.sentence: A porous medium is most often characterised by its porosity.

9528a15de611.title: Porous medium
9528a15de611.sentence: Other properties of the medium (e.g. permeability, tensile strength, electrical conductivity, tortuosity) can sometimes be derived from the respective properties of its constituents (solid matrix and fluid) and the media porosity and pores structure, but such a derivation is usually complex.

2afe3137d726.title: Porous medium
2afe3137d726.sentence: Often both the solid matrix and the pore network (also known as the pore space) are continuous, so as to form two interpenetrating continua such as in a sponge.

e5459330e639.title: Porous medium
e5459330e639.sentence: However, there is also a concept of closed porosity and effective porosity, i.e. the pore space accessible to flow.

710b8fcb3a32.title: Porous medium
710b8fcb3a32.sentence: The most fundamental law that characterizes this connection is Darcy's law, particularly applicable to fine-porous media.

a78d42cb35a6.title: Porous medium
a78d42cb35a6.sentence: In contrast, Forchheimer's law finds utility in the context of coarse-porous media.

febea0899f4d.title: Bearing capacity
febea0899f4d.sentence: In geotechnical engineering, bearing capacity is the capacity of soil to support the loads applied to the ground.

4bf69a74df62.title: Bearing capacity
4bf69a74df62.sentence: The bearing capacity of soil is the maximum average contact pressure between the foundation and the soil which should not produce shear failure in the soil.

7c33cb34ab1a.title: Bearing capacity
7c33cb34ab1a.sentence: Ultimate bearing capacity is the theoretical maximum pressure which can be supported without failure; allowable bearing capacity is the ultimate bearing capacity divided by a factor of safety.

58d2efad2e4f.title: Bearing capacity
58d2efad2e4f.sentence: Sometimes, on soft soil sites, large settlements may occur under loaded foundations without actual shear failure occurring; in such cases, the allowable bearing capacity is based on the maximum allowable settlement.

06a3dd80e0d9.title: Bearing capacity
06a3dd80e0d9.sentence: It depends upon the shear strength of soil as well as shape, size, depth and type of foundation.

079833e6d8dd.title: Bearing capacity
079833e6d8dd.sentence: There are three modes of failure that limit bearing capacity: general shear failure, local shear failure, and punching shear failure.

474f06c6ea3a.title: Earth shelter
474f06c6ea3a.sentence: Well-graded gravels have a large bearing capacity (about 8,000 pounds per square foot (39,000 kg/m2)), excellent drainage and a low frost heave potential.

049f87cd59b4.title: Soil structure
049f87cd59b4.sentence: In turn, reciprocally soil structure interacts and affects the root growth and function, soil fauna and microorganisms, water and solute transport processes, gas exchange, thermal conductivity and electrical conductivity, traffic bearing capacity, and many other aspects in relation with soil.

9607daafd48e.title: Shear strength (soil)
9607daafd48e.sentence: A more advanced understanding of the behaviour of soil undergoing shearing led to the development of the critical state theory of soil mechanics (Roscoe, Schofield & Wroth 1958).

72aecddb7e66.title: Shear strength (soil)
72aecddb7e66.sentence: In critical state soil mechanics, a distinct shear strength is identified where the soil undergoing shear does so at a constant volume, also called the 'critical state'.

22b9ef28df42.title: Shear strength (soil)
22b9ef28df42.sentence: Thus there are three commonly identified shear strengths for a soil undergoing shear:

ed58c7066f22.title: Shear strength (soil)
ed58c7066f22.sentence: - Critical state or constant volume strength τcv

d045539cdf8b.title: Shear strength (soil)
d045539cdf8b.sentence: - A loose soil will contract in volume on shearing, and may not develop any peak strength above critical state.

cd08b431dc5d.title: Shear strength (soil)
cd08b431dc5d.sentence: - A dense soil may contract slightly before granular interlock prevents further contraction (granular interlock is dependent on the shape of the grains and their initial packing arrangement).

f049d08e11d2.title: Shear strength (soil)
f049d08e11d2.sentence: In order to continue shearing once granular interlock has occurred, the soil must dilate (expand in volume).

2facaf0890e9.title: Shear strength (soil)
2facaf0890e9.sentence: As additional shear force is required to dilate the soil, a 'peak' strength occurs.

d1326faeaef6.title: Shear strength (soil)
d1326faeaef6.sentence: Once this peak strength caused by dilation has been overcome through continued shearing, the resistance provided by the soil to the applied shear stress decreases (termed "strain softening").

8f15f0a53b31.title: Soil mechanics
8f15f0a53b31.section: Shear behavior: stiffness and strength > Friction, interlocking and dilation
8f15f0a53b31.sentence: Furthermore, as dilative soil grains dilate, they become looser (their void ratio increases), and their rate of dilation decreases until they reach a critical void ratio.

accdc550365f.title: Soil mechanics
accdc550365f.section: Shear behavior: stiffness and strength > Friction, interlocking and dilation
accdc550365f.sentence: Contractive soils become denser as they shear, and their rate of contraction decreases until they reach a critical void ratio.

d8f91aead8b1.title: Soil mechanics
d8f91aead8b1.section: Shear behavior: stiffness and strength > Friction, interlocking and dilation
d8f91aead8b1.sentence: As a first approximation, the regions of contraction and dilation are separated by the critical state line.

b5e70ed30690.title: Shear strength (soil)
b5e70ed30690.sentence: The residual strength occurs for some soils where the shape of the particles that make up the soil become aligned during shearing (forming a slickenside), resulting in reduced resistance to continued shearing (further strain softening).

109fde70e0dc.title: Shear strength (soil)
109fde70e0dc.sentence: This is particularly true for most clays that comprise plate-like minerals, but is also observed in some granular soils with more elongate shaped grains.

ea5854666735.title: Shear strength (soil)
ea5854666735.sentence: Clays that do not have plate-like minerals (like allophanic clays) do not tend to exhibit residual strengths.

0f8754291a38.title: Shear strength (soil)
0f8754291a38.sentence: The drained shear strength is the shear strength of the soil when pore fluid pressures - generated during the course of shearing the soil - are able to dissipate during shearing.

9cabd3af02fd.title: Shear strength (soil)
9cabd3af02fd.sentence: It also applies where no pore water exists in the soil (the soil is dry) and hence pore fluid pressures are negligible.

9178bcf14f7b.title: Shear strength (soil)
9178bcf14f7b.sentence: It is commonly approximated using the Mohr-Coulomb equation.

9c1e8853c95e.title: Shear strength (soil)
9c1e8853c95e.sentence: (It was called "Coulomb's equation" by Karl von Terzaghi in 1942.) (Terzaghi 1942) combined it with the principle of effective stress.

879b88f8e865.sentence: - Soil composition (basic soil material): mineralogy, grain size and grain size distribution, shape of particles, pore fluid type and content, ions on grain and in pore fluid.

954b9a6cc777.sentence: If the rate of shearing is very large compared to the rate that water can be sucked into or squeezed out of the dilating or contracting pore spaces, then the shearing is called undrained shear, if the shearing is slow enough that the water pressures are negligible, the shearing is called drained shear.

f7478675b118.title: Pore space in soil

30743b5df746.title: Pore space in soil

f6c16966791d.title: Soil compaction (agriculture)
f6c16966791d.sentence: Soil compaction can occur naturally by the drying and wetting process called soil consolidation, or when external pressure is applied to the soil.

56ab7612c9e9.title: Soil compaction (agriculture)
56ab7612c9e9.sentence: The most relevant human-induced causes of soil compaction in agriculture are the use of heavy machineries, tillage practice itself, inappropriate choice of tillage systems, as well as livestock trampling.

ec4177f29077.title: Soil compaction (agriculture)
ec4177f29077.sentence: Use of large and heavy machineries for agriculture often causes not only topsoil but subsoil compaction.

d82b97653d3b.title: Soil compaction (agriculture)

7bbfb03de1e5.title: Soil compaction (agriculture)

6aad87ce9d4c.title: Soil compaction (agriculture)
6aad87ce9d4c.sentence: Whether heavy machinery is in use or not, tillage practice itself can cause soil compaction.

cb7ff0af5fa8.title: Soil compaction (agriculture)
cb7ff0af5fa8.sentence: It should however be noted that tillage activity could reduce topsoil compaction compared to no tillage activity in the long term.

8d0928a25a6b.title: Soil compaction (agriculture)
8d0928a25a6b.sentence: Significant livestock trampling resulting from livestock farming on meadows and agricultural land is also viewed major cause of soil compaction.

7cd2ddffcbb8.title: Soil compaction (agriculture)

0f24feb975bd.title: Particle mass density

2c0ac6cdccfa.title: Particle mass density

f37492f6ba6a.title: Particle mass density

7983b3af5857.title: Particle mass density

d51e2b273630.title: Particle mass density

08986018cee2.title: Particle mass density
