ccdb0b6a5f26.title: Soil consolidation
ccdb0b6a5f26.sentence: Laboratory data is used to construct a plot of strain or void ratio versus effective stress where the effective stress axis is on a logarithmic scale.

7d397f977015.title: Soil consolidation
7d397f977015.sentence: The plot's slope is the compression index or recompression index.

3b5f7dd3651c.title: Soil consolidation
3b5f7dd3651c.sentence: In the classical method developed by Terzaghi, soils are tested with an oedometer test to determine their compressibility.

65df5e7060f9.title: Soil consolidation
65df5e7060f9.sentence: The more compressible the clay, the more pronounced the influences of cation type and electrolyte concentration on compressibility.

985ed751045d.title: Soil consolidation
985ed751045d.sentence: When stress is removed from a consolidated soil, the soil will rebound, regaining some of the volume it had lost in the consolidation process.

d78b9a2d5231.title: Soil consolidation
d78b9a2d5231.sentence: If the stress is reapplied, the soil will consolidate again along a recompression curve, defined by the recompression index.

b3c0310a7683.title: Soil consolidation
b3c0310a7683.sentence: The first modern theoretical models for soil consolidation were proposed in the 1920s by Terzaghi and Fillunger, according to two substantially different approaches.

8ec8628007df.title: Soil consolidation
8ec8628007df.sentence: The former was based on diffusion equations in eulerian notation, whereas the latter considered the local Newton's law for both liquid and solid phases, in which main variables, such as partial pressure, porosity, local velocity etc., were involved by means of the mixture theory.

23618b7af606.title: Soil consolidation
23618b7af606.sentence: Terzaghi had an engineering approach to the problem of soil consolidation and provided simplified models that are still widely used in engineering practice today, whereas, on the other hand, Fillunger had a rigorous approach to the above problems and provided rigorous mathematical models that paid particular attention to the methods of local averaging of the involved variables.

3455c138e886.title: Soil consolidation
3455c138e886.sentence: Fillunger's model was very abstract and involved variables that were difficult to detect experimentally, and, therefore, it was not applicable to the study of real cases by engineers and/or designers.

a6852dc20da6.title: Soil consolidation
a6852dc20da6.sentence: The Terzaghi's model is currently the most utilized in engineering practice and is based on the diffusion equation.

e2827f7bd3f7.title: Soil consolidation
e2827f7bd3f7.sentence: Due to the different approach to the problem of consolidation by the two scientists, a bitter scientific dispute arose between them, and this unfortunately led to a tragic ending in 1937.

5d8421230bd0.title: Soil consolidation
5d8421230bd0.sentence: After Fillunger's suicide, his theoretical results were forgotten for decades, whereas the methods proposed by Terzaghi found widespread diffusion among scientists and professionals.

8d9123035ecb.title: Soil consolidation
8d9123035ecb.sentence: In the following decades Biot fully developed the three-dimensional soil consolidation theory, extending the one-dimensional model previously proposed by Terzaghi to more general hypotheses and introducing the set of basic equations of poroelasticity.

b465b0de4300.title: Soil consolidation
b465b0de4300.sentence: Today, the Terzaghis’ one dimensional model is still the most utilized by engineers for its conceptual simplicity and because it is based on experimental data, such as oedometer tests, which are relatively simple, reliable and inexpensive and for which theoretical solutions in closed form are well known.

ed8154aa0695.title: Soil consolidation
ed8154aa0695.sentence: A soil which had its load removed is considered to be "overconsolidated".

3434039cc0b9.title: Soil consolidation
3434039cc0b9.sentence: The highest stress that it has been subjected to is termed the "preconsolidation stress".

d34061a6e7c3.title: Soil consolidation
d34061a6e7c3.sentence: This is the case for soils that have previously had glaciers on them or that have been affected by land subsidence.

6424db8cb74e.title: Soil consolidation
6424db8cb74e.sentence: The "over-consolidation ratio" (OCR) is defined as the highest stress experienced divided by the current stress.

ab5f2f72ebf8.title: Soil consolidation
ab5f2f72ebf8.sentence: A soil that is currently experiencing its highest stress is said to be "normally consolidated" and has an OCR of one.

4d89e1dc7ee0.title: Soil consolidation
4d89e1dc7ee0.sentence: A soil could be considered "underconsolidated" or "unconsolidated" immediately after a new load is applied but before the excess pore water pressure has dissipated.

37806f6bca6d.title: Soil consolidation
37806f6bca6d.sentence: Cc can be replaced by Cr (the recompression index) for use in overconsolidated soils where the final effective stress is less than the preconsolidation stress.

02762d56efa4.title: Soil consolidation
02762d56efa4.sentence: When the final effective stress is greater than the preconsolidation stress, the two equations must be used in combination to model both the recompression portion and the virgin compression portion of the consolidation processes, as follows,

6f99acf19e8c.title: Soil consolidation
6f99acf19e8c.sentence: However, in soils with a high amount of organic material such as peat, the phenomenon of creep also occurs, whereby the soil changes volume gradually at constant effective stress.

374a0682c76e.title: Soil consolidation
374a0682c76e.sentence: This process of creep is sometimes known as "secondary consolidation" or "secondary compression" because it also involves gradual change of soil volume in response to an application of load; the designation "secondary" distinguishes it from "primary consolidation", which refers to volume change due to dissipation of excess pore water pressure.

644e46c5fae8.title: Soil consolidation
644e46c5fae8.sentence: To distinguish between the two mechanisms, "primary consolidation" refers to consolidation due to dissipation of excess water pressure, while "secondary consolidation" refers to the creep process.

87d91458578c.title: Soil consolidation
87d91458578c.sentence: Soil creep is typically caused by viscous behavior of the clay-water system and compression of organic matter.

b077367c3004.title: Soil consolidation
b077367c3004.sentence: Creep typically takes place over a longer time-scale than (primary) consolidation, such that even after the restoration of hydrostatic pressure some compression of soil takes place at slow rate.

e48a724b3b20.title: Soil consolidation
e48a724b3b20.sentence: This is the case for most types of sand and clay with low amounts of organic material.

5d00dc88c9b9.title: Peat
5d00dc88c9b9.sentence: This soil is problematic because it exhibits poor consolidation properties—it cannot be easily compacted to serve as a stable foundation to support loads, such as roads or buildings.

9465b8128807.title: Soil consolidation
9465b8128807.sentence: Analytically, the rate of creep is assumed to decay exponentially with time since application of load, giving the formula:

f47c1595503b.title: Soil consolidation
f47c1595503b.sentence: where H0 is the height of the consolidating medium; e0 is the initial void ratio; Ca is the secondary compression index; t is the length of time after consolidation considered; and t95 is the length of time for achieving 95% consolidation.

5fd416f35eda.title: Terzaghi's principle
5fd416f35eda.sentence: Terzaghi's principle states that when stress is applied to a porous material (soil, concrete, rock and other porous media), it is opposed also by the fluid pressure filling the pores in the material.

bf6721a733c7.title: Terzaghi's principle
bf6721a733c7.sentence: The principle states that all quantifiable changes in stress to a porous medium are a direct result of a change in effective stress.

b189f11ed51e.title: Terzaghi's principle
b189f11ed51e.sentence: Karl von Terzaghi introduced the idea in a series of papers in the 1920s based on his examination of building consolidation on soil.

af7ff8c7faa9.title: Terzaghi's principle
af7ff8c7faa9.sentence: The effective stress, {\displaystyle {\boldsymbol {\sigma }}_{eff}}, is related to total stress, {\displaystyle {\boldsymbol {\sigma }}}, and the pore pressure, {\displaystyle P}, by

d27419abb5fe.title: Terzaghi's principle
d27419abb5fe.sentence: The negative sign is there because the pore pressure serves to lessen the volume-changing stress; physically this is because there is fluid in the pores which bears a part of the total stress, so partially unloading the solid matrix from normal stresses.

17409dc2f845.title: Terzaghi's principle
17409dc2f845.sentence: Terzaghi's principle applies well to porous materials whose solid constituents are incompressible - soil, for example, is composed of grains of incompressible silica so that the volume change in soil during consolidation is due solely to the rearrangement of these constituents with respect to one another.

bfe688dd1eb7.title: Terzaghi's principle
bfe688dd1eb7.sentence: Generalizing Terzaghi's principle to include porous media (e.g., soil, rock, biological tissues, etc.) with compressible solid constituents was accomplished by Maurice Anthony Biot in the 1940s, giving birth to the theory of poroelasticity and poromechanics.

972ab5b3f431.title: Terzaghi's principle
972ab5b3f431.sentence: Though the first five assumptions are either likely to hold, or deviation will have no discernible effect, experimental results contradict the final three.

d2f419fd55fe.title: Terzaghi's principle
d2f419fd55fe.sentence: Darcy's law does not seem to hold at high hydraulic gradients, and both the coefficients of permeability and volume compressibility decrease during consolidation.

88d0520e4e4f.title: Terzaghi's principle
88d0520e4e4f.sentence: Finally, the relationship between void ratio and effective stress is not independent of time, again proven by experimental results.

1ed29e9c3d6a.title: Specific storage
1ed29e9c3d6a.sentence: Specific yield, also known as the drainable porosity, is a ratio and is the volumetric fraction of the bulk aquifer volume that a given aquifer will yield when all the water is allowed to drain out of it under the forces of gravity:

e68ffab6f087.title: Specific storage
e68ffab6f087.sentence: It is primarily used for unconfined aquifers since the elastic storage component, Ss, is relatively small and usually has an insignificant contribution.

17c000ba8c6e.title: Geotechnical engineering
17c000ba8c6e.sentence: Geotechnical engineers and engineering geologists perform geotechnical investigations to obtain information on the physical properties of soil and rock underlying and adjacent to a site to design earthworks and foundations for proposed structures and for the repair of distress to earthworks and structures caused by subsurface conditions.

01fe0b88b460.title: Geotechnical engineering
01fe0b88b460.sentence: Geotechnical investigations involve surface and subsurface exploration of a site, often including subsurface sampling and laboratory testing of retrieved soil samples.

fe8efd0cb684.title: Geotechnical engineering
fe8efd0cb684.sentence: Sometimes, geophysical methods are also used to obtain data, which include measurement of seismic waves (pressure, shear, and Rayleigh waves), surface-wave methods and downhole methods, and electromagnetic surveys (magnetometer, resistivity, and ground-penetrating radar).

5ff16f0ed25e.title: Geotechnical engineering
5ff16f0ed25e.sentence: Subsurface exploration usually involves in-situ testing (for example, the standard penetration test and cone penetration test).

dbc483a0a217.title: Geotechnical engineering
dbc483a0a217.sentence: The digging of test pits and trenching (particularly for locating faults and slide planes) may also be used to learn about soil conditions at depth.

df0b877ad0db.title: Geotechnical engineering
df0b877ad0db.sentence: The standard penetration test, which uses a thick-walled split spoon sampler, is the most common way to collect disturbed samples.

178b4a6d15ed.title: Geotechnical engineering
178b4a6d15ed.sentence: Piston samplers, employing a thin-walled tube, are most commonly used to collect less disturbed samples.

86dbf7193de4.title: Geotechnical engineering
86dbf7193de4.sentence: Geotechnical centrifuge modeling is another method of testing physical-scale models of geotechnical problems.

ddecad176b51.title: Geotechnical engineering
ddecad176b51.sentence: The use of a centrifuge enhances the similarity of the scale model tests involving soil because soil's strength and stiffness are susceptible to the confining pressure.

df552a80455a.title: Geotechnical engineering
df552a80455a.sentence: The centrifugal acceleration allows a researcher to obtain large (prototype-scale) stresses in small physical models.

db57c29cdc79.title: Penetrometer
db57c29cdc79.sentence: A penetrometer is a device to test the strength of a material.

0b03ec740d60.title: Penetrometer
0b03ec740d60.sentence: The penetrometer is dropped on the test subject or pressed against it and the depth of the resulting hole is measured.

b4295f256a53.title: Penetrometer
b4295f256a53.sentence: There are many types of penetrometer designed to be used on soil.

d1eea28324f6.title: Penetrometer
d1eea28324f6.sentence: They are usually round or cone shaped.

15556d4bf173.title: Penetrometer
15556d4bf173.sentence: The measurements find whether the soil is strong enough to build a road on.

c4a69462de3c.title: Soil compaction (agriculture)
c4a69462de3c.sentence: An increase in soil strength can be measured with a penetrometer, which is basically a device for measuring the resistance of a soil.

f84d8479a43a.title: Atterberg limits
f84d8479a43a.section: Laboratory tests > Liquid limit > Fall cone test
f84d8479a43a.sentence: - The results from the cone penetrometer do not depend on the skills or the judgement of the operator.

e43694f63e4b.title: Penetrometer
e43694f63e4b.sentence: Scientists also use a penetrometer to measure how much moisture is in soil.

870175e13c59.title: Penetrometer
870175e13c59.sentence: Penetrometers are used by space probes such as the Cassini–Huygens probe, to measure the amount of moisture in soil on other planets.

38045bc01cd0.title: Penetrometer
38045bc01cd0.sentence: Penetrometers are furthermore used in glaciology to measure the strength and nature of materials underlying a glacier at its bed.

e89c9447cefc.title: Penetrometer
e89c9447cefc.sentence: A penetrometer is also used in longer professional cricket matches, to measure how the pitch is holding up over the course of a multi-day match.

d266b73d42c5.title: Penetrometer
d266b73d42c5.sentence: British horse racing courses have been required, since 2009, to report the readings obtained using a penetrometer, on each day of a race meeting.

25906c875cdd.title: Soil compaction (agriculture)
25906c875cdd.sentence: Soil compaction can be identified either in the field, the laboratory or via remote sensing.

4cb560aed196.title: Soil compaction (agriculture)
4cb560aed196.sentence: In order to get reliable data and results a combination of different methods is necessary as "there is no single universal method available to identify compact soils".

97869c798c97.title: Soil compaction (agriculture)
97869c798c97.sentence: Phenomena like waterlogging on the surface or in subsurface layers, visible reduction in porosity and changes of soil structure, soil moisture and soil colour are indicators of soil compaction in the field.

7a757f89e582.title: Soil compaction (agriculture)
7a757f89e582.sentence: A blue-grey soil colour and a smell of hydrogen sulphide can occur in the top soil due to extenuated aeration.

640cffa61277.title: Soil compaction (agriculture)
640cffa61277.sentence: By means of patterns of crop growth, pale leaf colours and root growth, it is possible to draw conclusions to the extent of compaction.

cdc43c7b46d9.title: Soil compaction (agriculture)
cdc43c7b46d9.sentence: Especially when trying to identify soil compaction in the field with the measurements mentioned above it has been considered particularly important to make a comparison between potentially compacted soil and uncompacted soil nearby.

2b1d28d746cf.title: Soil compaction (agriculture)
2b1d28d746cf.sentence: Soil bulk density, pore-size distribution, water permeability and the relative apparent gas diffusion coefficient give a good overview of the permeability of soils to air and water and therefore on the degree of compaction.

189d0220df9f.title: Soil compaction (agriculture)
189d0220df9f.sentence: Since the coarse pores are most important for water infiltration, gas exchange and transport, focusing on them when measuring the porosity and the diffusion coefficient is recommended.

e782eee4a50f.title: Soil compaction (agriculture)
e782eee4a50f.sentence: As a prevention of soil compaction remote sensing can model the susceptibility of soils by considering soil texture, slope value, water regime and economic factors like the type of farming or the machinery being used.

84c9cebc55e6.title: Soil compaction (agriculture)
84c9cebc55e6.sentence: Since methods of remote sensing are not able to identify soil compaction directly there are limitations to identification, monitoring and quantifying, especially on a global scale.

06e601e826f5.title: Soil compaction (agriculture)
06e601e826f5.sentence: Soil compaction is often local and depends on many factors that may vary within a few square meters.

cedbd155a057.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/15%3A_Addressing_Compaction/15.02%3A_Diagnosing_Different_Types_of_Compaction
cedbd155a057.sentence: The first step is to decide whether compaction is a problem and which type is affecting your soils.

a866d4a08e08.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/15%3A_Addressing_Compaction/15.02%3A_Diagnosing_Different_Types_of_Compaction
a866d4a08e08.sentence: The symptoms, as well as remedies and preventive measures, are summarized in Table 15.1.

bfcc25d00b59.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/15%3A_Addressing_Compaction/15.02%3A_Diagnosing_Different_Types_of_Compaction
bfcc25d00b59.sentence: Surface seal or crust | Breakdown of surface aggregates and sealing of surface Poor seedling emergence Accelerated runoff and erosion | Eliminate tillage or reduce tillage intensity Maximize surface cover: leave residues on surface, grow cover crops Add organic matter

8855a3409b4e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/15%3A_Addressing_Compaction/15.02%3A_Diagnosing_Different_Types_of_Compaction
8855a3409b4e.sentence: Certain soil types, such as sandy loams and silt loams, are particularly susceptible.

db3766202725.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/15%3A_Addressing_Compaction/15.02%3A_Diagnosing_Different_Types_of_Compaction
db3766202725.sentence: Their aggregates usually aren’t very stable, and once broken down, the small particles fill in the pore space between the larger particles, making very dense crusts.

a9a8904f95da.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/15%3A_Addressing_Compaction/15.02%3A_Diagnosing_Different_Types_of_Compaction
a9a8904f95da.sentence: Surface layer | Deep wheel tracks Prolonged saturation or standing water Poor root growth and more disease symptoms Hard to dig and resistant to penetrometer Cloddy after tillage | Use zone builders or strip tillers to break compaction but minimize soil disturbance Use cover crops or rotation crops that can break up compacted soils Add organic matter Use better load distribution with equipment Use controlled traffic Don’t travel on soils that are wet Improve soil drainage

1cffa1b52815.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/15%3A_Addressing_Compaction/15.02%3A_Diagnosing_Different_Types_of_Compaction
1cffa1b52815.sentence: Compaction of the layer immediately below the surface can often be observed in the field through deep wheel tracks, extended periods of saturation, or even standing water following rain or irrigation.

1f93a58d16d5.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/15%3A_Addressing_Compaction/15.02%3A_Diagnosing_Different_Types_of_Compaction
1f93a58d16d5.sentence: Conversely, roots in a compacted surface layer are usually stubby and have few root hairs (Figure 15.3).

14571b66b8a0.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/15%3A_Addressing_Compaction/15.02%3A_Diagnosing_Different_Types_of_Compaction
14571b66b8a0.sentence: They often follow crooked paths as they try to find zones of weakness in the soil.

4dba31b728dc.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/15%3A_Addressing_Compaction/15.02%3A_Diagnosing_Different_Types_of_Compaction
4dba31b728dc.sentence: A field penetrometer, which we discuss in greater detail in Chapter 23, is an excellent tool to assess soil compaction (you can also push a simple wire flag into the soil).

745e44ffac43.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/15%3A_Addressing_Compaction/15.02%3A_Diagnosing_Different_Types_of_Compaction
745e44ffac43.sentence: Note that recently plowed soils may give a false impression of compaction: they are initially loose but will likely compact later in the season.

6e227ed8173a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/15%3A_Addressing_Compaction/15.02%3A_Diagnosing_Different_Types_of_Compaction
6e227ed8173a.sentence: No-tilled soils generally are firmer but have stronger structure and contain large pores from worm activity.

5371d5eb0c15.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/15%3A_Addressing_Compaction/15.02%3A_Diagnosing_Different_Types_of_Compaction
5371d5eb0c15.sentence: The easiest way to assess compaction in deeper soil layers is to use a penetrometer, which should be done when the soil is field-moist (not too wet, not too dry).

3f000a135ffb.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/15%3A_Addressing_Compaction/15.02%3A_Diagnosing_Different_Types_of_Compaction
3f000a135ffb.sentence: It is surprising how often you find the tool hitting much higher resistance once it reaches the bottom of the plow layer—typically down 6–8 inches—even if it has not actually been tilled for awhile.

3d8ea00e0b7c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/15%3A_Addressing_Compaction/15.02%3A_Diagnosing_Different_Types_of_Compaction
3d8ea00e0b7c.sentence: Roots are almost completely absent from the subsoil below severe plow pans and often move horizontally above the pan (see Figure 6.8).

f28ef5ca0978.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/15%3A_Addressing_Compaction/15.02%3A_Diagnosing_Different_Types_of_Compaction
f28ef5ca0978.sentence: If soil wetness persists, anaerobic conditions may occur, causing reduced growth and high denitrification losses (exhibited by leaf yellowing), especially in areas that have drainage problems.

328df1b18277.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/15%3A_Addressing_Compaction/15.02%3A_Diagnosing_Different_Types_of_Compaction
328df1b18277.sentence: Crops in their early growth stages are very susceptible to these problems (because roots are still shallow), and the plants may go through a noticeable period of stunted growth on compacted soils.

513fcd79b726.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/15%3A_Addressing_Compaction/15.02%3A_Diagnosing_Different_Types_of_Compaction
513fcd79b726.sentence: For example, during wet periods, dense, poorly aerated soils are more susceptible to infestations of fungal root diseases such as Phytophthora, Sclerotinia, Fusarium, Pythium, Rhizoctonia and Thieviopsis and plant-parasitic nematodes such as northern root-knot.

eb1d4c000835.title: Trampling
eb1d4c000835.sentence: Trampling is the act of walking on something repeatedly by humans or animals.

4d956641e744.title: Trampling
4d956641e744.sentence: Trampling on open ground can destroy the above ground parts of many plants and can compact the soil, thereby creating a distinct microenvironment that specific species may be adapted for, causing a disturbance to ecology and to archaeological sites.

e3472158eac3.title: Trampling
e3472158eac3.sentence: Studies of recreational trampling in alpine environments have found that repeated foot traffic can reduce vegetation cover and height, shift species composition, and damage soils through compaction (raising bulk density and reducing porosity), which can alter soil moisture and temperature regimes and increase surface runoff and erosion.

9f8d00b55658.title: Trampling
9f8d00b55658.sentence: In a simulated trampling experiment in the limestone Belianske Tatras (Slovakia), researchers applied controlled numbers of foot passes to plots in three native alpine plant communities in 2008 and re-tested the same sites after regeneration in 2022.

916b0eea6fb9.title: Trampling
916b0eea6fb9.sentence: They found that "recovered" communities could appear slightly more resistant while having already lost some moss, lichen, and vascular plant species years after the earlier disturbance, indicating that trampling impacts may be delayed and that apparent recovery can mask biodiversity loss; they also reported that the resistance of individual species varied between communities and with trampling intensity.

a9200a143d70.title: Grazing
a9200a143d70.sentence: Sometimes grazers can have beneficial environmental effects such as improving the soil with nutrient redistribution and aerating the soil by trampling, and by controlling fire and increasing biodiversity by removing biomass, controlling shrub growth and dispersing seeds.

77890fda2049.title: Regenerative agriculture
77890fda2049.sentence: Livestock herds trample plants, which is shown to increase soil restoration, stimulate plant regrowth, increase soil carbon storage, and water infiltration.

f1de3a00fa68.title: Representative elementary volume
f1de3a00fa68.sentence: In the theory of composite materials, the representative elementary volume (REV) (also called the representative volume element (RVE) or the unit cell) is the smallest volume over which a measurement can be made that will yield a value representative of the whole.

0ea3f7b3d8fc.title: Representative elementary volume
0ea3f7b3d8fc.sentence: If the sample is too small, the readings tend to oscillate.

b9ec3b77c7ed.title: Representative elementary volume
b9ec3b77c7ed.sentence: With increasing sample size, the oscillations begin to dampen out.

57dbe8c8a887.title: Representative elementary volume

9ec61982ba92.sentence: Simply shattering this pan allows for deeper root exploration.

ac9241494155.section: Organic Matter Helps Soils Resist Compaction

52f6cc0c54a6.sentence: Subsoiling relates to a range of methods to alleviate compaction below the 6- to 8-inch depths of normal tillage and is often done with heavy duty rippers (Figure 15.5) and large tractors.

b1f7093f38e7.sentence: Subsoiling is often erroneously seen as a cure for all types of soil compaction, but it does relatively little to address surface layer compaction that is caused by aggregate breakdown.

4cb27553bd4c.sentence: Subsoiling is a rather costly and energy consuming practice, and its use is difficult to justify on a regular basis.

616995681faf.sentence: Deep tillage tends to be more effective on coarse-textured soils (sands, gravels), as crops on those soils respond better to deeper rooting.

cfa0792cd44a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/15%3A_Addressing_Compaction/15.03%3A_Relieving_and_Preventing_Compaction

cfa0792cd44a.sentence: In fine-textured soils, the entire subsoil often has high strength values, so the effects of deep tillage are less beneficial.

c6c5155468eb.sentence: In some cases it may even be harmful for those soils, especially if the deep tillage was performed when the subsoil was wet and caused smearing, which may generate drainage problems.

69f5bb17f63c.sentence: After performing deep tillage, it is important to prevent future re-compaction of the soil by keeping heavy loads off the field and not tilling the soil when inappropriate soil moisture conditions exist, because otherwise the benefits are short lived.

fb9b04ca22cb.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/15%3A_Addressing_Compaction/15.03%3A_Relieving_and_Preventing_Compaction

fb9b04ca22cb.sentence: Soils that are naturally susceptible to subsoil compaction due to the washing down of fine particles may need repeated deep tillage.

d088602bd9fe.sentence: Aerators (Figure 15.4) have rotating tines that provide shallow compaction relief in dense surface layers but do minimal tillage damage and are especially useful when aeration is of concern.

5e88e3f92968.sentence: They are also used to incorporate manure with minimal tillage damage.

fb1515e4bfc9.sentence: It is especially effective at promoting root proliferation.

3afe92aad471.sentence: Yeoman’s plows achieve similar results with virtually no surface disturbance.

dc2b3d3823b0.sentence: Compacted soils frequently become “addicted” to tillage, and converting to no-till “cold turkey” may result in failure.

d2a560f31ef3.sentence: In general, the benefits of no-till take 2–5 years to be realized, but this timeline can be accelerated with the use of cover crops.

73d8ab4e7d2b.sentence: Crusting is a symptom of the breakdown of soil aggregates that occurs especially with intensively and clean-tilled soils.

3bbdb8a15242.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/15%3A_Addressing_Compaction/15.03%3A_Relieving_and_Preventing_Compaction
3bbdb8a15242.sentence: The best long-term approach is to reduce tillage intensity (or eliminate tillage altogether), leave residue or mulch on the surface, plant cover crops, and improve aggregate stability with organic matter additions.

71b64897014d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/15%3A_Addressing_Compaction/15.03%3A_Relieving_and_Preventing_Compaction

fa98bbde6958.title: Pore structure
fa98bbde6958.sentence: Pore structure is a common term employed to characterize the porosity, pore size, pore size distribution, and pore morphology (such as pore shape, surface roughness, and tortuosity of pore channels) of a porous medium.

7b3d757405d8.title: Pore structure
7b3d757405d8.sentence: The pore structure and fluid flow in porous media are intimately related.

303f69a9a90f.title: Pore structure
303f69a9a90f.sentence: With micro nanoscale pore radii, complex connectivity, and significant heterogeneity, the complexity of the pore structure affects the hydraulic conductivity and retention capacity of these fluids.

169bab4228cd.title: Pore structure
169bab4228cd.sentence: The intrinsic permeability is the attribute primarily influenced by the pore structure, and the fundamental physical factors governing fluid flow and distribution are the grain surface-to-volume ratio and grain shape.

ee91a5ba4e6a.title: Pore structure
ee91a5ba4e6a.sentence: The idea that the pore space is made up of a network of channels through which fluid can flow is particularly helpful.

284b669f8f6f.title: Pore structure

1d1b9eecc4e0.title: Pore structure

ee285ca564d7.sentence: The relative abundance of each pore size in a typical volume of soil is represented by the pore size distribution.

eeec480554cd.sentence: It is represented by the function f(r), whose value is proportional to the total volume of all pores whose effective radius is within an infinitesimal range centered on r.

c6aca445a266.sentence: And f(r) can be thought to have textural and structural components.

170b032152a2.sentence: Big pores may be found in both large and tiny particles, including clays, which promote aggregation and therefore the development of large interaggregate pores.

ac2083473331.sentence: Subdivisions of a pore size distribution in randomly structured media can express more specific characteristics of soils with more complex conceptualizations, such as the hysteresis of soil water retention.

9d84ae6be7a6.sentence: Mercury intrusion porosimetry and gas adsorption are common techniques for determining the pore size distribution of materials and power sources.

c628dfaf7e56.sentence: Mercury porosimetry determines the pore size distribution and quantifies the associated incursion amount by applying pressure to the non-wetting mercury.

e494d484a276.sentence: The material must be robust enough to withstand the pressure since mercury intrusion requires 140 MPa of pressure for pores smaller than 10 nm.

b7d08acace7b.title: Pore structure
b7d08acace7b.sentence: The pore morphology is the shape, surface roughness, and tortuosity of pore channels representing the liquid and gaseous phases.

4bced5ac64dd.title: Macropore
4bced5ac64dd.sentence: Tortuosity is basically a ratio between the actual path length and the shortest distance between two points.

bd8e8ba6f8a2.title: Tortuosity
bd8e8ba6f8a2.sentence: Tortuosity is widely used as a critical parameter to predict transport properties of porous media, such as rocks and soils.

78b001c3f2d2.title: Tortuosity
78b001c3f2d2.sentence: Hydraulic, electrical, diffusional, and thermal tortuosities are defined to describe different transport processes in porous media, while geometrical tortuosity is introduced to characterize the morphological property of porous microstructures.

25d3e676a122.title: Tortuosity
25d3e676a122.sentence: But unlike other standard microstructural properties, the concept of tortuosity is vague with multiple definitions and various evaluation methods introduced in different contexts.

11d2e8a9c3ab.title: Tortuosity
11d2e8a9c3ab.sentence: The simplest mathematical method to estimate tortuosity is the arc-chord ratio: the ratio of the length of the curve (C) to the distance between its ends (L):

87a76793ebd0.title: Tortuosity
87a76793ebd0.sentence: In many engineering domains dealing with mass transfer in porous materials, such as hydrogeology or heterogeneous catalysis, the tortuosity refers to the ratio of the diffusivity in the free space to the diffusivity in the porous medium (analogous to arc-chord ratio of path).

875b4395e09e.title: Tortuosity
875b4395e09e.sentence: Strictly speaking, however, the effective diffusivity is proportional to the reciprocal of the square of the geometrical tortuosity

a4f69a157c28.title: Infiltration (hydrology)
a4f69a157c28.sentence: Infiltration is the process by which water on the ground surface enters the soil.

9d03ea449b41.title: Infiltration (hydrology)
9d03ea449b41.sentence: Infiltration is caused by multiple factors including; gravity, capillary forces, absorption, and osmosis.

16eef6673811.title: Infiltration (hydrology)
16eef6673811.sentence: Many soil characteristics can also play a role in determining the rate at which infiltration occurs.

6fbbdef3372b.title: Infiltration (hydrology)
6fbbdef3372b.sentence: The infiltration capacity is defined as the maximum rate of infiltration.

ae8272c55d3d.title: Infiltration (hydrology)
ae8272c55d3d.sentence: It is most often measured in meters per day but can also be measured in other units of distance over time if necessary.

f2d779698121.title: Infiltration (hydrology)
f2d779698121.sentence: The infiltration capacity decreases as the soil moisture content of soils surface layers increases.

91dce119591b.title: Infiltration (hydrology)
91dce119591b.sentence: If the precipitation rate exceeds the infiltration rate, runoff will usually occur unless there is some physical barrier.

0e703680841c.title: Infiltration (hydrology)
0e703680841c.sentence: If rainfall occurs at a rate faster than the infiltration capacity runoff will occur.

6404d9c86864.title: Infiltration (hydrology)
6404d9c86864.sentence: The process of infiltration can continue only if there is room available for additional water at the soil surface.

8107a0606d63.title: Infiltration (hydrology)
8107a0606d63.sentence: The available volume for additional water in the soil depends on the porosity of the soil and the rate at which previously infiltrated water can move away from the surface through the soil.

38f093844f50.title: Infiltration (hydrology)
38f093844f50.sentence: Robert E. Horton suggested that infiltration capacity rapidly declines during the early part of a storm and then tends towards an approximately constant value after a couple of hours for the remainder of the event.

77e1ce1d975f.title: Infiltration (hydrology)
77e1ce1d975f.sentence: Previously infiltrated water fills the available storage spaces and reduces the capillary forces drawing water into the pores.

3f2cd0a3527b.title: Infiltration (hydrology)
3f2cd0a3527b.sentence: Clay particles in the soil may swell as they become wet and thereby reduce the size of the pores.

02e1b5b672b0.title: Infiltration (hydrology)
02e1b5b672b0.sentence: In areas where the ground is not protected by a layer of forest litter, raindrops can detach soil particles from the surface and wash fine particles into surface pores where they can impede the infiltration process.

f6f30b240653.title: Soil moisture
f6f30b240653.sentence: Water infiltration rates range from 0.25 cm per hour for high clay soils to 2.5 cm per hour for sand and well stabilized and aggregated soil structures.

3a9290fea0fd.title: Infiltration (hydrology)
3a9290fea0fd.sentence: Infiltrometers, parameters and rainfall simulators are all devices that can be used to measure infiltration rates.

db3a83a7ca95.title: Permeability (porous media)
db3a83a7ca95.sentence: In fluid mechanics, materials science and Earth sciences, the permeability of porous media (often, a rock or soil) is a measure of the ability for fluids (gas or liquid) to flow through the media; it is commonly symbolized as k.

7dc703dd9a05.title: Permeability (porous media)
7dc703dd9a05.sentence: Fluids can more easily flow through a material with high permeability than one with low permeability.

88e1bb0b3774.title: Permeability (porous media)
88e1bb0b3774.sentence: The permeability of a medium is related to the porosity, but also to the shapes of the pores in the medium and their level of connectedness.

63224480691e.title: Permeability (porous media)
63224480691e.sentence: Permeability is also affected by the pressure inside a material.

e4aea8277b98.title: Permeability (porous media)
e4aea8277b98.sentence: The SI unit for permeability is the square metre (m2).

472292a3382f.title: Permeability (porous media)
472292a3382f.sentence: A practical unit for permeability is the darcy (d), or more commonly the millidarcy (md) (1 d ≈ 10^−12 m2).

21941d327e96.title: Permeability (porous media)
21941d327e96.sentence: The name honors the French Engineer Henry Darcy who first described the flow of water through sand filters for potable water supply.

31fed4fe74ff.title: Permeability (porous media)
31fed4fe74ff.sentence: Permeability values for most materials commonly range typically from a fraction to several thousand millidarcys.

f80fa4ed231b.title: Permeability (porous media)
f80fa4ed231b.sentence: Unconsolidated sands may have permeabilities of over 5000 md.

8cbec9e9f48c.title: Permeability (porous media)
8cbec9e9f48c.sentence: The global proportionality constant for the flow of water through a porous medium is called the hydraulic conductivity (K, unit: m/s).

f979a0eef64a.title: Permeability (porous media)
f979a0eef64a.sentence: Permeability, or intrinsic permeability, (k, unit: m2) is a part of this, and is a specific property characteristic of the solid skeleton and the microstructure of the porous medium itself, independently of the nature and properties of the fluid flowing through the pores of the medium.

eb6b39626538.title: Permeability (porous media)
eb6b39626538.sentence: This allows to take into account the effect of temperature on the viscosity of the fluid flowing though the porous medium and to address other fluids than pure water, e.g., concentrated brines, petroleum, or organic solvents.

0c0574182241.title: Permeability (porous media)
0c0574182241.sentence: Permeability is typically determined in the lab by application of Darcy's law under steady state conditions or, more generally, by application of various solutions to the diffusion equation for unsteady flow conditions.

8af47a628f21.title: Permeability (porous media)
8af47a628f21.sentence: Permeability needs to be measured, either directly (using Darcy's law), or through estimation using empirically derived formulas.

6fa7a55c377a.title: Permeability (porous media)
6fa7a55c377a.sentence: However, for some simple models of porous media, permeability can be calculated (e.g., random close packing of identical spheres).

768ecad3bfd4.title: Permeability (porous media)
768ecad3bfd4.sentence: The concept of permeability is of importance in determining the flow characteristics of hydrocarbons in oil and gas reservoirs, and of groundwater in aquifers.

d2a85cc2f4d1.title: Permeability (porous media)
d2a85cc2f4d1.sentence: The concept also has many practical applications outside of geology, for example in chemical engineering (e.g., filtration), as well as in Civil Engineering when determining whether the ground conditions of a site are suitable for construction.

884d199a5d10.title: Permeability (porous media)
884d199a5d10.sentence: In naturally occurring materials, the permeability values range over many orders of magnitude (see table below for an example of this range).

fef051b57cbe.title: Permeability (porous media)

7d6446229a3a.title: Permeability (porous media)

a9f9f27572c0.title: Water content
a9f9f27572c0.sentence: Water content or moisture content is the quantity of water contained in a material, such as soil (called soil moisture), rock, ceramics, crops, or wood.

26f5b8aa3453.title: Water content
26f5b8aa3453.sentence: It is expressed as a ratio, which can range from 0 (completely dry) to the value of the materials' porosity at saturation.

f99fc61375df.title: Water content
f99fc61375df.sentence: It can be given on a volumetric or gravimetric (mass) basis.

7a28fc7f0fa2.title: Water content
7a28fc7f0fa2.sentence: Volumetric water content, θ, is defined mathematically as:

a8a7db27192f.title: Water content
a8a7db27192f.sentence: Gravimetric water content is expressed by mass (weight) as follows:

c4b49c66ea97.title: Water content
c4b49c66ea97.sentence: However, woodworking, geotechnics and soil science require the gravimetric moisture content to be expressed with respect to the sample's dry weight:

227cc6903d91.title: Water content
227cc6903d91.sentence: To convert gravimetric water content to volumetric water content, multiply the gravimetric water content by the bulk specific gravity SG of the material:

7ccfddb7ad0c.title: Water content
7ccfddb7ad0c.section: Classification and uses > Earth and agricultural sciences
7ccfddb7ad0c.sentence: In soil science, hydrology and agricultural sciences, water content has an important role for groundwater recharge, agriculture, and soil chemistry.

169d544e6dc7.title: Water content
169d544e6dc7.section: Classification and uses > Earth and agricultural sciences
169d544e6dc7.sentence: Observations have revealed generally that spatial variance in water content tends to increase as overall wetness increases in semiarid regions, to decrease as overall wetness increases in humid regions, and to peak under intermediate wetness conditions in temperate regions.

984f3e43431b.title: Soil moisture
984f3e43431b.sentence: Soil moisture is the water content of the soil.

382f7738e20b.title: Soil moisture
382f7738e20b.sentence: It can be expressed in terms of volume or weight.

b8b1ff829751.title: Soil moisture
b8b1ff829751.sentence: Water that enters a field is removed from it by runoff, drainage, evaporation or transpiration.

b460fdd893c9.title: Soil moisture
b460fdd893c9.sentence: Runoff is the water that flows on the surface to the edge of the field; drainage is the water that flows through the soil downward or toward the edge of the field underground; evaporative water loss from a field is that part of the water that evaporates into the atmosphere directly from the field's surface; transpiration is the loss of water from the field by its evaporation from the plant itself.

3c3dfb678679.title: Soil moisture
3c3dfb678679.sentence: Water affects soil formation, structure, stability and erosion but is of primary concern with respect to plant growth.

542f71f751bc.title: Soil moisture
542f71f751bc.sentence: - It constitutes 80–95% of the plant's protoplasm.

76d8ed9ce833.title: Soil moisture
76d8ed9ce833.sentence: - It is the solvent in which nutrients are carried to, into and throughout the plant.

f24b465532fd.title: Soil moisture
f24b465532fd.sentence: - It provides the turgidity by which the plant keeps itself in proper position.

716b0622d1f6.title: Soil moisture
716b0622d1f6.sentence: In a loam soil, solids constitute half the volume, gas one-quarter of the volume, and water one-quarter of the volume of which only half will be available to most plants, with a strong variation according to matric potential.

9c21b48ff236.title: Soil moisture
9c21b48ff236.sentence: Water moves in soil under the influence of gravity, osmosis and capillarity.

3a32074275fb.title: Soil moisture
3a32074275fb.sentence: As a plant grows, its roots remove water from the largest pores (macropores) first.

f579c4b05dc3.title: Soil moisture
f579c4b05dc3.sentence: Soon the larger pores hold only air, and the remaining water is found only in the intermediate- and smallest-sized pores (micropores).

f82602ac564e.title: Soil moisture
f82602ac564e.sentence: The water in the smallest pores is so strongly held to particle surfaces that plant roots cannot pull it away.

acbe34c8eeaa.title: Soil moisture
acbe34c8eeaa.sentence: Consequently, not all soil water is available to plants, with a strong dependence on texture.

0e0dea8cfa0d.title: Soil moisture
0e0dea8cfa0d.sentence: In addition, water alters the soil profile by dissolving and re-depositing mineral and organic solutes and colloids, often at lower levels, a process called leaching.

c1905aed9aa8.title: Soil moisture
c1905aed9aa8.sentence: Soil moisture measurement can be based on in situ probes (e.g., capacitance probes, neutron probes) or remote sensing methods.

acbc83835215.title: Drainage
acbc83835215.sentence: Drainage is the natural or artificial removal of a surface's water and sub-surface water from an area with excess water.

f50d2a6fc72b.title: Drainage
f50d2a6fc72b.sentence: The internal drainage of most agricultural soils can prevent severe waterlogging (anaerobic conditions that harm root growth), but many soils need artificial drainage to improve production or to manage water supplies.

4ced695cbb10.title: Drainage
4ced695cbb10.sentence: The Indus Valley Civilization had sewerage and drainage systems.

303dc6862be6.title: Drainage
303dc6862be6.sentence: All houses in the major cities of Harappa and Mohenjo-daro had access to water and drainage facilities.

069b19e9f59c.title: Drainage
069b19e9f59c.sentence: The invention of hollow-pipe drainage is credited to Sir Hugh Dalrymple, who died in 1753.

2895ac2fae4c.title: Drainage
2895ac2fae4c.sentence: Simple infrastructure such as open drains, pipes, and berms are still common.

f9e2dffb7713.title: Drainage
f9e2dffb7713.sentence: In modern times, more complex structures involving substantial earthworks and new technologies have been common as well.

df8f2076cbdd.title: Drainage
df8f2076cbdd.sentence: - Surface drains are typically used to manage runoff from paved surfaces, such as sidewalks and parking lots.

9fa3cdc06648.title: Drainage
9fa3cdc06648.sentence: - Subsurface drains, on the other hand, are designed to manage water that seeps into the soil beneath the planting surface.

3e1f3c9f9ccb.title: Drainage
3e1f3c9f9ccb.sentence: French drains, which are gravel-filled trenches with perforated pipes at the bottom, are the most common type of subsurface drain.

29543ca2b441.title: Drainage
29543ca2b441.sentence: Typical retaining walls are constructed of impermeable material, which can block the path of groundwater.

beddac44d756.title: Drainage
beddac44d756.sentence: When groundwater flow is obstructed, hydrostatic water pressure buildups against the wall and may cause significant damage.

c006c774d7b9.title: Drainage
c006c774d7b9.sentence: If the water pressure is not drained appropriately, retaining walls can bow, move, and fracture, causing seams to separate.

494708317970.title: Drainage
494708317970.sentence: The water pressure can also erode soil particles, leading to voids behind the wall and sinkholes in the above soil.

b938093de838.title: Drainage
b938093de838.section: Current practices > In the construction industry
b938093de838.sentence: Typically, most jurisdictions have some body of drainage law to govern to what degree a landowner can alter the drainage from their parcel.

8d5a0979f4e5.title: Hydraulic conductivity
8d5a0979f4e5.sentence: In science and engineering, hydraulic conductivity (K, in SI units of meters per second) is a property of porous materials, soils and rocks, that describes the ease with which a fluid (usually water) can move through the pore space, or fracture network.

18ee4bdf01ab.title: Hydraulic conductivity
18ee4bdf01ab.sentence: It depends on the intrinsic permeability (k, unit: m2) of the material, the degree of saturation, and on the density and viscosity of the fluid.

fd921136d3c3.title: Hydraulic conductivity
fd921136d3c3.sentence: By definition, hydraulic conductivity is the ratio of volume flux to hydraulic gradient yielding a quantitative measure of a saturated soil's ability to transmit water when subjected to a hydraulic gradient.

6532370f38ba.title: Hydraulic conductivity
6532370f38ba.sentence: Saturated hydraulic conductivity, Ksat, describes water movement through saturated media.

ab7f2c70dbe2.title: Hydraulic conductivity
ab7f2c70dbe2.sentence: Because of their high porosity and permeability, sand and gravel aquifers have higher hydraulic conductivity than clay or unfractured granite aquifers.

aeb3ff732322.title: Hydraulic conductivity
aeb3ff732322.sentence: Sand or gravel aquifers would thus be easier to extract water from (e.g., using a pumping well) because of their high transmissivity, compared to clay or unfractured bedrock aquifers.

3bd05e6ee36e.title: Hydraulic conductivity
3bd05e6ee36e.sentence: - range over many orders of magnitude (the distribution is often considered to be lognormal),

6168f5b51c2f.title: Hydraulic conductivity
6168f5b51c2f.sentence: - vary a large amount through space (sometimes considered to be randomly spatially distributed, or stochastic in nature),

97630723cab0.title: Hydraulic conductivity
97630723cab0.sentence: - are directional (in general K is a symmetric second-rank tensor; e.g., vertical K values can be several orders of magnitude smaller than horizontal K values),

b1652102aaba.title: Hydraulic conductivity
b1652102aaba.sentence: - are scale dependent (testing a m³ of aquifer will generally produce different results than a similar test on only a cm³ sample of the same aquifer),

677f75fc9e41.title: Hydraulic conductivity
677f75fc9e41.sentence: - are very dependent (in a non-linear way) on the water content, which makes solving the unsaturated flow equation difficult.

98d78edeb309.title: Hydraulic conductivity
98d78edeb309.sentence: In fact, the variably saturated K for a single material varies over a wider range than the saturated K values for all types of materials (see chart below for an illustrative range of the latter).

09e1ada49ea1.title: Hydraulic conductivity
09e1ada49ea1.sentence: - In the experimental approach the hydraulic conductivity is determined from hydraulic experiments that are interpreted using Darcy's law.

7fdbb44c4190.title: Hydraulic conductivity
7fdbb44c4190.sentence: Hydraulic conductivity has units with dimensions of length per time (e.g., m/s, ft/day and (gal/day)/ft2); transmissivity then has units with dimensions of length squared per time.

483c02b75983.title: Water potential
483c02b75983.sentence: Water potential is the potential energy of water per unit volume relative to pure water in reference conditions.

1abc70135814.title: Water potential
1abc70135814.sentence: Water potential quantifies the tendency of water to move from one area to another due to osmosis, gravity, mechanical pressure and matrix effects such as capillary action (which is caused by surface tension).

63d984a45018.title: Water potential
63d984a45018.sentence: If the flow is not restricted, water will move from an area of higher water potential to an area that is lower potential.

8a7ecedb0552.title: Water potential
8a7ecedb0552.sentence: For example, the addition of solutes lowers the potential (negative vector), while an increase in pressure increases the potential (positive vector).

b1bd06e7d55d.title: Water potential
b1bd06e7d55d.sentence: Water potential is typically expressed in potential energy per unit volume and very often is represented by the Greek letter ψ.

287da79be8e1.title: Water potential
287da79be8e1.sentence: Different conditions are also defined as reference depending on the application: for example, in soils, the reference condition is typically defined as pure water at the soil surface.

2823f6de768e.title: Soil moisture
2823f6de768e.sentence: Total water potential is a sum of matric potential which results from capillary action, osmotic potential for saline soil, and gravitational potential when dealing with downward water movement.

bcb198a071c7.title: Water potential
bcb198a071c7.sentence: At a potential of 0 kPa, the soil is in a saturation state.

c7cac11b1d63.title: Water potential
c7cac11b1d63.sentence: At a potential of −33 kPa, or −1/3 bar, (−10 kPa for sand), soil is at field capacity.

adbed2d30985.title: Water potential
adbed2d30985.sentence: At a potential of −1500 kPa, the soil is at its permanent wilting point, at which plant roots cannot extract the water through osmotic diffusion.

fb18026a7e45.title: Water potential
fb18026a7e45.sentence: In contrast, atmospheric water potentials are much more negative—a typical value for dry air is −100 MPa, though this value depends on the temperature and the humidity.

ae1c6798cdbc.title: Water potential
ae1c6798cdbc.sentence: Root water potential must be more negative than the soil, and the stem water potential must be an intermediate lower value than the roots but higher than the leaf water potential to create a passive flow of water from the soil to the roots, up the stem, to the leaves and then into the atmosphere.

1e74b4586914.title: Water potential
1e74b4586914.sentence: A tensiometer, electrical resistance gypsum block, neutron probes, or time-domain reflectometry (TDR) can be used to determine soil water potential energy.

5dd0391c6c17.title: Water potential
5dd0391c6c17.sentence: Tensiometers are limited to 0 to −85 kPa, electrical resistance blocks are limited to −90 to −1500 kPa, neutron probes are limited to 0 to −1500 kPa, and a TDR is limited to 0 to −10,000 kPa.

90a80121ab0a.title: Darcy's law
90a80121ab0a.sentence: Darcy's law is an equation that describes the flow of a fluid through a porous medium and through a Hele-Shaw cell.

532097228844.title: Darcy's law
532097228844.sentence: The law was formulated by Henry Darcy based on results of experiments on the flow of water through beds of sand, forming the basis of hydrogeology, a branch of earth sciences.

36a86506ce74.title: Darcy's law
36a86506ce74.sentence: Since the 1830s, French hydraulic engineer Henry Darcy studied flow rate of water in sand filters in an attempt to improve the municipal water system of the city of Dijon, France.

65bdcbfd3451.title: Darcy's law
65bdcbfd3451.sentence: He established his law empirically and published it in a construction report in 1856.

a9a97c5c1385.title: Darcy's law
a9a97c5c1385.sentence: It is analogous to Ohm's law in electrostatics, linearly relating the volume flow rate of the fluid to the hydraulic head difference (which is often just proportional to the pressure difference) via the hydraulic conductivity.

0d639a23ed35.title: Darcy's law
0d639a23ed35.sentence: The flux vector is analogous to the current density, head is analogous to voltage, and hydraulic conductivity is analogous to electrical conductivity.)

ebed0c37deaf.title: Darcy's law
ebed0c37deaf.sentence: The proportionality constant is linked to the permeability k of the medium, the dynamic viscosity of the fluid μ, the given distance L over which the pressure drop is computed, and the cross-sectional area A, in the form: Q=kAμLΔp

edb896187e55.title: Darcy's law
edb896187e55.sentence: Notice that the quantity 𝐪, often referred to as the Darcy flux or Darcy velocity, is not the velocity at which the fluid is travelling through the pores.

52728b210c3a.title: Darcy's law
52728b210c3a.sentence: It is the volumetric flux, or flow rate per unit area (See Flux Flummoxed, Ground Water.

dd20c6a99436.title: Darcy's law
dd20c6a99436.sentence: The flow velocity (u) is related to the flux (q) by the porosity (φ) with the following equation:

fea75b159d0e.title: Darcy's law
fea75b159d0e.sentence: - if there is no pressure gradient over a distance, no flow occurs (these are hydrostatic conditions),

24ddfb405849.title: Darcy's law
24ddfb405849.sentence: - if there is a pressure gradient, flow will occur from high pressure towards low pressure (opposite the direction of increasing gradient — hence the negative sign in Darcy's law),

03bc9dae967e.title: Darcy's law
03bc9dae967e.sentence: - the greater the pressure gradient (through the same formation material), the greater the discharge rate, and

0680e0b32df4.title: Darcy's law
0680e0b32df4.sentence: - the discharge rate of fluid will often be different — through different formation materials (or even through the same material, in a different direction) — even if the same pressure gradient exists in both cases.

97afe067250a.title: Darcy's law
97afe067250a.sentence: Darcy's law is only valid for slow, viscous flow; however, most groundwater flow cases fall in this category.

294eccb276e3.title: Darcy's law
294eccb276e3.sentence: Typically any flow with a Reynolds number less than one is clearly laminar, and it would be valid to apply Darcy's law.

984cc885f086.title: Darcy's law
984cc885f086.sentence: Experimental tests have shown that flow regimes with Reynolds numbers up to 10 may still be Darcian, as in the case of groundwater flow.

102a1dfd6e46.title: Darcy's law
102a1dfd6e46.sentence: Coarse-grained sediments also behave similarly, but in very coarse-grained sediments, the flow may be turbulent.

8eb33a3de578.title: Darcy's law
8eb33a3de578.sentence: In fact, Darcy's law is a special case of the Stokes equation for the momentum flux, in turn deriving from the momentum Navier–Stokes equation.

ea612b761d94.title: Darcy's law
ea612b761d94.sentence: Darcy's law is analogous to Fourier's law in the field of heat conduction, Ohm's law in the field of electrical networks, and Fick's law in diffusion theory.

8db0412c95b6.title: Soil water (retention)
8db0412c95b6.sentence: Soils can process and hold considerable amounts of water.

071d091e91a1.title: Soil water (retention)
071d091e91a1.sentence: Some of this water will steadily drain through the soil (via gravity) and end up in the waterways and streams, but much of it will be retained, despite the influence of gravity.

1307077e6b75.title: Soil water (retention)
1307077e6b75.sentence: They can take in water, and will keep doing so until they are full, or until the rate at which they can transmit water into and through the pores is exceeded.

57fab681ce2a.title: Soil water (retention)
57fab681ce2a.sentence: Much of this retained water can be used by plants and other organisms, also contributing to land productivity and soil health.

3f9004b8dd8c.title: Soil water (retention)
3f9004b8dd8c.sentence: The soil's ability to retain water is strongly related to particle size; water molecules hold more tightly to the fine particles of a clay soil than to coarser particles of a sandy soil, so clays generally retain more water.

6837f113ec1d.title: Soil water (retention)
6837f113ec1d.sentence: Conversely, sands provide easier passage or transmission of water through the profile.

a5c5aeb258ac.title: Soil water (retention)
a5c5aeb258ac.sentence: Clay type, organic content, and soil structure also influence soil water retention.

ec08773dfa67.title: Soil water (retention)
ec08773dfa67.sentence: Roughly speaking for agriculture (top layer soil), soil is 25% water, 25% air, 45% mineral, 5% other; water varies widely from about 1% to 90% due to several retention and drainage properties of a given soil.

586c39b90d8f.title: Soil water (retention)
586c39b90d8f.section: Soil water retention capacity > Soil water retention and organism
586c39b90d8f.sentence: It provides an ongoing supply of water to plants between periods of replenishment (infiltration), so as to allow their continued growth and survival.

1711833d228c.title: Soil water (retention)
1711833d228c.section: Soil water retention capacity > Soil water retention and organism
1711833d228c.sentence: For example, over much of temperate Victoria, Australia, this effect is seasonal and even inter-annual; the retained soil water that has accumulated in preceding wet winters permits survival of most perennial plants over typically dry summers when monthly evaporation exceeds rainfall.

990496f0e7be.title: Soil water (retention)
990496f0e7be.section: Soil water retention capacity > Soil water retention, water balance, and other influences
990496f0e7be.sentence: - Soil water that is not retained or used by plants may continue downward through the profile and contribute to the water table (the permanently saturated zone at the base of the profile); this is termed "recharge".

b8f6c69e0425.title: Soil water (retention)
b8f6c69e0425.section: Soil water retention capacity > Soil water retention, water balance, and other influences
b8f6c69e0425.sentence: Soil that is at field capacity (among other reasons) may preclude infiltration so to increase overland flow.

6e129756dbda.title: Soil water (retention)
6e129756dbda.section: Soil water retention capacity > Soil water retention, water balance, and other influences
6e129756dbda.sentence: - Soil water can affect the structural integrity or coherence of a soil; saturated soils can become unstable and result in structural failure and mass movement.

883ddff13be5.title: Soil water (retention)
883ddff13be5.section: Soil water retention capacity > Soil water retention, water balance, and other influences
883ddff13be5.sentence: Soil water, its changes over time and management are of interest to geo-technicians and soil conservationists with an interest in maintaining soil stability.

a1f7f344c7ca.title: Water retention curve
a1f7f344c7ca.sentence: Water retention curve is the relationship between the water content, θ, and the soil water potential, ψ.

196c40f96a3d.title: Water retention curve
196c40f96a3d.sentence: The soil moisture curve is characteristic for different soil types, and is also called the soil moisture characteristic.

3cd66f47a1b4.title: Water retention curve
3cd66f47a1b4.sentence: It is used to predict soil water storage, plant water supply (field capacity) and soil aggregate stability.

e2bcd86180dc.title: Water retention curve
e2bcd86180dc.sentence: At potentials close to zero, the soil is close to saturation, and water is held in the soil primarily by capillary forces.

e71cdedb5f4a.title: Water retention curve
e71cdedb5f4a.sentence: As θ decreases, binding of the water becomes stronger, and at small potentials (more negative, approaching wilting point) water is strongly bound in the smallest of pores, at contact points between grains and as films bound by adsorptive forces around particles.

2257344cab44.title: Water retention curve
2257344cab44.sentence: Sandy soils will involve mainly capillary binding, and will therefore release most of the water at higher potentials, while clayey soils, with adhesive and osmotic binding, will release water at lower (more negative) potentials.

b7792f12e1c0.title: Water retention curve
b7792f12e1c0.sentence: At any given potential, peaty soils will usually display much higher moisture contents than clayey soils, which would be expected to hold more water than sandy soils.

836b6471a90b.title: Water retention curve
836b6471a90b.sentence: The water holding capacity of any soil is due to the porosity and the nature of the bonding in the soil.

ca3b4bc1e99d.title: Water retention curve
ca3b4bc1e99d.sentence: Due to the hysteretic effect of water filling and draining the pores, different wetting and drying curves may be distinguished.

1506d8eb8bab.title: Water retention curve
1506d8eb8bab.sentence: In 1907, Edgar Buckingham created the first water retention curve.

939069274e1d.title: Water retention curve
939069274e1d.sentence: It was measured and made for six soils varying in texture from sand to clay.

34e725af3528.title: Water retention curve
34e725af3528.sentence: The data came from experiments made on soil columns 48 inch tall, where a constant water level maintained about 2 inches above the bottom through periodic addition of water from a side tube.

06627bd3ffad.title: Water table
06627bd3ffad.sentence: The water table is the upper surface of the phreatic zone or zone of saturation.

639f655a2409.title: Water table
639f655a2409.sentence: It can also be simply explained as the depth below which the ground is saturated.

604b8befdc5b.title: Water table
604b8befdc5b.sentence: The zone of saturation is where the pores and fractures of the ground are saturated with groundwater, which may be fresh, saline, or brackish, depending on the locality.

0c8259f3338d.title: Water table
0c8259f3338d.sentence: The portion above the water table is the vadose zone.

20263860924d.title: Water table
20263860924d.sentence: In coarse soils, the water table settles at the surface where the water pressure head is equal to the atmospheric pressure (where gauge pressure = 0).

e022510cf086.title: Water table
e022510cf086.sentence: In soils where capillary action is strong, the water table is pulled upward, forming a capillary fringe.

f60101d3e70a.title: Water table
f60101d3e70a.sentence: The water table may vary due to seasonal changes such as precipitation and evapotranspiration.

9e681e32196c.title: Water table
9e681e32196c.sentence: In some regions, for example, Great Britain or California, winter precipitation is often higher than summer precipitation and so the groundwater storage is not fully recharged in summer.

44d4e1192457.title: Water table
44d4e1192457.sentence: Consequently, the water table is lower during the summer.

32ec1bebe4f9.title: Water table
32ec1bebe4f9.sentence: This disparity between the level of the winter and summer water table is known as the "zone of intermittent saturation", wherein the water table will fluctuate in response to climatic conditions.

1678a13822dc.title: Water table
1678a13822dc.sentence: Within an aquifer, the water table is rarely horizontal, but reflects the surface relief due to the capillary effect (capillary fringe) in soils, sediments and other porous media.

57a8bd74ac52.title: Water table
57a8bd74ac52.sentence: The slope of the water table is known as the "hydraulic gradient", which depends on the rate at which water is added to and removed from the aquifer and the permeability of the material.

48be83d4ec62.title: Water table
48be83d4ec62.sentence: Springs, rivers, lakes and oases occur when the water table reaches the surface.

12c5b22fefc6.title: Water table

cbe60276a8e5.title: Macropore
cbe60276a8e5.sentence: In soil, macropores are defined as cavities that are larger than 75 μm.

19c5f432e497.title: Macropore
19c5f432e497.sentence: Functionally, pores of this size host preferential soil solution flow and rapid transport of solutes and colloids.

86974835c87a.title: Macropore
86974835c87a.sentence: Macropores increase the hydraulic conductivity of soil, allowing water to infiltrate and drain quickly, and shallow groundwater to move relatively rapidly via lateral flow.

91d8a27b100d.title: Macropore
91d8a27b100d.sentence: The larger spaces between aggregates are called macropores.

8a846c6b93f1.title: Macropore
8a846c6b93f1.sentence: Macropores can also be found in soil between larger individual mineral particles such as sand or gravel.

d2582db6602a.title: Macropore
d2582db6602a.sentence: Macropores can be formed under the influence of physical processes such as wet/dry and freeze/thaw cycles, which result in cracks and fissures of soils.

dd52a3b393b1.title: Macropore
dd52a3b393b1.sentence: Macropores created by biological activities are also called biopores.

7ecaf2ee05b1.title: Macropore
7ecaf2ee05b1.sentence: Soil fauna, especially burrowing species such as earthworms, contributes to the formation of macropores with their movement and activities in soils.

1c24b995d32e.title: Macropore
1c24b995d32e.sentence: In general, the formation of macropore is negatively related to soil depth as these physical and biological processes diminish with depth.

8044aee75183.title: Macropore
8044aee75183.section: Importance of soil macropores > Water and air movement
8044aee75183.sentence: Water can move freely under the influence of gravity in soil macropores when compared to micropores (much smaller pores in soils) where water is held by capillary forces.

c14eb1e97bd8.title: Physical properties of soil
c14eb1e97bd8.sentence: Pore size varies considerably; the smallest pores (cryptopores; <0.1 μm) hold water too tightly for use by plant roots; plant-available water is held in ultramicropores, micropores and mesopores (0.1–75 μm); and macropores (>75 μm) are generally air-filled when the soil is at field capacity.

2a5e55ea4418.title: Macropore
2a5e55ea4418.section: Importance of soil macropores > Water and air movement
2a5e55ea4418.sentence: Such attributes of macropores will allow fast movement of water into and across soils, that can significantly improve soil infiltration rate and permeability.

ab99ac00e6c3.title: Macropore
ab99ac00e6c3.section: Importance of soil macropores > Water and air movement
ab99ac00e6c3.sentence: It also contributes to groundwater recharge that replenish water resources.

66c895c89a6e.title: Macropore

66c895c89a6e.sentence: An extended network of macropores helps to improve gas exchange between soil and the atmosphere, especially when these macropores are connected to soil surface.

e9c198142def.title: Macropore
e9c198142def.section: Importance of soil macropores > Solute and pollutant transport
e9c198142def.sentence: For example, excessive nitrate converted from nitrogen fertilizers can be washed into groundwater under heavy rainfall or irrigation.

3271584d333b.title: Macropore
3271584d333b.sentence: This is particularly true to soils that are constantly subject to human disturbance, such as tilled agricultural fields where the shape and size of macropores can be altered by tillage.

d192f85c5a92.title: Macropore
d192f85c5a92.sentence: Soil macropores are easily affected by soil compaction.

ce712ca8c54f.title: Macropore
ce712ca8c54f.sentence: Compacted soils, for example in forest landings, usually have a low macropore proportion (macro-porosity) with impeded water movement.

c860df591ebf.title: Macropore
c860df591ebf.sentence: Organic matter can be incorporated into disturbed soils to improve their macro-porosity and related soil functions

6e4416d1dcea.title: Macropore
6e4416d1dcea.sentence: Within the context of porous solids (i.e., not porous aggregations such as soil), colloid and surface chemists define macropores as cavities that are larger than 50 nm.

a7de61c77260.title: Soil science
a7de61c77260.sentence: Depression storage capacity, in soil science, is the ability of a particular area of land to retain water in its pits and depressions, thus preventing it from flowing.

00b393adacd6.title: Soil science
00b393adacd6.sentence: Depression storage capacity, along with infiltration capacity, is one of the main factors involved in Horton overland flow, whereby water volume surpasses both infiltration and depression storage capacity and begins to flow horizontally across land, possibly leading to flooding and soil erosion.

dd85483ad06d.title: Soil science
dd85483ad06d.sentence: The study of land's depression storage capacity is important in the fields of geology, ecology, and especially hydrology.

acf06d89c755.title: Hydraulic head
acf06d89c755.sentence: Hydraulic head or piezometric head is a measurement related to liquid pressure (normalized by specific weight) and the liquid elevation above a vertical datum.

af6f2d953669.title: Hydraulic head
af6f2d953669.sentence: It is usually measured as an equivalent liquid surface elevation, expressed in units of length, at the entrance (or bottom) of a piezometer.

dabb9e666563.title: Hydraulic head

948a522767ca.title: Hydraulic head
948a522767ca.sentence: The total hydraulic head of a fluid is composed of pressure head and elevation head.

7bbbbd79fd73.title: Infiltrometer
7bbbbd79fd73.sentence: An infiltrometer is a device used to measure the rate of water infiltration into soil or other porous media.

1dbe95260f2c.title: Infiltrometer
1dbe95260f2c.sentence: Commonly used infiltrometers are single-ring and double-ring infiltrometers, disc permeameters, and falling head infiltrometers.

85a781e0492a.title: Infiltrometer
85a781e0492a.sentence: A single-ring infiltrometer involves driving a ring into the soil and supplying water in the ring either at constant head or falling head condition.

695d00a84c72.title: Infiltrometer
695d00a84c72.sentence: The supplying of water is done with a Mariotte's bottle.

4c90ccd8dfe6.title: Infiltrometer
4c90ccd8dfe6.sentence: Falling head refers to condition where water is supplied in the ring, and the water is allowed to drop with time.

97d59835724c.title: Infiltrometer
97d59835724c.sentence: The operator records how much water goes into the soil for a given time period.

bb03acc4770d.title: Infiltrometer
bb03acc4770d.sentence: Because infiltration capacity is the maximum infiltration rate, and if infiltration rate exceeds the infiltration capacity, runoff will be the consequence, therefore maintaining constant head means the rate of water supplied corresponds to the infiltration capacity.

293f504ef49b.title: Infiltrometer
293f504ef49b.sentence: The rate of which water goes into the soil is related to the soil's hydraulic conductivity.

90b7db4f17e7.title: Infiltrometer

f3e5efe7a0ad.title: Infiltrometer

ef0295c469f5.title: Infiltrometer
