1435c0ecc0a1.title: Disc permeameter
1435c0ecc0a1.sentence: Single and double ring infiltrometer only measures flow under ponded (saturated) conditions, and when used in soil with distinct macropores, preferential flow will dominate the flow.

937a1d57cbbb.title: Infiltration (hydrology)
937a1d57cbbb.sentence: The amount, type, and duration of precipitation all have an impact.

e366aefc23f1.title: Infiltration (hydrology)
e366aefc23f1.sentence: Rainfall leads to faster infiltration rates than any other precipitation event, such as snow or sleet.

53b9cc5b7386.title: Infiltration (hydrology)
53b9cc5b7386.sentence: Initially when the precipitation event first starts the infiltration is occurring rapidly as the soil is unsaturated, but as time continues the infiltration rate slows as the soil becomes more saturated.

594338e0fd16.title: Infiltration (hydrology)
594338e0fd16.section: Factors that affect infiltration > Soil characteristics
594338e0fd16.sentence: Soils that have smaller pore sizes, such as clay, have lower infiltration capacity and slower infiltration rates than soils that have large pore sizes, such as sands.

bbc842e62c2a.title: Infiltration (hydrology)
bbc842e62c2a.section: Factors that affect infiltration > Soil characteristics
bbc842e62c2a.sentence: One exception to this rule is when the clay is present in dry conditions.

4e2a767a8e37.title: Infiltration (hydrology)
4e2a767a8e37.section: Factors that affect infiltration > Soil characteristics
4e2a767a8e37.sentence: In this case, the soil can develop large cracks which lead to higher infiltration capacity.

68751dfa2529.title: Infiltration (hydrology)
68751dfa2529.section: Factors that affect infiltration > Soil characteristics
68751dfa2529.sentence: Compaction of soils results in decreased porosity within the soils, which decreases infiltration capacity.

5e21d187ecd5.title: Infiltration (hydrology)
5e21d187ecd5.section: Factors that affect infiltration > Soil characteristics
5e21d187ecd5.sentence: Hydrophobic soils can develop after wildfires have happened, which can greatly diminish or completely prevent infiltration from occurring.

2dc2ff183b53.title: Infiltration (hydrology)
2dc2ff183b53.section: Factors that affect infiltration > Soil moisture content
2dc2ff183b53.sentence: When soil is partially saturated then infiltration can occur at a moderate rate and fully unsaturated soils have the highest infiltration capacity.

93be069c2a78.title: Infiltration (hydrology)
93be069c2a78.section: Factors that affect infiltration > Soil moisture content
93be069c2a78.sentence: Soil that is already saturated has no more capacity to hold more water, therefore infiltration capacity has been reached and the rate cannot increase past this point.

5befe53e3898.title: Infiltration (hydrology)
5befe53e3898.section: Factors that affect infiltration > Organic materials in soils
5befe53e3898.sentence: Vegetation contains roots that extend into the soil which create cracks and fissures in the soil, allowing for more rapid infiltration and increased capacity.

422dd923113b.title: Infiltration (hydrology)
422dd923113b.section: Factors that affect infiltration > Organic materials in soils
422dd923113b.sentence: Similarly to vegetation, animals that burrow in the soil also create cracks in the soil structure.

3cd152552103.title: Infiltration (hydrology)
3cd152552103.section: Factors that affect infiltration > Organic materials in soils
3cd152552103.sentence: When no vegetation is present infiltration rates can be very low, which can lead to excessive runoff and increased erosion levels.

8164105745d9.title: Infiltration (hydrology)
8164105745d9.section: Factors that affect infiltration > Land cover

d8daccec0989.title: Infiltration (hydrology)

403c444f268c.title: Infiltration (hydrology)
403c444f268c.sentence: When the slope of the land is higher runoff occurs more readily which leads to lower infiltration rates.

c5c1ea636b03.title: Alkali soil
c5c1ea636b03.sentence: Alkali or alkaline soils are clay soils with high pH (generally greater than 8.5), often accompanied by poor soil structure and low infiltration capacity.

ebca7b3528ce.title: Alkali soil
ebca7b3528ce.sentence: Due to the low infiltration capacity, rainwater tends to stagnate on the soil surface and evaporate before it can be used by plant crops, and in dry periods, cultivation is hardly possible without copious irrigation and good drainage.

08f920f8dea6.title: Infiltration (hydrology)
08f920f8dea6.sentence: There are several ways to estimate the volume and water infiltration rate into the soil.

cd2a117d28e5.title: Infiltration (hydrology)
cd2a117d28e5.sentence: Infiltration is a component of the general mass balance hydrologic budget.

56f594247d11.title: Infiltration (hydrology)

5f0f58704979.title: Infiltration (hydrology)

d811cae456fc.sentence: At 0 to 33 kPa suction (field capacity), water is pushed through soil from the point of its application under the force of gravity and the pressure gradient created by differences in the pressure of water; this is called saturated flow.

b602ec556732.sentence: At higher suction, water movement is pulled by capillarity from wetter toward drier soil.

a21d97af5f41.title: Soil moisture
a21d97af5f41.sentence: This is caused by water's adhesion to soil solids, and is called unsaturated flow.

59460f96f58f.title: Soil moisture
59460f96f58f.sentence: Water is pulled by capillary action due to the adhesion force of water to the soil solids, producing a suction gradient from wet towards drier soil and from macropores to micropores.

4f042984f84b.sentence: Roots must seek out water as the unsaturated flow of water in soil can move only at a rate of up to 2.5 cm per day; as a result they are constantly dying and growing as they seek out high concentrations of soil moisture.

ab5f46a83921.sentence: - The amount of water already in the soil

bfc211efbc05.sentence: Warm soils take in water faster while frozen soils such as permafrost may not be able to absorb depending on the type of freezing.

f84f48fa3084.title: Pedotransfer function
f84f48fa3084.sentence: In soil science, pedotransfer functions (PTF) are predictive functions of certain soil properties using data from soil surveys.

bedcca48ff3d.title: Pedotransfer function
bedcca48ff3d.sentence: The term pedotransfer function was coined by Johan Bouma as translating data we have into what we need.

1cce39535597.title: Pedotransfer function
1cce39535597.sentence: Although not formally recognized and named until 1989, the concept of the pedotransfer function has long been applied to estimate soil properties that are difficult to determine.

9b70e2f505a7.title: Pedotransfer function
9b70e2f505a7.sentence: The most readily available data comes from a soil survey, such as the field morphology, soil texture, structure and pH.

2790e9ed5c63.title: Pedotransfer function
2790e9ed5c63.sentence: Pedotransfer functions add value to this basic information by translating them into estimates of other more laborious and expensively determined soil properties.

f42eba2aada4.title: Hydraulic conductivity
f42eba2aada4.section: Estimation by empirical approach > Pedotransfer function
f42eba2aada4.sentence: A pedotransfer function (PTF) is a specialized empirical estimation method, used primarily in the soil sciences, but increasingly used in hydrogeology.

f124924c624f.title: Pedotransfer function
f124924c624f.sentence: Pedotransfer functions utilize various regression analysis and data mining techniques to extract rules associating basic soil properties with more difficult to measure properties.

cd85b96e6f71.title: Pedotransfer function
cd85b96e6f71.sentence: Probably because of the particular difficulty, cost of measurement, and availability of large databases, the most comprehensive research in developing PTFs has been for the estimation of water retention curve and hydraulic conductivity.

229c0beb47cb.title: Pedotransfer function
229c0beb47cb.sentence: The first PTF came from the study of Lyman Briggs and McLane (1907).

f76106f7855e.title: Pedotransfer function
f76106f7855e.sentence: They determined the wilting coefficient, which is defined as percentage water content of a soil when the plants growing in that soil are first reduced to a wilted condition from which they cannot recover in an approximately saturated atmosphere without the addition of water to the soil, as a function of particle-size:

38089af88183.title: Pedotransfer function
38089af88183.sentence: In the 1960s various papers dealt with the estimation of FC, PWP, and AWC, notably in a series of papers by Salter and Williams (1965 etc.).

5d38699eb80d.title: Pedotransfer function
5d38699eb80d.sentence: They explored relationships between texture classes and available water capacity, which are now known as class PTFs.

d9d306376b05.title: Pedotransfer function
d9d306376b05.sentence: They also developed functions relating the particle-size distribution to AWC, now known as continuous PTFs.

dec665d4f8bb.title: Pedotransfer function
dec665d4f8bb.sentence: PTFs for estimating soil physical, mechanical, chemical and biological properties have also been developed.

b753a56f4c2b.title: Pedotransfer function
b753a56f4c2b.sentence: - ROSETTA – by Schaap et al. of the USDA, uses artificial neural networks

2bf519504530.title: Pedotransfer function
2bf519504530.sentence: McBratney et al. (2002) introduced the concept of a soil inference system, SINFERS, where pedotransfer functions are the knowledge rules for soil inference engines.

c7ff92c3ff6f.title: Pedotransfer function
c7ff92c3ff6f.sentence: A soil inference system takes measurements with a given level of certainty (source) and by means of logically linked pedotransfer functions (organiser) infers data that is not known with minimal inaccuracy (predictor).

1df15ad3bd8b.title: Impervious surface
1df15ad3bd8b.sentence: Impervious surfaces are mainly artificial structures—such as pavements (roads, sidewalks, driveways and parking lots, as well as industrial areas such as airports, ports and logistics and distribution centres, all of which use considerable paved areas) that are covered by water-resistant materials such as asphalt, concrete, brick, stone—and rooftops.

d0c3ed784e9f.title: Impervious surface
d0c3ed784e9f.sentence: Soils compacted by urban development are also highly impervious.

77e1cadfec6c.title: Impervious surface
77e1cadfec6c.sentence: - The pavement materials seal the soil surface, eliminating rainwater infiltration and natural groundwater recharge.

329a85a9e38b.title: Impervious surface
329a85a9e38b.sentence: - Impervious pavements deprive tree roots of aeration, eliminating the "urban forest" and the canopy shade that would otherwise moderate urban climate.

9e7ecf968c95.title: Impervious surface
9e7ecf968c95.sentence: The coverage increases with rising urbanization.

c7f1267601b2.title: Impervious surface
c7f1267601b2.sentence: In rural areas, impervious cover may only be one or two percent.

625f032e1b3e.title: Impervious surface
625f032e1b3e.sentence: In residential areas, coverage increases from about 10 percent in low-density subdivisions to over 50 percent in multifamily communities.

c3ec69a0fb47.title: Impervious surface
c3ec69a0fb47.sentence: In industrial and commercial areas, coverage rises above 70 percent.

5e53f6c0a81b.title: Impervious surface
5e53f6c0a81b.sentence: In regional shopping centers and dense urban areas, it is over 90 percent.

92b9d420563c.title: Impervious surface
92b9d420563c.sentence: (See urban sprawl.) Alternatively, urban structures can be built differently to make them function more like naturally pervious soils; examples of such alternative structures are porous pavements, green roofs and infiltration basins.

efb5b7f8f2f0.title: Water content
efb5b7f8f2f0.sentence: In addition to the direct and laboratory methods above, the following options are available.

fd73773ae6b0.title: Water content
fd73773ae6b0.section: Measurement > Soil moisture measurement > Geophysical methods
fd73773ae6b0.sentence: There are several geophysical methods available that can approximate in situ soil water content.

fcab336a5f10.title: Water content
fcab336a5f10.section: Measurement > Soil moisture measurement > Geophysical methods
fcab336a5f10.sentence: These methods include: time-domain reflectometry (TDR), neutron probe, frequency domain sensor, capacitance probe, amplitude domain reflectometry, electrical resistivity tomography, ground penetrating radar (GPR), and others that are sensitive to the physical properties of water.

eb148dbc2b70.title: Water content
eb148dbc2b70.section: Measurement > Soil moisture measurement > Geophysical methods
eb148dbc2b70.sentence: Geophysical sensors are often used to monitor soil moisture continuously in agricultural and scientific applications.

91491ed833aa.title: Soil moisture
91491ed833aa.sentence: Soil water can be measured in situ with soil moisture sensors or can be estimated at various scales and resolution: from local or wifi measures via sensors in the soil to satellite imagery that combines data capture and hydrological models.

f5c6002535c1.title: Soil moisture
f5c6002535c1.sentence: Each method exhibits pros and cons, and hence, the integration of different techniques may decrease the drawbacks of a single given method.

cb65af1aa91c.title: Water content
cb65af1aa91c.section: Classification and uses > Earth and agricultural sciences > Agriculture
cb65af1aa91c.sentence: Some agriculture professionals are beginning to use environmental measurements such as soil moisture to schedule irrigation.

5db3855a7f04.title: Water content
5db3855a7f04.section: Classification and uses > Earth and agricultural sciences > Agriculture
5db3855a7f04.sentence: This method is referred to as smart irrigation or soil cultivation.

be190f79241f.title: Time-domain reflectometer
be190f79241f.sentence: A time-domain reflectometer (TDR) is an electronic instrument used to determine the characteristics of electrical lines by observing reflected pulses.

4daf8b941ad1.title: Time-domain reflectometer
4daf8b941ad1.section: Usage > Used in the earth and agricultural sciences
4daf8b941ad1.sentence: A TDR is used to determine moisture content in soil and porous media.

d6fcb797d064.title: Time-domain reflectometer
d6fcb797d064.sentence: In order to measure those reflections, the TDR will transmit an incident signal onto the conductor and listen for its reflections.

ec5267925119.title: Time-domain reflectometer
ec5267925119.sentence: Instead, if there are impedance variations, then some of the incident signal will be reflected back to the source.

f97765cee97f.title: Time-domain reflectometer
f97765cee97f.sentence: The distance to the reflecting impedance can also be determined from the time that a pulse takes to return.

5ca95584e026.title: Time-domain reflectometer
5ca95584e026.section: Usage > Used in the earth and agricultural sciences
5ca95584e026.sentence: The key to TDR's success is its ability to accurately determine the permittivity (dielectric constant) of a material from wave propagation, due to the strong relationship between the permittivity of a material and its water content, as demonstrated in the pioneering works of Hoekstra and Delaney (1974) and Topp et al. (1980).

1220864c2c3f.title: Time-domain reflectometer
1220864c2c3f.section: Usage > Used in the earth and agricultural sciences
1220864c2c3f.sentence: The TDR method is a transmission line technique, and determines apparent permittivity (Ka) from the travel time of an electromagnetic wave that propagates along a transmission line, usually two or more parallel metal rods embedded in soil or sediment.

07fd3d1c4a5c.title: Time-domain reflectometer
07fd3d1c4a5c.section: Usage > Used in the earth and agricultural sciences
07fd3d1c4a5c.sentence: The probes are typically between 10 and 30 cm long and connected to the TDR via coaxial cable.

3ded6c2e1c18.title: Time-domain reflectometer
3ded6c2e1c18.sentence: In TDR technology, the impulse velocity is primarily affected by the permittivity of the medium through which the pulse propagates, which can vary greatly by the moisture content and temperature of the medium.

2be7589ffdb3.title: Time-domain reflectometer
2be7589ffdb3.sentence: This can be done by placing the TDRs in different soil layers and measuring the time of start of precipitation and the time that TDR indicates an increase in the soil moisture content.

47318939d59a.title: Time-domain reflectometer
47318939d59a.sentence: The depth of the TDR (d) is a known factor and the other is the time it takes the drop of water to reach that depth (t); therefore the speed of water infiltration (v) can be determined.

27a6fcccda04.title: Time-domain reflectometer
27a6fcccda04.sentence: Time domain reflectometers are commonly used for in-place testing of very long cable runs, where it is impractical to dig up or remove what may be a kilometers-long cable.

274fb77c1a9a.title: Time-domain reflectometer
274fb77c1a9a.sentence: Using a TDR, it is possible to pinpoint a fault to within centimetres.

c600f4b08a0a.title: TDR moisture sensor
c600f4b08a0a.sentence: The sensor contains a waveguide consisting of two, three, or more parallel wires which is connected via a coaxial cable to a voltage pulse generator which sends precisely defined voltage pulses into the sensor.

b104668bf10c.title: TDR moisture sensor
b104668bf10c.sentence: The rate of travel of the pulse in the probe is measured and related to moisture content, with slower travel indicating an increase of moisture.

3c65a0e84f36.title: TDR moisture sensor
3c65a0e84f36.sentence: Measurement usually involves inserting a sensor into the substance to be tested and then applying either Standard Waveform Analysis to determine the average moisture content along the sensor or Profile Analysis to provide moisture content at discrete points along the sensor.

8da4634abe03.title: TDR moisture sensor
8da4634abe03.sentence: Standard Waveform Analysis is unable to provide a spatial moisture profile.

7448d8ae201a.title: TDR moisture sensor
7448d8ae201a.sentence: This enables the moisture content to be mapped to the individual segments and therefore shows the spatial moisture distribution.

6c9d6009eb30.title: Soil moisture sensor
6c9d6009eb30.sentence: Soil moisture sensors measure the volumetric water content in soil.

b559acd2fbbe.title: Soil moisture sensor
b559acd2fbbe.sentence: Soil moisture sensors typically refer to sensors that estimate volumetric water content.

6995534c332c.title: Soil moisture sensor
6995534c332c.sentence: Since the direct gravimetric measurement of free soil moisture requires removing, drying, and weighing of a sample, soil moisture sensors measure the volumetric water content indirectly by using some other property of the soil, such as electrical resistance, dielectric constant, or interaction with neutrons, as a proxy for the moisture content.

92b906a73f26.title: Soil moisture sensor
92b906a73f26.sentence: The relation between the measured property and soil moisture must be calibrated and may vary depending on environmental factors such as soil type, temperature, or electric conductivity.

4cf2d04eded5.title: Soil moisture sensor
4cf2d04eded5.sentence: Technologies commonly used to indirectly measure volumetric water content (soil moisture) include:

0fd9a8b352be.title: Soil moisture sensor
0fd9a8b352be.sentence: - Frequency Domain Reflectometry (FDR soil moisture sensor): Measuring the impedance by applying a measuring frequency of several hundred MHz to short rods forming a transmission line.

660c8752a296.title: Soil moisture sensor
660c8752a296.sentence: - So called capacitance sensors use an open capacitor formed by a large PCB area are as part of an oscillating circuit.

25e5119a962e.title: Soil moisture sensor
25e5119a962e.sentence: - Time Domain Reflectometry (TDR soil moisture sensor): The dielectric constant of a certain volume element around the sensor is obtained by measuring the speed of propagation along a short single ended transmission line.

7178b3fb4464.title: Soil moisture sensor
7178b3fb4464.sentence: - Time Domain Transmission (TDR soil moisture sensor): Same as with TDR the speed of propagation along a short transmission line is measured, while on one end sits the sender and the receiver resides on the other end.

d07f04d90597.title: Soil moisture sensor
d07f04d90597.sentence: - Neutron moisture gauges: The moderator properties of water for neutrons are utilized to estimate soil moisture content between a source and detector probe.

76bf994f1594.title: Soil moisture sensor
76bf994f1594.sentence: - Soil resistivity: Measuring how strongly the soil resists the flow of electricity between two electrodes can be used to determine the soil moisture content.

e38bbe877cf4.title: Soil moisture sensor
e38bbe877cf4.sentence: - Galvanic cell: The amount of water present can be determined based on the voltage the soil produces because water acts as an electrolyte and produces electricity.

e33f96551363.title: Soil moisture sensor
e33f96551363.sentence: They are similar to FDR sensors but operate below 1 MHz and are more prone to noise factors.

d8f1eff9ebfe.title: Soil moisture sensor
d8f1eff9ebfe.sentence: Another class of sensors measure another property of moisture in soils called water potential; these sensors are usually referred to as soil water potential sensors and include tensiometers and gypsum blocks.

c43167dc32c8.title: Soil moisture sensor
c43167dc32c8.sentence: Measuring soil moisture is important for agricultural applications to help farmers manage their irrigation systems more efficiently.

f0d94fb6ce35.title: Soil moisture sensor
f0d94fb6ce35.sentence: Knowing the exact soil moisture conditions on their fields, not only are farmers able to generally use less water to grow a crop, they are also able to increase yields and the quality of the crop by improved management of soil moisture during critical plant growth stages.

237f737db139.title: Soil moisture sensor
237f737db139.sentence: In urban and suburban areas, landscapes and residential lawns are using soil moisture sensors to interface with an irrigation controller.

a841a1de4cf6.title: Soil moisture sensor
a841a1de4cf6.sentence: Connecting a soil moisture sensor to a simple irrigation clock will convert it into a "smart" irrigation controller that prevents irrigation cycles when the soil is already wet, e.g. following a recent rainfall event.

10f3ec591456.title: Capacitance probe
10f3ec591456.sentence: A capacitance sensor or dielectric sensor uses capacitance to measure the dielectric permittivity of a surrounding medium.

fa91eb11956c.title: Capacitance probe
fa91eb11956c.sentence: When the amount of water changes in the soil, a probe will measure a change in capacitance due to the change in dielectric permittivity that can be directly correlated with a change in water content.

34b0e01ad9c6.title: Capacitance probe
34b0e01ad9c6.sentence: The configuration is like the neutron probe where an access tube made of PVC is installed in the soil; probes can also be modular (comb-like) and connected to a logger.

af378c3755c7.title: Capacitance probe
af378c3755c7.sentence: Each capacitor sensor consists of two metal rings mounted on the circuit board at some distance from the top of the access tube.

cee807f47db5.title: Capacitance probe
cee807f47db5.sentence: These rings are a pair of electrodes, which form the plates of the capacitor with the soil acting as the dielectric in between.

3de826dc4c07.title: Capacitance probe
3de826dc4c07.sentence: The capacitor and the oscillator form a circuit, and changes in dielectric constant of surrounding media are detected by changes in the operating frequency.

7a5cb70d3ea2.title: Capacitance probe
7a5cb70d3ea2.sentence: - One application for such a device is measuring the water content of soil, where the volume of water in the total volume of soil most heavily influences the dielectric permittivity of the soil because the dielectric of water (80) is much greater than the other constituents of the soil (mineral soil: 4, organic matter: 4, air: 1).

5170a4b3e4a6.title: Capacitance probe
5170a4b3e4a6.sentence: The capacitance sensors are designed to oscillate in excess of 100 MHz inside the access tube in free air.

b7465f11e579.title: Capacitance probe
b7465f11e579.sentence: Capacitance sensors are now widely used in irrigation scheduling in agriculture around the world.

264fec6f1de0.title: Waterlogging (agriculture)
264fec6f1de0.sentence: Waterlogging is the saturation of soil with water.

4eeff69d72a4.title: Waterlogging (agriculture)
4eeff69d72a4.sentence: Soil may be regarded as waterlogged when it is nearly saturated with water much of the time such that its air phase is restricted and anaerobic conditions prevail.

ed21bf80d14e.title: Waterlogging (agriculture)
ed21bf80d14e.sentence: All plants, including crops, require air (specifically, oxygen) to respire, produce energy, and keep their cells alive.

1315602d686e.title: Waterlogging (agriculture)
1315602d686e.sentence: In agriculture, waterlogging typically blocks air from getting to the roots.

02596c8d7e44.title: Waterlogging (agriculture)
02596c8d7e44.sentence: In extreme cases of prolonged waterlogging, anaerobiosis occurs, the roots of mesophytes suffer, and the subsurface reducing atmosphere leads to such processes as denitrification, methanogenesis, and the reduction of iron and manganese oxides.

c80148252ac4.title: Waterlogging (agriculture)
c80148252ac4.sentence: With the exception of rice (Oryza sativa), most crops like maize and potato, are therefore highly intolerant to waterlogging.

ad980513f125.title: Waterlogging (agriculture)
ad980513f125.sentence: Roots can survive waterlogging by forming aerenchyma, inducing anaerobic metabolism, and changing root system architecture.

fde89075fa5d.title: Waterlogging (agriculture)
fde89075fa5d.sentence: In irrigated agricultural land, waterlogging is often accompanied by soil salinity as waterlogged soils prevent leaching of the salts imported by the irrigation water.

7725fa78533a.title: Agriculture
7725fa78533a.section: Environmental impact > Land and water issues
7725fa78533a.sentence: Agricultural water usage can also cause major environmental problems, including the destruction of natural wetlands, the spread of water-borne diseases, and land degradation through salinization and waterlogging, when irrigation is performed incorrectly.

df43cc1c3afa.title: Environmental impact of irrigation
df43cc1c3afa.sentence: - In the Indus Plains in Pakistan, more than 2 million hectares of land are waterlogged.

d4447085700c.title: Environmental impact of irrigation
d4447085700c.sentence: - In India, 2.19 million ha of land has been reported to suffer from waterlogging in irrigation canal commands.

4ae0ccb360e2.title: Watertable control
4ae0ccb360e2.sentence: In geotechnical engineering, watertable control is the practice of controlling the height of the water table by drainage.

bc7becf48290.title: Watertable control
bc7becf48290.sentence: Its main applications are in agricultural land (to improve the crop yield using agricultural drainage systems) and in cities to manage the extensive underground infrastructure that includes the foundations of large buildings, underground transit systems, and extensive utilities (water supply networks, sewerage, storm drains, and underground electrical grids).

ca0a3ee4ed23.title: Watertable control
ca0a3ee4ed23.sentence: Subsurface land drainage aims at controlling the water table of the groundwater in originally waterlogged land at a depth acceptable for the purpose for which the land is used.

f7a56e231c24.title: Watertable control
f7a56e231c24.sentence: The depth of the water table with drainage is greater than without.

eaf9fa37c1fc.title: Watertable control
eaf9fa37c1fc.sentence: Most crops need a water table at a minimum depth.

c1e1194af181.title: Watertable control
c1e1194af181.sentence: For some important food and fiber crops a classification was made because at shallower depths the crop suffers a yield decline.

2ebca933fa77.title: Watertable control
2ebca933fa77.sentence: Wheat, Nile Delta, Egypt | 45 | Very tolerant | Resists shallow water tables

10ca8b8971f2.title: Watertable control
10ca8b8971f2.sentence: Cotton, Nile Delta | 90 | Sensitive | Cotton needs dry feet, water table should be deep

10579d4a80b7.title: Watertable control
10579d4a80b7.sentence: The shallower the permissible depth of the water table, the lower the cost of the drainage system to be installed to achieve this depth.

0f3821ce57c0.title: Watertable control
0f3821ce57c0.sentence: However, the lowering of the originally too shallow depth by land drainage entails side effects.

f21550b30f5f.title: Watertable control
f21550b30f5f.sentence: These have also to be taken into account, including the costs of mitigation of negative side effects.

5142ba633473.title: Watertable control
5142ba633473.sentence: Historically, agricultural land drainage started with the digging of relatively shallow open ditches that received both runoff from the land surface and outflow of groundwater.

6facfeb5caee.title: Watertable control
6facfeb5caee.sentence: By the end of the 19th century and early in the 20th century it was felt that the ditches were a hindrance for the farm operations and the ditches were replaced by buried lines of clay pipes (tiles), each tile about 30 cm long.

e7a409e0830b.title: Watertable control
e7a409e0830b.sentence: Since 1960, one started using long, flexible, corrugated plastic (PVC or PE) pipes that could be installed efficiently in one go by trenching machines.

6e9ac9336f91.title: Watertable control
6e9ac9336f91.sentence: As a result of large scale developments, many modern drainage projects were over-designed, while the negative environmental side effects were ignored.

fbad25787afb.title: Watertable control
fbad25787afb.sentence: In circles with environmental concern, the profession of land drainage got a poor reputation, sometimes justly so, sometimes unjustified, notably when land drainage was confused with the more encompassing activity of wetland reclamation.

d4360429c2ce.title: Watertable control
d4360429c2ce.section: Description and definitions > Drainage by wells
d4360429c2ce.sentence: Subsurface drainage of groundwater can also be accomplished by pumped wells (vertical drainage, in contrast to horizontal drainage).

c070c44f4d85.title: Watertable control
c070c44f4d85.section: Description and definitions > Drainage by wells
c070c44f4d85.sentence: Drainage wells have been used extensively in the Salinity Control and Reclamation Program (SCARP) in the Indus valley of Pakistan.

d54008aea8e6.title: Watertable control
d54008aea8e6.section: Description and definitions > Drainage by wells
d54008aea8e6.sentence: Although the experiences were not overly successful, the feasibility of this technique in areas with deep and permeable aquifers is not to be discarded.

0f3cd464a054.title: Watertable control
0f3cd464a054.section: Description and definitions > Drainage by wells
0f3cd464a054.sentence: The well spacings in these areas can be so wide (more than 1000m) that the installation of vertical drainage systems could be relatively cheap compared to horizontal subsurface drainage (drainage by pipes, ditches, trenches, at a spacing of 100m or less).

d877a2964317.title: Watertable control
d877a2964317.sentence: In addition, land drainage can help with soil salinity control.

24bee38cad6e.title: Watertable control
24bee38cad6e.sentence: The soil's hydraulic conductivity plays an important role in drainage design.

4db122819841.title: Drainage
4db122819841.sentence: Wetland soils may need drainage to be used for agriculture.

cb9f7719afe5.title: Drainage
cb9f7719afe5.sentence: In each of these cases, appropriate drainage carries off temporary flushes of water to prevent damage to annual or perennial crops.

cea6eed05e86.title: Drainage
cea6eed05e86.sentence: In the northern United States and Europe, glaciation created numerous small lakes, which gradually filled with humus to make marshes.

0ba05d913ad3.title: Drainage
0ba05d913ad3.sentence: Some of these were drained using open ditches and trenches to make mucklands, which are primarily used for high-value crops such as vegetables.

214b2b5f6b4b.title: Drainage
214b2b5f6b4b.sentence: The invention of wind-powered pumping engines in the 15th century permitted some of the marginal land drainage.

5237beead625.title: Drainage
5237beead625.sentence: Still, the final drainage of the lake had to await the design of large steam-powered pumps and agreements between regional authorities.

96309007651c.title: Drainage
96309007651c.sentence: The lake was eliminated between 1849 and 1852, creating thousands of km2 of new land.

5ca0b955d246.title: Drainage
5ca0b955d246.sentence: Coastal plains and river deltas may have seasonally or permanently high water tables and must have drainage improvements if they are to be used for agriculture.

bacc8c351969.title: Drainage
bacc8c351969.sentence: An example is the flatwoods citrus-growing region of Florida, United States.

855772eb53a3.title: Drainage
855772eb53a3.sentence: After periods of high rainfall, drainage pumps are employed to prevent damage to the citrus groves from overly wet soils.

a9a87740072f.title: Drainage
a9a87740072f.sentence: Soils that are predominantly clay will pass water very slowly downward.

34d53170e68f.title: Drainage
34d53170e68f.sentence: Meanwhile, plant roots suffocate because the excessive water around the roots eliminates air movement through the soil.

9767842b3794.title: Drainage
9767842b3794.sentence: Other soils may have an impervious layer of mineralized soil, called a hardpan, or relatively impervious rock layers may underlie shallow soils.

e5b25054b305.title: Drainage
e5b25054b305.sentence: Soils that are otherwise excellent may be waterlogged for a week of the year, which is sufficient to kill fruit trees and cost the productivity of the land until replacements can be established.

a4aed466cfe9.title: Drainage
a4aed466cfe9.sentence: Rice production requires complete water control, as fields must be flooded or drained at different stages of the crop cycle.

2e0b9ebaba5b.title: Drainage
2e0b9ebaba5b.sentence: However, irrigation water always contains minerals and salts, which can be concentrated to toxic levels by evapotranspiration.

e0d2bf905903.title: Drainage
e0d2bf905903.sentence: Irrigated land may need periodic flushes with excessive irrigation water and drainage to control soil salinity.

87de8d8f6a77.title: Acid sulfate soil
87de8d8f6a77.sentence: Subsurface drainage of these soils is normally not advisable.

fdb3f3f16374.title: Acid sulfate soil
fdb3f3f16374.sentence: When cultivated, acid sulfate soils cannot be kept wet continuously because of climatic dry spells and shortages of irrigation water, surface drainage may help to remove the acidic and toxic chemicals (formed in the dry spells) during rainy periods.

2df5663a1196.title: Acid sulfate soil
2df5663a1196.sentence: In the long run surface drainage can help to reclaim acid sulfate soils.

f04bb30a2c53.title: Water potential
f04bb30a2c53.section: Components of water potential > Matrix potential (Matric potential)
f04bb30a2c53.sentence: When water is in contact with solid particles (e.g., clay or sand particles within soil), adhesive intermolecular forces between the water and the solid can be large and important.

53d3bd7fa8f7.title: Water potential
53d3bd7fa8f7.section: Components of water potential > Matrix potential (Matric potential)
53d3bd7fa8f7.sentence: The forces between the water molecules and the solid particles in combination with attraction among water molecules promote surface tension and the formation of menisci within the solid matrix.

01f02552dea3.title: Water potential
01f02552dea3.section: Components of water potential > Matrix potential (Matric potential)
01f02552dea3.sentence: Force is then required to break these menisci.

fa7935d466f0.title: Water potential
fa7935d466f0.section: Components of water potential > Matrix potential (Matric potential)
fa7935d466f0.sentence: The magnitude of matrix potential depends on the distances between solid particles—the width of the menisci (also capillary action and differing Pa at ends of the capillary)—and the chemical composition of the solid matrix (meniscus, macroscopic motion due to ionic attraction).

71c815a2128d.title: Water potential
71c815a2128d.section: Components of water potential > Matrix potential (Matric potential)
71c815a2128d.sentence: The matrix potential is always negative because the water attracted by the soil matrix has an energy state lower than that of pure water.

02a883a8b929.title: Water potential
02a883a8b929.section: Components of water potential > Matrix potential (Matric potential)
02a883a8b929.sentence: Matrix potential only occurs in unsaturated soil above the water table.

744661095920.title: Water potential
744661095920.section: Components of water potential > Matrix potential (Matric potential)
744661095920.sentence: If the matrix potential approaches a value of zero, nearly all soil pores are completely filled with water, i.e. fully saturated and at maximum retentive capacity.

cf905bfa3d3a.title: Water potential
cf905bfa3d3a.section: Components of water potential > Matrix potential (Matric potential)
cf905bfa3d3a.sentence: In the case that water drains into less-moist soil zones of similar porosity, the matrix potential is generally in the range of −10 to −30 kPa.

0518ba1f2cba.title: Water potential
0518ba1f2cba.section: Components of water potential > Matrix potential (Matric potential)
0518ba1f2cba.sentence: In many cases, the absolute value of matrix potential can be relatively large in comparison to the other components of water potential discussed above.

43864849ef73.title: Water potential
43864849ef73.section: Components of water potential > Matrix potential (Matric potential)
43864849ef73.sentence: Although water movement due to matrix potential may be slow, it is still extremely important in supplying water to plant roots and in engineering applications.

8460b1cbac2a.title: Hydrology
8460b1cbac2a.sentence: Hydrology (from Ancient Greek ὕδωρ (húdōr) 'water' and -λογία (-logía) 'study of') is the scientific study of the movement, distribution, and management of water on Earth and other planets, including the water cycle, water resources, and drainage basin sustainability.

25061766e3e7.title: Hydrology
25061766e3e7.sentence: Hydrology subdivides into surface water hydrology, groundwater hydrology (hydrogeology), and marine hydrology.

f6d1fe32eff8.title: Hydrology
f6d1fe32eff8.sentence: Infiltration is the process by which water enters the soil.

47c773f730ac.title: Hydrology
47c773f730ac.sentence: Some of the water is absorbed, and the rest percolates down to the water table.

637ffa6038de.title: Hydrology
637ffa6038de.sentence: Soil moisture can be measured in various ways; by capacitance probe, time domain reflectometer or tensiometer.

ee750a4502e9.title: Hydrology
ee750a4502e9.sentence: Other methods include solute sampling and geophysical methods.

f1495dd16295.title: Hydrology
f1495dd16295.sentence: - Ecohydrology is the study of interactions between organisms and the hydrologic cycle.

0c14115f8082.title: Infiltration (hydrology)
0c14115f8082.sentence: Named after the same Robert E. Horton mentioned above, Horton's equation is another viable option when measuring ground infiltration rates or volumes.

4071ce3bf060.title: Infiltration (hydrology)
4071ce3bf060.sentence: It is an empirical formula that says that infiltration starts at a constant rate, f0, and is decreasing exponentially with time, t.

eca173668cd8.title: Infiltration (hydrology)
eca173668cd8.sentence: After some time when the soil saturation level reaches a certain value, the rate of infiltration will level off to the rate fc.

cad056be79e8.title: Infiltration (hydrology)
cad056be79e8.sentence: fc is the constant or equilibrium infiltration rate after the soil has been saturated or the minimum infiltration rate;

81d8dd9ec452.title: Infiltration (hydrology)
81d8dd9ec452.sentence: It can be used to find the total volume of infiltration, F, after time t.

51744d9d44c6.title: Infiltration (hydrology)
51744d9d44c6.sentence: Named after its founder Kostiakov is an empirical equation that assumes that the intake rate declines over time according to a power function.

e90a77b124a1.title: Infiltration (hydrology)
e90a77b124a1.sentence: The major limitation of this expression is its reliance on the zero final intake rate.

737fcd5cd9d6.title: Infiltration (hydrology)
737fcd5cd9d6.sentence: In most cases, the infiltration rate instead approaches a finite steady value, which in some cases may occur after short periods of time.

f561285f9d19.title: Infiltration (hydrology)
f561285f9d19.sentence: The Kostiakov-Lewis variant, also known as the "Modified Kostiakov" equation corrects this by adding a steady intake term to the original equation.

0722e7553e05.title: Drainage
0722e7553e05.sentence: Geotextiles are synthetic textile fabrics specially manufactured for civil and environmental engineering applications.

fa7f54de7a12.title: Drainage
fa7f54de7a12.sentence: Geotextiles are designed to retain fine soil particles while allowing water to pass through.

43bc99f2464c.title: Drainage
43bc99f2464c.sentence: New storm water drainage systems incorporate geotextile filters that retain and prevent fine grains of soil from passing into and clogging the drain.

fd3871c66daf.title: Drainage
fd3871c66daf.sentence: In a typical drainage system, they would be laid along a trench which would then be filled with coarse granular material: gravel, sea shells, stone or rock.

6ea67dac7e5f.title: Drainage
6ea67dac7e5f.sentence: The geotextile is then folded over the top of the stone and the trench is then covered by soil.

095e3c6ff78f.title: Drainage
095e3c6ff78f.sentence: Groundwater seeps through the geotextile and flows through the stone to an outfell.

96ad72fd7a62.title: Drainage
96ad72fd7a62.sentence: In high groundwater conditions a perforated plastic (PVC or PE) pipe is laid along the base of the drain to increase the volume of water transported in the drain.

3152b630915f.title: Drainage
3152b630915f.sentence: Alternatively, a prefabricated plastic drainage system made of HDPE, often incorporating geotextile, coco fiber or rag filters can be considered.

7f07d13c22f9.title: Drainage
7f07d13c22f9.sentence: The use of these materials has become increasingly more common due to their ease of use, since they eliminate the need for transporting and laying stone drainage aggregate, which is invariably more expensive than a synthetic drain and concrete liners.

c11bbaa1a31d.title: Drainage
c11bbaa1a31d.sentence: Sustainable urban drainage systems (SUDS) are designed to encourage contractors to install drainage system that more closely mimic the natural flow of water in nature.

892354056cdb.title: Drainage
892354056cdb.sentence: The project focuses on designing a system "to provide drainage that more closely mimics the natural landscape prior to development than traditional piped systems".

7361ad3a0f5e.title: Drainage
7361ad3a0f5e.sentence: Seattle's Public Utilities created a pilot program called Street Edge Alternatives Project.

3e1c2e92acc9.title: Drainage
3e1c2e92acc9.sentence: The streets are characterized by ditches along the side of the roadway, with plantings designed throughout the area.

f2ebb66b580d.title: Drainage
f2ebb66b580d.sentence: An emphasis on non-curbed sidewalks allows water to flow more freely into the areas of permeable surface on the side of the streets.

8d70b5cc3d5a.title: Drainage
8d70b5cc3d5a.sentence: Monitoring conducted by Seattle Public Utilities reports a 99 percent reduction of storm water leaving the drainage project.

10b8fe904f4c.title: Drainage
10b8fe904f4c.sentence: Since 2010 local and neighbourhood planning in the UK is required by law to factor SUDS into any development projects that they are responsible for.

026dda81d454.title: Drainage system (agriculture)
026dda81d454.sentence: An agricultural drainage system is a system by which water is drained on or in the soil to enhance agricultural production of crops.

025e7210255a.title: Drainage system (agriculture)
025e7210255a.sentence: It may involve any combination of stormwater control, erosion control, and watertable control.

e8ab56135722.title: Drainage system (agriculture)
e8ab56135722.sentence: While there are more than two types of drainage systems employed in agriculture, there are two main types: (1) surface drainage and (2) sub-surface drainage.

821e856bc28f.title: Drainage system (agriculture)
821e856bc28f.sentence: The function of the field drainage system is to control the water table, whereas the function of the main drainage system is to collect, transport, and dispose of the water through an outfall or outlet.

7ad41eeceb40.title: Drainage system (agriculture)
7ad41eeceb40.sentence: The regular surface drainage systems, which start functioning as soon as there is an excess of rainfall or irrigation applied, operate entirely by gravity.

87e756397121.title: Drainage system (agriculture)
87e756397121.sentence: - Bedded systems, used in flat lands for crops other than rice;

42f3a0748e24.title: Drainage system (agriculture)
42f3a0748e24.sentence: - Graded systems, used in sloping land for crops other than rice.

e7024a50e564.title: Drainage system (agriculture)
e7024a50e564.sentence: The subsurface field drainage systems consist of horizontal or slightly sloping channels made in the soil; they can be open ditches, trenches, filled with brushwood and a soil cap, filled with stones and a soil cap, buried pipe drains, tile drains, or mole drains, but they can also consist of a series of wells.

eaecdfca1151.title: Drainage system (agriculture)
eaecdfca1151.sentence: Subsurface drainage by wells is often referred to as vertical drainage, and drainage by channels as horizontal drainage, but it is more clear to speak of "field drainage by wells" and "field drainage by ditches or pipes" respectively.

6d3358cb509f.title: Drainage system (agriculture)
6d3358cb509f.sentence: Modern buried pipe drains often consist of corrugated, flexible, and perforated plastic (PE or PVC) pipe lines wrapped with an envelope or filter material to improve the permeability around the pipes and to prevent entry of soil particles, which is especially important in fine sandy and silty soils.

887695e15823.title: Drainage system (agriculture)
887695e15823.sentence: Like the surface field drainage systems, the subsurface field drainage systems can also be differentiated in regular systems and checked (controlled) systems.

d1128b91edca.title: Drainage system (agriculture)
d1128b91edca.sentence: They can save much irrigation water.

b34bb0bba67d.title: Drainage system (agriculture)
b34bb0bba67d.sentence: In northwestern India, this practice has increased the irrigation efficiency and reduced the quantity of irrigation water needed, and has not led to any undue salinization.

5aa5a53dc543.title: Drainage system (agriculture)
5aa5a53dc543.sentence: Surface drainage systems are usually applied in relatively flat lands that have soils with a low or medium infiltration capacity, or in lands with high-intensity rainfalls that exceed the normal infiltration capacity, so that frequent waterlogging occurs on the soil surface.

25b836793fff.title: Drainage system (agriculture)
25b836793fff.sentence: Subsurface drainage systems are used when the drainage problem is mainly that of shallow water tables.

d454048dc7c2.title: Drainage system (agriculture)
d454048dc7c2.sentence: When the land needs a subsurface drainage system, but saline groundwater is present at great depth, it is better to employ a shallow, closely spaced system of pipes or ditches instead of a deep, widely spaced system.

7df9fef6c4e0.title: Drainage system (agriculture)
7df9fef6c4e0.sentence: The reason is that the deeper systems produce a more salty effluent than the shallow systems.

9061fbb2f7d1.title: Soil moisture
9061fbb2f7d1.sentence: Water potential in soil usually has negative values, and therefore it is also expressed in suction, which is defined as the minus of water potential.

e2d231277b94.title: Soil moisture
e2d231277b94.sentence: Suction has a positive value and can be regarded as the total force required to pull or push water out of soil.

541affb739f6.title: Soil moisture
541affb739f6.sentence: Common logarithm of suction in cm H2O is called pF.

6fb3d91d1c49.title: Soil moisture
6fb3d91d1c49.sentence: Water is retained in a soil when the adhesive force of attraction that water's hydrogen atoms have for the oxygen of soil particles is stronger than the cohesive forces that water's hydrogen feels for water oxygen atoms.

62117a74493a.title: Soil moisture
62117a74493a.sentence: The forces with which water is held in soils determine its availability to plants.

d0818f4dfd26.title: Soil moisture
d0818f4dfd26.sentence: Water potential or suction is expressed in units of kPa (10^3 pascal), bar (100 kPa), or cm H2O (approximately 0.098 kPa).

aaf64c0a229f.title: Soil moisture
aaf64c0a229f.sentence: But as the droplet is drawn down, the forces of adhesion of the water for the soil particles produce increasingly higher suction, finally up to 1500 kPa (pF = 4.2).

2d1504f3e86d.title: Soil moisture
2d1504f3e86d.sentence: At 1500 kPa suction, the soil water amount is called wilting point.

8e333a0a3b83.title: Soil moisture
8e333a0a3b83.sentence: The next level, called air-dry, occurs at 100,000 kPa suction (pF = 6).

09257d5432cc.title: Soil moisture
09257d5432cc.sentence: Finally the oven dry condition is reached at 1,000,000 kPa suction (pF = 7).

c0afe335e715.title: Disc permeameter
c0afe335e715.sentence: The disc permeameter is a field instrument used for measuring water infiltration in the soil, which is characterized by in situ saturated and unsaturated soil hydraulic properties.

0720a1a89198.title: Disc permeameter
0720a1a89198.sentence: It is mainly used to provide estimates of the hydraulic conductivity of the soil near saturation.

d1c9b8a80615.title: Disc permeameter
d1c9b8a80615.sentence: In the US it is known as the tension infiltrometer.

d749bdae1cb7.title: Disc permeameter
d749bdae1cb7.sentence: Therefore, many authors attempted to create a negative potential (tension) on the water flow.

1f6e5578b3da.title: Disc permeameter
1f6e5578b3da.sentence: This is to exclude macropores in the flow process, hence only measuring the soil matrix flow.

4785b04fbc28.title: Disc permeameter
4785b04fbc28.sentence: However, the sorptivity tube had many shortcomings, hence modifications to the design led to the development of the disc permeameter by Perroux and White (1988) from CSIRO.

342d1910ba82.title: Disc permeameter
342d1910ba82.sentence: Willard Gardner and Walter Gardner developed a negative head permeameter as early as 1939.

d791bde37be6.title: Disc permeameter
d791bde37be6.sentence: Based on this design, Brent Clothier and Ian White (1981) developed the sorptivity tube which can provide a constant negative potential (tension) on the soil surface.

fa5c57527ede.title: Disc permeameter
fa5c57527ede.sentence: The CSIRO disc permeameter of Perroux and White (1988) (not patented) comprises a nylon mesh supply membrane (with a very small diameter around 10–40 mm), a water reservoir and a bubbling tower.

eba5bd0f161b.title: Disc permeameter
eba5bd0f161b.sentence: The bubbling tower controls the potential h0 applied to the membrane by adjusting the water height in the air-inlet tube.

ee0b0f5bd76f.title: Disc permeameter
ee0b0f5bd76f.sentence: It can be used to supply potential ranging -200 mm to 0 mm, effectively excluding pores with diameter bigger than 0.075 mm.

e539bf9aca32.title: Tile drainage
e539bf9aca32.sentence: Tile drainage is a form of agricultural drainage system that removes excess sub-surface water from fields to allow sufficient air space within the soil, proper cultivation, and access by heavy machinery to tend and harvest crops.

ce4624b639c5.title: Tile drainage
ce4624b639c5.sentence: In a tile drainage system, a sort of "plumbing" is installed below the surface of agricultural fields, effectively consisting of a network of below-ground pipes that allow subsurface water to move out from between soil particles and into the tile line.

ba74c7022279.title: Tile drainage
ba74c7022279.sentence: The phrase "tile drainage" derives from its original composition from ceramic tiles of fired clay, which were similar to terracotta pipes yet not always shaped as pipes.

5580a912507f.title: Tile drainage
5580a912507f.sentence: Commonly HDPE and PVC tubing denominated "tile line" is used, although precast concrete and ceramic tiles are still used.

033b03e7b0ba.title: Land drains
033b03e7b0ba.sentence: In 1843 in England short earthenware pipes were first used laid edge to edge.

c200544f8118.title: Land drains
c200544f8118.sentence: Traditionally, land drains were formed in clay soils and peats by excavating a trench and forming a "tunnel" using flat stones.

e1d22d81bace.title: Land drains
e1d22d81bace.sentence: Agricultural land drains have to be installed sufficiently deep to avoid plough damage.

259b1ffbe16f.title: Tile drainage
259b1ffbe16f.sentence: Water enters the tile line either via the gaps between tile sections, in the case of older tile designs, or through small perforations in modern plastic tile.

09497796c39a.title: Tile drainage
09497796c39a.sentence: Water flowing through tile lines is often ultimately deposited into surface water points—lakes, streams, and rivers—located at a lower elevation than the source.

6029e4d4c33a.title: Tile drainage
6029e4d4c33a.sentence: By installing tile drainage, the water table is effectively lowered and plants can properly develop their roots.

c74f96f410d1.title: Tile drainage
c74f96f410d1.sentence: The lack of water saturation of soil permits oxygen to remain in the pores of the soil for use by roots.

ec9d1cdb8ab2.title: Tile drainage
ec9d1cdb8ab2.sentence: An increase in crop yield can be summarized as forcing plants to develop more roots so that they can absorb more nutrients and water.

4d7b07a4a013.title: Tile drainage
4d7b07a4a013.sentence: Sandier soils will need little, if any, additional drainage, whereas soils with high clay contents will hold their water tighter, requiring tile lines to be placed closer together.

55209648ab5b.title: Land drains
55209648ab5b.sentence: Holes or gaps have to be left in the pipes to allow water to transfer from the subsoil to the pipe and these tend to block with soil or allow silt into the pipe, so blocking it or reducing the flow of water.

c1ef600dfcdc.title: Land drains
c1ef600dfcdc.sentence: However, with time even the gravel becomes choked with soil/silt, so in the latest practice, the gravel is surrounded with a geotextile material which filters out soil particles.

faa4878b0217.title: Land drains
faa4878b0217.sentence: However, whatever the technology, all land drains have a finite life and eventually become ineffective due to the ingress of silt and/or the blocking of the surrounding filter media.

c9c13749804a.title: Tile drainage
c9c13749804a.sentence: In the perforations of tile drainage lines, just as in cracked or rusting water lines and sewer lines under town streets, these roots find the ideal combination of an entrance to enter and a plentiful water supply behind it.

1d3de195ead3.title: Tile drainage
1d3de195ead3.sentence: In some regions farmers must do continual maintenance of tile drainage lines to keep them open and operating correctly, with at least some clearing every year in one or another part of the system.

279c52cb5bde.title: Tile drainage
279c52cb5bde.sentence: - Adding structures such as flashboard risers in outlet canals to control the residence time of irrigation water in the root zone: When these structures are removed, subsurface drainage takes place more rapidly and the amount of water in ditches decreases.

3aed5ed5682c.title: Tile drainage
3aed5ed5682c.sentence: This technique permits not only to manage the level of water in fields but also allows maximum storage of water within the field for utilization by the crop.

d0aa5d99d98a.title: Bioclogging
d0aa5d99d98a.sentence: The microbial biomass obstructs pore spaces, creating an impermeable layer in the soil and significantly reducing water infiltration rates.

5c2f231f4af9.title: Bioclogging
5c2f231f4af9.sentence: Bioclogging occurs under continuous ponded infiltration at various field conditions such as artificial recharge ponds, percolation trenches, irrigation channels, sewage treatment systems, constructed wetlands, landfill liners and natural systems such as riverbeds and soils.

39e3f3fc226a.title: Bioclogging
39e3f3fc226a.section: General description > Change in permeability with time
39e3f3fc226a.sentence: Allison described that when soils are continuously submerged, permeability or saturated hydraulic conductivity changes in 3 key stages:

c9ab651ee257.title: Bioclogging
c9ab651ee257.section: General description > Change in permeability with time
c9ab651ee257.sentence: - After initiating field or laboratory tests, the permeability decreases to a minimum.

28c60f4a7a72.title: Bioclogging
28c60f4a7a72.section: General description > Change in permeability with time
28c60f4a7a72.sentence: - Permeability increases due to dissolving the entrapped air in soil into the percolating water.

b098c4b594ea.title: Bioclogging
b098c4b594ea.section: General description > Change in permeability with time
b098c4b594ea.sentence: - Permeability decreases for 2 to 4 weeks due to the disintegration of aggregates and biological clogging of soil pores with microbial cells and their synthesized products, slimes, or polysaccharides.

6f2887c25272.title: Bioclogging
6f2887c25272.section: General description > Various types of bioclogging
6f2887c25272.sentence: - Entrapment of gas bubbles such as methane produced by methane-producing microorganisms clog the soil pore and contributes to decreasing hydraulic conductivity.

e6cdbb7134bf.title: Bioclogging
e6cdbb7134bf.sentence: Bioclogging is a significant problem where water infiltration is hampered and countermeasures such as regular drying of the system can reduce the levels of bioclogging.

9f4055d0a165.title: Bioclogging
9f4055d0a165.section: Field observation > Field problem and countermeasures
9f4055d0a165.sentence: To minimize the bioclogging effects, pretreatment of the water to reduce suspended solids, nutrients, and organic carbon might be necessary.

17751887a260.title: Bioclogging
17751887a260.sentence: - Bioclogging plays a crucial role in sealing the bottoms of stabilization ponds for dairy farm wastewater treatment.

b1af8bfbe946.title: Bioclogging
b1af8bfbe946.sentence: Similarly, irrigation channels for seepage control may be inoculated with algae and bacteria to promote bioclogging for reducing water loss.

8e49e9fadeb6.title: Bioclogging
8e49e9fadeb6.sentence: - Turning to landfill liners, such as compacted clay liners, bioclogging emerges as a beneficial factor.

3be800775101.title: SaltMod
3be800775101.sentence: SaltMod is computer program for the prediction of the salinity of soil moisture, groundwater and drainage water, the depth of the watertable, and the drain discharge (hydrology) in irrigated agricultural lands, using different (geo)hydrologic conditions, varying water management options, including the use of ground water for irrigation, and several cropping rotation schedules.

11d6b5226c12.title: SaltMod
11d6b5226c12.sentence: Developer | Institute for Land Reclamation and Improvement (ILRI)

d4f09ccfbd09.title: SaltMod
d4f09ccfbd09.sentence: The computation method Saltmod is based on seasonal water balances of agricultural lands.

adbf5c852595.title: SaltMod
adbf5c852595.sentence: The number of seasons (Ns) can be chosen between a minimum of one and a maximum of four.

39185a12110b.title: SaltMod
39185a12110b.sentence: SaltMod's objective is to predict the long-term hydro-salinity in terms of general trends, not to arrive at exact predictions of how, for example, the situation would be on the first of April in ten years from now.

6c797197aeff.title: SaltMod
6c797197aeff.sentence: The majority of the computer models available for water and solute transport in the soil (e.g. Swatre, DrainMod) are based on Richard's differential equation for the movement of water in unsaturated soil in combination with a differential salinity dispersion equation.

8688aed800f7.title: SaltMod
8688aed800f7.sentence: The models require input of soil characteristics like the relation between unsaturated soil moisture content, water tension, hydraulic conductivity and dispersivity.

fd3026b98450.title: SaltMod
fd3026b98450.sentence: These relations vary to a great extent from place to place and are not easy to measure.

73c4432e0c2e.title: SaltMod
73c4432e0c2e.sentence: The models use short time steps and need at least a daily data base of hydrological phenomena.

a03a70533414.title: SaltMod
a03a70533414.sentence: Therefore, the SaltModod program was designed keeping in mind a relative simplicity of operation to facilitate the use by field technicians, engineers and project planners instead of specialized geo-hydrologists.

8e1813a6478b.title: SaltMod
8e1813a6478b.sentence: Saltmod accepts four different reservoirs, three of which are in the soil profile:

cd701307a2e4.title: SaltMod
cd701307a2e4.sentence: - an upper (shallow) soil reservoir or root zone

17acf7841bc0.title: SaltMod
17acf7841bc0.sentence: - an intermediate soil reservoir or transition zone

a59d43b7b92a.title: SaltMod
a59d43b7b92a.sentence: If a horizontal subsurface drainage system is present, this must be placed in the transition zone, which is then divided into two parts: an upper transition zone (above drain level) and a lower transition zone (below drain level).

c0094b4fffe8.title: SaltMod
c0094b4fffe8.sentence: Also it offers the possibility to introduce subsurface drainage systems at varying depths and with varying capacity so that they can be optimized.

b84a36665d50.title: SaltMod
b84a36665d50.sentence: Further, SaltMod gives the option of the re-use of drainage and well water (e.g. for irrigation) and it can account for farmers' response to waterlogging, soil salinity, water scarcity and over-pumping from the aquifer.

f1b450f4d73b.title: SaltMod
f1b450f4d73b.sentence: The responses influence the water and salt balances, which, in their turn, slow down the process of water logging and salinization.

fae848f66168.title: SaltMod
fae848f66168.sentence: Ultimately an equilibrium situation will be brought about.

9bd2ff7686e3.sentence: There are relatively simple and inexpensive laboratory tests that may be run to determine the hydraulic conductivity of a soil: constant-head method and falling-head method.

bfedfc02279d.sentence: Moisture stress is a form of abiotic stress that occurs when the moisture of plant tissues is reduced to suboptimal levels.

f35936922941.title: Moisture stress
f35936922941.sentence: Water stress occurs in response to atmospheric and soil water availability when the transpiration rate exceeds the rate of water uptake by the roots and cells lose turgor pressure.

2161956850a9.title: Osmosis
2161956850a9.sentence: Osmosis (/ɒzˈmoʊsɪs/, US also /ɒs-/) is the spontaneous net movement of solvent molecules through a selectively permeable membrane from a region of high water potential (region of lower solute concentration) to a region of low water potential (region of higher solute concentration), in the direction that tends to equalize the solute concentrations on the two sides.

30c7b56255f5.title: Osmosis
30c7b56255f5.sentence: Osmotic pressure is defined as the external pressure required to prevent net movement of solvent across the membrane.

161b176b3dc3.title: Osmosis
161b176b3dc3.sentence: Osmotic pressure is a colligative property, meaning that the osmotic pressure depends on the molar concentration of the solute but not on its identity.

0321857c798b.title: Osmosis
0321857c798b.sentence: Osmotic transport occurs through viscous flow of the solvent under a pressure gradient.

1df77ace0991.title: Osmosis
1df77ace0991.sentence: Therefore, osmotic solvent transport is a pressure-driven process, instead of random molecular diffusion.

adae711fa7ab.title: Osmosis
adae711fa7ab.sentence: Osmotic pressure is the main agent of support in many plants.

0c0ac2c6d5fa.title: Osmosis

770950d28a8b.title: Osmosis

c3072e8a2783.title: Osmosis
c3072e8a2783.sentence: When a plant cell is placed in a solution that is hypotonic relative to the cytoplasm, water moves into the cell and the cell swells to become turgid.

42095ece912d.sentence: Water has an unusually high surface tension of 71.99 mN/m at 25 °C which is caused by the strength of the hydrogen bonding between water molecules.

d412632f4d75.title: Properties of water
d412632f4d75.section: Physical properties > Polarity and hydrogen bonding > Capillary action
d412632f4d75.sentence: Because water has strong cohesive and adhesive forces, it exhibits capillary action.

68c32b8fab6d.title: Properties of water
68c32b8fab6d.section: Physical properties > Polarity and hydrogen bonding > Capillary action
68c32b8fab6d.sentence: Strong cohesion from hydrogen bonding and adhesion allows trees to transport water more than 100 m upward.

d473632bf7d1.title: Properties of water
d473632bf7d1.section: Physical properties > Water, ice, and vapor > Heat capacity and heats of vaporization and fusion
d473632bf7d1.sentence: Water has a very high specific heat capacity of 4184 J/(kg·K) at 20 °C (4182 J/(kg·K) at 25 °C)—the second-highest among all the heteroatomic species (after ammonia), as well as a high heat of vaporization (40.65 kJ/mol or 2257 kJ/kg at the normal boiling point), both of which are a result of the extensive hydrogen bonding between its molecules.

9ad690bfa6d9.title: Properties of water
9ad690bfa6d9.section: Physical properties > Water, ice, and vapor > Density of water and ice
9ad690bfa6d9.sentence: The density varies with temperature, but not linearly: as the temperature increases, the density rises to a peak at 3.98 °C (39.16 °F) and then decreases; the initial increase is unusual because most liquids undergo thermal expansion so that the density only decreases as a function of temperature.

9a83b6efee38.title: Properties of water
9a83b6efee38.section: Physical properties > Water, ice, and vapor > Density of water and ice
9a83b6efee38.sentence: The increase observed for water from 0 °C (32 °F) to 3.98 °C (39.16 °F) and for a few other liquids is described as negative thermal expansion.

057f853f6cca.title: Properties of water
057f853f6cca.section: Physical properties > Polarity and hydrogen bonding > Water as a solvent
057f853f6cca.sentence: Water is an excellent solvent due to its high dielectric constant.

32660e2517cf.title: Properties of water
32660e2517cf.section: Physical properties > Polarity and hydrogen bonding > Water as a solvent
32660e2517cf.sentence: Substances that mix well and dissolve in water are known as hydrophilic ("water-loving") substances, while those that do not mix well with water are known as hydrophobic ("water-fearing") substances.

2fa4ff437f0a.title: Properties of water
2fa4ff437f0a.sentence: The action of water on rock over long periods of time typically leads to weathering and water erosion, physical processes that convert solid rocks and minerals into soil and sediment, but under some conditions chemical reactions with water occur as well, resulting in metasomatism or mineral hydration, a type of chemical alteration of a rock which produces clay minerals.

cef00f4e05a4.title: Soil water (retention)
cef00f4e05a4.section: Soil water retention capacity > Soil water retention and climate
cef00f4e05a4.sentence: Soil moisture has an effect on the thermal properties of a soil profile, including conductance and heat capacity.

0c296a0f183c.title: Soil water (retention)
0c296a0f183c.section: Soil water retention capacity > Soil water retention and climate
0c296a0f183c.sentence: Recent climate modelling by Timbal et al. (2002) suggests a strong linkage between soil moisture and the persistence and variability of surface temperature and precipitation; further, that soil moisture is a significant consideration for the accuracy of "inter-annular" predications regarding the Australian climate.

0357ac4e67bc.title: Soil water (retention)
0357ac4e67bc.section: Soil water retention capacity > Soil water retention and climate
0357ac4e67bc.sentence: (more water causes soil to more slowly gain or lose temperature given equal heating; water has roughly double the heat capacity of soil)

0a61290ae3cd.title: Soil water (retention)
0a61290ae3cd.section: Soil water retention capacity > Soil water retention and climate
0a61290ae3cd.sentence: The association of soil moisture and soil thermal properties has a significant effect on temperature-related biological triggers, including seed germination, flowering, and faunal activity.

ad085013bb52.title: Soil moisture
ad085013bb52.sentence: Soil water is also important for climate modeling and numerical weather prediction.

ac42f14f20c5.title: Soil moisture
ac42f14f20c5.sentence: The Global Climate Observing System specified soil water as one of the 50 Essential Climate Variables (ECVs).

b208729f8dee.title: Throughflow
b208729f8dee.sentence: In hydrology, throughflow, a subtype of interflow (percolation), is the lateral unsaturated flow of water in the soil zone, typically through a highly permeable geologic unit overlying a less permeable one.

299d57c21ee5.title: Throughflow
299d57c21ee5.sentence: Once water infiltrates into the soil, it is still affected by gravity and infiltrates to the water table or, if permeability varies laterally, travels downslope.

91b139903e66.title: Throughflow
91b139903e66.sentence: Water thus returns to the surface, as return flow, before or on entering a stream or groundwater.

1587b37b03d0.title: Throughflow
1587b37b03d0.sentence: Throughflow usually occurs during peak hydrologic events (such as high precipitation).

6380252b6407.title: Throughflow
6380252b6407.sentence: Flow rates are dependent on the hydraulic conductivity of the geologic medium.

75989c2650be.title: Podsolisation
75989c2650be.sentence: Some bases remain in the soil, though others may be lost by throughflow.

1997966dec2f.title: Darcy (unit)
1997966dec2f.sentence: The darcy (or darcy unit) and millidarcy (md, or incorrectly mD) are units of permeability, named after Henry Darcy.

33ec835fc52d.title: Darcy (unit)
33ec835fc52d.sentence: A medium with a permeability of 1 darcy permits a flow of 1 cm3/s of a fluid with viscosity 1 cP (1 mPa·s) under a pressure gradient of 1 atm/cm acting across an area of 1 cm2.

9fc26955aa6c.title: Darcy (unit)
9fc26955aa6c.sentence: Converted to SI units, 1 darcy is equivalent to 9.869233×10^−13 m2 or 0.9869233 μm2.

f76a76b17462.title: Darcy (unit)
f76a76b17462.sentence: This conversion is usually approximated as 1 μm2.

8a3dd7ac7bbd.title: Darcy (unit)
8a3dd7ac7bbd.sentence: Typical values of permeability range as high as 100,000 darcys for gravel, to less than 0.01 microdarcys for granite.

f6ed47db3688.title: Darcy (unit)
f6ed47db3688.sentence: Sand has a permeability of approximately 1 darcy.

7fee9e964b19.title: Darcy (unit)
7fee9e964b19.sentence: They are not SI units, but they are widely used in petroleum engineering and geology.

086ccb2c2748.title: Darcy (unit)
086ccb2c2748.sentence: Specifically in the hydrology domain, permeability of soil or rock may also be defined as the flux of water under hydrostatic pressure (≈ 0.1 bar/m) at a temperature of 20 °C. In this specific setup, 1 darcy is equivalent to 0.831 m/day.

1ebe366c1d12.title: Soil Moisture Active Passive
1ebe366c1d12.sentence: Soil Moisture Active Passive (SMAP) is a NASA environmental monitoring satellite that measures soil moisture across the planet.

e3d92e3efc52.title: Soil Moisture Active Passive
e3d92e3efc52.sentence: SMAP provides measurements of the land surface soil moisture and freeze-thaw state with near-global revisit coverage in 2–3 days.

9c2fb66256d9.title: Soil Moisture Active Passive
9c2fb66256d9.sentence: It is designed to collect a global 'snapshot' of soil moisture every 2 to 3 days.

1dccc44fe882.title: Soil Moisture Active Passive
1dccc44fe882.sentence: With this frequency, changes from specific storms can be measured while also assessing impacts across seasons of the year.

483cff6f76d6.title: Soil Moisture Active Passive
483cff6f76d6.sentence: The SMAP measurement system consists of a radiometer (passive) instrument and a synthetic-aperture radar (active) instrument operating with multiple polarizations in the L-band range.

19582f4f4a4d.title: Soil Moisture Active Passive
19582f4f4a4d.sentence: On 2 September 2015, NASA announced that the amplifier failure meant that the radar could no longer return data.

f4d1d13a8f1a.title: Soil Moisture Active Passive
f4d1d13a8f1a.sentence: The science mission continues with data being returned only by the radiometer instrument.

1ecae8b796fd.title: Soil Moisture Active Passive
1ecae8b796fd.sentence: The instruments sense conditions in the top 5 cm of soil through moderate vegetation cover to yield globally mapped estimates of soil moisture and its freeze-thaw state.

4675aa7ca618.title: Soil Moisture Active Passive
4675aa7ca618.sentence: SMAP surface measurements are coupled with hydrologic models to infer soil moisture conditions in the root zone.

987cbe4a5248.title: Soil Moisture Active Passive
987cbe4a5248.sentence: SMAP soil moisture information improves the monitoring and forecasting of drought conditions, enabling new capabilities for mitigating drought impacts.

00ab7af5d2d3.title: Soil Moisture Active Passive
00ab7af5d2d3.section: Science and applications > Floods and landslides
00ab7af5d2d3.sentence: Hydrologic forecast systems calibrated and initialized with high-resolution soil moisture fields lead to improved flood forecasts and provide essential information on the potential for landslides.

0d1d4e9f6087.title: Soil Moisture Active Passive
0d1d4e9f6087.section: Science and applications > Weather and climate forecasting
0d1d4e9f6087.sentence: Initialization of numerical weather prediction models and seasonal climate models with accurate soil moisture information extend forecast lead times and enhance prediction skill.

debad2c45061.title: Soil Moisture Active Passive
debad2c45061.sentence: Improved seasonal soil moisture forecasts directly benefit famine early warning systems.
