fc7c991e537a.sentence: Several alternative retention models have been developed to account for different condition, including Brooks-Corey, Broadbridge-White, and Rogers-Stallybrass-Clements model.

353bf6bc58b1.title: Adhesion
353bf6bc58b1.sentence: Adhesion is the tendency of dissimilar particles or surfaces to cling to one another.

1f00b6d3647b.title: Adhesion
1f00b6d3647b.sentence: (Cohesion refers to the tendency of similar or identical particles and surfaces to cling to one another.)

1a319d9215c5.title: Adhesion
1a319d9215c5.sentence: Note 1: Adhesion requires energy that can come from chemical and/or physical linkages, the latter being reversible when enough energy is applied.

e3dacc5b1097.title: Adhesion
e3dacc5b1097.sentence: Five mechanisms of adhesion have been proposed to explain why one material sticks to another:

f0a9273fa433.title: Adhesion
f0a9273fa433.sentence: Chemical adhesion occurs when the surface atoms of two separate surfaces form ionic, covalent, or hydrogen bonds.

e09706e6a2d4.title: Adhesion
e09706e6a2d4.sentence: In dispersive adhesion, also known as physisorption, two materials are held together by van der Waals forces: the attraction between two molecules, each of which has a region of slight positive and negative charge.

d201a69e1240.title: Adhesion
d201a69e1240.sentence: Some conducting materials may pass electrons to form a difference in electrical charge at the joint.

4f878fe26130.title: Adhesion
4f878fe26130.sentence: Some materials may merge at the joint by diffusion.

62c7ccd7829e.title: Adhesion
62c7ccd7829e.sentence: In surface science, the term adhesion almost always refers to dispersive adhesion.

624821bf51bf.title: Adhesion
624821bf51bf.sentence: Generally, cases where the contact angle is low are considered of higher adhesion per unit area.

664947da4ac9.title: Adhesion
664947da4ac9.sentence: The strength of the adhesion between two materials depends on which of the above mechanisms occur between the two materials, and the surface area over which the two materials contact.

7f5c022d0385.title: Adhesion
7f5c022d0385.sentence: Materials that wet against each other tend to have a larger contact area than those that do not.

ffbad6a9802e.title: Plinthite
ffbad6a9802e.sentence: Plinthite (from the Greek plinthos, brick) is an iron-rich, humus-poor mixture of clay with quartz and other minerals.

672b8e7ba5fe.title: Plinthite
672b8e7ba5fe.sentence: Plinthite is a redoximorphic feature in highly weathered soil.

37f87b245bc3.title: Plinthite
37f87b245bc3.sentence: Generally, plinthite forms in a soil horizon that is saturated with water for some time during the year.

84f64b90b120.title: Plinthite
84f64b90b120.sentence: The product of pedogenesis, it commonly occurs as dark red redox concretions that usually form platy, polygonal, or reticulate patterns.

665e1fad3709.title: Plinthite
665e1fad3709.sentence: Plinthite does not harden irreversibly as a result of a single cycle of drying and rewetting.

62390c34db0c.title: Plinthite
62390c34db0c.sentence: After irreversible hardening, it is no longer considered plinthite but is called ironstone.

c8dcf8940c04.title: Plinthite
c8dcf8940c04.sentence: Plinthite is firm or very firm when the soil moisture content is near field capacity and hard when the moisture content is below the permanent wilting point.

d881f65d716b.title: Plinthite
d881f65d716b.sentence: In a moist soil, plinthite is soft enough to be cut with a spade.

7be32a3406cc.title: Plinthosol
7be32a3406cc.sentence: They are characterized by the presence of plinthite, petroplinthite, or pisoliths—concretions formed through pedogenic processes involving the accumulation of iron oxides.

c5d974d68616.title: Plinthosol
c5d974d68616.sentence: Though it may resemble a mineral when hardened, plinthite is a soil-forming (pedogenic) material rather than a true mineral.

bdb0275c5949.title: Surface tension
bdb0275c5949.sentence: Surface tension is the energy per unit area due to having a surface in a liquid.

0be7ac715120.title: Surface tension
0be7ac715120.sentence: It has the dimension of force per unit length, or energy per unit area.

5b8f7c374453.title: Surface tension
5b8f7c374453.sentence: Due to the cohesive forces, a molecule located away from the surface is pulled equally in every direction by neighboring liquid molecules, resulting in a net force of zero.

c78d3634b3c5.title: Surface tension
c78d3634b3c5.sentence: The molecules at the surface do not have an equal number of molecules on all sides of them and therefore are pulled inward.

3ab323e5be6b.title: Surface tension
3ab323e5be6b.sentence: This creates some internal pressure and forces liquid surfaces to contract to the minimum area.

1bbe3f9c6dba.title: Surface tension
1bbe3f9c6dba.sentence: Surface tension, then, is not a property of the liquid alone, but a property of the liquid's interface with another medium.

ff5d5333eace.title: Surface tension
ff5d5333eace.section: Thermodynamics > Thermodynamics of bubbles > Influence of temperature
ff5d5333eace.sentence: Surface tension is dependent on temperature.

92ad0d482ebd.title: Surface tension
92ad0d482ebd.section: Thermodynamics > Thermodynamics of bubbles > Influence of temperature
92ad0d482ebd.sentence: For that reason, when a value is given for the surface tension of an interface, temperature must be explicitly stated.

c3ecd863277e.title: Surface tension
c3ecd863277e.section: Thermodynamics > Thermodynamics of bubbles > Influence of temperature
c3ecd863277e.sentence: The general trend is that surface tension decreases with the increase of temperature, reaching a value of 0 at the critical temperature.

c022618359fb.title: Surface tension
c022618359fb.sentence: But if the pressure on one side of the surface differs from pressure on the other side, the pressure difference times surface area results in a normal force.

3541259d69a7.title: Surface tension
3541259d69a7.sentence: In order for the surface tension forces to cancel the force due to pressure, the surface must be curved.

5d44b8a48961.title: Capillary action
5d44b8a48961.sentence: Capillary action (sometimes called capillarity, capillary motion, capillary rise, capillary effect, or wicking) is the process of a liquid flowing in a narrow space without the assistance of external forces like gravity.

e9df04a02dcb.title: Capillary action
e9df04a02dcb.sentence: If the diameter of the tube is sufficiently small, then the combination of surface tension (which is caused by cohesion within the liquid) and adhesive forces between the liquid and container wall act to propel the liquid.

c0610f588515.title: Capillary action
c0610f588515.sentence: It occurs because of intermolecular forces between the liquid and surrounding plasma surfaces.

4617b0cd212c.title: Capillary action
4617b0cd212c.sentence: When the lower end of a glass tube is placed in a liquid, such as water, a concave meniscus forms.

3cd4d1aa68de.title: Capillary action
3cd4d1aa68de.sentence: The contact length (around the edge) between the top of the liquid column and the tube is proportional to the radius of the tube, while the weight of the liquid column is proportional to the square of the tube's radius.

7c21587d767f.title: Capillary action
7c21587d767f.sentence: So, a narrow tube will draw a liquid column along further than a wider tube will, given that the inner water molecules cohere sufficiently to the outer ones.

228880768324.sentence: In hydrology, capillary action describes the attraction of water molecules to soil particles.

0ba66086efb0.title: Capillary action
0ba66086efb0.sentence: Capillary action is responsible for moving groundwater from wet areas of the soil to dry areas.

4282a109d7b0.title: Capillary action
4282a109d7b0.sentence: Differences in soil potential (Ψm) drive capillary action in soil.

7551cd92af1c.title: Capillary action
7551cd92af1c.sentence: With some pairs of materials, such as mercury and glass, the intermolecular forces within the liquid exceed those between the solid and the liquid, so a convex meniscus forms and capillary action works in reverse.

365df6fec859.title: Alkali soil
365df6fec859.sentence: Where the underground water table is high and the land is subjected to high solar radiation, ground water oozes to the land surface due to capillary action and gets evaporated leaving the dissolved salts in the top layer of the soil.

32d20d47f2df.title: Alkali soil
32d20d47f2df.sentence: This is done to break the capillary pores in the soil to prevent water reaching the surface of the soil.

6169b7245e8c.title: Sorptivity
6169b7245e8c.sentence: In 1957 John Philip introduced the term sorptivity and defined it as a measure of the capacity of the medium to absorb or desorb liquid by capillarity.

13235355578c.title: Sorptivity
13235355578c.sentence: The sorptivity is widely used in characterizing soils and porous construction materials such as brick, stone and concrete.

e876190390ef.title: Sorptivity
e876190390ef.sentence: John R. Philip (1969) showed that sorptivity can be determined from horizontal infiltration where water flow is mostly controlled by capillary absorption: I=St where S is sorptivity and I is the cumulative infiltration (i.e. distance) at time t.

2c89da48d08d.title: Mariotte's bottle
2c89da48d08d.sentence: Mariotte's bottle is a device that delivers a constant rate of flow from closed bottles or tanks.

e9c7444d0cd4.title: Mariotte's bottle
e9c7444d0cd4.sentence: It is named after French physicist Edme Mariotte (1620-1684).

61913d64b352.title: Mariotte's bottle
61913d64b352.sentence: The design was first reported by McCarthy (1934).

79bafa2badcf.title: Mariotte's bottle
79bafa2badcf.sentence: As shown in the diagram, a stoppered reservoir is supplied with an air inlet and a siphon.

bba087f89e0b.title: Mariotte's bottle
bba087f89e0b.sentence: The pressure at the bottom of the air inlet is always the same as the pressure outside the reservoir, i.e. the atmospheric pressure.

991b6de6bcf7.title: Mariotte's bottle
991b6de6bcf7.sentence: If the entrance to the siphon is at the same depth, then it will always supply the water at atmospheric pressure and will deliver a flow under constant head height, regardless of the changing water level within the reservoir.

e29288145bbb.title: Mariotte's bottle
e29288145bbb.sentence: Constant head is important in simplifying constraint when measuring the movement of water in soil.

a783dc686615.sentence: The Guelph Permeameter measures unsaturated hydraulic conductivity in the field and uses this principle to create a constant head.

55daf0894237.title: Mariotte's bottle
55daf0894237.sentence: Single and double ring infiltrometers can also use the Marriotte's bottle.

f56d0da20651.title: Mariotte's bottle

0bdd032b2b2b.title: Macropore
0bdd032b2b2b.sentence: Soil macropores are not uniform but have an irregular geometry.

e8468804e2e0.title: Macropore
e8468804e2e0.sentence: They vary in shapes, sizes, and even surface roughness.

1cef0b06664b.title: Macropore
1cef0b06664b.sentence: When connected together, they form specific networks in soils.

65f387ea4af8.title: Macropore
65f387ea4af8.sentence: Therefore, the characteristics of these macropore networks can have significant influences on their functions in soils, especially in relation to water movement, aeration, and plant root growth.

46eb517c1efc.title: Macropore
46eb517c1efc.sentence: Higher connectivity of soil macropores is usually associated with higher soil permeability.

f52a6cc06593.title: Macropore
f52a6cc06593.sentence: Connection of macropores with soil surface and groundwater also contributes to water infiltration into soils and replenishment of groundwater.

7061ea390ddf.title: Macropore
7061ea390ddf.sentence: Interconnected soil macropores may not create continuous paths, especially across the soil boundaries.

e9f1672f78ca.title: Macropore
e9f1672f78ca.sentence: The existence of dead-end pores can block or slow down water and air movement.

09f7806614b6.title: Macropore
09f7806614b6.sentence: For example, higher continuousness of macropores can result in higher gas exchange between soil and the atmosphere while lead to better soil aeration.

a79c0ba7b4d7.title: Macropore
a79c0ba7b4d7.sentence: Continued connection of macropores will also provide extended spaces that plants can easily grow their roots into, without sacrificing aboveground biomass by allocating resources for their roots to search for new spaces in discontinued areas.

7d5922ebda2c.title: Macropore
7d5922ebda2c.sentence: The more sinuous the paths, the higher the resistance.

ff1baec39826.title: Hygroscopy
ff1baec39826.sentence: Hygroscopy is the phenomenon of attracting and holding water molecules by either absorption or adsorption from the surrounding environment, which is usually at normal or room temperature.

a192694dec80.title: Hygroscopy
a192694dec80.sentence: Hygroscopic substances include cellulose fibers (such as cotton and paper), sugar, caramel, honey, glycerol, ethanol, wood, methanol, sulfuric acid, many fertilizer chemicals, many salts and a wide variety of other substances.

1ce7ded072cf.title: Hygroscopy
1ce7ded072cf.sentence: The amount of moisture held by hygroscopic materials is usually proportional to the relative humidity.

68cf39de2b97.title: Hygroscopy
68cf39de2b97.sentence: Deliquescent materials are sufficiently hygroscopic that they dissolve in the water they absorb, forming an aqueous solution.

bce7fb98d79f.title: Hygroscopy
bce7fb98d79f.sentence: Unlike hygroscopy, however, deliquescence involves absorbing sufficient water to form an aqueous solution.

896b05577147.title: Hygroscopy
896b05577147.sentence: The characteristic relative humidity value at which dissolution occurs is called the deliquescence relative humidity (DRH) or critical relative humidity (CRH).

e322f0533e87.title: Hygroscopy
e322f0533e87.sentence: The DRH value depends on temperature and the form of the solid phase, specifically on the formation of crystalline hydrates.

148666cd6083.title: Soil
148666cd6083.sentence: In addition, the soil voids are saturated with water vapour, at least until the point of maximal hygroscopicity, beyond which a vapour-pressure deficit occurs in the soil pore space.

7fc448ac2e82.title: Hydropedology
7fc448ac2e82.sentence: Hydropedology is an emerging field formed from the intertwining branches of soil science and hydrology.

36a95bc251c7.title: Hydropedology
36a95bc251c7.sentence: In this case, hydropedology focuses on the interface between the hydrosphere and the pedosphere.

7622f7a1ac04.title: Hydropedology
7622f7a1ac04.sentence: Similar to hydrogeology, hydroclimatology, and ecohydrology, the emphasis is connections between hydrology and other of the earth's spheres.

42afa42d2bbb.title: Soil biomantle
42afa42d2bbb.sentence: It thus plays several essential hydropedological roles in the environment.

4be5d8f248e4.title: Impervious surface
4be5d8f248e4.sentence: Natural impervious areas are defined herein as land covers that can contribute a substantial amount of surface runoff during small and large storms, but commonly are classified as pervious areas.

042f605a4c4a.title: Impervious surface
042f605a4c4a.sentence: These natural impervious areas may include open water, wetlands, rock outcrops, barren ground (natural soils with low imperviousness), and areas of compacted soils.

ae9b9bbf24f5.title: Impervious surface
ae9b9bbf24f5.sentence: Natural impervious areas, depending on their nature and antecedent conditions, may produce stormflow from infiltration excess overland flow, saturation overland flow, or direct precipitation.

02e664ca59eb.title: Impervious surface
02e664ca59eb.sentence: Developed pervious areas may behave like impervious areas because development and subsequent use tends to compact soils and reduce infiltration rates.

ab1aafcfa38d.title: Impervious surface
ab1aafcfa38d.sentence: For example, Felton and Lull (1963) measured infiltration rates for forest soils and lawns to indicate a potential 80 percent reduction in infiltration as a result of development activities.

03a21d73304e.title: Impervious surface
03a21d73304e.sentence: Similarly, Taylor (1982) did infiltrometer tests in areas before and after suburban development and noted that topsoil alteration and compaction by construction activities reduced infiltration rates by more than 77 percent.

6ec97370335b.title: Impervious surface
6ec97370335b.sentence: The effects of natural impervious areas on runoff generation are expected to be more important in areas with low TIA than highly developed areas.

92219c01951d.title: Impervious surface
92219c01951d.sentence: The total impervious area (TIA), commonly referred to as impervious cover (IC) in calculations, can be expressed as a fraction (from zero to one) or a percentage.

0005ccf104a4.title: Impervious surface
0005ccf104a4.sentence: The total coverage by impervious surfaces in an area, such as a municipality or a drainage basin, is usually expressed as a percentage of the total land area.

3bc4ea019787.title: Impervious surface
3bc4ea019787.sentence: There are many methods for estimating TIA, including the use of the National Land Cover Data Set (NLCD) with a Geographic information system (GIS), land-use categories with categorical TIA estimates, a generalized percent developed area, and relations between population density and TIA.

da76c0ebf1c6.title: Impervious surface
da76c0ebf1c6.sentence: The NLCD consistently quantifies the percent anthropogenic TIA for the NLCD at a 30-meter (a 900 m2) pixel resolution throughout the Nation.

76e62d6d5c09.title: Impervious surface
76e62d6d5c09.sentence: Within the data set, each pixel is quantified as having a TIA value that ranges from 0 to 100 percent.

b56176b86e9d.title: Impervious surface
b56176b86e9d.sentence: The percentage imperviousness, commonly referred to as PIMP in calculations, is an important factor when considering drainage of water.

474117cde5e9.title: Impervious surface
474117cde5e9.sentence: An estimation of PIMP is given by PIMP = 6.4J^0.5 where J is the number of dwellings per hectare (Butler and Davies 2000).

7a94966fb85a.title: Impervious surface
7a94966fb85a.sentence: For example, woodland has a PIMP value of 10%, whereas dense commercial areas have a PIMP value of 100%.

5ad64b9f05e6.title: Impervious surface
5ad64b9f05e6.sentence: Homer and others (2007) indicate that about 76 percent of the conterminous United States is classified as having less than 1 percent impervious cover, 11 percent with impervious cover of 1 to 10 percent, 4 percent with an estimated impervious cover of 11 to 20 percent, 4.4 percent with an estimated impervious cover of 21 to 40 percent, and about 4.4 percent with an estimated impervious cover greater than 40 percent.

4a51dd813c56.title: Continuity equation
4a51dd813c56.sentence: A continuity equation or transport equation is an equation that describes the transport of some quantity.

42b668e5d4c9.title: Continuity equation
42b668e5d4c9.sentence: Continuity equations are a stronger, local form of conservation laws.

65cad4beef67.title: Continuity equation
65cad4beef67.sentence: The integral form of the continuity equation states that:

5cc2bfb0cb31.title: Continuity equation
5cc2bfb0cb31.sentence: - The amount of q in a region increases when additional q flows inward through the surface of the region, and decreases when it flows outward;

f7b6cf03e648.title: Continuity equation
f7b6cf03e648.sentence: - The amount of q in a region increases when new q is created inside the region, and decreases when q is destroyed;

d08f12da6193.title: Continuity equation
d08f12da6193.sentence: - Apart from these two processes, there is no other way for the amount of q in a region to change.

0b274cb6ec6e.title: Continuity equation
0b274cb6ec6e.sentence: Terms that generate q (i.e., σ > 0) or remove q (i.e., σ < 0) are referred to as sources and sinks respectively.

de6e1ee7842c.title: Continuity equation
de6e1ee7842c.sentence: In fluid dynamics, the continuity equation states that the rate at which mass enters a system is equal to the rate at which mass leaves the system plus the accumulation of mass within the system.

a27604de50f0.title: Continuity equation
a27604de50f0.sentence: The time derivative can be understood as the accumulation (or loss) of mass in the system, while the divergence term represents the difference in flow in versus flow out.

6cbbb17724c0.title: Soil inference system
6cbbb17724c0.sentence: Soil inference system (SINFERS) is the term proposed by McBratney et al. (2002) as a knowledge base to infer soil properties and populate the digital soil databases.

78ab86eb9ad1.title: Soil inference system
78ab86eb9ad1.sentence: SINFERS takes measurements with a given level of certainty and infers data that is not known with minimal uncertainties by means of logically linked predictive functions.

0c76912873d0.title: Soil inference system
0c76912873d0.sentence: These predictive functions, in a non-spatial context are referred to as pedotransfer functions.

501d99894522.title: Soil inference system
501d99894522.sentence: The basic assumption underlying SINFERS is that if one knows or is able to predict the basic fundamental properties of a soil, one should be able to infer all other physical and chemical properties using PTFs.

9f315ee106c8.title: Soil inference system
9f315ee106c8.sentence: Crucial to the operation of SINFERS are reliable inputs, the ability to link basic soil information, and the quantification of uncertainty.

fc295c80aaee.title: Soil inference system
fc295c80aaee.sentence: SINFERS computes new properties not only from an original input set, but also from all newly inferred properties.

3a02dd17e659.title: Soil inference system
3a02dd17e659.sentence: During 2007–2009, Grant Tranter of the University of Sydney, Australia in collaboration with Jason Morris of Morris Technical Solutions, US, completed a working prototype of SINFERS.

9a3065ca77c6.title: Hydraulic head
9a3065ca77c6.sentence: The hydraulic gradient is a vector gradient between two or more hydraulic head measurements over the length of the flow path.

c1387f7a9b3b.title: Hydraulic head
c1387f7a9b3b.sentence: The hydraulic gradient norm i, a dimensionless quantity (of kind length per length), can be calculated between two points with known head values as a ratio: i=dhdl where

d1761772940e.title: Hydraulic head
d1761772940e.sentence: - dh=h2−h1 is the difference between two hydraulic heads (length, usually in m or ft), and

50aeb109494e.title: Hydraulic head
50aeb109494e.sentence: - dl is the flow path length between the two piezometers (length, usually in m or ft)

a38207819d51.title: Hydraulic head
a38207819d51.sentence: For groundwater, it is also called the Darcy slope, since it determines the quantity of a Darcy flux or discharge.

bae19d377826.title: Hydraulic head
bae19d377826.sentence: In Cartesian coordinates, this can be expressed as: ∇h=(∂h∂x,∂h∂y,∂h∂z)=∂h∂x𝐢+∂h∂y𝐣+∂h∂z𝐤 This vector describes both the magnitude and the direction of the groundwater flow, where negative values indicate flow along the dimension, and zero indicates 'no flow'.

71b491ff5641.title: Hydraulic head
71b491ff5641.sentence: As with any other example in physics, energy must flow from high to low, which is why the flow is in the negative gradient.

a4a3c39e2081.title: Hydraulic head
a4a3c39e2081.sentence: This vector can be used in conjunction with Darcy's law and a tensor of hydraulic conductivity to determine the flux of water in three dimensions.

fa2ac1ea43b4.title: Infiltrometer
fa2ac1ea43b4.sentence: A double ring infiltrometer requires two rings: an inner and outer ring.

afd1a843735f.title: Infiltrometer
afd1a843735f.sentence: The purpose is to create a one-dimensional flow of water from the inner ring, as the analysis of data is simplified.

9ba8a548d8e0.title: Infiltrometer
9ba8a548d8e0.sentence: An inner ring is driven into the ground, and a second bigger ring around that to help control the flow of water through the first ring.

8ac99ba52aae.title: Infiltrometer
8ac99ba52aae.sentence: Water is supplied either with a constant or falling head condition, and the operator records how much water infiltrates from the inner ring into the soil over a given time period.

027130d993d7.title: Infiltrometer
027130d993d7.sentence: If water is flowing in one-dimension at steady state condition, and a unit gradient is present in the underlying soil, the infiltration rate is approximately equal to the saturated hydraulic conductivity.

9fc1da7e5adf.title: Infiltrometer
9fc1da7e5adf.sentence: The ASTM standard method specifies inner and outer rings of 30 and 60 cm diameters, respectively.

68cad222f891.title: Neutron probe
68cad222f891.sentence: A neutron probe is a device used to measure the quantity of water present in soil.

260fa596be03.title: Neutron probe
260fa596be03.sentence: A typical neutron probe contains a pellet of americium-241 and beryllium.

d7d211f0565c.title: Neutron probe
d7d211f0565c.sentence: The alpha particles emitted by the decay of the americium collide with the light beryllium nuclei, producing fast neutrons.

f592e7886e6d.title: Neutron probe
f592e7886e6d.sentence: When these fast neutrons collide with hydrogen nuclei present in the soil being studied, they lose much of their energy.

3d5f2baddf08.title: Neutron probe
3d5f2baddf08.sentence: The detection of slow neutrons returning to the probe allows an estimate of the amount of hydrogen present.

21249b79c794.title: Neutron probe
21249b79c794.sentence: Since water contains two atoms of hydrogen per molecule, this therefore gives a measure of soil moisture.

088af72ba4a7.title: Irrigation scheduling
088af72ba4a7.section: Methods of scheduling > Soil moisture measurement
088af72ba4a7.sentence: - Neutron Probes: Used in agriculture for highly accurate deep-soil readings.

fd1ebf13b590.title: Bound water
fd1ebf13b590.sentence: In hydrology, bound water, is an extremely thin layer of water surrounding mineral surfaces.

a1bee14baab8.title: Bound water
a1bee14baab8.sentence: The strong attraction between these surfaces causes an extremely thin water film (a few molecules thick) to form on the mineral surface.

e3eee1106387.title: Bound water
e3eee1106387.sentence: Water molecules have a strong electrical polarity, meaning that there is a very strong positive charge on one side of the molecule and a strong negative charge on the other.

615bf81e7fbb.title: Bound water
615bf81e7fbb.sentence: This causes the water molecules to bond to each other and to other charged surfaces, such as soil minerals.

c18e87d38122.title: Bound water
c18e87d38122.sentence: Clay in particular has a high ability to bond with water molecules.

2ac8d2b91b1e.title: Bound water
2ac8d2b91b1e.sentence: These water molecules are much less mobile than the rest of the water in the soil, and have significant effects on soil dielectric permittivity and freezing-thawing.

7ec7eb7798f4.title: Pressure head
7ec7eb7798f4.sentence: In fluid mechanics, pressure head is the height of a liquid column that corresponds to a particular pressure exerted by the liquid column on the base of its container.

372052e92d8f.title: Pressure head
372052e92d8f.sentence: ψ Psi (Greek) is pressure head (which is actually a length, typically in units of meters or centimetres of water)

5eabb6136963.title: Pressure head
5eabb6136963.sentence: Pressure head is a component of hydraulic head, in which it is combined with elevation head.

399e357d9e9c.title: Aquifer
399e357d9e9c.sentence: Saturated means the pressure head of the water is greater than atmospheric pressure (it has a gauge pressure > 0).

51721ab0dc05.title: Aquifer
51721ab0dc05.sentence: The definition of the water table is the surface where the pressure head is equal to atmospheric pressure (where gauge pressure = 0).

d38a282bb6e4.title: Aquifer
d38a282bb6e4.sentence: Unsaturated conditions occur above the water table where the pressure head is negative (absolute pressure can never be negative, but gauge pressure can) and the water that incompletely fills the pores of the aquifer material is under suction.

c0304e702914.title: Pressure head
c0304e702914.sentence: Scientists frequently use columns of water (or mercury) to measure pressure (manometric pressure measurement), since for a given fluid, pressure head is proportional to pressure.

b824cf863dd3.title: Hagen–Poiseuille equation
b824cf863dd3.sentence: In fluid dynamics, the Hagen–Poiseuille equation, also known as the Hagen–Poiseuille law, Poiseuille law or Poiseuille equation, is a physical law that gives the pressure drop in an incompressible and Newtonian fluid in laminar flow flowing through a long cylindrical pipe of constant cross section.

0864c968e2e8.title: Hagen–Poiseuille equation
0864c968e2e8.sentence: The assumptions of the equation are that the fluid is incompressible and Newtonian; the flow is laminar through a pipe of constant circular cross-section that is substantially longer than its diameter; and there is no acceleration of fluid in the pipe.

2e4796590880.title: Hagen–Poiseuille equation
2e4796590880.sentence: For velocities and pipe diameters above a threshold, actual fluid flow is not laminar but turbulent, leading to larger pressure drops than calculated by the Hagen–Poiseuille equation.

beb16a68840c.title: Hagen–Poiseuille equation
beb16a68840c.sentence: The equation does not hold close to the pipe entrance.

22140dc8fbf6.title: Hagen–Poiseuille equation
22140dc8fbf6.sentence: The equation fails in the limit of low viscosity, wide and/or short pipe.

95cd9805b517.title: Hagen–Poiseuille equation
95cd9805b517.sentence: Low viscosity or a wide pipe may result in turbulent flow, making it necessary to use more complex models, such as the Darcy–Weisbach equation.

386cc993f5fb.title: Hagen–Poiseuille equation
386cc993f5fb.sentence: It was experimentally derived independently by Jean Léonard Marie Poiseuille in 1838 and Gotthilf Heinrich Ludwig Hagen, and published by Hagen in 1839 and then by Poiseuille in 1840–41 and 1846.

45c6b2be60c9.title: Hagen–Poiseuille equation
45c6b2be60c9.sentence: The theoretical justification of the Poiseuille law was given by George Stokes in 1845.

b6352a367ac2.title: Soil moisture zone
b6352a367ac2.sentence: The soil moisture zone is the depth of soil from which plant roots extract water.

5b218544c3f4.title: Irrigation scheduling
5b218544c3f4.sentence: The goal is to apply enough water to fully wet the plant's root zone while minimizing overwatering and ensuring high water use efficiency (WUE).

2ea93696f926.title: Groundwater recharge
2ea93696f926.sentence: Recharge can help move excess salts that accumulate in the root zone to deeper soil layers, or into the groundwater system.

0c68b9518fe4.title: Frequency domain sensor
0c68b9518fe4.sentence: Frequency domain (FD) sensor is an instrument developed for measuring soil moisture content.

305ed79bb405.title: Frequency domain sensor
305ed79bb405.sentence: The instrument has an oscillating circuit, the sensing part of the sensor is embedded in the soil, and the operating frequency will depend on the value of soil's dielectric constant.

35736609a953.title: Frequency domain sensor
35736609a953.sentence: - Capacitance probe, or fringe capacitance sensor.

ea0f48c64d21.title: Frequency domain sensor
ea0f48c64d21.sentence: - Electrical impedance sensor consists of soil probes and uses electrical impedance measurement.

577528bccd28.title: Frequency domain sensor
577528bccd28.sentence: The most common configuration is based on the standing wave principle (Gaskin & Miller, 1996).

aa1dcaa923c5.title: Frequency domain sensor
aa1dcaa923c5.sentence: The device comprises a 100 MHz sinusoidal oscillator, a fixed impedance coaxial transmission line, and probe wires which are buried in the soil.

532568b43217.title: Frequency domain sensor
532568b43217.sentence: The oscillator signal is propagated along the transmission line into the soil probe, and if the probe's impedance differs from that of the transmission line, a proportion of the incident signal is reflected along the line towards the signal source.

8e096105ae4a.title: Frequency domain sensor
8e096105ae4a.sentence: Compared to time domain reflectometer (TDR), FD sensors are cheaper to build and have a faster response time.

f78534a8372e.title: Frequency domain sensor
f78534a8372e.sentence: However, because of the complex electrical field around the probe, the sensor needs to be calibrated for different soil types.

e120280bc9d4.title: Frequency domain sensor
e120280bc9d4.sentence: Some commercial sensors have been able to remove the soil type sensitivity by using a high frequency.

4decf2a4267b.title: Horton overland flow
4decf2a4267b.sentence: In soil science, Horton overland flow describes the tendency of water to flow horizontally across land surfaces when rainfall has exceeded infiltration capacity and depression storage capacity.

af007e6beba3.title: Horton overland flow
af007e6beba3.sentence: It is named after Robert E. Horton, the engineer who made the first detailed studies of the phenomenon.

f1b817ba6073.title: Surface runoff
f1b817ba6073.sentence: This is also called Hortonian overland flow (after Robert E. Horton), or unsaturated overland flow.

ce8de589ee06.title: Horton overland flow
ce8de589ee06.sentence: It is shallow, sheetlike, and fast-moving, and hence capable of extensively eroding soil and bedrock.

73c7a7a8ce94.title: Horton overland flow
73c7a7a8ce94.sentence: The process also poses a significant problem in areas with steep terrain, where water can build up great speed and where soil is less stable, and in farmlands, where soil is flat and loose.

d65d2740da54.title: Horton overland flow
d65d2740da54.sentence: Paved surfaces such as asphalt, which are designed to be flat and impermeable, rapidly achieve Horton overland flow.

2bc0cf792394.title: Horton overland flow
2bc0cf792394.sentence: Horton overland flow is most commonly encountered in urban construction sites and unpaved rural roads, where vegetation has been stripped away, exposing bare dirt.

a264c0210d8d.title: Hysteresis
a264c0210d8d.sentence: Matric potential hysteresis arises from differences in wetting behaviour causing dry medium to re-wet; that is, it depends on the saturation history of the porous medium.

8c3f1e47ea21.title: Hysteresis
8c3f1e47ea21.sentence: The relationship between matric water potential and water content is the basis of the water retention curve.

9de6c3a965ed.title: Hysteresis
9de6c3a965ed.sentence: Hysteretic behaviour means that, for example, at a matric potential (Ψm) of 5 kPa, the volumetric water content (θ) of a fine sandy soil matrix could be anything between 8% and 25%.

c8aef3164457.title: Hysteresis
c8aef3164457.sentence: Two other types of sensors used to measure soil water matric potential are also influenced by hysteresis effects within the sensor itself.

7b947ae7e4f3.title: Hysteresis
7b947ae7e4f3.sentence: As of 2002, only desorption curves are usually measured during calibration of soil moisture sensors.

6871791216bc.title: Capillary pressure
6871791216bc.sentence: In fluid statics, capillary pressure (pc) is the pressure between two immiscible fluids in a thin tube (see capillary action), resulting from the interactions of forces between the fluids and solid walls of the tube.

7475c0aa7c26.title: Capillary pressure
7475c0aa7c26.sentence: Regardless of the system, a pressure difference arises at the resulting curved interface between the two fluids.

548ab569730b.title: Capillary pressure
548ab569730b.sentence: The Young–Laplace equation is the force up description of capillary pressure, and the most commonly used variation of the capillary pressure equation:

a4e0086e31c1.title: Capillary pressure
a4e0086e31c1.sentence: r is the effective radius of the interface

37ffb56c4928.title: Capillary pressure
37ffb56c4928.sentence: θ is the wetting angle of the liquid on the surface of the capillary

ef7010e83d8a.title: Capillary pressure
ef7010e83d8a.sentence: The wetting phase is identified by its ability to preferentially diffuse across the capillary walls before the non-wetting phase.

1ab0e451f5f0.title: Capillary pressure
1ab0e451f5f0.sentence: The "wettability" of a fluid depends on its surface tension, the forces that drive a fluid's tendency to take up the minimal amount of space possible, and it is determined by the contact angle of the fluid.

e02af39765f1.title: Capillary pressure
e02af39765f1.sentence: A fluid's "wettability" can be controlled by varying capillary surface properties (e.g. roughness, hydrophilicity).

25e5bd9f9314.title: Capillary pressure
25e5bd9f9314.section: Applications > Petrochemical industry > Porous Plate Method
25e5bd9f9314.sentence: The Porous Plate Method is an accurate way to understand capillary pressure relationships in fluid-air systems.

60856830bce2.title: Capillary pressure
60856830bce2.section: Applications > Petrochemical industry > Porous Plate Method
60856830bce2.sentence: In this process, a sample saturated with water is placed on a flat plate, also saturated with water, inside a gas chamber.

485628b56121.title: Capillary pressure
485628b56121.section: Applications > Petrochemical industry > Porous Plate Method
485628b56121.sentence: Gas is injected at increasing pressures, thus displacing the water through the plate.

c8cffb9666a4.title: Capillary pressure
c8cffb9666a4.section: Applications > Petrochemical industry > Porous Plate Method
c8cffb9666a4.sentence: The pressure of the gas represents the capillary pressure, and the amount of water ejected from the porous plate is correlated to the water saturation of the sample.

bc23e28028b0.title: Capillary pressure
bc23e28028b0.sentence: In Beskow’s studies, he defined this soil moisture tension as “capillary pressure” (and soil water as “capillary water”).

9df698275067.title: Soil moisture
9df698275067.sentence: Preferential flow occurs along interconnected macropores, crevices, root and worm channels, which drain water under gravity.

902c136f480e.title: Macropore
902c136f480e.section: Importance of soil macropores > Water and air movement
902c136f480e.sentence: Connected macropores create these paths and result in the so-called preferential flows in soils.

9f202c55caca.title: Soil moisture
9f202c55caca.sentence: Tree roots, whether living or dead, create preferential channels for rainwater flow through soil, magnifying infiltration rates of water up to 27 times.

465ff354a3db.title: Macropore
465ff354a3db.section: Importance of soil macropores > Solute and pollutant transport
465ff354a3db.sentence: For instance, while preferential flow paths consist of macropores enhance the drainage of soil water, the dissolved nutrients can be carried away rapidly and lead to an uneven distribution of water as well as chemicals in the soils.

3e94456a5e67.title: Groundwater recharge
3e94456a5e67.sentence: This extreme form of preferential flow, accelerates the transport of contaminants and the erosion of such tunnels.

e9c0af7be7e8.title: Soil moisture
e9c0af7be7e8.sentence: Many models based on soil physics now allow for some representation of preferential flow as a dual continuum, dual porosity or dual permeability options, but these have generally been "bolted on" to the Richards solution without any rigorous physical underpinning.

5edffec88a5c.title: Kozeny–Carman equation
5edffec88a5c.sentence: The Kozeny–Carman equation (or Carman–Kozeny equation or Kozeny equation) is a relation used in the field of fluid dynamics to calculate the pressure drop of a fluid flowing through a packed bed of solids.

d63747700111.title: Kozeny–Carman equation
d63747700111.sentence: Combining these equations gives the final Kozeny equation for absolute (single phase) permeability:

4d87b968f270.title: Kozeny–Carman equation
4d87b968f270.sentence: The equation was first proposed by Kozeny (1927) and later modified by Carman (1937, 1956).

f9db648a2aa9.title: Kozeny–Carman equation
f9db648a2aa9.sentence: The equation was derived by Kozeny (1927) and Carman (1937, 1956) from a starting point of (a) modelling fluid flow in a packed bed as laminar fluid flow in a collection of curving passages/tubes crossing the packed bed and (b) Poiseuille's law describing laminar fluid flow in straight, circular section pipes.

10f916838d21.title: Kozeny–Carman equation
10f916838d21.sentence: - ε is the porosity of the bed (≃0.37 for randomly packed spheres);

8030cb30ff9c.title: Kozeny–Carman equation
8030cb30ff9c.sentence: - dp is the diameter of the volume equivalent spherical particle;

8f1c92ebab2d.title: Kozeny–Carman equation
8f1c92ebab2d.sentence: This equation is a particular case of Darcy's law, with a very specific permeability.

4c57fd252737.title: Kozeny–Carman equation
4c57fd252737.sentence: The equation is only valid for creeping flow, i.e. in the slowest limit of laminar flow.

0982f9546f8d.title: Kozeny–Carman equation
0982f9546f8d.sentence: This equation holds for flow through packed beds with particle Reynolds numbers up to approximately 1.0, after which point frequent shifting of flow channels in the bed causes considerable kinetic energy losses.

ac20cf8f89c0.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/05%3A_Soil_Physics_and_Water_Relations/5.07%3A_Soil-Water_Relations
ac20cf8f89c0.sentence: Water held within small soil pores by adhesion and cohesion is termed capillary water.

0b424fc1f6fb.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/05%3A_Soil_Physics_and_Water_Relations/5.07%3A_Soil-Water_Relations
0b424fc1f6fb.sentence: Only a portion of the total capillary water in the soil is available to plants.

84a6094a149c.sentence: Subsurface water may return to the surface in groundwater flow, such as from a spring, seep, or a water well, or subsurface return to streams, rivers, and oceans.

0f6833e0c2f8.title: Subsurface flow
0f6833e0c2f8.sentence: Water returns to the land surface at a lower elevation than where infiltration occurred, under the force of gravity or gravity induced pressures.

a5772d834dd8.title: Subsurface flow
a5772d834dd8.sentence: Groundwater tends to move slowly, and is replenished slowly, so it can remain in aquifers for thousands of years.

74d584efd631.title: Tile drainage
74d584efd631.section: Social and ecological effects of tile drainage
74d584efd631.sentence: Ecologically, the expansion of drainage systems has had tremendous negative effects.

6e2b6fbd59d0.title: Tile drainage
6e2b6fbd59d0.section: Social and ecological effects of tile drainage
6e2b6fbd59d0.sentence: Hundreds of thousands of wetland species experienced significant population declines as their habitat was increasingly fragmented and converted to other uses.

e9e8bb0d12c2.title: Tile drainage
e9e8bb0d12c2.section: Social and ecological effects of tile drainage
e9e8bb0d12c2.sentence: The process of tile drainage, used to dry soils quickly and efficiently, results in an efficient transmission of water to the river – so efficient that higher volumes of water are delivered to rivers.

1c86552be7f7.title: Tile drainage
1c86552be7f7.section: Social and ecological effects of tile drainage
1c86552be7f7.sentence: This loss of equilibrium results in extreme amounts of bank erosion, which results in over-burdensome sediment loads and critical impacts on natural environments and riverine habitats.

e30970583205.title: Tile drainage
e30970583205.section: Social and ecological effects of tile drainage
e30970583205.sentence: Drainage tile sometimes decreases soil erosion and runoff of some nutrients, including phosphorus.

774c7cd30b5d.title: Tile drainage
774c7cd30b5d.section: Social and ecological effects of tile drainage
774c7cd30b5d.sentence: The soil can filter the water before it enters the streams and rivers.

d3bdd50679d5.title: Tile drainage
d3bdd50679d5.section: Social and ecological effects of tile drainage
d3bdd50679d5.sentence: However, by bypassing surface improvements like conservation tillage or riparian buffers, tile drainage can also create problems with water quality and outflow from tile drainage tends to be extremely high in nitrogen.

ea25e3690b51.title: Tile drainage
ea25e3690b51.section: Social and ecological effects of tile drainage
ea25e3690b51.sentence: Since surface forms of conservation agriculture are less effective in tile-drained systems, different practices, such as controlled drainage or constructed wetlands, may be more effective.

7f7d66e28af9.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/05%3A_Soil_Physics_and_Water_Relations/5.07%3A_Soil-Water_Relations
7f7d66e28af9.sentence: Water moves through a soil in the large pores and drains away due to the force of gravity.

1fc6cb719c3f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/05%3A_Soil_Physics_and_Water_Relations/5.07%3A_Soil-Water_Relations
1fc6cb719c3f.sentence: This water is called gravitational water.

5e52865e78df.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/05%3A_Soil_Physics_and_Water_Relations/5.07%3A_Soil-Water_Relations
5e52865e78df.sentence: Gravitational water represents the difference in soil moisture content between the saturation condition and field capacity.

a67c5c57f09d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/05%3A_Soil_Physics_and_Water_Relations/5.07%3A_Soil-Water_Relations
a67c5c57f09d.sentence: Gravitational water = soil moisture content at saturation - soil moisture content at field capacity.

c028e8957582.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Soils_Laboratory_Manual_(Moorberg_and_Crouse)/03%3A_Soil_Physics/03.3%3A_Soil_and_Water_Relationships
c028e8957582.sentence: Gravitational water | water content at saturation – water held at field capacity

09dbd2c65557.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Soils_Laboratory_Manual_(Moorberg_and_Crouse)/03%3A_Soil_Physics/03.3%3A_Soil_and_Water_Relationships
09dbd2c65557.sentence: | water that drains from macropores too rapidly for plants to use

297923ac7eab.title: Vadose zone
297923ac7eab.sentence: The vadose zone (from the Latin word for "shallow"), also termed the unsaturated zone, is the part of Earth between the land surface and the top of the phreatic zone, the position at which the groundwater (the water in the soil's pores) is at atmospheric pressure.

ab0bded65486.title: Vadose zone
ab0bded65486.sentence: Hence, the vadose zone extends from the top of the ground surface to the water table.

da1c08b97e91.title: Vadose zone
da1c08b97e91.sentence: Water in the vadose zone has a pressure head less than atmospheric pressure, and is retained by a combination of adhesion (funiculary groundwater), and capillary action (capillary groundwater).

37ce02959ef3.title: Vadose zone
37ce02959ef3.sentence: If the vadose zone envelops soil, the water contained therein is termed soil moisture.

a303db6feca2.title: Vadose zone
a303db6feca2.sentence: The soil and rock in the vadose zone are not fully saturated with water; that is, the pores within them contain air as well as water.

3e73a84d5c58.title: Vadose zone
3e73a84d5c58.sentence: The vadose zone does not include the area that is still saturated above the water table, often referred to as the capillary fringe.

c5398dcda33e.title: Vadose zone
c5398dcda33e.sentence: In some places, the vadose zone is absent, as is common where there are lakes and marshes, and in some places, it is hundreds of meters thick, as is common in arid regions.

cc7a0ffa2a8f.title: Vadose zone
cc7a0ffa2a8f.sentence: The Richards equation is often used to mathematically describe the flow of water, which is based partially on Darcy's law.

79732f25846e.title: Vadose zone
79732f25846e.sentence: The vadose zone is often the main factor controlling water movement from the land surface to the aquifer.

f17155a53bad.title: Vadose zone
f17155a53bad.sentence: Thus, it strongly affects the rate of aquifer recharge and is critical for the use and management of groundwater.

f7dd608702bc.title: Vadose zone
f7dd608702bc.sentence: Flow rates and chemical reactions in the vadose zone also control whether, where, and how fast contaminants enter groundwater supplies.

876e78ce2cea.title: Vadose zone
876e78ce2cea.sentence: Unlike the aquifers of the underlying water-saturated phreatic zone, the vadose zone is not a source of readily available water for human consumption.

9e67e35c5c94.title: Vadose zone
9e67e35c5c94.sentence: It is of great importance in providing water and nutrients that are vital to the soil carbon sponge and the biosphere.

f75067b041fc.title: Vadose zone
f75067b041fc.sentence: It is intensively used for the cultivation of plants, construction of buildings, and disposal of waste.

fd450a82266a.title: Vadose zone
fd450a82266a.sentence: Movement of water within the vadose zone is studied within soil physics and hydrology, particularly hydrogeology, and is of importance to agriculture, contaminant transport, and flood control.

844b9ed6372d.title: Capillary fringe
844b9ed6372d.sentence: The capillary fringe is the subsurface layer in which groundwater seeps up from a water table by capillary action to fill pores.

c3639ae10e7d.title: Capillary fringe
c3639ae10e7d.sentence: Pores at the base of the capillary fringe are filled with water due to tension saturation.

83704617cbcd.title: Capillary fringe
83704617cbcd.sentence: This saturated portion of the capillary fringe is less than the total capillary rise because of the presence of a mix in pore size.

3d5584810fcd.title: Capillary fringe
3d5584810fcd.sentence: If the pore size is small and relatively uniform, it is possible that soils can be completely saturated with water for several feet above the water table.

f6137a8d42e7.title: Capillary fringe
f6137a8d42e7.sentence: Alternately, when the pore size is large, the saturated portion will extend only a few inches above the water table.

b6b11a7b42e2.title: Capillary fringe
b6b11a7b42e2.sentence: Capillary action supports a vadose zone above the saturated base, within which water content decreases with distance above the water table.

e86f9328e768.title: Capillary fringe
e86f9328e768.sentence: Some workers restrict their definition of the capillary fringe only to the tension-saturated base portion and exclude it wholly from the vadose zone.

f0bb1f92a5ec.title: Capillary fringe
f0bb1f92a5ec.sentence: This is more common among workers addressing solute transport and water flow.

5a365e83c838.title: Capillary fringe
5a365e83c838.sentence: Others define the capillary fringe as including both the tension-saturated and unsaturated portions.

ba4f64b9fd74.title: Capillary fringe
ba4f64b9fd74.sentence: This is the preferred definition among workers dealing with the remediation of salt affected soils as well as those dealing with the vapor phase of soil processes and bioremediation.

a0bdc35973f3.title: Soil
a0bdc35973f3.sentence: Rapid salination occurs when the land surface is within the capillary fringe of saline groundwater.

20deff1811d3.title: Redox gradient
20deff1811d3.sentence: In groundwater, this oxic-anoxic environment is referred to as the capillary fringe, where the water table meets soil and fills empty pores.

dbbd0677aef2.title: Septic drain field
dbbd0677aef2.sentence: Molecular diffusion controls the mixing of soluble organic compounds into the groundwater and the transport of oxygen from underlying groundwater or the capillary fringe of the groundwater surface to micro-organisms capable of catabolizing dissolved organic compounds remaining in the effluent plume.

9a831395ef03.title: Tensiometer (soil science)
9a831395ef03.sentence: A tensiometer in soil science is a measuring instrument used to determine the matric water potential ({\displaystyle \Psi _{m}}) (soil moisture tension) in the vadose zone.

b1dd229aa5e1.title: Tensiometer (soil science)
b1dd229aa5e1.sentence: This device typically consists of a glass or plastic tube with a porous ceramic cup and is filled with water.

a3a8f9d1d8ba.title: Tensiometer (soil science)
a3a8f9d1d8ba.sentence: The top of the tube has either a built-in vacuum gauge or a rubber cap used with a portable puncture tensiometer instrument, which uses a hypodermic needle to measure the pressure inside the tensiometer.

b5f83085133b.title: Tensiometer (soil science)
b5f83085133b.sentence: The tensiometer is buried in the soil, and a hand pump is used to pull a partial vacuum.

c2c91e0cae53.title: Tensiometer (soil science)
c2c91e0cae53.sentence: As water is pulled out of the soil by plants and evaporation, the vacuum inside the tube increases.

6d6d3844350f.title: Tensiometer (soil science)
6d6d3844350f.sentence: When the soil is wetted flow can also occur in the reverse direction: as water is added to the soil, the vacuum inside the tube pulls moisture from the soil and decreases.

8b518a42f928.title: Lorenzo A. Richards
8b518a42f928.sentence: The tensiometer was developed from the idea of using a semi-permeable, porous ceramic material to balance a pressure potential against a matric potential; once equilibrium had established, the matric potential of the soil could be determined by balancing the pressure potential.

2d8be8a6cb17.title: Tensiometer (soil science)
2d8be8a6cb17.sentence: When the water pressure in the tensiometer is determined to be in equilibrium with the water pressure in the soil, the tensiometer gauge reading represents the matric potential of the soil.

ddca18aff853.title: Tensiometer (soil science)
ddca18aff853.sentence: Such tensiometers are used in irrigation scheduling to help farmers and other irrigation managers to determine when to water.

9d2734ce4f2f.title: Tensiometer (soil science)
9d2734ce4f2f.sentence: In conjunction with a water retention curve, tensiometers can be used to determine how much to water.

c6ca6a41907d.title: Lorenzo A. Richards
c6ca6a41907d.sentence: Early in his career, Richards recognised the importance of capillary potential to plant-soil relations, and described the principles, construction and operation of the tensiometer.

fe75dc18dc99.title: Lorenzo A. Richards
fe75dc18dc99.sentence: He made continual improvements to his original design and the operation of the tensiometer.

96c9a5f275c3.title: Richards equation
96c9a5f275c3.sentence: The Richards equation represents the movement of water in unsaturated soils, and is attributed to Lorenzo A. Richards who published the equation in 1931.

640535025d34.title: Richards equation
640535025d34.sentence: The equation is based on Darcy-Buckingham law representing flow in porous media under variably saturated conditions, which is stated as

3891c1b70ffd.title: Richards equation
3891c1b70ffd.sentence: S is the source/sink term [T−1], typically root water uptake.

50d2f1722e3d.title: Richards equation
50d2f1722e3d.sentence: Then substituting the fluxes by the Darcy-Buckingham law the following mixed-form Richards equation is obtained:

2a38172b0b5f.title: Richards equation
2a38172b0b5f.sentence: Although attributed to L. A. Richards, the equation was originally introduced 9 years earlier by Lewis Fry Richardson in 1922.

7fbb158e5698.title: Richards equation
7fbb158e5698.sentence: It is a quasilinear partial differential equation; its analytical solution is often limited to specific initial and boundary conditions.

0a1a4a5ae13f.title: Richards equation
0a1a4a5ae13f.sentence: Proof of the existence and uniqueness of solution was given only in 1983 by Alt and Luckhaus.

63d013d323ee.title: Richards equation
63d013d323ee.sentence: The above-given mixed formulation involves two unknown variables: θ and h.

2a9a00aa17bf.title: Richards equation
2a9a00aa17bf.sentence: This can be easily resolved by considering constitutive relation θ(h), which is known as the water retention curve.

ecc6eed2737b.title: Richards equation
ecc6eed2737b.sentence: The Richards equation in any of its forms involves soil hydraulic properties, which is a set of five parameters representing soil type.

99dc5454b23d.title: Richards equation
99dc5454b23d.sentence: The soil hydraulic properties typically consist of water retention curve parameters by van Genuchten: (α,n,m,θs,θr), where α is the inverse of air entry value [L−1], n is the pore size distribution parameter [-], and m is usually assumed as m=1−1n.

91818f5174b2.title: Richards equation
91818f5174b2.sentence: Further the saturated hydraulic conductivity 𝐊s (which is for non isotropic environment a tensor of second order) should also be provided.

ed2ac7681af1.title: Richards equation
ed2ac7681af1.sentence: The Richards equation appears in many articles in the environmental literature because it describes the flow in the vadose zone between the atmosphere and the aquifer.

69cae58b4295.title: Richards equation
69cae58b4295.sentence: The numerical solution of the Richards equation is one of the most challenging problems in earth science.

5c2cd4e77a2a.title: Richards equation
5c2cd4e77a2a.sentence: Richards' equation has been criticized for being computationally expensive and unpredictable because there is no guarantee that a solver will converge for a particular set of soil constitutive relations.

426d7e181b83.title: Richards equation
426d7e181b83.sentence: The method has also been criticized for over-emphasizing the role of capillarity, and for being in some ways 'overly simplistic' In one dimensional simulations of rainfall infiltration into dry soils, fine spatial discretization less than one cm is required near the land surface, which is due to the small size of the representative elementary volume for multiphase flow in porous media.

e26240d1914e.title: Soil moisture velocity equation
e26240d1914e.sentence: The soil moisture velocity equation describes the speed that water moves vertically through unsaturated soil under the combined actions of gravity and capillarity, a process known as infiltration.

6115cd0ba68f.title: Soil moisture velocity equation
6115cd0ba68f.sentence: The equation is alternative form of the Richardson/Richards' equation.

8a9a17c5d84b.title: Soil moisture velocity equation
8a9a17c5d84b.sentence: The soil moisture velocity equation or SMVE is a Lagrangian reinterpretation of the Eulerian Richards' equation wherein the dependent variable is the position z of a wetting front of a particular moisture content θ with time.

d409859d2439.title: Soil moisture velocity equation
d409859d2439.sentence: The first term on the right-hand side of the SMVE is called the "advection-like" term, while the second term is called the "diffusion-like" term.

97b6f2858619.title: Soil moisture velocity equation
97b6f2858619.sentence: The first term on the right-hand side of the SMVE represents the two scalar drivers of flow, gravity and the integrated capillarity of the wetting front.

7816751fbccb.title: Soil moisture velocity equation
7816751fbccb.sentence: This term is strikingly similar to Fick's second law of diffusion.

36f8f02bbbba.title: Soil moisture velocity equation
36f8f02bbbba.sentence: This term represents the flux due to the shape of the wetting front −D(θ)∂2ψ/∂z2, divided by the spatial gradient of the capillary head ∂ψ/∂z.

5216ae055322.title: Soil moisture velocity equation
5216ae055322.sentence: Comparing against exact solutions of Richards' equation for infiltration into idealized soils developed by Ross & Parlange (1994) revealed that indeed, neglecting the diffusion-like term resulted in accuracy >99% in calculated cumulative infiltration.

55f73f1b4366.title: Soil moisture velocity equation
55f73f1b4366.sentence: This equation was converted into a set of three ordinary differential equations (ODEs) using the method of lines to convert the partial derivatives on the right-hand side of the equation into appropriate finite difference forms.

3d2bccae383c.title: Soil moisture velocity equation
3d2bccae383c.sentence: These three ODEs represent the dynamics of infiltrating water, falling slugs, and capillary groundwater, respectively.

505db541ffa2.title: Groundwater recharge
505db541ffa2.sentence: Rates of groundwater recharge are difficult to quantify.

981662b40d4c.title: Groundwater recharge
981662b40d4c.sentence: There are no widely applicable method available that can directly and accurately quantify the volume of rainwater that reaches the water table.

8f676ac8c108.title: Groundwater recharge
8f676ac8c108.sentence: This is because other related processes, such as evaporation, transpiration (or evapotranspiration) and infiltration processes must first be measured or estimated to determine the balance.

9fafa391bea3.title: Groundwater recharge
9fafa391bea3.sentence: The most common methods to estimate recharge rates are: chloride mass balance (CMB); soil physics methods; environmental and isotopic tracers; groundwater-level fluctuation methods; water balance (WB) methods (including groundwater models (GMs)); and the estimation of baseflow (BF) to rivers.

214c3e8534be.title: Groundwater recharge
214c3e8534be.sentence: The direct physical methods are those that attempt to actually measure the volume of water passing below the root zone.

e26277aa01c4.title: Groundwater recharge
e26277aa01c4.sentence: Indirect physical methods rely on the measurement or estimation of soil physical parameters, which along with soil physical principles, can be used to estimate the potential or actual recharge.

860ff6d4c2e5.title: Groundwater recharge
860ff6d4c2e5.sentence: Recharge can be estimated using numerical methods, using such codes as Hydrologic Evaluation of Landfill Performance, UNSAT-H, SHAW (short form of Simultaneous Heat and Water Transfer model), WEAP, and MIKE SHE.

5d88cd065dc7.title: Groundwater recharge
5d88cd065dc7.sentence: The codes generally use climate and soil data to arrive at a recharge estimate and use the Richards equation in some form to model groundwater flow in the vadose zone.

1d7de8d31b1c.title: Finite water-content vadose zone flow method
1d7de8d31b1c.sentence: The finite water-content vadose zone flux method represents a one-dimensional alternative to the numerical solution of Richards' equation for simulating the movement of water in unsaturated soils.
1d7de8d31b1c.key: Finite water-content vadose zone flow method

2263501ac4eb.title: Finite water-content vadose zone flow method
2263501ac4eb.sentence: The finite water-content method solves the advection-like term of the Soil Moisture Velocity Equation, which is an ordinary differential equation alternative to the Richards partial differential equation.
2263501ac4eb.key: Finite water-content vadose zone flow method

3229cb6c5f11.title: Finite water-content vadose zone flow method
3229cb6c5f11.sentence: The finite water-content vadose zone flux calculation method replaces the Richards' equation PDE with a set of three ordinary differential equations (ODEs).
3229cb6c5f11.key: Finite water-content vadose zone flow method

9dce39461aba.title: Finite water-content vadose zone flow method
9dce39461aba.sentence: These three ODEs represent the dynamics of infiltrating water, falling slugs, and capillary groundwater, respectively.
9dce39461aba.key: Finite water-content vadose zone flow method

5a47af2e4b65.title: Finite water-content vadose zone flow method
5a47af2e4b65.sentence: First, as an ordinary differential equation it is explicit, guaranteed to converge and computationally inexpensive to solve.
5a47af2e4b65.key: Finite water-content vadose zone flow method

999cf462c68d.title: Finite water-content vadose zone flow method
999cf462c68d.sentence: Second, using a finite volume solution methodology it is guaranteed to conserve mass.
999cf462c68d.key: Finite water-content vadose zone flow method

c70a07f68c7f.title: Finite water-content vadose zone flow method
c70a07f68c7f.sentence: The finite water content method readily simulates sharp wetting fronts, something that the Richards solution struggles with.
c70a07f68c7f.key: Finite water-content vadose zone flow method

ac3a076ba948.title: Finite water-content vadose zone flow method
ac3a076ba948.sentence: The main limiting assumption required to use the finite water-content method is that the soil be homogeneous in layers.
ac3a076ba948.key: Finite water-content vadose zone flow method

ed2a6869ff0f.title: Finite water-content vadose zone flow method
ed2a6869ff0f.sentence: The finite water content method lacks the effect of soil water diffusion.
ed2a6869ff0f.key: Finite water-content vadose zone flow method

786d4d0d6d8c.title: Finite water-content vadose zone flow method
786d4d0d6d8c.sentence: This omission does not affect the accuracy of flux calculations using the method because the mean of the diffusive flux is small.
786d4d0d6d8c.key: Finite water-content vadose zone flow method

562142c15518.title: Finite water-content vadose zone flow method
562142c15518.sentence: The method is thus far limited to 1-D in practical applications.
562142c15518.key: Finite water-content vadose zone flow method

61bd763e6977.title: Finite water-content vadose zone flow method
61bd763e6977.sentence: The finite water content vadose zone flux method works with any monotonic water retention curve/unsaturated hydraulic conductivity relations such as Brooks and Corey Clapp and Hornberger and van Genuchten-Mualem.
61bd763e6977.key: Finite water-content vadose zone flow method

0d7e9e097bb2.title: Phreatic zone
0d7e9e097bb2.sentence: The phreatic zone, saturated zone, or zone of saturation, is the part of an aquifer, below the water table, in which all pores and fractures are saturated with water.

0ef90921f96d.title: Phreatic zone
0ef90921f96d.sentence: The part above the water table is the vadose zone (also called unsaturated zone).

a17c4c58edfc.title: Phreatic
a17c4c58edfc.sentence: The phreatic zone, below the phreatic surface where rock and soil are saturated with water, is the counterpart of the vadose zone, or unsaturated zone, above.

94fada976327.title: Phreatic zone
94fada976327.sentence: The phreatic zone size, color, and depth may fluctuate with changes of season, and during wet and dry periods.

ab9ef2d1122f.title: Phreatic zone
ab9ef2d1122f.sentence: Depending on the characteristics of soil particles, their packing and porosity, the boundary of a saturated zone can be stable or instable, exhibiting fingering patterns known as Saffman–Taylor instability.

c91e7871958d.title: Phreatic
c91e7871958d.sentence: Phreatophytes are deep-rooted plants that obtain a significant portion of the water that it needs from the phreatic zone or near it.

6d8077ca2e2b.title: Interflow
6d8077ca2e2b.sentence: In hydrology, interflow is the lateral movement of water in the unsaturated zone, or vadose zone, that returns to the surface or enters a stream.

7ccb82b805c2.title: Interflow
7ccb82b805c2.sentence: Interflow occurs when water infiltrates (see infiltration (hydrology)) into the subsurface, hydraulic conductivity decreases with depth, and lateral flow proceeds downslope.

1a75db0618a0.title: Interflow
1a75db0618a0.sentence: Interflow is sometimes used interchangeably with throughflow; however, throughflow is specifically the subcomponent of interflow that returns to the surface, as overland flow, prior to entering a stream or becoming groundwater.

83f877a48e58.title: Interflow
83f877a48e58.sentence: As water accumulates in the subsurface, saturation may occur, and interflow may exfiltrate as return flows, becoming overland flow.

35a089b65cc6.title: Gully
35a089b65cc6.sentence: This erosion can result from interflow and soil piping (internal erosion) as well as surface runoff.

247a76b4e6df.title: Soil moisture
247a76b4e6df.sentence: Water flows through the ground unevenly, in the form of so-called gravity fingers, because of the surface tension between water particles.

0e3f2202df4d.sentence: K(θ) is the unsaturated hydraulic conductivity [L T−1],

9f28b61f4b4b.title: Richards equation
9f28b61f4b4b.sentence: 𝐊(h) is the unsaturated hydraulic conductivity [L/T];

e64c1de82664.title: Permanent wilting point
e64c1de82664.sentence: Permanent wilting point (PWP) or wilting point (WP) is defined as the minimum amount of water in the soil that the plant requires not to wilt.

f2922949735e.title: Permanent wilting point
f2922949735e.sentence: If the soil water content decreases to this or any lower point a plant wilts and can no longer recover its turgidity when placed in a saturated atmosphere for 12 hours.

babc3e8019f5.title: Permanent wilting point
babc3e8019f5.sentence: The physical definition of the wilting point, symbolically expressed as θpwp or θwp, is said by convention as the water content at −1,500 kPa (−15 bar) of suction pressure, or negative hydraulic head.

7325031567e7.title: Permanent wilting point
7325031567e7.sentence: Lorenzo A. Richards proposed it is taken as the soil water content when the soil is under a pressure of −15 bar.

3b1c7e5e738c.title: Soil moisture
3b1c7e5e738c.sentence: The wilting point is the minimum amount of water plants need to not wilt and approximates the boundary between available and unavailable water.

3299e3a914a0.title: Soil moisture
3299e3a914a0.sentence: At this point, seeds will not germinate, plants begin to wilt and then die unless they are able to recover after water replenishment thanks to species-specific adaptations.

012c6ce1caad.title: Soil moisture
012c6ce1caad.sentence: At that suction the plant cannot sustain its water needs as water is still being lost from the plant by transpiration, the plant's turgidity is lost, and it wilts, although stomatal closure may decrease transpiration and thus may retard wilting below the wilting point, in particular under adaptation or acclimatization to drought.

da07fb8f9841.title: Permanent wilting point
da07fb8f9841.sentence: Lyman Briggs and Homer LeRoy Shantz (1912) proposed the wilting coefficient, which is defined as the percentage water content of a soil when the plants growing in that soil are first reduced to a wilted condition from which they cannot recover in approximately saturated atmosphere without the addition of water to the soil.

bf0618d98863.title: Permanent wilting point
bf0618d98863.sentence: Frank Veihmeyer and Arthur Hendrickson from University of California-Davis found that it is a constant (characteristic) of the soil and is independent of environmental conditions.

d7f4ccd7a105.title: Lorenzo A. Richards
d7f4ccd7a105.sentence: The currently accepted moisture potential values defining the lower and upper limits for plant growth; at field capacity (−1/3 bar, or −33 J/kg) and permanent wilting point (−15 bar, or −1500 J/kg) were determined through experimental work by Richards and his colleagues.

9320ffcb1e54.title: Available water capacity
9320ffcb1e54.sentence: Available water capacity is the amount of water that can be stored in a soil profile and be available for growing crops.

13ace4bca741.title: Soil
13ace4bca741.sentence: Available water capacity is the amount of water held in a soil profile available to plants.

473f0bf71540.title: Available water capacity
473f0bf71540.sentence: It is also known as available water content (AWC), profile available water (PAW) or total available water (TAW).

56d35f3e6f6e.title: Available water capacity
56d35f3e6f6e.sentence: The concept, put forward by Frank Veihmeyer and Arthur Hendrickson, assumed that the water readily available to plants is the difference between the soil water content at field capacity (θfc) and permanent wilting point (θpwp):

38e9f9e91a99.title: Available water capacity
38e9f9e91a99.sentence: Daniel Hillel criticised that the terms FC and PWP were never clearly defined, and lack physical basis, and that soil water is never equally available within this range.

af649da1d667.title: Available water capacity
af649da1d667.sentence: Lorenzo A. Richards remarked that the concept of availability is oversimplified.

90f57b751676.title: Available water capacity
90f57b751676.sentence: He viewed that: the term availability involves two notions: (a) the ability of plant root to absorb and use the water with which it is in contact and (b) the readiness or velocity with which the soil water moves in to replace that which has been used by the plant.

941736affe7a.title: 1938 USDA soil taxonomy
941736affe7a.sentence: It has two sub-types: Rendzina soils are thin soils with limited available water capacity.

4ecb767c6dc6.title: Available water capacity
4ecb767c6dc6.sentence: Plant available water in sandy soils can be increased by the presence of sepiolite clay.

6977ab911ba3.title: Irrigation scheduling
6977ab911ba3.sentence: Irrigation scheduling is the process used by irrigation system managers to determine the correct frequency and duration of watering.

f7c84e4dbe85.title: Irrigation scheduling
f7c84e4dbe85.sentence: Irrigation scheduling can be grouped into three primary methodologies, ranging from observation to advanced data analytics.

a93a8e154cb8.title: Irrigation scheduling
a93a8e154cb8.sentence: - Visual cues: Monitoring plants for signs of water stress (wilting, leaf curling, or color changes) before watering.

2940cf728aca.title: Irrigation scheduling
2940cf728aca.sentence: - Feel and appearance method: Taking a soil sample by hand to estimate moisture content based on how the soil ribbons or clumps.

1b6321c2f349.title: Irrigation scheduling
1b6321c2f349.section: Methods of scheduling > Soil moisture measurement
1b6321c2f349.sentence: This method uses sensors placed directly in the root zone to measure the volumetric water content or soil water tension.

5ff8227e5a79.title: Irrigation scheduling
5ff8227e5a79.section: Methods of scheduling > Meteorological (water balance) method
5ff8227e5a79.sentence: Also known as the "Checkbook Method," this approach calculates the water balance of the soil.

0415226ce5a5.title: Irrigation scheduling
0415226ce5a5.section: Methods of scheduling > Soil moisture measurement
0415226ce5a5.sentence: - Tensiometers: Measure the force (tension) roots must exert to extract water.

d7be8ec2350c.title: Irrigation scheduling
d7be8ec2350c.section: Methods of scheduling > Soil moisture measurement
d7be8ec2350c.sentence: - Capacitance Sensors: Measure the dielectric permittivity of the soil to determine water volume.

ef310128318e.title: Irrigation scheduling
ef310128318e.sentence: Modern scheduling has evolved from simple calendar-based timers to "smart" systems that adapt dynamically to weather conditions and soil moisture levels.

de21b96dada5.title: Irrigation scheduling
de21b96dada5.sentence: Evapotranspiration (ET) controllers adjust irrigation schedules daily based on local weather conditions.

13caad08ea77.title: Irrigation scheduling
13caad08ea77.sentence: Instead of predicting water loss via weather data, these controllers measure actual soil moisture.

792baffeda7e.title: Irrigation scheduling
792baffeda7e.sentence: - Bypass System: The timer is set to run, but the cycle is interrupted (bypassed) if the soil moisture sensor detects wet soil.

ef02148c0c5f.title: Irrigation scheduling
ef02148c0c5f.sentence: - On-Demand System: The controller initiates irrigation only when the soil moisture sensor reaches a low threshold, regardless of time of day.

5d9de09ef9c8.title: Irrigation scheduling
5d9de09ef9c8.sentence: - Water Conservation: The EPA WaterSense program estimates that up to 50% of landscape water is wasted due to inefficient methods, and that smart controllers can significantly reduce this waste.

08c1dde11446.title: Irrigation scheduling
08c1dde11446.sentence: - Plant Health: Prevents root rot from overwatering and drought stress from underwatering.

4e1c7469d54a.title: Nutrient management
4e1c7469d54a.section: Nitrogen management > Reduction of greenhouse gas emissions > Reduction of N loss in runoff water and eroded soil
4e1c7469d54a.sentence: - The use of daily estimates of soil moisture and crop needs to schedule irrigation reduces the risk of surface runoff and soil erosion.

82ba906818d0.sentence: Conditions where soil is too dry to maintain reliable plant growth is referred to as agricultural drought, and is a particular focus of irrigation management.

2bc550526035.title: Water content
2bc550526035.section: Classification and uses > Earth and agricultural sciences > Agriculture
2bc550526035.sentence: Such conditions are common in arid and semi-arid environments.

6f77c4e9d5e2.title: Water content
6f77c4e9d5e2.section: Classification and uses > Earth and agricultural sciences > Agriculture
6f77c4e9d5e2.sentence: When a soil becomes too dry, plant transpiration drops because the water is increasingly bound to the soil particles by suction.

a31e054f966a.section: Classification and uses > Earth and agricultural sciences > Agriculture
a31e054f966a.sentence: Below the wilting point plants are no longer able to extract water.

34c56eb14894.title: Water content
34c56eb14894.section: Classification and uses > Earth and agricultural sciences > Agriculture
34c56eb14894.sentence: At this point they wilt and cease transpiring altogether.

080f867aac1e.title: Drought
080f867aac1e.sentence: - Agricultural or ecological droughts affect crop production or ecosystems in general.

72c80d026224.title: Drought
72c80d026224.sentence: This condition can also arise independently from any change in precipitation levels when either increased irrigation or soil conditions and erosion triggered by poorly planned agricultural endeavors cause a shortfall in water available to the crops.

f873183ec2f7.title: Irrigation scheduling
f873183ec2f7.sentence: MAD is the percentage of available soil water that can be depleted before plant stress occurs.

2a91c31f33bf.title: Irrigation scheduling
2a91c31f33bf.sentence: - Standard Crops: Often set at 50% depletion.

c6dac1d08e90.title: Irrigation scheduling
c6dac1d08e90.sentence: - Sensitive Crops: (e.g., Vegetables) may require watering at 30% depletion.

b119065f13fd.title: Irrigation scheduling
b119065f13fd.sentence: - Stress Tolerant: (e.g., Established trees) may tolerate 60-70% depletion.

caae1a0aeb59.title: Irrigation scheduling
caae1a0aeb59.section: Methods of scheduling > Soil moisture measurement
caae1a0aeb59.sentence: These sensors can act as a "thermostat" for irrigation, triggering the system only when moisture drops below a specific Management Allowed Depletion (MAD) threshold.

92bffcd64c48.sentence: Hygroscopic water is the water held between the Hygroscopic Coefficient and Oven dry.

cefd062e638d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/05%3A_Soil_Physics_and_Water_Relations/5.07%3A_Soil-Water_Relations
cefd062e638d.sentence: The Hygroscopic Coefficient is the condition when the last micro pore is drained of water and only films of water exist surrounding the soil particles.

c4307772934f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/05%3A_Soil_Physics_and_Water_Relations/5.07%3A_Soil-Water_Relations
c4307772934f.sentence: When a soil is air dry, the water present is held at water potentials ranging from -3000 to –10,000 kPa.

e8b2d62ad90d.sentence: The water in air dry soil is in equilibrium with the soil pore atmosphere which has about 98% relative humidity.
