adcf5baa6093.sentence: Soil dried at 105°C to a constant weight is considered oven dry.

a2bfee4814e8.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/05%3A_Soil_Physics_and_Water_Relations/5.07%3A_Soil-Water_Relations
a2bfee4814e8.sentence: The oven dry weight of soil is used as the reference weight to quantify the amount of water in mineral soils for all moisture conditions.

d9ff8dcc3d97.title: Evapotranspiration
d9ff8dcc3d97.sentence: Evapotranspiration (ET) refers to the combined processes that move water from the Earth's surface (open water and ice surfaces, bare soil and vegetation) into the atmosphere, including both evaporation and transpiration.

259b492d6f7e.title: Evapotranspiration
259b492d6f7e.sentence: - Evaporation: the movement of water directly to the air from sources such as the soil and water bodies.

48b3de843f77.title: Evapotranspiration
48b3de843f77.sentence: - Transpiration: the movement of water from root systems, through a plant, and exit into the air as water vapor.

310190dab0bd.title: Evapotranspiration
310190dab0bd.sentence: This exit occurs through stomata in the plant.

690888c78fdc.title: Soil moisture
690888c78fdc.section: Consumptive use and water use efficiency
690888c78fdc.sentence: Only a small fraction (0.1% to 1%) of the water used by a plant is held within the plant.

2399ace63c8b.title: Soil moisture
2399ace63c8b.section: Consumptive use and water use efficiency
2399ace63c8b.sentence: The majority is ultimately lost via transpiration.

f8a9e3779337.title: Evapotranspiration
f8a9e3779337.sentence: Evapotranspiration is typically measured in millimeters of water (i.e. volume of water moved per unit area of the Earth's surface) in a set unit of time.

cc495efd21ee.title: Evapotranspiration
cc495efd21ee.sentence: Globally, it is estimated that on average between three-fifths and three-quarters of land precipitation is returned to the atmosphere via evapotranspiration.

99c2f952a470.title: Evapotranspiration
99c2f952a470.sentence: Levels of evapotranspiration in a given area are primarily controlled by three factors: Firstly, the amount of water present which includes the amount of available water in both the soil and in larger bodies of water.

2e143fcd95d5.title: Evapotranspiration
2e143fcd95d5.sentence: Secondly, the amount of energy present in the air and soil (e.g. heat, measured by the global surface temperature); and thirdly the ability of the atmosphere to take up water (humidity) which can cause the air temperature to vary from location to location and therefore lead to an increase of decrease in total evapotranspiration.

0c7e5051b35b.title: Evapotranspiration
0c7e5051b35b.section: Influencing factors > Secondary factors > Soil and irrigation
0c7e5051b35b.sentence: Areas with lower moisture levels in the soil result in lower evapotranspiration interaction and will increase the surface temperature of the soil.

564f1b04e73d.title: Evapotranspiration
564f1b04e73d.section: Influencing factors > Secondary factors > Soil and irrigation
564f1b04e73d.sentence: If potential evapotranspiration is greater than the actual precipitation, then soil will dry out until conditions stabilize, unless irrigation is used.

a75979ce794e.title: Evapotranspiration
a75979ce794e.sentence: Evapotranspiration can be measured directly with a weighing or pan lysimeter.

d834c4bb009d.title: Evapotranspiration
d834c4bb009d.section: Measurements > Indirect estimation > Catchment water balance
d834c4bb009d.sentence: Evapotranspiration may be estimated by evaluating the water balance equation for a given area:.

b4c1fc9b4d2b.title: Evapotranspiration
b4c1fc9b4d2b.sentence: A second methodology for estimation is by calculating the energy balance.

3fc477487712.title: Evapotranspiration
3fc477487712.section: Measurements > Indirect estimation > Estimation from meteorological data
3fc477487712.sentence: Given meteorological data like wind, temperature, and humidity, reference ET can be calculated.

767f8ddecf7b.title: Ecohydrology
767f8ddecf7b.section: Basic equations and models > Water balance at a point
767f8ddecf7b.sentence: The water balance has four main components: infiltration of precipitation into the soil, evapotranspiration, leakage of water into deeper portions of the soil not accessible to the plant, and runoff from the ground surface.

38a72a4352e7.title: Soil moisture
38a72a4352e7.section: Consumptive use and water use efficiency
38a72a4352e7.sentence: Water use efficiency is measured by the transpiration ratio, which is the ratio of the total water transpired by a plant to the dry weight of the harvested plant.

1fceaf696f67.title: Soil moisture
1fceaf696f67.section: Consumptive use and water use efficiency
1fceaf696f67.sentence: Transpiration ratios for crops range from 300 to 700.

69d7785f76c2.title: Soil moisture
69d7785f76c2.section: Consumptive use and water use efficiency
69d7785f76c2.sentence: For example, alfalfa may have a transpiration ratio of 500; as a result, 500 kilograms of water will produce one kilogram of dry alfalfa.

30144785104c.title: Water balance
30144785104c.sentence: The law of water balance states that the inflows to any water system or area is equal to its outflows plus change in storage during a time interval.

c597df30e37c.title: Water balance
c597df30e37c.sentence: A system can be one of several hydrological or water domains, such as a column of soil, a drainage basin, an irrigation area or a city.

3008d5cf41fa.title: Water balance
3008d5cf41fa.sentence: The water balance is also referred to as a water budget.

dc26eba3d2b3.title: Water balance
dc26eba3d2b3.sentence: ΔS is the change in storage (in soil or the bedrock / groundwater)

3abd9cf9a5fa.title: Water balance
3abd9cf9a5fa.sentence: This equation uses the principles of conservation of mass in a closed system, whereby any water entering a system (via precipitation), must be transferred into either evaporation, transpiration, surface runoff (eventually reaching the channel and leaving in the form of river discharge), or stored in the ground.

e29101bb5f77.title: Water balance
e29101bb5f77.sentence: This equation requires the system to be closed, and where it is not (for example when surface runoff contributes to a different basin), this must be taken into account.

834d838e5803.title: Water balance
834d838e5803.sentence: Comparison of water budgets from different areas allows the effects of factors such as geology, soils, vegetation, and land use on the hydrologic cycle to be quantified.

2f210b649eaf.title: Water balance
2f210b649eaf.sentence: It is also used in irrigation, runoff assessment (e.g. through the RainOff model ), flood control and pollution control.

57244fd41692.title: Water balance
57244fd41692.sentence: Further it is used in the design of subsurface drainage systems which may be horizontal (i.e. using pipes, tile drains or ditches) or vertical (drainage by wells).

bdccde4672ee.title: Water balance
bdccde4672ee.sentence: Monthly water balance models had been studied since the 1940s.

0d343b5fc8c6.title: Ecohydrology
0d343b5fc8c6.sentence: Ecohydrology (from Greek οἶκος, oikos, "house(hold)"; ὕδωρ, hydōr, "water"; and -λογία, -logia) is an interdisciplinary scientific field studying the interactions between water and ecological systems.

4b09990fe630.title: Ecohydrology
4b09990fe630.sentence: It is considered a sub discipline of hydrology, with an ecological focus.

20320dd99bcc.title: Ecohydrology
20320dd99bcc.sentence: These interactions may take place within water bodies, such as rivers and lakes, or on land, in forests, deserts, and other terrestrial ecosystems.

69bf9c558538.title: Ecohydrology
69bf9c558538.sentence: Areas of research in ecohydrology include transpiration and plant water use, adaption of organisms to their water environment, influence of vegetation and benthic plants on stream flow and function, and feedbacks between ecological processes, the soil carbon sponge and the hydrological cycle.

b5ab4274541b.title: Ecohydrology
b5ab4274541b.section: Basic equations and models > Water balance at a point
b5ab4274541b.sentence: A fundamental equation in ecohydrology is the water balance at a point in the landscape.

ff2653cc2365.title: Ecohydrology
ff2653cc2365.section: Basic equations and models > Water balance at a point
ff2653cc2365.sentence: A water balance states that the amount water entering the soil must be equal to the amount of water leaving the soil plus the change in the amount of water stored in the soil.

92df2f036e8a.title: Ecohydrology
92df2f036e8a.section: Key concepts > Vegetation and water stress
92df2f036e8a.sentence: Where there is ample water, as in rainforests, plant growth is more dependent on nutrient availability.

10c121b82554.title: Ecohydrology
10c121b82554.section: Key concepts > Vegetation and water stress
10c121b82554.sentence: However, in semi-arid areas, like African savannas, vegetation type and distribution relate directly to the amount of water that plants can extract from the soil.

5d77dbbdaa3d.title: Lysimeter
5d77dbbdaa3d.sentence: A field lysimeter or simply lysimeter (from Greek λύσις (loosening) and the suffix -meter) is a container filled with soil, typically of cylindrical shape, which can be used to study the transport of water and material through the soil.

899f7a96c157.title: Lysimeter
899f7a96c157.sentence: This type of lysimeter can be equipped with different measuring probes at different depths (e.g., soil temperature, tensiometer for measuring water tension).

07087623056d.title: Lysimeter
07087623056d.sentence: Most lysimeters contain an opening at the bottom allowing the leachate to be collected and analyzed over time.

42e3d4b89dc8.title: Lysimeter
42e3d4b89dc8.sentence: - Operation: The lysimeter is placed on a scale and changes in weight are recorded over time, allowing for the calculation of evaporation, transpiration, and drainage

c380adb0575b.title: Lysimeter
c380adb0575b.sentence: Lysimeters can be used to measure the amount of actual evapotranspiration which is released by plants (usually crops or trees).

c2cb68d8d150.title: Lysimeter
c2cb68d8d150.sentence: - Operation: A porous cup is buried in the soil and a vacuum is applied to extract water from the surrounding soil; collected water can be analyzed for nutrients, contaminants, or other parameters

f3699c54e557.title: Lysimeter
f3699c54e557.sentence: - Operation: These lysimeters have a collection system to capture water that moved through the soil; collected water is analyzed to study leaching and nutrient transport

4c4d798dd4b0.title: Lysimeter
4c4d798dd4b0.sentence: In 1875 Edward Lewis Sturtevant, a botanist from Massachusetts, built the first lysimeter in the United States.

3a8a2eb8464e.title: Evapotranspiration
3a8a2eb8464e.sentence: Potential evapotranspiration (PET) or potential evaporation (PE) is the amount of water that would be evaporated and transpired by a specific crop, soil or ecosystem if there was sufficient water available.

001efb747f9f.title: Evapotranspiration
001efb747f9f.sentence: It is a reflection of the energy available to evaporate or transpire water, and of the wind available to transport the water vapor from the ground up into the lower atmosphere and away from the initial location.

89015ffbb81c.title: Evapotranspiration
89015ffbb81c.sentence: If the actual evapotranspiration (AET) is considered the net result of atmospheric demand for moisture from a surface and the ability of the surface to supply moisture, then PET is a measure of the demand side (also called evaporative demand).

313e3b5efe53.title: Evapotranspiration
313e3b5efe53.sentence: Potential evapotranspiration is higher in the summer, on clearer and less cloudy days, and closer to the equator, because of the higher levels of solar radiation that provides the energy (heat) for evaporation.

552ba2a4ff74.title: Evapotranspiration
552ba2a4ff74.sentence: Potential evapotranspiration is also higher on windy days because the evaporated moisture can be quickly moved from the ground or plant surface before it precipitates, allowing more evaporation to fill its place.

1b2a91efb6f1.title: Evapotranspiration
1b2a91efb6f1.sentence: Actual evapotranspiration is said to equal potential evapotranspiration when there is ample water present.

88142d19ea96.title: Evapotranspiration
88142d19ea96.sentence: Evapotranspiration can never be greater than potential evapotranspiration, but can be lower if there is not enough water to be evaporated or plants are unable to transpire maturely and readily.

533960125607.title: Evapotranspiration
533960125607.sentence: Often a value for the potential evapotranspiration is calculated at a nearby climatic station on a reference surface, conventionally on land dominated by short grass (though this may differ from station to station).

efefab1de6b2.title: Evapotranspiration
efefab1de6b2.sentence: This value is called the reference evapotranspiration (ET0).

d377fcb1a173.title: Evapotranspiration
d377fcb1a173.section: Measurements > Indirect estimation > Estimation from meteorological data
d377fcb1a173.sentence: The Penman–Monteith variation is recommended by the Food and Agriculture Organization and the American Society of Civil Engineers.

56898f223b71.title: Evapotranspiration
56898f223b71.section: Measurements > Indirect estimation > Estimation from meteorological data
56898f223b71.sentence: To convert the reference evapotranspiration to the actual crop evapotranspiration, a crop coefficient and a stress coefficient must be used.

a3b203b38fe5.title: Agricultural hydrology
a3b203b38fe5.sentence: Agricultural hydrology is the study of water balance components intervening in agricultural water management, especially in irrigation and drainage.

48b16381675d.title: Agricultural hydrology
48b16381675d.sentence: The water balance components can be grouped into components corresponding to zones in a vertical cross-section in the soil forming reservoirs with inflow, outflow and storage of water:

9312d74726dc.title: Agricultural hydrology
9312d74726dc.sentence: - the root zone or unsaturated (vadose zone) (R) with mainly vertical flows

58f0fccab03b.title: Agricultural hydrology
58f0fccab03b.sentence: - a transition zone (T) in which vertical and horizontal flows are converted

b317e8e60105.title: Agricultural hydrology
b317e8e60105.sentence: - the aquifer (Q) with mainly horizontal flows

d61bad196787.title: Agricultural hydrology
d61bad196787.section: Water balance components > Root zone water balance
d61bad196787.sentence: - Inf + Cap = Era + Per + Wr, where Wr is the change of water storage in the root zone

638208434647.title: Agricultural hydrology

2ca93aec5c71.title: Eddy covariance
2ca93aec5c71.sentence: The eddy covariance (also known as eddy correlation and eddy flux) is a key atmospheric measurement technique to measure and calculate vertical turbulent fluxes within atmospheric boundary layers.

c62cecc3cfa4.title: Eddy covariance
c62cecc3cfa4.sentence: The method analyses high-frequency wind and scalar atmospheric data series, gas, energy, and momentum, which yields values of fluxes of these properties.

1f9f72c0a134.title: Eddy covariance
1f9f72c0a134.sentence: In mathematical terms, eddy flux F is computed as a covariance between instantaneous deviation in vertical wind speed (w′) from the mean value (w¯) and instantaneous deviation in gas concentration, mixing ratio (s′), from its mean value (s¯), multiplied by mean air density (ρa).

f961ea52aec0.title: Eddy covariance
f961ea52aec0.sentence: It is a statistical method used in meteorology and other applications (micrometeorology, oceanography, hydrology, agricultural sciences, industrial and regulatory applications, etc.) to determine exchange rates of trace gases over natural ecosystems and agricultural fields, and to quantify gas emissions rates from other land and water areas.

0091dabcf9b5.title: Eddy covariance
0091dabcf9b5.sentence: It is frequently used to estimate momentum, heat, water vapour, carbon dioxide and methane fluxes.

e1cf48d6cac6.title: Eddy covariance
e1cf48d6cac6.sentence: The area from which the detected eddies originate is described probabilistically and called a flux footprint.

da8314b90e28.title: Eddy covariance
da8314b90e28.sentence: The flux footprint area is dynamic in size and shape, changing with wind direction, thermal stability and measurements height, and has a gradual border.

8a2a5a539099.title: Eddy covariance
8a2a5a539099.sentence: - Terrain is horizontal and uniform: average of fluctuations is zero; density fluctuations negligible; flow convergence & divergence negligible

0e4945d12307.title: Eddy covariance
0e4945d12307.sentence: - Flux is fully turbulent – most of the net vertical transfer is done by eddies

d3e12e01b0fb.title: Eddy covariance
d3e12e01b0fb.sentence: - Instruments can detect very small changes at high frequency, ranging from minimum of 5 Hz and to 40 Hz for tower-based measurements

0815dc040311.title: Penman–Monteith equation
0815dc040311.sentence: The Priestley–Taylor equation was developed as a substitute for the Penman-Monteith equation to remove dependence on observations.

9e590ebaf4b6.title: Penman–Monteith equation
9e590ebaf4b6.sentence: For Priestley–Taylor, only radiation (irradiance) observations are required.

5991b1ba7923.title: Penman–Monteith equation
5991b1ba7923.sentence: This is done by removing the aerodynamic terms from the Penman-Monteith equation and adding an empirically derived constant factor, α.

82d1f3dc54ef.title: Penman–Monteith equation
82d1f3dc54ef.sentence: Therefore, the equation for actual evaporation was found by taking reference evapotranspiration and multiplying it by α.

f60d95f0ca50.title: Penman–Monteith equation
f60d95f0ca50.sentence: However, observations revealed that actual evaporation was 1.26 times greater than reference evaporation.

9c616156fdc8.title: Penman–Monteith equation
9c616156fdc8.sentence: The assumption here is for vegetation with an abundant water supply (i.e. the plants have low moisture stress).

296b19272d72.title: Penman–Monteith equation
296b19272d72.sentence: Areas like arid regions with high moisture stress are estimated to have higher α values.

ffbe291ec684.title: Penman–Monteith equation
ffbe291ec684.section: Variations and alternatives > FAO 56 Penman-Monteith equation
ffbe291ec684.sentence: It is defined as the evapotranpiration for "[an] hypothetical reference crop with an assumed crop height of 0.12 m, a fixed surface resistance of 70 s m-1 and an albedo of 0.23." This reference surface is defined to represent "an extensive surface of green grass of uniform height, actively growing, completely shading the ground and with adequate water".

b76f30163662.title: Penman–Monteith equation
b76f30163662.sentence: The equation is widely used, and was derived by the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization for modeling reference evapotranspiration ET0.

ea3010950b69.title: Penman–Monteith equation
ea3010950b69.section: Variations and alternatives > FAO 56 Penman-Monteith equation
ea3010950b69.sentence: This reference evapotranspiration ET0 can then be used to evaluate the evapotranspiration rate ET from unstressed plants through crop coefficients Kc: ET = Kc * ET0.

c04eeab81afe.title: Crop coefficient
c04eeab81afe.sentence: Crop coefficients are properties of plants used in predicting evapotranspiration (ET).

ffc19fad4224.title: Crop coefficient
ffc19fad4224.sentence: The most basic crop coefficient, Kc, is simply the ratio of ET observed for the crop studied over that observed for the well calibrated reference crop under the same conditions.

21ec9991aca2.title: Crop coefficient
21ec9991aca2.sentence: Kc then becomes a function or series of values specific to the crop of interest through its growing season.

4c88c59799a8.title: Crop coefficient
4c88c59799a8.sentence: These can be quite elaborate in the case of certain maize varieties, but tend to use a trapezoidal or leaf area index (LAI) curve for common crop or vegetation canopies.

814cb80265d2.title: Evapotranspiration
814cb80265d2.section: Measurements > Indirect estimation > Estimation from meteorological data
814cb80265d2.sentence: Crop coefficients, as used in many hydrological models, usually change over the year because crops are seasonal and, in general, plant behaviour varies over the year: perennial plants mature over multiple seasons, while annuals do not survive more than a few, so stress responses can significantly depend upon many aspects of plant type and condition.

d21e6f5d00d0.title: Crop coefficient
d21e6f5d00d0.sentence: Stress coefficients, Ks, account for diminished ET due to specific stress factors.

2038a95f1c5a.title: Crop coefficient
2038a95f1c5a.sentence: These are often assumed to combine by multiplication.

eb80d40313e5.title: Crop coefficient
eb80d40313e5.sentence: Water stress is the most ubiquitous stress factor, often denoted as Kw.

149e6edcad2a.title: Crop coefficient
149e6edcad2a.sentence: Stress coefficients tend to be functions ranging between 0 and 1.

52475f3bbfa1.title: Crop coefficient
52475f3bbfa1.sentence: Crop coefficients can exceed 1 when the crop evapotranspiration exceeds that of RET.

892972f6b5a8.title: Soil moisture
892972f6b5a8.sentence: Most soil water is taken up by plants as passive absorption caused by the pulling force of water evaporating (transpiring) from the long column of water (xylem sap flow) that leads from the plant's roots to its leaves, according to the cohesion-tension theory.

2aa10f6e17d2.title: Soil moisture
2aa10f6e17d2.sentence: In addition, the high concentration of salts within plant roots creates an osmotic pressure gradient that pushes soil water into the roots.

58ee178ca1ad.title: Soil moisture
58ee178ca1ad.sentence: Osmotic absorption becomes more important during times of low water transpiration caused by lower temperatures (for example at night) or high humidity, and the reverse occurs under high temperature or low humidity.

25c24f672d89.title: Soil moisture
25c24f672d89.sentence: The upward movement of water and solutes (hydraulic lift) is regulated in the roots by the endodermis and in the plant foliage by stomatal conductance, and can be interrupted in root and shoot xylem vessels by cavitation, also called xylem embolism.

7f81ae93b867.title: Soil moisture
7f81ae93b867.sentence: A study of a single winter rye plant grown for four months in one cubic foot (0.0283 cubic meters) of loam soil showed that the plant developed 13,800,000 roots, a total of 620 km in length with 237 square meters in surface area; and 14 billion root hairs of 10,620 km total length and 400 square meters total area; for a total surface area of 638 square meters.

72eaec34466a.title: Soil moisture
72eaec34466a.sentence: In other words, the roots were in contact with only 1.2% of the soil volume.

edb45daec1a5.title: Soil moisture
edb45daec1a5.sentence: However, root extension should be viewed as a dynamic process, allowing new roots to explore a new volume of soil each day, increasing dramatically the total volume of soil explored over a given growth period, and thus the volume of water taken up by the root system over this period.

a7067d2a3bf6.title: Soil moisture
a7067d2a3bf6.sentence: Root architecture, i.e. the spatial configuration of the root system, plays a prominent role in the adaptation of plants to soil water and nutrient availability, and thus in plant productivity.

9d721f148ab1.title: Soil moisture
9d721f148ab1.sentence: When grain sorghum was exposed to soil suction as low as 1300 kPa during the seed head emergence through bloom and seed set stages of growth, its production was reduced by 34%.

89a518705fec.title: Soil moisture
89a518705fec.sentence: Plant roots must seek out water and grow preferentially in moister soil microsites, but some parts of the root system are also able to remoisten dry parts of the soil.

83b7eba17ab1.title: Transpiration
83b7eba17ab1.sentence: Transpiration is the process of water movement through a plant and its evaporation from aerial parts, such as leaves, stems and flowers.

3e109847a856.title: Transpiration
3e109847a856.sentence: It is a passive process that requires no energy expense by the plant.

f91d359f0db2.title: Transpiration
f91d359f0db2.sentence: Transpiration also cools plants, changes osmotic pressure of cells, and enables mass flow of mineral nutrients.

b4940de371b5.title: Transpiration
b4940de371b5.sentence: Water is necessary for plants, but only a small amount of water taken up by the roots is used for growth and metabolism.

a64c26c6a59a.title: Transpiration
a64c26c6a59a.sentence: The remaining 97–99.5% is lost by transpiration and guttation.

56c8b4e26f4b.title: Transpiration
56c8b4e26f4b.sentence: Two major factors influence the rate of water flow from the soil to the roots: the hydraulic conductivity of the soil and the magnitude of the pressure gradient through the soil.

155ac975ca4b.title: Transpiration
155ac975ca4b.sentence: Mass flow of liquid water from the roots to the leaves is driven in part by capillary action, but primarily driven by water potential differences.

842037f5b0fa.title: Transpiration
842037f5b0fa.sentence: When water uptake by the roots is less than the water lost to the atmosphere by evaporation, plants close small pores called stomata to decrease water loss, which slows down nutrient uptake and decreases CO2 absorption from the atmosphere limiting metabolic processes, photosynthesis, and growth.

b8131913202b.title: Transpiration
b8131913202b.sentence: Along with above-ground factors, soil temperature and moisture can influence stomatal opening, and thus transpiration rate.

12fb92ec5817.title: Transpiration
12fb92ec5817.sentence: Factors that effect root absorption of water include: moisture content of the soil, excessive soil fertility or salt content, poorly developed root systems, and those impacted by pathogenic bacteria and fungi such as pythium or rhizoctonia.

7a33e86bae00.title: Transpiration
7a33e86bae00.sentence: An acre of corn gives off about 3,000–4,000 U.S. gallons (11,000–15,000 liters) of water each day, and a large oak tree can transpire 40,000 U.S. gallons (150,000 liters) per year.

b5d4d8e10799.title: Transpiration
b5d4d8e10799.sentence: Isotope measurements indicate transpiration is the larger component of evapotranspiration.

168e383ff954.title: Transpiration
168e383ff954.sentence: Recent evidence from a global study of water stable isotopes shows that transpired water is isotopically different from groundwater and streams.

d1cadefefb48.title: Transpiration
d1cadefefb48.sentence: This suggests that soil water is not as well mixed as widely assumed.

d4a3c083f423.title: Transpiration
d4a3c083f423.sentence: Transpiration rates of plants can be measured by a number of techniques, including potometers, lysimeters, porometers, photosynthesis systems and thermometric sap flow sensors.

fd078ad7175f.title: Soil-plant-atmosphere continuum
fd078ad7175f.sentence: The soil-plant-atmosphere continuum (SPAC) is the pathway for water moving from soil through plants to the atmosphere.

5b7a26423f37.title: Soil-plant-atmosphere continuum
5b7a26423f37.sentence: Continuum in the description highlights the continuous nature of water connection through the pathway.

cb61c48f64c6.title: Soil-plant-atmosphere continuum
cb61c48f64c6.sentence: The low water potential of the atmosphere, and relatively higher (i.e. less negative) water potential inside leaves, leads to a diffusion gradient across the stomatal pores of leaves, drawing water out of the leaves as vapour.

969bcc64a89a.title: Soil-plant-atmosphere continuum
969bcc64a89a.sentence: As water vapour transpires out of the leaf, further water molecules evaporate off the surface of mesophyll cells to replace the lost molecules since water in the air inside leaves is maintained at saturation vapour pressure.

6140787674a4.title: Soil-plant-atmosphere continuum
6140787674a4.sentence: Water lost at the surface of cells is replaced by water from the xylem, which due to the cohesion-tension properties of water in the xylem of plants pulls additional water molecules through the xylem from the roots toward the leaf.

b0362b826715.title: Soil-plant-atmosphere continuum
b0362b826715.sentence: The transport of water along this pathway occurs in components, variously defined among scientific disciplines:

ac65809ed2c1.title: Soil-plant-atmosphere continuum
ac65809ed2c1.sentence: - Soil physics characterizes water in soil in terms of tension,

6363d1973705.title: Soil-plant-atmosphere continuum
6363d1973705.sentence: - Physiology of plants and animals characterizes water in organisms in terms of diffusion pressure deficit, and

432368066d1b.title: Soil-plant-atmosphere continuum
432368066d1b.sentence: - Meteorology uses vapour pressure or relative humidity to characterize atmospheric water.

6b74eadad79f.title: Soil-plant-atmosphere continuum
6b74eadad79f.sentence: >...concept recognising that the field with all its components (soil, plant, animals and the ambient atmosphere taken together) constitutes a physically integrated, dynamic system in which the various flow processes involving energy and matter occur simultaneously and interdependently like links in the chain.

7167eb546b7c.title: Soil-plant-atmosphere continuum
7167eb546b7c.sentence: This characterises the state of water in different components of the SPAC as expressions of the energy level or water potential of each.

5b8e0c2e5ac3.title: Soil-plant-atmosphere continuum
5b8e0c2e5ac3.sentence: Modelling of water transport between components relies on SPAC, as do studies of water potential gradients between segments.

1364fa9ab9fb.title: Wilting
1364fa9ab9fb.sentence: Wilting is the loss of rigidity of non-woody parts of plants.

d7f66aa96195.title: Wilting
d7f66aa96195.sentence: This occurs when the turgor pressure in non-lignified plant cells falls towards zero, as a result of diminished water in the cells.

ae8517029598.title: Wilting
ae8517029598.sentence: The rate of loss of water from the plant is greater than the absorption of water in the plant.

e07e110ca940.title: Wilting
e07e110ca940.sentence: - drought conditions, where the soil moisture drops below conditions most favorable for plant functioning;

41c6764a32b1.title: Wilting
41c6764a32b1.sentence: - high salinity, which causes water to diffuse from the plant cells and induce shrinkage;

34560acfe952.title: Wilting
34560acfe952.sentence: - saturated soil conditions, where roots are unable to obtain sufficient oxygen for cellular respiration, and so are unable to transport water into the plant; or

730f981cf524.title: Wilting
730f981cf524.sentence: The plants may recover during the night when evaporation is reduced as the stomata closes.

e1fce15683cf.title: Wilting
e1fce15683cf.sentence: Permanent wilting leads to the plant dying.

50b96e4ed5e4.title: Wilting
50b96e4ed5e4.sentence: Wilting also serves to reduce water loss, as it makes the leaves expose less surface area.

9be91fb9d7a8.title: Wilting
9be91fb9d7a8.sentence: Wilting diminishes the plant's ability to transpire, reproduce and grow.

695cd42e5417.title: Advection
695cd42e5417.sentence: In the fields of physics, engineering, and earth sciences, advection is the transport of a substance or quantity by bulk motion of a fluid.

ee9dd68076ca.title: Advection
ee9dd68076ca.sentence: Advection requires currents in the fluid, and so cannot happen in rigid solids.

22da174c4102.title: Advection
22da174c4102.sentence: It does not include transport of substances by molecular diffusion.

4ead49ceb5cb.title: Advection
4ead49ceb5cb.sentence: One easily visualized example of advection is the transport of ink dumped into a river.

aafd9cd20142.title: Advection
aafd9cd20142.sentence: Note that as it moves downstream, the "pulse" of ink will also spread via diffusion.

c965a507fb4c.title: Advection
c965a507fb4c.sentence: The sum of these processes is called convection.

7f38334a2a55.title: Hydrogeology
7f38334a2a55.sentence: The contaminants which are man-made (e.g., petroleum products, nitrate, chromium or radionuclides) or naturally occurring (e.g., arsenic, salinity), can be transported through three main mechanisms, advection (transport along the main direction of flow at seepage velocity), diffusion (migration of the contaminant from high to low concentration areas), and hydrodynamic dispersion (due to microscale heterogeneities present in the porous medium and non-uniform velocity distribution relative to seepage velocity).

9478b346ae36.title: Advection
9478b346ae36.sentence: The advection equation is a first-order hyperbolic partial differential equation that governs the motion of a conserved scalar field as it is advected by a known velocity vector field.

f6651c50299d.title: Advection
f6651c50299d.sentence: It is derived using the scalar field's conservation law, together with Gauss's theorem, and taking the infinitesimal limit.

35aa31fe050b.title: Hydrogeology
35aa31fe050b.sentence: Often we are interested in how the moving groundwater will transport dissolved contaminants around (the sub-field of contaminant hydrogeology).

d3fa780db776.title: Hydrogeology
d3fa780db776.sentence: Besides needing to understand where the groundwater is flowing, based on the other hydrologic properties discussed above, there are additional aquifer properties which affect how dissolved contaminants move with groundwater.

49184de33e02.title: Hydrogeology
49184de33e02.section: Subjects > Contaminant transport properties > Retardation by adsorption
49184de33e02.sentence: Unlike diffusion and dispersion, which simply spread the contaminant, the retardation factor changes its global average velocity, so that it can be much slower than that of water.

334c0a7779fc.title: Groundwater
334c0a7779fc.sentence: Its advancing boundary, often called a plume edge, can intersect with groundwater wells and surface water, such as seeps and springs, making the water supplies unsafe for humans and wildlife.

adebc27af23d.title: Groundwater
adebc27af23d.sentence: The movement of the plume, called a plume front, may be analyzed through a hydrological transport model or groundwater model.

4a4e58810967.title: Groundwater
4a4e58810967.sentence: Different mechanisms have influence on the transport of pollutants, e.g. diffusion, adsorption, precipitation, decay, in the groundwater.

c551feefb750.title: Hydrogeology
c551feefb750.section: Subjects > Contaminant transport properties > Hydrodynamic dispersion
c551feefb750.sentence: Hydrodynamic dispersivity (αL, αT) is an empirical factor which quantifies how much contaminants stray away from the path of the groundwater which is carrying it.

e9bca62bc39b.title: Hydrogeology
e9bca62bc39b.section: Subjects > Contaminant transport properties > Hydrodynamic dispersion
e9bca62bc39b.sentence: Some of the contaminants will be "behind" or "ahead" the mean groundwater, giving rise to a longitudinal dispersivity (αL), and some will be "to the sides of" the pure advective groundwater flow, leading to a transverse dispersivity (αT).

5079000e94cc.title: Hydrogeology
5079000e94cc.section: Subjects > Contaminant transport properties > Hydrodynamic dispersion
5079000e94cc.sentence: Dispersion in groundwater arises because each water "particle", passing beyond a soil particle, must choose where to go, whether left or right or up or down, so that the water "particles" (and their solute) are gradually spread in all directions around the mean path.

d918a4f7a672.title: Hydrogeology
d918a4f7a672.section: Subjects > Contaminant transport properties > Hydrodynamic dispersion
d918a4f7a672.sentence: This is the "microscopic" mechanism, on the scale of soil particles.

943613f1a7c9.title: Hydrogeology
943613f1a7c9.section: Subjects > Contaminant transport properties > Hydrodynamic dispersion
943613f1a7c9.sentence: More important, over long distances, can be the macroscopic inhomogeneities of the aquifer, which can have regions of larger or smaller permeability, so that some water can find a preferential path in one direction, some other in a different direction, so that the contaminant can be spread in a completely irregular way, like in a (three-dimensional) delta of a river.

0e027d6be8e1.title: Hydrogeology
0e027d6be8e1.section: Subjects > Contaminant transport properties > Hydrodynamic dispersion
0e027d6be8e1.sentence: Dispersivity is actually a factor which represents our lack of information about the system we are simulating.

276fe9c45529.title: Hydrogeology
276fe9c45529.section: Subjects > Contaminant transport properties > Hydrodynamic dispersion
276fe9c45529.sentence: There are many small details about the aquifer which are effectively averaged when using a macroscopic approach (e.g., tiny beds of gravel and clay in sand aquifers); these manifest themselves as an apparent dispersivity.

77ba69a0f4f8.title: Hydrogeology
77ba69a0f4f8.section: Subjects > Contaminant transport properties > Hydrodynamic dispersion
77ba69a0f4f8.sentence: Because of this, α is often claimed to be dependent on the length scale of the problem — the dispersivity found for transport through 1 m3 of aquifer is different from that for transport through 1 cm3 of the same aquifer material.

6e662ae9f831.title: Soil salinity control
6e662ae9f831.sentence: The models require the input of soil characteristics like the relations between variable unsaturated soil moisture content, water tension, water retention curve, unsaturated hydraulic conductivity, dispersity, and diffusivity.

2c40a875ffcf.title: Hydrogeology
2c40a875ffcf.section: Subjects > Contaminant transport properties > Retardation by adsorption
2c40a875ffcf.sentence: The retardation factor is another very important feature that make the motion of the contaminant to deviate from the average groundwater motion.

557cb2b435cd.title: Hydrogeology
557cb2b435cd.section: Subjects > Contaminant transport properties > Retardation by adsorption
557cb2b435cd.sentence: This is due to a chemico-physical effect: the adsorption to the soil, which holds the contaminant back and does not allow it to progress until the quantity corresponding to the chemical adsorption equilibrium has been adsorbed.

bd99e274a63e.title: Hydrogeology
bd99e274a63e.section: Subjects > Contaminant transport properties > Retardation by adsorption
bd99e274a63e.sentence: It is analogous to the retardation factor of chromatography.

9783b493383d.title: Hydrogeology
9783b493383d.section: Subjects > Contaminant transport properties > Retardation by adsorption
9783b493383d.sentence: This effect is particularly important for less soluble contaminants, which thus can move even hundreds or thousands times slower than water.

908d02ca7edb.title: Hydrogeology
908d02ca7edb.section: Subjects > Contaminant transport properties > Retardation by adsorption
908d02ca7edb.sentence: The effect of this phenomenon is that only more soluble species can cover long distances.

d76bde286996.title: Hydrogeology
d76bde286996.section: Subjects > Contaminant transport properties > Retardation by adsorption
d76bde286996.sentence: The retardation factor depends on the chemical nature of both the contaminant and the aquifer.

df9794a03a0a.title: Retardation factor
df9794a03a0a.sentence: In chromatography, the retardation factor, R, is the fraction of the sample in the mobile phase at equilibrium, defined as:

9fc373c3a5fb.title: Retardation factor
9fc373c3a5fb.sentence: R=quantity of substance in the mobile phasetotal quantity of substance in the system

a788b7b7e328.title: Retardation factor
a788b7b7e328.sentence: RF=migration distance of substancemigration distance of solvent front

6aaea2ced5ca.title: Retardation factor
6aaea2ced5ca.sentence: An RF value will always be in the range 0 to 1; if the substance moves, it can only move in the direction of the solvent flow, and cannot move faster than the solvent.

9e9ae21910fb.title: Retardation factor
9e9ae21910fb.sentence: For example, if particular substance in an unknown mixture travels 2.5 cm and the solvent front travels 5.0 cm, the retardation factor would be 0.50.

b74649c4b232.title: Hydrogeology
b74649c4b232.section: Subjects > Contaminant transport properties > Molecular diffusion
b74649c4b232.sentence: Diffusion is a fundamental physical phenomenon, which Albert Einstein characterized as Brownian motion, that describes the random thermal movement of molecules and small particles in gases and liquids.

16d386270e0a.title: Hydrogeology
16d386270e0a.section: Subjects > Contaminant transport properties > Molecular diffusion
16d386270e0a.sentence: It is an important phenomenon for small distances (it is essential for the achievement of thermodynamic equilibria), but, as the time necessary to cover a distance by diffusion is proportional to the square of the distance itself, it is less effective for spreading a solute over macroscopic distances on a short time scale.

fb664e9c1297.title: Hydrogeology
fb664e9c1297.section: Subjects > Contaminant transport properties > Molecular diffusion
fb664e9c1297.sentence: The diffusion coefficient, D, is typically quite small, and its effect can often be neglected (unless groundwater flow velocities are extremely low, as they are in clay aquitards).

e5aa7d4611be.title: Hydrogeology
e5aa7d4611be.section: Subjects > Contaminant transport properties > Molecular diffusion
e5aa7d4611be.sentence: It is important not to confuse diffusion with dispersion, as the former is a physical phenomenon and the latter is an empirical hydrodynamic factor which is cast into a similar form as diffusion, because its a convenient way to mathematically describe and solve the question.

0c7492b8ab4a.title: Convection–diffusion equation
0c7492b8ab4a.sentence: The convection–diffusion equation is a parabolic partial differential equation that combines the diffusion and convection (advection) equations.

2feda6db89d9.title: Convection–diffusion equation
2feda6db89d9.sentence: It describes physical phenomena where particles, energy, or other physical quantities are transferred inside a physical system due to two processes: diffusion and convection.

92a561f9875e.title: Convection–diffusion equation
92a561f9875e.sentence: Depending on context, the same equation can be called the advection–diffusion equation, drift–diffusion equation, or (generic) scalar transport equation.

3d1b2f05a330.title: Convection–diffusion equation
3d1b2f05a330.sentence: The convection–diffusion equation can be derived in a straightforward way from the continuity equation, which states that the rate of change for a scalar quantity in a differential control volume is given by flow and diffusion into and out of that part of the system along with any generation or consumption inside the control volume: ∂c∂t+∇⋅𝐣=R, where j is the total flux and R is a net volumetric source for c. There are two sources of flux in this situation.

b9cf40d3f5a8.title: Convection–diffusion equation
b9cf40d3f5a8.sentence: This is typically approximated by Fick's first law: 𝐣diff=−D∇c i.e., the flux of the diffusing material (relative to the bulk motion) in any part of the system is proportional to the local concentration gradient.

586eec640efd.title: Convection–diffusion equation
586eec640efd.sentence: Second, when there is overall convection or flow, there is an associated flux called advective flux: 𝐣adv=𝐯c The total flux (in a stationary coordinate system) is given by the sum of these two: 𝐣=𝐣diff+𝐣adv=−D∇c+𝐯c.

3d8a728eb2d8.title: Convection–diffusion equation
3d8a728eb2d8.sentence: - R describes sources or sinks of the quantity c, i.e. the creation or destruction of the quantity.

be7c34353825.title: Convection–diffusion equation
be7c34353825.sentence: For example, for a chemical species, R > 0 means that a chemical reaction is creating more of the species, and R < 0 means that a chemical reaction is destroying the species.

d54f228ecd86.title: Convection–diffusion equation
d54f228ecd86.sentence: For multiphase flows and flows in porous media, v is the (hypothetical) superficial velocity.

3b4081f20dd6.title: Soil salinity control
3b4081f20dd6.sentence: The majority of the computer models available for water and solute transport in the soil (e.g. SWAP, DrainMod-S, UnSatChem, and Hydrus) are based on Richard's differential equation for the movement of water in unsaturated soil in combination with Fick's differential convection–diffusion equation for advection and dispersion of salts.

078afe6b8676.title: Dye tracing
078afe6b8676.sentence: Dye tracing is a method of tracking and tracing various flows using dye as a flow tracer when added to a liquid.

a44597ce679b.title: Dye tracing
a44597ce679b.sentence: Dye tracking may be either qualitative, showing the presence of a particular flow, or quantitative, when the amount of the traced dye is measured by special instruments.

644abbeeeed8.title: Dye tracing
644abbeeeed8.sentence: Fluorescent dyes are often used in situations where there is insufficient lighting (e.g., sewers or cave waters), and where precise quantitative data are required (measured by a fluorometer).

1c4ac8189fbb.title: Dye tracing
1c4ac8189fbb.sentence: In 1871, fluorescein was among the first fluorescent dyes to be developed.

7b46c77d4685.title: Dye tracing
7b46c77d4685.sentence: Its disodium salt (under the trademark "uranine") was developed several years later and still remains among the best tracer dyes.

d3167eb4e64b.title: Dye tracing
d3167eb4e64b.sentence: Other popular tracer dyes are rhodamine, pyranine and sulforhodamine B.

f9c42b232c12.title: Dye tracing
f9c42b232c12.sentence: The presence of organic material, other chemicals, and sunlight can affect the intensity of dyes.

25ad567699d4.title: Dye tracing
25ad567699d4.sentence: - Limitations of use in acidic waters

2435fc75908e.title: Aquifer
2435fc75908e.section: Classification > Porous, karst, or fractured > Karst
2435fc75908e.sentence: For example, in the Barton Springs Edwards aquifer, dye traces measured the karst groundwater flow rates from 0.5 to 7 miles per day (0.8 to 11.3 km/d).

20b08fed26c0.title: Aquifer
20b08fed26c0.section: Classification > Porous, karst, or fractured > Karst
20b08fed26c0.sentence: U.S. Geological Survey dye tracing has determined that conventional groundwater models that assume a uniform distribution of porosity are not applicable for karst aquifers.

b6880d674b0b.title: Péclet number
b6880d674b0b.sentence: It is defined to be the ratio of the rate of advection of a physical quantity by the flow to the rate of diffusion of the same quantity driven by an appropriate gradient.

eab5ec6e25d0.title: Péclet number
eab5ec6e25d0.sentence: The Péclet number is defined as Pe=advective transport ratediffusive transport rate.

68703e94db04.title: Péclet number
68703e94db04.sentence: For mass transfer, it is defined as PeL=LuD=ReLSc,

53f149b86dc8.title: Péclet number
53f149b86dc8.sentence: where L is the characteristic length, u the local flow velocity, D the mass diffusion coefficient, Re the Reynolds number, Sc the Schmidt number.

a64b522c9bf0.title: Péclet number
a64b522c9bf0.sentence: In the context of species or mass transfer, the Péclet number is the product of the Reynolds number and the Schmidt number (Re × Sc).

aed08f6fb4ad.title: Péclet number
aed08f6fb4ad.sentence: Such ratio can also be re-written in terms of times, as a ratio between the characteristic temporal intervals of the system: PeL=u/LD/L2=L2/DL/u=diffusion timeadvection time.

3c1a13045d52.title: Péclet number
3c1a13045d52.sentence: For PeL≫1 the diffusion happens in a much longer time compared to the advection, and therefore the latter of the two phenomena predominates in the mass transport.

d7d9750fb22d.title: Colloid-facilitated transport
d7d9750fb22d.sentence: Colloid-facilitated transport designates a transport process by which colloidal particles serve as transport vector of diverse contaminants in the surface water (sea water, lakes, rivers, fresh water bodies) and in underground water circulating in fissured rocks (limestone, sandstone, granite,...).

9a6ebc099d0c.title: Colloid-facilitated transport
9a6ebc099d0c.sentence: The transport of colloidal particles in surface soils and in the ground can also occur, depending on the soil structure, soil compaction, and the particles size, but the importance of colloidal transport was only given sufficient attention during the 1980 years.

6798fff03198.title: Colloid-facilitated transport
6798fff03198.sentence: Radionuclides, heavy metals, and organic pollutants, easily sorb onto colloids suspended in water and that can easily act as contaminant carrier.

b644e9b20387.title: Colloid-facilitated transport
b644e9b20387.sentence: Various types of colloids are recognised: inorganic colloids (clay particles, silicates, iron oxy-hydroxides,...), organic colloids (humic and fulvic substances).

e740c44e1528.title: Colloid-facilitated transport
e740c44e1528.sentence: Colloids have been suspected for the long range transport of plutonium on the Nevada Nuclear Test Site.

c460557c7169.title: Colloid-facilitated transport
c460557c7169.sentence: However, the mobility of inorganic colloids is very low in compacted bentonites and in deep clay formations because of the process of ultrafiltration occurring in dense clay membrane.

0d9aff0d4319.title: Breakthrough curve
0d9aff0d4319.sentence: A breakthrough curve in adsorption is the course of the effluent adsorptive concentration at the outlet of a fixed bed adsorber.

d8707d37eb49.title: Breakthrough curve
d8707d37eb49.sentence: After becoming stationary one or more adsorptives are added to the carrier gas, resulting in a step-wise change of the inlet concentration.

02435091b98d.title: Breakthrough curve
02435091b98d.sentence: A fixed bed of porous materials (e.g. activated carbons and zeolites) is pressurized and purged with a carrier gas.

c1d2cb445897.title: Breakthrough curve
c1d2cb445897.sentence: This is in contrast to chromatographic separation processes, where pulse-wise changes of the inlet concentrations are used.

8b56b51124f0.title: Breakthrough curve
8b56b51124f0.sentence: The course of the adsorptive concentrations at the outlet of the fixed bed are monitored.

3f4eaccd16e6.title: Breakthrough curve
3f4eaccd16e6.sentence: Integration of the area above the entire breakthrough curve gives the maximum loading of the adsorptive material.

86977b37b1bc.title: Breakthrough curve
86977b37b1bc.sentence: Additionally, the duration of the breakthrough experiment until a certain threshold of the adsorptive concentration at the outlet can be measured, which enables the calculation of a technically usable sorption capacity.

86e6c3353c25.title: Breakthrough curve
86e6c3353c25.sentence: The shape of the breakthrough curves contains information about the mass transfer properties of the adsorptive-adsorbent system.

1e2c6b6db4cb.title: Breakthrough curve
1e2c6b6db4cb.sentence: These properties can be evaluated by applying simplified models and fitting to experimental data by simulations.

560eca8557fa.title: Breakthrough curve
560eca8557fa.sentence: Breakthrough curves are important for adsorptive separation technologies and for the characterization of porous materials.

03bf26b8dde0.title: Soil gas
03bf26b8dde0.sentence: Soil gases (soil atmosphere) are the gases found in the air space between soil components.

e530a70052ac.title: Soil gas
e530a70052ac.sentence: The spaces between the solid soil particles, if they do not contain water, are filled with air.

3f2a59d56d55.title: Soil gas
3f2a59d56d55.sentence: The primary soil gases are nitrogen, carbon dioxide and oxygen.

763bf1b75a79.title: Soil gas
763bf1b75a79.sentence: Other natural soil gases include nitric oxide, nitrous oxide, methane, and ammonia.

268c48879103.title: Soil gas
268c48879103.sentence: Oxygen is critical because it allows for respiration of both plant roots and soil organisms.

a100289a0daa.title: Soil gas
a100289a0daa.sentence: Gases fill soil pores in the soil structure as water drains or is removed from a soil pore by evaporation or root absorption.

630de3549606.title: Soil gas
630de3549606.sentence: Not only are both soil air and soil water very dynamic parts of soil, but both are often inversely related.

57bd0fe38b4b.title: Soil
57bd0fe38b4b.sentence: The consumption of oxygen by microbes and plant roots, and their release of carbon dioxide, decreases oxygen and increases carbon dioxide concentration.

7e7c43a304c1.title: Soil gas
7e7c43a304c1.sentence: The soil atmosphere is also made of a variety of volatile compounds emitted by soil organisms, as respiratory metabolites, allelopathic compounds or semiochemical signals used in within-species and between-species communication.

87f6658671ae.title: Soil
87f6658671ae.sentence: These volatiles are used as chemical cues, making soil atmosphere the seat of interaction networks playing a decisive role in the stability, dynamics and evolution of soil ecosystems.

8adbab400797.title: Soil
8adbab400797.sentence: Aerated soil is also a net sink of methane (CH4) but a net producer of methane (a strong heat-trapping greenhouse gas) when soils are depleted of oxygen and subject to elevated temperatures.

b44452570750.title: Soil gas
b44452570750.sentence: Soil is a net emitter of greenhouse gases, in particular when and where permafrost is thawing and degassing under the influence of climate warming.

df4f5d584123.title: Soil
df4f5d584123.sentence: Humans can get some idea of the soil atmosphere through the well-known 'after-the-rain' scent, when infiltering rainwater flushes out the whole soil atmosphere after a drought period, or when soil is excavated, a bulk property attributed in a reductionist manner to particular biochemical compounds such as petrichor or geosmin.

15c08b2190da.title: Greenhouse gas
15c08b2190da.sentence: Greenhouse gases (GHGs) are the gases in an atmosphere that trap heat, raising the surface temperature of astronomical bodies such as Earth.

9d624d713e44.title: Greenhouse gas
9d624d713e44.sentence: Unlike other gases, greenhouse gases absorb the radiations that a planet emits, resulting in the greenhouse effect.

a3634d5560ac.title: Greenhouse gas
a3634d5560ac.sentence: Without greenhouse gases in the atmosphere, the average temperature of Earth's surface would be about −18 °C (0 °F), rather than the present average of 15 °C (59 °F).

9ec9b08cca3c.title: Greenhouse gas
9ec9b08cca3c.sentence: 99% of the Earth's dry atmosphere (excluding water vapor) is made up of nitrogen (N 2) (78%) and oxygen (O 2) (21%).

988db4cd4c09.title: Greenhouse gas
988db4cd4c09.sentence: Because their molecules contain two atoms of the same element, they have no asymmetry in the distribution of their electrical charges, and so are almost totally unaffected by infrared thermal radiation, with only an extremely minor effect from collision-induced absorption.

6ec549ce0680.title: Greenhouse gas
6ec549ce0680.sentence: On the other hand, carbon dioxide (0.04%), methane, nitrous oxide and even less abundant trace gases account for less than 0.1% of Earth's atmosphere, but because their molecules contain atoms of different elements, there is an asymmetry in electric charge distribution which allows molecular vibrations to interact with electromagnetic radiation.

4bbe28fc593f.title: Greenhouse gas
4bbe28fc593f.section: Contributions of specific gases to the greenhouse effect > Special role of water vapor
4bbe28fc593f.sentence: Water vapor is the most important greenhouse gas overall, being responsible for 41–67% of the greenhouse effect, but its global concentrations are not directly affected by human activity.

205fedd08810.title: Greenhouse gas
205fedd08810.section: Contributions of specific gases to the greenhouse effect > Special role of water vapor
205fedd08810.sentence: While local water vapor concentrations can be affected by developments such as irrigation, it has little impact on the global scale due to its short residence time of about nine days.

20d0e5301c71.title: Greenhouse gas
20d0e5301c71.section: Contributions of specific gases to the greenhouse effect > Special role of water vapor
20d0e5301c71.sentence: Indirectly, an increase in global temperatures will also increase water vapor concentrations and thus their warming effect, in a process known as water vapor feedback.

6cf676db514d.title: Greenhouse gas
6cf676db514d.sentence: Atmospheric concentrations are determined by the balance between sources (emissions of the gas from human activities and natural systems) and sinks (the removal of the gas from the atmosphere by conversion to a different chemical compound or absorption by bodies of water).

460c4135e45f.title: Greenhouse gas
460c4135e45f.sentence: Individual atoms or molecules may be lost or deposited to sinks such as the soil, the oceans and other waters, or vegetation and other biological systems, reducing the excess to background concentrations.

088ea382b54a.title: Greenhouse gas
088ea382b54a.sentence: The annual airborne fraction for CO2 had been stable at 0.45 for the past six decades even as the emissions have been increasing.

1e73f249b50c.title: Greenhouse gas
1e73f249b50c.sentence: This means that the other 0.55 of emitted CO2 is absorbed by the land and atmosphere carbon sinks within the first year of an emission.

9a5e4a7c5f39.title: Greenhouse gas
9a5e4a7c5f39.sentence: The vast majority of carbon dioxide emissions by humans come from the burning of fossil fuels.

7abb6a108cac.title: Greenhouse gas
7abb6a108cac.sentence: Additional contributions come from cement manufacturing, fertilizer production, and changes in land use like deforestation.

4703573d9b4b.title: Greenhouse gas
4703573d9b4b.sentence: Methane emissions originate from agriculture, fossil fuel production, waste, and other sources.

32817658dbd7.title: Greenhouse gas
32817658dbd7.sentence: Rice paddies are a significant agricultural source of greenhouse gas emissions, contributing 22% of total agricultural methane and 11% of nitrous oxide emissions.

be3cc0d95214.title: Physical properties of soil
be3cc0d95214.sentence: Soil temperature depends on the ratio of the energy absorbed to that lost.

fc0268c1d9a8.title: Physical properties of soil
fc0268c1d9a8.sentence: Soil has a mean annual temperature from -10 to 26 °C according to biomes.

4d801e475731.title: Physical properties of soil
4d801e475731.sentence: Soil temperature regulates seed germination, breaking of seed dormancy, plant and root growth and the availability of nutrients.

1b762cf1c4da.title: Physical properties of soil
1b762cf1c4da.sentence: Soil temperature has important seasonal, monthly and daily variations, fluctuations in soil temperature being much lower with increasing soil depth.

dd7e260d4e99.title: Soil ecology
dd7e260d4e99.sentence: Soil temperature also varies with depth; upper soil layers are majorly influenced by air temperature, while deeper soil layers experience less temperature fluctuation.

98ef50cf3427.title: Physical properties of soil
98ef50cf3427.sentence: There are various factors that affect soil temperature, such as water content, soil color, and relief (slope, orientation, and elevation), and soil cover (shading and insulation), in addition to air temperature.

a2b08aa74b0a.title: Physical properties of soil
a2b08aa74b0a.sentence: Whiter soil tends to have a higher albedo than blacker soil cover, which encourages whiter soils to have lower soil temperatures.

d6a19eedbdf2.title: Physical properties of soil
d6a19eedbdf2.sentence: As such, wet soil usually warms more slowly than dry soil – wet surface soil is typically 3 to 6 °C colder than dry surface soil.

8c62f9f4649f.title: Physical properties of soil
8c62f9f4649f.sentence: The specific heat of soil is the energy required to raise the temperature of soil by 1 °C. The specific heat of soil increases as water content increases, since the heat capacity of water is greater than that of dry soil.

d45322a73968.title: Physical properties of soil
d45322a73968.sentence: Also, a tremendous energy (~584 cal/g or 2442 kJ/kg at 25 °C) is required to evaporate water (known as the heat of vaporization).

c84171fc0edb.title: Physical properties of soil
c84171fc0edb.sentence: Soil temperatures can be raised by drying soils or the use of clear plastic mulches.

8190040e9fe6.title: Physical properties of soil
8190040e9fe6.sentence: Organic mulches slow the warming of the soil.

0d9545d4316d.title: Physical properties of soil
0d9545d4316d.sentence: Heavy mulching (a type of soil cover) can slow the warming of soil in summer, and, at the same time, reduce fluctuations in surface temperature.

547e1dbf816d.title: Physical properties of soil
547e1dbf816d.sentence: Most often, agricultural activities must adapt to soil temperatures by:

7636c659dc32.title: Physical properties of soil
7636c659dc32.sentence: - maximizing germination and growth by timing of planting (also determined by photoperiod)

977b39338520.title: Physical properties of soil
977b39338520.sentence: - optimizing use of anhydrous ammonia by applying to soil below 10 °C (50 °F)

969f48189120.title: Physical properties of soil
969f48189120.sentence: - preventing heaving and thawing due to frosts from damaging shallow-rooted crops

9d2968b8dea8.title: Physical properties of soil
9d2968b8dea8.sentence: Soil temperatures are increasing worldwide under the influence of present-day global climate warming, with opposing views about expected effects on carbon capture and storage and feedback loops to climate change Most threats are about permafrost thawing and attended effects on carbon destocking and ecosystem collapse.

3c84e39b54cc.title: Soil gas
3c84e39b54cc.sentence: In soil, a concentration gradient causes net movement of molecules from high concentration to low concentration, which gives the movement of gas by diffusion.

5ea4d67e48d7.title: Soil
5ea4d67e48d7.sentence: Oxygen from above atmosphere diffuses in the soil where it is consumed and levels of carbon dioxide in excess of above atmosphere diffuse out with other gases (including greenhouse gases) as well as water vapor.

ec7eff914371.title: Soil gas
ec7eff914371.sentence: Gas molecules in soil are in continuous thermal motion according to the kinetic theory of gases, and there is also collision between molecules – a random walk process.

6dfecd5e9cb2.title: Soil gas
6dfecd5e9cb2.sentence: Numerically, it is explained by the Fick's law of diffusion.

356587780410.title: Soil
356587780410.sentence: It is the total pore space (porosity) of soil, not the pore size, and the degree of pore interconnection (or conversely pore sealing), together with water content, air turbulence and temperature, that determine the rate of diffusion of gases into and out of soil.

c867df6c41e1.title: Soil
c867df6c41e1.sentence: Movement of gases is by diffusion from high concentrations to lower, the diffusion coefficient decreasing with soil compaction.

48cb288c8bc9.title: Soil
48cb288c8bc9.sentence: Platy soil structure and soil compaction (low porosity) impede gas flow, and a deficiency of oxygen may encourage anaerobic bacteria to reduce (strip oxygen) from nitrate NO3 to the gases N2, N2O, and NO, which are then lost to the atmosphere, thereby depleting the soil of nitrogen, a detrimental process called denitrification.

1338aa39fd8c.title: Hydric soil
1338aa39fd8c.sentence: Gas diffusion in soil slows (some 10,000 times slower) when soil becomes saturated with water because there are no open passageways for air to travel.

b359d19ce21f.title: Soil gas
b359d19ce21f.sentence: More significantly, moreover, variation in soil gas composition due to seasonal, or even daily, temperature and/or moisture change can influence the rate of soil respiration.

7990611ab0e4.title: Soil gas
7990611ab0e4.sentence: In regions of the world where freezing of soils or drought is common, soil thawing and rewetting due to seasonal or meteorological changes influence soil gas flux.

7d2a6d27ab15.title: Soil gas
7d2a6d27ab15.sentence: Both processes hydrate the soil and increase nutrient availability leading to an increase in microbial activity.

1ebed88c29b0.title: Soil gas
1ebed88c29b0.sentence: Furthermore, for processes such as soil thawing and rewetting, for example, large sudden changes in soil respiration can cause increased flux of soil gases such as carbon dioxide and methane, which are greenhouse gases.

eaed4ee6f811.title: Soil aeration
eaed4ee6f811.sentence: Soil aeration is the mechanism of improving the exchange of gases between the atmosphere and soil.

0f313d6b19ad.title: Soil aeration
0f313d6b19ad.sentence: Through soil microbial activity and plant root respiration, certain gases such as oxygen will be depleted in the soil, while others, such as carbon dioxide, will build up in the soil.

248ba46cf14a.title: Soil aeration
248ba46cf14a.sentence: Lack of oxygen in the soil can impact plant growth.

c097a29cf32e.title: Soil aeration
c097a29cf32e.sentence: In addition to allowing the exchange of gases, soil aeration allows for water drainage and root growth.

1701f8b0d1ba.title: Soil aeration
1701f8b0d1ba.sentence: A common contributor to lack of soil aeration is soil compaction.

b6396caaa97a.title: Soil gas
b6396caaa97a.sentence: The network of pores within the soil aerates, or ventilates, the soil.

5cdaa89edc45.title: Soil gas
5cdaa89edc45.sentence: This aeration network becomes blocked when water enters soil pores.

d5974ddfe434.title: Soil ecology
d5974ddfe434.sentence: Both wind and atmospheric pressure play critical roles in soil aeration.

97e9003a77f2.title: Soil ecology
97e9003a77f2.sentence: In addition, convection and diffusion also influence the rates of soil aeration

3380eb8db1d4.title: Physical properties of soil
3380eb8db1d4.sentence: Soil structure has a strong influence on the larger pores that affect soil aeration, water infiltration and drainage.

c791f87a05e7.title: Plant nutrients in soil
c791f87a05e7.sentence: Examples of such conditions include waterlogging or soil compaction resulting in poor soil aeration, excessively high or low soil temperatures, and all above-ground conditions that result in low translocation of sugars to plant roots.

2072543a3e9e.title: Plant nutrients in soil
2072543a3e9e.sentence: This occurs when poor soil aeration limits free oxygen, forcing bacteria to use the oxygen in nitrate for their respiratory process.

4a44f289b164.title: Soil aeration
4a44f289b164.sentence: Liquid aeration involves applying a fortified liquid solution to the lawn.

38b8f68d475d.title: Soil aeration
38b8f68d475d.sentence: Commonly, the active ingredient is ammonium lauryl sulfate.

e1f8447f1c25.title: Soil aeration
e1f8447f1c25.sentence: The solution breaks down dense particles in the soil and loosens it up, decreasing compaction and allowing for aeration.

1c2a817198aa.title: Fertilizer
1c2a817198aa.sentence: Liming has also a decisive and positive influence on crop yields by couteracting soil acidification, a side-effect of plant growth and nutrient export by crops, improving soil structure, and thus soil aeration, and increasing soil biological activity, thereby soil fertility, in particular through increased nitrification.

690a9b0ece18.title: Soil animals
690a9b0ece18.sentence: The megafauna that lives in the soil eat organic matter, insects and small vertebrates since most fossorial animals just dig the soil without feeding on it, and thus are not directly involved in decomposition and microbial-faunal relationships, but their mechanical disturbance of soil horizons may contribute to improve nutrient availability, infiltration rate, soil aeration, mycorrhizal inoculation and seed germination, making them providers of important ecosystem services.

d5ec8eaaef97.title: Soil gas
d5ec8eaaef97.sentence: The composition of gases present in the soil's pores, referred to commonly as the soil atmosphere or atmosphere of the soil, is similar to that of the Earth's atmosphere.

e732221b9a0d.title: Soil gas
e732221b9a0d.sentence: Despite this spatial- and temporal-dependent fluctuation, soil gases typically boast greater concentrations of carbon dioxide and water vapor in comparison to the atmosphere.

1285acd11fc3.title: Soil
1285acd11fc3.sentence: Atmospheric CO2 concentration is 0.04%, but in the soil pore space it may range from 10 to 100 times that level, thus potentially contributing to the inhibition of root respiration.

d10c2429b073.title: Soil
d10c2429b073.sentence: At extreme levels, CO2 is toxic.

b619fac566ca.title: Soil chemistry
b619fac566ca.sentence: CO2 increases with the increase in the depth of soil because of decomposition of accumulated organic matter and abundance of plant roots.

61435673b221.title: Soil
61435673b221.sentence: Calcareous soils regulate CO2 concentration by carbonate buffering, contrary to acid soils in which all CO2 respired accumulates in the soil pore system.

c62d92d4f437.title: Soil gas
c62d92d4f437.sentence: Unlike the atmosphere, however, soil gas composition is less stagnant due to the various chemical and biological processes taking place in the soil.

d88056dbde2c.title: Soil gas
d88056dbde2c.sentence: The resulting changes in composition from these processes can be defined by their variation time (i.e. daily vs. seasonal).

f0e81d2b3d69.title: Soil gas
f0e81d2b3d69.sentence: Furthermore, concentrations of other gases, such as methane and nitrous oxide, are relatively minor yet significant in determining greenhouse gas flux and anthropogenic impacts on soils.

922a59ab368a.title: Soil chemistry
922a59ab368a.sentence: Important factors controlling the soil atmosphere are temperature, atmospheric pressure, wind/aeration and rainfall.

0d6a8c7e7022.title: Frost line
0d6a8c7e7022.sentence: The frost line—also known as frost depth or freezing depth—is most commonly the depth to which the groundwater in soil is expected to freeze.

7ee122727972.title: Frost line
7ee122727972.sentence: The frost depth depends on the climatic conditions of an area, the heat transfer properties of the soil and adjacent materials, and on nearby heat sources.

dde5a30a79a2.title: Frost line
dde5a30a79a2.sentence: For example, snow cover and asphalt insulate the ground and homes can heat the ground (see also heat island).

22398a21dec1.title: Frost line
22398a21dec1.sentence: The line varies by latitude, it is deeper closer to the poles.

7b70a724905a.title: Frost line
7b70a724905a.sentence: The maximum frost depth observed in the contiguous United States ranges from 0 to 8 feet (2.4 m).

63325669c5d4.title: Frost line
63325669c5d4.sentence: Alternatively, in Arctic and Antarctic locations the freezing depth is so deep that it becomes year-round permafrost, and the term "thaw depth" is used instead.

2b49add5cb4e.title: Frost line
2b49add5cb4e.sentence: Frost front refers to the varying position of the frost line during seasonal periods of freezing and thawing.

4d3e7023f387.title: Frost line
4d3e7023f387.sentence: Finally, in tropical regions, frost line may refer to the vertical geographic elevation below which frost does not occur.

e3883abccd3a.title: Frost line
e3883abccd3a.sentence: Building codes take frost depth into account because of frost heaving, which can damage buildings by moving their foundations.

6f4c4e14725e.title: Frost line
6f4c4e14725e.sentence: For this reason, foundations are generally built below the frost depth.

6b41d7e064ef.title: Frost line
6b41d7e064ef.sentence: Water and sewage pipes are typically buried below the frost line to prevent them from freezing.

296007b304ad.title: Frost line
296007b304ad.sentence: Alternatively, pipes may be insulated or heated using heat tape or similar products to allow for shallower depths.

b51ca4627d28.title: Frost line
b51ca4627d28.sentence: Due to additional cost, this method is typically only used where deeper trenching is not an option due to utility conflicts, shallow bedrock, or other conditions that make deeper excavation infeasible.

5e2f8d7c8283.title: Frost heaving
5e2f8d7c8283.sentence: Frost heaving (or a frost heave) is an upwards swelling of soil during freezing conditions caused by an increasing presence of ice as it grows towards the surface, upwards from the depth in the soil where freezing temperatures have penetrated into the soil (the freezing front or freezing boundary).

6300e61ceb72.title: Frost heaving
6300e61ceb72.sentence: Frost heaving requires a frost-susceptible soil, a continual supply of water below (a water table) and freezing temperatures, penetrating into the soil.

7ba97dfe66af.title: Frost heaving
7ba97dfe66af.sentence: Ice growth requires a water supply that delivers water to the freezing front via capillary action in certain soils.

3a2cbf2c156e.title: Frost heaving
3a2cbf2c156e.sentence: Yet the force of one or more growing ice lenses is sufficient to lift a layer of soil, as much as 1 foot (0.30 metres) or more.

f8f54e4c9430.title: Frost heaving
f8f54e4c9430.section: Mechanisms > Historical understanding of frost heaving
f8f54e4c9430.sentence: Since the molar volume of water expands by about 9% as it changes phase from water to ice at its bulk freezing point, 9% would be the maximum expansion possible owing to molar volume expansion, and even then only if the ice were rigidly constrained laterally in the soil so that the entire volume expansion had to occur vertically.

8b8ddadd4198.title: Frost heaving
8b8ddadd4198.section: Mechanisms > Historical understanding of frost heaving
8b8ddadd4198.sentence: By 1930, Stephen Taber, head of the Department of Geology at the University of South Carolina, had disproved the hypothesis that frost heaving results from molar volume expansion with freezing of water already present in the soil prior to the onset of subzero temperatures, i.e. with little contribution from the migration of water within the soil.

b7248d257e0d.title: Frost heaving
b7248d257e0d.section: Mechanisms > Historical understanding of frost heaving
b7248d257e0d.sentence: Taber demonstrated that liquid water migrates towards the freeze line within soil.

da78ed742dac.title: Frost heaving
da78ed742dac.section: Mechanisms > Historical understanding of frost heaving
da78ed742dac.sentence: He showed that other liquids, such as benzene, which contracts when it freezes, also produce frost heave.

98234e5ee92e.title: Frost heaving
98234e5ee92e.section: Mechanisms > Historical understanding of frost heaving
98234e5ee92e.sentence: This excluded molar volume changes as the dominant mechanism for vertical displacement of freezing soil.

7b9fd40c3988.title: Frost heaving
7b9fd40c3988.sentence: Differential frost heaving can crack road surfaces—contributing to springtime pothole formation—and damage building foundations.

808f8ea5f2ab.title: Frost heaving
808f8ea5f2ab.sentence: Frost heaves may occur in mechanically refrigerated cold-storage buildings and ice rinks.

97ebf5584280.title: Frost heaving
97ebf5584280.sentence: If a refrigerated building's foundation is placed on frost-susceptible soils with a water table within reach of the freezing front, then the floors of such structures may heave, due to the same mechanisms found in nature.

d5d4c66ed7ad.title: Frost heaving
d5d4c66ed7ad.sentence: The strategies include placement of non-frost-susceptible soil beneath the foundation, adding insulation to diminish the penetration of the freezing front, and heating the soil beneath the building sufficiently to keep it from freezing.

910fbe89184a.title: Frost heaving
910fbe89184a.sentence: Needle ice is essentially frost heaving that occurs at the beginning of the freezing season, before the freezing front has penetrated very far into the soil and there is no soil overburden to lift as a frost heave.

19ab55538550.title: Frost heaving
19ab55538550.section: Mechanisms > Historical understanding of frost heaving
19ab55538550.sentence: Urban Hjärne described frost effects in soil in 1694.

20e58847a89b.title: Needle ice
20e58847a89b.sentence: Needle ice is a needle-shaped column of ice formed by groundwater.

cc5325579969.title: Needle ice
cc5325579969.sentence: The process usually occurs at night when the air temperature reaches its minimum.

89c18b055d39.title: Needle ice
89c18b055d39.sentence: Needle ice forms when the temperature of the soil is above 0 °C (32 °F) and the surface temperature of the air is below 0 °C (32 °F).

9ea97c8c3da0.title: Needle ice
9ea97c8c3da0.sentence: Liquid water underground rises to the surface by capillary action, and then freezes and contributes to a growing needle-like ice column.

b42fa5aabb9c.title: Needle ice
b42fa5aabb9c.sentence: The ice needles are typically a few centimetres long.

3a91bd920fd1.title: Needle ice
3a91bd920fd1.sentence: Although the literature states that the largest recorded needle ice was at 10 cm in length, specimens 15-20 cm in length have been observed at Gerðuberg, for example.

9d26ea98dafc.title: Needle ice
9d26ea98dafc.sentence: In order for needle ice to form there needs to be a process of ice segregation, which only occurs in a porous medium when supercooled water freezes into existing ice, growing away from the ice/water interface.

e75f1ef213e1.title: Needle ice
e75f1ef213e1.sentence: Needle ice is most suitable in soils with a high silt and organic matter content.

28472f104af7.title: Needle ice
28472f104af7.sentence: While growing, they may lift or push away small soil particles.

0e01b269cdca.title: Needle ice
0e01b269cdca.sentence: The growth of needle ice lifts a detached, frozen soil crust riding on top of the layer of ice.

4226d0f454f8.title: Needle ice
4226d0f454f8.sentence: When the crust and the ice melt, the soil surface settles back irregularly.

7067c1a5f71b.title: Needle ice
7067c1a5f71b.sentence: This phenomenon is linked to erosion, particularly on streambanks.

25b350490217.title: Needle ice
25b350490217.sentence: On sloped surfaces, needle ice may be a factor contributing to soil creep.

d816d7723abd.title: Needle ice
d816d7723abd.sentence: Needle ice phenomena play a particularly significant role in patterned ground in periglacial environments.

f9e987a51f4a.title: Needle ice
f9e987a51f4a.sentence: Seedlings are often heaved to this surface by needle ice.

3fce92e03363.title: Needle ice
3fce92e03363.sentence: When the needle ice melts, the seedlings do not settle correctly back into the ground causing them to die.

926b120946dd.title: Needle ice
926b120946dd.sentence: Even if the seedlings are partially heaved by the needle ice, they can still die due to root desiccation.

cf330bc72a0f.title: Needle ice
cf330bc72a0f.sentence: Alternate names for needle ice are "frost pillars" ("Säuleneis" in German), "frost column", "Spew Ice", "Kammeis" (a German term meaning "comb ice"), "Stängeleis" (another German term referring to the stem-like structures), "shimobashira" (霜柱, a Japanese term meaning frost pillars), or "pipkrake" (from Swedish pipa (tube) and krake (weak, fine), coined in 1907 by Henrik Hesselman).

6d082ac8849f.title: Capillary pressure
6d082ac8849f.sentence: Taber’s initial work was related to understanding how the size of pores within the ground influenced the amount of frost heave.

7fae248ebe0b.title: Capillary pressure
7fae248ebe0b.sentence: He also discovered that frost heave is favorable for crystal growth and that a gradient of soil moisture tension drives water upward toward the freezing front near the top of the ground.

1bafed88da21.title: Soil thermal properties
1bafed88da21.sentence: The thermal properties of soil are a component of soil physics that has found important uses in engineering, climatology and agriculture.

7c876bf3ab06.title: Soil thermal properties
