7c876bf3ab06.sentence: While related to soil temperature, it is more accurately associated with the transfer of energy (mostly in the form of heat) throughout the soil, by radiation, conduction and convection.

b2ae7b0007ab.title: Soil thermal properties
b2ae7b0007ab.sentence: - Volumetric heat capacity, SI Units: J∙m−3∙K−1

4f2b670a2518.title: Soil thermal properties
4f2b670a2518.sentence: These properties influence how energy is partitioned in the soil profile.

05c36f81afe2.title: Soil thermal properties
05c36f81afe2.sentence: It is hard to say something general about the soil thermal properties at a certain location because these are in a constant state of flux from diurnal and seasonal variations.

35b7f7b3ee2f.title: Soil thermal properties
35b7f7b3ee2f.sentence: Apart from the basic soil composition, which is constant at one location, soil thermal properties are strongly influenced by the soil volumetric water content, volume fraction of solids and volume fraction of air.

96629b1b5ce1.title: Soil thermal properties
96629b1b5ce1.sentence: As such soil moisture properties and soil thermal properties are very closely linked and are often measured and reported together.

8160365a3c81.title: Soil thermal properties
8160365a3c81.sentence: Temperature variations are most extreme at the surface of the soil and these variations are transferred to sub surface layers but at reduced rates as depth increases.

e5426607f3e2.title: Soil thermal properties
e5426607f3e2.sentence: Additionally there is a time delay as to when maximum and minimum temperatures are achieved at increasing soil depth (sometimes referred to as thermal lag).

8e804446b1f9.title: Soil thermal properties
8e804446b1f9.sentence: The various methods of measuring soil thermal properties have been utilized to assist in diverse fields such as; the expansion and contraction of construction materials especially in freezing soils, longevity and efficiency of gas pipes or electrical cables buried in the ground, energy conservation schemes, in agriculture for timing of planting to ensure optimum seedling emergence and crop growth, measuring greenhouse gas emissions as heat effects the liberation of carbon dioxide from soil.

47dd772f6c23.title: Soil thermal properties
47dd772f6c23.sentence: Soil thermal properties are also becoming important in areas of environmental science such as determining water movement in radioactive waste and in locating buried land mines.

afce875fb48b.title: Permafrost
afce875fb48b.sentence: Permafrost (from perma- 'permanent' and frost) is soil or underwater sediment which continuously remains below 0 °C (32 °F) for two years or more; the oldest permafrost has been continuously frozen for around 700,000 years.

429702f5b554.title: Permafrost
429702f5b554.sentence: Permafrost is soil, rock or sediment that is frozen for more than two consecutive years.

597cdba87d35.title: Permafrost
597cdba87d35.sentence: In practice, this means that permafrost occurs at a mean annual temperature of 0 °C (32.0 °F) or below.

0ca00ad27c06.title: Permafrost
0ca00ad27c06.sentence: Around 15% of the exposed land surface of the Northern Hemisphere, and 11% of the global land surface, is underlain by permafrost, covering a total area of around 18 million km2 (6.9 million sq mi).

1102b830bfb7.title: Permafrost
1102b830bfb7.sentence: This includes large areas of Alaska, Canada, Greenland, and Siberia.

71bcd95c141f.title: Permafrost
71bcd95c141f.sentence: It is also located in high mountain regions, with the Tibetan Plateau being a prominent example.

97a6f8bd8948.title: Permafrost
97a6f8bd8948.sentence: Whilst the shallowest permafrost has a vertical extent of below a meter (3 ft), the deepest is greater than 1,500 m (4,900 ft).

562af2c8126d.title: Permafrost
562af2c8126d.sentence: The ground beneath glaciers and ice sheets is not usually defined as permafrost, so on land, permafrost is generally located beneath a so-called active layer of soil which freezes and thaws depending on the season.

c9e2b53dd4c9.title: Permafrost
c9e2b53dd4c9.sentence: Permafrost contains large amounts of dead biomass that has accumulated throughout millennia without having had the chance to fully decompose and release its carbon, making tundra soil a carbon sink.

616e26044f3e.title: Permafrost
616e26044f3e.sentence: As global warming heats the ecosystem, frozen soil thaws and becomes warm enough for decomposition to start anew, accelerating the permafrost carbon cycle.

194fae3cc3be.title: Permafrost
194fae3cc3be.sentence: Depending on conditions at the time of thaw, decomposition can release either carbon dioxide or methane, and these greenhouse gas emissions act as a climate change feedback.

fe6b491f6cd7.title: Permafrost
fe6b491f6cd7.sentence: Formerly frozen ground often contains enough ice that when it thaws, hydraulic saturation is suddenly exceeded, so the ground shifts substantially and may even collapse outright.

9cb49cb9f261.title: Permafrost
9cb49cb9f261.sentence: Many buildings and other infrastructure were built on permafrost when it was frozen and stable, and so are vulnerable to collapse if it thaws.

f405d5e0bed2.title: Ice lens
f405d5e0bed2.sentence: Ice lenses are bodies of ice formed when moisture, diffused within soil or rock, accumulates in a localized zone.

e3f21f4e3fdf.title: Ice lens
e3f21f4e3fdf.sentence: Ice lenses grow parallel to the surface and several centimeters to several decimeters (inches to feet) deep in the soil or rock.

dc5b6ab53459.title: Ice lens
dc5b6ab53459.sentence: The ice initially accumulates within small collocated pores or pre-existing crack, and, as long as the conditions remain favorable, continues to collect in the ice layer or ice lens, wedging the soil or rock apart.

b3e38cb89cef.title: Frost heaving
b3e38cb89cef.sentence: The dominant cause of soil displacement in frost heaving is the development of ice lenses.

7668cb11085e.title: Frost heaving
7668cb11085e.sentence: These lenses grow by the continual addition of water from a groundwater source that is lower in the soil and below the freezing line in the soil.

927f489631eb.title: Frost heaving
927f489631eb.sentence: The presence of frost-susceptible soil with a pore structure that allows capillary flow is essential to supplying water to the ice lenses as they form.

314354e9eac4.title: Frost heaving
314354e9eac4.sentence: Owing to the Gibbs–Thomson effect of the confinement of liquids in pores, water in soil can remain liquid at a temperature that is below the bulk freezing point of water.

19a9649e9396.title: Frost heaving
19a9649e9396.sentence: This effect allows water to percolate through the soil towards the ice lens, allowing the lens to grow.

3526f4c5bdae.title: Ice lens
3526f4c5bdae.sentence: Studies from 1990 have demonstrated that rock fracture by ice segregation (i.e., the fracture of intact rock by ice lenses that grow by drawing water from their surroundings during periods of sustained subfreezing temperatures) is a more effective weathering process than the freeze-thaw process which older texts proposed.

7fa5a7557b23.title: Ice lens
7fa5a7557b23.sentence: Although rock fracture in periglacial regions (alpine, subpolar and polar) has often been attributed to the freezing and volumetric expansion of water trapped within pores and cracks, the majority of frost heaving and of bedrock fracture results instead from ice segregation and lens growth in the near-surface frozen regions.

ddcf957ec8ed.title: Ice lens
ddcf957ec8ed.section: Description of the phenomena > Ice lenses in tundra
ddcf957ec8ed.sentence: Frost heave is common in arctic tundra because the permafrost maintains ground frozen at depth and prevents snowmelt and rain from draining.

b4559ad72e26.title: Ice lens
b4559ad72e26.section: Description of the phenomena > Ice lenses in tundra
b4559ad72e26.sentence: As a result, conditions are optimal for deep ice lens formation with large ice accumulations and significant soil displacement.

4bede952714f.title: Patterned ground
4bede952714f.sentence: Patterned ground is the distinct and often symmetrical natural pattern of geometric shapes formed by the deformation of ground material in periglacial regions.

7ef18f87c403.title: Patterned ground
7ef18f87c403.sentence: It is typically found in remote regions of the Arctic, Antarctica, and the Outback in Australia, but is also found anywhere that freezing and thawing of soil alternate; patterned ground has also been observed in the hyper-arid Atacama Desert and on Mars.

83932a443769.title: Patterned ground
83932a443769.sentence: The mechanism of the formation of patterned ground had long puzzled scientists but the introduction of computer-generated geological models in the past 20 years has allowed scientists to relate it to frost heaving, the expansion that occurs when wet, fine-grained, and porous soils freeze.

e78e7109147f.title: Patterned ground
e78e7109147f.sentence: In periglacial areas and areas affected by seasonal frost, repeated freezing and thawing of groundwater forces larger stones toward the surface, as smaller stones flow and settle underneath larger stones.

b94b6a871d4d.title: Patterned ground
b94b6a871d4d.sentence: These water-saturated areas of finer sediments have a much greater ability to expand and contract as freezing and thawing occur, leading to lateral forces which ultimately pile larger stones into clusters and stripes.

9f3726dda46c.title: Patterned ground
9f3726dda46c.sentence: Through time, repeated freeze-thaw cycles smooth out irregularities and odd-shaped piles to form the common polygons, circles, and stripes of patterned ground.

fe0a8636ad41.title: Patterned ground
fe0a8636ad41.sentence: Patterned ground can be found in a variety of forms.

14c537c9233b.title: Patterned ground
14c537c9233b.sentence: Circles range in size from a few centimeters to several meters in diameter.

4c6a08c59510.title: Patterned ground
4c6a08c59510.sentence: Steps can be developed from circles and polygons.

8344dcd74906.title: Patterned ground
8344dcd74906.sentence: Stripes are lines of stones, vegetation, and/or soil that typically form from transitioning steps on slopes at angles between 2° and 7°.

3da1764c8639.title: Patterned ground
3da1764c8639.sentence: Stripes can consist of either sorted or unsorted material.

be10248ccecd.title: Patterned ground
be10248ccecd.sentence: Polygons can form either in permafrost areas (as ice wedges) or in areas that are affected by seasonal frost.

4b96aa267849.title: Patterned ground
4b96aa267849.sentence: Patterned ground forms mostly within the active layer of permafrost.

1cdac1e0ef64.title: Frost heaving
1cdac1e0ef64.sentence: Frost heaving creates raised-soil landforms in various geometries, including circles, polygons and stripes, which may be described as palsas in soils that are rich in organic matter, such as peat, or lithalsa in more mineral-rich soils.

dcfdb72c5d3a.title: Frost heaving
dcfdb72c5d3a.sentence: Frost heaves occur in alpine regions, even near the equator, as illustrated by palsas on Mount Kenya.

b3df6733c976.title: Frost heaving
b3df6733c976.sentence: In Arctic permafrost regions, a related type of ground heaving over hundreds of years can create structures, as high as 60 metres, known as pingos, which are fed by an upwelling of ground water, instead of the capillary action that feeds the growth of frost heaves.

c3ede61574ac.title: Frost heaving
c3ede61574ac.sentence: Cryogenic earth hummocks are a small formation resulting from granular convection that appear in seasonally frozen ground and have many different names; in North America they are earth hummocks; thúfur in Greenland and Iceland; and pounus in Fennoscandia.

d2b6d8ea8ae5.title: Frost heaving
d2b6d8ea8ae5.sentence: In May 2008 the Mars Phoenix lander touched down on such a polygonal frost-heave landscape and quickly discovered ice a few centimetres below the surface.

611403720df3.title: Frost heaving
611403720df3.sentence: Polygonal forms apparently caused by frost heave have been observed in near-polar regions of Mars by the Mars Orbiter Camera (MOC) aboard the Mars Global Surveyor and the HiRISE camera on the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter.

279683a74481.title: Frost heaving
279683a74481.sentence: Frost-susceptible soils are those with pore sizes between particles and particle surface area that promote capillary flow.

f9f66d4b3451.title: Frost heaving
f9f66d4b3451.sentence: Such soil is referred to as "frost susceptible".

7bce8894f942.title: Frost heaving
7bce8894f942.sentence: Silty and loamy soil types, which contain fine particles, are examples of frost-susceptible soils.

02b45e444a1b.title: Frost heaving
02b45e444a1b.sentence: Many agencies classify materials as being frost susceptible if 10 percent or more constituent particles pass through a 0.075 mm (No. 200) sieve or 3 percent or more pass through a 0.02 mm (No. 635) sieve.

58d6b3311666.title: Frost heaving
58d6b3311666.sentence: Non-frost-susceptible soils may be too dense to promote water flow (low hydraulic conductivity) or too open in porosity to promote capillary flow.

e3fe850814d5.title: Frost heaving
e3fe850814d5.sentence: Examples include dense clays with a small pore size and therefore a low hydraulic conductivity and clean sands and gravels, which contain small amounts of fine particles and whose pore sizes are too open to promote capillary flow.

e593753b928d.title: Frost heaving
e593753b928d.sentence: Based on such research, standard tests exist to determine the relative frost and thaw weakening susceptibility of soils used in pavement systems by comparing the heave rate and thawed bearing ratio with values in an established classification system for soils where frost-susceptibility is uncertain.

812f0507c0fd.title: Frost heaving
812f0507c0fd.sentence: Another water-transport effect is the preservation of a few molecular layers of liquid water on the surface of the ice lens, and between ice and soil particles.

13ee75fd84a6.title: Frost heaving
13ee75fd84a6.sentence: When ice surrounds a fine soil particle as it premelts, the soil particle will be displaced downward towards the warm direction within the thermal gradient due to melting and refreezing of the thin film of water that surrounds the particle.

1afbccef5eec.title: Frost heaving
1afbccef5eec.sentence: Faraday reported in 1860 on the unfrozen layer of premelted water.

be78664c4152.title: Frost heaving
be78664c4152.sentence: The particle migrates downwards toward the warmer soil in a process that Faraday called "thermal regelation." This effect purifies the ice lenses as they form by repelling fine soil particles.

25c3adc5615f.title: Frost heaving
25c3adc5615f.sentence: The thickness of such a film is temperature dependent and is thinner on the colder side of the particle.

f14ce6182a9b.title: Frost heaving
f14ce6182a9b.sentence: Therefore, there is a continuous replenishment of water flowing from the warm side to the cold side of the particle, and continuous melting to re-establish the thicker film on the warm side.

4509d819f42e.title: Frost heaving
4509d819f42e.sentence: Thus a 10-nanometer film of unfrozen water around each micrometer-sized soil particle can move it 10 micrometers/day in a thermal gradient of as low as 1 °C m−1.

53faa7127415.title: Soil gas
53faa7127415.sentence: Soil gases have been used for multiple scientific studies to explore topics such as microseepage, earthquakes, and gaseous exchange between the soil and the atmosphere.

9acd04a4bad7.title: Soil gas
9acd04a4bad7.sentence: Microseepage refers to the limited release of hydrocarbons on the soil surface and can be used to look for petroleum deposits based on the assumption that hydrocarbons vertically migrate to the soil surface in small quantities.

e9950c1e2ad1.title: Soil gas
e9950c1e2ad1.sentence: Migration of soil gases, specifically radon, can also be examined as earthquake precursors.

d346263a0beb.title: Soil gas
d346263a0beb.sentence: Some environmental contaminants below ground produce gas which diffuses through the soil such as from landfill wastes, mining activities, and contamination by petroleum hydrocarbons which produce volatile organic compounds.

889242bb9565.title: Soil gas
889242bb9565.sentence: These fluxes and interactions between soil gases and atmospheric air can further be analyzed by distance from the soil surface.

aa503e705cdf.title: Lithalsa
aa503e705cdf.sentence: Lithalsa is a frost-induced raised land form in permafrost areas with mineral-rich soils, where a perennial ice lens has developed within the soil.

7f6759b17dd2.title: Lithalsa
7f6759b17dd2.sentence: The term sometimes also refers to palsas and pingos.

b7528b0c2347.title: Frost heaving
b7528b0c2347.sentence: The stony lithalsa (heaved mounds) found on the archipelago of Svalbard are an example.

ccba1695acaf.title: Albedo
ccba1695acaf.sentence: Albedo (/ælˈbiːdoʊ/ ⓘ al-BEE-doh; from Latin albedo 'whiteness') is the fraction of sunlight that is diffusely reflected by a body.

d7839142383e.title: Albedo
d7839142383e.sentence: It is measured on a scale from 0 (corresponding to a black body that absorbs all incident radiation) to 1 (corresponding to a body that reflects all incident radiation).

ced22d7a37fe.title: Albedo
ced22d7a37fe.sentence: This spectrum includes visible light (0.4–0.7 μm), which explains why surfaces with a low albedo appear dark (e.g., trees absorb most radiation), whereas surfaces with a high albedo appear bright (e.g., snow reflects most radiation).

ed467339d093.title: Albedo
ed467339d093.section: Examples of terrestrial albedo effects > Albedo–temperature feedback
ed467339d093.sentence: When the melted area reveals surfaces with lower albedo, such as grass, soil, or ocean, the effect is reversed: the darkening surface lowers albedo, increasing local temperatures, which induces more melting and thus reducing the albedo further, resulting in still more heating.

c60c4bbe49df.title: Albedo
c60c4bbe49df.section: Terrestrial albedo > Changes to albedo due to human activities
c60c4bbe49df.sentence: Human activities (e.g., deforestation, farming, and urbanization) change the albedo of various areas around the globe.

344b0b73094a.title: Microclimate
344b0b73094a.sentence: A microclimate (or micro-climate) refers to localized atmospheric conditions in the near-surface layer, which includes the air immediately above a surface as well as the shallow soil and water environments below it.

71b20e833c4e.title: Microclimate
71b20e833c4e.sentence: It is characterized by a set of persistent, measurable differences in the climate conditions from those in the adjacent surrounding areas.

c9098063d086.title: Microclimate
c9098063d086.sentence: A microclimate can range in size from a few meters to at most a few kilometers across.

25daacc74582.title: Microclimate
25daacc74582.section: Causes of microclimates > Contributing environmental factors that shape microclimates
25daacc74582.sentence: Soils made of components that retain moisture tend to moderate temperature fluctuations while soils made of components which dry easily produce higher daily temperature changes.

26003fce39d9.title: Microclimate
26003fce39d9.section: Causes of microclimates > Contributing environmental factors that shape microclimates
26003fce39d9.sentence: For example, soils heavy in clay, retain heat and moisture which moderates the near ground temperature and humidity.

0872f3a60f26.title: Microclimate
0872f3a60f26.section: Causes of microclimates > Contributing environmental factors that shape microclimates
0872f3a60f26.sentence: South-facing slopes in the Northern Hemisphere and north-facing slopes in the Southern Hemisphere are exposed to more direct sunlight than opposite slopes and are therefore warmer for longer periods of time, giving the slope a warmer microclimate than the areas around the slope.

7ca8705b0243.title: Microclimate
7ca8705b0243.section: Causes of microclimates > Contributing environmental factors that shape microclimates
7ca8705b0243.sentence: The lowest area of a glen may sometimes frost sooner or harder than a nearby spot uphill, because cold air sinks, a drying breeze may not reach the lowest bottom, and humidity lingers and precipitates, then freezes.

8f8ce2c79282.title: Microclimate
8f8ce2c79282.sentence: Microclimate management involves the modification of conditions to those which are optimized for growth and crop yield, such as the practices of irrigation, shading, windbreaks, and vegetation management, These modifications can help buffer crops from environmental extremes, such as heat and drought.

ec3ce89e43b9.title: Fick's laws of diffusion
ec3ce89e43b9.sentence: Fick's laws of diffusion describe diffusion and were first posited by Adolf Fick in 1855 on the basis of largely experimental results.

84556e1d5527.title: Fick's laws of diffusion
84556e1d5527.sentence: Fick's first law: Movement of particles from high to low concentration (diffusive flux) is directly proportional to the particle's concentration gradient.

5dff1faf687d.title: Fick's laws of diffusion
5dff1faf687d.sentence: Fick's second law: Prediction of change in concentration gradient with time due to diffusion.

9e3722afa3bf.title: Fick's laws of diffusion
9e3722afa3bf.sentence: In one (spatial) dimension, the law can be written in various forms, where the most common form (see) is in a molar basis:J=−Ddφdx,where

77ce21797e83.title: Fick's laws of diffusion
77ce21797e83.sentence: - D is the diffusion coefficient or diffusivity.

4dc25f972a11.title: Fick's laws of diffusion
4dc25f972a11.sentence: Its dimension is area per unit time,

58481be84cf2.title: Fick's laws of diffusion
58481be84cf2.sentence: It is a partial differential equation which in one dimension reads∂φ∂t=D∂2φ∂x2,where

970964685642.title: Fick's laws of diffusion
970964685642.sentence: In two or more dimensions we must use the Laplacian Δ=∇2, which generalises the second derivative, obtaining the equation ∂φ∂t=DΔφ.Fick's second law has the same mathematical form as the Heat equation and its fundamental solution is the same as the Heat kernel, except switching thermal conductivity k with diffusion coefficient D:φ(x,t)=14πDtexp⁡(−x24Dt).Derivation of Fick's second law

45c2f1d28f8c.title: Fick's laws of diffusion
45c2f1d28f8c.sentence: Fick's law is analogous to the relationships discovered at the same epoch by other eminent scientists: Darcy's law (hydraulic flow), Ohm's law (charge transport), and Fourier's law (heat transport).

57066085ec86.title: Fick's laws of diffusion
57066085ec86.sentence: Equations based on Fick's law have been commonly used to model transport processes in foods, neurons, biopolymers, pharmaceuticals, porous soils, population dynamics, nuclear materials, plasma physics, and semiconductor doping processes.

f50c7cf4ef9d.title: Fick's laws of diffusion
f50c7cf4ef9d.sentence: When a diffusion process does not follow Fick's laws (which happens in cases of diffusion through porous media and diffusion of swelling penetrants, among others), it is referred to as non-Fickian.

287d36c496c8.title: Diffusion
287d36c496c8.sentence: Diffusion is the net movement of anything (for example, atoms, ions, molecules, energy) generally from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration.

543d3a4770cf.title: Diffusion
543d3a4770cf.sentence: Diffusion is driven by a gradient in Gibbs free energy or chemical potential.

ee794945d101.title: Diffusion
ee794945d101.sentence: "Bulk flow" is the movement/flow of an entire body due to a pressure gradient (for example, water coming out of a tap).

60fca86fb2f5.title: Diffusion
60fca86fb2f5.sentence: "Diffusion" is the gradual movement/dispersion of concentration within a body with no net movement of matter.

40cea9979948.title: Diffusion
40cea9979948.section: Diffusion in the context of different disciplines
40cea9979948.sentence: According to Fick's laws, the diffusion flux is proportional to the negative gradient of concentrations.

ece16b053d50.title: Diffusion
ece16b053d50.section: Models > Normal single component concentration gradient
ece16b053d50.sentence: Fick's first law: The diffusion flux, 𝐉, is proportional to the negative gradient of spatial concentration, n(x,t):

64abc0678e24.title: Diffusion
64abc0678e24.sentence: Care must be taken to properly account for the porosity (Φ) of the porous medium in both the flux terms and the accumulation terms.

c85a0a15b904.title: Diffusion
c85a0a15b904.sentence: For example, as the porosity goes to zero, the molar flux in the porous medium goes to zero for a given concentration gradient.

a50217054b70.title: Diffusion
a50217054b70.section: Random walk (random motion) > Separation of diffusion from convection in gases
a50217054b70.sentence: Under normal conditions, molecular diffusion dominates only at lengths in the nanometre-to-millimetre range.

b472955a4af6.title: Partial pressure
b472955a4af6.sentence: In a mixture of gases, each constituent gas has a partial pressure which is the notional pressure of that constituent gas as if it alone occupied the entire volume of the original mixture at the same temperature.

57b64e9bc189.title: Partial pressure
57b64e9bc189.sentence: The total pressure of an ideal gas mixture is the sum of the partial pressures of the gases in the mixture (Dalton's Law).

f75374a70b2e.title: Partial pressure
f75374a70b2e.sentence: Dalton's law expresses the fact that the total pressure of a mixture of ideal gases is equal to the sum of the partial pressures of the individual gases in the mixture.

934f7e3607ab.title: Partial pressure
934f7e3607ab.sentence: That is, the mole fraction xi of an individual gas component in an ideal gas mixture can be expressed in terms of the component's partial pressure or the moles of the component: xi=pip=nin

1e9417080b8f.title: Partial pressure
1e9417080b8f.sentence: and the partial pressure of an individual gas component in an ideal gas can be obtained using this expression: pi=xi⋅p

c62d32be343d.title: Partial pressure
c62d32be343d.sentence: The mole fraction of a gas component in a gas mixture is equal to the volumetric fraction of that component in a gas mixture.

188ef4658c44.title: Partial pressure
188ef4658c44.sentence: Gases dissolve, diffuse, and react according to their partial pressures (which appear in reaction quotient or equilibrium constant of gas reactions) and not according to their concentrations in a gas mixture or as a solute in solution.

7f7f2fadbcd6.title: Partial pressure
7f7f2fadbcd6.sentence: In chemistry and thermodynamics, this concept is generalized to non-ideal gases and instead called fugacity.

2c21dd92c22c.title: Soil aeration
2c21dd92c22c.sentence: Soil aeration may be artificially enhanced by using mechanized or manual equipment to either puncture the soil with spikes (spike aeration) or remove approximately 1 in × 2 in (25 mm × 51 mm) cores of soil from the ground (core aeration).

7195d61efc9a.title: Soil aeration
7195d61efc9a.sentence: Spike aeration involves the use of an aeration machine with spikes up to a foot or more in length.

ca67008e303b.title: Soil aeration
ca67008e303b.sentence: It is sometimes used to address drainage issues in areas with turf.

31d1d26a4f1d.title: Soil aeration
31d1d26a4f1d.sentence: Core aeration is done on turf areas as a means of reducing turf compaction, reducing thatch buildup, improving the infiltration of water/nutrients, encouraging deeper roots, and creating an environment where grass seed can have direct contact with the soil.

26d4566087f6.title: Soil aeration
26d4566087f6.sentence: There are many types of lawn aerators including walk behind models, ride on versions and tractor pulled versions, as well as spiked shoes.

2014b14bb454.title: Molecular diffusion
2014b14bb454.sentence: Molecular diffusion is the motion of atoms, molecules, or other particles of a gas or liquid at temperatures above absolute zero.

48630c4df6b1.title: Molecular diffusion
48630c4df6b1.sentence: This type of diffusion explains the net flux of molecules from a region of higher concentration to one of lower concentration.

60340f066a10.title: Molecular diffusion
60340f066a10.sentence: The rate of this movement is a function of temperature, viscosity of the fluid, size and density (or their product, mass) of the particles.

478e66546b29.title: Molecular diffusion
478e66546b29.sentence: The result of diffusion is a gradual mixing of material such that the distribution of molecules is uniform.

031316204770.title: Molecular diffusion
031316204770.sentence: Since the molecules are still in motion, but an equilibrium has been established, the result of molecular diffusion is called a "dynamic equilibrium".

dce0c42cc50a.title: Molecular diffusion
dce0c42cc50a.sentence: - Tracer diffusion and Self-diffusion, which is a spontaneous mixing of molecules taking place in the absence of concentration (or chemical potential) gradient.

c293f08169a8.title: Molecular diffusion
c293f08169a8.sentence: - Chemical diffusion occurs in a presence of concentration (or chemical potential) gradient and it results in net transport of mass.

de1dae9a8dbf.title: Molecular diffusion
de1dae9a8dbf.sentence: NA=−DABdCAdx (only applicable for no bulk motion)

762c30967928.title: Molecular diffusion
762c30967928.sentence: where D is the diffusivity of A through B, proportional to the average molecular velocity and, therefore dependent on the temperature and pressure of gases.

cfcd6a08f3c9.title: Molecular diffusion
cfcd6a08f3c9.sentence: Of mass transport mechanisms, molecular diffusion is known as a slower one.

7bde10c42aac.title: Heat capacity
7bde10c42aac.sentence: Heat capacity or thermal capacity is a physical property of matter, defined as the amount of heat that must be supplied to an object to produce a unit change in its temperature.

1ef8224c055f.title: Heat capacity
1ef8224c055f.sentence: The SI unit of heat capacity is joule per kelvin (J/K).

9884548d4e99.title: Heat capacity
9884548d4e99.sentence: The corresponding intensive property is the specific heat capacity, found by dividing the heat capacity of an object by its mass.

05929fc32ded.title: Heat capacity
05929fc32ded.sentence: The volumetric heat capacity measures the heat capacity per volume.

59a919c2e3de.title: Heat capacity
59a919c2e3de.sentence: The value of this parameter usually varies considerably depending on the starting temperature T of the object and the pressure p applied to it.

6c4d8530b49b.title: Heat capacity
6c4d8530b49b.sentence: In particular, it typically varies dramatically with phase transitions such as melting or vaporization (see enthalpy of fusion and enthalpy of vaporization).

575affdff2d8.title: Heat capacity
575affdff2d8.sentence: The heat capacity may be well-defined even for heterogeneous objects, with separate parts made of different materials; such as an electric motor, a crucible with some metal, or a whole building.

6f8f56d49300.title: Heat capacity
6f8f56d49300.sentence: In many cases, the (isobaric) heat capacity of such objects can be computed by simply adding together the (isobaric) heat capacities of the individual parts.

1c9f407ca998.title: Thermal conductivity and resistivity
1c9f407ca998.sentence: In physics, particularly in thermodynamics, the thermal conductivity of a material is a measure of its intrinsic ability to locally conduct heat.

524d65839bcf.title: Thermal conductivity and resistivity
524d65839bcf.sentence: In the International System of Units (SI), thermal conductivity is measured in watts per meter-kelvin [W/(m⋅K)].

5affe2fb1466.title: Thermal conductivity and resistivity
5affe2fb1466.sentence: Thermal conduction is defined as the transport of energy due to random molecular motion across a temperature gradient.

1767307ec8d0.title: Thermal conductivity and resistivity
1767307ec8d0.sentence: It is distinguished from energy transport by convection and molecular work in that it does not involve macroscopic flows or work-performing internal stresses.

ac85b439af55.title: Thermal conductivity and resistivity
ac85b439af55.sentence: According to the second law of thermodynamics, heat flows from high to low temperature.

1166ef7a98eb.title: Thermal conductivity and resistivity
1166ef7a98eb.sentence: Broadly speaking, there are two categories of measurement techniques: steady-state and transient.

218eac815234.title: Thermal conductivity and resistivity
218eac815234.sentence: Steady-state techniques infer the thermal conductivity from measurements on the state of a material once a steady-state temperature profile has been reached, whereas transient techniques operate on the instantaneous state of a system during the approach to steady state.

45d22a9571e5.title: Thermal conductivity and resistivity
45d22a9571e5.sentence: When a material undergoes a phase change (e.g. from solid to liquid), the thermal conductivity may change abruptly.

29f18e6c3496.title: Thermal conductivity and resistivity
29f18e6c3496.sentence: For instance, when ice melts to form liquid water at 0 °C, the thermal conductivity changes from 2.18 W/(m⋅K) to 0.56 W/(m⋅K).

ea357f476a0b.title: Thermal conductivity and resistivity
ea357f476a0b.sentence: In the absence of convection, air and other gases are good insulators.

43d77112c9a2.title: Thermal conductivity and resistivity
43d77112c9a2.sentence: Therefore, many insulating materials function simply by having a large number of gas-filled pockets which obstruct heat conduction pathways.

5b15703ab829.title: Thermal conductivity and resistivity
5b15703ab829.sentence: Some substances, such as non-cubic crystals, can exhibit different thermal conductivities along different crystal axes.

826553f1a922.title: Thermal conductivity and resistivity
826553f1a922.sentence: Wood generally conducts better along the grain than across it.

5b0b9f535eac.title: Greenhouse gas
5b0b9f535eac.section: Contributions of specific gases to the greenhouse effect > Global warming potential (GWP) and CO2 equivalents
5b0b9f535eac.sentence: Global warming potential (GWP) is a measure of how much heat a greenhouse gas (GHG) traps in the atmosphere over a specific time period, relative to carbon dioxide (CO2).

edfa10634944.title: Greenhouse gas
edfa10634944.section: Contributions of specific gases to the greenhouse effect > Global warming potential (GWP) and CO2 equivalents
edfa10634944.sentence: It is a dimensionless quantity expressed as a multiple of warming caused by the same mass of CO2.

e5d573682543.title: Greenhouse gas
e5d573682543.section: Contributions of specific gases to the greenhouse effect > Global warming potential (GWP) and CO2 equivalents
e5d573682543.sentence: Therefore, by definition CO2 has a GWP of 1.

27d4a7ebea99.title: Greenhouse gas
27d4a7ebea99.section: Contributions of specific gases to the greenhouse effect > Global warming potential (GWP) and CO2 equivalents
27d4a7ebea99.sentence: For other gases, it depends on how strongly the gas absorbs thermal radiation, how quickly it leaves the atmosphere, and the time frame considered.

8f8d14b9c829.title: Greenhouse gas
8f8d14b9c829.section: Contributions of specific gases to the greenhouse effect > Global warming potential (GWP) and CO2 equivalents
8f8d14b9c829.sentence: For example, methane (CH4) has a GWP over 20 years (GWP-20) of 81.2 meaning that, a leak of a tonne of methane is equivalent to emitting 81.2 tonnes of CO2, both measured over 20 years.

16553939405b.title: Physical properties of soil
16553939405b.sentence: The specific heat capacity of pure water is ~ 1 calorie per gram, the specific heat capacity of dry soil is ~ 0.2 calories per gram, hence, the specific heat capacity of wet soil is ~ 0.2 to 1 calories per gram (0.8 to 4.2 kJ per kilogram).

a1aded9e1bcb.title: Specific heat capacity
a1aded9e1bcb.sentence: Liquid water has one of the highest specific heat capacities among common substances, about 4184 J⋅kg−1⋅K−1 at 20 °C, but that of ice, just below 0 °C, is only 2093 J⋅kg−1⋅K−1.

aad014e6ba86.title: Specific heat capacity
aad014e6ba86.sentence: The specific heat capacities of iron, granite, and hydrogen gas are about 449 J⋅kg−1⋅K−1, 790 J⋅kg−1⋅K−1, and 14300 J⋅kg−1⋅K−1, respectively.

3107fbee00a4.title: Frost boil
3107fbee00a4.sentence: A frost boil, also known as mud boils, a stony earth circles, frost scars, or mud circles, are small circular mounds of fresh soil material formed by frost action and cryoturbation.

b423eaad0591.title: Frost boil
b423eaad0591.sentence: They are typically 1 to 3 metres in diameter.

2217b597c829.title: Frost boil
2217b597c829.sentence: They are found typically found in periglacial or alpine environments where permafrost is present, and may damage roads and other man-made structures.

07e5f4128faa.title: Frost boil
07e5f4128faa.sentence: Frost boils are amongst the most common features of patterned ground, the pervasive process shaping the topology of soils in periglacial regions.

b88e4157bc09.title: Frost boil
b88e4157bc09.sentence: Frost boils are a type of nonsorted circle, and are characterized from other circles by barren centres of mineral soil and intercircle regions filled with vegetation and peat.

6db92bf50eef.title: Frost boil
6db92bf50eef.sentence: Soil that are silty or loamy, as described above, can hold larger moisture contents.

02c30b4e94ff.title: Frost boil
02c30b4e94ff.sentence: Thus, segregated ice lenses are formed preferentially in these locations.

6bac88ff3aa1.title: Frost boil
6bac88ff3aa1.sentence: The soil thus experiences greater frost heave than surrounding regions, becoming more highly elevated than its surroundings.

4361f311b516.title: Frost boil
4361f311b516.sentence: Over years, soil particles are preferentially transported upwards to form a frost boil.

9bcbc9c7737e.title: Frost boil
9bcbc9c7737e.sentence: Cyroturbation of this type is a slow process, often taking centuries for a single cycle.

d8b0d381a728.title: Frost boil
d8b0d381a728.sentence: The same found that heaving was considerably greater at centers (c. 9.5 mm per day) than margins (c. 1.6 mm per day).

ad30f529571e.title: Frost boil
ad30f529571e.sentence: Measurements conducted on frost boils in Adventdalen, Svalbard has found that the ground subsistence rates at center of frost boils of averaged 8 mm per day during late May but decreased to less than 1 mm per day in mid-July.

72b1007f16a3.title: Linear aeration
72b1007f16a3.sentence: Linear aeration is an aeration process that allows water to penetrate the soil and to be retained in the proper amounts.

1607950104d8.title: Linear aeration
1607950104d8.sentence: Subsequently, grooves are mechanically introduced into the soil profile to facilitate the infiltration of these amendments.

b03605e01b58.title: Linear aeration
b03605e01b58.sentence: In the process of linear aeration, organic amendments are applied directly to the soil surface during fallow periods between planting cycles.

a7789c6fec08.title: Linear aeration
a7789c6fec08.sentence: The grooves are then restored within the same operation, ensuring minimal disturbance to the soil structure and optimizing the integration of organic matter into the root zone.

562d86d8d6e9.title: Linear aeration
562d86d8d6e9.sentence: Additionally, it can also add organic nutrition and soil softeners (such as humus, topsoil, compost, sand or clay) if necessary.

de064202863f.title: Linear aeration
de064202863f.sentence: Linear aeration can help to alleviate excessive water in lawn areas.

3ac6c8893a82.title: Linear aeration
3ac6c8893a82.sentence: - Alleviates soil compaction in heavily traveled areas.

8b1977df4c8a.title: Linear aeration
8b1977df4c8a.sentence: - Reduces disruption of actual turf surface compared to coring or plugs aeration.

a766c824a879.title: Ice segregation
a766c824a879.sentence: Ice segregation is the geological phenomenon produced by the formation of ice lenses, which induce erosion when moisture, diffused within soil or rock, accumulates in a localized zone.

3c10cf2f0ae7.title: Ice segregation
3c10cf2f0ae7.sentence: The ice initially accumulates within small collocated pores or pre-existing cracks, and, as long as the conditions remain favorable, continues to collect in the ice layer or ice lens, wedging the soil or rock apart.

8ffde6d71772.title: Ice segregation
8ffde6d71772.sentence: The basic condition for ice segregation and frost heaving is existence of a region in soil or porous rock which is relatively permeable, is in a temperature range which allows the coexistence of ice and water (in a premelted state), and has a temperature gradient across the region.

637a02c7113c.title: Ice segregation
637a02c7113c.sentence: It grows rapidly until the heat liberated by freezing warms the ice lens boundary, reducing the temperature gradient and controlling the rate of further ice segregation.

f4a779f2e105.title: Ice segregation
f4a779f2e105.sentence: Under these conditions, ice grows in a single layer which gets progressively thicker.

c3afe3fd4ceb.title: Ice segregation
c3afe3fd4ceb.sentence: Hence the area through which the water is diffusing continues to cool until another ice segregation layer forms below the first layer.

d22458e0b03f.title: Ice segregation
d22458e0b03f.sentence: With sustained cold weather, this process can repeat, producing multiple ice layers (ice lenses), all parallel to the surface.

5cf765548812.title: Ice segregation
5cf765548812.sentence: At higher overburden pressures and at relatively warm surface temperatures, ice segregation cannot occur; the liquid present freezes within the pore space, with no bulk ice segregation and no measurable surface deformation or frost damage.

aa2e25f9edbc.title: Ice segregation
aa2e25f9edbc.sentence: However the majority of frost heaving and of bedrock fracture results instead from ice segregation in ice lenses in the near-surface frozen regions.

0de253ae9eef.title: Ice segregation

0caf56abe9ed.title: Goldich dissolution series
0caf56abe9ed.sentence: The Bowen's reaction series dictates that during fractional crystallization, olivine and Ca-plagioclase feldspars are the first to crystallize out of a melt, after which follows pyroxene, amphibole, biotite, Na-plagioglase, orthoclase feldspar, muscovite, and finally, quartz.

57a509d588f1.title: Bowen's reaction series

72326dbeef19.sentence: Felsic rocks tends to have relatively higher proportions of potassium and sodium, which can lead to secondary minerals rich in these ions, including Al-, Na- and K-rich clays such as kaolinite, montmorillonite and illite.

411be4c3a20e.title: Goldich dissolution series
411be4c3a20e.sentence: Experimental work by White and Brantley (2003) highlighted some of the limitations of the Goldich dissolution series, most notably that some variations in weathering rates of different minerals are not as pronounced as Goldich argues.

7e10e7dfa0ef.title: Goldich dissolution series
7e10e7dfa0ef.sentence: However, White and Brantley's experimental results demonstrate that the relative weathering rates of K-feldspar and plagioclase feldspar are quite similar, and mainly moderated by the extent to which the minerals had already been weathered (in an exponentially decreasing function).

b12bc1477483.title: Goldich dissolution series
b12bc1477483.sentence: This demonstrates that the Goldich series may not apply across all kinds of weathering processes, and likewise does not take into account the effect of exponential decay in weathering rate of a surface.

8397a1929483.title: Volcanic glass
8397a1929483.sentence: Volcanic glass is the amorphous (non-crystalline) product of rapidly cooling magma.

fcdff97870ee.title: Volcanic glass
fcdff97870ee.sentence: Volcanic glass is formed when magma is rapidly cooled.

9eeff88a653a.title: Volcanic glass
9eeff88a653a.sentence: Volcanic glass is chemically unstable and gradually breaks down over time.

04aa22a5d242.title: Volcanic glass
04aa22a5d242.sentence: Because it does not have a crystal structure, water can easily react with it.

7e5c62eb694c.title: Volcanic glass
7e5c62eb694c.sentence: This reaction removes some elements from the glass and causes new minerals to form.

823cae641cdd.title: Allophane
823cae641cdd.sentence: Allophane is a weathering or hydrothermal alteration product of volcanic glass and feldspars and sometimes has a composition similar to kaolinite but generally has a molar ratio of Al:Si = 2.

48c91e54de2f.title: Bentonite
48c91e54de2f.sentence: Bentonite usually forms from the weathering of volcanic ash in seawater, or by hydrothermal circulation through the porosity of volcanic ash beds, which converts (devitrification) the volcanic glass (obsidian, a volcanic glass with a chemical composition equivalent to rhyolite) present in the ash into clay minerals.

0cbf60f4e0d4.title: Andosol
0cbf60f4e0d4.sentence: - Vitric – Andosols with limited soil formation, still containing significant amounts of volcanic glasses.

757b29ae088e.title: Duripan
757b29ae088e.sentence: Soils with duripans are often geographically associated with areas of volcanic activity, and show evidence of ash or volcanic glass deposition.

5898d3f6ccf8.title: Glauconite
5898d3f6ccf8.sentence: Glauconite is an iron potassium phyllosilicate (mica group) mineral of characteristic green color which is very friable and has very low weathering resistance.

d3e56bf9adf6.title: Glauconite
d3e56bf9adf6.sentence: At the broadest level, glauconite is an authigenic mineral and forms commonly in marine settings.

27ac93643170.title: Glauconite
27ac93643170.sentence: It is commonly associated with low-oxygen conditions.

c009ea3cfd04.title: Glauconite
c009ea3cfd04.sentence: Normally, glauconite is considered a diagnostic mineral indicative of continental shelf marine depositional environments with slow rates of accumulation and gradational boundaries.

259d204e57de.title: Glauconite
259d204e57de.sentence: Glauconite, a major component of greensand, is a common source of potassium (K+) in plant fertilizers and is also used to adjust soil pH.

532d90cc1a71.title: Potash
532d90cc1a71.sentence: Manure and glauconite (greensand) are low-potassium-content sources that can be profitably transported only short distances to crop fields.

20018d2676f2.title: Konstantin Glinka
20018d2676f2.sentence: In 1896 he completed his Master's Thesis: "Glauconite, its origin, chemical composition and nature of weathering."

16676548e7b4.title: Jarosite
16676548e7b4.sentence: Jarosite is a basic hydrous sulfate of potassium and ferric iron (Fe-III) with a chemical formula of KFe3(SO4)2(OH)6.

87d7bcdd5d08.title: Jarosite
87d7bcdd5d08.sentence: This sulfate mineral is formed in ore deposits by the oxidation of iron sulfides.

04dd71ddb433.title: Jarosite
04dd71ddb433.sentence: Jarosite is often produced as a byproduct during the purification and refining of zinc and is also commonly associated with acid mine drainage and acid sulfate soil environments.

dffd8781b669.title: Jarosite
dffd8781b669.sentence: When jarosite forms from pyrite oxidation in sedimentary clays, the main sources of K+ are illite, a non-swelling clay, or K-feldspar.

1e0ebb58a9a8.title: Soil horizon
1e0ebb58a9a8.section: Horizons and layers according to the World Reference Base for Soil Resources > Suffixes
1e0ebb58a9a8.sentence: - j: Accumulation of jarosite and/or schwertmannite [j like jarosite] (H, O, A, E, B, C).

512436525e8d.title: Jarosite
512436525e8d.sentence: Ferric sulfate and jarosite have been detected by three martian rovers: Spirit, Opportunity and Curiosity.

75333b7f1338.title: Jarosite
75333b7f1338.sentence: These substances are indicative of strongly oxidizing conditions prevailing at the surface of Mars.

47922afe2099.title: Anatase
47922afe2099.sentence: Anatase is a metastable mineral form of titanium dioxide (TiO2) with a tetragonal crystal structure.

2941b429cf3d.title: Anatase
2941b429cf3d.sentence: Three other polymorphs (or mineral forms) of titanium dioxide are known to occur naturally: brookite, akaogiite, and rutile, with rutile being the most common and most stable of the bunch.

ec27d01bfba8.title: Anatase
ec27d01bfba8.sentence: Anatase is metastable at all temperatures and pressures, with rutile being the equilibrium polymorph.

0e08a2689aa6.title: Anatase
0e08a2689aa6.sentence: Nevertheless, anatase is often the first titanium dioxide phase to form in many processes due to its lower surface energy, with a transformation to rutile taking place at elevated temperatures.

f90e38b4ab4f.title: Anatase
f90e38b4ab4f.sentence: Anatase is formed at relatively low temperatures and found in minor concentrations in igneous and metamorphic rocks.

915b09a394aa.title: Anatase
915b09a394aa.sentence: Similar crystals of microscopic size are widely distributed in sedimentary rocks such as sandstones, clays, and slates, from which they may be separated by washing away the lighter constituents of the powdered rock.

5b988fa0c122.title: Anatase
5b988fa0c122.sentence: At temperatures between 550 and about 1000 °C, anatase converts to rutile.

95763333c4d3.title: Anatase
95763333c4d3.sentence: The temperature of this transformation strongly depends on impurities, or dopants, as well as the morphology of the sample.

76a3cd56b241.title: Anatase
76a3cd56b241.sentence: For example, anatase is less hard (5.5–6 vs. 6–6.5 on the Mohs scale) and less dense (specific gravity about 3.9 vs. 4.2) than rutile.

ef83c17100a0.title: Anatase
ef83c17100a0.sentence: Anatase is also optically negative, whereas rutile is optically positive.

c6982562f170.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
c6982562f170.section: SHEET SILICATES: PHYLLOSILICATES > Exchange Capacity and Specific Surface Area
c6982562f170.sentence: The two main differences among the phyllosilicates is their CEC and the amount of reactive surface area are summarized in Table 14.8.

c96d382960ec.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
c96d382960ec.section: SHEET SILICATES: PHYLLOSILICATES > Exchange Capacity and Specific Surface Area
c96d382960ec.sentence: Kaolinite has very little isomorphous substitution and is non-expanding.

1d0d1bfc782f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
1d0d1bfc782f.section: SHEET SILICATES: PHYLLOSILICATES > Exchange Capacity and Specific Surface Area
1d0d1bfc782f.sentence: Consequently, it has a very low CEC and all surface area is associated with the external surfaces of the structure.

0570266263ee.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
0570266263ee.section: SHEET SILICATES: PHYLLOSILICATES > Table 14.8. Ranges of cation exchange capacity (CEC) and internal and external surface area in common phyllosilicates and other colloids. (Adapted from Weil and Brady, 2017)

e284e32df1cf.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
e284e32df1cf.section: SHEET SILICATES: PHYLLOSILICATES > Exchange Capacity and Specific Surface Area
e284e32df1cf.sentence: Hydrous mica/illite and the chlorites have a significant amount of isomorphous substitution; however as their interlayer regions contain either tightly bound K+ or an additional hydroxide layer, respectively, which inhibits layer expansion.

04b779129ba2.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
04b779129ba2.section: SHEET SILICATES: PHYLLOSILICATES > Exchange Capacity and Specific Surface Area
04b779129ba2.sentence: Thus, CEC is limited and the structures are non-expandable.

5adac7fdf3f9.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
5adac7fdf3f9.section: SHEET SILICATES: PHYLLOSILICATES > Table 14.8. Ranges of cation exchange capacity (CEC) and internal and external surface area in common phyllosilicates and other colloids. (Adapted from Weil and Brady, 2017)

b8a23fd5e797.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
b8a23fd5e797.section: SHEET SILICATES: PHYLLOSILICATES > Table 14.8. Ranges of cation exchange capacity (CEC) and internal and external surface area in common phyllosilicates and other colloids. (Adapted from Weil and Brady, 2017)

16c328543375.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
16c328543375.section: SHEET SILICATES: PHYLLOSILICATES > Exchange Capacity and Specific Surface Area
16c328543375.sentence: Smectites have an intermediate amount of isomorphous substitution coupled with the ability to admit exchangeable cations into the interlayer region.

2426aacd2a15.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
2426aacd2a15.section: SHEET SILICATES: PHYLLOSILICATES > Exchange Capacity and Specific Surface Area
2426aacd2a15.sentence: Consequently, both CEC and total surface area is high.

96abd510ecad.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
96abd510ecad.section: SHEET SILICATES: PHYLLOSILICATES > Table 14.8. Ranges of cation exchange capacity (CEC) and internal and external surface area in common phyllosilicates and other colloids. (Adapted from Weil and Brady, 2017)

2b7670b51818.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
2b7670b51818.section: SHEET SILICATES: PHYLLOSILICATES > Exchange Capacity and Specific Surface Area
2b7670b51818.sentence: Soils containing smectites are noted for their high plasticity, cohesion and marked ability to swell when wet and shrink when dried.

ca1547a15b1c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
ca1547a15b1c.section: SHEET SILICATES: PHYLLOSILICATES > Exchange Capacity and Specific Surface Area
ca1547a15b1c.sentence: Vermiculites have more isomorphous substitution compared to smectites and thus have a higher CEC; however, most of the charge in vermiculites is concentrated within the tetrahedral sheets closer to the interlayer region and therefore has a greater electrostatic attraction for exchangeable cations in the interlayer region.

c3c6d7e01a3a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
c3c6d7e01a3a.section: SHEET SILICATES: PHYLLOSILICATES > Exchange Capacity and Specific Surface Area
c3c6d7e01a3a.sentence: As a result, although the total surface area of vermiculite is similar to the smectites, layer expansion of vermiculite structures is limited due to restricted entry of water into the interlayer region.

3a8efa7d8252.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
3a8efa7d8252.section: SHEET SILICATES: PHYLLOSILICATES > Table 14.8. Ranges of cation exchange capacity (CEC) and internal and external surface area in common phyllosilicates and other colloids. (Adapted from Weil and Brady, 2017)

1de8b39e3bc3.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
1de8b39e3bc3.section: SHEET SILICATES: PHYLLOSILICATES > Table 14.8. Ranges of cation exchange capacity (CEC) and internal and external surface area in common phyllosilicates and other colloids. (Adapted from Weil and Brady, 2017)

592c863df118.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
592c863df118.section: SHEET SILICATES: PHYLLOSILICATES > Table 14.8. Ranges of cation exchange capacity (CEC) and internal and external surface area in common phyllosilicates and other colloids. (Adapted from Weil and Brady, 2017)

5feaac0127b1.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
5feaac0127b1.section: MINERALS OF THE SAND-SIZE (2 mm – 0.05 mm) FRACTION > Quartz
5feaac0127b1.sentence: Quartz (SiO2) or more specifically, α-quartz (α-SiO2), is the most common mineral found in Canadian soils, typically accounting for the majority of the sand fraction (Figure 14.3).

34a35109b62c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
34a35109b62c.section: MINERALS OF THE SAND-SIZE (2 mm – 0.05 mm) FRACTION > Quartz
34a35109b62c.sentence: Quartz is a framework silicate (tectosilicate) with all four oxygen atoms in its silica tetrahedrons shared among adjacent Al,Si3 tetrahedra (Figure 14.6).

1c07c6d83ffd.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
1c07c6d83ffd.section: MINERALS OF THE SAND-SIZE (2 mm – 0.05 mm) FRACTION > Quartz
1c07c6d83ffd.sentence: When tetrahedra share all oxygen atoms with adjacent tetrahedra, they form a very strong 3-dimensional framework of Si-O bonds.

cbcc886de710.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
cbcc886de710.section: MINERALS OF THE SAND-SIZE (2 mm – 0.05 mm) FRACTION > Quartz

2e971bbf3f84.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
2e971bbf3f84.section: MINERALS OF THE SAND-SIZE (2 mm – 0.05 mm) FRACTION > Quartz
2e971bbf3f84.sentence: The negative charge of the O atoms is exactly balanced by Si requiring no other bonding ions.

f441ef45d3eb.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
f441ef45d3eb.section: MINERALS OF THE SAND-SIZE (2 mm – 0.05 mm) FRACTION > Quartz
f441ef45d3eb.sentence: The Si-O bonds are very strong covalent bonds, highly resistant to weathering but overall not chemically stable in soil.

fd2e823d2f46.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
fd2e823d2f46.section: MINERALS OF THE SAND-SIZE (2 mm – 0.05 mm) FRACTION > Quartz
fd2e823d2f46.sentence: The solubility of quartz is very low and the rate of weathering (dissolution) is extremely slow.

03c421e6a8e7.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
03c421e6a8e7.section: MINERALS OF THE SAND-SIZE (2 mm – 0.05 mm) FRACTION > Quartz
03c421e6a8e7.sentence: Quartz is, therefore, highly persistent in soil with a slow rate of dissolution compared to most other minerals leading to a far longer persistence, with relative quantities building up over time (e.g., Ae horizons of Podzolic and Luvisolic soils).

15cdcccd4fdb.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
15cdcccd4fdb.section: MINERALS OF THE SAND-SIZE (2 mm – 0.05 mm) FRACTION > Quartz
15cdcccd4fdb.sentence: Quartz usually constitutes about 40-60% of the sand (2.0–0.05 mm) fraction, a major fraction of the silt-size range (0.05-0.002 mm) and is present in small amounts in the clay-size (<0.002 mm) fraction of Canadian soils as well (see Figure 14.3).

c4f78c3a501e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
c4f78c3a501e.sentence: While primary minerals form by geological processes, secondary minerals are a by-product of chemical weathering formed either through the partial chemical alteration of primary minerals or through chemical precipitation from the reaction of components dissolved from other minerals.

08394c02e60e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Soils_Laboratory_Manual_(Moorberg_and_Crouse)/02%3A_Soil_Formation_Classification_and_Mapping/02.1%3A_Soil_Formation
08394c02e60e.sentence: Secondary minerals form from the decomposition products of primary minerals.

7f2ea96dbe29.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Soils_Laboratory_Manual_(Moorberg_and_Crouse)/02%3A_Soil_Formation_Classification_and_Mapping/02.1%3A_Soil_Formation
7f2ea96dbe29.sentence: Primary minerals form during cooling and solidification of the original molten material of the earth’s crust.

91ee6b58cdc9.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/01%3A_Digging_In/1.02%3A_Soil_Genesis
91ee6b58cdc9.section: WEATHERING > Table 2.3. Composition of average igneous rocks and three surface soils of increased weathering: temperate forest soils are the least weathered and tropical forested soils the most weathered. All values reported as percentages. Adapted from H.L. Bohn et al. (1979). Soil Chemistry. John Wiley and Sons, New York.
91ee6b58cdc9.sentence: Most metal oxides are weathering products from primary igneous silicates and are dominant in heavily weathered soils such as those in sub-tropical and tropical areas.

68aa34e6f538.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/01%3A_Digging_In/1.02%3A_Soil_Genesis
68aa34e6f538.section: WEATHERING > Table 2.3. Composition of average igneous rocks and three surface soils of increased weathering: temperate forest soils are the least weathered and tropical forested soils the most weathered. All values reported as percentages. Adapted from H.L. Bohn et al. (1979). Soil Chemistry. John Wiley and Sons, New York.
68aa34e6f538.sentence: These secondary minerals dominate older, more heavily weathered soils outside of Canada.

031471a2f28a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
031471a2f28a.sentence: Most secondary minerals are hydrated aluminosilicates or Fe and Al oxyhydroxides that are stable in soils.

e3e728e44fea.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
e3e728e44fea.sentence: Most hydrated aluminosilicates are classified as phyllosilicates or clay minerals which are the most abundant secondary minerals in Canadian soils.

50162ea781d4.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
50162ea781d4.sentence: Clay minerals are also the most chemically reactive inorganic phases in soils and both the amount and type of clay mineral influence many soil properties including:

25b1d0413420.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
25b1d0413420.section: PRIMARY vs. SECONDARY MINERALS > Can You Dig It!
25b1d0413420.sentence: Although secondary minerals are formed and are stable in soils at the surface of the Earth, the vast majority secondary minerals found in Canadian soils were formed in the distant past, prior to Late Wisconsin glaciation.

b05c3f30ef9e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
b05c3f30ef9e.section: PRIMARY vs. SECONDARY MINERALS > Can You Dig It!
b05c3f30ef9e.sentence: Although secondary minerals continue to form in our soils in response to chemical weathering, the total amounts produced since the last glacial event are very small compared to the amounts re-deposited during many repeated glaciations in the past.

6d67ff840412.title: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy
6d67ff840412.sentence: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS, EDX, EDXS or XEDS), sometimes called energy dispersive X-ray analysis (EDXA or EDAX) or energy dispersive X-ray microanalysis (EDXMA), is an analytical technique used for the elemental analysis or chemical characterization of a sample.

60d187c57beb.title: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy
60d187c57beb.sentence: It relies on an interaction of some source of X-ray excitation and a sample.

5418ea9a38f6.title: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy
5418ea9a38f6.sentence: Its characterization capabilities are due in large part to the fundamental principle that each element has a unique atomic structure allowing a unique set of peaks on its electromagnetic emission spectrum (which is the main principle of spectroscopy).

05039b4a27ac.title: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy
05039b4a27ac.sentence: The incident beam may excite an electron in an inner shell, ejecting it from the shell while creating an electron hole where the electron was.

5ff0ad705d6e.title: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy
5ff0ad705d6e.sentence: An electron from an outer, higher-energy shell then fills the hole, and the difference in energy between the higher-energy shell and the lower energy shell may be released in the form of an X-ray.

d7883f4a6038.title: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy
d7883f4a6038.sentence: As the energies of the X-rays are characteristic of the difference in energy between the two shells and of the atomic structure of the emitting element, EDS allows the elemental composition of the specimen to be measured.

1d7a2968ed30.title: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy
1d7a2968ed30.sentence: Electron beam excitation is used in electron microscopes, scanning electron microscopes (SEM) and scanning transmission electron microscopes (STEM).

337b72b19a28.title: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy
337b72b19a28.sentence: X-ray beam excitation is used in X-ray fluorescence (XRF) spectrometers.

bfe2e2574e47.title: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy
bfe2e2574e47.sentence: WDS has a much finer spectral resolution than EDS.

f02ec6d46eca.title: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy
f02ec6d46eca.sentence: WDS also avoids the problems associated with artifacts in EDS (false peaks, noise from the amplifiers, and microphonics).

b4aa76a03cdc.title: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy
b4aa76a03cdc.sentence: Many elements will have overlapping X-ray emission peaks (e.g., Ti Kβ and V Kα, Mn Kβ and Fe Kα).

51937e046157.title: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy
51937e046157.sentence: The likelihood of an X-ray escaping the specimen, and thus being available to detect and measure, depends on the energy of the X-ray and the composition, amount, and density of material it has to pass through to reach the detector.

ef7ee625fd85.title: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy
ef7ee625fd85.sentence: Because of this X-ray absorption effect and similar effects, accurate estimation of the sample composition from the measured X-ray emission spectrum requires the application of quantitative correction procedures, which are sometimes referred to as matrix corrections.

3687e2c78f9b.title: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy
3687e2c78f9b.sentence: There is a trend towards a newer EDS detector, called the silicon drift detector (SDD).

0bd8efadbadc.title: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy
0bd8efadbadc.sentence: The advantage lies in the extremely low capacitance of this anode, thereby utilizing shorter processing times and allowing very high throughput.

2e9b4a76c402.title: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy
2e9b4a76c402.sentence: - Ability to be stored and operated at relatively high temperatures, eliminating the need for liquid nitrogen cooling.

0d58b46e675d.title: Birnessite
0d58b46e675d.sentence: Birnessite (nominally MnO2·nH2O), also known as δ-MnO2, is a hydrous manganese dioxide mineral with a chemical formula of Na0.7Ca0.3Mn7O14·2.8H2O.

44302d8e747e.title: Birnessite
44302d8e747e.sentence: It is the main manganese mineral species at the Earth's surface, and commonly occurs as fine-grained, poorly crystallized aggregates in soils, sediments, grain and rock coatings (e.g., desert varnish), and marine ferromanganese nodules and crusts.

8c00e8e502ec.title: Birnessite
8c00e8e502ec.sentence: Biological Mn(II) oxidation is generally fast relative to abiotic Mn(II) oxidation processes, and for this reason the majority of natural birnessites is believed to be produced by microorganisms, especially bacteria, but also fungi.

3370979e347d.title: Birnessite
3370979e347d.sentence: The +4 charge deficit of a vacancy can be balanced by a large variety of interlayer cations forming inner-sphere complexes above and below the vacancies (e.g., Ca, Cu, Zn, Pb, Cd, Tl).

74f2ce598fd7.title: Chromium
74f2ce598fd7.sentence: In contrast, trivalent chromium can be oxidized to hexavalent chromium in soils by manganese oxides, such as Mn(III) and Mn(IV) compounds.

0916807d7987.title: Schwertmannite
0916807d7987.sentence: Schwertmannite is an iron-oxyhydroxysulfate mineral with an ideal chemical formula of Fe8O8(OH)6(SO4) · n H2O or Fe3+ 16O 16(OH,SO 4) 12–13·10–12 H 2O.

ed57c734a62c.title: Schwertmannite
ed57c734a62c.sentence: It is an opaque tetragonal mineral typically occurring as brownish yellow encrustations.

65578cfa1a22.title: Schwertmannite
65578cfa1a22.sentence: Schwertmannite (with a distinct "pin cushion" morphology) commonly forms in iron-rich, acidic sulfate waters in the pH-range of 2 – 4.

7a4f55571f70.title: Schwertmannite
7a4f55571f70.sentence: However, it is more commonly reported as an orange precipitate in streams and lakes affected by acid mine drainage.

664b472a2448.title: Schwertmannite
664b472a2448.sentence: Schwertmannite is also known to be central to iron-sulfur geochemistry in acid sulfate soils associated with coastal lowlands.

cf6ef205403b.title: Schwertmannite
cf6ef205403b.sentence: It was first described for an occurrence in Finland in 1994 and named for Udo Schwertmann (born 1927), a soil scientist at the Technical University of Munich, Munich, Germany.

e70d79b71b29.title: Soil carbon
e70d79b71b29.section: Forms of Carbon in Soil > Inorganic Carbon
e70d79b71b29.sentence: Carbonates can originate from the bedrock or parent material from which the soil forms, or can form in situ as pedogenic carbonate.

17b3ae7042fe.title: Soil horizon
17b3ae7042fe.section: Horizons and layers according to the FAO Guidelines for Soil Description (2006) > Subordinate characteristics
17b3ae7042fe.sentence: - k: Accumulation of pedogenic carbonates—no restriction.
