e1d04b1be9ad.title: Phaeozem
e1d04b1be9ad.sentence: A Phaeozem in the World Reference Base for Soil Resources (WRB) is a dark soil with a high base status, but without a secondary carbonates within one metre of the soil surface.

e268b352a09c.title: History of soil science
e268b352a09c.sentence: These processes are subject to quantitative study in soil physics, soil chemistry, soil mineralogy, and soil biology.

f54f2dbe7f6d.title: Botany
f54f2dbe7f6d.sentence: Most of the elements required for plant nutrition come from the chemical breakdown of soil minerals.

f6c634a7b6fb.title: Plant nutrients in soil
f6c634a7b6fb.sentence: As plant roots remove nutrients from the soil water solution, they are replenished as other ions move off of clay and humus (by ion exchange or desorption), are added from the weathering of soil minerals, and are released by the decomposition of soil organic matter.

450d41a05978.title: Soil matrix
450d41a05978.sentence: Many soil minerals, such as gypsum, calcite, feldspar or quartz particles, are small enough to be classified as clay based on their physical size, but chemically they do not afford the same utility as do mineralogically defined clay minerals.

d7af5fbf51b8.title: Phosphorus cycle
d7af5fbf51b8.section: Phosphorus in the environment > Phosphorus cycling
d7af5fbf51b8.sentence: Phosphorus retention by soil minerals (e.g., adsorption onto iron and aluminum oxyhydroxides in acidic soils and precipitation onto calcite in neutral-to-calcareous soils) is usually viewed as the most important process in controlling terrestrial P-bioavailability in the mineral soil.

2cc7a07feefc.title: Dissolved organic carbon
2cc7a07feefc.sentence: Hydrophobic molecules are preferentially partitioned onto soil minerals and have a longer retention time in soils than hydrophilic molecules.

27140b0dcc3d.title: Particulate organic matter
27140b0dcc3d.sentence: Typically it adheres to soil minerals, and plays an important role structuring soil.

2dc142c67fd3.title: Soil salinity
2dc142c67fd3.sentence: Over long periods of time, as soil minerals weather and release salts, these salts are flushed or leached out of the soil by drainage water in areas with sufficient precipitation or under irrigation, or may rise through capillarity and accumulate near the surface under intense evaporation during drought periods.

5e48fe91c151.title: History of soil science
5e48fe91c151.sentence: Meanwhile, advances in soil chemistry, soil physics, soil mineralogy, and soil biology, as well as in the basic sciences that underlie them, have added new tools and new dimensions to the study of soil formation.

b62ff787fffa.title: Powder diffraction
b62ff787fffa.sentence: Powder diffraction is a scientific technique using X-ray, neutron, or electron diffraction on powder or microcrystalline samples for structural characterization of materials.

633d4f8339dc.title: Powder diffraction
633d4f8339dc.sentence: The most widespread use of powder diffraction is in the identification and characterization of crystalline solids, each of which produces a distinctive diffraction pattern.

29fbff96f726.title: Powder diffraction
29fbff96f726.sentence: Both the positions (corresponding to lattice spacings) and the relative intensity of the lines in a diffraction pattern are indicative of a particular phase and material, providing a "fingerprint" for comparison.

971b91d75dca.title: Powder diffraction
971b91d75dca.sentence: A multi-phase mixture, e.g. a soil sample, will show more than one pattern superposed, allowing for the determination of the relative concentrations of phases in the mixture.

49ed8833305f.title: Powder diffraction
49ed8833305f.sentence: - the ability to analyze mixed phases, e.g. soil samples

dcacdfe58c2e.title: Bragg's law
dcacdfe58c2e.sentence: Bragg diffraction occurs when radiation of a wavelength λ comparable to atomic spacings is scattered in a specular fashion (mirror-like reflection) by planes of atoms in a crystalline material, and undergoes constructive interference.

ba7b0076ca47.title: Bragg's law
ba7b0076ca47.sentence: The glancing angle θ (see figure on the right, and note that this differs from the convention in Snell's law where θ is measured from the surface normal), the wavelength λ, and the "grating constant" d of the crystal are connected by the relation:nλ=2dsin⁡θwhere n is the diffraction order (n=1 is first order, n=2 is second order, n=3 is third order).

3a6280ddbc31.title: Bragg's law
3a6280ddbc31.sentence: Bragg diffraction (also referred to as the Bragg formulation of X-ray diffraction) was first proposed by Lawrence Bragg and his father, William Henry Bragg, in 1913 after their discovery that crystalline solids produced surprising patterns of reflected X-rays (in contrast to those produced with, for instance, a liquid).

e2a3e15ed268.title: Powder diffraction
e2a3e15ed268.sentence: The method has been historically used for the identification and classification of minerals, but it can be used for nearly any material, even amorphous ones, so long as a suitable reference pattern is known or can be constructed.

204abc192f45.title: Powder diffraction
204abc192f45.sentence: There are now over 1,047,661 reference materials in the 2021 Powder Diffraction File Databases, and these databases are interfaced to a wide variety of diffraction analysis software and distributed globally.

6f76ed974c9a.title: Powder diffraction
6f76ed974c9a.sentence: It is mostly used to characterize and identify phases, and to refine details of an already known structure, rather than solving unknown structures.

11288fb88381.title: X-ray fluorescence
11288fb88381.sentence: X-ray fluorescence (XRF) is the emission of characteristic "secondary" (or fluorescent) X-rays from a material that has been excited by being bombarded with high-energy X-rays or gamma rays.

6fe6cd47584b.title: X-ray fluorescence
6fe6cd47584b.sentence: By measuring the energy and intensity of these emitted "secondary" X-rays, scientists can identify which elements are present in the sample and in what quantities.

4376df92ee03.title: X-ray fluorescence
4376df92ee03.sentence: Thus, XRF is the basis of a non-destructive analytical technique widely used for elemental analysis and chemical analysis, particularly in the investigation of metals, glass, ceramics and building materials, and for research in geochemistry, forensic science, archaeology and art objects such as paintings.

a8cd77507920.title: X-ray fluorescence
a8cd77507920.section: Energy dispersive spectrometry > Wavelength dispersive spectrometry > Sample preparation
a8cd77507920.sentence: Ways of obtaining sample discs vary: metals may be machined to shape, minerals may be finely ground and pressed into a tablet, and glasses may be cast to the required shape.

1266606d6136.title: X-ray fluorescence
1266606d6136.section: Energy dispersive spectrometry > Wavelength dispersive spectrometry > Extracting analytical results
1266606d6136.sentence: Glasses most closely approach the ideal of homogeneity and isotropy, and for accurate work, minerals are usually prepared by dissolving them in a borate glass, and casting them into a flat disc or "bead".

3f4af0edba56.title: X-ray fluorescence
3f4af0edba56.section: Energy dispersive spectrometry > Wavelength dispersive spectrometry > Extracting analytical results
3f4af0edba56.sentence: When a powder is pressed into a tablet, the finer minerals concentrate at the surface.

a0fbeec5d9ce.title: X-ray fluorescence
a0fbeec5d9ce.section: Energy dispersive spectrometry > Wavelength dispersive spectrometry > Extracting analytical results
a0fbeec5d9ce.sentence: Mixtures of multiple crystalline components in mineral powders can result in absorption effects that deviate from those calculable from theory.

01356224c110.title: Cone penetration test
01356224c110.sentence: Additional tools such as laser-induced fluorescence, X-ray fluorescence, soil conductivity/resistivity, pH, temperature and membrane interface probe and cameras for capturing video imagery are also increasingly advanced in conjunction with the CPT probe.

ff8fa20d413c.title: Electron probe microanalysis
ff8fa20d413c.sentence: Electron probe microanalysis (EPMA), also known as electron probe X-ray microanalysis, electron microprobe analysis (EMPA) or electron probe analysis (EPA) is a microanalytical and imaging technique used to non-destructively determine the chemical element composition of small volumes of solid materials.

b906bd3163b7.title: Electron probe microanalysis
b906bd3163b7.sentence: In EPMA, the instrument bombards the sample with a high-intensity electron beam, which then emits X-rays.

594865470c7c.title: Electron probe microanalysis
594865470c7c.sentence: The X-ray wavelengths emitted are characteristic of particular chemical elements and are analyzed using X-ray spectroscopy.

12a44f718382.title: Electron probe microanalysis
12a44f718382.sentence: The same principle is also employed in wavelength- or energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (WDX, EDX) commonly used in scanning electron microscopes (SEM), but EPMA is characterized by a fixed electron beam rather than a scanning one and primarily used for elemental analysis rather than imaging.

8211e66b477e.title: Electron probe microanalysis
8211e66b477e.sentence: This technique is most commonly used by mineralogists and petrologists.

3481c0209b3a.title: Electron probe microanalysis
3481c0209b3a.sentence: Variations in chemical composition within a material (zoning), such as a mineral grain or metal, can be readily determined.

6c1edee95ec1.title: Electron probe microanalysis
6c1edee95ec1.sentence: The change in elemental composition from the center (also known as core) to the edge (or rim) of a mineral can yield information about the history of the crystal's formation, including the temperature, pressure, and chemistry of the surrounding medium.

873b240c7514.title: Tephrochronology
873b240c7514.sentence: Effective tephrochronology requires accurate geochemical fingerprinting (usually via an electron microprobe).

45846efd3723.title: Electron probe microanalysis
45846efd3723.sentence: This restricts WDS when analyzing geologically important elements such as H, Li, and Be.

d966256b948d.title: Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy
d966256b948d.sentence: Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) is a technique used to obtain an infrared spectrum of absorption or emission of a solid, liquid, or gaseous material.

352bbec671c4.title: Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy
352bbec671c4.sentence: An FTIR spectrometer collects high-resolution spectral data over a wide spectral range, from the near- to far-IR region.

adf2bafabd10.title: Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy
adf2bafabd10.sentence: The term Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy originates from the fact that a Fourier transform (a mathematical process) is required to convert the raw data into the actual spectrum.

a4d4ff378f6c.title: Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy
a4d4ff378f6c.section: Applications > Volatile content determination in geological materials
a4d4ff378f6c.sentence: FTIR spectroscopy is often used in geology to quantify volatile species, H2O and CO2, in minerals, glasses, and melt inclusions.

03b0147ce96f.title: Allophane
03b0147ce96f.sentence: Since it has short-range atomic order, it is a mineraloid, rather than a mineral, and can be identified by its distinctive infrared spectrum and its X-ray diffraction pattern.

8df755f8d7c6.title: Clay mineral
8df755f8d7c6.sentence: In addition to X-ray crystallography, these include electron diffraction methods, various spectroscopic methods such as Mössbauer spectroscopy, infrared spectroscopy, Raman spectroscopy, and SEM-EDS or automated mineralogy processes.

bf730dc640c8.title: Variscite
bf730dc640c8.sentence: Variscite is a relatively rare hydrated aluminium phosphate mineral (AlPO4·2H2O).

4245648a54ae.title: Variscite
4245648a54ae.sentence: Variscite is a secondary mineral formed by direct deposition from phosphate-bearing water which has reacted with aluminium-rich rocks in a near-surface environment.

dfeae35cafd5.title: Variscite
dfeae35cafd5.sentence: It occurs as fine-grained masses in nodules, cavity fillings, and crusts.

c716b957c331.title: Variscite
c716b957c331.sentence: Variscite often contains white veins of the calcium aluminium phosphate mineral crandallite.

8e15d1acd2ad.title: Variscite
8e15d1acd2ad.sentence: The green color results from the presence of small amounts of trivalent chromium (Cr3+).

d788f86289da.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
d788f86289da.section: DISTRIBUTION OF PHYLLOSILICATES IN CANADIAN SOILS
d788f86289da.sentence: The distribution of phyllosilicates in Canadian soil varies somewhat by physiographic region (Kodama, 1979); most phyllosilicates are inherited from the parent materials deposited by the retreat of the continental glaciers during the late Pleistocene.

7bfe919889d1.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
7bfe919889d1.section: DISTRIBUTION OF PHYLLOSILICATES IN CANADIAN SOILS
7bfe919889d1.sentence: For example, some clay minerals such as kaolinite, mica, (i.e., biotite and muscovite) and chlorite are inherited directly from the Canadian Shield.

be7b29b2d9d2.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
be7b29b2d9d2.section: DISTRIBUTION OF PHYLLOSILICATES IN CANADIAN SOILS
be7b29b2d9d2.sentence: Others in the Cordilleran region and Interior Plains Regions are derived from glacial degradation of sediments from the Cretaceous period (65 million years ago).

19dbefccd3cf.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
19dbefccd3cf.section: DISTRIBUTION OF PHYLLOSILICATES IN CANADIAN SOILS
19dbefccd3cf.sentence: The Interior Plains region of western Canada is commonly reported to contain smectite, clay-size mica, chlorite and some kaolinite, (Kodama, 1979; Dudas and Pawluk, 1982; Spiers et al. 1989a; Spiers et al. 1989b; Warren and Dudas, 1992).

14de3d36d21a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
14de3d36d21a.section: DISTRIBUTION OF PHYLLOSILICATES IN CANADIAN SOILS
14de3d36d21a.sentence: In contrast, the clay-size fraction of soils from the Western St. Lawrence Lowlands (Ontario) derived from much older sediments formed during the Devonian (359 million) and Silurian (443 million) periods and are dominated by clay-size mica, chlorite, vermiculite and kaolinite with some reports of traces of smectite (Kodama, 1979).

1191af7fdc37.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
1191af7fdc37.section: DISTRIBUTION OF PHYLLOSILICATES IN CANADIAN SOILS
1191af7fdc37.sentence: There is only weak evidence of alteration in the diverse clay mineral assemblages from the various physiographic regions and correlation is futile between generic types of soil.

f28a414c6481.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
f28a414c6481.section: DISTRIBUTION OF PHYLLOSILICATES IN CANADIAN SOILS
f28a414c6481.sentence: An exception is the Podzolic soils and to a lesser extent Brunisolic and Gleysolic soils where inherited chlorite minerals appear to weather to expandable phyllosilicates (Kodama, 1979).

7b85bb011511.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
7b85bb011511.sentence: Phosphate can easily combine with about 30 different elements forming over 300 minerals that contain P (Bleam, 2017).

1897c233e6fe.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
1897c233e6fe.sentence: The most common “pure” primary phosphate minerals are referred to by the group name “apatite” and given the general chemical formula: Ca5(PO4)3(F,Cl,OH).

36e60e07281b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
36e60e07281b.sentence: The average crustal abundance of P is reported as 1050 mg kg-1, while the total content of P in soils is typically in the range of 400–800 mg kg-1.

0efe40d440ca.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
0efe40d440ca.sentence: Names for specific mineral for the three common end members of apatite are as follows:

52ca39cccda0.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
52ca39cccda0.sentence: Rock phosphate or phosphorite generally contains the highest concentration of these minerals and is mined mostly for the production of phosphate fertilizers.

c8163c9444f2.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
c8163c9444f2.sentence: Generally phosphate in soil reacts readily with Ca2+, Al3+, and Fe2+ and Fe3+ forming a variety of secondary precipitates (Table 14.12).

fdfff67d279c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
fdfff67d279c.sentence: This includes phosphate derived from primary mineral sources and phosphate fertilizers.

8a8a30c92e1b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
8a8a30c92e1b.sentence: Iron phosphates (vivianite and strengite) are more common in sub-oxic soils where dissolved iron is more plentiful.

ed09c318b687.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
ed09c318b687.sentence: Aluminum phosphates (varisite) are most often associated with acidic soils where phosphate first precipitates as an amorphous intermediate that eventually transforms into varisite (Lindsay et al., 1959).

13731c85d52e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
13731c85d52e.sentence: Secondary calcium phosphates generally occur in calcareous soils containing limestone (mineral calcite) as a calcium source (Kar et al., 2012).

414aa5085763.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
414aa5085763.sentence: Secondary brushite is commonly precipitated in calcareous soils as a result of placing high concentrations of fertilizer in bands for crop production (McLaughlin et al., 2011).

27b4a40999d9.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
27b4a40999d9.sentence: Once brought to the Earth’s surface most primary minerals are not chemically stable.

4667661849df.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
4667661849df.sentence: Primary minerals weather and dissolve at different rates.

47b0065c1ec6.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
47b0065c1ec6.sentence: Although they persist in our soils, given enough geological time they will eventually succumb to the biogeochemical processes of the environment and gradually release their elemental components to the environment.

44b2dcd22149.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
44b2dcd22149.sentence: Generally, minerals containing Na, and K dissolve faster than those containing Ca and Mg, which in turn dissolve faster than minerals composed of Si, Al, and Fe.

57178c148735.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
57178c148735.sentence: Under reducing (absence of oxygen) conditions, Fe tends to be soluble and present as the Fe2+ ion.

81c1ac3b7b08.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
81c1ac3b7b08.sentence: Under oxidizing conditions, Fe2+ reacts with oxygen (oxidized) to form Fe3+ ions which in turn form insoluble oxyhydroxide minerals (effectively the composition of rust).

d21979a9e9b7.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
d21979a9e9b7.sentence: Carbonate minerals (principally CaCO3) are formed or dissolved depending on the pH of their bearing solution.

6a6b8ad17c73.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
6a6b8ad17c73.sentence: They precipitate under alkaline conditions and are dissolved under acid conditions.

6a15e46820f5.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
6a15e46820f5.sentence: Atmospheric CO2 reacts with the water to produce a weak acid (H2CO3) that dissolves carbonate (and other rock types).

a0926a7f594e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
a0926a7f594e.sentence: Deeper groundwater tends to be alkaline thus favouring precipitation of carbonate typically found deeper in soil profiles (C horizons).

949bf1e5542a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
949bf1e5542a.sentence: The majority of soil carbonates originate from primary sources, being inherited from sedimentary rocks, and some are secondary precipitates usually found in subsurface horizons.

bb1f7d691889.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
bb1f7d691889.sentence: There are about 80 known carbonate minerals; however, by far most common carbonate minerals found in Canadian soils are calcite (CaCO3) and dolomite ((Ca,Mg)CO3) derived primarily from Paleozoic bedrock.

37efba273fe9.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
37efba273fe9.sentence: Calcite is sparingly soluble, but solubility increases at lower soil pH values and is not usually found in soils with pH values less than 6.0.

a177dcd1d72d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
a177dcd1d72d.sentence: Calcite typically dissolves from the solum and is leached to become re-deposited in the lower soil profile, sometimes observed as secondary calcite nodules (Miller et al., 1987; Wang and Anderson, 2000).

c5e20a9914b9.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
c5e20a9914b9.section: CARBONATES > Table 14.11. Some common carbonate minerals
c5e20a9914b9.sentence: Like calcite, dolomite dissolves from the upper profile, contributing calcium to the precipitation of secondary calcite in the lower profile while the magnesium component is mostly leached or absorbed by plant roots.

c49443ef3a33.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
c49443ef3a33.sentence: Aragonite and other calcium carbonate minerals are neither common nor stable in soils.

5b81d5a6b492.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
5b81d5a6b492.section: CARBONATES > Table 14.11. Some common carbonate minerals
5b81d5a6b492.sentence: Trona | Na 2 CO 3 | Highly soluble in soil. Found mostly in Solonetzic soils at high pH (~9.5)

1e572990263d.section: CARBONATES > Table 14.11. Some common carbonate minerals
1e572990263d.sentence: Carbonates impart a number of properties to soil that include:

a426802adf17.section: CARBONATES > Table 14.11. Some common carbonate minerals

2a78dc1b4051.sentence: - maintaining high exchangeable Ca and Mg;

071e8ce15ba5.section: CARBONATES > Table 14.11. Some common carbonate minerals

3bdfb6f5eb79.sentence: - adsorbing/precipitating metals (e.g., Al, Zn, Pb, Fe, Ni, Mn); and,

be40135d0ab4.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
be40135d0ab4.section: CARBONATES > Table 14.11. Some common carbonate minerals

451f96ff2bd9.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
451f96ff2bd9.sentence: Sulphide minerals are not present in well to imperfectly drained soils but may found in some poorly drained Gleysolic or Organic soils.

99dc4378b878.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
99dc4378b878.sentence: The sulphide mineral pyrite (FeS2) is very common primary mineral in mine wastes but can occur in shales (a sedimentary rock contributing to some soils) and as a precipitate in some tidal soils in response to highly reducing conditions.

3fa30f63fb35.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
3fa30f63fb35.sentence: Pyrite once exposed to the atmosphere is easily oxidized releasing iron and sulphuric acid:

e3a4c33bd242.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
e3a4c33bd242.sentence: Soil pH values less than 2.0 may result from the oxidation of sulphides.

9e21c8e2d5a3.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
9e21c8e2d5a3.sentence: Anthropogenic exposition of sulfide minerals during mining operations or other excavations is primarily responsible for acid rock drainage (ARD).

7581505b202c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.01%3A_Soil_Mineralogy
7581505b202c.sentence: Sulphate derived from the oxidation of sulphides or other sources form gypsum (Table 14.13) usually in response to high pH and the presence of soluble Ca.

79735befb52b.title: Dithionite
79735befb52b.sentence: Dithionite is used in conjunction with complexing agents (for example, citric acid) to reduce iron(III) oxy-hydroxide into soluble iron(II) compounds and to remove amorphous iron(III)-bearing mineral phases in soil analyses (selective extraction).

2a28592f904b.title: Ammonium oxalate
2a28592f904b.sentence: Acid ammonium oxalate (ammonium oxalate acidified to pH 3 with oxalic acid) is commonly employed in soil chemical analysis to extract iron and aluminium from poorly-crystalline minerals (such as ferrihydrite), iron(II)-bearing minerals (such as magnetite) and organic matter.

2c5af7a29e59.title: Dithionite
2c5af7a29e59.sentence: At pH 7, its reduction potential is −0.66 V vs SHE.

7fca0935b4bd.title: Heavy mineral
7fca0935b4bd.sentence: In geology, a heavy mineral is a mineral with a density that is greater than 2.9 g/cm3, most commonly referring to dense components of siliciclastic sediments.

a8a6ee164ac3.title: Sandstone
a8a6ee164ac3.sentence: Common heavy minerals include zircon, tourmaline, rutile (hence ZTR), garnet, magnetite, or other dense, resistant minerals derived from the source rock.

52b2e3828c01.title: Sandstone
52b2e3828c01.sentence: These heavy minerals are commonly resistant to weathering and can be used as an indicator of sandstone maturity through the ZTR index.

cefaed7ce042.title: Heavy mineral
cefaed7ce042.sentence: A heavy mineral suite is the relative percentages of heavy minerals in a stone.

2f8f28653b56.title: Heavy mineral
2f8f28653b56.sentence: Heavy mineral suites are used to help determine the provenance and history of sedimentary rocks.

994cc8774e87.title: Heavy mineral
994cc8774e87.sentence: As heavy minerals are a minor constituent of most sedimentary rock, they must be separated out to be studied.

49eb9b5e8fd8.title: Heavy mineral
49eb9b5e8fd8.sentence: Heavy mineral separation generally uses a dense liquid in either a separatory funnel or centrifuge.

cf720cd2d263.title: Heavy mineral
cf720cd2d263.sentence: Liquids used include bromoform, tetrabromoethane, tribromoethane, methylene iodide, and polytungstate liquids.

98fb9c26eb81.title: Environmental magnetism
98fb9c26eb81.sentence: Environmental magnetism is the study of magnetism as it relates to the effects of climate, sediment transport, pollution and other environmental influences on magnetic minerals.

6526e0d6b996.title: Environmental magnetism
6526e0d6b996.sentence: The magnetic properties of minerals are used as proxies for environmental change in applications such as paleoclimate, paleoceanography, studies of the provenance of sediments, pollution and archeology.

5998751a52f8.title: Environmental magnetism
5998751a52f8.sentence: The main contributors to the magnetic properties of rocks are the iron oxides, including magnetite, maghemite, hematite; and iron sulfides (particularly greigite and pyrrhotite).

a3b1f23a4da6.title: Environmental magnetism
a3b1f23a4da6.sentence: Several parameters such as magnetic susceptibility and various kinds of remanence have been developed to represent certain features of the hysteresis.

bcb17686a63a.title: Environmental magnetism
bcb17686a63a.sentence: These parameters are then used to estimate mineral size and composition.

cecea61f6536.title: Environmental magnetism
cecea61f6536.sentence: The main advantages of using magnetic measurements are that magnetic minerals are almost ubiquitous and magnetic measurements are quick and non-invasive.

6ee99c9e88c9.title: Environmental magnetism
6ee99c9e88c9.sentence: In north-central China, blankets of loess that were deposited during glacial periods alternate with paleosols (fossil soils) that formed during warmer and wetter interglacials.

902b3db232ce.title: Environmental magnetism
902b3db232ce.sentence: The magnetic susceptibility profiles of these sediments have been dated using magnetostratigraphy, which identifies geomagnetic reversals, and correlated with climate indicators such as oxygen isotope stages.

8caafcfa79bc.title: Environmental magnetism
8caafcfa79bc.sentence: Ultimately, this work allowed environmental magnetists to map out the variations in the monsoon cycle during the Quaternary.

5d18cb3481af.title: Chernozem
5d18cb3481af.sentence: Soil magnetism increases when soil minerals goethite and ferrihydrite convert to maghemite on exposure to heat.

ebaca1880098.title: Strengite
ebaca1880098.sentence: Strengite is a relatively rare iron phosphate mineral with the formula: FePO4·2H2O.

1d34248c587f.title: Strengite
1d34248c587f.sentence: Lavender, pink or purple in hue, it is similar to variscite and is partially soluble, particularly in conditions where there is a low pH and low oxidation-reduction potential.

5e84487701cf.title: Strengite
5e84487701cf.sentence: The mineral is named after the German mineralogist Johann August Streng [de] (1830–1897).

61a209462b85.title: Soil chemistry
61a209462b85.sentence: Soil chemistry is the study of the chemical characteristics of soil.

6c0466151bbb.title: Soil chemistry
6c0466151bbb.sentence: Soil chemistry is affected by mineral composition, organic matter and environmental factors.

199df23b01e4.title: Soil chemistry
199df23b01e4.sentence: In the early 1870s a consulting chemist to the Royal Agricultural Society in England, named J. Thomas Way, performed many experiments on how soils exchange ions, and is considered the father of soil chemistry.

9c201c86ec79.title: Soil chemistry
9c201c86ec79.sentence: Until the late 1960s, soil chemistry focused primarily on chemical reactions in the soil that contribute to pedogenesis or that affect plant growth.

bb837d1248b8.title: Soil chemistry
bb837d1248b8.sentence: Since then, concerns have grown about environmental pollution, organic and inorganic soil contamination and potential ecological health and environmental health risks.

33c18b755a0a.title: Soil chemistry
33c18b755a0a.sentence: Consequently, the emphasis in soil chemistry has shifted from pedology and agricultural soil science to an emphasis on environmental soil science.

94d5ab6fb901.title: Soil chemistry
94d5ab6fb901.sentence: - The mineral components of the soil are derived from the parental rocks or regolith.

cf84b797b3c9.title: Soil chemistry
cf84b797b3c9.sentence: The minerals present about 90% of the total weight of the soil.

5be39afc8eef.title: Soil chemistry
5be39afc8eef.sentence: Plants play a role in soil chemistry by exchanging nutrients with microorganisms and absorbing nutrients, creating concentration gradients of cations and anions.

0fa5cc87f710.title: Soil chemistry
0fa5cc87f710.sentence: Many plant nutrients in soil undergo biogeochemical cycles throughout their environment.

d671c1ef04ee.title: Soil chemistry
d671c1ef04ee.sentence: For example, nitrogen moves from an isolated gaseous form to the compounds nitrate and nitrite as it moves through soil and becomes available to plants.

52573197c12a.title: Soil chemistry
52573197c12a.sentence: In comparison, an element like phosphorus transfers in mineral form, as it is contained in rock material.

b32eff685acb.title: Edaphology
b32eff685acb.section: Areas of study > Agricultural soil science
b32eff685acb.sentence: Agricultural soil science is the application of soil chemistry, physics, and biology dealing with the production of crops.

5fbb581c3338.title: Edaphology
5fbb581c3338.section: Areas of study > Agricultural soil science
5fbb581c3338.sentence: In terms of soil chemistry, it places particular emphasis on plant nutrients of importance to farming and horticulture, especially with regard to soil fertility and fertilizer components.

c1b49a8fd77c.title: Clay mineral
c1b49a8fd77c.sentence: Clay minerals are hydrous aluminium phyllosilicates (e.g. kaolin, Al2Si2O5(OH)4), sometimes with variable amounts of iron, magnesium, alkali metals, alkaline earths, and other cations found on or near some planetary surfaces.

93971630af20.title: Clay mineral
93971630af20.sentence: Clay particles were found to be predominantly sheet silicate (phyllosilicate) minerals, now grouped together as clay minerals.

c260debd4268.title: Clay mineral
c260debd4268.sentence: Clay minerals form in the presence of water and have been important to life, and many theories of abiogenesis involve them.

bbd54daeecdc.title: Clay mineral
bbd54daeecdc.sentence: Clay minerals are very common in soils, in fine-grained sedimentary rocks such as shale, mudstone, and siltstone and in fine-grained metamorphic slate and phyllite.

f7082a9e48df.title: Clay mineral
f7082a9e48df.sentence: Their structure is based on flat hexagonal sheets similar to those of the mica group of minerals.

d778449b6bc1.title: Clay mineral
d778449b6bc1.sentence: The chemistry of clay, including its capacity to retain nutrient cations such as potassium and ammonium, is important to soil fertility.

28e55e62c55c.title: Cation-exchange capacity
28e55e62c55c.sentence: Cation-exchange capacity arises from various negative charges on soil particle surfaces, especially those of clay minerals and soil organic matter.

552e78249775.title: Soil matrix
552e78249775.sentence: Most clays are crystalline, but some clays or some parts of clay minerals are amorphous.

fd8a06e21c5e.title: Soil matrix
fd8a06e21c5e.sentence: The clays of a soil are a mixture of the various types of clay, but one type often predominates according to soil type.

766e1570aaba.title: Clay mineral
766e1570aaba.sentence: The crystallographic structure of clay minerals became better understood in the 1930s with advancements in the x-ray diffraction (XRD) technique indispensable to deciphering their crystal lattice.

15c007b7f0f3.title: Clay mineral
15c007b7f0f3.sentence: Given the requirement of water, clay minerals are relatively rare in the Solar System, though they occur extensively on Earth where water has interacted with other minerals and organic matter.

f9e9434a3797.title: Clay mineral
f9e9434a3797.sentence: Clay minerals have been detected at several locations on Mars, including Echus Chasma, Mawrth Vallis, the Memnonia quadrangle and the Elysium quadrangle.

c90b1c23a690.title: Clay mineral
c90b1c23a690.sentence: Spectrography has confirmed their presence on celestial bodies including the dwarf planet Ceres, asteroid 101955 Bennu, and comet Tempel 1, as well as Jupiter's moon Europa.

646eb2ed9b81.title: Mica
646eb2ed9b81.sentence: Micas (/ˈmaɪkəz/) are a group of silicate minerals whose outstanding physical characteristic is that individual mica crystals can easily be split into fragile elastic plates.

ae0b753b9601.title: Mica
ae0b753b9601.sentence: This characteristic is described as perfect basal cleavage.

65ef556c1b00.title: Mica
65ef556c1b00.sentence: The mica group comprises 37 phyllosilicate minerals.

1ce544e24e3f.title: Mineral
1ce544e24e3f.sentence: Common examples of micas are muscovite, and the biotite series.

c24ff9b4a479.title: Mica
c24ff9b4a479.sentence: The crystal structure of mica is described as TOT-c, meaning that it is composed of parallel TOT layers weakly bonded to each other by cations (c).

5e3d73d89ee0.title: Mica
5e3d73d89ee0.sentence: The TOT layers in turn consist of two tetrahedral sheets (T) strongly bonded to the two faces of a single octahedral sheet (O).

d84fe79b1b2d.title: Mica
d84fe79b1b2d.sentence: The relatively weak ionic bonding between TOT layers gives mica its perfect basal cleavage.

6d6ded70ad1c.title: Mica
6d6ded70ad1c.sentence: In most micas, one in four silicon ions is replaced by an aluminium ion, while aluminium ions replace half the silicon ions in brittle micas.

f553c6ffff71.title: Mica
f553c6ffff71.sentence: The remaining negative charge of the TOT layer is neutralized by the interlayer cations (typically sodium, potassium, or calcium ions).

c12d59608723.title: Mica
c12d59608723.sentence: The octahedral sheet can be dioctahedral or trioctahedral.

4d160ba41dbe.title: Mica
4d160ba41dbe.sentence: A trioctahedral sheet has the structure of a sheet of the mineral brucite, with magnesium or ferrous iron being the most common cation.

a452a8019295.title: Mica
a452a8019295.sentence: A dioctahedral sheet has the structure and (typically) the composition of a gibbsite sheet, with aluminium being the cation.

f9e5b3526d9c.title: Mica
f9e5b3526d9c.sentence: Very fine-grained micas, which typically show more variation in ion and water content, are informally termed "clay micas".

607b9afaa0c7.title: Mica
607b9afaa0c7.sentence: - Illite with a K deficiency in the X site and correspondingly more Si in the Z site;

49ed30e61a38.title: Mica
49ed30e61a38.sentence: Mica is common in igneous and metamorphic rock and is occasionally found as small flakes in sedimentary rock.

598332e416d1.title: Illite
598332e416d1.sentence: Illite occurs as an altered product of muscovite and feldspar in weathering and hydrothermal environments; it may be a component of sericite.

68b34629655f.title: Dickite
68b34629655f.sentence: Dickite and other kaolin minerals are commonly developed by weathering of feldspars and muscovite.

369c9ac7c8ae.title: Goethite
369c9ac7c8ae.sentence: Goethite (/ˈɡɜːrtaɪt/, US also /ˈɡoʊθaɪt/) is a mineral of the diaspore group, consisting of iron(III) oxide-hydroxide, specifically the α-polymorph.

9df666c9b1fb.title: Goethite
9df666c9b1fb.sentence: Goethite is an iron oxyhydroxide containing ferric iron.

342865e6ae14.title: Goethite
342865e6ae14.sentence: It is found in soil and other low-temperature environments such as sediment.

a3ce13ea20f7.title: Goethite
a3ce13ea20f7.sentence: Goethite often forms through the weathering of other iron-rich minerals, and thus is a common component of soils, concentrated in laterite soils.

065c0c5139d3.title: Laterite
065c0c5139d3.sentence: Two types of laterite can be identified; both types consist of the minerals kaolinite, quartz, hematite and goethite.

c8bcf78ac346.title: Goethite
c8bcf78ac346.sentence: The formation of goethite is marked by the oxidation state change of Fe2+ (ferrous) to Fe3+ (ferric), which allows for goethite to exist at surface conditions.

4b03e42b22a9.title: Goethite
4b03e42b22a9.sentence: As iron-bearing minerals are brought to the zone of oxidation within the soil, the iron turns from iron(II) to iron(III), while the original shape of the parent mineral is retained.

a608708a8ee7.title: Goethite
a608708a8ee7.sentence: Because of this oxidation state change, goethite is commonly seen as a pseudomorph.

f0a1487138e7.title: Goethite
f0a1487138e7.sentence: It is the main component of rust and bog iron ore.

11505499d0d7.title: Goethite
11505499d0d7.sentence: It is frequently encountered in the swampy areas at the head of spring waters ('bog iron'), on cave floors, and on the bottom of lakes and small creeks.

fbf11efec0e7.title: Goethite
fbf11efec0e7.sentence: Color | Yellowish to reddish to dark brown or black

048aed91e9c1.title: Soil matrix
048aed91e9c1.section: Mineral colloids: soil clays > Sesquioxide clays
048aed91e9c1.sentence: Such soils range from yellow to red in colour according to the dominance of various iron oxides.

0e398d55235d.title: Soil matrix
0e398d55235d.section: Mineral colloids: soil clays > Sesquioxide clays
0e398d55235d.sentence: Such clays tend to hold phosphorus so tightly that it is unavailable for absorption by plants, in proportion to their content in goethite.

138f0d92d5a3.title: Goethite
138f0d92d5a3.sentence: Goethite has also been found to be produced by the excretion processes of certain bacteria types.

684ebf5b2a3a.title: Goethite
684ebf5b2a3a.sentence: Goethite has been well known since ancient times for its use as a pigment (brown ochre).

4d3cea584b58.title: Goethite
4d3cea584b58.sentence: It was first described in 1806 based on samples found in the Hollertszug Mine in Herdorf, Germany.

7182470bf24b.title: Goethite
7182470bf24b.sentence: The mineral was named after the German polymath and poet Johann Wolfgang von Goethe (1749–1832).

59c77680a00f.title: Diatomaceous earth
59c77680a00f.sentence: Diatomaceous earth (/ˌdaɪ.ətəˈmeɪʃəs/ DY-ə-tə-MAY-shəs), also known as diatomite (/daɪˈætəmaɪt/ dy-AT-ə-myte), celite, or kieselgur, is a naturally occurring, soft, siliceous sedimentary rock that can be crumbled into a fine white to off-white powder.

d66cd0b545c4.title: Diatomaceous earth
d66cd0b545c4.sentence: Diatomaceous earth consists of the fossilized remains of diatoms that accumulated over millions of years.

5f4077e14c9e.title: Diatomaceous earth
5f4077e14c9e.sentence: Diatomite forms by the accumulation of the amorphous silica (opal, SiO2·nH2O) remains of dead diatoms (microscopic single-celled algae) in lake sediment or marine sediments.

2fe185f7d5ba.title: Diatomaceous earth
2fe185f7d5ba.sentence: It is usually composed of 80% to 90% silica, 2% to 4% alumina minerals, and 0.5% to 2% iron oxide, although the precise composition of every deposit is different.

0b3485969274.title: Diatomaceous earth
0b3485969274.sentence: It has a particle size ranging from more than 3 mm to less than 1 μm, but typically 10 to 200 μm.

f8eac7717e65.title: Diatomaceous earth
f8eac7717e65.sentence: Depending on the granularity, this powder can have an abrasive feel, like that of pumice powder, and has a low density as a result of its high porosity.

fff00c2d3a8d.title: Soil horizon
fff00c2d3a8d.section: Horizons and layers according to the FAO Guidelines for Soil Description (2006) > Master horizons and layers
fff00c2d3a8d.sentence: L layers include coprogenous earth or sedimentary peat (mostly organic), diatomaceous earth (mostly siliceous), and marl (mostly calcareous).

f12fb240e15a.title: Diatomaceous earth
f12fb240e15a.sentence: In vegetable gardening it is sometimes used as a soil conditioner, because like perlite, vermiculite, and expanded clay, it retains water and nutrients, while draining fast and freely, allowing high oxygen circulation within the growing medium.

a70b78127961.title: Diatomaceous earth
a70b78127961.sentence: It is also used as a growing medium in potted plants, particularly as bonsai soil.

e30ab631319e.title: Colloid
e30ab631319e.sentence: A colloid is a mixture in which one substance, consisting of microscopically dispersed insoluble particles, is suspended throughout another substance.

1012fc2e11c2.title: Colloid
1012fc2e11c2.sentence: A colloid has a dispersed phase (the suspended particles) and a continuous phase (the medium of suspension).

8f20ce10dbdd.title: Colloid
8f20ce10dbdd.sentence: > The term colloidal refers to a state of subdivision, implying that the molecules or polymolecular particles dispersed in a medium have at least in one direction a dimension roughly between 1 nanometre and 1 micrometre, or that in a system discontinuities are found at distances of that order.

38590ba0e699.title: Colloid
38590ba0e699.sentence: It is not necessary for all three dimensions to be in the colloidal range…Nor is it necessary for the units of a colloidal system to be discrete…The size limits given above are not rigid since they will depend to some extent on the properties under consideration.

b30ea8f260b6.title: Colloid
b30ea8f260b6.sentence: Some colloids are translucent because of the Tyndall effect, which is the scattering of light by particles in the colloid.

752b981153ad.title: Colloid
752b981153ad.sentence: The following forces play an important role in the interaction of colloid particles:

80f62be2f611.title: Colloid
80f62be2f611.sentence: - Electrostatic interaction: Colloidal particles often carry an electrical charge and therefore attract or repel each other.

05c43aff7bb6.title: Colloid
05c43aff7bb6.sentence: This is known as van der Waals force, and is always present (unless the refractive indexes of the dispersed and continuous phases are matched), is short-range, and is attractive.

32b2d7d55bb2.title: Colloid
32b2d7d55bb2.sentence: - Steric forces: A repulsive steric force typically occurring due to adsorbed polymers coating a colloid's surface.

9e925f097e0e.title: Colloid
9e925f097e0e.sentence: - Depletion forces: An attractive entropic force arising from an osmotic pressure imbalance when colloids are suspended in a medium of much smaller particles or polymers called depletants.

66fc3f368929.title: Colloid
66fc3f368929.sentence: In soil science, the colloidal fraction in soils consists of tiny clay and humus particles that are less than 1μm in diameter and carry either positive and/or negative electrostatic charges that vary depending on the chemical conditions of the soil sample, i.e. soil pH.

68eebb1efa59.title: Colloid
68eebb1efa59.sentence: Various types of colloids are recognised: inorganic colloids (e.g. clay particles, silicates, iron oxy-hydroxides), organic colloids (humic and fulvic substances).

0fd3751ce8da.title: Colloid
0fd3751ce8da.sentence: This field of study began in 1845 with Francesco Selmi, who called them pseudosolutions, and was later expanded by Michael Faraday and Thomas Graham, who coined the term colloid in 1861.

fea7501270a7.title: Hematite
fea7501270a7.sentence: Hematite (/ˈhiːmətaɪt, ˈhɛm-/ HE(E)M-ə-tyte), also spelled as haematite, is a common iron oxide compound with the formula Fe2O3 and is widely found in rocks and soils.

5860da394d2e.title: Hematite
5860da394d2e.sentence: Clay-sized hematite crystals also may occur as a secondary mineral formed by weathering processes in soil, and along with other iron oxides or oxyhydroxides such as goethite, which is responsible for the red color of many tropical, ancient, or otherwise highly weathered soils.

9bd694dbf63f.title: Ferrihydrite
9bd694dbf63f.sentence: It is known to be a precursor of more crystalline minerals like hematite and goethite by aggregation-based crystal growth.

bcd27ab6e64e.title: Hematite
bcd27ab6e64e.sentence: The name hematite is derived from the Greek word for blood, αἷμα (haima), due to the red coloration found in some varieties of hematite.

3ed6ba10663f.title: Hematite
3ed6ba10663f.sentence: Ochre is a clay that is colored by varying amounts of hematite, varying between 20% and 70%.

d8497921acec.title: Hematite
d8497921acec.sentence: Red ochre contains unhydrated hematite, whereas yellow ochre contains hydrated hematite (Fe2O3 · H2O).

1178c4844d5f.title: Plinthosol
1178c4844d5f.sentence: Older ironstone crusts generally contain more hematite and boehmite than plinthite but lower overall sesquioxide content.

c82863f63d98.title: Clay mineral
c82863f63d98.sentence: Like all phyllosilicates, clay minerals are characterised by two-dimensional sheets of corner-sharing SiO4 tetrahedra or AlO4 octahedra.

e4c5b782241c.title: Clay mineral
e4c5b782241c.sentence: In clays, the tetrahedral sheets are always bonded to octahedral sheets formed from small cations, such as aluminum or magnesium, and coordinated by six oxygen atoms.

f27d38ff56d2.title: Clay mineral
f27d38ff56d2.sentence: Each silica tetrahedron shares three of its vertex oxygen ions with other tetrahedra, forming a hexagonal array in two dimensions.

132d5adea188.title: Clay mineral
132d5adea188.sentence: The fourth oxygen ion is not shared with another tetrahedron and all of the tetrahedra "point" in the same direction; i.e. all of the unshared oxygen ions are on the same side of the sheet.

a85e8470a70b.title: Clay mineral
a85e8470a70b.sentence: These unshared oxygen ions are called apical oxygen ions.

8cfae0939817.title: Clay mineral
8cfae0939817.sentence: The unshared vertex from the tetrahedral sheet also forms part of one side of the octahedral sheet, but an additional oxygen atom is located above the gap in the tetrahedral sheet at the center of the six tetrahedra.

cac8d005e270.title: Clay mineral
cac8d005e270.sentence: This oxygen atom is bonded to a hydrogen atom forming an OH group in the clay structure.

c992549388dd.title: Kaolinite
c992549388dd.sentence: The T sheet is so called because each silicon ion is surrounded by four oxygen ions forming a tetrahedron.

df3f712437d0.title: Kaolinite
df3f712437d0.sentence: The O sheet is so called because each aluminium ion is surrounded by six oxygen or hydroxyl ions arranged at the corners of an octahedron.

a74d503baa27.title: Clay mineral
a74d503baa27.sentence: Bonding between the tetrahedral and octahedral sheets requires that the tetrahedral sheet becomes corrugated or twisted, causing ditrigonal distortion to the hexagonal array, and the octahedral sheet is flattened.

cfb3521f094e.title: Clay mineral
cfb3521f094e.sentence: Depending on the composition of the tetrahedral and octahedral sheets, the layer will have no charge or will have a net negative charge.

1a8c0da395de.title: Clay mineral
1a8c0da395de.sentence: If the layers are charged this charge is balanced by interlayer cations such as Na+ or K+ or by a lone octahedral sheet.

96f88efef4b6.title: Clay mineral
96f88efef4b6.sentence: The crystal structure is formed from a stack of layers interspaced with the interlayers.

91aa317c465d.title: Clay mineral
91aa317c465d.sentence: Clay minerals can be classified as 1:1 or 2:1.

6d809205ff87.title: Clay mineral
6d809205ff87.sentence: A 1:1 clay would consist of one tetrahedral sheet and one octahedral sheet, and examples would be kaolinite and serpentine.

227e11e54008.title: Clay mineral
227e11e54008.sentence: A 2:1 clay consists of an octahedral sheet sandwiched between two tetrahedral sheets, and examples are talc, vermiculite, and montmorillonite.

f573c4b95369.title: Clay mineral
f573c4b95369.sentence: The layers in 1:1 clays are uncharged and are bonded by hydrogen bonds between layers, but 2:1 layers have a net negative charge and may be bonded together either by individual cations (such as potassium in illite or sodium or calcium in smectites) or by positively charged octahedral sheets (as in chlorites).

c1e69eba23cb.title: Clay mineral
c1e69eba23cb.sentence: - Kaolin group which includes the minerals kaolinite, dickite, halloysite, and nacrite (polymorphs of Al2Si2O5(OH)4).

5862ed0f3067.title: Clay mineral
5862ed0f3067.sentence: - Smectite group which includes dioctahedral smectites, such as montmorillonite, nontronite and beidellite, and trioctahedral smectites, such as saponite.

c0e147681c96.title: Clay mineral
c0e147681c96.sentence: - Illite group which includes the clay-micas.

822fbd8caa47.title: Clay mineral
822fbd8caa47.sentence: - Chlorite group includes a wide variety of similar minerals with considerable chemical variation.

782c05bee825.title: Clay mineral
782c05bee825.sentence: - Other 2:1 clay types exist such as palygorskite (also known as attapulgite) and sepiolite, clays with long water channels internal to their structure.

094453060b6c.title: Clay mineral
094453060b6c.sentence: Mixed layer clay variations exist for most of the above groups.

35a0d9fadde8.title: Clay mineral
35a0d9fadde8.sentence: Ordering is described as a random or regular order and is further described by the term reichweite, which is German for range or reach.

8bbaca99bd75.title: Clay mineral
8bbaca99bd75.sentence: R0 on the other hand describes random ordering, and other advanced ordering types are also found (R3, etc.).

5ee4f7c8d157.title: Clay mineral
5ee4f7c8d157.sentence: R1 ordered chlorite-smectite is known as corrensite, R1 illite-smectite is rectorite.

bb6769e22377.title: Soil matrix
bb6769e22377.sentence: Typically there are four main groups of clay minerals: kaolinite, montmorillonite-smectite, illite, and chlorite.

db8b239e8023.title: Vermiculite
db8b239e8023.sentence: Vermiculite is a hydrous phyllosilicate mineral which undergoes significant expansion when heated.

a5908d6bd373.title: Vermiculite
a5908d6bd373.sentence: Vermiculite is a 2:1 clay, meaning it has two tetrahedral sheets for every one octahedral sheet.

03039fa9b0eb.title: Vermiculite
03039fa9b0eb.sentence: Vermiculite forms by the weathering or hydrothermal alteration of biotite or phlogopite.

2ab3ff785290.title: Vermiculite
2ab3ff785290.sentence: Vermiculite clays are weathered micas in which the potassium ions between the molecular sheets are replaced by magnesium and iron ions.

8dd23705fc76.title: Vermiculite
8dd23705fc76.sentence: It is a limited-expansion clay with a medium shrink–swell capacity.

04a6c4a98de4.title: Soil matrix
04a6c4a98de4.section: Mineral colloids: soil clays > Alumino-silica clays
04a6c4a98de4.sentence: - Vermiculite is a mica-based clay similar to illite, but the crystals of clay are held together more loosely by hydrated magnesium and it will swell, but not as much as does montmorillonite.

22e1924ac9c7.title: Vermiculite
22e1924ac9c7.sentence: Vermiculite has a high cation-exchange capacity (CEC) at 100–150 meq/100 g.

3762c5f35405.title: Smectite
3762c5f35405.section: Role of interlayer cations in the swelling process
3762c5f35405.sentence: Only more expandable vermiculite and some rarer alumino-silicate minerals (zeolites) with inner channel structure can exhibit a higher CEC than smectite.

e6e4f49178f7.title: Vermiculite
e6e4f49178f7.sentence: Exfoliation occurs when the mineral is heated sufficiently; commercial furnaces can routinely produce this effect.

ae6339a93c30.title: Vermiculite
ae6339a93c30.sentence: Its name is from the Latin vermiculare, "to breed worms", for the manner in which it exfoliates when heated.

79edb59b5f26.title: Vermiculite
79edb59b5f26.sentence: Vermiculite was first described in 1824 for an occurrence in Millbury, Massachusetts.

78384419246c.title: Vermiculite
78384419246c.sentence: It occurs interlayered with chlorite, biotite and phlogopite.

7bbef8b160d1.title: Vermiculite
7bbef8b160d1.sentence: It typically occurs as an alteration product at the contact between felsic and mafic or ultramafic rocks such as pyroxenites and dunites.

b8a162e6e565.title: Vermiculite
b8a162e6e565.sentence: Pure vermiculite does not contain asbestos and is non-toxic.

fdeaa1270033.title: Vermiculite
fdeaa1270033.sentence: Although not all vermiculite contains asbestos, some products were made with vermiculite that contained asbestos until the early 1990s.

98a44b101172.title: Vermiculite
98a44b101172.sentence: The vermiculite deposit at the mine in Libby, Montana, was (and is) heavily contaminated with asbestos.

94428338ae9d.title: Kaolinite
94428338ae9d.sentence: Kaolinite (/ˈkeɪ.ələˌnaɪt, -lɪ-/ KAY-ə-lə-nyte, -⁠lih-; also called kaolin) is a clay mineral, having the chemical composition Al2Si2O5(OH)4.

3e484e677197.title: Kaolinite
3e484e677197.sentence: It is described as a 1:1 or TO clay mineral because its crystals consist of stacked TO layers.

fb2e5300223a.title: Kaolinite
fb2e5300223a.sentence: Kaolinite is a soft, earthy, usually white, mineral (dioctahedral phyllosilicate clay), produced by the chemical weathering of aluminium silicate minerals like feldspar.

948913e5b7b9.title: Kaolinite
948913e5b7b9.sentence: Each TO layer consists of a tetrahedral (T) sheet composed of silicon and oxygen ions bonded to an octahedral (O) sheet composed of oxygen, aluminium, and hydroxyl ions.

f0764fc52a6f.title: Kaolinite
f0764fc52a6f.sentence: The two sheets in each layer are strongly bonded together via shared oxygen ions, while layers are bonded via hydrogen bonding between oxygen on the outer face of the T sheet of one layer and hydroxyl on the outer face of the O sheet of the next layer.

2e7ccda97d1e.title: Kaolinite
2e7ccda97d1e.sentence: A kaolinite layer has no net electrical charge, thus there are no large cations (such as calcium, sodium, or potassium) between layers as with most other clay minerals.

975fdbc72909.title: Kaolinite
975fdbc72909.sentence: This accounts for kaolinite's relatively low ion exchange capacity.

4d2b8c0a2f30.title: Kaolinite
4d2b8c0a2f30.sentence: It has a low shrink–swell capacity and a low cation-exchange capacity (1–15 meq/100 g).

f1899ba7a083.title: Kaolinite
f1899ba7a083.sentence: The close hydrogen bonding between layers also hinders water molecules from infiltrating between layers, accounting for kaolinite's nonswelling character.

2b388c7ac414.title: Kaolinite
2b388c7ac414.sentence: When moistened, the tiny platelike crystals of kaolinite acquire a layer of water molecules that cause crystals to adhere to each other and give kaolin clay its cohesiveness.

56e013077e6e.title: Kaolinite
56e013077e6e.sentence: The bonds are weak enough to allow the plates to slip past each other when the clay is being molded, but strong enough to hold the plates in place and allow the molded clay to retain its shape.

f5f8989ffc5f.title: Kaolinite
f5f8989ffc5f.sentence: When the clay is dried, most of the water molecules are removed, and the plates hydrogen bond directly to each other, so that the dried clay is rigid but still fragile.

3f27be03ac18.title: Kaolinite
3f27be03ac18.sentence: If the clay is moistened again, it will once more become plastic.

65e25d15e0be.title: Cation-exchange capacity
65e25d15e0be.sentence: The surfaces of kaolinite, allophane and iron and aluminium oxides often carry positive charges.

10c595c001f9.title: Kaolinite
10c595c001f9.sentence: Kaolinite clay occurs in abundance in soils that have formed from the chemical weathering of rocks in hot, moist climates; for example in tropical rainforest areas.

43581a572131.title: Kaolinite
43581a572131.sentence: In the National Institute of Agronomic Studies and Research (INERA) classification system, soils in which the clay fraction is predominantly kaolinite are called kaolisol (from kaolin and soil).

26e8f4e0d0f3.title: Kaolinite
26e8f4e0d0f3.sentence: Rocks that are rich in kaolinite, and halloysite, are known as kaolin (/ˈkeɪ.əlɪn/) or china clay.

2cc323d5d73d.title: Kaolinite
2cc323d5d73d.sentence: Kaolin is an important raw material in many industries and applications.

ad03cc3d7f4b.title: Kaolinite
ad03cc3d7f4b.sentence: Following reduced demand from the paper industry, resulting from both competing minerals and the effect of digital media, in 2016 the market share was reported to be: paper, 36%; ceramics, 31%; paint, 7% and other, 26%.

ff96430551c1.title: Illite
ff96430551c1.sentence: Illite, also called hydromica or hydromuscovite, is a group of closely related non-expanding clay minerals.

0ad0d042b2f2.title: Illite
0ad0d042b2f2.sentence: Its structure is a 2:1 sandwich of silica tetrahedron (T) – alumina octahedron (O) – silica tetrahedron (T) layers.

41184d4adfe7.title: Illite
41184d4adfe7.sentence: Structurally, illite is quite similar to muscovite with slightly more silicon, magnesium, iron, and water and slightly less tetrahedral aluminium and interlayer potassium.

a637cce4dd3b.title: Illite
a637cce4dd3b.sentence: The space between this T-O-T sequence of layers is occupied by poorly hydrated potassium cations which are responsible for the absence of swelling.

3d0237e4bbb3.title: Bentonite
3d0237e4bbb3.section: Types > Illitisation of smectite clays by potassium ions and K-bentonite rock
3d0237e4bbb3.sentence: Illite is a high-charge TOT clay mineral, in which negatively charged sheets are bound relatively strongly by more numerous potassium cations, and so it is no longer a swelling clay and has few industrial uses.

3fa2404ff76b.title: Bentonite
3fa2404ff76b.section: Types > Illitisation of smectite clays by potassium ions and K-bentonite rock
3fa2404ff76b.sentence: Illite, the clay mineral, is a potassium-rich phyllosilicate formed from the alteration of smectic clay in contact with groundwater rich in K+ ions.

d1cdcc747524.title: Illite
d1cdcc747524.sentence: It is common in sediments, soils, and argillaceous sedimentary rocks as well as in some low grade metamorphic rocks.

522c45a55ecd.title: Kaolinite
522c45a55ecd.sentence: Comparing soils along a gradient towards progressively cooler or drier climates, the proportion of kaolinite decreases, while the proportion of other clay minerals such as illite (in cooler climates) or smectite (in drier climates) increases.

b3b78d258d48.title: Soil matrix
b3b78d258d48.section: Mineral colloids: soil clays > Alumino-silica clays
b3b78d258d48.sentence: The active surface area is reduced due to the potassium ionic bonds.

23d9e956404b.title: Soil matrix
23d9e956404b.section: Mineral colloids: soil clays > Alumino-silica clays
23d9e956404b.sentence: - Illite is a 2:1 clay similar in structure to montmorillonite but has potassium bridges between the faces of the clay crystals and the degree of swelling depends on the degree of weathering of potassium-feldspar.

bf239215a235.title: Illite
bf239215a235.sentence: Due to the small size, positive identification usually requires x-ray diffraction or SEM-EDS (automated mineralogy) analysis.

f03390834f88.title: Clay mineral
f03390834f88.section: Tests which verify that clay minerals are present
f03390834f88.sentence: The amount of illite is estimated from the K20 content since this is the only clay mineral containing potassium.

a1a145289117.title: Illite
a1a145289117.sentence: Illite was first described for occurrences in the Maquoketa shale in Calhoun County, Illinois, US, in 1937.

532205a02f66.title: Illite
532205a02f66.sentence: The name was derived from its type location in Illinois.

60736540ef95.title: Gibbsite
60736540ef95.sentence: Gibbsite, Al(OH)3, is one of the mineral forms of aluminium hydroxide.

c5d04b3197b2.title: Gibbsite
c5d04b3197b2.sentence: The basic structure forms stacked sheets of linked octahedra.

63d3e015a95a.title: Gibbsite
63d3e015a95a.sentence: Each octahedron is composed of an aluminium ion bonded to six hydroxide groups, and each hydroxide group is shared by two aluminium octahedra.

a0122ca48efc.title: Gibbsite
a0122ca48efc.sentence: One third of the potential octahedral spaces are missing a central aluminium.

3370bf6bd1ae.title: Gibbsite
3370bf6bd1ae.sentence: The result is a neutral sheet: with aluminium as a +3 ion and hydroxide a −1 ion, the net cationic charge of one aluminium per six hydroxides is (+3)/6 = +1/2, and likewise the net anionic charge of one hydroxide per two aluminium atoms is (−1)/2 = −1/2.

ae420d67c7eb.title: Gibbsite
ae420d67c7eb.sentence: The lack of a charge on the gibbsite sheets means that there is no charge to retain ions between the sheets and act as a "glue" to keep the sheets together.

ff033ea6352e.title: Gibbsite
ff033ea6352e.sentence: The sheets are only held together by weak residual bonds and this results in a very soft easily cleaved mineral.

50d749463e69.title: Gibbsite
50d749463e69.sentence: The neutral aluminium hydroxide sheets are found sandwiched between silicate sheets in important clay groups: the illite, kaolinite, and montmorillonite/smectite groups.

7db291377367.title: Gibbsite
7db291377367.sentence: The individual aluminium hydroxide layers are identical to the individual layers of gibbsite and are referred to as the gibbsite layers.

a0c877d8c046.title: Allophane
a0c877d8c046.sentence: Allophane can alter to form halloysite under resilicating aqueous conditions and can alter to form gibbsite under desilicating conditions.

08a618d2319d.title: Gibbsite
08a618d2319d.sentence: Gibbsite is an important ore of aluminium in that it is one of three main phases that make up the rock bauxite.

e97a26c8d2e3.title: Gibbsite
e97a26c8d2e3.sentence: Gibbsite is named after George Gibbs (1776–1833), an American mineral collector.

1146f6966a5d.title: Bauxite
1146f6966a5d.sentence: Bauxite (/ˈbɔːksaɪt/ ⓘ) is a sedimentary rock with a relatively high aluminium content.

288e01545dc2.title: Bauxite
288e01545dc2.sentence: It is the world's main source of aluminium and gallium.

cbbb24ef415d.title: Bauxite
cbbb24ef415d.sentence: Bauxite consists mostly aluminium minerals gibbsite (Al(OH)3), boehmite (γ-AlO(OH)), and diaspore (α-AlO(OH)), mixed with the two iron oxides goethite (FeO(OH)) and hematite (Fe2O3), the aluminium clay mineral kaolinite (Al2Si2O5(OH)4) and small amounts of anatase (TiO2) and ilmenite (FeTiO3 or FeO·TiO2).

140c4b0b91bf.title: Bauxite
140c4b0b91bf.sentence: - The lateritic bauxites are found mostly in the countries of the tropics.

f417d7c297fa.title: Bauxite
f417d7c297fa.sentence: They were formed by lateritization of various silicate rocks such as granite, gneiss, basalt, syenite, and shale.

0e03b4c73064.title: Bauxite
0e03b4c73064.sentence: - The carbonate bauxites occur predominantly in Europe, Guyana, Suriname, and Jamaica above carbonate rocks (limestone and dolomite), where they were formed by lateritic weathering and residual accumulation of intercalated clay layers – dispersed clays which were concentrated as the enclosing limestones gradually dissolved during chemical weathering.

d14048d5bc7c.title: Bauxite
d14048d5bc7c.sentence: In comparison with the iron-rich laterites, the formation of bauxites depends even more on intense weathering conditions in a location with very good drainage.

18e8126f3e0c.title: Bauxite
18e8126f3e0c.sentence: This enables the dissolution of the kaolinite and the precipitation of the gibbsite.

3c70e0b8de94.title: Bauxite
3c70e0b8de94.sentence: The aluminium hydroxide in the lateritic bauxite deposits is almost exclusively gibbsite.

96c008617a14.title: Bauxite
96c008617a14.sentence: Most of the world's bauxite deposits can be found within 1 to 20 metres (3 ft 3 in to 65 ft 7 in) of the Earth's surface.

ac0399b7c4a5.title: Bauxite
ac0399b7c4a5.sentence: Bauxite is usually strip mined because it is almost always found near the surface of the terrain, with little or no overburden.

b56052b4a9a3.title: Soil chemistry
b56052b4a9a3.sentence: A knowledge of environmental soil chemistry is paramount to predicting the fate of contaminants, as well as the processes by which they are initially released into the soil.

23dcb2576f78.title: Soil chemistry
23dcb2576f78.sentence: Once a chemical is exposed to the soil environment, myriad chemical reactions can occur that may increase or decrease contaminant toxicity.

488c77ca8dbe.title: Soil chemistry
488c77ca8dbe.sentence: These reactions include adsorption/desorption, precipitation, polymerization, dissolution, hydrolysis, hydration, complexation and oxidation/reduction.

db385883bd59.title: Soil chemistry
db385883bd59.sentence: Understanding these processes enable us to better predict the fate and toxicity of contaminants and provide the knowledge to develop scientifically correct, and cost-effective remediation strategies.

5aaad6e5a2b1.title: Soil chemistry
5aaad6e5a2b1.sentence: These reactions are often disregarded by scientists and engineers involved with environmental remediation.

a1ce044fb887.title: Soil chemistry
a1ce044fb887.sentence: New knowledge about the chemistry of soils often comes from studies in the laboratory, in which soil samples taken from undisturbed soil horizons in the field are used in experiments that include replicated treatments and controls.

d82e3ffc3351.title: Soil chemistry
d82e3ffc3351.sentence: In many cases, the soil samples are air dried at ambient temperatures (e.g., 25 °C (77 °F)) and sieved to a 2 mm size prior to storage for further study.

a0683810da03.title: Soil chemistry
a0683810da03.sentence: Such drying and sieving soil samples markedly disrupts soil structure, microbial population diversity, and chemical properties related to pH, oxidation-reduction status, manganese oxidation state, and dissolved organic matter; among other properties.

2aaad5cddf8c.title: Soil chemistry
2aaad5cddf8c.sentence: Renewed interest in recent decades has led many soil chemists to maintain soil samples in a field-moist condition and stored at 4 °C (39 °F) under aerobic conditions before and during investigations.

c0bbd33f6360.title: Soil chemistry
c0bbd33f6360.sentence: The first is known as batch equilibration.

b0c87d641c65.title: Soil chemistry
b0c87d641c65.sentence: The chemist adds a given volume of water or salt solution of known concentration of dissolved ions to a mass of soil (e.g., 25–mL of solution to 5–g of soil in a centrifuge tube or flask).

2244dc0905ab.title: Soil chemistry
2244dc0905ab.sentence: The soil slurry then is shaken or swirled for a given amount of time (e.g., 15 minutes to many hours) to establish a steady state or equilibrium condition prior to filtering or centrifuging at high speed to separate sand grains, silt particles, and clay colloids from the equilibrated solution.

c68654ca3267.title: Soil chemistry
c68654ca3267.sentence: In each case, the analysis quantifies the concentration or activity of an ion or molecule in the solution phase, and by multiplying the measured concentration or activity (e.g., in mg ion/mL) by the solution-to-soil ratio (mL of extraction solution/g soil), the chemist obtains the result in mg ion/g soil.

892a862a4b8c.title: Soil chemistry
892a862a4b8c.sentence: A related approach uses a known volume to solution to leach (infiltrate) the extracting solution through a quantity of soil in small columns at a controlled rate to simulate how rain, snow meltwater, and irrigation water pass through soils in the field.

395b8be46900.title: Soil chemistry
395b8be46900.sentence: Another approach to quantifying soil processes and phenomena uses in situ methods that do not disrupt the soil. as occurs when the soil is shaken or leached with an extracting soil solution.

069e80978a6a.title: Soil chemistry
069e80978a6a.sentence: These methods usually use surface spectroscopic techniques, such as Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, nuclear magnetic resonance, Mössbauer spectroscopy, and X-ray spectroscopy.

a7a30fc5c6f2.title: Soil chemistry
a7a30fc5c6f2.sentence: These approaches aim to obtain information on the chemical nature of the mineralogy and chemistry of particle and colloid surfaces, and how ions and molecules are associated with such surfaces by adsorption, complexation, and precipitation.

c8c66237f7eb.title: Soil matrix
c8c66237f7eb.sentence: It is a colloidal and most often a crystalline phyllosilicate material.

226eb4d6dad8.title: Soil
226eb4d6dad8.sentence: The negative or positive charges on colloid particles make them able to hold cations or anions, respectively, to their surfaces.

8eccea78a50a.title: Colloid
8eccea78a50a.sentence: Colloidal: State of subdivision such that the molecules or polymolecular particles dispersed in a medium have at least one dimension between approximately 1 nm and 1 μm, or that in a system discontinuities are found at distances of that order.

cd1b9621cc82.title: Soil
cd1b9621cc82.sentence: Similarly, positively charged sites on colloids can attract and release anions in the soil, giving the soil anion-exchange capacity.

afc981abb05d.title: Soil
afc981abb05d.sentence: The cation exchange, that takes place between colloids and soil water, buffers (moderates) soil pH, alters soil structure, and purifies percolating water by adsorbing cations of all types, both useful and harmful.

4cbf96ff5dc5.title: Soil matrix
4cbf96ff5dc5.sentence: In a wider sense clays can be classified as:

1ec24c447d7f.title: Soil matrix
1ec24c447d7f.sentence: - Layer Crystalline alumino-silica clays: montmorillonite, illite, vermiculite, chlorite, kaolinite.

facbebeff7a3.title: Soil matrix
facbebeff7a3.sentence: - Crystalline Chain carbonate and sulfate minerals: calcite (CaCO3), dolomite (CaMg(CO3)2) and gypsum (CaSO4·2H2O).

76949bf3ebc4.title: Soil matrix
76949bf3ebc4.sentence: - Amorphous clays: young mixtures of silica (SiO2-OH) and alumina (Al(OH)3) which have not had time to form regular crystals.

0cd002534b95.title: Soil matrix
0cd002534b95.sentence: - Sesquioxide clays: old, highly leached clays which result in oxides of iron, aluminium and titanium.

38e141b67836.title: Soil matrix
38e141b67836.sentence: In the extreme environment of high temperatures and the leaching caused by the heavy rain of tropical rain forests, the clay and organic colloids are largely destroyed.

57f40c1bda95.title: Soil matrix
57f40c1bda95.sentence: The heavy rains wash the alumino-silicate clays from the soil leaving only sesquioxide clays of low CEC.

2f4828c1e341.title: Van der Waals force
2f4828c1e341.sentence: In molecular physics and chemistry, the van der Waals force (sometimes van der Waals' force) is a distance-dependent interaction between atoms or molecules and one of the category of intermolecular force.

340776f338f4.title: Van der Waals force
340776f338f4.sentence: Unlike ionic or covalent bonds, these attractions do not result from a chemical electronic bond; they are comparatively weak and therefore more susceptible to disturbance.

75d9da240c8b.title: Van der Waals force
75d9da240c8b.sentence: The force results from a transient shift in electron density.

672d2cb012f3.title: Van der Waals force
672d2cb012f3.sentence: This shift generates a transient charge which a nearby atom can be attracted to or repelled by.

49195885ee92.title: Van der Waals force
49195885ee92.sentence: The force is repulsive at very short distances, reaches zero at an equilibrium distance characteristic for each atom, or molecule, and becomes attractive for distances larger than the equilibrium distance.

f1d1b5819662.title: Van der Waals force
f1d1b5819662.sentence: For individual atoms, the equilibrium distance is between 0.3 nm and 0.5 nm, depending on the atomic-specific diameter.

c31ea30d31e9.title: Van der Waals force
c31ea30d31e9.sentence: When the interatomic distance is greater than 1.0 nm the force is not strong enough to be easily observed as it decreases as a function of distance r approximately with the 7th power (~r−7).

6ea8598d5fff.title: Van der Waals force
6ea8598d5fff.sentence: The Van der Waals forces are usually described as a combination of the London dispersion forces between "instantaneously induced dipoles", Debye forces between permanent dipoles and induced dipoles, and the Keesom force between permanent molecular dipoles whose rotational orientations are dynamically averaged over time.

a2f71a7bf8ea.title: Van der Waals force
a2f71a7bf8ea.sentence: The induction and dispersion interactions are always attractive, irrespective of orientation, but the electrostatic interaction changes sign upon rotation of the molecules.

7cc31f48ef15.title: Van der Waals force
7cc31f48ef15.sentence: That is, the electrostatic force can be attractive or repulsive, depending on the mutual orientation of the molecules.

9387d6cb5f8c.title: Van der Waals force
9387d6cb5f8c.sentence: The strength of van der Waals bonds increases with higher polarizability of the participating atoms.

054af0cf9c38.title: Van der Waals force
054af0cf9c38.sentence: For example, the pairwise attractive van der Waals interaction energy between H (hydrogen) atoms in different H2 molecules equals 0.06 kJ/mol (0.6 meV) and the pairwise attractive interaction energy between O (oxygen) atoms in different O2 molecules equals 0.44 kJ/mol (4.6 meV).

28931c42b82c.title: Van der Waals force
28931c42b82c.sentence: For example, the pairwise Van der Waals interaction energy for more polarizable atoms such as S (sulfur) atoms in H2S and sulfides exceeds 1 kJ/mol (10 meV), and the pairwise interaction energy between even larger, more polarizable Xe (xenon) atoms is 2.35 kJ/mol (24.3 meV).

07701007eea9.title: Van der Waals force
07701007eea9.sentence: - The van der Waals forces are additive in nature, consisting of several individual interactions, and cannot be saturated.

75ca9b85b591.title: Van der Waals force
75ca9b85b591.sentence: Accordingly, van der Waals forces can range from weak to strong interactions, and support integral structural loads when multitudes of such interactions are present.

26981fbf6416.title: Van der Waals force
