26981fbf6416.section: Van der Waals forces between macroscopic objects
26981fbf6416.sentence: Consequently, the van der Waals forces become dominant for collections of very small particles such as very fine-grained dry powders (where there are no capillary forces present) even though the force of attraction is smaller in magnitude than it is for larger particles of the same substance.

774b1b093ac6.title: Van der Waals force
774b1b093ac6.section: Van der Waals forces between macroscopic objects
774b1b093ac6.sentence: Such powders are said to be cohesive, meaning they are not as easily fluidized or pneumatically conveyed as their more coarse-grained counterparts.

5a1224b7b9ab.title: Van der Waals force
5a1224b7b9ab.section: Van der Waals forces between macroscopic objects
5a1224b7b9ab.sentence: Generally, free-flow occurs with particles greater than about 250 μm.

088ac3e86a78.title: Bioavailability (soil)
088ac3e86a78.sentence: Organic contaminants may become sorbed or sequestered in organic matter through weak Van der Waals interactions or through hydrogen- or covalent bonding.

640e65cbcbc0.title: Adsorption
640e65cbcbc0.sentence: The exact nature of the bonding depends on the details of the species involved, but the adsorption process is generally classified as physisorption (characteristic of weak van der Waals forces) or chemisorption (characteristic of covalent bonding).

d21405e134aa.title: Soil matrix
d21405e134aa.section: Mineral colloids: soil clays > Alumino-silica clays
d21405e134aa.sentence: - Chlorite is similar to vermiculite, but the loose bonding by occasional hydrated magnesium, as in vermiculite, is replaced by a hydrated magnesium sheet, that firmly bonds the planes above and below it.

babaf2ae0663.title: Chlorite group
babaf2ae0663.sentence: By contrast, the TOT layers of chlorite contain some aluminium in place of silicon, which gives the layers an overall negative charge.

3949ffb23250.title: Chlorite group
3949ffb23250.sentence: These TOT layers are bound together by positively charged O layers, sometimes called brucite layers.

66bcca67e218.title: Chlorite group
66bcca67e218.sentence: Mica is also composed of aluminium-rich, negatively charged TOT layers, but these are bonded together by individual cations (such as potassium, sodium, or calcium ions) rather than a positively charged brucite layer.

862fdc709d06.title: Soil matrix
862fdc709d06.section: Mineral colloids: soil clays > Alumino-silica clays
862fdc709d06.sentence: It has two planes of silicon, one of aluminium and one of magnesium; hence it is a 2:2 clay.

ec403c296d57.title: Chlorite group
ec403c296d57.sentence: It is a nonswelling clay mineral, since water is not adsorbed in the interlayer spaces, and it has a relatively low cation exchange capacity.

44227fb2ec0b.title: Soil matrix
44227fb2ec0b.section: Mineral colloids: soil clays > Alumino-silica clays
44227fb2ec0b.sentence: Chlorite does not swell and it has low CEC.

31c9a5573ca9.title: Chlorite group
31c9a5573ca9.sentence: Chlorite is a common weathering product and is widespread in clay and in sedimentary rock containing clay minerals.

e7373616a015.title: Chlorite group
e7373616a015.sentence: The chlorites are the group of phyllosilicate minerals common in low-grade metamorphic rocks and in altered igneous rocks.

eecc4f550825.title: Chlorite group
eecc4f550825.sentence: The name chlorite is from the Greek chloros (χλωρός), meaning "green", in reference to its color.

2d24d0671503.title: Chlorite group
2d24d0671503.sentence: Chlorite minerals do not contain the element chlorine.

6b789ec4f27d.title: Ferrihydrite
6b789ec4f27d.sentence: Ferrihydrite (Fh) is a widespread hydrous ferric oxyhydroxide mineral at the Earth's surface, and a likely constituent in extraterrestrial materials.

8d5ead13832b.title: Ferrihydrite
8d5ead13832b.sentence: Ferrihydrite only exists as a fine grained and highly defective nanomaterial.

2480ef7d8af9.title: Ferrihydrite
2480ef7d8af9.sentence: It forms in several types of environments, from freshwater to marine systems, aquifers to hydrothermal hot springs and scales, soils, and areas affected by mining.

322cc73d5aaf.title: Ferrihydrite
322cc73d5aaf.sentence: It can be precipitated directly from oxygenated iron-rich aqueous solutions, or by bacteria either as a result of a metabolic activity or passive sorption of dissolved iron followed by nucleation reactions.

47543bd4e883.title: Ferrihydrite
47543bd4e883.sentence: Because of the small size of individual nanocrystals, Fh is nanoporous yielding large surface areas of several hundred square meters per gram.

2bf3730e777c.title: Ferrihydrite
2bf3730e777c.sentence: These properties confer a high ability to adsorb many environmentally important chemical species, including arsenic, lead, phosphate, and organic molecules (e.g., humic and fulvic acids).

6485a063a521.title: Ferrihydrite
6485a063a521.sentence: However, its transformation in natural systems generally is blocked by chemical impurities adsorbed at its surface, for example silica as most of natural ferrihydrites are siliceous.

f7e29f782db9.title: Ferrihydrite
f7e29f782db9.sentence: Under reducing conditions as those found in gley soils, or in deep environments depleted in oxygen, and often with the assistance of microbial activity, ferrihydrite can be transformed in green rust, a layered double hydroxide (LDH), also known as the mineral fougerite.

45811c3e131c.title: Ferrihydrite
45811c3e131c.sentence: However, a short exposure of green rust to atmospheric oxygen is sufficient to oxidize it back to ferrihydrite, making it a very elusive compound.

46628e0ccdef.title: Clay mineral
46628e0ccdef.section: Clay and the origins of life
46628e0ccdef.sentence: The clay hypothesis for the origin of life was proposed by Graham Cairns-Smith in 1985.

85d7881486d6.title: Clay mineral
85d7881486d6.section: Clay and the origins of life
85d7881486d6.sentence: It postulates that complex organic molecules arose gradually on pre-existing, non-organic replication surfaces of silicate crystals in contact with an aqueous solution.

8a8487a3062b.title: Clay mineral
8a8487a3062b.section: Clay and the origins of life
8a8487a3062b.sentence: The clay mineral montmorillonite has been shown to catalyze the polymerization of RNA in aqueous solution from nucleotide monomers, and the formation of membranes from lipids.

df7c9a28289d.title: Clay mineral
df7c9a28289d.section: Clay and the origins of life
df7c9a28289d.sentence: In 1998, Hyman Hartman proposed that "the first organisms were self-replicating iron-rich clays which fixed carbon dioxide into oxalic acid and other dicarboxylic acids.

40bddba7f7e4.title: Clay mineral
40bddba7f7e4.section: Tests which verify that clay minerals are present
40bddba7f7e4.sentence: The results of glycol adsorption, cation exchange capacity, X-ray diffraction, differential thermal analysis, and chemical tests all give data that may be used for quantitative estimations.

7d210438cb13.title: Clay mineral
7d210438cb13.sentence: Because clay minerals are usually (but not necessarily) ultrafine-grained, special analytical techniques are required for their identification and study.

bf9157c539ef.title: Clay mineral
bf9157c539ef.section: Tests which verify that clay minerals are present
bf9157c539ef.sentence: After the quantities of organic matter, carbonates, free oxides, and nonclay minerals have been determined, the percentages of clay minerals are estimated using the appropriate glycol adsorption, cation exchange capacity, K20, and DTA data.

1263ead76e07.title: Clay mineral
1263ead76e07.sentence: Glycol (mg/g) is the adsorption capacity for glycol, which occupies the interlayer sites when the clay is exposed to a vapor of ethylene glycol at 60 °C (140 °F) for eight hours.

14691ee0835e.title: Fougèrite
14691ee0835e.sentence: Fougèrite is a relatively recently described naturally occurring green rust mineral.

4f8c03c733d1.title: Fougèrite
4f8c03c733d1.sentence: It is the archetype of the fougèrite group in the larger hydrotalcite supergroup of naturally occurring layered double hydroxides.

fd321f14067e.title: Gleysol
fd321f14067e.sentence: Green rust, a layered double hydroxide (LDH) of Fe(II) and Fe(III) can be found as the mineral fougerite in gleysoils.

697be4eb60f8.title: Fougèrite
697be4eb60f8.sentence: Fougèrite was first found in forested soils near Fougères, Brittany, France, and recognised as a valid mineral species by the International Mineralogical Association in 2002.

329ef06c12b7.title: Fougèrite
329ef06c12b7.sentence: The structure is based on brucite-like layers containing Fe2+ and Fe3+ cations, O2− and OH− anions, with loosely bound [CO3]2− groups and H2O molecules between the layers.

aa127e61fd85.title: Fougèrite
aa127e61fd85.sentence: It is blue-green to bluish-gray in colour, and resembles clay minerals in habit, forming hexagonal platelets of submicron diameter.

3fee4c0a3242.title: Fougèrite
3fee4c0a3242.sentence: The mineral is unstable in air, and decomposes by oxidation, dehydration and decarbonation, to ferrihydrite, and ultimately to lepidocrocite or goethite, FeIIIO(OH).

6b70b1853db8.title: Flocculation
6b70b1853db8.sentence: In colloidal chemistry, flocculation is a process by which colloidal particles come out of suspension to sediment in the form of floc or flake, either spontaneously or due to the addition of a clarifying agent.

ed08f3222ec1.title: Flocculation
ed08f3222ec1.sentence: The action differs from precipitation in that, prior to flocculation, colloids are merely suspended, under the form of a stable dispersion (where the internal phase (solid) is dispersed throughout the external phase (fluid) through mechanical agitation) and are not truly dissolved in solution.

7f8df1455573.title: Flocculation
7f8df1455573.sentence: According to the IUPAC definition, flocculation is "a process of contact and adhesion whereby the particles of a dispersion form larger-size clusters".

301e4aac3837.title: Flocculation
301e4aac3837.sentence: In contrast to aggregation, agglomeration is a reversible process.

21f3861cae93.title: Flocculation
21f3861cae93.sentence: The particles that comprise agglomerates can be dispersed again.

9fe372bc286e.title: Flocculation
9fe372bc286e.sentence: In dispersed clay slurries, flocculation occurs after mechanical agitation ceases and the dispersed clay platelets spontaneously form flocs because of attractions between negative face charges and positive edge charges.

414cf62669da.title: Flocculation
414cf62669da.sentence: Flocculation behavior of soil colloids is closely related to freshwater quality.

156738faf841.title: Flocculation
156738faf841.sentence: High dispersibility of soil colloids not only directly causes turbidity of the surrounding water but it also induces eutrophication due to the adsorption of nutritional substances in rivers and lakes and even boats under the sea.

d7528a960725.title: Soil aggregate stability
d7528a960725.sentence: Inter-particle forces include: van der Waals forces, electrostatic forces, and hydrogen bonding.

fce06f723d0a.title: Physical properties of soil
fce06f723d0a.sentence: At the same time, the edges of the clay plates have a slight positive charge, due to the sorption of aluminium from the soil solution to exposed hydroxyl groups, thereby allowing the edges to adhere to the negative charges on the faces of other clay particles or to flocculate (form clumps).

2a856837f689.title: Physical properties of soil
2a856837f689.sentence: On the other hand, when monovalent ions, such as sodium, invade and displace the polyvalent cations (single displacement reaction), they weaken the positive charges on the edges, while the negative surface charges are relatively strengthened.

d15f50e5a553.title: Physical properties of soil
d15f50e5a553.sentence: This leaves negative charge on the clay faces that repel other clay, causing the particles to push apart, and by doing so deflocculate clay suspensions.

07d3ff8d6f0b.title: Flocculation
07d3ff8d6f0b.sentence: Basically, coagulation is a process of addition of coagulant to destabilize a stabilized charged particle.

4e1413a6fdce.title: Flocculation
4e1413a6fdce.sentence: Meanwhile, flocculation is a technique that promotes agglomeration and assists in the settling of particles.

5cc5857ed97c.title: Flocculation
5cc5857ed97c.sentence: The most common used coagulant is alum, Al2(SO4)3·14H2O.

2b58702ad0a0.title: Flocculation
2b58702ad0a0.sentence: During flocculation, gentle mixing accelerates the rate of particle collision, and the destabilized particles are further aggregated and enmeshed into larger precipitates.

3801b8f2d376.title: Flocculation
3801b8f2d376.sentence: Flocculation is affected by several parameters, including mixing shear and intensity, time and pH.

8e0c5132f992.title: Flocculation
8e0c5132f992.sentence: The process by which the dosage and choice of flocculant are selected is called a jar test.

824e9399e71c.title: Flocculation
824e9399e71c.sentence: The equipment used for jar testing consists of one or more beakers, each equipped with a paddle mixer.

935c2eb422b7.title: Flocculation
935c2eb422b7.sentence: After the addition of flocculants, rapid mixing takes place, followed by slow mixing and later the sedimentation process.

f4e54a7ff785.title: Flocculation
f4e54a7ff785.sentence: For drinking water, typical treatment processes consist of grates, coagulation, flocculation, sedimentation, granular filtration and disinfection.

c87016b87683.title: Flocculation
c87016b87683.sentence: Biopolymers, especially, chitosan, are increasingly popular as environmentally friendly flocculants.

2cedd8fe7236.title: Flocculation
2cedd8fe7236.sentence: Chitosan is not only biodegradable but also exhibits a unique ability to bind with a wide range of contaminants, including heavy metals and organic pollutants, effectively removing them from water sources.

e898b660726d.title: Zeta potential
e898b660726d.sentence: Zeta potential is the electrical potential at the slipping plane.

65f5b274a27f.title: Zeta potential
65f5b274a27f.sentence: This plane is the interface which separates mobile fluid from fluid that remains attached to the surface.

6e0128f530c0.title: Zeta potential
6e0128f530c0.sentence: Zeta potential is a scientific term for electrokinetic potential in colloidal dispersions.

84665227306c.title: Zeta potential
84665227306c.sentence: The usual units are volts (V) or, more commonly, millivolts (mV).

0f0a957a1ca5.title: Zeta potential
0f0a957a1ca5.sentence: In the colloidal chemistry literature, it is usually denoted using the Greek letter zeta (ζ), hence ζ-potential.

40532e184137.title: Zeta potential
40532e184137.sentence: However, zeta potential is not equal to the Stern potential or electric surface potential in the double layer, because these are defined at different locations.

0dd15418ef20.title: Zeta potential
0dd15418ef20.sentence: Nevertheless, zeta potential is often the only available path for characterization of double-layer properties.

c9b171d21f06.title: Zeta potential
c9b171d21f06.sentence: The zeta potential is an important and readily measurable indicator of the stability of colloidal dispersions.

04dd0b531a1e.title: Zeta potential
04dd0b531a1e.sentence: So, colloids with high zeta potential (negative or positive) are electrically stabilized while colloids with low zeta potentials tend to coagulate or flocculate as outlined in the table.

b578d700691c.title: Zeta potential
b578d700691c.sentence: In practice, the zeta potential of dispersion is measured by applying an electric field across the dispersion.

b2485daa384b.title: Zeta potential
b2485daa384b.sentence: Particles within the dispersion with a zeta potential will migrate toward the electrode of opposite charge with a velocity proportional to the magnitude of the zeta potential.

f87f765d6df1.title: Zeta potential
f87f765d6df1.sentence: This velocity is measured using the technique of the laser Doppler anemometer.

e19ba079ff2e.title: Zeta potential
e19ba079ff2e.sentence: Electrophoresis is used for estimating zeta potential of particulates, whereas streaming potential/current is used for porous bodies and flat surfaces.

7fb34f112361.title: Point of zero charge
7fb34f112361.sentence: Once satisfactory curves are obtained (acid/base amount—pH, and pH—zeta potential), the pzc is established as the common intersection point (cip) of the lines.

e563254a09a5.title: Allophane
e563254a09a5.sentence: Allophane is an amorphous to poorly crystalline hydrous aluminium silicate clay mineraloid.

c7a03faa4704.title: Allophane
c7a03faa4704.sentence: It typically forms under mildly acidic to neutral pH (5–7).

d00d85474ac8.title: Allophane
d00d85474ac8.sentence: Transmission electron micrographs show that it is generally made up of aggregates of hollow spherules ~3–5 nm in diameter.

4eaa166016e3.title: Allophane
4eaa166016e3.sentence: Its structure has been debated, but it is similar to clay minerals and is composed of curved alumina octahedral and silica tetrahedral layers.

845567f2e24e.title: Andisol
845567f2e24e.sentence: In USDA soil taxonomy, andisols are soils formed in volcanic ash and defined as soils containing high proportions of glass and amorphous colloidal materials, including allophane, imogolite and ferrihydrite.

9e120addd9e8.title: USDA soil taxonomy
9e120addd9e8.sentence: - Andisols: Form from volcanic ejecta, dominated by allophane or Al-humic complexes; Must have andic soil properties: high in poorly crystalline Fe and Al minerals, high in phosphorus, low bulk density, and high proportions of glass and amorphous colloidal materials, such as allophane, imogolite and ferrihydrite; high organic matter content, sometimes melanic epipedon; 0.7% of global and 1.7% of U.S. ice-free land.

cafc68035e8a.title: Imogolite
cafc68035e8a.sentence: Imogolite is an aluminium silicate clay mineral with the chemical formula Al2SiO3(OH)4.

d49d0538a92c.title: Imogolite
d49d0538a92c.sentence: Imogolite consists of a network of nanotubes with an outer diameter of ca. 2 nm and an inner diameter of ca. 1 nm.

f7bea1b1e4b1.title: Imogolite
f7bea1b1e4b1.sentence: It occurs in soils formed from volcanic ash and was first described in 1962 for an occurrence in Uemura, Kumamoto prefecture, Kyushu Region, Japan.

2e816aa3bce3.title: Imogolite
2e816aa3bce3.sentence: Its name originates from the Japanese word imogo, which refers to the brownish yellow soil derived from volcanic ash.

d7ad14e339a0.title: Imogolite
d7ad14e339a0.sentence: The tube walls are formed by continuous Al(OH)3 (gibbsite) sheets and orthosilicate anions (O3SiOH groups).

c43b3e4dd52d.title: Imogolite
c43b3e4dd52d.sentence: It occurs together with allophane, quartz, cristobalite, gibbsite, vermiculite and limonite.

7eda9e714364.title: Andosol
7eda9e714364.sentence: If the tephras are more basic or the climate is dry, amorphous colloidal materials, including allophane and imogolite, develop, and the Andosols are given the Silandic qualifier.

8a2ef4732607.title: Palygorskite
8a2ef4732607.sentence: Palygorskite or attapulgite is a magnesium aluminium phyllosilicate with the chemical formula (Mg,Al)2Si4O10(OH)·4(H2O) that occurs in a type of clay soil common to the Southeastern United States.

4af7c54e548c.title: Palygorskite
4af7c54e548c.sentence: It is one of the types of fuller's earth and commonly occurs as a fibrous clay mineral.

0eb0ba1ff72d.title: Palygorskite
0eb0ba1ff72d.sentence: Unlike layered phyllosilicates such as smectites, palygorskite has a chain-like crystal structure (ribbons) consisting of continuous tetrahedral silica chains linked to octahedral sheets of magnesium and aluminum, each ribbon being linked to the next by inversion of SiO4 tetrahedra along a set of Si-O-Si bonds.

1e7506ee7796.title: Palygorskite
1e7506ee7796.sentence: Palygorskite typically forms in shallow lacustrine, fluvial, palustrine or pedogenic environments.

a4f1a8d845d9.title: Palygorskite
a4f1a8d845d9.sentence: Its formation is enhanced by semi-arid conditions characterized by high evaporation rates and alkaline waters enriched in magnesium and silica.

9c1d588fca4d.title: Palygorskite
9c1d588fca4d.sentence: The palygorskite component is an acicular bristle-like crystalline form that does not swell or expand and typically exhibits a high specific surface area, ranging from about 75 to 400 m²/g depending on composition and processing.

8a58fd0dd06d.title: Palygorskite
8a58fd0dd06d.section: Mining and usage > Agricultural and livestock uses
8a58fd0dd06d.sentence: In agriculture, palygorskite is used as a carrier for fertilizers and crop protection products and as a soil amendment that improves water retention, aeration and nutrient availability.

f3deb6f25655.title: Vermiculite
f3deb6f25655.sentence: Exfoliated vermiculite is combined with other materials such as peat or composted pine bark to produce soilless growing medium for the professional horticulturalist and for the home gardener.

ec1197b3a440.title: Vermiculite
ec1197b3a440.sentence: The mixture helps retain air, fertilizer, and moisture, releasing them as the plant requires them.

d6f18195fadb.title: Vermiculite
d6f18195fadb.sentence: These mixes promote faster root growth and give quick anchorage to young roots.

912069fe4c29.title: Vermiculite
912069fe4c29.sentence: Vermiculite, alone or mixed with soil or peat, is used to germinate seeds; very little watering is required.

126c0f4a93c3.title: Vermiculite
126c0f4a93c3.sentence: Where the native soil is heavy or sticky, gentle mixing of vermiculite as a soil conditioner—up to one-half the volume of the soil—is recommended.

0b58a405bc89.title: Vermiculite
0b58a405bc89.sentence: This creates air channels and allows the soil mix to breathe.

f4cdc832298d.title: Vermiculite
f4cdc832298d.sentence: Where soils are sandy, mixing of vermiculite into the soil will allow the soil to hold the water and air needed for growth.

d93a74ec3bc1.title: Agrominerals
d93a74ec3bc1.sentence: These include using perlite to enhance the aeration of the soil, using pumice to control evaporation while one can use vermiculites and zeolites to store moisture.

b4916b78a7a0.title: Colloid
b4916b78a7a0.sentence: The stability of a colloidal system is defined by particles remaining suspended in solution and depends on the interaction forces between the particles.

06147071fae1.title: Colloid
06147071fae1.sentence: A colloid is stable if the interaction energy due to attractive forces between the colloidal particles is less than kT, where k is the Boltzmann constant and T is the absolute temperature.

23639fa609b3.title: Colloid
23639fa609b3.sentence: If the interaction energy is greater than kT, the attractive forces will prevail, and the colloidal particles will begin to clump together.

f83d647a6d37.title: Colloid
f83d647a6d37.sentence: This process is referred to generally as aggregation, but is also referred to as flocculation, coagulation or precipitation.

36a8c3634f3f.title: Colloid
36a8c3634f3f.sentence: For example, coagulation can be used to describe irreversible, permanent aggregation where the forces holding the particles together are stronger than any external forces caused by stirring or mixing.

afbf0c64e241.title: Colloid
afbf0c64e241.sentence: Flocculation can be used to describe reversible aggregation involving weaker attractive forces, and the aggregate is usually called a floc.

2ec0a9311551.title: Colloid
2ec0a9311551.sentence: Aggregation causes sedimentation or creaming, therefore the colloid is unstable: if either of these processes occur the colloid will no longer be a suspension.

b0478ae2c1a9.title: Colloid
b0478ae2c1a9.sentence: Electrostatic stabilization and steric stabilization are the two main mechanisms for stabilization against aggregation.

63c3e5fee19d.title: Colloid
63c3e5fee19d.sentence: The charge of colloidal particles is structured in an electrical double layer, where the particles are charged on the surface, but then attract counterions (ions of opposite charge) which surround the particle.

d9dab63ad40b.title: Colloid
d9dab63ad40b.sentence: - Steric stabilization consists absorbing a layer of a polymer or surfactant on the particles to prevent them from getting close in the range of attractive forces.

e0394f8e0e3c.title: Colloid
e0394f8e0e3c.sentence: This can be accomplished by the addition of salt to a suspension to reduce the Debye screening length (the width of the electrical double layer) of the particles.

cc97b97394fa.title: Colloid
cc97b97394fa.sentence: It is also accomplished by changing the pH of a suspension to effectively neutralise the surface charge of the particles in suspension.

13a022ef0467.title: Colloid
13a022ef0467.sentence: This removes the repulsive forces that keep colloidal particles separate and allows for aggregation due to van der Waals forces.

a53f0758cc3e.title: Colloid
a53f0758cc3e.sentence: When the magnitude of the zeta potential lies below a certain threshold, typically around ± 5mV, rapid coagulation or aggregation tends to occur.

e06a4c8d9a5c.title: Colloid
e06a4c8d9a5c.sentence: Polymer flocculants can bridge individual colloidal particles by attractive electrostatic interactions.

e38dd04d1e8e.title: Colloid
e38dd04d1e8e.sentence: For example, negatively charged colloidal silica or clay particles can be flocculated by the addition of a positively charged polymer.

400f519f8b2d.title: Colloid
400f519f8b2d.sentence: However, colloidal suspensions of higher-volume fraction form colloidal gels with viscoelastic properties.

4acc55a1df37.title: Colloid
4acc55a1df37.sentence: Viscoelastic colloidal gels, such as bentonite and toothpaste, flow like liquids under shear, but maintain their shape when shear is removed.

9d7f4d233f5b.title: Particle aggregation
9d7f4d233f5b.sentence: Particle agglomeration refers to the formation of assemblages in a suspension and represents a mechanism leading to the functional destabilization of colloidal systems.

baf9ae799db3.title: Particle aggregation
baf9ae799db3.sentence: During this process, particles dispersed in the liquid phase stick to each other, and spontaneously form irregular particle assemblages, flocs, or agglomerates.

17e1e6e3c744.title: Particle aggregation
17e1e6e3c744.sentence: This phenomenon is also referred to as coagulation or flocculation and such a suspension is also called unstable.

ccb565b54dbb.title: Particle aggregation
ccb565b54dbb.sentence: Particle agglomeration can be induced by adding salts or other chemicals referred to as coagulant or flocculant.

fb0a75fc3a91.title: Particle aggregation
fb0a75fc3a91.sentence: Particle agglomeration can be a reversible or irreversible process.

8b9b0d435a07.title: Particle aggregation
8b9b0d435a07.sentence: In the course of agglomeration, the agglomerates will grow in size, and as a consequence they may settle to the bottom of the container, which is referred to as sedimentation.

8f02bc6128fb.title: Particle aggregation
8f02bc6128fb.sentence: Alternatively, a colloidal gel may form in concentrated suspensions which changes its rheological properties.

0bc7e94a33b8.title: Particle aggregation
0bc7e94a33b8.sentence: The reverse process whereby particle agglomerates are re-dispersed as individual particles, referred to as peptization, hardly occurs spontaneously, but may occur under stirring or shear.

c96693bc8d1a.title: Particle aggregation
c96693bc8d1a.sentence: When salt is added to the suspension, the electrical double layer repulsion is screened, and van der Waals attraction become dominant and induce fast aggregation.

c54dac58200d.title: Particle aggregation
c54dac58200d.sentence: Since absolute aggregation rates are difficult to measure, one often refers to the dimensionless stability ratio W, defined as W=kfastk where kfast is the aggregation rate coefficient in the fast regime, and k the coefficient at the conditions of interest.

124c6828f597.title: Particle aggregation
124c6828f597.sentence: The stability ratio is close to unity in the fast regime, increases in the slow regime, and becomes very large when the suspension is stable.

fc73791d57fa.title: Particle aggregation
fc73791d57fa.sentence: The table below summarizes the critical coagulation concentration (CCC) ranges for different net charge of the counter ion.

726b1d283513.title: Particle aggregation
726b1d283513.sentence: Since particles are frequently negatively charged, multivalent metal cations thus represent highly effective coagulants.

1cbaa1d4a2ab.title: Particle aggregation
1cbaa1d4a2ab.sentence: Other mechanisms of colloid stabilization are equally possible, particularly, involving polymers.

c70e2d670cb3.title: Particle aggregation
c70e2d670cb3.sentence: When polymers chains adsorb to particles loosely, a polymer chain may bridge two particles, and induce bridging forces.

319659a88241.title: Particle aggregation
319659a88241.sentence: This situation is referred to as bridging flocculation.

1590e120eeb9.title: Particle aggregation
1590e120eeb9.sentence: When particle aggregation is solely driven by diffusion, one refers to perikinetic aggregation.

2add951ce92b.title: Particle aggregation
2add951ce92b.sentence: Aggregation can be enhanced through shear stress (e.g., stirring).

61590763cca2.title: Particle aggregation
61590763cca2.sentence: The latter case is called orthokinetic aggregation.

7b1c837fa112.title: Particle aggregation
7b1c837fa112.sentence: They are examples of mass fractals, whereby their mass M grows with their typical size characterized by the radius of gyration Rg as a power-law

133ab001fdbd.title: Particle aggregation
133ab001fdbd.sentence: Depending whether the aggregation is fast or slow, one refers to diffusion limited cluster aggregation (DLCA) or reaction limited cluster aggregation (RLCA).

ba5d8b1eac7b.title: Particle aggregation
ba5d8b1eac7b.sentence: DLCA clusters are loose and ramified (d ≈ 1.8), while the RLCA clusters are more compact (d ≈ 2.1).

fbc397361637.title: Muscovite
fbc397361637.sentence: Muscovite (also known as common mica, isinglass, or potash mica) is a hydrated phyllosilicate mineral of aluminium and potassium with formula KAl2(AlSi3O10)(OH)2.

007b477d1b0a.title: Muscovite
007b477d1b0a.sentence: Like all mica minerals, muscovite is a phyllosilicate (sheet silicate) mineral with a TOT-c structure.

47f870e10d0b.title: Muscovite
47f870e10d0b.sentence: In other words, a crystal of muscovite consists of layers (TOT) bonded to each other by potassium cations (c).

738b07d7fbf4.title: Muscovite
738b07d7fbf4.sentence: The relatively strong binding between oxygen anions and aluminium and silicon cations within a layer, compared with the weaker binding of potassium cations between layers, gives muscovite its perfect basal cleavage.

5f7acebf4a39.title: Muscovite
5f7acebf4a39.sentence: It has a highly perfect basal cleavage yielding remarkably thin laminae (sheets) which are often highly elastic.

60bb08479169.title: Muscovite
60bb08479169.sentence: Muscovite is the most common mica, found in granites, pegmatites, gneisses, and schists, and as a contact metamorphic rock or as a secondary mineral resulting from the alteration of topaz, feldspar, kyanite, etc. It is characteristic of peraluminous rock, in which the content of aluminum is relatively high.

a659deea2c14.title: Muscovite
a659deea2c14.sentence: The other common mica, biotite, is almost always much darker in color than muscovite.

08e8deb98df2.title: Muscovite
08e8deb98df2.sentence: Pyrophyllite and talc are softer than micas and have a greasy feel, while chlorite is green in color and its cleavage sheets are inelastic.

a2712f3873d1.title: Muscovite
a2712f3873d1.sentence: Up to 10% of the potassium may be replaced by sodium, and up to 20% of the hydroxide by fluorine.

1080e73055d0.title: Muscovite
1080e73055d0.sentence: Muscovite in which the mole fraction of silicon is greater than aluminium, and magnesium or iron replaces some of the aluminium to maintain charge balance, is called phengite.

b6ff0a6f7c00.title: X-ray diffraction
b6ff0a6f7c00.sentence: X-ray diffraction is a generic term for phenomena associated with changes in the direction of X-ray beams due to interactions with the electrons around atoms.

c2a2cc818c60.title: X-ray diffraction
c2a2cc818c60.sentence: It occurs due to elastic scattering, when there is no change in the energy of the waves.

55e99910ad9c.title: X-ray diffraction
55e99910ad9c.sentence: The resulting map of the directions of the X-rays far from the sample is called a diffraction pattern.

a616c5b73ebe.title: X-ray diffraction
a616c5b73ebe.section: Introduction to x-ray diffraction theory > Basics
a616c5b73ebe.sentence: Although these waves cancel one another out in most directions through destructive interference, they add constructively in a few specific directions.

b1d27361b50c.title: X-ray diffraction
b1d27361b50c.section: Introduction to x-ray diffraction theory > Basics
b1d27361b50c.sentence: An intuitive understanding of X-ray diffraction can be obtained from the Bragg model of diffraction.

4898910e4ce1.title: X-ray diffraction
4898910e4ce1.section: Introduction to x-ray diffraction theory > Basics
4898910e4ce1.sentence: In this model, a given reflection is associated with a set of evenly spaced sheets running through the crystal, usually passing through the centers of the atoms of the crystal lattice.

4dde34b2c086.title: X-ray diffraction
4dde34b2c086.section: Introduction to x-ray diffraction theory > Scattering amplitudes
4dde34b2c086.sentence: X-ray scattering is determined by the density of electrons within the crystal.

daad252592c3.title: X-ray diffraction
daad252592c3.section: Introduction to x-ray diffraction theory > Scattering amplitudes
daad252592c3.sentence: Hence the atomic nuclei, which are much heavier than an electron, contribute negligibly to the scattered X-rays.

3f8c0c48d6b1.title: X-ray diffraction
3f8c0c48d6b1.sentence: In such systems, electrons are boiled off of a cathode and accelerated through a strong electric potential of ~50 kV; having reached a high speed, the electrons collide with a metal plate, emitting bremsstrahlung and some strong spectral lines corresponding to the excitation of inner-shell electrons of the metal.

50bdd7a4a93a.title: X-ray diffraction
50bdd7a4a93a.sentence: The most common metal used is copper, which can be kept cool easily due to its high thermal conductivity, and which produces strong Kα and Kβ lines.

e16879027e9e.title: X-ray diffraction
e16879027e9e.sentence: Synchrotron radiation sources are some of the brightest light sources on earth and are some of the most powerful tools available for X-ray diffraction and crystallography.

3391f8de435e.title: X-ray diffraction
3391f8de435e.sentence: If single crystals of sufficient size cannot be obtained, various other X-ray methods can be applied to obtain less detailed information; such methods include fiber diffraction, powder diffraction and (if the sample is not crystallized) small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS).

d54b46d37ad6.title: X-ray diffraction
d54b46d37ad6.sentence: Bragg's view proved unpopular and the observation of X-ray diffraction by Max von Laue in 1912 confirmed that X-rays are a form of electromagnetic radiation.

5fcd0a4ce252.title: X-ray diffraction
5fcd0a4ce252.sentence: Therefore, neutron scattering is useful for observing the positions of light atoms with few electrons, especially hydrogen, which is essentially invisible in X-ray diffraction.

9b1833c81d3e.title: X-ray diffraction
9b1833c81d3e.sentence: Because they interact via the Coulomb forces the scattering of electrons by matter is 1000 or more times stronger than for X-rays.

04f4383e4ef5.title: Dispersion (chemistry)
04f4383e4ef5.sentence: A dispersion is a system in which distributed particles of one material are dispersed in a continuous phase of another material.

7eb4544e584d.title: Dispersion (chemistry)
7eb4544e584d.sentence: Dispersions are classified in a number of different ways, including how large the particles are in relation to the particles of the continuous phase, whether or not precipitation occurs, and the presence of Brownian motion.

880beb1e9156.title: Dispersion (chemistry)
880beb1e9156.sentence: In general, dispersions of particles sufficiently large for sedimentation are called suspensions, while those of smaller particles are called colloids and solutions.

a9c99bd05f99.title: Dispersion (chemistry)
a9c99bd05f99.sentence: Dispersion is a process by which (in the case of solid dispersing in a liquid) agglomerated particles are separated from each other, and a new interface between the inner surface of the liquid dispersion medium and the surface of the dispersed particles is generated.

32ebb4eeedf2.title: Dispersion (chemistry)
32ebb4eeedf2.sentence: This process is facilitated by molecular diffusion and convection.

13f3a44f7c4d.title: Dispersion (chemistry)
13f3a44f7c4d.sentence: Although both transport phenomena contribute to the dispersion of a material into the bulk, the mechanism of dispersion is primarily driven by convection in cases where there is significant turbulent flow in the bulk.

43b842398146.title: Dispersion (chemistry)
43b842398146.sentence: Diffusion is the dominant mechanism in the process of dispersion in cases of little to no turbulence in the bulk, where molecular diffusion is able to facilitate dispersion over a long period of time.

c976dfc38cd6.title: Dispersion (chemistry)
c976dfc38cd6.sentence: This is the reason why some liquid dispersions turn to become gels or even solid at a concentration of a dispersed phase above a critical concentration (which is dependent on particle size and interfacial tension).

9ce96f488164.title: Kaolinite
9ce96f488164.sentence: Low-temperature synthesis of clay minerals (with kaolinite as an example) has several aspects.

d6fbd2ebb39d.title: Kaolinite
d6fbd2ebb39d.sentence: This transformation seems to take place in soils without major changes in the environment, in a relatively short period of time, and at ambient temperature (and pressure).

f8948be76d30.title: Kaolinite
f8948be76d30.sentence: Fripiat and Herbillon (1971), in a review on the formation of kaolinite, raised the fundamental question how a disordered material (i.e., the amorphous fraction of tropical soils) could ever be transformed into a corresponding ordered structure.

ca88647c8e8a.title: Kaolinite
ca88647c8e8a.sentence: In the first place the silicic acid to be supplied to the growing crystal must be in a monomeric form, i.e., silica should be present in very dilute solution (Caillère et al., 1957; Caillère and Hénin, 1960; Wey and Siffert, 1962; Millot, 1970).

c4465f41d150.title: Kaolinite
c4465f41d150.sentence: The second aspect of the low-temperature synthesis of kaolinite is that the aluminium cations must be hexacoordinated with respect to oxygen (Caillère and Hénin, 1947; Caillère et al., 1953; Hénin and Robichet, 1955).

6efaa9ad2fbd.title: Kaolinite
6efaa9ad2fbd.sentence: Gastuche et al. (1962) and Caillère and Hénin (1962) have concluded that kaolinite can only ever be formed when the aluminium hydroxide is in the form of gibbsite.

eca02255fac2.title: Kaolinite
eca02255fac2.sentence: it can be seen that five molecules of water must be removed from the reaction for every molecule of kaolinite formed.

61ce676d44ea.title: Kaolinite
61ce676d44ea.sentence: While studying soil formation on a basaltic rock in Kivu (Zaïre), they noted how the occurrence of kaolinite depended on the "degrée de drainage" of the area involved.

596e32800f43.title: Kaolinite
596e32800f43.sentence: A clear distinction was found between areas with good drainage (i.e., areas with a marked difference between wet and dry seasons) and those areas with poor drainage (i.e., perennially swampy areas).

0aa1d46e6772.title: Kaolinite
0aa1d46e6772.sentence: Kaolinite was only found in the areas with distinct seasonal alternations between wet and dry.

a0bbab6111d0.title: Kaolinite
a0bbab6111d0.sentence: The possible significance of alternating wet and dry conditions on the transition of allophane into kaolinite has been stressed by Tamura and Jackson (1953).

9639b2edafa9.title: Aluminosilicate
9639b2edafa9.sentence: Aluminosilicate refers to materials containing anionic Si-O-Al linkages.

3b9df6db9a0e.title: Aluminosilicate
3b9df6db9a0e.sentence: Commonly, the associate cations are sodium (Na+), potassium (K+) and Hydrogen (H+).

bfe1014c949f.title: Aluminosilicate
bfe1014c949f.sentence: Such materials occur as minerals, coal combustion products and as synthetic materials, often in the form of zeolites.

0367ed83fdb5.title: Aluminosilicate
0367ed83fdb5.sentence: Both synthetic and natural aluminosilicates are of technical significance as structural materials, catalysts, and reagents.

ccdc088243c9.title: Aluminosilicate
ccdc088243c9.sentence: Feldspar is a common tectosilicate aluminosilicate mineral made of potassium, sodium, and calcium cations surrounded by a negatively charged network of silicon, aluminium and oxygen atoms.

647c9c58d616.title: Soil matrix
647c9c58d616.section: Mineral colloids: soil clays > Alumino-silica clays
647c9c58d616.sentence: Alumino-silica clays or aluminosilicate clays are characterized by their regular crystalline or quasi-crystalline structure.

f106dbbed17e.title: Aluminosilicate
f106dbbed17e.sentence: Naturally occurring microporous, hydrous aluminosilicate minerals are also referred to as zeolites.

9036c9edc87f.title: Aluminosilicate
9036c9edc87f.sentence: The Si/Al ratio is variable, which provides a means to tune the properties.

097f393d5652.title: DLVO theory
097f393d5652.sentence: In physical chemistry, the Derjaguin–Landau–Verwey–Overbeek (DLVO) theory explains the aggregation and kinetic stability of aqueous dispersions quantitatively and describes the force between charged surfaces interacting through a liquid medium.

7c5ae536f48e.title: DLVO theory
7c5ae536f48e.sentence: It combines the effects of the van der Waals attraction and the electrostatic repulsion due to the so-called double layer of counterions.

615ba03cbd21.title: DLVO theory
615ba03cbd21.sentence: The total potential energy is described as the sum of the attraction potential and the repulsion potential.

44c00ed70fc0.title: DLVO theory
44c00ed70fc0.sentence: When two particles approach each other, electrostatic repulsion increases and the interference between their electrical double layers increases.

4d4ffa850784.title: DLVO theory
4d4ffa850784.sentence: However, the Van der Waals attraction also increases as they get closer.

0ba9f276effa.title: DLVO theory
0ba9f276effa.sentence: At very close distances, the combination of these forces results in a deep attractive well, which is referred to as the primary minimum.

5926f1bfd6ce.title: DLVO theory
5926f1bfd6ce.sentence: At larger distances, the energy profile goes through a maximum, or energy barrier, and subsequently passes through a shallow minimum, which is referred to as the secondary minimum.

5b6247590d89.title: DLVO theory
5b6247590d89.sentence: The maximum energy needs to be greater than the thermal energy.

7c28f83fcad1.title: DLVO theory
7c28f83fcad1.sentence: Otherwise, particles will aggregate due to the attraction potential.

6d2d6a9a1c69.title: DLVO theory
6d2d6a9a1c69.sentence: The height of the barrier indicates how stable the system is.

ab49fb3388b5.title: DLVO theory
ab49fb3388b5.sentence: Particles coagulate and this process is not reversible.

f935307420ca.title: DLVO theory
f935307420ca.sentence: However, when the maximum energy barrier is too high to overcome, the colloid particles may stay in the secondary minimum, where particles are held together but more weakly than in the primary minimum.

1882c37154b6.title: DLVO theory
1882c37154b6.sentence: Particles form weak attractions but are easily redispersed.

14ad4f4c9c13.title: DLVO theory
14ad4f4c9c13.sentence: In 1941, Boris Derjaguin and Lev Landau introduced a theory for the stability of colloidal dispersions that invoked a fundamental instability driven by strong but short-ranged van der Waals attractions countered by the stabilizing influence of electrostatic repulsions.

bef8e2ec7bbd.title: DLVO theory
bef8e2ec7bbd.sentence: In 1948, Evert Verwey and Theodor Overbeek independently arrived at the same result.

d8ba52e0acb3.title: DLVO theory
d8ba52e0acb3.sentence: This so-called DLVO theory resolved the failure of the Levine–Dube theory to account for the dependence of colloidal dispersions' stability on the ionic strength of the electrolyte.

eebb64cd8d5c.title: DLVO theory
eebb64cd8d5c.sentence: This theory did not explain the observed instability of colloidal dispersions against irreversible aggregation in solutions of high ionic strength.

9d82b1ff9f2b.title: DLVO theory
9d82b1ff9f2b.sentence: - κ is the inverse of the Debye–Hückel screening length (λD); κ is given by κ2=4πλBn, and

ea42d39ef20c.title: DLVO theory
ea42d39ef20c.sentence: Additional forces beyond the DLVO construct have been reported to also play a major role in determining colloid stability.

91acb90a83ec.title: DLVO theory
91acb90a83ec.sentence: DLVO theory is not effective in describing ordering processes such as the evolution of colloidal crystals in dilute dispersions with low salt concentrations.

455d2c310c87.title: Halloysite
455d2c310c87.sentence: Halloysite is an aluminosilicate clay mineral with the empirical formula Al2Si2O5(OH)4.

58a4d2da2c9a.title: Halloysite
58a4d2da2c9a.sentence: It is a member of the kaolinite group.

447f812e427a.title: Halloysite
447f812e427a.sentence: Halloysite occurs primarily in recently exposed volcanic-derived soils, but it also forms from primary minerals in tropical soils or pre-glacially weathered materials.

bdbb6334f2dd.title: Halloysite
bdbb6334f2dd.sentence: Igneous rocks, especially glassy basaltic rocks are more susceptible to weathering and alteration forming halloysite.

044505d4ed0b.title: Halloysite
044505d4ed0b.sentence: Halloysite naturally occurs as small cylinders (nanotubes) that have a wall thickness of 10–15 atomic aluminosilicate sheets, an outer diameter of 50–60 nm, an inner diameter of 12–15 nm, and a length of 0.5–10 μm.

92b8a3f14c1f.title: Halloysite
92b8a3f14c1f.sentence: When hydrated, the clay exhibits a 1 nm spacing of the layers, and when dehydrated (meta-halloysite), the spacing is 0.7 nm.

2d09e474d808.title: Halloysite
2d09e474d808.sentence: The cation exchange capacity depends on the amount of hydration, as 2H2O has 5–10 meq/100 g, while 4H2O has 40–50 meq/100g.

fc13955ca9e8.title: Montmorillonite
fc13955ca9e8.sentence: Montmorillonite can then transform to palygorskite under dry conditions and to halloysite-10Å (endellite) in acidic conditions (pH 5 or lower).

5e0c01eb2cb3.title: Soil matrix
5e0c01eb2cb3.section: Mineral colloids: soil clays > Amorphous clays
5e0c01eb2cb3.sentence: They are mixtures of alumina and silica which have not formed the ordered crystal shape of alumino-silica clays which time would provide.

61b9883fd258.title: Soil matrix
61b9883fd258.section: Mineral colloids: soil clays > Amorphous clays
61b9883fd258.sentence: Amorphous clays are young, and commonly found in recent volcanic ash deposits such as tephra.

aaf782b2ed97.title: Soil matrix
aaf782b2ed97.section: Mineral colloids: soil clays > Amorphous clays
aaf782b2ed97.sentence: The majority of their negative charges originates from hydroxyl ions, which can gain or lose a hydrogen ion (H+) in response to soil pH, in such way as to buffer the soil pH.

739d81b6d204.title: Soil matrix
739d81b6d204.section: Mineral colloids: soil clays > Amorphous clays
739d81b6d204.sentence: They may have either a negative charge provided by the attached hydroxyl ion (OH−), which can attract a cation, or lose the hydrogen of the hydroxyl to solution and display a positive charge which can attract anions.

0b9f0fd1c422.title: Peptization
0b9f0fd1c422.sentence: The peptization of a liquid mixture is the process of converting the mixture into a colloid by shaking it with a suitable electrolyte called a peptizing agent.

37c3ecbefb95.title: Peptization
37c3ecbefb95.sentence: That is, the insoluble solid particles which have settled out of the mixture (i.e. the precipitate) are reformed into microscopic particles suspended in the mixture.

6206b234088d.title: Peptization
6206b234088d.sentence: Peptization is the reverse of flocculation, the aggregation of colloidal particles into precipitate; as such, it is also known as deflocculation.

ef3ffc1882a0.title: Peptization
ef3ffc1882a0.sentence: More correctly speaking, the electrical double layer existing at the surface of the particles is compressed by the added electrolyte and collapses at high ionic strength.

81acba89cd2b.title: Peptization
81acba89cd2b.sentence: The electrical repulsion no longer hinders the aggregation of particles and they can then coalesce to form a flocculent precipitate that is easy to filter.

5db0cc56334d.title: Peptization
5db0cc56334d.sentence: If the precipitate is washed with an excessive volume of deionised water, the electrical double layer present at the surface of the particles expands again and the electrical repulsion reappears: the precipitate peptizes and the particles pass again through the filter.

e900d950b383.title: Peptization
e900d950b383.sentence: Freshly precipitated aluminium or iron hydroxide is extremely difficult to filter because the very fine colloidal particles directly pass through a paper filter.

281bf90cce52.title: Sepiolite
281bf90cce52.sentence: Sepiolite, also known in English by the German loanword meerschaum (/ˈmɪərʃɔːm/ MEER-shawm, /-ʃəm/ -⁠shəm; German: [ˈmeːɐ̯ʃaʊm] ⓘ; meaning "sea foam"), is a soft white clay mineral, often used to make tobacco pipes (known as meerschaum pipes).

825c8e0c92bc.title: Sepiolite
825c8e0c92bc.sentence: A complex magnesium silicate, a typical chemical formula for which is Mg4Si6O15(OH)2·6H2O, it can be present in fibrous, fine-particulate, and solid forms.

c3d62fd1ab07.title: Sepiolite
c3d62fd1ab07.sentence: The fibrous clay minerals have been shown to exist as a continuous polysomatic series where the endmembers are sepiolite and palygorskite; there is a continuous variation in chemical composition from sepiolite, the most magnesic and trioctahedral endmember, to palygorskite, the least magnesic, most Al- and Fe-bearing, most dioctahedral endmember.

a7844c209184.title: Palygorskite
a7844c209184.sentence: Sepiolite is structurally similar but contains wider structural channels and exhibits a higher magnesium and lower aluminum content.

3990c49f6d35.title: Sepiolite
3990c49f6d35.sentence: Sepiolite occurs as a secondary mineral associated with serpentine.

8cdb8eb8556b.title: Sepiolite
8cdb8eb8556b.sentence: It can occur as a precipitate in arid environments.

18cb73628fb4.title: Sepiolite
18cb73628fb4.sentence: Significant quantities of sepiolite occur in soils of the arid west of South Africa.

0a556b528b94.title: Sepiolite
0a556b528b94.sentence: There is a geographic variation from the sepiolite-containing soils at the coast to palygorskite-containing soils inland that mirrors the sepiolite-palygorskite compositional continuum from sepiolite, the most magnesic and trioctahedral endmember at the coast, to palygorskite, the least magnesic endmember farthest inland.

06f7a8530d95.title: Sepiolite
06f7a8530d95.sentence: The positive environment effect in the arid region is that sepiolite increases plant available water in the sandy soils.

a728cccd81d6.title: Sepiolite
a728cccd81d6.sentence: A negative effect is that the cemented sepiolite causes considerable geotechnical and geometallurgical difficulty for extracting the heavy minerals from the sepiolite-rich sands.

9a33d38be6c2.title: Sepiolite
9a33d38be6c2.sentence: Sepiolite-cemented material has been termed "sepiocrete" as calcrete, silcrete or ferricrete is used to refer to materials cemented by calcite, silica or iron.

73ee5c680168.title: Sepiolite
73ee5c680168.sentence: Soils that contain significant quantities of sepiolite may be more appropriately termed "sepiolitic" or "petrosepiolitic" depending on the degree of cementation.

ff8ef79b1256.title: Clay mineral X-ray diffraction
ff8ef79b1256.sentence: X-rays are used to determine the crystal structure of materials.

b17c1c12b7fa.title: Clay mineral X-ray diffraction
b17c1c12b7fa.sentence: Chemically, clays are defined by crystal structure and chemical composition, often determined by clay mineral X-ray diffraction.

a56154001f1b.title: Clay mineral X-ray diffraction
a56154001f1b.sentence: Because of this, clay minerals are typically identified by preparing samples so that they are oriented to increase basal (00l) reflection.

911fc4368db8.title: Clay mineral X-ray diffraction
911fc4368db8.sentence: Since the atoms are arranged in some order in crystals, they tend to diffract the beam at certain angles and at certain intensities.

8f3233861433.title: Clay mineral X-ray diffraction
8f3233861433.sentence: The angles of the diffracted X-rays and the crystal structure of the material is calculated.

88e0490185c8.title: Clay mineral X-ray diffraction
88e0490185c8.sentence: It is also possible to determine if the material is not crystalline.

9768405618f9.title: Clay mineral X-ray diffraction
9768405618f9.sentence: Randomly oriented XRD samples are not as useful for clay minerals because clays typically have similar X and Y dimensions.

0cf11e6a24e3.title: Clay mineral X-ray diffraction
0cf11e6a24e3.sentence: The Z dimension differs from clay to clay and is most diagnostic because the Z dimension represents the height of the tetrahedral-octahedral (T-O) or tetrahedral-octahedral-tetrahedral (T-O-T) layer.

f4cbeff22343.title: Clay mineral X-ray diffraction
f4cbeff22343.sentence: The Z dimension can increase or decrease because of substitution of the central cation in both the tetrahedral and octahedral layers.

cfb6733445c3.title: Clay mineral X-ray diffraction
cfb6733445c3.sentence: The presence and size of a charge balancing cation in the inter-layer of T-O-T clays will also effect the Z dimension.

9ea9f3f31d82.title: Clay mineral X-ray diffraction
9ea9f3f31d82.sentence: D positions are calculated using Bragg’s law but because clay mineral analysis is one dimensional, l can substitute n, making the equation l λ = 2d sin Θ.

c07faa83bf19.title: Clay mineral X-ray diffraction
c07faa83bf19.sentence: When measuring the x-ray diffraction of clays, d is constant and λ is the known wavelength from the x-ray source, so the distance from one 00l peak to another is equal.

57ecb67e149a.title: Clay mineral X-ray diffraction
57ecb67e149a.section: X-ray diffraction of clays > Identification of clays using XRD
57ecb67e149a.sentence: Well-defined crystalline minerals have sharp peaks while clays, which range from crystalline to noncrystalline, produce broad peaks with noticeable width on both sides.

17df39f50b42.title: Clay mineral X-ray diffraction
17df39f50b42.section: X-ray diffraction of clays > Identification of clays using XRD
17df39f50b42.sentence: These peaks can be compared to known diffraction patterns for better identification but if some peaks are broader than others, it is likely that multiple clays are present.

256d16cd3dcb.title: Clay mineral X-ray diffraction
256d16cd3dcb.section: X-ray diffraction of clays > Identification of clays using XRD
256d16cd3dcb.sentence: The Clay Mineral Society maintains a collection clays for the purpose of comparison to unknown clays.

16ab4b444bc2.title: Clay mineral X-ray diffraction
16ab4b444bc2.section: X-ray diffraction of clays > Identification of clays using XRD
16ab4b444bc2.sentence: Diffraction patterns calculated using theoretical methods do not generally match with experimental diffraction patterns, so using diffraction patterns from known samples to help identify a clay is preferable to calculation.

ecc2ec2f9561.title: Clay mineral X-ray diffraction
ecc2ec2f9561.section: X-ray diffraction of clays > Identification of clays using XRD
ecc2ec2f9561.sentence: Clay minerals are almost always mixed with very small amounts of nonclay minerals which can produce intense peaks, even when there is very little of the sample is not a clay.

bd13f24cb319.title: Clay mineral X-ray diffraction
bd13f24cb319.section: X-ray diffraction of clays > Identification of clays using XRD
bd13f24cb319.sentence: Some common minerals associated with naturally occurring clays are; quartz, feldspars, zeolites, and carbonates organic matter is sometimes present.

fe7dc11111d3.title: Clay mineral X-ray diffraction
fe7dc11111d3.section: Preparation for clay mineral X-ray diffraction
fe7dc11111d3.sentence: Nonclay minerals can usually be separated by sieving samples at a small enough mesh.

c482effeb889.title: Clay mineral X-ray diffraction
c482effeb889.section: Preparation for clay mineral X-ray diffraction
c482effeb889.sentence: Lightly crushing breaks apart the soft clays while keeping harder nonclays intact for easier removal.

a891d6634735.title: Clay mineral X-ray diffraction
a891d6634735.section: Preparation for clay mineral X-ray diffraction
a891d6634735.sentence: Four methods are commonly used for sample preparation and vary in difficulty and appropriateness of use.

39089514d9a9.title: Clay mineral X-ray diffraction
39089514d9a9.section: Preparation for clay mineral X-ray diffraction > Glass slide method
39089514d9a9.sentence: Easiest and fastest of the four commonly used methods but also the least accurate.

4d7b10579e04.title: Clay mineral X-ray diffraction
4d7b10579e04.section: Preparation for clay mineral X-ray diffraction > Centrifuged porous plate
4d7b10579e04.sentence: Produces the best diffraction patterns out of the four most common methods but requires the most skill and is most time-consuming.

df267e41c041.title: Clay mineral X-ray diffraction
df267e41c041.section: Preparation for clay mineral X-ray diffraction > Centrifuged porous plate
df267e41c041.sentence: Centrifuging forces the liquid through the porous plate leaving the sample behind to be dried below 100 °C. An advantage of this method is that exchangeable cations can be removed by passing a chloride solution through the plate once the sample has been dried.

b35634eed9e7.title: Hydrous oxide
b35634eed9e7.sentence: Hydrous oxides are inorganic compounds of a metal, hydroxide, and weakly bound water.

3b0e9d063fca.title: Hydrous oxide
3b0e9d063fca.sentence: - Hydrous thorium oxide (THO) and hydrous titanium oxide (TiHO)

692c8ab9148b.title: Hydrous oxide
692c8ab9148b.sentence: Some of them, such as HFO and HAO, are precipitated in highly porous poorly crystalline or amorphous forms and therefore are good adsorbents used for example in water treatment.

627eb99b4ae1.title: Hydrous oxide
627eb99b4ae1.sentence: HFO and HAO may also result from oxidative weathering of rocks to produce iron an aluminum hydrous oxide clay soils.

864d60ce2d78.title: Iron oxide
864d60ce2d78.sentence: An iron oxide is a chemical compound composed of iron and oxygen.

d2af2a8581e2.title: Iron oxide
d2af2a8581e2.sentence: Ferric oxyhydroxides are a related class of compounds, perhaps the best known of which is rust.

9e609eade20b.title: Iron oxide
9e609eade20b.sentence: Iron oxides feature as ferrous (Fe(II)) or ferric (Fe(III)) or both.

b8e88e5be718.title: Iron oxide
b8e88e5be718.sentence: Only a few oxides are significant at the earth's surface, particularly wüstite, magnetite, and hematite.

2628883d4258.title: Iron oxide
2628883d4258.sentence: - ferrihydrite (Fe5HO8 · 4 H2O approx., or 5 Fe2O3 · 9 H2O, better recast as FeOOH · 0.4 H2O)

a90a6a2924d9.title: Iron oxide
a90a6a2924d9.sentence: - green rust (FeIII xFeII yOH3x + y − z (A−)z where A− is Cl− or 0.5 SO2−4)

924f6535f091.title: Iron(III) oxide-hydroxide
924f6535f091.sentence: Goethite and lepidocrocite, both crystallizing in orthorhombic system, are the most common forms of iron(III) oxyhydroxide and the most important mineral carriers of iron in soils.

c58501038639.title: Iron(III) oxide-hydroxide
c58501038639.sentence: The color of iron(III) oxyhydroxide ranges from yellow through dark-brown to black, depending on the degree of hydration, particle size and shape, and crystal structure.

7c8fe02685b6.title: Iron oxide
7c8fe02685b6.sentence: Species of bacteria, including Shewanella oneidensis, Geobacter sulfurreducens and Geobacter metallireducens, use iron oxides as terminal electron acceptors.

25c45313fcfb.title: Iron(III) oxide-hydroxide
25c45313fcfb.sentence: Iron(III) oxyhydroxide precipitates from solutions of iron(III) salts at pH between 6.5 and 8.

017f1fba3185.title: Iron(III) oxide-hydroxide
017f1fba3185.sentence: The compound also readily forms when iron(II) hydroxide is exposed to air:

f3ce94723e0c.title: Iron(III) oxide-hydroxide
f3ce94723e0c.sentence: Iron oxide-hydroxide is also used in aquarium water treatment as a phosphate binder.

5d688df25ce5.title: Iron(III) oxide-hydroxide
5d688df25ce5.sentence: Iron oxide-hydroxide nanoparticles have been studied as possible adsorbents for lead removal from aquatic media.

7289cc0a9e3b.title: Lepidocrocite
7289cc0a9e3b.sentence: Lepidocrocite (γ-FeO(OH)), also called esmeraldite or hydrohematite, is an iron oxide-hydroxide mineral.

9018187dc0b5.title: Lepidocrocite
9018187dc0b5.sentence: It is red to reddish brown and forms when iron-containing substances rust underwater.

01063806fbda.title: Lepidocrocite
01063806fbda.sentence: Lepidocrocite is commonly found in the weathering of primary iron minerals and in iron ore deposits.

c24d7afe13e5.title: Lepidocrocite
c24d7afe13e5.sentence: The structure of lepidocrocite is similar to the boehmite structure found in bauxite and consists of layered iron(III) oxide octahedra bonded by hydrogen bonding via hydroxide layers.

1808adef7522.title: Lepidocrocite
1808adef7522.sentence: This relatively weakly bonded layering accounts for the scaley habit of the mineral.

ed21491306ab.title: Green rust
ed21491306ab.sentence: In oxidizing environment, green rust generally turns into Fe3+ oxyhydroxides, namely α-FeOOH (goethite) and γ-FeOOH (lepidocrocite).

3ff91498e10f.title: Lepidocrocite
3ff91498e10f.sentence: It was first described in 1813 from the Zlaté Hory polymetallic ore deposit in Moravia, Czech Republic.

43cac5a50a51.title: Lepidocrocite
43cac5a50a51.sentence: The name is from the Greek lipis for scale and krokis for fibre.

5275eaf24aa4.title: Maghemite
5275eaf24aa4.sentence: Maghemite (Fe2O3, γ-Fe2O3) is a member of the family of iron oxides.

933e9182b02f.title: Maghemite
933e9182b02f.sentence: It has the same formula as hematite, but the same spinel ferrite structure as magnetite (Fe3O4) and is also ferrimagnetic.

f6d686f57770.title: Maghemite
f6d686f57770.sentence: Maghemite forms by weathering or low-temperature oxidation of spinels containing iron(II) such as magnetite or titanomagnetite.

41c7f4a81eec.title: Maghemite
41c7f4a81eec.sentence: Maghemite can also form through dehydration and transformation of certain iron oxyhydroxide minerals, such as lepidocrocite and ferrihydrite.

8fac25fdd23a.title: Maghemite
8fac25fdd23a.sentence: It occurs as widespread brown or yellow pigment in terrestrial sediments and soils.

f01f2b5567db.title: Maghemite
f01f2b5567db.sentence: It is known to also form in areas that have been subjected to bushfires (particularly in the Leonora area of Western Australia) magnetising iron minerals.

c26754f6c9b4.title: Chernozem
c26754f6c9b4.sentence: Temperatures sufficient to elevate maghemite on a landscape scale indicate the influence of fire.

66bfceff3e0e.title: Geoarchaeology
66bfceff3e0e.sentence: The magnetic susceptibility of soil reflects the presence of magnetic iron-oxide minerals, such as maghemite.

3065b35da22a.title: Limonite
3065b35da22a.sentence: Limonite (/ˈlaɪməˌnaɪt/) is an iron ore consisting of a mixture of hydrated iron(III) oxide-hydroxides in varying composition.

a9e697edf27a.title: Limonite
a9e697edf27a.sentence: Although originally defined as a single mineral, limonite is now recognized as a field term for a mixture of related hydrated iron oxide minerals, among them goethite, lepidocrocite, akaganeite, and jarosite.

b10fcd022693.title: Limonite
b10fcd022693.sentence: Determination of the precise mineral composition is practical only with X-ray diffraction techniques.

ec7e9dbcb59e.title: Limonite
ec7e9dbcb59e.sentence: Limonite usually forms from the hydration of hematite and magnetite, from the oxidation and hydration of iron rich sulfide minerals, and chemical weathering of other iron rich minerals such as olivine, pyroxene, amphibole, and biotite.

34784b70ac33.title: Limonite
34784b70ac33.sentence: It is often the major iron component in lateritic soils, and limonite laterite ores are a source of nickel and potentially cobalt and other valuable metals, present as trace elements.

3f1b8f397861.title: Limonite
3f1b8f397861.sentence: Limonite is named for the Ancient Greek word λειμών (leimṓn [leː.mɔ̌ːn]), meaning "wet meadow", or λίμνη (límnē [lím.nɛː]), meaning "marshy lake", as an allusion to its occurrence as bog iron ore in meadows and marshes.

51d0e16fed72.title: Limonite
51d0e16fed72.sentence: The streak of limonite on an unglazed porcelain plate is always yellowish brown, a character which distinguishes it from hematite with a red streak, or from magnetite with a black streak.

0a80df546969.title: Specific surface area
0a80df546969.sentence: Specific surface area (SSA) is a property of solids defined as the total surface area (SA) of a material per unit mass, (with units of m2/kg or m2/g).

32b0498d96a9.title: Specific surface area
32b0498d96a9.sentence: For this reason, in addition to the most commonly used Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (N2-BET) adsorption method, several techniques have been developed to measure the specific surface area of particulate materials at ambient temperatures and at controllable scales, including methylene blue (MB) staining, ethylene glycol monoethyl ether (EGME) adsorption, electrokinetic analysis of complex-ion adsorption and a Protein Retention (PR) method.

b4859a740116.title: Specific surface area
b4859a740116.sentence: The SSA can be measured by adsorption using the BET isotherm.

ecf2cd0e60e7.title: Specific surface area
ecf2cd0e60e7.sentence: Values obtained for specific surface area depend on the method of measurement.

ce58246f9805.title: Specific surface area
ce58246f9805.sentence: In adsorption based methods, the size of the adsorbate molecule (the probe molecule), the exposed crystallographic planes at the surface and measurement temperature all affect the obtained specific surface area.

0bd14f343568.title: Specific surface area
0bd14f343568.sentence: The SSA can be simply calculated from a particle size distribution, making some assumption about the particle shape.

6126b714231c.title: Specific surface area
6126b714231c.sentence: This method, however, fails to account for surface associated with the surface texture of the particles.

668522bd5c2f.title: Specific surface area
668522bd5c2f.sentence: This has the advantage of measuring the surface of fine structures and deep texture on the particles.

f3c1f2579a5d.title: Specific surface area
f3c1f2579a5d.sentence: However, the results can differ markedly depending on the substance adsorbed.

bbc2fb6facfa.title: Specific surface area
bbc2fb6facfa.sentence: The method is simple and quick, and yields a result that often correlates well with the chemical reactivity of a powder.

588175b23fb4.title: Specific surface area
588175b23fb4.sentence: However, it fails to measure much of the deep surface texture.

3f1c25902579.title: Specific surface area
3f1c25902579.sentence: A number of international standards exist for the measurement of specific surface area, including ISO standard 9277.

8fc57d7f301c.title: Soil
8fc57d7f301c.sentence: - Isomorphous substitution occurs in clay during its formation, when lower-valence cations substitute for higher-valence cations in the crystal structure.

f856675e6d2d.title: Soil matrix
f856675e6d2d.section: Mineral colloids: soil clays > Alumino-silica clays
f856675e6d2d.sentence: The substitution of lower-valence cations for higher-valence cations (isomorphous substitution) gives clay a local negative charge on an oxygen atom that attracts and holds water and positively charged soil cations, some of which are of value for plant growth.

c6a9e38a0286.title: Soil matrix
c6a9e38a0286.section: Mineral colloids: soil clays > Alumino-silica clays
c6a9e38a0286.sentence: During the clay formation process, Al3+ may substitute for Si4+ in the silica layer, and as much as one fourth of the aluminium Al3+ may be substituted by Zn2+, Mg2+ or Fe2+ in the alumina layer.

a7b19e52a6ad.title: Smectite
a7b19e52a6ad.sentence: As the +4 charges born by Si(IV), and normally compensated by −4 charges from the surrounding oxygen atoms, become +3 due to the substitution of Si(IV) by Al(III), an electrical imbalance occurs: +3 −4 = −1.

0cd5155a9352.title: Smectite
0cd5155a9352.sentence: The same reasoning also applies to the gibbsite central layer of the TOT elementary unit when an Al3+ ion is replaced by a Mg2+ ion in a gibbsite octahedra.

65755782f679.title: Smectite
65755782f679.sentence: The excess of negative charges in the TOT layer has to be compensated by the presence of positive cations in the interlayer.

b194deba26a4.title: Soil
b194deba26a4.sentence: Substitutions in the outermost layers are more effective than for the innermost layers, as the electric charge strength drops off as the square of the distance.

774425242b96.title: Montmorillonite
774425242b96.sentence: Montmorillonite is a subclass of smectite, a 2:1 phyllosilicate mineral characterized as having greater than 50% octahedral charge; its cation exchange capacity is due to isomorphous substitution of Mg for Al in the central alumina plane.

f7c7b8f835b4.title: Montmorillonite
f7c7b8f835b4.sentence: In contrast, beidellite is smectite with greater than 50% tetrahedral charge originating from isomorphous substitution of Al for Si in the silica sheet.

80bb010ae9c5.title: Soil matrix
80bb010ae9c5.section: Mineral colloids: soil clays > Alumino-silica clays
80bb010ae9c5.sentence: As a result, kaolinite does not swell in water and has a low specific surface area, and as almost no isomorphous substitution has occurred it has a low CEC.

1590d0d9e571.title: Soil matrix
1590d0d9e571.section: Mineral colloids: soil clays > Alumino-silica clays
1590d0d9e571.sentence: Isomorphous substitution occurs during the clay's formation and does not change with time.

84569873fdea.title: Soil
84569873fdea.sentence: Unlike permanent charges developed by isomorphous substitution, pH-dependent charges are variable and increase with increasing pH.

95ffa8f7c7ec.title: Smectite
95ffa8f7c7ec.sentence: A smectite (from Ancient Greek σμηκτός (smēktós) 'lubricated'; from σμηκτρίς (smēktrís) 'walker's earth, fuller's earth'; lit. 'rubbing earth; earth that has the property of cleaning') is a mineral mixture of various swelling sheet silicates (phyllosilicates), which have a three-layer 2:1 (TOT) structure and belong to the clay minerals.

d566d625687b.title: Smectite
d566d625687b.sentence: Smectites mainly consist of montmorillonite, but can often contain secondary minerals such as quartz and calcite.

cfd18cd8a8a6.title: Smectite
cfd18cd8a8a6.sentence: In clay mineralogy, smectite is synonym of montmorillonite (also the name of a pure clay mineral phase) to indicate a class of swelling clays.

46a13f6ed869.title: Smectite
46a13f6ed869.sentence: The term smectite is commonly used in Europe and in the UK while the term montmorillonite is preferred in North America, but both terms are equivalent and can be used interchangeably.

729cf7ab6d77.title: Smectite
729cf7ab6d77.sentence: For industrial and commercial applications, the term bentonite is mostly used in place of smectite or montmorillonite.

9e59aa9701f2.title: Smectite
9e59aa9701f2.sentence: The 2:1 layer (TOT) structure consists of two silica (SiO2) tetrahedral (T) layers which are electrostatically cross-linked via an Al2O3 (gibbsite), or Fe2O3, octahedral (O) central layer.

85fe7cc4f4c8.title: Smectite
85fe7cc4f4c8.sentence: The TOT elementary layers are not rigidly connected to each other but are separated by a free space: the interlayer hosting hydrated cations and water molecules.

5bdd2e41c142.title: Smectite
5bdd2e41c142.sentence: Smectite can swell because of the reversible incorporation of water and cations in the interlayer space.

be0ac94c58c6.title: Smectite
be0ac94c58c6.sentence: The TOT layers are negatively charged because of the isomorphic substitution of Si(IV) atoms by Al(III) atoms in the two external silica tetrahedral layers and because of the replacement of Al(III) or Fe(III) atoms by Mg2+ or Fe2+ cations in the inner gibbsite octahedral layer.

7af1ee33c12a.title: Smectite
7af1ee33c12a.section: Role of interlayer cations in the swelling process
7af1ee33c12a.sentence: As the interlayer space of smectites is more open and so more easily accessible to water and cations, smectites exhibit the highest cation-exchange capacity (CEC) of clay minerals commonly found in the soils.

12453cdaabad.title: Smectite
12453cdaabad.sentence: Smectites are formed from the weathering of basalt, gabbro, and silica-rich volcanic glass (e.g., pumice, obsidian, rhyolite, dacite).

8dbec1d92791.title: Smectite
8dbec1d92791.sentence: Many smectites are formed in volcanic hydrothermal system (such as geyser system) where hot water percolating through the porous matrix or the cracks of the volcanic ash deposit (pumice, pozzolan) dissolves most of amorphous silica (up to 50 wt.% of SiO2 can be dissolved), leaving smectite in place.

27d36f9775a5.title: Smectite
27d36f9775a5.sentence: Because of silica hydrolysis, most of silica was dissolved in seawater and removed from the ashes giving rise to the formation of smectites.

00c48e560e04.title: Atterberg limits
00c48e560e04.sentence: Soils when wet retain water, and some expand in volume (smectite clay).

db5c542d6455.title: Alkali soil
db5c542d6455.sentence: The clay soils containing montmorillonite or smectite (swelling clays) are more subject to alkalinity problems than illite or kaolinite clay soils.

ef4abdf24262.title: Montmorillonite
ef4abdf24262.sentence: Montmorillonite, a member of the smectite group, is a 2:1 clay, meaning that it has two tetrahedral sheets of silica sandwiching a central octahedral sheet of alumina.

70b9f8220950.title: Montmorillonite
70b9f8220950.sentence: Montmorillonite is a very soft phyllosilicate group of minerals that form when they precipitate from water solution as microscopic crystals, known as clay.

1fc5d6278df3.title: Montmorillonite
1fc5d6278df3.sentence: The water content of montmorillonite is variable and it increases greatly in volume when it absorbs water.

cce535d00b43.title: Montmorillonite
cce535d00b43.sentence: It is named after Montmorillon in France.

60df3f1485a8.title: Montmorillonite
60df3f1485a8.sentence: Montmorillonite was first described in 1847 for an occurrence in Montmorillon in the department of Vienne, France, more than 50 years before the discovery of bentonite in the US.

f0b1a242d17f.title: Montmorillonite
f0b1a242d17f.sentence: The particles are plate-shaped with an average diameter around 1 μm and a thickness of 0.96 nm; magnification of about 25,000 times, using an electron microscope, is required to resolve individual clay particles.

e2337e4b4c2b.title: Montmorillonite
e2337e4b4c2b.sentence: The substitution of lower valence cations in such instances leaves the nearby oxygen atoms with a net negative charge that can attract cations.

873fe3dd11b7.title: Montmorillonite
873fe3dd11b7.sentence: The individual crystals of montmorillonite clay are not tightly bound hence water can intervene, causing the clay to swell, hence montmorillonite is a characteristic component of swelling soil.

6875f76bfb72.title: Soil matrix
6875f76bfb72.section: Mineral colloids: soil clays > Alumino-silica clays
6875f76bfb72.sentence: The crystals are weakly held together and water may intervene, causing the clay to swell up to ten times its dry volume.

8cce0118c57d.title: Soil matrix
8cce0118c57d.section: Mineral colloids: soil clays > Alumino-silica clays
8cce0118c57d.sentence: As the crystals are not bonded face to face, the entire surface is exposed and available for surface reactions, hence it has a high cation exchange capacity (CEC).

9968d25abfa2.title: Soil matrix
9968d25abfa2.section: Mineral colloids: soil clays > Alumino-silica clays
9968d25abfa2.sentence: It occurs in soils which have had little leaching, hence it is found in arid regions, although it may also occur in humid climates, depending on its mineralogical origin.

f8a94feea2ba.title: Montmorillonite
f8a94feea2ba.sentence: It often occurs intermixed with chlorite, muscovite, illite, cookeite, and kaolinite.

7f57c3a1469f.title: Montmorillonite
7f57c3a1469f.sentence: It is also used as a soil additive to hold soil water in drought-prone soils, used in the construction of earthen dams and levees, and to prevent the leakage of fluids.

20f7fe89c71d.title: Montmorillonite
20f7fe89c71d.sentence: Montmorillonite is used in the oil drilling industry as a component of drilling mud, making the mud slurry viscous, which helps to keep the drill bit cool, and to remove drilled solids.

9b6c56c4c390.title: Bentonite
9b6c56c4c390.sentence: Bentonite (/ˈbɛntənaɪt/ BEN-tə-nyte) is an absorbent swelling clay consisting mostly of montmorillonite (a type of smectite) which can either be Na-montmorillonite or Ca-montmorillonite.

dc2447bb83a0.title: Bentonite
dc2447bb83a0.sentence: In geology, the term bentonite is applied to a type of claystone (a clay rock, not a clay mineral) composed mostly of montmorillonite (a clay mineral from the smectite group).

188770585902.title: Bentonite
188770585902.sentence: In the mineral alteration process, a large fraction (up to 40–50 wt.%) of amorphous silica is dissolved and leached away, leaving the bentonite deposit in place.

8b071705d13c.title: Bentonite
8b071705d13c.sentence: However, in commercial and industrial applications, the term bentonite is used more generally to refer to any swelling clay composed mostly of smectite clay minerals, which includes montmorillonite.

99eec84cfa5d.title: Bentonite
99eec84cfa5d.sentence: As a swelling clay, bentonite has the ability to absorb large quantities of water, which increases its volume by up to a factor of eight.

9f04912bf245.title: Bentonite
9f04912bf245.sentence: Na-montmorillonite has a considerably greater swelling capacity than Ca-montmorillonite.

38ed1ff9e797.title: Bentonite
38ed1ff9e797.sentence: Calcium bentonite may be converted to sodium bentonite (termed sodium beneficiation or sodium activation) to exhibit many of sodium bentonite's properties by an ion exchange process.

5c5c431c2c50.title: Bentonite
5c5c431c2c50.sentence: As commonly practiced, this means adding 5–10% of a soluble sodium salt such as sodium carbonate to wet bentonite, mixing well, and allowing time for the ion exchange to take place and water to remove the exchanged calcium.

092286fb81f4.title: Bentonite
092286fb81f4.sentence: The property of swelling also makes sodium bentonite useful as a sealant, since it provides a self-sealing, low permeability barrier.

3ef735d1ff91.title: Bentonite
3ef735d1ff91.sentence: It is used to line the base of landfills to prevent migration of leachate, for confining metal pollutants of groundwater, and for the sealing of subsurface disposal systems for spent nuclear fuel.

49ad346debc9.title: Fuller's earth
