49ad346debc9.sentence: Fuller's earth refers to various types of clay used as an absorbent, filter, or bleaching agent.

9d585b3acc75.title: Fuller's earth
9d585b3acc75.sentence: Products labeled Fuller's Earth typically consist of palygorskite (also known as attapulgite) or bentonite.

de9061b2fad8.title: Fuller's earth
de9061b2fad8.sentence: Fuller's earth consists primarily of hydrous aluminum silicates (clay minerals) of varying composition.

694f67b7f680.title: Fuller's earth
694f67b7f680.sentence: Common components are montmorillonite, kaolinite, and attapulgite.

9365e9cffe2c.title: Fuller's earth
9365e9cffe2c.sentence: In some localities fuller's earth refers to calcium bentonite, which is altered volcanic ash composed mostly of montmorillonite.

abc9376bcf35.title: Bentonite
abc9376bcf35.sentence: It is the main active ingredient of fuller's earth, probably one of the earliest industrial cleaning agents.

b434cf7521cc.title: Fuller's earth
b434cf7521cc.sentence: The English name reflects the historical use of the material for fulling (cleaning and shrinking) wool, by textile workers known as fullers.

904c94150e46.title: Fuller's earth
904c94150e46.sentence: In past centuries, fullers kneaded fuller's earth and water into woollen cloth to absorb lanolin, oils, and other greasy impurities as part of the cloth finishing process.

55951c94ffbe.title: Smectite
55951c94ffbe.section: Role of interlayer cations in the swelling process
55951c94ffbe.sentence: The main cations in the smectite interlayers are Na+ and Ca2+.

66428e3112a7.title: Smectite
66428e3112a7.section: Role of interlayer cations in the swelling process
66428e3112a7.sentence: The degree of hydration of the cations and their corresponding hydrated radii explain the swelling or the shrinking behaviour of phyllosilicates.

1b492f4bfee0.title: Smectite
1b492f4bfee0.section: Role of interlayer cations in the swelling process
1b492f4bfee0.sentence: The sodium cations are responsible for the highest swelling of smectite while calcium ions have lower swelling properties.

bd8a70396fbd.title: Smectite
bd8a70396fbd.section: Role of interlayer cations in the swelling process
bd8a70396fbd.sentence: Calcium smectite has significantly less swelling capacity than sodium smectite but is also less prone to shrinking when desiccated.

195c5a38af63.title: Smectite
195c5a38af63.section: Role of interlayer cations in the swelling process
195c5a38af63.sentence: Other cations such as Mg2+ and K+ ions exhibit even a more contrasted effect: highly hydrated magnesium ions are "swellers" as in vermiculite (totally expanded interlayer) while poorly hydrated potassium ions are "collapsers" like in illite (totally collapsed interlayer).

da9615e5d477.title: Bentonite
da9615e5d477.section: Types > Illitisation of smectite clays by potassium ions and K-bentonite rock
da9615e5d477.sentence: In contrast to the highly hydrated Na+ ions which act as "swellers" or "expanders" ions, poorly hydrated K+ ions behave as "collapsers" when exchanging with Na+ ions accessible in the interlayers space present between two TOT layers.

6e8832937db9.title: Montmorillonite
6e8832937db9.sentence: The amount of expansion is due largely to the type of exchangeable cation contained in the sample.

7613fd1e2a50.title: Montmorillonite
7613fd1e2a50.sentence: The presence of sodium as the predominant exchangeable cation can result in the clay swelling to several times its original volume.

c880cab5b6ad.title: Plant nutrients in soil
c880cab5b6ad.sentence: Ammonium fixation occurs mainly between the layers of 2:1 type clay minerals such as illite, vermiculite or montmorillonite, together with ions of similar ionic radius and low hydration energy such as potassium, but a small proportion of ammonium is also fixed in the silt fraction.

c100644ef989.title: Bentonite
c100644ef989.sentence: The application of clay technology by farmers in northeast Thailand, using bentonite clay, has dramatically reversed soil degradation and resulted in greater economic returns, with higher yields and higher output prices.

b08d0f5011f9.title: Bentonite
b08d0f5011f9.sentence: Studies carried out by The International Water Management Institute and partners in 2002–2003 focused on the application of locally sourced bentonite clays to degraded soils in the region.

c32356e28242.title: Bentonite
c32356e28242.sentence: Bentonite application also influenced the prices that farmers received for their crops.

f154cb9f8164.title: Bentonite
f154cb9f8164.sentence: These applications were carried out in structured field trials.

ecf3bf953818.title: Bentonite
ecf3bf953818.sentence: Applying bentonite clays effectively improved yields of forage sorghum grown under rain-fed conditions.

01a93a09a126.title: Bentonite
01a93a09a126.sentence: Production costs are higher, but due to higher production and the quality of the food, clay farmers could afford to invest and grow more and better food, compared to nonclay-using farmers.

9b16033a628d.title: Soil matrix
9b16033a628d.section: Mineral colloids: soil clays > Alumino-silica clays
9b16033a628d.sentence: Where rainfall is high, acid soils selectively leach more silica than alumina from the original clays, leaving kaolinite.

f21ce6944f5f.title: Soil matrix
f21ce6944f5f.section: Mineral colloids: soil clays > Alumino-silica clays
f21ce6944f5f.sentence: Even heavier weathering results in sesquioxide clays.

ea7142717dc2.title: Soil matrix
ea7142717dc2.sentence: The type of clay that is formed is a function of the parent material and the composition of the minerals in solution.

c26070e6e8eb.title: Kaolinite
c26070e6e8eb.sentence: Such climatically related differences in clay mineral content are often used to infer changes in climates in the geological past, where ancient soils have been buried and preserved.

3b6b5d2c3d06.title: Soil matrix
3b6b5d2c3d06.section: Mineral colloids: soil clays > Sesquioxide clays
3b6b5d2c3d06.sentence: It takes hundreds of thousands of years of leaching to create sesquioxide clays.

05f6a33a22dd.title: Soil matrix
05f6a33a22dd.section: Mineral colloids: soil clays > Sesquioxide clays
05f6a33a22dd.sentence: Sesqui is Latin for "one and one-half": there are three parts oxygen to two parts iron or aluminium; hence the ratio is one and one-half (not true for all).

5ca21acdfdd1.title: Soil matrix
5ca21acdfdd1.section: Mineral colloids: soil clays > Sesquioxide clays
5ca21acdfdd1.sentence: They are not sticky and do not swell, and soils high in them (e.g. lateritic soils) behave much like sand and can rapidly pass water.

bd27c5b73a96.title: Soil matrix
bd27c5b73a96.section: Mineral colloids: soil clays > Sesquioxide clays
bd27c5b73a96.sentence: Sesquioxides have low CEC but these variable-charge minerals are able to hold anions as well as cations.

e32be0bf8cbb.title: Soil matrix
e32be0bf8cbb.section: Mineral colloids: soil clays > Sesquioxide clays
e32be0bf8cbb.sentence: They are able to hold large quantities of phosphates, a sorptive process which can at least partly be inhibited in the presence of decomposed (humified) organic matter.

1447bc641fc2.title: Clay–water interaction
1447bc641fc2.sentence: Clay-water interaction is an all-inclusive term to describe various progressive interactions between clay minerals and water.

76509acf621d.title: Clay–water interaction
76509acf621d.sentence: Five descriptive terms describe the progressive interactions in a clay-water system.

06cb326055ee.title: Clay–water interaction
06cb326055ee.sentence: In the dry state, clay packets exist in face-to-face stacks like a deck of playing cards, but clay packets begin to change when exposed to water.

d6ba94e37bec.title: Clay–water interaction
d6ba94e37bec.sentence: (1) Hydration occurs as clay packets absorb water and swell.

180a9a629fba.title: Clay–water interaction
180a9a629fba.sentence: (2) Dispersion (or disaggregation) causes clay platelets to break apart and disperse into the water due to the loss of attractive forces as water moves the platelets further apart.

61fdb6aa9509.title: Clay–water interaction
61fdb6aa9509.sentence: (3) Flocculation begins when mechanical shearing stops, and platelets previously dispersed come together due to the attractive force of surface charges on the platelets.

be59500de202.title: Clay–water interaction
be59500de202.sentence: (4) Deflocculation, or peptization, the opposite effect, occurs when a chemical de-flocculant is added to flocculated mud; the positive edge charges are covered, and attraction forces are greatly reduced.

44b63ff08485.title: Clay–water interaction
44b63ff08485.sentence: (5) Aggregation, a result of ionic or thermal conditions, alters the hydrational layer around clay platelets, removes the deflocculant from positive edge charges, and allows platelets to assume a face-to-face structure.

e6e9af3adcfe.title: Clay mineral X-ray diffraction
e6e9af3adcfe.sentence: Si4+ is normally the center of the tetrahedral layer but Al3+ will often partially substitute and create a charge imbalance.

fa8ef0e89900.title: Clay mineral X-ray diffraction
fa8ef0e89900.sentence: When substitution of Al3+ for Si4+ creates a charge imbalance, an interlayer cation will fill in between tetrahedral layers to balance the charge of the clay.

89b260709af5.title: Nontronite
89b260709af5.sentence: Thus, nontronite is typically characterised by having most (usually greater than 60%) of the layer charge located in the tetrahedral sheet.

dee2c25a604e.title: Nontronite
dee2c25a604e.sentence: The layer charge is generally balanced by divalent calcium (Ca2+) or magnesium (Mg2+).

6d435d2c5d39.title: Birnessite
6d435d2c5d39.sentence: The Mn3+O6 and Mn4+O6 octahedra are fully ordered in raws in the MnO2 layers, such that every Mn3+-rich row alternates with two Mn4+-rich rows.10,11 The layer charge is offset by alkaline and alkali-earth cations (e.g., Na, K, Ca, Ba) into the interlayer region along with water molecules, and therefore TcBi has a cation-exchange capacity.

c8b6cc40bef4.title: Montmorillonite
c8b6cc40bef4.sentence: Members of this group include saponite, nontronite, beidellite, and hectorite.

167f2ca1ef09.title: Particle aggregation
167f2ca1ef09.sentence: This dependence reflects the Schulze–Hardy rule, which states that the CCC varies as the inverse sixth power of the counter ion charge.

95a68dd02879.title: Particle aggregation
95a68dd02879.sentence: The Schulze–Hardy rule can be derived from DLVO theory as well.

a3a8a4376557.title: Particle aggregation
a3a8a4376557.sentence: The CCC also depends on the type of ion somewhat, even if they carry the same charge.

c36343695936.title: Particle aggregation
c36343695936.sentence: This dependence may reflect different particle properties or different ion affinities to the particle surface.

ad20896c00d0.title: Peptization
ad20896c00d0.sentence: Multivalent cations are more efficient flocculants than monovalent cations: AlCl3 > CaCl2 > NaCl.

4c4ef27e0442.title: Clay chemistry
4c4ef27e0442.sentence: Clay chemistry is an applied subdiscipline of chemistry which studies the chemical structures, properties and reactions of or involving clays and clay minerals.

c8e06edc50df.title: Clay chemistry
c8e06edc50df.sentence: Properties of clay minerals include: nanometric scale layered construction, presence of fixed and interchangeable charges, possibility of adsorbing and intercalating molecules, ability of forming stable colloidal dispersions, possibility of tailored surface and interlayer chemical modification.

66e94053245d.title: Clay chemistry
66e94053245d.sentence: Their cation exchange capacity (CEC) is of great importance in the balance of the most common cations in soil (Na+, K+, NH4+, Ca2+, Mg2+) and pH control, with direct impact on the soil fertility.

11d17880650f.title: Clay chemistry
11d17880650f.sentence: The interactions of clay minerals with organic substances in the soil also play a vital role in the fixation of nutrients and fertility, as well as in the fixation or leaching of pesticides and other contaminants.

c5407176c1d3.title: Clay chemistry
c5407176c1d3.sentence: Presence of clay minerals in Mars, detected by the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter in 2009 was another strong evidence of the existence of water on the planet in previous geological eras.

d1f2c19ab089.title: Humic substance
d1f2c19ab089.sentence: Humic substances (HS) are relatively recalcitrant colored organic compounds naturally formed during long-term decomposition and transformation of biomass residues.

1bb461ba2be0.title: Humic substance
1bb461ba2be0.sentence: Humic substances constitute the majority of organic matter in soil, peat, coal, and sediments, and are important components of dissolved natural organic matter (NOM) in lakes (especially dystrophic lakes), rivers, and sea water.

c4a4f1070dd9.title: Humic substance
c4a4f1070dd9.sentence: Humic substances account for 50 – 90% of cation exchange capacity in soils.

34a89ef5bc37.title: Humic substance
34a89ef5bc37.sentence: "Humic substances" is an umbrella term covering humic acid, fulvic acid, and humin, which differ in solubility.

939a5a2e0c69.title: Humic substance
939a5a2e0c69.sentence: The color of humic substances varies from bright yellow to light or dark brown leading to black.

9218c69213ab.title: Humic substance
9218c69213ab.sentence: The term comes from humus, which in turn comes from the Latin word humus, meaning "soil, earth".

4121454a345d.title: Humic substance
4121454a345d.sentence: Humic substances are formed by the microbial degradation of dead biotic matter, such as lignin, cellulose, ligno-cellulose and charcoal.

e78ff86b13f9.title: Humic substance
e78ff86b13f9.sentence: The formation of HS in nature is one of the least understood aspects of humus chemistry and one of the most intriguing.

273fbd836fa6.title: Humic substance
273fbd836fa6.sentence: Historically, there have been three main theories to explain it: the lignin theory of Waksman (1932), the polyphenol theory, and the sugar-amine condensation theory of Maillard (1911).

987246c4d3a7.title: Humic substance
987246c4d3a7.sentence: In general, humic substances derived from soil and peat (which takes hundreds to thousands of years to form) have higher molecular weight, higher amounts of O and N, more carbohydrate units, and fewer polyaromatic units than humic substances derived from coal and leonardite (which takes millions of years to form).

aef2d7fa3996.title: Chelation
aef2d7fa3996.sentence: Chelation (/kiːˈleɪʃən/) is a type of bonding and sequestration of metal atoms.

5881434c9081.title: Chelation
5881434c9081.sentence: It involves two or more separate dative covalent bonds between a ligand and a single metal atom, thereby forming a ring structure.

1e92d1184c2e.title: Chelation
1e92d1184c2e.sentence: The ligand is called a chelant, chelator, chelating agent, or sequestering agent.

5b0f2d1920c2.title: Chelation
5b0f2d1920c2.sentence: It is usually an organic compound, but this is not a requirement.

f7dbfa37fd1d.title: Chelation
f7dbfa37fd1d.sentence: The word chelation is derived from Greek χηλή, chēlē, meaning "claw", because the ligand molecule or molecules hold the metal atom like the claws of a crab.

8935e7dc0155.title: Chelation
8935e7dc0155.sentence: The term chelate (/ˈkiːleɪt/) was first applied in 1920 by Sir Gilbert T. Morgan and H. D. K. Drew, who stated: "The adjective chelate, derived from the great claw or chele (Greek) of the crab or other crustaceans, is suggested for the caliper like groups which function as two associating units and fasten to the central atom so as to produce heterocyclic rings."

f332e809c711.title: Chelation
f332e809c711.sentence: Most metal complexes in the environment and in nature are bound in some form of chelate ring (e.g., with a humic acid or a protein).

4aaeb7a83b4a.title: Chelation
4aaeb7a83b4a.sentence: Thus, metal chelates are relevant to the mobilization of metals in the soil, the uptake and the accumulation of metals into plants and microorganisms.

199e609bdc4f.title: Humus
199e609bdc4f.sentence: - Humus is a negatively charged colloidal substance which increases the cation-exchange capacity of soil, hence its ability to store nutrients by chelation.

b16181bfcd6b.title: Chelation
b16181bfcd6b.sentence: Chelation is useful in the preparation of nutritional supplements, in chelation therapy to remove toxic metals from the body, as contrast agents in MRI scanning, in manufacturing using homogeneous catalysts, in chemical water treatment to assist in the removal of metals, and in fertilizers.

79ec2833bedb.title: Chelation
79ec2833bedb.sentence: Dechelation (or de-chelation) is a reverse process of the chelation in which the chelating agent is recovered by acidifying solution with a mineral acid to form a precipitate.

1f2409cbaba5.title: Sorption
1f2409cbaba5.sentence: Sorption is a physical and chemical process by which one substance becomes attached to another.

6fa571ebc3e0.title: Sorption
6fa571ebc3e0.sentence: "the incorporation of a substance in one state into another of a different state" (e.g., liquids being absorbed by a solid or gases being absorbed by a liquid);

ba024a8901d0.title: Sorption
ba024a8901d0.sentence: The physical adherence or bonding of ions and molecules onto the surface of another phase (e.g., reagents adsorbed to a solid catalyst surface);

44695edde736.title: Sorption
44695edde736.sentence: An exchange of ions between two electrolytes or between an electrolyte solution and a complex.

0c2b5dc40089.title: Sorption
0c2b5dc40089.sentence: The adsorption and absorption rate of a diluted solute in gas or liquid solution to a surface or interface can be calculated using Fick's laws of diffusion.

db6cf77fbb7d.title: Humus
db6cf77fbb7d.sentence: Much of the humus in most soils has persisted for more than 100 years, rather than having been decomposed into CO2, and can be regarded as stable; this organic matter has been protected from decomposition by microbial or enzyme action because it is hidden (occluded) inside small aggregates of soil particles, or tightly sorbed or complexed to clays.

7f2ad5c8e592.title: Molybdenum deficiency (plant disorder)
7f2ad5c8e592.sentence: For crops growing in soil, this may be a result of low concentrations of Mo in the soil as a whole (i.e. the parent material of the soil is low in Mo), or because the soil Mo is held in forms that are not available to plants – sorption of Mo is strongest in acid soils.

fe58a079d97a.title: Molybdenum deficiency (plant disorder)
fe58a079d97a.sentence: Liming of soils frequently relieves Mo deficiency by decreasing Mo sorption.

70024c9cee31.title: Alkali soil
70024c9cee31.sentence: The ammonium (NH+ 4) cation produced by urea hydrolysis which is a strongly sorbing cation exchanges with the weakly sorbing Na+ cation from the soil structure and Na+ is released into water.

5d70f75f0ff1.title: Adsorption
5d70f75f0ff1.sentence: Adsorption is the adhesion of atoms, ions, or molecules from a gas, liquid, or dissolved solid to a surface.

db89198c10c3.title: Adsorption
db89198c10c3.sentence: This process creates a film of the adsorbate on the surface of the adsorbent.

229dc3b79b9f.title: Adsorption
229dc3b79b9f.sentence: This process differs from absorption, in which a fluid (the absorbate) is dissolved by or permeates a liquid or solid (the absorbent).

44dd141b8830.title: Adsorption
44dd141b8830.sentence: While adsorption does often precede absorption, which involves the transfer of the absorbate into the volume of the absorbent material, alternatively, adsorption is distinctly a surface phenomenon, wherein the adsorbate does not penetrate through the material surface and into the bulk of the adsorbent.

0c015887fe5b.title: Adsorption
0c015887fe5b.sentence: The term sorption encompasses both adsorption and absorption, and desorption is the reverse of sorption.

4d717e6c7fdb.title: Adsorption
4d717e6c7fdb.sentence: Like surface tension, adsorption is a consequence of surface energy.

97955e3ba7ac.title: Adsorption
97955e3ba7ac.sentence: However, atoms on the surface of the adsorbent are not wholly surrounded by other adsorbent atoms and therefore can attract adsorbates.

6604b75288e1.title: Adsorption
6604b75288e1.sentence: It may also occur due to electrostatic attraction.

e43266f5d5cc.title: Adsorption
e43266f5d5cc.sentence: Adsorption, ion exchange, and chromatography are sorption processes in which certain adsorbates are selectively transferred from the fluid phase to the surface of insoluble, rigid particles suspended in a vessel or packed in a column.

cfcb7a34d05f.title: Adsorption
cfcb7a34d05f.sentence: In the case of physically adsorbed water, surface hydration can be eliminated simply through drying at conditions of temperature and pressure allowing full vaporization of water.

6aa6770d1514.title: Adsorption
6aa6770d1514.sentence: For chemically adsorbed water, hydration may be in the form of either dissociative adsorption, where H2O molecules are dissociated into surface adsorbed -H and -OH, or molecular adsorption (associative adsorption) where individual water molecules remain intact

c2ecd37382cc.title: Adsorption
c2ecd37382cc.sentence: The word "adsorption" was coined in 1881 by German physicist Heinrich Kayser (1853–1940).

bbae67ca8581.title: Cation-exchange capacity
bbae67ca8581.sentence: The amount of negative charge from deprotonation of clay hydroxy groups or organic matter depends on the pH of the surrounding solution.

288cf8310940.title: Soil

690e69720129.title: Leonardite
690e69720129.sentence: It is an oxidation product of lignite, associated with near-surface mining.

2966f130e48c.title: Leonardite
2966f130e48c.sentence: It is a rich source of humic acid (up to 90%) and is used as a soil conditioner, as a stabilizer for ion-exchange resins in water treatment, in the remediation of polluted environments and as a drilling additive.

5ddc80e21842.title: Leonardite
5ddc80e21842.sentence: Leonardite is found associated with near surface lignite deposits.

079d055b8c8d.title: Leonardite

f8e8eac1a391.title: Leonardite

5ca87b10aa2b.title: Leonardite

1b623fa19947.title: Leonardite

203b4f9e33e2.title: Humic substance

c583b960491a.title: Humic substance
c583b960491a.sentence: A more recent process known as hydrothermal humification and fulvification, allows the conversion of a wide range of biomass and biogenic residues into artificial humin, A-HA, and A-FA under controlled temperature (180 °C–250 °C) and autogenic pressure, similar to hydrothermal carbonization but in an alkaline solution, which results in the autoneutralization of the reaction medium through the conversion of biomass components—cellulose, hemicellulose, and lignin—within minutes to hours, compared to the natural process which takes years in nature.

e1ead10c41c8.title: Humic substance

d5388a8c47a4.title: Humic substance

02795801fbe1.title: Humic substance

ce7a0009a698.title: Humic substance

651f6287d2b9.title: Humic substance

c8849431862a.title: Humic substance
c8849431862a.sentence: A typical humic substance is a mixture of many molecules, some of which are based on a motif of aromatic nuclei with phenolic and carboxylic substituents, linked together; The functional groups that contribute most to surface charge and reactivity of humic substances are phenolic and carboxylic groups.

763b4288ff53.title: Humic substance
763b4288ff53.sentence: Humic substances commonly behave as mixtures of dibasic acids, with a pK1 value around 4 for protonation of carboxyl groups and around 8 for protonation of phenolate groups in HA.

fbe79e92659c.title: Humic substance

049b0607da11.title: Humic substance

87e9831bf319.title: Humic substance

9bac2bd1ec9e.title: Humic substance

3fda4017b928.title: Humic substance

616370dc5ab4.title: Humic substance

7eec31077d08.title: Humic substance
7eec31077d08.sentence: The traditional view has been that humic substances are hetero- poly-condensates, in varying associations with clay.

188f26870300.title: Humic substance

04cc1ed94711.title: Humic substance
04cc1ed94711.sentence: Rather, they represent a heterogeneous mixture of relatively small molecular components of the soil organic matter auto-assembled in supramolecular associations and are composed of a variety of compounds of biological origin and synthesized by abiotic and biotic reactions in soil and surface waters.

ef60ba013ef8.title: Humic substance
ef60ba013ef8.sentence: Organic matter soil amendments have been known by farmers to be beneficial to plant growth for longer than recorded history.

314c1225932d.title: Humic substance

f8dfb583680b.title: Adsorption
f8dfb583680b.sentence: The adsorption of gases and solutes is usually described through isotherms, that is, the amount of adsorbate on the adsorbent as a function of its pressure (if gas) or concentration (for liquid phase solutes) at constant temperature.

f965605e0056.title: Adsorption

95331feb580f.title: Adsorption

3f112d1357dd.title: Adsorption

1edc60c8c76f.title: Adsorption

451f34da3b81.title: Adsorption

cefa3c559167.title: Desorption
cefa3c559167.sentence: Desorption is the physical process where adsorbed atoms or molecules are released from a surface into the surrounding vacuum or fluid.

05234812fa28.title: Desorption
05234812fa28.sentence: Desorption is the reverse of the process of adsorption, which differs from absorption in that adsorption refers to substances bound to the surface, rather than being absorbed into the bulk.

32fcbd808396.title: Desorption
32fcbd808396.sentence: This occurs when a molecule gains enough energy to overcome the activation barrier and the binding energy that keep it attached to the surface.

0713782f6b30.title: Desorption
0713782f6b30.sentence: Desorption can occur from any of several processes, or a combination of them: it may result from heat (thermal energy); incident light such as infrared, visible, or ultraviolet photons; or an incident beam of energetic particles such as electrons.

b0122238333f.title: Desorption
b0122238333f.sentence: It may also occur following chemical reactions such as oxidation or reduction in an electrochemical cell or after a chemical reaction of adsorbed compounds in which the surface may act as a catalyst.

426dd2a686ea.title: Desorption

d721b14dc474.title: Desorption

7b4f9f5d87a7.title: Chelation

2c06bf053730.title: Equivalent (chemistry)
2c06bf053730.sentence: An equivalent (symbol: officially equiv; unofficially but often Eq) is the amount of a substance that reacts with (or is equivalent to) an arbitrary amount (typically one mole) of another substance in a given chemical reaction.

79f9b177da13.title: Equivalent (chemistry)

02d2ef2ff5b7.title: Equivalent (chemistry)

d0fb251d408d.title: Equivalent (chemistry)
d0fb251d408d.sentence: By this definition, the number of equivalents of a given ion in a solution is equal to the number of moles of that ion multiplied by its valence.

09222bc6b623.title: Equivalent (chemistry)

928e7fb770a1.title: Equivalent (chemistry)

97ea91323dc1.title: Equivalent (chemistry)

141c3405b4e2.title: Base-cation saturation ratio
141c3405b4e2.sentence: Base-cation saturation ratio (BCSR) is a method of interpreting soil test results that is widely used in sustainable agriculture, supported by the National Sustainable Agriculture Information Service (ATTRA) and claimed to be successfully in use on over a million acres (4,000 km2) of farmland worldwide.

218cd352a312.title: Base-cation saturation ratio
218cd352a312.sentence: In the BCSR system, soil cations are balanced according to varying ratios often stated as giving 'ideal' or 'balanced' soil.

63d715d1085b.title: Base-cation saturation ratio
63d715d1085b.sentence: These ratios can be between individual cations, such as the calcium to magnesium ratio, or they may be expressed as a percentage saturation of the cation exchange capacity (CEC) of the soil.

1e4ab0c48089.title: Base-cation saturation ratio
1e4ab0c48089.sentence: The traditional method, as used by most university laboratories, is known variously as the 'sufficiency level', sufficiency level of available nutrients (SLAN), or Index(UK) system.

2239511a0856.sentence: The sufficiency level system is concerned only with keeping plant-available nutrient levels within a well studied range, making sure there is neither a deficiency nor an excess.

27ac07889b4d.title: Base-cation saturation ratio
27ac07889b4d.sentence: Albrecht had been investigating cattle nutrition, having observed that certain pastures seemed conducive to good health, and at some point he came to the conclusion that the ideal balance of cations in the soil was "H, 10%; Ca, 60 to 75%; Mg, 10 to 20%; K, 2 to 5%; Na, 0.5 to 5.0%; and other cations, 5%".

b151e4d743d8.title: Base-cation saturation ratio

e28aff3e450b.title: Base-cation saturation ratio

A decade later Neal Kinsey co-wrote a book with Charles Walters called "Hands on Agronomy" in which he defined the ideal ratios as 60–70% Ca, 10–20% Mg, 3–5% K, 1% Na, 10–15 H, 2–4% other cations.

0d607df11652.title: Base-cation saturation ratio
0d607df11652.sentence: Kinsey's book has gone on to become the most widely known and influential work on the BCSR system.

5052071f40c1.title: Base-cation saturation ratio

3b3141fc1a90.title: Base-cation saturation ratio

c9bdbf8a19c4.title: Base-cation saturation ratio

41be182b07d7.title: Base-cation saturation ratio

ca5fd1e66b83.title: Base-richness

24b065baf943.title: Base-richness

f06e5a99cb02.title: Base-richness

0ae507314ff4.title: Base-richness

904f4d21d909.title: Base-richness
904f4d21d909.sentence: Base-poor environments are characteristic of areas where underlying rocks (below soil) are sandstone or granite, or where the water is derived directly from rainfall (ombrotrophic).

79012f1367f6.title: Base-richness

9b6c2ab5943f.sentence: In the physical sciences, a partition coefficient (P) or distribution coefficient (D) is the ratio of concentrations of a compound in a mixture of two immiscible solvents at equilibrium.

3309de874121.title: Partition coefficient
3309de874121.sentence: The partition coefficient generally refers to the concentration ratio of un-ionized species of compound, whereas the distribution coefficient refers to the concentration ratio of all species of the compound (ionized plus un-ionized).

9dff1e46c7de.title: Partition coefficient
9dff1e46c7de.sentence: Most commonly, one of the solvents is water, while the second is hydrophobic, such as 1-octanol.

246160dfce21.title: Partition coefficient
246160dfce21.sentence: Hence the partition coefficient measures how hydrophilic ("water-loving") or hydrophobic ("water-fearing") a chemical substance is.

9f8dd80ab892.title: Partition coefficient

69ca2e9abb16.title: Partition coefficient

b08a2d63593b.title: Coprecipitation
b08a2d63593b.sentence: In chemistry, coprecipitation (CPT) or co-precipitation is the carrying down by a precipitate of substances normally soluble under the conditions employed.

895e4b93f18e.title: Coprecipitation
895e4b93f18e.sentence: There are three main mechanisms of coprecipitation: inclusion, occlusion, and adsorption.

c6ef5df5fd4a.title: Coprecipitation
c6ef5df5fd4a.sentence: An inclusion (incorporation in the crystal lattice) occurs when the impurity occupies a lattice site in the crystal structure of the carrier, resulting in a crystallographic defect; this can happen when the ionic radius and charge of the impurity are similar to those of the carrier.

650b22892850.title: Coprecipitation
650b22892850.sentence: An occlusion occurs when an adsorbed impurity gets physically trapped inside the crystal as it grows.

5765e59e017b.title: Coprecipitation
5765e59e017b.sentence: An adsorbate is an impurity that is weakly, or strongly, bound (adsorbed) to the surface of the precipitate.

2cc017fd3b9f.title: Coprecipitation
2cc017fd3b9f.sentence: Since the trace element is too dilute (sometimes less than a part per trillion) to precipitate by conventional means, it is typically coprecipitated with a carrier, a substance that has a similar crystalline structure that can incorporate the desired element.

a7eb28128d00.title: Coprecipitation
a7eb28128d00.sentence: Besides its applications in chemical analysis and in radiochemistry, coprecipitation is also important to many environmental issues related to water resources, including acid mine drainage, radionuclide migration around waste repositories, toxic heavy metal transport at industrial and defense sites, metal concentrations in aquatic systems, and wastewater treatment technology.

5a1370193dd7.sentence: The Freundlich equation or Freundlich adsorption isotherm, an adsorption isotherm, is an empirical relationship between the quantity of a gas adsorbed into a solid surface and the gas pressure.

0764fe8ddc36.title: Freundlich equation

3b117f5f3d79.title: Freundlich equation
3b117f5f3d79.sentence: In Freundlich's notation (used for his experiments dealing with the adsorption of organic acids on coal in aqueous solutions), x/m signifies the ratio between the adsorbed mass or adsorbate x and the mass of the adsorbent m, which in Freundlich's studies was coal.

d7b5bfae14e3.title: Freundlich equation
d7b5bfae14e3.sentence: K and n are constants for a given adsorbate and adsorbent at a given temperature (from there, the term isotherm needed to avoid significant gas pressure fluctuations due to uncontrolled temperature variations in the case of adsorption experiments of a gas onto a solid phase).

27d4c8216b71.title: Freundlich equation

c39c771ca909.title: Freundlich equation

880921f32617.title: Freundlich equation

de7bf9a66341.title: Freundlich equation

06f73d797c9e.title: Freundlich equation

c82536c45321.title: Freundlich equation

412faa047e13.sentence: X-ray absorption fine structure (XAFS) is a specific structure observed in X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS).

849de6a6f01d.sentence: Information on the geometry of the local structure is provided by the analysis of the multiple scattering peaks in the XANES spectra.

6f1d12186c7a.title: Geochemical modeling

1ab0487c910d.title: Geochemical modeling
1ab0487c910d.sentence: Models can be constructed, for example, to understand the composition of natural waters; the mobility and breakdown of contaminants in flowing groundwater or surface water; the ion speciation of plant nutrients in soil and of regulated metals in stored solid wastes; the formation and dissolution of rocks and minerals in geologic formations in response to injection of industrial wastes, steam, or carbon dioxide; the dissolution of carbon dioxide in seawater and its effect on ocean acidification; and the generation of acidic waters and leaching of metals from mine wastes.

fbbd6aa3532b.title: Geochemical modeling
fbbd6aa3532b.sentence: Geochemical modeling or theoretical geochemistry is the practice of using chemical thermodynamics, chemical kinetics, or both, to analyze the chemical reactions that affect geologic systems, commonly with the aid of a computer.

e72b23ece23a.title: Geochemical modeling
e72b23ece23a.sentence: It is used in high-temperature geochemistry to simulate reactions occurring deep in the Earth's interior, in magma, for instance, or to model low-temperature reactions in aqueous solutions near the Earth's surface, the subject of this article.

ec61c5b919d9.title: Geochemical modeling
ec61c5b919d9.sentence: Garrels and Thompson (1962) first applied chemical modeling to geochemistry in 25 °C and one atmosphere total pressure.

85f0db94ab6a.title: Geochemical modeling
85f0db94ab6a.sentence: This coupling of mass transfer with an equilibrium model, known as a reaction path model, enabled geochemists to simulate reaction processes.

844178034fab.title: Geochemical modeling
844178034fab.sentence: Helgeson (1968) introduced the first computer program to solve equilibrium and reaction path models, which he and coworkers used to model geological processes like weathering, sediment diagenesis, evaporation, hydrothermal alteration, and ore deposition.

cba26aed66c6.title: Geochemical modeling
cba26aed66c6.sentence: Creating geochemical models of such systems begins by choosing the basis, the set of aqueous species, minerals, and gases which are used to write chemical reactions and express composition.

6baf00f1ac28.title: Geochemical modeling

5b28d380828a.title: Geochemical modeling

37fbdb6e284e.title: Geochemical modeling
37fbdb6e284e.sentence: Minerals with a saturation index (log Q/K) equal to zero are said to be in equilibrium with the fluid.

4806d1acb7bc.title: Geochemical modeling

aed0cd7f366c.title: Geochemical modeling
aed0cd7f366c.sentence: A mineral is undersaturated if its saturation index is negative, indicating that it is favored to dissolve.

3e85d0d763db.title: Geochemical modeling

b6af131f7e1d.title: Geochemical modeling

5326de2e38d6.title: Redox
5326de2e38d6.sentence: Redox (/ˈrɛdɒks/ RED-oks, /ˈriːdɒks/ REE-doks, reduction–oxidation or oxidation–reduction) is a type of chemical reaction in which the oxidation states of the reactants change.

b1d6cd45174d.title: Redox
b1d6cd45174d.sentence: Oxidation is the loss of electrons or an increase in the oxidation state.

f981fe5a663a.title: Redox
f981fe5a663a.sentence: Reduction is the gain of electrons or a decrease in the oxidation state.

d96141e3a338.title: Redox
d96141e3a338.sentence: The oxidation and reduction processes occur simultaneously in the chemical reaction.

f84ee58505bc.title: Redox
f84ee58505bc.sentence: The processes of oxidation and reduction occur simultaneously and cannot occur independently.

77954e782fc9.title: Redox
77954e782fc9.sentence: In atom transfer, an atom passes from one substrate to another; for example, in the rusting of iron the oxidation state of the iron atoms increases as the metal converts to an oxide and oxygen is reduced as it absorbs the released electrons.

7418ba2ab4fe.title: Redox
7418ba2ab4fe.sentence: Cellular respiration and photosynthesis, combustion, and the corrosion of metals all proceed through redox chemistry, as do the reactions that power batteries and other electrochemical cells.

b8e16d8e5a3b.title: Redox
b8e16d8e5a3b.sentence: In soils, sediments, and water, redox gradients drive the biogeochemical cycling of elements.

448621b732fe.title: Redox
448621b732fe.sentence: Oxidation originally implied a reaction with oxygen to form an oxide.

85c21d2e50ab.title: Redox
85c21d2e50ab.sentence: Ultimately, the meaning became generalized to include all processes that involve the loss of electrons or the increase in the oxidation state of a chemical species.

82545f986e8e.title: Redox
82545f986e8e.sentence: The word reduction originally referred to the loss in weight upon heating a metallic ore such as a metal oxide to extract the metal.

27db08232f3f.title: Redox

6767571a82e4.title: Redox

a8e2c4537697.title: Redox

6e1aae9d15ff.title: Redoximorphic features
6e1aae9d15ff.sentence: Redoximorphic features (RMFs) consist of color patterns in a soil that are caused by loss (depletion) or gain (concentration) of pigment compared to the matrix color, formed by oxidation/reduction of iron and/or manganese coupled with their removal, translocation, or accrual; or a soil matrix color controlled by the presence of iron (2+) The composition and responsible formation processes for a soil color or color pattern must be known or inferred before it can be described as an RMF.

b86cc4e91348.sentence: Aerobic conditions produce uniform or gradual colour changes, while reducing environments (anaerobic) result in rapid colour flow with complex, mottled patterns and points of colour concentration.

bcf9dbca7e7c.title: In situ chemical oxidation

c528086ddc0f.sentence: In some cases, the average oxidation state of an element is a fraction, such as ⁠8/3⁠ for iron in magnetite Fe3O4 (see below).

5c07d7b2e015.title: Redox
5c07d7b2e015.sentence: Substances that have the ability to reduce other substances (cause them to gain electrons) are said to be reductive or reducing and are known as reducing agents, reductants, or reducers.

76a08bc34b35.title: Redox
76a08bc34b35.sentence: The reductant transfers electrons to another substance and is thus itself oxidized.

89ed0072b637.title: Redox
89ed0072b637.sentence: Because it donates electrons, the reducing agent is also called an electron donor.

a68b9d32c071.title: Redox
a68b9d32c071.sentence: Electropositive elemental metals, such as lithium, sodium, magnesium, iron, zinc, and aluminium, are good reducing agents.

c1584ed0d68e.title: Redox
c1584ed0d68e.sentence: These metals donate electrons relatively readily.

8d09d3bd1d0f.title: Redox
8d09d3bd1d0f.sentence: Reducing equivalent refers to chemical species that transfer the equivalent of one electron in redox reactions.

c74409f5e46e.title: Redox
c74409f5e46e.sentence: The term is common in biochemistry.

595eec8c590c.title: Redox
595eec8c590c.sentence: A reducing equivalent can be an electron or a hydrogen atom as a hydride ion.

604107f730f9.title: Deep biosphere
604107f730f9.sentence: From highest to lowest redox potential, some common donors available in the subsurface are organic matter, hydrogen, methane, reduced sulfur compounds, reduced iron compounds and ammonium.

3ed89a7901e6.title: Redox gradient
3ed89a7901e6.sentence: The main source of electrons in soil is organic matter.

41e7540e6f47.title: Redox
41e7540e6f47.sentence: A redox couple is a reducing species and its corresponding oxidizing form, e.g., Fe2+ / Fe3+.The oxidation alone and the reduction alone are each called a half-reaction because two half-reactions always occur together to form a whole reaction.

e0dab10f0a23.title: Redox
e0dab10f0a23.sentence: In redox processes, the reductant transfers electrons to the oxidant.

53dad94d0806.title: Redox
53dad94d0806.sentence: Thus, in the reaction, the reductant or reducer or reducing agent loses electrons and is oxidized, while the oxidant or oxidizer or oxidizing agent gains electrons and is reduced.

7cfe718b4a1f.title: Redox
7cfe718b4a1f.sentence: The pair of an oxidizing and reducing agent that is involved in a particular reaction is called a redox pair.

720c06c22191.title: Redox
720c06c22191.sentence: In electrochemical reactions the oxidation and reduction processes do occur simultaneously but are separated in space.

6a4fdb34982a.title: Redox
6a4fdb34982a.sentence: For example, a reagent that is oxidized loses electrons; however, that reagent is referred to as the reducing agent.

da3927a2fcb2.title: Redox
da3927a2fcb2.sentence: Likewise, a reagent that is reduced gains electrons and is referred to as the oxidizing agent.

6cc06dc4853e.title: Redox
6cc06dc4853e.sentence: Each half-reaction has a standard electrode potential (Eo cell), which is equal to the potential difference or voltage at equilibrium under standard conditions of an electrochemical cell in which the cathode reaction is the half-reaction considered, and the anode is a standard hydrogen electrode where hydrogen is oxidized:

221096817e26.title: Redox
221096817e26.sentence: The electrode potential of each half-reaction is also known as its reduction potential (Eo red), or potential when the half-reaction takes place at a cathode.

bd20e38b7dae.title: Redox
bd20e38b7dae.sentence: The reduction potential is a measure of the tendency of the oxidizing agent to be reduced.

05062b4563b1.title: Redox
05062b4563b1.sentence: Its value is zero for H+ + e− → 1⁄2H2 by definition, positive for oxidizing agents stronger than H+ (e.g., +2.866 V for F2) and negative for oxidizing agents that are weaker than H+ (e.g., −0.763V for Zn2+).

0e2f4b9d11d7.title: Redox
0e2f4b9d11d7.sentence: For a redox reaction that takes place in a cell, the potential difference is:

5ac37e8b5485.title: Redox

53754788a246.title: Soil
53754788a246.sentence: Reduction potential is measured in volts or millivolts.

fcc55e85b93d.title: Redox gradient
fcc55e85b93d.sentence: Redox conditions are measured according to the redox potential (Eh) in volts, which represents the tendency for electrons to transfer from an electron donor to an electron acceptor.

ab7991796261.title: Reduction potential
ab7991796261.sentence: Redox potential (also known as oxidation / reduction potential, ORP, pe, Ered, or Eh) is a measure of the tendency of a chemical species to acquire electrons from, or lose electrons to, an electrode and thereby be reduced or oxidised respectively.

621a8bd2f693.title: Redox gradient
621a8bd2f693.sentence: An Eh of zero represents the redox couple of the standard hydrogen electrode H+/H2, a positive Eh indicates an oxidizing environment (electrons will be accepted), and a negative Eh indicates a reducing environment (electrons will be donated).

e0bf01c4e7ae.title: Redox gradient
e0bf01c4e7ae.sentence: Eh can be calculated using half reactions and the Nernst equation.

cd38ba73ad80.title: Redox gradient
cd38ba73ad80.sentence: Soil Eh generally ranges from −300 to +900 mV.

a00e88546a9a.title: Redox gradient
a00e88546a9a.sentence: Generally accepted Eh limits that are tolerable by plants are +300 mV < Eh < +700 mV.

3ee895935e86.title: Redox gradient
3ee895935e86.sentence: 300 mV is the boundary value that separates aerobic from anaerobic conditions in wetland soils.

09716e133d05.title: Redox gradient
09716e133d05.sentence: Redox potential (Eh) is also closely tied to pH, and both have significant influence on the function of soil-plant-microorganism systems.

3c9594023790.title: Pedosphere
3c9594023790.sentence: Higher redox potentials are found at lower pH levels.

988b6144a848.title: Pedosphere
988b6144a848.sentence: The redox potential is controlled by the oxidation state of the chemical species, pH and the amount of O2 there is in the system.

a780492c2719.title: Reduction potential
a780492c2719.sentence: Aerated surface water, rivers, lakes, oceans, rainwater, and acid mine water usually have oxidizing conditions (positive potentials).

6d550dd2665a.title: Reduction potential
6d550dd2665a.sentence: In places with limitations in air supply, such as submerged soils, swamps, and marine sediments, reducing conditions (negative potentials) are the norm.

df9c2e284429.title: Reduction potential
df9c2e284429.sentence: Strictly aerobic microorganisms are generally active at positive Eh values, whereas strict anaerobes are generally active at negative Eh values.

48f84c85aecc.title: Reduction potential
48f84c85aecc.sentence: Facultative anaerobes can be active at positive Eh values, and at negative Eh values in the presence of oxygen-bearing inorganic compounds, such as nitrates and sulfates.

e4f896b78960.title: Redox gradient
e4f896b78960.sentence: A redox gradient is a series of reduction-oxidation (redox) reactions sorted according to redox potential.

02f10678340d.title: Redox gradient
02f10678340d.sentence: These redox gradients form both spatially and temporally as a result of differences in microbial processes, chemical composition of the environment, and oxidative potential.

f99238f32966.title: Redox gradient
f99238f32966.sentence: Gradients are caused by varying physiochemical properties including availability of oxygen, soil hydrology, chemical species present, and microbial processes.

47b9bfa93313.title: Redox gradient
47b9bfa93313.sentence: Common environments where redox gradients exist are coastal marshes, lakes, contaminant plumes, and soils.

d8c470d29194.title: Redox gradient
d8c470d29194.sentence: Specific environments that are commonly characterized by redox gradients include waterlogged soils, wetlands, contaminant plumes, and marine pelagic and hemipelagic sediments.

c348da18da48.title: Redox gradient
c348da18da48.sentence: The Earth has a global redox gradient with an oxidizing environment at the surface and increasingly reducing conditions below the surface.

8a264e8668c8.title: Redox gradient
8a264e8668c8.sentence: Redox gradients are generally understood at the macro level, but characterization of redox reactions in heterogeneous environments at the micro-scale require further research and more sophisticated measurement techniques.

0ea6ac0b14ab.title: Electron donor
0ea6ac0b14ab.sentence: In chemistry, an electron donor is a chemical entity that transfers electrons to another compound.

97e08d222dd7.title: Electron donor
97e08d222dd7.sentence: It is a reducing agent that, by virtue of its donating electrons, is itself oxidized in the process.

36d68ac43d9c.title: Electron donor
36d68ac43d9c.sentence: In biology, electron donors release an electron during cellular respiration, resulting in the release of energy.

5b2347f2c2ff.title: Electron donor
5b2347f2c2ff.sentence: The final result of this process (electron transport chain) is an electron being donated to an electron acceptor.

1c2dd37422c3.title: Electron donor
1c2dd37422c3.sentence: Petroleum hydrocarbons, less chlorinated solvents like vinyl chloride, soil organic matter, and reduced inorganic compounds are all compounds that can act as electron donors.

7fe54cd28b8d.title: Electron donor
7fe54cd28b8d.sentence: These reactions are of interest not only because they allow organisms to obtain energy, but also because they are involved in the natural biodegradation of organic contaminants.

f4aa588ee195.title: Electron donor
f4aa588ee195.sentence: When clean-up professionals use monitored natural attenuation to clean up contaminated sites, biodegradation is one of the major contributing processes.

52c153d477d7.title: In situ chemical oxidation
52c153d477d7.sentence: Common oxidants used in this process are permanganate (both sodium permanganate and potassium permanganate), Fenton's Reagent, persulfate, and ozone.

9a305cfeb1c6.title: In situ chemical oxidation
9a305cfeb1c6.sentence: Other oxidants can be used, but these four are the most commonly used.

a856b0256239.title: In situ chemical oxidation
a856b0256239.sentence: Fenton's reagent (hydrogen peroxide catalyzed with iron) and potassium permanganate are the oxidants that have been used the longest and remain used widely.

147ca8b1efba.title: In situ chemical oxidation
147ca8b1efba.sentence: The specificity of permanganate (chlorinated solvents require double bonds) and consumption by non-target organic material in soil are examples of these limitations.

358d7bf9d989.title: In situ chemical oxidation
358d7bf9d989.sentence: Sodium persulfate was introduced for ISCO in the late 1990s because of the limitations in using peroxide or permanganate as oxidants.

d16aca1a5cd1.title: In situ chemical oxidation
d16aca1a5cd1.sentence: Persulfate is more stable, treats a wider range of contaminants, and is not consumed by soil organics as easily.

955e5d6c7d18.title: In situ chemical oxidation
955e5d6c7d18.sentence: When the peroxide is catalyzed by soluble iron it forms hydroxyl radicals(·OH) that oxidize contaminants such as chlorinated solvents, fuel oils, and BTEX.

5b0479e4cd90.title: In situ chemical oxidation
5b0479e4cd90.sentence: Traditional Fenton's reagent usually requires a significant pH reduction of the soils and groundwater in the treatment zone to allow for the introduction and distribution of aqueous iron as iron will oxidize and precipitate at a pH greater than 3.5.

0906c1e0f5c7.title: In situ chemical oxidation
0906c1e0f5c7.sentence: Due to this, there are controversies on whether ISCO using Fenton's reagent is really a Fenton reaction.

55193fb31235.title: In situ chemical oxidation
55193fb31235.sentence: Fortunately, ozone (O 3) is about 12 times more soluble than O 2 and, although it is still comparably insoluble, it is a strong oxidant.

fed8b672e33a.title: In situ chemical oxidation
fed8b672e33a.sentence: Because, unlike other oxidants used in ISCO, it is a gas, it needs to be injected into the contamination site from the bottom rather than the top.

4b9f424a0c84.title: In situ chemical oxidation
4b9f424a0c84.sentence: Tubes are built into the ground to transport the ozone to its starting place; the bubbles then rise to the surface.

7472536eec46.title: Redox gradient
7472536eec46.sentence: The redox ladder displays the order in which redox reactions occur based on the free energy gained from redox pairs.

e82448364d05.title: Redox gradient
e82448364d05.sentence: In a redox gradient, the most energetically favorable chemical reaction occurs at the "top" of the redox ladder and the least energetically favorable reaction occurs at the "bottom" of the ladder.

038caba94879.title: Redox gradient
038caba94879.sentence: The following is a list of common reactions that occur in the environment in order from oxidizing to reducing (organisms performing the reaction in parentheses):

c1d0a5af9d4c.title: Nitrate
c1d0a5af9d4c.sentence: The redox couple NO3−/N2 is at the top of the redox scale for the anaerobic respiration, just below the couple oxygen (O2/H2O), but above the couples Mn(IV)/Mn(II), Fe(III)/Fe(II), SO42−/HS−, CO2/CH4.

e5d3b5b55717.title: Redox gradient
e5d3b5b55717.sentence: Oxygen availability in sediments determines which microbial respiration pathways can occur, resulting in a vertical stratification of redox processes as oxygen availability decreases with depth.

b4b2055be08e.title: Redox gradient
b4b2055be08e.sentence: However, distribution of microorganisms cannot solely be determined from thermodynamics (redox ladder), but is also influenced by ecological and physiological factors.

665e6a603499.title: Anaerobic respiration
665e6a603499.sentence: Anaerobic respiration is respiration using inorganic electron acceptors other than molecular oxygen (O2) in its electron transport chain.

38276cfa6e5f.title: Anaerobic respiration
38276cfa6e5f.sentence: Anaerobes instead use less-oxidizing (in either thermodynamic or kinetics sense) substances such as nitrate (NO− 3), fumarate (C 4H 2O2− 4), sulfate (SO2− 4), or elemental sulfur (S), among others.

fd8cbd71fc50.title: Anaerobic respiration
fd8cbd71fc50.sentence: These terminal electron acceptors have smaller reduction potentials than O2.

4f3abb0f3658.title: Anaerobic respiration
4f3abb0f3658.sentence: Less energy per oxidized molecule is released.

c11a027e8313.title: Anaerobic respiration
c11a027e8313.sentence: Therefore, anaerobic respiration is less efficient than aerobic.

2be4b7ebc5b6.title: Anaerobic respiration
2be4b7ebc5b6.sentence: It differs from fermentation, a biochemical reaction which transfers electrons to organic compounds..

9de002efa0f5.title: Pedosphere
9de002efa0f5.sentence: Under a few millimeters of water, heterotrophic bacteria metabolize and consume oxygen.

256939203e40.title: Pedosphere
256939203e40.sentence: They therefore deplete the soil of oxygen and create the need for anaerobic respiration.

80cf4156dc92.title: Anaerobic respiration
80cf4156dc92.sentence: Even environments that contain oxygen, such as soil, have micro-environments that lack oxygen due to the slow diffusion characteristics of oxygen gas.

9937bed85fd7.title: Pedosphere
9937bed85fd7.sentence: Some anaerobic microbial processes include denitrification, sulfate reduction and methanogenesis and are responsible for the release of N2 (nitrogen), H2S (hydrogen sulfide) and CH4 (methane).

ff04875913bc.title: Pedosphere
ff04875913bc.sentence: Other anaerobic microbial processes are linked to changes in the oxidation state of iron and manganese.

27a9656e2aec.title: Anaerobic respiration
27a9656e2aec.sentence: An example of the ecological importance of anaerobic respiration is the use of nitrate as a terminal electron acceptor, or dissimilatory denitrification, which is the main route by which fixed nitrogen is returned to the atmosphere as molecular nitrogen gas.

10787d8f84b8.title: Anaerobic respiration
10787d8f84b8.sentence: Sulfate respiration produces hydrogen sulfide, which is responsible for the characteristic 'rotten egg' smell of coastal wetlands and has the capacity to precipitate heavy metal ions from solution, leading to the deposition of sulfidic metal ores.

041160ce7231.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
041160ce7231.sentence: Aerobic respiration releases carbon dioxide, while anaerobic respiration releases methane.

56bb68b90a3d.title: Pedosphere
56bb68b90a3d.sentence: As a result of anaerobic decomposition, the soil stores large amounts of organic carbon because the soil carbon sponge stays intact.

e605036126f5.title: Martinus Beijerinck
e605036126f5.sentence: Beijerinck discovered the phenomenon of bacterial sulfate reduction, a form of anaerobic respiration.

82c3bcc2bec7.title: Redox gradient
82c3bcc2bec7.sentence: In the event of a flood, saturated soils can shift from oxic to anoxic, creating a reducing environment as anaerobic microbial processes dominate.

d5059a7b2b7b.title: Redox gradient
d5059a7b2b7b.sentence: Soil Eh is also largely a function of hydrological conditions.

6a21badbb869.title: Redox gradient
6a21badbb869.sentence: With time, the starting Eh of a soil can be restored as water drains and the soil dries out.

c6a3cb983d2b.title: Redox gradient
c6a3cb983d2b.sentence: Moreover, small anoxic hotspots may develop within soil pore spaces, creating reducing conditions.

f0b802ac340b.title: Redox gradient
f0b802ac340b.sentence: Organic matter consumes oxygen as it decomposes, resulting in reducing soil conditions and lower Eh.

b18e17b46a52.title: Pedosphere
b18e17b46a52.sentence: Bacteria, heterotrophic organisms, consume oxygen while decomposing organic material.

7c8cc904f031.title: Canadian system of soil classification
7c8cc904f031.sentence: If flooding occurs when the soil temperature is above approximately 5 °C, microbial activity results in depletion of oxygen within a few days.

55b26f46671a.title: Canadian system of soil classification
55b26f46671a.sentence: Under such conditions, oxidized soil components (e.g., nitrate, ferric oxide) are reduced.

6f6389c6885c.title: Pedosphere
6f6389c6885c.sentence: At high redox potential, the oxidized form of iron, ferric iron (Fe3+), will be deposited commonly as hematite.

f42d0e225930.title: Pedosphere
f42d0e225930.sentence: In low redox conditions, decomposition rates decrease and the deposition of ferrous iron (Fe2+) increase.

c0f4c39ced76.title: Leaching (agriculture)
c0f4c39ced76.sentence: A decrease in the soils redox potential due to prolonged water saturation may lead to reductive dissolution of ferric iron minerals that are important P sorption sites.

71dd6780a185.title: Methanogenesis
71dd6780a185.sentence: Methanogenesis or biomethanation is the formation of methane coupled to energy conservation by microbes known as methanogens.

9404ef677663.title: Methanogenesis
9404ef677663.sentence: Organisms capable of producing methane for energy conservation have been identified only from the domain Archaea, a group phylogenetically distinct from both eukaryotes and bacteria, although many live in close association with anaerobic bacteria.

d6b1b0eae49c.title: Methanogenesis
d6b1b0eae49c.sentence: In anoxic environments, it is the final step in the decomposition of biomass.

ff0e5f9513a1.title: Pedosphere
ff0e5f9513a1.sentence: In most freshwater wetlands there is little sulfate (SO2− 4) so methanogenesis becomes the dominant form of decomposition by methanogenic bacteria only when sulfate is depleted.

a2a4b3a1d214.title: Deep biosphere
a2a4b3a1d214.sentence: In upper sediments, sulfate-reducing bacteria take up most of the hydrogen, while in lower sediments the sulfate is depleted and methanogens dominate.

a8a5d4e2d0b5.title: Fen
