a8a5d4e2d0b5.sentence: Methanogenic archaea that reside in the anaerobic layers of peat combine carbon dioxide and hydrogen gas to form methane and water.

a8fda88516da.title: Microbial ecology
a8fda88516da.sentence: For example, methanogens produce methane by reducing CO2 to CH4, while methanotrophs oxidise methane back to CO2.

61bda2e75bcc.title: Carbon cycle
61bda2e75bcc.section: Processes within fast carbon cycle > Terrestrial carbon in the water cycle
61bda2e75bcc.sentence: Methane production is also typically high in the anoxic sediments of floodplains, lakes, and reservoirs.

aa4ad36d2612.title: Methanogenesis
aa4ad36d2612.sentence: During advanced stages of organic decay, all electron acceptors become depleted except carbon dioxide.

4431d1e87b3c.title: Methanogenesis
4431d1e87b3c.sentence: Only methanogenesis and fermentation can occur in the absence of electron acceptors other than carbon.

c89f05884244.title: Methanogenesis
c89f05884244.sentence: Without methanogenesis, a great deal of carbon (in the form of fermentation products) would accumulate in anaerobic environments.

02305c461b68.title: Methanogenesis
02305c461b68.sentence: As a result, the process of methanogenesis is common in rice fields and wetlands as these areas are flooded fields and are a natural methane source.

6b5a5b57bac1.title: Methanogenesis
6b5a5b57bac1.sentence: The production of methane in flooded soils like these requires microbes that prefer low oxygen levels.

3186788171fd.title: Methanogenesis
3186788171fd.sentence: Aerating methanogenic soils increases levels of sulfates and nitrates, nutrients that reduce the production of methane.

f88a4af3121a.title: Methanogenesis
f88a4af3121a.sentence: Methanogenesis in upland soils is often localized within anoxic microsites, even when the bulk soil remains aerobic.

1a0238d3b908.title: Methanogenesis
1a0238d3b908.sentence: Methane is an important greenhouse gas with a global warming potential 25 times greater than carbon dioxide (averaged over 100 years).

584dbaa202bf.title: Paddy field
584dbaa202bf.sentence: A paddy field (or paddy) is a flooded field of arable land used for growing semiaquatic crops, most notably rice and taro.

f9acde1186a1.title: Paddy field
f9acde1186a1.sentence: Paddy field farming remains the dominant form of growing rice in modern times.

61df7fd3f655.title: Paddy field
61df7fd3f655.sentence: It originates from the Neolithic rice-farming cultures of the Yangtze River basin in southern China, associated with pre-Austronesian and Hmong-Mien cultures.

7f03387a810f.title: Paddy field
7f03387a810f.sentence: Paddy fields are a major source of atmospheric methane which contributes to global warming, having been estimated to contribute in the range of 50 to 100 million tonnes of the gas per annum.

0c3f95c2cb98.title: Paddy field
0c3f95c2cb98.sentence: Rice paddies are responsible for 10% of global methane emissions, roughly equal to the emissions of the aviation industry.

995ac041089c.title: Paddy field
995ac041089c.sentence: Studies have shown that this can be significantly reduced while boosting crop yield by draining the paddies to allow the soil to aerate to interrupt methane production.

28a05efc4205.title: Fertilizer
28a05efc4205.section: Environmental effects > Contribution to the greenhouse effect
28a05efc4205.sentence: Methane emissions from crop fields (notably rice paddy fields) are increased by the application of ammonium-based fertilizers.

1ec0b123b25f.title: Anthrosol
1ec0b123b25f.sentence: An anthrosol (or anthropogenic soil) in the World Reference Base for Soil Resources (WRB) is a type of soil that has been formed or heavily modified due to long-term human activity, such as from irrigation, addition of organic waste or wet-field cultivation used to create paddy fields.

255e1d935e4d.title: Dissimilatory metal-reducing microorganisms
255e1d935e4d.sentence: Dissimilatory metal-reducing microorganisms are a group of microorganisms (both bacteria and archaea) that can perform anaerobic respiration utilizing a metal as terminal electron acceptor rather than molecular oxygen (O2), which is the terminal electron acceptor reduced to water (H2O) in aerobic respiration.

c4e8a468d5fc.title: Dissimilatory metal-reducing microorganisms
c4e8a468d5fc.sentence: The most common metals used for this end are iron [Fe(III)] and manganese [Mn(IV)], which are reduced to Fe(II) and Mn(II) respectively, and most microorganisms that reduce Fe(III) can reduce Mn(IV) as well.

c16df9ede3a2.title: Dissimilatory metal-reducing microorganisms
c16df9ede3a2.sentence: But other metals and metalloids are also used as terminal electron acceptors, such as vanadium [V(V)], chromium [Cr(VI)], molybdenum [Mo(VI)], cobalt [Co(III)], palladium [Pd(II)], gold [Au(III)], and mercury [Hg(II)].

f4559f868e9f.title: Dissimilatory metal-reducing microorganisms
f4559f868e9f.section: Conditions and mechanisms for dissimilatory metal reduction
f4559f868e9f.sentence: The process of dissimilatory metal reduction occurs in the absence of oxygen (O2), but dissimilatory metal reducers include both obligate (strict) anaerobes, such as the family Geobacteraceae, and facultative anaerobes, such as Shewanella spp.

c6fcb993306d.title: Dissimilatory metal-reducing microorganisms
c6fcb993306d.section: Conditions and mechanisms for dissimilatory metal reduction
c6fcb993306d.sentence: In soil and sediment environments, where the pH is often neutral, metals like iron are found in their solid oxidized forms, and exhibit variable reduction potential, which can affect their use by microorganisms.

968b0c911af6.title: Dissimilatory metal-reducing microorganisms
968b0c911af6.section: Conditions and mechanisms for dissimilatory metal reduction
968b0c911af6.sentence: Due to the impermeability of the cell wall to minerals and the insolubility of metal oxides, dissimilatory metal reducers have developed ways to reduce metals extracellularly via electron transfer.

664bc3ce3286.title: Dissimilatory metal-reducing microorganisms
664bc3ce3286.section: Conditions and mechanisms for dissimilatory metal reduction
664bc3ce3286.sentence: Cytochromes c, which are transmembrane proteins, play an important role in transporting electrons from the cytosol to enzymes attached to the outside of the cell.

fab2306d9037.title: Dissimilatory metal-reducing microorganisms
fab2306d9037.section: Conditions and mechanisms for dissimilatory metal reduction
fab2306d9037.sentence: For instance, some species of dissimilatory metal reducers produce compounds that can dissolve insoluble minerals or act as electron shuttles, enabling them to perform metal reduction from a distance.

9f28ebcd0e74.title: Dissimilatory metal-reducing microorganisms
9f28ebcd0e74.section: Conditions and mechanisms for dissimilatory metal reduction
9f28ebcd0e74.sentence: Other organic compounds frequently found in soils and sediments, such as humic acids, may also act as electron shuttles.

9d085dffb36f.title: Dissimilatory metal-reducing microorganisms
9d085dffb36f.sentence: A wide range of Fe(III)-bearing minerals have been observed to function as terminal electron acceptors, including magnetite, hematite, goethite, lepidocrocite, ferrihydrite, hydrous ferric oxide, smectite, illite, jarosite, among others.

bc05dd2c48f7.title: Dissimilatory metal-reducing microorganisms
bc05dd2c48f7.sentence: In natural systems, secondary minerals may form as a byproduct of bacterial metal reduction.

d22b4607d3b8.title: Dissimilatory metal-reducing microorganisms
d22b4607d3b8.sentence: Commonly observed secondary minerals produced during experimental bio-reduction by dissimilatory metal reducers include magnetite, siderite, green rust, vivianite, and hydrous Fe(II)-carbonate.

d06d2ef51acd.title: Standard hydrogen electrode
d06d2ef51acd.sentence: In electrochemistry, the standard hydrogen electrode (abbreviated SHE), is a redox electrode which forms the basis of the thermodynamic scale of oxidation-reduction potentials.

c3f1cb6fca04.title: Standard hydrogen electrode
c3f1cb6fca04.sentence: Its absolute electrode potential is estimated to be 4.44 ± 0.02 V at 25 °C, but to form a basis for comparison with all other electrochemical reactions, hydrogen's standard electrode potential (E°) is declared to be zero volts at any temperature.

535365dbc457.title: Standard hydrogen electrode
535365dbc457.sentence: Potentials of all other electrodes are compared with that of the standard hydrogen electrode at the same temperature.

90de9436b9ac.title: Standard hydrogen electrode
90de9436b9ac.sentence: This was convenient because it could actually be constructed by "[immersing] a platinum electrode into a solution of 1 N strong acid and [bubbling] hydrogen gas through the solution at about 1 atm pressure".

0185a1522862.title: Standard hydrogen electrode
0185a1522862.sentence: SHE (standard hydrogen electrode): potential of a platinum electrode in a theoretical ideal solution (the current standard for zero potential for all temperatures)

47eb28d6f482.title: Obligate anaerobe
47eb28d6f482.sentence: Obligate anaerobes are microorganisms killed by normal atmospheric concentrations of oxygen (20.95% O2).

3a999f00a2eb.title: Obligate anaerobe
3a999f00a2eb.sentence: Oxygen tolerance varies between species, with some species capable of surviving in up to 8% oxygen, while others lose viability in environments with an oxygen concentration greater than 0.5%.

53984e7ddb92.title: Obligate anaerobe
53984e7ddb92.sentence: Bacteria that fall in between these two extremes may be classified as either facultative anaerobes, which can use oxygen but also survive without it, or microaerophiles, which need lower levels of oxygen.

87b72c137fb7.title: Obligate anaerobe
87b72c137fb7.sentence: Superoxide, hydrogen peroxide, and hydroxyl radicals are a class of compounds known as reactive oxygen species (ROS), highly reactant products that are damaging to microbes, including obligate anaerobes.

adfe050bd054.title: Obligate anaerobe
adfe050bd054.sentence: Aerobic organisms produce superoxide dismutase and catalase to detoxify these products, but obligate anaerobes produce these enzymes in very small quantities, or not at all.

296bd6e44f69.title: Obligate anaerobe
296bd6e44f69.sentence: Obligate anaerobes convert nutrients into energy through anaerobic respiration or fermentation.

21317bc664f5.title: Obligate anaerobe
21317bc664f5.sentence: Examples of alternative electron acceptors include sulfate, nitrate, iron, manganese, mercury, and carbon monoxide.

4f29eb894106.title: Obligate anaerobe
4f29eb894106.sentence: The energy yield of anaerobic respiration and fermentation (i.e. the number of ATP molecules generated) is less than in aerobic respiration.

4295cddf48de.title: Obligate anaerobe
4295cddf48de.sentence: Obligate anaerobes are found in oxygen-free environments such as the intestinal tracts of animals, the deep ocean, still waters, landfills, in deep sediments of soil.

c71063bfb5c6.title: Obligate anaerobe
c71063bfb5c6.sentence: Several species of the Mycobacterium, Streptomyces, and Rhodococcus genera are examples of obligate anaerobe found in soil.

3519f3704201.title: Methanogen
3519f3704201.sentence: Methanogens are anaerobic archaea that produce methane as a byproduct of their energy metabolism, i.e., catabolism.

41ed96f86259.title: Methanogen
41ed96f86259.sentence: Methane production, or methanogenesis, is the only biochemical pathway for ATP generation in methanogens.

7945d4fa22f1.title: Methanogen
7945d4fa22f1.sentence: All known methanogens belong exclusively to the domain Archaea, although some bacteria, plants, and animal cells are also known to produce methane.

0c42fdd065ba.title: Methanogen
0c42fdd065ba.sentence: Methanogens are common in various anoxic environments, such as marine and freshwater sediments, wetlands, the digestive tracts of animals, wastewater treatment plants, rice paddy soil, and landfills.

5cc9a8a33621.title: Methanogen
5cc9a8a33621.sentence: However, the degree of oxygen sensitivity varies, as methanogenesis has often been detected in temporarily oxygenated environments such as rice paddy soil, and various molecular mechanisms potentially involved in oxygen and reactive oxygen species (ROS) detoxification have been proposed.

41e7f9b699c5.title: Methanogen
41e7f9b699c5.sentence: For instance, a recently identified species Candidatus Methanothrix paradoxum common in wetlands and soil can function in anoxic microsites within aerobic environments but it is sensitive to the presence of oxygen even at trace level and cannot usually sustain oxygen stress for a prolonged time.

c691b2e26de3.title: Obligate anaerobe
c691b2e26de3.sentence: For example, methanogens grow at a redox potential lower than -0.3 V.

a4e385298aaa.title: Iron-oxidizing bacteria
a4e385298aaa.sentence: Iron-oxidizing bacteria (or iron bacteria) are chemotrophic bacteria that derive energy by oxidizing dissolved iron.

0426c0b4229b.title: Iron-oxidizing bacteria
0426c0b4229b.sentence: Iron-oxidizing bacteria colonize the transition zone where de-oxygenated water from an anaerobic environment flows into an aerobic environment.

d0c6bdec5725.title: Iron-oxidizing bacteria
d0c6bdec5725.sentence: When de-oxygenated water reaches a source of oxygen, iron bacteria convert dissolved iron into an insoluble reddish-brown gelatinous slime that discolors stream beds and can stain plumbing fixtures, clothing, or utensils washed with the water carrying it.

3efcaf6c91de.title: Iron-oxidizing bacteria
3efcaf6c91de.sentence: They are known to grow and proliferate in waters containing iron concentrations as low as 0.1 mg/L. However, at least 0.3 ppm of dissolved oxygen is needed to carry out the oxidation.

100d649cc7a8.title: Iron-oxidizing bacteria
100d649cc7a8.sentence: Anthropogenic hazards like landfill leachate, septic drain fields, or leakage of light petroleum fuels like gasoline are other possible sources of organic materials allowing soil microbes to de-oxygenate groundwater.

8945af905553.title: Iron-oxidizing bacteria
8945af905553.sentence: Groundwater containing dissolved organic material may be de-oxygenated by microorganisms feeding on that dissolved organic material.

b3351977e06f.title: Iron-oxidizing bacteria
b3351977e06f.sentence: Useful mineral deposits of bog iron ore have formed where groundwater has historically emerged and been exposed to atmospheric oxygen.

1496db1fa77f.title: Iron-oxidizing bacteria
1496db1fa77f.sentence: However, nitrate dependent microbial Fe(II) oxidation is a light independent metabolism that has been shown to support microbial growth in various freshwater and marine sediments (paddy soil, stream, brackish lagoon, hydrothermal, deep-sea sediments) and later on demonstrated as a pronounced metabolism within the water column at the oxygen minimum zone.

fc0e2354bdcb.title: Green rust
fc0e2354bdcb.sentence: Green rust is a generic name for various green crystalline chemical compounds containing iron(II) and iron(III) cations, the hydroxide (OH−) anion, and another anion such as carbonate (CO2− 3), chloride (Cl−), or sulfate (SO2− 4), in a layered double hydroxide (LDH) structure.

1e343942a920.title: Green rust
1e343942a920.sentence: It occurs in nature as the mineral fougerite.

8fc6f5180676.title: Green rust
8fc6f5180676.sentence: On the basis of Mössbauer spectroscopy, green rust is suspected to occur as mineral in certain bluish-green soils that are formed in alternating redox conditions, and turn ochre once exposed to air.

d33462cceacc.title: Green rust
d33462cceacc.sentence: Hexagonal crystals of green rust (carbonate and/or sulfate) have also been obtained as byproducts of bioreduction of ferric oxyhydroxides by dissimilatory iron-reducing bacteria, such as Shewanella putrefaciens, that couple the reduction of Fe3+ with the oxidation of organic matter.

3c8ccb77cfb3.title: Green rust
3c8ccb77cfb3.sentence: This process has been conjectured to occur in soil solutions and aquifers.

62fac55cf8b5.title: Green rust
62fac55cf8b5.sentence: Sulfate green rust has been shown to reduce nitrate NO− 3 and nitrite NO− 2 in solution to ammonium NH+ 4, with concurrent oxidation of Fe2+ to Fe3+.

b74ade675117.title: Manganese cycle
b74ade675117.sentence: The manganese cycle is the biogeochemical cycle of manganese through the atmosphere, hydrosphere, biosphere and lithosphere.

ae9351042495.title: Manganese cycle
ae9351042495.sentence: Manganese is a heavy metal that comprises about 0.1% of the Earth's crust and a necessary element for biological processes.

1039dff58a89.title: Manganese cycle
1039dff58a89.sentence: It is cycled through the Earth in similar ways to iron, but with distinct redox pathways.

2c0c95385796.title: Manganese cycle
2c0c95385796.sentence: There are bacteria that oxidise manganese to insoluble oxides, and others that reduce it to Mn2+ in order to use it.

78cb2f4ac04d.title: Manganese cycle
78cb2f4ac04d.sentence: Manganese in the lithosphere enters the hydrosphere from weathering of regolith as well as erosion and dissolution of bedrock in rivers; in solution it then makes its way into the ocean.

a136059b3bc5.title: Manganese cycle
a136059b3bc5.sentence: Once in the ocean, Mn can form minerals and sink to the ocean floor where the solid phase is buried.

c5162c4006e1.title: Manganese cycle
c5162c4006e1.sentence: The global manganese cycle is being altered by anthropogenic influences, such as mining and mineral processing for industrial use, as well as through the burning of fossil fuels.

03fd13b66195.title: Manganese cycle
03fd13b66195.section: Anthropogenic influences > Mining and mineral processing > Releases in soils
03fd13b66195.sentence: An analysis of datasets on the soil chemistry of North America and Europe revealed greater than 50% of Mn in ridge soils near iron or steel processing facilities was attributed to anthropogenic industrial inputs, whether through solid waste disposal or previously airborne particulates depositing in soils.

c32779c8ac1d.title: Redox gradient
c32779c8ac1d.sentence: Eh can be measured by collecting samples in the field and performing analyses in the lab, or by inserting an electrode into the environment to collect in situ measurements.

1e4c1111ee55.title: Redox gradient
1e4c1111ee55.sentence: Collecting a high number of samples can produce high spatial resolution, but at the cost of low temporal resolution since samples only reflect a singular a snapshot in time.

9b63b702be87.title: Redox gradient
9b63b702be87.sentence: In situ monitoring can provide high temporal resolution by collecting continuous real-time measurements, but low spatial resolution since the electrode is in a fixed location.

f096ad9516fb.title: Redox gradient
f096ad9516fb.sentence: Typical environments to measure redox potential are in bodies of water, soils, and sediments, all of which can exhibit high levels of heterogeneity.

6949a23874cd.title: Redox gradient
6949a23874cd.sentence: Redox properties can also be tracked with high spatial and temporal resolution through the use of induced-polarization imaging, however, further research is needed to fully understand contributions of redox species to polarization.

4de01f5b0fa6.title: Redox gradient
4de01f5b0fa6.sentence: Redox gradients form based on resource availability and physiochemical conditions (pH, salinity, temperature) and support stratified communities of microbes.

74a7ab7fccfb.title: Redox gradient
74a7ab7fccfb.sentence: Microbes carry out differing respiration processes (methanogenesis, sulfate reduction, etc.) based on the conditions around them and further amplify redox gradients present in the environment.

6878761f3927.title: Redox gradient
6878761f3927.sentence: The highest rates of organic pollutant degradation along a redox gradient are found at the oxic-anoxic interface.

5fab1b1808c5.title: Redox gradient
5fab1b1808c5.sentence: Because this transition zone is both oxic and anoxic, electron acceptors and donors are in high abundance and there is a high level of microbial activity, leading to the highest rates of contaminant biodegradation.

6fc1b8575699.title: Redox gradient
6fc1b8575699.sentence: Cable bacteria have been characterized as sulfide-oxidizing bacteria that assist in connecting these areas of undersupplied and excess electrons to complete the electron transport for otherwise unavailable redox reactions.

5f95161e001f.title: Redox gradient
5f95161e001f.sentence: The community of microbes—often metal- or sulfate-reducing bacteria—produces redox gradients on the micrometer scale as a function of spatial physiochemical variability.

f6d7e12037e1.title: Redox gradient
f6d7e12037e1.sentence: Redox gradients form in water columns and their sediments.

e7b939f6d3a7.title: Redox gradient
e7b939f6d3a7.sentence: Varying levels of oxygen (oxic, suboxic, hypoxic) within the water column alter redox chemistry and which redox reactions can occur.

c8cd6f834b83.title: Redox gradient
c8cd6f834b83.sentence: Development of oxygen minimum zones also contributes to formation of redox gradients.

51464cbb4de2.title: Redox gradient
51464cbb4de2.sentence: Benthic sediments exhibit redox gradients produced by variations in mineral composition, organic matter availability, structure, and sorption dynamics.

a6e3a4d869c1.title: Redox gradient
a6e3a4d869c1.sentence: Limited transport of dissolved electrons through subsurface sediments, combined with varying pore sizes of sediments creates significant heterogeneity in benthic sediments.

58f9ffc2364e.title: Solubility equilibrium
58f9ffc2364e.sentence: Solubility equilibrium is a type of dynamic equilibrium that exists when a chemical compound in the solid state is in chemical equilibrium with a solution of that compound.

3f4681021456.title: Solubility equilibrium
3f4681021456.sentence: This type of equilibrium is an example of dynamic equilibrium in that some individual molecules migrate between the solid and solution phases such that the rates of dissolution and precipitation are equal to one another.

9964533b3d91.title: Solubility equilibrium
9964533b3d91.sentence: Each solubility equilibrium is characterized by a temperature-dependent solubility product which functions like an equilibrium constant.

19cb3cc6311f.title: Solubility equilibrium
19cb3cc6311f.sentence: When equilibrium is established and the solid has not all dissolved, the solution is said to be saturated.

fee04bd6e9cf.title: Solubility equilibrium
fee04bd6e9cf.sentence: A solution containing a higher concentration of solute than the solubility is said to be supersaturated.

94c27cbb27d5.title: Solubility equilibrium
94c27cbb27d5.sentence: In each case an equilibrium constant can be specified as a quotient of activities.

728c6b953d50.title: Solubility equilibrium
728c6b953d50.sentence: However, use of activities is very inconvenient, so the equilibrium constant is usually divided by the quotient of activity coefficients, to become a quotient of concentrations.

42ea2894258a.title: Solubility equilibrium
42ea2894258a.sentence: Leaching of aluminium salts from rocks and soil by acid rain is another example of dissolution with reaction: alumino-silicates are bases which react with the acid to form soluble species, such as Al3+(aq).

5835ec045636.title: Precipitation (chemistry)
5835ec045636.sentence: In an aqueous solution, precipitation is the "sedimentation of a solid material (a precipitate) from a liquid solution".

e0b51c8afad0.title: Precipitation (chemistry)
e0b51c8afad0.sentence: Compounds precipitate from a solution when its concentration exceeds its solubility, i.e. the solution is supersaturated.

9cee8296b154.title: Precipitation (chemistry)
9cee8296b154.sentence: Precipitation occurs more rapidly from a strongly supersaturated solution.

1dab09c4eb2f.title: Precipitation (chemistry)
1dab09c4eb2f.sentence: Supersaturation can arise from temperature changes, solvent evaporation, or by mixing solvents.

23b1b2e75533.title: Precipitation (chemistry)
23b1b2e75533.sentence: Without sufficient attraction forces (e.g., Van der Waals force) to aggregate the solid particles together and to remove them from solution by gravity (settling), they remain in suspension and form colloids.

ef0e97864b50.title: Precipitation (chemistry)
ef0e97864b50.section: Concepts and complications > Digestion and ageing
ef0e97864b50.sentence: Digestion, or precipitate ageing, happens when a freshly formed precipitate is left, usually at a higher temperature, in the solution from which it precipitates.

40dd13014ad9.title: Precipitation (chemistry)
40dd13014ad9.section: Concepts and complications > Digestion and ageing
40dd13014ad9.sentence: It results in purer and larger recrystallized particles.

756264b81313.title: Precipitation (chemistry)
756264b81313.section: Concepts and complications > Digestion and ageing
756264b81313.sentence: Ostwald ripening is the physico-chemical process underlying digestion.

19057a46b000.title: Thermodynamic activity
19057a46b000.sentence: In thermodynamics, activity (symbol a) is a measure of the "effective concentration" of a species in a mixture, in the sense that the species' chemical potential depends on the activity of a real solution in the same way that it would depend on concentration for an ideal solution.

b75ff6e88f5a.title: Thermodynamic activity
b75ff6e88f5a.sentence: By convention, activity is treated as a dimensionless quantity, although its value depends on customary choices of standard state for the species.

1b577cf75761.title: Thermodynamic activity
1b577cf75761.sentence: The activity of pure substances in condensed phases (solids and liquids) is taken as a = 1.

a34e9f6d1482.title: Thermodynamic activity
a34e9f6d1482.sentence: Activity depends on temperature, pressure and composition of the mixture, among other things.

02e3839cfdd9.title: Thermodynamic activity
02e3839cfdd9.sentence: The activity depends on the choice of standard state such that changing the standard state will also change the activity.

62ae2584d6e2.title: Thermodynamic activity
62ae2584d6e2.sentence: Equilibrium constants should be defined by activities but, in practice, are often defined by concentrations instead.

2b79223d2c9f.title: Thermodynamic activity
2b79223d2c9f.sentence: The activity coefficient γ, which is also a dimensionless quantity, relates the activity to a measured mole fraction xi (or yi in the gas phase), molality bi, mass fraction wi, molar concentration (molarity) ci or mass concentration ρi:

e1e1a286a39b.title: Thermodynamic activity
e1e1a286a39b.sentence: When the activity coefficient is close to 1, the substance shows almost ideal behaviour according to Henry's law (but not necessarily in the sense of an ideal solution).

39102d51dbde.title: Thermodynamic activity
39102d51dbde.sentence: In a liquid solution the activity coefficient of a given ion (e.g. Ca2+) isn't measurable because it is experimentally impossible to independently measure the electrochemical potential of an ion in solution.

55906f28575e.title: Thermodynamic activity
55906f28575e.sentence: (One cannot add cations without putting in anions at the same time).

9912e8a1609c.title: Thermodynamic activity
9912e8a1609c.sentence: Even though γ+ and γ– cannot be determined separately, γ± is a measurable quantity that can also be predicted for sufficiently dilute systems using Debye–Hückel theory.

1c5e9b204798.title: Thermodynamic activity
1c5e9b204798.sentence: For water as solvent, the water activity aw is the equilibrated relative humidity.

a60c8b559d01.sentence: The reduction potential (pe) and pH are two known constraints on the solubility of Mn in soils.

508f0bfbe271.title: Pourbaix diagram
508f0bfbe271.sentence: In electrochemistry, and more generally in solution chemistry, a Pourbaix diagram, also known as a potential/pH diagram, EH–pH diagram or a pE/pH diagram, is a plot of possible thermodynamically stable phases (i.e., at chemical equilibrium) of an aqueous electrochemical system.

b4ae3abee016.title: Pourbaix diagram
b4ae3abee016.sentence: Boundaries (50 %/50 %) between the predominant chemical species (aqueous ions in solution, or solid phases) are represented by lines.

1f3da4d730cb.title: Pourbaix diagram
1f3da4d730cb.sentence: Similarly to phase diagrams, they do not allow for reaction rate or kinetic effects.

59faa14c1a4d.title: Pourbaix diagram
59faa14c1a4d.sentence: - Equilibrium is always assumed, though in practice it may differ.

98a04615b2f5.title: Pourbaix diagram
98a04615b2f5.sentence: Below this line, water is reduced to hydrogen, and it will usually not be possible to pass beyond this line as long as there is still water present in the system to be reduced.

116b7b45da1f.title: Pourbaix diagram
116b7b45da1f.sentence: Above this line, water is oxidized to form oxygen gas, and it will usually not be possible to pass beyond this line as long as there is still water present in the system to be oxidized.

38fb98447b21.title: Pourbaix diagram
38fb98447b21.sentence: Pourbaix diagrams have many applications in different fields dealing with e.g., corrosion problems, geochemistry, and environmental sciences.

fc1f87a6155e.title: Pourbaix diagram
fc1f87a6155e.sentence: The diagrams are named after Marcel Pourbaix (1904–1998), the Belgian engineer who invented them.

131f16747408.title: Manganese cycle
131f16747408.sentence: Manganese is an important soil micronutrient for plant growth, playing an essential role as a catalyst in the oxygen-evolving complex of photosystem II, a photosynthetic pathway.

3ff748a109ba.title: Manganese cycle
3ff748a109ba.sentence: Soil fungi in particular have been found to oxidize the reduced, soluble form of manganese (Mn2+) under anaerobic conditions, and may reprecipitate it as manganese oxides (Mn+3 to Mn+7) under aerobic conditions, where the preferred metabolic pathway typically involves the utilization of oxygen.

97a59967ec35.title: Manganese cycle
97a59967ec35.sentence: Though much of the total Mn that is cycled in soil is biologically-mediated, some inorganic reactions also contribute to Mn oxidation or precipitation of Mn oxides.

b3f60afb2965.title: Manganese cycle
b3f60afb2965.sentence: As pH increases, Mn speciation becomes less sensitive to variations in pe.

4f287aecd71a.title: Manganese cycle
4f287aecd71a.sentence: In acidic (pH = 5) soils with high reduction potentials (pe > 8), the forms of Mn are mostly reducible, with exchangeable and soluble Mn decreasing dramatically in concentration with increases in pe.

b524d08e3510.title: 1938 USDA soil taxonomy
b524d08e3510.sentence: Hydromorphic soils form in wetland conditions.

93a146065386.title: 1938 USDA soil taxonomy
93a146065386.sentence: There are two sub-types: Gley soils - These occur when the pore spaces between the grains become saturated with water and contain no air.

02b0e2497b13.title: 1938 USDA soil taxonomy
02b0e2497b13.sentence: This lack of oxygen leads to anaerobic conditions which reduce the iron in the parent rock.

b88dc3a7a1da.title: Plinthosol
b88dc3a7a1da.sentence: Key process | Accumulation of Fe under hydromorphic conditions

a33af478f8b0.title: Gypcrust
a33af478f8b0.sentence: Gypcretes form in four distinct conditions: in well-drained soils, as buried evaporates, in hydromorphic soils, or by the exposure of subsurface horizons by erosion.

1f7080160157.title: Zinc deficiency (plant disorder)
1f7080160157.sentence: Zinc deficiency is common in many different types of soil; some soils (sandy soils, histosols and soils developed from highly weathered parent material) have low total zinc concentrations, and others have low plant-available zinc due to strong zinc sorption (calcareous soils, highly weathered soils, vertisols, hydromorphic soils, saline soils).

28bfb8f10a2e.title: Soil salinity
28bfb8f10a2e.sentence: Soil salinity is the salt content in the soil; the process of increasing the salt content is known as salinization (also called salination in American English).

b128b391e11a.title: Soil salinity
b128b391e11a.sentence: The ions responsible for salinization are: Na+, K+, Ca2+, Mg2+ and Cl−.

92e6277c67cd.title: Soil salinity
92e6277c67cd.sentence: In addition to mineral weathering, salts are also deposited via dust and precipitation.

6f2595331ff7.title: Soil salinity
6f2595331ff7.sentence: Salts may accumulate in dry regions, leading to naturally saline soils.

7c5b4017117c.title: Soil salinity
7c5b4017117c.sentence: This is the case, for example, in large parts of Australia.

5a71316af9f2.title: Soil salinity
5a71316af9f2.sentence: It can also come about through artificial processes such as irrigation and road salt.

2ae14f2a567e.title: Soil salinity
2ae14f2a567e.sentence: Disrupting drainage patterns that provide leaching can also result in salt accumulations.

4d09ad150b2d.title: Soil salinity
4d09ad150b2d.sentence: An example of this occurred in Egypt in 1970 when the Aswan High Dam was built.

9ab2cbd93b2c.title: Soil salinity
9ab2cbd93b2c.sentence: After the construction, the continuous high level of the water table led to the salinization of arable land.

54e428e9d70d.title: Soil salinity
54e428e9d70d.sentence: The increase in aridity caused by human-induced global warming also contributes to the salinization of waterlogged soils.

9a36c9c10fd6.title: Soil salinity
9a36c9c10fd6.sentence: Salinity is an important land degradation problem.

cd4cfcd2e21d.title: Soil salinity
cd4cfcd2e21d.sentence: - Detrimental effects on plant growth and yield

14ffff811ae0.title: Soil salinity
14ffff811ae0.sentence: - Damage to infrastructure (roads, bricks, corrosion of pipes and cables)

b7dd0d3d3844.title: Soil salinity
b7dd0d3d3844.sentence: - Reduction of water quality for users, sedimentation problems, increased leaching of metals, especially copper, cadmium, manganese and zinc

8a60fa7335c9.title: Soil salinity
8a60fa7335c9.sentence: Soil salinity can be reduced by leaching soluble salts out of soil with excess irrigation water of good quality (i.e. poor in salts).

aed41c0b2f36.title: Soil salinity
aed41c0b2f36.sentence: Soil salinity control involves watertable control and flushing in combination with tile drainage or another form of subsurface drainage.

e91a03e90b18.title: Soil salinity
e91a03e90b18.sentence: Calcium has been found to have a positive effect in combating salinity in soils.

7f4750cc4765.title: Soil salinity
7f4750cc4765.sentence: It has been shown to ameliorate the negative effects that salinity has such as reduced water uptake by plants.

a5ec1c5329e1.title: Soil acidification
a5ec1c5329e1.sentence: Soil acidification is the buildup of hydrogen cations, which reduces the soil pH.

97586d0e6ead.title: Soil acidification
97586d0e6ead.sentence: Chemically, this happens when a proton donor gets added to the soil.

11b472e9c1e8.title: Soil acidification
11b472e9c1e8.sentence: The donor can be an acid, such as nitric acid, sulfuric acid, or carbonic acid.

72cfe212747c.title: Soil acidification
72cfe212747c.sentence: It can also be a compound such as aluminium sulfate, which reacts in the soil to release protons.

3a42ec71a3f8.title: Soil acidification
3a42ec71a3f8.sentence: Acidification also occurs when base cations such as calcium, magnesium, potassium and sodium are leached from the soil.

61ffa5e137b4.title: Soil acidification
61ffa5e137b4.sentence: Soil acidification naturally occurs as lichens and algae begin to break down rock surfaces.

a7717f8d49c1.title: Soil acidification
a7717f8d49c1.sentence: With time and weathering, soils become more acidic in natural ecosystems.

5c15561dc5ad.title: Soil
5c15561dc5ad.sentence: Soils are initially acid and remain such when their parent materials are low in basic cations (calcium, magnesium, potassium and sodium).

001d09bc46e8.title: Soil acidification
001d09bc46e8.sentence: Soil acidification rates can vary, and increase with certain factors such as acid rain, agriculture, and pollution.

8fa2027dd984.title: Soil acidification
8fa2027dd984.sentence: There are less nutrients available in the soil, larger impact of toxic elements to plants, and consequences to soil biological functions (such as nitrogen fixation).

4f4a06ed9858.title: Soil

9367187a33b5.title: Soil salinity control

fab270f1e8f7.title: Soil salinity control

ae1029c02a02.title: Soil salinity control

458ec446a2e3.title: Soil salinity control

e0e719e89b29.title: Soil salinity control

53f11938c254.sentence: It is a general term (not to be confused with duripan) for a zone of chemical precipitation and hardening formed at or near the surface of sedimentary bodies through pedogenic or non-pedogenic processes.

d1ea76ee6642.title: Duricrust

a9131f41cef2.title: Duricrust

9dce6796687d.title: Duricrust

a3b7436e9cef.title: Duricrust

63ac8a469fe3.title: Duricrust

feaa9854adc7.title: Gypcrust

feaa9854adc7.sentence: There are two models that are used to illustrate the influence groundwater has on the formations of duricrusts like gypcrust: per ascensum and per descensum.

31fb05995a26.sentence: The per ascensum model demonstrates a situation where the water table is relatively close to the surface, allowing solutions to be drawn upwards by evaporation and eventually cement near-surface sediments once they become concentrated enough to trigger precipitation.

de6de2f53246.title: Salinity in Australia
de6de2f53246.sentence: This salt may come from prevailing winds carrying ocean salt, the evaporation of inland seas, and from weathered parent rocks.

af4cb9a09112.title: Salinity in Australia

443657bf0c9c.title: Salinity in Australia

1c026bc35443.title: Salinity in Australia

7c76de0974d4.title: Salinity in Australia

c9e9061e8551.title: Salinity in Australia

6a4d51cd7055.title: Salinity in Australia

358759e9cb84.title: Salinity in Australia

16c89a8bf4d8.title: Pyrite
16c89a8bf4d8.sentence: The mineral pyrite (/ˈpaɪraɪt/ PY-ryte), or iron pyrite, also known as fool's gold, is an iron sulfide with the chemical formula FeS2 (iron (II) disulfide).

bd8237e99a16.title: Pyrite
bd8237e99a16.sentence: Pyrite is the most common of sulfide minerals and is widespread in igneous, metamorphic, and sedimentary rocks.

ccd39f066cd8.title: Pyrite
ccd39f066cd8.sentence: Pyrite is common as an accessory mineral in shale, where it is formed by precipitation from anoxic seawater, and coal beds often contain significant pyrite.

2cd63baaf298.title: Pyrite
2cd63baaf298.sentence: Iron pyrite is unstable when exposed to the oxidizing conditions prevailing at the Earth's surface: iron pyrite in contact with atmospheric oxygen and water, or damp, ultimately decomposes into iron oxyhydroxides (ferrihydrite, FeO(OH)) and sulfuric acid (H 2SO 4).

1f033ae7a9aa.title: Pyrite
1f033ae7a9aa.sentence: This process is accelerated by the action of Acidithiobacillus bacteria which oxidize pyrite to first produce ferrous ions (Fe2+), sulfate ions (SO2− 4), and release protons (H+, or H3O+).

b875c2494774.title: Pyrite
b875c2494774.sentence: These oxidation reactions occur more rapidly when pyrite is finely dispersed (framboidal crystals initially formed by sulfate reducing bacteria (SRB) in argillaceous sediments or dust from mining operations).

25b111f75374.title: Pyrite
25b111f75374.section: Hazards > Pyrite oxidation and acid mine drainage
25b111f75374.sentence: Pyrite oxidation by atmospheric O2 in the presence of moisture (H2O) initially produces ferrous ions (Fe2+) and sulfuric acid which dissociates into sulfate ions and protons, leading to acid mine drainage (AMD).

d3c6db3dbca2.title: Pyrite
d3c6db3dbca2.sentence: This has the secondary benefit of neutralizing the acid released by pyrite oxidation and therefore slowing the oxidation cycle described above, thus reducing the likelihood of spontaneous combustion.

50adb26da0dd.title: Sodium adsorption ratio
50adb26da0dd.sentence: The sodium adsorption ratio (SAR) is an irrigation water quality parameter used in the management of sodium-affected soils.

1f12d32d8df1.title: Sodium adsorption ratio
1f12d32d8df1.sentence: It is an indicator of the suitability of water for use in agricultural irrigation, as determined from the concentrations of the main alkaline and earth alkaline cations present in the water.

638aee471956.title: Sodium adsorption ratio
638aee471956.sentence: It is also a standard diagnostic parameter for the sodicity hazard of a soil, as determined from analysis of pore water extracted from the soil.

d8e80166cd6d.title: Alkali soil
d8e80166cd6d.sentence: - The sodium adsorption ratio (SAR,) The formula for calculating sodium adsorption ratio is: SAR = ⁠[Na+]/√[Ca2+/2 + Mg2+/2]⁠ = ⁠{Na+/23}/√{Ca2+/40 + Mg2+/24}⁠ where: [] stands for concentration in milliequivalents/liter (briefly meq/L), and { } stands for concentration in mg/L. It is seen that Mg (magnesium) is thought to play a similar role as Ca (calcium).

73efa140bbc8.title: Sodium adsorption ratio
73efa140bbc8.sentence: where sodium, calcium, and magnesium concentrations are expressed in milliequivalents/liter.

09739e6d4ae3.title: Sodium adsorption ratio
09739e6d4ae3.sentence: SAR allows assessment of the state of flocculation or of dispersion of clay aggregates in a soil.

33aa594b9946.title: Sodium adsorption ratio
33aa594b9946.sentence: If irrigation water with a high SAR is applied to a soil for years, the sodium in the water can displace the calcium and magnesium in the soil.

10bd07b2f412.title: Sodium adsorption ratio
10bd07b2f412.sentence: This will cause a decrease in the ability of the soil to form stable aggregates and a loss of soil structure and tilth.

3ca407adf14a.title: Sodium adsorption ratio
3ca407adf14a.sentence: This will also lead to a decrease in infiltration and permeability of the soil to water, leading to problems with crop production.

370158cd2810.title: Sodium adsorption ratio
370158cd2810.sentence: When SAR is less than 3, there will not be a problem.

c0a3c32881a4.title: Sodium adsorption ratio
c0a3c32881a4.sentence: Sandy soils will have less problems, but fine-textured soils will have severe problems if SAR is greater than 9.

fd5ad259d7a0.title: Alkali soil
fd5ad259d7a0.sentence: The SAR should not be much higher than 20 and preferably less than 10; When the soil has been exposed to water with a certain SAR value for some time, the ESP value tends to become about equal to the SAR value.

4308a54d8cc2.title: Sodium adsorption ratio
4308a54d8cc2.sentence: The concept of SAR addresses only the effects of sodium on the stability of soil aggregates.

f268581a5dbe.title: Sodium adsorption ratio
f268581a5dbe.sentence: The effect of potassium can be similarly treated by means of the potassium adsorption ratio (PAR).

e58a3cadeca9.title: Sodium adsorption ratio
e58a3cadeca9.sentence: To take into account simultaneously all major cations present in water, a new irrigation water quality parameter was defined: the cation ratio of structural stability (CROSS), a generalization of SAR.

cb691cc72d4f.title: Electrical resistivity and conductivity
cb691cc72d4f.sentence: In physics, electrical resistivity and electrical conductivity are two intrinsic properties of materials that measure a material's local, intrinsic ability to conduct electric current.

39628226854d.title: Electrical resistivity and conductivity
39628226854d.sentence: They are reciprocals of each other, so each can be deduced from the other.

6bac80b426a0.title: Electrical resistivity and conductivity
6bac80b426a0.sentence: The SI unit of electrical resistivity is the ohm-metre (Ω⋅m).

35ad81e619b3.title: Electrical resistivity and conductivity
35ad81e619b3.sentence: The SI unit of electrical conductivity is siemens per metre (S/m).

2f0ec3e8ddc3.title: Electrical resistivity and conductivity
2f0ec3e8ddc3.sentence: (See the adjacent diagram.) When this is the case, the resistance of the conductor is directly proportional to its length and inversely proportional to its cross-sectional area, where the electrical resistivity ρ (Greek: rho) is the constant of proportionality.

5c0f77bce080.title: Electrical resistivity and conductivity
5c0f77bce080.sentence: Resistivity and conductivity are intensive properties of materials, giving the opposition of a standard cube of material to current.

b707603c2ba3.title: Electrical resistivity and conductivity
b707603c2ba3.sentence: Electrical resistance and conductance are corresponding extensive properties that give the opposition of a specific object to electric current.

a7446ade388f.title: Electrical resistivity and conductivity
a7446ade388f.section: Causes of conductivity > In ionic liquids/electrolytes
a7446ade388f.sentence: In electrolytes, electrical conduction happens not by band electrons or holes, but by full atomic species (ions) travelling, each carrying an electrical charge.

1ac1aa5ccc53.title: Electrical resistivity and conductivity
1ac1aa5ccc53.section: Causes of conductivity > In ionic liquids/electrolytes
1ac1aa5ccc53.sentence: The resistivity of ionic solutions (electrolytes) varies tremendously with concentration – while distilled water is almost an insulator, salt water is a reasonable electrical conductor.

8ada690dbcbc.title: Electrical resistivity and conductivity
8ada690dbcbc.section: Resistivity and conductivity of various materials
8ada690dbcbc.sentence: - A conductor such as a metal has high conductivity and a low resistivity.

ce30b64baba1.title: Electrical resistivity and conductivity
ce30b64baba1.section: Resistivity and conductivity of various materials
ce30b64baba1.sentence: - An insulator such as glass has low conductivity and a high resistivity.

10a15d324cd5.title: Electrical resistivity and conductivity
10a15d324cd5.sentence: In general, intrinsic semiconductor resistivity decreases with increasing temperature.

f7541da70f5a.title: Environmental impact of irrigation
f7541da70f5a.sentence: The environmental impact of irrigation relates to the changes in quantity and quality of soil and water as a result of irrigation and the subsequent effects on natural and social conditions in river basins and downstream of an irrigation scheme.

0bbf6c585574.title: Environmental impact of irrigation
0bbf6c585574.sentence: Hydrological, or direct, effects of doing this include reduction in downstream river flow, increased evaporation in the irrigated area, increased level in the water table as groundwater recharge in the area is increased and flow increased in the irrigated area.

df09036592bf.title: Environmental impact of irrigation
df09036592bf.sentence: Indirect effects are those that have consequences that take longer to develop and may also be longer-lasting.

f1ae4e9b0313.title: Environmental impact of irrigation
f1ae4e9b0313.section: Adverse impacts > Increased groundwater recharge, waterlogging, soil salinity
f1ae4e9b0313.sentence: Although reasonably high irrigation efficiencies of 70% or more (i.e., losses of 30% or less) can occur with sophisticated techniques like sprinkler irrigation and drip irrigation or by well-managed surface irrigation, in practice the losses are commonly in the order of 40% to 60%.

5876ebffd68e.title: Environmental impact of irrigation
5876ebffd68e.section: Adverse impacts > Increased groundwater recharge, waterlogging, soil salinity

cf8d71bf2837.title: Environmental impact of irrigation

cf8d71bf2837.sentence: - where water tables are shallow, the irrigation applications are reduced.

d7dc4b7a21f9.sentence: As a result, the soil is no longer leached and soil salinity problems develop

b8ccac346800.title: Environmental impact of irrigation
b8ccac346800.sentence: Over-irrigation can cause deep drainage from rising water tables that can lead to problems of irrigation salinity requiring watertable control by some form of subsurface land drainage.

dd0d8e73a451.title: Environmental impact of irrigation
dd0d8e73a451.sentence: However, if the soil is under-irrigated, it gives poor soil salinity control, which leads to increased soil salinity with the consequent buildup of toxic salts on the soil surface in areas with high evaporation.

1a108a5764e1.title: Environmental impact of irrigation
1a108a5764e1.sentence: - Estimates indicate that roughly one-third of the irrigated land in the major irrigation countries is already badly affected by salinity or is expected to become so in the near future.

fd1f17b29f95.title: Environmental impact of irrigation
fd1f17b29f95.sentence: Present estimates for Israel are 13% of the irrigated land, Australia 20%, China 15%, Iraq 50%, Egypt 30%.

4878540355e6.title: Environmental impact of irrigation
4878540355e6.sentence: Irrigated land area worldwide occupies about 16% of the total agricultural area, and the crop yield of irrigated land is roughly 40% of the total yield.

58a064558625.title: Environmental impact of irrigation
58a064558625.section: Adverse impacts > Groundwater mining with wells, land subsidence
58a064558625.sentence: When more groundwater is pumped from wells than replenished, storage of water in the aquifer is being mined, and the use of that water is no longer sustainable.

aa6f298f0429.title: Environmental impact of irrigation
aa6f298f0429.sentence: This may cause water mining, land/soil subsidence, and, along the coast, saltwater intrusion.

178fd35a3780.title: Environmental impact of irrigation

4518239d06ef.title: Soil salinity control
4518239d06ef.sentence: Soil salinity is measured as the salt concentration of the soil solution in tems of g/L or electric conductivity (EC) in dS/m.

1415daec26ca.title: Soil salinity control
1415daec26ca.sentence: The relation between these two units is about 5/3: y g/L => 5y/3 dS/m.

fbbeb4b1613f.title: Soil salinity control
fbbeb4b1613f.sentence: Seawater may have a salt concentration of 30 g/L (3%) and an EC of 50 dS/m.

4c79e173d7d1.title: Soil salinity control
4c79e173d7d1.sentence: The standard for the determination of soil salinity is from an extract of a saturated paste of the soil, and the EC is then written as ECe.

1c80c6537fed.title: Soil salinity control
1c80c6537fed.sentence: The extract is obtained by centrifugation.

14ae89d8dc5a.title: Soil salinity control
14ae89d8dc5a.sentence: The salinity can more easily be measured, without centrifugation, in a 2:1 or 5:1 water:soil mixture (in terms of g water per g dry soil) than from a saturated paste.

23bdead361ad.title: Soil salinity control
23bdead361ad.sentence: The relation between ECe and EC2:1 is about 4, hence: ECe = 4EC1:2.

6391fa6499b5.title: Soil salinity control
6391fa6499b5.sentence: Soils are considered saline when the ECe > 4.

0dc65d43a72f.title: Soil salinity control
0dc65d43a72f.sentence: When 4 < ECe < 8, the soil is called slightly saline, when 8 < ECe < 16 it is called (moderately) saline, and when ECe > 16 severely saline.

8eb7165a9b05.title: Soil salinity control
8eb7165a9b05.sentence: Sensitive crops lose their vigor already in slightly saline soils; most crops are negatively affected by (moderately) saline soils, and only salinity resistant crops thrive in severely saline soils.

48de2230d98b.title: Soil acidification
48de2230d98b.sentence: Certain parent materials also contribute to soil acidification.

840aec4cca00.title: Soil acidification
840aec4cca00.sentence: Granites and their allied igneous rocks are called "acidic" because they have a lot of free quartz, which produces silicic acid on weathering.

53c71a70917e.title: Soil acidification
53c71a70917e.sentence: Some sedimentary rocks such as shale and coal are rich in sulfides, which, when hydrated and oxidized, produce sulfuric acid which is much stronger than silicic acid.

47bc3c04bd93.title: Soil acidification
47bc3c04bd93.sentence: Also, they have relatively low amounts of calcium and magnesium.

a6d1bb516bb8.title: Soil acidification
a6d1bb516bb8.sentence: Many coal soils are too acidic to support vigorous plant growth, and coal gives off strong precursors to acid rain when it is burned.

64e1c39ff389.title: Soil acidification
64e1c39ff389.sentence: Marine clays are also sulfide-rich in many cases, and such clays become very acidic if they are drained to an oxidizing state.

1677ef62aa3b.title: Soil acidification
1677ef62aa3b.sentence: Plant roots acidify soil by releasing protons and organic acids so as to chemically weather soil minerals.

7c1cc53ec369.title: Soil acidification
7c1cc53ec369.sentence: Decaying remains of dead plants on soil may also form organic acids which contribute to soil acidification.

f80c302ab3b1.title: Soil acidification
f80c302ab3b1.sentence: Acidification from leaf litter on the O-horizon is more pronounced under coniferous trees such as pine, spruce and fir, which return fewer base cations to the soil, rather than under deciduous trees; however, soil pH differences attributed to vegetation often preexisted that vegetation, and help select for species which tolerate them.

55dd9f876934.title: Soil acidification
55dd9f876934.sentence: Calcium accumulation in existing biomass also strongly affects soil pH - a factor which can vary from species to species.

ccc584038b10.title: Soil acidification
ccc584038b10.sentence: Soil acidification can cause damage to plants and organisms in the soil.

b9d328642efd.title: Soil acidification
b9d328642efd.sentence: In plants, soil acidification results in smaller, less durable roots.

cdbc10d6bd1f.title: Soil acidification
cdbc10d6bd1f.sentence: Acidic soils sometimes damage the root tips reducing further growth.

593d9ffdff9a.title: Soil acidification
593d9ffdff9a.sentence: Plant height is impaired and seed germination also decreases.

d89ad62efac7.title: Soil acidification
d89ad62efac7.sentence: Overall, stunted growth is seen in plants.

a23d876450b7.title: Soil acidification
a23d876450b7.sentence: In the soil, acidification reduces microbial and macrofaunal diversity.

59e95badcbd0.title: Soil acidification
59e95badcbd0.sentence: Soil acidification is directly linked to a decline in endangered species of plants.

537cb41ce6d7.title: Soil acidification
537cb41ce6d7.sentence: This causes essential base cations in the soil to leach away and increase the availability of toxic ions which impairs plant roots.

6db4ed91c299.title: Soil acidification
6db4ed91c299.sentence: Another consequence of aluminum in soils is aluminum toxicity, which inhibits root growth.

bc993248d033.title: Soil acidification
bc993248d033.sentence: If a plant is being affected by soil acidification, one can closely observe the plant leaves yellowing between the veins and/or stunted growth.

744bef6ec579.title: Soil acidification
744bef6ec579.sentence: However, the symptom of yellowing leaves isn't consistent with soil acidification as it can also result from alkaline soil conditions or nutrient deficient soil.

45a2a9a0a5f5.title: Soil acidification
45a2a9a0a5f5.sentence: At a larger scale, soil acidification is linked to losses in agricultural productivity due to these effects.

54769779858c.title: Soil acidification
54769779858c.sentence: Soil acidification is a common issue in long-term crop production which can be reduced by lime, organic amendments (e.g., straw and manure) and biochar application.

15006758d4a5.title: Soil acidification
15006758d4a5.sentence: Different management strategies may also be applied to prevent further acidification: using less acidifying fertilizers, considering fertilizer amount and application timing to reduce nitrate-nitrogen leaching, good irrigation management with acid-neutralizing water, and considering the ratio of basic nutrients to nitrogen in harvested crops.

ff5f1c5ad123.title: Soil acidification
ff5f1c5ad123.sentence: In sugarcane, soybean and corn crops grown in acidic soils, lime application resulted in nutrient restoration, increase in soil pH, increase in root biomass, and better plant health.

4b1363ef112f.title: Soil acidification
4b1363ef112f.sentence: Liming deeper in the soil is more effective than surface liming, but it can be more expensive and difficult.

ff7c4412e935.title: Soil acidification
ff7c4412e935.sentence: Sulfur fertilizers should only be used in responsive crops with a high rate of crop recovery.

e9932b894c92.title: Calcareous
e9932b894c92.sentence: The term calcareous can be applied to a sediment, sedimentary rock, or soil type, which is formed from or contains a high proportion of calcium carbonate, in the form of calcite or aragonite.

541d3b1c26af.title: Calcareous
541d3b1c26af.sentence: Calcareous (/kælˈkɛəriəs/) is an adjective meaning "mostly or partly composed of calcium carbonate", in other words, containing lime or being chalky.

f3d5e854ff85.title: Calcareous
f3d5e854ff85.sentence: They are characterized by the presence of calcium carbonate in the parent material; the carbonate-ion is a base.

efd50991c580.title: Calcareous
efd50991c580.sentence: Calcareous grassland is a form of grassland characteristic of soils containing much calcium carbonate from underlying chalk or limestone rock.

97e316556ba6.title: Calcisol
97e316556ba6.sentence: Calcisols are common in calcareous parent materials and widespread in arid and semi-arid environments.

3e7d2326e43c.title: Humus
3e7d2326e43c.sentence: In low acidity soil such as calcareous soils, the activity of these earthworms establish a mixture of the humus and the underlying mineral soil known as Mull humus.

759851acdec4.title: Caliche
759851acdec4.sentence: Caliche (/kəˈliːtʃiː/) is a soil accumulation of soluble calcium carbonate at depth, where it precipitates and binds other materials—such as gravel, sand, clay, and silt.

4322afb89442.title: Caliche
4322afb89442.sentence: It occurs worldwide, in aridisol and mollisol soil orders—generally in arid or semiarid regions, including in central and western Australia, in the Kalahari Desert, in the High Plains of the western United States, in the Sonoran Desert, Chihuahuan Desert and Mojave Desert of North America, and in eastern Saudi Arabia at Al-Hasa.

63bc06941a09.title: Caliche
63bc06941a09.sentence: Caliche is also known as calcrete, or kankar (in India and the United States).

d353be59c507.title: Caliche
d353be59c507.sentence: Layers vary from a few inches to feet thick, and multiple layers can exist in a single location.

12d2c789f0c7.title: Caliche
12d2c789f0c7.sentence: The caliche layer in a soil profile is sometimes called a K horizon.

384b0de01125.title: Caliche
384b0de01125.sentence: Caliche forms where annual precipitation is less than 65 centimeters (26 in) per year and the mean annual temperature exceeds 5 °C (41 °F).

5dafdee15f9f.title: Caliche
5dafdee15f9f.sentence: Higher rainfall leaches excess calcium completely from the soil, while in very arid climates, rainfall is inadequate to leach calcium at all and only thin surface layers of calcite are formed.

2ba6adad15e0.title: Caliche
2ba6adad15e0.sentence: Plant roots play an important role in caliche formation, by releasing large amounts of carbon dioxide into the A horizon of the soil.

ca238541a954.title: Caliche
ca238541a954.sentence: Carbon dioxide levels here can exceed 15 times normal atmospheric values.

05fdda003a01.title: Caliche
05fdda003a01.sentence: This allows calcium carbonate to dissolve as bicarbonate.

0230e951e4c9.title: Caliche
0230e951e4c9.sentence: Where rainfall is adequate but not excessive, the calcium bicarbonate is carried down into the B horizon.

06a84371746a.title: Caliche
06a84371746a.sentence: Here there is less biological activity, the carbon dioxide level is much lower, and the bicarbonate reverts to insoluble carbonate.

a8954c88cad2.title: Caliche
a8954c88cad2.sentence: When rainfall is around 35 centimeters (14 in) per year, the caliche layer will be as shallow as 25 centimeters (9.8 in).

f214a1bf5a15.title: Caliche
f214a1bf5a15.sentence: When rainfall is around 75 centimeters (30 in) per year, the caliche layer will be at a depth of around 125 centimeters (49 in).

2b89b5ec6f84.title: Caliche
2b89b5ec6f84.sentence: The caliche layer disappears completely in temperate climates if annual rainfall exceeds 100 centimeters (39 in).

e4915b996892.title: Caliche
e4915b996892.sentence: In general, caliche deposition is a slow process, requiring several thousand years.

26b6eb3b9646.title: Caliche
26b6eb3b9646.sentence: The source of the calcium in caliche may be the underlying bedrock, but caliche can form even over bedrock that is not rich in calcium.

5b7e7ba83ea4.title: Caliche
5b7e7ba83ea4.sentence: This is attributed to calcium brought in as aeolian dust.

ebd061b93a5f.title: Caliche
ebd061b93a5f.sentence: First, an impermeable caliche layer prevents water from draining properly, which can keep roots from getting enough oxygen, and potentially cause salts to build up in the soil and turn it basic.

97c7b99a911c.title: Caliche
97c7b99a911c.sentence: Second, the impermeable nature of caliche beds impairs plant roots, limiting access to nutrients, water, and sound anchorage.

c853bab101ca.title: Caliche
c853bab101ca.sentence: Basic soil, along with calcium carbonate from the caliche, can prevent plants from getting enough nutrients, especially iron.

9cb82f5b310b.title: Caliche
9cb82f5b310b.sentence: An iron deficiency makes the youngest leaves turn yellow.

e0d457b0f89b.sentence: Caliches can store significant amounts of carbon, making them of significance to the overall global carbon cycle.

988622144e7d.title: Osmotic pressure
988622144e7d.sentence: Osmotic pressure is the minimum pressure which needs to be applied to a solution to prevent the inward flow of its pure solvent across a semipermeable membrane.

d4f780164c01.title: Osmotic pressure
d4f780164c01.sentence: Osmosis occurs when two solutions containing different concentrations of solute are separated by a selectively permeable membrane.

b9e8215f12b2.title: Osmotic pressure

2606ed4bdec5.sentence: The proportionality to concentration means that osmotic pressure is a colligative property.

6e7e53ace437.title: Osmotic pressure
6e7e53ace437.sentence: When a biological cell is in a hypotonic environment, the cell interior accumulates water, water flows across the cell membrane into the cell, causing it to expand.

cafd85758479.title: Osmotic pressure
cafd85758479.sentence: In plant cells, the cell wall restricts the expansion, resulting in pressure on the cell wall from within called turgor pressure.

4eab7ae3d930.title: Osmotic pressure
4eab7ae3d930.sentence: Turgor pressure allows herbaceous plants to stand upright.

2d4154d9bb3b.title: Osmotic pressure
2d4154d9bb3b.sentence: It is also the determining factor for how plants regulate the aperture of their stomata.

d366f64d294e.title: Osmotic pressure
d366f64d294e.sentence: Osmotic pressure is the basis of filtering ("reverse osmosis"), a process commonly used in water purification.

628bea68c66a.title: Osmotic pressure
628bea68c66a.sentence: The water to be purified is placed in a chamber and put under an amount of pressure greater than the osmotic pressure exerted by the water and the solutes dissolved in it.

8f54b8372166.title: Osmotic pressure

cd073ac72f4c.title: Gypcrust
cd073ac72f4c.sentence: Gypcrete or gypcrust is a hardened layer of soil, consisting of around 95% gypsum (calcium sulfate).

f99c1725a3fe.title: Gypcrust
f99c1725a3fe.sentence: Gypcrete is the arid climate's equivalent to calcrete, which is a duricrust that is unable to generate in very arid climates.

476f173ae814.title: Gypcrust
476f173ae814.sentence: Gypcrust horizons can be up to 5 m (16 ft) thick with a 75–97% gypsum (CaSO4∙2H2O) content.

fa79fb7a707e.title: Gypcrust
fa79fb7a707e.sentence: The majority of gypsum-rich layers occur where the average annual rainfall is less than 250 mm because gypsum is moderately soluble (c. 2.6 g−1 at 25 °C) and is normally leached out under higher rainfall conditions.

31ab80ab03bf.title: Gypcrust
31ab80ab03bf.sentence: The development of gypcrust has three main stages.

d328bff26ce9.title: Gypcrust
d328bff26ce9.sentence: The first stage is primary crystallization of the surface brines or groundwater; the second stage is transportation and redeposition by wind or water; and the third stage is post-depositional alteration above or below the capillary fringe.

32d78e750a77.title: Gypcrust

262834d74188.title: Gypcrust

08558b051e4f.title: Halophyte
08558b051e4f.sentence: A halophyte is a salt-tolerant plant that grows in soil or waters of high salinity, coming into contact with saline water through its roots or by salt spray, such as in saline semi-deserts, mangrove swamps, marshes and sloughs, and seashores.

c06a92502e4f.title: Halophyte
c06a92502e4f.sentence: Relatively few plant species are halophytes—perhaps only 2% of all plant species.

3d05fc603a28.title: Halophyte
3d05fc603a28.sentence: The large majority of plant species are glycophytes, which are not salt-tolerant and are damaged fairly easily by high salinity.

99e8eb84fb37.title: Halophyte
99e8eb84fb37.sentence: One quantitative measure of salt tolerance (halotolerance) is the total dissolved solids in irrigation water that a plant can tolerate.

32e3c65d6737.title: Halophyte
32e3c65d6737.sentence: Beans and rice can tolerate about 1–3 g/L, and are considered glycophytes (as are most crop plants).

0f08873d2b18.title: Halophyte
0f08873d2b18.sentence: Plants such as barley (Hordeum vulgare) and the date palm (Phoenix dactylifera) can tolerate about 5 g/L, and can be considered as marginal halophytes.

622b47d31c90.title: Halophyte
622b47d31c90.sentence: At the other extreme, Salicornia bigelovii (dwarf glasswort) grows well at 70 g/L of dissolved solids, and is a promising halophyte for use as a crop.

95c6357dfd19.title: Halophyte
95c6357dfd19.sentence: Again, according to Iversen (1936), these plants are classified with respect to the salinity of the soil on which they grow.

0ee379d00f41.title: Halophyte
0ee379d00f41.sentence: - Oligo-halophytes (amount of NaCl in the soil is 0.01 to 0.1%)

c30ea26289d8.title: Halophyte
c30ea26289d8.sentence: - Meso-halophytes (amount of NaCl in the soil is 0.1 to 1%)

39cfe8797406.title: Halophyte
39cfe8797406.sentence: - Euhalophytes (amount of NaCl in the soil is >1%)

50418b0fc891.title: Halophyte
50418b0fc891.sentence: Halophytes like Suaeda salsa can store salt ions and rare-earth elements absorbed from soils in their tissues.

663a5d3ab404.title: Halophyte
663a5d3ab404.sentence: Halophytes can therefore be used in Phytoremediation measures to adjust salinity levels of surrounding soils.

247c0fee363b.title: Halophyte
247c0fee363b.sentence: These measures aim to allow glycophytes to survive in previously uninhabitable areas through an environmentally safe, and cost effective process.

687517c781e4.title: Soil salinity control
687517c781e4.sentence: The fluctuation of the water table helps in the breathing function of the soil while the expulsion of carbon dioxide (CO2) produced by the plant roots and the inhalation of fresh oxygen (O2) is promoted.

19b31c49fc3d.title: Soil salinity control
19b31c49fc3d.sentence: The establishing of a not-too-deep water table offers the additional advantage that excessive field irrigation is discouraged, as the crop yield would be negatively affected by the resulting elevated water table, and irrigation water may be saved.

d86f06a1d6d4.title: Soil salinity control
d86f06a1d6d4.sentence: In regions with pronounced dry and wet seasons, the drainage system may be operated in the wet season only, and closed during the dry season.

39ab56303454.title: Soil salinity control
39ab56303454.sentence: This practice of checked or controlled drainage saves irrigation water.

bfc24f760336.title: Soil salinity control
bfc24f760336.sentence: The vadose zone of the soil below the soil surface and the water table is subject to four main hydrological inflow and outflow factors:

c46eb70ab6ae.title: Soil salinity control
c46eb70ab6ae.sentence: - Infiltration of rain and irrigation water (Irr) into the soil through the soil surface (Inf):

195fde269dc0.title: Soil salinity control
195fde269dc0.sentence: - Evaporation of soil water through plants and directly into the air through the soil surface (Evap)

210ea84b2aad.title: Soil salinity control
210ea84b2aad.sentence: - Percolation of water from the unsaturated zone soil into the groundwater through the watertable (Perc)

7022b6684bd2.title: Soil salinity control
7022b6684bd2.sentence: - Capillary rise of groundwater moving by capillary suction forces into the unsaturated zone (Cap)

620d72e995ce.title: Soil salinity control
620d72e995ce.sentence: The leaching efficiency is often in the order of 0.7 to 0.8, but in poorly structured, heavy clay soils it may be less.

31f10264b965.title: Soil salinity control
31f10264b965.sentence: In the Leziria Grande polder in the delta of the Tagus river in Portugal it was found that the leaching efficiency was only 0.15.

94dd37ed7012.sentence: The desired soil salinity level Cd depends on the crop tolerance to salt.

774dd819912e.title: Soil salinity control

3616f96a0855.sentence: The models use short time steps and need at least a daily, if not hourly, database of hydrological phenomena.

e7d8e32d43f2.title: Soil salinity control
e7d8e32d43f2.sentence: Simpler models, like SaltMod, based on monthly or seasonal water and soil balances and an empirical capillary rise function, are also available.

0ce3ecde2d82.title: Soil salinity control
0ce3ecde2d82.sentence: Spatial variations owing to variations in topography can be simulated and predicted using salinity cum groundwater models, like SahysMod.

ca9a51583589.title: SahysMod
ca9a51583589.sentence: SahysMod is a computer program for the prediction of the salinity of soil moisture, groundwater and drainage water, the depth of the watertable, and the drain discharge in irrigated agricultural lands, using different hydrogeologic and aquifer conditions, varying water management options, including the use of ground water for irrigation, and several crop rotation schedules, whereby the spatial variations are accounted for through a network of polygons.

8296e68f4b0d.title: SahysMod
8296e68f4b0d.sentence: Therefore, the SahysMod program was designed keeping in mind a relative simplicity of operation to facilitate the use by field technicians, engineers and project planners instead of specialized geo-hydrologists.

d6c5131f514e.title: SahysMod
d6c5131f514e.section: Methods > Calculation of aquifer conditions in polygons
d6c5131f514e.sentence: The model calculates the ground water levels and the incoming and outgoing ground water flows between the polygons by a numerical solution of the well-known Boussinesq equation.

87b4417f2085.title: SahysMod
87b4417f2085.sentence: The model is based on seasonal input data and returns seasonal outputs.

2b19969b5955.title: SahysMod
2b19969b5955.sentence: The number of seasons per year can be chosen between a minimum of one and a maximum of four.

379b49351a4b.title: SahysMod
379b49351a4b.sentence: The model permits a maximum of 240 internal and 120 external polygons with a minimum of 3 and a maximum of 6 sides each.

af56e28f00d2.title: SahysMod
af56e28f00d2.sentence: The salt balances are calculated for each soil reservoir separately.

cc5f00708e6c.title: SahysMod
cc5f00708e6c.sentence: If required, farmers' responses to waterlogging and soil salinity can be automatically accounted for.

69c223ed7c47.title: Soil salinity control
69c223ed7c47.sentence: In irrigated lands with scarce water resources suffering from drainage (high water table) and soil salinity problems, strip cropping is sometimes practiced with strips of land where every other strip is irrigated while the strips in between are left permanently fallow.

dd29f9af0abd.title: Soil salinity control
dd29f9af0abd.sentence: Owing to the water application in the irrigated strips they have a higher water table which induces flow of groundwater to the unirrigated strips.

c703dd1221ac.title: Soil salinity control
c703dd1221ac.sentence: This flow functions as subsurface drainage for the irrigated strips, whereby the water table is maintained at a not-too-shallow depth, leaching of the soil is possible, and the soil salinity can be controlled at an acceptably low level.

b1851c7580c2.title: Soil salinity control
b1851c7580c2.sentence: In the unirrigated (sacrificial) strips the soil is dry and the groundwater comes up by capillary rise and evaporates leaving the salts behind, so that here the soil salinizes.

46556d9e980f.title: Soil salinity control
46556d9e980f.sentence: Nevertheless, they can have some use for livestock, sowing salinity resistant grasses or weeds.

62a6d57c5737.title: Soil salinity control
62a6d57c5737.sentence: Moreover, useful salt resistant trees can be planted like Casuarina, Eucalyptus, or Atriplex, keeping in mind that the trees have deep rooting systems and the salinity of the wet subsoil is less than of the topsoil.

cf1b57335d2b.title: Soil salinity control
cf1b57335d2b.sentence: The unirrigated strips can also be used for salt harvesting.

c4ff7e34475b.title: Alkalinity
c4ff7e34475b.sentence: Alkalinity (from Arabic: القلوية, romanized: al-qaly, lit. 'ashes of the saltwort') is the capacity of water to resist acidification.

ae7e390edfbd.title: Alkalinity
ae7e390edfbd.sentence: Alkalinity is the strength of a buffer solution composed of weak acids and their conjugate bases.

952d2f87ccc1.title: Alkalinity
952d2f87ccc1.sentence: It should not be confused with basicity, which is an absolute measurement on the pH scale.

1721e6068a44.title: Alkalinity
1721e6068a44.sentence: It is measured by titrating the solution with an acid such as HCl until its pH changes abruptly, or it reaches a known endpoint where that happens.

19b4eae8824d.title: Alkalinity
19b4eae8824d.sentence: Alkalinity is expressed in units of concentration, such as meq/L (milliequivalents per liter), μeq/kg (microequivalents per kilogram), or mg/L CaCO3 (milligrams per liter as calcium carbonate).

40a9849cf031.title: Alkalinity
40a9849cf031.sentence: In freshwater, particularly those on non-limestone terrains, alkalinities are low and involve a lot of ions.

65568938e451.title: Alkalinity
65568938e451.sentence: It is one of the best measures of the sensitivity of the stream to acid inputs.

59d50eb1daab.title: Alkalinity
59d50eb1daab.sentence: There can be long-term changes in the alkalinity of streams and rivers in response to human disturbances such as acid rain generated by SOx and NOx emissions.

83a560ab8fe8.title: Caliche
83a560ab8fe8.sentence: In the Atacama Desert in northern Chile, vast deposits of a mixture, also referred to as caliche, are composed of gypsum, sodium chloride and other salts, and sand, associated to salitre ("Chile saltpeter").

543d96ade037.title: Caliche
543d96ade037.sentence: Salitre, in turn, is a composite of sodium nitrate (NaNO3) and potassium nitrate (KNO3).

01af007a9951.title: Caliche
01af007a9951.sentence: The deposits contain an average of 7.5% sodium nitrate, as well as sodium sulfate (18.87%), sodium chloride (4.8%), and smaller amounts of potassium, calcium, magnesium, borate, iodine, and perchlorate.

ce3760369814.title: Caliche
ce3760369814.sentence: Salitre was an important source of export revenue for Chile until the early 1930s, when Europe began to produce both nitrates industrially in large quantities.

bcf7c0cf7c6c.title: Caliche
bcf7c0cf7c6c.sentence: Caliche is the main iodine ore in Chile and the country is the world's prime producer of this element in addition to hosting over half of the worlds reserves of iodine.

67d60ffad3e8.title: Caliche
67d60ffad3e8.sentence: While the formation of other caliches is relatively well understood, the origin of Chilean caliche is not clearly known.

4833f1b5d8b3.title: Caliche
4833f1b5d8b3.sentence: One possibility is that the deposits were formed when a prehistoric inland sea evaporated.

92bd0312ac1e.title: Caliche
92bd0312ac1e.sentence: Another theory is that it was deposited due to weathering of the Andes.

7cdf5867a219.title: Framboid
7cdf5867a219.sentence: A framboid is a micromorphological feature common to certain sedimentary minerals, particularly pyrite (FeS2).

156f8372f8e5.title: Framboid
156f8372f8e5.sentence: Framboidal structure comprises roughly spherical aggregates of discrete equi-regular euhedral microcrystallites of around 0.5 μm in diameter, with the average aggregate size ranging from 5-20 μm.

03389056fccc.title: Framboid
03389056fccc.sentence: The first known use of the term is ascribed to Rust in 1935 and is derived from the French 'framboise', meaning 'raspberry', reflecting the appearance of the structure under magnification.

09f6b82d336b.title: Acid sulfate soil
