d5215a415ad7.title: Acid sulfate soil
d5215a415ad7.sentence: This in turn reacts with dissolved ferrous iron, forming very fine grained and highly reactive framboid crystals of iron sulfides such as (pyrite).

a73371ef5048.title: Framboid
a73371ef5048.sentence: Framboidal pyrite is commonly found in coastal sediments, for instance marsh soils, marine and estuarine sediments, and beach sands.

a4c985c45543.title: Framboid
a4c985c45543.sentence: Greigite is considered an essential precursor of framboidal pyrite formation.

fda00ad9c062.title: Framboid
fda00ad9c062.sentence: Framboids were once thought to be fossilised bacterial colonies or microorganisms, but successful synthesis of this structure under laboratory conditions and observation of framboids in locations hostile to microbial life have discounted this theory.

2e3fdd531541.title: Brønsted–Lowry acid–base theory
2e3fdd531541.sentence: The Brønsted–Lowry theory (also called proton theory of acids and bases) is an acid–base reaction theory, developed independently in 1923 by physical chemists Johannes Nicolaus Brønsted (in Denmark) and Thomas Martin Lowry (in the United Kingdom).

825e908a5917.title: Brønsted–Lowry acid–base theory
825e908a5917.sentence: The acid, HA, is a proton donor which can lose a proton to become its conjugate base, A−.

ed77d7fed3d9.title: Brønsted–Lowry acid–base theory
ed77d7fed3d9.sentence: The base, B, is a proton acceptor which can become its conjugate acid, HB+.

0347dd3ebbbc.title: Brønsted–Lowry acid–base theory
0347dd3ebbbc.sentence: The basic concept of this theory is that when an acid and a base react with each other, the acid forms its conjugate base, and the base forms its conjugate acid by exchange of a proton (the hydrogen cation, or H+).

746b8b1e62d2.title: Brønsted–Lowry acid–base theory
746b8b1e62d2.sentence: In 1923, physical chemists Johannes Nicolaus Brønsted in Denmark and Thomas Martin Lowry in England both independently proposed the theory named after them.

5aca3eb8edfd.title: Brønsted–Lowry acid–base theory
5aca3eb8edfd.sentence: This theory generalises the Arrhenius theory.

ab490621e763.title: Brønsted–Lowry acid–base theory
ab490621e763.sentence: Acetic acid, CH3COOH, is an acid because it donates a proton to water (H2O) and becomes its conjugate base, the acetate ion (CH3COO−).

d77036aa7566.title: Brønsted–Lowry acid–base theory
d77036aa7566.sentence: H2O is a base because it accepts a proton from CH3COOH and becomes its conjugate acid, the hydronium ion (H3O+).

ff5dd872439c.title: Brønsted–Lowry acid–base theory
ff5dd872439c.sentence: One feature of the Brønsted–Lowry theory in contrast to Arrhenius theory is that it does not require an acid to dissociate.

28279fd2fc3c.title: Brønsted–Lowry acid–base theory
28279fd2fc3c.sentence: The essence of Brønsted–Lowry theory is that an acid is only such in relation to a base, and vice versa.

638f71872a4c.title: Brønsted–Lowry acid–base theory
638f71872a4c.sentence: Water is amphoteric as it can act as an acid or as a base.

d8d20fecbbf4.title: Brønsted–Lowry acid–base theory
d8d20fecbbf4.sentence: Another example is illustrated by substances like aluminium hydroxide, Al(OH)3 (also written as Al(OH)3(H2O)3).

0a5c9d1537ea.title: Brønsted–Lowry acid–base theory
0a5c9d1537ea.sentence: In the same year that Brønsted and Lowry published their theory, G. N. Lewis created an alternative theory of acid–base reactions.

d8977673ad89.title: Brønsted–Lowry acid–base theory
d8977673ad89.sentence: A Lewis base is a compound that can give an electron pair to a Lewis acid, a compound that can accept an electron pair.

6213a5e60ea3.title: Brønsted–Lowry acid–base theory
6213a5e60ea3.sentence: Lewis's proposal explains the Brønsted–Lowry classification using electronic structure.

07d0221c7a38.title: Buffer solution
07d0221c7a38.sentence: A buffer solution is a solution whose pH does not change significantly on dilution or if a small amount of strong acid or base is added to it at constant temperature.

21d95e0402f8.title: Buffer solution
21d95e0402f8.sentence: Buffer solutions resist pH change because of a chemical equilibrium between the weak acid HA and its conjugate base A−:

18b506feb204.title: Buffer solution
18b506feb204.sentence: When some strong acid is added to an equilibrium mixture of the weak acid and its conjugate base, hydrogen ions (H+) are added, and the equilibrium is shifted to the left, in accordance with Le Chatelier's principle.

c99c20cb61c0.title: Buffer solution
c99c20cb61c0.sentence: Because of this, the hydrogen ion concentration increases by less than the amount expected for the quantity of strong acid added.

3ba42d8f23b2.title: Buffer solution
3ba42d8f23b2.sentence: Similarly, if strong alkali is added to the mixture, the hydrogen ion concentration decreases by less than the amount expected for the quantity of alkali added.

2ced07297b20.title: Buffer solution
2ced07297b20.sentence: The pH changes relatively slowly in the buffer region, pH = pKa ± 1, centered at pH = 4.7, where [HA] = [A−].

1dfe8dc30134.title: Buffer solution
1dfe8dc30134.sentence: Once the acid is more than 95% deprotonated, the pH rises rapidly because most of the added alkali is consumed in the neutralization reaction.

52dc8d0d7328.title: Buffer solution
52dc8d0d7328.section: Principles > Buffer capacity and buffer index
52dc8d0d7328.sentence: The buffer capacity (β) is a measure of the amount (number of moles or gram-equivalents, Δn) of a strong acid or base added to a given volume (V) of solution required to change its pH by a given amount (ΔpH).

40654914e400.title: Buffer solution
40654914e400.section: Principles > Buffer capacity and buffer index
40654914e400.sentence: The buffer capacity (β) is highest when the addition of a large amount (Δn) of acid or base to the solution volume produces only a small pH change (ΔpH).

294fcadb9e21.title: Buffer solution
294fcadb9e21.section: Principles > Buffer capacity and buffer index
294fcadb9e21.sentence: The buffer index (also β) considers an infinitesimal change in pH (for mathematical calculation purposes), whereas the buffer capacity considers a macroscopic pH change of 1 pH unit (for titration measurements).

67e657d73cc6.title: Buffer solution
67e657d73cc6.sentence: Polyprotic acids are acids that can lose more than one proton.

d811ae590e96.title: Buffer solution

7f387630cf8c.title: Buffer solution

c2871165ff77.title: Buffer solution
c2871165ff77.sentence: Alternatively, a buffer mixture can be made from a mixture of an acid and its conjugate base.

c52eaaabcae4.title: Buffer solution
c52eaaabcae4.sentence: For example, an acetate buffer can be made from a mixture of acetic acid and sodium acetate.

f2de5bdadc0e.title: Buffer solution

ce62a03472b1.title: Buffer solution

c85f6a608aa2.sentence: Conductivity or specific conductance of an electrolyte solution is a measure of its ability to conduct electricity.

c7e28f4b278b.title: Conductivity (electrolytic)
c7e28f4b278b.sentence: Conductivity measurements are used routinely in many industrial and environmental applications as a fast, inexpensive and reliable way of measuring the ionic content in a solution.

1c9cb518e6ae.title: Conductivity (electrolytic)

9c2836e7a557.title: Acid sulfate soil
9c2836e7a557.sentence: For example, ABA is used to calculate the amount of neutralising agent (e.g., lime) required to neutralise stockpiled sulfidic material generated from excavation or dredging activities.

0168d43054f0.title: Acid sulfate soil
0168d43054f0.sentence: The standard Australian ABA system describes three operationally defined pools of acidity (mol H+ per tonne dry soil).

83dc9cd73d56.title: Acid sulfate soil

66856817f8a0.title: Acid sulfate soil
66856817f8a0.sentence: Potential Sulfidic Acidity (PSA) is a measure of the ‘oxidisable sulfur’ associated with Reduced Inorganic Sulfur (RIS) (e.g., iron sulfides and elemental sulfur) that may oxidise to produce sulfuric acid.

316668abd35c.title: Acid sulfate soil

316668abd35c.sentence: However, sulfate minerals (e.g., gypsum, epsomite, and jarosite) and organic matter typically constitute additional sources of sulfur in most sulfidic and sulfuric soils.

65f786e1c64a.sentence: Chromium Reducible Sulfur (SCR or CRS) accurately measures RIS without significant interference from these other sources of sulfur.

47b55f045185.title: Acid sulfate soil

47b55f045185.sentence: Oxidation of RIS occurs rapidly under ambient conditions This is especially true for iron monosulfides, which have a higher surface area than iron disulfides.

e7a17160ae99.section: Acid Base Accounting > Preservation of Acid Sulfate Soil Samples
e7a17160ae99.sentence: Consequently, acid sulfate soil samples should be immediately cooled to < 4°C to slow oxidation; and samples containing monosulfidic material should be immediately frozen (e.g., using a portable freezer or liquid nitrogen).

b0a47ac5be52.sentence: By raising the water table, after damage has been inflicted due to over-intensive drainage, the soils can be restored.

1124a6ad6d72.sentence: Therefore, acid sulfate soils may be described more technically as soils that contain sulfidic and/or sulfuric material.

cd19c6f0a602.title: Acid sulfate soil
cd19c6f0a602.section: Australian Terminology > Sulfidic and Sulfuric Material
cd19c6f0a602.sentence: Sulfidic material refers to “soil materials containing detectable inorganic sulfides (≥0.01% sulfidic sulfur) that can exist as horizons or layers at least 30 mm thick or as surficial features”, and is further divided into 3 classes: hyposulfidic, hypersulfidic, and monosulfidic.

a93bccfdc955.title: Acid sulfate soil
a93bccfdc955.section: Australian Terminology > Sulfidic and Sulfuric Material
a93bccfdc955.sentence: Sulfuric material refers to soil material that has a pH of less than 4 owing to the oxidation of sulfidic material.

b7a0fec31a89.title: Acid sulfate soil
b7a0fec31a89.section: Australian Terminology > Sulfidic and Sulfuric Material
b7a0fec31a89.sentence: Conceptually, hyposulfidic and hypersulfidic materials are used to distinguish between sulfidic material that, respectively, would not and would experience a drop in pH to below 4 if exposed to prevailing oxidising conditions.

8e1b2c580116.title: Acid sulfate soil
8e1b2c580116.sentence: Although the aerobic weathering of hyposulfidic material does not produce excess acidity, it typically generates a saline solution containing environmentally hazardous concentrations of metals and metalloids.Therefore, 'hyposulfidic material' should be used instead of 'self-neutralising acid sulfate soil'.

55f8c3392015.title: Acid sulfate soil
55f8c3392015.section: Australian Terminology > Sulfidic and Sulfuric Material
55f8c3392015.sentence: The terms ‘sulfidic material’ and ‘sulfuric material’ were primarily coined by Prof Delvin Fanning (University of Maryland), Prof Martin Rabenhorst (University of Maryland), and Prof Rob Fitzpatrick (University of Adelaide) – and have been incorporated into the Australian Soil Classification (ASC) and World Reference Base (WRB) as diagnostic features of soil.

b3183c573b3f.title: Acid sulfate soil
b3183c573b3f.sentence: The term 'self-neutralising' acid sulfate soils has been used to refer to sulfidic material which does not become acidic upon oxidation due to the presence of alkaline materials (e.g., marine carbonates) - which neutralise acidity generated by the oxidation of sulfidic material.

35fb67eddec8.title: Acid sulfate soil
35fb67eddec8.sentence: The use of this term is discouraged as it can give the impression that the soil is not hazardous.

d2cbd47936bd.title: Dryland salinity
d2cbd47936bd.sentence: Dryland salinity management often focuses on vegetation, yet it is the collective role of soils and vegetation that has an effect on the root cause of the problem, recharge.

604b738683e3.title: Dryland salinity
604b738683e3.sentence: Soil is considered in two contexts when it comes to dryland salinity: Recharge and discharge.

f50b6b24bf4d.title: Dryland salinity
f50b6b24bf4d.sentence: Soils absorb and store water according to their water holding or field capacity and how dry they are to start with.

625ebb633a01.title: Dryland salinity
625ebb633a01.sentence: The drier the soil when leading into winter, the more water can be stored that might otherwise leak to groundwater.

36c57cad3767.title: Dryland salinity
36c57cad3767.sentence: To reduce recharge to levels that existed in pre-clearing conditions is generally infeasible in most agricultural landscapes.

03cac2c9597a.title: Dryland salinity
03cac2c9597a.sentence: This is because there are too few profitable perennials that can replace crops or that can be adopted at the scale required.

a4710ac3b6fc.title: Dryland salinity
a4710ac3b6fc.sentence: In most recharge areas that are at risk of future salinity, the goal is to minimise recharge.

c83de295c55a.title: Dryland salinity
c83de295c55a.sentence: This can be done by planting wide-spaced trees (alley farming), areas of perennials on suitable soils, and by preventing soils from being left without a significant leaf area in winter and spring.

96bc4a25aea8.title: Dryland salinity
96bc4a25aea8.sentence: In discharge areas, salinity can be managed by establishing salt-tolerant plants or by engineering systems.

92bfa8650c90.title: Dryland salinity
92bfa8650c90.sentence: Engineering systems include deep open drains, pumps, siphons and various forms of surface water management.

453e4358fba6.title: Dryland salinity
453e4358fba6.sentence: In addition, recharge is the source of fresh groundwater, and a trade off between consumptive use and salinity should be acknowledged.

f98b2a2b5f1d.title: Dryland salinity
f98b2a2b5f1d.sentence: There are two types of salinity: Primary salinity (natural salinity) and secondary salinity (induced salinity).

3f4ba65ec138.title: Dryland salinity
3f4ba65ec138.sentence: Primary salinity naturally occurs in arid and saline environments such as salt lakes, marshes, pans and salt flats.

84e02f2a3e84.title: Dryland salinity
84e02f2a3e84.sentence: Natural accumulation of salt in soils is an outcome from previous cycles of drainage, desiccation and sea winds.

a51d37c55603.title: Dryland salinity
a51d37c55603.sentence: Secondary salinity is a direct result of human interaction with the land, during development, agriculture and irrigation.

3347ed6d5b62.title: Dryland salinity
3347ed6d5b62.sentence: Certain land practices have led to changes in the natural structure of the biosphere resulting in excess salting of the land, waterways and soils; thus having detrimental effects on biodiversity and the lands' productivity.

8a2ab8be9e63.title: Saltwater intrusion
8a2ab8be9e63.sentence: Saltwater intrusion is the movement of saline water into freshwater aquifers, which can lead to groundwater quality degradation, including drinking water sources, and other consequences.

601790b5e565.title: Saltwater intrusion
601790b5e565.sentence: Saltwater intrusion can naturally occur in coastal aquifers, owing to the hydraulic connection between groundwater and seawater.

b199b1d3affb.title: Saltwater intrusion
b199b1d3affb.sentence: Because saline water has a higher mineral content than freshwater, it is denser and has a higher water pressure.

2b1abdea8598.title: Saltwater intrusion
2b1abdea8598.sentence: As a result, saltwater can push inland beneath the freshwater.

0c058022cf95.title: Saltwater intrusion
0c058022cf95.sentence: Certain human activities, especially groundwater pumping from coastal freshwater wells, have increased saltwater intrusion in many coastal areas.

c4c4d4f772e3.title: Saltwater intrusion
c4c4d4f772e3.sentence: Water extraction drops the level of fresh groundwater, reducing its water pressure and allowing saltwater to flow further inland.

7b8693590846.title: Saltwater intrusion
7b8693590846.sentence: Other contributors to saltwater intrusion include navigation channels or agricultural and drainage channels, which provide conduits for saltwater to move inland.

152c959135b8.title: Saltwater intrusion
152c959135b8.sentence: Sea level rise caused by climate change also contributes to saltwater intrusion.

03f2e29d515c.title: Saltwater intrusion
03f2e29d515c.sentence: Saltwater intrusion can also be worsened by extreme events like hurricane storm surges.

98b7525515ea.title: Saltwater intrusion
98b7525515ea.sentence: The seawater intrusion (SWI) into rivers can lead to many negative consequences, especially on agricultural activities and live ecosystems in upstream areas of rivers.

b61da701d410.title: Saline seep
b61da701d410.sentence: A saline seep is seep of saline water, with an area of alkali salt crystals that form when the salty water reaches the surface and evaporates.

074a954f5e9a.title: Saline seep
074a954f5e9a.sentence: Various types of water movement form saline seeps, including capillary action from a water table under the surface, and a water table being brought to the surface in a flow.

f0a2642c2806.title: Dryland salinity
f0a2642c2806.sentence: When brackish to saline groundwater intersects the ground surface and discharges, this is termed saline discharge.

5dcd9960eb22.title: Dryland salinity
5dcd9960eb22.sentence: Areas of discharge are called saline seeps (when groundwater intersects the soil surface) or saline scalds (where water is lost by evaporation only).

86f49c2e4785.title: Saline seep
86f49c2e4785.sentence: Saline seeps are considered detrimental for agriculture, as they may reduce yields and restrict growth.

8b50df3a5bc2.title: Saline seep
8b50df3a5bc2.sentence: Biota adapted to saline conditions, often endemic, thrive in the specialized habitat.

98f58f2d5dfc.title: Halotolerance
98f58f2d5dfc.sentence: Halotolerance is the ability of organisms to live in salt concentrations beyond which is necessary for their growth.

edf898bfbf8c.title: Halotolerance
edf898bfbf8c.sentence: Halotolerant species are found in saline waters and soils.

6c1691305f9f.title: Halotolerance
6c1691305f9f.sentence: Halotolerant microorganisms include bacteria, archaea, and fungi.

d808729be913.title: Halotolerance
d808729be913.sentence: Halophilic microorganisms require salt to grow; halotolerant organisms may be classified as some degree halophilic, but are often contrasted from halophiles because halotolerant organisms do not require a high-salinity environment.

1fdcaf44ab58.title: Halotolerance
1fdcaf44ab58.sentence: High concentrations of salt in soil or water that plants live in can trigger ionic imbalances which cause complications in respiration and photosynthesis, leading to reduced rates of growth, injury and death in severe cases.

8a47924b4062.title: Halotolerance
8a47924b4062.sentence: Halotolerant organisms must cope with the stress of changing and high salinity; osmotic stress and ionic stress is put on cells in high salinity.

30d00a618838.title: Halotolerance
30d00a618838.sentence: An environment of high salinity leads to loss of water in the cell, so halotolerant organisms have developed mechanisms to retain water and sequester salt within the cell.

bf30cd2f30f5.title: Halotolerance
bf30cd2f30f5.sentence: Halotlerant bacteria effectively remediate saline soil by lowering the Na contents and sodium absorption ratios in soil and by degrading toxic compounds.

9c60092f603c.title: Maas–Hoffman model
9c60092f603c.sentence: The Maas–Hoffman model is a mathematical tool to characterize the relation between crop production and soil salinity.

c5657b67615c.title: Maas–Hoffman model
c5657b67615c.sentence: It describes the crop response by a broken line of which the first part is horizontal and the second is sloping downward.

e8059624484f.title: Maas–Hoffman model
e8059624484f.sentence: The breakpoint (Pb) or threshold is also called tolerance because up to that point the yield is unaffected by the salinity, so the salt is tolerated, while at greater salinity values the crops are affected negatively and the yield goes down.

658f7d5788b2.title: Maas–Hoffman model
658f7d5788b2.sentence: where Y is the crop production or yield, C is the maximum yield, X is the soil salinity, A is the slope (regression coefficient) of the descending line, and B is the regression constant of that line.

9d46eb9b2710.title: Maas–Hoffman model
9d46eb9b2710.sentence: The value of Pb is to be found by regression analysis and optimization so that the goodness of fit of the data to the model is maximum.

9214520c934c.title: Salt tolerance of crops
9214520c934c.sentence: Using the Maas–Hoffman model in situations with a flat trend in the tail-end may lead to a breakpoint with a low ECe value, owing to the employment of the condition to minimize the deviations of the model values from the observed values over the entire domain (i.e. including the tail-end).

afd42e0940e0.title: Maas–Hoffman model
afd42e0940e0.sentence: For growth factors, like the depth of the watertable, that affect crop production negatively at low values while there is no effect at high values, the inverted Maas–Hoffman model can be used.

508d0bf6d527.title: Road salt
508d0bf6d527.sentence: Road salt (also known as deicing salt, rock salt, snow salt or grit salt) is a salt used mainly as an anti-slip and deicing agent for roads, sidewalks and other transportation surfaces during the winter.

721e3dffe830.title: Road salt
721e3dffe830.sentence: Chloride ions from road salt can accumulate in soils, surface waters, and groundwater, where they persist and may harm aquatic ecosystems, roadside vegetation, and drinking water supplies.

6f06ac741e63.title: Road salt
6f06ac741e63.sentence: The most commonly used form is sodium chloride (NaCl), though other salts such as calcium chloride and magnesium chloride are also employed, especially in colder temperatures.

1511139e62b5.title: Road salt
1511139e62b5.sentence: Millions of tons of salt are applied to road surfaces yearly, making it one of the most extensively used chemical agents in urban infrastructure.

4d5a0e3f46f7.title: Road salt
4d5a0e3f46f7.sentence: The accumulation of salt in roadside soils adversely affects vegetation by increasing soil salinity, which can hinder plant growth and lead to the death of sensitive species.

db1b576e88b2.title: Road salt
db1b576e88b2.sentence: This degradation of plant life not only disrupts local ecosystems but also contributes to soil erosion.

56d954631d80.title: Deicing
56d954631d80.section: Environmental impact and mitigation > Road salt
56d954631d80.sentence: Environmental concerns primarily include the contamination of waterways, endangerment of wildlife, and soil salinization.

d5a40ec712e1.title: Van Genuchten–Gupta model
d5a40ec712e1.sentence: The Van Genuchten–Gupta model is an inverted S-curve applicable to crop yield and soil salinity relations.

99e020441a85.title: Van Genuchten–Gupta model
99e020441a85.sentence: It is named after Martinus Theodore van Genuchten and Satyandra K. Gupta's work from the 1990s.

eac1b55de861.title: Van Genuchten–Gupta model
eac1b55de861.sentence: where Y is the yield, Ym is the maximum yield of the model, C is salt concentration of the soil, C50 is the C value at 50% yield, and P is an exponent to be found by optimization and maximizing the model's goodness of fit to the data.

8e1d83a79ebb.title: Van Genuchten–Gupta model
8e1d83a79ebb.sentence: As an alternative, the logistic S-function can be used.

976bf9a9d84d.title: Van Genuchten–Gupta model
976bf9a9d84d.sentence: The third degree or cubic regression also offers a useful alternative.

14f433158ff0.sentence: Clay particles with considerable ESP (> 16), in contact with non-saline soil moisture have an expanded DDL zone and the soil swells (dispersion).

b7f0257a8b49.title: Gypsum
b7f0257a8b49.sentence: The exchangeable sodium percentage is also reduced by gypsum application.

69a7715d04ef.title: Alkali soil
69a7715d04ef.sentence: Alkali soils owe their unfavorable physico-chemical properties mainly to the dominating presence of sodium carbonate, which causes the soil to swell and makes it difficult to clarify/settle.

a3dd88cdd5a6.title: Alkali soil
a3dd88cdd5a6.sentence: Sometimes these soils are also referred to as alkaline sodic soils.

9be05359944e.title: Alkali soil
9be05359944e.sentence: They frequently have a hard calcareous layer 0.5 to 1 metre (1.6 to 3.3 ft) beneath the surface.

d66b83b323e6.title: Alkali soil
d66b83b323e6.sentence: Soil alkalinity is associated with the presence of sodium carbonate (Na2CO3) or sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO3) in the soil, either as a result of natural weathering of the soil minerals or brought in by irrigation and/or flood water.

06d85d2a565f.title: Alkali soil
06d85d2a565f.sentence: The natural cause is the presence of soil minerals producing sodium carbonate (Na2CO3) and sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO3) upon weathering.

658d16e51658.title: Alkali soil
658d16e51658.sentence: Na2CO3 is about 78000 times more soluble than CaCO3, so it can dissolve far larger amounts of CO2− 3, thus increasing pH to values higher than 8.5, which is above the maximum attainable pH when calcium carbonate and dissolved carbon dioxide are in equilibrium in the soil solution.

c20eb8bda5ed.title: Alkali soil
c20eb8bda5ed.sentence: The phenomenon results in deterioration of the soil structure, and especially crust formation and compaction of the top layer.

c66dfda42e11.title: Alkali soil
c66dfda42e11.sentence: Hence the infiltration capacity of the soil and the water availability in the soil is reduced, whereas the surface-waterlogging or surface runoff is increased.

a57196e49405.title: Alkali soil
a57196e49405.sentence: Alkalinity problems are more pronounced in clay soils than in loamy, silty or sandy soils.

f18078ddb0d8.title: Alkali soil
f18078ddb0d8.sentence: Alkaline soils, in principle, are not saline since the alkalinity problem is worse as the salinity is less.

2339b27c0fee.title: Alkali soil
2339b27c0fee.sentence: Agriculture in alkaline soils is therefore usually limited to crops tolerant to surface waterlogging (e.g. rice).

11e323d63e55.title: Alkali soil
11e323d63e55.sentence: By replacing calcium and magnesium with sodium softened water used in irrigation (surface or groundwater) dissolves soil organic matter and disperses clay mineral particles, resulting in poor soil structure and low infiltration capacity typical of alkali soils.

972ba4f8d2a2.title: Alkali soil
972ba4f8d2a2.sentence: The causes of soil alkalinity can be natural or man-made.

a2c6d48bcd1e.title: Alkali soil
a2c6d48bcd1e.sentence: The sodium in these salts enters into surface waters or groundwater in the process of production or consumption, enhancing water sodicity.

2c8ab67f1d0d.title: Alkali soil
2c8ab67f1d0d.sentence: Coal-fired boilers and power plants, when burning coal or lignite rich in limestone, produce a type of ash containing calcium oxide, known as fly ash.

c2db520898f3.title: Alkali soil
c2db520898f3.sentence: Calcium oxide readily dissolves in water to form slaked lime, Ca(OH)2, an effluent which is carried by runoff to rivers and irrigation systems which it pollutes unless clean coal technologies such as IGCC achieve zero water discharge.

e861fc2524a5.title: Alkali soil
e861fc2524a5.sentence: The process of lime softening precipitates Ca2+ and Mg2+ ions and thereby removes hardness in the water and also converts sodium bicarbonates in river water into sodium carbonate.

cec83bd8c777.title: Alkali soil
cec83bd8c777.sentence: The total global consumption of sodium chloride was 280 million tons in the year 2020.

03bc3736e1b5.title: Alkali soil
03bc3736e1b5.sentence: Sodium salt load problems are particularly egregious in downstream areas of intensively cultivated river basins in China, India, Egypt, Pakistan, West Asia, Australia, the Western United States, etc., due to accumulation of salts in the remaining water after meeting various transpiration and evaporation losses.

148d552523e3.title: Alkali soil
148d552523e3.sentence: While traditional reclamation often requires extensive chemical amendments and drainage infrastructure, aquaculture offers an alternative or complementary strategy by using water bodies to leach salts and problematic soil compounds, introduce organic matter, and create conditions for biological soil improvement.

5c6d495cf14b.title: Alkali soil
5c6d495cf14b.sentence: Since the 1990s, research and experimentation have been conducted in China and elsewhere for remediation and utilization of alkali land via combined agriculture and aquaculture practices, with considerable success and gains in experience.

292e1b77b2db.title: Alkali soil
292e1b77b2db.sentence: Despite technical, infrastructure and management challenges, aquaculture technology of utilizing inland saline-alkali water and non-arable land for seafood production is becoming mature, covering a wide range of seafood species including shrimps, crabs, shellfish and fish such as sea bass and grouper.

241dc1d846f6.title: Alkali soil
241dc1d846f6.sentence: In recent years, aquaculture (or salt-alkali land aquaculture) has been recommended by the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs of China as an economically viable and environmentally beneficial model for the transformation and utilization of saline-alkali land.

7c31869dbe19.title: Residual sodium carbonate index
7c31869dbe19.sentence: The residual sodium carbonate (RSC) index of irrigation water or soil water is used to indicate the alkalinity hazard for soil.

ee8422f3cf75.title: Residual sodium carbonate index
ee8422f3cf75.sentence: The RSC index is used to find the suitability of the water for irrigation in clay soils which have a high cation exchange capacity.

66b602ff6812.title: Residual sodium carbonate index
66b602ff6812.sentence: When dissolved sodium in comparison with dissolved calcium and magnesium is high in water, clay soil swells or undergoes dispersion which drastically reduces its infiltration capacity.

cdf66f06d21c.title: Alkali soil
cdf66f06d21c.sentence: - The residual sodium carbonate (RSC, meq/L): The formula for calculating the residual sodium carbonate is: RSC = [HCO− 3 + CO2− 3] − [Ca2+ + Mg2+] = {HCO− 3/61 + CO2− 3/30} − {Ca2+/20 + Mg2+/12} which must not be much higher than 1 and preferably less than 0.5.

8dea303fbf62.title: Residual sodium carbonate index
8dea303fbf62.sentence: RSC should not be higher than 1 and preferably less than +0.5 for considering the water use for irrigation.

0fb34925bebb.title: Residual sodium carbonate index
0fb34925bebb.sentence: However, high RSC index water does not enhance the osmotic pressure to impede the off take of water by the plant roots unlike high salinity water.

812fb15ea328.title: Residual sodium carbonate index
812fb15ea328.sentence: Clay soils irrigation with high RSC index water leads to fallow alkali soils formation.

904141162468.title: Residual sodium carbonate index
904141162468.sentence: Soda ash [Na2CO3] can be present in natural water from the weathering of basalt which is an igneous rock.

f7141834712f.title: Residual sodium carbonate index
f7141834712f.sentence: Lime [Ca(OH)2] can be present in natural water when rain water comes in contact with calcined minerals such as ash produced from the burning of calcareous coal or lignite in boilers.

46641b8a97aa.title: Residual sodium carbonate index
46641b8a97aa.sentence: Anthropogenic use of soda ash also finally adds to the RSC of the river water.

5337a4924c04.title: Residual sodium carbonate index
5337a4924c04.sentence: Where the river water and ground water are repeatedly used in the extensively irrigated river basins, the river water available in lower reaches is often rendered not useful in agriculture due to high RSC index or alkalinity.

7e2019acbe4a.title: Gypsum
7e2019acbe4a.sentence: Gypsum provides two of the secondary plant macronutrients, calcium and sulfur.

c96a89023808.title: Gypsum
c96a89023808.sentence: Unlike limestone, it generally does not affect soil pH.

25325234057c.title: Gypsum
25325234057c.sentence: - Reclamation of saline soils, regardless of pH.

152459c69f63.title: Gypsum
152459c69f63.sentence: When gypsum is added to sodic (saline) and acidic soil, the highly soluble form of boron (sodium metaborate) is converted to the less soluble calcium metaborate.

68a08f272482.title: Gypsum
68a08f272482.sentence: - Other soil conditioner uses: Gypsum reduces aluminium and boron toxicity in acidic soils.

b283a984dbfc.title: Gypsum
b283a984dbfc.sentence: It also improves soil structure, water absorption, and aeration.

f56d70f0d6d5.title: Gypsum
f56d70f0d6d5.sentence: - Fertilizer: In the late 18th and early 19th centuries, Nova Scotia gypsum, often referred to as plaster, was a highly sought fertilizer for wheat fields in the United States.

4c8401c02ca2.title: Alkali soil
4c8401c02ca2.sentence: Alternatively, gypsum (calcium sulfate, CaSO 4 · 2 H 2O) can also be applied as a source of Ca2+ ions to replace the sodium at the exchange complex.

31213d38eea9.title: Alkali soil
31213d38eea9.sentence: It is also possible to reclaim alkaline soils by adding acidifying minerals like pyrite or cheaper alum or aluminium sulfate.

956af75c078d.title: Alkali soil
956af75c078d.sentence: There must be enough natural drainage to the underground, or else an artificial subsurface drainage system must be present, to permit leaching of the excess sodium by percolation of rain and/or irrigation water through the soil profile.

7bf213b1720e.title: Alkali soil
7bf213b1720e.sentence: Gypsum also reacts with sodium carbonate to convert into sodium sulphate which is a neutral salt and does not contribute to high pH.

d666c9f1cb46.title: Alkali soil
d666c9f1cb46.sentence: Calcium chloride is also used to reclaim alkali soils.

e8e814bd20d6.title: Alkali soil
e8e814bd20d6.sentence: Calcium nitrate (a nitrogen fertilizer) has a similar effect, with NaNO3 in the leachate.

4a95da8bc919.title: Alkali soil
4a95da8bc919.sentence: Spent acids (HCl, H2SO4, etc.) can also be used to reduce the excess Na2CO3 in the soil/water.

478032a0fea5.title: Alkali soil
478032a0fea5.sentence: Alkaline soils with solid CaCO3 can be reclaimed with grass cultures, compost, waste hair/feathers, organic garbage, waste paper, rejected lemons/oranges, etc. ensuring the incorporation of much acidifying material (inorganic or organic material) into the soil, and enhancing dissolved Ca in the field water by releasing CO2 gas.

b71b3df96bcd.title: Alkali soil
b71b3df96bcd.sentence: Most efforts are therefore directed to improving the top layer only (say the first 10 cm of the soils), as the top layer is most sensitive to deterioration of the soil structure.

ae24a791e87f.title: Alkali soil
ae24a791e87f.sentence: The treatments, however, need to be repeated in a few (say 5) years' time, because of loss of applied substances through leaching (for mineral amendments) or decomposition (for organic amendments) processes, except when stabilized by mixing them with highly stable susbtrates (e.g. biochar).

751e12bef86e.title: Alkali soil
751e12bef86e.sentence: One way of reducing sodium carbonate is to cultivate halophytes such as glasswort or saltwort or barilla plants, a process called phytoremediation.

fe45372bbc0d.title: Alkali soil
fe45372bbc0d.sentence: Halophytes sequester the sodium carbonate they absorb from alkali soil into their tissues.

6565b9112b36.title: Alkali soil
6565b9112b36.sentence: The ash of these plants contains good quantity of sodium carbonate (known as soda) which can be commercially extracted in place of sodium carbonate derived from common salt which is highly energy intensive process.

350d67f1886b.title: Alkali soil
350d67f1886b.section: Soil improvement > Leaching saline sodic soils
350d67f1886b.sentence: Saline soils are mostly also sodic (the predominant salt is sodium chloride), but they do not have a very high pH nor a poor infiltration rate, because they have a good structure.

06b260af21ca.title: Alkali soil
06b260af21ca.section: Soil improvement > Leaching saline sodic soils
06b260af21ca.sentence: Upon leaching they are usually not converted into a (sodic) alkali soil as the Na+ ions are easily removed.

5db66e18af98.title: Alkali soil
5db66e18af98.section: Soil improvement > Leaching saline sodic soils
5db66e18af98.sentence: Therefore, saline (sodic) soils mostly do not need gypsum applications for their reclamation.

be628ea08082.title: Critical load
be628ea08082.sentence: In the study of air pollution, a critical load is defined as "a quantitative estimate of an exposure to one or more pollutants below which significant harmful effects on specified sensitive elements of the environment do not occur according to present knowledge".

dab37e1d78f6.title: Critical load
dab37e1d78f6.sentence: Air pollution research in relation to critical loads has focused on nitrogen and sulfur pollutants.

621f35ce83ff.title: Critical load
621f35ce83ff.sentence: Both sulfur and nitrogen deposition can acidify surface waters and soils.

572d0cd87f6c.title: Critical load
572d0cd87f6c.sentence: Sulfur and nitrogen, as acidifying agents, may change soil nutrient content by removing calcium and releasing toxic aluminum, further impacting plants and animals.

bbc178d7ee1c.title: Critical load
bbc178d7ee1c.sentence: When deposition is greater than the critical load of a pollutant for a particular location, it is considered a critical load exceedance, meaning the biota are at increased risk of ecological harm.

3abea38f7c10.title: Critical load
3abea38f7c10.sentence: To calculate a critical load, the target ecosystem must first be defined and in that ecosystem (e.g. a forest) a sensitive "element" must be identified (e.g. forest growth rate).

ee7342d96e44.title: Critical load
ee7342d96e44.sentence: The next step is to link the status of that element to some chemical criterion (e.g. the base cation to aluminium ratio, Bc/Al) and a critical limit (e.g. Bc/Al=1) which should not be violated.

633f26bb147c.title: Critical load
633f26bb147c.sentence: Finally, a mathematical model (e.g. the Simple Mass Balance model, SMB) needs to be created so that the deposition levels that result in the chemical criterion reaching exactly the critical limit can be calculated.

c37364f88c2f.title: Critical load
c37364f88c2f.sentence: Today a two-dimensional critical load function is often calculated, with the x-axis as N-deposition and the y-axis as S-deposition.

794ee20c987e.title: Critical load
794ee20c987e.sentence: The critical loads concept is a steady-state concept and that it therefore includes no information whatsoever regarding how long it takes before effects are visible.

1cd115ca0618.title: Critical load
1cd115ca0618.sentence: A simplified illustration of dynamic aspects is the target load function, which is the load at which the chemical criterion recovers before a chosen year, the target year.

060180f77dfa.title: Critical load
060180f77dfa.sentence: Empirical critical loads are derived based on observations of ecosystem responses (such as changes in plant diversity, soil nutrient levels, or fish health) to specific deposition levels.

7712b842036a.title: Critical load
7712b842036a.sentence: Steady-state mass balance critical loads are derived from mathematical mass-balance models under assumed or modeled equilibrium conditions.

488a309dd66a.title: Critical load
488a309dd66a.sentence: The models used to determine steady-state critical loads vary in complexity with regard to process representation but can include water and soil chemistry, mineral soil weathering rates, deposition data, and ecological response data.

c69eb0c44330.title: Biosaline agriculture
c69eb0c44330.sentence: Biosaline agriculture is the production and growth of plants in saline rich groundwater and/or soil.

2b6fc171af11.title: Biosaline agriculture
2b6fc171af11.sentence: Biosaline agriculture is a practice using saline water and salt-tolerant plants, known as halophytes, to remediate unproductive arable land or transform naturally saline environments into productive farmland.

adffd5c67ced.title: Biosaline agriculture
adffd5c67ced.sentence: Halophytes are the cornerstone of biosaline agriculture and serve a critical role in its many applications which include, but are not limited to, crop/forage production, desalination/restoration of high salinity environments, and uses medicinally and as biofuel.

12681e8b372a.title: Biosaline agriculture
12681e8b372a.sentence: By using high-salinity water for efficient irrigation, it helps to alleviate pressures on limited fresh water resources while also supporting forage production sites.

16421a474669.title: Biosaline agriculture
16421a474669.sentence: In many parts of the world, particularlyarid and semi-arid regions, coastal and inland areas typically have brackish and saline water sources.

39d0cb6bfda2.title: Biosaline agriculture
39d0cb6bfda2.sentence: Soil salinization is a global issue with an estimated one billion hectares of salt-affected soil worldwide, in both coastal and continental areas, and another one million hectares being added to this each year.

0f3d7110a2b2.title: Biosaline agriculture
0f3d7110a2b2.sentence: Salinity currently affects one quarter of global arable land, and is projected to double by 2050.

a405b06881be.title: Biosaline agriculture
a405b06881be.section: Applications of biosaline agriculture > Desalination and restoration
a405b06881be.sentence: Through consecutive growing cycles of halophytes, areas with degraded soil and water can be restored, making them more suitable for agricultural use.

978de1118c51.title: Biosaline agriculture
978de1118c51.section: Applications of biosaline agriculture > Desalination and restoration
978de1118c51.sentence: Halophytic plants are able to desalinate brackish water, accumulate heavy metals from soils and groundwater through bioaccumulation, while growing without freshwater reliance.

6ac12617a01f.title: Biosaline agriculture
6ac12617a01f.sentence: Salinity problems date back to Mesopotamian societies and biosaline solutions have been integrated in agriculture throughout history.

06beb2d954fb.title: Biosaline agriculture
06beb2d954fb.sentence: Widespread soil salinization led to the decline of Mesopotamian civilizations due to poor irrigation practices, mirroring agricultural water issues currently facing farmers.

e8cec113db9a.title: Biosaline agriculture
e8cec113db9a.sentence: The first of these salinity events can be traced back from 2400 BC to 1700 BC.

79c1a1d81d55.title: Biosaline agriculture
79c1a1d81d55.sentence: The formalized practice of biosaline agriculture was not officially established until the late 1990s.

39d92be46189.title: Biosaline agriculture
39d92be46189.sentence: The scientific field of biosaline agriculture gained recognition in the mid-to-late 1990s with the establishment of the International Center for Biosaline Agriculture (IBCA) in 1996; the center became fully operational in 1999.

4753b1cdb86c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/20%3A_Other_Fertility_Issues/20.03%3A_Cation_Exchange_Capacity_(CEC)_Management
4753b1cdb86c.sentence: The CEC in soils is due to well-humified (“very dead”) organic matter and clay minerals.

6e588d9687d1.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/20%3A_Other_Fertility_Issues/20.03%3A_Cation_Exchange_Capacity_(CEC)_Management
6e588d9687d1.sentence: The total CEC in a soil is the sum of the CEC due to organic matter and due to clays.

527f38131555.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/20%3A_Other_Fertility_Issues/20.03%3A_Cation_Exchange_Capacity_(CEC)_Management
527f38131555.sentence: In fine-textured soils with medium- to high-CEC clays, much of the CEC may be due to clays.

459bb38821e4.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/20%3A_Other_Fertility_Issues/20.03%3A_Cation_Exchange_Capacity_(CEC)_Management
459bb38821e4.sentence: Conversely, in sandy loams with little clay, or in some of the soils of the southeastern United States and of the tropics that contain clays with low CEC, organic matter may account for an overwhelming fraction of the total CEC.

d8ab59b0993e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/20%3A_Other_Fertility_Issues/20.03%3A_Cation_Exchange_Capacity_(CEC)_Management
d8ab59b0993e.section: Estimating Organic Matter's Contribution To A Soil's CEC
d8ab59b0993e.sentence: The CEC of a soil is usually expressed in terms of the number of milliequivalents (me) of negative charge per 100 grams of soil.

6348a1074329.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/20%3A_Other_Fertility_Issues/20.03%3A_Cation_Exchange_Capacity_(CEC)_Management
6348a1074329.section: Estimating Organic Matter's Contribution To A Soil's CEC
6348a1074329.sentence: (The actual number of charges represented by one me is about 6 followed by 20 zeros.) A useful rule of thumb for estimating the CEC due to organic matter is as follows: for every pH unit above pH 4.5, there is 1 me of CEC in 100 grams of soil for every percent of organic matter.

ced2de1e6ab0.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/20%3A_Other_Fertility_Issues/20.03%3A_Cation_Exchange_Capacity_(CEC)_Management
ced2de1e6ab0.section: Estimating Organic Matter's Contribution To A Soil's CEC
ced2de1e6ab0.sentence: Example 2: pH = 6 and 3% SOM → (6 – 4.5) x 3 = 4.5 me/100g

4f3b5b18d72b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/20%3A_Other_Fertility_Issues/20.05%3A_Remediation_of_Sodic_(Alkali)_and_Saline_Soils
4f3b5b18d72b.sentence: There are a number of ways to deal with saline soils that don’t have shallow salty groundwater.

c7981fdab25c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/20%3A_Other_Fertility_Issues/20.05%3A_Remediation_of_Sodic_(Alkali)_and_Saline_Soils
c7981fdab25c.sentence: One is to keep the soil continually moist.

1799072e58e5.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/20%3A_Other_Fertility_Issues/20.05%3A_Remediation_of_Sodic_(Alkali)_and_Saline_Soils
1799072e58e5.sentence: For example, if you use drip irrigation with low-salt water plus a surface mulch, the salt content will not get as high as it would if allowed to concentrate when the soil dries.

a364b4afde87.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/20%3A_Other_Fertility_Issues/20.05%3A_Remediation_of_Sodic_(Alkali)_and_Saline_Soils
a364b4afde87.sentence: Saline-tolerant plants include barley, bermuda grass, oak, rosemary and willow.

ab34bd43b69d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/20%3A_Other_Fertility_Issues/20.05%3A_Remediation_of_Sodic_(Alkali)_and_Saline_Soils
ab34bd43b69d.sentence: However, the only way to get rid of the salt is to add sufficient water to wash it below the root zone.

184c1fb60b1f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/20%3A_Other_Fertility_Issues/20.05%3A_Remediation_of_Sodic_(Alkali)_and_Saline_Soils
184c1fb60b1f.sentence: If the subsoil does not drain well, drainage tiles might need to be installed to lower the water table and remove the salty water leached from the soil.

dcbaf29058aa.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/20%3A_Other_Fertility_Issues/20.05%3A_Remediation_of_Sodic_(Alkali)_and_Saline_Soils
dcbaf29058aa.sentence: (However, this means that a high-salt water is being discharged into a ditch and may harm downstream water quality.

8824a49a734a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/20%3A_Other_Fertility_Issues/20.05%3A_Remediation_of_Sodic_(Alkali)_and_Saline_Soils
8824a49a734a.sentence: Sodic soils can also occur after major coastal flooding events, as the seawater washes a lot of sodium chloride through the flooded soil.

b7067c75430f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/20%3A_Other_Fertility_Issues/20.05%3A_Remediation_of_Sodic_(Alkali)_and_Saline_Soils
b7067c75430f.sentence: The same remediation method, adding gypsum (or lime when the soil is naturally acidic), helps restore the soils in those cases.

85c998142248.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/20%3A_Other_Fertility_Issues/20.02%3A_Other_Nutrients
85c998142248.sentence: Copper is another nutrient that is sometimes deficient in high-pH soils.

d4ef602d4bd1.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/20%3A_Other_Fertility_Issues/20.02%3A_Other_Nutrients
d4ef602d4bd1.sentence: It can also be deficient in organic soils (soils with 10–20% or more organic matter).

da3ba8a15b9a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/20%3A_Other_Fertility_Issues/20.02%3A_Other_Nutrients
da3ba8a15b9a.sentence: Some crops—for example, tomatoes, lettuce, beets, onions and spinach—have a relatively high copper need.

9bf09a7453fc.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/20%3A_Other_Fertility_Issues/20.02%3A_Other_Nutrients
9bf09a7453fc.sentence: A number of copper sources, such as copper sulfate and copper chelates, can be used to correct a copper deficiency.

db87faccc64b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/20%3A_Other_Fertility_Issues/20.02%3A_Other_Nutrients
db87faccc64b.sentence: (Those of you who grow garlic should know that a good supply of sulfur is important for the full development of garlic’s pungent flavor.) Much of the sulfur in soils occurs as organic matter, so building up and maintaining organic matter should result in sufficient sulfur nutrition for plants.

9717adece39d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/20%3A_Other_Fertility_Issues/20.02%3A_Other_Nutrients
9717adece39d.sentence: A deficiency is more likely to occur on acidic, sandy soils; soils with low organic matter levels and high nitrogen inputs; and soils that are cold and dry in the spring, which decreases sulfur mineralization from soil organic matter.

80febe659ea3.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/20%3A_Other_Fertility_Issues/20.02%3A_Other_Nutrients
80febe659ea3.sentence: Sulfur deficiency is becoming more common in certain regions now that there is less sulfur air pollution, which previously originated from combustion of high-sulfur forms of coal.

b0945c9dee56.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/20%3A_Other_Fertility_Issues/20.02%3A_Other_Nutrients
b0945c9dee56.sentence: (Now it is captured in power plant exhaust scrubbers, and the residue is sold as gypsum.) In the Great Plains, on the other hand, irrigation water may contain sufficient quantities of sulfur to supply crop needs even though the soils are deficient in sulfur.

c1b87674299a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/20%3A_Other_Fertility_Issues/20.04%3A_Soil_Acidity
c1b87674299a.sentence: The explanation for this is that almost all of the acid that must be neutralized in soils is “reserve acidity” associated with either organic matter or aluminum.

4f51968cb00b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/20%3A_Other_Fertility_Issues/20.04%3A_Soil_Acidity
4f51968cb00b.sentence: Almost all the acid in acidic soils is held in reserve on the solids, with an extremely small amount active in the soil water.

96c8fcf48bea.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/20%3A_Other_Fertility_Issues/20.04%3A_Soil_Acidity
96c8fcf48bea.sentence: If all that we needed to neutralize was the acid in the soil water, a few handfuls of lime per acre would be enough to do the job, even in a very acid soil.

1b420eb064ad.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/20%3A_Other_Fertility_Issues/20.04%3A_Soil_Acidity
1b420eb064ad.sentence: However, tons of lime per acre are needed to raise the pH.

e15302e2ea70.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/20%3A_Other_Fertility_Issues/20.04%3A_Soil_Acidity
e15302e2ea70.sentence: And as the acid (H+) is removed from organic matter, new CEC sites are created, increasing the soil’s ability to hold cations such as calcium and potassium.

fee1865e6ef9.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/20%3A_Other_Fertility_Issues/20.04%3A_Soil_Acidity
fee1865e6ef9.sentence: (It also works in reverse as soils are acidified: H+ strongly attaches to what had been CEC sites, removing their ability to hold onto calcium, magnesium, potassium and ammonium.)

3ed98bf90438.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/20%3A_Other_Fertility_Issues/20.04%3A_Soil_Acidity
3ed98bf90438.sentence: For example, alfalfa originated in a semiarid region where soil pH was high; alfalfa requires a pH in the range of 6.5–6.8 or higher (see Figure 20.1 for common soil pH levels).

d91cec58ee96.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/20%3A_Other_Fertility_Issues/20.04%3A_Soil_Acidity
d91cec58ee96.section: pH Management > Soil Sampling For pH
d91cec58ee96.sentence: Most states recommend a soil pH of around 6.8 only for the most sensitive crops, such as alfalfa, and of about 6.2–6.5 for many of the clovers.

7d0dcc1c3e9d.title: Alisol
7d0dcc1c3e9d.sentence: Aluminium and manganese toxicity is a very serious problem in Alisols, because at the low pH of these soils such generally insoluble metals become soluble and can poison plants which are not tolerant of them.

2b2977fb9854.title: Kurosol
2b2977fb9854.sentence: Aluminium and manganese toxicity may occur in strongly acidic horizons, particularly under waterlogged conditions, while molybdenum deficiency may also affect plant growth.

2c8f5cbcb251.title: Crushed stone
2c8f5cbcb251.sentence: Using aglime or agricultural lime, a finely-ground limestone or dolomite, to change the soil from acidic to nearly neutral particularly benefits crops by maximizing availability of plant nutrients, and also by reducing aluminum or manganese toxicity, promoting soil microbe activity, and improving the soil structure.

86dcd783e6c8.title: Efflorescence
86dcd783e6c8.sentence: In chemistry, efflorescence (from the Latin efflorescere, 'to flower') is the migration of a salt to the surface of a porous material, where it forms a coating.

7e7de1c38eb6.title: Efflorescence
7e7de1c38eb6.sentence: The essential process involves the dissolving of an internally held salt in water or occasionally, in another solvent.

2e5e57aa6d53.title: Efflorescence
2e5e57aa6d53.sentence: The water, with the salt now held in solution, migrates to the surface, then evaporates, leaving a coating of the salt.

27504e9955ce.title: Efflorescence
27504e9955ce.sentence: Efflorescence can occur in natural and built environments.

52e6700017ba.title: Efflorescence
52e6700017ba.sentence: In primary efflorescence, the water is the invader and the salt was already present internally; secondary efflorescence is the reverse process, where the salt is originally present externally and is then carried inside in solution.

539ae5c9fac4.title: Efflorescence
539ae5c9fac4.sentence: Efflorescence may clog the pores of porous materials, resulting in the destruction of those materials by internal water pressure, as seen in the spalling of brick.

b7fa9ecd8870.title: Soil biology
b7fa9ecd8870.sentence: Soil biology is the study of microbial and faunal activity and ecology in soil.

13754ac2026f.title: Soil biology
13754ac2026f.sentence: Soil life, soil biota, soil fauna, or edaphon is a collective term that encompasses all organisms that spend a significant portion of their life cycle within a soil profile, or at the soil-litter interface.

c4e7a98b8c04.title: Soil biology
c4e7a98b8c04.sentence: These organisms include earthworms, nematodes, protozoa, fungi, bacteria, different arthropods, as well as some reptiles (such as snakes), and species of burrowing mammals like gophers, moles and prairie dogs.

c68c2e940e24.title: Soil biology
c68c2e940e24.sentence: The soil is home to circa 59% of the world's biodiversity.

6bdbf1facaf6.title: Soil biology
6bdbf1facaf6.sentence: Soil organisms break down organic matter, making nutrients available for uptake by plants and other organisms.

ae167e3dd266.title: Soil biology
ae167e3dd266.sentence: The decomposition of organic matter by soil organisms has an immense influence on soil fertility, plant growth, soil structure, and carbon storage.

432803284962.title: Soil biology
432803284962.sentence: The nutrient content of the soil and its structure are important for plant well-being, but it is soil life that powers nutrient cycles and provides soil fertility.

0d908e4c59b7.title: Soil biology
0d908e4c59b7.sentence: Without the activities of soil organisms, organic materials would accumulate as undecayed litter at the soil surface, and there would be no humus and no nutrients available for plants.

88862c37e1a6.title: Soil biology
88862c37e1a6.sentence: The nutrients stored in the bodies of soil organisms prevent nutrient loss by leaching, in particular for nitrogen and phosphorus.

e7d0042d1fba.title: Soil biology
e7d0042d1fba.sentence: Microbial exudates act to maintain soil structure, and earthworms are important in bioturbation.

7a989cbdb064.title: Soil biology
7a989cbdb064.sentence: As a relatively new science, much remains unknown about soil biology and its effect on soil ecosystems.

235202b06090.title: Soil biology
235202b06090.sentence: The discovery of glomalin in 1996 indicates that the knowledge to correctly answer some of the most basic questions about the biogeochemical cycle in soils is lacking.

5415d49895ef.title: Soil microbiology
5415d49895ef.sentence: Soil microbiology is the study of microorganisms in soil, their functions, and how they affect soil properties.

5200fae1fa10.title: Soil microbiology
5200fae1fa10.sentence: Soil microorganisms can be classified as bacteria (including cyanobacteria and actinomycetes), archaea, fungi, algae, slime molds and protozoa.

d09724916eab.title: Soil microbiology
d09724916eab.sentence: It is believed that between two and four billion years ago, the first ancient cyanobacteria (also called blue-green algae) came about on Earth's oceans.

19e0868a2b4f.title: Soil microbiology
19e0868a2b4f.sentence: These bacteria could fix carbon by photosynthesis, fix nitrogen, in time multiplied, and as a result released oxygen into the atmosphere and nitrogen into the soil.

7455022e7408.title: Soil microbiology
7455022e7408.sentence: The diversity of microorganisms in soils is dependent on pH, soil texture, organic matter content, plant community composition, and contaminants such as heavy metals

80abf5627e73.title: Soil microbiology
80abf5627e73.sentence: In 2011, a team detected more than 33,000 bacterial and archaeal species on sugar beet roots.

220b55b90a02.title: Soil microbiology
220b55b90a02.sentence: Microbes can make nutrients in the soil more available to plants, produce hormones that spur growth, stimulate the plant immune system and trigger or dampen stress responses of plants.

fa8147483518.title: Soil microbiology
fa8147483518.sentence: In general a more diverse soil microbiome results in fewer plant diseases and higher crop yield.

73c5e0d01442.title: Soil ecology
73c5e0d01442.sentence: Interactions between members of the soil microhabitat take place via chemical signaling, which is mediated by soluble metabolites and volatile organic compounds in addition to extracellular polysaccharides.

2b494855b825.title: Soil ecology
2b494855b825.sentence: Microbes may also exchange metabolites to support each other's growth, e.g. the release of extracellular enzymes by ectomycorrhiza decomposes organic matter, and release nutrients which then benefit other members of the population.

802ade647367.title: Cover crop
802ade647367.sentence: In general, cover crops increase soil microbial activity, which has a positive effect on nitrogen availability in the soil, nitrogen uptake in target crops, and crop yields.

6c45587ae9f5.title: Biomineralization
6c45587ae9f5.sentence: Biomineralization, also written biomineralisation, is the process by which living organisms produce or retain inorganic minerals, often resulting in hardened or stiffened mineralized tissues.

bf73ccb61818.title: Biomineralization
bf73ccb61818.sentence: It is an extremely widespread phenomenon: all major lineages of the Earth's biosphere contain members that can form minerals, and over 60 different minerals have been identified in organisms.

6f2189ced292.title: Biomineralization
6f2189ced292.sentence: Most biominerals can be grouped by chemical composition into one of three distinct mineral classes: silicates, carbonates, or phosphates.

0fc65f05126e.title: Biomineralization
0fc65f05126e.sentence: Examples include silicates in algae, diatoms and sponges, carbonates in invertebrates, and calcium phosphates and carbonates in vertebrates.

2139ea84cdd5.title: Biomineralization
2139ea84cdd5.sentence: In terms of taxonomic distribution, the most common biominerals are the phosphate and carbonate salts of calcium that are used in conjunction with organic polymers such as collagen and chitin to give structural support to bones and shells.

60c481d5b6a8.title: Biomineralization
60c481d5b6a8.sentence: Other examples include copper, iron, and gold deposits involving bacteria.

c811c4ec2211.title: Biomineralization
c811c4ec2211.sentence: Microorganisms can precipitate metals from solution, contributing to the formation of ore deposits.

87a9f53b378f.title: Biomineralization
87a9f53b378f.sentence: They can also catalyze the dissolution of minerals.

b26628607e06.title: Biomineralization
b26628607e06.sentence: Biomineralization plays significant global roles terraforming the planet, as well as in biogeochemical cycles and as a carbon sink.

e277da33ce4e.title: Enhanced weathering
e277da33ce4e.section: Natural mineral weathering and ocean acidification
e277da33ce4e.sentence: Although some of the dissolved bicarbonate may react with soil acids during the passage through the soil profile to groundwater, water with dissolved bicarbonate ions (HCO3−) eventually ends up in the ocean, where the bicarbonate ions are biomineralized to carbonate minerals for shells and skeletons through the reaction:

44e86ea0f418.title: Biomineralization
44e86ea0f418.sentence: Biomineralization may be used to remediate groundwater contaminated with uranium.

7707fc353077.title: Biomineralization
7707fc353077.sentence: The biomineralization of uranium primarily involves the precipitation of uranium phosphate minerals associated with the release of phosphate by microorganisms.

b3d046da67fb.title: Biomineralization
b3d046da67fb.sentence: If the concentrations of phosphate and UO22+ are sufficiently high, minerals such as autunite (Ca(UO2)2(PO4)2•10-12H2O) or polycrystalline HUO2PO4 may form thus reducing the mobility of UO22+.

b4e6cd6e8400.title: Biomineralization
b4e6cd6e8400.sentence: The first evidence of biomineralization dates to some 750 million years ago, and sponge-grade organisms may have formed calcite skeletons 630 million years ago.

d4e5777d9f92.title: Biomineralization
d4e5777d9f92.sentence: Organisms have been producing mineralized skeletons for the past 550 million years.

4651bd98ac24.title: Soil ecology
4651bd98ac24.sentence: Soil ecology studies interactions among soil organisms and their environment.

784e24874349.title: Soil ecology
784e24874349.sentence: It is a branch of ecology particularly concerned with the cycling of nutrients, soil aggregate formation, and soil biodiversity.

273a7130ba81.title: Soil ecology
273a7130ba81.sentence: Soil is a heterogenous mixture of minerals and organic matter with variations in structure, nutrients, moisture, temperature, and pH that support different organisms depending on such combinations.

8f38895479c0.title: Soil ecology
8f38895479c0.sentence: Moisture is a significant limiting factor in terrestrial ecosystems and especially in the soil.

90eb64a97600.title: Soil ecology
90eb64a97600.sentence: Soil organisms are constantly confronted with the problem of dehydration.

81a7896c5065.title: Soil ecology
81a7896c5065.sentence: Soil microbial communities experience shifts in the diversity and composition during dehydration and rehydration cycles.

c340522184ac.title: Soil ecology
c340522184ac.sentence: Soil temperature influences biological and biochemical processes in soil, playing an important role in microbial and enzymatic activities, mineralization, and organic matter decomposition.

74da130690c7.title: Soil ecology
74da130690c7.sentence: The majority of these organisms are aerobic, so the amount of porous space, pore-size distribution, surface area, and oxygen levels are crucial to their life cycles and activities.

c2cc637cb0b2.title: Soil ecology
c2cc637cb0b2.sentence: The smallest creatures (microbes) use the micropores filled with air to grow, whereas other bigger animals require larger macropores or the water film surrounding the soil particles to move in search for food.

163eec6fd408.title: Soil ecology
163eec6fd408.sentence: Consequently, the horizontal patchy distribution of soil properties (soil temperature, moisture, pH, litter/nutrient availability, etc.) also drives the patchiness of the soil organisms across the landscape and has been one of the main arguments for explaining the great diversity observed in soil communities.

26ba706cc3c6.title: Soil ecology
26ba706cc3c6.sentence: Because soils also show vertical stratification of their elemental constituents along the soil profile as result of microclimate, soil texture, and resource quantity and quality differing between soil horizons, soil communities also change in abundance and structure with soil depth.

13f8f93a2a6e.title: Soil ecology
13f8f93a2a6e.sentence: Yet, soil organisms remain underrepresented in studies on soil processes and existing modeling exercises.

959838dab906.title: Soil ecology
959838dab906.sentence: This is a consequence of assuming that much below ground diversity is ecologically redundant and that soil food webs exhibit a higher degree of omnivory.

3d9417ac555f.title: Soil biodiversity
3d9417ac555f.sentence: Soil biodiversity refers to the relationship of soil to biodiversity and to aspects of the soil that can be managed in relative to biodiversity.

f83d5cbbf994.title: Soil biodiversity
f83d5cbbf994.sentence: Soil provides a vital habitat, primarily for microbes (including bacteria and fungi), but also for microfauna (such as protozoa and nematodes), mesofauna (such as microarthropods and enchytraeids), and macrofauna (such as earthworms, termites, and millipedes).

4a1a7951b3e1.title: Soil biodiversity
4a1a7951b3e1.sentence: The primary role of soil biota is to recycle organic matter that is derived from the "above-ground plant-based food web".

5d2dc1be5b09.title: Soil biodiversity
5d2dc1be5b09.sentence: Conversely, biological activity is a primary factor in soil's physical and chemical formation.

d2588ee3e841.title: Soil biodiversity
d2588ee3e841.sentence: For example, both natural and agricultural vegetation boundaries correspond closely to soil boundaries, even at continental and global scales.

887443827aed.title: Soil biodiversity
887443827aed.sentence: It is now uncontested that microbial exudates dominate the aggregation of soil particles and the protection of carbon from further degradation.

fde4ae2f0b83.title: Soil biodiversity
fde4ae2f0b83.sentence: It is estimated that a football pitch contains underground as many organisms as equal to the size of 500 sheep.

e3f8aff7a99f.title: Soil biodiversity
e3f8aff7a99f.sentence: It is not surprising that soil management directly affects biodiversity.

9e4c4d1673c1.title: Soil biodiversity
9e4c4d1673c1.sentence: Crop rotation, crop diversification, legume intercrops, and organic inputs are found to correlate with higher soil diversity by McDaniel et al. 2014 and Lori et al. 2017.

901c4873989b.title: Total organic carbon
901c4873989b.sentence: Total organic carbon (TOC) is an analytical parameter representing the concentration of organic carbon in a sample.

45f87ca38934.title: Total organic carbon
45f87ca38934.sentence: A typical analysis for total carbon (TC) measures both the total organic carbon (TOC) present and the complementing total inorganic carbon (TIC), the latter representing the amount of non-organic carbon, like carbon in carbonate minerals.

70176d433d73.title: Total organic carbon
70176d433d73.sentence: Subtracting the inorganic carbon from the total carbon yields TOC.

30b0432a8551.title: Total organic carbon
30b0432a8551.sentence: Since all TOC analyzers only actually measure total carbon, TOC analysis always requires some accounting for the inorganic carbon that is always present.

d9c7b2e867c8.title: Total organic carbon
d9c7b2e867c8.sentence: Another common variant of TOC analysis involves removing the TIC portion first and then measuring the leftover carbon.

ad489647a5d1.title: Total organic carbon
ad489647a5d1.sentence: This method involves purging an acidified sample with carbon-free air or nitrogen prior to measurement, and so is more accurately called non-purgeable organic carbon (NPOC).

08db344f31ec.title: Total organic carbon
08db344f31ec.sentence: Prepared samples are combusted from 1000 up to 1200 degrees C in an oxygen-rich atmosphere.

d1455de1c190.title: Total organic carbon
d1455de1c190.section: Measurement > Oxidation > High temperature catalytic oxidation
d1455de1c190.sentence: A manual or automated process injects the sample onto a catalyst in a combustion tube operated from 680 up to 950 degrees C in an oxygen rich atmosphere.

b3a1cd341815.title: Total organic carbon
b3a1cd341815.sentence: Most modern analyzers use non-dispersive infrared (NDIR) for detection of the carbon dioxide.

7c7275bac632.title: Soil contamination
7c7275bac632.sentence: The SGVs for ethyl benzene, phenol and toluene are dependent on the soil organic matter (SOM) content (which can be calculated from the total organic carbon (TOC) content).

c66cc26a2acc.title: Total organic carbon
c66cc26a2acc.sentence: For example, TOC may be used as a non-specific indicator of water quality, or TOC of source rock may be used as one factor in evaluating a petroleum play.

d772fa9b16e8.title: Total organic carbon
d772fa9b16e8.sentence: TOC is the first chemical analysis to be carried out on potential petroleum source rock in oil exploration.

65cbbdda3f3d.title: Oligotroph
65cbbdda3f3d.sentence: An oligotroph is an organism that can live in an environment that offers very low levels of nutrients.

3a9a358e4cf2.title: Oligotroph
3a9a358e4cf2.sentence: Etymologically, the word "oligotroph" is a combination of the Greek adjective oligos (ὀλίγος) meaning "few" and the adjective trophikos (τροφικός) meaning "feeding".

94e97f1186b0.title: Oligotroph
94e97f1186b0.sentence: They may be contrasted with copiotrophs, which prefer nutritionally rich environments.

89b7bb3858cf.title: Oligotroph
89b7bb3858cf.sentence: Oligotrophs are characterized by slow growth, low rates of metabolism, and generally low population density.

ade822b26db2.title: Oligotroph
ade822b26db2.sentence: The term "oligotrophic" is commonly used to describe terrestrial and aquatic environments with very low concentrations of nitrates, iron, phosphates, and carbon sources.

b0175457c617.title: Oligotroph
b0175457c617.sentence: These environments include deep oceanic sediments, caves, glacial and polar ice, deep subsurface soil, aquifers, ocean waters, and leached soils.

a5c9a851160e.title: Oligotroph
a5c9a851160e.sentence: Oligotrophs have acquired survival mechanisms that involve the expression of genes during periods of low nutrient conditions, which has allowed them to find success in various environments.

1f2e6192a2fb.title: Oligotroph
1f2e6192a2fb.sentence: The presence of excess nutrients overwhelm oligotrophs' metabolic systems, which cause them to struggle to regulate nutrient uptake.

a9dc2c71f42d.title: Oligotroph
a9dc2c71f42d.sentence: For example, oligotrophs' enzymes function well in low nutrient environments, but struggle in high nutrient environments.

7c8593dfdd63.title: Oligotroph
7c8593dfdd63.sentence: Examples of oligotrophic organisms are the cave-dwelling olm; the bacterium "Candidatus Pelagibacter communis", which is the most abundant organism in the ocean (with an estimated 2 × 10^28 individuals in total); and lichens, with their extremely low metabolic rate.

52c1a9a5d6a3.title: Effects of climate change on agriculture
52c1a9a5d6a3.section: Changes in the extent and quality of agricultural land > Erosion and soil fertility
52c1a9a5d6a3.sentence: Elevated carbon dioxide would increase the growth rates of plants and soil microbes, slowing the soil carbon cycle and favouring oligotrophs, which are slower-growing and more resource efficient than copiotrophs.
52c1a9a5d6a3.key: Effects of climate change on agriculture

5346b9bd3e88.title: Soil animals
5346b9bd3e88.sentence: Soil harbours a huge number of animal species (30% of arthropods live in soil), whether over their entire life or at least during larval stages.

f5b159041985.title: Soil animals
f5b159041985.sentence: Soil offers protection against environmental hazards, such as excess temperature and moisture fluctuations, in particular in arid and cold environments, as well as against predation.

64f35fd6136e.title: Soil animals
64f35fd6136e.sentence: Soil provisions food over the year, especially since omnivory seems the rule rather than the exception, and allows reproduction and egg deposition in a safe environment, even for those animals not currently living belowground.

0757570da56d.title: Soil animals
0757570da56d.sentence: Soil fauna have been classified, according to increasing body size, in soil microfauna (20 μm to 200 μm), mesofauna (200 μm to 2 mm), macrofauna (2 mm to 2 cm) and megafauna (more than 2 cm).

bd88337df460.title: Soil animals
bd88337df460.sentence: The size of soil animals determines their place along soil trophic networks (soil foodwebs), bigger species eating smaller species (predator-prey interactions) or modifying their environment (nested ecological niches).

9b946eb92eba.title: Soil animals
9b946eb92eba.sentence: Many soil invertebrates, and also some soil vertebrates, are tightly adapted to a subterranean concealed environment, being smaller, blind, depigmented, legfree or with reduced legs, and reproducing asexually, with negative consequences on their colonization rate when the environment is changing at landscape scale.

1dedf0f69d4e.title: Soil animals
1dedf0f69d4e.sentence: From a functional point of view soil animals are tightly interconnected with soil microorganisms (bacteria, archaea, fungi, algae).

cc77c25cb14f.title: Soil animals
cc77c25cb14f.sentence: Soil microorganisms provide food to saprophagous and microbivorous species, and play a significant role in the digestion of recalcitrant compounds by saprophagous animals.

e62a8712dd87.title: Soil animals
e62a8712dd87.sentence: In turn, soil animals, even the tiniest ones, create environments, e.g. digestive tracts, feces, cavities, favourable to soil microorganisms, allow their dispersal for those unable to move by their own means (e.g. non-motile bacteria), and regulate their populations.

29a7fd1084eb.title: Soil animals
29a7fd1084eb.sentence: It has been argued that soil could have been a crucible for the evolution of invertebrate terrestrial faunas, as an intermediary step in the transition from aquatic to aerial life.

5596d12e5da5.title: Soil animals
5596d12e5da5.sentence: The identification of soil animals, needing to be extracted (e.g. microarthropods, potworms, nematodes), expelled (earthworms), trapped (e.g. carabids) or searched by hand (e.g. termites, ants, millipedes, woodlice) before being observed under a dissecting, light microscope or electron microscope, has slowed down the development of soil zoology compared to the aboveground.

4d206d9e8a8a.title: Soil animals
4d206d9e8a8a.sentence: From a few decades on molecular tools such as DNA barcoding helped field ecologists to achieve complete lists of species or OTUs.

438f98c2db18.title: Soil animals
438f98c2db18.sentence: They will be most useful for giving us reliable estimates of soil biodiversity, taking into account the huge amount of cryptic species which cannot be identified by morphological criteria.

4bc12ed2d08d.title: Fertilizer
4bc12ed2d08d.section: Environmental effects > Soil > Changes in soil biology
4bc12ed2d08d.sentence: It is still debated whether and how fertilizers affect soil animals.

b1bd050b41fb.title: Fertilizer
b1bd050b41fb.section: Environmental effects > Soil > Changes in soil biology
b1bd050b41fb.sentence: Both organic and organic–mineral fertilizers increase the abundance of soil fauna whereas mineral fertilizers had no such effect, with idiosyncratic responses of soil animal groups masking overall effects.

d7ab2a863653.title: Earthworm
d7ab2a863653.sentence: An earthworm is a soil-dwelling terrestrial invertebrate that belongs to the phylum Annelida.
