d07e5a22b37c.title: Earthworm
d07e5a22b37c.sentence: The term is the common name for the largest members of the class (or subclass, depending on the author) Oligochaeta.

8f72ebe30557.title: Earthworm
8f72ebe30557.sentence: Earthworms are commonly found in moist, compost-rich soil, eating a wide variety of organic matters, which include detritus, living protozoa, nematodes, bacteria, fungi and algae (including diatoms and cyanobacteria).

4e03d62c1280.title: Earthworm
4e03d62c1280.sentence: They are one of nature's most important detritivores and coprophages, and also serve directly as food for many low-level consumers (predation) within the ecosystems (e.g. wild boars, moles, blackbirds, centipedes), ground beetles, flatworms.

ab939910aecd.title: Earthworm
ab939910aecd.sentence: Depending on the species, an adult earthworm can be from 10 mm (0.39 in) long and 1 mm (0.039 in) wide to 3 m (9.8 ft) long and over 25 mm (0.98 in) wide, but the typical Lumbricus terrestris grows to about 360 mm (14 in) long.

572415eba7ed.title: Earthworm
572415eba7ed.sentence: Earthworms travel underground by means of waves of muscular contractions which alternately shorten and lengthen the body (peristalsis).

538324462b76.title: Earthworm
538324462b76.sentence: The shortened part is anchored to the surrounding soil by tiny clawlike bristles (setae) set along its segmented length.

e322972a43a4.title: Earthworm
e322972a43a4.sentence: Earthworms have no special respiratory organs.

f7add3468f00.title: Earthworm
f7add3468f00.sentence: Gases are exchanged through the moist skin and capillaries, where the oxygen is picked up by the haemoglobin dissolved in the blood plasma and carbon dioxide is released.

6c98abb699da.title: Earthworm
6c98abb699da.sentence: Earthworm populations depend on both physical and chemical properties of the soil, such as temperature, moisture, pH, salts, aeration, and texture, as well as available food, competition, predation, and the ability of the species to reproduce and disperse.

ee890f05399a.title: Earthworm
ee890f05399a.sentence: Most favour neutral to slightly acidic soils.

d95c515792a7.title: Earthworm
d95c515792a7.sentence: One of the most important environmental factors is pH, but earthworms vary in their pH preferences, and through their engineering activities (summarized in the formation of earthworm mull humus) they are able to change pH in order to adapt it to their niche requirements (see niche construction and extended phenotype).

24ba4f5ed203.title: Earthworm
24ba4f5ed203.sentence: The earthworm activity aerates and mixes the soil (bioturbation), and is conducive to mineralization of nutrients and their uptake by vegetation together with incorporating organic matter and linking it to soil minerals.

fa5bea0e49a8.title: Earthworm
fa5bea0e49a8.sentence: Earthworms are environmental indicators of soil health.

2c422b8053de.title: Earthworm
2c422b8053de.sentence: The population size of earthworms indicates soil quality, as healthy soil would contain a larger number and biomass of earthworms, in particular endogeic and anecic species.

3bd829f4feb6.title: Earthworm
3bd829f4feb6.sentence: Earthworms feed on the decaying matter in the soil and analyzing the microbial contents of their digestive tracts (the earthworm microbiome) gives insight into the overall condition of the soil.

6142845dedd8.title: Earthworm
6142845dedd8.sentence: Nitrogenous fertilizers tend to create acidic conditions, which are fatal to the worms, and dead specimens are often found on the surface following the application of various pesticides, among which insecticides and fungicides are the most toxic.

2abf7db69441.title: Earthworm
2abf7db69441.sentence: Globally, certain earthworm populations have been devastated by deviation from organic production and the spraying of synthetic fertilizers and biocides, with at least three species now listed as extinct, but many more endangered.

aa6d32a34db2.title: Earthworm
aa6d32a34db2.sentence: As long ago as 1881 Charles Darwin wrote: "It may be doubted whether there are many other animals which have played so important a part in the history of the world, as have these lowly organized creatures." It has long been debated whether earthworms contribute to the disappearance of organic matter in the form of carbon dioxide and mineral nutrients or rather to its preservation in the form of humus.

055e8aa201b8.title: Detritivore
055e8aa201b8.sentence: Detritivores (also known as detrivores, detritophages, detritus feeders or detritus eaters) are heterotrophs that obtain nutrients by consuming detritus (decomposing plant and animal parts as well as feces).

914fbf705bb6.title: Detritivore
914fbf705bb6.sentence: Detritivores should be distinguished from other decomposers, such as many species of bacteria, fungi and protists, which are unable to ingest discrete lumps of matter.

50b8f58c7bb9.title: Detritivore
50b8f58c7bb9.sentence: Instead, these other decomposers live by absorbing and metabolizing on a molecular scale (saprotrophic nutrition).

e94f1a56b30f.title: Detritivore
e94f1a56b30f.sentence: The terms detritivore and decomposer are often used interchangeably, but they describe different organisms.

15613d32ce9d.title: Detritivore
15613d32ce9d.sentence: Typical detritivorous animals include millipedes, springtails, woodlice, dung flies, slugs, many terrestrial worms, sea stars, sea cucumbers, fiddler crabs, and some sedentary marine Polychaetes such as worms of the family Terebellidae.

117d1f6cfd92.title: Detritivore
117d1f6cfd92.sentence: Detritivores perform the first stage of remineralization, by fragmenting the dead plant matter, allowing decomposers to perform the second stage of remineralization.

3fe0101add3f.title: Detritivore
3fe0101add3f.sentence: The activity of detritivores is the reason why there is not an accumulation of plant litter in nature.

c025a007d48d.title: Detritivore
c025a007d48d.sentence: Plant tissues are made up of resilient molecules (e.g. cellulose, lignin, xylan) that decay at a much lower rate than other organic molecules.

16e27c56586a.title: Detritivore
16e27c56586a.sentence: Alongside decomposers, they reintroduce vital elements such as carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus, calcium, and potassium back into the soil, allowing plants to take in these elements and use them for growth.

110262d77e8c.title: Detritus
110262d77e8c.sentence: When these detritus feeders take in detritus with microorganisms multiplying on it, they mainly break down and absorb the microorganisms, which are rich in proteins, and excrete the detritus, which is mostly complex carbohydrates, having hardly broken it down at all.

41687ec40af1.title: Detritivore
41687ec40af1.sentence: Detritivore feeding behaviour is affected by rainfall; moist soil increases detritivore feeding and excretion.

4f2f6974703a.title: Detritivore
4f2f6974703a.sentence: Detritivores and decomposers that reside in the desert live in burrows underground to avoid the hot surface since underground conditions provide favorable living conditions for them.

987a0a899224.title: Detritivore
987a0a899224.sentence: Detritivores are the main organisms in clearing plant litter and recycling nutrients in the desert.

ac27060ee4fd.title: Detritivore
ac27060ee4fd.sentence: During the Carboniferous period, fungi and bacteria had yet to evolve the capacity to digest lignin, and so large deposits of dead plant tissue accumulated during this period, later becoming the fossil fuels.

7becd23bd154.title: Soil food web
7becd23bd154.sentence: The soil food web is the community of organisms living all or part of their lives in the soil.

679e221fdfc8.title: Soil food web
679e221fdfc8.sentence: Food webs describe the transfer of energy between species in an ecosystem.

d086c9114f3e.title: Soil food web
d086c9114f3e.sentence: While a food chain examines one linear energy pathway through an ecosystem, a food web is more complex and illustrates all of the potential pathways.

4f527d75a937.title: Soil food web
4f527d75a937.sentence: Plants use the sun’s energy to convert inorganic compounds into energy-rich, organic compounds, turning carbon dioxide and minerals into plant material by photosynthesis.

b1967243f06f.title: Soil food web
b1967243f06f.sentence: Plant flowers exude energy-rich nectar above ground and plant roots exude acids, sugars, and ectoenzymes into the rhizosphere, adjusting the pH and feeding the food web underground.

583bf60af135.title: Soil ecology
583bf60af135.sentence: They range in size from one-celled bacteria, algae, fungi, and protozoa, to more complex nematodes and micro-arthropods, to the visible earthworms, insects, small vertebrates, and plants.

362d5cc4628f.title: Soil food web
362d5cc4628f.sentence: At the end of the food chain, decomposers such as bacteria and fungi break down dead plant and animal material into simple nutrients.

6830a3568840.title: Soil
6830a3568840.sentence: This has been called the soil food web, through which all organic matter is processed as in a digestive system.

0d3b32db6fd2.title: Soil ecology
0d3b32db6fd2.sentence: Soil organisms decompose organic compounds, including manure, plant residues, and pesticides, preventing them from entering water and becoming pollutants.

9a268c7bdc97.title: Soil ecology
9a268c7bdc97.sentence: They sequester nitrogen and other nutrients that might otherwise enter groundwater, and they fix nitrogen from the atmosphere, making it available to plants.

0c9510bbad9e.title: Soil ecology
0c9510bbad9e.sentence: Many organisms enhance soil aggregation and porosity, thus increasing infiltration and reducing surface runoff.

e31678916c00.title: Soil ecology
e31678916c00.sentence: Soil organisms also prey on crop pests and are food for above-ground animals.

715340b2bdb6.title: Soil food web
715340b2bdb6.sentence: Until the last decade, it was believed that soil food webs were relatively simple, with low degrees of connectance and omnivory.

d6544405e623.title: Soil food web
d6544405e623.sentence: Soil ecologists discovered that omnivory in food webs was common, and that food chains could be long and complex and still remain resistant to disturbance by drying, freezing, and fumigation.

6c29cae9546f.title: Soil food web
6c29cae9546f.section: Interactions not included in food webs
6c29cae9546f.sentence: Litter transformers, mutualists, and ecosystem engineers all have strong impacts on their communities that cannot be characterized as either top-down or bottom-up.

37625fd0e9e0.title: Soil respiration
37625fd0e9e0.sentence: Soil respiration refers to the production of carbon dioxide when soil organisms respire.

cde513e794cf.title: Soil respiration
cde513e794cf.sentence: This includes respiration of plant roots, the rhizosphere, microbes and fauna.

4a343817da2b.title: Soil respiration
4a343817da2b.sentence: Soil respiration is a key ecosystem process that releases carbon from the soil in the form of CO2.

3f0bf443a001.title: Soil respiration
3f0bf443a001.sentence: CO2 is acquired by plants from the atmosphere and converted into organic compounds in the process of photosynthesis.

b35b675342e9.title: Soil respiration
b35b675342e9.sentence: This heterotrophic consumption releases CO2 and when this CO2 is released by below-ground organisms, it is considered soil respiration.

325e4b053475.title: Soil respiration
325e4b053475.sentence: The temperature, moisture, nutrient content and level of oxygen in the soil can produce extremely disparate rates of respiration.

33d26c693546.title: Soil respiration
33d26c693546.sentence: Soil respiration can vary spatially due to oxygen gradients within aggregates that create small anoxic microsites, where anaerobic metabolism dominates.

54778e0b9e74.title: Soil respiration
54778e0b9e74.sentence: Researchers have estimated that soil respiration accounts for 77 Pg of carbon released to the atmosphere each year.

e541b40526d9.title: Soil respiration
e541b40526d9.sentence: This level of release is greater than the carbon release due to anthropogenic sources (56 Pg per year) such as fossil fuel burning.

f74b6c4e8e59.title: Soil respiration
f74b6c4e8e59.sentence: The global soils contain up to 3150 Pg of carbon, of which 450 Pg exist in wetlands and 400 Pg in permanently frozen soils.

c3f4fafab78e.title: Soil respiration
c3f4fafab78e.sentence: The soils contain more than four times the carbon as the atmosphere.

98f6ebdc525c.title: Soil respiration
98f6ebdc525c.sentence: Thus, a small change in soil respiration can seriously alter the balance of atmosphere CO2 concentration versus soil carbon stores.

caeb969487d0.title: Soil respiration
caeb969487d0.sentence: A major component of soil respiration is from the decomposition of litter which releases CO2 to the environment while simultaneously immobilizing or mineralizing nutrients.

02071f586688.title: Soil respiration
02071f586688.sentence: Studies have shown that rates of soil respiration were associated with rates of microbial turnover and nitrogen mineralization.

3bbc5b838c59.title: Soil
3bbc5b838c59.sentence: Organic carbon held in soil is eventually returned to the atmosphere through the process of respiration carried out by heterotrophic organisms, but a substantial part is retained in the soil in the form of soil organic matter; tillage usually increases the rate of soil respiration, leading to the depletion of soil organic matter.

cd2612856ffb.title: Carbon cycle
cd2612856ffb.sentence: Between 1989 and 2008 soil respiration increased by about 0.1% per year.

8d9eb4be385a.title: Soil respiration
8d9eb4be385a.sentence: Soil respiration is also associated with positive feedback with global climate change.

09cde9f9cd65.title: Soil respiration
09cde9f9cd65.sentence: As global temperature rises, so will the rate of soil respiration across the globe thereby leading to a higher concentration of CO2 in the atmosphere, again leading to higher global temperatures.

f8e17b32cbec.title: Soil respiration
f8e17b32cbec.sentence: It is estimated that a rise in temperature by 2 °C will lead to an additional release of 10 Pg carbon per year to the atmosphere from soil respiration.

06ef19324199.title: Earthworm
06ef19324199.sentence: Earthworms are classified into three main ecophysiological categories: (1) leaf litter- or compost-dwelling worms that are nonburrowing, live at the soil-litter interface and eat decomposing organic matter (epigeic) e.g. Eisenia fetida; (2) topsoil- or subsoil-dwelling worms that feed on soil, burrow and cast within the soil, creating horizontal burrows in upper 10–30 cm of soil (endogeic); and (3) worms that construct permanent deep vertical burrows which they use to visit the surface to obtain plant material for food, such as leaves (anecic, meaning "reaching up"), e.g. Lumbricus terrestris.

095eea667bab.title: Earthworm
095eea667bab.sentence: Certain species of earthworm come to the surface and graze on the higher concentrations of organic matter present there, mixing it with the mineral soil (anecic earthworms).

a5fb704393d5.title: Earthworm
a5fb704393d5.sentence: Vermicomposting of organic wastes is currently processed using the epigeic Eisenia fetida and Eisenia andrei which are particularly adapted to the consumption of fresh organic matter without deepening in the substrate (contrary to the anecis Lumbricus terrestris) and which tolerate the heat generated in compost heaps.

68a78c5d33c1.title: Earthworm
68a78c5d33c1.sentence: The major benefits of earthworm activities to soil fertility for agriculture can be summarized as:

7210c43bd0c8.title: Earthworm
7210c43bd0c8.sentence: Earthworms accelerate nutrient cycling in the soil-plant system through fragmention and mixing, physical grinding and chemical digestion of plant debris.

b52ddbad1ce6.title: Earthworm
b52ddbad1ce6.sentence: This is achieved by the worm's actions (mainly of anecics) of pulling below the surface deposited organic matter such as leaf fall or manure, either for food or to plug its burrow.

ea2b35bd2c44.title: Earthworm
ea2b35bd2c44.sentence: Once in the burrow, the worm will shred the leaf, partially digest it and mingle it with the earth.

cc990b19109f.title: Earthworm
cc990b19109f.sentence: Worm casts (see bottom right) can contain 40 percent more humus than the top 9 inches (230 mm) of soil in which the worm is living.

403f1ab138ef.title: Earthworm
403f1ab138ef.sentence: - Chemical: In addition to dead organic matter, the earthworm also ingests any other soil particles that are small enough, including sand grains up to 1⁄20 inch (1.3 mm), into its gizzard, wherein those minute fragments of grit (gastroliths) grind everything into a fine paste which is then digested in the intestine, increased surface area favouring microbial colonization and enzymatic action.

3b2e0fa33fe5.title: Earthworm
3b2e0fa33fe5.sentence: When the worm excretes this paste in the form of casts, deposited on the surface or deeper in the soil, carbon, nitrogen and phosphorus are increased compared to the bulk soil and nutrients are changed to a plant-available form, increasing locally soil fertility.

40434645dca2.title: Earthworm
40434645dca2.sentence: In conditions where humus is plentiful, the weight of casts produced may be greater than 4.5 kilograms (9.9 lb) per worm per year.

d904c4e4844f.title: Earthworm
d904c4e4844f.sentence: - Physical: The earthworm's burrowing creates a multitude of channels through the soil and is of great value in maintaining the soil structure, enabling processes of aeration and drainage.

b32ee06631e7.title: Earthworm
b32ee06631e7.sentence: Research from the Station d'écologie Tropicale de Lamto (Ivory Coast) asserts that the earthworms positively influence the rate of macroaggregate formation (Soil structure#Granular|granular structure), an important feature for soil structure.

65d4534455d7.title: Earthworm
65d4534455d7.sentence: The stability of aggregates in response to water was also found to be improved when constructed by earthworms.

acb6ea794a77.title: Earthworm
acb6ea794a77.sentence: Darwin estimated that arable land contains up to 53,000 per acre (130,000/ha) of worms, but more recent research has produced figures suggesting that even poor soil may support 250,000 per acre (620,000/ha), whilst rich fertile farmland may have up to 1,750,000 per acre (4,300,000/ha), meaning that the weight of earthworms beneath a farmer's soil could be greater than that of the livestock upon its surface.

fa8b4771c914.title: Earthworm
fa8b4771c914.sentence: Richly organic topsoil populations of earthworms are much higher, averaging 500 per square metre (46/sq ft) and up to 400 g/m2, such that, for the 7 billion of us, each person alive today has support of 7 million earthworms.

f4265a5a7dbb.title: Earthworm
f4265a5a7dbb.sentence: It seems that there is now a consensus about the prominent role of earthworms in carbon sequestration due to the fact that part of organic matter is mineralized at or near the soil surface while the major part is incorporated in the deep soil where it is stabilized by links with clay minerals.

97d628e23f48.title: Earthworm
97d628e23f48.sentence: Though not fully quantified yet, greenhouse gas emissions (carbon dioxide, nitrous oxide, methane) of earthworms, direct or mediated by their strong influence on soil microbial communities, likely contribute to global warming, especially since top-dwelling earthworms increase the speed of carbon cycles and have been spread by humans into many new geographies.

5b28675b37e2.title: Petrichor
5b28675b37e2.sentence: Petrichor (/ˈpɛtrɪkɔːr/ PET-rik-or) is the earthy scent often associated with rain falling on dry soil or rock.

31c41923a950.title: Petrichor
31c41923a950.sentence: The term was introduced by Australian researchers Isabel Joy Bear and Richard Grenfell Thomas in a 1964 paper in Nature.

3a9fe01588ca.title: Petrichor
3a9fe01588ca.sentence: Thomas coined the term "petrichor" to refer to what had previously been known as "argillaceous odour".

4dd74d9759ac.title: Petrichor
4dd74d9759ac.sentence: The noun petrichor originated as a compound of two Greek words, πέτρα (meaning 'rock' or 'stone') and ἰχώρ ('ichor', the ethereal golden fluid that runs in the veins of Ancient Greek gods and goddesses).

b1150a53c960.title: Petrichor
b1150a53c960.sentence: Petrichor is associated with a mixture of volatile substances rather than a single chemical compound.

e1afda2d89c1.title: Petrichor
e1afda2d89c1.sentence: Some of these substances originate from plant-derived organic matter and accumulate on mineral surfaces during dry periods.

7296c1a73e64.title: Petrichor
7296c1a73e64.sentence: Increasing moisture can displace these materials from the pores of rocks and soil, allowing them to enter the surrounding air.

7394496c3f63.title: Petrichor
7394496c3f63.sentence: Other contributors include earthy-smelling microbial metabolites such as geosmin and 2-methylisoborneol, produced by bacteria including species of Streptomyces.

10471bf12fa1.title: Petrichor
10471bf12fa1.sentence: The Roman naturalist Pliny the Elder described a similar phenomenon in Natural History, observing that earth emits a particularly pleasant odour when rain follows prolonged drought.

a70010ae4279.title: Petrichor
a70010ae4279.sentence: Pliny regarded this scent as a characteristic of fertile soil.

620531d42574.title: Petrichor
620531d42574.sentence: In 1891, French chemists Marcellin Berthelot and G. André reported their investigations of the characteristic odour of soil in a paper entitled "Sur l'odeur propre de la terre" ("On the Earth's Own Smell"), published in Comptes rendus de l'Académie des Sciences.

46e0329eab24.title: Petrichor
46e0329eab24.sentence: They extracted an odorous substance from soil by steam distillation but were unable to establish its chemical identity.

f2dc7383f606.title: Petrichor
f2dc7383f606.sentence: In a follow-up paper, Bear and Thomas suggested in 1965 that the chemical components giving rise to the "argillaceous odour of petrichor" also slow seed germination and early plant growth.

61062a7cbfbd.title: Petrichor
61062a7cbfbd.sentence: Their experiments found that small quantities of oily extracts from mineral materials delayed the germination and development of several types of seeds.

a2776e327ad0.title: Petrichor
a2776e327ad0.sentence: Research in 2015 suggested a physical mechanism by which scent-bearing substances may be dispersed into the air.

4c72dedb0690.title: Petrichor
4c72dedb0690.sentence: Using high-speed photography, researchers at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology observed that raindrops impacting porous surfaces generate aerosols as trapped air bubbles rise and burst.

3d1e4e16b869.title: Petrichor
3d1e4e16b869.sentence: The researchers proposed that this process may contribute to the release of petrichor and found that light and moderate rainfall could produce more aerosols than heavier rainfall under the conditions investigated.

7ada94c11020.title: Petrichor
7ada94c11020.sentence: A 2026 study of dryland soils along an aridity gradient extending into Israel's Negev Desert identified 58 volatile organic compounds associated with soil rewetting and reported rapid increases in their emissions.

c3038d986b2c.title: Petrichor
c3038d986b2c.sentence: The researchers suggested that these emissions may contribute to atmospheric ozone and secondary aerosol formation, extending the investigation of petrichor beyond its characteristic smell to its possible effects on atmospheric chemistry.

d4f26cdecfde.title: Petrichor
d4f26cdecfde.sentence: The phenomenon was further scientifically described in a March 1964 paper by Australian researchers Isabel Bear and Dick Thomas, published in the journal Nature.

c5aa643bb8b4.title: Soil enzyme
c5aa643bb8b4.sentence: Soil enzymes are a group of enzymes found in soil.

dcbf8ba56bf1.title: Soil enzyme
dcbf8ba56bf1.sentence: They are excreted by soil microbes such as fungi, bacteria and archaea, and play a key role in decomposing soil organic matter into humus, in the process releasing nutrients essential for the growth of plants.

499a90c42d99.title: Soil microbiology
499a90c42d99.sentence: Most soil enzymes are produced by bacteria, fungi and plant roots.

28e2f7eb3fdd.title: Soil enzyme
28e2f7eb3fdd.sentence: Soil enzymes catalyse many biochemical reactions, degrading organic compounds (e.g. cellulose, lignin, starch, urea) and thus being prominent agents of nutrient cycles (e.g. carbon and nitrogen cycles).

e2f8cb1ced3b.title: Soil enzyme
e2f8cb1ced3b.sentence: Soil enzymes are intracellular, cell-associated or free enzymes produced by soil microorganisms, which use them to degrade macromolecules (e.g. cellulose, lignin, chitin) after-death produced by plants and animals, in order to ensure their growth and reproduction.

dbecd15f0022.title: Soil enzyme
dbecd15f0022.sentence: Soil enzymes are bound to clay and humic colloids which protect them against rapid degradation, although to the detriment of their activity with clay minerals, resulting in a trade-off between protection and activity.

1665f23e2dda.title: Soil enzyme
1665f23e2dda.sentence: The distribution of soil enzymes is highly heterogeneous, varying at millimetric scale according to the distribution of patches of nutrients and microbial biomass, plant roots, or colonies of specific microorganisms.

e2b88bcfc7ee.title: Soil enzyme
e2b88bcfc7ee.sentence: Soil enzymes also varies in concentration at meter (single-tree) to kilometer (catchment) scales in forested areas, with patterns of spatial variation specific to each enzyme system, and according to biomes in a given region.

9b469ec9db60.title: Soil enzyme
9b469ec9db60.sentence: Some soil enzymes such as ureases may be inhibited by ingredients in fertiliser to delay release of the nutrients over an extended period.

fe317f45ad88.title: Soil microbiology
fe317f45ad88.sentence: Enzyme activity is higher in plots that are fertilized with manure as compared to inorganic fertilizers, although other studies showed that a combination of mineral and organic fertilizers was better than manuring.

7752fbb7cd4c.title: Soil microbiology
7752fbb7cd4c.sentence: Their biochemical activity is a factor in both stabilization and degradation of soil structure.

89d9e1a998a4.title: Soil enzyme
89d9e1a998a4.sentence: As such they play a decisive role in the maintenance of soil health.

e7fb956b04ad.title: Soil biology
e7fb956b04ad.sentence: Bacteria are single-cell organisms and the most numerous denizens of agricultural fields, with populations ranging from 100 million to 3 billion in a 'teaspoon' of productive soil.

cc2b32f382aa.title: Soil microbiology
cc2b32f382aa.sentence: Bacteria and archaea (initially classified as bacteria), the smallest organisms in soil apart from viruses, are prokaryotic.

593bd54c25c1.title: Soil microbiology
593bd54c25c1.sentence: Up to 10 billion culturable bacterial cells inhabit each gram of soil in and around plant roots, a region known as the rhizosphere, which is a hotspot of microbial diversity, and in particular the rhizoplane.

dad3d051f14d.title: Soil biology
dad3d051f14d.sentence: Bacteria live in soil water, including the film of moisture surrounding soil particles, where some are able to swim by means of flagella.

023a3db9c9b4.title: Soil biology
023a3db9c9b4.sentence: They are capable of very rapid reproduction by binary fission (dividing into two) in favourable conditions.

3205a14b0077.title: Soil biology
3205a14b0077.sentence: The majority of the beneficial soil-dwelling bacteria need oxygen (and are thus termed aerobic bacteria), whilst those that do not require air are referred to as anaerobic, and tend to cause putrefaction of dead organic matter.

97b207a2b982.title: Soil biology
97b207a2b982.sentence: Aerobic bacteria are most active in a soil that is moist (but not saturated, as this will deprive aerobic bacteria of the air that they require), and neutral soil pH, and where there is plenty of food available (carbohydrates and micronutrients from organic matter).

065362ee8c99.title: Soil microbiology
065362ee8c99.sentence: Apart from the rhizosphere, where bacterial activity is stimulated by rhizodeposition and root exudation, most bacteria of the bulk soil are in a quiescent state, in the form of bacterial colonies embedded in a polysaccharidic matrix covered with clay platelets, and resistant to drought.

9e27f4d8e387.title: Soil microbiology
9e27f4d8e387.sentence: These bacterial microaggregates may remain in this state of quiescence for a long time, until being reached by exudates from growing root tips or the mucus of burrowing earthworms.

3e5336e84a69.title: Soil biology
3e5336e84a69.sentence: Hostile conditions will not completely kill bacteria; rather, the bacteria will stop growing and get into a dormant stage, often in the form of clay-coated quiescent colonies, and those individuals with pre-adaptive mutations or rapidly evolving better-adapted traits may compete better in the new conditions.

3ce011115013.title: Soil biology
3ce011115013.sentence: Some Gram-positive bacteria (e.g. Bacillus, Clostridium) produce spores in order to wait for more favourable circumstances, and Gram-negative bacteria get into a "nonculturable" resting stage.

a0abd52acc61.title: Soil biology
a0abd52acc61.sentence: This is carried out by free-living nitrogen-fixing (diazotroph) bacteria in the soil or water such as Azotobacter and heterocyst-bearing cyanobacteria (blue-green algae), or by those that live in close symbiosis with legumes, such as rhizobia, or with actinorhizal plants, such as Frankia.

01d22d9d05de.title: Soil biology
01d22d9d05de.sentence: Nitrification is a vital part of the nitrogen cycle, wherein certain chemolithotrophic nitrifying bacteria (e.g. Nitrosomonas), called autotrophic nitrifiers (manufacturing their own carbohydrate supply without using the process of photosynthesis) are able to transform nitrogen in the form of ammonium, which is produced by the decomposition of proteins, into nitrates, available to growing plants and once again converted to proteins.

1e88f41158fd.title: Soil biology
1e88f41158fd.sentence: The denitrification process caused by oxygen-free conditions converts nitrates and nitrites in soil into nitrogen gas or into gaseous compounds such as nitrous oxide or nitric oxide.

e2a551e0e9b6.title: Soil microbiology
e2a551e0e9b6.sentence: One of the most distinguished features of bacteria is their biochemical versatility.

c3f9e5714deb.title: Soil microbiology
c3f9e5714deb.sentence: A bacterial genus called Pseudomonas can metabolize a wide range of chemicals and fertilizers.

7233ecb5918e.title: Soil microbiology
7233ecb5918e.sentence: In contrast, another genus known as Nitrobacter can only derive its energy by oxidizing nitrite to nitrate.

1d9c4a35bb15.title: Soil microbiology
1d9c4a35bb15.sentence: Soil archaea are still poorly known but they could play a significant role in nitrification and methanogenesis.

92379afa5e4c.title: Soil microbiology
92379afa5e4c.sentence: Some bacteria can colonize minerals in the soil and help influence weathering and the breaking down of these minerals.

7db4bfb05785.title: Geosmin
7db4bfb05785.sentence: Geosmin (/dʒiˈɒzmɪn/ jee-OZ-min) is a chemical with a distinct earthy or musty odor.

4065f98694a4.title: Geosmin
4065f98694a4.sentence: It is produced by bacteria, especially cyanobacteria, often present in soil and water supplies.

5dfc2a91b5a9.title: Geosmin
5dfc2a91b5a9.sentence: Its name is derived from the Ancient Greek words geō- (γεω-), meaning "earth", and osmḗ (ὀσμή), meaning "smell".

277adc1cf85e.title: Geosmin
277adc1cf85e.sentence: The word was coined in 1965 by the American biochemist Nancy N. Gerber (1929–1985) and the French-American biologist Hubert A. Lechevalier (1926–2015).

3de3b5472ccf.title: Petrichor
3de3b5472ccf.sentence: They obtained the substance from cultures of actinomycetes, including Streptomyces griseus, and named it from the Greek words for earth and smell.

e9ccc66f19e3.title: Petrichor
e9ccc66f19e3.sentence: Gerber subsequently established the chemical structure of geosmin in 1968.

72cf385f6e10.title: Geosmin
72cf385f6e10.sentence: Geosmin is produced as a secondary metabolite by various blue-green algae (cyanobacteria), filamentous bacteria in the class Actinomyces, other prokaryotes, and various eukaryotes.

65138c4add39.title: Geosmin
65138c4add39.sentence: The main genera in the cyanobacteria that have been shown to produce geosmin include Anabaena, Phormidium, and Planktothrix, while the main genus in the Actinomyces that produces geosmin is Streptomyces.

4ffb8a90cc1e.title: Geosmin
4ffb8a90cc1e.sentence: Geosmin is responsible for the earthy taste of beetroots and a contributor to the strong scent, known as petrichor, that occurs when rain falls after a spell of dry weather or when soil is disturbed.

fd12085d0585.title: Geosmin
fd12085d0585.sentence: It is easily smelled by most people, having a very low odor detection threshold, ranging from 0.006 to 0.01 micrograms per liter in water.

951754a830c2.title: Geosmin
951754a830c2.sentence: In a study of 50 subjects, the mean odor detection threshold was 9.5 ng/L for naturally occurring (−)-geosmin and 78 ng/L for (+)-geosmin.

08c662cbda53.title: Geosmin
08c662cbda53.sentence: This makes the natural form roughly eight times more potent.

f25bd7db5f7d.title: Geosmin
f25bd7db5f7d.sentence: Geosmin, along with 2-methylisoborneol, are the major biological causes of muddy odor and flavor in drinking water worldwide and in farmed fish.

dc24dbefd388.title: Geosmin
dc24dbefd388.sentence: Despite its negative effects on the taste and odor of fish and drinking water, geosmin is nontoxic to humans.

5cb34d3bb540.title: Geosmin
5cb34d3bb540.sentence: Under acidic conditions, geosmin decomposes into odorless substances.

0e2acf267db7.title: Geosmin
0e2acf267db7.sentence: Geosmin and 2-methylisoborneol have been shown to attract springtails, Folsomia candida, which are believed to feed on and spread the spores of Streptomyces both through their feces and by attachment to their cuticle.

185c03153e64.title: Geosmin
185c03153e64.sentence: Additionally, geosmin has been found to repel the nematode Caenorhabditis elegans and reduced its contact with Streptomyces.

b4006cf9a13c.title: Geosmin
b4006cf9a13c.sentence: Geosmin cannot be removed from water using standard treatment processes, requiring a combination of integrated solutions which may not be available to all municipal water suppliers.

a30b20a0dea7.title: Geosmin
a30b20a0dea7.sentence: Possible advanced oxidation methods include photocatalysis, ozonation, and ultrasonication.

51283fcd2423.title: Soil biology
51283fcd2423.sentence: A gram of garden soil can contain around one million fungi, such as yeasts and moulds, and around 700 km fungal hyphae can live in 1 g of soil.

95293cc106fc.title: Soil biology
95293cc106fc.sentence: Fungi have no chlorophyll, and are not able to photosynthesise.

24ef93d99253.title: Soil biology
24ef93d99253.sentence: Fungi spread underground by sending long thin threads known as mycelium throughout the soil; these threads can be observed throughout many soils and compost heaps.

970052d2ac62.title: Soil microbiology
970052d2ac62.sentence: Fungi may be outnumbered by bacteria in cell counts, but they can contribute greater biomass and respiration rate in some soil types.

1676775f57d9.title: Soil biology
1676775f57d9.sentence: They cannot use atmospheric carbon dioxide as a source of carbon, therefore they are chemo-heterotrophic, meaning that, like animals, they require a chemical source of energy rather than being able to use light as an energy source, as well as organic substrates to get carbon for growth and development.

adbc857db7f0.title: Soil biology
adbc857db7f0.sentence: Given these requirements and the development of a dense hyphal network (mycelium) they actively participate to the degradation of freshly deposited organic remains and their transformation in humus (humification) and carbon dioxide (mineralization).

2b530c49887a.title: Soil biology
2b530c49887a.sentence: In terms of soil and humus creation, the most important fungi tend to be saprotrophic; that is, they live on dead or decaying organic matter, thus breaking it down and converting it to mineral forms (e.g. nitrate, ammonium, phosphate) that are available to the higher plants.

652099cc667b.title: Soil biology
652099cc667b.sentence: A succession of fungal species will colonise the dead matter, beginning with those that use sugars and starches, which are succeeded by those that are able to break down cellulose and lignins.

69a86766cef5.title: Soil biology
69a86766cef5.sentence: Many fungi are parasitic, often causing disease to their living host plant, although some have beneficial relationships with living plants, as illustrated below.

5c7b4c6a4120.title: Soil microbiology
5c7b4c6a4120.sentence: Fungi decay plant detritus, in particular wood, contribute to soil aggregation, are important as food sources for other, larger soil organisms, as soil-borne pathogens, or conversely as beneficial plant symbionts (e.g. mycorrhizae) and more generally they are important for soil health.

8ef6d848c015.title: Soil microbiology
8ef6d848c015.sentence: Compared with bacteria, fungi are relatively benefitted by acidic soils.

596f6350a5e3.title: Soil microbiology
596f6350a5e3.sentence: Fungi also grow well in dry, arid soils because fungi are aerobic, or dependent on oxygen, and the higher the moisture content in the soil, the less oxygen is present for them.

a865f94d6218.title: Soil biology
a865f94d6218.sentence: From the mycelium the fungus is able to throw up its fruiting bodies, the visible part above the soil (e.g., mushrooms, toadstools, and puffballs), which may contain millions of spores.

83748fe28e25.title: Soil biology
83748fe28e25.sentence: When the fruiting body bursts, these spores are dispersed through the air to settle in fresh environments, and are able to lie dormant for up to years until the right conditions for their activation arise or the right food is made available.

ba533c871a8c.title: Soil biology
ba533c871a8c.sentence: Fungal spores are dispersed by wind, water, but also by a variety of fungal-feeding animals, from small invertebrates (e.g. springtails) to big mammals (e.g. wild boars), helping them to colonize new, sometimes remote environments, hence the cosmopolitan distribution of many fungal species.

44b5d4a1d551.title: Actinomycetota
44b5d4a1d551.sentence: The Actinomycetota (previously known as "Actinobacteria") are a diverse phylum of Gram-positive bacteria with high guanine-cytosine content (GC content or G+C content).

da311d51895f.title: Actinomycetota
da311d51895f.sentence: In this role, the colonies often grow extensive mycelia, as fungi do, and the name of an important order of the phylum, Actinomycetales (the actinomycetes), reflects that they were long believed to be fungi.

d32263a9af29.title: Soil microbiology
d32263a9af29.sentence: Actinomycetes (or Actinobacteria) are bacteria, but they share some characteristics with fungi that are most likely a result of convergent evolution due to a common habitat and lifestyle.

837339c21ea4.title: Actinomycetota
837339c21ea4.sentence: In soil, they help decompose organic matter of dead organisms so the molecules can be taken up anew by plants.

8feaa2a15533.title: Soil biology
8feaa2a15533.sentence: Actinomycetota (actinomycetes, actinobacteria) are critical in the decomposition of organic matter and in humus formation.

1b0de54f0802.title: Soil biology
1b0de54f0802.sentence: They specialize in breaking down cellulose and lignin along with the tough chitin found in the exoskeletons of arthropods.

46a663f6bf99.title: Actinomycetota
46a663f6bf99.sentence: While this role is also played by fungi, actinomycetota are much smaller and likely do not occupy the same ecological niche.

db7b4587c6b4.title: Actinomycetota
db7b4587c6b4.sentence: Actinomycetota is one of the dominant bacterial phyla and contains one of the largest of bacterial genera: Streptomyces.

a32b2fd85c8e.title: Actinomycetota
a32b2fd85c8e.sentence: Streptomyces and other actinomycetota are major contributors to biological buffering of soils.

e9ea5cc09b9f.title: Actinomycetota
e9ea5cc09b9f.sentence: Some soil actinomycetota (such as Frankia) live symbiotically with the plants whose roots pervade the soil, fixing nitrogen for the plants in exchange for access to some of the plant's saccharides.

6b5f91c2e2ce.title: Soil biology
6b5f91c2e2ce.sentence: Their various production of volatile metabolites is responsible for the sweet earthy aroma associated with a good healthy soil.

5e06af9e0d55.title: Soil biology
5e06af9e0d55.sentence: They require plenty of air and a pH between 6.0 and 7.5, but are more tolerant of dry conditions than most other bacteria and fungi.

753364e6a208.title: Soil microbiology
753364e6a208.sentence: One of the most notable characteristics of the actinomycetes is their ability to produce antibiotics.

1549a47c5463.title: Soil microbiology
1549a47c5463.sentence: Streptomycin, neomycin, erythromycin and tetracycline are only a few examples of these antibiotics.

27175013be5d.title: Actinomycetota
27175013be5d.sentence: Actinomycetota, especially Streptomyces spp., are recognized as the producers of many bioactive metabolites that are useful to humans in medicine, such as antibacterials, antifungals, antivirals, antithrombotics, immunomodifiers, antitumor drugs, and enzyme inhibitors; and in agriculture, including insecticides, herbicides, fungicides, and growth-promoting substances for plants and animals.

2527e4718a6b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/04%3A_The_Living_Soil/4.02%3A_Soil_Microorganisms
2527e4718a6b.section: Bacteria > Relative Amounts of Bacteria and Fungi
2527e4718a6b.sentence: The actinomycetes, another group of bacteria, break large lignin molecules into smaller sizes.

4f29bc5f1ae1.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/04%3A_The_Living_Soil/4.02%3A_Soil_Microorganisms
4f29bc5f1ae1.section: Bacteria > Relative Amounts of Bacteria and Fungi
4f29bc5f1ae1.sentence: Lignin is a large and complex molecule found in plant tissue, especially stems, that is difficult for most organisms to break down.

03bc6f87edc3.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/04%3A_The_Living_Soil/4.02%3A_Soil_Microorganisms
03bc6f87edc3.section: Bacteria > Relative Amounts of Bacteria and Fungi
03bc6f87edc3.sentence: Lignin also frequently protects other molecules like cellulose from decomposition.

7ac102a5d2bb.title: Lumbricus terrestris
7ac102a5d2bb.sentence: Lumbricus terrestris is a large, reddish worm species thought to be native to Western Europe, now widely distributed around the world (along with several other lumbricids).

3d9a78c4b652.title: Lumbricus terrestris
3d9a78c4b652.sentence: In Britain, it is primarily called the common earthworm or lob worm (though the name is also applied to a marine polychaete).

1bb20a59c763.title: Lumbricus terrestris
1bb20a59c763.sentence: In North America, the term nightcrawler (or vitalis) is also used, and more specifically Canadian nightcrawler, referring to the fact that the large majority of these worms sold commercially (usually as fishing bait) are from Southern Ontario.

0f87769efa9d.title: Lumbricus terrestris
0f87769efa9d.sentence: Lumbricus terrestris is relatively large, pinkish to reddish-brown in colour, generally 110–200 millimetres (4.3–7.9 in) in length and about 7–10 millimetres (0.28–0.39 in) in diameter.

4b2608308a88.title: Lumbricus terrestris
4b2608308a88.sentence: Through much of Europe, it is the largest naturally occurring species of earthworm, typically reaching 20 to 25 cm in length when extended.

fbfc68ebe19a.title: Lumbricus terrestris
fbfc68ebe19a.sentence: Lumbricus terrestris is a deep-burrowing anecic earthworm which builds deep vertical burrows and surfaces to feed as opposed to burrowing through the soil for its food as endogeic species do.

d1cb74cd9afb.title: Lumbricus terrestris
d1cb74cd9afb.sentence: It removes litter from the soil surface, pulling it down into the mineral layer, and deposits casts of mixed organic and mineral material on the soil surface.

fa02f408b23f.title: Lumbricus terrestris
fa02f408b23f.sentence: It has invaded some areas with podzol soil profiles and destroyed their distinctive banded appearance (thick dark organic litter on the surface underlain by pale E horizon and below that brown or reddish B horizon), creating a new horizon sequence of thin litter and dark Ap (representing the worms' mixing zone) over the B.

944c8f905f99.title: Lumbricus terrestris
944c8f905f99.section: As an invasive species in North America
944c8f905f99.sentence: Lumbricus terrestris is considered invasive in the north central United States.

687b58302363.title: Lumbricus terrestris
687b58302363.section: As an invasive species in North America
687b58302363.sentence: It thrives in fence rows and woodlots and can lead to reductions in native herbaceous and tree regrowth.

7e67ec1c4582.title: Lumbricus terrestris
7e67ec1c4582.section: As an invasive species in North America
7e67ec1c4582.sentence: It does not do well in tilled fields because of pesticide exposure, physical injuries from farm equipment and a lack of nutrients.

a570a210df3d.title: Earthworm
a570a210df3d.sentence: Various worms are used in vermiculture, the practice of feeding organic waste to earthworms to transform it into vermicompost.

a23d5b2b5613.title: Earthworm
a23d5b2b5613.sentence: These are usually Eisenia fetida (or its close relative Eisenia andrei) commonly known as the brandling worm, or tiger worm or red wiggler.

d5f91638d231.title: Earthworm
d5f91638d231.sentence: They are distinct from soil-dwelling earthworms, living mainly in manure heaps.

9df6a14e20a8.title: Earthworm
9df6a14e20a8.sentence: In the tropics, the African nightcrawler Eudrilus eugeniae and the Indian blue Perionyx excavatus are used.

d135f3a88324.title: Compost
d135f3a88324.sentence: - Vermicompost (also called worm castings, worm humus, worm manure, or worm faeces) is the end product of the breakdown of organic matter by earthworms.

28f4938136ef.title: Compost
28f4938136ef.sentence: - Earthworms ingest partly composted material and excrete worm castings, making nitrogen, calcium, phosphorus, and magnesium available to plants.

224c3b5b6406.title: Earthworm
224c3b5b6406.sentence: Addition of this humified organic matter to the soil, preferably as a surface mulch, will improve moisture and nutrient availability, with beneficial effects on the soil microflora.

9fb63e8482e7.title: Ecosystem engineer
9fb63e8482e7.sentence: An ecosystem engineer is any species that creates, significantly modifies, maintains or destroys a habitat.

92d394491588.title: Soil biology
92d394491588.sentence: Earthworms, ants and termites, known as ecosystem engineers, mix the soil as they burrow, significantly affecting soil formation and organic matter dynamics.

3de5318cec4a.title: Ecosystem engineer
3de5318cec4a.sentence: Thus fungi are engineers controlling nutrient cycles in ecosystems.

4b89c61c539c.title: Ecosystem engineer
4b89c61c539c.sentence: In other words, they are identified as engineers because of their ability to modify resources, not because of their trophic effect.

a1b75a3367f2.title: Ecosystem engineer
a1b75a3367f2.sentence: Keystone species are typically essential because of their trophic effect, while ecosystem engineers are not.

0ccec2bc2013.title: Ecosystem engineer
0ccec2bc2013.sentence: Allogenic engineers modify the biophysical environment by mechanically changing living or nonliving materials from one form to another.

25eb471a3b7f.title: Ecosystem engineer
25eb471a3b7f.sentence: Autogenic engineers modify the environment by creating habitat through their body structures.

bf866cdf01dc.title: Ecosystem engineer
bf866cdf01dc.sentence: Examples include Sphagnum moss, which forms peatlands inhabited by species adapted to acidic, waterlogged conditions, and trees, whose trunks and branches serve as substrates and shelter for lichens, mosses, squirrels, birds and insects.

1c5f061da516.title: Soil biology
1c5f061da516.sentence: Burrowing soil detritivores, like earthworms, known as ecosystem engineers, ingest detritus and decompose it, while building a good granular soil structure and offering a habitat for various soil organisms.

02c014c028c4.title: Soil biology
02c014c028c4.sentence: Ants and termites are also often referred to as soil engineers because, when they create their nests, there are several chemical and physical changes made to the soil.

b23e7b8eefef.title: Soil biology
b23e7b8eefef.sentence: Among these changes are increasing presence of the most essential elements like carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorus, elements needed for plant growth.

0dc2b1875d13.title: Soil biology
0dc2b1875d13.sentence: They also can gather soil particles from differing depths of soil and deposit them in other places, leading to the mixing of soil so it is richer with nutrients and other elements.

73f1fb85e73b.title: Soil animals
73f1fb85e73b.sentence: Among bigger species, soil engineers (e.g. earthworms, ants, termites, moles, gophers) play a prominent role in soil formation and vegetation development, giving them the rank of ecosystem engineers.

54b41f6523de.title: Soil animals
54b41f6523de.sentence: Fossorial mammals contribute to disseminate mycorrhizal fungi when feeding on fruiting bodies, and facilitate seed germination in their excavated mounds, making them, beside and through their often reported influence on soil morphology, important agents of vegetation dynamics, giving them the rank of ecosystem engineers.

bf4e1137a7f7.title: Ecosystem engineer
bf4e1137a7f7.sentence: Prairie dogs are another terrestrial form of allogenic ecosystem engineers due to the fact that the species has the ability to perform substantial modifications by burrowing and turning soil.

324786b52fb3.title: Ecosystem engineer
324786b52fb3.sentence: They are able to influence soils and vegetation of the landscape while providing underground corridors for arthropods, avians, other small mammals, and reptiles.

7ed13de571a2.title: Ecosystem engineer
7ed13de571a2.sentence: Fungi are able to connect regions that are distant from one another and translocate nutrients between them.

e69cd6679c8f.title: Ecosystem engineer
e69cd6679c8f.sentence: Doing so they create nutritional niches for xylophagous invertebrates, supply trees with nitrogen translocated from previously predated animals or even form an "underground pipeline" that redistributes carbon between trees.

50e97a8f26b5.title: Soil animals
50e97a8f26b5.sentence: Soil microarthropods play a negligible role in soil bioturbation and soil pore formation, but enchytraeids dig the soil and create galleries in which they deposit their faeces, giving them the rank of ecosystem engineers in soils (or in times) with poor earthworm activity.

48185e255c3d.title: Enchytraeidae
48185e255c3d.sentence: Enchytraeids, like earthworms, are ecosystem engineers, influencing the soil structure by creating aggregates of various sizes.

d264163967dd.title: Soil contamination
d264163967dd.sentence: Detrimental impacts of contaminants on soil food chains result in dramatic changes in humus forms, mediated by the disappearance or reduced activity of key organisms, also called soil ecosystem engineers, e.g. earthworms, which are particularly sensitive to a wide range of soil contaminants.

ae18365ec02c.title: Bioturbation
ae18365ec02c.sentence: Bioturbation is defined as the reworking of soils and sediments by animals or plants.

747b8157de63.title: Bioturbation
747b8157de63.sentence: It includes burrowing, ingestion, and defecation of sediment grains.

d7a82941959b.title: Bioturbation
d7a82941959b.sentence: Bioturbating activities have a profound effect on the environment and are thought to be a primary driver of biodiversity.

aefee6afa08f.title: Bioturbation
aefee6afa08f.sentence: Walruses, salmon, and pocket gophers are examples of large bioturbators.

dff9af5a3fb6.title: Bioturbation
dff9af5a3fb6.sentence: Although the activities of these large macrofaunal bioturbators are more conspicuous, the dominant bioturbators are small invertebrates, such as earthworms, polychaetes, ghost shrimp, mud shrimp, and midge larvae.

cdf35c062d85.title: Bioturbation
cdf35c062d85.sentence: Bioturbation is sometimes confused with the process of bioirrigation, however these processes differ in what they are mixing; bioirrigation refers to the mixing of water and solutes in sediments and is an effect of bioturbation.

e4e1444cc0c8.title: Bioturbation
e4e1444cc0c8.sentence: Microbial communities are greatly influenced by bioturbator activities, as increased transport of more energetically favorable oxidants, such as oxygen, to typically highly reduced sediments at depth alters the microbial metabolic processes occurring around burrows.

b9f4dd9b1250.title: Bioturbation
b9f4dd9b1250.sentence: This increase in sediment metabolism and microbial activity further results in enhanced organic matter decomposition and sediment oxygen uptake.

5ce94c236eac.title: Bioturbation
5ce94c236eac.sentence: Burrows offer protection from predation and harsh environmental conditions.

3cceede07bb6.title: Bioturbation
3cceede07bb6.sentence: The formal study of bioturbation began in the 1800s by Charles Darwin experimenting in his garden.

982a010f571d.title: Bioturbation
982a010f571d.sentence: Excavations 30 years after the initial deposit of chalk revealed that the chalk was buried 18 centimeters under the sediment, which indicated a burial rate of 6 millimeters per year.

27ea3230f480.title: Bioturbation
27ea3230f480.sentence: Darwin attributed this burial to the activity of earthworms in the sediment and determined that these disruptions were important in soil formation.

7c381cc29b06.title: Bioturbation
7c381cc29b06.sentence: In 1891, geologist Nathaniel Shaler expanded Darwin's concept to include soil disruption by ants and trees.

fba1e2b4922f.title: Bioturbation
fba1e2b4922f.sentence: The term "bioturbation" was later coined by Rudolf Richter in 1952 to describe structures in sediment caused by living organisms.

f29541acc3bf.title: Bioturbation
f29541acc3bf.sentence: Since the 1980s, the term "bioturbation" has been widely used in soil and geomorphology literature to describe the reworking of soil and sediment by plants and animals.

557fc2f4febf.title: Bioturbation
557fc2f4febf.sentence: Since its onset around 539 million years ago, bioturbation has been responsible for changes in ocean chemistry, primarily through nutrient cycling.

589ab2e17455.title: Bioturbation
589ab2e17455.sentence: Bioturbation is thought to have been an important co-factor of the Cambrian Explosion, during which most major animal phyla appeared in the fossil record over a short time.

7f924d748d66.title: Humus form
7f924d748d66.section: Humus forms in a changing world > Pollution
7f924d748d66.sentence: Consequently, when keystone species are affected, such as soil engineers (earthworms, termites, ants, enchytraeids, etc.), organic matter decomposes more slowly, bioturbation is reduced, and the humus form evolves toward mor.

91535c3d799e.title: Symbiosis
91535c3d799e.sentence: Symbiosis (pl.: symbioses) is any close and long-term biological interaction between two organisms of different species.

d0aa04608955.title: Symbiosis
d0aa04608955.sentence: In 1879, Heinrich Anton de Bary defined symbiosis as "the living together of unlike organisms".

ac6b9b6b2f76.title: Symbiosis
ac6b9b6b2f76.sentence: The term is sometimes more exclusively used in a restricted, mutualistic sense, where both symbionts contribute to each other's subsistence.

5dd28722a40d.title: Symbiosis
5dd28722a40d.sentence: It can be obligate, meaning that one or both of the organisms depend on each other for survival, or facultative, meaning that they can subsist independently.

2fb3475d2b07.title: Symbiosis
2fb3475d2b07.sentence: When one organism lives on the surface of another, such as head lice on humans, it is called ectosymbiosis; when one partner lives inside the tissues of another, such as Symbiodinium within coral, it is termed endosymbiosis.

f0ce9e22e38a.title: Symbiosis
f0ce9e22e38a.sentence: Examples include diverse microbiomes: rhizobia, nitrogen-fixing bacteria that live in root nodules on legume roots; actinomycetes, nitrogen-fixing bacteria such as Frankia, which live in alder root nodules; single-celled algae inside reef-building corals; and bacterial endosymbionts that provide essential nutrients to about 10%–15% of insects.

0eb955b75b74.title: Symbiosis
0eb955b75b74.sentence: An example of antagonism is Juglans nigra (black walnut), secreting juglone, a substance which destroys many herbaceous plants within its root zone.

e1b998082b9e.title: Fungus
e1b998082b9e.sentence: Most fungi grow as hyphae, which are cylindrical, thread-like structures 2–10 μm in diameter and up to several centimeters in length.

edbbac4ad4b2.title: Fungus
edbbac4ad4b2.sentence: Along with bacteria, fungi are the major decomposers in most terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems, and therefore play a critical role in biogeochemical cycles and in many food webs.

5904f50b95ba.title: Fungus
5904f50b95ba.sentence: Hyphae grow at their tips (apices); new hyphae are typically formed by emergence of new tips along existing hyphae by a process called branching, or occasionally growing hyphal tips fork, giving rise to two parallel-growing hyphae.

80ffd8df7c02.title: Fungus
80ffd8df7c02.sentence: The growth of fungi as hyphae on or in solid substrates or as single cells in aquatic environments is adapted for the efficient extraction of nutrients, because these growth forms have high surface area to volume ratios.

590db09ecd67.title: Fungus
590db09ecd67.sentence: Hyphae are specifically adapted for growth on solid surfaces, and to invade substrates and tissues.

5a5b7729f2b1.title: Fungus
5a5b7729f2b1.sentence: Although commonly included in botany curricula and textbooks, fungi are more closely related to animals than to plants, and are placed with the animals in the monophyletic group of opisthokonts.

41ad89ab45ba.title: Fungus
41ad89ab45ba.sentence: Before the introduction of molecular methods for phylogenetic analysis, taxonomists considered fungi to be members of the plant kingdom because of similarities in lifestyle: both fungi and plants are mainly immobile, and have similarities in general morphology and growth habit.

9dd0dd50a2d3.title: Fungus
9dd0dd50a2d3.sentence: Mycorrhizal symbiosis between plants and fungi is one of the most well-known plant–fungus associations and is of significant importance for plant growth and persistence in many ecosystems; over 90% of all plant species engage in mycorrhizal relationships with fungi and are dependent upon this relationship for survival.

1ddfa29c515a.title: Fungus
1ddfa29c515a.sentence: The mycorrhizal symbiosis is ancient, dating back to at least 400 million years.

395c8a6edd39.title: Fungus
395c8a6edd39.section: Ecology > Symbiosis > With algae and cyanobacteria
395c8a6edd39.sentence: Lichens are a symbiotic relationship between fungi and photosynthetic algae or cyanobacteria.

1d0a84d1008e.title: Fungus
1d0a84d1008e.sentence: Several groups of ants cultivate fungi in the order Chaetothyriales for several purposes: as a food source, as a structural component of their nests, and as a part of an ant/plant symbiosis in the domatia (tiny chambers in plants that house arthropods).

1f4ad5f6ec45.title: Fungus
1f4ad5f6ec45.sentence: Many fungi are parasites on plants, animals (including humans), and other fungi.

1b409c08b988.title: Fungus
1b409c08b988.sentence: Serious pathogens of many cultivated plants causing extensive damage and losses to agriculture and forestry include the rice blast fungus Magnaporthe oryzae, tree pathogens such as Ophiostoma ulmi and Ophiostoma novo-ulmi causing Dutch elm disease, Cryphonectria parasitica responsible for chestnut blight, and Phymatotrichopsis omnivora causing Texas root rot, and plant pathogens in the genera Fusarium, Ustilago, Alternaria, and Cochliobolus.

f40089e19dcc.title: Fungus
f40089e19dcc.sentence: As of 2019, nine major lineages have been identified: Opisthosporidia, Chytridiomycota, Neocallimastigomycota, Blastocladiomycota, Zoopagomycotina, Mucoromycota, Glomeromycota, Ascomycota, and Basidiomycota.

8a7056e4f4ec.title: Fungus
8a7056e4f4ec.sentence: It recognizes seven phyla, two of which—the Ascomycota and the Basidiomycota—are contained within a branch representing subkingdom Dikarya, the most species rich and familiar group, including all the mushrooms, most food-spoilage molds, most plant pathogenic fungi, and the beer, wine, and bread yeasts.

41065ada3e03.title: Soil microbiology
41065ada3e03.sentence: By contrast, healthy soil can increase fertility in multiple ways, including supplying nutrients such as nitrogen and protecting against pests and diseases, while reducing the need for water and other inputs.

77bfb10bd422.title: Soil microbiology
77bfb10bd422.sentence: Farming can destroy soil's rhizobiome (rhizospheric microbial ecosystem) by using soil amendments such as fertilizer and pesticide without compensating for their detrimental effects.

fd96005fdede.title: Soil microbiology
fd96005fdede.sentence: Almost all registered microbes are biopesticides (biocontrol, bioprotection agents), now comprising about 10% of the global pesticide market.

3fc2190c37c1.title: Soil microbiology
3fc2190c37c1.sentence: Some microbes have been marketed for decades, such as Trichoderma biofungicide fungi that suppress other, pathogenic fungi, and the caterpillar killer Bacillus thuringiensis.

3a6191dc1fc1.title: Soil microbiology
3a6191dc1fc1.sentence: Many strains that seemed promising in the lab often failed to prove effective in the field, because of soil, climate and ecosystem effects, leading companies to skip the lab phase and emphasize field tests.

6cc1be08f37c.title: Soil microbiology
6cc1be08f37c.sentence: Serenade stimulates a high initial B. subtilis density, but levels decrease because the bacteria lacks a defensible ecological niche.

c14c14b4efa8.title: Soil microbiology
c14c14b4efa8.sentence: One way to compensate is to use multiple collaborating strains.

48116327755e.title: Soil microbiology
48116327755e.sentence: In both the US and Europe, companies have to provide regulatory authorities with evidence that both the individual strains and the product as a whole are safe, leading many existing products to label themselves "biostimulants" instead of "biopesticides".

fdad0064f7d7.title: Soil microbiology
fdad0064f7d7.sentence: Fertilizers deplete soil of organic matter, some of them (e.g. triple superphosphate) carry noxious trace elements (e.g. arsenic, cadmium), cause salination and acidification when in excess of plant nitrogen requirements, and suppress mycorrhizae above some threshold level, in particular with phosphorus; they can also turn symbiotic bacteria into competitors.

b6f20d78fcdc.title: Microbial inoculant
b6f20d78fcdc.sentence: Microbial inoculants, also known as soil inoculants or bioinoculants, are agricultural amendments that use beneficial rhizosphericic or endophytic microbes to promote plant health.

95c0d9525c91.title: Microbial inoculant
95c0d9525c91.sentence: Many of the microbes involved form symbiotic relationships with the target crops where both parties benefit (mutualism).

aa337b565dfb.title: Microbial inoculant
aa337b565dfb.sentence: While microbial inoculants are applied to improve plant nutrition, they can also be used to promote plant growth by stimulating plant hormone production.

fac43f5463c5.title: Microbial inoculant
fac43f5463c5.sentence: The rhizobacteria commonly applied as inoculants include nitrogen-fixers, phosphate-solubilisers and other root-associated beneficial bacteria which enhance the availability of the macronutrients nitrogen and phosphorus to the host plant.

ad67821fbd30.title: Microbial inoculant
ad67821fbd30.sentence: Such bacteria are commonly referred to as plant growth promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR).

2225df8f7808.title: Microbial inoculant
2225df8f7808.sentence: The most commonly applied rhizobacteria are Rhizobium and closely related genera.

e36f2df6226c.title: Microbial inoculant
e36f2df6226c.sentence: Rhizobium are nitrogen-fixing bacteria that form symbiotic associations within nodules on the roots of legumes.

a38fd9d2c27a.title: Microbial inoculant
a38fd9d2c27a.sentence: Arbuscular mycorrhiza (AM) has received attention as a potential agriculture amendment for its ability to access and provide the host plant phosphorus.

a68f9557ff7a.title: Microbial inoculant
a68f9557ff7a.sentence: Under a reduced fertilization greenhouse system that was inoculated with a mixture of AM fungi and rhizobacteria, tomato yields that were given from 100% fertility were attained at 70% fertility.

c94e748e9951.title: Microbial inoculant
c94e748e9951.sentence: Microbial inoculants can induce systemic acquired resistance (SAR) of crop species to several common crop diseases (provides resistance against pathogens).

2965901344d0.title: Microbial inoculant
2965901344d0.sentence: So far SAR has been demonstrated for powdery mildew (Blumeria hordei, as Blumeria graminis f. sp. hordei, Heitefuss, 2001), take-all (Gaeumannomyces graminis var. tritici, Khaosaad et al., 2007), leaf spot (Pseudomonas syringae, Ramos Solano et al., 2008) and root rot (Fusarium culmorum, Waller et al. 2005).

0a7e19107de0.title: Microbial inoculant
0a7e19107de0.sentence: The main benefit from dual inoculation is increased plant nutrient uptake from both soil and fertilizer.

a1e4d4aa237e.title: Microbial inoculant
a1e4d4aa237e.sentence: Multiple strains of inoculant have also been demonstrated to increase total nitrogenase activity compared to single strains of inoculants, even when only one strain is diazotrophic.

9915a62cad93.title: Microbial inoculant
9915a62cad93.sentence: However, it is increasingly recognized that microbial inoculants often modify the soil microbial community (Mawarda et al., 2020).

48063d0d0843.title: Microbial inoculant
48063d0d0843.sentence: Additionally, recent research (2024) suggests that as few as one in nine commercial products are beneficial.

8c4e630b5fde.title: Microbial inoculant
8c4e630b5fde.sentence: Common problems are crop mortality, unlabeled fertilizers and non-viability (doa = dead on arrival.) A global study found mycorrhizal colonization to be less than 10% when commercial products are used meaning that a lot of the estimated 836 million USD spent annually on commercial inoculants could be better spent.

cedd29b05029.title: Rhizobacteria
cedd29b05029.sentence: Though microbial inoculants can be beneficial for crops, they are not widely used in industrial agriculture, as large-scale application techniques have yet to become economically viable.

51b03a11661d.title: Bioturbation
51b03a11661d.sentence: Terrestrial bioturbation is important in soil production, burial, organic matter content, and downslope transport.

7c016eb7eac8.title: Bioturbation
7c016eb7eac8.sentence: Tree roots are sources of soil organic matter, with root growth and stump decay also contributing to soil transport and mixing.

73f1d8ae9b91.title: Bioturbation
73f1d8ae9b91.sentence: Death and decay of tree roots first delivers organic matter to the soil and then creates voids, decreasing soil density.

7ba90e81a404.title: Bioturbation
7ba90e81a404.sentence: Tree uprooting causes considerable soil displacement by producing mounds, mixing the soil, or inverting vertical sections of soil.

d0f8120eb15c.title: Bioturbation
d0f8120eb15c.sentence: Burrowing animals, such as earth worms and small mammals, form passageways for air and water transport which changes the soil properties, such as the vertical particle-size distribution, soil porosity, and nutrient content.

8851677b3122.title: Bioturbation
8851677b3122.sentence: Invertebrates that burrow and consume plant detritus help produce an organic-rich topsoil known as the soil biomantle, and thus contribute to the formation of soil horizons.

47c03d48eb05.title: Bioturbation
47c03d48eb05.sentence: Small mammals such as pocket gophers also play an important role in the production of soil, possibly with an equal magnitude to abiotic processes.

1b0e7b88987f.title: Bioturbation
1b0e7b88987f.sentence: Pocket gophers form above-ground mounds, which moves soil from the lower soil horizons to the surface, exposing minimally weathered rock to surface erosion processes, speeding soil formation.

1e655aade88e.title: Bioturbation
1e655aade88e.sentence: Pocket gophers are thought to play an important role in the downslope transport of soil, as the soil that forms their mounds is more susceptible to erosion and subsequent transport.

90da8861a6a0.title: Bioturbation
90da8861a6a0.sentence: The formation of surface mounds also buries surface vegetation, creating nutrient hotspots when the vegetation decomposes, increasing soil organic matter.

3ec93aaee476.title: Bioturbation
3ec93aaee476.sentence: Similar to tree root effects, the construction of burrows-even when backfilled- decreases soil density.

036bdf0e9d26.title: Bacteria
036bdf0e9d26.sentence: Bacterial metabolism is classified into nutritional groups on the basis of three major criteria: the source of energy, the electron donors used, and the source of carbon used for growth.

96967d7aa730.title: Bacteria
96967d7aa730.sentence: Phototrophic bacteria derive energy from light using photosynthesis, while chemotrophic bacteria breaking down chemical compounds through oxidation.

1713f54dd2dd.title: Bacteria
1713f54dd2dd.sentence: Bacteria that derive electrons from inorganic compounds such as hydrogen, carbon monoxide, or ammonia are called lithotrophs, while those that use organic compounds are called organotrophs.

5f989762d9e4.title: Bacteria
5f989762d9e4.sentence: Many bacteria, called heterotrophs, derive their carbon from other organic carbon.

3baf63a25617.title: Bacteria
3baf63a25617.sentence: Others, such as cyanobacteria and some purple bacteria, are autotrophic, meaning they obtain cellular carbon by fixing carbon dioxide.

cfe01e02b1ff.title: Bacteria
cfe01e02b1ff.sentence: Still, more specifically, aerobic organisms use oxygen as the terminal electron acceptor, while anaerobic organisms use other compounds such as nitrate, sulfate, or carbon dioxide.

291577680ae7.title: Bacteria
291577680ae7.sentence: Facultative anaerobes can switch between fermentation and different terminal electron acceptors depending on the environmental conditions in which they find themselves.

178bd9d9f9e2.title: Lithotroph
178bd9d9f9e2.sentence: Lithotrophs are a diverse group of organisms using an inorganic substrate (usually of mineral origin) to obtain reducing equivalents for use in biosynthesis (e.g., carbon dioxide fixation) or energy conservation (i.e., ATP production) via aerobic or anaerobic respiration.

ed5e11f241f4.title: Lithotroph
ed5e11f241f4.sentence: The term "lithotroph" was created from the Greek terms 'lithos' (rock) and 'troph' (consumer), meaning "eaters of rock".

b7e6d87c8451.title: Lithotroph
b7e6d87c8451.sentence: The term was suggested in 1946 by Lwoff and collaborators.

f42b79c76b0f.title: Lithotroph
f42b79c76b0f.sentence: While lithotrophs in the broader sense include photolithotrophs like plants, chemolithotrophs are exclusively microorganisms; no known macrofauna possesses the ability to use inorganic compounds as electron sources.

f1ab0da9c42b.title: Lithotroph
f1ab0da9c42b.sentence: Chemolithotrophs belong to the domains Bacteria and Archaea.

a1e031504527.title: Lithotroph
a1e031504527.sentence: Different from a lithotroph is an organotroph, an organism which obtains its reducing agents from the catabolism of organic compounds.

f10f22ea2629.title: Lithotroph
f10f22ea2629.sentence: - Lithoautotrophs are able to use carbon dioxide from the air as a carbon source, the same way plants do.

ca93e6756371.title: Lithotroph
ca93e6756371.sentence: - Lithoheterotrophs do not have the ability to fix carbon dioxide and must consume additional organic compounds in order to break them apart and use their carbon.

0534dfb9d1b8.title: Lithotroph
0534dfb9d1b8.sentence: Only a few bacteria are fully lithoheterotrophic.

190ee89de5cc.title: Lithotroph
190ee89de5cc.sentence: - Mixotrophs will take up and use organic material to complement their carbon dioxide fixation source (mix between autotrophy and heterotrophy).

224d252e282d.title: Lithotroph
224d252e282d.sentence: Many lithotrophs are recognized as mixotrophic in regard to their C-metabolism.

decc30c3cceb.title: Lithotroph
decc30c3cceb.sentence: Lithotrophs may be present in a variety of environments, including deep terrestrial subsurfaces, soils, mines, and in endolith communities.

69170379adbc.title: Lithotroph
69170379adbc.sentence: Lithotrophs participate in many geological processes, such as the formation of soil and the biogeochemical cycling of carbon, nitrogen, and other elements.

cecc050600bf.title: Lithotroph
cecc050600bf.sentence: Lithotrophs play an important role in the biological aspect of the iron cycle.

e0e559c9320c.title: Lithotroph
e0e559c9320c.sentence: These organisms can use iron as either an electron donor, Fe(II) → Fe(III), or as an electron acceptor, Fe (III) → Fe(II).

29e2b53cd28e.title: Lithotroph
29e2b53cd28e.sentence: The last universal common ancestor of life is thought to be a chemolithotroph.

1d3581b5fac1.title: Microbiologically induced calcite precipitation
1d3581b5fac1.sentence: Microbiologically induced calcium carbonate precipitation (MICP) is a bio-geochemical process that induces calcium carbonate precipitation within the soil matrix.

68e5a8c80c11.title: Microbiologically induced calcite precipitation
68e5a8c80c11.sentence: The main groups of microorganisms that can induce the carbonate precipitation are photosynthetic microorganisms such as cyanobacteria and microalgae; sulfate-reducing bacteria; and some species of microorganisms involved in nitrogen cycle.

8d6f44133862.title: Microbiologically induced calcite precipitation
8d6f44133862.sentence: Several mechanisms have been identified by which bacteria can induce the calcium carbonate precipitation, including urea hydrolysis, denitrification, sulfate production, and iron reduction.

9c44b2c11c69.title: Microbiologically induced calcite precipitation
9c44b2c11c69.sentence: There are three autotrophic pathways, which all result in depletion of carbon dioxide and favouring calcium carbonate precipitation.

6a882038b720.title: Microbiologically induced calcite precipitation
6a882038b720.sentence: In heterotrophic pathway, two metabolic cycles can be involved: the nitrogen cycle and the sulfur cycle.

98861b1c66df.title: Microbiologically induced calcite precipitation
98861b1c66df.section: Metabolic pathways > Heterotrophic pathway > Ureolysis or degradation of urea
98861b1c66df.sentence: The microbial urease catalyzes the hydrolysis of urea into ammonium and carbonate.

8a52b1335dfc.title: Microbiologically induced calcite precipitation
8a52b1335dfc.section: Metabolic pathways > Heterotrophic pathway > Ureolysis or degradation of urea
8a52b1335dfc.sentence: The production of hydroxide ions results in the increase of pH, which in turn can shift the bicarbonate equilibrium, resulting in the formation of carbonate ions (5)

73e5202e6406.title: Microbiologically induced calcite precipitation
73e5202e6406.section: Metabolic pathways > Heterotrophic pathway > Ureolysis or degradation of urea
73e5202e6406.sentence: The produced carbonate ions precipitate in the presence of calcium ions as calcium carbonate crystals (6).

535756de0e5d.title: Microbiologically induced calcite precipitation
535756de0e5d.section: Metabolic pathways > Heterotrophic pathway > Ureolysis or degradation of urea
535756de0e5d.sentence: The formation of a monolayer of calcite further increases the affinity of the bacteria to the soil surface, resulting in the production of multiple layers of calcite.

e2026467f950.title: Microbiologically induced calcite precipitation
e2026467f950.sentence: Calcium carbonate can be precipitated in three polymorphic forms, which in the order of their usual stabilities are calcite, aragonite and vaterite.

45a529048712.title: Microbiologically induced calcite precipitation
45a529048712.sentence: Biomineralization in the form of calcium carbonate precipitation can be traced back to the Precambrian period.

60ee8f7b263b.title: Microbiologically induced calcite precipitation
60ee8f7b263b.sentence: Several applications of this process have been proposed, such as remediation of cracks and corrosion prevention in concrete, biogrout, sequestration of radionuclides and heavy metals.

eb03317499e8.title: Microbiologically induced calcite precipitation
eb03317499e8.section: Possible applications > Remediation for heavy metal and radionuclide contamination
eb03317499e8.sentence: Microbially induced calcium carbonate precipitation of radionuclide and contaminant metals into calcite is a competitive co-precipitation reaction in which suitable divalent cations are incorporated into the calcite lattice.

b962dda8f314.title: Microbiologically induced calcite precipitation
b962dda8f314.section: Possible applications > Remediation for heavy metal and radionuclide contamination
b962dda8f314.sentence: The availability of lead in soil may reduced by its chelation with the MICP product, which is the mechanism responsible for lead immobilization.

95ae05e6eba2.title: Lithotroph
95ae05e6eba2.sentence: The term "chemolithotrophy" refers to a cell's acquisition of energy from the oxidation of inorganic compounds, also known as electron donors.

be8b6c961b59.title: Lithotroph
be8b6c961b59.sentence: A chemolithotroph is able to use inorganic reduced compounds in its energy-producing reactions.

de891675601b.title: Lithotroph
de891675601b.sentence: This group of organisms includes sulfur oxidizers, nitrifying bacteria, iron oxidizers, and hydrogen oxidizers.

f357db68c316.title: Lithotroph
f357db68c316.sentence: This process involves the oxidation of inorganic compounds coupled to ATP synthesis.

9b50a4c108cf.title: Lithotroph
9b50a4c108cf.section: Biochemistry > Chemolithotrophs > Overview of the metabolic process
9b50a4c108cf.sentence: In chemolithotrophs, the compounds – the electron donors – are oxidized in the cell, and the electrons are channeled into respiratory chains, ultimately producing ATP.

608c508362c8.title: Lithotroph
608c508362c8.sentence: The majority of chemolithotrophs are chemolithoautotrophs, able to fix carbon dioxide (CO2) through various metabolic pathways such as the Calvin cycle, a metabolic pathway in which CO2 is converted to glucose.

183f4d03b732.title: Lithotroph
183f4d03b732.sentence: The majority of lithotrophs fix carbon dioxide through the Calvin cycle, an energetically expensive process.

df710a542a28.title: Lithotroph
df710a542a28.section: Biochemistry > Chemolithotrophs > Overview of the metabolic process
df710a542a28.sentence: Nitrosifying bacteria | Nitrosomonas | NH 3 (ammonia) + 2H 2 O → NO − 2 (nitrite) + 7H + + 6e − | O 2 (oxygen) + 4H + + 4e − → 2H 2 O

a1fdf9e03b1b.title: Lithotroph
