a1fdf9e03b1b.section: Biochemistry > Chemolithotrophs > Overview of the metabolic process
a1fdf9e03b1b.sentence: Aerobic bacteria such as the nitrifying bacteria, Nitrobacter, use oxygen to oxidize nitrite to nitrate.

31d32af51f23.title: Lithotroph
31d32af51f23.section: Biochemistry > Chemolithotrophs > Overview of the metabolic process
31d32af51f23.sentence: The electron acceptor can be oxygen (in aerobic bacteria), but a variety of other electron acceptors, organic and inorganic, are also used by various species.

7bf1f20d4b6f.title: Lithotroph
7bf1f20d4b6f.section: Biochemistry > Chemolithotrophs > Overview of the metabolic process
7bf1f20d4b6f.sentence: Here are a few examples of chemolithotrophic pathways, any of which may use oxygen or nitrate as electron acceptors:

de2287d9a8c3.title: Lithotroph
de2287d9a8c3.section: Biochemistry > Chemolithotrophs > Overview of the metabolic process
de2287d9a8c3.sentence: The chemolithotrophs that are best documented are aerobes, though the list of these microorganisms that employ anaerobic respiration is growing.

657287a34af2.title: Lithotroph
657287a34af2.sentence: For example, the oxidation of hydrogen sulfide to elemental sulfur by ½O2 produces far less energy (50 kcal/mol or 210 kJ/mol) than the oxidation of elemental sulfur to sulfate (150 kcal/mol or 627 kJ/mol) by 3/2 O2.

e4e148508b39.title: Lithotroph
e4e148508b39.sentence: For some low-energy substrates, such as ferrous iron, the cells must cull through large amounts of inorganic substrate to secure just a small amount of energy.

393a69b88107.title: Lithotroph
393a69b88107.sentence: This makes their metabolic process inefficient in many places and hinders them from thriving.

ce16d4507f8e.title: Lithotroph
ce16d4507f8e.section: Biochemistry > Chemolithotrophs > Overview of the metabolic process
ce16d4507f8e.sentence: Plants use energy from sunlight to drive carbon dioxide fixation, but chemosynthesis can take place in the absence of sunlight (e.g., around a hydrothermal vent).

c78bef2812e5.title: Lithotroph
c78bef2812e5.sentence: Certain chemolithoautotrophic bacteria can also produce organic carbon, some even in the absence of light.

64420f3b55e1.title: Lithotroph
64420f3b55e1.sentence: Although they are sensitive to certain factors such as the quality of inorganic substrate, they are able to thrive under some of the most inhospitable conditions in the world, such as temperatures above 110 degrees Celsius and below 2 pH.

ea201d818427.title: Lithotroph
ea201d818427.sentence: This form of metabolism is believed to occur only in prokaryotes and was first characterized by Ukrainian microbiologist Sergei Winogradsky.

01c2956af07d.title: Sergei Winogradsky
01c2956af07d.sentence: Winogradsky discovered the first known form of lithotrophy during his research with Beggiatoa in 1887.

8b4badd71b64.title: Soil biodiversity
8b4badd71b64.sentence: This includes practices that influence soil volume, structure, biological, and chemical characteristics, and whether soil exhibits adverse effects such as reduced fertility, soil acidification, or salinisation.

ea42b53c81a4.title: Soil biodiversity
ea42b53c81a4.sentence: Soil erosion is, therefore, a major threat to soil biodiversity.

1d5ee204b8a4.title: Soil biodiversity
1d5ee204b8a4.sentence: A study in the Netherlands examined the correlation between soil pH and soil biodiversity in soils with pH below 5.

6e2affc1c337.title: Soil biodiversity
6e2affc1c337.sentence: A strong correlation was discovered, wherein the lower the pH the lower the biodiversity.

adf2bcfb74b2.title: Soil biodiversity
adf2bcfb74b2.sentence: The results were the same in grasslands as well as heathlands.

52f3b038878a.title: Soil biodiversity
52f3b038878a.sentence: It reduces the numbers of most macrofauna, including, for example, earthworm numbers (important in maintaining structural quality of the topsoil for plant growth).

2db04918290b.title: Soil biodiversity
2db04918290b.sentence: Also affected is rhizobium survival and persistence.

7ff987738208.title: Soil biodiversity
7ff987738208.sentence: Decomposition and nitrogen fixation may be reduced, which affects the survival of native vegetation.

220826ef1125.title: Soil biodiversity
220826ef1125.sentence: At low soil salinity, there is a lot of microbial activity, that results in an increase in soil respiration, which increases the carbon dioxide levels in the soil, producing a healthier environment for plants.

a2321084a132.title: Soil biodiversity
a2321084a132.sentence: As the salinity of the soil rises, there is more stress on microbes because there is less available water available to them, leading to less respiration.

8572fd9d7543.title: Soil biodiversity
8572fd9d7543.sentence: If the concentration occurs repeatedly, the soil becomes cement-like, with little or no structure.

fea30c7b1377.title: Soil biodiversity
fea30c7b1377.sentence: Extended exposure to high sodium levels results in a decrease in the amount of water retained and able to flow through the soil and a decrease in decomposition rates (this leaves the soil infertile and prohibits any future growth).

bd3274088ea1.title: Soil biodiversity
bd3274088ea1.sentence: But soil erosion leads to a loss of topsoil, organic matter, and nutrients; it breaks down soil structure and decreases water storage capacity, reducing fertility and water availability to plant roots.

cd235c634d21.title: Soil biodiversity
cd235c634d21.sentence: Still, the constant tilling of crops has caused the SOM to shift and redistribute, causing soil structure to deteriorate and altering soil organism populations (such as with earthworms).

790b6ef2f90c.title: Soil biodiversity
790b6ef2f90c.sentence: The use of KCl leads to high concentrations of chloride (Clˉ) in soil which cause increase in soil salinity affecting the development of plants and soil organisms.

5e366ec0e13b.title: Soil biodiversity
5e366ec0e13b.sentence: Chloride has a biocidal effect on the soil ecosystem, causing negative effects on the growth, mortality, and reproduction of organisms, which in turn jeopardizes soil biodiversity.

7b3a1e2ffa4d.title: Soil biodiversity
7b3a1e2ffa4d.sentence: In addition, this ion negatively affects nitrifying microorganisms, thus affecting nutrient availability in the soil.

aa015f360f6f.title: Hypha
aa015f360f6f.sentence: A hypha (from Ancient Greek ὑφή (huphḗ) 'web'; pl. hyphae) is a long, branching, filamentous structure of a fungus, oomycete, or actinobacterium.

1f875a1f021e.title: Hypha
1f875a1f021e.sentence: In most fungi, hyphae are the main mode of vegetative growth, and are collectively called a mycelium.

d8aa21c9d0d5.title: Hypha
d8aa21c9d0d5.sentence: A hypha consists of one or more cells surrounded by a tubular cell wall.

fe78b38b5acc.title: Hypha
fe78b38b5acc.sentence: The major structural polymer in fungal cell walls is typically chitin, in contrast to plants and oomycetes that have cellulosic cell walls.

8dad8a4a5ccc.title: Hypha
8dad8a4a5ccc.sentence: In most fungi, hyphae are divided into cells by internal cross-walls called "septa" (singular: septum).

270eaa528b62.title: Hypha
270eaa528b62.sentence: Septa are usually perforated by pores large enough for ribosomes, mitochondria, and sometimes nuclei to flow between cells.

0952f4b39948.title: Hypha
0952f4b39948.sentence: Hyphae have an average diameter of 4–6 μm.

6de61e6f83d1.title: Hypha
6de61e6f83d1.sentence: Many groups of fungi produce hyphae, and some form vast networks of mycelium; arbuscular mycorrhizal fungal hyphae alone have been estimated to extend approximately 110 quadrillion kilometres through Earth's topsoils.

2511f07ad3e7.title: Hypha
2511f07ad3e7.sentence: The arbuscules of mutualistic mycorrhizal fungi serve a similar function in nutrient exchange, so are important in assisting nutrient and water absorption by plants.

71f76a1393fb.title: Hypha
71f76a1393fb.sentence: Mycelial cords can be formed to transfer nutrients over larger distances.

4dee1a1f729b.title: Mycelium
4dee1a1f729b.sentence: Mycelium (pl.: mycelia) is a root-like structure of a fungus consisting of a mass of branching, thread-like hyphae.

c917dacf30d1.title: Mycelium
c917dacf30d1.sentence: Fungal colonies composed of mycelium are found in and on soil and many other substrates.

dbd35532c768.title: Mycelium
dbd35532c768.sentence: Mycelium may be minute, forming a colony that is too small to see, or may grow to span thousands of acres as in Armillaria.

0d653273570f.title: Mycelium
0d653273570f.sentence: It does this in a two-stage process.

86a764dafe27.title: Mycelium
86a764dafe27.sentence: First, the hyphae secrete enzymes onto or into the food source, which break down biological polymers into smaller units such as monomers.

48fd6279c73d.title: Mycelium
48fd6279c73d.sentence: These monomers are then absorbed into the mycelium by facilitated diffusion and active transport.

81d33c4a0f7f.title: Mycelium
81d33c4a0f7f.sentence: Mycelia are vital in terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems for their role in the decomposition of plant material.

340898bc8f98.title: Mycelium
340898bc8f98.sentence: They contribute to the organic fraction of soil, and their growth releases carbon dioxide back into the atmosphere (see carbon cycle).

d1da55640171.title: Mycelium
d1da55640171.sentence: Mycelial networks constitute 20-30% of soil biomass, though traditional biomass measures fail to detect them.

880b335dda5e.title: Mycelium
880b335dda5e.sentence: Ectomycorrhizal extramatrical mycelium, as well as the mycelium of arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi, increase the efficiency of water and nutrient absorption of most plants and confers resistance to some plant pathogens.

198e4039f913.title: Mycelium
198e4039f913.sentence: By some estimates, mycelial networks receive well over 10% of the photosynthesis output of their host plants.

5439bc5d7760.title: Mycelium
5439bc5d7760.sentence: Mycelium is an important food source for many soil invertebrates.

723d53dc3b59.title: Mycelium
723d53dc3b59.sentence: Fungi are essential for converting biomass into compost, as they decompose feedstock components such as lignin, which many other composting microorganisms cannot.

1f0367c3c7ea.title: Mycelium
1f0367c3c7ea.sentence: Petroleum products and some pesticides (typical soil contaminants) are organic molecules (i.e., they are built on a carbon structure), and thereby show a potential carbon source for fungi.

5317002402c6.title: Mycelium
5317002402c6.sentence: Hence, fungi have the potential to eradicate such pollutants from their environment unless the chemicals prove toxic to the fungus.

b3df29ef2460.title: Mycelium
b3df29ef2460.sentence: This biological degradation is a process known as mycoremediation.

7520726fe8f0.title: Mycelium
7520726fe8f0.sentence: When spread on logging roads, mycelium can act as a binder, holding disturbed new soil in place, thus preventing washouts until woody plants can establish roots.

ae73f5dbacac.title: Thatch (lawn)
ae73f5dbacac.sentence: In lawn care, thatch is a layer of organic matter that accumulates on a lawn around the base of the grass plants.

af978630cb60.title: Thatch (lawn)
af978630cb60.sentence: Thatch is a combination of living and dead plant matter including crowns, stolons, rhizomes, and roots.

395c64b26acf.title: Thatch (lawn)
395c64b26acf.sentence: Thatch is composed of about 25% lignin, a complex organic polymer that is highly resistant to decomposition.

117935d5e96b.title: Thatch (lawn)
117935d5e96b.sentence: Grass clippings do not generally contribute to thatch buildup as they can be easily broken down by soil microorganisms.

7ffe8ce4ca0d.title: Thatch (lawn)
7ffe8ce4ca0d.sentence: - Acidic soils may not be able to support sufficient populations of decomposing microorganisms

d41cb67e4e14.title: Thatch (lawn)
d41cb67e4e14.sentence: - Application of insecticides may reduce earthworm activity, leading to decreased bioturbation

9dfb6cec9a02.title: Thatch (lawn)
9dfb6cec9a02.sentence: - Over-application of nitrogen fertilizers can stimulate excess growth as well as contribute to soil acidity

2b31f97960da.title: Thatch (lawn)
2b31f97960da.sentence: A small amount of thatch may provide a beneficial insulating effect against fluctuations in temperature and moisture.

dab402bfba8d.title: Thatch (lawn)
dab402bfba8d.sentence: However, excessive thatch can cause root problems and lawn mower difficulties.

b461f4c6ba44.title: Thatch (lawn)
b461f4c6ba44.sentence: A dethatcher may be used to remove thatch from a lawn.

1fbceb7d94b1.title: Soil-borne pathogen
1fbceb7d94b1.sentence: A soil-borne pathogen (or soilborne pathogen) is a disease-causing agent which lives both in soil and in a plant host, and which will tend to infect undiseased plants which are grown in that soil.

fcc307f29795.title: Soil-borne pathogen
fcc307f29795.sentence: Common soil borne pathogens include Fusarium, Pythium, Rhizoctonia, Phytophthora, Verticillium, Rhizopus, Thielaviopsis, and nematodes including Meloidogyne.

a6be11eb5099.title: Laimosphere
a6be11eb5099.sentence: Propagules of soil-borne plant pathogens, whose germination is stimulated by a plant exudates in the laimosphere, can initiate hypocotyl and stem rots leading to "damping-off".

e61509bbf6f4.title: Fallow
e61509bbf6f4.sentence: The goal of fallowing is to allow the land to recover and store organic matter while retaining moisture and disrupting pest life cycles and soil-borne pathogens by temporarily removing their hosts.

74bf04ed0d6c.title: Soil solarization
74bf04ed0d6c.sentence: Soil solarization is a non-chemical environmentally friendly method for controlling pests using solar power to increase the soil temperature to levels at which many soil-borne plant pathogens will be killed or greatly weakened.

8a0642348433.title: Disease suppressive soils
8a0642348433.sentence: Recent research has demonstrated that disease-suppressive soils not only inhibit soilborne pathogens but also protect plants from insect pests.

96965ecc2301.title: Mycorrhiza
96965ecc2301.section: Function > Disease, drought and salinity resistance and its correlation to mycorrhizae
96965ecc2301.sentence: Mycorrhizal plants are often more resistant to diseases, such as those caused by microbial soil-borne pathogens.

a2f884d1db1b.title: Compost
a2f884d1db1b.section: Uses > Agriculture and gardening > Compost tea
a2f884d1db1b.sentence: They have also been shown to have a suppressive effect on plant pathogens and soil-borne diseases.

0bd28b9ae6f2.title: Hydroponics
0bd28b9ae6f2.sentence: Since hydroponics uses substrates instead of soil as the base for root growth, soil-borne diseases and pests are eliminated.

abd270cf7b01.title: Soil animals
abd270cf7b01.sentence: Soil macrofauna are invertebrates between 2 mm and 2 cm in size, which live in the soil or in leaf litter.

623b6a0590c7.title: Soil biology
623b6a0590c7.sentence: - Macrofauna: size range – 2 to 20 mm, e.g. woodlice, earthworms, beetles, millipedes, slugs, snails, ants, and harvestmen.

df0a905821f0.title: Soil animals
df0a905821f0.sentence: Known as soil engineers, earthworms, termites, ants, some millipedes (e.g. Polydesmida) and some insect larvae (e.g. tenebrionids), can make the pore spaces and hence can change the soil structure, one important aspect of soil morphology.

36ba2997802a.title: Soil animals
36ba2997802a.sentence: Macrofauna feed on leaf litter (e.g. millipedes, woodlice, slugs, snails, tipulid larvae, epigeic and anecic (e.g. Lumbricus terrestris) earthworms), wood (e.g. lower termites, xylophagous beetles), humus (e.g. endogeic earthworms, higher termites), roots (e.g. elaterid larvae) or animal prey (e.g. centipedes, spiders, harvestmen, carabids), flatworms).

f89277a8049e.title: Soil animals
f89277a8049e.sentence: Litter- and soil-feeding macrofauna contribute to litter and organic matter decomposition by comminuting plant remains and stimulating microbial activity of ingested soil, the so-called 'Sleeping beauty' paradigm, with the dormant bacteria as 'Sleeping Beauty' and the earthworm as 'Prince Charming'.

683ef0a3c613.title: Soil animals
683ef0a3c613.sentence: Enzymes of symbiotic gut microflora are necessary requirements of digestive capacities of saprophagous macrofauna, in particular those able to digest wood or soil organic matter.

14625ad89f89.title: Soil animals
14625ad89f89.sentence: In lower termites, symbiotic flagellates add their contribution to the digestion of lignocellulose in wood.

edc85ba3e28e.title: Soil animals
edc85ba3e28e.sentence: Ingested plant or soil material is finely ground in earthworm gizzards and finely chewed by termite mandibles and mixed with saliva, giving their faeces a pasty appearance, further hardened by drought as seen in the formation of stable structures such as earthworm casts and termite mounds.

793712e3ba35.title: Soil animals
793712e3ba35.sentence: By their size, their activity and abundance in the more fertile soils they condition the existence of various soil organisms and are typical of mull humus, harbouring a wide variety of trophic niches and more complex foodwebs.

5a45dd13dcfa.title: Soil animals
5a45dd13dcfa.sentence: Being more exacting in nutrients than smaller organisms, because of their accumulation of calcium and nitrogen in thick chitinous arthropod exoskeletons and mollusc shells, and the active secretion of nutrient-rich mucus by earthworms and molluscs, soil macroinvertebrates need a plant cover able to redistribute nutrients in the soil through fast leaf and root litter decomposition.

9c305ba2692f.title: Soil animals
9c305ba2692f.sentence: In turn, by favouring decomposer activity and nutrient cycling, macrofauna favours the growth of nutrient-exacting plant species, a positive aboveground-belowground feed-back which has been suggested to be a win-win evolutionarily stable strategy at the scale of the ecosystem in biomes with biologically favourable (not too cold, not too dry) climate and weatherable minerals in the parent rock.

d2dccc16e240.title: Termite
d2dccc16e240.sentence: Termites are a group of eusocial insects which consume a variety of decaying plant material, generally in the form of wood, leaf litter, and soil humus.

2f13b5beba90.title: Termite
2f13b5beba90.sentence: They are important decomposers of decaying plant matter in the subtropical and tropical regions of the world, and their recycling of wood and plant matter is of considerable ecological importance.

9e33ba474316.title: Termite
9e33ba474316.sentence: Many species are ecosystem engineers capable of altering many soil properties such as hydrology, decomposition, nutrient cycling, plant growth, and consequently surrounding biodiversity through the large mounds constructed by certain species.

d494a1534945.title: Termite
d494a1534945.sentence: Termites are primarily detritivores, consuming dead plants at any level of decomposition.

4305982c3163.title: Termite
4305982c3163.sentence: Meanwhile, the higher termites consume a wide variety of materials, including faeces, humus, grass, leaves and roots.

a941227e8d00.title: Termite
a941227e8d00.sentence: Of the 3,014 extant termite species currently classified, 754 are found in Africa, where mounds are extremely abundant in savannas, as islands of soil fertility.

74b1acdcbe95.title: Termite
74b1acdcbe95.sentence: Approximately 1.1 million active termite mounds can be found in the northern Kruger National Park alone.

c780e0257fdf.title: Termite
c780e0257fdf.sentence: Nests can be broadly separated into three main categories: hypogeal, i.e subterranean (completely below ground), epigeal (protruding above the soil surface), and arboreal (built above ground, but always connected to the ground via shelter tubes).

4c25c7e05bc9.title: Termite
4c25c7e05bc9.sentence: Most termites construct underground colonies rather than multifunctional nests and mounds.

0fb9ec461f71.title: Termite
0fb9ec461f71.sentence: Other building materials include partly digested plant material, used in carton nests (arboreal nests built from faecal elements and wood), and soil, used in subterranean nest and mound construction.

a74381507515.title: Fungivore
a74381507515.sentence: Around 330 species of termites in twelve genera of the subfamily Macrotermitinae cultivate a specialised fungus in the genus Termitomyces.

71f6762d351d.title: Fungivore
71f6762d351d.sentence: The fungus is kept in a specialised part of the nest in fungus cones.

22f49e5386d8.title: Fungivore
22f49e5386d8.sentence: Worker termites eat plant matter, producing faecal pellets which they continuously place on top of the cone.

654dae09a5ea.title: Termite
654dae09a5ea.section: Behaviour and ecology > Relationship with the environment
654dae09a5ea.sentence: The termite assemblages were considerably different among sites, with a conspicuous reduction in both diversity and abundance with increased disturbance, related to the reduction of tree density and soil cover, and with the intensity of trampling by cattle and goats.

bfda8637ecc5.title: Soil animals
bfda8637ecc5.sentence: Soil mesofauna are invertebrates between 0.2 mm and 2 mm in size, which live in the soil or in a leaf litter layer on the soil surface.

eeedfa0254e8.title: Soil animals
eeedfa0254e8.sentence: Members of this group include microarthropods (mites, springtails (collembola), proturans, diplurans, pseudoscorpions, symphyla, pauropods), and enchytraeids (potworms).

a9087019bead.title: Soil animals
a9087019bead.sentence: Soil mesofauna feed on a wide range of materials including other soil animals, microorganisms (bacteria, archaea, fungi, algae), live or decaying plant material, lichens, spores, and pollen.

2b846b19b570.title: Soil animals
2b846b19b570.sentence: By their intense consumption of plant remains (detritophagy) and microorganisms (microbivory) they play an important part in the carbon cycle and by their sensitivity to environmental hazards they are likely to be adversely affected by climate and land use change, and agricultural intensification.

e5b0fe0ed284.title: Soil animals
e5b0fe0ed284.sentence: Contrary to enchytraeids, soil microarthropods do not have the ability to reshape the soil and, therefore, are forced to use the existing macropore network for their locomotion and access to food resources.

396c7c296973.title: Soil animals
396c7c296973.sentence: This makes them highly sensitive to soil compaction, as it occurs under the influence of agricultural and sylvicultural intensification.

3925d221f43b.title: Soil animals
3925d221f43b.sentence: Fungal hyphae and spores are actively consumed by microarthropods and enchytraeids, giving them a prominent place in the regulation of fungal communities, including mycorrhizal fungi.

e25e2beba33e.title: Soil animals
e25e2beba33e.sentence: Fungal-feeding mesofauna play both a positive (through dissemination of spores and hyphal fragments) and a negative role (through severing connections) in mycorrhization and more generally in the development of soil fungal colonies and their ecosystem services (e.g. decomposition).

3e4ebd1471c0.title: Soil animals
3e4ebd1471c0.sentence: Predatory species (e. g. mesostimatid mites, pseudoscorpions) eat mainly on springtails, which are also submitted to an active predation from macrofauna (e. g. centipedes, ground beetles, spiders), making springtails, with their high reproductive rate and large populations, a pivotal component of soil food webs, mediating indirect effects of predation on soil ecosystem services.

21961f9cc316.title: Soil animals
21961f9cc316.sentence: The fecal material of soil macrofauna (e. g. earthworm casts) is eaten and broken down by mesofauna.

9237b89bbc18.title: Soil animals
9237b89bbc18.sentence: Earthworm casts are pulverized by enchytraeids eating on them, exemplifying the dynamic nature of soil aggregates and suggesting some kind of competition between two co-occurring ecosystem engineers of quite different size..

bb4dbce345b6.title: Soil animals
bb4dbce345b6.sentence: Environmental heterogeneity is often reflected in the species composition of mesofaunal communities, making these animals good bioindicators of soil quality.

4e86c8a926d1.title: Springtail
4e86c8a926d1.sentence: Springtails (class Collembola) form the largest of the three lineages of modern hexapods that are no longer considered insects, the others being Protura and Diplura.

47de8eef948b.title: Springtail
47de8eef948b.sentence: Springtails are omnivorous, free-living organisms that prefer moist conditions.

5f8451b48da7.title: Springtail
5f8451b48da7.sentence: In sheer numbers, they are reputed to be one of the most abundant of all macroscopic animals, with estimates of 100,000 individuals per square meter of ground, essentially everywhere on Earth where soil and related habitats (e.g. moss cushions, fallen wood, grass tufts, ant and termite nests) occur.

c95c22e09d28.title: Springtail
c95c22e09d28.sentence: There are more than 9,000 species worldwide.

22ce0038ffa2.title: Springtail
22ce0038ffa2.sentence: They do not directly engage in the decomposition of organic matter, but contribute to it indirectly through the fragmentation of organic matter and the control of soil microbial communities.

1048af07380d.title: Springtail
1048af07380d.sentence: Herbivorous and detritivorous species fragment biological material present in soil and leaf litter, supporting decomposition and increasing the availability of nutrients for plants and various species of microbes and fungi.

55e10af43dc5.title: Springtail
55e10af43dc5.sentence: Springtails are cryptozoa frequently found in leaf litter and other decaying material, where they are primarily detritivores and microbivores, and one of the main biological agents responsible for the control and the dissemination of soil microorganisms.

b205ae85e274.title: Springtail
b205ae85e274.sentence: Springtails commonly consume fungal hyphae and spores, but also have been found to consume plant material and pollen, animal remains, colloidal materials, minerals and bacteria.

c0165522917c.title: Springtail
c0165522917c.sentence: Streptomyces actinobacteria produce geosmin which attracts some species of springtails which feed on and spread their spores.

18a99a2969d8.title: Springtail
18a99a2969d8.sentence: In a mature deciduous woodland in temperate climate, leaf litter and vegetation typically support 30 to 40 species of springtails, and in the tropics the number may be over 100.

b688a80d0fd4.title: Springtail
b688a80d0fd4.sentence: The main ecological factor driving the local distribution of species is the vertical stratification of the ecosystem: in woodland a continuous change in species assemblages can be observed from tree canopies to ground vegetation then to plant litter down to deeper soil horizons.

c222a95f6329.title: Springtail
c222a95f6329.sentence: The horizontal distribution of springtail species is affected by environmental factors which act at the landscape scale, such as soil acidity, moisture and light.

7d8322322b3b.title: Springtail
7d8322322b3b.sentence: As a group, springtails are highly sensitive to desiccation, because of their tegumentary respiration, although some species with thin, permeable cuticles have been shown to resist severe drought by regulating the osmotic pressure of their body fluid.

b324be04fc0c.title: Springtail
b324be04fc0c.sentence: Springtails are consumed by mesostigmatan mites in various families, including Ascidae, Laelapidae, Parasitidae, Rhodacaridae and Veigaiidae.

ef8d53c0ab72.title: Springtail
ef8d53c0ab72.sentence: Predators also include various soil centipedes.

b63e6b7379db.title: Springtail
b63e6b7379db.sentence: Jumping, using the furcula as a spring, is the most common way to avoid predation, but jump escape cannot be performed easily in concealed environments such as litter, and more especially soil layers.

8e209ae26ac2.title: Springtail
8e209ae26ac2.sentence: Acute and chronic toxicity tests have been performed by researchers, mostly using the parthenogenetic isotomid Folsomia candida.

476c102d12e4.title: Springtail
476c102d12e4.sentence: Contrary to earthworms, but see and like many insects and molluscs, Collembola are very sensitive to herbicides.

7f12041dff1e.title: Springtail
7f12041dff1e.sentence: Collembola have been found to be useful as bio-indicators of soil quality.

c2ac51446e1c.title: Springtail
c2ac51446e1c.sentence: In managed turfgrass and urban lawn ecosystems, Collembola function as "thatch busters", playing a significant role in the decomposition of thatch, i.e. the layer of living and dead organic matter between the green vegetation and the soil surface.

20643dc13302.title: Enchytraeidae
20643dc13302.sentence: Enchytraeidae is a family of microdrile oligochaetes.

773ce680a900.title: Enchytraeidae
773ce680a900.sentence: They resemble small earthworms and include both terrestrial species known as potworms that live in highly organic terrestrial environments, as well as some that are marine.

aba42a3ebade.title: Enchytraeidae
aba42a3ebade.sentence: More than 700 species in about 30 genera have been described worldwide, although the true diversity of the family is thought to be much higher.

f65d98a54882.title: Enchytraeidae
f65d98a54882.sentence: Most species are small, whitish or transparent worms only a few millimetres long that feed on decaying organic matter and the microorganisms colonizing it, making them important contributors to decomposition and nutrient cycling in soils.

35090bc837df.title: Enchytraeidae
35090bc837df.sentence: Enchytraeids have been shown to feed on earthworm excrements (earthworm casts) which they pulverize and transform into fluffy masses of their own excrements (enchytraeid faeces), which form the bulk of Moder humus OH horizons.

89a460166e25.title: Enchytraeidae
89a460166e25.sentence: Enchytraeids are less sensitive than earthworms to agricultural intensification and replace them in soils with heavy pesticide use.

96dfe772d86c.title: Enchytraeidae
96dfe772d86c.sentence: Enchytraeids are now commonly used in ecotoxicity tests such as the enchytraeid reproduction test (ERT) guideline ISO 16387.

debe2e99b7d4.title: Soil microbiology
debe2e99b7d4.sentence: Myxomycetes (slime molds) and myxobacteria (slime bacteria) are among the most mysterious soil microorganisms.

08e6a8974ef4.title: Soil microbiology
08e6a8974ef4.sentence: Myxomycetes are eukaryotes, having nuclei and other cell organelles, while myxobacteria are prokaryotes, having their cellular components not enclosed in membranes, like bacteria (the domain to which myxobacteria pertain) and archaea.

b99e4b95690c.title: Soil microbiology
b99e4b95690c.sentence: Both are unicellular organisms forming syncytia for myxomycetes or swarms containing many cells kept together by intercellular molecular signals for myxobacteria.

eac6c9df1b4e.title: Soil microbiology
eac6c9df1b4e.sentence: These collective microorganisms are able to glide for foraging in a coordinated ('intelligent') manner, a complex phenomenon still largely unexplored.

2bb0ea0e1276.title: Soil microbiology
2bb0ea0e1276.sentence: Both groups sporulate (myxospores), forming fruiting bodies which can take different shapes and colors according to species, often iridescent and conspicuous.

9ac9b15427c7.title: Soil microbiology
9ac9b15427c7.sentence: Myxomycetes can make complex nutritional decisions, despite lacking a coordination center and comprising only a single vast multinucleate cell.

878485329adb.title: Soil microbiology
878485329adb.sentence: Algae can make their own carbon through photosynthesis, i.e. are autotrophs.

265eb6d61855.title: Soil microbiology
265eb6d61855.sentence: For algae to grow, they must be exposed to light because photosynthesis requires light, so soil algae are typically distributed evenly wherever sunlight and moderate moisture is available, and not far from the surface.

591cee351fc4.title: Soil microbiology
591cee351fc4.sentence: Algae do not have to be directly exposed to the sun, but can live below the soil surface given uniform temperature and moisture conditions, and are capable of facultative heterotrophy in the presence of easily available carbon sources (e.g. glucose).

2956eb22fd16.title: Soil microbiology
2956eb22fd16.sentence: Soil algae can be split up into Chlorophyceae and Bacillariophyceae (diatoms).

1f28e1fb839a.title: Soil microbiology
1f28e1fb839a.sentence: The Chlorophyceae usually only have chlorophyll as pigment which makes them green, while diatoms contain chlorophyll as well as other pigments such as the carotenoid fucoxanthin that make them golden-brown in color.

02720401abf9.title: Soil microbiology
02720401abf9.sentence: Synergistic interactions with rhizosphere bacteria in the promotion of plant growth have been demonstrated in Chlorella vulgaris.

7e159eb50906.title: Soil microbiology
7e159eb50906.sentence: Phages, viruses that infect bacteria, are some of the most understudied organisms, despite being considered one of the most abundant organisms present in microbial communities.

eca303e5e23b.title: Soil microbiology
eca303e5e23b.sentence: Viral richness, or the abundance and diversity of phages in an environment, is affected by seasonal changes, soil moisture content, physical location, and the presence and growth of plants.

67e8a0e981f1.title: Soil microbiology
67e8a0e981f1.sentence: Bacterial abundance in soil communities is an additional factor in viral richness, with an increase in bacterial abundance associated with increased phage abundance.

1854a0c89c9c.title: Soil microbiology
1854a0c89c9c.section: Phages > Morphological, genomic, and life cycle diversity
1854a0c89c9c.sentence: Soil phages may be lytic, lysogenic, or chronic.

76d455e4fc63.title: Soil microbiology
76d455e4fc63.section: Phages > Morphological, genomic, and life cycle diversity
76d455e4fc63.sentence: Lytic phages undergo the lytic cycle, during which viral reproduction lyses the cell, resulting in bacterial death and the release of virions.

612fdaa92796.title: Soil microbiology
612fdaa92796.section: Phages > Morphological, genomic, and life cycle diversity
612fdaa92796.sentence: Lysogenic phages integrate their genome into the host and replicate along with the host genome through the lysogenic cycle.

76a7fd18f565.title: Soil microbiology
76a7fd18f565.section: Phages > Morphological, genomic, and life cycle diversity
76a7fd18f565.sentence: An infection is considered to be chronic when virions are produced and released continuously without lysing and killing the host cell.

b36d91387b48.title: Soil microbiology
b36d91387b48.sentence: Lytic phages affect host populations which impact bacterial processes like carbon, nitrogen, sulfur, and phosphorus cycling in soil.

2f99e56062ae.title: Soil microbiology
2f99e56062ae.sentence: Although understudied, soil phages are significant contributors to soil health and affect microbial diversity through ecological and evolutionary roles, being considered as a major agent of horizontal gene transfer.

e56df27b2b6a.title: Soil microbiology
e56df27b2b6a.sentence: Bacteriophages may also be involved in plant pathogenesis through the killing of important bacteria that prevent infection in plants.

000dabeccdf2.title: Soil microbiology
000dabeccdf2.sentence: The lytic phage ΦGP100 is known to kill Pseudomonas fluorescens, which produces antifungals, thus opening plants up to fungal infections.

b2caac0d0492.title: Soil microbiology
b2caac0d0492.sentence: Protozoa are eukaryotic unicellular organisms (protists) that were some of the first microorganisms to reproduce sexually, a significant evolutionary step from duplication of spores, like those that many other soil microorganisms depend on, allowing silencing of deleterious mutations.

f213cf2a06e1.title: Soil microbiology
f213cf2a06e1.sentence: Protozoa can be split up into three categories: flagellates, amoebae and ciliates.

752501222769.title: Soil microbiology
752501222769.sentence: A large number of soil protozoa feed on bacteria, others feed on both bacteria and fungi, while some species are strictly mycophagous, and other soil protozoa are saprophagous, feeding on humus particles.

8c053de57e4f.title: Soil microbiology
8c053de57e4f.sentence: Flagellates are the smallest members of the protozoa group, and can be divided further based on whether they can participate in photosynthesis.

3fc9cdef8fc1.title: Soil microbiology
3fc9cdef8fc1.sentence: These heterotrophic flagellates are found mostly in soil where their number may occasionally be as high as several millions per gram of soil.

36d00c5e738f.title: Soil microbiology
36d00c5e738f.sentence: Naked amoebae move freely in water-filled pore spaces and in water films surrounding roots and aggregates, while testate amoebae are partly encapsulated in a chitinous or mineral shell which protects them from desiccation when fluid water retreats.

2090975ea6a3.title: Soil microbiology
2090975ea6a3.sentence: By their abundance, shape variety and the diversity of their adapatations to moisture variation they are good indicators of climate, making them prominent tools in the reconstruction of past environmental changes, from hundreds of years to millennia.

e786c5b53dd3.title: Soil microbiology
e786c5b53dd3.sentence: Ciliates are the largest of the protozoa group, and move by means of short, numerous cilia that produce beating movements.

ae965c3ad7bc.title: Protozoa
ae965c3ad7bc.sentence: Protozoa (sing.: protozoan or protozoon; alternative plural: protozoans) are a polyphyletic group of single-celled eukaryotes, either free-living or parasitic, that feed on organic matter such as other microorganisms or organic debris.

450cdd11e24b.title: Protozoa
450cdd11e24b.sentence: The term continues to be used in a loose way to describe single-celled protists (that is, eukaryotes that are not animals, plants, or fungi) that feed by heterotrophy.

02c7cb6fda6f.title: Protozoa
02c7cb6fda6f.sentence: The taxon 'Protozoa' fails to meet these standards, so grouping protozoa with animals, and treating them as closely related, became no longer justifiable.

76c9fd1fd9d0.title: Protozoa
76c9fd1fd9d0.sentence: Traditional textbook examples of protozoa are Amoeba, Paramecium, Euglena and Trypanosoma.

f331843fbca6.title: Protozoa
f331843fbca6.sentence: Protozoans, as traditionally defined, range in size from as little as 1 micrometre to several millimetres, or more.

eeaa34f1b718.title: Protozoa
eeaa34f1b718.sentence: The group includes flagellates (which move with the help of undulating and beating flagella).

5f86608fa231.title: Protozoa
5f86608fa231.sentence: Ciliates (which move by using hair-like structures called cilia) and amoebae (which move by the use of temporary extensions of cytoplasm called pseudopodia).

256f57a82485.title: Protozoa
256f57a82485.sentence: Free-living protozoa are common and often abundant in fresh, brackish and salt water, as well as other moist environments, such as soils and mosses.

9823cf5a3f6a.title: Protozoa
9823cf5a3f6a.sentence: All protozoa require a moist habitat; however, some can survive for long periods of time in dry environments, by forming resting cysts that enable them to remain dormant until conditions improve.

643c6828dabb.title: Protozoa
643c6828dabb.sentence: All protozoa are heterotrophic, deriving nutrients from other organisms, either by ingesting them whole by phagocytosis or taking up dissolved organic matter or micro-particles (osmotrophy).

a7ca6c0ce883.title: Protozoa
a7ca6c0ce883.sentence: Protozoa may also live as mixotrophs, combining a heterotrophic diet with some form of autotrophy.

e023d30ba56d.title: Protozoa
e023d30ba56d.sentence: Some protozoa form close associations with symbiotic photosynthetic algae (zoochlorellae), which live and grow within the membranes of the larger cell and provide nutrients to the host.

b7de461df470.title: Protozoa
b7de461df470.sentence: Protozoa mostly reproduce asexually by binary fission or multiple fission.

aa2e80713b0a.title: Protozoa
aa2e80713b0a.sentence: Many protozoa also exchange genetic material by sexual means (typically, through conjugation), but this is generally decoupled from reproduction.

4acb0c6bb90c.title: Protozoa
4acb0c6bb90c.sentence: They have a critical role in the mobilization of nutrients in ecosystems.

d55167e721d7.title: Protozoa
d55167e721d7.sentence: Within the microbial food web they include the most important bacterivores.

05d521d3631a.title: Protozoa
05d521d3631a.sentence: In part, they facilitate the transfer of bacterial and algal production to successive trophic levels, but also they solubilize the nutrients within microbial biomass, allowing stimulation of microbial growth.

787d038a48d2.title: Protozoa
787d038a48d2.sentence: Flagellated protozoa such as Trichonympha and Pyrsonympha inhabit the guts of termites, where they enable their insect host to digest wood by helping to break down complex sugars into smaller, more easily digested molecules.

8d3556a0bed2.title: Microbial loop
8d3556a0bed2.sentence: The microbial loop describes a trophic pathway where, in aquatic systems, dissolved organic carbon (DOC) is returned to higher trophic levels via its incorporation into bacterial biomass, and then coupled with the classic food chain formed by phytoplankton-zooplankton-nekton.

3abbadcac7fc.title: Microbial loop
3abbadcac7fc.sentence: In soil systems, the microbial loop refers to soil carbon.

5f02793d9243.title: Soil microbiology
5f02793d9243.sentence: In the rhizosphere protozoa are involved in a microbial loop, a positive feedback process involving growing roots, their exudates, the bacteria feeding on them, and bacterivorous protozoa which liberate in a plant-available form the nutrients entrapped in microbial biomass.

b55ec64cd1f6.title: Soil formation
b55ec64cd1f6.sentence: The growth of roots through the soil stimulates microbial populations, stimulating in turn the activity of their predators (notably amoeba and free-living nematodes), thereby increasing the mineralization rate, and in last turn root growth, a positive feedback called the soil microbial loop.

d194e8732a16.title: Microbial loop
d194e8732a16.sentence: The term microbial loop was coined by Farooq Azam, Tom Fenchel et al. in 1983 to include the role played by bacteria in the carbon and nutrient cycles of the marine environment.

030e7f8db37f.title: Microbial loop
030e7f8db37f.sentence: Recently the term "microbial food web" has been substituted for the term "microbial loop".

4241fee3f44c.title: Soil animals
4241fee3f44c.sentence: Although difficult to verify experimentally, Clarholm's microbial loop hypothesis explained how the growth of roots, when exploring a new environment, exerts a priming effect on quiescent soil bacteria which in turn are predated by naked amoeba, liberating nitrogen in a mineral form, further absorbed by root hairs, stimulating in turn the plant through a positive feedback process.

fb3ba55783d8.title: Microbial loop
fb3ba55783d8.sentence: To account for this, a conceptual model known as the microbial carbon pump, illustrated in the diagram on the right, has been developed to define how soil microorganisms transform and stabilise soil organic matter.

faf9898d52d7.title: Microbial loop
faf9898d52d7.sentence: As shown in the diagram, carbon dioxide in the atmosphere is fixed by plants (or autotrophic microorganisms) and added to soil through processes such as (1) root exudation of low-molecular weight simple carbon compounds, or deposition of leaf and root litter leading to accumulation of complex plant polysaccharides.

23f77870ed1e.title: Microbial loop
23f77870ed1e.sentence: (2) Through these processes, carbon is made bioavailable to the microbial metabolic "factory" and subsequently is either (3) respired to the atmosphere or (4) enters the stable carbon pool as microbial necromass.

9b6e9bfe3dd3.title: Microbial loop
9b6e9bfe3dd3.sentence: In this model, microbial metabolic activities for carbon turnover are segregated into two categories: ex vivo modification, referring to transformation of plant-derived carbon by extracellular enzymes, and in vivo turnover, for intracellular carbon used in microbial biomass turnover or deposited as dead microbial biomass, referred to as necromass.

07a0ea72b958.title: Microbial loop
07a0ea72b958.sentence: The contrasting impacts of catabolic activities that release soil organic carbon as carbon dioxide (CO2), versus anabolic pathways that produce stable carbon compounds, control net carbon retention rates.

170f33a1a748.title: Microbial loop
170f33a1a748.sentence: For example, plant-derived carbon inputs can prime microbial activity to decompose existing soil organic carbon at rates higher than model expectations, resulting in error within predictive models of carbon fluxes.

64c93bbd7ad0.title: Microbial loop
64c93bbd7ad0.sentence: Although soil microorganisms are known to support a plethora of biogeochemical functions related to carbon cycling, the vast majority of the soil microbiome remains uncultivated and has largely cryptic functions.

886cbfb6f4df.title: Microbial loop
886cbfb6f4df.sentence: This lack of knowledge results in uncertainty of the contribution of soil microorganisms to soil organic carbon cycling and hinders construction of accurate predictive models for global carbon flux under climate change.

7f195da389c8.title: Soil animals
7f195da389c8.sentence: Soil microfauna comprise unicellular (protozoa), and multicellular (nematodes, rotifers, tardigrades) organisms.

ae835eb0a10f.title: Soil animals
ae835eb0a10f.sentence: By their small size (20 μm to 200 μm) they are able to move within mesopores (30–75 μm) and macropores (>75 μm) where they find microorganisms (for microbivorous species) or other microfauna (for predatory species) as food.

6cfce820053a.title: Soil animals
6cfce820053a.sentence: To the exception of resting stages (e.g. eggs, cysts, dauer larvae) microfauna are more often in tight contact with water films surrounding soil aggregates and roots (rhizoplane).

08b479632a41.title: Soil animals
08b479632a41.sentence: Microfauna are involved in strong interactions with soil microorganisms, together consuming and stimulating them by rejuvenating microbial colonies.

b731c81b5a00.title: Soil animals
b731c81b5a00.sentence: Through the excretion of nutrients in a plant-available form (e.g. ammonium) they contribute to plant nutrition.

a49895a92243.title: Soil animals
a49895a92243.sentence: Because of their physiological and locomotory dependence to pore water microfauna are very sensitive to moisture fluctuations.

f03bcce6bc30.title: Soil animals
f03bcce6bc30.sentence: However, resistant life-cycle cryptobiotic stages (e.g. protozoan resting cysts, nematode dauer larva, rotifer anhydrobiotes, tardigrade tuns), allow them to stay and wait for better conditions, restoring fully active metabolism with a few hours.

2b47609d9077.title: Soil animals
2b47609d9077.sentence: It can thus be postulated that, contrary to most other soil invertebrates, soil microfauna will not suffer to a critical extent from climate warming, while they are highly sensitive to other man-induced global changes such as acid rains.

5bee57da40ec.title: Microfauna
5bee57da40ec.sentence: The ecological functions of the rhizosphere can be influenced by microfauna, specifically by nematodes and protozoa, which are abundant in soil.

73f8da4c37e8.title: Microfauna
73f8da4c37e8.sentence: For instance, the carbon cycling within the soil can be affected by nematodes that will feed on the roots of plants, impacting the organic carbon in the soil.

aceaa80f2f02.title: Microfauna
aceaa80f2f02.sentence: Similarly, soil protozoa are able to release phosphorus and nitrogen into the soil and higher trophic levels by dissolving the organic material and nutrients available.

3140b961c688.title: Microfauna
3140b961c688.sentence: For example, protozoa can help maintain the quality of the soil by grazing on soil bacteria.

26c0af5d1302.title: Microfauna
26c0af5d1302.sentence: Through their grazing, the protozoa can help maintain populations of bacteria, allowing the bacteria to more efficiently decompose dead organic material which will improve the fertility of the soil.

e121fb79b025.title: Microfauna
e121fb79b025.sentence: Soil micro-fauna can also impact microorganisms within the rhizosphere by affecting their diversity and accelerating microorganism turnover.

ce6e2bd9cc8c.title: Microfauna
ce6e2bd9cc8c.sentence: This happens because of the microfauna's selective grazing and their ability to influence the resources within the soil.

7e13842084aa.title: Nematode
7e13842084aa.sentence: The nematodes (/ˈnɛməˌtoʊdz, ˈniːmə-/ NEM-ə-tohdz, NEE-mə-), roundworms or eelworms constitute the phylum Nematoda (Ancient Greek: Νηματώδη; Latin: Nematoda).

5c84e8e0ab80.title: Nematode
5c84e8e0ab80.sentence: Most species are free-living, feeding on microorganisms, but many are parasitic.

3b9f5e93bf74.title: Nematode
3b9f5e93bf74.sentence: In total, 4.4 × 10^20 nematodes inhabit the Earth's topsoil, or approximately 60 billion for each human, with the highest densities observed in tundra and boreal forests.

9b6dbf1bf2c2.title: Nematode
9b6dbf1bf2c2.sentence: Their numerical dominance, often exceeding a million individuals per square meter and accounting for about 80% of all individual animals on Earth, their diversity of lifecycles, and their presence at various trophic levels point to an important role in many ecosystems.

05ea47f472cb.title: Nematode
05ea47f472cb.sentence: About 90% of nematodes reside in the top 15 cm (6") of soil.

d5714ad77d0b.title: Nematode
d5714ad77d0b.sentence: Nematodes do not decompose organic matter, but, instead, are parasitic and free-living organisms that feed on living material.

495afb8a0dbc.title: Nematode
495afb8a0dbc.sentence: Nematodes can effectively regulate bacterial population and community composition—they may eat up to 5,000 bacteria per minute.

157469ac6567.title: Nematode
157469ac6567.sentence: Also, nematodes can play an important role in the nitrogen cycle by way of nitrogen mineralization.

0fbdbe95ca93.title: Nematode
0fbdbe95ca93.sentence: One group of carnivorous fungi, the nematophagous fungi, are predators of soil nematodes.

6b93af707551.title: Nematode
6b93af707551.sentence: They can set enticements for the nematodes in the form of lassos or adhesive structures.

78e3d802b003.title: Nematode
78e3d802b003.sentence: They can also release powerful toxins when in contact with nematodes.

e602bf9a5e51.title: Nematode
e602bf9a5e51.sentence: Nematode species can be difficult to distinguish from one another.

9629b5a24080.title: Nematode
9629b5a24080.sentence: A 2013 survey of animal biodiversity suggested there are over 25,000.

5535c96c9c8a.title: Nematode
5535c96c9c8a.sentence: Although the highest estimates (up to 100 million species) have since been deprecated, estimates supported by rarefaction curves, together with the use of DNA barcoding and the increasing acknowledgment of widespread cryptic species among nematodes, have placed the figure closer to one million species.

92146fa61125.title: Nematode
92146fa61125.sentence: One roundworm of note, C. elegans, lives in the soil and has found much use as a model organism.

dc47d370d734.title: Nematode
dc47d370d734.sentence: In 2023 an individual of Panagrolaimus kolymaensis was revived after 46,000 years in Siberian permafrost.

a01eb8dc3a12.title: Entomopathogenic nematode
a01eb8dc3a12.sentence: Entomopathogenic nematodes (EPN) are a group of nematodes (thread worms), that cause death to insects.

a0a158389b54.title: Entomopathogenic nematode
a0a158389b54.sentence: Although many other parasitic thread worms cause diseases in living organisms (sterilizing or otherwise debilitating their host), entomopathogenic nematodes are specific in only infecting insects.

ecbb60068314.title: Entomopathogenic nematode
ecbb60068314.sentence: Entomopathogenic nematodes (EPNs) live parasitically inside the infected insect host, and so they are termed as endoparasitic.

abddf83e4488.title: Entomopathogenic nematode
abddf83e4488.sentence: They infect many different types of insects living in the soil like the larval forms of moths, butterflies, flies and beetles as well as adult forms of beetles, grasshoppers and crickets.

19848aaa3ca5.title: Entomopathogenic nematode
19848aaa3ca5.sentence: The cycle begins with an infective juvenile, whose only function is to seek out and infect new hosts.

46e76099b38f.title: Entomopathogenic nematode
46e76099b38f.sentence: "Nematodes.") After entering an insect, infective juveniles release an associated mutualistic bacterium from their gut which multiplies rapidly.

d4a5d5c83048.title: Entomopathogenic nematode
d4a5d5c83048.sentence: These bacteria of the genus Xenorhabdus or Photorhabdus, for steinerernematides and heterorhabditids, respectively—cause host mortality within 24–48 hours.

d2f85ffb53dc.title: Entomopathogenic nematode
d2f85ffb53dc.sentence: "Nematodes.") After about a week, hundreds of thousands of infective juveniles emerge and leave in search of new hosts, carrying with them an inoculation of mutualistic bacteria, received from the internal host environment (Boemare 2002, Gaugler 2006).

febff8f1f531.title: Entomopathogenic nematode
febff8f1f531.sentence: In order to ambush prey, some Steinernema species nictate, or raise their bodies off the soil surface so they are better poised to attach to passing insects, which are much larger in size (Campbell and Gaugler 1993).

442fb793aed5.title: Entomopathogenic nematode
442fb793aed5.sentence: For example, ambush predators such as Steinernema carpocapsae infect more insects on the surface, while cruising predators like Heterorhabditis bacteriophora infect insects that live deep in the soil (Campbell and Gaugler 1993).

e1d44c6ece3c.title: Entomopathogenic nematode
e1d44c6ece3c.sentence: In a study examining the tolerances of different EPN species to tillage, the density of a native nematode, H. bacteriophora, was unaffected by tillage, while the density of an introduced nematode, S. carpocapsae, decreased.

19b49f49d5af.title: Entomopathogenic nematode
19b49f49d5af.sentence: S. carpocapsae prefers to remain near the soil surface and so is more vulnerable to soil disturbance than H. bacteriophora, which forages deeper and can escape the effects of tillage.

b4161437590c.title: Entomopathogenic nematode
b4161437590c.sentence: The most commonly studied entomopathogenic nematodes are those that can be used in the biological control of harmful insects, the members of Steinernematidae and Heterorhabditidae.

a43e295f13ce.title: Entomopathogenic nematode
a43e295f13ce.sentence: Recently, studies have shown utilizing both EPNs (steinernematids and heterorhabditids) in combination for biological control of plum curculio in orchards in Northeast America have reduced populations by as much as 70–90% in the field, depending on insect stage, treatment timing and field conditions.

0715d565fa62.title: Entomopathogenic nematode
0715d565fa62.sentence: Efforts to control foliage-feeding pests with EPNs were equally unsuccessful, because nematodes are highly sensitive to UV light and desiccation.

f0893f86dca8.title: Bioturbation
f0893f86dca8.sentence: Bioturbation's effect on stratigraphy and the study of the archaeological record is immense.

1877e3218c52.title: Bioturbation
1877e3218c52.sentence: By redistributing material vertically and horizontally, bioturbation confuses the archaeological record and makes relative dating of artifacts more difficult.

3762773075f8.title: Bioturbation
3762773075f8.sentence: In stratigraphy, the Law of Stratification says that the topmost layer is the youngest layer, the next layer being older than the top layer but younger than the one below it, and so on.

9989196c21b0.title: Bioturbation
9989196c21b0.sentence: Stratigraphy is critical for archaeology because the relative age of strata helps to date the materials found within particular layers.

32fe460bff0b.title: Bioturbation
32fe460bff0b.sentence: Bioturbation's effects are not limited to the biological and are studied by archaeologists alongside geologists and biologists.

acfa9f22484c.title: Biomineralization
acfa9f22484c.sentence: The IMA's decision to exclude biogenic crystalline substances is a topic of contention among geologists and mineralogists.

d6b3bd7fe27c.title: Biomineralization
d6b3bd7fe27c.sentence: The geological definition of mineral normally excludes compounds that occur only in living beings.

167f096e3074.title: Biomineralization
167f096e3074.sentence: However, some minerals are often biogenic (such as calcite) or are organic compounds in the sense of chemistry (such as mellite).

20d4427847db.title: Biomineralization
20d4427847db.sentence: Moreover, living beings often synthesize inorganic minerals (such as hydroxylapatite) that also occur in rocks.

6aa0561c1552.title: Biomineralization
6aa0561c1552.sentence: The International Mineralogical Association (IMA) is the generally recognized standard body for the definition and nomenclature of mineral species.

c577280cc0a6.title: Biomineralization
c577280cc0a6.sentence: As of December 2020, the IMA recognizes 5,650 official mineral species out of 5,862 proposed or traditional ones.

110917a82b2c.title: Biomineralization
110917a82b2c.sentence: For example, Lowenstam (1981) stated that "organisms are capable of forming a diverse array of minerals, some of which cannot be formed inorganically in the biosphere."

b7941296a7ca.title: Biomineralization
b7941296a7ca.sentence: Skinner expanded the previous definition of a mineral to classify "element or compound, amorphous or crystalline, formed through biogeochemical processes," as a mineral.

9238b7c98978.title: Biomineralization
9238b7c98978.sentence: The group's scope includes mineral-forming microorganisms, which exist on nearly every rock, soil, and particle surface spanning the globe to depths of at least 1,600 metres below the sea floor and 70 kilometres into the stratosphere (possibly entering the mesosphere).

5d8a78a41bea.title: Biomineralization
5d8a78a41bea.sentence: Studies of their significant roles in geological processes, "geomycology", have shown that fungi are involved with biomineralization, biodegradation, and metal-fungal interactions.

360a3c712c83.title: Biomineralization
360a3c712c83.sentence: In studying fungi's roles in biomineralization, it has been found that fungi deposit minerals with the help of an organic matrix, such as a protein, that provides a nucleation site for the growth of biominerals.

11aa6b02443f.title: Biomineralization
11aa6b02443f.sentence: These fungal proteins that are found extracellularly aid in the size and morphology of the carbonate minerals precipitated by the fungi.

5079b2ede38b.title: Biomineralization
5079b2ede38b.sentence: In addition to precipitating carbonate minerals, fungi can also precipitate uranium-containing phosphate biominerals in the presence of organic phosphorus that acts as a substrate for the process.

57054695cd2b.title: Biomineralization
57054695cd2b.sentence: The fungi produce a hyphal matrix, also known as mycelium, that localizes and accumulates the uranium minerals that have been precipitated.

e52605155a75.title: Biomineralization
e52605155a75.sentence: Although uranium is often deemed toxic to living organisms, certain fungi such as Aspergillus niger and Paecilomyces javanicus can tolerate it.

ca79001ceb02.title: Biomineralization
ca79001ceb02.sentence: Though minerals can be produced by fungi, they can also be degraded, mainly by oxalic acid–producing strains of fungi.

682da890171d.title: Biomineralization
682da890171d.sentence: Oxalic acid production is increased in the presence of glucose for three organic acid producing fungi: Aspergillus niger, Serpula himantioides, and Trametes versicolor.

e086456aafb2.title: Biomineralization
e086456aafb2.sentence: These fungi have been found to corrode apatite and galena minerals.

5c648d902c84.title: Biomineralization
5c648d902c84.sentence: Mineralization can be subdivided into different categories depending on the following: the organisms or processes that create chemical conditions necessary for mineral formation, the origin of the substrate at the site of mineral precipitation, and the degree of control that the substrate has on crystal morphology, composition, and growth.

ae8073c66865.title: Biomineralization
ae8073c66865.sentence: These subcategories include biomineralization, organomineralization, and inorganic mineralization, which can be subdivided further.

3b423ddebb4b.title: Biomineralization
3b423ddebb4b.sentence: Biomineralization, biologically controlled mineralization, occurs when crystal morphology, growth, composition, and location are completely controlled by the cellular processes of a specific organism.

e052d15ea162.title: Biomineralization
e052d15ea162.sentence: Examples include the shells of invertebrates, such as molluscs and brachiopods.

8b5cec51ad61.title: Biomineralization
8b5cec51ad61.sentence: - Biologically induced mineralization occurs when the metabolic activity of microbes (e.g. bacteria) produces chemical conditions favorable for mineral formation.

279921a6acfa.title: Biomineralization
279921a6acfa.sentence: The substrate for mineral growth is the organic matrix, secreted by the microbial community, and affects crystal morphology and composition.

bcc333be2117.title: Biomineralization
bcc333be2117.sentence: Examples of this type of mineralization include calcareous or siliceous stromatolites and other microbial mats.

b6a77e2ce096.title: Biomineralization
b6a77e2ce096.sentence: - Biologically influenced mineralization takes place when chemical conditions surrounding the site of mineral formation are influenced by abiotic processes (e.g., evaporation or degassing).

8341da7aac7b.title: Biomineralization
8341da7aac7b.sentence: However, the organic matrix (secreted by microorganisms) is responsible for crystal morphology and composition.

f62eefba3c4c.title: Biomineralization
f62eefba3c4c.sentence: However, the usage of these terms varies widely in the scientific literature because there are no standardized definitions.

5a2d5db70db1.title: Biomineralization
5a2d5db70db1.sentence: The following definitions are based largely on a paper written by Dupraz et al. (2009), which provided a framework for differentiating these terms.

2801b2968cc4.title: Dwarf forest
2801b2968cc4.sentence: Dwarf forest, elfin forest, or pygmy forest is an uncommon ecosystem featuring miniature trees, inhabited by small species of fauna such as rodents and lizards.

30ccee4f1517.title: Dwarf forest
30ccee4f1517.sentence: They are usually located at high elevations, under conditions of sufficient air humidity but poor soil.

b4ee47a300c8.title: Dwarf forest
b4ee47a300c8.sentence: Two main dwarf forest ecosystem types exist, involving different species and environmental characteristics: coastal temperate and montane tropical regions.

b8d24224be95.title: Dwarf forest
b8d24224be95.sentence: The forests are characterized by small trees (5–8 m) with shallow root systems and abundant epiphytes.

f1aca02f54a0.title: Dwarf forest
f1aca02f54a0.sentence: The high wind speeds act as the determining factor of the stature in dwarf forest flora, especially on ridges and slopes.

1790a0e5fa60.title: Dwarf forest
1790a0e5fa60.sentence: At 6,834 hectares (16,890 acres) the extensive pygmy forest of Mount Hamiguitan is the largest known dwarf forest in the Philippines and possibly the world.

a840d01fb3ab.title: Worm cast
a840d01fb3ab.sentence: A worm cast is a structure created by worms, typically on soils or sand such as those found on beaches.

55978b4853b1.title: Worm cast
55978b4853b1.sentence: They are formed when worms process sediment while burrowing and expel the material at the surface, producing small piles, coils, or pellets of sand or soil.

95d54260f08a.title: Worm cast
95d54260f08a.sentence: Many worms ingest soil or sediment containing organic matter and microorganisms.

091d5bbbc1ef.title: Worm cast
091d5bbbc1ef.sentence: During digestion, mineral particles are mechanically fragmented and organic material is partially decomposed.

9e6392812191.title: Worm cast
9e6392812191.sentence: The processed material is expelled at the surface through the worm’s burrow, forming characteristic mounds or coils of sediment.

ac5f604516df.title: Worm cast
ac5f604516df.sentence: In terrestrial soils such as lawns and grasslands, worm casts produced by earthworms are often considered indicators of biologically active and healthy soil.

fc0f01f3f93c.title: Worm cast
fc0f01f3f93c.sentence: Worm casts often contain higher concentrations of plant-available nutrients than surrounding soil and contribute to improved soil structure by forming stable soil aggregates.

453ab2c86a72.title: Worm cast
453ab2c86a72.sentence: In marine and coastal environments, casts are commonly produced by burrowing polychaete worms living in sandy sediments.

12e4a7da5056.title: Worm cast
12e4a7da5056.sentence: These casts may appear as coiled or spaghetti-like structures on beaches or tidal flats.

a5e16d7f4d8a.title: Oribatida
a5e16d7f4d8a.sentence: Oribatida (formerly Cryptostigmata), also known as oribatid mites, moss mites or beetle mites, are either a suborder or an order of mites, in the "chewing Acariformes" clade Sarcoptiformes.

46f9618e58e9.title: Oribatida
46f9618e58e9.sentence: Oribatid mites are by far the most prevalent of all arthropods in forest soils, and are essential for breaking down organic detritus and distributing fungi.

fdf9d9dcf6c2.title: Oribatida
fdf9d9dcf6c2.sentence: They range in size from 0.2 to 1.4 millimetres (0.008 to 0.055 in).

5f3a897aceda.title: Oribatida
5f3a897aceda.sentence: There are currently 12,000 species that have been identified, but researchers estimate that there may be anywhere from 60,000 to 120,000 total species.

29ae3c1fc82f.title: Oribatida
29ae3c1fc82f.sentence: All these stages after the prelarva feed on a wide variety of material including living and dead plant and fungal material, lichens and carrion; some are predatory, but none is parasitic and feeding habits may differ between immatures and adults of the same species.

30dd49edb309.title: Oribatida
30dd49edb309.sentence: The Oribatida are of economic importance as hosts of various tapeworm species, and by increasing the breakdown of organic material in the soil, as do the earthworms.

180bcd001e18.title: Oribatida
180bcd001e18.sentence: However, contrary to many earthworms, they do not mix organic matter with mineral matter and are also known as scavengers.

de3cee97ef7e.title: Oribatida
de3cee97ef7e.sentence: When feeding on coniferous litter phthiracarid mites tunnel (mine) needles, feeding on parenchyma and accumulating their ovoid faeces at the inside, letting intact the surrounding epidermis.

27eec9287e4a.title: Oribatida
27eec9287e4a.sentence: Oribatid mites generally have low metabolic rates, slow development and low fecundity.

07ff62695ec0.title: Oribatida
07ff62695ec0.sentence: Species are iteroparous with adults living a relatively long time; for example, estimates of development time from egg to adult vary from several months to two years in temperate forest soils.

350848da1315.title: Oribatida
350848da1315.sentence: Some species are especially suited to dry conditions, or on bare lichen covered rocks, but the largest section of Oribatida prefers the moist forest floor and its accompanying litter, oribatid mite density being highest in forests with thick organic layers.

871f7b63291c.title: Soil respiration
871f7b63291c.sentence: Regulation of CO2 production in soil is due to various abiotic, or non-living, factors.

1d4994f97a34.title: Soil respiration
1d4994f97a34.sentence: Temperature, soil moisture and nitrogen all contribute to the rate of respiration in soil.

4edc51be2577.title: Soil respiration
4edc51be2577.sentence: Temperature will increase respiration exponentially to a maximum, at which point respiration will decrease to zero when enzymatic activity is interrupted.

49353024c3f6.title: Soil respiration
49353024c3f6.sentence: At temperatures over 35 °C (95 °F), root respiration begins to shut down completely.

4d894e0aa97f.title: Soil respiration
4d894e0aa97f.sentence: Cryophiles function optimally at temperatures below 20 °C (68 °F), mesophiles function best at temperatures between 20 and 40 °C (104 °F) and thermophiles function optimally at over 40 °C (104 °F).

13e2d21ccaed.title: Soil respiration
13e2d21ccaed.sentence: These cohorts will all function best at different conditions, so respiration may occur over a very broad range.

8b6b09aa24ac.title: Soil respiration
8b6b09aa24ac.section: Regulation of soil respiration > Soil moisture
8b6b09aa24ac.sentence: Soil respiration is low in dry conditions and increases to a maximum at intermediate moisture levels until it begins to decrease when moisture content excludes oxygen.

efe667820cfc.title: Soil respiration
efe667820cfc.section: Regulation of soil respiration > Soil moisture
efe667820cfc.sentence: This allows anaerobic conditions to prevail and depress aerobic microbial activity.

d77fc306524b.title: Soil respiration
d77fc306524b.sentence: Most available nitrogen is in the form of NO3−, which costs 0.4 units of CO2 to enter the root because energy must be used to move it up a concentration gradient.

93b6608fb172.title: Soil respiration
93b6608fb172.sentence: This step requires more energy, which equals 2 units of CO2 per molecule reduced.

5c653731dcc1.title: Soil respiration
5c653731dcc1.sentence: High nitrogen litter is considered high quality and is more readily decomposed by microorganisms than low quality litter.

80dd32412b22.title: Soil respiration
80dd32412b22.sentence: Different methods exist for the measurement of soil respiration rate and the determination of sources.

6f3ba80ef876.title: Soil respiration
6f3ba80ef876.sentence: Methods can be divided into field- and laboratory-based methods.

466aa9cf4838.title: Soil respiration
466aa9cf4838.section: Methods of measurement > Field methods > Types of long-term stand-alone instruments > Closed, non-steady state systems
466aa9cf4838.sentence: Closed systems take short-term measurements (typically over few minutes only) in a chamber sealed over the soil.

987326bd3f51.title: Primary nutritional groups
987326bd3f51.sentence: Primary nutritional groups are groups of organisms, divided according to the sources of energy, electrons, and carbon needed for living, growth, and reproduction.

85e3bdeef88b.title: Primary nutritional groups
85e3bdeef88b.sentence: The sources of energy can be light or chemical compounds, the source of electrons can be organic or inorganic, and the sources of carbon can also be of organic or inorganic origin..

5aebe26eff58.title: Primary nutritional groups
5aebe26eff58.sentence: Phototrophs absorb light in photoreceptors and transform it into chemical energy.

55552db2774a.title: Primary nutritional groups
55552db2774a.sentence: Chemotrophs directly absorb chemical energy from molecules.

806705cfe049.title: Primary nutritional groups
806705cfe049.sentence: Organotrophs use organic compounds as electron/hydrogen donors.

fb43f8806ce1.title: Primary nutritional groups
fb43f8806ce1.sentence: Lithotrophs use inorganic compounds as electron/hydrogen donors.

e8fff9c7fb2b.title: Primary nutritional groups
e8fff9c7fb2b.sentence: Heterotrophs metabolize organic compounds to obtain carbon for growth and development.

0e5186ed263b.title: Primary nutritional groups
0e5186ed263b.sentence: Autotrophs use carbon dioxide (CO2) as their source of carbon.

7640b32cf28f.title: Primary nutritional groups

09b8cf626c73.title: Primary nutritional groups
09b8cf626c73.sentence: A chemoorganoheterotrophic organism is one that requires organic substrates to get its carbon for growth and development, and that obtains its energy from the decomposition of an organic compound.

a3e06d8ce8e3.title: Primary nutritional groups
a3e06d8ce8e3.sentence: The terms aerobic respiration, anaerobic respiration, and fermentation (substrate-level phosphorylation) do not refer to primary nutritional groups, but simply reflect the different use of possible electron acceptors in particular organisms, such as O2 in aerobic respiration, nitrate (NO− 3) or sulfate (SO2− 4) in anaerobic respiration, or various metabolic intermediates in fermentation.

b775cd6dce99.title: Primary nutritional groups
b775cd6dce99.sentence: The organic or inorganic substances (e.g., oxygen) used as electron acceptors needed in the catabolic processes of aerobic or anaerobic respiration and fermentation are not taken into account here.

88557363342a.title: Primary nutritional groups
88557363342a.sentence: Organotrophic organisms are often also heterotrophic, using organic compounds as sources of both electrons and carbon.

a0d7288cfefa.title: Primary nutritional groups
a0d7288cfefa.sentence: Similarly, lithotrophic organisms are often also autotrophic, using inorganic sources of electrons and CO2 as their inorganic carbon source.

85aa094e6cc0.title: Primary nutritional groups

aca5a5232b24.title: Millipede
aca5a5232b24.sentence: Millipedes (originating from the Latin mille, "thousand", and pes, "foot") are a group of arthropods that are characterised by having two pairs of jointed legs on most body segments; they are known scientifically as the class Diplopoda, the name derived from this feature.

25975793d5bd.title: Millipede
25975793d5bd.sentence: Most millipedes are slow-moving detritivores, eating decaying leaves (e.g. forest litter) and other dead plant matter (e.g. coarse woody debris); however, some eat fungi or suck plant fluids.

15a4197f3286.title: Millipede
15a4197f3286.sentence: Typically forest floor dwellers, they live in leaf litter, dead wood, or soil, with a preference for humid conditions.

1fbf9544e999.title: Millipede
1fbf9544e999.sentence: They often play important roles in the breakdown and decomposition of plant litter: estimates of consumption rates for individual species range from 1 to 11 percent of all leaf litter, depending on species and region.

58fba1d0092d.title: Millipede
58fba1d0092d.sentence: The leaf litter is fragmented in the millipede gut and excreted as pellets of leaf fragments, algae, fungi, and bacteria, which facilitates further decomposition by the microorganisms.

6ed43dcf883d.title: Millipede
6ed43dcf883d.sentence: Burrowing activity when associated with the mixing of organic matter with mineral matter makes millipedes efficient soil ecosystem engineers, in particular in areas from which burrowing earthworms are absent for ecological or historical reasons.

6bb340a77574.title: Millipede
6bb340a77574.sentence: Where earthworm populations are low in tropical forests, millipedes play an important role in facilitating microbial decomposition of the leaf litter.

0da5ea404dc3.title: Lithotroph
0da5ea404dc3.sentence: Typically occurring in mining areas, this process concerns the active metabolism of pyrites and other reduced sulfur components to sulfate.

078ee185490b.title: Lithotroph

83b3a0417a61.title: Lithotroph

3ee480d85558.title: Lithotroph
3ee480d85558.sentence: Acid mine drainage drastically alters the acidity (pH values of 2–3) and chemistry of groundwater and streams, and may endanger plant and animal populations downstream of mining areas.

7aa511504d2b.title: Lithotroph

7e67976fba4c.title: Lithotroph

952a5a16d943.title: Lithotroph

1e928fef83d9.title: Lithotroph
1e928fef83d9.sentence: Colonization can initiate the process of organic compound decomposition: a primary factor for soil genesis.

53cc0d6461d0.title: Lithotroph
53cc0d6461d0.sentence: Such a mechanism has been attributed as part of the early evolutionary processes that helped shape the biological Earth.

2bc65aa1da20.title: Lithoautotroph
2bc65aa1da20.sentence: Lithoautotrophs participate in many geological processes, such as the weathering of parent material (bedrock) to form soil, as well as biogeochemical cycling of sulfur, potassium, and other elements.

50be6e1e1da7.title: Lithoautotroph
50be6e1e1da7.sentence: As they are responsible for the liberation of many crucial nutrients, and participate in the formation of soil, lithoautotrophs play a crucial role in the maintenance of life on Earth.

573dc2912396.title: Soil zoology

84f01076e862.sentence: Spatial patterns of soil biodiversity are difficult to explain, and its potential linkages to many soil processes and the overall ecosystem functioning are debated.

61679f156651.title: Chemotroph

3d640c763d5d.title: Chemotroph

fed47e4d775d.title: Chemotroph
fed47e4d775d.sentence: Chemoautotrophs are autotrophic organisms that can rely on chemosynthesis, i.e. deriving biological energy from chemical reactions of environmental inorganic substrates and synthesizing all necessary organic compounds from carbon dioxide.

74e259d3ed6d.title: Chemotroph

345fb8ab2b49.title: Chemotroph

c1ec2429b0d3.title: Chemotroph

b86a527704cd.title: Chemotroph

3869e49f2800.title: Chemotroph

613ccecad267.title: Chemotroph
613ccecad267.sentence: Due to the absence of these electron acceptors, methanogens can then catalyze the final step of the degradation of organic matter which is essential for anaerobic environments.

d356063163ef.title: Chemotroph

e688b769b522.title: Earthworms as invasive species

be255c6df649.title: Earthworms as invasive species

3ccdbf3e9b48.title: Earthworms as invasive species

1be9c90acead.title: Earthworms as invasive species

560ad41e9cc0.title: Earthworms as invasive species

4677fe0d45e2.title: Earthworms as invasive species
