e460c22342db.title: Earthworms as invasive species
e460c22342db.sentence: In areas that have already been colonized, the number of worms can be reduced by removal of introduced shrubs such as common buckthorn (Rhamnus cathartica) and honeysuckle (e.g., Lonicera × bella), which produce leaf litter favored by worms.

a5b7e0161503.title: Invasive earthworms of North America
a5b7e0161503.sentence: Invasive species of earthworms from the suborder Lumbricina have been expanding their range in North America.

d4ca8b62d153.title: Invasive earthworms of North America
d4ca8b62d153.sentence: Earthworms are shifting their ranges northwards into forests between 45° and 69° latitude in North America that have lacked native earthworms since the last ice age.

deb892850bfa.title: Invasive earthworms of North America
deb892850bfa.section: Influence on nutrient cycles and soil profiles
deb892850bfa.sentence: Most northern forests in North America lack native earthworms, which were largely wiped out when the ice sheets of the Wisconsin glaciation scoured much of the continent down to the bedrock.

1da66859d805.title: Invasive earthworms of North America
1da66859d805.section: Influence on nutrient cycles and soil profiles
1da66859d805.sentence: A deep detritus layer is thus characteristic of the native ecosystem of the region, and many native plants have evolved to rely on it.

bdc912399390.title: Invasive earthworms of North America
bdc912399390.section: Influence on nutrient cycles and soil profiles
bdc912399390.sentence: When earthworms are introduced into areas where they previously did not reside, the earthworms break up the organic layer.

42da5e37054d.title: Invasive earthworms of North America
42da5e37054d.section: Influence on nutrient cycles and soil profiles
42da5e37054d.sentence: They do this physically by burrowing, consuming and redistributing leaf litter, and leaving behind castings in the soil.

6fdbc3b71d51.title: Invasive earthworms of North America
6fdbc3b71d51.section: Influence on nutrient cycles and soil profiles
6fdbc3b71d51.sentence: They often mix the nutrients into the soil, out of the reach of all but the deeper tree roots.

ecf563e6a17f.title: Invasive earthworms of North America
ecf563e6a17f.section: Influence on nutrient cycles and soil profiles
ecf563e6a17f.sentence: Nutrients may then be leached and lost from the ecosystem entirely.

878f5463197c.title: Invasive earthworms of North America
878f5463197c.section: Influence on nutrient cycles and soil profiles
878f5463197c.sentence: Overall effects include a decrease in the thickness of the organic layer, increased mineralization, increased bulk density, spreading of the organic matter and humus, and increased rate of decomposition.

79e3cdac9bf7.title: Invasive earthworms of North America
79e3cdac9bf7.section: Influence on nutrient cycles and soil profiles
79e3cdac9bf7.sentence: Podzol soils lose their classic banded appearance when earthworms obliterate their eluvial (A2, Ae, or E) horizons.

b24855ea456d.title: Invasive earthworms of North America
b24855ea456d.sentence: Invasive earthworms have caused a decrease in diversity, seedling populations, forest floor organic matter volume, and overall habitat quality.

a2e676a4073b.title: Invasive earthworms of North America
a2e676a4073b.sentence: The addition of earthworms to an environment has been shown to decrease mycorrhizal associations with roots.

b387664825be.title: Invasive earthworms of North America
b387664825be.sentence: For example, in newly invaded forests buckthorn and garlic mustard, both invasive species, increase notably in population density.

9affa24aa4a5.title: Invasive earthworms of North America
9affa24aa4a5.sentence: Most of the invasive earthworms are European or Asian and came over in soil during the 18th century as Europeans began settling the North American continent.

f760b0b823df.title: Invasive earthworms of North America
f760b0b823df.sentence: The worms were originally transferred through the horticultural trade, probably in the soil bulbs of European plants carried to the Americas.

96994e6be83f.title: Invasive earthworms of North America
96994e6be83f.sentence: Now recreational practices and construction methods are the primary mode of transportation for the earthworms.

fec4a5ecccc7.title: Invasive earthworms of North America
fec4a5ecccc7.sentence: High salinity and sandy soils have greater resistance to earthworm spread.

20808ae9161d.title: Invasive earthworms of North America
20808ae9161d.sentence: Low pH and the presence of plant matter with a high carbon-to-nitrogen ratio (C:N) may promote resistance; conversely, high pH and low C:N ratios appear to confer greater susceptibility.

644ffacc9502.title: Invasive earthworms of North America
644ffacc9502.sentence: More recently than the invasion of European earthworms, Asian earthworms have been introduced by human activities.

8da99a4f6732.title: Invasive earthworms of North America
8da99a4f6732.sentence: Particularly of the genera Amynthas and Metaphire.

5afcd2ca1bc7.title: Invasive earthworms of North America
5afcd2ca1bc7.sentence: Evidence shows that Asian earthworms grow more rapidly, reproduce more quickly, and have greater flexibility in their diet than European species.

ded13f674fda.title: Invasive earthworms of North America
ded13f674fda.sentence: They can also exist at higher densities than European earthworm species.

69621e15c234.title: Invasive earthworms of North America
69621e15c234.sentence: These traits mean that jumping worms can consume organic matter more rapidly, stripping the forest floor of organic matter and temporarily flooding the system with nutrients.

999a878907b3.title: Invasive earthworms of North America
999a878907b3.sentence: There is no known way to remove the earthworms from the soil, so proposals have focused on ways to slow their spread.

f187e613e4c6.title: Invasive earthworms of North America
f187e613e4c6.sentence: One simple measure is to reduce the number of worms released during fishing practices.

51dd0bce5a6e.title: Invasive earthworms of North America
51dd0bce5a6e.sentence: The movement of dirt from one location to the other could also be regulated so that dirt from areas where earthworms are common is not moved into forests without the invasive species.

421ab9425498.sentence: To prevent the spread of invasive earthworms, it is recommended that people should only purchase compost or mulch that has been heated to appropriate temperatures and duration to reduce pathogens and kill the earthworm cocoons, or eggs.

10a73b53555c.title: Sporosarcina pasteurii
10a73b53555c.sentence: Sporosarcina pasteurii formerly known as Bacillus pasteurii from older taxonomies, is a gram positive bacterium with the ability to precipitate calcite and solidify sand given a calcium source and urea; through the process of microbiologically induced calcite precipitation (MICP) or biological cementation.

f90c8db36306.title: Sporosarcina pasteurii
f90c8db36306.sentence: S. pasteurii is a gram positive bacterium that is rod-like shaped in nature.

ae88f725cf68.title: Sporosarcina pasteurii
ae88f725cf68.sentence: It has the ability to form endospores in the right environmental conditions to enhance its survival, which is a characteristic of its bacillus class.

418a661ec520.title: Sporosarcina pasteurii
418a661ec520.sentence: It has dimensions of 0.5 to 1.2 microns in width and 1.3 to 4.0 microns in length.

37cb00df2612.title: Sporosarcina pasteurii
37cb00df2612.sentence: Because it is an alkaliphile, it thrives in basic environments of pH 9–10.

87585af1beb4.title: Sporosarcina pasteurii
87585af1beb4.sentence: It can survive relatively harsh conditions up to a pH of 11.2.

1a988d71dc6d.title: Sporosarcina pasteurii
1a988d71dc6d.sentence: S. pasteurii are soil-borne facultative anaerobes that are heterotrophic and require urea and ammonium for growth.

4aec077691d5.title: Sporosarcina pasteurii
4aec077691d5.sentence: The urea is used as the nitrogen and carbon source for the bacterium.

914fb804cf9f.title: Sporosarcina pasteurii
914fb804cf9f.sentence: S. pasteurii are able to induce the hydrolysis of urea and use it as a source of energy by producing and secreting the urease enzyme.

d41618704a9a.title: Sporosarcina pasteurii
d41618704a9a.sentence: S. pasteurii have the unique capability of hydrolyzing urea and through a series of reactions, produce carbonate ions.

cc14a8a09529.title: Sporosarcina pasteurii
cc14a8a09529.sentence: When the bacterium is placed in a calcite rich environment, the negatively charged carbonate ions react with the positive metal ions like calcium to precipitate calcium carbonate, or bio-cement.

62799653af91.title: Sporosarcina pasteurii
62799653af91.sentence: The calcium carbonate can then be used as a precipitate or can be crystallized as calcite to cement sand particles together.

c8bb6d23ac49.title: Sporosarcina pasteurii
c8bb6d23ac49.sentence: It is a commonly used for MICP since it is non-pathogenic and is able to produce high amounts of the enzyme urease which hydrolyzes urea to carbonate and ammonia.

cdc2dc9c79a7.title: Sporosarcina pasteurii
cdc2dc9c79a7.sentence: S. pasteurii have a purpose in improving construction material as in concrete or mortar.

da0a9f40a32e.title: Sporosarcina pasteurii
da0a9f40a32e.sentence: One solution is to embed this bacterium in the cracks and once it is activated using MICP.

0931d2bced4f.title: Sporosarcina pasteurii
0931d2bced4f.sentence: S. pasteurii has been proposed to be used as an ecologically sound biological construction material.

c633208541e2.title: Soil food web
c633208541e2.sentence: When ecologists use the term, bottom-up control, they are indicating that the biomass, abundance, or diversity of higher trophic levels depend on resources from lower trophic levels.

448f10f076d7.title: Soil food web
448f10f076d7.sentence: Bottom-up effects occur when the density of a resource affects the density of its consumer.

af4eda3d2ff0.title: Soil food web
af4eda3d2ff0.sentence: Correlations in abundance or biomass between consumers and their resources give evidence for bottom-up control.

5aeaccca57dd.title: Soil food web
5aeaccca57dd.sentence: In terrestrial ecosystems, the biomass of herbivores and detritivores increases with primary productivity.

39367b417817.title: Soil food web
39367b417817.sentence: An increase in primary productivity will result in a larger influx of leaf litter into the soil ecosystem, which will provide more resources for bacterial and fungal populations to grow.

a4ab16008c34.title: Soil food web
a4ab16008c34.sentence: More microbes will allow an increase in bacterial and fungal feeding nematodes, which are eaten by mites and other predatory nematodes.

306eee7f0f51.title: Soil food web
306eee7f0f51.sentence: Thus, the entire food web swells as more resources are added to the base.

c1b3eebc38b7.title: Soil food web
c1b3eebc38b7.section: Interactions not included in food webs
c1b3eebc38b7.sentence: This mutualistic relationship has been called an “external rumen”, similar to the mutualistic relationship between bacteria and cows.

714a58d8ddfb.title: Soil food web
714a58d8ddfb.section: Interactions not included in food webs
714a58d8ddfb.sentence: Decomposition of the fecal pellet by the microbes increases its nutrient value and the isopod is able to re-ingest the pellets.

32f98a019fab.title: Soil food web
32f98a019fab.section: Interactions not included in food webs
32f98a019fab.sentence: Litter transformers, such as isopods, consume dead plants and excrete fecal pellets.

1c9728357b86.title: Soil food web
1c9728357b86.section: Interactions not included in food webs
1c9728357b86.sentence: While on the surface this may not seem impressive, the fecal pellets are moister and higher in nutrients than the surrounding soil, which favors colonization by bacteria and fungi.

02a9fd5944fb.title: Soil food web
02a9fd5944fb.section: Interactions not included in food webs
02a9fd5944fb.sentence: When the isopods consume nutrient-poor litter, the microbes enrich it for them and isopods prevented from eating their own feces can die.

702be30198a5.title: Soil food web
702be30198a5.section: Interactions not included in food webs
702be30198a5.sentence: Fungi create nutritional niche for other organisms by enriching nutritionally extremely scarce food – the dead wood.

d7f8b12ae14e.title: Soil food web
d7f8b12ae14e.section: Interactions not included in food webs
d7f8b12ae14e.sentence: This allows xylophages to develop and in turn affect dead wood, contributing to wood decomposition and nutrient cycling in the forest floor.

ca7396dd8cac.title: Soil food web
ca7396dd8cac.section: Interactions not included in food webs
ca7396dd8cac.sentence: Despite their complexity, some interactions between species in the soil are not easily classified by food webs.

0b22e6cb4a86.title: Soil food web
0b22e6cb4a86.section: Interactions not included in food webs
0b22e6cb4a86.sentence: While soil food webs fit these sorts of interactions well, future research needs to include more complex interactions such as mutualisms and habitat modification.

ad6e636ee5ff.title: Soil food web
ad6e636ee5ff.sentence: Since soil organisms range in size from less than 0.1 mm (nematodes) to greater than 2 mm (earthworms) there are many different ways to extract them.

d32d54e1a292.title: Soil food web
d32d54e1a292.sentence: Most methods to extract small organisms are dynamic; they depend on the ability of the organisms to move out of the soil.

d3b197a71a5e.title: Soil food web
d3b197a71a5e.sentence: Soil samples are often taken using a metal core.

9a76a6240be2.title: Soil food web
9a76a6240be2.sentence: Larger macrofauna such as earthworms and insect larva can be removed by hand, but this is impossible for smaller nematodes and soil arthropods.

e215a8d2daba.title: Soil food web
e215a8d2daba.sentence: For example, a Berlese funnel, used to collect small arthropods, creates a light/heat gradient in the soil sample.

0458c3465704.title: Soil food web
0458c3465704.sentence: As the microarthropods move down, away from the light and heat, they fall through a funnel and into a collection vial.

9ad46a3c8ff4.title: Soil food web
9ad46a3c8ff4.sentence: The Baerman funnel is wet, however (while the Berlese funnel is dry) and does not depend on a light/heat gradient.

95bb953034ad.title: Soil food web
95bb953034ad.sentence: Nematodes move out of the soil and to the bottom of the funnel because, as they move, they are denser than water and are unable to swim.

5a3cfafb4d73.title: Soil food web
5a3cfafb4d73.sentence: The activity of microbes can be measured by their respiration and carbon dioxide release.

021cc4f0a3e9.title: Soil food web
021cc4f0a3e9.sentence: The cellular components of microbes can be extracted from soil and genetically profiled, or microbial biomass can be calculated by weighing the soil before and after fumigation.

40a39a3890c5.title: Soil food web
40a39a3890c5.sentence: Top-down control, therefore, refers to situations where the abundance, diversity or biomass of lower trophic levels depends on effects from consumers at higher trophic levels.

1195f86e6620.title: Soil food web
1195f86e6620.sentence: Top-down effects occur when the population density of a consumer affects that of its resource; for example, a predator affects the density of its prey.

2658a45f79f2.title: Soil food web
2658a45f79f2.sentence: In a trophic cascade, predators induce effects that cascade down food chain and affect biomass of organisms at least two links away.

895aa2c351a9.title: Soil food web
895aa2c351a9.sentence: The importance of trophic cascades and top-down control in terrestrial ecosystems is actively debated in ecology (reviewed in Shurin et al. 2006) and the issue of whether trophic cascades occur in soils is no less complex Trophic cascades do occur in both the bacterial and fungal energy channels.

69cc1b18c7a6.title: Soil food web
69cc1b18c7a6.sentence: However, cascades may be infrequent, because many other studies show no top-down effects of predators.

bb68ddbe59f9.title: Soil food web
bb68ddbe59f9.sentence: Besides the grazing effect, another barrier to top down control in soil ecosystems is widespread omnivory, which by increasing the number of trophic interactions, dampens effects from the top.

85afe02487a8.title: Soil food web
85afe02487a8.sentence: The soil environment is also a matrix of different temperatures, moistures and nutrient levels, and many organisms are able to become dormant to withstand difficult times.

e383ff761435.title: Soil food web
e383ff761435.sentence: Depending on conditions, predators may be separated from their potential prey by an insurmountable amount of space and time.

02066ff8b2dd.title: Soil food web
02066ff8b2dd.sentence: Any top-down effects that do occur will be limited in strength because soil food webs are donor controlled.

cf1af6b97d5a.title: Soil food web
cf1af6b97d5a.sentence: Donor control means that consumers have little or no effect on the renewal or input of their resources.

26196d49435f.title: Soil food web
26196d49435f.sentence: For example, aboveground herbivores can overgraze an area and decrease the grass population, but decomposers cannot directly influence the rate of falling plant litter.

646c4c71f07e.title: Soil food web
646c4c71f07e.sentence: For example, in a coastal shrubland food chain the native entomopathogenic nematode, Heterorhabditis marelatus, parasitized ghost moth caterpillars, and ghost moth caterpillars consumed the roots of bush lupine.

0044ede9ef15.title: Soil food web
0044ede9ef15.sentence: These results implied that the nematode, as a natural enemy of the ghost moth caterpillar, protected the plant from damage.

ea5b17596f7c.title: Soil food web
ea5b17596f7c.sentence: Top down control has applications in agriculture and is the principle behind biological control, the idea that plants can benefit from the application of their herbivore’s enemies.

b7dfa18e71cb.title: Soil food web
b7dfa18e71cb.sentence: Mathematical modeling in food webs has raised the question of whether complex or simple food webs are more stable.

1541879917ef.title: Soil food web
1541879917ef.sentence: These ideas stemmed from the mathematical models of May which predicted that complexity destabilized food webs.

21e730796475.title: Soil food web
21e730796475.sentence: May used community matrices in which species were randomly linked with random interaction strength to show that local stability decreases with complexity (measured as connectance), diversity, and average interaction strength among species.

d109ed85c784.title: Soil food web
d109ed85c784.sentence: The use of such random community matrices attracted much criticism.

863927f87903.title: Soil food web
863927f87903.sentence: It also became clear that soil food webs did not conform to these predictions.

d83e39e791dc.title: Soil food web
d83e39e791dc.sentence: Complex food webs may be more stable if the interaction strengths are weak and soil food webs appear to consist of many weak interactions and a few strong ones.

c75091e0ec09.title: Soil food web
c75091e0ec09.sentence: Donor controlled food webs may be inherently more stable, because it is difficult for primary consumers to overtax their resources.

b90eb0247977.title: Soil food web
b90eb0247977.sentence: The structure of the soil also acts as a buffer, separating organisms and preventing strong interactions.

b9019c984e20.title: Soil food web
b9019c984e20.sentence: Many soil organisms, for example bacteria, can remain dormant through difficult times and reproduce quickly once conditions improve, making them resilient to disturbance.

14773d47ffb2.title: Soil food web
14773d47ffb2.sentence: Stability of the system is reduced by the use of nitrogen-containing inorganic and organic fertilizers, which cause soil acidification.

7967b446ea99.title: Soil food web
7967b446ea99.sentence: There are three different types of food web representations: topological (or traditional) food webs, flow webs and interaction webs.

7c79f66eeb7d.title: Soil food web
7c79f66eeb7d.section: Types of food webs > Topological webs
7c79f66eeb7d.sentence: Early food webs were topological; they were descriptive and provided a nonquantitative picture of consumers, resources and the links between them.

e1251702aa35.title: Soil food web
e1251702aa35.section: Types of food webs > Topological webs
e1251702aa35.sentence: Pimm et al. (1991) described these webs as a map of which organisms in a community eat which other kinds.

66e4dbf58840.title: Soil food web
66e4dbf58840.section: Types of food webs > Topological webs
66e4dbf58840.sentence: The earliest topological food web, made in 1912, examined the predators and parasites of cotton boll weevil (reviewed by Pimm et al. 1991).

3d6f469d1fae.title: Soil food web
3d6f469d1fae.section: Types of food webs > Topological webs
3d6f469d1fae.sentence: One problem faced in standardizing such measurements is that there are often too many species for each to have a separate box.

2243562fb108.title: Soil food web
2243562fb108.section: Types of food webs > Topological webs
2243562fb108.sentence: Depending on the author, the number of species aggregated or separated into functional groups may be different.

532e3e3541e2.title: Soil food web
532e3e3541e2.sentence: An interaction web, shown above right, is similar to a topological web, but instead of showing the movement of energy or materials, the arrows show how one group influences another.

6fa241aba2e7.title: Soil food web
6fa241aba2e7.sentence: In interaction food web models, every link has two direct effects, one of the resource on the consumer and one of the consumer on the resource.

f0350a280587.title: Soil food web
f0350a280587.sentence: The effect of the resource on the consumer is positive, (the consumer gets to eat) and the effect on the resource by the consumer is negative (it is eaten).

d867942bbf32.title: Soil food web
d867942bbf32.sentence: These direct, trophic, effects can lead to indirect effects.

39a791c4f705.title: Soil food web
39a791c4f705.sentence: A community matrix model is a type of interaction web that uses differential equations to describe every link in the topological web.

877282347b19.title: Soil food web
877282347b19.sentence: Using Lotka–Volterra equations, that describe predator-prey interactions, and food web energetics data such as biomass and feeding rate, the strength of interactions between groups is calculated.

9e26250b1a29.title: Soil food web
9e26250b1a29.sentence: Miosis build on interconnected food chains, adding quantitative information on the movement of carbon or other nutrients from producers to consumers.

926a191c0fd3.title: Soil food web
926a191c0fd3.sentence: Hunt et al. (1987) published the first flow web for soil, describing the short grass prairie in Colorado, USA.

a3c82a9f6f96.title: Soil food web
a3c82a9f6f96.sentence: The authors estimated nitrogen transferral rates through the soil food web and calculated nitrogen mineralization rates for a range of soil organisms.

412d24017101.title: Soil food web
412d24017101.sentence: In order to create a flow web, a topological web is first constructed.

1ee139de2a7f.title: Soil food web
1ee139de2a7f.sentence: After the members of the web are decided, the biomass of each functional group is calculated, usually in kg carbon/hectare.

89580bd842d2.title: Soil food web
89580bd842d2.sentence: In order to calculate feeding rates, researchers assume that the population of the functional group is in equilibrium.

63fc7d79178c.title: Soil food web
63fc7d79178c.sentence: After constructing the first soil flow webs, researchers discovered that nutrients and energy flowed from lower resources to higher trophic levels through three main channels.

49b195bcd74a.title: Soil food web
49b195bcd74a.sentence: The bacterial and fungal channels had the largest energy flow, while the herbivory channel, in which organisms directly consumed plant roots, was smaller.

64ab100e6ed3.title: Soil food web
64ab100e6ed3.sentence: It is now widely recognized that bacteria and fungi are critical to the decomposition of carbon and nitrogen and play important roles in both the carbon cycle and nitrogen cycle.

c0aded5432b1.title: Nematode
c0aded5432b1.sentence: From agricultural and horticulture perspectives, the two categories of nematodes are the predatory ones, which kill garden pests; and the pest nematodes, which attack plants, or act as vectors spreading plant viruses between crop plants.

22e47be42c35.title: Nematode
22e47be42c35.sentence: Plant-parasitic nematodes include several groups causing severe crop losses, taking 10% of crops worldwide every year.

0a1f772bcc6b.title: Nematode
0a1f772bcc6b.sentence: The most common genera are Aphelenchoides (foliar nematodes), Ditylenchus, Globodera (potato cyst nematodes), Heterodera (soybean cyst nematodes), Longidorus, Meloidogyne (root-knot nematodes), Nacobbus, Pratylenchus (lesion nematodes), Trichodorus, and Xiphinema (dagger nematodes).

f9dcb89a0f81.title: Nematode
f9dcb89a0f81.sentence: Several phytoparasitic nematode species cause histological damages to roots, including the formation of visible galls (e.g. by root-knot nematodes), which are useful characters for their diagnostic in the field.

b2482c3f906e.title: Nematode
b2482c3f906e.sentence: Some nematode species transmit plant viruses through their feeding activity on roots.

9056e05caf90.title: Nematode
9056e05caf90.sentence: One of them is Xiphinema index, vector of grapevine fanleaf virus, an important disease of grapes, another one is Xiphinema diversicaudatum, vector of arabis mosaic virus.

0a752e34c3ba.title: Nematode
0a752e34c3ba.sentence: Rotations of plants with nematode-resistant species or varieties is one means of managing parasitic nematode infestations.

27a33a10c1c8.title: Nematode
27a33a10c1c8.sentence: For example, planting Tagetes marigolds as a cover crop just prior to planting a nematode-susceptible plant, has been shown to suppress nematodes.

48e7f9385d28.title: Nematode
48e7f9385d28.sentence: Another approach involves using natural antagonists, particularly bacteria and fungi, which have proven effective in suppressing plant-parasitic nematodes, such as the fungus Gliocladium roseum.

6a7ef4c9f173.title: Nematode
6a7ef4c9f173.sentence: CSIRO, the scientific research body of the Australian government, found a 13- to 14-fold reduction of nematode population densities in plots having Chinese mustard Brassica juncea green manure or seed meal in the soil.

4d74a66bc8b1.title: Nematode
4d74a66bc8b1.sentence: Soil steaming is an efficient method to kill nematodes before planting a crop, but indiscriminately eliminates both harmful and beneficial soil fauna.

71cb4c9dec5b.title: Microbial ecology
71cb4c9dec5b.sentence: Microbial ecology (or environmental microbiology) is a discipline where the interaction of microorganisms and their environment are studied.

1d1e8bc76704.title: Microbial ecology
1d1e8bc76704.sentence: Martinus Beijerinck invented the enrichment culture, a fundamental method culturing organisms for studying microbes from the environment.

b580101540c5.title: Microbial ecology
b580101540c5.sentence: Sergei Winogradsky was one of the first researchers to attempt to understand microorganisms outside of the medical context—making him among the first students of microbial ecology and environmental microbiology—discovering chemosynthesis and developing the Winogradsky column in the process.

147409b48768.title: Microbial ecology
147409b48768.sentence: In addition, he recognized the known bacteria that were responsible for the nitrogen cycle: denitrification, nitrification, and nitrogen fixation.

04df476db85f.title: Microbial ecology
04df476db85f.section: Important microbial roles in the environment
04df476db85f.sentence: The nitrogen cycle, phosphorus cycle, sulphur cycle, and carbon cycle depend on microorganisms also.

14638db08470.title: Microbial ecology
14638db08470.section: Important microbial roles in the environment
14638db08470.sentence: Through these biogeochemical cycles, microorganisms are able to make nutrients such as nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium available in the soil.

bbca9fe04ba4.title: Microbial ecology
bbca9fe04ba4.sentence: Some symbiotic relationships include mutualism, commensalism, amensalism, and parasitism.

01f149d9eb4e.title: Microbiome
01f149d9eb4e.sentence: A microbiome (from Ancient Greek μικρός (mikrós) 'small' and βίος (bíos) 'life') is the community of microorganisms that can usually be found living together in any given habitat.

93b5a15dd6ce.title: Microbiome
93b5a15dd6ce.sentence: In 1988, Whipps and colleagues working on the ecology of rhizosphere microorganisms provided the first definition of the term microbiome.

663e2dc88d97.title: Microbiome
663e2dc88d97.sentence: It was defined more precisely in 1988 by Whipps et al. as "a characteristic microbial community occupying a reasonably well-defined habitat which has distinct physio-chemical properties.

3ae4ad449475.title: Microbiome
3ae4ad449475.sentence: Relic DNA can be up to 40% of the sequenced DNA in soil, and was up to 33% of the total bacterial DNA on average in a broader analysis of habitats with the highest proportion of 80% in some samples.

d35967d60e26.title: Microbiome
d35967d60e26.sentence: The addition of synthetic nitrogen fertiliser may have little impact on soil microbiome structure or composition, but drastically reduces the microbiome network connectivity.

be7143e1d6a7.title: Microbiome
be7143e1d6a7.sentence: third-generation sequencing | 2008 | TerraGenome: Reference Soil Metagenome Project | |

8c3fdc1df836.title: Metagenomics
8c3fdc1df836.sentence: Metagenomics is the study of all genetic material from all organisms in a particular environment, (environmental DNA) providing insights into their composition, diversity, and functional potential.

50fe81b65764.title: Metagenomics
50fe81b65764.sentence: Metagenomics has allowed researchers to profile the microbial composition of environmental and clinical samples without the need for time-consuming culture of individual species.

083f3e5a4768.title: Metagenomics
083f3e5a4768.sentence: These studies demonstrated that the vast majority of microbial biodiversity had been missed by cultivation-based methods.

49504edae9d8.title: Metagenomics
49504edae9d8.sentence: Metagenomics is distinct from amplicon sequencing, also referred to as metabarcoding or PCR-based sequencing.

5ef092233023.title: Metagenomics
5ef092233023.sentence: The main difference is the underlying methodology, since metagenomics targets all DNA in a sample, while amplicon sequencing amplifies and sequences one or multiple specific genes.

e9ff52cf5a20.title: Metagenomics
e9ff52cf5a20.sentence: Amplicon sequencing provides mainly community profiles detailing which taxa are present in a sample, whereas metagenomics also recovers encoded enzymes and pathways.

644e918a517e.title: Metagenomics
644e918a517e.sentence: Amplicon sequencing was frequently used in early environmental gene sequencing focused on assessing specific highly conserved marker genes, such as the 16S rRNA gene, to profile microbial diversity.

88cb4a188b53.title: Metagenomics
88cb4a188b53.sentence: The insights gained from these breakthrough studies led Pace to propose the idea of cloning DNA directly from environmental samples as early as 1985.

52adfe331673.title: Metagenomics
52adfe331673.sentence: This led to the first report of isolating and cloning bulk DNA from an environmental sample, published by Pace and colleagues in 1991 while Pace was in the Department of Biology at Indiana University.

7f9f3dcd73dd.title: Metagenomics
7f9f3dcd73dd.sentence: The soils in which plants grow are inhabited by microbial communities, with one gram of soil containing around 10^9-10^10 microbial cells which comprise about one gigabase of sequence information.

9dd41f4f284a.title: Metagenomics
9dd41f4f284a.sentence: The microbial communities which inhabit soils are some of the most complex known to science, and remain poorly understood despite their economic importance.

ce863b39d917.title: Metagenomics
ce863b39d917.sentence: Functional metagenomics strategies are being used to explore the interactions between plants and microbes through cultivation-independent study of these microbial communities.

1cd7ea4f5d82.title: Metagenomics
1cd7ea4f5d82.sentence: By allowing insights into the role of previously uncultivated or rare community members in nutrient cycling and the promotion of plant growth, metagenomic approaches can contribute to improved disease detection in crops and livestock and the adaptation of enhanced farming practices which improve crop health by harnessing the relationship between microbes and plants.

5e367e614b02.title: Metagenomics
5e367e614b02.sentence: Because the collection of DNA from an environment is largely uncontrolled, the most abundant organisms in an environmental sample are most highly represented in the resulting sequence data.

8ac86f62c4b0.title: Metagenomics
8ac86f62c4b0.sentence: For instance, long-read whole-metagenome sequencing of soils in industrial technogenic zones has revealed that chronic heavy metal contamination fundamentally restructures the soil microbial community.

2756239e8dff.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/01%3A_Digging_In/1.06%3A_Soil_Biodiversity_and_Ecology
2756239e8dff.section: SOIL BIODIVERSITY > Distribution of soil biota > Biomarker approaches
2756239e8dff.sentence: For example, genes involved in producing a portion of the ribosome (protein synthesis factory present in every known organism) are commonly used to show similarity or dissimilarity in bacteria and archaea (16S rRNA gene), and fungi (18S rRNA gene or Internal Transcribed Spacer (ITS)), while a gene encoding for an oxidase enzyme involved in cellular respiration (Cytochrome Oxidase 1 (CO1) gene) is often used to show the relatedness of animal taxa.

72c75c9f1de9.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/01%3A_Digging_In/1.06%3A_Soil_Biodiversity_and_Ecology
72c75c9f1de9.section: SOIL BIODIVERSITY > Distribution of soil biota > Biomarker approaches
72c75c9f1de9.sentence: It is assumed that a more similar gene sequence between organisms means that they are evolutionarily more closely related.

098f824615b8.title: Oligotroph
098f824615b8.sentence: The oligotrophic soil environments include agricultural soil, frozen soil, et cetera.

185db7ec0d73.title: Oligotroph
185db7ec0d73.sentence: In terms of polar areas, such as Antarctic and Arctic region, the soil environment is considered as oligotrophic because the soil is frozen with low biological activities.

047af6786b3a.title: Oligotroph
047af6786b3a.sentence: Generally, the nutrient becomes less available along the depth of the soil environment, because on the surface, the organic compounds decomposed from the plant and animal debris are consumed quickly by other microbes, resulting in the lack of nutrient in the deeper level of soil.

47c71dc23b18.title: Oligotroph
47c71dc23b18.sentence: In addition, the metabolic waste produced by the microorganisms on the surface also causes the accumulation of toxic chemicals in the deeper area.

f0e8f6334396.title: Oligotroph
f0e8f6334396.sentence: Furthermore, oxygen and water are important for some metabolic pathways, but it is difficult for water and oxygen to diffuse as the depth increases.

e4830ea3cc86.title: Oligotroph
e4830ea3cc86.sentence: Some factors such as: soil aggregates, pores and extracellular enzymes, may help water, oxygen and other nutrients diffuse into the soil.

aff627d6efe1.title: Oligotroph
aff627d6efe1.sentence: The most abundant species in the frozen soil are Actinomycetota, Pseudomonadota, Acidobacteriota and Cyanobacteria, together with a small amount of archaea and fungi.

e403e7e10dc5.title: Oligotroph
e403e7e10dc5.sentence: Actinomycetota can maintain the activity of their metabolic enzymes and continue their biochemical reactions under a wide range of low temperature.

766f9d4b774a.title: Oligotroph
766f9d4b774a.sentence: Collimonas is one of the genera that are capable of living in the oligotrophic soil.

2e4b32cf77ac.title: Oligotroph
2e4b32cf77ac.sentence: One common feature of the environments where Collimonas lives is the presence of fungi, because Collimonas have the ability of not only hydrolyzing the chitin produced by fungi for nutrients, but also producing materials (e.g., P. fluorescens 2-79) to protect themselves from fungal infection.

09c6b872aa2d.title: Oligotroph
09c6b872aa2d.sentence: Additionally, Collimonas can also obtain electron sources from rocks and minerals by weathering.

71a104964833.title: Oligotroph
71a104964833.sentence: Plant adaptations to oligotrophic soils provide for greater and more efficient nutrient uptake, reduced nutrient consumption, and efficient nutrient storage.

72e5da2476d1.title: Oligotroph
72e5da2476d1.sentence: Improvements in nutrient uptake are facilitated by root adaptations such as nitrogen-fixing root nodules, mycorrhizae and cluster roots.

bb84942d08dc.title: Oligotroph
bb84942d08dc.sentence: Consumption is reduced by very slow growth rates, and by efficient use of low-availability nutrients; for example, the use of highly available ions to maintain turgor pressure, with low-availability nutrients reserved for the building of tissues.

a499286330dc.title: Oligotroph
a499286330dc.sentence: Despite these adaptations, nutrient requirement typically exceed uptake during the growing season, so many oligotrophic plants have the ability to store nutrients, for example, in trunk tissues, when demand is low, and remobilise them when demand increases.

3c540535acd9.title: Oligotroph
3c540535acd9.sentence: Thus, soils are extremely nutrient-poor and most vegetation must use strategies such as cluster roots to gain even the smallest quantities of such nutrients as phosphorus and sulfur.

da93c7379324.title: Oligotroph
da93c7379324.sentence: The sandplains and lateritic soils of southern Western Australia, where an extremely thick craton has precluded any geological activity since the Cambrian and there has been no glaciation to renew soils since the Carboniferous.

6e6dcab84b71.title: Oligotroph
6e6dcab84b71.sentence: The vegetation in these regions displays high levels of biodiversity, which can be comparable to a tropical rainforest in certain locations, and it and produces many species of wildflowers.

44154b25d496.title: Oligotroph
44154b25d496.sentence: An example of oligotrophic soils are those on white-sands, with soil pH lower than 5.0, on the Rio Negro basin on northern Amazonia that house very low-diversity, extremely fragile forests and savannahs drained by blackwater rivers; dark water colour due to high concentration of tannins, humic acids and other organic compounds derived from the very slow decomposition of plant matter.

ecc2d4f4e09a.title: Drilosphere
ecc2d4f4e09a.sentence: The drilosphere is the part of the soil influenced by earthworm secretions, burrowing and castings.

a6ec4d05e997.title: Drilosphere
a6ec4d05e997.sentence: Therefore, it is the fraction of soil which has gone through the digestive tract of earthworms, or the lining of an earthworm burrow.

03857418177a.title: Drilosphere
03857418177a.sentence: The average thickness of the drilosphere (lining of an earthworm burrow) is 2 mm, but it can be much wider (about 8 mm) around the burrows of litter-feeding earthworms.

872f3c897964.title: Drilosphere
872f3c897964.sentence: The drilosphere is generally richer in nitrogen, phosphorus, and humified organic material than the surrounding soil.

06c2c789dbb0.title: Drilosphere
06c2c789dbb0.sentence: This is probably because earthworms preferentially ingest plant residue such as leaf and root litter, or occasionally fungi.

717a17fb0761.title: Drilosphere
717a17fb0761.sentence: A study of one soil type found that contained within the drilosphere was 40 per cent of the aerobic (and 13 per cent of anaerobic) nitrogen-fixing bacteria and 16 per cent of the denitrifiers.

d83df45a84d8.title: Drilosphere
d83df45a84d8.sentence: Through the drilosphere, earthworms influence soil microbial communities, with effects on microbial processes related to soil organic matter and nutrient dynamics.

8c49ca1da68d.title: Fungus
8c49ca1da68d.sentence: In agriculture, fungi may be useful if they actively compete for nutrients and space with pathogenic microorganisms such as bacteria or other fungi via the competitive exclusion principle, or if they are parasites of these pathogens.

622808e55b7a.title: Fungus
622808e55b7a.section: Ecology > Symbiosis > As targets of mycoparasites
622808e55b7a.sentence: About 300 species of fungi and fungus-like organisms, belonging to 13 classes and 113 genera, are used as biocontrol agents against plant fungal diseases.

9597ce8b559c.title: Fungus
9597ce8b559c.section: Ecology > Symbiosis > As targets of mycoparasites
9597ce8b559c.sentence: Organisms that parasitize fungi are known as mycoparasitic organisms.

a567bbff8d02.title: Fungus
a567bbff8d02.sentence: Fungal reproduction is complex, reflecting the differences in lifestyles and genetic makeup within this diverse kingdom of organisms.

3beff5e9509f.title: Fungus
3beff5e9509f.sentence: It is estimated that a third of all fungi reproduce using more than one method of propagation; for example, reproduction may occur in two well-differentiated stages within the life cycle of a species, the teleomorph (sexual reproduction stage) and the anamorph (asexual reproduction stage).

67c540185bdb.title: Fungus
67c540185bdb.sentence: Asexual reproduction occurs via vegetative spores (conidia) or through mycelial fragmentation.

a698ff1f18e5.title: Fungus
a698ff1f18e5.sentence: Mycelial fragmentation occurs when a fungal mycelium separates into pieces, and each component grows into a separate mycelium.

0ea7446dca82.title: Fungus
0ea7446dca82.sentence: The spores of most of the researched species of fungi are transported by wind.

2af7c955e909.title: Fungus
2af7c955e909.sentence: Such species often produce dry or hydrophobic spores that do not absorb water and are readily scattered by raindrops, for example.

a0bab4cda1fa.title: Geomicrobiology
a0bab4cda1fa.sentence: Geomicrobiology is the scientific field at the intersection of geology and microbiology and is a major subfield of geobiology.

e8b571873bf0.title: Geomicrobiology
e8b571873bf0.sentence: It concerns the role of microbes on geological and geochemical processes and effects of minerals and metals to microbial growth, activity and survival.

dd8b7f76bfaa.title: Geomicrobiology
dd8b7f76bfaa.sentence: Such interactions occur in the geosphere (rocks, minerals, soils, and sediments), the atmosphere and the hydrosphere.

c23e00d210f8.title: Geomicrobiology
c23e00d210f8.sentence: Geomicrobiology studies microorganisms that are driving the Earth's biogeochemical cycles, mediating mineral precipitation and dissolution, and sorbing and concentrating metals.

933f38bf6134.title: Geomicrobiology
933f38bf6134.sentence: Some bacteria use metal ions as their energy source.

bbf2d6294bf1.title: Geomicrobiology
bbf2d6294bf1.sentence: They convert (or chemically reduce) the dissolved metal ions from one electrical state to another.

4506128fed90.title: Geomicrobiology
4506128fed90.sentence: This reduction releases energy for the bacteria's use, and, as a side product, serves to concentrate the metals into what ultimately become ore deposits.

6ce822cb7b93.title: Geomicrobiology
6ce822cb7b93.section: Environmental remediation > Soil and sediment: microbial remediation
6ce822cb7b93.sentence: Microbes play a key role in many biogeochemistry cycles and can effect a variety of soil properties, such as biotransformation of mineral and metal speciation, toxicity, mobility, mineral precipitation, and mineral dissolution.

11ea2f1d7401.title: Geomicrobiology
11ea2f1d7401.section: Environmental remediation > Soil and sediment: microbial remediation
11ea2f1d7401.sentence: Microbes play a role in the immobilization and detoxification of a variety of elements, such as metals, radionuclides, sulfur and phosphorus, in the soil.

5da00ab6a3bf.title: Geomicrobiology
5da00ab6a3bf.section: Environmental remediation > Soil and sediment: microbial remediation
5da00ab6a3bf.sentence: Cr(VI) is highly mobile, bioavailable and more toxic to flora and fauna, while Cr(III) is less toxic, more immobile and readily precipitates in soils with pH > 6.

bdc23bee3a1e.title: Geomicrobiology
bdc23bee3a1e.section: Environmental remediation > Soil and sediment: microbial remediation
bdc23bee3a1e.sentence: Utilizing microbes to facilitate the transformation of Cr(VI) to Cr(III) is an environmentally friendly, low cost bioremediation technique to help mitigate toxicity in the environment.

f4498eeac928.title: Geomicrobiology
f4498eeac928.sentence: For example, sulfate-reducing bacteria (SRB) produce H2S which precipitates metals as a metal sulfide.

8981aacbbaf6.title: Geomicrobiology
8981aacbbaf6.sentence: Studies have shown that the production of bicarbonate by microbes such as sulfate-reducing bacteria adds alkalinity to neutralize the acidity of the mine drainage waters.

851f4c040f60.title: Geomicrobiology
851f4c040f60.sentence: The applications include for example bioremediation, mining, climate change mitigation and public drinking water supplies.

3a488ecd9110.title: Soil animals
3a488ecd9110.sentence: Soil megafauna are soil animals (some bigger invertebrates but for the most part vertebrates) more than 2 cm in size, living in the soil where they dig nests and galleries (extensive tunnel networks) and eject earth at the soil surface as mounds.

b01631c69b1f.title: Soil animals
b01631c69b1f.sentence: They consist of fossorial mammals (e.g. moles, pocket gophers, voles, badgers, mole-rats, ground squirrels, suricates, lemmings), birds (e.g. miners), reptiles (e.g. skinks, gopher tortoises, burrowing snakes) and amphibians (e.g. caecilians, mole salamanders), bigger earthworms (e.g. megascolecids) and macroarthropods (e.g. scorpions, scolopendrids).

03ac24726c4d.title: Soil animals
03ac24726c4d.sentence: They are present in all biomes, but are more particularly represented in arid areas where the soil offers them a harbor against harshness of the environment (e.g. drought, heat, UV-radiation).

5ef44e48a18e.title: Soil biology
5ef44e48a18e.sentence: The animals even give back to the soil as their burrowing creates nutrient-rich patches and allows more water to infiltrate the soil by increasing porosity, thus decreasing runoff along slopes.

869f2fb34016.title: Soil animals
869f2fb34016.sentence: Often considered as pests by agriculturists, the disappearance of fossorial vertebrates from entire landscapes was considered as an ecological catastrophe, in particular in arid and semi-arid environments where they are often considered as keystone species for soil health.

20a556a8a147.title: Testate amoebae
20a556a8a147.sentence: Testate amoebae (formerly thecamoebians, Testacea or Thecamoeba) are a polyphyletic group of unicellular amoeboid protists, which differ from naked amoebae in the presence of a test that partially encloses the cell, with an aperture from which the pseudopodia emerge, that provides the amoeba with shelter from predators and environmental conditions.

54d9c0c6b90c.title: Testate amoebae
54d9c0c6b90c.sentence: The test of some species is produced entirely by the amoeba and may be organic, siliceous or calcareous depending on the species (autogenic tests), whereas in other cases the test is made up of particles of sediment collected by the amoeba which are then agglutinated together by secretions from within the cell (xenogenic tests).

901b798965c4.title: Testate amoebae
901b798965c4.sentence: Testate amoebae can be found in most freshwater environments, including lakes, rivers, cenotes, as well as mires and soils.

e41e165160a7.title: Soil microbiology
e41e165160a7.sentence: Testate amoebae may remain encysted until better conditions are fulfilled for feeding and reproduction.

561c3cc86b35.title: Testate amoebae
561c3cc86b35.sentence: The strong and resistant nature of the tests allows them to be preserved long after the amoeba has died.

f2049c8524c6.title: Testate amoebae
f2049c8524c6.sentence: These characteristics, along with the sensitivity that some species display to changes in environmental conditions (such as temperature, pH, and conductivity), has sparked their use as bioindicators and paleoclimate proxies in recent years.

ac963fa84605.title: Streptomyces
ac963fa84605.sentence: Streptomyces is the largest genus of Actinomycetota, and the type genus of the family Streptomycetaceae.

c07671a8bc02.title: Streptomyces
c07671a8bc02.sentence: Found predominantly in soil and decaying vegetation, most streptomycetes produce spores, and are noted for their distinct "earthy" odor that results from production of a volatile metabolite, geosmin.

6bbab3f11896.title: Streptomyces
6bbab3f11896.sentence: The genus Streptomyces includes aerobic, Gram-positive, multicellular, filamentous bacteria that produce well-developed vegetative hyphae (between 0.5–2.0 μm in diameter) with branches.

e70b4bc56432.title: Streptomyces
e70b4bc56432.sentence: They form a complex substrate mycelium that aids in scavenging organic compounds from their substrates.

fe5536fdd489.title: Streptomyces
fe5536fdd489.sentence: Streptomycetes produce over two-thirds of the clinically useful antibiotics of natural origin (e.g., neomycin, streptomycin, cypemycin, grisemycin, bottromycins and chloramphenicol).

a5fe79dcffbc.title: Streptomyces
a5fe79dcffbc.sentence: The antibiotic streptomycin takes its name directly from Streptomyces.

ec71fde08bc5.title: Streptomyces
ec71fde08bc5.sentence: Several species belonging to this genus have been found to be pathogenic to plants:

9c2cbe76c4fa.title: Streptomyces
9c2cbe76c4fa.sentence: - S. ipomoeae (soft rot disease in sweet potatoes)

9f0c7579c897.title: Copiotroph
9f0c7579c897.sentence: A copiotroph is an organism found in environments rich in nutrients, particularly carbon.

591879b36025.title: Copiotroph
591879b36025.sentence: They are the opposite to oligotrophs, which survive in much lower carbon concentrations.

bea57515aa5b.title: Copiotroph
bea57515aa5b.sentence: They grow in organic substrate conditions up to 100x higher than oligotrophs.

74a7711f721c.title: Copiotroph
74a7711f721c.sentence: The bacterial phyla can be differentiated into copiotrophic or oligotrophic categories that correspond and structure the functions of soil bacterial communities.

7714e06448c9.title: Copiotroph
7714e06448c9.sentence: If the soil has large amounts of organic C, it would then favor the copiotrophic bacteria.

d689130c9214.title: Copiotroph
d689130c9214.sentence: Copiotrophic bacteria are a key component in the soil C cycle.

2126a6a8d35f.title: Copiotroph
2126a6a8d35f.sentence: It is most important during the period of the year when vegetation is photosynthetically active and exudes large amounts of simple C compounds like sugar, amino acids, and organic acids.

01d8eba85628.title: Copiotroph
01d8eba85628.sentence: In these high resource environments, copiotrophs exhibit a "feast-and-famine" lifestyle.

266b9a0d5bf5.title: Copiotroph
266b9a0d5bf5.sentence: They utilize the available nutrients in the environment rapidly resulting in nutrient depletion which forces them to starve.

4e2eaacbae72.title: Copiotroph
4e2eaacbae72.sentence: Copiotrophs are also chemotactic, meaning they can detect nutrients in the environment.

4a2302e9afcc.title: Copiotroph
4a2302e9afcc.sentence: Oligotrophs can outcompete copiotrophs in low-nutrient environments.

c7aaf4ffc4c9.title: Copiotroph
c7aaf4ffc4c9.sentence: Copiotrophs are characterized by a high maximum growth rate.

39c86f893883.title: Copiotroph
39c86f893883.sentence: Oligotrophs have one ribosomal RNA operon while copiotrophs can contain up to fifteen operons.

d081d93b4986.title: Copiotroph
d081d93b4986.sentence: Copiotrophs tend to have a lower carbon use efficiency than oligotrophs.

c0a05d96beb9.title: Azotobacter
c0a05d96beb9.sentence: Azotobacter is a genus of usually motile, oval or spherical bacteria that form thick-walled cysts (and also has hard crust) and may produce large quantities of capsular slime.

adef939f8d04.title: Azotobacter
adef939f8d04.sentence: They are aerobic, free-living soil microbes that play an important role in the nitrogen cycle in nature, binding atmospheric nitrogen, which is inaccessible to plants, and releasing it in the form of ammonium ions into the soil (nitrogen fixation).

387f4e5f0be9.title: Azotobacter
387f4e5f0be9.sentence: Azotobacter species are ubiquitous in neutral and weakly basic soils, but not acidic soils.

02a28a0a81fb.title: Azotobacter
02a28a0a81fb.sentence: In dry soils, Azotobacter can survive in the form of cysts for up to 24 years.

be5d6956f25f.title: Azotobacter
be5d6956f25f.sentence: Azotobacter species are free-living, nitrogen-fixing bacteria; in contrast to Rhizobium species, they normally fix molecular nitrogen from the atmosphere without symbiotic relations with plants, although some Azotobacter species are associated with plants.

9c218908d30c.title: Azotobacter
9c218908d30c.sentence: Nitrogen fixation is inhibited in the presence of available nitrogen sources, such as ammonium ions and nitrates.

bfa581bf3280.title: Azotobacter
bfa581bf3280.sentence: Nitrogen fixation is highly sensitive to the presence of oxygen, so Azotobacter developed a special defensive mechanism against oxygen, namely a significant intensification of metabolism that reduces the concentration of oxygen in the cells.

d2907918d9ff.title: Azotobacter
d2907918d9ff.sentence: The basic one is molybdenum-iron nitrogenase.

29903b773ff5.title: Azotobacter
29903b773ff5.sentence: An alternative type contains vanadium; it is independent of molybdenum ions and is more active than the Mo-Fe nitrogenase at low temperatures.

67c18bf066b9.title: Azotobacter
67c18bf066b9.sentence: So it can fix nitrogen at temperatures as low as 5 °C and its low-temperature activity is 10 times higher than that of Mo-Fe nitrogenase.

28aa4f987293.title: Azotobacter
28aa4f987293.sentence: The first representative of the genus, Azotobacter chroococcum, was discovered and described in 1901 by Dutch microbiologist and botanist Martinus Beijerinck.

2d412eaf0de0.title: Azotobacter
2d412eaf0de0.sentence: Owing to their ability to fix molecular nitrogen and therefore increase the soil fertility and stimulate plant growth, Azotobacter species are widely used in agriculture, particularly in nitrogen biofertilizers such as azotobacterin.

2968bddcbcc9.title: Azotobacter
2968bddcbcc9.sentence: Azotobacter also synthesizes some biologically active substances, including some phytohormones such as auxins, thereby stimulating plant growth.

c91ace3aaca7.title: Bacterivore
c91ace3aaca7.sentence: A bacterivore is an organism which obtains energy and nutrients primarily or entirely from the consumption of bacteria.

16e638879b48.title: Bacterivore
16e638879b48.sentence: The term is most commonly used to describe free-living, heterotrophic, microscopic organisms such as nematodes as well as many species of amoeba and numerous other types of protozoans, but some macroscopic invertebrates are also bacterivores, including sponges, polychaetes, and certain molluscs and arthropods.

491782a08f70.title: Bacterivore
491782a08f70.sentence: Many bacterivorous organisms are adapted for generalist predation on any species of bacteria, but not all bacteria are easily digested; the spores of some species, such as Clostridium perfringens, will never be prey because of their cellular attributes.

2c49386141a6.title: Bacterivore
2c49386141a6.sentence: For instance, when scientists seek to assess microorganisms in samples from the environment (such as freshwater), the samples are often contaminated with microscopic bacterivores, which interfere with the growing of bacteria for study.

2dabefc6f7dd.title: Bacterivore
2dabefc6f7dd.sentence: Adding cycloheximide can inhibit the growth of bacterivores without affecting some bacterial species, but it has also been shown to inhibit the growth of some anaerobic prokaryotes.

46672a9b03ab.title: Fungivore
46672a9b03ab.sentence: Fungivory or mycophagy is the process of organisms consuming fungi.

5866265aeaec.title: Fungivore
5866265aeaec.sentence: Some of these, which only eat fungi, are called fungivores (or mycophages) whereas others eat fungi as only part of their diet, being omnivores.

49a024511078.title: Fungivore
49a024511078.sentence: Many different organisms have been recorded to gain their energy from consuming fungi, including birds, mammals, insects, plants, amoebas, gastropods, nematodes, bacteria and other fungi.

95ae4b9af8a2.title: Fungivore
95ae4b9af8a2.sentence: The fungal genus, Trichoderma produces enzymes such as chitinases which degrade the cell walls of other fungi.

733b79226573.title: Fungivore
733b79226573.sentence: They are able to detect other fungi and grow towards them, they then bind to the hyphae of other fungi using lectins on the host fungi as a receptor, forming an appressorium.

a3d082b35a96.title: Fungivore
a3d082b35a96.sentence: Trichoderma species have been recorded as protecting crops from Botrytis cinerea, Rhizoctonia solani, Alternaria solani, Glomerella graminicola, Phytophthora capsici, Magnaporthe grisea and Colletotrichum lindemuthianum; although this protection may not be entirely due to Trichoderma digesting these fungi, but by them improving plant disease resistance indirectly.

1bba2df97350.title: Fungivore
1bba2df97350.sentence: Bacterial mycophagy was a term coined in 2005, to describe the ability of some bacteria to "grow at the expense of living fungal hyphae".

dcc71598e1f9.title: Fungivore
dcc71598e1f9.sentence: The majority of our knowledge in this area relates to interactions between bacteria and fungi in the soil and in or around plants, little is known about interactions in marine and freshwater habitats, or those occurring on or inside animals.

ba35fdc50f05.title: Fungivore
ba35fdc50f05.sentence: Three insect lineages, beetles, ants and termites, independently evolved the ability to farm fungi between 40 and 60 million years ago.

6903612d3717.title: Fossorial
6903612d3717.sentence: A fossorial animal (from Latin fossor 'digger') is one that is adapted to digging and which lives primarily (but not solely) underground.

65a68f548878.title: Fossorial
65a68f548878.sentence: Examples of fossorial vertebrates are moles, badgers, naked mole-rats, meerkats, armadillos, wombats, and mole salamanders.

8920aecbbda0.title: Fossorial
8920aecbbda0.sentence: Among invertebrates, many molluscs (e.g., clams), insects (e.g., beetles, wasps, bees), and arachnids (e.g. spiders) are fossorial.

b883b1da3593.title: Fossorial
b883b1da3593.sentence: It is measured that small fossorials, such as ants, termites, and earthworms displace a massive amount of soil.

424cec8448f3.title: Fossorial
424cec8448f3.sentence: The total global rates displaced by these animals are equivalent to the total global rates of tectonic uplift.

27e3fa29e831.title: Fossorial
27e3fa29e831.sentence: The presence of burrowing animals also has a direct impact on the soil's composition, structure, and growing vegetation.

9073e8c3bd8b.title: Fossorial
9073e8c3bd8b.sentence: The net effect is usually composed of an alteration of the composition of plant species and increased plant diversity, which can cause issues with standing crops, as the homogeneity of the crops is affected.

02f67a3ad864.title: Fossorial
02f67a3ad864.sentence: Burrowing also impacts the nitrogen cycle in the affected soil.

bdf61842f855.title: Fossorial
bdf61842f855.sentence: Mounds and bare soils that contain burrowing animals have considerably higher amounts of NH+ 4 and NO− 3 as well as greater nitrification potential and microbial NO− 3 consumption than in vegetated soils.

17acd6775560.title: Fossorial
17acd6775560.sentence: The primary mechanism for this occurrence is caused by the removal of the covering grassland.

64e0f7b4cd41.title: Termite
64e0f7b4cd41.sentence: Nests are considered mounds if they protrude from the earth's surface.

804c30b8ad83.title: Termite
804c30b8ad83.sentence: Epigeal nests (mounds) protrude from the earth with ground contact and are made out of earth and mud.

ce2463d8c66b.title: Termite
ce2463d8c66b.sentence: A mound provides termites the same protection as a nest but is stronger.

d3980df2e19f.title: Termite
d3980df2e19f.sentence: Species in the genus Macrotermes arguably build the most complex structures in the insect world, constructing enormous mounds.

1280078679c9.title: Termite
1280078679c9.sentence: These mounds are among the largest in the world, reaching a height of 8 to 9 metres (26 to 29 feet), and consist of chimneys, pinnacles and ridges.

fa24e0baccba.title: Termite
fa24e0baccba.sentence: The tallest mound ever recorded was 12.8 metres (42 ft) long found in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

c7dc9b6f9d25.title: Termite
c7dc9b6f9d25.sentence: Mounds located in areas with torrential and continuous rainfall are at risk of mound erosion due to their clay-rich construction.

0749ac45c375.title: Termite
0749ac45c375.sentence: The sculptured mounds sometimes have elaborate and distinctive forms, such as those of the compass termite (Amitermes meridionalis and A. laurensis), which builds tall, wedge-shaped mounds with the long axis oriented approximately north–south, which gives them their common name.

87bd0101db2e.title: Termite
87bd0101db2e.sentence: This orientation has been experimentally shown to assist thermoregulation.

7b8ad31518c9.title: Termite
7b8ad31518c9.sentence: The north–south orientation causes the internal temperature of a mound to increase rapidly during the morning while avoiding overheating from the midday sun.

94589fec43c5.title: Termite
94589fec43c5.section: Behaviour and ecology > Relationship with other organisms
94589fec43c5.sentence: Mounds may also provide shelter and warmth to birds, lizards, snakes and scorpions.

99209fd12b37.title: Termite
99209fd12b37.section: Behaviour and ecology > Relationship with other organisms
99209fd12b37.sentence: 54 species of ants are known to inhabit Nasutitermes mounds, both occupied and abandoned ones.

a586ae26bc9c.title: Fungal loop hypothesis
a586ae26bc9c.sentence: The fungal loop hypothesis suggests that soil fungi in arid ecosystems connect the metabolic activity of plants and biological soil crusts which respond to different soil moisture levels.

45748f82aa3b.title: Fungal loop hypothesis
45748f82aa3b.sentence: Compiling diverse evidence such as limited accumulation of soil organic matter, high phenol oxidative and proteolytic enzyme potentials due to microbial activity, and symbioses between plants and fungi, the fungal loop hypothesis suggests that carbon and nutrients are cycled in biotic pools rather than leached or effluxed to the atmosphere during and between pulses of precipitation.

9a8e41d6e102.title: Fungal loop hypothesis
9a8e41d6e102.section: Theory development > The role of fungi in biogeochemical cycling
9a8e41d6e102.sentence: However, fungi can metabolize at higher temperatures and lower water potentials than bacteria.

854176dda346.title: Fungal loop hypothesis
854176dda346.section: Theory development > The role of fungi in biogeochemical cycling
854176dda346.sentence: Therefore, in arid ecosystems where precipitation falls during the hot season, fungi are likely the most important contributors to nutrient cycling due to their tolerance to temperature and ability to persist during long dry periods.

fa13704af781.title: Fungal loop hypothesis
fa13704af781.sentence: The fungal loop hypothesis suggests that biological soil crusts and associated microbes are able to become active after smaller water pulses compared to vascular plants, which require more water to become active.

42468ca98706.title: Fungal loop hypothesis
42468ca98706.sentence: However, fungi are able to take up the nutrients produced by biological soil crusts at lower water potentials, and keep them in the biotic pool until larger water pulses allow plants to become active and take up those nutrients.

86b27678d3d6.title: Fungal loop hypothesis
86b27678d3d6.sentence: Active plants then are able to contribute excess carbon from photosynthesis to their fungal symbionts.

96554e236c7c.title: Fungal loop hypothesis
96554e236c7c.sentence: However, direct experimental tests of the hypothesis in arid ecosystems are still relatively rare.

76368a0f3445.title: Fungal loop hypothesis
76368a0f3445.sentence: They found that organic and inorganic N could be dispersed up to 100 cm per day bidirectionally between plants and crust.

1f060bc0da35.title: Food web
1f060bc0da35.section: Kinds of food webs > Detrital web
1f060bc0da35.sentence: In a detrital web, plant and animal matter is broken down by decomposers, e.g., bacteria and fungi, and moves to detritivores and then carnivores.

08180660c351.title: Food web
08180660c351.section: Kinds of food webs > Detrital web
08180660c351.sentence: "Detritus can be broadly defined as any form of non-living organic matter, including different types of plant tissue (e.g. leaf litter, dead wood, aquatic macrophytes, algae), animal tissue (carrion), dead microbes, faeces (manure, dung, faecal pellets, guano, frass), as well as products secreted, excreted or exuded from organisms (e.g. extra-cellular polymers, nectar, root exudates and leachates, dissolved organic matter, extra-cellular matrix, mucilage).

5337b173a4fb.title: Food web
5337b173a4fb.sentence: Most of the primary production in an ecosystem is not consumed, but is recycled by detritus back into useful nutrients.

c9ec076a8134.title: Food web
c9ec076a8134.section: Kinds of food webs > Detrital web
c9ec076a8134.sentence: There are often relationships between the detrital web and the grazing web.

f806d32f88fc.title: Food web
f806d32f88fc.section: Kinds of food webs > Detrital web
f806d32f88fc.sentence: Mushrooms produced by decomposers in the detrital web become a food source for deer, squirrels, and mice in the grazing web.

e1b030c1dc76.title: Food web
e1b030c1dc76.section: Kinds of food webs > Detrital web
e1b030c1dc76.sentence: Earthworms eaten by robins are detritivores consuming decaying leaves.

8612de10c557.title: Food web
8612de10c557.sentence: The base or basal species in a food web are those species without prey and can include autotrophs or saprophytic detritivores (i.e., the community of decomposers in soil, biofilms, and periphyton).

01975d352f82.title: Food web
01975d352f82.sentence: Lindeman emphasized the important role of decomposer organisms in a trophic system of classification.

33fc0ca0c005.title: Organotroph
33fc0ca0c005.sentence: An organotroph is an organism that obtains hydrogen or electrons from organic substrates.

81073745fbba.title: Organotroph
81073745fbba.sentence: This term is used in microbiology to classify and describe organisms based on how they obtain electrons for their respiration processes.

ded381a58ec8.title: Organotroph
ded381a58ec8.sentence: The term was suggested in 1946 by Lwoff and collaborators.

36a76c19a4f0.title: Organotroph
36a76c19a4f0.sentence: Some organotrophs such as animals and many bacteria, are also heterotrophs.

7fede0333b52.title: Organotroph
7fede0333b52.sentence: Organotrophs can be either anaerobic or aerobic.

b4d623a585e5.title: Organotroph
b4d623a585e5.sentence: Different from an organotroph is a lithotroph, an organism which obtains its electrons from inorganic substrates.

943239bd7074.title: Microbial metabolism
943239bd7074.sentence: Microbial metabolism is the means by which a microbe obtains the energy and nutrients (e.g. carbon) it needs to live and reproduce.

2e6f470e5e29.title: Microbial metabolism
2e6f470e5e29.sentence: The specific metabolic properties of a microbe are the major factors in determining that microbe's ecological niche, and often allow for that microbe to be useful in industrial processes or responsible for biogeochemical cycles.

1944720a068c.title: Microbial metabolism
1944720a068c.sentence: All microbial metabolisms can be arranged according to three principles:

0537b7165f55.title: Microbial metabolism
0537b7165f55.sentence: - autotrophic – carbon is obtained from carbon dioxide (CO2)

0ebe8095a9d2.title: Microbial metabolism
0ebe8095a9d2.sentence: - heterotrophic – carbon is obtained from organic compounds

4d7936bb6679.title: Microbial metabolism
4d7936bb6679.sentence: - mixotrophic – carbon is obtained from both organic compounds and by fixing carbon dioxide

fa1ceb7e2e6a.title: Microbial metabolism
fa1ceb7e2e6a.sentence: - lithotrophic – reducing equivalents are obtained from inorganic compounds

b66d5d38ce44.title: Microbial metabolism
b66d5d38ce44.sentence: - organotrophic – reducing equivalents are obtained from organic compounds

8006a590a14c.title: Microbial metabolism
8006a590a14c.sentence: - phototrophic – energy is obtained from light

bad57fd38746.title: Microbial metabolism
bad57fd38746.sentence: - chemotrophic – energy is obtained from external chemical compounds

65c582361db4.title: Microbial metabolism
65c582361db4.sentence: - chemolithoautotrophs obtain energy from the oxidation of inorganic compounds and carbon from the fixation of carbon dioxide.

bb8707e9a205.title: Microbial metabolism
bb8707e9a205.sentence: Examples: Nitrifying bacteria, sulfur-oxidizing bacteria, iron-oxidizing bacteria, Knallgas-bacteria

1513dee50e06.title: Microbial metabolism
1513dee50e06.sentence: - chemoorganoheterotrophs obtain energy, carbon, and hydrogen for biosynthetic reactions from organic compounds.

6b495385cc01.title: Microbial metabolism
6b495385cc01.sentence: Escherichia coli, Bacillus spp., Actinomycetota; eukaryotes

8ad4e167bb33.title: Microbial metabolism
8ad4e167bb33.sentence: Fermentation is a specific type of heterotrophic metabolism that uses organic carbon instead of oxygen as a terminal electron acceptor.

4a54150c99af.title: Microbial metabolism
4a54150c99af.sentence: Many organisms can use fermentation under anaerobic conditions and aerobic respiration when oxygen is present.

51742076dfe5.title: Facultative anaerobic organism
51742076dfe5.sentence: A facultative anaerobic organism is an organism that makes ATP by aerobic respiration if oxygen is present, but is capable of switching to fermentation if oxygen is absent.

b9256a63aa85.title: Microbial metabolism
b9256a63aa85.section: Anaerobic respiration > Denitrification – nitrate as electron acceptor
b9256a63aa85.sentence: Many facultative anaerobes use denitrification because nitrate, like oxygen, has a high reduction potential.

697f8935e6c5.title: Microbial metabolism
697f8935e6c5.section: Anaerobic respiration > Denitrification – nitrate as electron acceptor
697f8935e6c5.sentence: Denitrification involves the stepwise reduction of nitrate to nitrite (NO− 2), nitric oxide (NO), nitrous oxide (N 2O), and dinitrogen (N 2) by the enzymes nitrate reductase, nitrite reductase, nitric oxide reductase, and nitrous oxide reductase, respectively.

6cd42ca77480.title: Microbial metabolism
6cd42ca77480.sentence: Methanotrophs are a specific type of methylotroph that are also able to use methane (CH 4) as a carbon source by oxidizing it sequentially to methanol (CH 3OH), formaldehyde (CH 2O), formate (HCOO−), and carbon dioxide CO2 initially using the enzyme methane monooxygenase.

98d38dcad541.title: Microbial metabolism
98d38dcad541.sentence: As oxygen is required for this process, all (conventional) methanotrophs are obligate aerobes.

83275daaf1a9.title: Microbial metabolism
83275daaf1a9.sentence: Both of these processes are extremely energetically poor leading to very slow growth rates for both types of organisms.

c4083bbced60.title: Microbial metabolism
c4083bbced60.sentence: In 2015, two groups independently showed the microbial genus Nitrospira is capable of complete nitrification (Comammox).

b8983990eb0f.title: Saprotrophic bacteria
b8983990eb0f.sentence: Saprotrophic bacteria are bacteria that are typically soil-dwelling and utilize saprotrophic nutrition as their primary energy source.

fbafec5eb2db.title: Saprotrophic bacteria
fbafec5eb2db.sentence: They obtain nutrients via absorptive nutrition, in which nutrients are externally digested by a variety of enzymes and subsequently absorbed by the saprotroph.

507727b0bd52.title: Saprotrophic bacteria
507727b0bd52.sentence: They are often associated with soil fungi that also use saprotrophic nutrition and both are classified as saprotrophs.

587339244d74.title: Saprotrophic bacteria
587339244d74.sentence: Saprotrophic organisms include fungi, bacteria, and water molds which are critical to decomposition and nutrient cycling, providing nutrition for consumers at higher trophic levels.

543b2faa5652.title: Saprotrophic bacteria
543b2faa5652.sentence: Compared to fungi, bacteria are considered more competitive in degrading easily available substrates.

c5e5ab8d1b0a.title: Saprotrophic bacteria
c5e5ab8d1b0a.sentence: However, bacteria’s higher demand for nitrogen and inability to translocate nutrients makes them less efficient decomposers than fungi.

d983a7a57df8.title: Saprotrophic bacteria
d983a7a57df8.sentence: Community composition and proliferation rates of saprotrophic indicator bacteria are often considered signals of community health in soil, aquatic, and bodily systems.

fb81fddd3cc4.title: Saprotrophic bacteria
fb81fddd3cc4.sentence: Saprotrophic bacterial growth rate is very sensitive to changes in environmental conditions, making it a good variable to detect rapid and subtle changes in microbial communities.

084d47727c8e.title: Saprotrophic bacteria
084d47727c8e.sentence: Some saprotrophic bacteria are common pathogens in medicine and agriculture, as they move readily between individuals via consumption or other modes of exposure, such as contact with excrement.

de28e0bb2579.title: Saprotrophic bacteria
de28e0bb2579.sentence: For example, certain bacteria may be vectors for food borne illnesses such as Escherichia coli.

59cc95d213e2.title: Saprotrophic bacteria
59cc95d213e2.sentence: Others have the ability to decompose cellulose, and are often found in the rumen of cows, aiding in their digestion by fermenting the cellulose in grass.

d030d679cc0b.title: Dwarf forest
d030d679cc0b.sentence: Formation of coastal elfin forests in northern California and Oregon, began with a series of marine terraces.

e2d740802607.title: Dwarf forest
e2d740802607.sentence: A combination of uplift and changes in ocean level formed a system of terraces, resulting in an “ecological staircase”, with each terrace approximately 100,000 years older than the one below it and supporting a distinct association of soils, microbes, plants, and animals.

3664d0cb4c60.title: Dwarf forest
3664d0cb4c60.sentence: The succession of plant communities that repeats on each terrace eventually forms a very specific podzol known as the Blacklock series, which offers an inhospitable environment for species and greatly stunts further growth on the terrace.

e5caae0dd26f.title: Dwarf forest
e5caae0dd26f.sentence: Part of this soil profile includes an underlying clay or iron hardpan.

d310b5e61f13.title: Dwarf forest
d310b5e61f13.sentence: - Mendocino pygmy forest in Mendocino County, California, for example, is an oligotrophic community caused by podzolized (nutrient-poor, highly acidic) soils.

1eeabfd2a06b.title: Dwarf forest
1eeabfd2a06b.sentence: Analyses of pygmy forest soils show low levels of macro- and micronutrients, and high levels of exchangeable aluminium, which limits the ability of plants to grow.

1115eaf60288.title: Dwarf forest
1115eaf60288.sentence: Low pH conditions support formation of an iron hardpan, preventing the trees from setting deep roots and preventing internal drainage of soil water.

4ce94c4d1097.title: Dwarf forest
4ce94c4d1097.sentence: As a result, the pine trees in the area are rarely more than three or four feet high, in a sort of natural bonsai effect.

1d703a1cc037.title: Dwarf forest
1d703a1cc037.sentence: Many of the tree trunks, though only an inch thick, contain 80 or more growth rings.

5116de8b6567.title: Dwarf forest
5116de8b6567.sentence: Only yards away, but with younger soils, the same species of tree grows many dozens of feet high.

232730140b90.title: Hans Jenny (pedologist)
232730140b90.sentence: One notable project was his study of the Mendocino pygmy forest, a remarkable community of ericaceous and coniferous plant species whose stunted growth and grotesquely twisted morphology reveal a long and tortured struggle for survival on a 500,000-year-old marine terrace.

06c94a7ef860.title: Soil retrogression and degradation
06c94a7ef860.sentence: The same soil may achieve several successive steady state conditions during its existence, as exhibited by the Pygmy forest sequence in Mendocino County, California.

cade98490078.title: Hans Jenny (pedologist)
cade98490078.sentence: Jenny did much of his pygmy forest research within the boundaries of Jug Handle State Natural Reserve, which, due to Hans and his wife Jean's lobbying, was designated the Pygmy Forest National Natural Landmark by the National Park Service in 1974.

b99b77b3aacb.title: Microbiologically induced calcite precipitation
b99b77b3aacb.sentence: The increase in shear strength, confined compressive strength, stiffness and liquefaction resistance was reported due to calcium carbonate precipitation resulting from microbial activity.

a009b7158b25.title: Microbiologically induced calcite precipitation
a009b7158b25.sentence: Triaxial compression tests on untreated and bio-cemented Ottawa sand have shown an increase in shear strength by a factor of 1.8.

7ac39ed69212.title: Microbiologically induced calcite precipitation
7ac39ed69212.sentence: Light microscopic imaging suggested that the mechanical strength enhancement of cemented sandy material is caused mostly due to point-to-point contacts of calcium carbonate crystals and adjacent sand grains.

d6e11dd3a6c4.title: Microbiologically induced calcite precipitation
d6e11dd3a6c4.sentence: Recent work has demonstrated that surface percolation or irrigation is also feasible and in fact provides more strength per amount of calcite provided because crystals form more readily at the bridging points between sand particles over which the water percolates.

f24d0e8808e4.title: Microbiologically induced calcite precipitation
f24d0e8808e4.sentence: MICP has the potential to be a cost-effective and green alternative to traditional methods of stabilizing soils, such as chemical grouting, which typically involve the injection of synthetic materials into the soil.

eb8679821e37.title: Microbiologically induced calcite precipitation
eb8679821e37.sentence: These synthetic additives are typically costly and can create environmental hazards by modifying the pH and contaminating soils and groundwater.

3f466fa2eb3a.title: Microbiologically induced calcite precipitation
3f466fa2eb3a.sentence: Excluding sodium silicate, all traditional chemical additives are toxic.

2e33062dd9ba.title: Microbiologically induced calcite precipitation
2e33062dd9ba.section: Possible applications > Liquefaction prevention > Possible limitations of MICP as a cementation technique
2e33062dd9ba.sentence: Bacteria are not expected to enter through pore throats smaller than approximately 0.4 μm.
