5f3df4f724d3.title: Microbiologically induced calcite precipitation
5f3df4f724d3.section: Possible applications > Liquefaction prevention > Possible limitations of MICP as a cementation technique
5f3df4f724d3.sentence: Based on the size of microorganism, the applicability of biocementation is limited to GW, GP, SW, SP, ML, and organic soils.

983f87189467.title: Microbiologically induced calcite precipitation
983f87189467.section: Possible applications > Liquefaction prevention > Possible limitations of MICP as a cementation technique
983f87189467.sentence: MICP may be limited to the soils containing limited amounts of fines due to the reduction in pore spaces in fine soils.

8394d1cef952.title: Microbiologically induced calcite precipitation
8394d1cef952.section: Possible applications > Liquefaction prevention > Possible limitations of MICP as a cementation technique
8394d1cef952.sentence: Many of these limitations can be overcome through the use of MICP through bio-stimulation - a process through which indigenous ureolytic soil bacteria are enriched in situ.

d256e291e55d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/10%3A_Soil_Ecology/10.02%3A_Humus
d256e291e55d.sentence: Humus is the stable, amorphous, heterogeneous fraction of the soil organic matter remaining after the major portion of added plant and animal residues have decomposed.

4d3e98c6c888.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/10%3A_Soil_Ecology/10.02%3A_Humus
4d3e98c6c888.sentence: It is bound to the surfaces of clays and hydrous oxides, which renders it resistant to microbial attack.

e5506f394681.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/10%3A_Soil_Ecology/10.02%3A_Humus
e5506f394681.sentence: Humus has a low bulk density (0.05 to 0.25 grams per cubic centimeter), is very finely divided (colloidal), and has a high porosity and water holding capacity.

1395c5b8fbad.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/10%3A_Soil_Ecology/10.02%3A_Humus
1395c5b8fbad.sentence: It has a very high cation exchange capacity (greater than 200 milliequivalents per 100 grams of pure humus or 200 centimoles(+) per kilogram of pure humus) which allows it to retain cations such as Ca2+, H+, K+, Mg2+, Na+, and NH4+ ions).

79b959c04918.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/10%3A_Soil_Ecology/10.02%3A_Humus
79b959c04918.sentence: Humus has a variable composition but approximates 50% carbon, 35% oxygen, 8 % hydrogen, 5% nitrogen, and 2% sulfur plus traces of all other essential elements for microbial life.

6e0bcf430876.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/10%3A_Soil_Ecology/10.02%3A_Humus
6e0bcf430876.sentence: It commonly is responsible for 20 to 30 % or more of the cation exchange capacity of soils.

0d0f74ebe275.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/10%3A_Soil_Ecology/10.02%3A_Humus
0d0f74ebe275.sentence: It buffers the soil against drastic chemical changes in pH in the root environment.

75622a5503ad.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/10%3A_Soil_Ecology/10.02%3A_Humus
75622a5503ad.sentence: Humus provides stability to soil peds by acting as a binding agent promoting soil aggregation.

0077e6a0c946.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/10%3A_Soil_Ecology/10.02%3A_Humus
0077e6a0c946.sentence: The humus content of arable soils averages between 2-3% and has a range of <1 to over 12%.

11dd3ed466ce.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/10%3A_Soil_Ecology/10.02%3A_Humus
11dd3ed466ce.sentence: The amount of organic material necessary to maintain the normal humus level in soil ranges from 1000 to 5000 kg/ha per year (1000 to 5000 pounds per acre-furrow-slice per year).

189853a192b7.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/10%3A_Soil_Ecology/10.02%3A_Humus
189853a192b7.sentence: Second, the addition of organic material to the soil will not permanently increase the soil’s humus content.

98be5e3847a3.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/10%3A_Soil_Ecology/10.02%3A_Humus
98be5e3847a3.sentence: The natural physical and biological changes in the soil will hasten the decomposition of the organic residues resulting after a few years in only a small quantity of the added material remaining as humus.

806b767144f5.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/10%3A_Soil_Ecology/10.02%3A_Humus
806b767144f5.sentence: Cultivated soils lose humus by biological decomposition at a rate of 1 to 2% per year.

449ad731dca6.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/10%3A_Soil_Ecology/10.02%3A_Humus
449ad731dca6.sentence: Crop rotations including grasses and legumes in conjunction with conservation tillage and crop residue management can be used to sustain the humus level and productivity of agricultural soils.

16905b1fb1ce.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/10%3A_Soil_Ecology/10.01%3A_Microbial_Activity_and_the_Carbon_Cycle
16905b1fb1ce.sentence: The process of soil organic matter decomposition and humus formation may be represented as a partial oxidation process as follows:

cb2c29ad1178.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/10%3A_Soil_Ecology/10.01%3A_Microbial_Activity_and_the_Carbon_Cycle
cb2c29ad1178.sentence: organic substances + O2 + microorganisms + suitable environment ------> CO2 + H2O + Energy (both as heat and for microbial growth) + humus + new microbial cells + inorganic plant nutrients (Ca2+, Cl-, Co2+, Cu2+, Fe2+, H3BO3, H2PO4-, K+, Mg2+, Mn2+, MoO42-, NH4+, Ni2+, S2-, and Zn2+)

9b03c910f008.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/10%3A_Soil_Ecology/10.01%3A_Microbial_Activity_and_the_Carbon_Cycle
9b03c910f008.sentence: Under natural soil conditions, organic residues undergo an initial rapid decomposition, which liberates large amounts of carbon dioxide, water, energy, and releases small quantities of inorganic nitrogen, phosphorus, sulfur and other plant nutrients.

979c9724cac6.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/10%3A_Soil_Ecology/10.01%3A_Microbial_Activity_and_the_Carbon_Cycle
979c9724cac6.sentence: Probably the most important function soil microorganisms serve is to recycle organic carbon to carbon dioxide, thereby maintaining photosynthesis on the earth.

90baf0d88325.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/10%3A_Soil_Ecology/10.01%3A_Microbial_Activity_and_the_Carbon_Cycle
90baf0d88325.sentence: Nutrients contained in the plant and animal tissue are transformed from unavailable organic forms to plant-available inorganic forms during the microbial oxidation.

05724e1b0e56.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/10%3A_Soil_Ecology/10.01%3A_Microbial_Activity_and_the_Carbon_Cycle
05724e1b0e56.sentence: Hence, organic matter acts similar to a very slow-release fertilizer and buffers the soil-plant environment against drastic fluctuations in available plant nutrients.

5c81a943572a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/10%3A_Soil_Ecology/10.01%3A_Microbial_Activity_and_the_Carbon_Cycle
5c81a943572a.sentence: A soil containing one percent organic matter contains up to 45 million kilocalories of potential energy per acre-furrow-slice.

8b6ab0c2ab9a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/10%3A_Soil_Ecology/10.01%3A_Microbial_Activity_and_the_Carbon_Cycle
8b6ab0c2ab9a.sentence: This energy is equivalent in heating value to about 6 tons of coal, or 31 barrels of crude oil or 168,000 cubic feet of natural gas.

5a52e2193166.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/10%3A_Soil_Ecology/10.01%3A_Microbial_Activity_and_the_Carbon_Cycle
5a52e2193166.sentence: Soil microorganisms use only a small amount of the energy from the decomposition of organic residues for building new cells.

a5e22f19b2bf.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/10%3A_Soil_Ecology/10.01%3A_Microbial_Activity_and_the_Carbon_Cycle
a5e22f19b2bf.sentence: The production of a single pound of soil organic matter from plant residues that have been amended with fertilizer nitrogen requires the total destruction of perhaps 10 to 20 pounds of plant residues to provide the energy for the process.

56e08247734a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/10%3A_Soil_Ecology/10.01%3A_Microbial_Activity_and_the_Carbon_Cycle
56e08247734a.sentence: Furthermore, whenever fresh residues are applied to soil, the decomposition of "humified" organic materials already present in the soil is accelerated.

d1a23196f332.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/10%3A_Soil_Ecology/10.01%3A_Microbial_Activity_and_the_Carbon_Cycle
d1a23196f332.sentence: The principal reasons for adding organic residues to soils are to modify the tilth of the soil, making seed bed preparation easier, to add plant nutrients, and to dispose of unusable or unwanted organic waste.

4306007f293e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/10%3A_Soil_Ecology/10.01%3A_Microbial_Activity_and_the_Carbon_Cycle
4306007f293e.sentence: Other benefits of adding organic matter to soils include improved soil structure, increased cation exchange capacity, increased water holding capacity, increased aeration, and a reduction in soil erosion.

80db699e2577.title: Ammonia fungi
80db699e2577.sentence: After ammonia application in forest soils, fungi can be classified into early phase ammonia fungi and late phase ammonia fungi depending on when they develop their fruiting bodies.

73c32002f96e.title: Ammonia fungi
73c32002f96e.sentence: Ammonia fungi develop in a specific order starting with anamorphic fungi, cup fungi (Ascomycota), and agaric fungi with small basidiomata.

0b5e8c198658.title: Ammonia fungi
0b5e8c198658.sentence: Anamorphic fungi develop first, being able to handle pH conditions above 8.

af292bb902f1.title: Ammonia fungi
af292bb902f1.sentence: Once they are able to reduce the pH to 7, ascomycota fungi develop.

200c025bf840.title: Ammonia fungi
200c025bf840.sentence: After the ascomycota fungi reduce the pH to 6, the smaller basidiomycota develop.

24ee09fc881c.title: Ammonia fungi
24ee09fc881c.sentence: EP fungi can develop anywhere from 20 to 200 days after the application of urea.

268520ce375c.title: Ammonia fungi
268520ce375c.sentence: These species occupy alkaline to neutral soils that have higher ammonium-nitrogen concentrations.

9cbf8f279f1c.title: Ammonia fungi
9cbf8f279f1c.sentence: EP ammonia fungi typically only occur in one cycle.

e65aeb7fef09.title: Ammonia fungi
e65aeb7fef09.sentence: Once the pH is in the range of 3.5–6.0 the late phase ammonia fungi, larger basidiomata, will develop, occupying weaker acidic conditions.

31f13aa1f88d.title: Ammonia fungi
31f13aa1f88d.sentence: These species are typically present 2–3 years after urea and ammonium applications.

9496085f0c95.title: Ammonia fungi
9496085f0c95.sentence: LP fungi use ammonium within the soil to develop and begin to turn it into nitrate-nitrogen gradually over time.

bba8eb8b16fe.title: Ammonia fungi
bba8eb8b16fe.sentence: Quantity and size of LP fungi are typically larger than EP fungi.

360729d7884f.title: Ammonia fungi
360729d7884f.sentence: LP ammonia fungi can occur over multiple cycles and typically last longer than EP fungi.

4cc85ca9636e.title: Ammonia fungi
4cc85ca9636e.sentence: LP fungi are biotrophic with few being saprobic.

7005ad69a5d3.title: Microarthropods
7005ad69a5d3.sentence: Microarthropods (from Micro… and Arthropods) are a special size group of small invertebrates of the phylum arthropods.

6efc1b11a082.title: Microarthropods
6efc1b11a082.sentence: Their sizes (usually from one to several millimeters) determine their habitats (usually soils), ecological features and methods of study.

36db2685eae3.title: Microarthropods
36db2685eae3.sentence: Microarthropods include mainly the following groups:

5039fcf0d12c.title: Microarthropods
5039fcf0d12c.sentence: - Soil mites: Oribatida, Mesostigmata, acariform mites and other small Arachnids

0f0a90cf39ed.title: Microarthropods
0f0a90cf39ed.sentence: Microarthropods are able to move only within existing pores in the soil.

bc74185e7282.title: Microarthropods
bc74185e7282.sentence: Microarthropods are found almost everywhere, most often in fallen leaves, soil litter and upper soil layers.

8567c3b10779.title: Microarthropods
8567c3b10779.sentence: They play an important role in accelerating the decomposition of organic matter and forming the soil structure.

0368363d1848.title: Microarthropods
0368363d1848.sentence: Microarthropod communities are bioindicators of environmental assessment, as they are very sensitive to changes in ecosystems.

8ca08675aed8.title: Mite
8ca08675aed8.sentence: Mites are small arachnids (eight-legged arthropods) of two large orders, the Acariformes and the Parasitiformes, which were historically grouped together in the subclass Acari.

9dd8ab7d24cb.title: Mite
9dd8ab7d24cb.sentence: The small size of most species makes them easily overlooked; some species live in water, many live in soil as decomposers, others live on plants, sometimes creating galls, while others are predators or parasites.

4786e7fdc944.title: Mite
4786e7fdc944.sentence: The mites living in soil consist of a range of taxa.

8fdc9aa82c72.title: Mite
8fdc9aa82c72.sentence: Oribatida and Prostigmata are more numerous in soil than Mesostigmata, and have more soil-dwelling species.

ad9e92b99fec.title: Mite
ad9e92b99fec.sentence: They inhabit organic debris of all kinds and are extremely numerous in leaf litter.

e1f36c9d57bb.title: Mite
e1f36c9d57bb.sentence: When soil is affected by an ecological disturbance such as agriculture, most mites (Astigmata, Mesostigmata and Prostigmata) recolonise it within a few months, whereas Oribatida take multiple years.

0640682d3568.title: Mite
0640682d3568.sentence: The majority are beneficial, living in the soil or aqueous environments and assisting in the decomposition of decaying organic material, as part of the carbon cycle.

92199d48c180.title: Mite
92199d48c180.section: Relationship with humans > Biological pest control
92199d48c180.sentence: Among the Laelapidae, Gaeolaelaps aculeifer and Stratiolaelaps scimitus are used to control fungus gnats, poultry red mites and various soil pests.

c9173eccf581.title: Nematophagous fungus
c9173eccf581.sentence: Nematophagous fungi are carnivorous fungi specialized in trapping and digesting nematodes.

9b75423ff218.title: Nematophagous fungus
9b75423ff218.sentence: Species exist that live inside the nematodes from the beginning and others that catch them, mostly with glue traps or in rings, some of which constrict on contact.

4920d2a56ef4.title: Nematophagous fungus
4920d2a56ef4.sentence: They employ techniques such as adhesive hyphal strands, adhesive knobs, adhesive nets formed from hyphal threads, loops of hyphae which tighten round any ensnared nematodes and non-constricting loops.

42e787f30fb0.title: Nematophagous fungus
42e787f30fb0.sentence: Another technique is to stun the nematodes using toxins, a method employed by Coprinus comatus, Stropharia rugosoannulata, and the family Pleurotaceae.

3043ec9d73ff.title: Nematophagous fungus
3043ec9d73ff.sentence: Some are parasitic, using their spores to gain entry into their prey, and some are egg parasites, inserting their hyphal tips into the eggs or cysts, or into females before the eggs are deposited.

c2dfadf84532.title: Nematophagous fungus
c2dfadf84532.sentence: Nematode-trapping fungi are mostly concentrated in the upper part of the soil, in pastures, leaf litter, mangroves and certain shallow aquatic habitats.

5878c1bb9504.title: Nematophagous fungus
5878c1bb9504.sentence: Fungi that feed on nematodes (as the most abundant and convenient prey species) mostly live in nitrogen-deficient habitats.

7a38deeef672.title: Nematophagous fungus
7a38deeef672.sentence: Arthrobotrys oligospora, a net-building species of fungus, can detect the presence of nematodes nearby in the soil and only builds its snares when they are present.

60f05a0725b9.title: Nematophagous fungus
60f05a0725b9.sentence: This is presumably because building the net is a highly energy-consuming process; the fungus is alerted to the presence of the nematode by detecting the pheromones, such as ascarosides, with which the worms communicate.

874c0a257e63.title: Nematophagous fungus
874c0a257e63.sentence: Some species of nematophagous fungi are being investigated for use in biological pest control.

f3df65b0a7d3.title: Nematophagous fungus
f3df65b0a7d3.sentence: Purpureocillium lilacinum, for example, infests the plant-parasitic Meloidogyne incognita, which attacks the roots of many cultivated plants.

35f870a77d80.title: Nematophagous fungus
35f870a77d80.sentence: Trials have provided varying results, with some strains being aggressive and others less pathogenic, and some strains that appeared promising in the lab proved ineffective in the field.

98cc9f9bb705.title: Phospholipid-derived fatty acids
98cc9f9bb705.sentence: Phospholipid-derived fatty acids (PLFAs) are widely used in microbial ecology as chemotaxonomic markers of bacteria and other organisms.

b98d31d3b87d.title: Phospholipid-derived fatty acids
b98d31d3b87d.sentence: PLFA analysis is a technique widely used for estimation of the total biomass and to observe broad changes in the community composition of the living microbiota of soil and aqueous environments.

026b3d9aa796.title: Phospholipid-derived fatty acids
026b3d9aa796.sentence: The basic premise is that as individual organisms (especially bacteria and fungi) die, phospholipids are rapidly degraded and the remaining phospholipid content of the sample is assumed to be from living organisms.

94aca1438ce6.title: Phospholipid-derived fatty acids
94aca1438ce6.sentence: Phospholipids can be saponified, which releases the fatty acids contained in their diglyceride tail.

17f1a6cd4410.title: Phospholipid-derived fatty acids
17f1a6cd4410.sentence: Once the phospholipids of an unknown sample are saponified, the composition of the resulting PLFA can be compared to the PLFA of known organisms to determine the identity of the sample organism.

364432af0a70.title: Phospholipid-derived fatty acids
364432af0a70.sentence: PLFA analysis was pioneered by D.C. White at the University of Tennessee, in the early to mid 1980s.

118853bf2a1d.title: Phospholipid-derived fatty acids
118853bf2a1d.section: Phospholipid fatty acid analysis > Background of PLFA analysis
118853bf2a1d.sentence: A 1965 article proposed using molecules produced by the organisms as biomarkers for the microbial communities.

8941cfc9cc32.title: Phospholipid-derived fatty acids
8941cfc9cc32.sentence: Soil microbial community analysis by PLFA has been a widely used technique due to the sensitive, reproducible measurement of the dominant portions of the soil microbiota and the fact that PLFA does not require cultivation of the organisms.

f4b9ebf80302.title: Phospholipid-derived fatty acids
f4b9ebf80302.sentence: Sampling of soil populations by culturing has proven not cost effective and results in biased results due to the differing ease of culturing of some organisms.

fe7229739bb1.title: Phospholipid-derived fatty acids
fe7229739bb1.section: Phospholipid fatty acid analysis > PLFA sample preparation
fe7229739bb1.sentence: The lipids were extracted from the dried soil sample by use of a chloroform-methanol-phosphate buffer mixture by use of a brief sonication followed by shaking for 2 hours and centrifugation to pellet the soil material.

58bc50639929.title: Phospholipid-derived fatty acids
58bc50639929.section: Phospholipid fatty acid analysis > Analysis of FAMEs
58bc50639929.sentence: Gas chromatography (GC) analysis of fatty acid methyl esters (FAMEs) is the method of choice for analysis of PLFAs from soil.

8e9d823935f0.title: Phospholipid-derived fatty acids
8e9d823935f0.sentence: However, there is increasing concern that some researchers are assigning PLFAs to specific microbial classes when in fact those PLFAs are present in a broad range of life forms.

b5cf3b732fa6.title: Phospholipid-derived fatty acids
b5cf3b732fa6.sentence: Phospholipids can occur in many biological classes (such as in plant roots, fungi, as well as in soil bacteria), so care has to be taken in over-assigning PLFA biomarkers to the wrong class.

9c168c7c64e4.title: Phospholipid-derived fatty acids
9c168c7c64e4.section: The PLFA components of soil microbiota
9c168c7c64e4.sentence: However, as the phospholipids of archaea are not ester linked as in bacteria, but are ether linked, they are not significantly present in routine PLFA sample preparation which is designed to cleave ester-linked fatty acids.

e1a1e981821e.title: Phospholipid-derived fatty acids
e1a1e981821e.sentence: The main drawback of PLFA has been that the extraction time is very long and cumbersome.

e7c1299fb440.title: Phospholipid-derived fatty acids
e7c1299fb440.sentence: A new 96-well plate PLFA extraction procedure has been developed which represents a 4-to-5 fold increase in throughput over traditional PLFA extraction methods.

0103930e8eda.title: Saprotrophic bacteria
0103930e8eda.sentence: Additionally, PHO's act as an indirect hydrolases in peat bogs, which accelerate the decomposition of soil organic matter.

216dba9c652b.title: Saprotrophic bacteria
216dba9c652b.sentence: PHO's break down phenolics, which inhibit hydrolases.

a14f2d38ee51.title: Saprotrophic bacteria
a14f2d38ee51.sentence: Thus, when microorganisms are limited, decomposition is also limited.

fce57bb3ae4e.title: Saprotrophic bacteria
fce57bb3ae4e.sentence: This process has been termed an "enzymatic latch."

92bb697d1522.title: Saprotrophic bacteria
92bb697d1522.sentence: Through saprotrophic nutrition, saprotrophic bacteria release microbial extracellular enzymes (MEEs) into the environment to break down soil organic matter (SOM).

e5f423f8e8fe.title: Saprotrophic bacteria
e5f423f8e8fe.sentence: MEEs are released when an organism's energy and nutrient needs are not being met.

0889ed33763a.title: Saprotrophic bacteria
0889ed33763a.sentence: This allows for the monitoring of MEEs as an indicator of nutrient availability in soil.

ca584e1a9bbb.title: Saprotrophic bacteria
ca584e1a9bbb.sentence: - Phenol oxidases (PHO): PHOs can biodegrade or detoxify aromatic pollutants into sources of carbon.

d7626d0b474f.title: Saprotrophic bacteria
d7626d0b474f.sentence: - β-glucosidase (GLU): GLUs are involved in securing energy sources and labile carbon for microorganisms.

c2ceb281192d.title: Saprotrophic bacteria
c2ceb281192d.sentence: This is accomplished through the catalysis of the release of monosaccharides and the hydrolysis of oligosaccharides.

21af6cc0cdb8.title: Saprotrophic bacteria
21af6cc0cdb8.sentence: - Acid (alkaline) phosphatase (AP): APs can be used as indicators for P mineralization potential and availability in soil.

1b9b975a0b09.title: Saprotrophic bacteria
1b9b975a0b09.sentence: Under normal soil conditions, bacterial biomass production remains relatively steady, as the growth of microorganisms is balanced by predation and other types of cell death.

8c4446514244.title: Saprotrophic bacteria
8c4446514244.sentence: Studies on bacterial growth rates using leucine or thymidine incorporation suggest the turnover times of soil bacterial communities to be in the order of days to weeks at a temperature of around 20 °C. Other studies have estimated a longer turnover time varying between 107–160 days at 25 °C. This large discrepancy could be due to differences in the methods used for these estimations, as well as differences in the incubation temperatures, which are of utmost importance in determining growth rates.

7ab552b541dd.title: Saprotrophic bacteria
7ab552b541dd.sentence: Bacterial growth in the rhizosphere presents a special situation, as it supports the rapid proliferation of bacteria compared with the surrounding soil due to the input of root exudates into the soil.

c4d9a890c387.title: Saprotrophic bacteria
c4d9a890c387.sentence: Here, bacterial turnover times are estimated to be in the range of just 12–19 hours, with shorter times exhibited on younger roots.

4185bc921685.title: Saprotrophic bacteria
4185bc921685.sentence: Soil moisture, indicated by carbon mineralization, is positively correlated with bacterial growth, with bacterial growth increasing as soil moisture content increases.

ce9bf4ca9a92.title: Saprotrophic bacteria
ce9bf4ca9a92.sentence: For example, a study utilizing the addition of different concentrations of glucose found that bacterial growth increased significantly at low concentrations, and was inhibited at very high concentrations.

dd3d6ad93200.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/10%3A_Soil_Ecology/10.03%3A_Soil_Microorganisms
dd3d6ad93200.sentence: Soil organisms usually comprise much less than 0.5 % of the dry soil mass.

5542259b0eb2.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/10%3A_Soil_Ecology/10.03%3A_Soil_Microorganisms
5542259b0eb2.sentence: The supply of nutrients, organic material for energy, and free oxygen gas affect microbial numbers.

7f1ecbade3c8.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/10%3A_Soil_Ecology/10.03%3A_Soil_Microorganisms
7f1ecbade3c8.sentence: The optimum temperature range for decay organisms is between 70-100 °F (about 20-40 °C).

0ec81f990d3b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/10%3A_Soil_Ecology/10.03%3A_Soil_Microorganisms
0ec81f990d3b.sentence: Soil temperatures outside this range will retard the activity of most soil organisms.

29f449b8b4b8.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/10%3A_Soil_Ecology/10.03%3A_Soil_Microorganisms
29f449b8b4b8.sentence: Excessive water in soil reduces the numbers and kinds of living organisms due to poor aeration.

9f8e573bf2ec.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/10%3A_Soil_Ecology/10.03%3A_Soil_Microorganisms
9f8e573bf2ec.sentence: However, at low moisture levels soil organisms thrive better than do higher plants.

300b82bbffdc.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/10%3A_Soil_Ecology/10.03%3A_Soil_Microorganisms
300b82bbffdc.sentence: Numbers of fungi, bacteria and actinomycetes vary with soil pH.

0887eb565cb0.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/10%3A_Soil_Ecology/10.03%3A_Soil_Microorganisms
0887eb565cb0.sentence: If pH of the soil is <6.0, the fungi become the dominant soil microorganisms.

5394b7443bcc.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/10%3A_Soil_Ecology/10.03%3A_Soil_Microorganisms
5394b7443bcc.sentence: Consequently, most direct additions of organisms (inoculation) to this community will be ineffective.

236944ad7ec4.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/10%3A_Soil_Ecology/10.03%3A_Soil_Microorganisms
236944ad7ec4.sentence: Usually, microbial populations will be altered more by changing the crop growing in the soil than by adding other microorganisms.

4640e3cb6770.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/04%3A_The_Living_Soil/4.06%3A_Biological_Diversity_Abundance_Activity_and_Balance
4640e3cb6770.sentence: Diverse populations of soil organisms maintain a system of checks and balances that can keep disease organisms or parasites from becoming major plant problems.

5b6738cc4b75.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/04%3A_The_Living_Soil/4.06%3A_Biological_Diversity_Abundance_Activity_and_Balance
5b6738cc4b75.sentence: Of all the organisms in soils, only a small number of bacteria, fungi, insects and nematodes might harm plants in any given year.

537b896858f1.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/04%3A_The_Living_Soil/4.06%3A_Biological_Diversity_Abundance_Activity_and_Balance
537b896858f1.sentence: Their negative impact is reduced in a more diverse soil biome.

79dfc79570ef.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/04%3A_The_Living_Soil/4.06%3A_Biological_Diversity_Abundance_Activity_and_Balance
79dfc79570ef.sentence: Some fungi kill nematodes, and others kill insects.

72bf8431420b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/04%3A_The_Living_Soil/4.06%3A_Biological_Diversity_Abundance_Activity_and_Balance
72bf8431420b.sentence: Still others produce antibiotics that kill bacteria.

73c9aca92a8b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/04%3A_The_Living_Soil/4.06%3A_Biological_Diversity_Abundance_Activity_and_Balance
73c9aca92a8b.sentence: Many protozoa, springtails and mites feed on disease-causing fungi and bacteria.

bbbce896c34b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/04%3A_The_Living_Soil/4.06%3A_Biological_Diversity_Abundance_Activity_and_Balance
bbbce896c34b.sentence: Beneficial organisms, such as the fungus Trichoderma and the bacteria Pseudomonas fluorescens, colonize plant roots and protect them from attack by harmful organisms.

b8dd26550c32.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/04%3A_The_Living_Soil/4.06%3A_Biological_Diversity_Abundance_Activity_and_Balance
b8dd26550c32.sentence: Some of these organisms or their byproducts, such as the insect-attacking chemical produced by Bacillus thuringiensis (BT), are now sold commercially as biological control agents.

50e8f85c48c6.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/04%3A_The_Living_Soil/4.06%3A_Biological_Diversity_Abundance_Activity_and_Balance
50e8f85c48c6.sentence: (Plants have also been genetically engineered to produce the toxin that BT produces in order to control crop-eating insects.) The effects of bacteria and fungi that suppress plant disease organisms are thought to arise from competition for nutrients, production of antagonistic substances, and/or direct parasitism.

040a0fff8743.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/04%3A_The_Living_Soil/4.06%3A_Biological_Diversity_Abundance_Activity_and_Balance
040a0fff8743.sentence: In addition, a number of beneficial soil organisms induce the immune systems of plants to defend the plants (systemic acquired resistance; see discussion in Chapter 8).

b3b22054b0ba.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/04%3A_The_Living_Soil/4.05%3A_Plant_Roots
b3b22054b0ba.sentence: Conversely, plant roots also influence the soil in which they grow.

002601cf235e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/04%3A_The_Living_Soil/4.05%3A_Plant_Roots
002601cf235e.sentence: The physical pressure of roots growing through soil helps form aggregates by bringing particles closer together.

647c6bc2f9ed.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/04%3A_The_Living_Soil/4.05%3A_Plant_Roots
647c6bc2f9ed.sentence: Small roots also help bind particles together.

f6d135e2d852.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/04%3A_The_Living_Soil/4.05%3A_Plant_Roots
f6d135e2d852.sentence: Root hairs, those small protrusions that grow from the outermost root layer (the epidermis), enable better access to water and nutrients by providing more contact with soil, and help form aggregates.

041cf1723474.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/04%3A_The_Living_Soil/4.05%3A_Plant_Roots
041cf1723474.sentence: In addition, many organic compounds are given off, or exuded, by plant roots and provide nourishment for soil organisms living on or near the roots.

20d1b29c5724.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/04%3A_The_Living_Soil/4.05%3A_Plant_Roots
20d1b29c5724.sentence: The zone surrounding roots is one of especially great numbers and activity of organisms that live off root exudates and sloughed-off cells.

2ea64a136fd3.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/04%3A_The_Living_Soil/4.05%3A_Plant_Roots
2ea64a136fd3.sentence: During early to mid-season, corn plants send about 20 percent of the sugars produced during photosynthesis to the roots.

2f2e6aba1434.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/04%3A_The_Living_Soil/4.05%3A_Plant_Roots
2f2e6aba1434.sentence: A sticky layer surrounding roots, called the mucigel, provides close contact between microorganisms, soil minerals and the plant (Figure 4.4).

70554e0f1658.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/04%3A_The_Living_Soil/4.05%3A_Plant_Roots
70554e0f1658.sentence: Plant roots also contribute to organic matter accumulation.

40ec149ff9f8.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/04%3A_The_Living_Soil/4.05%3A_Plant_Roots
40ec149ff9f8.sentence: They are usually well distributed in the soil and may be slower to decompose than surface residues, even if incorporated by plowing or harrowing.

04c420187757.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/04%3A_The_Living_Soil/4.05%3A_Plant_Roots
04c420187757.sentence: For plants with extensive root systems, such as grasses, the amount of living tissue below ground may actually be greater than the amount of leaves and stems we see above ground.

6b506f697403.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/04%3A_The_Living_Soil/4.05%3A_Plant_Roots
6b506f697403.sentence: Plant roots will not grow well if the soil is compact, is low in nutrients or water, includes high populations of root pathogens, has high or low pH, or has other problems.

cd8c8a7d31a1.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/10%3A_Soil_Ecology/10.12%3A_Activity_5_-_Winogradsky_Columns
cd8c8a7d31a1.sentence: Winogradsky columns will be set up-simple devices for constructing a stratified ecosystem-that illustrate different types of microbial metabolism in a colorful way.

4f8d8f48fb46.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/10%3A_Soil_Ecology/10.12%3A_Activity_5_-_Winogradsky_Columns
4f8d8f48fb46.sentence: Four Winogradsky columns will be set up: a control column and columns that contain added carbon, added sulfur, and carbon and sulfur.

a338179aa224.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/10%3A_Soil_Ecology/10.12%3A_Activity_5_-_Winogradsky_Columns
a338179aa224.sentence: - The newspaper contains cellulose, a source of carbon

0797ecbae6c2.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/10%3A_Soil_Ecology/10.12%3A_Activity_5_-_Winogradsky_Columns
0797ecbae6c2.sentence: - Egg yolk is a source of calcium sulfate in the column

d2794120d8d6.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/10%3A_Soil_Ecology/10.12%3A_Activity_5_-_Winogradsky_Columns
d2794120d8d6.sentence: - Winogradsky columns form oxygen concentration gradients.

97f1961bc5ab.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/10%3A_Soil_Ecology/10.12%3A_Activity_5_-_Winogradsky_Columns
97f1961bc5ab.sentence: - Winogradsky columns form sulfide concentration gradients as well.

78c6d737b36c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/10%3A_Soil_Ecology/10.12%3A_Activity_5_-_Winogradsky_Columns
78c6d737b36c.sentence: - Purple sulfur bacteria and green sulfur bacteria are two types of bacteria that use sulfide to support photosynthesis.

7f6047ea6a55.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/10%3A_Soil_Ecology/10.12%3A_Activity_5_-_Winogradsky_Columns
7f6047ea6a55.sentence: In general, green sulfur bacteria tolerate higher levels of sulfide than purple sulfur bacteria do.

b827678230e4.title: Sergei Winogradsky
b827678230e4.sentence: The Winogradsky column remains an important display of chemoautotrophy and microbial ecology, demonstrated in microbiology lectures around the world.

e4168db0acaf.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/04%3A_The_Living_Soil/4.02%3A_Soil_Microorganisms
e4168db0acaf.sentence: Some types of free-living bacteria are able to take nitrogen gas from the atmosphere and convert it into a form that plants can use to make amino acids and proteins.

e44971117a11.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/04%3A_The_Living_Soil/4.02%3A_Soil_Microorganisms
e44971117a11.sentence: Unfortunately, neither animals nor plants can use nitrogen gas (N2) for their nutrition.

c8519fd261b4.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/04%3A_The_Living_Soil/4.02%3A_Soil_Microorganisms
c8519fd261b4.sentence: Nor can plants use the nitrogen tied up as part of an organic molecule.

2ed7baf5d1dc.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/04%3A_The_Living_Soil/4.02%3A_Soil_Microorganisms
2ed7baf5d1dc.sentence: It needs to be converted to the inorganic forms of ammonium and nitrate to become available for plants to use.

552f5554f4e8.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/04%3A_The_Living_Soil/4.02%3A_Soil_Microorganisms
552f5554f4e8.sentence: This process involves bacteria and is called nitrogen mineralization.

c5f4a5b92541.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/04%3A_The_Living_Soil/4.02%3A_Soil_Microorganisms
c5f4a5b92541.sentence: Azospirillum and Azotobacter are two groups of free-living, nitrogen-fixing bacteria.

f6ac6a6aa6b4.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/04%3A_The_Living_Soil/4.02%3A_Soil_Microorganisms
f6ac6a6aa6b4.sentence: Along with supplying N, Azospirillum attaches to the root surfaces and promotes plant growth by producing a number of substances that help plants better tolerate various kinds of stress.

cdfe44b95915.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/04%3A_The_Living_Soil/4.02%3A_Soil_Microorganisms
cdfe44b95915.sentence: While these types of bacteria provide only a modest amount of nitrogen to the soil, this N addition is quite important to natural systems where nutrient cycling is efficient.

e1b470f48514.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/04%3A_The_Living_Soil/4.02%3A_Soil_Microorganisms
e1b470f48514.sentence: One such symbiotic relationship that is very important to agriculture involves the nitrogen-fixing rhizobia group of bacteria that live inside nodules formed on the roots of legumes.

d9ed0c06305c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/04%3A_The_Living_Soil/4.02%3A_Soil_Microorganisms
d9ed0c06305c.sentence: The symbiotic bacteria provide nitrogen in a form that leguminous plants can use, while the legume provides the bacteria with sugars for energy.

0415446719c2.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/04%3A_The_Living_Soil/4.02%3A_Soil_Microorganisms
0415446719c2.sentence: In an alfalfa field, the bacteria in the plant root nodules may fix hundreds of pounds of nitrogen per acre each year.

7fb0b789f5ff.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/04%3A_The_Living_Soil/4.02%3A_Soil_Microorganisms
7fb0b789f5ff.sentence: With peas, the amount of nitrogen fixed is much lower, around 30 to 50 pounds per acre.

0b84e12e8592.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/01%3A_Digging_In/1.06%3A_Soil_Biodiversity_and_Ecology
0b84e12e8592.section: SOIL BIODIVERSITY > Who lives in the soil?
0b84e12e8592.sentence: The range of sizes of organisms in soil ecosystems spans across nearly ten orders of magnitude!

0f13ed4282a6.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/01%3A_Digging_In/1.06%3A_Soil_Biodiversity_and_Ecology
0f13ed4282a6.section: SOIL BIODIVERSITY > Who lives in the soil?
0f13ed4282a6.sentence: For example, the smallest soil bacterium is ~0.5 micrometers in diameter (0.000005 m), soil-dwelling amphibians and mammals might typically be ~10 cm long (0.1 m), plant roots are typically in the 0.1 to 10 m length range, while certain pathogenic soil forest soil fungi grow thread-like mycelia that extend up to 1 km (1000 m) and beyond!

e23947b12c8f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/01%3A_Digging_In/1.06%3A_Soil_Biodiversity_and_Ecology
e23947b12c8f.section: SOIL BIODIVERSITY > Who lives in the soil? > Soil scientists and ecologists often use the following groups to describe soil biota:
e23947b12c8f.sentence: - Microflora: bacteria and archaea (the two domains of life termed prokaryotes, that is, organisms lacking nuclei and other organelles), algae and fungi.

111cb6c77462.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/01%3A_Digging_In/1.06%3A_Soil_Biodiversity_and_Ecology
111cb6c77462.section: SOIL BIODIVERSITY > Who lives in the soil? > Soil scientists and ecologists often use the following groups to describe soil biota:

1fe9aacb901c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/01%3A_Digging_In/1.06%3A_Soil_Biodiversity_and_Ecology
1fe9aacb901c.section: SOIL BIODIVERSITY > Who lives in the soil? > Soil scientists and ecologists often use the following groups to describe soil biota:
1fe9aacb901c.sentence: - Mesofauna: metazoans (referring to the animal phylum) with body sizes typically between 0.1 and 2 mm as well as the larger predatory and omnivorous nematodes.

710be5d2f729.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/01%3A_Digging_In/1.06%3A_Soil_Biodiversity_and_Ecology
710be5d2f729.section: SOIL BIODIVERSITY > Who lives in the soil? > Soil scientists and ecologists often use the following groups to describe soil biota:
710be5d2f729.sentence: - Macrofauna: all metazoan invertebrates and members of the chordate phylum (mammals, amphibians) larger than 2 mm.

889006d82521.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/01%3A_Digging_In/1.06%3A_Soil_Biodiversity_and_Ecology
889006d82521.section: SOIL BIODIVERSITY > Who lives in the soil? > Soil scientists and ecologists often use the following groups to describe soil biota:
889006d82521.sentence: For example, whereas the group name microflora implies “little plant”, only the algae and cyanobacteria are – like plants – photoautotrophs while many soil bacteria and all soil fungi are heterotrophs.

882903d7e032.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/01%3A_Digging_In/1.06%3A_Soil_Biodiversity_and_Ecology
882903d7e032.section: SOIL BIODIVERSITY > Who lives in the soil? > Soil scientists and ecologists often use the following groups to describe soil biota:
882903d7e032.sentence: Indeed a colony of A. ostoyae growing in the soil of a Douglas fir forest in Oregon (USA) covers multiple square kilometers and might be the largest organism (by area at least) on Earth!

847d1937d706.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/01%3A_Digging_In/1.06%3A_Soil_Biodiversity_and_Ecology
847d1937d706.section: SOIL BIODIVERSITY > Who lives in the soil? > Bacteria and archaea
847d1937d706.sentence: Being similar in size (typically just a one to a few micrometers in diameter), single cellular, and lacking organelles, it took until the early 1990s before bacteria and archaea were widely recognized as being clearly distinct groups from one another.

f8d34d5cf952.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/01%3A_Digging_In/1.06%3A_Soil_Biodiversity_and_Ecology
f8d34d5cf952.section: SOIL BIODIVERSITY > Who lives in the soil? > Bacteria and archaea
f8d34d5cf952.sentence: In fact, based on DNA sequence analyses, they are as dissimilar to each other as each of them is to higher plants or animals!

71d83c0ad66a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/01%3A_Digging_In/1.06%3A_Soil_Biodiversity_and_Ecology
71d83c0ad66a.section: SOIL BIODIVERSITY > Who lives in the soil? > Bacteria and archaea
71d83c0ad66a.sentence: Carl Woese from the University of Illinois (U.S.A) was the principal scientific force behind the first major redrawing of the tree of life (showing relatedness among all organisms) based on DNA sequences and proposed just three main branches representing the domains Bacteria, Archaea, and Eukarya.

7c5aa884836b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/04%3A_The_Living_Soil/4.03%3A_Small_and_Medium-Size_Soil_Animals
7c5aa884836b.section: Insects and Other Small- to Medium-Size Soil Animals
7c5aa884836b.sentence: Insects are another group of animals that inhabit soils.

c59f0c3ffc00.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/04%3A_The_Living_Soil/4.03%3A_Small_and_Medium-Size_Soil_Animals
c59f0c3ffc00.section: Insects and Other Small- to Medium-Size Soil Animals
c59f0c3ffc00.sentence: Common types of soil insects include termites, springtails, ants, fly larvae and beetles.

c15d50990580.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/04%3A_The_Living_Soil/4.03%3A_Small_and_Medium-Size_Soil_Animals
c15d50990580.section: Insects and Other Small- to Medium-Size Soil Animals
c15d50990580.sentence: Many insects are secondary and tertiary consumers.

5053dcb2809c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/04%3A_The_Living_Soil/4.03%3A_Small_and_Medium-Size_Soil_Animals
5053dcb2809c.section: Insects and Other Small- to Medium-Size Soil Animals
5053dcb2809c.sentence: Springtails feed on fungi and animal remains, and in turn are food for predacious mites.

fd96fe4f631d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/04%3A_The_Living_Soil/4.03%3A_Small_and_Medium-Size_Soil_Animals
fd96fe4f631d.section: Insects and Other Small- to Medium-Size Soil Animals
fd96fe4f631d.sentence: Many beetles, in particular, eat other types of soil animals such as caterpillars, ants, aphids and slugs.

a81943cd1e44.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/04%3A_The_Living_Soil/4.03%3A_Small_and_Medium-Size_Soil_Animals
a81943cd1e44.section: Insects and Other Small- to Medium-Size Soil Animals
a81943cd1e44.sentence: Some surface-dwelling beetles feed on weed seeds in the soil, and the dung beetle famously dines on fresh manure, with some species laying eggs in balls they make from manure and then bury.

23c69da61f23.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/04%3A_The_Living_Soil/4.03%3A_Small_and_Medium-Size_Soil_Animals
23c69da61f23.section: Insects and Other Small- to Medium-Size Soil Animals
23c69da61f23.sentence: Millipedes are primary consumers of plant residues, whereas centipedes tend to feed on other organisms.

9716f33286f5.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/04%3A_The_Living_Soil/4.03%3A_Small_and_Medium-Size_Soil_Animals
9716f33286f5.section: Insects and Other Small- to Medium-Size Soil Animals
9716f33286f5.sentence: Mites may feed on food sources like fungi, other mites, and insect eggs, although some feed directly on residues.

bf0442f047df.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/04%3A_The_Living_Soil/4.03%3A_Small_and_Medium-Size_Soil_Animals
bf0442f047df.section: Insects and Other Small- to Medium-Size Soil Animals
bf0442f047df.sentence: Spiders feed mainly on insects and keep insect pests from developing into large populations.

936b51d2f586.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/04%3A_The_Living_Soil/4.03%3A_Small_and_Medium-Size_Soil_Animals
936b51d2f586.section: Insects and Other Small- to Medium-Size Soil Animals
936b51d2f586.sentence: Termites, well-known feeders of woody material, also consume decomposed organic residues in the soil.

86e3b2a78d1b.title: Phospholipid-derived fatty acids
86e3b2a78d1b.section: Phospholipid fatty acid analysis > Background of PLFA analysis
86e3b2a78d1b.sentence: PLFA analysis can be used for microbial community structure and activity through the use of “signature” fatty acids.

034562c9388c.title: Phospholipid-derived fatty acids
034562c9388c.sentence: As the phospholipids of different groups of bacteria and fungi contain a variety of somewhat unusual fatty acids, they can serve as useful biomarkers for such groups.

a34b69c7c3aa.title: Phospholipid-derived fatty acids
a34b69c7c3aa.section: The PLFA components of soil microbiota
a34b69c7c3aa.sentence: The PLFA profiles of these Gram-positive species have high percentages of biomarker branched-chain fatty acids such as 15:0 iso and 15:0 anteiso.

c666d76d3e66.title: Phospholipid-derived fatty acids
c666d76d3e66.section: The PLFA components of soil microbiota
c666d76d3e66.sentence: Thus, the sum of the iso and anteiso fatty acids in a PLFA analysis may provide an estimate of the abundance of the Gram-positive bacteria (other than actinomycetes) in the sample.

f8aa150810e2.title: Phospholipid-derived fatty acids
f8aa150810e2.section: The PLFA components of soil microbiota
f8aa150810e2.sentence: This group of bacteria produce distinctive biomarker fatty acids having a methyl branch at the 10th carbon, such as 16:0 10-methyl and 18:0 10-methyl.

58783e1ec584.title: Phospholipid-derived fatty acids
58783e1ec584.section: The PLFA components of soil microbiota
58783e1ec584.sentence: Thus, in PLFA analysis, the sum of monounsaturated and cyclopropane fatty acids may provide an estimate of the abundance of Gram-negative bacteria.

c6b9367f8ad7.title: Phospholipid-derived fatty acids
c6b9367f8ad7.section: The PLFA components of soil microbiota
c6b9367f8ad7.sentence: A high ratio of cyclopropane to monounsaturated fatty acid indicates stress conditions.

fff1e5959941.title: Phospholipid-derived fatty acids
fff1e5959941.sentence: The polyunsaturated fatty acid, 18:2 ω6c (linoleic acid), is found in soil fungi, whereas the monounsaturated fatty acid, 16:1 ω5c, is predominant in Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF).

b1e2bc11348f.title: Phospholipid-derived fatty acids
b1e2bc11348f.section: The PLFA components of soil microbiota
b1e2bc11348f.sentence: Vesicles are lipid storage organs of AMF and these and the hyphae in the soil contain the fatty acids 18:2 w6c (often used as an indicator of fungal content of the PLFA analysis) as well as containing the fatty acid 16:1 w5c which has been recommended as a biomarker for AMF (PLFA fraction:AMF hyphae and NLFA fraction:AMF spores).

b553a8c2512a.title: Phospholipid-derived fatty acids
b553a8c2512a.section: The PLFA components of soil microbiota
b553a8c2512a.sentence: Using PLFA analysis in early sampling, the bacteria- archaea consortia in rice paddy soil was about 44% aerobic bacteria, 32% facultatively anaerobic- bacteria and 24% archaea.

65653bb7cdbc.title: Phospholipid-derived fatty acids
65653bb7cdbc.section: The PLFA components of soil microbiota
65653bb7cdbc.sentence: Under longer term flooding, the levels were 27%, 36% and 37% respectively and with total biomass being significantly lower.

ccbd740605e5.title: Soil ecology
ccbd740605e5.sentence: Soil moisture also affects carbon cycling, a phenomenon known as the Birch effect.

a9adfb9719be.title: Soil respiration
a9adfb9719be.section: Regulation of soil respiration > Soil moisture
a9adfb9719be.sentence: Under high soil moisture conditions, many bacteria take in too much water causing their cell membrane to lyse, or break.

67dbec7475eb.title: Soil respiration
67dbec7475eb.section: Regulation of soil respiration > Soil moisture
67dbec7475eb.sentence: This can decrease the rate of soil respiration temporarily, but the lysis of bacteria causes for a spike in resources for many other bacteria.

352d34740852.title: Soil respiration
352d34740852.section: Regulation of soil respiration > Soil moisture
352d34740852.sentence: This rapid increase in available labile substrates causes short-term enhanced soil respiration.

d587b4dd3ff0.title: Microbial biogeography
d587b4dd3ff0.sentence: Microbial biogeography is a subset of biogeography, a field that concerns the distribution of organisms across space and time.

96c4a265ef1e.title: Microbial biogeography
96c4a265ef1e.sentence: The aim of microbial biogeography is to reveal where microorganisms live, at what abundance, and why.

5349a39d08a9.title: Microbial biogeography
5349a39d08a9.sentence: In 1934, Lourens Baas Becking, based on his own research in California's salt lakes, as well as work by others on salt lakes worldwide, concluded that "everything is everywhere, but the environment selects".

970ea63315b3.title: Microbial biogeography
970ea63315b3.sentence: Baas Becking hypothesis of cosmopolitan microbial distribution would later be challenged by other works.

04f4996e91e7.title: Microbial biogeography
04f4996e91e7.sentence: However, recent studies show clear evidence for biogeographical patterns in microbial life, which challenge this common interpretation: the existence of microbial biogeographic patterns disputes the idea that "everything is everywhere" while also supporting the idea that environmental selection includes geography as well as historical events that can leave lasting signatures on microbial communities.

decf1f5cbd5b.title: Microbial biogeography
decf1f5cbd5b.sentence: The biogeography of microorganisms (i.e., organisms that cannot be seen with the naked eye, such as fungi and bacteria) is an emerging field enabled by ongoing advancements in genetic technologies, in particular cheaper DNA sequencing with higher throughput that now allows analysis of global datasets on microbial biology at the molecular level.

db046484868a.title: Microbial biogeography
db046484868a.section: Distinct patterns > Reversed and non-monotonous latitudinal diversity gradients
db046484868a.sentence: Larger organisms tend to exhibit latitudinal gradients in species diversity, with larger biodiversity existing in the tropics and decreasing toward more temperate polar regions.

1550130009e2.title: Microbial biogeography
1550130009e2.section: Distinct patterns > Reversed and non-monotonous latitudinal diversity gradients
1550130009e2.sentence: In contrast, studies on indoor fungal communities and global topsoil microbiomes found microbial biodiversity to be significantly higher in temperate zones than in the tropics.

3e4afdd96b85.title: Microbial biogeography
3e4afdd96b85.section: Distinct patterns > Reversed and non-monotonous latitudinal diversity gradients
3e4afdd96b85.sentence: On the other hand, the strong biogeographical pattern of soil bacteria is typically attributed to changes in environmental factors such as soil pH.

96b91f6bd0d4.title: Microbial biogeography
96b91f6bd0d4.section: Distinct patterns > Reversed and non-monotonous latitudinal diversity gradients
96b91f6bd0d4.sentence: However, soil pH may be a biogeographical proxy that is affected by a soils climatic water balance, which mediates carbon inputs and the connectivity of bacterial aqueous habitats.

2c8174b07d0a.title: Microbial biogeography
2c8174b07d0a.sentence: For example, soil bacterial diversity is shaped by the carbon input and connectivity in microscale aqueous habitats.

3ad7dec27930.title: Biofilm
3ad7dec27930.sentence: > Aggregate of microorganisms in which cells that are frequently embedded within a self-produced matrix of extracellular polymeric substances (EPSs) adhere to each other and/or to a surface.

258eaa871b30.title: Biofilm
258eaa871b30.sentence: A biofilm is a syntrophic community of microorganisms in which cells stick to each other and often also to a surface.

a6c01368370a.title: Biofilm
a6c01368370a.sentence: The self-produced matrix of extracellular polymeric substances, which is also referred to as slime, is a polymeric conglomeration generally composed of extracellular biopolymers in various structural forms.

e8892758a64b.title: Biofilm
e8892758a64b.sentence: These adherent cells become embedded within a slimy extracellular matrix composed of extracellular polymeric substances (EPSs) produced by them, which are typically a polymeric combination of extracellular polysaccharides, proteins, lipids and DNA.

6aa21a53648c.title: Biofilm
6aa21a53648c.sentence: A biofilm may also be considered a hydrogel, which is a complex polymer that contains many times its dry weight in water.

8093ff9359df.title: Biofilm
8093ff9359df.sentence: Because they have a three-dimensional structure and represent a community lifestyle for microorganisms, they have been metaphorically described as "cities for microbes." The biofilm allows sharing of nutrients among its residents and serves as a physical barrier against harmful environmental interactions such as desiccation, toxins/antibiotics, bacterivory and attacks from a host body's immune system.

4e1123158e4a.title: Biofilm
4e1123158e4a.sentence: The microbial cells growing in a biofilm are physiologically distinct from planktonic cells of the same organism, which, by contrast, are single cells that may float or swim in a liquid medium.

d61522670c24.title: Biofilm
d61522670c24.sentence: The EPS matrix also traps extracellular enzymes and keeps them in close proximity to the cells.

75a06d25bbbd.title: Biofilm
75a06d25bbbd.sentence: Thus, the matrix represents an external digestion system and allows for stable synergistic microconsortia of different species.

a219851e87d5.title: Biofilm
a219851e87d5.sentence: This matrix encases the cells within it and facilitates communication among them through biochemical signals as well as gene exchange.

24e21163ebe5.title: Bacteria
24e21163ebe5.sentence: In natural environments, such as soil or the surfaces of plants, the majority of bacteria are bound to surfaces in biofilms.

dbe1b0555c6b.title: Soil microbiology
dbe1b0555c6b.sentence: The more clay minerals that are found in an area can result in a higher abundance of bacteria living as biofilms at their surface.

eab6bd659eb0.title: Biofilm
eab6bd659eb0.sentence: Bacteria that have been shown to be beneficial and form biofilms include Bacillus, Pseudomonas, and Azospirillum.

47abd995be7d.title: Biofilm
47abd995be7d.sentence: Biofilms in the rhizosphere often result in pathogen or plant induced systemic resistances.

838bcb18d206.title: Biofilm
838bcb18d206.sentence: Plants that have been colonized by PGPR forming a biofilm have gained systemic resistances and are primed for defense against pathogens.

bb636c4345c3.title: Biofilm
bb636c4345c3.sentence: Due to biofilms being one of the most widely distributed and diverse microbial communities, they are an important contributor to the cycling of ecological nutrients including nitrogen, phosphorus, carbon, and oxygen.

96b1a189bf8d.title: Biofilm
96b1a189bf8d.sentence: Biofilms can play an important role in nitrogen cycling because their specialized structures create nutrient gradients that support nitrogen transformations.

e637b324d8e2.title: Biofilm
e637b324d8e2.sentence: In these processes, nitrifying microorganisms can oxidize ammonium to nitrite and nitrate while anoxic microbes, deeper in the matrix can support dendritification where nitrate is reduced to nitrogen gas.This biofilm mediated nitrogen cycling allows biofilms to couple nitrogen transformations more efficiently and supports the release of nitrogen for surrounding organisms to use.

4e3a8d3ea397.title: Biofilm
4e3a8d3ea397.sentence: Microbial activity within a biofilm matrix can promote biomineralization, including the precipitation of calcium carbonate (CaCO3).

d1f3b4bccad6.title: Biofilm
d1f3b4bccad6.sentence: In soil, they can cause bioclogging.

a7cf4f937ea9.title: Biofilm
a7cf4f937ea9.sentence: Microbial biofilms have many industrial applications such as the detoxification of environmental pollutants and wastewater treatments.

cb930fc707d3.title: Biofilm
cb930fc707d3.sentence: Slow sand filters rely on biofilm development in the same way to filter surface water from lake, spring or river sources for drinking purposes.

dbd39d7cd359.title: Extracellular polymeric substance
dbd39d7cd359.sentence: Extracellular polymeric substances (EPS) are natural polymers of high molecular weight secreted by microorganisms into their environment.

794446900a78.title: Extracellular polymeric substance
794446900a78.sentence: EPS are mostly composed of polysaccharides (exopolysaccharides) and proteins, but include other macromolecules such as DNA, lipids and humic substances.

129e36cf0800.title: Extracellular polymeric substance
129e36cf0800.sentence: EPS constitute 50% to 90% of a biofilm's total organic matter.

530c3518a23f.title: Extracellular polymeric substance
530c3518a23f.sentence: EPS establish the functional and structural integrity of biofilms, and are considered the fundamental component that determines the physicochemical properties of a biofilm.

8d6afe7f435a.title: Extracellular polymeric substance
8d6afe7f435a.sentence: EPS in the matrix of biofilms provides compositional support and protection of microbial communities from the harsh environments.

a96be1929d0b.title: Extracellular polymeric substance
a96be1929d0b.sentence: Afterwards, as biofilm becomes established, EPS provides physical stability and resistance to mechanical removal, antimicrobials, and host immunity.

c8048009341d.title: Extracellular polymeric substance
c8048009341d.sentence: Exopolysaccharides can facilitate the attachment of nitrogen-fixing bacteria to plant roots and soil particles, which mediates a symbiotic relationship.

639cdea90705.title: Extracellular polymeric substance
639cdea90705.sentence: This is important for colonization of roots and the rhizosphere, which is a key component of soil food webs and nutrient cycling in ecosystems.

0efa800d53d3.title: Bioclogging
0efa800d53d3.section: General description > Various types of bioclogging
0efa800d53d3.sentence: - Bioclogging by microbial cell bodies (such as bacteria, algae and fungus) and their synthesized byproducts such as extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) (also referred to as slime), which form biofilm or microcolony aggregation on soil particles are direct biological causes of the decrease in hydraulic conductivity.

b21a9eb20a5f.title: Extracellular polymeric substance
b21a9eb20a5f.sentence: Sediment stability can be increased by EPS, as it influences cohesion, permeability, and erosion of the sediment.

1b237580193e.title: Extracellular polymeric substance
1b237580193e.sentence: In a geomicrobiological context, EPS have been observed to affect precipitation of minerals, particularly carbonates.

0432c4f9a4ec.title: Extracellular polymeric substance
0432c4f9a4ec.sentence: Bacterial extracellular polymeric substances can aid in bioremediation of heavy metals as they have the capacity to adsorb metal cations, among other dissolved substances.

45873cf0a782.title: Extracellular polymeric substance
45873cf0a782.sentence: This can be useful in the treatment of wastewater systems, as biofilms are able to bind to and remove metals such as copper, lead, nickel, and cadmium.

b5990bdfc249.title: Extracellular polymeric substance
b5990bdfc249.sentence: Some contaminated soils contain high levels of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAH); EPS from the bacterium Zoogloea sp. and the fungus Aspergillus niger, are efficient at removing these toxic compounds.

f04a99796431.title: Extracellular polymeric substance
f04a99796431.sentence: EPS contain enzymes such as oxidoreductase and hydrolase, which are capable of degrading PAH.

ace232b8028a.title: Biofilm
ace232b8028a.sentence: Biofilms are the product of a microbial developmental process.

49557ca9d9af.title: Biofilm
49557ca9d9af.sentence: The process is summarized by five major stages of biofilm development.

ebdf63f54417.title: Biofilm
ebdf63f54417.sentence: The initiation of development starts in the first stage of initial reversible attachment which is initiated by the attachment of planktonic cells to a surface.

69338e837a48.title: Biofilm
69338e837a48.section: Origin and formation > Formation of biofilms
69338e837a48.sentence: The first colonist bacteria of a biofilm may adhere to the surface initially by the weak van der Waals forces and hydrophobic effects.

f826d3756c92.title: Biofilm
f826d3756c92.section: Origin and formation > Formation of biofilms
f826d3756c92.sentence: If the colonists are not immediately separated from the surface, they can anchor themselves more permanently using cell adhesion structures such as pili.

90ba60bd4d2e.title: Biofilm
90ba60bd4d2e.sentence: This initial attachment is then followed by the second stage of irreversible attachment where further microbial aggregation allows cells to attach to their initial foundation.

8e11d0ffd9e4.title: Biofilm
8e11d0ffd9e4.sentence: After attachment, stages three and four of formation allow for biofilm maturation, characterized by the appearance of cell clusters embedded into a matrix before completing these stages of maturation through the evolution of micro-colonies.

5a642cb488f7.title: Biofilm
5a642cb488f7.sentence: Finally, the fifth stage of development is dispersion, allowing for a fully developed and functional microbial biofilm.

1574bf7c1e6e.title: Biofilm
1574bf7c1e6e.sentence: Dispersal enables biofilms to spread and colonize new surfaces.

f11ab31b60ec.title: Root
f11ab31b60ec.sentence: In vascular plants, the roots are the organs of a plant that are modified to provide anchorage for the plant and take in water and nutrients into the plant body, which allows plants to grow taller and faster.

9e24a6d4a02b.title: Root
9e24a6d4a02b.sentence: They are most often below the surface of the soil, but roots can also be aerial or aerating, that is, growing up above the ground or especially above water.

cb947f37da63.title: Root
cb947f37da63.sentence: Their primary functions are anchorage, uptake (absorption) of water and dissolved minerals, and conduction of these resources to the shoot.

ac8bc896bde1.title: Root
ac8bc896bde1.sentence: Beyond these, roots carry out a range of important secondary and adaptive functions — storage of reserves, synthesis of growth regulators, gas exchange in waterlogged environments, facilitation of symbiotic nutrient acquisition, and vegetative propagation.

19647ad6ee84.title: Root
19647ad6ee84.sentence: Root epidermal cells and root hairs take up soil water and dissolved ions; these are then conducted to the shoot via the xylem.

f79a585e0473.title: Root
f79a585e0473.sentence: Root architecture (depth, spread) determines access to water and nutrients in different soil horizons.

7793dd672fd1.title: Root
7793dd672fd1.sentence: The root cap of new roots helps the root penetrate the soil.

a32525b5c783.title: Root
a32525b5c783.sentence: These root caps are sloughed off as the root goes deeper creating a slimy surface that provides lubrication.

8cf44aa5012f.title: Root
8cf44aa5012f.sentence: The roots of most vascular plant species enter into symbiosis with certain fungi to form mycorrhizae, and a large range of other organisms including bacteria also closely associate with roots.

f22dc5982158.title: Root
f22dc5982158.sentence: Grass root systems are beneficial at reducing soil erosion by holding the soil together.

d828348dca7a.title: Root
d828348dca7a.sentence: Perennial grasses that grow wild in rangelands contribute organic matter to the soil when their old roots decay after attacks by beneficial fungi, protozoa, bacteria, insects and worms release nutrients.

793652d4782f.title: Root
793652d4782f.sentence: The fossil record of roots—or rather, infilled voids where roots rotted after death—spans back to the late Silurian, about 430 million years ago.

fd112fd8818b.title: Root
fd112fd8818b.sentence: Their identification is difficult, because casts and molds of roots are so similar in appearance to animal burrows.

563c03942cc7.title: Fabaceae
563c03942cc7.sentence: The c. 19,000 known legume species amount to about 7% of flowering plant species.

a60f81ce1792.title: Fabaceae
a60f81ce1792.sentence: The family Fabaceae includes a number of plants that are common in agriculture, including Glycine max (soybean), Phaseolus (beans), Pisum sativum (pea), Cicer arietinum (chickpeas), Vicia faba (broad bean), Vigna unguiculata (cowpea), Medicago sativa (alfalfa), Arachis hypogaea (peanut), Ceratonia siliqua (carob), Tamarindus indica (tamarind), Trigonella foenum-graecum (fenugreek), and Glycyrrhiza glabra (liquorice).

2aaf2ce1ac26.title: Cover crop
2aaf2ce1ac26.sentence: Green manure crops are commonly leguminous, meaning they are part of the pea family, Fabaceae.

88dcaf27a0f5.title: Fabaceae
88dcaf27a0f5.sentence: Many Fabaceae host bacteria in their roots within structures called root nodules.

022ade26ad85.title: Fabaceae
022ade26ad85.sentence: These bacteria, known as rhizobia, have the ability to take nitrogen gas (N2) out of the air and convert it to a form of nitrogen that is usable to the host plant (NO3− or NH3).

021e1ec0c48a.title: Fabaceae
021e1ec0c48a.sentence: Nodule formation is common throughout the Fabaceae.

5b5d763b0226.title: Fabaceae
5b5d763b0226.sentence: Nodule formation is present in all the Fabaceae sub-families, although it is less common in the Caesalpinioideae.

2e914ba3c240.title: Fabaceae
2e914ba3c240.sentence: Even though nodule formation is common in the two monophyletic subfamilies Papilionoideae and Mimosoideae they also contain species that do not form nodules.

90f7a5acf838.title: Fabaceae
90f7a5acf838.sentence: Rhizobia are specific to particular host species although a rhizobia species may often infect more than one host species.

5bb51ed31104.title: Fabaceae
5bb51ed31104.sentence: This means that one plant species may be infected by more than one species of bacteria.

81073f446eac.title: Fabaceae
81073f446eac.sentence: For example, nodules in Acacia senegal can contain seven species of rhizobia belonging to three different genera.

290dd6bcbe90.title: Crop rotation
290dd6bcbe90.sentence: Legumes, plants of the family Fabaceae, have nodules on their roots which contain nitrogen-fixing bacteria called rhizobia.

ae0dd28bf98e.title: Taproot
ae0dd28bf98e.sentence: A taproot is a large, central, and dominant root from which other roots sprout laterally and horizontally.

d83867805689.title: Taproot
d83867805689.sentence: Typically, a taproot is somewhat straight and very thick, is tapering in shape, and grows straight down.

7472ca03f0eb.title: Taproot
7472ca03f0eb.sentence: Dicots, one of the two divisions of flowering plants (angiosperms), start with a taproot, which is one main root forming from the enlarging radicle of the seed.

af6bc00155d8.title: Taproot
af6bc00155d8.sentence: The tap root can be persistent throughout the life of the plant but is most often replaced later in the plant's development by a fibrous root system.

84c1f6e72645.title: Taproot
84c1f6e72645.sentence: Soil characteristics strongly influence the architecture of taproots; for example, deep and rich soils favour the development of vertical taproots in many oak species such as Quercus kelloggii, while clay soils promote the growth of multiple taproots.

70493f9f5ef0.title: Taproot
70493f9f5ef0.sentence: Many taproots are modified into storage organs.

c9432ae38f13.title: Taproot
c9432ae38f13.sentence: In some plants, such as the carrot, the taproot is a storage organ so well developed that it has been cultivated as a vegetable.

0e14164f9bb9.title: Taproot
0e14164f9bb9.sentence: - Fusiform root: this root is widest in the middle and tapers towards the top and the bottom: e.g. radish.

e124c65a785d.title: Taproot
e124c65a785d.sentence: It is very broad at the top and tapers suddenly like a tail at the bottom: e.g. turnip.

ebfc699b1efb.title: Taproot
ebfc699b1efb.sentence: Many plants with taproots are difficult to transplant, or even to grow in containers, because the root tends to grow deep rapidly and in many species comparatively slight obstacles or damage to the taproot will stunt or kill the plant.

62011bd96216.title: Taproot
62011bd96216.sentence: Among weeds with taproots dandelions are typical; being deep-rooted, they are hard to uproot and if the taproot breaks off near the top, the part that stays in the ground often resprouts such that, for effective control, the taproot needs to be severed at least several centimetres below ground level.

1c54d4c45cd7.title: Fibrous root system
1c54d4c45cd7.sentence: A fibrous root system is the opposite of a taproot system.

00f82ea24fb6.title: Fibrous root system
00f82ea24fb6.sentence: It is usually formed by thin, moderately branching roots growing from the stem.

e5858883af40.title: Root
e5858883af40.section: Types of roots > Fibrous root system
