e5858883af40.sentence: A fibrous root system consists of numerous, similarly sized roots that form a dense network near the soil surface.

92d67e831d0c.title: Fibrous root system
92d67e831d0c.sentence: A fibrous root system is universal in monocotyledonous plants and ferns.

64c4da9fdc69.title: Root
64c4da9fdc69.section: Types of roots > Fibrous root system
64c4da9fdc69.sentence: Typical examples are grasses (Poaceae), wheat and rice.

f0506eeeacf1.title: Root
f0506eeeacf1.section: Types of roots > Fibrous root system
f0506eeeacf1.sentence: In many species this network is composed largely of adventitious roots that arise from the stem base rather than the primary radicle.

cc8bcbeaadd7.title: Fibrous root system
cc8bcbeaadd7.sentence: This forms a mass of fine roots, with no distinct tap root, because the embryonic root dies back while the plant is still young and growing.

58b61397f1ba.title: Taproot
58b61397f1ba.sentence: For most plants species the radicle dies some time after seed germination, causing the development of a fibrous root system, which lacks a main downward-growing root.

4b01f5f66f0b.title: Root
4b01f5f66f0b.section: Types of roots > Fibrous root system
4b01f5f66f0b.sentence: Fibrous systems are effective at soil binding, rapid uptake of surface nutrients and erosion control.

6198e24dcb38.title: Fibrous root system
6198e24dcb38.sentence: Forages have a fibrous root system, which helps combat erosion by anchoring the plants to the top layer of the soil, and covering the entirety of the field, as it is a non-row crop.

d6d885f79bd0.title: Fibrous root system
d6d885f79bd0.sentence: Most trees begin life with a taproot, but after one to a few years change to a wide-spreading fibrous root system with mainly horizontal surface roots and only a few vertical, deep anchoring roots.

3ae3192895e4.title: Fibrous root system
3ae3192895e4.sentence: A typical mature tree 30–50 m tall has a root system that extends horizontally in all directions as far as the tree is tall or more, but well over 95% of the roots are in the top 50 cm depth of soil.

f50ffcf016ab.title: Phytoremediation
f50ffcf016ab.sentence: Root mats of meadow grasses are possibly effective at demobilising radiosource materials especially with certain combinations of other agricultural practices.

291a4e390101.title: Root
291a4e390101.sentence: There is a correlation of roots using the process of plant perception to sense their physical environment to grow, including the sensing of light, and physical barriers.

22854db578cc.title: Root
22854db578cc.sentence: Plants also sense gravity and respond through auxin pathways, resulting in gravitropism.

49bb2c324922.title: Root
49bb2c324922.sentence: Gravitropism directs roots to grow downward at germination, the growth mechanism of plants that also causes the shoot to grow upward.

ee6f504ce763.title: Root
ee6f504ce763.sentence: Different types of roots such as primary, seminal, lateral and crown are maintained at different gravitropic setpoint angles i.e. the direction in which they grow.

b1be73a1d4b7.title: Root
b1be73a1d4b7.sentence: The correct environment of air, mineral nutrients and water directs plant roots to grow in any direction to meet the plant's needs.

e8802fa3aaad.title: Root
e8802fa3aaad.sentence: Roots will shy or shrink away from dry or other poor soil conditions.

7ff7d91f0315.title: Root
7ff7d91f0315.sentence: Research indicates that plant roots growing in search of productive nutrition can sense and avoid soil compaction through diffusion of the gas ethylene.

7f3251ab8432.title: Root
7f3251ab8432.sentence: Research has shown that roots have ability to recognize 'self' and 'non-self' roots in same soil environment.

1c2cb1465039.title: Root
1c2cb1465039.sentence: Over time, roots can crack foundations, snap water lines, and lift sidewalks.

3d49003bdfda.title: Root
3d49003bdfda.sentence: In its simplest form, the term root system architecture (RSA) refers to the spatial configuration of a plant's root system.

37f31a1197f8.title: Root
37f31a1197f8.sentence: This system can be extremely complex and is dependent upon multiple factors such as the species of the plant itself, the composition of the soil and the availability of nutrients.

f090edda0890.title: Root
f090edda0890.sentence: Root architecture plays the important role of providing a secure supply of nutrients and water as well as anchorage and support.

04d0f2b92937.title: Root
04d0f2b92937.section: Root system architecture > Terms and components
04d0f2b92937.sentence: The main terms used to classify the architecture of a root system are:

96fea5991ae7.title: Root
96fea5991ae7.section: Root system architecture > Terms and components
96fea5991ae7.sentence: Topology | Pattern of branching (Herringbone, Dichotomous, Radial)

57c097401367.title: Root
57c097401367.section: Root system architecture > Terms and components

c7c8b09de316.title: Root
c7c8b09de316.section: Root system architecture > Terms and components

3e8f2909fe7a.title: Root
3e8f2909fe7a.section: Root system architecture > Terms and components
3e8f2909fe7a.sentence: Root angle | Radial angle of a lateral root's base around the parent root's circumference, the angle of a lateral root from its parent root, and the angle an entire system spreads.

77d65db808e2.title: Root
77d65db808e2.section: Root system architecture > Terms and components
77d65db808e2.sentence: Extrinsic factors affecting root architecture include gravity, light exposure, water and oxygen, as well as the availability or lack of nitrogen, phosphorus, sulphur, aluminium and sodium chloride.

fa1f330fff3b.title: Root
fa1f330fff3b.sentence: For example, a root system that has developed in dry soil may not be as efficient in flooded soil, yet plants are able to adapt to other changes in the environment, such as seasonal changes.

73659a9004dd.title: Root
73659a9004dd.sentence: The distribution of vascular plant roots within soil depends on plant form, the spatial and temporal availability of water and nutrients, and the physical properties of the soil.

fc83b9a5e7c1.title: Root
fc83b9a5e7c1.sentence: The majority of roots on most plants are however found relatively close to the surface where nutrient availability and aeration are more favourable for growth.

bc18370ca6d1.title: Root
bc18370ca6d1.sentence: Rooting depth may be physically restricted by rock or compacted soil close below the surface, or by anaerobic soil conditions.

9ab86d7b955d.title: Root
9ab86d7b955d.sentence: The deepest roots are generally found in deserts and temperate coniferous forests; the shallowest in tundra, boreal forest and temperate grasslands.

52d80754e32c.title: Active layer
52d80754e32c.sentence: This is important because roots of plants cannot penetrate beyond the active layer and are restricted by its thickness.

177ee844344f.title: Active layer
177ee844344f.sentence: Thus, in a continuous permafrost environment plants must have shallow roots, which restricts tree growth to specialised species such as Larix.

51f3bf3d6970.title: Root
51f3bf3d6970.sentence: Some roots can grow as deep as the tree is high.

d11921e1b187.title: Root
d11921e1b187.sentence: The deepest observed living root, at least 60 metres (200 ft) below the ground surface, was observed during the excavation of an open-pit mine in Arizona, US.

ef31ea790b52.title: Root
ef31ea790b52.sentence: The roots, or parts of roots, of many plant species have become specialized to serve adaptive purposes besides the two primary functions, described in the introduction.

3081bb7a63a4.title: Root
3081bb7a63a4.sentence: The two classical, broad categories are taproot and fibrous systems, but several specialised root types — notably adventitious, aerial, prop/stilt, climbing/adhesive, buttress, tuberous (storage) and floating roots — are biologically and ecologically important.

a4afe658e966.title: Root
a4afe658e966.sentence: - Proteoid roots or cluster roots: dense clusters of rootlets of limited growth that develop under low phosphate or low iron conditions in Proteaceae and some plants from the following families Betulaceae, Casuarinaceae, Elaeagnaceae, Moraceae, Fabaceae and Myricaceae.

90fb6f94eb45.title: Root
90fb6f94eb45.sentence: - Aerating roots (or knee root or knee or pneumatophores): roots rising above the ground, especially above water such as in some mangrove genera (Avicennia, Sonneratia).

2bf25b1a9a29.title: Root
2bf25b1a9a29.sentence: Specialised structures (pneumatophores, aerial roots) permit gas exchange where soil oxygen is limited, enabling respiration in mangroves and other hydrophytes.

e1f1c4ed7b8d.title: Root
e1f1c4ed7b8d.sentence: - Root nodules: roots that harbor nitrogen-fixing soil bacteria.

4736434bb5d3.title: Root
4736434bb5d3.sentence: Root nodules are found in virtually all legumes.

b3cbd7bba138.title: Root
b3cbd7bba138.sentence: - Coralloid roots: similar to root nodules, these provide nitrogen to the plant.

e09ac488f6c8.title: Root
e09ac488f6c8.sentence: They are often larger than nodules, branched, and located at or near the soil surface, and harbor nitrogen-fixing cyanobacteria.

d698110ff94d.title: Root
d698110ff94d.sentence: - Contractile roots: roots that pull bulbs or corms of monocots, such as hyacinth and lily, and some taproots, such as dandelion, deeper in the soil through expanding radially and contracting longitudinally.

aac80930e87f.title: Root hair
aac80930e87f.sentence: Root hairs or absorbent hairs, are outgrowths of epidermal cells, specialized cells at the tip of a plant root.

05570880994d.title: Root hair
05570880994d.sentence: They are lateral extensions of a single cell and are only rarely branched.

396973fb596a.title: Root hair
396973fb596a.sentence: The function of all root hairs is to collect water and mineral nutrients in the soil to be sent throughout the plant.

9eb4c0117e8a.title: Root hair
9eb4c0117e8a.sentence: Root hair cells improve plant water absorption by increasing root surface area to volume ratio which allows the root hair cell to take in more water.

62ca79b72bb8.title: Root hair
62ca79b72bb8.sentence: In roots, most water absorption happens through the root hairs.

4401a9477523.title: Root hair
4401a9477523.sentence: Root hair cells vary between 15 and 17 micrometers in diameter, and 80 and 1,500 micrometers in length.

48a782819646.title: Root hair
48a782819646.sentence: The length of root hairs allows them to penetrate between soil particles and prevents harmful bacterial organisms from entering the plant through the xylem vessels.

a3d8aa1cff3f.title: Root hair
a3d8aa1cff3f.sentence: Root hairs are found only in the zone of maturation, also called the zone of differentiation.

16a53d582bbe.title: Root hair
16a53d582bbe.sentence: They are not found in the zone of elongation, possibly because older root hairs are sheared off as the root elongates and moves through the soil.

d6ba594b77ce.title: Root hair
d6ba594b77ce.sentence: Root hair cells also secrete acids (e.g., malic and citric acid), which solubilize minerals by changing their oxidation state, making the ions easier to absorb.

b76a69cc651d.title: Root hair
b76a69cc651d.sentence: Root hairs are also important for nutrient uptake as they are main interface between plants and mycorrhizal fungi.

118d8efe4e17.title: Root hair
118d8efe4e17.sentence: Formation of this relationship for EM fungi begins with the colonization of the root hairs.

34c34d2e98fb.title: Root hair
34c34d2e98fb.sentence: The fungus then secretes diffusible factors, to which root hairs are highly sensitive, allowing the hyphae to penetrate into the epidermal cells and create a Hartig net in the first layers of the root cortex.

5006609d43e4.title: Root hair
5006609d43e4.sentence: They are also directly involved in the formation of root nodules in legume plants.

086d0cb6ac22.title: Root hair
086d0cb6ac22.sentence: The root hairs curl around the bacteria, which allows for the formation of an infection thread into the dividing cortical cells to form the nodule.

9574faedd5b1.title: Root hair
9574faedd5b1.sentence: Repotting or transplanting a plant can result in root hair cells being pulled off, perhaps to a significant extent, which can cause wilting.

40739675e0b4.title: Plant hormone
40739675e0b4.sentence: Plant hormones (or phytohormones) are signal molecules, produced within plants, that occur in extremely low concentrations.

4c491f786a70.title: Plant hormone
4c491f786a70.sentence: Plant hormones control all aspects of plant growth and development, including embryogenesis, the regulation of organ size, pathogen defense, stress tolerance and reproductive development.

85747a37f2e6.title: Plant hormone
85747a37f2e6.sentence: Unlike in animals (in which hormone production is restricted to specialized glands) each plant cell is capable of producing hormones.

ffcaacf370bb.title: Plant hormone
ffcaacf370bb.sentence: Plant hormones are not nutrients, but chemicals that in small amounts promote and influence the growth, development, and differentiation of cells and tissues.

82c2b90a74cd.title: Plant hormone
82c2b90a74cd.sentence: They are naturally produced within plants, though very similar chemicals are produced by fungi and bacteria that can also affect plant growth.

8eefdc4cb9be.title: Plant hormone
8eefdc4cb9be.sentence: Some phytohormones also occur in microorganisms, such as unicellular fungi and bacteria, however in these cases they do not play a hormonal role and can better be regarded as secondary metabolites.

4ebfa720407d.title: Plant hormone
4ebfa720407d.sentence: Auxins are compounds that positively influence cell enlargement, bud formation, and root initiation.

16659ae974d2.title: Plant hormone
16659ae974d2.sentence: Auxins act to inhibit the growth of buds lower down the stems in a phenomenon known as apical dominance, and also to promote lateral and adventitious root development and growth.

2c2a2e8ace80.title: Plant hormone
2c2a2e8ace80.sentence: Auxins, especially 1-naphthaleneacetic acid (NAA) and indole-3-butyric acid (IBA), are also commonly applied to stimulate root growth when taking cuttings of plants.

17f8a70b931b.title: Plant hormone
17f8a70b931b.sentence: Most commonly they are commercially available as "rooting hormone powder".

3a642bf085ad.title: Plant hormone
3a642bf085ad.sentence: Soon after plants are water-stressed and the roots are deficient in water, a signal moves up to the leaves, causing the formation of ABA precursors there, which then move to the roots.

2082c8608812.title: Plant hormone
2082c8608812.sentence: The roots then release ABA, which is translocated to the foliage through the vascular system and modulates potassium and sodium uptake within the guard cells, which then lose turgidity, closing the stomata.

f9dbc0d09fbb.title: Plant hormone
f9dbc0d09fbb.sentence: In plants under water stress, ABA plays a role in closing the stomata.

f812535e71be.title: Plant hormone
f812535e71be.sentence: Ethylene affects cell growth and cell shape; when a growing shoot or root hits an obstacle while underground, ethylene production greatly increases, preventing cell elongation and causing the stem to swell.

0976b6bde810.title: Plant hormone
0976b6bde810.sentence: It was later shown that SLs that are exuded into the soil also promote the growth of symbiotic arbuscular mycorrhizal (AM) fungi.

263225e64d43.title: Plant hormone
263225e64d43.sentence: Went and Thimann coined the term "phytohormone" and used it in the title of their 1937 book.

af53328179e9.title: Hydraulic redistribution
af53328179e9.sentence: Hydraulic redistribution is a passive mechanism where water is transported from moist to dry soils via subterranean networks.

e041db135178.title: Hydraulic redistribution
e041db135178.sentence: It occurs in vascular plants that commonly have roots in both wet and dry soils, especially plants with both taproots that grow vertically down to the water table, and lateral roots that sit close to the surface.

7fb2a424b3d6.title: Hydraulic redistribution
7fb2a424b3d6.sentence: In drought conditions, ground water is drawn up through the taproot to the laterals and exuded into the surface soil, replenishing that which was lost.

489393725b4c.title: Hydraulic redistribution
489393725b4c.sentence: Under flooding conditions, plant roots perform a similar function in the opposite direction.

d7f28bc3cb84.title: Hydraulic redistribution
d7f28bc3cb84.sentence: In plants that exhibit hydraulic redistribution, there are xylem pathways from the taproots to the laterals, such that the absence or abundance of water at the laterals creates a pressure potential analogous to that of transpirational pull.

5dccc8c580fa.title: Hydraulic redistribution
5dccc8c580fa.sentence: At that time, the hydraulic lift was described as the movement of water and soil nutrients from a vascularized host into the soil at night mostly.

c255804307fb.title: Hydraulic redistribution
c255804307fb.sentence: Then after studies in the 2000s, a more comprehensive word was taken into consideration where it described a bi-directional and passive movement exhibited by the plant roots and further assisted by mycorrhizal networks.

aea03afde484.title: Hydraulic redistribution
aea03afde484.sentence: Since then it was found that vascular plants are assisted by fungal networks which grow on the root system to promote water redistribution.

ea10a0c948f0.title: Hydraulic redistribution
ea10a0c948f0.sentence: The plant roots have been shown to smooth or homogenize the soil moisture.

fa96a284ae37.title: Hydraulic redistribution
fa96a284ae37.sentence: Water redistribution by plant roots has been found influencing crop irrigation, where watering schemes leave a harsh heterogeneity in soil moisture.

e51d277f4081.title: Hydraulic redistribution
e51d277f4081.sentence: This influencing process also assist in seedling success.

0f44fe92bef2.title: Hydraulic redistribution
0f44fe92bef2.sentence: Traditional methods of observating hydraulic redistribution include Deuterium isotope traces, sap flow, and soil moisture.

5a3b69af0eca.title: Hydraulic redistribution
5a3b69af0eca.sentence: Due to the ecological significance of hydraulically redistributed water, there is an ongoing effort to continue the categorization of plants exhibiting this behaviour and adapting this physiological process into land-surface models to improve model predictions.

c03287316082.title: Mutualism (biology)
c03287316082.sentence: Mutualism describes the ecological interaction between two or more species where each species has a net benefit.

c2546629cf06.title: Mutualism (biology)
c2546629cf06.sentence: - about 80% of land plants species rely on mycorrhizal relationships with fungi to provide them with inorganic compounds and trace elements.

9331235b294f.title: Mutualism (biology)
9331235b294f.sentence: Mutualistic relationships can be thought of as a form of "biological barter" in mycorrhizal associations between plant roots and fungi, with the plant providing carbohydrates to the fungus in return for primarily phosphate but also nitrogenous compounds.

f84cee2a5be2.title: Mutualism (biology)
f84cee2a5be2.sentence: Other examples include rhizobia bacteria that fix nitrogen for leguminous plants (family Fabaceae) in return for energy-containing carbohydrates.

af11bebaaeb6.title: Mutualism (biology)
af11bebaaeb6.sentence: For example, beans may grow up cornstalks as a trellis, while fixing nitrogen in the soil for the corn, a phenomenon that is used in Three Sisters farming.

599c8afa5702.title: Mutualism (biology)
599c8afa5702.sentence: Mutualism has also been linked to major evolutionary events, such as the evolution of the eukaryotic cell (symbiogenesis) and the colonization of land by plants in association with mycorrhizal fungi.

b0996590cb1b.title: Mutualism (biology)
b0996590cb1b.sentence: For example, plant lineages inhabiting nutrient-rich environments have evolutionarily abandoned mycorrhizal mutualisms many times independently.

5879e14e6f2f.title: Mutualism (biology)
5879e14e6f2f.sentence: Under certain conditions species of fungi previously in a state of mutualism can turn parasitic on weak or dying plants.

be7b568ae8fa.title: Root mucilage
be7b568ae8fa.sentence: Plant roots secrete a variety of organic molecules into the surrounding soil, such as proteins, enzymes, DNA, sugars and amino acids, which are the building blocks of life.

5f3978604f86.title: Root mucilage
5f3978604f86.sentence: This collective secretion is known as root exudate.

dcf1cec57c3b.title: Root mucilage
dcf1cec57c3b.sentence: This root exudate prevents root infection from bacteria and fungi, helps the roots to penetrate through the soil, and can create a micro-climate that is beneficial to the plant.

62fa9e8042c7.title: Soil formation
62fa9e8042c7.sentence: Plant root exudation supports microbial activity.

47f0ca9c7079.title: Soil carbon
47f0ca9c7079.section: Forms of Carbon in Soil > Organic carbon
47f0ca9c7079.sentence: Root exudates are another source of soil carbon.

9aa110b3b81a.title: Rhizosphere
9aa110b3b81a.sentence: Plant root exudates, such as organic acids, change the chemical structure and the biological communities of the rhizosphere in comparison with the bulk soil or parent soil.

8a2c47f19bf1.title: Disease suppressive soils
8a2c47f19bf1.sentence: Different species of plants release different exudates and therefore recruit different microbial communities to their rhizosphere from the microbes already present in the surrounding bulk soil.

28ad4d84b278.title: Plant nutrients in soil
28ad4d84b278.sentence: The soil mineral apatite is the most common mineral source of phosphorus, from which it can be extracted by microbial and root exudates, with an important contribution of arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi.

a8d4547978e5.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
a8d4547978e5.sentence: The growth of AM hyphae through the soil is controlled by host root exudates known as strigolactones, and the soil phosphorus concentration.

e2613725731d.title: Plant root exudates
e2613725731d.sentence: Quantifying how much photosynthetically fixed carbon is transferred to soil via plant root exudates is difficult, but 5% can be considered a rough estimate.

0e9b31518c11.title: Plant root exudates
0e9b31518c11.sentence: Arabidopsis seedlings grown in non-sibling exudates produced more lateral roots compared to those grown in exudates of kin or self-origin.

5bdbb9d1725d.title: Plant root exudates
5bdbb9d1725d.sentence: The Arabidopsis seedlings are capable of detecting the exudates around them and responding accordingly.

2efc37e3ae64.title: Plant root exudates
2efc37e3ae64.sentence: This ability may be beneficial for fitness, allowing plants to allocate fewer resources to competition when grown amongst kin.

72f369beb483.title: Rhizosphere
72f369beb483.sentence: The rhizosphere is the narrow region of soil or substrate that is directly influenced by root secretions and associated soil microorganisms known as the root microbiome.

1020b0d9c377.title: Rhizosphere
1020b0d9c377.sentence: The term "rhizosphere" was used first in 1904 by the German plant physiologist Lorenz Hiltner to describe how plant roots interface with the surrounding soil.

bc4d87d9cf22.title: Rhizosphere
bc4d87d9cf22.sentence: Hiltner postulated the rhizosphere was a region surrounding the plant roots and populated with microorganisms under some degree of control by chemicals released from the plant roots.

083b9806d7c5.title: Rhizosphere
083b9806d7c5.sentence: Soil pores in the rhizosphere can contain many bacteria and other microorganisms that feed on sloughed-off plant cells, termed rhizodeposition, and the proteins and sugars released by roots, termed root exudates.

e72c668a1904.title: Rhizosphere
e72c668a1904.sentence: Plant roots may exude 20–40% of the sugars and organic acids—photosynthetically fixed carbon.

c70a6042ce5c.title: Rhizosphere
c70a6042ce5c.sentence: Much of the nutrient cycling and disease suppression by antibiotics required by plants occurs immediately adjacent to roots due to root exudates and metabolic products of symbiotic and pathogenic communities of microorganisms.

d0353e210bd6.title: Rhizosphere
d0353e210bd6.sentence: Concentrations of organic acids and saccharides affect the ability of the biological communities to shuttle phosphorus, nitrogen, potassium, and water to the root cap, and the total availability of iron to the plant and to its neighbors.

4e11dbe00820.title: Rhizosphere
4e11dbe00820.sentence: Root respiration and exudation can generate Anoxic microsites in soil adjacent to roots, shaping microbial community structure.

be0a305123db.title: Bulk soil
be0a305123db.sentence: Another property, pH, is affected by soil proximity to roots, causing a raised pH in acid soils close to plant roots.

5c14d0922b24.title: Rhizosphere
5c14d0922b24.sentence: The rhizoplane refers to the root surface including its associated soil particles which closely interact with each other.

534037454d97.title: Mycorrhiza
534037454d97.sentence: A mycorrhiza (from Ancient Greek μύκης (múkēs) 'fungus' and ῥίζα (rhíza) 'root'; pl. mycorrhizae, mycorrhiza, or mycorrhizas) is a symbiotic association between a fungus and a plant, in which fungal hyphae and plant roots become interconnected and form an interface on the cellular level.

c5906f7d6067.title: Mycorrhiza
c5906f7d6067.sentence: The plant makes organic molecules by photosynthesis and supplies them to the fungus in the form of sugars or lipids, while the fungus supplies the plant with water and mineral nutrients, such as phosphorus, nitrogen, or zinc, taken from the soil.

c404d8ad858c.title: Mycorrhiza
c404d8ad858c.sentence: In a mycorrhizal association, the fungus colonizes the host plant's root tissues, either intracellularly as in arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi, or extracellularly as in ectomycorrhizal fungi.

469799bc838e.title: Mycorrhiza
469799bc838e.sentence: In particular species, or in particular circumstances, mycorrhizae may have a parasitic association with host plants.

3ca1f4cf19e8.title: Mycorrhiza
3ca1f4cf19e8.sentence: Mycorrhizas are present in 92% of plant families studied (80% of species), with arbuscular mycorrhizas being the ancestral and predominant form, and the most prevalent symbiotic association found in the plant kingdom.

fb79a331f5e9.title: Mycorrhiza
fb79a331f5e9.sentence: Most plant species form mycorrhizal associations, though some families like Brassicaceae and Chenopodiaceae cannot.

60ecf1c2a28a.title: Root microbiome
60ecf1c2a28a.sentence: In some ecosystems, up to 80% of plant nitrogen and 90% of plant phosphorus is acquired by mycorrhizal fungi.

43cd9f8ed7a3.title: Root microbiome
43cd9f8ed7a3.sentence: In return, plants may allocate ~20–40% of their carbon to mycorrhizae.

ce6ba80f1f31.title: Mycorrhiza
ce6ba80f1f31.sentence: Many factors are involved in the initiation of mycorrhizal symbiosis, but particularly influential is the plant's need for phosphorus.

a9bf1f15227c.title: Mycorrhiza
a9bf1f15227c.sentence: Experiments involving rice plants with a mutation disabling their ability to detect P starvation show that arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi detection, recruitment and colonization is prompted when the plant detects that it is starved of phosphorus.

5b05c2c423c1.title: Mycorrhiza
5b05c2c423c1.sentence: Nitrogen starvation also plays a role in initiating AMF symbiosis.

1751f0cb507e.title: Mycorrhiza
1751f0cb507e.sentence: Fossil and genetic evidence indicate that mycorrhizae emerged as early as 450-500 million years ago, potentially between fungus-like protists and algae.

0e70404da9ae.title: Mycorrhiza
0e70404da9ae.sentence: Genetic evidence indicates that all land plants share a single common ancestor, which appears to have quickly adopted mycorrhizal symbiosis, and research suggests that proto-mycorrhizal fungi were a key factor enabling plant terrestrialization.

0b8af4d21afc.title: Root microbiome
0b8af4d21afc.sentence: The root microbiome (also called rhizosphere microbiome) is the dynamic community of microorganisms associated with plant roots.

9f5bd20e2e81.title: Root microbiome
9f5bd20e2e81.sentence: Because they are rich in a variety of carbon compounds, plant roots provide unique environments for a diverse assemblage of soil microorganisms, including bacteria, fungi, and archaea.

b822cceba463.title: Root microbiome
b822cceba463.sentence: The microbial communities inside the root and in the rhizosphere are distinct from each other, and from the microbial communities of bulk soil, although there is some overlap in species composition.

532a70fa3816.title: Root microbiome
532a70fa3816.sentence: Beneficial microorganisms include bacteria that fix nitrogen, various microbes that promote plant growth, mycorrhizal fungi, mycoparasitic fungi, protozoa, and certain biocontrol microorganisms.

9dd783f9d447.title: Root microbiome
9dd783f9d447.sentence: Pathogenic microorganisms can also include certain bacteria, fungi, and nematodes that can colonize the rhizosphere.

dff91e5c2042.title: Root microbiome
dff91e5c2042.sentence: Symbionts associated with plant roots subsist off of photosynthetic products (carbon rich molecules) from the plant host and can exist anywhere on the mutualist/parasite continuum.

262671a85825.title: Root microbiome
262671a85825.sentence: Members of the root microbiome benefit from plant sugars or other carbon rich molecules.

e8994cc07f58.title: Root microbiome
e8994cc07f58.sentence: Mycorrhizal fungi can extend a great distance into bulk soil, thereby increasing the root system's reach and surface area, enabling mycorrhizal fungi to acquire a large percentage of its host plant's nutrients.

d64342288159.title: Root
d64342288159.sentence: Scientists have observed significant diversity of the microbial cover of roots at around 10 percent of three week old root segments covered.

f07d6b0dc3c2.title: Root
f07d6b0dc3c2.sentence: On younger roots there was even low coverage, but even on 3-month-old roots the coverage was only around 37%.

a756188fc3c9.title: Root
a756188fc3c9.sentence: Before the 1970s, scientists believed that the majority of the root surface was covered by microorganisms.

aa7f19bc51e9.title: Root microbiome
aa7f19bc51e9.sentence: Methanogen and ammonium-oxidizing archaea are prevalent members of the root microbiome, especially in anaerobic soils and wetlands.

df88cadec7e6.title: Root microbiome
df88cadec7e6.sentence: The study found that only about 8% of the core microbiota was consistently shared between soil and plants, suggesting that plants selectively recruit microbial taxa from the surrounding microbial pool according to developmental needs.

3c838d9fb368.title: Bulk soil
3c838d9fb368.sentence: Bulk soil is the soil outside of the rhizosphere that is not penetrated by plant roots.

d93623d4e226.title: Bulk soil
d93623d4e226.sentence: Natural organic compounds are much lower in bulk soil than in the rhizosphere.

5ab0493786b1.title: Bulk soil
5ab0493786b1.sentence: There are microbes in the bulk soil and the rhizosphere, the variation of microbes increases in the bulk soil and the abundance of microbes increases in the rhizosphere.

fa48a3b8a057.title: Soil carbon
fa48a3b8a057.section: Forms of Carbon in Soil > Organic carbon
fa48a3b8a057.sentence: Microbial populations are typically higher in the rhizosphere than in adjacent bulk soil.

36ca1ce44fd3.title: Bulk soil
36ca1ce44fd3.sentence: Furthermore, bulk soil inhabitants are generally smaller than identical species in the rhizosphere.

66f8ae1ac6bb.title: Bulk soil
66f8ae1ac6bb.sentence: Bulk soil tends to have smaller pores and greater moisture at a given matric potential than in the rhizosphere, affecting which microbes can survive there.

f25a407f246b.title: Soil formation
f25a407f246b.sentence: Out of root influence, in the bulk soil most bacteria are in a quiescent stage, forming micro-aggregates, i.e. mucilaginous colonies to which clay particles are glued, offering them a protection against desiccation and predation by soil microfauna (bacteriophagous protozoa and nematodes).

2ee874179c65.title: Bulk soil
2ee874179c65.sentence: Chemical properties of the bulk soil are organic matter, soil organic carbon, nutrient content, cation-exchange capacity (CEC), free ions (cations or anions), pH, and base saturation, and organisms.

5cf145d24367.title: Bulk soil
5cf145d24367.sentence: In terms of carbon cycling, bulk soil respiration is sensitive to fluctuations in temperature.

02ed5188e76a.title: Bulk soil
02ed5188e76a.sentence: Changes in soil chemistry, such as through addition of nutrients or warming temperatures, can heavily influence the microbial community, especially in sandy soils.

c29ef296903d.title: Mycorrhiza
c29ef296903d.sentence: The mycorrhizal mutualistic association provides the fungus with relatively constant and direct access to carbohydrates, such as glucose and sucrose.

b297f03963e1.title: Mycorrhiza
b297f03963e1.sentence: In return, the plant gains the benefits of the mycelium's higher absorptive capacity for water and mineral nutrients, partly because of the large surface area of fungal hyphae, which are much longer and finer than plant root hairs, and partly because some such fungi can mobilize soil minerals unavailable to the plants' roots.

a517822ccf0d.title: Mycorrhiza
a517822ccf0d.sentence: The effect is thus to improve the plant's mineral absorption capabilities.

e8506c2d6d51.title: Mycorrhiza
e8506c2d6d51.sentence: The carbohydrates are translocated from their source (usually leaves) to root tissue and on to the plant's fungal partners.

7debc63a7a8c.title: Mycorrhiza
7debc63a7a8c.sentence: Physically, most mycorrhizal mycelia are much smaller in diameter than the smallest root or root hair, and thus can explore soil material that roots and root hairs cannot reach, and provide a larger surface area for absorption.

683eb84d62d6.title: Mycorrhiza
683eb84d62d6.sentence: For example, they may secrete organic acids that dissolve or chelate many ions, or release them from minerals by ion exchange.

1cff599e6756.title: Mycorrhiza
1cff599e6756.sentence: Unaided plant roots may be unable to take up nutrients that are chemically or physically immobilised; examples include phosphate ions and micronutrients such as iron.

ca58887c6e05.title: Mycorrhiza
ca58887c6e05.sentence: One form of such immobilization occurs in soil with high clay content, or soils with a strongly basic pH.

2a85aa335f8e.title: Mycorrhiza
2a85aa335f8e.sentence: The mycelium of the mycorrhizal fungus can, however, access many such nutrient sources, and make them available to the plants they colonize.

6b253df6fefa.title: Mycorrhiza
6b253df6fefa.sentence: Another form of immobilisation is when nutrients are locked up in organic matter that is slow to decay, such as wood, and some mycorrhizal fungi act directly as decay organisms, mobilising the nutrients and passing some onto the host plants; for example, in some dystrophic forests, large amounts of phosphate and other nutrients are taken up by mycorrhizal hyphae acting directly on leaf litter, bypassing the need for soil uptake.

ee584c2bdc53.title: Mycorrhiza
ee584c2bdc53.sentence: Inga alley cropping, an agroforestry technique proposed as an alternative to slash and burn rainforest destruction, relies upon mycorrhiza within the root system of species of Inga to prevent the rain from washing phosphorus out of the soil.

663b7fca5887.title: Mycorrhiza
663b7fca5887.sentence: Mycorrhizae are especially beneficial for the plant partner in nutrient-poor soils.

413b455882a8.title: Mycorrhiza
413b455882a8.sentence: Recent research into ectomycorrhizal plants in boreal forests has indicated that mycorrhizal fungi and plants have a relationship that may be more complex than simply mutualistic.

891ec059db2a.title: Mycorrhiza
891ec059db2a.sentence: This relationship was noted when mycorrhizal fungi were unexpectedly found to be hoarding nitrogen from plant roots in times of nitrogen scarcity.

42c2f36611f8.title: Mycorrhiza
42c2f36611f8.sentence: Fungi have a protective role for plants rooted in soils with high metal concentrations, such as acidic and contaminated soils.

8991c0d35a7a.title: Mycorrhiza
8991c0d35a7a.section: Function > Disease, drought and salinity resistance and its correlation to mycorrhizae
8991c0d35a7a.sentence: Mycorrhizas have been found to secrete enzymes that are toxic to soil borne organisms such as nematodes.

f92c72dc389b.title: Mycorrhiza
f92c72dc389b.section: Function > Disease, drought and salinity resistance and its correlation to mycorrhizae
f92c72dc389b.sentence: More recent studies have shown that mycorrhizal associations result in a priming effect of plants that essentially acts as a primary immune response.

cd366c2d6800.title: Mycorrhiza
cd366c2d6800.section: Function > Disease, drought and salinity resistance and its correlation to mycorrhizae
cd366c2d6800.sentence: When this association is formed a defense response is activated similarly to the response that occurs when the plant is under attack.

f1c1dbc66b27.title: Mycorrhiza
f1c1dbc66b27.section: Function > Disease, drought and salinity resistance and its correlation to mycorrhizae
f1c1dbc66b27.sentence: As a result of this inoculation, defense responses are stronger in plants with mycorrhizal associations.

69b7e6e5a521.title: Mycorrhiza
69b7e6e5a521.section: Function > Disease, drought and salinity resistance and its correlation to mycorrhizae
69b7e6e5a521.sentence: Furthermore, mycorrhizal fungi was significantly correlated with soil physical variable, but only with water level and not with aggregate stability and can lead also to more resistant to the effects of drought.

0181be6d2401.title: Mycorrhiza
0181be6d2401.section: Function > Disease, drought and salinity resistance and its correlation to mycorrhizae
0181be6d2401.sentence: Moreover, the significance of mycorrhizal fungi also includes alleviation of salt stress and its beneficial effects on plant growth and productivity.

9795d9eeb581.title: Mycorrhiza
9795d9eeb581.section: Function > Disease, drought and salinity resistance and its correlation to mycorrhizae
9795d9eeb581.sentence: Although salinity can negatively affect mycorrhizal fungi, many reports show improved growth and performance of mycorrhizal plants under salt stress conditions.

e4e80a9f1e24.title: Mycorrhiza
e4e80a9f1e24.sentence: Pine trees inoculated with Pisolithus tinctorius planted in several contaminated sites displayed high tolerance to the prevailing contaminant, survivorship and growth.

2804fa817e1f.title: Mycorrhiza
2804fa817e1f.sentence: Another study discovered that zinc-tolerant strains of Suillus bovinus conferred resistance to plants of Pinus sylvestris.

1bb2f36cf734.title: Mycorrhiza
1bb2f36cf734.sentence: This was probably due to binding of the metal to the extramatricial mycelium of the fungus, without affecting the exchange of beneficial substances.

95912c2d2c21.title: Mycorrhiza
95912c2d2c21.sentence: There are multiple ways to categorize mycorrhizal symbiosis.

ab5e2dea5904.title: Mycorrhiza
ab5e2dea5904.sentence: The largest division is between ectomycorrhizas and endomycorrhizas.

cb6a5e093c2f.title: Mycorrhiza
cb6a5e093c2f.sentence: The two types are differentiated by the fact that the hyphae of ectomycorrhizal fungi do not penetrate individual cells within the root, while the hyphae of endomycorrhizal fungi penetrate the cell wall into the root's cell membrane.

faa8bef70a6f.title: Mycorrhiza
faa8bef70a6f.sentence: Other forms of mycorrhizae, including arbuscular, ericoid, arbutoid, monotropoid, and orchid mycorrhizas, are considered endomycorrhizae.

dd9538d061a0.title: Mycorrhiza
dd9538d061a0.sentence: The mycorrhizal lifestyle has independently convergently evolved multiple times in the history of Earth.

8dcd39a71aa1.title: Mycorrhiza
8dcd39a71aa1.sentence: Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi form their own monophyletic phylum, whereas other mycorrhizal fungi convergently evolved similar lifestyles.

27f4f166a281.title: Mycorrhiza
27f4f166a281.sentence: Endophytes are defined as organisms that can live within plant cells without causing harm to the plant.

fffe78ec3638.title: Mycorrhiza
fffe78ec3638.sentence: They are distinguishable from mycorrhizal fungi by the absence of nutrient-transferring structures for bringing in nutrients from outside the plant.

2b6df034ff0b.title: Mycorrhiza
2b6df034ff0b.sentence: Mycorrhizal fungi belonging to Mucoromycotina, known as "fine root endophytes" (MFREs), were mistakenly identified as arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi until recently.

a9dc676584e6.title: Mycorrhiza
a9dc676584e6.sentence: Unlike AMFs, they appear capable of surviving without a host.

e78e4ababd9d.title: Mycorrhiza
e78e4ababd9d.sentence: This group of mycorrhizal fungi is little understood, but appears to prefer wet, acidic soils and forms symbiotic relationships with liverworts, hornworts, lycophytes, and angiosperms.

6f317bb39e5d.title: Mycorrhiza
6f317bb39e5d.sentence: This type of mycorrhiza occurs in the subfamily Monotropoideae of the Ericaceae, as well as several genera in the Orchidaceae.

358a62587cf8.title: Mycorrhiza
358a62587cf8.sentence: These plants are heterotrophic or mixotrophic and derive their carbon from the fungus partner.

bdba3d5ea7c3.title: Mycorrhiza
bdba3d5ea7c3.sentence: This is thus a non-mutualistic, parasitic type of mycorrhizal symbiosis.

c7fdac1ee85f.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
c7fdac1ee85f.sentence: An arbuscular mycorrhiza (AM) (plural mycorrhizae) is a type of mycorrhiza in which the symbiont fungus (Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi, or AMF) penetrates the cortical cells of the roots of a vascular plant forming arbuscules.

65305d442275.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
65305d442275.sentence: They are characterized by the formation of unique tree-like structures, the arbuscules.

d9cad7634aab.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
d9cad7634aab.sentence: Arbuscules are the sites of exchange for phosphorus, carbon, water, and other nutrients.

89c7a02794b7.title: Mycorrhiza
89c7a02794b7.sentence: Often, balloon-like storage structures, termed vesicles, are also produced.

e7f034b943bb.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
e7f034b943bb.sentence: Arbuscular mycorrhizae are formed by fungi in the subphylum Glomeromycotina and some fungi from the Mucoromycotina.

f76589323604.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
f76589323604.sentence: AM fungi help plants to capture nutrients such as phosphorus, sulfur, nitrogen and micronutrients from the soil.

5f8e397c8870.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
5f8e397c8870.sentence: This symbiosis is a highly evolved mutualistic relationship found between fungi and plants, the most prevalent plant symbiosis known, and AMF is found in 80% of vascular plant families in existence today.

218821b6e5cd.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
218821b6e5cd.sentence: Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi are found in 80% of plant species and have been surveyed on all continents except Antarctica.

0eb2756182ec.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
0eb2756182ec.sentence: They have limited saprobic ability and depend on the plant for their carbon nutrition.

b3ff43c1bd3d.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
b3ff43c1bd3d.sentence: Up to 20% of the host plant's carbon may be transferred to the AM fungi.

b0d4d148d7cc.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
b0d4d148d7cc.sentence: There are an estimates 110-quadrillion kilometers of AM fungal hyphae in Earth's topsoils, with around 40% located in wild grasslands.

62809f3cbe05.title: Mycorrhiza
62809f3cbe05.sentence: A global analysis estimated that Earth's upper soils contain approximately 110-quadrillion kilometres of arbuscular mycorrhizal fungal hyphae, equivalent to about one-billion times the distance from Earth to the Sun, with a biomass of about 300 megatons of carbon, or roughly four to six times the biomass of all humans.

23a95d6f54e1.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
23a95d6f54e1.sentence: Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi are most frequent in plants growing on mineral soils, and are of extreme importance for plants growing in nutrient-deficient substrates such as in volcanic soil and sand dune environments.

9d0d38dfc91c.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
9d0d38dfc91c.sentence: There is a lower incidence of mycorrhizal colonization in very arid or nutrient-rich soils.

9d83314b0fff.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
9d83314b0fff.sentence: AM fungi enhance soil aggregate stability by the production of extraradical hyphae and a soil protein known as glomalin.

dcb22da9750f.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
dcb22da9750f.sentence: Members of the mustard family (Brassicaceae), such as cabbage, cauliflower, canola, and crambe, do not establish arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi on their roots.

a212f943c992.title: Ectomycorrhiza
a212f943c992.sentence: An ectomycorrhiza (from Ancient Greek ἐκτός (ektós) 'outside', μύκης (múkēs) 'fungus' and ῥίζα (rhíza) 'root'; abbreviated EcM; pl. ectomycorrhizae or ectomycorrhizas) is a form of symbiotic relationship that occurs between a fungal symbiont, or mycobiont, and the roots of various plant species.

fd18d04fd12a.title: Ectomycorrhiza
fd18d04fd12a.sentence: Unlike other mycorrhizal relationships, such as arbuscular mycorrhiza and ericoid mycorrhiza, ectomycorrhizal fungi do not penetrate their host's cell wall.

9c21153af5a2.title: Ectomycorrhiza
9c21153af5a2.sentence: Ectomycorrhizas are further differentiated from other mycorrhizas by the formation of a dense hyphal sheath, known as the mantle, surrounding the root surface.

9963de476e32.title: Ectomycorrhiza
9963de476e32.sentence: The mycobiont is often from the division Basidiomycota and Ascomycota, and more rarely from the Zygomycota.

cbc726a18f5b.title: Ectomycorrhiza
cbc726a18f5b.sentence: Instead they form an entirely intercellular interfaces known as the Hartig net, consisting of highly branched hyphae forming a latticework between epidermal and cortical root cells.

533a61ba63b7.title: Ectomycorrhiza
533a61ba63b7.sentence: This sheathing mantle can be up to 40 μm thick, with hyphae extending up to several centimeters into the surrounding soil.

949836cf9ef0.title: Ectomycorrhiza
949836cf9ef0.sentence: Ectomycorrhizae form on the roots of around 2% of plant species, usually woody plants, including species from the birch, dipterocarp, myrtle, beech, willow, pine and rose families.

731040579103.title: Mycorrhiza
731040579103.sentence: Ectomycorrhizae associate with relatively few plant species, only about 2% of plant species on Earth, but the species they associate with are mostly trees and woody plants that are highly dominant in their ecosystems, meaning plants in ectomycorrhizal relationships make up a large proportion of plant biomass.

7d5fd63b9229.title: Ectomycorrhiza
7d5fd63b9229.sentence: In most terrestrial ecosystems nitrogen is in short supply and is sequestered in organic matter that is hard to break down.

93051f088a28.title: Ectomycorrhiza
93051f088a28.sentence: Fungal symbionts thus offer two advantages to plants: the greater range of their hyphae when compared with roots, and a greater ability to extract nitrogen from the layer of soil in which organic matter lies.

5899885f2127.title: Ectomycorrhiza
5899885f2127.sentence: It has been estimated that ectomycorrhizal fungi receive approximately 15% of the host plant's food product and in return provide up to 86% of a host's nitrogen needs.

50301276ba04.title: Ectomycorrhiza
50301276ba04.sentence: Some studies have shown that if there is too much nitrogen available due to human use of fertilizer, plants can shift their resources away from the fungal network.

02076d279c47.title: Ectomycorrhiza
02076d279c47.sentence: In one study species richness declined dramatically with increasing nitrogen inputs, with over 30 species represented at low nitrogen sites and only 9 at high nitrogen sites.

e09d5a999e7c.title: Ectomycorrhiza
e09d5a999e7c.sentence: Although samples of ectomycorrhizas are usually taken from the surface horizon due to higher root density, ectomycorrhizas are known to occur in deep tree roots (a depth more than 2 meters), some occurring at least as deep as 4 m.

93a6f5331059.title: Ectomycorrhiza
93a6f5331059.sentence: Many species of EcM fungi in Europe have declined, due to factors including reduced tree vitality, conversion of forests to other uses, pollution and acidification of forest soils.

a65befe2e61b.title: Mycorrhiza
a65befe2e61b.sentence: The ectomycorrhizal fungus Laccaria bicolor has been found to lure and kill springtails to obtain nitrogen, some of which may then be transferred to the mycorrhizal host plant.

aa77dab346cf.title: Mycorrhiza
aa77dab346cf.sentence: In a study by Klironomos and Hart, Eastern White Pine inoculated with L. bicolor was able to derive up to 25% of its nitrogen from springtails.

0778acf4101c.title: Glomeromycota
0778acf4101c.sentence: Glomeromycota (often referred to as glomeromycetes, as they include only one class, Glomeromycetes) are one of eight currently recognized divisions within the kingdom Fungi, with approximately 230 described species.

e91bd7f24775.title: Glomeromycota
e91bd7f24775.sentence: Members of the Glomeromycota form arbuscular mycorrhizas (AMs) with the thalli of bryophytes and the roots of vascular land plants.

c21de1af54c4.title: Glomeromycota
c21de1af54c4.sentence: The arbuscular mycorrhizal species are terrestrial and widely distributed in soils worldwide where they form symbioses with the roots of the majority of plant species (>80%).

b03c8573b54f.title: Glomeromycota
b03c8573b54f.sentence: They can also be found in wetlands, including salt-marshes, and associated with epiphytic plants.

259d1665ae03.title: Glomeromycota
259d1665ae03.sentence: The majority of evidence shows that the Glomeromycota are dependent on land plants (Nostoc in the case of Geosiphon) for carbon and energy, but there is recent circumstantial evidence that some species may be able to lead an independent existence.

3b91f185655b.title: Glomeromycota
3b91f185655b.sentence: The biochemical and genetic characterization of the Glomeromycota has been hindered by their biotrophic nature, which impedes laboratory culturing.

19ffd3568e91.title: Glomeromycota
19ffd3568e91.sentence: The Glomeromycota have generally coenocytic (occasionally sparsely septate) mycelia and reproduce asexually through blastic development of the hyphal tip to produce spores (Glomerospores, blastospore) with diameters of 80–500 μm.

27903e118760.title: Glomeromycota
27903e118760.sentence: New colonization of AM fungi largely depends on the amount of inoculum present in the soil.

386c09959bb9.title: Glomeromycota
386c09959bb9.sentence: It has also been observed that the rate of root system colonization is directly correlated to spore density in the soil.

cb3bc6debc8a.title: Glomeromycota
cb3bc6debc8a.sentence: A metatranscriptomic survey of the Sevilleta Arid Lands found that 5.4% of the fungal rRNA reads mapped to Glomeromycota.

ddf0e155ab00.title: Glomeromycota
ddf0e155ab00.sentence: This result was inconsistent with previous PCR-based studies of community structure in the region, suggesting that previous PCR-based studies may have underestimated Glomeromycota abundance due to amplification biases.

08fae10bce3b.title: Mycorrhizal network
08fae10bce3b.sentence: A mycorrhizal network (also known as a common mycorrhizal network or CMN) is an underground network found in forests and other plant communities, created by the hyphae of mycorrhizal fungi joining with plant roots.

6555d4bb7813.title: Mycorrhizal network
6555d4bb7813.sentence: This network connects individual plants together.

8eda8d0a73f6.title: Mycorrhizal network
8eda8d0a73f6.sentence: The keyword "common" requires that two or more individual plants are connected by the same underground fungal network, through which matter of various types and functions may flow.

7520d7a8cf60.title: Mycorrhizal network
7520d7a8cf60.sentence: The plants themselves may be individuals of the same or different species.

cf02128efe93.title: Mycorrhizal network
cf02128efe93.sentence: There are two main types of mycorrhizal networks.

12af9f968ed8.title: Mycorrhizal network
12af9f968ed8.sentence: Arbuscular mycorrhizal networks are those in which fungal hyphae not only enter the plant's roots but also penetrate into the cells themselves.

c2993a4e83c3.title: Mycorrhizal network
c2993a4e83c3.sentence: Ectomycorrhizal networks send hyphae into the roots where they thread their way between the plant cells but do not penetrate cell walls.

9b34829d6a90.title: Mycorrhizal network
9b34829d6a90.sentence: However, tree species comprising the canopy of temperate and especially boreal forests in the Northern Hemisphere tend to associate with ectomycorrhizal fungi.

5c7abd920497.title: Mycorrhizal network
5c7abd920497.sentence: Mycorrhizal relationships are most commonly mutualistic, with both partners benefiting, but can be commensal or parasitic, and a single partnership may change between any of the three types of symbiosis at different times.

ffde6762045a.title: Mycorrhizal network
ffde6762045a.sentence: The formation and nature of these networks is context-dependent, and can be influenced by factors such as soil fertility, resource availability, host or mycosymbiont genotype, disturbance and seasonal variation.

ddcebea717df.title: Mycorrhizal network
ddcebea717df.section: Knowns, unknowns, and controversies > Proposed effects and functions of the mycorrhizal network > Potential nutrient and photosynthate transfer between plants
ddcebea717df.sentence: Numerous studies have reported that carbon, nitrogen and phosphorus are transferred between conspecific and heterospecific plants via AM and ECM networks.

17e155a9c7f2.title: Mycorrhizal network
17e155a9c7f2.section: Knowns, unknowns, and controversies > Proposed models > Source-sink model
17e155a9c7f2.sentence: Nitrogen has also been shown to flow from nitrogen-fixing plants to non-nitrogen fixing plants through a mycorrhizal network following a source-sink relationship.

aed90dbe81f6.title: Mycorrhizal network
aed90dbe81f6.section: Knowns, unknowns, and controversies > Research tools and methods > Isotopic labeling
aed90dbe81f6.sentence: By using carbon-13 and carbon-14 labels, researchers found that both tree species were trading carbon–that is to say, carbon was moving from tree to tree in both directions.

30282977c897.title: Mycorrhizal network
30282977c897.section: Knowns, unknowns, and controversies > Proposed models > Source-sink model
30282977c897.sentence: A further study with paper birch and Douglas fir demonstrated that the flow of carbon shifts direction more than once per season: in spring, newly budding birch receives carbon from green Douglas fir, in summer, stressed Douglas fir in the forest understory receives carbon from birch in full leaf, and in fall, birch again receives carbon from Douglas fir as birch trees shed their leaves and evergreen Douglas firs continue photosynthesizing.

0af17e12fd4f.title: Mycorrhizal network
0af17e12fd4f.section: Knowns, unknowns, and controversies > Research tools and methods > Isotopic labeling
0af17e12fd4f.sentence: At the end of the experiment, the Douglas fir was found to have a 2% to 3% net gain in carbon.

424b98ee0e8b.title: Ectomycorrhiza
424b98ee0e8b.sentence: For example, the rare isotope carbon-14 was added to a particular tree and later detected in nearby plants and seedlings.

1301a2338ee0.title: Ectomycorrhiza
1301a2338ee0.sentence: One study observed a bidirectional carbon transfer between Betula papyrifera and Pseudotsuga menziesii, primarily through the hyphae of the ectomycorrhiza.

a8d43cde9902.title: Mycorrhizal network
a8d43cde9902.section: Knowns, unknowns, and controversies > Evolutionary and adaptational perspectives
a8d43cde9902.sentence: These include increased establishment success, higher growth rate and survivorship of seedlings; improved inoculum availability for mycorrhizal infection; transfer of water, carbon, nitrogen and other limiting resources increasing the probability for colonization in less favorable conditions.

f7666dc8f1ee.title: Ectomycorrhiza
f7666dc8f1ee.sentence: However, not all plants are compatible with all fungal networks, so not all plants can exploit the benefits of established ectomycorrhizal linkages.

c38dd7e1baae.title: Ectomycorrhiza
c38dd7e1baae.sentence: The shared nutrient connection through CMNs has been suggested to be involved with other ecological processes such as seedling establishment, forest succession and other plant-plant interactions.

ca09dac713ea.title: Mycorrhizal network
ca09dac713ea.sentence: In one study, Simard watched as a Douglas fir that had been injured by insects appeared to send chemical warning signals to a ponderosa pine growing nearby.

a3c63eb0d507.title: Mycorrhizal network
a3c63eb0d507.sentence: The pine tree then produced defense enzymes to protect against the insect.

fe13a1953dec.title: Mycorrhiza
fe13a1953dec.sentence: Plants connected by mycorrhizal fungi in mycorrhizal networks can use these underground connections to communicate warning signals.

f184785fa4db.title: Mycorrhizal network
f184785fa4db.sentence: Mycorrhizal networks were discovered in 1997 by Suzanne Simard, professor of forest ecology at the University of British Columbia in Canada.

66582ac1fc04.title: Mycorrhizal network
66582ac1fc04.sentence: Referencing an analogous function served by the World Wide Web in human communities, the many roles that mycorrhizal networks appear to play in woodland have earned them a colloquial nickname: the "Wood Wide Web".

e78aa6cc1ad5.title: Mycorrhizal network
e78aa6cc1ad5.sentence: Many of the claims made about common mycorrhizal networks, including that they are ubiquitous in forests, that resources are transferred between plants through them, and that they are used to transfer warnings between trees, have been criticised as being not strongly supported by evidence.

b7bcb36d68a0.title: Mycorrhizal network
b7bcb36d68a0.section: Knowns, unknowns, and controversies > Limits and challenges to research
b7bcb36d68a0.sentence: The connectivity between plants believed to share a common mycorrhizal network is also difficult to verify in a natural ecosystem.

2d2ed24ae512.title: Mycorrhizal network
2d2ed24ae512.section: Knowns, unknowns, and controversies > Limits and challenges to research
2d2ed24ae512.sentence: While movement of resources between plants connected to the same mycorrhizal network has been shown, it is often unclear whether the transfer is direct, as though the mycelium is forming a literal "pipeline," or indirect, such as nutrients being released into the soil by fungi and then picked up by neighboring plants.

a4786fa2347e.title: Mycorrhiza
a4786fa2347e.sentence: Carbon has been shown to move from paper birch seedlings into adjacent Douglas-fir seedlings, although not conclusively through a common mycorrhizal network, thereby promoting succession in ecosystems.

3a9f7b00eefb.title: Soil biology
3a9f7b00eefb.sentence: Chemical signalling between plants through common mycorrhizal networks, although a beautiful concept, is still a matter of conjecture, more research being needed.

921016e45641.title: Mycorrhiza
921016e45641.sentence: In 2021, the Society for the Protection of Underground Networks was launched.

7feb91b08f9d.title: Rhizobacteria
7feb91b08f9d.sentence: Rhizobacteria are root-associated bacteria that can have a detrimental (parasitic varieties), neutral or beneficial effect on plant growth.

9d065a82b1df.title: Rhizobacteria
9d065a82b1df.sentence: The term usually refers to bacteria that form symbiotic relationships with many plants (mutualism).

10bdd5c4430e.title: Rhizobacteria
10bdd5c4430e.sentence: Rhizobacteria are often referred to as plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria, or PGPRs.

d2dd66ef97ef.title: Rhizobacteria
d2dd66ef97ef.sentence: Generally, about 2–5% of rhizosphere bacteria are PGPR.

f7f426ef01c0.title: Rhizobacteria
f7f426ef01c0.sentence: The two major classes of relationships are rhizospheric and endophytic.

85c777e19b3d.title: Rhizobacteria
85c777e19b3d.sentence: Rhizospheric relationships consist of the PGPRs that colonize the surface of the root, or superficial intercellular spaces of the host plant, often forming root nodules.

294438599f9c.title: Rhizobacteria
294438599f9c.sentence: Endophytic relationships involve the PGPRs residing and growing within the host plant in the apoplastic space.

baf38cc3168c.title: Rhizobacteria
baf38cc3168c.sentence: Nitrogen fixation is one of the most beneficial processes performed by rhizobacteria.

26e36d1781fc.title: Rhizobacteria
26e36d1781fc.sentence: Nitrogen is a vital nutrient to plants and gaseous nitrogen (N2) is not available to them due to the high energy required to break the triple bonds between the two atoms.

a72d826a7ea4.title: Rhizobacteria
a72d826a7ea4.sentence: Rhizobacteria, through nitrogen fixation, are able to convert gaseous nitrogen (N2) to ammonia (NH3) making it an available nutrient to the host plant which can support and enhance plant growth.

6653005e0820.title: Rhizobacteria
6653005e0820.sentence: Creating and maintaining root nodules for rhizobacteria can cost between 12 and 25% of the plant's total photosynthetic output.

a9dce2cb5cfb.title: Rhizobacteria
a9dce2cb5cfb.sentence: Phosphorus, a limiting nutrient for plant growth, can be plentiful in soil, but is most commonly found in insoluble forms.

6e83994113d6.title: Rhizobacteria
6e83994113d6.sentence: Organic acids and phosphotases released by rhizobacteria found in plant rhizospheres facilitate the conversion of insoluble forms of phosphorus to plant-available forms such as H2PO4−.

a7a1a1affa0f.title: Rhizosphere
a7a1a1affa0f.sentence: Non-symbiotic (or "free-living") nitrogen-fixing bacteria may reside in the rhizosphere just outside the roots of certain plants (including many grasses) and similarly "fix" nitrogen gas in the nutrient-rich plant rhizosphere.

f5e72a91945b.title: Rhizosphere
f5e72a91945b.sentence: For example, nitrogen-fixing bacteria in the rhizosphere of the rice plant exhibit diurnal cycles that mimic plant behavior and tend to supply more fixed nitrogen during growth stages when the plant exhibits a high demand for nitrogen.

9963bb02814c.title: Rhizosphere
9963bb02814c.sentence: The application of organic matter such as sugarcane straw, goat manure, and filtered mud has been shown to enhance the abundance and activity of free-living, plant-growth-promoting bacteria.

fb929efa586c.title: Rhizosphere
fb929efa586c.sentence: These stimulated communities, in turn, improve nutrient cycling (such as nitrogen fixation and phosphorus solubilization) and support crop growth, even in the absence of specialized root nodules.

dd7ed3974fe6.title: Rhizobacteria
dd7ed3974fe6.sentence: Legumes are well-known nitrogen-fixing crops and have been used for centuries in crop rotation to maintain the health of the soil.

f2aa8d4c0882.title: Rhizobacteria
f2aa8d4c0882.sentence: Once colonized, though, the rhizobacteria make the soil surrounding the plant more nutrient rich, which in turn can lead to competition with other plants.

fcd30ccf1125.title: Rhizobia
fcd30ccf1125.sentence: Rhizobia are diazotrophic bacteria that fix nitrogen after becoming established inside the root nodules of legumes (Fabaceae).

1e56fcd4c98a.title: Rhizobia
1e56fcd4c98a.sentence: Rhizobia are a "group of soil bacteria that infect the roots of legumes to form root nodules".

e4b3e804cdd8.title: Rhizobia
e4b3e804cdd8.sentence: To express genes for nitrogen fixation, rhizobia require a plant host; they cannot independently fix nitrogen.

18064c581061.title: Rhizobia
18064c581061.sentence: Once the legume dies, the nodule breaks down and releases the rhizobia back into the soil, where they can live individually or reinfect a new legume host.

22ef9dfdfd0e.title: Rhizobia
22ef9dfdfd0e.sentence: Rhizobia are found in the soil and, after infection, produce nodules in the legume where they fix nitrogen gas (N2) from the atmosphere, turning it into a more readily useful form of nitrogen: ammonia (NH3).

a7cf22eba475.title: Rhizobia
a7cf22eba475.sentence: From here, the nitrogen is exported from the nodules and used for growth in the legume.

1a6590e627c1.title: Rhizobia
1a6590e627c1.section: Symbiotic relationship > Nature of the mutualism
1a6590e627c1.sentence: The legume–rhizobium symbiosis is a classic example of mutualism—rhizobia supply ammonia or amino acids to the plant and, in return, receive organic acids (mainly malate and succinate, which are dicarboxylic acids) as a carbon and energy source.

7e5ccf89538c.title: Rhizobia
7e5ccf89538c.sentence: The first known species of rhizobia, Rhizobium leguminosarum, was identified in 1889, and all further species were initially placed in the Rhizobium genus.

9ab3fede81e2.title: Rhizobia
9ab3fede81e2.sentence: Rhizobia are a paraphyletic group that fall into two classes of Pseudomonadota—the alphaproteobacteria and betaproteobacteria.

8bf3ab92b8c5.title: Rhizobia
8bf3ab92b8c5.sentence: As shown below, most belong to the order Hyphomicrobiales, but several rhizobia occur in distinct bacterial orders of the Pseudomonadota.

c3c95278f616.title: Rhizobia
c3c95278f616.sentence: Although much of the nitrogen is removed when protein-rich grain or hay is harvested, significant amounts can remain in the soil for future crops.

4a8133e443bb.title: Rhizobia
4a8133e443bb.sentence: As a result of the nodulation process, after the harvest of the crop, there are higher levels of soil nitrate, which can then be used by the next crop.

e439efaa2593.title: Rhizobia
e439efaa2593.sentence: This is especially important when nitrogen fertilizer is not used, as in organic rotation schemes or in some less-industrialized countries.

bbb0dfe9f9d0.title: Rhizobia
bbb0dfe9f9d0.sentence: Inoculation with rhizobia tends to increase yield.

9a0503b7ebee.title: Rhizobia
9a0503b7ebee.sentence: 12–20 million hectares of soybeans are inoculated annually.

318a04df57e9.title: Rhizobacteria
318a04df57e9.sentence: Inoculation with PGPRs ensures efficient nitrogen fixation, and they have been employed in North American agriculture for over 100 years.

efa3dd875a9e.title: Rhizobia
efa3dd875a9e.section: Symbiotic relationship > Nature of the mutualism
efa3dd875a9e.sentence: Cheater strains may hoard plant resources such as polyhydroxybutyrate for the benefit of their own reproduction without fixing an appreciable amount of nitrogen.

e3a4e182f74c.title: Rhizobia
e3a4e182f74c.section: Symbiotic relationship > Evolutionary hypotheses > The sanctions hypothesis
e3a4e182f74c.sentence: In response to underperforming rhizobia, legume hosts can respond by imposing sanctions of varying severity to their nodules.

e99b6d2f9b7c.title: Rhizobia
e99b6d2f9b7c.section: Symbiotic relationship > Evolutionary hypotheses > The sanctions hypothesis
e99b6d2f9b7c.sentence: These sanctions include, but are not limited to, reduction of nodule growth, early nodule death, decreased carbon supply to nodules, or reduced oxygen supply to nodules that fix less nitrogen.

d9f87efd3aab.title: Rhizobia
d9f87efd3aab.sentence: The legume-rhizobia mutualism is context dependent; the benefits provided by rhizobia are lessened or absent under unfavorable environmental conditions.

ec3faadf912a.title: Rhizobia
ec3faadf912a.sentence: For example, nutrient deposition has led to the emergence of less productive strains of rhizobia and increased ambient temperatures have legumes reducing investment in the resource mutualism.

df0fd14ec810.title: Rhizobia
df0fd14ec810.sentence: Nutrient deposition is of particular issue to legumes as the increased availability of nitrogen allows nitrogen-limited plant species to quickly out compete legumes for light.

8cb64c7ad69d.title: Endophyte
8cb64c7ad69d.sentence: An endophyte is an endosymbiont, often a bacterium or fungus, that lives within a plant for at least part of its life cycle without causing apparent disease.

58997573993f.title: Endophyte
58997573993f.sentence: Endophytes are ubiquitous and have been found in all species of plants studied to date; however, most of the endophyte/plant relationships are not well understood.

d7ffa2f4bf54.title: Endophyte
d7ffa2f4bf54.sentence: Endophytes may be transmitted either vertically (directly from parent to offspring) or horizontally (among individuals).

ea9f388d4f63.title: Endophyte
ea9f388d4f63.sentence: Vertically transmitted fungal endophytes are typically considered clonal and transmit via fungal hyphae penetrating the embryo within the host's seeds, while reproduction of the fungi through asexual conidia or sexual spores leads to horizontal transmission, where endophytes may spread between plants in a population or community.

0001004c9427.title: Endophyte
0001004c9427.sentence: Endophytes and plants often engage in mutualism, with endophytes primarily aiding in the health and survival of the host plant with issues such as pathogens and disease, water stress, heat stress, nutrient availability and poor soil quality, salinity, and herbivory.

487e4c8223ad.title: Endophyte
487e4c8223ad.sentence: In exchange the endophyte receives carbon for energy from the plant host.

7306ee0c4836.title: Endophyte
7306ee0c4836.sentence: Systemic endophytes are defined as organisms that live within plant tissues for the entirety of its life cycle and participate in a symbiotic relationship without causing disease or harm to the plant at any point.

ce2f2589e26d.title: Endophyte
ce2f2589e26d.sentence: Non-systemic or transient endophytes on the other hand vary in number and diversity within their plant hosts under changing environmental conditions.

40c13693e0a2.title: Endophyte
40c13693e0a2.sentence: Non-systemic endophytes have also been shown to become pathogenic to their host plants under stressful or resource limited growing conditions.

620a0986e025.title: Endophyte
620a0986e025.sentence: Endophytes accomplish this by increasing the uptake of valuable land limited nutrients from the soil such as phosphorus and making other plant nutrients available to plants such as rock phosphate and atmospheric nitrogen which are normally trapped in forms that are inaccessible to plants.

0c72697cda89.title: Endophyte
0c72697cda89.sentence: One group of fungal endophytes are the arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi involving biotrophic Glomeromycota associated with various plant species.

2db55627e2e6.title: Endophyte
2db55627e2e6.sentence: Bacterial endophytes are polyphyletic, belonging to broad range of taxa, including α-Proteobacteria, β-Proteobacteria, γ-Proteobacteria, Firmicutes, Actinobacteria.

2d44d0f87f05.title: Endophyte
2d44d0f87f05.sentence: The use of fungicides has a negative effect on endophytic fungi and fertilizers reduce a plant's dependence on its endophytic symbiont.

6766b96342ea.title: Endophyte
6766b96342ea.sentence: Epichloë endophytes are being widely used commercially in turf grasses to enhance the performance of the turf and its resistance to biotic and abiotic stresses.

6a9af89ddf25.title: Glomus (fungus)
6a9af89ddf25.sentence: Glomus is a genus of arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi, all of its species forming symbiotic relationships (mycorrhizae) with plant roots.

700d21328576.title: Glomus (fungus)
700d21328576.sentence: Glomus is the largest genus of AM fungi, with about 85 species described, but is currently defined as non-monophyletic.

f97f1d370422.title: Glomus (fungus)
f97f1d370422.sentence: As with other AM fungi, all Glomus species are thought to be obligate symbionts, dependent on their mycorrhizal association with plant roots to complete their life cycle.

d1ce0866f2d3.title: Glomus (fungus)
d1ce0866f2d3.sentence: They cannot be cultured in the laboratory in the absence of a plant host.

fc710ea220d1.title: Glomus (fungus)
fc710ea220d1.sentence: Glomus species are found in nearly all terrestrial habitats, including arable land, deserts, grasslands, tropical forests, and tundras.

dd83f499ded7.title: Glomus (fungus)
dd83f499ded7.sentence: Several species of Glomus, including G. aggregatum, are cultured and sold as mycorrhizal inoculant for agricultural soils.

665e154bfb34.title: Glomus (fungus)
665e154bfb34.sentence: One species, G. macrocarpum (and possibly also G. microcarpum), causes tobacco stunt disease.

18d30845b6e8.title: Rhizophagus irregularis
18d30845b6e8.sentence: Rhizophagus irregularis (previously known as Glomus intraradices) is an arbuscular mycorrhizal fungus used as a soil inoculant in agriculture and horticulture.

6ca20ff8c915.title: Rhizophagus irregularis
6ca20ff8c915.sentence: Rhizophagus irregularis can be found in almost all soils, especially those populated with common host plants and in forests and grasslands.

b5367a8b7a66.title: Rhizophagus irregularis
b5367a8b7a66.sentence: Most agricultural crops will benefit from Rhizophagus irregularis inoculation.

b9adfc2efd4c.title: Rhizophagus irregularis
b9adfc2efd4c.sentence: In numerous scientific studies R. irregularis has been shown to increase phosphorus uptake in multiple plants as well as improve soil aggregation due to hyphae.

0d43c36cd107.title: Rhizophagus irregularis
0d43c36cd107.sentence: Because of these qualities, R. irregularis is commonly found in mycorrhizal based fertilizers.

23c2d100fe75.title: Rhizophagus irregularis
23c2d100fe75.sentence: Rhizophagus irregularis (previously known as Glomus intraradices) has been found to colonise new plants by means of spores, hyphae or fragments of roots colonized by the fungus

a9d2d18e4dd3.title: Rhizophagus irregularis
a9d2d18e4dd3.sentence: Rhizophagus irregularis is also commonly used in scientific studies of the effects of arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi on plant and soil improvement.

4be208a892a7.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
4be208a892a7.sentence: AM fungi take up the products of the plant host's photosynthesis as hexoses.

55e07c7dbe94.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
55e07c7dbe94.sentence: The main benefit of mycorrhizas to plants has been attributed to increased uptake of nutrients, especially phosphorus.

119b33253c64.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
119b33253c64.sentence: Inside the mycelium, hexose is converted to trehalose and glycogen.

8729d7b909b1.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
8729d7b909b1.sentence: Approximately 25% of the carbon translocated from the plant to the fungi is stored in the extraradical hyphae.

e3753b19906d.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
e3753b19906d.sentence: Phosphorus travels to the root or via diffusion and hyphae reduce the distance required for diffusion, thus increasing uptake.

ba3575189eb6.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
ba3575189eb6.sentence: The rate of phosphorus flowing into mycorrhizae can be up to six times that of the root hairs.

56b821c71a96.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
56b821c71a96.sentence: In some cases, the role of phosphorus uptake can be completely taken over by the mycorrhizal network, and all of the plant's phosphorus may be of hyphal origin.

1da4a1d8d045.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
1da4a1d8d045.sentence: Increasing the plant's carbon supply to the AM fungi increases uptake and transfer of phosphorus from fungi to plant.

2d5bf45dfeae.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
2d5bf45dfeae.sentence: Likewise, phosphorus uptake and transfer is lowered when the photosynthate supplied to the fungi is decreased.

5bd4e14f7bba.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
5bd4e14f7bba.sentence: In some cases, arbuscular mycorrhizae are poor symbionts, providing little phosphorus while taking relatively high amounts of carbon.

accfce118c89.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
accfce118c89.sentence: Mycorrhizae lower the root zone pH by selective uptake of NH4+ (ammonium-ions) and by releasing H+ ions.

3628fefe9fd9.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
3628fefe9fd9.sentence: Decreased soil pH increases the solubility of phosphorus precipitates.

cb9b9de04ada.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
cb9b9de04ada.sentence: The hyphal NH4+ uptake also increases the nitrogen flow to the plant as the soil's inner surfaces absorb ammonium and distribute it by diffusion.

f490e88cc5fe.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
f490e88cc5fe.sentence: AMF contributes a substantial amount of carbon to the rhizosphere through the growth and degeneration of the hyphal network.

2ae91a1e1944.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
2ae91a1e1944.sentence: This represents the host plant's considerable carbon investment in mycorrhizal network and contribution to the below-ground organic carbon pool.

58267aae979d.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
58267aae979d.sentence: There is great potential for low-input agriculture to manage the system in a way that promotes mycorrhizal symbiosis.

18667c75441e.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
18667c75441e.sentence: Agricultural practices such as reduced tillage, low phosphorus fertilizer usage, and perennialized cropping systems promote functional mycorrhizal symbiosis.

bf2e1bd8321d.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
bf2e1bd8321d.sentence: Conventional agriculture practices, such as tillage, heavy fertilizers and fungicides, poor crop rotations, and selection for plants that survive these conditions, hinder the ability of plants to form symbiosis with arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi.

d63bbcd97407.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
d63bbcd97407.sentence: By breaking apart the soil macro structure, the hyphal network is rendered non-infective (Miller et al. 1995, McGonigle & Miller 1999).

0b9acd6e0bd9.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
0b9acd6e0bd9.sentence: This, in turn, lowers the phosphorus input to the plants that are connected to the hyphal network (Figure 3, McGonigle & Miller 1999).

670040d89c59.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
670040d89c59.sentence: In reduced-tillage system, heavy phosphorus fertilizer input may not be required as compared to heavy-tillage systems.

b10246bc6371.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
b10246bc6371.sentence: Heavy usage of phosphorus fertilizer can inhibit mycorrhizal colonization and growth.

347d1f0d19c7.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
347d1f0d19c7.sentence: As the soil's phosphorus levels available to the plants increases, the amount of phosphorus also increases in the plant's tissues, and carbon drain on the plant by the AM fungi symbiosis become non-beneficial to the plant (Grant 2005).

dee0a90cbba9.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
dee0a90cbba9.sentence: A decrease in mycorrhizal colonization due to high soil-phosphorus levels can lead to plant deficiencies in other micronutrients that have mycorrhizal-mediated uptake such as copper (Timmer & Leyden 1980).

eacb5579fec6.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
eacb5579fec6.sentence: Mycorrhizal cover crops can be used to improve the mycorrhizal inoculum potential and hyphal network (Kabir and Koide 2000, Boswell et al.1998, Sorensen et al. 2005).

2a4cf0b44571.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
2a4cf0b44571.sentence: Growing a cover crop extends the time for AM growth into the autumn, winter, and spring.

6066eb7228b0.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
6066eb7228b0.sentence: The extraradical mycelia are able to survive the winter, providing rapid spring colonization and early season symbiosis (McGonigle and Miller 1999).

dd6acb637fcb.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
dd6acb637fcb.sentence: Some crops that are poor at seeking out nutrients in the soil are very dependent on AM fungi for phosphorus uptake.

9ebd07a81246.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
9ebd07a81246.sentence: For example, flax, which has poor chemotaxic ability, is highly dependent on AM-mediated phosphorus uptake at low and intermediate soil phosphorus concentrations (Thingstrup et al. 1998).

46718f4dfc79.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
46718f4dfc79.sentence: Management of AM fungi is especially important for organic and low-input agriculture systems where soil phosphorus is, in general, low, although all agroecosystems can benefit by promoting arbuscular mycorrhizae establishment.
