1e12bc951928.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
1e12bc951928.sentence: The benefits of AMF are greatest in systems where inputs are low.

d4e59d9a4cf7.title: Siderophore
d4e59d9a4cf7.sentence: Siderophores (Greek: "iron carrier") are small, high-affinity iron-chelating compounds that are secreted by microorganisms such as bacteria and fungi.

184093c8adec.title: Siderophore
184093c8adec.sentence: They help the organism accumulate iron.

096321d81b55.title: Siderophore
096321d81b55.sentence: Phytosiderophores are siderophores produced by plants.

207619ca55c8.title: Siderophore
207619ca55c8.sentence: In most aerobic environments, such as the soil or sea, iron exists in the ferric (Fe3+) state, which tends to form insoluble rust-like solids.

7924574a306c.title: Siderophore
7924574a306c.sentence: Microbes release siderophores to scavenge iron from these mineral phases by formation of soluble Fe3+ complexes that can be taken up by active transport mechanisms.

0643e8557a39.title: Siderophore
0643e8557a39.sentence: Although a widening range of siderophore functions is being appreciated, siderophores are among the strongest known (highest affinity) Fe3+ binding agents.

c38276841be0.title: Siderophore
c38276841be0.sentence: In response to iron limitation in their environment, genes involved in microbe siderophore production and uptake are derepressed, leading to manufacture of siderophores and the appropriate uptake proteins.

be650329c652.title: Siderophore
be650329c652.sentence: Although there is sufficient iron in most soils for plant growth, plant iron deficiency is a problem in calcareous soil, due to the low solubility of iron(III) hydroxide.

33b3ae9b4220.title: Siderophore
33b3ae9b4220.sentence: Calcareous soil accounts for 30% of the world's farmland.

e77eaa505218.title: Siderophore
e77eaa505218.sentence: Under such conditions graminaceous plants (grasses, cereals and rice) secrete phytosiderophores into the soil, a typical example being deoxymugineic acid.

a61d99ad0502.title: Siderophore
a61d99ad0502.sentence: When grown in an iron -deficient soil, roots of graminaceous plants secrete siderophores into the rhizosphere.

a48964f2ca18.title: Siderophore
a48964f2ca18.sentence: Common Gram-positive species are those belonging to the Actinomycetales and species of the genera Bacillus, Arthrobacter and Nocardia.

6d23ba7a55b7.title: Siderophore
6d23ba7a55b7.sentence: Many of these organisms produce and secrete ferrioxamines which lead to growth promotion of not only the producing organisms, but also other microbial populations that are able to utilize exogenous siderophores.

43bb1692ceb1.title: Siderophore
43bb1692ceb1.sentence: Soil fungi include Aspergillus and Penicillium predominantly produce ferrichromes.

1e2269ed0b6c.title: Siderophore
1e2269ed0b6c.sentence: This group of siderophores consist of cyclic hexapeptides and consequently are highly resistant to environmental degradation associated with the wide range of hydrolytic enzymes that are present in humic soil.

659719fa75f1.title: Siderophore
659719fa75f1.sentence: Soils containing decaying plant material possess pH values as low as 3–4.

5e56f58731c5.title: Siderophore
5e56f58731c5.sentence: Under such conditions organisms that produce hydroxamate siderophores have an advantage due to the extreme acid stability of these molecules.

039987d92e52.title: Siderophore
039987d92e52.sentence: Chemical compounds produced by microorganisms in the rhizosphere can also increase the availability and uptake of iron.

f8f4f10ba06d.title: Siderophore
f8f4f10ba06d.sentence: Plants such as oats are able to assimilate iron via these microbial siderophores.

874c3f660a55.title: Siderophore
874c3f660a55.sentence: Fluorescent pseudomonads have been recognized as biocontrol agents against certain soil-borne plant pathogens.

a8ce0782d57a.title: Siderophore
a8ce0782d57a.sentence: They produce yellow-green pigments (pyoverdines) which fluoresce under UV light and function as siderophores.

06051fecdb41.title: Siderophore
06051fecdb41.sentence: They deprive pathogens of the iron required for their growth and pathogenesis.

5e13545a1669.title: Siderophore
5e13545a1669.sentence: Siderophores, natural or synthetic, can chelate metal ions other than iron ions.

3c77944f905c.title: Siderophore
3c77944f905c.sentence: Examples include aluminium, gallium, chromium, copper, zinc, lead, manganese, cadmium, vanadium, zirconium, indium, plutonium, berkelium, californium, and uranium.

3beb9eb08420.title: Root nodule
3beb9eb08420.sentence: Root nodules are found on the roots of plants, primarily legumes, that form a symbiosis with nitrogen-fixing bacteria.

5e68b90e0f59.title: Root nodule
5e68b90e0f59.sentence: Under nitrogen-limiting conditions, capable plants form a symbiotic relationship with a host-specific strain of bacteria known as rhizobia in legumes and strains of actinobacteria of the genus Frankia in other nodulating plants.

83ed75b0df5e.title: Root nodule
83ed75b0df5e.sentence: Indeed, high nitrogen content blocks nodule development as there is no benefit for the plant of forming the symbiosis.

4ccc03c55a49.title: Root nodule
4ccc03c55a49.sentence: Legumes release organic compounds as secondary metabolites called flavonoids from their roots, which attract the rhizobia to them and which also activate nod genes in the bacteria to produce nod factors and initiate nodule formation.

76d45efa5d91.title: Root nodule
76d45efa5d91.sentence: These nod factors initiate root hair curling.

46bb0d607e6d.title: Root nodule
46bb0d607e6d.sentence: Within the root tip, a small tube called the infection thread forms, which provides a pathway for the Rhizobium to travel into the root epidermal cells as the root hair continues to curl.

4723b4539991.title: Root nodule
4723b4539991.sentence: Nitrogen fixation in the nodule is very oxygen sensitive.

0bd140bdde21.title: Root nodule
0bd140bdde21.sentence: Legume nodules harbor an iron containing protein called leghaemoglobin, closely related to animal myoglobin, to facilitate the diffusion of oxygen gas used in respiration.

a7fd3f1af94b.title: Root nodule
a7fd3f1af94b.sentence: The plant provides these cells with leghemoglobin, resulting in a distinct pink color.

cb3541996b0d.title: Root nodule
cb3541996b0d.sentence: The energy for splitting the nitrogen gas in the nodule comes from sugar that is translocated from the leaf (a product of photosynthesis).

5b6072ece68f.title: Root nodule
5b6072ece68f.sentence: Malate as a breakdown product of sucrose is the direct carbon source for the bacteroid.

9d52cfd57258.title: Root nodule
9d52cfd57258.sentence: Two main types of nodule have been described in legumes: determinate and indeterminate.

e7209a69615e.title: Root nodule
e7209a69615e.sentence: Determinate nodules are found on certain tribes of tropical legume such as those of the genera Glycine (soybean), Phaseolus (common bean), and Vigna. and on some temperate legumes such as Lotus.

4993cfb5f0b1.title: Root nodule
4993cfb5f0b1.sentence: These determinate nodules lose meristematic activity shortly after initiation, thus growth is due to cell expansion resulting in mature nodules which are spherical in shape.

6af7230cf885.title: Root nodule
6af7230cf885.sentence: They can be seen in Faboideae legumes such as Pisum (pea), Medicago (alfalfa), Trifolium (clover), and Vicia (vetch) and all mimosoid legumes such as acacias, the few nodulated caesalpinioid legumes such as partridge pea.

5ca70541cb60.title: Root nodule
5ca70541cb60.sentence: They earned the name "indeterminate" because they maintain an active apical meristem that produces new cells for growth over the life of the nodule.

e980fcfa4425.title: Root nodule
e980fcfa4425.sentence: Effective nodulation takes place approximately four weeks after crop planting, with the size, and shape of the nodules dependent on the crop.

689652641e9e.title: Root nodule
689652641e9e.sentence: The number of nodules, and their internal color, will indicate the status of nitrogen fixation in the plant.

6e5edb1dfcc7.title: Root nodule
6e5edb1dfcc7.sentence: Nodulation is controlled by a variety of processes, both external (heat, acidic soils, drought, nitrate) and internal (autoregulation of nodulation, ethylene).

9337ece84613.title: Root nodule
9337ece84613.sentence: Autoregulation of nodulation controls nodule numbers per plant through a systemic process involving the leaf.

eaf20ea19646.title: Root nodule
eaf20ea19646.sentence: When the plant dies, the fixed nitrogen is released, making it available to other plants, and this helps to fertilize the soil.

e4ca962b55a8.title: Root nodule
e4ca962b55a8.sentence: In many traditional farming practices, fields are rotated through various types of crops, which usually includes one consisting mainly or entirely of a leguminous crop such as clover, in order to take advantage of this.

2b65c099fc6e.title: Root mucilage
2b65c099fc6e.sentence: Root mucilage is made of plant-specific polysaccharides or long chains of sugar molecules.

be765eeed19d.title: Root mucilage
be765eeed19d.sentence: This polysaccharide secretion of root exudate forms a gelatinous substance that sticks to the caps of roots.

260d5253cb8a.title: Root mucilage
260d5253cb8a.sentence: Root mucilage is a part of a wider secrete from plant roots known as root exudate.

d3cadb6d419e.title: Root mucilage
d3cadb6d419e.sentence: Just how this root mucilage is secreted is debated, but there is growing evidence that mucilage derives from ruptured cells.

65b6d5735ac4.title: Root mucilage
65b6d5735ac4.sentence: As roots penetrate through the soil, many of the cells surrounding the caps of roots are continually shed and replaced.

18704a4ff7cc.title: Root mucilage
18704a4ff7cc.sentence: These ruptured or lysed cells release their component parts, which include the polysaccharides that form root mucilage.

7c614921b5a4.title: Root mucilage
7c614921b5a4.sentence: These polysaccharides come from the Golgi apparatus and plant cell wall, which are rich in plant-specific polysaccharides.

122b36706920.title: Root mucilage
122b36706920.sentence: Several scientists have determined the composition of plant root mucilage using monosaccharide analysis and linkage analysis, showing that Maize (Zea mays) root mucilage contains high levels of galactose, xylose, arabinose, rhamnose, and glucose, and lower levels of uronic acid, mannose, fucose, and glucuronic acid.

9cd7ac354814.title: Root mucilage
9cd7ac354814.sentence: With the following monosaccharides determined as well as their linkages, scientists have determined the presence of pectin, arabinogalactan proteins, xyloglucan, arabinan, and xylan, which are plant-specific polysaccharides within the root mucilage of plants.

c86abe27cc94.title: Root mucilage
c86abe27cc94.section: Importance and role of root mucilage
c86abe27cc94.sentence: Plants use up to 40% of their energy secreting root mucilage, which they generate from photosynthesis that takes place in the leaves.

80f1a068d751.title: Root mucilage
80f1a068d751.section: Importance and role of root mucilage
80f1a068d751.sentence: Root mucilage also helps soil to stick to roots.

342792fdc747.title: Root mucilage
342792fdc747.section: Importance and role of root mucilage
342792fdc747.sentence: The purpose of this is to maintain the plant's contact with the soil so that the plant can regulate the levels of water it can absorb, decrease friction so that roots can penetrate through the soil, and maintain a micro-climate.

e4a87989114d.title: Root mucilage
e4a87989114d.section: Importance and role of root mucilage
e4a87989114d.sentence: Root mucilage contributes to the particular hydrophysical properties of the rhizosphere, which can affect the plant's response to water deficit.

f0daaa8e1d9d.title: Root mucilage
f0daaa8e1d9d.section: Importance and role of root mucilage
f0daaa8e1d9d.sentence: For example, root mucilage can reduce evaporation and store water in the rhizosphere.

f7630f081f35.title: Root mucilage
f7630f081f35.section: Importance and role of root mucilage
f7630f081f35.sentence: Root mucilage plays a role in developing a symbiotic relationship with the soil-dwelling fungi.

6484bc193bb9.title: Root mucilage
6484bc193bb9.section: Importance and role of root mucilage
6484bc193bb9.sentence: In return, the fungi receive food in the form of carbohydrates from the plant in the form of broken-down root mucilage.

9e4ad0181306.title: Root mucilage
9e4ad0181306.section: Importance and role of root mucilage
9e4ad0181306.sentence: This important relationship is known to affect 94% of land plants, and benefits plants by increasing water and nutrient uptake from the soil, particularly phosphorus.

924255dd161c.title: Mucilage
924255dd161c.sentence: Sierra Mixe is a tall variety of maize with aerial roots that produce a sweet mucilage.

13f4a106b489.title: Mucilage
13f4a106b489.sentence: It survives in poor soils without fertilizer in Oaxaca, Mexico, and the mucilage has been shown to support nitrogen fixation through bacteria that thrive in its high-sugar, low-oxygen environment

0ece5834e712.title: Ericoid mycorrhiza
0ece5834e712.sentence: The ericoid mycorrhiza is a mutualistic relationship formed between members of the plant family Ericaceae and several lineages of mycorrhizal fungi.

240995469012.title: Ericoid mycorrhiza
240995469012.sentence: This symbiosis represents an important adaptation to acidic and nutrient poor soils that species in the Ericaceae typically inhabit, including boreal forests, bogs, and heathlands.

058a590e3a81.title: Ericoid mycorrhiza
058a590e3a81.sentence: Ericoid mycorrhizas are characterized by fungal coils that form in the epidermal cells of the fine hair roots of ericaceous species.

9c2692800465.title: Ericoid mycorrhiza
9c2692800465.sentence: The coil is the site where fungi exchange nutrients obtained from the soil for carbohydrates fixed through photosynthesis by the plant.

535d5f205f83.title: Ericoid mycorrhiza
535d5f205f83.sentence: Evidence suggests that coils only function for a period of a few weeks before the plant cell and fungal hyphae begin to degrade.

4f98b615ebef.title: Ericoid mycorrhiza
4f98b615ebef.sentence: Ericoid mycorrhizal fungi have been shown to have enzymatic capabilities to break down complex organic molecules.

4cfd7db46f69.title: Ericoid mycorrhiza
4cfd7db46f69.sentence: However, the primary function of these enzymatic capabilities is likely to access organic forms of nutrients, such as nitrogen, whose mineralized forms are in very limiting quantities in habitats typically occupied by ericaceous plants.

95e74774c9e7.title: Mycorrhiza
95e74774c9e7.sentence: They can extract nitrogen from cellulose, hemicellulose, lignin, pectin, and chitin.

36f66f9d868d.title: Humus form
36f66f9d868d.sentence: Fine root systems are also present in OH horizons, together with subterranean organs of heathland plants (e.g. Ericaceae) and their symbiotic fungal associates (ericoid mycorrhizae) which are able to decompose recalcitrant organic matter and transfer its nitrogen to the host plant.

c2109b549709.title: Humus form
c2109b549709.sentence: It has been demonstrated that nitrogen transfer occurs directly from slowly decomposing plant remains to vegetation, via the mycelium of ectomycorrhizal and ericoid fungi, in relation to the exploratory capacity of mycelia, at its maximum in mor.

1c2c962e63d5.title: Spermosphere
1c2c962e63d5.sentence: In plant science, the spermosphere is the zone surrounding a seed where soil, microorganisms, and seed germinating interact.

fbd280ea5920.title: Spermosphere
fbd280ea5920.sentence: The zone is a small area, typically 1–10 mm from the seed, but varying with seed type, the variety of soil microorganisms, the level of soil moisture, and other factors.

f8ab19437275.title: Spermosphere
f8ab19437275.sentence: Seeds exude various molecules that influence their surrounding microbial communities, either inhibiting or stimulating their growth.

fa9012b12438.title: Spermosphere
fa9012b12438.sentence: Soil type matters much more than seed type, specifically soil with a higher content of organic matter.

f412ae99422c.title: Spermosphere
f412ae99422c.sentence: Many plant pathogens such as Fusarium and Pythium ultimum can colonize a newly germinating seed within the first few hours of planting.

61e63f9d9e95.title: Spermosphere
61e63f9d9e95.sentence: The seed can exudate molecules and nutrients that attract beneficial microorganisms to their spermosphere which then prevent the colonization of pathogens.

26a5106b749a.title: Spermosphere
26a5106b749a.sentence: Because germination is a brief process, the spermosphere is transient, but the impact of the microbial activity within the spermosphere can have strong and long-lasting effects on the developing plant.

31e1f0b89124.title: Spermosphere
31e1f0b89124.sentence: With these biochemical effects, the spermosphere develops both downward—to form the rhizosphere (upon the emergence of the plant's radicle)—and upward to form the laimosphere, which is the soil surrounding the growing plant stem, and the phyllosphere, which is the microbial community on the part of the plant above the soil.

1b5f9e8f5b7f.title: Mycorrhiza
1b5f9e8f5b7f.sentence: However, a few species, known as dual-mycorrhizal plants, can simultaneously associate with both arbuscular and ectomycorrhizal fungi within the same root system.

11920e8e9272.title: Mycorrhiza
11920e8e9272.sentence: Plants typically form associations with only one type of mycorrhizal fungi.

3b8070f83aef.title: Mycorrhiza
3b8070f83aef.sentence: The costs and benefits of forming dual-mycorrhizal associations are not fully understood, but appear to be dependent on the plant's life stage and abiotic conditions.

70c665718faf.title: Mycorrhiza
70c665718faf.sentence: Mycorrhizal switching, the ability to shift between fungal types, has also been reported under a wide range of biotic and abiotic conditions.

c9e9a5593321.title: Mycorrhiza
c9e9a5593321.sentence: Dual-mycorrhizal plants often occupy broader geographical ranges and environmental niche spaces compared to plants restricted to a single mycorrhizal type.

a6142b629116.title: Mycorrhiza
a6142b629116.sentence: This allows such plants to spread into habitats where one of the two mycorrhizal fungi types might be absent.

93f3ed9abd8e.title: Mycorrhiza
93f3ed9abd8e.sentence: Thus, the role of dual mycorrhiza in primary and secondary succession, particularly in nutrient-poor soils, has been highlighted, as they can facilitate ecosystem recovery.

68657b317a89.title: Mycorrhiza
68657b317a89.sentence: Due to their unique capabilities, dual-mycorrhizal plants are increasingly recognised as key components in ecological restoration and reforestation, especially in regions where woodland tree species face limited access to mycorrhizal fungal inoculum.

475fb9a87e7a.title: Mycorrhiza
475fb9a87e7a.sentence: Ecological nucleation of ectomycorrhizal woodland tree species around dual-mycorrhizal Salix species has been observed within arbuscular mycorrhizal dominated vegetation.

a80ee3f3063f.title: Mycorrhiza
a80ee3f3063f.sentence: Earlier observations by others also contributed to understanding these root-fungal associations.

e2a60012d044.title: Mycorrhiza
e2a60012d044.sentence: In the 20th century, researchers expanded understanding of mycorrhizal diversity and prevalence across plant families.

df96ac12afff.title: Mycorrhiza
df96ac12afff.sentence: In 1881, Franciszek Kamieński had shown that the plant Monotropa hypopitys relied on fungi from neighboring trees for nutrition, highlighting fungal dependency.

94d3f6099b5f.title: Mycorrhiza
94d3f6099b5f.sentence: Mycorrhizal fungi were first formally described and named in 1885 by German botanist A.B. Frank, who coined the term "mycorrhiza".

2557f9c453fb.title: Mycorrhiza
2557f9c453fb.sentence: Noël Bernard established in 1899 that orchids like Neottia nidus-avis require a specific fungus for seed germination.

95f805f9f6a6.title: Mycorrhiza
95f805f9f6a6.sentence: Paleobotanists working on the Rhynie chert fossils demonstrated that mycorrhizal-like associations existed 407 million years ago in early land plants.

ea8d1d306af3.title: Mycorrhiza
ea8d1d306af3.sentence: Laccaria bicolor became the first ectomycorrhizal fungus to have its genome sequenced in 2008, revealing the genetic basis of symbiosis through gene duplications and specialized secreted proteins.

66f6414e6351.title: Mycorrhiza
66f6414e6351.sentence: This work opened the molecular era of mycorrhizal research.

323ad8a0f3b6.title: Mycorrhiza
323ad8a0f3b6.sentence: CO2 released by human activities is causing climate change and possible damage to mycorrhizae, but the direct effect of an increase in the gas should be to benefit plants and mycorrhizae if other factors are not limiting.

95d01b3980cf.title: Mycorrhiza
95d01b3980cf.sentence: Since mycorrhizae tend to do better in cooler temperatures, warming could be detrimental to them.

c618e1812c8e.title: Mycorrhiza
c618e1812c8e.sentence: In Arctic regions, nitrogen and water are harder for plants to obtain, making mycorrhizae crucial to plant growth.

b87f3c387486.title: Mycorrhiza
b87f3c387486.sentence: Gases such as SO2, NOx, and O3 produced by human activity may harm mycorrhizae, causing reduction in "propagules, the colonization of roots, degradation in connections between trees, reduction in the mycorrhizal incidence in trees, and reduction in the enzyme activity of ectomycorrhizal roots."

8e1f907a4d08.title: Ammonia fungi
8e1f907a4d08.sentence: Air pollution in particular can damage mycorrhizal structures.

a7485e7eb58a.title: Ammonia fungi
a7485e7eb58a.sentence: Decomposition of excessive ammonia in the atmosphere may actually cause harm to fine mycorrhizal structures.

5fd4769b3e34.title: Mycorrhiza
5fd4769b3e34.sentence: Plants grown in sterile soils and growth media often perform poorly without the addition of spores or hyphae of mycorrhizal fungi to colonise the plant roots and aid in the uptake of soil mineral nutrients.

0fed485c440c.title: Mycorrhiza
0fed485c440c.sentence: The absence of mycorrhizal fungi can also slow plant growth in early succession or on degraded landscapes.

d6de1e8b7c5d.title: Mycorrhiza
d6de1e8b7c5d.sentence: The introduction of alien mycorrhizal plants to nutrient-deficient ecosystems puts indigenous non-mycorrhizal plants at a competitive disadvantage.

d75d653d54e0.title: Mycorrhiza
d75d653d54e0.sentence: Suillus tomentosus, a basidiomycete fungus, produces specialized structures known as tuberculate ectomycorrhizae with its plant host lodgepole pine (Pinus contorta var. latifolia).

2a31441a1ed5.title: Mycorrhiza
2a31441a1ed5.sentence: These structures have been shown to host nitrogen fixing bacteria which contribute a significant amount of nitrogen and allow the pines to colonize nutrient-poor sites.

41e5db9252e1.title: Orchid mycorrhiza
41e5db9252e1.sentence: Orchid mycorrhizae are endomycorrhizal fungi which develop symbiotic relationships with the roots and seeds of plants of the family Orchidaceae.

223c43da71c7.title: Orchid mycorrhiza
223c43da71c7.sentence: Orchid seeds are very small (0.35mm to 1.50mm long), spindle-shaped, and have an opening at the pointed end.

18b0b93af11d.title: Orchid mycorrhiza
18b0b93af11d.sentence: Orchid mycorrhizae are critically important during orchid germination, as an orchid seed has virtually no energy reserve and obtains its carbon from the fungal symbiont.

d1c891fecdfe.title: Orchid mycorrhiza
d1c891fecdfe.sentence: Nearly all orchids are myco-heterotrophic at some point in their life cycle.

5329a8fa8e88.title: Orchid mycorrhiza
5329a8fa8e88.section: Fungal entry into orchid > Fungal pelotons and orchid root cortex
5329a8fa8e88.sentence: Shortly after the fungus enters an orchid, the fungus produces intracellular hyphal coils called pelotons in the embryos of developing seedlings and the roots of adult plants.

fe28dc92bb9d.title: Orchid mycorrhiza
fe28dc92bb9d.section: Fungal entry into orchid > Fungal pelotons and orchid root cortex
fe28dc92bb9d.sentence: The formation of pelotons in root cortical cells is a defining anatomical structure in orchid mycorrhiza that differentiate it from other forms of fungi.

e6dfe04cd302.title: Orchid mycorrhiza
e6dfe04cd302.sentence: The transfer of nitrogen and carbon as discussed above readily occurs through live pelotons, but it has been observed by Kuga 2014 and Rasumussen 2009 that large amount of carbon and nitrogen may also be taken up by the plant during the senescence and digestion of fungal pelotons.

426f923d9ba9.title: Orchid mycorrhiza
426f923d9ba9.sentence: The fungi that form orchid mycorrhizae are typically basidiomycetes.

00d41db913df.title: Orchid mycorrhiza
00d41db913df.sentence: These come from a range of taxa including Ceratobasidium (Rhizoctonia), Sebacina, Tulasnella and Russula species.

15dab80098d4.title: Orchid mycorrhiza
15dab80098d4.sentence: Phosphorus is a crucial nutrient needed by all plants and often phosphorus deficiency in soil will dictate the formation of a symbiotic relationship.

0a1f97865897.title: Orchid mycorrhiza
0a1f97865897.sentence: Phosphorus is obtained by the mycorrhizal fungus from the surrounding soil in three different forms; organic phosphorus, phosphate, and inorganic phosphorus compounds.

7514e5e80cf1.title: Rhizosphere
7514e5e80cf1.sentence: Although it goes beyond the rhizosphere area, it is notable that some plants secrete allelochemicals from their roots, which inhibits the growth of other organisms.

0a46fac4a5c4.title: Rhizosphere
0a46fac4a5c4.sentence: The rhizosphere also provides space to produce allelochemicals to control neighbours and relatives.

8e1347ff53d2.title: Rhizosphere
8e1347ff53d2.sentence: For example, garlic mustard produces a chemical that is believed to prevent mutualisms forming between the surrounding trees and mycorrhiza in mesic North American temperate forests where it is an invasive species.

888cabd8f6aa.title: Ectomycorrhiza
888cabd8f6aa.sentence: Invasive garlic mustard, Alliaria petiolata, and its allelochemical benzyl isothiocyanate were shown to inhibit the growth of three species of EcM fungi grown on white pine seedlings.

62aded0d0cd6.title: Cover crop
62aded0d0cd6.sentence: In addition to competition-based or physical weed suppression, certain cover crops are known to suppress weeds through allelopathy.

adab6caf5657.title: Cover crop
adab6caf5657.sentence: Some well known examples of allelopathic cover crops are Secale cereale (rye), Vicia villosa (hairy vetch), Trifolium pratense (red clover), Sorghum bicolor (sorghum-sudangrass), and species in the family Brassicaceae, particularly mustards.

0515a90e5ab0.title: Crop rotation
0515a90e5ab0.sentence: Thus rotation allows increased yields from nutrient availability but also alleviation of allelopathy and competitive weed environments.

c801748b9667.title: Rhizosphere
c801748b9667.sentence: The following are some methods commonly used or of interest in rhizosphere research.

1c3719ac3550.title: Rhizosphere
1c3719ac3550.sentence: Many of these methods include both field testing of the root systems and in-lab testing using simulated environments to perform experiments, such as pH determination.

855e19ff846e.title: Rhizosphere
855e19ff846e.sentence: High-Throughput Sequencing: Amplification and sequencing of marker genes such as 16S rRNA (for bacteria) and Internal Transcribed Spacer (ITS) region (for fungi) to determine microbial community composition and diversity.

33f1a1594dc4.title: Rhizosphere
33f1a1594dc4.sentence: Metagenomics and Metatranscriptomics: Shotgun sequencing of total DNA or RNA to assess the genetic potential and active gene expression of the entire rhizosphere microbial community.

25b12505d07b.title: Rhizosphere
25b12505d07b.sentence: - Various methods used to determine water movement in the rhizosphere e.g. microelectrodes and agar techniques for pH and microsampling of rhizosphere materials

fd63b2e61d8e.title: Rhizosphere
fd63b2e61d8e.sentence: - Pyrolysis–field ionization mass spectrometry allows for spectrometry of agricultural fields to find fulvic and humic acids and the extraction residues (humins) in certain studies and expanded to general organic compounds in other recent work.

5fd60a134bb7.title: Rhizosphere
5fd60a134bb7.sentence: A large number of signals can be exchanged involving the plant itself, insects, fungi, and microbes.

86985d3d0a3e.title: Rhizosphere
86985d3d0a3e.sentence: Usually, communication results from chemical responses of cells to signatory molecules from other cells.

0664aa689edb.title: Rhizosphere
0664aa689edb.sentence: The microbial community's composition is mainly shaped and recruited by hundreds of metabolites released in the soil by plant roots, which normally facilitate interactions with the biotic and abiotic environment.

87e212f3e29e.title: Rhizosphere
87e212f3e29e.sentence: Often the plant can modulate its diversity based on the benefits in terms of growth and health, such as with plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria.

04a784586bb9.title: Rhizosphere
04a784586bb9.sentence: Symbiotic nitrogen-fixing bacteria, such as Rhizobium species, detect compounds like flavonoids secreted by the roots of leguminous plants and then produce nod factors that signal to the plant that they are present and will lead to the formation of root nodules.

ee70545f5318.title: Rhizosphere
ee70545f5318.sentence: This symbiosis is a highly specific process in which the genetic and chemical communication signals are strictly plant-bacterium-specific.

23f3c561103c.title: Rhizosphere
23f3c561103c.sentence: Strigolactones, secreted and detected by mycorrhizal fungi, stimulate the germination of spores and initiate changes in the mycorrhiza that allow it to colonize the root.

26e6cc0d598b.title: Rhizosphere
26e6cc0d598b.sentence: The parasitic plant, Striga, also detects the presence of strigolactones and will germinate when it detects them; they will then move into the root, feeding off the nutrients present.

eeae71392f73.title: Rhizosphere
eeae71392f73.sentence: Nevertheless, a large number of nutrients issued by the plant can be of interest to pathogenic organisms, which can take advantage of plant products for their survival in the rhizosphere.

9cd82e3460c7.title: Hartig net
9cd82e3460c7.sentence: The Hartig net is the network of inward-growing hyphae, that extends into the plant host root, penetrating between plant cells in the root epidermis and cortex in ectomycorrhizal symbiosis.

ec8e328f1a96.title: Hartig net
ec8e328f1a96.sentence: The Hartig net is the site of mutualistic resource exchange between the fungus and the host plant.

b12412234270.title: Hartig net
b12412234270.sentence: Essential nutrients for plant growth are acquired from the soil by exploration and foraging of the extramatrical mycelium, then transported through the hyphal network across the mantle and into the Hartig net, where they are released by the fungi into the root apoplastic space for uptake by the plant.

940d1ccac39b.title: Hartig net
940d1ccac39b.sentence: The hyphae in the Hartig net acquire sugars from the plant root, which are transported to the external mycelium to provide a carbon source to sustain fungal growth.

012d8da51ad9.title: Hartig net
012d8da51ad9.sentence: The Hartig net supplies the plant root with chemical elements required for plant growth, such as nitrogen and phosphorus, potassium, and micronutrients in addition to water supplied to the roots through hyphal transport.

2433461b2db3.title: Hartig net
2433461b2db3.sentence: Fungi associating with plants in the Pinaceae form a robust Hartig net that penetrates between cells deep into the root cortex, while the Hartig net formation in ectomycorrhizal symbioses with many angiosperms may not extend beyond the root epidermis.

323a852ef271.title: Hartig net
323a852ef271.sentence: The Hartig net is named after Theodor Hartig, a 19th-century German forest biologist and botanist.

4d08b12fd297.title: Hartig net
4d08b12fd297.sentence: He reported research in 1842 on the anatomy of the interface between ectomycorrhizal fungi and tree roots.

e8bbbe24345e.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
e8bbbe24345e.sentence: Arbuscular mycorrhizal symbiosis affects the community and diversity of other organisms in the soil.

d3f6927d938c.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
d3f6927d938c.sentence: This can be directly seen by the release of exudates, or indirectly by a change in the plant species and plant exudates type and amount.

30cc464b72f7.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
30cc464b72f7.sentence: A change in the amount or composition of root exudates and fungal exudates due to the existing AM mycorrhizal colonization determines the diversity and abundance of the bacterial community in the rhizosphere.

5adfe7cab8e7.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
5adfe7cab8e7.sentence: Bacterial species differ in their abilities to compete for carbon compound root exudates.

b53af5de9b3c.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
b53af5de9b3c.sentence: When rhizobium bacteria are present in the soil, mycorrhizal colonization is increased due to an increase in the concentration of chemical signals involved in the establishment of symbiosis (Xie et al. 2003).

e221b2bf8218.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
e221b2bf8218.sentence: Effective mycorrhizal colonization can also increase the nodulations and symbiotic nitrogen fixation in mycorrhizal legumes.

e3ff11664927.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
e3ff11664927.sentence: Mycorrhizae diversity has been shown to increase plant species diversity as the potential number of associations increases.

7ed035957831.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
7ed035957831.sentence: Dominant arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi can prevent the invasion of non-mycorrhizal plants on land where they have established symbiosis and promote their mycorrhizal host.

6f3dc84d65b4.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
6f3dc84d65b4.sentence: AM fungi become less prevalent and diverse at higher soil nutrient and moisture concentrations, presumably because both plants allocate less carbon to AM fungi and AM fungi reallocate their resources to intraradical hyphae in these environmental conditions.

b1b2ad55e4ed.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
b1b2ad55e4ed.section: Molecular genetic analyses of arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi
b1b2ad55e4ed.sentence: Advances in molecular genetic technologies and tools have allowed microbial and mycorrhizal ecologists to ask new questions about the ecological and evolutionary roles of arbuscular mycorrhizal (AM) fungi as individuals, in communities and ecosystems.

6575cc0bde9e.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
6575cc0bde9e.section: Molecular genetic analyses of arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi > Overview of methods > DNA/RNA
6575cc0bde9e.sentence: Genetic analyses of AM fungi from soil and root samples range in their applicability to answer ecological or phylogenetic questions.

0255bee09220.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
0255bee09220.section: Molecular genetic analyses of arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi > Overview of methods > DNA/RNA
0255bee09220.sentence: DNA analyses utilize various nuclear markers to describe AM fungi and represent different regions of the nuclear ribosomal operon (18S rRNA) found in all eukaryotic organisms.

d6cafd3a8972.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
d6cafd3a8972.section: Molecular genetic analyses of arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi > Overview of methods > qPCR and qRT-PCR
d6cafd3a8972.sentence: Real-time PCR or quantitative PCR (qPCR), is becoming a well-established method to quickly amplify and simultaneously quantify targeted AM fungal DNA from biological samples (plant roots or soils).

f364eec81c1b.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
f364eec81c1b.section: Molecular genetic analyses of arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi > Overview of methods > PLFA/NLFA
f364eec81c1b.sentence: The fatty acid, 16:1ω5 is the most commonly used acid to characterize AM fungi in soils and can be used as a strong indicator of mycelial biomass in soil sample.

e5d7a9c4f052.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
e5d7a9c4f052.section: Molecular genetic analyses of arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi > Overview of methods > PLFA/NLFA
e5d7a9c4f052.sentence: For example, in AM fungi the proportion of the fatty acids, 16:1ω5 and 18:1ω7, in the phospholipid portion account for approximately 58% of total fatty acid composition.

d212c80a7c14.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
d212c80a7c14.section: Molecular genetic analyses of arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi > Overview of methods > PLFA/NLFA
d212c80a7c14.sentence: Energy is mainly stored in AM fungi as neutral lipids in storage structures like spores and vesicles.

ee89badbe1cb.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
ee89badbe1cb.section: Molecular genetic analyses of arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi > Overview of methods > PLFA/NLFA
ee89badbe1cb.sentence: Because of this NLFA correlates quite well with the number of spores in a given volume of soil.

f8f48aa110fd.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
f8f48aa110fd.section: Molecular genetic analyses of arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi > Overview of methods > PLFA/NLFA
f8f48aa110fd.sentence: The ratio of NLFA concentration to PLFA concentration (active mycelia) can then give the proportion of carbon allocated to storage structures (spores, measured as NLFA).

2941e2b42732.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
2941e2b42732.section: Molecular genetic analyses of arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi > Future research directions with AM fungi
2941e2b42732.sentence: Stable isotope probing (SIP) is a technique that can be used to determine the active metabolic function of individual taxa within a complex system of microbes.

0156fbde7a3a.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
0156fbde7a3a.section: Molecular genetic analyses of arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi > Future research directions with AM fungi > Stable Isotope Probing (SIP)
0156fbde7a3a.sentence: SIP, more explicitly DNA/RNA-based SIP, uses stable-isotope enriched substrates, such as 13C, 15N, or H218O, and then analyzes the 'labeled' markers using species specific DNA or RNA markers.

88fa1304b9c0.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
88fa1304b9c0.sentence: A relatively new approach to restoring land is to inoculate soil with AM fungi when reintroducing vegetation in ecological restoration projects (phytoremediation).

24cc3c6edb81.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
24cc3c6edb81.sentence: When restoring disturbed land, it is essential to replace not only the above ground vegetation but also biological and physical soil properties.

7ddb12cf6e3e.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
7ddb12cf6e3e.sentence: Disturbance of native plant communities in desertification-threatened areas is often followed by degradation of physical and biological soil properties, soil structure, nutrient availability, and organic matter.

0a295cbccd48.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
0a295cbccd48.sentence: Soils' quality parameters were significantly improved long-term when a mixture of indigenous arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi species was introduced compared to noninoculated soil and soil inoculated with a single exotic species of AM fungi.

e53f0d9b3f74.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
e53f0d9b3f74.sentence: The benefits were increased plant growth, increased phosphorus uptake and soil nitrogen content, higher soil organic matter content, and soil aggregation, attributed to higher legume nodulation in the presence of AM fungi, better water infiltration, and soil aeration due to soil aggregation.

435270d7c416.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
435270d7c416.sentence: Restoration of native AM fungi increases the success of ecological restoration projects and the rapidity of soil recovery.

1b2fb6d42e8b.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
1b2fb6d42e8b.sentence: Native strains of AM fungi enhance the extraction of heavy metal(s) from the polluted soils and make the soil healthy and suitable for crop production.

67af05bf89a9.title: Plant use of endophytic fungi in defense
67af05bf89a9.sentence: Plant use of endophytic fungi in defense occurs when endophytic fungi, which live symbiotically with the majority of plants by entering their cells, are utilized as an indirect defense against herbivores.
67af05bf89a9.key: Plant use of endophytic fungi in defense

4305f2799c53.title: Plant use of endophytic fungi in defense
4305f2799c53.sentence: In exchange for carbohydrate energy resources, the fungus provides benefits to the plant which can include increased water or nutrient uptake and protection from phytophagous insects, birds or mammals.
4305f2799c53.key: Plant use of endophytic fungi in defense

046a5672c647.title: Plant use of endophytic fungi in defense
046a5672c647.sentence: Once associated, the fungi alter nutrient content of the plant and enhance or begin production of secondary metabolites.
046a5672c647.key: Plant use of endophytic fungi in defense

cea026efd586.title: Plant use of endophytic fungi in defense
cea026efd586.sentence: The change in chemical composition acts to deter herbivory by insects, grazing by ungulates and/or oviposition by adult insects.
cea026efd586.key: Plant use of endophytic fungi in defense

79bc3a550a99.title: Plant use of endophytic fungi in defense
79bc3a550a99.section: Impacts on host plants > Herbivory prevention
79bc3a550a99.sentence: Even below-ground herbivores such as nematodes and root-feeding insects are reduced by endophyte infection.
79bc3a550a99.key: Plant use of endophytic fungi in defense

0073135fc6d8.title: Plant use of endophytic fungi in defense
0073135fc6d8.section: Importance to humans > Agriculture and livestock
0073135fc6d8.sentence: Endophytic fungi can even cause severe toxicity in grazing livestock, which is often referred to as fescue toxicosis.
0073135fc6d8.key: Plant use of endophytic fungi in defense

74bf9306064f.title: Plant use of endophytic fungi in defense
74bf9306064f.section: Importance to humans > Agriculture and livestock
74bf9306064f.sentence: The secondary chemicals produced by endophytic fungi when associated with their host plants can be very harmful to mammals including livestock and humans, causing more than 600 million dollars in losses due to dead livestock every year.
74bf9306064f.key: Plant use of endophytic fungi in defense

0da180ab93bf.title: Rhizobium
0da180ab93bf.sentence: Rhizobium is a genus of Gram-negative soil bacteria that are aerobic, rod-shaped nitrogen fixers.

9ba121e95127.title: Rhizobium
9ba121e95127.sentence: Rhizobium species form an endosymbiotic nitrogen-fixing association with roots of (primarily) legumes and other flowering plants.

576829b480fb.title: Rhizobium
576829b480fb.sentence: The bacteria colonize plant cells to form root nodules, where they convert atmospheric nitrogen into ammonia using the enzyme nitrogenase.

67310436e9b8.title: Rhizobium
67310436e9b8.sentence: The ammonia is shared with the host plant in the form of organic nitrogenous compounds such as glutamine or ureides.

76e7a72cee66.title: Rhizobium
76e7a72cee66.sentence: The plant, in turn, provides the bacteria with organic compounds made by photosynthesis.

8aa0706b65ae.title: Rhizobium
8aa0706b65ae.sentence: Martinus Beijerinck was the first to isolate and cultivate a microorganism from the nodules of legumes in 1888.

efbd52039018.title: Rhizobium
efbd52039018.sentence: He named it Bacillus radicicola, which is now placed in Bergey's Manual of Determinative Bacteriology under the genus Rhizobium.

7545d513bf0b.title: Rhizobium
7545d513bf0b.sentence: Rhizobium is also capable of solubilizing phosphate.

38206d2c915c.title: Rhizobium
38206d2c915c.sentence: Rhizobium rhizogenes is a pathogenic species of Rhizobium that causes hairy root disease by injecting a root-inducing T-DNA into the plants.

cc7b57cf3714.title: Ectomycorrhiza
cc7b57cf3714.sentence: In commercial forestry, the transplanting of crop trees to new locations often requires an accompanying ectomycorrhizal partner.

ffdbc9eae71a.title: Ectomycorrhiza
ffdbc9eae71a.sentence: The role of ectomycorrhizas in supporting their host plants has led to the suggestion that EcM fungi could be used in restoration projects aimed at re-establishing native plant species in ecosystems disrupted by a variety of issues.

0907b8ba7cc5.title: Ectomycorrhiza
0907b8ba7cc5.sentence: This is especially true of trees that have a high degree of specificity for their mycobiont, or trees that are being planted far from their native habitat among novel fungal species.

96c4c2dbab70.title: Ectomycorrhiza
96c4c2dbab70.sentence: This has been repeatedly shown in plantations involving obligate ectomycorrhizal trees, such as Eucalyptus and Pinus species.

54361f4aa1de.title: Ectomycorrhiza
54361f4aa1de.sentence: Mass planting of these species often requires an inoculum of native EcM fungi for the trees to prosper.

31f31e49f731.title: Ectomycorrhiza
31f31e49f731.sentence: Since the disappearance of mycorhizal fungi from a habitat constitutes a major soil disturbance event, their re-addition is an important part of establishing vegetation and restoring habitats.

06825f1c7f7d.title: Ectomycorrhiza
06825f1c7f7d.sentence: Sometimes ectomycorrhizal plantation species, such as pine and eucalyptus, are planted and promoted for their ability to act as a sink for atmospheric carbon.

8a23c4956c3d.title: Ectomycorrhiza
8a23c4956c3d.sentence: However, the ectomycorrhizal fungi of these species also tend to deplete soil carbon, making this use of plantations controversial.

36f9b1c52161.title: Ectomycorrhiza
36f9b1c52161.sentence: Ectomycorrhizal fungi are not prominent in agricultural and horticultural systems.

1592d1d1c5f9.title: Ectomycorrhiza
1592d1d1c5f9.sentence: Most of the economically relevant crop plants that form mycorrhizas tend to form them with arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi.

d0e2275c5cf6.title: Ectomycorrhiza
d0e2275c5cf6.sentence: Many studies also show that EcM fungi allow plants to tolerate soils with high concentrations of heavy metals, salts, radionuclides and organic pollutants.

1e59c70bd2b6.title: Ectomycorrhiza
1e59c70bd2b6.section: Resilience in challenging environments > Heavy metals
1e59c70bd2b6.sentence: Some ectomycorrhizal fungi are tolerant to heavy metals, with many species having the ability to colonize contaminated soils.

dc7480d681fc.title: Ectomycorrhiza
dc7480d681fc.section: Resilience in challenging environments > Heavy metals
dc7480d681fc.sentence: These mechanisms include reducing heavy metal uptake, sequestering and storing heavy metals within the cell, and excretion.

a5867e0831a0.title: Ectomycorrhiza
a5867e0831a0.section: Resilience in challenging environments > Heavy metals
a5867e0831a0.sentence: Heavy metal uptake can be reduced by sorption and metabolic inactivation at the cell wall and apoplast level.

8a732257bb93.title: Ectomycorrhiza
8a732257bb93.section: Resilience in challenging environments > Heavy metals
8a732257bb93.sentence: Once inside the cell, heavy metals can be immobilized in organo-metal complexes, made soluble, transformed into metallothioneins, involved in metal sequestration and/or stored in vacuoles in chemically inactive forms.

3c3fbbdac9a9.title: Ectomycorrhiza
3c3fbbdac9a9.section: Resilience in challenging environments > Heavy metals
3c3fbbdac9a9.sentence: Ectomycorrhizal fungi can also concentrate heavy metals in their fruiting bodies.

73f8c897137f.title: Ectomycorrhiza
73f8c897137f.section: Resilience in challenging environments > Heavy metals
73f8c897137f.sentence: Genetic differences between populations growing in toxic versus non-toxic habitats have rarely been reported, indicating that metal tolerance is widespread.

40d787f72c00.title: Ectomycorrhiza
40d787f72c00.section: Resilience in challenging environments > Heavy metals
40d787f72c00.sentence: There is, however, evidence for community shifts associated with heavy metals, with lower diversity associated with contaminated sites.

a3249ea2e714.title: Ectomycorrhiza
a3249ea2e714.section: Resilience in challenging environments > Heavy metals
a3249ea2e714.sentence: On the other hand, soils naturally rich in heavy metals, such as serpentine soils, do not seem to affect the diversity of ectomycorrhizal fungal communities.

80d7428360f2.title: Ectomycorrhiza
80d7428360f2.section: Resilience in challenging environments > Heavy metals
80d7428360f2.sentence: Suillus luteus and S. bovinus are good examples, with known ecotypes adapted to Zn, Cd and Cu.

86d6256abbd0.title: Ectomycorrhiza
86d6256abbd0.section: Resilience in challenging environments > Pollution and phytoremediation
86d6256abbd0.sentence: • High salt: A number of studies have shown that certain EcM fungi can help their hosts survive high soil salinity conditions.

a350fb3c1022.title: Ectomycorrhiza
a350fb3c1022.section: Resilience in challenging environments > Pollution and phytoremediation
a350fb3c1022.sentence: • Organic pollutants: Some EcM species are capable of decomposing persistent organic pollutants (POPs) such as organochlorides and polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs).

fb09d2b3e4dd.title: Ectomycorrhiza
fb09d2b3e4dd.section: Resilience in challenging environments > Pollution and phytoremediation
fb09d2b3e4dd.sentence: • Radionuclides: Many species of ectomycorrhizal fungi, including the Cortinariaceae, can hyperaccumulate radionuclides

0a8288fd6937.title: Klebsiella oxytoca
0a8288fd6937.sentence: Klebsiella oxytoca is a Gram-negative, rod-shaped bacterium that is closely related to K. pneumoniae, from which it is distinguished through its production of indole.

f99ab098833b.title: Klebsiella oxytoca
f99ab098833b.sentence: It is a diazotroph, able to colonise plant hosts and fix atmospheric nitrogen into a form which the plant can use.

076e2a97f15b.title: Klebsiella oxytoca
076e2a97f15b.sentence: Association of K. oxytoca with the barley rhizosphere during an entire vegetative period has been demonstrated.

3bce60477c3b.title: Klebsiella oxytoca
3bce60477c3b.sentence: The bacteria adhere strongly to root hairs, and less strongly to the surface of the zone of elongation and root cap mucilage.

0b76caec5f04.title: Plant–soil feedback
0b76caec5f04.sentence: Plant–soil feedback is a process where plants alter the biotic and abiotic qualities of soil they grow in, which then alters the ability of plants to grow in that soil in the future.

97b64c6b7a5e.title: Plant–soil feedback
97b64c6b7a5e.sentence: Negative plant–soil feedback occurs when plants are less able to grow in soil that was previously occupied by a member of the same species, and positive plant–soil feedback occurs when plants are more able to grow in soil that was previously occupied by a member of the same species.

6a8825dc0066.title: Plant–soil feedback
6a8825dc0066.sentence: Although it was originally assumed that negative plant–soil feedback was caused by plants depleting the soil of nutrients, recent work has suggested that a major cause of plant–soil feedback is a buildup of soil-borne pathogens.

d901c3a639fd.title: Plant–soil feedback
d901c3a639fd.sentence: Mutualism and allelopathy are also thought to cause plant–soil feedback.

64b17604dc3e.title: Plant–soil feedback
64b17604dc3e.sentence: Studies have shown that, on average, plant–soil feedback tends to be negative; however, there have been many notable exceptions, such as many invasive species.

b115906c3473.title: Plant–soil feedback
b115906c3473.sentence: Negative plant–soil feedback is thought to be an important factor in helping plants to coexist.

7ef2f8d61a5e.title: Plant–soil feedback
7ef2f8d61a5e.sentence: If a plant is over-abundant, then soil pathogens and other negative factors will become common, hurting its growth.

52f68afef057.title: Plant–soil feedback
52f68afef057.sentence: Similarly, if a plant becomes overly rare, then so too will its soil pathogens and other negative factors, helping its growth.

a42a6c6d0451.title: Plant–soil feedback
a42a6c6d0451.sentence: Negative plant–soil feedback has been called a particular case of the Janzen–Connell hypothesis.

1501ae5b8898.title: Plant–soil feedback
1501ae5b8898.sentence: Plant–soil feedback is best measured using Bever's interaction coefficient, Is.

25d085ead255.title: Plant–soil feedback
25d085ead255.sentence: To measure this quantity, one must measure the growth of two plants, both in soil conditioned by members of their own species (Gx(home) for species x), and in soil conditioned by members of the other species (Gx(away) for plant species x).

32b6de8e0d0b.title: Plant–soil feedback
32b6de8e0d0b.sentence: If Is is negative, it means that both species grow worse in their own site compared to their competitor's soil, and therefore plant–soil feedback helps these species to coexist.

b5df2dc18410.title: Ectomycorrhizal extramatrical mycelium
b5df2dc18410.sentence: Ectomycorrhizal extramatrical mycelium (also known as extraradical mycelium) is the collection of filamentous fungal hyphae emanating from ectomycorrhizas.

00072795fc1b.title: Ectomycorrhizal extramatrical mycelium
00072795fc1b.sentence: It may be composed of fine, hydrophilic hypha which branches frequently to explore and exploit the soil matrix or may aggregate to form rhizomorphs; highly differentiated, hydrophobic, enduring, transport structures.

ada519531249.title: Ectomycorrhizal extramatrical mycelium
ada519531249.sentence: Additionally, the presence of rhizomorphs or mycelial cords, can act comparably to xylem tissue in plants, where hollow tubes of vessel hyphae shuttle water and solubilized nutrients over long distances.

8333a381f1e0.title: Ectomycorrhizal extramatrical mycelium
8333a381f1e0.sentence: Apart from mycorrhizas, extramatrical mycelium is the primary vegetative body of ectomycorrhizal fungi.

f9fd46ca5471.title: Ectomycorrhizal extramatrical mycelium
f9fd46ca5471.sentence: It is the location of mineral acquisition, enzyme production, and a key means of colonizing new root tips.

18ef8058f378.title: Ectomycorrhizal extramatrical mycelium
18ef8058f378.sentence: Extramatrical mycelium facilitates the movement of carbon into the rhizosphere, moves carbon and nutrients between hosts and is an important food source for invertebrates.

62ec4de313db.title: Ectomycorrhizal extramatrical mycelium
62ec4de313db.sentence: Because ectomycorrhizas are small and possess a limited contact area with the surrounding soil, the presence of extramatrical hyphae significantly increases the surface area in contact with the surrounding environment.

9788e9d00ff0.title: Ectomycorrhizal extramatrical mycelium
9788e9d00ff0.sentence: Increased hyphal occupation of the soil allows the fungus to take greater advantage of water and nutrients otherwise inaccessible to plant roots and to more efficiently transport these resources back to the plant.

ed9fc84d048c.title: Ectomycorrhizal extramatrical mycelium
ed9fc84d048c.sentence: Laboratory studies predict that around 23% of plant-derived carbon is allocated to extrametrical mycelium, although an estimated 15-30% of this is lost to fungal respiration.

0a6ed6e50932.title: Ectomycorrhizal extramatrical mycelium
0a6ed6e50932.sentence: Much of the carbon allocated to extramatrical mycelium accumulates as fungal biomass, making up an estimated one-third of the total microbial biomass and one-half of the total dissolved organic carbon in some forest soils.

a46fc074ba33.title: Ectomycorrhizal extramatrical mycelium
a46fc074ba33.sentence: Extramatrical hyphae excrete a range of compounds into the soil matrix, accounting for as much as 40% of total carbon usage.

a53eaee82638.title: Ectomycorrhizal extramatrical mycelium
a53eaee82638.sentence: Extramatrical mycelium is the site of collection for phosphorus within the soil system.

04532d457d11.title: Ectomycorrhizal extramatrical mycelium
04532d457d11.sentence: This relationship is so strong that starving host plants of phosphorus is known to increase the growth of extramatrical mycelium tenfold.

3fe087f09362.title: Ectomycorrhizal extramatrical mycelium
3fe087f09362.sentence: Field studies have shown that extramatrical mycelium is more likely to proliferate in mineral soils than in organic material, and may be particularly absent in fresh leaf litter.

8a4dc475f3e0.title: Ectomycorrhizal extramatrical mycelium
8a4dc475f3e0.sentence: Determining the longevity of extramatrical mycelium is difficult, and estimates range from just a few months to several years.

dd6cb8d4c5bb.title: Ectomycorrhizal extramatrical mycelium
dd6cb8d4c5bb.sentence: Turnover rates are assessed in a variety of ways including direct observation and 14C dating.

5187339ec5cd.title: Ectomycorrhizal extramatrical mycelium
5187339ec5cd.sentence: In order to differentiate ectomycorrhizal mycelium from the mycelium of saprotrophic fungi, biomass estimates are often done by ergosterol or phospholipid fatty acid analysis, or by using sand-filled bags, which are likely to be avoided by saprotrophic fungi because they lack organic matter.

b85d8c99edd6.title: Nod factor
b85d8c99edd6.sentence: Nod factors (nodulation factors or NF), are signaling molecules produced by soil bacteria known as rhizobia in response to flavonoid exudation from plants under nitrogen limited conditions.

e040e6ba9e7b.title: Nod factor
e040e6ba9e7b.sentence: Nod factors initiate the establishment of a symbiotic relationship between legumes and rhizobia by inducing nodulation.

7305a545ff4b.title: Nod factor
7305a545ff4b.sentence: Nod factors structurally are lipochitooligosaccharides (LCOs) that consist of an N-acetyl-D-glucosamine chain linked through β-1,4 linkage with a fatty acid of variable identity attached to a non reducing nitrogen in the backbone with various functional group substitutions at the terminal or non-terminal residues.

fd02c1f36f3b.title: Nod factor
fd02c1f36f3b.sentence: - Presence or absence of strain-specific substitutions along the chain

00dc78f7a422.title: Nod factor
00dc78f7a422.sentence: Nod gene expression is induced by the presence of certain flavonoids in the soil, which are secreted by the plant and act as an attractant to bacteria and induce Nod factor production.

8adbfec88e3e.title: Nod factor
8adbfec88e3e.sentence: Flavonoids activate NodD, a LysR family transcription factor, which binds to the nod box and initiates the transcription of the nod genes which encode the proteins necessary for the production of a wide range of LCOs.

53ba8e2f75c7.title: Nod factor
53ba8e2f75c7.sentence: The two LysM (lysin motif) receptor kinases (NFR1 and NFR5) that appear to make up the Nod factor receptor were first isolated in the model legume Lotus japonicus in 2003.

0bbf6d8545f5.title: Nod factor
0bbf6d8545f5.sentence: Binding of Nod factors to these receptors depolarizes the plasma membrane of root hairs via an influx of Ca+2 which induce the expression of early nodulin (ENOD) genes and swelling of the root hairs.

84d003893a29.title: Nod factor
84d003893a29.sentence: Nod factor cause the fragmentation and rearrangement of actin network, which coupled with the reinstitution of cell growth lead to the curling of the root hair around the bacteria.

4ca16d45b172.title: Nod factor
4ca16d45b172.sentence: This is followed by the localized breakdown of the cell wall and the invagination of the plant cell membrane, allowing the bacterium to form an infection thread.

21eb9b25b165.title: Nod factor
21eb9b25b165.sentence: As the infection thread grows the rhizobia travel down its length towards the site of the nodule.

d3c5c416b96a.title: Nod factor
d3c5c416b96a.sentence: During this process the pericycle cells in plants become activated and cells in the inner cortex start growing and become the nodule primordium where the rhizobia infect and differentiate into bacteroids and fix nitrogen.

51c0172b996b.title: Root cap
51c0172b996b.sentence: The root cap (also called the calyptra) is a small but multitasking organ that covers the very tip of every growing plant root.

12e791af5927.title: Root cap
12e791af5927.sentence: It shields the delicate apical meristem from mechanical damage, lubricates the root's passage through soil, and houses specialised gravity-sensing cells that guide the root's overall direction of growth.

81c5f251788c.title: Root cap
81c5f251788c.sentence: Root caps contain statocytes (gravity-sensing cells) whose dense statoliths settle in response to gravity; if the cap is carefully removed a root loses its orientation and grows at random.

00ffcbe5c6ea.title: Root cap
00ffcbe5c6ea.sentence: Because of its sensor cells, the organ underpins gravitropism (sometimes called geoperception), helping the root grow downwards with gravity or reorient upwards against it.

0926ea79718e.title: Root cap
0926ea79718e.sentence: The cap also secretes a layer of mucilage that reduces friction and may foster signalling with the surrounding soil microbiota.

ff8b4cd91e0a.title: Root cap
ff8b4cd91e0a.sentence: The root cap is renewed continuously.

1d0918dd6413.title: Root cap
1d0918dd6413.sentence: Stem-cell files on its inner face divide to generate successive layers of columella and lateral root-cap cells; as the root advances, the oldest outer layers are sloughed off so the organ maintains a steady size.

19750e46bc26.title: Root cap
19750e46bc26.sentence: In cereals and many legumes these discarded layers separate as long-lived "border cells", whereas in Arabidopsis thaliana most surface cells undergo rapid, developmentally-programmed cell death before shedding.

f9b566ed5010.title: Laimosphere
f9b566ed5010.sentence: The laimosphere is the microbiologically enriched zone of soil that surrounds below-ground portions of plant stems; the laimosphere is analogous to the rhizosphere and spermosphere.

9d8cbabf6fa2.title: Laimosphere
9d8cbabf6fa2.sentence: The combining form laim- from laimos (Greek: λαιμός, "throat") denotes a connecting organ (neck) while -sphere indicates a zone of influence.

881a91f56175.title: Laimosphere
881a91f56175.sentence: Topographically, the laimosphere includes the soil around any portion of subterranean plant organs other than roots where exuded nutrients (especially sugars and amino acids) stimulate microbial activities.

4a9441bb1151.title: Laimosphere
4a9441bb1151.sentence: Subterranean plant organs with a laimosphere include hypocotyls, epicotyls, stems, stolons, corms, bulbs, and leaves.

6a366a24034c.title: Laimosphere
6a366a24034c.sentence: Pathogens commonly found to cause such diseases are species of Fusarium, Phoma, Phytophthora, Pythium, Rhizoctonia and Sclerotinia.

d9426e0a6fa1.title: Actinorhizal plant
d9426e0a6fa1.sentence: Actinorhizal plants are a group of angiosperms characterized by their ability to form a symbiosis with the nitrogen-fixing actinomycetota Frankia.

40da27065c97.title: Actinorhizal plant
40da27065c97.sentence: This association leads to the formation of nitrogen-fixing root nodules.

e8038ad7c45b.title: Actinorhizal plant
e8038ad7c45b.sentence: Actinorhizal plants are dicotyledons distributed within three orders, eight families and twenty-six genera, of the angiosperm clade.

f6fd5b7b3c98.title: Actinorhizal plant
f6fd5b7b3c98.sentence: The actinorhizal species are either trees or shrubs, except for those in the genus Datisca which are herbs.

c0673aac3d77.title: Actinorhizal plant
c0673aac3d77.sentence: Other species of actinorhizal plants are common in temperate regions like alder, bayberry, sweetfern, avens, mountain misery and coriaria.

597160a80a6c.title: Actinorhizal plant
597160a80a6c.sentence: Their ability to form nitrogen-fixing nodules confers a selective advantage in poor soils, and are therefore pioneer species where available nitrogen is scarce, such as moraines, volcanic flows or sand dunes.

a4071a602374.title: Actinorhizal plant
a4071a602374.sentence: Being among the first species to colonize these disturbed environments, actinorhizal shrubs and trees play a critical role, enriching the soil and enabling the establishment of other species in an ecological succession.

a2ea422f448a.title: Actinorhizal plant
a2ea422f448a.sentence: The nitrogen fixation rates measured for some alder species are as high as 300 kg of N2/ha/year, close to the highest rate reported in legumes.

93a6ccfd1f0b.title: Root nodule
93a6ccfd1f0b.sentence: According to a count in 1998, it includes about 200 species and accounts for roughly the same amount of nitrogen fixation as rhizobial symbioses.

3a7f638947c0.title: Actinorhizal plant
3a7f638947c0.sentence: Depending on the plant species, two mechanisms of infection have been described: The first is observed in casuarinas or alders and is called root hair infection.

281a0f462675.title: Actinorhizal plant
281a0f462675.sentence: In this case bacteria penetrate the root extracellularly, growing between epidermal cells then between cortical cells.

4f8a0868c1c6.title: Actinorhizal plant
4f8a0868c1c6.sentence: As in legumes, nodulation is favored by nitrogen deprivation and is inhibited by high nitrogen concentrations.

2b5fb7392073.title: Frankia
2b5fb7392073.sentence: Frankia is a genus of nitrogen-fixing bacteria that live in symbiosis with actinorhizal plants, similar to the Rhizobium bacteria found in the root nodules of legumes in the family Fabaceae.

68d4ae7c3a47.title: Frankia
68d4ae7c3a47.sentence: The bacteria are filamentous and convert atmospheric nitrogen into ammonia via the enzyme nitrogenase, a process known as nitrogen fixation.

6331178be747.title: Frankia
6331178be747.sentence: The bacteria can supply most or all of the nitrogen requirements of the host plant.

ac69dc717ef2.title: Frankia
ac69dc717ef2.sentence: As a result, actinorhizal plants colonise and often thrive in soils that are low in plant nutrients.

730398fe2902.title: Frankia
730398fe2902.sentence: Most Frankia strains are specific to different plant species.

8990f7ce9a3b.title: Frankia
8990f7ce9a3b.sentence: - All species in the genus Alnus in the family Betulaceae

96c5e591aea1.title: Frankia
96c5e591aea1.sentence: - Some species in all four genera in the family Casuarinaceae

c67d5fabd684.title: Frankia
c67d5fabd684.sentence: - All species in the three genera in the family Elaeagnaceae, Elaeagnus, Shepherdia, and Hippophae

86c3ed8f2473.title: Frankia
86c3ed8f2473.sentence: - All species in the genera Myrica, Morella, and Comptonia in the family Myricaceae.

82f239e57e13.title: Frankia
82f239e57e13.sentence: - All species in six genera in the family Rhamnaceae, Ceanothus, Colletia, Discaria, Trevoa, and possibly Adolphia

252cff20aa95.title: Frankia
252cff20aa95.sentence: Frankia forms nodules via two methods of root infection, intercellularly and intracellularly.

848c970fd9da.title: Frankia
848c970fd9da.sentence: Intracellular infection is characterized by initial root-hair deformation which is then infected by the filamentous Frankia.

5b942b3448ef.title: Frankia
5b942b3448ef.sentence: Instead, the filamentous Frankia invades the roots in the space between cells on the root.

c2e7d5dd9180.title: Frankia
c2e7d5dd9180.sentence: This then gives rise to a nodule primordium which feeds the bacteria via the vascular tissue of the plant allowing the nodule to mature.

1208eaea1e99.title: Frankia
1208eaea1e99.sentence: This genus was originally named by Jørgen Brunchorst, in 1886 to honor the German biologist Albert Bernhard Frank.

b8432f04bb59.title: Frankia
b8432f04bb59.sentence: Brunchorst considered the organism he had identified to be a filamentous fungus.

7bf1c548fad5.title: Frankia
7bf1c548fad5.sentence: Becking [de; nl] redefined the genus in 1970 as containing prokaryotic actinomycetes and created the family Frankiaceae within the Actinomycetales.

697abb024f06.title: Rhizobacteria
697abb024f06.sentence: Plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR) were first defined by Kloepper and Schroth to be soil bacteria that colonize the roots of plants following inoculation onto seed and that enhance plant growth.

1668ed877510.title: Rhizobacteria
1668ed877510.sentence: The term PGPRs was first used by Joseph W. Kloepper in the late 1970s and has become commonly used in scientific literature.

127a72709e45.title: Rhizobacteria
127a72709e45.section: Plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria > Mechanisms of action
127a72709e45.sentence: PGPRs have been reported to directly enhance plant growth by a variety of mechanisms:

f5d50bb582a4.title: Rhizobacteria
f5d50bb582a4.section: Plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria > Mechanisms of action
f5d50bb582a4.sentence: - fixation of atmospheric nitrogen transferred to the plant,

07187a642abd.title: Rhizobacteria
07187a642abd.section: Plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria > Mechanisms of action
07187a642abd.sentence: - solubilization of minerals such as phosphorus, and synthesis of phytohormones.

f7d7169e4238.title: Rhizobacteria
f7d7169e4238.section: Plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria > Mechanisms of action
f7d7169e4238.sentence: Direct mechanisms of plant growth promotion by PGPRs can be demonstrated in the absence of plant pathogens or other rhizosphere microorganisms, while indirect mechanisms involve the ability of PGPRs to reduce the harmful effects of plant pathogens on crop yield.

0873ad3a077b.title: Rhizobacteria
0873ad3a077b.sentence: Disease is suppressed through induced systemic resistance and through the production of antifungal metabolites.

c044ef97e8ed.title: Rhizobacteria
c044ef97e8ed.sentence: The following are implicit in the colonization process: ability to survive inoculation onto seed, to multiply in the spermosphere (region surrounding the seed) in response to seed exudates, to attach to the root surface, and to colonize the developing root system.

132d42cc6f27.title: Rhizobacteria
132d42cc6f27.sentence: The ineffectiveness of PGPR in the field has often been attributed to their inability to colonize plant roots.

4aa0eebdc400.title: Rhizobacteria
4aa0eebdc400.sentence: In agriculture, inoculant bacteria are often applied to the seed coat of seeds prior to being sown.

25b35b9632e4.title: Rhizobacteria
25b35b9632e4.sentence: Inoculated seeds are more likely to establish large enough rhizobacterial populations within the rhizosphere to produce notable beneficial effects on the crop.

75992a4cbab5.title: Rhizobacteria
75992a4cbab5.sentence: This approach has also been combined with an rRNA-targeting probe to monitor the metabolic activity of a rhizobacterial strain in the rhizosphere and showed that bacteria located at the root tip were most active.

1ab415c8e467.title: Root microbiome
1ab415c8e467.sentence: They are mostly rhizobacteria that belong to Pseudomonadota and Bacillota, with many examples from Pseudomonas and Bacillus genera.

43db6d91443a.title: Rhizobacteria
43db6d91443a.sentence: PGPR bacteria include Pseudomonas putida, Azospirillum fluorescens, and Azospirillum lipoferum and notable nitrogen-fixing bacteria associated with legumes includes Allorhizobium, Azorhizobium, Bradyrhizobium, and Rhizobium.

6ab2fad73786.title: Rhizobacteria
6ab2fad73786.section: Plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria > Mechanisms of action
6ab2fad73786.sentence: Development of PGPRs into biofertilisers and biopesticides could be a novel way of increasing crop yield and decreasing disease incidence, whilst decreasing dependency on chemical pesticides and fertilisers which can often have harmful effects on the local ecology and environment.

3afeed441190.title: Disease suppressive soils
3afeed441190.sentence: Disease suppressive soils function to prevent the establishment of pathogens in the rhizosphere of plants.

6f7da2703411.title: Disease suppressive soils
6f7da2703411.sentence: These soils develop through the establishment of beneficial microbes, known as plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR) in the rhizosphere of plant roots.

39b48ef8ccc8.title: Disease suppressive soils
39b48ef8ccc8.sentence: As beneficial bacteria occupy space around plant roots they outcompete harmful pathogens by releasing pathogenic suppressive metabolites.

b920ed677c86.title: Disease suppressive soils
b920ed677c86.sentence: When these fungi reach the rhizosphere they release enzymes that degrade the cell wall of plant root cells.

272f287d6fe6.title: Disease suppressive soils
272f287d6fe6.sentence: Beneficial Pseudomonas and Bacillus produce fungal suppressing metabolites that break up this migrating fungal hyphae.

c57023c78b71.title: Disease suppressive soils
c57023c78b71.sentence: Plants respond to pathogens by recruiting PGPR to their root rhizosphere from the bulk soil to fill in and prevent pathogen establishment.

c2a7233a95c6.title: Disease suppressive soils
c2a7233a95c6.sentence: PGPR are recruited through the natural release plant exudates from root cells as they push through the soil.

007908d1459a.title: Disease suppressive soils
007908d1459a.sentence: If a beneficial microbe genera is not present in a soil plants are not able to recruit it as a defense.

2cfc0141a1dd.title: Disease suppressive soils
2cfc0141a1dd.sentence: Therefore, suppressive soils are a function of the microbes already present in a soil and able to be recruited.

b95b3627cfe5.title: Disease suppressive soils
b95b3627cfe5.sentence: A greater diversity of plants in a soil leads to a greater diversity of microbes in the rhizosphere and furthermore can lead to greater suppression of soil diseases.

ad9c60305e10.title: Disease suppressive soils
ad9c60305e10.sentence: Management, such as informed crop rotation and soil solarization, can create suppressive soils that naturally suppress pathogens.

4ebd6a20255f.title: Soil solarization
4ebd6a20255f.sentence: It may also be described as a method of decontaminating soil or creating disease suppressive soils by the use of sunlight.

be664dae7fb2.title: Disease suppressive soils
be664dae7fb2.sentence: In particular, these soils can enhance plant resistance to leaf-feeding insects by promoting beneficial rhizosphere bacteria and priming plant defense mechanisms.

22015887bad1.title: Mycorrhizosphere
22015887bad1.sentence: The mycorrhizosphere includes "roots, hyphae of the directly connected mycorrhizal fungi, associated microorganisms and the soil within their direct influence".

3e532fb0f08d.title: Mycorrhizosphere
3e532fb0f08d.sentence: It is the region in which nutrients are released from the roots and the fungus increases the microbial population and its activities.

e8dda9d2fcd2.title: Mycorrhizosphere
e8dda9d2fcd2.sentence: Fungal hyphae are thinner than plant roots, which allows them to penetrate areas in the soil with moisture and nutrients that are inaccessible to roots.

851d04a415e5.title: Mycorrhizosphere
851d04a415e5.sentence: In some cases, mycorrhizal fungi in the mycorrhizosphere may ward off fungal plant pathogens.

32f76441b0b9.title: Mycorrhizosphere
32f76441b0b9.sentence: For example, the arbuscular mycorrhizal fungus Glomus intraradices reduces germination of the pathogen Fusarium oxysporum, but stimulates germination of a non-pathogenic fungus Trichoderma harzianum.

497f058dd83d.title: Mycorrhizosphere
497f058dd83d.sentence: Soil bacteria in the mycorrhizosphere influence plant growth in several ways: affecting the uptake of nutrients, providing protection against pathogens, contributing to nitrogen fixation, and contributing to mineral weathering.

476e6733fd26.title: Mycorrhizosphere
476e6733fd26.sentence: The type of mycorrhizae greatly influences the protozoal population in a mycorrhizosphere.

f6f751b9b8ba.title: Mycorrhizosphere
f6f751b9b8ba.sentence: For example, a Paxillus involutus–conifer mycorrhiza seems to reduce the density of protozoa in the resulting mycorrhizosphere, but mycorrhizae formed with Lactarius rufus and Suillus bovinus have the opposite effect.

1fb16025833b.title: Mycorrhizosphere
1fb16025833b.sentence: Other soil organisms that influence the mycorrhizosphere community include soil animals such as nematodes, mites, and earthworms, which forage on roots, hyphae and their associated microorganisms.

44770af238ba.title: Mycorrhiza helper bacteria
44770af238ba.sentence: Mycorrhiza helper bacteria (MHB) are a group of organisms that form symbiotic associations with both ectomycorrhiza and arbuscular mycorrhiza.

658624e13b13.title: Mycorrhiza helper bacteria
658624e13b13.sentence: These bacteria are naturally present in the soil, and form these complex interactions with fungi as plant root development starts to take shape.

b22d5b22eb8e.title: Mycorrhiza helper bacteria
b22d5b22eb8e.sentence: MHBs are diverse and belong to a wide variety of bacterial phyla including both Gram-negative and Gram-positive bacteria.

b86945aae74e.title: Mycorrhiza helper bacteria
b86945aae74e.sentence: Some of the most common MHBs observed in studies belong to the genera Pseudomonas and Streptomyces.

9e218f985948.title: Mycorrhiza helper bacteria
9e218f985948.sentence: There are a few genera that act as MHBs, but one of the most common is Bacillius.

5cf83cd33410.title: Mycorrhiza helper bacteria
5cf83cd33410.sentence: MHBs enhance mycorrhizal function, growth, nutrient uptake to the fungus and plant, improve soil conductance, aid against certain pathogens, and help promote defense mechanisms.

ae40425ceeeb.title: Mycorrhiza helper bacteria
ae40425ceeeb.sentence: MHBs can obtain both inorganic and organic nutrients in the soil through a direct process known as mineral-weathering which aids in the recycling of nutrients throughout the environment.

aa1ff9e2e8f9.title: Mycorrhiza helper bacteria
aa1ff9e2e8f9.sentence: The process of mineral-weathering releases protons and iron into the soil.

68eaee4d13dd.title: Mycorrhiza helper bacteria
68eaee4d13dd.sentence: This results in a lowering of the pH.

e7d968db87bb.title: Mycorrhiza helper bacteria
e7d968db87bb.sentence: Phosphate solubilizing rhizobacteria are the most common MHB that aids in phosphorus uptake.

1a0e7df9af08.title: Mycorrhiza helper bacteria
1a0e7df9af08.sentence: As a result, the MHB create a pool of phosphate that the mycorrhiza then use.

b3d0f05c613a.title: Mycorrhiza helper bacteria
b3d0f05c613a.sentence: The bacteria work in phosphorus-limited conditions to help the mycorrhiza establish and grow.

8281c49fe9af.title: Mycorrhiza helper bacteria
8281c49fe9af.sentence: The MHBs are able to fix nitrogen in the soil, and create pools of available nitrogen.

090740793ff4.title: Mycorrhiza helper bacteria
090740793ff4.sentence: However, MHBs do not cause plant modifications as legumes do, to help with nitrogen-fixation.

7036099e94f3.title: Mycorrhiza helper bacteria
7036099e94f3.sentence: Nitrogen-fixation is done only in the surrounding soil in relation to the mycorrhiza.

79f8318d6d68.title: Mycorrhiza helper bacteria
79f8318d6d68.sentence: MHBs help mycorrhiza establish symbiotic associations in stressful environments such as those high in toxic metals.

0be9d904c69d.title: Mycorrhiza helper bacteria
0be9d904c69d.sentence: MHBs help to prevent the uptake of toxic metals including lead, zinc, and cadmium.

480303075f5c.title: Mycorrhiza helper bacteria
480303075f5c.sentence: This relationship makes them great candidates for bioremediation.

61f0d7bc9e86.title: Mycorrhiza helper bacteria
61f0d7bc9e86.sentence: In the presence of a pathogenic fungus, most studies show that MHBs aid in fighting off pathogens.

56ab1a4c80b5.title: Mycorrhiza helper bacteria
56ab1a4c80b5.section: With pathogenic fungi > Defending against pathogenic fungi
56ab1a4c80b5.sentence: In one experiment researchers observed that MHBs produced acid in the surrounding environment, which helped to fight off various pathogens.

47536086ac58.title: Mycorrhiza helper bacteria
47536086ac58.section: With pathogenic fungi > Defending against pathogenic fungi
47536086ac58.sentence: Another study found that MHBs release antifungal metabolites into the soil.

ab1ddcd82f46.title: Mycorrhiza helper bacteria
ab1ddcd82f46.sentence: However, there have been a few cases where MHBs help to promote pathogenic effects of a fungus.

f64ee85441d7.title: Mycorrhiza helper bacteria
