f64ee85441d7.sentence: The mechanisms through which these interactions take shape are not well-understood and needs further study.

f3217ee98ec6.title: Common symbiosis signaling pathway
f3217ee98ec6.sentence: Strigolactones are carotenoid-derived signalling molecules that have a conserved tricyclic lactone structure also known as ABC rings.

5060a324166e.title: Common symbiosis signaling pathway
5060a324166e.sentence: In arbuscular mycorrhizal symbiosis, host plants synthesize and secrete strigolactones into the rhizosphere, which stimulate hyphal branching and directional growth of fungi towards the root.

4863ef6e9cd1.title: Mycorrhiza
4863ef6e9cd1.sentence: In arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi, the presence of strigolactones, a plant hormone, secreted from roots induces fungal spores in the soil to germinate, stimulates their metabolism, growth and branching, and prompts the fungi to release chemical signals the plant can detect.

a4fb58d98420.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
a4fb58d98420.sentence: Low-phosphorus concentrations in the soil increase hyphal growth and branching as well as induce plant exudation of compounds that control hyphal branching intensity.

9c6aa4de6118.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
9c6aa4de6118.sentence: Hyphae of fungi grown in the exudates from roots starved of phosphorus grew more and produced tertiary branches compared to those grown in exudates from plants given adequate phosphorus.

ea39dc853092.title: Strigolactone
ea39dc853092.section: Discovery and functions > Germination of parasitic plant
ea39dc853092.sentence: Strigolactones were first isolated in 1966 from cotton plants, specifically from the roots.

70dc0d721806.title: Strigolactone
70dc0d721806.section: Discovery and functions > Germination of parasitic plant
70dc0d721806.sentence: The isolation of strigolactones lead to a series of tests that proved that this compound was the necessary molecule to induce germination of Striga species.

45be253b1a4e.title: Strigolactone
45be253b1a4e.section: Discovery and functions > Germination of parasitic plant
45be253b1a4e.sentence: To induce germination of parasitic plants, strigolactones only needed to be present in trace amounts, in the order of 5 parts per million.

073a9c89ac97.title: Strigolactone
073a9c89ac97.sentence: Due to their mechanism of action, these molecules have been classified as plant hormones or phytohormones.

0c05060f1d9c.title: Strigolactone
0c05060f1d9c.sentence: Third, strigolactones have been identified as branching inhibition hormones in plants; when present, these compounds prevent excess bud growing in stem terminals, stopping the branching mechanism in plants.

bb56b82997c7.title: Strigolactone
bb56b82997c7.sentence: Since strigolactones are involved in the signaling pathway required for germination of parasitic species (such as Striga sp.), they have been a proposed target to control pests and overgrowth of these parasitic organism.

207af78d83b8.title: Strigolactone
207af78d83b8.sentence: Using a molecule similar to strigolactones could be the key to designing a chemical and biological mechanism to stop the colonization of a plant's root by parasitic plants.

215db277e903.title: Strigolactone
215db277e903.sentence: This discovery has implications for breeding Striga resistance in maize by modifying the strigolactone blend, potentially reducing the devastating effects of this parasitic weed in Africa.

1f85188a43ed.title: Fine root
1f85188a43ed.sentence: A fine root is most commonly defined as a plant root that is two millimeters or less in diameter.

a9d0c6069fe8.title: Fine root
a9d0c6069fe8.sentence: Fine roots may function in acquisition of soil resources (eg. nutrients, water) and/or resource transport, making them functionally most analogous to the leaves and twigs in a plant's shoot system.

75cb73a065ab.title: Fine root
75cb73a065ab.sentence: Fine roots collectively comprise the majority of total length of a root system in many perennial and annual plants.

91089f1851fd.title: Fine root
91089f1851fd.sentence: Fine roots have been shown to respond to soil nutrient patches.

60d659326c87.title: Fine root
60d659326c87.sentence: Responses include the lengthening of root segments and increased total length of fine roots, increased initiation of lateral roots, and increased branching.

42586a018b61.title: Fine root
42586a018b61.sentence: In multiple ecosystem types and forest stand ages, fine-root biomass has been found to decrease with increasing soil depth.

d81d3fc221c9.title: Fine root
d81d3fc221c9.sentence: Similarly, fine-root nitrogen concentration has been shown to be lower in deeper soil.

95527282b7dd.title: Fine root
95527282b7dd.sentence: In forest carbon and nutrient cycles, the formation, death, and decomposition of fine roots can account for 20-80% of total net primary production.

43d6b676c655.title: Fine root
43d6b676c655.sentence: Fine roots also release exudates, including labile carbon, during life processes and turnover.

477cf4eb1f8e.title: Fine root
477cf4eb1f8e.sentence: This directly affects soil organic carbon pools, and indirectly affects them by stimulating microbial activity.

597ca9a1c278.title: Fine root
597ca9a1c278.sentence: Plant roots support soil, which stabilizes sloped landscapes and limits soil erosion.

b30fbd3f5da9.title: Fine root
b30fbd3f5da9.sentence: Soil stability depends on root tensile strength.

7b8afcab3579.title: Fine root
7b8afcab3579.sentence: Root tensile strength increases with decreasing root diameter, so fine roots are stronger than coarse roots.

0adc46b41cd9.title: Fine root
0adc46b41cd9.sentence: In trees, fine roots are generally exclusively or dominantly colonized by a single mycorrhizal type, either arbuscular mycorrhizae or ectomycorrhizae.

1715ecf5b941.title: Nitrogen nutrition in the arbuscular mycorrhizal system
1715ecf5b941.sentence: The IRM is the site of nutrient exchange between the symbionts, while the ERM effectively serves as an extension of the plant's root system by increasing the surface area available for nutrient acquisition, including nitrogen, which can be taken up in the form of ammonium, nitrate or from organic sources.
1715ecf5b941.key: Nitrogen nutrition in the arbuscular mycorrhizal system

9e81e8223511.title: Nitrogen nutrition in the arbuscular mycorrhizal system
9e81e8223511.sentence: A large body of research has shown that AM fungi can, and do, transfer nitrogen to plants and transfer nitrogen between plants, including crop plants.
9e81e8223511.key: Nitrogen nutrition in the arbuscular mycorrhizal system

eecab2159ad8.title: Nitrogen nutrition in the arbuscular mycorrhizal system
eecab2159ad8.sentence: The intra-radical mycelia (IRM) are found within the root itself while the extra-radical mycelium (ERM) are tiny hyphal threads which reach far out into the soil.
eecab2159ad8.key: Nitrogen nutrition in the arbuscular mycorrhizal system

12c1951a4b98.title: Nitrogen nutrition in the arbuscular mycorrhizal system
12c1951a4b98.sentence: Working with an in vitro system, studies have shown that as much as 29% to 50% of the root nitrogen was taken up via the fungus.
12c1951a4b98.key: Nitrogen nutrition in the arbuscular mycorrhizal system

50a364b4ae50.title: Nitrogen nutrition in the arbuscular mycorrhizal system
50a364b4ae50.section: Role of nitrogen > Mechanism of action
50a364b4ae50.sentence: The current model, first put forth in 2005, proposes that the nitrogen taken up by the fungus is converted in the ERM to arginine, which is then transported to the IRM, where it is released as ammonium into the apoplast for the plant to use.
50a364b4ae50.key: Nitrogen nutrition in the arbuscular mycorrhizal system

8389172ddfdd.title: Nitrogen nutrition in the arbuscular mycorrhizal system
8389172ddfdd.section: Role of nitrogen > Community and ecology
8389172ddfdd.sentence: It has been demonstrated that nitrogen is transferred between plants via the hyphal network, sometimes in large amounts.
8389172ddfdd.key: Nitrogen nutrition in the arbuscular mycorrhizal system

b66d6db62c8f.title: Nitrogen nutrition in the arbuscular mycorrhizal system
b66d6db62c8f.section: Role of nitrogen > Community and ecology
b66d6db62c8f.sentence: For example, Cheng and Baumgartner found that about 25% of the labeled nitrogen supplied to a source plant, in this case a grass species, was transferred to the sink plant, grapevine.
b66d6db62c8f.key: Nitrogen nutrition in the arbuscular mycorrhizal system

833190ff366c.title: Nitrogen nutrition in the arbuscular mycorrhizal system
833190ff366c.sentence: In one field study, there was negligible transfer between soybeans and corn.
833190ff366c.key: Nitrogen nutrition in the arbuscular mycorrhizal system

bb16cc4d2ca1.title: Nitrogen nutrition in the arbuscular mycorrhizal system
bb16cc4d2ca1.sentence: However, it has not been shown conclusively that there is a growth benefit from AM due to nitrogen.
bb16cc4d2ca1.key: Nitrogen nutrition in the arbuscular mycorrhizal system

67c7363e2baf.title: Nitrogen nutrition in the arbuscular mycorrhizal system
67c7363e2baf.sentence: Some researchers doubt that AM contribute significantly to plant N status in nature.
67c7363e2baf.key: Nitrogen nutrition in the arbuscular mycorrhizal system

c2c2288732b3.title: Nitrogen nutrition in the arbuscular mycorrhizal system
c2c2288732b3.sentence: Furthermore, AM sometimes appears to be parasitic.
c2c2288732b3.key: Nitrogen nutrition in the arbuscular mycorrhizal system

715b194338d4.title: Nitrogen nutrition in the arbuscular mycorrhizal system
715b194338d4.sentence: This has primarily been seen under conditions of high nitrogen, which is not the usual state in a natural environment.
715b194338d4.key: Nitrogen nutrition in the arbuscular mycorrhizal system

489a306d8df0.title: Root microbiome
489a306d8df0.sentence: While some microbes may be purely mutualistic or parasitic, many may behave differently depending on the host species with which it is associated, environmental conditions, and host health.

98b4192f7026.title: Root microbiome
98b4192f7026.sentence: Parasites consume carbon from the plant without providing any benefit or providing insufficient benefit relative to their carbon consumption, thereby compromising host fitness.

b17476a8dd58.title: Root microbiome
b17476a8dd58.sentence: A host's immune response controls symbiont infection and growth rates.

aefd9e77c7e3.title: Root microbiome
aefd9e77c7e3.sentence: If a host's immune response is not able to control a particular microbial species, or if host immunity is compromised, the microbe-plant relationship will likely reside somewhere nearer the parasitic side of the mutualist-parasite continuum.

49cf30f21e60.title: Root microbiome
49cf30f21e60.sentence: Similarly, high nutrients can push some microbes into parasitic behavior, encouraging unchecked growth at a time when symbionts are no longer needed to aid with nutrient acquisition.

e9f1a131bbe0.title: Root microbiome
e9f1a131bbe0.sentence: Symbionts may be biotrophic (subsisting off of living tissue) or necrotrophic (subsisting off of dead tissue).

da7d22ce94fd.title: Root microbiome
da7d22ce94fd.sentence: There is an ongoing debate regarding what mechanisms are responsible for assembling individual microbes into communities.

9f96bd4cda67.title: Root microbiome
9f96bd4cda67.sentence: There are two primary competing hypotheses.

5d3f3fd1666d.title: Root microbiome
5d3f3fd1666d.sentence: One is that "everything is everywhere, but the environment selects," meaning biotic and abiotic factors pose the only constraints, through natural selection, to which microbes colonize what environments.

1b3f752573ef.title: Root microbiome
1b3f752573ef.sentence: Its counterpart is the hypothesis that neutral processes, such as distance and geographic barriers to dispersal, control microbial community assembly when taxa are equally fit within an environment.

cc2e80244b2f.title: Root microbiome
cc2e80244b2f.sentence: Most likely, both natural selection and neutral processes affect microbial community assembly, though certain microbial taxa may be more restricted by one process or the other depending on their physiological restrictions and mode of dispersion.

b76ccaebeedf.title: Root microbiome
b76ccaebeedf.sentence: For example, fine roots, root tips, and the main root are all associated with different communities, and the rhizosphere, root surface, and root tissue are all associated with different communities, likely due to the unique chemistry and nutrient status of each of these regions, which differ from those of the bulk soil.

c71c71eb1847.title: Root microbiome
c71c71eb1847.sentence: For instance, root exudates provide specific carbon compounds that are enriched in the rhizosphere, selecting for microbial taxa with matching metabolic traits and shaping root-associated communities accordingly.

8ee923270ff0.title: Root microbiome
8ee923270ff0.sentence: Abiotic mechanisms also affect root microbial community assembly because individual taxa have different optima along various environmental gradients, such as nutrient concentrations, pH, moisture, temperature, etc. In addition to chemical and climatic factors, soil structure and disturbance impact root biotic assembly.

c02e504e5c81.title: Lateral root
c02e504e5c81.sentence: Lateral roots, emerging from the pericycle (meristematic tissue), extend horizontally from the primary root (radicle) and over time make up the iconic branching pattern of root systems.

5ecf12aaf78b.title: Lateral root
5ecf12aaf78b.sentence: They contribute to anchoring the plant securely into the soil, increasing water uptake, and facilitate the extraction of nutrients required for the growth and development of the plant.

0be5dc22b305.title: Lateral root
0be5dc22b305.sentence: Lateral roots increase the surface area of a plant's root system and can be found in great abundance in several plant species.

9cb87a18e939.title: Lateral root
9cb87a18e939.sentence: In some cases, lateral roots have been found to form symbiotic relationships with rhizobia (bacteria) and mycorrhizae (fungi) found in the soil, to further increase surface area and increase nutrient uptake.

5aa16a6290aa.title: Lateral root
5aa16a6290aa.sentence: The number of lateral roots corresponds to the number of xylem bundles, and two lateral roots will never be found directly across from one another on the primary root.

112053aee15e.title: Lateral root
112053aee15e.sentence: The results from these mutants indicate that IAA is required for lateral roots in various stages of development.

5bd9aa194f21.title: Cluster root
5bd9aa194f21.sentence: Cluster roots, also known as proteoid roots, are plant roots that form clusters of closely spaced short lateral rootlets.

c9a479393a51.title: Cluster root
c9a479393a51.sentence: They may form a two- to five-centimetre-thick mat just beneath the leaf litter.

763e7f4d2c73.title: Cluster root
763e7f4d2c73.sentence: They enhance nutrient uptake, possibly by chemically modifying the soil environment to improve nutrient solubilisation.

8e51653f6b6a.title: Cluster root
8e51653f6b6a.sentence: They were first described by Adolf Engler in 1894, after he discovered them on plants of the family Proteaceae growing in Leipzig Botanic Gardens.

015124f7ca20.title: Cluster root
015124f7ca20.sentence: Proteoid roots are now known to occur in 27 different Proteaceae genera, plus around 30 species from other families, including Betulaceae, Casuarinaceae, Eleagnaceae, Leguminosae, Moraceae and Myricaceae.

66821f33804d.title: Cluster root
66821f33804d.sentence: Cultivated crops with proteoid roots include Lupinus and Macadamia.

779c521cf63d.title: Cluster root
779c521cf63d.sentence: In cultivation, only slow-release low-phosphorus fertilizers should be used, as higher levels cause phosphorus toxicity and sometimes iron deficiency, leading to plant death.

d249a9523086.title: Cluster root
d249a9523086.sentence: In 1960, Helen Purnell examined 44 species from ten Proteaceae genera, finding proteoid roots in every genus except Persoonia; she then coined the name "proteoid roots" in reference to the plant family in which it was known to occur.

ca8f5efbbd17.title: Rhizobacteria
ca8f5efbbd17.sentence: Studies conducted on sugar beet crops found that some root-colonizing bacteria were deleterious rhizobacteria (DRB).

cf7cf80115ee.title: Rhizobacteria
cf7cf80115ee.sentence: Sugar beet seeds inoculated with DRB had reduced germination rates, root lesions, reduced root elongation, root distortions, increased fungi infection, and decreased plant growth.

ca8bbda734c6.title: Rhizobacteria
ca8bbda734c6.sentence: In one trial the sugar beet yield was reduced by 48%.

7f4b60546cc1.title: Rhizobacteria
7f4b60546cc1.sentence: Six strains of rhizobacteria have been identified as being DRB.

2a26a600cd04.title: Rhizobacteria
2a26a600cd04.sentence: The strains are in the genera Enterobacter, Klebsiella, Citrobacter, Flavobacterium, Achromobacter, and Arthrobacter.

b247877e6b7f.title: Rhizobacteria
b247877e6b7f.sentence: The presence of PGPRs has proven to reduce and inhibit the colonization of DRB on sugar beet roots.

24275ae4e308.title: Rhizobacteria
24275ae4e308.sentence: Plots inoculated with PGPRs and DRBs had an increase in production of 39% while plots only treated with DRBs had a reduction in production of 30%.

614ec08ceb52.title: Bradyrhizobium
614ec08ceb52.sentence: Bradyrhizobium is a genus of Gram-negative soil bacteria, many of which fix nitrogen.

ffb013124e39.title: Bradyrhizobium
ffb013124e39.sentence: They are common soil-dwelling micro-organisms that can form symbiotic relationships with leguminous plant species where they fix nitrogen in exchange for carbohydrates from the plant.

72d97b43bce4.title: Bradyrhizobium
72d97b43bce4.sentence: They are slow-growing in contrast to Rhizobium species, which are considered fast-growing rhizobia.

992f0cf420ef.title: Bradyrhizobium
992f0cf420ef.sentence: In a liquid medium, Bradyrhizobium species take 3–5 days to create a moderate turbidity and 6–8 hours to double in population size.

5c1145b63a29.title: Bradyrhizobium
5c1145b63a29.sentence: - Bradyrhizobium japonicum nodulates soybeans, cowpeas, mung beans, and siratro.

8d4fc3399e20.title: Bradyrhizobium
8d4fc3399e20.sentence: - Bradyrhizobium elkanii, Bradyrhizobium diazoefficiens, and Bradyrhizobium liaoningense establish symbiosis with soybeans.

17933007d84b.title: Bradyrhizobium
17933007d84b.sentence: Commercial inoculants of Bradyrhizobium are available.

08202344684b.title: Bradyrhizobium
08202344684b.sentence: Bradyrhizobia are also major components of forest soil microbial communities, where strains isolated from these soils are not typically capable of nitrogen fixation or nodulation.

c90f6260df34.title: Bradyrhizobium
c90f6260df34.sentence: Grain legumes are cultivated on about 1.5 million km2 of land per year.

816da85a7e2c.title: Bradyrhizobium
816da85a7e2c.sentence: The amount of nitrogen fixed annually is about 44–66 million tons worldwide, providing almost half of all nitrogen used in agriculture.

b26eda0d69ad.title: Rhizotron
b26eda0d69ad.sentence: A Rhizotron (from rhizóō, "root" as a verb – see wikt:rhizo-) is a laboratory constructed underground in order to study the soil and its interactions with plants and animals.

b1503b1d598a.title: Rhizotron
b1503b1d598a.sentence: Rhizotrons are typically equipped with a central corridor with viewing windows into the soil profiles on either side.

d89cd2c89e7f.title: Rhizotron
d89cd2c89e7f.sentence: On the outside, separate bays are constructed to enable specific experiments to be carried out by varying the soil composition and the plant and animals contained therein.

c9477bd6436d.title: Rhizotron
c9477bd6436d.sentence: Rhizotrons are in use at Kew Gardens, at the USDA Northern Research Station at Houghton, Michigan, at Treborth Botanic Garden, near Bangor, Gwynedd, U.K. and at Charles Sturt University, Wagga Wagga, Australia.

5c42545aecc1.title: Azospirillum
5c42545aecc1.sentence: Azospirillum is a Gram-negative, microaerophilic, non-fermentative and nitrogen-fixing bacterial genus from the family of Rhodospirillaceae.

5186b65eec85.title: Azospirillum
5186b65eec85.sentence: Azospirillum bacteria can promote plant growth.

6984dab88839.title: Azospirillum
6984dab88839.sentence: Azospirillum are found in freshwater and soil habitats, especially in close relationships with plant roots.

6b4d8160240b.title: Azospirillum
6b4d8160240b.sentence: Over 113 species of plants in 35 different plant families have been documented to have benefited from association with a species of Azospirillum.

b20aa5cfdb29.title: Azospirillum
b20aa5cfdb29.sentence: Many Azospirillum excrete plant hormones that alter how the roots of plants grow.

9cae64bbe954.title: Azospirillum
9cae64bbe954.sentence: Affected roots frequently grow more branches and fine root hairs, which may help the plants acquire water and nutrients more efficiently.

281f77d29fab.title: Azospirillum
281f77d29fab.sentence: In addition to these changes, Azospirillum can also alter the forms of plant nutrients such as nitrogen and phosphorus to make them more available to plants.

00ceaebd5440.title: Azospirillum
00ceaebd5440.sentence: Azospirillum competes with pathogens on the roots for space and for trace nutrients such as iron.

02ac095069eb.title: Azospirillum
02ac095069eb.sentence: The plants' immune systems can also be primed by Azospirillum to resist attack by pathogens, a process known as induced systemic resistance.

553f4ed669a0.title: Azospirillum
553f4ed669a0.sentence: However, how much nitrogen Azospirillum contribute to crop plants via biological fixation is debated.

d9e245ae313a.title: Azospirillum
d9e245ae313a.sentence: In Brazil, during the 1970s, similar strains of this species were found associated with the roots of grain plants by scientists led by Dr. Johanna Döbereiner.

89bb281ac3c1.title: Azospirillum
89bb281ac3c1.sentence: Her group discovered that these bacteria had the ability to fix nitrogen.

89df9e9b9068.title: Azospirillum
89df9e9b9068.sentence: In 2009, the first commercial inoculants containing Azospirillum came on the market, and by 2018, over 3 million doses were applied annually to crops by farmers, mainly in South America.

42c4955657b7.title: Common symbiosis signaling pathway
42c4955657b7.sentence: The common symbiosis signaling pathway (CSSP) is a highly conserved signaling cascade in plants that allows them to interact with symbiotic microbes.

92d5b1a5773a.title: Common symbiosis signaling pathway
92d5b1a5773a.sentence: The common symbiosis signaling pathway occurs within plant root cells.

25144f6483b2.title: Common symbiosis signaling pathway
25144f6483b2.sentence: It corresponds to an ancestral pathway that plants use to interact with arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF).

8f8c36802dfa.title: Common symbiosis signaling pathway
8f8c36802dfa.sentence: It is known as "common" because different evolutionary younger symbioses also use this pathway, notably the root nodule symbiosis with nitrogen-fixing rhizobia bacteria.

b9a00ad864df.title: Common symbiosis signaling pathway
b9a00ad864df.sentence: The pathway is activated by both Nod-factor perception (for nodule forming rhizobia), as well as by Myc-factor perception that are released from AMF.

976a4269bc39.title: Common symbiosis signaling pathway
976a4269bc39.sentence: Myc factors or Nod factors are perceived by LysM receptor-like kinases at the plant plasma membrane, triggering downstream signaling through additional proteins such as SYMRK.

81588fd041c0.title: Common symbiosis signaling pathway
81588fd041c0.sentence: The signal is then transduced to the nucleus, where it generates nuclear calcium oscillations via ion channels and nucleoporins.

0ab4082cd171.title: Common symbiosis signaling pathway
0ab4082cd171.sentence: These calcium signals are decoded by the calcium- and calmodulin-dependent protein kinase CCaMK, which activates transcription factors such as CYCLOPS.

601e30e316a6.title: Common symbiosis signaling pathway
601e30e316a6.sentence: At this point in nodulation or AMF colonisation, downstream responses diverge depending on the symbiosis, with CYCLOPS regulating genes that control the formation of either arbuscules or nodules.

2a5eb66fd69c.title: Mycorrhiza
2a5eb66fd69c.sentence: The CSSP has origins predating the colonization of land by plants, demonstrating that the co-evolution of plants and arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi is over 500 million years old.

215a9d2ec5ea.title: Rhizobia
215a9d2ec5ea.sentence: Endomycorrhizal symbiosis can provide many insights into rhizobia symbiosis because recent genetic studies have suggested that rhizobia co-opted the signaling pathways from the more ancient endomycorrhizal symbiosis.

b85cc7e3a291.title: Rhizobia
b85cc7e3a291.sentence: For example, the plant recognition gene SYMRK (symbiosis receptor-like kinase) is involved in the perception of both the rhizobial Nod factors as well as the endomycorrhizal Myc-LCOs.

6d92ee7b09db.title: Ectomycorrhizal extramatrical mycelium
6d92ee7b09db.sentence: The mycelial growth pattern, extent of biomass accumulation, and the presence or absence of rhizomorphs are used to classify fungi by exploration type.

37309272a8c1.title: Ectomycorrhizal extramatrical mycelium
37309272a8c1.sentence: Agerer first proposed the designation of exploration types in 2001, and the concept has since been widely employed in studies of ectomycorrhizal ecology.

e59fb81c83d4.title: Ectomycorrhizal extramatrical mycelium
e59fb81c83d4.sentence: Four exploration types are commonly recognized: Contact, Short-distance, Medium-distance and Long-distance.

2382932449d7.title: Ectomycorrhizal extramatrical mycelium
2382932449d7.sentence: Long-distance exploration types are highly differentiated, forming rhizomorphs that contain hollow vessel-like transport tubes.

b15dca085b22.title: Ectomycorrhizal extramatrical mycelium
b15dca085b22.sentence: Long distance types are associated with increased levels of organic nitrogen uptake compared to other exploration types and are thought to be less competitive in disturbed systems in contrast to short distance types which are able to regenerate more efficiently after a disturbance event.

da5f592bd432.title: Ectomycorrhizal extramatrical mycelium
da5f592bd432.sentence: In pine systems, fungi that display short-distance exploration types are less able to colonize new roots spaced far from the mycorrhiza, and long-distance types dominate areas of low root density.

48c58d3e9b9c.title: Ectomycorrhizal extramatrical mycelium
48c58d3e9b9c.sentence: Conversely, short-distance exploration types tend to dominate areas of high root density where decreased carbon expenditure makes them more competitive than long-distance species.

1e20163ac0be.title: Ectomycorrhizal extramatrical mycelium
1e20163ac0be.sentence: Often, fungi fail to fit into a defined exploration type, falling instead along a gradient.

eded2d5ab675.title: Ectomycorrhizal extramatrical mycelium
eded2d5ab675.sentence: Detailed morphological characterization of exploration type has been defined for over 550 different ectomycorrhizal species and are compiled in Deemy Database.

d4777af35405.title: Aerial root
d4777af35405.sentence: These specialized aerial roots enable plants to breathe air in habitats with waterlogged soil.

7ca1d87d7d09.title: Aerial root
7ca1d87d7d09.sentence: The roots may grow downward from the stem or upward from typical roots.

56011af2b266.title: Aerial root
56011af2b266.sentence: Some botanists classify them as aerating roots rather than aerial roots if they emerge from the soil.

19565844e9a7.title: Aerial root
19565844e9a7.sentence: The surface of these roots is covered with porous lenticels, which lead to air-filled spongy tissue called aerenchyma.

75c25795654c.title: Aerial root
75c25795654c.sentence: This tissue facilitates the diffusion of gases throughout the plant, as oxygen diffusion coefficient in air is four orders of magnitude greater than in water.

b5d6025c1788.title: Aerial root
b5d6025c1788.sentence: Pneumatophores differentiate the black mangrove and grey mangrove from other mangrove species.

edfd3679f683.title: Aerial root
edfd3679f683.sentence: There are many types of aerial roots; some, such as mangrove, are used for aeration and not for water absorption.

835508f0e7b0.title: Aerial root
835508f0e7b0.sentence: Members of the subfamily Taxodioideae produce woody above-ground structures, known as cypress knees, that project upward from their horizontal roots.

4f994e5ca98d.title: Aerial root
4f994e5ca98d.sentence: One hypothesis suggests that these structures function as pneumatophores, facilitating gas exchange in waterlogged soils.

7d037ee38594.title: Aerial root
7d037ee38594.sentence: However, modern research has largely discredited this idea, as the knees lack aerenchyma and gas exchange through them is not significant.

0d4f16fb1158.title: Aerial root
0d4f16fb1158.sentence: Their true functions remain unclear, with alternative theories proposing roles such as nutrient acquisition or storage, structural support, or erosion prevention.

0767f839d1b8.title: Mycorrhizosphere
0767f839d1b8.section: Ecological Interactions > Role in Agricultural Soil Conservation
0767f839d1b8.sentence: Different agricultural methods’ cycle timings, mechanical implements, and chemical additives produce diverse effects upon soil ecology that may be beneficial or deleterious to the mycorrhizosphere upon which crops are dependent for nutrients (e.g. P, Zn, Cu, Fe, N, K, Ca, Mg) and pathogen resistance.

3e342ca032bf.title: Mycorrhizosphere
3e342ca032bf.section: Ecological Interactions > Role in Agricultural Soil Conservation
3e342ca032bf.sentence: Green agricultural practices that promote intercropping and reduce tillage, herbicides, and artificial fertilization increase AMF colonization.

cf84b330d60c.title: Mycorrhizosphere
cf84b330d60c.section: Ecological Interactions > Role in Agricultural Soil Conservation
cf84b330d60c.sentence: Hyphal soil penetration imparts erosion and nutritional depletion resistance through adhesive glomalin secretion, which improves the formation of stable aggregates in soil that contain nutrients, oxygen, and moisture, while accounting for approximately 5% of global organic carbon and nitrogen storage.

26c7016826f5.title: Mycorrhizosphere
26c7016826f5.section: Ecological Interactions > Role in Agricultural Soil Conservation
26c7016826f5.sentence: Conventional monocropping agriculture minimizes potential AMF symbiosis through reduced crop biodiversity, frequent tillage, and artificial fertilizer and herbicide use.

16459e044ced.title: Mycorrhizosphere
16459e044ced.section: Ecological Interactions > Role in Agricultural Soil Conservation
16459e044ced.sentence: Varying extents of tillage are utilized to aerate and homogenize the distribution of artificial fertilizers and moisture within soil, though they sever hyphal connections in mycorrhizal networks.

562611636c22.title: Mycorrhizosphere
562611636c22.section: Ecological Interactions > Role in Agricultural Soil Conservation
562611636c22.sentence: Though artificial fertilizers are commonly used to satisfy the increased agricultural nutrient demands for larger crop yields, these reduce plant reliance upon AMF networks and may thereby reduce plants’ symbiosis with mycorrhizae.

db08bf2583bd.title: Mycorrhizosphere
db08bf2583bd.section: Ecological Interactions > Role in Agricultural Soil Conservation
db08bf2583bd.sentence: Milpa agriculture is a traditional technique utilized by Mesoamerican communities that minimizes tillage and artificial fertilizer use as well as increasing host availability with endemic multicropping and the growth of ruderal species during fallow periods.

240cf4dd28fc.title: Mycorrhizosphere
240cf4dd28fc.section: Ecological Interactions > Role in Agricultural Soil Conservation
240cf4dd28fc.sentence: Notably, maize and legumes, commonly intercropped in Las Tres Hermanas milpa agriculture, share stored carbohydrates or nitrogen and phosphorus compounds, respectively.

89037f8a153d.title: Mycorrhizosphere
89037f8a153d.section: Ecological Interactions > Role in Agricultural Soil Conservation
89037f8a153d.sentence: It is through these milpa practices that maize yields are thereby greater when integrated by the mycorrhizosphere with intercropped beans.

13557cc9e969.title: Fine root
13557cc9e969.sentence: To account for this, root biologists have begun to define subcategories of fine roots based on root diameter, position in the root branching hierarchy, and function.

e89602e96fda.title: Fine root
e89602e96fda.sentence: This size-based definition is arbitrary, as it does not clearly or logically define fine roots based on anatomy, morphology, physiology, and/or function.

1d0431abf962.title: Fine root
1d0431abf962.sentence: Roots with a diameter less than 0.5 millimeters have been termed 'very fine roots'.

46aa2662c07d.title: Fine root
46aa2662c07d.sentence: This classification system assigns an order number to a root based on that root's position in the branching hierarchy of the root system, and is based on the Horton-Strahler scheme for ordering stream tributaries.

5b66c20cc740.title: Fine root
5b66c20cc740.sentence: The most distal segments of the root system (unbranched root segments that end in root tips) are classified as first-order roots.

af153c4fb1a5.title: Fine root
af153c4fb1a5.sentence: When two roots of the same order converge, the root that results from their combination is assigned the next highest root order (so two first-order roots merge to form a second-order root).

55197886c945.title: Fine root
55197886c945.sentence: Traits that have been shown to increase with root order include root diameter, life span, and secondary growth, while root nitrogen content, mycorrhizal colonization, and turnover have shown decreases with increasing root order.

b9f053440682.title: Fine root
b9f053440682.sentence: By this system, fine roots are classified as either absorptive fine roots or transport fine roots.

5af8da2d2815.title: Fine root
5af8da2d2815.sentence: Absorptive fine roots mostly function in acquiring soil resources and comprise the most distal segments of a root system (lower-order segments).

4f076e465caf.title: Fine root
4f076e465caf.sentence: Transport fine roots result from the merging of absorptive fine roots and are therefore higher in root order.

f56cc823f597.title: Plant-growth promoting fungi
f56cc823f597.sentence: Plant-growth promoting fungi (PGPF) are a diverse and heterogeneous group of non-pathogenic, filamentous, soil-borne fungi that colonize plant roots, particularly in the rhizosphere, and have a positive or mutualistic effect on plant health and development.

709a469f9b15.title: Plant-growth promoting fungi
709a469f9b15.sentence: PGPF, like their bacterial counterparts (PGPR - Plant Growth-Promoting Rhizobacteria), are a key component of the plant microbiome.

56f8e1fb8d04.title: Plant-growth promoting fungi
56f8e1fb8d04.sentence: Despite the name, not all fungi that promote plant growth are considered PGPF (e.g. mychorrhizal fungi).

bddeb45f2ad4.title: Plant-growth promoting fungi
bddeb45f2ad4.sentence: PGPF primarily belongs to the phylum Ascomycota, and a few of them belong to Basidiomycota and Zygomycota.

b443d2c2601f.title: Plant-growth promoting fungi
b443d2c2601f.sentence: The production of auxin (IAA) by fungi is a key component of their colonization strategy and promotion of root system architecture.

808ebed59b9e.title: Plant-growth promoting fungi
808ebed59b9e.sentence: PGPF also enhance the bioavailability and uptake of essential plant nutrients, as phosphorus solubilization is facilitated by the production of organic acids by PGPF and can be a component of their plant-growth promoting (PGP) effect.

cf738b2d8086.title: Plant-growth promoting fungi
cf738b2d8086.sentence: For micronutrients, they promote the utilization of decomposing organic matter through mineral solubilization and sequestering ferric ions via siderophores.

fa0cec7e1509.title: Plant-growth promoting fungi
fa0cec7e1509.sentence: Indirect mechanisms primarily involve protecting the plant by suppressing the growth of harmful soil microorganisms.

c04f88ac684e.title: Plant-growth promoting fungi
c04f88ac684e.sentence: Includes the production of inhibitory compounds (antibiotics), parasitism of pathogenic fungi (mycoparasitism), and competition for nutrients and colonization sites in the rhizosphere.

e083161f95a2.title: Plant-growth promoting fungi
e083161f95a2.sentence: A core indirect mechanism is the elicitation of Induced Systemic Resistance (ISR) in the host plant.

4a2ad8de76ff.title: Plant-growth promoting fungi
4a2ad8de76ff.sentence: Some PGPF species, like those in the genus Trichoderma, have the capacity for bioremediation of environmental pollutants, including heavy metals, organometallic compounds, and agrochemicals.

bcf2ef1db8fa.title: Soil formation
bcf2ef1db8fa.sentence: Plants have fine roots that excrete organic compounds (sugars, organic acids, mucilage), slough off cells (in particular at their tip), and are easily decomposed, adding organic matter to soil, a process called rhizodeposition.

82837bd741a3.title: Rhizosphere
82837bd741a3.sentence: This rhizodeposition comes in various forms of organic carbon and nitrogen that provide for the communities around plant roots and dramatically affect the chemistry surrounding the roots.

827f607e3908.title: Tilth
827f607e3908.sentence: The fungal hyphae networks can establish a role of enmeshment with EPS and rhizodeposition, thus improving aggregate stability.

c556bcbdd1e1.title: Rhizosphere
c556bcbdd1e1.sentence: Rhizodeposition allows for the growth of communities of microorganisms directly surrounding and inside plant roots.

acfab5008204.title: Rhizosphere
acfab5008204.sentence: This leads to complex interactions between species, including mutualism, predation/parasitism, and competition.

3369bd991236.title: Rhizosphere
3369bd991236.sentence: The food web in the rhizosphere can be considered as three different channels with two distinct sources of energy: the detritus-dependent channels are fungi and bacterial species, and the root energy-dependent channel consists of nematodes, symbiotic species, and some arthropods.

e358849b40c7.title: Rhizosphere
e358849b40c7.sentence: This bacterial channel is considered to be a faster channel because of the ability of species to focus on more accessible resources in the rhizosphere and have faster regeneration times compared with the fungal channel.

9e8fa31aa337.title: Rhizosphere
9e8fa31aa337.sentence: Predation by bacterial-feeding nematodes was shown to influence nitrogen availability and plant growth.

ae6380f77293.title: Rhizosphere
ae6380f77293.sentence: Plants and soil microflora indirectly compete against one another by tying up limiting resources, such as carbon and nitrogen, into their biomass.

c95fea74e36e.title: Rhizosphere
c95fea74e36e.sentence: Plants are less successful at the uptake of organic nitrogen, such as amino acids than the soil microflora that exists in the rhizosphere.

6235cc212b00.title: Rhizosphere
6235cc212b00.section: Ecology of the rhizosphere > Microbial consortium
6235cc212b00.sentence: Although various studies have shown that single microorganisms can benefit plants, it is increasingly evident that when a microbial consortium—two or more interacting microorganisms—is involved, additive or synergistic results can be expected.

2c3a63d41eba.title: Rhizosphere
2c3a63d41eba.section: Ecology of the rhizosphere > Microbial consortium
2c3a63d41eba.sentence: Rhizosphere microorganisms can influence one another, and the resulting consortia of PGPB + PGPB (e.g., a nitrogen-fixing bacterium such as Rhizobium spp. and Pseudomonas fluorescens), AMF + PGPB, and Trichoderma + PGPB may have synergetic effects on plant growth and fitness, providing the plant with enhanced benefits to overcome biotic and abiotic stress.

c10e2c250024.title: Rhizosphere
c10e2c250024.section: Ecology of the rhizosphere > Community structure
c10e2c250024.sentence: Intensive agricultural management, particularly long-term monoculture, can override these natural selection processes, leading to "soil sickness." This phenomenon is characterized by a shift in pathogenic and beneficial microbial populations, negatively impacting soil fertility and crop yield.

71820b07ba7f.title: Rhizosphere
71820b07ba7f.sentence: In addition to supporting beneficial communities, the accumulation of specific root exudates over time can create negative feedback loops for the host plant.

9a990c85925b.title: Rhizosphere
9a990c85925b.sentence: In aged tea plantations, the buildup of plant polyphenols in the soil has been directly linked to a detrimental shift in soil microbial communities, contributing to the decline in soil health and productivity known as soil sickness.

7c0a698e88d3.title: Plant litter
7c0a698e88d3.sentence: Plant litter (also leaf litter, tree litter, soil litter, litterfall, or duff) is dead plant material (such as leaves, bark, needles, twigs, and cladodes) that has fallen on the top layer of soil, commonly known as the litter layer or O-horizon ("O" for "organic").

557e910906b3.title: Plant litter
557e910906b3.sentence: Plant litter typically becomes detritus and releases nutrients into the soil when decomposed, and also forms a loose layer of covering that preserves soil moisture, reduces soil erosion and provides concealment for small epigeic and fossorial animals.

2098b142fbb1.title: Plant litter
2098b142fbb1.sentence: Litterfall is characterized as fresh, undecomposed, and easily recognizable (by species and type) plant debris.

2494e5c04429.title: Plant litter
2494e5c04429.sentence: Items larger than 2 cm diameter are referred to as coarse litter, while anything smaller is referred to as fine litter or litter.

914f85e11a72.title: Plant litter
914f85e11a72.sentence: For example, leaf tissues account for about 70 percent of litterfall in forests, but woody litter tends to increase with forest age.

94f469a320e8.title: Plant litter
94f469a320e8.sentence: In grasslands, there is very little aboveground perennial tissue so the annual litterfall is very low and quite nearly equal to the net primary production.

f88a6d28b949.title: Plant litter
f88a6d28b949.sentence: In soil science, soil litter is classified in three layers, which form on the surface of the O Horizon.

ec40a03583eb.title: Plant litter
ec40a03583eb.sentence: - L - organic horizon characterized by relatively undecomposed plant material (described above).

f133ef558a0e.title: Plant litter
f133ef558a0e.sentence: - F - organic horizon found beneath L characterized by accumulation of partly decomposed organic matter.

8473a5188d9d.title: Plant litter
8473a5188d9d.sentence: - H - organic horizon below F characterized by accumulation of fully decomposed organic matter mostly indiscernible

3b7e695884d9.title: Plant litter
3b7e695884d9.sentence: Specifically, litterfall declines with increasing latitude.

4f8f9f13835a.title: Plant litter
4f8f9f13835a.sentence: In tropical rainforests, there is a thin litter layer due to the rapid decomposition, while in boreal forests, the rate of decomposition is slower and leads to the accumulation of a thick litter layer, also known as a mor.

f47db75fd4c2.title: Plant litter
f47db75fd4c2.sentence: Soil litter protects soil aggregates from raindrop impact, preventing the release of clay and silt particles from plugging soil pores.

4d1cd13946a9.title: Plant litter
4d1cd13946a9.sentence: Surface detritus facilitates the capture and infiltration of rainwater into lower soil layers.

b6c1eed0d1dc.title: Plant litter
b6c1eed0d1dc.sentence: In addition soil litter reduces wind erosion by preventing soil from losing moisture and providing cover preventing soil transportation.

58822f296836.title: Plant litter
58822f296836.sentence: In every terrestrial ecosystem, the largest fraction of all net primary production is lost to herbivores and litter fall.

243cc2a1f4d1.title: Plant litter
243cc2a1f4d1.sentence: It is an important factor in ecosystem dynamics, as it is indicative of ecological productivity and may be useful in predicting regional nutrient cycling and soil fertility.

a4eb579e6c41.title: Plant litter
a4eb579e6c41.sentence: Soil litter can be completely removed depending on intensity and severity of wildfires and season.

8b19592c8d75.title: Plant litter
8b19592c8d75.sentence: Regions with high frequency wildfires have reduced vegetation density and reduced soil litter accumulation.

73ee19c77ac2.title: Plant litter
73ee19c77ac2.sentence: For instance, forest litter raking as a replacement for straw in husbandry is an old non-timber practice in forest management that has been widespread in Europe since the seventeenth century.

a3d75c00a22c.title: Plant litter
a3d75c00a22c.sentence: In 1853, an estimated 50 Tg of dry litter per year was raked in European forests, when the practice reached its peak.

9d9ffaad6eea.title: Plant litter
9d9ffaad6eea.sentence: This human disturbance, if not combined with other degradation factors, could promote podzolisation; if managed properly (for example, by burying litter removed after its use in animal husbandry), even the repeated removal of forest biomass may not have negative effects on pedogenesis.

c0dfd65b3903.title: Plant litter
c0dfd65b3903.sentence: The leaf litter found in primary forests is more abundant, deeper and holds more humidity than in secondary forests.

b96406d14633.title: Plant litter
b96406d14633.sentence: Non-terrestrial litterfall follows a very different path.

6368a5b73f9d.title: Plant litter
6368a5b73f9d.sentence: Litter is produced both inland by terrestrial plants and moved to the coast by fluvial processes, and by mangrove ecosystems.

c5644dc2edcc.title: Plant litter
c5644dc2edcc.sentence: From the coast Robertson & Daniel 1989 found it is then removed by the tide, crabs and microbes.

92b9faed34d0.title: Plant litter
92b9faed34d0.sentence: They also noticed that which of those three is most significant depends on the tidal regime.

8cc940d92581.title: Plant litter
8cc940d92581.sentence: Nordhaus et al. 2011 find crabs forage for leaves at low tide and if their detritivory is the predominant disposal route, they can take 80% of leaf material.

a981f2ed1216.title: Plant litter
a981f2ed1216.sentence: They find crabs pass a noticeable amount of undegraded lignins to both the sediments and water composition.

1e2a18c68503.title: Plant litter
1e2a18c68503.sentence: They also find that the exact carbonaceous contribution of each plant species can be traced from the plant, through the crab, to its sediment or water disposition in this way.

28e2020b8739.title: Glomalin
28e2020b8739.sentence: Glomalin is a hypothetical glycoprotein produced abundantly on hyphae and spores of arbuscular mycorrhizal (AM) fungi in soil and in roots.

b653a2188bd8.title: Glomalin
b653a2188bd8.sentence: Glomalin was proposed in 1996 by Sara F. Wright, a scientist at the USDA Agricultural Research Service, but it was not isolated and described yet.

76f77f847454.title: Glomalin
76f77f847454.sentence: The name comes from Glomerales, an order of fungi.

cdeb2adcdea3.title: Glomalin
cdeb2adcdea3.sentence: An elusive substance, it is mostly assumed to have a glue-like effect on soil, but it has not been isolated yet.

16ddae900ed9.title: Glomalin
16ddae900ed9.sentence: Glomalin is hypothesized to improve soil aggregate stability and decrease soil erosion.

9c1611e7e42e.title: Glomalin
9c1611e7e42e.sentence: A strong correlation has been found between GRSP and soil aggregate water stability in a wide variety of soils where organic material is the main binding agent, although the mechanism is not known.

88d3c6d74e1a.title: Glomalin
88d3c6d74e1a.sentence: When AM fungi are eliminated from soil through incubation of soil without host plants, the concentration of GRSP declines.

c7d00447b2f7.title: Glomalin
c7d00447b2f7.sentence: A similar decline in GRSP has also been observed in incubated soils from forested, afforested, and agricultural land and grasslands treated with fungicide.

73a54aa6b5d1.title: Glomalin
73a54aa6b5d1.sentence: Sampled GRSP takes 7–42 years to biodegrade and is thought to contribute up to 30 percent of the soil carbon where mycorrhizal fungi is present.

bd2c43cc240e.title: Epiphyte
bd2c43cc240e.sentence: An epiphyte (from Ancient Greek epi-, meaning 'upon', and phutón, meaning 'plant') is a plant or plant-like organism that grows on the surface of another plant or plant-like organism.

4221bf5b5d6e.title: Epiphyte
4221bf5b5d6e.sentence: It derives its moisture and nutrients from the air, rain, water (in marine environments) or from debris accumulating around it.

b50d778418a7.title: Epiphyte
b50d778418a7.sentence: The plants on which epiphytes grow are called phorophytes.

1bb8d66ce9bf.title: Epiphyte
1bb8d66ce9bf.sentence: Epiphytes differ from parasitic plants in that they grow on the host for physical support only, and do not draw nourishment from it.

566198e9f5cc.title: Epiphyte
566198e9f5cc.sentence: Epiphytic plants are sometimes called "air plants" because they do not root in soil.

c84c6d64aa8a.title: Epiphyte
c84c6d64aa8a.section: Epiphytes in terrestrial ecosystems > Plant nutrient relations
c84c6d64aa8a.sentence: Epiphytes are not connected to the soil, and consequently must get nutrients from other sources, such as fog, dew, rain and mist, or from nutrients being released from the ground rooted plants by decomposition or leaching, and dinitrogen fixation.

ef66ea4b0fb0.title: Epiphyte
ef66ea4b0fb0.section: Epiphytes in terrestrial ecosystems > Holo-epiphyte or hemi-epiphyte
ef66ea4b0fb0.sentence: Epiphytes can generally be categorized into holo-epiphytes or hemi-epiphytes.

ca8ab7a3388b.title: Epiphyte
ca8ab7a3388b.section: Epiphytes in terrestrial ecosystems > Holo-epiphyte or hemi-epiphyte
ca8ab7a3388b.sentence: A holo-epiphyte is a plant that spends its whole life cycle without contact with the ground and a hemi-epiphyte is a plant that spends only half of its life without the ground before the roots can reach or make contact with the ground.

45919d572c2e.title: Epiphyte
45919d572c2e.section: Epiphytes in terrestrial ecosystems > Holo-epiphyte or hemi-epiphyte
45919d572c2e.sentence: Orchids are a common example of holo-epiphytes and strangler figs are an example of hemi-epiphytes.

d8a01066502e.title: Epiphyte
d8a01066502e.section: Epiphytes in terrestrial ecosystems > Plant nutrient relations
d8a01066502e.sentence: Epiphytes can have a significant effect on the microenvironment of their host, and of ecosystems where they are abundant, as they hold water in the canopy and decrease water input to the soil.

909d83aaea35.title: Epiphyte
909d83aaea35.section: Epiphytes in terrestrial ecosystems > Plant nutrient relations
909d83aaea35.sentence: Epiphytes create a significantly cooler and more moist environment in the host plant canopy, potentially greatly reducing water loss by the host through transpiration.

2813c2b7dae7.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/02%3A_What_Is_Organic_Matter_and_Why_Is_It_So_Important/2.01%3A_Introduction
2813c2b7dae7.sentence: As we will discuss at the end of this chapter, organic matter has an overwhelming effect on almost all soil properties, although it is generally present in relatively small amounts.

60b9bb922b17.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/02%3A_What_Is_Organic_Matter_and_Why_Is_It_So_Important/2.01%3A_Introduction
60b9bb922b17.sentence: A typical agricultural soil has 1–6% organic matter by weight.

8c8cc77bca73.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/02%3A_What_Is_Organic_Matter_and_Why_Is_It_So_Important/2.01%3A_Introduction
8c8cc77bca73.sentence: It consists of three distinctly different parts: living organisms, fresh residues and molecules derived from well-decomposed residues.

35ae31fb6a8e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/02%3A_What_Is_Organic_Matter_and_Why_Is_It_So_Important/2.01%3A_Introduction
35ae31fb6a8e.sentence: These three parts of soil organic matter have been described as the living, the dead and the very dead.

4fc66f6cee96.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/02%3A_What_Is_Organic_Matter_and_Why_Is_It_So_Important/2.01%3A_Introduction
4fc66f6cee96.sentence: The living portion represents about 15% of the total soil organic matter.

bdf944e2dd07.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/02%3A_What_Is_Organic_Matter_and_Why_Is_It_So_Important/2.01%3A_Introduction
bdf944e2dd07.sentence: The range of organisms in soil is so great that it is estimated that they represent about 25% of the world’s total biodiversity.

a54655e6fe7b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/02%3A_What_Is_Organic_Matter_and_Why_Is_It_So_Important/2.01%3A_Introduction
a54655e6fe7b.sentence: The fresh residues, or “dead” organic matter, consist of recently deceased microorganisms, insects, earthworms, old plant roots, crop residues and recently added manures.

06dff7c616ef.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/02%3A_What_Is_Organic_Matter_and_Why_Is_It_So_Important/2.01%3A_Introduction
06dff7c616ef.sentence: This part of soil organic matter is the active, or easily decomposed, fraction.

127f2e37bef5.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/02%3A_What_Is_Organic_Matter_and_Why_Is_It_So_Important/2.01%3A_Introduction
127f2e37bef5.sentence: This active fraction of soil organic matter is the main supply of food for various organisms—microorganisms, insects and earthworms—living in the soil.

5e531fb0d8c3.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/02%3A_What_Is_Organic_Matter_and_Why_Is_It_So_Important/2.01%3A_Introduction
5e531fb0d8c3.sentence: These molecules generally do not last long in the soil.

04b70317f82a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/02%3A_What_Is_Organic_Matter_and_Why_Is_It_So_Important/2.01%3A_Introduction
04b70317f82a.sentence: Some cellular molecules such as lignin are decomposed, but it takes longer for organisms to do so.

b32a870b685a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/02%3A_What_Is_Organic_Matter_and_Why_Is_It_So_Important/2.01%3A_Introduction
b32a870b685a.sentence: This can make up a large fraction of the soil organic matter in poorly drained soils, like peats and mucks, as well as wetlands that have been taken into agricultural production.

9b3f3b154f35.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/02%3A_What_Is_Organic_Matter_and_Why_Is_It_So_Important/2.01%3A_Introduction
9b3f3b154f35.sentence: These hold large amounts of organic matter that was not decomposed due to waterlogging, but they don’t provide the same benefits as the fresh residues.

87a148c45676.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/02%3A_What_Is_Organic_Matter_and_Why_Is_It_So_Important/2.01%3A_Introduction
87a148c45676.sentence: Sticky substances on the skin of earthworms and other materials produced by fungi help bind particles together.

03fe79aefd94.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/02%3A_What_Is_Organic_Matter_and_Why_Is_It_So_Important/2.01%3A_Introduction
03fe79aefd94.sentence: Sticky substances on plant roots as well as the proliferation of fine roots and their associated mycorrhizae help promote development of stable soil aggregates.

a8412ffbfd89.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/02%3A_What_Is_Organic_Matter_and_Why_Is_It_So_Important/2.01%3A_Introduction
a8412ffbfd89.sentence: Organisms such as earthworms and some fungi also help to stabilize the soil’s structure (for example, by producing channels that allow water to infiltrate) and, thereby, improve soil water status and aeration.

26a720ffe2b4.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/02%3A_What_Is_Organic_Matter_and_Why_Is_It_So_Important/2.01%3A_Introduction
26a720ffe2b4.sentence: Organic chemical compounds produced during the decomposition of fresh residues also help to bind soil particles together and give the soil good structure.

643b584fb793.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/02%3A_What_Is_Organic_Matter_and_Why_Is_It_So_Important/2.01%3A_Introduction
643b584fb793.sentence: The amount of organic matter in soils is about twice the organic carbon level.

1869e396f3af.title: Organic matter
1869e396f3af.sentence: Organic matter, organic material or natural organic matter (NOM) is the large source of carbon-based compounds found within natural and engineered, terrestrial, and aquatic environments.

bdd01f67ef3b.title: Organic matter
bdd01f67ef3b.sentence: It is matter composed of organic compounds that have come from the feces and remains of organisms such as plants and animals.

a949cbae5707.title: Organic matter
a949cbae5707.sentence: Basic structures are created from cellulose, tannin, cutin, and lignin, along with other various proteins, lipids, and carbohydrates.

bde96b7bd34b.title: Organic matter
bde96b7bd34b.sentence: Following the death of an organism, these materials—along with shed tissues like roots and leaves—are decomposed by microbial and fungal activity.

b448f6ede86e.title: Organic matter
b448f6ede86e.sentence: Through a process of oxidative polymerization, these smaller degradation products can then recombine to form complex, larger-scale organic molecules.

e60063dc66e5.title: Organic matter
e60063dc66e5.sentence: When it decays to the point in which it is no longer recognizable, it is called soil organic matter.

487049c4991e.title: Organic matter
487049c4991e.sentence: When the organic matter has broken down into a stable substance that resists further decomposition it is called humus.

ea49cf4fb59e.title: Organic matter
ea49cf4fb59e.sentence: Organic matter is very important in the movement of nutrients in the environment and plays a role in water retention on the surface of the planet.

5ef15bf783a0.title: Organic matter
5ef15bf783a0.sentence: Organic matter acts as a buffer in aqueous solutions to maintain a neutral pH in the environment.

8ebf319a84a8.title: Organic matter
8ebf319a84a8.sentence: The buffer acting component has been proposed to be relevant for neutralizing acid rain.

ec1f78c45715.title: Organic matter
ec1f78c45715.sentence: The molecular weights of these compounds can vary drastically, depending on if they repolymerize or not, from 200 to 20,000 amu.

ce42f5d98cb2.title: Organic matter
ce42f5d98cb2.sentence: Up to one-third of the carbon present is in aromatic compounds in which the carbon atoms form usually six-membered rings.

1852e8983cc6.title: Organic matter
1852e8983cc6.sentence: These rings are very stable due to resonance stabilization, so they are challenging to break down.

92b3f2af519f.title: Organic matter
92b3f2af519f.sentence: Measurements of organic matter generally measure only organic compounds or carbon, and so are only an approximation of the level of once living or decomposed matter.

2029c8d91fa4.title: Organic matter
2029c8d91fa4.sentence: Aquatic organic matter can be further divided into two components: (1) dissolved organic matter (DOM), measured as colored dissolved organic matter (CDOM) or dissolved organic carbon (DOC), and (2) particulate organic matter (POM).

aa567c8100db.title: Organic matter
aa567c8100db.sentence: They are typically differentiated by that which can pass through a 0.45 micrometre filter (DOM), and that which cannot (POM).

87777ea040f0.title: Organic matter
87777ea040f0.sentence: The equation of "organic" with living organisms comes from the now-abandoned idea of vitalism, which attributed a special force to life that alone could create organic substances.

98aefeaf8a07.title: Organic matter
98aefeaf8a07.sentence: This idea was first questioned after Friedrich Wöhler artificially synthesized urea in 1828.

6c654ed39c1c.title: Decomposition
6c654ed39c1c.sentence: Decomposition is the process by which dead organic substances are broken down into simpler organic or inorganic matter such as carbon dioxide, water, simple sugars and mineral salts.

1db5175eed00.title: Decomposition
1db5175eed00.sentence: The process is a part of the nutrient cycle and is essential for recycling the finite matter that occupies physical space in the biosphere.

d26f6c3ef63f.title: Decomposition
d26f6c3ef63f.sentence: One can differentiate abiotic decomposition from biotic decomposition (biodegradation); the former means "the degradation of a substance by chemical or physical processes", e.g., hydrolysis; the latter means "the metabolic breakdown of materials into simpler components by living organisms", typically by microorganisms.

14631a9c9765.title: Decomposition
14631a9c9765.sentence: It begins with leaching by water; the most easily lost and soluble carbon compounds are liberated in this process.

d3bf70bbc584.title: Decomposition
d3bf70bbc584.sentence: Another early process is physical breakup or fragmentation of the plant material into smaller pieces, providing greater surface area for colonization and attack by decomposers.

3fb473e03ba8.title: Decomposition
3fb473e03ba8.sentence: In fallen dead parts of plants (plant litter), this process is largely carried out by saprophagous (detritivorous) soil invertebrate fauna, whereas in standing parts of plants, primarily parasitic life-forms such as parasitic plants (e.g. mistletoes), insects (e.g. aphids) and fungi (e.g. polypores) play a major role in breaking down matter, both directly and indirectly via a multitrophic cascading effect.

327fbe217e49.title: Decomposition
327fbe217e49.sentence: Following this, the plant detritus (consisting of cellulose, hemicellulose, microbial metabolites, and lignin) undergoes chemical alteration by microbes.

444a8cb2fbec.title: Soil organic matter
444a8cb2fbec.sentence: The reactions that occur can be included in one of three genera:

419a185209b3.title: Soil organic matter
419a185209b3.sentence: - Enzymatic oxidation that produces carbon dioxide, water, and heat.

135b8dae48f6.title: Soil organic matter
135b8dae48f6.sentence: It affects the majority of the matter.

8fe4b53dd131.title: Soil organic matter
8fe4b53dd131.sentence: - A series of specific reactions liberate and mineralize the essential elements nitrogen, phosphorus, and sulfur.

35e287df4fc5.title: Soil organic matter
35e287df4fc5.sentence: - Compounds that are resistant to microbial action are formed by modification of the original compounds or by microbial synthesis of new ones to produce humus.

84903066ccae.title: Decomposition
84903066ccae.sentence: The rate of decomposition is governed by three sets of factors: the physical environment (temperature, moisture and soil properties), the quantity and quality of the dead material available to decomposers, and the nature of the microbial community itself.

0e9999ba9644.title: Decomposition
0e9999ba9644.sentence: Decomposition rates are low under very wet or very dry conditions.

8ae65d949b26.title: Decomposition
8ae65d949b26.sentence: Decomposition rates are highest in damp, moist conditions with adequate levels of oxygen.

63302bd23bb9.title: Decomposition
63302bd23bb9.sentence: When the rains return and soils become wet, the osmotic gradient between the bacterial cells and the soil water causes the cells to gain water quickly.

0123dd251af9.title: Decomposition
0123dd251af9.sentence: Under these conditions, many bacterial cells burst, releasing a pulse of nutrients.

f8a653e09be3.title: Decomposition
f8a653e09be3.sentence: Substances like sugars and amino acids decompose readily and are considered labile.

bf70511c179f.title: Decomposition
bf70511c179f.sentence: Cellulose and hemicellulose, which are broken down more slowly, are "moderately labile".

b621dd6dbb3b.title: Decomposition
b621dd6dbb3b.sentence: Compounds which are more resistant to decay, like lignin or cutin, are considered recalcitrant.

fd619d3cb0b9.title: Soil organic matter
fd619d3cb0b9.sentence: Cellulose and hemicellulose undergo fast decomposition by fungi and bacteria, with a half-life of 12–18 days in a temperate climate.

0dd4d23e5458.title: Decomposition
0dd4d23e5458.sentence: The more labile compounds decompose quickly, leaving an increasing proportion of recalcitrant material called humus.

523640464ce3.title: Decomposition
523640464ce3.sentence: Decomposition rates also tend to be slower in acidic soils.

44312df2ac93.title: Decomposition
44312df2ac93.sentence: Soils which are rich in clay minerals tend to have lower decomposition rates, and thus, higher levels of organic matter.

4cc1b13482e6.title: Decomposition
4cc1b13482e6.sentence: Clay minerals also bind particles of organic material to their surface, making them less accessible to microbes.

b2b6bb4b6abd.title: Decomposition
b2b6bb4b6abd.sentence: Soil disturbance like tilling increases decomposition by increasing the amount of oxygen in the soil and by exposing new organic matter to soil microbes.

de8af8edb846.title: Decomposition
de8af8edb846.sentence: The chemical aspects of plant decomposition always involve the release of carbon dioxide.

835496d18228.title: Decomposition
835496d18228.sentence: In fact, decomposition contributes over 90 percent of carbon dioxide released each year.

6354095ce797.title: Humus
6354095ce797.sentence: Humus is the stable form of soil organic matter derived from decomposition of plant and animal substances.

af8af7cff91a.title: Soil organic matter
af8af7cff91a.sentence: Humus refers to organic matter that has been decomposed by soil microflora and fauna to the point where it is resistant to further breakdown.

723daa5ce868.title: Humus
723daa5ce868.sentence: Humus, which ranges in colour from brown to black, is largely composed of carbon, and contains high amounts of nitrogen, and smaller amounts of phosphorus and sulfur.

867917872b11.title: Humus
867917872b11.sentence: The ratio of carbon to nitrogen (C:N) of humus commonly ranges between 8:1 and 15:1 with the median being about 12:1.

1ebfd40751dd.title: Humus
1ebfd40751dd.sentence: Only the decomposed organic matter in soil is considered humus, while the portion still in the process of decomposition is referred to as detritus.

9d8cbd5c7894.title: Humus
9d8cbd5c7894.sentence: Since the respective stages of transformation are gradual, a precise distinction is not possible.

e4f070bb006c.title: Humus
e4f070bb006c.sentence: Neither humus nor detritus is dead matter; both are heavily permeated by microorganisms such as soil bacteria and fungi.

78b6b535726a.title: Soil organic matter
78b6b535726a.sentence: Humus usually constitutes only five percent of the soil or less by volume, but it is an essential source of nutrients and adds important textural qualities crucial to soil health and plant growth.

c420487fde57.title: Humus
c420487fde57.sentence: Humic layer or humus horizon is the organic matter above the topsoil and below leaf litter which is finely divided having a high surface area.

1154d07ed824.title: Humus
1154d07ed824.sentence: Humus can be found in many layers of the soil, but usually in the upper layers.

2e19f100cf90.title: Humus
2e19f100cf90.sentence: Humus is amorphous and lacks the cellular structure characteristic of organisms.

852ed6f2dfea.title: Humus
852ed6f2dfea.sentence: Humus retains moisture in the topsoil, in particular in soils with a coarse texture (e.g. sand).

db0008f3de6d.title: Humus
db0008f3de6d.sentence: Humus is the Latin word for "ground" or "earth".

7fac470059d3.title: Humus
7fac470059d3.sentence: In agriculture, "humus" sometimes also is used to describe mature or natural compost extracted from a woodland or other spontaneous source for use as a soil conditioner.

6876912e6020.title: Detritus
6876912e6020.sentence: In biology, detritus (/dəˈtraɪtəs/ or /ˈdɛtrɪtəs/) is organic matter made up of the decomposing remains of organisms and plant material, and also of feces.

2a5586f33faf.title: Detritus
2a5586f33faf.sentence: Detritus usually hosts communities of microorganisms that colonize and decompose (remineralise) it.

e069253e0da1.title: Detritus
e069253e0da1.sentence: Such microorganisms may be decomposers, detritivores, or coprophages.

12634b5ae030.title: Detritus
12634b5ae030.sentence: In terrestrial ecosystems detritus is present as plant litter and other organic matter that is intermixed with soil, known as soil organic matter.

2c92cafba7cd.title: Detritus
2c92cafba7cd.sentence: In ecosystems on land, detritus is deposited on the surface of the ground, taking forms such as the humic soil beneath a layer of fallen leaves.

2ded104f8bb1.title: Detritus
2ded104f8bb1.sentence: The remains of decaying plants or animals, or their tissue parts, and feces gradually lose their form due to physical processes and the action of decomposers, including grazers, bacteria, and fungi.

a68264ec5baa.title: Detritus
a68264ec5baa.sentence: In forests, the detritus is typically dominated by leaf, twig, and bacteria litter as measured by biomass dominance.

8ff97981b07e.title: Detritus
8ff97981b07e.sentence: This plant litter provides important cover for seedling protection as well as cover for a variety of arthropods, reptiles and amphibians.

baca16c102eb.title: Detritus
baca16c102eb.sentence: At the later stages of decomposition, mesophilic micro-organisms decompose residual detritus, generating heat from exothermic processes; such heat generation is associated with the well known phenomenon of the elevated temperature of composting.

f9f5b4a820bf.title: Detritus
f9f5b4a820bf.sentence: In ecosystems on land, far more essential material is broken down as dead material passing through the detritus chain than is broken down by being eaten by animals in a living state.

913b4f4b72eb.title: Detritus
913b4f4b72eb.sentence: In terrestrial ecosystems, the waste products of animals, and dead plants and plant material collect mainly on the ground, and as decomposition proceeds, plants are supplied with fertilizer in the form of inorganic salts.

2e129bb80d2d.title: Detritus
2e129bb80d2d.sentence: In aquatic ecosystems, especially freshwater systems, most of the detritus comes from nearby terrestrial ecosystems.

0195f4b581c5.title: Detritus
0195f4b581c5.sentence: Plant litter is the most important source of carbon in smaller order streams.

1af6c1203064.title: Detritus
1af6c1203064.sentence: In saltwater bodies, organic material breaks down and forms a marine snow.

73909920f52a.title: Detritus
73909920f52a.sentence: This example of detritus commonly consists of organic materials such as dead phytoplankton and zooplankton, the outer walls of diatoms and coccolithophores, dead skin and scales of fish, and fecal pellets.

c6628cd1aed1.title: Mineralization (soil science)
c6628cd1aed1.sentence: In soil science, mineralization is the decomposition (i.e., oxidation) of the chemical compounds in organic matter, by which the nutrients in those compounds are released in soluble inorganic forms that may be available to plants.

5426fbc22852.title: Mineralization (soil science)
5426fbc22852.sentence: Mineralization is the opposite of immobilization.

2843ffd9e3e1.title: Mineralization (soil science)
2843ffd9e3e1.sentence: Mineralization increases the bioavailability of the nutrients that were in the decomposing organic compounds, most notably (because of their quantities) nitrogen, phosphorus, and sulfur.

083b2f598515.title: Mineralization (soil science)
083b2f598515.sentence: Whether the decomposition of an organic compound will result in mineralization or immobilization is dependent on its concentration proportionate to that of the carbon in the organic matter.

f609ce8ebbb6.title: Mineralization (soil science)
f609ce8ebbb6.sentence: In general, organic matter contacting soil has too little nitrogen to support the biosynthetic needs of the decomposing soil microbial population.

85963aaf3736.title: Mineralization (soil science)
85963aaf3736.sentence: If the C:N ratio of the decomposing organic matter is above circa 30:1 then the decomposing microbes may absorb nitrogen in mineral form as, e. g., ammonium or nitrates.

c6935c9b3da4.title: Mineralization (soil science)
c6935c9b3da4.sentence: This mineral nitrogen is said to be immobilized.

37bb508d8ae1.title: Mineralization (soil science)
37bb508d8ae1.sentence: This may reduce the concentration of inorganic nitrogen in the soil and thus the nitrogen is not available to plants.

1a147fba442a.title: Mineralization (soil science)
1a147fba442a.sentence: As carbon dioxide is released during the generation of energy in decomposition, a process called "catabolism", the C:N ratio of the organic matter decreases.

88cb41dfaf26.title: Mineralization (soil science)
88cb41dfaf26.sentence: When the C:N ratio is less than circa 25:1, further decomposition causes mineralization by the simultaneous release of inorganic nitrogen as ammonium.

776c49cf00b6.title: Soil organic matter
776c49cf00b6.sentence: Nitrogen | NH 4 +, NO 2 −, NO 3 −, N 2 (gas), N 2 O (gas)

ed5885c3f271.title: Soil organic matter
ed5885c3f271.sentence: Carbon | CO 2, CO 3 2−, HCO 3 −, CH 4, C

75ef514b06d1.title: Humus
75ef514b06d1.sentence: Microorganisms decompose a large portion of the soil organic matter into inorganic minerals that the roots of plants can absorb as nutrients.

ab04d6d8795c.title: Humus
ab04d6d8795c.sentence: In this process, nitrogen (nitrogen cycle) and the other nutrients (nutrient cycle) in the decomposed organic matter are recycled.

4b4f0eb79a2f.title: Humus
4b4f0eb79a2f.sentence: Depending on the conditions in which the decomposition occurs, a fraction of the organic matter does not mineralize and instead is transformed by a process called humification.

ee2a0a569377.title: Mineralization (soil science)
ee2a0a569377.sentence: When the decomposition of organic matter is complete, the mineralized nitrogen therefrom adds to that already present in the soil and therefore increases the total mineral nitrogen in the soil.

9271cdab6ff7.title: Remineralisation
9271cdab6ff7.sentence: In biogeochemistry, remineralisation (or remineralization) refers to the breakdown or transformation of organic matter (those molecules derived from a biological source) into its simplest inorganic forms.

6d592aee21c2.title: Remineralisation
6d592aee21c2.sentence: Most organic carbon exists in a reduced form which is then oxidized by the oxidant (such as O2) into CO2 and energy that can be harnessed by the organism.

d4d13a447211.title: Remineralisation
d4d13a447211.sentence: This process generally produces CO2, water and a collection of simple nutrients like nitrate or phosphate that can then be taken up by other organisms.

c8656aa3c591.title: Particulate organic matter
c8656aa3c591.sentence: Particulate organic matter (POM) is a fraction of total organic matter operationally defined as that which does not pass through a filter pore size that typically ranges in size from 0.053 millimeters (53 μm) to 2 millimeters.

2ac20f7fb73f.title: Particulate organic matter
2ac20f7fb73f.sentence: Particulate organic matter (POM): is the organic matter that retains evidence of its original cellular structure, and is discussed further in the next section.

b02ed3265293.title: Particulate organic matter
b02ed3265293.section: Terrestrial ecosystems > Role of POM in soils
b02ed3265293.sentence: Particulate organic matter (POM) includes steadily decomposing plant litter and animal faeces, and the detritus from the activity of microorganisms.

48eff49830b6.title: Particulate organic matter
48eff49830b6.sentence: When land samples are isolated by sieving or filtration, this fraction includes partially decomposed detritus and plant material, pollen, and other materials.

77ddc6ef5680.title: Particulate organic matter
77ddc6ef5680.sentence: POC refers specifically to the mass of carbon in the particulate organic material, while POM refers to the total mass of the particulate organic matter.

1c879c9ccae4.title: Particulate organic matter
1c879c9ccae4.sentence: In this sense POC is a component of POM and there is typically about twice as much POM as POC.

976d04a2d2ef.title: Particulate organic matter
976d04a2d2ef.section: Terrestrial ecosystems > Role of POM in soils
976d04a2d2ef.sentence: Most of it continually undergoes decomposition by microorganisms (when conditions are sufficiently moist) and usually has a turnover time of less than 10 years.

fcd3707f7ea6.title: Particulate organic matter
fcd3707f7ea6.section: Terrestrial ecosystems > Role of POM in soils
fcd3707f7ea6.sentence: Less active parts may take 15 to 100 years to turnover.

17c9f3934f39.title: Particulate organic matter
17c9f3934f39.section: Terrestrial ecosystems > Role of POM in soils
17c9f3934f39.sentence: As it is decomposes, particulate organic matter provides much of the energy required by soil organisms as well as providing a steady release of nutrients into the soil environment.

c4263fb88e44.title: Particulate organic matter
c4263fb88e44.section: Terrestrial ecosystems > Role of POM in soils
c4263fb88e44.sentence: The amount of nutrients released (mineralized) during decomposition depends on the biological and chemical characteristics of the POM, such as the C:N ratio.

ff54c6d7b841.title: Particulate organic matter
ff54c6d7b841.section: Terrestrial ecosystems > Role of POM in soils
ff54c6d7b841.sentence: Fungal mycelium entangle soil particles and release sticky, cement-like, polysaccharides into the soil; ultimately forming soil aggregates

cb4792c93643.title: Particulate organic matter
cb4792c93643.sentence: POM also enhances soil structure leading to increased water infiltration, aeration and resistance to erosion.

a2bc5e94efe8.title: Particulate organic matter
a2bc5e94efe8.section: Terrestrial ecosystems > Role of POM in soils
a2bc5e94efe8.sentence: The addition of organic materials, such as manure or crop residues, typically results in an increase in POM.
