c4ae0ca95c7c.title: Particulate organic matter
c4ae0ca95c7c.section: Terrestrial ecosystems > Role of POM in soils
c4ae0ca95c7c.sentence: Alternatively, repeated tillage or soil disturbance increases the rate of decomposition by exposing soil organisms to oxygen and organic substrates; ultimately, depleting POM.

ab19e243e603.title: Particulate organic matter
ab19e243e603.section: Terrestrial ecosystems > Role of POM in soils
ab19e243e603.sentence: Reduction in POM content is observed when native grasslands are converted to agricultural land.

239509cc69f6.title: Particulate organic matter
239509cc69f6.section: Terrestrial ecosystems > Role of POM in soils
239509cc69f6.sentence: Because POM is a readily available (labile) source of soil nutrients, is a contributor to soil structure, and is highly sensitive to soil management, it is frequently used as an indicator to measure soil quality.

f69a5c5ab6b8.title: Particulate organic matter
f69a5c5ab6b8.sentence: In poorly managed soils, particularly on sloped ground, erosion and transport of soil sediment rich in POM can contaminate water bodies.

5698e889c62b.title: Particulate organic matter
5698e889c62b.sentence: Because POM provides a source of energy and nutrients, rapid build-up of organic matter in water can result in eutrophication.

892f4c5137c7.title: Humus
892f4c5137c7.sentence: Organisms which feed off the litter layer serve a key role in the formation of humus, known as humification.

7799fff5702e.title: Humus
7799fff5702e.sentence: The primary materials involved in the process of humification are plant detritus, dead animals and microbes (necromass), excreta of all soil organisms, and also black carbon resulting from past fires.

09c8b202a317.title: Humus
09c8b202a317.sentence: Organic matter is humified by a combination of saprotrophic fungi, bacteria, microbes and animals such as earthworms, nematodes, protozoa, and arthropods (see Soil biology and Soil animals).

9f8af1d0e815.title: Humus
9f8af1d0e815.sentence: Earthworms are a major contributor to this process, alongside many other invertebrates, microbial processes, and fungi.

742045d18247.title: Humus
742045d18247.sentence: Decay in the soil begins with the decomposition of sugars and starches from carbohydrates, which decompose easily as detritivores initially invade the dead plant organs, while the remaining cellulose and lignin decompose more slowly.

43e8a885989e.title: Humus
43e8a885989e.sentence: Simple proteins, organic acids, starches, and sugars decompose rapidly, while crude proteins, fats, waxes, and resins remain relatively unchanged for longer periods of time.

ddd1eb78f78a.title: Humus
ddd1eb78f78a.sentence: Lignin, which is quickly transformed by white-rot fungi, is one of the primary precursors of humus, together with by-products of microbial and animal activity.

35ab992c1145.title: Soil organic matter
35ab992c1145.sentence: As vegetal detritus decomposes, some microbially resistant compounds are let undecayed, including modified lignins, oils, fats, and waxes.

7598bfeb2d8c.title: Soil organic matter
7598bfeb2d8c.sentence: Secondly, some new compounds are synthesized, like polysaccharides and polyuronids.

15208f81751d.title: Soil organic matter
15208f81751d.sentence: These compounds are the basis of humus.

0babc4b7e636.title: Soil organic matter
0babc4b7e636.sentence: New reactions occur between these compounds and some proteins and other products that contain nitrogen, thus incorporating nitrogen and avoiding its mineralization.

9e23ef7fde27.title: Soil organic matter
9e23ef7fde27.sentence: Other nutrients are also protected in this way from mineralization.

531ac344877f.title: Humus
531ac344877f.sentence: Prior to modern analytical methods, early evidence led scientists to believe that humification resulted in concatenations of organic polymers resistant to the action of microorganisms, however recent research has demonstrated that microorganisms are capable of digesting humic substances in Redox reactions.

6403c72615a3.title: Humus
6403c72615a3.sentence: Humification can occur naturally in soil or artificially in the production of compost.

03fddc274e94.title: Chernozem
03fddc274e94.sentence: Humification can darken soils (melanization) even in the absence of a pyrogenic carbon component.

8da8206559af.title: Soil
8da8206559af.sentence: In the aim to sequester more carbon in the soil for alleviating the greenhouse effect it would be more efficient in the long-term to stimulate humification than to decrease litter decomposition.

71253e8cdc69.title: Humus
71253e8cdc69.sentence: The most useful functions of humus are in improving soil structure, all the more when associated with cations (e.g. calcium), and in providing a very large surface area that can hold nutrient elements until required by plants, an ion exchange function comparable to that of clay particles.

28587a638151.title: Humus
28587a638151.sentence: While these nutrient cations are available to plants, they are held in the soil and prevented from being leached by rain or irrigation.

d518cbf1ac20.title: Humus
d518cbf1ac20.sentence: The incorporation of oxygen into large organic molecular assemblages generates many active, negatively charged sites that bind to positively charged ions (cations) of plant nutrients, making them more available to the plant by way of ion exchange.

8155ecf69657.title: Soil organic matter
8155ecf69657.sentence: Humus has a high cation and anion exchange capacity that on a dry weight basis is many times greater than that of clay colloids.

73e017908720.title: Humus
73e017908720.sentence: - Humus can hold the equivalent of 80–90% of its weight in moisture and therefore increases the soil's capacity to withstand drought.

df05faab0ae3.title: Humus
df05faab0ae3.sentence: It helps the soil retain moisture by increasing microporosity and encourages the formation of good soil structure.

83f128b63cc6.title: Humus
83f128b63cc6.sentence: - During humification, microbes secrete sticky, gum-like mucilages; these contribute to the crumby structure (tilth) of the soil by adhering particles together and allowing greater aeration of the soil.

b00c1e00b12b.title: Humus
b00c1e00b12b.sentence: - The biochemical structure of humus enables it to moderate, i.e. buffer, excessive acidic or alkaline soil conditions.

32773ec5701d.title: Humus
32773ec5701d.sentence: Toxic substances such as heavy metals and excess nutrients can be chelated, i.e., bound to the organic molecules of humus, and so prevented from leaching away.

14dad7b968b3.title: Humus
14dad7b968b3.sentence: - The dark, usually brown or black, color of humus helps to warm cold soils in spring.

11cf83c1793b.title: Humus
11cf83c1793b.sentence: The ability of plants to absorb humic substances with their roots and metabolize them has been long debated.

fb791454364f.title: Humus
fb791454364f.sentence: There is now a consensus that humus functions hormonally rather than simply nutritionally in plant physiology, and that organic substances exuded by roots and transformed in humus by soil organisms are an evolved strategy by which plants "talk" to the soil.

ba3dd8506924.title: Humus
ba3dd8506924.sentence: The importance of chemically stable humus is thought by some to be the fertility it provides to soils in both a physical and chemical sense, though some agricultural experts put a greater focus on other features of it, such as its ability to control diseases.

0b19f8150fea.title: Humus
0b19f8150fea.sentence: Some judge earthworm humus (vermicompost) to be the optimal organic manure.

ca5ca70bed68.title: Humus
ca5ca70bed68.sentence: Most humus that is not protected in this way is decomposed within 10 years and can be regarded as less stable or more labile.

166cb7e16a65.title: Humus
166cb7e16a65.sentence: The mixing activity of soil-consuming invertebrates (e.g. earthworms, termites, some millipedes) contribute to the stability of humus by favouring the formation of mineral-organic complexes with clay minerals at the inside of their guts, hence more carbon sequestration in humus forms such as mull and amphi, with well-developed mineral-organic horizons, when compared with moder and mor where most organic matter accumulates at the soil surface.

33fd887229f7.title: Humus
33fd887229f7.sentence: Stable humus contributes few plant-available nutrients in soil, but it helps maintain its physical structure.

f71289db0f93.title: Humus
f71289db0f93.sentence: - "Effective humus" and "stable humus" are additional sources of nutrients for microbes: the former provides a readily available supply, and the latter acts as a long-term storage reservoir.

d814f4cc0277.title: Soil organic matter
d814f4cc0277.sentence: However, humus in its most stable forms (often called 'humin') may persist over centuries if not millennia.

ba6369e6072d.title: Soil organic matter
ba6369e6072d.sentence: Humus is less stable than the soil's mineral constituents, as it is reduced by microbial decomposition, and over time its concentration diminishes without the addition of new organic matter.

bdb7e7bd8040.title: Humus
bdb7e7bd8040.sentence: A very stable form of humus is formed from the slow oxidation of soil carbon after the incorporation of finely powdered charcoal into the topsoil, suggested to result from the grinding and mixing activity of a tropical earthworm.

89b47698db63.title: Humus
89b47698db63.sentence: This process is speculated to have been important in the formation of the unusually fertile Amazonian terra preta do Indio, also called Amazonian Dark Earths.

c1bfee9fc1a6.title: Humus
c1bfee9fc1a6.sentence: Only when it becomes stable and acquires its multi-century permanence, mostly via multiple interactions with the soil matrix, should molecular soil humus be considered to be of significance in removing the atmosphere's current carbon dioxide overload.

7ea740c40ba6.title: Carbon sink
7ea740c40ba6.sentence: Leaf litter and humus are rapidly oxidized and poorly retained in sub-tropical and tropical climate conditions due to high temperatures and extensive leaching by rainfall.

c27aeebae54c.title: Saprotroph
c27aeebae54c.sentence: A saprotroph is an organism that feeds on dead organic matter or waste by excreting chemicals to digest it, rather than eating it directly (as detritivores do).

d4ad81900dcd.title: Saprotroph
d4ad81900dcd.sentence: Saprotrophic digestion is most often performed by fungi (e.g. Mucor) and soil bacteria.

cdc31ca0bba2.title: Saprotroph
cdc31ca0bba2.sentence: Microscopic saprotrophs are sometimes called saprobes.

b1ed9de228d7.title: Saprotroph
b1ed9de228d7.sentence: - Proteins are broken down into their amino acid composites through the breaking of peptide bonds by proteases.

0cdd5d64a64f.title: Saprotroph
0cdd5d64a64f.sentence: - Lipids are broken down into fatty acids and glycerol by lipases.

f780bed52c57.title: Saprotroph
f780bed52c57.sentence: - Starch is broken down into pieces of simple disaccharides by amylases.

687fcb1c051f.title: Saprotroph
687fcb1c051f.sentence: - Cellulose, a major portion of plant cells, and therefore a major constituent of decaying matter is broken down into glucose.

adb64be3e606.title: Saprotroph
adb64be3e606.sentence: These products are re-absorbed into the hypha through the cell wall by endocytosis and passed on throughout the mycelium complex.

f2d012630172.title: Saprotroph
f2d012630172.sentence: This facilitates the passage of such materials throughout the organism and allows for growth and, if necessary, repair.

bb0816c24828.title: Saprotroph
bb0816c24828.sentence: - Presence of water: 80–90% of the mass of the fungi is water, and the fungi require excess water for absorption due to the evaporation of internally retained water.

4b89a650f466.title: Saprotroph
4b89a650f466.sentence: - Presence of oxygen: Very few saprotrophic organisms can endure anaerobic conditions as evidenced by their growth above media such as water or soil.

33ecfffb63f4.title: Saprotroph
33ecfffb63f4.sentence: - Neutral-acidic pH: The condition of neutral or mildly acidic conditions under pH 7 are required.

8abc859a04e6.title: Saprotroph
8abc859a04e6.sentence: - Low-medium temperature: The majority of saprotrophic organisms require temperatures between 1 and 35 °C (34 and 95 °F), with optimum growth occurring at 25 °C (77 °F).

f59cffef4708.title: Mycoremediation
f59cffef4708.sentence: Fungi are amongst the primary saprotrophic organisms in an ecosystem, as they are efficient in the decomposition of matter.

d4f63ab14c47.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
d4f63ab14c47.sentence: - Mycorrhizal fungi developed from saprobic fungi that became endosymbiotic.

ecd79ed6fe4c.title: Ectomycorrhiza
ecd79ed6fe4c.sentence: Molecular and phylogenetic analyses of fungal lineages suggest that EcM fungi have evolved and persisted numerous times from non-EcM ancestors such as humus and wood saprotrophic fungi.

1a16bf476f17.title: Saprotroph
1a16bf476f17.sentence: The Royal Horticultural Society states that saprotrophs recycle nutrients and therefore should be left in gardens if possible.

2a0459376ae8.title: Plant litter
2a0459376ae8.sentence: Litterfall is the dominant pathway for nutrient return to the soil, especially for nitrogen (N) and phosphorus (P).

e2ddcf03b964.title: Plant litter
e2ddcf03b964.section: Habitat and food > Detritivores and other decomposers
e2ddcf03b964.sentence: The consumption of the litterfall by decomposers results in the breakdown of simple carbon compounds into carbon dioxide (CO2) and water (H2O), and releases inorganic ions (like nitrogen and phosphorus) into the soil where the surrounding plants can then reabsorb the nutrients that were shed as litterfall.

b8a51fd63465.title: Plant litter
b8a51fd63465.sentence: During leaf senescence, a portion of the plant's nutrients are reabsorbed from the leaves.

a54d676b9d66.title: Plant litter
a54d676b9d66.sentence: Plants that grow in areas with low nutrient availability tend to produce litter with low nutrient concentrations, as a larger proportion of the available nutrients is reabsorbed.

12c4afa4d92f.title: Plant litter
12c4afa4d92f.sentence: Once the litterfall has settled, decomposition of the litter layer, accomplished through the leaching of nutrients by rainfall and throughfall and by the efforts of detritivores, releases the breakdown products into the soil below and therefore contributes to the cation exchange capacity of the soil.

e76d25d8a3a7.title: Plant litter
e76d25d8a3a7.sentence: This holds especially true for highly weathered tropical soils.

2a059c7546a7.title: Plant litter
2a059c7546a7.sentence: Leaching is the process by which cations such as iron (Fe) and aluminum (Al), as well as organic matter are removed from the litterfall and transported downward into the soil below.

2ff0968e41ac.title: Plant litter
2ff0968e41ac.sentence: Litterfall containing high nutrient concentrations will decompose more rapidly and asymptote as those nutrients decrease.

70e9cfce2f84.title: Plant litter
70e9cfce2f84.sentence: Knowing this, ecologists have been able to use nutrient concentrations as measured by remote sensing as an index of a potential rate of decomposition for any given area.

bfdc0000f64a.title: Plant litter
bfdc0000f64a.sentence: annual storage of nutrients in plant tissues + replacement of losses from litterfall and leaching = the amount of uptake in an ecosystem

01ce4801dc67.title: Plant litter
01ce4801dc67.sentence: Fungus plays a large role in cycling the nutrients from the plant litter back into the ecosystem.

a08f5a533260.title: Forest floor
a08f5a533260.sentence: The forest floor, also called detritus or duff, is the part of a forest ecosystem that mediates between the living, aboveground portion of the forest and the mineral/humus-rich soil, principally composed of decaying plant litter and other dead plant matters such as coarse woody debris.

4cb9435ed284.title: Forest floor
4cb9435ed284.sentence: In some countries, like Canada, forest floor refers to L, F and H organic horizons [jargon].

8f78ed313a56.title: Forest floor
8f78ed313a56.sentence: The F horizon consists of plant material in which decomposition is apparent, but the origins of plant residues are still distinguishable.

3f34839a7c9e.title: Forest floor
3f34839a7c9e.sentence: The H horizon consists of well-decomposed plant material so that plant residues are not recognizable, with the exception of some roots or wood.

831eebf2c661.title: Forest floor
831eebf2c661.sentence: Some specialists consider this zone to be equivalent to the soil horizon (O) whereas for others, this only includes the humus and the intermediate layer, excluding the litter.

48c54a3682e6.title: Forest floor
48c54a3682e6.sentence: It hosts a wide variety of decomposers and predators, including invertebrates, fungi, algae, bacteria, and archaea.

c350ff1807f6.title: Forest floor
c350ff1807f6.sentence: The forest floor serves as a bridge between the above ground living vegetation and the soil, and thus is a crucial component in nutrient transfer through the biogeochemical cycle.

dfdadb5aba1c.title: Forest floor
dfdadb5aba1c.sentence: Much of the energy and carbon fixed by forests is periodically added to the forest floor through litterfall, and a substantial portion of the nutrient requirements of forest ecosystems is supplied by decomposition of organic matter in the forest floor and soil surface.

f29699783804.title: Forest floor
f29699783804.sentence: The amount of material in the forest floor depends on the balance between inputs from litter production and outputs from decomposition, and amounts also reflect the site's disturbance history.

47d67d846c29.title: Forest floor
47d67d846c29.sentence: Both litter production and decomposition are functions of the site (e.g., wet versus dry; cold versus warm; nutrient rich versus nutrient poor) and the vegetation that occupies the site (e.g., conifer versus broadleaf).

67f909658c8c.title: Forest floor
67f909658c8c.sentence: Typically, forest floors are heaviest and deepest in boreal forests and mountain forests where decomposition rates are slow.

d75daee71c8f.title: Forest floor
d75daee71c8f.sentence: The lush vegetation is made possible by the abundance and rapid action of termites, millipedes and other organisms, which break down organic matter and promptly consign it to the mycorrhizal network.

b6e7335dfa1d.title: Forest floor
b6e7335dfa1d.sentence: Therefore, the leaf litter layer of tropical forests may be considerably less apparent, or virtually absent at certain times of the year.

a155018abca2.title: Forest floor
a155018abca2.sentence: The forest floor is also an important fuel source in forest fires.

962de7b999c7.title: Ectomycorrhiza
962de7b999c7.sentence: In one study concerning Douglas-fir seedlings, removal of forest floor debris and soil compaction decreased EcM fungal diversity and abundance by 60%.

d2410a17ccf2.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.02%3A_Natural_Factors
d2410a17ccf2.sentence: Traveling from north to south, higher average temperatures lead to less soil organic matter.

924268dd34f1.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.02%3A_Natural_Factors
924268dd34f1.sentence: As the climate gets warmer, two things tend to happen (as long as rainfall is sufficient): More vegetation is produced because the growing season is longer, and the rate of decomposition of organic materials in soils increases because soil organisms work more rapidly and are active for longer periods of the year at higher temperatures.

6531e6495163.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.02%3A_Natural_Factors
6531e6495163.sentence: Faster decomposition with warmer temperatures becomes the dominant influence determining soil organic matter levels.

d636e18c3fba.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.02%3A_Natural_Factors
d636e18c3fba.sentence: In the arctic and alpine regions there is not a lot of organic matter added to soils each year because of the very short season during which plants can grow.

fd07a71f5182.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.02%3A_Natural_Factors
fd07a71f5182.sentence: But arctic soils have high levels of organic matter because of the extremely slow decomposition rate caused by cold (and freezing) temperatures.

2a02499b4e8f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.02%3A_Natural_Factors
2a02499b4e8f.sentence: However, with the Arctic’s temperature increasing and with the thawing of frozen soils, organic matter can be rapidly lost as microorganisms use it to live and give off CO2 during their respiration.

f5f366d6b25a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.02%3A_Natural_Factors
f5f366d6b25a.sentence: Another greenhouse gas trapped in these soils, methane (CH4), is also being lost to the atmosphere.

7be72acb2c2c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.02%3A_Natural_Factors
7be72acb2c2c.sentence: Soils in arid climates usually have low amounts of organic matter.

cbe85e96e0bf.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.02%3A_Natural_Factors
cbe85e96e0bf.sentence: In a very dry climate, such as a desert, there is little growth of vegetation.

43b82c417bcc.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.02%3A_Natural_Factors
43b82c417bcc.sentence: Decomposition is also low because of low amounts of organic inputs and low microorganism activity when the soil is dry.

c9c2ecc7569a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.02%3A_Natural_Factors
c9c2ecc7569a.sentence: When it finally rains, a very rapid burst of decomposition of soil organic matter occurs.

f8670d3d57e2.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.02%3A_Natural_Factors
f8670d3d57e2.sentence: Soil organic matter levels generally increase as average annual precipitation increases.

3c99c1fd5b5c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.02%3A_Natural_Factors
3c99c1fd5b5c.sentence: With more rainfall, more water is available to plants, and more plant growth results.

fc986f7ef620.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.02%3A_Natural_Factors
fc986f7ef620.sentence: As rainfall increases, more residues return to the soil from grasses or trees.

af48baa3f048.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.02%3A_Natural_Factors
af48baa3f048.sentence: At the same time, soils in high rainfall areas may have less organic matter decomposition than well-aerated soils.

0f9c1db43e3b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.02%3A_Natural_Factors
0f9c1db43e3b.sentence: Decomposition is slowed by restricted aeration.

da86cb6fc359.title: Soil organic matter
da86cb6fc359.sentence: Temperature, soil moisture and topography are the major factors affecting the accumulation of organic matter in soils.

4749898108ff.title: Soil organic matter
4749898108ff.sentence: Organic matter tends to accumulate under wet or cold conditions where decomposer activity is impeded by low temperature or excess moisture which results in anaerobic conditions.

670dbcd59763.title: Soil organic matter
670dbcd59763.sentence: Conversely, excessive rain and high temperatures of tropical climates enable rapid decomposition of organic matter and leaching of plant nutrients.

f4189b0f43e1.title: Soil organic matter
f4189b0f43e1.sentence: Forest ecosystems on these soils rely on efficient recycling of nutrients and plant matter by the living plant and microbial biomass to maintain their productivity, a process which is disturbed by human activities.

80a4f9b0b520.title: Soil organic matter
80a4f9b0b520.sentence: Excessive slope, in particular in the presence of cultivation for the sake of agriculture, may encourage the erosion of the top layer of soil which holds most of the raw organic material that would otherwise eventually become humus.

306d05ac56f5.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/02%3A_What_Is_Organic_Matter_and_Why_Is_It_So_Important/2.03%3A_Organic_Matter_And_Natural_Cycles
306d05ac56f5.sentence: Carbon dioxide is removed from the atmosphere by plants and used to make all the organic molecules necessary for life.

245e5f068185.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/02%3A_What_Is_Organic_Matter_and_Why_Is_It_So_Important/2.03%3A_Organic_Matter_And_Natural_Cycles
245e5f068185.sentence: Sunlight provides plants with the energy they need to carry out this process.

8d46d0fa4d3c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/02%3A_What_Is_Organic_Matter_and_Why_Is_It_So_Important/2.03%3A_Organic_Matter_And_Natural_Cycles
8d46d0fa4d3c.sentence: Plants, as well as the animals feeding on plants, release carbon dioxide back into the atmosphere as they use organic molecules for energy.

dab20464f1d0.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/02%3A_What_Is_Organic_Matter_and_Why_Is_It_So_Important/2.03%3A_Organic_Matter_And_Natural_Cycles
dab20464f1d0.sentence: Carbon dioxide is also released to the atmosphere when fuels, such as gas, oil, coal and wood are burned.

30561cb64f2b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/02%3A_What_Is_Organic_Matter_and_Why_Is_It_So_Important/2.03%3A_Organic_Matter_And_Natural_Cycles
30561cb64f2b.section: The Carbon Cycle > Color and Organic Matter
30561cb64f2b.sentence: Soils are amassing the cumulative carbon and nutrient capture from plant production, and the largest amount of carbon present on the land is not in the living plants but is instead stored in soil organic matter.

34697eb58fda.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/02%3A_What_Is_Organic_Matter_and_Why_Is_It_So_Important/2.03%3A_Organic_Matter_And_Natural_Cycles
34697eb58fda.section: The Carbon Cycle > Color and Organic Matter
34697eb58fda.sentence: Soil organic matter contains an estimated four times as much carbon as living plants, and in fact carbon stored in all the world’s soils is two to three times the amount in the atmosphere.

fd42f0361a35.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/02%3A_What_Is_Organic_Matter_and_Why_Is_It_So_Important/2.03%3A_Organic_Matter_And_Natural_Cycles
fd42f0361a35.section: The Carbon Cycle > Color and Organic Matter
fd42f0361a35.sentence: There is as much carbon in seven inches of a soil with 1% organic matter as there is in the atmosphere above a field.

c380e29df566.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/02%3A_What_Is_Organic_Matter_and_Why_Is_It_So_Important/2.03%3A_Organic_Matter_And_Natural_Cycles
c380e29df566.section: The Carbon Cycle > Color and Organic Matter
c380e29df566.sentence: As soil organic matter is depleted, it becomes a source of carbon dioxide for the atmosphere.

9294a3bfe3b0.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/02%3A_What_Is_Organic_Matter_and_Why_Is_It_So_Important/2.03%3A_Organic_Matter_And_Natural_Cycles
9294a3bfe3b0.section: The Carbon Cycle > Color and Organic Matter
9294a3bfe3b0.sentence: Also, when forests are cleared and burned, a large amount of carbon dioxide is released.

e334e5e19b2d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/02%3A_What_Is_Organic_Matter_and_Why_Is_It_So_Important/2.03%3A_Organic_Matter_And_Natural_Cycles
e334e5e19b2d.section: The Carbon Cycle > Color and Organic Matter
e334e5e19b2d.sentence: A secondary, often larger flush of carbon dioxide is emitted from soil through the rapid depletion of soil organic matter following conversion of forests to agricultural practices.

f18928923a86.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/02%3A_What_Is_Organic_Matter_and_Why_Is_It_So_Important/2.03%3A_Organic_Matter_And_Natural_Cycles
f18928923a86.section: The Carbon Cycle > Climate Change and Soils
f18928923a86.sentence: The historical conversion of forests and grasslands to farming was responsible for a large transfer of carbon (from accelerated soil organic matter decomposition) into the atmosphere as CO2.

843e25ccda1e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/02%3A_What_Is_Organic_Matter_and_Why_Is_It_So_Important/2.03%3A_Organic_Matter_And_Natural_Cycles
843e25ccda1e.section: The Carbon Cycle > Climate Change and Soils
843e25ccda1e.sentence: This agricultural conversion is second to the burning of fossil fuels as the largest contributor to increasing atmospheric CO2 concentrations (remember, fossil fuels are derived from carbon stored in ancient plants).

c5edc9bc2fa8.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/02%3A_What_Is_Organic_Matter_and_Why_Is_It_So_Important/2.03%3A_Organic_Matter_And_Natural_Cycles
c5edc9bc2fa8.section: The Carbon Cycle > Climate Change and Soils
c5edc9bc2fa8.sentence: But soils managed in ways that build up organic matter can become net sinks for carbon storage and can enhance their health at the same time.

dca647c8e1db.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/02%3A_What_Is_Organic_Matter_and_Why_Is_It_So_Important/2.03%3A_Organic_Matter_And_Natural_Cycles
dca647c8e1db.section: The Carbon Cycle > Climate Change and Soils
dca647c8e1db.sentence: Increasing soil organic matter is no silver bullet for combating climate change, but it can help to slow the increase in CO2 for a while if done on a massive scale all over the world.

c206a60c4bc0.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/02%3A_What_Is_Organic_Matter_and_Why_Is_It_So_Important/2.03%3A_Organic_Matter_And_Natural_Cycles
c206a60c4bc0.section: The Carbon Cycle > Climate Change and Soils
c206a60c4bc0.sentence: It offers win-win outcomes because higher levels of organic matter also increase resilience of soils that are being confronted with the more intense storms and dry periods resulting from a warming planet with increasingly destabilized weather patterns.

24f4a0ca249c.title: Soil organic matter
24f4a0ca249c.sentence: Soil has a crucial function in the global carbon cycle, with the global soil carbon pool estimated to be 2,500 gigatons.

c015eab6631d.title: Soil organic matter
c015eab6631d.sentence: This is 3.3 times the amount of the atmospheric pool at 750 gigatons and 4.5 times the biotic pool at 560 gigatons.

4cc45799527f.title: Soil organic matter
4cc45799527f.sentence: The pool of organic carbon, which occurs primarily in the form of SOM, accounts for approximately 1,550 gigatons of the total global carbon pool, with soil inorganic carbon (SIC, mainly made of carbonates and bicarbonates) accounting for the remainder.

97d21dc45910.title: Decomposer
97d21dc45910.sentence: Decomposers are organisms that break down dead organisms and release the nutrients from the dead matter into the environment around them.

c6edee2e0b99.title: Decomposer
c6edee2e0b99.sentence: The term "decomposer" refers to a role in an ecosystem, not to a particular class or type of organism, or even to a specific capacity of those organisms.

34df088a38eb.title: Decomposer
34df088a38eb.sentence: The definition of "decomposer" therefore centers on the outcome of the decomposition process, rather than the types of organisms performing it.

7ec1d7d0a787.title: Decomposer
7ec1d7d0a787.sentence: "Decomposer" as a category, therefore, would include not just fungi and bacteria, which perform external digestion, but also invertebrates such as earthworms, woodlice, and sea cucumbers that digest dead matter internally and release nutrients locally via their feces.

76c6ce0b66bf.title: Decomposer
76c6ce0b66bf.sentence: "Detritivore" describes behavior and physiology, while "decomposer" describes an ecosystem role.

e5e8937540d4.title: Decomposer
e5e8937540d4.sentence: Therefore, an organism can be both a detritivore and a decomposer.

45632e187a62.title: Decomposer
45632e187a62.sentence: At the center of this definition are the organisms that benefit most directly from the increase in nutrient availability that results from decomposition; plants and other non-mobile (sessile) autotrophs cannot travel to seek out nutrients, and most cannot digest other organisms themselves.

563d815dcb1d.title: Decomposer
563d815dcb1d.sentence: They must therefore rely on decomposers to free up nutrients from dead matter that they can then absorb.

21c7b9227af0.title: Decomposer
21c7b9227af0.sentence: In terrestrial environments, decomposition happens mainly in or on soil, and decomposers' activities lead to increased soil fertility.

98d555e7ff2e.title: Decomposer
98d555e7ff2e.sentence: Some steps of the process occur via mechanical grinding and churning by things like earthworms and plant roots in a process called bioturbation.

381f7b16a9c2.title: Decomposer
381f7b16a9c2.sentence: Further breakdown, beyond those physical means, requires the presence of enzymes.

a7e77a5a5229.title: Decomposer
a7e77a5a5229.sentence: Enzymes for the digestion of molecules like fats, proteins, and starch are widespread and many organisms, from microbes to mammals, have them.

b613523b99bd.title: Decomposer
b613523b99bd.sentence: As a result, those molecules are the first to decompose in the environment.

8c0db471b3b4.title: Decomposer
8c0db471b3b4.sentence: Cellulose in dead plants is broken down by cellulase enzymes, which are present in far fewer organisms, and the enzymes needed to digest lignin, a chemically complex molecule in woody trees and shrubs, in fewer still.

c3225cc82f35.title: Decomposer
c3225cc82f35.sentence: The primary decomposer of litter in many ecosystems is fungi.

70233bea9893.title: Decomposer
70233bea9893.sentence: Bacteria are restricted to growing and feeding on the exposed surfaces of organic matter, but fungi can use their hyphae to penetrate larger pieces of organic matter below the surface.

1a81431dc343.title: Decomposer
1a81431dc343.sentence: Additionally, only wood-decay fungi have evolved lignin-modifying enzymes necessary to decompose lignin.

482d3eea91bf.title: Decomposer
482d3eea91bf.sentence: These two factors make fungi the primary decomposers in forests, where litter has high concentrations of lignin and often occurs in large pieces like fallen trees and branches.

a3d05738fe73.title: Humus form
a3d05738fe73.sentence: Humus form is the features of the topsoil and plant litter in a biome, such as mull humus form in deciduous forest or mor humus form in coniferous forest.

0b39686629a3.title: Humus form
0b39686629a3.sentence: Canadian Ministry of Forests (British Columbia): "The humus form is defined as a group of soil horizons located at or near the surface of a pedon, which have formed from organic residues, either separate from, or intermixed with mineral materials."

dcc485c8929d.title: Humus form
dcc485c8929d.sentence: Five humus systems have been described in terrestrial environments: mull, moder, mor, amphi, and tangel.

3b54ae1e205b.title: Humus form
3b54ae1e205b.sentence: Terrestrial humus forms are found in forests, woodlands, grasslands, heathlands, steppes, tundras, deserts and semi-deserts.

0a7417ba39d9.title: Humus form
0a7417ba39d9.sentence: Horizons that may comprise a humus form include L, F, H, and Ah, but not B or C."

d42631ad2b6a.title: Humus form
d42631ad2b6a.sentence: Humus form is important in ecosystem management, such as forest management, as it influences a forest's ability to regenerate through the establishment of new saplings and seedlings.

dec2e3c16d44.title: Humus form
dec2e3c16d44.section: Humus forms in a changing world > Vegetation dynamics
dec2e3c16d44.sentence: Forest regeneration, that is, the ability of juvenile forms of trees (seedlings, seedlings) to establish themselves successfully, relies to a large extent on the humus form.

c39096b5e11a.title: Humus form
c39096b5e11a.sentence: One of the key principles of humus form classifications is that humus profiles (humipedons) may evolve at a different rate from soil profiles (pedons).

d2fb680634c7.title: Humus form
d2fb680634c7.sentence: Given the prominent part taken by soil organisms, from bacteria to mammals, passing by plants and invertebrates, in the spatial arrangement and transformation of organic matter, humipedons display pluri-annual variations, while pedon changes take decades to centuries.

d2823362831f.title: Humus form
d2823362831f.sentence: Most classifications of humus are national (French, Belgian, German, Canadian, Russian, among many others) and do not embrace the variety of humus forms found over all world biomes, being mostly focused on forest soils and temperate climates.

799fb591d03f.title: Humus form
799fb591d03f.sentence: Early contributions to the knowledge of humus forms were made by Peter Erasmus Müller, a Danish forester.

ca51808da38e.title: Humus form
ca51808da38e.sentence: In his seminal contribution Studier over Skovjord: som bidrag til skovdyrkningens theori, later translated into German and French, Müller described muld (later germanized as mull) and mor, two modes of assemblage of organic and mineral matter, which he associated to two opposite classes of high and low productivity and soil fertility of Danish beechwoods.

2d624f03190a.title: Humus form
2d624f03190a.sentence: Moder was later added as a third forest humus form by Franz Hartmann, midway between mull and mor and previously described as 'insect mull' by Müller.

cce841d23c79.title: Humus form
cce841d23c79.sentence: At the same time Charles Darwin, one year before he died, published a detailed study of the formation of mull (called by him mould, reminiscent of the Danish muld).

63ed567132c3.title: Humus form
63ed567132c3.sentence: The humus forms present in peat bogs and marshes, due to their great variety, are subject to complex classifications, taking into account the stage of evolution towards terrestrial forms, depending on depth of the water table, its variations during the year and the nature of the dominant vegetation (sphagnum or herbaceous plants).

683368bddbab.title: Plant litter
683368bddbab.sentence: Litter provides habitat for a variety of organisms.

bb163eb90f20.title: Plant litter
bb163eb90f20.section: Habitat and food > Detritivores and other decomposers
bb163eb90f20.sentence: A litter layer of decomposing biomass provides a continuous energy source for macro- and micro-organisms.

c22c4f2aef1e.title: Plant litter
c22c4f2aef1e.section: Habitat and food > Detritivores and other decomposers
c22c4f2aef1e.sentence: Many organisms that live on the forest floor are decomposers, such as fungi.

97f600fb0478.title: Plant litter
97f600fb0478.section: Habitat and food > Detritivores and other decomposers
97f600fb0478.sentence: The community of decomposers in the litter layer also includes bacteria, amoeba, nematodes, rotifer, tardigrades, springtails, cryptostigmata, potworms, insect larvae, mollusks, oribatid mites, woodlice, and millipedes.

0ba7039161b8.title: Plant litter
0ba7039161b8.sentence: Certain plants are specially adapted for germinating and thriving in the litter layers.

64d965ccb7d4.title: Plant litter
64d965ccb7d4.sentence: For example, bluebell (Hyacinthoides non-scripta) shoots puncture the layer to emerge in spring.

bc89b496e87c.title: Plant litter
bc89b496e87c.sentence: Some plants with rhizomes, such as common wood sorrel (Oxalis acetosella) do well in this habitat.

a4eba1fcfcef.title: Plant litter
a4eba1fcfcef.sentence: Amphibians such as salamanders and caecilians inhabit the damp microclimate underneath fallen leaves for part or all of their life cycle.

6af4aa3eb3a9.title: Plant litter
6af4aa3eb3a9.sentence: Some species of birds, such as the ovenbird of eastern North America for example, require leaf litter for both foraging and material for nests.

44e92ab46230.title: Plant litter
44e92ab46230.sentence: Sometimes litterfall even provides energy to much larger mammals, such as in boreal forests where lichen litterfall is one of the main constituents of wintering deer and elk diets.

150474ce737d.title: Plant litter
150474ce737d.sentence: Researchers have described this continual replenishment of edible fragments as the "manna effect", a process that helps sustain caribou during periods when other food sources are buried under deep snow.

0dea05187b21.title: Plant litter
0dea05187b21.sentence: A litterbag is simply any type of container that can be set out in any given area for a specified amount of time to collect the plant litter that falls from the canopy above.

c9ae0cff0b74.title: Plant litter
c9ae0cff0b74.sentence: By confining fresh litter in the mesh bags and placing them on the ground, an ecologist can monitor and collect the decay measurements of that litter.

960b0df7be13.title: Plant litter
960b0df7be13.sentence: Litterbags are generally set in random locations within a given area and marked with GPS or local coordinates, and then monitored on a specific time interval.

c6fcf340d190.title: Plant litter
c6fcf340d190.sentence: When measuring bulk litterfall for an area, ecologists will weigh the dry contents of the litterbag.

d5162f891774.title: Plant litter
d5162f891774.sentence: litterfall (kg m−2 yr−1) = total litter mass (kg) / litterbag area (m2)

d3e3c400ed9d.title: Plant litter
d3e3c400ed9d.sentence: The mass-balance approach is also utilized in these experiments and suggests that the decomposition for a given amount of time should equal the input of litterfall for that same amount of time.

b4c10ee51880.title: Plant litter
b4c10ee51880.sentence: For study various groups from edaphic fauna you need a different mesh sizes in the litterbags

1b02a85eefce.title: Lignin
1b02a85eefce.sentence: Lignin is a class of complex organic polymers that form key structural materials in the support tissues of most plants.

05bd72f48fd6.title: Lignin
05bd72f48fd6.sentence: Lignins are particularly important in the formation of cell walls, especially in wood and bark, because they lend rigidity and do not rot easily.

7fd1b4323361.title: Lignin
7fd1b4323361.sentence: Chemically, lignins are polymers made by the cross-linking of phenolic precursors.

e6302baed02a.title: Lignin
e6302baed02a.sentence: Lignin fills the spaces in the cell wall between cellulose, hemicellulose, and pectin components, especially in vascular and support tissues: xylem tracheids, vessel elements and sclereid cells.

b950690d31a0.title: Lignin
b950690d31a0.sentence: It is covalently linked to hemicellulose and therefore cross-links different plant polysaccharides, conferring mechanical strength to the cell wall and by extension the plant as a whole.

a1c3ac8e9dde.title: Lignin
a1c3ac8e9dde.sentence: Thus, lignin makes it possible for the plant's vascular tissue to conduct water efficiently.

105ede47afa3.title: Lignin
105ede47afa3.sentence: In contrast to other bio-polymers (e.g. proteins, DNA, and even cellulose), lignin resists degradation.

f9ba1c0cae96.title: Lignin
f9ba1c0cae96.sentence: It is immune to both acid- and base-catalyzed hydrolysis.

ce2fa80e29ed.title: Lignin
ce2fa80e29ed.sentence: Because it is cross-linked with the other cell wall components, lignin minimizes the accessibility of cellulose and hemicellulose to microbial enzymes (e.g. Steric hindrance), leading to a reduced digestibility of biomass.

34489181c880.title: Lignin
34489181c880.sentence: Well-studied ligninolytic enzymes are found in Phanerochaete chrysosporium and other white rot fungi.

f40cce4a8b90.title: Lignin
f40cce4a8b90.sentence: Most fungal lignin degradation involves secreted peroxidases.

4155e8af0577.title: Soil organic matter
4155e8af0577.sentence: Lignin undergoes very slow decomposition, mainly by white rot fungi and actinomycetes; its half-life under temperate conditions is about six months.

1eaaa5563420.title: Soil organic matter
1eaaa5563420.sentence: It also reacts with proteins, which further increases its resistance to decomposition, including enzymatic decomposition by microbes.

4053f210f131.title: Humus
4053f210f131.sentence: Fully formed humus is essentially a collection of very large and complex molecules formed in part from lignin and other polyphenolic molecules of the original plant material (foliage, wood, bark), in part from similar molecules that have been produced by microbes.

554e579e4d04.title: Humus
554e579e4d04.sentence: It is difficult to define humus precisely because it is a very complex substance which is still not fully understood.

75780e46470c.title: Humus
75780e46470c.sentence: According to the classical conception of Selman Waksman, long-time reported in most textbooks of soil science, humus is different from decomposing soil organic matter.

1f72c3f773b0.title: Humus
1f72c3f773b0.sentence: The latter looks rough and has visible remains of the original plant, animal or microbial matter, while fully humified humus, on the contrary, is amorphous and has a uniformly dark, spongy, and jelly-like appearance.

a1d3fdca5a5c.title: Humus
a1d3fdca5a5c.sentence: However, when examined under a light microscope, humus may reveal tiny plant, animal, and microbial remains that have been mechanically, but not chemically, degraded.

f46faf7e09b8.title: Humus
f46faf7e09b8.sentence: During decomposition processes these polyphenols are modified chemically so that they are able to join up with one another to form very large molecules.

7d986e1ab482.title: Humus
7d986e1ab482.sentence: Some parts of these molecules are modified in such a way that protein molecules, amino acids, and amino sugars are able to attach themselves to the polyphenol "base" molecule.

2d0ed8667dae.title: Humus
2d0ed8667dae.sentence: As protein contains both nitrogen and sulfur, this attachment gives humus a moderate content of these two important plant nutrients.

424818ab2c10.title: Humus
424818ab2c10.sentence: Radiocarbon and other dating techniques have shown that the polyphenolic base of humus (mostly lignin and black carbon) can be very old, but the protein and carbohydrate attachments much younger, while to the light of modern concepts and methods the situation appears much more complex and unpredictable than previously thought.

6055a430993a.title: Humus
6055a430993a.sentence: It seems that microbes are able to pull protein off humus molecules rather more readily than they are able to break the polyphenolic base molecule itself.

6e051da1c5e4.title: Humus
6e051da1c5e4.sentence: As protein is removed its place may be taken by younger protein, or this younger protein may attach itself to another part of the humus molecule.

3e0e4d9a8871.title: Humus
3e0e4d9a8871.sentence: Researchers in the 1940s and 1960s tried using chemical separation to analyze plant and humic compounds in forest and agricultural soils, but this proved impossible because extractants interacted with the analysed organic matter and created many artefacts.

466ce9d848d5.title: Detritus
466ce9d848d5.sentence: A characteristic type of food chain called the detritus cycle takes place involving detritus feeders (detritivores), detritus and the microorganisms that multiply on it.

6498167899c7.title: Detritus
6498167899c7.sentence: Micro- and macro-organisms that feed on it rapidly consume and absorb materials such as proteins, lipids, and sugars that are low in molecular weight, while other compounds such as complex carbohydrates are decomposed more slowly.

343d9fbdebcf.title: Detritus
343d9fbdebcf.sentence: Accordingly, simultaneous to microorganisms' decomposition of the materials of dead plants and animals is their assimilation of decomposed compounds to construct more of their biomass (i.e., to grow their own bodies).

f479203a16a6.title: Detritus
f479203a16a6.sentence: At first, this dung is a poor source of nutrition, and so univalves pay no attention to it, but after several days, microorganisms begin to multiply on it again, its nutritional balance improves, and so they eat it again.

25156d2b1e81.title: Detritus
25156d2b1e81.sentence: Through this process of eating the detritus many times over and harvesting the microorganisms from it, the detritus thins out, becomes fractured and becomes easier for the microorganisms to use, and so the complex carbohydrates are also steadily broken down and disappear over time.

ab6039b56521.title: Detritus
ab6039b56521.sentence: What is left behind by the detritivores is then further broken down and recycled by decomposers, such as bacteria and fungi.

32f9397adbbd.title: Detritus
32f9397adbbd.sentence: In practical terms, the most important constituents of detritus are complex carbohydrates, which are persistent (difficult to break down), and the microorganisms which multiply using these absorb carbon from the detritus, and materials such as nitrogen and phosphorus from the water in their environment to synthesise the components of their own cells.

2503d86fec50.title: Polysaccharide
2503d86fec50.sentence: Polysaccharides (/ˌpɒl.i.ˈsæk.ə.raɪd/; from Ancient Greek πολύς (polús) 'many, much' and σάκχαρ (sákkhar) 'sugar') are "compounds consisting of a large number of monosaccharides linked glycosidically".

3a2f16b61d11.title: Polysaccharide
3a2f16b61d11.sentence: Their structures range from linear to highly branched polymers.

bf3b3df01028.title: Polysaccharide
bf3b3df01028.sentence: Examples include storage polysaccharides such as starch, glycogen, and galactogen and structural polysaccharides such as hemicellulose and chitin.

3960f7b0db8e.title: Polysaccharide
3960f7b0db8e.sentence: Pectins are a family of complex polysaccharides that contain 1,4-linked α-D-galactosyl uronic acid residues.

5eed5948c7f9.title: Polysaccharide
5eed5948c7f9.sentence: The structural components of plants are formed primarily from cellulose.

e9d9ec437950.title: Polysaccharide
e9d9ec437950.sentence: Many organisms can easily break down starches into glucose.

9c95bb726c51.title: Polysaccharide
9c95bb726c51.sentence: By contrast, few organisms can metabolize cellulose.

f74a1c296fff.title: Polysaccharide
f74a1c296fff.sentence: Some bacteria and protists can metabolize these carbohydrate types.

3a138c3e1985.title: Polysaccharide
3a138c3e1985.sentence: Ruminants and termites, for example, use microorganisms to process cellulose.

09d58085e698.title: Polysaccharide
09d58085e698.sentence: Bacteria and many other microbes, including fungi and algae, often secrete polysaccharides to help them adhere to surfaces and to prevent them from drying out.

9b0f88ebca64.title: Biofilm
9b0f88ebca64.section: Origin and formation > Formation of biofilms
9b0f88ebca64.sentence: Polysaccharide matrices typically enclose bacterial biofilms.

da04dd3588a4.title: Polysaccharide
da04dd3588a4.sentence: Wood is largely cellulose and lignin, while paper and cotton are nearly pure cellulose.

baf902503a46.title: Polysaccharide
baf902503a46.sentence: Humans and many animals lack an enzyme to break the beta-linkages, so they do not digest cellulose.

7ccb2937b074.title: Polysaccharide
7ccb2937b074.sentence: Certain animals, such as termites can digest cellulose, because bacteria possessing the enzyme are present in their gut.

1f49d9326ade.title: Polysaccharide
1f49d9326ade.sentence: It biodegrades in the presence of enzymes called chitinases, secreted by microorganisms such as bacteria and fungi and produced by some plants.

170adff62d24.title: Polysaccharide
170adff62d24.sentence: Some of these microorganisms have receptors to simple sugars from the decomposition of chitin.

f75a14e01b36.title: Polysaccharide
f75a14e01b36.sentence: If chitin is detected, they then produce enzymes to digest it by cleaving the glycosidic bonds in order to convert it to simple sugars and ammonia.

581a745404cf.title: Polysaccharide
581a745404cf.sentence: Chemically, chitin is closely related to chitosan (a more water-soluble derivative of chitin).

dfe0ffac3816.title: Priming (microbiology)
dfe0ffac3816.sentence: Priming or a "priming effect" is said to occur when something that is added to soil or compost affects the rate of decomposition occurring on the soil organic matter (SOM), either positively or negatively.

63c85c2f8cde.title: Organic matter
63c85c2f8cde.sentence: The phenomenon is generally caused by either pulsed or continuous changes to inputs of fresh organic matter (FOM).

fbe0f521c4e6.title: Organic matter
fbe0f521c4e6.sentence: Priming effects usually result in an acceleration of mineralization due to a trigger such as the FOM inputs.

bd2074365935.title: Organic matter
bd2074365935.sentence: The cause of this increase in decomposition has often been attributed to an increase in microbial activity resulting from higher energy and nutrient availability released from the FOM.

597bf8145b87.title: Organic matter
597bf8145b87.sentence: Priming effects can be either positive or negative depending on the reaction of the soil with the added substance.

03c9dcd33bba.title: Organic matter
03c9dcd33bba.sentence: A positive priming effect results in the acceleration of mineralization while a negative priming effect results in immobilization, leading to N unavailability.

ff0b33ff0924.title: Priming (microbiology)
ff0b33ff0924.sentence: Fertilizers, plant litter, detritus, and carbohydrate exudates from living roots, can potentially positively or negatively prime SOM decomposition.

3597402f14e8.title: Organic matter
3597402f14e8.sentence: Other soil treatments, besides organic matter inputs, which lead to this short-term change in turnover rates, include "input of mineral fertilizer, exudation of organic substances by roots, mere mechanical treatment of soil or its drying and rewetting."

89e957bdb49e.title: Organic matter
89e957bdb49e.sentence: The turnover rate of SOM in these areas is at least one order of magnitude higher than the bulk soil.

b03ac60a1364.title: Organic matter
b03ac60a1364.sentence: - The priming effect can arise either instantaneously or very shortly (potentially days or weeks) after the addition of a substance is made to the soil.

bfebff102249.title: Organic matter
bfebff102249.sentence: - The priming effect is larger in soils that are rich in C and N as compared to those poor in these nutrients.

7d0df9c46d46.title: Organic matter
7d0df9c46d46.sentence: - The size of the priming effect increases as the amount of added treatment to the soil increases.

813d80f4a830.title: Organic matter
813d80f4a830.sentence: - Real priming effects have not been observed in sterile environments.

ca17f104db25.title: Organic matter
ca17f104db25.sentence: Löhnis was the first to discover the priming effect phenomenon in 1926 through his studies of green manure decomposition and its effects on legume plants in soil.

bbdbbdf7e9ad.title: Organic matter
bbdbbdf7e9ad.sentence: He noticed that when adding fresh organic residues to the soil, it resulted in intensified mineralization by the humus N. It was not until 1953, though, that the term priming effect was given by Bingeman in his paper titled, The effect of the addition of organic material on the decomposition of an organic soil.

2db52b87a099.title: Organic matter
2db52b87a099.sentence: Despite these early contributions, the concept of the priming effect was widely disregarded until about the 1980s-1990s.

8d190ee2374c.title: Organic matter
8d190ee2374c.sentence: However, the mechanisms which lead to the priming effect are more complex than originally thought, and still remain generally misunderstood.

c7cc893c001a.title: Organic matter
c7cc893c001a.sentence: Recent findings suggest that the same priming effect mechanisms acting in soil systems may also be present in aquatic environments, which suggests a need for broader considerations of this phenomenon in the future.

66e5b5fe5a94.title: Hydrogen cycle
66e5b5fe5a94.sentence: The hydrogen cycle consists of hydrogen exchanges between biotic (living) and abiotic (non-living) sources and sinks of hydrogen-containing compounds.

1271532d63cd.title: Hydrogen cycle
1271532d63cd.sentence: Given the ubiquity of hydrogen atoms in inorganic and organic chemical compounds, the hydrogen cycle is focused on molecular hydrogen, H2.

c89623ceb83c.title: Hydrogen cycle
c89623ceb83c.sentence: Biological soil uptake is the dominant sink of atmospheric H2.

db1a3cdf4b34.title: Hydrogen cycle
db1a3cdf4b34.sentence: Hydrogen is produced by hydrogenases and nitrogenases enzymes in many microorganisms, some of which are being studied for their potential for biofuel production.

0208b3e6fb51.title: Hydrogen cycle
0208b3e6fb51.sentence: Fermentation produces H2 from organic matter as part of the anaerobic microbial food chain via light-dependent or light-independent pathways.

8f488375db3f.title: Hydrogen cycle
8f488375db3f.sentence: These H2-metabolizing enzymes are found in all three domains of life, and out of known genomes over 30% of microbial taxa contain hydrogenase genes.

9108fc977351.title: Hydrogen cycle
9108fc977351.sentence: Anaerobic H2 oxidation often occurs during interspecies hydrogen transfer in which H2 produced during fermentation is transferred to another organism, which uses the H2 to reduce CO2 to CH4 or acetate, SO2− 4 to H2S, or Fe3+ to Fe2+.

38125631c947.title: Hydrogen cycle
38125631c947.sentence: This makes hydrogen an indirect greenhouse gas.

8046386163eb.title: Hydrogen cycle
8046386163eb.sentence: For example, H2 can interfere with the removal of methane from the atmosphere.

6cb9a9cb4142.title: Mull humus
6cb9a9cb4142.sentence: Mull humus is distinguishable from the other terrestrial humus types moder, mor, amphi and tangel in characteristics, formation, nutrient cycling, productivity, etc. It is characterized by the granular structure of its A horizon and the absence of an OH horizon.

7472a0c19fee.title: Mull humus
7472a0c19fee.sentence: Mull is the product of the mixing activity of burrowing soil animals such as earthworms, ants, termites, moles or pocket gophers which create nests and burrows within the soil biomantle.

da537aa27ee6.title: Mull humus
da537aa27ee6.sentence: Due to the presence of various soil organisms, from microbes to mammals, and high biological activity in mull, the disappearance of plant litter is fast, and there are no distinct layers because thick organic horizons do not accumulate.

1ed4537ed303.title: Mull humus
1ed4537ed303.sentence: Conversely, the A horizon is well developed, resulting from the assemblage of humified organic matter with mineral particles.

16d8b3403c97.title: Mull humus
16d8b3403c97.sentence: Mull is present in deciduous forests, and its development is often associated with a mild climate in terms of warm temperature and moderate precipitation, also with rich soil parent materials.

b224c20966ea.title: Humus
b224c20966ea.sentence: Mull humus is commonly found in deciduous woodland and lowland grassland, where the decomposition of the litter layer to humus is quite rapid, leaving a minimal or non-present detritus layer.

5eeed3528642.title: Mull humus
5eeed3528642.sentence: Earthworms are the most widespread invertebrate group in the formation of mull.

4bd272100495.title: Mull humus
4bd272100495.sentence: Millipedes, in particular Polydesmida, have been described as mull-formers in old-growth forests of the Appalachians, still not invaded by burrowing European earthworms.

8cb12845e90a.title: Mull humus
8cb12845e90a.sentence: In arid and semi-arid environments darkling beetles have conspicuous fossorial habits, creating mull-like biogenic granular structures.

f4d8e9ed11ba.title: Mull humus
f4d8e9ed11ba.sentence: Fossorial mammals (e.g. voles, prairie dogs, pocket gophers), contribute to the formation of mull through their excavating, feeding and defecating activities.

d6cac2c2db31.title: Mull humus
d6cac2c2db31.sentence: Also, plants under mull humus produce litters that are easier decomposable with a low C:N ratio, allowing nutrient release, preventing immobilization, and encouraging high bioturbation.

9a715429d5d5.title: Mull humus
9a715429d5d5.sentence: Moreover, a relatively complete decomposition relates to more completely oxidized organic acids, promoting a higher value of pH and base saturation in the soil.

fb811ea68513.title: Mull humus
fb811ea68513.sentence: Associating with soil organisms, a positive feedback loop will be formed: the higher the litter quality, the faster organic matter decomposition, the faster nutrient cycling, and the faster vegetation growth.

ace71505e12f.title: Mull humus
ace71505e12f.sentence: Mull harbours a high biomass and species richness of soil fauna, ranging from megafauna to microfauna.

083a3bca2cfd.title: Humus form
083a3bca2cfd.section: Humus forms in a changing world > Climate change
083a3bca2cfd.sentence: In reality, in mull the litter does not accumulate on the surface but is quickly buried deep down, where it is bound to mineral matter in the form of organo-mineral assemblages that are more stable than the organic matter accumulated on the surface of mor and moder humus profiles.

4949af3750c6.title: Humus form
4949af3750c6.section: Humus forms in a changing world > Climate change
4949af3750c6.sentence: Mull therefore ultimately stores more carbon than moder or even mor forms.

f2ee1f2eed45.title: Mull humus
f2ee1f2eed45.sentence: In HUMUSICA, a worldwide classification of humus forms, Mull is considered as a humus system (abbreviation of humus interaction system) and subdivided in Eumull, Mesomull, Oligomull and Dysmull as humus forms, while Amphimull is considered as a separate humus system.

63d48852fb63.title: Mull humus
63d48852fb63.sentence: - Eumull: presence of a discontinuous OL horizon and a A horizon with a granular structure seasonally visible at the surface.

37f5f09ccb2b.title: Mull humus
37f5f09ccb2b.sentence: - Dysmull: presence of a continuous OF horizon under the continuous OL horizon and a A horizon with a granular structure.

8c9ee69b5560.title: Mor humus
8c9ee69b5560.sentence: Mor is a humus form occurring mostly in coniferous forests and ericaceous heathlands.

2602ade185f5.title: Mor humus
2602ade185f5.sentence: Mor humus ranks at the bottom of this scale and is characterized by very slow decomposition and accumulation of plant material.

4a0c8c0e858c.title: Mor humus
4a0c8c0e858c.sentence: Mor humus consists of evergreen needles, ericaceous twigs and foliage and woody debris that litter the forest floor.

702d73db1956.title: Mor humus
702d73db1956.sentence: This litter is slow to decompose, in part due to its chemical composition (low pH, low nutrient content, high lignin, tannin or terpenic content), but also because of the generally cool and wet conditions where mor humus is found.

8e30025d79a0.title: Mor humus
8e30025d79a0.sentence: This results in low bacterial activity and an absence of earthworms and a low presence of other soil fauna.

0fa13ba75b2b.title: Mor humus
0fa13ba75b2b.sentence: Soil bacteria are also unable to metabolize organic matter efficiently when pH is low.

538da309e63c.title: Mor humus
538da309e63c.sentence: Because of this, most of the organic matter decomposition in mor humus is carried out by fungi.

7c9824db26e6.title: Mor humus
7c9824db26e6.sentence: Mor humus has three distinct organic horizons: an OL horizon (litter horizon), atop an OF horizon (fermentation horizon), followed by a more or less thick (sometimes absent) OH horizon (humus horizon), before a sharp transition to the mineral soil (E horizon).

5375733c2a01.title: Mor humus
5375733c2a01.sentence: The OL horizon is very thick and is made up of undecomposed organic material.

458374eecf94.title: Mor humus
458374eecf94.sentence: A layered and compact-matted structure caused by the interweaving of plant roots and fungal hyphae make up the fermentation layer, with a very weak contribution of animal faeces, contrary to the OF horizon of moder.

46861f82ea88.title: Mor humus
46861f82ea88.sentence: Rather than being intimately mixed (clay, silt) or juxtaposed (sand) with mineral particles, like in the A horizon of mull or moder, organic matter, either in colloidal or dissolved form (DOC), is leached (eluviated) through the E horizon until deposited (illuviated) below in the B horizon, a process typical of podzolization.

341cce5bb934.title: Mor humus
341cce5bb934.sentence: The high volume of undecomposed organic matter in the OF horizon of mor humus leads to a high C:N ratio and can immobilize important plant nutrients such as nitrogen.

780ff65b1d89.title: Mor humus
780ff65b1d89.sentence: The high C:N and C:P ratios of mor humus slow the release of nutrients available to plants, restricting in turn plant development and favouring the production of a nutrient-poor litter, thus closing the feed-back loop between humus and vegetation.

db81419185bb.title: Mor humus
db81419185bb.sentence: Through their distinct yellow and white coloration, the fungal hyphae in this horizon are identifiable as cellulose-decomposing fungi, which are the primary decomposers of organic matter in mor humus, and ectomycorrhizal fungi (with conifers) and ericoid mycorrhizal fungi (with Ericaceae) which contribute to nitrogen uptake and transfer to their host plant, and act as a sink for carbon.

18607d4916b5.title: Humus form
18607d4916b5.sentence: Mor is associated with very cold climates, high altitude and latitude, or with very acidifying vegetation as in certain coniferous forests (notably pine) or in ericaceous heath, or even in highly polluted soils.

debd925e9ca7.title: Mor humus
debd925e9ca7.sentence: Far from being improper to plant growth and soil life and needing to be improved by fertiization, mor humus with its short food chains should be considered as the best ecological strategy by which plants, animals and microbes cope with the harsh environmental or nutritional conditions associated with high altitude, high latitude or nutrient-poor geological substrates (e.g. quartz sand, quartzite).

828c7313b7b0.title: Mor humus
828c7313b7b0.sentence: In the seminal work of Peter Erasmus Müller on Danish forest soils, which described mor for the first time, this humus form was called beech peat by analogy with sphagnum peat.

117181dd0686.title: Mor humus
117181dd0686.sentence: Despite the clear distinction between Mor and all other humus forms stemming from the absence of an A horizon and the sharp transition from the forest floor to the mineral soil, mor and moder (in particular Dysmoder) were often confused under the designation of raw humus, embracing a wide variety of variants, from poorly to highly biologically active.

4cf5b6a66240.title: Kerogen
4cf5b6a66240.sentence: Kerogen is solid, insoluble organic matter in sedimentary rocks.

5b5f23a71164.title: Kerogen
5b5f23a71164.sentence: It consists of a variety of organic materials, including dead plants, algae, and other microorganisms, that have been compressed and heated by geological processes.

9092fcc0ea60.title: Kerogen
9092fcc0ea60.sentence: Kerogen is formed during sedimentary diagenesis from the degradation of living matter.

c51c5407dc29.title: Kerogen
c51c5407dc29.sentence: This makes it the most abundant source of organic compounds on earth, exceeding the total organic content of living matter 10,000-fold.

629034f78992.title: Kerogen
629034f78992.sentence: Labile kerogen breaks down to generate principally liquid hydrocarbons (i.e., oil), refractory kerogen breaks down to generate principally gaseous hydrocarbons, and inert kerogen generates no hydrocarbons but forms graphite.

628389f119eb.title: Kerogen
628389f119eb.sentence: Type III kerogens are derived from terrestrial plant matter, specifically from precursor compounds including cellulose, lignin (a non-carbohydrate polymer formed from phenyl-propane units that binds the strings of cellulose together); terpenes and phenols.

86711ed8f1ef.title: Organic matter
86711ed8f1ef.sentence: Groundwater has its own sources of natural organic matter including:

7de0898c0052.title: Organic matter
7de0898c0052.sentence: - organic matter deposits, such as kerogen and coal.

f4cbe41bed44.title: Kerogen
f4cbe41bed44.sentence: The name kerogen was introduced by the Scottish organic chemist Alexander Crum Brown in 1906, derived from the Greek words for wax and origin (Greek: κηρός 'wax' and -gen, γένεσις 'origin').

6a2459a7033f.title: Humin
6a2459a7033f.sentence: Humins are carbon-based macromolecular substances, that can be found in soil chemistry or as a by-product from saccharide-based biorefinery processes.

43845cd63ed9.title: Humin
43845cd63ed9.sentence: The organic components can be subdivided into fractions that are soluble, largely humic acids, and insoluble, the humins.

2f35152d3d8e.title: Humin
2f35152d3d8e.sentence: Humins make up about 50% of the organic matter in soil.

b85691bbceaa.title: Soil organic matter
b85691bbceaa.sentence: - Humin is the genus that contains the matter that has the greatest molecular weight, is the darkest in color, is insoluble in acids and alkalis, and has the greatest resistance to microbial action.

899e0282ecef.title: Humic substance
899e0282ecef.sentence: Humin is not soluble in water at any pH.

1bce8817b587.title: Humin
1bce8817b587.sentence: Humins also produced during the dehydration of sugars, as occurs during the conversion of lignocellulosic biomass to smaller, higher value organic compounds such as 5-hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF).

b141fcb8eaee.title: Humin
b141fcb8eaee.section: Humins from biomass sources > Humin structure and mechanism of formation
b141fcb8eaee.sentence: These parameters also influence the mechanism of formation which is still a matter of debate.

2394fd29b28f.title: Moder humus
2394fd29b28f.sentence: Moder is a kind of humus form whose properties are the transition between mor humus and mull humus types.

87fbe4791a2f.title: Moder humus
87fbe4791a2f.sentence: Moder is characterized by a slow rate of litter decomposition by litter-dwelling organisms and fungi, leading to the accumulation of organic residues, mainly in the form of invertebrate fecal pellets.

af8527ab3043.title: Moder humus
af8527ab3043.sentence: Moder is similar to mor as it is made up of partially to fully humified organic components accumulated on the mineral soil, while compared to mull, moder is zoologically active.

74ce0cd4803b.title: Humus form
74ce0cd4803b.sentence: Moder is the product of the activity of non-burrowing animals, or those only burrowing over a very short distance.

fbcb52c9b87a.title: Moder humus
fbcb52c9b87a.sentence: The animals responsible for the fragmentation of litter and its transformation into humus belong to the detritivorous fauna, including microarthropods (e.g. springtails, oribatid mites), macroarthropods (e.g. millipedes, woodlice, insect larvae) but also molluscs (snails, slugs) and worms (epigeic earthworms, enchytraeids).

2e6b183a279f.title: Moder humus
2e6b183a279f.sentence: Moder is a forest floor type formed under coniferous forests, mixed-wood and pure deciduous forests.

5437adafe1e7.title: Moder humus
5437adafe1e7.sentence: Morder forms in deciduous forest situations when the soil has fewer bacteria and macro-invertebrates, such as earthworms, to decompose and bury the organic matter deposited on the soil surface, mainly because of high soil acidity and poor litter quality.

11afe7dca8e9.title: Moder humus
11afe7dca8e9.sentence: Moder' chemical characteristics show high acidity (low pH), total carbon, carbon-nitrogen ratio, and low cation exchange capacity, total nitrogen and base saturation.

cb382dd792db.title: Moder humus
cb382dd792db.sentence: Moder has a higher availability of nutrients than mor.

d644b767df1e.title: Moder humus
d644b767df1e.sentence: It is generally possible to observe four distinct horizons designated by OL, OF, OH and A.

445f76f7d14e.title: Humus form
445f76f7d14e.sentence: Although the OH horizon is considered a diagnostic horizon for moder (as opposed to mull) it is the intense biological activity within the OF horizon which truly marks the moder.

3deaa9b73994.title: Moder humus
3deaa9b73994.sentence: A distinctive aspect of the OF horizon and its loose nature is the abundance of soil animal droppings, which can be seen with the aid of a hand lens.

9dbdf6e3e784.title: Moder humus
9dbdf6e3e784.sentence: The A horizon of moder differs from that of mull and amphi by the size of peds, i.e. infra-millimetric animal faeces either purely organic when juxtaposed to sand particles or organo-mineral when finely mixed with silt or clay particles.

c28089be78c7.title: Moder humus
c28089be78c7.sentence: This horizon results from the burrowing and mixing activity (bioturbation) of small invertebrates, mostly enchytraeids.

fa31808cfc59.title: Moder humus
fa31808cfc59.sentence: Moder is the seat of intense biological activity in the forest floor, with a superficial development of the fine root system of trees, associated with a symbiotic ectomycorrhizal mycelium circulating between the accumulated animal faeces in which fungal hyphae penetrate to capture nutrients.

f50afd28dae9.title: Humus form
f50afd28dae9.sentence: Microscopic observation of moder OF horizon shows that ectomycorrhizal fungal hyphae penetrate the excreta of detritivorous fauna, thus creating a functional link between soil fauna and plants.

8e258d5e4d42.title: Moder humus
8e258d5e4d42.sentence: Moder has been described by Franz Hartmann, midway between mull and mor and was previously described as 'insect mull'.

67918276405b.title: Moder humus
67918276405b.sentence: In HUMUSICA, a worldwide classification of humus forms, Moder is considered as a humus system (abbreviation of humus interaction system) and subdivided in Hemimoder, Eumoder, and Dysmoder as humus forms.

be45c501983a.title: Moder humus
be45c501983a.sentence: - Eumoder: presence of a continuous OH horizon < 1 cm and a gradual transition to a A horizon with a microgranular structure.

89d49c6b0966.title: Moder humus
89d49c6b0966.sentence: - Dysmoder: presence of a continuous OH horizon > 1 cm and a gradual transition to a A horizon with a microgranular structure.

f859297b04cb.title: Particulate organic matter
f859297b04cb.sentence: As shown below, non-living organic matter in soils can be grouped into four distinct categories on the basis of size, behaviour and persistence.

1a911b55b8b5.title: Particulate organic matter
1a911b55b8b5.sentence: These categories are arranged in order of decreasing ability to decompose.

34ff808aa6ab.title: Particulate organic matter
34ff808aa6ab.sentence: Living organisms (including roots) contribute about 15% of the total organic matter in soil.

b1be103c7b1a.title: Particulate organic matter
b1be103c7b1a.sentence: What follows refers to the remaining 85% of the soil organic matter - the non-living component.

398de89310d5.title: Particulate organic matter
398de89310d5.sentence: Dissolved organic matter (DOM): is the organic matter which dissolves in soil water.

6067d755d937.title: Particulate organic matter
6067d755d937.sentence: It comprises the relatively simple organic compounds (e.g. organic acids, sugars and amino acids) which easily decompose.

860e789658f1.title: Particulate organic matter
860e789658f1.sentence: It has a turnover time of less than 12 months.

8e22eee6b9e8.title: Particulate organic matter
8e22eee6b9e8.sentence: Exudates from plant roots (mucilages and gums) are included here.

e869229b34a8.title: Particulate organic matter
e869229b34a8.sentence: Humus: is usually the largest proportion of organic matter in soil, contributing 45 to 75%.

3915a94a3ec7.title: Particulate organic matter
3915a94a3ec7.sentence: Humus is quite slow to decompose and exists in soil for decades.

949b43aa6905.title: Particulate organic matter
949b43aa6905.sentence: Resistant organic matter: has a high carbon content and includes charcoal, charred plant materials, graphite and coal.

83f7a4cd2711.title: Particulate organic matter
83f7a4cd2711.sentence: Turnover times are long and estimated in hundreds of years.

158592f33f53.title: Particulate organic matter
158592f33f53.sentence: It is not biologically active but contributes positively to soil structural properties, including water holding capacity, cation exchange capacity and thermal properties.

915290e6678e.title: Dissolved organic carbon
915290e6678e.sentence: Dissolved organic carbon (DOC) is the fraction of organic carbon operationally defined as that which can pass through a filter with a pore size typically between 0.22 and 0.7 micrometers.

b16d8209d747.title: Dissolved organic carbon
