b16d8209d747.sentence: Dissolved organic matter (DOM) is a closely related term often used interchangeably with DOC.

71728a451f2b.title: Dissolved organic carbon
71728a451f2b.sentence: While DOC refers specifically to the mass of carbon in the dissolved organic material, DOM refers to the total mass of the dissolved organic matter.

1638eb7e5966.title: Dissolved organic carbon
1638eb7e5966.sentence: Soil DOM can be derived from different sources (inputs), such as atmospheric carbon dissolved in rainfall, litter and crop residues, manure, root exudates, and decomposition of soil organic matter (SOM).

d91847f5676a.title: Dissolved organic carbon
d91847f5676a.sentence: Dissolved organic matter (DOM) is one of the most active and mobile carbon pools and has an important role in global carbon cycling.

aaf4b575fdfc.title: Dissolved organic carbon
aaf4b575fdfc.sentence: In addition, dissolved organic carbon (DOC) affects the soil negative electrical charges denitrification process, acid-base reactions in the soil solution, retention and translocation of nutrients (cations), and immobilization of heavy metals and xenobiotics.

362bf75d4cab.title: Dissolved organic carbon
362bf75d4cab.sentence: In the soil, DOM availability depends on its interactions with mineral components (e.g., clays, Fe and Al oxides) modulated by adsorption and desorption processes.

448464c3cf16.title: Dissolved organic carbon
448464c3cf16.sentence: In well-drained soils, leached DOC can reach the water table and release nutrients and pollutants that can contaminate groundwater, whereas runoff transports DOM and xenobiotics to other areas, rivers, and lakes.

93664d25ba4c.title: Humus form
93664d25ba4c.section: Humus forms in a changing world
93664d25ba4c.sentence: Like any ecosystem, the humus form is likely to evolve under the influence of environmental changes, e.g. vegetation dynamics, land use, pollution or climate change.

bd8ad389137b.title: Humus form
bd8ad389137b.section: Humus forms in a changing world > Vegetation dynamics
bd8ad389137b.sentence: Several authors have highlighted an increase in the thickness of organic horizons, associated with an evolution from mull, in the initial forest stages, towards moder under mature forest stands.

562a91db8deb.title: Humus form
562a91db8deb.section: Humus forms in a changing world > Vegetation dynamics
562a91db8deb.sentence: In old, natural or semi-natural forests, where natural regeneration takes place freely, a cycle is observed where mull and moder alternate.

92a7074dbfa6.title: Humus form
92a7074dbfa6.section: Humus forms in a changing world > Vegetation dynamics
92a7074dbfa6.sentence: The conversion of coniferous forests into deciduous forests is accompanied by a transition from moder to mull, the opposite being observed in conifer plantations succeeding to deciduous stands.

1791b2713d49.title: Humus form
1791b2713d49.section: Humus forms in a changing world > Land use
1791b2713d49.sentence: Organic farming, by promoting organic amendment and eliminating chemical fertilizers and synthetic pesticides, and conservation agriculture, by eliminating or greatly reducing ploughing, encourages the activity of earthworms and therefore the development of a humus form similar to the mull of meadows, pastures and deciduous forests, called agri-mull or agro-mull.

e2a1d0c0296a.title: Humus form
e2a1d0c0296a.section: Humus forms in a changing world > Pollution
e2a1d0c0296a.sentence: In this case, observing the humus form constitutes an inexpensive means of early detection and mapping of pollution at a large number of points before implementing more in-depth contamination assessment.

4eb7550f9149.title: Humus form
4eb7550f9149.section: Humus forms in a changing world > Climate change
4eb7550f9149.sentence: Statistically, the warmer the temperature, the more mull is encountered at the expense of forms with lesser decomposition and incorporation of organic matter (e.g. moder, more, tangel).

e88d761908a4.title: Humus form
e88d761908a4.section: Humus forms in a changing world > Climate change
e88d761908a4.sentence: Research in alpine grasslands demonstrates that a 3 °C temperature increase reduces soil humus content and destabilizes soil structure.

91d029d22c41.title: Humus form
91d029d22c41.section: Humus forms in a changing world > Climate change
91d029d22c41.sentence: Rising temperatures accelerate microbial decomposition processes, resulting in humus depletion and a negative carbon balance in many soils.

4f35b613f4b7.title: Humus form
4f35b613f4b7.section: Humus forms in a changing world > Vegetation dynamics
4f35b613f4b7.sentence: If it is absent from the vicinity or has only weak dispersal capabilities, which is the case for earthworms and more generally for non-flying soil invertebrates, humus-form responses are observed that do not go in the expected direction.

d1f3ac0d232a.title: Humus form
d1f3ac0d232a.section: Humus forms in a changing world > Vegetation dynamics
d1f3ac0d232a.sentence: This is why attempts have been made to inoculate earthworms, in the presence or absence of mineral or organic fertilization, to facilitate the evolution of humus form from moder to mull, considered better in terms of forest site quality, during conversions or to improve forest productivity on acidic soils.

8bdbc552bb68.title: Humus form
8bdbc552bb68.section: Humus forms in a changing world > Vegetation dynamics
8bdbc552bb68.sentence: The results are sometimes positive, sometimes negative if they do not take into account the requirements of soil organisms, particularly in cases of soil waterlogging (hydromorphy), to which earthworms are particularly sensitive.

2997a5888046.title: Humus form
2997a5888046.sentence: Humipedons display a succession of horizons according to decomposition stages of fallen plant litter and its progressive incorporation to mineral matter.

c9c573270ecb.title: Humus form
c9c573270ecb.sentence: The OL horizon (Oi in the USDA Soil Taxonomy) is made of recognizable leaves or needles without any prominent signs of fragmentation by litter-consuming soil animals.

686a5fda9e61.title: Humus form
686a5fda9e61.sentence: The OL horizon is present in all terrestrial humus forms, to the exception of the most active mull humus forms (e.g. Eumull) where it might be seasonally absent because of a fast decomposition rate of recently fallen litter.

446534761bb4.title: Humus form
446534761bb4.sentence: The OF horizon (Oe in the USDA Soil Taxonomy) is made of fragmented leaf or needle litter, from the feeding activity of soil animals (macrofauna and mesofauna).

82758fe0fce6.title: Humus form
82758fe0fce6.sentence: Litter debris are mixed with feces deposited by litter-consuming animals in the form of dark-coloured pellets of a size varying from 30-50 micrometres (enchytraeids, oribatid mites, springtails) to 1-2 millimetres (epigeic earthworms, millipedes, woodlice, molluscs).

1e130b68c4b2.title: Humus form
1e130b68c4b2.sentence: The OH horizon (Oa in the USDA Soil Taxonomy) is the product of transformation of plant remains by soil organisms once these remains are no longer visible, but the humus thus formed is still not incorporated with mineral matter.

a487f84d8a19.title: Humus form
a487f84d8a19.sentence: According to the soil animals which contributed the most to the faunal activity observed in the overlying OF horizon, the OH horizon may be seen as an accumulation of still visible fecal pellets (e.g. earthworms, ants, millipedes, woodlice, crane fly larvae for macrofauna, but also oribatid mites for mesofauna) or in the case of enchytraeids as a fine powder further compacted in depth.

aece3bfd4a08.title: Humus form
aece3bfd4a08.sentence: The A horizon results from the mixing of organic matter with mineral matter, mostly effected by burrowing soil animals (e.g. enchytraeids, earthworms, termites, ants, darkling beetles, gophers).

c0480c8be7de.title: Humus form
c0480c8be7de.sentence: Macroaggregates (> 250 μm) are built by macrofauna (e.g. earthworms, ants, termites) and megafauna (e.g. gophers), while microaggregates (< 250 μm) are built by mesofauna (e.g. enchytraeids, microarthropods).

3f5ccb12da1f.title: Humus form
3f5ccb12da1f.sentence: The E horizon appears as a white or grey (ashy) horizon, the lightness (Munsell colour value) of which varies with its carbon content, always feeble.

6c3b7f97e51a.title: Humus form
6c3b7f97e51a.sentence: Compared to the abovelying organic and mineral-organic horizons, the E horizon displays only poor signs of biological activity, being mainly the seat of leaching of water, solutes (e.g. nitrates, dissolved organic carbon) and colloids (e.g. clay, humus) through a mineral layer.

d6e5b464a991.title: Humus form
d6e5b464a991.sentence: They have been characterized on thin soil sections by soil micromorphologists, but their recognition in the field is easy, being aided by the use of a hand lens if necessary.

1ac63c96671e.title: Humus form
1ac63c96671e.sentence: They can be observed along a humus profile cut with a sharp knife along a trench or be successively collected by hand one by one from the top to the bottom of a small soil monolith.

86024e571fb7.title: Coarse woody debris
86024e571fb7.sentence: Coarse woody debris (CWD) or coarse woody habitat (CWH) refers to fallen dead trees and the remains of large branches on the ground in forests and in rivers or wetlands.

5819626abc05.title: Coarse woody debris
5819626abc05.sentence: The minimum size required for woody debris to be defined as "coarse" varies by author, ranging from 2.5–20 cm (1–8 in) in diameter.

7ec261d77edb.title: Coarse woody debris
7ec261d77edb.sentence: Coarse woody debris and its subsequent decomposition recycles nutrients that are essential for living organisms, such as carbon, nitrogen, potassium, and phosphorus.

546b6268bb38.title: Coarse woody debris
546b6268bb38.sentence: Saprotrophic fungi and detritivores such as bacteria and insects directly consume dead wood, releasing nutrients by converting them into other forms of organic matter which may then be consumed by other organisms.

c90cae68dc69.title: Coarse woody debris
c90cae68dc69.sentence: CWD, while itself not particularly rich in nitrogen, contributes nitrogen to the ecosystem by acting as a host for nonsymbiotic free-living nitrogen-fixing bacteria.

7d5a759c39ef.title: Coarse woody debris
7d5a759c39ef.sentence: Once the trees die, fungi and other saprotrophs transfer some of that carbon from CWD into the soil.

f62089700a01.title: Coarse woody debris
f62089700a01.sentence: This sequestration can continue in old-growth forests for hundreds of years.

a23e723180ce.title: Coarse woody debris
a23e723180ce.sentence: Coarse woody debris, particularly on slopes, stabilizes soils by slowing downslope movement of organic matter and mineral soil.

073983d6cc58.title: Coarse woody debris
073983d6cc58.sentence: Leaves and other debris collect behind CWD, allowing for decomposition to occur.

e6cafbb5c708.title: Coarse woody debris
e6cafbb5c708.sentence: Infiltration of precipitation is improved as well.

5ca1c59e8bc9.title: Coarse woody debris
5ca1c59e8bc9.sentence: During dry weather, CWD slows evaporation of soil moisture and provides damp microhabitats for moisture-sensitive organisms.

9327550f9692.title: Leaf mold
9327550f9692.sentence: Leaf mold (spelled leaf mould outside of the United States) is the compost produced by decomposition of shaded deciduous shrub and tree leaves, primarily by fungal breakdown in a slower, cooler manner as opposed to the bacterial degradation of leaves.

2167c7f11768.title: Leaf mold
2167c7f11768.sentence: Leaves shed in autumn tend to have a very low nitrogen content and are often dry.

a61a7c8a7557.title: Leaf mold
a61a7c8a7557.sentence: Their main constituents, cellulose and lignin, are two recalcitrant molecules resistant to degradation.

ee49a4f92358.title: Leaf mold
ee49a4f92358.sentence: Because of this, autumn leaves break down far more slowly than most other compost ingredients which may take a very long time on their own.

633fb12d9509.title: Leaf mold
633fb12d9509.sentence: Fungal decomposition of a heap of leaves in damp temperate climates can take between one and three years to break down into a dark brown fine powdery humic matter.

8b615ee531ff.title: Leaf mold
8b615ee531ff.sentence: A succession of different fungal species may be involved.

ce6216211d52.title: Leaf mold
ce6216211d52.sentence: A range of micro detritivores are also involved in converting the leaf material into a fine-grained humus, including many isopods, millipedes, earthworms, etc.

fb0a6c66cf25.title: Leaf mold
fb0a6c66cf25.sentence: It is a significant component of soil organic matter, particularly in temperate deciduous woodland.

83d7c484cbd6.title: Leaf mold
83d7c484cbd6.sentence: The slow rate of decomposition gradually releases plant nutrients bound up in the leaves back into the environment to be re-used by plants.

7546d041fcd8.title: Leaf mold
7546d041fcd8.sentence: Leaf mold is not high in nutrient content but is an excellent humic soil conditioner because its structure and moisture retention provide a good growing medium for seedling roots.

c918a19d6788.title: Canopy soils
c918a19d6788.sentence: Canopy soils, also known as arboreal soils, exist in areas of the forest canopy where branches, crevices, or some other physical feature on a tree can accumulate organic matter, such as leaves or fine branches.

c289984a44d7.title: Canopy soils
c289984a44d7.sentence: Eventually, this organic matter weathers into some semblance of a soil, and can reach depths of 30 cm in some temperate rainforests.

37e611316e00.title: Canopy soils
37e611316e00.sentence: Epiphytes can take root in the canopy soil, which accelerates the development of the soil by adding organic material and physically breaking up material with their root system.

655976b16009.title: Canopy soils
655976b16009.sentence: Older canopies can accumulate more material and create a deeper soil.

a72092191490.title: Canopy soils
a72092191490.sentence: Canopy soils higher in a forest's canopy will be more exposed to the elements, resulting in a higher exposure to sunlight and wind, which could result in extreme shifts in available soil moisture.

8f84b2fa81de.title: Canopy soils
8f84b2fa81de.sentence: This allows these lower canopy soils to accumulate more organic matter and nutrients, which allows them to be more productive.

702e544cb594.title: Canopy soils
702e544cb594.sentence: The intimate relationship that vascular epiphytes have with the formation of canopy soils means that the distributions of canopy soils follow a parallel distribution pattern, as it is the pattern of growth and decay of epiphytic growth that promotes the formation of canopy soils.

152ee1ce8743.title: Canopy soils
152ee1ce8743.sentence: The temperate zones in the southern hemisphere have a much greater abundance of vascular epiphytes than in the northern hemisphere, and they persist further into more polar latitudes.

dcef51b8f8e4.title: Canopy soils
dcef51b8f8e4.sentence: In contrast, temperate rainforests in the southern hemisphere remained largely ice-free.

7ee643bfe655.title: Canopy soils
7ee643bfe655.sentence: Human disturbance such as logging and climate change are leading contributors to the degradation of canopy soils and respective forests they occupy.

57a2c47769ea.title: Canopy soils

f1bc62623dfc.title: Canopy soils
f1bc62623dfc.sentence: Canopy soils are involved in biogeochemical cycling, specifically nitrogen cycling.

059ec492a6cd.title: Canopy soils
059ec492a6cd.sentence: The nitrogen cycling process observed in canopy soils not only contributes heavily to growth within the canopy, but can also affect the fertility of soil on the forest floor.

e80593d09821.title: Canopy soils
e80593d09821.sentence: The rate at which canopy soils release nitrogen is higher than that of forest floors, likely meaning canopy soils are a main siphon of nitrogen for epiphytes within a canopy.

993e1a43a383.title: Canopy soils
993e1a43a383.sentence: The nitrogen cycling process that occurs within canopy soils is an important source of nitrogen for epiphytes throughout different elevations.

d5d865f7815a.title: Canopy soils
d5d865f7815a.sentence: However, canopy soils' rate of gross nitrification is around the same or even lower compared to that of forest floor soil.

72e069652873.title: Canopy soils
72e069652873.sentence: This could be due to the higher acidity measured in canopy soils than observed in forest floor soils.

0eed4ec47b94.title: Canopy soils
0eed4ec47b94.sentence: Nitrogen gas fixation within canopy soils is tied closely with environmental variation as a whole, but specifically, this process is dependent on seasonal changes in tropical rainforest biomes.

628d30deb66d.title: Canopy soils
628d30deb66d.sentence: The nutrients that become stored within canopy soils can then be utilized by the epiphytes that grow in them, and even the tree that the canopy soil is accumulating in through the growth of canopy roots.

c401b2ca0f43.title: Canopy soils
c401b2ca0f43.sentence: This storage allows nutrients to be more closely cycled through an ecosystem, and prevents nutrients from being washed out of the system.

2f9942781ec7.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.01%3A_Introduction
2f9942781ec7.section: Storage of Organic Matter in Soil
2f9942781ec7.sentence: Organic matter is protected in soils by:

af02f62b331b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.01%3A_Introduction
af02f62b331b.section: Storage of Organic Matter in Soil
af02f62b331b.sentence: - Formation of strong chemical bonds between organic matter and clay particles (and fine silt)

b9616d4782fc.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.01%3A_Introduction
b9616d4782fc.section: Storage of Organic Matter in Soil

898148412855.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.01%3A_Introduction
898148412855.section: Storage of Organic Matter in Soil
898148412855.sentence: - Conversion into stable substances such as humic materials that are resistant to biological decomposition

6f9cba9b432b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.01%3A_Introduction
6f9cba9b432b.section: Storage of Organic Matter in Soil
6f9cba9b432b.sentence: Large aggregates are made up of many smaller ones that are held together by sticky substances from roots, bacterial colonies and fungal hyphae.

31ea4be15c62.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.01%3A_Introduction
31ea4be15c62.section: Storage of Organic Matter in Soil
31ea4be15c62.sentence: Organic matter in large aggregates—but outside of the small aggregates that make up the larger ones—and freely occurring particulate organic matter (the “dead”) are available for soil organisms to use.

70ebed59eede.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.01%3A_Introduction
70ebed59eede.section: Storage of Organic Matter in Soil
70ebed59eede.sentence: However, poor aeration resulting from restricted drainage because of a dense subsurface layer, compaction or being at the bottom of a slope or wetland area may cause a low rate of use of the organic matter.

8ee83a555230.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.01%3A_Introduction
8ee83a555230.section: Storage of Organic Matter in Soil
8ee83a555230.sentence: So the organic matter needs to be in a favorable chemical form and physical location for organisms to use it; plus, the environmental conditions in the soil—adequate moisture and aeration—need to be sufficient for most soil organisms to use the residues and thrive.

ce23f30640d6.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/09%3A_Managing_for_High-Quality_Soils_and_Focusing_on_Organic_Matter_Management/9.02%3A_Organic_Matter_Management
ce23f30640d6.section: Effects of Residue Characteristics on Soil
ce23f30640d6.sentence: Residues of various crops and manures have different properties and, therefore, have different effects on soil organic matter.

afa4e8224342.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/09%3A_Managing_for_High-Quality_Soils_and_Focusing_on_Organic_Matter_Management/9.02%3A_Organic_Matter_Management
afa4e8224342.section: Effects of Residue Characteristics on Soil
afa4e8224342.sentence: Materials with low amounts of harder-to-degrade hemicellulose, polyphenols and lignin, such as cover crops (especially legumes) when still very green and soybean residue, decompose rapidly (Figure 9.2) and have a shorter term effect on soil organic matter levels than residues with high levels of these chemicals (for example, cornstalks and wheat straw).

643e3c04b7d3.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/09%3A_Managing_for_High-Quality_Soils_and_Focusing_on_Organic_Matter_Management/9.02%3A_Organic_Matter_Management
643e3c04b7d3.section: Effects of Residue Characteristics on Soil
643e3c04b7d3.sentence: Manures, especially those that contain lots of bedding (high in hemicellulose, polyphenols and lignin), decompose more slowly and tend to have more long-lasting effects on total soil organic matter than do crop residues and manures without bedding.

f65c1e8b860b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/09%3A_Managing_for_High-Quality_Soils_and_Focusing_on_Organic_Matter_Management/9.02%3A_Organic_Matter_Management
f65c1e8b860b.section: Effects of Residue Characteristics on Soil
f65c1e8b860b.sentence: Also, cows and other ruminants—because they eat a diet containing lots of forages that are not completely decomposed during digestion—produce manure with longer lasting effects on soils than nonruminants, such as chickens and hogs, that are fed exclusively a high-grain and low-fiber diet.

78deed033bbc.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/09%3A_Managing_for_High-Quality_Soils_and_Focusing_on_Organic_Matter_Management/9.02%3A_Organic_Matter_Management
78deed033bbc.section: Effects of Residue Characteristics on Soil
78deed033bbc.sentence: In general, residues containing a lot of cellulose and other easy-to-decompose materials will have a greater effect on soil aggregation than compost, which has already undergone decomposition and contains less active organic matter.

bbd9e820ef5a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/09%3A_Managing_for_High-Quality_Soils_and_Focusing_on_Organic_Matter_Management/9.02%3A_Organic_Matter_Management
bbd9e820ef5a.section: Effects of Residue Characteristics on Soil
bbd9e820ef5a.sentence: Because aggregates are formed from byproducts of decomposition by soil organisms, organic additions like manures, cover crops, and straw will usually enhance aggregation more than compost.

9726944d5da1.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/09%3A_Managing_for_High-Quality_Soils_and_Focusing_on_Organic_Matter_Management/9.02%3A_Organic_Matter_Management
9726944d5da1.section: Effects of Residue Characteristics on Soil
9726944d5da1.sentence: (However, adding compost does improve soils in many ways, including increasing the waterholding capacity.)

5f53642f19c5.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/09%3A_Managing_for_High-Quality_Soils_and_Focusing_on_Organic_Matter_Management/9.02%3A_Organic_Matter_Management
5f53642f19c5.section: Effects of Residue Characteristics on Soil
5f53642f19c5.sentence: A variety of residues are needed to provide food to a diverse population of organisms, provide nutrients to plants and furnish materials that promote aggregation.

436fb22eb22f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/09%3A_Managing_for_High-Quality_Soils_and_Focusing_on_Organic_Matter_Management/9.02%3A_Organic_Matter_Management
436fb22eb22f.section: Effects of Residue Characteristics on Soil
436fb22eb22f.sentence: On the other hand, straw or sawdust (containing a lot of lignin) can be used to build up organic matter, but a nitrogen deficiency and an imbalance in soil microbial populations will occur unless a readily available source of nitrogen is added at the same time (see discussion of C:N ratios below).

04db9c3433e8.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/09%3A_Managing_for_High-Quality_Soils_and_Focusing_on_Organic_Matter_Management/9.02%3A_Organic_Matter_Management
04db9c3433e8.section: Effects of Residue Characteristics on Soil
04db9c3433e8.sentence: In addition, when insufficient nitrogen is present, less of the organic material added to soils actually ends up as humus.

de73b111b628.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/09%3A_Managing_for_High-Quality_Soils_and_Focusing_on_Organic_Matter_Management/9.02%3A_Organic_Matter_Management
de73b111b628.sentence: However, keep in mind that after residues are decomposed by soil organisms, only about 10–20% of the original amount is converted into stable humus.

793893c4cec9.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.09%3A_The_Dynamics_of_Raising_and_Maintaining_Soil_Organic_Matter_Levels
793893c4cec9.sentence: When you change practices on a soil depleted in organic matter, perhaps one that has been intensively row-cropped for years and has lost a lot of its original aggregation, organic matter will increase slowly, as diagrammed in Figure 3.7.

9a0116b0aa3e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.09%3A_The_Dynamics_of_Raising_and_Maintaining_Soil_Organic_Matter_Levels
9a0116b0aa3e.sentence: At first, any free mineral surfaces that are available for forming bonds with organic matter will form organic-mineral bonds.

04b3d935e772.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.09%3A_The_Dynamics_of_Raising_and_Maintaining_Soil_Organic_Matter_Levels
04b3d935e772.sentence: Once all possible mineral sites have been occupied by organic molecules and all of the small aggregates have been formed around organic matter particles, organic matter accumulates mainly as free particles, within the larger aggregates or completely unaffiliated with minerals.

66f9fa6abc7f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.09%3A_The_Dynamics_of_Raising_and_Maintaining_Soil_Organic_Matter_Levels
66f9fa6abc7f.sentence: Small aggregates will also form around particles of organic matter, such as the outer layer of dead soil microorganisms or fragments of relatively fresh residue.

8e3f06c010b5.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.09%3A_The_Dynamics_of_Raising_and_Maintaining_Soil_Organic_Matter_Levels
8e3f06c010b5.sentence: Then larger aggregates will form, made up of the smaller aggregates and held by a variety of means: frequently by mycorrhizal fungi and small roots.

033d44f46b24.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.09%3A_The_Dynamics_of_Raising_and_Maintaining_Soil_Organic_Matter_Levels
033d44f46b24.sentence: In a sense, the soil is “saturated” with organic matter as long as your practices don’t change.

137746d08554.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.09%3A_The_Dynamics_of_Raising_and_Maintaining_Soil_Organic_Matter_Levels
137746d08554.sentence: All the sites that protect organic matter (chemical bonding sites on clays and physically protected sites inside small aggregates) are occupied, and only free particles of organic matter can accumulate.

81d85fbd2700.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.09%3A_The_Dynamics_of_Raising_and_Maintaining_Soil_Organic_Matter_Levels
81d85fbd2700.sentence: But because there is little protection for the free particles of organic matter, they tend to decompose relatively rapidly under normal (oxidized) conditions.

516885509edb.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.09%3A_The_Dynamics_of_Raising_and_Maintaining_Soil_Organic_Matter_Levels
516885509edb.sentence: First, free particles of organic matter are depleted, and then physically protected organic matter becomes available to decomposers as aggregates are broken down.

40e6469fe40e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.09%3A_The_Dynamics_of_Raising_and_Maintaining_Soil_Organic_Matter_Levels
40e6469fe40e.sentence: What usually remains after many years of soil-depleting practices is organic matter that is tightly held by clay mineral particles and trapped inside very small (micro) aggregates.

8782258231c2.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.09%3A_The_Dynamics_of_Raising_and_Maintaining_Soil_Organic_Matter_Levels
8782258231c2.sentence: Organic matter can be increased much more readily in soils that have become depleted of organic matter than in soils that already have a good amount of organic matter given their texture and drainage condition.

91f4f503b199.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.09%3A_The_Dynamics_of_Raising_and_Maintaining_Soil_Organic_Matter_Levels
91f4f503b199.sentence: Soil organic matter levels can be maintained with lower additions of organic residues in high-clay-content soils with restricted aeration than in coarse-textured soils because of the slower decomposition.

a78b6d8495eb.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.09%3A_The_Dynamics_of_Raising_and_Maintaining_Soil_Organic_Matter_Levels
a78b6d8495eb.sentence: It is especially difficult to raise the organic matter content of soils that are very well aerated, such as coarse sands, because of low potential for aggregation (which shelters organic matter from microbial attack) and limited protective bonds with fine minerals.

5d4a8f0a4aef.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.09%3A_The_Dynamics_of_Raising_and_Maintaining_Soil_Organic_Matter_Levels
5d4a8f0a4aef.sentence: We are generalizing here, but some soils that are severely degraded (case 1, say from severe erosion or intensive tillage, etc.) have low organic matter levels (empty glass) and have the potential to increase and store much more.

869b2743e564.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.09%3A_The_Dynamics_of_Raising_and_Maintaining_Soil_Organic_Matter_Levels
869b2743e564.sentence: The in-between scenario (case 2) may be a conventional grain or vegetable farm where organic matter levels are suboptimal and can still be increased.

2029b9d88efb.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.09%3A_The_Dynamics_of_Raising_and_Maintaining_Soil_Organic_Matter_Levels
2029b9d88efb.sentence: Here the glass is nearly full and not much additional organic matter can be stored.

f4eda50fdc1f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.09%3A_The_Dynamics_of_Raising_and_Maintaining_Soil_Organic_Matter_Levels
f4eda50fdc1f.sentence: In such cases we should focus on protecting the existing organic matter levels by minimizing losses.

fab6b10dd773.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.09%3A_The_Dynamics_of_Raising_and_Maintaining_Soil_Organic_Matter_Levels
fab6b10dd773.sentence: In the context of carbon farming and raising overall soil organic matter levels, benefits will accrue more in cases 1 and 2 than in case 3, where the soil is already close to being saturated with organic matter.

9d96b503173a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.09%3A_The_Dynamics_of_Raising_and_Maintaining_Soil_Organic_Matter_Levels
9d96b503173a.sentence: Moreover, if farms that fit case 3 are located near those that fit cases 1 or 2, there are potential gains from transferring the excess organic residues, like manure from a livestock farm to a farm growing only grain crops.

56cd26547442.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.09%3A_The_Dynamics_of_Raising_and_Maintaining_Soil_Organic_Matter_Levels
56cd26547442.sentence: Assuming that the same management pattern has occurred for many years, a fairly simple model can be used to estimate the percent of organic matter in a soil when it reaches an equilibrium of gains and losses.

079b99a74ab9.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.09%3A_The_Dynamics_of_Raising_and_Maintaining_Soil_Organic_Matter_Levels
079b99a74ab9.sentence: To use the model you need to assume reasonable values for rates of addition of organic material and for soil organic matter decomposition rates in the soil.

5f0fd600a7ca.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.09%3A_The_Dynamics_of_Raising_and_Maintaining_Soil_Organic_Matter_Levels
5f0fd600a7ca.sentence: It takes about 5,000 pounds of organic residues added annually to a sandy loam soil (with an estimated decomposition rate of 3% per year) to result eventually in a soil with 1.7% organic matter.

509934125f60.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.09%3A_The_Dynamics_of_Raising_and_Maintaining_Soil_Organic_Matter_Levels
509934125f60.sentence: On the other hand, 7,500 pounds of residues added annually to a well-drained, coarse-textured soil (with a soil organic matter mineralization, or decomposition, rate of 5% per year) are estimated to result after many years in only 1.5% soil organic matter.

cacdaf45010b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.09%3A_The_Dynamics_of_Raising_and_Maintaining_Soil_Organic_Matter_Levels
cacdaf45010b.sentence: If a soil starts at 1% organic matter content, it will have an annual net gain of around 350 pounds of organic matter per acre in the first decade, decreasing to very small net gains after decades of following the same practices (Figure 3.8a).

a080e0e90c81.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.09%3A_The_Dynamics_of_Raising_and_Maintaining_Soil_Organic_Matter_Levels
a080e0e90c81.sentence: Thus, even though 5,000 pounds per acre are added each year, the net yearly gain decreases as the soil organic matter content reaches a steady state.

f1149819b6cb.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.07%3A_How_Much_Organic_Matter_Is_Enough
f1149819b6cb.sentence: For example, 2% organic matter in a sandy soil is very good and difficult to reach, but in a clay soil 2% indicates a greatly depleted situation.

6379ddec0569.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.07%3A_How_Much_Organic_Matter_Is_Enough
6379ddec0569.sentence: Some research has been conducted to determine the levels of organic matter where the fine soil mineral particles become saturated, having adsorbed as many organic compounds as possible.

6d278e9b6f1d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.07%3A_How_Much_Organic_Matter_Is_Enough
6d278e9b6f1d.sentence: In this calculation, a soil with 20% silt and clay, for example, can store a maximum of 3.6% organic matter, while a soil with 80% silt and clay can hold 6.1% organic matter.

5b4fe2ae4222.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.07%3A_How_Much_Organic_Matter_Is_Enough
5b4fe2ae4222.sentence: This does not include the additional particulate organic matter that may be either subject to rapid decomposition (active) or protected from decomposition by soil organisms inside small (micro) aggregates (part of the passive organic matter).

a8e9f828997e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.07%3A_How_Much_Organic_Matter_Is_Enough
a8e9f828997e.sentence: Organic matter accumulation takes place slowly and is difficult to detect in the short term by measurements of total soil organic matter.

91c5ad98af8e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.07%3A_How_Much_Organic_Matter_Is_Enough
91c5ad98af8e.sentence: It determines the amount of organic matter thought to be the active portion, is more sensitive to soil management than total organic matter and is an early indicator for soil health improvement (see Chapter 23).

47b47d6d4b65.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.07%3A_How_Much_Organic_Matter_Is_Enough
47b47d6d4b65.sentence: On slopes, strongly erodible soils, or soils that have been eroded already, require more input than soils on level lands.

6a77daeb05af.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.08%3A_Organic_Matter_and_Cropping_Systems
6a77daeb05af.sentence: Natural (virgin) soils generally have much higher organic matter levels than agricultural soils.

0f815e1be0fb.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.08%3A_Organic_Matter_and_Cropping_Systems
0f815e1be0fb.sentence: But there are also considerable differences among cropping systems that can be generalized as follows: In a cash grain operation, about 55–60% of the aboveground plant biomass is harvested as grain and sold off the farm, thereby returning less than half of the mass of the aboveground plant to the soil.

91fc745e7e7d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.08%3A_Organic_Matter_and_Cropping_Systems
91fc745e7e7d.sentence: The nutrients removed in the crops are replaced through fertilizers, but the carbon is not.

643225ab8564.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.08%3A_Organic_Matter_and_Cropping_Systems
643225ab8564.sentence: On dairy farms, on the other hand, the crops are commonly fully harvested as a forage and fed to the animals, and then most of the plant biomass, including nutrients and carbon, is returned to the field as manure.

251abc93632c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.08%3A_Organic_Matter_and_Cropping_Systems
251abc93632c.sentence: But a typical organic vegetable system imports a lot of compost or manure to maintain soil fertility and thereby applies quite a lot of organic matter to the soil.

4c2af8286c70.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.08%3A_Organic_Matter_and_Cropping_Systems
4c2af8286c70.sentence: Soils that were used to grow annual grain crops (corn, soybeans, wheat) averaged 2.9% organic matter and conventional processing vegetables averaged 2.7%.

23f95e3d71ba.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.08%3A_Organic_Matter_and_Cropping_Systems
23f95e3d71ba.sentence: Dairy fields averaged somewhat higher levels (3.4%) and mixed vegetables (mainly small organic farms) averaged 3.9% organic matter.

eea820e69413.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.08%3A_Organic_Matter_and_Cropping_Systems
eea820e69413.sentence: The highest organic matter levels, however, were measured for pastures (4.5%), where much of the plant is recycled as manure and the soil is not tilled.

c0fecac94af0.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.08%3A_Organic_Matter_and_Cropping_Systems
c0fecac94af0.sentence: A recent New York study analyzed soil organic matter levels and soil health for such distinctive cropping systems and found considerable differences (Table 3.3).

3724347d2201.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.08%3A_Organic_Matter_and_Cropping_Systems
3724347d2201.sentence: Aggregate stability, which is a good indicator of the physical health of the soil, is greater when the organic matter content is higher and the soil is not tilled (Table 3.3).

628da3cb4818.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.08%3A_Organic_Matter_and_Cropping_Systems
628da3cb4818.sentence: Conventional vegetable | Intensive tillage; mostly inorganic fertilizer; crop biomass removed | 2.7 | 27

40255f9a0af3.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.08%3A_Organic_Matter_and_Cropping_Systems
40255f9a0af3.sentence: Pasture | No-till; perennial forage crop; crop biomass mostly recycled through manure | 4.5 | 70

fcbd432bc7c0.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/09%3A_Managing_for_High-Quality_Soils_and_Focusing_on_Organic_Matter_Management/9.01%3A_Introduction
fcbd432bc7c0.sentence: All actions taken to improve soil health should contribute to one or more of the following: 1) growing healthy plants, 2) suppressing pests or 3) increasing beneficial organisms.

459a54107833.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/09%3A_Managing_for_High-Quality_Soils_and_Focusing_on_Organic_Matter_Management/9.01%3A_Introduction
459a54107833.sentence: These should be done using practices that also reduce environmental impacts.

cd134c247fb2.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/09%3A_Managing_for_High-Quality_Soils_and_Focusing_on_Organic_Matter_Management/9.01%3A_Introduction
cd134c247fb2.sentence: Soil health management practices that contribute to these overall goals can be grouped as follows: 1) minimize soil disturbance; 2) keep soil covered; 3) maximize biodiversity; 4) manage water to reduce runoff and promote crop needs and timely fieldwork; and 5) maintain desired range of pH and nutrients to grow healthy crops without excessive nutrient loss.

ae51d64a6776.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/09%3A_Managing_for_High-Quality_Soils_and_Focusing_on_Organic_Matter_Management/9.01%3A_Introduction
ae51d64a6776.sentence: First and foremost, various practices to build up and maintain high levels of soil organic matter are key to long-term sustainability because each practice has multiple positive effects, and all of the practices are related to enhancing soil and field habitat for growing plants.

b6e799eafb20.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/09%3A_Managing_for_High-Quality_Soils_and_Focusing_on_Organic_Matter_Management/9.01%3A_Introduction
b6e799eafb20.sentence: Second, developing and maintaining the best possible soil physical condition often require other types of practices in addition to those that directly impact soil organic matter.

a6f76dfbd204.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/09%3A_Managing_for_High-Quality_Soils_and_Focusing_on_Organic_Matter_Management/9.01%3A_Introduction
a6f76dfbd204.sentence: Last, although good organic matter management goes a long way toward providing good plant nutrition in an environmentally sound way, good nutrient management involves additional practices.

e03b82debd16.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/09%3A_Managing_for_High-Quality_Soils_and_Focusing_on_Organic_Matter_Management/9.04%3A_Besides_Organic_Matter_Management
e03b82debd16.sentence: Many of the practices that build up and maintain soil organic matter enrich the soil with nutrients or make it easier to manage nutrients in ways that satisfy crop needs and are also environmentally sound.

47f343a38f57.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/09%3A_Managing_for_High-Quality_Soils_and_Focusing_on_Organic_Matter_Management/9.04%3A_Besides_Organic_Matter_Management
47f343a38f57.sentence: However, specific nutrient management practices are needed, such as testing manure to check its nutrient content before applying additional nutrient sources.

548bdd8fd940.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/09%3A_Managing_for_High-Quality_Soils_and_Focusing_on_Organic_Matter_Management/9.04%3A_Besides_Organic_Matter_Management
548bdd8fd940.sentence: For example, a legume cover crop increases a soil’s active organic matter and reduces erosion, but it also adds nitrogen that can be used to nourish the next crop.

0df7330e8b8d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/09%3A_Managing_for_High-Quality_Soils_and_Focusing_on_Organic_Matter_Management/9.04%3A_Besides_Organic_Matter_Management
0df7330e8b8d.sentence: Cover crops and deep-rooted rotation crops help to cycle nitrate, potassium, calcium and magnesium that might be lost to leaching below crop roots.

0cdedec1e6b6.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/09%3A_Managing_for_High-Quality_Soils_and_Focusing_on_Organic_Matter_Management/9.04%3A_Besides_Organic_Matter_Management
0cdedec1e6b6.sentence: Importing mulches or manures onto the farm also adds nutrients along with organic materials.

6d1fe1fa9e04.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/09%3A_Managing_for_High-Quality_Soils_and_Focusing_on_Organic_Matter_Management/9.04%3A_Besides_Organic_Matter_Management
6d1fe1fa9e04.sentence: And as discussed above, it is possible to overload soils with nutrients by bringing large quantities of organic materials such as manures or composts from off the farm for routine annual applications.

2021e83dbb5e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/09%3A_Managing_for_High-Quality_Soils_and_Focusing_on_Organic_Matter_Management/9.04%3A_Besides_Organic_Matter_Management
2021e83dbb5e.sentence: Other examples of nutrient management practices not directly related to organic matter management include applying nutrients timed to plant needs, liming acidic soils and interpreting soil tests to decide on the appropriate amounts of nutrients to apply (see chapters 18 – 21).

b9944284df52.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.03%3A_Human_Influences
b9944284df52.sentence: Levels of soil organic matter may fluctuate during the different stages of a crop rotation.

d4fcdc035b23.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.03%3A_Human_Influences
d4fcdc035b23.sentence: While annual row crops under conventional moldboard-plow cultivation usually result in decreased soil organic matter, perennial legumes, grasses and legume-grass forage crops tend to increase soil organic matter.

9f4362c26cfd.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.03%3A_Human_Influences
9f4362c26cfd.sentence: The high amount of root production by hay and pasture crops, plus the lack of soil disturbance, causes organic matter to accumulate in the soil.

e96642909e1a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.03%3A_Human_Influences
e96642909e1a.sentence: Having sod crops as part of a rotation reduces the loss of topsoil, decreases decomposition of residues, and builds up organic matter by the extensive residue addition of plant roots.

3b2467adb151.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.03%3A_Human_Influences
3b2467adb151.sentence: When corn grain is harvested, more residues are left in the field than after soybean, wheat, potato or lettuce harvests.

7ee05dc18024.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.03%3A_Human_Influences
7ee05dc18024.sentence: When corn grain is harvested, more residues remain in the field than when the entire plant is harvested for silage or when stover is used for purposes like bioenergy (Figure 3.4).

96477b3aabd1.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.03%3A_Human_Influences
96477b3aabd1.sentence: Cover crops help protect soils from erosion during the part of the year between commercial crops when soils would otherwise be bare.

98655d6400bb.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.03%3A_Human_Influences
98655d6400bb.sentence: In addition to protecting organic-matter-rich topsoil from erosion, cover crops may add significant amounts of organic materials to soil.

8e5c6f070c0d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.03%3A_Human_Influences
8e5c6f070c0d.sentence: But the actual amount added is determined by the type of cover crop (grass species versus legumes versus brassicas, etc.) and how much biomass accumulates before it is suppressed/killed in order to plant the following commercial crop.

0a93e32a89b1.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.03%3A_Human_Influences
0a93e32a89b1.sentence: Erosion loss of topsoil that is rich in organic matter has dramatically reduced the total amount of organic matter stored in many soils after they were developed for agriculture.

c9dfa2c6d086.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.03%3A_Human_Influences
c9dfa2c6d086.sentence: However, agricultural practices greatly accelerate erosion whether by water, wind or even tillage practices themselves (see Chapter 16).

2fe20063ac65.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.03%3A_Human_Influences
2fe20063ac65.sentence: It is estimated that erosion in the United States is responsible for annual losses of about $1 billion in available nutrients and many times more in total soil nutrients.

3cf2af08d154.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.03%3A_Human_Influences
3cf2af08d154.sentence: In fact, yields may decrease by 5–10% when only moderate erosion occurs.

808f8d3e7e01.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.03%3A_Human_Influences
808f8d3e7e01.sentence: Yields may suffer a decrease of 10–20% or more with severe erosion.

b3284ca79de6.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.03%3A_Human_Influences
b3284ca79de6.sentence: The results of a study of three Midwestern soils (referred to as Corwin, Miami and Morley), shown in Table 3.1, indicate that erosion greatly affects both organic matter levels and water-holding ability.

75e16c3e4518.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.03%3A_Human_Influences
75e16c3e4518.sentence: An old practice that helps maintain or increase soil organic matter is to apply manures or other organic residues generated off the field.

e9411bcd3a0a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.03%3A_Human_Influences
e9411bcd3a0a.sentence: A study in Vermont found that between 20 and 30 tons (wet weight, including straw or sawdust bedding) of dairy manure per acre were needed to maintain soil organic matter levels when silage corn was grown each year.

0902376e9f60.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.03%3A_Human_Influences
0902376e9f60.sentence: Varying types of manure—bedded, liquid stored, digested, etc.—can produce very different effects on soil organic matter and nutrient availability.

f0bd56f90f65.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.03%3A_Human_Influences
f0bd56f90f65.sentence: Manures differ in their initial composition and are affected by how they are stored and handled in the field: for example, surface applied or incorporated, which we discuss in Chapter 12.

43fdcf7464ff.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/03%3A_Amount_of_Organic_Matter_in_Soils/3.03%3A_Human_Influences

13ec085b0564.title: Ecological stoichiometry
13ec085b0564.sentence: Ecological stoichiometry (more broadly referred to as biological stoichiometry) considers how the balance of energy and elements influences living systems.

7b4c2d1081e5.title: Ecological stoichiometry
7b4c2d1081e5.sentence: Specifically, how does the balance of energy and elements affect and how is this balance affected by organisms and their interactions.

a7042d353526.title: Ecological stoichiometry
a7042d353526.sentence: Similar to chemical stoichiometry, ecological stoichiometry is founded on constraints of mass balance as they apply to organisms and their interactions in ecosystems.

1687792f660c.title: Ecological stoichiometry
1687792f660c.sentence: Concepts of ecological stoichiometry have a long history in ecology with early references to the constraints of mass balance made by Liebig, Lotka, and Redfield.

dc3ece292297.title: Ecological stoichiometry
dc3ece292297.sentence: The difference, or mismatch, between the elemental demands of organisms and the elemental composition of resources leads to an elemental imbalance.

5992c8abefea.title: Ecological stoichiometry
5992c8abefea.sentence: Consider termites, which have a tissue carbon:nitrogen ratio (C:N) of about 5 yet consume wood with a C:N ratio of 300–1000.

0856fc5f60c0.title: Ecological stoichiometry
0856fc5f60c0.sentence: The ability to maintain internal chemical composition despite changes in the chemical composition and availability of resources is referred to as "stoichiometric homeostasis".

6d7e9e5019dc.title: Ecological stoichiometry
6d7e9e5019dc.sentence: Photoautotrophic organisms, such as algae and vascular plants, can exhibit a very wide range of physiological plasticity in elemental composition and thus have relatively weak stoichiometric homeostasis.

736188faf6f7.title: Ecological stoichiometry
736188faf6f7.sentence: In contrast, other organisms, such as multicellular animals, have close to strict homeostasis and they can be thought of as having distinct chemical composition.

7e7b83aa5ebe.title: Ecological stoichiometry
7e7b83aa5ebe.sentence: Ecological stoichiometry has been applied to studies of nutrient recycling, resource competition, animal growth, and nutrient limitation patterns in whole ecosystems.

4e5bb5476493.title: Ecological stoichiometry
4e5bb5476493.sentence: The growth rate hypothesis (GRH) addresses this phenomenon and states that the demands for phosphorus increase during active growth phases to produce P-rich nucleic acids in biomass production and are reflected in the P content of the consumer.

6149bd07d4c0.title: Isotope-ratio mass spectrometry
6149bd07d4c0.sentence: Isotope-ratio mass spectrometry (IRMS) is a specialization of mass spectrometry, in which mass spectrometric methods are used to measure the relative abundance of isotopes in a given sample.

61bd98d73532.title: Isotope-ratio mass spectrometry
61bd98d73532.sentence: This technique has two different applications in the earth and environmental sciences.

66c81b26bc75.title: Isotope-ratio mass spectrometry
66c81b26bc75.sentence: The analysis of 'stable isotopes' is normally concerned with measuring isotopic variations arising from mass-dependent isotopic fractionation in natural systems.

57c28eab3aa2.title: Isotope-ratio mass spectrometry
57c28eab3aa2.sentence: On the other hand, radiogenic isotope analysis involves measuring the abundances of decay-products of natural radioactivity, and is used in most long-lived radiometric dating methods.

36ea21a0905c.title: Isotope-ratio mass spectrometry
36ea21a0905c.sentence: Most instruments used for precise determination of isotope ratios are of the magnetic sector type.

d126a79ddbd3.title: Isotope-ratio mass spectrometry
d126a79ddbd3.sentence: First, it can be set up for multiple-collector analysis, and second, it gives high-quality 'peak shapes'.

35825d1d2d17.title: Isotope-ratio mass spectrometry
35825d1d2d17.sentence: In the most general terms the instrument operates by ionizing the sample of interest, accelerating it over a potential in the kilo-volt range, and separating the resulting stream of ions according to their mass-to-charge ratio (m/z).

7a06d202f2f1.title: Isotope-ratio mass spectrometry
7a06d202f2f1.sentence: The current of each ion beam is then measured using a 'Faraday cup' or multiplier detector.

0bd923379f91.title: Isotope-ratio mass spectrometry
0bd923379f91.sentence: Many radiogenic isotope measurements are made by ionization of a solid source, whereas stable isotope measurements of light elements (e.g. H, C, O) are usually made in an instrument with a gas source.

d5db76ebdbce.title: Isotope-ratio mass spectrometry
d5db76ebdbce.sentence: Samples must be introduced to the mass spectrometer as pure gases, achieved through combustion, gas chromatographic feeds, or chemical trapping.

96c1b21edc16.title: Isotope-ratio mass spectrometry
96c1b21edc16.sentence: For example, carbon isotope ratios are measured relative to the international standard for C. The C standard is produced from a fossil belemnite found in the Peedee Formation, which is a limestone formed in the Cretaceous period in South Carolina, U.S.A. The fossil is referred to as VPDB (Vienna Pee Dee Belemnite) and has 13C:12C ratio of 0.0112372.

fae465808704.title: Isotope-ratio mass spectrometry
fae465808704.sentence: Oxygen isotope ratios are measured relative the standard, V-SMOW (Vienna Standard Mean Ocean Water).

691cb1156a58.title: Isotope-ratio mass spectrometry

3924c02a0922.title: Stable-isotope probing
3924c02a0922.sentence: Stable-isotope probing (SIP) is a technique in microbial ecology for tracing uptake of nutrients in biogeochemical cycling by microorganisms.

639b36fc5fe3.title: Stable-isotope probing
639b36fc5fe3.sentence: A substrate is enriched with a heavier stable isotope that is consumed by the organisms to be studied.

a9bece7fc36f.title: Stable-isotope probing
a9bece7fc36f.sentence: Biomarkers with the heavier isotopes incorporated into them can be separated from biomarkers containing the more naturally abundant lighter isotope by isopycnic centrifugation.

95773e717e6e.title: Stable-isotope probing
95773e717e6e.sentence: For example, 13CO2 can be used to find out which organisms are actively photosynthesizing or consuming new photosynthate.

10fe3e595177.title: Stable-isotope probing
10fe3e595177.sentence: As the biomarker, DNA with 13C is then separated from DNA with 12C by centrifugation.

48befed734c0.title: Stable-isotope probing
48befed734c0.sentence: Sequencing the DNA identifies which organisms were consuming existing carbohydrates and which were using carbohydrates more recently produced from photosynthesis.

608995fbe1a1.title: Stable-isotope probing
608995fbe1a1.sentence: SIP with 18O-labeled water can be used to find out which organisms are actively growing, because oxygen from water is incorporated into DNA (and RNA) during synthesis.

b0cc3dbcde6c.title: Stable-isotope probing
b0cc3dbcde6c.sentence: When DNA is the biomarker, SIP can be performed using isotopically labeled C, H, O, or N, though 13C is used most often.

1696ac6aa990.title: Stable-isotope probing
1696ac6aa990.sentence: Similarly, nitrogen is less abundant in DNA (3.75 atoms per base, on average), so a weaker DNA buoyant density shift is observed with 15N- versus 13C-labeled or 18O-labeled substrates.

927221fd3e1f.title: Stable-isotope probing
927221fd3e1f.sentence: Because density shifts as a predictable function of the change in mass caused by isotope assimilation, stable isotope probing can be modeled to estimate the amount of isotope incorporation, an approach called quantitative stable isotope probing (qSIP), which has been applied to microbial communities in soils, marine sediments, and decomposing leaves to compare rates of growth and substrate assimilation among different microbial taxa.

4c119328302c.title: Isotope dilution
4c119328302c.sentence: Isotope dilution analysis is a method of determining the quantity of chemical substances.

0edaa12ed63f.title: Isotope dilution
0edaa12ed63f.sentence: In its most simple conception, the method of isotope dilution comprises the addition of known amounts of isotopically enriched substance to the analyzed sample.

d517f0270ab6.title: Isotope dilution
d517f0270ab6.sentence: Mixing of the isotopic standard with the sample effectively "dilutes" the isotopic enrichment of the standard and this forms the basis for the isotope dilution method.

f1a4e9d29ace.title: Isotope dilution
f1a4e9d29ace.sentence: Isotope dilution is classified as a method of internal standardisation, because the standard (isotopically enriched form of analyte) is added directly to the sample.

c3ba7dbab578.title: Isotope dilution
c3ba7dbab578.sentence: In addition, unlike traditional analytical methods which rely on signal intensity, isotope dilution employs signal ratios.

5692bc262182.title: Isotope dilution
5692bc262182.sentence: Owing to both of these advantages, the method of isotope dilution is regarded among chemistry measurement methods of the highest metrological standing.

07cbdbffd70a.title: Isotope dilution
07cbdbffd70a.sentence: Isotope dilution is almost exclusively employed with mass spectrometry in applications where high-accuracy is demanded.

3bed6ec73d6a.title: Isotope dilution
3bed6ec73d6a.sentence: For example, all National Metrology Institutes rely significantly on isotope dilution when producing certified reference materials.

71e984d71ec5.title: Isotope dilution
71e984d71ec5.sentence: In addition to high-precision analysis, isotope dilution is applied when low recovery of the analyte is encountered.

9c763b21596e.title: Isotope dilution
9c763b21596e.sentence: In a typical gas chromatography analysis, isotopic dilution can decrease the uncertainty of the measurement results from 5% to 1%.

1c105049b763.title: Isotope dilution
1c105049b763.sentence: It can also be used in mass spectrometry (commonly referred to as isotopic dilution mass spectrometry or IDMS), in which the isotopic ratio can be determined with precision typically better than 0.25%.

c35a5f3ef8d1.title: Isotope dilution
c35a5f3ef8d1.sentence: The single dilution method requires the knowledge of the isotopic composition of the isotopically enriched analyte (RB) and the amount of the enriched analyte added (nB).

3658b778bb6b.title: Isotope dilution
3658b778bb6b.sentence: Both of these variables are hard to establish since isotopically enriched substances are generally available in small quantities of questionable purity.

82c625cead2e.title: Isotope dilution

87bcc9e8fd96.title: Isotope dilution

fde394be9605.title: Microbial carbon pump
fde394be9605.sentence: The microbial carbon pump (MCP) is a biological process in the ocean where microorganisms, primarily bacteria and archaea, transform dissolved organic carbon (DOC) into refractory dissolved organic carbon (RDOC), which is resistant to further microbial degradation.

b68f2f07fc4d.title: Microbial carbon pump
b68f2f07fc4d.sentence: This process effectively sequesters carbon in the deep ocean for centuries to millennia, contributing significantly to long-term carbon storage and climate regulation.

b04152cdc97a.title: Microbial carbon pump
b04152cdc97a.sentence: This contrasts with the biological carbon pump, which sequesters carbon via sinking particulate organic matter (e.g., dead organisms or fecal pellets).

c56e0afeb614.title: Microbial carbon pump
c56e0afeb614.sentence: With this lowered activation energy, the additional carbon gets converted into CO2 instead of being used to build new microbial biomass.

53b08425b590.title: Q10 (temperature coefficient)
53b08425b590.sentence: Q10 is a measure of temperature sensitivity based on chemical reaction rates, and it applies to most physiological processes (e.g., respiration, digestion, photosynthesis).

148423e501c1.title: Q10 (temperature coefficient)
148423e501c1.sentence: Q10 is a unitless quantity, as it is the factor by which a rate changes.

e1c054b8da33.title: Q10 (temperature coefficient)
e1c054b8da33.sentence: If the reference temperature is 10 °C, Q10 represents the factor by which the rate is multiplied for each 10°C increase in temperature.

01456085bbb1.title: Q10 (temperature coefficient)
01456085bbb1.sentence: Rewriting this equation, the assumption behind Q10 is that the reaction rate R depends exponentially on temperature:

ad5c72293d75.title: Q10 (temperature coefficient)
ad5c72293d75.sentence: For most biological systems, the Q10 value is ~ 2 to 3 (the rate doubles or triples for every 10 °C increase in temperature).

eef3c11b5cc9.title: Q10 (temperature coefficient)
eef3c11b5cc9.sentence: In environmental sciences, the reference temperature for calculating Q10 is often chosen to be 0 °C or 10°C.

6ae9609fc7db.title: Q10 (temperature coefficient)
6ae9609fc7db.sentence: The Q10 temperature coefficient is a mathematical parameter that is thought to come from the late 19th century, in the work of van ’t Hoff.

7109d84da3d6.title: Soil classification

11392ec67200.title: Soil classification

4398a0685557.title: Soil classification
