53ebcf26b439.sentence: Soil classification is a dynamic subject, from the structure of the system, to the definitions of classes, to the application in the field.

9b291aaee849.title: World Reference Base for Soil Resources
9b291aaee849.sentence: The World Reference Base for Soil Resources (WRB) is an international soil classification system for naming soils and creating legends for soil maps.
9b291aaee849.key: World Reference Base for Soil Resources

8d44d89aea28.title: World Reference Base for Soil Resources
8d44d89aea28.sentence: It is edited by a working group of the International Union of Soil Sciences (IUSS).
8d44d89aea28.key: World Reference Base for Soil Resources

21fb403955a9.title: World Reference Base for Soil Resources
21fb403955a9.sentence: In 1992, the IRB working group decided to develop a new system named World Reference Base for Soil Resources (WRB) that should further develop the Revised Legend of the FAO soil classification and include some ideas of the more systematic IRB approach.
21fb403955a9.key: World Reference Base for Soil Resources

0294fe7d5862.title: World Reference Base for Soil Resources
0294fe7d5862.sentence: At the 16th World Congress of Soil Science in Montpellier in 1998, the first edition of the WRB was published.
0294fe7d5862.key: World Reference Base for Soil Resources

99bb425df4c6.title: World Reference Base for Soil Resources
99bb425df4c6.sentence: At the same congress, the ISSS endorsed the WRB as its correlation system for soil classification.
99bb425df4c6.key: World Reference Base for Soil Resources

f5e64c9047b7.title: World Reference Base for Soil Resources
f5e64c9047b7.sentence: (In 2014, the USDA soil taxonomy also received the status of a correlation system.) At the 18th World Congress of Soil Science in Philadelphia in 2006, the second edition of the WRB was presented, and at the 20th World Congress of Soil Science in Jeju in 2014, the third edition.
f5e64c9047b7.key: World Reference Base for Soil Resources

cb5687538797.title: World Reference Base for Soil Resources
cb5687538797.sentence: An update of the third edition was issued in 2015.
cb5687538797.key: World Reference Base for Soil Resources

e9bbeec43630.title: World Reference Base for Soil Resources
e9bbeec43630.sentence: At the 22nd World Congress of Soil Science in Glasgow in 2022, the fourth edition was published.
e9bbeec43630.key: World Reference Base for Soil Resources

62fbe8b9ba5a.title: World Reference Base for Soil Resources
62fbe8b9ba5a.sentence: The 4th edition is an open access document under the terms of the Creative Commons Attribution License, which permits use, distribution and reproduction in any medium, provided the original work is properly cited.
62fbe8b9ba5a.key: World Reference Base for Soil Resources

b11b77c8a0dd.title: World Reference Base for Soil Resources
b11b77c8a0dd.key: World Reference Base for Soil Resources

2901e5d473a8.title: World Reference Base for Soil Resources
2901e5d473a8.sentence: The first level has 32 Reference Soil Groups (RSGs).
2901e5d473a8.key: World Reference Base for Soil Resources

781228169059.title: World Reference Base for Soil Resources
781228169059.sentence: At the second level, for further differentiation, a set of qualifiers is added to the name of the RSG.
781228169059.key: World Reference Base for Soil Resources

2a0b190f5ed8.title: World Reference Base for Soil Resources
2a0b190f5ed8.key: World Reference Base for Soil Resources

4f3f44372420.title: World Reference Base for Soil Resources
4f3f44372420.sentence: The classification in WRB is based mainly on soil morphology (field and laboratory data) as an expression of pedogenesis.
4f3f44372420.key: World Reference Base for Soil Resources

8d396633a064.title: World Reference Base for Soil Resources
8d396633a064.sentence: Another difference with USDA soil taxonomy is that soil climate is regarded only as a soil-forming factor and not as a soil characteristic.
8d396633a064.key: World Reference Base for Soil Resources

9044cf53af4e.title: World Reference Base for Soil Resources
9044cf53af4e.sentence: The WRB has two hierarchical levels (see below) and has in that sense a similar approach as the French référencial pédologique (1992, 1995, 2008).
9044cf53af4e.key: World Reference Base for Soil Resources

f0b484d734e8.title: World Reference Base for Soil Resources
f0b484d734e8.sentence: Contrary to that, the USDA soil taxonomy is strongly hierarchical and has six levels.
f0b484d734e8.key: World Reference Base for Soil Resources

5562bb10fe7c.title: World Reference Base for Soil Resources
5562bb10fe7c.sentence: The WRB is not meant to replace national soil classification systems, which, for their area, may be more detailed than the WRB.
5562bb10fe7c.key: World Reference Base for Soil Resources

6e212656c047.title: Soil classification
6e212656c047.sentence: The European Union uses the World Reference Base for Soil Resources (WRB), currently the fourth edition is valid.

33c1904b4420.title: World Reference Base for Soil Resources
33c1904b4420.sentence: The names of the RSGs and the qualifiers start with capital letters.
33c1904b4420.key: World Reference Base for Soil Resources

891f50b4d566.title: World Reference Base for Soil Resources
891f50b4d566.sentence: They must be given in English and must not be translated into any other language in order to guarantee that a certain soil has the same name all over the world.
891f50b4d566.key: World Reference Base for Soil Resources

5d822d8e23c1.title: World Reference Base for Soil Resources
5d822d8e23c1.sentence: In 1982, the International Soil Science Society (ISSS; now: International Union of Soil Sciences, IUSS) established a working group named the International Reference Base for Soil Classification (IRB).
5d822d8e23c1.key: World Reference Base for Soil Resources

54b78194847b.title: World Reference Base for Soil Resources
54b78194847b.sentence: This draft was presented at the 15th World Congress of Soil Science in Acapulco in 1994.
54b78194847b.key: World Reference Base for Soil Resources

667959a01ba2.title: Soil type
667959a01ba2.sentence: A soil type is a taxonomic unit in soil science.

5300d4b075f8.title: Soil type
5300d4b075f8.sentence: All soils that share a certain set of well-defined properties form a distinctive soil type.

d6750e9f4d9a.title: Soil type
d6750e9f4d9a.sentence: In hierarchical soil classification systems, soil types mostly belong to the higher or intermediate level.

7b262542765f.title: Soil type
7b262542765f.sentence: A soil type can normally be subdivided into subtypes, and in many systems several soil types can be combined to entities of higher category.

3ad4e9a3e1c1.title: Soil type
3ad4e9a3e1c1.sentence: However, in the first classification system of the United States (Whitney, 1909), the soil type was the lowest level and the mapping unit.

80d47b71512a.title: Soil type
80d47b71512a.sentence: For the definition of soil types, some systems use primarily such characteristics that are the result of soil-forming processes (pedogenesis).

d0e4946216e6.title: Soil type
d0e4946216e6.sentence: An example is the German soil systematics.

3cc30433ecea.title: Soil type
3cc30433ecea.sentence: Other systems combine characteristics resulting from soil-forming processes and characteristics inherited from the parent material.

837a1a4eec4e.title: Soil type
837a1a4eec4e.sentence: Examples are the World Reference Base for Soil Resources (WRB) and the USDA soil taxonomy.

ceb9cbd20508.title: Soil type
ceb9cbd20508.sentence: Other systems do not ask whether the properties are the result of soil formation or not.

d873a8c0094b.title: Soil type
d873a8c0094b.sentence: An example is the Australian Soil Classification.

56106707aed0.title: Soil type
56106707aed0.sentence: A convenient way to define a soil type is referring to soil horizons.

3acbd39c0dc6.title: Soil type
3acbd39c0dc6.sentence: However, this is not always possible because some very initial soils may not even have a clear development of horizons.

5116892e8956.title: Soil type
5116892e8956.sentence: For other soils, it may be more convenient to define the soil type just referring to some properties common to the whole soil profile.

2b30e94c81f6.title: Soil type
2b30e94c81f6.sentence: For example, WRB defines the Arenosols by their sand content.

d3343cecfcbf.title: Soil type
d3343cecfcbf.sentence: Many soils are more or less strongly influenced by human activities.

e1b99777a7ee.title: Soil type
e1b99777a7ee.sentence: This is reflected by the definition of many soil types in various classification systems.

50bc4eb6625f.title: Soil type
50bc4eb6625f.sentence: Because soil type is a very general and widely used term, many soil classification systems do not use it for their definitions.

2dcae027edf8.title: Soil type
2dcae027edf8.sentence: The USDA soil taxonomy has six hierarchical levels that are named order, suborder, great group, subgroup, family, and series.

98c345215d58.title: Soil type
98c345215d58.sentence: The WRB calls the first level Reference Soil Group.

2aed467f6e48.title: USDA soil taxonomy
2aed467f6e48.sentence: A soil phase of series, originally called 'soil type' describes the soil surface texture, slope, stoniness, saltiness, erosion, and other conditions.

ee9b4f26582d.title: USDA soil taxonomy
ee9b4f26582d.sentence: USDA soil taxonomy (ST), developed by the United States Department of Agriculture and the National Cooperative Soil Survey, provides an elaborate classification of soil types according to several parameters (most commonly their properties) and in several levels: Order, Suborder, Great Group, Subgroup, Family, and Series.

64d151a3dabf.title: USDA soil taxonomy
64d151a3dabf.sentence: They are, from most general to specific: order, suborder, great group, subgroup, family and series.

3e1858d0d5bd.title: USDA soil taxonomy
3e1858d0d5bd.sentence: A taxonomy is an arrangement in a systematic manner; the USDA soil taxonomy has six levels of classification.

1c0ce6ca3429.title: USDA soil taxonomy
1c0ce6ca3429.sentence: There are 12 soil orders (the top hierarchical level) in soil taxonomy.

64b40f69a996.title: USDA soil taxonomy
64b40f69a996.sentence: Forty-seven suborders are recognized in the United States.

3772ca7d53e2.title: USDA soil taxonomy
3772ca7d53e2.sentence: About 185 great groups are recognized in the United States.

87aeafc0d54b.title: USDA soil taxonomy
87aeafc0d54b.sentence: About 1,000 soil subgroups are defined in the United States.

b1f518dc290e.title: USDA soil taxonomy
b1f518dc290e.sentence: About 4,500 soil families are recognised in the United States.

f68ea89e7370.title: USDA soil taxonomy
f68ea89e7370.sentence: More than 14,000 soil series are recognised in the United States.

52dbef8388b7.title: USDA soil taxonomy
52dbef8388b7.sentence: Soil properties that can be measured quantitatively are used in this classification system – they include: depth, moisture, temperature, texture, structure, cation exchange capacity, base saturation, clay mineralogy, organic matter content and salt content.

b6cf86b4fe27.title: USDA soil taxonomy
b6cf86b4fe27.sentence: The classification was originally developed by Guy Donald Smith, former director of the U.S. Department of Agriculture's soil survey investigations.

9525381b2900.title: Soil classification
9525381b2900.sentence: This is a substantial revision of the 1938 USDA soil taxonomy which was a strictly natural system.

5326532de0b7.title: National Cooperative Soil Survey
5326532de0b7.sentence: By 1945 the development of a new system began.

059feec74aa4.title: National Cooperative Soil Survey
059feec74aa4.sentence: A series of approximations followed and the 7th approximation came out in 1960.

4f738489fc4f.title: National Cooperative Soil Survey
4f738489fc4f.sentence: USDA soil taxonomy, with 10 soil orders came out in 1975.

b63f3f43d305.title: National Cooperative Soil Survey
b63f3f43d305.sentence: It was revised into the 2nd edition with 12 soil orders in 1999.

0cc6c6cc1592.title: Soil classification
0cc6c6cc1592.sentence: As indicated, this is a hierarchical system that is a hybrid of both natural and objective criteria.

cce66764145f.title: Soil classification
cce66764145f.sentence: Criteria are designed to guide choices in land use and soil management.

f8e333298952.title: Soil classification
f8e333298952.sentence: USDA soil taxonomy provides the core criteria for differentiating soil map units.

ac99264bb98d.title: USDA soil taxonomy
ac99264bb98d.sentence: The names of the orders end with the suffix -sol.

b5d660c4c75c.title: USDA soil taxonomy
b5d660c4c75c.sentence: The criteria for the different soil orders include properties that reflect major differences in the genesis of soils.

1efc84693f61.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/03%3A_Taxonomy/3.01%3A_Introduction
1efc84693f61.sentence: Soil Taxonomy is a quantitative system based on soil properties that can be observed or measured, organized in a hierarchy based on six categories beginning with 12 broad soil orders and narrowing in specificity to more than 23,000 series.

fd5a5617b900.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/03%3A_Taxonomy/3.01%3A_Introduction
fd5a5617b900.sentence: Soil Taxonomy helps in extrapolating soil management research among similar soils around the world.

e3edf86714e3.title: FAO soil classification
e3edf86714e3.sentence: The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) developed a supra-national classification, which offers useful generalizations about pedogenesis in relation to the interactions between the main soil-forming factors.

6d5008822499.title: World Reference Base for Soil Resources
6d5008822499.sentence: From 1971 to 1981, the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) and UNESCO published the Soil Map of the World, 10 volumes, scale 1: 5 M).
6d5008822499.key: World Reference Base for Soil Resources

6062235a8bd5.title: World Reference Base for Soil Resources
6062235a8bd5.sentence: The Legend for this map, published in 1974 under the leadership of Rudi Dudal, became the FAO soil classification.
6062235a8bd5.key: World Reference Base for Soil Resources

de4d98df6761.title: FAO soil classification
de4d98df6761.sentence: It was first published in form of the UNESCO Soil Map of the World (1974) (scale 1: 5 M.).

e22d57dbb431.title: World Reference Base for Soil Resources
e22d57dbb431.sentence: Many ideas from national soil classification systems were brought together in this worldwide-applicable system, among them the idea of diagnostic horizons as established in the '7th approximation to the USDA soil taxonomy' from 1960.
e22d57dbb431.key: World Reference Base for Soil Resources

42f2e9ef3dfa.title: Soil science
42f2e9ef3dfa.sentence: The FAO soil classification, in turn, borrowed from modern soil classification concepts, including USDA soil taxonomy.

96c7bc2651fb.title: FAO soil classification
96c7bc2651fb.sentence: The Soil Units (106) were mapped as Soil Associations, designated by the dominant soil unit:

f3e5c3307fc0.title: FAO soil classification
f3e5c3307fc0.sentence: - with soil phases (soil properties, such as saline, lithic, stony),

3eab84732c98.title: FAO soil classification
3eab84732c98.sentence: - with three textural classes (coarse, medium, and fine)

13243602124a.title: FAO soil classification
13243602124a.sentence: - three slopes classes superimposed (level to gently undulating, rolling to hilly, and steeply dissected to mountainous)

4ce2e6f61150.title: FAO soil classification
4ce2e6f61150.sentence: The FAO soil map was a very simple classification system with units very broad, but was the first truly international system, and most soils could be accommodated on the basis of their field descriptions.

0bac53e5105b.title: FAO soil classification
0bac53e5105b.sentence: The FAO soil map was intended for mapping soils at a continental scale but not at local scale.

73c430c9953d.title: FAO soil classification
73c430c9953d.sentence: In 1988 the FAO published a Revised Legend with 153 Soil Units forming 28 Major Soil Groupings.

41b1cb4c418c.title: FAO soil classification
41b1cb4c418c.sentence: It serves as basis for the Harmonized World Soil Database.

23e9160ff1d4.title: FAO soil classification
23e9160ff1d4.sentence: Originally developed as a legend to the Soil Map of the World, the classification was applied by United Nations sponsored projects.

1a74c6843263.title: FAO soil classification
1a74c6843263.sentence: Many countries modified this system to fit their particular needs.

5957b9a7681e.title: FAO soil classification
5957b9a7681e.sentence: Many of the names offered in that classification are known in many countries and do have similar meanings.

198c935286dd.title: FAO soil classification
198c935286dd.sentence: In 1998 this system was replaced by the World Reference Base for Soil Resources.

842de54eaf5a.title: Leptosol
842de54eaf5a.sentence: In the FAO soil classification for the FAO/UNESCO Soil Map of the World (1974) the Leptosols on calcareous rock were called Rendzinas, those on acid rock were Rankers.

a4b2e51b1f7d.title: Canadian system of soil classification
a4b2e51b1f7d.sentence: The Canadian System of Soil Classification is more closely related to the American system than any other, but they differ in several ways.

7e18263093cb.title: Canadian system of soil classification
7e18263093cb.sentence: The Canadian system is designed to cover only Canadian soils.

c58beecbde88.title: Canadian system of soil classification
c58beecbde88.sentence: In 1955, a taxonomic system of soil classification specific to Canadian conditions was introduced.

4e8581198771.title: Canadian system of soil classification
4e8581198771.sentence: This system was designed to differentiate soils created by pedogenic processes in cool climatic environments.

c9c3026eaeec.title: Canadian system of soil classification
c9c3026eaeec.sentence: Before 1955, Canadian soil testing was based on systems of classification which were similar to methods being used in the United States.

98fbd25a3c88.title: Canadian system of soil classification
98fbd25a3c88.sentence: From general to specific, the major categories in this system are: Orders, Great Groups, Subgroups, Families, and Series.

27a98c8646f0.title: Canadian system of soil classification
27a98c8646f0.sentence: The Canadian system dispenses with the sub-order hierarchical level.

4fd01c6d5ae8.title: Canadian system of soil classification
4fd01c6d5ae8.sentence: Solonetzic and Gleysolic soils are differentiated at the order level.

5559a44fcd1e.title: Canadian system of soil classification
5559a44fcd1e.sentence: At its most general level, the Canadian System recognizes ten different Soil Orders.

631030658796.title: Canadian system of soil classification
631030658796.section: Subgroups, families and series > Great Group
631030658796.sentence: The 31 great group classes are formed by subdividing order classes on the basis of soil properties that reflect differences in soil-forming processes (e.g., kinds and amounts of organic matter in surface soil horizons).

e7b66faf464c.title: Canadian system of soil classification
e7b66faf464c.sentence: To classify in a soil in practice, an identification key in The Canadian System of Soil Classification is used.

7190d6db20b2.title: Canadian system of soil classification
7190d6db20b2.sentence: Decisions are made based on the properties of the horizons, such as thickness, Munsell colour, pH, or evidence of other soil-forming processes (eg, eluviation).

d994ca27249c.title: Canadian system of soil classification
d994ca27249c.sentence: Subgroups are based on the sequence of horizons in the pedon.

7b5e73e6916f.title: Canadian system of soil classification
7b5e73e6916f.sentence: Many subgroups intergrade to other soil orders.

c6d0ab8816b1.title: Canadian system of soil classification
c6d0ab8816b1.sentence: Families are based on parent material properties and soil climate.

0667900f4e56.title: Canadian system of soil classification
0667900f4e56.sentence: The soil family designation is much more specific; e.g., Orthic Gray Luvisol, clayey, mixed (mineralogy), cold, subhumid.

e5cf2937c3d5.title: Canadian system of soil classification
e5cf2937c3d5.sentence: Thus, for example, the series name Breton implies all the basic properties of the Luvisolic order, the Gray Luvisol great group, the Orthic Gray Luvisol subgroup and the fine, loamy, mixed, cold subhumid family of that subgroup as well as series-specific properties.

983541eec949.title: Canadian system of soil classification
983541eec949.sentence: A series name implies so much specific information about soil properties that a wide range of interpretations can be made on the probable suitability of the soil for a variety of uses.

412ef1f3919b.title: Canadian system of soil classification
412ef1f3919b.sentence: Limits between classes are arbitrary as there are few sharp divisions of the soil continuum in nature.

2bfabf8ed579.title: Canadian system of soil classification
2bfabf8ed579.sentence: The soil classification system changes as knowledge grows through soil mapping and research in Canada and elsewhere.

9e3f8b6e3a19.title: Soil classification
9e3f8b6e3a19.sentence: Recent research on Canadian soils proposes the addition of a Leptosolic order (soils that are shallow or over bedrock), complementing existing USDA and international soil orders, and highlighting regional variations and ongoing refinement in soil classification systems.

afeabc5a3e90.title: Australian Soil Classification
afeabc5a3e90.sentence: The Australian Soil Classification is the classification system currently used to describe and classify soils in Australia.

694016728195.title: Australian Soil Classification
694016728195.sentence: It is a general-purpose, hierarchical classification system, and consists of five categorical levels from the most general to the most specific: Order, Suborder, Great Group, Subgroup, and Family.

eed076d99a3f.title: Australian Soil Classification
eed076d99a3f.sentence: The Australian Soil Classification was developed by Ray Isbell, a retired soil scientist with CSIRO, and first published in 1996.

5e671b0906d0.title: Australian Soil Classification
5e671b0906d0.sentence: A revised first edition was published in 2002, a second edition in 2010 and a third edition in March 2021.

85d3e29032f8.title: Australian Soil Classification
85d3e29032f8.sentence: Since Ray Isbell's death in 2001 the National Committee on Soil and Terrain has led the updates and improvements to the classification and this committee is now listed as a co-author with Ray Isbell.

ea09c15887ef.title: Australian Soil Classification
ea09c15887ef.section: Structure of the classification system > Order level
ea09c15887ef.sentence: At the top, most general, level of the Australian Soil Classification, there are fifteen Soil Orders.

87b8f217bdf3.title: Australian Soil Classification
87b8f217bdf3.section: Structure of the classification system > Order level
87b8f217bdf3.sentence: They are: Anthroposols, Arenosols, Calcarosols, Chromosols, Dermosols, Ferrosols, Hydrosols, Kandosols, Kurosols, Organosols, Podosols, Rudosols, Sodosols, Tenosols and Vertosols.

12d9bef3a5f1.title: Australian Soil Classification
12d9bef3a5f1.section: Structure of the classification system > Order level
12d9bef3a5f1.sentence: The character of many of the Soil Orders reflects the arid, strongly-weathered nature of the Australian continent.

1a74d85c64f6.title: Australian Soil Classification
1a74d85c64f6.section: Structure of the classification system > Suborder level
1a74d85c64f6.sentence: For the Vertosol, Kurosol, Sodosol, Chromosol, Ferrosol, Dermosol and Kandosol orders, the suborder-level categories reflect the dominant colour of the upper part of the B2 horizon.

e19d83937bb4.title: Australian Soil Classification
e19d83937bb4.section: Structure of the classification system > Suborder level
e19d83937bb4.sentence: There are five suborder colour categories, namely Red, Brown, Yellow, Grey and Black.

da456e7c0d77.title: Australian Soil Classification
da456e7c0d77.section: Structure of the classification system > Suborder level
da456e7c0d77.sentence: The full suborder designation then becomes Red Kurosol, Grey Vertosol, for example.

5bf750e1a72e.title: Australian Soil Classification
5bf750e1a72e.section: Structure of the classification system > Suborder level
5bf750e1a72e.sentence: The remaining soil orders have suborder categories that reflect unique characteristics of the given order.

73d5db0eb158.title: Australian Soil Classification
73d5db0eb158.section: Structure of the classification system > Suborder level
73d5db0eb158.sentence: For example, the Hydrosol order is split into Intertidal Hydrosols, Supratidal Hydrosols, Extratidal Hydrosols, Hypersalic Hydrosols, Salic Hydrosols, Redoxic Hydrosols and Oxyaquic Hydrosols.

7146e8b20baf.title: Histosol
7146e8b20baf.sentence: In the Australian Soil Classification, Histosols are called Organosols.

a44802fac9ce.title: Podzol
a44802fac9ce.sentence: - The Australian Soil Classification uses the term Podosols.

6ec48aef5f15.title: Soil classification
6ec48aef5f15.sentence: Modern engineering classification systems are designed to allow an easy transition from field observations to basic predictions of soil engineering properties and behaviors.

5cbb06d28387.title: Soil classification
5cbb06d28387.sentence: The USCS and additional engineering description is standardized in ASTM D 2487.

0d17672581b6.title: Soil classification
0d17672581b6.sentence: Other engineering soil classification systems in the United States include the AASHTO Soil Classification System, which classifies soils and aggregates relative to their suitability for pavement construction, and the Modified Burmister system, which works similarly to the USCS but includes more coding for various soil properties.

cd13d87b0543.title: Soil classification
cd13d87b0543.sentence: A full geotechnical engineering soil description will also include other properties of the soil including color, in-situ moisture content, in-situ strength, and somewhat more detail about the material properties of the soil than is provided by the USCS code.

54ec767cf898.title: Soil classification
54ec767cf898.sentence: For soil resources, experience has shown that a natural system approach to classification, i.e. grouping soils by their intrinsic property (soil morphology), behaviour, or genesis, results in classes that can be interpreted for many diverse uses.

b29ad413a7d7.title: Soil classification
b29ad413a7d7.sentence: This is in contrast to a technical system approach to soil classification, where soils are grouped according to their fitness for a specific use and their edaphic characteristics.

1e2ddf7626d8.title: Soil classification
1e2ddf7626d8.sentence: Natural system approaches to soil classification, such as the French Soil Reference System (Référentiel pédologique français) are based on presumed soil genesis.

46e08c0cbdfc.title: Soil classification
46e08c0cbdfc.sentence: Differing concepts of pedogenesis, and differences in the significance of morphological features to various land uses can affect the classification approach.

d2922072ab61.title: Soil classification
d2922072ab61.sentence: Soil taxonomy based soil map units are additionally sorted into classes based on technical classification systems.

36588f4afc95.title: Soil classification
36588f4afc95.sentence: Land Capability Classes, hydric soil, and prime farmland are some examples.

4a904d8f2b0e.title: Soil classification
4a904d8f2b0e.sentence: Another approach is numerical classification, also called ordination, where soil individuals are grouped by multivariate statistical methods such as cluster analysis.

2c986ca1c9d8.title: Soil classification
2c986ca1c9d8.sentence: This produces natural groupings without requiring any inference about soil genesis.

b7fa40463d4f.title: USDA soil taxonomy
b7fa40463d4f.sentence: The soil moisture regimes are defined based on the levels of the groundwater table and the amounts of soil water available to plants during a given year in a particular region.

3a09be924f84.title: USDA soil taxonomy
3a09be924f84.sentence: The soil moisture regime, often reflective of climatic factors, is a major determinant of the productivity of terrestrial ecosystems, including agricultural systems.

35ca58cb82c0.title: USDA soil taxonomy
35ca58cb82c0.sentence: These categories are terminology modifiers at the soil suborder level of characterization.

ff7090d4d931.title: USDA soil taxonomy
ff7090d4d931.sentence: Soil Moisture Regime | Aquic | Soil is saturated with water and virtually free of gaseous oxygen for sufficient periods of time, such that there is evidence of poor aeration (gleying and mottling); common in wetlands.

c9aa1213bd54.title: USDA soil taxonomy
c9aa1213bd54.sentence: Soil Moisture Regime | Udic | Soil moisture is sufficiently high year-round in most years to meet plant requirement; common in humid regions.

a4f84bfbd388.title: USDA soil taxonomy
a4f84bfbd388.sentence: Soil Moisture Regime | Ustic | Soil moisture is intermediate between Udic and Aridic regimes; generally, plant-available moisture during the growing season, but severe periods of drought may occur; common in semi-arid regions.

5ba1076ab486.title: USDA soil taxonomy
5ba1076ab486.sentence: Soil Moisture Regime | Aridic | Soil is dry for at least half of the growing season and moist for less than 90 consecutive days; common in arid (desert-like) regions.

5680b629dc04.title: USDA soil taxonomy
5680b629dc04.sentence: Soil Moisture Regime | Xeric | Soil moisture regime is found in Mediterranean-type climates, with cool, moist winters and warm, dry summers. Like the Ustic Regime, it is characterized as having long periods of drought in the summer.

5ffb6b9bdf9d.title: National Cooperative Soil Survey
5ffb6b9bdf9d.sentence: In 1920 Marbut began his work on a soil classification scheme.

c68a2fd0b7cf.title: National Cooperative Soil Survey
c68a2fd0b7cf.sentence: His classification scheme became the 1935 system that was modified to become the system published in the 1938 Yearbook of Agriculture, Soils and Men: the 1938 USDA soil taxonomy.

9cd869613ee0.title: National Cooperative Soil Survey
9cd869613ee0.sentence: At the highest level of classification the soils were divided into pedocals and pedalfers.

01a33686fce9.title: National Cooperative Soil Survey
01a33686fce9.sentence: Pedocals were used in the drier climates and referred to the carbonate rich soils.

01372bc5d86b.title: National Cooperative Soil Survey
01372bc5d86b.sentence: The Pedalfers began about at the Udic border and referred to soils rich in Aluminum (Alumen) and Iron (Ferrous).

6279723646d5.title: National Cooperative Soil Survey
6279723646d5.sentence: Alfer became the root term for Alfisols.

b5f96a1696bb.title: National Cooperative Soil Survey
b5f96a1696bb.sentence: Following 1938, classifying soil series according to the system met with mixed success.

d241bdddcae6.title: Soil classification
d241bdddcae6.sentence: The U.S. Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) requires the classification of soils to protect workers from injury when working in excavations and trenches.

b703cd0726bf.title: Soil classification
b703cd0726bf.sentence: OSHA uses three soil classifications plus one for rock, based primarily on strength but also other factors which affect the stability of cut slopes:

159980bf1fb8.title: Soil classification
159980bf1fb8.sentence: - Type A - cohesive, plastic soils with unconfined compressive strength greater than 1.5 ton per square foot (tsf)(144 kPa), and meeting several other requirements (which induces a lateral earth pressure of 25 psf per ft of depth)

980dc23fa08c.title: Soil classification
980dc23fa08c.sentence: - Type B - cohesive soils with unconfined compressive strength between 0.5 tsf (48 kPa) and 1.5 tsf (144 kPa), or unstable dry rock, or soils which would otherwise be Type A (lateral earth pressure of 45 psf per ft of depth)

137082a7bf15.title: Soil classification
137082a7bf15.sentence: - Type C - granular soils or cohesive soils with unconfined compressive strength less than 0.5 tsf (48 kPa) or any submerged or freely seeping soil or adversely bedded soils (lateral earth pressure of 80 psf per ft of depth)

415917ee562c.title: Soil classification
415917ee562c.sentence: Each of the soil classifications has implications for the way the excavation must be made or the protections (sloping, shoring, shielding, etc.) that must be provided to protect workers from collapse of the excavated bank.

208fed8c2f24.title: Soil classification
208fed8c2f24.sentence: These safety-based classifications differ from scientific soil taxonomy systems, as they are designed primarily to guide construction practices rather than to study soil formation or environmental characteristics.

e2a4402a1785.title: World Reference Base for Soil Resources
e2a4402a1785.sentence: The classification is based on diagnostic horizons, diagnostic properties and diagnostic materials, altogether called diagnostics:
e2a4402a1785.key: World Reference Base for Soil Resources

d771dee4a9f3.title: World Reference Base for Soil Resources
d771dee4a9f3.sentence: - Diagnostic horizons are typical results of soil-forming processes showing a minimum thickness and therefore a horizontal appearance, thus forming a recognizable layer in the soil.
d771dee4a9f3.key: World Reference Base for Soil Resources

04b5a933b0ce.title: World Reference Base for Soil Resources
04b5a933b0ce.sentence: - Diagnostic properties are typical results of soil-forming processes or reflect specific conditions of soil formation.
04b5a933b0ce.key: World Reference Base for Soil Resources

933d2883abc4.title: World Reference Base for Soil Resources
933d2883abc4.sentence: - Diagnostic materials are materials that significantly influence soil-forming processes (pedogenesis) or are indicative of them.
933d2883abc4.key: World Reference Base for Soil Resources

0027a81f1347.title: World Reference Base for Soil Resources
0027a81f1347.sentence: They may be inherited from the parent material or be the result of soil-forming processes.
0027a81f1347.key: World Reference Base for Soil Resources

a845fbdc9542.title: World Reference Base for Soil Resources
a845fbdc9542.sentence: The diagnostics have names (e. g. argic horizon, stagnic properties, fluvic material).
a845fbdc9542.key: World Reference Base for Soil Resources

144e6bcc7638.title: List of vineyard soil types
144e6bcc7638.sentence: The soil composition of vineyards is one of the most important viticultural considerations when planting grape vines.

f8d7d7a0d297.title: List of vineyard soil types
f8d7d7a0d297.sentence: The soil supports the root structure of the vine and influences the drainage levels and amount of minerals and nutrients that the vine is exposed to.

05b305d6f3f3.title: List of vineyard soil types
05b305d6f3f3.sentence: The ideal soil condition for a vine is a layer of thin topsoil and subsoil that sufficiently retains water but also has good drainage so that the roots do not become overly saturated.

d484144e7a37.title: List of vineyard soil types
d484144e7a37.sentence: The ability of the soil to retain heat and/or reflect it back up to the vine is also an important consideration that affects the ripening of the grapes.

9a82774afca8.title: List of vineyard soil types
9a82774afca8.sentence: - Kimmeridgian soil – A gray-colored limestone-based soil originally identified in Kimmeridge, England.

2c2777dfda14.title: List of vineyard soil types
2c2777dfda14.sentence: This is the principal soil type of the Loire Valley, Champagne and Burgundy regions.

3074d7cdf0d4.title: List of vineyard soil types
3074d7cdf0d4.sentence: - Sand – Warm, airy soil that is composed of tiny particles of weathered rocks.

cb8926925ba6.title: List of vineyard soil types
cb8926925ba6.sentence: One of the few soils that the phylloxera louse does not thrive in, the soil drains well but does not have good water retention.

12b2b84a3429.title: USDA soil taxonomy
12b2b84a3429.sentence: Soil temperature regimes, such as frigid, mesic, and thermic, are used to classify soils at some of the lower levels of the Soil Taxonomy.

49bedec6c158.title: USDA soil taxonomy
49bedec6c158.sentence: These regimes are based on the mean annual soil temperature (MAST), mean summer temperature, and the difference between mean summer and winter temperatures all at a soil depth of 50 cm.

70e2a6917f70.title: USDA soil taxonomy
70e2a6917f70.sentence: The cryic temperature regime distinguishes some higher-level groups.

760aef3a28f1.title: USDA soil taxonomy
760aef3a28f1.sentence: It is normally assumed that the MAST (in °C) equals the sum of the mean annual air temperature plus 2 °C. If the difference between mean summer and winter temperatures is less than 6 °C, then add "Iso" at the front of the name of the Soil Temperature Class.

4396600093fa.title: USDA soil taxonomy
4396600093fa.sentence: Soil temperature regime | Hyperthermic | 22 °C or higher

959b7311d6d8.title: USDA soil taxonomy
959b7311d6d8.sentence: The soil suborders within an order are differentiated on the basis of soil properties and horizons which depend on soil moisture and temperature.

b8f7a7a31db2.title: USDA soil taxonomy
b8f7a7a31db2.sentence: The soil great group category is a subdivision of a suborder in which the kind and sequence of soil horizons distinguish one soil from another.

bc00a29368d2.title: USDA soil taxonomy
bc00a29368d2.sentence: Horizons marked by clay, iron, humus and hard pans and soil features such as the expansion-contraction of clays (that produce self-mixing provided by clay), temperature, and marked quantities of various salts are used as distinguishing features.

2efb2d7c18af.title: USDA soil taxonomy
2efb2d7c18af.sentence: Suborder: Xeralfs Great Group: Durixeralfs Subgroup: Abruptic Durixeralfs Family: Fine, Mixed, Active, thermic Abruptic Durixeralfs Series: San Joaquin (soil)

ef1961a5df1d.title: USDA soil taxonomy
ef1961a5df1d.sentence: The great group categories are divided into three kinds of soil subgroups: typic, intergrade and extragrade.

5cd90a49241a.title: USDA soil taxonomy
5cd90a49241a.sentence: A typic subgroup represents the basic or 'typical' concept of the great group to which the described subgroup belongs.

2e1561a9f14a.title: USDA soil taxonomy
2e1561a9f14a.sentence: An intergrade subgroup describes the properties that suggest how it grades towards (is similar to) soils of other soil great groups, suborders or orders.

4fe40a49db90.title: USDA soil taxonomy
4fe40a49db90.sentence: These properties are not developed or expressed well enough to cause the soil to be included within the great group towards which they grade, but suggest similarities.

6ce30bb2b908.title: USDA soil taxonomy
6ce30bb2b908.sentence: Extragrade features are aberrant properties which prevent that soil from being included in another soil classification.

d5738b52a9b2.title: USDA soil taxonomy
d5738b52a9b2.sentence: A soil family category is a group of soils within a subgroup and describes the physical and chemical properties which affect the response of soil to agricultural management and engineering applications.

0f180115ac58.title: USDA soil taxonomy
0f180115ac58.sentence: For some soils the criteria also specify the percentage of silt, sand and coarse fragments such as gravel, cobbles and rocks.

a0ff685e083b.title: USDA soil taxonomy
a0ff685e083b.sentence: A family may contain several soil series which describe the physical location using the name of a prominent physical feature such as a river or town near where the soil sample was taken.

67103df49cac.title: USDA soil taxonomy
67103df49cac.sentence: Suborder: Fluvents Great Group: Torrifluvents Subgroup: Typic Torrifluvents Family: Fine-loamy, mixed, superactive, calcareous, Typic Torrifluvents Series: Jocity, Youngston.

6076cd029ec1.title: Soil series
6076cd029ec1.sentence: Soil series as established by the National Cooperative Soil Survey of the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Natural Resources Conservation Service are a level of classification in the USDA Soil Taxonomy classification system hierarchy.

33cd266e8fff.title: Soil series
33cd266e8fff.sentence: Soil series consist of pedons that are grouped together because of their similar pedogenesis, soil chemistry, and physical properties.

4248a186c167.title: Soil in the United States
4248a186c167.sentence: The Soil series is the lowest category of the national soil classification system.

8fd43582b5d0.title: Soil series
8fd43582b5d0.sentence: The actual object of classification is the so-called soil individual, or pedon.

474477320182.title: Soil series
474477320182.sentence: These result in soils which perform similarly for land use purposes.

7bb2a22d18c6.title: Soil series
7bb2a22d18c6.sentence: The soil series concept was originally introduced in 1903.

11865b07e877.title: Soil series
11865b07e877.sentence: Soil series were originally intended to consist of groups of soils which were thought to be the same in origin but different in texture.

247cccf4da8b.title: Soil series
247cccf4da8b.sentence: Soils were thought to be alike in origin if they were derived from the same kind of rocks or if they were derived in sediments derived from the same kind of rocks and deposited at the same time.

4cd608bcde6f.title: Soil series
4cd608bcde6f.sentence: A soil series name generally is derived from a town or landmark in or near the area where the soil series was first recognized.

e7a79f82e8f6.title: Soil series
e7a79f82e8f6.sentence: For example, the Haugan Series was first identified near Haugan, Montana.

b7f284ce5c90.title: Soil series
b7f284ce5c90.sentence: The distribution of a given series is not necessarily restricted to the boundaries of only one county or state—for example, the Hagerstown Series was first described near Hagerstown, Maryland, but has also been found as far away as Tennessee and Kentucky.

7b0b68753d4e.title: Soil in the United States
7b0b68753d4e.sentence: Soil series are the most homogenous classes in the system of taxonomy.

91686e5fc0e5.title: Soil series
91686e5fc0e5.sentence: Depending on the context, a soil series may be defined as either a taxonomic unit or a mapping unit.

e114ddc98f0e.title: Soil series
e114ddc98f0e.sentence: It is a conceptual entity that describes the "central nucleus" or essential characteristics of a class.

150f256621af.title: Soil series
150f256621af.sentence: On the other hand, a mapping unit delineates areas of soil in the landscape (i.e. adjacent pedons or polypedons) that possess similar characteristics.

82a825b95342.title: Soil series
82a825b95342.sentence: The characteristics of a soil series (taxonomic unit) may or may not overlap either fully or partially with the characteristics of pedons within a given mapping unit.

9cb520a8367b.title: Soil in the United States
9cb520a8367b.sentence: The name of a soil series is the common reference term, used to name soil map units.

1596e501e094.title: Soil series
1596e501e094.sentence: The name of a map unit is usually named after the dominant component within the mapping unit.

6632b492f7cc.title: Soil series
6632b492f7cc.sentence: For example, the dominant component of the mapping unit LhE—Lily sandy loam, 15 to 35 percent slopes, very stony in the Greenbrier County, West Virginia soil survey is the Lily series, which comprises 80% of the mapping unit.

15071c21e5d4.title: Soil series
15071c21e5d4.sentence: The remaining 20% of the mapping unit consists of the Dekalb series, Berks series, and "soils that have stones covering less of the surface" than the Lily series.

2c88c469c646.title: List of U.S. state soils
2c88c469c646.sentence: A state soil is a soil that has special significance to a particular state.

46806b8336cd.title: List of U.S. state soils
46806b8336cd.sentence: Each state in the United States has selected a state soil, twenty of which have been legislatively established.

de0480014f9a.title: List of U.S. state soils
de0480014f9a.sentence: These official state soils share the same level of distinction as official state flowers and birds.

49fd0f76ad7c.title: List of U.S. state soils
49fd0f76ad7c.sentence: Also, representative soils have been selected for Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands.

d3da99dd2549.title: Cecil (soil)
d3da99dd2549.sentence: It extends from Virginia through North Carolina (where it is the state soil), South Carolina, Georgia and Alabama, with the typic Cecil pedon actually located in Franklin County, NC.

66582bdece3b.title: Udic moisture regime
66582bdece3b.sentence: The udic moisture regime is common to soils of humid climates which have well-distributed rainfall, or which have enough rain in summer so that the amount of stored moisture plus rainfall is approximately equal to, or exceeds, the amount of evapotranspiration.

28bf55bff7b5.title: Udic moisture regime
28bf55bff7b5.sentence: Water moves down through the soil at some time in most years.

f9a1b1f03fdb.title: Udic moisture regime
f9a1b1f03fdb.sentence: Some soil suborders, like udalf (alfisol) and udept (inceptisol), have an udic moisture regime.

5693b1f5b380.title: AASHTO Soil Classification System
5693b1f5b380.sentence: The AASHTO Soil Classification System was developed by the American Association of State Highway and Transportation Officials, and is used as a guide for the classification of soils and soil-aggregate mixtures for highway construction purposes.
