e93bab485c6c.title: Argillic
e93bab485c6c.sentence: Argillic is a term used in the United States Department of Agriculture Soil taxonomy to describe a subsurface horizon categorized by clay-enrichment.

38a4552b4edc.title: Argillic
38a4552b4edc.sentence: Clay accumulation occurs in the mineral soil through primarily illuviation and translocation of preexisting clays with some formation in-situ in the soil.

40bf0b0f5f16.title: Argillic
40bf0b0f5f16.sentence: The argillic horizon is required for the classification of Alfisols and Ultisols and cannot be found in Histosols or Entisol.

ae8b86ac0cd8.title: Argillic
ae8b86ac0cd8.sentence: The argillic horizon can be found with variable frequency in the rest of the soil orders.

967a89f385ff.title: Argillic
967a89f385ff.sentence: USDA soil taxonomy describes five different characteristics of argillic horizons and states that most occurrences of argillic horizons will meet two or more of the characteristic criteria.

d56b3119ae2d.title: Argillic
d56b3119ae2d.sentence: - The argillic must have at least 1.2x the amount of clay of any overlying eluvial horizon.

01b75271bec0.title: Argillic
01b75271bec0.sentence: - Clay films or bridges (cutans and argillans) must be visible either with the naked eye or with the use of a hand lens.Cutans are deposits of colloidal (suspended in solution) clay particles on the surfaces of aggregates, and argillans are parallel layers of cutans.

6fcdd138a293.title: Argillic
6fcdd138a293.sentence: According to a study conduct by James Bockheim at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 2014, the argillic horizon is found in 44% of soil series across the United States.

d9333ab4c1e2.title: Argillic
d9333ab4c1e2.sentence: Fragipans are layers of soil with high bulk density and brittle characteristics that form commonly within argillic horizons but can also be found in albic horizons.

4e7b01a80cf1.title: Argillic
4e7b01a80cf1.sentence: It is analogous to the Argic horizon in the World Reference Base system of soil taxonomy used outside of the United States.

3d80b875cbdc.title: Argillic
3d80b875cbdc.sentence: The term Argic used by the WRB system also comes from this same root.

a41d2c912d43.title: Argillic
a41d2c912d43.section: Taxonomy > World Reference Base Taxonomy Requirements
a41d2c912d43.sentence: - The argic horizon must meet the texture requirements of containing 8% or more of clay by volume, and having a texture class that is not sand.

029b89a26eda.title: Argillic
029b89a26eda.sentence: Though the climates of these soils are no longer suitable for the formation of argillic horizons, their existence proves that at one point in the past the climate was hot enough and wet enough for their development.

55d6c531dfa1.title: Ranker (soil)
55d6c531dfa1.sentence: Ranker is soil developed over non-calcareous material, usually rock.

2cd82401da60.title: Ranker (soil)
2cd82401da60.sentence: It is often called A/C soil, as the topsoil, or A horizon, is immediately over a C horizon (unaltered parent material).

5d6bf44ae64c.title: Ranker (soil)
5d6bf44ae64c.sentence: It is regarded in some soil classifications as lithomorphic, a group which also includes rendzina, similar soil over calcareous material.

3354c8dc5cf4.title: Polish Soil Classification
3354c8dc5cf4.sentence: - Type 2.1 "Rankers" (Polish: Rankery; WRB: Haplic Regosol (Dystric) or (Dystic, Folic), Leptic Regosol (Skeletic); ST: Lithic or Typic Udorthents, Lithic Udifolists)

6229a6b825bb.title: Polish Soil Classification
6229a6b825bb.sentence: Weakly developed soils (Polish: Gleby słabo ukształtowane; WRB: Leptosols, Regosols; ST: Entisols)

6c42bf3cf6d1.title: Ustic
6c42bf3cf6d1.sentence: Ustic is a class of soil moisture regime.

0a724331e888.title: Ustic
0a724331e888.sentence: The ustic moisture regime (Latin: ustus, burnt) applies to soils in which moisture is present, but limited, at times in which conditions are suitable for plant growth.

1119b963989c.title: Ustic
1119b963989c.sentence: The ustic moisture regime is intermediate between the aridic regime and the udic regime.

239f9e4fe94f.title: Ustic
239f9e4fe94f.sentence: The ustic moisture regime is common in semi-arid and sub-humid climates.

f42daf85660e.title: Ustic
f42daf85660e.sentence: For a soil to be classified as ustic, averaged across the year, stored moisture plus rainfall is less than the amount of water lost from the soil via evapotranspiration.

ee80d79caf0c.title: Ustic
ee80d79caf0c.section: Plants in the Ustic Moisture Regime
ee80d79caf0c.sentence: A principle characteristic of ustic soil is that it is preferable for the cultivation of crops that are tolerant, albeit resistant, to periods of drought.

2bc87307e928.title: Ustic
2bc87307e928.section: Plants in the Ustic Moisture Regime
2bc87307e928.sentence: For example, under an ustic moisture regime the commercial growth of maize is generally considered to require supplemental irrigation: however, this is not required under an udic moisture regime.

8a50ba9fa1d6.title: Ustic
8a50ba9fa1d6.sentence: Regions possessing an ustic soil moisture regime have a significantly large window for the harvesting of crops at the onset of the dry season.

2ae8f89d3605.title: Ustic
2ae8f89d3605.sentence: For example, Brazilian farmers in the Cerrado region leverage on the warm dry season to harvest their grain at a more leisurely pace.

ec86ffdfc8ef.title: Polish Soil Classification
ec86ffdfc8ef.sentence: The Polish Soil Classification (Polish: Systematyka gleb Polski) is a soil classification system used to describe, classify and organize the knowledge about soils in Poland.

b98e0952bd07.title: Soil Science Society of Poland
b98e0952bd07.sentence: It is also initiator and publisher of subsequent editions of Polish Soil Classification.

46708a38abe2.title: Polish Soil Classification
46708a38abe2.sentence: Previous ones were published in 1956, 1959, 1974 and 1989, and they, following Dokuchaiev's ideas, were relied mostly on the natural's criteria (quality) like soil forming processes and soil morphological features (4th edition was transient because diagnostic soil horizons appeared there).

c4710c25dd05.title: Polish Soil Classification
c4710c25dd05.sentence: Presented below the 5th edition of Polish Soil Classification was published by Soil Science Society of Poland in 2011 and was in use to 2019 when 6th edition of Polish Soil Classification was published.

aad0d07cec95.title: Polish Soil Classification
aad0d07cec95.sentence: 5th edition of classification, where it was possible, was built on quantitative criteria, like quantitative described diagnostic horizons, diagnostic materials and diagnostic properties.

6136f9f19add.title: Polish Soil Classification
6136f9f19add.sentence: Multilateral look at the soil manifested, in all editions of classification, that each soil was described by three types of characteristics:

eced4a68dc78.title: Polish Soil Classification
eced4a68dc78.sentence: - Genetical genesis described by type of soil – Polish: typ gleby based on diagnostic horizons, materials and properties,

e457778b8cbc.title: Polish Soil Classification
e457778b8cbc.sentence: - Geological origin of bedrock described by Polish: rodzaj gleby what might be literally translated as "kind" or "sort" of soil,

ef2ec73cbea0.title: Polish Soil Classification
ef2ec73cbea0.sentence: - Soil texture described of Polish: gatunek gleby what might be literally translated as "class" or "species" of soil.

e10424844a2e.title: Polish Soil Classification
e10424844a2e.sentence: Type of soil is a basic unit of the classification.

f00ca757cb0e.title: Polish Soil Classification
f00ca757cb0e.sentence: Types of soil are grouped into soil orders.

1d9af343561f.title: Polish Soil Classification
1d9af343561f.sentence: They are identified based on the presence or absence of diagnostic horizons and properties reflecting the effect of specific groups of soil forming processes.

826eff27b486.title: Polish Soil Classification
826eff27b486.sentence: The classification derives much of international systems: USDA soil taxonomy (1999) and World Reference Base for Soil Resources - WRB (2006).

cbbf059f0f88.title: Polish Soil Classification
cbbf059f0f88.sentence: Rusty soils (Polish: Gleby rdzawoziemne; WRB: Arenosols; ST: Entisols - Psamments)

1cbea590476b.title: Polish Soil Classification
1cbea590476b.sentence: In this order are situated sandy soils with rusty sideric or rubic horison of weathering or iron accumulating.

efaf5dd101be.title: Miami (soil)
efaf5dd101be.sentence: The Miami soil series is the state soil of Indiana.

c0d7dab592a3.title: Miami (soil)
c0d7dab592a3.sentence: Miami soils formed in calcareous, loamy till on the Wisconsin Till Plains.

06a2302d8577.title: Miami (soil)
06a2302d8577.sentence: The Miami series consists of moderately well drained soils formed in as much as 18 inches (46 cm) of loess or silty material and in the underlying loamy till on till plains.

ba19dc1eb2a6.title: Miami (soil)
ba19dc1eb2a6.sentence: The native vegetation is hardwood forest.

d267ec6fc455.title: Miami (soil)
d267ec6fc455.sentence: There are 794,994 acres (3,217 km2) of Miami soils mapped in Indiana.

4416d57ba1f1.title: Miami (soil)
4416d57ba1f1.sentence: Miami soils are fertile and have a moderate available water capacity.

d19087f663d5.title: Miami (soil)
d19087f663d5.sentence: The less sloping Miami soils are used mainly for corn, soybeans, or winter wheat.

6ac498f252ce.title: Miami (soil)
6ac498f252ce.sentence: Indiana is nationally ranked for agricultural production because of the highly productive Miami soils along with other prime farmland soils in the State.

96811be27fd2.title: Miami (soil)
96811be27fd2.sentence: Miami soils are classified in USDA soil taxonomy as fine-loamy, mixed, active, mesic Oxyaquic Hapludalfs.

80639d43a8e9.title: National Cooperative Soil Survey
80639d43a8e9.sentence: By 1906 Miami soil series included 16 soil types from the glaciated regions and Norfolk series included 12 soil types from the coastal plains.

dea0a48d74f8.title: Pedalfer
dea0a48d74f8.sentence: Pedalfer is composed of aluminum and iron oxides.

8391f9b4624a.title: Pedalfer
8391f9b4624a.sentence: It is a subdivision of the zonal soil order comprising a large group of soils in which sesquioxides increase relative to silica during soil formation.

f92a479ba1ef.title: Pedalfer
f92a479ba1ef.sentence: Pedalfers have three subdivisions of which one is Lateritic soils.

8ee88132d3f7.title: Pedalfer
8ee88132d3f7.sentence: It is not used in the current United States system of soil classification but the term commonly shows up in college geology texts.

9764692ede67.title: Pedalfer
9764692ede67.sentence: Pedalfer is a formative element in the United States soil taxonomic system for the Alfisols soil order.

a6712cb552dd.title: Pedalfer
a6712cb552dd.sentence: Alf is the formative element in the Alfisol name, and refers to aluminium (Al) and iron (Fe).

a058b5473317.title: Canadian system of soil classification
a058b5473317.sentence: This order includes all soils that have developed B horizons but do not meet the requirements of any of the orders described previously.

57f40b05c6d4.title: Canadian system of soil classification
57f40b05c6d4.sentence: Many Brunisolic soils have brownish B horizons without much evidence of clay accumulation, as in Luvisolic soils, or of amorphous materials, as in Podzolic soils.

d378bb8d5bee.title: Canadian system of soil classification
d378bb8d5bee.sentence: With time and stable environmental conditions, some Brunisolic soils will evolve to Luvisolic soils; others, to Podzolic soils.

1e0b3d60d8e4.title: Canadian system of soil classification
1e0b3d60d8e4.sentence: Covering almost 790,000 km2 (8.6%) of Canada's land area, Brunisolic soils occur in association with other soils in all regions south of the permafrost zone.

1eb0e3233d49.title: Canadian system of soil classification
1eb0e3233d49.sentence: Four great groups are distinguished on the basis of organic matter enrichment in the A horizon and acidity.

8528a141934e.title: Canadian system of soil classification
8528a141934e.sentence: Melanic Brunisols have an Ah horizon at least 10 cm thick and a pH above 5.5.

8aaad3892ec8.title: Canadian system of soil classification
8aaad3892ec8.sentence: Sombric Brunisols have an Ah horizon at least 10 cm thick, and are acid and their pH is below 5.5.

f8832f94e2d4.title: Canadian system of soil classification
f8832f94e2d4.sentence: Eutric Brunisols have the same basic properties as Melanic Brunisols, except that the Ah horizon, if any, is less than 10 cm thick.

6dbf0b7f131d.title: Canadian system of soil classification
6dbf0b7f131d.sentence: Dystric Brunisols are acidic and do not have an Ah horizon 10 cm thick.

92b9efa08713.title: Canadian system of soil classification
92b9efa08713.sentence: These soils are composed predominantly of organic matter in the upper half metre (more than 30% organic matter by weight) and do not have permafrost near the surface.

940ba06f1cd0.title: Canadian system of soil classification
940ba06f1cd0.sentence: They are the major soils of peatlands (e.g., swamp, bog, fen).

1fa9e82a0366.title: Canadian system of soil classification
1fa9e82a0366.sentence: Most organic soils develop by the accumulation of plant materials from species that grow well in areas usually saturated with water.

7737cd9a0133.title: Canadian system of soil classification
7737cd9a0133.sentence: Some organic soils are composed largely of plant materials deposited in lakes; others, mainly of forest leaf litter on rocky slopes in areas of high rainfall.

db8648691b30.title: Canadian system of soil classification
db8648691b30.sentence: Organic soils cover almost 374,000 km2 (4.1%) of Canada's land area: large areas occur in Manitoba, Ontario and northern Alberta, smaller areas in other provinces and territories.

ecffdc1ca8f3.title: Canadian system of soil classification
ecffdc1ca8f3.sentence: Organic soils are subdivided into four great groups.

daa748cc17a9.title: Canadian system of soil classification
daa748cc17a9.sentence: common in Canada, consist predominantly of relatively undecomposed organic material with clearly visible plant fragments; resistant fibres account for over 40% by volume.

b65c995cd767.title: Canadian system of soil classification
b65c995cd767.sentence: Most soils derived from Sphagnum mosses are Fibrisols.

13affa65aa70.title: Canadian system of soil classification
13affa65aa70.sentence: are more highly decomposed and contain less fibrous material than Fibrisols (10–40% by volume).

e7a0d3de8cec.title: Canadian system of soil classification
e7a0d3de8cec.sentence: consist mainly of humified organic materials and may contain up to 10% fibre by volume.

bb6f43644053.title: Canadian system of soil classification
bb6f43644053.sentence: consist mainly of thick deposits of forest litter overlying bedrock, fractured bedrock or unconsolidated material.

920d880f791a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/01%3A_Digging_In/1.08%3A_Soil_Classification_and_Distribution
920d880f791a.section: WETLAND SOILS > Gleysols and Organic Soils
920d880f791a.sentence: The two orders for wetland soils in the CSSC are differentiated based on the presence or absence of O horizons.

dada69eea19c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/01%3A_Digging_In/1.08%3A_Soil_Classification_and_Distribution
dada69eea19c.section: WETLAND SOILS > Gleysols and Organic Soils
dada69eea19c.sentence: Where the O horizon is at least 40 cm thick, wetland soils are classified into the Organic order; where the O horizon is less than 40 cm or absent altogether, wetland soils are classified into the Gleysolic order (Figure 8.11).

77246d57abeb.title: Canadian system of soil classification
77246d57abeb.sentence: These soils have an A horizon darkened by the addition of organic matter, usually from the decay of grass roots.

74418961047b.title: Canadian system of soil classification
74418961047b.sentence: The A horizon is neutral to slightly acid and is well supplied with bases such as calcium.

37dbf53e48aa.title: Canadian system of soil classification
37dbf53e48aa.sentence: The C horizon usually contains calcium carbonate (lime); it may contain more soluble salts such as gypsum.

26584ba7edd6.title: Canadian system of soil classification
26584ba7edd6.sentence: Chernozemic soils have mean annual soil temperatures above 0 °C and occur in regions of semiarid and subhumid climates.

a618b87aa68f.title: Canadian system of soil classification
a618b87aa68f.sentence: Covering more than 4% of Canada's land area, they are the major class of soils in the southern Interior Plains, where grass is the dominant native vegetation.

059b42fbe5cc.title: Canadian system of soil classification
059b42fbe5cc.sentence: The four great groups of Chernozemic soils are distinguished based upon surface horizon colour, associated with the relative dryness of the soil.

ec4b96d41c9a.title: Canadian system of soil classification
ec4b96d41c9a.sentence: Brown soils have brownish A horizons and occur in the driest area of the Chernozemic region.

55cdda083c05.title: Canadian system of soil classification
55cdda083c05.sentence: Dark Brown soils have a darker A horizon than Brown soils, reflecting a somewhat higher precipitation and associated higher organic-matter content.

b7f559260ece.title: Canadian system of soil classification
b7f559260ece.sentence: Black soils, associated with subhumid climates and tall-grass native vegetation, have a black A horizon which is usually thicker than that of Brown or Dark Brown soils.

a5314e6cbcce.title: Canadian system of soil classification
a5314e6cbcce.sentence: Dark Gray soils are transitional between grassland Chernozemic soils and the more strongly leached soils of forested regions.

7a37177ef744.title: Canadian system of soil classification
7a37177ef744.sentence: These soils have permafrost (permanently frozen material) within one metre of the surface (2 m if the soil is strongly cryoturbated; i.e., disturbed by frost action).

0053a7d4965e.title: Canadian system of soil classification
0053a7d4965e.sentence: As permafrost is a barrier to roots and water, the active layer (seasonally thawed material) above it may become a saturated, semifluid material in spring.

14f0553b7bd5.title: Canadian system of soil classification
14f0553b7bd5.sentence: Melting of ice and frozen materials, resulting from disturbance of the surface vegetation (boreal forest or tundra), may cause slumping of the soil and disruption of roads, pipelines and buildings.

00bc2a045234.title: Canadian system of soil classification
00bc2a045234.sentence: Cryosolic soils, occupying about 3,672,000 km2 (about 40%) of Canada's land area, are dominant in much of the Yukon, Northwest Territories and Nunavut and occur in northern areas of all but the Atlantic provinces (excluding Labrador).

1096717914f1.title: Canadian system of soil classification
1096717914f1.sentence: The order and its three great groups were defined in 1973, after soil and terrain surveys in the Mackenzie Valley yielded new knowledge about the properties, genesis and significance of these soils.

242b25bbc98b.title: Canadian system of soil classification
242b25bbc98b.sentence: Turbic Cryosols have a patterned surface (hummocks, stone nets, etc.) and mixed horizons or other evidence of cryoturbation.

67ef05f39820.title: Canadian system of soil classification
67ef05f39820.sentence: Static Cryosols lack marked evidence of cryoturbation; they are associated with sandy or gravelly materials.

7dee12d10dba.title: Canadian system of soil classification
7dee12d10dba.sentence: Organic Cryosols are composed dominantly of organic materials (e.g., peat).

69638ef9ba28.title: Canadian system of soil classification
69638ef9ba28.sentence: These soils are periodically or permanently saturated with water and depleted of oxygen.

a0022f03dd3a.title: Canadian system of soil classification
a0022f03dd3a.sentence: Depletion of ferric oxide removes the brownish colour common to many soils, leaving them grey.

f2ea4a0c2941.title: Canadian system of soil classification
f2ea4a0c2941.sentence: Thus, Gleysolic soils are usually identified by their poor drainage and drab grey colour, sometimes accompanied by brown mottles.

543e149b5a58.title: Canadian system of soil classification
543e149b5a58.sentence: Gleysolic soils cover about 117,000 km2 (1.3%) of Canada's land area.

02e73180c8d4.title: Canadian system of soil classification
02e73180c8d4.sentence: They occur commonly in shallow depressions and level areas of subhumid and humid climate in association with other classes of soil on slopes and hills.

e18b8d4c736f.title: Canadian system of soil classification
e18b8d4c736f.sentence: Three great groups of Gleysolic soils are defined.

a70537725ba9.title: Canadian system of soil classification
a70537725ba9.sentence: Humic Gleysols have a dark A horizon enriched in organic matter.

25b51eba5c30.title: Canadian system of soil classification
25b51eba5c30.sentence: Luvic Gleysols have a leached (Ae) horizon underlain by a B horizon in which the clay has accumulated; they may have a dark surface horizon.

f9f5fe8f941c.title: Canadian system of soil classification
f9f5fe8f941c.sentence: These soils have eluvial horizons from which clay has been leached after snowmelt or heavy rains and illuvial horizons in which clay has been deposited; these horizons are designated Ae and Bt respectively.

d38947df2e99.title: Canadian system of soil classification
d38947df2e99.sentence: Luvisolic soils occur typically in forested areas of subhumid to humid climate where the parent materials contain appreciable clay.

b60f1ed63324.title: Canadian system of soil classification
b60f1ed63324.sentence: In saline or calcareous materials, clay translocation is preceded by leaching of salts and carbonates.

97eac7f92365.title: Canadian system of soil classification
97eac7f92365.sentence: Luvisolic soils cover about 809,000 km2 (8.8%) of Canada's land area.

1940ccc24de3.title: Canadian system of soil classification
1940ccc24de3.sentence: Large areas of Luvisolic soils occur in the central to northern Interior Plains; smaller areas in all regions south of the permafrost zone.

c1ccc2de9a79.title: Canadian system of soil classification
c1ccc2de9a79.sentence: The two great groups of Luvisolic soils are distinguished mainly on the basis of soil temperature.

67ffd3d99636.title: Canadian system of soil classification
67ffd3d99636.sentence: Their mean annual soil temperature is 8 °C or higher.

7aa2afd035cd.title: Canadian system of soil classification
7aa2afd035cd.sentence: The major area of Gray Brown Luvisols is found in the southern part of the Great Lakes-St Lawrence Lowlands.

43f2cbf069af.title: Canadian system of soil classification
43f2cbf069af.sentence: Gray Luvisols have eluvial and illuvial horizons and may have an Ah horizon if the mean annual soil temperature is below 8 °C. Vast areas of Gray Luvisols in the Boreal Forest Zone of the Interior Plains have thick, light grey eluvial horizons underlying the forest litter and thick Bt horizons with clay coating the surface of aggregates.

98258618ce19.title: Canadian system of soil classification
98258618ce19.sentence: These acid soils have a B horizon containing accumulations of amorphous materials composed of humified organic matter associated with aluminum and iron.

0123a3892585.title: Canadian system of soil classification
0123a3892585.sentence: They develop most commonly in sandy materials in areas of cold, humid climate under forest or shrub vegetation.

2044c829d096.title: Canadian system of soil classification
2044c829d096.sentence: Water moving downward through the relatively porous material leaches out basic elements (e.g., calcium), and acidic conditions develop.

fe11216cfadf.title: Canadian system of soil classification
fe11216cfadf.sentence: Soluble organic substances formed by decomposition of the forest litter attack soil minerals in surface horizons, and much of the iron and aluminum released combines with this organic material.

20fe798c0dea.title: Canadian system of soil classification
20fe798c0dea.sentence: When the proportion of aluminum and iron to organic matter reaches a critical level, the organic complex becomes insoluble and is deposited in the B horizon.

5ea47503f035.title: Canadian system of soil classification
5ea47503f035.sentence: Podzolic soils occupy 14.3% of the Canadian landmass, and occur in two widely separated areas, the Appalachian Uplands and Canadian Shield in the east, and British Columbia in the west, usually under coniferous forest and on non-calcareous parent material.

9f79702fbc9b.title: Canadian system of soil classification
9f79702fbc9b.sentence: They are divided among three great groups on the basis of the kind of Podzolic B horizon.

f1d6c40aaa27.title: Canadian system of soil classification
f1d6c40aaa27.sentence: Humic Podzols have a dark B horizon with a low iron content.

90bb423876ff.title: Canadian system of soil classification
90bb423876ff.sentence: Ferro-Humic Podzols have a dark reddish-brown or black B horizon containing at least 5% organic carbon and appreciable amounts (often 2% or more) of aluminum and iron in organic complexes.

7579d644f198.title: Canadian system of soil classification
7579d644f198.sentence: Humo-Ferric Podzols, the most common Podzolic soils in Canada, have a reddish-brown B horizon containing less than 5% organic carbon associated with aluminum and iron complexes.

efb610f64446.title: Canadian system of soil classification
efb610f64446.sentence: The properties of Regosolic soils are essentially those of the parent material.

9ba19819c698.title: Canadian system of soil classification
9ba19819c698.sentence: While these soils must be able to support plant life, they have not been stable long enough to develop deeply differentiated soil horizons.

a95d1fef9674.title: Canadian system of soil classification
a95d1fef9674.sentence: The term Regosol is derived from rego (from the Greek rhe¯gos meaning blanket) and sol (from Latin solum or soil).

996ebc7d16bd.title: Canadian system of soil classification
996ebc7d16bd.sentence: Regosolic soils cover about 0.8% of Canada's land area.

d6ea85086c7a.title: Canadian system of soil classification
d6ea85086c7a.sentence: have an Ah horizon at least 10 cm thick.

f3aebcce6648.title: Canadian system of soil classification
f3aebcce6648.sentence: These soils have B horizons that are very hard when dry, swelling to a sticky, compact mass when wet.

75dae032844d.title: Canadian system of soil classification
75dae032844d.sentence: Properties of the B horizons are associated with sodium ions that cause the clay to disperse readily and swell on wetting, thus closing the large pores and preventing water flow.

e1c795d4905b.title: Canadian system of soil classification
e1c795d4905b.sentence: They usually develop in saline parent materials in semiarid and subhumid regions.

f7c387489864.title: Canadian system of soil classification
f7c387489864.sentence: Solonetzic soils cover almost 73,000 km2 (0.7%) of Canada's land area; most occur in southern Alberta, because of the large areas of saline parent material and semiarid climate.

7e8c1113fe1e.title: Canadian system of soil classification
7e8c1113fe1e.sentence: The developmental sequence of Solonetzic soils is commonly from saline parent material to Solonetz, Solodized Solonetz and Solod.

67d9e36bc0c1.title: Canadian system of soil classification
67d9e36bc0c1.sentence: Resalinization may occur and reverse the process associated with leaching.

1a1d7dc8a914.title: Canadian system of soil classification
1a1d7dc8a914.sentence: These clay-rich soils shrink and swell markedly on drying and wetting.

a49c7a6d0d90.title: Canadian system of soil classification
a49c7a6d0d90.sentence: The physical disruption associated with shrinking and swelling produces shiny shear planes (slickensides) in the subsoil and either prevents the formation of subsurface horizons or severely disrupts and mixes them.

63c94efde4d4.title: Canadian system of soil classification
63c94efde4d4.sentence: When the soil swells on wetting, the former surficial material is mixed with the subsoil.

27c880b05040.title: Canadian system of soil classification
27c880b05040.sentence: Vertisolic soils develop mainly in clayey materials in semiarid to subhumid areas of the Interior Plains of Saskatchewan, Manitoba and Alberta and occupy less than 1% of the land area of Canada.

1cd932c20e09.title: Canadian system of soil classification
1cd932c20e09.sentence: The order and its two great groups were recognized in the Canadian system in the 1990s after extensive studies of pedons in the Great Plains.

8cc86da90f47.title: Canadian system of soil classification
8cc86da90f47.sentence: The Vertisol great group has a light-coloured A horizon that is not readily distinguishable, and the Humic Vertisol great group has a dark-coloured A horizon enriched in organic matter that is clearly distinguishable from the underlying soil material.

ad606ee6676c.title: Anthroposol
ad606ee6676c.sentence: Anthroposols are soils which have been profoundly modified or constructed by humans.

20fcadeb2c36.title: Anthroposol
20fcadeb2c36.sentence: They typically have one or more of their natural soil horizons modified, removed or replaced.

4117d1a1b1df.title: Anthroposol
4117d1a1b1df.sentence: Anthroposols are typically found on industrial, commercial, urban and resources extraction sites as well as throughout transportation, fuel and power corridors.

53b57bd058c3.title: Anthroposol
53b57bd058c3.sentence: Human-formed soils have historically been excluded from soil classification systems due in part to the fact that the criteria used for naturally-formed soils are often not applicable.

f479282d1db2.title: Anthroposol
f479282d1db2.sentence: However, many countries are recognizing their pervasiveness and the need for some type of common language and taxonomy.

f02b6a19a9f9.title: Anthroposol
f02b6a19a9f9.section: Classification of anthroposols > National Soil Classification Systems > Canada > Order
f02b6a19a9f9.sentence: Anthroposol - "soil that has been visibly disturbed by human activity and that have a D horizon [equal to or greater than] 10 cm thick or have had natural soil horizons removed."

356bf765cada.title: Anthroposol
356bf765cada.section: Classification of anthroposols > National Soil Classification Systems > Canada > Great Group
356bf765cada.sentence: - Technic: a D layer with more than 10% physical artifacts present.

3d3744600f6e.title: Anthroposol
3d3744600f6e.section: Classification of anthroposols > National Soil Classification Systems > Canada > Great Group
3d3744600f6e.sentence: - Spolic: D layer with less than 17% organic carbon

71b4bf727373.title: Anthroposol
71b4bf727373.section: Classification of anthroposols > National Soil Classification Systems > Canada
71b4bf727373.sentence: Tilled soils are not included in the proposed anthroposolic order within the Canadian System of Soil Classification and this disturbance is covered by use of suffix p to indicate a plowed horizon within other soil orders.

16e003a9efb4.title: Anthroposol
16e003a9efb4.section: Classification of anthroposols > World Reference Base for Soil Resources
16e003a9efb4.sentence: It outlines two larger anthropogenic sub-categories based on the degree of disturbance as well as the pervasiveness of the artifacts within:

8ff78bbb07ec.title: Anthroposol
8ff78bbb07ec.section: Classification of anthroposols > World Reference Base for Soil Resources
8ff78bbb07ec.sentence: - Anthrosol: soils under agricultural cultivation for long periods

e015484f4c18.title: Anthroposol
e015484f4c18.section: Classification of anthroposols > World Reference Base for Soil Resources
e015484f4c18.sentence: - Technosol: soils containing products and artifacts of industrial processes (often toxic).

841051ed6e9f.title: Kurosol
841051ed6e9f.sentence: Kurosols are soils belonging to one of the fifteen soil orders of the Australian Soil Classification.

2552c42b415e.title: Kurosol
2552c42b415e.sentence: Kurosols are characterised by a strong texture contrast between their surface (A) horizons and clay-rich subsoil (B) horizons, with the upper part of the B horizon being strongly acidic.

4ba778468e14.title: Kurosol
4ba778468e14.sentence: The defining characteristic distinguishing kurosols from the other major texture-contrast soil orders is the chemistry of the upper B horizon.

07ed2929d7ae.title: Kurosol
07ed2929d7ae.sentence: In kurosols it is strongly acidic, whereas the corresponding horizon in chromosols is neither strongly acidic nor sodic, and that of sodosols is sodic.

63f083322a70.title: Kurosol
63f083322a70.sentence: The strongly acidic subsoil generally has a pH below 5.5 when measured in water.

7f86c434531c.title: Kurosol
7f86c434531c.sentence: They are widespread in parts of eastern and southern Australia, particularly in higher-rainfall and extensively weathered landscapes.

d405ac40a461.title: Kurosol
d405ac40a461.sentence: Kurosols occur in several parts of Australia and are particularly associated with landscapes experiencing relatively high rainfall and leaching.

6c5577bf960c.title: Kurosol
6c5577bf960c.sentence: Their strong texture contrast can restrict root penetration and water movement into the clay-rich subsoil, while strongly acidic conditions can reduce the availability of some plant nutrients.

aa491803d75c.title: Kurosol
aa491803d75c.sentence: Agricultural management can include maintaining or increasing surface organic matter, reducing excessive tillage and, where appropriate, applying agricultural lime to increase the pH of acidic surface soils.

009a409621c4.title: Kurosol
009a409621c4.sentence: Acidity deeper within the subsoil is more difficult to ameliorate because surface-applied lime moves through the soil relatively slowly.

179bdf24c8d7.title: Référentiel pédologique
179bdf24c8d7.sentence: An English translation of soil types defined in "référentiel pedologique français" can be done this way. it is relevant for European soils:

b2d4c2e00ec3.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/03%3A_Taxonomy/3.01%3A_Introduction
b2d4c2e00ec3.section: IDENTIFICATION OF THE TAXONOMIC CLASS OF A SOIL
b2d4c2e00ec3.sentence: Classification of soils is determined using the systematic approach outlined in the Keys to Soil Taxonomy.

ae2956e5419c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/03%3A_Taxonomy/3.01%3A_Introduction
ae2956e5419c.section: IDENTIFICATION OF THE TAXONOMIC CLASS OF A SOIL
ae2956e5419c.sentence: Individuals must begin with the “Key to Soil Orders” and eliminate, one by one, the classes including criteria which do not meet the soil in question.

e4221673e8f9.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/03%3A_Taxonomy/3.01%3A_Introduction
e4221673e8f9.section: IDENTIFICATION OF THE TAXONOMIC CLASS OF A SOIL
e4221673e8f9.sentence: Whichever order’s criteria aligns best with the soil in question first will be the soil order selected.

b440d071adf4.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/03%3A_Taxonomy/3.01%3A_Introduction
b440d071adf4.section: IDENTIFICATION OF THE TAXONOMIC CLASS OF A SOIL
b440d071adf4.sentence: This process is used for all subsequent categories in the ordering of order, suborder, great group, and subgroup.

6b3b208693cd.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/03%3A_Taxonomy/3.01%3A_Introduction
6b3b208693cd.section: IDENTIFICATION OF THE TAXONOMIC CLASS OF A SOIL
6b3b208693cd.sentence: Family and Series are determined by other individual methods using criteria outlined in the Keys to Soil Taxonomy (2014).

cd2519f3c1e4.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/03%3A_Taxonomy/3.01%3A_Introduction
cd2519f3c1e4.section: IDENTIFICATION OF THE TAXONOMIC CLASS OF A SOIL > Suborder
cd2519f3c1e4.sentence: Soil suborders are determined based on soil moisture regimes and diagnostic features.

5879c1335e8e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/03%3A_Taxonomy/3.01%3A_Introduction
5879c1335e8e.section: IDENTIFICATION OF THE TAXONOMIC CLASS OF A SOIL > Great group
5879c1335e8e.sentence: The great group expresses the degree of diagnostic horizon expression within each suborder taxa.

956c2c9a0591.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/03%3A_Taxonomy/3.01%3A_Introduction
956c2c9a0591.section: IDENTIFICATION OF THE TAXONOMIC CLASS OF A SOIL > Subgroup
956c2c9a0591.sentence: A soil’s subgroup is defined by properties that are transitional or similar to those found in other orders, suborders, and great groups.

496933d42152.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/03%3A_Taxonomy/3.01%3A_Introduction
496933d42152.section: IDENTIFICATION OF THE TAXONOMIC CLASS OF A SOIL > Family
496933d42152.sentence: The family is typically comprised of more than one component that is determined for the soil in question using information detailed in chapter 17 of the Keys to Soil taxonomy.

ee28e540174f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/03%3A_Taxonomy/3.01%3A_Introduction
ee28e540174f.section: IDENTIFICATION OF THE TAXONOMIC CLASS OF A SOIL > Family
ee28e540174f.sentence: The technical family name is comprised of descriptive terms for family information such as, particle size class and mineralogy of control section, soil temperature regime, CEC, depth, rupture-resistance, etc.

cefdd8f31d2d.title: Greyzem
cefdd8f31d2d.sentence: Greyzem (from Anglo-Saxon, grey, and Russian, zemlja, earth) is a soil classification used in the FAO soil classification system which was introduced with the UNESCO Soil Map of the World in 1978.

c6fde3ef99e4.title: Greyzem
c6fde3ef99e4.sentence: The name is connotative of uncoated silt and quartz grains which are present in layers rich in organic matter.

2bb600f75744.title: Greyzem
2bb600f75744.sentence: Parent material | decalcified unconsolidated materials including eolian, fluvial and lacustrine deposits, solifluction material and glacial till.

a1d32e09337b.title: Greyzem
a1d32e09337b.sentence: Along with chernozems, kastanozems, and phaeozems, these four soil groups form a set of soil groups that are mainly found in steppe (aka pampa in South America or prairie in Northern America) regions.

9d85f5741ca3.title: Greyzem
9d85f5741ca3.sentence: It was one of the original 26 Great Groups and remained as one of the 28 groups in the 1988 revised version.

bc08cc3157eb.title: Greyzem
bc08cc3157eb.sentence: The greyzem classification contains two Soil Units:

2792e348cd1e.title: Greyzem
2792e348cd1e.sentence: - Gleyic greyzems – Greyzems showing gleyic properties within 100 cm of the surface

538143ad3ad1.title: Greyzem
538143ad3ad1.sentence: - Haplic greyzems – Greyzems lacking gleyic properties within 100 cm of the surface

42eb62c9d666.title: Greyzem
42eb62c9d666.sentence: Taxonomically, Greyzem would most closely correlate to Dark Grey Chernozem under the Canadian System of Soil Classification and Albolls and Boralfic Boroll subgroups under USDA soil taxonomy.

940a2d80eecd.title: Handbook of Australian Soils
940a2d80eecd.sentence: The first edition was published in 1968 and is based on the great soil group classification system published by J. A. Prescott in 1931.

a97f02b7e23a.title: Handbook of Australian Soils
a97f02b7e23a.sentence: It has since been superseded by the Australian Soil Classification.

cd203a82bc06.sentence: Order | Orders are based on properties of the profile that reflect the nature of the overall soil environment and the effects of the dominant soil-forming process.

0952a0bac378.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/01%3A_Digging_In/1.08%3A_Soil_Classification_and_Distribution

0952a0bac378.sentence: Great Group | Great groups are subdivisions of each order. The great groups reflect differences in the strengths of the major processes or a major contribution of a process in addition to the dominant one.

e0d32d4578ab.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/01%3A_Digging_In/1.08%3A_Soil_Classification_and_Distribution

e0d32d4578ab.sentence: Subgroup | Subgroups are subdivisions of great groups. Profiles are differentiated on (1) how closely they correspond to the central concept of the great group (termed Orthic); (2) transitional stages grading towards soils of another order; and (3) additional special features within the profile.

1643a9724e1a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/01%3A_Digging_In/1.08%3A_Soil_Classification_and_Distribution

1643a9724e1a.sentence: Family | Families are used to group series (see below) of the same subgroup that have similar response to management, engineering and related uses. The family level is seldom used in Canada.

a01e7c91cd7d.sentence: The assignment of a given soil profile to its taxonomic class is done by comparing the properties of the horizons in the field to a list of distinctive characteristics, called diagnostic properties.

c9056ffd1b13.title: Ustic

a429c9f1101f.title: Vertisol

e32c3be104ae.title: Ustic

6b39396dd9ae.title: Ustic
6b39396dd9ae.sentence: The moisture control section in the aridic moisture regime is dry when the temperature of soil, at a depth of 50 cm from the soil surface, is above 5 °C for more than half of the cumulative days per year and moist when it's above 8 °C for less than 90 consecutive days.

59bda6512a76.title: Ustic

35fe6691f562.sentence: The formation of these fertile carbon- and nutrient-rich zonal soils was longtime attributed to dry continental climate conditions and steppe or prairie vegetation (according to biomes) until it became admitted that past human activities (deposition of domestic and occupational wastes, charred residues, biomass ashes, burning, fertilisation) were a driving factor of Dark Earth formation, and that not only in the tropics.
