67d7e5b1b466.sentence: As outlined by Naeth et al. (2012) "Anthroposols are azonal soils, highly modified or constructed by human activity, with one or more natural horizons removed, removed and replaced, added to, or significantly modified." The defining features of anthroposols are:

760dde749094.title: 1938 USDA soil taxonomy
760dde749094.sentence: Calcimorphic or calcareous soils develop from a limestone.

6faa3bb3b176.title: 1938 USDA soil taxonomy
6faa3bb3b176.sentence: Terra rossa soils are deep red soils associated with higher rainfall than rendzina.

3d45f859b1ff.title: 1938 USDA soil taxonomy
3d45f859b1ff.sentence: This gives the soil a characteristic grey/blue colour with flecks of red.

9d5d77395e74.title: 1938 USDA soil taxonomy
9d5d77395e74.sentence: Peat soils form under circumstances that prevent the breakdown of vegetation completely.

2d73a097e16d.title: 1938 USDA soil taxonomy
2d73a097e16d.sentence: Halomorphic soils form due to soil salination.

a3f9ce2fa5d8.title: Paleopedology
a3f9ce2fa5d8.sentence: With the aid of X-ray diffraction, paleosols can now be classified into one of the 12 orders of soil taxonomy (Oxisols, Ultisols, Alfisols, Mollisols, Spodosols, Aridisols, Entisols, Inceptisols, Gelisols, Histosols, Vertisols and Andisols).

830d70eed2e7.title: Soil classification
830d70eed2e7.sentence: There are twelve recognized soil orders in the United States, each reflecting distinct soil-forming processes and characteristics such as climate, vegetation, and mineral composition.

e01517390c8f.title: USDA soil taxonomy
e01517390c8f.sentence: The above soil orders in sequence of increasing degree of development are Entisols, Inceptisols, Aridisols, Mollisols, Alfisols, Spodosols, Ultisols, and Oxisols.

1a2d087c7e76.title: USDA soil taxonomy
1a2d087c7e76.sentence: Histosols and Vertisols may appear in any of the above at any time during their development.

9854e79c3958.title: USDA soil taxonomy
9854e79c3958.sentence: - Oxisols: Most soil profile development; must have oxic horizon within 150 cm of soil surface; low nutrient availability; no argillic horizon; highly weathered; dominated by end-member clays, Al and Fe oxides; commonly in old landscapes in tropics; 7.6% of global and <0.01% of U.S. ice-free land.

77876d361769.title: USDA soil taxonomy
77876d361769.sentence: - Inceptisols: Similar to entisol, but beginning of a B horizon is evident; no diagnostic subsurface horizons; on landscapes continuously eroded or young deposits; cambic, sulfuric, calcic, gypsic, petrocalcic, or petrogypsic horizon, or with a mollic, umbric, or histic epipedon, or with an exchangeable sodium percentage of >15% or fragipan; 9.9% of global & 9.1% of U.S. ice-free land.

cfeff182a779.title: USDA soil taxonomy
cfeff182a779.sentence: "Soils of Mountains", which constitute the balance (11.6%), have a mixture of those listed above, or are classified as "Rugged Mountains" which have no soil.

0da82a5078bb.title: USDA soil taxonomy
0da82a5078bb.sentence: The percentages listed above are for land area free of ice.

f918ce998555.title: Mollisol
f918ce998555.sentence: Mollisol is a soil type which has deep, high organic matter, nutrient-enriched surface soil (a horizon), typically between 60 and 80 cm (24–31 in) in depth.

4f5507fbef2e.title: Mollisol
4f5507fbef2e.sentence: Mollisols typically occur in savannahs and mountain valleys (such as Central Asia, and the North American Great Plains).

fb57cd2b5b8d.title: Mollisol
fb57cd2b5b8d.sentence: These environments have historically been strongly influenced by fire and abundant pedoturbation from organisms such as ants and earthworms.

4e05748521d8.title: Mollisol
4e05748521d8.sentence: As the world's agriculturally most productive soil order, the Mollisols represent one of the most economically important soil orders.

acbc58692018.title: Mollisol
acbc58692018.sentence: It was estimated that in 2003, only 14 to 26 percent of grassland ecosystems remained in a relatively natural state (that is, they were not used for agriculture due to the fertility of the horizon).

9664cae9908c.title: Mollisol
9664cae9908c.sentence: Globally, they represent ~7% of ice-free land area.

3910b1b435b0.title: Mollisol
3910b1b435b0.sentence: In the World Reference Base for Soil Resources (WRB), Mollisols are split up into Chernozems, Kastanozems and Phaeozems.

88f61a8d66ba.title: Mollisol
88f61a8d66ba.sentence: Shallow or gravelly Mollisols may belong to the Leptosols.

e3bb3cfb2ee2.title: Mollisol
e3bb3cfb2ee2.sentence: Many Aquolls are Gleysols, Stagnosols or Planosols.

f16b6cc82ab6.title: Mollisol
f16b6cc82ab6.sentence: Their development is very closely associated with cooling and drying of the global climate that occurred during the Oligocene, Miocene and Pliocene.

271a193e24e6.title: Mollisol
271a193e24e6.sentence: Though most other soil orders known today were formed at the beginning of the Carboniferous Ice Age 280 million years ago, Mollisols are best known from the paleopedological record possibly as early as the Maastrichtian, though confidently found in the Eocene.

20af3240ea27.title: Vertisol
20af3240ea27.sentence: A vertisol is a Soil Order in the USDA soil taxonomy and a Reference Soil Group in the World Reference Base for Soil Resources (WRB).

ff7d5c3d83a6.title: Vertisol
ff7d5c3d83a6.sentence: Vertisols have a high content of expansive clay minerals (many of them belonging to the montmorillonites) that form deep cracks in drier seasons or years.

d1678cd14090.title: USDA soil taxonomy
d1678cd14090.sentence: - Vertisols: Usually mollic epipedon; high in shrinking and swelling clays; >30% clay to a depth of 50 cm; deep cracks (called gilgai) form when soil dries; form from parent material high in clay (e.g., shales, basins, exposed Bt horizons of old soils); 2.4% of global and 1.7% of U.S. ice-free land.

87cd003f155e.title: Vertisol
87cd003f155e.sentence: Vertisols typically form from highly basic rocks, such as basalt, in climates that are seasonally humid or subject to erratic droughts and floods, or that impeded drainage.

ff7a09464ba8.title: Vertisol
ff7a09464ba8.sentence: In a phenomenon known as argillipedoturbation, alternate shrinking and swelling causes self-ploughing, where the soil material consistently mixes itself, causing some vertisols to have an extremely deep A horizon and no B horizon.

84f410c781fa.title: Vertisol
84f410c781fa.sentence: This heaving of the underlying material to the surface often creates a microrelief known as gilgai.

84f67d450c22.title: Vertisol
84f67d450c22.sentence: Depending on the parent material and the climate, they can range from grey or red to the more familiar deep black (known as "black earths" in Australia, "black gumbo" in East Texas, "black cotton" soils in East Africa, and "turf soil" or "vlei soils" in South Africa).

e4434c975630.title: Vertisol
e4434c975630.sentence: Vertisols are found between 50°N and 45°S of the equator.

bc81c5e82668.title: Vertisol
bc81c5e82668.sentence: Major areas where vertisols are dominant are eastern Australia (especially inland Queensland and New South Wales), the Deccan Plateau of India, and parts of southern Sudan, Ethiopia, Kenya, Chad (the Gezira), South Africa, and the lower Paraná River in South America.

f6996d0dd7c0.title: Vertisol
f6996d0dd7c0.sentence: The natural vegetation of vertisols is grassland, savanna, or grassy woodland.

be4b38f26f9e.title: Vertisol
be4b38f26f9e.sentence: The heavy texture and unstable behaviour of the soil makes it difficult for many tree species to grow, and forest is uncommon.

ba6cdac25326.title: Vertisol
ba6cdac25326.sentence: Rainfed farming is very difficult because vertisols can be worked only under a very narrow range of moisture conditions: they are very hard when dry and very sticky when wet.

5a98f04da07f.title: Vertisol
5a98f04da07f.sentence: When irrigation is available, crops such as cotton, wheat, sorghum and rice can be grown.

06596005bc00.title: Vertisol
06596005bc00.sentence: Vertisols are especially suitable for rice because they are almost impermeable when saturated.

856bb57810b5.title: Vertisol
856bb57810b5.sentence: Vertisols are generally used for grazing of cattle or sheep.

a9cef9ca1d0a.title: Vertisol
a9cef9ca1d0a.sentence: The shrinking and swelling of vertisols can damage buildings and roads, leading to extensive subsidence.

d31dbb2b0fcf.title: Vertisol
d31dbb2b0fcf.sentence: However, the shrink-swell activity allows rapid recovery from compaction.

4ccfda26da87.title: Vertisol
4ccfda26da87.sentence: However, in Australia, vertisols are highly regarded, because they are among the few soils that are not acutely deficient in available phosphorus.

5a442ba9f6d6.title: Vertisol
5a442ba9f6d6.sentence: The WRB defines the diagnostic vertic horizon.

483e141ce50c.title: Vertisol
483e141ce50c.sentence: It is usually a subsoil horizon and has at least 30% clay, shrink-swell cracks and wedge-shaped aggregates and/or slickensides.

39a4e2977162.title: Vertisol
39a4e2977162.sentence: In the Australian Soil Classification it is called vertosol.

4953fc4b6f41.title: Alfisol
4953fc4b6f41.sentence: Alfisols are a soil order in USDA soil taxonomy.

9addfe1cbf01.title: Alfisol
9addfe1cbf01.sentence: They have a clay-enriched subsoil and relatively high native fertility.

578cc3ee8fb2.title: Alfisol
578cc3ee8fb2.sentence: Alfisols have undergone only moderate leaching.

b410be89dc26.title: Alfisol
b410be89dc26.sentence: Alfisols form in semi-arid to humid areas, typically under a hardwood forest cover.

abec8b924456.title: Curtis F. Marbut
abec8b924456.sentence: "Alfer" became the root term for alfisols.

cbb1da835d32.title: Alfisol
cbb1da835d32.sentence: Because of their productivity and abundance, Alfisols represent one of the more important soil orders for food and fiber production.

28ff50e1b89c.title: Alfisol
28ff50e1b89c.sentence: They are widely used both in agriculture and forestry, and are generally easier to keep fertile than other humid-climate soils, though those in Australia and Africa are still very deficient in nitrogen and available phosphorus.

471c4d797f4b.title: Alfisol
471c4d797f4b.sentence: Those in monsoonal tropical regions, however, have a tendency to acidify when heavily cultivated, especially when nitrogenous fertilizers are used.

96a33b287fb2.title: Alfisol
96a33b287fb2.sentence: Alfisols occupy around one-tenth of the Earth's ice-free land surface.

53f65a29e95b.title: Alfisol
53f65a29e95b.sentence: They are dominant in many areas, such as the Ohio River basin in the United States, southern and unglaciated Western Europe, the Baltic region and central European Russia, the drier parts of Peninsular India, Sudan in Africa, and many parts of South America.

99f8d3214715.title: Alfisol
99f8d3214715.sentence: In eastern North America, Alfisols are commonly found in glaciated areas while Ultisols are restricted to the areas south of the limit of maximum glaciation.

b2969a5acf96.title: Alfisol
b2969a5acf96.sentence: - Aqualfs – This suborder is saturated with water long enough to cause oxygen depletion.

1b83fa3c4e43.title: Alfisol
1b83fa3c4e43.sentence: - Cryalfs – This suborder occurs mainly in high elevations which tend to be cold with temperatures ranging from greater than 0 C to less than 8 C.

0daa22860afc.title: Alfisol
0daa22860afc.sentence: - Udalfs – This suborder is located in humid or subhumid climates.

3acd46795225.title: Alfisol
3acd46795225.sentence: - Ustalfs – This suborder is located in semiarid climates with wet summers and dry winters.

eebb8cacdc41.title: Alfisol
eebb8cacdc41.sentence: In the World Reference Base for Soil Resources (WRB), most Alfisols are classified as Luvisols or Lixisols, but some are classed as Retisols or Nitisols.

4ac38cc8af80.title: Alfisol
4ac38cc8af80.sentence: Aqualfs are mainly Stagnosols or Planosols.

26bd8a5162c4.title: Andisol
26bd8a5162c4.sentence: Because they are generally quite young, andisols typically are very fertile except in cases where phosphorus is easily fixed (this sometimes occurs in the tropics).

305764a0d701.title: Andisol
305764a0d701.sentence: They can usually support intensive cropping, with areas used for wet rice in Java supporting some of the densest populations in the world.

361b0fdfe736.title: Andisol
361b0fdfe736.sentence: Other andisol areas support crops of fruit, maize, tea, coffee, or tobacco.

ccba0b5c8171.title: Andisol
ccba0b5c8171.sentence: In the Pacific Northwest US, andisols support very productive forests.

4fdedb0d3c31.title: Andisol
4fdedb0d3c31.sentence: Andisols occupy about 1% of the global ice-free land area.

18a97e52546a.title: Andisol
18a97e52546a.sentence: Most occur around the Pacific Ring of Fire, with the largest areas found in central Chile, Ecuador, Colombia, Mexico, the Pacific Northwest US, Japan, Java and New Zealand's North Island.

ae9fac42f943.title: Andisol
ae9fac42f943.sentence: - Aquands – Andisols with a water table at or near the surface for much of the year.

e492b8ef1d1b.title: Andisol
e492b8ef1d1b.sentence: - Gelands – Andisols of very cold climates (mean annual temperature <0 °C).

e7fbc731dcdd.title: Andisol
e7fbc731dcdd.sentence: - Torrands – Andisols of very dry climates.

7574a35f2196.title: Andisol
7574a35f2196.sentence: - Ustands – Andisols of semiarid and subhumid climates.

ff5b7ee085dc.title: Andisol
ff5b7ee085dc.sentence: - Xerands – Temperate andisols with very dry summers and moist winters.

bdf4c56366a2.title: Andisol
bdf4c56366a2.sentence: - Vitrands – Relatively young andisols that are coarse-textured and dominated by glass.

305f02b2ff7b.title: Andisol
305f02b2ff7b.sentence: In the World Reference Base for Soil Resources (WRB), andisols are known as Andosols.

54a98aad728f.title: Andosol
54a98aad728f.sentence: Some Histosols (WRB) belong to the Andisols (ST), and some Andosols (WRB) belong to the Inceptisols (ST).

68e53329bec2.title: Andisol
68e53329bec2.sentence: Fossil andisols are known from areas far from present-day volcanic activity and have in some cases been dated as far back as the Mesoproterozoic 1.5 billion years ago.

c1c8ac21bb27.title: Histosol
c1c8ac21bb27.sentence: In both the World Reference Base for Soil Resources (WRB) and the USDA soil taxonomy, a Histosol is a soil consisting primarily of organic materials.

595b82dd044a.title: Histosol
595b82dd044a.sentence: They are defined as having 40 centimetres (16 in) or more of organic soil material starting within 40 cm from the soil surface.

7ebc15d0c1c7.title: Histosol
7ebc15d0c1c7.sentence: Organic soil material has an organic carbon content (by weight) of 12 percent or more (Soil Taxonomy) or 20 percent or more (WRB).

cfa3c111ead3.title: Histosol
cfa3c111ead3.sentence: These materials include muck (sapric soil material), mucky peat (hemic soil material), or peat (fibric soil material).

d8bd5cb96250.title: Histosol
d8bd5cb96250.sentence: - Fibrists – Histosols that are primarily made up of only slightly decomposed organic materials, often called peat.

8447b37fe102.title: Histosol
8447b37fe102.sentence: - Hemists – Histosols that are primarily made up of moderately decomposed organic materials.

c991841dcf9f.title: Histosol
c991841dcf9f.sentence: - Saprists – Histosols that are primarily made up of highly decomposed organic materials, often called muck.

13bfd47592f6.title: Histosol
13bfd47592f6.sentence: - Folists – Histosols that are not saturated with water for long periods of time during the year.

35c8fe41abff.title: Histosol
35c8fe41abff.sentence: - Wassists - Histosols that have a field observable water table 2 cm or more above the soil surface for more than 21 hours of each day in all years.

168d62efc534.title: Histosol
168d62efc534.sentence: Histosols form whenever organic matter forms at a more rapid rate than it is destroyed.

64c18ca16ffa.title: Histosol
64c18ca16ffa.sentence: This occurs because of restricted drainage precluding aerobic decomposition, and the remains of plants and animals remain within the soil.

d6f20e2d3308.title: Histosol
d6f20e2d3308.sentence: If accumulation continues for a long enough period, coal forms.

0c9725664224.title: Histosol
0c9725664224.sentence: Thus, Histosols are very important ecologically because they, and Gelisols, store large quantities of organic carbon.

edd8fc394ffd.title: Histosol
edd8fc394ffd.sentence: Organic material and therefore Histosols have very low bulk density.

046626920d25.title: Histosol
046626920d25.sentence: Many are acidic and very deficient in major plant nutrients, especially the raised bogs, which are saturated by rainwater and lack connection to nutrient-containing groundwater.

bc1f56efea26.title: Histosol
bc1f56efea26.sentence: Histosols are generally very difficult to cultivate because of the poor drainage and often low chemical fertility.

19cda98add17.title: Histosol
19cda98add17.sentence: However, Histosols formed on very recent glacial lands can often be very productive when drained and produce high-grade pasture for dairying or beef cattle.

3cfba97a7a05.title: Histosol
3cfba97a7a05.sentence: They can sometimes be used for fruit if carefully managed, but there is a great risk of the organic matter becoming dry powder and eroding under the influence of drying winds.

f35c7bf885ed.title: Histosol
f35c7bf885ed.sentence: Like Gelisols, Histosols have greatly restricted use for civil engineering purposes because heavy structures tend to subside in the wet soil.

604482303601.title: Histosol
604482303601.sentence: Most Histosols occur in Canada, Scandinavia, the West Siberian Plain, Sumatra, Borneo and New Guinea.

14e4b94496f0.title: Histosol
14e4b94496f0.sentence: Histosols are known by various other names in other countries, such as peat or muck.

1e1300fd16bc.title: Histosol
1e1300fd16bc.sentence: Fossil Histosols are known from the earliest extensive land vegetation in the Devonian.

2b5c4be23726.title: Aridisol
2b5c4be23726.sentence: Aridisols (or desert soils) are a soil order in USDA soil taxonomy.

2102809a6a12.title: Aridisol
2102809a6a12.sentence: Aridisols (from the Latin aridus, for "dry", and solum) form in an arid or semi-arid climate.

65c70bdccf1d.title: Aridisol
65c70bdccf1d.sentence: Water deficiency is the central defining characteristic of Aridisols.

08a94df95c5b.title: USDA soil taxonomy
08a94df95c5b.sentence: - Aridisol – dry soils forming under desert conditions which have fewer than 90 consecutive days of moisture during the growing season and are nonleached.

3648fd620933.title: Aridisol
3648fd620933.sentence: Also required is sufficient age to exhibit subsoil weathering and development.

1f235d21e087.title: Aridisol
1f235d21e087.sentence: Aridisols dominate the deserts and xeric shrublands, which occupy about one-third of the Earth's land surface.

334eb44cafbb.title: Aridisol
334eb44cafbb.sentence: Aridisols have a very low concentration of organic matter, reflecting the paucity of vegetative production on these dry soils.

958985dffb27.title: USDA soil taxonomy
958985dffb27.sentence: Soil formation is slow, and accumulated organic matter is scarce.

45c67c3890fc.title: Aridisol
45c67c3890fc.sentence: Limited leaching in aridisols often results in one or more subsurface soil horizons in which suspended or dissolved minerals have been deposited: silicate clays, sodium, calcium carbonate, gypsum, or soluble salts.

1fb68894a7c6.title: Aridisol
1fb68894a7c6.sentence: These subsoil horizons can also be cemented by carbonates, gypsum, or silica.

b71b53a71205.title: USDA soil taxonomy
b71b53a71205.sentence: They may have subsurface zones of caliche or duripan.

6df88574f9b2.title: USDA soil taxonomy
6df88574f9b2.sentence: Many aridisols have well-developed Bt horizons showing clay movement from past periods of greater moisture.

42909c927e99.title: Aridisol
42909c927e99.sentence: Accumulation of salts on the surface can result in salinization.

a631b0be5022.title: Aridisol
a631b0be5022.sentence: In the World Reference Base for Soil Resources (WRB), most Aridisols belong to the Calcisols, Gypsisols, Durisols and Solonchaks.

a4d3c65e2cb8.title: Ultisol
a4d3c65e2cb8.sentence: Ultisol, commonly known as red clay soil, is one of twelve soil orders in the United States Department of Agriculture soil taxonomy.

fd978a032397.title: USDA soil taxonomy
fd978a032397.sentence: - Ultisol – acid soils in the humid tropics and subtropics, which are depleted in calcium, magnesium and potassium (important plant nutrients).

12e367e6082b.title: Ultisol
12e367e6082b.sentence: They are defined as mineral soils which contain no calcareous (calcium carbonate containing) material anywhere within the soil, have less than 10% weatherable minerals in the extreme top layer of soil, and have less than 35% base saturation throughout the soil.

a85581de03e7.title: Ultisol
a85581de03e7.sentence: The word "Ultisol" is derived from "ultimate", because Ultisols were seen as the ultimate product of continuous weathering of minerals in a humid, temperate climate without new soil formation via glaciation.

9f0267f54154.title: Ultisol
9f0267f54154.sentence: Ultisols vary in color from purplish-red, to a bright reddish-orange, to pale yellowish-orange and (in cooler areas such as Pennsylvania) even some subdued yellowish-brown or grayish-brown tones.

7e887c9da6fc.title: Ultisol
7e887c9da6fc.sentence: The red and yellow colors result from the accumulation of iron oxide (rust), which is highly insoluble in water.

0b6f2f351b4d.title: Ultisol
0b6f2f351b4d.sentence: They are typically quite acidic, often having a pH of less than 5.

31c563c8dc8c.title: Ultisol
31c563c8dc8c.sentence: Ultisols can have a variety of clay minerals, but in many cases the dominant mineral is kaolinite.

1e6df964200b.title: Ultisol
1e6df964200b.sentence: Major nutrients, such as calcium and potassium, are typically deficient in Ultisols, which means they generally cannot be used for sedentary agriculture without the aid of lime and other fertilizers, such as superphosphate.

ba9f6b03fd3a.title: Ultisol
ba9f6b03fd3a.sentence: They can be easily exhausted, and require more careful management than Alfisols or Mollisols.

3d216ed7f3d6.title: Ultisol
3d216ed7f3d6.sentence: Where the organic matter content is high, as in Humults like the Olympic series, the soil is relatively fertile.

bcf3a65ee917.title: Ultisol
bcf3a65ee917.sentence: This clay has good bearing capacity and no shrink–swell property.

b7cf39fc0653.title: Ultisol
b7cf39fc0653.sentence: Consequently, well-drained kaolinitic Ultisols such as the Cecil series are suitable for urban development.

e36876a4d05a.title: Ultisol
e36876a4d05a.sentence: Ultisols are the dominant soils in the Southern United States (where the Cecil series is most famous), southeastern China, Southeast Asia, and some other subtropical and tropical areas.

7b17c7b24a2e.title: Ultisol
7b17c7b24a2e.sentence: Their northern limit (except fossil soils) is very sharply defined in North America by the limits of maximum glaciation during the Pleistocene, because Ultisols typically take hundreds of thousands of years to form—far longer than the length of an interglacial period today.

1e954a007595.title: Ultisol
1e954a007595.sentence: In the World Reference Base for Soil Resources (WRB), most Ultisols are known as Acrisols and Alisols.

180e02694bb5.title: Ultisol
180e02694bb5.sentence: Some belong to the Retisols or to the Nitisols.

6ce2100e405b.title: Oxisol
6ce2100e405b.sentence: Oxisols are a soil order in USDA soil taxonomy, best known for their occurrence in tropical rain forest within 25 degrees north and south of the Equator.

3f7b1102dc79.title: USDA soil taxonomy
3f7b1102dc79.sentence: - Oxisol – are heavily weathered, are rich in iron and aluminum oxides (sesquioxides) or kaolin but low in silica.

cde6ff64827f.title: Oxisol
cde6ff64827f.sentence: They are defined as soils containing at all depths no more than ten percent weatherable minerals, and low cation exchange capacity.

8a6c901738be.title: Oxisol
8a6c901738be.sentence: Oxisols are always a red or yellowish color, due to the high concentration of iron(III) and aluminium oxides and hydroxides.

0591da76984d.title: Oxisol
0591da76984d.sentence: They also contain quartz and kaolin, plus small amounts of other clay minerals and organic matter.

b6169694b036.title: Oxisol
b6169694b036.sentence: The word "oxisol" comes from "oxide" in reference to the dominance of oxide minerals such as bauxite.

65897d27f3ae.title: Oxisol
65897d27f3ae.sentence: Scientists originally thought that the heavy vegetation of tropical rain forests would provide rich nutrients, but as rainfall passes through the litter on the forest floor the rain is acidified and leaches minerals from the above soil layers.

7a73906e3de6.title: Oxisol
7a73906e3de6.sentence: This forces plants to get their nutrition from decaying litter as oxisols are quite infertile due to the lack of organic matter and the almost complete absence of soluble minerals leached by the wet and humid climate.

ed52651a3ea8.title: Oxisol
ed52651a3ea8.sentence: Permanent cropping of oxisols in low-income areas is very difficult because of low cation exchange capacities and high phosphorus fixation on iron and aluminium oxides (ligand exchange mechanism; inner sphere complex with phosphate).

6ef3c464bed3.title: Oxisol
6ef3c464bed3.sentence: On this account, oxisols are intensively exploited for agriculture in some regions which have enough wealth to support modern agricultural practices (including regular additions of lime and fertilizer).

fed15c2a880c.title: Oxisol
fed15c2a880c.sentence: A recent example of exploitation by modern methods involves the growing of soybeans in Brazil.

31023c7f2525.title: Oxisol
31023c7f2525.sentence: Present-day oxisols are found almost exclusively in tropical areas, in South America and Africa, almost always on highly stable continental cratons.

e61de1875562.title: Oxisol
e61de1875562.sentence: - Aquox – oxisols with a water table at or near the surface for much of the year

50dabfc960e9.title: Oxisol
50dabfc960e9.sentence: - Perox – oxisols of continuously humid climates, where precipitation exceeds evapotranspiration in all months

b680e7288b02.title: Oxisol
b680e7288b02.sentence: - Ustox – oxisols of semiarid and subhumid climates

70157ce12f51.title: Oxisol
70157ce12f51.sentence: Because the present climate can never produce enough weathering to produce oxisols, torrox soils are always paleosols formed during periods of much wetter climates.

ed1e12f3778c.title: Oxisol
ed1e12f3778c.sentence: They occur mainly in Southern Africa.

7652821583b0.title: Oxisol
7652821583b0.sentence: In the World Reference Base for Soil Resources (WRB), they belong mainly to the ferralsols, but some are plinthosols or nitisols.

48a4b6041e54.title: Oxisol
48a4b6041e54.sentence: Some oxisols have been previously classified as laterite soils.

c487620f9452.title: Oxisol
c487620f9452.sentence: Fossil oxisols are known from the first appearance of free oxygen in the atmosphere about 2,200 million years ago.

583293109f83.title: Oxisol
583293109f83.sentence: In warm periods like the Mesozoic and Paleocene, oxisols extended to areas that now have quite cool climates, extending well into North America and Europe.

1c80c86422d0.title: Entisol
1c80c86422d0.sentence: Entisols are soils, as defined under USDA soil taxonomy, that do not show any profile development other than an A-horizon (or “A” horizon).

5142d1dd355a.title: Entisol
5142d1dd355a.sentence: Entisols have no diagnostic horizons, and are unaltered from their parent material, which could be unconsolidated sediment, or rock.

022a0f35abfe.title: Entisol
022a0f35abfe.sentence: Entisols are the most common soils, occupying about 16% of the global ice-free land area.

ace4077007d6.title: Entisol
ace4077007d6.section: Causes of delayed or absent development
ace4077007d6.sentence: - Unweatherable parent materials – sand, iron oxide, aluminium oxide, kaolinite clay.

ab6223a42450.title: Entisol
ab6223a42450.section: Causes of delayed or absent development
ab6223a42450.sentence: - Erosion – common on shoulder slopes; other kinds also important.

a71dd3dc2077.title: Entisol
a71dd3dc2077.section: Causes of delayed or absent development
a71dd3dc2077.sentence: - Deposition – continuous, repeated deposition of new parent materials by flood as diluvium, aeolian processes which means by wind, slope processes as colluvium, mudflows, other means.

33b742222ca2.title: Entisol
33b742222ca2.section: Causes of delayed or absent development
33b742222ca2.sentence: - Shallow to bedrock – may be rock resistant to weathering, such as quartzite or ironstone.

bdd194316948.title: Entisol
bdd194316948.section: Causes of delayed or absent development
bdd194316948.sentence: - Toxic parent materials – serpentine soil, mine spoils, sulfidic clays.

55fe9d43c768.title: USDA soil taxonomy
55fe9d43c768.sentence: Commonly found on unconsolidated river and beach sediments of sand and clay or volcanic ash, some have an A horizon on top of bedrock.

67d564e99e58.title: Entisol
67d564e99e58.sentence: - Aquents – heavily saturated or soaked soils, mostly present at riparian locations (such as river banks, tidal mudflats, estuaries, etc).

9b99953aafb9.title: Entisol
9b99953aafb9.sentence: - Fluvents – alluvial soils, where development is prevented by repeated deposition of sediment during periodic flooding events; present in valleys or river deltas, especially those with high sediment load.

728b6184329d.title: Entisol
728b6184329d.sentence: - Orthents – shallow or "skeletal" soils; found at sites of recent erosion events, or very old landforms completely devoid of weatherable minerals.

b3c273c7133d.title: Entisol
b3c273c7133d.sentence: - Psamments – Entisols that are sandy (through all layers), and in which development is precluded by the impossibility of weathering the sand; formed from shifting or glacial sand dunes.

5eb196687f79.title: Entisol
5eb196687f79.sentence: - Wassents – Entisols that have a positive water potential at the soil surface for more than 21 hours of each day, in all years.

01a664572b8b.title: Entisol
01a664572b8b.sentence: Because of the diversity of their properties, suborders of entisols form individual Reference Soil Groups in the World Reference Base for Soil Resources (WRB): psamments correlate with arenosols, and fluvents with fluvisols.

1594fba58eeb.title: Entisol
1594fba58eeb.sentence: Many orthents belong to regosols or leptosols.

03fd97243f07.title: Entisol
03fd97243f07.sentence: Most wassents and aquic subgroups of other suborders belong to the gleysols.

1cfdaf6fe03a.title: Entisol
1cfdaf6fe03a.sentence: In Australia, most entisols are known as rudosols or tenosols.

b276cf25689d.title: Entisol
b276cf25689d.sentence: Most fossil soils, before the development of terrestrial vegetation in the Silurian, are entisols that show no distinct soil horizons.

82493ef7d9e6.title: Entisol
82493ef7d9e6.sentence: Entisols are common in the paleopedological record ever since the Silurian; however, unlike other soil orders (oxisol, ultisol, gelisol, etc) they do not have value as indicators of climate.

7cea1a8877f6.title: Inceptisol
7cea1a8877f6.sentence: Inceptisols are a soil order in USDA soil taxonomy.

24072ae88577.title: Inceptisol
24072ae88577.sentence: Inceptisols are young, meaning they have little to moderate development and weathering, but are more developed than Entisols.

f877fe43c917.title: Inceptisol
f877fe43c917.sentence: Soils that don't fall into any of the other classifications may default to being classified as an inceptisol.

de74a87e97d1.title: Inceptisol
de74a87e97d1.sentence: Other inceptisol profiles may or may not include a histic or plaggen epipedon, a calcic or petrocalcic horizon, and a duripan or fragipan layer.

ef9ca8dee484.title: Inceptisol
ef9ca8dee484.sentence: Inceptisols are found in a diverse array of environments, with the exception of extremes such as deserts and permafrost landscapes.

0471fb0c8325.title: Inceptisol
0471fb0c8325.sentence: Inceptisols are commonly found in rocky or mountainous areas, and sand dunes.

28b2c50d935c.title: Inceptisol
28b2c50d935c.sentence: They may also form in places with coastal, marine, and riverine deposition of sediments.

0ed229b17ecf.title: Inceptisol
0ed229b17ecf.sentence: Inceptisols can also be formed from late Pleistocene glacial drift.

da0e10219a40.title: Erosion
da0e10219a40.sentence: Inceptisols develop on eroded landscapes that, if stable, would have supported the formation of more developed Alfisols.

d6565f83729f.title: Inceptisol
d6565f83729f.sentence: Suborders of inceptisols are classified by temperature, moisture, saturation, and the type of epipedon.

d5692b848dfc.title: Inceptisol
d5692b848dfc.sentence: - Aquepts – Has a water table close to the surface or at the surface.

16f0bd6d4354.title: Inceptisol
16f0bd6d4354.sentence: - Gelepts – Found in very cold climates with no permafrost

f33a88b67bbc.title: Inceptisol
f33a88b67bbc.sentence: - Cryepts – Found in cold climates and high elevations

1390cd136224.title: Inceptisol
1390cd136224.sentence: - Udepts – Found in humid climates with decent to high precipitation

b7b602fe7556.title: Inceptisol
b7b602fe7556.sentence: - Ustepts – Found in semiarid and sub-humid climates that are moderately dry.

31af99068ca5.title: Inceptisol
31af99068ca5.sentence: - Xerepts – Found in areas with dry summers and moist winters.

72c9f643e21f.title: Inceptisol
72c9f643e21f.sentence: Due to the diversity in properties of inceptisols, they can be used to grow a variety of crops, however some may need additional management.

e85f0de452fe.title: Inceptisol
e85f0de452fe.sentence: Farming on inceptisols suborders such as ustepts and xerepts may not be recommended as the rainfall in the areas they occur may not be sufficient and may require extra investment from the farmer to ensure the crops are watered well.

fc0d3584b237.title: Inceptisol
fc0d3584b237.sentence: Farming on aquepts may require installing drainage pipes to lower the water table, allowing for aeration of the soil.

c7c6242b076f.title: Inceptisol
c7c6242b076f.sentence: However, drainage is not recommended in aquepts with a sulfuric horizon as it can create sulfuric acid, ruining the land if it's not managed properly.

4d0bee0c6926.title: Gelisol
4d0bee0c6926.sentence: Gelisols are an order in USDA soil taxonomy.

1c6d2a9e2aed.title: Gelisol
1c6d2a9e2aed.sentence: They are soils of very cold climates which are defined as containing permafrost within two meters (6 ft 7 in) of the soil surface.

1aed59a2ba65.title: USDA soil taxonomy
1aed59a2ba65.sentence: - Gelisols: Soils with permafrost within 100 cm or cryoturbation (frost churning) within 100 cm plus permafrost within 200 cm; commonly at high latitudes and elevations; 8.6% of global and 7.5% of U.S. ice-free land.

daec86f0af25.title: Gelisol
daec86f0af25.sentence: Because soil organic matter accumulates in the upper layer, most gelisols are black or dark brown in soil color, followed by a shallow mineral layer.

47a2ebb8c081.title: Gelisol
47a2ebb8c081.sentence: Despite the influence of glaciation in most areas where gelisols occur, chemically they are not highly fertile because nutrients, especially calcium and potassium, are very easily leached above the permafrost.

ce50e1f34d88.title: Gelisol
ce50e1f34d88.sentence: The permafrost greatly restricts the engineering use of gelisols, as large structures (e.g. buildings) subside as the frozen earth thaws when they are put in place.

7e9e15d3c963.title: Gelisol
7e9e15d3c963.sentence: Gelisols are found chiefly in Siberia, Alaska and Canada.

b2b804468c6b.title: Gelisol
b2b804468c6b.sentence: Smaller areas are found in the Andes (mainly near the intersection between Chile, Bolivia and Argentina), Tibet, northern Scandinavia and the ice-free parts of Greenland and Antarctica.

8998e13b9701.title: Active layer
8998e13b9701.section: Soil formation in the active layer
8998e13b9701.sentence: The slow rate of decomposition of organic material means gelisols (permafrost soils) are very important as a sink for carbon dioxide.

909672df78ac.title: Gelisol
909672df78ac.sentence: In soil taxonomy, gelisols key out before the histosols.

9384cf909e2f.title: Gelisol
9384cf909e2f.sentence: Organic permafrost soils are therefore gelisols (histels) in the soil taxonomy and histosols (cryic histosols) in the WRB.

34a37c08462d.title: Gelisol
34a37c08462d.sentence: In the World Reference Base for Soil Resources (WRB), most gelisols belong to the cryosols.

33ae0f95d0ab.title: Gelisol
33ae0f95d0ab.sentence: Fossil gelisols are known from as far back as Precambrian ice ages 900 million years ago.

88e4f6966443.title: Psamment
88e4f6966443.sentence: In USDA soil taxonomy, a Psamment is defined as an Entisol which consists basically of unconsolidated sand deposits, often found in shifting sand dunes but also in areas of very coarse-textured parent material subject to millions of years of weathering.

fd1eb9d78aec.title: Psamment
fd1eb9d78aec.sentence: A Psamment has no distinct soil horizons, and must consist entirely of material of loamy sand or coarser in texture.

6023b3a1ed88.title: Psamment
6023b3a1ed88.sentence: Psamments cover 3.4% of the global land mass.

7bf037b478bd.title: Psamment
7bf037b478bd.sentence: They occur throughout the world, being especially abundant in the deserts of Africa and Australia and on the ancient landforms of eastern South America.

73c87a3de7d3.title: Psamment
73c87a3de7d3.sentence: Areas dominated by Psamments also occur in other humid regions, notably in Florida and Nebraska (the Sand Hills).

f52efbd9d317.title: Psamment
f52efbd9d317.sentence: Psamments typically have very low water-holding capacities because the sand in the soil is not graded so that sands of varying coarseness are constantly mixed right through the soil.

f425a1cc1220.title: Psamment
f425a1cc1220.sentence: Because most sands are highly siliceous, Psamments are also extremely low in all essential nutrients, most especially phosphorus and are highly acidic in all except very arid climates.

2274c65fd923.title: Psamment
2274c65fd923.sentence: Psamments formed as a result of glacial erosion (common in northern Europe) are typically of rather higher native fertility because of their youth, but are still much less fertile than most soils in the regions they are located in.

930233f70227.title: Psamment
930233f70227.sentence: The vegetation on Psamments varies enormously owing to the variety of climates, but in many cases is remarkably well-adapted to the climate, as with the Fynbos of the Cape region in South Africa—famous for its remarkable biodiversity and the equally species-rich Kwongan of southwestern Western Australia.

c240cdd0feed.title: Psamment
c240cdd0feed.sentence: Few Psamments are farmed, and where they are, the cost is high because of the expense of fertilization.

a6d6e7b4e70e.title: Psamment
a6d6e7b4e70e.sentence: They are always much less productive than other soils in the same region even when fertilized, and require careful management because the sand is very easily eroded.

7316f3582c1d.title: Psamment
7316f3582c1d.sentence: In USDA soil taxonomy, Psamments are divided into:

beb19c265ede.title: Psamment
beb19c265ede.sentence: - Cryopsamments: Psamments that have a cryic soil temperature regime

6ef8e7891da9.title: Psamment
6ef8e7891da9.sentence: - Ustipsamments: other Psamments that have an ustic moisture regime

86691937f7db.title: Psamment
86691937f7db.sentence: - Xeropsamments: other Psamments that have a xeric moisture regime

d5e49bb78c91.title: Psamment
d5e49bb78c91.sentence: - Quartzipsamments: other Psamments that have, in the 0.02 to 2.0 mm fraction within the particle-size control section, a total of more than 90 percent (by weighted average) resistant minerals

3f3c7ba9f061.title: Psamment
3f3c7ba9f061.sentence: In the World Reference Base for Soil Resources (WRB), most Psamments belong to the Arenosols.

0f332fffcef8.title: Psamment
0f332fffcef8.sentence: However, Psamments of fluviatile, lacustrine or marine origin belong to the Fluvisols.

b102e228c158.title: Paleopedology
b102e228c158.sentence: Paleopedology (palaeopedology in the United Kingdom) is the discipline that studies soils of past geological eras, from quite recent (Quaternary) to the earliest periods of the Earth's history.

7133cbf0b394.title: Paleopedology
7133cbf0b394.sentence: Paleopedology can be seen either as a branch of soil science (pedology) or of paleontology, since the methods it uses are in many ways a well-defined combination of the two disciplines.

950d8f996806.title: Paleopedology
950d8f996806.sentence: Paleopedology's earliest developments arose from observations in Scotland circa 1795 whereby it was found that some soils in cliffs appeared to be remains of a former exposed land surface.

115fef90e089.title: Paleopedology
115fef90e089.sentence: In 1892 Eugene W. Hilgard had related soil and climate in the United States in the same manner, and by the 1950s analysis of Quaternary stratigraphy to monitor recent environmental changes in the northern hemisphere had become firmly established.

01ce34d979e2.title: Paleopedology
01ce34d979e2.sentence: This occurred because, by the 1920s, some soils in Russia had been found by K.D. Glinka that did not fit with present climates and were seen as relics of warmer climates in the past.

e84f3a475255.title: Paleopedology
e84f3a475255.sentence: It was only when the first relationships between soils and climate were observed in the Eurasian Steppe that there was any interest in applying the finds of former soils to past ecosystems.

201a82336ba0.title: Paleopedology
201a82336ba0.section: Finding soil fossils and their structure
201a82336ba0.sentence: Remains of former soils can either be found under deposited sediment in unglaciated areas or in extremely steep cliffs where the old soil can be seen below the younger present-day soil.

56573fac4fe2.title: Paleopedology
56573fac4fe2.section: Finding soil fossils and their structure
56573fac4fe2.sentence: In cases where volcanoes have been active, some soil fossils occur under the volcanic ash.

8657e57ccc0d.title: Paleopedology
8657e57ccc0d.section: Finding soil fossils and their structure
8657e57ccc0d.sentence: Soil fossils can also exist where a younger soil has been eroded (for instance by wind), as in the Badlands of South Dakota.

2a098de3416a.title: Paleopedology
2a098de3416a.section: Finding soil fossils and their structure
2a098de3416a.sentence: This occurs largely because almost all past soils have lost their former vegetative covering, and the organic matter they once supported has been used up by plants since the soil was buried.

3b3166595a39.title: Paleopedology
3b3166595a39.section: Finding soil fossils and their structure
3b3166595a39.sentence: Patterns of root traces including their shape and size, is good evidence for the vegetation type the former soil supported.

82cd8c81334e.title: Paleopedology
82cd8c81334e.sentence: Chemical analysis of soil fossils generally focuses on their lime content, which determines both their pH and how reactive they will be to dilute acids.

d9df2cad56db.title: Paleopedology
d9df2cad56db.sentence: This analysis can be of some use in determining the structure of a soil fossil, but today X-ray diffraction is preferred because it permits the crystal structure of the former soil to be determined.

4d447e6a6b14.title: Paleopedology
4d447e6a6b14.sentence: Interest in earlier soil fossils was much slower to grow but has steadily developed since the 1960s owing to the development of such techniques as X-ray diffraction which permit their classification.

8d6d20198ba5.title: Paleopedology
8d6d20198ba5.sentence: Many Precambrian soils, however, when examined do not fit the characteristics for any of these soil orders and have been placed in an order called green clays.

eafc23cf2194.title: Paleopedology
eafc23cf2194.sentence: The green colour is due to the presence of certain unoxidised minerals found in the primitive Earth because O2 was not present.

7e323061f418.title: Paleopedology
7e323061f418.sentence: This has allowed many developments in paleoecology and paleogeography to take place because soil chemistry can provide a good deal of evidence as to how life moved onto land during the Paleozoic era.

72335d7bce6f.title: Paleopedology
72335d7bce6f.sentence: Paleopedology is an important scientific discipline for the understanding of the ecology and evolution of ancient ecosystems, both on Earth and the emerging field of exoplanet research, or astropedology.

6c3d0db2d84b.title: Orthent
6c3d0db2d84b.sentence: Orthents are soils defined in USDA soil taxonomy as entisols that lack horizon development due to either steep slopes or parent materials that contain no permanent weatherable minerals (such as ironstone).

9a13889669d5.title: Orthent
9a13889669d5.sentence: Typically, Orthents are exceedingly shallow soils.

55c1ad2e7f02.title: Orthent
55c1ad2e7f02.sentence: They are often referred to as skeletal soils or, in the United Nations FAO soil classification, as lithosols.

90583f90e23a.title: Orthent
90583f90e23a.sentence: The basic requirement for recognition of an orthent is that any former soil has been either completely removed or so truncated that characteristics typical of all orders other than entisols are absent.

d14f4f63406d.title: Orthent
d14f4f63406d.sentence: Most orthents are found in very steep, mountainous regions where erodible material is so rapidly removed by erosion that a permanent covering of deep soil cannot establish itself.

fae60c3308cd.title: Orthent
fae60c3308cd.sentence: In Australia and a few regions of Africa, orthents occur in flat terrain because the parent rock contains absolutely no weatherable minerals except short-lived additions from rainfall, so that there is no breaking down of the minerals (chiefly iron oxides) in the rock.

890d8f0d5c2a.title: Orthent
890d8f0d5c2a.sentence: Because of their extreme shallowness and, usually, steepness and consequent high erosion hazard, orthents are not suitable for arable farming.

09fec41eaa5e.title: Orthent
09fec41eaa5e.sentence: The flora typically supported on them is generally of very poor nutritive value for grazing, so that typically only low livestock stocking rates are practicable.

de5b499b8bc3.title: Orthent
de5b499b8bc3.sentence: Many orthents are very important as habitat for wildlife.

c0fdd204186a.title: Entisol
c0fdd204186a.sentence: Orthents may sometimes indicate an extremely ancient landscape with minimal soil formation (i.e., Australia today).

a48f53c46a3a.title: Paleopedological record
a48f53c46a3a.sentence: The paleopedological record is, essentially, the fossil record of soils.

fcc928d821e4.title: Paleopedological record
fcc928d821e4.sentence: The paleopedological record consists chiefly of paleosols buried by flood sediments, or preserved at geological unconformities, especially plateau escarpments or sides of river valleys.

9aaf209a4956.title: Paleopedological record
9aaf209a4956.sentence: Other fossil soils occur in areas where volcanic activity has covered the ancient soils.

84c829ff5a5e.title: Paleopedological record
84c829ff5a5e.sentence: After burial, soil fossils tend to be altered by various chemical and physical processes.

86c93a43bb93.title: Paleopedological record
86c93a43bb93.sentence: - Decomposition of organic matter that was once present in the old soil.

5e6a5272568f.title: Paleopedological record
5e6a5272568f.sentence: - Oxidation of iron from Fe2+ to Fe3+ by O2 as the former soil becomes dry and more oxygen enters the soil.

4b66e0451ddd.title: Paleopedological record
4b66e0451ddd.sentence: - Drying out of hydrous ferric oxides to anhydrous oxides - again due to the presence of more available O2 in the dry environment.

1d8c85fe4c55.title: Paleopedological record
1d8c85fe4c55.sentence: The keys to recognising fossils of various soils include:

0b76f1156111.title: Paleopedological record
0b76f1156111.sentence: - Tubular structures that branch and thin irregularly downward or show the anatomy of fossilised root traces

82464909b1b0.title: Paleopedological record
82464909b1b0.sentence: - Gradational alteration down from a sharp lithological contact like that between land surface and soil horizons

1a2911e68b1e.title: Paleopedological record
1a2911e68b1e.sentence: - Complex patterns of cracks and mineral replacements like those of soil clods (peds) and planar cutans.

bf3ae42ae057.title: Paleopedological record
bf3ae42ae057.sentence: Soil fossils are usually classified by USDA soil taxonomy.

de2be301014a.title: Paleopedological record
de2be301014a.sentence: With the exception of some exceedingly old soils which have a clayey, grey-green horizon that is quite unlike any present soil and clearly formed in the absence of O2, most fossil soils can be classified into one of the twelve orders recognised by this system.

2c0980199ec9.title: Paleopedological record
2c0980199ec9.sentence: This is usually done by means of X-ray diffraction, which allows the various particles within the former soils to be analysed so that it can be seen to which order the soils correspond.

3f06a476710a.title: Paleopedological record
3f06a476710a.section: Records of the various soil groups
3f06a476710a.sentence: During the Precambrian, when life on land was precluded by a very thin or nonexistent ozone layer, soils were subject to much more rapid erosion and most fossils from this period are of undeveloped entisols or inceptisols.

6a36967990b6.title: Paleopedological record
6a36967990b6.section: Records of the various soil groups
6a36967990b6.sentence: Vertisols and aridisols have a continuous fossil record from Paleoproterozoic continents onwards (though little is known about when they were first vegetated), whilst a few andisol fossils are known from the Mesoproterozoic and more abundantly from the Ordovician just before land vegetation began to emerge.

7ba3c6947261.title: Paleopedological record
7ba3c6947261.section: Records of the various soil groups
7ba3c6947261.sentence: Outside of ice ages, oxisols have generally been the dominant soil order in the paleopedological record.

02de7fdcff82.title: Paleopedological record
02de7fdcff82.section: Records of the various soil groups
02de7fdcff82.sentence: This is because soil formation, after which oxisols take more weathering to form than any other soil order, has been almost non-existent outside eras of extensive continental glaciation.

a52786e1122b.title: Paleopedological record
a52786e1122b.section: Records of the various soil groups
a52786e1122b.sentence: This is not only because of the soils formed by glaciation itself, but also because mountain building, which is the other critical factor in producing new soil, has always coincided with a reduction in global temperatures and sea levels.

b89aeba061c2.title: Paleopedological record
b89aeba061c2.section: Records of the various soil groups
b89aeba061c2.sentence: The earliest land vegetation is found in Early Silurian entisols and inceptisols, and with the growth of land vegetation under a protective ozone layer several new soil orders emerged.

91d6f0de3b38.title: Paleopedological record
91d6f0de3b38.section: Records of the various soil groups
91d6f0de3b38.sentence: The first, histosols, emerged in the Devonian but are rare as fossils because most of their mass consists of organic materials that tend to decay quickly.

3996e2d479c1.title: Paleopedological record
3996e2d479c1.section: Records of the various soil groups
3996e2d479c1.sentence: Alfisols and ultisols emerged in the late Devonian and early Carboniferous, and have a continuous, though not rich, fossil record in eras since then.

5155fb315eb6.title: Paleopedological record
5155fb315eb6.section: Records of the various soil groups
5155fb315eb6.sentence: Mollisols, the major agricultural soils of the present, are unique in their geological youth, being known from the Eocene but common only from the Miocene, as grasslands evolved.

65d53375ca3f.title: Paleopedological record
65d53375ca3f.section: Records of the various soil groups
65d53375ca3f.sentence: Owing to their extreme climatic requirements, gelisol fossils are confined to the few periods of extensive continental glaciation - the earliest being 900 million years ago in the Neoproterozoic.

b5c88a8584ec.title: Paleopedological record
b5c88a8584ec.section: Records of the various soil groups
b5c88a8584ec.sentence: An important difference between the paleopedological record and the fossil record of plants and animals is that very few of the soils found are extinct types.

391bf1d969ac.title: Paleopedological record
391bf1d969ac.section: Records of the various soil groups
391bf1d969ac.sentence: Despite the difficulties of identification mentioned earlier, this makes paleopedology (the study of fossil soils) potentially very useful for understanding the ecological relationships in past ecosystems.

3f47cda1b363.title: Sapric
3f47cda1b363.sentence: A sapric is a subtype of a histosol wherein virtually all of the organic material has undergone sufficient decomposition to prevent the identification of plant parts and even fecal matter.

3ce3ab065ffd.title: Sapric
3ce3ab065ffd.sentence: The World Reference Base for Soil Resources (WRB) defines "sapric" (sa) as a histosol having less than one-sixth (by volume) of the organic material consisting of recognizable plant tissue within 100 cm of the soil surface.

6483116ef9c5.title: Sapric
6483116ef9c5.sentence: In the USDA soil taxonomy, sapric may be a subtype of a haplohemist or glacistel type, and may also be a diagnostic organic soil material whose fiber content is less than one-sixth of the volume.

4fc9e15d0227.title: Sapric
4fc9e15d0227.sentence: Muck is a sapric soil that is naturally waterlogged or is artificially drained.

f166a9235ff3.title: Sapric
f166a9235ff3.sentence: Muck soils are defined by the USDA NRCS as sapric organic soils that are saturated more than 30 cumulative days in normal years or are artificially drained.

69be70b95df2.title: Sapric
69be70b95df2.sentence: Muck soils fall under the Organic Order in the Canadian system of soil classification.

7d3ef0792bb5.title: Sapric
7d3ef0792bb5.sentence: Muck soils are organic soils, with a minimum of 30% organic matter and a depth of at least 40 cm.

30039998f419.title: Sapric
30039998f419.sentence: The soils are deep, dark colored, and friable, often underlain by marl, or marly clay.

f2e0bd782f55.title: Mollisol
f2e0bd782f55.sentence: Albolls—wet soils; aquic soil moisture regime with an eluvial horizon

a918748ff2d9.title: Mollisol
a918748ff2d9.sentence: Aquolls—wet soils; aquic soil moisture regime

9a6c6cc06807.title: Mollisol
9a6c6cc06807.sentence: Cryolls—cold climate; frigid or cryic soil temperature regime

09f327c173b3.title: Mollisol
09f327c173b3.sentence: Gelolls—very cold climate; mean annual soil temperature < 0 °C

20c89d4d7989.title: Mollisol
20c89d4d7989.sentence: Soils which are mostly similar to Mollisols but contain either continuous or discontinuous permafrost, consequently affected by cryoturbation are common in high mountain plateaus of Tibet and the Andean altiplano.

ea9fc727448e.title: Mollisol
ea9fc727448e.sentence: Such soils are called Molliturbels or Mollorthels and provide the best grazing land in such cold climates because they are not acidic like many other soils of very cold climates.

6763ac22d24b.title: Vertisol
6763ac22d24b.sentence: In the USDA soil taxonomy, vertisols are subdivided into:

69002f18ff41.title: Vertisol
69002f18ff41.sentence: - Cryerts: They have a cryic soil temperature regime.

5b3292320d9c.title: Vertisol
5b3292320d9c.sentence: They show cracks open for at least 60 consecutive days during the summer, but closed for at least 60 consecutive days during the winter.

453c3ad53aaf.title: Vertisol
453c3ad53aaf.sentence: - Usterts: They have cracks open for at least 90 cumulative days per year.

d00de457b1d0.title: Vertisol
d00de457b1d0.sentence: - Uderts: They have cracks open less than 90 cumulative days per year and less than 60 consecutive days during the summer.

bab28db975ed.title: Vertisol
bab28db975ed.sentence: When precipitation exceeds evapotranspiration, ponding may occur.

80955a41d660.title: Vertisol
80955a41d660.sentence: Manganese may partly be responsible for the dark color of the soil profile.

4b8002da74ce.title: Vertisol
4b8002da74ce.sentence: Cryerts are most extensive in the grassland and forest-grassland transitions zones of the Canadian Prairies and at similar latitudes in Russia.

637b2e6cfbe0.title: Vertisol
637b2e6cfbe0.sentence: - Xererts: These have a thermic, mesic, or frigid soil temperature regime.

f10d4f3ce59c.title: Vertisol
f10d4f3ce59c.sentence: Xererts are most extensive in the eastern Mediterranean and parts of California.

08ffeea9c9c9.title: Vertisol
08ffeea9c9c9.sentence: Globally, this suborder is the most extensive of the vertisols order, encompassing the vertisols of the tropics and monsoonal climates in Australia, India, and Africa.

4cbfe99d3e3d.title: Vertisol
4cbfe99d3e3d.sentence: - Torrerts: They have cracks closed for less than 60 consecutive days when the soil temperature at 50 cm is above 8 °C. These soils are not extensive in the U.S., and occur mostly in west Texas, New Mexico, Arizona, and South Dakota, but are the most extensive suborder of vertisols in Australia.

7e590936eca0.title: Vertisol
7e590936eca0.sentence: In some areas, cracks open only in drought years.

3ba654d947fc.title: Vertisol
3ba654d947fc.sentence: Uderts are of small extent globally, being most abundant in Uruguay and eastern Argentina, but also found in parts of Queensland and the "Black Belt" of Mississippi and Alabama.

2843d2b21882.title: Alfisol
2843d2b21882.sentence: The fossil record of Alfisols extends back to the Late Devonian.

dcb2b27fe012.title: Alfisol
dcb2b27fe012.sentence: The Alfisol paleosols were woodland soils and early forest soils.

24b0ef8ca5f5.title: Alfisol
24b0ef8ca5f5.sentence: Probably owing to their fertility, they are the oldest forest soils; vegetation on weathered Oxisols, by contrast, is not known earlier than Middle Permian.

b7db5465e1d3.title: Alfisol
b7db5465e1d3.sentence: The oldest of the Alfisol paleosol forest soils are in the paleosols of the Aztec Siltstone in Victoria Land, Antarctica.

ca12b4143c40.title: Alfisol
ca12b4143c40.sentence: From the fossil wood and spores found in the Aztec Siltstone, there is a strong indication that the trees were Archaeopteris-Callixylon.

c69f5e36c47f.title: Alfisol
c69f5e36c47f.sentence: The tapering geometry of large woody root traces is the most likely cause of the intimate relationship between Argillic horizons, Alfisols, and forests.

c1593512e1ba.title: Alfisol
c1593512e1ba.sentence: The large woody root traces can transport water and clay using their large pipes.

104ef3bf5229.title: Alfisol
104ef3bf5229.sentence: They are efficient at moving soil into a subsurface horizon when the plant dies and the roots decay.

9f68237a6be2.title: Alfisol
9f68237a6be2.sentence: All the tetrapod bones and tracks from the paleosol sequences of Late Devonian and Mississippian of New York and Pennsylvania, U.S.A. are found in Aridisols and Alfisols.

4ff1c3f34c99.title: Alfisol
4ff1c3f34c99.sentence: The ichnofacies of the ground-nesting bees, Celliforma, was formed in well drained Alfisols as well as Aridisols and Oxisols.

28eaf4d37557.title: Alfisol
28eaf4d37557.sentence: The Termitichnus ichnofacies, which included a large array of termite nests and pellets, is found in Oligocene Alfisols, Aridisols, and Oxisols.

021b7a868bc0.title: Ultisol
021b7a868bc0.sentence: The lack of organic matter in Ultisol makes it difficult for plants to grow without proper care and considerations.

14da5d5cfbd2.title: Ultisol
14da5d5cfbd2.sentence: Soil tests help indicate the pH, and red clay soil typically has a low pH.

2fb48e2cce96.title: Ultisol
2fb48e2cce96.sentence: Soil amendments are generally required each year in order to sustain flourishing plant life in regions with primarily Ultisol soil.

95865921339d.title: Ultisol
95865921339d.sentence: The use of soil tests, coupled with the corresponding provisions, can alleviate issues of nutrition and irrigation that can result from non porous Ultisol.

05c856abaa62.title: Ultisol
05c856abaa62.sentence: The addition of lime is used to help to increase the pH in soil and can help increase the pH in Ultisol as well.

bd67074259eb.title: Ultisol
bd67074259eb.sentence: Generally, gardeners aim to have 45% mineral, 5% organic matter and 50% pore space in their soil.

e1f9dafe346b.title: Ultisol
e1f9dafe346b.sentence: The composition of Ultisol in North Carolina, for reference, is approximately 16% pore space, 2% organic matter and 82% mineral.

5b96e13bc35f.title: Ultisol
5b96e13bc35f.sentence: The addition of mulch helps to make the soil more porous.

902662a404e9.title: Ultisol
902662a404e9.sentence: Specifically, adding a 2- to 3-inch layer of compost and manure should be mixed into the soil to match a shovel's depth.

5236fa913258.title: Ultisol
5236fa913258.sentence: However, microorganisms in the soil consume the same nutrients that plants use to grow so certain nutrients will remain unavailable to plants until the microorganisms completely break down the organic material and release nutrients.

b80a6f36f768.title: Ultisol
b80a6f36f768.sentence: To avoid the delay presented by this process, adding manure in the fall is advisable.

46bcd9990d25.title: Ultisol
46bcd9990d25.sentence: Some gardeners who live in areas with large amounts of red clay soil use raised beds or Hügelkultur to avoid having to amend the soil.

0305dc9ea119.title: Ultisol
0305dc9ea119.section: Gardening in Ultisol > Planting in Ultisol
0305dc9ea119.sentence: Plants found native to regions with high amounts of Ultisol can thrive.

9fafcc755fd2.title: Ultisol
9fafcc755fd2.section: Gardening in Ultisol > Planting in Ultisol
9fafcc755fd2.sentence: Generally, these species adapt to poorly drained, damp soils.

bc1876119fb6.title: Ultisol
bc1876119fb6.sentence: - Aquults: Ultisols with a water table at or near the surface for much of the year

a625e306ae8c.title: Ultisol
a625e306ae8c.sentence: - Humults: well-drained Ultisols that have high organic matter content

c62920513db8.title: Ultisol
c62920513db8.sentence: - Ustults: Ultisols of semiarid and subhumid climates

9f48cc3329d3.title: Ultisol
9f48cc3329d3.sentence: - Xerults: temperate Ultisols with arid summers and moist winters

cd74e891acd1.title: Cecil (soil)
cd74e891acd1.sentence: Originally mapped in Cecil County, Maryland in 1899, more than 10 million acres (40,000 km2) of the Cecil soil series (Fine, kaolinitic, thermic Typic Kanhapludults) are now mapped in the Piedmont region of the southeastern United States.

43f19affdb4e.title: Bama (soil)
43f19affdb4e.sentence: Bama soils are classified in USDA soil taxonomy as fine-loamy, siliceous, subactive, thermic Typic Paleudults.

7284eab65d40.title: Soil in the United States
7284eab65d40.sentence: The USDA soil taxonomy hierarchy includes orders, suborders, great groups, subgroups, families and series, with each series representing a unique kind of soil.

0aa8ffe1a0dc.title: Soil in the United States
0aa8ffe1a0dc.sentence: Thus the great diversity of geologic materials, geomorphic processes, climatic conditions, biotic assemblages and land surface ages in the United States is responsible for the presence of an enormous variety of mineral and organic soils.

2b19c920025c.title: Soil in the United States
2b19c920025c.sentence: In the United States, over 20,000 soil series have been identified.[1] Soil maps and associated data are available for more than 95 percent of the nation’s counties.[2]

4311b98ac683.title: Soil in the United States
4311b98ac683.sentence: Web Soil Survey (WSS) provides soil data and information produced by the National Cooperative Soil Survey.[5] It is operated by the USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service (NRCS) and provides access to the largest natural resource information system in the world.

2ebb36bbe8dc.title: Soil in the United States
2ebb36bbe8dc.sentence: NRCS has soil maps and data available online for more than 95 percent of the nation’s counties and anticipates having 100 percent in the near future.

5f5f2c76ad48.title: Soil in the United States
5f5f2c76ad48.sentence: The percentages of land area (in the US and associated territories, etc.) occupied by soils of the twelve orders have been estimated as:

e57e4f84ecd8.title: Soil in the United States
e57e4f84ecd8.sentence: In the US, Mollisols occur mostly on the Great Plains, and in some areas of the west.

32851ee31295.title: Soil in the United States
32851ee31295.sentence: Aridisols occur in parts of the western United States which are too dry for the growth of mesophytic plants.

dcf1720b4099.title: Soil in the United States
dcf1720b4099.sentence: In the US, Gelisols occur only in parts of Alaska; they are characterized by having permafrost within 100 cm of the surface.

b5ba2974cc31.title: Soil in the United States

627728a9af30.title: Soil in the United States

0de630085947.title: Soil in the United States

99ec911360ce.title: Paleopedology
99ec911360ce.sentence: In order to make an accurate assessment of the amount of soil formation that has occurred, the parent material must be known to establish a base line, or starting point in the soil's formation.

d362d22eea6d.title: Paleopedology
d362d22eea6d.sentence: The difficulty lies with the fact that the parent material no longer exists, and therefore its nature can only be estimated using nearby materials.

0dd6b6a3cb59.title: Paleopedology
0dd6b6a3cb59.sentence: During early formation, soils are not so different from their parent materials.

cd177cffeddf.title: Paleopedology
cd177cffeddf.sentence: With time however, soils will contain less features of their original parent material.

8727b13bb7ca.title: Paleopedology
8727b13bb7ca.sentence: This provides a starting point for understanding what role the parent material played during the formation of the soil.

e6fff0199d12.title: Paleopedology
e6fff0199d12.sentence: These estimates are typically based on four critical assumptions that should be recognized as assumptions and thus assessed cautiously when evaluating soils and paleosols.

060f2ffd01c5.title: Paleopedology
060f2ffd01c5.sentence: - The first assumption is that the parent material is fresh.

9377208a77c8.title: Paleopedology
9377208a77c8.sentence: - The second assumption is that the parent material had a uniform composition within the soil profile.

c73d5a1611e3.title: Paleopedology
c73d5a1611e3.sentence: - The third assumption is that at least one of the constituents of the parent material is unaltered by weathering and is still present.

419b67e309f1.title: Paleopedology
419b67e309f1.sentence: - The fourth assumption is that volume change is proportional to thickness and density.

345905b78d94.title: Paleopedology
345905b78d94.sentence: The main problem with this is that no constituents are fully immune to the broad weathering processes that exist in nature.

26d078c2cccb.title: Paleopedology
26d078c2cccb.sentence: For example, quartz is a fairly stable mineral in soils with pH>9, while alumina (Al2O3) is stable in between pH 4.5 and 8 (mostly in clay).

5355eceb34eb.title: Paleopedology
5355eceb34eb.sentence: Trace elements that are usually stable in soils over a wider range of environmental conditions include lead (Pb) and zirconium (Zr) but are not always sufficiently present to be useful.

f1f96a91a8b9.title: Paleopedology
f1f96a91a8b9.sentence: Soil climate is also a special kind of microclimate.

55c295a6b4fc.title: Paleopedology
55c295a6b4fc.sentence: It refers to the moisture, temperature, and other climatic indicators that are found within the pores of soil.

015afb6dfa84.title: Paleopedology
015afb6dfa84.sentence: For example, in well-drained soils, the soil climate is a somewhat subdued version of the regional climate.

14c877ea684d.title: Paleopedology
14c877ea684d.sentence: In waterlogged soils, soil climate is not related to regional climate because the temperature and oxygenation of waterlogged soils is more dependent on local groundwater paths and rates than on atmospheric conditions.

d43f5c3114f5.title: Paleopedology
d43f5c3114f5.sentence: The tendency to use climatic data for the classification of soils has been challenged by efforts to base the classification of soil on observable features within the soils.

9fe0394a1082.title: Paleopedology
9fe0394a1082.sentence: The classification of climate from paleosols can be related using climatically sensitive features of soils that are sensitive to particular climatic variables, but even the best of these features lack precision.

d27b42cd0060.title: Paleopedology
d27b42cd0060.sentence: This is because soils are not as sensitive as meteorological instruments for recording climatic conditions.

42fc9d7d096f.title: Paleopedology
42fc9d7d096f.sentence: However, in a fairly broad category, climate can be interpreted from the sensitive features found in soils.

d6ba3ad4770b.title: Paleopedology
d6ba3ad4770b.sentence: Estimates of other types of soil climate are now beginning to find their way into the classification of soils, the models for soil formation, and into the study of soil biology.

40bce2a87f77.title: Paleopedology
40bce2a87f77.sentence: A fossilized footprint, burrow, or coprolite (fossil feces), are examples of trace fossils (ichnofossils).

04f032117d85.title: Paleopedology
04f032117d85.sentence: These trace fossils do not represent any physical part of an organism, but rather are evidence of an organism's activity within its environment.

2337a3722246.title: Paleopedology
2337a3722246.sentence: A good example of this is root traces.

dcc2c7e13a7a.title: Paleopedology
dcc2c7e13a7a.sentence: Whereas a bone, leaf, or stem might provide enough information to positively identify a particular species, trace fossils rarely allow for such a precise identification.

e0e8b4ce482b.title: Paleopedology
e0e8b4ce482b.sentence: However, unlike fossilized body parts which can be affected by many variables, trace fossils are not often transported away and are usually found in the place where the organism lived.

7084de1c6efd.title: Paleopedology
7084de1c6efd.sentence: This advantage makes trace fossils in paleosols especially important because they allow for interpretation of the animal's behavior in its natural environment.

e63480717024.title: Paleopedology
e63480717024.sentence: A great example of this is the simple shallow fossilized burrows of solitary bees that make their homes in soil.

4be300baadad.title: Paleopedology
4be300baadad.sentence: Analyzing the pattern of root traces, the sequence of soil horizons, and other features can help identify the type of vegetation that was present during the formation of the soil.

859d2c1df1bb.title: Paleopedology
859d2c1df1bb.sentence: Examples of plant formation include forests, woodlands, and grasslands.

982531c0b043.title: Paleopedology
982531c0b043.sentence: Because it may not be possible to determine whether a particular plant was an oak, eucalyptus, or other species, plant formations in paleosols make it possible to identify an ancient woodland ecosystem from an ancient grassland ecosystem.

47fa566ac658.title: Paleopedology
47fa566ac658.sentence: Just as fossilized footprints, burrows, and coprolites represent trace fossils or organisms, paleosols can be considered trace fossils of an ancient ecosystem.

7c1f4ae31f98.title: Podzol
7c1f4ae31f98.sentence: Podzols, also known as podosols, spodosols, or espodossolos, are the typical soils of coniferous or boreal forests and also the typical soils of eucalypt forests and heathlands in southern Australia.

4ab8d45c4e90.title: Podzol
4ab8d45c4e90.sentence: Podzol means "under-ash" and is derived from the Russian под (pod) + зола́ (zola); the full form is подзо́листая по́чва (podzolistaya pochva), meaning "under-ashed soil".

ed9819ff0223.title: Podzol
ed9819ff0223.sentence: The term was first given in mid-1875 by Vasily Dokuchaev, and over time adopted by soil science.

ac0511a2f1e1.title: Podzol
ac0511a2f1e1.sentence: It refers to the common experience of Russian peasants of plowing up an apparent under-layer of ash (leached or E horizon) during first plowing of a virgin soil of that type.

9ae7e4261f31.title: Podzol
9ae7e4261f31.sentence: It is found under a layer of organic material in the process of decomposition, which is usually 5 to 10 centimetres (2.0 to 3.9 in) thick.

f7dbd67a4f71.title: Podzol
f7dbd67a4f71.sentence: The E horizon (or Ae in Canadian soil classification system), which is usually 4 to 8 centimetres (1.6 to 3.1 in) thick, is low in Fe and Al oxides and humus.

600d096d6541.title: Podzol
600d096d6541.sentence: The bleached soil horizon, which always has a higher value than the horizons above and below it, goes over into a red or red-brown horizon (so-called Podzolic B).

cf5ec65d1a84.title: Podzol
cf5ec65d1a84.sentence: Podzolization (or Podsolization) is a complex soil formation process by which dissolved organic matter and ions of iron and aluminium, released through weathering of various minerals, form organo-mineral complexes (chelates) and are moved from the upper parts of the soil profile and deposit in the deeper parts of soil.

06b5f29e49ac.title: Podzol
06b5f29e49ac.sentence: These soluble chelates then relocate with percolating water from the A (or E horizon) to the B horizon.

ce8aa1836473.title: Podzol
ce8aa1836473.sentence: Usually, the boundary between the B and eluvial Ae (or E) horizon is very distinct, and sometimes a hardpan (or Ortstein) can form, as the relocated Fe and Al and organic matter increase mineral particles, cementing them into this compacted layer.

c62cffff8ee2.title: Podzol
c62cffff8ee2.sentence: Podzols can occur on almost any parent material but generally derive from either quartz-rich sands and sandstone or sedimentary debris from magmatic rocks, provided there is high precipitation.

bad6947fa22c.title: Podzol
bad6947fa22c.sentence: Podzolization usually occurs under forest or heath vegetation and is common in cool and humid climates as these climates inhibit the activity of soil microbes in the topsoil.

6169da53d641.title: Podzol
6169da53d641.sentence: Overall, podzolization happens where the decomposition of organic matter is inhibited and as a result, acidic organic surface (mor) layers build up.

fd306f0e1814.title: Podzol
fd306f0e1814.sentence: Most Podzols are poor soils for agriculture due to the sandy portion, resulting in a low level of moisture and nutrients.

40845e2a7d0f.title: Podzol
40845e2a7d0f.sentence: A low pH further compounds issues, along with phosphate deficiencies and aluminum toxicity.

e9e2d5f3e015.title: Podzol
e9e2d5f3e015.sentence: The best agricultural use of Podzols is for grazing, although well-drained loamy types can be very productive for crops if lime and fertilizer are used.

791038ec0215.title: Podzol
791038ec0215.sentence: Podzols cover about 4,850,000 square kilometres (1,870,000 mi2) worldwide and are usually found under sclerophyllous woody vegetation.

9af0f00917c8.title: Podzol
9af0f00917c8.sentence: By extent Podzols are most common in temperate and boreal zones of the Northern Hemisphere but they can also be found in other settings including both temperate rainforests and tropical areas.

344e05685416.title: Podzol

69b37b76060b.title: Podzol

5221fb0e4451.title: Chernozem
5221fb0e4451.sentence: Chernozem (/ˈtʃɜːrnəzɛm/ CHUR-nə-zem), also called black soil, black earth, dark earth, regur soil or black cotton soil, is a black-colored soil containing a high percentage of humus (4% to 16%) and high percentages of phosphorus and ammonia compounds.

b0691b077b5a.title: Chernozem
b0691b077b5a.sentence: Chernozems are a Reference Soil Group of the World Reference Base for Soil Resources (WRB).

1d5573f301de.title: Chernozem
1d5573f301de.sentence: The name comes from the Russian terms for black (чёрный čjornyj) and soil, earth or land (земля zemlja).

7c151e044839.title: Chernozem
7c151e044839.sentence: Chernozem is very fertile and can produce high agricultural yields with its high moisture-storage capacity.

1499f6a3196c.title: Chernozem
1499f6a3196c.sentence: However, prolonged agricultural use of chernozems still require replenishment with fertilizers because they easily can get depleted of nutrients through continuous decrease in humus content.

cb8d1bea5fa9.title: Chernozem
cb8d1bea5fa9.sentence: Studies of the steppe soils of the Poltava region in the Russian Empire in 1883, conducted by geologist Vasily Dokuchaev, showed that the peasants called all soils by color, so the scientist began to use such names.

0324874a52fd.title: Chernozem
0324874a52fd.sentence: - 1883: Vasily Dokuchaev published his book Russian Chernozem with a complete study of this soil in European Russia.

873def7421a0.title: Chernozem
873def7421a0.sentence: Dokuchaev was the first to describe the chernozem of the European part of the Russian Empire, and discovered its fertility.

c21a0b5fe01c.title: Chernozem
c21a0b5fe01c.sentence: Chernozem covers about 230 million hectares of land.

5700412cedcf.title: Chernozem
5700412cedcf.sentence: There are two "chernozem belts" in the world.

459a7164bb1c.title: Chernozem
459a7164bb1c.sentence: One is the Eurasian Steppe that includes the Peri-Carpathian Steppe, East European Forest Steppe, Pontic-Caspian Steppe, Kazakh Steppe and Mongolian-Manchurian Steppe.

c1fb49221012.title: Chernozem
c1fb49221012.sentence: The other stretches from the Canadian Prairies in Manitoba through the Great Plains of the United States as far south as Kansas.

20b60f493910.title: Chernozem
20b60f493910.sentence: Chernozem layer thickness may vary widely, from several centimetres up to 1.5 metres (60 inches) in Ukraine, as well as the Red River Valley region in the northern United States and Canada (location of the prehistoric Lake Agassiz).

0c92ecd05b17.title: Solonchak

c03fc506c41b.title: Anthrosol
c03fc506c41b.sentence: Such soils can be formed from any parent soil, and are commonly found in areas where agriculture has been practiced for centuries.

d14eda3ae276.title: Anthrosol
d14eda3ae276.sentence: For example, in northwestern Europe anthrosols commonly have plaggic or terric (strongly affected by manure) horizons, and together they cover some 500,000 hectares.

2bdde97b12fd.title: Anthrosol
2bdde97b12fd.sentence: A high phosphate concentration is a common indicator of decaying organic matter, such as bones, tissue, or excrement.

6b5d2b8f0063.title: Anthrosol

0bf21a12e93d.title: Anthrosol

efd46c037dec.title: Anthrosol

01e469bd8e9c.title: Anthrosol
01e469bd8e9c.sentence: Anthrosols that can indicate such activity can be described as, for instance, plaggic (from the long-term use of manure to enrich soil), irragric (from the use of flood or surface irrigation), hortic (from deep cultivation, manure use and presence of other anthropogenic organic matter such as kitchen waste), anthraquic (from anthropos – man and aqua – water – meaning produced by man-made soil moisture management including irrigation or terracing).

6cbbbc3faf79.title: Anthrosol

f46d9ed64c7d.title: Anthrosol

2b4b4afb2d12.title: Anthrosol

0ebba3dac8e9.title: Anthrosol

70def897d6a0.title: Aridity
70def897d6a0.sentence: These areas, which make up approximately 43% of total global available land area, tend to fall upon degraded soils, and their health and functioning are key necessities of regulating ecosystems’ atmospheric components.

71391ba064a6.title: Aridity

d158f7f04de9.title: Aridity
