0a86e0682312.title: Aridity

d8118b526902.title: Aridity

d96548150faf.title: Desertification

c31dfe964d21.title: Gleysol
c31dfe964d21.sentence: A gleysol or gley soil is a hydric soil that unless drained is saturated with groundwater for long enough to develop a characteristic gleyic colour pattern.

a4b0c72a6f9f.title: Gleysol
a4b0c72a6f9f.sentence: The pattern is essentially made up of reddish, brownish, or yellowish colours at surfaces of soil particles and/or in the upper soil horizons mixed with greyish/blueish colours inside the peds and/or deeper in the soil.

6219c0580fed.title: Gleysol
6219c0580fed.sentence: Gleysols are also known as Gleyzems, meadow soils, Aqu-suborders of Entisols, Inceptisols and Mollisols (USDA soil taxonomy), or as groundwater soils and hydro-morphic soils.

7062fd085a17.title: Gleysol
7062fd085a17.sentence: In the World Reference Base for Soil Resources (WRB), soils with redox processes due to ascending groundwater belong to the Reference Soil Group Gleysols.

6a354eb5628d.title: Gleysol
6a354eb5628d.sentence: Soils with redox processes due to stagnant water are Stagnosols and Planosols.

ab833383d406.title: Gleysol
ab833383d406.sentence: Gleysols occur within a wide range of unconsolidated materials, mainly fluvial, marine and lacustrine sediments of Pleistocene or Holocene age, having basic to acidic mineralogy.

1d17b6c8ba66.title: Gleysol
1d17b6c8ba66.sentence: They are found in depression areas and low landscape positions with shallow groundwater.

0d6f808a0ff5.title: Gleysol
0d6f808a0ff5.sentence: Gleysols occupy an estimated 720 million hectares worldwide.

128aea8f58c4.title: Gleysol
128aea8f58c4.sentence: The largest extent of Gleysols is in northern Russia, Siberia, Canada, Alaska, China and Bangladesh.

28ddb049ade5.title: Gleysol
28ddb049ade5.sentence: An estimated 200 million hectares of gleysols are found in the tropics, mainly in the Amazon region, equatorial Africa, and the coastal swamps of Southeast Asia.

5da5b67d2bbb.title: Gleysol
5da5b67d2bbb.sentence: Farmers use artificially-drained gleysols for arable cropping, dairy farming and horticulture.

2f747235431c.title: Gleysol
2f747235431c.sentence: Gleysols in the tropics and subtropics are widely planted with rice.

5b8691e9e987.title: Fluvisol
5b8691e9e987.sentence: A fluvisol in the World Reference Base for Soil Resources (WRB) is a genetically young soil in alluvial deposits.

8dbb1476c697.title: Fluvisol
8dbb1476c697.sentence: Apart from river sediments, they also occur in lacustrine and marine deposits.

dd2b33952079.title: Fluvisol
dd2b33952079.sentence: Fluvisols are found on alluvial plains, river fans, valleys and tidal marshes on all continents and in all climate zones.

1ce3acad29b9.title: Fluvisol
1ce3acad29b9.sentence: The soils have a clear evidence of stratification.

b54170a64a82.title: Fluvisol
b54170a64a82.sentence: Soil horizons are weakly developed, but a distinct topsoil horizon (but no mollic or umbric horizon) may be present.

df1cb0a0334e.title: Fluvisol
df1cb0a0334e.sentence: Under natural conditions periodical flooding is fairly common.

fa0f1da2b732.title: Fluvisol
fa0f1da2b732.sentence: Fluvisols correlate with fluvents and fluvaquents of the USDA soil taxonomy.

4d509d8a5164.title: Fluvisol
4d509d8a5164.sentence: The good natural fertility of most fluvisols and their attractive dwelling sites on river levees and higher parts in marine landscapes were recognized in prehistoric times.

3c1c2b03c6ef.title: Fluvisol
3c1c2b03c6ef.sentence: Many dryland crops are grown on fluvisols, normally with some form of water control.

5fcd27deae7f.title: Fluvisol
5fcd27deae7f.sentence: On tropical Fluvisols with satisfactory irrigation and drainage paddy rice cultivation is widespread.

239a5397673e.title: Fluvisol
239a5397673e.sentence: Some coastal lowlands have fluvisols with sulphidic material within the profile (a thionic horizon).

993e61689431.title: Fluvisol
993e61689431.sentence: These acid sulfate soils have severe constraints for agricultural use as low pH-values, toxic aluminium levels and high concentrations of salts.

329cf463133b.title: Fluvisol
329cf463133b.sentence: Tidal lands that are strongly saline are best kept under mangroves or some other salt-vegetation.

5dde803e27fa.title: Fluvisol
5dde803e27fa.sentence: Major concentrations of fluvisols are found along rivers and lakes, e.g. in the Amazon Basin, the Ganges Plain of India, the plains near Lake Chad in Central Africa, and the marshlands of Brazil, Paraguay and northern Argentina.

6d4c80df2390.title: Fluvisol
6d4c80df2390.sentence: Also in deltaic areas, e.g. the deltas of the Ganges–Brahmaputra, Indus, Mekong, Mississippi, Nile, Niger, Orinoco, Po, Rhine, Rio de la Plata, and Zambezi.

088f2972af3f.title: Acrisol
088f2972af3f.sentence: An Acrisol is a Reference Soil Group of the World Reference Base for Soil Resources (WRB).

d1018694a183.title: Acrisol
d1018694a183.sentence: It is associated with humid, tropical climates, such as those found in Brazil, and often supports forested areas.

cb0d2029b6a8.title: Acrisol
cb0d2029b6a8.sentence: Acrisol's low fertility and toxic amounts of aluminium pose limitations to its agricultural use, favouring in many places its use for silviculture, low-intensity pasture, and protected areas.

ad65800fd665.title: Acrisol
ad65800fd665.sentence: Crops that can be successfully cultivated, if the climate allows, include tea, rubber tree, oil palm, coffee and sugar cane.

0b9cb6e2cfab.title: Terra preta
0b9cb6e2cfab.sentence: Terra preta zones are generally surrounded by terra comum ([ˈtɛʁɐ koˈmũ, ku-]), or "common soil"; these are infertile soils, mainly acrisols, but also ferralsols and arenosols.

e18a05122109.title: Leptosol
e18a05122109.sentence: A Leptosol in the World Reference Base for Soil Resources (WRB) is a very shallow soil over continuous rock or a deeper soil that is extremely rich in coarse fragments (gravelly and/or stony).

ef7a1677086f.title: Leptosol
ef7a1677086f.sentence: Leptosols cover approximately 1.7 billion hectares of the Earth's surface.

e763ee37d01f.title: Leptosol
e763ee37d01f.sentence: They are found from the tropics to the cold polar regions and from sea level to the highest peaks.

4858f595f1cc.title: Leptosol
4858f595f1cc.sentence: Leptosols are particularly widespread in mountain areas, notably in Asia, South America, northern Canada and Alaska; and in the Saharan and Arabian deserts.

b6817601ed60.title: Leptosol
b6817601ed60.sentence: Elsewhere, Leptosols can be found on hard rocks or where erosion has kept pace with soil formation or removed the top of the soil.

a1be057fc4a9.title: Leptosol
a1be057fc4a9.sentence: The very shallow, less than 10 cm deep, Lithic Leptosols in mountain regions are the most extensive Leptosols on Earth.

6e3c8c457f24.title: Rendzina
6e3c8c457f24.sentence: In the World Reference Base for Soil Resources, rendzina soils would be classified as leptosols, chernozems, kastanozems, or phaeozems, depending on their specific characteristics.

2603fcfbdf12.title: Leptosol
2603fcfbdf12.sentence: Leptosols are unattractive soils for rainfed agriculture because of their inability to hold water, but may sometimes have potential for tree crops or extensive grazing.

f23ae998093a.title: Cambisol
f23ae998093a.sentence: A Cambisol in the World Reference Base for Soil Resources (WRB) is a soil in the beginning of soil formation.

638c00a52315.title: Cambisol
638c00a52315.sentence: This is evident from weak, mostly brownish discolouration and/or structure formation in the soil profile.

e5a823200b58.title: Cambisol
e5a823200b58.sentence: Most of these soils make good agricultural land and are intensively used.

510926c519b1.title: Cambisol
510926c519b1.sentence: Cambisols in temperate climates are among the most productive soils on earth.

203d164f485a.title: Cambisol
203d164f485a.sentence: Cambisols cover an estimated 15 million square kilometres worldwide.

dc784492491d.title: Cambisol
dc784492491d.sentence: They are well represented in temperate and boreal regions that were under the influence of glaciation during the Pleistocene, partly because the soil's parent material is still young, but also because soil formation is comparatively slow in the cool, northern regions.

290de897cf43.title: Cambisol
290de897cf43.sentence: Cambisols are less common in the tropics and subtropics, but they are common in areas with active erosion where they may occur in association with mature tropical soils.

aa1ddf673520.title: Brown earth
aa1ddf673520.sentence: This gives rise to a universal division of these, generally brown and well drained soils into the weakly leached brown earths - called cambisols in the international World Reference Base for Soil Resources (WRB); and more leached brown podzolic soils in which there is an orange-brown B horizon, but no pale leached horizon between the A and the B horizons.

fceb82763eb5.title: Polish Soil Classification
fceb82763eb5.sentence: Brown forest soils (Brown earths, Polish: Gleby brunatnoziemne; WRB: Cambisols; ST: Inceptisols - Udepts)

3ce217a5b650.title: Luvisol
3ce217a5b650.sentence: Luvisols are a group of soils, comprising one of the 32 Reference Soil Groups in the international system of soil classification, the World Reference Base for Soil Resources (WRB).

f3c580da511b.title: Luvisol
f3c580da511b.sentence: The main characteristic of Luvisols is an argic horizon, a subsurface zone with higher clay content than the material above it.

f524e1ca7e43.title: Luvisol
f524e1ca7e43.sentence: This typically arises as clay is washed downward by water and accumulates at greater depth.

746784a36c6c.title: Luvisol
746784a36c6c.sentence: The clay minerals have not been extensively weathered and are therefore of the high-activity, 2:1 type, giving these soils high cation exchange capacities and high base saturation.

6e2c609406ac.title: Luvisol
6e2c609406ac.sentence: In uneroded landscapes, a lighter, clay-depleted eluvial horizon occurs above the argic horizon.

fd9cefda05d5.title: Luvisol
fd9cefda05d5.sentence: Luvisols cover 500–600 million ha of land area, mainly in the temperate zones.

d89b2ea027da.title: Luvisol
d89b2ea027da.sentence: They form on a wide variety of mineral parent materials.

6ffe00a387ec.title: Luvisol
6ffe00a387ec.sentence: They are widespread, especially in temperate climates, and are generally fertile.

e184da11ab6e.title: Luvisol
e184da11ab6e.sentence: Luvisols are widely used for agriculture.

70929b398028.title: Luvisol
70929b398028.sentence: In Mediterranean regions, the formation of hematite can produce red-coloured Chromic Luvisols.

82c773e8ac33.title: Duplex soil
82c773e8ac33.sentence: The term "duplex" is used in Australia for soils with contrasting texture between soil horizons, although such soils are found in other parts of the world with strong seasonal wetting and drying climate (e.g. Mediterranean), where they are called calcic and chromic luvisols.

35fd1ade295d.title: Luvisol
35fd1ade295d.sentence: In the USDA Soil Taxonomy, Luvisols are typically classified as Alfisols.

0d4e02c4105f.title: Luvisol
0d4e02c4105f.sentence: The Canadian system of soil classification includes Luvisols.

456958e52e7c.title: Technosol
456958e52e7c.sentence: A Technosol in the World Reference Base for Soil Resources is a Reference Soil Group that combines soils whose properties and pedogenesis are dominated by their technical origin.

c297da8aaae3.title: Technosol
c297da8aaae3.sentence: They contain either a significant amount of artefacts (something in the soil recognizably made or extracted from the earth by humans), some sort of geotechnical liner, or are sealed by technic hard material (hard material created by humans, having properties unlike natural rock).

cfd106f959bd.title: Technosol
cfd106f959bd.sentence: They include soils from wastes (landfills, sludge, cinders, mine spoils, and ashes), pavements with their underlying unconsolidated materials, soils with geomembranes, and constructed soils in human-made materials.

c64bb91a6393.title: Technosol
c64bb91a6393.sentence: Transported natural soil material does not qualify as Technosol and is described with the Transportic qualifier in WRB.

658b9a7b665b.title: Technosol
658b9a7b665b.sentence: Technosols are often referred to as urban or mine soils.

2d3359620867.title: Technosol
2d3359620867.sentence: Technosols are found throughout the world, e.g., at or near cities, roads, mines, refuse dumps, oil spills, and coal fly ash deposits.

e1d339e0e877.title: Technosol
e1d339e0e877.sentence: They occur primarily in urban and industrial areas, usually in small areas, and can be associated with other soil groups in a complex pattern.

e26fdc107b6f.title: Technosol
e26fdc107b6f.sentence: A Technosol could differentiate A and O horizons at rates of more than one centimeter per year.

a8278e8d5069.title: Technosol
a8278e8d5069.sentence: These soils are more likely to be contaminated than other soils.

4e89cb3525c8.title: Technosol
4e89cb3525c8.sentence: Many Technosols must be treated with care as they may contain toxic substances from industrial processes.

2e4c0f6b9075.title: Technosol
2e4c0f6b9075.sentence: As in the case of Andacollo in Chile some technosols are created on purpose to cover up wastes such as mine tailings.

71f7d9059e64.title: Technosol
71f7d9059e64.sentence: They are closely related to Anthrosols, soils created by long-term measures to enhance fertility for agricultural use, like the intensive addition of organic matter to soil, such as an old urban garden.

fc33805a0b86.title: Calcisol
fc33805a0b86.sentence: A Calcisol in the World Reference Base for Soil Resources (WRB) is a soil with a substantial secondary accumulation of lime.

802599e35b9f.title: Calcisol
802599e35b9f.sentence: Formerly Calcisols were internationally known as Desert soils and Takyrs.

23b713396ca5.title: Calcisol
23b713396ca5.sentence: They are found on level to hilly land in arid and semi-arid regions.

2c17c961435a.title: Calcisol
2c17c961435a.sentence: The natural vegetation is sparse and dominated by xerophytic shrubs and trees and/or ephemeral grasses.

2c38e9edf2c0.title: Calcisol
2c38e9edf2c0.sentence: Dryness, and in places also stoniness and/or the presence of a shallow petrocalcic horizon, limit the suitability of Calcisols for agriculture.

02f02dc2ef33.title: Calcisol
02f02dc2ef33.sentence: If irrigated, drained (to prevent salinisation) and fertilised, Calcisols can be highly productive under a wide variety of crops.

0192ccd252eb.title: Calcisol
0192ccd252eb.sentence: The total Calcisol area may well amount to some 10 million square kilometres, nearly all of it in the arid and semi-arid subtropics of both hemispheres.

530295d44de0.title: Regosol
530295d44de0.sentence: A Regosol in the World Reference Base for Soil Resources (WRB) is very weakly developed mineral soil in unconsolidated materials.

2f91cf7f699a.title: Regosol
2f91cf7f699a.sentence: The group of Regosols is a taxonomic rest group containing all soils that could not be accommodated in any of the other groups.

2c07f33358ee.title: Regosol
2c07f33358ee.sentence: Excluded from the Regosols are weakly developed soils that classify as Leptosols (very shallow soils), Arenosols (sandy soils) or Fluvisols (in recent alluvial deposits).

f68445cd21b6.title: Regosol
f68445cd21b6.sentence: Profile development is minimal as a consequence of young age and/or slow soil formation.

187c3879eaf7.title: Regosol
187c3879eaf7.sentence: Regosols are extensive in eroding lands, in particular in arid and semi-arid areas and in mountain regions.

a84035ffe8e0.title: Regosol
a84035ffe8e0.sentence: Regosols cover an estimated 260 million hectares worldwide, mainly in arid areas in the mid-western United States, Northern Africa, the Near East and Australia.

8a6a3f7a2fe7.title: Regosol
8a6a3f7a2fe7.sentence: Internationally, Regosols correlate with soil taxa that are marked by incipient soil formation such as Entisols in the USDA soil taxonomy or Rudosols and possibly some Tenosols in the Australian Soil Classification.

4ccdf8a2624b.title: Regosol
4ccdf8a2624b.sentence: Some Regosols are used for capital-intensive irrigated farming but the most common land use is low volume grazing.

ea7217a2168f.title: Regosol
ea7217a2168f.sentence: Regosols in mountain areas are best left under forest.

55de4f69ad0f.title: Alisol
55de4f69ad0f.sentence: An Alisol is a Reference Soil Group of the World Reference Base for Soil Resources (WRB).

6156f65796cc.title: Alisol
6156f65796cc.sentence: Alisols have an argic horizon, which has a high cation exchange capacity.

387bfa8faa3e.title: Alisol
387bfa8faa3e.sentence: In the subsoil, the base saturation is low.

6b0625c9a945.title: Alisol
6b0625c9a945.sentence: Compared to Lixisols, Acrisols and Ferralsols, Alisols have much higher-activity clays and are likely to be found on younger terrains or more geologically active regions such as Kyushu and Chugoku.

23712a7ef9f6.title: Alisol
23712a7ef9f6.sentence: Alisols occur in tropical and humid subtropical climates, but are also found in temperate regions.

772ce4ff5c43.title: Alisol
772ce4ff5c43.sentence: Alisols are acidic (increased by limited drainage) and therefore need liming, contain few nutrients and therefore need fertilizer, and do not have much surface coherence so are easily eroded.

5b7ffe267623.title: Andosol
5b7ffe267623.sentence: Andosols are soils found in volcanic areas formed in volcanic tephra.

31ddb81ec946.title: Andosol
31ddb81ec946.sentence: The name comes from Japanese an (暗 'dark') and do (土 'soil'), synonymous with kuroboku (黒ぼく).

3af383d13224.title: Andosol
3af383d13224.sentence: Andosols typically develop in parent materials containing high proportions of glass.

250c44859b42.title: Andosol
250c44859b42.sentence: If significant amounts of glasses are still present, they show vitric properties and receive the Vitric qualifier.

2c74df5bf042.title: Andosol
2c74df5bf042.sentence: With advanced weathering of the glasses, they show andic properties.

27e3d57ebcf1.title: Andosol
27e3d57ebcf1.sentence: In more acidic tephras in humid climates, complexes of organic matter with Al ions develop, and the Andosols are characterized by the Aluandic qualifier.

e4c65e0158dc.title: Andosol
e4c65e0158dc.sentence: In both cases, they contain many ferrihydrite and have a bulk density ≤ 0.9 kg/dm3.

1d791a639522.title: Andosol
1d791a639522.sentence: Andosols cover an estimated 1–2% of Earth's ice-free land surface.

85b9d064151d.title: Andosol
85b9d064151d.sentence: Most occur around the Pacific Ring of Fire, with the largest areas found in central Chile, Ecuador, Colombia, Mexico, the Pacific Northwest US, Japan, Java and New Zealand's North Island.

16e415f46689.title: Andosol
16e415f46689.sentence: Silandic Andosols are very fertile except in cases where phosphorus is easily fixed (as sometimes occurs in the tropics).

cb64d70e9770.title: Andosol
cb64d70e9770.sentence: They can usually support intensive cropping, with areas used for wet rice in Java supporting some of the densest populations in the world.

e55757a512d7.title: Andosol
e55757a512d7.sentence: In the USDA soil taxonomy (ST), many Andosols belong to the order of the Andisols.

fc80af8a50f6.title: Andosol
fc80af8a50f6.sentence: Fossil andosols are known from areas far from present-day volcanic activity and have in some cases been dated as far back as the Precambrian 1.5 billion years ago.

b014613fa495.title: Stagnosol
b014613fa495.sentence: A Stagnosol in the World Reference Base for Soil Resources (WRB) is soil with strong mottling of the soil profile due to redox processes caused by stagnating surface water.

a970cd28bb5e.title: Stagnosol
a970cd28bb5e.sentence: Stagnosols are periodically wet and mottled in the topsoil and subsoil, with or without concretions and/or bleaching.

0b4d1e53f909.title: Stagnosol
0b4d1e53f909.sentence: A common name in many national classification systems for most Stagnosols is pseudogley.

d8b7d4165a61.title: Stagnosol
d8b7d4165a61.sentence: Stagnosols occur on flat to gently sloping land in cool temperate to subtropical regions with humid to perhumid climate conditions.

223b6e76da9c.title: Stagnosol
223b6e76da9c.sentence: For the greater part in humid to perhumid temperate regions of West and Central Europe, North America, southeast Australia and Argentina.

bfcc2336bf62.title: Stagnosol
bfcc2336bf62.sentence: The agricultural suitability of Stagnosols is limited because of their oxygen deficiency resulting from stagnating water above a dense subsoil.

02b70173cebb.title: Stagnosol
02b70173cebb.sentence: However, in contrast to Gleysols, drainage with channels or pipes is in many cases insufficient.

3850c79436d7.title: Stagnosol
3850c79436d7.sentence: This may be achieved by deep loosening or deep ploughing.

361d7cddfc95.title: Stagnosol
361d7cddfc95.sentence: Drained Stagnosols can be fertile soils owing to their moderate degree of leaching.

cc04d7c882a5.title: Stagnosol
cc04d7c882a5.sentence: In the USDA soil taxonomy, many of them belong to the Aqualfs, Aquults, Aquents, Aquepts and Aquolls.

b34eea3b34b0.title: Planosol
b34eea3b34b0.sentence: A Planosol in the World Reference Base for Soil Resources is a soil with a light-coloured, coarse-textured, surface horizon that shows signs of periodic water stagnation and abruptly overlies a dense, slowly permeable subsoil with significantly more clay than the surface horizon.

3c0c6ed180c0.title: Planosol
3c0c6ed180c0.sentence: Geological stratification and/or a pedogenetic process of destruction and removal of clay has resulted in the relatively coarse-textured, light-coloured surface soil abruptly overlying finer textured subsoil; impeded downward percolation of water causes temporarily reducing conditions with a stagnic colour pattern, at least close to the abrupt textural change.

9ea746abd43e.title: Planosol
9ea746abd43e.sentence: In the US Soil Classification of 1938 used the name Planosols, whereas its successor, the USDA soil taxonomy, includes most Planosols in the Great Groups Albaqualfs, Albaquults and Argialbolls.

cb1a614072f9.title: Planosol
cb1a614072f9.sentence: Planosols cover an estimated 130 million hectares of the world.

760c82f84647.title: Planosol
760c82f84647.sentence: These soils are typically in seasonally waterlogged flat lands.

a0907b768362.title: Planosol
a0907b768362.sentence: Major areas with Planosols occur in subtropical and temperate regions with clear alternation of wet and dry seasons, as in South America (Uruguay, northeastern Argentina, Paraguay, eastern Bolivia, the Brazilian pampa, the Pantanal mato-grossense and northeastern Brazil), Africa (Sahelian zone, East and Southern Africa), the east of the United States of America, Southeast Asia (Bangladesh and Thailand), and Australia.

83b3754c1bde.title: Planosol
83b3754c1bde.sentence: Root development on natural unmodified Planosols is hindered severely by oxygen deficiency in wet periods, dense subsoil and, in places, by toxic levels of Al in the rootzone.

c6f801a21ae4.title: Planosol
c6f801a21ae4.sentence: Vast areas of Planosols are used for extensive grazing.

7ae36a328a89.title: Planosol
7ae36a328a89.sentence: Yields are modest even on drained and deeply loosened soils.

8997b274d1e0.title: Planosol
8997b274d1e0.sentence: Planosols in Southeast Asia are widely planted with paddy rice.

fee6ebeb79d3.title: Phaeozem
fee6ebeb79d3.sentence: Most Phaeozems correlate with the Udolls (Mollisols) of the USDA soil taxonomy.

d58c533c6b2e.title: Phaeozem
d58c533c6b2e.sentence: Phaeozems form from unconsolidated sediments such as loess and glacial till and typically have organic matter contents of about 5% and a pH of 5–7.

90a02d4f7c44.title: Phaeozem
90a02d4f7c44.sentence: These soils are found mainly in humid and sub-humid tall-grass steppes; there are extensive areas of them in the United States, Argentina and China.

bbd1d15e6507.title: Phaeozem
bbd1d15e6507.sentence: Intensive agricultural use is widespread and includes wheat, soybean and cotton production and improved pastures for cattle.

900760ccba61.title: Kastanozem
900760ccba61.sentence: Kastanozem (also known as "chestnut soil") is one of the 32 Reference Soil Groups of the World Reference Base for Soil Resources (WRB).

634e0a68dd41.title: Kastanozem
634e0a68dd41.sentence: They are rich in humus, and originally covered with early maturing native grasslands vegetation, which produces a characteristic brown surface layer in the first meter in depth.

ef4e81c9fdc2.title: Kastanozem
ef4e81c9fdc2.sentence: These soils are brighter than Chernozems, and are related to the Mollisols in the USDA soil taxonomy.

98df7e935e83.title: Kastanozem
98df7e935e83.sentence: They have a relative high level of exchangeable calcium ions and secondary carbonates starting within 70 cm of the mineral soil surface.

3cec50a50d65.title: Kastanozem
3cec50a50d65.sentence: Kastanozems are found in relatively dry zones with 200 to 450 mm of rainfall a year.

f029f56ce366.title: Kastanozem
f029f56ce366.sentence: The name has two origins: the Russian term 'каштановые почвы', 'каштанозем', where 'каштановые' is a shade of brown derived from the word "каштан" (kashtan), "chestnut" and refers to the color of its husk, and the Latin term castanea (chestnut).

78f00109a9d8.title: Lixisol
78f00109a9d8.sentence: Lixisols are a Reference Soil Group of the World Reference Base for Soil Resources (WRB).

dc33c8e9d134.title: Lixisol
dc33c8e9d134.sentence: They are soils with subsurface accumulation of low activity clays and high base saturation.

da0c2ce5af27.title: Lixisol
da0c2ce5af27.sentence: They develop under intensive tropical weathering conditions and subhumid to semi-arid climate.

9ce72f3972c4.title: Nitisol
9ce72f3972c4.sentence: Related FAO soil groups originating in tropical climates and also containing layers with clay accumulations are Acrisols and Lixisols.

73719c45bb51.title: Terra preta
73719c45bb51.section: Pedology > Organic matter and nutrients > Nutrients
73719c45bb51.sentence: In Amazonia, the provisioning of nutrients from the decomposition of naturally available organic matter fails as the heavy rainfalls wash away the released nutrients and the natural soils (ferralsols, acrisols, lixisols, arenosols, uxisols, etc.) lack the mineral matter to provide those nutrients.

cffbef160eef.title: Plaggen soil
cffbef160eef.sentence: Plaggen soil or plaggic anthrosol is a type of soil created in parts of northwest Europe in the Middle Ages, as a result of so-called "plaggen" agriculture on marginal podzol soils.

5853c5409d18.title: Plaggen soil
5853c5409d18.sentence: In order to fertilize the fields, pieces of heath or grass including roots and humus ("plaggen") were cut and used as bedding for cattle or sheep.

7b7c8091ab32.title: Plaggen soil
7b7c8091ab32.sentence: In springtime, this bedding, enriched with slurry was then spread over the fields near the village as manure.

b164a43a4504.title: Plaggen soil
b164a43a4504.sentence: The long term practice of this form of agriculture created a rich agricultural soil to a depth of between 40 cm and over 1.50 m, unlike modern arable soils, which tend to be just 30 centimetres deep.

1e590f6370bc.title: Plaggen soil
1e590f6370bc.sentence: The raised fields give rise to a typical landscape with sharp breaks in elevation and are called Plaggenesche in Germany or Es in Dutch.

d70503a005c0.title: Plaggen soil
d70503a005c0.sentence: This form of agriculture stopped around 1900 with the introduction of fertilizers.

bad66444657b.title: Plaggen soil
bad66444657b.sentence: In Orkney these soils were created already in the 12th to 13th centuries, and on some islands in Shetland these methods continued to be used until the 1960s.

ce4eb70f475d.title: Plaggen soil
ce4eb70f475d.sentence: The Maori of New Zealand's agriculture included plaggen soil forming practices that increased drainage for kumara crops.

20b9f6da4e7b.title: Nitisol
20b9f6da4e7b.sentence: Nitisol, in the World Reference Base for Soil Resources (WRB), is a deep, red, well-drained soil with a clay content of at least 30% and a polyhedral structure or a blocky structure, breaking into a polyhedral or a flat-edged structure.

05aad1895564.title: Nitisol
05aad1895564.sentence: Nitisols are technically defined by a significant accumulation of clay (30 percent or more by mass and extending as much as 150 cm [5 feet] below the surface) and by a blocky aggregate structure.

2baae0bd4a5b.title: Nitisol
2baae0bd4a5b.sentence: The soil aggregates show pressure faces.

a5d42fcd92b9.title: Nitisol
a5d42fcd92b9.sentence: Iron oxides and high-water content are believed to play important roles in creating the soil structure.

1a6c82c38e7f.title: Nitisol
1a6c82c38e7f.sentence: Nitisols form from fine-textured material weathered from intermediate to basic parent rock and kaolinite, halloysite and iron oxides dominate their clay mineralogy.

a3cc880b4e6d.title: Nitisol
a3cc880b4e6d.sentence: These soils are found in the tropics and subtropics; there are extensive areas of them in the tropical highlands of Ethiopia, Kenya, Democratic Republic of the Congo and Cameroon.

a9be977ae8ad.title: Umbrisol
a9be977ae8ad.sentence: In soil classification, an Umbrisol is a soil with a dark topsoil and in which organic matter has accumulated within the mineral surface soil—in most cases with low base saturation—to the extent that it significantly affects the behaviour and utilization of the soil.

5a480f0294e3.title: Umbrisol
5a480f0294e3.sentence: "Umbrisol" is a Reference Soil Group of the World Reference Base for Soil Resources (WRB).

487ab1c2fff4.title: Umbrisol
487ab1c2fff4.sentence: Umbrisols are the counterpart of comparable soils with a high base saturation (Chernozems, Kastanozems and Phaeozems).

c28d77749b4b.title: Umbrisol
c28d77749b4b.sentence: Umbrisols develop in weathering material of siliceous rock.

1ebe6a8b6d5b.title: Umbrisol
1ebe6a8b6d5b.sentence: Umbrisols occupy about 100,000,000 hectares (250,000,000 acres) throughout the world.

bffd653b4753.title: Umbrisol
bffd653b4753.sentence: Umbrisols occur above the actual tree line in the Andean, Himalayan and Central Asian mountain ranges; they are at lower altitudes in northern and western Europe where the former forest vegetation has been largely cleared, carry a vegetation of short grasses of low nutritional value.

c5a1710d2756.title: Umbrisol
c5a1710d2756.sentence: In Europe, Umbrisols occur along the northwest Atlantic seaboard, e.g. in Iceland, on the British Isles and in northwest Portugal and Spain.

5e788378ba28.title: Umbrisol
5e788378ba28.sentence: Umbrisols in North America are confined largely to the northwest Pacific seaboard.

f8210e93fe21.title: Umbrisol
f8210e93fe21.sentence: The predominance of sloping land and wet and cool climate conditions restricts utilization of many Umbrisols to extensive grazing.

e9da45666777.title: Umbrisol
e9da45666777.sentence: Management focuses on the introduction of improved grasses and correction of the soil pH by liming.

218499c58709.title: Umbrisol
218499c58709.sentence: Many Umbrisols are susceptible to erosion.

86cc6dc49a11.title: Umbrisol
86cc6dc49a11.sentence: In New Zealand, Umbrisols have been transformed into highly productive soils, used for intensive sheep and dairy farming, and production of cash crops.

15d2d93cd778.title: Umbrisol
15d2d93cd778.sentence: Many of such soils are classified in the USDA soil taxonomy as Great Groups of Entisols and Inceptisols, and as "Very dark-humus soils" in the Russian soil classification.

6b56a47316ce.title: Brown podzolic
6b56a47316ce.sentence: In the World Reference Base for Soil Resources, these soils are called Umbrisols, and the Soil Atlas of Europe shows a preponderance of this kind of soil in north-west Spain.

6fcec17a8630.title: Retisol
6fcec17a8630.sentence: A Retisol is a Reference Soil Group of the World Reference Base for Soil Resources (WRB).

81f211ad1006.title: Retisol
81f211ad1006.sentence: Retisols are characterized by clay migration and an additional specific feature: The clay-poorer and lighter coloured eluvial horizon intercalates netlike into the clay-richer more intensely coloured illuvial horizon.

f74432240163.title: Retisol
f74432240163.sentence: The illuvial horizon is the diagnostic argic horizon, and the intercalation is called retic properties (Latin: rete = net).

6738a730aec9.title: Retisol
6738a730aec9.sentence: Retisols were newly introduced with the third edition of the WRB in 2014.

d2f99a4a36a0.title: Retisol
d2f99a4a36a0.sentence: They include the narrower defined Albeluvisols of the first and second edition (1998 and 2006), which were abolished in 2014.

edec9aacaf58.title: Retisol
edec9aacaf58.sentence: The definition of the Retisols resembles the definition of the Podzoluvisols of the Legend (1974) and the Revised Legend (1988) of the FAO soil classification.

bdf55fb0854f.title: Retisol
bdf55fb0854f.sentence: Retisols occur mainly in periglacial areas of the last glaciation in Europe and North America.

cb21951e3c46.title: Retisol
cb21951e3c46.sentence: In Europe, they are found along a belt from Belgium through northern Germany, Poland and Belarus to Russia.

90f0f6baee31.title: Retisol
90f0f6baee31.sentence: Because the very specific retic properties are not so widespread, they normally do not cover larger areas.

21ece12b7899.title: Retisol
21ece12b7899.sentence: In the subsoil, the rainwater runs downwards predominantly in the clay-poorer parts, whereas the clay-richer and therefore also nutrient-richer parts are often insufficiently humid.

84e70a8592cc.title: Retisol
84e70a8592cc.sentence: The clay-richer parts are relatively dense and difficult to be rooted.

c94e1a085183.title: Retisol
c94e1a085183.sentence: These characteristics make the Retisols also unattractive for many soil animals, especially earthworms.

9f673420a9f7.title: Retisol
9f673420a9f7.sentence: Many are used as forest or pasture land.

78cf8050e11d.title: Black Dirt Region
78cf8050e11d.sentence: The Black Dirt Region is located in southern Orange County, New York and northern Sussex County, New Jersey.

c9bbb8f48c79.title: Black Dirt Region
c9bbb8f48c79.sentence: The Black Dirt Region takes its name from the dark, extremely fertile sapric soil left over from an ancient glacial lake bottom augmented by decades of past flooding of the Wallkill River.

7dcf5da0df1f.title: Black Dirt Region
7dcf5da0df1f.sentence: Farmers generally avoided the area in the early years of settlement because the soil, although rich, was frequently flooded and poorly drained.

c6898d44f845.title: Black Dirt Region
c6898d44f845.sentence: Instead, a drainage canal was constructed by General George D. Wickham through his property in 1835.

c5b5d4820599.title: Black Dirt Region
c5b5d4820599.sentence: Immigrants from Eastern Europe, particularly Poles and Volga Germans, had worked in similar soils in their native countries and began farming the former swampland.

c36ca8d12c7b.title: Black Dirt Region
c36ca8d12c7b.sentence: By the late 20th century, the region produced an average of 30,000 lb/acre of onion (3.4 kg/m2).

a0e6935730b2.title: Black Dirt Region
a0e6935730b2.sentence: Farmers in the region have been diversifying their crops to include lettuce, radish, potatoes, tomatoes, carrots, and, increasingly, sod, hemp, and cannabis.

e8cc5415f606.title: Black Dirt Region
e8cc5415f606.sentence: Development of the farmland is considered unlikely since the soil is inferior for building.

032c88dac9b1.title: Plinthosol
032c88dac9b1.sentence: Plinthosols are a reference soil group in the World Reference Base for Soil Resources (WRB), developed by the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO).

da288cec4af8.title: Plinthosol
da288cec4af8.sentence: A key diagnostic feature of these soils is the plinthic horizon, which begins within 50 cm of the soil surface, or 100 cm if it lies beneath an albic horizon or a horizon with stagnic properties.

34a63e054085.title: Plinthosol
34a63e054085.sentence: Plinthosols typically form in tropical environments with alternating wet and dry conditions, where fluctuating water tables promote the transformation of iron and clay minerals.

27386192e3ea.title: Plinthosol
27386192e3ea.sentence: Under saturated conditions, iron is reduced and becomes mobile in its ferrous form.

ec6f817682c4.title: Plinthosol
ec6f817682c4.sentence: Upon drying, it oxidizes and precipitates as ferric oxides and hydroxides.

feb6bb773077.title: Plinthosol
feb6bb773077.sentence: Over time, repeated wetting and drying cause these iron compounds to accumulate in mottled patterns, often appearing as platy, polygonal, or reticulate structures.

4024bde8a506.title: Plinthosol
4024bde8a506.sentence: Plinthite, a red, clay-rich material, hardens irreversibly into ironstone when exposed to repeated moisture cycles.

9198a3be1c20.title: Plinthosol
9198a3be1c20.sentence: Plinthite and petroplinthite are rich in hydrated iron and aluminium oxides, with iron oxide content occasionally exceeding 80%, though some units may contain about equal parts of each.

630eb9d475a1.title: Plinthosol
630eb9d475a1.sentence: Their natural fertility is low, and they are prone to waterlogging in bottomlands and drought in shallow or skeletal areas.

2b76006f8682.title: Plinthosol
2b76006f8682.sentence: In many regions outside the wet tropics, shallow petroplinthite restricts root growth, making the land unsuitable for conventional agriculture; such areas are often relegated to low-intensity grazing.

b0ac5979959f.title: Plinthosol
b0ac5979959f.sentence: Despite these constraints, some are still used for cultivating food and tree crops, such as cocoa in West Africa or cashew in India, though yields may be affected by seasonal drought.

a3b96ca036af.title: Plinthosol
a3b96ca036af.sentence: Soils containing plinthite are estimated to cover around 60 million hectares globally.

401536eb1680.title: Plinthosol
401536eb1680.sentence: Soft plinthite is most commonly found in humid tropical regions, particularly in the eastern Amazon Basin, the central Congo Basin, and parts of Southeast Asia.

65cc165e3b92.title: Plinthosol
65cc165e3b92.sentence: In drier tropical zones, such as the Sudano-Sahelian region, hardened plinthite (petroplinthite) forms extensive surface caps on exposed or elevated landforms.

75c703ed34ba.title: Gypsisol
75c703ed34ba.sentence: Gypsisols in the World Reference Base for Soil Resources (WRB) are soils with substantial secondary accumulation of gypsum (CaSO4.2H2O).

d3d5c57bdd2c.title: Gypsisol
d3d5c57bdd2c.sentence: They are found in the driest parts of the arid climate zone.

0fc351480756.title: Gypsisol
0fc351480756.sentence: Gypsisols are exclusive to arid regions; their worldwide extent is probably of the order of 100 million hectares.

9f96730a1c39.title: Gypsisol
9f96730a1c39.sentence: Major occurrences are in and around Mesopotamia in desert areas in the Middle East and adjacent central Asian republics, in the Libyan and Namib deserts, in southeast and central Australia and in the southwestern United States.

391bb944f654.title: Gypsisol
391bb944f654.sentence: In the USDA soil taxonomy they are classified as Gypsids (USDA Soil Taxonomy), in the Russian soil classification they are called Desert soils (USSR).

986ef63c702d.title: Gypsisol
986ef63c702d.sentence: Accumulation of calcium sulphate, with or without carbonates, is concentrated in and below the B horizon.

fedd080f7e2d.title: Gypsisol
fedd080f7e2d.sentence: Gypsisols are developed in mostly unconsolidated alluvial, colluvial and aeolian deposits of base-rich weathering material.

9b0fc306e0b3.title: Gypsisol
9b0fc306e0b3.sentence: Deep Gypsisols located close to water resources can be planted to a wide range of crops.

0839eadad8a9.title: Gypsisol
0839eadad8a9.sentence: Yields are severely depressed where a petrogypsic horizon occurs at shallow depth.

e6234fa0b4d0.title: Gypsisol
e6234fa0b4d0.sentence: Nutrient imbalance, stoniness, and uneven subsidence of the land surface upon dissolution of gypsum in percolating (irrigation) water are further limitations.

9acce60846b5.title: Gypsisol
9acce60846b5.sentence: Irrigation canals must be lined to prevent the canal walls from caving in.

31522a159c5f.title: Chernozem
31522a159c5f.sentence: As seen in the list above, the 19th and 20th-century discussions on the pedogenesis of chernozem originally stemmed from climatic conditions from the early Holocene to roughly 5500 BC.

eb39564f9305.title: Chernozem
eb39564f9305.sentence: - 1840: Sir Roderick Murchison (weathered from Jurassic marine shales)

e493304a9085.title: Chernozem
e493304a9085.sentence: However, no single paleoclimate reconstruction could accurately explain geochemical variations found in chernozems throughout central Europe.

2d77b2e7602b.title: Chernozem
2d77b2e7602b.sentence: Evidence of anthropic origins of stable pyrogenic carbon in chernozem led to improved formation theories.

9b6d2a14724b.title: Chernozem
9b6d2a14724b.sentence: - 1999: Michael W. I. Schmidt (neolithic biomass burning)

b9b106345426.title: Chernozem
b9b106345426.sentence: Vegetation burning could explain chernozem's high magnetic susceptibility, the highest of the major soil types.

8653fcf645ef.title: Chernozem
8653fcf645ef.sentence: Given the rarity of such natural phenomena in the modern day, magnetic susceptibility in chernozem likely relates to control of fire by early humans.

958a8d39f8ab.title: Chernozem
958a8d39f8ab.sentence: Given the symphony of pedogenic processes that contribute to the formation of dark earths, chernozem summarizes different types of black soils with the same appearance but different formation histories.

ffb6b1114900.title: Durisol
ffb6b1114900.sentence: A Durisol is a Reference Soil Group under the World Reference Base for Soil Resources (WRB) referring to free-draining soils in arid and semi-arid environments that contain grains cemented together by secondary silica (SiO2) in the upper metre of soil, occurring either as concretions (durinodes – duric horizon) or as a continuously cemented layer (duripan – hardpan (Australia) – dorbank (South Africa) – petroduric horizon).

6c105fa7a644.title: Durisol
6c105fa7a644.sentence: The name is derived from Latin durus for hard.

27afe5bab42b.title: Durisol
27afe5bab42b.sentence: They are found on level and slightly sloping alluvial plains, terraces and gently sloping piedmont plains in arid, semi-arid and Mediterranean regions.

08e0a9f10e45.title: Durisol
08e0a9f10e45.sentence: Eroded Durisols with exposed hard horizons (a petroduric horizon) are common in (gently) sloping terrain.

21b12f597f9c.title: Durisol
21b12f597f9c.sentence: Most Durisols can only be used for extensive grazing.

c5124ee43c51.title: Durisol
c5124ee43c51.sentence: Arable cropping of Durisols is limited to areas where irrigation water is available.

8429dec6461f.title: Durisol
8429dec6461f.sentence: Extensive areas of Durisols occur in Australia, in South Africa, Namibia and in the United States (notably in Nevada, California and Arizona); minor occurrences have been reported from Central and South America and from Kuwait.

615a587aeb5c.title: Durisol
615a587aeb5c.sentence: Durisols are a new introduction in international soil classification and have not often been mapped as such.

deda6263fe67.title: Durisol
deda6263fe67.sentence: A precise indication of their extent is not (yet) available.

a90da0ab3981.title: Retisol
a90da0ab3981.section: Relationships with other Reference Soil Groups
a90da0ab3981.sentence: The WRB defines five Reference soil Groups with a compulsory argic horizon.

707d3e6765ef.title: Retisol
707d3e6765ef.section: Relationships with other Reference Soil Groups
707d3e6765ef.sentence: Only the Retisols have retic properties.

de38418d582f.title: Retisol
de38418d582f.section: Relationships with other Reference Soil Groups
de38418d582f.sentence: The other four are differentiated according to the cation exchange capacity per kg clay at pH 7 (CEC / kg clay) in the argic horizon and according to the base saturation calculated per sum of exchangeable cations (BSeff) in the subsoil.

299c3ade28d4.title: Retisol
299c3ade28d4.section: Relationships with other Reference Soil Groups
299c3ade28d4.sentence: Soils with an argic horizon and retic properties that are dominated by stagnant water are classified as Retic Stagnosols.

2a79dd3e85f1.title: Albeluvisols
2a79dd3e85f1.sentence: Albeluvisol was a Reference Soil Group of the first edition (1998) and the second edition (2006) of the World Reference Base for Soil Resources (WRB).

3a6518b02c66.title: Albeluvisols
3a6518b02c66.sentence: In the third edition of the WRB (2014), Albeluvisols were replaced by the broader defined Retisols.

336a9b31178f.title: Albeluvisols
336a9b31178f.sentence: Albeluvisols correlate with Glossaqualfs, Glossocryalfs and Glossudalfs in the USDA soil taxonomy.

732cb5c5a50b.title: Albeluvisols
732cb5c5a50b.sentence: These soils are formed mostly in unconsolidated glacial till, lacustrine or fluvial materials or aeolian deposits such as loess.

0cd907e92944.title: Albeluvisols
0cd907e92944.sentence: They occur on flat to undulating plains under coniferous forest or mixed forest in boreal and temperate climates with cold winters and short cool summers.

67f07870e7d5.title: Albeluvisols
67f07870e7d5.sentence: Albeluvisols cover an estimated 320 million ha in Europe, North Asia, Central Asia and in North America.

4e5bf98bd775.title: Albeluvisols
4e5bf98bd775.sentence: - the continental regions that had permafrost in the Pleistocene of northeast Europe, northwest Asia and southern Canada, which constitute by far the largest areas of Albeluvisols;

229bf06f36b9.title: Albeluvisols
229bf06f36b9.sentence: The agricultural suitability of Albeluvisols is limited because of their acidity, low nutrient levels, tillage and drainage problems.

f1a080ece9e5.title: Albeluvisols
f1a080ece9e5.sentence: The Albeluvisols of the northern taiga zone are almost exclusively under forest with small areas used for pasture or hay fields.

176f2c458802.title: Peat
176f2c458802.sentence: Peat is an accumulation of partially decayed vegetation or organic matter.

f6898f6a82c7.title: Peat
f6898f6a82c7.sentence: It is unique to natural areas called peatlands, bogs, mires, moors, or muskegs.

a5648f018b01.title: Peat
a5648f018b01.sentence: Sphagnum moss, also called peat moss, is one of the most common components in peat, although many other plants can contribute.

79c265ada41a.title: Peat
79c265ada41a.sentence: Peat forms in wetland conditions, where flooding or stagnant water obstructs the flow of oxygen from the atmosphere, slowing the rate of decomposition.

3c4a450b02b9.title: Peat
3c4a450b02b9.sentence: Soils consisting primarily of peat are known as histosols.

eec6d2929947.title: Peat
eec6d2929947.sentence: By volume, there are about 4 trillion cubic metres of peat in the world.

381e61c46689.title: Peat
381e61c46689.sentence: Globally, peat stores up to 550 Gt of carbon, 42% of all soil carbon, which exceeds the carbon stored in all other vegetation types, including the world's forests, although it covers just 3% of the land's surface.

28d978abab6c.title: Peat
28d978abab6c.sentence: Peat is in principle a renewable source of energy.

855814edc976.title: Peat
855814edc976.sentence: However, its extraction rate in industrialized countries far exceeds its slow regrowth rate of 1 mm (0.04 in) per year, and it is also reported that peat regrowth takes place only in 30–40% of peatlands.

fc69042032bb.title: Peat
fc69042032bb.sentence: Over time, the formation of peat is often the first step in the geological formation of fossil fuels such as coal, particularly low-grade coal such as lignite.

a3fe2ac2d265.title: Peat
a3fe2ac2d265.sentence: Under certain conditions, peat will turn into lignite coal over geologic periods of time.

55a3e1ef26b9.title: Peat
55a3e1ef26b9.sentence: Centuries of burning and draining of peat by humans has released a significant amount of CO2 into the atmosphere, contributing to anthropogenic climate change.

2f2574001dad.title: Peat
2f2574001dad.sentence: Engineers may describe a soil as peat which has a relatively high percentage of organic material.

3a64a6224b71.title: Peat
3a64a6224b71.section: Environmental and ecological issues > Peat drainage
3a64a6224b71.sentence: Large areas of organic wetland (peat) soils are currently drained for agriculture, forestry and peat extraction (i.e. through canals).

0a340b69335c.title: Peat
0a340b69335c.section: Environmental and ecological issues > Peat drainage
0a340b69335c.sentence: As a result of peat drainage, the organic carbon—which built over thousands of years and is normally underwater—is suddenly exposed to the air.

cee5505e25fb.title: Peat
cee5505e25fb.section: Environmental and ecological issues > Peat drainage
cee5505e25fb.sentence: It decomposes and turns into carbon dioxide (CO2), which is released into the atmosphere.

e0b4e422de7a.title: Peat
e0b4e422de7a.section: Environmental and ecological issues > Peat drainage
e0b4e422de7a.sentence: Globally about 12% of current peatlands have been drained and damaged.

b40b0bc3ba21.title: Peat
b40b0bc3ba21.section: Environmental and ecological issues > Peat drainage
b40b0bc3ba21.sentence: As of 2022 they are estimated to emit 4% of human made greenhouse gases, not including fires.

8122b818f2b4.title: Peat
8122b818f2b4.section: Environmental and ecological issues > Peat drainage
8122b818f2b4.sentence: This not only destroys the habitat of many species but also heavily fuels climate change.

400a0db8589a.title: Peat
400a0db8589a.section: Characteristics and uses by nation > Netherlands
400a0db8589a.sentence: Two-and-a-half thousand years ago, the area now named the Netherlands was largely covered with peat.

3511d6e00cd4.title: Peat
3511d6e00cd4.section: Characteristics and uses by nation > Netherlands
3511d6e00cd4.sentence: Drainage, causing compaction and oxidation and excavation have reduced peatlands (>40 cm [16 in] peat) to about 2,733 km2 (1,055 sq mi) or 10% of the land area, mostly used as meadows.

630b7e89e794.title: Peat
630b7e89e794.section: Characteristics and uses by nation > United Kingdom > England
630b7e89e794.sentence: Peatlands in England store 584m tonnes of carbon in total but emit around 11 million tonnes of CO2 every year due to degradation and draining.

c810eefeae8f.title: Peat
c810eefeae8f.section: Environmental and ecological issues > Peat fires
c810eefeae8f.sentence: Peat can be a major fire hazard and is not extinguished by light rain.

220407eeaa10.title: Peat
220407eeaa10.section: Environmental and ecological issues > Peat fires
220407eeaa10.sentence: Peat fires may burn for great lengths of time, or smoulder underground and reignite after winter if an oxygen source is present.

01a261d063a6.title: Peat
01a261d063a6.section: Environmental and ecological issues > Peat fires
01a261d063a6.sentence: Peat has a high carbon content and can burn under low moisture conditions.

cdb147dc7836.title: Peat
cdb147dc7836.section: Environmental and ecological issues > Peat fires
cdb147dc7836.sentence: Once ignited by the presence of a heat source (e.g., a wildfire penetrating the subsurface), it smoulders.

e801bc827e8f.title: Peat
e801bc827e8f.section: Environmental and ecological issues > Peat fires
e801bc827e8f.sentence: These smouldering fires can burn undetected for very long periods of time (months, years, and even centuries ) propagating in a creeping fashion through the underground peat layer.

9921b5e2cf5f.title: Peat
9921b5e2cf5f.section: Environmental and ecological issues > Peat fires
9921b5e2cf5f.sentence: Despite the damage that the burning of raw peat can cause, bogs are naturally subject to wildfires and depend on the wildfires to keep woody competition from lowering the water table and shading out many bog plants.

79edf64a4c65.title: Peat
79edf64a4c65.section: Environmental and ecological issues > Peat fires
79edf64a4c65.sentence: It is estimated that in 1997, peat and forest fires in Indonesia released between 0.81 and 2.57 gigatonnes (0.89 and 2.83 billion short tons; 0.80 and 2.53 billion long tons) of carbon; equivalent to 13–40 percent of the amount released by global fossil fuel burning, and greater than the carbon uptake of the world's biosphere.

89db4581b580.title: Peat
89db4581b580.section: Environmental and ecological issues > Peat fires
89db4581b580.sentence: In the summer of 2010, an unusually high heat wave of up to 40 °C (104 °F) ignited large deposits of peat in Central Russia, burning thousands of houses and covering the capital of Moscow with a toxic smoke blanket.

111e932c8b2a.title: Peat
111e932c8b2a.section: Environmental and ecological issues > Peat fires
111e932c8b2a.sentence: In June 2019, despite some forest fire prevention methods being put in place, peat fires in the Arctic emitted 50 megatonnes (55 million short tons; 49 million long tons) of CO2, which is equal to Sweden's total annual emissions.

02ff3464db22.title: Peat
02ff3464db22.section: Environmental and ecological issues > Peat fires
02ff3464db22.sentence: The peat fires are linked to climate change, as they are much more likely to occur nowadays due to this effect.

95cd9e4db0a6.title: Peat
95cd9e4db0a6.sentence: Peat forms when plant material does not fully decay in acidic and anaerobic conditions.

72c2548343e6.title: Peat
72c2548343e6.sentence: It is composed mainly of wetland vegetation: principally bog plants including mosses, sedges and shrubs.

1b4d7924b00a.title: Peat
1b4d7924b00a.sentence: As it accumulates, the peat holds water.

ad95822cea0c.title: Peat
ad95822cea0c.sentence: This slowly creates wetter conditions that allow the area of wetland to expand.

38c2b63fffe5.title: Peat
38c2b63fffe5.sentence: The biological features of sphagnum mosses act to create a habitat aiding peat formation, a phenomenon termed 'habitat manipulation'.

a16e56daec07.title: Peat
a16e56daec07.sentence: For example, sphagnum mosses actively secrete tannins, which preserve organic material.

ecb63b2d20a6.title: Peat
ecb63b2d20a6.sentence: Sphagnum also have special water-retaining cells, known as hyaline cells, which can release water ensuring the bogland remains constantly wet which helps promote peat production.

e28357bce113.title: Peat
e28357bce113.sentence: Most modern peat bogs formed 12,000 years ago in high latitudes after the glaciers retreated at the end of the last ice age.

13f1a67b53cc.title: Peat
13f1a67b53cc.sentence: Peat usually accumulates slowly at the rate of about a millimetre per year.

1610bc17b223.title: Peat
1610bc17b223.sentence: In natural peatlands, the "annual rate of biomass production is greater than the rate of decomposition", but it takes "thousands of years for peatlands to develop the deposits of 1.5 to 2.3 m [4.9 to 7.5 ft], which is the average depth of the boreal [northern] peatlands", which store around 415 gigatonnes (Gt) of carbon (about 46 times 2019 global CO2 emissions).

2d149e0d1adf.title: Peat
2d149e0d1adf.sentence: The estimated carbon content is 415 gigatonnes (457 billion short tons) (northern peatlands), 50 Gt (55 billion short tons) (tropical peatlands) and 15 Gt (17 billion short tons) (South America).

eff2bdcc2973.title: Serpentine soil
eff2bdcc2973.sentence: Serpentine soil is an uncommon soil type produced by weathered ultramafic rock such as peridotite and its metamorphic derivatives such as serpentinite.

dce7e3bfa98b.title: Serpentine soil
dce7e3bfa98b.sentence: More precisely, serpentine soil contains minerals of the serpentine subgroup, especially antigorite, lizardite, and chrysotile or white asbestos, all of which are commonly found in ultramafic rocks.

00592d5e756b.title: Serpentine soil
00592d5e756b.sentence: Ultramafic rocks are igneous or metamorphic rocks that contain more than 70% iron or magnesium minerals.

c9b1cbd7d1f9.title: Serpentine soil
c9b1cbd7d1f9.sentence: Geologically, areas with serpentine bedrock are characteristically steep, rocky, and vulnerable to erosion, which causes many serpentine soils to be rather shallow.

8facb2956de6.title: Serpentine soil
8facb2956de6.sentence: The shallow soils and sparse vegetation lead to elevated soil temperatures and dry conditions.

ea70635a29cb.title: Serpentine soil
ea70635a29cb.sentence: The soil is often reddish, brown, or gray in color due to its high iron and low organic content.

28abd6a2aee3.title: Serpentine soil
28abd6a2aee3.sentence: Due to their ultramafic origin, serpentine soils also have a low calcium-to-magnesium ratio and have low levels of many essential nutrients such as nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), and potassium (K).

e64d32dea1a4.title: Serpentine soil
e64d32dea1a4.sentence: Serpentine soils contain high concentrations of heavy metals, including chromium, iron, cobalt, and nickel.

a46435f14bb4.title: Serpentine soil
a46435f14bb4.sentence: Serpentine soils exhibit distinct chemical and physical properties and are generally regarded as poor soils for agriculture.

df397ed7b2f1.title: Serpentine soil
df397ed7b2f1.sentence: Serpentinite is a meta-igneous rock formed by the metamorphic reaction of olivine-rich rock, peridotite, with water.

08df62be721c.title: Serpentine soil
08df62be721c.sentence: Serpentinite most often forms in oceanic crust near the surface of the earth, particularly where water circulates in cooling rock near mid-ocean ridges: masses of the resulting ultramafic rock are found in ophiolites incorporated in continental crust near present and past tectonic plate boundaries.

1c1f305bd108.title: Serpentine soil
1c1f305bd108.sentence: The rock often contains white streaks of chrysotile running through it, which are a type of naturally occurring asbestos.

a265bef703e1.title: Serpentine soil
a265bef703e1.sentence: Asbestos is linked to an array of human health conditions such as mesothelioma from long-time exposure of breathing in the dust particles.

1daf7527fc2d.title: Serpentine soil
1daf7527fc2d.sentence: Serpentine soils are widely distributed on Earth, in part mirroring the distribution of ophiolites.

609d17d79adb.title: Serpentine soil
609d17d79adb.sentence: There are outcroppings of serpentine soils in the Balkan Peninsula, Turkey, Newfoundland, the island of Cyprus, the Alps, Cuba, and New Caledonia.

7b04427fdc65.title: Serpentine soil
7b04427fdc65.sentence: In North America, the majority of the serpentine soils are in California; however, serpentine is also present in small but widely distributed areas on the eastern slope of the Appalachian Mountains in the eastern United States.

bc0b8aaa9e00.title: Serpentine soil
bc0b8aaa9e00.sentence: Serpentine soils can be amended to support crops and pasture land for cattle grazing.

82704e3f80ad.title: Serpentine soil
82704e3f80ad.sentence: This can be done by adding soluble calcium carriers such as gypsum to the soil.

dcd894475b57.title: Serpentine soil
dcd894475b57.sentence: By adding gypsum or other calcium compounds a more favourable calcium-to-magnesium ratio can be developed, creating a better balance of plant nutrients.

392ec98d8345.title: Serpentine soil
392ec98d8345.sentence: The unique plants that survive in serpentine soils have been used in the process of phytoremediation, a type of bioremediation.

6aaa1c37ec3a.title: Serpentine soil
6aaa1c37ec3a.sentence: Since these plants developed specialized adaptations to high concentrations of heavy metals, they have been used to remove heavy metals from polluted soil.

5051fa4e1741.title: Charcoal
5051fa4e1741.sentence: Charcoal is a lightweight black residue made of carbon that is produced by strongly heating wood (or other animal and plant materials) in minimal oxygen to remove all water and volatile constituents.

6f94a58bd4fb.title: Charcoal
6f94a58bd4fb.sentence: In the traditional version of this pyrolysis process, called charcoal burning, often by forming a charcoal kiln, the heat is supplied by burning part of the starting material itself, with a limited supply of oxygen.

9c9c60e141b6.title: Charcoal
9c9c60e141b6.sentence: The process typically involves stacking wood billets to form a conical pile, allowing air to enter through openings at the bottom, and igniting the pile gradually.

3dfc5b796419.title: Charcoal
3dfc5b796419.sentence: Modern methods of charcoal production involve carbonizing wood in retorts, yielding higher efficiencies compared to traditional kilning methods.

fac227ffc096.title: Charcoal
fac227ffc096.sentence: Although American gardeners have used charcoal for a short time, research on terra preta soils in Amazonia has discovered the widespread use of biochar by pre-Columbian natives to ameliorate unproductive soil into soil rich in carbon.

eda21ad00ecd.title: Charcoal
eda21ad00ecd.sentence: The technique may find modern application, both to improve soils and as a means of carbon sequestration.

987545efe32d.title: Biochar
987545efe32d.sentence: Biochar is a form of charcoal, sometimes modified, that is intended for organic use, as in soil.

f9ab0aa3832e.title: Charcoal
f9ab0aa3832e.sentence: Throughout history, the extensive production of charcoal has been a significant contributor to deforestation, particularly in regions like Central Europe.

2a371e76c7e1.title: Terra preta
2a371e76c7e1.sentence: Terra preta (Portuguese pronunciation: [ˈtɛʁɐ ˈpɾetɐ], literally "black earth" in Portuguese), also known as Amazonian dark earth or Indian black earth, is a type of very dark, fertile anthropogenic soil (anthrosol) found in the Amazon Basin.

9be32daa06c9.title: Terra preta
9be32daa06c9.sentence: Terra preta owes its characteristic black color to its weathered charcoal content, and was made by adding a mixture of charcoal, bones, broken pottery, compost and manure to the low fertility Amazonian soil.

433a24ab3c9f.title: Terra preta
433a24ab3c9f.sentence: A product of indigenous Amazonian soil management and slash-and-char agriculture, the charcoal is stable and remains in the soil for thousands of years, binding and retaining minerals and nutrients.

189c1a262cf7.title: Terra preta
189c1a262cf7.sentence: Terra preta is less prone to nutrient leaching because of its high concentration of charcoal, microbial life and organic matter.

0162172b99c6.title: Terra preta
0162172b99c6.sentence: Terra preta soils were created by the pre-Columbian farming communities between 450 BCE and 950 CE.

fd5367c347c3.title: Terra preta
fd5367c347c3.sentence: Soil depths can reach 2 meters (6.6 ft).

b0a71b38c857.title: Terra preta
b0a71b38c857.sentence: It is reported to regenerate itself at the rate of 1 centimeter (0.4 in) per year.

681a4ad0513e.title: Terra preta
681a4ad0513e.sentence: Deforested arable soils in the Amazon are productive for a short period of time before their nutrients are consumed or leached away by rain or flooding.

9af0f4c7a0cb.title: Terra preta
9af0f4c7a0cb.sentence: In the international soil classification system World Reference Base for Soil Resources (WRB) Terra preta is called Pretic Anthrosol.

1359be20e1b1.title: Terra preta
1359be20e1b1.sentence: The most common original soil before transformed into a terra preta is the Ferralsol.

4b1e575e0526.title: Terra preta
4b1e575e0526.sentence: Terra preta has a carbon content ranging from high to very high (more than 13–14% organic matter) in its A horizon, but without hydromorphic characteristics.

451a2cbee759.title: Terra preta
451a2cbee759.sentence: Terra preta soils are found mainly in the Brazilian Amazon, where Sombroek et al. estimate that they cover at least 0.1–0.3%, or 6,300 to 18,900 square kilometres (2,400 to 7,300 sq mi) of low forested Amazonia; but others estimate this surface at 10.0% or more (twice the area of Great Britain).

3ca1bd083e78.title: Terra preta
3ca1bd083e78.sentence: Terra preta exists in small plots averaging 20 hectares (49 acres), but areas of almost 360 hectares (890 acres) have also been reported.

2a94f7b0e17f.title: Terra preta
2a94f7b0e17f.section: Pedology > Organic matter and nutrients > Organic matter
2a94f7b0e17f.sentence: Terra preta's high concentration of charcoal supports a high concentration of organic matter (on average three times more than in the surrounding poor soils), up to 150 g/kg.

b327ef52e49a.title: Terra preta
b327ef52e49a.section: Pedology > Organic matter and nutrients > Nutrients
b327ef52e49a.sentence: The proportion of P reaches 200–400 mg/kg.

d739e6fdaeeb.title: Terra preta
d739e6fdaeeb.sentence: Terra mulata ("mulatto earth") is lighter or brownish in color.

c8b5136862ed.title: Terra preta
c8b5136862ed.sentence: Farmed areas around living areas are referred to as terra mulata.

3a56e8f7e337.title: Terra preta
3a56e8f7e337.sentence: Terra mulata soils are more fertile than surrounding soils but less fertile than terra preta, and were most likely intentionally improved using charcoal.

37011514b198.title: Terra preta
37011514b198.sentence: This type of soil appeared between 450 BCE and 950 CE at sites throughout the Amazon Basin.

dc5c2748d523.title: Brown earth
dc5c2748d523.sentence: Brown earth or brown soil is a type of soil.

bfeae8acf7f0.title: Brown earth
bfeae8acf7f0.sentence: They are well-drained fertile soils with a pH of between 5.0 and 6.5.

0ea24ca4171c.title: Brown earth
0ea24ca4171c.sentence: They are normally located in regions with a humid temperate climate.

5cb574a58877.title: Brown earth
5cb574a58877.sentence: Brown earths are mostly located between 35° and 55° north of the Equator.

46c6e5613849.title: Brown earth
46c6e5613849.sentence: The largest expanses cover western and central Europe, large areas of western and trans-Uralian Russia [ru], the east coast of America and eastern Asia.

f0969d54244e.title: Brown earth
f0969d54244e.sentence: Brown earths cover 45% of the land in England and Wales.

dbf7dc8d8656.title: Brown earth
dbf7dc8d8656.sentence: Rainfall totals are moderate, usually below 76 cm per year, and temperatures range from 4 °C in the winter to 18 °C in the summer.

e46709aee161.title: Brown earth
e46709aee161.sentence: Horizon A is usually a brownish colour, and over 20 cm in depth.

b56f224d3198.title: Brown earth
b56f224d3198.sentence: It is composed of mull humus (well decomposed alkaline organic matter) and mineral matter.

a48f90bfe0be.title: Brown earth
a48f90bfe0be.sentence: It is biologically active with many soil organisms and plant roots mixing the mull humus with mineral particles.

00cc7790ddec.title: Brown earth
00cc7790ddec.sentence: As a result, the boundary between the A and B horizons can be ill-defined in unploughed examples.

14de0b807596.title: Brown earth
14de0b807596.sentence: Horizon B is mostly composed of mineral matter which has been weathered from the parent material, but it often contains inclusions of more organic material carried in by organisms, especially earthworms.

f6a358b1989b.title: Brown earth
f6a358b1989b.sentence: It is lighter in colour than the A horizon, and is often weakly illuviated (enriched with material from overlying horizons).

307e6eaedbc4.title: Brown earth
307e6eaedbc4.sentence: Due to limited leaching only the more soluble bases are moved down through the profile.

2a1e4d5adeec.title: Brown earth
2a1e4d5adeec.sentence: The rich colour is the result of iron compounds, mainly complex oxides which, like rust, have a reddish-brown colour.

439f40daec4b.title: Brown earth
439f40daec4b.sentence: The B horizon lacks the grey colours and mottles characteristic of gley soils.

5fb35be4bd1c.title: Brown earth
5fb35be4bd1c.sentence: Brown earths are important, because they are permeable and usually easy to work throughout the year, so they are valued for agriculture.

ad9df9189439.title: Brown earth
ad9df9189439.sentence: Due to the reasonable natural fertility of brown earths, large tracts of deciduous woodland have been cut down and the land is now used for farming.

74de92e3d533.title: Brown earth
74de92e3d533.sentence: Brown earths are also classified in the German and Austrian soil taxonomy as "Braunerde." Braunerden are widespread and frequently occur on unconsolidated parent sand or loess parent materials.

29fe533de73d.title: Brown earth
29fe533de73d.sentence: Further east in Europe, in more continental climates, the soils show greater leaching of clay and other minerals, and are mapped as luvisols in the WRB.

9bd4660b4354.title: Brown earth
9bd4660b4354.sentence: These are rather similar to brown earths, and some other classifications, including the British and French, call these soils argillic brown earths (sol brun lessive), because they have an argillic, i.e. clay-enriched horizon at some depth well below the A horizon.

25915e74bc2a.title: Peat
25915e74bc2a.sentence: > In a peat profile there is a fossilized record of changes over time in the vegetation, pollen, spores, animals (from microscopic to the giant elk), and archaeological remains that have been deposited in place, as well as pollen, spores and particles brought in by wind and weather.

b59995db6c03.title: Peat
b59995db6c03.sentence: These remains are collectively termed the peat archives.

a23d0bb97c2a.title: Peat
a23d0bb97c2a.sentence: Because organic matter accumulates over thousands of years, peat deposits provide records of past vegetation and climate by preserving plant remains, such as pollen.

03eadbfdb6bc.title: Peat
03eadbfdb6bc.sentence: This allows the reconstruction of past environments and the study of land-use changes.

850c5e036a26.title: Peat
850c5e036a26.sentence: Authors Rydin and Jeglum in Biology of Habitats described the concept of peat archives, a phrase coined by influential peatland scientist Harry Godwin in 1981.

f5b9b25b0b3c.title: Peat
f5b9b25b0b3c.sentence: Scientists continue to compare modern mercury (Hg) accumulation rates in bogs with historical natural archives records in peat bogs and lake sediments to estimate the potential human impacts on the biogeochemical cycle of mercury, for example.

546727a65b58.title: Peat
546727a65b58.sentence: Over the years, different dating models and technologies for measuring date sediments and peat profiles accumulated over the last 100–150 years, have been used, including the widely used vertical distribution of 210Pb, the inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-SMS), and more recently the initial penetration (IP).

313d1fb424c9.title: Peat
313d1fb424c9.section: General uses > Peat archives > Bog bodies
313d1fb424c9.sentence: They are almost perfectly preserved by the tanning properties of the acidic water, as well as by the antibiotic properties of the organic component sphagnan.

a93e2110a992.title: Peat
a93e2110a992.section: General uses > Peat archives > Bog bodies
a93e2110a992.sentence: A famous example is the Tollund Man in Denmark.

5675d4a4e6d9.title: Peat
5675d4a4e6d9.section: General uses > Peat archives > Bog bodies
5675d4a4e6d9.sentence: Having been discovered in 1950 after being mistaken for a recent murder victim, he was exhumed for scientific purposes and dated to have lived during the 4th century BC.

c8433cd79b55.title: Peat
c8433cd79b55.sentence: Peat can be used as fuel once dried.

86ada5c4d06d.title: Peat
86ada5c4d06d.sentence: Traditionally, peat is cut by hand and left to dry in the sun.

947db2e30980.title: Peat
947db2e30980.sentence: In many countries, including Ireland and Scotland, peat was traditionally stacked to dry in rural areas and used for cooking and domestic heating.

1648b3154409.title: Peat
1648b3154409.sentence: This tradition can be traced back to the Roman period.

b8d784e667dd.title: Peat
b8d784e667dd.section: Characteristics and uses by nation > Ireland
b8d784e667dd.sentence: In Ireland, a state-owned company called Bord na Móna was responsible for managing peat extraction.

3f3176a6fe6b.title: Peat
3f3176a6fe6b.section: Characteristics and uses by nation > Ireland
3f3176a6fe6b.sentence: It processed the extracted peat into milled peat used in power stations and sold processed peat fuel in the form of peat briquettes, which is used for domestic heating.

196ae728c34a.title: Peat
196ae728c34a.section: Characteristics and uses by nation > Russia
196ae728c34a.sentence: In 1929, over 40% of the Soviet Union's electric energy came from peat, which dropped to 1% by 1980.

aaa680c6090c.title: Peat
aaa680c6090c.section: Characteristics and uses by nation > United Kingdom > Scotland
aaa680c6090c.sentence: Some Scotch whisky distilleries, such as those on Islay, use peat fires to dry malted barley.

1ddf0870d9b7.title: Peat
1ddf0870d9b7.section: Environmental and ecological issues > Erosion: peat hags
1ddf0870d9b7.sentence: Peat "hags" are a form of erosion which occurs at the sides of gullies that cut into the peat; they sometimes also occur in isolation.

e98deff7fb15.title: Peat
e98deff7fb15.section: Environmental and ecological issues > Erosion: peat hags
e98deff7fb15.sentence: The result is overhanging vegetation and peat.

3a351f592e2f.title: Peat
3a351f592e2f.section: Environmental and ecological issues > Erosion: peat hags
3a351f592e2f.sentence: Hags may result when flowing water cuts downwards into the peat and when fire or overgrazing exposes the peat surface.

96c79ca4237b.title: Peat
96c79ca4237b.section: Environmental and ecological issues > Erosion: peat hags
96c79ca4237b.sentence: Once the peat is exposed in these ways, it is prone to further erosion by wind, water and livestock.

af486a89a928.title: Peat
af486a89a928.section: Environmental and ecological issues > Erosion: peat hags
af486a89a928.sentence: Hags are too steep and unstable for vegetation to establish itself, so they continue to erode unless restorative action is taken.

926a0d44fb41.title: Peat
926a0d44fb41.sentence: Peat is used by gardeners and for horticulture in certain parts of the world, but this is being banned in some places.

f7a71090e3ae.title: Peat
f7a71090e3ae.sentence: While bark or coir-based peat-free potting soil mixes are on the rise, particularly in the UK, peat is still used as raw material for horticulture in some other European countries, Canada, as well as parts of the United States.

4f287da70173.title: Peat
4f287da70173.sentence: Peat has been discouraged as a soil additive by the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew, England, since 2003.

248773cfa49d.title: Peat
248773cfa49d.section: Environmental and ecological issues > Reduced usage
248773cfa49d.sentence: Peat-free options and policies have been adopted in various countries, for example the UK's Royal Horticultural Society promotes peat-free gardening.

67ed94b8744b.title: Peat
67ed94b8744b.section: Characteristics and uses by nation > United Kingdom
67ed94b8744b.sentence: In 1999, the UK government set a target for the country's horticulture industry to become 90% peat-free by 2010.

8f8ce6f73c67.title: Peat
8f8ce6f73c67.section: Environmental and ecological issues > Reduced usage
8f8ce6f73c67.sentence: Peat extraction has been forbidden in Chile since April 2024.

1edcffdc4a94.title: Peat
1edcffdc4a94.sentence: In controlled environment agriculture peat is often used to make grow cups (that then hold coco coir or other medium), but similarly recent life cycle analysis has shown it is better for the environment to replace them with re-usable plastic cups (peat cups have ~4.5 times higher carbon footprint and 35 % greater energy consumption than single-use plastic cups).

e05c76320bf3.title: Peat
e05c76320bf3.sentence: Peat material is either fibric, hemic, or sapric.

6daece56efc8.title: Peat
6daece56efc8.sentence: Fibric peats are the least decomposed and consist of intact fibre.

8fc12c1a0003.title: Peat
8fc12c1a0003.sentence: Hemic peats are partially decomposed and sapric are the most decomposed.

8fb5df54cdaa.title: Peat
8fb5df54cdaa.sentence: Phragmites peat are composed of reed grass, Phragmites australis, and other grasses.

e78decafc22d.title: Peat
e78decafc22d.sentence: It is denser than many other types of peat.

1ae4abe2c5d1.title: Peat
1ae4abe2c5d1.sentence: Around half of the area of northern peatlands is permafrost-affected, and this area represents around a tenth of the total permafrost area, and also a tenth (185 ± 66 Gt) of all permafrost carbon, equivalent to around half of the carbon stored in the atmosphere.

473f1dc26666.title: Peat
473f1dc26666.sentence: Dry peat is a good insulator (with a thermal conductivity of around 0.25 Wm−1K−1) and therefore plays an important role in protecting permafrost from thaw.

0c02e2391dae.title: Peat
0c02e2391dae.sentence: The insulating effect of dry peat also makes it integral to unique permafrost landforms such as palsas and permafrost peat plateaus.

865a0e420294.title: Peat
865a0e420294.sentence: Peatland permafrost thaw tends to result in an increase in methane emissions and a small increase in carbon dioxide uptake, meaning that it contributes to the permafrost carbon feedback.

4d194eea48c1.title: Peat
4d194eea48c1.sentence: Under 2 °C global warming, 0.7 million km2 of peatland permafrost could thaw, and with warming of +1.5 to 6 °C a cumulative 0.7 to 3 PgC of methane could be released as a result of permafrost peatland thaw by 2100.

baee486bc644.title: Peat
baee486bc644.sentence: Often, restoration is done by blocking drainage channels in the peatland, and allowing natural vegetation to recover.

06adfd8f2f10.title: Peat
06adfd8f2f10.sentence: Rehabilitation projects undertaken in North America and Europe usually focus on the rewetting of peatlands and revegetation of native species.

be2e6bea7875.title: Peat
be2e6bea7875.sentence: This acts to mitigate carbon release in the short term before the new growth of vegetation provides a new source of organic litter to fuel the peat formation in the long term.

a90d4cfd9722.title: Peat
a90d4cfd9722.sentence: Active peatland plant reintroduction successfully re-establishes typical plant communities within 5 years after restoration.

f6fdebfe1b7c.title: Peat
f6fdebfe1b7c.sentence: These support the return of animal, insect, and bird communities found in undisturbed similar environments.

e9f179beb94e.title: Peat
e9f179beb94e.sentence: The presence of pools in restoration projects increases the biodiversity by providing a variety of microhabitats.

01da21489bc2.title: Peat
01da21489bc2.sentence: The United Nations Convention on Biological Diversity highlights peatlands as key ecosystems to be conserved and protected.

60da031ac3ee.title: Peat
60da031ac3ee.sentence: Wetlands are also protected under the 1971 Ramsar Convention.

743ad98f59af.title: Rendzina
743ad98f59af.sentence: Rendzina (or rendsina) is a soil type recognized in various soil classification systems, including those of Britain and Germany as well as some obsolete systems.

a5112630e795.title: Rendzina
a5112630e795.sentence: They are humus-rich shallow soils that are usually formed from carbonate- or occasionally sulfate-rich parent material.

78f1ec8c3f01.title: Rendzina
78f1ec8c3f01.sentence: Limestone is by far the most common, but others include dolomite, gypsum, marble, chalk and marlstone.

f1c0286aadee.title: Rendzina
f1c0286aadee.sentence: Typical areas for rendzina soils are in karst and mountain landscapes, where carbonate-rich material occurs on slopes.

d48570e518c6.title: Rendzina
d48570e518c6.sentence: When water with dissolved carbon dioxide comes into contact with carbonate minerals, the carbonate is dissolved and leaches out with the water.

8d5a91e8234b.title: Rendzina
8d5a91e8234b.sentence: Loss of soluble minerals leaves the upper part of the soil enriched in insoluble materials, particularly clay minerals.

1c668a52112a.title: Rendzina
