1c668a52112a.sentence: At the same time, biological activity leads to an accumulation of humus in the surface soil, which is protected from further decomposition by the clay.

8dd61150c642.title: Rendzina
8dd61150c642.sentence: The combined effects of clay and humus content produce dark colours and crumb structure.

b88cba517019.title: Rendzina
b88cba517019.sentence: The rendzinas in Wales, for example constitute a simple A-C profile, a dark calcareous topsoil immediately over shattered limestone.

86b72974a9a1.title: Rendzina
86b72974a9a1.sentence: Typical pH for Rendzina soils is between 5 and 8, and base saturation is high.

4b8094c3c9b0.title: Rendzina
4b8094c3c9b0.sentence: Calcium and magnesium are abundant, but potassium content is often low, so nutrient imbalances are common.

2fb24dcbdc1b.title: Rendzina
2fb24dcbdc1b.sentence: Progressive breakdown of the parent material and loss of carbonate or gypsum will ultimately convert a rendzina into another soil type.

9c47804c83d9.title: Rendzina
9c47804c83d9.sentence: Since these processes occur relatively fast in comparison to weathering of most carbonate- and gypsum-free materials, rendzinas represent a transitory stage in soil development.

2190e611597e.title: Rendzina
2190e611597e.sentence: However, they can persist over the long term if soil loss by erosion counteracts the soil development process.

9e710e01f2ac.title: Rendzina
9e710e01f2ac.sentence: Mechanical tillage is hindered by their shallowness, and the small soil volume limits their capacity to store and supply water.

b2d2006b1f45.title: Rendzina
b2d2006b1f45.sentence: Additionally, these soils often occur on slopes, where the risk of erosion is high.

c7a2b9022e7a.title: Rendzina
c7a2b9022e7a.sentence: As a result, there is much semi-natural vegetation to be found in these areas.

f983bba1258c.title: Terra rossa (soil)
f983bba1258c.sentence: Terra rossa (Italian for 'red soil') is a well-drained, reddish, clayey to silty soil with neutral pH conditions and is typical of the Mediterranean region.

fdc7dcabd035.title: Terra rossa (soil)
fdc7dcabd035.sentence: The reddish color of terra rossa is the result of the preferential formation of hematite over goethite.

27d7f53a8eb5.title: Terra rossa (soil)
27d7f53a8eb5.sentence: This soil type typically occurs as a discontinuous layer that ranges from a few centimeters to several meters in thickness that covers limestone and dolomite bedrock in karst regions.

ce1407746af9.title: Terra rossa (soil)
ce1407746af9.sentence: The high internal drainage and neutral pH conditions of terra rossa are a result of the karstic nature of the underlying limestone and dolomite.

861a8a5d66d6.title: Terra rossa (soil)
861a8a5d66d6.sentence: Compared to most clay rich soils, terra rossa has surprisingly good drainage characteristics.

dbb38cf5db38.title: Terra rossa (soil)
dbb38cf5db38.sentence: This makes it a popular soil type for wine production.

3ec986524dce.title: Terra rossa (soil)
3ec986524dce.sentence: Among other wine regions, it is found in La Mancha in Spain and the Coonawarra, Fleurieu, Wrattonbully and Barossa Valley growing areas in Australia.

c0a2ebb304d1.title: Terra rossa (soil)
c0a2ebb304d1.sentence: In pedology, red Mediterranean soil, also known as terra rossa (Italian for "red soil") is a soil classification that has been formally superseded by the formal classifications of systems such as the FAO soil classification, but that is still in common use.

83712a65b27b.title: Terra rossa (soil)
83712a65b27b.sentence: The terra rossa classification was still, as of 1997, a part of the national soil classifications of countries such as Israel and Italy.

4ef3dd8691d6.title: Terra rossa (soil)
4ef3dd8691d6.sentence: The UNESCO/FAO World map equivalents are the chromic luvisols (a sub-order of the luvisols), and the USDA soil taxonomy equivalent is the rhodustalfs (a sub-order of the ustalfs).

07011e7e4f74.title: Terra rossa (soil)
07011e7e4f74.sentence: The most accelerated development of red Mediterranean soils occurred from the Miocene to the Late Pleistocene, due to the large amount of climate fluctuation in those periods.

cc509af2a53e.title: Dark earth
cc509af2a53e.sentence: In geology and archaeology, dark earth is a substratum, up to 1 metre (3 ft 3 in) thick, that indicates settlement over long periods of time.

82bd475fa92f.title: Dark earth
82bd475fa92f.sentence: The material is high in organic matter, including charcoal, which gives it its characteristic dark colour; it may also contain fragments of pottery, tile, animal bone and other artefacts.

96086b7a4d01.title: Dark earth
96086b7a4d01.sentence: It is interpreted as soil enriched with the sooty remains of thatched roofs from houses without chimneys, with other waste materials.

f5067771d8ae.title: Dark earth
f5067771d8ae.sentence: In some areas it appears to give the soil added fertility.

8100fca592af.title: Dark earth
8100fca592af.sentence: London's dark earth was originally called 'black earth' by archaeologists.

0d1e92b3383b.title: Dark earth
0d1e92b3383b.sentence: It was renamed 'dark earth' because of confusion with the chernozem (black earth soils in Russia), whose dark colour is traditionally (not universally) thought to come from humus, rather than soot.

00e8b48362e1.title: Dark earth
00e8b48362e1.sentence: In the Hebrides, it was customary to remove the thatch from the "black houses" every spring, and spread it on the fields as fertilizer, improved by the soot which it retained.

f4efe46dcf9b.title: Dark earth
f4efe46dcf9b.sentence: On Achill Island, special smoke huts were built in the fields, stone structures with sod roofs.

9ba2c68bf10f.title: Dark earth
9ba2c68bf10f.sentence: From October to May smoky fires burned inside them, and in spring the sods were spread on the fields.

51814ee86e1e.title: Dark earth
51814ee86e1e.sentence: In England, dark earth covers many areas that were built up in the Roman period, especially Londinium.

c996de2c0f9e.title: Dark earth
c996de2c0f9e.sentence: In the example of London, deposits underlying the ancient city's dark earth are often dated to between the 2nd to 5th century, the middle and later Roman period.

7f44026174bd.title: Dark earth
7f44026174bd.sentence: Overlying deposits are frequently dated to the 9th century when Saxon London was repopulated and began to expand.

88c559ecb938.title: Dark earth
88c559ecb938.sentence: Archaeologists have debated what London's dark earth layer may indicate about human use of the city.

13ea1b700f80.title: Dark earth
13ea1b700f80.sentence: It has been taken as evidence of refuse disposal or gardening during the Roman period on the site of previous buildings.

aedf05c07e8b.title: Dark earth
aedf05c07e8b.sentence: Alternatively, dark earth might have formed only after abandonment at the end of the Roman period.

2160059ffd73.title: Dark earth
2160059ffd73.sentence: Latest findings in France demonstrated that dark earth may originate from a change from stone to organic building materials; timber and straw will decay and build dark earth.

20adff7bb1d4.title: Dark earth
20adff7bb1d4.sentence: For a period of at least 700 years, West African farmers have enriched the rain forest soils around their towns with compost derived from kitchen, animal, agricultural, and fire waste to produce a signature dark earth.

b53a97df8926.title: Dark earth
b53a97df8926.sentence: In Sweden, dark earth covering 40 hectares (100 acres) has been found in Uppåkra, in Scania, southern Sweden, where a city-like settlement existed from about the year 1 until 1000 CE when the settlement shifted to modern day Lund.

b0c1e635db5c.title: Dark earth
b0c1e635db5c.sentence: Dark earth over 7 hectares (17 acres) has been found in the Viking city of Björkö (today called Birka), in central Sweden, close to modern Stockholm.

48e28969ad50.title: Terra preta
48e28969ad50.sentence: The transformation of biomass into charcoal produces a series of charcoal derivatives known as pyrogenic or black carbon, the composition of which varies from lightly charred organic matter, to soot particles rich in graphite formed by recomposition of free radicals.

55c8fbd12d12.title: Terra preta
55c8fbd12d12.sentence: Indigenous people added low temperature charcoal to poor soils.

52f73baa901c.title: Terra preta
52f73baa901c.sentence: Up to 9% black carbon has been measured in some terra preta (against 0.5% in surrounding soils).

75a3ad8e23e2.title: Terra preta
75a3ad8e23e2.sentence: Other measurements found carbon levels 70 times greater than in surrounding ferralsols, with approximate average values of 50 Mg/ha/m.

1e772cfc8a85.title: Terra preta
1e772cfc8a85.sentence: The chemical structure of charcoal in terra preta soils is characterized by poly-condensed aromatic groups that provide prolonged biological and chemical stability against microbial degradation; it also provides, after partial oxidation, the highest nutrient retention.

a29170255a48.title: Terra preta
a29170255a48.sentence: The nucleus of black carbon particles produced by the biomass remains aromatic even after thousands of years and presents the spectral characteristics of fresh charcoal.

041c5ebf46f1.title: Terra preta
041c5ebf46f1.sentence: The slow oxidation of charcoal creates carboxylic groups; these increase the cation exchange capacity of the soil.

24befa50e0aa.title: Terra preta
24befa50e0aa.sentence: Charcoal's porosity brings better retention of organic matter, of water and of dissolved nutrients, as well as of pollutants such as pesticides and aromatic poly-cyclic hydrocarbons.

c86eca2149a5.title: Terra preta
c86eca2149a5.section: Pedology > Organic matter and nutrients > Organic matter
c86eca2149a5.sentence: Charcoal's high absorption potential of organic molecules (and of water) is due to its porous structure.

e2f558e414c4.title: Terra preta
e2f558e414c4.sentence: Fresh charcoal must be "charged with nutrients" before it can function as a biotope.

ec70bdc5c128.title: Terra preta
ec70bdc5c128.sentence: Several experiments demonstrate that uncharged charcoal can bring a temporary depletion of available nutrients when first put into the soil, that is until its pores fill with nutrients.

d9d059d17199.title: Terra preta
d9d059d17199.sentence: This is overcome by soaking the charcoal for two to four weeks in any liquid nutrient (urine, plant tea, worm tea, etc.).

510c56f03b6c.title: Terra preta
510c56f03b6c.sentence: Low temperature charcoal (but not that from grasses or high cellulose materials) has an internal layer of biological petroleum condensates that the bacteria consume, and is similar to cellulose in its effects on microbial growth.

79899fd662be.title: Terra preta
79899fd662be.sentence: Charring at high temperature consumes that layer and brings little increase in soil fertility.

69c737162d6b.title: Terra preta
69c737162d6b.sentence: The peregrine earthworm Pontoscolex corethrurus (Oligochaeta: Glossoscolecidae) ingests charcoal and mixes it into a finely ground form with the mineral soil.

a23bbdcf67b7.title: Tropical peat
a23bbdcf67b7.sentence: Tropical peat is a type of histosol that is found in tropical latitudes, including South East Asia, Africa, and Central and South America.

b9b37725bed0.title: Tropical peat
b9b37725bed0.sentence: Tropical peat mostly consists of dead organic matter from trees instead of sphagnum which are commonly found in temperate peat.

9cc67945e6d5.title: Tropical peat
9cc67945e6d5.sentence: This soils usually contain high organic matter content, exceeding 75% with dry low bulk density around 0.2 mg/m3 (0.0 gr/cu ft).

6c9566048315.title: Tropical peat
6c9566048315.sentence: Estimates of the area (and hence volume) of tropical peatlands vary but a reasonable estimate is in the region of 380,000 square kilometres (150,000 sq mi).

30a2f469c30d.title: Tropical peat
30a2f469c30d.sentence: Although tropical peatlands only cover about 0.25% of the Earth's land surface they contain 50,000–70,000 million tonnes of carbon (about 3% global soil carbon).

a32e8aa2fc1f.title: Tropical peat
a32e8aa2fc1f.sentence: Areas of tropical peat are found mostly in South America (about 46% by area) although they are also found in Africa, Central America, Asia and elsewhere around the tropics.

ddce367da49c.title: Peat
ddce367da49c.sentence: The world's largest tropical peatland is located in Africa (the Democratic Republic of Congo).

e491072cba69.title: Tropical peat
e491072cba69.sentence: The native peat swamp forests contain a number of valuable timber-producing trees plus a range of other products of value to local communities, such as bark, resins and latex.

e76268b56d15.title: Tropical peat
e76268b56d15.sentence: In addition, tropical peatlands support diverse ecosystems and are home to a number of endangered species including the orangutan.

3d650c78e3a6.title: Tropical peat
3d650c78e3a6.sentence: Once the forest is removed and the peat is drained, the surface peat oxidises and loses stored carbon rapidly to the atmosphere (as carbon dioxide).

9e9ce591a651.title: Tropical peat
9e9ce591a651.sentence: This results in progressive loss of the peat surface, leading to local flooding and, due to the large areas involved, global climate change.

4fcf25ff3f19.title: Tropical peat
4fcf25ff3f19.sentence: Land-use changes and fire, mainly associated with plantation development and logging (deforestation and drainage), are reducing this carbon store and contributing to greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions.

da13de475268.title: Peat
da13de475268.section: Environmental and ecological issues > Peat fires
da13de475268.sentence: The recent burning of peat bogs in Indonesia, with their large and deep growths containing more than 50 billion tonnes (55 billion short tons; 49 billion long tons) of carbon, has contributed to increases in world carbon dioxide levels.

93ee5ac162ea.title: Tropical peat
93ee5ac162ea.sentence: Failure to account for such emissions results in underestimates of the rate of increase in atmospheric GHGs and the extent of human induced climate change.

da1ea6df0cb3.title: Red soil
da1ea6df0cb3.sentence: Red soil is a type of soil that typically develops in warm, temperate, and humid climates and comprises approximately 13% of Earth's soil.

ca2ac4c9900c.title: Red soil
ca2ac4c9900c.sentence: Red soils contain large amounts of clay and are generally derived from the weathering of ancient crystalline and metamorphic rock.

21e10fc1319b.title: Red soil
21e10fc1319b.sentence: It contains thin organic and organic-mineral layers of highly leached soil resting on a red layer of alluvium.

5de4fe745ed1.title: Red soil
5de4fe745ed1.sentence: They are named after their rich red color, varying from reddish brown to reddish yellow due to their high iron content.

640fe2c03f06.title: Red soil
640fe2c03f06.sentence: Red soils include multiple soil types (e.g. ultisols, alfisols, oxisols) that are classified as red soil when they develop a distinct reddish color, which can vary from reddish brown to reddish yellow due to their high iron content.

20d4b33bc239.title: Red soil
20d4b33bc239.sentence: There is not a singular composition that classifies all red soils.

d5d9bd5844cc.title: Red soil
d5d9bd5844cc.sentence: One type of red soil may be considered infertile in one region but nutrient-rich in another.

2588c9e80404.title: Red soil
2588c9e80404.sentence: Red soils are typically difficult for crop cultivation because high leaching leads to low water holding capacity, low nutrients, low organic matter (humus), and acidification.

72d5ff36dc14.title: Red soil
72d5ff36dc14.section: Soil fertility and management practices > Nutrient application
72d5ff36dc14.sentence: Red soils are often deficient in nitrogen due to local rainfall patterns (e.g. intense leaching of nitrates), soil erosion, which limits their growth properties in the absence of fertiization.

e455b9b6359f.title: Red soil
e455b9b6359f.section: Soil fertility and management practices > Nutrient application
e455b9b6359f.sentence: Phosphorus and potassium can also become limited after the land has been harvested repeatedly.

8dd9a3065ab1.title: Red soil
8dd9a3065ab1.section: Soil fertility and management practices > Liming
8dd9a3065ab1.sentence: Because red soils are generally acidic, liming is a valuable farming technique that allows crops intolerant of acidic environments to thrive in red soil.

3099a2e770bc.title: Red soil
3099a2e770bc.section: Soil fertility and management practices > Liming
3099a2e770bc.sentence: However, liming may have long-term environmental consequences on the soil, the stimulation of microbial activity decreasing the soil organic matter content, which may negatively affect the soil structure.

8036d5134bb4.title: Red soil
8036d5134bb4.section: Soil fertility and management practices > Organic matter
8036d5134bb4.sentence: Some strategies employed to practice this include the use of organic manure and establishing proper tillage systems for the land.

8c73f9f071ab.title: Red soil
8c73f9f071ab.section: Soil fertility and management practices > Crop rotation
8c73f9f071ab.sentence: It works by increasing the soil's organic matter content, which enhances its fertility and water retention capabilities.

751e6044d647.title: Red soil
751e6044d647.sentence: Red soils are an important resource because they make up such a large portion of farmland on the Earth, mainly in tropical, subtropical, and Mediterranean climatic zones.

b054c3e47734.title: Red soil
b054c3e47734.sentence: Red soil resources are estimated to cover 102 million hectare (1,020,000 square kilometers) of land in tropical and subtropical regions of China.

736f8647691f.title: Red soil
736f8647691f.sentence: Red soils denote the most extensive soil group of India, covering an area of about 350,000 km2 (10.6% of India's area) across the peninsula.

8c4088f0cc2c.title: Red soil
8c4088f0cc2c.sentence: These soils, also known ironically as the omnibus group due to its varied localized names and characteristics, have been developed over ancient crystalline and metamorphic rocks of the Pre-Cambrian shield, specifically granites, gneisses, and quartzites, typically evolving under conditions of low to moderate rainfall.

e89b8e410a26.title: Red soil
e89b8e410a26.sentence: In the uplands of India, the red soils are thin, poor and gravelly, sandy, or stony and porous, light-colored soils on which only highly tolerant food crops like bajra can be grown.

b79dff32a35d.title: Red soil
b79dff32a35d.sentence: In contrast, on the lower plains and valleys, they are rich, deep, dark-colored fertile loam which, under irrigation, can produce excellent crops like cotton, wheat, pulses, tobacco, jowar, linseed, millet, potatoes and fruits.

03b9c4858617.title: Brown podzolic
03b9c4858617.sentence: Brown podzolic soils are a subdivision of the Podzolic soils in the British soil classification.

41f8a68ea1ea.title: Brown podzolic
41f8a68ea1ea.sentence: They are common on hilly land in western Europe, in climates where precipitation of more than about 900mm exceeds evapotranspiration for a large part of the year, and summers are relatively cool.

2f0da934c925.title: Brown podzolic
2f0da934c925.sentence: These soils have large amounts (more than 5%) of organic carbon in the surface horizon, which is therefore dark in colour.

6784d70bbc8b.title: Brown podzolic
6784d70bbc8b.sentence: In unploughed situations there may be a "mor" humus layer in which the surface organic matter is only weakly mixed with the mineral component.

f49b6b652916.title: Brown podzolic
f49b6b652916.sentence: Unlike podzols proper, these soils have no continuous leached E horizon.

77c71a83126e.title: Brown podzolic
77c71a83126e.sentence: This is because they are formed on slopes where, over long periods, the topsoil weathered from higher up the slope is continually being carried down the slope by the action of rain, gravity and faunal activity.

f9be4cb1622e.title: Brown podzolic
f9be4cb1622e.sentence: Thus they are common in Ireland, Scotland, Wales (where they occupy about 20% of the country) and western England, especially Devon, Cornwall and the Lake District.

34af3973472b.title: Brown podzolic
34af3973472b.sentence: They also occur in the Appalachian Mountains and on the west coast of North America.

5bbae76bc357.title: Bay mud
5bbae76bc357.sentence: Bay mud consists of thick deposits of soft, unconsolidated silty clay, which is saturated with water; these soil layers are situated at the bottom of certain estuaries, which are normally in temperate regions that have experienced cyclical glacial cycles.

42f145073748.title: Bay mud
42f145073748.sentence: Bay mud manifests low shear strength, high compressibility and low permeability, making it hazardous to build upon in seismically active regions like the San Francisco Bay Area.

fa55e4656a22.title: Bay mud
fa55e4656a22.sentence: Typical bulk density of bay mud is approximately 1.3 grams per cubic centimetre.

fb83dbdc1a37.title: Bay mud
fb83dbdc1a37.sentence: First alluvial deposits of clays, silts and sand occur from streams tributary to a given bay.

1bd54f654842.title: Bay mud
1bd54f654842.sentence: Second, in periods of high glaciation, deposits of silts, sands and organic plus inorganic detritus (e.g. decomposition of estuarine diatoms) may form a separate distinct layer.

24693bae976d.title: Bay mud
24693bae976d.sentence: Very lightweight buildings can be constructed on bay mud sites if there is a thick enough layer of non-bay-mud soil above the bay mud, but buildings which impose significant loads must be supported on deep foundations bearing on stiffer layers below the bay mud, or obtaining support from friction in the bay mud.

a16d8a0f2572.title: Bay mud
a16d8a0f2572.sentence: Even with deep foundations, difficulties arise because the surrounding ground will likely settle over time, potentially damaging utility connections to the building and causing the entryway to sink below street level.

c5030bb08190.title: Bay mud
c5030bb08190.sentence: Bay muds often have a high organic content, consisting of decayed organisms at lower depths, but may also contain living creatures when they occur at the upper soil layer and become exposed by low tides; then, they are called mudflats, an important ecological zone for shorebirds and many types of marine organisms.

f0a8de3bd863.title: Bay mud
f0a8de3bd863.sentence: When the mud layer is exposed at the tidal fringe, mudflats result affording a unique ecotone that affords numerous shorebird species a safe feeding and resting habitat.

b04fbeda3f79.title: Bay mud
b04fbeda3f79.sentence: The muds are also an important substrate for primary marsh productivity including eelgrass, cordgrass and pickleweed.

271c222849da.title: Terra preta
271c222849da.sentence: The origins of the Amazonian dark earths were not immediately clear to later settlers.

e68ca2df6f34.title: Terra preta
e68ca2df6f34.sentence: Many terra preta soil structures are now thought to have formed under kitchen middens, as well as being manufactured intentionally on larger scales.

b30f47d8b56c.title: Terra preta
b30f47d8b56c.sentence: Recent research has reported that terra preta may be of natural origin, suggesting that pre-Columbian people intentionally utilized and improved existing areas of soil fertility scattered among areas of lower fertility.

6e2cbe18e02e.title: Terra preta
6e2cbe18e02e.sentence: One idea was that they resulted from ashfall from volcanoes in the Andes, since they occur more frequently on the brows of higher terraces.

8379d104bb7b.title: Terra preta
8379d104bb7b.sentence: Another theory considered its formation to be a result of sedimentation in tertiary lakes or in recent ponds.

a734aae1fe50.title: Terra preta
a734aae1fe50.sentence: Soils with elevated charcoal content and a common presence of pottery remains can accrete accidentally near living quarters as residues from food preparation, cooking fires, animal and fish bones, broken pottery, etc., accumulated.

b539744ee811.title: Terra preta
b539744ee811.sentence: The variations in Amazonian dark earths prevent clearly determining whether all of them were intentionally created for soil improvement or whether the lightest variants are a by-product of habitation.

482e15fe93b9.title: Terra preta
482e15fe93b9.section: Modern research on creating terra preta > Synthetic terra preta
482e15fe93b9.sentence: A newly coined term is 'synthetic terra preta'.

4500412b16c4.title: Terra preta
4500412b16c4.section: Modern research on creating terra preta > Synthetic terra preta
4500412b16c4.sentence: STP is a fertilizer consisting of materials thought to replicate the original materials, including crushed clay, blood and bone meal, manure and biochar is of particulate nature and capable of moving down the soil profile and improving soil fertility and carbon in the current soil peds and aggregates over a viable time frame.

91b017cdd2c8.title: Terra preta
91b017cdd2c8.section: Modern research on creating terra preta > Synthetic terra preta
91b017cdd2c8.sentence: Average poor tropical soils are easily enrichable to terra preta nova by the addition of charcoal and condensed smoke.

dc498279158f.title: Terra preta
dc498279158f.section: Modern research on creating terra preta > Synthetic terra preta
dc498279158f.sentence: Terra preta may be an important avenue of future carbon sequestration while reversing the current worldwide decline in soil fertility and associated desertification.

cffb53c3a90b.title: Terra preta
cffb53c3a90b.section: Modern research on creating terra preta > Synthetic terra preta
cffb53c3a90b.sentence: Whether this is possible on a larger scale has yet to be proven.

7b6c9d4d6bbc.title: Terra preta
7b6c9d4d6bbc.section: Modern research on creating terra preta > Terra preta sanitation
7b6c9d4d6bbc.sentence: Terra preta sanitation (TPS) systems have been studied as an alternative sanitation option by using the effects of lactic-aid conditions in urine-diverting dry toilets and a subsequent treatment by vermicomposting.

c6b1c388eb05.title: Brickearth
c6b1c388eb05.sentence: Brickearth is a term originally used to describe superficial windblown deposits found in southern England.

6b6d2f9952a6.title: Brickearth
6b6d2f9952a6.sentence: Brickearth is a superficial deposit of homogeneous loam or silt deposited during the Pleistocene geological period.

0ab5451b2972.title: Brickearth
0ab5451b2972.sentence: Brickearths are periglacial loess, a wind-blown dust deposited under extremely cold, dry, peri- or postglacial conditions.

dcb6f3caf796.title: Brickearth
dcb6f3caf796.sentence: The original deposition of the sediments occurred under cold climates where fluvial out-wash sediments from glaciers were subject to windy dry periods.

757a5227f996.title: Brickearth
757a5227f996.sentence: The exposed finer-grained sediments were picked up and transported by the wind and were deposited wherever the wind strength decreased.

ea5a01d28bd2.title: Brickearth
ea5a01d28bd2.sentence: Brickearth typically occurs in discontinuous spreads, across southern England and South Wales, south of a line from Pembroke in the west to Essex in the east in depths of up to a metre.

f32d2971a3df.title: Brickearth
f32d2971a3df.sentence: Commercially useful deposits of about 2m to 4m thick are present in Kent, Hertfordshire and Hampshire, overlying chalk, Thanet Beds or London Clay.

7eaccf84a239.title: Brickearth
7eaccf84a239.sentence: The name arises from its early use in making house bricks, its composition being suitable for brick-making without additional material being added; unlike clay, its bricks can be hardened (fused) at lower temperatures, including in wood-fired kilns.

cf2278d4b387.title: Brickearth
cf2278d4b387.sentence: Brickearth requires little or no admixture of other materials to render it suitable for the manufacture of 'stock bricks'.

928f3a853838.title: Brickearth
928f3a853838.sentence: The brickearth gives rise to rich and fertile soils which have been exploited for agriculture.

8f9ca603e598.title: Brickearth
8f9ca603e598.sentence: It is prone to rapid 'collapse' settlement when saturated with water and does not provide a firm foundation for buildings.

333ee09f126d.title: Fill dirt
333ee09f126d.sentence: Fill dirt (also called cleanfill, or just fill) is earthy material which is used to fill in a depression or hole in the ground or create mounds or otherwise artificially change the grade or elevation of real property.

b0f187e8899c.title: Fill dirt
b0f187e8899c.sentence: Fill dirt is usually subsoil (soil from beneath topsoil) and underlying soil parent material which has little soil organic matter or biological activity.

08b8e4beb1c1.title: Fill dirt
08b8e4beb1c1.sentence: Fill dirt is taken from a location where soil is being removed as a part of leveling an area for construction; it may also contain sand, rocks, and stones, as well as earth.

ebb3bef598c9.title: Fill dirt
ebb3bef598c9.sentence: Fill dirt should be as free of organic matter as possible since organic matter will decompose creating pockets of empty space within the fill which could result in settling.

6c60c1177b9c.title: Fill dirt
6c60c1177b9c.sentence: Uneven or excessive settling of the fill can result in damage to any structures built on the fill.

b7bdb850e61a.title: Fill dirt
b7bdb850e61a.sentence: A common use of fill dirt is in highway maintenance to build up the shoulders of highways so that the ground on either side of the pavement is at the same level as the pavement itself, and that the highway shoulders are sufficiently wide as to allow vehicles room to pull off the highway if needed.

7f650b001a8e.title: Fill dirt
7f650b001a8e.sentence: A second common use of fill dirt is to fill in a low-lying construction site to raise the level of the building foundation in order to reduce the chances of flooding.

19ffc95995f0.title: Fill dirt
19ffc95995f0.sentence: Several massive uses of fill dirt are with improvements to the Port of Seattle Sea-Tac Airport, the addition of a new runway to the Hartsfield–Jackson Atlanta International Airport in Atlanta, Georgia, and the Kansai International Airport off the coast of Osaka, Japan, a project involving the creation of a new man-made island of some five square kilometers.

381c1cc4c42c.title: Fill dirt
381c1cc4c42c.sentence: Fill dirt is most often mined from commercial sand and gravel mines then imported to the project site, and must meet specifications for gradation outlined by the Project's Geotechnical Engineer.

df66944c672e.title: Stagnogley
df66944c672e.sentence: A stagnogley soil is a type of non-alluvial, non-calcareous soil that is typically loamy or clayey soil with a dense, impervious, subsurface horizon.

c584d34245cf.title: Stagnogley
c584d34245cf.sentence: Stagnogley soils are related to the pseudogleys and are classified as gleyic soils.

9ee863af16b8.title: Stagnogley
9ee863af16b8.sentence: This type of soil, whose topsoil becomes bleached due to continual waterlogging, is often formed on sand-rich material over dense, sandy-loamy to silty-clayey subsoil—also called Sandkerf in German—in cool, moist climatic zones.

caf3c93edbe1.title: Stagnogley
caf3c93edbe1.sentence: This hygroscopic soil is nutrient-poor, often highly acidic, and poorly aerated, making it unsuitable for farming due to poor crop growth.

bd7421396c08.title: Stagnogley
bd7421396c08.sentence: With a shallow topsoil layer and a moderately stony subsoil, stagnogley soil is mainly used for woodland, supporting tree species that thrive well in these conditions, such as the English Oak.

36c6e6e1c4fb.title: Stagnogley
36c6e6e1c4fb.sentence: Where the soil is saturated all-year round, it turns into bog stagnogley and, eventually, into bog.

85b3183c62aa.title: Stagnogley
85b3183c62aa.sentence: Examples, known as missen occur in the Black Forest in Germany.

fe742ab516ad.title: Stagnogley
fe742ab516ad.sentence: Stagnogley soils occur in perhumid climates and also on steep slopes.

4db69b00c58e.title: Stagnogley
4db69b00c58e.sentence: They are found, for example, in the central European Central Upland ranges of the Black Forest, Ore Mountains and Eifel in waterlogged places, as well as on the Midvale Ridge in the UK.

2faf96c734c5.title: Subaqueous soil
2faf96c734c5.sentence: Subaqueous soils are soils formed in sediment found in shallow, permanently flooded environments or soils in any areas permanently covered by water too deep for the growth of rooted plants.

ece29fdfb521.title: Subaqueous soil
ece29fdfb521.sentence: The concept that sediments in shallow water environments undergo soil-forming processes, are capable of supporting rooted plants (such as Eelgrass), and meet the definition of soil according to criteria in Soil Taxonomy has been moving soil scientists into a new frontier of soil survey – mapping subaqueous soils.

e4348fec9ab8.title: Subaqueous soil
e4348fec9ab8.sentence: The difference between subaqueous and submerged soils is that submerged soils formed in an upland environment then became submerged as a result of rising water tables, flooding events (such as a Beaver Dam), or sea level rise.

5daa1d5e08c9.title: Subaqueous soil
5daa1d5e08c9.sentence: Subaqueous soils formed under a continuous water column (such as in an estuary), although their sediments may have originated from an upland area such as a dune.

1a606aa52ba6.title: Subaqueous soil
1a606aa52ba6.sentence: Although proposals to include permanently submersed sediments as soil have been put forth since the mid-1800s, it was not until the early 1990s that the concept of subaqueous soils was developed in the U.S. The pioneer in U.S. subaqueous soils is the late George Demas, a soil scientist working for the National Cooperative Soil Survey in the Chesapeake Bay region of Maryland.

7c3e466ec253.title: Subaqueous soil
7c3e466ec253.sentence: Dr. Demas observed that subaqueous areas met the definition of soil by being able to support rooted plant growth (such as Eelgrass) and had formed soil horizons.

5164d2640c84.title: Subaqueous soil
5164d2640c84.sentence: Further study revealed that these submersed sediments underwent other soil forming (pedogenic) processes including additions, losses, and transformations of energy and matter.

b42dac4c3713.title: Subaqueous soil
b42dac4c3713.sentence: The depth range of the water column where these soils may be found is not known, an arbitrary depth of 2.5 meters below the surface has been set for soil survey inventory but some states have extended this depth to 5 m (NAVD 88).

9ea7bab930a3.title: Subaqueous soil
9ea7bab930a3.sentence: In part, this lack of information has stemmed from an inadequate paradigm for subaqueous soils, which has not considered them "soils" at all, but rather as "sediments".

64ff8aa27a63.title: Subaqueous soil
64ff8aa27a63.sentence: During the last decade, it has been demonstrated that these "sediments" would be better understood as "soils" and that the sedimentary paradigm should give way to a pedological paradigm.

adfaf78758a0.title: Subaqueous soil
adfaf78758a0.sentence: An advantage of using the pedological approach to study shallow water habitat is that soils are studied as a collection of horizons that are linked vertically with depth and horizontally across the subaqueous landscape.

82d01a0b4a8a.title: Subaqueous soil
82d01a0b4a8a.sentence: - Could provide a major or missing dataset for submersed aquatic vegetation (SAV) restoration, estuarine protection, planning and management.

60a7830ac695.title: Subaqueous soil
60a7830ac695.section: Significance > Nitrogen dynamics in submerged soil
60a7830ac695.sentence: Such soil occurs in rice fields, wetlands, estuaries and flood plains.

3f2137b3a309.title: Subaqueous soil
3f2137b3a309.section: Significance > Nitrogen dynamics in submerged soil
3f2137b3a309.sentence: Nitrogen dynamics is different as that from aerated soil conditions affecting soil microorganisms and nitrogen cycle.

266fb6da8b39.title: Calcareous grassland
266fb6da8b39.sentence: Calcareous grassland (or alkaline grassland) is an ecosystem associated with thin basic soil, such as that on chalk and limestone downland.

addd6dadcd83.title: Calcareous grassland
addd6dadcd83.sentence: There are large areas of calcareous grassland in northwestern Europe, particularly areas of southern England, such as Salisbury Plain and the North and South Downs.

b2b376b0a664.title: Calcareous grassland
b2b376b0a664.sentence: The machair forms a different kind of calcareous grassland, where fertile low-lying plains are formed on ground that is calcium-rich due to shell sand (pulverised sea shells).

5de9034ac965.title: Calcareous grassland
5de9034ac965.sentence: Plants on calcareous grassland are typically short and hardy, and include grasses and herbs such as clover.

32bb49190714.title: Calcareous grassland
32bb49190714.sentence: Calcareous grassland is an important habitat for insects, particularly butterflies and ants, and is kept at a plagioclimax by grazing animals, usually sheep and sometimes cattle.

7cc92ab696da.title: Calcareous grassland
7cc92ab696da.sentence: Key factors promoting lichen diversity include the presence of stable flints, areas of nutrient-poor soil, and the presence of a small loess (windblown silt) fraction in the soil.

c65d75ee9b05.title: Calcareous grassland
c65d75ee9b05.sentence: Many calcareous grassland lichen communities have shown significant decline since the mid-20th century, attributed to factors such as reduced grazing, nitrogen deposition, and habitat loss.

dd32a3f2d560.title: Blue goo
dd32a3f2d560.sentence: Blue goo is a sticky, plasticky, blueish-grey, clay-textured soil derived from a highly weathered serpentinite mélange.

6a18cd1d4c17.title: Blue goo
6a18cd1d4c17.sentence: The name derives from the soil's color; a result of undergoing anaerobic conditions and becoming gleyed.

89eeb6353fc2.title: Blue goo
89eeb6353fc2.sentence: A greyer variation is called "grey goo".

ccc6559d40ee.title: Blue goo
ccc6559d40ee.sentence: The Franciscan Complex is the bedrock from which blue goo is derived.

5b7ba4480613.title: Blue goo
5b7ba4480613.sentence: It stretches along the coastline from Central California up to Southern Oregon and contains sheared materials from both the Pacific and North American Plates that have accumulated in the accretionary wedge.

a2e8f84624a7.title: Blue goo
a2e8f84624a7.sentence: The rock types that produce blue goo include: greenstones, cherts, basalts, shales, sandstones, schists, and serpenitites.

4a296305eff3.title: Blue goo
4a296305eff3.sentence: This mélange decomposed through weathering to form blue goo.

1213a8f5ed3f.title: Blue goo
1213a8f5ed3f.sentence: Clay soils like blue goo have the highest water-holding capacity when compared with other soils, giving them a low draining capacity.

3d28b61dc0a3.title: Blue goo
3d28b61dc0a3.sentence: Due to blue goo's clayey texture, it slips when overly saturated.

0a58995c9224.title: Blue goo
0a58995c9224.sentence: This slippage is increased in heavy rainfall areas and in shallow soils; deep soils have more total pore space and are not as prone to slippage.

e7fb123491e3.title: Blue goo
e7fb123491e3.sentence: These features contribute to the landslide-ridden environments found along the Northern Californian coast.

2ab6056d8e7f.title: Blue goo
2ab6056d8e7f.sentence: But blue goo has only been found in two Northern Californian regions located in Humboldt County: the Trinidad region and the Orick region.

ec4bc0cb733f.title: Takir (soil)
ec4bc0cb733f.sentence: Takir (takyr) (originally from Kazakh or another Turkic language) meaning "smooth, even, or bare", is a type of relief occurring in the deserts of Central Asia, similar to a salt flat in the southwestern United States.

03f6efbdbb59.title: Takir (soil)
03f6efbdbb59.sentence: A takyr is usually formed in a shallow depressed area with a heavy clay soil, which is submerged by water after seasonal rains.

274b29c7f75d.title: Takir (soil)
274b29c7f75d.sentence: After the water evaporates, a dried crust with fissures forms on the surface.

2d78d37169ae.title: Takir (soil)
2d78d37169ae.sentence: The crust is often colonized by filamentous cyanobacteria.

e52856ccf3a8.title: Takir (soil)
e52856ccf3a8.sentence: In the southwestern U.S. "takyrs" are known as "playas" or "salt flats", in Arab countries as "sabkha".

f1d716d577e4.title: Serpentine soil
f1d716d577e4.sentence: Serpentine barrens are a unique ecoregion found in parts of the United States in small but widely distributed areas of the Appalachian Mountains and the Coast Ranges of California, Oregon, and Washington.

ee76cba224ba.title: Serpentine soil
ee76cba224ba.sentence: Serpentine barrens, as at Grass Valley, California, often consist of grassland or savannas in areas where the climate would normally lead to the growth of forests.

7ece7146957f.title: Serpentine soil
7ece7146957f.sentence: Barrens are especially likely in ultramafic areas which never had substantial deposits of non-ultramafic, more nutrient-rich material as carried by water (including glaciers) or wind (which delivers loess, sand or volcanic ash).

0d42117c2c90.title: Serpentine soil
0d42117c2c90.sentence: The barrens occur on outcrops of altered ultramafic ophiolites.

d08a4da8068a.title: Serpentine soil
d08a4da8068a.sentence: An article from the Journal of Trace Elements in Medicine and Biology discerned that 20% of the grazing animals had toxic levels of nickel in their kidneys, and 32% had toxic levels of copper in their liver.

db42d2a17aa6.title: Serpentine soil
db42d2a17aa6.sentence: It was originally a grassland, but wildfire suppression led to the conversion of the area to forest.

09434f601071.title: Serpentine soil
09434f601071.sentence: In 1995, the United States Forest Service began active conservation management of the site, primarily with prescribed controlled burns, which, along with some manual cover removal, has been successful in regenerating populations of previously sparse species.

64164a331139.title: Serpentine soil
64164a331139.sentence: Ecologically, serpentine soils have three main traits: poor plant productivity, high rates of endemism, and vegetation types that are distinct from neighboring areas.

c458910c146e.title: Serpentine soil
c458910c146e.sentence: In order to overcome the chemical and physical challenges presented by serpentine soils, plants have developed tolerances to drought, heavy metals, and limited nutrients.

e5b0623bf886.title: Serpentine soil
e5b0623bf886.sentence: They will exhibit a "stunted" growth habit, with dull waxy, gray-green leaves (seen in Eriogonum libertini), which allow for water retention and sunlight reflection respectively.

4b87bc503887.title: Serpentine soil
4b87bc503887.sentence: Low calcium:magnesium ratios cause limited root growth and root activity, weak cell membranes, and reduced uptake of essential nutrients.

523d476531cd.title: Serpentine soil
523d476531cd.sentence: Heavy metals stunt growth, induce iron deficiency, cause chlorosis, and restrict root development.

109da894dc4b.title: Serpentine soil
109da894dc4b.sentence: An adaptive mechanism to high magnesium soils allocates more resources to deep-growing roots.

37d8a0c0971e.title: Serpentine soil
37d8a0c0971e.sentence: Multiple adaptive mechanisms to heavy metals include the exclusion of metals by restricting the uptake by the roots, compartmentalization of metals in various organs, or the development of toxicity tolerance.

8c2d9ef9538f.title: Serpentine soil
8c2d9ef9538f.sentence: In California, 45% of the taxa associated with serpentine are rare or endangered.

ff6fcbe7805c.title: Serpentine soil
ff6fcbe7805c.sentence: In California, 10% of the state's plants are serpentine endemics.

9af9bffc570c.title: Serpentine soil
9af9bffc570c.sentence: Adaptation to serpentine soils has evolved multiple times.

47a27d71d497.title: Serpentine soil
47a27d71d497.sentence: The heterogeneity of serpentine communities coupled with their patchy distribution limits gene flow but promotes speciation and diversification.

63a63996ab64.title: Duplex soil
63a63996ab64.sentence: Duplex soils are also termed "texture contrast soils".

8922ba7d644f.title: Duplex soil
8922ba7d644f.sentence: With the term "duplex soil", Northcote defined a primary profile in his Factual Key classification.

554704670a62.title: Duplex soil
554704670a62.sentence: He described a group of texture contrast soils where the B horizon is dominated by a texture class one and a half (or more) finer than the A horizon.

7db1dc1c645b.title: Duplex soil
7db1dc1c645b.sentence: In addition, the clear to sharp change between the two horizons must occur within 0.1 m.

36bdcd49cbd9.title: Duplex soil
36bdcd49cbd9.sentence: Texture in duplex soils is highly variable, with the topsoils ranging from coarse sand to clay loam and the subsoils from light to heavy clay.

99a134a81582.title: Duplex soil
99a134a81582.sentence: Some duplex soils are distinguished by the presence of an A2 bleached horizon, a character also used as a diagnostic key for the distinction between these types of soils.

3ac62a564e84.title: Duplex soil
3ac62a564e84.sentence: The diagnostic properties used by Northcote for the definition of duplex soils consider only the soil texture (texture contrast and type of boundary between horizons A and B) and the colour is used for their differentiation (i.e. brown, red and yellow duplex soils).

fd6d21880026.title: Duplex soil
fd6d21880026.sentence: Under the Australian Soil Classification they can be included in different orders such as Podosols, Sodosol, Chromosols or Kurosols.

f3f3a51c7352.title: Terra rossa (soil)
f3f3a51c7352.sentence: The origin of terra rossa, its parent material, and its relationship to underlying limestones and dolomites has been greatly debated over recent decades by geologists, geomorphologists, and soil scientists.

969173a5d78b.title: Terra rossa (soil)
969173a5d78b.sentence: One group of scientists argue that terra rossa likely developed from dissolution of the underlying carbonate rocks and the concentration of insoluble sediment and chert within it as the parent material of terra rossa.

430ba266dd39.title: Terra rossa (soil)
430ba266dd39.sentence: Another group of scientists argues that terra rossa cannot have been formed exclusively from the insoluble residue of underlying limestone and dolomite.

5969e06b83cc.title: Terra rossa (soil)
5969e06b83cc.sentence: A final group of scientists argues that terra rossa was formed by metasomatic replacement processes.

e13a40594981.title: Constructed soil
e13a40594981.sentence: Constructed soils (also called fabricated soils) are mixtures of organic and mineral material derived from a number of sources, including repurposed organic waste, that are designed to approximate natural soils and provide a growing medium for plants.

f613fb0e64fa.title: Constructed soil
f613fb0e64fa.sentence: Constructed soils are commonly used in the reclamation of degraded land where natural topsoil is either not present or has been contaminated.

32c2aac19aae.title: Constructed soil
32c2aac19aae.sentence: Examples of these sites include mines, landfills, and other industrial or urban areas.

ae7fb3eadc38.title: Constructed soil
ae7fb3eadc38.sentence: Constructed soils are classified as Technosols, and often form the upper layer, or layers, in a Technosol above a geomembrane or other barrier capping waste material.

3ade96502ca6.title: Constructed soil
3ade96502ca6.sentence: Use of constructed soils in restoring sites is preferable to importing topsoil from other locations.

9454ac675c1b.title: Constructed soil
9454ac675c1b.sentence: Topsoil harvesting means a second location will be degraded, and collection and transport expenses will generally be higher than using local materials to create a new soil.

511e54bac9ad.title: Constructed soil
511e54bac9ad.sentence: Constructed soils that are less than approximately 45 cm thick will tend to be homogenous topsoil mixtures.

8b7a297b4de6.title: Constructed soil
8b7a297b4de6.sentence: Lower quality and less expensive materials can be used for subsoil and substratum layers.

d10f5b3a738b.title: Constructed soil
d10f5b3a738b.sentence: C: substratum (parent material | Drainage layer with high porosity and high density (sand or gravel); no organic matter; thickness determined by drainage requirements

3c2aa7f36a96.title: Constructed soil
3c2aa7f36a96.sentence: Abrupt differences in soil properties at horizon boundaries (namely texture and bulk density) impacts the hydraulic functioning of a soil, determining the extent of lateral versus vertical flow and the presence of perched water in the soil.

a1fa060825ed.title: Constructed soil
a1fa060825ed.sentence: Constructed soils generally consist of three components: a mineral fraction, organic fraction, and carbon source.

ad1c1e30cd0e.title: Constructed soil
ad1c1e30cd0e.section: Components of constructed soils > Mineral fraction
ad1c1e30cd0e.sentence: The mineral fraction forms the matrix of the soil, determining the final texture (relative percentages of sand, silt, and clay).

455bd19a49d7.title: Constructed soil
455bd19a49d7.section: Components of constructed soils > Organic fraction
455bd19a49d7.sentence: It is necessary to provide essential macronutrients and micronutrients to plants and soil organisms.

633135d98b90.title: Constructed soil
633135d98b90.section: Components of constructed soils > Carbon fraction
633135d98b90.sentence: In constructed soils, the carbon source is distinguished from the organic component as it is made up of materials that will decompose slowly, providing organic matter over time.

d1d413ff344d.title: Constructed soil
d1d413ff344d.section: Components of constructed soils > Carbon fraction
d1d413ff344d.sentence: sand silt clay gravel | compost peat manure biosolids | sawdust wood pulp wood chips tree bark biochar straw

f1f9ddc1c204.title: Constructed soil
f1f9ddc1c204.section: Components of constructed soils > Organic fraction
f1f9ddc1c204.sentence: In topsoil, organic matter should not exceed 15% by weight, or approximately one-third of soil particles.

d644b18d0f13.title: Constructed soil
d644b18d0f13.section: Components of constructed soils > Organic fraction
d644b18d0f13.sentence: Above this limit, the soil will become prone to settlement, consolidation, and waterlogging.

83c8376bbe03.title: Constructed soil
83c8376bbe03.section: Components of constructed soils > Carbon fraction
83c8376bbe03.sentence: A moderate carbon-to-nitrogen ratio (C:N ~ 20:1) will keep this rate at a level that provides a sustained release of nutrients into the soil.

16b76f8ba61f.title: Constructed soil
16b76f8ba61f.sentence: However, constructed soils do not typically include this factor in the development of soil mixtures.

086028745014.title: Constructed soil
086028745014.sentence: It is expected that biotic processes will initiate themselves as a site revegetates and soil formation (pedogenesis) begins.

9b097f89bffe.title: Constructed soil
9b097f89bffe.sentence: Biotic processes are critical in the aggregation of soil particles and development of stable soil structure, something which constructed soils typically lack.

20bcdf43d50a.title: Constructed soil
20bcdf43d50a.sentence: Where applicable, constructed soils must meet regulatory requirements dictating the acceptable thresholds of certain soil characteristics.

fddce4d666b4.title: Constructed soil
fddce4d666b4.sentence: Pathogens, harmful trace elements, salinity, and pH must be at values that are not harmful to human or environmental health.

149be38e6e27.title: Latosol
149be38e6e27.sentence: Latosols, also known as tropical red earth, are soils found under tropical rainforests which have a relatively high content of iron and aluminium oxides.

fdd32e9eaa28.title: Latosol
fdd32e9eaa28.sentence: They are typically classified as oxisols (USDA soil taxonomy) or ferralsols (World Reference Base for Soil Resources).

3dddc676a9c7.title: Latosol
3dddc676a9c7.sentence: Latosols are red or yellowish-red in colour throughout and they do not have distinct horizons like a podsol.

d8d8a8464276.title: Latosol
d8d8a8464276.sentence: The red colour comes from the iron oxides in the soil.

f3606e3dfe61.title: Latosol
f3606e3dfe61.sentence: They are deep soils, often extending 20–30 m (66–98 ft) deep whereas podsols are 1–2 m (3 ft 3 in – 6 ft 7 in) deep.

fbb6346b612d.title: Latosol
fbb6346b612d.sentence: The soil generally contains a thin but very fertile layer of humus dropped from plants and animals in the forest above, followed by an infertile second layer due to rapid leaching caused by high rainfall.

c95d1507696a.title: Latosol
c95d1507696a.sentence: The latosol is completely reliant on the rainforest to maintain fertility, as all nutrients leach away quickly when the forest is felled and the layer of humus is no longer being replaced.

e8d0f4094bee.title: Gumbo (soil)
e8d0f4094bee.sentence: Gumbo soil is typically defined by the overwhelming presence of very fine particles of clay, but often has small amounts of sand and/or organic material.

78795a70facc.title: Gumbo (soil)
78795a70facc.sentence: Although gumbo soils are exceptional at water retention, they can be difficult to farm, as precipitation will turn gumbo into a unique muddy mess that is challenging to work using large commercial farming equipment.

dc1dbba33e94.title: Gumbo (soil)
dc1dbba33e94.sentence: Avoiding tillage of this type of soil through no-till farming appears strongly correlated with higher yields, as compared to more traditional tilling practices.

0fd3cde9dcb2.title: Mesotrophic soil
0fd3cde9dcb2.sentence: Mesotrophic soils are soils with a moderate inherent fertility compared to eutrophic and oligotrophic soils.

52c52fda4885.title: Mesotrophic soil
52c52fda4885.sentence: An indicator of soil fertility is its base status, which is expressed as a ratio relating the major nutrient cations (calcium, magnesium, potassium and sodium) found there to the soil's clay percentage.

db347fca5d71.title: Mesotrophic soil
db347fca5d71.sentence: This is commonly expressed in hundredths of a mole of cations per kilogram of clay, i.e. cmol (+) kg−1 clay.

33adc402eb2d.title: Acrotelm
33adc402eb2d.sentence: The acrotelm is one of two distinct layers in undisturbed peat bogs.

bf7ef6d25300.title: Acrotelm
bf7ef6d25300.sentence: The boundary between the two layers is defined by the transition from peat containing living plants (acrotelm) to peat containing dead plant material (catotelm).

8bbc9d26494c.title: Acrotelm
8bbc9d26494c.sentence: This typically coincides with the lowest level of the water table.

3c8bf1293f78.title: Acrotelm
3c8bf1293f78.sentence: Fluctuations in the position of the water table in a peat bog occur within the acrotelm, and hence conditions may vary from aerobic to anaerobic with time.

039532703d1a.title: Acrotelm
039532703d1a.sentence: In general, the acrotelm has a higher hydraulic conductivity and a lower bulk density than the catotelm.

ce8874cf7dcc.title: Acrotelm
ce8874cf7dcc.sentence: After ditching, the acrotelm becomes thicker and more effective, drying the peat and simplifying harvesting.

1bede420781e.title: Acrotelm
1bede420781e.sentence: Drainage and subsidence lower the elevation of the peat surface, significantly lowering the soil's hydraulic conductivity.

9073a92f51ab.title: Acrotelm
9073a92f51ab.section: Mined peatlands > Importance of atmospheric deposition
9073a92f51ab.sentence: Completely developed acrotelm, only found in ombrotrophic bogs, make it possible to study atmospheric deposition and how it affects ecosystems.

ff424b47d312.title: Dry quicksand

61b77ce10853.title: Soil fertility

72f71f8540ff.title: Soil fertility

e414a6f7964f.title: Soil fertility

e6ec0ef12cea.title: Soil fertility

c9e95476cd1b.title: Soil fertility

f4c16c501fe9.title: Soil fertility

b7d938559340.title: Nutrient management
b7d938559340.sentence: Nutrient management is the science and practice directed to link soil, crop, weather, and hydrologic factors with cultural, irrigation, and soil and water conservation practices to achieve optimal nutrient use efficiency, crop yields, crop quality, and economic returns, while reducing off-site transport of nutrients (fertilizer) that may impact the environment.

c0dc1a319d24.title: Nutrient management
c0dc1a319d24.sentence: It involves matching a specific field soil, climate, and crop management conditions to rate, source, timing, and place (commonly known as the 4R nutrient stewardship) of nutrient application.

eaa7f42e29a6.title: Nutrient management
eaa7f42e29a6.sentence: Important factors that need to be considered when managing nutrients include (a) the application of nutrients considering the achievable optimum yields and, in some cases, crop quality; (b) the management, application, and timing of nutrients using a budget based on all sources and sinks active at the site; and (c) the management of soil, water, and crop to minimize the off-site transport of nutrients from nutrient leaching out of the root zone, surface runoff, and volatilization (or other gas exchanges).

8588c731a85b.title: Nutrient management
8588c731a85b.sentence: There can be potential interactions because of differences in nutrient pathways and dynamics.

1a83a99a9248.title: Nutrient management

5140e9317e8e.title: Nutrient management

cf1d5f681684.title: Nutrient management
cf1d5f681684.sentence: The manual outlines the scientific principles behind each of the four Rs or "rights" (right source of nutrient, right application rate, right time, right place) and discusses the adoption of 4R practices on the farm, approaches to nutrient management planning, and measurement of sustainability performance.

c20c511c6d45.title: Climate change mitigation

4a5b6937df69.title: Liebig's law of the minimum
4a5b6937df69.sentence: It states that growth is dictated not by total resources available, but by the scarcest resource (limiting factor).

f7f248d461fd.title: Liebig's law of the minimum
f7f248d461fd.sentence: Liebig's law of the minimum, often simply called Liebig's law or the law of the minimum, is a principle developed in agricultural science by Carl Sprengel (1840) and later popularized by Justus von Liebig.

3995d56b3b21.title: Justus von Liebig
3995d56b3b21.sentence: Liebig also popularized Carl Sprengel's "theorem of minimum" (known as the law of the minimum), stating that plant growth is not determined by the total resources available, but by the scarcest available resource.

96874cbd111c.title: Liebig's law of the minimum
96874cbd111c.sentence: This was originally applied to plant or crop growth, where it was found that increasing the amount of plentiful nutrients did not increase plant growth.

c68aa2a55bce.title: Liebig's law of the minimum
c68aa2a55bce.sentence: Only by increasing the amount of the limiting nutrient (the one most scarce in relation to "need") was the growth of a plant or crop improved.

66efacafba12.title: Liebig's law of the minimum
66efacafba12.sentence: Liebig's law has been extended to biological populations (and is commonly used in ecosystem modelling).

a68b919c43ed.title: Liebig's law of the minimum
a68b919c43ed.sentence: For example, the growth of an organism such as a plant may be dependent on a number of different factors, such as sunlight or mineral nutrients (e.g., nitrate or phosphate).

8b7c167d772d.title: Liebig's law of the minimum
8b7c167d772d.sentence: For instance, it has been shown that in coastal upwelling zones, where macronutrients like phosphorus and nitrogen are abundant due to ocean circulation patterns and terrestrial runoff, iron can be limiting.

e64dc634c2ed.title: Liebig's law of the minimum
e64dc634c2ed.sentence: Additionally, in open ocean environments, where there are very few nutrients, macronutrients like phosphorus and nitrogen can be limiting.

fe0969e44971.title: Liebig's law of the minimum
fe0969e44971.sentence: This principle can be summed up in the aphorism, "The availability of the most abundant nutrient in the soil is only as good as the availability of the least abundant nutrient in the soil." Or the rough analog, "A chain is only as strong as its weakest link." Though diagnosis of limiting factors to crop yields is a common study, the approach has been criticized.

af4e5f9ee629.title: Plant nutrition
af4e5f9ee629.sentence: During recent decades the nearly two-century-old "law of minimum" or "Liebig's law" (that states that plant growth is controlled not by the total amount of resources available, but by the scarcest resource) has been replaced by several mathematical approaches that use different models in order to take the interactions between the individual nutrients into account.

f9d9bddff786.title: Liebig's law of the minimum
f9d9bddff786.sentence: More recently Liebig's law is starting to find an application in natural resource management where it surmises that growth in markets dependent upon natural resource inputs is restricted by the most limited input.

2acbcf5c0f87.title: Liebig's law of the minimum
2acbcf5c0f87.sentence: For example, Isaac Asimov noted, "We may be able to substitute nuclear power for coal power, and plastics for wood... but for phosphorus there is neither substitute nor replacement."

ac0e407e0aa4.title: Liebig's law of the minimum
ac0e407e0aa4.sentence: Where no substitutes exist, such as phosphorus, recycling will be necessary.

f1b0f11b7f6a.title: Limiting factor
f1b0f11b7f6a.sentence: In 1905 Frederick Blackman articulated the role of limiting factors as follows: "When a process is conditioned as to its rapidity by several separate factors the rate of the process is limited by the pace of the slowest factor." In terms of the magnitude of a function, he wrote, "When the magnitude of a function is limited by one of a set of possible factors, increase of that factor, and of that one alone, will be found to bring about an increase of the magnitude of the function." Application of the notion of limiting factors to agriculture in the nineteenth century was the work of Carl Sprengel and Justus von Liebig.

dc38c4a8f5c6.title: Limiting factor
dc38c4a8f5c6.sentence: Disciplines differ in their use of the term as to whether they allow the simultaneous existence of more than one limiting factor (which may then be called "co-limiting"), but they all require the existence of at least one non-limiting factor when the terms are used.

608a65890495.title: Plant nutrition
608a65890495.sentence: In relatively large amounts, the soil supplies nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, calcium, magnesium, and sulfur; these are often called the macronutrients.

4d364e9a9324.title: Plant nutrition

b4b2c5e63f94.title: Plant nutrition
b4b2c5e63f94.sentence: The macronutrients are taken up in larger quantities; hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen and carbon contribute to over 95% of a plant's entire biomass on a dry matter weight basis.

937d6e4b59bd.title: Plant nutrition
937d6e4b59bd.sentence: Micronutrients are present in plant tissue in quantities measured in parts per million, ranging from 0.1 to 200 ppm, or less than 0.02% dry weight.

806541096d73.title: Plant nutrition
806541096d73.sentence: - The micronutrients (or trace minerals): iron (Fe), boron (B), chlorine (Cl), manganese (Mn), zinc (Zn), copper (Cu), molybdenum (Mo), nickel (Ni)

b0c689426a9b.title: Plant nutrients in soil

bea806cf5246.title: Nutrient
bea806cf5246.sentence: In addition to carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen, nitrogen, phosphorus, and sulfur are also needed in relatively large quantities.

378d43a51a0c.title: Nutrient
378d43a51a0c.sentence: Together, these six are the elemental macronutrients for all organisms.

a64e565d299a.title: Soil fertility
a64e565d299a.sentence: Nitrogen and potassium are also needed in substantial amounts.

01000ff56507.title: Soil fertility
01000ff56507.sentence: For this reason these three elements are always identified on a commercial fertilizer analysis.

6ad547e6eeff.title: Soil fertility
6ad547e6eeff.sentence: Inorganic fertilizers are generally less labour intensive and have higher concentrations of nutrients than organic fertilizers.

c9ab871716e4.title: Soil fertility
c9ab871716e4.sentence: Also, since nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium generally must be in the inorganic forms to be taken up by plants, inorganic fertilizers are generally immediately bioavailable to plants without modification.

33c932544d1a.title: Soil fertility
33c932544d1a.sentence: As for the environment, over-reliance on inorganic fertilizers disrupts the natural nutrient balance in the soil, resulting in lower soil quality, loss of organic matter, and higher chances for erosion in the soil.

d93b0c68215c.title: Soil fertility
d93b0c68215c.sentence: Additionally, the water-soluble nitrate nitrogen in inorganic fertilizers does not provide for the long-term needs of the plant and creates water pollution.

b79889fa3136.title: Soil fertility
