680d5f8c6fbe.title: Micronutrient
680d5f8c6fbe.sentence: Micronutrients are essential chemicals required by organisms in small quantities to perform various biogeochemical processes and regulate physiological functions of cells and organs.

b06eec8bc180.title: Plant nutrients in soil
b06eec8bc180.sentence: They are required in very small amounts but are essential to plant health in that most are required parts of enzyme systems which are involved in plant metabolism.

a9534bb8da34.title: Plant nutrients in soil
a9534bb8da34.sentence: The micronutrients essential in plant life, in their order of importance, include chlorine, iron, manganese, boron, zinc, copper, and molybdenum.

36d5fda2fa46.title: Micronutrient
36d5fda2fa46.sentence: In fact, every process that supports the growth of a plant is mediated by some protein which contains one of the many micronutrients.

180ea94245c9.title: Micronutrient
180ea94245c9.sentence: For example, Mn is an essential micronutrient for many plants because it builds the structure of photosystem II which splits water molecules to harness energy from electrons.

97e4915b424a.title: Plant nutrition
97e4915b424a.sentence: It is involved in many enzyme processes; necessary for proper photosynthesis; involved in the manufacture of lignin (cell walls) and involved in grain production.

282a73aea193.title: Plant nutrition
282a73aea193.sentence: Manganese is necessary for photosynthesis, including the building of chloroplasts.

512f6b8f8233.title: Plant nutrition
512f6b8f8233.sentence: Chlorine, as compounded chloride, is necessary for osmosis and ionic balance; it also plays a role in photosynthesis.

c5772097ce43.title: Plant nutrition
c5772097ce43.sentence: Nickel is essential for activation of urease, an enzyme involved with nitrogen metabolism that is required to process urea.

f59e4973bd1a.title: Plant nutrition
f59e4973bd1a.sentence: Without nickel, toxic levels of urea accumulate, leading to the formation of necrotic lesions.

7c241a9a34e7.title: Plant nutrition
7c241a9a34e7.sentence: Molybdenum is part of the nitrate reductase enzyme (needed for the reduction of nitrate) and the nitrogenase enzyme (required for biological nitrogen fixation).

8378473561c4.title: Micronutrient
8378473561c4.section: Sources and transport of micronutrients > Natural cycling
8378473561c4.sentence: The original source of most nutrients, including micronutrients, is the geological reservoir, also called the slow pool.

a5fb860f8f69.title: Micronutrient
a5fb860f8f69.section: Sources and transport of micronutrients > Natural cycling
a5fb860f8f69.sentence: Micronutrients trapped in rocks and minerals must first be broken down through physical or chemical weathering before they can enter the fast pool, meaning they cycle between reservoirs on shorter timescales.

2794fa85b504.title: Plant nutrients in soil
2794fa85b504.sentence: They are generally available in the mineral component of the soil, but the heavy application of phosphates can cause a deficiency in zinc and iron by the formation of insoluble zinc and iron phosphates.

c72c852f58ae.title: Micronutrient
c72c852f58ae.sentence: Inadequate micronutrient uptake can result in deficiencies and even mortality in extreme cases.

2d1554014dd4.title: Micronutrient
2d1554014dd4.sentence: A lack in copper, iron, manganese, or zinc can cause chlorosis.

741477519a80.title: Micronutrient
741477519a80.sentence: Alternatively, elevated concentrations of micronutrients in soils can result in toxicity.

9bee437182d2.title: Plant nutrition
9bee437182d2.sentence: Some micronutrients can be applied as seed coatings.

82f9ee12380b.title: Plant nutrition
82f9ee12380b.sentence: Acidifying N fertilizers create micro-sites around the granule that keep micronutrient cations soluble for longer in alkaline soils, but high concentrations of P or C may negate these effects.

f4882255f57d.title: Plant nutrition
f4882255f57d.sentence: Nutrients can be moved in plants to where they are most needed.

04824a13cad6.title: Plant nutrition
04824a13cad6.sentence: However, not all nutrients are equally mobile.

0301bb601306.title: Plant nutrition
0301bb601306.sentence: For example, a plant will try to supply more nutrients to its younger leaves than to its older ones.

0dd78d07ab5e.title: Plant nutrition
0dd78d07ab5e.sentence: Nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium are mobile nutrients while the others have varying degrees of mobility.

ba90c2ed7379.title: Plant nutrition
ba90c2ed7379.sentence: When nutrients are mobile in the plant, symptoms of any deficiency become apparent first on the older leaves.

63a8a76b2fbd.title: Plant nutrition
63a8a76b2fbd.sentence: Magnesium is very mobile in plants, and, like potassium, when deficient is translocated from older to younger tissues, so that signs of deficiency appear first on the oldest tissues and then spread progressively to younger tissues.

ebf3e9b82b12.title: Plant nutrition
ebf3e9b82b12.sentence: Nitrogen is transported via the xylem from the roots to the leaf canopy as nitrate ions, or in an organic form, such as amino acids or amides.

6853cb744ae6.title: Plant nutrition
6853cb744ae6.sentence: Nitrogen can also be transported in the phloem sap as amides, amino acids and ureides; it is therefore mobile within the plant, and the older leaves exhibit chlorosis and necrosis earlier than the younger leaves.

bbd48ea4b448.title: Plant nutrition
bbd48ea4b448.sentence: Because calcium is phloem immobile, calcium deficiency can be seen in new growth.

047834063fe7.title: Plant nutrition
047834063fe7.sentence: When developing tissues are forced to rely on the xylem, calcium is supplied by transpiration only.

1ca064057374.title: Plant nutrition
1ca064057374.sentence: Boron is not relocatable in the plant via the phloem.

322e6e847e87.title: Plant nutrition
322e6e847e87.sentence: In plants, sulfur cannot be mobilized from older leaves for new growth, so deficiency symptoms are seen in the youngest tissues first.

6e00a4ffca00.title: Plant nutrition
6e00a4ffca00.sentence: When a less-mobile nutrient is deficient, the younger leaves suffer because the nutrient does not move up to them but stays in the older leaves.

8a65510e64a7.title: Plant nutrition
8a65510e64a7.sentence: This phenomenon is helpful in determining which nutrients a plant may be lacking.

00bec8aa91d9.title: Plant nutrition
00bec8aa91d9.sentence: The effect of a nutrient deficiency can vary from a subtle depression of growth rate to obvious stunting, deformity, discoloration, distress, and even death.

dfaac8947bb0.title: Plant nutrition
dfaac8947bb0.sentence: Visual symptoms distinctive enough to be useful in identifying a deficiency are rare.

43276406aa08.title: Plant nutrition
43276406aa08.sentence: Most deficiencies are multiple and moderate.

09de80240ccc.title: Plant nutrition
09de80240ccc.sentence: However, while a deficiency is seldom that of a single nutrient, nitrogen is commonly the nutrient in shortest supply.

fe719420e731.title: Plant nutrition
fe719420e731.sentence: Nitrogen deficiency most often results in stunted growth, slow growth, and chlorosis.

8da1a200d2c3.title: Plant nutrition
8da1a200d2c3.sentence: Nitrogen deficient plants will also exhibit a purple appearance on the stems, petioles and underside of leaves from an accumulation of anthocyanin pigments.

bf6ea8594412.title: Plant nutrition
bf6ea8594412.sentence: As noted by Russel: "Phosphate deficiency differs from nitrogen deficiency in being extremely difficult to diagnose, and crops can be suffering from extreme starvation without there being any obvious signs that lack of phosphate is the cause".

55941cfac195.title: Plant nutrition
55941cfac195.sentence: Phosphorus deficiency can produce symptoms similar to those of nitrogen deficiency, characterized by an intense green coloration or reddening in leaves due to lack of chlorophyll.

677977980155.title: Plant nutrition
677977980155.sentence: Occasionally the leaves may appear purple from an accumulation of anthocyanin.

a16667a68986.title: Plant nutrition
a16667a68986.section: Functions of nutrients > Macronutrients (secondary and tertiary) > Calcium
a16667a68986.sentence: A notable feature of calcium-deficient plants is a defective root system.

352b41521a5e.title: Plant nutrition
352b41521a5e.sentence: Calcium deficiency may arise in tissues that are fed by the phloem, causing blossom end rot in watermelons, peppers and tomatoes, empty peanut pods and bitter pits in apples.

0f0b5fc9abff.title: Plant nutrition
0f0b5fc9abff.sentence: In enclosed tissues, calcium deficiency can cause celery black heart and "brown heart" in greens like escarole.

5a8234be676f.title: Plant nutrition
5a8234be676f.sentence: Potassium deficiency may cause necrosis or interveinal chlorosis.

cf0688cf61db.title: Plant nutrition
cf0688cf61db.sentence: Deficiency may result in higher risk of pathogens, wilting, chlorosis, brown spotting, and higher chances of damage from frost and heat.

13e37f3f23f1.title: Plant nutrition
13e37f3f23f1.sentence: When potassium is moderately deficient, the effects first appear in the older tissues, and from there progress towards the growing points.

e87bd7d2f76f.title: Plant nutrition
e87bd7d2f76f.sentence: Fe, Mn and Cu effect new growth, causing green or yellow veins, Zn can effect old and new leaves, and B will be seem on terminal buds.

d0ad7ea7f0c6.title: Plant nutrition
d0ad7ea7f0c6.sentence: Mo deficiency is usually found on older growth.

910869b33357.title: Plant nutrition
910869b33357.sentence: Chlorosis of foliage is not always due to mineral nutrient deficiency.

a68568c34764.title: Plant nutrition
a68568c34764.sentence: Solarization can produce superficially similar effects, though mineral deficiency tends to cause premature defoliation, whereas solarization does not, nor does solarization depress nitrogen concentration.

6fae79f57620.title: Molybdenum deficiency (plant disorder)
6fae79f57620.sentence: Molybdenum (Mo) deficiency occurs when plant growth is limited because the plant cannot take up sufficient quantities of this essential micronutrient from its growing medium.

62f914c913a0.title: Molybdenum deficiency (plant disorder)
62f914c913a0.sentence: Symptoms are most common where both conditions apply, such as in acid sandy soils.

ac8c3b3387b2.title: Molybdenum deficiency (plant disorder)
ac8c3b3387b2.sentence: In plants, Mo is essential for several enzymes including:

d7d437d0958e.title: Molybdenum deficiency (plant disorder)
d7d437d0958e.sentence: - Nitrogenase, which is required for biological N2 fixation by both asymbiotic and symbiotic nitrogen-fixing bacteria;

b421c73a50e3.title: Molybdenum deficiency (plant disorder)
b421c73a50e3.sentence: - Nitrate reductase, which is required for the reduction of nitrate – this is necessary for the incorporation of nitrate-N in proteins; and

4e905ed23cac.title: Molybdenum deficiency (plant disorder)
4e905ed23cac.sentence: - Xanthine dehydrogenase, which is involved in the synthesis of uric acid from purines.

2e39d3023c5d.title: Molybdenum deficiency (plant disorder)
2e39d3023c5d.sentence: Molybdenum deficiency symptoms in most plants are associated with a build-up of nitrate in the affected plant part.

a0424289d2ce.title: Molybdenum deficiency (plant disorder)
a0424289d2ce.sentence: In legumes, inhibition of N2 fixation may lead to pale, yellowing, nitrogen-deficient plants.

aaa2189953dc.title: Molybdenum deficiency (plant disorder)
aaa2189953dc.sentence: - pale leaves with interveinal and marginal chlorosis (yellowing) and necrosis (scald);

698cca229dd9.title: Molybdenum deficiency (plant disorder)
698cca229dd9.sentence: - the whiptail disorder in Brassica crops (especially cauliflower);

85f8b5cea885.title: Molybdenum deficiency (plant disorder)
85f8b5cea885.sentence: Although Mo requirements vary among crops, Mo leaf concentrations (on a dry matter basis) in the range 0.2–2.0 mg kg−1 are adequate for most crops.

8b1f9b0762df.title: Molybdenum deficiency (plant disorder)
8b1f9b0762df.sentence: In many situations, however, a soil-, seed- or foliar application of a Mo fertilizer is far more cost-effective than the use of lime to increase Mo availability.

64e48b7215c4.title: Molybdenum deficiency (plant disorder)
64e48b7215c4.sentence: Sodium molybdate is a typical source of Mo.

d1ec22f81282.title: Plant nutrients in soil
d1ec22f81282.sentence: Nitrogen is the most critical element obtained by plants from the soil, to the exception of moist tropical forests (tropical rainforests) where phosphorus is the limiting soil nutrient, and nitrogen deficiency often limits plant growth through decreased photosynthetic rate.

d2e620db2d33.title: Plant nutrients in soil
d2e620db2d33.sentence: Plants can use nitrogen as either the ammonium cation (NH4+) or the anion nitrate (NO3−).

34ce5c4120a3.title: Plant nutrition
34ce5c4120a3.sentence: For example, nitrogen compounds comprise 40% to 50% of the dry matter of protoplasm, and it is a constituent of amino acids, the building blocks of proteins.

172f460fad70.title: Plant nutrition
172f460fad70.sentence: It is also an essential constituent of chlorophyll.

804ee5a865ad.title: Plant nutrition
804ee5a865ad.sentence: In many agricultural settings, nitrogen is the limiting nutrient for rapid growth.

f6c6125cf598.title: Plant nutrition
f6c6125cf598.sentence: There is an abundant supply of nitrogen in the earth's atmosphere—N2 gas comprises nearly 79% of air.

3d44c79bb8cc.title: Plant nutrition
3d44c79bb8cc.sentence: However, N2 is unavailable for use by most organisms because there is a triple bond between the two nitrogen atoms in the molecule, making it almost inert.

16e8080cd5a3.title: Plant nutrition
16e8080cd5a3.sentence: In order for nitrogen to be used for growth it must be "fixed" (combined) in the form of ammonium (NH+ 4) or nitrate (NO− 3) ions.

630b74ab01a5.title: Plant nutrients in soil
630b74ab01a5.sentence: Usually, most of the nitrogen in soil is bound within organic compounds that make up the soil organic matter, and must be mineralized to the ammonium or nitrate form before it can be taken up by most plants.

6831255eb5ee.title: Plant nutrients in soil
6831255eb5ee.sentence: However, symbiosis with mycorrhizal fungi allow plants to get access to the organic nitrogen pool where and when mineral forms of nitrogen are poorly available.

08431f9bb8d1.title: Plant nutrients in soil
08431f9bb8d1.sentence: Bacteria may on average add 50 kg nitrogen per hectare (net mineralization rate), and in an unfertilised field this is the most important source of usable nitrogen, corresponding roughly to 2% total soil nitrogen.

efca693eed95.title: Plant nutrients in soil
efca693eed95.sentence: It is estimated that such symbiotic bacteria in the root nodules of legumes add potentially 200 to 300 kilograms of nitrogen per hectare per year, which may be sufficient for the crop.

c86bbb4ac711.title: Plant nutrients in soil
c86bbb4ac711.sentence: Usually, grassland soils contain more soil nitrogen than forest soils, because of a higher turnover rate of grassland organic matter.

5f8abfe8e056.title: Plant nutrients in soil
5f8abfe8e056.sentence: Cultivation decreases soil nitrogen by exposing soil organic matter to decomposition by microorganisms, most losses being caused by denitrification, and soils under no-tillage maintain more soil nitrogen than tilled soils.

e6da67fbbb05.title: Plant nutrition
e6da67fbbb05.section: Availability and uptake > Solubility and soil pH
e6da67fbbb05.sentence: Most of the nitrogen taken up by plants is from the soil in the forms of NO− 3, although in acid environments such as boreal forests where nitrification is less likely to occur, ammonium NH+ 4 is more likely to be the dominating source of nitrogen.

a233d9d02340.title: Carbon-to-nitrogen ratio
a233d9d02340.sentence: A carbon-to-nitrogen ratio (C/N ratio or C:N ratio) is a ratio of the mass of carbon to that of nitrogen in organic residues.

c0a3fbda5c3f.title: Carbon-to-nitrogen ratio
c0a3fbda5c3f.sentence: In microbial communities like soil, the C:N ratio is a key indicator as it describes a balance between energetic foods (represented by carbon) and material to build protein with (represented by nitrogen).

89e5cad13401.title: Plant nutrients in soil
89e5cad13401.sentence: About 45% of a plant's dry mass is carbon; plant residues typically have a carbon to nitrogen ratio (C/N) of between 13:1 and 100:1.

4c9289ecc45d.title: Plant nutrients in soil
4c9289ecc45d.sentence: As long as the carbon to nitrogen ratio (C/N) of fresh residues in the soil is above 30:1, nitrogen will be in short supply for the nitrogen-rich microbal biomass (nitrogen deficiency), and other bacteria will uptake ammonium and to a lesser extent nitrate and incorporate them into their cells in the immobilization process.

3c814536b621.title: Plant nutrients in soil

29de5629b6b4.title: Carbon-to-nitrogen ratio

dad29c84b6a3.title: Carbon-to-nitrogen ratio

a20036b77780.title: Carbon-to-nitrogen ratio

50ece22a970e.title: Carbon-to-nitrogen ratio

2a933473c53b.title: Plant nutrients in soil
2a933473c53b.sentence: There are three basic mechanisms whereby nutrient ions dissolved in the soil solution are brought into contact with plant roots:

56a46ab60b3c.title: Plant nutrients in soil
56a46ab60b3c.sentence: To be taken up by a plant, a nutrient element must be located near the root surface; however, the supply of nutrients in contact with the root is rapidly depleted within a distance of ca. 2 mm.

5b2b7122bd26.title: Plant nutrients in soil
5b2b7122bd26.sentence: For the most part, nutrient ions must travel some distance in the soil solution to reach the root surface.

921f44b970d5.title: Plant nutrients in soil
921f44b970d5.sentence: This movement can take place by mass flow, as when dissolved nutrients are carried along with the soil water flowing toward a root that is actively drawing water from the soil.

5ea882356ca9.title: Plant nutrients in soil
5ea882356ca9.sentence: In this type of movement, the nutrient ions are somewhat analogous to leaves floating down a stream.

478d247087c1.title: Plant nutrients in soil
478d247087c1.sentence: The movement by mass flow requires the transpiration of water from the plant causing water and solution ions to also move toward the roots.

ac22ae395ca7.title: Plant nutrients in soil
ac22ae395ca7.sentence: In addition, nutrient ions continually move by diffusion from areas of greater concentration toward the nutrient-depleted areas of lower concentration around the root surface.

7eb2e66fb0f2.title: Plant nutrients in soil
7eb2e66fb0f2.sentence: That process is due to random motion, also called Brownian motion, of molecules within a gradient of decreasing concentration.

da13924871b6.title: Plant nutrients in soil
da13924871b6.sentence: By the mean of diffusion, plants can continue to take up nutrients even when transpiration stops following stomatal closure and thus mass flow is interrupted.

1c883bcb9094.title: Plant nutrients in soil
1c883bcb9094.sentence: Finally, root interception comes into play as roots continually grow into new, undepleted soil.

c84925db339e.title: Plant nutrients in soil
c84925db339e.sentence: Movement by root interception is slowest, being at the rate plants extend their roots.

fa128aaa24d2.title: Plant nutrients in soil
fa128aaa24d2.sentence: Table: Estimated relative importance of mass flow, diffusion and root interception as mechanisms in supplying plant nutrients to corn plant roots in soils

a7c546490570.title: Plant nutrients in soil
a7c546490570.sentence: In the above table, phosphorus and potassium nutrients move more by diffusion than they do by mass flow in the soil water solution, as they are rapidly taken up by the roots creating a concentration of almost zero near the roots (the plants cannot transpire enough water to draw more of those nutrients near the roots).

bc933abe7fdc.title: Plant nutrients in soil
bc933abe7fdc.sentence: Plants derive a large proportion of their anion nutrients from decomposing organic matter, which typically holds 90–95% of the soil nitrogen and sulfur and 20–75% of the soil phosphorus.

851375195525.title: Plant nutrients in soil
851375195525.sentence: Where crops are produced, the replenishment of nutrients in the soil must usually be augmented by the addition of fertilizer or organic matter.

503952c37b94.title: Plant nutrients in soil
503952c37b94.sentence: However, the rate at which plant roots remove nutrients may not cope with the rate at which they are replenished in the soil solution, stemming in nutrient limitation to plant growth.

609b86aeab7c.title: Plant nutrition
609b86aeab7c.sentence: Plants take up essential elements from the soil through their roots and from the air through their leaves.

f079d114842e.title: Plant nutrition
f079d114842e.sentence: The root, especially the root hair, a unique cell, is the essential organ for the uptake of nutrients.

cb3985fd9eb3.title: Plant nutrition
cb3985fd9eb3.sentence: Nutrient uptake in the soil is achieved by cation exchange, wherein root hairs pump hydrogen ions (H+) into the soil through proton pumps.

4c16c9195061.title: Plant nutrition
4c16c9195061.sentence: These hydrogen ions displace cations attached to negatively charged soil particles so that the cations are available for uptake by the root.

7a1bb5e8c74e.title: Plant nutrition
7a1bb5e8c74e.sentence: Nutrient ions are transported to the center of the root, the stele, in order for the nutrients to reach the conducting tissues, xylem and phloem.

7c78c72d7228.title: Plant nutrition
7c78c72d7228.sentence: The Casparian strip, a cell wall outside the stele but in the root, prevents passive flow of water and nutrients, helping to regulate the uptake of nutrients and water.

e9925334062e.title: Plant nutrition
e9925334062e.sentence: There are three fundamental ways plants uptake nutrients through the root:

d3b42c54e1c6.title: Plant nutrition
d3b42c54e1c6.sentence: - Simple diffusion occurs when a nonpolar molecule, such as O2, CO2, and NH3 follows a concentration gradient, moving passively through the cell lipid bilayer membrane without the use of transport proteins.

66f77e2b60e7.title: Plant nutrition
66f77e2b60e7.sentence: - Facilitated diffusion is the rapid movement of solutes or ions following a concentration gradient, facilitated by transport proteins.

78ab4b3fedeb.title: Plant nutrition
78ab4b3fedeb.sentence: - Active transport is the uptake by cells of ions or molecules against a concentration gradient; this requires an energy source, usually ATP, to power molecular pumps that move the ions or molecules through the membrane.

bf51bad24c79.title: Plant nutrients in soil
bf51bad24c79.sentence: Plants move ions out of their roots in an effort to move nutrients in from the soil, an exchange process which occurs in the root apoplast.

e490ebc611d4.title: Plant nutrients in soil
e490ebc611d4.sentence: Hydrogen H+ is exchanged for other cations, and carbonate (HCO3−) and hydroxide (OH−) anions are exchanged for nutrient anions.

904f1dac05e6.title: Plant nutrition

eeeb1bfbea46.title: Plant nutrients in soil
eeeb1bfbea46.sentence: Because nutrient uptake is an active metabolic process, conditions that inhibit root metabolism may also inhibit nutrient uptake.

02f3eb79b6a7.sentence: The C and N contents of feedstocks is generally known from lookup tables listing common types of feedstock.

5f4f8e34025a.sentence: The C:N ratio of mixed feedstocks is calculated by summing their C and N amounts together and dividing the two results.

dcf795f7ba63.title: Carbon-to-nitrogen ratio
dcf795f7ba63.sentence: In the analysis of sediments, C/N ratios are a proxy for paleoclimate research, having different uses whether the sediment cores are terrestrial-based or marine-based.

45b93ab3e328.title: Carbon-to-nitrogen ratio
45b93ab3e328.sentence: Therefore, the C/N ratio serves as a tool for understanding the sources of sedimentary organic matter, which can lead to information about the ecology, climate, and ocean circulation at different times in Earth's history.

875a8fae4087.title: Carbon-to-nitrogen ratio
875a8fae4087.sentence: C/N ratios in the range of 4-10:1 usually come from marine sources, whereas higher ratios are likely to come from a terrestrial source.

8400ebc20544.title: Carbon-to-nitrogen ratio
8400ebc20544.sentence: Vascular plants from terrestrial sources tend to have C/N ratios greater than 20.

4a9010939e8d.title: Carbon-to-nitrogen ratio
4a9010939e8d.sentence: The lack of cellulose, which has a chemical formula of (C6H10O5)n, and greater amount of proteins in algae versus vascular plants causes this significant difference in the C/N ratio.

d81deac40ed4.title: Carbon-to-nitrogen ratio

4c507a500a96.title: Carbon-to-nitrogen ratio

fb275146d4dc.title: Carbon-to-nitrogen ratio

40c0205391c8.sentence: Examples of devices that can be used to measure this ratio are the CHN analyzer and the continuous-flow isotope ratio mass spectrometer (CF-IRMS).

5cbdd94950db.title: Nutrient depletion
5cbdd94950db.sentence: Nutrient depletion is a form of resource depletion and refers to the loss of nutrients and micronutrients in a habitat or parts of the biosphere, most often the soil (soil depletion, soil degradation).

dc8bd3eea0e3.title: Nutrient depletion
dc8bd3eea0e3.sentence: The end result of nutrient depletion is nutrient deficiency, or the lack of key resources within a medium.

1fea71e5908b.title: Nutrient depletion
1fea71e5908b.sentence: The opposite effect is known as eutrophication or nutrient pollution.

cfebce2f1717.title: Nutrient depletion
cfebce2f1717.sentence: Both depletion and eutrophication lead to shifts in biodiversity and species abundance (usually a decline).

ff758d52150f.title: Nutrient depletion
ff758d52150f.sentence: However, nutrient depletion can also happen within organisms, as nutrients are usually the first link in the food chain.

dd0c448a07c5.title: Nutrient depletion
dd0c448a07c5.sentence: Thus, a loss of nutrients in a habitat will affect nutrient cycling and eventually the entire food chain.

aec72627a39e.title: Nutrient depletion
aec72627a39e.sentence: Nutrient depletion impacts humans through malnourishment and economic health.

0d9f977a94ef.title: Nutrient depletion
0d9f977a94ef.sentence: Using the same fertilizer and growing the same crop every year on the same land yields decreasing returns.

62bc3644362a.title: Nutrient depletion
62bc3644362a.sentence: Overfarming can turn fertile soil into barren land within a few years, creating land that cannot sustain life.

6ed6b58f2053.title: Iron deficiency (plant disorder)
6ed6b58f2053.sentence: Iron (Fe) deficiency is a plant disorder also known as "lime-induced chlorosis".

faa47bb798c2.title: Iron deficiency (plant disorder)
faa47bb798c2.sentence: Iron is needed to produce chlorophyll, hence its deficiency causes chlorosis.

f91d62048b20.title: Iron deficiency (plant disorder)
f91d62048b20.sentence: If soil iron concentration is high, in spite of this it can become unavailable for absorption if soil pH is higher than 6.5.

0ff24c0dd05a.title: Iron deficiency (plant disorder)
0ff24c0dd05a.sentence: Excess of elements such as manganese in the soil can interfere with plant iron uptake triggering iron deficiency.

52553a115b0d.title: Iron deficiency (plant disorder)
52553a115b0d.sentence: Yellowing (Chlorosis) occur in the newly emerging leaves instead of the older leaves and usually seen in the interveinal region.

a05a7d95d6d3.title: Iron deficiency (plant disorder)
a05a7d95d6d3.sentence: Chlorosis occurs in younger leaves because iron is not a mobile element, and as such, the younger leaves cannot draw iron from other areas of the plant.

2c9958f8376f.title: Iron deficiency (plant disorder)
2c9958f8376f.sentence: Any plant may be affected, but raspberries and pears are particularly susceptible, as well as most acid-loving plants such as azaleas and camellias.

d96185c60443.title: Iron deficiency (plant disorder)
d96185c60443.sentence: If the pH is over seven then consider soil remediation that will lower the pH toward the 6.5 - 7 range.

a0791fc96be7.title: Iron deficiency (plant disorder)
a0791fc96be7.sentence: i) adding compost, manure, peat or similar organic matter (warning.

cd912a8ca167.title: Iron deficiency (plant disorder)
cd912a8ca167.sentence: ii) applying Ammonium Sulphate as a Nitrogen fertilizer (acidifying fertilizer due to decomposition of ammonium ion to nitrate in the soil and root zone)

8260c89198c0.title: Iron deficiency (plant disorder)
8260c89198c0.sentence: iii) applying elemental Sulphur to the soil (oxidizes over the course of months to produce sulphate/sulphite and lower pH).

f3cf1584a2fa.title: Iron deficiency (plant disorder)
f3cf1584a2fa.sentence: Iron can be made available immediately to the plant by the use of iron sulphate or iron chelate compounds.

58599f26d524.title: Iron deficiency (plant disorder)
58599f26d524.sentence: Iron sulphate (Iron(II) sulfate) and iron EDTA are only useful in soil up to PH 7.1 but they can be used as a foliar spray (Foliar feeding).

51d38cfe666c.title: Mineral (nutrient)
51d38cfe666c.sentence: In the context of nutrition, a mineral is a chemical element.

59eb46704469.title: Mineral (nutrient)
59eb46704469.sentence: In fact, in nutrition, the term "mineral" refers more generally to all the other functional and structural elements found in living organisms.

9c9710b3780d.title: Mineral (nutrient)
9c9710b3780d.sentence: The four organogenic elements, namely carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, and nitrogen (CHON), that comprise roughly 96% of the human body by weight, are usually not considered as minerals (nutrient).

f2cd230d0788.title: Mineral (nutrient)
f2cd230d0788.sentence: Finally, although mineral and elements are in many ways synonymous, minerals are only bioavailable to the extent that they can be absorbed.

dc4e9516e3fe.title: Mineral (nutrient)
dc4e9516e3fe.sentence: To be absorbed, minerals either must be soluble or readily extractable by the consuming organism.

a1209b791fde.title: Mineral (nutrient)
a1209b791fde.sentence: For example, molybdenum is an essential mineral, but metallic molybdenum has no nutritional benefit.

00d640ae304b.title: Mineral (nutrient)
00d640ae304b.sentence: Many molybdates are sources of molybdenum.

cfd93741bdb7.title: Mineral (nutrient)
cfd93741bdb7.sentence: The list of minerals required for plants is similar to that for animals.

16c0ea69c8aa.title: Mineral (nutrient)
16c0ea69c8aa.sentence: Both use very similar enzymes, although differences exist.

cf8c55f466c1.title: Mineral (nutrient)
cf8c55f466c1.sentence: For example, legumes host molybdenum-containing nitrogenase, but animals do not.

74e705490bcc.title: Mineral (nutrient)
74e705490bcc.sentence: Many animals rely on hemoglobin (Fe) for oxygen transport, but plants do not.

ad04450ecd35.title: Mineral (nutrient)
ad04450ecd35.section: Elements considered possibly essential for humans but not confirmed
ad04450ecd35.sentence: Boron is essential to plants, but not humans, although depletion-repletion studies in humans showed benefits to bone and brain health.

04376861851b.title: Mineral (nutrient)
04376861851b.section: Elements considered possibly essential for humans but not confirmed
04376861851b.sentence: Silicon | Silicon is beneficial to most plants, but usually not essential. It seems to have beneficial effects in humans, strengthening bones and connective tissue, but these effects are still being studied. In any case deficiency symptoms do not arise because silicon occurs significantly in food made from plants.

977e5b86d91a.title: Mineral (nutrient)
977e5b86d91a.sentence: Fertilizers are often tailored to address mineral deficiencies in particular soils.

dd1d2dd2beaa.title: Mineral (nutrient)
dd1d2dd2beaa.sentence: Examples include molybdenum deficiency, manganese deficiency, zinc deficiency, and so on.

6f9927773037.title: Mineral (nutrient)
6f9927773037.section: Elements considered possibly essential for humans but not confirmed
6f9927773037.sentence: Definitive evidence for efficacy comes from the characterization of a biomolecule containing the element with an identifiable and testable function.

b8a83d4078b2.title: Mineral (nutrient)
b8a83d4078b2.section: Elements considered possibly essential for humans but not confirmed
b8a83d4078b2.sentence: Non-essential elements can sometimes appear in the body when they are chemically similar to essential elements (e.g. Rb+ and Cs+ replacing Na+), so that essentiality is not the same thing as uptake by a biological system.

ef7d263fb4e2.title: Chlorosis
ef7d263fb4e2.sentence: In botany, chlorosis is a condition in which leaves produce insufficient chlorophyll.

96b4ce34d91b.title: Chlorosis
96b4ce34d91b.sentence: As chlorophyll is responsible for the green color of leaves, chlorotic leaves are pale, yellow, or yellow-white.

6f3bfa51e74d.title: Chlorosis
6f3bfa51e74d.sentence: The affected plant has little or no ability to manufacture carbohydrates through photosynthesis and may die unless the cause of its chlorophyll insufficiency is treated and this may lead to a plant disease called rusts, although some chlorotic plants, such as the albino Arabidopsis thaliana mutant ppi2, are viable if supplied with exogenous sucrose.

ca4d8995a4e8.title: Chlorosis
ca4d8995a4e8.sentence: - a specific mineral deficiency in the soil, such as iron, magnesium or zinc

076a3873e7d9.title: Chlorosis
076a3873e7d9.sentence: - a soil pH at which minerals become unavailable for absorption by the roots

90e7de26dd6d.title: Chlorosis
90e7de26dd6d.sentence: In these soils the grapevine often struggles to pull sufficient levels of iron which is a needed component in the production of chlorophyll.

349e1732a439.title: Chlorosis
349e1732a439.sentence: However, many of these were less adapted to the lime-rich soils that were common in France's vineyards, in particular many of those that produced wines of top quality.

12ee14c6a004.title: Chlorosis
12ee14c6a004.sentence: Many grafted vines in lime-rich vineyards therefore showed signs of iron deficiency, and in France this specific form of chlorosis was termed chlorose calcaire.

72c144d4ae00.title: Chlorosis
72c144d4ae00.sentence: Specific nutrient deficiencies (often aggravated by high soil pH) may be corrected by supplemental feedings of iron, in the form of a chelate or sulphate, magnesium or nitrogen compounds in various combinations.

f54ea7ed49a7.title: Chlorosis

a01fb72edcf3.title: Chlorosis
a01fb72edcf3.sentence: Likewise, sulfur can be used to lower soil pH if it is too alkaline.

45e22eb1ba05.title: Plant nutrients in soil
45e22eb1ba05.sentence: Nutrients which enhance the health but whose deficiency does not stop the life cycle of plants include: cobalt, strontium, vanadium, silicon and nickel.

264ced5d5fc0.title: Plant nutrition
264ced5d5fc0.sentence: Silicon is not considered an essential element for plant growth and development.

ddcef381915e.title: Plant nutrition
ddcef381915e.sentence: In plants, silicon has been shown in experiments to strengthen cell walls, improve plant strength, health, and productivity.

909c79dee452.title: Plant nutrition
909c79dee452.sentence: There have been studies showing evidence of silicon improving drought and frost resistance, decreasing lodging potential and boosting the plant's natural pest and disease fighting systems.

d3ecd2637c99.title: Plant nutrition
d3ecd2637c99.sentence: Cobalt has proven to be beneficial to at least some plants although it does not appear to be essential for most species.

619e312ff5be.title: Plant nutrition
619e312ff5be.sentence: It has, however, been shown to be essential for nitrogen fixation by the nitrogen-fixing bacteria associated with legumes and other plants.

f0234e7109d8.title: Plant nutrition
f0234e7109d8.sentence: Sodium can potentially replace potassium's regulation of stomatal opening and closing.

481124d194e0.title: Plant nutrition
481124d194e0.sentence: - Essential for C4 plants rather C3

1c12bdaa532e.title: Plant nutrition
1c12bdaa532e.sentence: Selenium is probably not essential for flowering plants, but it can be beneficial; it can stimulate plant growth, improve tolerance of oxidative stress, and increase resistance to pathogens and herbivory.

d63774b8cb3e.title: Plant nutrition
d63774b8cb3e.section: Plant nutrition in agricultural systems > Fertilizers
d63774b8cb3e.sentence: Selenium is, however, an essential mineral element for animal (including human) nutrition and selenium deficiencies are known to occur when food or animal feed is grown on selenium-deficient soils.

df9894d357d9.title: Plant nutrition
df9894d357d9.section: Plant nutrition in agricultural systems > Fertilizers
df9894d357d9.sentence: The use of inorganic selenium fertilizers can increase selenium concentrations in edible crops and animal diets thereby improving animal health.

821ec0e6b2f3.title: Plant nutrition
821ec0e6b2f3.section: Functions of nutrients > Macronutrients (secondary and tertiary) > Calcium
821ec0e6b2f3.sentence: A major function is as a constituent of cell walls.

9c0126ec089d.title: Plant nutrients in soil
9c0126ec089d.sentence: Calcium is supplied to the plant in the form of exchangeable ions and moderately soluble minerals.

29cb96e6e1d7.title: Plant nutrients in soil
29cb96e6e1d7.sentence: Soil calcium can be in insoluble forms such as calcite, dolomite, in the soil solution in the form of a divalent cation or retained in exchangeable form at the surface of mineral and organic particles.

cb005508ca1c.title: Plant nutrients in soil
cb005508ca1c.sentence: Another main form is when calcium complexes with organic matter, forming covalent bonds between organic compounds which contribute to structural stability.

abb4fbfb0e4d.title: Plant nutrients in soil
abb4fbfb0e4d.sentence: Calcium is generally available but may be low as it is soluble and can be leached.

d0f2f3d6512f.title: Plant nutrients in soil
d0f2f3d6512f.sentence: It is thus low in sandy and heavily leached soil or strongly acidic mineral soils, resulting in excessive concentration of free hydrogen ions in the soil solution, and therefore these soils require liming.

8bbf54595dca.title: Plant nutrients in soil
8bbf54595dca.sentence: Calcium is more available on the soil colloids than is potassium because the common mineral calcite, CaCO3, is more soluble than potassium-bearing minerals such as feldspar.

5c5761e9c62b.title: Plant nutrients in soil
5c5761e9c62b.sentence: For example, in the case of calcium, which is generally plentiful in the soil solution, except when aluminium over competes calcium on cation exchange sites in very acid soils (pH less than 4), mass flow alone can usually bring sufficient amounts to the root surface.

98ba4f978019.title: Plant nutrition
98ba4f978019.section: Functions of nutrients > Macronutrients (secondary and tertiary) > Calcium
98ba4f978019.sentence: It is also intimately involved in meristems, and is particularly important in root development, with roles in cell division, cell elongation, and the detoxification of hydrogen ions.

f98fd89ec667.title: Plant nutrients in soil
f98fd89ec667.sentence: Calcium is considered as an essential component of plant cell membranes, a counterion for inorganic and organic anions in the vacuole, and an intracellular messenger in the cytosol, playing a role in cellular learning and memory.

05f0639cd663.title: Plant nutrients in soil
05f0639cd663.sentence: Plants obtain their carbon from atmospheric carbon dioxide through photosynthetic carboxylation, to which must be added the uptake of dissolved carbon from the soil solution and carbon transfer through mycorrhizal networks.

8fdef18daa3e.title: Plant nutrients in soil
8fdef18daa3e.sentence: Normal CO2 concentration in the atmosphere is 0.03%, this can be the factor limiting plant growth when no other factor like water or nutrient scarcity is involved.

51ad58a680bf.title: Soil fertility
51ad58a680bf.sentence: Peer-reviewed and published scientific studies have shown that increasing CO2 is highly effective at promoting plant growth up to levels over 300 ppm.

1b7bf3d29040.title: Plant nutrients in soil
1b7bf3d29040.sentence: Within the soil, CO2 concentration is 10 to 100 times that of atmospheric levels but may rise to toxic levels if the soil porosity is low or if diffusion is impeded by flooding.

82bd414ee595.title: Plant nutrition
82bd414ee595.section: Functions of nutrients > Macronutrients (secondary and tertiary) > Magnesium
82bd414ee595.sentence: The outstanding role of magnesium in plant nutrition is as a constituent of the chlorophyll molecule.

5d57d6617948.title: Plant nutrition
5d57d6617948.section: Functions of nutrients > Macronutrients (secondary and tertiary) > Magnesium
5d57d6617948.sentence: As a carrier, it is also involved in numerous enzyme reactions as an effective activator, in which it is closely associated with energy-supplying phosphorus compounds.

df4c7d482900.title: Plant nutrients in soil
df4c7d482900.sentence: Magnesium is one of the dominant exchangeable cations in most soils (after calcium and potassium).

122a82a6ff3a.title: Plant nutrients in soil
122a82a6ff3a.sentence: Primary minerals that weather to release magnesium include hornblende, biotite and vermiculite.

7b7ef0f880de.title: Plant nutrients in soil
7b7ef0f880de.sentence: Soil magnesium concentrations are generally sufficient for optimal plant growth, but highly weathered and sandy soils may be magnesium deficient due to leaching by heavy precipitation.

c5c74a21f79d.title: Plant nutrients in soil
c5c74a21f79d.sentence: Usable nitrogen may be lost from soils when it is in the form of nitrate, as it is easily leached, contrary to ammonium which is easily fixed.

9981cced4b15.title: Plant nutrients in soil
9981cced4b15.sentence: Further losses of nitrogen occur by denitrification, the process whereby soil bacteria convert nitrate (NO3−) to nitrogen gas, N2 or N2O.

78d08491c754.title: Plant nutrients in soil
78d08491c754.sentence: Ammonia volatilisation occurs when ammonium reacts chemically with an alkaline soil, converting NH4+ to NH3.

afcbfaf8feec.title: Plant nutrients in soil
afcbfaf8feec.sentence: Nitrogen may also be leached from the vadose zone if in the form of nitrate, acting as a pollutant if it reaches the water table or flows over land, more especially in agricultural soils under high use of nutrient fertilizers.

38de0cbe40d7.title: Plant nutrients in soil
38de0cbe40d7.sentence: Denitrification may cause the loss of 25 percent of the N applied on a heavy clay soil as fertilizer and manure.

d5b802e9c74e.title: Plant nutrients in soil
d5b802e9c74e.sentence: The application of ammonium fertiliser to such a field can result in volatilisation losses of as much as 87 percent.

737cb51651d5.title: Plant nutrients in soil
737cb51651d5.sentence: All kinds of nitrogen losses, whether by leaching or volatilization, are responsible for a large part of aquifer pollution and air pollution, with concomitant effects on soil acidification and eutrophication, a novel combination of environmental threats (acidity and excess nitrogen) to which extant organisms are badly adapted, causing severe biodiversity losses in natural ecosystems.

939249ff74e2.title: Nutrient management
939249ff74e2.section: Nitrogen management > Nitrogen management practices that improve nitrogen efficiency
939249ff74e2.sentence: Nitrogen management aims to maximize the efficiency with which crops use applied N. Improvements in nitrogen use efficiency are associated with decreases in N loss from the soil.

70398b1ef480.title: Nutrient management
70398b1ef480.sentence: Of the 16 essential plant nutrients, nitrogen is usually the most difficult to manage in field crop systems.

5ee2f0968403.title: Nutrient management
5ee2f0968403.sentence: This is because the quantity of plant-available nitrogen can change rapidly in response to changes in soil water status.

b00c46b0639b.title: Nutrient management
b00c46b0639b.sentence: Nitrogen can be lost from the plant-soil system by one or more of the following processes: leaching; surface runoff; soil erosion; ammonia volatilization; and denitrification.

4d4aebc265b4.title: Nutrient management
4d4aebc265b4.section: Nitrogen management > Reduction of greenhouse gas emissions > Prevention of the build-up of high soil nitrate concentrations
4d4aebc265b4.sentence: Nitrate is the form of nitrogen that is most susceptible to loss from the soil, through denitrification and leaching.

34f9f02665d2.title: Nutrient management
34f9f02665d2.section: Nitrogen management > Reduction of greenhouse gas emissions
34f9f02665d2.sentence: Through careful selection of nitrogen fertilizer source, rate, timing and placement practices, the nitrous oxide emissions per unit of crop produced can be substantially reduced, in some cases by up to half.

51185a47a903.title: Nutrient management
51185a47a903.section: Nitrogen management > Reduction of greenhouse gas emissions > Prevention of the build-up of high soil nitrate concentrations > Nitrogen rates
51185a47a903.sentence: - Fertilizer N rates should be corrected for N that is likely to be mineralized from soil organic matter and crop residues (especially legume residues).

0ac268a2cf9f.title: Nutrient management
0ac268a2cf9f.section: Nitrogen management > Reduction of greenhouse gas emissions > Prevention of the build-up of high soil nitrate concentrations > Nitrogen rates
0ac268a2cf9f.sentence: - Fertilizer N rates should allow for N applied in manure, in irrigation water, and from atmospheric deposition.

55d71f4974e3.title: Nutrient management
55d71f4974e3.section: Nitrogen management > Reduction of greenhouse gas emissions > Prevention of the build-up of high soil nitrate concentrations > Timing of N applications
55d71f4974e3.sentence: - Apply N close to the time when crops can utilize it.

b5eda001603a.title: Nutrient management
b5eda001603a.section: Nitrogen management > Reduction of greenhouse gas emissions > Prevention of the build-up of high soil nitrate concentrations > Timing of N applications
b5eda001603a.sentence: - Split applications, involving more than one application, allow efficient use of applied N and reduce the risk of N loss to the environment.

2f7dcee8f640.title: Nutrient management
2f7dcee8f640.section: Nitrogen management > Reduction of greenhouse gas emissions > Prevention of the build-up of high soil nitrate concentrations > N Forms, including slow or controlled release fertilizers and inhibitors
2f7dcee8f640.sentence: - Slow or controlled release fertilizer delays the availability of nitrogen to the plant until a time that is more appropriate for plant uptake - the risk of N loss through denitrification and leaching is reduced by limiting nitrate concentrations in the soil.

9043b2024ee6.title: Nutrient management
9043b2024ee6.section: Nitrogen management > Reduction of greenhouse gas emissions > Prevention of the build-up of high soil nitrate concentrations > N Forms, including slow or controlled release fertilizers and inhibitors
9043b2024ee6.sentence: - Nitrification inhibitors maintain applied N in the ammonium form for a longer period of time, thereby reducing leaching and denitrification losses.

027b3e02cfcb.title: Nutrient management
027b3e02cfcb.section: Nitrogen management > Reduction of greenhouse gas emissions > Reduction of the volatilization of N as ammonia gas
027b3e02cfcb.sentence: - Incorporation and/or injection of urea and ammonium-containing fertilizers decreases ammonia volatilization because good soil contact buffers pH and slows the generation of ammonia gas from ammonium ions.

da807dcd8244.title: Nutrient management
da807dcd8244.section: Nitrogen management > Reduction of greenhouse gas emissions > Reduction of the volatilization of N as ammonia gas
da807dcd8244.sentence: - Urease inhibitors temporarily block the function of the urease enzyme, maintaining urea-based fertilizers in the non-volatile urea form, reducing volatilization losses when these fertilizers are surface applied; these losses can be meaningful in high-residue, conservation tillage systems.

b8aba4baad2b.title: Nutrient management
b8aba4baad2b.section: Nitrogen management > Reduction of greenhouse gas emissions > Prevention of the build-up of high soil nitrate concentrations > N capture
b8aba4baad2b.sentence: - Cover crops capture residual nitrogen after crop harvest and recycle it as plant biomass.

61e0a65482d7.title: Nutrient management
61e0a65482d7.section: Nitrogen management > Reduction of greenhouse gas emissions > Prevention of the build-up of high soil nitrate concentrations > N capture
61e0a65482d7.sentence: - Rotation with deep-rooted crops helps capture nitrates deeper in the soil profile.

971b2f6a27b6.title: Nutrient management
971b2f6a27b6.section: Nitrogen management > Additional measures to minimize environmental impact > Conservation buffers
971b2f6a27b6.sentence: - Buffer vegetation takes up nitrogen, other nutrients, and reduces loss to water.

ac8ca3fc1b92.title: Nutrient management
ac8ca3fc1b92.section: Nitrogen management > Additional measures to minimize environmental impact > Constructed wetlands
ac8ca3fc1b92.sentence: - Constructed wetlands located strategically on the landscape to process drainage effluent reduces sediment and nitrate loads to surface water.

f69bee869d1d.title: Nutrient management
f69bee869d1d.section: Nitrogen management > Reduction of greenhouse gas emissions > Use of simulation models
f69bee869d1d.sentence: However, models (such as NLEAP and Adapt-N) that use soil, weather, crop, and field management data can be updated with day-to-day changes and thereby improve predictions of the fate of applied N. They allows farmers to make adaptive management decisions that can improve N-use efficiency and minimize N losses and environmental impact while maximizing profitability.

1510cd3835ae.title: Barren vegetation
1510cd3835ae.sentence: Barren vegetation describes an area of land where plant growth may be sparse, stunted, and/or contain limited biodiversity.

12c56c401946.title: Barren vegetation
12c56c401946.sentence: Environmental conditions such as toxic or infertile soil, high winds, coastal salt-spray, and climatic conditions are often key factors in poor plant growth and development.

4c4134055e0a.title: Barren vegetation
4c4134055e0a.sentence: Serpentine barrens are distinct due to the serpentine-rich soil produced by the hydration weathering and metamorphic transformation of ultramafic igneous bedrock.

9272edf9dfc7.title: Barren vegetation

4ede14ab2af2.title: Barren vegetation

5e62ad57b64c.title: Barren vegetation

4db2a96864a0.title: Barren vegetation

99dd2d9dbfff.title: Illinois Soil Nitrogen Test

2aa1622e0d46.title: Illinois Soil Nitrogen Test

fea4a671955a.title: Manganese deficiency (plant)

3c0a446667c0.title: Manganese deficiency (plant)

30a586f44595.title: Boron deficiency (plant disorder)
30a586f44595.sentence: Boron deficiency is a common deficiency of the micronutrient boron in plants.

770657ebdf02.title: Boron deficiency (plant disorder)
770657ebdf02.sentence: It is the most widespread micronutrient deficiency around the world and causes large losses in crop production and crop quality.

e1c02fd4aabd.title: Boron deficiency (plant disorder)
e1c02fd4aabd.sentence: Boron deficiency affects vegetative and reproductive growth of plants, resulting in inhibition of cell expansion, death of meristem, and reduced fertility.

bc9cd18f6f64.title: Boron deficiency (plant disorder)
bc9cd18f6f64.sentence: An adequate amount of boron in the soil is typically in a range of 0.5 to 1.0 mg/kg, with deficiency commonly observed below a threshold of 0.2 to 0.5 mg/kg depending on crop and soil type.

959d26c6a1ab.title: Boron deficiency (plant disorder)
959d26c6a1ab.sentence: Boron deficiency is also observed in basic soils with a high pH because in basic conditions boric acid exists in an undissociated form which the plant is unable to absorb.

160136b80359.title: Boron deficiency (plant disorder)

8a5963b7c402.title: Boron deficiency (plant disorder)
8a5963b7c402.sentence: Highly leached sandy soils are also characteristic of boron deficiency because the boron will not be retained in the soil.

9d93a2164a63.title: Boron deficiency (plant disorder)

2db995b2c97e.title: Boron deficiency (plant disorder)

63b2210f798f.title: Boron deficiency (plant disorder)

8af59e9553e9.title: Liebig's law of the minimum
8af59e9553e9.sentence: Dobenecks used the image of a barrel — often called "Liebig's barrel" — to explain Liebig's law.

2b9cf4700e86.title: Liebig's law of the minimum
2b9cf4700e86.sentence: Just as the maximum practical capacity of a barrel with staves of unequal length is limited by the length of the shortest stave.

2fbbea782da7.title: Liebig's law of the minimum
2fbbea782da7.sentence: Similarly, a plant's growth is limited by the nutrient in shortest supply.

aa718deee72e.title: Liebig's law of the minimum
aa718deee72e.sentence: Adaptation systems act as the cooper of Liebig's barrel and lengthens the shortest stave to improve barrel capacity.

76863c3fed75.title: Liebig's law of the minimum
76863c3fed75.sentence: Indeed, in well-adapted systems the limiting factor should be compensated as far as possible.

ab29faee66ce.title: Liebig's law of the minimum
ab29faee66ce.sentence: Due to the law of the minimum paradoxes, if we observe the Law of the Minimum in artificial systems, then under natural conditions adaptation will equalize the load of different factors and we can expect a violation of the law of the minimum.
