5e36157f2555.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/18%3A_Nutrient_Management/18.04%3A_Improving_Nutrient_Cycling_on_the_Farm
5e36157f2555.sentence: For economic and environmental reasons, it makes sense for plants to more efficiently utilize nutrient cycling on the farm.

17c34220f8cb.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/18%3A_Nutrient_Management/18.04%3A_Improving_Nutrient_Cycling_on_the_Farm
17c34220f8cb.sentence: Goals should include a reduction in long-distance nutrient flows, as well as the promotion of “true” on-farm cycling, in which nutrients return in the form of crop residue or manure to the fields from which they came.

22f88a474648.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/18%3A_Nutrient_Management/18.04%3A_Improving_Nutrient_Cycling_on_the_Farm
22f88a474648.sentence: - Reduce unintended losses by promoting water infiltration and better root health through enhanced management of soil organic matter and physical properties.

f0187b72b301.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/18%3A_Nutrient_Management/18.04%3A_Improving_Nutrient_Cycling_on_the_Farm
f0187b72b301.sentence: Proper irrigation water management involves applying the right amount of irrigation water needed to refill the root zone.

50787334f220.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/18%3A_Nutrient_Management/18.04%3A_Improving_Nutrient_Cycling_on_the_Farm
50787334f220.sentence: Applying excessive irrigation water can cause both runoff and leaching losses of nutrients.

5787fdc54dff.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/18%3A_Nutrient_Management/18.04%3A_Improving_Nutrient_Cycling_on_the_Farm
5787fdc54dff.sentence: (In arid climates occasional extra water applications will be needed to leach accumulating salts below the root zone.) In addition, compared to conventional annual row crops such as corn and soybeans, rotations that include cover crops and perennial grass and legume crops tend to result in less leaching loss of nitrate as well as runoff phosphorus loss.

7be4ade8c16a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/18%3A_Nutrient_Management/18.04%3A_Improving_Nutrient_Cycling_on_the_Farm
7be4ade8c16a.sentence: Test manures and credit their nutrient content before applying fertilizers or other amendments.

82cc5948b468.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/18%3A_Nutrient_Management/18.04%3A_Improving_Nutrient_Cycling_on_the_Farm
82cc5948b468.sentence: Test soils regularly to determine the nutrient status and whether or not manures, fertilizers or lime are needed.

fafaee31f880.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/18%3A_Nutrient_Management/18.04%3A_Improving_Nutrient_Cycling_on_the_Farm
fafaee31f880.sentence: Apply most nitrogen close to the time of crop uptake, and use recommendation tools that account for soil, weather and management practices.

49c1e08d7ba0.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/18%3A_Nutrient_Management/18.04%3A_Improving_Nutrient_Cycling_on_the_Farm
49c1e08d7ba0.sentence: Use forage legumes or legume cover crops to provide N to subsequent crops and to develop good soil structure.

8fbc1dca97fc.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/18%3A_Nutrient_Management/18.04%3A_Improving_Nutrient_Cycling_on_the_Farm
8fbc1dca97fc.sentence: Use cover crops to tie up nutrients during the off-season, enhance soil structure, reduce runoff and erosion, and provide microbes with fresh organic matter.

16970250b2fb.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/18%3A_Nutrient_Management/18.04%3A_Improving_Nutrient_Cycling_on_the_Farm
16970250b2fb.sentence: The best way to reduce nutrient exports per acre, as well as to make more use of forage legumes in rotations, is to add an animal (especially a ruminant) enterprise to a crop farm.

550ca0a8c820.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/18%3A_Nutrient_Management/18.04%3A_Improving_Nutrient_Cycling_on_the_Farm
550ca0a8c820.sentence: Compared with selling crops, feeding crops to animals and exporting animal products result in far fewer nutrients and carbon leaving the farm.

6db663f5a2a1.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/18%3A_Nutrient_Management/18.04%3A_Improving_Nutrient_Cycling_on_the_Farm
6db663f5a2a1.sentence: Keep in mind that, on the other hand, raising animals with mainly purchased feed overloads a farm with nutrients.

5bacc03713a8.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/18%3A_Nutrient_Management/18.04%3A_Improving_Nutrient_Cycling_on_the_Farm
5bacc03713a8.sentence: - Bring animal densities in line with the land base of the farm.

55dab3f7a43c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/18%3A_Nutrient_Management/18.04%3A_Improving_Nutrient_Cycling_on_the_Farm
55dab3f7a43c.sentence: - Tap local nutrient sources by seeking local organic materials, such as leaves or grass clippings from towns, aquatic weeds harvested from lakes, produce waste from markets and restaurants, food processing wastes and clean sewage sludges (see discussion on sewage sludge in Chapter 9).

fdc1da106b91.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/18%3A_Nutrient_Management/18.04%3A_Improving_Nutrient_Cycling_on_the_Farm
fdc1da106b91.sentence: During the composting process, volume and weight are greatly reduced (see Chapter 13), resulting in less material to transport.

52fa1e93707f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/18%3A_Nutrient_Management/18.04%3A_Improving_Nutrient_Cycling_on_the_Farm
52fa1e93707f.sentence: Local or regional compost exchanges can help remove nutrients from overburdened animal operations and place them on nutrient-deficient soils.

f5f4426524b7.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/18%3A_Nutrient_Management/18.04%3A_Improving_Nutrient_Cycling_on_the_Farm
f5f4426524b7.sentence: This is especially beneficial when a livestock farmer has too many animals and imports a high percentage of feed, and a neighboring vegetable or grain farmer has a need for nutrients and an inadequate land base for allowing a rotation that includes a forage legume.

0d81d03be479.title: Phosphorus deficiency
0d81d03be479.sentence: Phosphorus deficiency is a plant disorder associated with insufficient supply of phosphorus.

659ce66020ed.title: Phosphorus deficiency
659ce66020ed.sentence: Phosphorus refers here to salts of phosphates (PO3−4), monohydrogen phosphate (HPO2−4), and dihydrogen phosphate (H2PO−4).

5de976f13e37.title: Phosphorus deficiency
5de976f13e37.sentence: These anions readily interconvert, and the predominant species is determined by the pH of the solution or soil.

4757f8104120.title: Phosphorus deficiency
4757f8104120.sentence: A large portion of phosphorus in soil is in chemical compounds that plants can't absorb.

d590f779805c.title: Phosphorus deficiency
d590f779805c.sentence: Between pH 6 and 7, phosphorus makes the fewest bonds which render the nutrient unusable to plants.

dd0d25d08ddc.title: Phosphorus deficiency
dd0d25d08ddc.sentence: Hence, phosphorus deficient plants may mature at a slower rate than plants with adequate amounts of phosphorus.

4f4f10ce5e3c.title: Phosphorus deficiency
4f4f10ce5e3c.sentence: This imbalance of rates in phosphorus deficient plants leads to the buildup of excess carbohydrate within the plant as starch granules.

3bd299c9232e.title: Phosphorus deficiency
3bd299c9232e.sentence: In some plants the leaf pigment change as a result of this process can turn leaves a dark purplish color.

0f3af04f22e5.title: Phosphorus deficiency
0f3af04f22e5.sentence: Additionally, discoloration in plant leaves only occurs under fairly severe phosphorus deficiency so it is beneficial to planters and farmers to scientifically check phosphorus levels before discoloration occurs.

cc4dd74148ee.title: Phosphorus deficiency
cc4dd74148ee.sentence: The most prominent method of checking phosphorus levels is by soil testing.

ecd12d70986c.title: Phosphorus deficiency
ecd12d70986c.sentence: The major soil testing methods are Bray 1-P, Mehlich 3, and Olsen methods.

80bafa52d839.title: Phosphorus deficiency
80bafa52d839.sentence: These tests use chemical solutions to extract phosphorus from the soil.

25c01e7fd81d.title: Phosphorus deficiency
25c01e7fd81d.sentence: Colorimetry is used to determine this concentration.

a2d7073168f3.title: Phosphorus deficiency
a2d7073168f3.sentence: A change in root structure can also occur, where growth of lateral roots is favored while halting taproot growth.

6f7293d317a1.title: Phosphorus deficiency
6f7293d317a1.sentence: Root secretion of ribonucleases and acid phosphatases is promoted to scavange phosphorus, in some cases accompanied by organic acids that help degrade aluminum complexes with inorganic phosphate in soil.

a37b96a2e009.title: Phosphorus deficiency
a37b96a2e009.sentence: Along with root size, other root adaptations to low phosphorus, such as mycorrhizal symbioses, have been found to increase nutrient intake.

a6f66c97084d.title: Potassium deficiency (plants)
a6f66c97084d.sentence: Potassium deficiency, also known as potash deficiency, is a plant disorder caused by the depletion of potassium ions (K+) in the soil.

971cbaeec785.title: Potassium deficiency (plants)
971cbaeec785.sentence: It is most common in light, sandy soils with a low clay content, as potassium is highly soluble and will easily leach from soils that lack colloids.

7fe73665c26e.title: Potassium deficiency (plants)
7fe73665c26e.sentence: Typical symptoms of potassium deficiency in plants include brown scorching and curling of leaf tips as well as chlorosis (yellowing) between leaf veins.

1d63d87cc824.title: Potassium deficiency (plants)
1d63d87cc824.sentence: Often, potassium deficiency symptoms first appear on older (lower) leaves because potassium is a mobile nutrient, meaning that a plant can allocate potassium to younger leaves when it is K deficient.

eba6bddeef42.title: Potassium deficiency (plants)
eba6bddeef42.sentence: For many species, potassium-deficient plants are more susceptible to frost damage and certain diseases than plants with adequate potassium levels.

e9c07e21b4c2.title: Potassium deficiency (plants)
e9c07e21b4c2.sentence: However, increasing potassium concentration above the optimal level does not provide greater disease resistance.

d72045d67a9d.title: Potassium deficiency (plants)
d72045d67a9d.sentence: The most widely used potassium fertilizer is potassium chloride (muriate of potash).

e86446c140ed.title: Potassium deficiency (plants)
e86446c140ed.sentence: Adequate moisture is necessary for effective potassium uptake; low soil water reduces K uptake by plant roots.

cc8432012ce3.title: Potassium deficiency (plants)
cc8432012ce3.sentence: Liming acidic soils can increase potassium retention in some soils by reducing leaching; practices that increase soil organic matter can also increase potassium retention.

884ad0bbf23e.title: Micronutrient deficiency
884ad0bbf23e.section: Plants > List of essential trace minerals for plants
884ad0bbf23e.sentence: - Manganese activates some important enzymes involved in chlorophyll formation.

21b05b891a82.title: Micronutrient deficiency
21b05b891a82.section: Plants > List of essential trace minerals for plants
21b05b891a82.sentence: Manganese deficient plants will develop chlorosis between the veins of its leaves.

0f7955859c3a.title: Micronutrient deficiency
0f7955859c3a.section: Plants > List of essential trace minerals for plants
0f7955859c3a.sentence: The availability of manganese is partially dependent on soil pH.

e153af86e0ad.title: Micronutrient deficiency
e153af86e0ad.section: Plants > List of essential trace minerals for plants
e153af86e0ad.sentence: Some plants use it for nitrogen fixation, thus it may need to be added to some soils before seeding legumes.

7abafb731089.title: Micronutrient deficiency
7abafb731089.sentence: Micronutrients are distinguished from macronutrients (nitrogen, phosphorus, sulfur, potassium, calcium and magnesium) by the relatively low quantities needed by the plant.

5132d1138389.title: Micronutrient deficiency
5132d1138389.sentence: A number of elements are known to be needed in these small amounts for proper plant growth and development.

17a6d7423864.title: Zinc deficiency (plant disorder)
17a6d7423864.sentence: Zinc deficiency occurs when plant growth is limited because the plant cannot take up sufficient quantities of this essential micronutrient from its growing medium.

3099f7b8f93b.title: Zinc deficiency (plant disorder)
3099f7b8f93b.sentence: Soils low in organic matter (such as where topsoils have been removed), and compacted soils that restrict root proliferation also have a high risk of zinc deficiency.

a801887667f2.title: Zinc deficiency (plant disorder)
a801887667f2.sentence: Application of phosphorus fertilizers has frequently been associated with zinc deficiency; this may be due to enhanced sorption by clay minerals (especially iron oxides), suppression of vesicular arbuscular mycorrhizae and/or immobilization of zinc in plant tissues.

11c37fbccaf6.title: Zinc deficiency (plant disorder)
11c37fbccaf6.sentence: Liming of soils also frequently induces zinc deficiency by increasing zinc sorption.

96503fd1a405.title: Zinc deficiency (plant disorder)
96503fd1a405.sentence: Although zinc requirements vary among crops, zinc leaf concentrations (on a dry matter basis) in the range 20 to 100 mg/kg are adequate for most crops.

fc1f52ba5337.title: Zinc deficiency (plant disorder)
fc1f52ba5337.sentence: Zinc sulphate or zinc oxide can be applied to soils to correct zinc deficiency.

3d34ef0c1a3f.title: Zinc deficiency (plant disorder)
3d34ef0c1a3f.sentence: Recommended applications of actual zinc range from 5 to 100 kg/hectare but optimum levels of zinc vary with plant type and the severity of the deficiency.

0205462074f6.title: Zinc deficiency (plant disorder)
0205462074f6.sentence: Application of zinc may not correct zinc deficiency in alkaline soils because even with the addition of zinc, it may remain unavailable for plant absorption.

ceee87523072.title: Zinc deficiency (plant disorder)
ceee87523072.sentence: Almost half of the world's cereal crops are grown on zinc-deficient soils; as a result, zinc deficiency in humans is a widespread problem.

98efcab8f2e8.title: Copper in biology
98efcab8f2e8.sentence: Copper is an essential trace element that is vital to the health of all living things (plants, animals and microorganisms).

6595217c3759.title: Copper in biology
6595217c3759.sentence: Copper is an essential trace element (i.e., micronutrient) that is required for plant, animal, and human health.

b1cd9c405d24.title: Copper in biology
b1cd9c405d24.sentence: Copper proteins have diverse roles in biological electron transport and oxygen transportation, processes that exploit the easy interconversion of Cu(I) and Cu(II).

4cab355224d2.title: Copper in biology
4cab355224d2.sentence: Copper is essential in the aerobic respiration of all eukaryotes.

b8b480965ee7.title: Micronutrient deficiency
b8b480965ee7.section: Plants > List of essential trace minerals for plants
b8b480965ee7.sentence: - Copper is a component of some enzymes and of vitamin A. Symptoms of copper deficiency include browning of leaf tips and chlorosis.

d52d719caabe.title: Copper in biology
d52d719caabe.section: Plant and animal health > Plant health
d52d719caabe.sentence: Copper concentrations in soil are not uniform around the world.

62b8c0ce9001.title: Copper in biology
62b8c0ce9001.section: Plant and animal health > Plant health
62b8c0ce9001.sentence: In many areas, soils have insufficient levels of copper.

41599aa471b3.title: Copper in biology
41599aa471b3.section: Plant and animal health > Plant health
41599aa471b3.sentence: Soils that are naturally deficient in copper often require copper supplements before agricultural crops, such as cereals, can be grown.

411d8677aff7.title: Copper in biology
411d8677aff7.section: Plant and animal health > Plant health
411d8677aff7.sentence: The most effective strategy to counter copper deficiency is to supplement the soil with copper, usually in the form of copper sulfate.

0b6e3c9dab0a.title: Copper in biology
0b6e3c9dab0a.section: Plant and animal health > Plant health
0b6e3c9dab0a.sentence: Nitrogen fertilizers can worsen copper deficiency in agricultural soils.

7d655d96265c.title: Copper in biology
7d655d96265c.section: Plant and animal health > Plant health
7d655d96265c.sentence: The world's two most important food crops, rice and wheat, are highly susceptible to copper deficiency.

81624522d968.title: Copper in biology
81624522d968.section: Plant and animal health > Plant health
81624522d968.sentence: So are several other important foods, including citrus, oats, spinach and carrots.

cdf7988dd491.title: Copper in biology
cdf7988dd491.section: Plant and animal health > Plant health
cdf7988dd491.sentence: On the other hand, some foods including coconuts, soybeans and asparagus, are not particularly sensitive to copper-deficient soils.

d89dcf1eb568.title: Nitrogen assimilation
d89dcf1eb568.sentence: Nitrogen use efficiency (NUE) is the proportion of nitrogen present that a plant absorbs and uses.

e446a81bd662.title: Nitrogen assimilation
e446a81bd662.sentence: Worldwide, crops generally have less than 50% NUE.

984eb92042dd.title: Nitrogen assimilation
984eb92042dd.sentence: Improving nitrogen use efficiency and thus fertilizer efficiency is important to make agriculture more sustainable, by reducing pollution (fertilizer runoff) and production cost and increasing yield.

c7c2742a4188.title: Nitrogen assimilation
c7c2742a4188.sentence: Better fertilizers, improved crop management, selective breeding, and genetic engineering can increase NUE.

ca87bf9f429c.title: Nitrogen assimilation
ca87bf9f429c.sentence: Nitrogen use efficiency can be measured at various levels: the crop plant, the soil, by fertilizer input, by ecosystem productivity, etc.

1d5d2d8696a3.title: Law of Maximum
1d5d2d8696a3.sentence: The Law of Maximum also known as Law of the Maximum is a principle developed by Arthur Wallace which states that total growth of a crop or a plant is proportional to about 70 growth factors.

600e68f0fbf4.title: Law of Maximum
600e68f0fbf4.sentence: Growth will not be greater than the aggregate values of the growth factors.

729790769a94.title: Law of Maximum
729790769a94.sentence: The factors range from 0 for no growth to 1 for maximum growth.

feb609e8a429.title: Law of Maximum
feb609e8a429.sentence: Actual growth is calculated by the total multiplication of each growth factor.

ef8a00be6d33.title: Law of Maximum
ef8a00be6d33.sentence: Both low phosphorus | actual result 57% | 59% (83% x 71%)

48d76edeadeb.title: Law of Maximum
48d76edeadeb.section: Demonstrations of "Law of the Maximum" > Growth Factors > A. Adequacy of Nutrients
48d76edeadeb.sentence: Nitrogen Phosphorus Potassium Calcium Magnesium Sulfur Iron Zinc Manganese Copper Boron Chlorine Cobalt Sodium Nickel

efc3a7105869.title: Law of Maximum
efc3a7105869.section: Demonstrations of "Law of the Maximum" > Growth Factors > B. Non-nutrient elements and nutrients excesses that cause toxicities (stresses)
efc3a7105869.sentence: Nickel Cadmium Nickel Copper Boron Sodium chloride Aluminium Bicarbonate others

53b5fd7d4634.title: Law of Maximum
53b5fd7d4634.section: Demonstrations of "Law of the Maximum" > Growth Factors > D. Soil Conditioning requirement and physical processes
53b5fd7d4634.sentence: Low pH (soluble Al) high pH salinity, EC (electrical conductivity) either too low or too high, ratios of sand vs. silt vs. clay presence of rocks soil organic matter soil aeration limestone soil moisture conditions (frequency of rain or irrigation) depth to water table other subsoil conditions earthworms cation exchange capacity soil erosion (dust and water) redox, soil crusting structures of soil that give aeration and water penetration fixation of nutrients by soil hydrophobic conditions other aspects of soil quality, slope and topography of lands

a1a799001eec.title: Law of Maximum
a1a799001eec.section: Demonstrations of "Law of the Maximum" > Growth Factors > G. Management
a1a799001eec.sentence: Crop rotations timing of operations choice of tillage use of appropriate cultivars and varieties irrigation fertilizer distribution use of soil conditioners to correct problems

d7d948821623.title: Law of Maximum
d7d948821623.sentence: Without the correction of the limiting growth factors, nutrients, waters and other inputs are not fully or judicially used resulting in wasted resources.

d1c3a057842f.title: Calcium deficiency (plant)
d1c3a057842f.sentence: Calcium (Ca) deficiency is a plant disorder that can be caused by insufficient level of biologically available calcium in the growing medium, but is more frequently a product of low transpiration of the whole plant or more commonly the affected tissue.

8b41a9077d4e.title: Calcium deficiency (plant)
8b41a9077d4e.sentence: Plants are susceptible to such localized calcium deficiencies in low or non-transpiring tissues because calcium is not transported in the phloem.

d0332b4ac8ec.title: Calcium deficiency (plant)
d0332b4ac8ec.sentence: Generally, the new growth and rapidly growing tissues of the plant are affected first.

18c1a48e115f.title: Calcium deficiency (plant)
18c1a48e115f.sentence: Acidic, sandy, or coarse soils often contain less calcium.

7551e3838a5b.title: Calcium deficiency (plant)
7551e3838a5b.sentence: Soils containing high phosphorus are particularly susceptible to creating insoluble forms of calcium.

04b1247a92d4.title: Calcium deficiency (plant)
04b1247a92d4.sentence: 'Bitter pit' – fruit skins develop pits, brown spots appear on skin and/or in flesh and taste of those areas is bitter.

d2501dfb8434.title: Calcium deficiency (plant)
d2501dfb8434.sentence: 'Blossom end rot' – Symptoms start as sunken, dry decaying areas at the blossom end of the fruit, furthest away from the stem, not all fruit on a truss is necessarily affected.

c69eef91d63e.title: Calcium deficiency (plant)
c69eef91d63e.sentence: There is some evidence that plants like lettuce are more likely to experience tipburn (burned edges of leaves) if they're experiencing a deficiency of calcium.

3c9a7504af7f.title: Calcium deficiency (plant)
3c9a7504af7f.sentence: Calcium deficiency can sometimes be rectified by adding agricultural lime to acid soils, aiming at a pH of 6.5, unless the subject plants specifically prefer acidic soil.

bd1531849746.title: Calcium deficiency (plant)
bd1531849746.sentence: However, because of the nature of the disorder (i.e. poor transport of calcium to low transpiring tissues), the problem cannot generally be cured by the addition of calcium to the roots.

cefae5297b1c.title: Calcium deficiency (plant)
cefae5297b1c.sentence: Water management and preventing water stress is key to minimizing its occurrence.

d14c16b36b2a.title: Hoagland solution
d14c16b36b2a.sentence: The Hoagland solution (HS) is a hydroponic nutrient solution that was newly developed by Hoagland and Snyder in 1933, modified by Hoagland and Arnon in 1938, and revised by Arnon in 1950.

a1561027341e.title: Hoagland solution
a1561027341e.sentence: The Hoagland solution provides all essential elements for plant nutrition and is appropriate for supporting normal growth of a large variety of plant species.

673bc4714104.title: Hoagland solution
673bc4714104.sentence: It is one of the most popular standard solution compositions for growing plants, in the scientific world at least, with more than 21,000 citations listed by Google Scholar.

5e2d7d895a34.title: Hoagland solution
5e2d7d895a34.sentence: The artificial solution described by Dennis Hoagland in 1933, known as Hoagland solution (0), has been modified several times, mainly to add ferric chelates to keep iron effectively in solution, and to optimize the composition and concentration of trace elements other than iron, some of which are not generally credited with a function in plant nutrition.

8eda12d7825d.title: Hoagland solution
8eda12d7825d.sentence: In Hoagland's nutrient recipes of 1938, referred to as Hoagland solution (1, 2), the number of trace elements was subsequently reduced to the generally accepted essential elements (B, Mn, Zn, Cu, Mo, Fe, and Cl).

59e33d6fa640.title: Hoagland solution
59e33d6fa640.sentence: In Arnon's revision of 1950, only one concentration (Mo 0.011 ppm) was changed compared to 1938 (Mo 0.048 ppm), while the concentration of macronutrients of the Hoagland solutions (0), (1), and (2) remained the same since 1933, with the exception of calcium (Ca 160 ppm) in solution (2).

9c1429cecc1e.title: Hoagland solution
9c1429cecc1e.sentence: The Hoagland solution, originally intended to imitate a (nutrient-) rich soil solution, has high concentrations of N and K so it is very well suited for the development of large plants like tomato and bell pepper.

e865a2196259.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/18%3A_Nutrient_Management/18.05%3A_Using_Fertilizers_and_Amendments
e865a2196259.section: Nutrient Sources: Commercial Fertilizers Versus Organic Materials

90ccac6206de.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/18%3A_Nutrient_Management/18.02%3A_The_Bottom_Line-_Nutrients_and_Plant_Health_Pests_Profits_and_the_Environment
90ccac6206de.sentence: This early jump-start may then enable them to out-compete crop plants later on.

2d7b24e37ced.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/18%3A_Nutrient_Management/18.02%3A_The_Bottom_Line-_Nutrients_and_Plant_Health_Pests_Profits_and_the_Environment
2d7b24e37ced.sentence: Plants under nutrient stress may be stunted if nutrient levels are low, or they may grow too much foliage and not enough fruit if N is too plentiful relative to other nutrients.

0171b2bd122f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/18%3A_Nutrient_Management/18.02%3A_The_Bottom_Line-_Nutrients_and_Plant_Health_Pests_Profits_and_the_Environment
0171b2bd122f.sentence: Plants under nutrient stress grow abnormally, for example, in the presence of too low or too high N levels, and are not able to emit as much of the natural chemicals that signal beneficial insects capable of fighting insect pests that feed on leaves or fruit.

7c971c6f3644.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/18%3A_Nutrient_Management/18.02%3A_The_Bottom_Line-_Nutrients_and_Plant_Health_Pests_Profits_and_the_Environment

717b4628f222.sentence: Blossom-end rot of tomatoes is related to low calcium levels, often made worse by droughty conditions, or irregular rainfall or poor irrigation.

cddc1721513e.sentence: Plants should be healthy and have large root systems if a soil has good tilth, no subsurface compaction, good drainage, adequate water, a good supply of organic matter and a thriving soil biological community.

00d889b1e099.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/18%3A_Nutrient_Management/18.02%3A_The_Bottom_Line-_Nutrients_and_Plant_Health_Pests_Profits_and_the_Environment

0fa2854c3718.sentence: When soil-potassium levels are high, plants take up more potassium than needed for healthy growth.

8007251784dd.sentence: The term luxury consumption has been applied to this.

806b65c9d1fd.title: Fertilizer
806b65c9d1fd.sentence: Macro-nutrients are present in plant tissue in quantities from 0.15% to 6.0% on a dry matter (DM) (0% moisture) basis but they are sometimes consumed in larger quantities than required (luxury consumption), in particular when fertilizers are used in excess of plant requirements (overfertilization).

72f2d84df7d3.title: Plant nutrients in soil
72f2d84df7d3.sentence: Calcium uptake by roots is essential for plant nutrition, contrary to an old tenet that it was luxury consumption.

e1860e0969fb.title: Fertilizer
e1860e0969fb.sentence: Although calcium uptake by plant roots has long-time been considered as luxury consumption, it is now considered as an essential element for its various roles in the maintenance of the integrity of plant cell walls and cell membranes.

5050e14e872c.title: Plant nutrition
5050e14e872c.section: Availability and uptake > Root environment > Root temperature
5050e14e872c.sentence: Potassium intake increases with root temperature and depresses calcium uptake.

5afbc5d91182.title: Biogeochemical cycle
5afbc5d91182.sentence: A biogeochemical cycle, or more generally a cycle of matter, is the movement and transformation of chemical elements and compounds between living organisms, the atmosphere, and the Earth's crust.

c6c8861b6d12.title: Biogeochemical cycle
c6c8861b6d12.sentence: In each cycle, the chemical element or molecule is transformed and cycled by living organisms and through various geological forms and reservoirs, including the atmosphere, the soil and the oceans.

0eb05319c90d.title: Biogeochemical cycle
0eb05319c90d.sentence: Energy flows directionally through ecosystems, entering as sunlight (or inorganic molecules for chemoautotrophs) and leaving as heat during the many transfers between trophic levels.

03448e7156b6.title: Biogeochemical cycle
03448e7156b6.sentence: However, the matter that makes up living organisms is conserved and recycled.

93cde9d83607.title: Biogeochemical cycle
93cde9d83607.sentence: Major biogeochemical cycles include the carbon cycle, the nitrogen cycle and the water cycle.

c89912e035ad.title: Biogeochemical cycle
c89912e035ad.sentence: There are biogeochemical cycles for many other elements, such as for oxygen, hydrogen, phosphorus, calcium, iron, sulfur, mercury and selenium.

0ce456d9fb8e.title: Biogeochemical cycle
0ce456d9fb8e.sentence: The six most common elements associated with organic molecules — carbon, nitrogen, hydrogen, oxygen, phosphorus, and sulfur — take a variety of chemical forms and may exist for long periods in the atmosphere, on land, in water, or beneath the Earth's surface.

586ba083f400.title: Biogeochemical cycle
586ba083f400.sentence: Biogeochemical cycles operate by moving substances, which may also undergo chemical rearrangements, through pathways in the biotic compartment and the abiotic compartments of Earth.

8d4a6b8c8334.title: Biogeochemical cycle
8d4a6b8c8334.sentence: The biotic compartment is the biosphere and the abiotic compartments are the atmosphere, lithosphere and hydrosphere.

a71d2c464018.title: Biogeochemical cycle
a71d2c464018.sentence: Microorganisms drive much of the biogeochemical cycling in the earth system.

54299be081a4.title: Biogeochemical cycle
54299be081a4.sentence: Biological processes include the influence of microorganisms, which are critical drivers of biogeochemical cycling.

e1448d00b862.title: Biogeochemical cycle
e1448d00b862.sentence: Without microorganisms many of these processes would not occur, with significant impact on the functioning of land and ocean ecosystems and the planet's biogeochemical cycles as a whole.

e590ddb0edc0.title: Biogeochemical cycle
e590ddb0edc0.sentence: The cycles are interconnected and play important roles regulating climate, supporting the growth of plants, phytoplankton and other organisms, and maintaining the health of ecosystems generally.

ea9d0219bb31.title: Biogeochemical cycle
ea9d0219bb31.sentence: Human activities such as burning fossil fuels and using large amounts of fertilizer can disrupt cycles, contributing to climate change, pollution, and other environmental problems.

940255446a89.title: Nitrogen cycle
940255446a89.sentence: The nitrogen cycle is the biogeochemical cycle by which nitrogen is converted into multiple chemical forms as it circulates among atmospheric, terrestrial, and marine ecosystems.

e853011a8d9c.title: Nitrogen cycle
e853011a8d9c.sentence: Important processes in the nitrogen cycle include fixation, ammonification, nitrification, and denitrification.

e41d6b390134.title: Nitrogen cycle
e41d6b390134.sentence: The conversion of nitrogen can be carried out through both biological and physical processes.

9db1fa23758e.title: Nitrogen cycle
9db1fa23758e.sentence: The majority of Earth's atmosphere (78%) is atmospheric nitrogen, making it the largest source of nitrogen.

6905266c79ee.title: Nitrogen cycle
6905266c79ee.sentence: However, atmospheric nitrogen has limited availability for biological use, leading to a scarcity of usable nitrogen in many types of ecosystems.

5c063df2eebd.title: Nitrogen cycle
5c063df2eebd.sentence: Nitrogen is present in the environment in a wide variety of chemical forms including organic nitrogen, ammonium (NH+4), nitrite (NO−2), nitrate (NO−3), nitrous oxide (N2O), nitric oxide (NO) or nitrogen gas (N2).

3583c407a99c.title: Nitrogen cycle
3583c407a99c.sentence: Organic nitrogen may be in the form of a living organism, humus or in the intermediate products of organic matter decomposition.

62981c6c5ed0.title: Nitrogen cycle
62981c6c5ed0.sentence: Many of these processes are carried out by microbes, either in their effort to harvest energy or to accumulate nitrogen in a form needed for their growth.

22048f5ee2ae.title: Nitrogen cycle
22048f5ee2ae.sentence: Though nitrogen fixation is the primary source of plant-available nitrogen in most ecosystems, in areas with nitrogen-rich bedrock, the breakdown of this rock also serves as a nitrogen source.

e720fd75279c.title: Nitrogen cycle
e720fd75279c.sentence: The nitrogen cycle is of particular interest to ecologists because nitrogen availability can affect the rate of key ecosystem processes, including primary production and decomposition.

cd405b8bcdb1.title: Nitrogen cycle
cd405b8bcdb1.sentence: Human activities such as fossil fuel combustion, use of artificial nitrogen fertilizers, and release of nitrogen in wastewater have dramatically altered the global nitrogen cycle.

2f7a3b7b37b6.title: Nitrogen cycle
2f7a3b7b37b6.sentence: Human modification of the global nitrogen cycle can negatively affect the natural environment system and also human health.

57aa2bdad44f.title: Nitrogen cycle
57aa2bdad44f.sentence: The nitrogen cycle is an important process in the ocean as well.

79ab9111fbfe.title: Nitrogen cycle
79ab9111fbfe.sentence: Nitrogen cannot be utilized by phytoplankton as N 2 so it must undergo nitrogen fixation which is performed predominately by cyanobacteria.

8d8a81716cd6.title: Nitrogen fixation
8d8a81716cd6.sentence: Nitrogen fixation is a chemical process by which the abundant but relatively inert molecular dinitrogen (N 2) is converted into bioavailable nitrogen compounds such as ammonia (NH 3) and nitrates (NO− 3).

55db12f70248.title: Nitrogen fixation
55db12f70248.sentence: Atmospheric nitrogen cannot be metabolized by most organisms, because its triple covalent bond is very strong.

a3a476f10961.title: Nitrogen fixation
a3a476f10961.sentence: It occurs both biologically and abiologically, the latter either naturally through weather phenomena (e.g. lightning) or artificially by chemical industries.

c076c54b0616.title: Nitrogen fixation
c076c54b0616.sentence: Biological nitrogen fixation or diazotrophy is catalyzed by enzymes called nitrogenases, produced by microorganisms such as cyanobacteria and rhizobia.

f460ac755ce0.title: Nitrogen cycle
f460ac755ce0.sentence: Between 5 and 10 billion kg per year are fixed by lightning strikes, but most fixation is done by free-living or symbiotic bacteria known as diazotrophs.

28070efc2d99.title: Nitrogen fixation
28070efc2d99.sentence: These compounds cannot be used by plants, but as this molecule cools, it reacts with oxygen to form nitrogen dioxide (NO 2), which in turn reacts with water to produce nitrous acid (HNO 2) or nitric acid (HNO 3).

61b6490017b2.title: Nitrogen fixation
61b6490017b2.sentence: When these acids seep into the soil, they produce nitrate (NO3−), which is of use to plants.

02e4295b1f0e.title: Nitrogen fixation
02e4295b1f0e.sentence: Some nitrogen-fixing bacteria have symbiotic relationships with plants, especially legumes, mosses, and aquatic ferns such as Azolla.

5c7573157741.title: Nitrogen fixation
5c7573157741.sentence: Looser non-symbiotic relationships between diazotrophs and plants are often referred to as associative, as seen in nitrogen fixation on rice roots.

7a050f8f3146.title: Nitrogen cycle
7a050f8f3146.sentence: Today, about 30% of the total fixed nitrogen is produced industrially using the Haber-Bosch process, which uses high temperatures and pressures to convert nitrogen gas and a hydrogen source (natural gas or petroleum) into ammonia.

de2d9b76b362.title: Nitrogen fixation
de2d9b76b362.sentence: Nitrogen fixation is a key component of the nitrogen cycle and is essential to life on Earth, as all vital organic compounds such as DNA and proteins contain nitrogen.

e8037f124e10.title: Phosphorus cycle
e8037f124e10.sentence: The phosphorus cycle is the biogeochemical cycle that involves the movement of phosphorus through the lithosphere, hydrosphere, and biosphere.

81b24f04111d.title: Phosphorus cycle
81b24f04111d.sentence: Unlike many other biogeochemical cycles, the atmosphere does not play a significant role in the movement of phosphorus, because phosphorus and phosphorus-based materials do not enter the gaseous phase readily, as the main source of gaseous phosphorus, phosphine, is only produced in isolated and specific conditions.

6cfe9bc956c6.title: Phosphorus cycle
6cfe9bc956c6.sentence: Therefore, the phosphorus cycle is primarily examined studying the movement of orthophosphate (PO3−4), the form of phosphorus that is most commonly seen in the environment, through terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems.

b8b68daa1021.title: Phosphorus cycle
b8b68daa1021.sentence: Living organisms require phosphorus, a vital component of DNA, RNA, and ATP, for their proper functioning.

179e0ce68a36.title: Phosphorus cycle
179e0ce68a36.sentence: Phosphorus also enters in the composition of phospholipids present in cell membranes.

8f1c16f58540.title: Phosphorus cycle
8f1c16f58540.sentence: Plants assimilate phosphorus as phosphate and incorporate it into organic compounds.

529401b86e7a.title: Phosphorus cycle
529401b86e7a.section: Phosphorus in the environment > Phosphorus cycling
529401b86e7a.sentence: Phosphates move quickly through plants and animals; however, the processes that move them through the soil or ocean are very slow, making the phosphorus cycle overall one of the slowest biogeochemical cycles.

24874b264a91.title: Phosphorus cycle
24874b264a91.sentence: In the long-term global cycle, however, the major transfer is driven by tectonic movement over geologic time and weathering of phosphate containing rock such as apatite.

fb3011798857.title: Phosphorus cycle
fb3011798857.section: Phosphorus in the environment > Phosphorus cycling
fb3011798857.sentence: In terrestrial systems, bioavailable P ('reactive P') mainly comes from weathering of phosphorus-containing rocks.

df63e9c116a1.title: Phosphorus cycle
df63e9c116a1.sentence: Short-term transformation of phosphorus is chemical, biological, or microbiological.

fcd6742ce707.title: Phosphorus cycle
fcd6742ce707.sentence: Soil microorganisms act as both sinks and sources of available phosphorus in the biogeochemical cycle.

a3b26bc0e924.title: Phosphorus cycle
a3b26bc0e924.sentence: Low concentration of phosphorus in soils reduces plant growth and slows soil microbial growth, as shown in studies of soil microbial biomass.

46bc22279ba5.title: Phosphorus cycle
46bc22279ba5.section: Phosphorus in the environment > Phosphorus cycling
46bc22279ba5.sentence: Soil phosphorus is usually transported to rivers and lakes and can then either be buried in lake sediments or transported to the ocean via river runoff.

c8ca067c3dd2.title: Phosphorus cycle
c8ca067c3dd2.section: Phosphorus in the environment > Phosphorus cycling
c8ca067c3dd2.sentence: The vast majority of phosphorus is remineralized within the water column, and approximately 1% of associated phosphorus carried to the deep sea by the falling particles is removed from the ocean reservoir by burial in sediments.

8c77fc3754ae.title: Phosphorus cycle
8c77fc3754ae.section: Phosphorus in the environment > Ecological function
8c77fc3754ae.sentence: Phosphates which are found in fertilizers, sewage and detergents, can cause pollution in lakes and streams.

53c1530937e9.title: Phosphorus cycle
53c1530937e9.section: Phosphorus in the environment > Ecological function
53c1530937e9.sentence: Over-enrichment of phosphate in both fresh and inshore marine waters can lead to massive algae blooms.

731296f6c904.title: Phosphorus cycle
731296f6c904.section: Phosphorus in the environment > Ecological function
731296f6c904.sentence: Freshwater algal blooms are generally caused by excess phosphorus, while those that take place in saltwater tend to result from excess nitrogen.

fb0981bf246f.title: Sulfur cycle
fb0981bf246f.sentence: The sulfur cycle is a biogeochemical cycle in which the sulfur moves between rocks, waterways and living systems.

a76bc38ee7f5.title: Sulfur cycle
a76bc38ee7f5.sentence: The global sulfur cycle involves the transformations of sulfur species through different oxidation states, which play an important role in both geological and biological processes.

34c02873ce4d.title: Sulfur cycle
34c02873ce4d.sentence: It is important in geology as it affects many minerals and in life because sulfur is an essential element (CHNOPS), being a constituent of many proteins and cofactors, and sulfur compounds can be used as oxidants or reductants in cellular respiration.

025dbea544f7.title: Sulfur cycle
025dbea544f7.sentence: Sulfur is found in oxidation states ranging from +6 in SO2− 4 to −2 in sulfides.

42ac15722ac1.title: Sulfur cycle
42ac15722ac1.sentence: Thus, elemental sulfur can either give or receive electrons depending on its environment.

03278ee65da4.title: Sulfur cycle
03278ee65da4.sentence: - Mineralization of organic sulfur into inorganic forms, such as hydrogen sulfide (H2S), elemental sulfur, as well as sulfide minerals.

2baacca0a429.title: Sulfur cycle
2baacca0a429.sentence: Desulfurization in which organic molecules containing sulfur can be desulfurized, producing hydrogen sulfide gas (H2S, oxidation state = –2).

8af946ace6b9.title: Sulfur cycle
8af946ace6b9.sentence: An analogous process for organic nitrogen compounds is deamination.

8ae677b311bb.title: Sulfur cycle
8ae677b311bb.sentence: - Oxidation of hydrogen sulfide, sulfide, and elemental sulfur (S) to sulfate (SO2− 4).

ff6c8aae7fbd.title: Sulfur cycle
ff6c8aae7fbd.sentence: Oxidation of elemental sulfur by sulfur oxidizers produces sulfate.

e3a2a8194428.title: Sulfur cycle
e3a2a8194428.sentence: - Reduction of sulfate and sulfite to sulfide.

da958b04ad94.title: Sulfur cycle
da958b04ad94.sentence: Dissimilative sulfate reduction in which sulfate reducers generate hydrogen sulfide from sulfate.

c5bbb76d8502.title: Sulfur cycle
c5bbb76d8502.sentence: Assimilative sulfate reduction (see also sulfur assimilation) in which sulfate (SO2− 4) is reduced by plants, fungi and various prokaryotes.

ae776ce7e870.title: Sulfur cycle
ae776ce7e870.sentence: Without human impact sulfur would stay tied up in rocks for millions of years until it was uplifted through tectonic events and then released through erosion and weathering processes.

db13da68939c.title: Sulfur cycle
db13da68939c.sentence: However, the biosphere does not act as a major sink for sulfur, instead the majority of sulfur is found in seawater or sedimentary rocks including: pyrite rich shales, evaporite rocks (anhydrite and baryte), and calcium and magnesium carbonates (i.e. carbonate-associated sulfate).

01caf5181622.title: Nutrient cycle
01caf5181622.sentence: A nutrient cycle (or ecological recycling) is the movement and exchange of inorganic and organic matter back into the production of matter.

48256a484523.title: Nutrient cycle
48256a484523.sentence: Energy flow is a unidirectional and noncyclic pathway, whereas the movement of mineral nutrients is cyclic.

0c62b9eb8f74.title: Nutrient cycle
0c62b9eb8f74.sentence: Mineral cycles include the carbon cycle, sulfur cycle, nitrogen cycle, water cycle, phosphorus cycle, oxygen cycle, among others that continually recycle along with other mineral nutrients into productive ecological nutrition.

7461b3abf55e.title: Nutrient cycle
7461b3abf55e.sentence: There is much overlap between the terms for the biogeochemical cycle and nutrient cycle.

ecb20c4e1a39.title: Nutrient cycle
ecb20c4e1a39.sentence: Most textbooks integrate the two and seem to treat them as synonymous terms.

7c9f9a30ed76.title: Nutrient cycle
7c9f9a30ed76.sentence: The nutrient cycle is more often used in direct reference to the idea of an intra-system cycle, where an ecosystem functions as a unit.

fcea4198194b.title: Nutrient cycle
fcea4198194b.sentence: Nutrient cycling occurs in ecosystems that participate in the "larger biogeochemical cycles of the earth through a system of inputs and outputs."

8052d00ce46c.title: Nutrient cycle
8052d00ce46c.sentence: Recycling in ecology is regulated to a large extent during the process of decomposition.

7acae5c40ab8.title: Nutrient cycle
7acae5c40ab8.sentence: Cellulose-degrading enzymes participate in the natural, ecological recycling of plant material." Different ecosystems can vary in their recycling rates of litter, which creates a complex feedback on factors such as the competitive dominance of certain plant species.

6800bede2220.title: Nutrient cycle
6800bede2220.sentence: There are regional and spatial differences in the rates of growth and exchange of materials, where some ecosystems may be in nutrient debt (sinks) where others will have extra supply (sources).

dc06ee74837f.title: Nutrient cycle
dc06ee74837f.sentence: These differences relate to climate, topography, and geological history leaving behind different sources of parent material.

5e4b133ce0e7.title: Nutrient cycle
5e4b133ce0e7.sentence: The bodies of dead worms passively contribute mineral nutrients to the soil.

770a0b70ddf6.title: Nutrient cycle
770a0b70ddf6.sentence: The worms also mechanically modify the physical structure of the soil as they crawl about (bioturbation) and digest on the molds of organic matter they pull from the soil litter.

608166770fee.title: Nutrient cycle
608166770fee.sentence: These activities transport nutrients into the mineral layers of soil.

587e8ff71822.title: Nutrient cycle
587e8ff71822.sentence: Worms discard wastes that create worm castings containing undigested materials where bacteria and other decomposers gain access to the nutrients.

44bb2db092b0.title: Nutrient cycle
44bb2db092b0.sentence: Organic agricultural ecosystems rely on the services of biodiversity for the recycling of nutrients through soils instead of relying on the supplementation of synthetic fertilizers.

6eeef5310c8d.title: Nutrient cycle
6eeef5310c8d.sentence: Where produce from an organic farm leaves the farm gate for the market the system becomes an open cycle and nutrients may need to be replaced through alternative methods.

654675fcac09.title: Nutrient cycle
654675fcac09.sentence: Even earlier, in 1749, Carl Linnaeus wrote: "the economy of nature we understand the all-wise disposition of the creator in relation to natural things, by which they are fitted to produce general ends, and reciprocal uses", in reference to the balance of nature in his book Oeconomia Naturae.

c9d3371b4708.title: Nutrient cycle
c9d3371b4708.sentence: In this book, he captured the notion of ecological recycling: "The 'reciprocal uses' are the key to the whole idea, for 'the death, and destruction of one thing should always be subservient to the restitution of another;' thus mould spurs the decay of dead plants to nourish the soil, and the earth then 'offers again to plants from its bosom, what it has received from them.'" The basic idea of a balance of nature, however, can be traced back to the Greeks: Democritus, Epicurus, and their Roman disciple Lucretius.

30ddaed2d64e.title: Nutrient cycle
30ddaed2d64e.sentence: From 1836 to 1876, Jean Baptiste Boussingault demonstrated the nutritional necessity of minerals and nitrogen for plant growth and development.

c39f10bbbe17.title: Nutrient cycle
c39f10bbbe17.sentence: "In 1872, Cohn described the 'cycle of life' as the "entire arrangement of nature" in which the dissolution of dead organic bodies provided the materials necessary for new life.

01151d26d4c1.title: Nutrient cycle
01151d26d4c1.sentence: However, the term nutrient cycle predates biogeochemistry in a pamphlet on silviculture in 1899: "These demands by no means pass over the fact that at places where sufficient quantities of humus are available and where, in case of continuous decomposition of litter, a stable, nutrient humus is present, considerable quantities of nutrients are also available from the biogenic nutrient cycle for the standing timber.

63109d553964.title: Nutrient cycle
63109d553964.sentence: In 1926, Vernadsky coined the term biogeochemistry as a sub-discipline of geochemistry.

518bf00f2ffd.title: Immobilization (soil science)
518bf00f2ffd.sentence: Immobilization in soil science is the conversion of inorganic compounds to organic compounds by microorganisms or plants by which the compounds become inaccessible to plants.

d0f039c4ce95.title: Immobilization (soil science)
d0f039c4ce95.sentence: Immobilization is the opposite of mineralization.

07b0b9ff7673.title: Immobilization (soil science)
07b0b9ff7673.sentence: Immobilization is therefore a biological process controlled by bacteria that consume inorganic nitrogen and form amino acids and biological macromolecules (organic forms).

57c56c1ffc27.title: Immobilization (soil science)
57c56c1ffc27.sentence: In immobilization, inorganic nutrients are taken up by soil microbes and become unavailable for plant uptake.

45430ce82d8e.title: Immobilization (soil science)
45430ce82d8e.sentence: Immobilization and mineralization are continuous processes that occur concurrently whereby nitrogen of the decomposing system is steadily transformed from an inorganic to an organic state by immobilization and from an organic to an inorganic state by decay and mineralization.

aa4ddfe17455.title: Immobilization (soil science)
aa4ddfe17455.sentence: Whether nitrogen is mineralized or immobilized depends on the C/N ratio of the plant residues.

2c549f525dfa.title: Immobilization (soil science)
2c549f525dfa.sentence: If the C:N ratio of the decomposing plant material is above about 30:1 the soil microbial population may take nitrogen in mineral form (e.g. nitrate).

423187c7f159.title: Immobilization (soil science)
423187c7f159.sentence: This mineral nitrogen is said to be immobilized.

8c29f9ced60a.title: Immobilization (soil science)
8c29f9ced60a.sentence: When the C:N ratio falls below about 25:1 further decomposition results in simultaneous mineralization of nitrogen which is in excess to that required by the microbial population.

05b0eeb3cc2f.title: Immobilization (soil science)
05b0eeb3cc2f.sentence: For example, incorporating materials high in carbon to nitrogen ratio such as saw dust and straw will stimulate soil microbial activity, increase demand for nitrogen, leading to immobilization.

3b365d6ac623.title: Immobilization (soil science)
3b365d6ac623.sentence: Microorganisms out-compete plants for NH4+ and NO3- during immobilization, and therefore plants can easily become nitrogen deficient.

597a29cc08f9.title: Immobilization (soil science)
597a29cc08f9.sentence: As carbon dioxide is released via decomposition the C:N ratio of the organic matter decreases, and the microbial demand for mineral nitrogen is decreased.

8e1be7b4333b.title: Immobilization (soil science)
8e1be7b4333b.sentence: When decomposition is virtually complete soil mineral nitrogen will be higher than it was initially due to mineralization of the plant residue nitrogen.

e6ddf0da702f.title: Immobilization (soil science)
e6ddf0da702f.section: C:N Ratio > Mechanisms of nitrogen immobilization
e6ddf0da702f.sentence: There are two mechanisms of nitrogen immobilization: Nitrogen accumulation in microbial biomass and accumulation of nitrogen in by-products of microbial activity.

5cf5aa9d3619.title: Calcium cycle
5cf5aa9d3619.sentence: The calcium cycle is a transfer of calcium between dissolved and solid phases.

9e821a6c491c.title: Calcium cycle
9e821a6c491c.sentence: Calcium moves through these different media as it cycles throughout the Earth.

78c333ffc8cd.title: Calcium cycle
78c333ffc8cd.section: Calcium weathering and inputs to seawater
78c333ffc8cd.sentence: Calcium is stored in geologic reservoirs, most commonly in the form of calcium carbonate or as calcium silicate.

8cfed3002ae6.title: Calcium cycle
8cfed3002ae6.section: Calcium weathering and inputs to seawater
8cfed3002ae6.sentence: Calcium-containing rocks include calcite, dolomite, phosphate, and gypsum.

142b8d36099b.title: Calcium cycle
142b8d36099b.section: Calcium weathering and inputs to seawater
142b8d36099b.sentence: Rocks slowly dissolve by physical and chemical processes, carrying calcium ions into rivers and oceans.

fbe05475b912.title: Calcium cycle
fbe05475b912.section: Calcium weathering and inputs to seawater
fbe05475b912.sentence: Ca2+-containing minerals are often more easily weathered than Mg2+ minerals, so Ca2+ is often more enriched in waterways than Mg2+.

2a4075672eea.title: Calcium cycle
2a4075672eea.sentence: When deposited in the form of lime, it cannot be used by plants.

a574e06f754f.title: Calcium cycle
a574e06f754f.sentence: To combat this, carbon dioxide produced by plants reacts with water in the environment to produce carbonic acid.

ab3392898f75.title: Calcium cycle
ab3392898f75.sentence: Carbonic acid is then able to dissolve limestone, enabling the release of calcium ions.

83f9a9945210.title: Calcium cycle
83f9a9945210.sentence: This reaction is more readily available with smaller particles of limestone than it is with large pieces of rock due to the increased surface area.

a40d62fb2397.title: Calcium cycle
a40d62fb2397.sentence: When lime is leached into soil, calcium levels inevitably increase, both stabilising pH and enabling calcium to mix with water to form Ca2+ ions, thus making it soluble and accessible to plants to be absorbed and utilised by the root system.

1994a1b998e8.title: Calcium cycle
1994a1b998e8.sentence: The calcium ions travel up the xylem of the plant alongside water to reach the leaves.

5c38b42f2002.title: Calcium cycle
5c38b42f2002.sentence: The plant can utilise this calcium in the form of calcium pectate to stabilise cell walls and provide rigidity.

4e2c33f077fa.title: Calcium cycle
4e2c33f077fa.sentence: Calcium is also used by plant enzymes to signal growth and coordinate life-promoting processes.

53526ff154b7.title: Calcium cycle
53526ff154b7.sentence: Additionally, the release of calcium ions enables microorganisms to access phosphorus and other micro nutrients with greater ease, improving the soil ecosystem drastically thus indirectly promoting plant growth and nutrition.

c9f09102b9af.title: Calcium cycle
c9f09102b9af.sentence: Inevitable plant and animal death results in the return of calcium contained within the organism back into the soil to be utilised by other plants.

dd1a9ed201be.title: Calcium cycle
dd1a9ed201be.sentence: Decomposing organisms break them down, returning the calcium back into the soil and enabling the cycling of calcium to continue.

b7adf0d8f389.title: Calcium cycle
b7adf0d8f389.sentence: It is however important to note the modern introduction of calcium into the soil by humans (through fertilisers and other horticultural products) has resulted in a higher concentration of calcium contained within soil.

d212f974d628.title: Calcium cycle
d212f974d628.section: Biogenic calcium carbonate and the biological pump
d212f974d628.sentence: Biogenic calcium carbonate is formed when marine organisms, such as coccolithophores, corals, pteropods, and other mollusks transform calcium ions and bicarbonate into shells and exoskeletons of calcite or aragonite, both forms of calcium carbonate.

dd1258bb8ded.title: Calcium cycle
dd1258bb8ded.section: Biogenic calcium carbonate and the biological pump
dd1258bb8ded.sentence: This is the dominant sink for dissolved calcium in the ocean.

f42880a1deb5.title: Calcium cycle
f42880a1deb5.section: Biogenic calcium carbonate and the biological pump
f42880a1deb5.sentence: This is the origin of both marine and terrestrial limestone.

9a2feaa5683f.title: Nitrogen cycle
9a2feaa5683f.sentence: Bacteria and fungi convert this organic nitrogen into ammonia and sometimes ammonium through a series of processes called ammonification or mineralization.

058b25d3666c.title: Nitrogen cycle
058b25d3666c.sentence: When a plant or animal dies or an animal expels waste, the initial form of nitrogen is organic, present in forms such as amino acids and DNA.

524285221f12.title: Nitrogen cycle
524285221f12.sentence: This is the last step in the nitrogen cycle step involving organic compounds.

01d42f44aeee.title: Nitrogen cycle
01d42f44aeee.sentence: Myriad enzymes are involved including dehydrogenases, proteases, and deaminases such as glutamate dehydrogenase and glutamine synthetase.

1c88dea0629e.title: Nitrogen cycle
1c88dea0629e.sentence: Nitrogen mineralization and ammonification have a positive correlation with organic nitrogen in the soil, soil microbial biomass, and average annual precipitation.

6bb8f21cffb8.title: Nitrogen cycle
6bb8f21cffb8.sentence: They also respond closely to changes in temperature.

9b315cec14e8.title: Nitrogen cycle
9b315cec14e8.sentence: However, these processes slow in the presence of vegetation with high carbon to nitrogen ratios and fertilization with sugar.

a7707fe20852.title: Nitrification
a7707fe20852.sentence: Together with ammonification, nitrification forms a mineralization process that refers to the complete decomposition of organic material, with the release of available nitrogen compounds.

bf18f1b3b840.title: Fen
bf18f1b3b840.section: Hydrology and biogeochemistry > Nutrient cycling > Nitrogen
bf18f1b3b840.sentence: When the organic matter in peat is decomposed in the absence of oxygen, ammonium is produced via ammonification.

32f3d0e23dab.title: Nitrification
32f3d0e23dab.sentence: Nitrification is the biological oxidation of ammonia to nitrate via the intermediary nitrite.

ee0d672d23c6.title: Nitrification
ee0d672d23c6.sentence: Nitrification is an important step in the nitrogen cycle in soil.

bf410560c91d.title: Nitrification
bf410560c91d.sentence: Nitrification is an aerobic process performed by small groups of autotrophic bacteria and archaea.

9488a647bba9.title: Nitrification
9488a647bba9.sentence: Both steps are producing energy to be coupled to ATP synthesis.

a6634ab186fe.title: Nitrification
a6634ab186fe.sentence: Nitrifying organisms are chemoautotrophs, and use carbon dioxide as their carbon source for growth.

58df98640a6f.title: Nitrification
58df98640a6f.sentence: The process of nitrification begins with the first stage of ammonia oxidation, where ammonia (NH3) or ammonium (NH4+) get converted into nitrite (NO2−).

dab546d1745f.title: Nitrification
dab546d1745f.sentence: This first stage is sometimes known as nitritation.

209dedda85fe.title: Nitrification
209dedda85fe.sentence: It is performed by two groups of organisms, ammonia-oxidizing bacteria (AOB) and ammonia-oxidizing archaea (AOA).

a0a1e5fb9a3b.title: Nitrification
a0a1e5fb9a3b.sentence: The transformation of ammonia to nitrite is usually the rate limiting step of nitrification.

603cbcb09009.title: Nitrification
603cbcb09009.sentence: The second step of nitrification is the oxidation of nitrite into nitrate.

ad0aadc21d71.title: Nitrification
ad0aadc21d71.sentence: This process is sometimes known as nitratation.

68b71ba865d1.title: Nitrification
68b71ba865d1.sentence: Nitrite oxidation is conducted by nitrite-oxidizing bacteria (NOB) from the taxa Nitrospirota, Nitrospinota, Pseudomonadota and Chloroflexota.

9764f3032295.title: Nitrification
9764f3032295.sentence: The process of complete nitrification may occur through separate organisms or entirely within one organism, as in comammox bacteria.

7ab8ee514ac8.section: Factors Affecting Nitrification Rates > Soil conditions
7ab8ee514ac8.sentence: Soil conditions that have an effect on nitrification rates include:

0b195cb697ce.section: Factors Affecting Nitrification Rates > Soil conditions

4da5b0204b01.title: Nitrification
4da5b0204b01.sentence: Soil, consisting of polyanionic clays and silicates, generally has a net anionic charge.

c71ca80d7fde.title: Nitrification
c71ca80d7fde.sentence: Consequently, ammonium (NH4+) binds tightly to the soil, but nitrate ions (NO3−) do not.

b8f1d5bce71f.title: Nitrification
b8f1d5bce71f.sentence: Nitrification is important in agricultural systems, where fertilizer is often applied as ammonia.

a77ba29eff1a.title: Nitrification
a77ba29eff1a.sentence: Conversion of this ammonia to nitrate increases nitrogen leaching because nitrate is more water-soluble than ammonia.

0d2b5a8e14da.title: Nitrification
0d2b5a8e14da.sentence: Nitrification inhibitors are also of interest from an environmental standpoint because of the production of nitrates and nitrous oxide from the nitrification process.

b346fbfff072.title: Nitrification
b346fbfff072.sentence: Nitrous oxide (N2O), although its atmospheric concentration is much lower than that of CO2, has a global warming potential of about 300 times greater than carbon dioxide and contributes 6% of planetary warming due to greenhouse gases.

823efc0790f9.title: Nitrifying bacteria
823efc0790f9.sentence: Nitrifying bacteria are chemolithotrophic organisms that include species of genera such as Nitrosomonas, Nitrosococcus, Nitrobacter, Nitrospina, Nitrospira and Nitrococcus.

c742700186fd.title: Nitrifying bacteria
c742700186fd.sentence: These bacteria get their energy from the oxidation of inorganic nitrogen compounds.

21221e74f792.title: Nitrifying bacteria
21221e74f792.sentence: Types include ammonia-oxidizing bacteria (AOB) and nitrite-oxidizing bacteria (NOB).

6a9a96513b8e.title: Nitrifying bacteria
6a9a96513b8e.sentence: Nitrification in nature is a two-step oxidation process of ammonium (NH+4) or ammonia (NH3) to nitrite (NO−2) and then to nitrate (NO−3) catalyzed by two ubiquitous bacterial groups growing together.

90df647c051e.title: Nitrifying bacteria
90df647c051e.sentence: The first reaction is oxidation of ammonium to nitrite by ammonia oxidizing bacteria (AOB) represented by members of Betaproteobacteria and Gammaproteobacteria.

fe42785eb42a.title: Nitrifying bacteria
fe42785eb42a.sentence: The second reaction is oxidation of nitrite (NO−2) to nitrate by nitrite-oxidizing bacteria (NOB), represented by the members of Nitrospinota, Nitrospirota, Pseudomonadota, and Chloroflexota.

b10dc0766259.title: Nitrifying bacteria
b10dc0766259.sentence: Many species of nitrifying bacteria have complex internal membrane systems that are the location for key enzymes in nitrification: ammonia monooxygenase (which oxidizes ammonia to hydroxylamine), hydroxylamine oxidoreductase (which oxidizes hydroxylamine to nitric oxide - which is further oxidized to nitrite by a currently unidentified enzyme), and nitrite oxidoreductase (which oxidizes nitrite to nitrate).

de844f0f46c0.title: Nitrifying bacteria
de844f0f46c0.sentence: Nitrifying bacteria are present in distinct taxonomical groups and are found in highest numbers where considerable amounts of ammonia are present (such as areas with extensive protein decomposition, and sewage treatment plants).

2cec8d66ff49.title: Nitrification
2cec8d66ff49.sentence: They contribute to the transformation of ammonia derived from organic matter decomposition or fertilizers into nitrite, which subsequently serves as a substrate for nitrite-oxidizing bacteria (NOB).

61ee232bc556.sentence: This two-step process was described already in 1890 by the Ukrainian microbiologist Sergei Winogradsky.

e5d98bff0cd2.title: Nitrosomonas
e5d98bff0cd2.sentence: Nitrosomonas is a genus of Gram-negative bacteria belonging to the class Betaproteobacteria.

6e14bb347b93.title: Nitrosomonas
6e14bb347b93.sentence: It is one of the five genera of ammonia-oxidizing bacteria and, as an obligate chemolithoautotroph, uses ammonia (NH3) as an energy source and carbon dioxide (CO2) as a carbon source in the presence of oxygen.

c2bae4aad82c.title: Nitrosomonas
c2bae4aad82c.sentence: The oxidation of ammonia to hydroxylamine is catalyzed by ammonia monooxygenase (AMO), a membrane-bound, multisubstrate enzyme.

32db798c2a08.title: Nitrosomonas

1fb9165ae5dc.title: Nitrosomonas

96e380f19c91.title: Nitrosomonas
96e380f19c91.sentence: Nitrosomonas species are generally found in the highest numbers in habitats with an abundance of ammonia (examples include environments with plentiful protein decomposition and in wastewater treatment) and thrive in a pH range of 6.0–9.0 and a temperature range of 20–30 °C (68–86 °F).

88e3ac50392a.title: Nitrosomonas
88e3ac50392a.sentence: They are especially prevalent in shallow coastal sediments and in upwelling zones, such as the Peruvian coast and the Arabian Sea, but can also be found in fertilized soils.

b42a2b5cc4b7.title: Nitrosomonas
b42a2b5cc4b7.sentence: In agriculture, nitrification by Nitrosomonas is problematic because the oxidized nitrite from ammonia can persist in the soil, leading to leaching and reduced availability for plants.

056086accfec.title: Nitrosomonas
056086accfec.sentence: Nitrification can be slowed by inhibitors that retard the oxidation of ammonia to nitrites by inhibiting the activity of Nitrosomonas and other ammonia-oxidizing bacteria, thereby minimizing or preventing the loss of nitrate.

628deddc8ad3.title: Nitrosomonas
628deddc8ad3.sentence: Nitrosomonas is used in activated sludge in aerobic wastewater treatment; nitrification treatment reduces nitrogen compounds in the water, avoiding environmental issues such as ammonia toxicity and groundwater contamination.

d3f9e1ed9f8c.title: Reactive nitrogen
d3f9e1ed9f8c.sentence: Reactive nitrogen ("Nr"), also known as fixed nitrogen, refers to all forms of nitrogen present in the environment except for molecular nitrogen (N 2).

f794b8f668d9.title: Reactive nitrogen
f794b8f668d9.sentence: While nitrogen is an essential element for life on Earth, molecular nitrogen is comparatively unreactive, and must be converted to other chemical forms via nitrogen fixation before it can be used for growth.

29e69ef9b871.title: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle
29e69ef9b871.sentence: N2 has a strong triple bond, and so a significant amount of energy (226 kcal mol−1) is required to convert N2 to Nr.

98c7b6108794.title: Reactive nitrogen

c922e2431ca7.title: Reactive nitrogen

ba78068666b2.sentence: The Haber process, also called the Haber–Bosch process, is the main industrial method for making ammonia.

d1b02bbf81b2.title: Haber process

0d922783822f.title: Haber process

70e105aaa466.title: Haber process

978cc0ac58af.title: Haber process

ed635a339953.title: Haber process

1c6d4f376ce1.title: Haber process
1c6d4f376ce1.sentence: Thus, the Haber process serves as the "detonator of the population explosion", enabling the global population to increase from 1.6 billion in 1900 to 7.7 billion by November 2018.

f4c4d98aed13.title: Haber process

d70ba1a2647d.title: Haber process
d70ba1a2647d.sentence: The energy-intensity of the process contributes to climate change and other environmental problems such as the leaching of nitrates into groundwater, rivers, ponds, and lakes; expanding dead zones in coastal ocean waters, resulting from recurrent eutrophication; atmospheric deposition of nitrates and ammonia affecting natural ecosystems; higher emissions of nitrous oxide (N2O), now the third most important greenhouse gas following CO2 and CH4.

6e9dddde5b61.title: Haber process
6e9dddde5b61.sentence: The use of synthetic nitrogen fertilisers reduces the incentive for farmers to use more sustainable crop rotations which include legumes for their natural nitrogen-fixing ability.

4fb1e4236507.title: Iron cycle
4fb1e4236507.sentence: The iron cycle (Fe) is the biogeochemical cycle of iron through the atmosphere, hydrosphere, biosphere and lithosphere.

65ca9adbea24.title: Iron cycle
65ca9adbea24.sentence: The cycling of iron between its +2 and +3 oxidation states is referred to as the iron cycle.

b10196a5eb15.title: Iron cycle
b10196a5eb15.sentence: Iron is an essential micronutrient for life form.

1b4f30a7651a.title: Iron cycle
1b4f30a7651a.sentence: It is a key component of hemoglobin, important to nitrogen fixation as part of the Nitrogenase enzyme family, and as part of the iron-sulfur core of ferredoxin it facilitates electron transport in chloroplasts, eukaryotic mitochondria, and bacteria.

6a53d9d3edf3.title: Iron cycle
6a53d9d3edf3.sentence: The ferric form, Fe3+, is more stable in the presence of oxygen gas.

89a46fd085e3.title: Iron cycle
89a46fd085e3.sentence: While Fe is highly abundant in the Earth's crust, it is less common in oxygenated surface waters.

96c6d02a3042.title: Iron cycle
96c6d02a3042.sentence: Due to the high reactivity of Fe2+ with oxygen and low solubility of Fe3+, iron is a limiting nutrient in most regions of the world.

91c16bb8984e.title: Iron cycle
91c16bb8984e.sentence: Iron-oxidizing bacteria play an important role in the iron cycle by converting soluble ferrous iron, Fe (II), into insoluble ferric iron, Fe (III).

862ce94b0ebf.title: Iron cycle
862ce94b0ebf.sentence: Extracellular electron transfer occurs when a bacterium, in the absence of oxygen, utilizes metals in its environment as a final electron acceptor.

677b7e56b765.title: Iron cycle
677b7e56b765.sentence: Examples of bacteria such as Shewanella spp., Geobacter spp., and some Enterococcus spp. use this form of metabolism.

f0495d30e68a.title: Iron cycle
f0495d30e68a.sentence: This is an important metabolic process because it reduces ferric iron to ferrous iron, which is more readily bioavailable.

5711b5a4a038.title: Iron cycle
5711b5a4a038.sentence: Fe(III) can form iron hydroxides, which bind tightly to phosphorus, removing it from the bioavailable phosphorus pool, limiting primary productivity.

99221a6d159b.title: Iron cycle
99221a6d159b.sentence: In anoxic conditions, Fe(III) can be reduced, used by microbes to be the final electron acceptor from either organic carbon or H2.

82463e5c0d76.title: Iron cycle
82463e5c0d76.sentence: This releases the phosphorus back into the water for biological use.

5c38b417728f.title: Iron cycle
5c38b417728f.sentence: In anoxic conditions, Fe(II) can donate an electron that is accepted by NO3− which is oxidized to several different forms of nitrogen compounds, NO2−, N2O, N2, and NH4+, while Fe(II) is reduced to Fe(III).

4d708be4544d.title: Oxygen cycle
4d708be4544d.sentence: The oxygen cycle refers to the various movements of oxygen through the Earth's atmosphere (air), biosphere (flora and fauna), hydrosphere (water bodies and glaciers) and the lithosphere (the Earth's crust).

a5332a8dc75e.title: Oxygen cycle
a5332a8dc75e.sentence: It is the biogeochemical cycle of oxygen atoms between different oxidation states in ions, oxides and molecules through redox reactions within and between the spheres/reservoirs of the planet Earth.

795d94bfeb82.title: Oxygen cycle
795d94bfeb82.sentence: By far the largest reservoir of Earth's oxygen is within the silicate and oxide minerals of the crust and mantle (99.5% by weight).

362ac67ea126.title: Oxygen cycle

3fcb9d63d702.title: Denitrification
3fcb9d63d702.sentence: Denitrification is a microbially facilitated process where nitrate (NO3−) is reduced and ultimately produces molecular nitrogen (N2) through a series of intermediate gaseous nitrogen oxide products.

a6bcb7913a9b.title: Denitrification
a6bcb7913a9b.sentence: Facultative anaerobic bacteria perform denitrification as a type of respiration that reduces oxidized forms of nitrogen in response to the oxidation of an electron donor such as organic matter.

477a522e7bd0.title: Nitrogen cycle

25a35f58c5e6.title: Denitrification
25a35f58c5e6.sentence: The preferred nitrogen electron acceptors in order of most to least thermodynamically favorable include nitrate (NO3−), nitrite (NO2−), nitric oxide (NO), nitrous oxide (N2O), finally resulting in the production of N2, completing the nitrogen cycle.

1eef2ebbfa6d.title: Denitrification
1eef2ebbfa6d.sentence: Denitrifying microbes require a very low oxygen concentration of less than 10%, as well as an electron donor, like organic C, hydrogen gas, or reduced sulfur for energy.

64830f581189.title: Nitrogen cycle
64830f581189.sentence: Denitrification happens in anaerobic conditions e.g. waterlogged soils.

98ba700cd506.title: Nitrogen cycle
98ba700cd506.sentence: The denitrifying bacteria use nitrates in the soil to carry out respiration and consequently produce nitrogen gas, which is inert and unavailable to plants.

cd77bb2620b5.title: Denitrification
cd77bb2620b5.sentence: Denitrification can leak N2O, which is an ozone-depleting substance and a greenhouse gas that can have a considerable influence on global warming.

00ee5d54907b.title: Denitrification
00ee5d54907b.sentence: Soil pH and texture are both factors that can moderate denitrification, with higher pH levels driving the reaction more to completion.

9fd38c357f59.title: Denitrification
9fd38c357f59.sentence: Additionally, environmental factors can also influence whether denitrification proceeds to completion, characterized by the complete reduction of NO3− to N2 rather than releasing N2O as an end product.

66c1bbae5b08.title: Denitrification
66c1bbae5b08.sentence: Nutrient composition, particularly the ratio of carbon to nitrogen, is a strong contributor to complete denitrification, with a 2:1 ratio of C:N being able to facilitate full nitrate reduction regardless of temperature or carbon source.

962272471bbe.title: Denitrification
962272471bbe.sentence: Since denitrification can remove NO3−, reducing its leaching to groundwater, it can be strategically used to treat sewage or animal residues of high nitrogen content.

a28f3256436a.title: Denitrifying bacteria
a28f3256436a.sentence: Denitrifying bacteria are a diverse group of bacteria that encompass many different phyla.

28cef057d944.title: Denitrifying bacteria
28cef057d944.sentence: This group of bacteria, together with denitrifying fungi and archaea, is capable of performing denitrification as part of the nitrogen cycle.

084d26460f10.title: Denitrifying bacteria
084d26460f10.sentence: Denitrification is performed by a variety of denitrifying bacteria that are widely distributed in soils and sediments and that use oxidized nitrogen compounds such as nitrate and nitrite in the absence of oxygen as a terminal electron acceptor.

38de7712273e.title: Denitrifying bacteria
38de7712273e.sentence: Denitrifying bacteria have been identified in over 50 genera with over 125 different species and are estimated to represent 10-15% of bacteria population in water, soil and sediment.

a6c314dbf887.title: Denitrifying bacteria
a6c314dbf887.sentence: The majority of denitrifying bacteria are facultative aerobic heterotrophs that switch from aerobic respiration to denitrification when oxygen as an available terminal electron acceptor (TEA) runs out.

225955d7480b.sentence: Human activities account for over one-third of N2O emissions (35% of total global N2O emissions), with about 20% originating from agricultural sources such as fertilizer use, manure management, and aquaculture.
