f22e9ebc57b1.title: Nitrogen cycle
f22e9ebc57b1.section: Consequence of human modification of the nitrogen cycle > Impacts on human health: nitrate accumulation in drinking water
f22e9ebc57b1.sentence: Excessive use of N-fertilizer in agriculture has been a significant source of nitrate pollution in groundwater and surface water.

7a74737f455f.title: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle
7a74737f455f.sentence: During the 1970s scientists began to recognize that N inputs were accumulating in the environment and affecting ecosystems.
7a74737f455f.key: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle

25bfa6a4c33e.title: Nitrogen cycle
25bfa6a4c33e.sentence: Plants can absorb nitrate or ammonium from the soil by their root hairs.

dcca1c3ac4fe.title: Nitrogen cycle
dcca1c3ac4fe.sentence: If nitrate is absorbed, it is first reduced to nitrite ions and then ammonium ions for incorporation into amino acids, nucleic acids, and chlorophyll.

33e8f9100c6c.title: Nitrogen cycle
33e8f9100c6c.sentence: In plants that have a symbiotic relationship with rhizobia, some nitrogen is assimilated in the form of ammonium ions directly from the nodules.

d64b2672ca4e.title: Nitrogen cycle
d64b2672ca4e.sentence: The plant provides amino acids to the bacteroids so ammonia assimilation is not required and the bacteroids pass amino acids (with the newly fixed nitrogen) back to the plant, thus forming an interdependent relationship.

8ddf1cde9b56.title: Nitrogen cycle
8ddf1cde9b56.sentence: While many animals, fungi, and other heterotrophic organisms obtain nitrogen by ingestion of amino acids, nucleotides, and other small organic molecules, other heterotrophs (including many bacteria) are able to utilize inorganic compounds, such as ammonium as sole N sources.

4b263eff24f7.title: Mercury cycle
4b263eff24f7.sentence: The mercury cycle is a biogeochemical cycle influenced by natural and anthropogenic processes that transform mercury through multiple chemical forms and environments.

74aaae0633ce.title: Mercury cycle
74aaae0633ce.sentence: Mercury exists in three oxidation states: 0 (elemental mercury), I (mercurous mercury), and II (mercuric mercury).

30047681186f.title: Mercury cycle
30047681186f.sentence: Weathering of minerals and geothermal activity release mercury to the environment.

999abc36ed73.title: Mercury cycle
999abc36ed73.sentence: Active volcanoes are another significant primary source of natural mercury.

f9ad3c92f8fb.title: Mercury cycle
f9ad3c92f8fb.sentence: There are only a few significant mercury ores, most notably the mercury sulfide mineral, cinnabar.

218e90778216.title: Mercury cycle
218e90778216.sentence: Anthropogenic primary sources of mercury include gold mining, burning coal, and production of non-iron metals, such as copper or lead.

c3880586eecd.title: Mercury cycle
c3880586eecd.sentence: Annually, over 5000 metric tons of mercury is released to the atmosphere by primary emissions and secondary re-emissions.

7a8a45f243a7.title: Mercury cycle
7a8a45f243a7.sentence: Inorganic mercury can be converted by bacteria and archaea into methylmercury ([CH3Hg]+), which bioaccumulates in marine species such as tuna and swordfish and biomagnifies further up the food chain.

410178968f1b.title: Biogeochemical cycle
410178968f1b.sentence: This place is called a reservoir, which, for example, includes such things as coal deposits that are storing carbon for a long period of time.

2f1826d6340f.title: Biogeochemical cycle
2f1826d6340f.sentence: When chemicals are held for only short periods of time, they are being held in exchange pools.

69ad4ee92d51.title: Biogeochemical cycle
69ad4ee92d51.sentence: The amount of time that a chemical is held in one place is called its residence time or turnover time (also called the renewal time or exit age).

47c4964a363d.title: Biogeochemical cycle
47c4964a363d.sentence: The chemicals are sometimes held for long periods of time in one place.

1259beec7531.title: Biogeochemical cycle
1259beec7531.sentence: Examples of exchange pools include plants and animals.

84dbf41402d0.title: Biogeochemical cycle
84dbf41402d0.sentence: Plants and animals temporarily use carbon in their systems and then release it back into the air or surrounding medium.

d46d3decd600.title: Biogeochemical cycle
d46d3decd600.sentence: Generally, reservoirs are abiotic factors whereas exchange pools are biotic factors.

dd2a06fe6b79.title: Biogeochemistry
dd2a06fe6b79.sentence: Biogeochemistry is the scientific discipline that involves the study of the chemical, physical, geological, and biological processes and reactions that govern the composition of the natural environment (including the biosphere, the cryosphere, the hydrosphere, the pedosphere, the atmosphere, and the lithosphere).

8c39854d07eb.title: Biogeochemistry
8c39854d07eb.sentence: In particular, biogeochemistry is the study of biogeochemical cycles, the cycles of chemical elements such as carbon and nitrogen, and their interactions with and incorporation into living things transported through earth scale biological systems in space and time.

cabffe6032ad.title: Biogeochemistry
cabffe6032ad.sentence: Particular emphasis is placed on the study of carbon, nitrogen, oxygen, sulfur, iron, and phosphorus cycles.

873724bf85ca.title: Biogeochemistry
873724bf85ca.sentence: Agricultural interest in 18th-century soil chemistry led to better understanding of nutrients and their connection to biochemical processes.

c09784889bd6.title: Biogeochemistry
c09784889bd6.sentence: This relationship between the cycles of organic life and their chemical products was further expanded upon by Dumas and Boussingault in a 1844 paper that is considered an important milestone in the development of biogeochemistry.

c0051da9500a.title: Biogeochemistry
c0051da9500a.sentence: The founder of modern biogeochemistry was Vladimir Vernadsky, a Russian and Ukrainian scientist whose 1926 book The Biosphere, in the tradition of Mendeleev, formulated a physics of the Earth as a living whole.

c7f5af2a9ee7.title: Biogeochemistry
c7f5af2a9ee7.sentence: Biogeochemistry is a systems science closely related to systems ecology.

dbd19408ab8d.title: Biogeochemistry
dbd19408ab8d.sentence: Since this is a highly interdisciplinary field, these are situated within a wide range of host disciplines including: atmospheric sciences, biology, ecology, geomicrobiology, environmental chemistry, geology, oceanography and soil science.

6749c55f689c.title: Biogeochemistry
6749c55f689c.sentence: Some important research fields for biogeochemistry include:

f7cce1b2cb32.title: Biogeochemistry
f7cce1b2cb32.sentence: - soil and water acidification recovery processes

0edf7012ecef.title: Biogeochemistry
0edf7012ecef.sentence: Evolutionary biogeochemistry is a branch of modern biogeochemistry that applies the study of biogeochemical cycles to the geologic history of the Earth.

3f7e2be3c3a1.title: Biogeochemistry
3f7e2be3c3a1.sentence: This field investigates the origin of biogeochemical cycles and how they have changed throughout the planet's history, specifically in relation to the evolution of life.

e47445b48b1b.title: Diazotroph
e47445b48b1b.sentence: Diazotrophs are organisms capable of nitrogen fixation, i.e. converting the relatively inert diatomic nitrogen (N2) in Earth's atmosphere into bioavailable compound forms such as ammonia.

3ae1ea20eecd.title: Diazotroph
3ae1ea20eecd.sentence: Diazotrophs are typically microorganisms such as bacteria and archaea, with examples being rhizobia and Frankia and Azospirillum.

34aa52608dbf.title: Diazotroph
34aa52608dbf.sentence: Diazotrophs are scattered across Bacteria taxonomic groups (as well as a couple of Archaea).

2e324cd81c11.title: Diazotroph
2e324cd81c11.sentence: Nitrogen fixation is an energetically costly process and is thus reduced when other sources of nitrogen are available, and, for many species, when oxygen is at high partial pressure.

45dba3709a64.title: Diazotroph
45dba3709a64.sentence: Symbiotic diazotrophs have traditionally been considered to be more relevant to global nitrogen cycles, as the plant hosts may produce a favorable environment for diazotrophy, but free-living diazotrophs are also significant nitrogen fixers.

4962dfe34935.title: Diazotroph
4962dfe34935.sentence: - Anaerobes—these are obligate anaerobes that cannot tolerate oxygen even if they are not fixing nitrogen.

d5d90f44c204.title: Diazotroph
d5d90f44c204.sentence: They live in habitats low in oxygen, such as soils and decaying vegetable matter.

10a21e6196ff.title: Nitrogen fixation
10a21e6196ff.sentence: Several obligately anaerobic bacteria fix nitrogen including many (but not all) Clostridium spp. Some archaea such as Methanosarcina acetivorans also fix nitrogen, and several other methanogenic taxa, are significant contributors to nitrogen fixation in oxygen-deficient soils.

a8235a6d7e57.title: Diazotroph
a8235a6d7e57.sentence: Azotobacter vinelandii is the most studied of these organisms.

c0d653b4d877.title: Diazotroph
c0d653b4d877.sentence: It uses very high respiration rates, and protective compounds, to prevent oxygen damage.

b5110c27569f.title: Diazotroph
b5110c27569f.sentence: The fern association is important agriculturally: the water fern Azolla harbouring Anabaena is an important green manure for rice culture.

0ff66d79186a.title: Diazotroph
0ff66d79186a.sentence: In the terrestrial ecosystem, the diazotroph fix the (N2) from the atmosphere and provide the available nitrogen for the primary producer.

bbd8a61afe13.title: Diazotroph
bbd8a61afe13.sentence: Also the available nitrogen fixed by the diazotroph is environmentally sustainable, which can reduce the use of fertilizer, which can be an important topic in agricultural research.

fe0184462caa.title: Phosphorus cycle
fe0184462caa.section: Phosphorus in the environment > Phosphatic minerals
fe0184462caa.sentence: The availability of phosphorus in an ecosystem is restricted by its rate of release during weathering.

f277790c618d.title: Phosphorus cycle
f277790c618d.section: Phosphorus in the environment > Phosphatic minerals
f277790c618d.sentence: The release of phosphorus from apatite dissolution is a key control on ecosystem productivity.

1569d03b17a1.title: Phosphorus cycle
1569d03b17a1.section: Phosphorus in the environment > Phosphatic minerals
1569d03b17a1.sentence: The primary mineral with significant phosphorus content, apatite [Ca5(PO4)3OH] undergoes carbonation.

3a759614bd73.title: Phosphorus cycle
3a759614bd73.section: Phosphorus in the environment > Phosphatic minerals
3a759614bd73.sentence: Little of this released phosphorus is taken up by biota, as it mainly reacts with other soil minerals.

2b002a39f991.title: Phosphorus cycle
2b002a39f991.section: Phosphorus in the environment > Phosphatic minerals
2b002a39f991.sentence: This leads to phosphorus becoming unavailable to organisms in the later stage of weathering and soil development as it will precipitate into rocks.

1756e6cc943c.title: Phosphorus cycle
1756e6cc943c.sentence: On the land, phosphorus gradually becomes less available to plants over thousands of years, since it is slowly lost in runoff.

bc289996d3cf.title: Phosphorus cycle
bc289996d3cf.section: Phosphorus in the environment > Phosphatic minerals
bc289996d3cf.sentence: Available phosphorus is found in a biogeochemical cycle in the upper soil profile, while phosphorus found at lower depths is primarily involved in geochemical reactions with secondary minerals.

a6b16dea1a1d.title: Phosphorus cycle
a6b16dea1a1d.section: Phosphorus in the environment > Dust Storms
a6b16dea1a1d.sentence: Although phosphorus does not have a major atmospheric component, phosphorus sediments can be moved during dust storms.

6c30182d0a59.title: Phosphorus cycle
6c30182d0a59.section: Phosphorus in the environment > Dust Storms
6c30182d0a59.sentence: Most of Earth's phosphorus is in rocks, and dust contains weathered rock particles from this parent material.

8150b093636b.title: Phosphorus cycle
8150b093636b.section: Phosphorus in the environment > Dust Storms
8150b093636b.sentence: Phosphorus carried in by wind from Northern Africa to the Amazon basin is thought to play a significant role supporting the rich biodiversity of the Amazon rainforest.

631a51577da5.title: Phosphorus cycle
631a51577da5.section: Phosphorus in the environment > Phosphorus cycling
631a51577da5.sentence: This process can lead to the low level of dissolved phosphorus concentrations in soil solution.

e2af6520a343.title: Phosphate solubilizing bacteria
e2af6520a343.sentence: However, a large portion of soluble inorganic phosphate which is applied to the soil as chemical fertilizer is immobilized rapidly and becomes unavailable to plants.

14707cfca30e.title: Phosphorus cycle
14707cfca30e.section: Phosphorus in the environment > Phosphorus cycling
14707cfca30e.sentence: Various physiological strategies are used by plants and microorganisms for obtaining phosphorus from this low level of phosphorus concentration.

d356b12a4f59.title: Phosphate solubilizing bacteria
d356b12a4f59.sentence: Phosphate is often adsorbed onto the surface of different type of minerals, for example iron containing minerals.

6f023901ca2b.title: Phosphate solubilizing bacteria
6f023901ca2b.sentence: Recent data suggest that bacteria growing under phosphorus starvation release iron-chelating molecules.

38eca4db6737.title: Phosphate solubilizing bacteria
38eca4db6737.sentence: Considering the geochemical interaction between these two elements, the authors suggest that some bacteria can dissolve iron-containing minerals in order to access the adsorbed phosphate.

4c7d74195033.title: Phosphorus cycle
4c7d74195033.sentence: In poorly drained soils or in areas where snowmelt can cause periodic waterlogging, reducing conditions can be attained in 7–10 days.

ed656614efb9.title: Phosphorus cycle
ed656614efb9.sentence: This causes a sharp increase in phosphorus concentration in solution, and phosphorus can be leached.

c6c45bfd3fe0.title: Phosphorus cycle
c6c45bfd3fe0.sentence: In addition, reducing the soil causes a shift in phosphorus from resilient to more labile forms.

a62c4946c193.title: Silica cycle
a62c4946c193.sentence: The silica cycle is the biogeochemical cycle in which biogenic silica is transported between the Earth's systems.

e27d2f47eece.title: Silica cycle
e27d2f47eece.sentence: The primary source of silicate to the terrestrial biosphere is weathering.

f1d98fb09f3f.title: Silica cycle
f1d98fb09f3f.sentence: The process and rate of weathering is variable, depending on rainfall, runoff, vegetation, lithology, and topography.

2d49a1c0d84a.title: Silica cycle
2d49a1c0d84a.sentence: Plants can readily uptake silicate in the form of H4SiO4 for the formation of phytoliths.

2d45b9f7d252.title: Silica cycle
2d45b9f7d252.sentence: Phytoliths are tiny rigid structures found within plant cells that aid in the structural integrity of the plant.

fc9b7e74a642.title: Silica cycle
fc9b7e74a642.sentence: Phytoliths also serve to protect the plants from consumption by herbivores who are unable to consume and digest silica-rich plants efficiently.

61aabad173dc.title: Silica cycle
61aabad173dc.sentence: Silica release from phytolith degradation or dissolution is estimated to occur at a rate double that of global silicate mineral weathering.

77ce71e9568d.title: Silica cycle
77ce71e9568d.sentence: The major sink of the terrestrial silica cycle is export to the ocean by rivers.

d6a9756b409d.title: Silica cycle
d6a9756b409d.sentence: The rate of this transport is approximately 6 Tmol Si yr−1.

867baf800c44.title: Silica cycle
867baf800c44.sentence: The rise in agriculture of the past 400 years has increased the exposure rocks and soils, which has resulted in increased rates of silicate weathering.

249aa8828e76.title: Silica cycle
249aa8828e76.sentence: In turn, the leaching of amorphous silica stocks from soils has also increased, delivering higher concentrations of dissolved silica in rivers.

31de0ccf70a8.title: Silica cycle
31de0ccf70a8.sentence: The silica cycle has significant overlap with the carbon cycle (see carbonate–silicate cycle) and plays an important role in the sequestration of carbon through continental weathering, biogenic export and burial as oozes on geologic timescales.

14570b5ba080.title: Nitrification
14570b5ba080.sentence: When comparing AOB and AOA, AOA dominate in both soils and marine environments, suggesting that Nitrososphaerota (formerly Thaumarchaeota) may be greater contributors to ammonia oxidation in these environments.

7605c4268de7.title: Nitrification
7605c4268de7.sentence: Prior to the discovery of archaea capable of ammonia oxidation, ammonia-oxidizing bacteria (AOB) were considered the only organisms capable of ammonia oxidation.

20f2c41276f2.title: Nitrification
20f2c41276f2.sentence: Since their discovery in 2005, two isolates of AOAs have been cultivated: Nitrosopumilus maritimus and Nitrososphaera viennensis.

dbee776de067.title: Nitrification
dbee776de067.sentence: Crenarchaeol, which is generally thought to be produced exclusively by AOA (specifically Nitrososphaerota), has been proposed as a biomarker for AOA and ammonia oxidation.

1694fb7a213d.title: Nitrification
1694fb7a213d.sentence: In 1877, Jean-Jacques Schloesing and Achille Müntz, two French agricultural chemists working in Paris, proved that nitrification is indeed microbially mediated process by the experiments with liquid sewage and artificial soil matrix (sterilized sand with powdered chalk).

b4b73b674980.title: Nitrification
b4b73b674980.sentence: R. Warington made also the first observation that nitrification is a two-step process in 1879 which was confirmed by John Munro in 1886.

f0a3a1474489.title: Nitrification
f0a3a1474489.sentence: The idea that oxidation of ammonia to nitrate is in fact a biological process was first given by Louis Pasteur in 1862.

d02dbaee4195.title: Nitrification
d02dbaee4195.sentence: Their findings were confirmed soon (in 1878) by Robert Warington who was investigating nitrification ability of garden soil at the Rothamsted experimental station in Harpenden in England.

9744a321fd16.title: Nitrification
9744a321fd16.sentence: The first pure nitrifier (ammonia-oxidizing) was most probably isolated in 1890 by Percy Frankland and Grace Frankland, two English scientists from Scotland.

bb278f98fc90.title: Nitrification
bb278f98fc90.sentence: S. Winogradsky succeeded just one year later in 1891.

74bc15e1a373.title: Bioavailability (soil)
74bc15e1a373.sentence: Bioavailability, in environmental and soil sciences, represents the amount of an element or compound that is accessible to an organism for uptake or adsorption across its cellular membrane.

b8ae78d866aa.title: Bioavailability (soil)
b8ae78d866aa.sentence: In environmental and agricultural applications, bioavailability most often refers to availability of contaminants, such as organic pollutants or heavy metals, in soil systems and is also used frequently in determining potential risk of land application of sewage sludge or other inorganic/organic waste materials.

8778b418cfdb.title: Bioavailability (soil)
8778b418cfdb.sentence: Almost exclusively, plant roots and soil organisms uptake contaminants that are dissolved in water.

33dd740151c1.title: Bioavailability (soil)
33dd740151c1.sentence: In these forms, contaminants are relatively inaccessible to microbial or plant uptake and must dissociate and re-dissolve into the soil solution to become biological available.

bfef40e5259c.title: Bioavailability (soil)
bfef40e5259c.sentence: - Soil properties, such as pH, ion exchange capacity, soil organic matter content, texture and porosity influence bioavailability.

4733adf681c8.title: Bioavailability (soil)
4733adf681c8.sentence: Because soils with higher ion exchange and organic matter content offer more opportunities for adsorption, typically they exhibit lower bioavailability.

c6da987593a3.title: Bioavailability (soil)
c6da987593a3.sentence: - As the contact time between the contaminant and soil increases, a decrease in bioavailability is observed, termed “ageing”, due to diffusion and sorption processes with mineral and organic fractions of soil.

0d83c46aa5fb.title: Nitrobacter
0d83c46aa5fb.sentence: Nitrobacter is a genus comprising rod-shaped, gram-negative, and chemoautotrophic bacteria.

bfab6bbc7a45.title: Nitrobacter
bfab6bbc7a45.sentence: Nitrobacter play an important role in the nitrogen cycle by oxidizing nitrite into nitrate in soil and marine systems.

3011efe0310a.title: Nitrobacter
3011efe0310a.sentence: Unlike plants, where electron transfer in photosynthesis provides the energy for carbon fixation, Nitrobacter uses energy from the oxidation of nitrite ions, NO2−, into nitrate ions, NO3−, to fulfill their energy needs.

c467e2cb8603.title: Nitrobacter
c467e2cb8603.sentence: Nitrobacter fix carbon dioxide via the Calvin cycle for their carbon requirements.

db8eb61dd1e0.title: Nitrobacter
db8eb61dd1e0.sentence: Thermodynamically, nitrite oxidation gives a yield (∆G°′) of only -74 kJ mol−1 NO2−.

6a5655dc1e5a.title: Nitrobacter
6a5655dc1e5a.sentence: As a result, Nitrobacter has developed a highly specialized metabolism to derive energy from the oxidation of nitrite.

96420536df4f.title: Nitrobacter
96420536df4f.sentence: Nitrobacter cells are obligate aerobes and have a doubling time of about 13 hours.

814c9a9c2d02.title: Nitrobacter
814c9a9c2d02.sentence: Since all members in the genus Nitrobacter are obligate aerobes, oxygen along with phosphorus tend to be factors that limit their capability to perform nitrite oxidation.

e9506844b69a.title: Nitrobacter
e9506844b69a.sentence: The genus Nitrobacter is widely distributed in both aquatic and terrestrial environments.

19754c215d98.title: Nitrobacter
19754c215d98.sentence: The primary ecological role of members of the genus Nitrobacter is to oxidize nitrite to nitrate, a primary source of inorganic nitrogen for plants.

d21d5c98a9a1.title: Nitrobacter
d21d5c98a9a1.sentence: Cells in the genus Nitrobacter have an optimum pH for growth between 7.3 and 7.5.

b325196c3cdc.title: Nitrobacter
b325196c3cdc.sentence: In 1890, Ukrainian-Russian microbiologist Sergei Winogradsky isolated the first pure cultures of nitrifying bacteria which are capable of growth in the absence of organic matter and sunlight.

7fe22d28d75f.title: Nitrobacter
7fe22d28d75f.sentence: In 1891, English chemist Robert Warington proposed a two-stage mechanism for nitrification, mediated by two distinct genera of bacteria.

c98969d686db.title: Nitrobacter
c98969d686db.sentence: Winogradsky named the bacteria responsible for the oxidation of nitrite to nitrate Nitrobacter in his subsequent study on microbial nitrification in 1892.

3a905874ad88.sentence: This pathway involves the reduction of sulfate by organic compounds to produce hydrogen sulfide, which occurs in both processes.

ad481a9c215d.sentence: Through the dissimilatory sulfate reduction pathway, sulfate can be reduced either bacterially (bacterial sulfate reduction) or inorganically (thermochemical sulfate reduction).

ccfcf21ae529.sentence: For both, various organic compounds and dissolved sulfate are the reactants, and the products or by-products are as follows: H2S, CO2, carbonates, elemental sulfur and metal sulfides.
