62b0d8efda12.sentence: Organic acids are the main organic reactants for BSR and branched/n-alkanes are the main organic reactants for TSR.

2dd2b3ed2c2c.title: Gypsum
2dd2b3ed2c2c.sentence: Under reducing conditions, the sulfates it contains can be reduced back to sulfide by sulfate-reducing bacteria.

fce532dcfe39.title: Biomineralization
fce532dcfe39.sentence: - Pyrite and marcasite in sedimentary rocks deposited by sulfate-reducing bacteria

7508dfab2270.title: Martinus Beijerinck
7508dfab2270.sentence: Spirillum desulfuricans, now known as Desulfovibrio desulfuricans, the first known sulfate-reducing bacterium, was isolated and described by Beijerinck.

aaf0c9f59dc4.title: Sulfate-reducing microorganism
aaf0c9f59dc4.sentence: Sulfate-reducing microorganisms (SRM) or sulfate-reducing prokaryotes (SRP) are a group composed of sulfate-reducing bacteria (SRB) and sulfate-reducing archaea (SRA), both of which can perform anaerobic respiration utilizing sulfate (SO2− 4) as terminal electron acceptor, reducing it to hydrogen sulfide (H2S).

5812c45b0396.title: Sulfate-reducing microorganism
5812c45b0396.sentence: Therefore, these sulfidogenic microorganisms "breathe" sulfate rather than molecular oxygen (O2), which is the terminal electron acceptor reduced to water (H2O) in aerobic respiration.

72e3f478a479.title: Sulfate-reducing microorganism
72e3f478a479.sentence: Many organisms reduce small amounts of sulfates in order to synthesize sulfur-containing cell components; this is known as assimilatory sulfate reduction.

2cb851b0729d.title: Sulfate-reducing microorganism
2cb851b0729d.sentence: By contrast, the sulfate-reducing microorganisms considered here reduce sulfate in large amounts to obtain energy and expel the resulting sulfide as waste; this is known as dissimilatory sulfate reduction.

5c7162ca2b58.title: Sulfate-reducing microorganism
5c7162ca2b58.sentence: Sulfate-reducing microorganisms are common in anaerobic environments where they aid in the degradation of organic materials.

75fc7a382350.title: Sulfate-reducing microorganism
75fc7a382350.sentence: In these anaerobic environments, fermenting bacteria extract energy from large organic molecules; the resulting smaller compounds such as organic acids and alcohols are further oxidized by acetogens and methanogens and the competing sulfate-reducing microorganisms.

9e66e38163ca.title: Sulfate-reducing microorganism
9e66e38163ca.sentence: The toxic hydrogen sulfide is a waste product of sulfate-reducing microorganisms; its rotten egg odor is often a marker for the presence of sulfate-reducing microorganisms in nature.

169883482ebd.title: Sulfate-reducing microorganism
169883482ebd.sentence: Sulfate-reducing microorganisms are responsible for the sulfurous odors of salt marshes and mud flats.

0c2afd3eaa57.title: Sulfate-reducing microorganism
0c2afd3eaa57.sentence: Much of the hydrogen sulfide will react with metal ions in the water to produce metal sulfides.

7f19eb4f2283.title: Sulfate-reducing microorganism
7f19eb4f2283.sentence: These metal sulfides, such as ferrous sulfide (FeS), are insoluble and often black or brown, leading to the dark color of sludge.

21076e03e10c.title: Sulfate-reducing microorganism
21076e03e10c.sentence: Sulfate-reducing bacteria also generate neurotoxic methylmercury as a byproduct of their metabolism, through methylation of inorganic mercury present in their surroundings.

ed6f6c6f15bb.title: Sulfate-reducing microorganism
ed6f6c6f15bb.sentence: They are known to be the dominant source of this bioaccumulative form of mercury in aquatic systems.

9a0fa071fa41.title: Sulfate-reducing microorganism
9a0fa071fa41.sentence: Some sulfate-reducing microorganisms can reduce hydrocarbons, and they have been used to clean up contaminated soils.

f2394a683bb5.title: Sulfur cycle
f2394a683bb5.sentence: The burning of coal, natural gas, and other fossil fuels has greatly increased the amount of sulfur in the atmosphere and ocean and depleted the sedimentary rock sink.

6e970f55e565.title: Sulfur cycle
6e970f55e565.sentence: Therefore, human activities do not cause a major change in the global pools of sulfur, but they do produce massive changes in the annual flux of sulfur through the atmosphere.

f30f04b4abf8.title: Sulfur cycle
f30f04b4abf8.sentence: Humans are mining coal and extracting petroleum from the Earth's crust at a rate that mobilizes 150 × 10^12 gS/yr, which is more than double the rate of 100 years ago.

2f2ca71021bb.title: Sulfur cycle
2f2ca71021bb.sentence: When SO2 is emitted as an air pollutant, it forms sulfuric acid through reactions with water in the atmosphere.

21c2e3ae508b.title: Sulfur cycle
21c2e3ae508b.sentence: Once the acid is completely dissociated in water the pH can drop to 4.3 or lower causing damage to both man-made and natural systems.

2866568c591b.title: Sulfur cycle
2866568c591b.sentence: Over the most polluted areas there has been a 30-fold increase in sulfate deposition.

06b585ce2d75.title: Sulfur cycle
06b585ce2d75.sentence: Recently sulfur deficiency has become widespread in many countries in Europe.

7376a5544c20.title: Sulfur cycle
7376a5544c20.sentence: Because of actions taken to limit acid rains atmospheric inputs of sulfur continue to decrease, As a result, the deficit in the sulfur input is likely to increase unless sulfur fertilizers are used.

159ba6c54434.title: Sulfur cycle
159ba6c54434.sentence: As it is an important nutrient for plants, sulfur is increasingly used as a component of fertilizers.

71a5f388d41a.title: Phosphorus cycle
71a5f388d41a.sentence: Humans have greatly influenced the phosphorus cycle by mining phosphate rock.

58f7adf22726.title: Phosphorus cycle
58f7adf22726.sentence: Human activities have caused major changes to the global phosphorus cycle primarily through the mining and subsequent transformation of phosphorus minerals for use in fertilizer and industrial products.

830e3e6ccfed.title: Phosphorus cycle
830e3e6ccfed.sentence: Since the 1840s, when the technology to mine and extract phosphorus became more prevalent, approximately 110 teragrams of phosphorus has been added to the environment.

bb36e2117302.title: Phosphorus cycle
bb36e2117302.sentence: This trend appears to be continuing, as from 1900 to 2022, the amount of phosphorus mined globally has increased 72-fold, with an expected annual increase of 4%.

1fb951111f71.title: Phosphorus cycle
1fb951111f71.sentence: Most of this mining is done to produce fertilizers which can be used on a global scale.

2a0430b324bf.title: Phosphorus cycle
2a0430b324bf.sentence: However, at the rate humans are mining, the geological system can not quickly restore what is lost.

2652694d8da2.title: Phosphorus cycle
2652694d8da2.sentence: Other human processes can have detrimental effects on the phosphorus cycle, such as the repeated application of liquid hog manure in excess to crops.

2ea47bfbde91.title: Phosphorus cycle
2ea47bfbde91.sentence: Applying biosolids may also increase available phosphorus in soil.

c0e79e5cc686.title: Phosphorus cycle
c0e79e5cc686.section: Phosphorus in the environment > Interaction with nitrogen
c0e79e5cc686.sentence: In the last 40 years, the N:P ratio has increased from 19:1 to 30:1, meaning P is less available to ecosystems.

be78f0c22e18.title: Phosphorus cycle
be78f0c22e18.section: Phosphorus in the environment > Phosphatic minerals
be78f0c22e18.sentence: The availability of organic phosphorus to support microbial, plant and animal growth depends on the rate of their degradation to generate free phosphate.

8da5d2018c2c.title: Phosphorus cycle
8da5d2018c2c.section: Phosphorus in the environment > Phosphatic minerals
8da5d2018c2c.sentence: Enzymatic hydrolysis of organic phosphorus is an essential step in the biogeochemical phosphorus cycle, including the phosphorus nutrition of plants and microorganisms and the transfer of organic phosphorus from soil to bodies of water.

6907265da599.title: Phosphorus cycle
6907265da599.section: Phosphorus in the environment > Phosphatic minerals
6907265da599.sentence: There are various enzymes such as phosphatases, nucleases and phytase involved for the degradation.

d96b34d6224c.title: Phosphorus cycle
d96b34d6224c.section: Phosphorus in the environment > Phosphatic minerals
d96b34d6224c.sentence: Plant growth depends on the rapid root uptake of phosphorus released from dead organic matter in the biochemical cycle.

f238cdb11d8b.title: Urease
f238cdb11d8b.sentence: Ureases are nickel-containing metalloenzymes of high molecular weight.

a62ec0c268df.title: Urease
a62ec0c268df.sentence: These enzymes catalyze the hydrolysis of urea into carbon dioxide and ammonia:

6bd2267adcde.title: Urease
6bd2267adcde.sentence: The hydrolysis of urea occurs in two stages.

512875a225e4.title: Urease
512875a225e4.sentence: In the first stage, ammonia and carbamic acid are produced.

18dd9ef11de4.title: Urease
18dd9ef11de4.sentence: Urease activity increases the pH of its environment as ammonia is produced, which is basic.

461c83095cfb.title: Urease
461c83095cfb.sentence: Urease is important because of its role in the nitrogen cycle as a key catalyst in the reaction converting urea to ammonium and CO2.

a5198f470e95.title: Urease
a5198f470e95.sentence: Urease occurs as a soil enzyme, likely because soil microorganisms benefit from the nitrogen made available by urea degradation in the form of ammonium.

b08d470cadf0.title: Urease
b08d470cadf0.sentence: Urea is found naturally in the environment and is also artificially introduced, comprising more than half of all synthetic nitrogen fertilizers used globally.

1415a1010b76.title: Urease
1415a1010b76.section: Occurrence and applications in agriculture > Inhibition in fertilizers
1415a1010b76.sentence: The inhibition of urease is a significant goal in agriculture because the rapid breakdown of urea-based fertilizers is wasteful and environmentally damaging.

301ab3758b59.title: Urease
301ab3758b59.section: Occurrence and applications in agriculture > Inhibition in fertilizers
301ab3758b59.sentence: Phenyl phosphorodiamidate and N-(n-butyl)thiophosphoric triamide are two such inhibitors.

c070a8af3960.title: Urease
c070a8af3960.sentence: Environmental urease activity is often measured as an indicator of the health of microbial communities.

0fe2f2b26261.title: Potassium cycle
0fe2f2b26261.sentence: The potassium (K) cycle is the biogeochemical cycle that describes the movement of potassium throughout the Earth's lithosphere, biosphere, atmosphere, and hydrosphere.

b684605b8d71.title: Potassium cycle
b684605b8d71.sentence: Along with nitrogen and phosphorus, potassium is one of the three major nutrients that plants require in large quantities.

098ba7f75e72.title: Potassium cycle
098ba7f75e72.sentence: Potassium is essential to stomata control in plants and is also essential for muscles contraction in humans.

a1916f7ca073.title: Potassium cycle
a1916f7ca073.sentence: By weight, K totals to 2.6% of the Earth's crust.

abb2a6d7836a.title: Potassium cycle
abb2a6d7836a.sentence: Stored in primary minerals (feldspar, biotite, and muscovite), chemical weathering releases potassium into the soil to account for up to 11% of plant demand.

5e1ef6aa533e.title: Potassium cycle
5e1ef6aa533e.sentence: Some plants and bacteria also release organic acids into the soil that make K accessible for their use.

eb98cac8194e.title: Potassium cycle
eb98cac8194e.sentence: A portion of potassium uptake in plants can be attributed to weathering of primary minerals, but plants can also ‘pump’ potassium from deeper soil layers to increase levels of surface K.

c9868cb7444c.title: Potassium cycle
c9868cb7444c.sentence: The most abundant ion in plant cells is the potassium ion.

50fe5faecfa0.title: Potassium cycle
50fe5faecfa0.sentence: Potassium stored in plant matter can be returned to the soil during decomposition, especially in areas of higher rainfall that experience higher leaching rates.

626bca0a794e.title: Potassium cycle
626bca0a794e.sentence: Potassium leaching occurs at higher rates than nitrogen and phosphorus, likely because it only exists in the soluble ion form (K+) in the plant.

68cb9a06c30d.title: Potassium cycle
68cb9a06c30d.sentence: Nitrogen and phosphorus are typically incorporated into large, complex molecules that are more difficult to leach through cell membranes than the small K+ ion.

ef722d5b8ca3.title: Potassium cycle
ef722d5b8ca3.sentence: Application of potassium is necessary in agriculture because the removal of potassium from the soil through plant uptake and crop removal occurs at a faster rate than the replacement through rock weathering.

4c3a91342c28.title: Potassium cycle
4c3a91342c28.sentence: An estimated 32 × 10^6 tonnes (32 Tg) of potassium are mined from the Earth each year, of which 28 × 10^6 tonnes (28 Tg) are applied to crop fields annually.

5618063a037c.title: Potassium cycle
5618063a037c.sentence: Potassium is most commonly applied as potassium chloride (KCl), but also referred to as potash and K2O.

05e32ae18f87.title: Potassium cycle
05e32ae18f87.sentence: Potassium depletion in soils can be minimized by leaving crop residues on soils, allowing the plant matter to decay and release their stored potassium back into the soil.

f4b003471009.title: Potassium cycle
f4b003471009.sentence: At the current consumption rate, K2O reserves are expected to last 100 years.

508f1d080ce2.title: Potassium cycle
508f1d080ce2.sentence: Leaching and erosion carry 1.4 × 10^9 tonnes (1400 Tg) yr−1 of potassium in soil solution into groundwater, rivers, and oceans.

d76fd1bb6d84.title: Potassium cycle
d76fd1bb6d84.sentence: The hydrosphere is the largest reservoir for potassium, holding an estimated 552.7 × 10^12 tonnes (552.7 × 10^6 Tg).

a34267ea9e08.title: Nitrogen fixation
a34267ea9e08.sentence: The protein complex nitrogenase is responsible for catalyzing the reduction of nitrogen gas (N2) to ammonia (NH3).

301ae561bd94.title: Nitrogen fixation
301ae561bd94.sentence: Nitrogenase consist of two proteins, a catalytic iron-dependent protein, commonly referred to as MoFe protein and a reducing iron-only protein (Fe protein).

8a935b65a90b.title: Nitrogen fixation
8a935b65a90b.sentence: The conversion of N 2 into ammonia occurs at a metal cluster called FeMoco, an abbreviation for the iron-molybdenum cofactor.

93149b309904.title: Nitrogen fixation
93149b309904.sentence: Nitrogenase has three different forms (Nif, Anf, and Vnf) that correspond with the metal found in the active site of the protein (molybdenum, iron, and vanadium respectively).

c991f51d790b.title: Nitrogen fixation
c991f51d790b.sentence: The process is coupled to the hydrolysis of 16 equivalents of ATP and is accompanied by the co-formation of one equivalent of H 2.

0410cb410cc1.title: Nitrogen fixation
0410cb410cc1.sentence: Nitrogenases are rapidly degraded by oxygen.

3a3089a6aef1.title: Nitrogen fixation
3a3089a6aef1.sentence: For this reason, many bacteria cease production of the enzyme in the presence of oxygen.

f69960e930be.title: Nitrogen fixation
f69960e930be.sentence: In cyanobacteria, this enzyme system is housed in a specialized cell called the heterocyst.

b9607f2f5f77.title: Nitrous oxide
b9607f2f5f77.sentence: Microbial processes that generate nitrous oxide may be classified as nitrification and denitrification.

ffac5e6db7d3.title: Nitrous oxide
ffac5e6db7d3.sentence: Most of the N2O emitted into the atmosphere, from natural and anthropogenic sources, is produced by microorganisms such as denitrifying bacteria and fungi in soils and oceans.

2628fb4c8b45.title: Nitrous oxide
2628fb4c8b45.sentence: - aerobic autotrophic nitrification, the stepwise oxidation of ammonia (NH3) to nitrite (NO−2) and to nitrate (NO−3)

914d5be41789.title: Nitrous oxide
914d5be41789.sentence: - anaerobic heterotrophic denitrification, the stepwise reduction of NO−3 to NO−2, nitric oxide (NO), N2O and ultimately N2, where facultative anaerobe bacteria use NO−3 as an electron acceptor in the respiration of organic material in the condition of insufficient oxygen (O2)

81cbdcf64b3b.title: Nitrous oxide
81cbdcf64b3b.sentence: - nitrifier denitrification, which is carried out by autotrophic NH3-oxidising bacteria and the pathway whereby ammonia (NH3) is oxidised to nitrite (NO−2), followed by the reduction of NO−2 to nitric oxide (NO), N2O and molecular nitrogen (N2)

c91f98f4bbd0.title: Nitrous oxide
c91f98f4bbd0.sentence: These processes are affected by soil chemical and physical properties such as the availability of mineral nitrogen and organic matter, acidity and soil type, as well as climate-related factors such as soil temperature and water content.

124968e880bd.title: Nitrous oxide
124968e880bd.sentence: Soils under natural vegetation are an important source of nitrous oxide, accounting for 60% of all naturally produced emissions.

69a477923402.title: Nitrous oxide
69a477923402.sentence: The main components of anthropogenic emissions are fertilised agricultural soils and livestock manure (42%), runoff and leaching of fertilisers (25%), biomass burning (10%), fossil fuel combustion and industrial processes (10%), biological degradation of other nitrogen-containing atmospheric emissions (9%) and human sewage (5%).

a86a30ce57da.title: Nitrous oxide
a86a30ce57da.sentence: Agriculture enhances nitrous oxide production through soil cultivation, the use of nitrogen fertilisers and animal waste handling.

6e266f601cc1.title: Nitrous oxide
6e266f601cc1.sentence: These activities stimulate naturally occurring bacteria to produce more nitrous oxide.

53639d40e364.title: Nitrous oxide
53639d40e364.sentence: Nitrous oxide emissions from soil can be challenging to measure as they vary markedly over time and space, and the majority of a year's emissions may occur when conditions are favorable during "hot moments" and/or at favorable locations known as "hotspots".

7e90dbe91673.title: Nitrous oxide
7e90dbe91673.sentence: N2O is the third most important greenhouse gas for global warming and one of the most used ozone-depleting substance in the last century.

2ef2d86a26f7.title: Biochar
2ef2d86a26f7.sentence: Modest additions of biochar reduce nitrous oxide (N 2O) emissions by up to 80% and eliminate methane emissions, which are both more potent greenhouse gases than CO2.

6096c7591859.title: Denitrifying bacteria
6096c7591859.section: Oxidation of methane and denitrification > Anaerobic oxidation of methane coupled to denitrification
6096c7591859.sentence: Anaerobic denitrification coupled to methane oxidation was first observed in 2008, with the isolation of a methane-oxidizing bacterial strain found to oxidize methane independently.

6e735ae6004e.title: Denitrifying bacteria
6e735ae6004e.section: Oxidation of methane and denitrification > Anaerobic oxidation of methane coupled to denitrification
6e735ae6004e.sentence: This process uses the excess electrons from methane oxidation to reduce nitrates, effectively removing both fixed nitrogen and methane from aquatic systems in habitats ranging from sediment to peat bogs to stratified water columns.

342261f33aa5.title: Denitrifying bacteria
342261f33aa5.section: Oxidation of methane and denitrification > Anaerobic oxidation of methane coupled to denitrification
342261f33aa5.sentence: Anaerobic denitrification as a mechanism has been shown to be capable of removing the excess nitrate caused by fertilizer runoff, even in hypoxic conditions.

dfe13ff2b5ae.title: Denitrifying bacteria
dfe13ff2b5ae.section: Oxidation of methane and denitrification > Role of denitrifying bacteria as a methane sink
dfe13ff2b5ae.sentence: A study conducted on Europe's Lake Constance found that anaerobic methane oxidation coupled to denitrification – also referred to as nitrate/nitrite-dependent anaerobic methane oxidation (n-damo) – is a dominant sink of methane in deep lakes.

c77f8d8fac52.title: Denitrifying bacteria
c77f8d8fac52.section: Oxidation of methane and denitrification > Role of denitrifying bacteria as a methane sink
c77f8d8fac52.sentence: In the case of Lake Constance, this is carried out by M. oxyfera-like bacteria.

d87d98d71b92.title: Nitrospira
d87d98d71b92.sentence: Nitrospira (from Latin: nitro, meaning "nitrate" and Greek: spira, meaning "spiral") is a genus of bacteria within the monophyletic clade of the Nitrospirota phylum.

ac0b64c7b373.title: Nitrospira
ac0b64c7b373.sentence: Nitrospira is a ubiquitous bacterium that plays a role in the nitrogen cycle by performing nitrite oxidation in the second step of nitrification.

e07163cb1f61.title: Nitrospira
e07163cb1f61.sentence: The first member of this genus was described 1986 by Watson et al., isolated from the Gulf of Maine.

e4b25bfb45fe.title: Nitrospira
e4b25bfb45fe.sentence: Nitrospira live in a wide array of environments including but not limited to, drinking water systems, waste treatment plants, rice paddies, forest soils, geothermal springs, and sponge tissue.

3111fe4ab378.title: Nitrospira
3111fe4ab378.sentence: Populations were initially thought to be limited to marine ecosystems, but it was later discovered to be well-suited for numerous habitats, including activated sludge of wastewater treatment systems, natural biological marine settings (such as the Seine River in France and beaches in Cape Cod in the United States), water circulation biofilters in aquarium tanks, terrestrial systems, fresh and salt water ecosystems, agricultural lands and hot springs.

aee4fe662ae1.title: Nitrospira
aee4fe662ae1.sentence: Despite being abundant in many natural and engineered ecosystems Nitrospira are difficult to culture, so most knowledge of them is from molecular and genomic data.

314d916e33af.title: Nitrospira
314d916e33af.sentence: Ever since nitrifying bacteria were discovered it was accepted that nitrification occurred in two steps, although it would be energetically favourable for one organism to do both steps.

e4811fd99cdc.title: Nitrospira
e4811fd99cdc.sentence: Recently Nitrospira members with the abilities to perform complete nitrification (comammox bacteria) have also been discovered and cultivated as in the case of Nitrospira inopinata.

4a2a2710223c.title: Nitrospira
4a2a2710223c.sentence: New studies also show that Nitrospira can use urea as a source of nutrients.

781c290f9066.title: Nitrospira
781c290f9066.sentence: Urease encoded within their genome can break urea down to CO2 and ammonia.

a53481b60ade.title: Nitrospira
a53481b60ade.sentence: The CO2 can be assimilated by anabolism while the ammonia and organic by-product released by Nitrospira allow ammonium oxidizers and other microbes to co-exist in the same microenvironment.

1591159ff4b3.title: Comammox
1591159ff4b3.sentence: Comammox (COMplete AMMonia OXidation) is the name attributed to an organism that can convert ammonia into nitrite and then into nitrate through the process of nitrification.

a34bde91fc28.title: Comammox
a34bde91fc28.sentence: Nitrification has traditionally been thought to be a two-step process, where ammonia-oxidizing bacteria and archaea oxidize ammonia to nitrite and then nitrite-oxidizing bacteria convert to nitrate.

832f489c671d.title: Comammox
832f489c671d.sentence: Complete conversion of ammonia into nitrate by a single microorganism was first predicted in 2006.

ed9396a8f0b0.title: Comammox
ed9396a8f0b0.sentence: In 2015 the presence of microorganisms that could carry out both conversion processes was discovered within the genus Nitrospira, and the nitrogen cycle was updated.

ae7a1ba6ffb8.title: Comammox
ae7a1ba6ffb8.sentence: Complete nitrification step yield more energy (∆G°′ = −349 kJ mol−1 NH3) than either single oxidation alone (∆G°′ = −275 kJ mol−1 NH3 for ammonia oxidation to nitrite and ∆G°′ = −74 kJ mol−1 NO2− for nitrite oxidation to nitrate).

ad49e7fde09b.title: Comammox
ad49e7fde09b.sentence: Comammox have been identified in many ecosystems, including natural freshwater and terrestrial ecosystems.

955acef60eae.title: Comammox
955acef60eae.sentence: Comammox have been found in many engineered systems including aquaculture biofiltration units, drinking water treatment and distribution systems, and wastewater treatment plants.

2877d0e3acf2.title: Comammox
2877d0e3acf2.sentence: Notably commamox genes were not found to be abundant in oceans.

b9bdc2889513.title: Anammox
b9bdc2889513.sentence: Anammox, an abbreviation for ‘anaerobic ammonium oxidation’, is a globally important microbial process of the nitrogen cycle that takes place in many natural environments.

85a1ff7eca53.title: Anammox
85a1ff7eca53.sentence: In the anammox reaction, nitrite and ammonium ions are converted directly into diatomic nitrogen and water.

27926cdc971e.title: Anammox
27926cdc971e.sentence: The bacteria that perform the anammox process are genera that belong to the phylum Planctomycetota.

71811a85f3f3.title: Anammox
71811a85f3f3.sentence: The bacteria mediating this process were identified in 1999, and were a great surprise for the scientific community.

d5df25cecb57.title: Anammox
d5df25cecb57.sentence: The anammox bacteria all possess one anammoxosome, a lipid bilayer membrane-bound compartment inside the cytoplasm in which the anammox process takes place.

26552a2b4a45.title: Anammox
26552a2b4a45.sentence: Essentially, denitrification needs organic carbon to function.

15708d242784.title: Anammox
15708d242784.sentence: Anammox bacteria does not utilize organic carbon, instead, it directly utilizes ammonium (NH4+) and nitrite (NO2-).

555683b6f837.title: Anammox
555683b6f837.section: Biogeochemical significance > Benthic and terrestrial ecosystems
555683b6f837.sentence: Anammox has also been in found in other different environments and ecosystems including freshwater lakes, riverbanks, and agricultural soils (like rice paddies).

a734f1948601.title: Anammox
a734f1948601.section: Biogeochemical significance > Benthic and terrestrial ecosystems
a734f1948601.sentence: From a climate based perspective, anammox is seen as a cleaner way of removing nitrogen in comparison to denitrification since it is able to produce a lesser amount of nitrous oxide (N2O) which is known to be a powerful greenhouse gas.

ffd7d4b8678c.title: Anammox
ffd7d4b8678c.sentence: However, now we are aware that anammox can account for an estimated amount of 30-50% of the nitrogen loss in the ocean.

e8e91b48284e.title: Phosphatase
e8e91b48284e.sentence: In biochemistry, a phosphatase is an enzyme that uses water to cleave a phosphoric acid monoester into a phosphate ion and an alcohol.

70bead40b20b.title: Phosphatase
70bead40b20b.sentence: Because a phosphatase enzyme catalyzes the hydrolysis of its substrate, it is a subcategory of hydrolases.

6368f6954fae.title: Phosphatase
6368f6954fae.sentence: Water is split in the reaction, with the -OH group attaching to the phosphate ion, and the H+ protonating the hydroxyl group of the other product.

1bdadf984eac.title: Phosphatase
1bdadf984eac.sentence: The net result of the reaction is the destruction of a phosphomonoester and the creation of both a phosphate ion and a molecule with a free hydroxyl group.

8c89ee88da9b.title: Phosphatase
8c89ee88da9b.sentence: Whereas phosphatases remove phosphate groups from molecules, kinases catalyze the transfer of phosphate groups to molecules from ATP.

2bf127868b43.title: Phosphatase
2bf127868b43.sentence: Phosphatase enzymes are not to be confused with phosphorylase enzymes, which catalyze the transfer of a phosphate group from hydrogen phosphate to an acceptor.

0ebc944ca90d.title: Phosphatase
0ebc944ca90d.sentence: Within the larger class of phosphatase, the Enzyme Commission recognizes 104 distinct enzyme families.

861c140a21ae.title: Phosphatase
861c140a21ae.sentence: Phosphatases are classified by substrate specificity and sequence homology in catalytic domains.

533ac0f90b3d.title: Phosphatase
533ac0f90b3d.sentence: Despite their classification into over one hundred families, all phosphatases still catalyze the same general hydrolysis reaction.

b0c095a5431e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/01%3A_Digging_In/1.07%3A_Soil_Nutrient_Cycling
b0c095a5431e.section: SOIL NUTRIENT CYCLES > Phosphorus Cycling > Reactions that contribute plant-available phosphorus
b0c095a5431e.sentence: The biological source is organic phosphorus, which is hydrolyzed by phosphatase enzymes from plant roots and soil microorganisms.

265598e899e8.title: Leghemoglobin
265598e899e8.sentence: Leghemoglobin (also leghaemoglobin or legoglobin) is an oxygen-carrying phytoglobin found in the nitrogen-fixing root nodules of leguminous plants.

54947d87458e.title: Leghemoglobin
54947d87458e.sentence: It is produced by these plants in response to the roots being colonized by nitrogen-fixing bacteria, termed rhizobia, as part of the symbiotic interaction between plant and bacterium: roots not colonized by Rhizobium do not synthesise leghemoglobin.

130161ae7f1f.title: Leghemoglobin
130161ae7f1f.sentence: Leghemoglobin has close chemical and structural similarities to hemoglobin, and, like hemoglobin, is red in colour.

7163c695e624.title: Leghemoglobin
7163c695e624.sentence: In plants colonised by Rhizobium, such as alfalfa or soybeans, the presence of oxygen in the root nodules would reduce the activity of the oxygen-sensitive nitrogenase, which is an enzyme responsible for the fixation of atmospheric nitrogen.

b46fc73870cc.title: Leghemoglobin
b46fc73870cc.sentence: That being said, nitrogen fixation is an extremely energetically costly process, so aerobic respiration, which necessitates high oxygen concentration, is necessary in the cells of the root nodule.

b368cb0344d4.title: Leghemoglobin
b368cb0344d4.sentence: Leghemoglobin maintains a free oxygen concentration that is low enough to allow nitrogenase to function, but a high enough total oxygen concentration (free and bound to leghemoglobin) for aerobic respiration.

307d174f9c10.title: Leghemoglobin
307d174f9c10.sentence: Leghemoglobins accumulate to millimolar concentrations in the cytoplasm of infected plant cells prior to nitrogen fixation to buffer free oxygen in the nanomolar range, which can avoid inactivation of oxygen-labile nitrogenase while keeping a high enough oxygen flux for respiration in the cell.

311d1e707f13.title: Leghemoglobin
311d1e707f13.sentence: The leghemoglobins are required for SNF but are not required for plant growth and development in the presence of an external source of fixed nitrogen.

4ec7789dea7b.title: Leghemoglobin
4ec7789dea7b.sentence: Results of a 1995 study suggested that the low free oxygen concentration in root nodule cells is actually due to the low oxygen permeability of root nodule cells.

8a28eeebaf01.title: Leghemoglobin
8a28eeebaf01.sentence: It follows that the main purpose of leghemoglobin is to scavenge the limited free oxygen in the cell and deliver it to mitochondria for respiration.

24ecf54fbbe7.title: Leghemoglobin
24ecf54fbbe7.sentence: But, scientists of a later 2005 article suggest that leghemoglobin is responsible both for buffering oxygen concentration, and for delivery of oxygen to mitochondria.

5cf3cfe54a5f.title: Leghemoglobin
5cf3cfe54a5f.sentence: Their leghemoglobin knockout studies showed that leghemoglobin actually does significantly decrease the free oxygen concentration in root nodule cells, and that nitrogenase expression was eliminated in leghemoglobin knockout mutants, assumably due to the degradation of nitrogenase with high free oxygen concentration.

4ea236334904.title: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle
4ea236334904.sentence: This sequential transfer between ecosystems is termed the nitrogen cascade.
4ea236334904.key: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle

b17dcc5e8f3d.title: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle
b17dcc5e8f3d.sentence: The above system responses to reactive nitrogen (Nr) inputs are almost all exclusively studied separately; however, research increasingly indicates that nitrogen loading problems are linked by multiple pathways transporting nutrients across system boundaries.
b17dcc5e8f3d.key: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle

fdc42e024019.title: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle
fdc42e024019.sentence: During the cascade, some systems accumulate Nr, which results in a time lag in the cascade and enhanced effects of Nr on the environment in which it accumulates.
fdc42e024019.key: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle

f12941c65270.title: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle
f12941c65270.sentence: Most Nr applied to global agroecosystems cascades through the atmosphere and aquatic and terrestrial ecosystems until it is converted to N2, primarily through denitrification.
f12941c65270.key: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle

9d052236d710.title: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle
9d052236d710.sentence: Although terrestrial denitrification produces gaseous intermediates (nitric oxide [NO] and nitrous oxide [N2O]), the last step—microbial production of N2— is critical because atmospheric N2 is a sink for Nr.
9d052236d710.key: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle

e4e8c370f5d1.title: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle
e4e8c370f5d1.sentence: Many studies have clearly demonstrated that managed buffer strips and wetlands can remove significant amounts of nitrate (NO3−) from agricultural systems through denitrification.
e4e8c370f5d1.key: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle

9180c843088b.title: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle
9180c843088b.sentence: Such management may help attenuate the undesirable cascading effects and eliminate environmental Nr accumulation.
9180c843088b.key: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle

44a93b7a87ad.title: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle
44a93b7a87ad.section: Impacts of anthropogenic inputs on the nitrogen cycle > Biosphere
44a93b7a87ad.sentence: Terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems receive Nr inputs from the atmosphere through wet and dry deposition.
44a93b7a87ad.key: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle

88410623e385.title: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle
88410623e385.section: Impacts of anthropogenic inputs on the nitrogen cycle > Biosphere
88410623e385.sentence: Atmospheric Nr species can be deposited to ecosystems in precipitation (e.g., NO3−, NH4+, organic N compounds), as gases (e.g., NH3 and gaseous nitric acid [HNO3]), or as aerosols (e.g., ammonium nitrate [NH4NO3]).
88410623e385.key: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle

77ec4afacd31.title: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle
77ec4afacd31.section: Impacts of anthropogenic inputs on the nitrogen cycle > Biosphere
77ec4afacd31.sentence: Increased N deposition can acidify soils, streams, and lakes and alter forest and grassland productivity.
77ec4afacd31.key: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle

7afeb7c3ca0b.title: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle
7afeb7c3ca0b.section: Impacts of anthropogenic inputs on the nitrogen cycle > Biosphere
7afeb7c3ca0b.sentence: In grassland ecosystems, N inputs have produced initial increases in productivity followed by declines as critical thresholds are exceeded.
7afeb7c3ca0b.key: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle

6987f40be540.title: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle
6987f40be540.section: Impacts of anthropogenic inputs on the nitrogen cycle > Biosphere > Terrestrial ecosystems > Impacts on plant species diversity
6987f40be540.sentence: Several nutrient addition studies have shown that increased N inputs lead to dominance of fast-growing plant species, with associated declines in species richness.
6987f40be540.key: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle

696e92aec2f6.title: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle
696e92aec2f6.section: Impacts of anthropogenic inputs on the nitrogen cycle > Biosphere > Terrestrial ecosystems > Impacts on plant species diversity
696e92aec2f6.sentence: Fast growing species have a greater affinity for nitrogen uptake, and will crowd out slower growing plant species by blocking access to sunlight with their higher above ground biomass.
696e92aec2f6.key: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle

c94aeb0ef541.title: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle
c94aeb0ef541.section: Impacts of anthropogenic inputs on the nitrogen cycle > Biosphere > Terrestrial ecosystems > Impacts on plant species diversity
c94aeb0ef541.sentence: Heathlands are characterized by N-poor soils, which exclude N-demanding grasses; however, with increasing N deposition and soil acidification, invading grasslands replace lowland heath.
c94aeb0ef541.key: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle

599c939098b7.title: Nitrogen cycle
599c939098b7.section: Consequence of human modification of the nitrogen cycle > Impacts on natural systems
599c939098b7.sentence: Ammonia and ammonium – two reduced forms of nitrogen – can be detrimental over time due to increased toxicity toward sensitive species of plants, particularly those that are accustomed to using nitrate as their source of nitrogen, causing poor development of their roots and shoots.

8d6872a575f8.title: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle
8d6872a575f8.section: Impacts of anthropogenic inputs on the nitrogen cycle > Biosphere > Terrestrial ecosystems > Impacts on productivity and nutrient cycling
8d6872a575f8.sentence: When available N exceeds the ecosystem's (i.e., vegetation, soil, and microbes, etc.) uptake capacity, N saturation occurs and excess N is lost to surface waters, groundwater, and the atmosphere.
8d6872a575f8.key: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle

0efc4040f1e6.title: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle
0efc4040f1e6.section: Impacts of anthropogenic inputs on the nitrogen cycle > Biosphere > Terrestrial ecosystems > Impacts on productivity and nutrient cycling
0efc4040f1e6.sentence: Added N is often rapidly immobilized by microbes, and the effect of the remaining available N depends on the plant community's capacity for N uptake.
0efc4040f1e6.key: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle

8863761c9b1a.title: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle
8863761c9b1a.section: Impacts of anthropogenic inputs on the nitrogen cycle > Biosphere > Terrestrial ecosystems > Impacts on productivity and nutrient cycling
8863761c9b1a.sentence: Numerous studies have demonstrated both positive and negative impacts of atmospheric N deposition on forest productivity and carbon storage.
8863761c9b1a.key: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle

2799b5ad5bca.title: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle
2799b5ad5bca.section: Impacts of anthropogenic inputs on the nitrogen cycle > Biosphere > Terrestrial ecosystems > Impacts on productivity and nutrient cycling
2799b5ad5bca.sentence: These findings negate previous hypotheses that increased N inputs would increase NPP and carbon sequestration.
2799b5ad5bca.key: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle

26bdea9a8ad7.title: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle
26bdea9a8ad7.section: Impacts of anthropogenic inputs on the nitrogen cycle > Biosphere > Terrestrial ecosystems > Impacts on productivity and nutrient cycling
26bdea9a8ad7.sentence: N saturation can result in nutrient imbalances (e.g., loss of calcium due to nitrate leaching) and possible forest decline.
26bdea9a8ad7.key: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle

c5745ca6f2d7.title: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle
c5745ca6f2d7.section: Impacts of anthropogenic inputs on the nitrogen cycle > Biosphere > Terrestrial ecosystems > Impacts on productivity and nutrient cycling
c5745ca6f2d7.sentence: A 15-year study of chronic N additions at the Harvard Forest Long Term Ecological Research (LTER) program has elucidated many impacts of increased nitrogen deposition on nutrient cycling in temperate forests.
c5745ca6f2d7.key: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle

e14c192e87e0.title: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle
e14c192e87e0.section: Impacts of anthropogenic inputs on the nitrogen cycle > Biosphere > Terrestrial ecosystems > Impacts on productivity and nutrient cycling
e14c192e87e0.sentence: It found that chronic N additions resulted in greater leaching losses, increased pine mortality, and cessation of biomass accumulation.
e14c192e87e0.key: Human impact on the nitrogen cycle

4b6731633930.title: Dissimilatory nitrate reduction to ammonium
4b6731633930.sentence: Dissimilatory nitrate reduction to ammonium (DNRA), also known as nitrate/nitrite ammonification, is the result of anaerobic respiration by chemoorganoheterotrophic microbes using nitrate (NO3−) as an electron acceptor for respiration.

a7157531d536.title: Dissimilatory nitrate reduction to ammonium
a7157531d536.sentence: In anaerobic conditions microbes which undertake DNRA oxidise organic matter and use nitrate (rather than oxygen) as an electron acceptor, reducing it to nitrite, and then to ammonium (NO3− → NO2− → NH4+).

87270c36315e.title: Dissimilatory nitrate reduction to ammonium
87270c36315e.sentence: Unlike denitrification, it acts to conserve bioavailable nitrogen in the system, producing soluble ammonium rather than unreactive nitrogen gas (N2).

05af38686e59.title: Dissimilatory nitrate reduction to ammonium
05af38686e59.sentence: The balance of denitrification and DNRA is important to the nitrogen cycle of an environment as both use NO3− but, unlike denitrification, which produces gaseous, non-bioavailable N2 (a sink of nitrogen), DNRA produces bioavailable, soluble NH4+.

84099088a0eb.title: Dissimilatory nitrate reduction to ammonium
84099088a0eb.sentence: Both denitrifiers and nitrate ammonifiers are competing for NO3− in the environment.

dc514375c2ce.title: Dissimilatory nitrate reduction to ammonium
dc514375c2ce.sentence: Each step is mediated by a different enzyme, the first step of dissimilatory nitrate reduction to ammonium is usually mediated by a periplasmic nitrate reductase.

d6b0ae0ebff2.title: Dissimilatory nitrate reduction to ammonium
d6b0ae0ebff2.sentence: The second step (respiratory NO2− reduction to NH4+) is mediated by cytochrome c nitrite reductase, occurring at the periplasmic membrane surface.

57071d4a4e2c.title: Denitrification
57071d4a4e2c.sentence: Direct reduction from nitrate to ammonium, a process known as dissimilatory nitrate reduction to ammonium or DNRA, is also possible for organisms that have the nrf-gene.

9f191620af58.title: Dissimilatory nitrate reduction to ammonium
9f191620af58.sentence: Despite DNRA not producing nitrous oxide (N2O) as an intermediate during nitrate reduction (as denitrification does), N2O may still be released as a byproduct, thus DNRA may also act as a sink of fixed, bioavailable nitrogen.

75d8ec36ffe0.title: Dissimilatory nitrate reduction to ammonium
75d8ec36ffe0.sentence: DNRA's production of N2O may be enhanced at higher pH levels.

573fbba0e28b.title: Dissimilatory nitrate reduction to ammonium
573fbba0e28b.sentence: Usually DNRA is about 15% of the total nitrate reduction rate, which includes both DNRA and denitrification.

fe1696e6b127.title: Dissimilatory nitrate reduction to ammonium
fe1696e6b127.sentence: This is may be especially pronounced when NO3− is limiting compared to organic carbon, as organic carbon is oxidised more 'efficiently' per NO3− (as each molecule NO3− is reduced farther).

05bf3a6d7fe7.title: Dissimilatory nitrate reduction to ammonium
05bf3a6d7fe7.sentence: - Ecosystems where organic matter has a high C/N ratio

aaba3f15b4ce.title: Dissimilatory nitrate reduction to ammonium
aaba3f15b4ce.sentence: Dissimilatory nitrate reduction to ammonium is more common in prokaryotes but may also occur in eukaryotic microorganisms.

66c86f2eecef.title: Dissimilatory nitrate reduction to ammonium
66c86f2eecef.sentence: DNRA is a component of the terrestrial and oceanic nitrogen cycle.

8f56e81e5b4b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.01%3A_Introduction
8f56e81e5b4b.sentence: When carbon or nutrients move from one place to another, that is a flow, and it connects a source with a destination.

6f77525ebd7e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.01%3A_Introduction
6f77525ebd7e.sentence: Nutrient cycling can occur in various settings and scales: on a farm, in a grassland or forest, or even globally.

8bc74c048413.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.01%3A_Introduction
8bc74c048413.sentence: When you buy fertilizers, nutrients are “flowing” onto the farm.

cb059bcf2397.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.01%3A_Introduction
cb059bcf2397.sentence: When you buy animal feed, both nutrients and carbon are flowing onto the farm.

1d6ee3c4c1c0.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.01%3A_Introduction
1d6ee3c4c1c0.sentence: When you sell sweet corn, apples, alfalfa hay, meat or milk, nutrients and carbon are flowing off the farm.

3e412f82c418.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.01%3A_Introduction
3e412f82c418.sentence: Flows that involve products entering or leaving the farm gate are managed intentionally, whether or not you are thinking about those products in terms of nutrients or carbon.

894a6dfe09e2.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.01%3A_Introduction
894a6dfe09e2.sentence: Other flows are unplanned—for example, when nitrate is lost from the soil by leaching to groundwater or when runoff waters take nutrients along with eroded topsoil to a nearby stream.

63b8b9291c4d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.01%3A_Introduction
63b8b9291c4d.sentence: When crops are harvested and brought to the barn to feed animals, that is a nutrient flow, as is the return of animal manure to the land.

3b7b9670f7f5.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.01%3A_Introduction
3b7b9670f7f5.sentence: Together these two flows are a cycle because nutrients and carbon return to the fields from which they came.

32e6c2356e04.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.01%3A_Introduction
32e6c2356e04.sentence: In forests and natural grassland, the cycling of nutrients is very efficient, nearly 100%.

48d212ed3fab.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.01%3A_Introduction
48d212ed3fab.sentence: However, in many types of agriculture, especially modern specialized farming, there is little real cycling of nutrients because there is no easy way to return the large quantity of nutrients and carbon shipped off the farm (and sometimes across continents and oceans).

3528d400ed70.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.01%3A_Introduction
3528d400ed70.sentence: In addition, nutrients in crop residues don’t cycle very efficiently when the soil is without living plants for long periods; and nutrient runoff and leaching losses are much larger compared to natural systems.

55dcfb0a3651.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.01%3A_Introduction
55dcfb0a3651.sentence: But the cycling of soil nutrients is intimately connected to organic matter, over half of which is carbon.

8020358cbd51.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.04%3A_Flow_Patterns_at_Farm_Scale
8020358cbd51.sentence: When considering the whole farm, there are three main nutrient flow patterns, each one with implications for the long-term functioning of the farm and the environment: 1) imports of nutrients are less than exports, 2) imports are greater than exports or 3) imports are equal to exports.

37c12a5e5567.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.04%3A_Flow_Patterns_at_Farm_Scale
37c12a5e5567.sentence: Farms with a negative nutrient balance are “living off capital” and drawing down the supplies of nutrients from minerals and organic matter.

dcd7c296344d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.04%3A_Flow_Patterns_at_Farm_Scale
dcd7c296344d.sentence: But at some point, the availability of one or more nutrients or organic matter (carbon) becomes so low that crop yields decrease.

cef58c1a4028.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.04%3A_Flow_Patterns_at_Farm_Scale
cef58c1a4028.sentence: Farms that exclusively grow grain or vegetables have a lot of nutrients flowing onto the farm and relatively high annual carbon and nutrient exports when crops are sold (Figure 7.5a).

f2f7fcce0e84.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.04%3A_Flow_Patterns_at_Farm_Scale
f2f7fcce0e84.sentence: For example, the annual export of nutrients is about 135 pounds of nitrogen, 25 pounds of phosphorus and 35 pounds of potassium per acre for corn grain and about 150 pounds of nitrogen, 20 pounds of phosphorus and 130 pounds of potassium per acre for grass hay.

a4136ed90dee.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.04%3A_Flow_Patterns_at_Farm_Scale
a4136ed90dee.sentence: On integrated crop-livestock farms that produce their own feed, imports and exports of nutrients should be relatively small relative to the land farmed and close to balanced.

b0d86f144132.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.04%3A_Flow_Patterns_at_Farm_Scale
b0d86f144132.sentence: Most of the nutrients on this type of operation complete a true cycle on the farm: They are taken up from the soil by plants, which are eaten by the animals, and most of the nutrients are then returned to the soil as manure and urine.

9006bc5cbfca.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.04%3A_Flow_Patterns_at_Farm_Scale
9006bc5cbfca.sentence: It is easier to balance nutrient imports and exports on a mixed crop-livestock and grass-fed beef farms than on either a crop farm or a livestock farm that depends significantly on imported feeds.

9546cd1a0823.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.04%3A_Flow_Patterns_at_Farm_Scale
9546cd1a0823.sentence: Animal farms with inadequate land bases to produce all needed feed pose a different type of problem (Figure 7.5c).

aa3e36bffd04.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.04%3A_Flow_Patterns_at_Farm_Scale
aa3e36bffd04.sentence: When imports are greater than exports, nutrients accumulate on the farm and significant amounts may be lost by leaching to groundwater or in runoff waters with resulting environmental damage.

87f5cb239065.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.04%3A_Flow_Patterns_at_Farm_Scale
87f5cb239065.sentence: Nitrogen and phosphorus are the main nutrients that flow from farms that become water pollutants.

9c4cdc7cd5da.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.04%3A_Flow_Patterns_at_Farm_Scale
9c4cdc7cd5da.sentence: From the environmental perspective and for the sake of long-term soil health, fertility should be raised to, and then maintained at, optimal levels.

e2fb70c4471b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.04%3A_Flow_Patterns_at_Farm_Scale
e2fb70c4471b.sentence: The best way to keep desirable levels once they are reached is to roughly balance inflows and outflows.

cb2e45438b1f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.04%3A_Flow_Patterns_at_Farm_Scale
cb2e45438b1f.sentence: Soil tests can be very helpful in fine-tuning a fertility program and making sure that levels are not building up too high or being drawn down too low (see Chapter 21).

ba926b4ae8ef.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.04%3A_Flow_Patterns_at_Farm_Scale
ba926b4ae8ef.sentence: It should be fairly easy to balance nutrient inflows and outflows on crop farms, at least theoretically, but carbon cycling is difficult.

f4ac1ff5d5ae.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.04%3A_Flow_Patterns_at_Farm_Scale
f4ac1ff5d5ae.sentence: But leftover residue (carbon-based plant material in aboveground residue and roots) from annual crops doesn’t normally replace the organic matter lost during the year of cropping.

fa28352be6d5.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.04%3A_Flow_Patterns_at_Farm_Scale
fa28352be6d5.sentence: Replenishing extra soil carbon occurs only when applying organic fertilizers like manure or compost, through intensive cover cropping, or by adding perennial hay (grass/legume) crops to the rotation.

ad775bb12b21.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.04%3A_Flow_Patterns_at_Farm_Scale
ad775bb12b21.section: N Balance As An Environmental Indicator
ad775bb12b21.sentence: A farm may aim to balance imports and exports of nutrients and carbon, but it also needs to aim for an optimum distribution onto its fields.

c1dd1d96bc55.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.04%3A_Flow_Patterns_at_Farm_Scale
c1dd1d96bc55.section: N Balance As An Environmental Indicator
c1dd1d96bc55.sentence: In the past, fields around barns received much more manure and typically had excess nutrients compared to those farther away.

26a4b8f637db.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.04%3A_Flow_Patterns_at_Farm_Scale
26a4b8f637db.section: N Balance As An Environmental Indicator
26a4b8f637db.sentence: But with regular soil testing and good manure management planning, farms can balance nutrients and carbon for each individual field.

d29d5e8a3874.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.04%3A_Flow_Patterns_at_Farm_Scale
d29d5e8a3874.section: N Balance As An Environmental Indicator
d29d5e8a3874.sentence: Moreover, livestock farms that use well-planned rotational pasture systems, common in places like New Zealand, don’t have manure transportation issues and prevent nutrient concentration.

750439dde8b3.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.03%3A_Cycling_and_Flows_in_Modern_Agriculture
750439dde8b3.sentence: Older farming styles with integrated crops and animals had good cycling of carbon and nutrients.

83ed5c46b9ee.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.03%3A_Cycling_and_Flows_in_Modern_Agriculture
83ed5c46b9ee.sentence: The first major break in this cycle occurred as cities developed and carbon and nutrients began to routinely travel with farm products to feed the growing urban populations many miles away.

fd03c8bbadf1.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.03%3A_Cycling_and_Flows_in_Modern_Agriculture
fd03c8bbadf1.sentence: It is rare for the carbon and nutrients to return to the soils on which the crops and animals were originally raised (Figure 7.4b).

051c783ed2da.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.03%3A_Cycling_and_Flows_in_Modern_Agriculture
051c783ed2da.sentence: Thus, nutrients and carbon accumulated in urban sewage and polluted waterways around the world.

7096bbc8cae0.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.03%3A_Cycling_and_Flows_in_Modern_Agriculture
7096bbc8cae0.sentence: Even with the building of many new sewage treatment plants in the 1970s and 1980s, effluent containing nutrients still flows into waterways, and sewage sludges are not always handled in an environmentally sound manner.

70da5c466452.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.03%3A_Cycling_and_Flows_in_Modern_Agriculture
70da5c466452.sentence: The trend toward farm specialization, mostly driven by economic forces, has resulted in the second break in nutrient and carbon cycling due to the separation of animals from the land that grows their feed.

75cc1649a17b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.03%3A_Cycling_and_Flows_in_Modern_Agriculture
75cc1649a17b.sentence: With specialized large-scale animal facilities (Figure 7.4c), nutrients and carbon accumulate in manure while crop farmers purchase large quantities of inorganic fertilizers to keep their fields from becoming nutrient deficient, but they don’t usually replace all of the carbon that is lost because organic matter decomposes during the year.

0855407d7877.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.05%3A_Flow_Patterns_at_Large_Scale
0855407d7877.sentence: We have looked at carbon and nutrient balances on farms, but a larger-scale break in nutrient cycling occurs as agricultural products are shipped long distances across continents or even oceans.

3cdfe13525ec.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.05%3A_Flow_Patterns_at_Large_Scale
3cdfe13525ec.sentence: The nutrients from crop farms travel a long way to animal farms and are replaced with fertilizers from a completely different place.

c582a38334e2.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.05%3A_Flow_Patterns_at_Large_Scale
c582a38334e2.sentence: Meanwhile, the animal farms become overloaded with nutrients.

489ba75b1885.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.05%3A_Flow_Patterns_at_Large_Scale
489ba75b1885.sentence: On average, the food we eat has traveled about 1,300 miles from field to processor to distributor to consumer.

a3d82f9486a2.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.05%3A_Flow_Patterns_at_Large_Scale
a3d82f9486a2.sentence: The nutrients in concentrated commercial fertilizers also travel large distances from the mine or factory to distributors and then to the field, like potassium from Saskatchewan to Ohio, or phosphorus from Morocco to Germany.

bd63636b71a4.sentence: The selenium cycle is a biological cycle of selenium similar to the cycles of carbon, nitrogen, and sulfur.

5aa203d8307a.title: Selenium cycle
5aa203d8307a.sentence: Within the cycle, there are organisms which reduce the most oxidized form of the element and different organisms complete the cycle by oxidizing the reduced element to the initial state.

d71228719e3f.title: Selenium cycle
d71228719e3f.sentence: In the selenium cycle it has been found that bacteria, fungi, and plants, especially species of Astragalus, metabolize the most oxidized forms of selenium, selenate or selenite, to selenide.

435f3b35a6b0.title: Selenium cycle
435f3b35a6b0.sentence: Evidence for a selenium cycle is found through the study of selenium accumulator plants.

d5deeb7ddeca.title: Selenium cycle
d5deeb7ddeca.sentence: These plants are found in semi-arid, seleniferous soils.

4f1c3964c2ce.title: Selenium cycle

75518677fdbc.title: Selenium cycle
75518677fdbc.sentence: If the compounds were not oxidized, then an increase in organic selenium would be seen, but selenium in these areas is mainly inorganic.

729512870cf5.title: Selenium cycle

55e76b0ca518.title: Selenium cycle

4b6235866e6f.title: Selenium cycle

29fb4ad4abff.title: Selenium cycle
29fb4ad4abff.sentence: The first process is oxidation and methylation of inorganic and organic selenium by plant roots and microorganisms.

e89b28c4d5a4.sentence: In enzymology, a nitrous oxide reductase also known as nitrogen:acceptor oxidoreductase (N2O-forming) is an enzyme that catalyzes the final step in bacterial denitrification, the reduction of nitrous oxide to dinitrogen.

b9e82d763d65.title: Nitrous-oxide reductase

54caf6425090.title: Nitrous-oxide reductase

582cf213c7e4.title: Potassium cycle
582cf213c7e4.sentence: Potassium exists in its highest concentrations in the upper most layers of soil, stored in three pools: fixed K, exchangeable K, and solution K.

fcd7d41bef82.title: Potassium cycle
fcd7d41bef82.sentence: Exchangeable K is potassium adsorbed onto clay particles and organic matter and accounts for 1-2% of total soil K.

884d301d9484.title: Potassium cycle
884d301d9484.sentence: Potassium in soil solution is the most readily available form of K for plants to absorb, but only amounts to 0.1-0.2% of total soil K.

c6648c1b398e.sentence: Phosphate solubilizing bacteria (PSB) are beneficial bacteria capable of solubilizing inorganic phosphate from insoluble compounds.

aded3f8dbe40.title: Phosphate solubilizing bacteria
aded3f8dbe40.sentence: It is generally accepted that the mechanism of mineral phosphate solubilization by PSB strains is associated with the release of low molecular weight organic acids, through which their hydroxyl and carboxyl groups chelate the cations (ions that have positive charge on it) bound to phosphate, thereby converting it into soluble forms.

0efd6968ffd6.title: Sulfur assimilation
0efd6968ffd6.sentence: Sulfur assimilation is the process by which living organisms incorporate sulfur into their biological molecules.

0b0e65140210.title: Sulfur assimilation
0b0e65140210.sentence: Sulfate is actively taken up across the plasma membrane of the root cells, subsequently loaded into the xylem vessels and transported to the shoot by the transpiration stream.

fecb12e56b1d.title: Sulfur assimilation
fecb12e56b1d.sentence: The uptake and transport of sulfate is ATP-dependent.

85d0d51f50eb.title: Sulfur assimilation
85d0d51f50eb.sentence: In plants, sulfate is absorbed by the roots and then transported to the chloroplasts by the transpiration stream where the sulfur are reduced to sulfide with the help of a series of enzymatic reactions.

65d4d78c44a0.title: Sulfur assimilation
65d4d78c44a0.sentence: Furthermore, the reduced sulfur is incorporated into cysteine, an amino acid that is a precursor to many other sulfur-containing compounds.

b34fa6751c2a.title: Sulfur assimilation

6e53b3f3dbdb.title: Sulfur assimilation

0f1cc2d9db48.title: Sulfur assimilation

f075c82af09c.title: Sulfur assimilation

24ddc84314f9.sentence: Recent research explored the use of the N balance as a simple and easily measured metric for sustainable N use.

3384c0050ea0.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.04%3A_Flow_Patterns_at_Farm_Scale
3384c0050ea0.section: N Balance As An Environmental Indicator
3384c0050ea0.sentence: It is calculated as N inputs through nutrient additions minus N outputs through crop harvest on a seasonal basis.

8815ee2703ab.section: N Balance As An Environmental Indicator
8815ee2703ab.sentence: Optimum N balances are generally between 0 and +50 pounds per acre.

2bf04cd9a2cb.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.04%3A_Flow_Patterns_at_Farm_Scale
2bf04cd9a2cb.section: N Balance As An Environmental Indicator
2bf04cd9a2cb.sentence: If the N balance is below 0, the soil is being mined of nitrogen.

61e364e35b10.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.04%3A_Flow_Patterns_at_Farm_Scale
61e364e35b10.section: N Balance As An Environmental Indicator
61e364e35b10.sentence: If it is above 50 pounds per acre, there is excess that causes environmental damage.

973094814c22.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.04%3A_Flow_Patterns_at_Farm_Scale
973094814c22.section: N Balance As An Environmental Indicator
973094814c22.sentence: The 50 pounds per acre allowance reflects the fact that N use is never 100% efficient and some modest losses are often unavoidable under current practices.

fec14b04504f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.04%3A_Flow_Patterns_at_Farm_Scale
fec14b04504f.section: N Balance As An Environmental Indicator
fec14b04504f.sentence: As we discuss in Chapter 19, nitrogen is difficult to manage and some losses as nitrate leaching and N2O gaseous losses are unavoidable.

819bcf60cb38.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.04%3A_Flow_Patterns_at_Farm_Scale
819bcf60cb38.section: N Balance As An Environmental Indicator
819bcf60cb38.sentence: Most grain farms in the developed world import more nitrogen than they export through their crops, meaning the N balance is positive.

29b7840d27f1.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.04%3A_Flow_Patterns_at_Farm_Scale
29b7840d27f1.section: N Balance As An Environmental Indicator
29b7840d27f1.sentence: It is difficult for farmers to reach the optimum N balance range if they don’t carefully manage the nitrogen through the 4R practices (Chapter 18) and through the use of cover crops to catch excess nitrogen at the end of the season (Chapter 10).

a2ba126f7f05.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.04%3A_Flow_Patterns_at_Farm_Scale
a2ba126f7f05.section: N Balance As An Environmental Indicator
a2ba126f7f05.sentence: Better rotations that include crops that leach very low amounts of nitrate will reduce the average losses over the period of the rotation.

995b073a55c2.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.04%3A_Flow_Patterns_at_Farm_Scale
995b073a55c2.sentence: Potential problems can occur even when fertilizer imports and crop exports are more or less in balance.

57bf23a7eec9.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.04%3A_Flow_Patterns_at_Farm_Scale
57bf23a7eec9.sentence: However, even when imports and exports are approximately the same, significant unintended losses may occur.

e5f05c2f8789.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.04%3A_Flow_Patterns_at_Farm_Scale
e5f05c2f8789.sentence: With high-yielding corn, the amount of N fertilizer applied may be similar to the amount taken up by the corn: perhaps 150–160 pounds of N applied in fertilizer versus 160 pounds in the corn grain.

ecf72909ffa7.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.04%3A_Flow_Patterns_at_Farm_Scale
ecf72909ffa7.sentence: But a lot of the N applied is tied up in organic matter or lost by leaching or denitrification.

b067994433a4.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.04%3A_Flow_Patterns_at_Farm_Scale
b067994433a4.sentence: When corn goes through its two-month-long growth spurt, it increases rapidly in height and then fills its grain.

47ab37f4b3f6.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.04%3A_Flow_Patterns_at_Farm_Scale
47ab37f4b3f6.sentence: During this phase it needs to take up large quantities of nitrogen each day, usually as nitrate.

6ced90b8510a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.04%3A_Flow_Patterns_at_Farm_Scale
6ced90b8510a.sentence: Potential pollution problems arise when the combination of soil-derived and fertilizer-derived available nitrogen greatly exceeds the crop’s need.

5c5a3800df92.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.04%3A_Flow_Patterns_at_Farm_Scale
5c5a3800df92.sentence: In most years there’s a lot of nitrate left over after corn harvest that can leach into groundwater during the fall, winter or early spring.

0f01de87c999.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.04%3A_Flow_Patterns_at_Farm_Scale
0f01de87c999.sentence: Rates of loss depend on the amount of precipitation during these periods but can be in the range of 30–70 pounds per acre (excess nitrate may also be converted into the greenhouse gas nitrous oxide).

0c2b91559874.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.04%3A_Flow_Patterns_at_Farm_Scale
0c2b91559874.sentence: The best ways to decrease soil nitrate at the end of the season and to limit nitrate losses are to 1) precisely predict the crop’s seasonal needs, accounting for all N sources including fertilizer and organic; 2) time N application close to when the crop needs it; and 3) plant a quick-establishing cover crop such as cereal rye to catch excess N. But, rotations with corn appearing less frequently would also help reduce nitrate pollution of water.

fc8e896b0898.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.05%3A_Flow_Patterns_at_Large_Scale
fc8e896b0898.section: Global Grain Trade And Nutrient-Carbon Flows
fc8e896b0898.sentence: They greatly impact the global flow of nutrients and carbon, the basic ingredients for healthy soil.

98bd262411f4.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.05%3A_Flow_Patterns_at_Large_Scale
98bd262411f4.section: Global Grain Trade And Nutrient-Carbon Flows
98bd262411f4.sentence: With the large transfer of grains, and associated carbon and nutrients, from one region to another, deficiencies are created with the exporters and excesses with the importers.

3f7df73389e9.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.05%3A_Flow_Patterns_at_Large_Scale
3f7df73389e9.section: Global Grain Trade And Nutrient-Carbon Flows
3f7df73389e9.sentence: The most prominent transfers involve corn and soybeans shipped from the Americas to East Asia, Europe and the Middle East.

0f504281b78a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.05%3A_Flow_Patterns_at_Large_Scale
0f504281b78a.section: Global Grain Trade And Nutrient-Carbon Flows
0f504281b78a.sentence: The import of these grain crops is heavily driven by higher demand for animal protein and edible oils as a result of rising living standards and diversifying diets.

5e4aec9a4953.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.05%3A_Flow_Patterns_at_Large_Scale
5e4aec9a4953.section: Global Grain Trade And Nutrient-Carbon Flows
5e4aec9a4953.sentence: The Americas have a large agricultural land base and are the primary exporter of those grains, with the United States, Brazil and Argentina accounting for almost 90% of the soybean and 75% of the global corn exports that are mostly used to raise animals in other parts of the world (Figure 7.6).

a218c8b96652.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.05%3A_Flow_Patterns_at_Large_Scale
a218c8b96652.section: Global Grain Trade And Nutrient-Carbon Flows
a218c8b96652.sentence: U.S. grain areas have been fairly stable over the past decades, but the South American countries have met the higher global demand by putting extensive areas of grassland, savannah and even rainforest into crop production.

6c5b2c43cec6.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.05%3A_Flow_Patterns_at_Large_Scale
6c5b2c43cec6.section: Global Grain Trade And Nutrient-Carbon Flows
6c5b2c43cec6.sentence: Evidence is emerging that the breadbasket soils in the Americas are becoming less healthy and have lost organic matter.

1bb6403c5f80.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.05%3A_Flow_Patterns_at_Large_Scale
1bb6403c5f80.section: Global Grain Trade And Nutrient-Carbon Flows
1bb6403c5f80.sentence: The importing countries have many livestock farms that accumulate nutrients and have water pollution concerns.
