2207b20b5739.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.05%3A_Flow_Patterns_at_Large_Scale
2207b20b5739.section: Global Grain Trade And Nutrient-Carbon Flows
2207b20b5739.sentence: Hypoxia (dead zones) is an increasing problem in the seas around Japan, Korea, China and northern Europe.

63522455821c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.05%3A_Flow_Patterns_at_Large_Scale
63522455821c.sentence: National and international food trade occasionally provides benefits by reducing the effects of regional micronutrient deficiencies in the importing country.

2b0878e59961.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/07%3A_Carbon_and_Nutrient_Cycles_and_Flows/7.05%3A_Flow_Patterns_at_Large_Scale
2b0878e59961.sentence: European selenium intake is enhanced by importing wheat grown on U.S. soils, which are naturally higher in the nutrient.

979f8b22ac4e.title: Nitrogen-15 tracing
979f8b22ac4e.sentence: Nitrogen-15 (15N) tracing is a technique to study the nitrogen cycle using the heavier, stable nitrogen isotope 15N.

b0341c51c22b.title: Nitrogen-15 tracing
b0341c51c22b.sentence: Despite the different weights, 15N is involved in the same chemical reactions as the more abundant 14N and is therefore used to trace and quantify conversions of one nitrogen compound to another.

39f53d795d06.title: Nitrogen-15 tracing
39f53d795d06.sentence: 15N tracing allows researchers to distinguish specific nitrogen conversions from a network of simultaneous reactions; e.g. ammonium can at the same time be oxidised by autotrophic microorganisms, produced by mineralisation of organic matter, produced by dissimilatory nitrate reduction and assimilated by microbes and plants.

daa3f6e57bb3.title: Nitrogen-15 tracing
daa3f6e57bb3.sentence: In this case, quantifying the absolute amounts of ammonium does not explain how it is produced or consumed.

c54e7e88aaff.title: Nitrogen-15 tracing
c54e7e88aaff.sentence: The natural 15N abundances are expressed in delta (δ) notation relative to the 15N concentration in the air.

008367eb2eed.title: Nitrogen-15 tracing
008367eb2eed.sentence: Natural abundance techniques can be applied without artificial disturbance.

e350ca28eddb.title: Nitrogen-15 tracing
e350ca28eddb.sentence: Apart from δ values, the site preference of 15N and 14N (isotopomers) for the inner or outer position within the nitrous oxide molecule has been used to determine its sources (nitrification or denitrification).

5b804db3bd75.title: Nitrogen-15 tracing
5b804db3bd75.sentence: When nitrogen substrates are artificially enriched (labeled) with 15N, the product of a reaction can directly be linked to its substrate.

06be3b3b71ce.title: Nitrogen-15 tracing
06be3b3b71ce.sentence: In contrast to natural abundance techniques, 15N labeling allows to precisely calculate reaction rates.

de99c1f5c306.title: Nitrogen-15 tracing
de99c1f5c306.sentence: The amendment of additional nitrogen can also be a bias by changing natural nitrogen transformations.

e8122d3c2a99.title: Nitrogen-15 tracing
e8122d3c2a99.sentence: In agricultural soil, however, application of 15N enriched tracers, such as ammonium and nitrate, resembles conventional fertilisation practise.

3f84b179f0ce.title: Nitrogen-15 tracing
3f84b179f0ce.sentence: A way to calculate nitrogen transformation rates in soil can be achieved by numerical approximation that takes different, simultaneous nitrogen transformations into account.

0c9aa306a92f.title: Nitrogen-15 tracing
0c9aa306a92f.sentence: A numerical tool to study the nitrogen cycle is the Ntrace model based on a Markov chain Monte Carlo simulation.

f7e1c63d958d.title: Fertilizer
f7e1c63d958d.sentence: A fertilizer or fertiliser is any material of natural or synthetic origin that is applied to soil or to plant tissues to supply plant nutrients.

430ed79bc090.title: Fertilizer
430ed79bc090.sentence: Fertilizers may be distinct from liming materials or other non-nutrient soil amendments.

f32eeb7232ec.title: Fertilizer
f32eeb7232ec.sentence: For most modern agricultural practices, fertilization focuses on three main macronutrients: nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), and potassium (K) with occasional addition of supplements like rock flour for micronutrients.

21d26b4e1405.title: Fertilizer
21d26b4e1405.sentence: Fertilizers enhance the growth of plants.

0936599d99e0.title: Fertilizer
0936599d99e0.sentence: This goal is met in two ways, the traditional one being additives that provide nutrients.

924820c0d60f.title: Fertilizer
924820c0d60f.sentence: The second mode by which some fertilizers act is to enhance the effectiveness of the soil by modifying its water-holding capacity and aeration.

b9f3b5172445.title: Fertilizer
b9f3b5172445.sentence: Historically, fertilization came from natural or organic sources: compost, animal manure, human manure, harvested minerals, crop rotations, and byproducts of human-nature industries (e.g. fish processing waste, or bloodmeal from animal slaughter).

100e810be659.title: Fertilizer
100e810be659.sentence: Fertilizers are commonly used for growing all crops, with application rates depending on soil fertility, usually as measured by a soil test and according to the particular crop.

2f1d20bb5445.title: Fertilizer
2f1d20bb5445.sentence: Legumes, for example, fix nitrogen from the atmosphere and generally do not require nitrogen fertilizer, hence their promising use for ensuring agriculture sustainability.

d8133a1593af.title: Fertilizer
d8133a1593af.sentence: Conservative estimates report 30 to 50% of crop yields are attributed to natural or synthetic commercial fertilizers.

4975efdeb57c.title: Fertilizer
4975efdeb57c.sentence: Agricultural use of inorganic fertilizers in 2023 was 190 million tonnes of nutrients, of which 112 million tonnes (58%) was nitrogen.

31a0cb98f5da.title: Fertilizer
31a0cb98f5da.sentence: Fertilizers, especially when applied excessively, can have environmental consequences such as water pollution and eutrophication due to nutrient runoff.

0c435d44626e.title: Fertilizer
0c435d44626e.sentence: In some cases contamination and pollution of soil result by accumulation of heavy metals contained in some fertilizers collected through mining.

77d96b562b16.title: Compost
77d96b562b16.sentence: Compost is a mixture of ingredients used as plant fertilizer and to improve soil's physical, chemical, and biological properties.

3a50fb162a3a.title: Compost
3a50fb162a3a.sentence: It is commonly prepared by decomposing plant and food waste, recycling organic materials, and manure.

f499fe96ca59.title: Compost
f499fe96ca59.sentence: The resulting mixture is rich in plant nutrients and beneficial organisms, such as bacteria, protozoa, nematodes, and fungi.

2d6fe87cad0b.title: Compost
2d6fe87cad0b.sentence: The benefits of compost include providing nutrients to crops as fertilizer, acting as a soil conditioner, increasing the humus or humic acid contents of the soil, and introducing beneficial microbes that help to suppress pathogens in the soil and reduce soil-borne diseases.

34383b716e00.title: Compost
34383b716e00.sentence: Compost adds organic matter to the soil and increases the nutrient content and biodiversity of microbes in soil.

48d5007afaae.title: Compost
48d5007afaae.sentence: Compost improves soil fertility in gardens, landscaping, horticulture, urban agriculture, and organic farming, reducing dependency on commercial chemical fertilizers.

d1338a73adb7.title: Compost
d1338a73adb7.sentence: Composting is an important part of waste management, since food and other compostable materials make up about 20% of waste in landfills, and due to anaerobic conditions, these materials take longer to biodegrade in the landfill.

b03cf9991adb.title: Compost
b03cf9991adb.sentence: Composting offers an environmentally superior alternative to using organic material for landfill because composting reduces methane emissions due to anaerobic conditions, and provides economic and environmental co-benefits.

6c0205efa1cb.title: Compost
6c0205efa1cb.sentence: For example, compost can also be used for land and stream reclamation, wetland construction, and landfill cover.

eb87575f9404.title: Bioremediation
eb87575f9404.sentence: Some examples of bioremediation related technologies are phytoremediation, bioventing, bioattenuation, biosparging, composting (biopiles and windrows), and landfarming.

3676df10e6b7.title: Compost
3676df10e6b7.sentence: Composting dates back to at least the early Roman Empire and was mentioned as early as Cato the Elder's 160 BCE piece De Agri Cultura.

1857ae68bd17.title: Compost
1857ae68bd17.sentence: The first industrial station for the transformation of urban organic materials into compost was set up in Wels, Austria, in the year 1921.

e2556dc8e15d.title: Soil conditioner
e2556dc8e15d.sentence: A soil conditioner is a product which is added to soil to improve the soil’s physical qualities, usually its fertility (ability to provide nutrition for plants) and sometimes its mechanics.

217d605d36db.title: Soil conditioner
217d605d36db.sentence: In general usage, the term "soil conditioner" is often thought of as a subset of the category soil amendments (or soil improvement, soil condition), which more often is understood to include a wide range of fertilizers and non-organic materials.

676298e6e343.title: Soil conditioner
676298e6e343.sentence: Some examples include biochar, bone meal, blood meal, coffee grounds, compost, compost tea, coir, manure, straw, peat, sphagnum moss, vermiculite, sulfur, lime, hydroabsorbant polymers, biosolids, and rock flour.

740b9a46841e.title: Soil conditioner
740b9a46841e.sentence: The most common use of soil conditioners is to improve soil structure.

b6ee9da3db42.title: Soil conditioner
b6ee9da3db42.sentence: Soil compaction impedes root growth, decreasing the ability of plants to take up nutrients and water.

980a29b9e4c8.title: Soil conditioner
980a29b9e4c8.sentence: Soil conditioners can add more loft and texture to keep the soil loose.

adb18a26ab8a.title: Soil conditioner
adb18a26ab8a.sentence: Many soil amendments also add nutrients such as carbon and nitrogen, as well as beneficial bacteria.

6df21c6f7c1e.title: Soil conditioner
6df21c6f7c1e.sentence: Additional nutrients, such as calcium, magnesium and phosphorus, may be augmented by amendments as well.

64b7a0824895.title: Soil conditioner
64b7a0824895.sentence: Soil amendments can also greatly increase the cation exchange capacity (CEC) of soils.

5cc8594a94df.title: Soil conditioner
5cc8594a94df.sentence: The addition of organic material for instance can greatly improve the water retention abilities of sandy soils and they can be added to adjust the pH of the soil to meet the needs of specific plants or to make highly acidic or alkaline soils more usable.

071441ee76c1.title: Soil conditioner
071441ee76c1.sentence: Soil testing should be performed prior to applying a soil conditioner to learn more about the composition and structure of the soil.

1978561b930e.title: Soil conditioner
1978561b930e.sentence: This testing will determine which conditioners will be more appropriate for the available conditions.

2bd3a2e7b6fe.title: Soil conditioner
2bd3a2e7b6fe.sentence: For example, salts, nitrogen, metals and other nutrients that are present in many soil amendments are not productive when added in excess, and can actually be detrimental to plant health.

212c03917279.title: Soil conditioner
212c03917279.sentence: (See fertilizer burn.) Runoff of excess nutrients into waterways also occurs, which is harmful to the water quality and, through it, the environment.

75a41e113df0.title: Soil conditioner
75a41e113df0.sentence: In the context of construction soil conditioning is also called soil stabilization.

81adffed4051.title: Mulch
81adffed4051.sentence: A mulch is a layer of material applied to the surface of soil.

036c70943b40.title: Mulch
036c70943b40.sentence: Reasons for applying mulch include conservation of soil moisture, improving fertility and health of the soil, reducing weed growth, and enhancing the visual appeal of the area.

64a880f18b9d.title: Mulch
64a880f18b9d.sentence: Many materials are used as mulches, which are used to retain soil moisture, regulate soil temperature, suppress weed growth, and for aesthetics.

0a74db7c085b.title: Mulch
0a74db7c085b.sentence: Mulch is usually, but not exclusively, organic in nature.

363fccb236bc.title: Mulch
363fccb236bc.sentence: It may be permanent (e.g. plastic sheeting) or temporary (e.g. bark chips).

6df1237bbbc1.title: Mulch
6df1237bbbc1.sentence: Mulch layers are normally 5 centimetres (2 in) or more deep when applied.

42e801d2b341.title: Mulch
42e801d2b341.sentence: Towards the beginning of the growing season, mulches serve initially to warm the soil by helping it retain heat which is otherwise lost during the night.

19a28639dc6a.title: Mulch
19a28639dc6a.sentence: This allows early seeding and transplanting of certain crops, and encourages faster growth.

4de26ef0785b.title: Mulch
4de26ef0785b.sentence: As the season progresses, mulch stabilizes the soil temperature and moisture, and prevents the growing of weeds from seeds.

9fd36accbf4e.title: Mulch
9fd36accbf4e.sentence: Mulch forms a layer between the soil and the atmosphere reducing evaporation.

1d30bc0948ad.title: Mulch
1d30bc0948ad.sentence: However, mulch can also prevent water from reaching the soil by absorbing or blocking water from light rains and overly thick layers of mulch can reduce oxygen in the soil.

5fbf88893ab3.title: Mulch
5fbf88893ab3.sentence: Mulches of manure and compost will be incorporated naturally into the soil by the activity of worms and other organisms.

f56753894149.title: Mulch
f56753894149.sentence: They are applied to the soil surface, around trees, paths, flower beds, to prevent soil erosion on slopes, and in production areas for flower and vegetable crops.

37ac67ac8b79.title: Mulch
37ac67ac8b79.sentence: Use takes into consideration availability, cost, appearance, the effect it has on the soil—including chemical reactions and pH, durability, combustibility, rate of decomposition, how clean it is—some can contain weed seeds or plant pathogens.

97567ca137f3.title: Biochar
97567ca137f3.sentence: Biochar is defined by the International Biochar Initiative as the "solid material obtained from the thermochemical conversion of biomass in an oxygen-limited environment".

066c23472d40.title: Biochar
066c23472d40.sentence: It is the lightweight black remnants remaining after the pyrolysis of biomass, consisting of carbon and ashes.

512d5cd983b2.title: Biochar
512d5cd983b2.sentence: Despite its name, biochar is sterile immediately after production and only gains biological life following assisted or incidental exposure to biota.

eac815217a26.title: Biochar
eac815217a26.sentence: Biochar is mainly used in soils to increase soil aeration, reduce soil emissions of greenhouse gases, improve soil fertility, reduce nutrient leaching, reduce soil acidity, and potentially increase the water content of coarse soils.

9bae46d876bc.title: Biochar
9bae46d876bc.sentence: However, when applied excessively or made from feedstock unsuitable for the soil type, biochar soil amendments also have the potential for negative effects, including harming soil biota, reducing available water content, altering soil pH, and increasing salinity.

023beb4b30b8.title: Biochar
023beb4b30b8.sentence: Due to its refractory stability, biochar can stay in soils or other environments for thousands of years.

55a1e6db367f.title: Biochar
55a1e6db367f.sentence: This has given rise to the concept of biochar carbon removal, a process of carbon sequestration in the form of biochar.

3ac4fe3b56a0.title: Biochar
3ac4fe3b56a0.sentence: Pre-Columbian Amazonians produced biochar by smoldering agricultural waste (i.e., covering burning biomass with soil) in pits or trenches.

1e0b1acfd7fb.title: Biochar
1e0b1acfd7fb.sentence: It is not known if they intentionally used biochar to enhance soil productivity.

83be0d10e043.title: Biochar
83be0d10e043.sentence: European settlers called it terra preta de Indio.

45844278ad4f.title: Biochar
45844278ad4f.sentence: The word "biochar" is a late-20th century English neologism derived from the Greek word 'βίος' (bios, 'life') and 'char' (charcoal produced by carbonization of biomass).

1dba0d5e5589.title: Biochar
1dba0d5e5589.sentence: Beyond soil application, biochar can be used for slash-and-char farming, for water retention in soil, and as an additive for animal fodder.

e8304d9c886e.title: Biochar
e8304d9c886e.sentence: Biochar has been shown to be an effective SCM, reducing concrete production emissions while maintaining required strength and ductility properties.

fdd452970fb3.title: Biochar
fdd452970fb3.sentence: Biochar is reported to remove contaminants such as heavy metals, dyes, organic pollutants.

553bd709f2c7.title: Fertilizer
553bd709f2c7.sentence: Synthetic fertilizers used in agriculture have wide-reaching environmental consequences.

20ed1edccae6.title: Fertilizer
20ed1edccae6.sentence: The use of fertilizer has also led to a number of direct environmental consequences: agricultural runoff which leads to downstream effects like ocean dead zones and waterway contamination, soil microbiome degradation, and accumulation of toxic compounds in ecosystems.

5e080fa0e141.title: Fertilizer
5e080fa0e141.sentence: According to the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) Special Report on Climate Change and Land, production of these fertilizers and associated land use practices are drivers of global warming.

57b32f9fce78.title: Fertilizer
57b32f9fce78.sentence: Indirect environmental impacts include: N-crop-pest cascades, increased greenhouse gas emissions and environmental impacts of fracking for the natural gas used in the Haber process, the agricultural boom which is partially responsible for the rapid growth in human population and large-scale industrial agricultural practices associated with it causing pressure on biodiversity, habitat destruction and fragmentation, and agricultural soil loss.

6368c870a96c.title: Fertilizer
6368c870a96c.section: Environmental effects > Fossil fuel consumption and sustainability
6368c870a96c.sentence: Most synthetic fertilizer is fed from fossil fuel, using fossil energy and methane for producing hydrogen used in the synthesis of ammonia by the Haber process, as well as various chemical reactions used in the synthesis of most fertilizers (e.g. urea, ammonium nitrate, superphosphate).

ca9e56cbe420.title: Fertilizer
ca9e56cbe420.section: Environmental effects > Fossil fuel consumption and sustainability
ca9e56cbe420.sentence: Some alternatives have been proposed for the production of hydrogen, such as solar energy, waste treatment, or electrolysis.

05f5322f759c.title: Fertilizer
05f5322f759c.sentence: The excess use of organic amendments (e.g. pig slurry) may have detrimental effects on water quality through contamination of the aquifer and subsequent eutrophication of the water bodies it feds.

405be97513cc.title: Fertilizer
405be97513cc.sentence: Most policy and regulatory approaches to address these issues focus on pivoting agricultural practices towards sustainable or regenerative agricultural practices: these use less synthetic fertilizers (for example sustainable agriculture), better soil management (for example no-till agriculture) and more organic fertilizers (for example organic farming, conservation agriculture, biodynamic agriculture).

013530fbc31c.title: Fertilizer
013530fbc31c.sentence: Sustainable agricultural practices, such as reduced tillage and planting buffer strips, can minimize these adverse environmental effects.

67aa24b7ee58.title: Fertilizer
67aa24b7ee58.section: Application > Timing and amount of application
67aa24b7ee58.sentence: The timing of application of fertilizers (here only mineral fertilizers will be considered) is a function of crop requirements, weather condition and market opportunities.

01a631616eec.title: Fertilizer
01a631616eec.section: Application > Timing and amount of application
01a631616eec.sentence: It varies in nature and amount according to the type of agriculture (e.g. intensive farming versus conservation agriculture, grassland versus arable land), and the presence or absence of signs of nutrient deficiencies.

7fbea2b0a26f.title: Fertilizer
7fbea2b0a26f.section: Application > Timing and amount of application
7fbea2b0a26f.sentence: Timing fertilization with peak nutrient uptake demand is essential for optimizing both yield and quality.

f11701350d93.title: Fertilizer
f11701350d93.section: Application > Timing and amount of application
f11701350d93.sentence: In general, nutrient uptake rates are highest from early to midgrowing season, which is why fertilization near the time of seeding is generally very effective.

a535de830538.title: Fertilizer
a535de830538.section: Application > Timing and amount of application
a535de830538.sentence: With fall-planted grains (e.g. winter wheat), fall N fertilization followed by spring topdressing is likely the best combination of fertilization practices to optimize yield.

0c9b757f6caa.title: Fertilizer
0c9b757f6caa.section: Application > Timing and amount of application
0c9b757f6caa.sentence: The application of a soluble mineral fertilizer (e.g. ammonium nitrate) is avoided during heavy rainfall because most of it would be lost for the crop and would rapidly pollute the aquifer.

7803ac1278c4.title: Fertilizer
7803ac1278c4.section: Application > Timing and amount of application
7803ac1278c4.sentence: In conservation agriculture (including no-till farming, permaculture) as well as other non-organic alternatives to intensive farming (e.g. smallholding agriculture) the application of mineral fertilizers is reduced to the strict requirements of the cultivated plants and sometimes is quite unnecessary.

df4c12abcfb0.title: Fertilizer
df4c12abcfb0.section: Application > Timing and amount of application
df4c12abcfb0.sentence: After harvest of a main crop (e.g. wheat, maize, potatoes) a catch crop can be sown, using plant species with a rapid growth rate and high demand of nitrogen (e.g. white mustard).

69c964ec79ca.title: Fertilizer
69c964ec79ca.section: Application > Timing and amount of application
69c964ec79ca.sentence: This allows excess nitrogen, in particular the very mobile nitrate anion, to be taken up and transformed in plant proteins before contaminating the groundwater, and the associated geochemical processes, which would rapidly occur in the absence of plant cover.

3626019f1457.title: Fertilizer
3626019f1457.section: Application > Timing and amount of application
3626019f1457.sentence: The catch crop is further buried, allowing its transformation in humus in which nitrogen is fixed according to various stable chemical bonds.

864a291c236b.title: Fertilizer
864a291c236b.sentence: Fertilizers typically provide, in varying proportions:

cafcfc0a1389.title: Fertilizer
cafcfc0a1389.sentence: - Micronutrients: copper (Cu), iron (Fe), manganese (Mn), molybdenum (Mo), zinc (Zn), and boron (B).

65931c8e1578.title: Fertilizer
65931c8e1578.sentence: - Phosphorus (P): development of roots, flowers, seeds and fruit;

1daea801da01.title: Fertilizer
1daea801da01.sentence: - Potassium (K): strong stem growth, movement of water in plants, promotion of flowering and fruiting;

852e6c2e05e9.title: Fertilizer
852e6c2e05e9.sentence: The nutrients required for healthy plant life are classified according to the elements, but the elements are not used as fertilizers.

2076c4188bfb.title: Fertilizer
2076c4188bfb.sentence: Instead, compounds containing these elements are the basis of fertilizers.

37d5c2caaa58.title: Fertilizer
37d5c2caaa58.sentence: Nitrogen is the most important fertilizer since nitrogen is present in proteins (amide bonds between amino acids), DNA (puric and pyrimidic [check spelling] bases), and other components (e.g., tetrapyrrolic heme in chlorophyll).

0e60e59265c9.title: Fertilizer
0e60e59265c9.sentence: Although nitrogen makes up most of the atmosphere, it is in a form that is unavailable to plants.

83a1eb2f6601.title: Fertilizer
83a1eb2f6601.sentence: Nitrogen is made available to plants through weathering of nitrogen-containing parent rocks and nitrogen fixation.

7624f93503c5.title: Fertilizer
7624f93503c5.sentence: Only some free-living (e.g. Clostridium) and symbiotic bacteria living in root systems of host plants (notably legumes) can fix atmospheric nitrogen (N2) by converting it to ammonia (NH3) and amino acids which are available to plants.

ba8eaaef9a1b.title: Fertilizer
ba8eaaef9a1b.sentence: Phosphate (PO3−4) is required for the production of DNA (genetic code) and ATP, the main energy carrier in cells, as well as certain lipids (phospholipids, the main components of the lipidic double layer of the cell membranes).

0d68210a637c.title: Fertilizer
0d68210a637c.sentence: Fertilizers are classified in several ways.

aeda00aa5582.title: Fertilizer
aeda00aa5582.sentence: They are classified according to whether they provide a single nutrient (e.g., K, P, or N), in which case they are classified as straight fertilizers.

c3cfbd3a6335.title: Fertilizer
c3cfbd3a6335.sentence: Multinutrient fertilizers (or complex fertilizers) provide two or more nutrients, for example, N and P combined.

3c68b35c2f07.title: Fertilizer
3c68b35c2f07.sentence: Fertilizers are also sometimes classified as inorganic (the topic of most of this article) versus organic.

d6b1aa3ecc57.title: Fertilizer
d6b1aa3ecc57.sentence: Inorganic fertilizers exclude carbon-containing materials except urea.

8337eb99477b.title: Fertilizer
8337eb99477b.sentence: Inorganic are sometimes called synthetic fertilizers since various chemical treatments are required for their manufacture.

403e0d7f9f8a.title: Fertilizer
403e0d7f9f8a.sentence: Organic fertilizers are usually (recycled) plant- or animal-derived matter (e.g. compost, manure, respectively).

6ef0807d81e5.title: Fertilizer
6ef0807d81e5.sentence: Major two-component fertilizers provide both nitrogen and phosphorus to the plants.

09a812bcdb5e.title: Fertilizer
09a812bcdb5e.sentence: NPK fertilizers are three-component fertilizers providing nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium.

8e881f576cf8.title: Fertilizer
8e881f576cf8.sentence: There exist two types of NPK fertilizers: compound and blends.

18e13df82187.title: Fertilizer
18e13df82187.sentence: Compound NPK fertilizers contain chemically bound ingredients, while blended NPK fertilizers are physical mixtures of single nutrient components.

7e1e3a03ce51.title: Fertilizer
7e1e3a03ce51.sentence: More than 90% of a typical superphosphate fertilizer is water-soluble.

6c626435340c.title: Fertilizer
6c626435340c.sentence: About 85% of MAP and DAP fertilizers are soluble in water.

457b8c672a2e.title: Fertilizer
457b8c672a2e.sentence: Nitrogen fertilizers are made from ammonia (NH3) produced by the Haber–Bosch process.

87aec05328ba.title: Fertilizer
87aec05328ba.sentence: In this energy-intensive process, natural gas (CH4) usually supplies the hydrogen, and the nitrogen (N2) is derived from the air.

ad6b032d3947.title: Fertilizer
ad6b032d3947.sentence: This ammonia is used as a feedstock for all other nitrogen fertilizers, such as anhydrous ammonium nitrate (NH4NO3) and urea (CO(NH2)2).

f21686cc105e.title: Fertilizer
f21686cc105e.sentence: Nitrates are also produced from ammonia by the Ostwald process.

4b2b6f136141.title: Fertilizer
4b2b6f136141.sentence: The main nitrogen-based straight fertilizer is ammonia (NH3), ionized in solution as ammonium (NH4+), applied in the form of salts or derivatives, including:

f43fac487a9c.title: Fertilizer
f43fac487a9c.sentence: - Ammonium nitrate (NH4NO3) with 34-35% nitrogen is widely used.

7497e8dd8191.title: Fertilizer
7497e8dd8191.sentence: - Calcium ammonium nitrate Is a blend of 20-30% limestone CaCO3 or dolomite CaMg(CO3)2 and 70-80% ammonium nitrate with 24-28% nitrogen.

c2622b9a2abf.title: Fertilizer
c2622b9a2abf.sentence: Deposits of sodium nitrate (NaNO3) (Chilean saltpeter) are also found in the Atacama Desert in Chile and were one of the original (1830) nitrogen-rich fertilizers used.

9e8ac1e231be.title: Fertilizer
9e8ac1e231be.sentence: It is still mined for fertilizer use.

e5f5c535095f.title: Fertilizer
e5f5c535095f.sentence: It is estimated that a third of annual global food production uses ammonia from the Haber–Bosch process and that this supports nearly half the world's population.

a6cf4f915d11.title: Fertilizer
a6cf4f915d11.section: Environmental effects > Contribution to the greenhouse effect
a6cf4f915d11.sentence: Nitrogen fertilizer was used at a rate of about 110 million tons (of N) per year in 2012.

1f0ec17257e1.title: Fertilizer
1f0ec17257e1.sentence: Only a fraction of the nitrogen-based fertilizers is converted to plant matter.

cb79fe2d78a7.title: Fertilizer
cb79fe2d78a7.sentence: The remainder accumulates in the soil or is lost as run-off.

64b64ce0c037.title: Fertilizer
64b64ce0c037.sentence: Ammonia-oxidizing bacteria (AOB), such as species of Nitrosomonas, oxidize ammonia (NH3) to nitrite (NO−2), a process termed nitrification.

250b04fe62c4.title: Fertilizer
250b04fe62c4.sentence: Nitrite-oxidizing bacteria, especially Nitrobacter, oxidize nitrite (NO−2) to nitrate (NO−3), which is extremely soluble and mobile, being leached easily to groundwater then to rivers then to the sea, and is a major cause of eutrophication and algal blooms in rivers, lakes and sea shores.

99f734dacfb6.title: Urea
99f734dacfb6.sentence: Urea, also called carbamide (because it is a diamide of carbonic acid), is an organic compound with chemical formula CO(NH2)2.

28c9a3cccb3b.title: Urea
28c9a3cccb3b.sentence: Urea serves an important role in the cellular metabolism of nitrogen-containing compounds by animals and is the main nitrogen-containing substance in the urine of mammals.

fc9bd9d66e87.title: Urea
fc9bd9d66e87.sentence: Urea is widely used in fertilizers as a source of nitrogen (N).

79a9c581d300.title: Urea
79a9c581d300.sentence: More than 90% of world industrial production of urea is for use as a nitrogen-release fertilizer.

1d0b10f013b1.title: Urea
1d0b10f013b1.sentence: Urea has the highest nitrogen content of all solid nitrogenous fertilizers in common use.

5da0cbcd99a8.title: Urea
5da0cbcd99a8.sentence: Therefore, it has a low transportation cost per unit of nitrogen nutrient.

38cd6b8ffd23.title: Fertilizer
38cd6b8ffd23.sentence: - Urea (CO(NH2)2), with 45-46% nitrogen, another popular source of nitrogen, having the advantage that it is solid and non-explosive, unlike ammonia and ammonium nitrate.

dc9cb2088984.title: Fertilizer
dc9cb2088984.sentence: Many soil bacteria possess the enzyme urease, which catalyzes the conversion of urea to ammonium ion (NH+4) and bicarbonate ion (HCO−3).

bc74c608f635.title: Urea
bc74c608f635.sentence: Urea breaks down in the soil to give ammonium ions (NH+4).

961ed8561cd6.title: Urea
961ed8561cd6.sentence: The ammonium is taken up by the plant through its roots.

e80df20bef36.title: Urea
e80df20bef36.sentence: In some soils, the ammonium is oxidized by bacteria to give nitrate (NO−3), which is also a nitrogen-rich plant nutrient.

648ef72ef7db.title: Urea
648ef72ef7db.sentence: The loss of nitrogenous compounds to the atmosphere and runoff is wasteful and environmentally damaging so urea is sometimes modified to enhance the efficiency of its agricultural use.

0e9530bee2d3.title: Urea
0e9530bee2d3.sentence: Techniques to make controlled-release fertilizers that slow the release of nitrogen include the encapsulation of urea in an inert sealant, and conversion of urea into derivatives such as urea-formaldehyde compounds, which degrade into ammonia at a pace matching plants' nutritional requirements.

24b3037c2b04.title: Urea
24b3037c2b04.sentence: The most common impurity of synthetic urea is biuret, which impairs plant growth.

81f33c20ee3b.title: Alkali soil
81f33c20ee3b.sentence: Where urea is made available cheaply to farmers, it is also used to reduce soil alkalinity/salinity primarily before being used as a fertilizer.

0def90728188.title: Urea
0def90728188.sentence: Urea can cause algal blooms to produce toxins, and its presence in the runoff from fertilized land may play a role in the increase of toxic blooms.

d85f530b25b9.title: Urea
d85f530b25b9.sentence: In 1828, Friedrich Wöhler showed that urea can be produced from inorganic starting materials, an important conceptual milestone in chemistry.

6cde580c9523.title: Urea
6cde580c9523.sentence: This showed for the first time that a substance previously known only as a byproduct of life could be synthesized in the laboratory from non-biological starting materials, thereby contradicting the widely held doctrine of vitalism, which stated that organic compounds could only be derived from living organisms.

fdd25fb14c60.title: Leachate
fdd25fb14c60.sentence: A leachate is any liquid that passes through matter and extracts soluble or suspended solids, or any other component of the material it passed through.

f9196f9fa41e.title: Leachate
f9196f9fa41e.sentence: Leachate is a widely used term in the environmental sciences where it has the specific meaning of a liquid that contains environmentally-harmful substances that can enter the environment.

af729569cf84.title: Leachate
af729569cf84.sentence: It is commonly used in the context of land-filling of decomposable or industrial waste.

08ee85c58ab0.title: Leachate
08ee85c58ab0.sentence: Composting sites in areas and/or times of high rainfall also produce leachate.

cddd1012f78c.title: Leachate
cddd1012f78c.sentence: The critical portion then involves exposure to precipitation, which causes the decomposed matter to flow, becoming runoff and therefore leachate.

c590057dfd9e.title: Leachate
c590057dfd9e.sentence: Leachate is associated with stockpiled coal and with waste materials from metal ore mining and other rock extraction processes, especially those in which sulfide containing materials are exposed to air producing sulfuric acid, often with elevated metal concentrations.

02a9daebca1e.title: Acid sulfate soil
02a9daebca1e.sentence: Flushing of acidic leachate to groundwater and surface waters can cause a number of impacts, including:

63e4e2768b17.title: Acid sulfate soil
63e4e2768b17.sentence: The impacts of acid sulfate soil leachate may persist over a long time, and/or peak seasonally (after dry periods with the first rains).

c5c8b830e5a6.title: Agricultural lime
c5c8b830e5a6.sentence: Agricultural lime, also called aglime, agricultural limestone, garden lime or liming, is a soil additive made from pulverized limestone or chalk.

eb8d176c9886.title: Agricultural lime
eb8d176c9886.sentence: The primary active component is calcium carbonate.

c802f78a85ca.title: Agricultural lime
c802f78a85ca.sentence: Unlike the types of lime called quicklime (calcium oxide) and slaked lime (calcium hydroxide), powdered limestone does not require lime burning in a lime kiln; it only requires milling.

e694d23c52b4.title: Agricultural lime
e694d23c52b4.sentence: All of these types of lime are sometimes used as soil conditioners, with a common theme of providing a base to correct acidity, but lime for farm fields today is often crushed limestone.

0802f6169ae1.title: Agricultural lime
0802f6169ae1.sentence: - it increases the pH of acidic soil, reducing soil acidity and increasing alkalinity

3bf5d97426fb.title: Agricultural lime
3bf5d97426fb.sentence: - it provides a source of calcium for plants

9617ae628640.title: Agricultural lime
9617ae628640.sentence: - it improves water penetration for acidic soils

cb7a441661fc.title: Agricultural lime
cb7a441661fc.sentence: - it improves the uptake of major plant nutrients (nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium) of plants growing on acid soils.

a3c47b607e21.title: Agricultural lime
a3c47b607e21.sentence: Lime is not a fertilizer but can be used in combination with fertilizers.

b60ee1a8dd5e.title: Agricultural lime
b60ee1a8dd5e.sentence: Locations that have high rainfall levels become acidic through leaching.

812bd9cc86c2.title: Agricultural lime
812bd9cc86c2.sentence: Land used for crop and livestock purposes loses minerals over time by crop removal and becomes acidic.

b8edc3bdd9df.title: Agricultural lime
b8edc3bdd9df.sentence: The application of modern chemical fertilizers is a major contributor to soil acid by the process in which the plant nutrients react in the soil.

ba89b8ace666.title: Agricultural lime
ba89b8ace666.sentence: Dolomitic lime may be used as a soil input to provide similar effects as agricultural lime, while supplying magnesium in addition to calcium.

eab5ec04bccc.title: Agricultural lime
eab5ec04bccc.sentence: The best way to determine if the soil is acidic or deficient in calcium or magnesium is with a soil test which a university with an agricultural education department can provide at low cost.

88a9cc265fb9.title: Agricultural lime
88a9cc265fb9.sentence: Historically, liming of farm fields in centuries past was often done with burnt lime; the difference is at least partially explained by the fact that affordable mass-production-scale fine milling of stone and ore relies on technologies developed since the mid-19th century.

32f15b62f134.title: Soil pH
32f15b62f134.section: Changing soil pH > Increasing pH of acidic soil
32f15b62f134.sentence: Amendments (soil conditioners) other than agricultural lime that can be used to increase the pH of soil include wood ash, industrial calcium oxide (burnt lime), magnesium oxide, basic slag (calcium silicate), silicate rock dust, and oyster shells.

2b7b7d9b984f.title: Liming (soil)
2b7b7d9b984f.sentence: Liming is the application of calcium- (Ca) and magnesium (Mg)-rich materials in various forms, including marl, chalk, limestone, burnt lime or hydrated lime to soil.

e71d656fe8bc.title: Liming (soil)
e71d656fe8bc.sentence: In acid soils, these materials react as a base and neutralize soil acidity.

47c657cee38b.title: Liming (soil)
47c657cee38b.sentence: This often improves plant growth and increases the activity of soil bacteria, but oversupply may result in harm to plant life.

a0d7dbb16ce1.title: Liming (soil)
a0d7dbb16ce1.sentence: Most acid soils are saturated with aluminum rather than hydrogen ions.

75931503f8d0.title: Liming (soil)
75931503f8d0.sentence: Soil acidity generally results from hydrolysis of aluminum.

e665409fe162.title: Molybdenum deficiency (plant disorder)
e665409fe162.sentence: Raising the soil pH by liming frequently relieves Mo deficiency.

202c627d21cf.title: Liming (soil)
202c627d21cf.section: Impact on soil properties > Effect on soil organic carbon
202c627d21cf.sentence: An agricultural study at the Faculty of Forestry in Freising, Germany, that compared tree stocks two and twenty years after liming found that liming promotes nitrate leaching and decreases the phosphorus content of some leaves.

8aedaff4c332.title: Liming (soil)
8aedaff4c332.sentence: Modern liming was preceded by marling, a process of spreading raw chalk and lime debris across soil, in an attempt to modify pH or aggregate size.

d53cb19ad4a4.title: Liming (soil)
d53cb19ad4a4.sentence: Evidence of these practices dates to the 1200's and the earliest examples are taken from the modern British Isles.

0d6b9e8f76f0.title: Carbon farming
0d6b9e8f76f0.sentence: Carbon farming is a set of agricultural methods that aim to store carbon in the soil and biomass.

c8246f864016.title: Carbon farming
c8246f864016.sentence: The overall goal of carbon farming is to create a net loss of carbon from the atmosphere.

7edcfe919a95.title: Carbon farming
7edcfe919a95.sentence: Agricultural methods for carbon farming include adjusting how tillage and livestock grazing is done, using organic mulch or compost, working with biochar and terra preta, and changing the crop types.

1c0618682d78.title: Carbon farming
1c0618682d78.sentence: Methods used in forestry include reforestation and bamboo farming.

918443de8f04.title: Carbon farming
918443de8f04.sentence: When a soil is converted from natural land or semi natural land, such as forests, woodlands, grasslands, steppes and savannas, the SOC content in the soil reduces by about 30–40%.

ecc62c7628d4.title: Carbon farming
ecc62c7628d4.sentence: The carbon loss from the soil is due to the removal of plant material containing carbon, via harvesting.

3e6a847a67b0.title: Carbon farming
3e6a847a67b0.sentence: The decrease can be counteracted by increasing carbon input.

8bc9f10325b7.title: Carbon farming
8bc9f10325b7.sentence: This can be done via several strategies, e.g. leaving harvest residues on the field, using manure or rotating perennial crops.

701b6b7e9b3d.title: Carbon farming
701b6b7e9b3d.sentence: Perennial crops have a larger below ground biomass fraction, which increases the SOC content.

3065272e9a7e.title: Carbon farming
3065272e9a7e.sentence: Increasing organic matter content in soils aids plant growth, improves soil water retention capacity and reduces fertilizer use.

61087c71cd75.title: Carbon farming
61087c71cd75.sentence: However, the effects of soil sequestration can be reversed.

a3595dd37d66.title: Carbon farming
a3595dd37d66.sentence: If the soil is disrupted or intensive tillage practices are used, the soil becomes a net source of greenhouse gases.

5f752c7325ea.title: Carbon farming
5f752c7325ea.sentence: Typically after several decades of sequestration, the soil becomes saturated and ceases to absorb carbon.

0144ccde55ad.title: Carbon farming
0144ccde55ad.section: Methods used in agriculture > Adjusting tillage
0144ccde55ad.sentence: Plowing splits soil aggregates and allows microorganisms to consume their organic compounds.

883ededb219c.title: Carbon farming
883ededb219c.section: Methods used in agriculture > Adjusting tillage
883ededb219c.sentence: The increased microbial activity releases nutrients, initially boosting yield.

46814d98becf.title: Carbon farming
46814d98becf.section: Methods used in agriculture > Adjusting tillage
46814d98becf.sentence: Thereafter the loss of structure reduces soil's ability to hold water and resist erosion, thereby reducing yield.

3c2754db0ecc.title: Carbon farming
3c2754db0ecc.sentence: Carbon farming tends to be more expensive than conventional agricultural practices.

0d884be4463d.title: Carbon farming
0d884be4463d.sentence: Depending on the region, carbon farmings costs US$3-130 per tonne of carbon dioxide sequestered.

4c08c1e5738f.title: Carbon farming
4c08c1e5738f.sentence: Some countries provide subsidies to farmers to use carbon farming methods.

9a10c7c5cf1f.title: Carbon farming
9a10c7c5cf1f.sentence: As of 2016, variants of carbon farming reached hundreds of millions of hectares globally, of the nearly 5 billion hectares (1.2×10^10 acres) of world farmland.

99f4fcc27f28.title: Perlite
99f4fcc27f28.sentence: Perlite is an amorphous volcanic glass that has a relatively high water content, typically formed by the hydration of obsidian.

6db02a0c0c44.title: Perlite
6db02a0c0c44.sentence: It occurs naturally and has the unusual property of greatly expanding when heated sufficiently.

466d428c9faa.title: Perlite
466d428c9faa.sentence: Perlite softens when it reaches temperatures of 850–900 °C (1,560–1,650 °F).

8ee654611465.title: Perlite
8ee654611465.sentence: Water trapped in the structure of the material vaporises and escapes, and this causes the expansion of the material to 7–16 times its original volume.

82766672c560.title: Perlite
82766672c560.sentence: The expanded material is a brilliant white, due to the reflectivity of the trapped bubbles.

4b897e6b0d11.title: Perlite
4b897e6b0d11.sentence: When used as an amendment, it has high permeability and low water retention and helps prevent soil compaction.

af187e7dec04.title: Perlite
af187e7dec04.sentence: In horticulture, perlite can be used as a soil amendment or alone as a medium for hydroponics or for starting cuttings.

4f6a67ddbbbe.title: Potting soil
4f6a67ddbbbe.sentence: Perlite and vermiculite improve both aeration and water retention.

8e8342d871b2.title: Potting soil
8e8342d871b2.sentence: Cacti and succulents require sharp drainage, thus requiring a much larger percentage of perlite or sand.

8ca8df46828b.title: Compost
8ca8df46828b.sentence: Compost can be tilled directly into the soil or growing medium to boost the level of organic matter and the overall fertility of the soil.

54b030e3ecb7.title: Compost
54b030e3ecb7.sentence: Compost can be added to soil, coir, or peat, as a tilth improver, supplying humus and nutrients.

2a8f8c87888e.title: Compost
2a8f8c87888e.sentence: On open ground for growing wheat, corn, soybeans, and similar crops, compost can be broadcast across the top of the soil using spreader trucks or spreaders pulled behind a tractor.

9f53291711e8.title: Compost
9f53291711e8.sentence: It is expected that the spread layer is very thin (approximately 6 mm (0.24 in)) and worked into the soil prior to planting.

73a5c31302fa.title: Compost
73a5c31302fa.sentence: Application rates of 25 mm (0.98 in) or more are not unusual when trying to rebuild poor soils or control erosion.

db854443cd7f.title: Compost
db854443cd7f.sentence: Although it is rarely used alone, plants can flourish from mixed soil that includes a mix of compost with other additives such as sand, grit, bark chips, vermiculite, perlite, or clay granules to produce loam.

488e1ebddd36.title: Compost
488e1ebddd36.sentence: It is very common to see blends of 20–30% compost used for transplanting seedlings.

d333fd494e80.title: Compost
d333fd494e80.sentence: Generally, direct seeding into a compost is not recommended due to the speed with which it may dry, the possible presence of phytotoxins in immature compost that may inhibit germination, and the possible tie up of nitrogen by incompletely decomposed lignin.

eaaa6313610c.title: Compost
eaaa6313610c.sentence: Compost that is ready to be used as an additive is dark brown or even black with an earthy smell.

82b1b82432da.title: Compost
82b1b82432da.sentence: Compost can be used to increase plant immunity to diseases and pests.

cc53d23fb112.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/13%3A_Making_and_Using_Composts/13.04%3A_Using_Composts
cc53d23fb112.sentence: Finished composts provide relatively low amounts of readily available nutrients.

55b51e9ab685.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/13%3A_Making_and_Using_Composts/13.04%3A_Using_Composts
55b51e9ab685.sentence: During composting, much of the nitrogen is converted into more stable organic forms, although potassium and phosphorus availability remain unchanged.

dcf82236abbd.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/13%3A_Making_and_Using_Composts/13.04%3A_Using_Composts
dcf82236abbd.sentence: Even though most composts don’t supply a large amount of available nitrogen per ton, they still supply fair amounts of other nutrients in available forms and greatly help the fertility of soil by increasing organic matter and by slowly releasing nutrients.

9053e88c8d45.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/13%3A_Making_and_Using_Composts/13.04%3A_Using_Composts
9053e88c8d45.sentence: Composts should not be applied annually at high rates.

ca8aa79ebad1.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/13%3A_Making_and_Using_Composts/13.04%3A_Using_Composts
ca8aa79ebad1.sentence: For example, if high amounts of compost are applied to meet a crop’s nitrogen needs (remember, compost is relatively low in available nitrogen), then nutrients like phosphorus and potassium are applied in excessive amounts and can accumulate in the soil.

a2298c74afdf.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/13%3A_Making_and_Using_Composts/13.04%3A_Using_Composts
a2298c74afdf.sentence: Also, salts may build up if there is not enough rainfall to wash them out of the soil (like under high tunnels and in greenhouses).

9075fb60ab33.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/13%3A_Making_and_Using_Composts/13.04%3A_Using_Composts
9075fb60ab33.sentence: It is recommended to monitor the soil through regular soil tests and to change the fertility strategy accordingly (for example, by using a legume cover crop as a nitrogen source and reducing compost applications).

5b2f84192543.title: Compost
5b2f84192543.sentence: Composting is an aerobic method of decomposing organic solid wastes, so it can be used to recycle organic material.

ea1d7dacb14d.title: Compost
ea1d7dacb14d.sentence: The process involves decomposing organic material into a humus-like material, known as compost, which is a good fertilizer for plants.

6ea36381fe04.title: Compost
6ea36381fe04.sentence: Composting organisms require four equally important ingredients to work effectively:

20886fc0f2bc.title: Compost
20886fc0f2bc.sentence: - Carbon is needed for energy; the microbial oxidation of carbon produces the heat required for other parts of the composting process.

124bf49c8cea.title: Compost
124bf49c8cea.sentence: - Nitrogen is needed to grow and reproduce more organisms to oxidize the carbon.

1501a8aacdf8.title: Compost
1501a8aacdf8.sentence: - Oxygen is required for oxidizing the carbon, the decomposition process.

6eeabcf3517a.title: Compost
6eeabcf3517a.sentence: - Water is necessary in the right amounts to maintain activity without causing locally anaerobic conditions.

3fe55f1f568c.title: Compost
3fe55f1f568c.sentence: Aerobic bacteria need oxygen levels above 5% to perform the processes needed for composting.

ac42ded0166c.title: Compost
ac42ded0166c.sentence: Active management of the pile (e.g., turning over the compost heap) is needed to maintain sufficient oxygen and the right moisture level.

1425200b66e4.title: Compost
1425200b66e4.sentence: Aerobic bacteria and fungi manage the chemical process by converting the inputs into heat, carbon dioxide, and ammonium ions.

22d08d8890f0.title: Compost
22d08d8890f0.sentence: The materials break down into humus in a process taking months.

f67bf00f091f.title: Compost
f67bf00f091f.sentence: Composting is most efficient with a carbon-to-nitrogen ratio of about 25:1.

a779802adc60.title: Compost
a779802adc60.sentence: Above 30, the substrate is nitrogen starved.

af425a8bc9aa.title: Compost
af425a8bc9aa.sentence: Below 15, it is likely to outgas a portion of nitrogen as ammonia.

ff02c6efbfe2.title: Compost
ff02c6efbfe2.sentence: At the most basic level, composting requires gathering a mix of green waste (nitrogen-rich materials such as leaves, grass, and food scraps) and brown waste (woody materials rich in carbon, such as stalks, paper, and wood chips).

70c27a788d49.title: Compost
70c27a788d49.sentence: Fresh grass clippings have an average ratio of about 15:1 and dry autumn leaves about 50:1 depending upon species.

f0a511cb4623.title: Compost
f0a511cb4623.sentence: The air/water balance is critical to maintaining high temperatures 130–160 °F (54–71 °C) until the materials are broken down.

42b1ed95d405.title: Compost
42b1ed95d405.section: Materials that can be composted > Animal manure and bedding
42b1ed95d405.sentence: On many farms, the basic composting ingredients are animal manure generated on the farm as a nitrogen source, and bedding as the carbon source.

a37be25e7ba6.title: Compost
a37be25e7ba6.section: Materials that can be composted > Animal manure and bedding
a37be25e7ba6.sentence: Straw and sawdust are common bedding materials.

a9cde2233b8b.title: Compost
a9cde2233b8b.section: Materials that can be composted > Animal manure and bedding
a9cde2233b8b.sentence: Poultry manure must be blended with high-carbon, low-nitrogen materials.

6d0c40e53238.title: Compost
6d0c40e53238.section: Materials that can be composted > Animal manure and bedding
6d0c40e53238.sentence: Swine manure, which is very wet and usually not mixed with bedding material, must be mixed with straw or similar raw materials.

024f4a88d579.title: Fertilizer
024f4a88d579.section: Environmental effects > Soil > Changes in soil biology
024f4a88d579.sentence: High levels of fertilizer may cause the breakdown of the symbiotic relationships between plant roots and mycorrhizal fungi, in particular when in excess of plant requirements.

e1bc3a787b57.title: Fertilizer
e1bc3a787b57.section: Environmental effects > Soil > Changes in soil biology
e1bc3a787b57.sentence: Chemical fertilizers stimulates the growth of microbial populations but did not change their richness and diversity, while decreases in enzymatic activity have been registered.

9c5e0d5148c8.title: Fertilizer
9c5e0d5148c8.section: Environmental effects > Soil > Changes in soil biology
9c5e0d5148c8.sentence: The combination of soil acidification and high nitrogen content was probably unknown to most soil organisms before the advent of industrial agriculture.

1f3bccb7d49d.title: Fertilizer
1f3bccb7d49d.section: Environmental effects > Soil > Changes in soil biology
1f3bccb7d49d.sentence: This unexpected combination of excess nutrient availability and acid stress causes a depletion in the sustainability of animal and microbial communities by weakening the linkages between aboveground and belowground components of agroecosystems.

b459690051f0.title: Fertilizer
b459690051f0.section: Environmental effects > Soil > Changes in soil biology
b459690051f0.sentence: Sphagnum bogs are now shifting from carbon sinks (thanks to the accumulation of recalcitrant sphagnum litter and anoxic conditions) to carbon sources under the influence of nitrogen deposition and subsequent stimulation of decomposer activity.

1edb497257f4.title: Fertilizer
1edb497257f4.section: Environmental effects > Contribution to the greenhouse effect
1edb497257f4.sentence: The amount of greenhouse gases carbon dioxide, methane and nitrous oxide produced during the manufacture and use of nitrogen fertilizer is estimated as around 5% of anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions.

d3e0a4170418.title: Fertilizer
d3e0a4170418.section: Environmental effects > Contribution to the greenhouse effect
d3e0a4170418.sentence: One third is produced during the production and two thirds during the use of fertilizers.

3c8dc13e83cc.title: Fertilizer
3c8dc13e83cc.section: Environmental effects > Contribution to the greenhouse effect
3c8dc13e83cc.sentence: Nitrate is converted by soil bacteria to nitrous oxide, a greenhouse gas.

1118d32aef62.title: Fertilizer
1118d32aef62.section: Environmental effects > Contribution to the greenhouse effect
1118d32aef62.sentence: Nitrous oxide (N2O) is the third most important greenhouse gas after carbon dioxide and methane.

4764f4137bcc.title: Fertilizer
4764f4137bcc.section: Environmental effects > Contribution to the greenhouse effect
4764f4137bcc.sentence: It has 296 times greater greenhouse effect per ton than carbon dioxide.

5d87974da508.title: Fertilizer
5d87974da508.section: Environmental effects > Contribution to the greenhouse effect
5d87974da508.sentence: It also contributes to stratospheric ozone depletion.

4f3676efa369.title: Fertilizer
4f3676efa369.section: Environmental effects > Contribution to the greenhouse effect
4f3676efa369.sentence: Nitrous oxide emissions by humans, most of which are from fertilizer, between 2007 and 2016 were estimated at 700 million tons of CO2 equivalent.

9da3e6a0ac51.title: Fertilizer
9da3e6a0ac51.sentence: Micronutrients are consumed in smaller quantities and are present in plant tissue on the order of parts-per-million (ppm), ranging from 0.15 to 400 ppm or less than 0.04% dry matter.

652b3ff12568.title: Fertilizer
652b3ff12568.sentence: Typical micronutrients are boron, zinc, molybdenum, iron, and manganese.

5c8732939524.title: Fertilizer
5c8732939524.sentence: These elements are often required as co-enzymes for enzymes essential to the plant's metabolism.

11972283568a.title: Fertilizer
11972283568a.sentence: Because these elements enable catalysts (enzymes), their impact far exceeds their concentration.

f1a9572f2291.title: Fertilizer
f1a9572f2291.sentence: These elements are provided as water-soluble salts.

d55535f281fd.title: Fertilizer
d55535f281fd.sentence: Iron presents special problems because it converts from soluble (ferrous) to insoluble bio-unavailable (ferric) compounds at moderate soil pH and phosphate concentrations.

25cdd03f8592.title: Fertilizer
25cdd03f8592.sentence: The micronutrient needs depend on the plant and the environment.

0a3cb225fbb2.title: Fertilizer
0a3cb225fbb2.sentence: For example, sugar beets appear to require boron, and legumes require cobalt, while environmental conditions such as heat or drought make boron less available for plants, causing boron deficiency.

ebe583592929.title: Fertilizer
ebe583592929.section: Environmental effects > Soil > Trace mineral depletion
ebe583592929.sentence: Many other soils around the world are deficient in zinc, leading to deficiency in both plants and humans, and zinc fertilizers are widely used to solve this problem.

d2483a7bede1.title: Fertilizer
d2483a7bede1.sentence: Fertilizers are applied to crops both as solids and as liquid.

7ac83dfcbe0c.title: Fertilizer
7ac83dfcbe0c.sentence: Solid fertilizer is typically granulated or powdered.

f3625949bc54.title: Fertilizer
f3625949bc54.sentence: Liquid fertilizers comprise aqueous solutions of ammonia, aqueous solutions of ammonium nitrate or urea.

b41d0ec1ea07.title: Fertilizer
b41d0ec1ea07.sentence: About 90% of fertilizers are applied as solids.

7d7296a5ea1a.title: Fertilizer
7d7296a5ea1a.sentence: The most widely used solid inorganic fertilizers are urea, diammonium phosphate and potassium chloride.

a0b23ef275d7.title: Fertilizer
a0b23ef275d7.sentence: Advantages of liquid fertilizer are its more rapid effect and easier coverage.

e8b1eda28c68.title: Fertilizer
e8b1eda28c68.sentence: Granulated fertilizers are more economical to ship and store, not to mention easier to apply.

49ade44c36d0.title: Fertilizer
49ade44c36d0.sentence: The addition of fertilizer to irrigation water is called fertigation.

f11812935faa.title: Fertigation
f11812935faa.sentence: It is usually practiced on the high-value crops such as vegetables, turf, fruit trees, and ornamentals.

0a10b42e2238.title: Fertigation
0a10b42e2238.sentence: - Accurate placement of nutrient, where the water goes the nutrient goes as well.

b40982aa1c9e.title: Fertigation
b40982aa1c9e.sentence: - Ability to "micro dose", feeding the plants just enough so nutrients can be absorbed and are not left to be washed down to storm water next time it rains.

539988e64e74.title: Fertigation
539988e64e74.sentence: Leaching is decreased often through methods used to employ fertigation.

f1ff56dc75c7.title: Fertilizer
f1ff56dc75c7.section: Environmental effects > Soil > Trace mineral depletion
f1ff56dc75c7.sentence: Attention has been addressed to the decreasing concentrations of micronutrients such as iron, zinc, copper and magnesium in many foods over the last 50–60 years.

cacd94c78d41.title: Fertilizer
cacd94c78d41.section: Environmental effects > Soil > Trace mineral depletion
cacd94c78d41.sentence: Intensive farming practices, including the use of synthetic fertilizers, are frequently suggested as reasons for these declines and organic farming is often suggested as a solution.

2c5b3e14ccb6.title: Fertilizer
2c5b3e14ccb6.section: Environmental effects > Soil > Trace mineral depletion
2c5b3e14ccb6.sentence: Although improved crop yields resulting from NPK fertilizers are known to dilute the concentrations of other nutrients in plants, much of the measured decline can be attributed to the use of progressively higher-yielding crop varieties that produce foods with lower mineral concentrations than their less-productive ancestors.

c831d399bebc.title: Fertilizer
c831d399bebc.section: Environmental effects > Soil > Trace mineral depletion
c831d399bebc.sentence: It is, therefore, unlikely that organic farming or reduced use of fertilizers (e.g. conservation agriculture) will solve the problem; foods with high nutrient density are posited to be achieved using older, lower-yielding varieties or the development of new high-yield, nutrient-dense varieties.

5fbf8dc3f944.title: Fertilizer
5fbf8dc3f944.section: Environmental effects > Soil > Trace mineral depletion
5fbf8dc3f944.sentence: Fertilizers are, in fact, more likely to solve trace mineral deficiency problems than cause them: in Western Australia deficiencies of zinc, copper, manganese, iron and molybdenum were identified as limiting the growth of broad-acre crops and pastures in the 1940s and 1950s.

d074f3803220.title: Fertilizer
d074f3803220.section: Environmental effects > Soil > Trace mineral depletion
d074f3803220.sentence: Since this time these trace elements are routinely added to fertilizers used in agriculture in this state.

4b1a2924a905.title: Biofertilizer
4b1a2924a905.sentence: A biofertilizer is a substance containing living micro-organisms which, when applied to seeds, plant surfaces, or soil, colonize the rhizosphere or the interior of the plant and promote growth by increasing the supply or availability of primary nutrients to the host plant.

8b2281347ad8.title: Biofertilizer
8b2281347ad8.sentence: Biofertilizers add nutrients through the natural processes of nitrogen fixation, solubilizing phosphorus, and stimulating plant growth through the synthesis of growth-promoting substances.

e10543212719.title: Biofertilizer
e10543212719.sentence: The micro-organisms in biofertilizers restore the soil's natural nutrient cycle and build soil organic matter.

3871f5bb6163.title: Biofertilizer
3871f5bb6163.sentence: Plant-growth promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR) and mycorrhizae are generally thought to increase the fixation of atmospheric nitrogen, convert inorganic phosphorus compounds into soluble forms, increase the bioavailability of minerals in the soil, and synthesize phytohormones that promote growth, such as auxins and gibberellin.

e83081a224e2.title: Biofertilizer
e83081a224e2.sentence: Biofertilizers can be expected to reduce the use of synthetic fertilizers and pesticides, but they are not yet able to replace their use.

bf9a3af8e7f8.title: Biofertilizer
bf9a3af8e7f8.sentence: Biofertilizers offers an alternative solution for such agrochemicals, and show yield increase of up to about 10–40% by increasing protein contents, essential amino acids, and vitamins, and by nitrogen fixation.

f73954835575.title: Biofertilizer
f73954835575.sentence: Besides promoting growth by multiple mechanisms, biofertilizers produces substances suppressing phytopathogens, guarding plants from abiotic and biotic stresses and detoxification of belowground pollutants.

de9b537addfb.title: Biofertilizer
de9b537addfb.sentence: It can also provide protection against drought and some soil-borne diseases.

f8e0d93b1732.title: Biofertilizer
f8e0d93b1732.sentence: Biofertilizers have been shown to have varying effects in different environments, and even within the same environment.

07a22af06196.title: Biofertilizer
07a22af06196.sentence: They however, have been shown to have the most profound effects in drier climates.

b4d1e1ca8c75.title: Biofertilizer
b4d1e1ca8c75.sentence: - Compost is commonly used as biofertilizers.

d13fd09dd0f1.title: Biofertilizer
d13fd09dd0f1.sentence: It can be used directly on the soil or by using compost-derived products such as extracts or compost-tea made by fermenting compost mass.

e6f342a9a3b0.title: Biofertilizer
e6f342a9a3b0.sentence: Vermicompost-based innoculants proposed by permaculture methods, Korean natural farming and JADAM are examples of biofertilizers.

ce7dc0f3d87a.title: Rock flour
ce7dc0f3d87a.sentence: Rock flour, or glacial flour, consists of fine-grained, silt-sized particles of rock, generated by mechanical grinding of bedrock by glacial erosion or by artificial grinding to a similar size.

bffca2aa7644.title: Rock flour
bffca2aa7644.sentence: Although clay-sized, the flour particles are not clay minerals but typically ground-up quartz and feldspar.

89d2ed74f6ac.title: Rock flour
89d2ed74f6ac.sentence: Rock flour particles may travel great distances either suspended in water or carried by the wind, in the latter case forming deposits called loess.

4cb606af7f8a.title: Rock flour
4cb606af7f8a.sentence: Rock flour, artificial or natural, is a source of plant micronutrients (minerals trace elements) widely used in organic farming practices as a soil conditioner.

217054076c36.title: Rock flour
217054076c36.sentence: The igneous rocks basalt and granite often contain the highest mineral content, whereas limestone, considered inferior in this consideration, is often deficient in the majority of essential macro-compounds, trace elements, and micronutrients.

8eed4a401c52.title: Rock flour
8eed4a401c52.sentence: A 2022 study found that basalt dust improved soil fertility and increased available phosphorus, potassium, calcium and magnesium levels compared to soil without the basalt dust in a period of several months.

9d84a6ea9bf3.title: Rock flour
9d84a6ea9bf3.sentence: In forestry, rock flour can gradually increase the pH and buffering status of soils via its slow-release liming properties and increase tree radial growth if nitrogen is not deficient, even up to 34 years after the application.

5353a26cb7d7.title: Rock flour
5353a26cb7d7.sentence: In some soils which display poor levels of nutrients, application rates of 10 up to 50 tonnes per hectare are required.

2418170913bc.title: Rock flour
2418170913bc.sentence: An early experimenter was the German miller, Julius Hensel, author of Bread from Stones, who reported successful results with steinmehl (stonemeal) in the 1890s.

0c07b53676b2.title: Marl
0c07b53676b2.sentence: Marl is an earthy material rich in carbonate minerals, clays, and silt.

97c6a66667e3.title: Marl
97c6a66667e3.sentence: When hardened into rock, this becomes marlstone.

bd0012dcebdc.title: Marl
bd0012dcebdc.sentence: These typically contain 35–65% clay and 65–35% carbonate.

0073e4de04b7.title: Marl
0073e4de04b7.sentence: The dominant carbonate mineral in most marls is calcite, but other carbonate minerals such as aragonite or dolomite may be present.

68e18632ebe4.title: Marl
68e18632ebe4.sentence: It is formed in marine or freshwater environments, often through the activities of algae.

8a4094997523.title: Marl
8a4094997523.sentence: They are most often found in areas of recent glaciation and are characterized by alkaline water, rich in dissolved calcium carbonate, from which carbonate minerals are deposited.

84107d23640d.title: Fen
84107d23640d.sentence: In extreme rich fens, calcium carbonate can precipitate out of solution to form marl deposits.

6f1bdc62bb77.title: Marl
6f1bdc62bb77.sentence: Marl has been used as a soil conditioner and neutralizing agent for acid soil and in the manufacture of Portland cement.

068b887e871c.title: Marl
068b887e871c.section: Economic geology > Historical use in agriculture
068b887e871c.sentence: In addition to increasing available calcium, marl is valuable for improving soil structure and decreasing soil acidity and thereby making other nutrients more available.

1c574957e850.title: Marl
1c574957e850.section: Economic geology > Modern agricultural and aquacultural uses
1c574957e850.sentence: Because the carbonate in marl is predominantly calcium carbonate, magnesium deficiency may be seen in crops treated with marl if they are not also supplemented with magnesium.

404378307547.title: Vermicompost
404378307547.sentence: Vermicompost (vermi-compost) is the product of the decomposition process using various species of worms, usually red wigglers, white worms, and other earthworms, to create a mixture of decomposing vegetable or food waste, bedding materials, and vermicast.

096670db993e.title: Vermicompost
096670db993e.sentence: The earthworm species (or composting worms) most often used are red wigglers (Eisenia fetida or Eisenia andrei), though European nightcrawlers (Eisenia hortensis, synonym Dendrobaena veneta) and red earthworm (Lumbricus rubellus) could also be used.

ef878b00b955.title: Vermicompost
ef878b00b955.sentence: The two closely related species are anecic: they like to burrow underground and come up for food.

d17a9d7bf81c.title: Vermicompost
d17a9d7bf81c.sentence: As a result, they adapt poorly to shallow compost bins and should be avoided.

5a4c2b9059ab.title: Vermicompost
5a4c2b9059ab.sentence: These excreta have been shown to contain reduced levels of contaminants and a higher saturation of nutrients than the organic materials before vermicomposting.

3c8c75df88af.title: Compost
3c8c75df88af.sentence: These castings have been shown to contain reduced levels of contaminants and a higher saturation of nutrients than the organic materials before vermicomposting.

4b0bb632b08a.title: Vermicompost
4b0bb632b08a.sentence: Vermicomposting has gained popularity in both industrial and domestic settings because, as compared with conventional composting, it provides a way to treat organic wastes more quickly.

76b439449878.title: Vermicompost
76b439449878.sentence: In manure composting, the use of vermicomposting generates products that have lower salinity levels, as well as a more neutral pH.

94dc454833a4.title: Vermicompost
94dc454833a4.sentence: Vermicompost has been shown to be richer in many nutrients than compost produced by other composting methods.

deed2b60036a.title: Vermicompost
deed2b60036a.sentence: Unlike other compost, worm castings also contain worm mucus which helps prevent nutrients from washing away with the first watering and holds moisture better than plain soil.

746d8201523f.title: Vermicompost
746d8201523f.sentence: Additionally, the mucous layer created by worms which surrounds their castings allows for a "time release" effect, meaning not all nutrients are released at once.

ccc3e18d9749.title: Vermicompost
ccc3e18d9749.sentence: - Microbial activity in worm castings is 10 to 20 times higher than in the soil and organic matter that the worm ingests

83d3b30d46d3.title: Vermicompost
83d3b30d46d3.sentence: The most common worms used in composting systems, redworms (Eisenia fetida, Eisenia andrei, and Lumbricus rubellus) feed most rapidly at temperatures of 15–25 °C (59–77 °F).

68c099b5dd52.title: Vermicompost
68c099b5dd52.sentence: Moisture must be maintained above 50%, as lower moisture content will not support worm respiration and can increase worm mortality.

0e9ba9f91cdc.title: Vermicompost
0e9ba9f91cdc.sentence: Operating moisture-content range should be 70–90%, with a suggested content of 70–80% for vermicomposting operations.

2a919703c9a3.title: Vermicompost
2a919703c9a3.sentence: Vermicompost can be mixed directly into the soil, or mixed with water to make a liquid fertilizer known as worm tea.

c3f2c026d2eb.title: Vermicompost
c3f2c026d2eb.sentence: The light brown waste liquid, or leachate, that drains into the bottom of some vermicomposting systems is not to be confused with worm tea.

2496097e8b32.title: Vermicompost
2496097e8b32.sentence: It is an uncomposted byproduct from when water-rich foods break down and may contain pathogens and toxins.

e96aa45c8ef7.title: Vermicompost
e96aa45c8ef7.sentence: Vermicomposting can also be applied for treatment of sewage.

21674bc9c753.title: Vermicompost
21674bc9c753.sentence: A variation of the process is vermifiltration (or vermidigestion) which is used to remove organic matter, pathogens, and oxygen demand from wastewater or directly from blackwater of flush toilets.

07af040e5546.title: Reuse of human excreta
07af040e5546.sentence: A guide by the Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences provides a list of treatment technologies for sanitation resource recovery: Vermicomposting and vermifiltration, black soldier fly composting, algae cultivation, microbial fuel cell, nitrification and distillation of urine, struvite precipitation, incineration, carbonization, solar drying, membranes, filters, alkaline dehydration of urine, ammonia sanitization/urea treatment, and lime sanitization.

1a81d48b5932.title: Controlled-release fertiliser
1a81d48b5932.sentence: A controlled-release fertiliser (CRF) is a granulated fertiliser that releases nutrients gradually into the soil (i.e., with a controlled release period).

2197b6a7e6cc.title: Controlled-release fertiliser
2197b6a7e6cc.sentence: Controlled-release fertilizer is also known as controlled-availability fertilizer, delayed-release fertilizer, metered-release fertilizer, or slow-acting fertilizer.

bb80b5acccc0.title: Controlled-release fertiliser
bb80b5acccc0.sentence: Usually CRF refers to nitrogen-based fertilizers.

3cce920c9626.title: Controlled-release fertiliser
3cce920c9626.sentence: Conventional fertilisers are soluble in water, the nutrients disperse.

9df1831a3ab8.title: Controlled-release fertiliser
9df1831a3ab8.sentence: Because controlled-release fertilisers are not water-soluble, their nutrients disperse into the soil more slowly.

4a5c8cf27d4c.title: Controlled-release fertiliser
4a5c8cf27d4c.sentence: The rate of the release is determined by various main factors: (i) the low solubility of the compounds in the soil moisture, (ii) the breakdown of protective coating applied to fertilizer pellets, and (iii) the conversion of the chemicals into ammonia or similarly effective plant nutrient.

5a4212750556.title: Controlled-release fertiliser
5a4212750556.sentence: The fertiliser granules may have an insoluble substrate or a semi-permeable jacket that prevents dissolution while allowing nutrients to flow outward.

2c2bf915a569.title: Controlled-release fertiliser
2c2bf915a569.sentence: Controlled-nitrogen-release technologies based on polymers derived from combining urea and formaldehyde were first produced in 1936 and commercialized in 1955.

edab6308b7f5.title: Controlled-release fertiliser
edab6308b7f5.sentence: Most slow-release fertilizers are derivatives of urea, a straight fertilizer providing nitrogen.

d1634ebbf6a0.title: Controlled-release fertiliser
d1634ebbf6a0.sentence: Isobutylidenediurea ("IBDU") and urea-formaldehyde slowly convert in the soil to urea, which is rapidly uptaken by plants.

31f3334a1525.title: Controlled-release fertiliser
31f3334a1525.sentence: Controlled release fertilizers are traditional fertilizers encapsulated in a shell that degrades at a specified rate.

4da4bb07e5c6.title: Controlled-release fertiliser
4da4bb07e5c6.sentence: Sulfur is a typical encapsulation material.

fd669c9627a1.title: Controlled-release fertiliser
fd669c9627a1.sentence: Other coated products use thermoplastics (and sometimes ethylene-vinyl acetate and surfactants, etc.) to produce diffusion-controlled release of urea or other fertilizers.

407038184c50.title: Controlled-release fertiliser
407038184c50.sentence: The slow-release properties depend on the degradation of the secondary sealant by soil microbes as well as mechanical imperfections (cracks, etc.) in the capsule.

313d9e4def47.title: Controlled-release fertiliser
313d9e4def47.sentence: 6 to 16 weeks of delayed release in turf applications is typical.

26c9c4447499.title: Controlled-release fertiliser
26c9c4447499.sentence: Many factors motivate the use of CRF, including more efficient use of the fertilizer.

2011518b0408.title: Controlled-release fertiliser
2011518b0408.sentence: Illustrating the problem, it is estimated that, on average, 16% of conventional nitrogen-based fertilizers is lost by evaporation (as NH3, N2O, N2) or run-off ammonia.

021060184747.title: Controlled-release fertiliser
021060184747.sentence: Another factor favoring CRT protecting crops from chemical damage (fertiliser burn).

1263d18a3c0d.title: Controlled-release fertiliser
1263d18a3c0d.sentence: Finally important advantages are economic: fewer applications and the use of less fertiliser overall.

ce51c0d43828.title: Controlled-release fertiliser
ce51c0d43828.sentence: The results (yield) is in most cases improved by >10%.

93ada3af240d.title: Controlled-release fertiliser
93ada3af240d.sentence: CRF has the potential to decrease nitrogenous pollution, which leads to eutrophication.

182fc5d67821.title: Controlled-release fertiliser
182fc5d67821.sentence: The efficient use of nitrogen-base fertilizers is also relevant to the emission of N 2O into the atmosphere each year, of which 36% is due to human activity.

f4f850b56001.title: Controlled-release fertiliser
f4f850b56001.sentence: The anthropogenic N 2O is produced by microorganisms acting on ammonia faster than the plant can uptake this nutrient.

06f39e185fe5.title: Biochar
06f39e185fe5.sentence: Biochar may be plowed into soils in crop fields or added to gardens to enhance their fertility and stability and for medium- to long-term carbon sequestration in these soils.

20fd260fc1e6.title: Biochar
20fd260fc1e6.sentence: It even shows good results when top-dressed.

f09a6d4491a8.title: Biochar
f09a6d4491a8.sentence: Studies reported positive effects from biochar on crop production in degraded and nutrient–poor soils.

7f699c717eda.title: Biochar
7f699c717eda.sentence: Biochar is hygroscopic due to its porous structure and high specific surface area.

1ebe0f6fbf51.title: Biochar
1ebe0f6fbf51.sentence: Due to its porosity, the small holes in biochar can keep water and dissolved minerals in the upper layers of soil, assisting plant growth and reducing the need for and expense of fertilizer.

4d447380fe8e.title: Biochar
4d447380fe8e.sentence: Biochar reduces leaching of E. coli through sandy soils depending on application rate, feedstock, pyrolysis temperature, soil moisture content, soil texture, and surface properties of the bacteria.

da0852c87499.title: Biochar
da0852c87499.sentence: Biochar can remove heavy metals from the soil.

642bcbb02572.title: Biochar
642bcbb02572.sentence: Soil biologist Elaine Ingham highlighted its suitability as a habitat for beneficial soil microorganisms.

b77868d04432.title: Biochar
b77868d04432.sentence: Application rates of 2.5–20 tonnes per hectare (1.0–8.1 t/acre) appear required to improve plant yields significantly.

ead421bf7795.title: Biochar
ead421bf7795.sentence: Biochar costs in developed countries vary from $300–$7,000/tonne, which is generally impractical for the farmer/horticulturalist and prohibitive for low-input field crops.

ae5f22a66ae6.title: Biochar
ae5f22a66ae6.sentence: However, because of its high adsorption capacity, biochar may reduce pesticide efficacy.

59cec80e6d3f.title: Biochar
59cec80e6d3f.sentence: High-surface-area biochars may be particularly problematic.

0343574df668.title: Biochar
