0343574df668.sentence: Biochar's impacts are dependent on its properties as well as the amount applied, although knowledge about the important mechanisms and properties is limited.

3a9cbdf99a0e.title: Biochar
3a9cbdf99a0e.sentence: Biochar impact may depend on regional conditions including soil type, soil condition (depleted or healthy), temperature, and humidity.

1e1f80f572c4.title: Biochar
1e1f80f572c4.sentence: The refractory stability of biochar leads to the concept of biochar carbon removal, a process of carbon sequestration in the form of biochar.

e47d464c0227.title: Biochar
e47d464c0227.sentence: The biochar production process also releases CO2 (up to 50% of the biomass); however, the remaining carbon content becomes indefinitely stable.

7651bd129bc1.title: Biochar
7651bd129bc1.sentence: Biochar can sequester carbon in the soil for hundreds to thousands of years, like coal.

50ac44925411.title: Biochar
50ac44925411.sentence: According to the World Bank, "biochar retains between 10 percent and 70 percent (on average about 50 percent) of the carbon present in the original biomass and slows down the rate of carbon decomposition by one or two orders of magnitude, that is, in the scale of centuries or millennia".

b036f579dc2f.title: Biochar
b036f579dc2f.sentence: Carbon removal can be achieved when high-quality biochar is applied to soils, or added as a substitute material to construction materials such as concrete and tar.

617349f88ad3.title: Biochar
617349f88ad3.sentence: Long-term effects of biochar on carbon sequestration have been examined using soil from arable fields in Belgium with charcoal-enriched black spots dating from before 1870 from charcoal production mound kilns.

f2a8a3ab8020.title: Biochar
f2a8a3ab8020.sentence: This study showed that soil treated over a long period with charcoal showed a higher proportion of maize-derived carbon and decreased respiration, attributed to physical protection, carbon saturation of microbial communities, and, potentially, slightly higher annual primary production.

419f05463570.title: Biochar
419f05463570.sentence: Overall, this study evidences the capacity of biochar to enhance carbon sequestration through reduced carbon turnover.

21472efe1fd7.title: Biochar
21472efe1fd7.sentence: In addition, biochar can promote indirect carbon sequestration by increasing crop yield while potentially reducing carbon mineralization.

1793e798bd7e.title: Biochar
1793e798bd7e.sentence: A 2021 review estimated potential CO2 removal from 1.6 to 3.2 billion tonnes per year, and by 2023 it had become a lucrative business renovated by carbon credits.

9fbf984891d0.title: Biochar
9fbf984891d0.sentence: While early scenario studies focused on technical maxima and suggested that several gigatonnes of CO2 equivalent could be avoided annually, more recent work emphasizes that economically feasible deployment is likely to be smaller, with global removal potentials of roughly 0.3–1.8 Gt CO2 per year under carbon prices below US$100 per tonne.

dc7085f6d2cb.title: Biochar
dc7085f6d2cb.sentence: Real world implementation remains at an early stage: global biochar production is estimated to be on the order of a few hundred thousand tonnes per year, delivering well under 1 Mt CO2 per year of certified removal, though voluntary carbon market deliveries and installed capacity have grown quickly in recent years.

2a1236ab3c6c.title: Biochar
2a1236ab3c6c.sentence: However a 2018 study doubted enough biomass would be available to achieve significant carbon sequestration.

22ecda0bbfe4.title: Biochar
22ecda0bbfe4.sentence: The rapid expansion of publications on biochar has led to concerns in the literature that expectations for its climate role could trigger a 'boom and bust' cycle if projected benefits are not realized at scale.

72f28fa3d01e.title: Biochar
72f28fa3d01e.sentence: Early works proposing the use of biochar for carbon dioxide removal to create a long-term stable carbon sink were published in the early 2000s.

a874859388f8.title: Compost
a874859388f8.sentence: Organisms can break down organic matter in compost if provided with the correct mixture of water, oxygen, carbon, and nitrogen.

52815d3730db.title: Compost
52815d3730db.sentence: They fall into two broad categories: chemical decomposers, which perform chemical processes on the organic waste, and physical decomposers, which process the waste into smaller pieces through methods such as grinding, tearing, chewing, and digesting.

20762a0a8f20.title: Compost
20762a0a8f20.sentence: - Bacteria are the most abundant and important of all the microorganisms found in compost.

97e1de100c87.title: Compost
97e1de100c87.sentence: Bacteria process carbon and nitrogen and excrete plant-available nutrients such as nitrogen, phosphorus, and magnesium.

a84ee27d2e73.title: Compost
a84ee27d2e73.sentence: Depending on the phase of composting, mesophilic or thermophilic bacteria may be the most prominent.

c4cd5d20d136.title: Compost
c4cd5d20d136.sentence: - Actinomycetota are needed to break down paper products such as newspaper, bark, etc., and other large molecules such as lignin and cellulose that are more difficult to decompose.

f5d0117a740b.title: Compost
f5d0117a740b.sentence: The "pleasant, earthy smell of compost" is attributed to Actinomycetota.

976ebc601ab9.title: Compost
976ebc601ab9.sentence: - Fungi such as molds and yeasts help break down materials that bacteria cannot, especially cellulose and lignin in woody material.

0cac6f8ab907.title: Compost
0cac6f8ab907.sentence: The tunnels they create as they move through the compost also increase aeration and drainage.

9b5f8e1fbe12.title: Compost
9b5f8e1fbe12.sentence: - Thermophilic bacteria do not reproduce and are not active between −5 and 25 °C (23 and 77 °F), yet are found throughout soil.

c0e242a9dc95.title: Compost
c0e242a9dc95.sentence: They activate once the mesophilic bacteria have begun to break down organic matter and increase the temperature to their optimal range.

cbe86f6bdf25.title: Compost
cbe86f6bdf25.sentence: Thermophilic bacteria thrive at higher temperatures, reaching 40–60 °C (104–140 °F) in typical mixes.

b7e58f3c4df0.title: Compost
b7e58f3c4df0.section: Uses > Agriculture and gardening > Compost tea
b7e58f3c4df0.sentence: Compost tea is made up of extracts of fermented water leached from composted materials.

9af0cbcd374a.title: Compost
9af0cbcd374a.section: Uses > Agriculture and gardening > Compost tea
9af0cbcd374a.sentence: Compost teas are generally produced from adding compost to water in a ratio of 1:4–1:10, occasionally stirring to release microbes.

26f11365aa86.title: Compost
26f11365aa86.section: Uses > Agriculture and gardening > Compost tea
26f11365aa86.sentence: Composts can be either aerated or non-aerated depending on its fermentation process.

4eb59af63e7e.title: Compost
4eb59af63e7e.section: Uses > Agriculture and gardening > Compost tea
4eb59af63e7e.sentence: Field studies have shown the benefits of adding compost teas to crops due to organic matter input, increased nutrient availability, and increased microbial activity.

f6fab2fd9661.title: Compost
f6fab2fd9661.section: Uses > Agriculture and gardening > Compost tea
f6fab2fd9661.sentence: Aerated compost tea brews faster and generates more microbes, but has potential for human pathogen regrowth, particularly when one adds additional nutrients to the mixture.

677bd27284b1.title: Compost
677bd27284b1.section: Uses > Agriculture and gardening > Compost tea
677bd27284b1.sentence: Non-aerated compost tea is cheaper and less labor-intensive, but there are conflicting studies regarding the risks of phytotoxicity and human pathogen regrowth.

761b58ca34a6.title: Compost
761b58ca34a6.section: Uses > Agriculture and gardening > Compost tea
761b58ca34a6.sentence: Adding nutrients to compost tea can be beneficial for disease suppression, although it can trigger the regrowth of human pathogens like E. coli and Salmonella.

bc49ad2e7369.title: Compost
bc49ad2e7369.section: Uses > Agriculture and gardening > Compost extract
bc49ad2e7369.sentence: Compost extracts are unfermented or non-brewed extracts of leached compost contents dissolved in any solvent.

7010372ac49b.title: Compost
7010372ac49b.sentence: Aerated compost teas are more effective than compost extracts.

bb9ded30922a.title: Compost
bb9ded30922a.section: Composting technologies > Industrial-scale composting > In-vessel composting
bb9ded30922a.sentence: In-vessel composting generally describes a group of methods that confine the composting materials within a building, container, or vessel.

bedc2b808ac3.title: Compost
bedc2b808ac3.section: Composting technologies > Industrial-scale composting > Aerated static-pile composting
bedc2b808ac3.sentence: Aerated static pile (ASP) composting refers to systems using forced aeration to keep compost material aerobic without physical manipulation.

0228be002587.title: Compost
0228be002587.section: Composting technologies > Industrial-scale composting > Windrow composting
0228be002587.sentence: In agriculture, windrow composting is the production of compost by piling organic matter or biodegradable waste, such as animal manure and crop residues, in long rows – windrow.

e1824a1fc24b.title: Compost
e1824a1fc24b.section: Composting technologies > Industrial-scale composting > In-vessel composting
e1824a1fc24b.sentence: In-vessel composting systems can consist of metal or plastic tanks or concrete bunkers in which air flow and temperature can be controlled, using the principles of a "bioreactor".

2b3a0dcabad9.title: Compost
2b3a0dcabad9.section: Composting technologies > Industrial-scale composting > In-vessel composting
2b3a0dcabad9.sentence: In-vessel composting is generally used for putrescible municipal scale organic waste processing, including final treatment of sewage biosolids, food waste, or the organic fraction of municipal solid waste.

aa65d52aa510.title: Compost
aa65d52aa510.section: Composting technologies > Industrial-scale composting > In-vessel composting
aa65d52aa510.sentence: In-vessel composting allows for sanitization of pathogens so the waste can be reclaimed as a soil amendment, while minimizing the environmental impact in the form of odors, runoff or emissions.

4b1cc829d39f.title: Compost
4b1cc829d39f.section: Composting technologies > Industrial-scale composting > Aerated static-pile composting
4b1cc829d39f.sentence: This is typically done by placing mixed feedstocks on perforated piping where air is then either pumped up (positive aeration), sucked down (negative aeration), or pumped and sucked (reversing aeration) through the material.

1da9b49a284d.title: Compost
1da9b49a284d.section: Composting technologies > Industrial-scale composting > Aerated static-pile composting
1da9b49a284d.sentence: Many ASPs are protected from rain and precipitation with a roof, reducing leachate generation and allowing operators to evaporate detained water through biodrying.

f5b9ed82e15a.title: Compost
f5b9ed82e15a.sentence: Large-scale composting operations, such as windrow composting, may exceed this temperature, potentially killing beneficial soil microorganisms but also pasteurizing the waste.

8c73411e9111.title: Compost
8c73411e9111.sentence: Under ideal conditions, composting proceeds through three major phases:

1d6aafea9c8b.title: Compost
1d6aafea9c8b.sentence: - Mesophilic phase: The initial, mesophilic phase is when the decomposition is carried out under moderate temperatures by mesophilic microorganisms.

3a32c5f96ec5.title: Compost
3a32c5f96ec5.sentence: - Thermophilic phase: As the temperature rises, a second, thermophilic phase starts, in which various thermophilic bacteria carry out the decomposition under higher temperatures (50 to 60 °C (122 to 140 °F)).

21eaedb60a44.title: Compost
21eaedb60a44.sentence: - Maturation phase: As the supply of high-energy compounds dwindles, the temperature starts to decrease.

90e7e5381422.title: Compost
90e7e5381422.sentence: Afterwards they cure it, which makes the fresh compost more bioavailable for plants.

3d44023bdc57.title: Compost
3d44023bdc57.sentence: Semicomposting is the degradation process that handles volumes of organic waste lower than that recommended for composting and therefore does not present a thermophilic stage, because mesophilic microorganisms are the only responsible ones, for the degradation of organic matter.

6bfb058c08a0.title: Compost
6bfb058c08a0.section: Fundamentals > Hot and cold composting – impact on timing
6bfb058c08a0.sentence: The time required to compost material relates to the volume of material, the particle size of the inputs (e.g. wood chips break down faster than branches), and the amount of mixing and aeration.

81b93446e37f.title: Compost
81b93446e37f.section: Fundamentals > Hot and cold composting – impact on timing
81b93446e37f.sentence: This is hot composting and is the usual method for large-scale municipal facilities and agricultural operations.

8c3bcdcc2c7f.title: Compost
8c3bcdcc2c7f.section: Fundamentals > Hot and cold composting – impact on timing
8c3bcdcc2c7f.sentence: Cold composting is a slower process that can take up to a year to complete.

404087ca0f81.title: Compost
404087ca0f81.section: Fundamentals > Hot and cold composting – impact on timing
404087ca0f81.sentence: Generally, larger piles reach higher temperatures and remain in a thermophilic stage for days or weeks.

0de8f24773a5.title: Compost
0de8f24773a5.section: Fundamentals > Hot and cold composting – impact on timing
0de8f24773a5.sentence: The Berkeley method produces finished compost in 18 days.

fa27aa23ec05.title: Compost
fa27aa23ec05.section: Fundamentals > Hot and cold composting – impact on timing
fa27aa23ec05.sentence: It requires assembly of at least 1 cubic metre (35 cu ft) of material at the outset and needs turning every two days after an initial four-day phase.

064406498859.title: Compost
064406498859.section: Fundamentals > Hot and cold composting – impact on timing
064406498859.sentence: Such short processes involve some changes to traditional methods, including smaller, more homogenized particle sizes in the input materials, controlling carbon-to-nitrogen ratio (C:N) at 30:1 or less, and careful monitoring of the moisture level.

b8f077cf2bc8.title: Compost
b8f077cf2bc8.section: Fundamentals > Hot and cold composting – impact on timing
b8f077cf2bc8.sentence: Piles smaller than 1 cubic metre (35 cu ft) tend not to reach and maintain high temperatures.

0c49df34d3bb.title: Compost
0c49df34d3bb.section: Fundamentals > Hot and cold composting – impact on timing
0c49df34d3bb.sentence: Turning is not necessary with cold composting, although a risk exists that parts of the pile may go anaerobic as it becomes compacted or waterlogged.

157f13d9f49f.title: Compost
157f13d9f49f.sentence: Composting can destroy some pathogens and seeds, by reaching certain temperatures.

86c0a97daf84.title: Compost
86c0a97daf84.sentence: Dealing with stabilized compost – i.e. composted material in which microorganisms have finished digesting the organic matter and the temperature has reached between 50 and 70 °C (122 and 158 °F) – poses very little risk, as these temperatures kill pathogens and even make oocysts unviable.

3ba1eb3d58d0.title: Compost
3ba1eb3d58d0.sentence: The temperature at which a pathogen dies depends on the pathogen, how long the temperature is maintained (seconds to weeks), and pH.

87618b849e27.title: Compost
87618b849e27.sentence: Compost products such as compost tea and compost extracts have been found to have an inhibitory effect on Fusarium oxysporum, Rhizoctonia species, and Pythium debaryanum, plant pathogens that can cause crop diseases.

24be4050967a.title: Compost
24be4050967a.sentence: Compost is a good source of biocontrol agents like B. subtilis, B. licheniformis, and P. chrysogenum that fight plant pathogens.

d5793358b557.title: Compost
d5793358b557.sentence: Sterilizing the compost, compost tea, or compost extracts reduces the effect of pathogen suppression.

d7aa46a114cc.title: Compost

049670a4ca22.sentence: However, if urea is applied to the soil surface, a meaningful fraction of applied fertilizer nitrogen may be lost to the atmosphere as ammonia gas; this only occurs under certain conditions.

04b19b670e10.title: Ammonia volatilization from urea
04b19b670e10.sentence: Rapid decomposition of carbamic acid occurs without enzyme catalysis to form ammonia and carbon dioxide.

7cc14f4900ac.title: Ammonia volatilization from urea
7cc14f4900ac.sentence: The ammonia will likely escape to the atmosphere unless it reacts with water to form ammonium (NH4+) according to the following reaction:

96451c911a25.title: Ammonia volatilization from urea
96451c911a25.sentence: This is important because ammonium is a plant available source of nitrogen while ammonia is not.

6bfc0945db3f.title: Ammonia volatilization from urea
6bfc0945db3f.sentence: Additionally, the formation of the hydroxide ion may cause soils around the applied urea particle to have a pH around 9.0 which increases ammonia volatilization.

c9625f52a601.title: Ammonia volatilization from urea
c9625f52a601.sentence: This area is also highly toxic due to elevated ammonia concentration for several hours so it is recommended that urea based fertilizers not be applied or banded with planted seed at a rate that exceeds 10–20 kg/ha, depending on the crop species.

3645fecba188.title: Ammonia volatilization from urea
3645fecba188.sentence: It is important that there is adequate moisture because up to thirty percent of the available nitrogen can be lost through atmospheric volatilization within seventy-two hours of application.

b88f607e728c.title: Ammonia volatilization from urea
b88f607e728c.sentence: The amount of ammonia volatilization depends on several environmental factors, including temperature, pH, and the soil water content.

316c18e98de0.title: Ammonia volatilization from urea
316c18e98de0.sentence: One study has shown complete hydrolysis of urea within two days of application on such soils.

8a2c588038bf.title: Ammonia volatilization from urea
8a2c588038bf.sentence: In acidic soils (pH 5.2) the urea took twice as long to hydrolyze.

53145ad2f380.title: Ammonia volatilization from urea
53145ad2f380.sentence: Surface residues, such as thatch and plant stubble exhibit increased urease activity.

cbf250c1fa48.title: Ammonia volatilization from urea
cbf250c1fa48.sentence: Soils that have high organic matter content also tend to have higher urease concentrations.

7f76f5b6298c.title: Ammonia volatilization from urea
7f76f5b6298c.sentence: More urease results in greater hydrolysis of urea and ammonia volatilization, particularly if urea fails to move into the soil.

61a861162e90.title: Ammonia volatilization from urea
61a861162e90.sentence: Ideally, a manager should attempt to apply nitrogen immediately before a moderate rain event (0.1 inch), allowing urea to dissolve and move into the soil.

3c8d194ca14c.title: Ammonia volatilization from urea
3c8d194ca14c.sentence: Urea (46-0-0) accounts for more than fifty percent of the world's nitrogenous fertilizers.

bd638b2d3aa1.title: Ammonia volatilization from urea
bd638b2d3aa1.sentence: Ammonia volatilization reduces the economic efficiency of agricultural cropping systems.

9286df1d62c9.title: Ammonia volatilization from urea
9286df1d62c9.sentence: Either yield will be reduced or additional costs will be incurred from additional nitrogen fertilizer.

d0af5ab321f5.title: Fertilizer burn
d0af5ab321f5.sentence: Fertilizer burns occur when the use of too much fertilizer, the wrong type of fertilizer, or too little water with a fertilizer causes damage to a plant.

5f1b9352fd52.title: Fertilizer burn
5f1b9352fd52.sentence: Although fertilizer is used to help a plant grow by providing nutrients, too much will result in excess salt, nitrogen, or ammonia which have adverse effects on a plant.

18a24726f6fa.title: Fertilizer burn
18a24726f6fa.sentence: An excess of these nutrients can damage the plant's ability to photosynthesize and cellularly respire, causing visible burns.

61417dd4c779.title: Fertilizer burn
61417dd4c779.section: Salt index and effects > Low Osmotic Pressure
61417dd4c779.sentence: Low osmotic pressure is when there is a higher concentration of salts outside the root cell membrane, so water will not move across the membrane.

c1a2f17600ea.title: Fertilizer burn
c1a2f17600ea.section: Salt index and effects > Low Osmotic Pressure
c1a2f17600ea.sentence: Water may even leave the root system in an attempt to equalize the concentration of salts in the soil.

f51a1bd78dcf.title: Fertilizer burn
f51a1bd78dcf.section: Causes and pathophysiology > Fertilizer burns due to low osmotic pressure.
f51a1bd78dcf.sentence: With water not entering the plant, the plant will respond as it does in a drought.

2c0f6100f217.title: Fertilizer burn
2c0f6100f217.sentence: The beginning signs of fertilizer burn include white salt marks and crust in the plant container and/or around the roots.

d3c55339f68a.title: Fertilizer burn
d3c55339f68a.sentence: - The leaves of the plant will turn brown and die.

0696653b6ebf.title: Fertilizer burn
0696653b6ebf.sentence: - The roots may turn brown indicating root rot.

69faceb946dc.title: Fertilizer burn
69faceb946dc.sentence: Dry, overheated, and sunburnt plants are most susceptible to fertilizer burns.

b40d892b21bf.title: Fertilizer burn
b40d892b21bf.sentence: - Water the plant heavily to wash the accumulation of salt away.

7482ce5553e0.title: Fertilizer burn
7482ce5553e0.sentence: - Remove the plant and its roots from the pot, carefully clean the roots and repot the plant.

d68f49b3a371.title: Fertilizer
d68f49b3a371.sentence: Potash is a mixture of potassium minerals used to make potassium (chemical symbol: K) fertilizers.

c5c56d5fb8c4.title: Potash
c5c56d5fb8c4.sentence: Potassium is the third major plant and crop nutrient after nitrogen and phosphorus.

58d4913c91c0.title: Potash
58d4913c91c0.sentence: It has been used since antiquity as a soil fertilizer (about 90% of current use).

7bcf619025ca.title: Fertilizer
7bcf619025ca.sentence: The main potassium-based straight fertilizer is muriate of potash (MOP, 95–99% KCl).

362c362c814e.title: Fertilizer
362c362c814e.sentence: In fact, potash fertilizers are usually potassium chloride, potassium sulfate, potassium carbonate, or potassium nitrate.

3a6372ac6a58.title: Fertilizer
3a6372ac6a58.sentence: Sometimes potash is referred to as K2O, as a matter of convenience to those describing the potassium content.

588a8e6603b4.title: Potash
588a8e6603b4.sentence: Potash fertilizer | To the early 20th century: potassium carbonate (K 2 CO 3); from the late-19th century: one or more compounds of potassium chloride (KCl), potassium sulfate (K 2 SO 4), or potassium nitrate (KNO 3). Does not contain potassium oxide (K 2 O), which plants do not take up; the amount of potassium is reported as K 2 O equivalent (i.e. if in K 2 O form), however, to allow direct comparison between different fertilizers using different types of potash.

bc4cbdd8d277.title: Potash
bc4cbdd8d277.sentence: The term potash derives from pot ash, either plant ashes or wood ashes that were soaked in water in a pot, which was the primary means of manufacturing potash before the Industrial Era.

5cc8f43a2451.title: Potash
5cc8f43a2451.sentence: The deposits are a naturally occurring mixture of potassium chloride (KCl; mineral name sylvite) and sodium chloride (NaCl; mineral name halite), more commonly known as table salt.

1900c77ab2af.title: Potash
1900c77ab2af.section: Mining > Shaft mining and strip mining
1900c77ab2af.sentence: Potash ores are typically rich in potassium chloride (KCl), sodium chloride (NaCl) and other salts and clays, and are typically obtained by conventional shaft mining with the extracted ore ground into a powder.

e6f51907b22d.title: Potash
e6f51907b22d.section: Mining > Shaft mining and strip mining
e6f51907b22d.sentence: In above-ground processing plants, the KCl is separated from the mixture to produce a high-analysis potassium fertilizer.

969106b8e4ea.title: Potash
969106b8e4ea.sentence: In 2021, the worldwide production of potash exceeded 71.9 million tonnes (~45.4 million tonnes K2O equivalent), and Canada is the largest producer of potash, the majority of which is used as fertilizer; other major producers include Russia and Belarus.

ae003b5eff74.title: Potash
ae003b5eff74.sentence: The world's largest consumers of potash are China, the United States, Brazil, and India.

c54bfc5fd0ff.title: Potash
c54bfc5fd0ff.sentence: Potash is important for agriculture because it improves water retention, yield, nutrient value, taste, color, texture and disease resistance of food crops.

b6cdd6db215e.title: Raised-bed gardening
b6cdd6db215e.sentence: Raised-bed gardening is a form of gardening in which the soil is raised above ground level and usually enclosed in some way.

13be4450f380.title: Raised-bed gardening
13be4450f380.sentence: The soil is usually enriched with compost.

e91534db2cec.title: Raised-bed gardening
e91534db2cec.sentence: Vegetables are grown in geometric patterns, much closer together than in conventional row gardening.

e46c72fbf52d.title: Raised-bed gardening
e46c72fbf52d.sentence: The spacing is such that when the vegetables are fully grown, their leaves just barely touch each other, creating a microclimate in which weed growth is suppressed and moisture is conserved.

bb0585ce67d6.title: Raised-bed gardening
bb0585ce67d6.sentence: Since the gardener does not walk on the raised beds, the soil is not compacted and the roots have an easier time growing.

ec4233d26ddc.title: Raised-bed gardening
ec4233d26ddc.sentence: Raised beds produce a variety of benefits: they extend the planting season, they can reduce weeds if designed and planted properly, and they reduce the need to use poor native soil.

8de42497593e.title: Raised-bed gardening
8de42497593e.sentence: They can be used effectively to control erosion and recycle and conserve water and nutrients by building them along contour lines on slopes.

71a4a98b5148.title: Ultisol
71a4a98b5148.sentence: By using raised beds, gardeners avoid having to deal with Ultisols altogether.

250038fc46e2.title: Hügelkultur
250038fc46e2.sentence: Hügelkultur (German pronunciation: [ˈhyːɡl̩kʊlˌtuːɐ̯], alternative spelling without umlaut: Huegelkultur), literally mound culture or hill culture, is a horticultural technique where a mound constructed from decaying wood debris and other compostable biomass plant materials is later (or immediately) planted as a raised bed.

d3a29ea389d0.title: Hügelkultur
d3a29ea389d0.sentence: Considered a permaculture practice, advocates claim that the technique helps to improve soil fertility, water retention, and soil warming, thus benefitting plants grown on or near such mounds.

d11e585a8f7c.title: Hügelkultur
d11e585a8f7c.sentence: Though the technique is alleged to have been practiced in German and Eastern European societies for hundreds of years, the term was first published in a 1962 German gardening booklet by Herrman Andrä.

c034f7a4e8b9.title: Hügelkultur
c034f7a4e8b9.sentence: Wood breaks down relatively slowly because it has one of the highest carbon to nitrogen ratios of all organic matter that is used in composting.

a49a71e5e98a.title: Hügelkultur
a49a71e5e98a.sentence: The decomposition process may, in the short term, take more nitrogen from the soil through microbial activity (nitrogen immobilization), if not enough nitrogen is available.

52566c50b530.title: Hügelkultur
52566c50b530.sentence: Thus, in the short term, the fertility of the soil may be decreased before, eventually, perhaps after one to two years, the nitrogen level is increased past the original level.

8493a87cb7cc.title: Hügelkultur
8493a87cb7cc.sentence: There are few peer-reviewed scientific studies available regarding the efficacy of the technique.

32352d902dd6.title: Hügelkultur
32352d902dd6.sentence: Samples from hügel sites contained almost twice as much water as those from flat control plots.

236ff8d0d0d2.title: Hügelkultur
236ff8d0d0d2.sentence: Some have criticised the technique as lacking genuine scientific principles, and running counter to the ecological principles of soil building with litterfall.

8ba92fd52ee8.title: Hügelkultur
8ba92fd52ee8.sentence: Hügelkultur is said to replicate the natural process of decomposition that occurs on forest floors, however in natural ecosystems wood would be present at the soil surface.

224cfa20b0a9.title: Foliar feeding
224cfa20b0a9.sentence: Foliar feeding is a technique of feeding plants by applying liquid fertilizer directly to the leaves.

282153f38c86.title: Foliar feeding
282153f38c86.sentence: Plants are able to absorb essential elements through their leaves.

fa20a080b98a.title: Foliar feeding
fa20a080b98a.sentence: The absorption takes place through their stomata and also through their epidermis.

a1b666dc7fce.title: Foliar feeding
a1b666dc7fce.sentence: H. B. Tukey was head of Michigan State University (MSU) Department of Horticulture in the 1950s.

139a41b1df61.title: Foliar feeding
139a41b1df61.sentence: Working with S. H. Wittwer, they demonstrated that foliar feeding is effective.

ba171309db83.title: Foliar feeding
ba171309db83.sentence: Radioactive phosphorus and potassium were applied to foliage.

b2a32ddf4570.title: Foliar feeding
b2a32ddf4570.sentence: The nutrients were transported at the rate of about one foot per hour to all parts of the plants.

837e0e894f22.title: Foliar feeding
837e0e894f22.sentence: Foliar application has been shown to avoid the problem of leaching-out in soils and prompts a quick reaction in the plant.

f00f33abe16e.title: Foliar feeding
f00f33abe16e.sentence: Foliar application of phosphorus, zinc, and iron brings the greatest benefit in comparison with addition to soil where phosphorus becomes fixed in a form inaccessible to the plant and where zinc and iron are less available.

fcd75887f33d.title: Foliar feeding
fcd75887f33d.sentence: Foliar feeding is generally done in the early morning or late evening, preferably at temperatures below 24 °C (75 °F), because heat causes the pores on some species' leaves to close.

2f4ef33fda2f.title: Soil conditioner
2f4ef33fda2f.sentence: Because of their ability to absorb several hundred times their own weight in water, polyacrylamides and polymethacrylates (also known as hydroabsorbent polymers, superabsorbent polymers or hydrogels) were tested in agriculture, horticulture and landscaping beginning in the 1960s.

8239442717e8.title: Soil conditioner
8239442717e8.sentence: The first synthetic soil conditioners were introduced in the 1950s, when the chemical hydrolysed polyacrylonitrile was the most used.

f1e7d54bd6df.title: Soil conditioner
f1e7d54bd6df.sentence: Interest disappeared when experiments proved them to be phytotoxic due to their high acrylamide monomer residue.

cce3b0e03c1d.title: Soil conditioner
cce3b0e03c1d.sentence: Although manufacturing advances later brought the monomer concentration down below the toxic level, scientific literature shows few successes in utilizing these polymers for increasing plant quality or survival.

4547e1529ba1.title: Soil conditioner
4547e1529ba1.sentence: The criteria by which such materials are judged most often remains their cost-effectiveness, their ability to increase soil moisture for longer periods, stimulate microbiological activity, increase nutrient levels and improve plant survival rates.

65ac6ec5bf5c.title: Soil conditioner
65ac6ec5bf5c.sentence: Polyacrylamides have been widely investigated as soil conditioners.

7b9e48c06aec.title: Soil conditioner
7b9e48c06aec.sentence: They were introduced as "linear soil conditioner" in the 1950s by Monsanto Company under the trade name Krilium.

0988404961d4.title: Soil conditioner
0988404961d4.sentence: The soil conditioning technology was presented at a symposium on "Improvement of Soil Structure" held in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania on December 29, 1951.

ce849259f159.title: Soil conditioner
ce849259f159.sentence: Water-soluble soil conditioners offer the following benefits:

6a0a57d27bef.title: Soil conditioner

47362f57999f.title: Soil conditioner
47362f57999f.sentence: - increase water infiltration into soils containing clay

82f0e74d6ecd.title: Soil conditioner
82f0e74d6ecd.sentence: - make friable soil that is easy to cultivate

36032e6cbb9b.title: Soil conditioner
36032e6cbb9b.sentence: - make soil dry quicker after rain or irrigation, so that the soil can be worked sooner

41ab37324fd7.title: Soil conditioner
41ab37324fd7.sentence: The cross-linked forms of polyacrylamide, which strongly retain water, are often used for horticultural and agricultural under trade names such as Broadleaf P4 and Swell-Gel.

7a92b63cecf4.title: Soil conditioner
7a92b63cecf4.sentence: Polyacrylamide is also used in some potting soil.

e809959f363f.title: Soil conditioner
e809959f363f.sentence: In addition to use on farm lands, these polymers are used at construction sites for erosion control, in order to protect the water quality of nearby rivers and streams.

691e2ce4dec8.title: Fertilizer
691e2ce4dec8.sentence: Organic fertilizers can describe those fertilizers with a biological origin, i.e. derived from living or formerly living materials.

724abb1ace19.title: Fertilizer
724abb1ace19.sentence: Fertilizers of an organic origin (the first definition) include animal wastes, plant wastes from agriculture, seaweed, compost, and treated sewage sludge (biosolids).

6d000a35fd53.title: Fertilizer
6d000a35fd53.sentence: Beyond manures, animal sources can include products from animal slaughters: bloodmeal, bone meal, feather meal, hides, hoofs, and horns all are typical components.

e9e1581b2c20.title: Fertilizer
e9e1581b2c20.sentence: Organic fertilizers can also describe commercially available and frequently packaged products that strive to follow the expectations and restrictions adopted by organic farming and environmentally friendly gardening, i.e. related systems of food and plant production that significantly limit or strictly avoid the use of synthetic fertilizers and pesticides.

db3b8dca16e4.title: Fertilizer
db3b8dca16e4.sentence: Organically derived materials available to industry such as sewage sludge may not be acceptable components of organic farming and gardening, because of factors ranging from residual contaminants to public perception.

592b40f28efc.title: Fertilizer
592b40f28efc.sentence: No matter the definition nor composition, most of these products contain less-concentrated nutrients, and the nutrients are not as easily quantified.

30dd89af0b69.title: Fertilizer
30dd89af0b69.sentence: They can offer soil-building advantages as well as be appealing to those who are trying to farm or garden more naturally.

883fa04e3a91.title: Fertilizer
883fa04e3a91.sentence: These same organic soil texturizers (as well as compost, etc.) may increase the availability of nutrients through improved cation-exchange capacity, or through increased growth of microorganisms that in turn increase availability of certain plant nutrients.

fc22298def82.title: Fertilizer
fc22298def82.sentence: In terms of volume, peat is the most widely used packaged organic soil amendment.

bafca7eddfba.title: Fertilizer
bafca7eddfba.sentence: It is an immature form of coal which improves soil aeration and moisture and thus soil biological activity but confers no direct nutritional value to the plants.

564d2c879c9b.title: Fertilizer
564d2c879c9b.sentence: It is therefore not a fertilizer as defined in the beginning of the article, but rather an amendment.

45bbfeb52a7d.title: Fertilizer
45bbfeb52a7d.sentence: Fresh sawdust can consume soil nutrients as it breaks down and is colonized by wood-decay fungi, causing nitrogen deficiency (nitrogen drawdown) in the absence of nutrient addition.

005321f394b9.title: Fertilizer
005321f394b9.sentence: However, this property can be used to capture excess mineral nitrogen.

2ade13a6b35f.title: Organic fertilizer
2ade13a6b35f.sentence: Organic fertilizer nutrient content, solubility, and nutrient release rates are typically much lower than mineral (inorganic) fertilizers.

03eae390822b.title: Organic fertilizer
03eae390822b.sentence: This may be however desired as a form of slow-release fertilizer containing insoluble nitrogen.

3a2a1474689c.title: Organic fertilizer
3a2a1474689c.sentence: By their nature, organic fertilizers increase physical and biological nutrient storage mechanisms in soils, mitigating risks of over-fertilization.

e3ce4c705d21.title: Manure
e3ce4c705d21.sentence: Manure is organic matter that is used as organic fertilizer in agriculture.

5c64a474aec0.title: Manure
5c64a474aec0.sentence: Most manure consists of animal feces; other sources include compost and green manure.

478c79a5bcd6.title: Manure
478c79a5bcd6.sentence: There are in the 21st century three main classes of manures used in soil management, as laid out below.

19bb7611bb0e.title: Manure
19bb7611bb0e.sentence: Manures contribute to the fertility of soil by adding organic matter and nutrients, such as nitrogen, that are utilised by bacteria, fungi, and other organisms in the soil.

9a09672da0cd.title: Manure
9a09672da0cd.sentence: Higher organisms then feed on the fungi and bacteria in a chain of life that comprises the soil food web.

ac2527fe241f.title: Fertilizer
ac2527fe241f.sentence: Egyptians, Romans, Babylonians, and early Germans are all recorded as using minerals or manure to enhance the productivity of their farms.

91a0033833b9.title: Manure
91a0033833b9.sentence: The term artificial manure, formerly in wide use, referred to artificial fertilizers; the latter term is the one usually used today for such manures.

9fecf3a1dda0.title: Manure
9fecf3a1dda0.sentence: Manure is also commercially composted and bagged and sold as a soil amendment.

46541d3cac32.title: Green manure
46541d3cac32.sentence: In agriculture, a green manure is a crop specifically cultivated to be incorporated into the soil while still green.

0eaa47983796.title: Green manure
0eaa47983796.sentence: Typically, the green manure's biomass is incorporated with a plow or disk, as is often done with (brown) manure.

e4a97c6e05b1.title: Green manure
e4a97c6e05b1.sentence: The primary goal is to add organic matter to the soil for its benefits.

2d188fbc3734.title: Green manure
2d188fbc3734.sentence: Green manuring is often used with legume crops to add nitrogen to the soil for following crops, especially in organic farming, but is also used in conventional farming.

731a54b6ad76.title: Green manure
731a54b6ad76.sentence: Legumes such as clover and vetch have bacteria in their roots that turn nitrogen from the air into a form plants can use, which acts as a natural fertilizer for the next crop.

6525a1ea9804.title: Green manure
6525a1ea9804.sentence: Leguminous green manures such as clover and vetch contain nitrogen-fixing symbiotic bacteria in root nodules that fix atmospheric nitrogen in a form that plants can use.

e3ed25b9c7f5.title: Green manure
e3ed25b9c7f5.sentence: Depending on the species of cover crop grown, the amount of nitrogen released into the soil lies between 45 and 224 kg/ha (40 and 200 lb/acre).

cfc5b0c7b5e4.title: Green manure
cfc5b0c7b5e4.sentence: With green manure use, the amount of nitrogen that is available to the succeeding crop is usually in the range of 40-60% of the total amount of nitrogen that is contained within the green manure crop.

ec6674d48c02.title: Green manure
ec6674d48c02.sentence: As the plant material breaks down, it also releases other nutrients, such as phosphorus, potassium and sulfur.

1138f80fedb8.title: Green manure
1138f80fedb8.sentence: Some deep-rooted species bring up nutrients that shallower-rooted crops cannot reach.

b45333e1ba40.title: Green manure
b45333e1ba40.sentence: Microbial activity from incorporation of cover crops into the soil leads to the formation of mycelium and viscous materials which benefit the health of the soil by increasing its soil structure (i.e. by aggregation).

5ae2555c7fa8.title: Green manure
5ae2555c7fa8.sentence: The increased percentage of organic matter (biomass) improves water infiltration and retention, aeration, and other soil characteristics.

e0186a973367.title: Green manure
e0186a973367.sentence: Further aeration of the soil results from the ability of the root systems of many green manure crops to efficiently penetrate compact soils.

927acfcef795.title: Green manure
927acfcef795.sentence: While growing, the crop also protects the ground: it suppresses weeds, helps control erosion, provides food for pollinators and habitat for beneficial insects, and can reduce some pests and diseases.

211daa3fac78.title: Green manure
211daa3fac78.sentence: Greek farmers were plowing beans into the soil by about 300 BC, and the Romans did the same with faba beans and lupines.

186c92a4ed79.title: Green manure
186c92a4ed79.sentence: European colonists brought the practice to North America, where rye, buckwheat and oats were common green manure crops.

fcc53efe8f59.title: Manure
fcc53efe8f59.sentence: Common forms of animal manure include farmyard manure (or farm slurry (liquid manure).

e95b4f1a16be.title: Manure
e95b4f1a16be.sentence: Farmyard manure also contains plant material (often straw), which has been used as bedding for animals and has absorbed the feces and urine.

4ac3c8a1e9fc.title: Manure
4ac3c8a1e9fc.sentence: Agricultural manure in liquid form, known as slurry, is produced by more intensive livestock rearing systems where concrete or slats are used instead of straw bedding.

b9f84beb8d18.title: Manure
b9f84beb8d18.sentence: Manure from different animals such as horses, cattle, pigs, sheep, chickens, turkeys, rabbits, as well as guano from seabirds and bats, all have different properties and qualities and require different application rates when used as fertilizer.

c42d91d6c126.title: Manure
c42d91d6c126.sentence: For instance, sheep manure is high in nitrogen and potash, while pig manure is relatively low in both.

d45dcb8400f7.title: Manure
d45dcb8400f7.sentence: Cattle manure is a good source of nitrogen as well as organic carbon.

e78701d2d3dc.title: Manure
e78701d2d3dc.sentence: Chicken litter, coming from a bird, is very concentrated in nitrogen and phosphate and is prized for both properties.

2ba553607c80.title: Manure
2ba553607c80.sentence: It can improve the soil structure (aggregation) so that the soil holds more nutrients and water, and therefore becomes more fertile.

8f34b64b47c5.title: Manure
8f34b64b47c5.sentence: Animal manure also encourages soil microbial activity which promotes the soil's trace mineral supply, improving plant nutrition.

2f1d2cc99663.title: Manure
2f1d2cc99663.sentence: Poultry droppings are harmful to plants when fresh, but after a period of composting are valuable fertilizers.

65b30002ef8b.title: Manure
65b30002ef8b.sentence: Horses mainly eat grass and a few weeds, so horse manure can contain grass and weed seeds, because horses do not digest seeds as cattle do.

47bc79b27298.title: Manure
47bc79b27298.sentence: Animal manures with a particularly unpleasant odor (such as slurries from intensive pig farming) are usually knifed (injected) directly into the soil to reduce release of the odor.

5496014b5c5e.title: Manure
5496014b5c5e.sentence: Manure from pigs and cattle is usually spread on fields using a manure spreader.

4c3be70defd0.title: Bone meal
4c3be70defd0.sentence: Bone meal (or bonemeal) is a mixture of finely and coarsely ground animal bones and slaughter-house waste products.

d7342bf32924.title: Bone meal
d7342bf32924.sentence: It is used as a dietary supplement to supply calcium and phosphorus to monogastric livestock in the form of hydroxyapatite, or as a slow-release organic fertilizer to supply phosphorus, calcium, and a small amount of nitrogen to plants.

33006f7d0c1a.title: Bone meal
33006f7d0c1a.sentence: Bone meal provides phosphorus and calcium to plants, along with a largely inconsequential amount of nitrogen.

370651da8909.title: Bone meal
370651da8909.sentence: The N-P-K rating of bone meal is typically 3–15–0 along with a calcium content of around 12% (18% CaO equiv.), although it can vary quite a bit depending on the source from 1–13–0 to 3–22–0.

e26787d908f3.title: Bone meal
e26787d908f3.sentence: As bone meal is water-insoluble, it needs to be broken down before the plant can absorb it, either by soil acidity or by microbial activity producing acids.

fee4ab118c5f.title: Bone meal
fee4ab118c5f.sentence: According to the Colorado State University, it can only be broken down in acidic soil (pH < 7.0) and releases its nutrients over a span of 1 to 4 months.

dacec3097527.title: Bone meal
dacec3097527.sentence: The process was first suggested by Justus von Liebig (dissolving animal bones in sulphuric acid) around 1840 and first used in Britain by James Robertson in Ellon, Aberdeenshire in 1841.

ed86e0119cb9.title: Bone meal
ed86e0119cb9.sentence: Before Liebig, the expansion of agriculture had depleted the soil of essential nutrients.

b90697b50b27.title: Bone meal
b90697b50b27.sentence: In desperation, farmers collected the bones from major battlefields like the Battle of Waterloo and the Battle of Austerlitz to crush them and refertilize the soil.

5cc53618b024.title: Seaweed fertiliser
5cc53618b024.sentence: Seaweed fertiliser is organic fertilizer made from seaweed that is used in agriculture to increase soil fertility and plant growth.

da317009596d.title: Seaweed fertiliser
da317009596d.sentence: Brown seaweeds are most commonly used for fertilizer production, at present and historically.

f8c6444a7711.title: Seaweed fertiliser
f8c6444a7711.sentence: Seaweed fertilizer can be used as a crude addition to soil as mulch, composted to break down the hardy raw material, or dried and pulverized to make the nutrients more bioavailable to plant roots.

dcd75ed9ecc8.title: Seaweed fertiliser
dcd75ed9ecc8.sentence: Seaweed fertilizer can be applied in a number of different forms, including refined liquid extracts and dried, pulverized organic material.

653118161529.title: Seaweed fertiliser
653118161529.section: Functions and benefits of seaweed fertilizer > Fertilization
653118161529.sentence: Because seaweed is rich in micro and macronutrients, humic acids, and phytohormones, it enhances soil fertility.

40a0a08059e3.title: Seaweed fertiliser
40a0a08059e3.section: Functions and benefits of seaweed fertilizer > Fertilization
40a0a08059e3.sentence: The application of seaweed fertilizers can also result in enhanced tolerance to abiotic stressors that generally inhibit crop growth and yield such as low moisture, high salinity, and freezing temperatures.

c9016402ea39.title: Seaweed fertiliser
c9016402ea39.section: Functions and benefits of seaweed fertilizer > Soil conditioning
c9016402ea39.sentence: As a soil conditioner, seaweed fertilizer can improve the physical qualities of soil, such as aeration and water retention.

95f4a166d16d.title: Seaweed fertiliser
95f4a166d16d.section: Functions and benefits of seaweed fertilizer > Soil conditioning
95f4a166d16d.sentence: Clay soils that lack organic matter and porosity benefit from the humic acid and soluble alginates found in seaweed.

810e93fcbb76.title: Seaweed fertiliser
810e93fcbb76.section: Functions and benefits of seaweed fertilizer > Soil conditioning
810e93fcbb76.sentence: These compounds bond with metallic radicals which cause the clay particles to aggregate, thereby improving the texture, aeration, and retention of the soil by stimulating clay disaggregation.

bdb9e47c7569.title: Seaweed fertiliser
bdb9e47c7569.section: Functions and benefits of seaweed fertilizer > Bio-remediation of polluted soils
bdb9e47c7569.sentence: Heavy metals accumulated by seaweed fertilizer may transfer to crops in some cases, causing significant implications for the public health.

b7bf8930cde9.title: Seaweed fertiliser
b7bf8930cde9.sentence: There are however ongoing challenges associated with the use and production of seaweed fertilizer including the spread of diseases and invasive species, the risk of heavy-metal accumulation, and the efficiency and refinement of production methods.

5e2c4d6cb2ca.title: Guano
5e2c4d6cb2ca.sentence: Guano (Spanish from Quechua: wanu) is the accumulated excrement of seabirds or bats.

615321e300c7.title: Guano
615321e300c7.sentence: Guano is a highly effective fertiliser due to the high content of nitrogen, phosphate, and potassium, all key nutrients essential for plant growth.

470c096b8d46.title: Guano
470c096b8d46.sentence: Seabird guano is the fecal excrement from marine birds and has an organic matter content greater than 40%, and is a source of nitrogen (N) and available phosphate (P2O5).

534637d9fead.title: Guano
534637d9fead.sentence: Bat guano is partially decomposed bat excrement and has an organic matter content greater than 40%; it is a source of nitrogen, and may contain up to 6% available phosphate (P2O5).

b5cadabfef2a.title: Guano
b5cadabfef2a.section: History of human use > Bird guano > Indigenous use
b5cadabfef2a.sentence: The word "guano" originates from the Andean language Quechua, in which it refers to any form of dung used as an agricultural fertiliser.

bdc793abbda8.title: Guano
bdc793abbda8.section: History of human use > Bird guano > Indigenous use
bdc793abbda8.sentence: Archaeological evidence suggests that Andean people collected seabird guano from small islands and points off the desert coast of Peru for use as a soil amendment and perhaps as long as 5,000 years.

e8c56050083a.title: Guano
e8c56050083a.section: History of human use > Bird guano > The Guano Age (1802–1884)
e8c56050083a.sentence: In November 1802, Prussian geographer and explorer Alexander von Humboldt first encountered guano and began investigating its fertilising properties at Callao in Peru, and his subsequent writings on this topic made the subject well known in Europe.

a266da55fa27.title: Guano
a266da55fa27.section: History of human use > Bird guano > The Guano Age (1802–1884)
a266da55fa27.sentence: Cornish chemist Humphry Davy delivered a series of lectures which he compiled into an 1813 bestselling book about the role of nitrogenous manure as a fertiliser, Elements of Agricultural Chemistry.

b8c8738d4b52.title: Guano
b8c8738d4b52.section: History of human use > Bird guano > The Guano Age (1802–1884)
b8c8738d4b52.sentence: It highlighted the special efficacy of Peruvian guano, noting that it made the "sterile plains" of Peru fruitful.

491eec1d9b50.title: Guano
491eec1d9b50.section: History of human use > Bird guano > Western discovery (1548–1800)
491eec1d9b50.sentence: Although the first shipments of guano reached Spain as early as 1700, it did not become a popular product in Europe until the 19th century.

a72dae666e9f.title: Guano
a72dae666e9f.sentence: The 19th-century seabird guano trade played a pivotal role in the development of modern input-intensive farming.

64e26f6cf36f.title: Guano
64e26f6cf36f.section: History of human use > Bird guano > The Guano Age (1802–1884)
64e26f6cf36f.sentence: Though Europe had marine seabird colonies and thus, guano, it was of poorer quality because its potency was leached by high levels of rainfall and humidity.

d2220b59eaf1.title: Guano
d2220b59eaf1.sentence: Demand for guano rapidly declined after 1910 with the development of the Haber–Bosch process for extracting nitrogen from the atmosphere.

6d59144235f0.title: Guano
6d59144235f0.section: History of human use > Bird guano > Decline and resurgence
6d59144235f0.sentence: With the rising popularity of organic food in the twenty-first century, the demand for guano has started to rise again.

589ded94c17d.title: Guano
589ded94c17d.sentence: Unsustainable seabird guano mining processes have resulted in permanent habitat destruction and the loss of millions of seabirds.

c54597533182.title: Guano
c54597533182.sentence: Unsustainable harvesting of bat guano may cause bats to abandon their roost.

b2c9133407f4.title: Manure
b2c9133407f4.sentence: Any quantity of animal manure may be a source of pathogens or food spoilage organisms which may be carried by flies, rodents, or a range of other vector organisms and cause disease or put food safety at risk.

df166c61bc41.title: Manure
df166c61bc41.section: Uses > Animal manure > Issues > Livestock antibiotics
df166c61bc41.sentence: In 2007, a University of Minnesota study indicated that foods such as corn, lettuce, and potatoes have been found to accumulate antibiotics from soils spread with animal manure that contains these drugs.

5f9c0d5c6efb.title: Manure
5f9c0d5c6efb.sentence: In intensive agricultural land use, animal manure is often not used as targeted as mineral fertilizers, and thus, the nitrogen utilization efficiency is poor.

b69d544ff7db.title: Manure
b69d544ff7db.sentence: Manure can emit the greenhouse gas nitrous oxide, contributing to climate change.

1f15d46dad0c.title: Manure
1f15d46dad0c.section: Uses > Animal manure > Issues > Livestock antibiotics
1f15d46dad0c.sentence: For instance, by Soil Association Standard 4.7.38, most organic arable farmers either have their own supply of manure (which would, therefore, not normally contain drug residues) or else rely on green manure crops for the extra fertility (if any nonorganic manure is used by organic farmers, then it usually has to be rotted or composted to degrade any residues of drugs and eliminate any pathogenic bacteria—Standard 4.7.38, Soil Association organic farming standards).

04441b561a3a.title: Manure management
04441b561a3a.sentence: Manure management refers to capture, storage, treatment, and utilization of animal manures in an environmentally sustainable manner.

5689a5bd6871.title: Manure management
5689a5bd6871.sentence: Animal manure (also referred to as animal waste) can occur in a liquid, slurry, or solid form.

179ea83fe593.title: Manure management
179ea83fe593.sentence: Manure includes not just livestock feces, but also livestock bedding, urine and other body sections.

a7c05cd14ae6.title: Manure management
a7c05cd14ae6.sentence: Manure management is a component of nutrient management.

6fe25cfab55c.title: Manure management
6fe25cfab55c.sentence: It should be utilized by distribution on fields in amounts that enrich soils without causing water pollution or unacceptably high levels of nutrient enrichment.

ee53d98086a5.title: Manure management
ee53d98086a5.section: Risks posed by gases in livestock manure
ee53d98086a5.sentence: Livestock manure produces several gases including four main toxic gases, hydrogen sulfide, methane, ammonia and carbon dioxide.

2e22889511ff.title: Manure management
2e22889511ff.section: Risks posed by gases in livestock manure
2e22889511ff.sentence: The highest concentrations of these gases are noted during manure agitation, stirring the manure to homogenize the manure for pumping out of the storage.

1ca4e1be0acd.title: Manure management
1ca4e1be0acd.sentence: In confined spaces the gasses from manure can lethally asphyxiate humans.

6228953c4db9.title: Manure management
6228953c4db9.sentence: The typical odor threshold for H2S is 0.01 to 1.5 ppm with the loss of smell occurring at levels around 100 to 150 ppm.

c8f1fc4b2772.title: Manure management
c8f1fc4b2772.sentence: Concentrations of 500 to 700 ppm can result in death within 30 to 60 minutes, 700 to 1000 ppm result in death within minutes, while death is nearly instantaneous at levels of 1000 to 2000 ppm.

b57bf687db09.title: Manure management
b57bf687db09.section: Risks of Livestock Manure Mismanagement > Air Contamination
b57bf687db09.sentence: In fact, approximately 33% of global emissions of ammonia could have been attributed to manure in 2018.

e0229c756239.title: Manure management
e0229c756239.section: Risks of Livestock Manure Mismanagement > Soil & Crop Contamination
e0229c756239.sentence: Manure over-application and the air pollution that leads to acid rain can cause soil acidification.

ad4ef65068a5.title: Manure management
ad4ef65068a5.section: Risks of Livestock Manure Mismanagement > Soil & Crop Contamination
ad4ef65068a5.sentence: Over-application of manure can also lead to heavy-metal buildup in the soil.

b313ad14d613.title: Manure management
b313ad14d613.section: Risks of Livestock Manure Mismanagement > Soil & Crop Contamination
b313ad14d613.sentence: This, in combination with soil acidification, can result in reduced soil fertility, which harms agricultural productivity.

25e664f66bc8.title: Manure management
25e664f66bc8.section: Risks of Livestock Manure Mismanagement > Water Contamination
25e664f66bc8.sentence: Poor management can lead to agricultural runoff carrying nutrients, pathogens, antibiotics, hormones, heavy metals, and pesticides from manure-fertilized fields and waste dumping/storage sites into nearby water bodies, or to these contaminants leaching into groundwater.

cbf8b6df3614.title: Manure management
cbf8b6df3614.section: Risks of Livestock Manure Mismanagement > Water Contamination
cbf8b6df3614.sentence: Nutrient pollution (e.g., ammonia, nitrogen, phosphorus) causes eutrophication of surface water and can lead to the proliferation of toxic algae and oxygen-depleted zones where aquatic life cannot thrive.

a3e2c7d95794.title: Manure management
a3e2c7d95794.section: Livestock Manure Management Practices to Mitigate Risks > Anaerobic Digestion
a3e2c7d95794.sentence: Anaerobic digestion is a process that involves decomposing manure into biogas (a carbon-neutral renewable energy source) and digestate (a nutrient-rich by-product that can be used as fertilizer) in the absence of oxygen.

621bd5d77012.title: Manure management
621bd5d77012.section: Livestock Manure Management Practices to Mitigate Risks > Composting
621bd5d77012.sentence: Composting is a manure management practice that involves decomposing manure into a “nutrient-rich soil conditioner” in the presence of oxygen.

9ca42e8e5d24.title: Manure management
9ca42e8e5d24.section: Livestock Manure Management Practices to Mitigate Risks > Manure Separation & Treatment
9ca42e8e5d24.sentence: Manure separation and treatment involves multi-step processes that separate livestock manure into solid and liquid components that are stored and utilized separately.

82ca47885d69.title: Manure management
82ca47885d69.section: Livestock Manure Management Practices to Mitigate Risks > Buffer Zone Planting
82ca47885d69.sentence: Buffer zones are vegetation strips planted to separate manure storage/treatment sites from livestock areas or water bodies.

eafccbeb12d1.title: Mulch
eafccbeb12d1.sentence: Groundcovers are plants which grow close to the ground, under the main crop, to slow the development of weeds and provide other benefits of mulch.

bb620867b7bf.title: Mulch
bb620867b7bf.sentence: They are usually fast-growing plants that continue growing with the main crops.

859616a4f053.title: Mulch
859616a4f053.sentence: By contrast, cover crops are incorporated into the soil or killed with herbicides.

a2419ee714f9.title: Mulch
a2419ee714f9.sentence: However, live mulches also may need to be mechanically or chemically killed eventually to prevent competition with the main crop.

5b1fa36524e3.title: Mulch
5b1fa36524e3.sentence: Some groundcovers can perform additional roles in the garden such as nitrogen fixation in the case of clovers, dynamic accumulation of nutrients from the subsoil in the case of creeping comfrey (Symphytum ibericum), and even food production in the case of Rubus tricolor.

0b2011bed905.title: Mulch
0b2011bed905.sentence: Organic mulches decay over time and are temporary.

3822d4df1ec7.title: Mulch
3822d4df1ec7.sentence: - Organic residues: grass clippings, leaves, hay, straw, kitchen scraps, comfrey, shredded bark, whole bark nuggets, sawdust, shells, woodchips, shredded newspaper, cardboard, wool, animal manure, etc. Many of these materials also act as a direct composting system, such as the mulched clippings of a mulching lawn mower, or other organics applied as sheet composting.

c8200dfbc43b.title: Mulch
c8200dfbc43b.sentence: Some mulches such as straw, peat, sawdust and other wood products may for a while negatively affect plant growth because of their wide carbon to nitrogen ratio, because bacteria and fungi that decompose the materials remove nitrogen from the surrounding soil for growth.

efb02bc65d20.title: Mulch
efb02bc65d20.sentence: Organic mulches can mat down, forming a barrier that blocks water and air flow between the soil and the atmosphere.

cbcb82432bef.title: Mulch
cbcb82432bef.sentence: Vertically applied organic mulches can wick water from the soil to the surface, which can dry out the soil.

8912caecb6d3.title: Mulch
8912caecb6d3.sentence: - Compost: fully composted materials (humus) are used to avoid possible phytotoxicity problems.

4e7352d29b74.title: Mulch
4e7352d29b74.sentence: Materials that are free of seeds are ideally used, to prevent weeds being introduced by the mulch.

82d35ebd87b4.title: Mulch
82d35ebd87b4.sentence: When wetted and dried, it can form a dense crust that does not allow water to soak in.

d8990ac47758.title: Mulch
d8990ac47758.sentence: It can also lower the pH of the soil surface, making it useful as a mulch under acid loving plants.

584dfbf7251d.title: Mulch
584dfbf7251d.sentence: - Plastic mulch: crops grow through slits or holes in thin plastic sheeting.

44d091c5162b.title: Mulch
44d091c5162b.sentence: This method is predominant in large-scale vegetable growing, with millions of acres cultivated under plastic mulch worldwide each year.

e6e556677746.title: Mulch
e6e556677746.sentence: Drip irrigation is often required, with drip tape laid under the plastic, as plastic mulch is impermeable to water.

d53f516d7856.title: Mulch
d53f516d7856.section: Materials > Synthetic > Polypropylene and polyethylene mulch
d53f516d7856.sentence: The black and clear mulches capture sunlight and warm the soil increasing the growth rate.

a920682fc1de.title: Mulch
a920682fc1de.section: Materials > Synthetic > Polypropylene and polyethylene mulch
a920682fc1de.sentence: This mulch needs to be manually removed at the end of the season since when it starts to break down it breaks down into smaller pieces.

cb975b579768.title: Mulch
cb975b579768.section: Materials > Synthetic > Polypropylene and polyethylene mulch
cb975b579768.sentence: If the mulch is not removed before it starts to break down eventually it will break down into ketones and aldehydes polluting the soil.

554c10d24fb7.title: Mulch
554c10d24fb7.sentence: Biodegradable mulches are made out of plant starches and sugars or polyester fibers.

1af09d0423de.title: Mulch
1af09d0423de.sentence: Microorganisms in the soil break down the mulch into two components, water and carbon dioxide, leaving no toxic residues behind.

ee8efefb1cb0.title: Mulch
ee8efefb1cb0.sentence: This source of mulch requires less manual labor since it does not need to be removed at the end of the season and can actually be tilled into the soil.

56f8c5f48138.title: Mulch
56f8c5f48138.sentence: Organic mulches often smell like freshly cut wood but sometimes they start to smell like vinegar, ammonia, sulfur or silage.

e03783fbac3e.title: Mulch
e03783fbac3e.sentence: When this occurs, the process may become anaerobic and produce phytotoxic materials in small quantities.

378b10edab77.title: Mulch
378b10edab77.sentence: This happens when material with ample nitrogen content is not rotated often enough and it forms pockets of increased decomposition.

994957cc0c69.title: Mulch
994957cc0c69.sentence: Once exposed to the air, the process quickly reverts to an aerobic process, but the anaerobic metabolites may be present for a period of time.

07d88457fc4b.title: Mulch
07d88457fc4b.sentence: Plants low to the ground or freshly planted are the most susceptible, and phytotoxicity from the produced chemicals may prevent germination of some seeds.

5d839784e3be.title: Biochar
5d839784e3be.sentence: Biochar is a high-carbon, fine-grained residue that is produced via pyrolysis.

8eeb5bdd0cd4.title: Biochar
8eeb5bdd0cd4.sentence: It is the direct thermal decomposition of biomass in the absence of oxygen, which prevents combustion, and produces a mixture of solids (biochar), liquid (bio-oil), and gas (syngas) products.

0552b1d852bb.title: Biochar
0552b1d852bb.sentence: The specific yield from pyrolysis (the step of gasification that produces biochar) is dependent on process conditions such as temperature, heating rate, and residence time.

f917a42f24ce.title: Biochar
f917a42f24ce.sentence: These parameters can be tuned to produce either more energy or more biochar.

fe9a4638fc23.title: Biochar
fe9a4638fc23.sentence: Gasifiers produce most of the biochar sold in the United States.

a7b47cf04af5.title: Biochar
a7b47cf04af5.sentence: The gasification process consists of four main stages: oxidation, drying, pyrolysis, and reduction.

228bf6931cc9.title: Biochar
228bf6931cc9.sentence: Temperature during pyrolysis in gasifiers is 250–550 °C (523–823 K), 600–800 °C (873–1,073 K) in the reduction zone, and 800–1,000 °C (1,070–1,270 K) in the combustion zone.

637e86e78ee0.title: Biochar
637e86e78ee0.sentence: Smallholder farmers in developing countries easily produce their own biochar without special equipment.

6260a4e1609f.title: Biochar
6260a4e1609f.sentence: They make piles of crop waste (e.g., maize stalks, rice straw, or wheat straw), light the piles on the top, and quench the embers with dirt or water to make biochar.

e99991ab51fb.title: Biochar
e99991ab51fb.sentence: This method greatly reduces smoke compared to traditional methods of burning crop waste.

6bf870fcf7ec.title: Biochar
6bf870fcf7ec.sentence: This method is known as the top-down burn or conservation burn.

3982cb58b1b5.title: Biochar
3982cb58b1b5.sentence: Besides pyrolysis, torrefaction and hydrothermal carbonization processes can also thermally decompose biomass to the solid material.

0b8be739a51b.title: Biochar
0b8be739a51b.sentence: And although hydrothermal carbonization can produce a carbon-rich solid product, the process is evidently different from the conventional thermal conversion process, so the product is therefore defined as "hydrochar" rather than "biochar".

7c3443c56562.title: Slash-and-char
7c3443c56562.sentence: Slash-and-char is an alternative to slash-and-burn that has a lesser effect on the environment.

8e0448d877aa.title: Slash-and-char
8e0448d877aa.sentence: It is the practice of charring the biomass resulting from the slashing instead of burning it.

7f2deadc504f.title: Slash-and-char
7f2deadc504f.sentence: Due to incomplete combustion (pyrolysis) the resulting residue matter charcoal can be utilized as biochar to improve the soil fertility.

f05337e3b3fa.title: Biochar
f05337e3b3fa.sentence: Slash-and-burn leaves only 3% of the carbon from the organic material in the soil whereas slash-and-char can retain up to 50%.

4113549150f1.title: Slash-and-char
4113549150f1.sentence: Switching to slash-and-char can sequester up to 50% of the carbon in a highly stable form.

d4c306ef5023.title: Biochar
d4c306ef5023.sentence: The global potential for carbon sequestration by shifting from slash-and-burn to slash-and-char farming techniques has been estimated to between 0.22 and 0.42 Gt C/yr.

b62ff552c1f4.title: Biochar
b62ff552c1f4.sentence: This is unlike slash-and-burn soils, which quickly become depleted of nutrients, forcing farmers to abandon fields, producing a continuous slash-and-burn cycle.

62e18909ab70.title: Biochar
62e18909ab70.sentence: Additionally, by improving soil's till-ability, fertility, and productivity, biochar-enhanced soils can indefinitely sustain agricultural production.

240fa58f7de6.title: Slash-and-char
240fa58f7de6.sentence: It results in the creation of biochar, which can then be mixed with biomass such as crop residues, food waste, or manure and buried in the soil to bring about the formation of terra preta.

521ad10fb0e2.title: Biochar
521ad10fb0e2.sentence: The physical and chemical properties of biochars as determined by feedstocks and technologies are crucial.

6159c0b35bba.title: Biochar
6159c0b35bba.sentence: Characterization data explain their performance in a specific use.

a53293699542.title: Biochar
a53293699542.sentence: Properties can be categorized in several respects, including the proximate and elemental composition, pH value, and porosity.

557ce05518c1.title: Biochar
557ce05518c1.sentence: For example, guidelines published by the International Biochar Initiative provide standardized evaluation methods.

b9079eb0824c.title: Biochar
b9079eb0824c.sentence: The atomic ratios of biochar, including H/C and O/C, correlate with the properties that are relevant to organic content, such as polarity and aromaticity.

57d3d808cea5.title: Biochar
57d3d808cea5.sentence: In the carbonization process, both the H/C and O/C atomic ratios decrease due to the release of functional groups that contain hydrogen and oxygen.

00573b579eab.title: Biochar
