cbe728907704.title: Night soil
cbe728907704.sentence: Night soil is a historical euphemism for human excreta collected from cesspools, privies, pail closets, pit latrines, privy middens, septic tanks, etc. This material was removed from the immediate area, usually at night, by workers employed in this trade.

37c196adad2e.title: Night soil
37c196adad2e.sentence: Night soil was produced as a result of a sanitation system in areas without sewer systems or septic tanks.

d2ee9782e68d.title: Night soil
d2ee9782e68d.sentence: In this system of waste management, human feces are collected without dilution in water.

b335ecc5e7a9.title: Night soil
b335ecc5e7a9.sentence: Sometimes it could be transported out of towns and sold on as a fertilizer.

6b193f935da5.title: Night soil
6b193f935da5.sentence: The use of unprocessed human feces as fertilizer is a risky practice as it may contain disease-causing pathogens.

5171ac579713.title: Night soil
5171ac579713.sentence: Common parasitic worm infections, such as ascariasis, in these countries are linked to night soil use in agriculture, because the helminth eggs are in feces and can thus be transmitted from one infected person to another person (fecal-oral transmission of disease).

f57b0a600441.title: Night soil
f57b0a600441.sentence: These risks are reduced by proper fecal sludge management, e.g. via composting.

4e63d0127781.title: Night soil
4e63d0127781.sentence: The safe reduction of human excreta into compost is possible.

7793db1ffb66.title: Night soil
7793db1ffb66.sentence: The sewage system of ancient Athens collected the sewage of the city in a large reservoir and then channelled it to the Cephissus river valley for use as fertilizer.

ae6b5eeff204.title: Night soil
ae6b5eeff204.sentence: In the city of Edo, compost merchants gathered feces to sell to farmers.

7de3da01b212.title: Night soil
7de3da01b212.sentence: The Aztecs, in particular, are well known for their famous chinampas, artificial islands made of mud and human waste used to grow crops that could be harvested up to seven times a year.

68f69312b2e5.title: Reuse of human excreta
68f69312b2e5.sentence: Beneficial uses of the treated excreta may focus on using the plant-available nutrients (mainly nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium) that are contained in the treated excreta.

04540533d3ff.title: Reuse of human excreta
04540533d3ff.sentence: They may also make use of the organic matter and energy contained in the excreta.

767ba2afcf9b.title: Reuse of human excreta
767ba2afcf9b.sentence: The most common reuse of excreta is as fertilizer and soil conditioner in agriculture.

b1d5ed0c6155.title: Reuse of human excreta
b1d5ed0c6155.sentence: This is also called a "closing the loop" approach for sanitation with agriculture.

6eba28b0b826.title: Reuse of human excreta
6eba28b0b826.sentence: It is a central aspect of the ecological sanitation approach.

64a6ac5bbaf6.title: Reuse of human excreta
64a6ac5bbaf6.sentence: There are several "human excreta derived fertilizers" which vary in their properties and fertilizing characteristics, for example: urine, dried feces, composted feces, fecal sludge, sewage, sewage sludge.

95ffeb395ed8.title: Reuse of human excreta
95ffeb395ed8.sentence: Options include urine diversion and dehydration of feces (urine-diverting dry toilets), composting (composting toilets or external composting processes), sewage sludge treatment technologies and a range of fecal sludge treatment processes.

b257e1228be6.title: Reuse of human excreta
b257e1228be6.sentence: They all achieve various degrees of pathogen removal and reduction in water content for easier handling.

07770f3129c7.title: Reuse of human excreta
07770f3129c7.section: As fertilizer > Comparison to other fertilizers
07770f3129c7.sentence: In Africa, for example, the theoretical quantities of nutrients that can be recovered from human excreta are comparable with all current fertilizer use on the continent.

0e8955599148.title: Reuse of human excreta
0e8955599148.section: As fertilizer > Comparison to other fertilizers
0e8955599148.sentence: Therefore, reuse can support increased food production and also provide an alternative to chemical fertilizers, which is often unaffordable to small-holder farmers.

2120e17fe4c4.title: Reuse of human excreta
2120e17fe4c4.section: As fertilizer > Comparison to other fertilizers
2120e17fe4c4.sentence: Phosphate ores contain heavy metals such as cadmium and uranium, which can reach the food chain via mineral phosphate fertilizer.

8ae3d40e47d6.title: Reuse of human excreta
8ae3d40e47d6.section: As fertilizer > Comparison to other fertilizers
8ae3d40e47d6.sentence: This does not apply to excreta-based fertilizers (unless the human's food was contaminated beyond safe limits to start with), which is an advantage.

d37c44bcace5.title: Reuse of human excreta
d37c44bcace5.section: As fertilizer > Comparison to other fertilizers
d37c44bcace5.sentence: Fertilizing elements of organic fertilizers are mostly bound in carbonaceous reduced compounds.

e93884368cce.title: Reuse of human excreta
e93884368cce.section: As fertilizer > Comparison to other fertilizers
e93884368cce.sentence: If these are already partially oxidized as in the compost, the fertilizing minerals are adsorbed on the degradation products (humic acids) etc. Thus, they exhibit a slow-release effect and are usually less rapidly leached compared to mineral fertilizers.

842d4c647fa4.title: Reuse of human excreta
842d4c647fa4.section: Health and environmental aspects of agricultural use > Nitrate pollution
842d4c647fa4.sentence: This also applies to excreta-based fertilizer since it also contains nitrogen.

4060a4dbc9dd.title: Reuse of human excreta
4060a4dbc9dd.section: Health and environmental aspects of agricultural use > Nitrate pollution
4060a4dbc9dd.sentence: Excessive nitrogen, which plants do not take up, is transformed into nitrate, which is easily leached.

45d206c5b11d.title: Reuse of human excreta
45d206c5b11d.section: Health and environmental aspects of agricultural use > Pharmaceutical residues
45d206c5b11d.sentence: In fact, the pharmaceutical residues in the excreta are degraded better in terrestrial systems (soil) than in aquatic systems.

5065388c00a2.title: Reuse of human excreta
5065388c00a2.sentence: The nutrients and organic matter which are contained in human excreta or in domestic wastewater (sewage) have been used in agriculture in many countries for centuries.

d0fcb4c84b2b.title: Reuse of human excreta
d0fcb4c84b2b.sentence: However, this practice is often carried out in an unregulated and unsafe manner in developing countries.

fbe36b0dffdc.title: Biosolids
fbe36b0dffdc.sentence: Biosolids are solid organic matter recovered from a sewage treatment process and used as fertilizer.

b5f7e22c0a6a.title: Reuse of human excreta
b5f7e22c0a6a.sentence: The use of treated sewage sludge (after treatment also called "biosolids") as a soil conditioner or fertilizer is possible but is a controversial topic in some countries (such as USA, some countries in Europe) due to the chemical pollutants it may contain, such as heavy metals and environmental persistent pharmaceutical pollutants.

03573360acc1.title: Biosolids
03573360acc1.sentence: In the 1920s, the farming community began also to use sewage sludge from local wastewater treatment plants.

05d44a44e4ec.title: Biosolids
05d44a44e4ec.sentence: Scientific research over many years has confirmed that these biosolids contain similar nutrients to those in animal manures.

625f4f34872c.title: Biosolids
625f4f34872c.sentence: Biosolids may contain macronutrients nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium and sulphur with micronutrients copper, zinc, calcium, magnesium, iron, boron, molybdenum and manganese.

943cbf5df95a.title: Biosolids
943cbf5df95a.sentence: Biosolids contain 60–65% organic matter and stimulate soil microbe activity.

818e46d3eedd.title: Sewage sludge
818e46d3eedd.sentence: Treated biosolids can be produced in cake, granular, pellet, or liquid form and are spread over land before being incorporated into the soil or injected directly into the soil by specialist contractors.

28966b4bd7f0.title: Biosolids
28966b4bd7f0.sentence: Biosolids contains synthetic organic compounds, radionuclides and heavy metals.

de3ad74dbac8.title: Biosolids
de3ad74dbac8.sentence: Several farms that had spread biosolids as fertilizer were found to have PFAS contaminated soil, groundwater, animals and crops.

862b42607de6.title: Biosolids
862b42607de6.sentence: Some municipalities, states or countries have banned the use of biosolids on farmland.

e73d13458c1d.title: Sewage sludge
e73d13458c1d.sentence: Use of sewage sludge has shown an increase in level of soil available phosphorus and soil salinity.

38d863c43ded.title: Biosolids
38d863c43ded.sentence: The peer-reviewed study found PFAS levels in the resulting biochar to be below detectable limits, suggesting that high-temperature pyrolysis may provide a localized and effective approach to PFAS elimination in biosolids.

7081d848aa75.title: Biosolids
7081d848aa75.sentence: - Anaerobic Digestion: Micro-organisms decompose the sludge in the absence of oxygen either at mesophilic (at 35 °C) or thermophilic (between 50° and 57 °C) temperatures.

938052e3a65e.title: Biosolids
938052e3a65e.sentence: - Aerobic Digestion: Micro-organisms decompose the sludge in the presence of oxygen either at ambient and mesophilic (10 °C to 40 °C) or auto-thermal (40 °C to 80 °C) temperatures.

e3c721ad4f43.title: Biosolids
e3c721ad4f43.sentence: - Composting: A biological process where organic matter decomposes to produce humus after the addition of some dry bulking material such as sawdust, wood chips, or shredded yard waste under controlled aerobic conditions.

12f32d7fd2b0.title: Biosolids
12f32d7fd2b0.sentence: - Alkaline Treatment: The sludge is mixed with alkaline materials such as lime or cement kiln dust, or incinerator fly ash and maintained at pH above 12 for 24 hours (for Class B) or at temperature 70 °C for 30 minutes (for Class A).

0e02196cbb39.title: Biosolids
0e02196cbb39.sentence: - Heat Drying: Either convention or conduction dryers are used to dry the biosolids

1d5048393b5c.title: Biosolids
1d5048393b5c.sentence: - Dewatering: The separation of the water from biosolids is done to obtain a semi-solid or solid product by using a dewatering technologies (centrifuges, belt filter presses, plate and frame filter presses, and drying beds and lagoons).

9caaf5919c70.title: Compost
9caaf5919c70.section: Materials that can be composted > Human excreta
9caaf5919c70.sentence: Human excreta, sometimes called "humanure" in the composting context, can be added as an input to the composting process since it is a nutrient-rich organic material.

175f5fd75b67.title: Compost
175f5fd75b67.section: Materials that can be composted > Human excreta
175f5fd75b67.sentence: In soil, humanure helps to build organic matter, foster micronutrients, and develop healthy microbial communities.

057dd607c382.title: Compost
057dd607c382.section: Materials that can be composted > Human excreta
057dd607c382.sentence: Nitrogen, which serves as a building block for important plant amino acids, is found in solid human waste.

c4392c99bb78.title: Compost
c4392c99bb78.section: Materials that can be composted > Human excreta
c4392c99bb78.sentence: Phosphorus, which helps plants convert sunlight into energy in the form of ATP, can be found in liquid human waste.

1a794ae6cdcc.title: Compost
1a794ae6cdcc.section: Materials that can be composted > Human excreta
1a794ae6cdcc.sentence: It is also an excellent source of potassium as a soil nutrient.

9bb7e918b1e4.title: Compost
9bb7e918b1e4.section: Materials that can be composted > Human excreta
9bb7e918b1e4.sentence: In the case of home composting, a wide range of microorganisms, including bacteria, viruses, and parasitic worms, can be present in feces, and improper processing can pose significant health risks.

fd8149764f38.title: Compost
fd8149764f38.section: Materials that can be composted > Human excreta
fd8149764f38.sentence: Humanure's potential to spread disease can be managed through proper fermentation process, which can kill or neutralize pathogens and parasite eggs within two weeks to six months, depending on climate.

e33c279aa6c8.title: Compost
e33c279aa6c8.section: Materials that can be composted > Human excreta
e33c279aa6c8.sentence: Adding urine to compost can increase temperatures, so can increase its ability to destroy pathogens and unwanted seeds.

d67bdd4e5ac5.title: Compost
d67bdd4e5ac5.section: Materials that can be composted > Human excreta
d67bdd4e5ac5.sentence: Unlike feces, urine does not attract disease-spreading flies (such as houseflies or blowflies), and it does not contain the most hardy of pathogens, such as parasitic worm eggs.

4327afb59068.title: Compost
4327afb59068.section: Materials that can be composted > Human excreta
4327afb59068.sentence: The term "humanure" is a neologism coined by organic farmer Joseph Jenkins.

ad2c50a17ed6.title: Compost
ad2c50a17ed6.section: Composting technologies > Other systems at household level > Composting toilets
ad2c50a17ed6.sentence: A composting toilet is a type of dry toilet that treats human waste by a biological process called composting.

af3bf4a8ee3e.title: Compost
af3bf4a8ee3e.section: Composting technologies > Other systems at household level > Composting toilets
af3bf4a8ee3e.sentence: This process leads to the decomposition of organic matter and turns human waste into compost-like material.

c47009027ccf.title: Compost
c47009027ccf.section: Composting technologies > Other systems at household level > Composting toilets
c47009027ccf.sentence: Most composting toilets use no water for flushing and are therefore called "dry toilets".

fd0121eec234.title: Compost
fd0121eec234.section: Composting technologies > Other systems at household level > Composting toilets
fd0121eec234.sentence: In many composting toilet designs, a carbon additive such as sawdust, coconut coir, or peat moss is added after each use.

2542585c86c3.title: Compost
2542585c86c3.section: Composting technologies > Other systems at household level > Composting toilets
2542585c86c3.sentence: This practice creates air pockets in the human waste to promote aerobic decomposition.

fd952dbf1c7c.title: Compost
fd952dbf1c7c.section: Composting technologies > Other systems at household level > Composting toilets
fd952dbf1c7c.sentence: This also improves the carbon-to-nitrogen ratio and reduces potential odor.

e233b49fbea5.title: Compost
e233b49fbea5.section: Composting technologies > Other systems at household level > Composting toilets
e233b49fbea5.sentence: Most composting toilet systems rely on mesophilic composting.

5337b2b754f5.title: Compost
5337b2b754f5.section: Composting technologies > Other systems at household level > Composting toilets
5337b2b754f5.sentence: Longer retention time in the composting chamber also facilitates pathogen die-off.

70513b19fdd9.title: Compost
70513b19fdd9.section: Composting technologies > Other systems at household level > Composting toilets
70513b19fdd9.sentence: The end product can also be moved to a secondary system – usually another composting step – to allow more time for mesophilic composting to further reduce pathogens.

e4b5e03802a6.title: Compost
e4b5e03802a6.section: Composting technologies > Other systems at household level > Composting toilets
e4b5e03802a6.sentence: Composting toilets, together with the secondary composting step, produce a humus-like end product that can be used to enrich soil if local regulations allow this.

91bd05c95841.title: Reuse of human excreta
91bd05c95841.sentence: The nutrients in compost from a composting toilet have a higher plant availability than dried feces from a typical urine-diverting dry toilet.

ab441cb6c6ee.title: Reuse of human excreta
ab441cb6c6ee.sentence: In any case, the use of compost from composting toilets in one's own garden can be regarded as safe and is the main method of use for compost from composting toilets.

7a814f90319d.title: Reuse of human excreta
7a814f90319d.sentence: One limiting factor may be legal restrictions due to the possibility that pathogens remain in the compost.

b83509b74d24.title: Reuse of human excreta
b83509b74d24.sentence: Urine contains large quantities of nitrogen (mostly as urea), as well as reasonable quantities of dissolved potassium.

0bb3ff735804.title: Reuse of human excreta
0bb3ff735804.sentence: Applying urine as fertilizer has been called "closing the cycle of agricultural nutrient flows" or ecological sanitation or ecosan.

616055960da6.title: Reuse of human excreta
616055960da6.sentence: Urine typically contains 70% of the nitrogen and more than half the potassium found in sewage, while making up less than 1% of the overall volume.

5bccc4ac52a1.title: Reuse of human excreta
5bccc4ac52a1.sentence: Typical design values for nutrients excreted with urine are: 4 kg nitrogen per person per year, 0.36 kg phosphorus per person per year and 1.0 kg potassium per person per year.

815bc1c31b01.title: Reuse of human excreta
815bc1c31b01.sentence: Urine's nutrient content, when expressed with the international fertilizer convention of N:P2O5:K2O, is approximately 7:1.5:2.2.

bdd6762d147a.title: Reuse of human excreta
bdd6762d147a.sentence: These are design values but the actual values vary with diet.

4b4026229342.title: Reuse of human excreta
4b4026229342.sentence: In particular, the nitrogen content in urine is related to quantity of protein in the diet: A high protein diet results in high urea levels in urine.

4c47da49d2c9.title: Reuse of human excreta
4c47da49d2c9.sentence: The nitrogen content in urine is proportional to the total food protein in the person's diet, and the phosphorus content is proportional to the sum of total food protein and vegetal food protein.

490ae8206f75.title: Reuse of human excreta
490ae8206f75.sentence: Urine fertilizer is usually applied diluted with water because undiluted urine can chemically burn the leaves or roots of some plants, causing plant injury, particularly if the soil moisture content is low.

26d9cf175bb1.title: Reuse of human excreta
26d9cf175bb1.sentence: When diluted with water (at a 1:5 ratio for container-grown annual crops with fresh growing medium each season or a 1:8 ratio for more general use), it can be applied directly to soil as a fertilizer.

1f2cc4281c56.title: Reuse of human excreta
1f2cc4281c56.sentence: The fertilization effect of urine has been found to be comparable to that of commercial nitrogen fertilizers.

ba777b4b885d.title: Reuse of human excreta
ba777b4b885d.sentence: Concentrations of heavy metals such as lead, mercury, and cadmium, commonly found in sewage sludge, are much lower in urine.

c479be8b9c5e.title: Reuse of human excreta
c479be8b9c5e.sentence: The general limitations to using urine as fertilizer depend mainly on the potential for buildup of excess nitrogen (due to the high ratio of that macronutrient), and inorganic salts such as sodium chloride, which are also part of the wastes excreted by the renal system.

82233cb4b067.title: Reuse of human excreta
82233cb4b067.sentence: Over-fertilization with urine or other nitrogen fertilizers can result in too much ammonia for plants to absorb, acidic conditions, or other phytotoxicity.

2a09a4ccdba6.title: Reuse of human excreta
2a09a4ccdba6.sentence: During storage, the urea in urine is rapidly hydrolyzed by urease, creating ammonia.

25238bc11c9a.title: Reuse of human excreta
25238bc11c9a.sentence: Urine can be distributed via perforated hoses buried ~10 cm under the surface of the soil among crop plants, thus minimizing risk of odors, loss of nutrients due to volatilization, or transmission of pathogens.

d15e0b5ef5d2.title: Reuse of human excreta
d15e0b5ef5d2.sentence: The health risks of using urine as a source of fertilizer are generally regarded as negligible, especially when dispersed in soil rather than on the part of a plant that is consumed.

fe5c3dc6190c.title: Azolla
fe5c3dc6190c.sentence: Azolla (commonly called mosquito fern, water fern, and fairy moss) is a genus of seven species of aquatic ferns in the family Salviniaceae.

df1886fd6a2a.title: Azolla
df1886fd6a2a.sentence: They form a symbiotic relationship with the cyanobacterium Anabaena azollae, which lives outside the cells of its host and which fixes atmospheric nitrogen.

71db91db4fa6.title: Azolla
71db91db4fa6.sentence: Unlike all other known plants, its symbiotic microorganism transfers directly from one generation to the next.

6afd3c69e863.title: Azolla
6afd3c69e863.sentence: Azolla is a highly productive plant that can double its biomass in 1.9 days, depending on growing conditions.

0e01605c7cee.title: Azolla
0e01605c7cee.sentence: The plant can yield can reach 8–10 tonnes fresh matter per hectare in Asian paddy fields.

14df1ee851d1.title: Azolla
14df1ee851d1.sentence: When rice paddies are flooded in the spring, they can be planted with Azolla, which then quickly multiplies to cover the water, suppressing weeds.

25d6b10303a7.title: Azolla
25d6b10303a7.sentence: The rotting plant material resulting from the die-off of this Azolla releases nitrogen into the water for the rice plants, providing up to nine tonnes of protein per hectare per year.

b7514be0775f.title: Azolla
b7514be0775f.sentence: The nitrogen-fixing capability of Azolla has led to widespread use as a biofertiliser, especially in parts of southeast Asia.

ffb4ac014dda.title: Azolla
ffb4ac014dda.section: Applications > Food and animal feed > Companion plant
ffb4ac014dda.sentence: Rice farmers used Azolla as a rice biofertilizer 1500 years ago.

084fd56b00a1.title: Azolla
084fd56b00a1.section: Applications > Food and animal feed > Companion plant
084fd56b00a1.sentence: The earliest known written record of this practice is in a book written by Jia Sixie in 554 CE in Qimin Yaoshu (Essential Techniques for the Welfare of the People).

0e6c9f2a57ba.title: Isobutylidenediurea
0e6c9f2a57ba.sentence: Isobutylidenediurea (abbreviated IBDU) is an organic compound with the formula (CH3)2CHCH{NHC(O)NH2}2.

99869dae6bf0.title: Isobutylidenediurea
99869dae6bf0.sentence: It functions as a controlled-release fertiliser owing to its low solubility, which limits the rate of its hydrolysis to urea, which is a fast-acting fertiliser.

14ef0f971c4f.title: Isobutylidenediurea
14ef0f971c4f.sentence: It is a derivative of urea (OC(NH2)2), which itself is highly soluble in water, but IBDU is not.

60c8f0df33dd.title: Isobutylidenediurea
60c8f0df33dd.sentence: It is produced by the condensation reaction of isobutyraldehyde and two equivalents of urea:

e534d84e464d.title: Isobutylidenediurea
e534d84e464d.sentence: The controlled-release process is the reverse of the above reaction, which only occurs after the IBDU dissolves.

cefc8d4a9426.title: Isobutylidenediurea
cefc8d4a9426.sentence: A number of CRF's have been developed based on urea.

90c3910ec741.title: Isobutylidenediurea
90c3910ec741.sentence: Related to IBDU is crotonylidene diurea (Crotodur).

606046d5482c.title: Isobutylidenediurea
606046d5482c.sentence: Simpler are various urea-formaldehyde materials such as ureaform, which consists of methylene diurea and dimethylene triurea.

c403569f11c1.title: Bokashi (horticulture)
c403569f11c1.sentence: Bokashi (also referred to as bokashi composting, bokashi fermentation and fermented composting) is an anaerobic composting method that converts food waste and organic matter into a soil amendment using specialized bran.

23d5ffc4d8ed.title: Bokashi (horticulture)
23d5ffc4d8ed.sentence: - Organic matter is inoculated with yeast, photosynthetic bacteria, and lactic acid bacteria.

7baba84cde0e.title: Bokashi (horticulture)
7baba84cde0e.sentence: These will convert a fraction of the carbohydrates in the input to lactic acid by homolactic fermentation.

80cb67f5a434.title: Bokashi (horticulture)
80cb67f5a434.sentence: - Fermented anaerobically (more precisely, microaerobically) for a few weeks at typical room temperatures in an airtight vessel, the organic matter is preserved by the acid, in a process closely related to the making of some fermented foods and silage.

47a03bfd1e3e.title: Bokashi (horticulture)
47a03bfd1e3e.sentence: - The preserve is mixed into soil that has naturally occurring micro-organisms.

735cf93c395f.title: Bokashi (horticulture)
735cf93c395f.sentence: - Suffused with lactate, the preserve is readily consumed by the indigenous soil life, primarily the bacteria, 'disappearing' within a very few weeks at normal temperatures.

457b89fa9225.title: Bokashi (horticulture)
457b89fa9225.sentence: Earthworm action is typically prominent as bacteria are themselves consumed, such that the amended soil acquires a texture associated with vermicompost.

23b3b3b87d84.title: Bokashi (horticulture)
23b3b3b87d84.section: Characteristics > Emissions > Carbon, gases and energy
23b3b3b87d84.sentence: As a result, a bokashi bucket barely heats up and remains at ambient temperature.

c397bc6d1cdc.title: Bokashi (horticulture)
c397bc6d1cdc.section: Characteristics > Emissions > Carbon, gases and energy
c397bc6d1cdc.sentence: Compost, which is aerobic, "burns up" much of the carbon into carbon dioxide to sustain the metabolism of microbes as it matures.

d634e81fc4bc.title: Bokashi (horticulture)
d634e81fc4bc.section: Characteristics > Emissions > Carbon, gases and energy
d634e81fc4bc.sentence: In addition, compost can also lose the key plant nutrient nitrogen (in the potent greenhouse gas nitrous oxide and in ammonia), while bokashi almost does not.

abcf6c3603fc.title: Bokashi (horticulture)
abcf6c3603fc.sentence: The nature of bokashi reduces risk of nutrient leaching, and does not emit the greenhouse gas nor heat typically released by traditional hot compost methods.

36b79412c271.title: Bokashi (horticulture)
36b79412c271.sentence: The practice of bokashi is believed to have its earliest roots in ancient Korea.

4fbb32a67a03.title: Bokashi (horticulture)
4fbb32a67a03.sentence: A commercial Japanese bokashi method was developed by Teruo Higa in 1982 under the 'EM' trademark (short for Effective Microorganisms).

3930c3c7ba9a.title: Bokashi (horticulture)
3930c3c7ba9a.sentence: EM became the best known form of bokashi worldwide, mainly in household use, claiming to have reached over 120 countries.

e0c9edaed107.title: Digestate
e0c9edaed107.sentence: Digestate is the material remaining after the anaerobic digestion (decomposition under low oxygen conditions) of a biodegradable feedstock.

d4afbf9b4273.title: Digestate
d4afbf9b4273.sentence: Anaerobic digestion produces two main products: digestate and biogas.

aad76e4168ab.title: Digestate
aad76e4168ab.sentence: - Sewage sludges: Liquid sludge, untreated sewage sludge, composted sludge, and lime treated sludge.

96a2fc777e02.title: Digestate
96a2fc777e02.sentence: - Animal wastes: Animal fats, animal blood, food remains, stomach contents, rumen contents, animal carcasses, and poultry, fish, and livestock manure.

f6a6860bdc22.title: Digestate
f6a6860bdc22.sentence: - Energy crops: Usually corn, maize, millet, and clover.

77f6bbf72e3b.title: Digestate
77f6bbf72e3b.sentence: - Municipal wastes: Food waste, coffee/tea filters, organic leftovers, bakery waste, and kitchen waste.

70e1bcd6c7e1.title: Digestate
70e1bcd6c7e1.sentence: The chemical make-up of the digestate produced can vary depending on what feedstock is used.

5ee2f346c892.title: Digestate
5ee2f346c892.sentence: Since acidogenesis is early in the process of anaerobic digestion, most of the organic matter has not been fully degraded leaving a digestate that is fibrous and consists of structural plant matter including lignin and cellulose.

51075653b165.title: Digestate
51075653b165.sentence: Thus, it is often referred to as solid digestate.

c4d2b2ad8454.title: Digestate
c4d2b2ad8454.sentence: Acidogenic digestate has high moisture retention properties.

4ecd0945e3eb.title: Digestate
4ecd0945e3eb.sentence: By this point most of the organic matter has broken down leaving behind the Methanogenic digestate known as a sludge (sometimes called a liquor or liquid digestate).

77e251888a79.title: Digestate
77e251888a79.sentence: The sludge is high in nutrients such as ammoniums and potassium.

066d0f06a7bd.title: Digestate
066d0f06a7bd.sentence: The liquid fraction constitutes up to 90% of the digestate by volume, contains 2–6% dry matter, particles <1.2 mm in size, and most of the soluble nitrogen and potassium, while the solid fraction retains most of the digestate phosphorus, and contains dry matter content ˃ 15%.

5054483a276c.title: Digestate
5054483a276c.sentence: Generally the ammonia content of the digestate accounts for approximately 60-80% of the total nitrogen content, but for a feedstock like kitchen food waste it can be as high as 99%.

eb50cab554f9.title: Digestate
eb50cab554f9.sentence: Digestate has also been reported to have a higher phosphorus and potassium concentration than that of composts.

6224de9a5ea0.title: Digestate
6224de9a5ea0.sentence: The primary use of digestate is as a soil conditioner.

67a12a6989f5.title: Digestate
67a12a6989f5.sentence: Acidogenic digestate provides moisture retention and organic content for soils.

deed236c9877.title: Digestate
deed236c9877.sentence: Methanogenic digestate provides nutrients for plant growth.

760db5b42618.title: Digestate
760db5b42618.sentence: It can also be used to protect soils against erosion.

843e2adae684.title: Digestate
843e2adae684.sentence: Digestate is technically not compost although it is similar to it in physical and chemical characteristics.

337e14cc7129.title: Digestate
337e14cc7129.sentence: Compost is produced by aerobic digestion-decomposition by aerobes.

c8bf011f518b.title: Digestate
c8bf011f518b.sentence: This includes fungi and bacteria which are able to break down the lignin and cellulose to a greater extent.

77211a406cc8.title: Digestate
77211a406cc8.sentence: Chemical quality needs to be considered in terms of heavy metals and other inorganic contaminant, persistent organic compounds and the content of macro-elements such as nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium.

19ffe1b3f29b.title: Digestate
19ffe1b3f29b.sentence: Depending on their source, biowastes can contain pathogens, which can lead to the spreading of human, animal or plant diseases if not appropriately managed.

23c227ea1589.title: Digestate
23c227ea1589.sentence: In the UK the Publicly Available Specification (called PAS110) governs the definition of digestate derived from the anaerobic digestion of source-segregated biodegradable materials.

aeb74a005cb6.title: Digestate
aeb74a005cb6.sentence: If a biogas plant meets the standard, its digestate will be regarded as having been fully recovered and to have ceased to be waste, and it can be sold with the name "bio-fertiliser".

0ee09a4690a4.title: Reuse of human excreta

8d6d0c1e3881.title: Reuse of human excreta
8d6d0c1e3881.sentence: According to the 2004 "proposed Swedish default values", an average Swedish adult excretes 0.55 kg nitrogen, 0.18 kg phosphorus, and 0.36 kg potassium as feces per year.

07a5a94929b9.title: Reuse of human excreta
07a5a94929b9.sentence: The yearly mass is 51 kg wet and 11 kg dried, so that wet feces would have a NPK% value of 1.1:0.8:0.9.

4a19c53054b0.title: Reuse of human excreta
4a19c53054b0.sentence: Urine can contain up to 90 percent of the nitrogen, up to 50 percent of the phosphorus, and up to 70 percent of the potassium present in human excreta.

ed4a2295667e.title: Reuse of human excreta
ed4a2295667e.sentence: Fecal sludge is defined as "coming from onsite sanitation technologies, and has not been transported through a sewer." Examples of onsite technologies include pit latrines, unsewered public ablution blocks, septic tanks and dry toilets.

93cf791f6823.title: Reuse of human excreta
93cf791f6823.sentence: Fecal sludge can be treated by a variety of methods to render it suitable for reuse in agriculture.

b5fecd762ea7.title: Reuse of human excreta
b5fecd762ea7.sentence: These include (usually carried out in combination) dewatering, thickening, drying (in sludge drying beds), composting, pelletization, and anaerobic digestion.

a986570dab00.title: Reuse of human excreta
a986570dab00.sentence: World Health Organization Guidelines from 2006 have set up a framework describing how this reuse can be done safely by following a "multiple barrier approach".

4296c0b13792.sentence: In 2006 the World Health Organization (WHO) provided guidelines on safe reuse of wastewater, excreta, and greywater.

b7b6b1be8c31.sentence: The multiple barrier concept to reuse, which is the key cornerstone of this publication, has led to a clear understanding of how excreta reuse can be done safely.

7748893b7658.title: Reuse of human excreta

cec2e2990feb.sentence: It mainly depends on which other barriers will be put in place, according to the multiple-barrier concept.

eb2c6ffb4403.section: Health and environmental aspects of agricultural use > Pathogens > Treatment of excreta for pathogen removal
eb2c6ffb4403.sentence: Temperature is a treatment parameter with an established relationship to pathogen inactivation across all pathogen groups: Temperatures above 50 °C (122 °F) can inactivate most pathogens.

6c8262a5adab.title: Reuse of human excreta
6c8262a5adab.section: Health and environmental aspects of agricultural use > Pathogens > Treatment of excreta for pathogen removal
6c8262a5adab.sentence: Therefore, thermal sanitization is utilized in several technologies, such as thermophilic composting and thermophilic anaerobic digestion, and potentially in sun drying.

e375d3dcc9e1.section: Health and environmental aspects of agricultural use > Pathogens > Treatment of excreta for pathogen removal
e375d3dcc9e1.sentence: Alkaline conditions (pH value above 10) can also deactivate pathogens.

e43f8cba2e80.title: Reuse of human excreta
e43f8cba2e80.section: Health and environmental aspects of agricultural use > Pathogens > Treatment of excreta for pathogen removal
e43f8cba2e80.sentence: This can be achieved with ammonia sanitization or lime treatment.

44370cb3d6a0.title: Reuse of human excreta
44370cb3d6a0.section: Health and environmental aspects of agricultural use > Pathogens > Indicator organisms
44370cb3d6a0.sentence: As indicator organisms in reuse schemes, helminth eggs are commonly used because they are among the most difficult to destroy in most treatment processes.

2f6a516bf5e8.title: Liming (soil)
2f6a516bf5e8.sentence: This concept of "corrected lime potential" to define the degree of base saturation in soils became the basis for procedures now used in soil testing laboratories to determine the "lime requirement" of soils.

1f86523206f6.title: Liming (soil)
1f86523206f6.sentence: The degree to which a given amount of lime per unit of soil volume will increase soil pH depends on the buffer capacity of the soil (this is generally related to soil cation exchange capacity or CEC).

273e1c7cd145.title: Liming (soil)
273e1c7cd145.sentence: Soils with low CEC will usually show a more marked pH increase than soils with high CEC.

180a7d9be934.title: Liming (soil)
180a7d9be934.sentence: But the low-CEC soils will witness more rapid leaching of the added bases, and so will see a quicker return to original acidity unless additional liming is done.

5709bcca63e2.title: Liming (soil)
5709bcca63e2.sentence: Over-liming is most likely to occur on soil that has low CEC, such as sand which is deficient in buffering agents such as organic matter and clay.

ad5c9b8ee824.title: Liming (soil)
ad5c9b8ee824.section: Impact on soil properties > Effect on soil organic carbon
ad5c9b8ee824.sentence: The net effect of soil liming on soil organic carbon is primarily the result of three processes.

cbf2da73afbf.title: Liming (soil)
cbf2da73afbf.section: Impact on soil properties > Effect on soil organic carbon
cbf2da73afbf.sentence: As soil liming ameliorates soil conditions that inhibit plant growth, an increase in plant productivity is expected.

732f9ba877b9.title: Liming (soil)
732f9ba877b9.section: Impact on soil properties > Effect on soil organic carbon
732f9ba877b9.sentence: The higher yields resulting from lime applications will produce increased returns of organic matter to the soil in the form of dying roots and decaying crop residue.

24ee4863afde.title: Liming (soil)
24ee4863afde.section: Impact on soil properties > Effect on soil organic carbon
24ee4863afde.sentence: - Increased organic matter mineralization due to a more favorable pH.

7e3bff8f5f31.title: Liming (soil)
7e3bff8f5f31.section: Impact on soil properties > Effect on soil organic carbon
7e3bff8f5f31.sentence: Lime applications are known to have short-term stimulating effects on soil biological activity, thus favoring organic matter mineralization and very likely accelerating organic matter turnover rates in soil.

466b5dfbd259.title: Liming (soil)
466b5dfbd259.section: Impact on soil properties > Effect on soil organic carbon
466b5dfbd259.sentence: - Amelioration of soil structure leading to a reduction of mineralization by means of protecting soil organic carbon.

784d61eafdf9.title: Liming (soil)
784d61eafdf9.section: Impact on soil properties > Effect on soil organic carbon
784d61eafdf9.sentence: Liming is known to ameliorate soil structure, as high Ca2+ concentrations and high ionic strength in the soil solution enhance the flocculation of clay minerals and, in turn, form more stable soil aggregates.

7f214c794675.title: Liming (soil)
7f214c794675.sentence: Liming can also improve aggregate stability on clay soils.

bcc48ba92a64.title: Liming (soil)
bcc48ba92a64.sentence: For this purpose structure lime, products containing calcium oxide (CaO) or hydroxide (Ca(OH)2) in mixes with calcium carbonate (CaCO3), are often used.

3acbac02c753.title: Liming (soil)
3acbac02c753.sentence: Structure liming can reduce losses of clay and nutrients from soil aggregates.

c8abf5b1ad49.title: Marl
c8abf5b1ad49.section: Economic geology > Historical use in agriculture
c8abf5b1ad49.sentence: Marl is one of the oldest soil amendments used in agriculture.

915da73759b6.title: Marl
915da73759b6.section: Economic geology > Historical use in agriculture
915da73759b6.sentence: It was used sporadically in Britain beginning in prehistoric times and its use was mentioned by Pliny the Elder in the 1st century.

56413f7c8c65.title: Marl
56413f7c8c65.section: Economic geology > Historical use in agriculture
56413f7c8c65.sentence: Its more widespread use from the 16th century on contributed to the early modern agricultural revolution.

1952f7093084.title: Marl
1952f7093084.section: Economic geology > Historical use in agriculture
1952f7093084.sentence: Marl was used extensively in Britain, particularly in Lancashire, during the 18th century.

b1d0e7ab31a7.title: Marl
b1d0e7ab31a7.section: Economic geology > Historical use in agriculture
b1d0e7ab31a7.sentence: The marl was normally extracted close to its point of use, so that almost every field had a marl pit, but some marl was transported greater distances by railroad.

4699ae5fb25c.title: Marl
4699ae5fb25c.section: Economic geology > Historical use in agriculture
4699ae5fb25c.sentence: However, marl was gradually replaced by lime and imported mineral fertilizers early in the 19th century.

aef505c5fffe.title: Marl
aef505c5fffe.section: Economic geology > Historical use in agriculture
aef505c5fffe.sentence: By the late 19th century, marl was being mined on an industrial scale in New Jersey and was increasingly being used on a more scientific basis, with marl being classified by grade and the state geological survey publishing detailed chemical analyses.

a014b8e880d1.title: Agricultural lime
a014b8e880d1.sentence: A 2019 study demonstrated that agricultural lime affects strontium-based mobility studies, which attempt to identify where individual prehistoric people lived.

6365fe7f1211.title: Agricultural lime
6365fe7f1211.sentence: Agricultural lime has a significant effect in areas with calcium-poor soils.

b6d50c3692c7.title: Agricultural lime
b6d50c3692c7.sentence: In a systematic study of the Karup River in Denmark, more than half of the strontium in the river's catchment was found to come from runoff of agricultural lime and not from the surrounding natural environment.

9d428b7efa41.title: Agricultural lime
9d428b7efa41.sentence: Such introduction of agricultural lime has resulted in researchers wrongly concluding that certain prehistoric individuals originated far abroad from their burial sites, because strontium isotopic results measured in their remains and personal effects were compared to burial sites contaminated by agricultural lime.

0c9e6510ea30.title: Agricultural lime
0c9e6510ea30.sentence: Calcium Carbonate Equivalent (CCE) and the Effective Calcium Carbonate Equivalent (ECCE) give a numeric value to the effectiveness of different liming materials.

52eca4139320.title: Agricultural lime
52eca4139320.sentence: The CCE compares the chemistry of a particular quarry's stone with the neutralizing power of pure calcium carbonate.

94aa91e6bea8.title: Agricultural lime
94aa91e6bea8.sentence: Because each molecule of magnesium carbonate is lighter than calcium carbonate, limestones containing magnesium carbonate (dolomite) can have a CCE greater than 100 percent.

77d24be2d52c.title: Agricultural lime
77d24be2d52c.sentence: Because the acids in soil are relatively weak, agricultural limestones must be ground to a small particle size to be effective.

4cc520754e02.title: Agricultural lime
4cc520754e02.sentence: Particles larger than 8 mesh are of little or no value, particles between 8 mesh and 60 mesh are somewhat effective, and particles smaller than 60 mesh are 100 percent effective.

ba29c60721bf.title: Agricultural lime
ba29c60721bf.sentence: By combining the CCE and its particle size, the Effective Calcium Carbonate Equivalent (ECCE) is determined.

692f82798614.title: Agricultural lime
692f82798614.sentence: The ECCE is percentage comparison of a particular agricultural limestone with pure calcium carbonate with all particles smaller than 60 mesh.

171af09396ad.title: Agricultural lime
171af09396ad.sentence: Typically the aglime materials in commercial use will have ECCE ranging from 45 percent to 110 percent.

0dff06f956cd.title: Marl
0dff06f956cd.section: Economic geology > Modern agricultural and aquacultural uses
0dff06f956cd.sentence: The rate of application must be adjusted for the reduced content of calcium carbonate versus straight lime, expressed as the calcium carbonate equivalent.

0290166789c4.title: Agricultural lime
0290166789c4.sentence: Brazil's vast inland cerrado region was regarded as unfit for farming before the 1960s because the soil was too acidic and poor in nutrients, according to Nobel Peace Prize winner Norman Borlaug, an American plant scientist referred to as the father of the Green Revolution.

120b4500cfa8.title: Agricultural lime
120b4500cfa8.sentence: However, from the 1960s, vast quantities of lime (pulverised chalk or limestone) were poured into the soil to reduce acidity.

477330ad81ad.title: Agricultural lime
477330ad81ad.sentence: The effort continued, and in the late 1990s, between 14 million and 16 million tonnes of lime were spread on Brazilian fields each year.

c73249cc4f5f.title: Agricultural lime
c73249cc4f5f.sentence: The quantity rose to 25 million tonnes in 2003 and 2004, equalling around five tonnes of lime per hectare.

f24971c08ea0.title: Agricultural lime
f24971c08ea0.sentence: As a result, Brazil has become the world's second biggest soybean exporter, and thanks to the boom in animal feed production, Brazil is now the biggest exporter of beef and poultry in the world.

99b7413dc2ce.sentence: Compost sequesters carbon in a stable (not easily accessed) form.

8116e1fefed5.title: Carbon farming

8116e1fefed5.sentence: Carbon farmers spread it over the soil surface without tilling.

ad446e69ade6.title: Carbon farming
ad446e69ade6.section: Methods used in agriculture > Using organic mulch and compost
ad446e69ade6.sentence: A 2013 study found that a single compost application significantly and durably increased grassland carbon storage by 25–70%.

72444ace07bc.title: Carbon farming
72444ace07bc.section: Methods used in agriculture > Using organic mulch and compost
72444ace07bc.sentence: Both tested sites showed large increases in grassland productivity: a forage increase of 78% in a drier valley site, while a wetter coastal site averaged an increase of 42%.

410358fe6e8c.title: Carbon farming
