410358fe6e8c.sentence: CH 4 and N 2O and emissions did not increase significantly.

35fb4be783bd.title: Carbon farming
35fb4be783bd.sentence: Composting is not an NRCS-approved technique and its impacts on native species and greenhouse emissions during production have not been fully resolved.

650fc7dd3055.title: Carbon farming
650fc7dd3055.sentence: Further, commercial compost supplies are too limited to cover large amounts of land.

831b673e7e66.title: Carbon farming
831b673e7e66.section: Methods used in agriculture > Adjusting livestock grazing
831b673e7e66.sentence: By regularly rotating the herd through multiple paddocks (as often as daily) the paddocks can rest/recover between grazing periods.

115f8e526676.title: Carbon farming
115f8e526676.section: Methods used in agriculture > Adjusting livestock grazing
115f8e526676.sentence: However, many researchers have argued the approach is unable to provide the benefits claimed.

172014905d8e.title: Carbon farming
172014905d8e.section: Methods used in agriculture > Adjusting livestock grazing
172014905d8e.sentence: Annual grasses have shallower roots and die once they are grazed.

648bcca2bd51.title: Carbon farming
648bcca2bd51.section: Methods used in agriculture > Adjusting livestock grazing
648bcca2bd51.sentence: Rotational grazing leads to the replacement of annuals by perennials with deeper roots, which can recover after grazing.

1f97e814d2c3.title: Carbon farming
1f97e814d2c3.section: Methods used in agriculture > Adjusting livestock grazing
1f97e814d2c3.sentence: A small amount of carbon may be sequestered in grassland soils through root exudates and manure.

251b05cef82a.title: Carbon farming
251b05cef82a.section: Methods used in agriculture > Adjusting livestock grazing
251b05cef82a.sentence: Ruminants like cows and sheep produce not only CO2, but also methane due to the microbes residing in their digestive system.

4483a22622b7.title: Carbon farming
4483a22622b7.section: Methods used in agriculture > Adjusting livestock grazing
4483a22622b7.sentence: Moreover, several peer-reviewed studies have found that excluding livestock completely from semi-arid grasslands can lead to significant recovery of vegetation and soil carbon sequestration.

5e1491ff3a4a.title: Green manure
5e1491ff3a4a.sentence: Green manure is broken down into plant nutrient components by heterotrophic bacteria that consumes organic matter.

5033e20d2dd0.title: Green manure
5033e20d2dd0.sentence: Warmth and moisture contribute to this process, similar to creating compost fertilizer.

203034ea73a6.title: Green manure
203034ea73a6.sentence: The plant matter releases large amounts of carbon dioxide and weak acids that react with insoluble soil minerals to release beneficial nutrients.

be8a748227d4.title: Green manure
be8a748227d4.sentence: Soils that are high in calcium minerals, for example, can be given green manure to generate a higher phosphate content in the soil, which in turn acts as a fertilizer.

f5c7c9ea4f59.title: Green manure
f5c7c9ea4f59.sentence: The ratio of carbon to nitrogen in a plant is a crucial factor to consider, since it will impact the nutrient content of the soil and may starve a crop of nitrogen, if the incorrect plants are used to make green manure.

fa3c1c3b245c.title: Green manure
fa3c1c3b245c.sentence: The ratio of carbon to nitrogen will differ from species to species, and depending upon the age of the plant.

20d248a558ae.title: Green manure
20d248a558ae.sentence: The ratio is referred to as C:N. The value of N is always one, whereas the value of carbon or carbohydrates is expressed in a value of about 10 up to 90; the ratio must be less than 30:1 to prevent the manure bacteria from depleting existing nitrogen in the soil.

b931e05b8ad7.title: Green manure
b931e05b8ad7.sentence: Mixing green manures into the soil without enough time before crop planting could stop the flow of nitrogen (nitrogen immobilization).

cf7e8b8a9f55.title: Green manure
cf7e8b8a9f55.sentence: When nitrogen stops flowing there won't be enough nutrients for the next crop planting.

0f3db7cc033d.title: Wood ash
0f3db7cc033d.sentence: Wood ash is the powdery residue remaining after the combustion of wood, such as burning wood in a fireplace, bonfire, or an industrial power plant.

aef90cfd7a16.title: Wood ash
aef90cfd7a16.sentence: It is largely composed of calcium compounds, along with other non-combustible trace elements present in the wood, and has been used for many purposes throughout history.

89cecc9f2c73.title: Wood ash
89cecc9f2c73.sentence: Wood ash can be used as a fertilizer used to enrich agricultural soil nutrition.

28b603ddce43.title: Wood ash
28b603ddce43.sentence: In this role, wood ash serves as a source of potassium and calcium carbonate, the latter acting as a liming agent to neutralize acidic soils.

6b2d7bc8f661.title: Wood ash
6b2d7bc8f661.sentence: Much of wood ash contains calcium carbonate (CaCO3) as its major component, representing 25% or even 45% of total ash weight.

9b08e070e71d.title: Wood ash
9b08e070e71d.sentence: The burning of wood results in about 6–10% ashes on average.

b15b54ab1f6a.title: Wood ash
b15b54ab1f6a.sentence: Also the conditions of the combustion affect the composition and amount of the residue ash, thus higher temperature will reduce the ash yield.

a7b5da3c281f.title: Wood ash
a7b5da3c281f.sentence: The study has found that at raised temperature Potassium (K), Sulphur (S), Boron (B), Sodium (Na) and Copper (Cu) decreased, whereas Magnesium (Mg), Phosphorus (P), Manganese (Mn), Aluminium (Al), Iron (Fe), and Silicon (Si) did not change relative to calcium (Ca).

09f67f6ff7b2.title: Wood ash
09f67f6ff7b2.sentence: There are trace elements of iron (Fe), manganese (Mn), zinc (Zn), copper (Cu) and some heavy metals.

f3c7077fed12.title: Biofertilizer
f3c7077fed12.sentence: Rhizobium, Azotobacter, Azospirillum and blue-green algae (BGA) are perhaps the species with the longest history of use as biofertilizers.

93359a47648b.title: Biofertilizer
93359a47648b.sentence: Rhizobium inoculant is used for leguminous crops.

9c3425431720.title: Biofertilizer
9c3425431720.sentence: Azotobacter can be used with crops like wheat, maize, mustard, cotton, potato, and other vegetable crops.

ff8541ef708b.title: Biofertilizer
ff8541ef708b.sentence: Azospirillum inoculations are recommended mainly for sorghum, millets, maize, sugarcane, and wheat.

3cb77f316d93.title: Biofertilizer
3cb77f316d93.sentence: Blue-green algae belonging to the cyanobacteria genera Nostoc, Anabaena, Tolypothrix, and Aulosira fix atmospheric nitrogen and are used as inoculants for paddy crops grown in both upland and lowland conditions.

3d59be29d844.title: Biofertilizer
3d59be29d844.sentence: Anabaena, in association with the water fern Azolla, can contribute nitrogen up to 60 kg/ha/season and can also enrich soils with organic matter.

c86499d3508a.title: Biofertilizer
c86499d3508a.sentence: - Bacillus spp. (in particular B. amyloliquefaciens, B. mojavensis, B. thuringiensis, B. licheniformis, and B. subtilis).

62a1805a868b.title: Biofertilizer
62a1805a868b.sentence: - Trichoderma spp. (such as T. viride, T. harzianum, T. reesei, T. longibrachiatum, T. atroviride, T. koningii)

d0cb03c4067d.title: Biofertilizer
d0cb03c4067d.sentence: Seaweeds are rich in various types of mineral elements (potassium, phosphorus, trace elements, etc.), hence they are extensively used as a form of manure replacement by people of coastal districts.

539b7a8af131.title: Fertilizer burn
539b7a8af131.sentence: Fertilizers contain differing salt concentrations which alter their 'salt index.' A salt index measures the relative change in osmotic pressure in water after a given salt has been added compared to sodium nitrate, which is assigned a value of 100.

48ba26b40f61.title: Fertilizer burn
48ba26b40f61.sentence: Salt indexes can have some relation to the rate of fertilizer burn in plants, with fertilizers of a salt index above 20 not being recommended for use with particularly sensitive crops.

ea7c7b15ff7c.title: Fertilizer burn
ea7c7b15ff7c.sentence: - Use of too much fertilizer of the correct salt index.

1fb642477e72.title: Fertilizer burn
1fb642477e72.sentence: This causes a buildup of salts and nutrients in the soil and thus a fertilizer burn from low osmotic pressure.

7d862ef64eca.title: Fertilizer burn
7d862ef64eca.sentence: - Use of a fertilizer with too high of a salt index.

d70276bf8af4.title: Fertilizer burn
d70276bf8af4.sentence: This will cause a buildup of salt and nutrients in the soil and thus a fertilizer burn from low osmotic pressure.

9bfd199554d9.title: Coated urea
9bfd199554d9.sentence: Coated urea fertilizers are a group of controlled release fertilizers consisting of prills of urea coated in less-soluble chemicals such as sulfur, polymers, other products or a combination.

acc0a284e7fe.title: Coated urea
acc0a284e7fe.sentence: These fertilizers mitigate some of the negative aspects of urea fertilization, such as fertilizer burn.

2b56507b1348.title: Coated urea
2b56507b1348.sentence: These coatings permit the gradual release of urea in a controlled fashion, allowing for less-frequent applications.

94642e84c3c1.title: Coated urea
94642e84c3c1.sentence: Sulfur-coated urea, or SCU, fertilizers release nitrogen via water penetration through cracks and micropores in the coating.

f9966a60913c.title: Coated urea
f9966a60913c.sentence: Sulfur-coated products typically range from 32% to 41% elemental nitrogen by weight.

fd4ae0d40b31.title: Coated urea
fd4ae0d40b31.sentence: The sulfur coating process was originally developed by the Tennessee Valley Authority.

aa852bd02d0e.title: Coated urea
aa852bd02d0e.sentence: The particles of fertilizer may in turn be sealed with wax to slow release further still, making microbial degradation necessary to permit water penetration.

04b96098a904.title: Coated urea
04b96098a904.sentence: Polymer-coated urea, also called plastic-coated urea, or PCU, fertilizers can permit a more precise rate of nitrogen release than sulfur-coated urea products.

3fb9b536b036.title: Coated urea
3fb9b536b036.sentence: It's possible to produce polymer-coated products where the nitrogen release can be delayed for 10 months after application.

728ae217688f.title: Coated urea
728ae217688f.sentence: The primary disadvantage of polymer-coated urea products is their relatively high cost compared to sulfur-coated urea.

85e02ea9d494.title: Coated urea
85e02ea9d494.sentence: Typically, these products consist of urea, coated with a layer of sulfur, which is in turn coated with a layer of polymer.

0f23f5295b74.title: Coated urea
0f23f5295b74.sentence: These products are generally used as less-expensive alternatives to purely plastic-coated products, while still providing precise nitrogen release characteristics.

37096bd85ae4.title: Ammonia volatilization from urea
37096bd85ae4.sentence: Urease inhibitors prevent the urease enzyme from breaking down the urea.

365dff501a45.title: Ammonia volatilization from urea
365dff501a45.sentence: Fertilizer is often applied when field conditions are not optimal, particularly in large scale operations.

809a48e2f9ed.title: Ammonia volatilization from urea
809a48e2f9ed.sentence: Most studies, indicate that nitrogen losses can be reduced in these situations when a urease inhibitor is applied to the fertilizer.

e85c4cd42ab5.title: Ammonia volatilization from urea
e85c4cd42ab5.sentence: This increases the probability that urea will be absorbed into the soil after a rain event rather than volatilized into the atmosphere.

5bf1e46b8662.title: Ammonia volatilization from urea
5bf1e46b8662.sentence: This causes subsequent hydrolyzation to occur below the soil surface and decreases atmospheric losses.

4ed2df686d17.title: Ammonia volatilization from urea
4ed2df686d17.sentence: The use of inhibitors also decreases the localized zones of high pH common with untreated urea.

b0f00bdcb33f.title: N-(n-Butyl)thiophosphoric triamide
b0f00bdcb33f.sentence: A white solid, NBPT is an "enhanced efficiency fertilizer", intended to limit the release of nitrogen-containing gases following fertilization.

84dda40aa1ce.title: N-(n-Butyl)thiophosphoric triamide
84dda40aa1ce.sentence: NBPT functions as an inhibitor of the enzyme urease.

23747ad03134.title: N-(n-Butyl)thiophosphoric triamide
23747ad03134.sentence: Approximately 0.5% by weight NBPT is mixed with the urea.

b2bd7fd56042.title: Fertilizer
b2bd7fd56042.section: Application > Chemicals that affect nitrogen uptake
b2bd7fd56042.sentence: Various chemicals are used to enhance the efficiency of nitrogen-based fertilizers.

da7058147271.title: Fertilizer
da7058147271.section: Application > Chemicals that affect nitrogen uptake
da7058147271.sentence: Urease inhibitors are used to slow the hydrolytic conversion of urea into ammonia catalyzed by ureases, ammonia being prone to evaporation as well as nitrification.

3f254f2294b1.title: Controlled-release fertiliser
3f254f2294b1.sentence: - Nitrification inhibitor: A substance that inhibits the biological oxidation of ammoniacal-N to nitrate-N.

4bb8ffaa82f1.title: Fertilizer
4bb8ffaa82f1.section: Application > Chemicals that affect nitrogen uptake
4bb8ffaa82f1.sentence: A popular inhibitor of ureases is N-(n-butyl)thiophosphoric triamide (NBPT).

759818198aee.title: Controlled-release fertiliser
759818198aee.sentence: Urease inhibitors, at levels of 0.05 weight percent, are added to urea-based fertilizers to control its conversion to ammonia.

dd779ccc2888.title: Controlled-release fertiliser
dd779ccc2888.sentence: - Stabilized nitrogen fertilizer: A fertilizer to which a nitrogen stabilizer has been added.

0ed36b0a15f2.title: Controlled-release fertiliser
0ed36b0a15f2.sentence: A nitrogen stabilizer is a substance added to a fertilizer which extends the time the nitrogen component of the fertilizer remains in the soil in the urea-N or ammoniacal-N form.

8489dcbb5536.title: Fertilizer
8489dcbb5536.section: Application > Chemicals that affect nitrogen uptake
8489dcbb5536.sentence: In this way farmers can limit the polluting effects of nitrogen run-off.

dd9794476192.title: Fertilizer
dd9794476192.sentence: NPK rating is a rating system describing the amount of nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium in a fertilizer.

c281926e8d0f.title: Fertilizer
c281926e8d0f.sentence: NPK ratings consist of three numbers separated by dashes (e.g., 10-10-10 or 16–4–8) describing the chemical content of fertilizers.

a42c99dcef9b.title: Fertilizer
a42c99dcef9b.sentence: The first number represents the percentage of nitrogen in the product; the second number, P2O5; the third, K2O.

2a0681dd7ecf.title: Fertilizer
2a0681dd7ecf.sentence: Fertilizers do not actually contain P2O5 or K2O, but the system is a conventional shorthand for the amount of phosphorus (P) or potassium (K) in a fertilizer.

7a9927cc2b28.title: Labeling of fertilizer
7a9927cc2b28.section: Common labeling conventions > Other labeling conventions
7a9927cc2b28.sentence: In the U.K., fertilizer labeling regulations allow for reporting the elemental mass fractions of phosphorus and potassium.

0d3532897e04.title: Labeling of fertilizer
0d3532897e04.section: Common labeling conventions > Other labeling conventions
0d3532897e04.sentence: The regulations stipulate that this should be done in parentheses after the standard N-P-K values, as in "15-30-15 (15-13-13)".

70ffd567b860.title: Fertilizer
70ffd567b860.sentence: Most fertilizers are labeled according to this N-P-K convention, although Australian convention, following an N-P-K-S system, adds a fourth number for sulfur, and uses elemental values for all values including P and K.

7ca3b9396393.title: Ammonium nitrate
7ca3b9396393.sentence: Ammonium nitrate is an important fertilizer with NPK rating 34-0-0 (34% nitrogen).

97e4900543b0.title: Ammonium nitrate
97e4900543b0.section: Production, reactions and crystalline phases > Reactions
97e4900543b0.sentence: As ammonium nitrate is a salt, both the cation, NH+4, and the anion, NO−3, may take part in chemical reactions.

905a8301f67b.title: Ammonium nitrate
905a8301f67b.sentence: Whilst less concentrated than urea (46-0-0), ammonium nitrate is more stable and does not rapidly lose nitrogen to the atmosphere.

510d3eb4d5c3.title: Ammonium nitrate
510d3eb4d5c3.sentence: The industrial production of ammonium nitrate entails the acid-base reaction of ammonia with nitric acid:

0752de9b88a8.title: Ammonium nitrate
0752de9b88a8.sentence: The ammonia required for this process is obtained by the Haber process from nitrogen and hydrogen.

15d37af3fe81.title: Ammonium nitrate
15d37af3fe81.sentence: Ammonium nitrate is found as the natural mineral gwihabaite (formerly known as nitrammite) – the ammonium analogue of saltpetre (mineralogical name: niter) – in the driest regions of the Atacama Desert in Chile, often as a crust on the ground or in conjunction with other nitrate, iodate, and halide minerals.

a80982be529a.title: Ammonium nitrate
a80982be529a.sentence: Ammonium nitrate was mined there until the Haber–Bosch process made it possible to synthesize nitrates from atmospheric nitrogen, rendering nitrate mining obsolete.

e383aa8c72ed.title: Ammonium nitrate
e383aa8c72ed.sentence: Ammonium nitrate readily forms explosive mixtures with varying properties when combined with explosives such as TNT or with fuels like aluminium powder or fuel oil.

0fc51faf8578.title: Ammonia volatilization from urea
0fc51faf8578.sentence: Since urea is not an oxidizer at standard temperature and pressure, it is safer to handle and less of a security risk than other common nitrogen fertilizers, such as ammonium nitrate.

957afabec127.title: UAN
957afabec127.sentence: UAN is a solution of urea and ammonium nitrate in water used as a fertilizer.

122b3e42740f.title: UAN
122b3e42740f.sentence: The combination of urea and ammonium nitrate has an extremely low critical relative humidity (18% at 30 °C) and can therefore only be used in liquid fertilizers.

e993451dc6af.title: Urea
e993451dc6af.sentence: In admixture, the combined solubility of ammonium nitrate and urea is so much higher than that of either component alone that it gives a stable solution with a total nitrogen content (32%) approaching that of solid ammonium nitrate (33.5%), though not, of course, that of urea itself (46%).

6f63a79e1a90.title: UAN
6f63a79e1a90.sentence: The most commonly used grade of these fertilizer solutions is UAN 32.0.0 (32%N) known as UN32 or UN-32, which consists of 45% ammonium nitrate, 35% urea and only 20% water.

0dbd5bb73bca.title: UAN
0dbd5bb73bca.sentence: Other grades are UAN 28, UAN 30 and UAN 18.

3501a0c4782f.title: UAN
3501a0c4782f.sentence: The solutions are quite corrosive towards mild steel (up to 0.5 inches (1.3 cm) per year on C1010 steel) and are therefore generally equipped with a corrosion inhibitor to protect tanks, pipelines, nozzles, etc. Urea–ammonium nitrate solutions should not be combined with calcium ammonium nitrate (CAN-17) or other solutions prepared from calcium nitrate.

d420e8a3e715.title: UAN
d420e8a3e715.sentence: A thick, milky-white insoluble precipitate forms that may plug nozzles.

41c48b289bf2.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.10%3A_Grazing
41c48b289bf2.sentence: But using what’s sometimes called management intensive grazing (MIG), in which animals are rotated through many pastures and do not re-graze a paddock until plants have sufficiently regrown, has shown great improvement in pasture productivity and animal health.

f4b3ed8c5a6c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.10%3A_Grazing
f4b3ed8c5a6c.sentence: But these continually grazed 0r very infrequently rotated pastures produced poorly as animals ate the regrowth again and again, weakening plants.

4b92954c6d9b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.10%3A_Grazing
4b92954c6d9b.sentence: Plants need to grow to a reasonable size before root reserves can be fully replenished, and continually regrazing early shoot regrowth depletes root reserves, making it harder for the plant to regrow again after grazing.

b450dc495e04.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.10%3A_Grazing
b450dc495e04.sentence: Depending on the season and weather, the rotation cycle can be as short as a week or 10 days and as long as 6–8 weeks.

2d0eb7710cac.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.10%3A_Grazing
2d0eb7710cac.sentence: For dairy farms using MIG, cows are turned out to a fresh paddock after each milking (Figure 12.3).

10e5d821cae8.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.10%3A_Grazing
10e5d821cae8.sentence: A well-managed grazing system has inherent efficiencies because the harvesting and fertilization require no (or limited) equipment and human labor.

f2a954204fcf.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.10%3A_Grazing
f2a954204fcf.sentence: The use of the newer styles of fencing and electric fence chargers make it easy to quickly set up new grazing paddocks, and once dairy or beef cows are trained to electric fences, a single-strand electric internal fence is enough to contain them in the paddock.

b020b6634511.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.10%3A_Grazing
b020b6634511.sentence: But in most cases cows grazing on high-quality, intensively managed pastures result in a lower cost of production once you factor in lower labor and machinery needs for such tasks as cleaning barns, spreading manure, harvesting crops, transporting animals to barns and feeding them out.

1cdaaf3b2235.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.10%3A_Grazing
1cdaaf3b2235.sentence: Well-managed pastures promote good soil health because they combine three beneficial practices: perennial forage crops, absence of tillage and regular manure additions.

642eb15d4969.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.10%3A_Grazing
642eb15d4969.sentence: A soil health study involving a wide range of New York cropping systems confirmed that pasture fields had far better scores than other cropping systems for soil organic matter content, active carbon, protein, respiration, available water capacity and aggregate stability.

a1d994126384.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.10%3A_Grazing
a1d994126384.sentence: Sometimes intensive grazing is taken to an extreme level through mob grazing, where extremely high stocking densities (100,000 pounds of animals per acre) are used for very short time periods (8–12 hours).

82452b3d0712.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.10%3A_Grazing
82452b3d0712.sentence: This approach is used as a soil amelioration technique, where animals suppress or kill poor quality plant species and with their hoofs help to reseed the paddock with more productive species.

dec221ab45fa.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.10%3A_Grazing
dec221ab45fa.sentence: In some situations animals are allowed to roam over larger rangeland areas but are stocked densely during the night time.

c280457d4be6.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.10%3A_Grazing
c280457d4be6.sentence: The carbon, nutrients and seeds gathered during the day are excreted into the smaller area and provide a significant boost for soil fertility and revegetation (as discussed with “plaggen soils” in Chapter 7).

0b8aefcd1972.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.10%3A_Grazing
0b8aefcd1972.sentence: - Grazing annual crop residue works with an annual row crop system where the grain is harvested and the residues are grazed during the dormant periods in the autumn, winter or dry season.

c9623e581e71.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.10%3A_Grazing
c9623e581e71.sentence: Although this does not meet annual feed needs, it reduces feed costs and improves nutrient and carbon cycling.

195f4dc2dd33.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.10%3A_Grazing
195f4dc2dd33.sentence: Cattle grazing of corn residue in winter is common in the Great Plains and has been shown to increase soil health and crop yields.

3068c5d241d9.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.10%3A_Grazing
3068c5d241d9.sentence: - Swath grazing involves annual crops such as barley and triticale, cut in the autumn.

8d40f6466801.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.10%3A_Grazing
8d40f6466801.sentence: They are left in swaths (heaped rows) for grazing, mostly for beef cattle (Figure 12.5).

b0e41cb13676.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.10%3A_Grazing
b0e41cb13676.sentence: Swath grazing improves forage accessibility, especially when there is deep snow, by concentrating and stacking the forage into narrow swaths.

119f77548d1f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.01%3A_Introduction
119f77548d1f.sentence: Most such farms import some or all of their feed, sometimes from far away, requiring the supplying crop farms to use large amounts of fertilizers to replace nutrients exported to the animal operations.

6eefe89ae732.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.01%3A_Introduction
6eefe89ae732.sentence: At the same time the large amounts of manure that accumulate on the animal farms—relative to their land base—may lead to applying quantities of manure that contain more nutrients than needed by crops, resulting in pollution of ground and/or surface waters.

7229422342be.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.01%3A_Introduction
7229422342be.sentence: A substantial portion of the U.S. poultry, beef and hogs is raised in huge factory-size operations (concentrated animal feeding operations, or CAFOs), but there are many problems associated with these systems.

2cbfbcad9a9d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.01%3A_Introduction
2cbfbcad9a9d.sentence: (see Chapter 7, “Nutrient Cycles and Flows” for a discussion of patterns of nutrient movement into and out of farms.) Storing large amounts of manure for periodic spreading (as occurs on CAFOs) creates a potential pollution problem and under certain conditions direct contamination of surface waters.

65c71c8cf679.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.01%3A_Introduction
65c71c8cf679.sentence: When crops are fed to animals, most nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium contained in the feeds are excreted as waste products.

97cef016e008.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.01%3A_Introduction
97cef016e008.sentence: Thus, when animal products are the main sales from the farm, relatively few nutrients (relative to what animals ate) leave the farm.

6a94d038a563.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.01%3A_Introduction
6a94d038a563.sentence: On the other hand, farms that exclusively produce annual grain crops, such as corn, soybeans, wheat and sorghum, or even vegetables, export a lot of nutrients contained in their crops.

855c221a5a31.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.01%3A_Introduction
855c221a5a31.sentence: Another issue is that farms concentrating on production of annual crops usually have no reason to include perennial forage crops in their rotations.

e261a8adede1.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.01%3A_Introduction
e261a8adede1.sentence: Exclusively growing annuals, especially only one or two crops, makes weed control more challenging, deprives the land of the improved soil health of multi-year grasses and legumes, allows disease and insect pests to flourish, and requires large amounts of nitrogen fertilizer to be applied for most crops.

4a9740b72186.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.01%3A_Introduction
4a9740b72186.sentence: Integrating livestock into the farm operation can make it more sustainable but also makes it more complex.

ffa43e491fe7.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.01%3A_Introduction
ffa43e491fe7.sentence: If not implemented in the right way it can also increase environmental problems.

a8bac00e9271.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.01%3A_Introduction
a8bac00e9271.sentence: There are major differences between the way N and P behave in soils (Figure 19.1, Table 19.1).

ded641201ed9.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.01%3A_Introduction
ded641201ed9.sentence: Nitrate, the primary form in which plants absorb nitrogen from the soil, is very mobile in soils, while P movement in soils is very limited.

ee6d0fed2066.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.01%3A_Introduction
ee6d0fed2066.sentence: But aside from legumes that can produce their own N because of the bacteria living in root nodules, crop plants get their N from decomposing organic matter.

ca8119a6ca12.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.01%3A_Introduction
ca8119a6ca12.sentence: On the other hand, there is no biological process that can add P to soils, and plants get their P from soil minerals as well as from decomposing organic matter.

c3d29dce93f4.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.01%3A_Introduction
c3d29dce93f4.sentence: Nitrogen becomes available from decomposing soil organic matter, commonly supplying about one third or more of crop uptake. N is mostly available to plants as nitrate (NO 3 –), a form that is very mobile in soils. Some ammonium (NH 4 +) and small nitrogen-containing organic molecules such as amino acids are also taken up by plants. Nitrate can be easily lost in large quantities by leaching to groundwater or by conversion to gases (N 2, N 2 O). Nitrogen can be added to soils by biological N fixation (legumes). Cover crops can store nitrogen that would otherwise be lost by leaching and denitrification, providing the N to the following crop. | Phosphorus becomes available from decomposing soil organic matter and minerals. P is relatively immobile and is only available to plants in small concentrations as dissolved phosphorus in the soil solution, mainly as H 2 PO 4 – and HPO 4 –2. P is mainly lost from soils through runoff and erosion. However, excessive fertilizer P or manure application on well-structured soils and on those with tile drainage has resulted in P loss to drainage water. No equivalent reaction can add new P to soil, although many bacteria and some fungi (especially mycorrhizae) help plants take up more P. Cover crops can mobilize P from soil and store it in their tissue, providing extra P to the following crop.

1ad4ab25c236.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.01%3A_Introduction
1ad4ab25c236.sentence: Most N loss from soils occurs when nitrate leaches, is converted into gases by the process of denitrification, or is volatilized from surface ammonium.

56545938a458.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.01%3A_Introduction
56545938a458.sentence: When water exceeds plant needs, large amounts of nitrate may leach from sandy soils, while denitrification is generally more significant in heavy loams and clays.

024029fe4e1d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.01%3A_Introduction
024029fe4e1d.sentence: On the other hand, P is lost from soils in lesser quantities when it is carried away in runoff or in sediments eroded from fields, construction sites and other exposed soil (see Figure 19.1 for a comparison between relative pathways for N and P losses).

e4661db49135.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.01%3A_Introduction
e4661db49135.sentence: But generally lower P losses are associated with higher impact per unit of nutrient on water quality, so the overall environmental concerns with both N and P are therefore significant.

d28233bb28d0.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.01%3A_Introduction
d28233bb28d0.sentence: However, small quantities of P loss have great effects on water quality because P is the nutrient that frequently limits the growth of freshwater aquatic weeds, algae and cyanobacteria (also called “blue green algae”).

dee81c6bf718.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.01%3A_Introduction
dee81c6bf718.sentence: Phosphorus leaching is a concern in fields that are artificially drained.

c9e239aa9b93.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.01%3A_Introduction
c9e239aa9b93.sentence: With many years of excessive manure or compost application, soils saturated with P (often sands with low P sorption capacity) can start leaking P with the percolating water and can discharge it through drain lines or ditches.

13bcf2036852.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.01%3A_Introduction
13bcf2036852.sentence: Also, liquid manure can move through preferential flow paths (wormholes, root holes, cracks, etc., especially in clay soils) directly to subsurface drain lines and contaminate water in ditches, which is then discharged into streams and lakes (see also Chapter 17).

cd6b99ee2729.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.03%3A_Planning_for_N_and_P_Management
cd6b99ee2729.section: Cover Crops Enhance P For Following Crop
cd6b99ee2729.sentence: Cover crops mobilize and take up a significant amount of P through mycorrhizae and other organisms of the root microbiome.

bbdb5fa1ddb0.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.03%3A_Planning_for_N_and_P_Management
bbdb5fa1ddb0.section: Cover Crops Enhance P For Following Crop
bbdb5fa1ddb0.sentence: Later, as they decompose, this P becomes available for the following crops to use.

b0b5f576c28b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.01%3A_Introduction
b0b5f576c28b.sentence: However, there are other problems associated with using more N than needed: 1) groundwater and surface water become polluted with nitrates; 2) more N2O (a potent greenhouse gas and source of ozone depletion) is produced during denitrification in soil; 3) a lot of energy is consumed in producing N, so wasting N is the same as wasting energy; 4) using higher N than needed is associated with accelerated decomposition and loss of soil organic matter; and 5) very high rates of N are frequently associated with high levels of insect damage.

a562ca592cee.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.01%3A_Introduction
a562ca592cee.sentence: In addition, the manufacture, transportation and application of N fertilizers are very energy intensive.

1b5614262b65.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.01%3A_Introduction
1b5614262b65.sentence: Of all the energy used to produce corn (including the manufacture and operation of field equipment), the manufacture and application of N fertilizer represents close to 30%.

c3941b4f9d4b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/13%3A_Making_and_Using_Composts/13.05%3A_Advantages_of_Composting
c3941b4f9d4b.sentence: Composted material is less bulky than the original feedstock, making it less costly to transport.

bb141c54d97c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/13%3A_Making_and_Using_Composts/13.05%3A_Advantages_of_Composting
bb141c54d97c.sentence: It is also easier and more pleasant to handle.

51571386c215.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/13%3A_Making_and_Using_Composts/13.05%3A_Advantages_of_Composting
51571386c215.sentence: During the composting process, carbon dioxide and water are lost to the atmosphere and the size of the pile decreases by 30–60%.

74f9ecf6adbf.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/13%3A_Making_and_Using_Composts/13.05%3A_Advantages_of_Composting
74f9ecf6adbf.sentence: In addition, many weed seeds and disease-causing organisms may be killed by the high temperatures in the pile.

ba84aadcd1ca.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/13%3A_Making_and_Using_Composts/13.05%3A_Advantages_of_Composting
ba84aadcd1ca.sentence: Flies, a common problem around manures and other organic wastes, are much less of a problem with composts.

3fd9579cae97.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/13%3A_Making_and_Using_Composts/13.05%3A_Advantages_of_Composting
3fd9579cae97.sentence: Composted material, with about half the bulk and weight of manure, and a higher commercial value, can be economically transported over significant distances to locations where nutrients are needed.

2d33205b290c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/13%3A_Making_and_Using_Composts/13.05%3A_Advantages_of_Composting
2d33205b290c.sentence: Composting reduces or eliminates the decline in nitrogen availability that commonly occurs when organic materials, such as sawdust or straw, are added directly to soil.

04fb6add4812.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/13%3A_Making_and_Using_Composts/13.05%3A_Advantages_of_Composting
04fb6add4812.sentence: Also, since making compost decreases the solubility of nutrients, composting may help lessen pollution in streams, lakes and groundwater.

ce34d9f78d23.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/13%3A_Making_and_Using_Composts/13.05%3A_Advantages_of_Composting
ce34d9f78d23.sentence: In addition, the high temperatures and biological activity during the composting process can help to decrease antibiotic levels in manures, which can be taken up by crops growing on manured land.

4d15b5bae017.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/13%3A_Making_and_Using_Composts/13.05%3A_Advantages_of_Composting
4d15b5bae017.sentence: Compost can also be stored more easily than the bulk feedstocks, so it can be applied when soil and weather conditions are optimal.

96d6d3074ebc.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/13%3A_Making_and_Using_Composts/13.05%3A_Advantages_of_Composting
96d6d3074ebc.sentence: But composting that manure makes it easier and more economical to move off a farm with excess nutrients and to help improve nearby fields, gardens and landscapes with local organic resources that would otherwise mostly be a nuisance.

cf19e4d73dbf.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/13%3A_Making_and_Using_Composts/13.05%3A_Advantages_of_Composting
cf19e4d73dbf.sentence: On many poultry farms and on beef feedlots, where high animal populations on limited land may make manure application a potential environmental problem, composting may be the best method for handling the wastes and removing the excess nutrients.

c188d29fe6ff.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/13%3A_Making_and_Using_Composts/13.05%3A_Advantages_of_Composting
c188d29fe6ff.sentence: Compared with fresh residues, composts may not stimulate as much production of the sticky gums that help hold aggregates together.

0c2227a34c1e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/13%3A_Making_and_Using_Composts/13.05%3A_Advantages_of_Composting
0c2227a34c1e.sentence: Also, some uncomposted materials have more nutrients readily available to feed plants than do composts.

ca6930fc71c8.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/13%3A_Making_and_Using_Composts/13.05%3A_Advantages_of_Composting
ca6930fc71c8.sentence: Finally, more labor and energy usually are needed to compost residues than when simply applying the uncomposted residues directly.

9094129347a3.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/13%3A_Making_and_Using_Composts/13.05%3A_Advantages_of_Composting
9094129347a3.sentence: In general, composting makes most sense when 1) the feedstock materials are difficult to handle, unsafe in the open environment, or have odor concerns (like livestock carcasses, or food processing waste), 2) the waste material cannot be used locally and needs to be transported over distances before field application (like urban tree leaves), 3) there are concerns with pathogens (like pet, zoo or human waste) or 4) there is a good market for the use of compost (like farms near urban areas).

b6f21fa264ce.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.03%3A_Planning_for_N_and_P_Management
b6f21fa264ce.sentence: Although N and P behave very differently in soils, the general approaches to their management are similar (Table 19.2).

ed114ef55e90.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.02%3A_Management_of_N_and_P
ed114ef55e90.sentence: Nitrogen and phosphorus behave very differently in soils, but many of the management strategies are actually the same or very similar.

037819bcee18.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.02%3A_Management_of_N_and_P
037819bcee18.sentence: - Take all nutrient sources into account.

3051107c21e6.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.02%3A_Management_of_N_and_P
3051107c21e6.sentence: - Use manure and compost tests to determine nutrient contributions.

e0a9df3cf7e4.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.02%3A_Management_of_N_and_P
e0a9df3cf7e4.sentence: - Consider nutrients in decomposing crop residues (for N only).

f064c0c0c7d3.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.02%3A_Management_of_N_and_P
f064c0c0c7d3.sentence: - Reduce losses and enhance uptake (use 4R-Plus principles, fertilizer application using the right rate, at the right time, in the right place, in the right amount, plus conservation practices; see Chapter 18).

e1d558a9f2bb.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.02%3A_Management_of_N_and_P
e1d558a9f2bb.sentence: - Use localized placement of fertilizers below the soil surface whenever possible.

c76f855417cd.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.02%3A_Management_of_N_and_P
c76f855417cd.sentence: - Split fertilizer application if leaching or denitrification losses are a potential problem (almost always for N only).

c94dcb00d09e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.02%3A_Management_of_N_and_P
c94dcb00d09e.sentence: - Apply nutrients when leaching or runoff threats are minimal.

46aa3193ac85.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.02%3A_Management_of_N_and_P
46aa3193ac85.sentence: Cover crops combined with minimal or no tillage is a set of practices that work well together.

fa7bb48c741e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.02%3A_Management_of_N_and_P
fa7bb48c741e.sentence: They improve soil structure; reduce the loss of nutrients through leaching, runoff and erosion; reduce denitrification loss of nitrates; and tie up N and P that otherwise might be lost between cash crops by storing these nutrients in organic forms.

e2c003253777.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.03%3A_Planning_for_N_and_P_Management
e2c003253777.sentence: Reduce tillage in order to leave residues on the surface and to decrease runoff and erosion. | Reduce tillage in order to leave residues on the surface, to decrease runoff and erosion, and to keep mycorrhizal network intact.

1e3a6c72e756.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.03%3A_Planning_for_N_and_P_Management
1e3a6c72e756.sentence: Use sod-type forage crops in rotation to reduce nitrate leaching and runoff, making N more available to following crops. | Use sod-type forage crops in rotation to reduce the amount of runoff and erosion losses of P, making P more available to the following crop.

694bcd6f9eab.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.03%3A_Planning_for_N_and_P_Management
694bcd6f9eab.sentence: Use grass cover crops, such as cereal rye, to capture soil nitrates leftover following the economic crop. | Use grass cover crops, such as cereal rye, to protect soil against erosion.

5ef3a792b061.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.03%3A_Planning_for_N_and_P_Management
5ef3a792b061.sentence: Time N applications as close to crop uptake as possible, and place to reduce runoff or gaseous losses. | Time and place P application to reduce runoff potential.

036bce052444.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.03%3A_Planning_for_N_and_P_Management
036bce052444.sentence: If you’re growing a crop for which a reliable in-season adaptive method is available, like the PSNT, a sensor or a computer model, you can hold off applying most of the fertilizer until the crop indicates a need.

5bcb6895dec3.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.03%3A_Planning_for_N_and_P_Management
5bcb6895dec3.sentence: At that point, apply N as a sidedress or topdress.

16a286e9b200.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/13%3A_Making_and_Using_Composts/13.02%3A_Making_Composts
16a286e9b200.sentence: Oxygen moves into the pile while carbon dioxide, moisture and heat rise out of it.

1d09a3b156bf.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/13%3A_Making_and_Using_Composts/13.02%3A_Making_Composts
1d09a3b156bf.sentence: The materials need to fit together in a way that allows oxygen from the air to flow in freely.

2456d014dd58.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/13%3A_Making_and_Using_Composts/13.02%3A_Making_Composts
2456d014dd58.sentence: On the other hand, it is also important that not too much heat escapes from the center of the pile.

607a46a84832.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/13%3A_Making_and_Using_Composts/13.02%3A_Making_Composts
607a46a84832.sentence: If small sizes of organic materials are used, a “bulking agent” may be needed to make sure that enough air can enter the pile.
