79edd15ddfe6.section: Fixed and Adaptive Methods for Estimating Crop N Needs
79edd15ddfe6.sentence: Pre-plant nitrate and labile N tests measure soil nitrate, soil nitrate plus ammonium, or readily available organic nitrogen in the soil early in the season to guide N fertilizer applications at planting.

0c6848d09951.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.02%3A_Management_of_N_and_P
0c6848d09951.section: Fixed and Adaptive Methods for Estimating Crop N Needs
0c6848d09951.sentence: These approaches are more effective in drier climates, like in the U.S. Great Plains where seasonal gains of inorganic forms of N are more predictable and losses from leaching or denitrification are generally minimal.

7c0e687cf615.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.02%3A_Management_of_N_and_P
7c0e687cf615.section: Fixed and Adaptive Methods for Estimating Crop N Needs
7c0e687cf615.sentence: These approaches cannot incorporate the seasonal weather effects, as the samples are analyzed prior to the growing season, which inherently limits its precision compared to the PSNT.

ee29512ce2a7.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.02%3A_Management_of_N_and_P
ee29512ce2a7.section: Fixed and Adaptive Methods for Estimating Crop N Needs
ee29512ce2a7.sentence: Leaf chlorophyll meters that measure light transmission in leaves and satellite, aerial, drone or tractor-mounted sensors that determine light reflection from leaves are used for assessing leaf or canopy N status and biomass, which can then guide sidedress N applications.

5460f0dfd7e5.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.02%3A_Management_of_N_and_P
5460f0dfd7e5.section: Fixed and Adaptive Methods for Estimating Crop N Needs
5460f0dfd7e5.sentence: Environmental information systems and dynamic simulation models are now also being employed for N management, with successful applications for wheat and corn.

ce741ee456d6.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.02%3A_Management_of_N_and_P
ce741ee456d6.section: Fixed and Adaptive Methods for Estimating Crop N Needs
ce741ee456d6.sentence: This approach takes advantage of increasingly sophisticated environmental databases, such as radar-based, high-resolution precipitation estimates and detailed soil databases, and can be used to provide input information for computer models.

01b24445d1f5.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.02%3A_Management_of_N_and_P
01b24445d1f5.sentence: Available N in soil depends on recent weather.

26a53a983a38.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.02%3A_Management_of_N_and_P
26a53a983a38.sentence: The need for supplemental N fertilizer depends on early season weather.

1b023d32b161.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.02%3A_Management_of_N_and_P
1b023d32b161.sentence: After increasing for a period, mineral N decreases during a wet spring because leaching and denitrification losses are greater than N being converted to mineral forms.

abc54fe1f71e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.02%3A_Management_of_N_and_P
abc54fe1f71e.sentence: More mineral N is available for plants when the spring is drier.

4f2722db74e3.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.02%3A_Management_of_N_and_P
4f2722db74e3.sentence: Mineral forms of N begin to accumulate in soil in the spring but may be lost by leaching and denitrification during a very wet period (Figure 19.2).

6311b75a2612.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.02%3A_Management_of_N_and_P
6311b75a2612.sentence: These processes are greatly dependent on soil organic matter contents, additional N contributions from organic amendments, and weather-related factors like soil temperature (higher temperatures increase N mineralization) and soil wetness (saturated soils cause large leaching and denitrification losses, especially when soils are warm).

cbe5c82f1e86.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.02%3A_Management_of_N_and_P
cbe5c82f1e86.sentence: The primary reason is that the amounts of plant-available N, mostly nitrate, can fluctuate rapidly as organic matter is mineralized and as N is lost through leaching or denitrification.

6cdc22a32c0d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.02%3A_Management_of_N_and_P
6cdc22a32c0d.sentence: When plants germinate in the spring, it takes a while until they begin to grow rapidly and take up a lot of N (Figure 19.3).

f51f6d71c70d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.02%3A_Management_of_N_and_P
f51f6d71c70d.sentence: In years with unusually wet weather in the spring, an extra amount of sidedress (or topdress) N may be needed to compensate for relatively high mineral N loss from soil (Figure 19.3).

a0b9ac9dfab8.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.02%3A_Management_of_N_and_P
a0b9ac9dfab8.sentence: Research on corn in Minnesota from 2015 to 2019—where 75 percent of the sites evaluated had one month during the growing season with 150 percent of normal rainfall—indicated using sidedress N with some N applied before planting didn't decrease yields and actually increased yields by an average of 11 bushels an acre in a quarter of situations.

7effa4024bf6.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.02%3A_Management_of_N_and_P
7effa4024bf6.sentence: On the other hand, in dry years, especially drought spells during the critical pollination period, yields will be reduced, and the N uptake and needed N fertilizer are therefore lower (not shown in Figure 19.3).

4c3fe88ba729.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.02%3A_Management_of_N_and_P
4c3fe88ba729.sentence: However, you really don’t know at normal sidedress time whether there will be a drought during pollination, so there is no way to adjust for that.

415d98074a47.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.02%3A_Management_of_N_and_P
415d98074a47.sentence: Since most plant-available P in soils is relatively strongly adsorbed by organic matter and clay minerals, estimating P availability is routinely done through soil tests.

949d4fddd9ee.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.02%3A_Management_of_N_and_P
949d4fddd9ee.sentence: Estimating N fertilizer needs is more complex, and soil tests generally cannot provide all the answers.

1151412d03e2.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.11%3A_Potential_Problems_Using_Manures
1151412d03e2.sentence: When manures are applied regularly to a field to provide enough nitrogen for a crop like corn, phosphorus and potassium build up to levels way in excess of crop needs (see Table 12.2).

95d61166cf06.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.11%3A_Potential_Problems_Using_Manures
95d61166cf06.sentence: It is often mistakenly believed that it results from the fact that manure nutrient ratios are out of balance with crop uptake requirements (especially more P).

933dd6e537c8.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.11%3A_Potential_Problems_Using_Manures
933dd6e537c8.sentence: Nutrient ratios for most manures (Table 12.1) are actually equivalent to a crop’s needs (roughly a 2:1 ratio for nitrogen and phosphorus).

0776c9e80864.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.11%3A_Potential_Problems_Using_Manures
0776c9e80864.sentence: If most nitrogen was conserved through good timing and application methods—applied immediately prior to the growing season or in a standing crop, and injected or incorporated—the manure rate necessary to meet crop nitrogen requirement can be substantially lowered and the accumulation of P and K in soil reduced!

ba1ea27b9899.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.11%3A_Potential_Problems_Using_Manures
ba1ea27b9899.sentence: When soil P levels have already built up and manure applications are restricted based on allowed P additions, as required by some nutrient management plans, N-conserving management means that less fertilizer N will be needed.

28753976be55.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.11%3A_Potential_Problems_Using_Manures
28753976be55.sentence: Erosion of phosphorus-rich topsoils contributes sediments and P to streams and lakes, polluting surface waters.

a8764f19be05.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.11%3A_Potential_Problems_Using_Manures
a8764f19be05.sentence: When very high P buildup occurs, it may also be wise to switch the application to other fields or to use strict soil conservation practices to trap sediments before they enter a stream.

606ed96b3ab8.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.11%3A_Potential_Problems_Using_Manures
606ed96b3ab8.sentence: Including rotation crops that do not need manure for N, such as alfalfa, allows a “draw-down” of phosphorus that accumulates from manure application to grains.

cf9274b8494c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.03%3A_Planning_for_N_and_P_Management
cf9274b8494c.section: Using Organic Sources of Phosphorus and Potassium
cf9274b8494c.sentence: After many years of continuous application of these sources to meet N needs, soil test levels for P and potassium may be in the excessive range.

b608a6c8afc3.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.03%3A_Planning_for_N_and_P_Management
b608a6c8afc3.section: Using Organic Sources of Phosphorus and Potassium
b608a6c8afc3.sentence: Although there are a number of ways to deal with this issue, all solutions require reduced applications of fertilizer P and P-containing organic amendments.

d17645ca133a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.03%3A_Planning_for_N_and_P_Management
d17645ca133a.section: Using Organic Sources of Phosphorus and Potassium
d17645ca133a.sentence: If it’s a farm-wide problem, some manure may need to be exported and N fertilizer or legumes relied on to provide N to grain crops.

5a27934b4042.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.03%3A_Planning_for_N_and_P_Management
5a27934b4042.section: Using Organic Sources of Phosphorus and Potassium
5a27934b4042.sentence: Sometimes, it’s just a question of better distribution of manure around the various fields: getting to those fields far from the barn more regularly.

8fad60213a98.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.03%3A_Planning_for_N_and_P_Management
8fad60213a98.section: Using Organic Sources of Phosphorus and Potassium
8fad60213a98.sentence: Changing the rotation to include crops such as alfalfa, for which no manure N is needed, can help.

15110eeb1137.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.03%3A_Planning_for_N_and_P_Management
15110eeb1137.section: Using Organic Sources of Phosphorus and Potassium
15110eeb1137.sentence: However, if you’re raising livestock on a limited land base, you should make arrangements to have the manure used on a neighboring farm or sell the manure to a composting facility.

150f83747e7b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.04%3A_Managing_High-P_Soils
150f83747e7b.sentence: High-P soils occur because of a history of either excessive applications of P fertilizers or, more commonly, application of lots of manure.

90769ad5157a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.04%3A_Managing_High-P_Soils
90769ad5157a.sentence: This is a problem on livestock farms with limited land and where a medium-to-high percentage of feed is imported.

61c03b3f4b61.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.04%3A_Managing_High-P_Soils
61c03b3f4b61.sentence: The nutrients imported in feeds may greatly exceed the nutrients exported in animal products.

d19add4365b7.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.04%3A_Managing_High-P_Soils
d19add4365b7.sentence: In addition, where manures or composts are used at recommended rates for providing sufficient N to crops, more P than needed usually is added.

b0447eacb3f9.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.04%3A_Managing_High-P_Soils
b0447eacb3f9.sentence: However, it is especially important to reduce the risk of environmental harm from those high-P soils that are also likely to produce significant runoff (because of slope, fine texture, poor structure or poor drainage).

085d42514e01.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.04%3A_Managing_High-P_Soils
085d42514e01.sentence: If the farm is near a critical water resource that is impacted by field runoff or tile drainage, aggressive measures are needed to reduce the impact.

c416d3c2c7d4.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.04%3A_Managing_High-P_Soils
c416d3c2c7d4.sentence: Conversely, small vegetable operations or urban farms on flat ground where fields are surrounded by grass berms or alleyways pose much lower risk, and high soil-P levels are generally more acceptable.

e7ac53cce6fa.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.04%3A_Managing_High-P_Soils
e7ac53cce6fa.sentence: - First, deal with the “front end” and reduce animal P intake to the lowest levels needed.

c6918d8ee39d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.04%3A_Managing_High-P_Soils
c6918d8ee39d.sentence: Not that long ago a survey found that the average dairy herd in the United States was fed about 25% more P than recommended by the standard authority (the National Research Council, or NRC).

ed50fff58a10.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.04%3A_Managing_High-P_Soils
ed50fff58a10.sentence: - Second, reduce or eliminate applications of extra P. For a livestock farm, this may mean obtaining the use of more land to grow crops, to spread manure over a larger land area, or to swap fields with nearby farms that don’t have high-P problems.

7412ba5be2b5.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.04%3A_Managing_High-P_Soils
7412ba5be2b5.sentence: For a crop farm, this may mean using legume cover crops and forages in rotations to supply N without adding P. The cover crops and forage rotation crops are also helpful to build up and maintain good organic matter levels in the absence of importing manures or composts, or other organic material from off the farm.

8d7d441a8768.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.04%3A_Managing_High-P_Soils
8d7d441a8768.sentence: Also, don’t use a high-P source to meet N demands.

44a93222b19e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.04%3A_Managing_High-P_Soils
44a93222b19e.sentence: Compost has many benefits, but if used to provide N fertility, it will build up P over the long term.

296b69a1a156.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.04%3A_Managing_High-P_Soils
296b69a1a156.sentence: - Third, reduce runoff and erosion to minimal levels.

6fcd8d287533.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.04%3A_Managing_High-P_Soils
6fcd8d287533.sentence: Anything that helps water infiltration or impedes water and sediments from leaving the field—reduced tillage, strip cropping along the contour, cover crops, grassed waterways, riparian buffer strips, etc.—decreases problems caused by high-P soils.

80dd1bd1d249.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.04%3A_Managing_High-P_Soils
80dd1bd1d249.sentence: (Note: Significant P losses in tile drainage water have been observed, especially from fields where large amounts of liquid manure are applied.)

d315291c7278.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.04%3A_Managing_High-P_Soils
d315291c7278.sentence: Soil-test P will slowly decrease over the years once P imports, in the form of fertilizers, organic amendments or feeds, are reduced or eliminated.

211d0d994eac.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.04%3A_Managing_High-P_Soils
211d0d994eac.sentence: Soils should be tested every two to three years for other reasons, anyway.

82bfdcf2cbb1.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.04%3A_Managing_High-P_Soils
82bfdcf2cbb1.sentence: Phosphorus accumulates especially rapidly in the surface of no-till soils that have received large applications of manure or fertilizer over the years.

b3f2241cdce2.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.04%3A_Managing_High-P_Soils
b3f2241cdce2.sentence: One management option in these cases is a one-time tillage of the soil to incorporate the high-P soil layer.

8a2be0a03d4b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.04%3A_Managing_High-P_Soils
8a2be0a03d4b.sentence: If this is done, use practices that don’t result in building up surface soil P once again, such as applying P as starter near the seed and injection (especially liquid manure) instead of broadcast applications.

7ba8ff8d7315.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.04%3A_Managing_High-P_Soils
7ba8ff8d7315.sentence: Using so much extra can cost dairy farmers thousands of dollars to feed a 100-cow herd supplemental P that the animals don’t need and that ends up as a potential pollutant.

ab8ba09ef49e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/13%3A_Making_and_Using_Composts/13.04%3A_Using_Composts
ab8ba09ef49e.sentence: Research by Harry Hoitink and coworkers at Ohio State University shows that composts can suppress root and leaf diseases of plants.

aece6ce69ff6.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/13%3A_Making_and_Using_Composts/13.04%3A_Using_Composts
aece6ce69ff6.sentence: This suppression comes about because the plants are generally healthier (microorganisms produce plant hormones as well as chelates that make micronutrients more available) and are therefore better able to resist infection.

2c87113e5792.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/13%3A_Making_and_Using_Composts/13.04%3A_Using_Composts
2c87113e5792.sentence: Beneficial organisms compete with disease organisms for nutrients and either directly consume the disease-causing organisms or produce antibiotics that kill bacteria.

0d381fa05b20.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/13%3A_Making_and_Using_Composts/13.04%3A_Using_Composts
0d381fa05b20.sentence: Some organisms, such as springtails and mites, “actually search out pathogen propagules in soils and devour them,” according to Hoitink.

ecbae9d149b0.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/13%3A_Making_and_Using_Composts/13.04%3A_Using_Composts
ecbae9d149b0.sentence: In addition, Hoitink found that potting mixes containing composts “rich in biodegradable organic matter support microorganisms that induce systemic resistance in plants.

04be080aac54.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/13%3A_Making_and_Using_Composts/13.04%3A_Using_Composts
04be080aac54.sentence: These plants have elevated levels of biochemical activity relative to disease control and are better prepared to defend themselves against diseases.” This includes resistance to both root and leaf diseases.

15cf05a1febe.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/13%3A_Making_and_Using_Composts/13.04%3A_Using_Composts
15cf05a1febe.sentence: Composts rich in available nitrogen may actually stimulate certain diseases, as was found for phytophthora root rot on soybeans, as well as for fusarium wilts and fire blight on other crops.

0af016ffd7ab.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/13%3A_Making_and_Using_Composts/13.04%3A_Using_Composts
0af016ffd7ab.sentence: Applying these composts many months before cropping, allowing the salts to leach away, or blending them with low-nitrogen composts prior to application, reduces the risk of stimulating diseases.

080f492dd1c7.title: Liquid manure
080f492dd1c7.sentence: Liquid manure is a mixture of animal waste and organic matter used as an agricultural fertilizer, sometimes thinned with water.

c34fe47e1ffd.title: Liquid manure
c34fe47e1ffd.sentence: It can be aged in a slurry pit to concentrate it.

9b1b42b2c4c2.title: Liquid manure
9b1b42b2c4c2.sentence: Liquid manure was developed in the 20th-century as an alternative to fermented manure.

39a078299fe3.title: Liquid manure
39a078299fe3.sentence: Manure in both forms is used as a nutrient-enriched fertilizer for plants, containing high levels of nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium present in farm animals' excretions and originating from the food they consume.

418bc2dfd28a.title: Liquid manure
418bc2dfd28a.sentence: Current American fertilizer practice dates back to the Post–World War II economic expansion era.

96149e4cd79c.title: Liquid manure
96149e4cd79c.sentence: Powerful motorised tractors allowed farmers to haul large, heavy tanks on trailers around their fields, allowing liquids such as liquid manure to be easily and evenly applied near the plant root.

a508fd3daf57.title: Liquid manure
a508fd3daf57.sentence: Particular attention is paid to concentrated animal feeding operations (CAFOs) because they are the source of most of the liquid manure that is spread on fields of vegetables in the United States.

38a2a157861a.title: Liquid manure
38a2a157861a.sentence: Since at least 1982, health authorities have recognised that the O157:H7 bacteria, which has been responsible for significant numbers of human deaths, spreads through fecal transmission.

eabd81aebba3.title: Liquid manure
eabd81aebba3.sentence: Rainwater runoff from these CAFOs was identified in the fatal Walkerton E. coli outbreak as the contaminant of municipal wellwater used for human consumption.

1bcefbf0baa9.title: Landfill leachate
1bcefbf0baa9.sentence: Landfill leachate is contaminated liquid formed when rain or another source of water enters a landfill and comes in contact with waste, which may then flow into and contaminate local groundwater if not properly managed.

5368c7115374.title: Landfill leachate
5368c7115374.sentence: The generation of leachate is caused principally by precipitation percolating through waste deposited in a landfill.

e7cd20ca6044.title: Landfill leachate
e7cd20ca6044.sentence: Landfill leachate varies widely in composition depending on the age of the landfill and the type of waste that it contains.

eed4a2506b79.title: Landfill leachate
eed4a2506b79.sentence: It usually contains both dissolved and suspended material.

1d71de616a44.title: Landfill leachate
1d71de616a44.sentence: Additional leachate volume is produced during this decomposition of carbonaceous material producing a wide range of other materials including methane, carbon dioxide and a complex mixture of organic acids, aldehydes, alcohols and simple sugars.

9163e14538b8.title: Landfill leachate
9163e14538b8.sentence: The risks of leachate generation can be mitigated by properly designed and engineered landfill sites, such as those that are constructed on geologically impermeable materials or sites that use impermeable liners made of geomembranes or engineered clay.

f7eeab4d8b6b.title: Landfill leachate
f7eeab4d8b6b.sentence: In a 2012 survey performed in New York State, all surveyed double-lined landfill cells had leakage rates of less than 500 liters per hectare per day.

6e6788c3a9da.title: Laterite
6e6788c3a9da.sentence: A study, using both laboratory tests and pilot-scale constructed wetlands, reports the effectiveness of granular laterite in removing phosphorus and heavy metals from landfill leachate.

09dc09f9638b.title: Fertilizer
09dc09f9638b.sentence: Management of soil fertility has preoccupied farmers since the beginning of agriculture.

a57fdec515c6.title: Fertilizer
a57fdec515c6.sentence: However, starting in the 19th century, after innovations in plant nutrition following Justus von Liebig's discoveries, an agricultural industry developed around synthetically created agrochemical fertilizers.

a4516bbaf471.title: History of fertilizer
a4516bbaf471.sentence: Although it was previously thought that the concept of fertilizer use may have only dated back 2,000 to 3,000 years, it is now believed that early farmers were using manure to fertilize their crops as long as 8,000 years ago.

9b673b396e07.title: History of fertilizer
9b673b396e07.sentence: Egyptians, Romans, Babylonians, and early Germans all are recorded as using minerals and/or manure to enhance the productivity of their farms.

a91e2016f07e.title: History of fertilizer
a91e2016f07e.sentence: In the Andes, they used guano for at least 1500 years, before the European countries started importing it in the 19th century for their increasing demands due to the industrial revolution.

2757d6dff380.title: History of fertilizer
2757d6dff380.sentence: In this century, "guano" was taken in large quantities from Peru and Chile (and later also from Namibia and other areas) to Europe and the USA, motivating the War of the Pacific between Peru, Chile and Bolivia.

6ec22fb122a8.title: Fertilizer
6ec22fb122a8.sentence: The scientific research of plant nutrition started well before the work of German chemist Justus von Liebig although his name is most mentioned as the "father of the fertilizer industry".

6ac80a55df45.title: History of fertilizer
6ac80a55df45.section: Key men in Europe and their inventions > Justus von Liebig
6ac80a55df45.sentence: His influential works first denounced the Albrecht Thaer theory of humus, arguing first the importance of ammonia, and later promoting the importance of inorganic minerals to plant nutrition.

b8f693d93287.title: Fertilizer
b8f693d93287.sentence: John Bennet Lawes, an English entrepreneur, began experimenting on the effects of various manures on plants growing in pots in 1837, and a year or two later the experiments were extended to crops in the field.

c9e1ed37981b.title: Fertilizer
c9e1ed37981b.sentence: One immediate consequence was that in 1842 he patented a manure formed by treating phosphates with sulfuric acid, and thus was the first to create the artificial manure industry.

277bad1a7e7f.title: History of fertilizer
277bad1a7e7f.section: Key men in Europe and their inventions > Sir John Bennet Lawes
277bad1a7e7f.sentence: In the succeeding year he enlisted the services of Joseph Henry Gilbert, who had studied under Liebig at the University of Giessen, as director of research at the Rothamsted Experimental Station which he founded on his estate.

2cf160d918e6.title: History of fertilizer
2cf160d918e6.section: Key men in Europe and their inventions > Sir John Bennet Lawes
2cf160d918e6.sentence: To this day, the Rothamsted research station the pair founded still investigates the impact of inorganic and organic fertilizers on crop yields.

ce45e199d560.title: Fertilizer
ce45e199d560.sentence: The Birkeland–Eyde process was one of the competing industrial processes at the beginning of nitrogen-based fertilizer production.

2ffeb9a9ace8.title: Fertilizer
2ffeb9a9ace8.sentence: This process was used to fix atmospheric nitrogen (N2) into nitric acid (HNO3), one of several chemical processes called nitrogen fixation.

5bad96532e12.title: Fertilizer
5bad96532e12.sentence: The 1910s and 1920s witnessed the rise of the Haber process and the Ostwald process.

db8091b54a99.title: Fertilizer
db8091b54a99.sentence: In the latter half of the 20th century, increased use of nitrogen fertilizers (800% increase between 1961 and 2019) has been a crucial component of the increased productivity of conventional food systems as part of the so-called "Green Revolution".

4bce3aeaa724.title: Fertilizer
4bce3aeaa724.sentence: The use of phosphate fertilizers has also increased from 9 million tonnes per year in 1960 to 40 million tonnes per year in 2000, but future phosphorus fertilizer availability is now a critical issue.

cdd72b14c975.title: Labeling of fertilizer
cdd72b14c975.sentence: The values in an NPK fertilizer label are related to the concentrations (by weight) of phosphorus and potassium elements as follows:

1e6f0d698d0f.title: Labeling of fertilizer
1e6f0d698d0f.sentence: - P 2O 5 consists of 56.4% elemental oxygen and 43.6% elemental phosphorus by weight.

5a1a77c736ac.title: Labeling of fertilizer
5a1a77c736ac.sentence: Therefore, the elemental phosphorus percentage of a fertilizer is 0.436 times its P value.

a4bf1cd23fdd.title: Labeling of fertilizer
a4bf1cd23fdd.sentence: - K 2O consists of 17% oxygen and 83% elemental potassium by weight.

dcd67c6ddea4.title: Labeling of fertilizer
dcd67c6ddea4.sentence: Therefore, the elemental potassium percentage is 0.83 times the K value.

2b6f17d587c9.title: Labeling of fertilizer
2b6f17d587c9.sentence: The N value in NPK labels represents actual percentage of nitrogen element by weight, so it does not need to be converted.

9f98535a2284.title: Labeling of fertilizer
9f98535a2284.sentence: So, for example, an 18−51−20 fertilizer contains by weight

0a003387bc44.title: Labeling of fertilizer
0a003387bc44.sentence: Therefore, pure KCl is 39.09/(39.09 + 35.45) = 52% potassium and 48% chlorine by weight.

8502e1438a5f.title: Labeling of fertilizer
8502e1438a5f.sentence: Pure KCl fertilizer would thus be labeled 0-0-63.

1e9de8cdf881.title: Labeling of fertilizer
1e9de8cdf881.sentence: Since sylvite contains other compounds that contribute no N, P, or K, it is usually labeled 0-0-60.

4299425f01bd.title: Ecological sanitation
4299425f01bd.sentence: Ecological sanitation, commonly abbreviated as ecosan (also spelled eco-san or EcoSan), and also known as circular sanitation as a reference to the circular economy, is an approach to sanitation provision which aims to safely reuse excreta in agriculture.

4be65c8d53a2.title: Ecological sanitation
4be65c8d53a2.sentence: It is an approach, rather than a technology or a device which is characterized by a desire to "close the loop", mainly for the nutrients and organic matter between sanitation and agriculture in a safe manner.

0ca178a61d42.title: Ecological sanitation
0ca178a61d42.sentence: The most common technology used in ecosan systems is the urine-diverting dry toilet, but ecosan systems can also use other technologies, such as vacuum toilets coupled with biogas plants, constructed wetlands, composting toilets and so forth.

b02ae894b1d6.title: Ecological sanitation
b02ae894b1d6.sentence: However, the ecosan concept should not be limited to one particular type of toilet.

a61c377f8c26.title: Ecological sanitation
a61c377f8c26.section: Overview > Resource recovery > Reuse as fertilizer
a61c377f8c26.sentence: Agricultural trials around the world have shown measurable benefits of using treated excreta in agriculture as a fertilizer and soil conditioner.

82faddbb7c73.title: Ecological sanitation
82faddbb7c73.section: Overview > Resource recovery > Reuse as fertilizer
82faddbb7c73.sentence: This applies in particular to the use of urine.

bf17ff68257d.title: Ecological sanitation
bf17ff68257d.sentence: Another aspect that ecosan systems are trying to address is the possible upcoming shortage of phosphorus.

eccc839b6df0.title: Ecological sanitation
eccc839b6df0.sentence: One review of global phosphate supply suggested that if collected, phosphate in urine could supply 22% of the total demand.

89414a5918aa.title: Ecological sanitation
89414a5918aa.sentence: The safety of ecosan systems in terms of pathogen destruction during the various treatment processes is a continuous topic of debate between proponents and opponents of ecosan systems.

0e795a0b544b.title: Ecological sanitation
0e795a0b544b.sentence: However, the publication of the WHO Guidelines on Reuse, with its multiple barrier concept, has gone a long way in establishing a common framework for safe reuse.

d10db5ea2f57.title: Ecological sanitation
d10db5ea2f57.sentence: The term "ecosan" was first used in 1995 and the first project started in 1996 in Ethiopia, by an NGO called Sudea.

4df0244eca41.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.03%3A_Manure
4df0244eca41.sentence: The economic contribution of farm manures can be considerable.

d0d86097906f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.03%3A_Manure
d0d86097906f.sentence: Once cheap fertilizers became widely available after World War II, many farmers, Extension agents and scientists looked down their noses at manure.

f0c4ccb1dd6e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.03%3A_Manure
f0c4ccb1dd6e.sentence: People thought more about how to get rid of manure than how to put it to good use.

6f16fa8461cd.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.03%3A_Manure
6f16fa8461cd.sentence: We now know that manure, like money, is better spread around than concentrated in a few places.

e78365349887.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.03%3A_Manure
e78365349887.sentence: On a national basis, the manure from 100 million cattle, 120 million hogs and 9 billion chickens contains about 23 million tons of nitrogen (and this doesn’t even include the manure from 324 million layers and 250 million turkeys).

aad70bc2ec25.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.03%3A_Manure
aad70bc2ec25.sentence: The value of the nutrients in manure from a 100-cow dairy farm may exceed $20,000 per year; manure from a 100-sow farrow-to-finish operation is worth about $16,000; and manure from a 20,000 bird broiler operation is worth about $6,000.

c1ffe7206094.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.03%3A_Manure
c1ffe7206094.sentence: The benefits to soil organic matter buildup, such as enhanced soil structure, and better diversity and activity of soil organisms, may double the value of the manure.

3a70f90fa876.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.06%3A_Chemical_Characteristics_of_Manures
3a70f90fa876.sentence: A high percentage of the nutrients in feeds passes right through animals and ends up in their manure.

974175ba6aaa.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.06%3A_Chemical_Characteristics_of_Manures
974175ba6aaa.sentence: These nutrients are available for recycling on cropland.

44c594096edc.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.06%3A_Chemical_Characteristics_of_Manures
44c594096edc.sentence: Depending on the feed ration and animal type, over 70% of the nitrogen, 60% of the phosphorus and 80% of the potassium fed may pass through the animal as manure.

b419a6b9303e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.06%3A_Chemical_Characteristics_of_Manures
b419a6b9303e.sentence: In addition to the nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium contributions given in Table 12.1, manures contain significant amounts of other nutrients, such as calcium, magnesium and sulfur.

c82406209131.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.06%3A_Chemical_Characteristics_of_Manures
c82406209131.sentence: For example, in regions that tend to lack the micronutrient zinc, there is rarely any crop deficiency found on soils receiving regular manure applications.

ec16cdaf239b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.06%3A_Chemical_Characteristics_of_Manures
ec16cdaf239b.sentence: Differences in feeds, mineral supplements, bedding materials and storage systems make manure analyses quite variable.

04c0518bd8c6.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.06%3A_Chemical_Characteristics_of_Manures
04c0518bd8c6.sentence: Manure analysis is of critical importance for routine manure use and should be a routine part of the nutrient management program on animal-based farms.

329889e2d945.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.06%3A_Chemical_Characteristics_of_Manures
329889e2d945.sentence: For example, while the average liquid dairy manure is around 25 pounds of N per 1,000 gallons, there are manures that might be 10 pounds N or less, or 40 pounds N or more, per 1,000 gallons.

417e8a7187b8.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.06%3A_Chemical_Characteristics_of_Manures
417e8a7187b8.sentence: Poultry manure is significantly higher in nitrogen and phosphorus than the other manure types.

9a8ed2204a83.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/13%3A_Making_and_Using_Composts/13.03%3A_Other_Composting_Techniques
9a8ed2204a83.sentence: Instead of making piles, small farmers in developing countries often dig pits for composting (Figure 13.4), especially in dry and hot climates.

7bdb7b49dbbe.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/13%3A_Making_and_Using_Composts/13.03%3A_Other_Composting_Techniques
7bdb7b49dbbe.sentence: Many home composters prefer using vessels to facilitate the turning process, to have better control over temperature and moisture conditions, and to keep out rodents.

f83ebb96f2d2.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/13%3A_Making_and_Using_Composts/13.03%3A_Other_Composting_Techniques
f83ebb96f2d2.sentence: The pits can be covered with soil material to prevent animals from getting into them, and they retain moisture in the compost material better.

eeaa9c466610.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/13%3A_Making_and_Using_Composts/13.03%3A_Other_Composting_Techniques
eeaa9c466610.sentence: But these systems are generally not economical for large-scale commercial operations.

a28437ac5aa9.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.02%3A_Types_of_Crop-Livestock_Farms
a28437ac5aa9.sentence: There are two general types of integrated livestock-crop farms in which all or nearly all of the animal feed is grown on the farm.

180ddb3c8812.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.02%3A_Types_of_Crop-Livestock_Farms
180ddb3c8812.sentence: There are those that mainly sell animal products and match their animal numbers to the carrying capacity of their land.

d17a7025ea2b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.02%3A_Types_of_Crop-Livestock_Farms
d17a7025ea2b.sentence: They produce all or almost all of the feed needed for their own animals.

be3810e93772.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.02%3A_Types_of_Crop-Livestock_Farms
be3810e93772.sentence: Examples of these farms are beef operations based on pasture grazing and stored hay from the farm (“grass-fed”); hog farms with animals on pasture and supplemental feed produced on the farm; and dairy farms that produce all needed grain and forage, some relying on pastures for seasonal forage needs.

a38297a62fc1.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.02%3A_Types_of_Crop-Livestock_Farms
a38297a62fc1.sentence: Second, there are diversified farms that raise all the feed for their animals but sell a range of crops and animal products.

7a41ccf93bfa.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.02%3A_Types_of_Crop-Livestock_Farms
7a41ccf93bfa.sentence: Having a number of marketable products provides some protection against the seasonal failure of a single product and the vagaries of market price fluctuations.

62935ed00bf5.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.02%3A_Types_of_Crop-Livestock_Farms
62935ed00bf5.sentence: Crops can be fed to animals and manures are returned to the soil, thereby providing a continuous supply of organic materials.

957ae9f7febb.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.02%3A_Types_of_Crop-Livestock_Farms
957ae9f7febb.sentence: For many livestock operations, perennial forage crops are an integral part of the cropping system, thereby reducing erosion potential and helping maintain or increase soil organic matter while improving soil physical and biological properties.

9d4aa9008eb3.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.05%3A_Manure_Handling_Systems
9d4aa9008eb3.sentence: The type of barn on the dairy farm farmstead frequently determines how manure is handled.

7967193da252.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.05%3A_Manure_Handling_Systems
7967193da252.sentence: Dairy cow manure containing a fair amount of bedding, usually around 20% dry matter or higher, is spread as a solid.

e560c6e40053.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.05%3A_Manure_Handling_Systems
e560c6e40053.sentence: Liquid manure-handling systems are common where animals are kept in a “free stall” barn and minimal bedding is added to the manure.

a2a7e7e29bad.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.05%3A_Manure_Handling_Systems
a2a7e7e29bad.sentence: Liquid manure is usually in the range of 2–12% dry matter (88% or more water), with the lower dry matter if water is flushed from alleys and passed through a liquid-solid separator or if large amounts of runoff enter the storage lagoon.

cd10c29757dd.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.05%3A_Manure_Handling_Systems
cd10c29757dd.sentence: Manures with characteristics between solid and liquid, with dry matter of 12–20%, are usually referred to as semi-solid.

86e690f028f8.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.05%3A_Manure_Handling_Systems
86e690f028f8.sentence: Pasture cow manure is unmixed with water or bedding and falls into this category.

e9c9202566bb.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.05%3A_Manure_Handling_Systems
e9c9202566bb.sentence: With this, you help stabilize nutrients (although considerable ammonium is usually lost in the process), have a smaller amount of material to spread, and have a more pleasant material to spread, which is a big plus if neighbors have complained about manure odors.

da39808ade80.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.05%3A_Manure_Handling_Systems
da39808ade80.sentence: Separating the liquid allows for direct composting of the solids without any added materials.

0403f8e0403c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.05%3A_Manure_Handling_Systems
0403f8e0403c.sentence: It also allows for easier transport of the solid portion of the manure for sale or to apply to remote fields.

0a61ec5abe9f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.05%3A_Manure_Handling_Systems
0a61ec5abe9f.sentence: However, with composting barns, the manure is stirred or turned twice daily with a modified cultivator on a skid steer loader or with a small tractor to a depth of 8–10 inches; ceiling fans are sometimes used to help aerate and dry the pack during each milking.

400d5a5f8b4c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.05%3A_Manure_Handling_Systems
400d5a5f8b4c.sentence: In the spring and fall some or all of the bedding can be removed and spread directly or can be built into a traditional compost pile for finishing.

c972cc45deac.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.05%3A_Manure_Handling_Systems
c972cc45deac.sentence: More recently, vermicomposting has been introduced as a way to process dairy manure.

70d1045abea6.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.05%3A_Manure_Handling_Systems
70d1045abea6.sentence: In this case, worms digest the manure, and the castings provide a high-quality soil amendment (see Chapter 13).

e00cfe489e0d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.05%3A_Manure_Handling_Systems
e00cfe489e0d.sentence: The larger, more industrial-scale farms mainly use little to no bedding, with slatted floors over the manure pit, and they keep the animals clean by frequently washing the floors.

1cc01dd58d72.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.05%3A_Manure_Handling_Systems
1cc01dd58d72.sentence: The liquid manure is held in ponds for spreading, mostly in the spring before crops are planted, and in the fall after crops have been harvested.

6ed25b8fde20.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.05%3A_Manure_Handling_Systems
6ed25b8fde20.sentence: Farmers raising hogs on a relatively small scale sometimes use hoop houses, frequently placed in fields, with bedding on the floor.

0fac0662d6c4.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.02%3A_Management_of_N_and_P
0fac0662d6c4.section: Evaluation at the End of the Season
0fac0662d6c4.sentence: To evaluate the success of a fertility recommendation, farmers sometimes plant field strips with different N rates and compare yields at the end of the season.

23b7135a5575.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.02%3A_Management_of_N_and_P
23b7135a5575.section: Evaluation at the End of the Season
23b7135a5575.sentence: These methods are neither fixed nor adaptive approaches for the current year, since evaluation is made at the end of the season, but they may help farmers make changes to their fertilizer application rates in following years.

2381b274d583.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.02%3A_Management_of_N_and_P
2381b274d583.section: Evaluation at the End of the Season
2381b274d583.sentence: Another option is to sample for soil nitrate after harvest, sometimes called a “report card” assessment, to evaluate residual levels of available N. The lower stalk nitrate test is also sometimes used to assess, after the growing season, whether corn N rates were approximately right or too low or too high.

5ba2803d31db.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.02%3A_Management_of_N_and_P
5ba2803d31db.section: Fixed and Adaptive Methods for Estimating Crop N Needs
5ba2803d31db.sentence: Several leading U.S. corn-producing states have adopted the maximum return to N (MRTN) approach, another fixed method that largely abandons the mass-balance approach.

1095d1d9fdf0.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.02%3A_Management_of_N_and_P
1095d1d9fdf0.section: Fixed and Adaptive Methods for Estimating Crop N Needs
1095d1d9fdf0.sentence: The rate with the largest average net return to the farmer over multiple years is the MRTN, and the recommendations vary with grain and fertilizer prices.

7c16eb4c9539.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.02%3A_Management_of_N_and_P
7c16eb4c9539.section: Fixed and Adaptive Methods for Estimating Crop N Needs
7c16eb4c9539.sentence: It provides generalized recommendations based on extensive field trials, model-fitting and economic analyses.

b849e141b560.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.02%3A_Management_of_N_and_P
b849e141b560.section: Fixed and Adaptive Methods for Estimating Crop N Needs
b849e141b560.sentence: The MRTN recommendations are based on comprehensive field information, but owing to generalizing over large areas and over many seasons, it does not account for the soil and weather factors that affect N availability and is therefore inherently imprecise for an individual field.

d8fc9bac644a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.02%3A_Management_of_N_and_P
d8fc9bac644a.sentence: When using organic fertilizers, the higher the percent N in the compost or in the other material, the more N will become available to plants.

5dbdbec69066.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.02%3A_Management_of_N_and_P
5dbdbec69066.sentence: Little to no N will be available to plants if the amendment is around 2% N or less (corresponding to a high C:N ratio).

4d0e8bfbc55a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.02%3A_Management_of_N_and_P
4d0e8bfbc55a.sentence: But if it’s around 5% N, about 40% of the N in the amendment will be available.

2babb8b91b43.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.02%3A_Management_of_N_and_P
2babb8b91b43.sentence: And if it’s 10% or 15% N (corresponding to a very low C:N ratio), 70 percent or more of the N in the amendment will be available to crops.

4ce24ae8cafe.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.02%3A_Management_of_N_and_P
4ce24ae8cafe.sentence: Good N and P management practices take into account the large amount of plant-available nutrients that come from the soil, especially soil organic matter and any additional organic sources like manure, compost, or a rotation crop or cover crop.

32ff5efd53ab.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.02%3A_Management_of_N_and_P
32ff5efd53ab.sentence: Fertilizer should be used only to supplement the soil’s supply in order to provide full plant nutrition (Figure 19.2).

25b0aa92f683.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.02%3A_Management_of_N_and_P
25b0aa92f683.sentence: Organic farmers try to meet all demands through these soil sources because additional organic fertilizers are generally very expensive.

6d0bd8069bf5.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.02%3A_Management_of_N_and_P
6d0bd8069bf5.section: Fixed and Adaptive Methods for Estimating Crop N Needs
6d0bd8069bf5.sentence: The pre-sidedress nitrate test (PSNT) measures soil nitrate content in the surface layer of 0–12 inches and allows for adaptive sidedress or topdress N applications.

ccefb3b2da7c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.02%3A_Management_of_N_and_P
ccefb3b2da7c.section: Fixed and Adaptive Methods for Estimating Crop N Needs
ccefb3b2da7c.sentence: It implicitly incorporates information on early season weather conditions (Figure 19.2) and is especially successful in identifying N-sufficient sites: those that do not need additional N fertilizer.

e4e8588fef6d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.02%3A_Management_of_N_and_P
e4e8588fef6d.section: Fixed and Adaptive Methods for Estimating Crop N Needs
e4e8588fef6d.sentence: It requires a special sampling effort during a short time window in late spring, and it is sensitive to timing and mineralization rates during the early spring.

1df6e7afb2a3.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.02%3A_Management_of_N_and_P
1df6e7afb2a3.section: Fixed and Adaptive Methods for Estimating Crop N Needs
1df6e7afb2a3.sentence: The PSNT is usually called the late spring nitrate test (LSNT) in the midwestern United States.

a0378138a666.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/19%3A_Management_of_Nitrogen_and_Phosphorus/19.03%3A_Planning_for_N_and_P_Management
a0378138a666.section: Reducing N and P Losses > New Technology For Corn Nitrogen Fertilization
a0378138a666.sentence: The PSNT was the first approach that addressed these dynamic processes and therefore provided inherently more precise N fertilizer recommendations and eliminated a lot of unnecessary N applications.

5bcfe8de99b9.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.11%3A_Potential_Problems_Using_Manures
5bcfe8de99b9.sentence: In grazing systems the animal excrements are directly deposited on the surface (in the case of cattle, colloquially referred to as “cow pies”).

072a49c0eb19.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.11%3A_Potential_Problems_Using_Manures
072a49c0eb19.sentence: But because these cow pies are unevenly distributed, they generate small areas with concentrated nutrients while areas in between the “pies” have less nutrients and may still benefit from additional fertilizer.

99ef37a69639.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.11%3A_Potential_Problems_Using_Manures
99ef37a69639.sentence: Some of the ammonium/urea is lost to the atmosphere as the manure dries, similar to non-incorporated manure from confined animal systems.

1d596c98663f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.11%3A_Potential_Problems_Using_Manures
1d596c98663f.sentence: Overall, this reduces concerns with N leaching, and runoff tends to be low due to high vegetative cover on pastures.

e3f7ee06e6e1.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.11%3A_Potential_Problems_Using_Manures
e3f7ee06e6e1.sentence: For this reason, nitrate leaching may still be a concern with intensively managed and fertilized dairy pastures.

6b456e880bf5.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.11%3A_Potential_Problems_Using_Manures
6b456e880bf5.sentence: Although they don’t usually realize it, they are importing large quantities of nutrients in the feed that then remain on the farm as manures.

e95c04b33958.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.11%3A_Potential_Problems_Using_Manures
e95c04b33958.sentence: On integrated crop-livestock farms it is commonly possible to produce all or nearly all the feed needs for the livestock.

6b46a8548981.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.11%3A_Potential_Problems_Using_Manures
6b46a8548981.sentence: This helps to keep nutrient imports and exports close to balanced, one of the advantages of integrated farms.

ad9a628d496d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.11%3A_Potential_Problems_Using_Manures
ad9a628d496d.sentence: More commonly, farms produce most of their own feed but animal numbers exceed the production from the farm’s own land base.

1cf5ed8d2a55.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.11%3A_Potential_Problems_Using_Manures

cfffdcdad899.sentence: For a more detailed discussion of N and P management, see Chapter 19.) When P buildup is a concern, the Phosphorus Index is a tool used to assess the potential for P to move from agricultural fields to surface water.

f4732a10746d.sentence: This allows a nutrient planner to estimate whether P movement risk is low, medium or high, and to suggest appropriate mitigation measures.

e6c95a872fce.sentence: Nitrogen in manure occurs in three main forms: ammonium (NH4+), urea (a soluble organic form, easily converted to ammonium) and solid organic N. Ammonium is readily available to plants, and urea is quickly converted to ammonium in soils.

3194265133b4.sentence: However, while readily available when incorporated in soil, both ammonium and urea are subject to loss as ammonia gas when left on the surface under drying conditions— with significant losses occurring within hours of applying to the soil surface.

279e14b52326.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.08%3A_Using_Manures
279e14b52326.sentence: The 20% leaching loss of potassium from stacked dairy manure mentioned above occurred because potassium was mostly found in the liquid portion of the manure.

8d0687824458.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.08%3A_Using_Manures
8d0687824458.sentence: As materials containing urea or ammonium dry on the soil surface, the ammonium is converted to ammonia gas (NH3) and lost to the atmosphere (also causing odor concerns).

bff220d2ac41.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.08%3A_Using_Manures
bff220d2ac41.sentence: About half of the total nitrogen in dairy manure comes from the urea in urine that quickly converts to ammonium (NH4+).

0b280f10e57b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.08%3A_Using_Manures
0b280f10e57b.sentence: This ammonium represents almost all of the readily available nitrogen present in dairy manure.

00d0b8cc1616.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.08%3A_Using_Manures
00d0b8cc1616.sentence: If dairy manure stays on the soil surface, about 25% of the nitrogen is lost after one day and 45% is lost after four days, but that 45% of the total represents around 70% of the readily available nitrogen.

3e345a12c57b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.08%3A_Using_Manures
3e345a12c57b.sentence: This problem is significantly lessened if about half an inch or more of rainfall occurs shortly after manure application, leaching ammonium from the manure into the soil.

63b0988490d4.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.08%3A_Using_Manures
63b0988490d4.sentence: For the most nitrogen benefit to crops, manures should be incorporated into the soil in the spring immediately after spreading on the surface.

28d174bf2fee.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.08%3A_Using_Manures
28d174bf2fee.sentence: Fall injection of liquid manure, instead of broadcasting on the surface and then disking or plowing, may greatly reduce the loss of ammonia nitrogen.

5cd225922b79.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.08%3A_Using_Manures
5cd225922b79.sentence: Leaving manure on the soil surface is also a problem because runoff waters may carry significant amounts of nutrients from the field.

b30838a21a42.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.08%3A_Using_Manures
b30838a21a42.sentence: When this happens, crops don’t benefit as much from the manure application, and surface waters become polluted.

d095e233b219.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.08%3A_Using_Manures
d095e233b219.sentence: Although the best use of manure is to apply it near the time when the crop needs the nutrients, sometimes time and labor management or insufficient storage capacity causes farmers to apply it at other times.

6f12654179af.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.08%3A_Using_Manures
6f12654179af.sentence: Manures are best applied to annual crops, such as corn, small grains and vegetables, in one dose just before soil tillage (unless a high amount of bedding is used, which might tie up nitrogen for a while—see the discussion of C:N ratios in Chapter 9).

d4321a765b51.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.08%3A_Using_Manures
d4321a765b51.sentence: If the manure is surface applied, this allows for rapid incorporation by plow, chisel, harrow, disk or aerator.

7c363e38f933.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.08%3A_Using_Manures
7c363e38f933.sentence: If injected, no further tillage may be needed, but application close to planting time is still best, because the possibility of loss by runoff and erosion is reduced.

7d1e087499aa.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.08%3A_Using_Manures
7d1e087499aa.sentence: Fall manure applications on annual row crops, such as corn, may result in considerable nitrogen loss, even if manure is incorporated.

49fd6f41a379.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.08%3A_Using_Manures
49fd6f41a379.sentence: Fall-applied manure in humid climates allows ammonium conversion to nitrate and then leaching and denitrification before nitrogen is available to next year’s crop.

7e7735dc5e37.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.08%3A_Using_Manures
7e7735dc5e37.sentence: A three-year New York study showed about twice the N leaching losses from fall-applied compared to spring-applied liquid manure on corn silage, and the losses were greatest with early fall application when the soils were still warm and allowed for manure decomposition.

4acb6888539f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.08%3A_Using_Manures
4acb6888539f.sentence: Without any added nitrogen, perennial grass hay crops are constantly nitrogen deficient.

cfcb1c847c4c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.08%3A_Using_Manures
cfcb1c847c4c.sentence: Application of a moderate rate of manure, about 50–75 pounds worth of available nitrogen, in early spring and following each harvest is the best way to apply manure.
