8537d0fc11bb.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.08%3A_Using_Manures
8537d0fc11bb.sentence: Spring applications may be at higher rates, but wet soils in early spring may not allow manure application without causing significant compaction.

bc583c6135a6.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.08%3A_Using_Manures
bc583c6135a6.sentence: Although legal in most states, it is not a good practice to apply manures when the ground is frozen or covered with snow.

1d5b07aa655f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.08%3A_Using_Manures
1d5b07aa655f.sentence: The nutrient losses that can occur with runoff from winter applied manure are both an economic loss to the farm and an environmental concern.

7d7b628b35ba.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/12%3A_Integrating_Crops_and_Livestock/12.08%3A_Using_Manures
7d7b628b35ba.sentence: However, there are windows of opportunity for incorporating and injecting winter applied manure during periods when the soil has a shallow frozen layer, 2–4 inches thick (frost tillage; see Chapter 16).

2bc65ad67b58.title: Polyhalite
2bc65ad67b58.sentence: Polyhalite is an evaporite mineral, a hydrated sulfate of potassium, calcium and magnesium with formula: K2Ca2Mg(SO4)4·2H2O.

b4c1a5579d54.title: Polyhalite
b4c1a5579d54.sentence: It is used as a valuable fertilizer.

4a45a92cc80c.title: Polyhalite
4a45a92cc80c.sentence: Polyhalite is used as a fertilizer since it contains four important nutrients and is low in chloride:

43b5b4931091.title: Polyhalite
43b5b4931091.sentence: - 14% K2O as from sulfate of potash

098a0263cf6f.title: Polyhalite
098a0263cf6f.sentence: Soil amendment: Polyhalite can help to improve the drainage and fertility of soil.

8f031dee0e9a.title: Polyhalite
8f031dee0e9a.sentence: It can also help to reduce the acidity of soil.

098a304cb8c2.title: Polyhalite
098a304cb8c2.sentence: The only polyhalite mined in the world comes from a layer of rock over 1,000 m (3,300 ft) below North Yorkshire and extending off the North Sea coast in the UK, deposited 260 million years ago.

ce5d06e70673.title: Polyhalite
ce5d06e70673.sentence: In 2010, the first mining operations of this polyhalite mineral layer commenced at Boulby Mine, and the mine is in 2023 the only producer of polyhalite, marketed by ICL Group Ltd. as Polysulphate.

b99162ea1765.title: Nutrient budgeting
b99162ea1765.sentence: Nutrient budgets are comparisons of nutrients applied to the soil to those taken up by crops.

97a1800ac90a.title: Nutrient budgeting
97a1800ac90a.sentence: A nutrient budget takes into account all the nutrient inputs on a farm and all those removed from the land.

6e5889ceec16.title: Nutrient budgeting
6e5889ceec16.sentence: The most obvious source of nutrients in this situation is fertilizer, but this is only part of the picture.

cd315390bd1f.title: Nutrient budgeting
cd315390bd1f.sentence: Other inputs come with rainfall, in supplements brought on to the farm and in effluent – either farm or dairy factory – spread on the land.

e7ab525475c2.title: Nutrient budgeting
e7ab525475c2.sentence: Nutrients are removed from the farm in stock sold on, products (meat, milk, wool), crops sold or fed out off farm, and through processes such as nitrate leaching, volatilization and phosphate run-off etc.

b625645eb466.title: Nutrient budgeting
b625645eb466.sentence: An accurate nutrient budget is an important tool to provide an early indication of potential problems arising from (i) a nutrient surplus (inputs>outputs), leading to an accumulation of nutrients and increased risk of loss or (ii) a deficit (outputs>inputs), depleting nutrient reserves and increasing the risk of deficiencies and reduced crop yields.

3a83ac1ce649.title: Nutrient budgeting
3a83ac1ce649.sentence: A nutrient budget isn't as exact as a financial statement.

6a376c95756b.title: Nutrient budgeting
6a376c95756b.sentence: Limits and assumptions should be incorporated when compiling a budget including the average nutrient removal coefficient values if they are not specific to a certain field.

10d7f6570f11.title: Nutrient budgeting
10d7f6570f11.sentence: By examining the historical yields of crops take from specific fields, you can calculate nutrient removal over time.

455c13fddf6f.title: Nutrient budgeting
455c13fddf6f.sentence: If so, it should be counted as input.

9b735f8aefc3.title: Nutrient budgeting
9b735f8aefc3.sentence: It is a critical best management practice (BMP) in the 4R strategy.

c0fc02cf7333.title: Nutrient budgeting
c0fc02cf7333.sentence: By utilizing Variable-Rate Application (VRA), managers can balance the nutrient budget by applying precise amounts of fertilizer only where uptake potential is highest.

5ff340465ab5.title: Nutrient budgeting
5ff340465ab5.sentence: This minimizes the surplus side of the budget, reducing nutrient leaching into urban watersheds.

776a6bd6719c.title: Crop residue
776a6bd6719c.sentence: Fertilizer placement can significantly affect the efficiency of crop uptake.

904ae4788978.title: Agrochemical
904ae4788978.sentence: Conventional application methods include foliar sprays, and root drenches, broadcasting of granules, and seed coating.

35e1f25ae8dc.title: Green Revolution
35e1f25ae8dc.section: Agricultural production and food security > Environmental impact > Greenhouse gas emissions
35e1f25ae8dc.sentence: Poorly regulated applications of nitrogen fertilizer that exceed the amount used by plants, such as broadcast applications of urea, result in emissions of nitrous oxide, a potent greenhouse gas, and in water pollution.

1a6f4904e46f.title: Fertilizer
1a6f4904e46f.sentence: Phosphate fertilizers are obtained by extraction from phosphate rock, which contains two principal phosphorus-containing minerals, fluorapatite Ca5(PO4)3F (CFA) and hydroxyapatite Ca5(PO4)3OH.

f35c8ca08bc3.title: Fertilizer
f35c8ca08bc3.sentence: These minerals are converted into water-soluble phosphate salts by treatment with acids.

ef7b6d97be85.title: Fertilizer
ef7b6d97be85.sentence: The large production of sulfuric acid is primarily motivated by this application.

744d12c21a71.title: Fertilizer
744d12c21a71.sentence: The main straight phosphate fertilizers are the superphosphates:

91a11a2df82e.title: Fertilizer
91a11a2df82e.sentence: - Single superphosphate (SSP) consisting of 14–18% P2O5, again in the form of Ca(H2PO4)2, but also phosphogypsum (CaSO4 · 2 H2O).

7e70944e5238.title: Fertilizer
7e70944e5238.sentence: - Triple superphosphate (TSP) typically consists of 44–48% of P2O5 and no gypsum.

d0052c8bb61d.title: Fertilizer
d0052c8bb61d.sentence: Billions of kg of phosphate rock are mined annually, but the size and quality of the remaining ore is decreasing.

059216e490b9.title: Fertilizer
059216e490b9.sentence: For each ton of phosphoric acid produced by the processing of phosphate rock, five tons of waste are generated.

4d68276fc9f7.title: Fertilizer
4d68276fc9f7.sentence: This waste takes the form of impure, useless, radioactive solid called phosphogypsum.

a0b4da86368d.title: Fertilizer
a0b4da86368d.sentence: Estimates range from 100,000,000 and 280,000,000 tons of phosphogypsum waste produced annually worldwide.

7231bb60de00.title: Fertilizer
7231bb60de00.sentence: A maize crop yielding 6–9 tonnes of grain per hectare (2.5 acres) requires 31–50 kilograms (68–110 lb) of phosphate fertilizer to be applied; soybean crops require about half, 20–25 kg per hectare.

da784d34716b.title: Fertilizer
da784d34716b.sentence: The main contributor to eutrophication is phosphate, which is normally a limiting nutrient, besides nitrogen; high P concentrations promote the growth of cyanobacteria and algae, the demise of which consumes oxygen.

ad4afd5b6a7e.title: Fertilizer
ad4afd5b6a7e.section: Environmental effects > Soil > Accumulation of toxic elements > Cadmium
ad4afd5b6a7e.sentence: The concentration of cadmium in phosphorus-containing fertilizers varies considerably and can be problematic.

ca3a1b09bfe5.title: Fertilizer
ca3a1b09bfe5.section: Environmental effects > Soil > Accumulation of toxic elements > Cadmium
ca3a1b09bfe5.sentence: For example, mono-ammonium phosphate fertilizer may have a cadmium content of as low as 0.14 mg/kg or as high as 50.9 mg/kg.

d101e77b0f4d.title: Fertilizer
d101e77b0f4d.section: Environmental effects > Soil > Accumulation of toxic elements > Cadmium
d101e77b0f4d.sentence: The phosphate rock used in their manufacture can contain as much as 188 mg/kg cadmium Examples are deposits on Nauru and the Christmas Islands.

3d82980201f2.title: Fertilizer
3d82980201f2.section: Environmental effects > Soil > Accumulation of toxic elements > Cadmium
3d82980201f2.sentence: Continuous use of high-cadmium fertilizer can contaminate soils and plants.

b83828e7f4f7.title: Fertilizer
b83828e7f4f7.section: Environmental effects > Soil > Accumulation of toxic elements > Cadmium
b83828e7f4f7.sentence: Producers of phosphorus-containing fertilizers now select phosphate rock based on the cadmium content.

be05b00e5115.title: Fertilizer
be05b00e5115.section: Environmental effects > Soil > Accumulation of toxic elements > Fluoride
be05b00e5115.sentence: Phosphate rocks contain high levels of fluoride in the form of fluorapatite.

7157abf8d2cb.title: Fertilizer
7157abf8d2cb.section: Environmental effects > Soil > Accumulation of toxic elements > Fluoride
7157abf8d2cb.sentence: Consequently, the widespread use of phosphate fertilizers has increased soil fluoride concentrations.

109bb9c4ecae.title: Fertilizer
109bb9c4ecae.section: Environmental effects > Soil > Accumulation of toxic elements > Fluoride
109bb9c4ecae.sentence: It has been found that food contamination from fertilizer is of little concern as plants accumulate little fluoride from the soil; of greater concern is the possibility of fluoride toxicity to livestock that ingest contaminated soil.

4a199e040e44.title: Fertilizer
4a199e040e44.section: Environmental effects > Soil > Accumulation of toxic elements > Radioactive elements
4a199e040e44.sentence: Uranium-238 concentrations can range from 7 to 100 pCi/g (picocuries per gram) in phosphate rock and from 1 to 67 pCi/g in phosphate fertilizers.

803ac95e6cb0.title: Fertilizer
803ac95e6cb0.section: Environmental effects > Soil > Accumulation of toxic elements > Radioactive elements
803ac95e6cb0.sentence: Where high annual rates of phosphorus fertilizer are used, this can result in uranium-238 concentrations in soils and drainage waters that are several times greater than are normally present.

91f3849ce5cd.title: Fertilizer
91f3849ce5cd.section: Environmental effects > Soil > Accumulation of toxic elements > Radioactive elements
91f3849ce5cd.sentence: However, the impact of these increases on the risk to human health from radionuclidic contamination of foods is very small (less than 0.05 mSv/y).

7869a5e3bcf7.title: Fertilizer
7869a5e3bcf7.section: Environmental effects > Soil > Accumulation of toxic elements > Other metals
7869a5e3bcf7.sentence: Steel industry wastes such as steel slag are often recycled as a soil amendment or for the production of fertilizers due to their high Ca and Mg content and various trace elements necessary for plant growth.

88044652335c.title: Fertilizer
88044652335c.section: Environmental effects > Soil > Accumulation of toxic elements > Other metals
88044652335c.sentence: Among them are arsenic, cadmium, chromium, and nickel, while steel slag amendment rather contribute to immobilize lead in the soil and thus to decrease its toxicity to the cultivated plant.

1da242a17f30.title: Fertilizer
1da242a17f30.section: Environmental effects > Soil > Accumulation of toxic elements > Other metals
1da242a17f30.sentence: The incorporation of biochar to steel slag make even the mixture a good amendement for the (passivation) of heavy metals in agricultural soil.

60eec7099d27.title: Fertilizer
60eec7099d27.sentence: Phosphorus and nitrogen fertilizers can affect soil, surface water, and groundwater due to the dispersion of minerals into waterways under high rainfall, snowmelt and can leach into groundwater over time.

1506461c67d3.title: Fertilizer
1506461c67d3.sentence: High application rates of nitrogen-containing fertilizers combined with the high water solubility of nitrate leads to increased runoff into surface water as well as leaching into groundwater, thereby causing groundwater pollution.

67dbb3fbffeb.title: Fertilizer
67dbb3fbffeb.sentence: Agricultural run-off is a major contributor to the eutrophication of freshwater bodies.

f5044e384a7c.title: Fertilizer
f5044e384a7c.sentence: The nitrogen-rich compounds found in fertilizer runoff are the primary cause of serious oxygen depletion in many parts of oceans, especially in coastal zones, lakes and rivers.

bc949e0efaf6.title: Fertilizer
bc949e0efaf6.sentence: The number of oceanic dead zones near inhabited coastlines is increasing.

9504927ee8ae.title: Fertilizer
9504927ee8ae.sentence: The excessive use of nitrogen-containing fertilizers (be they synthetic or natural) is particularly damaging, as much of the nitrogen that is not taken up by plants is transformed into nitrate which is easily leached.

b77ff7a0e106.title: Fertilizer
b77ff7a0e106.sentence: Nitrate levels above 10 mg/L (10 ppm) in groundwater can cause 'blue baby syndrome' (acquired methemoglobinemia).

25610fd30ff4.title: Fertilizer
25610fd30ff4.sentence: In cases where eutrophication can be reversed, it may nevertheless take decades and need significant soil management before the accumulated nitrates in groundwater can be broken down by natural denitrification.

68dba8c86b20.title: Phosphorite
68dba8c86b20.sentence: Phosphorite, phosphate rock or rock phosphate is a non-detrital sedimentary rock that contains high amounts of phosphate minerals.

4390dae18fd4.title: Phosphorite
4390dae18fd4.sentence: The phosphate content of phosphorite (or grade of phosphate rock) varies greatly, from 4% to 20% phosphorus pentoxide (P2O5).

5cdc139c5343.title: Phosphorite
5cdc139c5343.sentence: By comparison, the average phosphorus content of sedimentary rocks is less than 0.2%.

fce239f03aa5.title: Phosphorite
fce239f03aa5.sentence: This occurs through washing, screening, deliming, magnetic separation or flotation.

25edf8c5e62a.title: Phosphorite
25edf8c5e62a.sentence: For use in the chemical fertilizer industry, beneficiated rock phosphate must be concentrated to levels of at least 28% phosphorus pentoxide (P2O5).

090af2f8ab39.title: Phosphorite
090af2f8ab39.sentence: However, most marketed grades of phosphate rock are 30% or more.

8340cb8c20bf.title: Phosphorite
8340cb8c20bf.sentence: The phosphate is present as fluorapatite Ca5(PO4)3F typically in cryptocrystalline masses (grain sizes < 1 μm) referred to as collophane-sedimentary apatite deposits of uncertain origin.

9f6ea72e7216.title: Phosphorite
9f6ea72e7216.sentence: It is also present as hydroxyapatite Ca5(PO4)3OH or Ca10(PO4)6(OH)2, which is often dissolved from vertebrate bones and teeth.

afed7108ef43.title: Phosphorite
afed7108ef43.sentence: Commonly, phosphates are deposited in very shallow, near-shore marine or low-energy environments.

c11237d3af87.title: Phosphorite
c11237d3af87.sentence: The most common occurrence of phosphorites is related to strong marine upwelling of sediments.

dada458e4c9d.title: Phosphorite
dada458e4c9d.sentence: Upwelling is caused by deep water currents that are brought to the surface near the coast, where a large deposition of phosphorites may occur.

ad1a7f0be6ba.title: Phosphorite
ad1a7f0be6ba.sentence: Approximately 90% of rock phosphate production is used for fertilizer and animal feed supplements, and the balance for industrial chemicals.

8954ffc474e2.title: Phosphorite
8954ffc474e2.sentence: This rock phosphate is then either solubilized to produce wet-process phosphoric acid, or smelted to produce elemental phosphorus.

260cde2e389b.title: Phosphorite
260cde2e389b.sentence: Phosphoric acid is reacted with phosphate rock to make the fertilizer triple superphosphate or with anhydrous ammonia to produce the ammonium phosphate fertilizers.

fb461ed1d112.title: Phosphorite
fb461ed1d112.sentence: As of December 2018, the world's total economic demonstrated resource of rock phosphate is 70 gigatonnes, which occurs principally as sedimentary marine phosphorites.

9fd04168cbfa.title: Phosphorite
9fd04168cbfa.sentence: Worldwide, the resources of high-grade ore are declining, and use of lower grade ore may become more attractive.

38420873d56d.title: Phosphorite
38420873d56d.sentence: Beneficiated rock phosphate is also marketed and accepted as an "organic" alternative to "chemical" phosphate fertilizer, which has been further concentrated from it, because it is perceived as being more "natural".

d6dcf679c1a9.title: Phosphorite
d6dcf679c1a9.sentence: According to a report for the FAO, it can be more sustainable to apply rock phosphate as a fertilizer in certain soil types and countries, although it has many drawbacks.

6d2b9256e638.title: Phosphorite
6d2b9256e638.sentence: According to the report, it may have higher sustainability compared to more concentrated fertilizers because of reduced manufacturing costs and the possibility of local procurement of the refined ore.

9f0de33125c9.title: Superphosphate
9f0de33125c9.sentence: Superphosphate is a chemical fertiliser first synthesised in the 1840s by reacting bones with sulfuric acid.

47b490802ac6.title: Superphosphate
47b490802ac6.sentence: Subsequently, other phosphate-rich deposits such as phosphorite were discovered and used.

508312f99eb6.title: Superphosphate
508312f99eb6.sentence: The process was subsequently improved by reacting phosphate coprolites with sulfuric acid.

b6d157773a7e.title: Superphosphate
b6d157773a7e.sentence: John Bennet Lawes, who farmed in Hertfordshire, learnt of these discoveries and conducted his own research at his farm at Rothamsted (later an agricultural research station), naming the resultant product "super phosphate of lime".

cf132b0a7be7.title: Superphosphate
cf132b0a7be7.sentence: He patented the discovery, and in 1842, started producing superphosphate from fossilised dinosaur dung on an industrial scale; this was the first chemical manure produced in the world.

31a97128e0ac.title: Superphosphate
31a97128e0ac.sentence: The advantage of superphosphate fertilisers is that a significant proportion of the phosphate content is soluble and is immediately available to plants.

002fb19aabdf.title: Superphosphate
002fb19aabdf.sentence: It thus provides a very quick boost to plant growth.

c5cb12f071a8.title: Superphosphate
c5cb12f071a8.sentence: Superphosphate is relatively cheap compared to other available sources of phosphate.

fc38d5a5a7ec.title: Superphosphate
fc38d5a5a7ec.sentence: The lower price contributes to its widespread adoption, particularly in developing regions where the costs of agricultural inputs are a significant consideration.

60720b038d84.title: Superphosphate
60720b038d84.sentence: The fate of phosphates in soil is complicated as they readily form complexes with other minerals such as clays, and aluminium and iron salts, and may be generally unavailable to plants except by weathering and through the action of bacterial and the soil microbiome.

be6d8fdd0d3e.title: Superphosphate
be6d8fdd0d3e.sentence: However, the complex soil dynamics tend to immobilize phosphate in mineral complexes or organic ligands reducing the availability to plants.

e63f77b64ae1.title: Superphosphate
e63f77b64ae1.sentence: Single superphosphate is produced using the traditional method of extraction of phosphate rock with sulfuric acid, an approximate 1:1 mixture of Ca(H2PO4)2 and CaSO4.

ac8d5937a6d2.title: Superphosphate
ac8d5937a6d2.sentence: It primarily consists of monocalcium phosphate, Ca(H2PO4)2.

7ca2f848aa77.title: Superphosphate
7ca2f848aa77.sentence: It is obtained by treating phosphate rock with phosphoric acid.

db77973e6081.title: Superphosphate
db77973e6081.sentence: The term, "double superphosphate", refers to a mixture of triple and single superphosphate, resulting from the extraction of phosphate rock with a mixture of phosphoric and sulfuric acids.

725a874c8873.title: Superphosphate
725a874c8873.sentence: Typical fertiliser-grade triple superphosphate contains 45% P2O5eq, single superphosphate 20% P2O5eq.

8d01038a73ae.title: Superphosphate
8d01038a73ae.sentence: Continuous use of superphosphate can lead to soil acidification, particularly on poorly buffered soils, altering pH levels and potentially limiting nutrient availability.

b87707925677.title: Superphosphate
b87707925677.sentence: However, the key quality that made superphosphate so attractive—the solubility of the phosphate—also created an ongoing demand for the product as the soluble phosphorus salts and phosphate bound to fine sediments are eluted from fields into rivers and streams where they became lost to agriculture but help to encourage unwelcome eutrophication.

294812737db0.title: Superphosphate
294812737db0.sentence: Leaching of sediments from soil can lead to elevated phosphate concentrations in the receiving watercourse.

f4d6f528f177.title: Reuse of human excreta
f4d6f528f177.sentence: In the case of phosphorus in particular, reuse of excreta is one known method to recover phosphorus to mitigate the potential shortage (also known as "peak phosphorus") of economical mined phosphorus.

c36bbdc025ad.title: Reuse of human excreta
c36bbdc025ad.sentence: Mined phosphorus is a limited resource that is used up by fertilizer production, a shortage of which would threaten worldwide food security.

b773b77077f7.title: Reuse of human excreta
b773b77077f7.sentence: Therefore, phosphorus from excreta-based fertilizers is an interesting alternative to fertilizers containing mined phosphate ore.

47a744e5f6fb.title: Reuse of human excreta
47a744e5f6fb.sentence: Besides concentration, simple chemical processes can be used to extract pure substances: nitrogen as nitrates (similar to medieval nitre beds) and phosphorus as struvite.

d47228de42d9.title: Reuse of human excreta
d47228de42d9.sentence: Sludge treatment liquids (after anaerobic digestion) can be used as an input source for a process to recover phosphorus in the form of struvite for use as fertilizer.

c9fc2bb06ab5.title: Microbial inoculant
c9fc2bb06ab5.sentence: This 30% reduction in fertilizer application can aid in the reduction of nutrient pollution, and help prolong finite mineral resources such as phosphorus (Peak phosphorus).

36d114c530a1.title: Phosphate rich organic manure
36d114c530a1.sentence: Phosphate rich organic manure is a type of fertilizer used as an alternative to diammonium phosphate and single super phosphate.

2721bfef1195.title: Phosphate rich organic manure
2721bfef1195.sentence: Phosphate rich organic manure is produced by co-composting high-grade (32% P2O5 +/- 2%) rock phosphate in very fine size (say 80% finer than 54 microns).

8a9f570114bb.title: Phosphate rich organic manure
8a9f570114bb.sentence: The finer the rock phosphate, the better is the agronomic efficiency of Phosphate rich organic manure.

7800361a6c85.title: Phosphate rich organic manure
7800361a6c85.sentence: Phosphorus in rock phosphate mineral is mostly in the form of tricalcium phosphate, which is water-insoluble.

254032433fe3.title: Phosphate rich organic manure
254032433fe3.sentence: Microorganisms produce organic acids, which cause the slow dissolution of phosphorus from rock phosphate dust added to the soil, allowing more phosphorus uptake by the plant roots.

d446c379fc15.title: Phosphate rich organic manure
d446c379fc15.sentence: Organic manure can prevent ions of other elements from locking phosphorus into insoluble forms.

57918da046ee.title: Phosphate rich organic manure
57918da046ee.sentence: Phosphorus dissolution in the soil is most favorable at a pH between 5.5 and 7.

bded86836898.title: Phosphate rich organic manure
bded86836898.sentence: Ions of aluminum, iron, and manganese prevent phosphorus dissolution by keeping local pH below 5.5, and magnesium and calcium ions prevent the pH from dropping below 7, preventing the release of phosphorus from its stable molecule.

91b335ff1811.title: Phosphate rich organic manure
91b335ff1811.sentence: Research indicates that this substance may be a more efficient way of adding phosphorus to soil than applying chemical fertilizers.

df8db740f984.title: Phosphate rich organic manure
df8db740f984.sentence: Other benefits of phosphate rich organic manure are that it supplies phosphorus to the second crop planted in a treated area as efficiently as the first, and that it can be produced using acidic waste solids recovered from the discharge of biogas plants.

8ff6a1c7b47a.title: Diammonium phosphate
8ff6a1c7b47a.sentence: Diammonium phosphate (DAP; IUPAC name diammonium hydrogen phosphate; chemical formula (NH4)2(HPO4)) is one of a series of water-soluble ammonium phosphate salts that can be produced when ammonia reacts with phosphoric acid.

0708953c2350.title: Diammonium phosphate
0708953c2350.sentence: DAP is used as a fertilizer.

b2b9c8119caf.title: Diammonium phosphate
b2b9c8119caf.sentence: The typical NPK ratio is 18-46-0 (18% N, 46% P2O5, 0% K2O).

b08fb53279e0.title: Diammonium phosphate
b08fb53279e0.sentence: When applied as plant fertilizer, it temporarily increases the soil pH, but over a long term the treated ground becomes more acidic than before, upon nitrification of the ammonium.

10f0136c1644.title: Diammonium phosphate
10f0136c1644.sentence: The average pH in solution is 7.5–8.

7ad1023e4338.title: Diammonium phosphate
7ad1023e4338.sentence: It is incompatible with alkaline chemicals because its ammonium ion is more likely to convert to ammonia in a high-pH environment.

cb96bbdcd0fb.title: Diammonium phosphate
cb96bbdcd0fb.sentence: According to the diammonium phosphate MSDS from CF Industries, Inc., decomposition starts as low as 70 °C: "Hazardous Decomposition Products: Gradually loses ammonia when exposed to air at room temperature.

309fcbb341c9.title: Diammonium phosphate
309fcbb341c9.sentence: Decomposes to ammonia and monoammonium phosphate at around 70 °C (158 °F).

a2876c98f126.title: Struvite
a2876c98f126.sentence: Struvite (magnesium ammonium phosphate, sometimes abbreviated as MAP) is a phosphate mineral with formula: NH4MgPO4·6H2O.

85c4382e8ede.title: Struvite
85c4382e8ede.sentence: Struvite readily forms in alkaline conditions where its constituent ions are present.

ba9af2596c6b.title: Struvite
ba9af2596c6b.sentence: Struvite, also referred to as MAP, forms when there is a mole to mole to mole ratio (1:1:1) of magnesium, ammonia and phosphate in the wastewater.

6991ef211377.title: Struvite
6991ef211377.sentence: It is sparingly soluble in neutral and alkaline conditions, but readily soluble in acid.

3589bc15fcf4.title: Struvite
3589bc15fcf4.sentence: Struvite can be a problem in sewage and waste water treatment, particularly after anaerobic digesters release ammonium and phosphate from waste material.

955fd9214433.title: Struvite
955fd9214433.sentence: Struvite can form a scale on lines and belts, in centrifuges and pumps, clog system pipes and other equipment including the anaerobic digester itself.

d1630b8d7311.title: Struvite
d1630b8d7311.sentence: Recovery of phosphorus from wastestreams as struvite and recycling those nutrients into agriculture as fertilizer appears promising, particularly in agricultural manure and municipal waste water treatment plants.

b50e95dc0e60.title: Struvite
b50e95dc0e60.sentence: Use of struvite as an agricultural fertilizer was first described in 1857.

1c89f4056b1b.title: Struvite
1c89f4056b1b.sentence: It contains phosphorus and nitrogen, two of the three major plant macronutrients, with magnesium being a minor macronutrient as well.

363ca56b96ea.title: Struvite
363ca56b96ea.sentence: Struvite can be produced from urine by adjusting pH (often just by waiting for urease-producing bacteria to work) and adding magnesium.

7ec007617fd5.title: Phosphogypsum
7ec007617fd5.sentence: Phosphogypsum (PG) is the calcium sulfate hydrate formed as a by-product of the production of fertilizer, particularly phosphoric acid, from phosphate rock.

c824e24544b3.title: Phosphogypsum
c824e24544b3.sentence: It is mainly composed of gypsum (CaSO4 · 2 H2O).

8d346fad3cdc.title: Phosphogypsum
8d346fad3cdc.sentence: About five tons of phosphogypsum are generated per ton of phosphoric acid production.

3687bcea4428.title: Phosphogypsum
3687bcea4428.sentence: Annually, the estimated generation of phosphogypsum worldwide is 100 to 280 million metric tons.

5daf2f57be37.title: Phosphogypsum
5daf2f57be37.sentence: It is radioactive due to the presence of naturally occurring uranium (5–10 ppm) and thorium, and their daughter nuclides radium, radon, polonium, etc. Marine-deposited phosphate typically has a higher level of radioactivity than igneous phosphate deposits, because uranium is present in seawater at about 3 ppb (roughly 85 ppb of total dissolved solids).

c52e54cba153.title: Phosphogypsum
c52e54cba153.sentence: Although gypsum is a widely used material in the construction industry, phosphogypsum is usually not used, but is stored indefinitely because of its weak radioactivity caused by the presence of naturally occurring uranium (U) and thorium (Th), and their daughter isotopes radium (Ra), radon (Rn) and polonium (Po).

5801a16ee56c.title: Phosphogypsum
5801a16ee56c.sentence: According to Taylor (2009), "up to 15% of world PG production is used to make building materials, as a soil amendment and as a set controller in the manufacture of Portland cement".

63ed1d9d3960.title: Phosphogypsum
63ed1d9d3960.sentence: The United States Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) has banned most applications of phosphogypsum having a 226Ra concentration of greater than 10 picocurie/gram (0.4 Bq/g) in 1990.

c8584cc3efbe.title: Phosphogypsum
c8584cc3efbe.sentence: Phosphogypsum may pollute the environment by its phosphorus content causing eutrophication, by its toxic heavy metal content, and by its radioactivity.

37ac0c7e2550.title: Phosphogypsum
37ac0c7e2550.sentence: More substantial however is the leaching of the contents of phosphogypsum into the water table and consequently soil, exacerbated by the fact that PG is often transported as a slurry.

27cdf0768154.title: Water cycle
27cdf0768154.sentence: The water cycle (or hydrologic cycle or hydrological cycle) is a biogeochemical cycle that involves the continuous change in form of water on, above and below the surface of the Earth across different reservoirs.

f5a475f3a462.title: Water cycle
f5a475f3a462.sentence: The processes that drive these movements, or fluxes, are evaporation, transpiration, condensation, precipitation, sublimation, infiltration, surface runoff, and subsurface flow.

d2530f2072f3.title: Water cycle
d2530f2072f3.sentence: The water cycle is powered by the energy emitted from the sun.

dde4c3fa10e5.title: Water cycle
dde4c3fa10e5.sentence: Most water falls as rain back into the ocean or onto land, where the water flows over the ground as surface runoff.

2dbf38356f05.title: Water cycle
2dbf38356f05.sentence: Not all runoff flows into rivers; much of it soaks into the ground as infiltration.

466ec88a3b02.title: Water cycle
466ec88a3b02.sentence: Once infiltrated, the water becomes soil moisture or groundwater.

e39a38197999.title: Water cycle
e39a38197999.sentence: Some infiltration stays close to the land surface and can seep back into surface-water bodies (and the ocean) as groundwater discharge or be taken up by plants and transferred back to the atmosphere as water vapor by transpiration.

a902cbf9f0c4.title: Water cycle
a902cbf9f0c4.sentence: Some water infiltrates deep into the ground and replenishes aquifers, which can store freshwater for long periods of time.

80ffabf653cd.title: Water cycle
80ffabf653cd.sentence: Groundwater tends to move slowly and is replenished slowly, so it can remain in aquifers for thousands of years.

d762b77c475e.title: Water cycle
d762b77c475e.sentence: Two other ways that water gets into the atmosphere is through snow and ice sublimating into water vapor and through evapotranspiration which is water transpired from plants and evaporated from the soil.

9b3cf8dbb9e4.title: Water cycle
9b3cf8dbb9e4.sentence: Evaporation often implicitly includes transpiration from plants, though together they are specifically referred to as evapotranspiration.

fb24364491e9.title: Water cycle
fb24364491e9.sentence: Approximately 505,000 km3 (121,000 cu mi) of water falls as precipitation each year, 398,000 km3 (95,000 cu mi) of it over the oceans.

934b8d7cc7e5.title: Water cycle
934b8d7cc7e5.sentence: It also reshapes the geological features of the Earth, through processes of weathering, erosion, and deposition.

012160e7afbc.title: Water cycle
012160e7afbc.sentence: Runoff is responsible for almost all of the transport of eroded sediment and phosphorus from land to waterbodies.

c0ea138c1b5d.title: Water cycle
c0ea138c1b5d.sentence: A recent global study using water stable isotopes, however, shows that not all soil moisture is equally available for groundwater recharge or for plant transpiration.

89fb19bfe2cd.title: Surface runoff
89fb19bfe2cd.sentence: Surface runoff (also known as overland flow or terrestrial runoff) is the unconfined flow of water over the ground surface, in contrast to channel runoff (or stream flow).

e9bc3b68d0ca.title: Surface runoff
e9bc3b68d0ca.sentence: It occurs when excess rainwater, stormwater, meltwater, or other sources, can no longer sufficiently rapidly infiltrate into the soil.

d47f599cc4d1.title: Surface runoff
d47f599cc4d1.sentence: This can occur when the soil is saturated by water to its full capacity, and the rain arrives more quickly than the soil can absorb it.

b1dce3e9e518.title: Surface runoff
b1dce3e9e518.sentence: Surface runoff often occurs because impervious areas (such as roofs and pavement) do not allow water to soak into the ground.

b6c75f09a505.title: Surface runoff
b6c75f09a505.sentence: Surface runoff is a major component of the water cycle.

64151c6b8413.title: Surface runoff
64151c6b8413.sentence: It is the primary agent of soil erosion by water.

c4af88be9dd2.title: Surface runoff
c4af88be9dd2.sentence: The land area producing runoff that drains to a common point is called a drainage basin.

f55eed16a427.title: Surface runoff
f55eed16a427.sentence: However, not all rainfall will produce runoff because storage from soils can absorb light showers.

dc58c8b4d43d.title: Surface runoff
dc58c8b4d43d.section: Effects of surface runoff > Erosion and deposition
dc58c8b4d43d.sentence: The soil particles carried in runoff vary in size from about 0.001 millimeter to 1.0 millimeter in diameter.

7231cbf5b896.title: Surface runoff
7231cbf5b896.section: Effects of surface runoff > Erosion and deposition
7231cbf5b896.sentence: Larger particles settle over short transport distances, whereas small particles can be carried over long distances suspended in the water column.

b0b60d38c6e5.title: Surface runoff
b0b60d38c6e5.sentence: Runoff that occurs on the ground surface before reaching a channel can be a nonpoint source of pollution, as it can carry human-made contaminants or natural forms of pollution (such as rotting leaves).

94cef5adffbc.title: Surface runoff
94cef5adffbc.sentence: Human-made contaminants in runoff include petroleum, pesticides, fertilizers and others.

4116a5bb3d4e.title: Surface runoff
4116a5bb3d4e.sentence: Much agricultural pollution is exacerbated by surface runoff, leading to a number of downstream impacts, including nutrient pollution that causes eutrophication.

3e68013f2f41.title: Surface runoff
3e68013f2f41.sentence: In addition to causing water erosion and pollution, surface runoff in urban areas is a primary cause of urban flooding, which can result in property damage, damp and mold in basements, and street flooding.

df2a2d4460af.title: Subsidence
df2a2d4460af.sentence: Subsidence is a general term for downward vertical movement of the Earth's surface, which can be caused by both natural processes and human activities.

b79271b60808.title: Subsidence
b79271b60808.sentence: Subsidence involves little or no horizontal movement, which distinguishes it from slope movement.

041ebd9827d8.title: Subsidence
041ebd9827d8.sentence: Processes that lead to subsidence include dissolution of underlying carbonate rock by groundwater; gradual compaction of sediments; withdrawal of fluid lava from beneath a solidified crust of rock; mining; pumping of subsurface fluids, such as groundwater or petroleum; or warping of the Earth's crust by tectonic forces.

f32016af0419.title: Subsidence
f32016af0419.sentence: Pumping of groundwater or petroleum has led to subsidence of as much as 9 meters (30 ft) in many locations around the world and incurring costs measured in hundreds of millions of US dollars.

8c8ea60d7e54.title: Subsidence
8c8ea60d7e54.sentence: Subsidence causes major problems in karst terrains, where dissolution of limestone by fluid flow in the subsurface creates voids (i.e., caves).

dfed55d4017e.title: Subsidence
dfed55d4017e.sentence: If the roof of a void becomes too weak, it can collapse and the overlying rock and earth will fall into the space, causing subsidence at the surface.

1e53dccd9f3d.title: Subsidence
1e53dccd9f3d.sentence: This type of subsidence can cause sinkholes which can be many hundreds of meters deep.

07072618d32f.title: Subsidence
07072618d32f.sentence: High buildings can create land subsidence by pressing the soil beneath with their weight.

a482d63d6cd9.title: Subsidence
a482d63d6cd9.sentence: The problem is already felt in New York City, the San Francisco Bay Area, and Lagos.

b97d9a94ad8c.title: Subsidence
b97d9a94ad8c.sentence: This elevation reduction increases the risk of flooding, particularly in river flood plains and delta areas.

095a2e844cac.title: Subsidence
095a2e844cac.sentence: Land subsidence can lead to differential settlements in buildings and other infrastructures, causing angular distortions.

0f5d0644c4cf.title: Subsidence
0f5d0644c4cf.sentence: When these angular distortions exceed certain values, the structures can become damaged, resulting in issues such as tilting or cracking.

6c6a8a24b8cd.title: Stormwater
6c6a8a24b8cd.sentence: Stormwater, also written storm water, is water that originates from precipitation (storm), including heavy rain and meltwater from hail and snow.

6e7a6bca5a2b.title: Stormwater
6e7a6bca5a2b.sentence: Stormwater can soak into the soil (infiltrate) and become groundwater, be stored on depressed land surface in ponds and puddles, evaporate back into the atmosphere, or contribute to surface runoff.

ec090ef81f41.title: Stormwater
ec090ef81f41.sentence: Most runoff is conveyed directly as surface water to nearby streams, rivers or other large water bodies (wetlands, lakes and oceans) without treatment.

db3c4807737f.title: Stormwater
db3c4807737f.sentence: In natural landscapes, such as forests, soil absorbs much of the stormwater.

63f7cedb6a1f.title: Stormwater
63f7cedb6a1f.sentence: Plants also reduce stormwater by improving infiltration, intercepting precipitation as it falls, and by taking up water through their roots.

5b090d711c23.title: Stormwater
5b090d711c23.sentence: With less vegetation and more impervious surfaces (parking lots, roads, buildings, compacted soil), developed areas allow less rain to infiltrate into the ground, and more runoff is generated than in undeveloped conditions.

b7f42e0f65ff.title: Stormwater
b7f42e0f65ff.sentence: This greatly increases the volume of water in waterways and the discharge of those waterways, leading to erosion and flooding.

aa2152779e53.title: Stormwater
aa2152779e53.sentence: Because the water is flushed out of the watershed during the storm event, little infiltrates the soil, replenishes groundwater, or supplies stream baseflow in dry weather.

516ad698353e.title: Stormwater
516ad698353e.sentence: Such pollutants include trash, sediment, nutrients, bacteria, pesticides, metals, and petroleum byproducts.

b3783af67293.title: Stormwater
b3783af67293.sentence: A first flush is the initial runoff of a rainstorm.

21f5b25c07c8.title: Stormwater
21f5b25c07c8.sentence: During this phase, polluted water entering storm drains in areas with high proportions of impervious surfaces is typically more concentrated compared to the remainder of the storm.

8c64450c06d0.title: Stormwater
8c64450c06d0.sentence: The effect of phosphorus, either dissolved from (fertilizers) or bound to sediment particles from construction or agriculture runoff, causes algae and toxic cyanobacteria (aka Blue-green algae) blooms in receiving lakes.

570886c05d8e.title: Stormwater
570886c05d8e.sentence: Stormwater management facilities (SWMF) are generally designed using Stokes' law to allow rudimentary treatment through the settling particulate matter larger than 40 micron in size and to impound water to reduce downstream flooding.

26542a40d51d.title: Runoff (hydrology)
26542a40d51d.sentence: Runoff is the flow of water across the earth, and is a major component in the hydrological cycle.

0d649e354247.title: Runoff (hydrology)
0d649e354247.sentence: Runoff that flows over land before reaching a watercourse is referred to as surface runoff or overland flow.

c7261f36c427.title: Runoff (hydrology)
c7261f36c427.sentence: Once in a watercourse, runoff is referred to as streamflow, channel runoff, or river runoff.

9864b82a51da.title: Runoff (hydrology)
9864b82a51da.sentence: It occurs when excess rainwater, stormwater, meltwater, or other sources, can no longer sufficiently rapidly infiltrate into the soil.

5eed410143b6.title: Runoff (hydrology)
5eed410143b6.sentence: This can occur when the soil is saturated by water to its full capacity, and the rain arrives more quickly than the soil can absorb it.

e9bcb50fa69a.title: Runoff (hydrology)
e9bcb50fa69a.sentence: Surface runoff often occurs because impervious areas (such as roofs and pavement) do not allow water to soak into the ground.

893990935c22.title: Runoff (hydrology)
893990935c22.sentence: Water flowing in channels comes from surface runoff from adjacent hillslopes, from groundwater flow out of the ground, and from water discharged from pipes.

a887274d6612.title: Runoff (hydrology)
a887274d6612.sentence: The discharge of water flowing in a channel is measured using stream gauges or can be estimated by the Manning equation.

c8c5052a747d.title: Runoff (hydrology)
c8c5052a747d.sentence: Flooding occurs when the volume of water exceeds the capacity of the channel.

3733e997f172.title: Runoff (hydrology)
3733e997f172.sentence: The record of flow over time is called a hydrograph.

5bedba1da9d5.title: Straw
5bedba1da9d5.sentence: Straw is an agricultural byproduct consisting of the dry stalks of cereal plants after the grain and chaff have been removed.

cedcbe61efc8.title: Straw
cedcbe61efc8.sentence: It makes up about half of the yield by weight of cereal crops such as barley, oats, rice, rye and wheat.

58859c6e6e16.title: Straw
58859c6e6e16.sentence: Straw bales are sometimes used for sediment control at construction sites.

c00dbf7a418d.title: Straw
c00dbf7a418d.sentence: However, bales are often ineffective in protecting water quality and are maintenance-intensive.

59140807cbbe.title: Straw
59140807cbbe.sentence: For these reasons the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and various state agencies recommend use of alternative sediment control practices where possible, such as silt fences, fiber rolls and geotextiles.

16969f390f8d.title: Straw
16969f390f8d.sentence: They can also be used as burned area emergency response, as ground cover or as in-stream check dams.

65f7be5e0040.title: Straw
65f7be5e0040.sentence: Straw also makes an excellent mulch.

3db90063d329.title: Cob (material)
3db90063d329.sentence: Cob, cobb, or clom (in Wales) is a natural building material made from subsoil, water, fibrous organic material (typically straw), and sometimes lime.

be9c567ab684.title: Adobe
be9c567ab684.sentence: An adobe brick is a composite material made of earth mixed with water and an organic material such as straw or dung.

88b0fad5a90c.title: Retention basin
88b0fad5a90c.sentence: A retention basin, sometimes called a retention pond, wet detention basin, or storm water management pond (SWMP), is an artificial pond with vegetation around the perimeter and a permanent pool of water in its design.

4d277959433f.title: Retention basin
4d277959433f.sentence: It is used to manage stormwater runoff, for protection against flooding, for erosion control, and to serve as an artificial wetland and improve the water quality in adjacent bodies of water.

208f410b7756.title: Retention basin
208f410b7756.sentence: It is distinguished from a detention basin, sometimes called a "dry pond", which temporarily stores water after a storm, but eventually empties out at a controlled rate to a downstream water body.

1fd7feaa3887.title: Retention basin
1fd7feaa3887.sentence: It also differs from an infiltration basin which is designed to direct stormwater to groundwater through permeable soils.

cde57bbb94ef.title: Retention basin
cde57bbb94ef.sentence: In urban areas, impervious surfaces (roofs, roads) reduce the time spent by rainfall before entering into the stormwater drainage system.

1fd8a39ce2aa.title: Retention basin
1fd8a39ce2aa.sentence: The function of a stormwater pond is to contain this surge and release it slowly.

ee3af19aa767.title: Retention basin
ee3af19aa767.sentence: This slow release mitigates the size and intensity of storm-induced flooding on downstream receiving waters.

cbeb28bd2377.title: Retention basin
cbeb28bd2377.sentence: Stormwater ponds also collect suspended sediments, which are often found in high concentrations in stormwater due to upstream construction and sand applications to roadways.

08538deaee44.title: Retention basin
08538deaee44.sentence: Vegetation also provides water quality benefits by removing soluble nutrients through uptake.

4d20fe4fb8ae.title: Retention basin
4d20fe4fb8ae.sentence: Sometimes they act as a replacement for the natural absorption of a forest or other natural process that was lost when an area is developed.

1dbcd478f132.title: Retention basin
1dbcd478f132.sentence: Wet ponds are frequently used for water quality improvement, groundwater recharge, flood protection, aesthetic improvement, or any combination of these.

ddc38102fe35.title: Bioswale
ddc38102fe35.sentence: Bioswales are channels designed to concentrate and convey stormwater runoff while removing debris and pollution.

f3cc1fcab95c.title: Bioswale
f3cc1fcab95c.sentence: Bioswales are typically vegetated, mulched, or xeriscaped.

1904b402500e.title: Bioswale
1904b402500e.sentence: They consist of a swaled drainage course with gently sloped sides (less than 6%).

b72468c41518.title: Bioswale
b72468c41518.sentence: Bioswales require a certain soil composition that does not contain more than 5% clay.

2907ca6777bd.title: Bioswale
2907ca6777bd.sentence: Bioswale design is intended to safely maximize the time water spends in the swale, which aids the collection and removal of pollutants, silt and debris.

c3b2ce38cbeb.title: Bioswale
c3b2ce38cbeb.sentence: As the storm water runoff flows through the bioswale, the pollutants are captured and settled by the leaves and stems of the plants.

475fbbe1562d.title: Bioswale
475fbbe1562d.sentence: The pollutants then enter the soil where they decompose or can be broken down by bacteria in healthy soil.

492a1938f3f7.title: Bioswale
492a1938f3f7.sentence: Bioswales are useful low-impact development work to decrease the velocity of stormwater runoff while removing pollutants from the discharge.

bc83536bc914.title: Bioswale
bc83536bc914.sentence: Bioswales can also be beneficial in recharging groundwater, reducing flooding and erosion, and creating a valuable habitat for pollinators.

32a58a482f74.title: Bioswale
32a58a482f74.sentence: Bioswales are created to handle the first flush of pollutants during the event of rain, therefore, locations that have high areas of impervious surface such as roads, parking lots, or rooftops can benefit from additions of bioswales.

55b0a1e0914a.title: Bioswale
55b0a1e0914a.sentence: In permaculture, swales are used for water harvesting.

333e425edc65.title: Land development
333e425edc65.sentence: Land development is the alteration of landscape in any number of ways, such as:

8f769274b7df.title: Land development
8f769274b7df.sentence: - Changing landforms from a natural or semi-natural state for a purpose such as agriculture or housing

8c4ad4f194f2.title: Land development
8c4ad4f194f2.sentence: - Subdividing real estate into lots, typically for the purpose of building homes

9f827e3e7c00.title: Land development
9f827e3e7c00.section: Conversion of landforms > Conversion to building land
9f827e3e7c00.sentence: Conversion to building land is as a rule associated with road building, which in itself already brings topsoil abrasion, soil compaction and modification of the soil's chemical composition through soil stabilization, creation of impervious surfaces and, subsequently, (polluted) surface runoff water.

d0bdfffc1b57.title: Land development
d0bdfffc1b57.section: Conversion of landforms > Conversion to building land
d0bdfffc1b57.sentence: Construction activity often effectively seals off a larger part of the soil from rainfall and the nutrient cycle, so that the soil below buildings and roads is effectively "consumed" and made infertile.

fda69d5714a9.title: Land development
fda69d5714a9.section: Conversion of landforms > Conversion to farmland
fda69d5714a9.sentence: New creation of farmland (or 'agricultural land conversion') will rely on the conversion and development of previous forests, savannas or grassland.

cc3da63c3cdf.title: Land development
cc3da63c3cdf.section: Conversion of landforms > Conversion to farmland
cc3da63c3cdf.sentence: Starting from forests, land is made arable by assarting or slash-and-burn.

1f54700593e7.title: Land development
1f54700593e7.section: Conversion of landforms > Conversion to farmland
1f54700593e7.sentence: Recreation of farmland from wasteland, deserts or previous impervious surfaces is considerably less frequent because of the degraded or missing fertile soil in the latter.

9b81fd18f3c7.title: Land development
9b81fd18f3c7.sentence: "Land improvement" in the economic sense can often lead to land degradation from the ecological perspective.

b7964c3ddadd.title: Land development
b7964c3ddadd.sentence: - Desertification, soil erosion and ecological shifts due to drainage

5ec81cb2a4c4.title: Water cycle
5ec81cb2a4c4.section: Changes caused by humans > Land cover and land use changes
5ec81cb2a4c4.sentence: Human activities can alter the water cycle at the local or regional level.

26d9aae47aad.title: Water cycle
26d9aae47aad.section: Changes caused by humans > Land cover and land use changes
26d9aae47aad.sentence: This happens due to changes in land use and land cover.

404084edd036.title: Water cycle
404084edd036.section: Changes caused by humans > Land cover and land use changes
404084edd036.sentence: Examples of common land use changes include urbanization, agricultural expansion, and deforestation.

b8ea7ad0446b.title: Water cycle
b8ea7ad0446b.section: Changes caused by humans > Land cover and land use changes
b8ea7ad0446b.sentence: These changes can increase soil compaction and impervious surface cover which decrease the infiltration capacity of soils and result in greater surface runoff rates.

120297344af6.title: Water cycle
120297344af6.section: Changes caused by humans > Land cover and land use changes
120297344af6.sentence: Deforestation has local and regional effects; at the local level it reduces soil moisture, evaporation, rainfall, and snowfall; at the regional level it can cause temperature changes that affect rainfall patterns.

26b8c608d9f3.title: Water cycle
26b8c608d9f3.section: Changes caused by humans > Land cover and land use changes
26b8c608d9f3.sentence: Stormwater drains function to decrease runoff rates, regulate flow rates, and increase groundwater recharge.

4ef6585dbf58.title: Water cycle
4ef6585dbf58.section: Changes caused by humans > Land cover and land use changes
4ef6585dbf58.sentence: Leakage from sewage pipes may artificially contribute to groundwater recharge, resulting in higher stream baseflow conditions and groundwater contamination.

183d83c67ed9.title: Surface runoff
183d83c67ed9.sentence: Mitigation of adverse impacts of runoff can take several forms:

53d267b000ce.title: Surface runoff
53d267b000ce.sentence: - Land use development controls aimed at minimizing impervious surfaces in urban areas

9494724785e3.title: Surface runoff
9494724785e3.sentence: - Erosion controls for farms and construction sites

753916466b1f.title: Surface runoff
753916466b1f.sentence: - Flood control and retrofit programs, such as green infrastructure

292afad1b8e0.title: Surface runoff
292afad1b8e0.sentence: - Chemical use and handling controls in agriculture, landscape maintenance, industrial use, etc.

e9eb715eccb5.title: Surface runoff
e9eb715eccb5.sentence: Many municipalities have produced guidelines and codes (zoning and related ordinances) for land developers that encourage minimum width sidewalks, use of pavers set in earth for driveways and walkways and other design techniques to allow maximum water infiltration in urban settings.

86fb6e85080d.title: Surface runoff
86fb6e85080d.sentence: In the 1960s some state and local governments began to focus their efforts on mitigation of construction runoff by requiring builders to implement erosion and sediment controls (ESCs).

f5011333bf8b.title: Surface runoff
f5011333bf8b.sentence: This included such techniques as: use of straw bales and barriers to slow runoff on slopes, installation of silt fences, programming construction for months that have less rainfall and minimizing extent and duration of exposed graded areas.

edcbb7b93dc3.title: Surface runoff
edcbb7b93dc3.sentence: Some of the techniques commonly applied are: provision of holding ponds (also called detention basins or balancing lakes) to buffer riverine peak flows, use of energy dissipators in channels to reduce stream velocity and land use controls to minimize runoff.

764f68d7e171.title: Surface runoff
764f68d7e171.sentence: Methods commonly applied are: requirements for double containment of underground storage tanks, registration of hazardous materials usage, reduction in numbers of allowed pesticides and more stringent regulation of fertilizers and herbicides in landscape maintenance.

dad6b6d336d8.title: Surface runoff
dad6b6d336d8.sentence: When the soil is saturated and the depression storage filled, and rain continues to fall, the rainfall will immediately produce surface runoff.

0d8293f29aeb.title: Surface runoff
0d8293f29aeb.sentence: This runoff is called saturation excess overland flow, saturated overland flow, or Dunne runoff.

58f2b80f7412.title: Surface runoff
58f2b80f7412.sentence: The level of antecedent soil moisture is one factor affecting the time until soil becomes saturated.

0f19d9c286b8.title: Surface runoff
0f19d9c286b8.sentence: The higher the level of antecedent soil moisture, the more quickly the soil becomes saturated.

ed289ca2c2fd.title: Surface runoff
ed289ca2c2fd.sentence: Once the soil is saturated, runoff occurs.

30391bc2e7ef.title: Soil erosion
30391bc2e7ef.section: Factors affecting soil erosion > Soil structure and composition
30391bc2e7ef.sentence: Wet, saturated soils will not be able to absorb as much rainwater, leading to higher levels of surface runoff and thus higher erosivity for a given volume of rainfall.

55b44434f6bd.title: Surface runoff
55b44434f6bd.sentence: After water infiltrates the soil on an up-slope portion of a hill, the water may flow laterally through the soil, and exfiltrate (flow out of the soil) closer to a channel.

aa9de25f5e1c.title: Surface runoff
aa9de25f5e1c.sentence: This is called subsurface return flow or throughflow.

c5bab8386c6e.title: Surface runoff
c5bab8386c6e.sentence: As it flows, the amount of runoff may be reduced in a number of possible ways: a small portion of it may evapotranspire; water may become temporarily stored in microtopographic depressions; and a portion of it may infiltrate as it flows overland.

9050b722a3cf.title: Surface runoff
9050b722a3cf.sentence: Any remaining surface water eventually flows into a receiving water body such as a river, lake, estuary or ocean.

9c5865d15b32.title: Surface runoff
9c5865d15b32.sentence: Urban runoff is surface runoff of rainwater, landscape irrigation, and car washing created by urbanization.

afa0e44e2539.title: Surface runoff
afa0e44e2539.sentence: Impervious surfaces (roads, parking lots and sidewalks) are constructed during land development.

a4a9b2d90643.title: Surface runoff
a4a9b2d90643.sentence: During rain, storms, and other precipitation events, these surfaces (built from materials such as asphalt and concrete), along with rooftops, carry polluted stormwater to storm drains, instead of allowing the water to percolate through soil.

53c887d92043.title: Surface runoff
53c887d92043.sentence: This causes lowering of the water table (because groundwater recharge is lessened) and flooding since the amount of water that remains on the surface is greater.

6f1959e1d75e.title: Surface runoff
6f1959e1d75e.sentence: Increased runoff reduces groundwater recharge, thus lowering the water table and making droughts worse, especially for agricultural farmers and others who depend on the water wells.

b87dde217739.title: Surface runoff
b87dde217739.sentence: Most municipal storm sewer systems discharge untreated stormwater to streams, rivers, and bays.

88e75efc3f60.title: Surface runoff
88e75efc3f60.sentence: It is instead forced directly into streams or storm water runoff drains, where erosion and siltation can be major problems, even when flooding is not.

ae1d01c3b849.title: Subsidence
ae1d01c3b849.sentence: Seasonal drying of the soil results in a lowering of both the volume and the surface of the soil.

ee0f50950db7.title: Subsidence
ee0f50950db7.sentence: That can lead to the opposite of subsidence, known as heave or swelling of the soil, when the tree declines or is felled.

95e97993f1c6.title: Subsidence
95e97993f1c6.sentence: Many soils contain significant proportions of clay.

8cbfae4760a7.title: Subsidence
8cbfae4760a7.sentence: Because of the very small particle size, they are affected by changes in soil moisture content.

fab1cc820438.title: Subsidence
fab1cc820438.sentence: If building foundations are above the level reached by seasonal drying, they move, possibly resulting in damage to the building in the form of tapering cracks.

6b4e3f12398a.title: Subsidence
6b4e3f12398a.sentence: Trees and other vegetation can have a significant local effect on seasonal drying of soils.

d2008b9c82bb.title: Subsidence
d2008b9c82bb.sentence: Over a number of years, a cumulative drying occurs as the tree grows.

363673eb41f5.title: Subsidence
363673eb41f5.sentence: As the cumulative moisture deficit is reversed, which can last up to 25 years, the surface level around the tree will rise and expand laterally.

6cb6f8f33548.title: Stormwater
6cb6f8f33548.sentence: Managing the quantity and quality of stormwater is termed, "Stormwater Management." The term Best Management Practice (BMP) or stormwater control measure (SCM) is often used to refer to both structural or engineered control devices and systems (e.g. retention ponds) to treat or store polluted stormwater, as well as operational or procedural practices (e.g. street sweeping).

3493e0cbd35f.title: Stormwater
3493e0cbd35f.sentence: - planning and construction of stormwater systems like retention basins, buried vaults with various kinds of media filters, and vortex separators to remove coarse solids before they pollute surface waters or groundwater resources;

16174edc2545.title: Stormwater
16174edc2545.sentence: - building nature-based solutions such as ponds, swales, constructed wetlands or green infrastructure solutions to work with existing or "hard" drainage structures, such as pipes and concrete channels (constructed wetlands built for stormwater treatment can also serve as habitat for plants, amphibians and fish)

18a236d5fb26.title: Stormwater
18a236d5fb26.sentence: Passive treatment technologies use the energy of water flowing by gravity through ditches, canals, culverts, pipes or other constructed conveyances to enable treatment.

b77f61229b73.title: Stormwater
b77f61229b73.sentence: Self-dosing products, such as gel flocculants, are placed in the flowing water where sediment particles, colloids and flow energy combine to release the required dosage, thereby creating heavy flocs which can then be easily filtered or settled.

e5bf6f0679b8.title: Stormwater
e5bf6f0679b8.sentence: Natural woven fibers like jute are often used in ditch bottoms to act as filtration media.

5f169d8f0a63.title: Stormwater
5f169d8f0a63.sentence: Silt retention mats can also be placed in situ to capture floccules.

27800bc290c9.title: Stormwater
27800bc290c9.section: Stormwater treatment > Stormwater creation of sinkhole collapses
27800bc290c9.sentence: Instead, the stormwater enters the subsurface drainage system by moving down through the ground.

a5a2b3672680.title: Stormwater
a5a2b3672680.section: Stormwater treatment > Stormwater creation of sinkhole collapses
a5a2b3672680.sentence: When the subsurface water flow becomes great enough to transport soil and rock fragments, the karst openings grow rapidly.

415435fa6dfb.title: Stormwater
415435fa6dfb.section: Stormwater treatment > Stormwater creation of sinkhole collapses
415435fa6dfb.sentence: In undisturbed areas with natural subsurface (karst) drainage, soil and rock fragments choke karst openings, thereby being a self-limitation to the growth of openings.

d09187911f1e.title: Stormwater
d09187911f1e.section: Stormwater treatment > Stormwater creation of sinkhole collapses
d09187911f1e.sentence: The undisturbed karst drainage system becomes balanced with the climate so it can drain the water produced by most storms.

ae3264db1ac5.title: Stormwater
ae3264db1ac5.section: Stormwater treatment > Stormwater creation of sinkhole collapses
ae3264db1ac5.sentence: In urban areas with natural subsurface karst drainage there are no surface streams for the increased stormwater from impervious surfaces such as roofs, parking lots, and streets to receive drainage.

04872a66f5bd.title: Stormwater
04872a66f5bd.section: Stormwater treatment > Stormwater creation of sinkhole collapses
04872a66f5bd.sentence: Where karst openings are roofed by supportive (competent) limestone, there frequently is no surface warning that an opening has grown so large it will suddenly collapse catastrophically.

fe43b433fbe4.title: Stormwater
fe43b433fbe4.section: Stormwater treatment > Stormwater creation of sinkhole collapses
fe43b433fbe4.sentence: It is recommended that land-use planning agencies avoid karst areas when considering new development projects.

c27894e567da.title: Runoff (hydrology)
c27894e567da.sentence: A runoff models or rainfall-runoff model describes how rainfall is converted into runoff in a drainage basin (catchment area or watershed).

82a5882ab576.title: Runoff (hydrology)
82a5882ab576.sentence: More precisely, it produces a surface runoff hydrograph in response to a rainfall event, represented by and input as a hyetograph.

5974a6b7c944.title: Runoff (hydrology)
5974a6b7c944.sentence: Rainfall-runoff models need to be calibrated before they can be used.

9f88e5a47da6.title: Runoff (hydrology)
9f88e5a47da6.sentence: A well known runoff model is the linear reservoir, but in practice it has limited applicability.

68f2b6663748.title: Runoff (hydrology)
68f2b6663748.sentence: The runoff model with a non-linear reservoir is more universally applicable, but still it holds only for catchments whose surface area is limited by the condition that the rainfall can be considered more or less uniformly distributed over the area.

55cc41d7922d.title: Runoff (hydrology)
55cc41d7922d.sentence: When the study area is too large, it can be divided into sub-catchments and the various runoff hydrographs may be combined using flood routing techniques.

ad221936c325.title: Hydrological transport model
ad221936c325.sentence: An hydrological transport model is a mathematical model used to simulate the flow of rivers, streams, groundwater movement or drainage front displacement, and calculate water quality parameters.

ff3ee5ae9f86.title: Hydrological transport model
ff3ee5ae9f86.sentence: These models generally came into use in the 1960s and 1970s when demand for numerical forecasting of water quality and drainage was driven by environmental legislation, and at a similar time widespread access to significant computer power became available.

ad97419d91fc.title: Hydrological transport model
ad97419d91fc.sentence: Physically based models (sometimes known as deterministic, comprehensive or process-based models) try to represent the physical processes observed in the real world.

79cbe8970617.title: Hydrological transport model
79cbe8970617.sentence: Typically, such models contain representations of surface runoff, subsurface flow, evapotranspiration, and channel flow, but they can be far more complicated.

258469008a69.title: Hydrological transport model
258469008a69.sentence: These models based on data are black box systems, using mathematical and statistical concepts to link a certain input (for instance rainfall) to the model output (for instance runoff).

ac277b4a39c8.title: Hydrological transport model
ac277b4a39c8.sentence: A key component of a hydrological transport model is the surface runoff element, which allows assessment of sediment, fertilizer, pesticide and other chemical contaminants.

2d2c5d88eee9.title: Hydrological transport model
2d2c5d88eee9.sentence: Robert E. Horton's seminal work on surface runoff along with his coupling of quantitative treatment of erosion laid the groundwork for modern chemical transport hydrology.

a6e7fef68531.title: Quick clay
a6e7fef68531.sentence: The thickness of EDL depends on the salinity of water.

d4aa88fedd43.title: Quick clay
d4aa88fedd43.sentence: Clay mineral particles are always negatively charged because of the presence of permanent negative charges and pH dependent charges at their surface.

2e0e5d19aeaa.title: Quick clay
2e0e5d19aeaa.sentence: Because of the need to respect electro-neutrality and a net zero electrical charge balance, these negative electrical charges are always compensated by the positive charges born by cations (such as Na+) adsorbed onto the surface of the clay, or present in the clay pore water.

651e4fa49a20.title: Quick clay
651e4fa49a20.sentence: Exchangeable cations are present in the clay minerals interlayers and on the external basal planes of clay platelets.

c8b1b2c761c5.title: Quick clay
c8b1b2c761c5.sentence: Under salty conditions (at high ionic strength) EDL is compressed (or said to be collapsed).

b96d25e22c96.title: Quick clay
b96d25e22c96.sentence: It facilitates the aggregation of clay platelets which flocculate and stick together in a more stable aggregates structure.

301dd535fdad.title: Quick clay
301dd535fdad.sentence: After the marine clay deposit is uplifted and is no longer exposed to salt water conditions, rainwater can slowly infiltrate the poorly compacted clay layer and the excess of NaCl present in seawater can also diffuse out of the clay.

419678a04da0.title: Quick clay
419678a04da0.sentence: As a result, the EDL is less compressed and can expand.

bf6f62141c44.title: Quick clay
bf6f62141c44.sentence: It results in a stronger electrostatic repulsion between negatively charged clay platelets which can more easily become dispersed and form stable suspensions in water (peptization phenomenon).

122d5442302c.title: Quick clay
122d5442302c.sentence: The effect leads to a destabilization of the clay aggregates structure.

52cdc3365720.title: Quick clay
52cdc3365720.sentence: Quick clay regains strength rapidly when salt is again added (compression of the EDL), which allows clay particles to restore their cohesion with one another.

d0996f690705.title: Runoff curve number
d0996f690705.sentence: To account for different soils' ability to infiltrate, NRCS has divided soils into four hydrologic soil groups (HSGs).

015277ae8bfe.title: Runoff curve number
015277ae8bfe.sentence: The NRCS curve number is related to soil type, soil infiltration capability, land use, and the depth of the seasonal high water table.

8e8535684ef2.title: Runoff curve number
8e8535684ef2.sentence: - HSG Group A (low runoff potential): Soils with high infiltration rates even when thoroughly wetted.

363693e3ba26.title: Runoff curve number
363693e3ba26.sentence: These consist chiefly of deep, well-drained sands and gravels.

87de9f0081de.title: Runoff curve number
87de9f0081de.sentence: These soils have a high rate of water transmission (final infiltration rate greater than 0.30 in (7.6 mm) per hour).

59b15d53a7be.title: Runoff curve number
59b15d53a7be.sentence: These soils have a moderate rate of water transmission (final infiltration rate of 0.15–0.30 in (3.8–7.6 mm) per hour).

807d257edae4.title: Runoff curve number
807d257edae4.sentence: These soils have a slow rate of water transmission (final infiltration rate 0.05–0.15 in (1.3–3.8 mm) per hour).

46afdb62f326.title: Runoff curve number
46afdb62f326.sentence: These consist chiefly of soils with a layer that impedes downward movement of water or soils with moderately fine to fine textures.

42dd8f109515.title: Runoff curve number
42dd8f109515.sentence: - HSG Group D (high runoff potential): Soils with very slow infiltration rates when thoroughly wetted.

d14ec2149cff.title: Runoff curve number
d14ec2149cff.sentence: These consist chiefly of clay soils with a high swelling potential, soils with a permanent high water table, soils with a claypan or clay layer at or near the surface, and shallow soils over nearly impervious materials.

896506aba384.title: Runoff curve number
896506aba384.sentence: These soils have a very slow rate of water transmission (final infiltration rate less than 0.05 in (1.3 mm) per hour).

0dda13d3363b.title: Runoff curve number
0dda13d3363b.sentence: Selection of a hydrologic soil group should be done based on measured infiltration rates, soil survey (such as the NRCS Web Soil Survey), or judgement from a qualified soil science or geotechnical professional.

691515b2974b.title: Runoff curve number
691515b2974b.sentence: The runoff curve number (also called a curve number or simply CN) is an empirical parameter used in hydrology for predicting direct runoff or infiltration from rainfall excess.

a15508bf3933.title: Runoff curve number
a15508bf3933.sentence: The curve number method was developed by the USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service, which was formerly called the Soil Conservation Service or SCS—the number is still popularly known as a "SCS runoff curve number" in the literature.

ed64df18399d.title: Runoff curve number
ed64df18399d.sentence: The runoff curve number was developed from an empirical analysis of runoff from small catchments and hillslope plots monitored by the USDA.

92428c4eb25d.title: Runoff curve number
92428c4eb25d.sentence: The runoff curve number is based on the area's hydrologic soil group, land use, treatment and hydrologic condition.

3156ffc24bde.title: Runoff curve number
3156ffc24bde.sentence: CN has a range from 30 to 100; lower numbers indicate low runoff potential while larger numbers are for increasing runoff potential.

cf5867d027c2.title: Runoff curve number
cf5867d027c2.sentence: The lower the curve number, the more permeable the soil is.

241e3b88c9c9.title: Runoff curve number
241e3b88c9c9.sentence: Ia is the initial abstraction ([L]; in), or the amount of water before runoff, such as infiltration, or rainfall interception by vegetation; historically, it has generally been assumed that Ia=0.2S, although more recent research has found that Ia=0.05S may be a more appropriate relationship in urbanized watersheds where the CN is updated to reflect developed conditions.

b125571483c9.title: Runoff curve number
b125571483c9.sentence: As can be seen in the curve number equation, runoff cannot begin until the initial abstraction has been met.

514c0383e3e1.title: Runoff curve number
514c0383e3e1.sentence: The curve number methodology is an event-based calculation, and should not be used for a single annual rainfall value, as this will incorrectly miss the effects of antecedent moisture and the necessity of an initial abstraction threshold.

ecb4f3604042.title: Runoff curve number
ecb4f3604042.sentence: Runoff is affected by the soil moisture before a precipitation event, the antecedent moisture condition (AMC).

32a39b61511a.title: Runoff curve number
32a39b61511a.sentence: The other moisture conditions are dry, AMC I or CNI, and moist, AMC III or CNIII.

64659a163573.title: Runoff curve number
64659a163573.sentence: It is widely used and is an efficient method for determining the approximate amount of direct runoff from a rainfall event in a particular area.

46b4ae2aed5d.title: Soil and Water Assessment Tool
46b4ae2aed5d.sentence: Soil and Water Assessment Tool (SWAT) is a free and open source hydrology model and GIS computer simulation sponsored by the USDA.

ab3e46fd526b.title: Soil and Water Assessment Tool
ab3e46fd526b.sentence: SWAT is a well known geographic hydrological model in use by many universities and government agencies around the world, and integrates with commercial products like ArcGIS.

17ed7b62dc4e.title: Soil erosion
17ed7b62dc4e.sentence: Soil erosion is the denudation or wearing away of the upper layer of soil.

5c78828bfe15.title: Soil erosion
5c78828bfe15.sentence: It is a form of soil degradation.

b5d5de1e9b5b.title: Soil erosion
b5d5de1e9b5b.sentence: This natural process is caused by the dynamic activity of erosive agents, that is, water (e.g. landslide, flooding), ice (e.g. glaciers), snow (e.g. avalanches, snow gliding), air (e.g. wind), plants (e.g. tree uprooting), and animals (including humans).

f232fcbb982d.title: Soil erosion
f232fcbb982d.sentence: In accordance with these agents, erosion is sometimes divided into water erosion, glacial erosion, snow erosion, wind (aeolian) erosion, zoogenic erosion and anthropogenic erosion such as tillage erosion.

1ae504c7fa9d.title: Soil erosion
1ae504c7fa9d.sentence: Soil erosion may be a slow process that continues relatively unnoticed, or it may occur at an alarming rate causing a serious loss of topsoil.

1fa524b89996.title: Soil erosion
1fa524b89996.sentence: Human activities have increased by ca. 28 times the rate at which erosion is naturally occurring world-wide.

8f1ca9673a4a.title: Soil erosion
8f1ca9673a4a.sentence: Excessive (or accelerated) erosion causes both "on-site" and "off-site" problems.

1dac1f7f97f9.title: Soil erosion
1dac1f7f97f9.sentence: On-site impacts include decreases in agricultural productivity and (on natural landscapes) ecological collapse, both because of loss of the nutrient-rich upper soil layers.

4f9b5910c04e.title: Soil erosion
4f9b5910c04e.sentence: In some cases, the eventual result is desertification.

a55068fbe0c2.title: Soil erosion
a55068fbe0c2.sentence: Off-site effects include sedimentation of waterways and eutrophication of water bodies, as well as sediment-related damage to roads and houses.

ea84f4fb4657.title: Soil erosion
ea84f4fb4657.sentence: Water and wind erosion are the two primary causes of land degradation; combined, they are responsible for about 84% of the global extent of degraded land, making excessive erosion one of the most significant environmental problems worldwide.

32ee1bd97055.title: Soil erosion
32ee1bd97055.sentence: Each year, about 75 billion tons of soil is eroded from the land, a rate that is about 13–40 times as fast as the natural rate of erosion.

e770d11817ca.title: Soil erosion
e770d11817ca.sentence: According to a new study published in Nature Communications, almost 36 billion tons of soil is lost every year due to water, and deforestation and other changes in land use make the problem worse.

06cf1906534a.title: Soil erosion
06cf1906534a.section: Physical processes > Rainfall and surface runoff
06cf1906534a.sentence: Rainfall, and the surface runoff which may result from rainfall, produce four main types of soil erosion: splash erosion, sheet erosion, rill erosion, and gully erosion.

35ab98e2ca14.title: Soil erosion
35ab98e2ca14.section: Physical processes > Rainfall and surface runoff
35ab98e2ca14.sentence: If the soil is saturated, or if the rainfall rate is greater than the rate at which water can infiltrate into the soil, surface runoff occurs.

0551ba42da9f.title: Soil erosion
0551ba42da9f.section: Physical processes > Rainfall and surface runoff
0551ba42da9f.sentence: If the runoff has sufficient flow energy, it will transport loosened soil particles (sediment) down the slope.

dbaa6beb3e08.title: Soil erosion
dbaa6beb3e08.section: Physical processes > Rainfall and surface runoff
dbaa6beb3e08.sentence: Splash erosion is generally seen as the first and least severe stage in the soil erosion process, which is followed by sheet erosion, then rill erosion and finally gully erosion (the most severe of the four).

f03971a37af4.title: Surface runoff
f03971a37af4.section: Effects of surface runoff > Erosion and deposition
f03971a37af4.sentence: Soil surface roughness may cause runoff to become concentrated into narrower flow paths: as these incise, the small but well-defined channels which are formed are known as rills.

5f659f1a2820.title: Surface runoff
5f659f1a2820.section: Effects of surface runoff > Erosion and deposition
5f659f1a2820.sentence: If runoff continues to incise and enlarge rills, they may eventually grow to become gullies.

c7aaff49c0da.title: Soil erosion
c7aaff49c0da.sentence: Eroded hilltops are actually caused by tillage erosion as water erosion mainly causes soil losses in the midslope and lowerslope segments of a slope, not the hilltops.

37081420fd2f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/05%3A_Soil_Physics_and_Water_Relations/5.08%3A_Soil_Erosion
37081420fd2f.sentence: Water erosion… begins with detachment as rain drops bombard soil aggregates, separating some of them from the aggregate.

a4c006b2e682.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/05%3A_Soil_Physics_and_Water_Relations/5.08%3A_Soil_Erosion
a4c006b2e682.sentence: These stand-alone soil particles are much smaller and are more easily transported.

229e91ac3507.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/05%3A_Soil_Physics_and_Water_Relations/5.08%3A_Soil_Erosion
