229e91ac3507.sentence: Transport can happen due to splashes from the raindrop, or from running water carrying sediment downhill.

10032d897bf7.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/05%3A_Soil_Physics_and_Water_Relations/5.08%3A_Soil_Erosion
10032d897bf7.sentence: The majority of soil erosion is due to sheet and rill erosion.

645fc3c92394.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/05%3A_Soil_Physics_and_Water_Relations/5.08%3A_Soil_Erosion
645fc3c92394.sentence: Rills can be smoothed by tillage equipment.

78ff870b4abe.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/05%3A_Soil_Physics_and_Water_Relations/5.08%3A_Soil_Erosion
78ff870b4abe.sentence: If enough water gathers, a gully can form, which is essentially a large rill that is so deep that it cannot be smoothed by tillage equipment.

79dcdbde1de5.title: Soil erosion
79dcdbde1de5.sentence: The amount and intensity of precipitation is the main climatic factor governing soil erosion by water.

256928d910d7.title: Soil erosion
256928d910d7.sentence: In some areas of the world (e.g. the Midwestern United States and the Amazon Rainforest), rainfall intensity is the primary determinant of erosivity, with higher intensity rainfall generally resulting in more soil erosion by water.

c7456083cc10.title: Soil erosion
c7456083cc10.sentence: The relationship is particularly strong if heavy rainfall occurs at times when, or in locations where, the soil's surface is not well protected by vegetation.

2a61587b7e36.title: Soil erosion
2a61587b7e36.sentence: The size and velocity of rain drops is also an important factor.

cb0ca229a64f.title: Soil erosion
cb0ca229a64f.sentence: Larger and higher-velocity rain drops have greater kinetic energy, and thus their impact will displace soil particles by larger distances than smaller, slower-moving rain drops.

4eddb40bca6f.title: Soil erosion
4eddb40bca6f.sentence: In other regions of the world (e.g. western Europe), runoff and erosion result from relatively low intensities of stratiform rainfall falling onto previously saturated soil.

e5090800a850.title: Soil erosion
e5090800a850.sentence: In such situations, rainfall amount rather than intensity is the main factor determining the severity of soil erosion by water.

db310249f2c0.title: Soil erosion
db310249f2c0.section: Monitoring, measuring and modelling soil erosion
db310249f2c0.sentence: where R is the rainfall erosivity factor, K is the soil erodibility factor, L and S are topographic factors representing length and slope, respectively, C is the cover and management factor and P is the support practices factor.

fc4136789d13.title: Soil erosion
fc4136789d13.sentence: An extensive global data collection effort produced the Global Rainfall Erosivity Database (GloREDa) which includes rainfall erosivity for 3,625 stations and covers 63 countries.

0b04690e31e4.title: Soil erosion
0b04690e31e4.sentence: This first ever Global Rainfall Erosivity Database was used to develop a global erosivity map at 30 arc-seconds(~1 km) based on sophisticated geostatistical process.

6c8298f69e7f.title: Soil erosion
6c8298f69e7f.sentence: Wind erosion is of two primary varieties: deflation, where the wind picks up and carries away loose particles; and abrasion, where surfaces are worn down as they are struck by airborne particles carried by wind.

a38b20b8cb8d.title: Soil erosion
a38b20b8cb8d.sentence: Wind erosion is a major geomorphological force, especially in arid and semi-arid regions.

85e81d546019.title: Soil erosion
85e81d546019.sentence: It is also a major source of land degradation, evaporation, desertification, harmful airborne dust, and crop damage—especially after being increased far above natural rates by human activities such as deforestation, urbanization, and agriculture.

154f68921ecb.title: Soil erosion
154f68921ecb.sentence: Deflation is divided into three categories: (1) surface creep, where larger, heavier particles slide or roll along the ground; (2) saltation, where particles are lifted a short height into the air, and bounce and saltate across the surface of the soil; and (3) suspension, where very small and light particles are lifted into the air by the wind, and are often carried for long distances (e.g. Saharan dust).

eff0a25c1431.title: Soil erosion
eff0a25c1431.sentence: Saltation is responsible for the majority (50–70%) of wind erosion, followed by suspension (30–40%), and then surface creep (5–25%).

0fadd9c1edc3.title: Soil erosion
0fadd9c1edc3.sentence: Silty soils (e.g. loess) tend to be the most affected by wind erosion; silt particles are relatively easily detached and carried away.

f4f40b15af60.title: Soil erosion
f4f40b15af60.sentence: Wind erosion requires strong winds, particularly during times of drought when vegetation is sparse and soil is dry (and so is more erodible).

5e2322f35f5b.title: Soil erosion
5e2322f35f5b.sentence: Wind erosion is much more severe in arid areas and during times of drought.

f268681de795.title: Soil erosion
f268681de795.sentence: For example, in the Great Plains, it is estimated that soil loss due to wind erosion can be as much as 6100 times greater in drought years than in wet years.

741c3957404f.title: Soil erosion
741c3957404f.section: Human activities that aid soil erosion > Agricultural practices
741c3957404f.sentence: Tillage also increases wind erosion rates, by dehydrating the soil and breaking it up into smaller particles that can be picked up by the wind.

a89f1a4e0d45.title: Soil erosion
a89f1a4e0d45.section: Human activities that aid soil erosion > Agricultural practices
a89f1a4e0d45.sentence: Exacerbating this is the fact that most of the trees are generally removed from agricultural fields, allowing winds to have long, open runs to travel over at higher speeds.

56ea9d2f96b5.title: Soil erosion
56ea9d2f96b5.section: Factors affecting soil erosion > Vegetative cover
56ea9d2f96b5.sentence: It shelters the soil from winds, which results in decreased wind erosion, as well as advantageous changes in microclimate.

259ac57fa727.title: Soil erosion
259ac57fa727.sentence: Windbreaks (also called shelterbelts) are rows of trees and shrubs that are planted along the edges of agricultural fields, to shield the fields against winds.

978b7163c86b.title: Soil erosion
978b7163c86b.sentence: In addition to significantly reducing wind erosion, windbreaks provide many other benefits such as improved microclimates for crops (which are sheltered from the dehydrating and otherwise damaging effects of wind), habitat for beneficial bird species, carbon sequestration, and aesthetic improvements to the agricultural landscape.

6f9b2612794e.title: Erosion control
6f9b2612794e.sentence: Erosion control is the practice of preventing or controlling wind or water erosion in agriculture, land development, coastal areas, river banks and construction.

c58904762c27.title: Erosion control
c58904762c27.sentence: Effective erosion controls handle surface runoff and are important techniques in preventing water pollution, soil loss, wildlife habitat loss and human property loss.

afb74790ae1f.title: Erosion control
afb74790ae1f.sentence: The controls often involve the creation of a physical barrier, such as vegetation or rock, to absorb some of the energy of the wind or water that is causing the erosion.

58ac9e968972.title: Erosion control
58ac9e968972.sentence: Examples of erosion control methods include the following:

adca2787a73c.title: Soil erosion
adca2787a73c.sentence: Terracing is an extremely effective means of erosion control, which has been practiced for thousands of years by people all over the world.

47f33714734c.title: Soil erosion
47f33714734c.sentence: Traditional planting methods, such as mixed-cropping (instead of monocropping) and crop rotation, have also been shown to significantly reduce erosion rates.

fb69b4fbf43c.title: Soil erosion
fb69b4fbf43c.sentence: Crop residues play a role in the mitigation of erosion by conservation tillage methods, because they reduce the impact of raindrops breaking up the soil particles.

e887601c06e0.title: Soil erosion
e887601c06e0.sentence: Forages have a fibrous root system, which helps combat erosion by anchoring the plants to the top layer of the soil, and covering the entirety of the field, as it is a non-row crop.

7a3118626a81.title: Soil erosion
7a3118626a81.sentence: Agroforestry, the mixing of agricultural crops with trees, is an efficient mean of mitigating soil erosion, in particular in tropical climates with heavy rains, but also everywhere land has been severely degraded by intensive agriculture activities (e.g. ravine lands).

da4e7286c3b4.title: Erosion control
da4e7286c3b4.sentence: On construction sites they are often implemented in conjunction with sediment controls such as sediment basins and silt fences.

8e8fd29e5008.title: Erosion control
8e8fd29e5008.sentence: In urban areas erosion controls are often part of stormwater runoff management programs required by local governments.

1fb0ef4a6acf.title: Erosion control
1fb0ef4a6acf.sentence: Bank erosion is a natural process: without it, rivers would not meander and change course.

c589ddb552a5.title: Erosion control
c589ddb552a5.sentence: In many places, whether or not the banks are unstable due to human activities, people try to keep a river in a single place.

dddc8b67c05b.title: Erosion control
dddc8b67c05b.sentence: One way that this is done is by placing riprap or gabions along the bank.

473fe89f3948.title: Erosion control
473fe89f3948.sentence: Since the 1920s and 1930s scientists have been creating mathematical models for understanding the mechanisms of soil erosion and resulting sediment surface runoff, including an early paper by Albert Einstein applying Baer's law.

f04eccddd980.title: Dust
f04eccddd980.sentence: Dust is made of fine particles of solid matter.

a8587117dd56.title: Dust
a8587117dd56.sentence: On Earth, it generally consists of particles in the atmosphere that come from various sources such as soil lifted by wind (an aeolian process), volcanic eruptions, and pollution.

156a9fb2a8a8.title: Dust
156a9fb2a8a8.sentence: Dust can be considered an aerosol when fine particles remain suspended in the atmosphere for extended time.

c5bb6353e455.title: Dust
c5bb6353e455.sentence: Atmospheric or wind-borne fugitive dust, also known as aeolian process dust, as transported through the troposphere, primarily comes from saltation and dry regions where high-speed winds can remove mostly silt-sized, up to 1/16mm, material that will abrade susceptible surfaces to create more dust.

5fe049a9f996.title: Dust
5fe049a9f996.sentence: This includes areas where grazing, ploughing, vehicle use, and other human behaviors have further destabilized the land, though not all dust source areas have been largely affected by anthropogenic impacts.

d7889a41324f.title: Dust
d7889a41324f.sentence: Dust-producing surfaces cover one-third of the global land area, roughly 13 billion hectares, made up of hyper-arid regions like the Sahara, which covers 0.9 billion hectares, and drylands, which occupy 5.2 billion hectares.

aecdcdf00cad.title: Dust
aecdcdf00cad.sentence: Saharan dust, in particular, can be transported and deposited as far as the Caribbean and the Amazon basin and may affect air temperature, ocean temperature, and rainfall amounts.

4b18fdbc46c0.title: Aeolian processes
4b18fdbc46c0.sentence: - An average of 132 million tons of dust from the Sahara (primarily the Sahel and Bodélé Depression) across the Atlantic each year.

314ead511caf.title: Soil erosion
314ead511caf.section: Global environmental effects > Airborne dust pollution
314ead511caf.sentence: Soil particles picked up during wind erosion of soil are a major source of air pollution, in the form of airborne particulates called dust.

07dde80ffff3.title: Soil erosion
07dde80ffff3.section: Global environmental effects > Airborne dust pollution
07dde80ffff3.sentence: These airborne soil particles are often contaminated with toxic chemicals such as pesticides or petroleum fuels, posing ecological and public health hazards when they later land, or are inhaled/ingested.

01172683785c.title: Soil erosion
01172683785c.section: Global environmental effects > Airborne dust pollution
01172683785c.sentence: Dust from erosion acts to suppress rainfall and changes the sky color from blue to white, which leads to an increase in red sunsets.

f6fb0d963de1.title: Soil erosion
f6fb0d963de1.section: Global environmental effects > Airborne dust pollution
f6fb0d963de1.sentence: Dust events have been linked to a decline in the health of coral reefs across the Caribbean and Florida, primarily since the 1970s.

46bd2917026e.title: Dust
46bd2917026e.sentence: Dust poses a health risk to children, older people, and those with respiratory diseases.

ca165b330ee3.title: Soil erosion
ca165b330ee3.section: Factors affecting soil erosion > Vegetative cover
ca165b330ee3.sentence: Vegetation acts as an interface between the atmosphere and the soil.

0fbf800c8bd0.title: Soil erosion
0fbf800c8bd0.sentence: The most effective known method for erosion prevention is to increase vegetative cover on the land, which helps prevent both wind and water erosion.

18fe51d149a1.title: Soil erosion
18fe51d149a1.section: Factors affecting soil erosion > Vegetative cover
18fe51d149a1.sentence: The roots of the plants bind the soil together, and interweave with other roots, forming a more solid mass that is less susceptible to both water and wind erosion.

eaf5f0d0dce5.title: Soil erosion
eaf5f0d0dce5.section: Factors affecting soil erosion > Vegetative cover
eaf5f0d0dce5.sentence: The removal of vegetation increases the rate of surface erosion.

6053fd327f50.title: Soil erosion
6053fd327f50.section: Human activities that aid soil erosion > Deforestation
6053fd327f50.sentence: In an undisturbed forest, the mineral soil is protected by a layer of leaf litter and humus that covers the forest floor.

e065d8eec458.title: Soil erosion
e065d8eec458.section: Human activities that aid soil erosion > Deforestation
e065d8eec458.sentence: These two layers form a protective mat over the soil that absorbs the impact of rain drops.

0b3b1ae8ac87.title: Soil erosion
0b3b1ae8ac87.section: Human activities that aid soil erosion > Deforestation
0b3b1ae8ac87.sentence: They are porous and highly permeable to rainfall, and allow rainwater to slow percolate into the soil below, instead of flowing over the surface as runoff.

c0255de0ccb2.title: Soil erosion
c0255de0ccb2.section: Human activities that aid soil erosion > Deforestation
c0255de0ccb2.sentence: However it is the forest floor, more than the canopy, that prevents surface erosion.

dd853f605b8d.title: Soil erosion
dd853f605b8d.section: Human activities that aid soil erosion > Deforestation
dd853f605b8d.sentence: The terminal velocity of rain drops is reached in about 8 metres (26 feet).

4dbfa2050093.title: Soil erosion
4dbfa2050093.section: Human activities that aid soil erosion > Deforestation
4dbfa2050093.sentence: Because forest canopies are usually higher than this, rain drops can often regain terminal velocity even after striking the canopy.

dce693158a24.title: Soil erosion
dce693158a24.section: Human activities that aid soil erosion > Agricultural practices
dce693158a24.sentence: Unsustainable agricultural practices increase rates of erosion by one to two orders of magnitude over the natural rate and far exceed replacement by soil production.

01c45b66491d.title: Soil erosion
01c45b66491d.section: Human activities that aid soil erosion > Agricultural practices
01c45b66491d.sentence: The tillage of agricultural lands, which breaks up soil into finer particles, is one of the primary factors.

ceb4d9775b3d.title: Soil erosion
ceb4d9775b3d.section: Human activities that aid soil erosion > Agricultural practices
ceb4d9775b3d.sentence: The problem has been exacerbated in modern times, due to mechanized agricultural equipment that allows for deep plowing, which severely increases the amount of soil that is available for transport by water erosion.

70a787487152.title: Soil erosion
70a787487152.section: Human activities that aid soil erosion > Agricultural practices
70a787487152.sentence: Others include monocropping, farming on steep slopes, pesticide and chemical fertilizer usage (which kill organisms that bind soil together), row-cropping, and the use of surface irrigation.

8a49268ef6bf.title: Soil erosion
8a49268ef6bf.section: Human activities that aid soil erosion > Agricultural practices
8a49268ef6bf.sentence: Heavy grazing reduces vegetative cover and causes severe soil compaction, both of which increase erosion rates.

18d3b465574e.title: Soil erosion
18d3b465574e.section: Human activities that aid soil erosion > Agricultural practices
18d3b465574e.sentence: A complex overall situation with respect to defining nutrient losses from soils, could arise as a result of the size selective nature of soil erosion events.

27fceda7b951.title: Soil erosion
27fceda7b951.section: Human activities that aid soil erosion > Agricultural practices
27fceda7b951.sentence: Loss of total phosphorus, for instance, in the finer eroded fraction is greater relative to the whole soil.

afb52267e396.title: Erosion
afb52267e396.sentence: At agriculture sites in the Appalachian Mountains, intensive farming practices have caused erosion at up to 100 times the natural rate of erosion in the region.

4c202bffdd77.title: Soil erosion
4c202bffdd77.sentence: There is a higher potential for erosion when producing potatoes than when growing cereals, or oilseed crops.

7786793bc27e.title: Surface runoff
7786793bc27e.section: Effects of surface runoff > Erosion and deposition
7786793bc27e.sentence: Over a third of the U.S. Corn Belt has completely lost its topsoil.

d3f72d9fba81.title: Surface runoff
d3f72d9fba81.section: Effects of surface runoff > Erosion and deposition
d3f72d9fba81.sentence: Switching to no-till practices would reduce soil erosion from U.S. agricultural fields by more than 70 percent.

df19e7cd32de.title: Erodibility
df19e7cd32de.sentence: Erodability (or erodibility) is the inherent yielding or nonresistance of soils and rocks to erosion.

9fa7660f15d0.title: Erodibility
9fa7660f15d0.sentence: A high erodibility implies that the same amount of work exerted by the erosion processes leads to a larger removal of material.

c34557b7458d.title: Erodibility
c34557b7458d.sentence: Soil erodibility is a lumped parameter that represents an integrated annual value of the soil profile reaction to the process of soil detachment and transport by raindrops and surface flow.

bb1a7dc5df14.sentence: where R is the rainfall erosivity factor, K is the soil erodibility, L and S are topographic factors representing length and slope, and C and P are cropping management factors.

b5f9fbf40442.title: Soil erosion
b5f9fbf40442.section: Factors affecting soil erosion > Soil structure and composition
b5f9fbf40442.sentence: Sediments containing more clay minerals tend to be more resistant to erosion than those with sand or silt, because the clay helps bind soil particles together.

44b3f6e65e44.title: Soil erosion
44b3f6e65e44.section: Factors affecting soil erosion > Soil structure and composition
44b3f6e65e44.sentence: Soil containing high levels of organic matter are often more resistant to erosion, because the organic materials coagulate soil colloids and create a stronger, more stable soil structure.

9f0cfb3060c4.title: Rill
9f0cfb3060c4.section: Rills created by erosion > Significance of rill erosion
9f0cfb3060c4.sentence: They are also very common in agricultural areas because sustained agriculture depletes the soil of much of its organic content, increasing the erodibility of the soil.

49ea84e35431.title: Soil erosion
49ea84e35431.section: Factors affecting soil erosion > Soil structure and composition
49ea84e35431.sentence: More compacted soils will have a larger amount of surface runoff than less compacted soils.

f8419409da24.title: Erodibility
f8419409da24.sentence: Other factors such as the stone content (referred as stoniness), which acts as protection against soil erosion, are very significant in Mediterranean countries.

bd5b5cf13d85.title: Erodibility
bd5b5cf13d85.sentence: This model can also be applied to soils.

813a9a444a8e.title: Erodibility
813a9a444a8e.sentence: In this case, the erodibility, Kτ, can be estimated using a hole erosion test or a jet erosion test.

0389d570aeb0.title: Soil erosion
0389d570aeb0.section: Monitoring, measuring and modelling soil erosion
0389d570aeb0.sentence: These can be measured using geotechnical engineering methods such as the hole erosion test or the jet erosion test.

b23de27e2b00.title: Soil erosion
b23de27e2b00.section: Human activities that aid soil erosion > Climate change
b23de27e2b00.sentence: The warmer atmospheric temperatures observed over the past decades are expected to lead to a more vigorous hydrological cycle, including more extreme rainfall events.

357012e601e1.title: Soil erosion
357012e601e1.section: Human activities that aid soil erosion > Climate change
357012e601e1.sentence: Soil erosion rates are expected to change in response to changes in climate for a variety of reasons.

6176262c2d0b.title: Soil erosion
6176262c2d0b.section: Human activities that aid soil erosion > Climate change
6176262c2d0b.sentence: Studies on soil erosion suggest that increased rainfall amounts and intensities will lead to greater rates of soil erosion.

20680ed603ef.title: Soil erosion
20680ed603ef.section: Human activities that aid soil erosion > Climate change
20680ed603ef.sentence: Thus, if rainfall amounts and intensities increase in many parts of the world as expected, erosion will also increase, unless amelioration measures are taken.

0362bee5ba12.title: Soil erosion
0362bee5ba12.section: Human activities that aid soil erosion > Climate change
0362bee5ba12.sentence: Studies by Pruski and Nearing indicated that, other factors such as land use unconsidered, it is reasonable to expect approximately a 1.7% change in soil erosion for each 1% change in total precipitation under climate change.

fd259496d743.title: Soil erosion
fd259496d743.section: Human activities that aid soil erosion > Climate change
fd259496d743.sentence: Studies performed at the onset of the 21st century predicted increases of rainfall erosivity over the 21st century by 17% in the United States, by 18% in Europe, and globally 30 to 66%.

3101c5d190d4.title: Soil erosion
3101c5d190d4.section: Human activities that aid soil erosion > Climate change
3101c5d190d4.sentence: Other reasons include: a) changes in plant canopy caused by shifts in plant biomass production associated with moisture regime; b) changes in litter cover on the ground caused by changes in both plant residue decomposition rates driven by temperature and moisture dependent soil microbial activity as well as plant biomass production rates; c) changes in soil moisture due to shifting precipitation regimes and evapotranspiration rates, which changes infiltration and runoff ratios; d) soil erodibility changes due to decrease in soil organic matter concentrations in soils that lead to a soil structure that is more susceptible to erosion and increased runoff due to increased soil surface sealing and crusting; e) a shift of winter precipitation from non-erosive snow to erosive rainfall due to increasing winter temperatures; f) melting of permafrost, which induces an erodible soil state from a previously non-erodible one; and g) shifts in land use made necessary to accommodate new climatic regimes.

99f923531659.title: Soil erosion
99f923531659.section: Human activities that aid soil erosion > Deforestation
99f923531659.sentence: Deforestation causes increased erosion rates due to exposure of mineral soil by removing the humus and litter layers from the soil surface, removing the vegetative cover that binds soil together, and causing heavy soil compaction from logging equipment.

7e51d7923a51.title: Soil erosion
7e51d7923a51.section: Human activities that aid soil erosion > Deforestation
7e51d7923a51.sentence: Once trees have been removed by fire or logging, infiltration rates become high and erosion low to the degree the forest floor remains intact.

c17175a53b93.title: Soil erosion
c17175a53b93.section: Human activities that aid soil erosion > Deforestation
c17175a53b93.sentence: Severe fires can lead to significant further erosion if followed by heavy rainfall.

be2d6c7ed376.title: Soil erosion
be2d6c7ed376.section: Human activities that aid soil erosion > Deforestation
be2d6c7ed376.sentence: Globally one of the largest contributors to erosive soil loss is the slash-and-burn treatment of tropical forests.

2d6f04823b42.title: Soil erosion
2d6f04823b42.section: Human activities that aid soil erosion > Deforestation
2d6f04823b42.sentence: It has been shown in Brazil that along a complete cycle of slash-and-burn cultivation (including forest regrowth) runoff and soil loss decrease exponentially from the burned phase of shifting to the early stages of secondary forest, exhibiting patterns similar to those of a forested area after just 4–5 years of regeneration.

9568f36745e8.title: Soil erosion
9568f36745e8.section: Human activities that aid soil erosion > Deforestation
9568f36745e8.sentence: Another Brazilian study showed that a fallow period of 15 years after a crop cycle of slash-and-burn agriculture can restore the original soil conditions.

4b48763b3357.title: Soil erosion
4b48763b3357.sentence: The topography of the land determines the velocity at which surface runoff will flow, which in turn determines the erosivity of the runoff.

885e5e7cb007.title: Soil erosion
885e5e7cb007.sentence: Longer, steeper slopes (especially those without adequate vegetative cover) are more susceptible to very high rates of erosion during heavy rains than shorter, less steep slopes.

2099d92a7372.title: Soil erosion
2099d92a7372.sentence: Steeper terrain is also more prone to mudslides, landslides, and other forms of gravitational erosion processes.

e3a50167b4dd.title: Soil erosion
e3a50167b4dd.section: Physical processes > Rainfall and surface runoff
e3a50167b4dd.sentence: In splash erosion, the impact of a falling raindrop creates a small crater in the soil, ejecting soil particles.

db6b659dfaee.title: Surface runoff
db6b659dfaee.section: Effects of surface runoff > Erosion and deposition
db6b659dfaee.sentence: Splash erosion is the result of mechanical collision of raindrops with the soil surface: soil particles which are dislodged by the impact then move with the surface runoff.

1caca018c7a2.title: Soil erosion
1caca018c7a2.section: Physical processes > Rainfall and surface runoff
1caca018c7a2.sentence: The distance the ejected soil particles travel can be as much as 0.6 m (two feet) vertically and 1.5 m (five feet) horizontally on level ground and in the absence of wind.

f38d4473a006.title: Soil erosion
f38d4473a006.section: Human activities that aid soil erosion > Deforestation
f38d4473a006.sentence: The vegetative cover acts to reduce the velocity of the raindrops that strike the foliage and stems before hitting the ground, reducing their kinetic energy.

49d709c7be79.title: Nonpoint source pollution
49d709c7be79.sentence: The farmer leaves crop residues from previous plantings on and in the ground to help reduce splash and sheet erosion.

9b4be4986138.title: Soil erosion
9b4be4986138.section: Human activities that aid soil erosion > Roads and human impact
9b4be4986138.sentence: Human Impact has major effects on erosion processes, first by denuding the land of vegetative cover, altering drainage patterns, and compacting the soil during construction, and next by covering the land in an impermeable layer of asphalt or concrete that increases the amount of surface runoff and increases surface wind speeds.

74343c509d93.title: Soil erosion
74343c509d93.section: Human activities that aid soil erosion > Roads and human impact
74343c509d93.sentence: Much of the sediment carried in runoff from urban areas (especially roads) is highly contaminated with fuel, oil, and other chemicals.

d999fe5770ea.title: Soil erosion
d999fe5770ea.section: Human activities that aid soil erosion > Roads and human impact
d999fe5770ea.sentence: This increased runoff, in addition to eroding and degrading the land that it flows over, also causes major disruption to surrounding watersheds by altering the volume and rate of water that flows through them, and filling them with chemically polluted sedimentation.

7c908adaf729.title: Soil erosion
7c908adaf729.section: Human activities that aid soil erosion > Roads and human impact
7c908adaf729.sentence: The increased flow of water through local waterways also causes a large increase in the rate of bank erosion.

cecd21cf7c95.title: Rill
cecd21cf7c95.sentence: In hillslope geomorphology, a rill is a shallow channel (no more than a few inches/centimeters deep) cut into soil by the erosive action of flowing surface water.

20afb690f265.title: Rill
20afb690f265.sentence: Similar but smaller incised channels are known as microrills; larger incised channels are known as gullies.

ce1283211dd3.title: Rill
ce1283211dd3.sentence: Rills are narrow and shallow channels which are eroded into unprotected soil by hillslope runoff.

acfd2b92c5e3.title: Rill
acfd2b92c5e3.sentence: Since soil is regularly left bare during agricultural operations, rills may form on farmland during these vulnerable periods.

eca21c237e5f.title: Rill
eca21c237e5f.sentence: Rills may also form when bare soil is left exposed following deforestation, or during construction activities.

46e01fded8f5.title: Rill
46e01fded8f5.sentence: Rills are fairly easily visible when first incised, so they are often the first indication of an ongoing erosion problem.

d8da2ed8c46a.title: Soil erosion
d8da2ed8c46a.section: Physical processes > Rainfall and surface runoff
d8da2ed8c46a.sentence: Flow depths in rills are typically of the order of a few centimeters (about an inch) or less and along-channel slopes may be quite steep.

0119f3f72152.title: Soil erosion
0119f3f72152.section: Physical processes > Rainfall and surface runoff
0119f3f72152.sentence: This means that rills exhibit hydraulic physics very different from water flowing through the deeper wider channels of streams and rivers.

d47155a6333a.title: Rill
d47155a6333a.section: Rills created by erosion > Significance of rill erosion
d47155a6333a.sentence: Some estimates claim rill flow has a carrying capacity of nearly ten times that of non-rill, or interrill, areas.

45303305598e.title: Rill
45303305598e.section: Rills created by erosion > Significance of rill erosion
45303305598e.sentence: In a moderate rainfall, rill flow can carry rock fragments up to 9 cm in diameter downslope.

ef2e765491c2.title: Rill
ef2e765491c2.section: Rills created by erosion > Significance of rill erosion
ef2e765491c2.sentence: Agricultural machines, such as tractors, compact the soil to the point where water flows over the surface rather than seeping into the soil.

129e3d547f48.title: Rill
129e3d547f48.section: Rills created by erosion > Significance of rill erosion
129e3d547f48.sentence: Tractor wheel impressions often channel water, providing a perfect environment for generating rills.

6c16ddb71ea2.title: Rill
6c16ddb71ea2.sentence: Unless soil conservation measures are put into place, rills on regularly eroding areas may eventually develop into larger erosional features such as gullies or even (in semi-arid regions) into badlands.

4137bc5dedce.title: Rill
4137bc5dedce.section: Rills created by erosion > Significance of rill erosion
4137bc5dedce.sentence: Under proper field management, rills are small and are easily repaired by contour tilling the soil.

8209ba1186a4.title: Rill
8209ba1186a4.section: Rills created by erosion > Significance of rill erosion
8209ba1186a4.sentence: In 1987, scientist J. Poesen conducted an experiment on the Huldenberg field in Belgium which revealed that during a moderate rainfall, rill erosion removed as much as 200 kg (in submerged weight) of rock.

caf05f216fb4.title: Gully
caf05f216fb4.sentence: A gully is a landform created by running water, mass movement, or both, which erodes soil to a sharp angle, typically on a hillside or in river floodplains or terraces.

9e3ad6a3261c.title: Gully
9e3ad6a3261c.sentence: Gullies resemble large ditches or small valleys, but are metres to tens of metres in depth and width, are characterized by a distinct 'headscarp' or 'headwall' and progress by headward (i.e., upstream) erosion.

c232f3c01333.title: Gully
c232f3c01333.sentence: A gully may grow in length through headward (i.e., upstream) erosion at a knickpoint.

bdc5f7dbd297.title: Gully
bdc5f7dbd297.sentence: Gullies are commonly related to intermittent or ephemeral water flow, usually associated with localised intense or protracted rainfall events or snowmelt.

3539c72e1fe2.title: Gully
3539c72e1fe2.sentence: Gullies develop when a rill is neglected for an extended time, thickening and expanding as soil erosion persists.

611fa887a322.title: Gully
611fa887a322.sentence: Gullies can be formed and accelerated by cultivation practices on hillslopes (often gentle gradients) in farmland, and they can develop rapidly in rangelands from existing natural erosion forms subject to vegetative cover removal and livestock activity.

5e8e286b5337.title: Gully
5e8e286b5337.sentence: Hillsides are more prone to gully erosion when they are cleared of vegetation cover through deforestation, overgrazing, or other means.

dbf425d8b58e.title: Gully
dbf425d8b58e.sentence: Gullies in rangelands can be initiated by concentrated water flow down tracks worn by livestock or vehicle tracks.

68e3c072e3c0.title: Gully
68e3c072e3c0.sentence: The erosion processes include incision and bank erosion by water flow, mass movement of saturated or unsaturated bank or wall material, groundwater seepage - sapping the overlying material, collapse of soil pipes or tunnels in dispersive soils, or a combination of these to a greater or lesser degree.

9c4ca1962221.title: Gully
9c4ca1962221.sentence: Gullies reduce the productivity of farmlands where they incise into the land and produce sediment that may choke downstream waterbodies and reduce water quality within the drainage system and lake or coastal system.

ae8459349e72.title: Gully
ae8459349e72.sentence: The total soil loss from gully formation and subsequent downstream river sedimentation can be substantial, especially from unstable soil materials prone to dispersion.

121f3279aeec.title: Soil erosion
121f3279aeec.section: Monitoring, measuring and modelling soil erosion
121f3279aeec.sentence: One major problem is that the USLE cannot simulate gully erosion, and so erosion from gullies is ignored in any USLE-based assessment of erosion.

3b63c6d6223f.title: Soil erosion
3b63c6d6223f.section: Monitoring, measuring and modelling soil erosion
3b63c6d6223f.sentence: Yet erosion from gullies can be a substantial proportion (10–80%) of total erosion on cultivated and grazed land.

be228a4adc8b.title: Soil erosion
be228a4adc8b.section: Human activities that aid soil erosion > Deforestation
be228a4adc8b.sentence: For example, on the Madagascar high central plateau, comprising approximately ten percent of that country's land area, virtually the entire landscape is sterile of vegetation, with gully erosive furrows typically in excess of 50 metres (160 ft) deep and 1 kilometre (0.6 miles) wide.

dd172b154ea7.title: Gully
dd172b154ea7.sentence: The earliest known usage of the term is from 1657.

81bf4f21f664.title: Universal Soil Loss Equation
81bf4f21f664.sentence: The Universal Soil Loss Equation (USLE) is a widely used mathematical model that describes soil erosion processes.

046a38973da2.title: Universal Soil Loss Equation
046a38973da2.sentence: The USLE is composed of six factors to predict the long-term average annual soil loss (A).

459d53dfe776.title: Universal Soil Loss Equation
459d53dfe776.sentence: The equation includes the rainfall erosivity factor (R), the soil erodibility factor (K), the topographic factors (L and S), and the cropping management factors (C and P).

63a9d37770c7.title: Universal Soil Loss Equation
63a9d37770c7.sentence: The USLE was developed from erosion plot and rainfall simulator experiments.

62525345c547.title: Universal Soil Loss Equation
62525345c547.sentence: The USLE was developed in the U.S., based on soil erosion data collected beginning in the 1930s by the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) Soil Conservation Service (now the USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service).

686813b86b0a.title: Universal Soil Loss Equation
686813b86b0a.sentence: The unit plot is defined as the standard plot condition to determine the soil's erodibility.

6813c6e6a152.title: Universal Soil Loss Equation
6813c6e6a152.sentence: These conditions are when the LS factor = 1 (slope = 9% and length = 22.1 m (72.6 ft) where the plot is fallow and tillage is up and down slope and no conservation practices are applied (CP=1).

41c55a681070.title: Universal Soil Loss Equation
41c55a681070.sentence: A simpler method to predict K was presented by Wischmeier et al. which includes the particle size of the soil, organic matter content, soil structure and profile permeability.

05240313ac95.title: Universal Soil Loss Equation
05240313ac95.sentence: The soil erodibility factor K can be approximated from a nomograph if this information is known.

bb24a226a4dd.title: Universal Soil Loss Equation
bb24a226a4dd.sentence: The LS factors can easily be determined from a slope effect chart by knowing the length and gradient of the slope.

ca6558bf2262.title: Universal Soil Loss Equation
ca6558bf2262.sentence: The cropping management factor (C) and conservation practices factor (P) are more difficult to obtain and must be determined empirically from plot data.

a21033c51898.title: Soil erosion
a21033c51898.section: Monitoring, measuring and modelling soil erosion
a21033c51898.sentence: The most commonly used model for predicting soil loss from water erosion is the Universal Soil Loss Equation (USLE).

f10b15ff4e08.title: Universal Soil Loss Equation
f10b15ff4e08.sentence: The USLE or one of its derivatives are main models used by United States government agencies to measure water erosion.

6cef9b0c5420.title: Universal Soil Loss Equation
6cef9b0c5420.sentence: The model has been used for decades for purposes of conservation planning both in the United States where it originated and around the world, and has been used to help implement the United States' multibillion-dollar conservation program.

a0d9d7ad4dff.title: Soil erosion
a0d9d7ad4dff.section: Monitoring, measuring and modelling soil erosion
a0d9d7ad4dff.sentence: Despite the USLE's plot-scale spatial basis, the model has often been used to estimate soil erosion on much larger areas, such as watersheds, continents, and globally.

0d0a928ae5f9.title: Universal Soil Loss Equation
0d0a928ae5f9.sentence: The Revised Universal Soil Loss Equation (RUSLE) and the Modified Universal Soil Loss Equation (MUSLE) continue to be used for similar purposes.

9fc2e5300fb0.title: Soil erosion
9fc2e5300fb0.section: Monitoring, measuring and modelling soil erosion
9fc2e5300fb0.sentence: Some of these remain USLE-based, e.g. the G2 model.

2fe1434c5fe8.title: Soil erosion
2fe1434c5fe8.section: Monitoring, measuring and modelling soil erosion
2fe1434c5fe8.sentence: This was developed in the 1960s and 1970s.

994dc8dc8618.title: Erosion prediction
994dc8dc8618.sentence: Erosion prediction is the process of predicting where erosion may happen in the future using data.

13289c2ca86b.title: Erosion prediction
13289c2ca86b.sentence: There are dozens of erosion prediction models.

949704dbe66f.title: Erosion prediction
949704dbe66f.sentence: Some models focus on long-term (natural or geological) erosion, as a component of landscape evolution.

a568ef477dd6.title: Erosion prediction
a568ef477dd6.sentence: However, many erosion models were developed to quantify the effects of accelerated soil erosion i.e. soil erosion as influenced by human activity.

bf9f2af89c53.title: Erosion prediction
bf9f2af89c53.sentence: The aim of the majority of soil erosion models is to predict average rates (often an annual average rate) of soil loss from an area such as a plot, a field or a catchment/watershed under various land management techniques.

e870990b6dec.title: Erosion prediction
e870990b6dec.sentence: Most soil erosion models consider only soil erosion by water, however a few aim to predict wind erosion.

04f397275d1e.title: Erosion prediction
04f397275d1e.sentence: Models which consider tillage erosion are rare.

4bfd5be7e389.title: Erosion prediction
4bfd5be7e389.sentence: Few soil erosion models consider gully erosion, mostly due to difficulties in modelling these large erosional features.

f627e8f3fb46.title: Universal Soil Loss Equation
f627e8f3fb46.sentence: Process-based (physically based) models mathematically describe the erosion processes of detachment, transport, and deposition and through the solutions of the equations describing those processes provide estimates of soil loss and sediment yields from specified land surface areas.

1a32d5138652.title: Universal Soil Loss Equation
1a32d5138652.sentence: Empirical models relate management and environmental factors directly to soil loss and/or sedimentary yields through statistical relationships.

c8bfb3ff328b.title: Universal Soil Loss Equation
c8bfb3ff328b.sentence: Erosion science is not sufficiently advanced for there to exist completely process-based models which do not include empirical aspects.

478da3d5f31b.title: Universal Soil Loss Equation
478da3d5f31b.sentence: Current research effort involving erosion modeling is weighted toward the development of process-based erosion models.

eed8bc353c44.title: Universal Soil Loss Equation
eed8bc353c44.sentence: On the other hand, the standard model for most erosion assessment and conservation planning is the empirically based USLE, and there continues to be active research and development of USLE-based erosion prediction technology.

9b5bf7275a10.title: Erosion prediction
9b5bf7275a10.sentence: Two of the more widely used soil erosion models in North America are the Revised Universal Soil Loss Equation (RUSLE) and the Water Erosion Prediction Project erosion model (WEPP).

9832dd1e5f64.title: Erosion prediction
9832dd1e5f64.sentence: There is often a wide discrepancy between predicted and observed erosion rates.

ff8147913780.title: Erosion prediction
ff8147913780.sentence: Thus soil erosion models are still better as research tools than as public policy and regulatory instruments or for prescriptive design measures for constructed landforms.

cd916010c975.title: Erosion prediction
cd916010c975.sentence: However soil erosion models may provide useful guidance for the design engineer if adequately calibrated and verified for local conditions and if the design accounts for the uncertainty.

8620519d3d68.title: Soil erosion
8620519d3d68.section: Monitoring, measuring and modelling soil erosion
8620519d3d68.sentence: Erosion models are also non-linear, which makes them difficult to work with numerically, and makes it difficult or impossible to scale up to making predictions about large areas from data collected by sampling smaller plots.

65e7fb20916e.title: Riparian buffer
65e7fb20916e.sentence: A riparian buffer or stream buffer is a vegetated area (a "buffer strip") near a stream, usually forested, which helps shade and partially protect the stream from the impact of adjacent land uses.

8662408d808b.title: Riparian buffer
8662408d808b.sentence: Riparian buffers act to intercept sediment, nutrients, pesticides, and other materials in surface runoff and reduce nutrients and other pollutants in shallow subsurface water flow.

247e205a1e2e.title: Riparian buffer
247e205a1e2e.sentence: Riparian buffers also stabilise the bank surrounding the water body which is important since erosion can be a major problem in agricultural regions when cut (eroded) banks can take land out of production.

75fe359ade52.title: Riparian buffer
75fe359ade52.sentence: Erosion can also lead to sedimentation and siltation of downstream lakes, ponds, and reservoirs.

5d4851bc381e.title: Riparian buffer
5d4851bc381e.sentence: It is generally recommended that native species be chosen to plant in these three zones, with the general width of the buffer being 50 feet (15 m) on each side of the stream.

343d036ebf6e.title: Riparian buffer
343d036ebf6e.sentence: It consists mostly of native grasses and serves primarily to slow water runoff and begin to absorb contaminants before they reach the other zones.

b6fc8a31646c.title: Riparian buffer
b6fc8a31646c.sentence: Usually made up of native shrubs, this zone provides a habitat for wildlife, including nesting areas for bird species.

a3fde53f0188.title: Riparian buffer
a3fde53f0188.sentence: This zone should function mainly to shade the water source and act as a bank stabilizer.

2f629335cad4.title: Riparian buffer
2f629335cad4.sentence: The zone should include large native tree species that grow fast and can quickly act to perform these tasks.

50c5490ee74b.title: Riparian buffer
50c5490ee74b.sentence: A study done by the University of Georgia, conducted over a nine-year period, monitored the amounts of fertilizers that reached the watershed from the source of the application.

00e04950e9c4.title: Riparian buffer
00e04950e9c4.sentence: It found that these buffers removed at least 60% of the nitrogen in the runoff, and at least 65% of the phosphorus from the fertilizer application.

ec586f7d7287.title: Geotextile
ec586f7d7287.sentence: Geotextiles are versatile permeable fabrics that, when used in conjunction with soil, can effectively perform multiple functions, including separation, filtration, reinforcement, protection, and drainage.

2478ff7788e1.title: Geotextile
2478ff7788e1.sentence: Typically crafted from polypropylene or polyester, geotextile fabrics are available in two primary forms: woven, which resembles traditional mail bag sacking, and nonwoven, which resembles felt.

5056d0149a4c.title: Geotextile
5056d0149a4c.sentence: Overall, these materials are referred to as geosynthetics and each configuration—geonets, geosynthetic clay liners, geogrids, geotextile tubes, and others—can yield benefits in geotechnical and environmental engineering design.

229e8d15d257.title: Geotextile
229e8d15d257.sentence: Geotextiles were originally intended to be a substitute for granular soil filters.

169df20f6214.title: Geotextile
169df20f6214.sentence: In the 1950s, R.J. Barrett began working using geotextiles behind precast concrete seawalls, under precast concrete erosion control blocks, beneath large stone riprap, and in other erosion control situations.

d0fd483c33ec.title: Geotextile
d0fd483c33ec.sentence: Geotextiles and related products have many applications and currently support many civil engineering applications including roads, airfields, railroads, embankments, retaining structures, reservoirs, canals, dams, bank protection, coastal engineering and construction site silt fences or to form a geotextile tube.

5b416e30003b.title: Geotextile
5b416e30003b.sentence: Geotextiles are used as matting to stabilize flow in stream channels and swales.

d9890dd38308.title: Geotextile
d9890dd38308.sentence: In addition, geotextiles allow planting on steep slopes, further securing the slope.

1328ced4fb10.title: Geotextile
1328ced4fb10.sentence: Coir (coconut fiber) geotextiles are popular for erosion control, slope stabilization and bioengineering, due to the fabric's substantial mechanical strength.

9e3e59c3d6df.title: Geotextile
9e3e59c3d6df.sentence: Coir geotextiles last approximately 3 to 5 years depending on the fabric weight.

bae93b43523d.title: Geotextile
bae93b43523d.sentence: The product degrades into humus, enriching the soil.

def43426e503.title: Soil loss tolerance
def43426e503.sentence: Soil loss tolerance for a specific soil, also known as the T value, is the maximum average annual soil loss expressed as tons per acre per year that will permit current production levels to be maintained economically and indefinitely.

8235ecf563f4.title: Soil loss tolerance
8235ecf563f4.sentence: T values range from 1 to 5 tons per acre per year.

ae736e333006.title: Soil loss tolerance
ae736e333006.sentence: It is calculated with the formula T=υQρC+R(1−C).

27a0e6b4794b.title: Soil loss tolerance
27a0e6b4794b.sentence: The idea of soil loss tolerance was initially devised by the Soil Conservation Service (known presently as the NRCS).

9840544db0c6.title: Soil loss tolerance
9840544db0c6.sentence: It is based on the minimum soil loss rate required to reduce organic content and harm crop productivity in agricultural contexts.

6ebbd5151178.title: Soil loss tolerance
6ebbd5151178.sentence: From 1961 to 1962, several groups of soil in the United States were designated with T values ranging from 2 to 6 tons per acre per year.

f45d6c638763.title: Soil loss tolerance
f45d6c638763.sentence: The rate was subsequently adjusted to 1 to 5 tons per acre per year.

033fddfb1048.title: Soil loss tolerance
033fddfb1048.sentence: The value was adapted for use in conservation management beginning in the mid-1960s.

328f9ed3e667.title: Soil loss tolerance
328f9ed3e667.sentence: According to the United States Department of Agriculture's National Resource Conservation Service, in 2007 in the US, 99 million acres (28% of all cropland) were eroding above soil loss tolerance (T) rates.

8eed45af85a1.title: Soil loss tolerance
8eed45af85a1.sentence: This was compared to 169 million acres (40% of cropland) in 1982.

d7d545581ab2.title: Soil loss tolerance
d7d545581ab2.sentence: T values are also spatially heterogeneous, meaning that a single T value given to a region may not reflect the diversity of soil characteristics present, and may misrepresent erosion risks in certain areas.

0510f1b046f4.title: Soil loss tolerance
0510f1b046f4.sentence: The soil loss tolerance equation may not be universally applicable, especially in regions with high amounts of soluble carbonate minerals, such as Karst formations.

172233deaee4.title: Soil loss tolerance
172233deaee4.sentence: It is argued that T values should not be the only factor considered, and that real soil loss and the ratio between real loss and soil loss tolerance should be used to accurately assess the risk that soil loss poses.

5b94948e432e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.02%3A_Tolerable_Soil_Loss
5b94948e432e.sentence: For a deep soil with a rooting depth of greater than 5 feet, the T value is 5 tons per acre per year (11 metric tons per hectare).

6f9b91a6297e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.02%3A_Tolerable_Soil_Loss
6f9b91a6297e.sentence: Still, 5 tons is equal to about.03 inch of soil depth (about.08 centimeters), and if soil loss continued at that rate, at the end of 33 years about 1 inch would be lost.

0cb088c976f9.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.02%3A_Tolerable_Soil_Loss
0cb088c976f9.sentence: The soil loss “tolerance” amount is reduced for soils with less rooting depth.

afe8f5d42b4f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.02%3A_Tolerable_Soil_Loss
afe8f5d42b4f.sentence: When rooting depth is less than 10 inches, the tolerable rate of soil loss is the same as losing 0.006 inches per year and is equivalent to 1 inch of loss in 167 years.

ed2637a7efa0.title: Mineral dust
ed2637a7efa0.sentence: Mineral dust is an atmospheric aerosol originated from the suspension of minerals constituting the soil, composed of various oxides and carbonates.

8e3465f768ef.title: Mineral dust
8e3465f768ef.sentence: Mineral dust is mainly constituted of the oxides (SiO2, Al2O3, FeO, Fe2O3, CaO, and others) and carbonates (CaCO3, MgCO3) that constitute the Earth's crust.

21aa17e9cd18.title: Mineral dust
21aa17e9cd18.sentence: Global mineral dust emissions are estimated at 1000-5000 million tons per year, of which the largest part is attributed to deserts.

830afd33319e.title: Mineral dust
830afd33319e.sentence: Although this aerosol class is usually considered of natural origin, it is estimated that about a quarter of mineral dust emissions could be ascribed to human activities through desertification and land use changes.

61acf009ec49.title: Mineral dust
61acf009ec49.sentence: The Sahara is the major source on Earth of mineral dust (60-200 million tons per year).

e1cc5ab2069f.title: Mineral dust
e1cc5ab2069f.sentence: Additionally, it plays a significant role in the nutrient inflow to the Amazon rainforest.

4c929439cf72.title: Mineral dust
4c929439cf72.sentence: In the Mediterranean region, Saharan dust is important as it represents the major source of nutrients for phytoplankton and other aquatic organisms.

cebf3e5fa935.title: Mineral dust
cebf3e5fa935.sentence: In Eastern Asia, mineral dust events that originate in the Gobi Desert (Southern Mongolia and Northern China) during springtime give rise to the phenomenon called Asian dust.

d9785d455044.title: Mineral dust
d9785d455044.sentence: Areas affected by Asian dust experience decreased visibility and health problems, such as sore throat and respiratory difficulties.

1feb4f9d40f2.title: Mineral dust
1feb4f9d40f2.sentence: The effects of Asian dust, however, are not strictly negative, as it is thought that its deposition enriches the soil with important trace minerals.

57fc0f8c3070.title: Mineral dust
57fc0f8c3070.sentence: Although dust storms in the Gobi desert have occurred from time to time throughout history, they became a pronounced problem in the second half of the 20th century due to intensified agricultural pressure and desertification.

f5d65e1d7a21.title: Mineral dust
f5d65e1d7a21.section: North American dust > Relationship to drought
f5d65e1d7a21.sentence: Soil moisture is an important variable controlling dust emissions, along with vegetation cover, wind speed and soil type.

30bacd083ce3.title: Mineral dust
30bacd083ce3.sentence: Dust deposition has increased dramatically since the early 1800s compared to the natural background due to the intensification of human activities.

9878832a2fa4.title: Mineral dust
9878832a2fa4.section: North American dust > Relationship to drought
9878832a2fa4.sentence: They also found that sediment supply played a key role as evidenced from a 60% increase in deposition in the 1800s due to accelerating land disturbance.

db42889be9e9.title: Mineral dust
db42889be9e9.section: North American dust > Relationship to drought
db42889be9e9.sentence: Several studies based on modern observations show positive relationships (i.e. increasing drought increases dust) between dust and drought conditions in each dust cycle phase, from emissions, to atmospheric burden, to deposition.

c740a819fdce.title: Mineral dust
c740a819fdce.section: North American dust > Relationship to drought
c740a819fdce.sentence: However, studies based on paleo records of dust deposition (e.g. using lake sediment) that specifically looked at megadroughts show both increases and no change in dust deposition.

4e6c9b099886.title: Mineral dust
4e6c9b099886.section: North American dust > Relationship to drought
4e6c9b099886.sentence: Instead, they found that dust deposition is more likely controlled by transport mechanisms and sediment supply than by hydroclimate.

cb95adadefe7.title: Jet erosion test
cb95adadefe7.sentence: The jet erosion test (JET), or jet index test, is a method used in geotechnical engineering to quantify the resistance of a soil to erosion.

ca867ee56ffc.title: Jet erosion test
ca867ee56ffc.sentence: The test can be applied in-situ after preparing a field site, or it can be applied in a laboratory on either an intact or a remolded soil sample.

9dc839c79d02.title: Jet erosion test
9dc839c79d02.sentence: The test consists of mounting a jet tube inside of an enclosed cylinder and releasing a turbulent downpour of water onto a soil specimen at a constant hydraulic head.

a3507a4ffc28.title: Jet erosion test
a3507a4ffc28.sentence: If the shear stress applied by the jet stream exceeds the critical shear stress for erosion of the soil, the jet will erode soil particles, causing a scour hole to form.

1546c6c0d717.title: Jet erosion test
1546c6c0d717.sentence: The depth of the scour hole is then measured at specified time intervals.

dfb00bee6f9c.title: Jet erosion test
dfb00bee6f9c.sentence: Fitting the measured erosion rate (Er) to the following equation allows the estimation of the erodibility of the soil (kd) and the critical shear stress (τc), provided that the applied shear stress (τ) is estimated precisely:

e675aa632a17.title: Jet erosion test
e675aa632a17.sentence: A quantitative measure of erodibility allows for the prediction of erosion, assisting with the design of structures such as vegetated channels, road embankments, dams, levees, and spillways.

c2eefbf5e36e.title: Jet erosion test
c2eefbf5e36e.sentence: One of the results of the test is the jet erosion index (Ji), which can be correlated with the soil erodibility.

4ec8249ecffb.title: Jet erosion test
4ec8249ecffb.sentence: Typically, the jet erosion index ranges from 0 to 0.03.

e69f839f4d98.title: Jet erosion test
e69f839f4d98.sentence: As of 2017, there is no universally accepted methodology to determine the erodibility of a soil.

c3a11c7ead59.title: Jet erosion test
c3a11c7ead59.sentence: Additionally, depending on the method used to fit the results to the above equation, the predicted values of kd for a given τc can be up to 100 times smaller or larger due to predictive uncertainty.

d06afe493aaf.title: Dust
d06afe493aaf.sentence: Dust control is the suppression of solid particles with diameters less than 500 micrometers (i.e. half a millimeter).

407fdeb75eeb.title: Dust
407fdeb75eeb.sentence: Most governmental Environmental Protection Agencies, including the United States Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) mandate that facilities generating fugitive dust minimize or mitigate the production of dust in their operation.

757ce81ab1c9.title: Dust
757ce81ab1c9.sentence: The most frequent dust control violations occur at new residential housing developments in urban areas.

beb3f740d344.title: Dust
beb3f740d344.sentence: Control measures include such simple practices as spraying construction and demolition sites with water, and preventing the tracking of dust onto adjacent roads.

3750a02f7a68.title: Dust
3750a02f7a68.sentence: Dust in such places may be suppressed by mechanical methods, including paving or laying down gravel, or stabilizing the surface with water, vegetable oils or other dust suppressants, or by using water misters to suppress dust that is already airborne.[2]

0dd99f6250e3.title: Dust
0dd99f6250e3.sentence: Road dust may be suppressed by mechanical removal methods like a street sweeper or vehicles equipped with vacuum cleaners, or by spraying the dusty road with vegetable oil, calcium chloride, water, or other dust suppressants.

315c73d15cbb.title: Dust
315c73d15cbb.sentence: - Reducing dust related health risks that include allergic reactions, pneumonia and asthmatic attacks.

7facfbc21f55.title: Dust
7facfbc21f55.sentence: - Improving visibility and road traffic safety.

9a13a9631268.title: Tillage erosion
9a13a9631268.sentence: Tillage erosion is a form of soil erosion occurring in cultivated fields due to the movement of soil by tillage.

115d83dcbc58.title: Tillage erosion
115d83dcbc58.sentence: There is growing evidence that tillage erosion is a major soil erosion process in agricultural lands, surpassing water and wind erosion in many fields all around the world, especially on sloping and hilly lands.

97e86dfb8733.title: Tillage erosion
97e86dfb8733.sentence: A signature spatial pattern of soil erosion shown in many water erosion handbooks and pamphlets, the eroded hilltops, is actually caused by tillage erosion as water erosion mainly causes soil losses in the midslope and lowerslope segments of a slope, not the hilltops.

0f6fad69350c.title: Tillage erosion
0f6fad69350c.sentence: Local topography related tillage erosion is most pronounced in hummocky landscapes with eroded hilltops that often exhibit a light soil color due to the loss of organic-rich topsoil, a phenomenon often mistakenly assumed to be the result of water erosion.

c704c96a6644.title: Tillage erosion
c704c96a6644.sentence: Conceptually, the process of tillage erosion (ETi) can be described as a function of tillage erosivity (ET) and landscape erodibility (EL):

5bf06a12a8d9.title: Tillage erosion
5bf06a12a8d9.sentence: Tillage erosivity (ET) is defined as the propensity of a tillage operation, or a sequence of operations, to erode soil and is affected by the design and operation of the tillage implement (e.g., the size, arrangement and shape of tillage tools, tillage speed and depth).

117bc7bcfa3b.title: Tillage erosion
117bc7bcfa3b.sentence: Landscape erodibility (EL) is defined as the propensity of a landscape to be eroded by tillage and is affected by the landscape topography (e.g., slope gradient and slope curvature) and soil properties (e.g., texture, structure, bulk density and soil moisture content).

21ffe252f113.title: Tillage erosion
21ffe252f113.sentence: Tillage erosion occurs as a result of changes in tillage translocation (soil movement by tillage) across the field.

1a4dc4f82b1f.title: Tillage erosion
1a4dc4f82b1f.sentence: Tillage translocation is expressed as a linear function of slope gradient (θ) and slope curvature (φ):

7499f5ec4eef.title: Tillage erosion
7499f5ec4eef.sentence: Typical spatial patterns of tillage erosion observed in cultivated field are either local topography related: soil loss from hilltops (convexities) and soil accumulation in depressions (concavities); or field boundary related: soil loss from the downside of a field boundary and soil accumulation in the upper-side of a field boundary.

0a382b5f0ca2.title: Tillage erosion
0a382b5f0ca2.sentence: Field boundary related tillage erosion is determined by not only topography but also tillage directions and it is responsible for the forming of tillage banks and terraces.

1ad0ae41327e.title: Tillage erosion
1ad0ae41327e.sentence: As the top soil layer is getting thinner, subsequent tillage operations will bring up sublayer soil and mix it into the tillage layer.

b03ba245a9ff.title: Tillage erosion
b03ba245a9ff.sentence: Over time, with the vertical and horizontal mixing, tillage translocation will cause the spread the subsoil from the eroding portion to over the entire field, including areas of tillage accumulation.

8073de307730.title: Tillage erosion
8073de307730.sentence: Subsoil often has undesirable soil properties for crop growth (e.g., less organic carbon, poor structure).

9db7a9c05f12.title: Tillage erosion
9db7a9c05f12.sentence: When subsoil is mixed into the tillage layer due to tillage erosion, crop productivity will be negatively impacted.

6ad0470f02f8.title: Tillage erosion
6ad0470f02f8.section: Effects > Linkages and interactions with other erosion processes
6ad0470f02f8.sentence: For example, soil degradation caused by tillage erosion likely will increase the erodibility of the soil to water and wind erosion.

ac5317a68009.title: Tillage erosion
ac5317a68009.sentence: Tillage erosion can be mitigated by reducing the intensity of tillage.

4c50cf4caa3d.title: Tillage erosion
4c50cf4caa3d.sentence: This includes reducing the frequency of tillage, the speed and depth of tillage, and the size of the tillage implement.

8b3781702a2a.title: Tillage erosion
8b3781702a2a.sentence: Contour tillage will reduce the variation of tillage speed and depth, resulting in reduced changes in tillage translocation across the field.

ea844038d98f.title: Tillage erosion
ea844038d98f.sentence: In addition, downslope movement of soil can be compensated by using a reversible moldboard plough to throw the furrow upslope.

dc4fa78a5c7e.title: Tillage erosion
dc4fa78a5c7e.sentence: Physically moving soil from accumulation areas (e.g., depressions) to the eroding portion of the field (e.g., hilltops), a practice termed soil landscape restoration, can mitigate the impact of tillage erosion by restoring soil productivity at the eroding portion of the field.

4859c95dad04.title: Grassed waterway
4859c95dad04.sentence: A grassed waterway is a 2-to-48-meter-wide (6.6-to-157.5-foot) native grassland strip of green belt.

6d309aa33089.title: Grassed waterway
6d309aa33089.sentence: It is generally installed in the thalweg, the deepest continuous line along a valley or watercourse, of a cultivated dry valley in order to control erosion.

29da87637eeb.title: Grassed waterway
29da87637eeb.sentence: Runoff generated on cropland during storms or long winter rains concentrates in the thalweg where it can lead to rill or gully erosion.

acd67f876392.title: Grassed waterway
acd67f876392.sentence: Rills and gullies further concentrate runoff and speed up its transfer, which can worsen damage occurring downstream.

4466588ddc33.title: Grassed waterway
4466588ddc33.sentence: In this context, a grassed waterway allows increasing soil cohesion and roughness.

1e50336e1890.title: Grassed waterway
1e50336e1890.sentence: It also prevents the formation of rills and gullies.

ffc6b1fd9cd6.title: Grassed waterway
ffc6b1fd9cd6.sentence: Furthermore, it can slow down runoff and allow its re-infiltration during long winter rains.

d4e99ea801b5.title: Grassed waterway
d4e99ea801b5.sentence: In contrast, its infiltration capacity is generally not sufficient to reinfiltrate runoff produced by heavy spring and summer storms.

9581060763d8.title: Grassed waterway
9581060763d8.sentence: It can therefore be useful to combine it with extra measures, like the installation of earthen dams across the grassed waterway, in order to buffer runoff temporarily.

37d4a7b917b3.title: Grassed waterway
37d4a7b917b3.sentence: Confusion between "grassed waterway" and "vegetative filter strips" should be avoided.

bb2541ba9634.title: Grassed waterway
bb2541ba9634.sentence: The latter are generally narrower (only a few metres wide) and rather installed along rivers as well as along or within cultivated fields.

74ecd3d6fb54.title: Revegetation
74ecd3d6fb54.sentence: Revegetation is the process of replanting and rebuilding the soil of disturbed land.

dab17eb58d80.title: Revegetation
dab17eb58d80.sentence: This may be a natural process produced by plant colonization and succession, manmade rewilding projects, accelerated process designed to repair damage to a landscape due to wildfire, mining, flood, or other cause.

7a9edcbb080a.title: Revegetation
7a9edcbb080a.sentence: The motivations behind revegetation are diverse, answering needs that are both technical and aesthetic, but it is usually erosion prevention that is the primary reason.

ce6eafbb6a68.title: Revegetation
ce6eafbb6a68.sentence: Revegetation helps prevent soil erosion, enhances the ability of the soil to absorb more water in significant rain events, and in conjunction reduces turbidity dramatically in adjoining bodies of water.

b3a4a4710473.title: Revegetation
b3a4a4710473.sentence: Originally the process was simply one of applying seed and fertilizer to disturbed lands, usually grasses or clover.

a49073b35ef9.title: Revegetation
a49073b35ef9.sentence: The fibrous root network of grasses is useful for short-term erosion control, particularly on sloping ground.

2b734c637a35.title: Revegetation
2b734c637a35.sentence: Mine reclamation may involve soil amendment, replacement, or creation, particularly for areas that have been strip mined or suffered severe erosion or soil compaction.

87c5f6011c54.title: Revegetation
87c5f6011c54.sentence: Mycorrhizae, symbiotic fungal-plant communities, are important to the success of revegetation efforts.

50b5a1be3dbe.title: Revegetation
50b5a1be3dbe.sentence: Most woody plant species need these root-fungi communities to thrive, and nursery or greenhouse transplants may not have sufficient or correct mycorrhizae for good survival.

f281feaef955.title: Prairie restoration
f281feaef955.sentence: Prairie restoration is a conservation effort to restore prairie lands that were destroyed due to industrial, agricultural, commercial, or residential development.

741cf63aeabf.title: Prairie restoration
741cf63aeabf.sentence: The primary aim is to return areas and ecosystems to their previous state before their depletion.

04f4b5bfabe4.title: Prairie restoration
04f4b5bfabe4.sentence: They plowed up the tallgrasses and wild flowers in the area.

fc2249253ef5.title: Prairie restoration
fc2249253ef5.sentence: By 1849 most species of prairie grass had disappeared to make room for crops (i.e.: soybeans, corn, etc.).

d1a7a191cf92.title: Prairie restoration
d1a7a191cf92.sentence: Particularly with land previously dominated by prairie grasses, the loss of the tallgrass extensive fibrous root system left the soil exposed and unbound.

f166bdc31c4b.title: Prairie restoration
f166bdc31c4b.sentence: Ecologically, prairie restoration aids in conservation of earth's topsoil, which is often exposed to erosion from wind and rain (worsened by climate change's heavier and frequent rain) when prairies are plowed under to make way for new commerce.

2d14f102b9eb.title: Prairie restoration
2d14f102b9eb.sentence: Prairie grass collects this carbon from the atmosphere through photosynthesis and stores it in its soil.

fc5c3d2225e2.title: Prairie restoration
fc5c3d2225e2.sentence: Prairie soil is also useful for carbon sequestration.

e13f9900ff5e.title: Prairie restoration
e13f9900ff5e.section: Planting and aftercare of prairie plants
e13f9900ff5e.sentence: In Europe, when restoring previous crop land with prairie grasses, the most frequently used techniques involve: spontaneous succession, sowing seed mixtures, transfer of plant material, topsoil removal and transfer.

ef76c5aa1b1f.title: WEPP
ef76c5aa1b1f.sentence: The Water Erosion Prediction Project (WEPP) model is a physically based erosion simulation model built on the fundamentals of hydrology, plant science, hydraulics, and erosion mechanics.

d846ffb54c44.title: WEPP
d846ffb54c44.sentence: The model was developed by an interagency team of scientists to replace the Universal Soil Loss Equation (USLE) and has been widely used in the United States and the world.

3ba641f0bf12.title: WEPP
3ba641f0bf12.sentence: The WEPP model has been improved continuously since its public delivery in 1995, and is applicable for a variety of areas (e.g., cropland, rangeland, forestry, fisheries, and surface coal mining).

a46f04f04340.title: WEPP
a46f04f04340.sentence: WEPP requires four inputs, i.e., climate, topography, soil, and management (vegetation); and provides various types of outputs, including water balance (surface runoff, subsurface flow, and evapotranspiration), soil detachment and deposition at points along the slope, sediment delivery, and vegetation growth.

9775ff8fce15.title: WEPP
9775ff8fce15.sentence: WEPP is applicable for a wide range of geographic and land-use and management conditions, and capable of predicting spatial and temporal distributions of soil detachment and deposition on an event or continuous basis at both small (hillslopes, roads, small parcels) and large (watershed) scales.

2e76d2bdd5b4.title: WEPP
2e76d2bdd5b4.sentence: In WEPP watershed applications, multiple hillslopes, channels, and impoundments can be linked together, and runoff and sediment yield from the entire catchment predicted.

d854bb965431.title: WEPP
d854bb965431.sentence: WEPP can provide daily runoff, subsurface flow, and sediment output categorized into five particle-size classes: primary clay, primary silt, small aggregates, large aggregates, and primary sand, allowing calculation of selective sediment transport, and enrichment of the fine sediment sizes.

3776c0cd7694.title: Rill
3776c0cd7694.section: Rills created by erosion > Rill initiation
3776c0cd7694.sentence: Rills begin to form when the runoff shear stress, the ability of surface runoff to detach soil particles, overcomes the soil's shear strength, the ability of soil to resist force working parallel to the soil's surface.

6083c1ea3c4d.title: Rill
6083c1ea3c4d.section: Rills created by erosion > Rill initiation
6083c1ea3c4d.sentence: This begins the erosion process as water breaks soil particles free and carries them down the slope.

4f2e8f42fa2c.title: Rill
4f2e8f42fa2c.section: Rills created by erosion > Rill initiation
4f2e8f42fa2c.sentence: These forces explain why sandy, loamy soils are especially susceptible to the formation of rills, whereas dense clays tend to resist rill formation.

a46829f60545.title: Rill
a46829f60545.section: Rills created by erosion > Rill initiation
a46829f60545.sentence: Therefore, the formation of rills is primarily controlled by the slope of the hillside.

70eb0e67336e.title: Rill
70eb0e67336e.section: Rills created by erosion > Rill initiation
70eb0e67336e.sentence: Slope controls the depth of the rills, while the length of the slope and the soil's permeability control the number of incisions in an area.

a1f2c0eb4408.title: Rill
a1f2c0eb4408.section: Rills created by erosion > Rill initiation
a1f2c0eb4408.sentence: Each type of soil has a threshold value, a slope angle below which water velocity cannot produce sufficient force to dislodge enough soil particles for rills to form.

711f56c900e2.title: Rill
711f56c900e2.section: Rills created by erosion > Rill initiation
711f56c900e2.sentence: For instance, on many non-cohesive slopes, this threshold value hovers around an angle of 2 degrees with a shear velocity between 3 and 3.5 cm/s.

ea67bac66d19.title: Rill
ea67bac66d19.section: Rills created by erosion > Rill initiation
ea67bac66d19.sentence: Up to 37% of erosion in a rill-ridden area may derive from mass movement, or collapse, of rill sidewalls.

24b5462fd024.title: Rill
24b5462fd024.section: Rills created by erosion > Rill initiation
24b5462fd024.sentence: As water flows through a rill, it will undercut into the walls, triggering collapse.

3d83aa2703cf.title: Rill
3d83aa2703cf.section: Rills created by erosion > Rill initiation
3d83aa2703cf.sentence: Also, as water seeps into the soil of the walls, they weaken, amplifying the chance of wall collapse.

52d3e6521f3f.title: Sheet erosion
52d3e6521f3f.sentence: Sheet erosion or sheet wash is the even erosion of substrate along a wide area.

07d87d9df791.title: Sheet erosion
07d87d9df791.sentence: Water moving fairly uniformly with a similar thickness over a surface is called sheet flow, and is the cause of sheet erosion.

f46aec8e4638.title: Sheet erosion
f46aec8e4638.sentence: Sheet erosion implies that any flow of water that causes the erosion is not canalized.

9f261c485f8a.title: Sheet erosion
9f261c485f8a.sentence: Sheet erosion occurs in two steps.

60d070c750a4.title: Sheet erosion
60d070c750a4.sentence: First, rainsplash dislodges small particles of the substrate and then the particles are carried away, usually short distances, by a thin and uniform layer of water (sheet flow).

ef9221a62e5a.title: Sheet erosion
ef9221a62e5a.sentence: Transport by the sheet flow is usually over small distances, meaning that sheet erosion is a low magnitude process.

a74083912076.title: Sheet erosion
a74083912076.sentence: However, the frequency over time with which this occurs may be high, compensating for the small change observed in each individual episode of sheet erosion.

94cb93c94373.title: Sheet erosion
94cb93c94373.sentence: Sheet erosion is common in recently ploughed fields and bare ground where the substrate, typically soil, is not consolidated.

fdce08882d2e.title: Sheet erosion
fdce08882d2e.sentence: The sheet erosion caused by a single rainstorm may account for the loss of up to hundred tons of small particles in an acre.

d32d46aa3d1a.title: Sheet erosion
d32d46aa3d1a.sentence: If a hillslope surface contains many irregularities, sheet erosion may give way to erosion along small channels called rills, which can then converge forming gullies.

53c87389ffe8.title: Universal Soil Loss Equation
53c87389ffe8.sentence: They are described in soil loss ratios (C or P with / C or P without).

831dd74248e1.title: Universal Soil Loss Equation
831dd74248e1.sentence: However, determining the P factor has proven to be challenging as there is usually a lack of geospatial information on the specific soil conservation practices in a given region.

9606ae0b5007.title: Universal Soil Loss Equation
9606ae0b5007.sentence: Thus, to estimate the P factor value in the RUSLE formula, a combination of land use type and slope gradient is often used, where a lower value indicates more effective control of soil erosion.

dcae977d8060.title: Universal Soil Loss Equation
dcae977d8060.sentence: Creating field boundaries, such as stone walls, hedgerows, earth banks, and lynchets, effectively prevented or reduced soil erosion in pre-industrial agriculture.

81d371eec730.title: Universal Soil Loss Equation
81d371eec730.sentence: Recently, a novel P-factor model for Europe has been developed from the data retrieved during a statistical survey that recorded the occurrence of stone walls and grass margins in EU countries.

c72e3f2a21b0.title: Universal Soil Loss Equation
c72e3f2a21b0.sentence: It has been demonstrated that landscape archaeology has the potential to fill this gap in the data about soil conservation practices using a GIS-based tool called Historic Landscape Characterisation (HLC).

b02b100dadcf.title: Rainfall simulator
b02b100dadcf.sentence: A rainfall simulator is used in soil science and hydrology to study how soil reacts to rainfall.

c5ef30d8909c.title: Rainfall simulator
c5ef30d8909c.sentence: Natural rainfall is difficult to use in experimentation because its timing and intensity cannot be reliably reproduced.

94dfeb8c55cc.title: Rainfall simulator
94dfeb8c55cc.sentence: Using simulated rainfall significantly speeds the study of erosion, surface runoff and leaching.

ab4588df4ca3.title: Rainfall simulator
ab4588df4ca3.sentence: In the 1930s, pioneers of erosion studies tightened control of their experiments by building the first rainfall simulators, ‌ ordinary sprinkle cans or pipes with holes.

15bfb4ffb87c.title: Rainfall simulator
15bfb4ffb87c.sentence: These holes were replaced in the 1960s with full cone nozzles, carefully selected to accurately approximate:

df14d1d9df2a.title: Rainfall simulator
df14d1d9df2a.sentence: - The size of a rainfall water drop

733ac822c3b1.title: Rainfall simulator
733ac822c3b1.sentence: - The velocity of a drop as it strikes the ground

e76a0dd12bff.title: Rainfall simulator
e76a0dd12bff.sentence: - The uniformity of drops across a plot, to assure an accurate simulation of rainfall

6a196d6b684f.title: Rainfall simulator
