6a196d6b684f.sentence: By the 1980s, solenoid valves could modulate water flow to dynamically vary the intensity of simulated rainfall, much as rainfall intensity naturally varies in storms.

36611abbc43a.title: Rainfall simulator
36611abbc43a.sentence: As the technology matured in the early 1990s, rainfall simulators were used in the United States as part of the Water Erosion Prediction Project to update the universal soil loss equation.

bb199e5c9407.title: Rainfall simulator
bb199e5c9407.sentence: In erosion studies, if no crop canopy is present over the soil, the size distribution and terminal velocity of the raindrop must be accurately simulated, as they affect splash erosion.

a8b2ce9769a4.title: Rainfall simulator
a8b2ce9769a4.sentence: Drop generator height is important in many scientific simulators to ensure water droplets approach terminal velocity in the downward direction.

eafc409e473d.title: Post-fire hillslope stabilization treatments
eafc409e473d.sentence: Post-fire hillslope stabilization treatments are treatments aimed at stabilizing fire-affected slopes by counteracting the negative impact of fire on vegetation and soil properties.

30fa3a9de917.title: Post-fire hillslope stabilization treatments
30fa3a9de917.sentence: The final objective of these treatments is reducing the risk of catastrophic runoff and erosion events and protecting valued resources downhill.

bcadc05a81d3.title: Post-fire hillslope stabilization treatments
bcadc05a81d3.sentence: Vegetation fires usually partially or totally consume the canopy, above-ground organic residue (litter), fine roots, and soil organic compounds, reducing soil protection, enhancing soil water repellency, and compromising soil stability.

572bcc4df288.title: Post-fire hillslope stabilization treatments
572bcc4df288.sentence: The combined effect of fire and the occurrence of heavy rainfall in the post-fire season can lead to catastrophic hydrologic and erosion events with severe impacts on population and valued resources downhill such as housing, infrastructure, water supply systems, and critical habitats.

aa0fc6e3a764.title: Post-fire hillslope stabilization treatments
aa0fc6e3a764.sentence: For example, high intensity rainfall after the Thomas Fire in California (USA) led to catastrophic floods and debris flows in 2018 with 20 people dead, 300 houses destroyed, and critical infrastructures severely affected.

747e0e07fd90.title: Post-fire hillslope stabilization treatments
747e0e07fd90.section: Classification of post-fire hillslope stabilization treatments
747e0e07fd90.sentence: - Counteracting the effect of fire on the soil protection provided by the vegetation and surface cover: treatments such as seeding and mulching are aimed at reducing runoff and erosion by providing protection to the soil surface.

78fdad27483e.title: Post-fire hillslope stabilization treatments
78fdad27483e.section: Classification of post-fire hillslope stabilization treatments
78fdad27483e.sentence: - Counteracting the effect of fire on specific soil properties involved in the runoff and erosion processes: treatments that seek for offsetting fire effects on soils such as enhanced soil water repellency (surfactants) or decreased soil aggregation (flocculants).

c1170c2c4513.title: Post-fire hillslope stabilization treatments
c1170c2c4513.section: Classification of post-fire hillslope stabilization treatments
c1170c2c4513.sentence: - Reducing slope length: treatments such as the erosion barriers are intended to reduce the amount of sediments that reach values-at-risk downhill by reducing the slope length and, thus, runoff velocity and erosion potential.

9e6e3aa0ac4d.title: Post-fire hillslope stabilization treatments
9e6e3aa0ac4d.section: Types, selection, and implementation of post-fire treatments
9e6e3aa0ac4d.sentence: Since the highest risk of catastrophic events happens during the first year after the fire, the implementation of any emergency treatment must be conducted quickly after the fire.

f54afb9bae09.title: Post-fire hillslope stabilization treatments
f54afb9bae09.section: Types, selection, and implementation of post-fire treatments
f54afb9bae09.sentence: Seeding have been the post-fire hillslope mitigation treatment most frequently used in the world and mainly in the USA (in the 1970s and 1980s 75% of the burned areas treated in the USA were seeded ).

73f54776ec24.title: Post-fire hillslope stabilization treatments
73f54776ec24.section: Types, selection, and implementation of post-fire treatments
73f54776ec24.sentence: However, negative side-effects such as the potential introduction of non-native species, negative interactions with the recover of native vegetation, and its low efficiency during the first year after the fire before their germination contributed to the reduction of its use (in the 2000s only 30% of the burned areas treated in the USA were seeded ).

a20edd1e481f.title: Tillage erosion
a20edd1e481f.sentence: Tillage erosion can be measured via the measurement of tillage translocation or the measurement of soil loss and accumulation.

1d7a9ca79148.title: Tillage erosion
1d7a9ca79148.sentence: Tillage translocation is normally measured with a tracer that is incorporated into the soil in plots.

355ec80cb646.title: Tillage erosion
355ec80cb646.sentence: The distributions of the tracer before and after tillage are used to calculate tillage translocation.

2da329ff0947.title: Tillage erosion
2da329ff0947.sentence: Two types of tracers, point tracers, and bulk tracers are being used.

a775f73ab068.title: Tillage erosion
a775f73ab068.sentence: Soil loss and accumulation by tillage erosion can be estimated from changes in surface elevation.

9f793c618912.title: Tillage erosion
9f793c618912.sentence: For example, elevation of a tilled field can be compared to an adjacent reference object that has not been eroded such as a fence line or hedgerow.

90553b0e78ca.title: Tillage erosion
90553b0e78ca.sentence: Elevation change can also be determined by taking repeated measurements of the soil surface elevations with high accuracy topographic survey techniques such as RTK GPS, total station and close range photogrammetry.

3d500f449040.title: Tillage erosion
3d500f449040.sentence: Another way to estimate soil loss and accumulation is to measure the changes in soil properties, such as soil organic matter content.

fa47d02834f5.title: Tillage erosion
fa47d02834f5.sentence: However, soil organic matter can be affected by many factors so it is not a very reliable method.

4e92725d942e.title: Tillage erosion
4e92725d942e.sentence: Since the 1980s, radioisotopes such as Cs-137 and Pb-210 have been used to provide much more accurate soil erosion estimates.

7ecfa6e69cb5.title: Tillage erosion
7ecfa6e69cb5.sentence: - The Tillage Erosion Prediction (TEP) model is designed to calculate net soil movement for individual hillslope segments across a field transect for individual tillage operations.

69727ad4b0ba.title: Tillage erosion
69727ad4b0ba.sentence: - The Soil Redistribution by Tillage (SORET) model is of the spatial distribution type and can perform 3D simulations of soil redistribution in DEMs on the field scale.

cdec585e3d5b.title: Tillage erosion
cdec585e3d5b.sentence: Input data include hillslope length, slope gradient of the eroding segment, and the erosivity of the tillage operations (β value).

81472cfe8f07.title: Tillage erosion
81472cfe8f07.sentence: Input data include hillslope segment elevation, slope gradient, and segment length as well as the erosivity of the tillage operations (β value).

1b4256f1ffca.title: Tillage erosion
1b4256f1ffca.sentence: - The Water and Tillage Erosion Model (WaTEM) is a model designed to calculate both water and tillage erosion rate at each grid node in Digital Elevation Model (DEM).

518abd32ba4d.title: Tillage erosion
518abd32ba4d.sentence: The tillage erosion component of WaTEM simulates the soil redistribution in DEM using a diffusion-type equation and assumes that all soil translocation occurs in the direction of steepest slope, irrespective of the pattern of tillage.

dba74499aa16.title: Tillage erosion
dba74499aa16.sentence: It takes into account the tillage pattern (directions) and can calculate tillage translocation in the directions parallel and perpendicular to the direction of tillage.

c8b591c4bd06.title: Tillage erosion
c8b591c4bd06.sentence: - The Tillage Erosion Model (TillEM) calculates point-tillage-erosion rates on grid nodes of a DEM along the lines both parallel and perpendicular to the direction of tillage, representing forward and lateral tillage translocation, which is very similar to the SORET model.

cda8e82aaa9b.title: Erosion index
cda8e82aaa9b.sentence: The erosion index (EI, also called the erodibility index) is created by dividing potential erosion (from all sources except gully erosion) by the T value, which is the rate of soil erosion above which long term productivity may be adversely affected.

2eb305cf6b8d.title: Erosion index
2eb305cf6b8d.sentence: The erodibility index is used in conjunction with conservation compliance and the Conservation Reserve Program.

200feec95869.title: Erosion index
200feec95869.sentence: For example, one of the eligibility requirements for the CRP is that land have an EI greater than 8.

81e8f7a90b3b.title: Erosion
81e8f7a90b3b.sentence: Often in the United States, farmers cultivating highly erodible land must comply with a conservation plan to be eligible for agricultural assistance.

35abad754e1b.title: Universal Soil Loss Equation
35abad754e1b.sentence: Various techniques have emerged over the last few decades to compute the five RUSLE factors.

b366e6bd76d0.title: Erosion prediction
b366e6bd76d0.sentence: Much of the mineland erosion literature is solely focused on fitting or improving RUSLE parameters.

9be0e98c9e82.title: Wind erosion equation
9be0e98c9e82.sentence: The Wind Erosion Equation (WEQ) is a mathematical model used to estimate the potential average annual soil loss (E) from a field due to wind erosion.

ead1567b9370.title: Wind erosion equation
ead1567b9370.sentence: A wind erosion equation is an equation used to design wind erosion control systems, which considers soil erodibility, soil roughness, climate, the unsheltered distance across a field, and the vegetative cover on the ground.

915a81600560.title: Wind erosion equation
915a81600560.sentence: This equation incorporates several key variables: the Soil Erodibility Index (I), which measures the susceptibility of soil to erosion; the Soil Ridge Roughness Factor (K), reflecting the surface roughness and its impact on wind flow; the Climatic Factor (C), representing the influence of wind speed and frequency on erosion; the Unsheltered Median Travel Distance (L), indicating the distance over which wind can travel unimpeded across a field; and the Equivalent Quantity of Vegetative Cover (V), accounting for the protective effect of vegetation in reducing soil erosion.

b1a666c70b2c.title: Wind erosion equation
b1a666c70b2c.sentence: Research indicates that soil movement commences when wind speeds surpass a critical threshold and the rate of erosion aligns with the cube of the friction velocity.

b17835084333.title: Wind erosion equation
b17835084333.sentence: The potency of wind in causing soil movement is notably correlated with the cube of the wind's speed and its persistence.

c908063591fd.title: Wind erosion equation
c908063591fd.sentence: Friction velocity, denoted as U∗, is a meteorological term for wind speed at the Earth's surface and can be quantified using the equation:

657584eea121.title: Wind erosion equation
657584eea121.sentence: In this equation, U represents the wind velocity measured at height z, and k is the von Kármán constant, roughly valued at 0.4.

81af746e1908.title: Wind erosion equation
81af746e1908.sentence: This relationship is indicative of the logarithmic wind profile, which describes the variation of wind speed with altitude, influenced by surface texture and atmospheric conditions.

a18e1646b132.title: Wind erosion equation
a18e1646b132.sentence: Records of detailed wind velocities and directions are predominantly sourced from strategic locations such as airports or military bases.

d6e83f1afc54.title: Wind erosion equation
d6e83f1afc54.sentence: The scarcity of these records, often limited in both geographical scope and historical range—frequently dating back to the World War II era—poses significant limitations to the research.

258df8534b12.title: Sediment
258df8534b12.sentence: In Earth and planetary sciences, sediment is a solid material made of loose particles that is transported to a new location where it is deposited.

9ba02e8b6ef8.title: Sediment
9ba02e8b6ef8.sentence: It occurs naturally and, through the processes of weathering and erosion, is broken down and subsequently transported by the action of wind, water, or ice or by the force of gravity acting on the particles.

5f44e82d4489.title: Sediment
5f44e82d4489.sentence: Sediments are most often transported by water (fluvial processes), but also wind (aeolian processes) and glaciers.

06a7f5bd9079.title: Sediment
06a7f5bd9079.sentence: Beach sands and river channel deposits are examples of fluvial transport and deposition, though sediment also often settles out of slow-moving or standing water in lakes and oceans.

2d6abe4d5c1b.title: Sediment
2d6abe4d5c1b.sentence: Desert sand dunes and loess are examples of aeolian transport and deposition.

90e82e032f8e.title: Sediment
90e82e032f8e.sentence: Glacial moraine deposits and till are ice-transported sediments.

b69f2daf7b2b.title: Sediment
b69f2daf7b2b.sentence: For example, sand and silt can be carried in suspension in river water and on reaching the sea bed deposited by sedimentation; if buried, they may eventually become sandstone and siltstone (sedimentary rocks) through lithification.

d9aeb35f19d3.title: Sediment
d9aeb35f19d3.sentence: Sediment can be classified based on its grain size, grain shape, and composition.

0ec70f6b200c.title: Sediment
0ec70f6b200c.sentence: Sediment size is measured on a log base 2 scale, called the "Phi" scale, which classifies particles by size from "colloid" to "boulder".

71b67f21f84a.title: Sediment
71b67f21f84a.sentence: This leads to an ambiguity in which clay can be used as both a size-range and a composition (see clay minerals).

d85203b306b2.title: Sediment
d85203b306b2.sentence: Seas, oceans, and lakes accumulate sediment over time.

82f1aca2f48c.title: Sediment
82f1aca2f48c.sentence: The sediment can consist of terrigenous material, which originates on land, but may be deposited in either terrestrial, marine, or lacustrine (lake) environments, or of sediments (often biological) originating in the body of water.

8219aa6ddcda.title: Sediment
8219aa6ddcda.sentence: Terrigenous material is often supplied by nearby rivers and streams or reworked marine sediment (e.g. sand).

d0c244dcfac4.title: Sediment
d0c244dcfac4.sentence: Lake bed sediments that have not solidified into rock can be used to determine past climatic conditions.

b06bf3d85c08.title: Erosion
b06bf3d85c08.sentence: Erosion is the action of surface processes (such as water flow or wind) that removes soil, rock, or dissolved material from one location on the Earth's crust and then transports it to another location where it is deposited.

6e777ea6f244.title: Erosion
6e777ea6f244.sentence: Erosion is distinct from weathering which involves no movement.

589115665a5b.title: Erosion
589115665a5b.sentence: Removal of rock or soil as clastic sediment is referred to as physical or mechanical erosion; this contrasts with chemical erosion, where soil or rock material is removed from an area by dissolution.

b12b0e79359c.title: Erosion
b12b0e79359c.sentence: Eroded sediment or solutes may be transported just a few millimetres, or for thousands of kilometres.

8a81c468b07a.title: Erosion
8a81c468b07a.sentence: Agents of erosion include rainfall; bedrock wear in rivers; coastal erosion by the sea and waves; glacial plucking, abrasion, and scour; areal flooding; wind abrasion; groundwater processes; and mass movement processes in steep landscapes like landslides and debris flows.

ca61a475c360.title: Erosion
ca61a475c360.sentence: Typically, physical erosion proceeds the fastest on steeply sloping surfaces, and rates may also be sensitive to some climatically controlled properties including amounts of water supplied (e.g., by rain), storminess, wind speed, wave fetch, or atmospheric temperature (especially for some ice-related processes).

34e954b5b74b.title: Erosion
34e954b5b74b.sentence: The transport of eroded materials from their original location is followed by deposition, which is arrival and emplacement of material at a new location.

4d30d52134d6.title: Erosion
4d30d52134d6.sentence: If the erosion rate exceeds soil formation, erosion destroys the soil.

56e6bc7411d1.title: Erosion
56e6bc7411d1.sentence: Lower rates of erosion can prevent the formation of soil features that take time to develop.

36f66829cab4.title: Aeolian processes
36f66829cab4.sentence: Aeolian processes are those processes of erosion, transport, and deposition of sediments that are caused by wind at or near the surface of the earth.

86393b3b37c4.title: Aeolian processes
86393b3b37c4.sentence: They are effective agents in regions with sparse vegetation, a lack of soil moisture and a large supply of unconsolidated sediments.

e9ea15cab626.title: Aeolian processes
e9ea15cab626.sentence: Aeolian processes are most important in areas where there is little or no vegetation.

d76587ffe869.title: Aeolian processes
d76587ffe869.sentence: Although water is a much more powerful eroding force than wind, aeolian processes are important in arid environments such as deserts.

4aa4bb14aa52.title: Aeolian processes
4aa4bb14aa52.sentence: Worldwide, erosion by water is more important than erosion by wind, but wind erosion is important in semiarid and arid regions.

6d0102473914.title: Aeolian processes
6d0102473914.sentence: However, aeolian deposits are not restricted to arid climates.

335056685d7e.title: Aeolian processes
335056685d7e.sentence: They are also seen along shorelines; Along stream courses in semiarid climates; in areas of ample sand weathered from weakly cemented sandstone outcrops; and in areas of glacial outwash.

7d42dd4e83ee.title: Aeolian processes
7d42dd4e83ee.sentence: As a result, there are distinct sandy (erg) and silty (loess) aeolian deposits, with only limited interbedding between the two.

1f70625ec1b4.title: Aeolian processes
1f70625ec1b4.sentence: Loess deposits are found further from the original source of sediments than ergs.

fad39a285eea.title: Aeolian processes
fad39a285eea.sentence: Attrition is the wearing down by collisions of particles entrained in a moving fluid.

9ece43f3fc1e.title: Aeolian processes
9ece43f3fc1e.sentence: It is effective at rounding sand grains and at giving them a distinctive frosted surface texture.

713a54b6045e.title: Aeolian processes
713a54b6045e.sentence: Collisions between windborne particles is a major source of dust in the size range of 2-5 microns.

155ad8767bc7.title: Aeolian processes
155ad8767bc7.sentence: For example, wind transports minerals from the Sahara to the Amazon basin.

def32e97439f.title: Aeolian processes
def32e97439f.sentence: Saharan dust is also responsible for forming red clay soils in southern Europe.

bbc4a58ef67e.title: Aeolian processes
bbc4a58ef67e.sentence: The term is derived from the name of the Greek god Aeolus, the keeper of the winds.

3597d7d4bca5.title: Sediment control
3597d7d4bca5.sentence: A sediment control is a practice or device designed to keep eroded soil on a construction site, so that it does not wash off and cause water pollution to a nearby stream, river, lake, or sea.

f213133142de.title: Sediment control
f213133142de.sentence: Sediment controls are usually employed together with erosion controls, which are designed to prevent or minimize erosion and thus reduce the need for sediment controls.

b95bea972b8b.title: Sediment control
b95bea972b8b.sentence: Sediment controls are generally designed to be temporary measures, however, some can be used for storm water management purposes.

4b29c24801ce.title: Sediment control
4b29c24801ce.sentence: All states in the U.S. have laws requiring installation of erosion and sediment controls (ESCs) on construction sites of a specified size.

cc11039e397d.title: Sediment control
cc11039e397d.sentence: Federal regulations require ESCs on sites 1 acre (0.40 ha) and larger.

1fccc51ee5b5.title: Sediment control
1fccc51ee5b5.sentence: The sediment controls must be installed before the beginning of land disturbance (i.e. land clearing, grubbing and grading) and must be maintained during the entire disturbance phase of construction.

f5fc28762e5e.title: Surface runoff
f5fc28762e5e.sentence: Montgomery County, Maryland implemented the first local government sediment control program in 1965, and this was followed by a statewide program in Maryland in 1970.

0847d06c8722.title: Soil erosion
0847d06c8722.section: Global environmental effects > Sedimentation of aquatic ecosystems
0847d06c8722.sentence: Soil erosion (especially from agricultural activity) is considered to be the leading global cause of diffuse water pollution, due to the effects of the excess sediments flowing into the world's waterways.

dae6f4b97e57.title: Soil erosion
dae6f4b97e57.section: Global environmental effects > Sedimentation of aquatic ecosystems
dae6f4b97e57.sentence: The effect of increased sediments loads on aquatic ecosystems can be catastrophic.

01f3f40fed87.title: Soil erosion
01f3f40fed87.section: Global environmental effects > Sedimentation of aquatic ecosystems
01f3f40fed87.sentence: The sediments themselves act as pollutants, as well as being carriers for other pollutants, such as attached pesticide molecules or heavy metals.

d26c03624bec.title: Sediment
d26c03624bec.section: Environmental issues > Erosion and agricultural sediment delivery to rivers
d26c03624bec.sentence: Loss of soil due to erosion removes useful farmland, adds to sediment loads, and can help transport anthropogenic fertilizers into the river system, which leads to eutrophication.

b5426f025fc1.title: Soil erosion
b5426f025fc1.section: Global environmental effects > Sedimentation of aquatic ecosystems
b5426f025fc1.sentence: Silt can smother the spawning beds of fish, by filling in the space between gravel on the stream bed.

63f77d47be3e.title: Soil erosion
63f77d47be3e.section: Global environmental effects > Sedimentation of aquatic ecosystems
63f77d47be3e.sentence: It also reduces their food supply, and causes major respiratory issues for them as sediment enters their gills.

a23c0173930d.title: Soil erosion
a23c0173930d.section: Global environmental effects > Sedimentation of aquatic ecosystems
a23c0173930d.sentence: The biodiversity of aquatic plant and algal life is reduced, and invertebrates are also unable to survive and reproduce.

ba4bc3c715f7.title: Soil erosion
ba4bc3c715f7.section: Global environmental effects > Sedimentation of aquatic ecosystems
ba4bc3c715f7.sentence: From the Yellow River, over 1.6 billion tons of sediment flows into the ocean each year, originating primarily from water erosion in the Loess Plateau region of the northwest.

84232bea8c26.title: Sediment
84232bea8c26.section: Environmental issues > Erosion and agricultural sediment delivery to rivers
84232bea8c26.sentence: For example, on the Madagascar high central plateau, which constitutes approximately ten percent of that country's land area, most of the land area is devegetated, and gullies have eroded into the underlying soil to form distinctive gulleys called lavakas.

07ca6c804ce3.title: Sediment
07ca6c804ce3.section: Environmental issues > Erosion and agricultural sediment delivery to rivers
07ca6c804ce3.sentence: Some areas have as many as 150 lavakas/square kilometer, and lavakas may account for 84% of all sediments carried off by rivers.

724f7e16cee8.title: Sediment
724f7e16cee8.section: Environmental issues > Erosion and agricultural sediment delivery to rivers
724f7e16cee8.sentence: This siltation results in discoloration of rivers to a dark red brown color and leads to fish kills.

bb6945e4e6e9.title: Sediment
bb6945e4e6e9.section: Environmental issues > Coastal development and sedimentation near coral reefs
bb6945e4e6e9.sentence: Watershed development near coral reefs is a primary cause of sediment-related coral stress.

1be1e5d1f558.title: Sediment
1be1e5d1f558.section: Environmental issues > Coastal development and sedimentation near coral reefs
1be1e5d1f558.sentence: Sediment can negatively affect corals in many ways, such as by physically smothering them, abrading their surfaces, causing corals to expend energy during sediment removal, and causing algal blooms that can ultimately lead to less space on the seafloor where juvenile corals (polyps) can settle.

47aa2f7e9d5a.title: Sediment
47aa2f7e9d5a.section: Environmental issues > Erosion and agricultural sediment delivery to rivers
47aa2f7e9d5a.sentence: The cost of removing an estimated 135 million m3 of accumulated sediments due to water erosion only is likely exceeding 2.3 billion euro (€) annually in the EU and UK, with large regional differences between countries.

924d3326460a.title: Mass wasting
924d3326460a.sentence: Mass wasting, also known as mass movement, is a general term for the movement of rock or soil down slopes under the force of gravity.

ac729bb94ad0.title: Mass wasting
ac729bb94ad0.sentence: It differs from other processes of erosion in that the debris transported by mass wasting is not entrained in a moving medium, such as water, wind, or ice.

cfb3396737ef.title: Mass wasting
cfb3396737ef.sentence: Types of mass wasting include creep, solifluction, rockfalls, debris flows, and landslides, each with its own characteristic features, and taking place over timescales from seconds to hundreds of years.

07f0bb958282.title: Mass wasting
07f0bb958282.sentence: The presence of water usually aids mass wasting, but the water is not abundant enough to be regarded as a transporting medium.

99a8e8e70ca3.title: Mass wasting
99a8e8e70ca3.sentence: With increasing water content, the mass wasting takes the form of debris avalanches, then earthflows, then mudflows.

f05c37efcc0a.title: Mass wasting
f05c37efcc0a.sentence: Further increase in water content produces a sheetflood, which is a form of sheet erosion rather than mass wasting.

cb9b78d51f8d.title: Mass wasting
cb9b78d51f8d.sentence: Based on how the soil, regolith or rock moves downslope as a whole, mass movements can be broadly classified as either creeps or landslides.

b7452ec1b756.title: Mass wasting
b7452ec1b756.sentence: Subsidence is sometimes also regarded as a form of mass wasting.

c131c8bf2e3c.title: Soil erosion
c131c8bf2e3c.sentence: Mass movement is an important part of the erosional process, and is often the first stage in the breakdown and transport of weathered materials in mountainous areas.

99087ab86cdc.title: Soil erosion
99087ab86cdc.sentence: It moves material from higher elevations to lower elevations where other eroding agents such as streams and glaciers can then pick up the material and move it to even lower elevations.

8e6cba2c894d.title: Mass wasting
8e6cba2c894d.sentence: Unconsolidated or weak debris are more susceptible to mass wasting, as are materials that lose cohesion when wetted.

e98f1726345e.title: Mass wasting
e98f1726345e.sentence: - Topography, such as steep slopes or cliffs.

d54d7abb8b6b.title: Mass wasting
d54d7abb8b6b.sentence: - Climate, with large temperature swings, frequent freezing and thawing, or abundant rainfall

a03317d61f4a.title: Mass wasting
a03317d61f4a.sentence: - Undercutting of the slope by excavation or erosion

016beb15f507.title: Mass wasting
016beb15f507.sentence: More gradual mass wasting, such as soil creep, poses challenges to civil engineering, as creep can deform roadways and structures and break pipelines.

56141a1db2c3.title: Mass wasting
56141a1db2c3.sentence: Rapid mass wasting events, such as landslides, can be deadly and destructive.

d35bd7789f57.title: Mass wasting
d35bd7789f57.sentence: Mitigation methods include slope stabilization, construction of walls, catchment dams, or other structures to contain rockfall or debris flows, afforestation, or improved drainage of source areas.

883b1358092e.title: Downhill creep
883b1358092e.sentence: Downhill creep, also known as soil creep or commonly just creep, is a type of creep characterized by the slow, downward progression of rock and soil down a low grade slope; it can also refer to slow deformation of such materials as a result of prolonged pressure and stress.

d517866b6cbd.title: Downhill creep
d517866b6cbd.sentence: Creep may appear to an observer to be continuous, but it really is the sum of numerous minute, discrete movements of slope material caused by the force of gravity.

4b037736e1f9.title: Mass wasting
4b037736e1f9.sentence: The steeper the slope, the faster the creep.

7ddd01eaf574.title: Downhill creep
7ddd01eaf574.sentence: Friction, being the primary force to resist gravity, is produced when one body of material slides past another offering a mechanical resistance between the two which acts to hold objects (or slopes) in place.

2101c219daa4.title: Downhill creep
2101c219daa4.sentence: As slope on a hill increases, the gravitational force that is perpendicular to the slope decreases and results in less friction between the material that could cause the slope to slide.

f46c36770a04.title: Downhill creep
f46c36770a04.sentence: The water offers cohesion to the sand which binds the sand particles together.

cd4a6ff2a5c4.title: Downhill creep
cd4a6ff2a5c4.sentence: This is because the presence of too much water fills the pores between the grains with water creating a slip plane between the particles and offering no cohesion causing them to slip and slide away.

f88112eaf5a2.title: Downhill creep
f88112eaf5a2.sentence: The presence of water may help the hillside stay put and give it cohesion, but in a very wet environment or during or after a large amount of precipitation the pores between the grains can become saturated with water and cause the ground to slide along the slip plane it creates.

40c38aec146d.title: Downhill creep
40c38aec146d.sentence: Creep can also be caused by the expansion of materials such as clay when they are exposed to water.

8ff58bb995bc.title: Downhill creep
8ff58bb995bc.sentence: Clay expands when wet, then contracts after drying.

8440dfeaaf35.title: Downhill creep
8440dfeaaf35.sentence: The expansion portion pushes downhill, then the contraction results in consolidation at the new offset.

f8cf0fe3dfcb.title: Mass wasting
f8cf0fe3dfcb.sentence: The surface soil can migrate under the influence of cycles of freezing and thawing, or hot and cold temperatures, inching its way towards the bottom of the slope forming terracettes.

f5b65bbfc754.title: Downhill creep
f5b65bbfc754.sentence: Objects resting on top of the soil are carried by it as it descends the slope.

6daf72f9e3e7.title: Downhill creep

4ff85825f7c3.title: Slope stability
4ff85825f7c3.sentence: Slope stability refers to the condition of inclined soil or rock slopes to withstand or undergo movement; the opposite condition is called slope instability or slope failure.

a78ffdf31a42.title: Slope stability
a78ffdf31a42.sentence: The stability condition of slopes is a subject of study and research in soil mechanics, geotechnical engineering, and engineering geology.

b88056cc72d8.title: Slope stability
b88056cc72d8.sentence: Analyses are generally aimed at understanding the causes of an occurred slope failure, or the factors that can potentially trigger a slope movement, resulting in a landslide, as well as at preventing the initiation of such movement, slowing it down or arresting it through mitigation countermeasures.

abaf868c0bc5.title: Slope stability
abaf868c0bc5.sentence: The stability of a slope is essentially controlled by the ratio between the available shear strength and the acting shear stress, which can be expressed in terms of a safety factor if these quantities are integrated over a potential (or actual) sliding surface.

e507dc8cd366.title: Slope stability
e507dc8cd366.sentence: A slope can be globally stable if the safety factor, computed along any potential sliding surface running from the top of the slope to its toe, is always larger than 1.

5124af62a6c2.title: Slope stability
5124af62a6c2.sentence: The smallest value of the safety factor will be taken as representing the global stability condition of the slope.

679973b6baf3.title: Slope stability
679973b6baf3.sentence: Values of the global or local safety factors close to 1 (typically comprised between 1 and 1.3, depending on regulations) indicate marginally stable slopes that require attention, monitoring and/or an engineering intervention (slope stabilization) to increase the safety factor and reduce the probability of a slope movement.

48024d5a38d9.title: Slope stability
48024d5a38d9.sentence: A previously stable slope can be affected by a number of predisposing factors or processes that reduce stability - either by increasing the shear stress or by decreasing the shear strength - and can ultimately result in slope failure.

3f45a2ddbc50.title: Slope stability
3f45a2ddbc50.sentence: Factors that can trigger slope failure include hydrologic events (such as intense or prolonged rainfall, rapid snowmelt, progressive soil saturation, increase of water pressure within the slope), earthquakes (including aftershocks), internal erosion (piping), surface or toe erosion, artificial slope loading (for instance due to the construction of a building), slope cutting (for instance to make space for roadways, railways, or buildings), or slope flooding (for instance by filling an artificial lake after damming a river).

bf43d27fb463.title: Slope stability
bf43d27fb463.sentence: Such slips often occur after a period of heavy rain, when the pore water pressure at the slip surface increases, reducing the effective normal stress and thus diminishing the restraining friction along the slip line.

38b0b216103d.title: Slope stability
38b0b216103d.sentence: This is combined with increased soil weight due to the added groundwater.

db97c3cac00e.title: Slope stability
db97c3cac00e.sentence: Nevertheless, failures in 'pure' clay can be quite close to circular.

ef65839a8ed0.title: Slope stability
ef65839a8ed0.sentence: At the other extreme, slab-shaped slips on hillsides can remove a layer of soil from the top of the underlying bedrock.

ebcf30616873.title: Slope stability
ebcf30616873.sentence: Reportedly, a higher water content can stabilize a slope and increase the angle of repose.

138a2513f2f8.title: Slope stability
138a2513f2f8.sentence: Generally, finer-grained soils rich in clay and silt retain more water than coarser sandy soils.

c4b68906b7ef.title: Landslide
c4b68906b7ef.sentence: Landslides, also known as landslips, rockslips, rockfalls, mudslides, mudslips or rockslides, are several forms of mass wasting that may include a wide range of ground movements, such as rockfalls, mudflows, shallow or deep-seated slope failures and debris flows.

083497745c98.title: Landslide
083497745c98.sentence: Landslides occur in a variety of environments, characterized by either steep or gentle slope gradients, from mountain ranges to coastal cliffs or even underwater, in which case they are called submarine landslides.

0c849cc938b3.title: Landslide
0c849cc938b3.sentence: Gravity is the primary driving force for a landslide to occur, but there are other factors affecting slope stability that produce specific conditions that make a slope prone to failure.

722249b4df34.title: Landslide
722249b4df34.sentence: Landslides occur when the slope (or a portion of it) undergoes some processes that change its condition from stable to unstable.

f04ff36f4841.title: Landslide
f04ff36f4841.sentence: This is essentially due to a decrease in the shear strength of the slope material, an increase in the shear stress borne by the material, or a combination of the two.

8d3d4673dbba.title: Landslide
8d3d4673dbba.sentence: In many cases, the landslide is triggered by a specific event (such as heavy rainfall, an earthquake, a slope cut to build a road, and many others), although this is not always identifiable.

12dc85b2d4eb.title: Landslide
12dc85b2d4eb.sentence: - increase in water content (loss of suction) or saturation by rain water infiltration, snow melting, or glaciers melting;

84c90f5c71ec.title: Landslide
84c90f5c71ec.sentence: - rising of groundwater and increase of pore water pressure (e.g. due to aquifer recharge in rainy seasons, or by rain water infiltration);

c9af3f98cdf4.title: Landslide
c9af3f98cdf4.sentence: - loss or absence of vertical vegetative structure, soil nutrients, and soil structure (e.g. after a wildfire);

6a2774df40c2.title: Landslide
6a2774df40c2.sentence: - erosion of the top of a slope by rivers or sea waves;

97d953720ff2.title: Landslide
97d953720ff2.sentence: - physical and chemical weathering (e.g. by repeated freezing and thawing, heating and cooling, salt leaking in the groundwater or mineral dissolution);

71897d9d0c21.title: Landslide
71897d9d0c21.sentence: - ground shaking caused by earthquakes, which can destabilize the slope directly (e.g., by inducing soil liquefaction) or weaken the material and cause movement that will eventually produce a landslide;

3fca11c67a0e.title: Landslide
3fca11c67a0e.sentence: - earthwork (e.g. by altering the shape of a slope, or imposing new loads);

aba29050940f.title: Landslide
aba29050940f.sentence: - in shallow soils, the removal of deep-rooted vegetation that binds colluvium to bedrock;

2e69d26b6d65.title: Landslide
2e69d26b6d65.sentence: Land degradation frequently leads to less stabilization of soil by vegetation.

3d7c95220698.title: Landslide
3d7c95220698.sentence: Land degradation and extreme rainfall can increase the frequency of erosion and landslide phenomena.

f140d4c6144e.title: Landslide

68a17a607354.title: Landslide

9c722678c24f.title: Landslide
9c722678c24f.sentence: Landslides that occur undersea, or have impact into water e.g. significant rockfall or volcanic collapse into the sea, can generate tsunamis.

638c34a2f548.title: Sediment transport
638c34a2f548.sentence: Sediment transport is the movement of solid particles (sediment), typically due to a combination of gravity acting on the sediment, and the movement of the fluid in which the sediment is entrained.

ffa7de97b05a.title: Sediment transport
ffa7de97b05a.sentence: Sediment transport occurs in natural systems where the particles are clastic rocks (sand, gravel, boulders, etc.), mud, or clay; the fluid is air, water, or ice; and the force of gravity acts to move the particles along the sloping surface on which they are resting.

00e33bd867dd.title: Sediment transport
00e33bd867dd.sentence: Knowledge of sediment transport is most often used to determine whether erosion or deposition will occur, the magnitude of this erosion or deposition, and the time and distance over which it will occur.

ecb7b0f9eeb3.title: Sediment
ecb7b0f9eeb3.sentence: Stronger flows will increase the lift and drag on the particle, causing it to rise, while larger or denser particles will be more likely to fall through the flow.

9a597c16c0c2.title: Sediment

61756ef9befb.title: Sediment

8b340c860029.title: Sediment
8b340c860029.sentence: In geography and geology, fluvial sediment processes or fluvial sediment transport are associated with rivers and streams and the deposits and landforms created by sediments.

1444c10237e5.sentence: In an abrasion process, debris in the basal ice scrapes along the bed, polishing and gouging the underlying rocks, similar to sandpaper on wood.

150b95047a48.title: Erosion
150b95047a48.sentence: Glaciers can also cause pieces of bedrock to crack off in the process of plucking.

e68e20fca911.title: Erosion

19f20aed04e3.title: Erosion

3fb91eb2de6f.title: Erosion
3fb91eb2de6f.sentence: These processes, combined with erosion and transport by the water network beneath the glacier, leave behind glacial landforms such as moraines, drumlins, ground moraine (till), glaciokarst, kames, kame deltas, moulins, and glacial erratics in their wake, typically at the terminus or during glacier retreat.

d32bb6bcc99f.title: Erosion

9c978c7514a4.title: Erosion

a7b347588dc9.title: Solifluction
a7b347588dc9.sentence: In solifluction lobes sediments form a tongue-shaped feature due to differential downhill flow rates.

07ca98bcadee.title: Solifluction
07ca98bcadee.sentence: In contrast, solifluction sheet sediments move more or less uniformly downslope, thus being a less selective form of erosion than solifluction lobes.

1e6ba6b7b1c6.title: Solifluction
1e6ba6b7b1c6.sentence: Deposits of slow periglacial solifluction compromise poorly stratified diamicton and diamicton where stratification is wholly lacking.

59e11ac89deb.title: Solifluction
59e11ac89deb.sentence: When stratification can be seen it is often distinguished by a buried organic soil.

2a5b3597d94f.title: Internal erosion
2a5b3597d94f.sentence: Internal erosion is the formation of voids within a soil caused by the removal of material by seepage.

2659b54e91bf.title: Internal erosion
2659b54e91bf.sentence: Internal erosion occurs when the hydraulic forces exerted by water seeping through the pores and cracks of the material in the dam and/or foundation are sufficient to detach particles and transport them out of the dam structure.

3b87e852662b.title: Internal erosion
3b87e852662b.sentence: It is the second most common cause of failure in levees and one of the leading causes of failures in earth dams, responsible for about half of embankment dam failures.

880a7f079dac.title: Internal erosion
880a7f079dac.sentence: Internal erosion is especially dangerous because there may be no external evidence, or only subtle evidence, that it is taking place.

87628c35f487.title: Internal erosion
87628c35f487.sentence: Usually a sand boil can be found, but the boil might be hidden under water.

ac6647aafc8e.title: Internal erosion
ac6647aafc8e.sentence: A dam may breach within a few hours after evidence of internal erosion becomes obvious.

e0ba31a36855.title: Internal erosion
e0ba31a36855.sentence: Piping is a related phenomenon and is defined as the progressive development of internal erosion by seepage, appearing downstream as a hole discharging water.

eb8ef6d5662c.title: Internal erosion
eb8ef6d5662c.sentence: Piping is induced by regressive erosion of particles from downstream and along the upstream line towards an outside environment until a continuous pipe is formed.

fce8dbc25c8b.title: Internal erosion
fce8dbc25c8b.section: Internal erosion and the piping process
fce8dbc25c8b.sentence: Internal erosion is also classified in four types, dependent on failure path, how the erosion initiates and progresses, and its location:

c9c78e04376d.title: Internal erosion
c9c78e04376d.section: Internal erosion and the piping process
c9c78e04376d.sentence: - Concentrated leak: seeping water erodes and enlarges a crack until a breach occurs.

77e371609be2.title: Internal erosion
77e371609be2.section: Internal erosion and the piping process
77e371609be2.sentence: - Backward erosion: initiated at the exit point of the seepage path, this type of erosion occurs when the hydraulic gradient is sufficiently high to cause particle detachment and transport; a pipe forms backwards from the exit point until breach.

20ba44f042f2.title: Internal erosion
20ba44f042f2.section: Internal erosion and the piping process
20ba44f042f2.sentence: - Suffusion: occurs in soils with a wide range of particle sizes.

f3f63b02fb08.title: Internal erosion
f3f63b02fb08.section: Internal erosion and the piping process
f3f63b02fb08.sentence: Finer soil particles are eroded through the voids between coarser particles.

2c8fa6b339cb.title: Internal erosion
2c8fa6b339cb.section: Internal erosion and the piping process
2c8fa6b339cb.sentence: - Soil contact erosion: a phenomenon called sheet flow occurs at interfaces between coarse and fine soils.

465f0f3c0d94.title: Internal erosion
465f0f3c0d94.section: Internal erosion and the piping process > Suffusion
465f0f3c0d94.sentence: Suffusion occurs when water flows through widely-graded or gap-graded, cohesionless soils.

595c8ce44173.title: Internal erosion
595c8ce44173.section: Internal erosion and the piping process
595c8ce44173.sentence: Soils susceptible to suffusion are termed internally unstable.

e2e6832bf63e.title: Internal erosion
e2e6832bf63e.section: Internal erosion and the piping process > Suffusion
e2e6832bf63e.sentence: The finer particles are transported by seepage, and the coarse particles carry most of the effective stress.

fe018284550a.title: Internal erosion
fe018284550a.sentence: Filters trap eroded particles while still allowing seepage, and are normally coarser and more permeable than the filtered soil.

8dfe6511e227.title: Internal erosion
8dfe6511e227.sentence: - Self-filtration: also defined as stability, the filter must be internally stable.

3979c9116ac6.title: Internal erosion
3979c9116ac6.sentence: - No cohesion: the filter must not have the ability to maintain cracks or the ability to cement.

1c4441ae66ab.title: Internal erosion
1c4441ae66ab.sentence: - Drainage: the filter must be sufficiently permeable to allow water pressure to dissipate.

359c6fa13f5f.title: Internal erosion
359c6fa13f5f.sentence: - Strength: the filter must be capable of transferring stresses within the dam without being crushed.

f18e8d2e4e16.title: Internal erosion
f18e8d2e4e16.section: Internal erosion and the piping process > Concentrated leak
f18e8d2e4e16.sentence: The critical hydraulic shear stress τc required for the initiation of concentrated leak erosion can be estimated using laboratory testing, such as the hole erosion test (HET) or the jet erosion test (JET).

0355b7ff40f5.title: Quick clay
0355b7ff40f5.sentence: Quick clay, also known as Leda clay and Champlain Sea clay in Canada, is any of several distinctively sensitive glaciomarine clays found in Canada, Norway, Russia, Sweden, Finland, the United States, and other locations around the world.

112c065f7b55.title: Quick clay
112c065f7b55.sentence: The clay is so unstable that when a mass of quick clay is subjected to sufficient stress, the material behavior may drastically change from that of a particulate material to that of a watery fluid.

1ae12fdc6fc6.title: Quick clay
1ae12fdc6fc6.sentence: Quick clay has a remolded strength which is much less than its strength upon initial loading.

e1b0359be4df.title: Quick clay
e1b0359be4df.sentence: This is caused by its highly unstable clay particle structure.

00a47936db5e.title: Silt
00a47936db5e.sentence: Quick clay (a combination of very fine silt and clay-sized particles from glacial grinding) is a particular challenge for civil engineering.

3d37981b91e0.title: Quick clay
3d37981b91e0.sentence: Quick clay is originally deposited in a marine environment.

0d3ee15e5a8b.title: Quick clay
0d3ee15e5a8b.sentence: Quick clay is found only in countries close to the North Pole, such as Russia, Canada, Norway, Sweden, Finland, and the United States (in Alaska), since they were glaciated during the Pleistocene epoch.

e3edbebcbf5b.title: Quick clay
e3edbebcbf5b.sentence: In Canada, the clay is associated primarily with the Pleistocene-era Champlain Sea, in the modern Ottawa Valley, the St. Lawrence Valley, and the Saguenay River regions.

e8d17ae03843.title: Quick clay
e8d17ae03843.sentence: Landslides occur because of the sudden soil liquefaction caused by external solicitations such as vibrations induced by an earthquake, or massive rainfalls.

01f668090746.title: Quick clay
01f668090746.sentence: In Canada alone, it has been associated with more than 250 mapped landslides.

94069a4be47b.title: Quick clay
94069a4be47b.sentence: In modern times, areas known to have quick clay deposits are commonly tested in advance of any major human development.

6cec4b6f2db7.title: Debris flow
6cec4b6f2db7.sentence: Debris flows are geological phenomena in which water-laden masses of soil and fragmented rock flow down mountainsides, funnel into stream channels, entrain objects in their paths, and form thick, muddy deposits on valley floors.

5be74c0a6a8c.title: Debris flow
5be74c0a6a8c.sentence: They generally have bulk densities comparable to those of rockslides and other types of landslides (roughly 2000 kilograms per cubic meter), but owing to widespread sediment liquefaction caused by high pore-fluid pressures, they can flow almost as fluidly as water.

2a55f6395229.title: Debris flow
2a55f6395229.sentence: Debris flows have volumetric sediment concentrations exceeding about 40 to 50%, and the remainder of a flow's volume consists of water.

eddd3ddd079f.title: Debris flow
eddd3ddd079f.sentence: Sediment-rich water floods with solid concentrations ranging from about 10 to 40% behave somewhat differently from debris flows and are known as hyperconcentrated floods.

d77c3a0907ca.title: Debris flow
d77c3a0907ca.sentence: Media reports often use the term mudflow to describe debris flows, but true mudflows are composed mostly of grains smaller than sand.

11eb01dc9739.title: Debris flow
11eb01dc9739.sentence: In all cases the chief conditions required for debris flow initiation include the presence of slopes steeper than about 25 degrees, the availability of abundant loose sediment, soil, or weathered rock, and sufficient water to bring this loose material to a state of almost complete saturation (with all the pore space filled).

6b372112296b.title: Debris flow
6b372112296b.sentence: Debris flows can be triggered by intense rainfall or snowmelt, by dam-break or glacial outburst floods, or by landsliding that may or may not be associated with intense rain or earthquakes.

21078031c24b.title: Debris flow
21078031c24b.sentence: Debris flows can be more frequent following forest and brush fires, as experience in southern California demonstrates.

caf7dc5daf80.title: Debris flow
caf7dc5daf80.sentence: Debris flows descending steep channels commonly attain speeds that surpass 10 m/s (36 km/h), although some large flows can reach speeds that are much greater.

8ee1f35f51d5.title: Debris flow
8ee1f35f51d5.sentence: Debris flows with volumes ranging up to about 100,000 cubic meters occur frequently in mountainous regions worldwide.

05c0487c3fe8.title: Debris flow
05c0487c3fe8.sentence: The front, or 'head' of a debris-flow surge often contains an abundance of coarse material such as boulders and logs that impart a great deal of friction.

760b3768d73a.title: Debris flow
760b3768d73a.sentence: Trailing behind the high-friction flow head is a lower-friction, mostly liquefied flow body that contains a higher percentage of sand, silt and clay.

5c74da6fdc78.title: Debris flow
5c74da6fdc78.sentence: Fully exposed deposits commonly have lobate forms with boulder-rich snouts, and the lateral margins of debris-flow deposits and paths are commonly marked by the presence of boulder-rich lateral levees.

9f1550eef3c3.title: Debris flow
9f1550eef3c3.sentence: This poor sorting of sediment grains distinguishes debris-flow deposits from most water-laid sediments.

2ca96fb219ee.title: Debris flow
2ca96fb219ee.sentence: They make up significant percentages of many alluvial fans and debris cones along steep mountain fronts.

40cd3187ba11.title: Debris flow
40cd3187ba11.sentence: Notable debris-flow disasters of the twentieth century involved more than 20,000 fatalities in Armero, Colombia, in 1985 and tens of thousands in Vargas State, Venezuela, in 1999.

472a6d02b854.title: Debris flow
472a6d02b854.sentence: To prevent debris flows reaching property and people, a debris basin may be constructed.

e160827b9394.title: Debris flow
e160827b9394.sentence: Such constructions are considered to be a last resort because they are expensive to construct and require commitment to annual maintenance.

7692b0e3a723.title: Deposition (geology)
7692b0e3a723.sentence: Deposition is the geological process in which sediments, soil and rocks are added to a landform or landmass.

4e626040f861.title: Deposition (geology)
4e626040f861.sentence: Wind, ice, water, and gravity transport previously weathered surface material, which, at the loss of enough kinetic energy in the fluid, is deposited, building up layers of sediment.

a3f221e10dad.title: Deposition (geology)
a3f221e10dad.sentence: This occurs when the forces responsible for sediment transportation are no longer sufficient to overcome the forces of gravity and friction, creating a resistance to motion; this is known as the null point hypothesis.

ee7f2068c3e6.title: Deposition (geology)
ee7f2068c3e6.section: Null point hypothesis > Deposition of non-cohesive sediments
ee7f2068c3e6.sentence: Large-grain sediments transported by either bedload or suspended load will come to rest when there is insufficient bed shear stress and fluid turbulence to keep the sediment moving; with the suspended load this can be some distance as the particles need to fall through the water column.

4ff8cb3327a7.title: Deposition (geology)
4ff8cb3327a7.section: Null point hypothesis > Deposition of cohesive sediments
4ff8cb3327a7.sentence: The cohesion of sediment occurs with the small grain sizes associated with silts and clays, or particles smaller than 4ϕ on the phi scale.

4348130a4a77.title: Deposition (geology)
4348130a4a77.section: Null point hypothesis > Deposition of cohesive sediments
4348130a4a77.sentence: If these fine particles remain dispersed in the water column, Stokes law applies to the settling velocity of the individual grains, although due to seawater being a strong electrolyte bonding agent, flocculation occurs where individual particles create an electrical bond adhering each other together to form flocs.

1e25d79ff99e.title: Deposition (geology)
1e25d79ff99e.sentence: Deposition can also refer to the buildup of sediment from organically derived matter or chemical processes.

4c4ead824f00.title: Deposition (geology)
4c4ead824f00.sentence: For example, chalk is made up partly of the microscopic calcium carbonate skeletons of marine plankton, the deposition of which induced chemical processes (diagenesis) to deposit further calcium carbonate.

bb6a3a796e96.title: Deposition (geology)
bb6a3a796e96.sentence: Similarly, the formation of coal begins with the deposition of organic material, mainly from plants, in anaerobic conditions.

95886593ce67.title: Aeolian processes
95886593ce67.sentence: Particles are transported by winds through suspension, saltation (skipping or bouncing) and creeping (rolling or sliding) along the ground.

05d68eb49ef5.title: Aeolian processes
05d68eb49ef5.sentence: The minimum wind velocity to initiate transport is called the fluid threshold or static threshold and is the wind velocity required to begin dislodging grains from the surface.

0eb992eed02c.title: Aeolian processes
0eb992eed02c.sentence: Once transport is initiated, there is a cascade effect from grains tearing loose other grains, so that transport continues until the wind velocity drops below the dynamic threshold or impact threshold, which is usually less than the fluid threshold.

74b2828d9a8d.title: Aeolian processes
74b2828d9a8d.sentence: In other words, there is hysteresis in the wind transport system.

346027eb872b.title: Aeolian processes
346027eb872b.sentence: Turbulent air motion supports the weight of suspended particles and allows them to be transported for great distances.

ca72114dfddb.title: Aeolian processes
ca72114dfddb.sentence: Wind is particularly effective at separating sediment grains under 0.05 mm in size from coarser grains as suspended particles.

2c789fc64aae.title: Aeolian processes
2c789fc64aae.sentence: Saltation is most important for grains of up to 2 mm in size.

fc8fa347af6f.title: Aeolian processes
fc8fa347af6f.sentence: A saltating grain may hit other grains that jump up to continue the saltation.

c85e6d2871a0.title: Aeolian processes
c85e6d2871a0.sentence: The grain may also hit larger grains (over 2 mm in size) that are too heavy to hop, but that slowly creep forward as they are pushed by saltating grains.

7c4a966d1353.title: Aeolian processes
7c4a966d1353.sentence: Surface creep accounts for as much as 25 percent of grain movement in a desert.

8f845e90450a.title: Aeolian processes
8f845e90450a.sentence: Vegetation is effective at suppressing aeolian transport.

8ee41fc9096e.title: Aeolian processes
8ee41fc9096e.sentence: Vegetation cover of as little as 15% is sufficient to eliminate most sand transport.

4d646116a4c6.title: Aeolian processes
4d646116a4c6.sentence: Deflation is the lifting and removal of loose material from the surface by wind turbulence.

a10c7adb9c84.title: Aeolian processes
a10c7adb9c84.sentence: It takes place by three mechanisms: traction/surface creep, saltation, and suspension.

c854628a1ab9.title: Aeolian processes
c854628a1ab9.sentence: Saltation likely accounts for 50–70 % of deflation, while suspension accounts for 30–40 % and surface creep accounts for 5–25 %.

b9abe5d6e2ed.title: Aeolian processes
b9abe5d6e2ed.sentence: Regions which experience intense and sustained erosion are called deflation zones.

92b075ce8c9e.title: Aeolian processes
92b075ce8c9e.sentence: Most aeolian deflation zones are composed of desert pavement, a sheet-like surface of rock fragments that remains after wind and water have removed the fine particles.

5f40c2f50f36.title: Aeolian processes
5f40c2f50f36.sentence: The rock mantle in desert pavements protects the underlying material from further deflation.

217082708668.title: Aeolian processes
217082708668.sentence: Blowouts are hollows formed by wind deflation.

6e481d150ada.title: Aeolian processes
6e481d150ada.sentence: The smallest are mere dimples 0.3 meters (1 ft) deep and 3 meters (10 ft) in diameter.

916a3f2228df.title: Aeolian processes
916a3f2228df.sentence: The largest include the blowout hollows of Mongolia, which can be 8 kilometers (5 mi) across and 60 to 100 meters (200 to 400 ft) deep.

8ac3a1ae9f5e.title: Aeolian processes
8ac3a1ae9f5e.sentence: A dune is an accumulations of sediment blown by the wind into a mound or ridge.

c50b5752e2c7.title: Aeolian processes
c50b5752e2c7.sentence: They differ from sand shadows or sand drifts in that they are independent of any topographic obstacle.

ab4cc5b6bff9.title: Aeolian processes
ab4cc5b6bff9.sentence: Dunes have gentle upwind slopes on the windward side.

2d49c0761949.title: Aeolian processes
2d49c0761949.sentence: The downwind portion of the dune, the lee slope, is commonly a steep avalanche slope referred to as a slipface.

bd4bb5e77ed3.title: Aeolian processes
bd4bb5e77ed3.sentence: Transverse dunes occur in areas dominated by a single direction of the prevailing wind.

de290cd0dd51.title: Aeolian processes
de290cd0dd51.sentence: In areas where sand is not abundant, transverse dunes take the form of barchans or crescent dunes.

70d47365aa15.title: Aeolian processes
70d47365aa15.sentence: Linear dunes can be traced up to tens of kilometers, with heights sometimes in excess of 70 meters (230 ft).

f9b72168d34a.title: Aeolian processes
f9b72168d34a.sentence: Complex dunes (star dunes or rhourd dunes) are characterized by having more than two slip faces.

53c7299dc065.title: Aeolian processes
53c7299dc065.sentence: Vegetated parabolic dunes are crescent-shaped, but the ends of the crescent point upwind, not downwind.

eb74bf9d13ac.title: Aeolian processes
eb74bf9d13ac.sentence: They form from the interaction of vegetation patches with active sand sources, such as blowouts.

4aba2b346dfe.title: Aeolian processes
4aba2b346dfe.sentence: He recognized two basic dune types, the crescentic dune, which he called "barchan", and the linear dune, which he called longitudinal or "seif" (Arabic for "sword").

6fea55f2b7f3.title: Aeolian processes
6fea55f2b7f3.sentence: In 1941, John Tilton Hack added parabolic dunes, which are strongly influenced by vegetation, to the list of dune types.

9125bf04d577.title: Aeolian processes
9125bf04d577.sentence: Abrasion (also sometimes called corrasion) is the process of wind-driven grains knocking or wearing material off of landforms.

0cef1e4451fd.title: Aeolian processes
0cef1e4451fd.sentence: It was once considered a major contributor to desert erosion, but by the mid-20th Century, it had come to be considered much less important.

9b26f233dda2.title: Aeolian processes
9b26f233dda2.sentence: Many desert features once attributed to wind abrasion, including wind caves, mushroom rocks, and the honeycomb weathering called tafoni, are now attributed to differential weathering, rainwash, deflation rather than abrasion, or other processes.

f77d2c5cf16f.title: Aeolian processes
f77d2c5cf16f.sentence: Wind can normally lift sand only a short distance, with most windborne sand remaining within 50 centimeters (20 in) of the surface and practically none normally being carried above 2 meters (6 ft).

82cfeab01e39.title: Aeolian processes
82cfeab01e39.sentence: Yardangs are one kind of desert feature that is widely attributed to wind abrasion.

bf049503a449.title: Aeolian processes
bf049503a449.sentence: These are rock ridges, up to tens of meters high and kilometers long, that have been streamlined by desert winds.

d1cf7d17bd3d.title: Aeolian processes
d1cf7d17bd3d.sentence: They form mostly in softer material such as silts.

2e07f2f66370.title: Aeolian processes
2e07f2f66370.sentence: Polished or faceted surfaces called ventifacts are rare, requiring abundant sand, powerful winds, and a lack of vegetation for their formation.

5adbdc5ea5b3.title: Landslide
5adbdc5ea5b3.sentence: Climate-change impact on temperature, both average rainfall and rainfall extremes, and evapotranspiration may affect landslide distribution, frequency and intensity.

314f8111ab2f.title: Landslide
314f8111ab2f.sentence: However, this impact shows strong variability in different areas.

fbd8342fdf6f.title: Landslide
fbd8342fdf6f.sentence: Therefore, the effects of climate change on landslides need to be studied on a regional scale.

28e7a2432d9f.title: Landslide
28e7a2432d9f.sentence: Climate change can have both positive and negative impacts on landslides.

fe73efce8fdf.title: Landslide
fe73efce8fdf.sentence: Temperature rise may increase evapotranspiration, leading to a reduction in soil moisture and stimulate vegetation growth, also due to a CO2 increase in the atmosphere.

2f8d87c6084d.title: Landslide
2f8d87c6084d.sentence: Both effects may reduce landslides in some conditions.

edf31f6aa5fb.title: Landslide
edf31f6aa5fb.sentence: On the other side, temperature rise causes an increase of landslides due to

f82fad2034d7.title: Landslide
f82fad2034d7.sentence: - the acceleration of snowmelt and an increase of rain on snow during spring, leading to strong infiltration events.

47f6968db960.title: Landslide
47f6968db960.sentence: - Permafrost degradation that reduces the cohesion of soils and rock masses due to the loss of interstitial ice.

d393ca5e5420.title: Landslide
d393ca5e5420.sentence: This mainly occurs at high elevation.

c4b08cc0bcb8.title: Landslide
c4b08cc0bcb8.sentence: - Glacier retreat that has the dual effect of relieving mountain slopes and increasing their steepness.

7b0875bbfcc1.title: Landslide
7b0875bbfcc1.sentence: Weather extremes are expected to increase due to climate change including heavy precipitation.

09c57a8d92a1.title: Landslide
09c57a8d92a1.sentence: This yields negative effects on landslides due to focused infiltration in soil and rock and an increase of runoff events, which may trigger debris flows.

ce174d661090.title: Landslide
ce174d661090.sentence: Landslide hazard analysis and mapping can provide useful information for catastrophic loss reduction, and assist in the development of guidelines for sustainable land-use planning.

d8b309ec8f31.title: Landslide
d8b309ec8f31.sentence: The analysis is used to identify the factors that are related to landslides, estimate the relative contribution of factors causing slope failures, establish a relation between the factors and landslides, and to predict the landslide hazard in the future based on such a relationship.

553a305ba215.title: Landslide
553a305ba215.sentence: The factors that have been used for landslide hazard analysis can usually be grouped into geomorphology, geology, land use/land cover, and hydrogeology.

821dee1ff372.title: Landslide
821dee1ff372.sentence: Since many factors are considered for landslide hazard mapping, geographic information system (GIS) is an appropriate tool because it has functions of collection, storage, manipulation, display, and analysis of large amounts of spatially referenced data which can be handled fast and effectively.

b6a228745739.title: Landslide
b6a228745739.sentence: Before and after aerial photographs and satellite imagery are used to gather landslide characteristics, like distribution and classification, and factors like slope, lithology, and land use/land cover to be used to help predict future events.

171a4fa4973e.title: Landslide
171a4fa4973e.sentence: In general, to predict landslides, one must assume that their occurrence is determined by certain geologic factors, and that future landslides will occur under the same conditions as past events.

85a2cf78dc9d.title: Landslide
85a2cf78dc9d.sentence: Therefore, it is necessary to establish a relationship between the geomorphologic conditions in which the past events took place and the expected future conditions.

40ce018197e9.title: Landslide
40ce018197e9.sentence: Such maps should show the locations of previous events as well as clearly indicate the probable locations of future events.

d9982fba7221.title: Landslide
d9982fba7221.sentence: The monitoring of landslides is essential for estimating the dangerous situations, making it possible to issue alerts on time, to avoid loses of lives and property, and to have proper planning and reducing measures in place.

085fb5028004.title: Landslide
085fb5028004.sentence: - InSAR (Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar): This remote sensing technique measures ground displacement over time with high precision.

99fd7de0c9d3.title: Landslide
99fd7de0c9d3.sentence: It is ideal for large-scale monitoring.

b8f337b0293d.title: Landslide
b8f337b0293d.sentence: - LiDAR (Light Detection and Ranging): Provides detailed 3D models of terrain to detect changes over time by comparison of different point clouds acquired over time.

2c2da8b7053d.title: Landslide
2c2da8b7053d.sentence: - UAVs (Unmanned Aerial Vehicles): This technique captures high-resolution images and topographic data in inaccessible areas.

938326ecef4c.title: Landslide
938326ecef4c.sentence: - GPS (Global Positioning System): Tracks ground movements at specific points over time using a constellation of satellites orbiting around the Earth.

5d78c6289def.title: Landslide
5d78c6289def.sentence: - Topographic surveys: Measures displacements of marked targets on a slope.

40afba9c2ade.title: Landslide
40afba9c2ade.sentence: - Ground-based radar (GB-SAR): Continuously monitors surface deformation using a SAR sensor and detects movement in real-time.

08a2416f7303.title: Landslide
08a2416f7303.sentence: - Piezometers: Monitors groundwater levels and pore water pressure, which are critical triggers for landslides.

9441d83c8616.title: Landslide
9441d83c8616.sentence: - Inclinometers: Detects subsurface movements by monitoring changes in the inclination of a borehole.

8693fa7d3a22.title: Landslide
8693fa7d3a22.sentence: - Extensometers: Measures displacement along cracks or tension zones.

105d841a12cd.title: Landslide
105d841a12cd.sentence: - Tiltmeters: Detects small angular changes in the slope surface or retaining walls.

15ac1122de19.title: Landslide
15ac1122de19.sentence: A landslide in which the sliding surface is located within the soil mantle or weathered bedrock (typically to a depth from few decimeters to some meters) is called a shallow landslide.

c20ccd244ac4.title: Landslide
c20ccd244ac4.sentence: Deep-seated landslides are those in which the sliding surface is mostly deeply located, for instance well below the maximum rooting depth of trees.

eb0c58904534.title: Landslide
eb0c58904534.sentence: Debris slides and debris flows are usually shallow.

34f21acf62a4.title: Landslide
34f21acf62a4.sentence: Shallow landslides can often happen in areas that have slopes with high permeable soils on top of low permeable soils.

a2d9760756d8.title: Landslide
a2d9760756d8.sentence: The low permeable soil traps the water in the shallower soil generating high water pressures.

926bdac65663.title: Landslide
926bdac65663.sentence: As the top soil is filled with water, it can become unstable and slide downslope.

626255303683.title: Landslide
626255303683.sentence: They usually involve deep regolith, weathered rock, and/or bedrock and include large slope failures associated with translational, rotational, or complex movements.

3e8e667d43a2.title: Landslide
3e8e667d43a2.sentence: They tend to form along a plane of weakness such as a fault or bedding plane.

0b6fef2dc35d.title: Landslide
0b6fef2dc35d.sentence: They can be visually identified by concave scarps at the top and steep areas at the toe.

32832a641333.title: Landslide
32832a641333.sentence: Deep-seated landslides also shape landscapes over geological timescales and produce sediment that strongly alters the course of fluvial streams.

30e7012abee0.title: Silt fence
30e7012abee0.sentence: A silt fence, sometimes (misleadingly) called a filter fence, is a temporary sediment control device used on construction sites to protect water quality in nearby streams, rivers, lakes and seas from sediment (loose soil) in stormwater runoff.

5acc4468affa.title: Silt fence
5acc4468affa.sentence: A typical fence consists of a piece of synthetic filter fabric (also called a geotextile) stretched between a series of wooden or metal fence stakes along a horizontal contour level.

97a761ef5568.title: Silt fence
97a761ef5568.sentence: The stakes are installed on the downhill side of the fence, and the bottom edge of the fabric can be trenched into the soil and backfilled on the uphill side, although it is quite difficult to move the trenched "spoil" from the downside to the upside of the trench.

9a15e4c2a433.title: Silt fence
9a15e4c2a433.sentence: The design/placement of the silt fence should create a pooling of runoff, which then allows sedimentation to occur.

b1b0f655d295.title: Silt fence
b1b0f655d295.sentence: Water can seep through the silt fence fabric, but the fabric often becomes "blocked off" with fine soil particles (all sediment-retention devices have this challenge, and none of them "filter" storm water for very long).

22524e6d953c.title: Silt fence
22524e6d953c.sentence: Silt fences are widely used on construction sites in North America and elsewhere, due to their low cost and simple design.

a3c7de51f881.title: Silt fence
a3c7de51f881.sentence: Although there have been few field tests of silt fences installed at construction sites, these tests have shown generally poor results.

d3e6f4e8c2ec.title: Silt fence
d3e6f4e8c2ec.sentence: Silt fences may perform poorly for a variety of reasons, including improper location (e.g. placing fence where it will not pond runoff water), improper installation (e.g. failure to adequately embed and backfill the lower edge of fabric in the soil) and lack of maintenance—fabric falling off of the posts, or posts knocked down.

d0a6349c86de.title: Silt fence
d0a6349c86de.section: Design and installation > Static slicing installation
d0a6349c86de.sentence: The technique involves inserting a narrow blade into the soil with a wedge-type point on its tip to slightly disrupt the soil upward, while simultaneously inserting the silt fence fabric into the slot with a moving pivot, while the machine is moving forward.

7d2df896e6d0.title: Silt fence
7d2df896e6d0.section: Design and installation > Static slicing installation
7d2df896e6d0.sentence: This step is followed by mechanical soil compaction, setting of fence posts, and attaching the fabric.

10d86e2badfe.title: Silt fence
10d86e2badfe.sentence: Since 1998, static slicing the material into the ground has proven to be the most efficient and most effective installation method because slicing maintains the soil on both sides of the fence, and is conducive to proper compaction—which is critical to performance, as well.

7b7566a1e999.title: Dust storm
7b7566a1e999.sentence: A dust storm, also called a sandstorm, is a meteorological phenomenon common in arid and semi-arid regions.

915e0fdc687d.title: Dust storm
915e0fdc687d.sentence: Dust storms arise when a gust front or other strong wind blows loose sand and dirt from a dry surface.

8c5283fa4a98.title: Aeolian processes
8c5283fa4a98.sentence: Dust storms are wind storms that have entrained enough dust to reduce visibility to less than 1 kilometer (0.6 mi).

b5b6acc9a1be.title: Dust storm
b5b6acc9a1be.sentence: As the force of dust passing over loosely held particles increases, particles of sand first start to vibrate, then to move across the surface in a process called saltation.

8cb8ea8837d9.title: Dust storm
8cb8ea8837d9.sentence: As they repeatedly strike the ground, they loosen and break off smaller particles of dust which then begin to travel in suspension.

b914bbea0fe9.title: Dust storm
b914bbea0fe9.sentence: Drought and wind contribute to the emergence of dust storms, as do poor farming and grazing practices by exposing the dust and sand to the wind.

e68556214a94.title: Dust storm
e68556214a94.sentence: Wildfires can lead to dust storms as well.

eb8bd050d807.title: Dust storm
eb8bd050d807.sentence: One poor farming practice which contributes to dust storms is dryland farming.

9ffd8aebf80f.title: Dust storm
9ffd8aebf80f.sentence: Particularly poor dryland farming techniques are intensive tillage or not having established crops or cover crops when storms strike at particularly vulnerable times prior to revegetation.

d745eee09bdd.title: Dust storm
d745eee09bdd.sentence: Gust fronts may be produced by the outflow of rain-cooled air from an intense thunderstorm.

6cf689a9c22c.title: Dust storm
6cf689a9c22c.sentence: Or, the wind gusts may be produced by a dry cold front: that is, a cold front that is moving into a dry air mass and is producing no precipitation—the type of dust storm which was common during the Dust Bowl years in the U.S. Following the passage of a dry cold front, convective instability resulting from cooler air riding over heated ground can maintain the dust storm initiated at the front.

43f08021edaf.title: Dust storm
43f08021edaf.section: Physical and environmental effects > Economic impact
43f08021edaf.sentence: Dust storms cause soil loss from the drylands, and worse, they preferentially remove organic matter and the nutrient-rich lightest particles, thereby reducing agricultural productivity.

06af8cba49c3.title: Dust storm
06af8cba49c3.section: Physical and environmental effects > Economic impact
06af8cba49c3.sentence: Also, the abrasive effect of the storm damages young crop plants.

78698082f672.title: Dust storm
78698082f672.sentence: Saharan dust storms have increased approximately 10-fold during the half-century since the 1950s, causing topsoil loss in Niger, Chad, northern Nigeria, and Burkina Faso.

121eb5186b18.title: Dust storm
121eb5186b18.section: Physical and environmental effects > Health impact
121eb5186b18.sentence: Dust pneumonia is the result of large amounts of dust being inhaled.

a6cdfb9d1170.title: Dust storm
a6cdfb9d1170.section: Physical and environmental effects > Health impact
a6cdfb9d1170.sentence: Prolonged and unprotected exposure of the respiratory system in a dust storm can also cause silicosis, which, if left untreated, will lead to asphyxiation; silicosis is an incurable condition that may also lead to lung cancer.

f73e32bcf05e.title: Dust storm
f73e32bcf05e.section: Physical and environmental effects > Economic impact
f73e32bcf05e.sentence: Dust can also have beneficial effects where it deposits: Central and South American rainforests get significant quantities of mineral nutrients from the Sahara; iron-poor ocean regions get iron; and dust in Hawaii increases plantain growth.

b830e2ee69dc.title: Dust storm
b830e2ee69dc.section: Physical and environmental effects > Economic impact
b830e2ee69dc.sentence: In northern China as well as the mid-western U.S., ancient dust storm deposits known as loess are highly fertile soils, but they are also a significant source of contemporary dust storms when soil-securing vegetation is disturbed.

e3a31c8b64a4.title: Dust storm
e3a31c8b64a4.sentence: Starting in 1978, China has been creating a great green wall by planting trees in the Gobi desert to reclaim land from the desert.

a9f31d82c22e.title: Dust Bowl
a9f31d82c22e.sentence: The Dust Bowl (1930–1940) was a period of severe dust storms and arid weather conditions that greatly damaged the agriculture and ecology of the High Plains and North American prairies.

010892f0d9fc.title: Dust Bowl
010892f0d9fc.sentence: In the United States, it primarily affected farmland in western Kansas, the Oklahoma and Texas panhandles, southeast Colorado, and northeast New Mexico.

655e8529f20f.title: Dust Bowl
655e8529f20f.sentence: The drought and erosion of the Dust Bowl affected 100 million acres (400,000 km2) that centered on the Texas Panhandle and Oklahoma Panhandle and touched adjacent sections of New Mexico, Colorado, and Kansas.

0e5829790734.title: Dust Bowl
0e5829790734.sentence: The phenomenon was caused by a combination of natural factors, including severe drought, and human behavior, including the destruction of natural topsoil by settlers who did not use dryland farming methods to prevent wind erosion.

abe9a48bed34.title: Dust Bowl
abe9a48bed34.sentence: With insufficient understanding of the ecology of the plains, farmers had conducted extensive deep plowing of the Great Plains' virgin topsoil during the previous decade; this displaced the native, deep-rooted grasses that normally trapped soil and moisture even during periods of drought and high winds.

5cf6965c21db.title: Dust Bowl
5cf6965c21db.sentence: The widespread conversion of the land by deep plowing and other soil preparation methods to enable agriculture eliminated the native grasses that held the soil in place and helped retain moisture during dry periods.

654d630f84c4.title: Dust Bowl
654d630f84c4.sentence: Furthermore, cotton farmers left fields bare during the winter, when winds in the High Plains are highest, and burned the stubble as a means to control weeds before planting, thereby depriving the soil of organic nutrients and surface vegetation.

9f0d7115d801.title: Dust Bowl
9f0d7115d801.sentence: The drought came in three waves: 1934, 1936, and 1939–1940, but some regions of the High Plains experienced drought conditions for as long as eight years.

083a02d4d15a.title: Dust Bowl
083a02d4d15a.sentence: The drought dried the topsoil and over time it became friable, reduced to a powdery consistency in some places.

a06bc77f1761.title: Dust Bowl
a06bc77f1761.sentence: The persistent dry weather caused crops to fail, leaving the plowed fields exposed to wind erosion.

1b00f73c2983.title: Dust Bowl
