1b00f73c2983.sentence: These choking billows of dust – named "black blizzards" or "black rollers" – traveled cross-country, reaching as far as the East Coast and striking such cities as New York City and Washington, D.C. On the plains, they often reduced visibility to three feet (1 m) or less.

f1333a4777a3.title: Dust Bowl
f1333a4777a3.sentence: Beginning on May 9, 1934, a strong, two-day dust storm removed massive amounts of Great Plains topsoil in one of the worst such storms of the Dust Bowl.

4aa700c5d14a.title: Dust Bowl
4aa700c5d14a.sentence: The dust clouds blew all the way to Chicago, where they deposited 12 million pounds (5,400 tonnes) of dust.

f2794290bb5f.title: Dust Bowl
f2794290bb5f.sentence: In many regions, more than 75% of the topsoil was blown away by the end of the 1930s.

f95f24a24fb4.title: Dust Bowl
f95f24a24fb4.sentence: Government's greatly expanded participation in land management and soil conservation was an important result of the disaster.

3d8e479b3dbb.title: Dust Bowl
3d8e479b3dbb.sentence: The first recorded dust storm occurred on September 14, 1930.

fccdc9aecf1d.title: Dust Bowl
fccdc9aecf1d.sentence: On April 14, 1935, known as "Black Sunday", the day started out clear and warm, with temperatures in the 80s and the air completely still, causing many people to let down their guard.

8cae526643d5.title: Dust Bowl
8cae526643d5.sentence: Associated Press reporter Robert E. Geiger happened to be in Boise City, Oklahoma, to witness the "Black Sunday" black blizzards of April 14, 1935; Edward Stanley, the Kansas City news editor of the Associated Press, coined the term "Dust Bowl" while rewriting Geiger's news story.

c38ecc3c9795.title: Dust Bowl
c38ecc3c9795.sentence: During President Franklin D. Roosevelt's first 100 days in office in 1933, his administration quickly initiated programs to conserve soil and restore the region's ecological balance.

f1278b635063.title: Dust Bowl
f1278b635063.sentence: Interior Secretary Harold L. Ickes established the Soil Erosion Service in August 1933 under Hugh Hammond Bennett.

2da445d82ee0.title: Dust Bowl
2da445d82ee0.sentence: In 1935, it was transferred and reorganized under the Department of Agriculture and renamed the Soil Conservation Service.

d88d4e3fc2f8.title: Dust Bowl
d88d4e3fc2f8.sentence: It is now known as the Natural Resources Conservation Service (NRCS).

17f77c4fbcc2.title: Dust Bowl
17f77c4fbcc2.sentence: Roosevelt ordered the Civilian Conservation Corps to plant the Great Plains Shelterbelt, a huge belt of more than 200 million trees from Canada to Abilene, Texas, to break the wind, hold water in the soil, and hold the soil in place.

4682ef250255.title: Dust Bowl
4682ef250255.sentence: The administration also began to educate farmers on soil conservation and anti-erosion techniques, including crop rotation, strip farming, contour plowing, and terracing.

5f9e91123a41.title: Dust Bowl
5f9e91123a41.sentence: In 1937, the federal government began an aggressive campaign to encourage Dust Bowl farmers to adopt planting and plowing methods that conserved the soil.

857f028e5150.title: Dust Bowl
857f028e5150.sentence: The government paid reluctant farmers a dollar an acre (equivalent to $22 in 2025) to use the new methods.

37cffb8dac5f.title: Dust Bowl
37cffb8dac5f.sentence: By 1938, the massive conservation effort had reduced the amount of blowing soil by 65%.

3f433148ca8a.title: Dust Bowl
3f433148ca8a.sentence: Aside from the short-term economic consequences of erosion, the Dust Bowl had severe long-term economic consequences.

c498a6858972.title: Dust Bowl
c498a6858972.sentence: The abandonment of homesteads and financial ruin resulting from catastrophic topsoil loss led to widespread hunger and poverty.

5711938d3e2a.title: Dust Bowl
5711938d3e2a.sentence: The economy adjusted predominantly through large relative population declines in more-eroded counties, both during the 1930s and through the 1950s.

fe4b66f343bb.title: Dust Bowl
fe4b66f343bb.sentence: By 1940, counties that had experienced the most erosion had a greater decline in agricultural land values.

5b5f93067373.title: Dust Bowl
5b5f93067373.sentence: The per-acre value of farmland declined by 28% in high-erosion counties and 17% in medium-erosion counties, relative to land value changes in low-erosion counties.

e1b40e2e7c3d.title: Dust Bowl
e1b40e2e7c3d.sentence: In highly eroded areas, less than 25% of the original agricultural losses were recovered.

111ad4b3323c.title: Dust Bowl
111ad4b3323c.sentence: Even over the long term, the land's agricultural value often failed to return to pre-Dust Bowl levels.

181e2014f5cf.title: Dust Bowl
181e2014f5cf.sentence: Because the amount of topsoil had been reduced, it would have been more productive to shift from crops and wheat to animals and hay.

bf91c64d2181.title: Dust Bowl
bf91c64d2181.sentence: The economic effects persisted in part because of farmers' failure to switch to more appropriate crops for highly eroded areas.

a6bb39ac0739.title: Dust Bowl
a6bb39ac0739.sentence: Because banks failed in the Dust Bowl region at a higher rate than elsewhere, farmers could not get the credit they needed to obtain capital to shift crop production.

56398019d272.title: Earthflow
56398019d272.sentence: An earthflow (earth flow) is a downslope viscous flow of fine-grained materials that have been saturated with water and moves under the pull of gravity.

c92e3233aea4.title: Earthflow
c92e3233aea4.sentence: It is an intermediate type of mass wasting that is between downhill creep and mudflow.

caca4ab37425.title: Earthflow
caca4ab37425.sentence: Though earthflows are a lot like mudflows, overall they are slower and are covered with solid material carried along by flow from within.

ead6908424cf.title: Earthflow
ead6908424cf.sentence: The types of materials that are susceptible to earthflows are clay, fine sand and silt, and fine-grained pyroclastic material.

7dfe9e11ba1e.title: Earthflow
7dfe9e11ba1e.sentence: When the ground materials become saturated with enough water, they will start flowing (soil liquefaction).

70b79264a03e.title: Earthflow
70b79264a03e.sentence: The velocity of the flow is dictated by water content: the higher the water content is, the higher the velocity will be.

42dbcde802cb.title: Earthflow
42dbcde802cb.sentence: Because of the dependency on water content for the velocity of the flow, it can take minutes or years for the materials to move down the slope.

8db62b90dbb5.title: Earthflow
8db62b90dbb5.sentence: An earthflow may affect as few as several square meters or up to several hectares in either time frame.

c1165699651f.title: Earthflow
c1165699651f.sentence: One of the best mitigation techniques to avoid serious earthflow and landslide damage is properly draining the slope of water, especially in places of high levels of precipitation.

d255ce915690.title: Earthflow
d255ce915690.sentence: - Slopes that have been undercut or loaded with more sediment for human construction

ba1ea56b91cf.title: Earthflow
ba1ea56b91cf.sentence: - Slopes that have been undercut by rivers or stream beds

dd2d45b46191.title: Earthflow
dd2d45b46191.sentence: - Hill slopes made up of clay, silt, or other fine-grained materials

5509a7f7f498.title: Denudation
5509a7f7f498.sentence: Denudation is the geological process in which moving water, ice, wind, and waves erode the Earth's surface, leading to a reduction in elevation and in relief of landforms and landscapes.

0b46e0f3f911.title: Denudation
0b46e0f3f911.sentence: Although the terms erosion and denudation are used interchangeably, erosion is the transport of soil and rocks from one location to another, and denudation is the sum of processes, including erosion, that result in the lowering of Earth's surface.

f9df3e1b4fb3.title: Denudation
f9df3e1b4fb3.sentence: Denudation incorporates the mechanical, biological, and chemical processes of erosion, weathering, and mass wasting.

44fea6ba8bbb.title: Denudation
44fea6ba8bbb.sentence: Denudation can involve the removal of both solid particles and dissolved material.

ad05915eec06.title: Denudation
ad05915eec06.sentence: - Anthropogenic (human) activity, including agriculture, damming, mining, and deforestation;

ad244b160f1f.title: Denudation
ad244b160f1f.sentence: - Biosphere, via animals, plants, and microorganisms contributing to chemical and physical weathering;

adb18287fb2b.title: Denudation
adb18287fb2b.sentence: - Climate, most directly through chemical weathering from rain, but also because climate dictates what kind of weathering occurs;

66c6af8bfc20.title: Denudation
66c6af8bfc20.sentence: - Lithology or the type of rock;

78f438b9b632.title: Denudation
78f438b9b632.sentence: - Surface topography and changes to surface topography, such as mass wasting and erosion; and

0e72f683686e.title: Denudation
0e72f683686e.sentence: - Tectonic activity, such as deformation, the changing of rocks due to stress mainly from tectonic forces, and orogeny, the process that forms mountains.

30a9e9165cb6.title: Denudation
30a9e9165cb6.sentence: Endogenous processes such as volcanoes, earthquakes, and tectonic uplift can expose continental crust to the exogenous processes of weathering, erosion, and mass wasting.

0aef2f1adbfe.title: Denudation
0aef2f1adbfe.sentence: Research is also being done to find the relationship between denudation and isostasy; the more denudation occurs, the lighter the crust becomes in an area, which allows for uplift.

1c42103db4f1.title: Denudation
1c42103db4f1.sentence: Denudation rates are usually much lower than the rates of uplift and average orogeny rates can be eight times the maximum average denudation.

c3d5deed2dc4.title: Denudation
c3d5deed2dc4.sentence: Hutton and Playfair suggested over a period of time, a landscape would eventually be worn down to erosional planes at or near sea level, which gave the theory the name "planation".

f5b24ca2da21.title: Denudation
f5b24ca2da21.sentence: Peneplanation was a cycle in which young landscapes are produced by uplift and denuded down to sea level, which is the base level.

1bf734108dd5.title: Denudation
1bf734108dd5.sentence: The final blow to peneplanation came in 1964 when a team led by Luna Leopold published Fluvial Processes in Geomorphology, which links landforms with measurable precipitation-infiltration runoff processes and concluded no peneplains exist over large areas in modern times, and any historical peneplains would have to be proven to exist, rather than inferred from modern geology.

8db3e057576f.title: Denudation
8db3e057576f.sentence: In 1785, Scottish physician James Hutton proposed an Earth history based on observable processes over an unlimited amount of time, which marked a shift from assumptions based on faith to reasoning based on logic and observation.

4e573150ab94.title: Sedimentation
4e573150ab94.sentence: Sedimentation is the deposition of sediments.

225a8490d77f.title: Sedimentation
225a8490d77f.sentence: It takes place when particles in suspension settle out of the fluid in which they are entrained and come to rest against a barrier.

3a1f5fc010ae.title: Sedimentation
3a1f5fc010ae.sentence: Settling is the falling of suspended particles through the liquid, whereas sedimentation is the final result of the settling process.

fe4a22dae770.title: Sedimentation
fe4a22dae770.sentence: - Type 1 sedimentation is characterized by particles that settle discretely at a constant settling velocity, or by the deposition of Iron-Rich minerals to streamlines down to the point source.

3ca7bf9896a0.title: Sedimentation
3ca7bf9896a0.sentence: They settle as individual particles and do not flocculate (stick to each other) during settling.

33c596bdb6f9.title: Sedimentation
33c596bdb6f9.sentence: - Type 2 sedimentation is characterized by particles that flocculate during sedimentation and because of this their size is constantly changing and therefore their settling velocity is changing.

ba224dd767e5.title: Sedimentation
ba224dd767e5.sentence: In this process the particles are at a high concentration (greater than 1000 mg/L) such that the particles tend to settle as a mass and a distinct clear zone and sludge zone are present.

95800eccb445.title: Sedimentation
95800eccb445.sentence: Rates of sedimentation vary from less than 3 millimeters (0.12 in) per thousand years for pelagic sediment to several meters per thousand years in portions of major river deltas.

13594f2d2bdd.title: Sedimentation
13594f2d2bdd.sentence: Sedimentation enhancing strategies are environmental management projects aiming to restore and facilitate land-building processes in deltas.

8253119b9005.title: Sedimentation
8253119b9005.sentence: Sediment availability and deposition are important because deltas naturally subside and therefore need sediment accumulation to maintain their elevation, particularly considering increasing rates of sea-level rise.

106e93ab9458.title: Sedimentation
106e93ab9458.sentence: Sedimentation enhancing strategies aim to increase sedimentation on the delta plain primarily by restoring the exchange of water and sediments between rivers and low-lying delta plains.

ec1817a3b85d.title: Siltation
ec1817a3b85d.sentence: Siltation is water pollution caused by particulate terrestrial clastic material, with a particle size dominated by silt or clay.

b4553a48bdd7.title: Siltation
b4553a48bdd7.sentence: It refers both to the increased concentration of suspended sediments and to the increased accumulation (temporary or permanent) of fine sediments on bottoms where they are undesirable.

a5bf457ecfaf.title: Siltation
a5bf457ecfaf.sentence: Siltation is most often caused by soil erosion or sediment spill.

75770640afb2.title: Siltation
75770640afb2.sentence: In water, the main pollution source is sediment spill from dredging, the transportation of dredged material on barges, and the deposition of dredged material in or near water.

ba063ce5299f.title: Siltation
ba063ce5299f.sentence: In rural areas, the erosion source is typically soil degradation by intensive or inadequate agricultural practices, leading to soil erosion, especially in fine-grained soils such as loess.

02cf947090ed.title: Siltation
02cf947090ed.sentence: In urban areas, the erosion source is typically construction activities, which involve clearing the original land-covering vegetation and temporarily creating something akin to an urban desert from which fines are easily washed out during rainstorms.

aeae83b84ba8.title: Siltation
aeae83b84ba8.sentence: Source measurements of erosion may be very difficult since the lost material may be a fraction of a millimeter per year.

23c489e5a216.title: Siltation
23c489e5a216.sentence: Therefore, the approach taken is typically to measure the sediment in transport in the stream, by measuring the sediment concentration and multiplying that with the discharge; for example, 50 mg/L (1.8×10^−6 lb/cu in) times 30 m3/s (1,100 cu ft/s) gives 1.5 kg/s (200 lb/min).

5e3bd7b3ec5e.title: Siltation
5e3bd7b3ec5e.sentence: The suspended sediment may interfere with the food gathering of filtering organisms, and the sediment accumulation on the bottom may bury organisms to the point that they starve or even die.

5cb198f21291.title: Siltation
5cb198f21291.sentence: An accumulation of as little as 1 mm (0.039 in) may kill coral polyps.

2ace16707e8d.title: Siltation
2ace16707e8d.sentence: Generally speaking, hard bottom communities and mussel banks (including oysters) are more sensitive to siltation than sand and mud bottoms.

4340c0a395f1.title: Siltation
4340c0a395f1.sentence: In rural areas, the first line of defense is to maintain land cover and prevent soil erosion in the first place.

caeb572990fd.title: Siltation
caeb572990fd.sentence: The second line of defense is to trap the material before it reaches the stream network (known as sediment control).

78bd8d303c89.title: Siltation
78bd8d303c89.sentence: In urban areas, the defenses are to keep land uncovered for as short a time as possible during construction and to use silt screens to prevent the sediment from getting released in water bodies.

36e52380f63f.title: Siltation
36e52380f63f.sentence: Siltation can also affect navigation channels or irrigation channels.

fca3d1a088f1.title: Siltation
fca3d1a088f1.sentence: Once sedimentation has occurred, in irrigation or navigation channels, dredging is often the only remedy.

7d2cdf8cc2d2.title: River bank failure
7d2cdf8cc2d2.sentence: A river bank failure is a sudden mass wasting off the bank of a stream, which can be caused when the gravitational forces acting on the bankside rocks and soils exceed the adhesive and cohesive forces that hold them together.

64201275af6a.title: River bank failure
64201275af6a.sentence: All rivers and creeks experience bank erosion due to constant friction, shearing and solvation between the water current and the pedosphere contacting the streamflow, but a catastrophic failure of the bankside is dependent on the location, the surrounding conditions and the rate at which such erosion is occurring.

af7bf404f820.title: River bank failure
af7bf404f820.sentence: Bank erosion is accelerated by higher discharge (e.g. due to floods) which increases both the flow rate and the water level (which increases the contact area between water and soil); by helicoidal flow upon the outside of a riverbend (which corrade it into a steep or concave cut bank); and by downcutting of riparian surface runoff rills/gullies (which fragmentate the bankside into mechanically separate segments), all of which compromise the overall structural integrity of the bank over time.

e4de3479a387.title: River bank failure
e4de3479a387.sentence: River bank failures can also be catalyzed by additional weight upon the bank (e.g. landslides towards the bank, parking of vehicles, or even just people standing at the edge), downpours and soil saturation (which destabilizes the soil), undermining of the bankside by groundwater flow, burrows and artificial boring/piling, vegetation changes (which alters the anti-erosion properties of the rhizosphere) and sudden, repeated shocks (e.g. earthquakes) and/or tectonic activity.

bee9c990e37b.title: River bank failure
bee9c990e37b.sentence: Adding to these stresses can be increased saturation caused by irrigation and septics, which reduce the soil's strength.

ca374fa66e48.title: River bank failure
ca374fa66e48.sentence: While deep rooted vegetation can increase the strength of river banks, replacement with grass and shallower rooted vegetation can actually weaken the soil.

e22843771dbf.title: River bank failure
e22843771dbf.sentence: The toe zone is the area which is most susceptible to erosion.

635816ebe365.title: River bank failure
635816ebe365.sentence: Because it is located in between the ordinary water level and the low water level, it is strongly affected by currents and erosional events.

557eb3eff340.title: River bank failure
557eb3eff340.sentence: The most common type of bank is a stratified or interstratified bank, which consists of cohesionless layers interbedded with cohesive layers.

2b1ec5946c3f.title: River bank failure
2b1ec5946c3f.section: Modes of failure > Hydraulically induced failure
2b1ec5946c3f.sentence: Hydraulic processes at or below the surface of the water may entrain sediment and directly cause erosion.

49b2c6d6fd7c.title: River bank failure
49b2c6d6fd7c.sentence: Geotechnical failure usually occurs due to stresses on the bank exceeding the forces the bank can accommodate.

e8302c6a466d.title: River bank failure
e8302c6a466d.sentence: Changes in the valley floor slope can influence alluvial rivers, which can happen due to tectonics.

e5fc5a49d8b2.title: River bank failure
e5fc5a49d8b2.sentence: Gravitational failure includes shallow and rotational slides, slab and cantilever failures, and earthflows and dry granular flows.

666b2f6cbb78.title: River bank failure
666b2f6cbb78.sentence: Failures in cohesive soils will be in rotational or planar failure surfaces, while in non-cohesive soils failures will be in an avalanche fashion.

50bbffef6536.title: Sediment basin
50bbffef6536.sentence: A sediment basin is a temporary pond built on a construction site to capture eroded or disturbed soil that is washed off during rain storms, and protect the water quality of a nearby stream, river, lake, or bay.

229ee0eeacb6.title: Sediment basin
229ee0eeacb6.sentence: The sediment-laden soil settles in the pond before the runoff is discharged.

767792dd2b18.title: Sediment basin
767792dd2b18.sentence: Sediment basins are typically used on construction sites of 5 acres (20,000 m2) or more, where there is sufficient room.

e3792abadcc2.title: Sediment basin
e3792abadcc2.sentence: On smaller construction sites, where a basin is not practical, sediment traps may be used.

b96a3407f71e.title: Sediment basin
b96a3407f71e.sentence: The trap is basically an embankment built along a waterway or low-lying area on the site.

4e524c8310c4.title: Sediment basin
4e524c8310c4.sentence: They are typically installed at the perimeter of a site and above storm drain inlets, to keep sediment from entering the drainage system.

147fb9691ffa.title: Sediment basin
147fb9691ffa.sentence: On some construction projects, the sediment basin is cleaned out after the soil disturbance (earth-moving) phase of the project, and modified to function as a permanent stormwater management system for the completed site, either as a detention basin or a retention basin.

4c89e14f92f0.title: Mudflow
4c89e14f92f0.sentence: A mudflow, also known as mudslide or mud flow, is a form of mass wasting involving fast-moving flow of debris and dirt that has become liquified by the addition of water.

243b8591c881.title: Mudflow
243b8591c881.sentence: Such flows can move at speeds ranging from three to five metres per second (9.8 to 16.4 ft/s).

633ffdb8f7c8.title: Mudflow
633ffdb8f7c8.sentence: Mudflows contain a significant proportion of clay, which makes them more fluid than debris flows, allowing them to travel farther and across lower slope angles.

3a708b195975.title: Mudflow
3a708b195975.sentence: They are composed of at least 50% silt and clay-sized materials and up to 30% water.

5e9051426058.title: Mudflow
5e9051426058.sentence: Mudflows often start as slides, becoming flows as water is entrained along the flow path; such events are often called mud failures.

3a5473765259.title: Mudflow
3a5473765259.sentence: Heavy rainfall, snowmelt, or high levels of groundwater flowing through cracked bedrock may trigger a movement of soil or sediments in landslides that continue as mudflows.

0bf474391c59.title: Mudflow
0bf474391c59.sentence: The point where a muddy material begins to flow depends on its grain size, the water content, and the slope of the topography.

55907019cfe2.title: Gelifluction
55907019cfe2.sentence: Gelifluction, very similar to solifluction, is the seasonal freeze-thaw action upon waterlogging topsoils which induces downslope movement.

0cc254a8d211.title: Gelifluction
0cc254a8d211.sentence: Gelifluction is prominent in periglacial regions where snow falls during six to eight months of the year.

d252a0719fd1.title: Gelifluction
d252a0719fd1.sentence: In spring, the snow and ice melt, and the landscape is effectively inundated with half a year's worth of rainfall in the space of a couple of days.

26d49965626f.title: Gelifluction
26d49965626f.sentence: The top soil becomes waterlogged, and flows like a liquid.

6c8caf1e29d5.title: Gelifluction
6c8caf1e29d5.sentence: Because the wet soil behaves like a fluid, gelifluction is a form of mass movement that can occur on slopes with a slope angle of less than half a degree.

ace2da1ef8b5.title: Gelifluction
ace2da1ef8b5.sentence: The most distinctive landforms created by gelifluction include gelifluction lobes and gelifluction benches.

30d790cd999f.title: Gelifluction
30d790cd999f.sentence: The former refer to tongue-shaped deposits of geliflucted material orientated downslope that tend to form on slopes of between 10° and 20°, whereas the latter refer to terrace-like deposits forming on gentler slopes with a long axis running parallel to the slope contour.

771f97879595.title: Gelifluction
771f97879595.sentence: A lobe is usually measured in terms of its front (riser) and its length upslope (tread); gelifluction lobes typically have risers of up to 5 metres (16 ft) and treads of up to 50 metres (160 ft).

485350545295.title: Fiber roll
485350545295.sentence: A fiber roll is a temporary erosion control and sediment control device used on construction sites to protect water quality in nearby streams, rivers, lakes and seas from sediment erosion.

f84a365b7be6.title: Fiber roll
f84a365b7be6.sentence: It is made of straw, coconut fiber or similar material formed into a tubular roll.

2b6031da16bd.title: Fiber roll
2b6031da16bd.sentence: Each fiber roll is installed on a horizontal contour level in shallow trenches 2 to 4 inches (5 to 10 cm) deep and fastened to the ground with wooden stakes.

4fa60fee58cb.title: Fiber roll
4fa60fee58cb.sentence: The steeper the slope, the more rows of evenly spaced horizontal contour level fiber rolls are used.

ea04b1ed75ed.title: Fiber roll
ea04b1ed75ed.sentence: Each horizontal contour level row of fiber rolls is installed on slopes, ending with one at the base of the slope, below an active construction area before soil disturbance (earth moving) begins.

a7a10cdfb6f4.title: Fiber roll
a7a10cdfb6f4.sentence: During rain storms, the rolls intercept surface stormwater runoff (but not concentrating or channeling the runoff) and reduce the velocity of flow.

865c6b4373be.title: Fiber roll
865c6b4373be.sentence: Water passes through a fiber roll while leaving behind the sediment on the uphill side of the roll, thereby reducing sediment erosion.

9a98f3fa36ea.title: Fiber roll
9a98f3fa36ea.sentence: Properly installed fiber rolls are effective at trapping sediment, generally more effectively than straw bales.

9c769378276b.title: Fiber roll
9c769378276b.sentence: - Fiber rolls should not be used on very steep land that is prone to mudslides, landslides or creep.

5e326fa0bfb2.title: Fiber roll
5e326fa0bfb2.sentence: - If fiber rolls are not properly staked into the ground, they may be carried away by high flows.

c762ce7b0ef7.title: Sediment control
c762ce7b0ef7.sentence: Treatment of silt impacted water using equipment and chemical addition, commonly called an active treatment system, is a relatively new form of sediment control for the construction industry.

a64f8b66868d.title: Sediment control
a64f8b66868d.sentence: Sediment-laden stormwater is collected and or pumped, and a chemical flocculant is added to aide in clarification.

1ccf6f1e5fb3.title: Sediment control
1ccf6f1e5fb3.sentence: These systems are designed to reduce Total Suspended Solids (TSS) from entering nearby water bodies where silt pollution can be of environmental concern.

d48ce4f052fc.title: Sediment control
d48ce4f052fc.sentence: - Natural Polymers: Derived from natural sources, such as starch, chitosan, and guar gum.

4ed22e40d293.title: Sediment control
4ed22e40d293.sentence: - Synthetic Polymers: These include polyacrylamide and their derivatives, which can be tailored to specific water treatment needs.

777174c07c16.title: Sediment control
777174c07c16.sentence: - Inorganic Flocculants: Aluminum Sulfate (Alum), Ferric Chloride, Ferric Sulfate, Polyaluminum chloride

713cb99a6963.title: Sediment control
713cb99a6963.sentence: The water is then either filtered (sand or cartridge filter,) or settled (lamella clarifier or weir tank) prior to discharge.

4ba6424be19c.title: Sediment control
4ba6424be19c.sentence: Extreme caution should be observed when using cationic flocculants like chitosan or positively charged polyacrylamide or polyDADMAC which cause hypoxia in fish.

30dd3244ec03.title: Sediment control
30dd3244ec03.sentence: The use of anionic, negatively charged, flocculants is best practice on open loop treatment systems to ensure the protection aquatic habitat, fish and invertebrates.

235af3564862.title: Sediment control
235af3564862.sentence: Passive treatment systems use the energy of water flowing by gravity through ditches, canals, culverts or other constructed conveyances to effect treatment.

15ae4ebdbebb.title: Sediment control
15ae4ebdbebb.sentence: Self dosing products, such as Gel Flocculants, are placed in the flowing water where sediment particles, colloids and flow energy combine to release the required dosage, thereby creating heavy flocs which can then be easily filtered or settled.

2df4781a2755.title: Sediment control
2df4781a2755.sentence: Natural woven fibers like jute are often used in ditch bottoms to act as filtration media.

ed25bb60abbb.title: Sediment control
ed25bb60abbb.sentence: Sedimentation ponds are often utilized as a deposition area to clarify the water and concentrate the material.

15828791456f.title: Sediment control
15828791456f.sentence: These types of systems are low carbon as no external power source is needed, they require little skill to operate, minimal maintenance and are effective at reducing Total Suspended Solids, some heavy metals and the nutrient phosphorus.

e12aab4df535.title: Sediment control
e12aab4df535.sentence: Stormwater management facilities (SWMF's) are generally designed Stokes' law to remove particulate matter larger than 40 micron in size, or to detain water to reduce downstream flooding.

d26b622077c4.title: Fluvial sediment processes
d26b622077c4.sentence: In geography and geology, fluvial sediment processes or fluvial sediment transport are associated with rivers and streams and the deposits and landforms created by sediments.

49f047d2953e.title: Fluvial sediment processes
49f047d2953e.sentence: Fluvial sediment processes include the motion of sediment and erosion or deposition on the river bed.

14f465aec156.title: Fluvial sediment processes
14f465aec156.sentence: The movement of water across the stream bed exerts a shear stress directly onto the bed.

e53738773189.title: Fluvial sediment processes
e53738773189.sentence: If the cohesive strength of the substrate is lower than the shear exerted, or the bed is composed of loose sediment which can be mobilized by such stresses, then the bed will be lowered purely by clearwater flow.

a31ee4410656.title: Fluvial sediment processes
a31ee4410656.sentence: In addition, if the river carries significant quantities of sediment, this material can act as tools to enhance wear of the bed (abrasion).

debb0cc26efd.title: Fluvial sediment processes
debb0cc26efd.sentence: At the same time the fragments themselves are ground down, becoming smaller and more rounded (attrition).

a70bdf1bfa47.title: Fluvial sediment processes
a70bdf1bfa47.sentence: Sediment in rivers is transported as either bedload (the coarser fragments which move close to the bed) or suspended load (finer fragments carried in the water).

87e550f5c69c.title: Fluvial sediment processes
87e550f5c69c.sentence: There is also a component carried as dissolved material.

1819e94cc9a0.title: Fluvial sediment processes
1819e94cc9a0.sentence: Where the river flow is fast, more particles are picked up than dropped.

124a42329c50.title: Fluvial sediment processes
124a42329c50.sentence: Where the river flow is slow, more particles are dropped than picked up.

e1dba9b1a201.title: Fluvial sediment processes
e1dba9b1a201.sentence: Areas where more particles are dropped are called alluvial or flood plains, and the dropped particles are called alluvium.

6bf9bb12f56f.title: Fluvial sediment processes
6bf9bb12f56f.sentence: These relationships are shown in the following table for the Rouse number, which is a ratio of sediment settling velocity (fall velocity) to upwards velocity.

56b5a05a2e38.title: Fluvial sediment processes
56b5a05a2e38.sentence: Sediment moved by water can be larger than sediment moved by air because water has both a higher density and viscosity.

735c83f740b7.title: Fluvial sediment processes
735c83f740b7.sentence: In typical rivers the largest carried sediment is of sand and gravel size, but larger floods can carry cobbles and even boulders.

01683427e390.title: Fluvial sediment processes
01683427e390.sentence: It has been estimated that the Mississippi River annually carries 406 million tons of sediment to the sea, the Yellow River 796 million tons, and the Po River in Italy 67 million tons.

b075bec1ec92.title: Fluvial sediment processes
b075bec1ec92.sentence: Sediment motion can create self-organized structures such as ripples, dunes, or antidunes on the river or stream bed.

0b698e97b548.title: Fluvial sediment processes
0b698e97b548.sentence: These bedforms are often preserved in sedimentary rocks and can be used to estimate the direction and magnitude of the flow that deposited the sediment.

f572bf999d96.title: Saltation (geology)
f572bf999d96.sentence: In geology, saltation (from Latin saltus 'leap, jump') is a specific type of particle transport by fluids such as wind or water.

fd4728f80f0b.title: Saltation (geology)
fd4728f80f0b.sentence: It occurs when loose materials are removed from a bed and carried by the fluid, before being transported back to the surface.

2bf896502428.title: Saltation (geology)
2bf896502428.sentence: At low fluid velocities, loose material rolls downstream, staying in contact with the surface.

c73af8406f96.title: Saltation (geology)
c73af8406f96.sentence: This is called creep or reptation.

0ec2cc88cee0.title: Saltation (geology)
0ec2cc88cee0.sentence: Once the wind speed reaches a certain critical value, termed the impact or fluid threshold, the drag and lift forces exerted by the fluid are sufficient to lift some particles from the surface.

ab6a2f9d1e89.title: Saltation (geology)
ab6a2f9d1e89.sentence: These particles are accelerated by the fluid, and pulled downward by gravity, causing them to travel in roughly ballistic trajectories.

61b0e82ac16e.title: Saltation (geology)
61b0e82ac16e.sentence: If a particle has obtained sufficient speed from the acceleration by the fluid, it can eject, or splash, other particles in saltation, which propagates the process.

75f2dc9e98df.title: Saltation (geology)
75f2dc9e98df.sentence: In air, this process of saltation bombardment creates most of the dust in dust storms.

c15db74ba715.title: Saltation (geology)
c15db74ba715.sentence: Suspension generally affects small particles ('small' means ~70 micrometres or less for particles in air).

619e166d3b4f.title: Saltation (geology)
619e166d3b4f.sentence: For these particles, vertical drag forces due to turbulent fluctuations in the fluid are similar in magnitude to the weight of the particle.

e5d32cf1598f.title: Saltation (geology)
e5d32cf1598f.sentence: Examples include pebble transport by rivers, sand drift over desert surfaces, soil blowing over fields, and snow drift over smooth surfaces such as those in the Arctic or Canadian Prairies.

e5e03dd19306.title: Saltation (geology)
e5e03dd19306.sentence: A fence designed with holes can mitigate saltation by reducing particle speed, and sand accumulates on the leeward side of the fence.

2b10ff266457.title: Hole erosion test
2b10ff266457.sentence: The hole erosion test (HET) is a method used in geotechnical engineering to quantify the resistance of a soil to erosion, and is specifically relevant to the topic of internal erosion in embankment dams.

77f6cc97300a.title: Hole erosion test
77f6cc97300a.sentence: The standard hole erosion test consists of first compacting the soil sample in a standard mold.

b5e80d80050d.title: Hole erosion test
b5e80d80050d.sentence: Then, a small hole (typically 6 mm) is drilled lengthwise through the soil.

952f3da3fd79.title: Hole erosion test
952f3da3fd79.sentence: As the liquid (typically water) flows through the hole, the soil should erode and the hole will expand.

145348280f60.title: Hole erosion test
145348280f60.sentence: The flow rate should be measured throughout the procedure.

28bed08595ba.title: Hole erosion test
28bed08595ba.sentence: From the change in diameter of the hole over time, the rate of erosion can thus be plotted against applied hydraulic shear stress and fit to the following equation:

9a5c7487e0ac.title: Hole erosion test
9a5c7487e0ac.sentence: where Er is the rate of erosion over time, kd is the soil erodibility, and τc is the critical shear stress for erosion.

fc9128cd6981.title: Hole erosion test
fc9128cd6981.sentence: In the design and engineering of embankment dams, the critical shear stress provided by this test indicates the maximum shear stress that a fluid (such as water) can apply to a soil before a concentrated leak forms and erosion begins.

444aa6b8407c.title: Hole erosion test
444aa6b8407c.sentence: The numerical measure of soil erodibility can be used to predict how quickly this erosion will progress, and it can be found as an input in various computer simulations for dam failure.

92c29331c913.title: Hole erosion test
92c29331c913.sentence: The modified hole erosion test (HET-P) seeks to rectify these issues with the addition of a pitot-static tube.

2c5d09b3b1f1.title: Hole erosion test
2c5d09b3b1f1.sentence: This allows for the direct measurement of total hydraulic head, thus accounting for the total energy loss between the upstream and downstream ends of the soil sample.

21eab527563c.title: Hole erosion test
21eab527563c.sentence: The modified hole erosion test results in significantly smaller values for the critical shear stress - this is makes the results of the test more consistent with other tests, such as the Rotating Cylinder Test or the Jet Erosion Test.

1d9db31d7b8e.title: Gully
1d9db31d7b8e.section: Formation and consequences > Prevention of gullies > Stabilising gullies
1d9db31d7b8e.sentence: Stabilizing gullies entails altering water flow to lessen scouring, sediment buildup, and revegetation.

d1896d3d0fba.title: Gully
d1896d3d0fba.section: Formation and consequences > Prevention of gullies
d1896d3d0fba.sentence: Effective land management techniques can prevent gullies.

be591bbd5cae.title: Gully
be591bbd5cae.section: Formation and consequences > Prevention of gullies
be591bbd5cae.sentence: These techniques include keeping vegetation along drainage lines, using more water, classifying drainage lines as distinct land classes, stabilizing erosion, preventing vermin, distributing runoff evenly, keeping soil organic matter levels high, and avoiding over-cultivation.

925590d0a51b.title: Gully
925590d0a51b.section: Formation and consequences > Prevention of gullies > Stabilising gullies
925590d0a51b.sentence: Water can be securely moved from the natural level to the gully floor using a variety of structures, including drop structures, pipe structures, grass chutes, and rock chutes.

37edee97b577.title: Gully
37edee97b577.section: Formation and consequences > Prevention of gullies > Stabilising gullies
37edee97b577.sentence: Vegetation can reestablish itself thanks to sediments deposited over flatter gradients.

77fe8c8272ed.title: Gully
77fe8c8272ed.section: Formation and consequences > Prevention of gullies > Stabilising gullies
77fe8c8272ed.sentence: Until the restoration is finished, damaged areas should be walled off.

40aab4e9cf8d.title: Gully
40aab4e9cf8d.section: Formation and consequences > Prevention of gullies
40aab4e9cf8d.sentence: Information on gully prevention and control methods is dispersed and often lacking, especially regarding success rates and efficacy.

20243c04fdd6.title: Gully
20243c04fdd6.section: Formation and consequences > Prevention of gullies
20243c04fdd6.sentence: Biophysical environment, terrain, climate, and geomorphology affect runoff, sediment properties and gully stability.

21fdde7e2878.title: Gully
21fdde7e2878.section: Formation and consequences > Prevention of gullies
21fdde7e2878.sentence: These factors can lead to the failure of gully control techniques.

57a37028f2c3.title: Marine clay
57a37028f2c3.sentence: Marine clays are fine-grained sedimentary deposits composed primarily of clay minerals that accumulate in coastal environments.

14573b758f4b.title: Marine clay
14573b758f4b.sentence: They are typically derived from the weathering of continental rocks, transported to an ocean, where they settle and consolidate on the seabed.

ebe162c6cb4d.title: Marine clay
ebe162c6cb4d.sentence: Marine clays commonly contain minerals such as illite, smectite, kaolinite, and chlorite, along with varying amounts of silt, organic matter, and biogenic materials.

0fc02b25eaa5.title: Marine clay
0fc02b25eaa5.sentence: The saline conditions during deposition influence their structure and bonding, often producing high natural water contents, and low permeability.

05aa7c3df74f.title: Marine clay
05aa7c3df74f.sentence: Marine clays exhibit high sensitivity, meaning their internal structure is fragile and can lose much of its strength when disturbed.

f4d5419cd51d.title: Marine clay
f4d5419cd51d.sentence: When clay is deposited in the ocean, the presence of excess ions in seawater causes a loose, open structure of the clay particles to form, a process known as flocculation.

97d9dd1dd11c.title: Marine clay
97d9dd1dd11c.sentence: Once stranded and dried by ancient changing ocean levels, this open framework means that such clay is open to water infiltration.

3133ec9c6b12.title: Marine clay
3133ec9c6b12.sentence: Where marine clay overlies peat, it may mark a marine flooding surface.

fb4a22b890ba.title: Marine clay
fb4a22b890ba.sentence: This transition reflects the landward shift of coastal geography during a phase of relative sea-level rise.

eb6ec3081d5c.title: Vegetation and slope stability
eb6ec3081d5c.sentence: Vegetation and slope stability are interrelated by the ability of the plant life growing on slopes to both promote and hinder the stability of the slope.

1acc0433d684.title: Vegetation and slope stability
1acc0433d684.sentence: The relationship is a complex combination of the type of soil, the rainfall regime, the plant species present, the slope aspect, and the steepness of the slope.

cff15862bd86.title: Vegetation and slope stability
cff15862bd86.sentence: There are four major ways in which vegetation influences slope stability: wind throwing, the removal of water, mass of vegetation (surcharge), and mechanical reinforcement of roots.

2a8412cb4a68.title: Vegetation and slope stability
2a8412cb4a68.sentence: Wind throw is the toppling of a tree due to the force of the wind, this exposes the root plate and adjacent soil beneath the tree and influences slope stability.

f82174709421.title: Vegetation and slope stability
f82174709421.sentence: Wind throw is a factor when considering one tree on a slope; however, it is of lesser importance when considering general slope stability for a body of trees as the wind forces involved represent a smaller percentage of the potential disturbing forces and the trees which are in the centre of the group will be sheltered by those on the outside.

2cbf5353f3ff.title: Vegetation and slope stability
2cbf5353f3ff.sentence: The mass of vegetation is only likely to have an influence on slope stability when larger trees are growing on the slope.

dbac703aa583.title: Vegetation and slope stability
dbac703aa583.sentence: A tree of 30–50m height is likely to have a loading of approximately 100–150 kN/m2.

8cf1b3d1e87f.title: Vegetation and slope stability
8cf1b3d1e87f.sentence: The larger trees should be planted at the toe of the slope with a potential rotational failure as this could increase the factor of safety by 10%.

307b9e041593.title: Vegetation and slope stability
307b9e041593.sentence: However, if the tree is planted at the top of the slope this could reduce the factor of safety by 10%.

025546cd2968.title: Vegetation and slope stability
025546cd2968.sentence: If larger trees are removed from the toe area of a slope there will be both a reduction in soil strength due to the loss of evapotranspiration effects and a reduction in applied loading which may result in temporary suctions in clay soils which could lead to softening as the available water is drawn in to compensate for the suction forces.

4afd557cca1d.title: Vegetation and slope stability
4afd557cca1d.sentence: Knowledge of the underlying slope stability as a function of the soil type, its age, horizon development, compaction, and other impacts is a major underlying aspect of understanding how vegetation can alter the stability of the slope.

33b38bd90032.title: Slope stability
33b38bd90032.sentence: Slope stability analysis is a static or dynamic, analytical or empirical method to evaluate the stability of slopes of soil- and rock-fill dams, embankments, excavated slopes, and natural slopes in soil and rock.

c9a8a7c09e9b.title: Slope stability
c9a8a7c09e9b.sentence: It is performed to assess the safe design of a human-made or natural slopes (e.g. embankments, road cuts, open-pit mining, excavations, landfills etc.) and the equilibrium conditions.

ecc36b4f31ec.title: Slope stability
ecc36b4f31ec.sentence: Successful design of the slope requires geological information and site characteristics, e.g. properties of soil/rock mass, slope geometry, groundwater conditions, alternation of materials by faulting, joint or discontinuity systems, movements and tension in joints, earthquake activity etc.

7a36b48fab9f.title: Slope stability
7a36b48fab9f.sentence: Water pressure acting in the pore spaces, fractures or other discontinuities in the materials that make up the pit slope will reduce the strength of those materials.

1b4d80c7733b.title: Slope stability
1b4d80c7733b.sentence: For example, limit equilibrium is most commonly used and simple solution method, but it can become inadequate if the slope fails by complex mechanisms (e.g. internal deformation and brittle fracture, progressive creep, liquefaction of weaker soil layers, etc.).

539452026487.title: Slope stability
539452026487.sentence: In these cases more sophisticated numerical modelling techniques should be utilised.

90a993448ed6.title: Slope stability
90a993448ed6.sentence: The probability of this happening can be calculated in advance using a simple 2-D circular analysis package.

c3b335d693f8.title: Slope stability
c3b335d693f8.sentence: A primary difficulty with analysis is locating the most-probable slip plane for any given situation.

620347005ee1.title: Slope stability
620347005ee1.sentence: Real-life failures in naturally deposited mixed soils are not necessarily circular but, prior to computers, it was far easier to analyze such a simplified geometry.

ac571d10f17e.title: Slope stability
ac571d10f17e.sentence: Since the stability of the slope can be impacted by external events such as precipitation, an important concern in civil/geotechnical engineering is the stabilization of slopes.

0e17932b2e62.title: Landslide
0e17932b2e62.sentence: Landslide mitigation refers to human construction activities on slopes undertaken with the goal of lessening the effect of landslides.

c7e546a199f6.title: Landslide
c7e546a199f6.sentence: Instead, they are classified by the sort of slope stabilization method used:

14b2b631df1f.title: Landslide
14b2b631df1f.sentence: - Geometric methods, in which the geometry of the hillside is changed (in general the slope);

b9914fa56317.title: Landslide
b9914fa56317.sentence: - Hydrogeological methods, in which an attempt is made to lower the groundwater level or to reduce the water content of the material

b4cb7ff029df.title: Landslide
b4cb7ff029df.sentence: - Chemical and mechanical methods, in which attempts are made to increase the shear strength of the unstable mass or to introduce active external forces (e.g. anchors, rock or ground nailing) or passive (e.g. structural wells, piles or reinforced ground) to counteract the destabilizing forces.

638db9cd98cf.title: Slope stability
638db9cd98cf.sentence: The application of vegetation to increase the slope stability against erosion and landslide is a form of bioengineering that is widely used in areas where the landslide depth is shallow.

f60c8ad908ae.title: Slope stability
f60c8ad908ae.sentence: Vegetation increases the stability of the slope mechanically, by reinforcing the soils through plant roots, which stabilize the upper part of the soil.

76def3da0e98.title: Slope stability
76def3da0e98.sentence: Vegetation also stabilizes the slope via hydrologic processes, by the reduction of soil moisture content through the interception of precipitation and transpiration.

d483d3899c68.title: Slope stability
d483d3899c68.sentence: This results in a drier soil that is less susceptible to mass wasting.

1e9fd7c79702.title: Slope stability
1e9fd7c79702.sentence: - Flattening of slopes results in reduction in weight which makes the slope more stable

7f6c5b44bb6c.title: Slope stability
7f6c5b44bb6c.sentence: - Providing lateral supports by piles or retaining walls

f3587c19888d.title: Slope stability
f3587c19888d.sentence: - Grouting or cement injections into specific zones

83cb18298390.title: Slope stability
83cb18298390.sentence: - Consolidation by surcharging or electro osmosis increases the stability of slope

620a2e77ef2a.title: Slope stability
620a2e77ef2a.sentence: Stability can thus be significantly improved by installing drainage paths to reduce the destabilizing forces.

42a8f4fe1d00.title: Mass wasting
42a8f4fe1d00.sentence: Mass wasting affects geomorphology, most often in subtle, small-scale ways, but occasionally more spectacularly.

8d0fc2b198b0.title: Mass wasting
8d0fc2b198b0.sentence: Solifluction produces lobed or sheetlike deposits, with fairly definite edges, in which clasts (rock fragments) are oriented perpendicular to the contours of the deposit.

a2e91e8dab66.title: Mass wasting
a2e91e8dab66.sentence: Rockfall can produce talus slopes at the feet of cliffs.

fd94a96cbfbc.title: Mass wasting
fd94a96cbfbc.sentence: Landslides can produce scarps and step-like small terraces.

216711ec5c46.title: Mass wasting
216711ec5c46.sentence: Debris flow deposits take the form of long, narrow tracks of very poorly sorted material.

84861cc7ba25.title: Mass wasting
84861cc7ba25.sentence: These may have natural levees at the sides of the tracks, and sometimes consist of lenses of rock fragments alternating with lenses of fine-grained earthy material.

edc5596f469f.title: Mass wasting
edc5596f469f.sentence: Debris flows often form much of the upper slopes of alluvial fans.

78ad8cf8333a.title: Baer–Babinet law
78ad8cf8333a.sentence: In geography, the Baer–Babinet law, sometimes called Baer's law, identifies a way in which the process of formation of rivers is influenced by the rotation of the Earth.

6fa13cd95bd9.title: Baer–Babinet law
6fa13cd95bd9.sentence: According to the hypothesis, because of the rotation of the Earth, erosion occurs mostly on the right banks of rivers in the Northern Hemisphere, and in the Southern Hemisphere on the left banks.

40a1c62b1837.title: Baer–Babinet law
40a1c62b1837.sentence: The concept was originally introduced by French physicist Jacques Babinet in 1859 using mathematical deduction and Coriolis force.

8e2fd295a670.title: Baer–Babinet law
8e2fd295a670.sentence: A more definitive explanation was given by Baltic German scientist Karl Ernst von Baer in 1860.

f708f491d039.title: Baer–Babinet law
f708f491d039.sentence: Although it is possible that an aggregate measurement of all rivers would lead to a correlation with the Baer–Babinet law, the Coriolis force is orders of magnitude weaker than the local forces on the river channel from its flow.

715f814fb1a2.title: Baer–Babinet law
715f814fb1a2.sentence: Therefore, this is unlikely to be important in any given river.

23c2c441a83a.title: Baer–Babinet law
23c2c441a83a.sentence: Albert Einstein wrote a paper in 1926 explaining the true causes of the phenomenon (see tea leaf paradox).

b5ca9ee1a621.title: Soil sloughing
b5ca9ee1a621.sentence: Sloughing is a relatively shallow phenomenon involving the uppermost layers of the soil.

abd586180b38.title: Soil sloughing
abd586180b38.sentence: Soil sloughs off for the same reasons as landslides in general, with very wet soil being among the leading factors.

6c1a49b2d7ff.title: Soil sloughing
6c1a49b2d7ff.sentence: Unabated soil sloughing can end in massive bank or slope failure.

707d0cd30a6e.title: Soil sloughing
707d0cd30a6e.sentence: Increasing water content would lead to a weaker shear strength, which in turn decreases the cohesion, leading to soil sloughing.

04d39d57e9ec.title: Soil sloughing
04d39d57e9ec.section: Impact on soil quality > Soil Water
04d39d57e9ec.sentence: Active pore water pressure can reduce the shear strength by up to 60% and lower cohesion through leaching and eluviation.

8a471d826e23.title: Soil sloughing
8a471d826e23.sentence: Bare soils are more likely to slough than soils with plant cover in part because the roots help hold the surface against gravity.

48c2e43216bc.title: Soil sloughing
48c2e43216bc.sentence: The likelihood of soil sloughing can increase after vegetation is removed along banks and slopes.

3cfa466b9ae1.title: Soil sloughing
3cfa466b9ae1.section: Impact on soil quality > Soil Water
3cfa466b9ae1.sentence: The loss of root strength following harvesting decreases the safety factor to a level where a moderate storm with associated pore water pressure rise can result in slope failure, despite increased root reinforcement thereafter.

04c0ddf6fabf.title: Fluvio-thermal erosion
04c0ddf6fabf.sentence: In geomorphology fluvio-thermal erosion is the combined mechanical and thermal erosion of an unfrozen river or stream against ice-rich soils and sediments.

8ead3f4dae5e.title: Fluvio-thermal erosion
8ead3f4dae5e.sentence: The erosional process includes the thawing of ice sediments by a strong water flow and once the surface is unfrozen, mechanical erosion occurs only if hydraulic forces are powerful enough to incise the riverbank material.

9103c84f661e.title: Fluvio-thermal erosion
9103c84f661e.sentence: This kind of erosion sometimes causes the banks to collapse into the river, and when this occurs collapses are commonly controlled by ice wedges.

ada902d8c1f2.title: Fluvio-thermal erosion
ada902d8c1f2.sentence: Melting of the ice within a porous material reduces the strength of the material, rendering it easily breakable and removable.

d54f77cab722.title: Fluvio-thermal erosion
d54f77cab722.sentence: During the winter when water level is low, a thick sheet of ice forms on top of the Lena River, that is sometimes as much as 2 m thick.

7960e866d971.title: Fluvio-thermal erosion
7960e866d971.sentence: Over the course of just a few days in May or June, water discharge can increase by 10x its velocity.

5988aa3f8f44.title: Fluvio-thermal erosion
5988aa3f8f44.sentence: For the Lena, the banks are observed to retreat approximately 40 m per year.

8dfaff9b6e08.title: Fluvio-thermal erosion
8dfaff9b6e08.sentence: Based on lab models carried out in a cold room, high water temperature, ice temperature, and discharge are shown to be the main contributors of thermal erosion, whereas high ice content in the soil is shown to slow down the thermal erosion process.

cb2bba10f3b6.title: Time-domain reflectometer
cb2bba10f3b6.sentence: Time domain reflectometry has also been utilized to monitor slope movement in a variety of geotechnical settings, including highway cuts, rail beds, and open pit mines (Dowding & O'Connor, 1984, 2000a, 2000b; Kane & Beck, 1999).

e9d64646fa77.title: Time-domain reflectometer
e9d64646fa77.sentence: In TDR stability monitoring applications, a coaxial cable is installed in a vertical borehole passing through the region of concern.

2ca93bf5350a.title: Time-domain reflectometer
2ca93bf5350a.sentence: The electrical impedance at any point along a coaxial cable changes with deformation of the insulator between the conductors.

324439f19da4.title: Time-domain reflectometer
324439f19da4.sentence: A brittle grout surrounds the cable to translate earth movement into an abrupt cable deformation that shows up as a detectable peak in the reflectance trace.

24951771bc97.title: Time-domain reflectometer
24951771bc97.sentence: Until recently, the technique was relatively insensitive to small slope movements and could not be automated because it relied on human detection of changes in the reflectance trace over time.

1d74608fed5e.title: Time-domain reflectometer
1d74608fed5e.sentence: Farrington and Sargand (2004) developed a simple signal processing technique using numerical derivatives to extract reliable indications of slope movement from the TDR data much earlier than by conventional interpretation.

fc3c28e59937.title: Time-domain reflectometer
fc3c28e59937.sentence: Another application of TDRs in geotechnical engineering is to determine the soil moisture content.

a48e0414f1ae.title: Time-domain reflectometer
a48e0414f1ae.sentence: This is a good method to assess the effectiveness of Best Management Practices (BMPs) in reducing stormwater surface runoff.

bc3d163bacb2.title: Suspended load
bc3d163bacb2.sentence: The suspended load of a flow of fluid, such as a river, is the portion of its sediment uplifted by the fluid's flow in the process of sediment transportation.

d41da7272eea.title: Suspended load
d41da7272eea.sentence: It is kept suspended by the fluid's turbulence.

03b9e862d4de.title: Suspended load
03b9e862d4de.sentence: Suspended load generally consists of fine sand, silt and clay size particles although larger particles (coarser sands) may be carried in the lower water column in more intense flows.

626ee53b76fc.title: Suspended load
626ee53b76fc.sentence: The suspended load is one of the three layers of the fluvial sediment transportation system.

2086007957d4.title: Suspended load
2086007957d4.sentence: The suspended load is the middle layer that consists of the smaller sediment that's suspended.

278786c1faa2.title: Suspended load
278786c1faa2.sentence: The wash load is uppermost layer which consist of the smallest sediment that can be seen with the naked eye; however, the wash load gets easily mixed with suspended load during transportation due to the very similar process.

ca59a574de84.title: Suspended load
ca59a574de84.sentence: The boundary between bed load and suspended load is not straightforward because whether a particle is in suspension or not depends on the flow velocity – it is easy to imagine a particle moving between bed load, part-suspension and full suspension in a fluid with variable flow.

5098fab3fd9b.title: Suspended load
5098fab3fd9b.sentence: Suspended loads required the Velocity to keep the sediment transporting above the bed.

3ad0999761af.title: Suspended load
3ad0999761af.sentence: With low velocity the sediment will deposit.

57da13e264f8.title: Sediment transport
57da13e264f8.sentence: The sediments entrained in a flow can be transported along the bed as bed load in the form of sliding and rolling grains, or in suspension as suspended load advected by the main flow.

669d56d2598d.title: Sediment transport
669d56d2598d.sentence: Bed load moves by rolling, sliding, and hopping (or saltating) over the bed, and moves at a small fraction of the fluid flow velocity.

1773ec8747d1.title: Sediment transport
1773ec8747d1.sentence: Bed load is generally thought to constitute 5–10% of the total sediment load in a stream, making it less important in terms of mass balance.

80f56c8b77a7.title: Sediment transport
80f56c8b77a7.sentence: Suspended load is carried in the lower to middle parts of the flow, and moves at a large fraction of the mean flow velocity in the stream.

c1e1ccff8169.title: Sediment transport
c1e1ccff8169.sentence: Some sediment materials may also come from the upstream reaches and be carried downstream in the form of wash load.

68c8fb772da7.title: Sediment transport
68c8fb772da7.sentence: Wash load is carried within the water column as part of the flow, and therefore moves with the mean velocity of main stream.

fbccea0d3314.title: Sediment transport
fbccea0d3314.sentence: Wash load concentrations are approximately uniform in the water column.

da71110b1919.title: Sediment transport
da71110b1919.sentence: The location in the flow in which a particle is entrained is determined by the Rouse number, which is determined by the density ρs and diameter d of the sediment particle, and the density ρ and kinematic viscosity ν of the fluid, determine in which part of the flow the sediment particle will be carried.

3a77e47ac132.title: Sediment transport
3a77e47ac132.sentence: Here, the Rouse number is given by P. The term in the numerator is the (downwards) sediment the sediment settling velocity ws, which is discussed below.

81847c405710.title: Sediment transport
81847c405710.sentence: Small particles will have a slower settling velocity than heavier particles, as seen in the figure.

4d70b619e38f.title: Sediment transport
4d70b619e38f.sentence: This has implications for many aspects of sediment transport, for example, how far downstream a particle might be advected in a river.

d7c151a765df.title: Sediment transport
d7c151a765df.sentence: Generally, for small particles (laminar approximation), it can be calculated with Stokes' Law.

39bd8e349556.title: Sediment transport
39bd8e349556.sentence: In 1935, Filip Hjulström created the Hjulström curve, a graph which shows the relationship between the size of sediment and the velocity required to erode (lift it), transport it, or deposit it.

f94aac7cc5e8.title: Sediment transport
f94aac7cc5e8.sentence: Åke Sundborg later modified the Hjulström curve to show separate curves for the movement threshold corresponding to several water depths, as is necessary if the flow velocity rather than the boundary shear stress (as in the Shields diagram) is used for the flow strength.

dbe342066f83.title: Sediment transport
dbe342066f83.sentence: This curve has no more than a historical value nowadays, although its simplicity is still attractive.

1e92a3c92376.title: Sediment transport
1e92a3c92376.sentence: Among the drawbacks of this curve are that it does not take the water depth into account and more importantly, that it does not show that sedimentation is caused by flow velocity deceleration and erosion is caused by flow acceleration.

e0382fad22b4.title: Sediment transport
e0382fad22b4.sentence: The dimensionless Shields diagram is now unanimously accepted for initiation of sediment motion in rivers.

d09ed495be09.title: Sediment transport
d09ed495be09.section: Initiation of motion > Critical shear stress
d09ed495be09.sentence: The Shields diagram empirically shows how the dimensionless critical shear stress (i.e. the dimensionless shear stress required for the initiation of motion) is a function of a particular form of the particle Reynolds number, Rep or Reynolds number related to the particle.

b50fbebd0796.title: Stream power
b50fbebd0796.sentence: Stream power, originally derived by R. A. Bagnold in the 1960s, is the amount of energy the water in a river or stream is exerting on the sides and bottom of the river.

d2fa3c2c9a21.title: Stream power
d2fa3c2c9a21.sentence: Stream power is the result of multiplying the density of the water, the acceleration of the water due to gravity, the volume of water flowing through the river, and the slope of that water.

50f55843fb09.title: Stream power
50f55843fb09.sentence: where Ω is the stream power, ρ is the density of water (1000 kg/m3), g is acceleration due to gravity (9.8 m/s2), Q is discharge (m3/s), and S is the channel slope.

5818d3739825.title: Stream power
5818d3739825.sentence: Stream power is the rate of energy dissipation against the bed and banks of a river or stream per unit downstream length.

38d3e6929bdc.title: Stream power
38d3e6929bdc.section: Various Forms > Unit (or Specific) Stream power
38d3e6929bdc.sentence: Unit stream power is stream power per unit channel width, and is given by the equation:

0ef76e9b5506.title: Stream power
0ef76e9b5506.section: Various Forms > Unit (or Specific) Stream power
0ef76e9b5506.sentence: Normalizing the stream power by the width of the river allows for a better comparison between rivers of various widths.

8ad4dc89757a.title: Stream power
8ad4dc89757a.section: Various Forms > Unit (or Specific) Stream power
8ad4dc89757a.sentence: This also provides a better estimation of the sediment carrying capacity of the river as wide rivers with high stream power are exerting less force per surface area than a narrow river with the same stream power, as they are losing the same amount of energy but in the narrow river it is concentrated into a smaller area.

45d1aa829157.title: Stream power
45d1aa829157.section: Various Forms > Critical Unit Stream Power
45d1aa829157.sentence: Critical unit stream power is the amount of stream power needed to displace a grain of a specific size, it is given by the equation:

1e04d31889a9.title: Stream power
1e04d31889a9.section: Relationships to other variables > Size of displaced sediment
1e04d31889a9.sentence: Critical stream power can be used to determine the stream competency of a river, which is a measure to determine the largest grain size that will be moved by a river.

a7b004b014de.title: Stream power
a7b004b014de.section: Applications > Landscape evolution > Sensitivity to erosion
a7b004b014de.sentence: Stream power has also been used as a criterion to determine whether a river is in a state of reshaping itself or whether it is stable.

7a95a2ae3348.title: Stream power
7a95a2ae3348.section: Applications > Landscape evolution > Sensitivity to erosion
7a95a2ae3348.sentence: A value of unit stream power between 30 and 35 W m−2 in which this transition occurs has been found by multiple studies.

1fe666b55dad.title: Stream power
1fe666b55dad.sentence: Stream power is used extensively in models of landscape evolution and river incision.

3a966b0f7eee.title: Stream power
3a966b0f7eee.sentence: Stream power can also be used to guide culvert and bridge design in order to maintain healthy stream morphology in which fish are able to continuing traversing the water course and no erosion processes are initiated.

193076bea9b5.title: Fech fech
193076bea9b5.sentence: Fech fech (Arabic: فش فش) is a very fine powder caused by the erosion of clay-limestone terrain and it is most commonly found in deserts.

6a138fdf81f8.title: Fech fech
6a138fdf81f8.sentence: It consists of a surface horizon of pulverized soil with low particle cohesion protected under a thin crust.

0774b7d2bdc4.title: Fech fech
0774b7d2bdc4.sentence: Fech fech is derived from ancient lake muds or on certain argillaceous rocks and is one of the desert surfaces that produces dust.

94606271c352.title: Fech fech
94606271c352.sentence: It is not determinable from the surface and can therefore pose a significant transportation hazard acting as a surprise "trap" as the ground collapses beneath a vehicle, miring it in a quicksand-like substance.

94e8a4b19f32.title: Fech fech
94e8a4b19f32.sentence: Fech fech is common in the Qattara Depression in Egypt, making that portion of the Sahara Desert impassable by most vehicles.

8dee8a37764c.title: Bank erosion
8dee8a37764c.sentence: Bank erosion is the wearing away of the banks of a stream or river.

b80c91ec700f.title: Bank erosion
b80c91ec700f.sentence: This is distinguished from erosion of the bed of the watercourse, which is referred to as scour.

6adf58ca188b.title: Bank erosion
6adf58ca188b.sentence: There are two primary mechanisms of stream bank erosion: fluvial erosion and mass failure.

d7f1e132eb90.title: Bank erosion
d7f1e132eb90.sentence: Fluvial erosion is the direct removal of soil particles by flowing water.

f1413ddc5deb.title: Bank erosion
f1413ddc5deb.sentence: Mass failure occurs when the weight of a stream bank is greater than the strength of the soil, causing the bank to collapse.

28956bd138da.title: Bank erosion
28956bd138da.sentence: These two erosion processes are linked as fluvial erosion of the bottom of the bank creates a steeper bank angle or overhanging soil blocks which are more unstable and likely to collapse.

ede419f479a6.title: Bank erosion
ede419f479a6.sentence: This occurs when groundwater flows out of a stream bank with enough force to erode the bank material.

53b9ba1df41d.title: Bank erosion
53b9ba1df41d.sentence: If concentrated, seepage erosion can be called piping because a “pipe” of soil is eroded.

97e9a8ae6354.title: Bank erosion
97e9a8ae6354.sentence: Generally, banks with vegetation erode more slowly than those without.

0c3966f6abe5.title: Bank erosion
0c3966f6abe5.sentence: Roots generally increase the strength of bank material, making a bank less prone to mass failure.

ea11802f6520.title: Bank erosion
ea11802f6520.sentence: However, trees can also add significant weight to the tops of stream banks and may actually decrease stability.

c20206d1a3f7.title: Bank erosion
c20206d1a3f7.sentence: A direct method is to insert metal rods (called "erosion pins") into the bank and marking the position of the bank surface along the rods at different times.

cc068f2de9db.title: Bank erosion
cc068f2de9db.sentence: Another common method is to survey a stream cross section repeatedly over time.

2af727ffa478.title: Bank erosion
2af727ffa478.sentence: Aerial and satellite imagery can be used to measure rates of bank erosion and river channel migration at larger spatial scales by comparing bank locations at various times.

b0346ab752e6.title: Desert pavement
b0346ab752e6.sentence: A desert pavement, also called reg (in western Sahara), serir (in eastern Sahara), gibber (in Australia), hamada (western Sahara and Middle East), or saï (in central Asia) is a desert surface covered with closely packed, interlocking angular or rounded rock fragments of pebble and cobble size.

83742ce10601.title: Desert pavement
83742ce10601.sentence: A common hypothesis suggests that they form through the gradual removal of sand, dust and other fine-grained material by the wind and intermittent rain, leaving the larger fragments behind.

9d2e351ee9bd.title: Desert pavement
9d2e351ee9bd.sentence: The removal of small particles by wind does not continue indefinitely, because once the pavement forms, it acts as a barrier to resist further erosion.

0b59691c507d.title: Desert pavement
0b59691c507d.sentence: The small particles collect underneath the pavement surface, forming a vesicular A soil horizon (designated "Av").

e9f130741dad.title: Desert pavement
e9f130741dad.sentence: A newer hypothesis suggests that desert pavements form through deposition of windblown dust atop preexisting rocks.

4017791491b4.title: Desert pavement
4017791491b4.sentence: The dust then settles beneath the rocks, forming a layer of soil, while the rocks at the top crack and begin to merge into desert pavement.

2aba7c8e05b1.title: Desert pavement
2aba7c8e05b1.sentence: In 1995, researchers conducted a study in the Mojave Desert using helium-3 dating where they determined the rocks to be of older age than the soil beneath, leading to the conclusion of "stone pavements [being] born at the surface."

8f3f3b1d8736.title: Desert pavement
8f3f3b1d8736.sentence: The presence of desert pavement typically is used as an indicator for the aridity of an area and the relative age of geomorphic surfaces.

b083c2bea199.title: Desert pavement
b083c2bea199.sentence: Studies look at pavements on alluvial surfaces and show that older surfaces have more developed pavements with small, angular rocks that are well sorted and tightly packed together.

674f52f6d963.title: Shear strength (discontinuity)
674f52f6d963.sentence: The shear strength of a discontinuity in a soil or rock mass may have a strong impact on the mechanical behavior of a soil or rock mass.

332e395bc019.title: Shear strength (discontinuity)
332e395bc019.sentence: The shear strength of a discontinuity is often considerably lower than the shear strength of the blocks of intact material in between the discontinuities, and therefore influences, for example, tunnel, foundation, or slope engineering, but also the stability of natural slopes.

0a31f125aae6.title: Shear strength (discontinuity)
0a31f125aae6.sentence: Many slopes, natural and man-made, fail due to a low shear strength of discontinuities in the soil or rock mass in the slope.

226344ce51e4.title: Shear strength (discontinuity)
226344ce51e4.sentence: The shear strength along a discontinuity in a soil or rock mass in geotechnical engineering is governed by the persistence of the discontinuity, roughness of discontinuity surfaces, infill material in the discontinuity, presence and pressure of gasses and fluids (e.g. water, oil), and possible solution (e.g. karst) and cementation along the discontinuity.

e6af2b80d778.title: Shear strength (discontinuity)
e6af2b80d778.sentence: Further the shear strength is dependent on whether the discontinuity has moved before in the geological history (i.e. are the asperities on opposing walls of the discontinuity fitting or non-fitting, or have the asperities been sheared off).

998ad34a3556.title: Shear strength (discontinuity)
998ad34a3556.sentence: For example, the modulus of deformation is reduced, and the deformation becomes plastic (i.e. non-reversible deformation on reduction of stress) rather than elastic (i.e. reversible deformation).

22fca8fbd9bc.title: Shear strength (discontinuity)
22fca8fbd9bc.sentence: This may cause, for example, larger settlement of foundations, which is also permanent even if the load is only temporary.

12da3f8db186.title: Shear strength (discontinuity)
12da3f8db186.sentence: For real discontinuities no analytical calculation method exists.

d8e6f334318a.title: Shear strength (discontinuity)
d8e6f334318a.sentence: Testing on various scales in the laboratory or in the field, or empirical calculations based on characterizing the discontinuity are used to establish the shear strength.

bebf057ce196.title: Shear strength (discontinuity)
bebf057ce196.sentence: - Direct shear test or (Golder) shearbox test

e86f2226c663.title: Quick clay
e86f2226c663.sentence: All of the ground-up rock was deposited in the surrounding ocean, which had penetrated significantly inland.

0923ad712e84.title: Quick clay
0923ad712e84.sentence: When the glaciers retreated, the land mass rose (post-glacial rebound), the clay was exposed, and formed the soil mass for new vegetation.

9e9562cf7398.title: Quick clay
9e9562cf7398.sentence: The final result was that the ionic 'glue' of the clay was weakened, to give a weak, loose soil skeleton, enclosing significant amounts of water (high sensitivity with high moisture content).

64c4a43ea1bd.title: Quick clay
64c4a43ea1bd.sentence: At the height of the past glaciation (about 20,000 years ago), the land was 'pushed' down by the weight of the ice (isostatic depression).

b4f16943da7e.title: Quick clay
b4f16943da7e.sentence: The loose deposition of the silt and clay particles in the marine environment, allowed an unusual flocculation to take place.

5eca71ed03f1.title: Quick clay
5eca71ed03f1.sentence: Essentially, this formed a strongly bonded soil skeleton, which was 'glued' by highly mobile sea-salt ions.

54a1fc3d7fd3.title: Quick clay
54a1fc3d7fd3.sentence: The rainwater in these northern countries was quite aggressive to these clays, perhaps because it was softer (containing less calcium), or the higher silt content allowed more rainwater and snowmelt to penetrate.

411121eb5c56.title: Quick clay
411121eb5c56.sentence: Quick clay deposits are rarely located directly at the ground surface, but are typically covered by a normal layer of topsoil.

5aba7ac4b754.title: Quick clay
5aba7ac4b754.sentence: While this topsoil can absorb most normal stresses, such as normal rainfall or a modest earth tremor, a shock that exceeds the capacity of the topsoil layer — such as a larger earthquake, a large mass added near a slope, or an abnormal rainfall which leaves the topsoil fully saturated so that additional water has nowhere to permeate except into the clay — can disturb the clay and initiate the process of liquefaction.

ee1e2a58c0d1.title: Quick clay
ee1e2a58c0d1.sentence: These landslides are retrogressive, meaning they usually start at water, and progress upwards at slow walking speed, although particularly deep quick clay layers on sloped regions may collapse much more rapidly, or in very large chunks that can slide at great speed due to the liquid nature of the disturbed clay.

b44afc84815d.title: Quick clay
b44afc84815d.sentence: They have been known to penetrate kilometers inland, and consume everything in their path.

cb622dbce495.title: Quick clay
cb622dbce495.sentence: Because the clay layer is typically covered with topsoil, a location which is vulnerable to a quick clay landslide is usually identifiable only by soil testing, and is rarely obvious to a casual observer.

2b2ddcbbfa66.title: Quick clay
2b2ddcbbfa66.sentence: Thus human settlements and transportation links have often been built on or near clay deposits, resulting in a number of notable catastrophes:

38939ad3e3a9.title: Quick clay
38939ad3e3a9.sentence: - On 19 May 1893, a landslide in Verdal Municipality, Norway, killed 116 people and destroyed 105 farms.

578359ee460c.title: Quick clay
578359ee460c.sentence: - Another famous flow of quick clay in Rissa Municipality, Norway, in 1978 caused about 33 hectares (82 acres) of farmland to liquefy and flow into the lake Botn over a few hours, with the loss of one life.

9b0c1af7aea2.title: Quick clay
9b0c1af7aea2.sentence: It is not always possible to entirely avoid building on a quick clay site, although modern engineering techniques have found technical precautions which can be taken to mitigate the risk of disaster.

c2bdc227a6b2.title: Quick clay
c2bdc227a6b2.sentence: For example, when Ontario's Highway 416 had to pass through a quick clay deposit near Nepean, lighter fill materials such as polystyrene were used for the road bed, vertical wick drains were inserted along the route and groundwater cutoff walls were built under the highway to limit water infiltration into the clay.

7da63ee6509f.title: Quick clay
7da63ee6509f.sentence: - On 4 May 1971, 31 lives were lost when 40 homes were swallowed in a retrogressive flowslide in Saint-Jean-Vianney, Quebec, resulting in the relocation of the entire town when the government declared the area uninhabitable due to the presence of Leda clay.

f85a838e5eb3.title: Legacy sediment
f85a838e5eb3.sentence: Legacy sediment (LS) refers to depositional bodies of sediment inherited from the increase of human activities since the Neolithic.

9b23a6481763.title: Legacy sediment
9b23a6481763.sentence: These include a broad range of land use and land cover changes, such as agricultural clearance, lumbering and clearance of native vegetation, mining, road building, and urbanization, as well as alterations brought to river systems in the form of dams and other engineering structures meant to control and regulate natural fluvial processes (erosion, deposition, lateral migration, meandering).

2585ae34a496.title: Legacy sediment
2585ae34a496.sentence: > "Legacy Sediment (n.)
