Are sediments that (1) were eroded from upland slopes during several centuries of intensive land clearing, agriculture, and milling (in the eastern U.S., this occurred from the late 17th to late 19th Centuries); (2) collected along stream corridors and valley bottoms, burying pre-settlement streams, floodplains, wetlands, and dry valleys; and that altered the hydrologic, biologic, aquatic, riparian, and chemical functions of pre-settlement streams and floodplains; (3) accumulated behind ubiquitous low-head mill dams in slackwater environments, resulting in thick accumulations of fine-grained sediment, which distinguishes legacy sediment from fluvial deposits associated with meandering streams; (4) can also accumulate as coarser grained, more poorly sorted colluvial (not associated with stream transport) deposits, usually at valley margins; (5) can contain varying amounts of total phosphorus and nitrogen, which contribute to nutrient loads in downstream waterways from bank erosion processes..."

d3f5f895a0ce.title: Legacy sediment
d3f5f895a0ce.sentence: For example, even though accelerated anthropogenic soil erosion has increased sediment transport of rivers across the globe by 2.3 (± 0.6) billion metric tons per year, sediment delivery to the world's coasts and oceans has been reduced by 1.4 (± 0.3) billion metric tons per year because of retention within reservoirs.

0d88befafc94.title: Legacy sediment
0d88befafc94.sentence: The most common contaminants that can absorb fine sediment are trace metals, nutrients (e.g. nitrogen, phosphorus), polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), pathogens, polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs), pesticides, volatile organic compounds (VOCs).

e7ec1a4e6e9d.title: Legacy sediment
e7ec1a4e6e9d.sentence: Wastewater treatment can remove contaminated sediment within less than a year, but heavy metals and synthetic chemicals may remain within river sediments at toxic standards for decades to centuries.

8847488c919d.title: River bank failure
8847488c919d.sentence: River bank failure is dependent on many solutions, the most common of which are lime stabilization and retaining walls, riprap and sheet piling, maintaining deep vegetation, windrows and trenches, sacks and blocks, gabions and mattresses, soil-cement, and avoiding the construction of structures near the banks of the river.

25585db7de11.title: River bank failure
25585db7de11.sentence: Riprap made of rocks and other materials, arranged in a way as to inhibit erosional processes on a river bank.

4709c9c128b9.title: River bank failure
4709c9c128b9.sentence: This method is expensive and can experience failure, but has the ability to be used for large areas.

9036ec7c9824.title: River bank failure
9036ec7c9824.sentence: Gabions are stacked, rectangular wire boxes filled with stones.

35d513d2d301.title: River bank failure
35d513d2d301.sentence: They are useful on steep slopes when the water is too fast for the use of a riprap technique.

c45da41573e6.title: River bank failure
c45da41573e6.sentence: Trees will provide for deep and dense root systems, increasing the stresses a river bank will accommodate.

e144d0479d3d.title: River bank failure
e144d0479d3d.sentence: Cuttings may be tied together into fascines, and placed into shallow trenches parallel to the bank of the river.

db50dfe07b75.title: River bank failure
db50dfe07b75.sentence: Typically, willows and cottonwood poles are the most useful materials, however, fiber products may also be used are then partially buried and staked in place.

0a3031889351.title: River bank failure
0a3031889351.sentence: The structures hold the soil in place and protect the stream bank from erosion.

0f870031684b.title: River bank failure
0f870031684b.sentence: The use of vegetation to counteract erosional processes is the most labor-intensive method to employ, while also the least expensive.

60d0f2260856.title: River bank failure
60d0f2260856.sentence: On steep banks, however, trees may not be able to stabilize the toe of the bank, and the weight of the tree itself may lead to failure.

0600fc26d66f.title: Headward erosion
0600fc26d66f.sentence: Headward erosion is erosion at the origin of a stream channel, which causes the origin to move back away from the direction of the stream flow, lengthening the stream channel.

007e485267d0.title: Headward erosion
007e485267d0.sentence: Headward erosion is a fluvial process of erosion that lengthens a stream, a valley or a gully at its head and also enlarges its drainage basin.

fcf24fdcb534.title: Headward erosion
fcf24fdcb534.sentence: Once a stream has begun to cut back, the erosion is sped up by the steep gradient the water is flowing down.

90f3d84fe754.title: Headward erosion
90f3d84fe754.section: Stream types created by headward erosion
90f3d84fe754.sentence: The water collects in channels where the velocity and erosional power increase, cutting into and extending the heads of gullies.

e950e4391df5.title: Headward erosion
e950e4391df5.sentence: If this continues long enough, it can cause a stream to break through into a neighboring watershed and capture drainage that previously flowed to another stream.

d942149bd892.title: Headward erosion
d942149bd892.sentence: For example, headward erosion by the Shenandoah River, a tributary of the Potomac River in the U.S. state of Virginia, permitted the Shenandoah to capture successively the original upstream segments of Beaverdam Creek, Gap Run and Goose Creek, three smaller tributaries of the Potomac.

1117162c1f14.title: Headward erosion
1117162c1f14.section: Drainage patterns created by headward erosion
1117162c1f14.sentence: Headward erosion creates three major kinds of drainage patterns: dendritic patterns, trellis patterns, and rectangular and angular patterns.

348079514c41.title: Headward erosion
348079514c41.section: Drainage patterns created by headward erosion
348079514c41.sentence: - Dendritic patterns form in homogenous landforms where the underlying bedrock has no structural control over where the water flows.

5e4f5e29d78b.title: Headward erosion
5e4f5e29d78b.section: Drainage patterns created by headward erosion
5e4f5e29d78b.sentence: - Trellis patterns form where the underlying bedrock contains repeating weaker and stronger types of rock.

894458770776.title: Headward erosion
894458770776.section: Drainage patterns created by headward erosion
894458770776.sentence: These usually form in jointed igneous bedrocks, horizontal sedimentary beds with well-developed jointing or intersecting faults.

3c508ec20c26.title: Aggradation
3c508ec20c26.sentence: Aggradation (or alluviation) in geology is the increase in land elevation, typically in a river system, due to the deposition of sediment.

9061c9231889.title: Aggradation
9061c9231889.sentence: Aggradation occurs in areas in which the supply of sediment is greater than the amount of material that the system is able to transport.

56e98ff4f953.title: Aggradation
56e98ff4f953.sentence: The mass balance between sediment being transported and sediment in the bed is described by the Exner equation.

f3881dd89882.title: Aggradation
f3881dd89882.sentence: Typical aggradational environments include lowland alluvial rivers, river deltas, and alluvial fans.

465c8702b3d3.title: Aggradation
465c8702b3d3.sentence: Aggradational environments are often undergoing slow subsidence which balances the increase in land surface elevation due to aggradation.

da1118848903.title: Aggradation
da1118848903.sentence: In another example, the quantity of sediment entering a river channel may increase when climate becomes drier.

c8a511168dca.title: Aggradation
c8a511168dca.sentence: The increase in sediment is caused by a decrease in soil binding that results from plant growth being suppressed.

3e4438e1b127.title: Aggradation
3e4438e1b127.sentence: The drier conditions cause river flow to decrease at the same time as sediment is being supplied in greater quantities, resulting in the river becoming choked with sediment.

8108a8a2404b.title: Aggradation
8108a8a2404b.sentence: Aggradation can be caused by changes in climate, land use, and geologic activity, such as volcanic eruption, earthquakes, and faulting.

430faa9778bd.title: Aggradation
430faa9778bd.sentence: In 2009, a report by researchers from the University of Colorado at Boulder in the journal Nature Geoscience said that reduced aggradation was contributing to an increased risk of flooding in many river deltas.

4e9dbb6a3c71.title: Entrainment (physical geography)
4e9dbb6a3c71.sentence: In physical geography, entrainment is the process by which surface sediment is incorporated into a fluid flow (such as air, water or even ice) as part of the operation of erosion.

8ccb7cb00d1e.title: Fluvial sediment processes
8ccb7cb00d1e.sentence: For each grain size there is a specific flow velocity at which the grains start to move, called entrainment velocity.

f70bdcd3a327.title: Fluvial sediment processes
f70bdcd3a327.sentence: However the grains will continue to be transported even if the velocity falls below the entrainment velocity due to the reduced (or removed) friction between the grains and the river bed.

5e3d0e7bc7d8.title: Fluvial sediment processes
5e3d0e7bc7d8.sentence: Eventually the velocity will fall low enough for the grains to be deposited.

484c5146906a.title: Fluvial sediment processes
484c5146906a.sentence: This is shown by the Hjulström curve.

2b4348e603eb.title: Shear velocity
2b4348e603eb.sentence: Shear velocity, also called friction velocity, is a form by which a shear stress may be re-written in units of velocity.

568934f777c9.title: Shear velocity
568934f777c9.sentence: - Diffusion and dispersion of particles, tracers, and contaminants in fluid flows

7e9818472fd2.title: Shear velocity
7e9818472fd2.sentence: - The velocity profile near the boundary of a flow (see Law of the wall)

1feada2815cd.title: Shear velocity
1feada2815cd.sentence: - Transport of sediment in a channel

760e17167442.title: Shear velocity
760e17167442.sentence: Shear velocity scales well to rates of dispersion and bedload sediment transport.

2eb481ebfe1b.title: Shear velocity
2eb481ebfe1b.sentence: A general rule is that the shear velocity is between 5% and 10% of the mean flow velocity.

0879a45d9f9b.title: Shear velocity
0879a45d9f9b.sentence: Within the lowest portion of the planetary boundary layer a semi-empirical log wind profile is commonly used to describe the vertical distribution of horizontal mean wind speeds.

98df5d05adc3.title: Shear velocity
98df5d05adc3.sentence: Thus, you can extract the friction velocity by knowing the wind velocity at two levels (z).

1d0866b7e519.title: Shear velocity
1d0866b7e519.sentence: The zero-plane displacement (d) is the height in meters above the ground at which zero wind speed is achieved as a result of flow obstacles such as trees or buildings.

d03e03c3febb.title: Shear velocity
d03e03c3febb.sentence: Displacement height or roughness length can be approximated as 2/3 to 3/4 of the average height of the obstacles.

30f546c03a50.title: Badlands
30f546c03a50.sentence: Badlands are a type of dry terrain where softer sedimentary rocks and clay-rich soils have been extensively eroded.

fc41b3c00d46.title: Badlands
fc41b3c00d46.sentence: They are characterized by steep slopes, minimal vegetation, lack of a substantial regolith, and high drainage density.

6b2d250dc8c4.title: Badlands
6b2d250dc8c4.sentence: Badlands have a very high drainage density of 48 to 464 kilometres per square kilometre (77 to 747 miles per square mile).

bd11f11965e3.title: Badlands
bd11f11965e3.sentence: Badlands arise from a combination of an impermeable but easily eroded ground surface, sparse vegetation, and infrequent but heavy rainfall.

ab5440710f3e.title: Badlands
ab5440710f3e.sentence: Where sudden precipitation cannot penetrate impermeable clays, it is channeled into a very dense system of streamlets that erode a dense system of ever-enlarging, coalescing gulleys and ravines.

a7f431f8ef40.title: Badlands
a7f431f8ef40.sentence: However, it has been estimated that the badlands of Badlands National Park erode at the relatively high rate of about one inch or 25 millimetres per year.

db34a0c14cd6.title: Badlands
db34a0c14cd6.sentence: The presence of bentonite clay further increases erodibility, as can rejuvenation of the drainage system from regional uplift, as occurred at Badlands National Park.

9afbc5819259.title: Badlands
9afbc5819259.sentence: Although most badland topography is natural, badlands have been produced artificially by destruction of vegetation cover, through overgrazing, acid rain, or acid mine drainage.

51cc849866fa.title: Badlands
51cc849866fa.sentence: The Cheltenham Badlands in Caledon, Ontario, are an example of badlands produced by poor farming practices.

ede63d43c3cc.title: Denudation
ede63d43c3cc.sentence: Denudation is measured in the wearing down of Earth's surface in inches or centimeters per 1000 years.

1c899c946a87.title: Denudation
1c899c946a87.sentence: The most common way of measuring denudation is from stream load measurements taken at gauging stations.

8c7e1e5dced9.title: Denudation
8c7e1e5dced9.sentence: The suspended load, bed load, and dissolved load are included in measurements.

0a575ae4404f.title: Denudation
0a575ae4404f.sentence: The weight of the load is converted to volumetric units and the load volume is divided by the area of the watershed above the gauging station.

37508cd4f307.title: Denudation
37508cd4f307.sentence: The most common isotopes used are 26Al and 10Be; however, 10Be is used more often in these analyses.

0a2a142bce96.title: Denudation
0a2a142bce96.sentence: On average, the concentration of undisturbed cosmogenic isotopes in sediment leaving a particular basin is inversely related to the rate at which that basin is eroding.

938dcdfeca38.title: Denudation
938dcdfeca38.sentence: An issue with this method of measurement is the high annual variation in fluvial erosion, which can be up to a factor of five between successive years.

ce947f98b54a.title: Denudation
ce947f98b54a.sentence: This rate is intended as an estimate and often assumes uniform erosion, among other things, to simplify calculations.

af9f5f783c60.title: Denudation
af9f5f783c60.sentence: An important equation for denudation is the stream power law: E=KAmSn, where E is erosion rate, K is the erodibility constant, A is drainage area, S is channel gradient, and m and n are functions that are usually given beforehand or assumed based on the location.

b50e56f39e5c.title: Shields parameter
b50e56f39e5c.sentence: The Shields parameter, also called the Shields criterion or Shields number, is a nondimensional number used to calculate the initiation of motion of sediment in a fluid flow.

6de944c252ac.title: Shields parameter
6de944c252ac.sentence: This parameter has been developed by Albert F. Shields, and is called later Shields parameter.

207de190243a.title: Shields parameter
207de190243a.sentence: It is a form of non-dimensionalization of a shear stress, and is typically denoted ψ or θ.

25910a049202.title: Shields parameter
25910a049202.sentence: - τ is a dimensional shear stress,

461d4b1c6a11.title: Shields parameter
461d4b1c6a11.sentence: - ρs is the density of the sediment,

fffbe93d6c63.title: Shields parameter
fffbe93d6c63.sentence: - ρ is the density of the fluid,

9df14eee9724.title: Shields parameter
9df14eee9724.sentence: - D is a characteristic particle diameter of the sediment.

a97e5c61b60e.title: Shields parameter
a97e5c61b60e.sentence: By multiplying the top and bottom of the Shields parameter by D2, you can see that it is proportional to the ratio of fluid force on the particle to the weight of the particle.

96a360dc83b4.title: Shields parameter
96a360dc83b4.sentence: The critical shear stress and also the critical Shields number (τ∗ and θ∗) describe the conditions when the sediment starts moving.

7da2845f02dc.title: Shields parameter
7da2845f02dc.sentence: Note that the shear stress is a property of the current, while the critical shear stress is a property of the sediment.

484ea01f0842.title: Suspended load
484ea01f0842.sentence: The Shields Diagram (based on the Shields formula) uses the critical shear stress and Reynolds number to estimate transportation rate.

fbf634021138.title: Suspended load
fbf634021138.sentence: The Shields Diagram is considered a more precise chart to estimate suspended load.

9f27f2ad6132.title: Corrasion
9f27f2ad6132.sentence: Corrasion is a geomorphological term for the process of mechanical erosion of the earth's surface caused when materials are transported across it by running water, waves, glaciers, wind or gravitational movement downslope.

cbec350de96e.title: Corrasion
cbec350de96e.sentence: An example is the wearing away of rock on a river or seabed by the impact or grinding action of particles moving with the water.

c808cbe82c54.title: Corrasion
c808cbe82c54.sentence: The resultant effect on the rock is called abrasion.

8375b1572645.title: Corrasion
8375b1572645.sentence: Corrasion is different from corrosion which is due to chemical and solvent action of water on soluble or partly soluble rocks when they come in contact.

7c745d0cfd6b.title: Corrasion
7c745d0cfd6b.sentence: - Lateral corrasion: the sideways erosion which widens the river.

31a6bf24e0c4.title: Corrasion
31a6bf24e0c4.sentence: - Vertical corrasion: downward erosion which deepens the river valley.

1546004c6409.title: Marine clay
1546004c6409.sentence: Once the clay is deposited on the ocean floor it can change its structure through a process known as flocculation, process by which fine particulates are caused to clump together or floc.

633f3053f974.title: Marine clay
633f3053f974.sentence: Particles can become suspended in water; heavier sand settles quickly, while finer silt and clay particles remain suspended longer.

ffe756a6b33a.title: Marine clay
ffe756a6b33a.sentence: Marine clay particles, being very small and often negatively charged, can resist settling and sometimes stay suspended indefinitely, this is also known as turbidity, in which suspended particles create a murky brown color.

b2e02a7a9788.title: Marine clay
b2e02a7a9788.sentence: In estuarine systems, the changes in physicochemical conditions from the river side to the sea side triggers flocculation and leads to estuarine siltation.

983aa635ac31.title: Marine clay
983aa635ac31.sentence: This is one of the main causes for the dredging activities in harbors.

1da1355f9841.title: Marine clay
1da1355f9841.sentence: Organic matter in particular plays a major role in marine clay flocculation as it can adhere to marine clay particles.

3cfe67ff5f32.title: Marine clay
3cfe67ff5f32.sentence: Marine clay particles can adopt different arrangements, and their structure and behavior depend on the types of exchange cations (charged ions of sodium, potassium, or calcium) that attach to them.

fd8881b9a0bf.title: Marine clay
fd8881b9a0bf.sentence: Different cations lead to different arrangements and therefore different properties of the clay.

72864b7a5d7c.title: Marine clay
72864b7a5d7c.sentence: Construction in marine clays thus presents a geotechnical engineering challenge.

8b61eb8aeafa.title: Marine clay
8b61eb8aeafa.sentence: Marine clays are sensitive to weathering, which affects soil mechanics and support under structural loads, and limits both bearing capacity and associated service life.

c471d056a7a8.title: Marine clay
c471d056a7a8.sentence: Pavements constructed over marine clay subgrades soils, reduce long‑term durability and increased whole-life costs.

0b67c06e2750.title: Marine clay
0b67c06e2750.sentence: These quick clays have a very high-risk factor associated with them if they are built upon, as they are very unstable due to the fact that liquefaction happens when it becomes saturated and literally flows, causing mass wasting events to happen.

5b020e436af6.title: Marine clay
5b020e436af6.sentence: Geotechnical problems posed by marine clay can be handled by various ground improvement techniques.

8096d78f76a2.title: Marine clay
8096d78f76a2.sentence: Marine clay can be stabilized by mixing it with cement and fly ash binding materials in specific proportions.

9e4800774773.title: Marine clay
9e4800774773.sentence: Marine clays are used as low‑permeability liners for limiting landfill leachate.

20ca6bba0d9d.title: Marine clay
20ca6bba0d9d.sentence: Marine clay minerals also provide landfills with useful adsorptive properties.

ca6fe3a4b847.title: Marine clay
ca6fe3a4b847.sentence: Marine clays have been used in ancient and traditional ceramics for heat resistant ceramics products like cookware, and refractory bricks.

ae0d62a80a4e.title: Vegetation and slope stability
ae0d62a80a4e.sentence: Roots reinforce the soil by growing across failure planes, root columns acting as piles, and by limiting surface erosion.

ea0087b1deff.title: Vegetation and slope stability
ea0087b1deff.section: Mechanical reinforcement of roots > Root growth across failure planes
ea0087b1deff.sentence: When roots grow across the plane of potential failure there is an increase in shear strength by binding particles.

22b7b273dbb5.title: Vegetation and slope stability
22b7b273dbb5.section: Mechanical reinforcement of roots > Root growth across failure planes
22b7b273dbb5.sentence: The roots anchor the unstable surficial soil into the deeper stable layers or bedrock.

851e5c1c1e36.title: Vegetation and slope stability
851e5c1c1e36.section: Mechanical reinforcement of roots > Root reinforcement model
851e5c1c1e36.sentence: The root Reinforced Earth root model is the result of the root elongation across a potential slip plane which produces a tensile root force which is transferred to the soil by cohesive and frictional contacts between the root and the soil.

7a2114c956b1.title: Vegetation and slope stability
7a2114c956b1.section: Mechanical reinforcement of roots > Root growth across failure planes
7a2114c956b1.sentence: However, the strength exerted by roots generally only extends down to 1 m (3.3 ft) while most failures occur between 1.2–1.5 m (3.9–4.9 ft) soil depth.

bbd170f73517.title: Vegetation and slope stability
bbd170f73517.section: Mechanical reinforcement of roots > Limitation of surface erosion
bbd170f73517.sentence: Vegetation can also control water erosion by limiting surface processes such as sheet wash and overland flow.

763b42457b0b.title: Vegetation and slope stability
763b42457b0b.section: Mechanical reinforcement of roots > Limitation of surface erosion
763b42457b0b.sentence: Fine roots are thought to help keep the surface soil together and prevent surface erosion.

6fb29a284d11.title: Vegetation and slope stability
6fb29a284d11.section: Mechanical reinforcement of roots > Limitation of surface erosion
6fb29a284d11.sentence: The fine root network may have an apparent enhanced cohesion, which is comparable to geosynthetic mesh elements.

0080c085c6b3.title: Vegetation and slope stability
0080c085c6b3.section: Mechanical reinforcement of roots > Limitation of surface erosion
0080c085c6b3.sentence: The limitation of surface erosion processes is particularly apparent in areas of shrub and grass where the fine root distribution is consistent and clearly defined; however, cohesion is generally limited to the top 1 m (3.3 ft) of soil.

7d01074bad98.title: Vegetation and slope stability
7d01074bad98.section: Mechanical reinforcement of roots > Tensile root strength contribution and pull out resistance
7d01074bad98.sentence: The pull out resistance of a root is the measured resistance of root structure to be pulled out of the ground and is likely to be only a little less than the measured tensile strength of the root which is the roots resistance to breaking as measured in the laboratory.

65fea669453f.title: Vegetation and slope stability
65fea669453f.section: Mechanical reinforcement of roots > Tensile root strength contribution and pull out resistance
65fea669453f.sentence: The tensile root strength of a range of diameters over a range of species has been tested in the laboratory and has been found to be approximately 5–60 MN/m2.

38aa06bd324b.title: Vegetation and slope stability
38aa06bd324b.section: Mechanical reinforcement of roots > Type A failure
38aa06bd324b.sentence: Roots that do not have branches generally fail in tension and pull straight out of the ground with only minimal resistance.

7dd8df19cd9d.title: Vegetation and slope stability
7dd8df19cd9d.section: Mechanical reinforcement of roots > Type B failure
7dd8df19cd9d.sentence: Type B failure occurs when branched roots initially reach their maximum peak resistance then sustain a high resistance which slowly reduces as the branches of the roots fail after significant strain.

bdee3e6ebf4d.title: Vegetation and slope stability
bdee3e6ebf4d.section: Mechanical reinforcement of roots > Type C failure
bdee3e6ebf4d.sentence: These roots break with increasingly applied force in stages in the form of stepped peaks corresponding to the progressive breaking of roots of greater diameters.

fe002424b21a.title: Vegetation and slope stability
fe002424b21a.section: Mechanical reinforcement of roots > Factors which affect root pull out resistance
fe002424b21a.sentence: The studies also showed that there is a positive correlation between maximum root pull out resistance and root diameter for hawthorn and oat root.

4e3921f667e3.title: Vegetation and slope stability
4e3921f667e3.section: Mechanical reinforcement of roots > Factors which affect root pull out resistance
4e3921f667e3.sentence: Smaller diameter roots had a lower pull out resistance or breaking force than the larger diameter roots.

a98579a99490.title: Vegetation and slope stability
a98579a99490.section: Mechanical reinforcement of roots > Factors which affect root pull out resistance
a98579a99490.sentence: In a pull out test the root is likely to fail at weak points such as branching points, nodes or damaged areas.

2b3fab52571b.title: Vegetation and slope stability
2b3fab52571b.section: Mechanical reinforcement of roots > Tensile root strength contribution and pull out resistance
2b3fab52571b.sentence: In order for the root to actually enhance slope stability the root must have sufficient embedment and adhesion with the soil.

b56f28ce0765.title: Vegetation and slope stability
b56f28ce0765.section: Mechanical reinforcement of roots > Tensile root strength contribution and pull out resistance
b56f28ce0765.sentence: The way that roots interact with the soil is intricate but for engineering purposes the available force contributions may be measured with in situ pull out tests.

798f7e5456c7.title: Vegetation and slope stability
798f7e5456c7.sentence: Vegetation influences slope stability by removing water through transpiration.

3997f61ac546.title: Vegetation and slope stability
3997f61ac546.sentence: The major effect of transpiration is the reduction of soil pore water pressures which counteracts the loss of strength which occurs through wetting, this is most readily seen as a loss of moisture around trees.

cadf91e57d29.title: Vegetation and slope stability
cadf91e57d29.sentence: The ability to transpire in wet conditions is severely reduced and therefore any increase in soil strength previously gained in evaporation and transpiration will be lost or significantly reduced, consequently the effects of transpiration cannot be taken into account at these times.

3292661fa5ad.title: Vegetation and slope stability
3292661fa5ad.sentence: However it can be assumed that the chance of slope failure following saturation by storm events or periods of extended rainfall will be lessened as a result of transpiration.

7f69c0bf0f31.title: Vegetation and slope stability
7f69c0bf0f31.sentence: Studies in Malaysia have shown that there is a significant relationship between root length density, soil water content and ultimately slope stability.

036094c1ffc4.title: Vegetation and slope stability
036094c1ffc4.sentence: Slopes that had high root density (due to dense vegetation on the surface) were less likely to undergo slope failure.

b677504cc8c6.title: Vegetation and slope stability
b677504cc8c6.sentence: This is because a high root length density results in low soil water content which in turn results in an increase in shear strength and a decrease in soil permeability.

a6b8f8c0c2fb.title: Vegetation and slope stability
a6b8f8c0c2fb.sentence: Desiccation cracks can potentially be extended by vegetation in dry weather promoting the deeper penetration of water to a potential slip plane and increased water pressure into the soil during the wet periods.

b746a907feff.title: Vegetation and slope stability
b746a907feff.sentence: Shading helps prevent the desiccation of the soils which results in shrinkage and cracking allowing the deep penetration of rain water.

061ab59cb5a0.title: Landslide classification
061ab59cb5a0.sentence: The landslide causes are the reasons that a landslide occurred in that location and at that time and may be considered to be factors that made the slope vulnerable to failure, that predispose the slope to becoming unstable.

3661abc59cd3.title: Landslide classification
3661abc59cd3.sentence: The trigger is the single event that finally initiated the landslide.

b0116ea8d64d.title: Landslide classification
b0116ea8d64d.sentence: Thus, causes combine to make a slope vulnerable to failure, and the trigger finally initiates the movement.

fa0aa083e356.title: Landslide classification
fa0aa083e356.sentence: Landslides can have many causes but can only have one trigger.

470b22c30465.title: Landslide classification
470b22c30465.sentence: Usually, it is relatively easy to determine the trigger after the landslide has occurred (although it is generally very difficult to determine the exact nature of landslide triggers ahead of a movement event).

6018d53ef9b8.title: Landslide classification
6018d53ef9b8.sentence: Landslide causes include geological factors, morphological factors, physical factors and factors associated with human activity.

eb2874aa79e7.title: Landslide classification
eb2874aa79e7.section: Classification factors > B7) Causes of the movements
eb2874aa79e7.sentence: Terzaghi describes causes as "internal" and "external" referring to modifications in the conditions of the stability of the bodies.

ab378188c13b.title: Landslide classification
ab378188c13b.section: Classification factors > B7) Causes of the movements
ab378188c13b.sentence: Whilst the internal causes induce modifications in the material itself which decrease its resistance to shear stress, the external causes generally induce an increase of shear stress, so that block or bodies are no longer stable.

87be3d95adf3.title: Landslide classification
87be3d95adf3.sentence: Landslides occur during earthquakes as a result of two separate but interconnected processes: seismic shaking and pore water pressure generation.

79480935ec26.title: Landslide classification
79480935ec26.sentence: The maximum acceleration is usually seen at the crest of the slope or along the ridge line, meaning that it is a characteristic of seismically triggered landslides that they extend to the top of the slope.

4551def9e2d8.title: Landslide classification
4551def9e2d8.sentence: In the majority of cases the main trigger of landslides is heavy or prolonged rainfall.

611081121d00.title: Landslide classification
611081121d00.sentence: A global survey of landslide occurrence in the 12 months to the end of September 2003 revealed that there were 210 damaging landslide events worldwide.

5265cd17ca98.title: Landslide classification
5265cd17ca98.sentence: Of these, over 90% were triggered by heavy rainfall.

a4d3d055b729.title: Landslide classification
a4d3d055b729.sentence: Rainfall triggers a large amount of landslides principally because the rainfall drives an increase in pore water pressure within the soil.

7a53f230d596.title: Landslide classification
7a53f230d596.sentence: When the slope fills with water, the fluid pressure provides the block with buoyancy, reducing the resistance to movement.

d94d12a3e337.title: Landslide classification
d94d12a3e337.sentence: In addition, in some cases fluid pressures can act down the slope as a result of groundwater flow to provide a hydraulic push to the landslide that further decreases the stability.

00f2efc5151d.title: Landslide classification
00f2efc5151d.sentence: - Fluidization of debris from earlier events to form debris flows;

d080601bbcda.title: Landslide classification
d080601bbcda.sentence: - Loss of suction forces in silty materials, leading to generally shallow failures (this may be an important mechanism in residual soils in tropical areas following deforestation);

c54e8264214c.title: Landslide classification
c54e8264214c.sentence: - Undercutting of the toe of the slope through river erosion.

6a8a90fe5154.title: Landslide classification
6a8a90fe5154.sentence: - Destabilizing of non-lithified earth materials through soil-piping.

7519e54bc2a8.title: Landslide classification
7519e54bc2a8.sentence: Finally, Caine (1980) established a worldwide threshold:

71e597c1c6b5.title: Landslide classification
71e597c1c6b5.sentence: I = 14.82 D - 0.39 where: I is the rainfall intensity (mm·h−1), D is duration of rainfall (h)

e3cb3aa35f6f.title: Landslide classification
e3cb3aa35f6f.sentence: This threshold applies over time periods of 10 minutes to 10 days.

be1ffbc6071e.title: River
be1ffbc6071e.sentence: The sediment yield of a river is the quantity of sand per unit area within a watershed that is removed over a period of time.

bae9633e8805.title: River
bae9633e8805.sentence: The monitoring of the sediment yield of a river is important for ecologists to understand the health of its ecosystems, the rate of erosion of the river's environment, and the effects of human activity.

e70d769e4d77.title: Legacy sediment
e70d769e4d77.sentence: For example, changing crops from grains to potatoes in late 19th century Poland resulted in such increased sediment yields, that meandering rivers metamorphosed into braided rivers.

e673a81ff66c.title: Legacy sediment
e673a81ff66c.sentence: Sedimentation is reduced or removed altogether when human activities reduce sediment yields from upstream (e.g. dams and reservoirs within upland regions, sediment detention basins) or reduce the river channel's physical complexity (e.g. channelization, drainage) or disconnect river channels from adjacent floodplains and wetlands (e.g. levees, removal of beaver dams and logjams/large woody debris).

c991c8555998.title: Badlands
c991c8555998.sentence: In addition to surface erosion, badlands sometimes have well-developed piping, which is a system of pipes, joints, caverns, and other connected void spaces in the subsurface through which water can drain.

b5b8b67a1789.title: Dam
b5b8b67a1789.sentence: A risk unique to earthen embankment dams is "piping": a small leak through or under the permeable dam structure gradually erodes the soil, until a small channel is formed, which – if untreated – may lead to dam failure.

d411d8e4714d.title: Buffer strip
d411d8e4714d.sentence: Filter strips are areas of grass or other permanent vegetation that protect riparian areas from sediment runoff, pesticides, pathogens, organics and nutrients.

617a52f952c1.title: Conservation Reserve Program
617a52f952c1.sentence: Filter strips and buffer strips along the edge of agricultural fields can intercept the runoff materials and keep them from leaving the field.

1e63097f1ee8.title: Buffer strip
1e63097f1ee8.sentence: Filter strips work best when other conservation practices are used in order to drain water in their direction.

9460dd7b9d14.title: Buffer strip
9460dd7b9d14.sentence: Filter strips were originally used mostly in agriculture, but now are a common practice in urban areas where water quality has become an increasingly important issue.

bde7f8d0e578.title: Riparian buffer
bde7f8d0e578.sentence: The US National Agroforestry Center has developed a filter strip design tool called AgBufferBuilder, which is a GIS-based computer program for designing vegetative filter strips around agricultural fields that utilizes terrain analysis to account for spatially non-uniform runoff.

2f86457d8e9c.title: Wetland
2f86457d8e9c.sentence: A wetland is a distinct semi-aquatic ecosystem whose groundcovers are flooded or saturated in water, either permanently, for years or decades, or only seasonally.

93158e2b5b4e.title: Wetland
93158e2b5b4e.sentence: Flooding results in oxygen-poor (anoxic) processes taking place, especially in the soils.

dc8bafb3a383.title: Wetland
dc8bafb3a383.sentence: Wetlands form a transitional zone between waterbodies and dry lands, and are different from other terrestrial or aquatic ecosystems due to their vegetation's roots having adapted to oxygen-poor waterlogged soils.

1eb5195129e3.title: Wetland
1eb5195129e3.sentence: A more concise definition is a community composed of hydric soil and hydrophytes.

efc9e2009c96.title: Wetland
efc9e2009c96.sentence: There are four main kinds of wetlands – marsh, swamp, bog, and fen (bogs and fens being types of peatlands or mires).

8e32c272b4da.title: Wetland
8e32c272b4da.sentence: For example, marshes are wetlands dominated by emergent herbaceous vegetation such as reeds, cattails, and sedges.

c650901120ce.title: Wetland
c650901120ce.sentence: Swamps are dominated by woody vegetation, such as trees and shrubs (although reed swamps in Europe are dominated by reeds, not trees).

7278f7b3a82d.title: Wetland
7278f7b3a82d.sentence: Examples of wetlands classified by the sources of water include tidal wetlands, where the water source is ocean tides; estuaries, water source is mixed tidal and river waters; floodplains, water source is excess water from overflowed rivers or lakes; and bogs and vernal ponds, water source is rainfall or meltwater, sometimes mediated through groundwater springs.

2fd62a73f0ae.title: Wetland
2fd62a73f0ae.sentence: In the US, the best known classifications are the Cowardin classification system and the hydrogeomorphic (HGM) classification system.

756517ac3bad.title: Wetland
756517ac3bad.sentence: The Cowardin system includes five main types of wetlands: marine (ocean-associated), estuarine (mixed ocean- and river-associated), riverine (within river channels), lacustrine (lake-associated) and palustrine (inland nontidal habitats).

3c8e58457a87.title: Wetland
3c8e58457a87.sentence: The definition used for regulation by the United States government is: 'The term "wetlands" means those areas that are inundated or saturated by surface or ground water at a frequency and duration to support, and that under normal circumstances do support, a prevalence of vegetation typically adapted for life in saturated soil conditions.

ed5935df6832.title: Hydric soil
ed5935df6832.sentence: This term is part of the legal definition of a wetland included in the United States Food Security Act of 1985 (P.L. 99-198).

9dca49af19b8.title: Peat
9dca49af19b8.sentence: About 60% of the world's wetlands are made of peat.

25278621d7e2.title: Wetland
25278621d7e2.sentence: Wetlands exist on every continent, except Antarctica.

3abf8d3f7dea.title: Wetland
3abf8d3f7dea.sentence: The world's largest wetlands include the Amazon River basin, the West Siberian Plain, the Pantanal in South America, and the Sundarbans in the Ganges-Brahmaputra delta.

4ee768caf6af.title: Wetland
4ee768caf6af.sentence: Wetlands are more threatened by environmental degradation than any other ecosystem on Earth, according to the Millennium Ecosystem Assessment from 2005.

491e1835a2b1.title: Peatland
491e1835a2b1.sentence: Wetlands are also protected under the 1971 Ramsar Convention.

5bd01963e47a.title: Peatland
5bd01963e47a.sentence: A peatland is a type of wetland whose soils consist of organic matter from decaying plants, forming layers of peat.

1e7dd8a7c4d2.title: Peatland
1e7dd8a7c4d2.sentence: Peatlands arise because of incomplete decomposition of organic matter, usually litter from vegetation, due to water-logging and subsequent anoxia.

adc5633f47ce.title: Peatland
adc5633f47ce.sentence: Botanists and ecologists use the word "peatland" as a general term for any terrain dominated by peat to a depth of at least 30 cm (12 in), even if it has been completely drained (i.e. a peatland can be dry).

6b26c6595ccc.title: Peatland
6b26c6595ccc.sentence: The formation of peatlands is primarily controlled by climatic conditions such as precipitation and temperature, although terrain relief is a major factor as waterlogging occurs more easily on flatter ground and in basins.

216ee706e96d.title: Peatland
216ee706e96d.sentence: Mires occur wherever conditions are right for peat accumulation: largely where organic matter is constantly waterlogged.

66c74b62bd9d.title: Peatland
66c74b62bd9d.sentence: Hence the distribution of mires is dependent on topography, climate, parent material, biota and time.

cd575c75c5e3.title: Peatland
cd575c75c5e3.sentence: Peat formation typically initiates as a paludification of a mineral soil forest, terrestrialisation of lakes, or primary peat formation on bare soils on previously glaciated areas.

1b06d4b6c122.title: Peatland
1b06d4b6c122.sentence: Topographically, accumulating peat elevates the ground surface above the original topography.

f2ee2a908dce.title: Peatland
f2ee2a908dce.sentence: Mires can reach considerable heights above the underlying mineral soil or bedrock: peat depths of above 10 m have been commonly recorded in temperate regions (many temperate and most boreal mires were removed by ice sheets in the last Ice Age), and above 25 m in tropical regions.[7] When the absolute decay rate of peat in the catotelm (the lower, water-saturated zone of the peat layer) matches the rate of input of new peat into the catotelm, the mire will stop growing in height.[8]

aacf6bfeb934.title: Peatland
aacf6bfeb934.sentence: Peat has very high cation-exchange capacity due to its high organic matter content: cations such as Ca²⁺ are preferentially adsorbed onto the peat in exchange for H+ ions.

08426c5e5490.title: Peatland
08426c5e5490.sentence: Water passing through peat declines in nutrients and pH.

f665d18c6336.title: Peatland
f665d18c6336.sentence: Therefore, mires are typically nutrient-poor and acidic unless the inflow of groundwater (bringing in supplementary cations) is high.

f54b86a31158.title: Peatland
f54b86a31158.sentence: Peatlands are estimated to cover around 3% of the globe's surface, although estimating the extent of their cover worldwide is difficult due to the varying accuracy and methodologies of land surveys from many countries.

18f996541dbb.title: Peatland
18f996541dbb.sentence: Peatlands are used by humans in modern times for a range of purposes, the most dominant being agriculture and forestry, which accounts for around a quarter of global peatland area.

3b50de97ea77.title: Peatland
3b50de97ea77.sentence: This involves cutting drainage ditches to lower the water table with the intended purpose of enhancing the productivity of forest cover or for use as pasture or cropland.

3f07627ef3ab.title: Landscape ecology
3f07627ef3ab.sentence: Landscape ecology is the science of studying and improving relationships between ecological processes in the environment and particular ecosystems.

0b613b9057bb.title: Landscape ecology
0b613b9057bb.sentence: This is done within a variety of landscape scales, development spatial patterns, and organizational levels of research and policy.

0bcf9454f00a.title: Landscape ecology
0bcf9454f00a.sentence: Landscapes are spatially heterogeneous geographic areas characterized by diverse interacting patches or ecosystems, ranging from relatively natural terrestrial and aquatic systems such as forests, grasslands, and lakes to human-dominated environments including agricultural and urban settings.

0257643fd524.title: Landscape ecology
0257643fd524.sentence: The most salient characteristics of landscape ecology are its emphasis on the relationship among pattern, process and scales, and its focus on broad-scale ecological and environmental issues.

e95c4f3bbba9.title: Landscape ecology
e95c4f3bbba9.sentence: The main difference from traditional ecological studies, which frequently assume that systems are spatially homogenous, is the consideration of spatial patterns.

64ed71120060.title: Landscape ecology
64ed71120060.sentence: While general ecology theory and its sub-disciplines focused on the study of more homogenous, discrete community units organized in a hierarchical structure (typically as ecosystems, populations, species, and communities), landscape ecology built upon heterogeneity in space and time.

626b20a25418.title: Landscape ecology
626b20a25418.sentence: The German term Landschaftsökologie – thus landscape ecology – was coined by German geographer Carl Troll in 1939.

f21cfa03b2f9.title: Landscape ecology
f21cfa03b2f9.sentence: He developed this terminology and many early concepts of landscape ecology as part of his early work, which consisted of applying aerial photograph interpretation to studies of interactions between environment and vegetation.

8141e763b190.title: Landscape ecology
8141e763b190.sentence: By 1980, landscape ecology was a discrete, established discipline.

cd0bcc0c792a.title: Landscape ecology
cd0bcc0c792a.sentence: It was marked by the organization of the International Association for Landscape Ecology (IALE) in 1982.

c538cd6e388a.title: Landscape ecology
c538cd6e388a.sentence: Landscape ecology relies on advanced technologies such as remote sensing, GIS, and models.

31d6e9f26e57.title: Landscape ecology
31d6e9f26e57.sentence: An example would be determining the amount of carbon present in the soil based on landform over a landscape, derived from GIS maps, vegetation types, and rainfall data for a region.

cda6bc952876.title: Landscape ecology
cda6bc952876.sentence: Landscape ecology also includes geomorphology as applied to the design and architecture of landscapes.

3338ba948179.title: Landscape ecology
3338ba948179.sentence: Geomorphology is the study of how geological formations are responsible for the structure of a landscape.

50486b1baf13.title: Landscape ecology
50486b1baf13.sentence: Landscape ecology explicitly includes humans as entities that cause functional changes on the landscape.

02e7f0d90c05.title: Landscape ecology
02e7f0d90c05.sentence: It also proposes ways for restoring degraded landscapes.

54dbd24c7bde.title: Hydric soil
54dbd24c7bde.sentence: Hydric soil is soil which is permanently or seasonally saturated by water, resulting in anaerobic conditions, as found in wetlands.

c2dd951f49aa.title: Hydric soil
c2dd951f49aa.sentence: This is important because plant roots respire (that is, they consume oxygen and carbohydrates while releasing carbon dioxide) and there must be sufficient air—especially oxygen—in the soil to support most forms of soil life.

9bf8677c33ed.title: Hydric soil
9bf8677c33ed.sentence: In addition to plant roots, most forms of soil microorganisms need oxygen to survive.

52221f627243.title: Hydric soil
52221f627243.sentence: This is true of the more well-known soil animals as well, such as ants, earthworms and moles.

ebe293d513ac.title: Hydric soil
ebe293d513ac.sentence: Air normally moves through interconnected pores by forces such as changes in atmospheric pressure, the flushing action of rainwater, and by simple diffusion.

b9ef737747b4.title: Hydric soil
b9ef737747b4.sentence: But soils can often become saturated with water due to rainfall and flooding.

38b722ab0566.title: Hydric soil
38b722ab0566.sentence: When this anaerobic environment continues for long periods during the growing season, quite different biological and chemical reactions begin to dominate, compared with aerobic soils.

4e7f7945aa80.title: Hydric soil
4e7f7945aa80.sentence: In soils where saturation with water is prolonged and is repeated for many years, unique soil properties usually develop that can be recognized in the field.

41e63bc3c7b7.title: Hydric soil
41e63bc3c7b7.sentence: Soils with these unique properties are called hydric soils, and although they may occupy a relatively small portion of the landscape, they maintain important soil functions in the environment.

857356ba1d6c.title: Hydric soil
857356ba1d6c.sentence: The plants found in hydric soils often have aerenchyma, internal spaces in stems and rhizomes, that allow atmospheric oxygen to be transported to the rooting zone.

e3aa2fb34cdb.title: Hydric soil
e3aa2fb34cdb.sentence: Hence, many wetlands are dominated by plants with aerenchyma; common examples include cattails, sedges and water-lilies.

c6915047ea5d.title: Swamp
c6915047ea5d.sentence: Swamps and marshes are specific types of wetlands that form along waterbodies containing rich, hydric soils.

b3df5e9f2d54.title: Freshwater marsh
b3df5e9f2d54.sentence: Soils in freshwater marshes are considered hydric; soils that are saturated during the growing season and have anaerobic, or no oxygen, conditions due to the saturation.

6195bcdd1afc.title: Marsh
6195bcdd1afc.sentence: In ecology, a marsh is a wetland that is dominated by herbaceous plants rather than by woody plants.

8dab71363f8c.title: Marsh
8dab71363f8c.sentence: More in general, the word can be used for any low-lying and seasonally waterlogged terrain.

66f5add497c4.title: Marsh
66f5add497c4.sentence: In Europe and in agricultural literature, low-lying meadows that require draining and embanked polderlands are also referred to as marshes or marshland.

096b0be3c3e8.title: Marsh
096b0be3c3e8.sentence: Marshes can often be found at the edges of lakes and streams, where they form a transition between the aquatic and terrestrial ecosystems.

627c24b154ea.title: Marsh
627c24b154ea.sentence: This form of vegetation is what differentiates marshes from other types of wetland such as swamps, which are dominated by trees, and mires, which are wetlands that have accumulated deposits of acidic peat.

d71a93dda9c0.title: Marsh
d71a93dda9c0.sentence: The pH in marshes tends to be neutral to alkaline, as opposed to bogs, where peat accumulates under more acid conditions.

a0aa308e09ee.title: Marsh
a0aa308e09ee.sentence: The plants must be able to survive in wet mud with low oxygen levels.

bb867be1f6c1.title: Marsh
bb867be1f6c1.sentence: Many of these plants, therefore, have aerenchyma, channels within the stem that allow air to move from the leaves into the rooting zone.

69f6953f678d.title: Marsh
69f6953f678d.sentence: The three main types of marsh are salt marshes, freshwater tidal marshes, and freshwater marshes.

d6320cebce66.title: Marsh
d6320cebce66.sentence: Marshes differ depending mainly on their location and salinity.

e757ef3ef381.title: Marsh
e757ef3ef381.sentence: Saltwater marshes are found around the world in mid to high latitudes, wherever there are sections of protected coastline.

a5ac1d8f50bb.title: Marsh
a5ac1d8f50bb.sentence: They are located close enough to the shoreline that the motion of the tides affects them, and, sporadically, they are covered with water.

e98130ef331f.title: Marsh
e98130ef331f.sentence: Salt marshes are most commonly found in lagoons, estuaries, and on the sheltered side of a shingle or sandspit.

032fac2d401d.title: Marsh
032fac2d401d.sentence: They flourish where the rate of sediment buildup is greater than the rate at which the land level is sinking.

72bd5431073d.title: Marsh
72bd5431073d.sentence: This biological productivity means that marshes contain 0.1% of global sequestered terrestrial carbon.

0e9facb21f28.title: Marsh
0e9facb21f28.sentence: Though some marshes are expected to migrate upland, most natural marshlands will be threatened by sea level rise and associated erosion.

16f3570f34fb.title: Swamp
16f3570f34fb.sentence: A swamp is a forested wetland.

d401e281c922.title: Swamp
d401e281c922.sentence: Swamps are wetlands consisting of saturated soils or standing water and are dominated by water-tolerant woody vegetation such as shrubs, bushes, and trees.

64ecbdc69d46.title: Swamp
64ecbdc69d46.sentence: Swamps are considered to be transition zones because both land and water play a role in creating this environment.

dbc6e98e8ab9.title: Swamp
dbc6e98e8ab9.sentence: The water of a swamp may be fresh water, brackish water, or seawater.

9c21af3c4ec7.title: Swamp
9c21af3c4ec7.sentence: Freshwater swamps form along large rivers or lakes where they are critically dependent upon rainwater and seasonal flooding to maintain natural water level fluctuations.

ec6a01fd49a5.title: Swamp
ec6a01fd49a5.sentence: Saltwater swamps are found along tropical and subtropical coastlines.

dec9368662ea.title: Swamp
dec9368662ea.sentence: Swamps are characterized by their saturated soils and slow-moving waters.

a6cc17d81858.title: Swamp
a6cc17d81858.sentence: The water that accumulates in swamps comes from a variety of sources including precipitation, groundwater, tides and freshwater flooding.

8b539f02b1fd.title: Swamp
8b539f02b1fd.sentence: The hydrology of a swamp is a key factor in its biogeochemical environment, which includes the levels and availability of resources like oxygen, nutrients, pH, and toxicity.

3c3568577adc.title: Swamp
3c3568577adc.sentence: As water flows through the swamp, nutrients, sediment and pollutants are naturally filtered out.

7c06ddc11cee.title: Swamp
7c06ddc11cee.sentence: Any remaining or excess chemicals present will accumulate at the bottom of the swamp, being removed from the water and buried within the sediment.

c56ce3d2c719.title: Swamp
c56ce3d2c719.sentence: The two main types of swamp are "true" or swamp forests and "transitional" or shrub swamps.

8b420981eb2c.title: Peatland
8b420981eb2c.sentence: Some swamps can also be peatlands (e.g. peat swamp forest), while marshes are generally not considered to be peatlands.

ab807c21f109.title: Peatland
ab807c21f109.sentence: Like fens, swamps typically have a higher pH level and higher nutrient availability than bogs.

c5e1f939aed0.title: Swamp
c5e1f939aed0.sentence: The largest swamp in the world is the Amazon River floodplain, which is particularly significant for its large number of fish and tree species.

2d93e504929d.title: Swamp
2d93e504929d.sentence: Some of the world's largest swamps are found along major rivers such as the Amazon, the Mississippi, and the Congo.

e76270cc6206.title: Salt marsh
e76270cc6206.sentence: A salt marsh, saltmarsh or salting, also known as a coastal marsh, is a tidal wetland in the upper coastal intertidal zone between land and sea that is regularly flooded by tides of seawater or brackish water.

af8392e95c40.title: Salt marsh
af8392e95c40.sentence: It is a unique marine coastal ecosystem dominated by dense stands of salt-tolerant plants such as herbs, grasses, or low shrubs.

4f94c0c6a386.title: Salt marsh
4f94c0c6a386.sentence: These plants are terrestrial in origin and are essential to the stability of the salt marsh in trapping and binding sediments.

36470e9a6279.title: Salt marsh
36470e9a6279.sentence: The formation begins as tidal flats gain elevation relative to sea level by sediment accretion, and subsequently the rate and duration of tidal flooding decreases so that vegetation can colonize on the exposed surface.

4b481852c5d5.title: Salt marsh
4b481852c5d5.section: Microbial life in salt marshes > Chemo(litho)autotrophs in salt marshes > Why are sulfate-reducing bacteria in salt marshes?
4b481852c5d5.sentence: Salt marshes are the ideal environment for sulfate-reducing bacteria.

6afec89fd18f.title: Salt marsh
6afec89fd18f.section: Microbial life in salt marshes > Chemo(litho)autotrophs in salt marshes > Why are sulfate-reducing bacteria in salt marshes?
6afec89fd18f.sentence: The sulfate-reducing bacteria tend to live in anoxic conditions, such as in salt marshes, because they require reduced compounds to produce their energy.

0e6332069297.title: Salt marsh
0e6332069297.section: Microbial life in salt marshes > Chemo(litho)autotrophs in salt marshes > Why are sulfate-reducing bacteria in salt marshes?
0e6332069297.sentence: Since there is a high sedimentation rate and a high amount of organic matter, the conditions of the sediment are usually dependably anoxic.

6de069e773ac.title: Salt marsh
6de069e773ac.section: Microbial life in salt marshes > Microbial decomposition activity within salt marshes
6de069e773ac.sentence: Nutrient cycling in salt marshes is highly promoted by the resident community of bacteria and fungi involved in remineralizing organic matter.

9a2b7e984ea8.title: Salt marsh
9a2b7e984ea8.section: Microbial life in salt marshes > Microbial decomposition activity within salt marshes
9a2b7e984ea8.sentence: Bacteria are responsible for the degradation of up to 88% of lignocellulotic material in salt marshes.

10a789a8aded.title: Salt marsh
10a789a8aded.section: Microbial life in salt marshes > Chemo(litho)autotrophs in salt marshes > Abundance and significance of chemolithoautotroph nitrifiers within salt marshes
10a789a8aded.sentence: Within salt marshes, chemolithoautotrophic nitrifying bacteria are also frequently identified, including Betaproteobacteria ammonia oxidizers such as Nitrosomonas and Nitrosospira.

70aef4b840a1.title: Salt marsh
70aef4b840a1.section: Microbial life in salt marshes > Photoautotrophic bacteria > Cyanobacteria in salt marshes
70aef4b840a1.sentence: Cyanobacteria are important nitrogen fixers in salt marshes, and provide nitrogen to organisms like diatoms and microalgae.

896687943a7d.title: Floodplain
896687943a7d.sentence: A floodplain or flood plain or bottomlands is an area of land adjacent to a river that stretches from the banks of the river channel to the base of the enclosing valley and experiences flooding during periods of high discharge.

fac081256b96.title: Floodplain
fac081256b96.sentence: The soils usually consist of clays, silts, sands, and gravels deposited during floods.

161335757de2.title: Floodplain
161335757de2.sentence: Because of regular flooding, floodplains frequently have high soil fertility since nutrients are deposited with the flood waters.

4153f89a4216.title: Floodplain
4153f89a4216.sentence: This can encourage farming; some important agricultural regions, such as the Nile and Mississippi river basins, heavily exploit floodplains.

f0780c7af86e.title: Floodplain
f0780c7af86e.sentence: Most floodplains are formed by deposition on the inside of river meanders and by overbank flow.

51f70d143a22.title: Floodplain
51f70d143a22.sentence: Wherever the river meanders, the flowing water erodes the river bank on the outside of the meander.

7c985fd47a25.title: Floodplain
7c985fd47a25.sentence: This is described as lateral accretion since the deposition builds the point bar laterally into the river channel.

460a29d79356.title: Floodplain
460a29d79356.sentence: In undisturbed river systems, overbank flow is frequent, typically occurring every one to two years, regardless of climate or topography.

39e885d62300.title: Floodplain
39e885d62300.sentence: Flow over the banks of the river deposits a thin veneer of sediments that is coarsest and thickest close to the channel.

fdd60d3c5412.title: Floodplain
fdd60d3c5412.sentence: This is described as vertical accretion, since the deposits build upwards.

0c6b2800e6dd.title: Floodplain
0c6b2800e6dd.sentence: Natural levees are ridges along river banks that form from rapid deposition from the overbank flow.

d08e72a09b7b.title: Floodplain
d08e72a09b7b.sentence: Most of the suspended sand is deposited on the levees, leaving the silt and clay sediments to be deposited as floodplain mud further from the river.

a75d14e2db46.title: Floodplain
a75d14e2db46.sentence: The quantity of sediments in a floodplain greatly exceeds the river load of sediments.

aed75493e0f0.title: Floodplain
aed75493e0f0.sentence: Thus, floodplains are an important storage site for sediments during their transport from where they are generated to their ultimate depositional environment.

3b822d0b1206.title: Floodplain
3b822d0b1206.sentence: Portions of the abandoned floodplain may be preserved as fluvial terraces.

55b107b18240.title: Floodplain
55b107b18240.sentence: At much longer intervals, the river may abandon the channel belt and build a new one at another position on the floodplain.

999c2535a734.title: Floodplain
999c2535a734.sentence: This process is called avulsion and occurs at intervals of 10–1000 years.

c73bb771acdd.title: Wetland
c73bb771acdd.section: Disturbances and human impacts > Drainage of floodplains
c73bb771acdd.sentence: Drainage of floodplains or development activities that narrow floodplain corridors (such as the construction of levees) reduces the ability of coupled river-floodplain systems to control flood damage.

eaa4818af87c.title: Wetland
eaa4818af87c.section: Disturbances and human impacts > Drainage of floodplains
eaa4818af87c.sentence: Loss of wetland floodplains results in more severe and damaging flooding.

9dd801fb4db2.title: Ombrotrophic
9dd801fb4db2.sentence: Ombrotrophic ('cloud-fed'), from Ancient Greek ὄμβρος (ómbros) meaning 'rain' and τροφή (trofē) meaning 'food', refers to soils or vegetation which receive all of their water and nutrients from precipitation, rather than from streams or springs.

0e77c4289dde.title: Ombrotrophic
0e77c4289dde.sentence: Such environments are hydrologically isolated from the surrounding landscape, and since rain is acidic and very low in nutrients, they are home to organisms tolerant of acidic, low-nutrient environments.

06304e02ff62.title: Ombrotrophic
06304e02ff62.sentence: The hydrology of these environments are directly related to their climate, as precipitation is the water and nutrient source, and temperatures dictate how quickly water evaporates from these systems.

9e94c7a3b75a.title: Ombrotrophic
9e94c7a3b75a.sentence: Ombrotrophic circumstances may occur even in landscapes composed of limestone or other nutrient-rich substrates – for example, in high-rainfall areas, limestone boulders may be capped by acidic ombrotrophic bog vegetation.

dfbf57521166.title: Ombrotrophic
dfbf57521166.sentence: In most cases, ombrotrophic bogs are extremely nutrient deficient, relying solely on precipitation and atmospheric dust for nutrient supply.

4ae0841b47a4.title: Ombrotrophic
4ae0841b47a4.sentence: However, while ombrotrophic peat decomposes slowly, some nutrient release does occur.

2f0d85a6de30.title: Ombrotrophic
2f0d85a6de30.sentence: For example, microelements like zinc, copper, and manganese are easily mobilized.

f02cbdc45c93.title: Ombrotrophic
f02cbdc45c93.sentence: It was found that mercury and lead are immobile in ombrotrophic peat, indicating that their distribution can be used to determine temporal changes in deposition and suggesting that ombrotrophic bogs can serve as reliable records of historic atmospheric mercury deposition.

94457685056e.title: Ombrotrophic
94457685056e.sentence: High nitrogen deposition levels in Europe have led to changes in plant species composition in peatlands and tundra, with documented increases in vascular plant biomass and decreases in moss abundance, particularly the genus Sphagnum.

01038375e545.title: Ombrotrophic
01038375e545.sentence: This moss is critical in bogs for its ability to absorb and retain moisture and nutrients from the atmosphere, and to retard vascular plant growth, thus contributing to carbon sequestration.

47b0173cb8ea.title: Bog
47b0173cb8ea.sentence: A bog or bogland is a wetland that accumulates peat as a deposit of dead plant materials – often mosses, typically sphagnum moss.

d1f128139fb5.title: Bog
d1f128139fb5.sentence: It is one of the four main types of wetlands.

931adc79ab00.title: Bog
931adc79ab00.sentence: - Peat is present, usually thicker than 30 centimetres (12 in).

28a4187c556a.title: Bog
28a4187c556a.sentence: - The wetland receives most of its water and nutrients from precipitation (ombrotrophic) rather than surface or groundwater (minerotrophic).

a4f8af718681.title: Bog
a4f8af718681.sentence: - The wetland is strongly acidic (bogs near coastal areas may be less acidic due to sea spray).

e619f2ece6c8.title: Bog
e619f2ece6c8.sentence: In contrast to fens, they derive most of their water from precipitation rather than mineral-rich ground or surface water.

b4d561981bf3.title: Bog
b4d561981bf3.sentence: Because fens are supplied with mineral-rich water, they tend to range from slightly acidic to slightly basic, while bogs are always acidic because precipitation lacks the dissolved minerals (e.g. calcium, magnesium, carbonate) that act to buffer the natural acidity of atmospheric carbon dioxide.

3b993dcaf139.title: Bog
3b993dcaf139.sentence: In general, the low fertility and cool climate result in relatively slow plant growth, but decay is even slower due to low oxygen levels in saturated bog soils.

e91d7c5fb70f.title: Bog
e91d7c5fb70f.sentence: Large areas of the landscape can be covered many meters deep in peat.

7ad024547510.title: Bog
7ad024547510.sentence: They are generally found in cooler northern climates and are formed in poorly draining lake basins.

f95ba8b727c6.title: Bog
f95ba8b727c6.sentence: Bogs are widely distributed in cold, temperate climes, mostly in boreal ecosystems in the Northern Hemisphere.

7831cd1988fe.title: Bog
7831cd1988fe.section: Types > By location and water source > Valley bog
7831cd1988fe.sentence: These develop in gently sloping valleys or hollows.

2b20275cd239.title: Bog
2b20275cd239.section: Types > By location and water source > Valley bog
2b20275cd239.sentence: A layer of peat fills the deepest part of the valley, and a stream may run through the surface of the bog.

75213fb2ab92.title: Bog
75213fb2ab92.section: Types > By location and water source > Valley bog
75213fb2ab92.sentence: Valley bogs may develop in relatively dry and warm climates, but because they rely on ground or surface water, they only occur on acidic substrates.

e9346a1a36e3.title: Bog
e9346a1a36e3.section: Types > By location and water source > Quaking bog
e9346a1a36e3.sentence: A quaking bog, schwingmoor, or swingmoor is a form of floating bog occurring in wetter parts of valley bogs and raised bogs and sometimes around the edges of acidic lakes.

47cfc65a2db5.title: Bog
47cfc65a2db5.section: Types > By location and water source > Quaking bog
47cfc65a2db5.sentence: The bog vegetation, mostly sphagnum moss anchored by sedges (such as Carex lasiocarpa), forms a floating mat approximately half a meter thick on the surface of water or above very wet peat.

863b856f6b20.title: Bog
863b856f6b20.section: Types > By location and water source > Quaking bog
863b856f6b20.sentence: Walking on the surface causes it to move – larger movements may cause visible ripples on the surface, or they may even make trees sway.

34aededf6268.title: Bog
34aededf6268.sentence: The anaerobic environment and presence of tannic acids within bogs can result in the remarkable preservation of organic material.

5b548550a1d8.title: Bog
5b548550a1d8.sentence: This process happens because of the low oxygen levels of bogs in combination with the high acidity.

2fe1e1fd3bf6.title: Bog
2fe1e1fd3bf6.sentence: They have yielded extremely well-preserved bog bodies, with hair, organs, and skin intact, buried there thousands of years ago after apparent Germanic and Celtic human sacrifice.

a96a2e2b26f4.title: Bog
a96a2e2b26f4.sentence: Undisturbed, bogs function as a carbon sink.

fe80cf21106e.title: Bog
fe80cf21106e.sentence: Once the peat has been extracted it can be difficult to restore the wetland, since peat accumulation is a slow process.

8b23c397c890.title: Muskeg
8b23c397c890.sentence: Muskeg (Ojibwe: mashkiig; Cree: maskēk; French: fondrière de mousse, lit. moss bog) is a peat-forming ecosystem found in several northern climates, most commonly in Arctic and boreal areas.

6f2b2d7efc06.title: Muskeg
6f2b2d7efc06.sentence: Muskeg is approximately synonymous with bog or peatland, and is a standard term in Canada and Alaska.

139e36dabcb7.title: Muskeg
139e36dabcb7.sentence: The term became common in these areas because it is of Cree origin, maskēk (ᒪᐢᑫᐠ) meaning "low-lying marsh".

60ef62dc715c.title: Muskeg
60ef62dc715c.sentence: Muskeg consists of organic material in various states of decomposition (as peat), ranging from fairly intact sphagnum moss, to sedge peat, to highly decomposed humus.

8697e81f1b4f.title: Muskeg
8697e81f1b4f.sentence: Pieces of wood can make up five to fifteen percent of the peat soil.

bd255b099492.title: Muskeg
bd255b099492.sentence: Muskeg forms because permafrost, clay or bedrock prevents water drainage.

063219e8c1b5.title: Muskeg
063219e8c1b5.sentence: The water from rain and snow collects, forming permanently waterlogged vegetation and stagnant pools.

59e92eaa2cb6.title: Muskeg
59e92eaa2cb6.sentence: It needs two conditions to develop: abundant rain and cool summers.

5e7c8e2ddd11.title: Muskeg
5e7c8e2ddd11.sentence: If the same plant lands in water or on saturated soil, it decomposes differently.

aaa78acda34c.title: Muskeg
aaa78acda34c.sentence: Less oxygen is available under water, so aerobic bacteria and fungi fail to colonize the submerged debris effectively.

1130d975bfce.title: Muskeg
1130d975bfce.sentence: In addition, cool temperatures stunt bacterial and fungal growth.

bfb37a16e77c.title: Muskeg
bfb37a16e77c.sentence: This causes slow decomposition, and thus the plant debris gradually accumulates to form peat and eventually muskeg.

f22728a65d6a.title: Muskeg
f22728a65d6a.sentence: The sphagnum moss forming it can hold fifteen to thirty times its own weight in water, which allows the spongy wet muskeg to also form on sloping ground.

bed262c2afbd.title: Muskeg
bed262c2afbd.sentence: Depending on the underlying topography of the land, muskeg can reach depths greater than 30 metres (100 ft).

cf5b84e32ab9.title: Muskeg
cf5b84e32ab9.sentence: Muskeg is wet, acidic, and relatively infertile, which prevents large trees from growing, although stunted shore pine, cottonwood, some species of willow, and black spruce are typically found in these habitats.

dc83a53a9751.title: Muskeg
dc83a53a9751.sentence: The water table tends to be near the surface.

0bb19a64faa9.title: Muskeg
0bb19a64faa9.sentence: Muskeg can be a significant impediment to transportation.

b279bcde9b09.title: Muskeg
b279bcde9b09.sentence: Many other instances have been reported of heavy construction equipment vanishing into muskeg in the spring as the frozen muskeg beneath the vehicle thawed.

a1f3ddb385a7.title: Muskeg
a1f3ddb385a7.sentence: Construction in muskeg-laden areas sometimes requires the complete removal of the soil and filling with gravel.

6eb53633c90c.title: Muskeg
6eb53633c90c.sentence: If the muskeg is not completely cleared to bedrock, its high water content will cause buckling and distortion from winter freezing, much like permafrost.

31c1065bd021.title: Muskeg
31c1065bd021.sentence: One method of working atop muskeg is to place large logs on the ground, covered with a thick layer of clay or other stable material.

3d51dd5fd9b3.title: Muskeg
3d51dd5fd9b3.sentence: This is commonly called a corduroy road.

9987d44f5a60.title: Muskeg
9987d44f5a60.sentence: However temporary winter access roads on muskeg (ice road), created by clearing the insulating snow and allowing the muskeg to freeze, are more commonly used as they are cheaper to construct and easier to decommission.

b63a4d9a7c8c.title: Slump (geology)
b63a4d9a7c8c.sentence: A slump is a form of mass wasting that occurs when a coherent mass of loosely consolidated materials or a rock layer moves a short distance down a slope.

b5184cd413a5.title: Slump (geology)
b5184cd413a5.sentence: Movement is characterized by sliding along a concave-upward or planar surface.

7db73ad486d0.title: Slump (geology)
7db73ad486d0.sentence: Translational slumps occur when a detached landmass moves along a planar surface.

a5f715664f97.title: Slump (geology)
a5f715664f97.sentence: Common planar surfaces of failure include joints or bedding planes, especially where a permeable layer overrides an impermeable surface.

ab7cf5e381fd.title: Slump (geology)
ab7cf5e381fd.sentence: A rotational slump occurs when a slump block, composed of sediment or rock, slides along a concave-upward slip surface with rotation about an axis parallel to the slope.

01193318b6dd.title: Slump (geology)
01193318b6dd.sentence: Rotational movement causes the original surface of the block to become less steep, and the top of the slump is rotated backward.

259ffecbc7b2.title: Slump (geology)
259ffecbc7b2.sentence: The cut which forms as the landmass breaks away from the slope is called the scarp and is often cliff-like and concave.

5c7a76799a61.title: Slump (geology)
5c7a76799a61.sentence: The upper surface of the blocks are rotated backwards, forming depressions which may accumulate water to create ponds or swampy areas.

0f071d7d45ba.title: Slump (geology)
0f071d7d45ba.sentence: However, hummocky ridges may form near the toe of the slump.

23d5cfcc4f52.title: Slump (geology)
23d5cfcc4f52.sentence: Causes of slumping include earthquake shocks, thorough wetting, freezing and thawing, undercutting, and loading of a slope.

a7f26461bda7.title: Slump (geology)
a7f26461bda7.sentence: Slumps frequently form due to removal of a slope base, either from natural or manmade processes.

220e7db669a3.title: Slump (geology)
220e7db669a3.sentence: Stream or wave erosion, as well as road construction are common instigators for slumping.

cae4b9a72190.title: Slump (geology)
cae4b9a72190.sentence: Thorough wetting is a common cause, which explains why slumping is often associated with heavy rainfall, storm events and earthflows.

74db9caac4ad.title: Slump (geology)
74db9caac4ad.sentence: Rain provides lubrication for the material to slide, and increases the self-mass of the material.

1bac6f42547f.title: Slump (geology)
1bac6f42547f.sentence: Both factors increase the rate of slumping.

34060445b160.title: Slump (geology)
34060445b160.sentence: Addition of water and loss of sediment cohesion at the toe may transform slumping material into an earthflow.

7fef4ea357b8.title: Slump (geology)
7fef4ea357b8.sentence: The speed of slump varies widely, ranging from meters per second, to meters per year.

3ac9ff2e0515.title: Slump (geology)
3ac9ff2e0515.sentence: Sudden slumps usually occur after earthquakes or heavy continuing rains, and can stabilize within a few hours.

f8f156cdc305.title: Slump (geology)
f8f156cdc305.sentence: Most slumps develop over comparatively longer periods, taking months or years to reach stability.

66485686d775.title: Erosion
66485686d775.sentence: Slumping happens on steep hillsides, occurring along distinct fracture zones, often within materials like clay that, once released, may move quite rapidly downhill.

ba3c74257116.title: Soil erosion
ba3c74257116.sentence: Much of this erosion occurs as the weakened banks fail in large slumps.

45de8bcffd11.title: Polder
45de8bcffd11.sentence: A polder (Dutch pronunciation: [ˈpɔldər] ⓘ) is a low-lying tract of land that forms an artificial hydrological entity, enclosed by embankments known as dikes.

03bfe0356b62.title: Polder
03bfe0356b62.sentence: The three types of polder are:

847a666d1b3f.title: Polder
847a666d1b3f.sentence: - Land reclaimed from a body of water, such as a lake or the seabed

78d1c2607f4e.title: Polder
78d1c2607f4e.sentence: - Flood plains separated from the sea or river by a dike

4b0df0c2ae70.title: Polder
4b0df0c2ae70.sentence: - Marshes separated from the surrounding water by a dike and subsequently drained; these are also known as koogs, especially in Germany

cd0a85dcbe6c.title: Polder
cd0a85dcbe6c.sentence: Water enters the low-lying polder through infiltration and water pressure of groundwater, or rainfall, or transport of water by rivers and canals.

f5c0d1aa477f.title: Polder
f5c0d1aa477f.sentence: This usually means that the polder has an excess of water, which is pumped out or drained by opening sluices at low tide.

47fc259cb738.title: Polder
47fc259cb738.sentence: The ground level in drained marshes subsides over time.

ad43e9b2f15f.title: Polder
ad43e9b2f15f.sentence: Polder land made up of peat (former marshland) will sink in relation to its previous level, because of peat decomposing when exposed to oxygen from the air.

3a469f7d32ff.title: Polder
3a469f7d32ff.sentence: All polders will eventually be below the surrounding water level some or all of the time.

a5b21c73e417.title: Polder
a5b21c73e417.sentence: Polders are most commonly, though not exclusively, found in river deltas, former fenlands, and coastal areas.

67ee519e23a0.title: Polder
67ee519e23a0.sentence: Polders are at risk of flooding at all times, and care must be taken to protect the surrounding dikes.

ecd94caff349.title: Polder
ecd94caff349.sentence: Dikes are typically built with locally available materials, and each material has its own risks: sand is prone to collapse owing to saturation by water; dry peat is lighter than water and potentially unable to retain water in very dry seasons.

e654346d633d.title: Marsh
e654346d633d.sentence: Large tracts of tidal marsh have been embanked and artificially drained.

4707970d334d.title: Marsh
4707970d334d.sentence: They are usually known by the Dutch name of polders.

be49531c50b0.title: Marsh
be49531c50b0.sentence: In Northern Germany and Scandinavia they are called Marschland, Marsch or marsk; in France marais maritime.

44e9693c9d90.title: Marsh
44e9693c9d90.sentence: In the Netherlands and Belgium, they are designated as marine clay districts.

adb7fee986da.title: Polder
adb7fee986da.sentence: The Dutch have a long history of reclamation of marshes and fenland, resulting in some 3,000 polders nationwide.

09be4b8a616b.title: Polder
09be4b8a616b.sentence: The Netherlands has a large area of polders: as much as 20% of the land area has at some point in the past been reclaimed from the sea.

c99f588d10c4.title: Soil structure
c99f588d10c4.sentence: The penetration of burrowing earthworms in areas deprived of them (e.g. in recent polders) has been observed to improve soil structure.

9859e6d68b9b.title: Polder
9859e6d68b9b.sentence: The first polders were constructed in the 11th century.

bc0fcf54a64e.title: Polder
bc0fcf54a64e.sentence: The oldest extant polder is the Achtermeer polder, from 1533.

6a6ee262190d.title: Riparian zone
6a6ee262190d.sentence: A riparian zone or riparian area is the interface between land and a river or stream.

e39f23ee752c.title: Riparian zone
e39f23ee752c.sentence: Plant habitats and communities along the river margins and banks are called riparian vegetation, characterized by hydrophilic plants.

a5a60069cd28.title: Riparian zone
a5a60069cd28.sentence: Riparian zones are important in ecology, environmental resource management, and civil engineering because of their role in soil conservation, their habitat biodiversity, and the influence they have on terrestrial and semiaquatic fauna as well as aquatic ecosystems, including grasslands, woodlands, wetlands, and even non-vegetative areas.

34a56d331ebb.title: Riparian zone
34a56d331ebb.sentence: These zones are important natural biofilters, protecting aquatic environments from excessive sedimentation, polluted surface runoff, and erosion.

a1d19dbbc9e7.title: Riparian zone
a1d19dbbc9e7.sentence: The meandering curves of a river, combined with vegetation and root systems, slow the flow of water, which reduces soil erosion and flood damage.

578fc59fb879.title: Riparian zone
578fc59fb879.sentence: Sediment is trapped, reducing suspended solids to create less turbid water, replenish soils, and build stream banks.

516c93da7ab0.title: Riparian zone
