516c93da7ab0.sentence: Riparian zones can play a role in lowering nitrate contamination in surface runoff, such as manure and other fertilizers from agricultural fields, that would otherwise damage ecosystems and human health.

79c2a2828197.title: Riparian zone
79c2a2828197.sentence: Particularly, the attenuation of nitrate or denitrification of the nitrates from fertilizer in this buffer zone is important.

97f6a23fce0b.title: Riparian zone
97f6a23fce0b.sentence: The use of wetland riparian zones shows a particularly high rate of removal of nitrate entering a stream and thus has a place in agricultural management.

b7d9ab7d56c6.title: Riparian zone
b7d9ab7d56c6.sentence: If the area adjacent to a watercourse has standing water or saturated soil for as long as a season, it is normally termed a wetland because of its hydric soil characteristics.

ab5d18176bf0.title: Riparian zone
ab5d18176bf0.sentence: The vegetation surrounding the stream helps to shade the water, mitigating water temperature changes.

623066b71a63.title: Riparian zone
623066b71a63.sentence: Thinning of riparian zones has been observed to cause increased maximum temperatures, higher fluctuations in temperature, and elevated temperatures being observed more frequently and for longer periods of time.

afac52d0db38.title: Riparian zone
afac52d0db38.sentence: When riparian zones are damaged by construction, agriculture or silviculture, biological restoration can take place, usually by human intervention in erosion control and revegetation.

4ee5ec9df290.title: Minerotrophic
4ee5ec9df290.sentence: Minerotrophic refers to environments that receive nutrients primarily through groundwater that flows through mineral-rich soils or rock, or surface water flowing over land.

48c782d10a7d.title: Minerotrophic
48c782d10a7d.sentence: The hydrologic process behind minerotrophic wetlands results in water that has acquired dissolved chemicals which raise the nutrient levels and reduce the acidity.

e15e6f17aeec.title: Minerotrophic
e15e6f17aeec.sentence: If dissolved chemicals include chemical bases such as calcium or magnesium ions, the water is referred to as base-rich and is neutral or alkaline.

6ef0856b11c7.title: Minerotrophic
6ef0856b11c7.sentence: Of the various wetland types, fens and rich fens are often minerotrophic while poor fens and bogs are often ombrotrophic.

db3425cf6808.title: Minerotrophic
db3425cf6808.sentence: Marshes and swamps may also be fed through groundwater sources to a degree.

748714d774f5.title: Minerotrophic
748714d774f5.sentence: Chemical ions are transported to wetlands via their hydrological system, and in turn affect pH, conductivity, and nutrient levels.

cbf5e86d14f1.title: Minerotrophic
cbf5e86d14f1.sentence: Chemical and nutrient dynamics may differ depending on a minerotrophic wetland’s hydrological setting, which could include water discharge dominated, recharge dominated, or some combination of both.

e67096311434.title: Minerotrophic
e67096311434.sentence: These characteristics also vary seasonally, as average groundwater levels increase and decrease at different times of the year.

6822fb8c5c9f.title: Minerotrophic
6822fb8c5c9f.sentence: Additional factors such as geological conditions, soil type, and surface morphology may also influence the characteristics of a wetland in tandem with hydrological setting.

8e05d6ab455a.title: Minerotrophic
8e05d6ab455a.sentence: Stable water and nutrient availability via groundwater systems allows for a diverse array of plant species to grow in minerotrophic wetlands.

41451b00a5a7.title: Minerotrophic
41451b00a5a7.sentence: This also allows for peat to accumulate provided the water does not flow too quickly.

4b8192da6c66.title: Minerotrophic
4b8192da6c66.sentence: Minerotrophic, “minerogenous”, and “geogenous” are now often used interchangeably, although the latter two terms refer primarily to hydrological systems, while the former refers to nutrient dynamics.

6e24c61c8881.title: Fen
6e24c61c8881.sentence: A fen is a type of peat-accumulating wetland fed by mineral-rich ground or surface water.

6b041330e86e.title: Fen
6b041330e86e.sentence: It is one of the main types of wetland along with marshes, swamps, and bogs.

49b3b1e982c7.title: Fen
49b3b1e982c7.sentence: Bogs and fens, both peat-forming ecosystems, are also known as mires.

cbfb475e099a.title: Fen
cbfb475e099a.sentence: The unique water chemistry of fens is a result of the ground or surface water input.

824a1c48c00c.title: Fen
824a1c48c00c.sentence: Typically, this input results in higher mineral concentrations and a more basic pH than found in bogs.

d8bb038d5d9f.title: Fen
d8bb038d5d9f.sentence: Fen soils are constantly inundated because the water table is at or near the surface.

45b8eb96db34.title: Fen
45b8eb96db34.sentence: The result is anaerobic (oxygen-free) soils due to the slow rate at which oxygen diffuses into waterlogged soil.

539d7e273e64.title: Fen
539d7e273e64.sentence: Groundwater chemistry, in turn, is largely determined by the geology of the rocks that the groundwater flows through.

142b464fc0ee.title: Fen
142b464fc0ee.sentence: Thus, the characteristics of a fen, especially its pH, are directly influenced by the type of rocks its groundwater supply contacts. pH is a major factor in determining fen species composition and richness, with more basic fens called "rich" and more acidic fens called "poor." Rich fens tend to be highly biodiverse and harbor a number of rare or endangered species, and biodiversity tends to decrease as the richness of fen decreases.

e87865a16dcd.title: Fen
e87865a16dcd.sentence: Fens tend to be found above rocks that are rich in calcium, such as limestone.

f3328f46b77b.title: Fen
f3328f46b77b.sentence: As peat accumulates in a fen, groundwater input can be reduced or cut off, making the fen ombrotrophic rather than minerotrophic.

5d3af0fd637d.title: Fen
5d3af0fd637d.sentence: In this way, fens can become more acidic and transition to bogs over time.

4c3cdca0ffc6.title: Fen
4c3cdca0ffc6.sentence: Locally, fens are most often found at the intersection of terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems, such as the headwaters of streams and rivers.

358dbd636b94.title: Fen
358dbd636b94.sentence: It is estimated that there are approximately 1.1 million square kilometers of fens worldwide, but quantifying the extent of fens is difficult.

32ea2965be67.title: Fen
32ea2965be67.section: Threats and conservation > Threats to fens
32ea2965be67.sentence: Draining a fen directly is particularly damaging because it lowers the water table.

88867483cce5.title: Fen
88867483cce5.section: Threats and conservation > Threats to fens
88867483cce5.sentence: A lower water table can increase aeration and dry out peat, allowing for aerobic decomposition or burning of the organic matter in peat.

17f663640b2f.title: Fen
17f663640b2f.section: Threats and conservation > Threats to fens
17f663640b2f.sentence: Disrupting groundwater flow into the fen with nearby human activities such as quarrying or residential development can alter water and nutrient inputs to the fen.

7115f05a990b.title: Fen
7115f05a990b.section: Threats and conservation > Threats to fens
7115f05a990b.sentence: This can make the fen more ombrotrophic (dependent on precipitation), which results in acidification and a change in water chemistry.

fdb470f6a70d.title: Geomorphology
fdb470f6a70d.sentence: Geomorphology (from Ancient Greek γῆ (gê) 'earth', μορφή (morphḗ) 'form' and λόγος (lógos) 'study') is the scientific study of the origin and evolution of topographic and bathymetric features generated by physical, chemical or biological processes operating at or near Earth's surface.

38157bd8769b.title: Geomorphology
38157bd8769b.sentence: Surface processes comprise the action of water, wind, ice, wildfire, and life on the surface of the Earth, along with chemical reactions that form soils and alter material properties, the stability and rate of change of topography under the force of gravity, and other factors, such as (in the very recent past) human alteration of the landscape.

d6c53d38de59.title: Geomorphology
d6c53d38de59.sentence: On progressively smaller scales, similar ideas apply, where individual landforms evolve in response to the balance of additive processes (uplift and deposition) and subtractive processes (subsidence and erosion).

c84fde3c270c.title: Geomorphology
c84fde3c270c.sentence: Geomorphically relevant processes generally fall into (1) the production of regolith by weathering and erosion, (2) the transport of that material, and (3) its eventual deposition.

9fd54ddac4ac.title: Geomorphology
9fd54ddac4ac.sentence: Soil geomorphologists investigate soil profiles and chemistry to learn about the history of a particular landscape and understand how climate, biota, and rock interact.

bcf37cee609a.title: Geomorphology
bcf37cee609a.sentence: Soil, regolith, and rock move downslope under the force of gravity via creep, slides, flows, topples, and falls.

45163e45cad0.title: Geomorphology
45163e45cad0.sentence: On the Earth, biological processes such as burrowing or tree throw may play important roles in setting the rates of some hillslope processes.

af599c92535b.title: Geomorphology
af599c92535b.sentence: Weathering is the chemical and physical disruption of earth materials in place on exposure to atmospheric or near surface agents, and is typically studied by soil scientists and environmental chemists, but is an essential component of geomorphology because it is what provides the material that can be moved in the first place.

70da2df9dc1d.title: Geomorphology
70da2df9dc1d.sentence: Practical applications of geomorphology include hazard assessment (such as landslide prediction and mitigation), river control and stream restoration, and coastal protection.

072359303be9.title: Freshwater marsh
072359303be9.sentence: A freshwater marsh is a non-forested marsh wetland that contains shallow fresh water, and is continuously or frequently flooded.

af72f78759cc.title: Freshwater marsh
af72f78759cc.sentence: Freshwater marshes are usually found near the mouths of rivers, along lakes, or are present in low-lying areas with low drainage like abandoned oxbow lakes.

415f262e3ac3.title: Freshwater marsh
415f262e3ac3.sentence: Unlike its counterpart the salt marsh, which is regularly flushed with sea water, freshwater marshes receive the majority of their water from surface water.

f2ad1e56b421.title: Freshwater marsh
f2ad1e56b421.sentence: The soils in freshwater marshes have high organic matter due to slow decomposition rates and are often black or brown.

80105fa669ec.title: Freshwater marsh
80105fa669ec.sentence: The anaerobic conditions of the soils are caused by microbial activity that deplete oxygen, which are then reverted to anaerobic processes that accumulate or deplete reduced iron and other minerals creating distinct soil morphology characteristics.

775e4cf7ced4.title: Freshwater marsh
775e4cf7ced4.sentence: Freshwater marshes can be broken into several types including river marshes, lacustrine (lake), tidal freshwater, and palustrine depressional.

c68027574494.title: Freshwater marsh
c68027574494.section: Types of freshwater marshes > Palustrine depressional
c68027574494.sentence: Palustrine depressional marshes, sometimes also called basin or slope marshes, occur in hydrologically isolated areas such as a depression or on a hill slope.

7a80b4e62728.title: Freshwater marsh
7a80b4e62728.section: Types of freshwater marshes > Palustrine depressional
7a80b4e62728.sentence: These marshes are not connected to rivers, lakes or oceans, but can be and frequently are fed by groundwater springs or seepages.

7841debdd8b1.title: Fen
7841debdd8b1.sentence: Bogs and fens can be thought of as two ecosystems on a gradient from poor to rich, with bogs at the poor end, extremely rich fens at the rich end, and poor fens in between.

c265bba02bb0.title: Fen
c265bba02bb0.sentence: In this context, "rich" and "poor" refer to the species richness, or how biodiverse a fen or bog is.

80cc611052e5.title: Fen
80cc611052e5.sentence: The richness of these species is strongly influenced by pH and concentrations of calcium and bicarbonate.

a6c150c2dc21.title: Fen
a6c150c2dc21.section: Hydrology and biogeochemistry > Bog–rich-fen gradient > Rich fens
a6c150c2dc21.sentence: Rich fens are strongly minerotrophic; that is, a large proportion of their water comes from mineral-rich ground or surface water.

a05b827cabcb.title: Fen
a05b827cabcb.section: Hydrology and biogeochemistry > Bog–rich-fen gradient > Rich fens
a05b827cabcb.sentence: This water is dominated by calcium and bicarbonate, resulting in a slightly acidic to slightly basic pH characteristic of rich fens.

6b4090bcdad1.title: Fen
6b4090bcdad1.section: Hydrology and biogeochemistry > Bog–rich-fen gradient > Rich fens
6b4090bcdad1.sentence: Rich and intermediate rich fens are generally neutral to slightly acidic, with a pH of approximately 7 to 5.

b4f26e9a8b91.title: Fen
b4f26e9a8b91.sentence: When groundwater flows past calcareous (calcium-rich) rocks like limestone (calcium carbonate), a small amount dissolves and is carried to the fen supplied by the groundwater.

b2858e3a6bb1.title: Fen
b2858e3a6bb1.sentence: When calcium carbonate dissolves, it produces bicarbonate and a calcium cation according to the following equilibrium:

cbfabfe1d620.title: Fen
cbfabfe1d620.section: Hydrology and biogeochemistry > Bog–rich-fen gradient > Rich fens
cbfabfe1d620.sentence: The richest fens are the extreme rich (marl) fens, where marl deposits are often build up.

a75c19a55c58.title: Fen
a75c19a55c58.section: Hydrology and biogeochemistry > Bog–rich-fen gradient > Rich fens
a75c19a55c58.sentence: These are often pH 7 or greater.

b2d647e74521.title: Fen
b2d647e74521.sentence: Calcium carbonate precipitates out of solution when the partial pressure of carbon dioxide in the solution falls.

ec067d325d2e.title: Fen
ec067d325d2e.sentence: The decrease in carbon dioxide partial pressure is caused by uptake by plants for photosynthesis or direct loss to the atmosphere.

ab8122b2b780.title: Fen
ab8122b2b780.section: Hydrology and biogeochemistry > Bog–rich-fen gradient > Rich fens
ab8122b2b780.sentence: Rich fens are not always very productive; at high calcium concentrations, calcium ions bind to phosphate anions, reducing the availability of phosphorus and decreasing primary production.

543fe53e4b93.title: Fen
543fe53e4b93.section: Hydrology and biogeochemistry > Bog–rich-fen gradient > Poor fens
543fe53e4b93.sentence: They are much more acidic than their rich counterparts, with a pH of approximately 5.5 to 4.

e83200e9a2cf.title: Fen
e83200e9a2cf.section: Hydrology and biogeochemistry > Bog–rich-fen gradient > Poor fens
e83200e9a2cf.sentence: Peat in poor fens tends to be thicker than that of rich fens, which cuts off vegetation access to the mineral-rich soil underneath.

b3af34febed6.title: Fen
b3af34febed6.section: Hydrology and biogeochemistry > Bog–rich-fen gradient > Poor fens
b3af34febed6.sentence: In addition, the thicker peat reduces the influence of mineral-rich groundwater that buffers the pH.

cbb902eb5012.title: Fen
cbb902eb5012.section: Hydrology and biogeochemistry > Bog–rich-fen gradient > Poor fens
cbb902eb5012.sentence: This makes the fen more ombrotrophic, or dependent on nutrient-poor precipitation for its water and nutrients.

2bf91fa3cd91.title: Fen
2bf91fa3cd91.section: Hydrology and biogeochemistry > Bog–rich-fen gradient > Poor fens
2bf91fa3cd91.sentence: Poor fens may also form in areas where the groundwater supplying the fen flows through sediments that don't dissolve well or have low buffering capacity when dissolved.

9e3aa1808b14.title: Fen
9e3aa1808b14.sentence: The same effect is observed when groundwater flows through minerals with low solubility, such as sand.

2a6df6bf37e1.title: Fen
2a6df6bf37e1.section: Hydrology and biogeochemistry > Bog–rich-fen gradient > Poor fens
2a6df6bf37e1.sentence: Poor fens, like bogs, are dominated by Sphagnum mosses, which acidify the fen and decrease nutrient availability.

5f315438c4eb.title: Fen
5f315438c4eb.section: Hydrology and biogeochemistry > Bog–rich-fen gradient > Rich fens
5f315438c4eb.sentence: However, an accumulation of mosses such as Sphagnum can lead to the acidification of the rich fen, potentially converting it into a poor fen.

7efb1887de80.title: Fen
7efb1887de80.sentence: Like all wetlands, they play an important role in nutrient cycling because they are located at the interface of aerobic (oxic) and anaerobic (anoxic) environments.

1b6c5778b2de.title: Fen
1b6c5778b2de.sentence: Most wetlands have a thin top layer of oxygenated soil in contact with the atmosphere or oxygenated surface waters.

20491b46c9ae.title: Fen
20491b46c9ae.sentence: Nutrients and minerals may cycle between this oxidized top layer and the reduced layer below, undergoing oxidation and reduction reactions by the microbial communities adapted to each layer.

cdef26c01d75.title: Fen
cdef26c01d75.sentence: Many important reactions take place in the reduced layer, including denitrification, manganese reduction, iron reduction, sulfate reduction, and methanogenesis.

c45aea049aa8.title: Fen
c45aea049aa8.section: Hydrology and biogeochemistry > Nutrient cycling > Carbon
c45aea049aa8.sentence: Once in the wetland, organic carbon generally has three main fates: oxidation to CO2 by aerobic respiration, burial as organic matter in peat, or decomposition to methane.

92603597b6a7.title: Fen
92603597b6a7.section: Hydrology and biogeochemistry > Nutrient cycling > Carbon
92603597b6a7.sentence: In peatlands, including fens, primary production by plants is greater than decomposition, which results in the accumulation of organic matter as peat.

018e97c03bfb.title: Fen
018e97c03bfb.section: Hydrology and biogeochemistry > Nutrient cycling > Carbon
018e97c03bfb.sentence: Peatlands dominated by brown mosses and sedges such as fens have been found to emit a greater amount of methane than Sphagnum-dominated peatlands such as bogs.

ab357d269bf4.title: Fen
ab357d269bf4.section: Hydrology and biogeochemistry > Nutrient cycling > Nitrogen
ab357d269bf4.sentence: In the oxidized surface layer of the wetland, this ammonium is oxidized to nitrite and nitrate by nitrification.

7a950affb260.title: Fen
7a950affb260.section: Hydrology and biogeochemistry > Nutrient cycling > Nitrogen
7a950affb260.sentence: The production of ammonium in the reduced layer and its consumption in the top oxidized layer drives upward diffusion of ammonium.

03936d787170.title: Fen
03936d787170.section: Hydrology and biogeochemistry > Nutrient cycling > Nitrogen
03936d787170.sentence: Likewise, nitrate production in the oxidized layer and nitrate consumption in the reduced layer by denitrification drives downward diffusion of nitrate.

bc830118b7e6.title: Fen
bc830118b7e6.section: Hydrology and biogeochemistry > Nutrient cycling > Nitrogen
bc830118b7e6.sentence: Denitrification in the reduced layer produces nitrogen gas and some nitrous oxide, which then exit the wetland to the atmosphere.

c01d7adab75d.title: Fen
c01d7adab75d.section: Hydrology and biogeochemistry > Nutrient cycling > Nitrogen
c01d7adab75d.sentence: Nitrogen, along with phosphorus, controls how fertile a wetland is.

de10715736c9.title: Fen
de10715736c9.section: Hydrology and biogeochemistry > Nutrient cycling > Phosphorus
de10715736c9.sentence: Almost all of the phosphorus that arrives in a wetland does so through sediments or plant litter from other ecosystems.

7d292f90d466.title: Fen
7d292f90d466.section: Hydrology and biogeochemistry > Nutrient cycling > Phosphorus
7d292f90d466.sentence: Iron can bind to high levels of inorganic phosphate within the fen, leading to a toxic environment and inhibition of plant growth.

b4e65fd2a9aa.title: Fen
b4e65fd2a9aa.section: Hydrology and biogeochemistry > Nutrient cycling > Phosphorus
b4e65fd2a9aa.sentence: Peat soils play a role in preventing the bonding of irons to phosphate by providing high levels of organic anions for iron to bind to instead of inorganic anions such as phosphate.

9ee8bfcc199d.title: Fen
9ee8bfcc199d.sentence: Because wetlands are hotspots for nutrient transformations and often serve as nutrient sinks, they may be constructed to treat nutrient-rich waters created by human activities.

69a7bc81c656.title: Peatland
69a7bc81c656.sentence: Peatlands are the largest natural carbon store on land.

aab06bdb534a.title: Peatland
aab06bdb534a.section: Biochemical processes > Carbon storage and methanogenesis
aab06bdb534a.sentence: Despite accounting for just 3% of Earth's land surfaces, peatlands are collectively a major carbon store containing between 500 and 700 billion tonnes of carbon.

1657324a4d1b.title: Peatland
1657324a4d1b.section: Biochemical processes > Carbon storage and methanogenesis
1657324a4d1b.sentence: Carbon stored within peatlands equates to over half the amount of carbon found in the atmosphere.

c73604715ede.title: Peatland
c73604715ede.section: Biochemical processes > Carbon storage and methanogenesis
c73604715ede.sentence: The sequestration of carbon dioxide takes place at the surface via the process of photosynthesis, while losses of carbon dioxide occur through living plants via autotrophic respiration and from the litter and peat via heterotrophic respiration.

131668c14a21.title: Peatland
131668c14a21.section: Biochemical processes > Carbon storage and methanogenesis
131668c14a21.sentence: In their natural state, mires are a small atmospheric carbon dioxide sink through the photosynthesis of peat vegetation, which outweighs their release of greenhouse gases.

7cc6ae2ff1f9.title: Peatland
7cc6ae2ff1f9.section: Biochemical processes > Carbon storage and methanogenesis
7cc6ae2ff1f9.sentence: On the other hand, most mires are generally net emitters of methane and nitrous oxide.

7ff864bffffe.title: Peatland
7ff864bffffe.section: Biochemical processes > Carbon storage and methanogenesis
7ff864bffffe.sentence: Due to the continued CO2 sequestration over millennia, and because of the longer atmospheric lifespan of the CO2 molecules compared with methane and nitrous oxide, peatlands have had a net cooling effect on the atmosphere.

39748d3bfe9a.title: Peatland
39748d3bfe9a.section: Biochemical processes > Carbon storage and methanogenesis
39748d3bfe9a.sentence: The water table position of a peatland is the main control of its carbon release to the atmosphere.

163b48dd5789.title: Peatland
163b48dd5789.section: Biochemical processes > Carbon storage and methanogenesis
163b48dd5789.sentence: When the water table rises after a rainstorm, the peat and its microbes are submerged under water inhibiting access to oxygen, reducing CO2 release via respiration.

a15155f9e39c.title: Peatland
a15155f9e39c.section: Biochemical processes > Carbon storage and methanogenesis
a15155f9e39c.sentence: Carbon dioxide release increases when the water table falls lower, such as during a drought, as this increases the availability of oxygen to the aerobic microbes thus accelerating peat decomposition.

9f669df4eb90.title: Peatland
9f669df4eb90.section: Biochemical processes > Carbon storage and methanogenesis
9f669df4eb90.sentence: Methanogens are strictly anaerobic organisms and produce methane from organic matter in anoxic conditions below the water table level, while some of that methane is oxidised by methanotrophs above the water table level.

53d3064f2866.title: Peatland
53d3064f2866.section: Biochemical processes > Carbon storage and methanogenesis
53d3064f2866.sentence: Therefore, changes in water table level influence the size of these methane production and consumption zones.

6cb7b523f940.title: Peatland
6cb7b523f940.section: Biochemical processes > Carbon storage and methanogenesis
6cb7b523f940.sentence: Increased soil temperatures also contribute to increased seasonal methane flux.

c35f4482f189.title: Peatland
c35f4482f189.section: Biochemical processes > Carbon storage and methanogenesis
c35f4482f189.sentence: A study in Alaska found that methane may vary by as much as 300% seasonally with wetter and warmer soil conditions due to climate change.

f0a69451c543.title: Peatland
f0a69451c543.section: Impacts on global climate > Drainage for agriculture and forestry
f0a69451c543.sentence: By allowing oxygen to enter the peat column within a mire, drainage disrupts the balance between peat accumulation and decomposition, and the subsequent oxidative degradation results in the release of carbon into the atmosphere.

9fcb1d8f1647.title: Peatland
9fcb1d8f1647.section: Impacts on global climate > Drainage for agriculture and forestry
9fcb1d8f1647.sentence: As such, drainage of mires for agriculture transforms them from net carbon sinks to net carbon emitters.

a0e9efc7b0af.title: Peatland
a0e9efc7b0af.sentence: Northern peatlands were mostly built up during the Holocene after the retreat of Pleistocene glaciers, but in contrast tropical peatlands are much older.

34ca5dac5e2b.title: Peatland
34ca5dac5e2b.sentence: Total northern peat carbon stocks are estimated to be 1055 Gt C.

d025ece2a544.title: Raised bog
d025ece2a544.sentence: Raised bogs, also called ombrotrophic bogs, are acidic, wet habitats that are poor in mineral salts and are home to flora and fauna that can cope with such extreme conditions.

35084971e608.title: Raised bog
35084971e608.sentence: Raised bogs, unlike fens, are exclusively fed by precipitation (ombrotrophy) and from mineral salts introduced from the air.

6f4d887cb598.title: Raised bog
6f4d887cb598.sentence: Thus the bog rises slowly above the groundwater level, hence its name.

a1d023ecbd1b.title: Raised bog
a1d023ecbd1b.sentence: At first, fens emerged under the influence of groundwater (minerotrophy).

2bc7299a59d0.title: Raised bog
2bc7299a59d0.sentence: Oxygen deficiencies and high acidity in the constantly moist substrate inhibited the decomposition of dead plant parts and led to peat formation.

cf35ac04d8a4.title: Raised bog
cf35ac04d8a4.sentence: It becomes fed solely by rainwater, which is low in mineral salts, and has no access to salts in the groundwater.

1bea289e9874.title: Raised bog
1bea289e9874.sentence: By contrast, mire-formed raised bogs are created directly on the mineral substrate of low-salt areas without having been initially formed as fens (see figure on the left in the sequence).

5884ef11474e.title: Raised bog
5884ef11474e.sentence: The quantity of precipitation has to be greater than the water losses through discharge and evaporation.

ceb307a983d6.title: Raised bog
ceb307a983d6.sentence: In addition, the precipitation must be evenly spread through the year.

2268742e78ef.title: Raised bog
2268742e78ef.sentence: Raised bogs in Europe have been developing for about 11,000 years, since the beginning of the Holocene and after the retreat of the last ice sheet.

ebb8ddd93b33.title: Raised bog
ebb8ddd93b33.sentence: The main constituents of the peat are rootless peat mosses that grow slowly in height whilst at the same time the lower layer becomes peat as air is excluded.

9309193ca6aa.title: Raised bog
9309193ca6aa.sentence: The peat layer grows about a millimetre per year.

2a076225f142.title: Raised bog
2a076225f142.sentence: The 'acrotelm' (Greek: akros = highest; telma = bog) is the upper part and includes the vegetation layer and the bog 'floor'.

dfb9f6624432.title: Raised bog
dfb9f6624432.sentence: The "catotelm" (Greek: kato = below) is the underlying water-saturated part with less biological activity.

ee48eb8f24ef.title: Raised bog
ee48eb8f24ef.sentence: In raised bogs, the upper peat layer is called white peat, since it consists of largely undecomposed light brown peat mosses.

7ccc86fce6d8.title: Raised bog
7ccc86fce6d8.sentence: The lower layer is black peat, which is already well humified and has a black-brown colour with still recognizable plant remains.

48f2f433be03.title: Bog
48f2f433be03.section: Types > By location and water source > Raised bog
48f2f433be03.sentence: The dome is typically a few meters high in the center and is often surrounded by strips of fen or other wetland vegetation at the edges or along streamsides where groundwater can percolate into the wetland.

a17cda3f415e.title: Bog
a17cda3f415e.section: Types > By location and water source > Raised bog
a17cda3f415e.sentence: The various types of raised bog may be divided into:

0bd4d354c125.title: Bog
0bd4d354c125.section: Types > By location and water source > Raised bog

3161b98ef583.title: Bog
3161b98ef583.section: Types > By location and water source > Raised bog

6d8efff54d66.title: Bog
6d8efff54d66.section: Types > By location and water source > Raised bog

c7f1f560a234.title: Bog
c7f1f560a234.section: Types > By location and water source > Raised bog

1d35a44f0610.title: Bog
1d35a44f0610.section: Types > By location and water source > Raised bog

d82d0b279593.title: Raised bog
d82d0b279593.sentence: Raised bogs are very threatened by peat cutting and pollution by mineral salts from the surrounding land (due to agriculture and industry).

744e0a4b1ac5.title: Raised bog
744e0a4b1ac5.sentence: The last great raised bog regions are found in western Siberia and Canada.

8420776eaa6e.title: Alluvial fan
8420776eaa6e.sentence: An alluvial fan is an accumulation of sediments that fans outwards from a concentrated source of sediments, such as a narrow canyon emerging from an escarpment.

949a4d160b9c.title: Alluvial fan
949a4d160b9c.sentence: This accumulation is shaped like a section of a shallow cone, with its apex at the source of sediments.

50dabfeed4bf.title: Alluvial fan
50dabfeed4bf.sentence: Alluvial fans typically form where a flow of sediment or rocks emerge from a confined channel and are suddenly free to spread out in many directions.

4d450ad465da.title: Alluvial fan
4d450ad465da.sentence: The transition from a narrow channel to a wide open area reduces the carrying capacity of flow and results in deposition of sediments.

f8921d2732ce.title: Alluvial fan
f8921d2732ce.sentence: They range in area from less than 1 square kilometer (0.4 sq mi) to almost 20,000 square kilometers (7,700 sq mi).

ad269376c7f5.title: Alluvial fan
ad269376c7f5.sentence: Alluvial fans vary greatly in size, from only a few meters across at the base to as much as 150 kilometers across, with a slope of 1.5 to 25 degrees.

5747e4f7a6d9.title: Alluvial fan
5747e4f7a6d9.sentence: The slope measured from the apex is generally concave, with the steepest slope near the apex (the proximal fan or fanhead) and becoming less steep further out (the medial fan or midfan) and shallowing at the edges of the fan (the distal fan or outer fan).

6db3824fd370.title: Alluvial fan
6db3824fd370.sentence: The sediments in an alluvial fan are usually coarse and poorly sorted, with the coarsest sediments found on the proximal fan.

25ecc9417566.title: Alluvial fan
25ecc9417566.sentence: Alluvial fans are characterized by coarse sedimentation, though the sediments making up the fan become less coarse further from the apex.

f4a95d1f1fa4.title: Alluvial fan
f4a95d1f1fa4.sentence: This channel is subject to blockage by accumulated sediments or debris flows, which causes flow to periodically break out of its old channel (nodal avulsion) and shift to a part of the fan with a steeper gradient, where deposition resumes.

8ff0be6639a9.title: Alluvial fan
8ff0be6639a9.sentence: As a result, normally only part of the fan is active at any particular time, and the bypassed areas may undergo soil formation or erosion.

da2731406e3c.title: Alluvial fan
da2731406e3c.sentence: Usually only one lobe is active at a time, and inactive lobes may develop desert varnish or develop a soil profile from eolian dust deposition, on time scales of 1,000 to 10,000 years.

a40cb59a1f33.title: Alluvial fan
a40cb59a1f33.sentence: Alluvial fans can be dominated by debris flows (debris flow fans) or stream flow (fluvial fans).

3014dd4042d0.title: Alluvial fan
3014dd4042d0.sentence: These may include hyperconcentrated flows containing 20% to 45% sediments, which are intermediate between sheetfloods having 20% or less of sediments and debris flows with more than 45% sediments.

c0685390fa66.title: Alluvial fan
c0685390fa66.sentence: The beds of coarse sediments associated with alluvial fans form aquifers that are the most important groundwater reservoirs in many regions.

258aeb59ddc9.title: Alluvial fan
258aeb59ddc9.sentence: Many urban, industrial, and agricultural areas are located on alluvial fans, including the conurbations of Los Angeles, California; Salt Lake City, Utah; and Denver, Colorado, in the western United States, and in many other parts of the world.

380e658191d8.title: Alluvial fan
380e658191d8.sentence: When numerous rivers and streams exit a mountain front onto a plain, the fans can combine to form a continuous apron.

7ace51c9d4f1.title: Alluvial fan
7ace51c9d4f1.sentence: This is referred to as a bajada or piedmont alluvial plain.

8685ce660221.title: Alluvial fan
8685ce660221.sentence: A shift of the feeder channel (a nodal avulsion) can lead to catastrophic flooding, as occurred on the Kosi River fan in 2008.

f947aa51015e.title: Paludification
f947aa51015e.sentence: Paludification is the most common process by which peatlands in the boreal zone are formed.

4a4ca56f331f.title: Paludification
4a4ca56f331f.sentence: Paludification involves peat accumulation on previously drier, vegetated habitats in mineral soils, representing a shift from forests, grasslands, or long-exposed bare land to peatland, with organic soils initiating and thickening as peat accumulates.

7e770f4dfa70.title: Paludification
7e770f4dfa70.sentence: The process is characterized by peat initialization on previously drier and vegetated habitats over inorganic soils, with no fully aquatic phase.

9e6067b61bc3.title: Paludification
9e6067b61bc3.sentence: Central to the process is the hydrological balance, which must be positive (wet) during the growing season for paludification to proceed.

f771a1efad26.title: Paludification
f771a1efad26.sentence: The hydrological balance can simply be defined as the difference between the incoming and outgoing amount of water (e.g. precipitation minus evapotranspiration and minus runoff).

88507b069e19.title: Paludification
88507b069e19.sentence: The development of a paludified soil requires a positive hydrological balance during the growing season.

e08e6e60f2fc.title: Paludification
e08e6e60f2fc.sentence: The initiation of this accumulation of organic matter (i.e. peat), can be controlled by both allogenic (i.e. external to the ecosystem) and autogenic (i.e. internal to the ecosystem) factors.

a541ff3532c7.title: Paludification
a541ff3532c7.sentence: Usually it is considered that factors such as climate, geomorphology, geology and soils control this balance.

1a843269360b.title: Paludification
1a843269360b.sentence: However, paludification may also be just a result of the local accumulation of peat (i.e. autogenic factor).

9572ccd26c9b.title: Paludification
9572ccd26c9b.sentence: Such a shift could be caused by an increase in water inputs or a decrease in outputs.

b05a467d534d.title: Paludification
b05a467d534d.sentence: Human activity such as tree removal, natural or human induced forest fires, increase in precipitation, and podsolization, etc. are processes which could change those in- and outputs.

47cafe2cb14b.title: Paludification
47cafe2cb14b.sentence: The factor geomorphology (and also topography) creates spatial diversity in the hydrological characteristics of the landscape.

143a7a225e45.title: Paludification
143a7a225e45.sentence: The flat topography (and thus low slopes) in the two major peatlands in the world, located in the West Siberian Plain and in the Hudson/James Bay Lowlands of Canada respectively, illustrate the significance of this factor.

aa489f79d40f.title: Paludification
aa489f79d40f.sentence: When the mineral soil is composed of heavy clay, the soil will act as an impermeable substrate that facilitates water accumulation.

da38b21fb33b.title: Paludification
da38b21fb33b.sentence: Simply an increase in surface water from melting permafrost can cause increased paludification in boreal ecosystems.

9eafe055011e.title: Paludification
9eafe055011e.sentence: Especially because of the negative effects paludification has for the boreal forests.

d587823a40fb.title: Paludification
d587823a40fb.sentence: - Reduction in soil temperature, soil aeration, nutrient availability, decomposition rates

5460c5a23b6b.title: Paludification
5460c5a23b6b.sentence: - Formation of permafrost in certain areas

df883b215111.title: Marsh
df883b215111.sentence: Prairie potholes are found in northern North America, such as the Prairie Pothole Region.

d6f9bd6a0d96.title: Marsh
d6f9bd6a0d96.sentence: Glaciers once covered these landscapes, and as a result, shallow depressions were formed in great numbers.

84c682d2c367.title: Marsh
84c682d2c367.sentence: These depressions fill with water in the spring.

f9279bce3658.title: Marsh
f9279bce3658.sentence: Some pools only occur seasonally, while others retain enough water to be present all year.

db664384100b.title: Groundwater recharge
db664384100b.sentence: Groundwater recharge is typical in small wetlands such as prairie potholes, which can contribute significantly to recharge of regional groundwater resources.

c0fc20c71fe2.title: Marsh
c0fc20c71fe2.sentence: They provide important breeding habitats for many species of waterfowl.

9768618aeb59.title: Marsh
9768618aeb59.section: Types of marshes > Freshwater marshes > Vernal pools
9768618aeb59.sentence: Vernal pools are a type of marsh found only seasonally in shallow depressions in the land.

b68056ba5282.title: Marsh
b68056ba5282.section: Types of marshes > Freshwater marshes > Vernal pools
b68056ba5282.sentence: They can be covered in shallow water, but in the summer and fall, they can be completely dry.

fbc7037fd548.title: Mima mounds
fbc7037fd548.sentence: Vernal pools are shallow surficial depressions that seasonally fill with water during winter and spring rains and dry up during dry summer months.

a46e07497c7c.title: Mima mounds
a46e07497c7c.sentence: Vernal pools form where an impermeable or very slowly permeable layer underlies small and shallow depressions and creates a perched water table.

108d0e28a981.title: Mima mounds
108d0e28a981.sentence: The impermeable or very slowly permeable layer typically consists of either soil horizons such as duripans or claypans or bedrock in the form of volcanic mud or lava flows.

705b7daf7471.title: Mima mounds
705b7daf7471.sentence: Within California, vernal pools are quite commonly associated with Mima Mounds.

537e0738aab2.title: Mima mounds
537e0738aab2.sentence: These landforms are characterized by strongly developed soils that usually have a relatively impermeable layer (claypan or silcrete duripan) in the subsoil.

3470cce4d4ef.title: Mima mounds
3470cce4d4ef.sentence: This impermeable layer locally impedes drainage and creates perched water levels and causes the formation of vernal pools within the intermound depressions that are associated with Mima Mounds.

d66f0cfb797d.title: Mima mounds
d66f0cfb797d.sentence: Vernal pools are typically small, shallow, and complex ephemeral wetlands that only have internal drainage because they are hydrologically isolated from perennial inflow by a ring of Mima Mounds.

045fe64253a7.title: Mima mounds
045fe64253a7.sentence: Although the ponded water that fills vernal pools comes and goes throughout the year, it is present at least for a short time in most years.

44d91a75f06c.title: Marsh
44d91a75f06c.section: Types of marshes > Freshwater marshes > Vernal pools
44d91a75f06c.sentence: Many amphibian species depend upon vernal pools for spring breeding; these ponds provide a habitat free from fish, which eat the eggs and young of amphibians.

0d8ac54a0ae1.title: Marsh
0d8ac54a0ae1.section: Types of marshes > Freshwater marshes > Wet meadows
0d8ac54a0ae1.sentence: They are regularly flooded but are often dry in the summer.

47d6ef855228.title: Marsh
47d6ef855228.section: Types of marshes > Freshwater marshes > Wet meadows
47d6ef855228.sentence: Wet meadows occur in shallow lake basins, low-lying depressions, and the land between shallow marshes and upland areas.

8b6719766bee.title: Marsh
8b6719766bee.section: Types of marshes > Freshwater marshes > Wet meadows
8b6719766bee.sentence: They also happen on the edges of large lakes and rivers.

38346c39b32d.title: Marsh
38346c39b32d.section: Types of marshes > Freshwater marshes > Wet meadows
38346c39b32d.sentence: Wet meadows often have very high plant diversity and high densities of buried seeds.

649940ce154e.title: Shrub swamp
649940ce154e.sentence: As a wet meadow matures it begins to fill in with vegetation and as this decomposes the soil thickens creating high spots (hummocks) above the water.

9870b4d23f3c.title: Shrub swamp
9870b4d23f3c.sentence: Shrubs and small trees begin to grow on these.

9b11aff8a78a.title: Shrub swamp
9b11aff8a78a.sentence: They are often considered transitional ("mid-successional") between wet meadows or fens and conifer or hardwood swamps.

fc4f2642e7ff.title: Palsa
fc4f2642e7ff.sentence: Palsas are peat mounds with a permanently frozen peat and mineral soil core.

514d8e629835.title: Palsa
514d8e629835.sentence: They are a typical phenomenon in the polar and subpolar zone of discontinuous permafrost.

b3f2bb6ffd74.title: Palsa
b3f2bb6ffd74.sentence: Palsas can be up to 150 m (490 ft) in diameter and can reach a height of 12 m (39 ft).

1a5e8c1993ee.title: Palsa
1a5e8c1993ee.sentence: One of their characteristics is having steep slopes that rise above the mire surface.

ba645c9cbc6d.title: Palsa
ba645c9cbc6d.sentence: Dry peat is a good insulator, but wet peat conducts heat better, and frozen peat is even better at conducting heat.

57449416d18c.title: Palsa
57449416d18c.sentence: This means that cold can penetrate deep into the peat layers, and that heat can easily flow from deeper wet layers in winter, whereas the dry peat on the palsa surface insulates the frozen core and prevents it from thawing in the summer.

a31236a77f11.title: Palsa
a31236a77f11.sentence: This means that palsas can survive in a climate where the mean annual temperature is just below the freezing point.

169f842a0f08.title: Palsa
169f842a0f08.sentence: Palsas may be initiated in areas of a moor or bog where the winter freezing front penetrates relatively faster than surrounding areas, perhaps due to an unusually thin cover of snow.

82780a00d52b.title: Palsa
82780a00d52b.sentence: This contributes to the formation of an ice lens which grows by drawing up surrounding water.

fade528fcf1f.title: Palsa
fade528fcf1f.sentence: The overlying soil layer is gradually lifted up by frost heaving.

eb5e9fdd3edf.title: Palsa
eb5e9fdd3edf.section: Effects of climate change > Palsa and GHG-fluxes
eb5e9fdd3edf.sentence: Therefore, an increase in temperature and precipitation may induce thawing of frozen peat and subsidence of the peat surface.

9e959fda360b.title: Palsa
9e959fda360b.section: Effects of climate change > Palsa and GHG-fluxes
9e959fda360b.sentence: This results in a thicker active layer and wetter conditions.

5aaed230661c.title: Palsa
5aaed230661c.section: Effects of climate change > Palsa and GHG-fluxes
5aaed230661c.sentence: The associated changes in greenhouse gases fluxes are increased CO2 uptake and increased methane emission, mainly due to the expansion of tall graminoids.

11360968fbc7.title: Land loss
11360968fbc7.sentence: Land loss is the term typically used to refer to the conversion of coastal land to open water by natural processes and human activities.

7a6ec5878445.title: Land loss
7a6ec5878445.sentence: The term land loss includes coastal erosion.

62d9221dafbd.title: Land loss
62d9221dafbd.sentence: It is a much broader term than coastal erosion because land loss also includes land converted to open water around the edges of estuaries and interior bays and lakes and by subsidence of coastal plain wetlands.

9743f35ebbff.title: Land loss
9743f35ebbff.sentence: The main causes of land loss are coastal erosion, inadequate sediment supply, subsidence, and sea level rise.

2f7be1bca235.title: Land loss
2f7be1bca235.sentence: The large delta plains of the world, including the Danube, Ganges, Brahmaputra, Indus, Mahanadi, Mangoky, McKenzie, Mississippi, Niger, Nile, Shatt el Arab, Volga, Yellow, Yukon, and Zambezi deltas, have all suffered significant land loss as the result of either coastal erosion, internal conversion of wetlands to open water, or a combination of both.

be8c54fa0435.title: Aspect (geography)
be8c54fa0435.sentence: In physical geography and physical geology, aspect (also known as exposure) is the compass direction or azimuth that a terrain surface faces.

894412d38b03.title: Aspect (geography)
894412d38b03.sentence: Aspect is complemented by grade (or inclination angle) to characterize the surface gradient.

465b689c7854.title: Aspect (geography)
465b689c7854.sentence: The direction a slope faces can affect the physical and biotic features of the slope, known as a slope effect.

2a4762745997.title: Aspect (geography)
2a4762745997.sentence: In the Northern Hemisphere, the north side of slopes is often shaded, while the southern side receives more solar radiation for a given surface area insolation because the slope is tilted toward the Sun and is not shaded directly by the Earth itself.

32863c4a71a0.title: Aspect (geography)
32863c4a71a0.sentence: The aspect of a slope can make very significant influences on its local climate (microclimate).

2f6c8a2f3efb.title: Aspect (geography)
2f6c8a2f3efb.sentence: Similarly, in the Northern Hemisphere a south-facing slope (more open to sunlight and warm winds) will therefore generally be warmer and drier due to higher levels of evapotranspiration than a north-facing slope.

2e8e44a20d2b.title: Aspect (geography)
2e8e44a20d2b.sentence: Strong slopes with equatorward aspects tend to have soil organic matter levels and seasonal influences similar to level slopes at lower elevation whereas poleward aspects have soil development similarities to level soils at higher elevations.

e33d03bdee30.title: Aspect (geography)
e33d03bdee30.sentence: Outside of the tropics, soils with an aspect directed toward an early afternoon solar position will typically have the lowest soil moisture content and lowest soil organic matter content relative to other available aspects in a locale.

90238dcdbff2.title: Aspect (geography)
90238dcdbff2.sentence: Soils with a prevailing windward aspect will typically be shallower, and often with more developed subsoil characteristics, than adjacent soils on the leeward where decelerating winds tend to deposit more air-borne particulate material.

e0769b0783f3.title: Ramsar Convention
e0769b0783f3.sentence: The Ramsar Convention on Wetlands of International Importance Especially as Waterfowl Habitat is an international treaty for the conservation and sustainable use of Ramsar sites (wetlands).

30263386c34a.title: Ramsar Convention
30263386c34a.sentence: It is also known as the Convention on Wetlands.

d1aa43476e00.title: Ramsar Convention
d1aa43476e00.sentence: It is named after the city of Ramsar in Iran, where the convention was signed in 1971.

54da37880df5.title: Ramsar Convention
54da37880df5.sentence: The conference, which adopted the terms of the agreement, was held in the Iranian Caspian Sea resort of Ramsar on 2 February 1971.

aa6da8ecd36c.title: Wetland
aa6da8ecd36c.sentence: - Article 1.1: "...wetlands are areas of marsh, fen, peatland or water, whether natural or artificial, permanent or temporary, with water that is static or flowing, fresh, brackish or salt, including areas of marine water the depth of which at low tide does not exceed six meters."

7f360ec75d77.title: Ramsar Convention
7f360ec75d77.section: List of wetlands of international importance
7f360ec75d77.sentence: The list of wetlands of international importance included 2,531 Ramsar sites in February 2025 covering over 2.6 million square kilometres (1,000,000 sq mi).

1940f1e99e51.title: Ramsar Convention
1940f1e99e51.section: List of wetlands of international importance
1940f1e99e51.sentence: The countries with most sites are the United Kingdom with 175 and Mexico with 142.

531168717ca0.title: Ramsar Convention
531168717ca0.sentence: February 2 is World Wetlands Day, marking the convention's adoption on 2 February 1971.

de446baee6db.title: Ramsar Convention
de446baee6db.sentence: Established to raise awareness about the value of wetlands for humanity and the planet, WWD was celebrated for the first time in 1997, and has grown since then.

11942775f678.title: Ramsar Convention
11942775f678.section: Deficiencies in the treaty and its implementation
11942775f678.sentence: Despite its quasi-universal application, the domestic response to this treaty is often half-hearted and inadequate.

6c41f270f6eb.title: Landscape ecology
6c41f270f6eb.sentence: Patch, a term fundamental to landscape ecology, is defined as a relatively homogeneous area that differs from its surroundings.

b4e5ac3272aa.title: Landscape ecology
b4e5ac3272aa.sentence: A network is an interconnected system of corridors while mosaic describes the pattern of patches, corridors, and matrix that form a landscape in its entirety.

3fcb21d497b0.title: Landscape ecology
3fcb21d497b0.sentence: Patches are the basic unit of the landscape that change and fluctuate, a process called patch dynamics.

8e3e2006db4c.title: Landscape ecology
8e3e2006db4c.sentence: Matrix is the "background ecological system" of a landscape with a high degree of connectivity.

e8d2e5d49603.title: Landscape ecology
e8d2e5d49603.sentence: Connectivity is the measure of how connected or spatially continuous a corridor, network, or matrix is.

5ca7382dc36d.title: Landscape ecology
5ca7382dc36d.sentence: Corridors have important functions as strips of a particular type of landscape differing from adjacent land on both sides.

acdd99b61b26.title: Landscape ecology
acdd99b61b26.sentence: An important consequence of repeated, random clearing (whether by natural disturbance or human activity) is that contiguous cover can break down into isolated patches.

e63a685e7dc3.title: Landscape ecology
e63a685e7dc3.sentence: This happens when the area cleared exceeds a critical level, which means that landscapes exhibit two phases: connected and disconnected.

077d301c9d47.title: Landscape ecology
077d301c9d47.section: Important terms > Ecotones, ecoclines, and ecotopes
077d301c9d47.sentence: A type of boundary is the ecotone, or the transitional zone between two communities.

97900ba06ba8.title: Landscape ecology
97900ba06ba8.section: Important terms > Ecotones, ecoclines, and ecotopes
97900ba06ba8.sentence: Ecotones can arise naturally, such as a lakeshore, or can be human-created, such as a cleared agricultural field from a forest.

f3e3e9b67d46.title: Landscape ecology
f3e3e9b67d46.section: Important terms > Ecotones, ecoclines, and ecotopes
f3e3e9b67d46.sentence: Classic examples of ecotones include fencerows, forest to marshlands transitions, forest to grassland transitions, or land-water interfaces such as riparian zones in forests.

9903ec585e87.title: Landscape ecology
9903ec585e87.section: Important terms > Ecotones, ecoclines, and ecotopes
9903ec585e87.sentence: The ecotonal community retains characteristics of each bordering community and often contains species not found in the adjacent communities.

3637c919a7d9.title: Landscape ecology
3637c919a7d9.section: Important terms > Ecotones, ecoclines, and ecotopes
3637c919a7d9.sentence: An ecocline is another type of landscape boundary, but it is a gradual and continuous change in environmental conditions of an ecosystem or community.

73a6ddb45a28.title: Landscape ecology
73a6ddb45a28.section: Important terms > Ecotones, ecoclines, and ecotopes
73a6ddb45a28.sentence: An ecotope is a spatial term representing the smallest ecologically distinct unit in mapping and classification of landscapes.

1d35db2882ac.title: Landscape ecology
1d35db2882ac.section: Important terms > Ecotones, ecoclines, and ecotopes
1d35db2882ac.sentence: Relatively homogeneous, they are spatially explicit landscape units used to stratify landscapes into ecologically distinct features.

3bf85cb6d40b.title: Landscape ecology
3bf85cb6d40b.section: Important terms > Scale and heterogeneity (incorporating composition, structure, and function)
3bf85cb6d40b.sentence: A landscape with structure and pattern implies that it has spatial heterogeneity, or the uneven distribution of objects across the landscape.

31c5562083ec.title: Landscape ecology
31c5562083ec.sentence: Heterogeneity is the measure of how parts of a landscape differ from one another.

8ea35cac950d.title: Landscape ecology
8ea35cac950d.section: Important terms > Scale and heterogeneity (incorporating composition, structure, and function)
8ea35cac950d.sentence: Heterogeneity is a key element of landscape ecology that separates this discipline from other branches of ecology.

e062d0639e68.title: Landscape ecology
e062d0639e68.section: Important terms > Scale and heterogeneity (incorporating composition, structure, and function)
e062d0639e68.sentence: A main concept in landscape ecology is scale.

a659c363447f.title: Landscape ecology
a659c363447f.section: Important terms > Scale and heterogeneity (incorporating composition, structure, and function)
a659c363447f.sentence: Scale represents the real world as translated onto a map, relating distance on a map image and the corresponding distance on earth.

96e4233d7760.title: Landscape ecology
96e4233d7760.section: Important terms > Scale and heterogeneity (incorporating composition, structure, and function)
96e4233d7760.sentence: Scale is also the spatial or temporal measure of an object or a process, or amount of spatial resolution.

ffc66ddbe67b.title: Landscape ecology
ffc66ddbe67b.section: Important terms > Scale and heterogeneity (incorporating composition, structure, and function)
ffc66ddbe67b.sentence: Applied to landscape ecology, composition refers to the number of patch types (see below) represented on a landscape and their relative abundance.

ab29e8ac4753.title: Landscape ecology
ab29e8ac4753.section: Important terms > Scale and heterogeneity (incorporating composition, structure, and function)
ab29e8ac4753.sentence: For example, the amount of forest or wetland, the length of forest edge, or the density of roads can be aspects of landscape composition.

b279905febfe.title: Landscape ecology
b279905febfe.section: Important terms > Scale and heterogeneity (incorporating composition, structure, and function)
b279905febfe.sentence: Structure is determined by the composition, the configuration, and the proportion of different patches across the landscape, while function refers to how each element in the landscape interacts based on its life cycle events.

cbad29a49a43.title: Landscape ecology
cbad29a49a43.sentence: Landscape ecology theory includes the landscape stability principle, which emphasizes the importance of landscape structural heterogeneity in developing resistance to disturbances, recovery from disturbances, and promoting total system stability.

6fc9a2cff528.title: Blanket bog
6fc9a2cff528.sentence: Blanket bog or blanket mire, or also known as featherbed bog, is an area of peatland, forming where there is a climate of high rainfall and a low level of evapotranspiration, allowing peat to develop not only in wet hollows but over large expanses of undulating ground.

e29ab2a92efe.title: Blanket bog
e29ab2a92efe.sentence: The blanketing of the ground with a variable depth of peat gives the habitat type its name.

791a6eefd5ad.title: Bog
791a6eefd5ad.section: Types > By location and water source > Blanket bog
791a6eefd5ad.sentence: In cool climates with consistently high rainfall (on more than c. 235 days a year), the ground surface may remain waterlogged for much of the time, providing conditions for the development of bog vegetation.

483a4a707b2d.title: Bog
483a4a707b2d.section: Types > By location and water source > Blanket bog
483a4a707b2d.sentence: Although a blanket bog is more common on acidic substrates, under some conditions it may also develop on neutral or even alkaline ones, if abundant acidic rainwater predominates over the groundwater.

1cc8269784c9.title: Blanket bog
1cc8269784c9.sentence: The current distribution of blanket bogs globally remains unknown but they are found extensively throughout the Northern Hemisphere.

df8c91bc4599.title: Blanket bog
df8c91bc4599.sentence: Well-studied examples are found in Ireland and Scotland, but vast areas of North American tundra also qualify as blanket bogs.

8e6b155ecd67.title: Blanket bog
8e6b155ecd67.sentence: In the Southern Hemisphere, they are less well-developed due to the relatively low latitudes of the main land areas, though similar environments are reported in Patagonia, the Falkland Islands and New Zealand.

9f40ae545ccd.title: Blanket bog
9f40ae545ccd.sentence: In some areas of Europe, the spread of blanket bogs is traced to deforestation by prehistoric cultures.

8c6447148b07.title: Börde
8c6447148b07.sentence: A börde (German pronunciation: [ˈbœʁdə]; plural: börden [ˈbœʁdn̩]) is a region of highly fertile lowland in North Germany, a "fertile plain".

b63fc534e5ab.title: Börde
b63fc534e5ab.sentence: These regions coincide closely with areas of flat, fertile loess soil and few trees.

2875a370d011.title: Börde
2875a370d011.sentence: These landscapes often cover great areas and are particularly important for arable farming on account of their rich soils.

283c69e5d967.title: Börde
283c69e5d967.sentence: Börden extend from the North German geest to the perimeter of the German Central Uplands and consist of loess that has been predominantly deposited by east winds.

b9854e335123.title: Börde
b9854e335123.sentence: The loess layers are up to 10 metres thick and tend to attenuate differences in relief.

38bef47dc04d.title: Börde
38bef47dc04d.sentence: In some places the loess lies over boulder clay (on the rivers Weser, Leine and Oker), in others over Mesozoic and Tertiary sedimentary rocks (in the Hellwegbörden and the foreland of the Harz Mountains).

9555ec1525be.title: Börde
9555ec1525be.sentence: In the (sub-)oceanic climatic region the loess has been largely decalcified and loamified.

279595099215.title: Börde
279595099215.sentence: The resulting black earth soils are some of the best soils in Germany.

0a5db0424c03.title: Börde
0a5db0424c03.sentence: The northern edge of the loess region is not only a soil and vegetation boundary, but also a settlement zone - cities like Minden, Hanover or Magdeburg lie on the loess boundary.

6842ada5b14a.title: Peat swamp forest
6842ada5b14a.sentence: Peat swamp forests are tropical moist forests where waterlogged soil prevents dead leaves and wood from fully decomposing.

33d33f1a147c.title: Peat swamp forest
33d33f1a147c.sentence: Over time, this creates a thick layer of acidic peat.

a68188b61cc2.title: Peat swamp forest
a68188b61cc2.sentence: They are a kind of wetland which store and accumulate vast amounts of carbon as soil organic matter—much more than forests on mineral soil contain.

a1c7f58908a3.title: Peat swamp forest
a1c7f58908a3.sentence: The stability of these forests has important implications for climate change; they are among the largest near-surface reserves of terrestrial organic carbon.

0f5c2d895370.title: Peat swamp forest
0f5c2d895370.sentence: Tropical peat forms on low-lying areas, such as river deltas, floodplains or shallow oxbow lakes.

e043eb8c4fae.title: Peat swamp forest
e043eb8c4fae.sentence: This peat accumulation often forms a convex shape called a dome, which could rise up to 4 m (13 ft) on coastal peat and up to 18 m (59 ft) on inland peat.

aa6d66312aaf.title: Peat swamp forest
aa6d66312aaf.sentence: At the beginning of its formation, peat is largely topogenous or minerotrophic, receiving high nutrient input from rivers or groundwater.

359cd8e2d4ba.title: Peat swamp forest
359cd8e2d4ba.sentence: As the peat thickens and the dome becomes elevated, the top of the peat is no longer affected by the river or groundwater input, instead soil becomes ombrotrophic, exclusively obtaining water from the precipitation Input only from the rain causes a low nutrient and mineral content, especially calcium.

48a97b96b79e.title: Peat swamp forest
48a97b96b79e.sentence: The peat thus becomes highly acidic and only able to support low biodiversity and stunted forest.

efbf10f660c8.title: Peat swamp forest
efbf10f660c8.sentence: About 62% of the world's tropical peat lands occur in the Indomalayan realm (80% in Indonesia, 11% in Malaysia, 6% in Papua New Guinea, and pockets in Brunei, Vietnam, the Philippines, and Thailand).

404ffd782fec.title: Peat swamp forest
404ffd782fec.sentence: 36% of the world's tropical peat occurs in Africa's central Congo Basin.

442e81c46aaf.title: Peat swamp forest
442e81c46aaf.sentence: Beginning in 1996 under the Mega Rice Project (MRP), the government of Indonesia drained over 1 million hectares of the Borneo peat swamp forests for conversion to agricultural land.

f48b7665cdb7.title: Peat swamp forest
f48b7665cdb7.sentence: Peat fires, drainage and deforestation enhance the decomposition of soil organic matter, increasing the release of stored carbon into the atmosphere as carbon dioxide.

77f8461a5fdc.title: Wetland
77f8461a5fdc.sentence: A constructed wetland is an artificial wetland to treat sewage, greywater, stormwater runoff or industrial wastewater.

d4c504ba0981.title: Wetland
d4c504ba0981.sentence: Constructed wetlands are engineered systems that use the natural functions of vegetation, soil, and organisms to provide secondary treatment to wastewater.

1fb1799cb5b4.title: Wetland
1fb1799cb5b4.sentence: Constructed wetlands are designed to remove water pollutants such as suspended solids, organic matter and nutrients (nitrogen and phosphorus).

c2ed64b1679c.title: Wetland
c2ed64b1679c.sentence: Similar to natural wetlands, constructed wetlands also act as a biofilter and/or can remove a range of pollutants (such as organic matter, nutrients, pathogens, heavy metals) from the water.

fd8bbebc9e3c.title: Wetland
fd8bbebc9e3c.sentence: All types of pathogens (i.e., bacteria, viruses, protozoans and helminths) are expected to be removed to some extent in a constructed wetland.

aa836811552b.title: Wetland
aa836811552b.sentence: Subsurface wetlands provide greater pathogen removal than surface wetlands.

9f50b703ae20.title: Wetland
9f50b703ae20.sentence: It may also be designed for land reclamation after mining, or as a mitigation step for natural areas lost to land development.

f518d5dcb25b.title: Wetland
f518d5dcb25b.sentence: An example of how a natural wetland is used to provide some degree of sewage treatment is the East Kolkata Wetlands in Kolkata, India.

a5e89b296d67.title: Wetland
a5e89b296d67.sentence: The wetlands cover 125 square kilometres (48 sq mi), and are used to treat Kolkata's sewage.

f6fb7ce39e3b.title: Wetland
f6fb7ce39e3b.sentence: The nutrients contained in the wastewater sustain fish farms and agriculture.

9ae196881b6b.title: Fen
9ae196881b6b.sentence: Once commonly drained for conversion to agricultural purposes or for urban development, wetlands, including fens, are now recognized to offer society a range of services that may include:

c414451a9a0a.title: Swamp
c414451a9a0a.sentence: Ecologists recognize that swamps provide ecological services including flood control, fish production, water purification, carbon storage, and wildlife habitats.

4fe5f8592dca.title: Wetland
4fe5f8592dca.sentence: A natural function of wetland vegetation is the up-take, storage, and (for nitrate) the removal of nutrients found in runoff water from the surrounding landscapes.

dddb29d178ef.title: Wetland
dddb29d178ef.sentence: Wetland vegetation acts as a physical barrier to slow water flow and then trap sediment for both short or long periods of time.

5674c644506b.title: Wetland
5674c644506b.sentence: Suspended sediment can contain heavy metals that are also retained when wetlands trap the sediment.

61e7a61debe9.title: Wetland
61e7a61debe9.section: Ecosystem services > Storage reservoirs and flood protection
61e7a61debe9.sentence: "The floodplains of major rivers act as natural storage reservoirs, enabling excess water to spread out over a wide area, which reduces its depth and speed.

85194bb9c448.title: Wetland
85194bb9c448.section: Ecosystem services > Storage reservoirs and flood protection
85194bb9c448.sentence: Wetlands close to the headwaters of streams and rivers can slow down rainwater runoff and spring snowmelt so that it does not run straight off the land into water courses.

7eb87286e569.title: Fen
7eb87286e569.section: Ecosystem services > Carbon sequestration and global warming
7eb87286e569.sentence: Fens, as peat-forming ecosystems, sequester large quantities of carbon as peat, preventing its release into the atmosphere as carbon dioxide.

bc2f1c040b54.title: Fen
bc2f1c040b54.section: Ecosystem services > Carbon sequestration and global warming
bc2f1c040b54.sentence: Destruction of the peat layer in fens can release carbon stores into the atmosphere.

0a56621c2044.title: Wetland
0a56621c2044.sentence: To replace these wetland ecosystem services, enormous amounts of money would need to be spent on water purification plants, dams, levees, and other hard infrastructure, and many of the services are impossible to replace.

5344e2b813b8.title: Wetland
5344e2b813b8.section: Climate change aspects > Greenhouse gas emissions
5344e2b813b8.sentence: Greenhouse gas emissions from wetlands of concern consist primarily of methane and nitrous oxide emissions.

ccc3d9f1bca8.title: Wetland
ccc3d9f1bca8.section: Climate change aspects > Greenhouse gas emissions
ccc3d9f1bca8.sentence: Wetlands are the largest natural source of atmospheric methane in the world, and are therefore a major area of concern with respect to climate change.

a6fcab5647e1.title: Wetland
a6fcab5647e1.section: Climate change aspects > Greenhouse gas emissions
a6fcab5647e1.sentence: Wetlands account for approximately 20–30% of atmospheric methane through emissions from soils and plants, and contribute an approximate average of 161 Tg of methane to the atmosphere per year.

d4be13324303.title: Wetland
d4be13324303.section: Climate change aspects > Greenhouse gas emissions
d4be13324303.sentence: Because the microbes that live in warm, moist environments consume oxygen more rapidly than it can diffuse in from the atmosphere, wetlands are the ideal anaerobic environments for fermentation as well as methanogen activity.

1081caf1cd05.title: Wetland
1081caf1cd05.section: Climate change aspects > Greenhouse gas emissions
1081caf1cd05.sentence: A warmer, more anaerobic environment with soil rich in organic matter would allow for more efficient methanogenesis.

f1a252a995e4.title: Wetland
f1a252a995e4.section: Climate change aspects > Greenhouse gas emissions
f1a252a995e4.sentence: As a result of peat drainage, the organic carbon that had built up over thousands of years and is normally under water is suddenly exposed to the air.

8bd4ebc59dd6.title: Wetland
8bd4ebc59dd6.section: Climate change aspects > Greenhouse gas emissions
8bd4ebc59dd6.sentence: The peat decomposes and is converted into carbon dioxide (CO2), which is then released into the atmosphere.

aaf4e8aba316.title: Wetland
aaf4e8aba316.section: Climate change aspects > Greenhouse gas emissions
aaf4e8aba316.sentence: While peatlands constitute only 3% of the world's land area, their degradation produces 7% of all CO2 emissions.

5b3d5c91f8ce.title: Wetland
5b3d5c91f8ce.section: Climate change aspects > Greenhouse gas emissions
5b3d5c91f8ce.sentence: Some wetlands are a significant source of methane emissions and some are also emitters of nitrous oxide.

5e12f465a5a7.title: Wetland
5e12f465a5a7.section: Climate change aspects > Greenhouse gas emissions
5e12f465a5a7.sentence: Nitrous oxide is a greenhouse gas with a global warming potential 300 times that of carbon dioxide and is the dominant ozone-depleting substance emitted in the 21st century.

e1e18fa10642.title: Wetland
e1e18fa10642.section: Climate change aspects > Greenhouse gas emissions
e1e18fa10642.sentence: Wetlands can also act as a sink for greenhouse gases.

8e05068a60a0.title: Wetland
8e05068a60a0.sentence: The most important factor producing wetlands is hydrology, or flooding.

57d5bab0d913.title: Wetland
57d5bab0d913.sentence: Wetland hydrology is associated with the spatial and temporal dispersion, flow, and physio-chemical attributes of surface and ground waters.

966e22226ebb.title: Wetland
966e22226ebb.sentence: The duration of flooding or prolonged soil saturation by groundwater determines whether the resulting wetland has aquatic, marsh or swamp vegetation.

321006acc430.title: Wetland
321006acc430.sentence: Sources of hydrological flows into wetlands are predominantly precipitation, surface water (saltwater or freshwater), and groundwater.

733a3c6ab236.title: Wetland
733a3c6ab236.sentence: Water flows out of wetlands by evapotranspiration, surface flows and tides, and subsurface water outflow.

e0fc4f2136c1.title: Wetland
e0fc4f2136c1.sentence: Hydrodynamics (the movement of water through and from a wetland) affects hydro-periods (temporal fluctuations in water levels) by controlling the water balance and water storage within a wetland.

0343a85437b4.title: Wetland
0343a85437b4.sentence: Wetlands are generally minerotrophic (waters contain dissolved materials from soils) with the exception of ombrotrophic bogs that are fed only by water from precipitation.

abba5088b47e.title: Wetland
abba5088b47e.sentence: Because bogs receive most of their water from precipitation and humidity from the atmosphere, their water usually has low mineral ionic composition.

ae06f092249d.title: Wetland
ae06f092249d.sentence: Fen peatlands receive water both from precipitation and ground water in varying amounts so their water chemistry ranges from acidic with low levels of dissolved minerals to alkaline with high accumulation of calcium and magnesium.

c3dfa4e405ff.title: Wetland
c3dfa4e405ff.sentence: Wetlands can also act as recharge areas when the surrounding water table is low and as a discharge zone when it is high.

0aa44a4a0b11.title: Swamp
0aa44a4a0b11.sentence: Historically, humans have been known to drain or fill swamps and other wetlands in order to create more space for human development and to reduce the threat of diseases borne by swamp insects.

f3eb8265dd14.title: Swamp
f3eb8265dd14.sentence: Wetlands are removed and replaced with land that is then used for things like agriculture, real estate, and recreational uses.

aa017205aa9a.title: Freshwater marsh
aa017205aa9a.sentence: Wetlands are frequently being destroyed for development, agriculture, and other uses.

22dcd217022d.title: Freshwater marsh
22dcd217022d.sentence: Wetlands have decreased by as much as 50% since 1900 and in some parts of the world by 90%.

8a81a5ce38bf.title: Swamp
8a81a5ce38bf.sentence: Europe has likely lost nearly half its wetlands.

4b3fb7406b53.title: Wetland
4b3fb7406b53.section: Disturbances and human impacts > Conversion to dry land
4b3fb7406b53.sentence: To increase economic productivity, wetlands are often converted into dry land with dykes and drains and used for agricultural purposes.

48b26321d82b.title: Wetland
48b26321d82b.section: Disturbances and human impacts > Conversion to dry land
48b26321d82b.sentence: Once settlements are constructed and protected by dykes, the settlements then become vulnerable to land subsidence and ever increasing risk of flooding.

50f1520da040.title: Wetland
50f1520da040.section: Disturbances and human impacts > Conversion to dry land
50f1520da040.sentence: The Mississippi River Delta around New Orleans, Louisiana is a well-known example; the Danube Delta in Europe is another.

221854ddaf14.title: Peatland
221854ddaf14.sentence: The total area of mires has declined globally due to drainage for agriculture, forestry and peat harvesting.

f8b1f3b8e3c0.title: Peatland
f8b1f3b8e3c0.sentence: For example, more than 50% of the original European mire area which is more than 300,000 km2 has been lost.

bc36846f9060.title: Swamp
bc36846f9060.sentence: Often the simplest steps to restoring swamps involve plugging drainage ditches and removing levees.

b120b5d015c3.title: Freshwater marsh
b120b5d015c3.sentence: Reverting rivers back to their natural state will allow nearby marshes to form again.

19019f332d29.title: Freshwater marsh
19019f332d29.sentence: Another way to restore freshwater marshes is to break down levees, dikes, and berms that impede rivers from flooding.

c99ba7b248e1.title: Peatland
c99ba7b248e1.sentence: A peatland that is actively forming peat is called a mire.

4df418a4d55f.title: Peatland
4df418a4d55f.sentence: A peatland that is still capable of forming new peat is called a mire, while drained and converted peatlands might still have a peat layer but are not considered mires as the formation of new peat has ceased.

42804e03be2c.title: Peatland
42804e03be2c.sentence: There are two types of mire: bog and fen.

99b7e1673aac.title: Peatland
99b7e1673aac.sentence: A bog is a mire that, due to its raised location relative to the surrounding landscape, obtains all its water solely from precipitation (ombrotrophic).

60be39fd40c1.title: Peatland
60be39fd40c1.sentence: A fen is located on a slope, flat, or in a depression and gets most of its water from the surrounding mineral soil or from groundwater (minerotrophic).

2be4abfd8789.title: Peatland
2be4abfd8789.sentence: All mires are initially fens when the peat starts to form, and may turn into bogs once the height of the peat layer reaches above the surrounding land.

a6cae056d19a.title: Peatland
a6cae056d19a.sentence: A marsh is a type of wetland within which vegetation is rooted in mineral soil.

f751df2d70b0.title: Shrub swamp
f751df2d70b0.sentence: Shrub swamps — also called scrub swamps or buttonbush swamps — are a type of freshwater wetland ecosystem occurring in areas too wet to become swamps ("true" or freshwater swamp forest), but too dry or too shallow to become marshes.

e00fdcef1afc.title: Shrub swamp
e00fdcef1afc.sentence: Creation of shrub swamps often follows a catastrophic event in a forested swamp (flood, cutting, fire, or windstorm).

65aa7af66bab.title: Shrub swamp
65aa7af66bab.sentence: Another route of development is via drained meadows and fens which progress to shrub swamps as a transitional state to forested swamps.

5944c234cd61.title: Shrub swamp
5944c234cd61.sentence: Shrub swamp water comes from run-off, streams and rivers and the water moves in and out of the swamp throughout the year.

1ddc1c748c3f.title: Shrub swamp
1ddc1c748c3f.sentence: Consequently, they tend to be drier than wet meadows or forested swamps and permit water intolerant plant species to grow on the hummocks.

896b7834f999.title: Shrub swamp
896b7834f999.sentence: Shrub swamps typically occur on organic soils, such as muck and shallow peat soils.

219c656afb7a.title: Shrub swamp
219c656afb7a.sentence: By some classifications, shrub swamps must have at least 50% shrub cover and less than 20% tree cover.

7c929023f159.title: Flark
7c929023f159.sentence: A flark is a depression or hollow within a bog.

ac311ae1469b.title: Flark
ac311ae1469b.sentence: Flarks typically occur as a series of parallel depressions, separated by intervening ridges known as strings.

ff79555e93e9.title: Flark
ff79555e93e9.sentence: Early theories suggested that flarks were formed by frost heaving, but flarks have since been found in areas where frost heaving does not occur.

a9922ba6a750.title: Flark
a9922ba6a750.sentence: Flarks are now thought to form when the peat that forms the base of the bog becomes so thick that it slides downslope due to its own weight.

18ced23b09eb.title: Flark
18ced23b09eb.sentence: Irregularities in the underlying terrain halt the slide of the peat, causing flarks to form downslope from the obstruction as the downslope peat tears away from the portion of the peat mass held back by the underlying obstruction.

fda3d82c576b.title: Flark
fda3d82c576b.sentence: Another theory suggests that flarks are formed by areas within the bog which experience accelerated rates of decay, causing depressions in the bog.

07b032a3326c.title: Gilgai
07b032a3326c.sentence: A gilgai is a small, ephemeral lake formed from a surface depression in expanding clay soils.

bdbc37fc260f.title: Gilgai
bdbc37fc260f.sentence: Gilgai is also used to refer to the overall micro-relief in such areas, consisting of mounds and depressions.

ac76e7f4f794.title: Gilgai
ac76e7f4f794.sentence: Gilgais are thought to form in vertisols through repeated cycles of swelling when wet and subsequent shrinkage upon drying.

8ef8f1164e86.title: Gilgai
8ef8f1164e86.sentence: That action, known as argillipedoturbation, causes the soil to crack when dry, allowing loose soil material to fill the cracks.

8e4b413c5da8.title: Gilgai
8e4b413c5da8.sentence: When the soil swells upon subsequent re-wetting, the soil pressure cannot be dispersed into the now-full cracks and the soil is forced sideways causing a mound to form between cracks and a depression to form at the location of the crack.

e61e94feb947.title: Gilgai
e61e94feb947.sentence: That process is then exaggerated as the depressions hold water and thus become wetter and swell more than the mounds, causing even greater shrinkage and cracking.

a5cfebb3fdb6.title: Gilgai
a5cfebb3fdb6.sentence: In addition, the cracks channel water deeply into the soil, causing even greater swelling and subsequent cracking of the depression areas.

e2cdcde38d5d.title: Gilgai
e2cdcde38d5d.sentence: Each cycle of swelling, shrinkage and cracking becomes more exaggerated and the landscape eventually becomes covered by a repeated pattern of mounds and depressions.

3cc720a487b2.title: Gilgai
3cc720a487b2.sentence: The pools are commonly a few metres across and less than 30 cm (12 in) deep but, in some instances, they may be several metres deep and up to 100 m (330 ft) across.

63558d189cfa.title: Gilgai
63558d189cfa.sentence: Gilgais are found worldwide wherever there are cracking clay soils and marked wet and dry seasons.

c945a93730e3.title: Gilgai
c945a93730e3.sentence: The movement of soil associated with gilgai formation damages infrastructure, including building foundations, roads and railway lines, and the undulations interfere with crop harvesting.

df39994f959d.title: Gilgai
df39994f959d.sentence: Crayfish burrow in the wet basins and ants build up the mounds, magnifying the formations through bioturbation.

1fe42402d5bd.title: Gilgai
1fe42402d5bd.sentence: Gilgais are structurally similar to the patterned ground of frigid regions, but periglacial soil polygons are formed instead, by repeated freeze-thaw cycles.

1c2dce06ace8.title: Palustrine wetland
1c2dce06ace8.sentence: Palustrine wetlands include any inland wetland that contains ocean-derived salts in concentrations of less than 0.5 parts per thousand, and is non-tidal.

47fb2ed73075.title: Palustrine wetland
47fb2ed73075.sentence: Wetlands within this category include inland marshes and swamps as well as bogs, fens, pocosins, tundra and floodplains.

5fa1c8ed449b.title: Palustrine wetland
5fa1c8ed449b.sentence: Palustrine wetlands are one of five systems of wetlands within the Cowardin classification system.

5b5cbfd4304a.title: Palustrine wetland
