5b5cbfd4304a.sentence: This system was created by Lewis Cowardin and others from the United States Fish and Wildlife Service in 1987.

d832d7f34b02.title: Palustrine wetland
d832d7f34b02.sentence: - Marine wetlands, exposed to the open ocean

f0e0354efffc.title: Palustrine wetland
f0e0354efffc.sentence: - Estuarine wetlands, partially enclosed by land and containing a mix of fresh and salt water

a54884f90dd0.title: Palustrine wetland
a54884f90dd0.sentence: - Riverine wetlands, associated with flowing water

63a7528051d5.title: Palustrine wetland
63a7528051d5.sentence: - Lacustrine wetlands, associated with a lake or other body of fresh water

cd493201c0a1.title: Palustrine wetland
cd493201c0a1.sentence: This different groups of vegetation are aquatic bed, emergent, scrub-shrub, and forested.

e8d9f957da12.title: Palustrine wetland
e8d9f957da12.sentence: - Scrub-shrub wetland is dominated by woody vegetation less than 20 feet tall, such as buttonbush, alders, and many kinds of saplings.

175ac2a22f4f.title: Palustrine wetland
175ac2a22f4f.sentence: - Forested palustrine wetland is dominated by woody vegetation over 20 feet tall.

b85416099e13.title: Freshwater marsh
b85416099e13.section: Types of freshwater marshes > Palustrine depressional
b85416099e13.sentence: These include but are not limited to vernal pools, playas or playa lakes, and prairie potholes.

0536a38a6846.title: Floodplain
0536a38a6846.section: Floodplain soils > Oxygen in floodplain soils
0536a38a6846.sentence: Floodplain soil composition is unique and varies widely based on microtopography.

934035a43ec6.title: Floodplain
934035a43ec6.section: Floodplain soils > Oxygen in floodplain soils
934035a43ec6.sentence: Floodplain soil stays aerated for long periods in between flooding events, but during flooding, saturated soil can become oxygen-depleted if it stands stagnant for long enough.

edb5513bb211.title: Floodplain
edb5513bb211.section: Floodplain soils > Oxygen in floodplain soils
edb5513bb211.sentence: More soil oxygen is available at higher elevations farther from the river.

0d8deed60287.title: Floodplain
0d8deed60287.section: Floodplain soils > Oxygen in floodplain soils
0d8deed60287.sentence: Floodplain forests generally experience alternating periods of aerobic and anaerobic soil microbe activity, affecting fine root development and desiccation.

88c802fee58f.title: Floodplain
88c802fee58f.section: Floodplain soils > Phosphorus cycling in floodplain soils
88c802fee58f.sentence: Floodplains have high buffering capacity for phosphorus to prevent nutrient loss to river outputs.

95107b0fa1fa.title: Floodplain
95107b0fa1fa.section: Floodplain soils > Phosphorus cycling in floodplain soils
95107b0fa1fa.sentence: Under conditions of stream connectivity, phosphorus is better able to be cycled, and sediments and nutrients are more readily retained.

bfb68045b397.title: Floodplain
bfb68045b397.section: Floodplain soils > Phosphorus cycling in floodplain soils
bfb68045b397.sentence: Wet/dry cycling within the floodplain greatly impacts phosphorus availability because it alters water level, redox state, pH, and physical properties of minerals.

c25ea0568658.title: Floodplain
c25ea0568658.section: Floodplain soils > Phosphorus cycling in floodplain soils
c25ea0568658.sentence: Dry soils that were previously inundated have reduced availability of phosphorus and increased affinity for obtaining phosphorus.

e1d5f953deac.title: Hillslope evolution
e1d5f953deac.sentence: Hillslope evolution is the changes in the erosion rates, erosion styles and form of slopes of hills and mountains over time.

7b6c9db94b54.title: Hillslope evolution
7b6c9db94b54.sentence: During most of the 20th century three models of hillslope evolution were widely diffused: slope decline, slope replacement and parallel slope retreat.

315fac52db1e.title: Hillslope evolution
315fac52db1e.sentence: Until the 1950s models of hillslope form evolution were central in geomorphology.

7eea2a1a3df5.title: Hillslope evolution
7eea2a1a3df5.sentence: Slope decline was proposed by William Morris Davis in his cycle of erosion theory.

8dc85afabc64.title: Hillslope evolution
8dc85afabc64.sentence: It consists of a gradual decrease in slope angle as stream incision slows down.

dd8cff76eeb1.title: Hillslope evolution
dd8cff76eeb1.sentence: This is accompanied by slopes becoming more gentle as they accumulate with fine-grained regolith stemming from weathering.

488c4f2e379b.title: Hillslope evolution
488c4f2e379b.sentence: Slope replacement was first proposed by Walther Penck challenging Davis' ideas on slope development.

6c8f7a54a9f1.title: Hillslope evolution
6c8f7a54a9f1.sentence: Slope replacement describes an evolution of slopes that is associated with decreasing rates of over-all erosion (denudation).

fc4d055b3762.title: Hillslope evolution
fc4d055b3762.sentence: It begins with a flattening of the lowermost slope that propagates upward and backward making the uppermost slope recede and decrease its angle while it remains steeper than the lower portions.

2d492384f285.title: Hillslope evolution
2d492384f285.sentence: In Penck's own words: "The flattening of slopes always occurs from the bottom upward".

18eb6131f262.title: Hillslope evolution
18eb6131f262.sentence: Slopes will evolve by parallel retreat when a slopes rock mass strength remains constant and basal debris, like talus, is continuously removed.

f0f2c15208e3.title: Hillslope evolution
f0f2c15208e3.sentence: In reality, however, such uniform rock strength is rare.

beccf2c83cb8.title: Hillslope evolution
beccf2c83cb8.sentence: Such a structural control, however, is often found in areas where hard horizontal rock layers of basalt or hard sedimentary rock overlie softer rocks.

e12b85d9c0eb.title: Hillslope evolution
e12b85d9c0eb.sentence: Parallel slope and scarp retreat, albeit proposed by early geomorphologists, was notably championed by Lester Charles King.

22434074df31.title: Hillslope evolution
22434074df31.sentence: King considered scarp retreat and the coalescence of pediments into pediplains a dominant processes across the globe.

d67841317b23.title: Hillslope evolution
d67841317b23.sentence: Further he claimed that slope decline was a special case of slope development seen only in very weak rocks that could not maintain a scarp.

da65aecef9ff.title: Hillslope evolution
da65aecef9ff.sentence: Slopes that are convex upslope and concave downslope and have no free face were held by King to be a form that became common in the late Tertiary.

1224c03da0c8.title: Hillslope evolution
1224c03da0c8.sentence: King argued that this was the result of more slowly acting surface wash caused by carpets of grass which in turn would have resulted in relatively more soil creep.

e4747856d65f.title: Hillslope evolution
e4747856d65f.sentence: The notion that slopes in an area do not develop all at the same time is known as unequal activity.

8f05a796c0ef.title: Hillslope evolution
8f05a796c0ef.sentence: Colin Hayter Crick, who coined the term, proposed that unequal activity may be regulated by removal of debris at the base of slopes.

009f90d970d2.title: Hillslope evolution
009f90d970d2.sentence: From this it is derived that landscapes and slopes with limited river erosion may in many cases be considered as stagnant in their evolution.

34d8dbd42e1c.title: Hillslope evolution
34d8dbd42e1c.sentence: The modern understanding is that the evolution of slopes is much more complex than the classical models of decline, replacement and retreat imply.

ef2bcec02027.title: Hydric soil
ef2bcec02027.sentence: A hydric soil is defined by federal law to mean "soil that, in its undrained condition, is saturated, flooded, or ponded long enough during a growing season to develop an anaerobic condition that supports the growth and regeneration of hydrophytic vegetation".

210d123b9f6f.title: Hydric soil
210d123b9f6f.sentence: This definition is provided in the controlling regulations to the Wetland Conservation Provisions of the FSA of 1985(7 C.F.R 12) and is used by the U.S.D.A. Natural Resources Conservation Service in the administration of the Wetland Conservation Compliance provisions ("Swampbuster") contained in the FSA of 1985.

32de0bc0bf36.title: Hydric soil
32de0bc0bf36.sentence: In adopting this definition in 1985, Congress attempted to capture the duration of waterlogged condition of a hydric soil by adding that a hydric soil is waterlogged long enough to support not only the growth of plants adapted to life in anaerobic conditions but also the regeneration of such plants.

1f0f3307ed1e.title: Hydric soil
1f0f3307ed1e.sentence: Another common definition of a hydric soils is provided by the National Technical Committee of Hydric Soils (NTCHS) as "a soil that formed under conditions of saturation, flooding, or ponding long enough during the growing season to develop anaerobic conditions in the upper part." The NTCHS hydric soil definition is used by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers and the Environmental Protection Agency in their joint responsibilities in the administration of Section 404 of the Clean Water Act (1972).

ab694ee6267d.title: Suffosion
ab694ee6267d.sentence: Suffosion is one of the two geological processes by which subsidence sinkholes or dolines are formed, the other being due to collapse of an underlying cave or void, with most sinkholes formed by the suffosion process.

08e3c10a2c64.title: Suffosion
08e3c10a2c64.sentence: Suffosion occurs when loose soil, loess, or other non-cohesive material lies on top of a limestone substratum containing fissures and joints.

2d3c87d5c9e9.title: Suffosion
2d3c87d5c9e9.sentence: Rain and surface water gradually wash this material through these fissures and into caves beneath.

779d9799b478.title: Suffosion
779d9799b478.sentence: Over time, this creates a depression on the landscape of varying depth.

f02940af2ebb.title: Suffosion
f02940af2ebb.sentence: Suffosion sinkholes are normally associated with karst topography although they may form in other types of rock including chalk, gypsum and basalt.

033aa1371a7a.title: Suffosion
033aa1371a7a.sentence: Suffosion is a destructive process that creates instability leading to collapse of the soil structure, characterized by both mass loss and volumetric contraction.

09dfe77673ba.title: Suffosion
09dfe77673ba.sentence: In suffosion, coarser particles lose their point-to-point contact.

1addb069fbfe.title: Suffosion
1addb069fbfe.sentence: This is in contrast to suffusion, which is non-destructive and is characterized by mass loss without change in volume.

36379a894b63.title: Suffosion
36379a894b63.sentence: In suffusion, coarser particles remain in point-to-point contact and fine particles are removed through the voids between them.

c2d3a19b3869.title: String bog
c2d3a19b3869.sentence: A string bog or string mire is a bog consisting of slightly elevated ridges and islands, with woody plants, alternating with flat, wet sedge mat areas.

3553038abe27.title: String bog
3553038abe27.sentence: String bogs occur on slightly sloping surfaces, with the ridges at right angles to the direction of water flow.

888061257740.title: String bog
888061257740.sentence: A string bog has a pattern of narrow (2–3 meters wide), low (less than 1 meter high) ridges oriented at right angles to the direction of drainage with wet depressions or pools occurring between the ridges.

fd01cb797d24.title: String bog
fd01cb797d24.sentence: The water and peat are very low in nutrients because the water has been derived from other ombrotrophic wetlands, which receive all of their water and nutrients from precipitation rather than from streams or springs.

a946e6ea8285.title: String bog
a946e6ea8285.sentence: The peat thickness is greater than 1 meter.

05356785bb4a.title: Bog
05356785bb4a.section: Types > By location and water source > Blanket bog
05356785bb4a.sentence: In periglacial climates a patterned form of blanket bog may occur, known as a string bog.

58bb5902529a.title: String bog
58bb5902529a.sentence: String bogs are features associated with periglacial climates, where the temperature results in long periods of subzero temperatures.

0a87a1b70d33.title: String bog
0a87a1b70d33.sentence: The active layer exists as a frozen ground for long periods and melts in the spring thaw.

ed892d59a262.title: String bog
ed892d59a262.sentence: String bogs are also known as aapa moors or aapa mires (from Finnish aapasuo) or Strangmoor (from the German).

2f44047f9824.title: Hummock
2f44047f9824.sentence: In geology, a hummock is a small knoll or mound above ground.

78f52e1dd72c.title: Hummock
78f52e1dd72c.sentence: They are typically less than 15 meters (50 ft) in height and tend to appear in groups or fields.

a487bc10cda1.title: Hummock
a487bc10cda1.sentence: Hummocks in the shape of low ridges of drier peat moss typically form part of the structure of certain types of raised bog, such as plateau, kermi, palsa or string bog.

fcb33254c8a3.title: Hummock
fcb33254c8a3.sentence: The hummocks alternate with shallow wet depressions or flarks.

e44eb75579df.title: Hummock
e44eb75579df.sentence: Swamp hummocks are mounds typically initiated as fallen trunks or branches covered with moss and rising above the swamp floor.

072264f5226f.title: Hummock
072264f5226f.sentence: The low-lying areas between hummocks are called hollows.

207e56c0688f.title: Hummock
207e56c0688f.sentence: They usually develop in fine-grained soils with light to moderate vegetation in areas of low relief where there is adequate moisture to fuel cryogenic processes.

a9ebd7ea0358.title: Hummock
a9ebd7ea0358.section: Cryogenic earth hummocks > Differential frost heave (cryostatic pressure hypothesis)
a9ebd7ea0358.sentence: This is the most widely accepted explanation of cryogenic hummock genesis.

b19a7ea56749.title: Hummock
b19a7ea56749.sentence: Hummock excavation normally reveals a disturbed soil profile, often with irregular streaks of organic matter or other colorations suggesting fluidity at some point in the past.

51bd7445edbc.title: Hummock
51bd7445edbc.sentence: The disturbance, a form of cryoturbation, often extends to a depth roughly equal to the hummock’s height.

0619575bc422.title: Soil-surface roughness
0619575bc422.sentence: Soil-surface roughness (SSR) are vertical variations present in the micro- and macro-relief of a soil surface, as well as their statistical distribution.

8a7dc03b1615.title: Soil-surface roughness
8a7dc03b1615.sentence: The two first classes account for the so-called microroughness, which has been shown to be largely influenced on an event and seasonal timescale by rainfall and tillage, respectively.

ff29fd735276.title: Soil-surface roughness
ff29fd735276.sentence: Microroughness is most commonly quantified by means of the Random Roughness, which is essentially the standard deviation of bed surface elevation data around the mean elevation, after correction for slope using the best-fit plane and removal of tillage effects in the individual height readings.

c18640eb4658.title: Soil-surface roughness
c18640eb4658.sentence: Rainfall impact can lead to either a decay or increase in microroughnesss, depending upon initial microroughness conditions and soil properties.

766ec221d21e.title: Soil-surface roughness
766ec221d21e.sentence: On rough soil surfaces, the action of rainsplash detachment tends to smoothen the edges of soil surface roughness, leading to an overall decrease in RR.

0e189523dc9b.title: Soil-surface roughness
0e189523dc9b.sentence: However, a recent study which examined the response of smooth soil surfaces on rainfall showed that RR can considerably increase for low initial microroughness length scales in the order of 0 – 5 mm.

5f00badfbc3e.title: Hydrosere
5f00badfbc3e.sentence: A hydrosere is a plant succession which occurs in an area of fresh water such as in oxbow lakes and kettle lakes.

e8061da1797b.title: Hydrosere
e8061da1797b.sentence: In time, an area of open freshwater will naturally dry out, ultimately becoming woodland.

a07592859403.title: Hydrosere
a07592859403.sentence: The early changes are allogenic as inorganic particles such as sand and clay are washed from catchment areas and begin filling the basin of the water body.

24b03620b7b1.title: Hydrosere
24b03620b7b1.sentence: Later, remains of dead plants also fill up these bodies and contribute to further changes in the environment.

7a3e860b21a7.title: Hydrosere
7a3e860b21a7.sentence: The succession from open water to climax woodland takes centuries or millennia.

f6b4d3d3a5ce.title: Hydrosere
f6b4d3d3a5ce.sentence: They settle down to the bottom of the pond after death, and decay into humus that mixes with silt and clay particles brought into the basin by run off water and wave action and form soil.

7abe24beac14.title: Hydrosere
7abe24beac14.sentence: As soil builds up, the pond becomes shallower and further environmental changes follow.

f2ff93d97300.title: Hydrosere
f2ff93d97300.sentence: These plants have creeping rhizomes which knit the mud together to produce large quantities of leaf litter.

f8033fd20adb.title: Hydrosere
f8033fd20adb.sentence: This litter is resistant to decay and reed peat builds up, accelerating the autogenic change.

dd261626211f.title: Hydrosere
dd261626211f.sentence: Eventually the sedge peat accumulates above the water level and soil is no longer totally waterlogged.

c1a0878e13dd.title: Hydrosere
c1a0878e13dd.sentence: The overall changes taking place during development of successional communities are building up of substratum, shallowing of water, addition of humus and minerals, soil building and aeration of soil.

b7c2d1ce946e.title: Pedotope
b7c2d1ce946e.sentence: Pedotope is the total soil component of the abiotic matrix present in an ecotope.

9147c034b8f7.title: Pedotope
9147c034b8f7.sentence: The pedotope is not one particular kind of soil, nor even the dominant kind of soil available in a location, but rather the total soil component (of all varieties) available in the location.

532b81384213.title: Mima mounds
532b81384213.sentence: Mima mounds /ˈmaɪmə/ are low, flattened, circular to oval, domelike, natural mounds that are composed of loose, unstratified, often gravelly sediment that is an overthickened A horizon.

478ea77de08c.title: Mima mounds
478ea77de08c.sentence: These mounds range in diameter from 3 m (9.8 ft) to more than 50 m (160 ft); in height 30 cm (12 in) to greater than 2 m (6.6 ft); and in concentration from several to greater than 50 mounds per hectare, at times forming conspicuous natural patterns.

b61802f74823.title: Mima mounds
b61802f74823.sentence: Theories for the origin of Mima mounds include burrowing by pocket gophers; accumulation of wind-blown (aeolian) sediments around vegetation to form coppice dunes or nebkhas; seismic ground shaking by major earthquakes, though none have been observed to form Mima mounds; and shrinking and swelling of clays in hog-wallow or gilgai landforms.

40c8276bdfee.title: Mima mounds
40c8276bdfee.sentence: Researchers in the 1940s found that Mima mounds tend to form in areas with poorly draining soils, so the "Fossorial Rodent Hypothesis" proposed that gophers build mounds as an evolutionary response to low water tables.

bed3cc6ebf78.title: Mima mounds
bed3cc6ebf78.sentence: Metal tracers implanted in a Mima mound field in San Diego demonstrated that gophers unexpectedly pushed soil upwards towards the center of the mounds instead of pushing the soil downward.

8bc47606e913.title: Mima mounds
8bc47606e913.sentence: However, the mounds were already fully formed and the gophers may have just been maintaining them.

d27d706e94da.title: Mima mounds
d27d706e94da.sentence: These Mima Mounds are typically located on stable landforms that are greater than 100,000 years old.

264011db0f0b.title: Hillslope evolution
264011db0f0b.sentence: Contrary to early conceptual models that attempt to predict slope form a number of numerical models of erosion focus on describing what is happening at any given time, and are not concerned with changes in form.

ef6201386c16.title: Hillslope evolution
ef6201386c16.sentence: Using the heat transfer equation of Fourier as template W.E.H. Culling reasoned the flux of mass across the height gradient of a slope would could be described in a similar fashion as:

4f0158305b5d.title: Hillslope evolution
4f0158305b5d.sentence: K is a rate constant (L2/T), and ∇z the gradient or height difference between two points at a slope divided by their horizontal distance.

a7444a1a20f0.title: Hillslope evolution
a7444a1a20f0.sentence: This model imply sediment fluxes can be estimated from the slope angles (∇z).

3b9d75b9c016.title: Hillslope evolution
3b9d75b9c016.sentence: This has been shown to be true for low-angle slopes.

cd3d3f27e0e1.title: Hillslope evolution
cd3d3f27e0e1.sentence: For more steep slopes it is not possible to infer sediment fluxes.

7343c041deb7.title: Hillslope evolution
7343c041deb7.sentence: Sc stands here for the critical gradient which at which erosion and sediment fluxes runs away.

29fa1662f542.title: Hillslope evolution
29fa1662f542.sentence: On the contrary when ∇z approaches Sc erosion rates becomes extremely high.

443cdaab921d.title: Hillslope evolution
443cdaab921d.sentence: This last feature may represent the behavior of landslides in steep terrain.

c16648cfa01e.title: Hillslope evolution
c16648cfa01e.sentence: As shown by equation 2 the angle of steep slopes changes very little even at very high increases of erosion rates, meaning that it is not possible to infer erosion rates from topography in steep slopes other than hinting they are much higher than for lower angle slopes.

f5ec0b797494.title: Hillslope evolution
f5ec0b797494.sentence: Beginning with the works of Grove Karl Gilbert (1909) and William Morris Davis (1892), soil-mantled convex or parabolic hills have long been held to reflect steady state equilibrium conditions of soil production and soil erosion.

6b76e437f275.title: Hillslope evolution
6b76e437f275.sentence: Contrary to what an equilibrium between the erosion rates functions described above and the soil production function should imply soil depth can vary considerably in parabolic hills as result of stochastic bedrock weathering into soil.

6ddcee47dea5.title: Hillslope evolution
6ddcee47dea5.sentence: This means that the expected soil formation rates from the soil production function might vary greatly across a landscape in geomorphic equilibrium.

3e383846d295.title: Hillslope evolution
3e383846d295.sentence: Numerical modelling indicate that in periglacial settings broad low-angle convex hilltops can form in no less than millions of years.

9b514a2ffe6b.title: Hillslope evolution
9b514a2ffe6b.sentence: Convex hills are often associated to tors.

1e2e661f85f2.title: Hillslope evolution
1e2e661f85f2.sentence: The presence of numerous tors would thus indicate that the original landscape was steeper and not flatter than present-day landscape.

0730d45ec694.title: Irrigation
0730d45ec694.sentence: Irrigation in agriculture is the practice of applying controlled amounts of water to land to help grow crops, landscape plants, and lawns.

ea0ebdc43617.title: Irrigation
ea0ebdc43617.sentence: Irrigation has been a key aspect of agriculture for over 5,000 years and has been developed by many cultures worldwide.

1fc1aba53142.title: Irrigation
1fc1aba53142.sentence: Some of the earliest known use of the technology dates to the 6th millennium BCE in Khuzistan in the south-west of Iran.

20bceea3d5b1.title: Irrigation
20bceea3d5b1.sentence: Irrigation helps to grow crops, maintain landscapes, and revegetate disturbed soils in dry areas and during times of below-average rainfall.

ffc0248756d7.title: Irrigation
ffc0248756d7.sentence: In addition to these uses, irrigation is also employed to protect crops from frost, suppress weed growth in grain fields, and prevent soil consolidation.

4a9eca4c39d6.title: Irrigation
4a9eca4c39d6.sentence: Irrigation water can come from groundwater (extracted from springs or by using wells), from surface water (withdrawn from rivers, lakes or reservoirs) or from non-conventional sources like treated wastewater, desalinated water, drainage water, or fog collection.

d64787ac4e91.title: Irrigation
d64787ac4e91.sentence: Irrigation can be supplementary to rainfall, which is common in many parts of the world as rainfed agriculture, or it can be full irrigation, where crops rarely rely on any contribution from rainfall.

96ba15903bf3.title: Irrigation
96ba15903bf3.sentence: Full irrigation is less common and occurs only in arid landscapes with very low rainfall or when crops are grown in semi-arid areas outside the rainy season.

03f23039fff1.title: Irrigation
03f23039fff1.sentence: Several irrigation methods differ in how water is supplied to plants.

d0538391216d.title: Irrigation
d0538391216d.sentence: Surface irrigation, also known as gravity irrigation, is the oldest form of irrigation and has been in use for thousands of years.

19e617455606.title: Irrigation
19e617455606.sentence: In sprinkler irrigation, water is piped to one or more central locations within the field and distributed by overhead high-pressure water devices.

59e93eacc234.title: Irrigation
59e93eacc234.sentence: Micro-irrigation is a system that distributes water under low pressure through a piped network and applies it as a small discharge to each plant.

a54bd6cc981d.title: Irrigation
a54bd6cc981d.sentence: It involves artificially raising the water table to moisten the soil below the root zone of plants.

d00d3c2186e8.title: Irrigation
d00d3c2186e8.sentence: The global land area equipped for irrigation reached 355 million ha in 2023, an increase of 23% from the 289 million ha of 2000 and more than twice the land area equipped for irrigation in the 1960s.

65eab86c7e3c.title: Irrigation
65eab86c7e3c.sentence: The world’s total irrigated land area more than doubled between 1964 and 2023 and by 2023, 23% of all croplands were equipped for irrigation.

e35d338d3b9d.title: Irrigation
e35d338d3b9d.sentence: On average, the yield of irrigated land is 76% higher than that of rain fed land.

45b603aa1bc3.title: Irrigation
45b603aa1bc3.sentence: Drainage, which involves the removal of surface and sub-surface water from a given location, is often studied in conjunction with irrigation.

16aeca097138.title: Irrigation
16aeca097138.sentence: Often both may be required together to assure sustained high-level production of crops.

8923b78355d4.title: Irrigation
8923b78355d4.sentence: Over-irrigation can cause deep drainage from rising water tables, which can lead to irrigation salinity problems, requiring watertable control through some form of subsurface land drainage.

21e321ba82c9.title: Irrigation
21e321ba82c9.sentence: - Underirrigation or irrigation giving only just enough water for the plant (e.g., in drip line irrigation) gives poor soil salinity control, which leads to increased soil salinity with consequent buildup of toxic salts on the soil surface in areas with high evaporation.

0b6f1da5e9f3.title: Crop rotation
0b6f1da5e9f3.sentence: Crop rotation is the practice of growing a series of different types of crops in the same area across a sequence of growing seasons.

afdbf6c46da9.title: Crop rotation
afdbf6c46da9.sentence: This practice reduces the reliance of crops on one set of nutrients, pest and weed pressure, along with the probability of developing resistant pests and weeds.

bb2c2c8d6d02.title: Crop rotation
bb2c2c8d6d02.sentence: Conversely, a well-designed crop rotation can reduce the need for synthetic fertilizers and herbicides by better using ecosystem services from a diverse set of crops.

4ae371a90945.title: Crop rotation
4ae371a90945.sentence: Additionally, crop rotations can improve soil structure and organic matter, which reduces erosion and increases farm system resilience.

805489f5a508.title: Crop rotation
805489f5a508.sentence: A great advantage of crop rotation comes from the interrelationship of nitrogen-fixing crops with nitrogen-demanding crops.

8091e307bbea.title: Crop rotation
8091e307bbea.sentence: Legumes, like alfalfa and clover, collect available nitrogen from the atmosphere and store it in nodules on their root structure.

b59a509563f6.title: Crop rotation
b59a509563f6.sentence: When the plant is harvested, the biomass of uncollected roots breaks down, making the stored nitrogen available to future crops.

db83069ff002.title: Crop rotation
db83069ff002.sentence: The changing of crops in a sequence decreases the population level of pests by (1) interrupting pest life cycles and (2) interrupting pest habitat.

ff9770c14d69.title: Crop rotation
ff9770c14d69.sentence: Plants within the same taxonomic family tend to have similar pests and pathogens.

9f1117e42c04.title: Crop rotation
9f1117e42c04.sentence: For example, giving adequate attention to plant family is essential to mitigating pests and pathogens.

7d34e0213647.title: Crop rotation
7d34e0213647.sentence: Crop rotations greatly increase soil organic carbon (SOC) content, the main constituent of soil organic matter.

3a19f9970823.title: Crop rotation
3a19f9970823.sentence: Highly diverse rotations spanning long periods of time have shown to be even more effective in increasing SOC, while soil disturbances (e.g. from tillage) are responsible for exponential decline in SOC levels.

eda056099b60.title: Crop rotation
eda056099b60.sentence: In Brazil, conversion to no-till methods combined with intensive crop rotations has been shown an SOC sequestration rate of 0.41 tonnes per hectare per year.

1d138b980dc3.title: Crop rotation
1d138b980dc3.sentence: From the 9th century to the 11th century, farmers in Europe transitioned from a two-field system to a three-field system.

c25cda40c60c.title: Crop rotation
c25cda40c60c.sentence: The sequence of four crops (wheat, turnips, barley and clover), included a fodder crop and a grazing crop, allowing livestock to be bred year-round.

f95e1c518350.title: Crop rotation
f95e1c518350.sentence: The four-field crop rotation became a key development in the British Agricultural Revolution.

f3f58b4eb99c.title: Crop rotation
f3f58b4eb99c.sentence: Improper implementation of a crop rotation plan may lead to imbalances in the soil nutrient composition or a buildup of pathogens affecting a critical crop.

dc880487ac15.title: Crop rotation
dc880487ac15.sentence: The consequences of faulty rotation may take years to become apparent even to experienced soil scientists and can take just as long to correct.

9553ba9a6b56.title: Crop rotation
9553ba9a6b56.sentence: The British agriculturist Charles Townshend (1674–1738) popularised this system in the 18th century.

1fe652901089.title: Leaching (agriculture)
1fe652901089.sentence: In agriculture, leaching is the loss of water-soluble plant nutrients from the soil, due to rain and irrigation.

84e05910a186.title: Leaching (agriculture)
84e05910a186.sentence: Soil structure, crop planting, type and application rates of fertilizers, and other factors are taken into account to avoid excessive nutrient loss.

4f933c6bf23b.title: Leaching (agriculture)
4f933c6bf23b.sentence: Leaching may also refer to the practice of applying a small amount of excess irrigation where the water has a high salt content to avoid salts from building up in the soil (salinity control).

6367113f8546.title: Leaching (agriculture)
6367113f8546.sentence: Where this is practiced, drainage must also usually be employed, to carry away the excess water.

3b8e8dead891.title: Leaching (agriculture)
3b8e8dead891.sentence: Leaching is a natural environment concern when it contributes to groundwater contamination.

1118b5c87344.title: Leaching (agriculture)
1118b5c87344.sentence: As water from rain, flooding, or other sources seeps into the ground, it can dissolve chemicals and carry them into the underground water supply.

a2cfd6b18bd4.title: Leaching (agriculture)
a2cfd6b18bd4.sentence: Of particular concern are hazardous waste dumps and landfills, and, in agriculture, excess fertilizer, improperly stored animal manure, and biocides (e.g. pesticides, fungicides, insecticides and herbicides).

51e00336769e.title: Leaching (agriculture)
51e00336769e.sentence: Finally, leaching of NO3 from acidic sources can increase the loss of calcium and other soil nutrients, thereby reducing an ecosystem's productivity.

efe9cee9a18c.title: Cover crop
efe9cee9a18c.sentence: The catch crops take up surplus nitrogen remaining from fertilization of the previous crop, preventing it from being lost through leaching, or gaseous denitrification or volatilization.

6b0cded247b1.title: Land reclamation
6b0cded247b1.sentence: Land reclamation, often known as reclamation, and also known as land fill (not to be confused with a waste landfill), is the process of creating new land from oceans, seas, riverbeds or lake beds.

a27aab485369.title: Land reclamation
a27aab485369.sentence: The land reclaimed is known as reclamation ground, reclaimed land, or land fill.

e3d47f33b7f6.title: Land reclamation
e3d47f33b7f6.sentence: The simplest method involves filling the area with large amounts of heavy rock or cement, then filling with clay and dirt until the desired height is reached.

517b91db1dc6.title: Land reclamation
517b91db1dc6.sentence: The process is called "infilling" and the material used to fill the space is generally called "infill".

484aaf8c9586.title: Land reclamation
484aaf8c9586.sentence: Draining of submerged wetlands is often used to reclaim land for agricultural use.

d0cb3b503af4.title: Land reclamation
d0cb3b503af4.sentence: Land dredging is also another method of land reclamation.

d1a98b405727.title: Land reclamation
d1a98b405727.sentence: In ancient Egypt, the rulers of the Twelfth Dynasty (c. 2000–1800 BC) undertook a far-sighted land reclamation scheme to increase agricultural output.

05f1a628573b.title: Land reclamation
05f1a628573b.sentence: They constructed levees and canals to connect the Faiyum with the Bahr Yussef waterway, diverting water that would have flowed into Lake Moeris and causing gradual evaporation around the lake's edges, creating new farmland from the reclaimed land.

6118981bdd12.title: Land reclamation
6118981bdd12.sentence: Netherlands | About 1 ⁄ 6 (almost 17%) of the entire country, or about 7,000 km 2 (2,700 sq mi) in total, has been reclaimed from the sea, lakes, marshes and swamps. The province of Flevoland has almost completely been reclaimed from the Zuiderzee.

784fa0ab1db5.title: Land reclamation
784fa0ab1db5.section: List of reclaimed land by country and territory

3620fc19d9bf.title: Land reclamation
3620fc19d9bf.sentence: Reclaimed land is highly susceptible to soil liquefaction during earthquakes, which can amplify the amount of damage that occurs to buildings and infrastructure.

47600f5a5c05.title: Soil consolidation
47600f5a5c05.sentence: Types of construction project where consolidation often poses technical risk include land reclamation, the construction of embankments, and tunnel and basement excavation in clay.

f234620c96ff.title: Land reclamation
f234620c96ff.sentence: Subsidence is another issue, both from soil compaction on filled land, and also when wetlands are enclosed by levees and drained to create polders.

45d59034e1f7.title: Land reclamation
45d59034e1f7.sentence: Drained marshes will eventually sink below the surrounding water level, increasing the danger from flooding.

7ef162840384.title: Land reclamation
7ef162840384.sentence: Draining wetlands for ploughing, for example, is a form of habitat destruction.

e82b451ed299.title: Land reclamation
e82b451ed299.sentence: It is estimated that nearly 65% of tidal flats around the Yellow Sea have been reclaimed.

9c2845fbb4d7.title: Land reclamation
9c2845fbb4d7.sentence: In some parts of the world, new reclamation projects are restricted or no longer allowed, due to environmental protection laws.

d19c8ae25bc0.title: Land reclamation
d19c8ae25bc0.sentence: Another early large-scale project was the Beemster Polder in the Netherlands, adding 70 square kilometres (27 sq mi) of land in 1612.

80ef507f083b.title: Herbicide
80ef507f083b.sentence: Herbicides (US: /ˈɜːrbɪsaɪdz/, UK: /ˈhɜːr-/), also commonly known as weed killers, are substances used to control undesired plants, also known as weeds.

8ece327161cf.title: Herbicide
8ece327161cf.sentence: Selective herbicides control specific weed species while leaving the desired crop relatively unharmed, while non-selective herbicides (sometimes called "total weed killers") kill plants indiscriminately.

10f1a65b0749.title: Herbicide
10f1a65b0749.sentence: The combined effects of herbicides, nitrogen fertilizer, and improved cultivars has increased yields (per acre) of major crops by three to six times from 1900 to 2000.

a85800efbbc2.title: Herbicide
a85800efbbc2.sentence: Prior to the widespread use of herbicides, cultural controls, such as altering soil pH, salinity, or fertility levels, were used to control weeds.

d7bf67da9f2b.title: Herbicide
d7bf67da9f2b.sentence: The major breakthroughs occurred during the Second World War as the result of research conducted independently in the United Kingdom and the United States into the potential use of herbicides in war.

e0918766988d.title: Herbicide
e0918766988d.sentence: It was marketed as Roundup in 1971.

d45dc9d92103.title: Herbicide
d45dc9d92103.sentence: Since the development of glyphosate-resistant crop plants, it is now used very extensively for selective weed control in growing crops.

35ab97e47528.title: Herbicide
35ab97e47528.section: Health and environmental effects > Ecological effects
35ab97e47528.sentence: Herbicide use generally has negative impacts on many aspects of the environment.

d5510e79ca25.title: Herbicide
d5510e79ca25.section: Health and environmental effects > Ecological effects
d5510e79ca25.sentence: Insects, non-targeted plants, animals, and aquatic systems subject to serious damage from herbicides.

bca277afc04e.title: Herbicide
bca277afc04e.sentence: One major complication to the use of herbicides for weed control is the ability of plants to evolve herbicide resistance, rendering the herbicides ineffective against target plants.

019be8f5e8e3.title: Herbicide
019be8f5e8e3.section: Resistance > Approaches to treating resistant weeds > Mixtures and sequences
019be8f5e8e3.sentence: The use of two or more herbicides which have differing modes of action can reduce the selection for resistant genotypes.

c6a3b8caa08c.title: Carbon farming
c6a3b8caa08c.sentence: Another criticism says that no-till practices may increase herbicide use, diminishing or eliminating carbon benefits.

981267a88afe.title: Agricultural soil science
981267a88afe.sentence: Agricultural soil science is a branch of soil science that deals with the study of edaphic conditions as they relate to the production of food and fiber.

3108958724fe.title: Agricultural soil science
3108958724fe.sentence: In this context, it is also a constituent of the field of agronomy and is thus also described as soil agronomy.

d05e07900815.title: Agricultural soil science
d05e07900815.sentence: Prior to the development of pedology in the 19th century, agricultural soil science (or edaphology) was the only branch of soil science.

a984fd585b64.title: Soil
a984fd585b64.sentence: Agricultural soil science was the primeval domain of soil knowledge, long time before the advent of pedology in the 19th century.

d0a1962de905.title: Agricultural soil science
d0a1962de905.sentence: Agricultural soil science studies the chemical, physical, biological, and mineralogical composition of soils as they relate to agriculture.

a5424616372f.title: Agricultural soil science
a5424616372f.sentence: Agricultural soil scientists develop methods that will improve the use of soil and increase the production of food and fiber crops.

5e52c5ffc8dc.title: Agricultural soil science
5e52c5ffc8dc.section: Kinds of soil and their variables
5e52c5ffc8dc.sentence: Some soil variables of special interest to agricultural soil science are:

0b41baef7207.title: Agricultural soil science
0b41baef7207.section: Kinds of soil and their variables
0b41baef7207.sentence: - Soil texture or soil composition: Soils are composed of solid particles of various sizes.

fee31960eccc.title: Agricultural soil science
fee31960eccc.section: Kinds of soil and their variables
fee31960eccc.sentence: - Aeration and porosity: Atmospheric air contains elements such as oxygen, nitrogen, carbon and others.

59dbd1d684fb.title: Agricultural soil science
59dbd1d684fb.section: Kinds of soil and their variables
59dbd1d684fb.sentence: - Drainage: In soils of bad drainage the water delivered through rain or irrigation may pool and stagnate.

b5ee6dee8aab.title: Agricultural soil science
b5ee6dee8aab.section: Kinds of soil and their variables
b5ee6dee8aab.sentence: - Water content: Without soil moisture, more exactly when soil moisture falls below the wilting point, there is no transpiration, no growth and plants wilt.

dcb50a938184.title: Agricultural soil science
dcb50a938184.section: Kinds of soil and their variables
dcb50a938184.sentence: - Water potential: Water potential describes the tendency of the water to flow from one area of the soil to another.

d945d8fa0678.title: Agricultural soil science
d945d8fa0678.section: Kinds of soil and their variables
d945d8fa0678.sentence: - Horizonation: Typically found in advanced and mature soils, horizonation refers to the creation of soil layers with differing characteristics.

8791c473c03c.title: Agricultural soil science
8791c473c03c.section: Kinds of soil and their variables
8791c473c03c.sentence: - Fertility: A fertile soil is one rich in nutrients and organic matter.

1cad81672395.title: Agricultural soil science
1cad81672395.section: Kinds of soil and their variables
1cad81672395.sentence: - Soil acidity or soil pH and cation-exchange capacity: Root cells act as hydrogen pumps and the surrounding concentration of hydrogen ions affects their ability to absorb nutrients. pH is a measure of this concentration.

4ef7be86f649.title: Agricultural soil science
4ef7be86f649.sentence: They conduct research in irrigation and drainage, tillage, soil classification, plant nutrition, soil fertility, and other areas, e.g. greenhouse effect mitigation.

3ac7c1a640c9.title: Agricultural soil science
3ac7c1a640c9.sentence: Soil degradation such as erosion, compaction, lowered fertility, and contamination continue to be serious concerns.

de35368f2a19.title: Agricultural soil science
de35368f2a19.sentence: Emphasis continues to grow on the importance of soil sustainability.

dc89428c1e27.title: Agricultural soil science
dc89428c1e27.sentence: Agricultural soil scientists study ways to make soils more productive and to make this production sustainable in the long term.

86a2d74cec31.title: Agricultural soil science
86a2d74cec31.sentence: Although maximizing agricultural production (both plant and animal) is a valid goal in the frame of human population growth, sometimes it may come at high cost which can be readily evident, e.g. massive crop diseases stemming from monocultures, or the long-term impact of chemical fertilizers and pesticides on groundwater contamination and human health.

5293dc3081a2.title: Edaphology
5293dc3081a2.section: Areas of study > Agricultural soil science
5293dc3081a2.sentence: Soil husbandry is a strong tradition within agricultural soil science.

89f518497a56.title: Potting soil
89f518497a56.sentence: Potting soil or growing media, also known as potting mix or potting compost (UK), is a substrate used to grow plants in containers.

472135e54f75.title: Potting soil
472135e54f75.sentence: Despite the name, this mixture typically uses little to no actual soil.

54b77d2a9069.title: Potting soil
54b77d2a9069.sentence: Soils are minimally used as growing media because they compact and lose pore space after repeated watering and can be too heavy for growing potted plants.

5891a511dea3.title: Potting soil
5891a511dea3.sentence: Materials used in the preparation of growing media include but are not limited to: peat, vermiculite, coconut coir, treebark chips, wood fibers, perlite, mineral wool, small amounts of actual soil, recycled paper fibers, rice hulls, sand and calcined clays.

a56b49f7c213.title: Potting soil
a56b49f7c213.sentence: Mediums used for growing plants in pots typically are a mix of organic and inorganic ingredients.

1d05c0d9e49c.title: Potting soil
1d05c0d9e49c.sentence: Typical potting mixes include one or more materials which retain moisture, one or more materials which aid in aeration and drainage, and fertilizer.

b23e0d5db2ee.title: Potting soil
b23e0d5db2ee.sentence: Moisture-retaining materials and aerating materials can be combined in any ratio, depending on the particular needs of the plant.

87260ffb9a51.title: Potting soil
87260ffb9a51.sentence: Good growing mediums have a number of properties including moisture and nutrient retention capacity, quick water infiltration, pore space for aeration (plants roots need oxygen), drainage for excess water, decompose slowly, and provide support for the plants growing in them.

3237a930bcdf.title: Potting soil
3237a930bcdf.sentence: They also have an optimal range of pH, cation exchange properties, and lack substance that are toxic to plants These are also dependent on the type of plant grown since there is wide variation in moisture and nutrient needs among different plants.

ee033bc55968.title: Potting soil
ee033bc55968.sentence: This part is usually made up of peat (usually with limestone to reduce acidity) or coconut coir.

73503621e181.title: Potting soil
73503621e181.sentence: Limestone (for raising pH) contains mostly calcium (calcite), but can also contain magnesium (dolomitic).

ed0acd14141c.title: Potting soil
ed0acd14141c.sentence: The latter is preferred as it supplies both elements.

1f32134c6688.title: Potting soil
1f32134c6688.sentence: A typical proportion of limestone to peat is 8.5 pounds per cubic yard (5.0 kg/m3).

f1bdfad80828.title: Potting soil
f1bdfad80828.sentence: Coir contains a high amount of electrolytes (salts).

af4a607f86b9.title: Potting soil
af4a607f86b9.sentence: In fact, untreated coir contains too much sodium and potassium for plant growth, so it is washed and then buffered (partially replacing salts with other minerals, usually calcium and magnesium) to produce the growth medium.

9c931d9e85bd.title: Potting soil
9c931d9e85bd.sentence: The use of peat is controversial since the harvesting of peat moss from peatlands (which includes unique habitats such as bogs and fens) can degrade these peatlands.

c7fef16bcc13.title: Potting soil
c7fef16bcc13.sentence: Peat also has a very slow accumulation rate, as little as 1mm per year, so they take a long time to regenerate.

529033835995.title: Potting soil
529033835995.sentence: Peatlands are also carbon sinks, constituting 3% of the world's surface but storing up to 30% of the carbon sequestered in the soil.

6252c9157aff.title: Potting soil
6252c9157aff.sentence: Commercially available potting soil is usually sterilized, in order to avoid the spread of weeds and plant diseases.

341a478c6002.title: Potting soil
341a478c6002.sentence: Legionnaires' disease outbreaks due to potting mix have been reported in Australia, New Zealand, the Netherlands, the United States, and Japan.

11aecd01a609.title: Potting soil
11aecd01a609.sentence: The first recorded use of the term is from an 1861 issue of the American Agriculturist.

8b73215031c9.title: Organic farming
8b73215031c9.sentence: Organic farming, also known as organic agriculture or ecological farming, or biological farming, is an agricultural system that emphasizes the use of naturally occurring, non-synthetic inputs, such as compost manure, green manure, and bone meal and places emphasis on techniques such as crop rotation, companion planting, and mixed cropping.

a9de7c1bb580.title: Organic farming
a9de7c1bb580.sentence: Organic agriculture can be defined as "an integrated farming system that strives for sustainability, the enhancement of soil fertility and biological diversity while, with rare exceptions, prohibiting synthetic pesticides, antibiotics, synthetic fertilizers, genetically modified organisms, and growth hormones".

38a6918dc288.title: Organic farming
38a6918dc288.sentence: It originated early in the 20th century in reaction to rapidly changing farming practices.

19b5cb190ad4.title: Organic farming
19b5cb190ad4.sentence: These new agricultural techniques, while beneficial in the short-term, had serious longer-term side-effects, such as soil compaction, erosion, and declines in overall soil fertility, along with health concerns about toxic chemicals entering the food supply.

beaaf45f6905.title: Organic farming
beaaf45f6905.sentence: In 1940, Howard published his An Agricultural Testament.

ac919c999fa3.title: Organic farming
ac919c999fa3.sentence: In this book he adopted Northbourne's terminology of "organic farming".

01058d70b6f0.title: Organic farming
01058d70b6f0.sentence: Howard's work spread widely, and he became known as the "father of organic farming" for his work in applying scientific knowledge and principles to various traditional and natural methods.

58d09f2b592f.title: Organic farming
58d09f2b592f.sentence: As of 2022, organic farming is practiced in 188 countries and approximately 96,000,000 hectares (240,000,000 acres) worldwide were farmed organically by 4.5 million farmers, representing approximately 2 percent of total world farmland.

f894364f9d07.title: Organic farming
f894364f9d07.sentence: A 2012 meta-analysis found that productivity is on average 25% lower for organic farming than conventional farming.

74c02b4bd8f8.title: Organic farming
74c02b4bd8f8.sentence: Another meta-analysis published in the journal Agricultural Systems in 2011 analyzed 362 datasets and found that organic yields were on average 80% of conventional yields.

462efe96934b.title: Organic farming
462efe96934b.sentence: According to a 2012 meta-analysis of 71 studies, nitrogen leaching, nitrous oxide emissions, ammonia emissions, eutrophication potential and acidification potential were higher for organic products.

710323b72296.title: Organic farming
710323b72296.sentence: Specifically, the emission per area of land is lower, but per amount of food produced is higher.

49140e649451.title: Organic farming
49140e649451.sentence: This is due to the lower crop yield of organic farms.

8753a1eff453.title: Organic farming
8753a1eff453.sentence: Organic farming can be beneficial on biodiversity and environmental protection at local level; however, because organic farming can produce lower yields compared to intensive farming, leading to increased pressure to convert more non-agricultural land to agricultural use in order to produce similar yields, it can cause loss of biodiversity and negative climate effects.

8e8cd9a4e971.title: Surface irrigation
8e8cd9a4e971.sentence: Surface irrigation is where water is applied and distributed over the soil surface by gravity.

af5d4d5b5eb8.title: Surface irrigation
af5d4d5b5eb8.sentence: It is by far the most common form of irrigation throughout the world and has been practiced in many areas virtually unchanged for thousands of years.

b0e4e82813ab.title: Surface irrigation
b0e4e82813ab.sentence: Surface irrigation is often referred to as flood irrigation, implying that the water distribution is uncontrolled and therefore, inherently inefficient.

143ce58d6ff8.title: Surface irrigation
143ce58d6ff8.sentence: In reality, some of the irrigation practices grouped under this name involve a significant degree of management (for example surge irrigation).

de90dc6917b2.title: Surface irrigation
de90dc6917b2.sentence: The process of surface irrigation can be described using four phases.

6efa23de5b9e.title: Surface irrigation
6efa23de5b9e.sentence: The advance phase refers to that length of time as water is applied to the top end of the field and flows or advances over the field length.

c21d57e0ebee.title: Surface irrigation
c21d57e0ebee.sentence: The period of time between the end of the advance phase and the shut-off of the inflow is termed the wetting, ponding or storage phase.

ec8a32430e05.title: Surface irrigation
ec8a32430e05.sentence: The depletion phase is that short period of time after cut-off when the length of the field is still submerged.

6deb0326a3aa.title: Surface irrigation
6deb0326a3aa.sentence: The recession phase describes the time period while the water front is retreating towards the downstream end of the field.

9d1a21498cb8.title: Surface irrigation
9d1a21498cb8.sentence: The depth of water applied to any point in the field is a function of the opportunity time, the length of time for which water is present on the soil surface.

a06d000c562d.title: Surface irrigation
a06d000c562d.section: Types of surface irrigation > Bay/border strip irrigation
a06d000c562d.sentence: Border strip, otherwise known as border check or bay irrigation could be considered as a hybrid of level basin and furrow irrigation.

4ab3ac4fe824.title: Surface irrigation
4ab3ac4fe824.section: Types of surface irrigation > Bay/border strip irrigation
4ab3ac4fe824.sentence: The field is divided into a number of bays or strips, each bay is separated by raised earth check banks (borders).

4bc67f140489.title: Surface irrigation
4bc67f140489.section: Types of surface irrigation > Bay/border strip irrigation
4bc67f140489.sentence: The bays are typically longer and narrower compared to basin irrigation and are orientated to align lengthwise with the slope of the field.

b4483b38be41.title: Surface irrigation
b4483b38be41.section: Types of surface irrigation > Bay/border strip irrigation
b4483b38be41.sentence: One common use of this technique includes the irrigation of pasture for dairy production.

e6e93cbbec74.title: Surface irrigation
e6e93cbbec74.sentence: - Waterlogging – Can cause the plant to shut down delaying further growth until sufficient water drains from the rootzone.

782446278b26.title: Surface irrigation
782446278b26.sentence: - Deep drainage - Overirrigation may cause water to move below the root zone resulting in rising water tables.

4500a05d5f92.title: Surface irrigation
4500a05d5f92.sentence: In regions with naturally occurring saline soil layers (for example salinity in south eastern Australia) or saline aquifers, these rising water tables may bring salt up into the root zone leading to problems of irrigation salinity.

37bdd5726bdd.title: Surface irrigation
37bdd5726bdd.sentence: While this is a lesser issue for surface irrigation compared to other irrigation methods (due to the comparatively high leaching fraction), lack of subsurface drainage may restrict the leaching of salts from the soil.

0e134b6e446f.title: Monocropping
0e134b6e446f.sentence: In agriculture, monocropping is the practice of growing a single crop year after year on the same land.

256005294a51.title: Monocropping
256005294a51.sentence: Monocropping is also referred to as continuous cropping, as in "continuous corn." Monocropping allows for farmers to have consistent crops throughout their entire farm.

5e82be433926.title: Monocropping
5e82be433926.sentence: Maize, soybeans, and wheat are three common crops often monocropped.

1d5ad77594d7.title: Monocropping
1d5ad77594d7.sentence: They can plant only the most profitable crop, use the same seed, pest control, machinery, and growing method on their entire farm, which may increase overall farm profitability.

5e9e87bb462d.title: Crop rotation
5e9e87bb462d.sentence: Growing the same crop in the same place for many years in a row, known as monocropping, gradually depletes the soil of certain nutrients and promotes the proliferation of specialized pest and weed populations adapted to that crop system.

415e3395bdcc.title: Monocropping
415e3395bdcc.sentence: While economically a very efficient system, allowing for specialization in equipment and crop production, monocropping is also controversial, as it damages the soil ecology (including depletion or reduction in diversity of soil nutrients) and provide an unbuffered niche for parasitic species, increasing crop vulnerability to opportunistic insects, plants, and microorganisms.

1822a7381ac7.title: Monocropping
1822a7381ac7.sentence: The result is a more fragile ecosystem with an increased dependency on pesticides and artificial fertilizers.

430521c21e7b.title: Monocropping
430521c21e7b.sentence: The concentrated presence of a single cultivar, genetically adapted with a single resistance strategy, presents a situation in which an entire crop can be wiped out very quickly by a single opportunistic species.

177bca160016.title: Monocropping
177bca160016.sentence: An example of this would be the Great Famine of Ireland in 1845–1849.

4ff3165d2911.title: Monocropping
4ff3165d2911.sentence: For example, a well-known concern is pesticides and fertilizers seeping into surrounding soil and groundwater from extensive monocropped acreage in the U.S. and abroad.

8d3c930b2e68.title: Monocropping
8d3c930b2e68.sentence: The controversies surrounding monocropping are complex, but traditionally the core issues concern the balance between its advantages in increasing short-term food production—especially in hunger-prone regions—and its disadvantages with respect to long-term land stewardship and the fostering of local economic independence and ecological sustainability.

b513c2ee3213.title: Monocropping
b513c2ee3213.sentence: Advocates of monocropping believe polyculture production would be costly and unable to feed everyone, while critics of monocropping dispute these claims and attribute them to corporate special interest groups, citing the damage that monocropping causes to societies and the environment.

c1e4f7a79a09.title: Fallow
c1e4f7a79a09.sentence: Fallow is a farming technique in which arable land is left without sowing for one or more vegetative cycles.

ff8e44cc22eb.title: Fallow
ff8e44cc22eb.sentence: Crop rotation systems typically called for some of a farmer's fields to be left fallow each year.

54415a77a819.title: Crop rotation
54415a77a819.sentence: Under a two-field rotation, half the land was planted in a year, while the other half lay fallow.

fbbe4147f05e.title: Fallow
fbbe4147f05e.sentence: The increase in intensive farming, including the use of cover crops in lieu of fallow practices, has caused a loss of acreage of fallow land, as well as field margins, hedges, and wasteland.

ec8f5d06c9d7.title: Crop rotation
ec8f5d06c9d7.sentence: This is very important because depending on a particular region's climate, a field could be the most vulnerable to erosion when it is under fallow.

285538f87a3d.title: Crop rotation
285538f87a3d.sentence: Zero tillage is a fundamental management practice that promotes crop stubble retention under longer unplanned fallows when crops cannot be planted.

ee5f72a9d64d.title: Crop rotation
ee5f72a9d64d.sentence: Such management practices that succeed in retaining suitable soil cover in areas under fallow will ultimately reduce soil loss.

c51b9a08dcc6.title: Cover crop
c51b9a08dcc6.sentence: For example, researchers found that when using Melilotus officinalis (yellow sweetclover) as a cover crop in an improved fallow system (where a fallow period is intentionally improved by any number of different management practices, including the planting of cover crops), weed biomass only constituted between 1–12% of total standing biomass at the end of the cover crop growing season.

8eec382e77e5.title: Irrigation
8eec382e77e5.sentence: Water use efficiency in the field can be determined as follows:

a813b02e0f4d.title: Irrigation
a813b02e0f4d.sentence: - Field Water Efficiency (%) = (Water Transpired by Crop ÷ Water Applied to Field) x 100

2047c0929231.title: Irrigation
2047c0929231.sentence: Low application efficiency indicates that the amount of water applied to the field exceeds the crop or field requirements.

6dbab98f2f67.title: Irrigation
6dbab98f2f67.sentence: Low efficiency usually means that excess water is lost through seepage or runoff, both of which can result in loss of crop nutrients or pesticides with potential adverse impacts on the surrounding environment.

3676fd44db8e.title: Irrigation
3676fd44db8e.sentence: Increasing the application efficiency means that the amount of crop produced per unit of water increases.

0d7c88044a4e.title: Irrigation
0d7c88044a4e.sentence: Irrigation often requires pumping energy (electricity or fossil fuels) to deliver water to the field or to supply the required operating pressure.

ddff5832c7b8.title: Irrigation
ddff5832c7b8.sentence: Hence, increased efficiency will reduce both water and energy costs per unit of agricultural production.

6a7a8e39f99f.title: Irrigation
6a7a8e39f99f.sentence: Improving the efficiency of irrigation is usually achieved in one of two ways: either by improving the system design or by optimizing the irrigation management.

1278acc999b6.title: Irrigation
1278acc999b6.sentence: Improving system design includes converting from one form of irrigation to another (e.g., from furrow to drip irrigation) and making small changes to the current system (e.g., adjusting flow rates and operating pressures).

e96872c85d90.title: Irrigation
e96872c85d90.sentence: Irrigation management refers to the scheduling of irrigation events and decisions about how much water to apply.

a88e5812da9e.title: Irrigation
a88e5812da9e.sentence: In sprinkler or overhead irrigation, water is piped to one or more central locations within the field and distributed by overhead high-pressure sprinklers or guns.

c6a9af7334ae.title: Irrigation
c6a9af7334ae.section: Irrigation methods > Sprinkler irrigation > Center pivot
c6a9af7334ae.sentence: Center pivot irrigation is a form of sprinkler irrigation utilising several segments of pipe (usually galvanized steel or aluminium) joined and supported by trusses, mounted on wheeled towers with sprinklers positioned along its length.

38c9227f6f00.title: Irrigation
38c9227f6f00.section: Irrigation methods > Sprinkler irrigation > Center pivot
38c9227f6f00.sentence: The system moves in a circular pattern and is fed with water from the pivot point at the center of the arc.

aad1f69006e4.title: Irrigation
aad1f69006e4.section: Irrigation methods > Sprinkler irrigation > Center pivot
aad1f69006e4.sentence: These systems are found and used in all parts of the world and allow irrigation of all types of terrain.

5aa22b2af54e.title: Irrigation
5aa22b2af54e.section: Irrigation methods > Sprinkler irrigation > Center pivot
5aa22b2af54e.sentence: As of 2017, most center pivot systems have drops hanging from a U-shaped pipe attached at the top of the pipe with sprinkler heads that are positioned a few feet (at most) above the crop, thus limiting evaporative losses.

2c9cd1ebfed8.title: Irrigation
2c9cd1ebfed8.section: Irrigation methods > Sprinkler irrigation > Center pivot
2c9cd1ebfed8.sentence: Drops can also be used with drag hoses or bubblers that deposit the water directly on the ground between crops.

63c9485bcc3a.title: Irrigation
63c9485bcc3a.section: Irrigation methods > Sprinkler irrigation > Center pivot
63c9485bcc3a.sentence: This type of system is known as LEPA (Low Energy Precision Application).

3b106366768d.title: Salt tolerance of crops

efb98cbb3961.sentence: In very arid regions or on sandy soils, the preferred method is to apply the irrigation water as slowly as possible.

9973c3e751fa.title: Soil solarization
9973c3e751fa.sentence: Soil solarization weakens and kills fungi, bacteria, nematodes, and insect and mite pests along with weeds in the soil by mulching and covering the soil with a tarp, usually with a transparent polyethylene cover to trap solar energy.

8912af2ace9a.title: Soil solarization
8912af2ace9a.sentence: To increase the effectiveness of solar heating requires optimal seasonal temperatures, mulching during high temperatures and solar irradiation, and moist soil conditions.

e7efb165d861.title: Soil solarization
e7efb165d861.sentence: Soil solarization practices require that soil temperatures reach 35-60 degrees Celsius (95 to 140°F), which kills pathogens in the top 30 centimeters of soil.

fd67098a0e7e.title: Soil solarization
fd67098a0e7e.sentence: Soil temperatures are lower when decreasing in soil depth and it is necessary to continue the mulching process to control for pathogens.

b6a950e46dda.title: Soil solarization
b6a950e46dda.sentence: Solarization does not sterilize the soil completely.

f41ea430eed3.title: Soil solarization
f41ea430eed3.sentence: Soil solarization creates a beneficial microbial community by killing up to 90% of pathogens.

57630ff8dd03.title: Soil solarization
57630ff8dd03.sentence: Soil solarization causes a decrease in beneficial microbes, however beneficial bacteria like Bacillus species are able to survive and flourish under high temperatures in solarized soils.

23e55a40ac42.title: Soil solarization
23e55a40ac42.sentence: The number of beneficial microbes increases over time and makes solarized soils more resistant to pathogens.

b57069e5203f.title: Soil solarization
b57069e5203f.sentence: More specifically, a study reported after eight days of solarization 100% of Verticillium dahliae (a fungus that causes farm crops to wilt and die) was killed at a depth of 25 centimeters.

0ea543f3cc2f.title: Soil solarization
0ea543f3cc2f.sentence: With solarization, soil is mulched during the hottest months (rather than the coldest, as in conventional plasticulture which is aimed at protecting the crop) in order to increase the maximal temperatures in an attempt to achieve lethal heat levels.

d22d342d5070.title: Soil solarization
d22d342d5070.sentence: Soil solarization is the third approach for soil disinfestation.

7ffaf346d0c5.title: Soil solarization
7ffaf346d0c5.sentence: The two other main approaches, soil steaming and fumigation, were developed at the end of the 19th century.

4219e67ca782.title: Soil solarization
4219e67ca782.sentence: Soil solarization is a hydrothermal process of disinfecting the soil of pests, accomplished by solar power (referred to as solar heating of the soil in early publications) and is relatively a new soil disinfestation method, first described in extensive scientific detail by Katan in 1976.

8578eabc2eac.title: Soil solarization
8578eabc2eac.sentence: In the first 10 years following the influential 1976 publication, soil solarization was investigated in at least 24 countries and 30 years after it has been applied in more than 60 countries, mostly in hot regions, although there were some important exceptions.

e9b1ab33df4c.title: Soil solarization
e9b1ab33df4c.sentence: Some environmental concerns have been noticed, too, in particular because of the uncontrolled fate of plastic sheets, while biodegradable materials proved to be less effective for weed control, and the often reported (inherent to the method) reduction of microbial richness.

0684c7827744.title: Integrated pest management
0684c7827744.sentence: Integrated pest management (IPM), also known as integrated pest control (IPC) combines both non-chemical and chemical practices for economic control of pests, reducing reliance on chemicals while improving productivity and health.

5ea5a087e565.title: Integrated pest management
5ea5a087e565.sentence: > "IPM is the careful consideration of all available pest control techniques and subsequent integration of appropriate measures that discourage the development of pest populations.

23e7565864be.title: Integrated pest management
23e7565864be.sentence: It combines biological, chemical, physical and crop specific (cultural) management strategies and practices to grow healthy crops and minimize the use of pesticides, reducing or minimizing risks posed by pesticides to human health and the environment for sustainable pest management."

d7769daa5a3c.title: Integrated pest management
d7769daa5a3c.sentence: Cultural practices—The first line of defense for a garden or farm is to select varieties suited to local growing conditions such as resistant varieties and maintain healthy crops.

70e369454c20.title: Integrated pest management
70e369454c20.sentence: Cultural practices may include techniques such as crop rotation and intercropping to promote healthy growing conditions.

0ec315e7c6c9.title: Integrated pest management
0ec315e7c6c9.sentence: Acceptable pest levels—IPM holds that wiping out an entire pest population is often impossible, and the attempt can be expensive and unsafe.

7ddb3fe77b66.title: Integrated pest management
7ddb3fe77b66.sentence: Emphasis is placed on control, not eradication.

2e73c13c3c22.title: Integrated pest management
2e73c13c3c22.sentence: Responsible use of pesticides involves using them only as required and often only at specific times in a pest's life cycle.

837425cc5f5b.title: Nonpoint source pollution
837425cc5f5b.sentence: To minimize pesticide impacts, farmers may use Integrated Pest Management (IPM) techniques (which can include biological pest control) to maintain control over pests, reduce reliance on chemical pesticides, and protect water quality.

1dc5f404943b.title: Crop yield
1dc5f404943b.sentence: In agriculture, the yield is a measurement of the amount of a crop grown, or product such as wool, meat or milk produced, per unit area of land.

8017fe329dba.title: Crop yield
8017fe329dba.sentence: The units by which the yield of a crop is usually measured today are kilograms per hectare or bushels per acre.

6653844419eb.title: Crop yield
6653844419eb.sentence: Long-term cereal yields in the United Kingdom were some 500 kg/ha in medieval times, jumping to 2000 kg/ha in the Industrial Revolution, and jumping again to 8000 kg/ha in the Green Revolution.

5d35c96432ca.title: Crop yield
5d35c96432ca.sentence: Innovations, such as the use of fertilizer, the creation of better farming tools, and new methods of farming and improved crop varieties have improved yields.

8a2c47b7566d.title: Crop yield
8a2c47b7566d.sentence: In 2025, around 1.7 billion people live in areas experiencing sizeable degradation-induced crop yield losses.

a3e31340b966.title: Crop yield
a3e31340b966.sentence: Middle-income countries are the most affected, accounting for nearly 1 billion people, while in high-income countries, intensive input use sustains yields but masks degradation and increases environmental harm.

0ee9732f81b0.title: Precision agriculture
0ee9732f81b0.sentence: Precision agriculture is a management strategy that gathers, processes and analyzes temporal, spatial and individual plant and animal data and combines it with other information to support management decisions according to estimated variability for improved resource use efficiency, productivity, quality, profitability and sustainability of agricultural production.

3b267bd6105a.title: Precision agriculture
3b267bd6105a.sentence: The practice of precision agriculture has been enabled by the advent of GPS and GNSS.

af07d04e5afc.title: Precision agriculture
af07d04e5afc.sentence: The farmer's and/or researcher's ability to locate their precise position in a field allows for the creation of maps of the spatial variability of as many variables as can be measured (e.g. crop yield, terrain features/topography, organic matter content, moisture levels, nitrogen levels, pH, EC, Mg, K, and others).

a40d0add4b41.title: Precision agriculture
a40d0add4b41.sentence: Beyond machinery, precision agriculture also analyzes the spatial variability within fields, such as how terrain attributes (geomorphology) and soil properties affect crop growth and water distribution (hydrology).[] The goal of precision agriculture research is to define a decision support system for whole farm management with the goal of optimizing returns on inputs while preserving resources.

e523b4e23d37.title: Precision agriculture
e523b4e23d37.sentence: The first wave of the precision agricultural revolution came in the forms of satellite and aerial imagery, weather prediction, variable rate fertilizer application, and crop health indicators.

dabf8b6a08a4.title: Precision agriculture
dabf8b6a08a4.sentence: The second wave aggregates the machine data for even more precise planting, topographical mapping, and soil data.

9e9dbb9e2bf1.title: Precision agriculture
9e9dbb9e2bf1.sentence: Precision agriculture management practices can significantly reduce the amount of nutrient and other crop inputs used while boosting yields.

71a4c1231da5.title: Precision agriculture
71a4c1231da5.sentence: Applying the right amount of chemicals in the right place and at the right time benefits crops, soils and groundwater, and thus the entire crop cycle.

cb07f780cd96.title: Precision agriculture
cb07f780cd96.sentence: - crop science: by matching farming practices more closely to crop needs (e.g. fertilizer inputs);

911520100647.title: Precision agriculture
911520100647.sentence: - environmental protection: by reducing environmental risks and footprint of farming (e.g. limiting leaching of nitrogen);

14a7dfae92bc.title: Precision agriculture
14a7dfae92bc.sentence: GPS also reduces the amount of compaction to the ground by following previously made guidance lines.

3e793a7f649f.title: Precision agriculture
3e793a7f649f.sentence: The concept of precision agriculture first emerged in the United States in the early 1980s.

8059b98f853a.title: Precision agriculture
8059b98f853a.sentence: In 1985, researchers at the University of Minnesota varied lime inputs in crop fields.

e515903493b0.title: Precision agriculture
e515903493b0.sentence: It was also at this time that the practice of grid sampling appeared (applying a fixed grid of one sample per hectare).

73f5cd6a3f0e.title: Precision agriculture
73f5cd6a3f0e.section: Emerging technologies > The Internet of things
73f5cd6a3f0e.sentence: Moisture sensors in the soil determine the best times to remotely water plants.

972aa666216d.title: Precision agriculture
972aa666216d.sentence: This allows for robots to deliver the perfect amount of fertilizer or for IoT devices to provide the perfect quantity of water directly to the soil.

fb9c76c06330.title: Green Revolution
fb9c76c06330.sentence: The Green Revolution, or the Third Agricultural Revolution, was a period during which technology transfer initiatives resulted in a significant increase in crop yields.

73e90cf57dc4.title: Green Revolution
73e90cf57dc4.sentence: The basic approach was the development of high-yielding varieties of cereal grains, expansion of irrigation infrastructure, modernization of management techniques, distribution of hybridized seeds, synthetic fertilizers, and pesticides to farmers.

1c94a2e04ca0.title: Green Revolution
1c94a2e04ca0.section: Agricultural production and food security > Technological developments > High-yielding varieties
1c94a2e04ca0.sentence: HYVs have higher nitrogen-absorbing potential than other varieties.

26cb2e507d3a.title: Green Revolution
26cb2e507d3a.section: Agricultural production and food security > Technological developments > High-yielding varieties
26cb2e507d3a.sentence: Since cereals that absorbed extra nitrogen would typically lodge, or fall over before harvest, semi-dwarfing genes were bred into their genomes.

6d174a14f3f5.title: Green Revolution
6d174a14f3f5.section: Agricultural production and food security > Technological developments > High-yielding varieties
6d174a14f3f5.sentence: High-yielding varieties significantly outperform traditional varieties in the presence of adequate irrigation, pesticides, and fertilizers.

7655310a8a32.title: Green Revolution
7655310a8a32.section: Agricultural production and food security > Technological developments > High-yielding varieties
7655310a8a32.sentence: In the absence of these inputs, traditional varieties may outperform high-yielding varieties.

7faffd5f9efa.title: Green Revolution
7faffd5f9efa.sentence: A key leader was agricultural scientist Norman Borlaug, the "Father of the Green Revolution", who received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1970.

e7d7fe6fb490.title: Green Revolution
e7d7fe6fb490.section: Agricultural production and food security > Production increases
e7d7fe6fb490.sentence: By one 2021 estimate, the Green Revolution increased yields by 44% between 1965 and 2010.

2ccff8690164.title: Green Revolution
2ccff8690164.section: Agricultural production and food security > Production increases
2ccff8690164.sentence: Cereal production more than doubled in developing nations between the years 1961–1985.

4e66c36ed52e.title: Green Revolution
4e66c36ed52e.section: Agricultural production and food security > Production increases
4e66c36ed52e.sentence: While agricultural output increased as a result of the Green Revolution, the energy input to produce a crop has increased faster, so that the ratio of crops produced to energy input has decreased over time.

089285a7d20a.title: Green Revolution
089285a7d20a.section: Agricultural production and food security > Production increases
089285a7d20a.sentence: Green Revolution techniques also heavily rely on agricultural machinery and chemical fertilizers, pesticides, herbicides, and defoliants; which, as of 2014, are derived from crude oil, making agriculture increasingly reliant on crude oil extraction.

61eca073b4cb.title: Food security
61eca073b4cb.section: Causes of food insecurity > Environmental degradation and overuse > Land degradation
61eca073b4cb.sentence: While the Green Revolution was critical in supporting a larger population through the mid-1900s to now by increasing crop yields, it has also resulted in environmental degradation particularly through land use, soil degradation, and deforestation.

387ccd7f1c15.title: Food security
387ccd7f1c15.section: Causes of food insecurity > Environmental degradation and overuse > Land degradation
387ccd7f1c15.sentence: Over-farming of agricultural land due to the Green Revolution has caused contamination and erosion of soil, and a reduction in biodiversity due to pesticide usage (as well as deforestation).

09e8d5c0cff8.title: Green Revolution
09e8d5c0cff8.section: Agricultural production and food security > Environmental impact > Biodiversity
09e8d5c0cff8.sentence: However, land degradation and soil nutrients depletion have forced farmers to clear forested areas in order to maintain production.

aa9ce79fd30b.title: Green Revolution
aa9ce79fd30b.section: Agricultural production and food security > Environmental impact > Biodiversity
aa9ce79fd30b.sentence: For example, the development of wheat varieties tolerant to acid soil conditions with high aluminium content permitted the introduction of agriculture in the Cerrado semi-humid tropical savanna.

e40001099660.title: Crop rotation
e40001099660.sentence: Agronomists describe the benefits to yield in rotated crops as "The Rotation Effect".

801f223ef887.title: Crop rotation
801f223ef887.sentence: The factors related to the increase are broadly due to alleviation of the negative factors of monoculture cropping systems.

eb064b63946a.title: Crop rotation
eb064b63946a.sentence: Specifically, improved nutrition; pest, pathogen, and weed stress reduction; and improved soil structure have been found in some cases to be correlated to beneficial rotation effects.

2954b444d78a.title: Crop rotation
2954b444d78a.sentence: The use of different species in rotation allows for increased soil organic matter, greater soil structure, and improvement of the chemical and biological soil environment for crops.

7185d26adaf0.title: Crop rotation
7185d26adaf0.sentence: With more soil organic matter, water infiltration and retention improves, providing increased drought tolerance and decreased erosion.
