ee823b5f42e8.title: Crop rotation
ee823b5f42e8.sentence: The reduced need for intensive tillage under crop rotation allows biomass aggregation to lead to greater nutrient retention and utilization, decreasing the need for added nutrients.

e46aaec1e3c8.title: Crop rotation
e46aaec1e3c8.sentence: With tillage, disruption and oxidation of soil creates a less conducive environment for diversity and proliferation of microorganisms in the soil.

caa1b2168116.title: Crop rotation
caa1b2168116.sentence: So, where "active" soil organic matter is a key to productive soil, soil with low microbial activity provides significantly fewer nutrients to plants; this is true even though the quantity of biomass left in the soil may be the same.

4212c08bad46.title: Crop rotation
4212c08bad46.sentence: Less reliance is placed on purchased inputs and over time crops can maintain production goals with fewer inputs.

0777664ff824.title: Land reclamation
0777664ff824.sentence: Agriculture was a driver of land reclamation before industrialisation.

e63005f91b67.title: Land reclamation
e63005f91b67.sentence: A related practice is the draining of swampy or seasonally submerged wetlands to convert them to farmland.

a403c65fee69.title: Land reclamation
a403c65fee69.sentence: In South China, farmers reclaimed paddy fields by enclosing an area with a stone wall on the sea shore near a river mouth or river delta.

4aae0a9706e9.title: Land reclamation
4aae0a9706e9.sentence: The species of rice that are grown on these grounds are more salt tolerant.

8b329424f707.title: Land reclamation
8b329424f707.sentence: Another use of such enclosed land is the creation of fish ponds.

d5077e174eba.title: Land reclamation
d5077e174eba.sentence: While this does not create new land exactly, it allows commercially productive use of land that would otherwise be restricted to wildlife habitat.

a6c8192d2270.title: Land reclamation
a6c8192d2270.sentence: It is also an important method of mosquito control.

2af1cecc2958.title: Salt marsh
2af1cecc2958.sentence: In the past, salt marshes were perceived as coastal 'wastelands,' causing considerable loss and change of these ecosystems through land reclamation for agriculture, urban development, salt production and recreation.

d220d4fe3757.title: Soil steam sterilization
d220d4fe3757.sentence: Soil steam sterilization (soil steaming) is a farming technique that sterilizes or partially sterilizes soil with steam in open fields or greenhouses.

e3e79675cf32.title: Soil steam sterilization
e3e79675cf32.sentence: Steam effectively kills weeds, bacteria, fungi and viruses by heating the soil to levels that cause enzyme inactivation or the unfolding and coagulation of vital cellular proteins.

6eecd7be743a.title: Soil steam sterilization
6eecd7be743a.sentence: Biologically, soil steaming is considered a partial disinfection, since heat-resistant spore-forming bacteria can survive the process and revitalize the soil after cooling.

4ab17997120e.title: Soil steam sterilization
4ab17997120e.sentence: This process achieves true sterilization, completely disinfecting the soil and rendering all microorganisms, spores, viruses, fungi, and pathogens entirely inactive.

1e692d30c704.title: Soil steam sterilization
1e692d30c704.sentence: It is now considered the best and most effective way to disinfect sick soil, potting soil, and compost.

f8e386a9bee6.title: Soil steam sterilization
f8e386a9bee6.sentence: Soil steaming is considered a good alternative to bromomethane, whose production and use was curtailed by the Montreal Protocol.

c6cd7d2fb0d6.title: Soil steam sterilization
c6cd7d2fb0d6.sentence: Soil steaming is also effective for addressing soil fatigue, which is the degradation of soil health and fertility arising from improper agricultural management practices.

f7c22f788ff6.title: Soil steam sterilization
f7c22f788ff6.sentence: Steaming the soil has been shown to effectively release nutritive substances blocked within fatigued soil.

5a90efe0bf30.title: Soil steam sterilization
5a90efe0bf30.sentence: Methods like "integrated steaming" can promote a target-oriented resettlement of steamed soil with beneficial organisms.

4d28e41f1b54.title: Soil steam sterilization
4d28e41f1b54.sentence: In the process, the soil is first freed from all organisms and then revitalized and microbiologically buffered through the injection of a soil activator based on compost which contains a natural mixture of favorable microorganisms (e.g. Bacillus subtilis, etc.).

987861e3ee13.title: Soil steam sterilization
987861e3ee13.sentence: Modern soil steam sterilization was first developed in 1888 in Germany.

515d80d7dc71.title: Soil steam sterilization
515d80d7dc71.sentence: It was first commercially used in the United States in 1893.

26018fb599a3.title: Soil steam sterilization
26018fb599a3.sentence: Modern steaming methods often rely on superheated steam at 180–200 °C (356–392 °F) to achieve optimal soil disinfection.

a929003e55c7.title: Soil steam sterilization
a929003e55c7.sentence: In the 2020s, the technique started to be adapted for use in construction and in the production of technosol, to kill seeds and weeds in soil as a method of remediating invasive alien species.[1]

e398e1a4398d.title: Shifting cultivation
e398e1a4398d.sentence: Shifting cultivation is an agricultural system in which plots of land are cultivated temporarily, then abandoned while post-disturbance fallow vegetation is allowed to freely grow while the cultivator moves on to another plot.

5b9a78bc535e.title: Shifting cultivation
5b9a78bc535e.sentence: The period of cultivation is usually terminated when the soil shows signs of exhaustion or, more commonly, when the field is overrun by weeds.

42aabf6ab8d6.title: Shifting cultivation
42aabf6ab8d6.sentence: The period of time during which the field is cultivated is usually shorter than the period over which the land is allowed to regenerate by lying fallow.

9d87dabda50e.title: Shifting cultivation
9d87dabda50e.sentence: Land is often cleared by slash-and-burn methods—trees, bushes and forests are cleared by slashing, and the remaining vegetation is burnt.

9376312e9a55.title: Shifting cultivation
9376312e9a55.sentence: The ashes add potash to the soil.

572b8b6fec9b.title: Shifting cultivation
572b8b6fec9b.sentence: Shifting cultivation was one of the first forms of agriculture practiced by humans and its survival into the modern world suggests that it is a flexible and highly adaptive means of production.

e1bf88cff945.title: Shifting cultivation
e1bf88cff945.section: In the contemporary world and global environmental change
e1bf88cff945.sentence: One of the outcomes of cash incomes has been rapid population growth among indigenous groups of former shifting cultivators that has placed pressure on their traditional long fallow farming systems.

8519c178aea2.title: Shifting cultivation
8519c178aea2.section: In the contemporary world and global environmental change
8519c178aea2.sentence: Increased cash incomes often are spent on chain saws, which have enabled larger areas to be cleared for cultivation.

0d78a1b145c9.title: Shifting cultivation
0d78a1b145c9.section: In the contemporary world and global environmental change
0d78a1b145c9.sentence: Fallow periods have been reduced and cropping periods extended.

0db037be202e.title: Shifting cultivation
0db037be202e.section: In the contemporary world and global environmental change
0db037be202e.sentence: The settlers practice what appears to be shifting cultivation but which is in fact a one-cycle slash and burn followed by continuous cropping, with no intention to long fallow.

6b1da1ff3548.title: Shifting cultivation
6b1da1ff3548.section: In the contemporary world and global environmental change
6b1da1ff3548.sentence: Clearing of trees and the permanent cultivation of fragile soils in a tropical environment with little attempt to replace lost nutrients may cause rapid degradation of the fragile soils.

4df485fd3ad8.title: Shifting cultivation
4df485fd3ad8.section: In the contemporary world and global environmental change
4df485fd3ad8.sentence: Shifting cultivation was assessed by the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) to be one of the causes of deforestation while logging was not.

088c64ca5c19.title: Shifting cultivation
088c64ca5c19.section: In the contemporary world and global environmental change
088c64ca5c19.sentence: The apparent discrimination against shifting cultivators caused a confrontation between FAO and environmental groups, who saw the FAO supporting commercial logging interests against the rights of indigenous people (Potter 1993, 108).

426ffb89ebe9.title: Slash-and-burn agriculture
426ffb89ebe9.sentence: Slash-and-burn agriculture is a form of shifting cultivation in agriculture that involves the cutting and burning of plants in a forest or woodland to create a field called a swidden.

69ff14d73db9.title: Slash-and-burn agriculture
69ff14d73db9.sentence: The downed vegetation, or "slash", is left out to dry, usually right before the rainiest part of the year.

d493fad06afb.title: Slash-and-burn agriculture
d493fad06afb.sentence: The biomass is then burned, resulting in a nutrient-rich layer of ash which increases soil fertility and temporarily eliminates weeds and pests.

b0ceb8f4a3fb.title: Slash-and-burn agriculture
b0ceb8f4a3fb.sentence: After about three to five years, the plot's productivity decreases due to depletion of nutrients along with weed and pest invasion, causing farmers to abandon the plot and move to a new area.

e6bd4f5bf879.title: Slash-and-burn agriculture
e6bd4f5bf879.sentence: The time it takes for a swidden to recover depends on the location and can be as little as five years to more than twenty years, after which the plot can be slashed and burned again, repeating the cycle.

995647d33c6c.title: Slash-and-burn agriculture
995647d33c6c.sentence: A rough estimate says that about 200–300 million people worldwide use slash-and-burn agricultural techniques.

80c0a47badf7.title: Slash-and-burn agriculture
80c0a47badf7.sentence: Because the leached soil in many tropical regions, such as the Amazon, are nutritionally extremely poor, slash-and-burn is one of the only types of agriculture which can be practiced in these areas.

c663920dcdd6.title: Slash-and-burn agriculture
c663920dcdd6.sentence: A huge amount of land, or a low density of people, is required for sustainable slash-and-burn.

01aac8f24a9b.title: Slash-and-burn agriculture
01aac8f24a9b.sentence: When slash-and-burn is practiced in the same area too often, e.g., because the human population density has increased to an unsustainable level, the forest will eventually be destroyed.

d0e038124ad3.title: Slash-and-burn agriculture
d0e038124ad3.sentence: While slash-and-burn agriculture has historically been sustainable in areas with low population density, increasing populations have accelerated the rate of deforestation, depleting the Earth's carbon reservoirs.

d0b1a5a4fc0c.title: Slash-and-burn agriculture
d0b1a5a4fc0c.sentence: Not allowing the slashed vegetation to burn completely and ploughing the resultant charcoal into the soil (slash-and-char) has been proposed as a way to boost yields.

173033750cf1.title: Herbicide
173033750cf1.sentence: An herbicide is described as having low residual activity if it is neutralized within a short time of application (within a few weeks or months) – typically this is due to rainfall, or reactions in the soil.

c02fdd803f6a.title: Herbicide
c02fdd803f6a.sentence: A herbicide described as having high residual activity will remain potent for the long term in the soil.

0d2696f95f06.title: Herbicide
0d2696f95f06.sentence: For some compounds, the residual activity can leave the ground almost permanently barren.

114761f0f545.title: Herbicide
114761f0f545.sentence: The triazine family of herbicides, which includes atrazine, was introduced in the 1950s; they have the current distinction of being the herbicide family of greatest concern regarding groundwater contamination.

61680035e761.title: Herbicide
61680035e761.sentence: Atrazine does not break down readily (within a few weeks) after being applied to soils of above-neutral pH.

ac3dc40ecd0f.title: Herbicide
ac3dc40ecd0f.sentence: Under alkaline soil conditions, atrazine may be carried into the soil profile as far as the water table by soil water following rainfall causing the aforementioned contamination.

8cb8d7131219.title: Herbicide
8cb8d7131219.sentence: Atrazine is thus said to have "carryover", a generally undesirable property for herbicides.

8ed3d69af68b.title: Herbicide
8ed3d69af68b.sentence: Many modern herbicides used in agriculture and gardening are specifically formulated to degrade within a short period after application.

fe992cab9ccf.title: Agricultural pollution
fe992cab9ccf.sentence: The persistence of pesticides and herbicides persist depends on the compound's unique chemistry.

21f580320a78.title: Herbicide
21f580320a78.sentence: - Soil applied: Herbicides applied to the soil are usually taken up by the root or shoot of the emerging seedlings and are used as preplant or preemergence treatment.

1a6af2e34952.title: Herbicide
1a6af2e34952.sentence: Herbicide adsorption to soil colloids or organic matter often reduces the amount available for weed absorption.

d2b44362827b.title: Herbicide
d2b44362827b.sentence: Positioning of the herbicide in the correct layer of soil is very important, which can be achieved mechanically and by rainfall.

2aae69861b1c.title: Herbicide
2aae69861b1c.sentence: Herbicides on the soil surface are subjected to several processes that reduce their availability.

07ac330082ac.title: Herbicide
07ac330082ac.sentence: Volatility and photolysis are two common processes that reduce the availability of herbicides.

f4899f32f7c6.title: Herbicide
f4899f32f7c6.sentence: Many soil-applied herbicides are absorbed through plant shoots while they are still underground leading to their death or injury.

f50d4c8a73e3.title: Herbicide
f50d4c8a73e3.sentence: EPTC and trifluralin are soil-applied herbicides.

42945effe2f2.title: Herbicide
42945effe2f2.sentence: Glyphosate, 2,4-D, and dicamba are foliar-applied herbicides.

26eaedd55ece.title: Leaching (agriculture)
26eaedd55ece.sentence: Leaching is an important transport pathway for P losses from agricultural fields in predominantly flat areas with sandy soils or soils prone to preferential flow.

6a121657b3eb.title: Leaching (agriculture)
6a121657b3eb.sentence: As opposed to nitrogen phosphorus does interact with soil particles via adsorption and desorption.

d9539c3e318b.title: Leaching (agriculture)
d9539c3e318b.sentence: Important potential adsorption sites for P in soils are surfaces of iron and aluminum oxides or hydroxides such as gibbsite or ferrihydrite.

6030edd74a66.title: Leaching (agriculture)
6030edd74a66.sentence: Soils, especially those rich in such minerals do hence have a potential to store P added with fertilizer or manure.

01c3a36e9161.title: Leaching (agriculture)
01c3a36e9161.sentence: Many cultivated soils have been receiving fertilizer or manure P in amounts frequently exceeding the crop demand and this often over decades.

7bc9801eb359.title: Leaching (agriculture)
7bc9801eb359.sentence: Phosphorus added to such soils leaches simply because most of the potential adsorption sites are occupied by P input from the past, so called “legacy phosphorus”.

7bcb1c2c1db3.title: Leaching (agriculture)
7bcb1c2c1db3.sentence: Phosphorus adsorbed to these minerals is consequently released into the soil solution as well and may be leached.

371c093b9c73.title: Leaching (agriculture)
371c093b9c73.sentence: This process is of special concern in the restoration of natural wetlands that have previously been drained for agricultural production.

a43552b5c51b.title: Leaching (agriculture)
a43552b5c51b.sentence: Phosphorus (P) is a key nutrient regarding the eutrophication of surface waters and has been shown to limit algae growth in lake environments.

02e3cc62c06b.title: Leaching (agriculture)
02e3cc62c06b.sentence: Loss of P from agricultural fields has long been recognized as one of the major threats to surface water quality.

b0f02f2c99d6.title: Coir
b0f02f2c99d6.sentence: Coir (/ˈkɔɪər/), also called coconut fibre, is a plant fibre extracted from the outer husk of coconut, used in products such as floor mats, doormats, brushes, and mattresses, as well as horticulturally in potting mixes and soil amendments.

20918ed8908a.title: Coir
20918ed8908a.sentence: The name coco peat may refer either to coir or the pith or a mixture, as both have good water-retaining properties as a substitute for peat.

534096e7c2ab.title: Coir
534096e7c2ab.sentence: Out of increasing concern regarding the sustainability of producing sphagnum (peat moss) and peat from peatlands, usage of alternative substrates has been on the rise; the plantation byproduct coir is one commonly used substitute.

2bd694178357.title: Coir
2bd694178357.sentence: - As a substitute for peat, because it is free of bacteria and most fungal spores, and is sustainably produced without the environmental damage caused by peat mining.

19868ccd6360.title: Coir
19868ccd6360.sentence: Coir fibre pith or coir dust can hold large quantities of water, just like a sponge.

0184a1831bde.title: Coir
0184a1831bde.sentence: A single kilogramme of dry coco peat will expand to 15 litres of moist coco peat.

c3a5b8436cf3.title: Coir
c3a5b8436cf3.sentence: Coco peat generally has an acidity in the range of pH - 5.5 to 6.5, which is slightly too acidic for some plants, but many popular plants can tolerate this pH range.

4ed51fc695b8.title: Coir
4ed51fc695b8.sentence: Because coir pith is high in sodium and potassium, it is treated before use as a growth medium for plants or fungi by soaking in a calcium buffering solution; most coir sold for growing purposes is said to be pre-treated.

f1f9bcc5575d.title: Coir
f1f9bcc5575d.sentence: Coir is naturally rich in potassium, which can lead to magnesium and calcium deficiencies in soilless horticultural media.

d8ada63d6faa.title: Coir
d8ada63d6faa.sentence: Due to low levels of nutrients in its composition, coco peat is usually not the sole component in the medium used to grow plants.

1f4403ab0ff2.title: Coir
1f4403ab0ff2.sentence: Some coco peat is not fully decomposed when it arrives and will use up available nitrogen as it does so (known as drawdown), competing with the plant if there is not enough.

ecd41dc2fba8.title: Land restoration
ecd41dc2fba8.sentence: Land restoration, which may include renaturalisation or rewilding, is the process of restoring land to a different or previous state with an intended purpose.

f0203c91459d.title: Land restoration
f0203c91459d.sentence: Ecological destruction or degradation, to which land restoration serves as an antidote, is usually the consequence of human influence's intended or unintended consequences.

069eaaac5fa0.title: Land restoration
069eaaac5fa0.sentence: This can include pollution, deforestation, salination, or species endangerment, among many more.

1379d5aff874.title: Land restoration
1379d5aff874.sentence: Land restoration is not the same as land reclamation, where existing ecosystems are altered or destroyed to give way for cultivation or construction.

c20193be8aa9.title: Land restoration
c20193be8aa9.sentence: Additionally, in order to monitor the success of a restoration project, a reference model or reference ecosystem should be selected in order to make comparisons.

eba28ccea125.title: Land restoration
eba28ccea125.sentence: Adaptive management is "an approach for simultaneously managing and learning about natural resources." It is the primary method used in managing land restoration projects, as natural resources can respond to management interventions; however, the durability and desirability of these responses are uncertain and depend on a combination of controllable and uncontrollable factors.

eb74ab0b5140.title: Land restoration
eb74ab0b5140.sentence: Therefore, adapting how a project is managed based on responses from the ecosystem is a more informed approach to landscape restoration.

85d266c92dc2.title: Land restoration
85d266c92dc2.sentence: Stabilizing and fixating the soil is usually done in several phases.

61c30f66512e.title: Land restoration
61c30f66512e.sentence: The first phase is fixating the soil to such extent that dune movement is ceased.

6de0bc1c20dc.title: Land restoration
6de0bc1c20dc.sentence: This is done by grasses, and plants providing wind protection such as shelterbelts, windbreaks and woodlots.

3300d58217eb.title: Land restoration
3300d58217eb.sentence: The second phase involves improving/enriching the soil by planting nitrogen-fixating plants and using the soil immediately to grow crops.

7061269b9d8f.title: Land restoration
7061269b9d8f.sentence: In addition, each year the plots are used for another type of crop (known as crop rotation) to prevent depleting the soil on specific trace elements.

08dbeb921902.title: Monoculture
08dbeb921902.sentence: In agriculture, monoculture is the practice of growing one crop species in a field at a time.

14febd8dfb49.title: Monoculture
14febd8dfb49.sentence: Note that the distinction between monoculture and polyculture is not the same as between monocropping and intercropping.

8f1e8ff77103.title: Monoculture
8f1e8ff77103.sentence: The first two describe diversity in space, as does intercropping.

16ff0c2d34cd.title: Monoculture
16ff0c2d34cd.sentence: Monocropping and crop rotation describe diversity over time.

1f16702a3aeb.title: Monoculture
1f16702a3aeb.sentence: Monocultures increase ease and efficiency in planting, managing, and harvesting crops short-term, often with the help of machinery.

06c67c610542.title: Monoculture
06c67c610542.sentence: However, monocultures are more susceptible to diseases or pest outbreaks long-term due to localized reductions in biodiversity and nutrient depletion.

17561bcf7610.title: Monoculture
17561bcf7610.sentence: Monocultures of perennials, such as African palm oil, sugarcane, tea and pines, can change soil chemistry leading to soil acidification, degradation, and soil-borne diseases, ultimately having a negative impact on agricultural productivity and sustainability.

34b5ac494d07.title: Monoculture
34b5ac494d07.sentence: As soil health declines, use of synthetic fertilizers on monocultural fields increases, often having negative implications on human health via chemical run-off.

c96066a0242c.title: Monoculture
c96066a0242c.sentence: For example, excess nitrogen from synthetic fertilizers can leach into ground and surface waters, leading to nitrate contamination of drinking water.

48de6ef1c082.title: Salt tolerance of crops
48de6ef1c082.sentence: Salt tolerance of crops is the maximum salt level a crop tolerates without losing its productivity while it is affected negatively at higher levels.

34eb8be4fa88.title: Salt tolerance of crops
34eb8be4fa88.sentence: The salt level is often taken as the soil salinity or the salinity of the irrigation water.

3d2529faccdb.title: Salt tolerance of crops
3d2529faccdb.sentence: Salt tolerance is of importance in irrigated lands in (semi)arid regions where the soil salinity problem can be extensive as a result of the salinization occurring here.

6a83e6cd9d54.title: Salt tolerance of crops
6a83e6cd9d54.sentence: It concerns hundreds of millions of hectares.

c09d88b3ba66.title: Salt tolerance of crops
c09d88b3ba66.sentence: A regional distribution of the 3,230,000 km2 of saline land worldwide is shown in salt affected area based on the FAO/UNESCO Soil Map of the World.

e48e9946e57e.title: Salt tolerance of crops
e48e9946e57e.sentence: In Australia the following classification of sprinkler irrigation water salinity was developed:

aed4ca6a718b.title: Salt tolerance of crops
aed4ca6a718b.sentence: Tolerant | >710 | >458 | Cauliflower, cotton, safflower, sesame, sorghum, sunflower

d0c53057856a.title: Salt tolerance of crops
d0c53057856a.sentence: One of the first studies made on soil salinity and plant response was published in the USDA Agriculture Handbook No. 60, 1954.

dbdb67993399.title: Salt tolerance of crops
dbdb67993399.sentence: More than 20 years later Maas and Hoffman published the results of an extensive study on salt tolerance.

a626806ede34.title: Salt tolerance of crops
a626806ede34.sentence: A comprehensive survey of tolerances reported worldwide was made by the FAO in 2002.

c7750c395ed6.title: Salt tolerance of crops
c7750c395ed6.sentence: Most studies were made with pot or drum experiments or in lysimeters under controlled conditions.

3b0c72ae6167.title: Salt tolerance of crops
3b0c72ae6167.sentence: The collection of field data under farmers' conditions was rare, probably due to the greater efforts and higher costs involved, the lack of control of plant growing conditions other than soil salinity, and the larger random variation in crop yields and soil salinity.

bb22aca954fe.title: Salt tolerance of crops
bb22aca954fe.sentence: Yet, with statistical methods, it is possible to detect the tolerance level from field data.

d8e4b477a651.title: Salt tolerance of crops
d8e4b477a651.sentence: Presently a considerable amount of research is undertaken to develop agricultural crops with a higher salt tolerance to enhance crop cultivation in salinity stricken regions.

876181492077.title: Precision agriculture
876181492077.sentence: Intra and inter-field variability may result from a number of factors.

02aecd742fd7.title: Precision agriculture
02aecd742fd7.sentence: These include climatic conditions (hail, drought, rain, etc.), soils (texture, depth, nitrogen levels), cropping practices (no-till farming), weeds, and disease.

78a68dbcd6ee.title: Precision agriculture
78a68dbcd6ee.sentence: Permanent indicators—chiefly soil indicators—provide farmers with information about the main environmental constants.

3714a7e6daeb.title: Precision agriculture
3714a7e6daeb.sentence: Point indicators allow them to track a crop's status, i.e., to see whether diseases are developing, if the crop is suffering from water stress, nitrogen stress, or lodging, whether it has been damaged by ice, and so on.

4eef3823d1fa.title: Precision agriculture
4eef3823d1fa.sentence: Using soil maps, farmers can pursue two strategies to adjust field inputs:

9ea2027b85d2.title: Precision agriculture
9ea2027b85d2.sentence: - Predictive approach: based on analysis of static indicators (soil, resistivity, field history, etc.) during the crop cycle.

b17c8e55ae1e.title: Precision agriculture
b17c8e55ae1e.sentence: - Control approach: information from static indicators is regularly updated during the crop cycle by:

306219092e44.title: Precision agriculture
306219092e44.sentence: - sampling: weighing biomass, measuring leaf chlorophyll content, weighing fruit, etc.

3eb7c889a29d.title: Precision agriculture
3eb7c889a29d.sentence: - remote sensing: measuring parameters like temperature (air/soil), humidity (air/soil/leaf), wind or stem diameter is possible thanks to Wireless Sensor Networks and Internet of things (IoT)

6fe19054301a.title: Precision agriculture
6fe19054301a.sentence: This information may come from weather stations and other sensors (soil electrical resistivity, detection with the naked eye, satellite imagery, etc.).

172208268d69.title: Potting soil
172208268d69.sentence: The main method is a saturated media extract (SME), which tests the chemical contents of a water extract of the mix.

d7423c030292.title: Potting soil
d7423c030292.sentence: A soil test may be done to analyze the chemistry of a potting mix, despite the mix not necessarily being made of soil.

14e38c056571.title: Potting soil
14e38c056571.sentence: As an approximation for indoor home planting, the mix is generally treated as greenhouse growth medium.

2ade36fd0c80.title: Potting soil
2ade36fd0c80.sentence: Table: Reference levels for potting mix by the SME method

4611ce14d34f.title: Potting soil
4611ce14d34f.sentence: Nutrients not supplied by the bulk will need to be supplied by the fertilizer.

4df09ff56aab.title: Potting soil
4df09ff56aab.sentence: In conventional mixes they may be slow-release formulae of synthetic fertilizers, while organic mixes will use organic source such as compost (e.g. leaf mold, bark compost or recycled mushroom compost).

536c57e66dfa.title: Potting soil
536c57e66dfa.sentence: For compost, the maximum recommended amount is 1 part compost to 1 part bulking material.

257ca1d71e4f.title: Potting soil
257ca1d71e4f.sentence: The growth medium should be adapted to each plant's (and growth stage's) preference for aeration, drainage, nutrition, and pH.

f787a949b364.title: Potting soil
f787a949b364.sentence: For seed starting, a "germination mix" is typically light-weight and suitable for starting small-seeded plants.

4834c925b6f9.title: Potting soil
4834c925b6f9.sentence: A "seed starting" mix is suitable for larger seeded crops.

fadabadd2595.title: Potting soil
fadabadd2595.sentence: Following early growth, most plants prefer a potting mix that is more well-draining.

9e79d1084a42.title: Potting soil
9e79d1084a42.sentence: Carnivorous plants, such as the Venus flytrap and the pitcher plant, prefer the nutrient-poor, acidic soils common to bogs and fens, while water-based plants thrive in a heavier topsoil mix.

b9ccd5c38cca.title: Potting soil
b9ccd5c38cca.sentence: Cuttings generally develop better root systems when rooted in a soil-less potting mix than when propagated in water.

842368326320.title: Potting soil
842368326320.sentence: Suitable media include perlite, vermiculite, sand and sphagnum moss.

c32712327422.title: Dryland farming
c32712327422.sentence: Dryland farming and dry farming encompass agricultural techniques for growing crops without irrigation.

685afcf9e974.title: Dryland farming
685afcf9e974.sentence: Dryland farming is associated with drylands, areas characterized by a cool wet season (which charges the soil with virtually all the moisture that the crops will receive prior to harvest) followed by a warm dry season.

f35c475ff78d.title: Dryland farming
f35c475ff78d.sentence: Dry farming depends on making the best use of the "bank" of soil moisture that was created by winter rainfall.

8af1b19ffb5c.title: Dryland farming
8af1b19ffb5c.sentence: These crops grow using the winter water stored in the soil, rather than depending on rainfall during the growing season.

84736eb87ad1.title: Dryland farming
84736eb87ad1.sentence: Successful dryland farming is possible with as little as 9 inches (230 millimetres) of precipitation a year; higher rainfall increases the variety of crops.

2c19ab35f04f.title: Dryland farming
2c19ab35f04f.sentence: - Wider than normal spacing, to provide a larger bank of moisture for each plant.

e52d3670d87d.title: Dryland farming
e52d3670d87d.sentence: - Strict weed control, to ensure that weeds do not consume soil moisture needed by the cultivated plants.

3824610a16d8.title: Dryland farming
3824610a16d8.section: Other considerations > Capturing and conservation of moisture
3824610a16d8.sentence: Techniques include summer fallow rotation (in which one crop is grown on two seasons' precipitation, leaving standing stubble and crop residue to trap snow), and preventing runoff by terracing fields.

c930f9d4436f.title: Dryland farming
c930f9d4436f.sentence: Some of the theories of dryland farming developed in the late 19th and early 20th centuries claimed to be scientific but were in reality pseudoscientific and did not stand up to empirical testing.

1e7a83064360.title: Dryland farming
1e7a83064360.sentence: For example, it was alleged that tillage would seal in moisture, but such "dust mulching" ideas are based on what people imagine should happen, or have been told, rather than what testing actually confirms.

8328d9213b54.title: Dryland farming
8328d9213b54.sentence: In actuality, it has been shown that tillage increases water losses to evaporation.

8951d7c6c52a.title: Dryland farming
8951d7c6c52a.sentence: The nature of dryland farming makes it particularly susceptible to erosion, especially wind erosion.

ebecef29a353.title: Dryland farming
ebecef29a353.sentence: The fact that a fallow period must be included in the crop rotation means that fields cannot always be protected by a cover crop, which might otherwise offer protection against erosion.

05bb27ca0c46.title: Dryland farming
05bb27ca0c46.sentence: Some techniques for conserving soil moisture (such as frequent tillage to kill weeds) are at odds with techniques for conserving topsoil.

6d852e886069.title: Dryland farming
6d852e886069.sentence: Since healthy topsoil is critical to sustainable agriculture, in particular within arid areas, its preservation is generally considered the most important long-term goal of a dryland farming operation.

4510193ffc9a.title: Dryland farming
4510193ffc9a.sentence: Erosion control techniques such as windbreaks, reduced tillage or no-till, spreading straw (or other mulch on particularly susceptible ground), and strip farming are used to minimize topsoil loss.

2e0fcce715bd.title: Agrominerals
2e0fcce715bd.sentence: Agrominerals (also known as stone bread or petrol fertilizer) are minerals of importance to agriculture and horticulture industries for they can provide essential plant nutrients.

84145af95803.title: Agrominerals
84145af95803.sentence: Some agrominerals occur naturally or can be processed to be used as alternative fertilizers or soil amendments.

a8b1a463ebb5.title: Agrominerals
a8b1a463ebb5.sentence: The term agromineral was created in the 19th century and is now one of the leading research topics for sustainable agriculture.

1fccf7683e3e.title: Agrominerals
1fccf7683e3e.sentence: At first agrominerals were used to help recreate soil conditions for exotic plants.

e7e041b3a539.title: Agrominerals
e7e041b3a539.sentence: Potash is one of the major sources for potassium and phosphorus and one of the original agrominerals.

7d3fcd8d5968.title: Agrominerals
7d3fcd8d5968.sentence: The other concern with the potash ore is the supply is finite and is running out, hence the increase in pricing.

9fea5ab3830b.title: Agrominerals
9fea5ab3830b.sentence: Alternative sources are being researched, due to potash finite supply and cost.

f4ee5adcebf9.title: Agrominerals
f4ee5adcebf9.sentence: While studying alternative ways to replenish ground nutrients, it has been found that agrominerals can also help mitigate other issues such climate change, water preservation and soil management.

c27f323e5ef0.title: Agrogeology
c27f323e5ef0.sentence: Agrogeology is the study of the origins of minerals known as agrominerals and their applications.

ff1ea5e3cef4.title: Agrogeology
ff1ea5e3cef4.sentence: Agrogeology can also be defined as the application of geology to problems in agriculture, particularly in reference to soil productivity and health.

390b7445a2a6.title: Agrogeology
390b7445a2a6.sentence: This field is a combination of a few different fields, including geology, soil science, agronomy, and chemistry.

1b64f539ad9a.title: Agrogeology
1b64f539ad9a.sentence: The overall objective is to advance agricultural production by using geological resources to improve chemical and physical aspects of soil.

3ee8f2d7d271.title: Agrominerals
3ee8f2d7d271.sentence: The study of agrominerals is termed agrogeology, and agrogeologists are concerned with issues such as the replenishment of soil fertility in areas where agrominerals have been depleted by unsustainable farming methods.

667c2800fc86.title: Agrogeology
667c2800fc86.sentence: The first agrogeology project to receive major funding was the Tanzania-Canada project (1989).

a3f52160be1b.title: Agrogeology
a3f52160be1b.sentence: This project took place in southern Tanzania as a way to assist farmers in increasing soil productivity by finding and testing local raw materials.

9bf63227fdaf.title: Agrogeology
9bf63227fdaf.sentence: However, the use of raw materials as fertilizer is a practice that dates back to the 1800s.

61573e9559b2.title: Agrogeology
61573e9559b2.section: List of other raw materials used in agriculture
61573e9559b2.sentence: Apatite - a major source of slow release of phosphate in acidic soils.

26d196456b04.title: Agrogeology
26d196456b04.section: List of other raw materials used in agriculture
26d196456b04.sentence: Carbonate - contains liming materials used to solve problems of acidity and related toxicities.

a412065fe17e.title: Agrogeology
a412065fe17e.section: List of other raw materials used in agriculture
a412065fe17e.sentence: Malachite – useful for correction of copper deficiencies

eb4aeac011f1.title: Agrogeology
eb4aeac011f1.section: List of other raw materials used in agriculture
eb4aeac011f1.sentence: Scoria – useful as a mulching material to conserve soil water and provide slow release of nutrients.

ca90f97b1f57.title: Agrogeology
ca90f97b1f57.section: List of other raw materials used in agriculture
ca90f97b1f57.sentence: Zeolite – useful in conserving nitrogen and releasing phosphorus from apatite couple reaction, also raises pH

7bed024e3e45.title: Organic farming
7bed024e3e45.sentence: Supporters claim that organically managed soil has a higher quality and higher water retention.

d552b0d0c347.title: Organic farming
d552b0d0c347.sentence: An 18-year study of organic methods on nutrient-depleted soil concluded that conventional methods were superior for soil fertility and yield for nutrient-depleted soils in cold-temperate climates, arguing that much of the benefit from organic farming derives from imported materials that could not be regarded as self-sustaining.

36b0a6d1c4ce.title: Organic farming
36b0a6d1c4ce.sentence: This may help increase yields for organic farms in drought years.

ba7c75f38634.title: Organic farming
ba7c75f38634.sentence: Organic farming can build up soil organic matter better than conventional no-till farming, which suggests long-term yield benefits from organic farming.

e57ca7e111bd.title: Organic farming
e57ca7e111bd.sentence: However, a 2007 study by the USDA's Agricultural Research Service has found that manure applications in tilled organic farming are better at building up the soil than no-till.

be3806ae6f05.title: Organic farming
be3806ae6f05.sentence: Gunsmoke Farms, a 137 square kilometres (53 square miles) organic farming project in South Dakota, suffered from massive soil erosion as result of tilling after it switched to organic farming.

7b87797880a3.title: Organic farming
7b87797880a3.sentence: Organic farming relies more heavily on the natural breakdown of organic matter than the average conventional farm, using techniques like green manure and composting, to replace nutrients taken from the soil by previous crops.

09f7293649df.title: Organic farming
09f7293649df.sentence: This biological process, driven by microorganisms such as mycorrhiza and earthworms, releases nutrients available to plants throughout the growing season.

8e2af132c46b.title: Organic farming
8e2af132c46b.sentence: Supplying enough nitrogen and particularly synchronization, so that plants get enough nitrogen at the time when they need it most, is a challenge for organic farmers.

d25f3b07a78d.title: Organic farming
d25f3b07a78d.sentence: Crop rotation and green manure ("cover crops") help to provide nitrogen through legumes (more precisely, the family Fabaceae), which fix nitrogen from the atmosphere through symbiosis with rhizobial bacteria.

f8d00d750992.title: Organic farming
f8d00d750992.sentence: Organic farmers also use animal manure and certain processed fertilizers, such as seed meal and various mineral powders such as rock phosphate and green sand, a naturally occurring form of potash that provides potassium.

18df02805fd6.title: Organic farming
18df02805fd6.sentence: Farms without livestock ("stockless") may find it more difficult to maintain soil fertility and may rely more on external inputs, such as imported manure, as well as grain legumes and green manures, although grain legumes may fix limited nitrogen because they are harvested.

fa820d6937d4.title: Organic farming
fa820d6937d4.sentence: Manure is very bulky and is often not cost-effective to transport more than a short distance from the source.

882281d15e90.title: Center-pivot irrigation
882281d15e90.sentence: Center-pivot irrigation (sometimes called central-pivot irrigation), also called water-wheel and circle irrigation, is a method of crop irrigation in which equipment rotates around a pivot and crops are watered with sprinklers.

7dcfecadc696.title: Center-pivot irrigation
7dcfecadc696.sentence: A circular area centered on a pivot is irrigated, often creating a circular pattern in crops when viewed from above (sometimes referred to as crop circles, not to be confused with those formed by circular flattening of a section of a crop in a field).

01379915a074.title: Center-pivot irrigation
01379915a074.sentence: Center-pivot irrigation is a form of overhead sprinkler irrigation consisting of several segments of pipe (usually galvanized steel or aluminum) with sprinklers positioned along their length, joined together and supported by trusses, and mounted on wheeled towers.

a0736d3d15ae.title: Center-pivot irrigation
a0736d3d15ae.sentence: The machine moves in a circular pattern and is fed with water from the pivot point at the center of the circle.

a8a5ffc714ec.title: Center-pivot irrigation
a8a5ffc714ec.sentence: Center pivots are typically less than 500 meters (1,600 ft) in length (circle radius), with the most common size being the standard 400-meter (1⁄4 mi) machine, which covers about 50 hectares (125 acres) of land.

71ffb3fb3367.title: Center-pivot irrigation
71ffb3fb3367.sentence: Most center-pivot systems now have drops hanging from a U-shaped pipe called a gooseneck attached at the top of the pipe with sprinkler heads that are positioned a few feet (at most) above the crop, thus limiting evaporative losses and wind drift.

cd2c8da5495b.title: Center-pivot irrigation
cd2c8da5495b.sentence: Drops can also be used with drag hoses or bubblers that deposit the water directly on the ground between crops.

1c5e2a8dba58.title: Center-pivot irrigation
1c5e2a8dba58.sentence: This type of system is known as LEPA (Low Energy Precision Application) and is often associated with the construction of small dams along the furrow length (termed furrow diking/dyking).

a2ecb5f6b70b.title: Center-pivot irrigation
a2ecb5f6b70b.sentence: Also, center-pivot irrigation can reduce the amount of soil tillage.

ae8a48d41974.title: Center-pivot irrigation
ae8a48d41974.sentence: Therefore, it helps reduce water runoff and soil erosion that can occur with ground irrigation.

23fd4fe819f8.title: Center-pivot irrigation
23fd4fe819f8.sentence: In parts of the United States, sixty years of the profitable business of intensive farming using huge center-pivot irrigators has emptied parts of the Ogallala Aquifer (also known as the High Plains Aquifer).

8cce31984d0f.title: Center-pivot irrigation
8cce31984d0f.sentence: At some places, during maximum extraction, the water table dropped more than 1.5 m (5 ft) per year.

bc26c1cec80b.title: Agrominerals
bc26c1cec80b.sentence: The process of replenishing mineral levels in a soil is called soil remineralization.

128c07216f03.title: Agrominerals
128c07216f03.sentence: The process of using agrominerals starts with crushing rocks into a "rock powder," than using the powder to replenish soil nutrients.

8203d47e0229.title: Agrominerals
8203d47e0229.sentence: Remineralization looks into the process of taking rock powders and incorporating it into the soil as a way to replenish the nutrients in the ground.

5e3b0a99b486.title: Agrogeology
5e3b0a99b486.sentence: Multi-nutrient rock fertilizers are slow releasing fertilizers that contain micro-nutrients, such as potassium, calcium, and magnesium, as well as smaller amounts of macro-nutrients like phosphorus.

4340b370888c.title: Agrogeology
4340b370888c.sentence: The idea is to mimic natural weathering that happens to parent material in the soil over long periods of time.

849d126e3e06.title: Agrominerals
849d126e3e06.sentence: Remineralization using rock powder can provide up to 5 years' worth of nutrients in a soil.

e3d2a15cdea0.title: Agrominerals
e3d2a15cdea0.sentence: With rock powder the plant absorbs only what it needs, and any unused minerals will remain crystalized until it is used.

b96a03aaba61.title: Agrominerals
b96a03aaba61.sentence: While chemical fertilizers use dissolvable salts to deliver the nutrients to the plant, whatever is not absorb will run off into the nearest groundwater.

76c931bb8b90.title: Agrominerals
76c931bb8b90.sentence: When used in the combination with organic fertilizer, rock powder has proven to be just as effective as chemical fertilizer for a much smaller cost.

54c9c40966cd.title: Agrogeology
54c9c40966cd.sentence: Other benefits of these rock fertilizers include raising the pH of the soils and being able to locally source materials from mining waste.

fd4f88dec63c.title: Agrogeology
fd4f88dec63c.sentence: This method is not without downsides: it requires a high amount of application, the release rate of nutrients is slow, and as compared to industrial fertilizers, it's not as effective as other agronomic methods.

a06b1ff4834f.title: Agrogeology
a06b1ff4834f.sentence: While using multi-nutrient rock fertilizers can't replace industrial fertilizers, it does have other benefits.

24ee5b2477bc.title: Agrominerals
24ee5b2477bc.sentence: Rates are dependent on factors like organic matter, pH levels, secondary clay precipitation.

96c31a5b3dfa.title: Agrominerals
96c31a5b3dfa.sentence: This is a major area of research since their dissolution kinetics are not fully understood.

69d3a3915f3f.title: Agrominerals
69d3a3915f3f.sentence: One of the major challenges is recreating the field conditions in the lab, in many cases the solubility rates in the lab are 2-5 magnitudes higher than the ones in the field.

ddf0cc2a3bee.title: Agrominerals
ddf0cc2a3bee.sentence: Volcanic rocks were thought to be a good source for rock powder but it was determined that it contains toxic elements as well.

5823d0aed781.title: Agrominerals
5823d0aed781.sentence: Research has been done into phosphate rocks, but these too have the issue of containing heavy and radioactive elements.

c400d75e682a.title: Agrominerals
c400d75e682a.sentence: When nutrients from certain powders are absorbed, cations are released in the soil which reacts to with carbon dioxide to create carbonate minerals, which can serve as a carbon sink for the carbon cycle.

23056185c507.title: Agrominerals
23056185c507.sentence: The use of rock powder in remineralization has the potential to help mitigate global warming.

601eaa9fd545.title: Surface irrigation
601eaa9fd545.section: Types of surface irrigation > Basin irrigation
601eaa9fd545.sentence: Level basin irrigation has historically been used in small areas having level surfaces that are surrounded by earth banks.

c8167b1cefc8.title: Surface irrigation
c8167b1cefc8.section: Types of surface irrigation > Basin irrigation
c8167b1cefc8.sentence: The water is applied rapidly to the entire basin and is allowed to infiltrate.

9e02487120e9.title: Surface irrigation
9e02487120e9.section: Types of surface irrigation > Basin irrigation
9e02487120e9.sentence: Basin irrigation is favored in soils with relatively low infiltration rates.

d9a42dfce59d.title: Surface irrigation
d9a42dfce59d.section: Types of surface irrigation > Basin irrigation
d9a42dfce59d.sentence: In traditional basins no water is permitted to drain from the field once it is irrigated.

d6d0814bb52e.title: Surface irrigation
d6d0814bb52e.section: Types of surface irrigation > Basin irrigation
d6d0814bb52e.sentence: Fields are typically set up to follow the natural contours of the land but the introduction of laser levelling and land grading has permitted the construction of large rectangular basins that are more appropriate for mechanised broadacre cropping.

d18caf0cf1b9.title: Surface irrigation
d18caf0cf1b9.section: Types of surface irrigation > Basin irrigation > Drainback level basins
d18caf0cf1b9.sentence: Drainback level basins (DBLBs) or contour basins are a variant of basin irrigation where the field is divided into a number of terraced rectangular bays which are graded level or have no significant slope.

ac52535ad2cb.title: Surface irrigation
ac52535ad2cb.section: Types of surface irrigation > Basin irrigation > Drainback level basins
ac52535ad2cb.sentence: Water is applied to the first bay (usually the highest in elevation) and then the desired depth of applied water is permitted to drain back off that bay and flow to the next bay which is at a lower elevation than the first.

bbe792ec5810.title: Surface irrigation
bbe792ec5810.section: Types of surface irrigation > Basin irrigation > Drainback level basins
bbe792ec5810.sentence: These systems are commonly used in Australia where rice and wheat are grown in rotation.

07e268eddeba.title: Surface irrigation
07e268eddeba.section: Types of surface irrigation > Furrow irrigation
07e268eddeba.sentence: Furrow irrigation is conducted by creating small parallel channels along the length of the field parallel to the direction of its predominant slope.

ad94531a5ad5.title: Surface irrigation
ad94531a5ad5.section: Types of surface irrigation > Furrow irrigation
ad94531a5ad5.sentence: Water is applied to the top end of each furrow and flows down the field under the influence of gravity.

a885933f10ac.title: Surface irrigation
a885933f10ac.section: Types of surface irrigation > Furrow irrigation
a885933f10ac.sentence: The speed of water movement is determined by many factors such as slope, surface roughness, and furrow shape, but most importantly by the inflow rate and soil infiltration rate.

8f108971f172.title: Surface irrigation
8f108971f172.section: Types of surface irrigation > Furrow irrigation
8f108971f172.sentence: Furrows may range anywhere from less than 100 to 2,000 m (0.062 to 1.243 mi) long depending on the soil type, location, and crop type.

29d8aba65aa3.title: Surface irrigation
29d8aba65aa3.section: Types of surface irrigation > Furrow irrigation
29d8aba65aa3.sentence: Furrow irrigation is particularly suited to broadacre row crops such as cotton, maize, and sugar cane.

20fb6e30a474.title: Surface irrigation
20fb6e30a474.section: Types of surface irrigation > Furrow irrigation
20fb6e30a474.sentence: The water can take a considerable period of time to reach the other end, meaning water has been infiltrating for a longer period of time at the top end of the field.

b08c6798933a.title: Surface irrigation
b08c6798933a.section: Types of surface irrigation > Furrow irrigation
b08c6798933a.sentence: This results in poor uniformity with high application at the top end with lower application at the bottom end.

7c7bd4580210.title: Surface irrigation
7c7bd4580210.section: Types of surface irrigation > Furrow irrigation
7c7bd4580210.sentence: Increasing the advance rate not only improves the uniformity but also reduces the total volume of water required to complete the irrigation.

816ed36800e4.title: Surface irrigation
816ed36800e4.section: Types of surface irrigation > Furrow irrigation > Surge irrigation
816ed36800e4.sentence: Surge Irrigation is a variant of furrow irrigation where the water supply is pulsed on and off in planned time periods (e.g. on for 1 hour off for 1½ hour).

11508ace2d23.title: Surface irrigation
11508ace2d23.section: Types of surface irrigation > Furrow irrigation > Surge irrigation
11508ace2d23.sentence: The wetting and drying cycles reduce infiltration rates resulting in faster advance rates and higher uniformity than continuous flow.

4cd0bd58a96d.title: Surface irrigation
4cd0bd58a96d.section: Types of surface irrigation > Furrow irrigation > Surge irrigation
4cd0bd58a96d.sentence: The reduction in infiltration is a result of surface consolidation, filling of cracks and micro pores and the disintegration of soil particles during rapid wetting and consequent surface sealing during each drying phase.

0fa2db98b780.title: Surface irrigation
0fa2db98b780.section: Types of surface irrigation > Furrow irrigation > Surge irrigation
0fa2db98b780.sentence: The effectiveness of surge irrigation is soil type dependent; for example, many clay soils experience a rapid sealing behaviour under continuous flow and therefore surge irrigation offers little benefit.

ac66180628e1.title: Surface irrigation
ac66180628e1.section: Types of surface irrigation > Spate irrigation
ac66180628e1.sentence: Spate irrigation (from the English word spate, meaning: a. a flood or inundation. b. a river flooding its banks) uses seasonal floods of rivers, streams, ponds and lakes to fill water storage basins.

4aa3d8b6a016.title: Surface irrigation
4aa3d8b6a016.section: Types of surface irrigation > Spate irrigation
4aa3d8b6a016.sentence: In spate irrigation, water is diverted from normally dry river beds when the river is in spate.

4be14afcc1cd.title: Surface irrigation
4be14afcc1cd.section: Types of surface irrigation > Spate irrigation
4be14afcc1cd.sentence: It is an ancient method of irrigation in arid and semi-arid climates in the Middle East, North Africa, West Asia, East Africa and parts of Latin America.

0dc88633f0d1.title: Surface irrigation
0dc88633f0d1.section: Types of surface irrigation > Spate irrigation
0dc88633f0d1.sentence: This may be done by free intakes, by diversion spurs or by bunds, that are built across the river bed.

727093eacb37.title: Surface irrigation
727093eacb37.section: Types of surface irrigation > Spate irrigation
727093eacb37.sentence: The flood water, typically lasting a few hours or a few days, is channelled through a network of primary, secondary and sometimes tertiary flood channels.

5328efd32067.title: Surface irrigation
5328efd32067.section: Types of surface irrigation > Spate irrigation
5328efd32067.sentence: Command areas may range from anything between a few hectares to over 25,000 hectares (62,000 acres).

a2f166d76647.title: Surface irrigation
a2f166d76647.section: Types of surface irrigation > Spate irrigation
a2f166d76647.sentence: Because fast-moving water is capable of moving very large amounts of sediment, the heights of river banks and the composition of their beds can change rapidly.

34bda189caed.title: Fallow
34bda189caed.sentence: Fallow syndrome is when a crop has insufficient nutrient uptake due to the lack of arbuscular mycorhizae (AM fungi) in the soil following a fallow period.

19d1a9fcaf74.title: Fallow
19d1a9fcaf74.sentence: Crops such as corn that are prone to fallow syndrome should not follow a period of fallow, but instead should follow a cover crop which is a host for AM fungi, such as oats or other small grain crops.

b04a0e97b33d.title: Fallow
b04a0e97b33d.sentence: The presence of any plant roots, including weeds, can reduce occurrence of fallow syndrome.

1b85b668e726.title: Fallow
1b85b668e726.sentence: Nowadays, agricultural fields are routinely planted with cover crops to prevent erosion, keep down weeds, provide a green manure, and reduce the risk of fallow syndrome.

a6a1a24e89d8.title: Fertigation
a6a1a24e89d8.sentence: Fertigation is the injection of fertilizers, used for soil amendments, water amendments and other water-soluble products into an irrigation system.

72daa5882bb4.title: Fertigation
72daa5882bb4.sentence: Fertigation is used to add additional nutrients or to correct nutrient deficiencies detected in plant tissue analysis.

30c998ec244b.title: Fertigation
30c998ec244b.sentence: Nitrogen is the most commonly used plant nutrient.

b1bf79973919.title: Fertigation
b1bf79973919.sentence: Commonly, anhydrous ammonia, ammonium nitrate, and urea are used as bioavailable sources of nitrogen.

9d5156ca100f.title: Fertigation
9d5156ca100f.sentence: Like nitrogen, plants require these substances to live but they must be contained in other chemical substances such as monoammonium phosphate or diammonium phosphate to serve as bioavailable nutrients.

7c292e535fe0.title: Fertigation
7c292e535fe0.sentence: A common source of potassium is muriate of potash which is chemically potassium chloride.

4a3fe92cb405.title: Fertigation
4a3fe92cb405.sentence: - Application of nutrients can be controlled at the precise time and rate necessary.

cc7dbe25112e.title: Fertigation
cc7dbe25112e.sentence: Drip irrigation using fertigation can also increase yield and quality of fruit and flowers, especially in subsurface drip systems rather than above surface drip tape.

57c77cc08f17.title: Fertigation
57c77cc08f17.sentence: Because of the potential risk of contamination in the potable (drinking) water supply, a backflow prevention device is required for most fertigation systems.

a4981c77d8d3.title: Regenerative agriculture
a4981c77d8d3.sentence: Holistically managed grazing is a practice that is based on consistent rotation of livestock herds onto different fields in order to mimic how natural herds would graze.

517362517194.title: Regenerative agriculture
517362517194.sentence: There is mixed evidence on the carbon sequestration potential of regenerative grazing.

9c9ecd74c793.title: Regenerative agriculture
9c9ecd74c793.sentence: A meta-analysis of relevant studies between 1972 and 2016 found that Holistic Planned Grazing had no better effect than continuous grazing on plant cover and biomass, although it may have benefited some areas with higher precipitation.

f100c2ed9e1e.title: Regenerative agriculture
f100c2ed9e1e.sentence: One study found that regenerative grazing management, particularly adaptive multi-paddock (AMP) grazing, has been shown to reduce soil degradation compared to continuous grazing and thus has the potential to mitigate carbon emissions from soil.

ef54e2bc870b.title: Regenerative agriculture
ef54e2bc870b.sentence: Another study found that crop rotation and maintenance of permanent cover crops help to reduce soil erosion as well, and in conjunction with AMP grazing, may result in net carbon sequestration.

c854545b6724.title: Regenerative agriculture
c854545b6724.sentence: According to a 2016 study published by the Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences, the actual rate at which improved grazing management could contribute to carbon sequestration is seven times lower than the claims made by Savory.

81933e34cbae.title: Regenerative agriculture
81933e34cbae.sentence: The study concludes that holistic management cannot reverse climate change.

69da99a6c07e.title: Intercropping
69da99a6c07e.sentence: Alley cropping has crop strips alternating with rows of closely spaced tree or hedge species.

68cf2276ffbf.title: Intercropping
68cf2276ffbf.sentence: Normally, the trees are pruned before planting the crop.

80c685d24113.title: Intercropping
80c685d24113.sentence: The cut leafy material - for example, from Alchornea cordifolia and Acioa barteri - is spread over the crop area to provide nutrients.

68220252bb88.title: Intercropping
68220252bb88.sentence: In addition to nutrients, the hedges serve as windbreaks and reduce erosion.

898252ea497d.title: Intercropping
898252ea497d.sentence: Inga trees, native to Central and South America, grow well on acid soils of tropical rainforest or former rainforest.

193afe78dd29.title: Intercropping
193afe78dd29.sentence: They are leguminous, fixing nitrogen into a form usable by plants.

610540935088.title: Intercropping
610540935088.sentence: The leaves form a thick mulch that protects both soil and roots from sun and rain.

178576031f70.title: Intercropping
178576031f70.sentence: The trees form a thick canopy that cuts off light from the weeds below, and withstand annual pruning.

10961bfc71a8.title: Intercropping
10961bfc71a8.sentence: It increases yields and is more sustainable as it allows the land to be cultivated repeatedly, eliminating the need for slash and burn to get fertile plots.

35140d7ea4d7.title: Intercropping
35140d7ea4d7.sentence: Inga alley cropping offers an alternative to the ecologically destructive slash and burn cultivation.

964ca72b8e06.title: Agroforestry
964ca72b8e06.sentence: The difference is that, with alley cropping, the trees are in single rows.

b30b8e55cb2b.title: Agroforestry
b30b8e55cb2b.sentence: With strip cropping, the trees or shrubs are planted in wide strips.

0c23e6648864.title: Biofumigation
0c23e6648864.sentence: Biofumigation is a method of pest control in agriculture, a variant of fumigation where the gaseous active substance—fumigant—is produced by decomposition of plant material freshly chopped and buried in the soil for this purpose.

4b1d04af6182.title: Biofumigation
4b1d04af6182.sentence: Plants from the Brassicaceae family (e.g., mustards, cauliflower, and broccoli) are primarily used due to their high glucosinolate content; in the process of decomposition, glucosinolates are broken down to volatile isothiocyanates which are toxic to soil organisms such as bacteria, fungi and nematodes, but less toxic and persistent in the environment than synthetic fumigants.

63d323a0bebb.title: Biofumigation
63d323a0bebb.sentence: Alternatively, grasses such as sorghum can be used, in which case hydrogen cyanide is produced to similar effect.

d32f2a66cdc7.title: Biofumigation
d32f2a66cdc7.sentence: The method consists of mowing and chopping the plants during flowering to ensure maximum glucosinolate content and speed up decomposition.

4c22c059695c.title: Biofumigation
4c22c059695c.sentence: The ground needs to be irrigated to field capacity, after which the chopped material is incorporated into the top layer and covered with impermeable film to prevent the gas from escaping.

45904b7ea4ae.title: Biofumigation
45904b7ea4ae.sentence: After three or four weeks, the film is removed and the ground is ready for planting 24 hours later.

65c09a9f8fff.title: Biofumigation
65c09a9f8fff.sentence: Additionally, it can serve to replenish the nutrient content of the soil and promote growth of beneficial organisms.

d9454a774f3f.title: Biofumigation
d9454a774f3f.sentence: On the other hand, it requires changes in cultivation practice due to the time needed for the method to take effect, can be costly if biofumigant-producing plants need to be brought from elsewhere (i. e. if they are not used in crop rotation to be chopped and buried on site), and is difficult to standardize due to varying active substance content in different cultivars.

890d321af607.title: Agrogeology
890d321af607.sentence: Rock phosphate, also known as phosphorite, can be used as a sustainable, cost-effective method to mend problems associated with plant growth.

6eaa77650063.title: Agrogeology
6eaa77650063.sentence: Rock phosphate is mined from clay deposits that contain phosphorus.

c87088206e79.title: Agrogeology
c87088206e79.sentence: These rocks are mostly sedimentary, one example being limestone.

785ae3f3d6c5.title: Agrogeology
785ae3f3d6c5.sentence: A high percentage of traditional fertilizers intended to mend phosphorus-deficient soils end up becoming insoluble complexes in the soil.

41d60ba47cb6.title: Agrogeology
41d60ba47cb6.sentence: This presents a need for constant reapplication.

d6a898e54a39.title: Agrogeology
d6a898e54a39.sentence: Unlike other elements that are soluble and easily accessible, rock phosphate needs to be processed in order to make the phosphorus in them available for plant and soil intake.

7fe79925817b.title: Agrogeology
7fe79925817b.sentence: Microbial solubilization of rock phosphate through fungi has been found to be able to break down inorganic phosphate into soluble forms by processes that produce organic acids.

f1794016981e.title: Agrogeology
f1794016981e.sentence: Once it is ground and impurities are removed, water and sulfuric acid is added to the phosphate rock which generates gypsum crystals, a way of getting rid of what we don't want, leaving phosphorus as an acidic liquid.

b80c3ef3795a.title: Agrogeology
b80c3ef3795a.sentence: Then vapor ammonia is applied to the liquid phosphorus and the end products are phosphorus granules.

72506891f996.title: Agrogeology
72506891f996.sentence: Residual dust from mining has also been used in conjunction with processed fertilizer in order to improve plant development.

4195072f3e0e.title: Agrogeology
4195072f3e0e.sentence: A study in Zimbabwe suggests that this mixture increases plant growth, phosphorus levels, and organic carbon.

8a24a06233b6.title: Zaï
8a24a06233b6.sentence: Zaï or tassa is a farming technique of digging pits in less permeable soil to catch water and concentrate compost.

5a150fc0ff9c.title: Zaï
5a150fc0ff9c.sentence: The pits are between 15 and 50 centimetres (0.5 and 2 ft) across and around 5 to 15 centimetres (2 to 6 in) deep, spaced approximately 80 centimetres (3 ft) apart.

3b60e1d136bc.title: Zaï
3b60e1d136bc.sentence: The technique is traditionally used in western Sahel (Burkina Faso, Niger, Mali) to restore degraded drylands and increase soil fertility.

9e27ca1a07ec.title: Zaï
9e27ca1a07ec.sentence: The technique has also been adopted by smallholder farmers in semi-arid regions of East Africa, particularly in Kenya, where farmers in counties such as Kitui use it in combination with modern agricultural practices to improve water retention and crop yields in dryland conditions.

e8f4821d718f.title: Zaï
e8f4821d718f.sentence: Zaï holes were reintroduced since the 1980s by Yacouba Sawadogo, a farmer from Burkina Faso, who introduced the innovation of filling them with manure and compost to provide plant nutrients.

0b16479b91f1.title: Zaï
0b16479b91f1.sentence: The manure attracts termites, whose tunnels help further break up the soil.

2ebca090811c.title: Zaï
2ebca090811c.sentence: Zaï holes help by improving the yields of trees, sorghum, and millet by up to 500 percent.

e68543b9433a.title: Biosolarization
e68543b9433a.sentence: Biosolarization is an alternative technology to soil fumigation used in agriculture.

48406d55ff3c.title: Biosolarization
48406d55ff3c.sentence: Biosolarization adds the use of organic amendments or compost to the soil before it is covered with plastic, which speeds up the solarization process by decreasing the soil treatment time through increased microbial activity.

7a6f8b873e65.title: Biosolarization
7a6f8b873e65.sentence: It is closely related to biofumigation and soil solarization, or the use of solar power to control nematodes, bacteria, fungi and other pests that damage crops.

12e506f36d46.title: Biosolarization
12e506f36d46.sentence: Research conducted in Spain on the use of biosolarization in strawberry fruit production has shown it to be a sustainable and cost effective option.

b3fdb6d6efc5.title: Biosolarization
b3fdb6d6efc5.sentence: The practice of biosolarization is being used among small agricultural operations in California.

fe32254a1690.title: Biosolarization
fe32254a1690.sentence: Biosolarization can also use as organic waste management practice.

423a4df5887b.title: Biosolarization
423a4df5887b.sentence: Recent studies showed the potential of food industrial residues as soil amendments that can improve the efficiency of biosolarization.

e0f523f5fd5b.title: Natural farming
e0f523f5fd5b.sentence: Natural farming (自然農法, shizen nōhō), also referred to as "the Fukuoka Method", "the natural way of farming", or "do-nothing farming", is an ecological farming approach established by Masanobu Fukuoka (1913–2008).

dacf7c148bf6.title: Natural farming
dacf7c148bf6.sentence: Rather than offering a structured method, Fukuoka distilled the natural farming mindset into five principles:

17c14da6cdf8.title: Natural farming
17c14da6cdf8.sentence: Fukuoka specifies that the ground remain covered by weeds, white clover, alfalfa, herbaceous legumes, and sometimes deliberately sown herbaceous plants.

0c863b6f3bbe.title: Natural farming
0c863b6f3bbe.sentence: Periodically ground layer plants including weeds may be cut and left on the surface, returning their nutrients to the soil, while suppressing weed growth.

df160c985f9c.title: Natural farming
df160c985f9c.sentence: Straw from the previous crop mulches the topsoil.

3bbc3357a601.title: Natural farming
3bbc3357a601.sentence: Natural farming is a closed system, one that demands no human-supplied inputs and mimics natural conditions.

9890251c90e1.title: Natural farming
9890251c90e1.sentence: Fukuoka's natural farming practice rejected the use of modern technology, and after twenty-five years, his farm demonstrated consistently comparable yields to that of the most technologically advanced farms in Japan, doing so without the pollution, soil loss, energy consumption, and environmental degradation inherent in these modern types of farming.

91c7119cc7b6.title: Natural farming
91c7119cc7b6.sentence: Fukuoka avoided the creation of terraces in his farm, even though terraces were common in China and Japan in his time.

28cdecedf98f.title: Natural farming
28cdecedf98f.sentence: Instead, he prevented soil erosion by simply growing trees and shrubs on slopes.

b520e8499dd2.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.03%3A_Rotations_and_Soil_Organic_Matter_Levels
b520e8499dd2.sentence: The types of crops you grow, their yields, the amount of roots produced, the portion of the crop harvested and how you manage crop residues will all affect soil organic matter.

e3769c78a9cf.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.03%3A_Rotations_and_Soil_Organic_Matter_Levels
e3769c78a9cf.sentence: The decrease in organic matter levels when row crops are planted on a virgin forest or prairie soil is very rapid for the first five to 10 years, but, eventually, a low level equilibrium is reached.

6f625e4a2f9d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.03%3A_Rotations_and_Soil_Organic_Matter_Levels
6f625e4a2f9d.sentence: After that, soil organic matter levels remain stable, as long as production practices aren’t changed.

a88237b42841.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.03%3A_Rotations_and_Soil_Organic_Matter_Levels
a88237b42841.sentence: Soil organic matter levels increase when the cropping system is changed from a cultivated crop to a grass or mixed grass–legume sod.

66f7fce439a2.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.03%3A_Rotations_and_Soil_Organic_Matter_Levels
66f7fce439a2.sentence: However, the increase is usually much slower than the decrease that occurred under continuous tillage because rotations that include perennials reduce the total amount of tillage and the associated soil organic matter losses.

828c748e3e47.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.03%3A_Rotations_and_Soil_Organic_Matter_Levels
828c748e3e47.sentence: More than 9 inches of topsoil were lost during 60 years of continuous corn.

d6d7f4763a2d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.03%3A_Rotations_and_Soil_Organic_Matter_Levels
d6d7f4763a2d.sentence: The amount of soil lost each year from the continuous corn plots was equivalent to 21 tons per acre.

adf6bed1500e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.03%3A_Rotations_and_Soil_Organic_Matter_Levels
adf6bed1500e.sentence: Differences in erosion and organic matter decomposition resulted in soil organic matter levels of 2.2% for the unfertilized timothy and 1.2% for the continuous corn plots.

c44394a12a7f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.03%3A_Rotations_and_Soil_Organic_Matter_Levels
c44394a12a7f.sentence: A six-year rotation consisting of corn, oats, wheat, clover and two years of timothy resulted in about 70% as much topsoil as was found in the timothy soil, a much better result than with continuous corn.

edb1d36fbeff.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.03%3A_Rotations_and_Soil_Organic_Matter_Levels
edb1d36fbeff.sentence: In an experiment in eastern Canada, continuous corn led to annual increases in organic matter of about 100 pounds per acre, while two years of corn followed by two years of alfalfa increased organic matter by about 500 pounds per acre per year, and four years of alfalfa increased organic matter by 800 pounds per acre per year.

cce77d515d4f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.03%3A_Rotations_and_Soil_Organic_Matter_Levels
cce77d515d4f.sentence: Keep in mind that these amounts are small compared to the amounts of organic matter in most soils: 3% organic matter represents about 60,000 pounds per acre to a depth of 6 inches.

ad0cff79e1d3.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.03%3A_Rotations_and_Soil_Organic_Matter_Levels
ad0cff79e1d3.sentence: First, the rate of decomposition of soil organic matter decreases because the soil is not continually being disturbed.

172a94438dd5.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.03%3A_Rotations_and_Soil_Organic_Matter_Levels
172a94438dd5.sentence: (This also happens when using no-till planting, even for non-sod crops such as corn.) Second, grass and legume sods develop extensive root systems, part of which will naturally die each year and add new organic matter to the soil.

fb37a3495418.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.03%3A_Rotations_and_Soil_Organic_Matter_Levels
fb37a3495418.sentence: Older roots of grasses die, even during the growing season, and provide sources of fresh, active organic matter.

1721ccbe8031.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.03%3A_Rotations_and_Soil_Organic_Matter_Levels
1721ccbe8031.sentence: Also, as soil organic matter increases to such an extent that mineral surfaces are fully saturated with organic matter and the soil is already highly aggregated, organic matter content increases plateau no matter how much is added in crop residue, manures and composts.

568d3d10ed51.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.03%3A_Rotations_and_Soil_Organic_Matter_Levels
568d3d10ed51.sentence: Experiments in a semiarid region in Oregon found that the total amount of microorganisms in a two-year wheat-fallow system was only about 25% of the amount found under pasture.

9f8d4971fc57.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.03%3A_Rotations_and_Soil_Organic_Matter_Levels
9f8d4971fc57.sentence: Conventional moldboard plow tillage systems are known to decrease the populations of earthworms and other soil organisms.

97654aeae4a6.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.03%3A_Rotations_and_Soil_Organic_Matter_Levels
97654aeae4a6.sentence: Including perennial forages in the rotation enhances this effect.

1b4eb6243b70.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.02%3A_Benefits_of_Cover_Crops
1b4eb6243b70.sentence: While this term is used generally, different types of plants are grown as cover crops to achieve a number of primary purposes:

5757df86dd73.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.02%3A_Benefits_of_Cover_Crops
5757df86dd73.sentence: Catching and cycling nutrients: typically grasses such as cereal rye and oats.

ab0c327c1985.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.02%3A_Benefits_of_Cover_Crops
ab0c327c1985.sentence: Fixing nitrogen via symbiotic relationship with Rhizobium bacteria (green manures): typically legumes (e.g., hairy vetch and red clover).

8dfcf02e59cc.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.02%3A_Benefits_of_Cover_Crops
8dfcf02e59cc.sentence: Smothering weeds: typically competitive, fast-growing species (e.g., buckwheat, sorghum-sudangrass, cereals).

9925d9f86f1a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.02%3A_Benefits_of_Cover_Crops
9925d9f86f1a.sentence: Biofumigating pests with glucosinolates and isothiocyanates: typically brassicas (e.g., mustards and radishes).

b217e8b7ef1b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.02%3A_Benefits_of_Cover_Crops
b217e8b7ef1b.sentence: Loosening compacted soil: typically strong-rooted crops (e.g., cereal rye, radishes, hairy vetch, alfalfa).

36de2fffca32.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.02%3A_Benefits_of_Cover_Crops
36de2fffca32.sentence: Growing biomass and organic matter: typically fast-growing crops (e.g., sorghum-sudangrass, cereal rye, sunn hemp).

bd8fa86c47eb.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.02%3A_Benefits_of_Cover_Crops
