bd8fa86c47eb.sentence: Plant ecologists separate these into canopy functions (where benefits are primarily derived from the aboveground biomass) and root functions (where benefits are from the belowground biomass), and the selection of a cover crop may be based on the specific desired traits.

2f58fc3a76c6.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.02%3A_Benefits_of_Cover_Crops
2f58fc3a76c6.sentence: Grass cover crops are more likely than legumes to increase soil organic matter.

ecbfdc143845.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.02%3A_Benefits_of_Cover_Crops
ecbfdc143845.sentence: In that regard, we generally don’t fully appreciate their rooting systems unless we dig them up because some cover crops grow as much or more biomass underground than above, thereby directly benefiting the soil.

09f84d731448.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.02%3A_Benefits_of_Cover_Crops
09f84d731448.sentence: Good production of hairy vetch or crimson clover cover crops may yield from 1 1/2 to more than 4 tons of dry weight per acre if allowed to grow long enough.

5589e74d31a3.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.02%3A_Benefits_of_Cover_Crops
5589e74d31a3.sentence: Likewise, if a vigorous grass cover crop like cereal rye is grown to maturity, it can produce 3–5 tons of residue.

a3ae03ea14e4.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.02%3A_Benefits_of_Cover_Crops
a3ae03ea14e4.sentence: However, the amount of residue produced by an early terminated cover crop may be very modest, as little as half a ton of dry matter per acre.

068af708a098.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.02%3A_Benefits_of_Cover_Crops
068af708a098.sentence: A five-year experiment with clover in California showed that cover crops increased organic matter in the top 2 inches from 1.3%–2.6% and in the 2- to 6-inch layer from 1%–1.2%.

315dc325aa83.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.02%3A_Benefits_of_Cover_Crops
315dc325aa83.sentence: Researchers found, when the results of many experiments were examined together, that including cover crops led to an organic matter increase of 8.5% over original levels and an increase of soil nitrogen by 12.8%.

6a4a3f158717.title: Deficit irrigation
6a4a3f158717.sentence: > Deficit irrigation is an optimization strategy in which irrigation is applied during drought-sensitive growth stages of a crop.

69fa04bd4771.title: Deficit irrigation
69fa04bd4771.sentence: Outside these periods, irrigation is limited or even unnecessary if rainfall provides a minimum supply of water.

163e2d10aa09.title: Deficit irrigation
163e2d10aa09.sentence: While this inevitably results in plant drought stress and consequently in production loss, DI maximizes irrigation water productivity, which is the main limiting factor (English, 1990).

a5ea46cff0db.title: Deficit irrigation
a5ea46cff0db.sentence: In other words, DI aims at stabilizing yields and at obtaining maximum crop water productivity rather than maximum yields (Zhang and Oweis, 1999).

aa291e940bd4.title: Deficit irrigation
aa291e940bd4.sentence: Crop water productivity (WP) or water use efficiency (WUE) expressed in kg/m³ is an efficiency term, expressing the amount of marketable product (e.g. kilograms of grain) in relation to the amount of input needed to produce that output (cubic meters of water).

12eb364e7e7f.title: Deficit irrigation
12eb364e7e7f.sentence: Representative values of WUE for cereals at field level, expressed with evapotranspiration in the denominator, can vary between 0.10 and 4 kg/m3.

a9b4c22d01b2.title: Deficit irrigation
a9b4c22d01b2.sentence: Experiments in Turkey and India indicated that the irrigation water use for cotton could be reduced to up to 60 percent of the total crop water requirement with limited yield losses.

436737a29874.title: Deficit irrigation
436737a29874.sentence: This is the case when crops are sensitive to drought stress throughout the complete season, such as maize.

f2fcf5ab47b7.title: Deficit irrigation
f2fcf5ab47b7.sentence: - reduces nutrient loss by leaching of the root zone, which results in better groundwater quality and lower fertilizer needs as for cultivation under full irrigation;

2b76b7b5cfde.title: Deficit irrigation
2b76b7b5cfde.sentence: - Because irrigation is applied more efficiently, the risk for soil salinization is higher under DI as compared to full irrigation.

e20cf6f01b96.title: Hydroponics
e20cf6f01b96.sentence: Hydroponics is a type of horticulture and a subset of hydroculture which involves growing plants, usually crops or medicinal plants, without soil, by using water-based mineral nutrient solutions in an artificial environment.

8a5481001e4b.title: Hydroponics
8a5481001e4b.sentence: Terrestrial or aquatic plants may grow freely with their roots exposed to the nutritious liquid or the roots may be mechanically supported by an inert medium such as perlite, gravel, or other substrates.

757732f6b209.title: Hydroponics
757732f6b209.sentence: Different media are appropriate for different growing techniques.

04e0a8399c2c.title: Hydroponics
04e0a8399c2c.sentence: Rock wool (mineral wool) is the most widely used medium in hydroponics.

90ca17918151.title: Hydroponics
90ca17918151.sentence: Rock wool is made from molten rock, basalt or 'slag' that is spun into bundles of single filament fibres, and bonded into a medium capable of capillary action, and is, in effect, protected from most common microbiological degradation.

3a15b8697ca9.title: Hydroponics
3a15b8697ca9.sentence: Mineral wool products can be engineered to hold large quantities of water and air that aid root growth and nutrient uptake in hydroponics; their fibrous nature also provides a good mechanical structure to hold the plant stable.

1958de163612.title: Hydroponics
1958de163612.sentence: The naturally high pH of mineral wool makes them initially unsuitable to plant growth and requires "conditioning" to produce a wool with an appropriate, stable pH.

13dda293b484.title: Hydroponics
13dda293b484.section: Substrates (growing support materials) > Expanded clay aggregate
13dda293b484.sentence: The clay is formed into round pellets and fired in rotary kilns at 1,200 °C (2,190 °F).

00e5dfe304df.title: Hydroponics
00e5dfe304df.section: Substrates (growing support materials) > Expanded clay aggregate
00e5dfe304df.sentence: This causes the clay to expand, like popcorn, and become porous.

bcd89990fde9.title: Hydroponics
bcd89990fde9.section: Substrates (growing support materials) > Expanded clay aggregate
bcd89990fde9.sentence: The clay pellets are inert, pH-neutral, and do not contain any nutrient value.

121e82c6a03f.title: Hydroponics
121e82c6a03f.section: Substrates (growing support materials) > Expanded clay aggregate
121e82c6a03f.sentence: It is light in weight, and does not compact over time.

9dca45bff54b.title: Hydroponics
9dca45bff54b.sentence: When exposed to water, the brown, dry, chunky and fibrous material expands nearly three or four times its original size.

12f2887f0926.title: Hydroponics
12f2887f0926.sentence: This characteristic combined with coconut coir's water retention capacity and resistance to pests and diseases make it an effective growth medium.

ff7e09bc4acd.title: Hydroponics
ff7e09bc4acd.sentence: This process removes salt, tannins and phenolic compounds through substantial water washing.

41f743695bb4.title: Hydroponics
41f743695bb4.sentence: Contaminated water is a byproduct of this process, as three hundred to six hundred liters of water per one cubic meter of coir are needed.

4b880194b317.title: Hydroponics
4b880194b317.sentence: Perlite has similar properties and uses to vermiculite but, in general, holds more air and less water and is buoyant.

d294f5c86999.title: Hydroponics
d294f5c86999.sentence: Vermiculite holds more water than perlite and has a natural "wicking" property that can draw water and nutrients in a passive hydroponic system.

f358ff5ed3c5.title: Hydroponics
f358ff5ed3c5.sentence: If too much water and not enough air surrounds the plants roots, it is possible to gradually lower the medium's water-retention capability by mixing in increasing quantities of perlite.

e951b59311ef.title: Mineral wool
e951b59311ef.sentence: Mineral wool (also known as stone wool, mineral cotton, mineral fiber, man-made mineral fiber (MMMF), and man-made vitreous fiber (MMVF)) is any fibrous material formed by spinning or drawing molten mineral or rock materials such as slag and ceramics.

e6755795d1e6.title: Mineral wool
e6755795d1e6.sentence: Applications include thermal insulation (as both structural insulation and pipe insulation), filtration, soundproofing, and hydroponic growth medium.

0d8f01ab821a.title: Mineral wool
0d8f01ab821a.sentence: Mineral wool products can be engineered to hold large quantities of water and air that aid root growth and nutrient uptake in hydroponics; their fibrous nature also provides a good mechanical structure to hold the plant stable.

20fcc443dee9.title: Mineral wool
20fcc443dee9.sentence: The naturally high pH of mineral wool makes them initially unsuitable to plant growth and requires "conditioning" to produce a wool with an appropriate, stable pH.

5e8322fa3c97.title: Mineral wool
5e8322fa3c97.sentence: Conditioning methods include pre-soaking mineral wool in a nutrient solution adjusted to pH 5.5 until it stops bubbling.

08cd0ad9b732.title: Mineral wool
08cd0ad9b732.sentence: Stone wool is a furnace product of molten rock at a temperature of about 1600°C through which a stream of air or steam is blown.

bacc654dce4f.title: Mineral wool
bacc654dce4f.sentence: The final product is a mass of fine, intertwined fibers with a typical diameter of 2 to 6 micrometers.

0fc285a04d16.title: Expanded clay aggregate
0fc285a04d16.sentence: Expanded clay (exclay) or lightweight expanded clay aggregate (LECA) is a lightweight aggregate made by heating clay to around 1,200 °C (2,190 °F) in a rotary kiln.

a7486ffacf01.title: Expanded clay aggregate
a7486ffacf01.sentence: The heating process causes gases trapped in the clay to expand, forming thousands of small bubbles and giving the material a porous structure.

69b75440fd03.title: Expanded clay aggregate
69b75440fd03.sentence: LECA is usually produced in different sizes and densities from 0.1 millimetres (0.004 in) up to 25 millimetres (1.0 in), commonly 0–4 mm, 4–10 mm, 10–25 mm and densities of 250, 280, 330, and 510 kg/m3.

97357e55257b.title: Expanded clay aggregate
97357e55257b.sentence: LECA can be mixed with heavy soil to improve its aeration and drainage.

f0e5f9fa2bbd.title: Expanded clay aggregate
f0e5f9fa2bbd.sentence: It is commonly used as a growing medium in hydroponics systems since blended with other growing mediums such as soil and peat, it can improve compaction resistance, and drainage, retain water during periods of drought, insulate roots during frost, and provide roots with increased oxygen levels promoting very vigorous growth.

8ac89b3b9473.title: Expanded clay aggregate
8ac89b3b9473.sentence: In the horticultural practice of hydroponics, LECA is a favored medium for growing plants within; the round shape provides excellent aeration at the root level, while the LECA clay pieces themselves become saturated with water and plant food, thus giving the roots a consistent supply of both.

b14bdf2e5c68.title: Expanded clay aggregate
b14bdf2e5c68.sentence: So-called semi-hydroponics or passive hydroponics (also called "semi-hydro") is a popular, simplified method of hydroponics, most commonly utilized for houseplants and tropical species.

ecaedc2e3df3.title: Expanded clay aggregate
ecaedc2e3df3.sentence: Only the very bottom of the pot needs to touch this reservoir; the LECA, being porous by nature, gradually wicks moisture and nutrients up and becomes saturated, allowing the plant to feed and drink at a consistent rate.

ef2be7645858.title: Soil steam sterilization
ef2be7645858.section: Types of Soil Steaming In Practice
ef2be7645858.sentence: Different types of steam application include substrate steaming, surface steaming, and deep soil steaming.

2a23469afd0c.title: Soil steam sterilization
2a23469afd0c.section: Types of Soil Steaming In Practice > Surface steaming
2a23469afd0c.sentence: In order to pick the most suitable steaming method, certain factors have to be considered such as soil structure, plant culture and area performance.

aabc666d7efb.title: Soil steam sterilization
aabc666d7efb.section: Types of Soil Steaming In Practice > Sheet steaming
aabc666d7efb.sentence: Surface steaming with special sheets (sheet steaming) is a method which has been established for decades in order to steam large areas reaching from 15 to 400 m2 (160 to 4,310 ft2) in one step.

1b15dbbb8e53.title: Soil steam sterilization
1b15dbbb8e53.section: Types of Soil Steaming In Practice > Sheet steaming
1b15dbbb8e53.sentence: Single working step areas up to 400 m2 can be steamed in 4–5 hours down to 25–30 cm (9.8–11.8 in) depth and 90 °C (194 °F).

aa97c3bd1421.title: Soil steam sterilization
aa97c3bd1421.section: Types of Soil Steaming In Practice > Sheet steaming
aa97c3bd1421.sentence: The usage of heat resistant, non-decomposing insulation fleece saves up to 50% energy, reduces the steaming time significantly and improves penetration.

98e00cf1776b.title: Soil steam sterilization
98e00cf1776b.section: Types of Soil Steaming In Practice > Depth steaming with vacuum
98e00cf1776b.sentence: Steaming with vacuum which is induced through a mobile or fixed installed pipe system in the depth of the area to be steamed, is the method that reaches the best penetration.

423cd5f27288.title: Soil steam sterilization
423cd5f27288.section: Types of Soil Steaming In Practice > Depth steaming with vacuum
423cd5f27288.sentence: Despite high capital cost, the fixed installation of drainage systems is reasonable for intensively used areas since steaming depths of up to 80 cm (2.6 ft) can be achieved.

485720d4619c.title: Soil steam sterilization
485720d4619c.section: Types of Soil Steaming In Practice > Negative pressure technique
485720d4619c.sentence: Negative pressure technique generates appropriate soil temperature at a 60 cm (2.0 ft) depth and complete control of nematodes, fungi and weeds is achieved.

d3edcf043f10.title: Soil steam sterilization
d3edcf043f10.section: Types of Soil Steaming In Practice > Combined surface and depth injection of steam (Sandwich Steaming)
d3edcf043f10.sentence: Sandwich steaming, which was developed in a project among DEIAFA, University of Turin (Italy, www.deiafa.unito.it) and Ferrari Costruzioni Meccaniche (see image), represents a combination of depth and surface steaming, offers an efficient method to induce hot steam into the soil.

4b51b31a4a44.title: Soil steam sterilization
4b51b31a4a44.section: Types of Soil Steaming In Practice > Combined surface and depth injection of steam (Sandwich Steaming)
4b51b31a4a44.sentence: The steam is simultaneously pushed into the soil from the surface and from the depth.

2873733df756.title: Soil steam sterilization
2873733df756.section: Types of Soil Steaming In Practice > Container / Stack steaming
2873733df756.sentence: Stack steaming is used when steam treating compost and substrates such as turf.

591bb15678b8.title: Soil steam sterilization
591bb15678b8.section: Types of Soil Steaming In Practice > Container / Stack steaming
591bb15678b8.sentence: Depending on the amount, the material to be steamed is piled up to 70 cm (2.3 ft) height in steaming boxes or in small dump trailers.

0a1c085d692b.title: Soil steam sterilization
0a1c085d692b.section: Types of Soil Steaming In Practice > Container / Stack steaming
0a1c085d692b.sentence: The amount of soil steamed should be tuned in a way that steaming time amounts to at most 1.5 h in order to avoid large quantities of condensed water in the bottom layers of the soil.

f9f2056384bb.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.04%3A_Cover_Crop_Management
f9f2056384bb.sentence: Cover cropping can play an important role in N management, whether the need is to supply N for grains or vegetables, or to lower available N at the end of the season to reduce losses.

3037384b25e2.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.04%3A_Cover_Crop_Management
3037384b25e2.sentence: If a legume is productive and allowed to grow to the bud stage to gain sufficient size (biomass), quite a bit of N will be made available to the next crop, from 70 to well over 100 pounds per acre.

3bee4f700cdb.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.04%3A_Cover_Crop_Management
3bee4f700cdb.sentence: Hairy vetch and crimson clover are two of the many choices that farmers frequently turn to in order to produce a lot of N, but other legumes may prove useful as sources of N.

43b119036624.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.04%3A_Cover_Crop_Management
43b119036624.sentence: The amount of N that will be made available to the following crop depends on the stage of growth, the amount of growth (biomass), and the N content of the cover crop or cover crop mix.

c7af62ea5b2c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.04%3A_Cover_Crop_Management
c7af62ea5b2c.sentence: Small cover crops whose leaves are deep green, for example, in early spring, will contain a high percent of N, over 3 percent.

87178bafbc51.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.04%3A_Cover_Crop_Management
87178bafbc51.sentence: But because there is so little mass of material, the plants contain low total amounts of N. The N percent of a cover crop such as cereal rye tends to decrease (from over 3 percent) as the plant grows more leaves and then when the stem elongates and flowering and maturity occurs, ending up well below 1 percent N with a C:N ratio of 80 or more.

5d0fd684d44b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.04%3A_Cover_Crop_Management
5d0fd684d44b.sentence: If the crop has a low percent N (around 1.5%–2% N), as is common with small grains when stems elongate and flowering begins, little to no N can be counted on to help the following crop because soil organisms use all the N present as they decompose the residue.

a8e2f372d869.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.03%3A_Types_of_Cover_Crops
a8e2f372d869.sentence: Commonly used grass cover crops include the annual cereals (rye, wheat, triticale, barley oats), annual or perennial forage grasses such as ryegrass, and warm-season grasses such as sorghum-sudangrass.

12ff16d5bf31.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.03%3A_Types_of_Cover_Crops
12ff16d5bf31.sentence: Grasses, with their fibrous root systems, are very useful for scavenging nutrients, especially nitrogen, left over from a previous crop.

e7e909611a34.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.03%3A_Types_of_Cover_Crops
e7e909611a34.sentence: They tend to have extensive root systems (Figure 10.4), and some establish rapidly and can greatly reduce erosion.

dccaee215763.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.03%3A_Types_of_Cover_Crops
dccaee215763.sentence: In addition, they can produce large amounts of residue and a large amount of roots.

1ebe4dd2fae4.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.03%3A_Types_of_Cover_Crops
1ebe4dd2fae4.sentence: Both the residue and the roots can help add organic matter to the soil.

ce9e2d049d62.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.03%3A_Types_of_Cover_Crops
ce9e2d049d62.sentence: The aboveground residue also can help suppress weed germination and growth.

18c230cafb15.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.03%3A_Types_of_Cover_Crops
18c230cafb15.sentence: Left: Cereal rye grows in late fall and early spring, and is an effective catch crop and soil conditioner in cool regions.

c06ff86c4b9f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.03%3A_Types_of_Cover_Crops
c06ff86c4b9f.sentence: It is widely used in Maryland to reduce nutrient loading into the Chesapeake Bay.

bf5400adbb72.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.03%3A_Types_of_Cover_Crops
bf5400adbb72.sentence: Leguminous plants are often very good cover crops.

e8f3605301a0.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.03%3A_Types_of_Cover_Crops
e8f3605301a0.sentence: Summer annual legumes, usually grown only during the summer, include soybeans, cowpeas and sunn hemp.

b7c16545b312.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.03%3A_Types_of_Cover_Crops
b7c16545b312.sentence: Winter annual legumes that are normally planted in the fall and counted on to overwinter include winter field peas (such as Austrian), crimson clover, hairy vetch, Balansa clover and subterranean clover.

ebc008dd791b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.03%3A_Types_of_Cover_Crops
ebc008dd791b.sentence: Sweet yellow clover is an example of a biennial legume, while perennial legumes include red clover, white clover and alfalfa.

b9b8d3c12180.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.03%3A_Types_of_Cover_Crops
b9b8d3c12180.sentence: Crimson clover is considered one of the best cover crops for areas with mild climates, like the southeastern United States and the southern Plains, such as Oklahoma and parts of Texas.

c647e12a069c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.03%3A_Types_of_Cover_Crops
c647e12a069c.sentence: Where adapted, it grows in the fall and winter, and matures more rapidly than most other legumes.

ff02ff88aa24.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.03%3A_Types_of_Cover_Crops
ff02ff88aa24.sentence: It also contributes a relatively large amount of nitrogen to the following crop.

52a980f55877.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.03%3A_Types_of_Cover_Crops
52a980f55877.sentence: Because it is not very winter hardy, crimson clover is not usually a good choice in hardiness zones 4 or colder, and it can be marginal in zone 5 (snow cover and/or early planting can help with winter survival).

3ced9df32db7.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.03%3A_Types_of_Cover_Crops
3ced9df32db7.sentence: Crimson clover does not grow well on high-pH (calcareous) or poorly drained soils.

3a1b8e02bf02.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.03%3A_Types_of_Cover_Crops
3a1b8e02bf02.sentence: Austrian winter peas (bred for winter hardiness) and Canadian field peas (bred for good spring growth) tend to establish quickly and grow rapidly in cool moist climates, producing a significant amount of residue: 2 1/2 tons or more of dry matter.

d737a476847f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.03%3A_Types_of_Cover_Crops
d737a476847f.sentence: They fix plentiful amounts of nitrogen, from 100–150 or more pounds per acre.

cd8e5450b7ac.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.03%3A_Types_of_Cover_Crops
cd8e5450b7ac.sentence: Cowpeas are native to Central Africa and do well in hot climates.

88f3789c3a50.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.03%3A_Types_of_Cover_Crops
88f3789c3a50.sentence: The cowpea is, however, killed by even a mild frost.

9c8197f58d10.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.03%3A_Types_of_Cover_Crops
9c8197f58d10.sentence: It is deep rooted and is able to do well under droughty conditions.

5123cea9a2b7.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.03%3A_Types_of_Cover_Crops
5123cea9a2b7.sentence: It usually does better on low-fertility soils than crimson clover.

22fd932133b8.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.03%3A_Types_of_Cover_Crops
22fd932133b8.sentence: It establishes easily and rapidly and develops a dense cover, which makes it a good choice for weed suppression.

e841f731a546.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.03%3A_Types_of_Cover_Crops
e841f731a546.sentence: Berseem has the advantage of being unlikely to cause bloat in grazing livestock.

a4ac5d5ea7f6.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.03%3A_Types_of_Cover_Crops
a4ac5d5ea7f6.sentence: Sweet clover (yellow blossom) is a reasonably winter hardy, biennial, vigorous growing crop with an ability to get its roots into compacted subsoils.

80b9398a1c3a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.03%3A_Types_of_Cover_Crops
80b9398a1c3a.sentence: Sweet clover requires a soil pH near neutrality and a high calcium level; it does poorly in wet, clayey soils.

b4b9eaa57884.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.03%3A_Types_of_Cover_Crops
b4b9eaa57884.sentence: Red clover is vigorous, shade tolerant, winter hardy, and can be established relatively easily.

fe5f1d42b8e2.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.03%3A_Types_of_Cover_Crops
fe5f1d42b8e2.sentence: It is commonly interseeded in early spring with small grains.

5c778320f291.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.03%3A_Types_of_Cover_Crops
5c778320f291.sentence: Because it starts growing slowly, there is minimal competition between it and the small grain.

b9324e62e080.title: Multiple cropping
b9324e62e080.sentence: In agriculture, multiple cropping or multicropping is the practice of growing two or more crops in the same piece of land during one year, instead of just one crop.

110121a61545.title: Multiple cropping
110121a61545.sentence: When multiple crops are grown simultaneously, this is also known as intercropping.

3ac134cd47aa.title: Multiple cropping
3ac134cd47aa.sentence: It can take the form of double-cropping, in which a second crop is planted after the first has been harvested.

b52433ee214a.title: Multiple cropping
b52433ee214a.sentence: In the Garhwal Himalaya of India, a practice called barahnaja involves sowing 12 or more crops on the same plot, including various types of beans, grains, and millets, and harvesting them at different times.

4d1ad3cd4cf2.title: Multiple cropping
4d1ad3cd4cf2.sentence: Overall costs of input decreases, cost spent on fertilizers, irrigation, labour, etc. reduces because of growing two or more than two crops on the same field.

4718b800135c.title: Multiple cropping
4718b800135c.sentence: Risk of weed growth, pest and disease infestation reduces because of mutual relationship within the crop.

00849556b3ba.title: Multiple cropping
00849556b3ba.sentence: However, only 5% of global rainfed cropland is under multiple cropping, while 40% of global irrigated cropland is under multiple cropping.

6d213fdf34c4.title: Bromomethane
6d213fdf34c4.sentence: Bromomethane, commonly known as methyl bromide, is an organobromine compound with formula CH3Br.

fba8983e7a6e.title: Bromomethane
fba8983e7a6e.sentence: It is widely applied as a soil sterilant, mainly for production of seed but also for some crops such as strawberries and almonds.

e6ed39b79e92.title: Bromomethane
e6ed39b79e92.sentence: Bromomethane is safer and more effective than some other soil sterilants.

196083093390.title: Bromomethane
196083093390.sentence: Bromomethane is readily photolyzed in the atmosphere to release bromine radicals, which are far more destructive to stratospheric ozone than chlorine.

923453463014.title: Bromomethane
923453463014.sentence: As such, it is subject to phase-out requirements of the 1987 Montreal Protocol on Ozone Depleting Substances.

aaf6d74f0768.title: Bromomethane
aaf6d74f0768.sentence: All developed countries in the Montreal Protocol reduced both manufactured and imported amounts by 25% in 1999, 50% 2001, 75% 2003, 100% 2005.

60b3df51a4c1.title: Bromomethane
60b3df51a4c1.sentence: Its loss to the seed industry has resulted in changes to cultural practices, with increased reliance on soil steam sterilization, mechanical roguing, and fallow seasons.

93f63996e8e6.title: Bromomethane
93f63996e8e6.sentence: - Chloropicrin has been used in combination with bromomethane, and standalone is a common alternative fumigant.

5e8e12767d4e.title: Bromomethane
5e8e12767d4e.sentence: - 1,3-Dichloropropene replaces some of both the fungicide and nematicide effects of BM, but is not a full-efficacy replacement.

6f76dee77cb5.title: Bromomethane
6f76dee77cb5.sentence: - Methyl isothiocyanate is the breakdown product/a.i. of two applied products, metam sodium and granular dazomet.

1b69a8a81492.title: Bromomethane
1b69a8a81492.sentence: MITC does not redistribute through the soil as well as BM.

be7eac147329.title: Bromomethane
be7eac147329.sentence: Requires significantly more irrigation for activation.

df39e8c87819.title: Variable rate application
df39e8c87819.sentence: In precision agriculture, variable rate application (VRA) refers to the application of a material, such that the rate of application is based on the precise location, or qualities of the area that the material is being applied to.

3584041a22c7.title: Variable rate application
3584041a22c7.sentence: This is different from uniform application, and can be used to save money (using less product), and lessen the environmental impact.

565f4adac6c5.title: Variable rate application
565f4adac6c5.sentence: Variable rate application can be either map based or sensor based.

1b5d9f832909.title: Variable rate application
1b5d9f832909.sentence: - Map based VRA is pre-planned, and applications are based on VRA prescription maps that an agronomist or advisor prepares based on data sources.

54d11c694ca1.title: Variable rate application
54d11c694ca1.sentence: - Sensor based VRA is calculated realtime, based on sensors that are local to the variable rate applicator.

2736e9bbe2dc.title: Variable rate application
2736e9bbe2dc.sentence: Prescription maps can be created using electromagnetic induction, which is considered to be cost-effective, and non-destructive.

788427ad8a5d.title: Variable rate application
788427ad8a5d.sentence: Crops do not always require a uniform application, as some areas will have different nutrient requirements due to their location (soil properties, sunlight).

c272cb5d2626.title: Variable rate application
c272cb5d2626.sentence: Variable rate fertilizer spreaders can be used to increase or decrease fertilizer application rate, using a global positioning system (GPS).

9bc13f9b52b4.title: Precision agriculture
9bc13f9b52b4.sentence: For example, the use of fleet digitalization techniques and GPS trackers reduces fuel consumption for agriculture, while variable rate application of nutrients or pesticides can potentially reduce the use of these inputs, thereby saving costs and reducing harmful runoff into the waterways.

902ba0a8e8ac.title: Salt tolerance of crops
902ba0a8e8ac.sentence: ECe 0–2 non-saline soil ECe 2–4 slightly saline, yield of sensitive crops reduced ECe 4–8 moderately saline, yield reduction of many crops ECe 8–16 saline, normal yield for salt tolerant crops only ECe > 16 reasonable crop yields only for very tolerant crops

dcb251e7bbec.title: Salt tolerance of crops
dcb251e7bbec.sentence: The most common parameter used in soil salinity is the electric conductivity of the extract (ECe) of a saturated soil paste in units of deciSiemens per metre (dS/m) (previously measured in millimhos per centimeter (mmho/cm)).

060e4b589972.title: Crop tolerance to seawater
060e4b589972.sentence: Author Schleiff presented a classification of salt tolerance of crops based on ECe in dS/m that may be summarized as follows:

8574673a6468.title: Crop tolerance to seawater
8574673a6468.sentence: The main difference with the classification published by Richards in the USDA Agriculture Handbook No. 60, 1954 is that the classes are narrower with steps of 2 dS/m instead of 4.

ffc126708366.title: Crop tolerance to seawater
ffc126708366.sentence: Crop tolerance to seawater is the ability of an agricultural crop to withstand the high salinity induced by irrigation with seawater, or a mixture of fresh water and seawater.

e0693eb4f5fb.title: Crop tolerance to seawater
e0693eb4f5fb.sentence: There are crops that can grow on seawater and demonstration farms have shown the feasibility.

d5043db14652.title: Crop tolerance to seawater
d5043db14652.sentence: The government of the Netherlands reports a breakthrough in food security as specific varieties of potatoes, carrots, red onions, white cabbage and broccoli appear to thrive if they are irrigated with salt water.

8b0711b76968.title: Crop tolerance to seawater
8b0711b76968.sentence: The Salt Farm Texel, a farm on the island of Texel, The Netherlands, is testing the salt tolerance of crops under controlled field conditions.

660772a935ed.title: Crop tolerance to seawater
660772a935ed.sentence: There are 56 experimental plots of 160 m2 each that are treated in eight replicas with seven different salt concentrations.

782546c32887.title: Crop tolerance to seawater
782546c32887.sentence: These concentrations are obtained with intensive daily drip irrigations of 10 or more mm (i.e. more than 10 liter per m2 per day) with water having a salt concentration expressed in electric conductivity (EC) of 2, 4, 8, 12, 16, 20 and 35 dS/m.

666b903612d5.title: Crop tolerance to seawater
666b903612d5.sentence: The range of EC values is obtained by mixing fresh water with the appropriate amount of seawater having a salinity corresponding to an EC value of about 50 dS/m.

8a2db74cdea6.sentence: It’s impossible to recommend specific rotations for a wide variety of situations.

01e623905fe7.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.09%3A_Rotation_Examples
01e623905fe7.sentence: Every farm has its own unique combination of soil and climate, and of human, animal and machine resources.

da8ce8937687.sentence: A five- to seven-year rotation was common in the mixed livestock-crop farms of the northern Midwest and the Northeast during the first half of the 20th century.

095c0faf0198.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.09%3A_Rotation_Examples
095c0faf0198.sentence: The most nitrogen-demanding crop, corn, followed the pasture, and grain was harvested only two of every five to seven years.

bd5a4adb2f8b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.09%3A_Rotation_Examples
bd5a4adb2f8b.sentence: A less-nitrogen-demanding crop, oats, was planted in the second year as a “nurse crop” when the grass-legume hay was seeded.

399f9c83bd60.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.09%3A_Rotation_Examples
399f9c83bd60.sentence: This rotation maintained soil organic matter in many situations, or at least didn’t cause it to decrease too much.

a94d74f7e2cd.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.09%3A_Rotation_Examples
a94d74f7e2cd.sentence: In the Corn Belt region of the Midwest, a change in rotations occurred as pesticides and fertilizers became readily available, animals were fed in large feedlots instead of on integrated crop-livestock farms, and grain export markets were developed.

9304c90b3a17.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.09%3A_Rotation_Examples
9304c90b3a17.sentence: In addition, government commodity price support programs unintentionally encouraged farmers to narrow production to just two feed grains.

ff44b90c1a3e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.09%3A_Rotation_Examples
ff44b90c1a3e.sentence: The two-year corn-soybean rotation is better than monoculture, but it has a number of problems, including erosion, groundwater pollution with nitrates and herbicides, soil organic matter depletion, and in some situations, increased insect problems.

1876eeeb22b2.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.09%3A_Rotation_Examples
1876eeeb22b2.sentence: Soybeans leave minimal amounts of residues.

41c9fab61a97.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.01%3A_Introduction
41c9fab61a97.sentence: There are multiple ways to diversify cropping systems, and there are good reasons to do so.

ebb265602b2e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.01%3A_Introduction
ebb265602b2e.sentence: Diversity over time in a field, year to year, is achieved by using cover crops and by rotating a number of crops.

81e0c966ff83.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.01%3A_Introduction
81e0c966ff83.sentence: You can also diversify spatially, or across your farm’s landscape, by planting different crops in different fields or in strips within fields.

616ef1a39c0e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.01%3A_Introduction
616ef1a39c0e.sentence: A well-planned crop rotation—for example, one that might use the same sequence of crops but staggered differently from one field to the next in a given year or season—provides diversification both over time and across the farm landscape.

389ecbdb461b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.01%3A_Introduction
389ecbdb461b.sentence: Crop diversification can also occur with less frequent rotations by using perennials.

9059f437cab2.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.01%3A_Introduction
9059f437cab2.sentence: For example, dairy farmers may grow alfalfa for three to four years before it is rotated to corn.

159c17c73a48.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.01%3A_Introduction
159c17c73a48.sentence: Agroforestry, the growing of tree species together with annual crops or other perennials, affords another way of adding habitat diversity to a farm.

e1701b7aeb26.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.01%3A_Introduction
e1701b7aeb26.sentence: Integrating livestock and cropping brings yet another dimension of diversity by introducing animals onto the farm.

d28634a04346.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.01%3A_Introduction
d28634a04346.sentence: One important ecological principle is that diversity contributes to stability and productivity (see discussion in Chapter 8).

92a70d664004.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.08%3A_General_Principles
92a70d664004.sentence: Try to consider the following principles when you’re thinking about a new rotation:

89746153f96a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.08%3A_General_Principles
89746153f96a.sentence: - Follow a legume forage crop, such as clover or alfalfa, with a high-nitrogen-demanding crop, such as corn, to take advantage of the nitrogen supply.

440693fe2805.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.08%3A_General_Principles
440693fe2805.sentence: - Grow less of nitrogen-demanding crops, such as oats, barley and wheat, in the second or third year after a legume sod.

5c4dfa3df649.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.08%3A_General_Principles
5c4dfa3df649.sentence: - If possible, grow the same annual crop for only one year to decrease the likelihood of insects, diseases and nematodes becoming a problem.

d67bb23eeb8b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.08%3A_General_Principles
d67bb23eeb8b.sentence: - Don’t follow a crop with a closely related species, since insect, disease and nematode problems are frequently shared by members of closely related crops.

1586458f005e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.08%3A_General_Principles
1586458f005e.sentence: (Note: For many years, the western corn rootworm was effectively controlled by alternating between corn and soybeans.

533a3bfc7d52.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.08%3A_General_Principles
533a3bfc7d52.sentence: Recently, populations of the rootworm with a longer resting period have developed in isolated regions, and they are able to survive this simple two-year rotation.)

57b2edf02341.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.08%3A_General_Principles
57b2edf02341.sentence: - If specific nematodes are known problems, consider planting nonhost plants, such as grain crops for root-knot nematodes, for a few years to decrease populations before planting a very susceptible crop such as carrots or lettuce.

6317a0804bf6.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.08%3A_General_Principles
6317a0804bf6.sentence: Small grains compete strongly against weeds and may inhibit germination of weed seeds; row crops permit midseason cultivation; and sod crops that are mowed regularly or grazed intensively help control annual weeds.

59b1c408d290.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.08%3A_General_Principles
59b1c408d290.sentence: - Use longer periods of perennial crops, such as a forage legume, on sloping land and on highly erosive soils.

a45ba68bde8c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.08%3A_General_Principles
a45ba68bde8c.sentence: - Try to grow a deep-rooted crop, such as alfalfa, safflowers or sunflowers, as part of the rotation.

59ec58120ba9.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.08%3A_General_Principles
59ec58120ba9.sentence: These crops scavenge the subsoil for nutrients and water, and channels left from decayed roots can promote water infiltration.

2f5f1f4af506.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.08%3A_General_Principles
2f5f1f4af506.sentence: - In regions with limited rainfall, the amount of water used by a crop may be a critically important issue, usually one of the most important issues.

4052dd053c71.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.08%3A_General_Principles
4052dd053c71.sentence: Without plentiful irrigation, growing high-water-use crops such as hay, as well as sunflowers and safflowers, may not leave sufficient moisture in the soil for the next crop in the rotation.

9a25f0dcbd60.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.08%3A_General_Principles
9a25f0dcbd60.sentence: (It is estimated that less than 25% of the rainfall that falls during the 14-month fallow period in the Central High Plains is made available to a following crop of winter wheat.) (See the box “Flexible Cropping Systems” and Table 11.2 for discussion and information on flexible, or dynamic, cropping systems.) Growing winter small grains in a rotation offers a number of possibilities depending on weather and the farm’s needs.

6677fc08e2d0.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.05%3A_Species_Richness_and_Active_Rooting_Periods
6677fc08e2d0.sentence: The percent of the time that living roots are present during a rotation is important.

fd0d3d663ddd.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.05%3A_Species_Richness_and_Active_Rooting_Periods
fd0d3d663ddd.sentence: The period that active roots are present varies considerably, ranging from 32% of the time for a corn-soybean rotation to 57% for a soybean-wheat rotation to 76% for a three-year, soybean-wheat-corn rotation (Table 11.1).

82747165de08.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.05%3A_Species_Richness_and_Active_Rooting_Periods
82747165de08.sentence: Just adding winter wheat to a corn-soybean alternation can greatly increase the time that active roots are present.

8507fd077d93.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.05%3A_Species_Richness_and_Active_Rooting_Periods
8507fd077d93.sentence: (Doing so also assists in controlling weeds, increases corn yields and provides another crop to sell.) This is primarily the result of the fact that winter annuals, perennials and cover crops extend the growing period compared to summer annuals.

8670cdda7dda.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.05%3A_Species_Richness_and_Active_Rooting_Periods
8670cdda7dda.sentence: As mentioned above, when soils are covered with living vegetation for a longer period of time, there tends to be decreased erosion, decreased loss of nitrate and less groundwater contamination.

f3219a8bbe67.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.07%3A_Farm_Labor_and_Economics
f3219a8bbe67.sentence: If you grow only one or two row crops, you must work incredibly long hours during planting and harvesting seasons, and not as much at other times.

2d9a36f0b477.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.07%3A_Farm_Labor_and_Economics
2d9a36f0b477.sentence: In addition, when you grow a more diversified group of crops, you are less affected by price fluctuations of one or two crops.

16678246e536.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.07%3A_Farm_Labor_and_Economics
16678246e536.sentence: Including forage hay crops and early harvested crops along with those that are traditionally harvested in the fall would allow you to spread your labor over the growing season, which would make the farm more easy to manage by family labor alone.

bafa57b30f55.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.07%3A_Farm_Labor_and_Economics
bafa57b30f55.sentence: This may provide more year-round income and year-to-year financial stability.

8e8044c85624.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.07%3A_Farm_Labor_and_Economics
8e8044c85624.sentence: You may need more equipment to grow a number of different crops.

33b71f93fef9.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.07%3A_Farm_Labor_and_Economics
33b71f93fef9.sentence: There may be conflicts between labor needs for different crops, like weed cultivation and side-dressing nitrogen fertilizer for corn at the same time as harvesting hay.

1fe07d0a62f5.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.07%3A_Farm_Labor_and_Economics
1fe07d0a62f5.sentence: Well-integrated livestock-crop operations with multi-species grazing have less need for specialized equipment, and the animals can do much of their own harvesting and manure spreading during the grazing season, saving human labor.

32edc3bf2b1f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.07%3A_Farm_Labor_and_Economics
32edc3bf2b1f.sentence: It also diversifies farm income and overall helps cycle nutrients and carbon on the farm.

c228d8267cc6.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.06%3A_Rotations_Water_Quality_and_Gaseous_Losses_of_N
c228d8267cc6.sentence: Diversified rotations offer many benefits when compared to very simple ones.

0b882e3623f0.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.06%3A_Rotations_Water_Quality_and_Gaseous_Losses_of_N
0b882e3623f0.sentence: For example, an experiment in South Dakota compared the simple corn-soybean crop alternation with a four-year corn-field pea-winter wheat-soybean rotation.

8385268123e0.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.06%3A_Rotations_Water_Quality_and_Gaseous_Losses_of_N
8385268123e0.sentence: Researchers found that, compared to corn-soybean alternation, soybean yields were higher in the four-year rotation, more organic matter accumulated in the soil, and less nitrous oxide gas (N2O), a greenhouse gas, was lost to the atmosphere.

04a291d5f1a0.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.06%3A_Rotations_Water_Quality_and_Gaseous_Losses_of_N
04a291d5f1a0.sentence: When annual crops are grown and planted in the spring, such as with corn and soybeans, there is a considerable amount of time when the soil is not occupied by living plant roots.

eb08e93d06d1.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.06%3A_Rotations_Water_Quality_and_Gaseous_Losses_of_N
eb08e93d06d1.sentence: This means that for a large portion of the year there are no living plants to take up nutrients, especially nitrate, that can leach out of the soil.

f79ec74c1079.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.06%3A_Rotations_Water_Quality_and_Gaseous_Losses_of_N
f79ec74c1079.sentence: This is especially a problem in the midwestern and northeastern United States, where many soils have tile drainage, which accentuates the discharge of high-nitrate water into streams and rivers.

61603abfa8af.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.06%3A_Rotations_Water_Quality_and_Gaseous_Losses_of_N
61603abfa8af.sentence: In addition to not taking up nutrients, the lack of growing plants means that the soils are wetter and more apt to produce runoff, erosion and leaching.

fc94107634e4.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.06%3A_Rotations_Water_Quality_and_Gaseous_Losses_of_N
fc94107634e4.sentence: Thus, rotations that include perennial forages and winter grains help maintain or enhance the quality of both ground and surface waters.

f78bc3df4056.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.06%3A_Rotations_Water_Quality_and_Gaseous_Losses_of_N
f78bc3df4056.sentence: And, while intensive use of cover crops helps water quality in a similar way, cover crops should not be viewed as a substitute for a good rotation of economic crops.

5bf25a291f6a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.06%3A_Rotations_Water_Quality_and_Gaseous_Losses_of_N
5bf25a291f6a.sentence: It’s the combination of the positive effects of both good rotations and routine cover crop use that provides the greatest improvements in soil physical, chemical and biological characteristics.

592fca271a11.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.04%3A_Cover_Crop_Management
592fca271a11.sentence: Cover crops can cause serious problems if not managed carefully.

486147152024.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.04%3A_Cover_Crop_Management
486147152024.sentence: They can deplete soil moisture; they can become weeds; and, when used as an intercrop, they can compete with the cash crop for water, light and nutrients.

ba6d3a1dcf3a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.04%3A_Cover_Crop_Management
ba6d3a1dcf3a.sentence: They also tend to be somewhat costly in terms of seed and establishment, so you want to ensure that the benefits pay off.

b793fb96cf6f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.04%3A_Cover_Crop_Management
b793fb96cf6f.sentence: In drier areas and on droughty soils, such as sands, late killing of a winter cover crop may result in moisture deficiency for the main summer crop.

08ab16ea1a42.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.04%3A_Cover_Crop_Management
08ab16ea1a42.sentence: However, in warm, humid climates where no-till methods are practiced, allowing the cover crop to grow longer means fewer problems with soil being very wet or saturated at planting, and more residue and water conservation for the main crop later in the season.

15947da2427b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.04%3A_Cover_Crop_Management
15947da2427b.sentence: Greater formation of large (macro) pores with cover crops leads to more rainfall infiltration, while higher organic matter levels following their use leads to greater soil waterholding capacity.

e6246d6138bc.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.04%3A_Cover_Crop_Management
e6246d6138bc.sentence: Surface residue also slows runoff of rainfall, which allows more to infiltrate into the soil.

de63b361f3e5.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.04%3A_Cover_Crop_Management
de63b361f3e5.sentence: Although most farmers use single species of cover crops in their fields, mixtures of different cover crops offer combined benefits.

7a44ebeb870d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.04%3A_Cover_Crop_Management
7a44ebeb870d.sentence: The most common mixture is a grass and legume, such as cereal rye and hairy vetch, oats and red clover, or field peas and a small grain.

a79b68c702f7.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.04%3A_Cover_Crop_Management
a79b68c702f7.sentence: Mixed stands usually do a better job of suppressing weeds than a single species.

a613892e60b5.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.04%3A_Cover_Crop_Management
a613892e60b5.sentence: Growing legumes with small grains helps compensate for the decreases in nitrogen availability for the following crop when small grains are allowed to mature.

8e0bcd01fda4.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.04%3A_Cover_Crop_Management
8e0bcd01fda4.sentence: In the mid-Atlantic region, the cereal rye-hairy vetch mixture has been shown to provide another advantage for managing nitrogen: When a lot of nitrate is left in the soil at the end of the season, the rye is stimulated (reducing leaching losses).

ad07d3537b9d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.04%3A_Cover_Crop_Management
ad07d3537b9d.sentence: When little nitrogen is available, the vetch competes better with the rye, fixing more nitrogen for the next crop.

f9866cca50ec.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.04%3A_Cover_Crop_Management
f9866cca50ec.sentence: A crop that grows erect, such as cereal rye, may provide support for hairy vetch and enable it to grow better.

24e421077c0a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.04%3A_Cover_Crop_Management
24e421077c0a.sentence: Mowing close to the ground kills vetch supported by rye easier than vetch alone.

d304fe2bdd0b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.04%3A_Cover_Crop_Management
d304fe2bdd0b.sentence: In no-till production systems, this may allow for mowing instead of herbicide use.

9b936b783285.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.04%3A_Cover_Crop_Management
9b936b783285.sentence: There are three ways to time the planting of a cover crop in relation to your cash crops: 1) plant a cover crop for an entire growing season; 2) plant a cover crop after the harvest of a cash crop and before planting the next cash crop; and 3) interseeding, or planting a cover crop into a growing cash crop.

9656ec344ee8.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.04%3A_Cover_Crop_Management
9656ec344ee8.sentence: If you want to accumulate a lot of organic matter, it’s best to grow a high-biomass mix of cover crops for the whole growing season (see Figure 10.7a), which means no income-generating crop will be grown that year.

3c06154c9a72.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.04%3A_Cover_Crop_Management
3c06154c9a72.sentence: This may be especially useful with very infertile or eroded soils and when transitioning to organic farming.

1a7211fd81f0.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.04%3A_Cover_Crop_Management
1a7211fd81f0.sentence: Most farmers sow cover crops after the cash crop has been harvested (Figure 10.7b).

70a51f58ad11.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.04%3A_Cover_Crop_Management
70a51f58ad11.sentence: In this case, as with the system shown in Figure 10.7a, there is no competition between the cover crop and the main crop.

1ef8be1e0516.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.04%3A_Cover_Crop_Management
1ef8be1e0516.sentence: The seeds can be no-till planted with a grain drill or a row crop planter (no need for a high clearance interseeder) instead of broadcast, resulting in better cover crop stands.

e16ef63e1c8c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.04%3A_Cover_Crop_Management
e16ef63e1c8c.sentence: If possible, tillage should be avoided prior to cover crop seeding to maximize the soil health benefits that cover crops provide.

c9364b2fe4f9.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.04%3A_Cover_Crop_Management
c9364b2fe4f9.sentence: The approach you take will depend on your reason for planting a cover crop, your cash crops, the length of the growing season and the climate.

b46705b6cf1d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.04%3A_Cover_Crop_Management
b46705b6cf1d.sentence: No matter when you establish cover crops, they are usually killed or drastically weakened before or during soil preparation for the next cash crop.

195d38f0b773.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.04%3A_Cover_Crop_Management
195d38f0b773.sentence: This preparation is usually done by one of the following approaches: mowing once they’ve flowered (most annuals can be killed that way), using herbicides and no-till, plowing into the soil (with or without use of herbicides), or mowing, rolling and crimping and no-till planting in the same operation, or naturally by winter injury.

6ef78cb8d471.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.04%3A_Cover_Crop_Management
6ef78cb8d471.sentence: In some cases it is a good idea to leave a week or two between the time a cover crop is tilled in or killed and the time a main crop is planted.

86cdbc07ca94.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.04%3A_Cover_Crop_Management
86cdbc07ca94.sentence: This allows some decomposition to occur and may lessen problems of nitrogen immobilization and allelopathic effects, as well as avoiding increased seed decay and damping-off diseases (especially under wet conditions) and problems with cutworm and wireworm.

f4bf01606c8b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.04%3A_Cover_Crop_Management
f4bf01606c8b.sentence: It also may allow for the establishment of a better seedbed for small-seeded crops, such as some of the vegetables.

42b495392e6c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.04%3A_Cover_Crop_Management
42b495392e6c.sentence: Studies have found that a sudex cover crop is especially allelopathic and that tomatoes, broccoli and lettuce should not be planted until six to eight weeks to allow for thorough leaching of residue.

b4a3fc7d7c4c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.04%3A_Cover_Crop_Management
b4a3fc7d7c4c.section: Planting Cover Crops > Cover Crop Selection And Plant Parasitic Nematodes
b4a3fc7d7c4c.sentence: If nematodes become a problem in your crops (common in many vegetables such as lettuce, carrots, onions and potatoes, as well as in some agronomic crops), carefully select cover crops to help limit the damage.

4b83d93b1b40.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.04%3A_Cover_Crop_Management
4b83d93b1b40.section: Planting Cover Crops > Cover Crop Selection And Plant Parasitic Nematodes
4b83d93b1b40.sentence: For example, the root-knot nematode (M. hapla) is a pest of many vegetable crops, as well as of alfalfa, soybeans and clover, but all the grain crops—corn, as well as small grains—are nonhosts.

0edf68d4f1a7.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.04%3A_Cover_Crop_Management
0edf68d4f1a7.section: Planting Cover Crops > Cover Crop Selection And Plant Parasitic Nematodes
0edf68d4f1a7.sentence: Growing grains as cover crops helps reduce nematode numbers.

8f189049eaa9.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.04%3A_Cover_Crop_Management
8f189049eaa9.section: Planting Cover Crops > Cover Crop Selection And Plant Parasitic Nematodes
8f189049eaa9.sentence: If the infestation is very bad, consider two full seasons with grain crops before returning to susceptible crops.

434b21a97ec7.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.04%3A_Cover_Crop_Management
434b21a97ec7.section: Planting Cover Crops > Cover Crop Selection And Plant Parasitic Nematodes
434b21a97ec7.sentence: The root-lesion nematode (P. penetrans) is more of a challenge because most crops, including almost all grains, can be hosts for this organism.

97fea9932bf6.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.04%3A_Cover_Crop_Management
97fea9932bf6.section: Planting Cover Crops > Cover Crop Selection And Plant Parasitic Nematodes
97fea9932bf6.sentence: Whatever you do, don’t plant a legume cover crop such as hairy vetch if you have an infestation of root-lesion nematodes; it will actually stimulate nematode numbers.

0211e23703e9.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.04%3A_Cover_Crop_Management
0211e23703e9.section: Planting Cover Crops > Cover Crop Selection And Plant Parasitic Nematodes
0211e23703e9.sentence: However, sudangrass, sorghum-sudan crosses and ryegrass, as well as pearl millet (a grain crop from Africa, grown in the United States mainly as a warm-season forage crop) have been reported to dramatically decrease nematode numbers.

17f7f60cb8da.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.04%3A_Cover_Crop_Management
17f7f60cb8da.section: Planting Cover Crops > Cover Crop Selection And Plant Parasitic Nematodes
17f7f60cb8da.sentence: The suppressive activity of such cover crops is due to their poor host status to the lesion nematode, general stimulation of microbial antagonists and the release of toxic products during decomposition.

b4a0861516a7.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.04%3A_Cover_Crop_Management
b4a0861516a7.section: Planting Cover Crops > Cover Crop Selection And Plant Parasitic Nematodes
b4a0861516a7.sentence: Forage-type pearl millet, sudangrass and brassicas such as mustard, rapeseed, oilseed radish and flax, all provide some biofumigation effect because when they decompose after incorporation, they produce compounds that are toxic to nematodes.

ed9ffde81169.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.04%3A_Cover_Crop_Management
ed9ffde81169.section: Planting Cover Crops > "Planting Green" Into Cover Crops
ed9ffde81169.sentence: However, more and more farmers are now "planting green," where the cash crop is directly seeded into a still living cover crop.

40e85a2af739.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.04%3A_Cover_Crop_Management
40e85a2af739.section: Planting Cover Crops > "Planting Green" Into Cover Crops
40e85a2af739.sentence: In the past, the recommendation was to leave a week or two between the time the cover crop was killed and when the cash crop was planted.

519b14bae456.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.04%3A_Cover_Crop_Management
519b14bae456.section: Planting Cover Crops > "Planting Green" Into Cover Crops
519b14bae456.sentence: That is still the best approach in certain situations, such as in a dry spring.

4e7856f80dd4.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.04%3A_Cover_Crop_Management
4e7856f80dd4.section: Planting Cover Crops > "Planting Green" Into Cover Crops
4e7856f80dd4.sentence: See the box “Farmers Say Cover Crops Help the Bottom Line.”) Most often, the cover crop is sprayed with an herbicide shortly after the cash crop is planted.
