bf86fd918998.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.04%3A_Cover_Crop_Management
bf86fd918998.section: Planting Cover Crops > "Planting Green" Into Cover Crops
bf86fd918998.sentence: For example, good suppression of hairy vetch in a no-till system has been obtained with the use of a modified rolling stalk chopper at early bloom.

01d7fc7602f8.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.04%3A_Cover_Crop_Management
01d7fc7602f8.section: Planting Cover Crops > "Planting Green" Into Cover Crops
01d7fc7602f8.sentence: Farmers are also experiencing good cover crop suppression using cereal rye and a roller-crimper that goes ahead of the tractor, allowing the possibility of no-till planting a main crop at the same time as suppressing the cover crop (see Figure 16.10).

79c0c9937590.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.04%3A_Cover_Crop_Management
79c0c9937590.section: Planting Cover Crops > "Planting Green" Into Cover Crops
79c0c9937590.sentence: Although not recommended for most direct-seeded vegetable crops, this has been successfully used for soybeans, corn and cotton.

d5c96d9314c4.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.03%3A_Types_of_Cover_Crops
d5c96d9314c4.sentence: Buckwheat is a summer annual that is easily killed by frost (Figure 10.5, right).

8266083d5173.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.03%3A_Types_of_Cover_Crops
8266083d5173.sentence: It also grows rapidly and completes its life cycle quickly, taking around six weeks from planting into a warm soil until the early flowering stage.

9d5e0063dbab.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.03%3A_Types_of_Cover_Crops
9d5e0063dbab.sentence: Buckwheat can grow more than 2 feet tall in the month following planting.

e5f38db0368a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.03%3A_Types_of_Cover_Crops
e5f38db0368a.sentence: It will grow better than many other cover crops in low-fertility soils but is less tolerant of compacted soils.

0ad625b8f658.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.03%3A_Types_of_Cover_Crops
0ad625b8f658.sentence: It competes well with weeds because it grows so fast and, therefore, is sometimes used to suppress weeds following an early spring vegetable crop.

e04ed297878a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.03%3A_Types_of_Cover_Crops
e04ed297878a.sentence: It has also been reported to suppress important root pathogens, including Thielaviopsis and Rhizoctonia species.

ddf47abd7aae.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.03%3A_Types_of_Cover_Crops
ddf47abd7aae.sentence: Its seeds are not “hard” and do not persist for multiple years in the soil, but it can reseed itself and become a volunteer weed.

2fbc50ed979c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.03%3A_Types_of_Cover_Crops
2fbc50ed979c.sentence: Mow, roll, or till it before seeds develop to prevent reseeding.

49d3edb97521.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.03%3A_Types_of_Cover_Crops
49d3edb97521.section: Other Crops > Cover Crops In Perennial Systems
49d3edb97521.sentence: In perennial systems like orchards and vineyards, groundcover management (floor management) can help improve soil health and crop quality.

3a17d1f6e272.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.03%3A_Types_of_Cover_Crops
3a17d1f6e272.section: Other Crops > Cover Crops In Perennial Systems
3a17d1f6e272.sentence: In this case, the cover crop should be a perennial with special characteristics.

e22711b7f2da.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.03%3A_Types_of_Cover_Crops
e22711b7f2da.section: Other Crops > Cover Crops In Perennial Systems
e22711b7f2da.sentence: It should not overly compete with the main crop, and it should be persistent with minimal maintenance and provide good erosion and weed control.

6d135c3b8cc2.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.03%3A_Types_of_Cover_Crops
6d135c3b8cc2.section: Other Crops > Cover Crops In Perennial Systems
6d135c3b8cc2.sentence: Also, it should be able to tolerate the conditions of the orchard floor, such as shade, traffic and drought.

5a880075284b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.03%3A_Types_of_Cover_Crops
5a880075284b.section: Other Crops > Cover Crops In Perennial Systems
5a880075284b.sentence: Basically, it functions more as a living mulch and therefore should not be too aggressive or spread laterally.

0b8494ecf824.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.03%3A_Types_of_Cover_Crops
0b8494ecf824.section: Other Crops > Cover Crops In Perennial Systems
0b8494ecf824.sentence: A good species for this purpose is Dutch white clover, which also provides modest amounts of nitrogen.

bd65f695a645.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.03%3A_Types_of_Cover_Crops
bd65f695a645.section: Other Crops > Cover Crops In Perennial Systems
bd65f695a645.sentence: Perennial grasses like certain fescues can be attractive as a ground cover if they have a low-growing habit with dense, fine roots and require minimal mowing.

49b76ea6012a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/10%3A_Cover_Crops/10.03%3A_Types_of_Cover_Crops
49b76ea6012a.section: Other Crops > Cover Crops In Perennial Systems
49b76ea6012a.sentence: Sometimes, cover crops are used to deliberately compete with grapevines to reduce excessive vegetative growth, but in this situation they are kept away from the immediate vicinity of the vines.

910cfb38592f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.07%3A_Farm_Labor_and_Economics
910cfb38592f.sentence: Carefully selected rotations, especially when alternating between grains and broadleaf plants, can greatly assist control of plant diseases and nematodes.

22547509d245.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.07%3A_Farm_Labor_and_Economics
22547509d245.sentence: Sometimes a one-year break is sufficient for disease control, while for other diseases a number of years of growing a nonhost crop is needed to sufficiently reduce inoculum levels.

cb04a3faec0d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.07%3A_Farm_Labor_and_Economics
cb04a3faec0d.sentence: Inclusion of pulse crops in a rotation seems to stimulate beneficial organisms and reduce the severity of cereal root diseases.

3a92d63a9ebd.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.07%3A_Farm_Labor_and_Economics
3a92d63a9ebd.sentence: Severity of common root rot of wheat and barley is reduced by taking a multiyear break to grow broadleaf plants.

7284acd2d581.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.07%3A_Farm_Labor_and_Economics
7284acd2d581.sentence: However, some diseases or nematodes have a wider host range, and more care is needed in developing or changing rotations if these are present.

27d87a97cc05.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.07%3A_Farm_Labor_and_Economics
27d87a97cc05.sentence: In addition, some diseases enter the field on contaminated seed, while others, like wheat leaf rust, can travel with the wind for long distances.

37118f935742.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.07%3A_Farm_Labor_and_Economics
37118f935742.sentence: Other tactics, aside from rotations, are needed to deal with such diseases.

febf81a43270.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.10%3A_Agroforestry
febf81a43270.sentence: Faidherbia albida is a tropical legume tree that thrives in seasonally dry climates and can be used both in silvopasture systems and in alley cropping systems.

da0604616c8d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.10%3A_Agroforestry
da0604616c8d.sentence: Its leaves are feather-like, and its canopy is therefore not overly dense and permits light penetration for crops like corn or pasture grasses.

85f605f91dd8.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.10%3A_Agroforestry
85f605f91dd8.sentence: Also, it has a deep taproot and grows foliage in the dry season when other forage sources are limited.

377bbfdb35ac.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.10%3A_Agroforestry
377bbfdb35ac.sentence: Faidherbia blooms at the end of the dry season and thereby provides food for bees.

4c2f286a75c2.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.10%3A_Agroforestry
4c2f286a75c2.sentence: Its seed pods are feed for livestock or wild game, and the woody parts make good fuel.

28f1627792c6.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.10%3A_Agroforestry
28f1627792c6.sentence: Forest farming does not separate the land into distinct growing zones like alley cropping but grows understory crops within an established forest, either a natural forest or a timber planting.

b142c83ba61b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.10%3A_Agroforestry
b142c83ba61b.sentence: In this system, the shade from the trees is actually a desired quality because the planted or wild understory crops thrive in such an environment.

481010aa504d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.10%3A_Agroforestry
481010aa504d.sentence: Typical examples are medicinal herbs like ginseng, certain types of mushrooms, fruits like elderberries, and ornamentals like rhododendrons and moss.

206c1649b926.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.10%3A_Agroforestry
206c1649b926.sentence: Many of these understory crops can be quite profitable.

223affacc8bb.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.10%3A_Agroforestry
223affacc8bb.sentence: Silvopasture systems involve the integration of trees and grazing livestock operations on the same land (Figure 11.5).

6704e3c80dac.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.10%3A_Agroforestry
6704e3c80dac.sentence: They provide both harvestable forest products and animal forage, offering both short- and long-term income sources.

242e4587ad2c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.10%3A_Agroforestry
242e4587ad2c.sentence: In temperate climates, cool-season grasses may grow better during the hotter times of the year with partial shade provided by the trees (while critical early growth is not affected until leaf-out).

4294975dfea0.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.10%3A_Agroforestry
4294975dfea0.sentence: In hotter climates, the trees help keep the grazing animals cool.

21faf94ae196.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.10%3A_Agroforestry
21faf94ae196.sentence: Silvopasture systems still require the use of agronomic principles, like appropriate selection of forages, fertilization and rotational grazing systems that maximize vegetative plant growth and harvest.

32326456eb3e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.10%3A_Agroforestry
32326456eb3e.sentence: As discussed in Chapter 14, silvopasture systems may also be beneficial on landslide-prone slopes by stabilizing the soil (see Figure 14.12).

5b6f54d0d37f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.10%3A_Agroforestry
5b6f54d0d37f.sentence: Transitional systems take advantage of the increased shading and changed microclimate as trees mature.

6433298260de.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.10%3A_Agroforestry
6433298260de.sentence: For example, landowners may initially use an alley cropping system where annual crops are grown between young trees, which is then transitioned into silvopasture, forest forming or an orchard.

c36bf978f69d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/11%3A_Diversifying_Cropping_Systems/11.10%3A_Agroforestry
c36bf978f69d.sentence: Alternatively they may decide to trim the trees and continue alley cropping.

64c05236dec7.title: Cover crop
64c05236dec7.sentence: Cover crops manage soil erosion, soil fertility, soil quality, water, weeds, pests, diseases, biodiversity and wildlife in an agroecosystem—an ecological system managed and shaped by humans.

3d2954a6b4ff.title: Agroecology
3d2954a6b4ff.sentence: The system properties of agroecosystems studied may include: productivity, stability, sustainability and equitability.

bbb0a03a29e3.title: Agroecology
bbb0a03a29e3.sentence: According to Dalgaard et al., it probably was the concept of "process ecology" such as studied by Arthur Tansley in the 1930s which inspired Harper's 1974 concept of agroecosystems, which they consider the foundation of modern agroecology.

f0eec66b6d16.title: Cover crop
f0eec66b6d16.sentence: Soil erosion is a process that can irreparably reduce the productive capacity of an agroecosystem.

8c863ca0a75e.title: Cover crop
8c863ca0a75e.sentence: Although cover crops can perform multiple functions in an agroecosystem simultaneously, they are often grown for the sole purpose of preventing soil erosion.

a43182816419.title: Agroecology
a43182816419.sentence: Agroecology is an academic discipline that studies ecological processes applied to agricultural production systems.

11ef5564b193.title: Agroecology
11ef5564b193.sentence: The term can refer to a science, a movement, or an agricultural practice.

cef2837d3a4f.title: Agroecology
cef2837d3a4f.sentence: The field of agroecology is not associated with any one particular method of farming, whether it be organic, regenerative, integrated, or industrial, intensive or extensive, although some use the name specifically for alternative agriculture.

6ae9d488b519.title: Agroecology
6ae9d488b519.sentence: Agroecology is inherently multidisciplinary, including sciences such as agronomy, ecology, environmental science, sociology, economics, history and others.

3088236e6309.title: Agroecology
3088236e6309.sentence: Agroecology uses different sciences to understand elements of ecosystems such as soil properties and plant-insect interactions, as well as using social sciences to understand the effects of farming practices on rural communities, economic constraints to developing new production methods, or cultural factors determining farming practices.

6251b09df092.title: Agroecology
6251b09df092.sentence: One perspective emphasizes ecosystem agroecology, which draws from system ecology and focuses on understanding farms as integrated ecological systems.

fea803622200.title: Agroecology
fea803622200.sentence: This approach analyzes energy flows, nutrient cycles, and the ecological interactions among biotic and abiotic components of an agroecosystem.

2417b75465ac.title: Agroecology
2417b75465ac.sentence: - A set of agricultural practices that harness ecological processes, biodiversity, nutrient recycling, agroforestry, intercropping, composting, and other nature-based methods.

4adf1ac0ef3f.title: Agroecology
4adf1ac0ef3f.sentence: There are three varieties of agroecology that are both well defined and have a certification regime.

47a5f8bdc6bd.title: Agroecology
47a5f8bdc6bd.sentence: These are firstly biodynamic farming, secondly organic agriculture, and thirdly Green Food (managed by China Green Food).

9493231d84c4.title: Agroecology
9493231d84c4.sentence: Biodynamics is the oldest of the certified agroecologies, Organics is the most widely practiced certified agroecology (in 188 countries), and Green Food is the newest certified agroecology and was developed in China.

1933d4cc5edc.title: Agroecology
1933d4cc5edc.sentence: Wezel et al. say the first mention of the term agroecology was in 1928, with the publication of the term by Basil Bensin.

9d474751ccfc.title: Agroecology
9d474751ccfc.sentence: Tischler's 1965 book Agrarökologie may be the first to be titled 'agroecology'.

b38ca6371406.title: Agroecology
b38ca6371406.sentence: Academic research areas that focus on topics related to agriculture or ecology, such as agronomy, veterinary science, environmental science, and others, are heatedly debating which model of agriculture or agroecology should be supported through policy.

150d3944ffa8.title: Agroecology
150d3944ffa8.sentence: Agricultural departments of different countries support agroecology to varying degrees, with the UN perhaps its most prominent proponent.

e029a4a3d5d3.title: Allelopathy
e029a4a3d5d3.sentence: In 1832, the Swiss botanist De Candolle suggested that crop plant exudates were responsible for an agriculture problem called soil sickness.

809a4a5d6b87.title: Tillage
809a4a5d6b87.sentence: Tillage is the agricultural preparation of soil by mechanical agitation of various types, such as digging, stirring, and overturning.

5fc6f972160d.title: Tillage
5fc6f972160d.sentence: Examples of human-powered tilling methods using hand tools include shoveling, picking, mattock work, hoeing, and raking.

f90ef541c063.title: Tillage
f90ef541c063.sentence: Examples of draft-animal-powered or mechanized work include ploughing (overturning with moldboards or chiseling with chisel shanks), rototilling, rolling with cultipackers or other rollers, harrowing, and cultivating with cultivator shanks (teeth).

65523a2b8dd4.title: Tillage
65523a2b8dd4.sentence: Tillage that is deeper and more thorough is classified as primary, and tillage that is shallower and sometimes more selective of location is secondary.

98a9f34d76fc.title: Tillage
98a9f34d76fc.sentence: Harrowing and rototilling often combine primary and secondary tillage into one operation.

9c674fbd16ed.title: Tillage
9c674fbd16ed.sentence: Within agriculture, both can refer to any kind of soil agitation.

bd7e9511c47a.title: Tillage
bd7e9511c47a.sentence: Additionally, "cultivation" or "cultivating" may refer to an even narrower sense of shallow, selective secondary tillage of row crop fields that kills weeds while sparing the crop plants.

930c942cbc00.title: Tillage
930c942cbc00.sentence: The tillage kills the weeds via two mechanisms: uprooting them, burying their leaves (cutting off their photosynthesis), or a combination of both.

623fbf73726a.title: Tillage
623fbf73726a.sentence: Weed control both prevents the crop plants from being outcompeted by the weeds (for water and sunlight) and prevents the weeds from reaching their seed stage, thus reducing future weed population aggressiveness.

42a9701fc9a2.title: Tillage
42a9701fc9a2.sentence: In 1731, English writer Jethro Tull published the book "Horse-Hoeing Husbandry: An Essay on the Principles of Vegetation and Tillage," which argued that soil needed to be pulverized into fine powder for plants to make use of it.

4953278cbdd8.title: Tillage
4953278cbdd8.sentence: Tull wrote that each subsequent tillage of the soil would increase its fertility, and that it was impossible to till the soil too much.

7b848279d903.title: Tillage
7b848279d903.sentence: However, scientific observation has shown that the opposite is true; tillage causes soil to lose structural qualities that allow plant roots, water, and nutrients to penetrate it, accelerates soil loss by erosion, and results in soil compaction.

0f10548c17d8.title: Tillage
0f10548c17d8.sentence: However, the destruction of the prairie grasses and tillage of the fertile topsoil of the American Midwest caused the Dust Bowl, in which the soil was blown away and stirred up into dust storms that blackened the sky.

54a95d9e3a1d.title: Tillage
54a95d9e3a1d.sentence: This prompted re-consideration of tillage techniques, but in the United States as of 2019, 3 trillion pounds of soil were estimated to be lost due to erosion while adoption of improved techniques for controlling erosion are still not widespread.

b8f59849fb3f.title: Tillage
b8f59849fb3f.sentence: Modern agricultural science has greatly reduced the use of tillage.

841026fc5094.title: Tillage
841026fc5094.sentence: Crops can be grown for several years without any tillage through the use of herbicides to control weeds, crop varieties that tolerate packed soil, and equipment that can plant seeds or fumigate the soil without really digging it up.

dbd5fd2cec37.title: Tillage
dbd5fd2cec37.sentence: Soon after 1900, the farm tractor was introduced, which made modern large-scale agriculture possible.

8f32fab3dd08.title: Plough
8f32fab3dd08.sentence: A plough or plow (US) (both pronounced /plaʊ/) is a farm tool for loosening or turning soil before sowing seed or planting.

e90539f24913.title: Plough
e90539f24913.sentence: The prime purpose of ploughing is to turn over the uppermost soil, bringing fresh nutrients to the surface while burying weeds and crop remains to decay.

7b67ec2660c7.title: Plough
7b67ec2660c7.sentence: Trenches cut by the plough are called furrows.

f64df0ca34b0.title: Plough
f64df0ca34b0.sentence: Ploughing and cultivating soil evens the content of the upper 12 to 25 centimetres (5 to 10 in) layer of soil, where most plant feeder roots grow.

9620201f597d.title: Plough
9620201f597d.sentence: In modern use, a ploughed field is normally left to dry and then harrowed before planting.

577fb4769f49.title: Plough
577fb4769f49.sentence: Ploughs were initially powered by humans, but the use of farm animals is considerably more efficient.

0a50aae5c6e9.title: Plough
0a50aae5c6e9.sentence: The earliest animals worked were oxen.

11a39703fd2b.title: Plough
11a39703fd2b.sentence: Later, horses and mules were used in many areas.

ccd37c18fdd3.title: Plough
ccd37c18fdd3.sentence: With the Industrial Revolution came the possibility of steam engines to pull ploughs.

fee23fb6fbab.title: Plough
fee23fb6fbab.sentence: These in turn were superseded by internal-combustion-powered tractors in the early 20th century.

260f40689273.title: Plough
260f40689273.sentence: The earliest ploughs had no wheels; such a plough was known to the Romans as an aratrum.

07a3fe4faa0b.title: Plough
07a3fe4faa0b.sentence: Celtic peoples first came to use wheeled ploughs in the Roman era.

2c40e8215170.title: Plough
2c40e8215170.sentence: The plough appears in one of the oldest surviving pieces of written literature, from the 3rd millennium BC, where it is personified and debating with another tool, the hoe, over which is better: a Sumerian disputation poem known as the Debate between the hoe and the plough.

e433c83adbf5.title: Plough
e433c83adbf5.sentence: Looking for a polished, slicker surface for a plough, he experimented with portions of saw blades, and by 1837 was making polished, cast steel ploughs.

8c87260e3f62.title: Plough
8c87260e3f62.sentence: Then in 1837 John Deere introduced a steel plough; it was so much stronger than iron designs that it could work soil in US areas previously thought unsuitable for farming.

d3a25026863b.title: Tillage
d3a25026863b.sentence: The steel plow allowed farming in the American Midwest, where tough prairie grasses and rocks caused trouble.

d71b89cf4dc1.title: Plough
d71b89cf4dc1.sentence: Use of the traditional plough has decreased in some areas threatened by soil damage and erosion.

b518546a1004.title: Plough
b518546a1004.sentence: Used instead is shallower ploughing or other less-invasive conservation tillage.

855cfded351b.title: Plough
855cfded351b.sentence: Joseph Foljambe in Rotherham, England, in 1730, used new shapes based on the Rotherham plough, which covered the mould board with iron.

959add24a109.title: Plough
959add24a109.sentence: In 1789 Robert Ransome, an iron founder in Ipswich, started casting ploughshares in a disused malting at St Margaret's Ditches.

55199c567398.title: Arable land
55199c567398.sentence: Arable land (from Latin arābilis 'able to be ploughed or farmed') is any land capable of being ploughed and used to grow crops.

04eb105a17a7.title: Arable land
04eb105a17a7.sentence: > Arable land is the land under temporary agricultural crops (multiple-cropped areas are counted only once), temporary meadows for mowing or pasture, land under market and kitchen gardens and land temporarily fallow (less than five years).

4eec534fe101.title: Arable land
4eec534fe101.sentence: The abandoned land resulting from shifting cultivation is not included in this category.

5ff300414cf7.title: Arable land
5ff300414cf7.sentence: Data for 'Arable land' are not meant to indicate the amount of land that is potentially cultivable.

2dc1b3a0e42f.title: Arable land
2dc1b3a0e42f.sentence: A more concise definition appearing in the Eurostat glossary similarly refers to actual rather than potential uses: "land worked (ploughed or tilled) regularly, generally under a system of crop rotation".

86d9bc946f19.title: Arable land
86d9bc946f19.sentence: According to the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations, in 2013, the world's arable land amounted to 1.407 billion hectares, out of a total of 4.924 billion hectares of land used for agriculture.

7dabdedf8878.title: Arable land
7dabdedf8878.sentence: Agricultural land that is not arable according to the FAO definition above includes:

a32513226b5e.title: Arable land
a32513226b5e.sentence: - Meadows and pastures – land used as pasture and grazed range, and those natural grasslands and sedge meadows that are used for hay production in some regions.

2585da9691b9.title: Arable land
2585da9691b9.sentence: - Permanent crop – land that produces crops from woody vegetation, e.g. orchard land, vineyards, coffee plantations, rubber plantations, and land producing nut trees;

87f3c1b88848.title: Arable land
87f3c1b88848.sentence: Land that is not arable, in the sense of lacking capability or suitability for cultivation for crop production, has one or more limitations – a lack of sufficient freshwater for irrigation, stoniness, steepness, adverse climate, excessive wetness with the impracticality of drainage, excessive salts, or a combination of these, among others.

365b1ab2fde2.title: Clay
365b1ab2fde2.sentence: In agriculture, clay content is a major factor in determining land arability.

a9e15e3e6fbf.title: Arable land
a9e15e3e6fbf.sentence: For example, United States NRCS statistics indicate that about 59 percent of US non-federal pasture and unforested rangeland is unsuitable for cultivation, yet such land has value for grazing of livestock.

ef1394b54ae4.title: Arable land
ef1394b54ae4.section: Changes in arability > Land degradation > Examples
ef1394b54ae4.sentence: - Each year, arable land is lost due to desertification and human-induced erosion.

777b9f81e050.title: Arable land
777b9f81e050.section: Changes in arability > Land degradation > Examples
777b9f81e050.sentence: Improper irrigation of farmland can wick the sodium, calcium, and magnesium from the soil and water to the surface.

5315e5751bdf.title: Arable land
5315e5751bdf.section: Changes in arability > Land degradation > Examples
5315e5751bdf.sentence: This process steadily concentrates salt in the root zone, decreasing productivity for crops that are not salt-tolerant.

629b3868f60e.title: Effects of climate change on agriculture
629b3868f60e.section: Changes in the extent and quality of agricultural land > Thawing of potentially arable land
629b3868f60e.sentence: Climate change may increase the amount of arable land by reducing the amount of frozen land.
629b3868f60e.key: Effects of climate change on agriculture

667fd30dbc6d.title: Tillage
667fd30dbc6d.sentence: - Loosens and aerates the top layer of soil or horizon A, which facilitates planting the crop.

a9b43ea629d4.title: Tillage
a9b43ea629d4.sentence: - Helps mix harvest residue, organic matter (humus), and nutrients evenly into the soil.

07a8b8ff7509.title: Tillage
07a8b8ff7509.sentence: - When done in autumn, helps exposed soil crumble over winter through frosting and defrosting, which helps prepare a smooth surface for spring planting.

e7a269bc74c7.title: Tillage
e7a269bc74c7.sentence: - Can reduce infestations of slugs, cut worms, army worms, and harmful insects as they are attracted by leftover residues from former crops.

8cdde4203fc2.title: Tillage
8cdde4203fc2.sentence: - Reduces the risk of crop diseases which can be harbored in surface residues.

26787e968296.title: Tillage
26787e968296.sentence: - Dries the soil before seeding (in wetter climates, tillage aids in keeping the soil drier).

72c72d8f8963.title: Tillage
72c72d8f8963.sentence: - Soil loses nutrients, like nitrogen and fertilizer, and its ability to store water.

5440d6d32409.title: Tillage
5440d6d32409.sentence: - Decreases the water infiltration rate of soil.

9765d7f4dbae.title: Tillage
9765d7f4dbae.sentence: (Results in more runoff and erosion as the soil absorbs water more slowly than before)

bbbb6e354b51.title: Tillage
bbbb6e354b51.sentence: - Tilling the soil results in dislodging the cohesiveness of the soil particles, thereby inducing erosion.

76d791cd29b7.title: Tillage
76d791cd29b7.sentence: - Reduces organic matter in the soil.

7737a5746fcd.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza
7737a5746fcd.sentence: Tillage reduces the inoculation potential of the soil and the efficacy of mycorrhizaes by disrupting the extraradical hyphal network (Miller et al. 1995, McGonigle & Miller 1999, Mozafar et al. 2000).

9f21cdb95425.title: Tillage
9f21cdb95425.sentence: - Compaction of the soil, also known as a tillage pan.

ecc3b47b2a4e.title: Tillage
ecc3b47b2a4e.sentence: - Eutrophication (nutrient runoff into a body of water).

21f5f0980b45.title: Tillage
21f5f0980b45.sentence: Primary tillage loosens the soil and mixes in fertilizer or plant material, resulting in soil with a rough texture.

eace723b8812.title: Tillage
eace723b8812.sentence: Primary tillage such as ploughing tends to produce a rough surface finish, whereas secondary tillage tends to produce a smoother surface finish, such as that required to make a good seedbed for many crops.

d647254aabe3.title: Tillage
d647254aabe3.sentence: Primary tillage is usually conducted after the last harvest, when the soil is wet enough to allow plowing but also allows good traction.

430825e7ffca.title: Tillage
430825e7ffca.sentence: The objective of primary tillage is to attain a reasonable depth of soft soil, incorporate crop residues, kill weeds, and to aerate the soil.

cbd2fbd905a5.title: Tillage
cbd2fbd905a5.sentence: Secondary tillage is any subsequent tillage, to incorporate fertilizers, reduce the soil to a finer tilth, level the surface, or control weeds.

10a86209400e.title: Tillage
10a86209400e.sentence: Secondary tillage produces finer soil and sometimes shapes the rows, preparing the seed bed.

bf045539db7e.title: Tillage
bf045539db7e.sentence: - The seedbed preparation can be done with harrows (of which there are many types and subtypes), dibbles, hoes, shovels, rotary tillers, subsoilers, ridge- or bed-forming tillers, rollers, or cultivators.

9bb75fd22970.title: Tillage
9bb75fd22970.sentence: - The weed control, to the extent that it is done via tillage, is usually achieved with cultivators or hoes, which disturb the top few centimeters of soil around the crop plants but with minimal disturbance of the crop plants themselves.

2083754f5a5e.title: Harrow (tool)
2083754f5a5e.sentence: In agriculture, a harrow is a farm implement used for surface tillage.

afc23bf334d5.title: Harrow (tool)
afc23bf334d5.sentence: It is used after ploughing for breaking up and smoothing out the surface of the soil.

09851896cacc.title: Harrow (tool)
09851896cacc.sentence: Coarser harrowing may also be used to remove weeds and to cover seed after sowing.

c499a3cdd4ec.title: Harrow (tool)
c499a3cdd4ec.sentence: Harrows differ from ploughs, which cut the upper 12 to 25 centimetre (5 to 10 in) layer of soil, and leave furrows, parallel trenches.

d6e103700fe0.title: Harrow (tool)
d6e103700fe0.sentence: Harrows differ from cultivators in that they disturb the whole surface of the soil, while a cultivator instead disturbs only narrow tracks between the crop rows to kill weeds.

05cda79d5c27.title: Harrow (tool)
05cda79d5c27.sentence: There are four general types of harrows: disc harrows, tine harrows (including spring-tooth harrows, drag harrows, and spike harrows), chain harrows, and chain-disk harrows.

1471e7ba11f1.title: Harrow (tool)
1471e7ba11f1.sentence: The disk harrow is used first to slice up the large clods left by the mould-board plough, followed by the spring-tooth harrow.

39ca521b20ca.title: Harrow (tool)
39ca521b20ca.sentence: The result is a smooth field with powdery dirt at the surface.

5eae9eaf3ca5.title: Harrow (tool)
5eae9eaf3ca5.sentence: Chain harrows are often used for lighter work, such as leveling the tilth or covering the seed, while disc harrows are typically used for heavy work, such as following ploughing to break up the sod.

c04ae296e671.title: Harrow (tool)
c04ae296e671.sentence: Where harrowing provides a very fine tilth or the soil is very light so that it might easily be wind-blown, a roller is often added as the last of the set.

dda4d8689d24.title: Harrow (tool)
dda4d8689d24.sentence: A rotary power harrow, or simply a power harrow, has vertical tines that are mounted in sets.

956db1304e25.title: Harrow (tool)
956db1304e25.sentence: Each set of tines is rotated on a vertical axis so that soil near the tines is moved in a horizontal direction.

898bf8fa20fe.title: Harrow (tool)
898bf8fa20fe.sentence: The result is that, unlike with a rotary tiller, soil layers are not turned over or inverted, which is useful in preventing dormant weed seeds from being brought to the surface, and there is no horizontal slicing of the subsurface soil that can lead to hardpan formation.

92cc08d8fc33.title: Harrow (tool)
92cc08d8fc33.sentence: The rake developed into other implements such as the harrow by the end of the Han dynasty.

5899ee0876de.title: Harrow (tool)
5899ee0876de.sentence: Two kinds of tined harrows were known during the Han dynasty, the flat harrow known as the pa, which was used throughout China in both wet and dry fields, and the vertical harrow known as the chao, which was only used in wet rice fields in the south.

ab762bfd92d1.title: Harrow (tool)
ab762bfd92d1.sentence: In China, the rake had appeared by the Han dynasty (202 BC – 220 AD).

d903b3bb5286.title: Contour plowing
d903b3bb5286.sentence: Contour plowing or contour farming is the farming practice of plowing and/or planting across a slope following its elevation contour lines.

bb850d675ec3.title: Contour plowing
bb850d675ec3.sentence: In contour plowing, the ruts made by the plow run perpendicular rather than parallel to the slopes, generally furrows that curve around the land and are level.

7c83a9392396.title: Contour plowing
7c83a9392396.sentence: These contour line furrows create a water break, reducing the formation of rills and gullies during heavy precipitation and allowing more time for the water to settle into the soil.

d4639473f708.title: Contour plowing
d4639473f708.sentence: This method is also known for preventing tillage erosion.

8d15838a9009.title: Contour plowing
8d15838a9009.sentence: Tillage erosion is the soil movement and erosion by tilling a given plot of land.

add20f48ca63.title: Contour plowing
add20f48ca63.sentence: Contour plowing has been proven to reduce fertilizer loss, power, time consumption, and wear on machines, as well as to increase crop yields and reduce soil erosion.

45ad9f80c12a.title: Contour plowing
45ad9f80c12a.sentence: Demonstrations showed that contour farming, under ideal conditions, will increase yields of row crops by up to 50%, with increases of between 5 and 10% being common.

5671ed431046.title: Contour plowing
5671ed431046.sentence: The Phoenicians first developed the practice of contour farming and spread it throughout the Mediterranean.

8e6c50ba9138.title: Contour plowing
8e6c50ba9138.sentence: However, the Romans preferred cultivation in straight furrows and this practice became standard.

5ae9a10394a4.title: Contour plowing
5ae9a10394a4.sentence: The US Department of Agriculture established the Soil Conservation Service in 1935 during the Dust Bowl when it became apparent that soil erosion was a huge problem along with desertification.

110a56c278ca.title: Contour plowing
110a56c278ca.sentence: This was one of the main procedures promoted by the US Soil Conservation Service (the current Natural Resources Conservation Service) during the 1930s.

90cce2f6cadf.title: Contour plowing
90cce2f6cadf.sentence: By 1938, the introduction of new agricultural techniques, such as contour plowing, had reduced soil loss by 65% despite the continuation of the drought.

2bcf415ac60a.title: Contour plowing
2bcf415ac60a.sentence: The practice is effective only on slopes with between 2% and 10% gradient and when rainfall does not exceed a certain amount within a certain period.

1f2b4a689ffe.title: Contour plowing
1f2b4a689ffe.sentence: On steeper slopes and areas with greater rainfall, a procedure known as strip cropping is used with contour farming to provide additional protection.

3b7d8a12e2a2.title: Contour plowing
3b7d8a12e2a2.sentence: Contour farming is most effective when used with other soil conservation methods such as terrace farming, and the use of cover crops.

b5c43f878222.title: Contour plowing
b5c43f878222.sentence: A similar practice is contour bunding where stones are placed around the contours of slopes.

4c15197182f7.title: Crop residue
4c15197182f7.sentence: - Field residues are materials left in an agricultural field or orchard after the crop has been harvested.

a3e51c42f57f.title: Crop residue
a3e51c42f57f.sentence: These residues include stalks and stubble (stems), leaves and seed pods.

02f2b067e84c.title: Illinois Soil Nitrogen Test
02f2b067e84c.sentence: Within the corn belt, stalks and other crop residues are left in the field with the intention of enhancing the amount of organic material in the soil.

7f432259b43b.title: Nutrient management
7f432259b43b.section: Nitrogen management > Reduction of greenhouse gas emissions > Water management > Conservation tillage
7f432259b43b.sentence: Historically, crop residue, was regarded by farmers as trash and was discarded; however, research has shown that there are many benefits to retaining more than 50% of crop residue on soil surfaces for the promotion of enriched soil health, nutrient cycling, reduction in erosion, and increased microbial activity and diversity.

500cf1587f68.title: Sustainable agriculture
500cf1587f68.sentence: Crop residues left covering the surface of the soil may result in reduced evaporation of water, a lower surface soil temperature, and reduction of wind effects.

6c4417226785.title: Nutrient management
6c4417226785.section: Nitrogen management > Reduction of greenhouse gas emissions > Water management > Conservation tillage
6c4417226785.sentence: Decaying crop residue increases the available routes in the soil that allow water to be absorbed quickly and is beneficial with or without irrigation, leading to the reduced use of supplemental irrigation (Conservation Tillage Systems in the Southeast, 2023).

7ef5cc935dea.title: Tillage
7ef5cc935dea.sentence: Intensive tillage leaves less than 15% crop residue cover or less than 500 pounds per acre (560 kg/ha) of small grain residue.

58c40457b06d.title: Tillage
58c40457b06d.sentence: Reduced tillage leaves between 15 and 30% crop residue cover on the soil or 500 to 1000 pounds per acre (560 to 1100 kg/ha) of small grain residue during the critical erosion period.

a67ecd6fbf31.title: Tillage
a67ecd6fbf31.sentence: Conservation tillage leaves at least 30% of crop residue on the soil surface, or at least 1,000 lb/ac (1,100 kg/ha) of small grain residue on the surface during the critical soil erosion period.

db2fc65c6d0a.title: Crop residue
db2fc65c6d0a.sentence: Their release (called mineralization) occurs over a period of years.

2bd1e283dd4b.title: Crop residue
2bd1e283dd4b.sentence: As a rough guide, cereal straw releases about 10 to 15 per cent of its nutrients and pea residues release about 35 percent of their nutrients by the next year.

772fc40737e9.title: Crop residue
772fc40737e9.sentence: N is released fairly quickly from residue when the content is higher than 1.5 per cent (such as in pea residues).

fb8fc80e3748.title: Crop residue
fb8fc80e3748.sentence: In contrast, below 1.2 per cent (such as cereal residue), soil-available N is fixed (called immobilization) by the microbes as they decompose the residue.

1dc6b3330cd3.title: No-till farming
1dc6b3330cd3.sentence: Conservation tillage is a group of practices that reduce the amount of tillage needed.

5405df8fb5b1.title: Tillage
5405df8fb5b1.sentence: This slows water movement, which reduces the amount of soil erosion.

53d9dd2de5f8.title: Tillage
53d9dd2de5f8.sentence: Conservation tillage also benefits farmers by reducing fuel consumption and soil compaction.

2d271d4c3ef8.title: Tillage
2d271d4c3ef8.sentence: By reducing the number of times the farmer travels over the field, significant savings in fuel and labor are made.

cb51dbe8f69b.title: Tillage
cb51dbe8f69b.sentence: Additionally, conservation tillage has been found to benefit predatory arthropods that can enhance pest control.

29cf32d57456.title: Tillage
29cf32d57456.sentence: - No-till – plows, disks, et cetera are not used.

1c5a66207dc9.title: Tillage
1c5a66207dc9.sentence: - Strip-till – Narrow strips are tilled where seeds will be planted, leaving the soil in between the rows untilled.

674eb66d77f9.title: Tillage
674eb66d77f9.sentence: - Mulch-till - Soil is covered with mulch to conserve heat and moisture.

91cd36700668.title: Tillage
91cd36700668.sentence: - Rotational tillage – Tilling the soil every two years or less often (every other year, or every third year, etc.).

5c013ba8be4a.title: Tillage
5c013ba8be4a.sentence: Conservation tillage is used on over 370 million acres, mostly in South America, Oceania and North America.

fa1f424430b3.title: Tillage
fa1f424430b3.sentence: In most years since 1997, conservation tillage was used in US cropland more than intensive or reduced tillage.

a172991460e9.title: Carbon farming
a172991460e9.sentence: By 2014 more than 75% of Canadian Prairies' cropland had adopted "conservation tillage" and more than 50% had adopted no-till.

4c3118d1a7bd.title: Nutrient management
4c3118d1a7bd.section: Nitrogen management > Reduction of greenhouse gas emissions > Water management > Conservation tillage
4c3118d1a7bd.sentence: Researchers found a nearly 60 percent reduction in run-off losses in crops that underwent conservation tillage (Conservation Tillage Systems in the Southeast, 2023).

b684fe4f6352.title: Nutrient management
b684fe4f6352.section: Nitrogen management > Reduction of greenhouse gas emissions > Water management > Conservation tillage
b684fe4f6352.sentence: Conservation tillage improves water conservation and reduces run-off by protecting soil from crusting, a seal that forms on the soil surface that has undergone intensive tillage practices.

40ae5a4c3188.title: Tillage
40ae5a4c3188.sentence: However, conservation tillage delays warming of the soil due to the reduction of dark earth exposure to the warmth of the spring sun, thus delaying the planting of the next year's spring crop of corn.

fc7b19926e15.title: Tillage erosion
fc7b19926e15.sentence: However, conservation tillage equipment designed to reduce water erosion may not be able to reduce tillage erosion and field operations traditionally not considered tillage operations may cause significant amount of tillage erosion (e.g., harvesting for potato).

39b14fe6421f.title: No-till farming
39b14fe6421f.sentence: No-till farming (also known as zero tillage or direct drilling) is an agricultural technique for growing crops or pasture without disturbing the soil through tillage.

8825b24f5dd5.title: No-till farming
8825b24f5dd5.sentence: No-till farming decreases the amount of soil erosion tillage causes in certain soils, especially in sandy and dry soils on sloping terrain.

a03f5b96a50c.title: No-till farming
a03f5b96a50c.section: Benefits and issues > Environmental > Soil and desertification
a03f5b96a50c.sentence: The first inch of no-till soil contains more aggregates and is two to seven times less vulnerable than that of ploughed soil.

fad9dd0956fe.title: No-till farming
fad9dd0956fe.sentence: No-till farming improves water retention: crop residues help water from natural precipitation and irrigation to infiltrate the soil.

d3422052011c.title: No-till farming
d3422052011c.sentence: Evaporation from tilling increases the amount of water by around 1/3 to 3/4 inches (0.85 to 1.9 cm) per pass.

4e74c22c5d92.title: No-till farming
4e74c22c5d92.sentence: There are three basic methods of no-till farming.

837d7ab98e9b.title: No-till farming
837d7ab98e9b.sentence: "Sod seeding" is when crops are sown with seeding machinery into a sod produced by applying herbicides on a cover crop (killing that vegetation).

dc61d905e16f.title: No-till farming
dc61d905e16f.sentence: "Direct seeding" is when crops are sown through the residue of previous crop.

58b0127b1af6.title: No-till farming
58b0127b1af6.sentence: "Surface seeding" or "direct seeding" is when seeds are left on the surface of the soil; on flatlands, this requires no machinery and minimal labor.

ac527a1ad6ba.title: No-till farming
ac527a1ad6ba.sentence: No-till is the practice of never tilling a field.

cc03d4198ce1.title: No-till farming
cc03d4198ce1.sentence: No-till and strip tillage are both forms of conservation tillage.

bcc0d96ddb64.title: No-till farming
bcc0d96ddb64.sentence: No-till farming is not equivalent to conservation tillage or strip tillage.

f447fb612900.title: No-till farming
f447fb612900.sentence: A formalized opposition to plowing started in the 1940s with Edward H. Faulkner, author of Plowman's Folly.

24aa7615b84f.title: No-till farming
24aa7615b84f.sentence: It was not until the development after WWII of powerful herbicides such as paraquat that various researchers and farmers started to try out the idea.

23c4f681aa15.title: No-till farming
23c4f681aa15.sentence: In 1999, about 45 million ha (170,000 mi2) was under no-till farming worldwide, which increased to 72 million ha (280,000 mi2) in 2003 and to 111 million ha (430,000 mi2) in 2009.

a9aed0f9a84e.title: No-till farming
a9aed0f9a84e.section: Adoption across the world > South America
a9aed0f9a84e.sentence: South America had the highest adoption of no-till farming in the world, which in 2014 constituted 47% of the total global area under no-till farming.

667150e7ebd8.title: No-till farming
667150e7ebd8.section: Benefits and issues > Profit, economics, yield
667150e7ebd8.sentence: A problem with no-till farming is that the soil warms and dries more slowly in spring, which may delay planting.

5cc8d3d9f157.title: No-till farming
5cc8d3d9f157.section: Benefits and issues > Profit, economics, yield
5cc8d3d9f157.sentence: The slower warming is due to crop residue being a lighter color than the soil exposed in conventional tillage, which absorbs less solar energy.

bc17eb67410f.title: No-till farming
bc17eb67410f.section: Benefits and issues > Costs and management > Fertilizer
bc17eb67410f.sentence: One of the most common yield reducers is nitrogen being immobilized in the crop residue, which can take a few months to several years to decompose, depending on the crop's C to N ratio and the local environment.

b091e564aa28.title: No-till farming
b091e564aa28.section: Benefits and issues > Costs and management > Fertilizer
b091e564aa28.sentence: Fertilizer needs to be applied at a higher rate.

043d8e557ad2.title: No-till farming
043d8e557ad2.section: Benefits and issues > Costs and management > Fertilizer
043d8e557ad2.sentence: After a transition period (4–5 years for Kansas, USA) the soil may build up in organic matter.

7b6660cd663d.title: No-till farming
7b6660cd663d.sentence: The first adopters of no-till include Klingman (North Carolina), Edward Faulkner, L. A. Porter (New Zealand), Harry and Lawrence Young (Herndon, Kentucky), and the Instituto de Pesquisas Agropecuarias Meridional (1971 in Brazil) with Herbert Bartz.

f3c6cf4aee3a.title: Tillage
f3c6cf4aee3a.sentence: Site preparation is any of the various treatments applied to a site to ready it for seeding or planting.

ea2590f2cde7.title: Tillage
ea2590f2cde7.sentence: Site preparation is the work that is done before a forest area is regenerated.

1b3cd8290bce.title: Tillage
1b3cd8290bce.sentence: The purpose is to facilitate the regeneration of that site by the chosen method.

4a4f9b0bd0c8.title: Tillage
4a4f9b0bd0c8.sentence: Site preparation may be designed to achieve, singly or in any combination, improved access by reducing or rearranging slash and ameliorating adverse forest floor, soil, vegetation, or other biotic factors.

f00425b7e53e.title: Tillage
f00425b7e53e.section: Site preparation of forest land > Mechanical
f00425b7e53e.sentence: According to J. Hall (1970), in Ontario at least, the most widely used site preparation technique was post-harvest mechanical scarification by equipment front-mounted on a bulldozer (blade, rake, V-plow, or teeth), or dragged behind a tractor (Imsett or S.F.I. scarifier, or rolling chopper).

068c7b322b8b.title: Tillage
068c7b322b8b.section: Site preparation of forest land > Orientation of linear site preparation
068c7b322b8b.sentence: A disk-trenching experiment in the Sub-boreal Spruce Zone in interior British Columbia investigated the effect on growth of young outplants (lodgepole pine) in 13 microsite planting positions: berm, hinge, and trench in each of north, south, east, and west aspects, as well as in untreated locations between the furrows.

25883a46b2e4.title: Tillage
25883a46b2e4.section: Site preparation of forest land > Orientation of linear site preparation
25883a46b2e4.sentence: Tenth-year stem volumes of trees on south-, east-, and west-facing microsites were significantly greater than those of trees on north-facing and untreated microsites.

79cf25fd9577.title: Tillage
79cf25fd9577.section: Site preparation of forest land > Orientation of linear site preparation
79cf25fd9577.sentence: However, planting spot selection was seen to be more important overall than trench orientation.

89157068ba3c.title: Tillage
89157068ba3c.sentence: Intensive tillage often involves multiple operations with implements such as a mold board, disk, or chisel plow.

ca1c0c887ade.title: Tillage
ca1c0c887ade.sentence: After this, a finisher with a harrow, rolling basket, and cutter can be used to prepare the seed bed.

05825c8842f2.title: Tillage
05825c8842f2.sentence: This type of tillage is often referred to as conventional tillage, but as conservational tillage is now more widely used than intensive tillage (in the United States), it is often not appropriate to refer to this type of tillage as conventional.

963d60997d43.title: Conventional tillage
963d60997d43.sentence: Conventional tillage refers to tillage operations considered standard for a specific location and crop and that tend to bury the crop residues; usually considered as a base for determining the cost effectiveness of erosion control practices.

5964cc0a2cdc.title: Tillage
5964cc0a2cdc.sentence: - Greater speeds, when using certain tillage implements (disks and chisel plows), lead to more intensive tillage (i.e., less residue is on the soil surface).

8cd444946718.title: Tillage
8cd444946718.sentence: - Increasing the angle of disks causes residues to be buried more deeply.

ce1c491e6bbb.title: Tillage
ce1c491e6bbb.section: Site preparation of forest land > Mounding
ce1c491e6bbb.sentence: Site preparation treatments that create raised planting spots have commonly improved outplant performance on sites subject to low soil temperature and excess soil moisture.

223df17386e6.title: Tillage
223df17386e6.section: Site preparation of forest land > Mounding
223df17386e6.sentence: The mounds warmed up quickest, and at soil depths of 0.5 cm and 10 cm averaged 10 and 7 °C higher, respectively, than in the control.

3f861f8bb860.title: Tillage
3f861f8bb860.section: Site preparation of forest land > Mounding
3f861f8bb860.sentence: Mounds reached mean soil temperatures of 10 °C at 10 cm depth 5 days after planting, but the control did not reach that temperature until 58 days after planting.

865134c3a671.title: Tillage
865134c3a671.section: Site preparation of forest land > Mounding
865134c3a671.sentence: During the first growing season, mounds had 3 times as many days with a mean soil temperature greater than 10 °C than did the control microsites.

f8f9d472567a.title: Tillage
f8f9d472567a.section: Site preparation of forest land > Mounding
f8f9d472567a.sentence: Assuming that incident light in the 100–600 μE/m2/s intensity range is the most important for photosynthesis, the mounds received over 4 times the total daily light energy that reached the control microsites.

0afa06839248.title: Tillage
0afa06839248.sentence: This may involve the use of a chisel plow, field cultivators, or other implements.

46d7be85875c.title: Tillage
46d7be85875c.sentence: - Percentage residue is used to compare tillage systems because the amount of crop residue affects the soil loss due to erosion.

b24a4f73db39.title: Tillage
b24a4f73db39.section: Site preparation of forest land > Burning
b24a4f73db39.sentence: Broadcast burning is commonly used to prepare clearcut sites for planting, e.g., in central British Columbia, and in the temperate region of North America generally.

4bbb5190c971.title: Tillage
4bbb5190c971.section: Site preparation of forest land > Burning
4bbb5190c971.sentence: Prescribed burning is carried out primarily for slash hazard reduction and to improve site conditions for regeneration; all or some of the following benefits may accrue:

3f376394e7f8.title: Tillage
3f376394e7f8.section: Site preparation of forest land > Burning
3f376394e7f8.sentence: Changes in soil chemical properties associated with burning include significantly increased pH, which Macadam (1987) in the Sub-boreal Spruce Zone of central British Columbia found persisting more than a year after the burn.

c63dab644f75.title: Tillage
c63dab644f75.section: Site preparation of forest land > Burning
c63dab644f75.sentence: The change in pH depends on the severity of the burn and the amount consumed; the increase can be as much as 2 units, a 100-fold change.

01e762ed91d8.title: Tillage
01e762ed91d8.section: Site preparation of forest land > Burning
01e762ed91d8.sentence: Deficiencies of copper and iron in the foliage of white spruce on burned clearcuts in central British Columbia might be attributable to elevated pH levels.

78da134ca45b.title: Tillage
78da134ca45b.section: Site preparation of forest land > Burning
78da134ca45b.sentence: Phosphorus availability also increased, both in the forest floor and in the 0 cm to 15 cm mineral soil layer, and the increase was still evident, albeit somewhat diminished, 21 months after burning.

7b9e7de9c1b0.title: Tillage
7b9e7de9c1b0.section: Site preparation of forest land > Burning
7b9e7de9c1b0.sentence: However, in another study in the same Sub-boreal Spruce Zone found that although it increased immediately after the burn, phosphorus availability had dropped to below pre-burn levels within 9 months.

3b2054a65b2c.title: Tillage
3b2054a65b2c.section: Site preparation of forest land > Burning
3b2054a65b2c.sentence: Nitrogen will be lost from the site by burning, though concentrations in remaining forest floor were found by Macadam (1987) to have increased in two out of six plots, the others showing decreases.

540c88f91f2c.title: Tillage
540c88f91f2c.section: Site preparation of forest land > Burning
540c88f91f2c.sentence: Tarrant (1954), for instance, found only 4% of a 140-ha slash burn had burned severely, 47% had burned lightly, and 49% was unburned.

9b636b4e370e.title: Tillage
9b636b4e370e.sentence: Tilling can damage ancient structures such as long barrows.

953abb960bfe.title: Tillage
953abb960bfe.sentence: In the UK, half of the long barrows in Gloucestershire and almost all the burial mounds in Essex have been damaged.

d1129fff57a1.title: Tillage
d1129fff57a1.sentence: According to English Heritage in 2003, ploughing with modern powerful tractors had done as much damage in the last six decades as traditional farming did in the previous six centuries.

1b026e8e1825.title: No-till farming
1b026e8e1825.section: Benefits and issues > Environmental > Greenhouse gases
1b026e8e1825.sentence: No-till farming has been claimed to increase soil organic matter, and thus increase carbon sequestration.

f0bd48405c51.title: No-till farming
f0bd48405c51.section: Benefits and issues > Environmental > Greenhouse gases
f0bd48405c51.sentence: There is debate over whether the increased sequestration sometimes detected is actually occurring or is due to flawed testing methods or other factors.

583d7b86986d.title: No-till farming
583d7b86986d.section: Benefits and issues > Environmental > Greenhouse gases
583d7b86986d.sentence: While many studies report soil organic carbon increases in no-till systems, others conclude that these effects may not be observed in all systems, depending on factors, such as climate and topsoil carbon content.

1cb20ef55ff7.title: No-till farming
1cb20ef55ff7.section: Benefits and issues > Environmental > Greenhouse gases
1cb20ef55ff7.sentence: A 2014 study claimed that certain no-till systems may sequester less carbon than conventional tillage systems, saying that the "no-till subsurface layer is often losing more soil organic carbon stock over time than is gained in the surface layer." The study also highlighted the need for a uniform definition of soil organic carbon sequestration among researchers.

295289859510.title: No-till farming
295289859510.section: Benefits and issues > Environmental > Greenhouse gases
295289859510.sentence: A 2020 study demonstrated that the combination of no-till and cover cropping could be an effective approach to climate change mitigation by sequestering more carbon than either practice alone, suggesting that the two practices have a synergistic effect in carbon capture.

bbd998ab4153.title: No-till farming
bbd998ab4153.section: Benefits and issues > Environmental > Greenhouse gases
bbd998ab4153.sentence: No-till farming reduces nitrous oxide (N2O) emissions by 40-70%, depending on rotation.

043de3f9f208.title: No-till farming
043de3f9f208.section: Benefits and issues > Environmental > Greenhouse gases
043de3f9f208.sentence: Nitrous oxide is a potent greenhouse gas, 300 times stronger than CO2, and stays in the atmosphere for 120 years.

ccc19862cef3.title: No-till farming
ccc19862cef3.sentence: The potential for global cooling as a result of increased albedo in no-till croplands is similar in magnitude to other biogeochemical carbon sequestration processes.

9c9ff8da0841.title: Plough
9c9ff8da0841.sentence: A major advance for this type of farming was the turn plough, also known as the mould-board plough (UK), moldboard plow (U.S.), or frame-plough.

1ee8f7fc7e7c.title: Plough
1ee8f7fc7e7c.sentence: This releases a rectangular strip of sod to be lifted by the share and carried by the mould board up and over, so that the strip of sod (slice of the topsoil) that is being cut lifts and rolls over as the plough moves forward, dropping back upside down into the furrow and onto the turned soil from the previous run down the field.

12de6080fcf1.title: Plough
12de6080fcf1.sentence: When dragged through a field, the coulter cuts down into the soil and the share cuts horizontally from the previous furrow to the vertical cut.

f0a8b22c8a70.title: Plough
f0a8b22c8a70.sentence: It turns the furrow slice slowly almost without breaking it, and is normally used for shallow ploughing (maximum 200 mm (7.9 in) depth).

f559119241c8.title: Plough
f559119241c8.sentence: It is normally used for very deep ploughing (300 mm (12 in) deep or more).

fb92fbfc3f4b.title: Plough
fb92fbfc3f4b.sentence: Being intermediate between the two mould boards described above, it has a performance that comes in between (approximately 250 mm (9.8 in) deep), with less shattering than the digger mouldboard.

ca8981d65883.title: Plough
ca8981d65883.sentence: The heavy iron moldboard plough was invented in China's Han Empire in the 1st and 2nd century, and from there it spread to the Netherlands, which led the Agricultural Revolution.

533ff1597e94.title: Plough
533ff1597e94.sentence: The mould-board plough greatly reduced the time needed to prepare a field and so allowed a farmer to work a larger area of land.

07eecfc3b31b.title: Plough
07eecfc3b31b.sentence: In addition, the resulting pattern of low (under the mould board) and high (beside it) ridges in the soil forms water channels, allowing the soil to drain.

e2ce9cf19989.title: Plough
e2ce9cf19989.sentence: Mould-board ploughing in cold and temperate climates, down to 20 cm (7.9 in), aerates the soil by loosening it.

605fb03ca92f.title: Plough
605fb03ca92f.sentence: It incorporates crop residues, solid manures, limestone, and commercial fertilisers alongside oxygen, reducing nitrogen losses by denitrification, accelerating mineralisation, and raising short-term nitrogen availability for turning organic matter into humus.

6d9926c2dc13.title: Plough
6d9926c2dc13.sentence: It facilitates seeding with a lighter seed, controls many crop enemies (slugs, crane flies, seedcorn maggots-bean seed flies, borers), and raises the number of "soil-eating" earthworms (endogic), but deters vertical-dwelling earthworms (anecic).

16b446afbdd4.title: Plough
16b446afbdd4.sentence: Ploughing leaves little crop residue on the surface that might otherwise reduce both wind and water erosion.

c1e6db8be0da.title: Plough
c1e6db8be0da.sentence: Over-ploughing can lead to the formation of hardpan.

2e95be0823df.title: Plough
2e95be0823df.sentence: Because of this runner, the mould board plough is harder to turn around than the scratch plough, and its introduction brought about a change in the shape of fields – from mostly square fields into longer rectangular "strips" (hence the introduction of the furlong).

db6a94115914.title: No-till farming
db6a94115914.section: Benefits and issues > Costs and management > Increased herbicide use
db6a94115914.sentence: One of the purposes of tilling is to remove weeds.

14ab0e61b3a8.title: Strip-till
14ab0e61b3a8.section: Challenges of both Strip-till and No-till systems
14ab0e61b3a8.sentence: In place of cultivation, a farmer can suppress weeds by managing a cover crop, mowing, crimping, or herbicide application.

4f0366b02dda.title: No-till farming
4f0366b02dda.section: Benefits and issues > Costs and management > Increased herbicide use
4f0366b02dda.sentence: Herbicides such as glyphosate are commonly used in place of tillage for seedbed preparation, which leads to more herbicide use in comparison to conventional tillage.

fee8a406a2a7.title: No-till farming
fee8a406a2a7.section: Benefits and issues > Costs and management > Increased herbicide use
fee8a406a2a7.sentence: With no-till farming, residue from the previous year's crops lie on the surface of the field, which can cause different, greater, or more frequent disease or weed problems compared to tillage farming.

9c1e383d37e3.title: No-till farming
9c1e383d37e3.section: Benefits and issues > Costs and management > Increased herbicide use
9c1e383d37e3.sentence: The use of cover crops to help control weeds also increases organic residue in the soil (and nutrients, when using legumes).

86bf0956b483.title: No-till farming
86bf0956b483.section: Benefits and issues > Costs and management > Increased herbicide use
86bf0956b483.sentence: Cover crops then need to be killed so that the newly planted crops can get enough light, water, nutrients, etc.

6dc0f8f1376e.title: No-till farming
6dc0f8f1376e.section: Benefits and issues > Costs and management > Increased herbicide use
6dc0f8f1376e.sentence: Cover crops typically must be crimped when they enter the flowering stage.

cbb9f66a351a.title: No-till farming
cbb9f66a351a.section: Benefits and issues > Costs and management > Increased herbicide use
cbb9f66a351a.sentence: The residue is then planted through, and left as a mulch.

ba86ac08337b.title: No-till farming
ba86ac08337b.section: Benefits and issues > Costs and management > Increased herbicide use
ba86ac08337b.sentence: The use of herbicides is not strictly necessary, as demonstrated in natural farming, permaculture, and other practices related to sustainable agriculture.

84948204be26.title: No-till farming
84948204be26.section: Benefits and issues > Costs and management > Increased herbicide use
84948204be26.sentence: Alternatives include winter cover crops, soil solarization, or burning.

f8fb10f48d75.title: Three-field system
f8fb10f48d75.sentence: The three-field system is a regime of crop rotation in which a field is planted with one set of crops one year, a different set in the second year, and left fallow in the third year.

c1d5da897ded.title: Three-field system
c1d5da897ded.sentence: Under this system, the arable land of an estate or village was divided into three large fields: one was planted in the autumn with winter wheat or rye; the second field was planted with crops such as peas, lentils, or beans; and the third was left fallow (unplanted).

01d2ce4c1c68.title: Three-field system
01d2ce4c1c68.sentence: Cereal crops deplete the ground of nitrogen, but legumes can fix nitrogen and so fertilize the soil.

e285a7e85003.title: Three-field system
e285a7e85003.sentence: The fallow fields would overgrow with weeds which were used for grazing farm animals.

5bff490379b3.title: Three-field system
5bff490379b3.sentence: Their excrement fertilized that field's soil to regain its nutrients.

e17709a46be6.title: Three-field system
e17709a46be6.sentence: Crop assignments were rotated every year, so each field segment would be planted for two out of every three years.

20e271d17d7f.title: Three-field system
20e271d17d7f.sentence: Previously a two-field system had been in place, with half the land being left fallow.

e326508b5c0f.title: Three-field system
e326508b5c0f.sentence: The technique was first used in China in the Eastern Zhou period and arose independently in Europe in the medieval period.

6b1e0f396a68.title: Three-field system
6b1e0f396a68.sentence: In Europe, the change to a three-field system happened from the 9th century to the 11th century.

82b232e70697.title: Three-field system
82b232e70697.sentence: The three-field system needed more plowing of land, and its introduction coincided with the adoption of the moldboard plow.

cf544fbf5b85.title: Three-field system
cf544fbf5b85.sentence: The legume crop needed summer rain to succeed, and so the three-field system was less successful around the Mediterranean.

0c8d4f4db755.title: Arable land
0c8d4f4db755.sentence: Land incapable of being cultivated for the production of crops can sometimes be converted to arable land.

418768b4ffd9.title: Arable land
418768b4ffd9.sentence: Making non-arable land arable often involves digging new irrigation canals and new wells, aqueducts, desalination plants, planting trees for shade in the desert, hydroponics, fertilizer, nitrogen fertilizer, pesticides, reverse osmosis water processors, PET film insulation or other insulation against heat and cold, digging ditches and hills for protection against the wind, and installing greenhouses with internal light and heat for protection against the cold outside and to provide light in cloudy areas.

bc8f452e1266.title: Arable land
bc8f452e1266.sentence: Such modifications are often prohibitively expensive.

46af4fea9bd9.title: Arable land
46af4fea9bd9.sentence: - Aran Islands: These islands off the west coast of Ireland (not to be confused with the Isle of Arran in Scotland's Firth of Clyde) were unsuitable for arable farming because they were too rocky.

bf7a015587ff.title: Arable land
bf7a015587ff.sentence: The people covered the islands with a shallow layer of seaweed and sand from the ocean.

748e838e9eeb.title: Arable land
748e838e9eeb.sentence: Today, crops are grown there, even though the islands are still considered non-arable.

3dd41a779b06.title: Arable land
3dd41a779b06.sentence: - Slash and burn agriculture uses nutrients from the wood ash, but these are exhausted within a few years.

8d366e72ae1a.title: Arable land
8d366e72ae1a.sentence: - Terra preta, fertile tropical soils produced by adding charcoal.

aed6c52e6640.title: Keyline design
aed6c52e6640.sentence: Keyline design is a system of principles and techniques of developing rural and urban landscapes to optimize use of their water resources.

fbbf8b6dd1fe.title: Keyline design
fbbf8b6dd1fe.sentence: Australian farmer and engineer P. A. Yeomans invented and developed Keyline design in his books The Keyline Plan, The Challenge of Landscape, Water For Every Farm, and The City Forest.

5b6e2d585d4a.title: Keyline design
5b6e2d585d4a.sentence: In a smooth, grassy valley, a location designated the keypoint is identified at which the lower and more level portion of the primary valley floor suddenly steepens higher.

2c72a182ad24.title: Keyline design
2c72a182ad24.sentence: The keyline of this primary valley is determined by pegging a contour line that conforms to the natural shape of the valley through the keypoint, such that all points on the keyline are at the same elevation as the keypoint.

0c6165b5b6d6.title: Keyline design
0c6165b5b6d6.sentence: Contour plowing both above and below the keyline and parallel to it is necessarily "off-contour", but the developing pattern tends to drift rainwater runoff away from the center of the valley and, incidentally, prevent erosion of its soil.

133a63c44bc3.title: Keyline design
133a63c44bc3.sentence: Random contour plowing also becomes off-contour but usually with the opposite effect on runoff, namely causing it to quickly run off ridges and concentrate in valleys.

f22d1a53702f.title: Keyline design
f22d1a53702f.sentence: This pattern of cultivation allows more time for water to infiltrate.

bbf84754d960.title: Keyline design
bbf84754d960.sentence: In many nations, including Australia, it is important to optimize the infiltration of rainfall, and Keyline cultivation accomplishes this while delaying the concentration of runoff that could damage the land.

19af76383171.title: Keyline design
19af76383171.sentence: The foundation of Yeomans' Keyline design system is the Keyline Scale of Permanence (KSOP), which was the outcome of 15 years of adaptive experimentation on his properties Yobarnie and Nevallan.

ed8ad84aa3c8.title: Keyline design
ed8ad84aa3c8.sentence: In response, he developed the Seepage Line System, a flexible, iterative approach that replaces fixed keylines with custom-shaped contour ditches, tailored to site-specific topography.

13e67f596496.title: Keyline design
13e67f596496.sentence: These individually designed lines enhance water infiltration, reduce erosion, and allow for overflow management during extreme weather.

7acbf75d2b40.title: Keyline design
7acbf75d2b40.sentence: Research and field trials in Lower Saxony and Hesse confirm its effectiveness in reducing surface runoff and supporting water-retentive agroforestry systems.

976cde4d8bbb.title: Keyline design
976cde4d8bbb.sentence: P. A. Yeomans published the first book on Keyline design in 1954.

93fd56d81b27.title: Stubble burning
93fd56d81b27.sentence: Stubble burning is the practice of intentionally setting fire to the straw stubble that remains after grains, such as rice and wheat, have been harvested.

49448608fad7.title: Stubble burning
49448608fad7.sentence: The technique is used to quickly and cheaply clear fields.

16a832d04092.title: Stubble burning
16a832d04092.sentence: - Helps to combat pests and weeds

8785344e15f0.title: Stubble burning
8785344e15f0.sentence: - Additionally, prolonged stubble burning kills beneficial microflora and fauna in soil which reduces organic matter and destroys the carbon-nitrogen equilibrium.

628d315a34e5.title: Stubble burning
628d315a34e5.sentence: Stubble burning has been associated with increasing air pollution over the past few decades due to the particulate matter contamination it distributes into the atmosphere.

c25aa95dc113.title: Stubble burning
c25aa95dc113.section: Effects > Health concerns related to stubble burning
c25aa95dc113.sentence: A wide array of health disorders are associated with the stubble burning emission releases which have caused people to develop lung cancer and respiratory infections.

85789a198386.title: Stubble burning
85789a198386.section: Effects > Health concerns related to stubble burning
85789a198386.sentence: Not only that but the smog from the stubble burning also severely affects people with Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disorder as it worsens their health conditions.

e5adba0cc998.title: Stubble burning
e5adba0cc998.sentence: In countries such as India and Pakistan, stubble burning is illegal.

d2b6d7d63a3a.title: Stubble burning
d2b6d7d63a3a.sentence: Enforcement is weak, allowing the practice to continue.

61026971e705.title: Stubble burning
61026971e705.sentence: - Stubble burning has been effectively prohibited since 1993 in the United Kingdom.

b2f3a7cb67ee.title: Stubble burning
b2f3a7cb67ee.sentence: Spraying an enzyme, which decomposes the stubble into useful fertiliser, improves the soil, avoids air pollution and prevents carbon dioxide emissions.

0517e3570ad1.title: Stubble burning
0517e3570ad1.sentence: Agriculture residues can have other uses, such as in particle board and biofuel, though these uses can still cause problems like erosion and nutrient loss.

a735f6e239ba.title: Plough
a735f6e239ba.sentence: However, domestication of oxen in Mesopotamia and the Indus Valley Civilisation, perhaps as early as the 6th millennium BC, provided mankind with the draft power needed to develop the larger, animal-drawn true ard (or scratch plough).

45bd9c6604fb.title: Plough
45bd9c6604fb.sentence: The earliest was the bow ard, which consists of a draft-pole (or beam) pierced by a thinner vertical pointed stick called the head (or body), with one end being the stilt (handle) and the other a share (cutting blade) dragged through the topsoil to cut a shallow furrow suitable for most cereal crops.

af497485cbc5.title: Plough
af497485cbc5.sentence: A ploughed field, from c. 2800 BCE, was also discovered at Kalibangan, India.

3ac766c0b863.title: Plough
