3ac766c0b863.sentence: Because the ard left a strip of undisturbed earth between furrows, the fields were often cross-ploughed lengthwise and breadth-wise, which tended to form squarish Celtic fields.

8db854d4b107.title: Plough
8db854d4b107.sentence: The heavy soils of Northern Europe were difficult to work with a scratch plough.:43 In fact, the ard is best suited to loamy or sandy soils that are naturally fertilised by annual flooding, as in the Nile Delta and Fertile Crescent, and to a lesser extent any other cereal-growing region with light or thin soil.

ddc436e963f6.title: Plough
ddc436e963f6.sentence: The chisel plough is a common tool for deep tillage (prepared land) with limited soil disruption.

be7de8141236.title: Plough
be7de8141236.sentence: Its main function is to loosen and aerate the soils, while leaving crop residue on top.

8fe81fdc7405.title: Plough
8fe81fdc7405.sentence: Unlike many other ploughs, the chisel will not invert or turn the soil.

aa46499babaf.title: Plough
aa46499babaf.sentence: This feature has made it a useful addition to no-till and low-till farming practices that attempt to maximise the erosion-preventing benefits of keeping organic matter and farming residues present on the soil surface throughout the year.

6e8faad7f2c7.title: Plough
6e8faad7f2c7.sentence: Thus the chisel plough is considered by some to be more sustainable than other types of plough, such as the mould-board plough.

88756e90b741.title: Plough
88756e90b741.sentence: This plough can be used to reduce the effects of soil compaction and to help break up ploughpan and hardpan.

47db4c4203c4.title: Plough
47db4c4203c4.sentence: Basically the chisel plough is a heavy-duty field cultivator intended to operate at depths from 15 cm (5.9 in) to as much as 46 cm (18 in).

2253f1a5bf5a.title: Plough
2253f1a5bf5a.sentence: When ploughing with a chisel plough, 10–20 horsepower (7.5–14.9 kW) per shank is required, depending on depth.

ca6988c89c87.title: Plough
ca6988c89c87.sentence: Cultivator teeth work near the surface, usually for weed control, whereas chisel plough shanks work deep under the surface; therefore, cultivation takes much less power per shank than does chisel ploughing.

eabff650c32f.title: Plough
eabff650c32f.sentence: These ploughs were fairly fragile and unsuitable for the heavier soils of northern Europe.

ae50d129d6f5.title: Plough
ae50d129d6f5.sentence: The introduction of wheels to replace the runner allowed the weight of the plough to increase, and in turn enabled the use of a larger mould-board faced in metal.

7884f8bcfebc.title: Plough
7884f8bcfebc.sentence: By the Han period the entire ploughshare was made of cast iron.

50fb88c1f461.title: Plough
50fb88c1f461.sentence: These are the earliest known heavy, mould-board iron ploughs.

9c073198ffa2.title: Plough
9c073198ffa2.sentence: General adoption of the carruca heavy plough in Europe seems to have accompanied adoption of the three-field system in the later-8th and early-9th centuries, leading to improved agricultural productivity per unit of land in northern Europe.

62835f870bc7.title: Plough
62835f870bc7.section: Effects of mould-board ploughing > Social effects
62835f870bc7.sentence: Use of the mouldboard plough in Europe typically required cooperation between multiple households, since four to eight oxen (later horses) were needed to pull the heavy instrument through the soil, and this was more than a typical peasant household could muster on its own.

77893d35f0de.title: Plough
77893d35f0de.section: Effects of mould-board ploughing > Social effects
77893d35f0de.sentence: Thus, the introduction of the mouldboard plough made farming more of a communal effort and contributed to the rise of the manorial system in Northern Europe.

8c6aa97c3d20.title: Plough
8c6aa97c3d20.sentence: These heavy ploughs led to greater food production, coinciding with a marked increase in the world's population in the second millennium AD.

35290ef5e824.title: Plough
35290ef5e824.sentence: When agriculture was first developed, soil was turned using simple hand-held digging sticks and hoes.

d53d6dd4ed98.title: Plough
d53d6dd4ed98.sentence: These were used in highly fertile areas, such as the banks of the Nile, where the annual flood rejuvenates the soil, to create drills (furrows) in which to plant seeds.

ff9aca5b2aa9.title: Plough
ff9aca5b2aa9.sentence: Digging sticks, hoes and mattocks were not invented in any one place, and hoe cultivation must have been common everywhere agriculture was practised.

8c72043bf5bb.title: Plough
8c72043bf5bb.sentence: Hoe-farming is the traditional tillage method in tropical or sub-tropical regions, which are marked by stony soils, steep slope gradients, predominant root crops, and coarse grains grown at wide intervals.

fea666852f14.title: Plough
fea666852f14.sentence: The mole plough allows under-drainage to be installed without trenches, or breaks up the deep impermeable soil layers that impede it.

a6b898c8b67d.title: Plough
a6b898c8b67d.sentence: When dragged over ground, it leaves a channel deep under it that acts as a drain.

bb83d5471b33.title: Plough
bb83d5471b33.sentence: The bullet-shaped share forms a tunnel in the soil about 75 mm (3.0 in) diameter and the expander presses the soil outwards to form a long-lasting drainage channel.

6468322b88dc.title: Plough
6468322b88dc.sentence: The small tunnels (mole drains) that mole ploughs form lie at a depth of up to 950 mm (37 in) at an angle to the pipe drains.

28bf4c6c5328.title: Plough
28bf4c6c5328.sentence: Water from the mole drains seeps into the pipes and runs along them into a ditch.

9e4d689a5adf.title: Plough
9e4d689a5adf.sentence: Compacting a tennis ball-sized sample from moling depth by hand, then pushing a pencil through is a simple check to find if the subsoil is in the right condition for mole ploughing.

7b8152539b2f.title: Plough
7b8152539b2f.sentence: If the hole stays intact without splitting the ball, the soil is in ideal condition for the mole plough.

a31c2c829f21.title: Plough
a31c2c829f21.sentence: Heavy land requires draining to reduce its water content to a level efficient for plant growth.

f9011e468deb.title: Cultivator
f9011e468deb.sentence: A cultivator is a piece of agricultural equipment used for secondary tillage.

5a67f89eae6e.title: Cultivator
5a67f89eae6e.sentence: One sense of the name means a frame with teeth (also called shanks) that pierce the soil as they are dragged through it linearly.

67aeb2b5b668.title: Cultivator
67aeb2b5b668.sentence: Another sense of the name means machines that use the rotary motion of disks or teeth to accomplish a similar result, such as a rotary tiller (sometimes called rotavator).

f28c709288a2.title: Cultivator
f28c709288a2.sentence: Cultivators stir and pulverize the soil, either before planting (to aerate the soil and prepare a smooth, loose seedbed) or after the crop has begun growing (to kill weeds—controlled disturbance of the topsoil close to the crop plants kills the surrounding weeds by uprooting them, burying their leaves to disrupt their photosynthesis or a combination of both).

eeef9bff03f6.title: Cultivator
eeef9bff03f6.sentence: Unlike a harrow, which disturbs the entire surface of the soil, cultivators are designed to disturb the soil in careful patterns, sparing the crop plants but disrupting the weeds.

f525daf5d660.title: Cultivator
f525daf5d660.sentence: Cultivators of the toothed type are often similar in form to chisel plows, but their goals are different.

c1bf09b0328d.title: Cultivator
c1bf09b0328d.sentence: Cultivators' teeth work near the surface, usually for weed control, whereas chisel plow shanks work deep beneath the surface, breaking up the hardened layer on top.

fda3f459db59.title: Cultivator
fda3f459db59.sentence: The main function of the field cultivator is to prepare a proper seedbed for the crop to be planted into, to bury crop residue in the soil (helping to warm the soil before planting), to control weeds, and to mix and incorporate the soil to ensure the growing crop has enough water and nutrients to grow well during the growing season.

b7bb0308c9b8.title: Vertical tillage
b7bb0308c9b8.sentence: Vertical tillage (VT) is a system of principles and guidelines similar to conservation agriculture (CA) in that it aims to improve soil health, increase water infiltration and decrease soil erosion and compaction (improve bulk density).

f7f290e420de.title: Vertical tillage
f7f290e420de.sentence: With varying degrees of soil movement, it aims to not invert the soil and keep residue on the surface where it protects the soil.

2bb3e5087cd7.title: Vertical tillage
2bb3e5087cd7.sentence: It usually includes small forward-facing discs that limit soil inversion and slices the residue for faster decomposition and to get a seeder or planter into the heavy residue-laden fields.

40b16ed542e9.title: Vertical tillage
40b16ed542e9.sentence: Many times it also includes a deep ripping tool for breaking up hard pans and compaction created from traditional tillage implements and heavy equipment like large tractors and combine harvesters.

1abe3c3cd703.title: Vertical tillage
1abe3c3cd703.sentence: Its proponents compare it and even include it into no-till and conservation agriculture categories.

ad91351b9ad1.title: Vertical tillage
ad91351b9ad1.sentence: Its detractors may concede the above advantages but claim the vigorous soil movement excludes it from no-till and CA categories.

23d7b59aef9b.title: Vertical tillage
23d7b59aef9b.sentence: This is important particularly in the United States, where it may exclude farmers in collection of direct farm payments from the US government that aims to promote no-till to conserve soil and keep it in place.

18b141891446.title: Vertical tillage
18b141891446.sentence: Besides this controversy, there is considerable variation in the definition of what constitutes VT, even among its proponents.

5063d0f270af.title: Optimum water content for tillage
5063d0f270af.sentence: The optimum water content for tillage (OPT) is defined as the moisture content of soil at which tillage produces the largest number of small aggregates.

4643a8f77c82.title: Optimum water content for tillage
4643a8f77c82.sentence: The OPT can be determined in relation to the volumetric water content at the lower Plastic Limit of the soil (PL).

ff749ea2ed8f.title: Optimum water content for tillage
ff749ea2ed8f.sentence: For several soils the OPT has been found to equal 0.9 PL, although there are a number of limitations with the use of the lower plastic limit in determining the optimal moisture content.

7a78fe126eea.title: Optimum water content for tillage
7a78fe126eea.sentence: Firstly it is a property of a moulded soil and not an undisturbed soil in the field and secondly, many sandy soils are not plastic and do not have a lower plastic limit.

069d8a072b64.title: Optimum water content for tillage
069d8a072b64.section: Relationships between water content at field capacity (FC) and Plastic Limit(PL)
069d8a072b64.sentence: Many clay soils drain very slowly, and as a result they are usually wetter than PL unless they are dried by water extraction by plant uptake.

c56233644dab.title: Optimum water content for tillage
c56233644dab.sentence: Soil friability is the tendency of a mass of soil to crumble under the action of an applied force.

5e37df9004a7.title: Optimum water content for tillage
5e37df9004a7.sentence: This has been found to be maximum at the PL of a soil.

b6ba76c07ec1.title: Disc harrow
b6ba76c07ec1.sentence: A disk harrow is a harrow whose cutting edges are a row of concave metal discs, which may be scalloped or set at an oblique angle.

8265397e0955.title: Disc harrow
8265397e0955.sentence: It is an agricultural implement that is used to till the soil where crops are to be planted.

5014b5c90874.title: Disc harrow
5014b5c90874.sentence: It is used to chop up unwanted weeds or crop residue.

064b9a9a149b.title: Disc harrow
064b9a9a149b.sentence: The discs are also offset so that they are not parallel with the overall direction of the implement.

77996cf8dc78.title: Disc harrow
77996cf8dc78.sentence: This arrangement ensures that the discs will repeatedly slice any ground to which they are applied.

097baee878dd.title: Disc harrow
097baee878dd.sentence: The concavity of the discs as well as their offset angle causes them to loosen and lift the soil that they cut.

ccd8491c5c3f.title: Disc harrow
ccd8491c5c3f.sentence: Primary heavy duty disc harrows of 265 to 1,000 pounds (120 to 454 kg) per disc are mainly used to break up virgin land, to chop material/residue, and to incorporate it into the top soil.

4248e30f28b7.title: Disc harrow
4248e30f28b7.sentence: Disc harrows incorporate remaining residue into the top soil, promoting the rapid decay of the dead plant material.

10fc8782dfb6.title: Disc harrow
10fc8782dfb6.sentence: Lighter secondary disc harrows are primarily used to break down soil clods into smaller pieces.

11d7dba83ee8.title: Disc harrow
11d7dba83ee8.sentence: By doing so, water penetrates more easily into the soil, soil aeration is increased, and the activity of soil biota is enhanced; the final result is a seed bed that is suitable for planting.

f98f3ad5ed74.title: Disc harrow
f98f3ad5ed74.sentence: A disc harrow is the preferred method of incorporating both agricultural lime (either dolomitic or calcitic lime) and agricultural gypsum, and disc harrowing achieves a 50/50 mix with the soil when set correctly, thereby reducing acid saturation in the top soil and so promoting strong, healthy root development.

5c14a280dd20.title: Disc harrow
5c14a280dd20.sentence: Lime does not move in the soil, and this poses a critical challenge to sustainable zero-till farming, especially considering that chemical fertilizers are generally used by farmers around the world.

70182a6b4721.title: Seedbed
70182a6b4721.sentence: A seedbed or seedling bed is the local soil environment in which seeds are planted.

7764a84806c6.title: Seedbed
7764a84806c6.sentence: The soil of a seedbed needs to be loose and smoothed, without large lumps.

6cdb3830494e.title: Seedbed
6cdb3830494e.sentence: These traits are needed so that seeds can be planted easily, and at a specific depth for best germination.

9ad03c749749.title: Seedbed
9ad03c749749.sentence: Seedbed preparation in farm fields often involves secondary tillage via harrows and cultivators.

80e21c6f7d9b.title: Seedbed
80e21c6f7d9b.sentence: This may follow primary tillage (if any) by moldboard plows or chisel plows.

756f0154e841.title: Seedbed
756f0154e841.sentence: No-till farming methods avoid tillage for seedbed preparation as well as later weed control.

44bcec705403.title: Seedbed
44bcec705403.sentence: Compacted soil will be broken up by digging.

a8f63fcbe1a3.title: Seedbed
a8f63fcbe1a3.sentence: This allows air and water to enter, and helps the seedling penetrate the soil.

5965508a2dce.title: Seedbed
5965508a2dce.sentence: Smaller seeds require a finer soil structure.

db698385dc89.title: Seedbed
db698385dc89.sentence: The soil structure may be improved by the introduction of organic matter such as compost or peat.

3b7bc25e6cd0.title: Deep plowing
3b7bc25e6cd0.sentence: Deep plowing is a plowing to a depth greater than 50 cm (20 in) as compared to ordinary plowing which rarely exceeds 20 cm (8 in).

9d1ccddc4573.title: Deep plowing
9d1ccddc4573.sentence: The purpose of deep plowing is to modify the soil water retention characteristics over the long term.

2ade5e7b4a1f.title: Deep plowing
2ade5e7b4a1f.sentence: In one long-term test, lasting 35 years, the mean annual grain yield was 2,800 lbs per acre (3,138 kg per ha) with deep plowing, which was 10% greater than the 2,550 lbs per acre (2,858 kg per ha) yield in unplowed plots.

28dddc328053.title: Deep plowing
28dddc328053.sentence: In soils like Podsol deep plowing can break up hardpan and aid in releasing soil nutrients.

e50d9caf6475.title: Deep plowing
e50d9caf6475.sentence: Under certain conditions, it is recommended to use deep plowing in preparing the soil for planting new vineyards.

b919921faece.title: Deep plowing
b919921faece.sentence: There is a movement away from plowing altogether and from deep plowing in particular.

68195affb1d0.title: Deep plowing
68195affb1d0.sentence: The theory is that this will stop the loss of topsoil, increase the organic content of soil and reduce runoff of fertilizer and pesticides into rivers.

47703770b00c.title: Deep plowing
47703770b00c.sentence: Another part of the no-plowing theory is that ground moisture would be conserved; but this was shown to be incorrect by a 35-year study.

894749a5ee91.title: Minimum tillage
894749a5ee91.sentence: Minimum tillage is a soil conservation system like strip-till with the goal of minimum soil manipulation necessary for a successful crop production.

c24662a7ad83.title: Minimum tillage
c24662a7ad83.sentence: It is a tillage method that does not turn the soil over, in contrast to intensive tillage, which changes the soil structure using ploughs.

50598be24173.title: Minimum tillage
50598be24173.sentence: In minimum tillage, primary tillage is completely avoided and only secondary tillage is practiced to a small extent.

6d6bd33d9ae3.title: Minimum tillage
6d6bd33d9ae3.sentence: Minimum tillage includes practices like minimum furrowing, use of organic fertilizer, use of biological methods to control pests, and minimum use of chemicals.

14d108e13f9b.title: No-till farming
14d108e13f9b.sentence: In some cases minimum tillage or "low-till" methods combine till and no-till methods.

e43010454183.title: No-till farming
e43010454183.sentence: For example, some approaches may use shallow cultivation (i.e. using a disc harrow) but no plowing or may use strip tillage.

1e65398d4e4d.title: Strip-till
1e65398d4e4d.sentence: Strip-till is a conservation system that uses a minimum tillage.

097a847b1bcb.title: Strip-till
097a847b1bcb.sentence: It combines the soil drying and warming benefits of conventional tillage with the soil-protecting advantages of no-till by disturbing only the portion of the soil that is to contain the seed row.

5c19640256e9.title: Tillage
5c19640256e9.sentence: Zone or strip tillage is a form of modified deep tillage in which only narrow strips are tilled, leaving soil in between the rows untilled.

9ffd9517571f.title: Strip-till
9ffd9517571f.sentence: Each row that has been strip-tilled is usually about eight to ten inches wide.

4af681338dc3.title: Tillage
4af681338dc3.sentence: In comparison to no-till, which relies on the previous year's plant residue to protect the soil and aids in postponement of the warming of the soil and crop growth in Northern climates, zone tillage produces a strip approximately five inches wide that simultaneously breaks up plow pans, assists in warming the soil and helps to prepare a seedbed.

39b2a2ca2470.title: Tillage
39b2a2ca2470.sentence: This type of tillage agitates the soil to help reduce soil compaction problems and to improve internal soil drainage.

9914da5a9854.title: Strip-till
9914da5a9854.sentence: However, strip-till also has a similar effect on soil properties as conventional tillage systems because the farmer still breaks the soil's crust which allows aerobic conditions to speed the decay of organic matter.

98a71323ef9d.title: Strip-till
98a71323ef9d.sentence: A two-year study found that strip-till did not affect the amount of soil organic carbon or its extractable phosphorus.

a390fd7d2de9.title: Strip-till
a390fd7d2de9.sentence: At the same time the field is strip-tilled, the fertilizer or chemical may be applied.

ab6156a40430.title: Strip-till
ab6156a40430.sentence: Furthermore, when liquid fertilizer is being applied, it can be directly applied in these rows where the seed is being planted, reducing the amount of fertilizer needed while improving proximity of the fertilizer to the roots.

f29d0df1edc5.title: Strip-till
f29d0df1edc5.sentence: Strip tillage can reduce the amount of trips through a field down to two or possibly one trip when using a strip till implement combined with other machinery such as a planter, fertilizer spreader, and chemical sprayer.

d9445ef965e1.title: Strip-till
d9445ef965e1.sentence: This can save the farmer a considerable amount of time and fuel, while reducing soil compaction due to few passes in a field.

ff2faf972dda.title: Strip-till
ff2faf972dda.sentence: Strip-till conserves more soil moisture compared to intensive tillage systems.

0232d304b442.title: Strip-till
0232d304b442.sentence: However, compared to no-till, strip-till may in some cases reduce soil moisture.

1e5686dc6afe.title: Strip-till
1e5686dc6afe.sentence: The system will still allow for some soil water contact that could cause erosion, however, the amount of erosion on a strip-tilled field would be light compared to the amount of erosion on an intensively tilled field.

ea1ea8902725.title: Strip-till
ea1ea8902725.sentence: In a low phosphorus site, yield was 43.5 bushels/acre (2,925.5 kg/hectare) in strip-till compared to 41.5 bu/a (2,791 kg/ha) in a no-till system.

d81af8fb8428.title: Strip-till
d81af8fb8428.sentence: Yield is comparable to that of intensive tillage systems — without the cost.

d4deb31ebb2c.title: Stubble-mulching
d4deb31ebb2c.sentence: Stubble-mulching refers to leaving the stubble or crop residue essentially in place on the land as a surface cover during a fallow period.

170eab7504e5.title: Stubble-mulching
170eab7504e5.sentence: Stubble-mulching can prevent soil erosion from wind or water and conserve soil moisture.

fa9cf3b13af2.title: Controlled traffic farming
fa9cf3b13af2.sentence: Controlled traffic farming (CTF) is a management tool which is used to reduce the damage to soils caused by heavy or repeated agricultural machinery passes on the land.

165304275511.title: Controlled traffic farming
165304275511.sentence: Controlled traffic farming is a system which confines all machinery loads to the least possible area of permanent traffic lanes.

4904bb5ff54e.title: Controlled traffic farming
4904bb5ff54e.sentence: Current farming systems allow machines to run at random over the land, compacting around 75% of the area within one season and the whole area by the second season.

ac344e885901.title: Controlled traffic farming
ac344e885901.sentence: A proper CTF system on the other hand can reduce tracking to just 15% and this is always in the same place.

4cb13d6885b5.title: Controlled traffic farming
4cb13d6885b5.sentence: Controlled traffic farming can be achieved on any scale but to get tracked areas to the minimum possible, there are three requirements:

255b96e71aa4.title: Controlled traffic farming
255b96e71aa4.sentence: - To match implement widths so that adjacent passes are in the same place for all machines working in the field.

719e9a97931b.title: Controlled traffic farming
719e9a97931b.sentence: - To match the track widths (the distance between wheel centres on the same axle) of all field machinery.

3b6830d71d2e.title: Controlled traffic farming
3b6830d71d2e.sentence: - To keep machines in exactly the same place year in year out.

a2b3d4f93477.title: Controlled traffic farming
a2b3d4f93477.sentence: Keeping machines in exactly the same place is most easily achieved with a satellite guidance system based on an RTK correction signal and auto-steer.

e3ec42256fed.title: Controlled traffic farming
e3ec42256fed.sentence: Only the RTK system can guarantee to keep vehicles in the same place year in year out and it also achieves the highest pass to pass accuracy of around ± 2 cm.

4bd5d1938d27.title: Controlled traffic farming
4bd5d1938d27.sentence: - improves soil porosity meaning there is more space for water and air;

9af4c8511422.title: Controlled traffic farming
9af4c8511422.sentence: - improves water infiltration which reduces the potential for soil erosion and increases water availability to the crop;

2f438ea57ee6.title: Controlled traffic farming
2f438ea57ee6.sentence: - improves drainage which avoids waterlogging and the potential for nitrous oxide and methane emissions and methane oxidation.

1ed0ff35ef66.title: Controlled traffic farming
1ed0ff35ef66.sentence: - improves crop rooting and the efficiency of nutrient uptake, leading to less waste and potential for environmental pollution.

e203900bbe04.title: Controlled traffic farming
e203900bbe04.sentence: CTF is a tool; it does not include a prescription for tillage although most growers adopting CTF use little or none because soil structure does not need to be repaired.

b046db6b1b78.title: Controlled traffic farming
b046db6b1b78.sentence: Soils don't recover quickly, taking as much as a few years (e.g., >5 years, particularly in soils without swelling-shrinking properties).

e7652783b2f2.title: Controlled traffic farming
e7652783b2f2.sentence: The initial investment in technology and infrastructure for a CTF can be high.

cb623e1fd4bc.title: Controlled traffic farming
cb623e1fd4bc.sentence: The implementation of CTF requires special equipment such as GPS control, precision farming technology and machines adapted to work on transport routes.

10d1cd67b258.title: Mulch-till
10d1cd67b258.sentence: In agriculture, mulch tillage (or mulch-till) is a seeding method where a hundred percent of the soil surface is disturbed by tillage, crop residues are mixed with the soil and a certain amount of residues remain on the soil surface.

d0b967e83e38.title: Mulch-till
d0b967e83e38.sentence: A great variety of cultivator implements are used to perform mulch-till.

281affa711c2.title: Mulch-till
281affa711c2.sentence: The method falls under the umbrella term of conservation tillage in the United States.

a5889203ded6.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/16%3A_Minimizing_Tillage/16.02%3A_Tillage_Systems
a5889203ded6.sentence: In cases where one pass is followed by another, the remaining residue cover can be estimated by multiplication.

15dab9cdfc68.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/16%3A_Minimizing_Tillage/16.02%3A_Tillage_Systems
15dab9cdfc68.sentence: Each pass of a tillage tool incorporates some residue and thereby reduces the amount of residue on the surface that helps reduce runoff and erosion.

00c3a73ba452.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/16%3A_Minimizing_Tillage/16.02%3A_Tillage_Systems
00c3a73ba452.sentence: For example, starting with 80% residue cover after a grain corn crop harvest and over-wintering, the sequence of 1) a chisel with straight points, 2) a tandem disk, 3) a field cultivator and 4) a row crop planter is expected to leave 0.8 (80%) x 0.7 (70%) x 0.45 (45%) x.75 (75%) = 0.19, or an estimated 19% of residue remaining on the surface, thereby not qualifying as conservation tillage.

daa4ee6d0646.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/16%3A_Minimizing_Tillage/16.02%3A_Tillage_Systems
daa4ee6d0646.sentence: By eliminating the tandem disk and keeping the soil slightly rougher, the residue level will be 42%.

5957cb8dc0ab.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/16%3A_Minimizing_Tillage/16.02%3A_Tillage_Systems
5957cb8dc0ab.sentence: Note: Speed, depth and soil moisture can affect the amounts.

15de649360b5.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/16%3A_Minimizing_Tillage/16.02%3A_Tillage_Systems
15de649360b5.sentence: Although residue cover greatly influences erosion potential, it also is affected by factors such as surface roughness and soil loosening.

9afa7749b62b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/16%3A_Minimizing_Tillage/16.01%3A_Introduction
9afa7749b62b.sentence: Tillage was first done by farmers who grew small-grain crops, such as wheat, rye and barley, primarily in western Asia (the Fertile Crescent), Europe and northern Africa.

ad6d0f0612bd.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/16%3A_Minimizing_Tillage/16.01%3A_Introduction
ad6d0f0612bd.sentence: The primary reason was to create a fine, clean seedbed, thereby greatly improving germination over broadcasting seed on untilled ground.

bdd3dd5e2083.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/16%3A_Minimizing_Tillage/16.01%3A_Introduction
bdd3dd5e2083.sentence: It also gave the crop a head start against a new flush of weeds and stimulated mineralization of organic nutrients to forms that plants could use.

5b38e96da0b4.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/16%3A_Minimizing_Tillage/16.01%3A_Introduction
5b38e96da0b4.sentence: Although this cropping system lasted for many centuries, it resulted in excessive erosion, organic matter loss and nutrient depletion, especially in the Mediterranean region, where it caused extensive soil degradation.

cce511ff796a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/16%3A_Minimizing_Tillage/16.01%3A_Introduction
cce511ff796a.section: Jethro Tull And Tillage: A Mixed Legacy And An Important Lesson
cce511ff796a.sentence: Jethro Tull (1674–1741) was an early English agricultural experimentalist whose book The New Horse Hoeing Husbandry: An Essay on the Principles of Tillage and Vegetation was published in 1731.

60d339661e2e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/16%3A_Minimizing_Tillage/16.01%3A_Introduction
60d339661e2e.section: Jethro Tull And Tillage: A Mixed Legacy And An Important Lesson
60d339661e2e.sentence: He designed a drill with a rotating grooved cylinder (now referred to as a coulter) that directed seeds to a furrow and subsequently covered them to provide good seed-soil contact.

eeb9e39523c9.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/16%3A_Minimizing_Tillage/16.01%3A_Introduction
eeb9e39523c9.section: Jethro Tull And Tillage: A Mixed Legacy And An Important Lesson
eeb9e39523c9.sentence: Tull believed that intensive tillage was needed not only for good seed-soil contact but also for plant nutrition, which he believed was provided by small soil particles.

e308c18e8d6f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/16%3A_Minimizing_Tillage/16.01%3A_Introduction
e308c18e8d6f.section: Jethro Tull And Tillage: A Mixed Legacy And An Important Lesson
e308c18e8d6f.sentence: He grew wheat for 13 consecutive years without adding manure; he basically accomplished this by mining the soil of nutrients that were released from repeated soil pulverization.

150230b99a77.sentence: So, interestingly, in the context of current interests in reduced tillage, Pre-Columbian American farmers did not use full-field tillage for crop production.

3b6db6b8ab1a.sentence: They instead used mostly direct seeding with planting sticks (Figure 16.1), or manual hoes that created small mounds (“hills”).

5883bf032614.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/16%3A_Minimizing_Tillage/16.01%3A_Introduction
5883bf032614.section: Jethro Tull And Tillage: A Mixed Legacy And An Important Lesson
5883bf032614.sentence: In contrast with the cereal-based systems (wheat, rye, barley, rice) of growing only one crop in a monoculture, these fields often included the intercropping of two or three plant species growing at the same time, like the corn, beans and squash (“Three Sisters”) system in North America.

ca2866e04f78.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/16%3A_Minimizing_Tillage/16.03%3A_Which_Tillage_System_is_Right_for_Your_Farm
ca2866e04f78.sentence: It can be done after frost has entered the soil but before it has penetrated more than about 2 inches (5 centimeters).

ecee6e5f8012.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/16%3A_Minimizing_Tillage/16.03%3A_Which_Tillage_System_is_Right_for_Your_Farm
ecee6e5f8012.sentence: Water moves upward to the freezing front and the soil underneath dries.

2d18313d8cf1.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/16%3A_Minimizing_Tillage/16.03%3A_Which_Tillage_System_is_Right_for_Your_Farm
2d18313d8cf1.sentence: This frozen state makes the soil tillable as long as the frost layer is not too thick.

0735a3b3fa89.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/16%3A_Minimizing_Tillage/16.03%3A_Which_Tillage_System_is_Right_for_Your_Farm

5972498ffe1e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/16%3A_Minimizing_Tillage/16.03%3A_Which_Tillage_System_is_Right_for_Your_Farm
5972498ffe1e.sentence: The resulting rough surface is favorable for water infiltration and runoff prevention.

5b19a78b5245.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/16%3A_Minimizing_Tillage/16.03%3A_Which_Tillage_System_is_Right_for_Your_Farm
5b19a78b5245.sentence: Some livestock farmers like frost tillage as a way to incorporate or inject manure in the winter without concerns about compaction from heavy equipment (see also Figure 12.2).

3a2d1586c150.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/16%3A_Minimizing_Tillage/16.03%3A_Which_Tillage_System_is_Right_for_Your_Farm
3a2d1586c150.sentence: Recent research in Nebraska and Australia indicates that occasional tillage, also called strategic tillage, does not have negative impacts on soil health.

8020b485548e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/16%3A_Minimizing_Tillage/16.03%3A_Which_Tillage_System_is_Right_for_Your_Farm
8020b485548e.sentence: But it should only be done for a well-identified purpose like weed or insect control, incorporation of immobile amendments, or compaction relief (say, after a harvest during a wet period).

ac97a15e2965.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/16%3A_Minimizing_Tillage/16.03%3A_Which_Tillage_System_is_Right_for_Your_Farm
ac97a15e2965.sentence: So if strategic tillage is used, it should be done on a very limited basis (once every 5–10 years) and is best accomplished with tools that still leave surface residue.

f367e4029444.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/16%3A_Minimizing_Tillage/16.03%3A_Which_Tillage_System_is_Right_for_Your_Farm
f367e4029444.sentence: A flexible tillage program may offer benefits, but be aware that any tillage can readily destroy the favorable soil structure built up by years of no-till management.

c02ed830af01.title: Plough
c02ed830af01.sentence: Typically, farmers break that up with a subsoiler, which acts as a long, sharp knife slicing through the hardened layer of soil deep below the surface.

39a1f21fdcb4.title: Subsoiler
39a1f21fdcb4.sentence: A subsoiler or flat lifter is a piece of agricultural equipment used for deep tillage, loosening and breaking up soil at depths below the levels worked by moldboard ploughs, disc harrows, or rototillers.

5b9a30a83ef7.title: Subsoiler
5b9a30a83ef7.sentence: The subsoiler consists of three or more heavy vertical shanks (standards) mounted on a toolbar or frame with shear bolts.

408f713a5e20.title: Subsoiler
408f713a5e20.sentence: Most such tools will break up and turn over surface soil to a depth of 15–20 cm (6–8 in), whereas a subsoiler will break up and loosen soil to twice those depths.

9f9b397a1036.title: Subsoiler
9f9b397a1036.sentence: They can be operated at depths of 45–75 cm (18–30 in) or more.

4059c0f978f4.title: Subsoiler
4059c0f978f4.sentence: In agriculture angled wings are used to lift and shatter the hardpan that builds up due to compaction.

8a4c19becc39.title: Subsoiler
8a4c19becc39.sentence: The subsoiler is a tillage tool which will improve growth in all crops where soil compaction is a problem.

d753b2ca6858.title: Subsoiler
d753b2ca6858.sentence: When a field is optimally subsoiled, crops will perform well during hot and dry seasons because roots penetrate soil layers deeper to reach moisture and nutrients.

7b19e652d9c3.title: Subsoiler
7b19e652d9c3.sentence: In wet conditions, the water passes more easily through the shattered areas, reducing the possibility of crops drowning.

9f4690d8f9ae.title: Subsoiler
9f4690d8f9ae.sentence: Subsoiling is a slow operation and requires high power input: 60 to 100 horsepower (45 to 75 kW) to pull a single subsoil point through a hard soil.

b89e2d1a2e64.title: Subsoiler
b89e2d1a2e64.sentence: Shanks should be able to reach 2.5–5 cm (1–2 in) below the deepest compacted layer.

a0bae231936e.title: Subsoiler
a0bae231936e.sentence: A subsoiler should not be confused with a mole plough: an agricultural implement used to create underground drainage channels, a technique known as mole drainage.

520a1597ae03.title: Plough
520a1597ae03.sentence: The para-plough, or paraplow, loosens compacted soil layers 3 to 4 dm (12 to 16 inches) deep while maintaining high surface residue levels.

5485f9e95f40.title: Plough
5485f9e95f40.sentence: It is primary tillage implement for deep ploughing without inversion.

0f6526aa3ecb.title: Nutrient management
0f6526aa3ecb.section: Nitrogen management > Reduction of greenhouse gas emissions > Water management > Conservation tillage
0f6526aa3ecb.sentence: - Conservation tillage includes several cultivation practices such as no-till, in-row subsoiling, strip-till, or ridge-till processes, which aim to increase the soil surface with 30% or more of crop residue.

dab1d0cb046c.title: Tillage
dab1d0cb046c.sentence: In areas that are not well-drained, deep tillage may be used as an alternative to installing more expensive tile drainage.

59f0d775bc5a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/16%3A_Minimizing_Tillage/16.01%3A_Introduction
59f0d775bc5a.section: Technologies That Have Lessened The Need For Tillage
59f0d775bc5a.sentence: Ridge-till and bedding | Allows easy incorporation of fertilizers and amendments Provides some weed control as ridges are built Allows seed zone on ridge/bed to dry and warm more quickly Reduces soil saturation after excessive rainfall Fixed travel lanes reduce overall compaction | Is hard to use with sod-type or narrow-row crop in rotation Requires fixed travel lanes and wheel spacing to be adjusted to travel between ridges | Cost and energy use vary depending on intensity level of ridging and bedding Environmental impacts generally between plowing and no-till

1da94f27ffe2.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/16%3A_Minimizing_Tillage/16.03%3A_Which_Tillage_System_is_Right_for_Your_Farm
1da94f27ffe2.sentence: Crops grown on fields that do not drain in a timely manner tend to benefit greatly from ridging or bedding because the sensitive seedling root zone remains aerobic during wet periods.

633d311caf40.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/16%3A_Minimizing_Tillage/16.03%3A_Which_Tillage_System_is_Right_for_Your_Farm
633d311caf40.sentence: These systems also use controlled traffic lanes, which greatly reduce compaction problems, although matching wheel spacing and tire widths for planting and harvesting equipment is sometimes a challenging task, as we discussed in Chapter 15.

4f8501377090.title: Soil conservation
4f8501377090.sentence: Soil conservation is the prevention of loss of the topmost layer of the soil from erosion or prevention of reduced fertility caused by over usage, acidification, salinization or other chemical soil contamination.

7fa0d484e094.title: Soil conservation
7fa0d484e094.sentence: Techniques for improved soil conservation include crop rotation, cover crops, conservation tillage and planted windbreaks, affect both erosion and fertility.

6e49af8eba01.title: Soil conservation
6e49af8eba01.sentence: A consequence of deforestation is typically large-scale erosion, loss of soil nutrients and sometimes total desertification.

99453b649975.title: Soil conservation
99453b649975.sentence: Farmers have practiced soil conservation for millennia.

cb420d88cd08.title: Soil conservation
cb420d88cd08.sentence: Contour plowing was practiced by the ancient Phoenicians for slopes between two and ten percent.

e5cdfbcdf577.title: Soil conservation
e5cdfbcdf577.sentence: In Europe, policies such as the Common Agricultural Policy are targeting the application of best management practices such as reduced tillage, winter cover crops, plant residues and grass margins in order to better address soil conservation.

38591eb8996e.title: Soil conservation
38591eb8996e.sentence: Salinity in soil is caused by irrigating with salty water.

732e3ead269d.title: Soil conservation
732e3ead269d.sentence: Water then evaporates from the soil leaving the salt behind.

a8b2f6977fd1.title: Soil conservation
a8b2f6977fd1.sentence: Salinity occurs on drylands from overirrigation and in areas with shallow saline water tables.

b2849299092b.title: Soil conservation
b2849299092b.sentence: Salinity is estimated to affect about one third of the earth's arable land.

9acdaeccf9d8.title: Soil conservation
9acdaeccf9d8.sentence: Each one percent increase in soil organic matter helps soil hold 20,000 gallons more water per acre.

142450a14a7d.title: Soil conservation
142450a14a7d.sentence: Political and economic action is further required to solve the erosion problem.

edef53e096a8.title: Soil conservation
edef53e096a8.sentence: A simple governance hurdle concerns how we value the land and this can be changed by cultural adaptation.

6fce27625fef.title: Cover crop
6fce27625fef.sentence: In agriculture, cover crops are plants that are planted to cover the soil rather than for the purpose of being harvested.

f1a065f9544a.title: Cover crop
f1a065f9544a.sentence: Cover crops may be an off-season crop planted after harvesting the cash crop.

a17e4ae7317e.title: Cover crop
a17e4ae7317e.sentence: Cover crops are nurse crops in that they increase the survival of the main crop being harvested, and are often grown over the winter.

968e3fb3d8f9.title: Cover crop
968e3fb3d8f9.sentence: Cover crops reduce soil loss by improving soil structure and increasing infiltration, protecting the soil surface, scattering raindrop energy, and reducing the velocity of the movement of water over the soil surface.

a0031abd11b5.title: Cover crop
a0031abd11b5.sentence: Additionally, vast cover crop root networks help anchor the soil in place and increase soil porosity, producing suitable habitat networks for soil macrofauna.

701b724115cf.title: Cover crop
701b724115cf.sentence: Cover crops can increase microbial activity in the soil, which has a positive effect on nitrogen availability, nitrogen uptake in target crops, and crop yields.

faa535013d4b.title: Cover crop
faa535013d4b.section: Soil quality management > Soil health and ecosystem services
faa535013d4b.sentence: A global meta-analysis of 102 field studies reported that cover crops increased saturated hydraulic conductivity by about 106%, and raised total organic carbon and total nitrogen in the topsoil by approximately 10% and 20%, respectively, relative to systems without cover crops.

598272381043.title: Cover crop
598272381043.section: Soil quality management > Soil health and ecosystem services
598272381043.sentence: At the same time, meta-analyses highlight important trade-offs and context dependence: in some environments, cover crops may reduce soil water availability to the following cash crop or have neutral or variable effects on yields, particularly in semi-arid regions or when termination is poorly timed, and long-term impacts on productivity and profitability are still uncertain in several climatic zones due to limited multi-decadal studies.

3a030c4eb862.title: Cover crop
3a030c4eb862.sentence: Just before cover crops are killed (by such practices including mowing, tilling, discing, rolling, or herbicide application) they contain a large amount of moisture.

ca9cc6804ca9.title: Terrace (earthworks)
ca9cc6804ca9.sentence: A terrace in agriculture is a flat surface that has been cut into hills or mountains to provide areas for the cultivation for crops, as a method of more effective farming.

4fd70d13c869.title: Terrace (earthworks)
4fd70d13c869.sentence: Terrace agriculture or cultivation is when these platforms are created successively down the terrain in a pattern that resembles the steps of a staircase.

a79ab114289e.title: Terrace (earthworks)
a79ab114289e.sentence: Terraced fields decrease both erosion and surface runoff, and may be used to support growing crops that require irrigation, such as rice.

4e6f5d182b15.title: Soil conservation
4e6f5d182b15.sentence: Terraces are protected from erosion by other soil barriers.

8b3bac187ece.title: Soil conservation
8b3bac187ece.sentence: Terraced farming is more common on small farms.

2259cea626f0.title: Terrace (earthworks)
2259cea626f0.sentence: Terraced paddy fields are used widely in rice, wheat and barley farming in east, south, southwest, and southeast Asia, as well as the Mediterranean Basin, Africa, and South America.

6b9f66bcedb0.title: Terrace (earthworks)
6b9f66bcedb0.sentence: The Yemen Highlands are known for their terrace systems which were constructed at the beginning of Bronze Age in the 3rd millennium BC.

c801f875545b.title: Terrace (earthworks)
c801f875545b.sentence: Similar early terrace systems have been documented in the Levant, where archaeological and geomorphological evidence supports terrace farming as early as the 4th millennium BCE, with widespread implementation in the Bronze and Iron Ages across arid environments such as the Negev Desert and Petra region.

ab20e0784098.title: Terrace (earthworks)
ab20e0784098.sentence: In the South American Andes, farmers have used terraces, known as andenes, for over a thousand years to farm potatoes, maize, and other native crops.

8a0ae9d01097.title: Terrace (earthworks)
8a0ae9d01097.sentence: Terraced farming was developed by the Wari culture and other peoples of the south-central Andes before 1000 AD, centuries before they were used by the Inca, who adopted them.

ff42c68db362.title: Terrace (earthworks)
ff42c68db362.sentence: The terraces were built to make the most efficient use of shallow soil and to enable irrigation of crops by allowing runoff to occur through the outlet.

3e665f0dbafd.title: Terrace (earthworks)
3e665f0dbafd.sentence: In the Mediterranean region, Optically Stimulated Luminescence (OSL) profiling and dating has revealed a major intensification of terrace construction during the later Middle Ages (c. AD 1100–1600), indicating a significant investment of labor in landscape modification during this period.

5125d2b3028d.title: Terrace (earthworks)
5125d2b3028d.sentence: Despite their prevalence, there is a lack of consensus among scholars regarding their construction date.

e6a7215b700f.title: Terrace (earthworks)
e6a7215b700f.sentence: Various theories have been proposed, with Zvi Ron suggesting that their origins date back to ancient times, Finkelstein proposing the Middle Bronze Age, and Feig, Stager, and Harel suggesting the Iron Age.

ec45aa91c6e4.title: Terrace (earthworks)
ec45aa91c6e4.sentence: Seligman suggested that while some terraces were established in ancient times, the majority of them are more likely to have originated during the Roman and Byzantine periods.

13aff805d386.title: Soil management
13aff805d386.sentence: Soil management is the application of operations, practices, and treatments to protect soil and enhance its performance (such as soil fertility or soil mechanics).

d86dc3dcf4e6.title: Soil management
d86dc3dcf4e6.sentence: It includes soil conservation, soil amendment, and optimal soil health.

098d5de8f88c.title: Soil management
098d5de8f88c.sentence: In agriculture, some amount of soil management is needed both in nonorganic and organic types to prevent agricultural land from becoming less productive over decades.

4261cf6ec408.title: Soil management
4261cf6ec408.sentence: Organic farming in particular emphasizes optimal soil management, because it uses soil health as the exclusive or nearly exclusive source of its fertilization and pest control.

91792dd45839.title: Soil management
91792dd45839.sentence: - Controlling traffic on the soil surface helps to reduce soil compaction, which can reduce aeration and water infiltration.

a8cf3668b79f.title: Soil management
a8cf3668b79f.sentence: - Planting cover crops that keep the soil anchored and covered in off-seasons so that the soil is not eroded by wind and rain.

476afc83260b.title: Soil management
476afc83260b.sentence: - Crop rotations for row crops alternate high-residue crops with lower-residue crops to increase the amount of plant material left on the surface of the soil during the year to protect the soil from erosion.

6e39445b849c.title: Soil management
6e39445b849c.sentence: Conventional tillage is the most intense tillage system and disturbs the deepest level of soils.

f43ef95f07ff.title: Soil management
f43ef95f07ff.sentence: Reduced-tillage or no-till operations limit the amount of soil disturbance while cultivating a new crop, and help to maintain plant residues on the surface of the soil for erosion protection and water retention.

37dafcbd1011.title: Soil management
37dafcbd1011.sentence: - Using fertilizers increases nutrients such as nitrogen, phosphorus, sulfur, and potassium in the soil.

519fab654cc0.title: Soil management
519fab654cc0.sentence: The use of fertilizers influences soil pH and often acidifies soils, with the exception of potassium fertilizer.

06a6b8741c45.title: Soil management
06a6b8741c45.sentence: - Adding organic matter to the soil surface can increase carbon in the soil and the abundance and diversity of microbial organisms in the soil.

8856b429a629.title: Soil management
8856b429a629.sentence: Project Drawdown highlights three major soil management practices as actionable steps for climate change mitigation: improved nutrient management, conservation agriculture (including no-till agriculture), and use of regenerative agriculture.

13e72fffdc70.title: Windbreak
13e72fffdc70.sentence: A windbreak (shelterbelt) is a planting usually made up of one or more rows of trees or shrubs planted in such a manner as to provide shelter from the wind and to protect soil from erosion.

971b04acd5e3.title: Soil conservation
971b04acd5e3.sentence: Windbreaks are sufficiently dense rows of trees at the windward exposure of an agricultural field subject to wind erosion.

c8b8461f400e.title: Land restoration
c8b8461f400e.sentence: Shelterbelts are wind protections composed of rows of trees, arranged perpendicular to the prevailing wind, while woodlots are more extensive areas of woodland.

3bf609a6ed72.title: Soil conservation
3bf609a6ed72.sentence: Evergreen species provide year-round protection; however, as long as foliage is present in the seasons of bare soil surfaces, the effect of deciduous trees may be adequate.

80f84944b8c8.title: Desertification
80f84944b8c8.sentence: Windbreaks are made from trees and bushes and are used to reduce soil erosion and evapotranspiration.

548ec249db32.title: Desertification
548ec249db32.sentence: Fixating the soil is often done through the use of shelter belts, woodlots and windbreaks.

e46fcbcf22c2.title: Drought
e46fcbcf22c2.sentence: Therefore, windbreaks (such as big trees and bushes) are often planted by farmers to reduce the wind erosion of loess.

69ce50c75a05.title: Buffer strip
69ce50c75a05.sentence: Windbreaks can also serve as an area that separates fields and protects them from spray drift of pesticides.

98b143bf1d59.title: Windbreak
98b143bf1d59.sentence: Windbreaks can mitigate the effects of pesticide drift.

22ab8b582c31.title: Windbreak
22ab8b582c31.sentence: This results in slower wind speed further downwind, reaching a minimum at a distance of about 3 to 5 times the windbreak's height.

cf7e57b8506e.title: Windbreak
cf7e57b8506e.sentence: Beyond that point wind speed recovers, aided by the overlying, faster-moving stream.

1e849476f15d.title: Windbreak
1e849476f15d.sentence: Farmers sometimes use windbreaks to keep snow drifts on farm land that will provide water when the snow melts in the spring.

fe010f940333.title: Agroforestry
fe010f940333.sentence: Agroforestry (also known as agro-sylviculture or forest farming) is a land use management system that integrates trees with crops or pasture.

9f45abba6531.title: Agroforestry
9f45abba6531.sentence: An agroforestry system is intensively managed to optimize helpful interactions between the plants and animals included, and "uses the forest as a model of practices".

ff8038a6160a.title: Agroforestry
ff8038a6160a.sentence: The term "agroforestry" was coined in 1973 by Canadian forester John Bene, but the concept includes agricultural practices that have existed for millennia.

9b301756c914.title: Agroforestry
9b301756c914.sentence: Ninety-one countries and areas reported a total land area subject to agroforestry of 55.4 million hectares in 2025.

b195bf14bf7b.title: Agroforestry
b195bf14bf7b.sentence: The majority (39.3 million ha) of this area is in Asia, mostly South and Southeast Asia, with India and Indonesia accounting for almost 100% of the regional total and for 70% of the global total.

9654bac2519a.title: Agroforestry
9654bac2519a.sentence: Depleted soil can be protected from soil erosion by groundcover plants such as naturally growing grasses in agroforestry systems.

32cc82ab624a.title: Agroforestry
32cc82ab624a.sentence: Trees can help reduce water runoff by decreasing water flow and evaporation and thereby allowing for increased soil infiltration.

1c1c9d0fb707.title: Agroforestry
1c1c9d0fb707.sentence: Agroforestry can also utilise nitrogen-fixing plants such as legumes to restore soil nitrogen fertility.

17f5fc000e41.title: Agroforestry
17f5fc000e41.sentence: Agroforestry practices can increase carbon stocks in soil and woody biomass.

9263c7ef74cb.title: Agroforestry
9263c7ef74cb.sentence: The United States Department of Agriculture distinguishes five applications of agroforestry for temperate climates, namely alley cropping, forest farming, riparian forest buffers, silvopasture, and windbreaks.

72acdc458c44.title: Agroforestry
72acdc458c44.sentence: This region was historically used for slash-and-burn subsistence agriculture.

f065f260dd87.title: Agroforestry
f065f260dd87.sentence: Due to heavy seasonal floods, the exposed soil was washed away, leaving infertile barren soil exposed to the dry season.

8b6b99409768.title: Agroforestry
8b6b99409768.sentence: - Thin and prune hillside secondary forest, leaving individual beneficial trees, especially nitrogen-fixing trees.

178385e04722.title: Agroforestry
178385e04722.sentence: They help reduce soil erosion, maintain soil moisture, provide shade and provide an input of nitrogen-rich organic matter in the form of litter.

fc1843998483.title: Strip farming
fc1843998483.sentence: Strip cropping is a method of farming which involves cultivating a field partitioned into long, narrow strips which are alternated in a crop rotation system.

e37137657279.title: Strip farming
e37137657279.sentence: It is used when a slope is too steep or when there is no alternative method of preventing soil erosion.

6eb0bee5b908.title: Strip farming
6eb0bee5b908.sentence: The most common crop choices for strip cropping are closely sown crops such as hay, wheat, or other forages which are alternated with strips of row crops, such as corn, soybeans, cotton, or sugar beets.

26abe2ade56d.title: Strip farming
26abe2ade56d.sentence: The forages serve primarily as cover crops.

a27569f3f810.title: Strip farming
a27569f3f810.sentence: The growing of a cultivated crop (as corn) in strips alternating with strips of a sod-forming crop (as hay) is arranged to follow an approximate contour of the land and minimize erosion.

3445cfe98fec.title: Strip farming
3445cfe98fec.sentence: Strip cropping helps to stop soil erosion by creating natural dams for water and preserving the strength of the soil.

ab38dbac8cfd.title: Strip farming
ab38dbac8cfd.sentence: When strips of soil are strong enough to slow down water from moving through them, the weaker soil cannot wash away as it normally would.

55abe7afdc82.title: Strip farming
55abe7afdc82.sentence: The width of strips is determined by a number of factors, with the two most important being the average wind velocity in a specific site and the features of the slope, particularly the gradient.

a41d66acbc1b.title: Strip farming
a41d66acbc1b.sentence: Each strip typically ranges from 25 feet (7.6 m) to 75 feet (23 m) in width, but certain conditions may necessitate widths outside of this range.

dd31ff629ba9.title: Strip farming
dd31ff629ba9.sentence: A minimum width of 50 feet (15 m) is ideal for the use of most farm equipment.

1a4652d9c851.title: Strip farming
1a4652d9c851.sentence: The term strip cropping also refers to a method of dry farming sometimes used in areas including parts of the Great Plains of the United States and the Prairies of Canada.

e1adc4368d2e.title: Strip farming
e1adc4368d2e.sentence: To accumulate moisture in those dry areas, cropland is periodically left fallow.

6bfa77e6eac2.title: Strip farming
6bfa77e6eac2.sentence: Typically, the fallow and planted areas are organized in parallel long, narrow strips that are oriented normal to the prevailing winds to minimize the erosion of soil from the bare fields.

76819e532b6f.title: Strip farming
76819e532b6f.sentence: Contour strip cropping employs a crop rotation system down a slope to minimize runoff and rain velocity.

6d9b56e2f703.title: Strip farming
6d9b56e2f703.sentence: It is used mainly on gentle slope gradients.

619d44a72a8e.title: Strip farming
619d44a72a8e.sentence: The width of protective strips is often higher than that of the row crop strips, so they may effectively intercept runoff.

9c6f870cdb0b.title: Strip farming
9c6f870cdb0b.sentence: Intercropping is the practice of growing two or more crops in the same field.

7915a07d7d6b.title: Strip farming
7915a07d7d6b.sentence: The field is still divided into strips, but the strips are narrower and contiguous, which helps facilitate modern farm machinery as well as allows adjoining plants to benefit from synergistic growth effects.

7218de8233fd.title: Strip farming
7218de8233fd.sentence: In the Midwestern United States, prairie strips integrate "native plant species into farm fields as contour buffers and edge-of-field filters." Prairie strips attract pollinators, build soil health, help prevent erosion, and provide wildlife habitat.

57aaa4819e9c.title: Soil stabilization
57aaa4819e9c.sentence: Soil stabilization is a general term for any physical, chemical, mechanical, biological, or combined method of changing a natural soil to meet an engineering purpose.

3151c747f03a.title: Soil stabilization
3151c747f03a.sentence: Improvements include increasing weight-bearing capabilities, tensile strength, and overall performance of unstable subsoils, sands, and waste materials in order to strengthen road pavements.

6e713f11a53f.title: Soil stabilization
6e713f11a53f.sentence: Bitumen, tar emulsions, asphalt, cement, and lime can be used as binding agents for producing a road base.

d39ca6d6a90c.title: Soil stabilization
d39ca6d6a90c.sentence: Cement fly ash, lime fly ash (separately, or with cement or lime), bitumen, tar, cement kiln dust (CKD), tree resin, and ionic stabilizers are all commonly used stabilizing agents.

ed2e9c26ba94.title: Soil stabilization
ed2e9c26ba94.sentence: However, bitumen is not an environmentally friendly product and becomes brittle when it dries out.

28dc22bcf6b6.title: Soil stabilization
28dc22bcf6b6.sentence: However, this can often be an expensive component and not an environmentally friendly alternative.

ecf407c2fa96.title: Soil stabilization
ecf407c2fa96.sentence: Some renewable technologies are enzymes, surfactants, biopolymers, synthetic polymers, co-polymer-based products, cross-linking styrene acrylic polymers, tree resins, ionic stabilizers, fiber reinforcement, calcium chloride, calcite, sodium chloride, magnesium chloride, and more.

aab998e010ec.title: Soil stabilization
aab998e010ec.sentence: Some of these new stabilizing techniques create hydrophobic surfaces and mass that prevent road failure from water penetration or heavy frosts by inhibiting the ingress of water into the treated layer.

e1cf4e94ff55.title: Soil stabilization
e1cf4e94ff55.sentence: Many environmentally friendly alternatives have essentially the same formula as soap powders, merely lubricating and realigning the soil with no effective binding property.

3fa34ac4af64.title: Soil stabilization
3fa34ac4af64.sentence: Many of the new approaches rely on large amounts of clay with its inherent binding properties.

80cb0282a7d6.title: Soil stabilization
80cb0282a7d6.sentence: Another soil stabilization method called the Deep Mixing Method is non-destructive and effective at improving load bearing capacity of weak or loose soil strata.

f27726ca507e.title: Soil stabilization
f27726ca507e.sentence: This method uses a small, penny-sized injection probe and minimizes debris and is ideal for re-compaction and consolidation of weak soil strata, increasing and improving load-bearing capacity under structures, and the remediation of shallow and deep sinkhole problems.

cd03956cb071.title: Shrink–swell capacity
cd03956cb071.sentence: Yet another solution is a process called soil stabilization, in which additional materials are added to the soil to limit its ability to shrink and swell.

d8ad15bed66d.title: Cover crop
d8ad15bed66d.sentence: One of the primary uses of cover crops is to increase soil fertility.

9032d6cf7c27.title: Cover crop
9032d6cf7c27.sentence: Of the various nutrients, the impact that cover crops have on nitrogen management has received the most attention from researchers and farmers because nitrogen is often the most limiting nutrient in crop production.

7a00e4208673.title: Cover crop
7a00e4208673.sentence: These types of cover crops are referred to as "green manure".

7f7908f5f172.title: Cover crop
7f7908f5f172.sentence: Often, green manure crops are grown for a specific period, and then plowed under before reaching full maturity to improve soil fertility and quality.

9b02467ebd91.title: Cover crop
9b02467ebd91.sentence: Lupins is nodulated by the soil microorganism Bradyrhizobium sp. (Lupinus).

debbb1e0959c.title: Cover crop
debbb1e0959c.sentence: These bacteria convert biologically unavailable atmospheric nitrogen gas (N 2) to biologically available ammonium (NH+ 4) through the process of biological nitrogen fixation.

289d5309816f.title: Cover crop
289d5309816f.sentence: Leguminous cover crops are typically high in nitrogen and can often provide the required quantity of nitrogen for crop production.

e0733de4cbee.title: Cover crop
e0733de4cbee.sentence: In conventional farming, this nitrogen is typically applied in chemical fertilizer form.

c8ad0bf7fbee.title: Cover crop
c8ad0bf7fbee.sentence: This quality of cover crops is called fertilizer replacement value.

63396f09988b.title: Cover crop
63396f09988b.sentence: Some scientists believe that widespread biological nitrogen fixation, achieved mainly through the use of cover crops, is the only alternative to industrial nitrogen fixation in the effort to maintain or increase future food production levels.

86b16756bbf6.title: Cover crop
86b16756bbf6.sentence: Industrial nitrogen fixation has been criticized as an unsustainable source of nitrogen for food production due to its reliance on fossil fuel energy and the environmental impacts associated with chemical nitrogen fertilizer use in agriculture.

682d8161a1b1.title: Cover crop
682d8161a1b1.sentence: Such widespread environmental impacts include nitrogen fertilizer losses into waterways, which can lead to eutrophication (nutrient loading) and ensuing hypoxia (oxygen depletion) of large bodies of water.

a72e4b846b84.title: Cover crop
a72e4b846b84.sentence: An example of this is in the Mississippi Valley Basin, where years of fertilizer nitrogen loading into the watershed from agricultural production have resulted in an annual summer hypoxic "dead zone" off the Gulf of Mexico that reached an area of over 22,000 square kilometres (8,500 sq mi) in 2017.

2543aeeb1120.title: Cover crop
2543aeeb1120.sentence: An example of green manure use comes from Nigeria, where the cover crop Mucuna pruriens (velvet bean) has been found to increase the availability of phosphorus in soil after a farmer applies rock phosphate.

bb6de756ddc3.title: Conservation agriculture
bb6de756ddc3.sentence: Conservation agriculture (CA) can be defined by a statement given by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations as "Conservation Agriculture (CA) is a farming system that can prevent losses of arable land while regenerating degraded lands.

af5ff846d4d5.title: Conservation agriculture
af5ff846d4d5.sentence: It promotes minimum soil disturbance (i.e. no-till farming), maintenance of a permanent soil cover, and diversification of plant species.

7f00c836acc0.title: Soil management
7f00c836acc0.sentence: Conservation agriculture has three main practices: minimizing soil disturbance, maintaining permanent soil coverage, and diversifying crop species.

121839ecf9d1.title: Agricultural pollution
121839ecf9d1.section: Abiotic sources > Organic farming and conservation agriculture in mitigation > Conservation agriculture
121839ecf9d1.sentence: Conservation agriculture relies on principles of minimal soil disturbance, the use of mulch and/or cover crops as soil cover, and crop species diversification.

967998e69041.title: Soil management
967998e69041.sentence: Alternatives include conservation, regenerative, and organic agriculture, which can be broadly grouped as sustainable agriculture.

d1a1ad2f93f7.title: Soil management
d1a1ad2f93f7.sentence: Conventional agriculture is driven by industrialization and aims to maximize efficiency.

16fe9c2eba0e.title: Conservation agriculture
16fe9c2eba0e.sentence: It was believed that tilling the soil would increase fertility within the soil through mineralization that takes place in the soil.

595a965453eb.title: Conservation agriculture
595a965453eb.sentence: Today tillage is seen as destroying organic matter that can be found within the soil cover.

ed93e1a5c7ef.title: Conservation agriculture
ed93e1a5c7ef.sentence: Tilling of soil can cause severe erosion and crusting which leads to a decrease in soil fertility.

8e6e8bbd7e15.title: Conservation agriculture
8e6e8bbd7e15.sentence: The presence of mulching also reduce the velocity of runoff and the impact of rain drops thus reducing soil erosion and runoff.

3bca09719f94.title: Conservation agriculture
3bca09719f94.sentence: This type of ground cover also helps keep the temperature and moisture levels of the soil at a higher level rather than if it was tilled every year (FAO 2007).

6f6e11e175db.title: Conservation agriculture
6f6e11e175db.sentence: Producers can save 30% to 40% of time and labor by practicing the no-till process.

4678a982da17.title: Conservation agriculture
4678a982da17.sentence: It can be many years before a producer will start to see better yields than he/she has had previously.

af964d36ffb0.title: Conservation agriculture
af964d36ffb0.sentence: When starting to use CA, a producer may have to buy new planters or drills in order to produce effectively.

9a9d5b9d9d6f.title: Conservation agriculture
9a9d5b9d9d6f.sentence: The application of CA requires a critical level of crop residues remaining on the surface, while traditionally most of these residues are used for feeding livestock.

92c227e64e60.title: Soil conservation
92c227e64e60.section: Methods > Reducing the use of pesticides
92c227e64e60.sentence: The use of pesticides can contaminate the soil, and nearby vegetation and water sources for a long time.

13b3ea03b4d4.title: Soil conservation
13b3ea03b4d4.section: Methods > Reducing the use of pesticides
13b3ea03b4d4.sentence: They affect soil structure and (biotic and abiotic) composition.

88b3ad6c2e4c.title: Soil conservation
88b3ad6c2e4c.section: Methods > Reducing the use of pesticides
88b3ad6c2e4c.sentence: Alternatives to pesticides are available and include food irradiation, phytosanitary irradiation, methods of cultivation, use of biological pest controls (such as pheromones and microbial pesticides), genetic engineering (mostly of crops), and methods of interfering with insect breeding.

49e214bf3a58.title: Soil conservation
49e214bf3a58.section: Methods > Reducing the use of pesticides
49e214bf3a58.sentence: Application of composted yard waste has also been used as a way of controlling pests.

2a45185e697a.title: Soil conservation
2a45185e697a.section: Methods > Reducing the use of pesticides
2a45185e697a.sentence: Differentiated taxation schemes are among the options investigated in the academic literature to reducing their use.

209d400e848f.title: Soil conservation
209d400e848f.sentence: Soil-conservation farming involves no-till farming, "green manures" and other soil-enhancing practices which make it hard for the soils to be equalized.

5660532c88b3.title: Soil conservation
5660532c88b3.sentence: They can revive damaged soil, minimize erosion, encourage plant growth, eliminate the use of nitrogen fertilizer or fungicide, produce above-average yields and protect crops during droughts or flooding.

a156993f2b21.title: Soil conservation
a156993f2b21.sentence: The result is less labor and lower costs that increase farmers’ profits.

249658293624.title: Soil conservation
249658293624.sentence: No-till farming and cover crops act as sinks for nitrogen and other nutrients.

1d2955bd1fd9.title: Soil conservation
1d2955bd1fd9.sentence: This increases the amount of soil organic matter.

e67025f9f4d8.title: Soil conservation
e67025f9f4d8.sentence: Repeated plowing/tilling degrades soil, killing its beneficial fungi and earthworms.

bb730128ff20.title: Soil conservation
bb730128ff20.sentence: Once damaged, soil may take multiple seasons to fully recover, even in optimal circumstances.

d626c81ed75d.title: Soil conservation
d626c81ed75d.sentence: Critics argue that no-till and related methods are impractical and too expensive for many growers, partly because it requires new equipment.

3ebea138bcb7.title: Soil conservation
3ebea138bcb7.sentence: They cite advantages for conventional tilling depending on the geography, crops and soil conditions.

9520aa0217b7.title: Soil conservation
9520aa0217b7.sentence: Some farmers have contended that no-till complicates pest control, delays planting and that post-harvest residues, especially for corn, are hard to manage.

da464c3434df.title: Soil management
da464c3434df.sentence: According to the EPA, agricultural soil management practices can lead to production and emission of nitrous oxide (N2O), a major greenhouse gas and air pollutant.

e3d9ea5de1d7.title: Soil management
e3d9ea5de1d7.sentence: Soils can sequester carbon dioxide (CO2) from the atmosphere, primarily by storing carbon as soil organic carbon (SOC) through the process of photosynthesis.

b22a0cec61da.title: Soil management
b22a0cec61da.sentence: Activities that can contribute to N2O emissions include fertilizer usage, irrigation and tillage.

c50bb9ab7d9c.title: Soil management
c50bb9ab7d9c.sentence: The management of soils accounts for over half of the emissions are from the Agriculture sector.

b4cf0bf8fd50.title: Soil management
b4cf0bf8fd50.sentence: Using biochar may decrease N2O emissions from soils by an average of 54%.

2bb15bc3151f.title: Soil management
2bb15bc3151f.sentence: Converting natural land to agricultural land releases carbon back into the atmosphere.

0906d5b412d1.title: Soil management
0906d5b412d1.sentence: The amount of carbon a soil can sequester depends on the climate, current and historical land-use and management.

67fa003837eb.title: Soil management
67fa003837eb.sentence: Cropland has the potential to sequester 0.5–1.2 Pg C/year and grazing and pasture land could sequester 0.3–0.7 Pg C/year.

08aa7b04197a.title: Soil management
08aa7b04197a.sentence: There are three overarching practices that improve carbon sequestration in soils: increasing biomass inputs, decreasing SOC losses, and increasing the mean residence time (MRT) of SOC.

b40eed350ff0.title: Soil management
b40eed350ff0.sentence: Methods that significantly enhance carbon sequestration in soil include no-till farming, residue mulching, cover cropping, and crop rotation, all of which are more widely used in organic farming than in conventional farming.

9a08ad903a48.title: Lynchet
9a08ad903a48.sentence: A lynchet or linchet is an earth terrace found on the side of a hill.

4a6528973dab.title: Lynchet
4a6528973dab.sentence: Lynchets are a feature of ancient field systems of the British Isles.

3c6d14a70e17.title: Lynchet
3c6d14a70e17.sentence: They are commonly found in vertical rows and more commonly referred to as "strip lynchets".

248f878f87c0.title: Lynchet
248f878f87c0.sentence: Lynchets appear predominantly in Southern Britain and many are in areas close to Iron Age forts and other earthworks, including later Roman earthworks and earlier barrows from the Neolithic and Bronze Age periods.

eeda36de67a0.title: Lynchet
eeda36de67a0.sentence: The traditional theory on the formation of lynchets is that they may form naturally on the downslope of a field ploughed over a long period of time.

f2da13462081.title: Lynchet
f2da13462081.sentence: The disturbed soil slips down the hillside to create a "positive lynchet" (where the new surface is higher than the original surface), while the area reduced in level becomes a "negative lynchet" (where the new surface is lower).

163437fc1914.title: Lynchet
163437fc1914.sentence: The size, location, spacing and number of rows of many strip lynchets indicates that many were man-made.

f784735d3630.title: Lynchet
f784735d3630.sentence: It is most likely that lynchets were dug to maximise the use of land for agriculture, although they may have had other, ceremonial uses.

d533d9fc2ef0.title: Lynchet
d533d9fc2ef0.sentence: The word is the diminutive form of lynch, now rarely appearing in the English language, indicating an agricultural terrace; it is cognate with the golf links.

a2a7eb999def.title: Terrace (earthworks)
a2a7eb999def.sentence: In Old English, a terrace was also called a "lynch" (lynchet).

96fd752b4df4.title: Cover crop
96fd752b4df4.sentence: By reducing soil erosion, cover crops often also reduce both the rate and quantity of water that drains off the field, which would normally pose environmental risks to waterways and ecosystems downstream.

fbadae3196d1.title: Cover crop
fbadae3196d1.sentence: Also, as stated above, cover crop root growth results in the formation of soil pores, which, in addition to enhancing soil macrofauna habitat provides pathways for water to filter through the soil profile rather than draining off the field as surface flow.

e87d541930c5.title: Cover crop
e87d541930c5.sentence: Cover crop biomass acts as a physical barrier between rainfall and the soil surface, allowing raindrops to steadily trickle down through the soil profile.

a46d4617e832.title: Cover crop
a46d4617e832.sentence: With increased water infiltration, the potential for soil water storage and the recharge of aquifers can be improved.

cff1c2a5129e.title: Cover crop
cff1c2a5129e.sentence: In agroecosystems where water for crop production is in short supply, cover crops can be used as a mulch to conserve water by shading and cooling the soil surface.

186b59833c09.title: Cover crop
186b59833c09.sentence: This reduces the evaporation of soil moisture and helps preserve soil nutrients.

bff90453eedb.title: Cover crop
bff90453eedb.sentence: Some cover crops are used as trap crops, to attract pests away from the crop of value and toward what the pest sees as a more favorable habitat.

1797a5693dc7.title: Cover crop
1797a5693dc7.sentence: Cover crops can contribute to pest management by improving soil health and disrupting pest and disease cycles.

97555e3ee148.title: Cover crop
97555e3ee148.sentence: Other cover crops are used to attract natural predators of pests by imitating elements of their habitat.

1d9fbafb0cae.title: Cover crop
1d9fbafb0cae.sentence: Species in the family Brassicaceae, such as mustards, have been widely shown to suppress fungal disease populations through the release of naturally occurring toxic chemicals during the degradation of glucosinolate compounds in their plant cell tissues.

bf2e185cbff1.title: Cover crop
bf2e185cbff1.sentence: Another example of trap crops is nematode-resistant white mustard (Sinapis alba) and radish (Raphanus sativus).

2d721621b4cd.title: Cover crop
2d721621b4cd.sentence: After entering the roots they cannot reproduce in the root due to a hypersensitive resistance reaction of the plant.

de774aa730c8.title: Cover crop
de774aa730c8.sentence: Hence the nematode population is greatly reduced, by 70–99%, depending on species and cultivation time.

abffcc3fae6f.title: Cover crop
abffcc3fae6f.sentence: Grasses, legumes, and brassicas have been shown to reduce erosion, increase soil organic matter, and enhance microbial activity, supporting more resilient cash crops and reducing yield loss to insect pests and pathogens..

8fef222a474d.title: Cover crop
