8fef222a474d.sentence: Findings on the relationship between cover crop presence and predator–pest population dynamics have been mixed, suggesting the need for detailed information on specific cover crop types and management practices to best complement a given integrated pest management strategy.

560b43af3ad4.title: Cover crop
560b43af3ad4.sentence: Some cover crops suppress weeds both during growth and after death.

51b88c30e626.title: Cover crop
51b88c30e626.sentence: During growth these cover crops compete vigorously with weeds for available space, light, and nutrients, and after death they smother the next flush of weeds by forming a mulch layer on the soil surface.

954ce093f3c2.title: Cover crop
954ce093f3c2.sentence: If the cover crop is flattened down on the soil surface rather than incorporated into the soil as a green manure after its growth is terminated, it can form a nearly impenetrable mat.

de76d03ed0e2.title: Cover crop
de76d03ed0e2.sentence: This drastically reduces light transmittance to weed seeds, which in many cases reduces weed seed germination rates.

79b799cd0e01.title: Cover crop
79b799cd0e01.sentence: This is often termed the cover crop smother effect.

c0ce2959bcdf.title: Cover crop
c0ce2959bcdf.sentence: This occurs when certain biochemical cover crop compounds are degraded that happen to be toxic to, or inhibit seed germination of, other plant species.

f2e850a208ce.title: Cover crop
f2e850a208ce.sentence: Furthermore, after cover crop termination, the yellow sweetclover residues suppressed weeds to levels 75–97% lower than in fallow (no yellow sweetclover) systems.

6aaed0d4cb52.title: Cover crop
6aaed0d4cb52.sentence: In one study, rye cover crop residues were found to have provided between 80% and 95% control of early season broadleaf weeds when used as a mulch during the production of different cash crops such as soybean, tobacco, corn, and sunflower.

e11b615f5d0b.title: Biological pest control
e11b615f5d0b.sentence: Biological control or biocontrol is a method of controlling pests, whether animals, weed plants, or pathogens of animals or of plants by using other organisms.

052be1849a3f.title: Biological pest control
052be1849a3f.sentence: It relies on predation, parasitism, and herbivory, but typically involves an active human management role.

59f571df1a10.title: Biological pest control
59f571df1a10.sentence: It can be a component of integrated pest management (IPM) programs.

1b4c85683f77.title: Biological pest control
1b4c85683f77.sentence: There are three basic biological pest control strategies: importation, augmentation and conservation.

8947d2629b47.title: Biological pest control
8947d2629b47.sentence: Importation or classical biological control is the introduction of a pest's natural enemies to a new locale where they do not occur naturally.

e1f96f5ce6df.title: Biological pest control
e1f96f5ce6df.sentence: Augmentation involves the supplemental release of natural enemies that occur in a particular area, boosting the naturally occurring populations there.

01b5ab1b6998.title: Biological pest control
01b5ab1b6998.sentence: The conservation of existing natural enemies in an environment is the third method of biological pest control.

1286d9fae9df.title: Biological pest control
1286d9fae9df.sentence: Natural enemies are already adapted to the habitat and to the target pest, and their conservation can be simple and cost-effective, as when nectar-producing crop plants are grown in the borders of rice fields.

c2a8001f8103.title: Biological pest control
c2a8001f8103.sentence: These provide nectar to support parasitoids and predators of planthopper pests and have been demonstrated to be so effective (reducing pest densities by 10- or even 100-fold) that farmers sprayed 70% less insecticides and enjoyed yields boosted by 5%.

1e41eea5710a.title: Biological pest control
1e41eea5710a.sentence: Bacillus thuringiensis, a soil-dwelling bacterium, is the most widely applied species of bacteria used for biological control, with at least four sub-species used against Lepidopteran (moth, butterfly), Coleopteran (beetle) and Dipteran (true fly) insect pests.

ad034ec145ca.title: Biological pest control
ad034ec145ca.sentence: Bacteria used for biological control infect insects via their digestive tracts, so they offer only limited options for controlling insects with sucking mouth parts such as aphids and scale insects.

0e2a5253c14c.title: Biological pest control
0e2a5253c14c.sentence: Early instances were often unofficial and not based on research; some introduced species subsequently became serious pests themselves.

ee47b3fe5ffa.title: Biological pest control
ee47b3fe5ffa.sentence: An introduced control does not always target only the intended pest species; it can also target native species.

1a088a18711a.title: Contour trenching
1a088a18711a.sentence: Contour trenching (a.k.a., Continuous Contour Trench or CCT) is an agricultural technique that can be easily applied in arid sub-Sahara areas to allow for water, and soil conservation, and to increase agricultural production.

1c173399bb9b.title: Contour trenching
1c173399bb9b.sentence: Trenches can be artificially dug along the contour lines, across the slope so that water flowing down the hill is retained by the trench, and is infiltrating the soil below.

be477d01546f.title: Contour trenching
be477d01546f.sentence: Between two trenches crops can benefit during the growing season (when there is less rain) from the subsoil water reserve gathered during the rainy season.

4e569abe17cb.title: Contour trenching
4e569abe17cb.sentence: - The rain water does not immediately run off the hill,

78d0d713bb1f.title: Contour trenching
78d0d713bb1f.sentence: - Crops do not suffer later on from water shortage,

34d52d9b1f6b.title: Contour trenching
34d52d9b1f6b.sentence: - Fertile soil particles are not lost by water and wind erosion.

c62b267ae326.title: Contour trenching
c62b267ae326.sentence: Depending on the slope of the hill, the parallel trenches can be closer or further from one another.

65d9c7b0a4b4.title: Contour trenching
65d9c7b0a4b4.sentence: The dimensions, and the format of the trench should correspond to the local climate and soil conditions.

88baf9125709.title: Contour trenching
88baf9125709.sentence: The trench should be big enough to keep all the water; no water should spill over the downhill border.

f806804884f1.title: Contour trenching
f806804884f1.sentence: The upside of the trench should be protected against erosion, by means of e.g. grass, shrubs, or fabric.

4722a8859080.title: Desertification
4722a8859080.sentence: Another technique that is useful is contour trenching.

3b4bfc2ef8cc.title: Buffer strip
3b4bfc2ef8cc.sentence: A buffer strip is an area of land maintained in permanent vegetation that helps to control air quality, soil quality, and water quality, along with other environmental problems, dealing primarily on land that is used in agriculture.

db61b34e870d.title: Buffer strip
db61b34e870d.sentence: Buffer strips trap sediment, and enhance filtration of nutrients and pesticides by slowing down surface runoff that could enter the local surface waters.

d6157e26a973.title: Buffer strip
d6157e26a973.sentence: Buffer strips mitigate runoff through plant life: root systems of the planted vegetation in these buffers hold soil particles together which alleviate the soil of wind erosion and stabilize stream banks providing protection against substantial erosion and landslides.

2bea300a435b.title: Buffer strip
2bea300a435b.sentence: Buffer strips can have several different configurations of vegetation found on them varying from simply grass to combinations of grass, trees, and shrubs.

ffac97c24f7f.title: Buffer strip
ffac97c24f7f.sentence: Areas with diverse vegetation provide more protection from nutrient and pesticide flow and at the same time provide better biodiversity amongst plants and animals.

6a89ccfdddad.title: Buffer strip
6a89ccfdddad.sentence: Many country, state, and local governments provide financial incentives for conservation programs such as buffer strips because they help stabilize the environment, help reduce nitrogen emissions to water and soil loss by wind erosion, while simultaneously providing substantial environmental co-benefits, even when the land is being used.

c17b471605e2.title: Buffer strip
c17b471605e2.sentence: As viewed by the Natural Resources Conservation Service, soil drainage is the number one priority for location of certain grasses.

3855dbcc31d7.title: Buffer strip
3855dbcc31d7.sentence: Poorer drainage causes less infiltration of water into the soil as groundwater recharge causing ponding and flooding of surrounding crops.

2ee206c8d362.title: Buffer strip
2ee206c8d362.sentence: Higher drainage becomes more droughty which hinders the establishment of certain grasses good for waterways.

339b4995cd45.title: Buffer strip
339b4995cd45.sentence: Medium soil drainage becomes the most suitable for planting.

4c04e8c30fb0.title: Buffer strip
4c04e8c30fb0.sentence: The NRCS has shown contour strip cropping provides the greatest effectiveness when slopes of the area are within 4-8%.

abfec22040a5.title: Soil Conservation and Domestic Allotment Act of 1936
abfec22040a5.sentence: L. 74–461, enacted February 29, 1936) is a United States federal law that allowed the government to pay farmers to reduce production so as to conserve soil and prevent erosion.
abfec22040a5.key: Soil Conservation and Domestic Allotment Act of 1936

41cb67199f05.title: Soil Conservation and Domestic Allotment Act of 1936
41cb67199f05.sentence: The Act was passed in response to the Supreme Court's declaration that the Agricultural Adjustment Act (AAA) was unconstitutional.
41cb67199f05.key: Soil Conservation and Domestic Allotment Act of 1936

f62382f3ab26.title: Soil Conservation and Domestic Allotment Act of 1936
f62382f3ab26.sentence: 163 on April 27, 1935 in an attempt to address farm erosion problems by bringing within its policy and purposes, the improvements and preservation of national soil resources.
f62382f3ab26.key: Soil Conservation and Domestic Allotment Act of 1936

22b6c7e75056.title: Soil Conservation and Domestic Allotment Act of 1936
22b6c7e75056.sentence: L. 74–461 and renaming the legislation the Soil Conservation and Domestic Allotment Act with the express purpose of encouraging the use of soil resources in such a manner as to preserve and improve fertility, promote economic use, and diminish the exploitation and unprofitable use of the national soil resources.
22b6c7e75056.key: Soil Conservation and Domestic Allotment Act of 1936

e6d527642af9.title: Soil Conservation and Domestic Allotment Act of 1936
e6d527642af9.sentence: It meant to help with some of the problems with the previous Act, most notably its failure to protect sharecroppers and tenant farmers.
e6d527642af9.key: Soil Conservation and Domestic Allotment Act of 1936

c9728312bbc8.title: Soil Conservation and Domestic Allotment Act of 1936
c9728312bbc8.sentence: Landlords were now required to share the payments they received from the government for cutting back production with those who worked on their land.
c9728312bbc8.key: Soil Conservation and Domestic Allotment Act of 1936

b0b631274335.title: Soil Conservation and Domestic Allotment Act of 1936
b0b631274335.sentence: The Act also gave directives to conserve the soil in the "high plains"—soil that was being raised into huge dust bowls during the 1930s.
b0b631274335.key: Soil Conservation and Domestic Allotment Act of 1936

30a7e1cb78ea.title: Soil Conservation and Domestic Allotment Act of 1936
30a7e1cb78ea.sentence: The Act both educated farmers on how to use their lands without damaging them, and took immediate action to contain the dust bowl's effects—notably by planting trees and native grass.
30a7e1cb78ea.key: Soil Conservation and Domestic Allotment Act of 1936

a5a3c9fa6f9b.title: Soil Conservation and Domestic Allotment Act of 1936
a5a3c9fa6f9b.sentence: Franklin D. Roosevelt signed the Act into law on February 29, 1936.
a5a3c9fa6f9b.key: Soil Conservation and Domestic Allotment Act of 1936

8fe2f2d001ab.title: Terracette
8fe2f2d001ab.sentence: A terracette is a landform consisting of a hillside ridge arranged as part of sub-parallel "step-like sequences" of such ridges.

3a374256b494.title: Terracette
3a374256b494.sentence: It may also be described as a small, irregular step-like formation on steep hillslopes, especially on those used for pasture which are formed by soil creep or erosion of surface soils exacerbated by the trampling of livestock such as sheep or cattle.

a0518a87ec40.title: Terracette
a0518a87ec40.sentence: Synonyms are: catstep, cattle terracing, sheep or cattle track.

1a633913910c.title: Terracette
1a633913910c.sentence: One explanation holds that terracettes are formed when saturated soil particles expand, then contract as they dry, causing them to move slowly downhill.

a6d95c619c69.title: Terracette
a6d95c619c69.sentence: Early investigators such as C. Darwin (1904) believed that animals grazing the hillsides caused terracettes, but further examination revealed places where they abruptly end at steep rock faces or at soils of different composition.

d585b4c33be8.title: Terracette
d585b4c33be8.sentence: Other sites show livestock trails cutting across terracettes.

d1cb66e534d3.title: Terracette
d1cb66e534d3.sentence: Geomorphologists Vincent and Clarke have also cast doubt about the ability of animals alone to create such regular steps or ridges.

7fc3a64e8275.title: Great Plains Shelterbelt
7fc3a64e8275.sentence: The Great Plains Shelterbelt was a project to create windbreaks in the Great Plains states of the United States, that began in 1934.

4fdeb97646f1.title: Great Plains Shelterbelt
4fdeb97646f1.sentence: President Franklin D. Roosevelt initiated the project in response to the severe dust storms of the Dust Bowl, which resulted in significant soil erosion.

75bfe9afd324.title: Great Plains Shelterbelt
75bfe9afd324.sentence: The United States Forest Service believed that planting trees on the perimeters of farms would reduce wind velocity and lessen evaporation of moisture from the soil.

080b7e2f4976.title: Great Plains Shelterbelt
080b7e2f4976.sentence: By 1942, 30,233 shelterbelts had been planted, which contained 220 million trees and covered 18,600 square miles (48,000 km2).

ebe0237d24e5.title: Great Plains Shelterbelt
ebe0237d24e5.sentence: By 1942, 220 million trees had been planted, covering 18,600 square miles (48,000 km2) in a 100-mile (160-kilometre) wide zone from the Canadian border in North Dakota to the Brazos River in Texas.

08be5579433e.title: Great Plains Shelterbelt
08be5579433e.sentence: Native trees, such as red cedar and green ash, were planted along fence rows separating properties, and farmers were paid to plant and cultivate them.

e5a526df4968.title: Great Plains Shelterbelt
e5a526df4968.sentence: Oklahoma's first State Forester, George R. Phillips, had the distinction of planting the very first tree in the federal program's very first shelterbelt in 1935.

8500de8ece3a.title: Great Plains Shelterbelt
8500de8ece3a.sentence: The first tree was an Austrian pine planted on the H.E. Curtis farm near Willow, Oklahoma, on March 18.

03ff06eb038f.title: Great Plains Shelterbelt
03ff06eb038f.sentence: When disputes arose over funding sources (the project was considered to be a long-term strategy and therefore ineligible for emergency relief funds), FDR transferred the program to the Works Progress Administration (WPA).

835be07291d2.title: Great Plains Shelterbelt
835be07291d2.sentence: The U.S. Forest Service and Civilian Conservation Corps assisted.

b98378d87eb2.title: Great Plains Shelterbelt
b98378d87eb2.sentence: As of 2010^, "Many shelterbelts in Kansas and throughout the central Great Plains are old and are no longer providing the benefits that they used to", according to Kansas State Forester Larry Biles.

2ab6ee5655b4.title: Great Plains Shelterbelt
2ab6ee5655b4.sentence: > Today, the growth and vigor of many of the trees has declined due to close spacing, age, and invasion of undesirable, short-lived trees.

f6c29365dcba.title: Great Plains Shelterbelt
f6c29365dcba.sentence: In 2010, federal grants were made available for shelterbelt maintenance and restoration in Kansas, North Dakota, South Dakota, and Nebraska as part of the Central Great Plains Shelterbelt Renovation and the Central Great Plains Forested Riparian Buffer CCPI proposals.

db8c29fec3e4.title: Check dam
db8c29fec3e4.sentence: A check dam is a small, sometimes temporary, dam constructed across a swale, drainage ditch, or waterway to counteract erosion by reducing water flow velocity.

23d094eb0a85.title: Check dam
23d094eb0a85.sentence: A check dam placed in a ditch, swale, or channel interrupts the flow of water and flattens the gradient of the channel, thereby reducing the velocity.

538f211bd342.title: Check dam
538f211bd342.sentence: In turn, this obstruction induces infiltration and reduces erosion.

be080568f786.title: Check dam
be080568f786.sentence: Although some sedimentation may result behind the dam, check dams do not primarily function as sediment-trapping devices.

083d75a99da2.title: Check dam
083d75a99da2.sentence: Coarse and medium-grained sediment from runoff tends to be deposited behind check dams, while finer grains flow through.

f9fb2bff7fa6.title: Check dam
f9fb2bff7fa6.sentence: In arid areas, check dams are often built to increase groundwater recharge in a process called managed aquifer recharge.

ac5d64b78912.title: Check dam
ac5d64b78912.sentence: Because they are typically used as temporary structures, they are often made of cheap and accessible materials such as rocks, gravel, logs, hay bales, and sandbags.

d9a8c0b5da9a.title: Check dam
d9a8c0b5da9a.sentence: Check dams are usually less than 2 to 3 feet (0.61 to 0.91 m) high. and the center of the dam should be at least 6 in (0.15 m) lower than its edges.

87d602ce4f12.title: Catch crop
87d602ce4f12.sentence: In agriculture, a catch crop is a fast-growing crop that is grown between successive plantings of a main crop.

4f287ff6417d.title: Catch crop
4f287ff6417d.sentence: It is a specific type of cover crop that is grown between two main crops.

b2b7d1ef11b6.title: Cover crop
b2b7d1ef11b6.sentence: Catch crops are typically fast-growing annual cereal species adapted to scavenge available nitrogen efficiently from the soil.

8af90f64a94f.title: Cover crop
8af90f64a94f.sentence: As well as bringing nitrogen into agroecosystems through biological nitrogen fixation, types of cover crops known as "catch crops" are used to retain and recycle soil nitrogen already present.

d287b62b4f59.title: Cover crop
d287b62b4f59.sentence: The nitrogen fixed in catch crop biomass is released back into the soil once the cash crop is incorporated as a green manure or otherwise begins to decompose.

dbd107008ad9.title: Catch crop
dbd107008ad9.sentence: Catch crops help protect soil against water erosion through its residue which increases soil roughness.

25fc2a0f1af0.title: Catch crop
25fc2a0f1af0.sentence: The residue serves as a soil surface protection from splash effects as well contributes to lowering the surface runoff.

f212d2be5299.title: Catch crop
f212d2be5299.sentence: Certain catch crop species are also able to create biopores by decaying roots which create flow paths in the soil causing an increase of water infiltration.

abe7794b31d9.title: Catch crop
abe7794b31d9.sentence: Those factors include harvesting date, soil tillage, and sow timing being the most crucial.

e6ea572ce80d.title: Catch crop
e6ea572ce80d.sentence: When timing of sowing is postponed from the date that was recommended a decrease of catch crop efficiency, growth and over performance occurs where studies have shown a decrease uptake of N.

e757a36ffbd6.title: Soil stabilization
e757a36ffbd6.sentence: Road departments and private industry may apply liquid or powdered magnesium chloride to control dust and erosion on unimproved (dirt or gravel) roads and dusty job sites such as quarries because it is relatively inexpensive to purchase and apply.

59ee8dd2f11d.title: Soil stabilization
59ee8dd2f11d.sentence: Its hygroscopy makes it absorb moisture from the air, limiting the number of smaller particles (silts and clays) that become airborne.

388d816f8fab.title: Soil stabilization
388d816f8fab.sentence: - Absorbing water from the air at 32% relative humidity, almost independent of temperature

e9e188602739.title: Soil stabilization
e9e188602739.sentence: As a road stabilizer, magnesium chloride binds gravel and clay particles to keep them from leaving the road.

7480c88a5911.title: Soil stabilization
7480c88a5911.sentence: The water-absorbing (hygroscopic) characteristics of magnesium chloride prevent the road from drying out, which keeps gravel on the ground.

a40d46767741.title: Soil stabilization
a40d46767741.sentence: To control or mitigate dust, chlorides need moisture to work effectively so it works better in humid than in arid climates.

328dfceab78f.title: Soil stabilization
328dfceab78f.sentence: The most significant benefit of applying dust control products is the reduction in gravel road maintenance costs.

3cb458f5f816.title: Soil stabilization
3cb458f5f816.sentence: The use of magnesium chloride on roads remains controversial.

57e89bf412de.title: Soil stabilization
57e89bf412de.sentence: Advocates claim that it produces cleaner air, which leads to better health as fugitive dust can cause health problems in the young, elderly, and people with respiratory conditions; and greater safety through improved road conditions, including increased driver visibility and decreased risks caused by loose gravel, soft spots, road roughness, and flying rocks.

f21d4f9796f0.title: Soil stabilization
f21d4f9796f0.sentence: The salts, when used on road surfaces, will dissolve during wet weather and be transported into the groundwater through infiltration and/or runoff into surface water bodies.

f6382a445fcc.title: Soil stabilization
f6382a445fcc.sentence: Groundwater infiltration can be a problem and the chloride ion in drinking water is considered a problem when concentrations exceed 250 mg/L. It is therefore regulated by the United States' EPA's drinking water standards.

571658864772.title: Soil stabilization
571658864772.sentence: As far as plants and vegetation are concerned, the accumulation of salts in the soil adversely affects their physiology and morphology by increasing the osmotic pressure of the soil solution, altering the plant's mineral nutrition, and accumulating specific ions to toxic concentrations in the plants.

d691d7131ad9.title: Soil stabilization
d691d7131ad9.sentence: Soil can also be stabilized mechanically with stabilization geosynthetics; for example, geogrids or geocells, a 3D mechanical soil stabilization technique.

39b689ff4fc7.title: Soil stabilization
39b689ff4fc7.sentence: Stabilization is achieved via the confinement of particle movement to improve the strength of the entire layer.

343d8ab33dc1.title: Soil stabilization
343d8ab33dc1.sentence: Confinement in geogrids is by means of interlock between the aggregate and grid (and tensioned membrane), and in geocells, by cell wall confinement (hoop) stress on the aggregate.

8d7eef06d1da.title: Soil stabilization
8d7eef06d1da.sentence: Full-scale field investigations on forest roads in Sweden have shown that geocell-reinforced sections can significantly increase bearing capacity and reduce permanent surface deformation under repeated traffic loading compared with conventional unreinforced road structures.

12e077ce9d5a.title: Soil stabilization
12e077ce9d5a.sentence: The study further demonstrated that locally sourced infill materials used within geocell systems may provide performance comparable to or better than imported crushed aggregates, indicating potential reductions in material demand, transport requirements, and environmental impact for low-volume road construction.

9755e229e08c.title: Soil stabilization
9755e229e08c.sentence: Improved drainage techniques have also been used as a stabilization approach by reducing excess pore water and enhancing load-bearing capacity.

f5759eaf9384.title: Soil stabilization
f5759eaf9384.sentence: Methods such as the use of stone mattresses have been shown to improve structural performance of unpaved and forest roads by facilitating drainage and distributing loads more effectively under traffic conditions.

fa365f51e68f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.04%3A_Addressing_Runoff_and_Erosion
fa365f51e68f.sentence: The numerous methods of controlling soil and water can be grouped into two general approaches: structural measures and agronomic practices.

447a62ead924.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.04%3A_Addressing_Runoff_and_Erosion
447a62ead924.sentence: Creating structures for reducing erosion generally involves engineering practices, in which an initial investment is made to build terraces, diversion ditches, drop structures, etc. Agronomic practices focus on changes in soil and crop management and on using vegetative solutions, such as reduced tillage, cover cropping and planting vegetation in critical areas.

7d53bd67f23e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.04%3A_Addressing_Runoff_and_Erosion
7d53bd67f23e.sentence: - Structures generally focus on containing runoff and sediment once erosion has been initiated, i.e., they trap sediment that has already eroded.

a43cef1cb496.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.04%3A_Addressing_Runoff_and_Erosion
a43cef1cb496.sentence: Conversely, agronomic measures try to prevent erosion from occurring in the first place by decreasing runoff potential.

4919791e920a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.04%3A_Addressing_Runoff_and_Erosion
4919791e920a.sentence: - Structures are often more expensive to build and maintain (with significant upfront expense) than are agronomic measures, while they also tend to be less effective.

7ba3cdbde103.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.04%3A_Addressing_Runoff_and_Erosion
7ba3cdbde103.sentence: Therefore, the use of soil-building conservation management practices is preferred for long-term sustainability of crop production, and they are also the first choice for controlling runoff and erosion.

c5ac6ee0ceca.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.04%3A_Addressing_Runoff_and_Erosion
c5ac6ee0ceca.sentence: Structural measures still have a place but are primarily to complement agronomic measures.

975e15e11bc3.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.04%3A_Addressing_Runoff_and_Erosion
975e15e11bc3.sentence: - Agronomic measures help control erosion while also improving soil health and crop productivity.

be9a194a3725.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.04%3A_Addressing_Runoff_and_Erosion
be9a194a3725.sentence: - Significant advances have been made in farm machinery and methodologies for conservation tillage systems that make use of crop rotations and cover crops.

81a30cafa11a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.04%3A_Addressing_Runoff_and_Erosion
81a30cafa11a.sentence: Appropriate conservation methods may vary among fields and farms, but recently there has been a clear trend away from structural measures in favor of agronomic practices.

3c0948cfbe0f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.04%3A_Addressing_Runoff_and_Erosion
3c0948cfbe0f.sentence: Erosion reduction works by either decreasing the shear forces of water and wind or by keeping soil in a condition in which it can’t easily erode.

57db125d0f31.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.04%3A_Addressing_Runoff_and_Erosion
57db125d0f31.sentence: Many conservation practices actually reduce erosion by using both approaches.

f8a21d571608.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.03%3A_Off-Site_Effects
f8a21d571608.sentence: The soil removed from fields also has significant negative effects off the farm, as sediment accumulates in streams, rivers, reservoirs and estuaries, or blowing dust reaches towns and cities.

987158096741.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.03%3A_Off-Site_Effects
987158096741.sentence: In fact, sediment remains the No. 1 contaminant for most waters around the world, and it often also carries other pollutants like nutrients, pesticides and other chemicals.

696e1861fce7.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.03%3A_Off-Site_Effects
696e1861fce7.sentence: From a purely economic perspective, the off-site costs of soil erosion affecting fisheries, recreation and industry can be greater than the lost agricultural productivity, especially if the receiving waters are used by many people.

2d7a6cc7b988.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.03%3A_Off-Site_Effects
2d7a6cc7b988.sentence: Many conservationists argue that any amount of erosion is unacceptable, even when losses are less than T. This is a good point, as small amounts of soil can have an outsize impact on water and air quality, meaning that soil losses less than T may be tolerable in terms of agricultural productivity but not in terms of environmental quality.

3a18ba714df0.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.03%3A_Off-Site_Effects
3a18ba714df0.sentence: This is especially the case when dealing with soils that are high in clay content, where the particles become suspended as colloids in runoff water.

36618c71e906.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.03%3A_Off-Site_Effects
36618c71e906.sentence: The particles do not settle out in ponds or filter strips and can be transported long distances from the source, along with nutrients and pesticides (Figure 6.2, right photo).

abbe52423ead.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.03%3A_Off-Site_Effects
abbe52423ead.sentence: Similarly, clay and silt particles suspended in the air can be transported long distances and can cause respiratory problems.

ba5a5fcca63c.title: Prairie strips
ba5a5fcca63c.sentence: Prairie strips are strips of native perennial vegetation that are strategically integrated into row crop fields.

4139a833e07a.title: Prairie strips
4139a833e07a.sentence: This technique is used in conservation farming to improve biodiversity, and protect soil and water.

0b90ec5a6e47.title: Prairie strips
0b90ec5a6e47.sentence: 10% of a corn field set aside for native vegetation can reduce sediment movement by 95%.

0e8ecca2e26c.title: Prairie strips
0e8ecca2e26c.sentence: Phosphorus and nitrogen lost through run off are reduced by 90% and 85% respectively.

69f6803fa8e4.title: Prairie strips
69f6803fa8e4.sentence: Native prairie vegetation improves soil stability, reduces soil erosion and nutrient runoff, and concentrates more organic carbon in soil than corn and soybean crops.

ec691faf03c4.title: Prairie strips
ec691faf03c4.sentence: Farmers can take odd areas or difficult-to-farm areas out of production as they integrate native plant species into farm fields as contour buffers and edge-of-field filters.

07702f09b75b.title: Prairie strips
07702f09b75b.sentence: They found that prairie strips supported twice the number of aphid-eating insects than soybean fields.

8a45591b3b43.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.04%3A_Addressing_Runoff_and_Erosion
8a45591b3b43.sentence: - Keep the soil covered: water and wind erosion occur almost exclusively when the soil is exposed.

5026054cc6bd.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.04%3A_Addressing_Runoff_and_Erosion
5026054cc6bd.sentence: Live plants are the best way to protect the soil and to stimulate soil health.

78e98e0ee4ce.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.04%3A_Addressing_Runoff_and_Erosion
78e98e0ee4ce.sentence: - Use management practices that increase aggregation and infiltration.

d95a5cde759d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.04%3A_Addressing_Runoff_and_Erosion
d95a5cde759d.sentence: - Do not disturb the soil unless it is well covered.

82b86600e69c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.04%3A_Addressing_Runoff_and_Erosion
82b86600e69c.sentence: Loose, exposed soil is more erodible than stable soil, like in no-till systems.

a08976096a37.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.04%3A_Addressing_Runoff_and_Erosion
a08976096a37.sentence: Loosening may initially reduce runoff potential, but this effect is generally short lived, as the soil will settle.

3be3983fa126.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.04%3A_Addressing_Runoff_and_Erosion
3be3983fa126.sentence: Focus on areas with high risk—those where runoff water concentrates—and maximize the use of inexpensive biological approaches like grass seeding in waterways and filter strips.

93e8bb9e7573.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.04%3A_Addressing_Runoff_and_Erosion
93e8bb9e7573.sentence: For example, in temperate areas the soil is most susceptible after the winter fallow, and in semiarid regions it is most fragile after the dry period when heavy rains begin and there is little surface cover.

fbe35f744210.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.04%3A_Addressing_Runoff_and_Erosion
fbe35f744210.sentence: - Evaluate whether areas of erodible land are better taken out of production.

8c859ebfe672.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.04%3A_Addressing_Runoff_and_Erosion
8c859ebfe672.sentence: If these areas are not profitable, more benefit is gained from government payments as part of conservation reserve or set-aside programs.

c61bd313939d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.04%3A_Addressing_Runoff_and_Erosion
c61bd313939d.sentence: Transitioning to tillage systems that increase surface cover and reduce disturbance (Figure 14.3) is therefore the single most effective approach to reducing erosion.

ea7601401793.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.04%3A_Addressing_Runoff_and_Erosion
ea7601401793.sentence: Incidentally, reduced tillage also generally provides better economic returns than does conventional tillage.

964f59249232.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.04%3A_Addressing_Runoff_and_Erosion
964f59249232.sentence: Leaving a rougher soil surface by eliminating secondary tillage passes and packers that crush natural soil aggregates saves considerable labor time and wear and tear on machinery.

f2c7e77f8d55.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.04%3A_Addressing_Runoff_and_Erosion
f2c7e77f8d55.sentence: It also significantly reduces runoff and erosion losses by preventing aggregate dispersion and surface sealing from intense rainfall (see Figure 6.11).

fa2c059943ff.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.04%3A_Addressing_Runoff_and_Erosion
fa2c059943ff.sentence: For example, an Ohio experiment in which runoff from conventionally tilled and no-till continuous-corn fields was monitored showed that over a four-year period, runoff averaged about 7 inches of water each year for conventional tillage and less than 0.1 inch for the no-till planting system.

342ab8bbf376.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.04%3A_Addressing_Runoff_and_Erosion
342ab8bbf376.sentence: Reducing or eliminating tillage also diminishes tillage erosion and keeps soil from being moved downhill.

387335e10f79.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.04%3A_Addressing_Runoff_and_Erosion
387335e10f79.sentence: The gradual losses of soil from upslope areas expose subsoil and may in many cases further aggravate runoff and erosion.

3e39f8ee546f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.04%3A_Addressing_Runoff_and_Erosion
3e39f8ee546f.sentence: If tilling is required to reduce compaction, do it with tools that limit disturbance (e.g., zone builders or strip tillers).

145a67fa8ec4.title: Bioretention
145a67fa8ec4.sentence: Bioretention is the process in which contaminants and sedimentation are removed from stormwater runoff.

27b07ff2d94d.title: Bioretention
27b07ff2d94d.sentence: The term "Bioretention" refers to the fact that the biomass in the treatment media, such as plants and bacteria, retains, absorbs, breaks down, and cycles contaminants found in runoff.

ec3d5deb4f0b.title: Bioretention
ec3d5deb4f0b.sentence: Stormwater is firstly directed into the designed treatment area, which conventionally consists of a sand bed (which serves as a transition to the actual soil), a filter media layer (which consists of layered materials of various composition), and plants atop the filter media.

17d66c7d8a42.title: Bioretention
17d66c7d8a42.sentence: Stored water in the bioretention area planting soil exfiltrates over a period of days into the underlying soils.

6b4a0feea7b5.title: Bioretention
6b4a0feea7b5.sentence: Filtration, adsorption, chemical transformation, and biological degradation are the main methods of pollutant treatment in bioretention.

df29e8ee62aa.title: Bioretention
df29e8ee62aa.sentence: The clay in the planting soil provides adsorption sites for hydrocarbons, heavy metals, nutrients and other pollutants.

88ce8ab81ae5.title: Bioretention
88ce8ab81ae5.sentence: Sites with loamy sand soils are especially appropriate for bioretention because the excavated soil can be backfilled and used as the planting soil, thus eliminating the cost of importing planting soil.

b7486e6d259d.title: Bioretention
b7486e6d259d.sentence: An unstable surrounding soil stratum and soils with a clay content greater than 25 percent may preclude the use of bioretention, as would a site with slopes greater than 20 percent or a site with mature trees that would be removed during construction of the best management practices.

48c87ca63adc.title: Bioretention
48c87ca63adc.sentence: In laboratory experiments, bioretention cells removed 94%, 88%, 95%, and >95% of zinc, copper, lead, and cadmium, respectively from water with metal concentrations typical of stormwater runoff.

c6ab15ca93bb.title: Bioretention
c6ab15ca93bb.sentence: While this is a great benefit for water quality improvement, bioretention systems have a finite capacity for heavy metal removal.

27175d013bff.title: Bioretention
27175d013bff.sentence: Therefore, removal and replacement of the bioretention layer will become necessary in areas with heavy metal pollutants in stormwater runoff to extend the life of the treatment system.

63a82e18b56a.title: Buffer strip
63a82e18b56a.sentence: Contour buffer strips are strips of perennial vegetation alternated with wider cultivated strips of cropland.

d38ebe6b8c26.title: Buffer strip
d38ebe6b8c26.sentence: This type of buffer strip is most effective when runoff water enters uniformly as sheetflow.

e0d77e9c9d0d.title: Buffer strip
e0d77e9c9d0d.sentence: They are very adapted to trapping pesticides and reducing rill erosion.

be9e7a264e7a.title: Buffer strip
be9e7a264e7a.sentence: These buffers need to be at least 15 feet (4.6 m) wide and make up for 20 to 30 percent of slope of an area.

a3c6c754c068.title: Buffer strip
a3c6c754c068.sentence: A lot of the time contour buffers can be used as a very inexpensive substitute for terraces.

c830d35ce133.title: Buffer strip
c830d35ce133.sentence: Vegetative barriers are narrower buffer strips of hardy, native, perennial grasses or shrubs planted in parallel rows to crops.

ee2c780bc0ae.title: Buffer strip
ee2c780bc0ae.sentence: They are very effective in reducing wind and water erosion which results in sediment trapping and water infiltration.

aa432f994bfc.title: Buffer strip
aa432f994bfc.sentence: They function in a similar fashion to a contour buffer strip, just much narrower.

9b53563d005b.title: Buffer strip
9b53563d005b.sentence: These strips are very important in protecting stream banks and water quality.

073c6f37cd89.title: Buffer strip
073c6f37cd89.sentence: Field borders are bands or strips of perennial vegetation that is found on the edge of a cropland field.

f86da038b08c.title: Buffer strip
f86da038b08c.sentence: Field borders help with runoff only when it flows over the strip.

8c64f7c36f47.title: Buffer strip
8c64f7c36f47.sentence: Field borders are effective in reducing wind and water erosion and provide great wildlife habitat.

f791ee48f028.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.01%3A_Introduction
f791ee48f028.section: Erosion Is A Natural Process, But...
f791ee48f028.sentence: Erosion of rock and soil is a natural process that over the eons has caused the lowering of mountains and the formation of river valleys and deltas.

afab1fc36632.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.01%3A_Introduction
afab1fc36632.section: Erosion Is A Natural Process, But...
afab1fc36632.sentence: The problem in agricultural soils is greatly accelerated erosion that is especially severe when the soil is bare, unprotected by living plants, their roots or residue mulch.

f7eff3cf60cb.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.01%3A_Introduction
f7eff3cf60cb.section: Erosion Is A Natural Process, But...
f7eff3cf60cb.sentence: And natural erosion is going on all the time as water, ice and wind have their effects on rock and soil.

5e32dac0dea0.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.01%3A_Introduction
5e32dac0dea0.section: Erosion Is A Natural Process, But...
5e32dac0dea0.sentence: One dramatic example of such erosion is the dust picked up by winds just south of Africa’s Sahara Desert—the Sahel region of transition from desert to savannah—traveling some 3,000 miles to South America and the Caribbean, and occasionally reaching the southeastern United States.

a3750fa3bde5.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.01%3A_Introduction
a3750fa3bde5.section: Erosion Is A Natural Process, But...
a3750fa3bde5.sentence: This dust is thought to be a major source of phosphorus for the Amazon River basin, balancing losses that occur there.

012da72ea33c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.01%3A_Introduction
012da72ea33c.section: Erosion Is A Natural Process, But...
012da72ea33c.sentence: Also, breaking up of soil aggregates with tillage lessens rainfall infiltration into soil, which worsens runoff and erosion.

7c51edc9e1e9.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.01%3A_Introduction
7c51edc9e1e9.section: Erosion Is A Natural Process, But...
7c51edc9e1e9.sentence: Intense or prolonged rainstorms are major causes of water erosion and landslides, while drought and strong winds are critical factors in wind erosion.

4a4196636811.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.01%3A_Introduction
4a4196636811.section: Erosion Is A Natural Process, But...
4a4196636811.sentence: In Chapter 6 we discussed how some soils (especially silts) with poor aggregation are more susceptible than other soils, especially those with good aggregation.

04b11bf4f186.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.01%3A_Introduction
04b11bf4f186.section: Erosion Is A Natural Process, But...
04b11bf4f186.sentence: This is reflected in the soil erodibility ratings, which soil conservationists use to plan control practices.

f353a5be140e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.05%3A_Other_Practices_and_Structures_for_Soil_Conservation
f353a5be140e.sentence: For example, diversion ditches are channels or swales that are constructed across slopes to divert water across the slope to a waterway or pond (Figure 14.7).

120180ea565c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.05%3A_Other_Practices_and_Structures_for_Soil_Conservation
120180ea565c.sentence: Their primary purpose is to channel water away from upslope areas and prevent the downslope accumulation and concentration of runoff water that would then generate scouring and gullies.

3134e41565cf.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.05%3A_Other_Practices_and_Structures_for_Soil_Conservation
3134e41565cf.sentence: A narrow filter strip is located on the upslope edge to remove sediment.

3e92fba5d2af.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.05%3A_Other_Practices_and_Structures_for_Soil_Conservation
3e92fba5d2af.sentence: Finally, a few words about landslides.

1077c3914f99.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.05%3A_Other_Practices_and_Structures_for_Soil_Conservation
1077c3914f99.sentence: They are difficult to control, and unstable steep slopes are therefore best left in forest cover.

32a4b2217232.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.05%3A_Other_Practices_and_Structures_for_Soil_Conservation
32a4b2217232.sentence: A compromise solution is the use of wide-spaced trees that allow for some soil stabilization by roots but that leave enough sunlight for a pasture or crops (Figure 14.12), a form of silviculture we also discussed in Chapter 11.

ed356f854a3d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.05%3A_Other_Practices_and_Structures_for_Soil_Conservation
ed356f854a3d.sentence: Figure 14.12.(Right) An experiment with wide-spaced poplar trees planted in a New Zealand pasture to reduce landslide risk.

50f146ed471b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.05%3A_Other_Practices_and_Structures_for_Soil_Conservation
50f146ed471b.sentence: In some cases, horizontal drains are installed in critical zones to allow dewatering and to prevent supersaturation during prolonged rains.

81f1fae3f746.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.05%3A_Other_Practices_and_Structures_for_Soil_Conservation
81f1fae3f746.sentence: But these are expensive to install and are more commonly used in urban areas and along roads where landslides on steep slopes are great hazards.

ada21022d1d6.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.05%3A_Other_Practices_and_Structures_for_Soil_Conservation
ada21022d1d6.sentence: Wind erosion is reduced with most of the same practices that control water erosion by keeping the soil covered and increasing aggregation: reduced tillage or no-till, cover cropping and perennial rotation crops.

7118d760f915.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.05%3A_Other_Practices_and_Structures_for_Soil_Conservation
7118d760f915.sentence: In addition, practices that increase the roughness of the soil surface diminish the effects of wind erosion.

88afd281a8aa.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.05%3A_Other_Practices_and_Structures_for_Soil_Conservation
88afd281a8aa.sentence: The rougher surface increases turbulent air movement near the land surface and reduces the wind’s shear and ability to sweep soil material into the air.

9aaf716ad5e6.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.05%3A_Other_Practices_and_Structures_for_Soil_Conservation
9aaf716ad5e6.sentence: Therefore, if fields are tilled and cover crops are not used, it makes sense to leave soil in a rough-tilled state when crops aren’t growing.

e1f6e27074da.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.05%3A_Other_Practices_and_Structures_for_Soil_Conservation
e1f6e27074da.sentence: Also, tree shelterbelts planted at regular distances perpendicular to the main wind direction act as windbreaks and help reduce evaporative demand from dry winds (Figure 14.11).

2455f1f28616.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.05%3A_Other_Practices_and_Structures_for_Soil_Conservation
2455f1f28616.sentence: They have recently received new attention as ecological corridors in agricultural landscapes that help increase biodiversity and may fit with the principles of alley cropping (Chapter 11).

d1046b9ccda1.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.04%3A_Addressing_Runoff_and_Erosion
d1046b9ccda1.sentence: Cover crops frequently can be grown during seasons when the soil is especially susceptible to erosion, such as the winter and early spring in temperate climates, or early dry seasons in semiarid climates.

1660de42f7f3.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.04%3A_Addressing_Runoff_and_Erosion
1660de42f7f3.sentence: They add organic residues to the soil and help maintain soil aggregation and levels of organic matter.

f87ec89479b4.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.04%3A_Addressing_Runoff_and_Erosion
f87ec89479b4.sentence: Their roots help to bind soil and hold it in place.

81551b8897f9.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.04%3A_Addressing_Runoff_and_Erosion
81551b8897f9.sentence: Because raindrops lose most of their energy when they hit leaves and drip to the ground, less soil crusting occurs.

8c474d95731a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.04%3A_Addressing_Runoff_and_Erosion
8c474d95731a.sentence: Cover crops are especially effective at reducing erosion if they are cut and mulched or rolled and crimped, rather than incorporated.

6ee5b33b3e5b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.04%3A_Addressing_Runoff_and_Erosion
6ee5b33b3e5b.sentence: Ideally, this is done when the cover crop has nearly matured (typically, milk stage)—that is, when it is somewhat lignified but seeds are not yet viable and C:N ratios are not so high as to cause nutrient immobilization.

dea3d4a4c5bb.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.04%3A_Addressing_Runoff_and_Erosion
dea3d4a4c5bb.sentence: In recent years, new methods of cover cropping, mulching and no-tillage crop production, often jointly referred to as conservation agriculture, have been worked out by innovative farmers in several regions of the world (Figure 14.4; see also the farmer case study at the end of this chapter).

a61c6138e906.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.04%3A_Addressing_Runoff_and_Erosion
a61c6138e906.sentence: This practice has revolutionized farming in parts of temperate South America, with rapid and widespread adoption in recent years.

c61c06d476a0.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.04%3A_Addressing_Runoff_and_Erosion
c61c06d476a0.sentence: It has been shown to virtually eliminate runoff and erosion, and also appears to have great benefits for moisture conservation, nitrogen cycling, weed control, reduced fuel consumption and time savings, which altogether can result in significant increases in farm profitability.

540c0a89cd19.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.04%3A_Addressing_Runoff_and_Erosion
540c0a89cd19.sentence: Maintaining good soil organic matter levels helps keep topsoil in place.

3c12c800b9fc.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.04%3A_Addressing_Runoff_and_Erosion
3c12c800b9fc.sentence: A soil with more organic matter usually has better soil aggregation and less surface sealing/crusting.

46a2aa7f7c8a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.04%3A_Addressing_Runoff_and_Erosion
46a2aa7f7c8a.sentence: These conditions ensure that more water is able to infiltrate the soil instead of running off the field, taking soil with it.

1676a147ff70.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.04%3A_Addressing_Runoff_and_Erosion
1676a147ff70.sentence: Reduced tillage and the use of cover crops already help build organic matter levels, but regularly providing additional organic materials like compost or manure stimulates earthworm activity and results in larger and more stable soil aggregates.

a1da36864733.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.04%3A_Addressing_Runoff_and_Erosion
a1da36864733.sentence: Direct injection of liquid organic materials in a zone-till or no-till system is a recent approach that allows for reduced soil disturbance and minimal concerns about manure runoff and odor problems (Figure 14.6).

256b47d0d025.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.04%3A_Addressing_Runoff_and_Erosion
256b47d0d025.sentence: Grass and legume forage crops can help lessen erosion because they maintain a cover on most of the soil surface for the whole year.

3b025ae15a98.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.04%3A_Addressing_Runoff_and_Erosion
3b025ae15a98.sentence: Their extensive root systems hold soil in place.

113d55d2e358.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.04%3A_Addressing_Runoff_and_Erosion
113d55d2e358.sentence: When they are rotated with annual row crops, the increased soil health helps maintain lower erosion and runoff rates during that part of the crop cycle.

0bd4dc26e625.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.04%3A_Addressing_Runoff_and_Erosion
0bd4dc26e625.sentence: In such a system, strips of perennial sod crops and row crops are laid out across the slope, and erosion from the row crop is filtered out when the water reaches the sod strip.

4e856d2316b4.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.04%3A_Addressing_Runoff_and_Erosion
4e856d2316b4.sentence: Each crop may be grown for two to five years on a strip, which is then rotated into the other crop.

3993f87cdb4e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.04%3A_Addressing_Runoff_and_Erosion
3993f87cdb4e.sentence: Researchers in the state of Washington found that erosion on winter wheat fields was about 4 tons per acre each year when a sod crop was included in the rotation, compared to about 15 tons when it was not included.

c2b176730c65.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.04%3A_Addressing_Runoff_and_Erosion
c2b176730c65.sentence: Permanent sod, as hayland or pasture, is a good choice for steep soils or other soils that erode easily, although slumping and landslides may become a concern with extremely steep slopes.

ec4148892afb.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.04%3A_Addressing_Runoff_and_Erosion
ec4148892afb.section: Significance of Plant Residues and Competing Uses
ec4148892afb.sentence: Surface residues are important because they intercept raindrops and can slow down water running over the surface.

396697a7cefe.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.04%3A_Addressing_Runoff_and_Erosion
396697a7cefe.section: Significance of Plant Residues and Competing Uses
396697a7cefe.sentence: The amount of residue on the surface may be less than 5% for the moldboard plow, while continuous no-till planting may leave 90% or more of the surface covered by crop residues.

e2353fcd4b64.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.04%3A_Addressing_Runoff_and_Erosion
e2353fcd4b64.section: Significance of Plant Residues and Competing Uses
e2353fcd4b64.sentence: Other reduced tillage systems, such as chiseling and disking (as a primary tillage operation), typically leave more than 30% of the surface covered by crop residues.

ce9c097954b2.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.04%3A_Addressing_Runoff_and_Erosion
ce9c097954b2.section: Significance of Plant Residues and Competing Uses
ce9c097954b2.sentence: Research has shown that 100% soil cover virtually eliminates runoff and erosion on most agricultural lands.

b88c8f2fb533.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.04%3A_Addressing_Runoff_and_Erosion
b88c8f2fb533.section: Significance of Plant Residues and Competing Uses
b88c8f2fb533.sentence: Even 30% soil cover reduces erosion by 70%.

b3eb2b234816.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.04%3A_Addressing_Runoff_and_Erosion
b3eb2b234816.section: Significance of Plant Residues and Competing Uses
b3eb2b234816.sentence: As discussed in Chapter 9, there are many competing uses for crop residues as fuel sources, as well as building materials.

87846d2ef55e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.04%3A_Addressing_Runoff_and_Erosion
87846d2ef55e.section: Significance of Plant Residues and Competing Uses
87846d2ef55e.sentence: Unfortunately, permanent removal of large quantities of crop residues will have a detrimental effect on soil health and on the soil’s ability to withstand water and wind erosion, especially when there is no return of organic materials as manure.

fbde05113d9e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.03%3A_Off-Site_Effects
fbde05113d9e.sentence: It’s difficult to fully appreciate erosion’s damage potential because the most severe erosion occurs during rare weather events and climate anomalies.

16fe8ed56ace.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.03%3A_Off-Site_Effects
16fe8ed56ace.sentence: And about one-third of the water erosion damage that occurs in a particular field during a 30 year period commonly results from a single extreme rainfall event.

a760cd5650d9.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/14%3A_Reducing_Runoff_and_Erosion/14.03%3A_Off-Site_Effects
a760cd5650d9.sentence: Wind erosion during the Dust Bowl days of the 1930s, which resulted from a decade of extremely dry years, was especially damaging.

75091e3e3a33.title: Vetiver System
75091e3e3a33.sentence: The Vetiver System (VS) is a system of soil and water conservation whose main component is the use of the vetiver plant in hedgerows.

b37a3bcc1a10.title: Vetiver System
b37a3bcc1a10.sentence: When Vetiver is planted as a hedgerow across a slope, it forms a dense vegetative barrier that slows and spreads rainfall runoff.

8a7b26cf95e5.title: Vetiver System
8a7b26cf95e5.sentence: A hedgerow stays where it is planted and the sediment that is spread out behind the hedgerow gradually accumulates to form a long-lasting terrace.

f27281ab723a.title: Vetiver System
f27281ab723a.sentence: Its massive, finely structured root system can grow fast - in some applications, rooting depth can reach 10–12 ft (3–4 m) in the first year.

08b96a27fcc3.title: Vetiver System
08b96a27fcc3.sentence: Combined with a deep and strong root system, a wide range of pH tolerance (from about pH 3 to pH 11), a high tolerance to most heavy metals, an ability to remove from soil and water large quantities of nitrates, phosphates and farm chemicals, the vetiver plant can be used for soil and water conservation, engineered construction site stabilization, pollution control (constructed wetlands), and other uses where soil and water come together.

047cfd896d9a.title: Vetiver System
047cfd896d9a.sentence: A good hedge reduces rainfall runoff by as much as 70% and sediment by as much as 90%.

b3daf4dc4fae.title: Vetiver System
b3daf4dc4fae.sentence: The Vetiver System is used in more than 100 countries for soil and water conservation, infrastructure stabilization, pollution control, waste water treatment, mitigation and rehabilitation, sediment control, prevention of storm damage and other environmental protection applications (through bioengineering and phytoremediation).

bf6bd823a951.title: Soil survey
bf6bd823a951.sentence: Soil survey, or soil mapping, is the process of classifying soil types and other soil properties in a given area and geo-encoding such information.

4186a0e11659.title: Soil survey
4186a0e11659.sentence: Soil surveys apply the principles of soil science and draw heavily from geomorphology, theories of soil formation, physical geography, and analysis of vegetation and land use patterns.

91d92587ccc5.title: Soil survey
91d92587ccc5.sentence: Primary data for the soil survey are acquired by field sampling and by remote sensing.

315dd1abbe42.title: Soil survey
315dd1abbe42.sentence: Remote sensing principally uses aerial photography, but LiDAR and other digital techniques are steadily gaining in popularity.

43ce506f19d6.title: Soil survey
43ce506f19d6.sentence: In the past, a soil scientist would take hard-copies of aerial photography, topographic maps, and mapping keys into the field with them.

221575a31058.title: Soil survey
221575a31058.sentence: Today, a growing number of soil scientists bring a ruggedized tablet computer and GPS into the field with them.

662a722da2fd.title: Soil survey
662a722da2fd.sentence: The tablet may be loaded with digital aerial photos, LiDAR, topography, soil geodatabases, mapping keys, and more.

310bbee01523.title: Soil survey
310bbee01523.sentence: In the United States, these surveys were once published in book form for individual counties by the National Cooperative Soil Survey.

034b342b7336.title: Soil survey
034b342b7336.sentence: In the past it could take years to publish a paper soil survey.

b418f62a74f2.title: Soil survey
b418f62a74f2.sentence: Today, soil surveys are no longer published in book form; they are published to the web and accessed on NRCS Web Soil Survey where a person can create a custom soil survey.

b9491b7c6506.title: Soil survey
b9491b7c6506.sentence: Today it takes only moments for changes to go live to the public.

e4eee5193ce0.title: Soil survey
e4eee5193ce0.sentence: Typical information in a published county soil survey includes the following:

3cbbc7938aea.title: Soil survey
3cbbc7938aea.sentence: - a general soil map for comparing the sustainability of large sections of the county

f7d008fd902d.title: Soil survey
f7d008fd902d.sentence: - a detailed map with specific soil series outlined and indexed

5f7b1d84040f.title: Soil survey
5f7b1d84040f.sentence: - a section on the use and management of soils

058ee78babc6.title: Soil survey
058ee78babc6.sentence: - tables containing land use suitability based on standards set by the Natural Resources Conservation Service.

8a3ca5ee35f3.title: Soil science
8a3ca5ee35f3.sentence: Along the second half of the 20th century soil mapping was currently achieved by field survey and reporting contours of soil types on geographic maps at varying scales according to countries and purposes.

a06b91f30ac6.title: Soil map
a06b91f30ac6.sentence: A soil map is a geographical representation showing diversity of soil types or soil properties (soil pH, textures, organic matter, depths of horizons etc.) in the area of interest.

22abd7129c1c.title: Soil map
22abd7129c1c.sentence: It is typically the result of a soil survey inventory, i.e. soil survey.

7647025fa16c.title: Soil map
7647025fa16c.sentence: Traditional soil maps typically show only general distribution of soils, accompanied by the soil survey report.

2c4e4d541787.title: Soil map
2c4e4d541787.sentence: Soil maps are most commonly used for land evaluation, spatial planning, agricultural extension, environmental protection and similar projects.

3ba7265aaa67.title: Soil map
3ba7265aaa67.sentence: Many new soil maps are derived using digital soil mapping techniques.

30b585ada97b.title: Soil map
30b585ada97b.sentence: Such maps are typically richer in context and show higher spatial detail, yet are not necessarily more accurate than traditional soil maps.

5e78934cb1ee.title: Soil map
5e78934cb1ee.sentence: Soil maps produced using (geo)statistical technique can also include an estimate of the model uncertainty.

fc66b2e615b8.title: Soil map
fc66b2e615b8.sentence: It is important to distinguish between the following types of soil maps:

d87f7ee9b9d7.title: Soil map
d87f7ee9b9d7.sentence: - hand-drawn soil polygon maps representing distribution of soil types;

af58f72ecff0.title: Soil map
af58f72ecff0.sentence: - simulated or predicted 2D/3D soil property maps (primary or secondary soil properties);

63f6df7a6785.title: Soil map
63f6df7a6785.sentence: One should also distinguish soil maps that display primary soil attributes, i.e. the soil attributes originally described or measured in the field, and the soil inferred attributes also called secondary soil information, i.e. the properties of the soils in the context of the soil use: soil production capacity, soil reaction to certain use, soil functions, soil degradation measures, etc.

2c1d38f033e4.title: Prime farmland
2c1d38f033e4.sentence: Prime farmland is a designation assigned by U.S. Department of Agriculture defining land that has the best combination of physical and chemical characteristics for producing food, feed, forage, fiber, and oilseed crops and is also available for these land uses.

96b764ee8eb0.title: Prime farmland
96b764ee8eb0.sentence: Prime farmland "has the soil quality, growing season, and moisture supply needed to produce economically sustained high yields of crops when treated and managed according to acceptable farming methods, including water management.".

9a674f4f2ae0.title: Prime farmland
9a674f4f2ae0.sentence: In general, prime farmlands have an adequate and dependable water supply from precipitation or irrigation, a favorable temperature and growing season, acceptable acidity or alkalinity, acceptable salt and sodium content, and few or no rocks.

33932da28ef0.title: Prime farmland
33932da28ef0.sentence: Prime farmlands are not excessively erodible or saturated with water for a long period of time, and they either do not flood frequently or are protected from flooding.

595facd3736f.title: Prime farmland
595facd3736f.sentence: Because many of today's major cities were historically founded in agriculturally rich areas, prime farmland tends to be (by virtue of its location) well suited to "growing" houses.

422e32f0165b.title: Prime farmland
422e32f0165b.sentence: USDA prime farmland designation helps growth management and resource conservation efforts in urban growth areas to use zoning and conservation easements in order to preserve prime farmland resources, maintain local economic diversity, and establish green belts.

21c06c813170.title: Prime farmland
21c06c813170.sentence: Other designations used by USDA to complement Prime Farmland are Farmland of statewide importance, Farmland of local importance, and Unique farmland.

9df420af136a.title: Prime farmland
9df420af136a.sentence: Unique farmland is land other than prime farmland that is used for the production of specific high value food and fiber crops.

bd4fa1a7c5ab.title: Prime farmland
bd4fa1a7c5ab.sentence: Examples of crops are tree nuts, olives, cranberries, citruses and other fruits, and vegetables.

517c24ac3f3e.title: Prime farmland
517c24ac3f3e.sentence: Criteria for defining and delineating these lands are determined by the appropriate state or local agencies in cooperation with USDA.

dd5c00e2516b.title: Prime farmland
dd5c00e2516b.sentence: A universal method for the demarcation of Prime Farmland (PF) soils that considers both science and policy is highly necessary, as when PF soils occupy < 60% of an area their preservation is hard.

855bab924236.title: Land use
855bab924236.sentence: Land use, land cover, or land use/land cover (LU/LC) is a description of what happens on a parcel of land.

42019c29d245.title: Land use
42019c29d245.sentence: It concerns the benefits derived from using the land, and also the land management actions that humans carry out there.

212fae84fba8.title: Land use
212fae84fba8.sentence: The IPCC defines the term land use as the "total of arrangements, activities and inputs applied to a parcel of land".

3a1ac6304d6e.title: Land use
3a1ac6304d6e.sentence: The same report groups land use into the following categories: forest land, cropland (agricultural land), grassland, wetlands, settlements and other lands.

106210f72a67.title: Land use
106210f72a67.sentence: Another definition is that of the United Nations' Food and Agriculture Organization: "Land use concerns the products and/or benefits obtained from use of the land as well as the land management actions (activities) carried out by humans to produce those products and benefits."

cfabae85ce29.title: Land use
