cfabae85ce29.sentence: Land use and land management practices have a major impact on natural resources including water, soil, nutrients, plants and animals.

ca2687344b57.title: Land use
ca2687344b57.sentence: Effects of land use choices and changes by humans include, for example, urban sprawl, soil erosion, soil degradation, land degradation and desertification.

7c83e6366092.title: Land use
7c83e6366092.sentence: As of 2015, the total arable land is 10.7% of the land surface, with 1.3% being permanent cropland.

28d7fcbffb4b.title: Land use
28d7fcbffb4b.sentence: As of the early 1990s, about 13% of the Earth was considered arable land, with 26% in pasture, 32% forests and woodland, and 1.5% urban areas.

5e59997f6cbc.title: Land use
5e59997f6cbc.sentence: Commonly, political jurisdictions will undertake land-use planning and regulate the use of land in an attempt to avoid land-use conflicts.

3f3bf1726d53.title: Land use
3f3bf1726d53.sentence: Land use plans are implemented through land division and use ordinances and regulations, such as zoning regulations.

2078ec8c0dac.title: Land use
2078ec8c0dac.sentence: The urban growth boundary is one form of land-use regulation.

26a9d801d93d.title: Remote sensing
26a9d801d93d.sentence: Remote sensing is the acquisition of information about an object or area from a distance, without touching it, as opposed to measuring it on-site observation.

903ca32ed1c2.title: Remote sensing
903ca32ed1c2.sentence: In current usage, the term remote sensing generally refers to the use of satellite- or airborne-based sensor technologies to detect and classify objects on Earth.

a298e4068ea7.title: Remote sensing
a298e4068ea7.sentence: It may be split into "active" remote sensing (when a signal is emitted by a sensor mounted on a satellite or aircraft to the object and its reflection is detected by the sensor) and "passive" remote sensing (when the reflection of sunlight is detected by the sensor).

35f47c18db54.title: Remote sensing
35f47c18db54.section: Data acquisition > Applications of remote sensing > Hydrology
35f47c18db54.sentence: Many of the variables constituting the terrestrial water balance, for example surface water storage, soil moisture, precipitation, evapotranspiration, and snow and ice, are measurable using remote sensing at various spatial-temporal resolutions and accuracies.

499ccb92dd35.title: Remote sensing
499ccb92dd35.section: Data acquisition > Applications of remote sensing > Aerial platforms and Satellites
499ccb92dd35.sentence: Maps of land cover and land use from thematic mapping can be used to prospect for minerals, detect or monitor land usage, detect invasive vegetation, deforestation, and examine the health of indigenous plants and crops (satellite crop monitoring), including entire farming regions or forests.

5426f5359f2f.title: Remote sensing
5426f5359f2f.section: Data acquisition > Applications of remote sensing > Hyperspectral Imaging
5426f5359f2f.sentence: Remote sensing is often utilized in the collection of agricultural and environmental statistics, usually combining classified satellite images with ground truth data collected on a sample selected on an area sampling frame.

09342e93b317.title: Remote sensing
09342e93b317.section: Data acquisition > Applications of remote sensing > Land Cover Statistics and Reference Data
09342e93b317.sentence: Ground truth or reference data to train and validate image classification require a field survey if we are targeting annual crops or individual forest species, but may be substituted by photointerpretation if we look at wider classes that can be reliably identified on aerial photos or satellite images.

cee643e4d8b9.title: Remote sensing
cee643e4d8b9.section: Data acquisition > Applications of remote sensing > Radar
cee643e4d8b9.sentence: Interferometric synthetic aperture radar is used to produce precise digital elevation models of large scale terrain (See RADARSAT, TerraSAR-X, Magellan).

7258f8b36c63.title: Soil value
7258f8b36c63.sentence: Soil value (German: Bodenwertzahl) or BWZ is a comparative assessment of soil quality used in Germany.

576463de8a82.title: Soil value
576463de8a82.sentence: It is determined from soil sampling data and ranges from 0 (very low) to 100 (very high).

1766d1335d2f.title: Soil value
1766d1335d2f.sentence: According to the Geological Service of the state of North Rhine-Westphalia, the soil value of arable land is based on a field assessment framework which combines an assessment of soil type, soil condition (soil development) and the parent material of which the soil is composed.

0869645d65d9.title: Soil value
0869645d65d9.sentence: The result, the soil value, expresses the relative net income that, under normal and proper management, is determined only by the profitability of the soil.

8e813fa5dd47.title: Soil value
8e813fa5dd47.sentence: Additions or deductions in this value to take account of variations in yield due to terrain and climate (e.g. average annual temperature) give the field value (Ackerzahl).

e09599d430f5.title: Soil value
e09599d430f5.sentence: Another measure, the field value (Ackerzahl), is derived from the soil value, taking account of other factors such as climate and location e.g. along the edge of woodland.

850c29fe2eb5.title: Soil value
850c29fe2eb5.sentence: As a yardstick for soil quality, a "Reich Standard Farm" was set up during the Third Reich in the parish of Eickendorf in the Magdeburger Börde, an exceptionally rich arable region.

d5c0ccebbd04.title: Soil value
d5c0ccebbd04.sentence: During the Reich Soil Assessment (Reichsbodenschätzung) following the Soil Assessment Act in 1934 a soil value of 100 was established in the leading Reich farm of Haberhauffe/Jäger.

a556eb552680.title: Soil value
a556eb552680.sentence: It was the basis of comparison for the tax rating of farms in Germany.

2a5e9a6254c2.title: Soil value
2a5e9a6254c2.sentence: During later measurements, an even higher value of BWZ – 102.8 – was measured in Mölme, about 20 km east of Hildesheim within the municipality of Söhlde.

4ecfd03e65ee.title: Soil value
4ecfd03e65ee.sentence: It is the highest value ever recorded in Germany.

3880539e2d7c.title: Geographic information system
3880539e2d7c.sentence: A geographic information system (GIS) consists of integrated computer hardware and software that store, manage, analyze, edit, output, and visualize geographic data.

286af1ce9f61.title: Geographic information system
286af1ce9f61.sentence: GIS provides the ability to relate previously unrelated information, through the use of location as the "key index variable".

876b3abd8424.title: Geographic information system
876b3abd8424.sentence: Developed by Roger Tomlinson, it was called the Canada Geographic Information System (CGIS) and was used to store, analyze, and manipulate data collected for the Canada Land Inventory, an effort to determine the land capability for rural Canada by mapping information about soils, agriculture, recreation, wildlife, waterfowl, forestry and land use at a scale of 1:50,000.

3a9090604e40.title: Geographic information system
3a9090604e40.sentence: GIS data represent phenomena that exist in the real world, such as roads, land use, elevation, trees, waterways, and states.

4f0297efbedf.title: Geographic information system
4f0297efbedf.sentence: Other types of geographic phenomena, such as events (e.g., location of World War II battles), processes (e.g., extent of suburbanization), and masses (e.g., types of soil in an area) are represented less commonly or indirectly, or are modeled in analysis procedures rather than data.

b751b2789041.title: Geographic information system
b751b2789041.section: Geospatial data management > Data acquisition > Primary data capture
b751b2789041.sentence: Survey data can be directly entered into a GIS from digital data collection systems on survey instruments using a technique called coordinate geometry (COGO).

9e56602594ee.title: Digital soil mapping
9e56602594ee.sentence: Digital soil mapping (DSM) in soil science, also referred to as predictive soil mapping or pedometric mapping, is the computer-assisted production of digital maps of soil types and soil properties.

af4c10ad08f0.title: Digital soil mapping
af4c10ad08f0.sentence: The international Working Group on Digital Soil Mapping (WG-DSM) defines digital soil mapping as "the creation and the population of a geographically referenced soil databases generated at a given resolution by using field and laboratory observation methods coupled with environmental data through quantitative relationships."

aded8ca9b451.title: Digital soil mapping
aded8ca9b451.sentence: DSM can rely upon, but is considered to be distinct from traditional soil mapping, which involves manual delineation of soil boundaries by field soil scientists.

2a4d8f0e97f0.title: Digital soil mapping
2a4d8f0e97f0.sentence: Non-digital soil maps produced as result of manual delineation of soil mapping units may also be digitized or surveyors may draw boundaries using field computers, hence both traditional, knowledge-based and technology and data-driven soil mapping frameworks are in essence digital.

62bd55b23f2d.title: Digital soil mapping
62bd55b23f2d.sentence: - technological advances, including GPS receivers, field scanners, and remote sensing, and

9d94871db565.title: Digital soil mapping
9d94871db565.sentence: - computational advances, including geostatistical interpolation and inference algorithms, GIS, digital elevation model, and data mining

ce6bfd16f3a6.title: Digital soil mapping
ce6bfd16f3a6.sentence: In digital soil mapping, semi-automated techniques and technologies are used to acquire, process and visualize information on soils and auxiliary information, so that the result can be obtained at cheaper costs.

abed0880710f.title: Digital soil mapping
abed0880710f.sentence: Products of the data-driven or statistical soil mapping are commonly assessed for the accuracy and uncertainty and can be more easily updated when new information comes available.

31266228d28f.title: Digital soil mapping
31266228d28f.sentence: Digital soil mapping tries to overcome some of the drawbacks of the traditional soil maps that are often only focused on delineating soil-classes i.e. soil types.

65fb3e25309c.title: Digital soil mapping
65fb3e25309c.sentence: - do not provide information for modeling the dynamics of soil conditions and

22ed665ad647.title: Digital soil mapping
22ed665ad647.sentence: - are inflexible to quantitative studies on the functionality of soils.

a6c638478dd3.title: Digital soil mapping
a6c638478dd3.sentence: An example of successful digital soil mapping application is the physical properties (soil texture, bulk density) developed in the European Union with around 20,000 topsoil samples of LUCAS database.

df06dd639e5c.title: Digital soil mapping
df06dd639e5c.sentence: Another example are maps of soil properties for the entire world (250 m cell size), with quantified uncertainty, generated by ISRIC - World Soil Information using state-of-the-art machine learning methods (SoilGrids) that use as inputs point data from a large global soil profile database (WoSIS) and over 400 global environmental covariates.

21c83e3d6ea9.title: Soil survey
21c83e3d6ea9.sentence: Soil survey information can be used to predict or estimate the potentials and limitations of soils for many specific uses.

63257808540c.title: Soil survey
63257808540c.sentence: The information in a soil survey can be used by farmers and ranchers to help determine whether a particular soil type is suited for crops or livestock and what type of soil management might be required.

71d51a69fcf5.title: Soil survey
71d51a69fcf5.sentence: An architect or engineer might use the engineering properties of a soil to determine whether it is suitable for a certain type of construction.

02d165b73e89.title: Soil survey
02d165b73e89.sentence: The information must be interpreted to be usable by professional planners and others.

717ab01f31f2.title: Soil survey
717ab01f31f2.sentence: Predictions based on soil surveys serve as a basis for judgment about land use and management for areas ranging from small tracts to regions of several million acres.

a9c5506f96f9.title: Soil survey
a9c5506f96f9.sentence: These predictions, however, must be evaluated along with economic, social, and environmental considerations before they can be used to make valid recommendations for land use and management.

a153e8540393.title: Digital elevation model
a153e8540393.sentence: A digital elevation model (DEM) or digital surface model (DSM) is a 3D computer graphics representation of elevation data to represent terrain or overlaying objects, commonly of a planet, moon, or asteroid.

f745d329f53c.title: Digital elevation model
f745d329f53c.sentence: A digital terrain model (DTM) represents specifically the ground surface while DEM and DSM may represent tree top canopy or building roofs.

18bdee5fbcd4.title: Digital elevation model
18bdee5fbcd4.sentence: In contrast to a DSM, the digital terrain model (DTM) represents the bare ground surface without any objects like plants and buildings (see the figure on the right).

61e634d12f27.title: Digital elevation model
61e634d12f27.sentence: There is no universal usage of the terms digital elevation model (DEM), digital terrain model (DTM) and digital surface model (DSM) in scientific literature.

8d6a2a77df75.title: Digital elevation model
8d6a2a77df75.sentence: The DEM could be acquired through techniques such as photogrammetry, lidar, IfSAR or InSAR, land surveying, etc. (Li et al. 2005).

45b815c6996d.title: Digital elevation model
45b815c6996d.sentence: DEMs are commonly built using data collected using remote sensing techniques, but they may also be built from land surveying.

2dfe29f315f2.title: Digital elevation model
2dfe29f315f2.sentence: While a DSM may be useful for landscape modeling, city modeling and visualization applications, a DTM is often required for flood or drainage modeling, land-use studies, geological applications, and other applications, and in planetary science.

5acaa310354e.title: Digital elevation model
5acaa310354e.sentence: DEMs are used often in geographic information systems (GIS), and are the most common basis for digitally produced relief maps.

1ee769a5aceb.title: Digital elevation model
1ee769a5aceb.sentence: - Modeling soils wetness with Cartographic Depth to Water Indexes (DTW-index)

8ff8d5bb6abc.title: European Soil Database
8ff8d5bb6abc.sentence: The European Soil Database is the only harmonized soil database in Europe from which many other data information and services are derived.

118c7cec9769.title: European Soil Database
118c7cec9769.sentence: For instance, the European Soil Database v2 Raster Library contains raster (grid) data files with cell sizes of 1 km x 1 km for a large number of soil related parameters.

fd80e8263444.title: European Soil Database
fd80e8263444.sentence: Each grid is aligned with the INSPIRE reference grid.

3d55a57906ce.title: European Soil Database
3d55a57906ce.sentence: These rasters are in the public domain and allow expert users to use the data for instance to run soil-, water- and air related models.

19533f2a28f2.title: European Soil Database
19533f2a28f2.sentence: The many rasters include parameters such as soil texture (clay, silt and sand), parent material, WRB soil type, Obstacle to roots, soil depth, Impermeability, Soil Water Regime, Water Management System, mineralogy, cation exchange capacity, packing density, available water capacity.

904192089cee.title: European Soil Database
904192089cee.sentence: The European Soil Database is based on experts' knowledge.

5986d98ff28c.title: European Soil Database
5986d98ff28c.sentence: In an attempt to expand soil data at European scale, the European Commission Joint Research Centre runs the LUCAS topsoil survey collecting soil samples across the soils of European Union.

ee632c4cf394.title: Soil carbon
ee632c4cf394.section: Soil carbon and climate change > Measuring data on soil organic carbon > Europe
ee632c4cf394.sentence: The most homogeneous and comprehensive data on the organic carbon/matter content of European soils remain those that can be extracted and/or derived from the European Soil Database in combination with associated databases on land cover, climate, and topography.

dd89dce2a11c.title: SSURGO
dd89dce2a11c.sentence: SSURGO (Soil Survey Geographic database) refers to digital soils data produced and distributed by the Natural Resources Conservation Service (NRCS) - National Cartography and Geospatial Center (NCGC) in the United States.

7c98a8ee6769.title: SSURGO
7c98a8ee6769.sentence: The database has information on soil types and their distribution.

cd83910be2b3.title: SSURGO
cd83910be2b3.sentence: The information covers soil characteristics, soil properties, and addresses limits, risks and suitability for various uses.

1a81ff0ff27c.title: Natural Resources Conservation Service
1a81ff0ff27c.sentence: Information is maintained in the Soil Survey Geographic database (SSURGO) dataset.

dfab6efebae9.title: Soil in the United States
dfab6efebae9.sentence: The site is updated and maintained online as the single authoritative source of soil survey information.[6]

947d71b15f87.title: Pedometric mapping
947d71b15f87.sentence: Pedometrics is the application of mathematical and statistical methods to the study of the distribution and genesis of soils.

1108a5d941d5.title: Pedometric mapping
1108a5d941d5.sentence: The term is a portmanteau of the Greek roots pedos (soil) and metron (measurement).

7e1efccf6919.title: Pedometric mapping
7e1efccf6919.sentence: Pedometrics addresses soil-related problems when there is uncertainty due to deterministic or stochastic variation, vagueness and lack of knowledge of soil properties and processes.

83ee0768264b.title: Pedometric mapping
83ee0768264b.sentence: Simulation models incorporate uncertainty by adopting chaos theory, statistical distribution, or fuzzy logic.

bcdd9841e3a8.title: Pedometric mapping
bcdd9841e3a8.sentence: Its advance is also linked to improvements in remote and close-range sensing.

16c24844577e.title: Pedometric mapping
16c24844577e.sentence: Pedometrics addresses pedology from the perspective of emerging scientific fields such as wavelets analysis, fuzzy set theory and data mining in soil data modelling applications.

d378b878c8d7.title: Pedometric mapping
d378b878c8d7.sentence: Pedometric mapping, or statistical soil mapping, is data-driven generation of soil property and class maps that is based on use of statistical methods.

c2dbba415f71.title: Pedometric mapping
c2dbba415f71.sentence: Its main objectives are to predict values of some soil variable at unobserved locations, and to access the uncertainty of that estimate using statistical inference i.e. statistically optimal approaches.

dd470fedd851.title: Pedometric mapping
dd470fedd851.sentence: It is largely based on applying geostatistics in soil science, and other statistical methods used in pedometrics.

1399043313c2.title: Pedometric mapping
1399043313c2.sentence: From the application point of view, its main objective is to accurately predict response of a soil-plant ecosystem to various soil management strategies—that is, to generate maps of soil properties and soil classes that can be used for other environmental models and decision-making.

6d42f1f08bf5.title: Pedometric mapping
6d42f1f08bf5.sentence: In traditional soil survey, spatial distribution of soil properties and soil bodies can be inferred from mental models, leading to manual delineations.

ddcaef0e667d.title: Pedometric mapping
ddcaef0e667d.sentence: Such methods can be considered subjective, and it is hence difficult or impossible to statistically assess the accuracy of such maps without additional field sampling.

ee0a5521bb69.title: Pedometric mapping
ee0a5521bb69.sentence: With pedometric mapping, all outputs are based on rigorous statistical computing, and are hence reproducible.

3bb3d1c4c59c.title: Pedometric mapping
3bb3d1c4c59c.sentence: Pedometric mapping is based largely on extensive and detailed covariate layers, such as Digital Elevation Model (DEM) derivatives, remote sensing imagery, climatic, land cover and geological GIS layers and imagery.

a50947c89ba8.title: Pedometric mapping
a50947c89ba8.sentence: Its evolution can be closely connected with the emergence of new technologies and global, publicly available data sources such as the SRTM DEM, MODIS, ASTER and Landsat imagery, gamma radiometrics and LiDAR imagery, and new automated mapping methods.

1b2cbef06ca4.title: Pedometric mapping
1b2cbef06ca4.sentence: Target variables | Soil types (soil series) | Analytical soil properties

fcf3d2d62af0.title: Pedometric mapping
fcf3d2d62af0.sentence: Spatial data model | Discrete (soil bodies) | Continuous/hybrid (quantities / probabilities)

88e3188b7e38.title: Pedometric mapping
88e3188b7e38.sentence: Data representation | Polygon maps + attribute tables (2D) | Gridded maps (2D/3D) + prediction error map or simulations

cfb1973bdaef.title: Pedometric mapping
cfb1973bdaef.sentence: Pedometric analyses rely strictly on geostatistics, whereas digital soil mapping uses more traditional soil-mapping concepts not strictly pedometric in nature.

c72491d22e5c.title: Pedometric mapping
c72491d22e5c.sentence: Pedometric mapping does not produce maps delineating discrete soil types.

b43a3a35a44c.title: Pedometric mapping
b43a3a35a44c.sentence: Pedometric mapping methods differ based on the steps of soil survey data processing:

bd7cff2634df.title: Pedometric mapping
bd7cff2634df.sentence: One of the main theoretical bases for pedometric mapping is the universal model of soil variation:

2d4944b131d4.title: Pedometric mapping
2d4944b131d4.sentence: ...where m(𝐬) is the deterministic part of soil variation, ε′(𝐬) is the stochastic, spatially auto-correlated part of variation, and ε″ is the remaining residual variation (measurement errors, short-range variability etc.) that is also possibly dependent on 𝐬, but is not modeled.

0f7b879ccbe5.title: Pedometric mapping
0f7b879ccbe5.sentence: This model was first introduced by French mathematician Georges Matheron, and has proven the Best Unbiased Linear Predictor for spatial data.

610a76362ce9.title: Pedometric mapping
610a76362ce9.sentence: One way of using this model to produce predictions or simulations is by regression-kriging (also known as universal kriging).

5acc83b60b8a.title: Pedometric mapping
5acc83b60b8a.sentence: With soil data, the model's deterministic component is often based on the soil forming factors of climate, organism, relief, parent material (lithology), and time.

8846804952e5.title: Pedometric mapping
8846804952e5.sentence: This conceptual model, known as the CLORPT model, was introduced to soil-landscape modelling by Hans Jenny.

2bdd7df3f112.title: Land use
2bdd7df3f112.sentence: Land use change is "the change from one land-use category to another".

1069bba718d0.title: Land use
1069bba718d0.sentence: Human activity is the most significant cause of land cover change, and humans are also directly impacted by the environmental consequences of these changes.

63d7c5d97f7e.title: Land use
63d7c5d97f7e.sentence: Land-use change, together with use of fossil fuels, are the major anthropogenic sources of carbon dioxide, a dominant greenhouse gas.

874d6d70423e.title: Land use
874d6d70423e.section: Examples of land use change > Deforestation
874d6d70423e.sentence: Deforestation is the systematic and permanent conversion of previously forested land for other uses.

d3a63b656a00.title: Land use
d3a63b656a00.section: Examples of land use change > Deforestation
d3a63b656a00.sentence: It has historically been a primary facilitator of land use and land cover change.

71aaac21226c.title: Land use
71aaac21226c.section: Examples of land use change > Deforestation
71aaac21226c.sentence: However, since the invention of agriculture, global forest cover has diminished by 35%.

1ca76fa0d82c.title: Land use
1ca76fa0d82c.section: Examples of land use change > Urbanization
1ca76fa0d82c.sentence: Although urbanized areas cover just 3% of the Earth's surface, they nevertheless have a significant impact on land use and land cover change.

1f6ad827db4c.title: Land use
1f6ad827db4c.section: Examples of land use change > Urbanization
1f6ad827db4c.sentence: Increases in urbanization lead to increases in consumption, which puts increased pressure on surrounding rural lands.

cf2d388823ed.title: Land use
cf2d388823ed.section: Examples of land use change > Urbanization
cf2d388823ed.sentence: The outward spread of urban areas can also take over adjacent land formerly used for crop cultivation.

681be11f3512.title: Land use
681be11f3512.section: Analytical methods > Land cover monitoring and assessments
681be11f3512.sentence: To this end, scientists use a variety of tools, including satellite imagery and other sources of remotely sensed data (e.g., aircraft imagery), field observations, historical accounts, and reconstruction modeling.

d142d15fe699.title: Land use
d142d15fe699.section: Analytical methods > Land cover monitoring and assessments
d142d15fe699.sentence: These tools, particularly satellite imagery, allow land change scientists to accurately monitor land-change rates and create a consistent, long-term record to quantify change variability over time.

0192b1b2ba8a.title: Land use
0192b1b2ba8a.sentence: A key method for studying risk and vulnerability is land change modeling (LCM), which can be used to simulate changes and land use and land cover.

2c6771b16ab7.title: Land use
2c6771b16ab7.sentence: LCMs can be used to predict how land use and land cover may change under alternate circumstances, which is useful for risk assessment, in that it allows for the prediction of potential impacts and can be used to inform policy decisions, albeit with some uncertainty.

37c3439c2f5d.title: Aerial photography
37c3439c2f5d.sentence: Aerial photography (or airborne imagery) is the taking of photographs from an aircraft or other airborne platforms.

1f54e5bc9973.title: Aerial photography
1f54e5bc9973.sentence: Aerial photography typically refers specifically to bird's-eye view images that focus on landscapes and surface objects, and should not be confused with air-to-air photography, where one or more aircraft are used as chase planes that "chase" and photograph other aircraft in flight.

8089c512f257.title: Aerial photography
8089c512f257.sentence: Vertical aerial photography is used in cartography (particularly in photogrammetric surveys, which are often the basis for topographic maps), land-use planning, aerial archaeology.

ea94e39a3362.title: Aerial photography
ea94e39a3362.sentence: During the 1930s, the company pioneered the science of photogrammetry (mapping from aerial photographs), with the Ordnance Survey amongst the company's clients.

4908b94ec0cc.title: Aerial photography
4908b94ec0cc.sentence: One of its first government contracts was an aerial survey of New Mexico to study soil erosion.

36621bc2a24f.title: Remote sensing
36621bc2a24f.section: Data acquisition > Applications of remote sensing > Aerial platforms and Satellites
36621bc2a24f.sentence: Stereoscopic pairs of aerial photographs have often been used to make topographic maps by imagery and terrain analysts in trafficability and highway departments for potential routes, in addition to modelling terrestrial habitat features.

71af7ac3b63e.title: Land Suitability classification
71af7ac3b63e.sentence: The Land Suitability Classification is a soil evaluation method, developed by FAO.

e1ba81ca0e9f.title: Land Suitability classification
e1ba81ca0e9f.sentence: FAO stated that Land suitability is the fitness of a given type of land for a defined use.

c475f50110d0.title: Land Suitability classification
c475f50110d0.sentence: The process of land suitability classification is the appraisal and grouping of specific areas of land in terms of their suitability for defined uses.

2699f889dc80.title: Land Suitability classification
2699f889dc80.sentence: The land may be considered in its present condition or after improvements.

e148a81dcc18.title: Land Suitability classification
e148a81dcc18.sentence: Four categories of decreasing generalization are recognized:

71ccd20fa8b9.title: Land Suitability classification
71ccd20fa8b9.sentence: - I. Land Suitability Orders: reflecting kinds of suitability.

55043a455081.title: Land Suitability classification
55043a455081.sentence: Land Suitability Classes: reflecting degrees of suitability within Orders.

99206997e379.title: Land Suitability classification
99206997e379.sentence: Land Suitability Subclasses: reflecting kinds of limitation, or main kinds of improvement measures required, within Classes.

9871dbf5e0ec.title: Land Suitability classification
9871dbf5e0ec.sentence: Land Suitability Units: reflecting minor differences in required management within Subclasses

999e8f70a870.title: Land Suitability classification
999e8f70a870.sentence: There are two orders represented in maps, tables, etc. by the symbols S and N respectively.

dd78bd2fc449.title: Land Suitability classification
dd78bd2fc449.sentence: Land on which sustained use of the kind under consideration is expected to yield benefits which justify the inputs, without unacceptable risk of damage to land resources.

7c30f767de66.title: Land Suitability classification
7c30f767de66.sentence: Land which has qualities that appear to preclude sustained use of the kind under consideration.

246453711f3c.title: Land Suitability classification
246453711f3c.sentence: It may be that the proposed use is technically impracticable, such as the irrigation of rocky steep land, or that it would cause severe environmental degradation, such as the cultivation of steep slopes.

168d2ad8f931.title: Land Suitability classification
168d2ad8f931.sentence: Frequently, however, the reason is economic: that the value of the expected benefits does not justify the expected costs of the inputs that would be required.

7b0ac040f96d.title: Climate change
7b0ac040f96d.sentence: Climate change affects land suitability for many crops, with suitable areas for given crops usually moving to higher latitudes and altitudes.

9aa2028afebc.title: Storie index
9aa2028afebc.sentence: The Storie index is a method of soil rating based on soil characteristics that govern the land's potential use and productivity capacity.

674d3d025915.title: Storie index
674d3d025915.sentence: Developed by R. Earl Storie at University of California, Berkeley in the 1930s as a method of land valuation, it is independent of other physical or economic factors that might determine the desirability of growing certain plants in a given location.

c4ad7a6b9c26.title: Storie index
c4ad7a6b9c26.sentence: - E: Climate (only if it is not homogeneous, if so than it should not be included in the formula);

d46bcad43f9c.title: Storie index
d46bcad43f9c.sentence: The index is calculated from the multiplication of these parameters, that is: Sindex = A x B x C x D x E

217f9ca7e89b.title: Storie index
217f9ca7e89b.sentence: The disadvantage of this method is that if we have a value of zero in any category, then the result will be zero and won't be suitable for using.

0079c4ca8b89.title: Storie index
0079c4ca8b89.sentence: Another disadvantage is that the ratings are subjective.

b4f9dc89bd24.title: Storie index
b4f9dc89bd24.sentence: This methodology was updated in again in 2008 by O'Geen et al. to correct for some of the subjectivity. https://anrcatalog.ucanr.edu/pdf/8335.pdf

d75ced2f3a71.title: Land use capability map
d75ced2f3a71.sentence: Land use capability maps are maps created to represent the potential uses of a "unit" of land.

58e7a19ed5ff.title: Land use capability map
58e7a19ed5ff.sentence: The former shows the potential uses (usually in relation to farming) whilst the latter shows the actual use for the land at the present time.

39bc7fdd6e37.title: Land use capability map
39bc7fdd6e37.sentence: They are measured using various indicators, although the most common are five physical factors (rock type, soil type, slope, erosion degree and type, and vegetation).

9ffff3dc1881.title: Land use capability map
9ffff3dc1881.sentence: In more scientific terms, these can be classed as lithology, edaphology, topography, gradient, and biotic features.

b76586887995.title: Land use capability map
b76586887995.sentence: Land use capability maps must not be confused with land use maps.

803e3f873d69.title: National Cooperative Soil Survey
803e3f873d69.sentence: In 1951, the SCS developed the Land Capability System.

259a7e2e2c58.title: National Cooperative Soil Survey
259a7e2e2c58.sentence: National Cooperative Soil Survey standards assure the soil survey data is consistent with the Land Capability Classification System.

4e7e9761b3d1.title: Site index
4e7e9761b3d1.sentence: Site index is a term used in forestry to describe the potential for forest trees to grow at a particular location or "site".

e395cd1b4ac5.title: Site index
e395cd1b4ac5.sentence: Site index is used to measure the productivity of the site and the management options for that site and reports the height of dominant and co-dominant trees in a stand at a base age such as 25, 50 and 100 years.

022b17dfe32b.title: Site index
022b17dfe32b.sentence: For example, a red oak with an age of 50 years and a height of 70 feet (21 m) will have a site index of 70.

9283f32922f3.title: Site index
9283f32922f3.sentence: Common methods used to determine site index are based on tree height, plant composition and the use of soil maps.

dcb05f6c8175.title: Site index
dcb05f6c8175.sentence: Determining site index from plant composition is often referred to as the indicator-plant approach.

30d0446e6e88.title: Site index
30d0446e6e88.sentence: Site index is determined from plant composition by the presence, abundance, and size of understory plants.

bd1ada983034.title: Site index
bd1ada983034.sentence: In the United States, site index can be determined from soil maps provided by the Natural Resources Conservation Service (NRCS).

936224b9ec35.title: Site index
936224b9ec35.sentence: Soil surveys were conducted by the NRCS and site index was measured for these soils.

f760e2715725.title: Site index
f760e2715725.sentence: Tables were compiled of the relationships between different soils and different site indexes for important species of that area.

656c5b9f01d4.title: Site index
656c5b9f01d4.sentence: Indirect methods include estimations based on relationships among dominant species, lesser vegetation characteristics or site indicators, as well as topographic, climatic, and edaphic factors.

a9e8b72dddb7.title: Site index
a9e8b72dddb7.sentence: Site index has been the most widely used means of estimating site productivity in North America, despite some shortcomings.

b56a6b6ec188.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/04%3A_Mapping_Survey/4.03%3A_Challenges_in_soil_surveying
b56a6b6ec188.sentence: Because soil series vary so much in slope, degree of erosion, number and size of stones, or some other feature affecting their use, practical suggestions about their management could not be made if they were shown on the soil map as one unit.

df2bcf6063ed.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/04%3A_Mapping_Survey/4.03%3A_Challenges_in_soil_surveying
df2bcf6063ed.sentence: Such soil series are divided into soil phases.

db7069e72989.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/04%3A_Mapping_Survey/4.03%3A_Challenges_in_soil_surveying
db7069e72989.sentence: The name of the soil phase indicates the surface feature most affecting its management.

e3edb03faea5.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/04%3A_Mapping_Survey/4.03%3A_Challenges_in_soil_surveying
e3edb03faea5.sentence: For example, Vina loam, 0 to 2 percent slopes; Vina loam, 2 to 9 percent slopes; Vina gravelly loam, 2 to 9 percent slopes; and Vina silty clay loam, 2 to 9 percent slopes are four soil phases of the Vina series.

3d93e7b4409e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/04%3A_Mapping_Survey/4.03%3A_Challenges_in_soil_surveying
3d93e7b4409e.sentence: The area enclosed within each continuous line on a soil map is the delineation of a map unit.

d96545a82db1.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/04%3A_Mapping_Survey/4.03%3A_Challenges_in_soil_surveying
d96545a82db1.sentence: The map unit includes the soil phase and all inclusions.

f1aa0edc99fb.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/04%3A_Mapping_Survey/4.02%3A_What_is_a_soil_survey
f1aa0edc99fb.sentence: These low value areas are mapped on a small scale and the resulting study is called a reconnaissance survey.

7673fa744ba6.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/04%3A_Mapping_Survey/4.02%3A_What_is_a_soil_survey
7673fa744ba6.sentence: The reconnaissance survey identifies areas and regions dominated by soil associations in contrast to the detailed map where specific soils are delineated.

079761df171c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/04%3A_Mapping_Survey/4.02%3A_What_is_a_soil_survey
079761df171c.sentence: Large expanses of land that are of little direct value for agricultural or forest uses often are too poor to justify this high cost.

f1c4d3c90d05.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/04%3A_Mapping_Survey/4.04%3A_Responsibility_for_soil_surveys
f1c4d3c90d05.sentence: The United States Department of Agriculture Natural Resource Conservation Service (USDA NRCS) today provides these soil surveys in a digital format through the Web Soil Survey (United States Department of Agriculture Natural Resources Conservation Service, 2016).

69dabaf672f1.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/04%3A_Mapping_Survey/4.04%3A_Responsibility_for_soil_surveys
69dabaf672f1.sentence: The Web Soil Survey provides all the information previously contained in the county soil survey reports.

ba2894d024a4.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/04%3A_Mapping_Survey/4.04%3A_Responsibility_for_soil_surveys
ba2894d024a4.sentence: It also contains additional tools and information that has not been available in printed versions of the soil surveys.

a761d0b76010.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/04%3A_Mapping_Survey/4.04%3A_Responsibility_for_soil_surveys
a761d0b76010.sentence: Another advantage of the Web Soil Survey is that the information contained in it can be updated as needed, instead of being updated following new surveys of the same county, which take 30 to 60 years!

c7ebbda7f358.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/04%3A_Mapping_Survey/4.05%3A_Activity_1_-_Using_Web_Soil_Survey
c7ebbda7f358.sentence: - Your AOI can be anywhere in the United States where soil survey information is available.

c7a897909e47.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/04%3A_Mapping_Survey/4.05%3A_Activity_1_-_Using_Web_Soil_Survey
c7a897909e47.sentence: For the AOI you have selected, go to the Soil Map tab (located near top of page) to generate a map showing the AOI and its component soil map units.

a6ca9944e41b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/04%3A_Mapping_Survey/4.05%3A_Activity_1_-_Using_Web_Soil_Survey
a6ca9944e41b.sentence: Generate the soil map report for your AOI (go to the “shopping cart” and generate a pdf).

5518aa8e8540.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/04%3A_Mapping_Survey/4.05%3A_Activity_1_-_Using_Web_Soil_Survey
5518aa8e8540.sentence: Go to the Soil Data Explorer tab and then select the tab heading entitled Soil Properties and Qualities.

3c78d3cb4560.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/04%3A_Mapping_Survey/4.05%3A_Activity_1_-_Using_Web_Soil_Survey
3c78d3cb4560.sentence: Select Water Features and determine Depth to Water Table for your map unit.

47fbb9813819.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/04%3A_Mapping_Survey/4.05%3A_Activity_1_-_Using_Web_Soil_Survey
47fbb9813819.sentence: What is the Surface Texture for your map unit? _______________________

b190723b5b03.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/04%3A_Mapping_Survey/4.05%3A_Activity_1_-_Using_Web_Soil_Survey
b190723b5b03.sentence: Find the Bulk Density (One-Third Bar) for the surface layer of your map unit (you will have to use Advanced Options > Layer Options > Surface Layer to get information for the surface layer).

18a5ff257dcf.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/04%3A_Mapping_Survey/4.05%3A_Activity_1_-_Using_Web_Soil_Survey
18a5ff257dcf.sentence: Find the pH (1 to 1 water) for the surface soil layer of your map unit (you will have to use Advanced Options > Layer Options > Surface Layer to get information for the surface layer).

459a10f15ca5.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/04%3A_Mapping_Survey/4.05%3A_Activity_1_-_Using_Web_Soil_Survey
459a10f15ca5.sentence: Find the Depth to Any Soil Restrictive Layer for your map unit (default settings are OK).

d0cca5eb17c3.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/04%3A_Mapping_Survey/4.05%3A_Activity_1_-_Using_Web_Soil_Survey
d0cca5eb17c3.sentence: While still under the Soil Data Explorer tab, select the tab heading entitled Suitabilities and Limitations for Use – it’s located immediately to the left of the Soil Properties and Qualities tab heading.

bbd0ac0825f7.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/04%3A_Mapping_Survey/4.05%3A_Activity_1_-_Using_Web_Soil_Survey
bbd0ac0825f7.sentence: Determine the suitability of your soil map unit for Dwellings with Basements.

889a9abd43e5.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/04%3A_Mapping_Survey/4.05%3A_Activity_1_-_Using_Web_Soil_Survey
889a9abd43e5.sentence: Determine the suitability of your soil map unit for Local Roads and Streets.

50dbc8125c37.sentence: Click on the Vegetative Productivity tab.

cd9913d48908.sentence: Determine the suitability of your soil map unit for Disposal of Wastewater by Irrigation (default settings are OK).
