edfe6aaa8cad.title: Land Suitability classification
edfe6aaa8cad.sentence: Land suitability Classes reflect degrees of suitability.

dd83ce15a926.title: Land Suitability classification
dd83ce15a926.sentence: The classes are numbered consecutively, by Arabic numbers, in sequence of decreasing degrees of suitability within the Order.

931814ca83d0.title: Land Suitability classification
931814ca83d0.sentence: Within the Order Suitable the number of classes is not specified.

842493032c95.title: Land Suitability classification
842493032c95.sentence: The number of classes recognized should be kept to the minimum necessary to meet interpretative aims; five should probably be the most ever used.

0b7c8fa70bcc.title: Land Suitability classification
0b7c8fa70bcc.sentence: If three Classes are recognized within the Order Suitable, as can often be recommended, the following names and definitions may be appropriate in a qualitative classification:

28ba317e99b6.title: Land Suitability classification
28ba317e99b6.sentence: - Class S1 Highly Suitable: Land having no significant limitations to sustained application of a given use, or only minor limitations that will not significantly reduce productivity or benefits and will not raise inputs above an acceptable level.

d7ccd123f0e0.title: Land Suitability classification
d7ccd123f0e0.sentence: - Class S2 Moderately Suitable: Land having limitations which in aggregate are moderately severe for sustained application of a given use; the limitations will reduce productivity or benefits and increase required inputs to the extent that the overall advantage to be gained from the use, although still attractive, will be appreciably inferior to that expected on Class S1 land.

9c5a89c5f54f.title: Land Suitability classification
9c5a89c5f54f.sentence: - Class S3 Marginally Suitable: Land having limitations which in aggregate are severe for sustained application of a given use and will so reduce productivity or benefits, or increase required inputs, that this expenditure will be only marginally justified.

dc174c359ecc.title: Land Suitability classification
dc174c359ecc.sentence: Within the Order Not Suitable, there are normally two Classes:

a0b1e25d61f2.title: Land Suitability classification
a0b1e25d61f2.sentence: - Class N1 Currently Not Suitable: Land having limitations which may be surmountable in time but which cannot be corrected with existing knowledge at currently acceptable cost; the limitations are so severe as to preclude successful sustained use of the land in the given manner.

dd5d5050c2f6.title: Land Suitability classification
dd5d5050c2f6.sentence: - Class N2 Permanently Not Suitable: Land having limitations which appear so severe as to preclude any possibilities Of successful sustained use of the land in the given manner.

19a63b7cdd04.title: Soil map
19a63b7cdd04.sentence: A Soil Information System is basically a systematic collection of complete (values of the target soil variables available for the whole area of interest) and consistent gridded or vector soil property and/or class maps with an attached report, user manual and/or metadata.

b8483c5d04b0.title: Soil map
b8483c5d04b0.sentence: In this context, soil maps are only visualizations of the soil resource inventories commonly stored in a Soil Information System (SIS), of which the major part is a Soil Geographical Database.

2cb5b79d4ecb.title: Soil map
2cb5b79d4ecb.sentence: A SIS is in the most cases, a combination of polygon and point maps linked with attribute tables for profile observations, soil mapping units and soil classes.

8a03e48f22c2.title: International Soil Reference and Information Centre
8a03e48f22c2.sentence: - Strengthening Soil Information Systems on national, regional, and continental level
8a03e48f22c2.key: International Soil Reference and Information Centre

a1a7c58dcb50.title: Soil governance
a1a7c58dcb50.sentence: Currently, under the GSP framework, a new global soil information system will be developed.

a2ac57d04ca7.title: Site index
a2ac57d04ca7.sentence: These values are then used on a graph or an equation called a site index curve.

b7a86d012a80.title: Site index
b7a86d012a80.sentence: This will estimate height at index age (site index).

adb9dd524598.title: Site index
adb9dd524598.sentence: Height is obtained from a site tree, usually a dominant or co-dominant tree (referred to as canopy position) in a stand and is estimated using an instrument called a clinometer, or measured using a laser hypsometer or releskop.

794f423a2ab1.title: Site index
794f423a2ab1.sentence: Age is calculated using an instrument called an increment borer or from planting records for even aged stands.

819eddf8a4db.title: Site index
819eddf8a4db.sentence: A tree is measured to be 60 feet (18 m) in overall height, and the stand age is determined to be 50 years old.

90b7a57ac9f6.title: Site index
90b7a57ac9f6.sentence: To find site index from a site index curve, one would find age 50 along the x-axis and then find 60 feet (18 m) along the y-axis.

5b13d2b02411.title: Site index
5b13d2b02411.sentence: Where these two points intersect one would find the nearest line, which represents the site index for that stand.

d1d2bc5f6bd0.title: Site index
d1d2bc5f6bd0.sentence: An example of a site index equation is: lnS=lnHd-b1(A−1-Ai−1)

48ade0c30690.title: Site index
48ade0c30690.sentence: Where S is site index, Ai is index age, Hd is height of dominants and co-dominants and A is stand age.

33ca3f975ca4.title: Site index
33ca3f975ca4.sentence: Since it is so difficult to predict early growth rates of planted white spruce, site index curves cannot be reliably extended below about 15 years (Stiell 1976).

a5ed46b07392.title: Gas chromatography
a5ed46b07392.sentence: Gas chromatography (GC) is a common type of chromatography used in analytical chemistry for separating and analyzing compounds that can be vaporized without decomposition.

a323ed67178a.title: Gas chromatography
a323ed67178a.sentence: Professionals working with GC analyze the content of a chemical product, for example in assuring the quality of products in the chemical industry; or measuring chemicals in soil, air or water, such as soil gases.

3b01de865e8a.title: Dumas method
3b01de865e8a.sentence: The final column uses gas chromatography to separate nitrogen from carbon dioxide and water.

e6ba36bd3eda.title: Elemental analysis
e6ba36bd3eda.sentence: Elemental analysis is a process where a sample of some material (e.g., soil, waste or drinking water, bodily fluids, minerals, chemical compounds) is analyzed for its elemental and sometimes isotopic composition.

ab46facc1f6d.title: Elemental analysis
ab46facc1f6d.sentence: The most common form of elemental analysis, CHNS analysis, is accomplished by combustion analysis.

00f75c00763d.title: Combustion analysis
00f75c00763d.sentence: Applications for combustion analysis involve only the elements of carbon (C), hydrogen (H), nitrogen (N), and sulfur (S) as combustion of materials containing them convert these elements to their oxidized form (CO2, H2O, NO or NO2, and SO2) under high temperature high oxygen conditions.

7c7d639edac7.title: Combustion analysis
7c7d639edac7.sentence: This instrument calculates the percentages of elemental concentrations based on the Dumas method, using flash combustion of the sample to cause an instantaneous oxidation into simple compounds which are then detected with thermal conductivity detection or infrared spectroscopy.

927957a16a50.title: Dumas method
927957a16a50.sentence: Combust a sample of known mass to 800–900 °C in the presence of an atmosphere that is oxygen-rich and nitrogen-free.

32cee1a799ee.title: Dumas method
32cee1a799ee.sentence: At the end of the column, there is a thermal conductivity (k) detector.

bceba1574710.title: Dumas method
bceba1574710.sentence: It has been developed into a considerably faster method than the Kjeldahl method, and can take a few minutes per measurement, as compared to the hour or more for Kjeldahl.

a965e546d296.title: Dumas method
a965e546d296.sentence: It also does not make use of toxic chemicals or catalysts.

d96456fa865a.title: Inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectroscopy
d96456fa865a.sentence: Inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectroscopy (ICP-AES), also referred to as inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy (ICP-OES), is an analytical technique used for the detection of chemical elements.
d96456fa865a.key: Inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectroscopy

e09bed618a51.title: Inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectroscopy
e09bed618a51.sentence: It is a type of emission spectroscopy that uses the inductively coupled plasma to produce excited atoms and ions that emit electromagnetic radiation at wavelengths characteristic of a particular element.
e09bed618a51.key: Inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectroscopy

2dee543fa13f.title: Inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectroscopy
2dee543fa13f.sentence: The source temperature is in the range from 6000 to 10,000 K. The intensity of the emissions from various wavelengths of light are proportional to the concentrations of the elements within the sample.
2dee543fa13f.key: Inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectroscopy

156d459a456f.title: Inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectroscopy
156d459a456f.sentence: A peristaltic pump delivers an aqueous or organic sample into an analytical nebulizer where it is changed into mist and introduced directly inside the plasma flame.
156d459a456f.key: Inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectroscopy

249c696e9748.title: Inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectroscopy
249c696e9748.sentence: In units using these detector arrays, the intensities of all wavelengths (within the system's range) can be measured simultaneously, allowing the instrument to analyze for every element to which the unit is sensitive all at once.
249c696e9748.key: Inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectroscopy

894a886b5a60.title: Inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectroscopy
894a886b5a60.sentence: Thus, samples can be analyzed very quickly.
894a886b5a60.key: Inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectroscopy

cbf22a72c6a9.title: Inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectroscopy
cbf22a72c6a9.sentence: The intensity of each line is then compared to previously measured intensities of known concentrations of the elements, and their concentrations are then computed by interpolation along the calibration lines (use of a calibration curve).
cbf22a72c6a9.key: Inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectroscopy

ca51444f2f30.title: Inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectroscopy
ca51444f2f30.sentence: It is also fast becoming the analytical method of choice for the determination of nutrient levels in agricultural soils.
ca51444f2f30.key: Inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectroscopy

d0e9992fc8d5.title: Inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectroscopy
d0e9992fc8d5.sentence: This information is then used to calculate the amount of fertiliser required to maximise crop yield and quality.
d0e9992fc8d5.key: Inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectroscopy

eb25df3b79f8.title: Inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectroscopy
eb25df3b79f8.sentence: ICP-AES is often used for analysis of trace elements in soil, and it is for that reason it is often used in forensics to ascertain the origin of soil samples found at crime scenes or on victims etc. Taking one sample from a control and determining the metal composition and taking the sample obtained from evidence and determine that metal composition allows a comparison to be made.
eb25df3b79f8.key: Inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectroscopy

69086948f67f.title: Inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectroscopy
69086948f67f.sentence: ICP-AES has largely supplanted older analytical methods like gravimetric analysis for routine multi-element trace analysis.
69086948f67f.key: Inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectroscopy

da7e7ce7ce9f.title: Inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectroscopy
da7e7ce7ce9f.sentence: In 1964 Stanley Greenfield working at Albright & Wilson was the first to use ICP for non experimental analysis.
da7e7ce7ce9f.key: Inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectroscopy

dd82b8c5bf17.title: Inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry
dd82b8c5bf17.sentence: Inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) is a type of mass spectrometry that uses an inductively coupled plasma to ionize the sample.

7e6832de6c95.title: Inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry
7e6832de6c95.sentence: It is known and used for its ability to detect metals and several non-metals in liquid samples at very low concentrations.

7ff61a378744.title: Inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry
7ff61a378744.sentence: Compared to atomic absorption spectroscopy, ICP-MS has greater speed, precision, and sensitivity.

e40f2ccbd8c9.title: Inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry
e40f2ccbd8c9.sentence: Unlike atomic absorption spectroscopy, which can only measure a single element at a time, ICP-MS has the capability to scan for all elements simultaneously.

aa57da54ca91.title: Inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry
aa57da54ca91.sentence: The ICP-MS allows determination of elements with atomic mass ranges 7 to 250 (Li to U), and sometimes higher.

4a6eba71f2fe.title: Inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry
4a6eba71f2fe.sentence: With this combination, a dynamic range of 12 orders of magnitude, from 1 part per quadrillion (ppq) to 100 parts per million (ppm) is possible.

425e43475c44.title: Inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry
425e43475c44.sentence: It can detect different isotopes of the same element, which makes it a versatile tool in isotopic labeling.

2f6bb041fdbb.title: Inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry
2f6bb041fdbb.sentence: Such applications include water testing for municipalities or private individuals all the way to soil, water and other material analysis for industrial purposes.

0ed97d5f8d88.title: Pedosphere
0ed97d5f8d88.sentence: By using analytical geochemical tools such as X-ray fluorescence or inductively coupled mass spectrometry the two forms of Fe (Fe2+ and Fe3+) can be measured in ancient rocks therefore determining the redox potential for ancient soils.

d208ec39e8bd.title: Atomic absorption spectroscopy
d208ec39e8bd.sentence: Atomic absorption spectroscopy (AAS) is an elemental analysis method for determining the concentration of metals in a given sample.

4850b5832910.title: Atomic absorption spectroscopy
4850b5832910.sentence: The principle of AAS relies on the vaporization of metals within a sample when introduced to a flame.

d44cdff3af45.title: Atomic absorption spectroscopy
d44cdff3af45.sentence: Every ground state metal absorbs light radiation (and excites) at a different wavelength.

bfd3a44ea8c9.title: Atomic absorption spectroscopy
bfd3a44ea8c9.sentence: The total absorbed radiation at a specific wavelength by an element in the sample is proportional to the density of atoms of the element.

36dcf73acd09.title: Soil chemistry
36dcf73acd09.sentence: The filtrate or centrifugate then is analyzed using one of several methods, including ion specific electrodes, atomic absorption spectrophotometry, inductively coupled plasma spectrometry, ion chromatography, and colorimetric methods.

fe4b5337d6ae.title: Atomic absorption spectroscopy
fe4b5337d6ae.sentence: This technique is typically used for determinations in the mg/L range and may be extended down to a few μg/L for some elements.

80b4cec71a21.title: Atomic absorption spectroscopy
80b4cec71a21.sentence: Its sensitivity is 2–3 orders of magnitude higher than that of flame AAS, so that determinations in the low μg L−1 range (for a typical sample volume of 20 μL) and ng g−1 range (for a typical sample mass of 1 mg) can be carried out.

6cd974b1eca8.title: Atomic absorption spectroscopy
6cd974b1eca8.sentence: The modern form of AAS was largely developed during the 1950s by a team of Australian chemists led by Sir Alan Walsh at the Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation, Division of Chemical Physics, in Melbourne, Australia.

bd2e6662960d.title: Atomic absorption spectroscopy
bd2e6662960d.sentence: This variety of applications results in AAS being used in fields from agriculture to medicine.

c13f2cd1fdfa.title: Atomic absorption spectroscopy
c13f2cd1fdfa.sentence: Alan Walsh first described AAS in an article titled "The Application of Atomic Absorption Spectra to Chemical Analysis" published in 1955 by the journal Spectrachemica Acta.

accf77ed1269.title: Loss on ignition
accf77ed1269.sentence: Loss on ignition (LOI) is a test used in inorganic analytical chemistry and soil science, particularly in the analysis of minerals and the chemical makeup of soil.

b752e85d06c6.title: Loss on ignition
b752e85d06c6.sentence: It consists of strongly heating ("igniting") a sample of the material at a specified temperature, allowing volatile substances to escape, until its mass ceases to change.

6acda66de769.title: Loss on ignition
6acda66de769.sentence: The simple test typically consists of placing a few grams of the material in a tared, pre-ignited crucible and determining its mass, placing it in a temperature-controlled furnace for a set time, cooling it in a controlled (e.g., water-free, CO2-free) atmosphere, and re-determining the mass.

698f5123fc38.title: Loss on ignition
698f5123fc38.sentence: Depending on what the researcher is trying to determine in the soil, the temperature of the device can be set to the corresponding temperature.

7504a350dfc3.title: Loss on ignition
7504a350dfc3.sentence: The amount of mass lost after the LOI treatment is equal to the mass of the component the researcher is trying to determine.

c252809e1428.title: Loss on ignition
c252809e1428.sentence: A soil sample left overnight in a drying oven at 100 °C would have its water content completely evaporated by morning.

cc5543a7b54b.title: Loss on ignition
cc5543a7b54b.sentence: This could allow the researchers to determine the amount of water initially in the soil sample and its porosity by comparing the change in weight of the sample before and after the evaporation.

d87755e93853.title: Loss on ignition
d87755e93853.sentence: Typically, this method is used to determine water content levels, carbon levels, amount of organic matter levels, amount of volatile compounds.

8e74f7b436c2.title: Loss on ignition
8e74f7b436c2.sentence: The volatile materials lost usually consist of 'combined water' (hydrates and labile hydroxy-compounds) and carbon dioxide from carbonates.

db13a07e31d0.title: Geoarchaeology
db13a07e31d0.section: Techniques Used > Loss on Ignition Testing
db13a07e31d0.sentence: Samples taken from a known location in the profile, collected by column sampling, are weighed and placed in a furnace oven, which burns off the organic content.

99f0d8213ee9.title: Geoarchaeology
99f0d8213ee9.section: Techniques Used > Loss on Ignition Testing
99f0d8213ee9.sentence: The cooked sample is then weighed again, and the resulting loss in weight of the sample indicates the organic content in the profile at a given depth.

415daab0ce1a.title: Geoarchaeology
415daab0ce1a.section: Techniques Used > Loss on Ignition Testing
415daab0ce1a.sentence: This technique is often used to detect buried soil horizons that may not be visible to the naked eye.

7e4550798010.title: Geoarchaeology
7e4550798010.section: Techniques Used > Loss on Ignition Testing
7e4550798010.sentence: Comparative measurements down the profile are made, and a sudden rise in organic content at some point in the profile, combined with other indicators, is strong evidence for buried surfaces.

368c5d3115ce.title: Loss on ignition
368c5d3115ce.sentence: A variant of the test in which mass change is continually monitored as the temperature changes is called thermogravimetry.

d16b83b85dcf.title: Kjeldahl method
d16b83b85dcf.sentence: The Kjeldahl method or Kjeldahl digestion (Danish pronunciation: [ˈkʰelˌtɛˀl]) in analytical chemistry is a method for the quantitative determination of a sample's organic nitrogen plus ammonia/ammonium (NH3/NH4+).

3517fc7db6bf.title: Kjeldahl method
3517fc7db6bf.sentence: The method consists of heating a sample to 360–410 °C with concentrated sulfuric acid (H2SO4), which decomposes, or digests, the organic sample by oxidation to liberate the reduced nitrogen as stable ammonium sulfate: (NH4)2SO4.

6c3b5ded7251.title: Kjeldahl method
6c3b5ded7251.sentence: NaOH converts dissolved ammonium (NH4+) to gaseous ammonia (NH3), which boils off the sample solution.

77b5189b67e1.title: Kjeldahl method
77b5189b67e1.sentence: Ammonia bubbles through the standard acid solution and reacts back to ammonium salts with the weak or strong acid.

8299adcd277c.title: Kjeldahl method
8299adcd277c.sentence: Ammonium ion concentration in the acid solution, and thus the amount of nitrogen in the sample, is measured via titration.

1fdfc1907a46.title: Kjeldahl method
1fdfc1907a46.sentence: Without modification, other forms of inorganic nitrogen, for instance nitrate, are not included in this measurement.

1ba755975472.title: Kjeldahl method
1ba755975472.sentence: Total Kjeldahl nitrogen or TKN is the sum of nitrogen bound in organic substances, nitrogen in ammonia (NH3-N) and in ammonium (NH4+-N) in the chemical analysis of soil, water, or waste water (e.g. sewage treatment plant effluent).

65ce2e60c90e.title: Kjeldahl method
65ce2e60c90e.sentence: It is also used to assay soils, waste waters, fertilizers and other materials.

94ecb8692edd.title: Kjeldahl method
94ecb8692edd.sentence: Catalysts like selenium, Hg2SO4 or CuSO4 are often added to accelerate the digestion.

993c218c354a.title: Kjeldahl method
993c218c354a.sentence: Na2SO4 or K2SO4 is also added to increase the boiling point of H2SO4.

b2a9c547dfec.title: Kjeldahl method
b2a9c547dfec.sentence: Additional disadvantages, such as the need to use concentrated sulfuric acid at high temperature and the relatively long testing time (an hour or more), compare unfavorably with the Dumas method for measuring crude protein content.

a7de1b24e7c3.title: Kjeldahl method
a7de1b24e7c3.sentence: This method was developed by the Danish chemist Johan Kjeldahl in 1883.

5e5caebf657d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.03%3A_Accuracy_of_Recommendations_Based_on_Soil_Tests
5e5caebf657d.section: Asking The Plant What It Thinks
5e5caebf657d.sentence: The ultimate word about the quality of a test is whether a crop will respond to added fertilizer the way a test value indicates it should.

af805541cd2d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.03%3A_Accuracy_of_Recommendations_Based_on_Soil_Tests
af805541cd2d.section: Asking The Plant What It Thinks
af805541cd2d.sentence: Without running these experiments—evaluating yield increases with added fertilizer at different soil test levels—there is no way to know what is considered a “good” soil test.

10fb313bcb37.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.03%3A_Accuracy_of_Recommendations_Based_on_Soil_Tests
10fb313bcb37.sentence: Soil tests and their recommendations, although a critical component of fertility management, are not 100% accurate.

f98f2fedcff0.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.03%3A_Accuracy_of_Recommendations_Based_on_Soil_Tests
f98f2fedcff0.sentence: Soil tests are an estimate of a limited number of plant nutrients based on a small sample, which is supposed to represent many acres in a field.

b0ea35395e99.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.03%3A_Accuracy_of_Recommendations_Based_on_Soil_Tests
b0ea35395e99.section: Asking The Plant What It Thinks
b0ea35395e99.sentence: They do this by running experiments over a number of years on many different fields around the state or region.

ab46e26d7da9.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.03%3A_Accuracy_of_Recommendations_Based_on_Soil_Tests
ab46e26d7da9.section: Asking The Plant What It Thinks
ab46e26d7da9.sentence: This is done by first taking a soil sample and then laying out plots and applying a few different levels of the nutrient (let’s say P) to the different plots, always including plots that received no added P. When crops are harvested in each plot, it is possible to determine what the plant “thought” about the soil test level.

d8fa154d4f85.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.03%3A_Accuracy_of_Recommendations_Based_on_Soil_Tests
d8fa154d4f85.section: Asking The Plant What It Thinks
d8fa154d4f85.sentence: If the plant was not able to get enough of the nutrient in the control plots, there will be a yield increase between those and the plots receiving P application.

2dd17207be64.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.03%3A_Accuracy_of_Recommendations_Based_on_Soil_Tests
2dd17207be64.section: Asking The Plant What It Thinks
2dd17207be64.sentence: But until the multi-year effort of correlating a proposed test with plant response is made on a variety of soil and under various weather conditions, it is not possible to know if the test is useful or not.

ea7d0af05e11.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.03%3A_Accuracy_of_Recommendations_Based_on_Soil_Tests
ea7d0af05e11.section: Asking The Plant What It Thinks
ea7d0af05e11.sentence: Also, this type of research is often first done on small plots on research farms and needs to be validated in fields of commercial farms.

f18bff65e2cc.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.03%3A_Accuracy_of_Recommendations_Based_on_Soil_Tests
f18bff65e2cc.sentence: This could happen if the soil test is not well calibrated for the particular soil in question (and because the soil had sufficient availability of the nutrient for the crop despite the low test level) or because of harm caused by poor drainage or compaction.

9c6a822ce12e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.03%3A_Accuracy_of_Recommendations_Based_on_Soil_Tests
9c6a822ce12e.sentence: Occasionally, using extra nutrients on a high-testing soil increases crop yields.

ee1e9199c334.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.03%3A_Accuracy_of_Recommendations_Based_on_Soil_Tests
ee1e9199c334.sentence: Weather conditions may have made the nutrient less available than indicated by the soil test.

5100a2ff02e4.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.02%3A_Taking_Soil_Samples
5100a2ff02e4.sentence: The usual time to take soil samples for general fertility evaluation is in the fall or the spring, before the growing season has begun.

25b74b2a541c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.02%3A_Taking_Soil_Samples
25b74b2a541c.sentence: - Take cores from at least 15–20 spots randomly selected over the field (or a zone in a field) to obtain a representative sample.

3e2de7537865.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.02%3A_Taking_Soil_Samples
3e2de7537865.sentence: These samples are analyzed for pH and lime requirements as well as for phosphorus, potassium, calcium and magnesium.

e910ed3a115d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.02%3A_Taking_Soil_Samples
e910ed3a115d.sentence: Whether you sample a particular field in the fall or in the early spring, stay consistent and repeat samples at approximately the same time of the year and use the same laboratory for analysis.

9ff091247492.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.02%3A_Taking_Soil_Samples
9ff091247492.sentence: Taking many cores for a single sample is critical for obtaining meaningful soil test results, independent of the size of the field or zone.

bcd6bfa818af.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.02%3A_Taking_Soil_Samples
bcd6bfa818af.sentence: One sample should not represent more than 10–20 acres.

02f25a3e48b2.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.02%3A_Taking_Soil_Samples
02f25a3e48b2.sentence: For precision zone or grid fertility management, consider a sample for every 1–5 acres.

3680eb1ddc14.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.02%3A_Taking_Soil_Samples
3680eb1ddc14.sentence: Avoid old fence rows, dead furrows and other spots that are not representative of the whole field.

38050528e52d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.02%3A_Taking_Soil_Samples
38050528e52d.sentence: - Take separate samples from problem areas if they can be treated separately.

20bf7c6ed355.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.02%3A_Taking_Soil_Samples
20bf7c6ed355.sentence: - Soils are not homogeneous: nutrient levels can vary widely with different crop histories or topographic settings.

1959e498f102.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.02%3A_Taking_Soil_Samples
1959e498f102.sentence: - In cultivated fields, sample to plow depth.

55b1a9af6cfa.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.02%3A_Taking_Soil_Samples
55b1a9af6cfa.sentence: - Sample permanent pastures to a 3- or 4-inch depth.

ad5d7455c6a0.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.02%3A_Taking_Soil_Samples
ad5d7455c6a0.sentence: - Take two samples from no-till fields: one to a 6-inch depth for lime and fertilizer recommendations, and one to a 2-inch depth to monitor surface acidity.

80bf093dc0a4.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.02%3A_Taking_Soil_Samples
80bf093dc0a4.sentence: - Collect the samples in a clean container.

f2fb8a9b83c1.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.02%3A_Taking_Soil_Samples
f2fb8a9b83c1.sentence: - Mix the core samplings, remove roots and stones, and allow the mixed sample to air dry.

955e2af428d4.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.02%3A_Taking_Soil_Samples
955e2af428d4.sentence: - Sample fields at least every three years and at the same season of the year each time.

06e0d0ab9d74.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.06%3A_Soil_Testing_for_P
06e0d0ab9d74.sentence: The methods used to estimate available P vary from region to region and sometimes from state to state within a region (Table 21.1).

2c452d9a13c6.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.06%3A_Soil_Testing_for_P
2c452d9a13c6.sentence: Although the relative test value for a given soil is usually similar according to different soil tests (for example, a soil testing high in P by one procedure is generally also high by another procedure), the actual numbers can be different (Table 21.2).

aea66d590dc8.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.05%3A_Soil_Testing_for_Nitrogen
aea66d590dc8.sentence: Arid and semiarid Midwest, west, and northwest | Olsen AB-DTPA

e187bc8cc174.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.05%3A_Soil_Testing_for_Nitrogen
e187bc8cc174.sentence: Humid Midwest, mid-Atlantic, Southeast, and eastern Canada | Mehlich 3 Bray 1 (also called Bray P-1 or Bray-Kurtz P)

1324482fefad.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.05%3A_Soil_Testing_for_Nitrogen
1324482fefad.sentence: Northeast (New York and parts of New England), some labs in Idaho and Washington | Morgan or modified Morgan Mehlich 3

4877c5b3ff72.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.05%3A_Soil_Testing_for_Nitrogen
4877c5b3ff72.sentence: Washington and Oregon | Bray 1 for acidic soils Olsen for alkaline soils

735b1f1f40bf.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.05%3A_Soil_Testing_for_Nitrogen
735b1f1f40bf.sentence: Some labs also have a Very High category. **If the soil is calcareous (has free calcium carbonate in the soil), the Olsen soil test “optimum” range would be higher, with over 25 ppm soil test P for a zero P fertilizer recommendation.

63cbf7122916.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.05%3A_Soil_Testing_for_Nitrogen
63cbf7122916.sentence: Also note: Units are in parts per million phosphorus (ppm P), and ranges used for recommendations may vary from state to state; Low and Medium indicates a high to moderate probability to increase yield by adding P fertilizer; Optimum indicates that there is a low probability for increasing yield with added P fertilizer; High soil test levels indicate increasing potential for P pollution in runoff.

57ab7128a1f3.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.06%3A_Soil_Testing_for_P
57ab7128a1f3.sentence: The various soil tests for P take into account a large portion of the available P contained in recently applied manures and the amount that will become available from the soil minerals.

2d8c18ebc882.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.06%3A_Soil_Testing_for_P
2d8c18ebc882.sentence: However, if there is a large amount of active organic matter in your soils from crop residues or manure additions in previous years, there may well be more available P for plants than indicated by the soil test.

9603c15869f1.title: Ion chromatography
9603c15869f1.sentence: Ion chromatography (or ion-exchange chromatography; abbreviated IC or IEC) is a form of chromatography that separates ions and ionizable polar molecules based on their affinity to the ion exchanger.

31702ba6bdc4.title: Ion chromatography
31702ba6bdc4.sentence: Anion-exchange chromatography is when the stationary phase is positively charged and negatively charged molecules (meaning that pH for chromatography is greater than the pI) are loaded to be attracted to it.

b7c71364dd8f.title: Ion chromatography
b7c71364dd8f.sentence: In this type of chromatography, the stationary phase is negatively charged and positively charged molecules are loaded to be attracted to it.

45417f860912.title: Ion chromatography
45417f860912.sentence: It is a popular method for analyzing anionic elements or complexes that help solve environmentally relevant problems.

5e3ae6e3bb9a.title: Ion chromatography
5e3ae6e3bb9a.sentence: Ion chromatography was originally introduced by two English researchers, agricultural Sir Thompson and chemist J T Way.

6662e69a07a7.title: Ion chromatography
6662e69a07a7.sentence: They performed ion methods to treat clays with the salts, resulting in the extraction of ammonia in addition to the release of calcium.

d8bb1383c3fd.title: Sample preparation
d8bb1383c3fd.sentence: In analytical chemistry, sample preparation (working-up) refers to the ways in which a sample is treated prior to its analyses.

a007c1bb8d5d.title: Sample preparation
a007c1bb8d5d.sentence: Preparation is a very important step in most analytical techniques, because the techniques are often not responsive to the analyte in its in-situ form, or the results are distorted by interfering species.

30b7fa628dd6.title: Sample preparation
30b7fa628dd6.sentence: Sample preparation could involve: crushing and dissolution, chemical digestion with acid or alkali, sample extraction, sample clean up and sample pre-concentration.

63a2d95d5d66.title: Sample preparation
63a2d95d5d66.sentence: Sample preparation may involve dissolution, extraction, reaction with some chemical species, pulverizing, treatment with a chelating agent (e.g. EDTA), masking, filtering, dilution, sub-sampling or many other techniques.

1b18373e12af.title: Certified reference materials
1b18373e12af.sentence: Certified reference materials (CRMs) are 'controls' or standards used to check the quality and metrological traceability of products, to validate analytical measurement methods, or for the calibration of instruments.

811ca05ebb7b.title: Certified reference materials
811ca05ebb7b.sentence: Since most analytical instrumentation is comparative, it requires a sample of known composition (reference material) for accurate calibration.

d28803ed6e53.title: Certified reference materials
d28803ed6e53.sentence: These reference materials are produced under stringent manufacturing procedures and differ from laboratory reagents in their certification and the traceability of the data provided.

6b3f876565d2.title: Certified reference materials
6b3f876565d2.sentence: Reference material characterized by a metrologically valid procedure for one or more specified properties, accompanied by a certificate that provides the value of the specified property, its associated uncertainty, and a statement of metrological traceability.

7609e494308e.title: Certified reference materials
7609e494308e.sentence: Quality management systems involving laboratory accreditation under national and international accreditation/certification standards such as ISO/IEC 17025 require metrological traceability to Certified Reference Materials (where possible) when using reference materials for calibration.

c31935438abb.title: Certified reference materials
c31935438abb.sentence: Certified Reference Materials are preferred where available.

17cedbb31b5c.title: Certified reference materials
17cedbb31b5c.sentence: ILAC describes the following five types of reference material:

af1e96f41304.title: Certified reference materials
af1e96f41304.sentence: - Pure substances; essentially pure chemicals, characterised for chemical purity and/or trace impurities.

b45103d87f0a.title: Certified reference materials
b45103d87f0a.sentence: - Standard solutions and gas mixtures, often prepared gravimetrically from pure substances.

8c0ae9adf735.title: Certified reference materials
8c0ae9adf735.sentence: - Matrix reference materials, characterised for the composition of specified major, minor or trace chemical constituents.

e7753f57f94d.title: Certified reference materials
e7753f57f94d.sentence: - Physico-chemical reference materials, characterised for properties such as melting point, viscosity, or optical density.

78554f64748e.title: Certified reference materials
78554f64748e.sentence: - Reference objects or artifacts, characterised for functional properties such as taste, odour, octane number, flash point and hardness.

b6b834b73bdd.title: Certified reference materials
b6b834b73bdd.sentence: These are typically produced by homogenization of a naturally occurring material followed by measurement of each analyte.

b91ec0ced843.title: Certified reference materials
b91ec0ced843.sentence: For natural materials, homogenization is often critical; natural materials are rarely homogeneous on the scale of grams so production of a solid natural matrix reference material typically involves processing to a fine powder or paste.

561ba516af07.title: Certified reference materials
561ba516af07.sentence: Typically 10-30 CRM units are taken from the batch at random; stratified random sampling is recommended so that the selected units are spread across the batch.

da0b2b1b4bb9.title: Certified reference materials
da0b2b1b4bb9.sentence: An equal number of subsamples (usually two or three) is then taken from each CRM unit and measured.

2c42cf93ec9a.title: Certified reference materials
2c42cf93ec9a.section: Production > Stability assessment > Stability assessment and testing strategies
2c42cf93ec9a.sentence: There are two important strategies for CRM stability testing; simple real-time studies and accelerated testing.

c625dcd378bb.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.10%3A_Adjusting_a_Soil_Test_Recommendation
c625dcd378bb.sentence: Category | Very low | Low | Optimum | High | Excessive

d5574e600afe.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.10%3A_Adjusting_a_Soil_Test_Recommendation
d5574e600afe.sentence: Probability of response to added nutrient | Very high | High | Low | Very low

48465db0e3ac.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.10%3A_Adjusting_a_Soil_Test_Recommendation
48465db0e3ac.sentence: *Soil sample taken to 1 foot when corn is 6–12 inches tall.

58718bfb592c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.10%3A_Adjusting_a_Soil_Test_Recommendation
58718bfb592c.sentence: Most soil test reports use information that you supply about manure use and previous crops to adapt a general recommendation to your situation.

1b056c401ed4.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.10%3A_Adjusting_a_Soil_Test_Recommendation
1b056c401ed4.sentence: Also, you usually don’t get credit for the nitrogen produced by legume cover crops because most forms don’t even ask about their use.

08a5d91f4ba2.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.10%3A_Adjusting_a_Soil_Test_Recommendation
08a5d91f4ba2.sentence: What happens if you decide to apply manure after you sent in the form along with the soil sample?

4ef0e3db6352.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.09%3A_Interpreting_Soil_Test_Results
4ef0e3db6352.sentence: We’ve come across unusual soil test results from time to time.

3faf2868cf7f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.09%3A_Interpreting_Soil_Test_Results
3faf2868cf7f.sentence: A few examples and their typical causes:

ab336e78e967.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.09%3A_Interpreting_Soil_Test_Results
ab336e78e967.sentence: - Very high phosphorus levels: high poultry or other manure application over many years.

a320ec0bc8c3.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.09%3A_Interpreting_Soil_Test_Results
a320ec0bc8c3.sentence: - Very high pH and high calcium levels relative to potassium and magnesium: large amounts of lime-stabilized sewage sludge used.

b5050c32e922.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.09%3A_Interpreting_Soil_Test_Results
b5050c32e922.sentence: - Very high salt concentration in humid regions: recent application of large amounts of poultry manure in high tunnel greenhouses where rainfall is not able to leach salts, or located immediately adjacent to a road where deicing salt was used.

5b187869de34.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.09%3A_Interpreting_Soil_Test_Results
5b187869de34.sentence: - Very high calcium levels given the soil’s texture and organic matter content: the soil test used an acid solution, such as the Morgan, Mehlich 1 or Mehlich 3, to extract soils containing free limestone, causing some of the lime to dissolve.

107a92f2a8e0.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.09%3A_Interpreting_Soil_Test_Results
107a92f2a8e0.sentence: - Soil pH >7 and very low P: the soil test used an acid such as found in Mehlich I, Bray or Mehlich 3 on an alkaline, calcareous soil.

16cf4d8e0ef4.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.09%3A_Interpreting_Soil_Test_Results
16cf4d8e0ef4.sentence: (In this case, the soil neutralizes much of the acid, so little P is extracted.)

ea80b1aaf31c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.09%3A_Interpreting_Soil_Test_Results
ea80b1aaf31c.sentence: Many labs estimate the CEC that would exist at pH 7 (or even higher).

71ef49c08b63.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.09%3A_Interpreting_Soil_Test_Results
71ef49c08b63.sentence: Because we feel that the soil’s current CEC is of most interest (see Chapter 20), the CEC is estimated by summing the exchangeable bases.

168f31609568.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.05%3A_Soil_Testing_for_Nitrogen
168f31609568.sentence: Since nitrogen management is a challenge for many of the common crops (corn, wheat, rice, oilseed rape, etc.) and is also an expensive input, there has been a significant amount of research into new technologies that allow a farmer or consultant to assess a crop’s N status during the season.

8d44bb66acc0.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.05%3A_Soil_Testing_for_Nitrogen
8d44bb66acc0.sentence: Generally four types of approaches are used:

2c4b818fdbe0.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.05%3A_Soil_Testing_for_Nitrogen
2c4b818fdbe0.sentence: - Chlorophyll meters are handheld devices that indirectly estimate chlorophyll content in a crop leaf, which is an indicator of its N status (Figure 21.3, left).

264f01dfaf18.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.05%3A_Soil_Testing_for_Nitrogen
264f01dfaf18.sentence: It requires field visits and adequate leaf sampling to represent different zones in the field.

820d9aad1322.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.05%3A_Soil_Testing_for_Nitrogen
820d9aad1322.sentence: They are primarily used for final fertilizer applications in cereals, especially when aiming for certain protein contents.

fd31850f0893.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.05%3A_Soil_Testing_for_Nitrogen
fd31850f0893.sentence: - Canopy reflectance sensors can be handheld or equipment-mounted devices that measure reflectance without contacting the leaf (Figure 21.3, right).

9d70b85f0c83.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.05%3A_Soil_Testing_for_Nitrogen
9d70b85f0c83.sentence: Both sense the light reflectance properties of a crop canopy in the near infrared and red (or red-edge) bands, which can be related to crop growth and N uptake.

862df0340967.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.05%3A_Soil_Testing_for_Nitrogen
862df0340967.sentence: When equipment mounted, it allows for on-the-go adjustment of N rates throughout a field, which in most cases also requires the establishment of a high-N reference strip in the field for use in calibrating the sensor.

05dc3a342f45.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.05%3A_Soil_Testing_for_Nitrogen
05dc3a342f45.sentence: - Satellite, aircraft or drone imagery can be used to extract reflectance information that can be related to a crop’s N status (Figure 21.4, left), usually also using near infrared and red/red-edge bands, with resolutions in the 30–90 foot (10–30 meter) range.

9596bdc544fb.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.05%3A_Soil_Testing_for_Nitrogen
9596bdc544fb.sentence: The satellite-derived images are generally available every few days but are highly impacted by cloud cover, which can obstruct fields during critical decision times.

259a5d623329.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.05%3A_Soil_Testing_for_Nitrogen
259a5d623329.sentence: Aircraft and drone imaging can avoid cloud issues but are more expensive.

bfadeea701db.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.05%3A_Soil_Testing_for_Nitrogen
bfadeea701db.sentence: - Computer models simulate a field’s N dynamics and allow for daily estimation of the soil and crop N status (Figure 21.4, right).

d13ac864e5ab.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.05%3A_Soil_Testing_for_Nitrogen
d13ac864e5ab.sentence: Use of computer models is relatively inexpensive and scalable.

fe6272e9bd9c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.05%3A_Soil_Testing_for_Nitrogen
fe6272e9bd9c.sentence: It allows for daily monitoring and is good at integrating other data sources into recommendations, but it does not involve direct field observations.

154dd8a306b2.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.12%3A_Managing_Field_Nutrient_Variability
154dd8a306b2.sentence: Many large fields have considerable variation in soil types and fertility levels.

ab21932e1819.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.12%3A_Managing_Field_Nutrient_Variability
ab21932e1819.sentence: Aside from when automated sensors and models are used to determine nitrogen fertilizer needs, site-specific management requires the collection of multiple soil samples within the field, which are then analyzed separately.

c75d1e98c3fe.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.12%3A_Managing_Field_Nutrient_Variability
c75d1e98c3fe.sentence: The general recommendation is for 2.5- to 5-acre grid sampling, especially for fields that have received variable manure and fertilizer rates.

8a66b63258a9.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.12%3A_Managing_Field_Nutrient_Variability
8a66b63258a9.sentence: In some areas, one-acre grids are sampled.

fb0393197af6.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.12%3A_Managing_Field_Nutrient_Variability
fb0393197af6.sentence: The suggested sampling procedure is called unaligned because in order to get a better picture of the field as a whole, grid points should not follow a straight line because you may unknowingly pick up a past applicator malfunction.

7706e5fe9a51.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.12%3A_Managing_Field_Nutrient_Variability
7706e5fe9a51.sentence: Grid points can be designed with the use of precision agriculture software packages or by ensuring that sampling points are taken by moving a few feet off the regular grid in random directions (Figure 21.5).

9b89c6777415.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.12%3A_Managing_Field_Nutrient_Variability
9b89c6777415.sentence: Grid sampling still requires 10–15 individual cores to be taken within about a 30-foot area around each grid point.

75992d2d9564.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.12%3A_Managing_Field_Nutrient_Variability
75992d2d9564.sentence: Grid soil testing may not be needed every time you sample the field—it is an expensive and time-consuming effort—but it is recommended to evaluate site-specific nutrient levels in larger fields at least once in a rotation, each time lime may be needed, or every five to eight years.

aef43a703cdf.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.12%3A_Managing_Field_Nutrient_Variability
aef43a703cdf.sentence: Sometimes, sampling is done based on mapping units from a soil survey, but in many cases the fertility patterns don’t follow the soil maps.

f737d6b772fb.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.13%3A_Testing_High_Tunnel_Soils
f737d6b772fb.sentence: Because of the high nutrient levels that are needed in tunnels, fertilizer recommendations based on routine "field soil tests" (using extracts to estimate availability of reserve nutrients) must be adjusted upwards.

62c62ae15c62.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.13%3A_Testing_High_Tunnel_Soils
62c62ae15c62.sentence: In addition, because transplants are expected to start growing immediately after being set in the tunnels, and because rainfall does not leach salts from the soil, a "potting soil test" such as the saturated media extract is also useful.

30e2e1af6972.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.13%3A_Testing_High_Tunnel_Soils
30e2e1af6972.sentence: With a longer growing season, good cultural practices, pest management and sufficient nutrients, tomatoes can yield many times what is achievable outdoors, reaching the equivalent of 60–80 tons per acre.

e31ec81190e7.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.13%3A_Testing_High_Tunnel_Soils
e31ec81190e7.sentence: The amount of nutrients needed by such large yields is impressive: equivalent to 200–300 pounds of N, 300–400 pounds of phosphate (P2O5) and 700–900 pounds of potash (K2O) per acre.

661345ddafa7.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/21%3A_Analyzing_Your_Soil_and_Crop/21.13%3A_Testing_High_Tunnel_Soils
661345ddafa7.sentence: That test measures water-soluble nutrient levels (immediately available nutrients), including nitrate-N and ammonium-N, as well as salinity (total salt) levels.

edccfdd71a20.title: Soil horizon
edccfdd71a20.section: Horizons and layers according to the World Reference Base for Soil Resources
edccfdd71a20.sentence: The whole soil comprises fine earth, coarse fragments, artefacts, cemented parts, and dead plant residues of any size.

37969720cb14.title: Granite
37969720cb14.sentence: Feldspars also weather slowly in cool climes, allowing sand to dominate the fine-earth fraction.

752b8120034b.title: Ion-selective electrode
752b8120034b.sentence: An ion-selective electrode (ISE), also known as a specific ion electrode (SIE), is a simple membrane-based potentiometric device which measures the activity of ions in solution.

83bb1a53c134.title: Ion-selective electrode
83bb1a53c134.sentence: It is a transducer (or sensor) that converts the change in the concentration of a specific ion dissolved in a solution into an electrical potential.

bdf1ca31330e.title: Ion-selective electrode
bdf1ca31330e.sentence: The voltage is theoretically dependent on the logarithm of the ionic activity, according to the Nernst equation.

920601794706.title: Ion-selective electrode
920601794706.sentence: All ISE measurements are made with a comparison to an internal reference electrode with a known concentration of the analyte being measured.

7ce219c1b0ac.title: Ion-selective electrode
7ce219c1b0ac.section: Types of ion-selective membrane > Glass membranes
7ce219c1b0ac.sentence: A very common example of this type of electrode is the pH glass electrode.

0f0c83db5715.title: Ion-selective electrode
0f0c83db5715.sentence: Analysis with ISEs expands throughout a range of technological fields such as biology, chemistry, environmental science and other industrial workplaces like agriculture.

0b133fc2cc97.title: Ion-selective electrode
0b133fc2cc97.sentence: The response of the electrode and galvanometer is temperature sensitive, and also 'drifts' over time, requiring recalibration frequently during a series of measurements, ideally at least one calibration sample before and after each test sample.

71b83f85bfd0.title: Ammonium acetate
71b83f85bfd0.sentence: - a reagent in agricultural chemistry for determination of soil CEC (cation exchange capacity) and determination of available potassium in soil wherein the ammonium ion acts as a replacement cation for potassium.

7989f183e248.title: Ammonium acetate
7989f183e248.sentence: When dissolving ammonium acetate in pure water, the resulting solution typically has a pH of 7, because the equal amounts of acetate and ammonium neutralize each other.

4cfd0e2fc7e2.title: Ammonium acetate

915e662cdceb.sentence: This uses the 'molybdate blue' reaction, where the depth of the colour is proportional to phosphorus concentration.

37a981a58921.title: Molybdenum blue
37a981a58921.section: Uses in quantitative analysis > Colorimetric determination of P, As, Si and Ge

19a3f690b2d5.sentence: This anion is then reduced by, for example, ascorbic acid or SnCl2, to form the blue coloured β-keggin ion, PMo 12O7− 40.

18a1f1c2abbc.title: Geoarchaeology
18a1f1c2abbc.section: Techniques Used > Phosphate and Orthophosphate Content with Spectrophotometry
18a1f1c2abbc.sentence: Whatever method is used to get the phosphorus from the soil into solution, the process of detecting it is usually the same.

6b37dccea9cc.title: Geoarchaeology
6b37dccea9cc.section: Techniques Used > Phosphate and Orthophosphate Content with Spectrophotometry
6b37dccea9cc.sentence: In the lab, this is measured using a colorimeter, in which light passing through a standard cell produces an electric current proportional to the light attenuation.

75b942bae328.title: Geoarchaeology
75b942bae328.section: Techniques Used > Phosphate and Orthophosphate Content with Spectrophotometry
75b942bae328.sentence: In the field, the same reaction is used on detector sticks compared to a colour chart.

3a011e2094ba.title: Molybdenum blue

3a011e2094ba.sentence: This colorimetric method is ineffective when comparable amounts of arsenate are present in solution with phosphate.

660fc5d0f322.title: Molybdenum blue

ea4e2b5f2f40.title: Geoarchaeology
