ea4e2b5f2f40.sentence: Phosphate concentrations can be plotted on archaeological plans to show former activity areas and are also used to prospect for sites on the broader landscape.

9a256dd4097e.title: Soil morphology
9a256dd4097e.sentence: Soil micromorphology refers to the description, measurement, and interpretation of soil features that are too small to be observed by the unassisted eye.

69d4e7405735.title: Soil morphology
69d4e7405735.sentence: While micromorphological descriptions may begin in the field with the use of a 10x hand lens, much more can be described using thin sections made of the soil with the aid of a petrographic polarizing light microscope.

9c9e238048c0.title: Soil morphology
9c9e238048c0.sentence: Soil micromorphology has been a recognized technique in soil science for some 50 years and experience from pedogenic and paleosol studies first permitted its use in the investigation of archaeologically buried soils.

ddac2d2774b9.title: Soil morphology
ddac2d2774b9.sentence: More recently, the science has expanded to encompass the characterization of all archeological soils and sediments and has been successful in providing unique cultural and paleoenvironmental information from a whole range of archaeological sites.

aece27e78a39.title: Thin section
aece27e78a39.sentence: In optical mineralogy and petrography, a thin section (or petrographic thin section) is a thin slice of a rock or mineral sample, prepared in a laboratory, for use with a polarizing petrographic microscope, electron microscope and electron microprobe.

66d6a50bddad.title: Thin section
66d6a50bddad.sentence: It is then mounted on a glass slide and then ground smooth using progressively finer abrasive grit until the sample is only 30 μm thick.

0828f1eddd9a.title: Thin section
0828f1eddd9a.sentence: When placed between two polarizing filters set at right angles to each other, the optical properties of the minerals in the thin section alter the colour and intensity of the light as seen by the viewer.

547bc68bc525.title: Thin section
547bc68bc525.sentence: As different minerals have different optical properties, most rock-forming minerals can be easily identified.

0c2f71478525.title: Thin section
0c2f71478525.sentence: The method uses the Michel-Lévy interference colour chart to determine thickness, typically using quartz as the thickness gauge because it is one of the most abundant minerals.

fed975c626ff.title: Optical mineralogy
fed975c626ff.sentence: The structure of the rock - the relation of its components to one another - is usually clearly indicated, whether it is fragmented or massive; the presence of glassy matter in contradistinction to a completely crystalline or "holo-crystalline" condition; the nature and origin of organic fragments; banding, foliation or lamination; the pumiceous or porous structure of many lavas.

83bba30681b3.title: Optical mineralogy
83bba30681b3.sentence: These and many other characters, though often not visible in the hand specimens of a rock, are rendered obvious by the examination of a microscopic section.

8418aa2a720b.title: Paleosol
8418aa2a720b.section: Identification > Soil types > Andisol (volcanic ash soil)
8418aa2a720b.sentence: At least 60% recognizable pyroclastic fragments in thin sections are characteristic of this paleosol.

5dd05a04744a.title: Image analysis
5dd05a04744a.sentence: Image analysis or imagery analysis is the extraction of meaningful information from images; mainly from digital images by means of digital image processing techniques.

73a7138c91d1.title: Image analysis
73a7138c91d1.sentence: Computers are indispensable for the analysis of large amounts of data, for tasks that require complex computation, or for the extraction of quantitative information.

d4974f0d4e89.title: Image analysis
d4974f0d4e89.sentence: On the other hand, the human visual cortex is an excellent image analysis apparatus, especially for extracting higher-level information, and for many applications — including medicine, security, and remote sensing — human analysts still cannot be replaced by computers.

f2169bb355e2.title: Image analysis
f2169bb355e2.sentence: Object-based image analysis (OBIA) involves two typical processes, segmentation and classification.

5b310a0148cc.title: Image analysis
5b310a0148cc.sentence: Segmentation helps to group pixels into homogeneous objects.

6e3a588d83cf.title: Image analysis
6e3a588d83cf.sentence: Over-segmentation is often preferred over under-segmentation when classifying high-resolution images.

28097d733a6c.title: Image analysis
28097d733a6c.sentence: - metallography, such as determining the mineral content of a rock sample.

3742b4ac51b3.title: Soil biomantle
3742b4ac51b3.sentence: The criterion, however, becomes moot and irrelevant in the case of megabiofabric produced in some biomantles – namely the cloddy and chunky surface-spoil heaps produced by small-to-large burrowing vertebrates (rodents, badgers, aardvarks, elephants) and by tree uprooting.

dbfc7b8180e7.title: Polarized light microscopy
dbfc7b8180e7.sentence: Polarized light microscopy can mean any of a number of optical microscopy techniques involving polarized light.

d53e6b7a8109.title: Polarized light microscopy
d53e6b7a8109.sentence: These illumination techniques are most commonly used on birefringent samples where the polarized light interacts strongly with the sample and so generates contrast with the background.

6be4e512ef4c.title: Polarized light microscopy
6be4e512ef4c.sentence: Scientists will often use a device called a polarizing plate to convert natural light into polarized light.

86f6e65c9603.title: Polarized light microscopy
86f6e65c9603.sentence: Polarized light microscopy is used extensively in optical mineralogy.

097b93180a3d.title: Polarized light microscopy
097b93180a3d.sentence: More complex microscopy techniques which take advantage of polarized light include differential interference contrast microscopy and interference reflection microscopy.

19e60c666ca2.title: Mineral alteration
19e60c666ca2.sentence: Mineral alteration is the various natural processes that alter a mineral's chemical composition or crystallography.

ace129d73830.title: Optical mineralogy
ace129d73830.sentence: Some minerals decompose readily and become turbid and semi-transparent (e.g. feldspar); others remain always perfectly fresh and clear (e.g. quartz), while others yield characteristic secondary products (such as green chlorite after biotite).

b0914de4c54d.title: Mineral alteration
b0914de4c54d.sentence: Mineral alteration is essentially governed by the laws of thermodynamics related to energy conservation, relevant to environmental conditions, often in presence of catalysts, the most common and influential being water (H2O).

a0ecb47a0556.title: X-ray microtomography
a0ecb47a0556.sentence: In radiography, X-ray microtomography uses X-rays to create cross-sections of a physical object that can be used to recreate a virtual model (3D model) without destroying the original object.

9dc46637a5ae.title: X-ray microtomography
9dc46637a5ae.sentence: These pixel sizes have also resulted in creation of its synonyms high-resolution X-ray tomography, micro-computed tomography (micro-CT or μCT), and similar terms.

3fe6d4424f57.title: X-ray microtomography
3fe6d4424f57.sentence: In one setup, the X-ray source and detector are typically stationary during the scan while the sample/animal rotates.

5dd99bfa7ec0.title: X-ray microtomography
5dd99bfa7ec0.sentence: The second setup, much more like a clinical CT scanner, is gantry based where the animal/specimen is stationary in space while the X-ray tube and detector rotate around.

d7455c5f7063.title: X-ray microtomography
d7455c5f7063.section: Working principle > Imaging system > Cone beam reconstruction
d7455c5f7063.sentence: The cone-beam system is based on a 2D X-ray detector (camera) and an electronic X-ray source, creating projection images that later will be used to reconstruct the image cross-sections.

adc771399865.title: X-ray microtomography
adc771399865.sentence: Instead, it is possible for a software program to build a volume by 'stacking' the individual slices one on top of the other.

be5617134516.title: X-ray microtomography
be5617134516.sentence: This is an example of a regular volumetric grid, with each volume element, or voxel represented by a single value that is obtained by sampling the immediate area surrounding the voxel.

29cf5c9582aa.title: X-ray microtomography
29cf5c9582aa.sentence: Where different structures have similar threshold density, it can become impossible to separate them simply by adjusting volume rendering parameters.

006c4221bbd7.title: X-ray microtomography
006c4221bbd7.sentence: The solution is called segmentation, a manual or automatic procedure that can remove the unwanted structures from the image.

096811c46e91.title: X-ray microtomography
096811c46e91.sentence: In geology it is used to analyze micro pores in the reservoir rocks, it can be used in microfacies analysis for sequence stratigraphy.

ce8f0a395aeb.title: Spatial analysis
ce8f0a395aeb.sentence: Spatial analysis is any of the formal techniques which study entities using their topological, geometric, or geographic properties, primarily used in urban design.

8d80493fbad0.title: Spatial analysis
8d80493fbad0.sentence: Spatial analysis includes a variety of techniques using different analytic approaches, especially spatial statistics.

975a37e42153.title: Spatial analysis
975a37e42153.sentence: Spatial interpolation methods estimate the variables at unobserved locations in geographic space based on the values at observed locations.

40ee1959f709.title: Spatial analysis
40ee1959f709.sentence: Spatial regression methods capture spatial dependency in regression analysis, avoiding statistical problems such as unstable parameters and unreliable significance tests, as well as providing information on spatial relationships among the variables involved.

41593099a2a2.title: Spatial analysis
41593099a2a2.sentence: Spatial autocorrelation statistics measure and analyze the degree of dependency among observations in a geographic space.

772620dea863.title: Spatial analysis
772620dea863.sentence: Classic spatial autocorrelation statistics include Moran's I, Geary's C, Getis's G and the standard deviational ellipse.

089b981caf17.title: Spatial analysis
089b981caf17.section: Geospatial and hydrospatial analysis > Geographical information system usage
089b981caf17.sentence: Geographic information systems (GIS) — a large domain that provides a variety of capabilities designed to capture, store, manipulate, analyze, manage, and present all types of geographical data — utilizes geospatial and hydrospatial analysis in a variety of contexts, operations and applications.

27e4562e5716.title: Spatial analysis
27e4562e5716.section: Geospatial and hydrospatial analysis > Geographical information system usage > Basic operations
27e4562e5716.sentence: Vector-based GIS is typically related to operations such as map overlay (combining two or more maps or map layers according to predefined rules), simple buffering (identifying regions of a map within a specified distance of one or more features, such as towns, roads or rivers) and similar basic operations.

92cad5c05d11.title: Spatial analysis
92cad5c05d11.section: Fundamental issues > Common errors in spatial analysis > Ecological fallacy
92cad5c05d11.sentence: The ecological fallacy describes errors due to performing analyses on aggregate data when trying to reach conclusions on the individual units.

544b2cb14973.title: Spatial analysis
544b2cb14973.section: Fundamental issues > Common errors in spatial analysis > Locational fallacy
544b2cb14973.sentence: The locational fallacy refers to error due to the particular spatial characterization chosen for the elements of study, in particular choice of placement for the spatial presence of the element.

ccd528f2ba9b.title: Spatial analysis
ccd528f2ba9b.sentence: Spatial sampling involves determining a limited number of locations in geographic space for faithfully measuring phenomena that are subject to dependency and heterogeneity.

043fc7ab2ba3.title: Spatial analysis
043fc7ab2ba3.sentence: Basic spatial sampling schemes include random, clustered and systematic.

bb02ec7e9bce.title: Landsat program
bb02ec7e9bce.sentence: The Landsat program is the longest-running enterprise that has acquired satellite imagery of Earth.

22d64bbbedf0.title: Landsat program
22d64bbbedf0.sentence: On 23 July 1972, the Earth Resources Technology Satellite was launched.

46329c0c9940.title: Landsat program
46329c0c9940.sentence: This was eventually renamed to Landsat 1 in 1975.

eb2e5a1b5b27.title: Landsat program
eb2e5a1b5b27.sentence: The most recent, Landsat 9, was launched on 27 September 2021.

874d7ad4240f.title: Landsat program
874d7ad4240f.sentence: Landsat 7 data has eight spectral bands with spatial resolutions ranging from 15 to 60 m (49 to 197 ft); the temporal resolution is 16 days.

aa0c19d4b2e5.title: Landsat program
aa0c19d4b2e5.sentence: Each Landsat scene is about 115 miles long and 115 miles wide (or 100 nautical miles long and 100 nautical miles wide, or 185 kilometers long and 185 kilometers wide).

f42cd4c3afc4.title: Landsat program
f42cd4c3afc4.sentence: Landsat 1 through 5 carried the Landsat Multispectral Scanner (MSS).

aa3ce2416e87.title: Landsat program
aa3ce2416e87.sentence: Landsat 4 and 5 carried both the MSS and Thematic Mapper (TM) instruments.

313873a998b9.title: Landsat program
313873a998b9.sentence: Landsat 7 uses the Enhanced Thematic Mapper Plus (ETM+) scanner.

7183f344a37e.title: Landsat program
7183f344a37e.sentence: Landsat 8 uses two instruments, the Operational Land Imager (OLI) for optical bands and the Thermal Infrared Sensor (TIRS) for thermal bands.

ecb9a76838f3.title: Landsat program
ecb9a76838f3.sentence: Landsat imagery provides one of the longest uninterrupted time series available from any single remote sensing program, spanning from 1972 to the present.

4f3ecc135650.title: Landsat program
4f3ecc135650.sentence: Land cover-determination is a common use of Landsat imagery around the world.

518928cf8892.title: Geomorphometry
518928cf8892.sentence: Geomorphometry, or geomorphometrics (Ancient Greek: γῆ, romanized: gê, lit. 'earth' + Ancient Greek: μορφή, romanized: morphḗ, lit. 'form, shape' + Ancient Greek: μέτρον, romanized: métron, lit. 'measure'), is the science and practice of measuring the characteristics of terrain, the shape of the surface of the Earth, and the effects of this surface form on human and natural geography.

c255d74eec57.title: Geomorphometry
c255d74eec57.sentence: In simple terms, geomorphometry aims at extracting (land) surface parameters (morphometric, hydrological, climatic, etc.) and objects (watersheds, stream networks, landforms, etc.) using input digital land surface model (also known as digital elevation model, DEM) and parameterization software.

8182be102171.title: Geomorphometry
8182be102171.sentence: Extracted surface parameters and objects can then be used, for example, to improve mapping and modeling of soils, vegetation, land use, geomorphological and geological features and similar.

0d6f8d4d5cee.title: Geomorphometry
0d6f8d4d5cee.sentence: With the rapid increase of sources of DEMs today (and mainly due to the Shuttle Radar Topography Mission and LIDAR-based projects), extraction of land surface parameters is becoming more and more attractive to numerous fields ranging from precision agriculture, soil-landscape modeling, climatic and hydrological applications to urban planning, education, and space research.

eb972317c8af.title: Geomorphometry
eb972317c8af.sentence: The topography of almost all Earth has been sampled or scanned today so that DEMs are available at resolutions of 100 m or better at a global scale.

3b6d0901d58f.title: Geomorphometry
3b6d0901d58f.sentence: Slope or grade measures how steep the terrain is at any point on the surface, deviating from a horizontal surface.

53264e08a16d.title: Geomorphometry
53264e08a16d.sentence: The aspect of the terrain at any point on the surface is the direction the slope is "facing," or the cardinal direction of the steepest downhill slope.

dcf65fdac0d2.title: Geomorphometry
dcf65fdac0d2.sentence: Deriving slope from a raster digital elevation model requires calculating a discrete approximation of the surface derivative based on the elevation of a cell and those of its surrounding cells, and several methods have been developed.

67210e28a96c.title: Geomorphometry
67210e28a96c.sentence: For example, the Horne method, implemented in ArcGIS, uses the elevation of a cell and its eight immediate neighbors, spaced by the cell size or resolution r:

4cba773395bd.title: Geomorphometry
4cba773395bd.sentence: Because water flows downhill, the surface derivatives of the terrain surface can predict surface stream flow.

a393517e1d86.title: Geomorphometry
a393517e1d86.sentence: Although geomorphometry started with the ideas of Brisson (1808) and Gauss (1827), the field did not evolve much until the development of GIS and DEM datasets in the 1970s.

4ed3cbdb8c10.title: Ground-penetrating radar
4ed3cbdb8c10.sentence: Ground-penetrating radar (GPR) is a geophysical method that uses radar pulses to image the subsurface.

438c098409e9.title: Ground-penetrating radar
438c098409e9.sentence: This nondestructive method uses electromagnetic radiation in the microwave band (UHF/VHF frequencies) of the radio spectrum, and detects the reflected signals from subsurface structures.

4765c697cfae.title: Ground-penetrating radar
4765c697cfae.sentence: GPR uses high-frequency (usually polarized) radio waves, usually in the range 10 MHz to 2.6 GHz.

c8783ad7f93d.title: Ground-penetrating radar
c8783ad7f93d.sentence: When the energy encounters a buried object or a boundary between materials having different permittivities, it may be reflected or refracted or scattered back to the surface.

c973ff168693.title: Ground-penetrating radar
c973ff168693.sentence: Dry sandy soils or massive dry materials such as granite, limestone, and concrete tend to be resistive rather than conductive, and the depth of penetration could be up to 15 metres (50 ft).

759e7f688396.title: Ground-penetrating radar
759e7f688396.sentence: However, in moist or clay-laden soils and materials with high electrical conductivity, penetration may be as little as a few centimetres.

00c2228fbcee.title: Ground-penetrating radar
00c2228fbcee.sentence: Thus operating frequency is always a trade-off between resolution and penetration.

829a977f5f22.title: Ground-penetrating radar
829a977f5f22.sentence: The most significant performance limitation of GPR is in high-conductivity materials such as clay soils and soils that are salt contaminated.

f8a04bd8c027.title: Ground-penetrating radar
f8a04bd8c027.sentence: Performance is also limited by signal scattering in heterogeneous conditions (e.g. rocky soils).

b00f13f7d264.title: Ground-penetrating radar
b00f13f7d264.sentence: In the Earth sciences it is used to study bedrock, soils, groundwater, and ice.

13665e8a3882.title: Ground-penetrating radar
13665e8a3882.sentence: Cross borehole GPR has developed within the field of hydrogeophysics to be a valuable means of assessing the presence and amount of soil water.

f81b405f1511.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
f81b405f1511.section: DIGITAL SOIL MAPPING > The scorpan Model
f81b405f1511.sentence: To fully make the theoretical transition from conventional to digital soil mapping approaches, McBratney et al. (2003) proposed the scorpan model as an extension of the clorpt model in the following:

533f7ef3b9cd.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
533f7ef3b9cd.section: DIGITAL SOIL MAPPING > The scorpan Model
533f7ef3b9cd.sentence: The scorpan model shares the same variables as the clorpt model, which includes climate (c), organisms (o), relief (r), parent material (p), and time/age (a).

8a4d58ce23da.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
8a4d58ce23da.section: DIGITAL SOIL MAPPING > The scorpan Model
8a4d58ce23da.sentence: The additional variables include s, which represents the intrinsic properties of the soil (e.g., the spectral properties of the soil) that may be captured by various remote and proximal sensors; and n, which represents the spatial coordinates of a sample or the location relative to another geographical phenomenon (e.g., distance to river).

18f54ea39462.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
18f54ea39462.section: DIGITAL SOIL MAPPING > The scorpan Model
18f54ea39462.sentence: Here, individual scorpan factors, or a combination of them, are used to predict the distribution of a soil property or soil class, S, of interest using a quantitative function, f (), that represents the soil-environmental relationship.

e0496dc23ef3.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
e0496dc23ef3.section: DIGITAL SOIL MAPPING > Representing the scorpan Factors
e0496dc23ef3.sentence: The effectiveness of the scorpan model is in its flexibility to integrate data from existing soil surveys and geospatial datasets acquired from multiple sources, such as remote sensing data, digital elevation data, climate data, land use data, and geological data (McKenzie and Ryan, 1999).

2764a6166f7d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
2764a6166f7d.section: DIGITAL SOIL MAPPING > Representing the scorpan Factors
2764a6166f7d.sentence: These scorpan factors are represented in the raster format and therefore, each dataset also has a corresponding spatial resolution and projection system.

97d03d0755f0.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
97d03d0755f0.section: DIGITAL SOIL MAPPING > Representing the scorpan Factors
97d03d0755f0.sentence: Hence, each individual dataset may need to be re-projected into a common projection system and scaled to a uniform spatial resolution so that all the individual cells of the various datasets are spatially aligned (Figure 17.8).

d8c482201d46.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
d8c482201d46.section: DIGITAL SOIL MAPPING > Representing the scorpan Factors > Relief (r)
d8c482201d46.sentence: It is well recognized that the r factor is the most used factor within DSM (McBratney et al., 2003).

46b9647b6eda.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
46b9647b6eda.section: DIGITAL SOIL MAPPING > Representing the scorpan Factors > Relief (r)
46b9647b6eda.sentence: One of the staples in DSM research has been the use of a digital elevation model (DEM)—a raster that is made up of elevation values.

1e29c673a3c7.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
1e29c673a3c7.section: DIGITAL SOIL MAPPING > Representing the scorpan Factors > Soil (s)
1e29c673a3c7.sentence: The s factor is the second most frequently used factor in DSM studies (McBratney et al., 2003).

2ed058cf2160.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
2ed058cf2160.section: DIGITAL SOIL MAPPING > Representing the scorpan Factors > Climate (c)
2ed058cf2160.sentence: This factor is one of the least used scorpan factors (McBratney et al., 2003)—several possible explanations comes to mind.

2b2c0d750b74.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
2b2c0d750b74.section: DIGITAL SOIL MAPPING > Representing the scorpan Factors > Climate (c)
2b2c0d750b74.sentence: Firstly, the local climate is largely influenced by topography and as a result, topographic indices such as elevation and aspect may be used as a proxy for a climate variable due to the relationship between elevation and the environmental lapse-rate and the relationship between slope-face direction and temperature (Schaetzl and Anderson, 2005).

6c57214ccf40.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
6c57214ccf40.section: DIGITAL SOIL MAPPING > Representing the scorpan Factors > Age (a)
6c57214ccf40.sentence: The age factor may be used to describe how long pedogenesis has occurred and may be estimated as the age of the ground or material from which the soil has developed (McBratney et al., 2003).

97dce3760573.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
97dce3760573.section: DIGITAL SOIL MAPPING > Representing the scorpan Factors > Age (a)
97dce3760573.sentence: Within DSM, there are very few examples where this information has been used due to the difficulty in characterizing the age of soil within a format that would be conducive for use within a GIS.

77e6093277a0.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
77e6093277a0.section: DIGITAL SOIL MAPPING > Representing the scorpan Factors > Spatial Position (n)
77e6093277a0.sentence: The n factor may be incorporated in several ways: using the spatial coordinates of soil sample locations or using a raster layer that represents the distance to some geographical phenomenon.

4f0647d6b1e0.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
4f0647d6b1e0.sentence: Hence, pedometrics—a branch of soil science that applies “mathematical and statistical methods for the study of the distribution and genesis of soils” (Webster, 1994)—has been an emerging field of research, globally.

49fbb168469a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
49fbb168469a.sentence: Although pedometric techniques for producing digital soil maps (DSM) have existed since as early as the 1970s (e.g., Webster and Burrough, 1972a, 1972b), technological advances have facilitated the production of DSM products since the 2000s (McBratney et al., 2003; Scull et al., 2003; Minasny and McBratney, 2016).

3ad5a4f09bc2.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
3ad5a4f09bc2.section: DIGITAL SOIL MAPPING > Prediction of Soil Classes and Properties
3ad5a4f09bc2.sentence: Developing a soil map using DSM techniques largely requires the following three ingredients:

3bea22ada802.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
3bea22ada802.section: DIGITAL SOIL MAPPING > Prediction of Soil Classes and Properties
3bea22ada802.sentence: - a suite of environmental layers (i.e., predictors or covariates) that represent the scorpan factors;

b3049735f182.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
b3049735f182.section: DIGITAL SOIL MAPPING > Prediction of Soil Classes and Properties
b3049735f182.sentence: - soil data that are geospatially referenced; and

b64912e6d3dc.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
b64912e6d3dc.section: DIGITAL SOIL MAPPING > Prediction of Soil Classes and Properties
b64912e6d3dc.sentence: - a model that characterizes the relationship between the soil data and the environment in order to make predictions for unsampled locations.

67f5026050c1.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
67f5026050c1.section: DIGITAL SOIL MAPPING > Prediction of Soil Classes and Properties
67f5026050c1.sentence: Typically, DSM techniques involve a form of supervised learning where a training dataset is first created by spatially intersecting the sample locations (with measured soil properties) with the underlying suite of environmental layers.

e4f8b0f74f77.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
e4f8b0f74f77.section: DIGITAL SOIL MAPPING > Prediction of Soil Classes and Properties
e4f8b0f74f77.sentence: Using a predictive model, the relationship between the soil response variable and the environmental predictor layers is established using a classification or regression function (i.e., model fitting).

cac979122787.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
cac979122787.section: DIGITAL SOIL MAPPING > Prediction of Soil Classes and Properties
cac979122787.sentence: Once the predictive model is fitted with the training data, it is then applied to the set environmental layers to predict the soil properties or classes at unsampled locations.

20a3a7b55e22.title: Electromagnetic induction
20a3a7b55e22.sentence: Electromagnetic induction or magnetic induction is the production of an electromotive force (emf) across an electrical conductor in a changing magnetic field.

9f2c305fb7bd.title: Electromagnetic induction
9f2c305fb7bd.sentence: Electromagnetic induction was discovered by Michael Faraday, published in 1831.

004d3e4e5926.title: Electromagnetic induction
004d3e4e5926.sentence: It was discovered independently by Joseph Henry in 1832.

b4f07fd6b685.title: Electromagnetic induction
b4f07fd6b685.sentence: Michael Faraday is generally credited with the discovery of induction in 1831, and James Clerk Maxwell mathematically described it as Faraday's law of induction.

f3ea6e735f9b.title: Electromagnetic induction
f3ea6e735f9b.section: Theory > Faraday's law of induction and Lenz's law
f3ea6e735f9b.sentence: The most widespread version of this law states that the induced electromotive force in any closed circuit is equal to the rate of change of the magnetic flux enclosed by the circuit: ℰ=−dΦBdt, where ℰ is the emf and ΦB is the magnetic flux.

792f1edadc79.title: Electromagnetic induction
792f1edadc79.section: Theory > Faraday's law of induction and Lenz's law
792f1edadc79.sentence: The direction of the electromotive force is given by Lenz's law which states that an induced current will flow in the direction that will oppose the change which produced it.

189782556df8.title: Electromagnetic induction
189782556df8.sentence: When the electric current in a loop of wire changes, the changing current creates a changing magnetic field.

4cdd9f4e531e.title: Electromagnetic induction
4cdd9f4e531e.sentence: A second wire in reach of this magnetic field will experience this change in magnetic field as a change in its coupled magnetic flux, dΦBdt.

3068c883e838.title: Electromagnetic induction
3068c883e838.sentence: Therefore, an electromotive force is set up in the second loop called the induced emf or transformer emf.

62314fe24f0e.title: Electromagnetic induction
62314fe24f0e.sentence: Electrical conductors moving through a steady magnetic field, or stationary conductors within a changing magnetic field, will have circular currents induced within them by induction, called eddy currents.

87a33f833599.title: Electromagnetic induction
87a33f833599.sentence: Eddy currents flow in closed loops in planes perpendicular to the magnetic field.

0e1379bedd44.title: Electrical resistivity tomography
0e1379bedd44.sentence: Electrical resistivity tomography (ERT) or electrical resistivity imaging (ERI) is a geophysical technique for imaging sub-surface structures from electrical resistivity measurements made at the surface, or by electrodes in one or more boreholes.

b6b7ea0f4d09.title: Electrical resistivity tomography
b6b7ea0f4d09.sentence: The method of measuring subsurface resistivity involves placing four electrodes in the ground in a line at equal spacing, applying a measured AC current to the outer two electrodes, and measuring the AC voltage between the inner two electrodes.

9ecfcd10cbb3.title: Electrical resistivity tomography
9ecfcd10cbb3.sentence: A measured resistance is calculated by dividing the measured voltage by the measured current.

78322ebc536a.title: Electrical resistivity tomography
78322ebc536a.sentence: This resistance is then multiplied by a geometric factor that includes the spacing between each electrode to determine the apparent resistivity.

2f0ea3ebb61c.title: Electrical resistivity tomography
2f0ea3ebb61c.sentence: In general, an increase in soil moisture results in a reduction in soil resistivity.

e7d5add66f59.title: Electrical resistivity tomography
e7d5add66f59.sentence: The difference in resistivity between a soil in a dry and in a saturated condition may be several orders of magnitude.

298b6d4c2b4b.title: Electrical resistivity tomography
298b6d4c2b4b.sentence: The pore fluid provides the only electrical path in sands, while both the pore fluid and the surface charged particles provide electrical paths in clays.

26d129a33b5e.title: Electrical resistivity tomography
26d129a33b5e.sentence: Electrode spacings of 0.75, 1.5, 3.0, 6.0, and 12.0 m are typically used for shallow depths (<10 m) of investigations.

4ec830c27cd7.title: Electrical resistivity tomography
4ec830c27cd7.sentence: The depth of investigation is typically less than the maximum electrode spacing.

9f8598934264.title: Electrical resistivity tomography
9f8598934264.sentence: - Soil moisture mapping: ERT helps assess soil moisture content for precision agriculture.

abc80e1439fc.title: Electrical resistivity tomography
abc80e1439fc.sentence: - Root zone imaging: ERT is used to visualize plant root structures and soil-root interactions.

827b32f7a6c2.title: Electrical resistivity tomography
827b32f7a6c2.sentence: - Contaminant mapping: ERT is used to monitor and delineate the spread of contaminants in soil and groundwater.

5e2e1c2a720d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
5e2e1c2a720d.sentence: Two major achievements contributed to the development of conventional soil survey methods in North America.

9aaa3759b4d7.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
9aaa3759b4d7.sentence: The first achievement was the formalization of Hans Jenny’s Factors of Soil Formation (1941) and the second was the formalization of national soil taxonomic systems in the US (Soil Taxonomy; Soil Survey Staff, 1975) and Canada (The Canadian System of Soil Classification, CSSC; Canada Soil Survey Committee, 1978; See Chapter 8).

98f007765caa.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
98f007765caa.section: CONVENTIONAL SOIL MAPPING > Producing Conventional Soil Maps
98f007765caa.sentence: MacMillan et al. (1992) describes the steps involved in making a conventional soil map, beginning with the preliminary steps of defining the objectives, compiling background information, and initial legend development.

f9dd7c377e68.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
f9dd7c377e68.section: CONVENTIONAL SOIL MAPPING > Producing Conventional Soil Maps
f9dd7c377e68.sentence: The preliminary (primarily office based) steps are followed by soil inspections, field mapping, and correlation.

28f63302f178.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
28f63302f178.section: CONVENTIONAL SOIL MAPPING > Producing Conventional Soil Maps
28f63302f178.sentence: Finally, the map is produced, and a report written.

a75b81f88b5c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
a75b81f88b5c.section: CONVENTIONAL SOIL MAPPING > Conventional Representations of Soil
a75b81f88b5c.sentence: Soils may be represented in several ways: a profile, pedon, polypedon, or map unit (Figure 17.1).

48b611d8c8ab.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
48b611d8c8ab.section: CONVENTIONAL SOIL MAPPING > Conventional Representations of Soil
48b611d8c8ab.sentence: The soil profile is a 2-dimensional representation and the pedon is a 3-dimensional representation that typically is 1–3 m laterally and 1–2 m vertically.

0bcde812215d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
0bcde812215d.section: CONVENTIONAL SOIL MAPPING > Conventional Representations of Soil
0bcde812215d.sentence: In principal, the properties of the pedon should not vary horizontally (only vertically) and when several similar pedons are connected, it is referred to as a polypedon.

4229018dc966.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
4229018dc966.section: CONVENTIONAL SOIL MAPPING > Conventional Representations of Soil
4229018dc966.sentence: The polypedon concept differs from a map unit because the map unit, a distinct polygon that is mapped by soil surveyors, is an areal representation of a polypedon or a polypedon complex.

a5d6900a12b9.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
a5d6900a12b9.section: CONVENTIONAL SOIL MAPPING > The Evolution of Conventional Soil Maps
a5d6900a12b9.sentence: Firstly, the data in a chloropleth map is represented as discrete classes where the conditions are assumed to be homogenous within the map unit (Hole, 1978).

c6370c4c8952.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
c6370c4c8952.section: CONVENTIONAL SOIL MAPPING > The Evolution of Conventional Soil Maps
c6370c4c8952.sentence: Furthermore, it is also recognized that a significant amount of spatial generalization (i.e., simplification) within the map unit occurs due to inclusions of subdominant soils that are too small to be mapped at the map scale (Hole and Campbell, 1985).

5390cdd063e0.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
5390cdd063e0.section: CONVENTIONAL SOIL MAPPING > The Evolution of Conventional Soil Maps
5390cdd063e0.sentence: In addition, the changes in soil are not necessarily discrete (as suggested by the use of boundaries), but rather, they are fuzzy where the soil attributes between two neighbouring map units are an intergrade of the soil properties of the two units (Zhu and Band, 1994; Schaetzl and Anderson, 2005).

9bd47d16f693.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
9bd47d16f693.section: CONVENTIONAL SOIL MAPPING > The Evolution of Conventional Soil Maps
9bd47d16f693.sentence: Although it would be ideal to have a soil map that consists of only simple mapping units, increasing the proportion of ‘pure’ map units within a map has been shown to result in an exponential increase in cost for developing the map (Bie et al., 1973).

6576e80429dc.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
6576e80429dc.section: CONVENTIONAL SOIL MAPPING > The Evolution of Conventional Soil Maps
6576e80429dc.sentence: Consequently, inconsistencies manifested themselves in soil maps as mismatched boundaries of map units amongst different counties, states/provinces, and countries (Figure 17.3; Thompson et al., 2012; Dewitte et al., 2013).

020c35a42d5b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
020c35a42d5b.section: CONVENTIONAL SOIL MAPPING > The Evolution of Conventional Soil Maps
020c35a42d5b.sentence: In addition, inconsistencies may also lead to problems such as having multiple soil series with the same soil properties, which results in redundancy, or even worse, where two soil series with the same name have completely different soil properties (Thompson et al., 2012).

c124ee53fa42.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
c124ee53fa42.section: CONVENTIONAL SOIL MAPPING > The Evolution of Conventional Soil Maps
c124ee53fa42.sentence: Despite these limitations, in many parts of Canada and the world, legacy soil maps incorporate vast amounts of information derived from field inspections and soil surveyor knowledge.

50aab094e2f1.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
50aab094e2f1.section: CONVENTIONAL SOIL MAPPING > The Evolution of Conventional Soil Maps
50aab094e2f1.sentence: For these reasons, they represent an important source of training data for the development of digital soil maps to meet current needs.

a764f67b6786.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
a764f67b6786.sentence: Here, we describe the term ‘accuracy’ as being the difference between the observed and predicted values at a location (Brus et al., 2011); whereby we can describe the accuracy as being ‘higher’ as the difference decreases.

ec68831336b7.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
ec68831336b7.sentence: However, in both cases, accuracy assessment must be carried out using an independent (i.e., validation or test) dataset that was not used to train the model.

51ced0955cf3.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
51ced0955cf3.sentence: When assessing the accuracy of categorical predictions (e.g., soil series, soil parent material type), we generally rely on overall accuracy and Cohen’s kappa coefficient as the main metrics.

16bbd4439f3d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
16bbd4439f3d.sentence: The overall accuracy is the proportion of observations that were correctly predicted for the independent dataset; whereas kappa accounts for the by-chance agreement between the observed and predicted classes.

f87dd863899d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
f87dd863899d.sentence: Both metrics range from 0 to 1, where a value of 1 represents high accuracy.

7cafa218851c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
7cafa218851c.sentence: When assessing the accuracy of continuous predictions (e.g. bulk density, soil organic carbon), the mean square error (MSE), root mean square error (RMSE), coefficient of determination (R2), and Lin’s concordance correlation coefficient (CCC) are often used.

0f19b8d28cd5.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
0f19b8d28cd5.sentence: The MSE is effectively the average squared difference between the observed and predicted values; in comparison, the RMSE, is the square root of MSE and is expressed in the same units as the soil variable.

07b419315ccb.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
07b419315ccb.sentence: In both cases, a lower MSE or RMSE represents a more accurate model.

c869415cd026.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
c869415cd026.sentence: It is critical to note that R2 does not represent accuracy because it does not account for model bias whereby the model may consistently overpredict or underpredict a soil variable.

dfba6ed724b2.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
dfba6ed724b2.sentence: Instead, the more appropriate metric is to use CCC, which represents the goodness of fit along a 45° line on a scatterplot of observed and predicted values.

0fc61ac6e0d5.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
0fc61ac6e0d5.sentence: Values of CCC range from 0 to 1, where values of 1 represent scenarios where the predicted values match the observed values and thus indicates high prediction accuracy and precision.

3d0a34356f21.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
3d0a34356f21.sentence: How we present soil patterns on a soil map is based on a predictive model, which is never truly free of errors; hence, quantitatively estimating the uncertainty of digital soil maps is just as important as validating it because it will allow users to assess the usefulness of the maps and how those maps may be used (Heuvelink, 1998).

e351dd63a0d2.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
e351dd63a0d2.sentence: It is important to recognize that along with all environmental modelling activities, models are simply abstract representations of the real world and that there are uncertainties about the true properties of the soil.

d1e4503ed774.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
d1e4503ed774.sentence: Uncertainties are accumulated and propagated from three sources: the measured soil property, the environmental predictors representing the scorpan factors, and the predictive model.

2e96e1e5cdf5.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
2e96e1e5cdf5.sentence: Uncertainty in Soil Properties: Whenever a soil sample is taken to a lab, there will always be differences in analytical techniques that may contribute errors when measuring various soil properties.

2d07e592ee86.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
2d07e592ee86.sentence: In some situations, the soil response variables may be inferred from other soil variables that are easier to measure using pedotransfer functions whereby errors may be further propagated.

fea8a57dc05e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
fea8a57dc05e.sentence: Uncertainties could also arise when recording the spatial location of sample points when using a GPS, whereby some GPSs are more accurate than others.

c8f5e90871b3.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
c8f5e90871b3.sentence: For example, vertical uncertainties may be present with DEMs as well as measurement uncertainty from remote and proximal soil sensors.

80b9e7c38055.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
80b9e7c38055.sentence: When using conventional soil maps or geology maps in the polygon format, the composition of the polygon, polygon boundaries, and map scale may all contribute to uncertainty.

3033f8c235ba.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
3033f8c235ba.sentence: Uncertainty in Predictive Model: As previously discussed, the choice of predictive model may result in drastically different soil maps; and hence, the structure of the model may be another source of uncertainty.

e3b081b0e5d7.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
e3b081b0e5d7.sentence: The relationships between the environmental predictors and soil properties may be linear, non-linear, or a combination of both, and certain types of models are more effective at capturing those relationships than others.

58e9b002d9bd.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
58e9b002d9bd.sentence: Finally, some modelling approaches (e.g., model trees) are a hybrid of linear and non-linear models and are therefore able to capture both types of relationships.

b4a251a28d38.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
b4a251a28d38.sentence: Due to the importance of recognizing uncertainty in model outputs, international mapping standards (e.g., GlobalSoilMap.net) often require the inclusion of a 90% prediction interval map as well as the lower (5%) and upper (95%) prediction limits (Figure 17.22).

b9b4a4564467.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
b9b4a4564467.sentence: Here, we assume that with a 90% confidence level, the real value of a soil property will be within the prediction interval.

1c80bb419713.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
1c80bb419713.sentence: Therefore, when interpreting these uncertainty maps, the uncertainty will increase as the 90% prediction interval width increases.

7f09c6a22bb1.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.04%3A_Digital_Soil_Mapping
7f09c6a22bb1.sentence: It should be noted that this representation of uncertainty only applies to continuous soil variables.

37b562f700e4.title: Spatial scale
37b562f700e4.sentence: Spatial scale is a specific application of the term "scale" for describing or categorizing (e.g. into orders of magnitude) the size of a space (hence spatial), or the extent at which a phenomenon or process occurs.

f25c6943bf18.title: Spatial scale
f25c6943bf18.sentence: Micro | 1 m – 1 km | 1 m 2 – 1 km 2 | local

6112b9804d1b.title: Spatial scale
6112b9804d1b.sentence: Meso | 1 km - 100 km | 1 km 2 - 10,000 km 2 | regional

180d95e22186.title: Spatial scale
180d95e22186.sentence: Macro | 100 km - 10,000 km | 10,000 km 2 - 100,000,000 km 2 | continental

b2f07e8836bb.title: Spatial scale
b2f07e8836bb.sentence: These divisions are somewhat arbitrary; where, on this table, mega- is assigned global scope, it may only apply continentally or even regionally in other contexts.

807bf6c4fc51.title: Spatial scale
807bf6c4fc51.sentence: The interpretations of meso- and macro- must then be adjusted accordingly.

d2747e30b397.title: Multispectral imaging
d2747e30b397.sentence: Multispectral imaging captures image data within specific wavelength ranges across the electromagnetic spectrum.

b544b03f9e0b.title: Multispectral imaging
b544b03f9e0b.sentence: The wavelengths may be separated by filters or detected with the use of instruments that are sensitive to particular wavelengths, including light from frequencies beyond the visible light range (i.e. infrared and ultraviolet).

0a89b3906d3d.title: Multispectral imaging
0a89b3906d3d.sentence: Multispectral imaging measures light in a small number (typically 3 to 15) of spectral bands.

0de6c5883b7e.title: Multispectral imaging
0de6c5883b7e.sentence: Hyperspectral imaging is a special case of spectral imaging where often hundreds of contiguous spectral bands are available.

dc3dddd134ad.title: Multispectral imaging
dc3dddd134ad.sentence: Such images allow the water depth, vegetation coverage, soil moisture content, and the presence of fires to be seen, all in a single image.

8c0a05d5f77a.title: Multispectral imaging
8c0a05d5f77a.section: Spectral band usage > Typical spectral bands
8c0a05d5f77a.sentence: - Mid-infrared (MIR), 1550–1750 nm, is used for imaging vegetation, soil moisture content, and some forest fires.

e90f059b2cb9.title: Multispectral imaging
e90f059b2cb9.section: Spectral band usage > Typical spectral bands
e90f059b2cb9.sentence: - Far-infrared (FIR), 2080–2350 nm, is used for imaging soil, moisture, geological features, silicates, clays, and fires.

01cacb129286.title: Multispectral imaging
01cacb129286.section: Applications > Military target tracking > Land mine detection
01cacb129286.sentence: Surface and sub-surface soil possess different physical and chemical properties that appear in spectral analysis.

c6f5d516861b.title: Multispectral imaging
c6f5d516861b.section: Applications > Military target tracking > Land mine detection
c6f5d516861b.sentence: Disturbed soil has increased emissivity in the wavelength range of 8.5 to 9.5 micrometers while demonstrating no change in wavelengths greater than 10 micrometers.

c8e798c6729f.title: Hyperspectral imaging
c8e798c6729f.sentence: The goal of hyperspectral imaging is to obtain the spectrum for each pixel in the image of a scene, with the purpose of finding objects, identifying materials, or detecting processes.

96d85d53a97f.title: Hyperspectral imaging
96d85d53a97f.sentence: In hyperspectral imaging, the recorded spectra have fine wavelength resolution and cover a wide range of wavelengths.

06b093c571cb.title: Hyperspectral imaging
06b093c571cb.sentence: Hyperspectral imaging measures continuous spectral bands, as opposed to multiband imaging which measures spaced spectral bands.

32748a5b2b8c.title: Hyperspectral imaging
32748a5b2b8c.sentence: Certain objects leave unique "fingerprints" in the electromagnetic spectrum.

b76a378301af.title: Hyperspectral imaging
b76a378301af.sentence: Known as spectral signatures, these "fingerprints" enable identification of the materials that make up a scanned object.

0947fe3ab38b.title: Near-infrared spectroscopy
0947fe3ab38b.sentence: Hyperspectral imaging has been applied for a wide range of uses, including the remote investigation of plants and soils.

4a38748d8d73.title: Near-infrared spectroscopy
4a38748d8d73.sentence: Data can be collected from instruments on airplanes, satellites or unmanned aerial systems to assess ground cover and soil chemistry.

ebc02095a9c2.title: Hyperspectral imaging
ebc02095a9c2.sentence: Furthermore, work is under way to use hyperspectral data to detect the chemical composition of plants, which can be used to detect the nutrient and water status of wheat in irrigated systems.

78703f4c39ec.title: Hyperspectral imaging
78703f4c39ec.sentence: HSI cameras can also be used to detect stress from heavy metals in plants and become an earlier and faster alternative to post-harvest wet chemical methods.

a3f8333f91b9.title: Hyperspectral imaging
a3f8333f91b9.sentence: Although hyperspectral imaging is often treated as a surface-analysis technique, it can also probe beneath the surface, with information depth depending on the spectral range and sample properties.

5216fa5c8d9a.title: Normalized difference vegetation index
5216fa5c8d9a.sentence: The normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) is a widely used metric for quantifying the health and density of vegetation using sensor data.

d4e4347f59d6.title: Normalized difference vegetation index
d4e4347f59d6.sentence: It is calculated from spectrometric data at two specific bands: red and near-infrared.

47c88c42ce23.title: Normalized difference vegetation index
47c88c42ce23.sentence: The index is easy to interpret: NDVI will be a value between -1 and 1, where values close to zero will indicate little to no vegetation, negative values are associated with non-land surfaces or water, and higher values correspond to healthy, dense vegetation.

d16fee61f4d8.title: Normalized difference vegetation index
d16fee61f4d8.sentence: The pigment in plant leaves, chlorophyll, strongly absorbs visible light (from 400 to 700 nm) for use in photosynthesis.

37324418e8c3.title: Normalized difference vegetation index
37324418e8c3.sentence: The cell structure of the leaves, on the other hand, strongly reflects near-infrared light (from 700 to 1100 nm).

104516fda5d6.title: Normalized difference vegetation index
104516fda5d6.sentence: - soils which generally exhibit a near-infrared spectral reflectance somewhat larger than the red, and thus tend to also generate rather small positive NDVI values (say 0.1 to 0.2).

6cda6dd40840.title: Normalized difference vegetation index
6cda6dd40840.sentence: - Soil effects: Soils tend to darken when wet, so that their reflectance is a direct function of water content.

5a4f6df19163.title: Normalized difference vegetation index
5a4f6df19163.sentence: If the spectral response to moistening is not exactly the same in the two spectral bands, the NDVI of an area can appear to change as a result of soil moisture changes (precipitation or evaporation) and not because of vegetation changes.

16730eb71a25.title: Normalized difference vegetation index
16730eb71a25.sentence: A number of derivatives and alternatives to NDVI have been proposed in the scientific literature to address these limitations, including the Perpendicular Vegetation Index, the soil-adjusted vegetation index, the atmospherically resistant vegetation index and the global environment monitoring index.

aa5a8d459659.title: Normalized difference vegetation index
aa5a8d459659.sentence: A current alternative adopted by USGS is the enhanced vegetation index (EVI), correcting for soil effects, canopy background, and aerosol influences.

5545946587f0.title: Modifiable areal unit problem
5545946587f0.sentence: The modifiable areal unit problem (MAUP) is a source of statistical bias that can significantly impact the results of statistical hypothesis tests.

1f3de5d2439d.title: Modifiable areal unit problem
1f3de5d2439d.sentence: The MAUP affects results when point-based measures of spatial phenomena are aggregated into spatial partitions or areal units (such as regions or districts) as in, for example, population density or illness rates.

584ea59988cb.title: Modifiable areal unit problem
584ea59988cb.sentence: The resulting summary values (e.g., totals, rates, proportions, densities) are influenced by both the shape and scale of the aggregation unit.

8e283646a38f.title: Modifiable areal unit problem
8e283646a38f.sentence: A census choropleth map calculating population density using state boundaries will yield radically different results from a map that calculates density based on county boundaries.

1963f0442249.title: Modifiable areal unit problem
1963f0442249.sentence: First, the scale effect causes variation in statistical results between different levels of aggregation (radial distance).

8c8adaf8dacf.title: Modifiable areal unit problem
8c8adaf8dacf.sentence: Generally, correlation increases as areal unit size increases.

863888e5df11.title: Modifiable areal unit problem
863888e5df11.sentence: The zoning effect describes variation in correlation statistics caused by the regrouping of data into different configurations at the same scale (areal shape).

81704d0631f7.title: Modifiable areal unit problem
81704d0631f7.sentence: This issue was first recognized by Gehlke and Biehl in 1934, and later described in detail in an entry in the Concepts and Techniques in Modern Geography (CATMOG) series by Stan Openshaw (1984) as well as in the book by Giuseppe Arbia (1988).

9a15bfd6479b.title: Modifiable areal unit problem
9a15bfd6479b.sentence: MAUP is closely related to the topic of ecological fallacy and ecological bias (Arbia, 1988).

5de68bacc4bb.title: Modifiable areal unit problem
5de68bacc4bb.sentence: This topic is of particular importance because in some cases data aggregation can obscure a strong correlation between variables, making the relationship appear weak or even negative.

0f992bdca079.title: Modifiable areal unit problem
0f992bdca079.sentence: Conversely, MAUP can cause random variables to appear as if there is a significant association where there is not.

1b7750aedc9c.title: Modifiable areal unit problem
1b7750aedc9c.sentence: Until a more analytical solution to MAUP is discovered, spatial sensitivity analysis using a variety of areal units is recommended as a methodology to estimate the uncertainty of correlation and regression coefficients due to ecological bias.

98460f9c7abd.title: Spatial variability
98460f9c7abd.sentence: Spatial variability occurs when a quantity that is measured at different spatial locations exhibits values that differ across the locations.

c01cf7283134.title: Spatial variability
c01cf7283134.sentence: Spatial variability can be assessed using spatial descriptive statistics such as the range.

22e5df03268a.title: Spatial variability
22e5df03268a.sentence: Then the uncertainty about z(x) is reduced to zero, whereas its spatial variability still exists.

41c0e6c1ddf8.title: Spatial variability
41c0e6c1ddf8.sentence: Uncertainty is closely related to the amount of spatial variability, but it is also strongly dependent upon sampling.

aeaefe9ea79d.title: Spatial variability
aeaefe9ea79d.sentence: Geostatistical analyses have been strictly performed to study the spatial variability of pesticide sorption and degradation in the field.

1d9336ae7ee3.title: Spatial variability
1d9336ae7ee3.sentence: Describing uncertainty using geostatistics is not an activity exempt from uncertainty itself as variogram uncertainty may be large and spatial interpolation may be undertaken using different techniques.

7bba4c161d6c.title: Nutrient budgeting
7bba4c161d6c.sentence: Unlike uniform agricultural fields, urban landscapes and golf courses exhibit high spatial variability in soil composition.

0ab95145060a.title: Geostatistics
0ab95145060a.sentence: Geostatistics is a branch of statistics focusing on spatial or spatiotemporal datasets.

b3710ccf24cb.title: Geostatistics
b3710ccf24cb.sentence: Developed originally to predict probability distributions of ore grades for mining operations, it is currently applied in diverse disciplines including petroleum geology, hydrogeology, hydrology, meteorology, oceanography, geochemistry, geometallurgy, geography, forestry, environmental control, landscape ecology, soil science, and agriculture (esp. in precision farming).

609194e237c8.title: Geostatistics
609194e237c8.sentence: A number of simpler interpolation methods/algorithms, such as inverse distance weighting, bilinear interpolation and nearest-neighbor interpolation, were already well known before geostatistics.

c11ab998f3e6.title: Geostatistics
c11ab998f3e6.sentence: Geostatistics goes beyond the interpolation problem by considering the studied phenomenon at unknown locations as a set of correlated random variables.

dc759e379667.title: Geostatistics
dc759e379667.sentence: The spatial continuity of the random variables is described by a model of spatial continuity that can be either a parametric function in the case of variogram-based geostatistics, or have a non-parametric form when using other methods such as multiple-point simulation or pseudo-genetic techniques.

bc9782a08e0a.title: Geostatistics
bc9782a08e0a.sentence: Typically, if the value of Z is known at locations close to x (or in the neighborhood of x) one can constrain the CDF of Z(x) by this neighborhood: if a high spatial continuity is assumed, Z(x) can only have values similar to the ones found in the neighborhood.

80bb70a97094.title: Geostatistics
80bb70a97094.sentence: By applying a single spatial model on an entire domain, one makes the assumption that Z is a stationary process.

348ae9de2b28.title: Geostatistics
348ae9de2b28.sentence: It means that the same statistical properties are applicable on the entire domain.

09ee90379da2.title: Geostatistics
09ee90379da2.sentence: Several geostatistical methods provide ways of relaxing this stationarity assumption.

0a6dd2a3df14.title: Geostatistics
0a6dd2a3df14.sentence: - Estimating the value for Z(x), typically by the expectation, the median or the mode of the CDF f(z,x).

d2c3f6b43f3b.title: Geostatistics
d2c3f6b43f3b.sentence: This is generally done by creating several alternative maps of Z, called realizations.

2a23bd25c8e8.title: Geostatistics
2a23bd25c8e8.sentence: All associated workflows are then considering ensemble of realizations, and consequently ensemble of predictions that allow for probabilistic forecasting.

36fded195577.title: Geostatistics
36fded195577.sentence: Bayesian inference is playing an increasingly important role in geostatistics.

18f660d627b0.title: Geostatistics
18f660d627b0.sentence: Bayesian estimation implements kriging through a spatial process, most commonly a Gaussian process, and updates the process using Bayes' theorem to calculate its posterior.

8540837673b3.title: Variogram
8540837673b3.sentence: A variogram is the graphical representation of the spatial dependence between pairs of data points, commonly used in geostatistics and spatial statistics.

6b448530ce6a.title: Variogram
6b448530ce6a.sentence: The variogram is the key function in geostatistics as it will be used to fit a model of the temporal/spatial correlation of the observed phenomenon.

acab8fb69f45.title: Variogram
acab8fb69f45.sentence: The semivariogram γ(h) was first defined by Matheron (1963) as half the average squared difference between a function and a translated copy of the function separated at distance h.

2ecf7f304a8b.title: Variogram
2ecf7f304a8b.sentence: For example, the value f(M) could represent the iron content in soil, at some location M (with geographic coordinates of latitude, longitude, and elevation) over some region V with element of volume dV.

cf9ce9ded7bd.title: Variogram
cf9ce9ded7bd.sentence: Samples taken far apart will vary more than samples taken close to each other.

f940a7431d25.title: Variogram
f940a7431d25.sentence: In practice it is impossible to sample everywhere, so the empirical variogram is used instead.

8f52539e642f.title: Variogram
8f52539e642f.sentence: Then for each pair of points i,j, the square of the difference in the observation (e.g., soil sample content or pixel intensity) is found (|zi−zj|2).

4c729f5e14d2.title: Variogram
4c729f5e14d2.sentence: - nugget n: The height of the jump of the semivariogram at the discontinuity at the origin.

a96efb4396d5.title: Variogram
a96efb4396d5.sentence: - sill s: Limit of the variogram tending to infinity lag distances.

182c314a8f09.title: Variogram
182c314a8f09.sentence: - range r: The distance in which the difference of the variogram from the sill becomes negligible.

6c7765125cd3.title: Variogram
6c7765125cd3.sentence: In models with a fixed sill, it is the distance at which this is first reached; for models with an asymptotic sill, it is conventionally taken to be the distance when the semivariance first reaches 95% of the sill.

2166e52acfbf.title: Variogram
2166e52acfbf.sentence: The empirical variogram cannot be computed at every lag distance h and due to variation in the estimation it is not ensured that it is a valid variogram, as defined above.

1421021abecb.title: Variogram
1421021abecb.sentence: In applied geostatistics the empirical variograms are thus often approximated by model function ensuring validity.

3d2cebfb4562.title: Variogram
3d2cebfb4562.sentence: This explains why only a limited number of variogram models are used: most commonly, the linear, the spherical, the Gaussian, and the exponential models.

541acf9a2161.title: Variogram
541acf9a2161.sentence: One is thus making a distinction between the experimental variogram that is a visualization of a possible spatial/temporal correlation and the variogram model that is further used to define the weights of the kriging function.

24be8a49a3f2.title: Variogram
24be8a49a3f2.sentence: The empirical variogram is used in geostatistics as a first estimate of the variogram model needed for spatial interpolation by kriging.

620a30103815.title: Variogram
620a30103815.sentence: Moreover, the term "variogram" is sometimes used to denote the semivariogram, and the symbol γ is sometimes used for the variogram, which brings some confusion.

a8b2099d8c9f.title: Variogram
a8b2099d8c9f.sentence: Likewise, the term semivariance can be misleading, since the values shown in a variogram are entire variances of observations at a given spatial separation (lag).

56f3af2cac31.title: Multivariate interpolation
56f3af2cac31.sentence: When the variates are spatial coordinates, it is also known as spatial interpolation.

b693d6c204e1.title: Multivariate interpolation
b693d6c204e1.sentence: The function to be interpolated is known at given points {\displaystyle (x_{i},y_{i},z_{i},\dots)} and the interpolation problem consists of yielding values at arbitrary points {\displaystyle (x,y,z,\dots)}.

d4910933ef66.title: Multivariate interpolation
d4910933ef66.sentence: Multivariate interpolation is particularly important in geostatistics, where it is used to create a digital elevation model from a set of points on the Earth's surface (for example, spot heights in a topographic survey or depths in a hydrographic survey).

7ccbd50a252a.title: Multivariate interpolation
7ccbd50a252a.sentence: Schemes defined for scattered data on an irregular grid are more general.

729c1ffc6ed9.title: Multivariate interpolation
729c1ffc6ed9.sentence: Gridding is the process of converting irregularly spaced data to a regular grid (gridded data).

98169ffaaf65.title: Geographic information system
98169ffaaf65.sentence: Digital elevation models, triangulated irregular networks, edge-finding algorithms, Thiessen polygons, Fourier analysis, (weighted) moving averages, inverse distance weighting, kriging, spline, and trend surface analysis are all mathematical methods to produce interpolative data.

45388e700f61.title: Kriging
45388e700f61.sentence: In statistics, originally in geostatistics, kriging or Kriging (/ˈkriːɡɪŋ/), also known as Gaussian process regression, is a method of interpolation based on Gaussian process governed by prior covariances.

16fa71617809.title: Kriging
16fa71617809.section: Main principles > Related terms and techniques
16fa71617809.sentence: Kriging predicts the value of a function at a given point by computing a weighted average of the known values of the function in the neighborhood of the point.

5a64df85f46e.title: Kriging
5a64df85f46e.sentence: The theoretical basis for the method was developed by the French mathematician Georges Matheron in 1960, based on the master's thesis of Danie G. Krige, the pioneering plotter of distance-weighted average gold grades at the Witwatersrand reef complex in South Africa.

d5ec24c0ce95.title: Kriging
d5ec24c0ce95.sentence: Krige sought to estimate the most likely distribution of gold based on samples from a few boreholes.

015303ab9256.title: Kriging
015303ab9256.sentence: Under suitable assumptions of the prior, kriging gives the best linear unbiased prediction (BLUP) at unsampled locations.

cf39855d1a32.title: Kriging
cf39855d1a32.sentence: Kriging seeks to minimize the mean square value of the following error in estimating Z(x0), subject to lack of bias:

027a4fec5ca9.title: Kriging
027a4fec5ca9.sentence: Since the random function is stationary, E[Z(xi)]=E[Z(x0)]=m, the weights must sum to 1 in order to ensure that the model is unbiased.

bb236a7783e0.title: Kriging
bb236a7783e0.sentence: - grows when the covariance between the samples and the point to estimate decreases.

226037bc26d5.title: Kriging
226037bc26d5.sentence: This means that, when the samples are farther away from x0, the estimation becomes worse;

9d2d8932b85e.title: Kriging
9d2d8932b85e.sentence: - does not depend on the values of the samples, which means that the same spatial configuration (with the same geometrical relations between samples and the point to estimate) always reproduces the same estimation variance in any part of the area A; this way, the variance does not measure the uncertainty of estimation produced by the local variable.

42e30772a5fd.title: Kriging
42e30772a5fd.sentence: The set of random variables constitutes a random function, of which only one realization is known – the set z(xi) of observed data.

48f229a005f1.title: Kriging
48f229a005f1.sentence: The proposed solution in the geostatistical formalism consists in assuming various degrees of stationarity in the random function, in order to make the inference of some statistic values possible.

9f0ee9d8d242.title: Kriging
9f0ee9d8d242.sentence: - Simple kriging assumes stationarity of the first moment over the entire domain with a known mean: E{Z(x)}=E{Z(x0)}=m, where m is the known mean.

0577764eaf80.title: Kriging
0577764eaf80.sentence: - Ordinary kriging assumes constant unknown mean only over the search neighborhood of x0.

a0337654d748.title: Kriging
a0337654d748.sentence: - Universal kriging assumes a general polynomial trend model, such as linear trend model E{Z(x)}=∑k=0pβkfk(x).

cc0826d35004.title: Kriging
cc0826d35004.sentence: - Indicator kriging uses indicator functions instead of the process itself, in order to estimate transition probabilities.

0812e60a14ff.title: Kriging
0812e60a14ff.sentence: - Co-kriging denotes the joint kriging of data from multiple sources with a relationship between the different data sources.

6f321a7d6466.title: Kriging
6f321a7d6466.sentence: Though computationally intensive in its basic formulation, kriging can be scaled to larger problems using various approximation methods.

0dc43145bc74.title: Regression-kriging
0dc43145bc74.sentence: In applied statistics and geostatistics, regression-kriging (RK) is a spatial prediction technique that combines a regression of the dependent variable on auxiliary variables (such as parameters derived from digital elevation modelling, remote sensing/imagery, and thematic maps) with interpolation (kriging) of the regression residuals.

b3db3f357722.title: Regression-kriging
b3db3f357722.sentence: It is mathematically equivalent to the interpolation method variously called universal kriging and kriging with external drift, where auxiliary predictors are used directly to solve the kriging weights.

00c7c2f2901b.title: Regression-kriging
00c7c2f2901b.sentence: In fact, both universal kriging, kriging with external drift, and regression-kriging are basically the same technique.

8c0a2f4bb1af.title: Regression-kriging
8c0a2f4bb1af.sentence: Matheron (1969) proposed that a value of a target variable at some location can be modeled as a sum of the deterministic and stochastic components:

a6845f13e699.title: Regression-kriging
a6845f13e699.sentence: which he termed universal model of spatial variation.

dd0030e745c9.title: Regression-kriging
dd0030e745c9.sentence: Both deterministic and stochastic components of spatial variation can be modeled separately.

f3b47fe34f43.sentence: Inverse distance weighting (IDW) is a type of deterministic method for multivariate interpolation with a known homogeneously scattered set of points.

5c568cb2d525.sentence: Random forests or random decision forests is an ensemble learning method for classification, regression and other tasks that works by creating a multitude of decision trees during training.

5d041acc452e.title: Random forest

4b0a76b02ab3.title: Random forest

b29ec776d061.title: Random forest

2223307e947c.title: Random forest

27728b9261de.sentence: At its most basic, the sampling design seeks to sample representatively from the geographic area of interest and all the soil forming factors (i.e., covariates); the underlying assumption is that the spatial variability of soil properties being predicted can be explained by the environmental covariates.

3a8337ec2a18.sentence: The most commonly used geometric approaches include grid sampling (GS), simple random sampling (SRS), stratified random sampling (StRS), transect sampling (TS), cluster sampling (CS) and nested sampling (NS).
