f3ecdf8dc69d.sentence: Fuzzy clustering (also referred to as soft clustering or soft k-means) is a form of clustering in which each data point can belong to more than one cluster.

0be93bc21bc6.title: Fuzzy clustering
0be93bc21bc6.sentence: In non-fuzzy clustering (also known as hard clustering), data are divided into distinct clusters, where each data point can only belong to exactly one cluster.

11ded397a1bc.title: Fuzzy clustering
11ded397a1bc.sentence: In fuzzy clustering, data points can potentially belong to multiple clusters.

c88d8e633148.title: Fuzzy clustering
c88d8e633148.sentence: Membership grades are assigned to each of the data points (tags).

138ae885edd8.title: Fuzzy clustering
138ae885edd8.sentence: Thus, points on the edge of a cluster, with lower membership grades, may be in the cluster to a lesser degree than points in the center of cluster.

e658c1637b59.title: Fuzzy clustering
e658c1637b59.sentence: Fuzzy c-means (FCM) clustering was developed by J.C. Dunn in 1973, and improved by J.C. Bezdek in 1981.

049964fd9428.title: Fuzzy clustering
049964fd9428.sentence: The fuzzy c-means algorithm is very similar to the k-means algorithm:

ca0416beb0ea.title: Fuzzy clustering
ca0416beb0ea.sentence: With fuzzy c-means, the centroid of a cluster is the mean of all points, weighted by their degree of belonging to the cluster, or, mathematically,

c5625d3e34cc.title: Fuzzy clustering
c5625d3e34cc.sentence: - Repeat until the algorithm has converged (that is, the coefficients' change between two iterations is no more than ε, the given sensitivity threshold):

7bd09ca9dc2d.title: Fuzzy clustering
7bd09ca9dc2d.sentence: where m is the hyper- parameter that controls how fuzzy the cluster will be (Where the fuzzier cluster means the cluster is less clear, and a data point can belong to multiple clusters at the same time.).

4eda3ff2a998.title: Fuzzy clustering
4eda3ff2a998.section: Fuzzy C-means clustering > Comparison to K-means clustering
4eda3ff2a998.sentence: In Fuzzy C-means, the degree of fuzziness is parametrized by m∈(1,∞), where a larger m results in fuzzier clusters.

6c5c6f24ee99.title: Fuzzy clustering
6c5c6f24ee99.section: Fuzzy C-means clustering > Comparison to K-means clustering
6c5c6f24ee99.sentence: In the limit m→1, the memberships, wij, converge to 0 or 1, and the Fuzzy C-means objective coincides with that of K-means.

0064c8343993.title: Fuzzy clustering
0064c8343993.section: Fuzzy C-means clustering > Comparison to K-means clustering
0064c8343993.sentence: In the absence of experimentation or domain knowledge, m is commonly set to 2.

a70ad6f6c792.title: Fuzzy clustering
a70ad6f6c792.section: Fuzzy C-means clustering > Comparison to K-means clustering
a70ad6f6c792.sentence: The algorithm minimizes intra-cluster variance as well, but has the same problems as 'k'-means; the minimum is a local minimum, and the results depend on the initial choice of weights.

b3889a6109ed.title: World Soil Museum
b3889a6109ed.sentence: Key data holdings include a large set of quality assessed and standardised soil profile data for the world (WoSIS) and a collection of soil property maps for the world (SoilGrids) derived using digital soil mapping based on WoSIS and a large selection of environmental covariates for the globe.

6dba1e8da8ed.title: International Soil Reference and Information Centre

efe2f809f77b.title: Gamma-ray spectrometer
efe2f809f77b.sentence: Gamma-ray spectrometers have been widely used for the elemental and isotopic analysis of bodies in the Solar System, especially the Moon and Mars.

360da10583d5.title: Gamma-ray spectrometer
360da10583d5.sentence: Thus an orbiting instrument can in principle map the surface distribution of the elements for an entire planet or other body, provided that it does not have an excessively thick atmosphere as is the case with Earth, Venus and the giant planets.

79a1cb7fc50c.title: Gamma-ray spectrometer
79a1cb7fc50c.section: Planetary gamma-ray spectrometers > How a GRS works
79a1cb7fc50c.sentence: Incoming cosmic rays—some of the highest-energy particles—collide with the nucleus of atoms in the soil.

fb93ce8b54d2.title: Gamma-ray spectrometer
fb93ce8b54d2.section: Planetary gamma-ray spectrometers > How a GRS works
fb93ce8b54d2.sentence: When nuclei are hit with such energy, neutrons are released, which scatter and collide with other nuclei.

e54aa539af99.title: Gamma-ray spectrometer
e54aa539af99.section: Planetary gamma-ray spectrometers > How a GRS works
e54aa539af99.sentence: The nuclei get "excited" in the process, and emit gamma rays to release the extra energy so they can return to their normal rest state.

de85d8c5ac23.title: Gamma-ray spectrometer
de85d8c5ac23.section: Planetary gamma-ray spectrometers > How a GRS works
de85d8c5ac23.sentence: While the energy represented in these emissions determines which elements are present, the intensity of the spectrum reveals the elements concentrations.

733791d26a0a.title: Gamma-ray spectrometer
733791d26a0a.sentence: They are able to measure the abundance and distribution of about 20 primary elements of the periodic table, including silicon, oxygen, iron, magnesium, potassium, aluminum, calcium, sulfur, and carbon.

74efc9e8abeb.title: Gamma-ray spectrometer
74efc9e8abeb.sentence: By measuring neutrons, it is possible to calculate the abundance of hydrogen, thus inferring the presence of water.

69677bb5e5aa.title: Gamma-ray spectrometer
69677bb5e5aa.sentence: The neutron detectors are sensitive to concentrations of hydrogen in the upper meter of the surface.

6ab2d20323df.title: Gamma-ray spectrometer
6ab2d20323df.sentence: To determine the elemental makeup of the Martian surface, Mars Odyssey uses a gamma-ray spectrometer and two neutron detectors.

5183d4ed5acc.title: Latin hypercube sampling
5183d4ed5acc.sentence: Latin hypercube sampling (LHS) is a statistical method for generating a near-random sample of parameter values from a multidimensional distribution.

4b8f1c5b731e.title: Latin hypercube sampling
4b8f1c5b731e.sentence: When sampling a function of N variables, the range of each variable is divided into M equally probable intervals.

017fecf44742.title: Latin hypercube sampling
017fecf44742.sentence: M sample points are then placed to satisfy the Latin hypercube requirements; this forces the number of divisions, M, to be equal for each variable.

04514b854146.title: Latin hypercube sampling
04514b854146.sentence: Such configuration is similar to having N rooks on a chess board without threatening each other.

b6689d88e1d2.title: Latin hypercube sampling
b6689d88e1d2.sentence: This sampling scheme does not require more samples for more dimensions (variables); this independence is one of the main advantages of this sampling scheme.

63da9ddd768b.title: Latin hypercube sampling
63da9ddd768b.sentence: Another advantage is that multiple random samples can be taken in sequence, remembering which samples were taken so far.

1e64fb454a3c.title: Latin hypercube sampling
1e64fb454a3c.sentence: One does not necessarily need to know beforehand how many sample points are needed.

6d9ce4339dd2.title: Latin hypercube sampling
6d9ce4339dd2.sentence: - In Latin hypercube sampling one must first decide how many sample points to use and for each sample point remember in which row and column the sample point was taken.

44d56666f5a9.title: Latin hypercube sampling
44d56666f5a9.sentence: All sample points are then chosen simultaneously making sure that the total set of sample points is a Latin hypercube sample and that each subspace is sampled with the same density.

450b5bd59171.title: Uncertainty quantification
450b5bd59171.sentence: Uncertainty Quantification (UQ) is the science of quantitative characterization and estimation of uncertainties in both computational and real world applications.

005434072402.title: Uncertainty quantification
005434072402.sentence: It tries to determine how likely certain outcomes are if some aspects of the system are not exactly known.

497e36200cf1.title: Uncertainty quantification
497e36200cf1.sentence: There are two major types of problems in uncertainty quantification: one is the forward propagation of uncertainty (where the various sources of uncertainty are propagated through the model to predict the overall uncertainty in the system response) and the other is the inverse assessment of model uncertainty and parameter uncertainty (where the model parameters are calibrated simultaneously using test data).

4f4e15e25e36.title: Uncertainty quantification
4f4e15e25e36.sentence: - To evaluate low-order moments of the outputs, i.e. mean and variance.

1bb096e5f99e.title: Uncertainty quantification
1bb096e5f99e.sentence: - To evaluate the reliability of the outputs.

e743f2fbd0f4.title: Uncertainty quantification
e743f2fbd0f4.sentence: - To assess the complete probability distribution of the outputs.

7a93e29d9fe9.title: Uncertainty quantification
7a93e29d9fe9.sentence: Given some experimental measurements of a system and some computer simulation results from its mathematical model, inverse uncertainty quantification estimates the discrepancy between the experiment and the mathematical model (which is called bias correction), and estimates the values of unknown parameters in the model if there are any (which is called parameter calibration or simply calibration).

c2b25999f497.title: Uncertainty quantification
c2b25999f497.sentence: There are basically six categories of probabilistic approaches for uncertainty propagation:

024f57b3ac92.title: Uncertainty quantification
024f57b3ac92.sentence: - Simulation-based methods: Monte Carlo simulations, importance sampling, adaptive sampling, etc.

1aa10108812c.title: Uncertainty quantification
1aa10108812c.sentence: - General surrogate-based methods: In a non-intrusive approach, a surrogate model is learnt in order to replace the experiment or the simulation with a cheap and fast approximation.

00cf2b45532a.title: Uncertainty quantification
00cf2b45532a.sentence: - Local expansion-based methods: Taylor series, perturbation method, etc. These methods have advantages when dealing with relatively small input variability and outputs that don't express high nonlinearity.

06ed2ebf939d.title: Uncertainty quantification
06ed2ebf939d.sentence: - Most probable point (MPP)-based methods: first-order reliability method (FORM) and second-order reliability method (SORM).

97fd09c8a7e7.title: Uncertainty quantification
97fd09c8a7e7.sentence: Generally this is a much more difficult problem than forward uncertainty propagation; however it is of great importance since it is typically implemented in a model updating process.

ee84656c7aaf.title: Uncertainty quantification
ee84656c7aaf.sentence: - Dimensionality issue: The computational cost increases dramatically with the dimensionality of the problem, i.e. the number of input variables and/or the number of unknown parameters.

6f77618b23cb.title: Uncertainty quantification
6f77618b23cb.sentence: - Identifiability issue: Multiple combinations of unknown parameters and discrepancy function can yield the same experimental prediction.

bcb0543d4d03.title: Near-infrared spectroscopy
bcb0543d4d03.sentence: Near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) is a spectroscopic method that uses the near-infrared region of the electromagnetic spectrum (from 780 nm to 2500 nm).

662e4612aeba.title: Near-infrared spectroscopy
662e4612aeba.sentence: Near-infrared spectroscopy is based on molecular overtone and combination vibrations.

082f7c667fdc.title: Near-infrared spectroscopy
082f7c667fdc.sentence: (NIR absorption bands are typically 10–100 times weaker than the corresponding fundamental mid-IR absorption band.) The lower absorption allows NIR radiation to penetrate much further into a sample than mid infrared radiation.

17b9f863b3a0.title: Near-infrared spectroscopy
17b9f863b3a0.sentence: Near-infrared spectroscopy is, therefore, not a particularly sensitive technique, but it can be very useful in probing bulk material with little to no sample preparation.

00ee223b9498.title: Near-infrared spectroscopy
00ee223b9498.sentence: The molecular overtone and combination bands seen in the near-IR are typically very broad, leading to complex spectra; it can be difficult to assign specific features to specific chemical components.

66311a6c7592.title: Near-infrared spectroscopy
66311a6c7592.sentence: Multivariate (multiple variables) calibration techniques (e.g., principal components analysis, partial least squares, or artificial neural networks) are often employed to extract the desired chemical information.

4963c58012bf.title: Near-infrared spectroscopy
4963c58012bf.sentence: Careful development of a set of calibration samples and application of multivariate calibration techniques is essential for near-infrared analytical methods.

764d3d2f5e3d.title: Near-infrared spectroscopy
764d3d2f5e3d.sentence: In the 1980s, Karl Norris (while working at the USDA Instrumentation Research Laboratory, Beltsville, USA) pioneered the use NIR spectroscopy for quality assessments of agricultural products.

957041947c87.title: Near-infrared spectroscopy
957041947c87.sentence: It is widely used to quantify the composition of agricultural products because it meets the criteria of being accurate, reliable, rapid, non-destructive, and inexpensive.

cf5e7e854c72.title: Soil test
cf5e7e854c72.sentence: Lab tests are more accurate and often utilize very precise flow injection technology (or Near InfraRed (NIR) scanning).

292b95558baa.title: Chemometrics
292b95558baa.sentence: Chemometrics is the science of extracting information from chemical systems by data-driven means.

a4ff7dcdde14.title: Chemometrics
a4ff7dcdde14.sentence: Chemometrics is inherently interdisciplinary, using methods frequently employed in core data-analytic disciplines such as multivariate statistics, applied mathematics, and computer science, in order to address problems in chemistry, biochemistry, medicine, biology and chemical engineering.

e0aa46867550.title: Chemometrics
e0aa46867550.sentence: The term 'chemometrics' was coined by Svante Wold in a 1971 grant application, and the International Chemometrics Society was formed shortly thereafter by Svante Wold and Bruce Kowalski, two pioneers in the field.

7ee8f44fca87.title: Chemometrics
7ee8f44fca87.sentence: Although one could argue that even the earliest analytical experiments in chemistry involved a form of chemometrics, the field is generally recognized to have emerged in the 1970s as computers became increasingly exploited for scientific investigation.

48165fa2ab0e.title: Chemometrics
48165fa2ab0e.sentence: Data from infrared and UV/visible spectroscopy are often counted in thousands of measurements per sample.

642777fa88df.title: Chemometrics
642777fa88df.sentence: This is primarily because, while the datasets may be highly multivariate there is strong and often linear low-rank structure present.

24d78de2486e.title: Chemometrics
24d78de2486e.sentence: PCA and PLS have been shown over time very effective at empirically modeling the more chemically interesting low-rank structure, exploiting the interrelationships or 'latent variables' in the data, and providing alternative compact coordinate systems for further numerical analysis such as regression, clustering, and pattern recognition.

5c83d5026abd.title: Chemometrics
5c83d5026abd.sentence: The performance of quantitative models is usually specified by root mean squared error in predicting the attribute of interest, and the performance of classifiers as a true-positive rate/false-positive rate pairs (or a full ROC curve).

6789b21e8c02.title: Chemometrics
6789b21e8c02.sentence: Chemometric model selection usually involves the use of tools such as resampling (including bootstrap, permutation, cross-validation).

ba00f217f6f5.title: Partial least squares regression
ba00f217f6f5.sentence: Partial least squares (PLS) regression is a statistical method that bears some relation to principal components regression and is a reduced rank regression; instead of finding hyperplanes of maximum variance between the response and independent variables, it finds a linear regression model by projecting the predicted variables and the observable variables to a new space of maximum covariance (see below).

b2fa1e8b1fca.title: Partial least squares regression
b2fa1e8b1fca.sentence: Because both the X and Y data are projected to new spaces, the PLS family of methods are known as bilinear factor models.

0f2e2a47eb72.title: Partial least squares regression
0f2e2a47eb72.sentence: PLS is used to find the fundamental relations between two matrices (X and Y), i.e. a latent variable approach to modeling the covariance structures in these two spaces.

cf2c55cfc709.title: Partial least squares regression
cf2c55cfc709.sentence: A PLS model will try to find the multidimensional direction in the X space that explains the maximum multidimensional variance direction in the Y space.

5514e342d0ec.title: Partial least squares regression
5514e342d0ec.sentence: PLS regression is particularly suited when the matrix of predictors has more variables than observations, and when there is multicollinearity among X values.

ea85c831b57b.title: Partial least squares regression
ea85c831b57b.sentence: By contrast, standard regression will fail in these cases (unless it is regularized).

f498a23cab6f.title: Partial least squares regression
f498a23cab6f.sentence: Partial least squares was introduced by the Swedish statistician Herman O. A. Wold, who then developed it with his son, Svante Wold.

3103333e60fa.title: Partial least squares regression
3103333e60fa.sentence: Although the original applications were in the social sciences, PLS regression is today most widely used in chemometrics and related areas.

a35e054e29c5.title: Partial least squares regression
a35e054e29c5.sentence: PLS is composed of iteratively repeating the following steps k times (for k components):

2a03a5624f2f.title: Partial least squares regression
2a03a5624f2f.sentence: - finding the directions of maximal covariance in input and output space

2b9829d26c80.title: Partial least squares regression
2b9829d26c80.sentence: - performing least squares regression on the input score

f686949d71b0.title: Partial least squares regression
f686949d71b0.sentence: PLS1 is a widely used algorithm appropriate for the vector Y case.

a498c110d604.title: Partial least squares regression
a498c110d604.sentence: Partial least squares discriminant analysis (PLS-DA) is a variant used when the Y is categorical.

1a2bd43df8f5.title: Chemometrics
1a2bd43df8f5.sentence: The objective is to develop models which can be used to predict properties of interest based on measured properties of the chemical system, such as pressure, flow, temperature, infrared, Raman, NMR spectra and mass spectra.

4233566c6991.title: Chemometrics
4233566c6991.sentence: The process requires a calibration or training data set, which includes reference values for the properties of interest for prediction, and the measured attributes believed to correspond to these properties.

04a93853cf43.title: Chemometrics
04a93853cf43.sentence: For case 1), for example, one can assemble data from a number of samples, including concentrations for an analyte of interest for each sample (the reference) and the corresponding infrared spectrum of that sample.

23b4c9e1f102.title: Chemometrics
23b4c9e1f102.sentence: Multivariate calibration techniques such as partial-least squares regression, or principal component regression (and near countless other methods) are then used to construct a mathematical model that relates the multivariate response (spectrum) to the concentration of the analyte of interest, and such a model can be used to efficiently predict the concentrations of new samples.

8903633433f8.title: Chemometrics
8903633433f8.sentence: Techniques in multivariate calibration are often broadly categorized as classical or inverse methods.

e58cd32c0347.title: Chemometrics
e58cd32c0347.sentence: The principal difference between these approaches is that in classical calibration the models are solved such that they are optimal in describing the measured analytical responses (e.g., spectra) and can therefore be considered optimal descriptors, whereas in inverse methods the models are solved to be optimal in predicting the properties of interest (e.g., concentrations, optimal predictors).

f4d0f3bb3ed1.title: Chemometrics
f4d0f3bb3ed1.sentence: Inverse methods usually require less physical knowledge of the chemical system, and at least in theory provide superior predictions in the mean-squared error sense, and hence inverse approaches tend to be more frequently applied in contemporary multivariate calibration.

2ec82a1b5c02.title: Chemometrics
2ec82a1b5c02.sentence: The main advantages of the use of multivariate calibration techniques is that fast, cheap, or non-destructive analytical measurements (such as optical spectroscopy) can be used to estimate sample properties which would otherwise require time-consuming, expensive or destructive testing (such as LC-MS).

165423e0a379.title: Chemometrics
165423e0a379.sentence: Equally important is that multivariate calibration allows for accurate quantitative analysis in the presence of heavy interference by other analytes.

d5a1aede4c01.title: Chemometrics
d5a1aede4c01.sentence: The selectivity of the analytical method is provided as much by the mathematical calibration, as the analytical measurement modalities.

a88169055aec.title: Chemometrics
a88169055aec.sentence: For example, near-infrared spectra, which are extremely broad and non-selective compared to other analytical techniques (such as infrared or Raman spectra), can often be used successfully in conjunction with carefully developed multivariate calibration methods to predict concentrations of analytes in very complex matrices.

065e7c874d22.title: Carbon cycle
065e7c874d22.sentence: The carbon cycle is a part of the biogeochemical cycle where carbon is exchanged among the biosphere, pedosphere, geosphere, hydrosphere, and atmosphere of Earth.

69ca9a7f6c3c.title: Carbon cycle
69ca9a7f6c3c.sentence: Carbon is the main component of biological compounds as well as a major component of many rocks such as limestone.

4c2dbc531e1d.title: Carbon cycle
4c2dbc531e1d.sentence: The global carbon cycle is now usually divided into the following major reservoirs of carbon (also called carbon pools) interconnected by pathways of exchange:

b521c3327228.title: Carbon cycle
b521c3327228.sentence: - Ocean, including dissolved inorganic carbon and living and non-living marine biota

d7606fe5974e.title: Carbon cycle
d7606fe5974e.sentence: - Sediments, including fossil fuels, freshwater systems, and non-living organic material.

98c2e56c28ef.title: Carbon cycle
98c2e56c28ef.sentence: The carbon exchanges between reservoirs occur as the result of various chemical, physical, geological, and biological processes.

121e799963be.title: Carbon cycle
121e799963be.sentence: The ocean contains the largest active pool of carbon near the surface of the Earth.

3df60a53cc8e.title: Carbon cycle
3df60a53cc8e.sentence: Carbon dioxide is removed from the atmosphere primarily through photosynthesis and enters the terrestrial and oceanic biospheres.

a6940807ccb3.title: Carbon cycle
a6940807ccb3.sentence: The natural flows of carbon between the atmosphere, ocean, terrestrial ecosystems, and sediments are fairly balanced; so carbon levels would be roughly stable without human influence.

27a273a4b8d0.title: Carbon cycle
27a273a4b8d0.sentence: Humans have disturbed the carbon cycle for many centuries.

a94efdb42b94.title: Carbon cycle
a94efdb42b94.sentence: They have done so by modifying land use and by mining and burning carbon from ancient organic remains (coal, petroleum and gas).

9a52f069b219.title: Carbon cycle
9a52f069b219.sentence: Carbon dioxide in the atmosphere has increased nearly 52% over pre-industrial levels by 2020, resulting in global warming.

f00cb19b549b.title: Carbon cycle
f00cb19b549b.section: Human influence on fast carbon cycle > Climate change
f00cb19b549b.sentence: Carbon sinks in the land and the ocean each currently take up about one-quarter of anthropogenic carbon emissions each year.

bc50ad80c52c.title: Soil carbon
bc50ad80c52c.sentence: Soil carbon is the solid carbon stored in global soils.

1195b8ac727a.title: Soil carbon
1195b8ac727a.sentence: This includes both soil organic matter, derived from plant, animal, and microbial tissues, and inorganic carbon as carbonate minerals.

1f2f5cc507f8.title: Soil carbon
1f2f5cc507f8.sentence: Soil carbon contributes to vital functions of soil in ecosystems, including water holding capacity, nutrient retention, and soil structure.

57c1bd2f5a62.title: Soil carbon
57c1bd2f5a62.sentence: Of the 2,700 Gt of carbon stored in soils worldwide, 1550 GtC is organic and 950 GtC is inorganic carbon, which is approximately three times greater than the current atmospheric carbon and 240 times higher compared with the current annual fossil fuel emission.

6c9f84bc6a44.title: Soil carbon
6c9f84bc6a44.sentence: The balance of soil carbon is held in peat and wetlands (150 GtC), and in plant litter at the soil surface (50 GtC).

99838dade3d5.title: Soil carbon
99838dade3d5.sentence: While many environmental factors affect the total stored carbon in terrestrial ecosystems, photosynthesis, respiration, and decomposition are the main drivers in balancing the total amount of stored carbon on land.

94d48650e64f.title: Soil carbon
94d48650e64f.sentence: About 60 GtC/yr accumulates in the soil.

85b616803817.title: Soil carbon
85b616803817.sentence: An equivalent 60 GtC/yr is respired from soil, joining the 60 GtC/yr plant respiration to return to the atmosphere.

683e0c5ed4ea.title: Soil carbon
683e0c5ed4ea.sentence: Soil carbon is a carbon sink in the global carbon cycle, playing a role in biogeochemistry, climate change mitigation.

2cf86e3f6a8f.title: Soil carbon
2cf86e3f6a8f.sentence: As such, data on soil carbon quality and change is important to constructing global climate models.

a02a510d20c9.title: Soil carbon
a02a510d20c9.sentence: Human activities have caused a massive loss of soil organic carbon; however, there is potential for human activity to intentionally divert carbon back to the soil.

b2d6cfc1b94d.title: Soil carbon
b2d6cfc1b94d.sentence: Globally, data on soil organic carbon is inconsistent, with some regions having far more comprehensive data than others.

2a3722bd9c65.title: Carbon sink
2a3722bd9c65.sentence: A carbon sink is a natural or artificial carbon sequestration process that "removes a greenhouse gas, an aerosol or a precursor of a greenhouse gas from the atmosphere".

d8a5a24b081a.title: Carbon sink
d8a5a24b081a.sentence: A carbon sink is a type of carbon pool that has the capability to take up more carbon from the atmosphere than it releases.

15e9db17aaa1.title: Carbon sink
15e9db17aaa1.sentence: These sinks form an important part of the natural carbon cycle.

c01aeccac8ef.title: Carbon sink
c01aeccac8ef.sentence: Globally, the two most important carbon sinks are vegetation and the ocean.

8c0e08cc1728.title: Carbon sink
8c0e08cc1728.sentence: Soil is an important carbon storage medium.

fedf1bf901d6.title: Carbon sink
fedf1bf901d6.sentence: - Soil is a carbon store and active carbon sink.

3ee3f4b9c6d8.title: Carbon sink
3ee3f4b9c6d8.sentence: - Photosynthesis by terrestrial plants with grass and trees allows them to serve as carbon sinks during growing seasons.

a4718dbee7d6.title: Carbon sink
a4718dbee7d6.sentence: - Absorption of carbon dioxide by the oceans via solubility and biological pumps.

0b92d40c53bc.title: Carbon sink
0b92d40c53bc.sentence: Artificial carbon sinks are those that store carbon in building materials or deep underground (geologic carbon sequestration).

a695b2a9fd98.title: Carbon sink
a695b2a9fd98.sentence: No major artificial systems remove carbon from the atmosphere on a large scale yet.

d8a78e6fa559.title: Carbon sink
d8a78e6fa559.sentence: In the case of non-CO2 greenhouse gases, sinks need not store the gas.

0f16362ba228.title: Carbon sink
0f16362ba228.sentence: For example, nitrous oxide can be reduced to harmless N2.

7d71c393ef6e.title: Carbon sink
7d71c393ef6e.sentence: In the past, human practices like deforestation and industrial agriculture have depleted natural carbon sinks.

851f2217883e.title: Carbon sink
851f2217883e.sentence: This kind of land use change has been one of the causes of climate change.

584c96fac72d.title: Carbon sink
584c96fac72d.sentence: For climate change mitigation purposes, the maintenance and enhancement of natural carbon sinks, mainly soils and forests, is important.

0127bd450a66.title: Climate change mitigation
0127bd450a66.sentence: Climate change mitigation, also called decarbonisation, is an action to limit the greenhouse gases in the atmosphere that cause climate change.

ebe3ec378c12.title: Climate change mitigation
ebe3ec378c12.sentence: Climate change mitigation actions include conserving energy and replacing fossil fuels with clean energy sources.

59ebe62c0849.title: Climate change mitigation
59ebe62c0849.sentence: An important mitigation measure is "preserving and enhancing carbon sinks".

631893eb1940.title: Climate change mitigation
631893eb1940.sentence: This refers to the management of Earth's natural carbon sinks in a way that preserves or increases their capability to remove CO2 from the atmosphere and to store it durably.

238393aad205.title: Climate change mitigation
238393aad205.sentence: Scientists call this process also carbon sequestration.

064b056a4499.title: Climate change mitigation
064b056a4499.sentence: Land-based mitigation options are referred to as "AFOLU mitigation options" in the 2022 IPCC report on mitigation.

106a871b02fd.title: Climate change mitigation
106a871b02fd.sentence: The economic potential of these activities has been estimated to be 4.2 to 7.4 gigatonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent (GtCO2 -eq) per year.

167ef80495b6.title: Climate change mitigation
167ef80495b6.section: Mitigation by sector > Agriculture, forestry and land use
167ef80495b6.sentence: Almost 20% of greenhouse gas emissions come from the agriculture and forestry sector.

bc4b440e8937.title: Carbon sequestration
bc4b440e8937.sentence: Carbon sequestration is a natural process of storing carbon in a carbon pool.

48f4121c994b.title: Carbon sequestration
48f4121c994b.sentence: The IPCC Sixth Assessment Report defines carbon sequestration as "The process of storing carbon in a carbon pool".

80144ccfa1db.title: Carbon sequestration
80144ccfa1db.sentence: It plays a crucial role in effectively managing the global carbon cycle and limiting climate change by reducing the amount of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere.

df1cbbdff5c8.title: Carbon sequestration
df1cbbdff5c8.sentence: There are two main types of carbon sequestration: biologic (also called biosequestration) and geologic.

e22f57257372.title: Carbon sequestration
e22f57257372.sentence: Biological carbon sequestration (also called biosequestration) is the capture and storage of the atmospheric greenhouse gas carbon dioxide by continual and enhanced biological processes.

84e053081fd9.title: Carbon sequestration
84e053081fd9.sentence: These processes can be accelerated for example through changes in land use and agricultural practices, called carbon farming.

9c15a119775d.title: Carbon sequestration
9c15a119775d.sentence: The United States Geological Survey (USGS) defines carbon sequestration as follows: "Carbon sequestration is the process of capturing and storing atmospheric carbon dioxide." Because the wording in this definition makes it very similar to the definition of carbon capture and storage (CCS), carbon sequestration is sometimes confounded with CCS (the IPCC defines CCS as "a process in which a relatively pure stream of carbon dioxide (CO2) from industrial sources is separated, treated and transported to a long-term storage location").

a01781eb937f.title: Carbon sequestration
a01781eb937f.sentence: It involves using technology to capture and sequester (store) CO 2 that is produced from human activities underground or under the sea bed.

dde7acb83718.title: Carbon sequestration
dde7acb83718.sentence: However, biological stores (such as forests and kelp beds) may be temporary carbon sinks, as long-term sequestration cannot be guaranteed.

e57e35e748c9.title: Carbon sequestration
e57e35e748c9.sentence: Wildfires, disease, economic pressures, and changing political priorities may release the sequestered carbon back into the atmosphere.

2a1dbca7698e.title: Carbon sequestration
2a1dbca7698e.sentence: Carbon dioxide that has been removed from the atmosphere can also be stored in the Earth's crust by injecting it underground, or in the form of insoluble carbonate salts.

94200de8a2f4.title: Carbon sequestration
94200de8a2f4.sentence: The latter process is called mineral sequestration.

5396ec325796.title: Carbon sequestration
5396ec325796.sentence: This means the carbon is "locked away" for thousands to millions of years.

e5bb2a31d763.title: Carbon sequestration
e5bb2a31d763.section: Biological carbon sequestration on land > Agriculture
e5bb2a31d763.sentence: When soil is converted from natural land or semi-natural land, such as forests, woodlands, grasslands, steppes, and savannas, the SOC content in the soil reduces by about 30–40%.

73e7893b555f.title: Carbon sequestration
73e7893b555f.section: Biological carbon sequestration on land > Agriculture
73e7893b555f.sentence: When land use changes, the carbon in the soil will either increase or decrease, and this change will continue until the soil reaches a new equilibrium.

ad0e075d0236.title: Carbon sequestration
ad0e075d0236.section: Biological carbon sequestration on land > Agriculture
ad0e075d0236.sentence: This can be done with several strategies, e.g. leave harvest residues on the field, use manure as fertilizer, or include perennial crops in the rotation.

3393fb588a63.title: Carbon sequestration
3393fb588a63.section: Biological carbon sequestration on land > Agriculture
3393fb588a63.sentence: Perennial crops have a larger below-ground biomass fraction, which increases the SOC content.

62434450d6f3.title: Carbon sequestration
62434450d6f3.section: Biological carbon sequestration on land > Agriculture
62434450d6f3.sentence: About 70% of the global soil organic carbon in non-permafrost areas is found in the deeper soil within the upper metre and is stabilized by mineral-organic associations.

1b950c7173bc.title: Soil carbon
1b950c7173bc.sentence: Climate change has significant impacts on soil formation, as temperature and moisture levels alter the development of chemical and physical properties in the soil.

afb739ba44f3.title: Soil carbon
afb739ba44f3.sentence: Therefore, changes in climate will likely impact the soil in many ways, including the fertility, salinity, moisture, temperature, SOC, sequestration, aggregation etc.

65cf87db2779.title: Soil carbon
65cf87db2779.sentence: Anthropogenic activities such as deforestation cause releases of carbon from this pool, which may significantly increase the concentration of greenhouse gas (GHG) in the atmosphere.

a86babaa91ac.title: Soil carbon
a86babaa91ac.sentence: Soil also has carbon sequestration abilities where carbon dioxide is fixed in the soil by plant uptakes.

603c9e478628.title: Soil carbon
603c9e478628.sentence: This accounts for the majority of the soil organic matter (SOM) in the ground, and creates a large storage pool (around 1500 Pg) for carbon in just the first few meters of soil and 20-40% of that organic carbon has a residence life exceeding 100 years.

5b812c45c442.title: Soil carbon
5b812c45c442.sentence: Forest soils constitute a large pool of carbon.

15a7990988d5.title: Soil carbon
15a7990988d5.sentence: Microorganisms play an important role in breaking down carbon in the soil.

8c47f44cf2af.title: Soil carbon
8c47f44cf2af.sentence: Changes in their activity due to rising temperatures could possibly influence and even contribute to climate change.

56926e140c97.title: Soil carbon
56926e140c97.section: Soil carbon and climate change > Measuring data on soil organic carbon
56926e140c97.sentence: For example, in polar regions where temperatures are more susceptible to drastic changes, melting permafrost can expose more land which leads to higher rates of plant growth and eventually, higher carbon absorption.

df031904f573.title: Soil carbon
df031904f573.section: Soil carbon and climate change > Measuring data on soil organic carbon
df031904f573.sentence: In contrast, tropical environments experience worsening soil quality because soil aggregation levels decrease with higher temperatures.

8f69b9467fae.title: Soil carbon
8f69b9467fae.sentence: Researchers are interested in discovering ways that human intervention can adequately restore carbon to the soils, through farming and other practices.

58e78d911e81.title: Effects of climate change on agriculture
58e78d911e81.sentence: There are numerous effects of climate change on agriculture, many of which are making it harder for agricultural activities to provide global food security.
58e78d911e81.key: Effects of climate change on agriculture

552fa88de05a.title: Effects of climate change on agriculture
552fa88de05a.sentence: Recent research has found that climate change is likely to exacerbate the existing environmental impacts of agriculture by lowering crop productivity, reducing the effectiveness of agrochemicals, increasing soil erosion and pest pressures, and thereby driving greater use of land, water and inputs.
552fa88de05a.key: Effects of climate change on agriculture

30316feb11e0.title: Effects of climate change on agriculture
30316feb11e0.sentence: Rising temperatures and changing weather patterns often result in lower crop yields due to water scarcity caused by drought, heat waves and flooding.
30316feb11e0.key: Effects of climate change on agriculture

9ce786747173.title: Effects of climate change on agriculture
9ce786747173.sentence: One study found that 1°C of warming was associated with a 3 to 7% decrease in global yields of major staple crops.
9ce786747173.key: Effects of climate change on agriculture

772f7a137d9f.title: Effects of climate change on agriculture
772f7a137d9f.sentence: On the coasts, some agricultural land is expected to be lost to sea level rise, while melting glaciers could result in less irrigation water being available.
772f7a137d9f.key: Effects of climate change on agriculture

e472d2f453d8.title: Effects of climate change on agriculture
e472d2f453d8.sentence: On the other hand, more arable land may become available as frozen land thaws.
e472d2f453d8.key: Effects of climate change on agriculture

10323e6cc1a9.title: Effects of climate change on agriculture
10323e6cc1a9.sentence: Other effects include erosion and changes in soil fertility and the length of growing seasons.
10323e6cc1a9.key: Effects of climate change on agriculture

35632dec8e1a.title: Effects of climate change on agriculture
35632dec8e1a.sentence: This effect offsets a small portion of the detrimental effects of climate change on agriculture.
35632dec8e1a.key: Effects of climate change on agriculture

101a299fd754.title: Effects of climate change on agriculture
101a299fd754.sentence: However, it comes at the expense of lower levels of essential micronutrients in the crops.
101a299fd754.key: Effects of climate change on agriculture

4e063f406381.title: Effects of climate change on agriculture
4e063f406381.sentence: Furthermore, CO2 fertilization has little effect on C4 crops like maize.
4e063f406381.key: Effects of climate change on agriculture

c5454be23d5b.title: Effects of climate change on agriculture
c5454be23d5b.sentence: The future degree of soil erosion and groundwater depletion are further uncertainties.
c5454be23d5b.key: Effects of climate change on agriculture

04e1136b0f6e.title: Effects of climate change on agriculture
04e1136b0f6e.sentence: Adaptation can occur through changes in management practices, agricultural innovation, institutional changes, and climate-smart agriculture.
04e1136b0f6e.key: Effects of climate change on agriculture

ef8620986be6.title: Soil carbon
ef8620986be6.sentence: Soil inorganic carbon consists of mineral forms of carbon, either from weathering of parent material, or from reaction of soil minerals with atmospheric CO2.

ecc2459e9dca.title: Soil carbon
ecc2459e9dca.section: Forms of Carbon in Soil > Inorganic Carbon
ecc2459e9dca.sentence: In arid and semi-arid environments, a majority of soil carbon occurs in the form of inorganic carbonates, such as the minerals calcite and dolomite.

c8dbf339f5ce.title: Soil carbon
c8dbf339f5ce.sentence: Carbonate minerals are the dominant form of soil carbon in desert climates.

303b6967fbba.title: Carbon cycle
303b6967fbba.sentence: Most carbon in the terrestrial biosphere is organic carbon, while about a third of soil carbon is stored in inorganic forms, such as calcium carbonate.

1b817cc60e5e.title: Enhanced weathering
1b817cc60e5e.section: Natural mineral weathering and ocean acidification
1b817cc60e5e.sentence: These are reversible reactions, so if the carbonate encounters H ions from acids, such as in soils, they will react to form water and release CO2 back to the atmosphere.

df1ff4a5d05b.title: Soil carbon
df1ff4a5d05b.sentence: Soil organic carbon is present as soil organic matter.

0b042c18f45a.title: Soil carbon
0b042c18f45a.section: Forms of Carbon in Soil > Organic carbon
0b042c18f45a.sentence: Soil organic carbon is part of soil organic matter, which contains approximately 50% carbon by dry weight, with the remaining mass made up primarily of hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, and sulfur.

15ddd6ed294f.title: Soil carbon
15ddd6ed294f.section: Forms of Carbon in Soil > Organic carbon
15ddd6ed294f.sentence: In humid environments, the majority of soil carbon is organic.

bf418ab870c0.title: Soil carbon
bf418ab870c0.section: Forms of Carbon in Soil > Organic carbon
bf418ab870c0.sentence: Detritus resulting from plant senescence is the major source of soil organic carbon, as organic matter is added to soil in the form of plant roots, fallen leaves, and crop residue.

8a31e56246da.title: Soil carbon
8a31e56246da.section: Forms of Carbon in Soil > Organic carbon
8a31e56246da.sentence: Animal bodies and excreta also add organic matter, and thus carbon, to the soil.

13dc71ee0f47.title: Soil carbon
13dc71ee0f47.section: Forms of Carbon in Soil > Organic carbon
13dc71ee0f47.sentence: 5–20% of the total carbon carbon fixed by plants during photosynthesis is supplied as root exudates in support of rhizospheric mutualistic biota.

b4be3c515082.title: Soil carbon
b4be3c515082.section: Forms of Carbon in Soil > Organic carbon
b4be3c515082.sentence: As exudates, plant roots feed carbon to mycorrhizal fungi in exchange for stored nutrients.

45e1c3bc3c55.title: Soil carbon
45e1c3bc3c55.section: Forms of Carbon in Soil > Organic carbon
45e1c3bc3c55.sentence: Some plant compounds, such as cellulose, starches, proteins, and lipids, are readily degraded by microbes, resulting in short residence times, while more persistent forms of organic C include lignin, humus, organic matter encapsulated in soil aggregates and charcoal.

df9b9ed25a89.title: Soil carbon
df9b9ed25a89.section: Forms of Carbon in Soil > Organic carbon
df9b9ed25a89.sentence: These resist alteration and have long residence times.

e27c6c933735.title: Soil carbon
e27c6c933735.section: Forms of Carbon in Soil > Organic carbon
e27c6c933735.sentence: Topsoil ranges from 0.5% to 3.0% organic carbon for most upland soils.

f14e8562ef1c.title: Soil carbon
f14e8562ef1c.section: Forms of Carbon in Soil > Organic carbon
f14e8562ef1c.sentence: Soils with less than 0.5% organic C are mostly limited to desert areas.

e664e95d3565.title: Soil carbon
e664e95d3565.section: Forms of Carbon in Soil > Organic carbon
e664e95d3565.sentence: Soils containing greater than 12–18% organic carbon are generally classified as organic soils.

1f17a8e607d2.title: Soil carbon
1f17a8e607d2.section: Forms of Carbon in Soil > Organic carbon
1f17a8e607d2.sentence: High levels of organic C develop in soils when organic matter additions are greater than losses, typically in areas with limited drainage such that water saturation prevents decomposition, including swamps, bogs, and marshes.

55f88c2f242a.title: Soil carbon
55f88c2f242a.section: Forms of Carbon in Soil > Organic carbon
55f88c2f242a.sentence: Fire derived forms of carbon are present in most soils as unweathered charcoal and weathered black carbon.

254f6b5e647c.title: Soil carbon
254f6b5e647c.section: Forms of Carbon in Soil > Organic carbon
254f6b5e647c.sentence: Soil organic carbon is typically 5–50% derived from char, with levels above 50% encountered in mollisol, chernozem, and terra preta soils.

afbfb22ce8d4.title: Soil carbon
afbfb22ce8d4.section: Soil carbon and climate change > Managing soil carbon
afbfb22ce8d4.sentence: It has long been encouraged that farmers adjust practices to maintain or increase the organic component in the soil.

4fbe4578b2c2.title: Soil carbon
4fbe4578b2c2.section: Soil carbon and climate change > Managing soil carbon
4fbe4578b2c2.sentence: On one hand, practices that hasten oxidation of carbon (such as burning crop stubbles or over-cultivation) are discouraged; on the other hand, incorporation of organic material (such as in manuring) has been encouraged.

7ad5a4492993.title: Soil carbon
7ad5a4492993.section: Soil carbon and climate change > Managing soil carbon
7ad5a4492993.sentence: The exchange of carbon between soils and the atmosphere is a significant part of the global carbon cycle.

92fa3b1a3806.title: Soil carbon
92fa3b1a3806.section: Soil carbon and climate change > Managing soil carbon
92fa3b1a3806.sentence: Several factors affect the variation that exists in soil organic matter and soil carbon; the most significant has, in contemporary times, been the influence of humans and agricultural systems.

bcc896618359.title: Soil carbon
bcc896618359.section: Soil carbon and climate change > Managing soil carbon
bcc896618359.sentence: Although exact quantities are difficult to measure, human activities have caused substantial losses of soil organic carbon through land use changes, such as deforestation and other agricultural practices.

4afe9a31df82.title: Soil carbon
4afe9a31df82.section: Soil carbon and climate change > Managing soil carbon
4afe9a31df82.sentence: Also, fire removes soil cover and leads to immediate and continuing losses of soil organic carbon.

128aa0ef28be.title: Soil carbon
128aa0ef28be.section: Soil carbon and climate change > Managing soil carbon
128aa0ef28be.sentence: Additionally, tillage and drainage both expose soil organic matter to oxygen and oxidation.

0bb975e9467f.title: Soil carbon
0bb975e9467f.section: Soil carbon and climate change > Managing soil carbon
0bb975e9467f.sentence: In the Netherlands, East Anglia, Florida, and the California Delta, subsidence of peat lands from oxidation has been severe as a result of tillage and drainage.

b6dd6500aaea.title: Soil carbon
b6dd6500aaea.section: Soil carbon and climate change > Managing soil carbon
b6dd6500aaea.sentence: Grazing management that exposes soil (through either excessive or insufficient recovery periods) can also cause losses of soil organic carbon.

159d18ad68bb.title: Soil carbon
159d18ad68bb.section: Soil carbon and climate change > Managing soil carbon
159d18ad68bb.sentence: Increasing soil carbon is not a straightforward matter; it is made complex by the relative activity of soil biota, which can consume and release carbon and are made more active by the addition of nitrogen fertilizers.

9e0e9fb0da35.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/01%3A_Digging_In/1.03%3A_Soil_Organic_Matter
9e0e9fb0da35.section: HOW CAN WE MANAGE SOIL ORGANIC MATTER? > Land Management
9e0e9fb0da35.sentence: Because of past losses of carbon from agricultural soils, these have significant capacity to store more carbon.

fb954cd1c233.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/01%3A_Digging_In/1.03%3A_Soil_Organic_Matter
fb954cd1c233.section: HOW CAN WE MANAGE SOIL ORGANIC MATTER? > Land Management
fb954cd1c233.sentence: Specifically, some can decrease soil carbon losses including: reduction in tillage intensity and reduction in summer fallow.

b152b1dc0cb6.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/01%3A_Digging_In/1.03%3A_Soil_Organic_Matter
b152b1dc0cb6.section: HOW CAN WE MANAGE SOIL ORGANIC MATTER? > Land Management
b152b1dc0cb6.sentence: Some measures contribute by increasing carbon inputs to soils, either by adding carbon from other sources (e.g. manure, biochar), or by promoting greater plant inputs to soils (e.g., by growing cover crops, improving residue retention, increasing use of perennials, and optimizing fertilization).

94a358e0c15a.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
94a358e0c15a.sentence: The permafrost carbon cycle or Arctic carbon cycle is a sub-cycle of the larger global carbon cycle.

95963f4fc29e.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
95963f4fc29e.sentence: The permafrost carbon cycle deals with the transfer of carbon from permafrost soils to terrestrial vegetation and microbes, to the atmosphere, back to vegetation, and, finally, back to permafrost soils through burial and sedimentation due to cryogenic processes.

20f2bbf16d8b.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
20f2bbf16d8b.sentence: Some of this carbon is transferred to the ocean and other portions of the globe through the global carbon cycle.

5cf340fe3d9a.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
5cf340fe3d9a.sentence: The cycle includes the exchange of carbon dioxide and methane between terrestrial components and the atmosphere, as well as the transfer of carbon between land and water as methane, dissolved organic carbon, dissolved inorganic carbon, particulate inorganic carbon, and particulate organic carbon.

14422e6aaee7.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
14422e6aaee7.sentence: Permafrost affected soils cover nearly 9% of the Earth's land area, yet store between 25 and 50% of the soil organic carbon.

bd6e76eab63f.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
bd6e76eab63f.sentence: Because permafrost responds to climate changes slowly, carbon storage removes carbon from the atmosphere for long periods of time.

a8f1d9bbdaae.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
a8f1d9bbdaae.sentence: Radiocarbon dating techniques reveal that carbon within permafrost is often thousands of years old.

624915ce6935.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
624915ce6935.sentence: Permafrost represents a large carbon reservoir, one which was often neglected in the initial research determining global terrestrial carbon reservoirs.

fb011ba57fcd.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
fb011ba57fcd.sentence: Until recently, the amount of carbon present in permafrost was not taken into account in climate models and global carbon budgets.

00a12d4129cd.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
00a12d4129cd.sentence: Since the start of the 2000s, however, far more attention has been paid to the subject, with an enormous growth both in general attention and in the scientific research output.

ac55a55a24ed.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
ac55a55a24ed.sentence: Microbial respiration is the primary process through which old permafrost carbon is re-activated and enters the atmosphere.

a3f946ba7784.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
a3f946ba7784.sentence: The rate of microbial decomposition within organic soils, including thawed permafrost, depends on environmental controls, such as soil temperature, moisture availability, nutrient availability, and oxygen availability.

92ec8b4d9b03.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
92ec8b4d9b03.sentence: In particular, sufficient concentrations of iron oxides in some permafrost soils can inhibit microbial respiration and prevent carbon mobilization: however, this protection only lasts until carbon is separated from the iron oxides by Fe-reducing bacteria, which is only a matter of time under the typical conditions.

11a4b0e0e5d7.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
11a4b0e0e5d7.sentence: Moreover, other elements such as iron and aluminum can adsorb some of the mobilized soil carbon before it reaches the atmosphere, and they are particularly prominent in the mineral sand layers which often overlay permafrost.

00cfd63880db.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
00cfd63880db.sentence: Altogether, the likelihood of the entire carbon pool mobilizing and entering the atmosphere is low despite the large volumes stored in the soil.

b56e73c5c024.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
b56e73c5c024.sentence: Much of the ground underlain by permafrost will remain frozen even if warming temperatures increase the thaw depth or increase thermokarsting and permafrost degradation.

614373e19b45.title: Pingo
614373e19b45.sentence: Pingos are intrapermafrost ice-cored hills, 3–70 m (10–230 ft) high and 30–1,000 m (98–3,281 ft) in diameter.

494bb141ce47.title: Pingo
494bb141ce47.sentence: They are typically conical in shape and grow and persist only in permafrost environments, such as the Arctic and subarctic.

f9fe2fb7a368.title: Pingo
f9fe2fb7a368.sentence: A pingo is a periglacial landform, which is defined as a non-glacial landform or process linked to colder climates.

3304fc2a9139.title: Pingo
3304fc2a9139.sentence: It is estimated that there are more than 11,000 pingos on Earth, with the Tuktoyaktuk peninsula area having the greatest concentration at a total of 1,350.

9bca0dc9c684.title: Pingo
9bca0dc9c684.sentence: Closed systems, also known as hydrostatic pingos, are formed as a result of hydrostatic pressure that has built up within the core of pingos due to water.

21e11b08b134.title: Pingo
21e11b08b134.sentence: This type of closed system pingos is formed in an area where a lake has been infilled with sediment.

4252eae4719d.title: Pingo
4252eae4719d.sentence: Hydraulic (open-system) pingos result from groundwater flowing from an outside source, i.e. sub-permafrost or intra-permafrost aquifers.

a1006abdf5ef.title: Pingo
a1006abdf5ef.sentence: These are often formed in a thin, discontinuous permafrost.

d91d43519e94.title: Pingo
d91d43519e94.sentence: Pingos usually grow only a couple of centimetres per year, with Ibyuk Pingo growing at a rate of 2 cm (0.79 in) a year, and the largest take decades or even centuries to form.

23fcdbd5e4c0.title: Pingo
23fcdbd5e4c0.sentence: Pingos can collapse due to the melting of the supporting ice and give rise to a depression in the landscape showing an inverse shape (horizontal mirror).

79520ba41459.title: Pingo
79520ba41459.sentence: Evidence of collapsed pingos in an area suggests that there was once permafrost.

6e46af3a9ed2.title: Pingo
6e46af3a9ed2.sentence: In 1825, John Franklin made the earliest description of a pingo when he climbed a small pingo on Ellice Island in the Mackenzie Delta.

fc208552a82c.title: Pingo
fc208552a82c.sentence: However, it was in 1938 that the term pingo was first borrowed from the Inuvialuit by the Arctic botanist Alf Erling Porsild in his paper on Earth mounds of the western Arctic coast of Canada and Alaska.

772dfd8de5ca.title: Pingo
772dfd8de5ca.sentence: The term pingo, which in Inuvialuktun means conical hill, has now been accepted as a scientific term in English-language literature.

1fd629fff70f.title: Active layer
1fd629fff70f.sentence: In environments containing permafrost, the active layer is the top layer of soil that thaws during the summer and freezes again during the autumn.

1767f6b55d4a.title: Active layer
1767f6b55d4a.sentence: In all climates, whether they contain permafrost or not, the temperature in the lower levels of the soil will remain more stable than that at the surface, where the influence of the ambient temperature is greatest.

bca14964356d.title: Active layer
bca14964356d.sentence: This means that, over many years, the influence of cooling in winter and heating in summer (in temperate climates) will decrease as depth increases.

be7dfd025a81.title: Active layer
be7dfd025a81.sentence: If the winter temperature is below the freezing point of water, a frost front will form in the soil.

3876e5644b02.title: Active layer
3876e5644b02.sentence: This "frost front" is the boundary between frozen and unfrozen soil, and with the coming of spring and summer, the soil is thawed, always from the top down.

42e68ff77af1.title: Active layer
42e68ff77af1.sentence: When there is not sufficient heat to thaw the frozen soil completely, permafrost forms.

6d9f3ac4476d.title: Active layer
6d9f3ac4476d.sentence: The active layer in this environment consists of the top layers of soil which thaws during the summer, while the inactive layer refers to the soil below which is frozen year-round because the heat fails to penetrate.

2c948e62d451.title: Permafrost
2c948e62d451.sentence: The border between active layer and permafrost itself is sometimes called permafrost table.

6849a9624f9f.title: Active layer
6849a9624f9f.sentence: Liquid water cannot flow below the active layer, with the result that permafrost environments tend to be very poorly drained and boggy.

fbeacbae83fd.title: Permafrost
fbeacbae83fd.sentence: Active layer thickness is measured during its maximum extent at the end of summer: as of 2018, the average thickness in the Northern Hemisphere is ~145 centimetres (4.76 ft), but there are significant regional differences.

c71ecefb3c81.title: Permafrost
c71ecefb3c81.sentence: Northeastern Siberia, Alaska and Greenland have the most solid permafrost with the lowest extent of active layer (less than 50 centimetres (1.6 ft) on average, and sometimes only 30 centimetres (0.98 ft)), while southern Norway and the Mongolian Plateau are the only areas where the average active layer is deeper than 600 centimetres (20 ft), with the record of 10 metres (33 ft).

2d08a4f85bd9.title: Carbon sink
2d08a4f85bd9.sentence: Soils represent a short to long-term carbon storage medium and contain more carbon than all terrestrial vegetation and the atmosphere combined.

6b42e3b676b5.title: Carbon sink
6b42e3b676b5.sentence: Plant litter and other biomass including charcoal accumulates as organic matter in soils, and is degraded by chemical weathering and biological degradation.

537004d252f4.title: Carbon sink
537004d252f4.sentence: More recalcitrant organic carbon polymers such as cellulose, hemi-cellulose, lignin, aliphatic compounds, waxes and terpenoids are collectively retained as humus.
