77812d0acab5.title: Terrestrial biological carbon cycle
77812d0acab5.section: Movement of carbon in the terrestrial biosphere
77812d0acab5.sentence: Most carbon in the terrestrial biosphere is stored in forests: they hold 86% of the planet's terrestrial above-ground carbon and forest soils also hold 73% of the planet's soil carbon.

cbe91df51b43.title: Terrestrial biological carbon cycle
cbe91df51b43.section: Carbon exchange between the terrestrial biosphere and other systems > Atmosphere
cbe91df51b43.sentence: About half of the gross primary production is respired by plants directly back into the atmosphere.

4de070fbd6aa.title: Terrestrial biological carbon cycle
4de070fbd6aa.section: Carbon exchange between the terrestrial biosphere and other systems > Atmosphere
4de070fbd6aa.sentence: Part of the net primary production, or the remaining carbon absorbed by the biosphere, is emitted back into the atmosphere through fires and heterotrophic respiration.

2c8b7ffbeb85.title: Terrestrial biological carbon cycle
2c8b7ffbeb85.section: Carbon exchange between the terrestrial biosphere and other systems > Atmosphere
2c8b7ffbeb85.sentence: The rest is converted into soil organic carbon, which is released more slowly, or "inert" dissolved carbon, which can remain in the biosphere for an unknown period of time.

6410b60451f6.title: Carbon cycle
6410b60451f6.section: Human influence on fast carbon cycle > Land use changes
6410b60451f6.sentence: More directly, it often leads to the release of carbon from terrestrial ecosystems into the atmosphere.

340465d01d82.title: Carbon cycle
340465d01d82.section: Human influence on fast carbon cycle > Land use changes
340465d01d82.sentence: Deforestation for agricultural purposes removes forests, which hold large amounts of carbon, and replaces them, generally with agricultural or urban areas.

0bba347804c3.title: Carbon cycle
0bba347804c3.section: Human influence on fast carbon cycle > Land use changes
0bba347804c3.sentence: Since the invention of agriculture, humans have directly and gradually influenced the carbon cycle over century-long timescales by modifying the mixture of vegetation in the terrestrial biosphere.

4285639813a6.title: Carbon cycle
4285639813a6.section: Human influence on fast carbon cycle > Land use changes
4285639813a6.sentence: Both of these replacement land cover types store comparatively small amounts of carbon so that the net result of the transition is that more carbon stays in the atmosphere.

0607fa71050c.title: Carbon cycle
0607fa71050c.section: Human influence on fast carbon cycle > Land use changes
0607fa71050c.sentence: Over the past several centuries, direct and indirect human-caused land use and land cover change (LUCC) has led to the loss of biodiversity, which lowers ecosystems' resilience to environmental stresses and decreases their ability to remove carbon from the atmosphere.

5d84ab46c26a.title: Carbon cycle
5d84ab46c26a.section: Human influence on fast carbon cycle > Land use changes
5d84ab46c26a.sentence: However, the effects on the atmosphere and overall carbon cycle can be intentionally and/or naturally reversed with reforestation.

242e5d6fff2d.title: Permafrost
242e5d6fff2d.sentence: A range of elevations in both the Northern and Southern Hemisphere are cold enough to support perennially frozen ground: some of the best-known examples include the Canadian Rockies, the European Alps, Himalaya and the Tien Shan.

9d3277414099.title: Permafrost
9d3277414099.sentence: In general, it has been found that extensive alpine permafrost requires mean annual air temperature of −3 °C (27 °F), though this can vary depending on local topography, and some mountain areas are known to support permafrost at −1 °C (30 °F).

fe6232b413d9.title: Permafrost
fe6232b413d9.sentence: Alpine permafrost is particularly difficult to study, and systematic research efforts did not begin until the 1970s.

6aad87b89732.title: Permafrost
6aad87b89732.sentence: As recently as 2009, permafrost had been discovered in a new area – Africa's highest peak, Mount Kilimanjaro (4,700 m (15,400 ft) above sea level and approximately 3° south of the equator).

31d36276e28f.title: Permafrost
31d36276e28f.sentence: In 2014, a collection of regional estimates of alpine permafrost extent had established a global extent of 3,560,000 km2 (1,370,000 mi2).

1a64a13c5462.title: Permafrost
1a64a13c5462.section: Classification and extent > Continuity of coverage > Continuous permafrost

ba509b9b24e5.title: Permafrost
ba509b9b24e5.sentence: It is also possible for subsurface alpine permafrost to be covered by warmer, vegetation-supporting soil.

2ce8f5c70151.title: Permafrost
2ce8f5c70151.sentence: Building on permafrost is difficult because the heat of the building (or pipeline) can spread to the soil, thawing it.

53c5ef523dc6.title: Permafrost
53c5ef523dc6.sentence: A common solution is placing foundations on wood piles, a technique pioneered by Soviet engineer Mikhail Kim in Norilsk.

ddca48242504.title: Permafrost
ddca48242504.sentence: As ice content turns to water, the ground's ability to provide structural support is weakened, until the building is destabilized.

d8fa284a7263.title: Permafrost
d8fa284a7263.sentence: There are only two large cities in the world built in areas of continuous permafrost (where the frozen soil forms an unbroken, below-zero sheet) and both are in Russia – Norilsk in Krasnoyarsk Krai and Yakutsk in the Sakha Republic.

ef78777b74a9.title: Permafrost
ef78777b74a9.sentence: The Melnikov Permafrost Institute in Yakutsk found that pile foundations should extend down to 15 metres (49 ft) to avoid the risk of buildings sinking.

23625e0789d3.title: Permafrost
23625e0789d3.sentence: At this depth the temperature does not change with the seasons, remaining at about −5 °C (23 °F).

62cbb781f33d.title: Permafrost
62cbb781f33d.sentence: Two other approaches are building on an extensive gravel pad (usually 1–2 m (3 ft 3 in – 6 ft 7 in) thick); or using anhydrous ammonia heat pipes.

a57680780130.title: Permafrost
a57680780130.sentence: The Trans-Alaska Pipeline System uses heat pipes built into vertical supports to prevent the pipeline from sinking and the Qingzang railway in Tibet employs a variety of methods to keep the ground cool, both in areas with frost-susceptible soil.

806bf9aab479.title: Permafrost
806bf9aab479.sentence: Between the middle of the 19th century and the middle of the 20th century, most of the literature on basic permafrost science and the engineering aspects of permafrost was written in Russian.

b03c2e4dea6d.title: Permafrost
b03c2e4dea6d.sentence: This marked the beginning of modern scientific collaboration on the subject.

991d59dbef84.title: Permafrost
991d59dbef84.sentence: One of the earliest written reports describing the existence of permafrost dates to 1684, when well excavation efforts in Yakutsk were stumped by its presence.

3b5716ff4676.title: Permafrost
3b5716ff4676.sentence: Baer began publishing works on permafrost in 1838 and is often considered the "founder of scientific permafrost research." Baer laid the foundation for modern permafrost terminology by compiling and analyzing all available data on ground ice and permafrost.

147b83e2ee6e.title: Permafrost
147b83e2ee6e.sentence: Baer is also known to have composed the world's first permafrost textbook in 1843, Materialien zur Kenntniss des unvergänglichen Boden-Eises in Sibirien (Materials for the study of the perennial ground-ice in Siberia), written in his native German.

8f8e710f6da9.title: Permafrost
8f8e710f6da9.sentence: Beginning in 1942, Siemon William Muller delved into the relevant Russian literature held by the Library of Congress and the U.S. Geological Survey Library so that he was able to furnish the government an engineering field guide and a technical report about permafrost by 1943.

7505a763a529.title: Permafrost
7505a763a529.sentence: That report coined the English term as a contraction of permanently frozen ground, in what was considered a direct translation of the Russian term vechnaia merzlota (Russian: вечная мерзлота).

7ea2caa300a2.title: Permafrost
7ea2caa300a2.sentence: Between 11 and 15 November 1963, the First International Conference on Permafrost took place on the grounds of Purdue University in the American town of West Lafayette, Indiana.

33ec06b1099a.title: Permafrost
33ec06b1099a.sentence: During the Fourth conference in 1983, a special meeting between the "Big Four" participant countries (US, USSR, China, and Canada) officially created the International Permafrost Association.

f11779a150b3.title: Permafrost
f11779a150b3.sentence: When the ice content of a permafrost exceeds 250 percent (ice to dry soil by mass) it is classified as massive ice.

25c0e1630a82.title: Permafrost
25c0e1630a82.sentence: Massive icy beds have a minimum thickness of at least 2 m and a short diameter of at least 10 m.

c1ee26390738.title: Permafrost
c1ee26390738.sentence: Massive ice bodies can range in composition, in every conceivable gradation from icy mud to pure ice.

dd1db61b3f1a.title: Permafrost
dd1db61b3f1a.sentence: While there are four categories of ice in permafrost – pore ice, ice wedges (also known as vein ice), buried surface ice and intrasedimental (sometimes also called constitutional) ice – only the last two tend to be large enough to qualify as massive ground ice.

4667d8fe9acf.title: Permafrost
4667d8fe9acf.sentence: The latter is the dominant type, formed after crystallizational differentiation in wet sediments, which occurs when water migrates to the freezing front under the influence of van der Waals forces.

dab28ce18b59.title: Permafrost
dab28ce18b59.sentence: This is a slow process, which primarily occurs in silts with salinity less than 20% of seawater: silt sediments with higher salinity and clay sediments instead have water movement prior to ice formation dominated by rheological processes.

b2378200f861.title: Permafrost
b2378200f861.sentence: Consequently, it takes between 1 and 1000 years to form intrasedimental ice in the top 2.5 meters of clay sediments, yet it takes between 10 and 10,000 years for peat sediments and between 1,000 and 1,000,000 years for silt sediments.

d962b6c23fe2.title: Yedoma
d962b6c23fe2.sentence: Yedoma /ˈjɛdəmə/ (Russian: е́дома) is an organic-rich (about 2% carbon by mass) Pleistocene-age permafrost with ice content of 50–90% by volume.

664be1324b0f.title: Yedoma
664be1324b0f.sentence: The Yedoma region currently occupies an area of more than one million square kilometers from northeast Siberia to Alaska and Canada, and in many regions is tens of meters thick.

854f48353142.title: Yedoma
854f48353142.sentence: Yedoma are abundant in the cold regions of eastern Siberia, such as northern Yakutia, as well as in Alaska and the Yukon.

ba153350f7d6.title: Yedoma
ba153350f7d6.sentence: Yedoma usually form in lowlands or stretches of land with rolling hills where ice wedge polygonal networks are present, in stable relief features with accumulation zones of poor drainage, severe cold and arid continental climate zones resulting in scanty vegetation cover, intense periglacial weathering processes, as well as the proximity of sediment sources, such as low mountain ranges and foothills.

852a0cbcbfc9.title: Yedoma
852a0cbcbfc9.sentence: The amount of carbon trapped in this type of permafrost is much more prevalent than originally thought and may be about 210 to 500 Gt, that is a multiple of the amount of carbon released into the air each year by the burning of fossil fuels.

d8911fa80da9.title: Yedoma
d8911fa80da9.sentence: Thawing yedoma is a significant source of atmospheric methane (about 4 Tg of CH 4 per year).

0326e171e43e.title: Yedoma
0326e171e43e.sentence: At the end of the last ice age, at the Pleistocene–Holocene transition, thawing yedoma and the resulting thermokarst lakes may have produced 33 to 87% of the high-latitude increase in atmospheric methane concentration.

cc1b30ded98e.title: Permafrost
cc1b30ded98e.section: Classification and extent > Past extent of permafrost
cc1b30ded98e.sentence: At the Last Glacial Maximum, continuous permafrost covered a much greater area than it does today, covering all of ice-free Europe south to about Szeged (southeastern Hungary) and the Sea of Azov (then dry land) and East Asia south to present-day Changchun and Abashiri.

b043b163c7e6.title: Permafrost
b043b163c7e6.section: Classification and extent > Past extent of permafrost
b043b163c7e6.sentence: In North America, only an extremely narrow belt of permafrost existed south of the ice sheet at about the latitude of New Jersey through southern Iowa and northern Missouri, but permafrost was more extensive in the drier western regions where it extended to the southern border of Idaho and Oregon.

a04c8ae6dc39.title: Permafrost
a04c8ae6dc39.section: Classification and extent > Past extent of permafrost
a04c8ae6dc39.sentence: In the Southern Hemisphere, there is some evidence for former permafrost from this period in central Otago and Argentine Patagonia, but was probably discontinuous, and is related to the tundra.

68e933c7d949.title: Permafrost
68e933c7d949.sentence: Permafrost extends to a base depth where geothermal heat from the Earth and the mean annual temperature at the surface achieve an equilibrium temperature of 0 °C (32 °F).

df47f1359071.title: Permafrost
df47f1359071.sentence: This base depth of permafrost can vary wildly – it is less than a meter (3 ft) in the areas where it is shallowest, yet reaches 1,493 m (4,898 ft) in the northern Lena and Yana River basins in Siberia.

7acf4feb2c9e.title: Permafrost
7acf4feb2c9e.sentence: Calculations indicate that the formation time of permafrost greatly slows past the first several metres.

87f3ca086dd6.title: Permafrost
87f3ca086dd6.sentence: For instance, over half a million years was required to form the deep permafrost underlying Prudhoe Bay, Alaska, a time period extending over several glacial and interglacial cycles of the Pleistocene.

e509c23cd8f4.title: Permafrost
e509c23cd8f4.sentence: Base depth is affected by the underlying geology, and particularly by thermal conductivity, which is lower for permafrost in soil than in bedrock.

575171b9fd1b.title: Permafrost
575171b9fd1b.sentence: Lower conductivity leaves permafrost less affected by the geothermal gradient, which is the rate of increasing temperature with respect to increasing depth in the Earth's interior.

e7cabbc28299.title: Permafrost
e7cabbc28299.sentence: Only plants with shallow roots can survive in the presence of permafrost.

fc81a27ebfac.title: Permafrost
fc81a27ebfac.sentence: While permafrost soil is frozen, it is not completely inhospitable to microorganisms, though their numbers can vary widely, typically from 1 to 1000 million per gram of soil.

169556397ef8.title: Permafrost
169556397ef8.sentence: Black spruce tolerates limited rooting zones, and dominates flora where permafrost is extensive.

cff3df8ff00d.title: Permafrost
cff3df8ff00d.sentence: Most of the bacteria and fungi found in permafrost cannot be cultured in the laboratory, but the identity of the microorganisms can be revealed by DNA-based techniques.

120a149d0822.title: Permafrost
120a149d0822.sentence: In the presently living species, scientists observed a variety of adaptations for sub-zero conditions, including reduced and anaerobic metabolic processes.

c2019a46f36d.title: Permafrost
c2019a46f36d.sentence: Permafrost processes such as thermal contraction generating cracks which eventually become ice wedges and solifluction – gradual movement of soil down the slope as it repeatedly freezes and thaws – often lead to the formation of ground polygons, rings, steps and other forms of patterned ground found in arctic, periglacial and alpine areas.

4dc4f0433a8b.title: Permafrost
4dc4f0433a8b.sentence: In ice-rich permafrost areas, melting of ground ice initiates thermokarst landforms such as thermokarst lakes, thaw slumps, thermal-erosion gullies, and active layer detachments.

3468db420558.title: Permafrost
3468db420558.sentence: Notably, unusually deep permafrost in Arctic moorlands and bogs often attracts meltwater in warmer seasons, which pools and freezes to form ice lenses, and the surrounding ground begins to jut outward at a slope.

eef06ab15988.title: Permafrost
eef06ab15988.sentence: This can eventually result in the formation of large-scale land forms around this core of permafrost, such as palsas – long (15–150 m (49–492 ft)), wide (10–30 m (33–98 ft)) yet shallow (<1–6 m (3 ft 3 in – 19 ft 8 in) tall) peat mounds – and the even larger pingos, which can be 3–70 m (10–230 ft) high and 30–1,000 m (98–3,281 ft) in diameter.

9ac72b5f3436.title: Permafrost
9ac72b5f3436.section: Impacts of climate change > Thaw-induced ground instability > Infrastructure
9ac72b5f3436.sentence: Consequently, a wide range of infrastructure in permafrost areas is threatened by the thaw.

3914676c195a.title: Permafrost
3914676c195a.section: Impacts of climate change > Thaw-induced ground instability > Infrastructure
3914676c195a.sentence: As of 2021, there are 1162 settlements located directly atop the Arctic permafrost, which host an estimated 5 million people.

b0406210c844.title: Permafrost
b0406210c844.section: Impacts of climate change > Thaw-induced ground instability > Infrastructure
b0406210c844.sentence: By 2050, permafrost layer below 42% of these settlements is expected to thaw, affecting all their inhabitants (currently 3.3 million people).

cb5af38fbc49.title: Permafrost
cb5af38fbc49.section: Impacts of climate change > Thaw-induced ground instability > Infrastructure
cb5af38fbc49.sentence: By 2050, it's estimated that nearly 70% of global infrastructure located in the permafrost areas would be at high risk of permafrost thaw, including 30–50% of "critical" infrastructure.

f861b0b43e2a.title: Permafrost
f861b0b43e2a.section: Impacts of climate change > Thaw-induced ground instability > Infrastructure
f861b0b43e2a.sentence: The associated costs could reach tens of billions of dollars by the second half of the century.

c3c557fb8290.title: Permafrost
c3c557fb8290.section: Impacts of climate change > Thaw-induced ground instability > Infrastructure
c3c557fb8290.sentence: In Alaska alone, damages to infrastructure by the end of the century would amount to $4.6 billion (at 2015 dollar value) if RCP8.5, the high-emission climate change scenario, were realized.

70335ce1f33d.title: Permafrost
70335ce1f33d.section: Impacts of climate change > Thaw-induced ground instability > Infrastructure
70335ce1f33d.sentence: It is warming at twice the global average rate, and 40% of it is already considered "warm" permafrost, making it particularly unstable.

a107f2a1f51a.title: Permafrost
a107f2a1f51a.section: Impacts of climate change > Thaw-induced ground instability > Infrastructure
a107f2a1f51a.sentence: There are also 9,389 km of roads, and around 30% are already sustaining damage from permafrost thaw.

94c5a9b94dc9.title: Permafrost
94c5a9b94dc9.sentence: Furthermore, between 13,000 and 20,000 sites contaminated with toxic waste are present in the permafrost, as well as natural mercury deposits, which are all liable to leak and pollute the environment as the warming progresses.

bc4deca8ee68.title: Permafrost
bc4deca8ee68.section: Impacts of climate change > Release of toxic pollutants
bc4deca8ee68.sentence: For much of the 20th century, it was believed that permafrost would "indefinitely" preserve anything buried there, and this made deep permafrost areas popular locations for hazardous waste disposal.

3838d700bad8.title: Permafrost
3838d700bad8.section: Impacts of climate change > Release of toxic pollutants
3838d700bad8.sentence: This means that as of 2023, there are ~4500 industrial facilities in the Arctic permafrost areas which either actively process or store hazardous chemicals.

879df1f2e820.title: Permafrost
879df1f2e820.section: Impacts of climate change > Release of toxic pollutants
879df1f2e820.sentence: Additionally, there are between 13,000 and 20,000 sites which have been heavily contaminated, 70% of them in Russia, and their pollution is currently trapped in the permafrost.

ec630392681e.title: Permafrost
ec630392681e.section: Impacts of climate change > Release of toxic pollutants
ec630392681e.sentence: An estimated 800,000 tons of mercury are frozen in the permafrost soil.

4ef8988ed608.title: Permafrost
4ef8988ed608.section: Impacts of climate change > Release of toxic pollutants
4ef8988ed608.sentence: According to observations, around 70% of it is simply taken up by vegetation after the thaw.

6e173d77fe73.title: Permafrost
6e173d77fe73.section: Impacts of climate change > Release of toxic pollutants
6e173d77fe73.sentence: Under RCP8.5, enough mercury will enter the Yukon River basin by 2050 to make its fish unsafe to eat under the EPA guidelines.

496d37c3e350.title: Permafrost
496d37c3e350.section: Impacts of climate change > Revival of ancient organisms > Microorganisms
496d37c3e350.sentence: This has motivated concerns that permafrost thaw could free previously unknown microorganisms, which may be capable of infecting either humans or important livestock and crops, potentially resulting in damaging epidemics or pandemics.

5bd04e029f98.title: Permafrost
5bd04e029f98.section: Impacts of climate change > Revival of ancient organisms > Plants
5bd04e029f98.sentence: The study demonstrated that living tissue can survive ice preservation for tens of thousands of years.

f83e8cfa6bb6.title: Permafrost
f83e8cfa6bb6.section: Impacts of climate change > Revival of ancient organisms > Microorganisms
f83e8cfa6bb6.sentence: Bacteria are known for being able to remain dormant to survive adverse conditions, and viruses are not metabolically active outside of host cells in the first place.

4057fc7a7555.title: Permafrost
4057fc7a7555.section: Impacts of climate change > Revival of ancient organisms > Microorganisms
4057fc7a7555.sentence: At the same time, notable pathogens like influenza and smallpox appear unable to survive being thawed, and other scientists argue that the risk of ancient microorganisms being both able to survive the thaw and to threaten humans is not scientifically plausible.

c82a5b3867c3.title: Permafrost
c82a5b3867c3.sentence: However, this is considered unlikely, and a scientific review on the subject describes the risks as "generally low".

b6cb9b9615df.title: Permafrost
b6cb9b9615df.section: Impacts of climate change > Revival of ancient organisms > Plants
b6cb9b9615df.sentence: In 2012, Russian researchers proved that permafrost could serve as a natural repository for ancient life forms by reviving a sample of Silene stenophylla from 30,000-year-old tissue found in an Ice Age squirrel burrow in the Siberian permafrost.

fb958aa805e4.title: Permafrost
fb958aa805e4.section: Impacts of climate change > Revival of ancient organisms > Plants
fb958aa805e4.sentence: This is the oldest plant tissue ever revived.

07d9955526e0.title: Permafrost
07d9955526e0.sentence: Subsea permafrost occurs beneath the seabed and exists in the continental shelves of the polar regions.

c71e1c36ba5c.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
c71e1c36ba5c.section: Carbon release from the permafrost > Subsea permafrost
c71e1c36ba5c.sentence: Thus, it can be defined as "the unglaciated continental shelf areas exposed during the Last Glacial Maximum (LGM, ~26 500 BP) that are currently inundated".

68ee9fbb826e.title: Permafrost
68ee9fbb826e.sentence: These areas formed during the last Ice Age, when a larger portion of Earth's water was bound up in ice sheets on land and when sea levels were low.

7af38640e685.title: Permafrost
7af38640e685.sentence: As the ice sheets melted to again become seawater during the Holocene glacial retreat, coastal permafrost became submerged shelves under relatively warm and salty boundary conditions, compared to surface permafrost.

98b6468fb8bb.title: Permafrost
98b6468fb8bb.sentence: Since then, these conditions led to the gradual and ongoing decline of subsea permafrost extent.

66d5b09d2f3d.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
66d5b09d2f3d.section: Carbon release from the permafrost > Subsea permafrost
66d5b09d2f3d.sentence: The size of today's subsea permafrost has been estimated at 2 million km2 (~1/5 of the terrestrial permafrost domain size), which constitutes a 30–50% reduction since the LGM.

284b845f78f8.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
284b845f78f8.section: Carbon release from the permafrost > Subsea permafrost
284b845f78f8.sentence: Containing around 560 GtC in OM and 45 GtC in CH4, with a current release of 18 and 38 MtC per year respectively, which is due to the warming and thawing that the subsea permafrost domain has been experiencing since after the LGM (~14000 years ago).

422f07a95f6e.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
422f07a95f6e.section: Carbon release from the permafrost > Subsea permafrost
422f07a95f6e.sentence: In fact, because the subsea permafrost systems responds at millennial timescales to climate warming, the current carbon fluxes it is emitting to the water are in response to climatic changes occurring after the LGM.

cfa0975e3d9b.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
cfa0975e3d9b.section: Carbon release from the permafrost > Subsea permafrost
cfa0975e3d9b.sentence: According to predictions under a business-as-usual emissions scenario RCP 8.5, by 2100, 43 GtC could be released from the subsea permafrost domain, and 190 GtC by the year 2300.

1c9eac55cbe8.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
1c9eac55cbe8.section: Carbon release from the permafrost > Subsea permafrost
1c9eac55cbe8.sentence: Therefore, human-driven climate change effects on subsea permafrost will only be seen hundreds or thousands of years from today.

f6c3e407b1b0.title: Permafrost
f6c3e407b1b0.section: Impacts of climate change > Thaw-induced ground instability
f6c3e407b1b0.sentence: As the water drains or evaporates, soil structure weakens and sometimes becomes viscous until it regains strength with decreasing moisture content.

e2c13d91ad37.title: Permafrost
e2c13d91ad37.section: Impacts of climate change > Thaw-induced ground instability
e2c13d91ad37.sentence: As climate warms, permafrost thaws, decreasing slope stability and increasing stress through buildup of pore-water pressure, which may ultimately lead to slope failure and rockfalls.

b4150ec82ed0.title: Permafrost
b4150ec82ed0.section: Impacts of climate change > Thaw-induced ground instability
b4150ec82ed0.sentence: One visible sign of permafrost degradation is the random displacement of trees from their vertical orientation in permafrost areas.

f54560bfb882.title: Permafrost
f54560bfb882.section: Impacts of climate change > Thaw-induced ground instability
f54560bfb882.sentence: Global warming has been increasing permafrost slope disturbances and sediment supplies to fluvial systems, resulting in exceptional increases in river sediment.

1d6ce064d9eb.title: Permafrost
1d6ce064d9eb.section: Impacts of climate change > Thaw-induced ground instability
1d6ce064d9eb.sentence: On the other hands, disturbance of formerly hard soil increases drainage of water reservoirs in northern wetlands.

66a9b9b25c3f.title: Permafrost
66a9b9b25c3f.section: Impacts of climate change > Thaw-induced ground instability
66a9b9b25c3f.sentence: This can dry them out and compromise the survival of plants and animals used to the wetland ecosystem.

88a6b17f01c7.title: Permafrost
88a6b17f01c7.section: Impacts of climate change > Thaw-induced ground instability
88a6b17f01c7.sentence: The 1987 Val Pola landslide that killed 22 people in the Italian Alps is considered one such example.

89f3289a0987.title: Permafrost
89f3289a0987.section: Impacts of climate change > Thaw-induced ground instability
89f3289a0987.sentence: Permafrost thaw can also result in the formation of frozen debris lobes (FDLs), which are defined as "slow-moving landslides composed of soil, rocks, trees, and ice".

f7566283ff67.title: Permafrost
f7566283ff67.section: Impacts of climate change > Thaw-induced ground instability
f7566283ff67.sentence: As of December 2021, there were 43 frozen debris lobes identified in the southern Brooks Range, where they could potentially threaten both the Trans Alaska Pipeline System (TAPS) corridor and the Dalton Highway, which is the main transport link between the Interior Alaska and the Alaska North Slope.

09b0b78c34ae.title: Methanotroph
09b0b78c34ae.sentence: Methanotrophs (sometimes called methanophiles) are prokaryotes that metabolize methane as their source of carbon and chemical energy.

d1139cb8eb76.title: Methanotroph
d1139cb8eb76.sentence: They are bacteria or archaea, can grow aerobically or anaerobically, and require single-carbon compounds to survive.

456b9d47a8ce.title: Methanotroph
456b9d47a8ce.sentence: Their habitats include wetlands, soils, marshes, rice paddies, landfills, aquatic systems (lakes, oceans, streams) and more.

dbb1c1c17f98.title: Methanotroph
dbb1c1c17f98.sentence: Methanotrophs are especially common in or near environments where methane is produced, although some methanotrophs can oxidize atmospheric methane.

c1ff832f5322.title: Methanotroph
c1ff832f5322.sentence: They are of special interest to researchers studying global warming, as they play a significant role in the global methane budget, by reducing the amount of methane emitted to the atmosphere.

b8ab33df042d.title: Methanotroph
b8ab33df042d.sentence: Under aerobic conditions, methanotrophs combine oxygen and methane to form formaldehyde, which is then incorporated into organic compounds via the serine pathway or the ribulose monophosphate (RuMP) pathway, and carbon dioxide, which is released.

d8febbdbabf8.title: Methanotroph
d8febbdbabf8.sentence: Methanotrophs oxidize methane by first initiating reduction of molecular oxygen (O2) to hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) and transformation of methane to methanol (CH3OH) using methane monooxygenases (MMOs).

7ca051ce869b.title: Methanotroph
7ca051ce869b.sentence: Generally, Type I methanotrophs tend to dominate in cold, anaerobic environments, meaning there is limited oxygen availability, which often have high methane concentrations.

d10f8c6328e6.title: Methanotroph
d10f8c6328e6.sentence: Type II methanotrophs tend to be more tolerant of stress and dominate in methane limited environments and acidic pHs.

a7349dcdb0f2.title: Methanotroph
a7349dcdb0f2.sentence: This can happen in anoxic habitats such as marine or lake sediments, oxygen minimum zones, anoxic water columns, rice paddies and soils.

589bae0b6162.title: Methanotroph
589bae0b6162.sentence: Some specific methanotrophs can reduce nitrate, nitrite, iron, sulfate, or manganese ions and couple that to methane oxidation without syntrophic partner.

90ffeab1e54e.title: Mycorrhizal fungi and soil carbon storage
90ffeab1e54e.sentence: While much research has been done on how plants, free-living microbial decomposers, and soil minerals affect this pool of carbon, it is recently coming to light that mycorrhizal fungi—symbiotic fungi that associate with roots of almost all living plants—may play an important role in maintaining this pool as well.
90ffeab1e54e.key: Mycorrhizal fungi and soil carbon storage

215bbb347639.title: Mycorrhizal fungi and soil carbon storage
215bbb347639.sentence: Soil carbon storage is an important function of terrestrial ecosystems.
215bbb347639.key: Mycorrhizal fungi and soil carbon storage

8e0b23c32454.title: Mycorrhizal fungi and soil carbon storage
8e0b23c32454.sentence: Measurements of plant carbon allocation to mycorrhizal fungi have been estimated to be 5 to 20% of total plant carbon uptake, and in some ecosystems the biomass of mycorrhizal fungi can be comparable to the biomass of fine roots.
8e0b23c32454.key: Mycorrhizal fungi and soil carbon storage

fad0fc88fc0b.title: Mycorrhizal fungi and soil carbon storage
fad0fc88fc0b.sentence: Recent research has shown that mycorrhizal fungi hold 50 to 70 percent of the total carbon stored in leaf litter and soil on forested islands in Sweden.
fad0fc88fc0b.key: Mycorrhizal fungi and soil carbon storage

485110a31ae8.title: Mycorrhizal fungi and soil carbon storage
485110a31ae8.sentence: Turnover of mycorrhizal biomass into the soil carbon pool is thought to be rapid and has been shown in some ecosystems to be the dominant pathway by which living carbon enters the soil carbon pool.
485110a31ae8.key: Mycorrhizal fungi and soil carbon storage

9e472d5512b6.title: Mycorrhizal fungi and soil carbon storage
9e472d5512b6.sentence: Evidence is presented for arbuscular and ectomycorrhizal fungi separately as they are phylogenetically distinct and often function in very different ways.
9e472d5512b6.key: Mycorrhizal fungi and soil carbon storage

e96e38e7e85c.title: Mycorrhizal fungi and soil carbon storage
e96e38e7e85c.sentence: Evidence is equivocal on this point, as ectomycorrhizal colonization does increase fine root decomposition rates substantially compared to uncolonized roots in some ecosystems, while Pinus edulis roots colonized predominately by ectomycorrhizal fungi from the Ascomycota group have been found to decompose more slowly than uncolonized controls.
e96e38e7e85c.key: Mycorrhizal fungi and soil carbon storage

95e1956faa6c.title: Effects of climate change on agriculture
95e1956faa6c.sentence: Greenhouse gas emissions from agriculture are large: the agriculture, forestry and land use sectors contribute between 13% and 21% of global greenhouse gas emissions.

e94b45b40a39.sentence: Farm practices such as reducing tillage, decreasing empty land, returning biomass residue of crops to the soil, and increasing the use of cover crops can reduce carbon emissions.

357d58fbac86.title: Tipping points in the climate system
357d58fbac86.sentence: In climate science, a tipping point is a critical threshold that, when crossed, leads to large, accelerating and often irreversible changes in the climate system.
357d58fbac86.key: Tipping points in the climate system

12c25f402e55.title: Tipping points in the climate system
12c25f402e55.sentence: The IPCC Sixth Assessment Report defines a tipping point as a "critical threshold beyond which a system reorganizes, often abruptly and/or irreversibly".
12c25f402e55.key: Tipping points in the climate system

15ab82dabc0d.title: Tipping points in the climate system
15ab82dabc0d.sentence: It can be brought about by a small disturbance causing a disproportionately large change in the system.
15ab82dabc0d.key: Tipping points in the climate system

21b57be3e79f.title: Tipping points in the climate system
21b57be3e79f.sentence: It can also be associated with self-reinforcing feedbacks, which could lead to changes in the climate system irreversible on a human timescale.
21b57be3e79f.key: Tipping points in the climate system

624ad542b11e.title: Tipping points in the climate system
624ad542b11e.sentence: Examples of tipping points include thawing permafrost, which will release methane, a powerful greenhouse gas, or melting ice sheets and glaciers reducing Earth's albedo, which would warm the planet faster.
624ad542b11e.key: Tipping points in the climate system

370c56c324e9.title: Tipping points in the climate system
370c56c324e9.sentence: Crossing a threshold in one part of the climate system may trigger another tipping element to tip into a new state.
370c56c324e9.key: Tipping points in the climate system

38b348436f1e.title: Tipping points in the climate system
38b348436f1e.section: Other tipping points > Cascading tipping points
38b348436f1e.sentence: Such sequences of thresholds are called cascading tipping points, an example of a domino effect.
38b348436f1e.key: Tipping points in the climate system

bdcb57fa9af8.title: Tipping points in the climate system
bdcb57fa9af8.sentence: Three types of tipping points have been identified—bifurcation, noise-induced and rate-dependent.

86c646418eba.key: Tipping points in the climate system

bcc7db87a7fd.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
bcc7db87a7fd.sentence: As climate change increases mean annual air temperatures throughout the Arctic, it extends permafrost thaw and deepens the active layer, exposing old carbon that has been in storage for decades to millennia to biogenic processes which facilitate its entrance into the atmosphere.

b186b2e05542.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
b186b2e05542.sentence: The warming also intensifies Arctic water cycle, and the increased amounts of warmer rain are another factor which increases permafrost thaw depths.

30ae6ae1f1c4.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
30ae6ae1f1c4.sentence: The amount of carbon that will be released from warming conditions depends on depth of thaw, carbon content within the thawed soil, physical changes to the environment and microbial and vegetation activity in the soil.

fbd73ddaaad1.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
fbd73ddaaad1.sentence: On the other hand, once the permafrost area thaws, it will not go back to being permafrost for centuries even if the temperature increase reversed, making it one of the best-known examples of tipping points in the climate system.

b2eef82d1b86.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
b2eef82d1b86.sentence: A 1993 study suggested that while the tundra was a carbon sink until the end of the 1970s, it had already transitioned to a net carbon source by the time the study concluded.

c4ef7c7ac3e1.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
c4ef7c7ac3e1.sentence: The 2019 Arctic Report Card estimated that Arctic permafrost releases between 0.3 and 0.6 Pg C per year.

6e0ed5500ee7.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
6e0ed5500ee7.sentence: That same year, a study settled on the 0.6 Pg C figure, as the net difference between the annual emissions of 1,66 Pg C during the winter season (October–April), and the model-estimated vegetation carbon uptake of 1 Pg C during the growing season.

488ccb4c8039.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
488ccb4c8039.sentence: In 2022, this was challenged by a study which used a record of atmospheric observations between 1980 and 2017, and found that permafrost regions have been gaining carbon on net, as process-based models underestimated net CO2 uptake in the permafrost regions and overestimated it in the forested regions, where increased respiration in response to warming offsets more of the gains than was previously understood.

07938da4807f.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
07938da4807f.sentence: This is a substantial difference, as while biogenic methane lasts less than 12 years in the atmosphere, its global warming potential is around 80 times larger than that of CO2 over a 20-year period and between 28 and 40 times larger over a 100-year period.

098666030d63.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
098666030d63.sentence: Notably, estimates of carbon release alone do not fully represent the impact of permafrost thaw on climate change.

45f6148ed869.title: Permafrost
45f6148ed869.section: Impacts of climate change > Climate change feedback
45f6148ed869.sentence: As recent warming deepens the active layer subject to permafrost thaw, this exposes formerly stored carbon to biogenic processes which facilitate its entrance into the atmosphere as carbon dioxide and methane.

2f0a8e2ef892.title: Permafrost
2f0a8e2ef892.section: Impacts of climate change > Climate change feedback
2f0a8e2ef892.sentence: Because carbon emissions from permafrost thaw contribute to the same warming which facilitates the thaw, it is a well-known example of a positive climate change feedback.

65485b194265.title: Permafrost
65485b194265.section: Impacts of climate change > Climate change feedback
65485b194265.sentence: In the northern circumpolar region, permafrost contains organic matter equivalent to 1400–1650 billion tons of pure carbon, which was built up over thousands of years.

70386b330bd1.title: Permafrost
70386b330bd1.section: Impacts of climate change > Climate change feedback
70386b330bd1.sentence: This amount equals almost half of all organic material in all soils, and it is about twice the carbon content of the atmosphere, or around four times larger than the human emissions of carbon between the start of the Industrial Revolution and 2011.

70ed7b99cb47.title: Permafrost
70ed7b99cb47.section: Impacts of climate change > Climate change feedback
70ed7b99cb47.sentence: Further, most of this carbon (~1,035 billion tons) is stored in what is defined as the near-surface permafrost, no deeper than 3 metres (9.8 ft) below the surface.

f458d581ff55.title: Permafrost
f458d581ff55.section: Impacts of climate change > Climate change feedback
f458d581ff55.sentence: However, only a fraction of this stored carbon is expected to enter the atmosphere.

d449878638ac.title: Permafrost
d449878638ac.section: Impacts of climate change > Climate change feedback
d449878638ac.sentence: This is because carbon can be released through either aerobic or anaerobic respiration, which results in carbon dioxide (CO2) or methane (CH4) emissions, respectively.

1e933967e8ab.title: Permafrost
1e933967e8ab.section: Impacts of climate change > Climate change feedback
1e933967e8ab.sentence: While only a small fraction of permafrost carbon will enter the atmosphere as methane, those emissions will cause 40–70% of the total warming caused by permafrost thaw during the 21st century.

34396c2c4c5b.title: Permafrost
34396c2c4c5b.section: Impacts of climate change > Climate change feedback
34396c2c4c5b.sentence: Some of the emissions caused by permafrost thaw will be offset by this increased plant growth, but the exact proportion is uncertain.

f41fbe2a3891.title: Permafrost
f41fbe2a3891.section: Impacts of climate change > Climate change feedback
f41fbe2a3891.sentence: It is considered very unlikely that this greening could offset all of the emissions from permafrost thaw during the 21st century, and even less likely that it could continue to keep pace with those emissions after the 21st century.

df1ac87f8753.title: Permafrost
df1ac87f8753.section: Impacts of climate change > Climate change feedback
df1ac87f8753.sentence: Further, climate change also increases the risk of wildfires in the Arctic, which can substantially accelerate emissions of permafrost carbon.

3b16eedf395c.title: Permafrost
3b16eedf395c.section: Impacts of climate change > Climate change feedback > Impact on global temperatures
3b16eedf395c.sentence: The IPCC Sixth Assessment Report estimates that carbon dioxide and methane released from permafrost could amount to the equivalent of 14–175 billion tonnes of carbon dioxide per 1 °C (1.8 °F) of warming.

cdad08d9bd05.title: Permafrost
cdad08d9bd05.sentence: There is widespread agreement that the emissions will be smaller than human-caused emissions and are not large enough to result in runaway warming.

4812c4f05c70.title: Permafrost
4812c4f05c70.section: Impacts of climate change > Climate change feedback > Impact on global temperatures
4812c4f05c70.sentence: A 2018 paper estimated that if global warming was limited to 2 °C (3.6 °F), gradual permafrost thaw would add around 0.09 °C (0.16 °F) to global temperatures by 2100, while a 2022 review concluded that every 1 °C (1.8 °F) of global warming would cause 0.04 °C (0.072 °F) and 0.11 °C (0.20 °F) from abrupt thaw by the year 2100 and 2300.

4f6da0373d1b.title: Permafrost
4f6da0373d1b.section: Impacts of climate change > Climate change feedback > Impact on global temperatures
4f6da0373d1b.sentence: Around 4 °C (7.2 °F) of global warming, abrupt (around 50 years) and widespread collapse of permafrost areas could occur, resulting in an additional warming of 0.2–0.4 °C (0.36–0.72 °F).

4363ba398567.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
4363ba398567.sentence: It is estimated that the total soil organic carbon (SOC) stock in northern circumpolar permafrost region equals around 1,460–1,600 Pg.

b187d7ce947a.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
b187d7ce947a.sentence: This estimation of the amount of carbon stored in permafrost soils is more than double the amount currently in the atmosphere.

7730e71751d9.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
7730e71751d9.sentence: (1 Pg = 1 Gt = 10^15g) With the Tibetan Plateau carbon content included, the total carbon pools in the permafrost of the Northern Hemisphere is likely to be around 1832 Gt.

1bd81153fc36.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
1bd81153fc36.sentence: Soil column in the permafrost soils is generally broken into three horizons, 0–30 cm, 0–100 cm, and 1–300 cm.

e9cee7b8432b.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
e9cee7b8432b.sentence: The uppermost horizon (0–30 cm) contains approximately 200 Pg of organic carbon.

352bdc87e1c8.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
352bdc87e1c8.sentence: The 0–100 cm horizon contains an estimated 500 Pg of organic carbon, and the 0–300 cm horizon contains an estimated 1024 Pg of organic carbon.

83f3f718b15a.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
83f3f718b15a.sentence: These estimates more than doubled the previously known carbon pools in permafrost soils.

db9e0c669888.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
db9e0c669888.sentence: Additional carbon stocks exist in yedoma (400 Pg), carbon rich loess deposits found throughout Siberia and isolated regions of North America, and deltaic deposits (240 Pg) throughout the Arctic.

56667be79c7b.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
56667be79c7b.sentence: These deposits are generally deeper than the 3 m investigated in traditional studies.

9db9a3c12699.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
9db9a3c12699.sentence: In 2003, Tarnocai, et al. used the Northern and Mid Latitudes Soil Database to make a determination of carbon stocks in cryosols—soils containing permafrost within two meters of the soil surface.

5504feaa4958.title: Thermokarst
5504feaa4958.sentence: Thermokarst is a type of terrain characterised by very irregular surfaces of marshy hollows and small hummocks formed when ice-rich permafrost thaws.

845c72b8a2fd.title: Thermokarst
845c72b8a2fd.sentence: The land surface type occurs in Arctic areas, and on a smaller scale in mountainous areas such as the Himalayas and the Swiss Alps.

c12c6428946d.title: Thermokarst
c12c6428946d.sentence: These pitted surfaces resemble clusters of small lakes formed by dissolution of limestone in some karst areas, which is how they came to have "karst" attached to their name, even though no limestone is actually present.

0b8fa24876cd.title: Thermokarst
0b8fa24876cd.sentence: A thermokarst lake, also called a thaw lake, tundra lake, thaw depression, or tundra pond, is a body of freshwater, usually shallow, that is formed in a depression formed by thawing ice-rich permafrost.

a0182b4aaefa.title: Thermokarst
a0182b4aaefa.sentence: A key indicator of thermokarst lakes is the occurrence of excess ground ice as well as having an ice content with greater than 30% by volume.

db71426bd2d3.title: Thermokarst
db71426bd2d3.sentence: Thermokarst lakes tend to form and disappear in a cyclical manner, resulting in a predictable life cycle (see "life cycle" below).

9eaf3688424c.title: Thermokarst
9eaf3688424c.sentence: The presence of thaw lakes in a region results in a thermal disturbance as the water warms the ground.

98c20856c8c3.title: Thermokarst
98c20856c8c3.sentence: The depth of permafrost below a lake will generally be shallower and if the lake is of sufficient depth, a talik is present.

489eac291138.title: Thermokarst
489eac291138.sentence: The formation of permafrost thaw lakes due to warming climate is a positive feedback loop, as methane, nitrous oxide and carbon dioxide are released as permafrost thaws, contributing to further climate warming.

a49669c0c357.title: Talik
a49669c0c357.sentence: A talik is a zone of year-round unfrozen ground located in the middle of a permafrost area.

8acb35569ad8.title: Talik
8acb35569ad8.sentence: In regions of continuous permafrost, taliks often occur underneath shallow thermokarst lakes and rivers, where the deep water does not freeze in winter and thus the soil underneath does not freeze either.

6caa3b426682.title: Talik
6caa3b426682.sentence: Taliks are sometimes distinguished as closed, open, or through.

b31e07194ef9.title: Talik
b31e07194ef9.sentence: These terms refer to whether the talik is surrounded by permafrost, open at the top (e.g. a thermokarst lake), or open both at the top and above an unfrozen layer beneath the permafrost.

3bbbfb45ff53.title: Talik
3bbbfb45ff53.sentence: Findings from a scientific study suggest a more widespread occurrence of open taliks within fault zones and areas influenced by large rivers.

089ea6d3960d.title: Soil carbon sponge
089ea6d3960d.sentence: Soil carbon sponge (or soil sponge) is porous, well-aggregated soil in good health, better able to absorb and retain water.

db091f84bc81.title: Soil carbon sponge
db091f84bc81.sentence: Australian microbiologist and climatologist, Walter Jehne, articulated the concept of the soil carbon sponge in his 2017 paper, Regenerate Earth, connecting soil carbon with a restored water cycle able to induce planetary cooling through evaporative cooling and higher reflectance of denser green vegetation.

0923c974ea55.title: Soil carbon sponge
0923c974ea55.sentence: A soil carbon sponge has densities much lighter (1 gram/cc) as compared to the parent mineral soil (2.6–3.5 grams/cc).

a9550b59ee73.title: Soil carbon sponge
a9550b59ee73.sentence: Intensive farming practices that leave bare soils, cultivate extensively, apply water-needy fertilizers and biocides and extensively irrigate have accelerated the oxidation of soil carbon as CO2.

548443e843c8.title: Soil carbon sponge
548443e843c8.sentence: These oxidative practices reduce the depth and function of soil carbon sponges.

9eb969cfaeff.title: Soil carbon sponge
9eb969cfaeff.sentence: Soil carbon sponges can be negatively affected by fire and flooding.

01e682559379.title: Soil carbon sponge
01e682559379.sentence: Afforestation, reforestation and cover cropping are methods to build and improve soil carbon sponges.

47634cf6a63e.title: Soil carbon sponge
47634cf6a63e.sentence: Soil carbon sponges also serve as carbon sinks.

7e6fde743995.title: Thaw depth
7e6fde743995.sentence: In soil science, the thaw depth or thaw line is the instantaneous level down to which the soil has warmed to zero degrees Celsius.

e1dbf55b6de6.title: Thaw depth
e1dbf55b6de6.sentence: The layer of soil over the thaw depth is called the active layer, while the soil below is called permafrost.

04afe8d000cd.title: Thaw depth
04afe8d000cd.sentence: The active layer thickness is the maximum thaw depth over a period of two years.

f8c995735b79.title: Thaw depth
f8c995735b79.sentence: The primary factor that determines the thaw depth is the maximal air temperature.

a0e3f68e8d75.title: Active layer
a0e3f68e8d75.sentence: If it is only a little above 0 °C, the active layer can be very thin (only 10 cm on Ellesmere Island), whilst if it is quite warm, it is much thicker (about 2.5 m at Yakutsk), and if the permafrost is discontinuous and soil begins thawing earlier, it can be still thicker (5 meters at Yellowknife).

fa677bd2b028.title: Active layer
fa677bd2b028.sentence: The parent material of the soil is also important: active layers in soils made of sandy or gravelly parent materials can be up to five times deeper than those made from loam- or clay-rich parent material.

8cac7fa930ac.title: Active layer
8cac7fa930ac.sentence: This is because the coarser material allows for much greater conductivity of heat down into the soil.

b1ba8a42c5bb.title: Thaw depth
b1ba8a42c5bb.sentence: The soil type is another important factor: coarser textures of the parent material have higher thermal conductivity, and, e.g., sandy soils have much deeper thaw line than clays.

6d7c552b5260.title: Thaw depth
6d7c552b5260.sentence: Other factors are the vegetation and the percentage of the soil organic matter, which influence the bulk density of the soil, and hence thermal conductivity.

28634faa3b0b.title: Thaw depth
28634faa3b0b.sentence: The knowledge of the thaw depth is important for the two major reasons: its influence on the ecology and on construction (buildings, pipelines, roads, etc.).

8cfe6740431b.title: Syngenetic permafrost growth
8cfe6740431b.sentence: Syngenetic permafrost growth is a mode of the growth of permafrost whereby additional material is deposited to a permafrost site during freezing conditions, causing the permafrost layer to build upwards.

5a66cc944c03.title: Syngenetic permafrost growth
5a66cc944c03.sentence: It is cited as an efficient mode of permafrost growth, compared with heterogenetic permafrost growth, which occurs when freezing temperatures penetrate into previously unfrozen ground of uniform composition.

3c481702fb1e.title: Syngenetic permafrost growth
3c481702fb1e.sentence: Syngenetic deposition of frozen materials comes from any of a variety of sources, sediment from streams and rivers, material fallen from hillsides, material blown by the wind, and material deposited at the bottom of lakes.

d509b7b4bf09.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
d509b7b4bf09.sentence: - The first process that captures carbon and stores it is syngenetic permafrost growth.

177986e182dc.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
177986e182dc.sentence: As this process occurs, the organic and mineral soil that is deposited is incorporated into the permafrost as the permafrost surface rises.

f015ed9cc2be.title: Syngenetic permafrost growth
f015ed9cc2be.sentence: Ice wedges that intrude into cracks in permafrost may be regarded as syngenetic, if they grow upwards.

7a556155180c.title: Syngenetic permafrost growth
7a556155180c.sentence: Studies of such formations are partly based on observations in the Cold Regions Research and Engineering Laboratory tunnel into permafrost near Fairbanks, Alaska.

0e2865ebec2e.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
0e2865ebec2e.section: Carbon release from the permafrost > Carbon dioxide emissions
0e2865ebec2e.sentence: Most of the permafrost soil are oxic and provide a suitable environment for aerobic microbial respiration.

1fbd9f74435b.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
1fbd9f74435b.section: Carbon release from the permafrost > Carbon dioxide emissions
1fbd9f74435b.sentence: As such, carbon dioxide emissions account for the overwhelming majority of permafrost emissions and of the Arctic emissions in general.

07a570d4f5d4.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
07a570d4f5d4.section: Carbon release from the permafrost > Carbon dioxide emissions
07a570d4f5d4.sentence: There's some debate over whether the observed emissions from permafrost soils primarily constitute microbial respiration of ancient carbon, or simply greater respiration of modern-day carbon (i.e. leaf litter), due to warmer soils intensifying microbial metabolism.

653c7c68faa5.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
653c7c68faa5.section: Carbon release from the permafrost > Carbon dioxide emissions
653c7c68faa5.sentence: Studies published in the early 2020s indicate that while soil microbiota still primarily consumes and respires modern carbon when plants grow during the spring and summer, these microorganisms then sustain themselves on ancient carbon during the winter, releasing it into the atmosphere.

8c519e5475d6.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
8c519e5475d6.section: Carbon release from the permafrost > Carbon dioxide emissions
8c519e5475d6.sentence: On the other hand, former permafrost areas consistently see increased vegetation growth, or primary production, as plants can set down deeper roots in the thawed soil and grow larger and uptake more carbon.

b7c6a54581ab.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
b7c6a54581ab.section: Carbon release from the permafrost > Carbon dioxide emissions
b7c6a54581ab.sentence: This is generally the main counteracting feedback on permafrost carbon emissions.

bd891bbe2cc4.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
bd891bbe2cc4.section: Carbon release from the permafrost > Carbon dioxide emissions
bd891bbe2cc4.sentence: Moreover, thawed areas become more vulnerable to wildfires, which alter landscape and release large quantities of stored organic carbon through combustion.

2f706331a39f.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
2f706331a39f.section: Carbon release from the permafrost > Carbon dioxide emissions
2f706331a39f.sentence: Removal of the protective organic mat that insulates the soil exposes the underlying soil and permafrost to increased solar radiation, which in turn increases the soil temperature, active layer thickness, and changes soil moisture.

f8bfb87db3fd.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
f8bfb87db3fd.sentence: Carbon storage in permafrost is the result of two primary processes.

d7562ddaf070.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
d7562ddaf070.sentence: Organic carbon derived from terrestrial vegetation must be incorporated into the soil column and subsequently be incorporated into permafrost to be effectively stored.

5e526d3fcb1c.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
5e526d3fcb1c.sentence: Carbon is not produced by permafrost.

0f6762d27568.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
0f6762d27568.sentence: This process is the result of a constant active layer where thickness and energy exchange between permafrost, active layer, biosphere, and atmosphere, resulting in the vertical increase of the soil surface elevation.

2cf8d8b4de18.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
2cf8d8b4de18.sentence: This aggradation of soil is the result of aeolian or fluvial sedimentation and/or peat formation.

716b4115e21a.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
716b4115e21a.sentence: Peat accumulation rates are as high as 0.5mm/yr while sedimentation may cause a rise of 0.7mm/yr.

04fbe093f5a2.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
04fbe093f5a2.sentence: - The second process responsible for storing carbon is cryoturbation, the mixing of soil due to freeze-thaw cycles.

ae13eb8b1ee2.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
ae13eb8b1ee2.sentence: Frost heaving is the most common form of cryoturbation.

8bc357a82699.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
8bc357a82699.sentence: Eventually, carbon that originates at the surface moves deep enough into the active layer to be incorporated into permafrost.

c43d2552f4fd.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
c43d2552f4fd.sentence: When cryoturbation and the deposition of sediments act together carbon storage rates increase.

50abd8ad1661.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
50abd8ad1661.section: Carbon release from the permafrost > Methane emissions
50abd8ad1661.sentence: Methanogenesis requires thoroughly anaerobic environments, which slow down the mobilization of old carbon.

8829ff1866f4.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
8829ff1866f4.section: Carbon release from the permafrost > Methane emissions
8829ff1866f4.sentence: Since methanogenesis requires anaerobic environments, it is frequently associated with Arctic lakes, where the emergence of bubbles of methane can be observed.

2ce407a99aca.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
2ce407a99aca.section: Carbon release from the permafrost > Methane emissions
2ce407a99aca.sentence: 2022 observations indicate that at least half of the methane produced within thermokarst lakes reaches the atmosphere.

54449e030d50.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
54449e030d50.section: Carbon release from the permafrost > Methane emissions
54449e030d50.sentence: A 2015 Nature review estimated that the cumulative emissions from thawed anaerobic permafrost sites were 75–85% lower than the cumulative emissions from aerobic sites, and that even there, methane emissions amounted to only 3 to 7% of CO2 emitted in situ (by weight of carbon).

774e73e20bf8.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
774e73e20bf8.section: Carbon release from the permafrost > Methane emissions
774e73e20bf8.sentence: In 2018, however, another study in Nature Climate Change performed seven-year incubation experiments and found that methane production became equivalent to CO2 production once a methanogenic microbial community became established at the anaerobic site.

5c1eb390d2f8.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
5c1eb390d2f8.section: Carbon release from the permafrost > Methane emissions
5c1eb390d2f8.sentence: For instance, a 2017 paper suggested that even in the thawing peatlands with frequent thermokarst lakes, less than 10% of methane emissions can be attributed to the old, thawed carbon, and the rest is anaerobic decomposition of modern carbon.

3dd42a99a73f.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
3dd42a99a73f.section: Carbon release from the permafrost > Methane emissions
3dd42a99a73f.sentence: In 2022, a paper demonstrated that peatland methane emissions from permafrost thaw are initially quite high (82 milligrams of methane per square meter per day), but decline by nearly three times as the permafrost bog matures, suggesting a reduction in methane emissions in several decades to a century following abrupt thaw.

b6d63f53e60e.title: Arctic methane emissions
b6d63f53e60e.sentence: Arctic methane emissions contribute to a rise in methane concentrations in the atmosphere.

98b355ff5567.title: Arctic methane emissions
98b355ff5567.sentence: In the Arctic, the main human-influenced sources of methane are thawing permafrost, Arctic sea ice melting, clathrate breakdown and Greenland ice sheet melting.

08a7f11d33d1.title: Arctic methane emissions
08a7f11d33d1.sentence: This methane release results in a positive climate change feedback (that is, one that amplifies warming), as methane is a powerful greenhouse gas.

21ac151aca54.title: Arctic methane emissions
21ac151aca54.sentence: When permafrost thaws due to global warming, large amounts of organic material can become available for methanogenesis and may therefore be released as methane.

4a3955af0819.title: Arctic methane emissions
4a3955af0819.section: Sources of methane in the Arctic
4a3955af0819.sentence: Permafrost contains almost twice as much carbon as the atmosphere, with ~20 Gt of permafrost-associated methane trapped in methane clathrates.

942c995b48d0.title: Arctic methane emissions
942c995b48d0.section: Sources of methane in the Arctic
942c995b48d0.sentence: A 2024 assessment estimated the total methane emissions from Arctic–Boreal landforms to be approximately 48.7 (13.3–86.9) Tg CH4/year, with marine sources contributing around 4.9 (0.4–19.4) Tg CH4/year.

6dd07934e9be.title: Arctic methane emissions
6dd07934e9be.section: Sources of methane in the Arctic > Thawing permafrost
6dd07934e9be.sentence: Methanogenesis requires thoroughly anaerobic environments, which slow down the mobilization of old carbon.

ea04c47e4ce1.section: Sources of methane in the Arctic > Thawing permafrost
ea04c47e4ce1.sentence: A 2015 Nature review estimated that the cumulative emissions from thawed anaerobic permafrost sites were 75–85% lower than the cumulative emissions from aerobic sites, and that even there, methane emissions amounted to only 3 to 7% of CO2 emitted in situ (by weight of carbon).

4f2b1dd3ae5c.title: Arctic methane emissions
4f2b1dd3ae5c.section: Sources of methane in the Arctic > Thawing permafrost
4f2b1dd3ae5c.sentence: In 2018, however, another study in Nature Climate Change performed seven-year incubation experiments and found that methane production became equivalent to CO2 production once a methanogenic microbial community became established at the anaerobic site.

972f31f960b9.title: Arctic methane emissions
972f31f960b9.section: Sources of methane in the Arctic > Thawing permafrost
972f31f960b9.sentence: Since methanogenesis requires anaerobic environments, it is frequently associated with Arctic lakes, where the emergence of bubbles of methane can be observed.

13eba5a61032.title: Arctic methane emissions
13eba5a61032.section: Sources of methane in the Arctic > Thawing permafrost
13eba5a61032.sentence: 2022 observations indicate that at least half of the methane produced within thermokarst lakes reaches the atmosphere.

7955841b73b3.title: Arctic methane emissions
7955841b73b3.sentence: Radiocarbon dating of trace methane in lake bubbles and soil organic carbon concluded that 0.2 to 2.5 Pg of permafrost carbon has been released as methane and carbon dioxide over the last 60 years.

ad51b43efbd2.title: Arctic methane emissions
ad51b43efbd2.sentence: However, there is currently no evidence connecting the Arctic to this recent acceleration.

b6b5e944ba3e.title: Arctic methane emissions
b6b5e944ba3e.sentence: The study suggested that tropical wetland methane emissions were the culprit behind the recent growth trend, and this hypothesis was reinforced by a 2022 paper connecting tropical terrestrial emissions to 80% of the global atmospheric methane trends between 2010 and 2019.

a0c9fba0d67d.title: Arctic methane emissions
a0c9fba0d67d.sentence: Nevertheless, the Arctic's role in global methane trends is considered very likely to increase in the future.

66144bba1f18.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
66144bba1f18.section: Carbon release from the permafrost > Cumulative
66144bba1f18.sentence: In 2011, preliminary computer analyses suggested that permafrost emissions could be equivalent to around 15% of anthropogenic emissions.

69fdc9cfa1e5.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
69fdc9cfa1e5.section: Carbon release from the permafrost > Cumulative
69fdc9cfa1e5.sentence: Their figures for combined permafrost emissions by 2100 amounted to 150–200 billion tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent under 1.5 °C (2.7 °F) of warming, 220–300 billion tonnes under 2 °C (3.6 °F) and 400–500 billion tonnes if the warming was allowed to exceed 4 °C (7.2 °F).

60152029dc32.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
60152029dc32.section: Carbon release from the permafrost > Cumulative
60152029dc32.sentence: However, neither study was able to take abrupt thaw into account.

8def370714f7.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
8def370714f7.section: Carbon release from the permafrost > Cumulative
8def370714f7.sentence: In 2020, a study of the northern permafrost peatlands (a smaller subset of the entire permafrost area, covering 3.7 million km2 out of the estimated 18 million km2) would amount to ~1% of anthropogenic radiative forcing by 2100, and that this proportion remains the same in all warming scenarios considered, from 1.5 °C (2.7 °F) to 6 °C (11 °F).

64c057977f8b.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
64c057977f8b.section: Carbon release from the permafrost > Cumulative
64c057977f8b.sentence: It had further suggested that after 200 more years, those peatlands would have absorbed more carbon than what they had emitted into the atmosphere.

4ec7ff4291d1.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
4ec7ff4291d1.section: Carbon release from the permafrost > Cumulative
4ec7ff4291d1.sentence: In 2021, a group of prominent permafrost researchers like Merritt Turetsky had presented their collective estimate of permafrost emissions, including the abrupt thaw processes, as part of an effort to advocate for a 50% reduction in anthropogenic emissions by 2030 as a necessary milestone to help reach net zero by 2050.

38d85d090653.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
38d85d090653.section: Carbon release from the permafrost > Cumulative
38d85d090653.sentence: An updated 2022 assessment of climate tipping points concluded that abrupt permafrost thaw would add 50% to gradual thaw rates, and would add 14 billion tons of carbon dioxide equivalent emissions by 2100 and 35 billion tons by 2300 per every degree of warming.

4376d0fc558d.title: Land use, land-use change, and forestry
4376d0fc558d.sentence: Land use, land-use change, and forestry (LULUCF), also referred to as forestry and other land use (FOLU) or agriculture, forestry and other land use (AFOLU), is defined as a "greenhouse gas inventory sector that covers emissions and removals of greenhouse gases resulting from direct human-induced land use such as settlements and commercial uses, land-use change, and forestry activities."
4376d0fc558d.key: Land use, land-use change, and forestry

7a526a5943c4.title: Land use, land-use change, and forestry
7a526a5943c4.sentence: LULUCF has impacts on the global carbon cycle and as such, these activities can add or remove carbon dioxide (or, more generally, carbon) from the atmosphere, influencing climate.
7a526a5943c4.key: Land use, land-use change, and forestry

a01c91cdf94a.title: Land use, land-use change, and forestry
a01c91cdf94a.sentence: LULUCF has been the subject of two major reports by the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC), but is difficult to measure.
a01c91cdf94a.key: Land use, land-use change, and forestry

a7af4ac9d478.title: Land use, land-use change, and forestry
a7af4ac9d478.sentence: IPCC estimates that land-use change (e.g. conversion of forest into agricultural land) contributes a net 1.6 ± 0.8 Gt carbon per year to the atmosphere.
a7af4ac9d478.key: Land use, land-use change, and forestry

87131c27a510.title: Land use, land-use change, and forestry
87131c27a510.sentence: For comparison, the major source of CO2, namely emissions from fossil fuel combustion and cement production, amount to 6.3 ± 0.6 Gt carbon per year.

9d36f2ac25bd.title: Land use, land-use change, and forestry
9d36f2ac25bd.sentence: Updated assessments report that emissions from land-use, land-use change and forestry averaged 1.1 ± 0.7 Gt C yr⁻¹ (4.1 ± 2.6 Gt CO₂ yr⁻¹) over 2014–2023 and a preliminary projection of 1.2 ± 0.7 Gt C yr⁻¹ (4.2 ± 2.6 Gt CO₂ yr⁻¹) for 2024
9d36f2ac25bd.key: Land use, land-use change, and forestry

55c37036365f.title: Land use, land-use change, and forestry
55c37036365f.sentence: It is mandatory for Annex 1 Parties to account for changes in carbon stocks resulting from deforestation, reforestation and afforestation (B Article 3.3) and voluntary to account for emissions from forest management, cropland management, grazing land management and revegetation (B. Article 3.4).

e7bed35f361b.title: Land use, land-use change, and forestry
e7bed35f361b.sentence: Land-use change alters not just atmospheric CO2 concentration but also land surface biophysics such as albedo and evapotranspiration, both of which affect climate.
