d4962c1a62ab.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
d4962c1a62ab.section: Carbon release from the permafrost > Methane emissions
d4962c1a62ab.sentence: Altogether, these two processes - hillside collapse (also known as retrogressive thaw slump, or RTS) and thermokarst lake formation - are collectively described as abrupt thaw, as they can rapidly expose substantial volumes of soil to microbial respiration in a matter of days, as opposed to the gradual, cm by cm, thaw of formerly frozen soil which dominates across most permafrost environments.

bdc764e1e3c8.title: Arctic methane emissions
bdc764e1e3c8.section: Sources of methane in the Arctic > Thawing permafrost
bdc764e1e3c8.sentence: Altogether, these two processes - hillside collapse (also known as retrogressive thaw slump, or RTS) and thermokarst lake formation - are collectively described as abrupt thaw, as they can rapidly expose substantial volumes of soil to microbial respiration in a matter of days, as opposed to the gradual, cm by cm, thaw of formerly frozen soil which dominates across most permafrost environments.

e03a31aa6290.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
e03a31aa6290.section: Carbon release from the permafrost > Methane emissions
e03a31aa6290.sentence: Another example occurred in the wake of a 2020 Siberian heatwave, which was found to have increased RTS numbers 17-fold across the northern Taymyr Peninsula – from 82 to 1404, while the resultant soil carbon mobilization increased 28-fold, to an average of 11 grams of carbon per square meter per year across the peninsula (with a range between 5 and 38 grams).

0fabf1e03a53.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
0fabf1e03a53.section: Carbon release from the permafrost > Methane emissions
0fabf1e03a53.sentence: Thus, abrupt thaw adds between 60 and 100 gigatonnes of carbon by 2300, increasing carbon emissions by ~125–190% when compared to gradual thaw alone.

ee79d1df36c0.title: Permafrost
ee79d1df36c0.section: Impacts of climate change > Climate change feedback
ee79d1df36c0.sentence: Much of the uncertainty about the eventual extent of permafrost methane emissions is caused by the difficulty of accounting for the recently discovered abrupt thaw processes, which often increase the fraction of methane emitted over carbon dioxide in comparison to the usual gradual thaw processes.

a46f16a96a48.title: Permafrost carbon cycle
a46f16a96a48.section: Carbon release from the permafrost > Methane emissions
a46f16a96a48.sentence: Until recently, Permafrost carbon feedback (PCF) modeling had mainly focused on gradual permafrost thaw, due to the difficulty of modelling abrupt thaw, and because of the flawed assumptions about the rates of methane production.

10db0dcd7ed3.title: Arctic methane emissions
10db0dcd7ed3.section: Sources of methane in the Arctic > Thawing permafrost
10db0dcd7ed3.sentence: This rapidity was illustrated in 2019, when three permafrost sites which would have been safe from thawing under the "intermediate" Representative Concentration Pathway 4.5 for 70 more years had undergone abrupt thaw.

423498f6c038.title: Arctic methane emissions
423498f6c038.section: Sources of methane in the Arctic > Thawing permafrost
423498f6c038.sentence: In 2022, a paper demonstrated that peatland methane emissions from permafrost thaw are initially quite high (82 milligrams of methane per square meter per day), but decline by nearly three times as the permafrost bog matures, suggesting a reduction in methane emissions in several decades to a century following abrupt thaw.

cb9a25a35139.title: Black carbon
cb9a25a35139.sentence: The term black carbon is also used in soil science and geology, referring to deposited atmospheric black carbon or directly incorporated black carbon from vegetation fires.

a89c29f6615e.title: Black carbon
a89c29f6615e.sentence: Black carbon (BC) is the light-absorbing refractory form of elemental carbon remaining after pyrolysis (e.g., charcoal) or produced by incomplete combustion (e.g. soot).

a22ead48b3e4.title: Black carbon
a22ead48b3e4.sentence: Typically, black carbon accounts for 1 to 6%, and up to 60% of the total organic carbon stored in soils is contributed by black carbon.

869a16d2ad27.title: Black carbon
869a16d2ad27.sentence: Especially for tropical soils black carbon serves as a reservoir for nutrients.

df4ba5fab481.title: Black carbon
df4ba5fab481.sentence: Experiments showed that soils without high amounts of black carbon are significantly less fertile than soils that contain black carbon.

da1695e3dc71.title: Black carbon
da1695e3dc71.sentence: An example of this increased soil fertility is the Terra preta soils of central Amazonia, presumably human-made by pre-Columbian native populations.

7157a6a361ae.title: Black carbon
7157a6a361ae.sentence: Terra preta soils have, on average, three times higher soil organic matter (SOM) content, higher nutrient levels, and a better nutrient retention capacity than surrounding infertile soils.

20386069f73b.title: Black carbon
20386069f73b.sentence: In this context, the slash and burn agricultural practice used in tropical regions does not only enhance productivity by releasing nutrients from the burned vegetation but also by adding black carbon to the soil.

7400ee5b75dd.title: Black carbon
7400ee5b75dd.sentence: Nonetheless, for sustainable management, a slash-and-char practice would be better to prevent high emissions of CO2 and volatile black carbon.

e8aefa428dbe.title: Active layer
e8aefa428dbe.sentence: Pereletok is a layer of frozen ground that remains frozen for multiple summers but eventually thaws.

dc2faededff2.title: Active layer
dc2faededff2.sentence: Pereletok is a Russian word that translates to “that which survives over the summer” and is also known as intergelisol.

ff2d0c95b433.title: Active layer
ff2d0c95b433.sentence: Because of its relatively short period in frozen form, pereletok can be considered a portion of the active layer that remains frozen for an unusually long period due to a particularly cool summer or particularly cold winter.

e7a1ad99984e.title: Active layer
e7a1ad99984e.sentence: The distinction between pereletok and permafrost does not seem to be universally defined and practically speaking, distinguishing the two in the field is difficult.

12910ecb80f6.title: Active layer
12910ecb80f6.section: Soil formation in the active layer
12910ecb80f6.sentence: However, variation in the composition of soils due to differences in parent rock are very marked in permafrost regions due to the low rate of weathering in the very cold climate.

62e0259140fa.title: Active layer
62e0259140fa.section: Soil formation in the active layer
62e0259140fa.sentence: This storage of carbon means thawing of permafrost may accelerate global warming - some suggest the difference could become very significant especially if the carbon has been stored since before the recent glacial maxima.

7500c6db1a8a.title: Soil carbon feedback
7500c6db1a8a.section: Impact on climate change > Tipping point
7500c6db1a8a.sentence: A study published in 2011 identified a so-called compost-bomb instability, related to a tipping point with explosive soil carbon releases from peatlands.

b820d70d611d.title: Soil carbon feedback
b820d70d611d.section: Impact on climate change > Tipping point
b820d70d611d.sentence: The authors noted that there is a unique stable soil carbon equilibrium for any fixed atmospheric temperature.

f4f26a527139.title: Soil carbon feedback
f4f26a527139.sentence: Climate models do not account for effects of biochemical heat release associated with microbial decomposition.

4919f403fbce.title: Soil carbon feedback
4919f403fbce.section: Impact on climate change > Tipping point
4919f403fbce.sentence: Despite the prediction that the carbon balance of peatlands is going to shift from a sink to a source this century, peatland ecosystems are still omitted from the main Earth system models and integrated assessment models.

a69e4a99bd94.title: Climate change feedbacks
a69e4a99bd94.section: Biogeophysical and biogeochemical feedbacks > CO2 feedbacks (mostly negative)
a69e4a99bd94.sentence: There are positive and negative climate feedbacks from Earth's carbon cycle.

2bcbcee19b25.title: Climate change feedbacks
2bcbcee19b25.section: Biogeophysical and biogeochemical feedbacks > CO2 feedbacks (mostly negative)
2bcbcee19b25.sentence: Altogether, carbon sinks in the land and ocean absorb around half of the current emissions.

4ef9b88f7f74.title: Climate change feedbacks
4ef9b88f7f74.section: Biogeophysical and biogeochemical feedbacks > CO2 feedbacks (mostly negative)
4ef9b88f7f74.sentence: In the future, if the emissions decrease, the fraction they absorb will increase, and they will absorb up to three-quarters of the remaining emissions - yet, the raw amount absorbed will decrease from the present.

75020d02457b.title: Climate change feedbacks
75020d02457b.section: Biogeophysical and biogeochemical feedbacks > CO2 feedbacks (mostly negative)
75020d02457b.sentence: On the contrary, if the emissions will increase, then the raw amount absorbed will increase from now, yet the fraction could decline to one-third by the end of the 21st century.

235ffdb9fe9d.title: Climate change feedbacks
235ffdb9fe9d.section: Biogeophysical and biogeochemical feedbacks > CO2 feedbacks (mostly negative)
235ffdb9fe9d.sentence: If the emissions remain very high after the 21st century, carbon sinks would eventually be completely overwhelmed, with the ocean sink diminished further and land ecosystems outright becoming a net source.

108054e32d6c.title: Climate change feedbacks
108054e32d6c.section: Biogeophysical and biogeochemical feedbacks > CO2 feedbacks (mostly negative) > Primary production through photosynthesis
108054e32d6c.sentence: Net primary productivity of plants' and phytoplankton grows as the increased CO2 fuels their photosynthesis in what is known as the CO2 fertilization effect.

69b3f2335808.title: Climate change feedbacks
69b3f2335808.section: Biogeophysical and biogeochemical feedbacks > CO2 feedbacks (mostly negative) > Primary production through photosynthesis
69b3f2335808.sentence: Additionally, plants require less water as the atmospheric CO2 concentrations increase, because they lose less moisture to evapotranspiration through open stomata (the pores in leaves through which CO2 is absorbed).

9e1ebe7363c0.title: Climate change feedbacks
9e1ebe7363c0.section: Biogeophysical and biogeochemical feedbacks > CO2 feedbacks (mostly negative) > Chemical weathering
9e1ebe7363c0.sentence: Chemical weathering over the geological long term acts to remove CO2 from the atmosphere.

0066e4b8fd73.title: Climate change feedbacks
0066e4b8fd73.section: Biogeophysical and biogeochemical feedbacks > CO2 feedbacks (mostly negative) > Chemical weathering
0066e4b8fd73.sentence: With current global warming, weathering is increasing, demonstrating significant feedbacks between climate and Earth surface.

af19a31e4d93.title: Biochar carbon removal
af19a31e4d93.sentence: Permanence in carbon products is a good indicator of the quality or durability of the material.

960430abcb1f.title: Biochar carbon removal
960430abcb1f.sentence: It also describes the amount of time that carbon can be stored in a material.

112d641d4baf.title: Biochar carbon removal
112d641d4baf.sentence: Multi-pool modelling of biochar soil amendments indicates a centennial – millennial turnover rate, depending on factors like feedstocks used, production conditions, application rates and the characteristics of depositional sites.

1a4d51eee0cd.title: Biochar carbon removal
1a4d51eee0cd.sentence: There is evidence that biochar, produced at pyrolysis temperature over 600 °C (1,112 °F), resembles inertinite and thus highly stable.

ff22d94b1b5e.title: Biochar carbon removal
ff22d94b1b5e.sentence: If produced under certain conditions, 97% of the total organic carbon in biochar is highly refractory carbon, i.e. carbon that has near infinite stability.

cb9e38a17aa2.title: Biochar carbon removal
cb9e38a17aa2.sentence: For biochar produced at temperatures between 350 °C and 800 °C, the measured labile carbon fraction ranges from approximately 16% to 1%, and incubation experiments to date have primarily captured the degradation of this labile fraction, leaving the decay rate of the recalcitrant fraction empirically unquantified.

be9f04ff4f43.title: Biochar carbon removal
be9f04ff4f43.sentence: In some cases amendment studies and meta-analyses have pointed to undesired effects of biochar soil amendments, such as sub-centennial biochar turnover (though such estimates may partly reflect parameterisation deficiencies in the underlying decay models rather than actual biochar instability), increased GHG fluxes and degradation of non-biochar soil carbon stocks.

e12c557c5b8b.title: Biochar carbon removal
e12c557c5b8b.sentence: However, a re-analysis of the metadata underlying the two-pool decay model has identified significant parameterisation deficiencies, finding that the labile carbon fraction (C1) is disproportionately small (median 0.6%) and effectively reduces the model to a single-pool approach that overestimates biochar decay rates.

64c3a8b9281a.title: Biochar carbon removal
64c3a8b9281a.sentence: Research suggests that the permanance and therewith removal potential of biochar is generally underestimated due to oversimplified methodologies, including parameterisation deficiencies in the prevalent two-pool decay model that effectively apply labile-fraction decay constants to the entire biochar mass.

b7e5b995e442.title: Biochar carbon removal
b7e5b995e442.sentence: Biochar Carbon Removal is increasingly seen as a promising negative emissions technology suitable for offsetting and carbon markets.

2b2730ea7ba3.title: Biochar carbon removal
2b2730ea7ba3.sentence: For the purpose of generating carbon credits, there are several internationally recognised voluntary biochar standards and methodologies.

fa001e72d024.title: Biochar carbon removal
fa001e72d024.sentence: Due to significant carbon abatement cost levels of biochar carbon removal, biochar carbon credits trade at prices an order of magnitude higher than carbon credits based on conventional mitigation methods such as emission reductions and nature-based solutions.

45f77874b182.title: Biochar carbon removal
45f77874b182.sentence: In 2024, biochar projects made up the majority of carbon dioxide removal (CDR) purchases, representing 86% of the total volume bought.

d99ada9a8971.title: Biochar carbon removal
d99ada9a8971.sentence: Several biochar production and carbon credit standards define criteria for permissible biomass feedstocks for biochar carbon removal.

6d5bae7d9895.title: Biochar carbon removal
6d5bae7d9895.sentence: For example, the European Biochar Certificate (EBC) features a positive list of permissible biomasses for the production of biochar.

33624ad04254.title: Biochar carbon removal
33624ad04254.sentence: In order for a credit to be certified, suppliers must be carbon net-negative, meaning they sequester more carbon than they use in the creation and distribution of biochar.

972754fa98a6.title: Enhanced weathering
972754fa98a6.section: Natural mineral weathering and ocean acidification
972754fa98a6.sentence: When silicate or carbonate minerals are exposed to rainwater or groundwater, they slowly dissolve due to carbonation weathering; that is, the water (H2O) and carbon dioxide (CO2) present in the atmosphere form carbonic acid (H2CO3) by the reaction:

921862e38e93.title: Enhanced weathering
921862e38e93.section: Natural mineral weathering and ocean acidification
921862e38e93.sentence: As a result of these two chemical reactions (carbonation and dissolution), minerals, water, and carbon dioxide combine, which alters the chemical composition of minerals and removes CO2 from the atmosphere.

ea589848e745.title: Enhanced weathering
ea589848e745.section: Natural mineral weathering and ocean acidification
ea589848e745.sentence: For silicate weathering, the theoretical net effect of dissolution and precipitation is 1 mol of CO2 sequestered for every mol of Ca2+ or Mg2+ weathered out of the mineral.

f3e637742b1c.title: Enhanced weathering
f3e637742b1c.section: Natural mineral weathering and ocean acidification
f3e637742b1c.sentence: Given that some of the dissolved cations react with existing alkalinity in the solution to form CO32− ions, the ratio is not exactly 1:1 in natural systems but is a function of temperature and CO2 partial pressure.

8e654d6e6822.title: Enhanced weathering
8e654d6e6822.section: Natural mineral weathering and ocean acidification
8e654d6e6822.sentence: The net CO2 sequestration of carbonate weathering reaction and carbonate precipitation reaction is zero.

58ce1dfb591a.title: Enhanced weathering
58ce1dfb591a.section: Natural mineral weathering and ocean acidification
58ce1dfb591a.sentence: Over geological time periods these processes are thought to stabilize the Earth's climate.

13a7136f7fa0.title: Enhanced weathering
13a7136f7fa0.section: Natural mineral weathering and ocean acidification
13a7136f7fa0.sentence: Applying limestone (a calcium carbonate) to acid soils neutralizes the H ions but releases CO2 from the limestone.

16540678ceee.title: Enhanced weathering
16540678ceee.sentence: Enhanced weathering, also termed ocean alkalinity enhancement when proposed for carbon credit systems, is a process that aims to accelerate natural weathering by spreading finely ground silicate rock, such as basalt, onto surfaces, speeding up chemical reactions between rocks, water, and air.

ba1f0bdf0c43.title: Enhanced weathering
ba1f0bdf0c43.sentence: Enhanced weathering is a chemical approach to removing carbon dioxide involving land-based or ocean-based techniques.

cd696c23b0b1.title: Enhanced weathering
cd696c23b0b1.sentence: It also removes carbon dioxide (CO2) from the atmosphere through the formation of carbonic acid, permanently storing it in solid carbonate minerals or ocean alkalinity.

b78f0f24fed5.title: Enhanced weathering
b78f0f24fed5.sentence: One example of a land-based enhanced weathering technique is in-situ carbonation of silicates.

c665818e4cad.title: Enhanced weathering
c665818e4cad.sentence: Ultramafic rock, for example, has the potential to store hundreds to thousands of years' worth of CO2 emissions.

f7edece129d9.title: Enhanced weathering
f7edece129d9.sentence: Although existing mine tailings or alkaline industrial silicate minerals (such as steel slags, construction and demolition waste, or ash from biomass incineration) may be used at first, mining more basalt might eventually be required to limit climate change.

d6314e1aaea9.title: Enhanced weathering
d6314e1aaea9.sentence: Mixing the soil with crushed rock such as silicate benefits not only the health of plants, but also carbon sequestration when calcium or magnesium are present.

a459fccfb409.title: Enhanced weathering
a459fccfb409.sentence: In July 2020, a group of scientists assessed that the geo-engineering technique of enhanced rock weathering, i.e., spreading finely crushed basalt on fields, has potential use for carbon dioxide removal by nations, identifying costs, opportunities, and engineering challenges.

a2e1c19cc15d.title: Enhanced weathering
a2e1c19cc15d.sentence: In a 2020 techno-economical analysis, the cost of utilizing this method on cropland was estimated at US$80–180 per tonne of CO2.

afb0a63c9f69.title: Enhanced weathering
afb0a63c9f69.sentence: This is comparable with other methods of removing carbon dioxide from the atmosphere currently available (BECCS (US$100–200 per tonne of CO2) – Bio-Energy with Carbon Capture and Storage) and direct air capture and storage at large scale deployment and low-cost energy inputs (US$100–300 per tonne of CO2).

92f4f04c3d53.title: Climate change mitigation
92f4f04c3d53.section: Preserving and enhancing carbon sinks > Enhanced weathering
92f4f04c3d53.sentence: Enhanced weathering could remove 2–4 Gt of CO2 per year.

c760510aa589.title: Climate change mitigation
c760510aa589.section: Preserving and enhancing carbon sinks > Enhanced weathering
c760510aa589.sentence: Cost estimates are in the US$50–200 per tonne range of CO2.

61b854e49964.title: Enhanced weathering
61b854e49964.sentence: The enhanced dissolution and carbonation of silicates ("mineral carbonation") was first proposed by Seifritz in 1990, and developed initially by Lackner et al. and further by the Albany Research Center.

02288a265a40.title: Enhanced weathering
02288a265a40.sentence: This early research investigated the carbonation of extracted and crushed silicates at elevated temperatures (~180 °C) and partial pressures of CO2 (~15 MPa) inside controlled reactors ("ex-situ mineral carbonation").

8f1e34c9cbc0.title: Enhanced weathering
8f1e34c9cbc0.sentence: Some research explores the potential of "in-situ mineral carbonation" in which the CO2 is injected into silicate rock formations to promote carbonate formation underground (see Carbfix).

9d6281487396.title: Enhanced weathering
9d6281487396.sentence: Mineral carbonation research has largely focused on the sequestration of CO2 from flue gas.

9833d81b6a3f.title: Enhanced weathering
9833d81b6a3f.sentence: It could be used for geoengineering if the source of CO2 was derived from the atmosphere, e.g. through direct air capture or biomass-CCS.

6743b883dd5d.title: Enhanced weathering
6743b883dd5d.sentence: Soil remineralization contributes to the enhanced weathering process.

3ef95fc87d39.title: Enhanced weathering
3ef95fc87d39.sentence: Enhanced weathering was initially used to refer specifically to the spreading of crushed silicate minerals on the land surface.

fd606e65db23.title: Enhanced weathering
fd606e65db23.sentence: Next to geochemical constraints, i.e., the reactive surface area of the rock feedstock, and the solution pH and pH buffer capacity of the receiving soil, the biological activity in soils has been shown to promote the dissolution of silicate minerals, but there is still uncertainty surrounding how quickly this may happen.

d55381e7a89c.title: Enhanced weathering
d55381e7a89c.sentence: Because the weathering rate is a function of saturation of the dissolving mineral in solution (decreasing to zero in fully saturated solutions), some have suggested that lack of rainfall may limit terrestrial enhanced weathering, although others suggest that secondary mineral formation or biological uptake may suppress saturation and promote weathering.

fad2b30d042b.title: Enhanced weathering
fad2b30d042b.sentence: The amount of energy that is required for comminution depends on the rate at which the minerals dissolve (less comminution is required for rapid mineral dissolution).

d539449dbeb2.title: Enhanced weathering
d539449dbeb2.sentence: A 2012 study suggested a large range in potential cost of enhanced weathering, largely due to the uncertainty surrounding mineral dissolution rates.

ad3b01355c36.title: Talik
ad3b01355c36.sentence: Due to climate fluctuations or changes, some permafrost regions may develop an unfrozen layer between the seasonal thawing and freezing surface layer and the permafrost.

ba87c93973b0.title: Talik
ba87c93973b0.sentence: This layer is called a supra-permafrost ("above the permafrost") talik; it differs from traditional taliks, which are usually associated with water bodies, in that a supra-permafrost talik occurs because the ground that thaws in summer does not fully refreeze in winter.

f21410062143.title: Talik
f21410062143.sentence: Calculations show that climate warming induces supra-permafrost taliks in moderately cold regions.

bc53464dff0b.title: Talik
bc53464dff0b.sentence: In much colder regions, warming causes a deeper summer thaw without forming a talik layer, whereas in warm, shallow permafrost regions, permafrost quickly disappears.

f2d70943452c.title: Talik
f2d70943452c.sentence: Over time and with continued increases in air temperature or snow depth, this talik layer becomes progressively thicker, and the deep permafrost layer eventually vanishes.

8c1bcf300ce5.title: Talik
8c1bcf300ce5.sentence: This type of talik has recently been observed in Russia.

8343ffd7a22e.title: Mycorrhizal fungi and soil carbon storage
8343ffd7a22e.sentence: Soil aggregation can physically protect organic carbon from decay by soil microbes.
8343ffd7a22e.key: Mycorrhizal fungi and soil carbon storage

aebb873a98a4.title: Mycorrhizal fungi and soil carbon storage
aebb873a98a4.sentence: There is much evidence that arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi increase soil aggregate formation, and that aggregate formation may be mediated by the arbuscular mycorrhizal protein glomalin.
aebb873a98a4.key: Mycorrhizal fungi and soil carbon storage

5fcc9dfd0ff7.title: Mycorrhizal fungi and soil carbon storage
5fcc9dfd0ff7.sentence: More aggregate formation can result in more soil carbon storage.
5fcc9dfd0ff7.key: Mycorrhizal fungi and soil carbon storage

065eb52234f2.title: Mycorrhizal fungi and soil carbon storage
065eb52234f2.sentence: Therefore, even if glomalin itself is not exceptionally recalcitrant and chemically resistant to decomposition (as described above) it may still contribute to soil carbon storage by physically protecting other organic matter from decomposition by promoting soil aggregation.
065eb52234f2.key: Mycorrhizal fungi and soil carbon storage

b7a5c7b14d69.title: Mycorrhizal fungi and soil carbon storage
b7a5c7b14d69.sentence: There is little information regarding the role of ectomycorrhizal fungi in soil aggregate stability.
b7a5c7b14d69.key: Mycorrhizal fungi and soil carbon storage

c88cec933b7b.title: Mycorrhizal fungi and soil carbon storage
c88cec933b7b.sentence: There are anecdotal accounts of ectomycorrhizal fungi increasing aggregation in sand in-growth bags commonly used to trap these fungi, but no current evidence that they promote aggregate formation or stability in field soils.
c88cec933b7b.key: Mycorrhizal fungi and soil carbon storage

66938d607259.title: Mycorrhizal fungi and soil carbon storage
66938d607259.sentence: The mechanism presented is that ectomycorrhizal fungi can compete with free-living decomposers for nutrients, and thereby limit the rate of total decomposition.
66938d607259.key: Mycorrhizal fungi and soil carbon storage

e74c4b00d41c.title: Mycorrhizal fungi and soil carbon storage
e74c4b00d41c.sentence: Koide and Wu (2003) made a strong case that the effect of ectomycorrhizal fungi on reducing decomposition may have more to do with competition for soil water than soil nutrients.
e74c4b00d41c.key: Mycorrhizal fungi and soil carbon storage

cc81d3ddac66.title: Mycorrhizal fungi and soil carbon storage
cc81d3ddac66.sentence: The first report of mycorrhizal inhibition of decomposition was in 1971 and came from ectomycorrhizal Pinus radiata plantations in New Zealand.
cc81d3ddac66.key: Mycorrhizal fungi and soil carbon storage

a567744266bc.title: Mycorrhizal fungi and soil carbon storage
a567744266bc.sentence: Authors show that excluding roots and mycorrhizal fungi resulted in net carbon loss, and that the result could not be explained by soil disturbance effects.
a567744266bc.key: Mycorrhizal fungi and soil carbon storage

f234f580febe.title: Mycorrhizal fungi and soil carbon storage
f234f580febe.sentence: Since then there have been several other reports of ectomycorrhizal fungi reducing activity and decomposition rates of free-living decomposers and thereby increasing soil carbon storage.
f234f580febe.key: Mycorrhizal fungi and soil carbon storage

cdf945666bf9.title: Mycorrhizal fungi and soil carbon storage
cdf945666bf9.sentence: A theoretical ecosystem model recently demonstrated that greater access to organic nitrogen by mycorrhizal fungi should slow decomposition of soil carbon by free-living decomposers by inducing nutrient limitation.
cdf945666bf9.key: Mycorrhizal fungi and soil carbon storage

16c56f592e57.title: Mycorrhizal fungi and soil carbon storage
16c56f592e57.sentence: Since arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi are thought to lack the ability to produce the enzymes to catalyze this decomposition it is generally thought that they stimulate free-living decomposer communities to increase activity by exuding labile energy substrates, a process termed priming.
16c56f592e57.key: Mycorrhizal fungi and soil carbon storage

19687c7c5454.title: Mycorrhizal fungi and soil carbon storage
19687c7c5454.sentence: Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi have been shown to increase soil carbon decomposition in nutrient rich patches.
19687c7c5454.key: Mycorrhizal fungi and soil carbon storage

e3309618f897.title: Mycorrhizal fungi and soil carbon storage
e3309618f897.sentence: Recent lab experiments have shown that the presence of arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi increases losses of soil carbon compared to soils where arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi are excluded, and that the difference is greater under elevated CO2 when the abundance of arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi is greater.
e3309618f897.key: Mycorrhizal fungi and soil carbon storage

b7336a7648c0.title: Mycorrhizal fungi and soil carbon storage
b7336a7648c0.sentence: The evidence for ectomycorrhizal priming is so far inconclusive.
b7336a7648c0.key: Mycorrhizal fungi and soil carbon storage

42921f3897b8.title: Mycorrhizal fungi and soil carbon storage

3ec5cd7de12b.title: Desertification
3ec5cd7de12b.sentence: Desertification has been defined in the text of the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD) as "land degradation in arid, semi-arid and dry sub-humid regions resulting from various factors, including climatic variations and human activities."

dca40e022921.title: Desertification
dca40e022921.sentence: This definition clearly demonstrated the interconnectedness of desertification and human activities, in particular land use and land management practices.

5904dbce4fb7.title: Desertification
5904dbce4fb7.sentence: It also highlighted the economic, social and environmental implications of desertification.

1c43eede7ae1.title: Desertification

244e30f41ae6.title: Desertification

6a221e74d2b3.title: Desertification

78cf2aa2d96b.title: Desertification

c80020ccf8cc.title: Desertification

3f25bf051f72.title: Desertification

80477a64cbc1.title: Desertification

fc77ea2d0ebd.title: Desertification

7783e443c1a8.title: Desertification

18007dda8705.title: Desertification

656a243e1aa5.title: Desertification

75560bc38376.title: Desertification

f81e6b7bc1d3.title: Desertification

c89564766b33.title: Desertification
c89564766b33.sentence: The climate of the Sahara has undergone enormous variations over the last few hundred thousand years, oscillating between wet (grassland) and dry (desert) every 20,000 years (a phenomenon believed to be caused by long-term changes in the North African climate cycle that alters the path of the North African Monsoon, caused by an approximately 40,000-year cycle in which the axial tilt of the earth changes between 22° and 24.5°).

d1e1ea93c0f4.title: Desertification

09be8d42a7d9.title: Desertification

4b94555aa6bf.title: Desertification

0a06614e71e9.title: Desertification

1f5b78cc2469.title: Desertification

fb535554f9cb.title: Desertification
fb535554f9cb.sentence: Historical evidence shows that the serious and extensive land deterioration occurring several centuries ago in arid regions had three centers: the Mediterranean, the Mesopotamian Valley, and the Loess Plateau of China, where population was dense.

681ea0abd04e.title: Desertification

899b1db2d937.title: Land degradation
899b1db2d937.sentence: Land degradation on farms is shaped by local choices and global drivers such as trade, climate change and demographic transitions.

522c5e1b32d0.title: Land degradation
522c5e1b32d0.sentence: By 2025 unsustainable farming and management practices led to the degradation of 996 Mha of agricultural lands; this accounts for over 60% of human-induced land degradation, which affects a total area of more than 1660 million hectares.

1eceb0517ad6.title: Land degradation
1eceb0517ad6.sentence: In high-income countries with intensive agricultural systems, the per hectare production losses from degradation are particularly severe, though often masked by heavy application of synthetic fertilizers and other inputs.

5a91b2184ade.title: Land degradation

d37a5682ebcd.title: Land degradation

2946690f8bef.title: Land degradation

f4a1144812b9.title: Land degradation
f4a1144812b9.sentence: Southern Asia and sub-Saharan Africa are regions where degraded lands coincide with high poverty rates and childhood stunting.

83264b1678ae.title: Land degradation
83264b1678ae.sentence: Sensitivity and resilience are measures of the vulnerability of a landscape to degradation.

de1733747ae8.title: Land degradation
de1733747ae8.sentence: These two factors combine to explain the degree of vulnerability.

f7e81a6931a6.title: Land degradation
f7e81a6931a6.sentence: Sensitivity is the degree to which a land system undergoes change due to natural forces, human intervention or a combination of both.

858fdc7ca718.title: Land degradation
858fdc7ca718.sentence: Resilience is the ability of a landscape to absorb change, without significantly altering the relationship between the relative importance and numbers of individuals and species that compose the community.

3a8904861f94.title: Land degradation
3a8904861f94.sentence: It also refers to the ability of the region to return to its original state after being changed in some way.

d7bd58f7bb04.title: Land degradation
d7bd58f7bb04.sentence: The resilience of a landscape can be increased or decreased through human interaction based upon different methods of land-use management.

6145df483d3a.title: Land degradation
6145df483d3a.sentence: Land that is degraded becomes less resilient than undegraded land, which can lead to even further degradation through shocks to the landscape.

b33498fe94b8.title: Land degradation
b33498fe94b8.sentence: In addition to the usual types of land degradation that have been known for centuries (water, wind and mechanical erosion, physical, chemical and biological degradation), four other types have emerged in the last 50 years:

fc4e3d410915.title: Land degradation
fc4e3d410915.sentence: - pollution, often chemical, due to agricultural, industrial, mining or commercial activities;

b81605b7c34d.title: Land degradation
b81605b7c34d.sentence: - loss of arable land due to urban construction, road building, land conversion, agricultural expansion, etc.;

bda63976d1c3.title: Land degradation
bda63976d1c3.sentence: - land-use constraints associated with armed conflicts.

3ed5a850314c.title: Land degradation
3ed5a850314c.sentence: Overall, more than 36 types of land degradation can be assessed.

b06523f10174.title: Land degradation
b06523f10174.sentence: All are induced or aggravated by human activities, e.g. soil erosion, soil contamination, soil acidification, sheet erosion, silting, aridification, salinization, urbanization, etc.

bc60dbc9de33.title: Grassland degradation
bc60dbc9de33.sentence: Grassland degradation, also called vegetation or steppe degradation, is a biotic disturbance in which grass struggles to grow or can no longer exist on a piece of land due to causes such as overgrazing, burrowing of small mammals, and climate change.

21ad538676f1.title: Grassland degradation
21ad538676f1.sentence: Since the 1970s, it has been observed to affect plains and plateaus of alpine meadows or grasslands, most notably being in the Philippines and in the Tibetan and Inner Mongolian region of China, where 2,460 km2 (950 sq mi) of grassland is degraded each year.

702bd1b55799.title: Grassland degradation
702bd1b55799.sentence: It takes years and sometimes even decades, depending on what is happening to that piece of land, for a grassland to become degraded.

fbf56168ff84.title: Grassland degradation
fbf56168ff84.sentence: The process is slow and gradual, but so is restoring degraded grassland.

1c66f2a52a99.title: Grassland degradation
1c66f2a52a99.sentence: Initially, only patches of grass appear to die and appear brown; but the degradation process, if not addressed, can spread to many acres of land.

e632bd4e6479.title: Grassland degradation
e632bd4e6479.sentence: The increase in average temperatures of regions makes them less suitable for grass to grow due to the more rapid evaporation of water that was formerly utilized by the grass.

192958d1972f.title: Grassland degradation
192958d1972f.sentence: Furthermore, neither periods of much rain nor stretches of drought, both of which become more prevalent with climate change, encourage the growing of grass.

0d6d94259756.title: Grassland degradation
0d6d94259756.sentence: Some scientists, however, write off climate change as an insignificant cause of degradation.

5dc45caaed3d.title: Grassland degradation
5dc45caaed3d.sentence: Degradation has been shown to appear when humans move into such areas to build, for example, roads or settlements.

0fff510dcb96.title: Grassland degradation
0fff510dcb96.sentence: Roads reduce the area where grass can grow successfully; the settlements constructed by herdsmen have proven to be the most damaging to grassland since they are accompanied by their animals, which further harm the region.

1665e27fab79.title: Grassland degradation
1665e27fab79.sentence: Also when humans convert natural grassland into farmland, they often harshly farm it by repeatedly planting the same crops year after year, and by having to do this, the soil quality is lowered when these crops suck the nutrients out of the ground.

9ef84287dbe0.title: Grassland degradation
9ef84287dbe0.sentence: Another cause of degradation by man is deforestation.

505b7f795e39.title: Grassland degradation
505b7f795e39.sentence: The gathering of medicinal plants, particularly in China, also contributed to a certain extent to degraded grasslands.

a89a74c54485.title: Grassland degradation
a89a74c54485.sentence: Two of the more logical outcomes are the decrease in arable land and a drop off in the amount of crops harvested.

3112f80b53d0.title: Grassland degradation
3112f80b53d0.sentence: These two similar outcomes in some way only lead to more degradation in that farmers, who now see their land as useless, just move on to perhaps a smaller plot of land, since that is all their money can afford, after having to surrender their prior property.

f81405b7bea8.title: Grassland degradation
f81405b7bea8.sentence: Hence, smaller plots are easier to be overgrazed and worked to exhaustion.

07a8d645cc6a.title: Grassland degradation
07a8d645cc6a.sentence: Also, the numbers of livestock tend to decrease with grassland degradation, mainly because there is less grass to be eaten.

e13f1969d6e1.title: Grassland degradation
e13f1969d6e1.sentence: Proof of this decline is that presently 15–20% of Tibetan Plateau species are now considered endangered, and now because of this animal and plant absence, the soil quality of these degraded lands is very poor.

9836a65affea.title: Grassland degradation
9836a65affea.sentence: As a result of such carbon and nitrogen loss in the Tibetan Plateau, $8,033/ha and $13,315/ha were respectively lost in economic terms.

4a21631d744b.title: Grassland degradation
4a21631d744b.sentence: Erosion of soil becomes a bigger problem, since no longer are there as many plants to anchor in the soil.

a6d42e49849b.title: Grassland degradation
a6d42e49849b.sentence: Soils are further weakened by dust storms whose frequency increases because of degradation.

250af81a6697.title: Grassland degradation
250af81a6697.sentence: With a dramatic decrease in plant diversity in this ecosystem, more carbon and nitrogen may be released into the atmosphere.

8ebbecb8e40c.title: Grassland degradation
8ebbecb8e40c.sentence: In the northern Chinese province alone, 400 million are affected every year with an associated 54 billion yuan of annual economic loss due to grassland degradation.

d81e3293ca12.title: Woody plant encroachment
d81e3293ca12.sentence: Woody plant encroachment is a natural phenomenon characterised by the area expansion and density increase of woody plants, bushes and shrubs, at the expense of the herbaceous layer, grasses and forbs.

4e2fc0b6cfc2.title: Woody plant encroachment
4e2fc0b6cfc2.sentence: Woody plant encroachment is the increase in abundance of indigenous woody plants, such as shrubs and bushes, at the expense of herbaceous plants, grasses and forbs, in grasslands and shrublands.

fbcf354482c8.title: Woody plant encroachment
fbcf354482c8.sentence: It refers to the expansion of native plants and not the spread of alien invasive species.

93c0d413e2ef.title: Woody plant encroachment
93c0d413e2ef.sentence: As opposed to invasive species, which are deliberately or accidentally introduced species, encroacher species are indigenous to the respective ecosystem and their classification as encroachers depends on whether they outcompete other indigenous species in the same ecosystem over time.

6d58d1ea6f62.title: Woody plant encroachment
6d58d1ea6f62.sentence: It predominantly occurs in grasslands, savannas and woodlands and can cause regime shifts from open grasslands and savannas to closed woodlands.

7ab32f03263c.title: Woody plant encroachment
7ab32f03263c.sentence: Woody encroachment occurs on all continents, affecting an estimated total area of 500 million hectares (5 million square kilometres).

8f59e9c56a94.title: Woody plant encroachment
8f59e9c56a94.sentence: Woody encroachment occurs at 1 percent per decade in the Eurasian steppes, 10–20 percent in North America, 8 percent in South America, 2.4 percent in Africa and 1 percent in Australia.

a36c30ad8fd1.title: Woody plant encroachment
a36c30ad8fd1.sentence: However, it has occurred at unparalleled rates since the mid-19th century.

ac0b515778a0.title: Woody plant encroachment
ac0b515778a0.sentence: As such, it is classified as a type of grassland degradation, which occurs through direct and indirect human impact during the Anthropocene.

7d0a4c41c231.title: Woody plant encroachment
7d0a4c41c231.sentence: Encroachment is commonly identified as a form of land degradation, with severe negative consequences for various ecosystem services, such as biodiversity, groundwater recharge, carbon storage capacity and herbivore carrying capacity.

dccb757c6c0d.title: Woody plant encroachment
dccb757c6c0d.sentence: Woody encroachment is often interpreted as a symptom of land degradation due to its negative impacts on key ecosystem services, but is also argued to be a form of natural succession.

bebf4912eb2f.title: Woody plant encroachment
bebf4912eb2f.sentence: In arid ecosystems woody encroachment is sometimes regarded as a form of land degradation and an expression of desertification Due to its ambiguous role in these dry ecosystems, it has been termed "green desertification".

05e6955b2284.title: Woody plant encroachment
05e6955b2284.sentence: A key difference is that during woody encroachment the herbaceous cover in the inter-canopy zones can remain intact, while during desertification these zones degrade and turn into bare soil devoid of organic matter.

9cc39caa8635.title: Woody plant encroachment
9cc39caa8635.section: Ecological and socio-economic impacts > Soil and vegetation structure
9cc39caa8635.sentence: Soil quality can decline significantly in arid and semi-arid regions under woody encroachment, manifesting through reduced soil moisture levels, nutrient availability and microbial activity.

1163be1c2e69.title: Woody plant encroachment
1163be1c2e69.section: Ecological and socio-economic impacts > Soil and vegetation structure
1163be1c2e69.sentence: Conversely, in Mediterranean and very humid climates, woody encroachment often leads to enhanced soil quality by increasing concentrations of carbon, nitrogen and phosphorus, especially in the topsoil.

e8c322222c61.title: Woody plant encroachment
e8c322222c61.section: Ecological and socio-economic impacts > Land productivity and rural livelihoods
e8c322222c61.sentence: In North America, each 1 percent increase in woody cover implies a reduction of 0.6 to 1.6 cattle per 100 hectares.

49f8974d5780.title: Great Green Wall (China)
49f8974d5780.sentence: The Great Green Wall, officially known as the Three-North Shelter Forest Program (simplified Chinese: 三北防护林; traditional Chinese: 三北防護林; pinyin: Sānběi Fánghùlín), is a series of human-planted windbreaking forest strips (shelterbelts) in China, designed to hold back the expansion of the Gobi Desert and provide timber to the local population.

4ead0968645c.title: Great Green Wall (China)
4ead0968645c.sentence: The program started in 1978 and is planned to complete around 2050, at which point it will be expected to have created a vast green barrier spanning approximately 4,828 kilometres (3,000 mi) long and up to 1,448 kilometres (900 mi) wide in certain regions, and will encompass around 88 million acres of forests.

a894cac2e294.title: Great Green Wall (China)
a894cac2e294.sentence: The Green Wall project was started in 1978, with the proposed result of raising northern China's forest cover from 5 to 15 percent, thereby reducing desertification.

4cb463d1b19b.title: Great Green Wall (China)
4cb463d1b19b.sentence: 29.7% of China had been desertified by the year 2000, with the rate of change increasing almost every year.

c03f0853d932.title: Great Green Wall (China)

a521893ac7dd.title: Great Green Wall (China)

38924506b882.title: Great Green Wall (Africa)
38924506b882.sentence: The Great Green Wall or Great Green Wall for the Sahara and the Sahel (French: Grande Muraille Verte pour le Sahara et le Sahel; Arabic: السور الأخضر العظيم, romanized: as-Sūr al-ʾAkhḍar al-ʿAẓīm) is a project adopted by the African Union in 2007, initially conceived as a way to combat desertification in the Sahel region and hold back expansion of the Sahara Desert, by planting a wall of trees stretching across the entire Sahel from Djibouti City, Djibouti, to Dakar, Senegal.

b84586aca331.title: Great Green Wall (Africa)
b84586aca331.sentence: The original dimensions of the "wall" were to be 15 km (9 mi) wide and 7,775 km (4,831 mi) long, but the program expanded to encompass nations in both northern and western Africa.

6930cc371da9.title: Great Green Wall (Africa)
6930cc371da9.sentence: The concept evolved into promoting water harvesting techniques, greenery protection and improving indigenous land use techniques, aimed at creating a mosaic of green and productive landscapes across North Africa.

4032cccb380e.title: Great Green Wall (Africa)
4032cccb380e.sentence: The ongoing goal of the project is to restore 100 million hectares (250 million acres) of degraded land, capture 250 million tonnes of carbon dioxide, and create 10 million jobs in the process, all by 2030.

45be8a6ff76a.title: Desertification
45be8a6ff76a.sentence: The purpose of this mammoth planting initiative is to enhance retention of water in the ground following the seasonal rainfall, thus promoting land rehabilitation and future agriculture.

068db44b2270.title: Great Green Wall (Africa)
068db44b2270.sentence: In the 1950s British explorer Richard St. Barbe Baker made an expedition in the Sahara.

90eae983a992.title: Great Green Wall (Africa)
90eae983a992.sentence: During St. Barbe's 40,000-kilometre (25,000 mi) expedition he proposed a "Green front" to act as a 50-kilometre-deep (30 mi) tree buffer to contain the expanding desert.

d79dccd2bfb1.title: Great Green Wall (Africa)

b1cf864b62a2.title: Great Green Wall (Africa)

826a56dbf67a.title: Great Green Wall (Africa)

8fabfac9631e.title: Great Green Wall (Africa)

f21a7bf4c23c.title: Farmer-managed natural regeneration
f21a7bf4c23c.sentence: Farmer-managed natural regeneration (FMNR) is a low-cost, sustainable land restoration technique used to combat poverty and hunger amongst poor subsistence farmers in developing countries by increasing food and timber production, and resilience to climate extremes.

0547574a9982.title: Farmer-managed natural regeneration
0547574a9982.sentence: It involves the systematic regeneration and management of trees and shrubs from tree stumps, roots and seeds.

c90974287cb0.title: Farmer-managed natural regeneration
c90974287cb0.sentence: FMNR was developed by the Australian agricultural economist Tony Rinaudo in the 1980s in West Africa.

9bb38344d70d.title: Farmer-managed natural regeneration
9bb38344d70d.sentence: FMNR adapts centuries-old methods of woodland management, called coppicing and pollarding, to produce continuous tree-growth for fuel, building materials, food and fodder without the need for frequent and costly replanting.

2bfd66c0d303.title: Farmer-managed natural regeneration
2bfd66c0d303.sentence: In fact, these living tree stumps are so numerous they constitute a vast 'underground forest' just waiting for some care to grow and provide multiple benefits at little or no cost.

dc05d98aceaf.title: Farmer-managed natural regeneration
dc05d98aceaf.sentence: Each stump can produce between 10 and 30 stems each.

981d4405ea5a.title: Farmer-managed natural regeneration
981d4405ea5a.sentence: The tallest and straightest stems are selected and the remaining stems culled.

3b4c7fa0da25.title: Farmer-managed natural regeneration
3b4c7fa0da25.sentence: When FMNR trees are integrated into crops and grazing pastures there is an increase in crop yields, soil fertility and organic matter, soil moisture and leaf fodder.

ba6ad6f8a22d.title: Farmer-managed natural regeneration
ba6ad6f8a22d.sentence: There is also a decrease in wind and heat damage, and soil erosion.

cc9778112482.title: Desertification
cc9778112482.sentence: The residue from pruned trees can be used to provide mulching for fields thus increasing soil water retention and reducing evaporation.

677b228aac04.title: Farmer-managed natural regeneration
677b228aac04.sentence: Trials, long-running programs and anecdotal data indicate that FMNR can at least double crop yields on low fertility soils.

7ad3026d5bac.title: Farmer-managed natural regeneration
7ad3026d5bac.sentence: Faidherbia albida, also known as the 'fertiliser tree', is popular for intercropping across the Sahel as it fixes nitrogen into the soil, provides fodder for livestock, and shade for crops and livestock.

c80733d0fffb.title: Farmer-managed natural regeneration
c80733d0fffb.sentence: Leaf fall contributes useful nutrients and organic matter to the soil.

7755ee15e2f4.title: Farmer-managed natural regeneration
7755ee15e2f4.sentence: By 2004 it was ascertained that FMNR was being practised on over five million hectares or 50 percent of Niger's farmland – an average reforestation rate of 250,000 hectares per year over a 20-year period.

1c05b59ea88e.title: Farmer-managed natural regeneration
1c05b59ea88e.sentence: Despite investing millions of dollars and thousands of hours of labour, there was little overall impact.

2aa1662fc725.title: Farmer-managed natural regeneration
2aa1662fc725.sentence: In Niger, from the 1930s until 1993, forestry laws took tree ownership and responsibility for the care of trees out of the hands of the people.

60a86476cdf3.title: Rangeland management
60a86476cdf3.sentence: Rangeland management (also range management, range science, or arid-land management) is a natural science that centers around the study of rangelands and the "conservation and sustainable management [of Arid-Lands] for the benefit of current societies and future generations".

4f61ab1ff368.title: Rangeland management
4f61ab1ff368.sentence: Range management is defined by Holechek et al. as the "manipulation of rangeland components to obtain optimum combination of goods and services for society on a sustained basis".

c3711780a070.title: Rangeland management
c3711780a070.sentence: Rangeland management was developed in the United States in response to rangeland deterioration and in some cases, denudation, due to overgrazing and other misuse of arid lands as demonstrated by the 20th century "Dust Bowl" and described in Hardin's 1968 "Tragedy of the Commons".

bbadbea2d02d.title: Rangeland management
bbadbea2d02d.sentence: Historically, the discipline focused on the manipulation of grazing and the proper use of rangeland vegetation for livestock.

21f9f1df0e15.title: Rangeland management
21f9f1df0e15.sentence: Key management components seek to optimize such goods and services through the protection and enhancement of soils, riparian zones, watersheds, and vegetation complexes, sustainably improving outputs of consumable range products such as red meat, wildlife, water, wood, fiber, leather, energy resource extraction, and outdoor recreation, as well as maintaining a focus on the manipulation of grazing activities of large herbivores to maintain or improve animal and plant production.

41cf77963fdb.title: Rangeland management
41cf77963fdb.sentence: Range management's focus has been expanded to include the host of ecosystem services that rangelands provide to humans world-wide.

263287239589.title: Rangeland management
263287239589.sentence: With increasing levels of rangeland degradation, for example as evident through woody plant encroachment, active rehabilitation efforts become part of rangeland management.

5eac1f8be67f.title: Rangeland management
5eac1f8be67f.section: Modern application > United States of America
5eac1f8be67f.sentence: Emerging evidence suggests that rangelands are extremely vulnerable to the threats of climate change, as more severe heatwaves, droughts, evaporation, and catastrophic flood events will consequentially alter ecological states, and negatively affect forage production, both of which will negatively impact ecosystem functioning and the sustainable production of ecosystem services.

ab08234dd34a.title: Rangeland management
ab08234dd34a.sentence: The Range Science curriculum is strongly tied to animal science, as well as plant ecology, soil science, wildlife management, climatology and anthropology.

5b5cefe41286.title: Soil sealing
5b5cefe41286.sentence: A complete soil unsealing process involves entirely removing any human-made materials like asphalt and cement that obstruct the soil's natural functions, thereby restoring its ability to perform its natural processes.

2ab1aa362e71.title: Soil sealing
2ab1aa362e71.sentence: Due to mostly irreversible losses, soil unsealing is very difficult.

b3a2b97600ba.title: Soil sealing
b3a2b97600ba.sentence: There is very limited research about the process of soil unsealing.

e80e26dfcc1c.title: Soil sealing
e80e26dfcc1c.sentence: - Transforming urban, barren, or previously used dumping soils into spaces for urban parks, green roofs, and gardens.

2804ac1988c0.title: Soil sealing

bae2bac504e4.title: Soil sealing

fa3f59b3fb30.title: Soil sealing
fa3f59b3fb30.sentence: A field trial in Palermo, Italy, applying minimal-disturbance de-sealing techniques to long-sealed urban soils found that vegetated rehabilitation stabilised water infiltration and increased microbial activity over eighteen months, while crushed-asphalt treatments preserved higher permeability but supported less vegetation cover.

ece8e0e6d2dd.title: Drylands
ece8e0e6d2dd.sentence: Dryland restoration is often understood in two ways; either to restore a dryland to its previous functionality or to avoid further degradation.

28d8eeef44d1.title: Drylands
28d8eeef44d1.sentence: The first perspective is based on the restoration of the degraded dryland areas themselves.

51cdc85b9b4d.title: Drylands
51cdc85b9b4d.sentence: The second emphasises preventative and adaptive land management to support ecosystem services and functionalities.

4a72c6d5515a.title: Drylands
4a72c6d5515a.sentence: Restoration efforts in dryland areas are particularly challenging because of rare and variable precipitation, high temperatures, low soil fertility, and invasive species.

a7d93ccb7e85.title: Drylands
a7d93ccb7e85.section: Dryland restoration > Restoration techniques > Restoration islands
a7d93ccb7e85.sentence: Restoration islands use small, strategically located plantings (islands) to make use of limited resources.

5faaa0a1114e.title: Drylands
5faaa0a1114e.section: Dryland restoration > Restoration techniques > Restoration islands
5faaa0a1114e.sentence: Once established, the island plantations proliferate (nucleate) into neighboring areas.

527b033bde5a.title: Drylands
527b033bde5a.section: Dryland restoration > Restoration techniques > Restoration islands
527b033bde5a.sentence: This strategy is best suited to address the patchiness of dryland vegetation, because restoration islands can be placed in the most promising locations and are less resource-intensive than large-scale plantations.

7d906110ca76.title: Drylands
7d906110ca76.section: Dryland restoration > Restoration techniques > Restoration islands
7d906110ca76.sentence: Other benefits include reduced fire risk, lower soil erosion, weed control, seed sources for long-term restoration, and habitat for wildlife.

f15dbd2a15b1.title: Drylands

f15dbd2a15b1.sentence: They contribute to seed dispersal, pest control, nutrient cycling, water infiltration, and soil structure, thus increasing vegetation productivity.

7412179edfdb.title: Drylands
7412179edfdb.section: Dryland restoration > Restoration techniques > Use of soil fauna
7412179edfdb.sentence: Supporting measures include using endemic species, restoration islands as nucleation sites, and mulching to increase soil moisture.

c928ab6b8f0d.sentence: Rangelands cover about 25% of drylands globally.
