e0fde4e9555c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/06%3A_Soil_Degradation-_Erosion_Compaction_and_Contamination/6.04%3A_Consequences_of_Compaction
e0fde4e9555c.sentence: Notably, the large pores are lost as they are compressed into smaller ones (Figure 6.13).

ae1a379e9f98.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/06%3A_Soil_Degradation-_Erosion_Compaction_and_Contamination/6.04%3A_Consequences_of_Compaction
ae1a379e9f98.sentence: This can restrict root growth and the activity of soil organisms.

214fd3af87ee.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/06%3A_Soil_Degradation-_Erosion_Compaction_and_Contamination/6.04%3A_Consequences_of_Compaction
214fd3af87ee.sentence: Loss of large pores between aggregates is particularly harmful for fine- and medium-textured soils that depend on those pores for good infiltration and percolation of water, as well as air exchange with the atmosphere.

1b4840591af6.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/06%3A_Soil_Degradation-_Erosion_Compaction_and_Contamination/6.04%3A_Consequences_of_Compaction
1b4840591af6.sentence: Although compaction can also damage coarse-textured soils, the impact is less severe.

2e55c48830dd.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/06%3A_Soil_Degradation-_Erosion_Compaction_and_Contamination/6.04%3A_Consequences_of_Compaction
2e55c48830dd.sentence: Compacted soil becomes hard when it dries, as it has many small pores that can hold water under high suction and pull particles tightly together.

a24ea3a89504.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/06%3A_Soil_Degradation-_Erosion_Compaction_and_Contamination/6.04%3A_Consequences_of_Compaction
a24ea3a89504.sentence: The resistance to penetration for a moist, high-quality soil is usually well below the critical level where root growth ceases for most crops: 300 pounds per square inch (psi, or 2 megapascals).

060eb081fcdd.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/06%3A_Soil_Degradation-_Erosion_Compaction_and_Contamination/6.04%3A_Consequences_of_Compaction
060eb081fcdd.sentence: When it dries, a compacted soil hardens quicker than a well-structured soil, rapidly becoming so hard that it is well above the critical 300-psi level that restricts root growth.

ca4efcda9a64.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/06%3A_Soil_Degradation-_Erosion_Compaction_and_Contamination/6.04%3A_Consequences_of_Compaction
ca4efcda9a64.sentence: Actively growing roots need large pores with diameters greater than about 0.1 millimeter, the size of most root tips.

f1a581c55373.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/06%3A_Soil_Degradation-_Erosion_Compaction_and_Contamination/6.04%3A_Consequences_of_Compaction
f1a581c55373.sentence: Compacted soils that have few or no large pores don’t allow plants to be effectively rooted, thus limiting water and nutrient uptake.

5c981411fb0f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/06%3A_Soil_Degradation-_Erosion_Compaction_and_Contamination/6.04%3A_Consequences_of_Compaction
5c981411fb0f.sentence: The root system will probably develop short, thick roots and few fine roots or root hairs (Figure 5.6, Figure 6.8).

b81858996a4b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/06%3A_Soil_Degradation-_Erosion_Compaction_and_Contamination/6.04%3A_Consequences_of_Compaction
b81858996a4b.sentence: These roots have thickened tissue and are not efficient at taking up water and nutrients.

c97c77b078c6.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/06%3A_Soil_Degradation-_Erosion_Compaction_and_Contamination/6.04%3A_Consequences_of_Compaction
c97c77b078c6.sentence: A root system that’s up against mechanical barriers sends a hormonal signal to the plant shoot, which then slows down respiration and growth.

310f9b2fde5a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/06%3A_Soil_Degradation-_Erosion_Compaction_and_Contamination/6.04%3A_Consequences_of_Compaction
310f9b2fde5a.sentence: In fact, because some of the same hormones are involved—and mechanical resistance increases when the soil dries—it is often difficult to separate the effects of compaction from those of drought.

b42e08af1f3f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/06%3A_Soil_Degradation-_Erosion_Compaction_and_Contamination/6.04%3A_Consequences_of_Compaction
b42e08af1f3f.sentence: The limitation on deep root growth by subsoil compaction reduces the volume of soil from which plant roots can extract water and nutrients, and increases the probability of yield losses from drought stress.

7ab7791df795.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/06%3A_Soil_Degradation-_Erosion_Compaction_and_Contamination/6.04%3A_Consequences_of_Compaction
7ab7791df795.sentence: Earthworms and insects, for example, need large pores to move around and access organic materials, while aerobic bacteria and fungi need air exchange.

2668e531e878.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/06%3A_Soil_Degradation-_Erosion_Compaction_and_Contamination/6.04%3A_Consequences_of_Compaction
2668e531e878.sentence: Therefore, compacted soils typically have much lower populations of these beneficial organisms, but they return remarkably quickly when better practices are adopted.

232ee41611da.title: Woody plant encroachment
232ee41611da.sentence: The term bush control, or brush management, refers to actions that are targeted at controlling the density and composition of bushes and shrubs in a given area.

a7cfb57f373b.title: Woody plant encroachment
a7cfb57f373b.sentence: It is widely accepted that encroaching indigenous woody plants are to be reduced in numbers, but not eradicated.

bb38b879c847.title: Woody plant encroachment
bb38b879c847.sentence: This is critical as these plants provide important functions in the respective ecosystems, e.g. they serve as habitat for animals.

d91aad414538.title: Woody plant encroachment
d91aad414538.sentence: Three different categories of control measures can be distinguished:

fbf58c866e61.title: Woody plant encroachment
fbf58c866e61.sentence: - Preventive measures: application of proven good management practices to prevent the excessive growth of woody species, e.g. through appropriate stocking rates and rotational grazing in the case of rangeland agriculture.

aa15c8cbc439.title: Woody plant encroachment
aa15c8cbc439.sentence: - Responsive measures: the reduction of bush densities through targeted bush harvesting or other forms of removal (bush thinning).

c5223cb36980.title: Woody plant encroachment
c5223cb36980.sentence: - Maintenance measures: repeated or continuous measures of maintaining the bush density and composition that has been established through bush thinning.

d183ac0f9ad2.title: Woody plant encroachment
d183ac0f9ad2.sentence: It is generally assumed that preventative measures are a more cost-effective method to combat woody encroachment than treating ecosystems once degradation has occurred.

71e19ce750ab.title: Woody plant encroachment
71e19ce750ab.sentence: Evidence from a shrub-cover gradient likewise suggests that bush control is most effective when initiated at the early stages of encroachment (around 3% shrub cover), the stage at which trade-offs among ecosystem functions are strongest and below-ground species richness still sustains grassland productivity.

4b2de710199e.title: Woody plant encroachment
4b2de710199e.sentence: Encroached grasslands can constitute a stable state, meaning that without intervention the vegetation will not return to its previous composition.

056d27151232.title: Woody plant encroachment
056d27151232.sentence: The application of chemicals, for example, can lead to higher carbon losses than mechanical shrub thinning.

01a297edd1cc.title: Woody plant encroachment
01a297edd1cc.sentence: Causes include land-use intensification, such as overgrazing, as well as the suppression of wildfires and the reduction in numbers of wild herbivores.

df3138d61251.title: Woody plant encroachment
df3138d61251.sentence: Both local drivers (i.e. related to land use practices) as well as global drivers can cause woody plant encroachment.

5824dfbc5fad.title: Woody plant encroachment
5824dfbc5fad.sentence: According to the two-layer theory, grasses use topsoil moisture, while woody plants predominantly use subsoil moisture.

538571113928.title: Woody plant encroachment
538571113928.sentence: If grasses are reduced by overgrazing, this reduces their water intake and allows more water to penetrate into the subsoil for the use by woody plants.

6bc149a7bf5e.title: Woody plant encroachment
6bc149a7bf5e.sentence: For example, coarse-textured soils promote woody plant growth, while fine-textured soils limit it.

329dbc181bb4.title: Woody plant encroachment
329dbc181bb4.sentence: Moreover, the likelihood of woody encroachment is influenced by soil moisture and soil nutrient availability, which is why it often occurs on downslope locations and cooler slopes.

280cc9f11f26.title: Woody plant encroachment
280cc9f11f26.sentence: Woody plants with C3 photosynthetic pathway thrive under high CO2 concentrations, as opposed to grasses with C4 photosynthetic pathway.

0bbb9c962a8e.title: Woody plant encroachment
0bbb9c962a8e.sentence: For example, if rainfall intensity increases, deep soil water typically increases, which in turn benefits bushes more than grasses.

9d232b8d9406.title: Woody plant encroachment
9d232b8d9406.section: Ecological and socio-economic impacts > Carbon sequestration
9d232b8d9406.sentence: Considering above-ground biomass alone, woody plant encroachment may appear to function as a carbon sink.

413ecd1023f2.title: Woody plant encroachment
413ecd1023f2.section: Ecological and socio-economic impacts > Carbon sequestration
413ecd1023f2.sentence: However, when accounting for losses in the herbaceous layer and changes in soil organic carbon (SOC), the quantification of terrestrial carbon pools and associated fluxes becomes significantly more complex and highly context-dependent.

f40edcb5d52e.title: Woody plant encroachment
f40edcb5d52e.section: Ecological and socio-economic impacts > Carbon sequestration
f40edcb5d52e.sentence: Several studies have found that gains in above-ground carbon during encroachment can be entirely offset by losses in below-ground carbon.

a0ab9bd2607f.title: Woody plant encroachment
a0ab9bd2607f.section: Ecological and socio-economic impacts > Carbon sequestration
a0ab9bd2607f.sentence: The impact of woody encroachment on soil organic carbon is found to be dependent on rainfall, with soil organic carbon increasing in dry ecosystems and decreasing in mesic ecosystems under encroachment.

d6e2d69ef054.title: Woody plant encroachment
d6e2d69ef054.section: Ecological and socio-economic impacts > Carbon sequestration
d6e2d69ef054.sentence: In tropical savanna soils, most soil organic carbon is derived from grass, not woody plants.

70095c194275.title: Woody plant encroachment
70095c194275.section: Ecological and socio-economic impacts > Carbon sequestration
70095c194275.sentence: A meta-analysis of 142 studies found that shrub encroachment alters soil organic carbon (0–50 cm), with changes ranging between -50 and 300 percent.

848dd36f40e8.title: Woody plant encroachment
848dd36f40e8.section: Ecological and socio-economic impacts > Carbon sequestration
848dd36f40e8.sentence: Soil organic carbon increased under the following conditions: semi-arid and humid regions, encroachment by leguminous shrubs as opposed to non-legumes, sandy soils as opposed to clay soils.

b198c74b14ce.title: Woody plant encroachment
b198c74b14ce.section: Ecological and socio-economic impacts > Carbon sequestration
b198c74b14ce.sentence: An important factor is that rooting depth increases with woody encroachment, on average by 38 cm and up to 65 cm.

98449b1200bb.title: Woody plant encroachment
98449b1200bb.section: Ecological and socio-economic impacts > Groundwater recharge and soil moisture
98449b1200bb.sentence: Woody plant encroachment is frequently linked to reduced groundwater recharge, based on evidence that bushes consume significantly more rainwater than grasses and encroachment alters water streamflow.

2723843f2f16.title: Woody plant encroachment
2723843f2f16.section: Ecological and socio-economic impacts > Groundwater recharge and soil moisture
2723843f2f16.sentence: Besides groundwater recharge, woody encroachment increases tree transpiration and evaporation of soil moisture, due to increased canopy cover.

9d536ba496e6.title: Woody plant encroachment
9d536ba496e6.section: Ecological and socio-economic impacts > Groundwater recharge and soil moisture
9d536ba496e6.sentence: Woody plant encroachment can accelerate soil drought through enhanced soil porosity.

70d7e79cb92f.title: Woody plant encroachment
70d7e79cb92f.section: Ecological and socio-economic impacts > Groundwater recharge and soil moisture
70d7e79cb92f.sentence: Studies in South Africa have shown that approximately 44% of rainfall is captured by woody canopies and evaporated back into the atmosphere under woody encroachment.

e906a8cd688b.title: Woody plant encroachment
e906a8cd688b.section: Ecological and socio-economic impacts > Groundwater recharge and soil moisture
e906a8cd688b.sentence: It was found that up to 10% less rain enters the soil overall under woody encroachment.

b07eff07ab93.title: Woody plant encroachment
b07eff07ab93.section: Ecological and socio-economic impacts > Groundwater recharge and soil moisture
b07eff07ab93.sentence: In arid and semi-arid environments, woody encroachment has been shown to reduce stream flows.

3889d05649e8.title: Woody plant encroachment
3889d05649e8.section: Ecological and socio-economic impacts > Groundwater recharge and soil moisture
3889d05649e8.sentence: Further, woody plant control can effectively improve the connectivity of water resources.

6a49536aed72.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/06%3A_Soil_Degradation-_Erosion_Compaction_and_Contamination/6.03%3A_Soil_Tilth_and_Compaction
6a49536aed72.sentence: Shallow compaction, which is compaction of the surface layer or plow layer, occurs to some extent in all intensively worked agricultural soils.

e91e54e483a6.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/06%3A_Soil_Degradation-_Erosion_Compaction_and_Contamination/6.03%3A_Soil_Tilth_and_Compaction
e91e54e483a6.sentence: It is the result of a loss of soil aggregation that typically has three primary causes: erosion, reduced organic matter levels and forces exerted by the weight of field equipment.

86d10118f76c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/06%3A_Soil_Degradation-_Erosion_Compaction_and_Contamination/6.03%3A_Soil_Tilth_and_Compaction
86d10118f76c.sentence: The first two result in reduced supplies of sticky binding materials and a subsequent loss of aggregation.

e8fae5525673.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/06%3A_Soil_Degradation-_Erosion_Compaction_and_Contamination/6.03%3A_Soil_Tilth_and_Compaction
e8fae5525673.sentence: When a soil is wetter than the plastic limit, it may become seriously compacted if tilled or trafficked because soil aggregates are pushed together into a smeared, dense mass.

e00d7d7ae730.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/06%3A_Soil_Degradation-_Erosion_Compaction_and_Contamination/6.03%3A_Soil_Tilth_and_Compaction
e00d7d7ae730.sentence: This may be observed when you see shiny, cloddy furrows or deep tire ruts in a field (Figure 6.10).

b994b3bfd674.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/06%3A_Soil_Degradation-_Erosion_Compaction_and_Contamination/6.03%3A_Soil_Tilth_and_Compaction
b994b3bfd674.sentence: The soil is more resistant to deformation when the soil is friable (the water content is below the plastic limit).

01ebb05c5957.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/06%3A_Soil_Degradation-_Erosion_Compaction_and_Contamination/6.03%3A_Soil_Tilth_and_Compaction
01ebb05c5957.sentence: It crumbles when tilled and aggregates resist compaction by field traffic.

505869ebc89e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/06%3A_Soil_Degradation-_Erosion_Compaction_and_Contamination/6.03%3A_Soil_Tilth_and_Compaction
505869ebc89e.sentence: For example, as coarse-textured sandy soils drain, they rapidly change from being plastic to being friable.

d192d72201a5.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/06%3A_Soil_Degradation-_Erosion_Compaction_and_Contamination/6.03%3A_Soil_Tilth_and_Compaction
d192d72201a5.sentence: Fine-textured loams and clays need longer drying periods to lose enough water to become friable.

3b6645567fac.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/06%3A_Soil_Degradation-_Erosion_Compaction_and_Contamination/6.03%3A_Soil_Tilth_and_Compaction
3b6645567fac.sentence: Similarly, when soils are frozen and the soil particles are fused by ice, the soil becomes solid and resistant to compaction.

7f15e529fa36.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/06%3A_Soil_Degradation-_Erosion_Compaction_and_Contamination/6.03%3A_Soil_Tilth_and_Compaction
7f15e529fa36.sentence: The energy of raindrops disperses wet aggregates, pounding them apart so that particles settle into a thin, dense layer.

9e2b8026b9c6.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/06%3A_Soil_Degradation-_Erosion_Compaction_and_Contamination/6.03%3A_Soil_Tilth_and_Compaction
9e2b8026b9c6.sentence: The sealing of the soil reduces water infiltration, and the surface forms a hard crust when dried.

518b44e94f8d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/06%3A_Soil_Degradation-_Erosion_Compaction_and_Contamination/6.03%3A_Soil_Tilth_and_Compaction
518b44e94f8d.sentence: Crusting generally occurs after tillage and planting when the soil is unprotected, and it can delay or prevent seedling emergence.

dafd3e112359.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/06%3A_Soil_Degradation-_Erosion_Compaction_and_Contamination/6.03%3A_Soil_Tilth_and_Compaction
dafd3e112359.sentence: You can reduce surface crusting by leaving more residue on the surface and by maintaining strong soil aggregation.

27d20f716bb3.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/06%3A_Soil_Degradation-_Erosion_Compaction_and_Contamination/6.03%3A_Soil_Tilth_and_Compaction
27d20f716bb3.sentence: Tillage operations often become part of a vicious cycle in which a compacted soil tills up very cloddy (Figure 6.11a) and then requires extensive secondary tillage and packing trips to create a satisfactory seedbed (Figure 6.11b).

7ed02f55fa1d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/06%3A_Soil_Degradation-_Erosion_Compaction_and_Contamination/6.03%3A_Soil_Tilth_and_Compaction
7ed02f55fa1d.sentence: Natural aggregates break down, and organic matter decomposes in the process—contributing to more compaction in the future.

db3d849cdc36.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/06%3A_Soil_Degradation-_Erosion_Compaction_and_Contamination/6.03%3A_Soil_Tilth_and_Compaction
db3d849cdc36.sentence: Subsoil compaction occurs deeper in the soil and is sometimes referred to as a plow pan, although it is commonly caused by more than just plowing.

fb8f3e5b88b1.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/06%3A_Soil_Degradation-_Erosion_Compaction_and_Contamination/6.03%3A_Soil_Tilth_and_Compaction
fb8f3e5b88b1.sentence: Subsoil is prone to compaction because it is usually wetter, denser, higher in clay content, lower in organic matter, and less aggregated than topsoil.

94472b5b86d9.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/06%3A_Soil_Degradation-_Erosion_Compaction_and_Contamination/6.03%3A_Soil_Tilth_and_Compaction
94472b5b86d9.sentence: Also, subsoil is not loosened by regular tillage and cannot easily be amended with additions of organic materials.

6adf7e76faaf.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/06%3A_Soil_Degradation-_Erosion_Compaction_and_Contamination/6.03%3A_Soil_Tilth_and_Compaction
6adf7e76faaf.sentence: Another challenge is that the subsoil is by definition buried and therefore compaction is invisible unless you dig down or push a rod into the soil.Subsoil compaction occurs when farmers run heavy vehicles, especially those with poor weight distribution.

0c6bc140bef2.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/06%3A_Soil_Degradation-_Erosion_Compaction_and_Contamination/6.03%3A_Soil_Tilth_and_Compaction
0c6bc140bef2.sentence: The load exerted on the surface is transferred into the soil along a cone-shaped pattern (Figure 6.12).

ccc453217d2a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/06%3A_Soil_Degradation-_Erosion_Compaction_and_Contamination/6.03%3A_Soil_Tilth_and_Compaction
ccc453217d2a.sentence: With increasing depth, the compaction force is distributed over a larger area, thereby reducing the pressure in deeper layers.

6e77a04be054.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/06%3A_Soil_Degradation-_Erosion_Compaction_and_Contamination/6.03%3A_Soil_Tilth_and_Compaction
6e77a04be054.sentence: When the loading force at the surface is small, say through foot or hoof traffic or a light tractor, the pressure exerted deep in the soil is minimal.

c8bfe81a085e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/06%3A_Soil_Degradation-_Erosion_Compaction_and_Contamination/6.03%3A_Soil_Tilth_and_Compaction
c8bfe81a085e.sentence: But when the load is high from heavy equipment, like with a heavy manure spreader or combine, the pressures at depth are sufficient to cause considerable soil compaction.

0bbc1db6a604.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/06%3A_Soil_Degradation-_Erosion_Compaction_and_Contamination/6.03%3A_Soil_Tilth_and_Compaction
0bbc1db6a604.sentence: When the soil is wet, the force causing compaction near the surface is more easily transferred to the subsoil, which causes even more compaction damage.

98f44b802dbc.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/06%3A_Soil_Degradation-_Erosion_Compaction_and_Contamination/6.03%3A_Soil_Tilth_and_Compaction
98f44b802dbc.sentence: Plows cause compaction because the weight of the plow plus the lifting of the furrow slices results in high downward forces from the plow share (bottom) onto the soil layer immediately underneath.

4f80b8b2a456.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/06%3A_Soil_Degradation-_Erosion_Compaction_and_Contamination/6.03%3A_Soil_Tilth_and_Compaction
4f80b8b2a456.sentence: Disks also have much of their weight concentrated at the bottom of the disk and can cause shallow pans.

7bc764a1e481.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/06%3A_Soil_Degradation-_Erosion_Compaction_and_Contamination/6.03%3A_Soil_Tilth_and_Compaction
7bc764a1e481.sentence: Subsoil compaction may also occur during moldboard plowing when a set of tractor wheels is placed in the open furrow, thereby applying wheel pressure directly to the soil below the plow layer.

9a9c6d3c12ed.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/06%3A_Soil_Degradation-_Erosion_Compaction_and_Contamination/6.03%3A_Soil_Tilth_and_Compaction
9a9c6d3c12ed.sentence: Overall, these pans are very common in soil that has been plowed, sometimes even many years after the field was converted to no-till.

24c078ad1b86.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/06%3A_Soil_Degradation-_Erosion_Compaction_and_Contamination/6.03%3A_Soil_Tilth_and_Compaction
24c078ad1b86.sentence: To be sure that a soil is ready for equipment use, you can do the simple “ball test” by taking a handful of soil from the lower part of the plow layer and trying to make a ball out of it.

fd160d1d6787.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/06%3A_Soil_Degradation-_Erosion_Compaction_and_Contamination/6.03%3A_Soil_Tilth_and_Compaction
fd160d1d6787.sentence: If it molds easily and sticks together, the soil is too wet.

b2794d0f6959.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/06%3A_Soil_Degradation-_Erosion_Compaction_and_Contamination/6.03%3A_Soil_Tilth_and_Compaction
b2794d0f6959.sentence: If it crumbles readily, it is sufficiently dry for tillage or heavy traffic.

2a5947124d74.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/15%3A_Addressing_Compaction/15.02%3A_Diagnosing_Different_Types_of_Compaction
2a5947124d74.sentence: When soil aggregates become weaker from loss of the organic matter, silt and clay particles can wash down and settle in the subsoil pores, thereby creating a dense layer.

f575503a5d45.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/15%3A_Addressing_Compaction/15.02%3A_Diagnosing_Different_Types_of_Compaction
f575503a5d45.sentence: This is especially a concern with soils that contain about equal amounts of sand, silt and clay, and where the clay minerals are of the non-swelling 1:1 type.

b5f572a8d528.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/15%3A_Addressing_Compaction/15.02%3A_Diagnosing_Different_Types_of_Compaction
b5f572a8d528.sentence: Also, tropical oxisols have naturally high clay contents with very strong aggregates, but when they are limed, the raised pH causes the clay particles to disperse and wash into pores in the lower soil.

a37d27ca42b4.title: Grassland degradation
a37d27ca42b4.sentence: There are three main degrees of degraded grassland: light, moderate, and high.

3c1f6a2b5bb4.title: Grassland degradation
3c1f6a2b5bb4.sentence: These stages are sequential so no grassland can be highly degraded without first being lightly and moderately degraded and so forth.

1da4fe74d4e7.title: Grassland degradation
1da4fe74d4e7.sentence: Lightly degraded grassland is the least potent of the three and is characterized by patches of dead or no grass, spottily dispersed throughout the land.

261ce3284007.title: Grassland degradation
261ce3284007.sentence: Plant and animal diversity starts to lessen but becomes really apparent in moderately degraded grasslands, in which patches of dead grass increase in size and number.

bcf6cccb068b.title: Grassland degradation
bcf6cccb068b.sentence: Also during this stage, pests, be they rats, insects, or other grassland animals, start to disturb the environment by damaging the soil through, for instance, extracting from the soil nutrients vital to a plant's well-being or by just damaging to plants themselves.

0b4d304ffe8a.title: Grassland degradation
0b4d304ffe8a.sentence: The grasslands that are affected the worst are highly degraded, which can be recognized by the vast expanse of dead grass.

40a2eacf64b1.title: Grassland degradation
40a2eacf64b1.sentence: This quality makes this land neither arable nor suitable for livestock.

35108b484b9c.title: Grassland degradation
35108b484b9c.sentence: Hence, it makes sense that the animal and plant diversity is extremely low.

b96d385ec31f.title: Grassland degradation
b96d385ec31f.sentence: The few plants that do inhabit this area are quite poisonous and ward off any animals or plants potentially trying to move back in.

8ad2879a4c6a.title: Grassland degradation
8ad2879a4c6a.sentence: Heitutan is a term that signifies severely degraded grasslands.

6c57811dd3b5.title: Grassland degradation
6c57811dd3b5.sentence: A more common and more extreme term to describe degraded grassland is "black beach" or "black-soil-land", which is exactly what it sounds like: land with nothing but black, unusable soil that extends 10–15 cm below the ground level.

e53ff36f09f1.title: Grassland degradation
e53ff36f09f1.sentence: Also, there are certain ways that degraded land should be counteracted, depending upon its severity.

7295581b470a.title: Grassland degradation
7295581b470a.sentence: In general, it takes time for implanted methods to restore degraded grassland fully.

261aca31ee96.title: Grassland degradation
261aca31ee96.sentence: Successful grassland restoration has several dimensions, including recognition in policy, standardisation of indicators of degradation, scientific innovation, knowledge transfer and data sharing.

fb79b5726468.title: Grassland degradation
fb79b5726468.sentence: The earlier the problem is addressed, the easier it is to restore that plot of land.

15fc438bc2ef.title: Grassland degradation
15fc438bc2ef.sentence: For an area that is lightly degraded, fencing, fertilizing, or weeding.

fcca3f47a343.title: Grassland degradation
fcca3f47a343.sentence: Fencing an area off allows for that plot of land to be reprieved from grazing until it reaches its normal, healthy state, in which no more patches of dead grass exist.

2fa7aa5f9927.title: Grassland degradation
2fa7aa5f9927.sentence: In some cases, grazing can even be continued as long as its intensity is decreased and the situation is monitored.

c6c3c623b962.title: Grassland degradation
c6c3c623b962.sentence: For instance, a method as simple as seasonally rotating fields in which animals graze have been see as effective.

1ccca125bba1.title: Grassland degradation
1ccca125bba1.sentence: More structured efforts must be put into place to combat moderately degraded grasslands.

ad9e4754f610.title: Grassland degradation
ad9e4754f610.sentence: These actions include reseeding and rodent control, whose goal is not to extinguish that population but rather to manage it so that it does not further degrade the land.

29bfdf447fdf.title: Grassland degradation
29bfdf447fdf.sentence: Active brush control can serve to restore areas affected by woody plant encroachment.

d247dd76abfe.title: Grassland degradation
d247dd76abfe.sentence: As for highly degraded plots of land, planting semi-artificial grassland is the umbrella term that is used to address this type of restoration.

bd08ea599109.title: Grassland degradation
bd08ea599109.sentence: It includes weed control, fertilizing, reseeding, rodent control, and scarification.

1479d5623862.title: Grassland degradation
1479d5623862.sentence: Semi-artificial grassland works best when the highly degraded land has 30% or more plant coverage.

104eef1c19ba.title: Grassland degradation
104eef1c19ba.sentence: For degraded plots that are worse off, and hence typically fall under the category of black soil or severely degraded Heitutan grassland, artificial grassland is required and entails weed and rodent control, plowing, seeding, and fertilizing.

2efecace0a3d.title: Grassland degradation
2efecace0a3d.sentence: An increase in small animal populations has led to some grassland being degraded.

923944093505.title: Grassland degradation
923944093505.sentence: These animals include the Himalayan marmots, the Brandt's and plateau vole, and the plateau pika and zokor.

90e160946994.title: Grassland degradation
90e160946994.sentence: They damage this environment mainly through their burrowing into the ground and gnawing at the grass and other plants.

ac1daee7583b.title: Grassland degradation
ac1daee7583b.sentence: Both of these actions encourage soil erosion and make it more difficult for plants to firmly ground themselves to this poor terrain.

4f4d9d3b9700.title: Grassland degradation
4f4d9d3b9700.sentence: Hence, grass has a tougher time growing, and the terrain becomes spottily doused with grass.

d39996f71405.title: Grassland degradation
d39996f71405.sentence: However, some do not think these animals contribute to grassland degradation.

3ff4ecc021d7.title: Grassland degradation
3ff4ecc021d7.sentence: They claim that such burrowing aids in the recycling of nutrients in the soil and that the rise in population is only normal since grazing levels in these areas have also risen.

37fab7861f7f.title: Grassland degradation
37fab7861f7f.sentence: Rodent control can be in the form of either shooting, sterilizing, or poisoning the rodents.

94ea2d36da38.title: Grassland degradation
94ea2d36da38.sentence: The administered poison must have a low toxicity so that it does not cause further damage to other animals or plants; a popular toxin that has worked well is Botulin toxin C.

e6ce09b5376a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/06%3A_Soil_Degradation-_Erosion_Compaction_and_Contamination/6.05%3A_The_Water_Range_for_Best_Plant_Growth
e6ce09b5376a.sentence: The limitations to plant growth caused by compaction and water extremes can be combined into the concept of the optimum water range for plant growth: the range of water contents under which plant growth is not reduced by drought, mechanical stress or lack of aeration (Figure 6.15).

ea3ed98b8419.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/06%3A_Soil_Degradation-_Erosion_Compaction_and_Contamination/6.05%3A_The_Water_Range_for_Best_Plant_Growth
ea3ed98b8419.sentence: This range, referred to by scientists as the least-limiting water range, is bounded on two sides: when the soil is too wet and when it’s too dry.

9cab8c1e065d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/06%3A_Soil_Degradation-_Erosion_Compaction_and_Contamination/6.05%3A_The_Water_Range_for_Best_Plant_Growth
9cab8c1e065d.sentence: The optimum water range in a well-structured soil has its field capacity on the wet end, as water above that moisture content is quickly drained out by gravity.

f153db4a449b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/06%3A_Soil_Degradation-_Erosion_Compaction_and_Contamination/6.05%3A_The_Water_Range_for_Best_Plant_Growth
f153db4a449b.sentence: On the dry end is the wilting point, beyond which the soil holds water too tightly to be used by plants.

cf34652e1dfc.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/06%3A_Soil_Degradation-_Erosion_Compaction_and_Contamination/6.05%3A_The_Water_Range_for_Best_Plant_Growth
cf34652e1dfc.sentence: However, the soil water range for best growth in a compacted soil is much narrower.

0198945debdc.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/06%3A_Soil_Degradation-_Erosion_Compaction_and_Contamination/6.05%3A_The_Water_Range_for_Best_Plant_Growth
0198945debdc.sentence: Even after a severely compacted soil drains to field capacity, it is still too wet because it lacks large pores and is thus poorly aerated.

2239572114ac.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/06%3A_Soil_Degradation-_Erosion_Compaction_and_Contamination/6.05%3A_The_Water_Range_for_Best_Plant_Growth
2239572114ac.sentence: Good aeration requires at least 20% of the pore space (about 10% of the volume of the whole soil) to be air filled.

708956736bae.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/06%3A_Soil_Degradation-_Erosion_Compaction_and_Contamination/6.05%3A_The_Water_Range_for_Best_Plant_Growth
708956736bae.sentence: On the dry end, plant growth in a compacted soil is commonly limited by soil hardness rather than by lack of available water.

d981012a2fcd.title: Nonlimiting water range
d981012a2fcd.sentence: John Letey (1985) from UC Riverside introduced the NLWR concept in an attempt to integrate several physical properties associated with plant or root growth to refine the concept of available water capacity.

06e37a0c922b.title: Nonlimiting water range
06e37a0c922b.sentence: Alvaro Pires da Silva, Bev Kay, and Ed Perfect (University of Guelph, Ontario) (1994) refined the concept and termed it least limiting water range (LLWR).

0157ad4f072c.title: Woody plant encroachment
0157ad4f072c.sentence: This applies to cases of land abandonment, for example when previous agricultural land is abandoned and woody plants re-establish.

174d4fa12a46.title: Land degradation
174d4fa12a46.sentence: Threshold effects associated with land degradation may lead to land abandonment in areas with a long history of intensive agricultural systems.

4fe44c798a30.title: Woody plant encroachment
4fe44c798a30.sentence: Conversely, land abandonment can likewise lead to woody encroachment.

dde613f6406c.title: Effects of climate change on agriculture
dde613f6406c.sentence: Also farmland values are projected to decrease in parts of southern Europe by more than 80% by 2100, which could result in land abandonment.

508429b80954.title: Land degradation
508429b80954.section: Prevention and reversal > Prevention > Sustainable land management
508429b80954.sentence: The United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 15 has a target to restore degraded land and soil and achieve a land degradation-neutral world by 2030.

d98ceaae5995.title: Land degradation
d98ceaae5995.section: Prevention and reversal > Prevention > Sustainable land management
d98ceaae5995.sentence: The full title of Target 15.3 is: "By 2030, combat desertification, restore degraded land and soil, including land affected by desertification, drought and floods, and strive to achieve a land degradation-neutral world."

9213116a46d8.title: Land degradation
9213116a46d8.section: Causes > Climate change and land degradation
9213116a46d8.sentence: Launched at UNCCD COP 13 in 2017, the LDN Fund invests in projects that generate environmental benefits, socio-economic benefits, and financial returns for investors.

66bebcec93f2.title: Land degradation
66bebcec93f2.section: Causes > Climate change and land degradation
66bebcec93f2.sentence: The Fund was initially capitalized at US$100 million and is expected to grow to US$300 million.

8e427fdb5c28.title: Land degradation
8e427fdb5c28.section: Causes > Climate change and land degradation
8e427fdb5c28.sentence: In 2009 the European Investment Bank agreed to invest up to $45 million in the Land Degradation Neutrality Fund (LDN Fund).

0fa9d241ed78.title: Rain garden
0fa9d241ed78.sentence: Rain gardens, also called bioretention facilities, are one of a variety of practices designed to increase reabsorption of rain runoff by the soil.

be12a4039d13.title: Rain garden
be12a4039d13.sentence: Rain gardens are designed landscape sites that reduce the flow rate, total quantity, and pollutant load of runoff from impervious urban areas like roofs, driveways, walkways, parking lots, and compacted lawn areas.

e3828d7c4942.title: Rain garden
e3828d7c4942.sentence: Rain gardens rely on plants and natural or engineered soil medium to retain stormwater and increase the lag time of infiltration, while remediating and filtering pollutants carried by urban runoff.

eaac9091b94a.title: Rain garden
eaac9091b94a.sentence: Deep plant roots also create additional channels for stormwater to filter into the ground.

fa170d16ea98.title: Rain garden
fa170d16ea98.sentence: Root systems enhance infiltration, maintain or even augment soil permeability, provide moisture redistribution, and sustain diverse microbial populations involved in biofiltration.

efef68486fad.title: Rain garden
efef68486fad.sentence: Microbes help to break down organic compounds (including some pollutants) and remove nitrogen.

1003199eb1ff.title: Rain garden
1003199eb1ff.sentence: Stormwater quality can be controlled by bioretention through settling, filtration, assimilation, adsorption, degradation, and decomposition.

644b5887c4a2.title: Rain garden
644b5887c4a2.sentence: Dissolved chemical substances from the water also bind to the surfaces of plant roots, soil particles, and other organic matter in the substrate and are rendered ineffective.

7d73059b9ffc.title: Rain garden
7d73059b9ffc.sentence: Soil microorganisms break down remaining chemicals and small organic matter and effectively decompose the pollutants into a saturated soil matter.

44aa239d4fc5.title: Rain garden
44aa239d4fc5.section: Purpose > Pollutant removal > Pollutant Removal Performance
44aa239d4fc5.sentence: According to data from the International Stormwater BMP Database, typical removal rates for rain gardens include 80% for total suspended solids (TSS), 50–60% for heavy metals, and significant reductions in nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus.

9c3891968a6b.title: Rain garden
9c3891968a6b.section: Purpose > Pollutant removal > Pollutant Removal Performance
9c3891968a6b.sentence: A 2025 meta-analysis of field studies reported average reductions in total nitrogen and total phosphorus loads of approximately 55% and 62%, respectively, in bioretention systems.

d2d55fed8cb1.title: Rain garden
d2d55fed8cb1.sentence: While rain gardens always allow for restored groundwater recharge, and reduced stormwater volumes, they may not improve pollution unless remediation materials are included in the design of the filtration layers.

400fef54a4d1.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/22%3A_Soils_for_Urban_Farms_Gardens_and_Green_Spaces/22.03%3A_Testing_for_Soil_Contaminants
400fef54a4d1.sentence: When evaluating a plot of land for its suitability for urban farming or gardening, the first step is to research its history.

2be1a1ea81a1.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/22%3A_Soils_for_Urban_Farms_Gardens_and_Green_Spaces/22.03%3A_Testing_for_Soil_Contaminants
2be1a1ea81a1.sentence: Try talking to the property owner, and use the internet, public library, city hall or tax assessor’s office to seek records that would reveal past uses.

ac54fe026ab5.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/22%3A_Soils_for_Urban_Farms_Gardens_and_Green_Spaces/22.03%3A_Testing_for_Soil_Contaminants
ac54fe026ab5.sentence: Useful records include old aerial photos, maps, permits and tax records.

865163661387.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/22%3A_Soils_for_Urban_Farms_Gardens_and_Green_Spaces/22.03%3A_Testing_for_Soil_Contaminants
865163661387.sentence: Also, visit the site to see whether potential sources of contamination are nearby, such as old houses with peeling paint or a highway.

c703d8f8bdf2.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/22%3A_Soils_for_Urban_Farms_Gardens_and_Green_Spaces/22.03%3A_Testing_for_Soil_Contaminants
c703d8f8bdf2.sentence: Generally, a site that has a long history as a green space or residential property will have fewer problems than one with a commercial or industrial past (Table 22.1).

4e68be0c91b9.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/22%3A_Soils_for_Urban_Farms_Gardens_and_Green_Spaces/22.03%3A_Testing_for_Soil_Contaminants
4e68be0c91b9.sentence: Also, while there are interim guidelines published by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA, Brownfields and Urban Agriculture: Interim Guidelines for Safe Gardening Practices, 2011), there are no established federal rules for what soil contaminant levels are considered safe for urban agriculture, so you should work with these qualified professionals to interpret the results of tests and make a plan to recondition the soil.

f5e3430f44d3.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/22%3A_Soils_for_Urban_Farms_Gardens_and_Green_Spaces/22.03%3A_Testing_for_Soil_Contaminants
f5e3430f44d3.sentence: At a minimum, the EPA recommends that urban soils be tested for pH, percent organic matter, nutrients, micronutrients and metals, including lead.

8ee2bfe6a81e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/22%3A_Soils_for_Urban_Farms_Gardens_and_Green_Spaces/22.03%3A_Testing_for_Soil_Contaminants
8ee2bfe6a81e.sentence: When testing for potential contaminants, you may need to collect samples separately for each contaminant you want to test for, and your sampling procedure for each may vary.

5c1fd39e3a43.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/22%3A_Soils_for_Urban_Farms_Gardens_and_Green_Spaces/22.03%3A_Testing_for_Soil_Contaminants
5c1fd39e3a43.sentence: For example, you may collect samples at different depths depending on the suspected contaminant (a heavy metal near the surface versus a solvent that may have leached into the soil), or the intended use of different sections of the property (a play area versus a growing area).

867f0e023196.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/22%3A_Soils_for_Urban_Farms_Gardens_and_Green_Spaces/22.03%3A_Testing_for_Soil_Contaminants
867f0e023196.sentence: The distribution of contaminants can be unpredictable, so testing in many locations in the plot may be required.

bf7705780e6f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/22%3A_Soils_for_Urban_Farms_Gardens_and_Green_Spaces/22.03%3A_Testing_for_Soil_Contaminants
bf7705780e6f.sentence: These can include areas next to old buildings with peeling paint (a higher risk of lead), patches of bare ground where vegetation would otherwise be expected (a sign of compaction or concentrations of toxic compounds), or near stormwater drainage features (which could be bringing petroleum-based compounds, pesticides or other chemicals onto the property from the surrounding neighborhood).

21d46361bac6.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/22%3A_Soils_for_Urban_Farms_Gardens_and_Green_Spaces/22.03%3A_Testing_for_Soil_Contaminants
21d46361bac6.sentence: Note that the presence of lead in the soil rarely causes physical damage to plants.

4621da6e4b91.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/22%3A_Soils_for_Urban_Farms_Gardens_and_Green_Spaces/22.03%3A_Testing_for_Soil_Contaminants
4621da6e4b91.sentence: On the other hand, other metals, such as copper, zinc and nickel can be phytotoxic at high concentrations.

88ad69db94c6.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/22%3A_Soils_for_Urban_Farms_Gardens_and_Green_Spaces/22.03%3A_Testing_for_Soil_Contaminants
88ad69db94c6.sentence: A thorough site assessment of a property should also take into account other conditions that could affect its viability for urban farming or gardening, such as slope and drainage patterns, the presence of aboveground and belowground utility lines, or existing unwanted structures, including possibly the buried foundations of previous buildings.

49fb7a1c4294.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/22%3A_Soils_for_Urban_Farms_Gardens_and_Green_Spaces/22.02%3A_Common_Challenges_with_Urban_Soils
49fb7a1c4294.sentence: Soil contamination is much more prevalent in urban areas than in agricultural ones.

f3dd9536d30b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/22%3A_Soils_for_Urban_Farms_Gardens_and_Green_Spaces/22.02%3A_Common_Challenges_with_Urban_Soils
f3dd9536d30b.sentence: In urban soils, lead is the most common contaminant to pay attention to.

307c6ed17559.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/22%3A_Soils_for_Urban_Farms_Gardens_and_Green_Spaces/22.02%3A_Common_Challenges_with_Urban_Soils
307c6ed17559.sentence: It is prevalent due to its long-time use in gasoline (banned since 1989 in the United States) and paint (banned since 1978 for residential use).

0e581da081df.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/22%3A_Soils_for_Urban_Farms_Gardens_and_Green_Spaces/22.02%3A_Common_Challenges_with_Urban_Soils
0e581da081df.sentence: But there is a wide range of other contaminants from current and past land uses that could pose problems, such as petroleum products and legacy pesticides (lead arsenate, copper sulfate, etc.) (Table 22.1).

586e492c917c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/22%3A_Soils_for_Urban_Farms_Gardens_and_Green_Spaces/22.02%3A_Common_Challenges_with_Urban_Soils
586e492c917c.sentence: Cases that are of special concerns include former industrial sites, areas along major roads, recent construction sites, waste disposal sites and junkyards.

404a50c986a0.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/22%3A_Soils_for_Urban_Farms_Gardens_and_Green_Spaces/22.02%3A_Common_Challenges_with_Urban_Soils
404a50c986a0.sentence: In some cases, contaminants can end up on a property from distant sources through atmospheric deposition (the process by which particles and gases in the air, such as those that come from tailpipe emissions, settle on the ground or in bodies of water).

8c13b915ce5a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/22%3A_Soils_for_Urban_Farms_Gardens_and_Green_Spaces/22.02%3A_Common_Challenges_with_Urban_Soils
8c13b915ce5a.sentence: People are exposed to soil contaminants through different possible pathways:

1faccd272b4d.sentence: The risk is greatest when the soil is left bare, especially with chemicals that are concentrated at the soil surface.

38dec61a3c3b.sentence: In urban situations, the strategies outlined here should generally be considered and used in that order, from physical to chemical to biological.

286186db81b4.title: Soil health
286186db81b4.sentence: Specific benchmarks used to evaluate soil health include CO2 release, humus levels, microbial activity, and available calcium.

89d50e9b2453.title: Ecosystem service
89d50e9b2453.sentence: Ecosystem services are the various benefits that humans derive from ecosystems.

88f2ada77f6d.title: Ecosystem service
88f2ada77f6d.sentence: The interconnected living and non-living components of the natural environment offer benefits such as pollination of crops, clean air and water, decomposition of wastes, and flood control.

0cc76a1c0a64.title: Ecosystem service
0cc76a1c0a64.sentence: Ecosystem services are grouped into categories of services, which was popularized in the early 2000s by the Millennium Ecosystem Assessment (MA) initiative by the United Nations.

67caa13cd24f.title: Ecosystem service
67caa13cd24f.sentence: These are provisioning services, such as the production of food and water; regulating services, such as the control of climate and disease; supporting services, such as nutrient cycles and oxygen production; and cultural services, such as recreation, tourism, and spiritual gratification.

0b135b429253.title: Ecosystem service
0b135b429253.sentence: Supporting services include for example nutrient cycling, primary production, soil formation, habitat provision.

dbe5e18775af.title: Ecosystem service
dbe5e18775af.sentence: These services make it possible for the ecosystems to continue providing services such as food supply, flood regulation, and water purification.

4529018a72f6.title: Ecosystem service
4529018a72f6.sentence: In fact, some services directly affect the livelihood of neighboring human populations (such as fresh water, food or aesthetic value, etc.) while other services affect general environmental conditions by which humans are indirectly impacted (such as climate change, erosion regulation or natural hazard regulation, etc.).

b3fd94c7500b.title: Ecosystem service
b3fd94c7500b.sentence: An example for water purification as an ecosystem service is as follows: In New York City, where the quality of drinking water had fallen below standards required by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), authorities opted to restore the polluted Catskill Watershed that had previously provided the city with the ecosystem service of water purification.

c2b5d8bebd05.title: Ecosystem service
c2b5d8bebd05.sentence: Once the input of sewage and pesticides to the watershed area was reduced, natural abiotic processes such as soil absorption and filtration of chemicals, together with biotic recycling via root systems and soil microorganisms, water quality improved to levels that met government standards.

fd9121d14849.title: Ecosystem service
fd9121d14849.sentence: The cost of this investment in natural capital was estimated at $1–1.5 billion, which contrasted dramatically with the estimated $6–8 billion cost of constructing a water filtration plant plus the $300 million annual running costs.

bcd26e2c1c51.title: Ecosystem service
bcd26e2c1c51.sentence: Evaluations of ecosystem services may include assigning an economic value to them.

31addb4f3d9f.title: Environmental soil science
31addb4f3d9f.sentence: Environmental soil science is the study of the interaction of humans with the pedosphere as well as critical aspects of the biosphere, the lithosphere, the hydrosphere, and the atmosphere.

b2a739861068.title: Edaphology
b2a739861068.section: Areas of study > Environmental soil science
b2a739861068.sentence: Environmental soil science studies our interaction with the pedosphere on beyond crop production.

0955c825cc4b.title: Environmental soil science
0955c825cc4b.sentence: Environmental soil science addresses both the fundamental and applied aspects of the field including: buffers and surface water quality, vadose zone functions, septic drain field site assessment and function, land treatment of wastewater, stormwater, erosion control, soil contamination with metals and pesticides, remediation of contaminated soils, restoration of wetlands, soil degradation, nutrient management, movement of viruses and bacteria in soils and waters, bioremediation, application of molecular biology and genetic engineering to development of soil microbes that can degrade hazardous pollutants, land use, global warming, acid rain, and the study of anthropogenic soils, such as terra preta.

3539589898aa.title: Environmental soil science
3539589898aa.sentence: Much of the research done in environmental soil science is produced through the use of models.

34b27319e13d.title: Soil health
34b27319e13d.sentence: Soil health is the condition of the soil in a defined space and at a defined scale relative to a set of benchmarks that encompass healthy functioning.

6b3c368d82ef.title: Soil health
6b3c368d82ef.sentence: The definition of soil health may vary between users of the term as alternative users may place differing priorities upon the multiple functions of a soil.

cd1c7b1a5bf1.title: Soil health
cd1c7b1a5bf1.sentence: Therefore, the term soil health can only be understood within the context of the user of the term, and their aspirations of a soil, as well as by the boundary definition of the soil at issue.

0718a95f9f51.title: Soil health

aecf861ce005.title: Soil health

59856990c4e8.title: Soil health
59856990c4e8.sentence: Different soils will have different benchmarks of health depending on the "inherited" qualities, and on the geographic circumstance of the soil.

d52806efeea0.title: Soil health

f61a7f7e5401.sentence: No-till gardening seeks to minimise disturbance to the soil community so as to maintain soil structure and organic matter.

40a6ac009633.title: Permaculture
40a6ac009633.sentence: Keyline design is a technique for maximizing the beneficial use of water resources.

f741562cd29d.title: Permaculture
f741562cd29d.sentence: Vermicomposting is a common practice in permaculture.

7436a0a788d7.title: Permaculture
7436a0a788d7.sentence: Permaculture as a popular movement has been largely isolated from scientific literature, and has been criticised for a lack of clear definition or rigorous methodology.

ac237b703a01.title: Permaculture
ac237b703a01.sentence: This divide has led some to criticise permaculture as pseudo-scientific or to call for a more clear methodology to be used.

656c23b56efa.title: Permaculture
656c23b56efa.sentence: Despite a long divide, some 21st-century studies have supported the claims that permaculture improves soil quality and biodiversity, and have identified it as a social movement capable of promoting agroecological transition away from conventional agriculture.

6d9bc77f698c.title: Permaculture
6d9bc77f698c.sentence: In 2024, Reiff and colleagues stated that permaculture is a "sustainable alternative to conventional agriculture", and that it "strongly" enhances carbon stocks, soil quality, and biodiversity, making it "an effective tool to promote sustainable agriculture, ensure sustainable production patterns, combat climate change and halt and reverse land degradation and biodiversity loss." They point out that most of permaculture's most common methods, such as agroforestry, polycultures, and water harvesting features, are also backed by peer-reviewed research.

484da96f9129.title: Soil quality
484da96f9129.sentence: Soil quality is primarily measured by chemical, physical, and biological indicators because soil function cannot easily be measured directly.

a2b112d36fac.title: Soil quality
a2b112d36fac.sentence: The physical category of soil quality indicators consists of tests that measure soil texture, bulk density, porosity, water content at saturation, aggregate stability, penetration resistance, and more.

037126850b1c.title: Soil quality
037126850b1c.sentence: These measures provide hydrological information, such the level of water infiltration and water availability to plants.

a7b400c22be2.title: Soil quality
a7b400c22be2.sentence: Chemical indicators include pH and nutrient levels.

da8a2297c8c6.title: Soil quality
da8a2297c8c6.sentence: A typical soil test only evaluates chemical soil properties.

6080cee262d1.title: Soil quality
6080cee262d1.sentence: The movement and biological functions of soil organisms (including earthworms, millipedes, centipedes, ants, and spiders) impact soil processes such as the regulation of soil structure, degradation of contaminants, and nutrient cycling.

e6d2e73b3417.title: Soil quality
e6d2e73b3417.sentence: Soil quality can be evaluated using the Soil Management Assessment Framework.

aaad3c2471fd.title: Soil quality
aaad3c2471fd.sentence: Soil quality in agricultural terms is measured on a scale of soil value (Bodenwertzahl) in Germany.

966bb534be6d.title: Soil quality
966bb534be6d.sentence: There are very few soil quality monitoring systems that can provide near real-time information on these indicators but almost all of these systems are currently reported only at the research level.

0d0297ce4986.title: Soil regeneration
0d0297ce4986.sentence: Soil degradation is a decline in soil condition caused by poor management practices.

5be5e845721f.title: Soil regeneration
5be5e845721f.sentence: Soils can be degraded in four general ways:

e70fd4f6fc44.title: Soil regeneration
e70fd4f6fc44.sentence: - Erosion - soil is displaced as the result of water run-off of wind.

f3a1717b740b.title: Soil regeneration
f3a1717b740b.sentence: Typically this occurs when agricultural fields are left bare.

01c1f60178cb.title: Soil regeneration
01c1f60178cb.sentence: - Physical - the structure of the soil is changed in a way that inhibits the flow of water and air into the soil.

cc036435b5cb.title: Soil regeneration
cc036435b5cb.sentence: Compaction by large vehicles is typical form of physical degradation.

d0064ce51281.title: Soil regeneration
d0064ce51281.sentence: - Chemical - the soil becomes contaminated with pollutants such as heavy metals or hydrocarbons.

5fd05b3f0751.title: Soil regeneration
5fd05b3f0751.sentence: Acidification, salinization, nutrient leaching, and toxin contamination are a few types of chemical degradation.

b0e3e623a3ad.title: Soil regeneration
b0e3e623a3ad.sentence: Toxins can accumulate in the soil from industrial processes like mining and waste management.

d8d521be09a1.title: Soil regeneration
d8d521be09a1.sentence: - Biological - the loss of biological activity in the soil typically as a result of eutrophication, where the accumulation of fertilizer inhibits microorganisms that fix nitrogen.

037f238c47d9.title: Soil regeneration
037f238c47d9.sentence: Some biological examples include biodiversity loss, emitting greenhouse gasses, reduced carbon content, and a reduced capacity to sequester carbon.

66b5eae34558.title: Soil regeneration
66b5eae34558.sentence: One third of the globe's land has degraded soil, especially the tropics and subtropics with around 500 million hectares degraded.

6871ca46de3f.title: Soil regeneration
6871ca46de3f.sentence: Excessive or unnecessary tillage, particularly ploughing, is a common cause of degradation.

f1deb136c1d0.title: Soil regeneration
f1deb136c1d0.sentence: The upturning of soils makes them vulnerable to wind erosion.

8dc7c3c53a59.title: Soil regeneration
8dc7c3c53a59.sentence: The use of farm vehicles on soils can also cause soil compaction decreasing the permeability of soils to air and water.

1755b46bf743.title: Soil regeneration
1755b46bf743.sentence: The use of chemical fertilizer inhibits nitrogen fixing fungi and bacteria in the rhizosphere and increase activity of nitrogen oxidizing microbes, leading to an increase of nitrous oxide emissions from soil.

6d8b2241763b.title: Soil regeneration
6d8b2241763b.sentence: The effects of agricultural soil degradation can create a positive feedback loop.

4ef044fe7e7d.title: Soil regeneration
4ef044fe7e7d.sentence: For instance, the decrease of soil fertility as a result of mechanical degradation can be compensated with the use of chemical fertilizers, which decrease the rhizospehere's capacity to produce ammonia, which requires more fertilizer applications.

dd0acff5f983.title: Soil regeneration
dd0acff5f983.sentence: Overgrazing results in the loss of plant roots in soils, which reduced both organic content in soils and inhibits the natural symbiosis between plants and the soil microbiome.

ee14348adf97.title: Soil regeneration
ee14348adf97.sentence: The construction of urban environments frequently involves the compaction of soil and the sealing of soils under layers of concrete, asphalt, and other materials.

93762493cd18.title: Soil regeneration
93762493cd18.sentence: Sealing materials also decrease the natural absorption of rain water by soil causing intensification of water run-off during storms.

3eede6f09058.title: Soil regeneration
3eede6f09058.sentence: The increased flow of water causes soil erosion.

f821b8c440e5.title: Soil regeneration
f821b8c440e5.sentence: Cities also concentrate pollutants that can leach into soils.

fa6cd7dcb097.title: Soil regeneration
fa6cd7dcb097.sentence: There are many ways to regenerate soil and improve soil quality, such as land management by conservation agriculture.

3c8db604e1fe.title: Soil regeneration
3c8db604e1fe.sentence: These conservation agricultural practices utilize many techniques and resources to maintain healthy soil.

eaf37e4bbcfd.title: Soil regeneration
eaf37e4bbcfd.sentence: As one historical review put it, "Accelerated soil erosion has plagued the earth since the dawn of settled agriculture, and has been a major issue in the rise and fall of early civilization." Certain agricultural practices can deplete the soil of carbon, such as monoculture, where only one type of crop is harvested in a field season after season.

9f3036208d2f.title: Soil regeneration
9f3036208d2f.sentence: This depletes nutrients from the soil because each type of plant has a specific set of nutrients that it requires to grow or that it can fix back into the soil.

7b24fb9f86e8.title: Soil regeneration
7b24fb9f86e8.sentence: With a lack of plant diversity, only certain nutrients will be absorbed.

7b79c40f8708.title: Soil regeneration
7b79c40f8708.sentence: Over time, these nutrients will be depleted from the soil.

f113241aadcc.title: Soil regeneration
f113241aadcc.sentence: Some examples are cover cropping, crop rotation, reducing soil disturbance, retaining mulch, and integrated nutrient management.

abf42d3c4816.title: Soil regeneration
abf42d3c4816.sentence: These practices have many benefits, including increased carbon sequestration and reducing the use of fossil fuels.

76f6e4512623.title: Soil regeneration
76f6e4512623.sentence: Permaculture (from "permanent" and "agriculture") is a type of conservation agriculture that seeks to mimic natural ecosystems and minimize human involvement for maintenance.

34899cab7e5b.title: Soil regeneration
34899cab7e5b.sentence: Permaculture practices use mixed crops to balance nutrient flux in the soil, attempt to use native vegetation as much as possible, and use perennial crops where suitable.

ec2f94a054b4.title: Soil regeneration
ec2f94a054b4.sentence: Permaculture practices also avoid tilling and soil disturbance.

70944e1b5fec.title: Soil regeneration
70944e1b5fec.sentence: These approaches improve soil health over time by reducing soil disturbance and allowing for more sustained interactions between the soil microbiome and plant roots.

ff13be54541a.title: Soil regeneration
ff13be54541a.sentence: Holistic management stems from the work of Allan Savory, who observes that planned grazing can improve soil health and reverse the effects of desertification by increasing biomass.

df990b49e7a5.title: Soil regeneration
df990b49e7a5.sentence: There are also many kinds of soil amendments, both organic and inorganic.

184abfb83efc.title: Soil regeneration
184abfb83efc.sentence: They promote soil quality in a variety of ways, such as sequestering toxins, balancing the pH of the soil, adding nutrients, and promoting the activity of organisms.

7420bb567341.title: Soil regeneration
7420bb567341.sentence: The current conditions of the soil will determine which type of amendment and how much to use.

286777d78917.title: Soil regeneration
286777d78917.sentence: Inorganic amendments are generally used for things like improving the texture and structure of the soil, balancing the pH, and limiting the bioavailability of heavy metal toxins.

bc51d02ade7f.title: Soil regeneration
bc51d02ade7f.sentence: There are two types of inorganic amendments: alkaline and mineral.

efcee0d5768e.title: Soil regeneration
efcee0d5768e.sentence: Some examples of inorganic amendments include wood ash, ground limestone, and red mud.

249b81b772e8.title: Soil regeneration
249b81b772e8.sentence: Mineral amendments include gypsum and dredged materials.

98a7d27bb398.title: Soil regeneration
98a7d27bb398.sentence: Organic amendments improve biological activity, water permeability, and soil structure.

43f9ec5397f2.title: Soil regeneration
43f9ec5397f2.sentence: Mulch, for example, reduces erosion and helps to maintain the temperature of the soil.

81151f349122.title: Soil regeneration
81151f349122.sentence: Adding compost increases the moisture and nutrient content of the soil and promotes biological activity.

b803af5e20ef.title: Soil regeneration
b803af5e20ef.sentence: Biochar is an amendment that is full of carbon and is created by pyrolysis, a high-temperature decomposition process.

886c2a9860ec.title: Soil regeneration
886c2a9860ec.sentence: Wastes from animals are common soil amendments, usually their manure.

18c247ee0cbd.title: Soil regeneration
18c247ee0cbd.sentence: Biosolids can be high in nutrient content, so should be used sparingly.

9ad9e00bc6ba.title: Soil resilience
9ad9e00bc6ba.sentence: Soil resilience refers to the ability of a soil to resist or recover their healthy state in response to destabilising influences.

e5477df05f58.title: Soil resilience
e5477df05f58.sentence: This is a subset of a notion of environmental resilience.

f9b39763cd7a.title: Soil resilience
f9b39763cd7a.sentence: Soil resistance, a related term refers to the ability of soil to resist changes or the extent to which a soil will recover from any cropping or management change.

f82ffd726c5e.title: Soil resilience
f82ffd726c5e.sentence: The term is distinct from Soil resilience as resistance is the inherent capacity to withstand disturbance, while resilience is the capacity to recover after disturbance.

32c6c7172213.title: Soil resilience
32c6c7172213.sentence: Soil resilience should first be looked at in terms of soil formation and development (pedogenesis), a continuous process taking thousands of years – this puts into context the short time that humans have so extensively utilised, changed and depended directly on soil.

81aae50d7b89.title: Soil resilience
81aae50d7b89.sentence: Pedogenesis is the result of five factors: the first two are parent material and topography, which are passive and contribute to soil mass and position; the next two are climate and the biosphere, which are active and supply the energy in soil formation.

d045f44d0a22.title: Soil resilience
d045f44d0a22.sentence: It is the active factors in soil formation that vary so as to constitute an environmental change or shock.

e50a8bc983fd.title: Soil resilience
e50a8bc983fd.sentence: - Over millions of years the soil has endured varying atmospheric conditions including a complete absence of oxygen and associated behaviour of soil elements in a reducing environment, and the establishment of life – particularly of terrestrial vegetation 420 million years ago.

6961b5035356.title: Soil resilience
6961b5035356.sentence: - Over ten thousand years and following the last ice age, though average climate has remained relatively stable, the soil has faced periods of extended wet, dry and fire.

35d80129c116.title: Soil resilience
35d80129c116.sentence: - Constant or evolving state? – Do we expect that the soil to remain constant – to continue to provide the same environmental and commercial services as at present, or; that it will establish a new equilibrium?

d967172adfa3.title: Soil resilience
d967172adfa3.sentence: - How long will it take? – How long do we expect soils to ‘hold out’ or adjust, and are we realistic about pedological time?

e07deba3d2ca.title: Soil resilience
e07deba3d2ca.sentence: The resilience of the soil is limited by the rate and extent of change we impose compared with the time that soil requires to recover.

ceb7091e15b0.title: Soil resilience
ceb7091e15b0.sentence: The pressure that we impose on the soil in terms of biosphere (direct human impacts included) and climate constitute environmental change – the rate of this change compared to other changes over pedological time constitutes a shock.

c64ecac2580c.title: Soil resilience
c64ecac2580c.sentence: In Australia, the above questions are relevant given the strong dependence on the soil, yet the significant degradation of soils over little more than 200 years due to adoption of European styled agriculture.

55b7e485a843.title: Soil resilience
55b7e485a843.sentence: Our expectation has been one of ongoing environmental and commercial service, yet the practices applied have been unsustainable and have led to such soil related problems as salinity, acidity, nutrient decline, erosion and structure decline.

e203046a8ea8.title: Food and Agriculture Organization
e203046a8ea8.sentence: The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) is a specialized agency of the United Nations that leads international efforts to defeat hunger and improve nutrition and food security.

2acef108bb3e.title: Food and Agriculture Organization
2acef108bb3e.sentence: It was founded on 16 October 1945 in Quebec City, Canada.

7e9a56eb0cb6.title: Food and Agriculture Organization
7e9a56eb0cb6.sentence: The FAO comprises 194 members, including 193 countries and one member organization, the European Union (EU).

3b0be4f61578.title: Food and Agriculture Organization
3b0be4f61578.sentence: Its headquarters is in Rome, Italy, and it maintains regional and field offices worldwide, operating in over 130 countries.

66a0838d20fc.title: Food and Agriculture Organization
66a0838d20fc.sentence: It helps governments and development agencies coordinate their activities to improve and develop agriculture, forestry, fisheries, and land and water resources.

fe338ee1c420.title: Food and Agriculture Organization
fe338ee1c420.sentence: It also conducts research, provides technical assistance to projects, operates educational and training programs, and collects agricultural output, production, and development data.

33729867560e.title: Food and Agriculture Organization
33729867560e.sentence: FAO and the World Health Organization created the Codex Alimentarius Commission in 1961 to develop food standards, guidelines, and texts such as codes of practice under the Joint FAO/WHO Food Standards Programme.

21b892eea099.title: Land rehabilitation
21b892eea099.sentence: Land rehabilitation as a part of environmental remediation is the process of returning the land in a given area to some degree of its former state, after some process (industry, natural disasters, etc.) has resulted in its damage.

236f803864fc.title: Land rehabilitation
236f803864fc.sentence: Many projects and developments will result in the land becoming degraded, for example mining, farming and forestry.

c8a1a5d0cec7.title: Land rehabilitation
c8a1a5d0cec7.sentence: In some jurisdictions, including parts of the United States, the term "reclamation" can refer to land rehabilitation, as in returning disturbed lands to an improved state, instead of the land fill of water bodies.

bb7bc0bef899.title: Land rehabilitation
