bb7bc0bef899.sentence: - Waste dumps are contoured to flatten them out, to further stabilize them against erosion.

8576072410ac.title: Land rehabilitation
8576072410ac.sentence: - If the ore contains sulfides it is usually covered with a layer of clay to prevent access of rain and oxygen from the air, which can oxidize the sulfides to produce sulfuric acid.

f8d2ee819a30.title: Land rehabilitation
f8d2ee819a30.sentence: - Landfills are covered with topsoil, and vegetation is planted to help consolidate the material.

b0f2f4c0e910.title: Land rehabilitation
b0f2f4c0e910.sentence: - Tailings dams are left to evaporate, then covered with waste rock, clay if need be, and soil, which is planted to stabilize it.

a602ca9edf02.title: Land rehabilitation
a602ca9edf02.sentence: The Australian mine rehabilitation bonds totals $9.49 billion, with the state of NSW bond totaling $2.68bn in 2019.

55651480d75c.title: Land rehabilitation
55651480d75c.sentence: The cost of reclaiming the abandoned mines in the US is estimated at $9.6bn.

c19533a5ad6d.title: Soil governance
c19533a5ad6d.sentence: Soil governance refers to the policies, strategies, and the processes of decision-making employed by nation states and local governments regarding the use of soil.

f4701c1771f9.title: Soil governance
f4701c1771f9.sentence: Globally, governance of the soil has been limited to an agricultural perspective due to increased food insecurity from the most populated regions on earth.

fdd858bf11b1.title: Soil governance
fdd858bf11b1.sentence: In the developing world, soil governance is biased towards promoting sustainable agriculture and ensuring food security.

06ddece46a22.title: Soil governance
06ddece46a22.sentence: Governance of the soil differs from soil management.

5269ebdd4ca8.title: Soil governance
5269ebdd4ca8.sentence: Soil management involves practices and techniques used to increase and maintain soil fertility, structure, and carbon sequestration, etc.

2e899f6e4833.title: Soil governance
2e899f6e4833.sentence: Governing the soil requires international and national collaboration between governments, local authorities, industries and citizens to ensure implementation of coherent policies that encourage practices and methodologies that regulate usage of the resource to avoid conflict between users to promote sustainable land management.

86db3ea50e32.title: Soil governance
86db3ea50e32.sentence: The need to monitor and avoid the negative effects of agricultural land use such as soil erosion has formed the basis of the discourse and awareness on soil governance, and has also seen the emergence of science and technology as the link between soil management and governance.

c19e52bba27e.title: Soil governance
c19e52bba27e.sentence: Soil governance mechanisms are usually encapsulated within the context of land governance, with little focus on urban and industrial soil governance especially in developing countries that have rapid urbanization rates; thus, soil governance is highly interlinked with other atmospheric and anthropogenic processes which may contribute to the difficulty in distinguishing it as an entity.

832a0b49a0f5.title: Soil governance
832a0b49a0f5.sentence: However, soil remains as the primary medium for food production, thus global soil governance is directed towards the impacts of soil degradation on food production and conflicts that arise between the need for human settlements and space available for food production.

c29b4000bad1.title: Soil governance
c29b4000bad1.sentence: With an aim to make soil data available to all, the Food and Agriculture Organization and UNESCO created a global soil map in 1981 as the main information on the distribution of soil resources.

b57229b010b7.title: Soil governance
b57229b010b7.sentence: The global soil map is a global consortium between academic, regional and national scientific institutions coordinated by stakeholders according to the respective regions.

7080d59cbaef.title: Soil governance
7080d59cbaef.sentence: Using Geographic Information Systems (GIS), Remote sensing and emerging technologies a global soil map will be created to represent different soil types.

c68ba4758c6f.title: Soil governance
c68ba4758c6f.sentence: The consortium is led by the ISRIC-World Soil Information, whose mandate to increase knowledge on soils through data collection and dissemination and development of technologies and methodologies for digital soil mapping.

878d09c3e8a1.title: Soil governance
878d09c3e8a1.sentence: In 2002, the International Union of Soil Sciences proposed December 5 to be "World Soil Day" to celebrate the importance of soil in our lives.

f586352d6ea2.title: Soil governance
f586352d6ea2.sentence: Under the framework of the GSP, the sixty-eighth session of the United Nations General Assembly in December 2013 designated December 5 as the World Soil Day and declared 2015 as the International Year of Soils with the aim to raise awareness on the importance of soils for ecosystem functions and food security.

de8ad3c4009f.title: Soil regeneration
de8ad3c4009f.section: Climate change and the carbon cycle
de8ad3c4009f.sentence: Since humans began practising agriculture, it is estimated that 133 billion tonnes of carbon has been depleted from soil.

592d9fcfc6a4.title: Soil regeneration
592d9fcfc6a4.section: Climate change and the carbon cycle
592d9fcfc6a4.sentence: By means of fossil fuels and intensive farming, much of the natural carbon in the Earth's pedosphere has been released into the atmosphere, contributing to greenhouse gasses.

d2be5c056831.title: Soil regeneration
d2be5c056831.section: Climate change and the carbon cycle
d2be5c056831.sentence: In the natural carbon cycle, 61 billion tonnes of carbon is released annually from soils through decomposition and oxidation of soil organic carbon.

e888dcf12e9c.title: Soil regeneration
e888dcf12e9c.section: Climate change and the carbon cycle
e888dcf12e9c.sentence: A similar amount of carbon is deposited into soils through the decomposition of biomass and through symbiosis between plants and the soil microbiome.

e155bec55196.title: Soil regeneration
e155bec55196.section: Climate change and the carbon cycle
e155bec55196.sentence: The top two meters of soil contain an estimated 3,012 billion tonnes of carbon.

5804b799d8a5.title: Soil regeneration
5804b799d8a5.section: Climate change and the carbon cycle
5804b799d8a5.sentence: This is more than the total carbon stored in the atmosphere and in vegetation, 879 billion tonnes and 600 billion tonnes respectively.

1141078aef07.title: Soil regeneration
1141078aef07.section: Climate change and the carbon cycle
1141078aef07.sentence: The majority of this carbon loss has occurred in the last two centuries with the introduction of mechanised agriculture.

646d9b0236ef.title: Soil regeneration
646d9b0236ef.section: Climate change and the carbon cycle
646d9b0236ef.sentence: The reduction of emissions from soil reduces overall emissions of greenhouse gases and regenerative practices can be used as a form of natural carbon dioxide removal.

fa50c1bc7e73.title: Mine reclamation
fa50c1bc7e73.sentence: Mine reclamation is the process of modifying land that has been mined to restore it to an ecologically functional or economically usable state.

6ab6ae3d6570.title: Mine reclamation
6ab6ae3d6570.sentence: In open cut mines rocky material is used for backfilling the excavation.

cab0f711e044.title: Mine reclamation
cab0f711e044.sentence: A layer of soil that was stored in the premining is placed on top of the rocky material.

24add453bbeb.title: Mine reclamation
24add453bbeb.sentence: On top of this layer is placed a layer of topsoil.

add5d6205389.title: Mine reclamation
add5d6205389.sentence: The final step is the restoration of vegetation and long-term development of plant succession.

47b560938c61.title: Mine reclamation
47b560938c61.sentence: Returning the landscape to its original state is not possible in all cases.

e6f97ecbffbf.title: Mine reclamation
e6f97ecbffbf.sentence: In most cases the physical and chemical stabilization of mine waste is the limit of mine remediation.

8570e11f6768.title: Mine reclamation
8570e11f6768.sentence: - Create a suitable rooting medium for good tree growth that is no less than four feet deep and made of topsoil, weathered sandstone, and/or the best available material.

16e41ef7722c.title: Mine reclamation
16e41ef7722c.sentence: - Loosely grade the topsoil or topsoil substitute established in step one to create a non-compacted growth medium.

2297e441d5cc.title: Mine reclamation
2297e441d5cc.section: United States > Under the Surface Mining Control and Reclamation Act of 1977
2297e441d5cc.sentence: The Surface Mining Control and Reclamation Act of 1977 (SMCRA) is the primary federal law that regulates the environmental effects of coal mining in the United States.

403db80fbf34.title: Mine reclamation
403db80fbf34.section: United States > Under the Surface Mining Control and Reclamation Act of 1977
403db80fbf34.sentence: Under SMCRA, prior to receiving a mining permit, operators must present a detailed and comprehensive plan for reclaiming the land after mining has been completed.

a685c6bd0afb.title: Mine reclamation
a685c6bd0afb.section: United States > Under the Surface Mining Control and Reclamation Act of 1977
a685c6bd0afb.sentence: In addition to providing the reclamation plan, operators must also post a performance bond to ensure that monies will be available to complete the reclamation if the operator goes out of business prior to finishing the reclamation or is otherwise unable to complete the reclamation.

d79764ba01bc.title: Mine reclamation
d79764ba01bc.section: United States > Abandoned Mine Lands Program
d79764ba01bc.sentence: Mine operators must pay a tax of $0.12 per ton for underground mined coal and $0.28 per ton for surfaced mined coal; the proceeds from this tax are put into the Abandoned Mine Reclamation Fund (created by SMCRA) to pay for the reclamation of abandoned mines.

232ff7a7b12e.title: Soil bioengineering
232ff7a7b12e.sentence: Soil bioengineering, also called ground bioengineering, is the use of living plant materials to provide some engineering function.

12f75ab01253.title: Soil bioengineering
12f75ab01253.sentence: It pursues technological, ecological, economic as well as design goals and seeks to achieve these primarily by making use of living materials, i.e. seeds, plants, part of plants and plant communities, and employing them in near–natural constructions while exploiting the manifold abilities inherent in plants.

c40971e96da7.title: Soil bioengineering
c40971e96da7.sentence: Soil and Water Bioengineering is a discipline of civil engineering.

a639d76a9c16.title: Soil bioengineering
a639d76a9c16.sentence: Soil bioengineering may sometimes be a substitute for classical engineering works; however, in most cases it is a meaningful and necessary method of complementing the latter.

c93e337ba1b7.title: Soil bioengineering
c93e337ba1b7.sentence: Soil bioengineering techniques have been used for many centuries.

85325e54edfe.title: Soil bioengineering
85325e54edfe.sentence: More recently Schiechtl (1980) has encouraged the use of soil bioengineering with a variety of European examples.

c5bc2662fdf4.title: Soil bioengineering
c5bc2662fdf4.sentence: Soil bioengineering is now widely practiced throughout the world for the treatment of erosion and unstable slopes.

2833b0e066e0.title: Soil bioengineering
2833b0e066e0.sentence: Its application suggests itself in all fields of soil and hydraulic engineering, especially for slope and embankment stabilization and erosion control.

c3e7a807b9e6.title: Soil bioengineering
c3e7a807b9e6.section: Fields of application and plants for soil bioengineering control works
c3e7a807b9e6.sentence: Soil bioengineering methods can be applied wherever the plants which are used as living building materials are able to grow well and develop.

29f566c21d1e.title: Soil bioengineering
29f566c21d1e.section: Fields of application and plants for soil bioengineering control works
29f566c21d1e.sentence: This is the case in tropical, subtropical and temperate zones whereas there are obvious limits to plant growth in dry and cold regions, i.e. where arid, semi–arid and frost zones prevail.

36f2fb957627.title: Soil bioengineering
36f2fb957627.section: Fields of application and plants for soil bioengineering control works
36f2fb957627.sentence: However, limits are most frequently imposed in alpine and arctic regions.

92c9171cfc9b.title: Soil bioengineering
92c9171cfc9b.section: Fields of application and plants for soil bioengineering control works
92c9171cfc9b.sentence: The more impoverished a region is in species, the less suited it is for the application of bioengineering methods.

5b64ede47628.title: Soil bioengineering
5b64ede47628.section: Functions and effects of soil bioengineering structures > Technical functions
5b64ede47628.sentence: - protection of soil surface from erosion by wind, precipitation, frost and flowing water

43aaab8d1bad.title: Soil bioengineering
43aaab8d1bad.section: Functions and effects of soil bioengineering structures > Technical functions
43aaab8d1bad.sentence: - reduction of flow velocity along banks

f42cc9280c5e.title: Soil bioengineering
f42cc9280c5e.section: Functions and effects of soil bioengineering structures > Technical functions
f42cc9280c5e.sentence: - surface and/or deep soil cohesion and stabilization

cf25fb45f315.title: Soil bioengineering
cf25fb45f315.section: Functions and effects of soil bioengineering structures > Technical functions
cf25fb45f315.sentence: - aiding the deposition of snow, drift sand and sediments

9f08ed0d231d.title: Soil bioengineering
9f08ed0d231d.section: Functions and effects of soil bioengineering structures > Technical functions
9f08ed0d231d.sentence: - increasing soil roughness and thus preventing avalanche release

5c19f1141fe0.title: Soil bioengineering
5c19f1141fe0.section: Functions and effects of soil bioengineering structures > Ecological functions
5c19f1141fe0.sentence: - improvement of water regime by improved soil interception and storage capability as well as water consumption by plants

b66836e5e019.title: Soil bioengineering
b66836e5e019.section: Functions and effects of soil bioengineering structures > Ecological functions
b66836e5e019.sentence: - mechanical soil amelioration by the roots of plants

1bbf11ff624a.title: Soil bioengineering
1bbf11ff624a.section: Functions and effects of soil bioengineering structures > Ecological functions
1bbf11ff624a.sentence: - balancing of temperature conditions in near–ground layers of air and in the soil

337d9c3661ef.title: Soil bioengineering
337d9c3661ef.section: Functions and effects of soil bioengineering structures > Ecological functions
337d9c3661ef.sentence: - improvement of nutrient content in the soil and thus of soil fertility on previously raw soils

c4123f7c7084.title: Soil bioengineering
c4123f7c7084.section: Functions and effects of soil bioengineering structures > Ecological functions

539e202d1cf1.title: Soil bioengineering
539e202d1cf1.section: Functions and effects of soil bioengineering structures > Landscaping functions
539e202d1cf1.sentence: - healing of wounds inflicted on the landscape by disasters (e.g. landslides, wildfires, hurricanes) and humans (e.g. exploitation of mineral resources, construction work, deposition of overburden, tunnel excavation material, industrial and domestic waste)

f1f90b7aa21d.title: Soil bioengineering
f1f90b7aa21d.section: Functions and effects of soil bioengineering structures > Landscaping functions
f1f90b7aa21d.sentence: - integration of structures into the landscape (e.g. through landscaping)

1e705cf1b0bd.title: Soil bioengineering
1e705cf1b0bd.section: Functions and effects of soil bioengineering structures > Economic effects
1e705cf1b0bd.sentence: Bioengineering control works are not always necessarily cheaper in construction when compared to classical engineering structures.

2a726872edfb.title: Soil bioengineering
2a726872edfb.section: Functions and effects of soil bioengineering structures > Economic effects
2a726872edfb.sentence: However, when taking into account their lifetime including their service and maintenance, they will normally turn out to be more economical.

78a01901ae75.title: Soil bioengineering
78a01901ae75.section: Functions and effects of soil bioengineering structures > Economic effects
78a01901ae75.sentence: The result of soil bioengineering protection works are living systems which develop further and maintain their balance by natural succession (i.e. by dynamic self–control, without artificial input of energy).

9d9e6dab0d3a.title: Soil functions
9d9e6dab0d3a.sentence: Soil maps can depict soil properties and functions in the context of specific soil functions such as agricultural food production, environmental protection, and civil engineering considerations.

c38c941154e1.title: Soil functions
c38c941154e1.sentence: Soil mapping is the identification, description, ad delineation on a map of different types of soil based on direct field observations or on indirect inferences from souch sources such as aerial photographs.

49e722c7279f.title: Soil functions
49e722c7279f.sentence: Maps can depict functional interpretations of specific properties such as critical nutrient levels, heavy-metal levels or can depict interpretation of multiple properties such as a map of erosion risk index.

266020dc9737.title: Soil functions
266020dc9737.sentence: Mapping of function specific soil properties is an extension of soil survey, using maps of soil components together with auxiliary information (including pedotransfer functions and soil inference models) to depict inferences about the specific performance of soil mapping units.

1ff5be5e21d7.title: Soil functions
1ff5be5e21d7.sentence: Environmental interactions such as regulating water supplies, water loos, utilization, contamination, and purification are all affected by the soil.

9fdeb39ed9c8.title: Soil functions
9fdeb39ed9c8.sentence: They can filter, buffer, and transform materials between the atmosphere, the plant cover, and the water table.

b57af290f5f4.title: Soil functions
b57af290f5f4.sentence: Through filtering, soil acts as a filter and captures contaminants through soil particles.

8c736deb6278.title: Soil functions
8c736deb6278.sentence: Contaminants are captured by the soil particles and water comes out cleaner in the aquifers and rivers.

ea8817598975.title: Soil functions
ea8817598975.sentence: Soil interacts with the environment to transform and decompose waste materials in to new materials.

7cfd82294025.title: Soil functions
7cfd82294025.sentence: Lastly, it can accumulate large amounts of carbon as soil organic matter, thus reducing the total concentration of carbon dioxide that can mitigate global climate change.

166a59c1e5d8.title: Septic drain field
166a59c1e5d8.sentence: Septic drain fields, also called leach fields or leach drains, are subsurface wastewater disposal facilities used to remove contaminants and impurities from the liquid that emerges after anaerobic digestion in a septic tank.

5fc934913e4a.title: Septic drain field
5fc934913e4a.sentence: Organic materials in the liquid are catabolized by a microbial ecosystem.

177e03b622d9.title: Septic drain field
177e03b622d9.sentence: A septic drain field, a septic tank, and associated piping compose a septic system.

e95e97a500b1.title: Septic drain field
e95e97a500b1.sentence: The drain field typically consists of an arrangement of trenches containing perforated pipes and porous material (often gravel) covered by a layer of soil to prevent animals (and surface runoff) from reaching the wastewater distributed within those trenches.

2f064ceb698a.title: Septic drain field
2f064ceb698a.sentence: Primary design considerations are both hydraulic for the volume of wastewater requiring disposal and catabolic for the long-term biochemical oxygen demand of that wastewater.

682fbb8e162f.title: Septic drain field
682fbb8e162f.sentence: Just as a septic tank is sized to support a community of anaerobic organisms capable of liquefying anticipated amounts of putrescible materials in wastewater, a drain field should be sized to support a community of aerobic soil microorganisms capable of decomposing the anaerobic septic tank's effluent into aerobic water.

f2658e27f97a.title: Septic drain field
f2658e27f97a.sentence: The biofilm on the walls of the drain field trenches will use atmospheric oxygen in the trenches to catabolize organic compounds in septic tank effluent.

e481f6bc0e39.title: Septic drain field
e481f6bc0e39.sentence: Hydrogen sulfide odors or iron bacteria may be observed in nearby wells or surface waters when effluent has not been completely oxidized before reaching those areas.

59b71b268fe1.title: Septic drain field
59b71b268fe1.sentence: Septic tank and drain field microorganisms have very limited capability for catabolizing petroleum products and chlorinated solvents, and cannot remove dissolved metals; however, some may be absorbed into septic tank sludge or drain field soils, and concentrations may be diluted by other groundwater in the vicinity of the drain field.

87ea8d0bd810.title: Septic drain field
87ea8d0bd810.sentence: Laundry bleach may slow or stop microbial activity in the drain field, and sanitizing or deodorizing chemicals may have similar effects.

55b40229ef92.title: Septic drain field
55b40229ef92.section: Operation and maintenance > Dosing schedules or resting periods
55b40229ef92.sentence: A drain field may be designed to offer several separate disposal areas for effluent from a single septic tank.

19622599df0e.title: Septic drain field
19622599df0e.section: Operation and maintenance > Dosing schedules or resting periods
19622599df0e.sentence: One area may be "rested" while effluent is routed to a different area.

bfce438f1122.title: Septic drain field
bfce438f1122.section: Operation and maintenance > Dosing schedules or resting periods
bfce438f1122.sentence: The nematode community in the resting drain field continues feeding on the accumulated biofilm and fats when the anaerobic septic tank effluent is no longer available.

10e208660cdb.title: Septic drain field
10e208660cdb.section: Operation and maintenance > Dosing schedules or resting periods
10e208660cdb.sentence: This natural cleansing process may reduce bioclogging to improve the hydraulic capacity of the field by increasing the available interstitial area of the soil as the accumulated organic material is oxidized.

1eb331d4465a.title: Septic drain field
1eb331d4465a.section: Operation and maintenance > Dosing schedules or resting periods
1eb331d4465a.sentence: The percolation rate after resting may approach, but is unlikely to match, the original clean water percolation rate of the site.

ee7a27f3e233.title: Septic drain field
ee7a27f3e233.sentence: When a septic tank is used in combination with a biofilter, the height and catabolic area of the drain field may be reduced.

70780e26df64.title: Septic drain field
70780e26df64.sentence: The biofilter will not reduce the volume of liquid that must percolate into the soil, but it may reduce the oxygen demand of organic materials in that liquid.

be35d733d312.title: Septic drain field
be35d733d312.sentence: Biofilter technology may allow higher-density residential construction, minimal site disturbance, and more usable land for trees, swimming pools, or gardens.

277999b86700.title: Septic tank
277999b86700.sentence: A septic tank is an underground chamber made of concrete, fiberglass, or plastic through which domestic wastewater (sewage) flows for basic sewage treatment.

d69a7f0fd94b.title: Septic tank
d69a7f0fd94b.sentence: Settling and anaerobic digestion processes reduce solids and organics, but the treatment efficiency is only moderate (referred to as "primary treatment").

be57eacb5297.title: Septic tank
be57eacb5297.sentence: Wastewater enters the first chamber of the tank, allowing solids to settle and scum to float.

6b46407a2e88.title: Septic tank
6b46407a2e88.sentence: The settled solids are anaerobically digested, reducing the volume of solids.

4ac530e035bf.title: Septic tank
4ac530e035bf.sentence: One option for the effluent is the draining into the septic drain field, also referred to as a leach field, drain field or seepage field, depending upon locality.

7dd7c70a7d8d.title: Septic tank
7dd7c70a7d8d.sentence: A percolation test is required prior to installation to ensure the porosity of the soil is adequate to serve as a drain field.

8ca5b49ac9be.title: Septic tank
8ca5b49ac9be.sentence: The rate of accumulation of sludge—also called septage or fecal sludge—is faster than the rate of decomposition.

e8ea25f18cba.title: Septic tank
e8ea25f18cba.sentence: Therefore, the accumulated fecal sludge must be periodically removed, which is commonly done with a vacuum truck.

2746eee94d80.title: Septic tank
2746eee94d80.sentence: Some systems require pumping every few years or sooner, while others may be able to go 10–20 years between pumpings.

4faa8373b289.title: Septic tank
4faa8373b289.section: Environmental concerns > Nutrients in the effluent
4faa8373b289.sentence: Septic tanks by themselves are ineffective at removing nitrogen compounds that have potential to cause algal blooms in waterways into which affected water from a septic system finds its way.

49041701531a.title: Septic tank
49041701531a.section: Environmental concerns > Nutrients in the effluent
49041701531a.sentence: The soil's capacity to retain phosphorus is usually large enough to handle the load through a normal residential septic tank.

9db0fa429220.title: Septic tank
9db0fa429220.section: Environmental concerns > Nutrients in the effluent
9db0fa429220.sentence: Because of limited particle surface area, these soils can become saturated with phosphates.

4a094e906619.title: Septic tank
4a094e906619.section: Environmental concerns > Nutrients in the effluent
4a094e906619.sentence: Phosphates will progress beyond the treatment area, posing a threat of eutrophication to surface waters.

5f6586afacd1.title: Septic tank
5f6586afacd1.sentence: In the United States, the 2008 American Housing Survey indicated that about 20 percent of all households rely on septic tanks, and that the overwhelming majority of systems are located in rural (50%) and suburban (47%) areas.

29401da58b17.title: Septic tank
29401da58b17.sentence: In areas with high population density, groundwater pollution beyond acceptable limits may occur.

9df081d7321c.title: Septic drain field
9df081d7321c.sentence: Many health departments require a percolation test ("perc" test) to determine the suitability of drain-field soil to receive septic tank effluent.

2adfd26d42d1.title: Septic drain field
2adfd26d42d1.sentence: Alternatively, where seasonal high water tables limit system sizing, health districts can size the leach field by relying on soil morphological features to determine how suitable the drain field soil is for receiving septic tank effluent.

72c8b00058c8.title: Septic drain field
72c8b00058c8.sentence: The goal of percolation testing is to ensure the soil is sufficiently permeable for septic tank effluent to percolate away from the drain field, yet fine-grained enough to detain pathogenic bacteria and viruses for soil treatment to occur.

2de19c7f5ba8.title: Septic drain field
2de19c7f5ba8.sentence: Percolation tests measure the rate at which clean water disperses through a disposal trench into the soil.

e3baf5de9bb4.title: Septic drain field
e3baf5de9bb4.sentence: Aerobic soil conditions are needed to kill pathogens before they can travel far enough to reach a water well or surface water supply.

976de94fec16.title: Septic drain field
976de94fec16.sentence: Coarse soils, sand, and gravel can transmit wastewater away from the drain field before pathogens are destroyed.

0ce0e06fd9ad.title: Septic drain field
0ce0e06fd9ad.sentence: Silt and clay effectively filter out pathogens but limit wastewater flow rates.

1df0f3b4a133.title: Septic drain field
1df0f3b4a133.sentence: In this approach, the engineer or soil scientist evaluates soil characteristics, such as texture, structure, consistency, pore and root distribution, and color signatures left by water table fluctuation.

e7e5144a726b.title: Septic drain field
e7e5144a726b.sentence: Several factors may reduce observed percolation rates when the drain field receives anoxic septic tank effluent:

205e1d296262.title: Septic drain field
205e1d296262.sentence: - Microbial colonies catabolizing soluble organic compounds from the septic tank effluent will adhere to soil particles and reduce the interstitial area available for water flow between soil particles.

dc2efbc7ccd6.title: Septic drain field
dc2efbc7ccd6.sentence: These colonies tend to form a low-permeability biofilm of gelatinous slime at the soil interface of the disposal trench.

1821cd9d2244.title: Septic drain field
1821cd9d2244.sentence: - Insoluble particles small enough to be carried through the septic tank will accumulate at the soil interface of the disposal trench; non-biodegradable particles like synthetic fiber lint from laundry, mineral soil from washing, or bone and eggshell fragments from garbage disposals will remain to fill interstitial areas formerly available for water flow out of the trench.

b420b654832f.title: Septic drain field
b420b654832f.sentence: - Cooking fats or petroleum products emulsified by detergents or dissolved by solvents can flow through prior to anaerobic liquefaction when septic tank volume is too small to offer adequate residence time and may congeal as a hydrophobic layer on the soil interface of the disposal trench.

7cc32a3ba9db.title: Septic drain field
7cc32a3ba9db.sentence: - Rising groundwater levels may reduce the available hydraulic head (or vertical distance), causing gravitational water flow away from the disposal trench.

744d52d16e31.title: Septic drain field
744d52d16e31.sentence: - Frozen ground may seasonally reduce the cross-sectional area available for flow or evaporation.

81bae0fb52ef.title: Holistic management (agriculture)
81bae0fb52ef.sentence: In agriculture, holistic management (from ὅλος holos, a Greek word meaning "all, whole, entire, total") is an approach to managing resources that was originally developed by Allan Savory for grazing management.

cc3245240b20.title: Holistic management (agriculture)
cc3245240b20.sentence: "Holistic management" describes a systems thinking approach to managing resources.

4532f5c18cca.title: Holistic management (agriculture)
4532f5c18cca.sentence: Originally developed by Allan Savory, it is now being adapted for use in managing other systems with complex social, ecological and economic factors.

7210149ca0c7.title: Holistic management (agriculture)
7210149ca0c7.sentence: The Holistic Management decision-making framework uses six key steps to guide the management of resources:

ee1f1a8b4c20.title: Holistic management (agriculture)
ee1f1a8b4c20.sentence: - Define in its entirety what you are managing.

a4cab7617f50.title: Holistic management (agriculture)
a4cab7617f50.sentence: - Watch for the earliest indicators of ecosystem health.

57f2f5fde254.title: Holistic management (agriculture)
57f2f5fde254.sentence: One of the best examples of an early indicator of a poorly functioning environment is patches of bare ground.

556605971535.title: Holistic management (agriculture)
556605971535.sentence: The eight tools for managing natural resources are money/labor, human creativity, grazing, animal impact, fire, rest, living organisms and science/technology.

32266db7269c.title: Holistic management (agriculture)
32266db7269c.sentence: - Test your decisions with questions that are designed to help ensure all your decisions are socially, environmentally and financially sound for both the short and long term.

eac064567802.title: Holistic management (agriculture)
eac064567802.sentence: - Nature functions as a holistic community with a mutualistic relationship between people, animals and the land.

b7ad1d671b3d.title: Holistic management (agriculture)
b7ad1d671b3d.sentence: If you remove or change the behavior of any keystone species like the large grazing herds, you have an unexpected and wide-ranging negative impact on other areas of the environment.

c911dfb7a077.title: Holistic management (agriculture)
c911dfb7a077.sentence: - Animal husbandry using domestic species can be used as a substitute for lost keystone species.

da547eb4f6bf.title: Holistic management (agriculture)
da547eb4f6bf.sentence: - Time and timing is the most important factor when planning land use.

020337ffd04d.title: Holistic management (agriculture)
020337ffd04d.sentence: A meta-analysis of relevant studies between 1972 and 2016 found that Holistic Planned Grazing had no better effect than continuous grazing on plant cover, plant biomass and animal production, although it may have benefited some areas with higher precipitation.

34f9c9b35c26.title: Holistic management (agriculture)
34f9c9b35c26.sentence: However, a 2022 review of 22 "farm-scale" studies, many of which included adaptive management, again found that Holistic Management had no effect on or reduced plant or animal productivity.

01dc64617caa.title: Holistic management (agriculture)
01dc64617caa.sentence: In addition to a grazing method, Holistic Management involves goal setting, experiential learning and an emphasis on monitoring and adaptive decision-making that have not been captured by many scientific field trials.

eebd2813b3e4.title: Holistic management (agriculture)
eebd2813b3e4.sentence: Conversely, at least three studies have documented soil improvement as measured by soil carbon, soil nitrogen, soil biota, water retention, nutrient-holding capacity, and ground litter on grazed land using multi-pasture grazing methods compared to continuously grazed land.

01e6e98c957e.title: Holistic management (agriculture)
01e6e98c957e.sentence: According to a 2016 study published by the Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences, the actual rate at which improved grazing management could contribute to carbon sequestration is seven times lower than the claims made by Savory.

1516ac0ae1eb.title: Holistic management (agriculture)
1516ac0ae1eb.sentence: A 2011 study found that multi-paddock grazing of the type endorsed by Savory resulted in more soil carbon sequestration than heavy continuous grazing, but very slightly less soil carbon sequestration than "graze exclosure" (excluding grazing livestock from land).

7e22ef75b0ca.title: Onsite sewage facility
7e22ef75b0ca.sentence: Onsite sewage facilities (OSSF), also called septic systems, are wastewater systems designed to treat and dispose of effluent on the same property that produces the wastewater, in areas not served by public sewage infrastructure.

7f47aa6b9a4e.title: Onsite sewage facility
7f47aa6b9a4e.sentence: Most onsite wastewater treatment systems are of the conventional type, consisting of a septic tank and a subsurface wastewater infiltration system (SWIS).

3dcedd9c55f3.title: Onsite sewage facility
3dcedd9c55f3.sentence: OSSFs account for approximately 25% of all domestic wastewater treatment in the US.

b2d92df9844b.title: Onsite sewage facility
b2d92df9844b.sentence: In virtually all engineered onsite sewage facilities, recycling and decomposition by natural organisms is still the primary mechanism of sewage disposal.

9fc7d9d0ce97.title: Onsite sewage facility
9fc7d9d0ce97.sentence: Giving the organisms the time they need to decompose wastes is accomplished by establishing minimum sewage retention and settling times, and minimum liquid flow distances between sewage disposal sites and surface water or water wells.

e51a6d70c508.title: Onsite sewage facility
e51a6d70c508.sentence: Site evaluations integrate detailed analyses of regional hydrology, geology, and water resources with site specific characterization of soils, slopes, structures, property lines, and other site features to further define system design requirements and determine the physical placement of system components.

cbe6f9983c90.title: Onsite sewage facility
cbe6f9983c90.section: Usage and norms by country > United States > Public health and water resource impacts
cbe6f9983c90.sentence: State and tribal agencies report that onsite septic systems currently constitute the third most common source of groundwater pollution and that these systems have failed because of inappropriate siting or design or inadequate long-term maintenance (USEPA, 1996a).

359429a08cbc.title: Soil Health Card Scheme
359429a08cbc.sentence: Soil Health Card Scheme is a scheme launched by the Government of India on 19 February 2015.

359bffb0a663.title: Soil Health Card Scheme
359bffb0a663.sentence: Under the scheme, the government plans to issue soil cards to farmers which will carry crop-wise recommendations of nutrients and fertilisers required for the individual farms to help farmers to improve productivity through judicious use of inputs.

c848b252de13.title: Soil Health Card Scheme
c848b252de13.sentence: The scheme aims at promoting soil test based and balanced use of fertilisers to enable farmers to realise higher yields at lower cost.

f26159a9fdef.title: Soil Health Card Scheme
f26159a9fdef.sentence: Thereafter the experts will analyse the strength and weaknesses (micro-nutrients deficiency) of the soil and suggest measures to deal with it.

ceb669e07353.title: Soil Health Card Scheme
ceb669e07353.sentence: An amount of ₹568 crore (US$61 million) was allocated by the government for the scheme.

bfd078122212.title: Soil Health Card Scheme
bfd078122212.sentence: In 2016 Union budget of India, ₹100 crore (US$11 million) has been allocated to states for making soil health cards and set up labs.

2557ad63faca.title: Soil Health Card Scheme
2557ad63faca.sentence: As of July 2015, only 34 lakh Soil Health Cards (SHC) were issued to farmers as against a target of 84 lakh for the year 2015–16.

fa6021dc3139.title: Soil Health Card Scheme
fa6021dc3139.sentence: As on 16.05.2017, 725 lakh Soil Health Cards have been distributed to the farmers.

5c04e869d070.title: Soil governance
5c04e869d070.sentence: In attempts to increase knowledge on soils and soil management, the government of Gujarat initiated the Soil Health Cards Programme in 2006 that was "expected to bridge the gap between Scientists, agricultural extension workers, farmers and input-output dealers".

76bd61b7fb23.title: Soil governance
76bd61b7fb23.sentence: Increasing knowledge on soil management, increased output, and reduced costs for farmers and contributed to Gujarat's agriculture growth rate that was three times the national growth rate in 2009.

565f7732ea5f.title: Soil governance
565f7732ea5f.sentence: The success of the scheme has facilitated its implementation at a national level under the Ministry of Agriculture.

17dd9b091c86.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.03%3A_What_Kind_of_Soil_Do_You_Want
17dd9b091c86.sentence: Farmers sometimes use the term soil health to describe the condition of the soil.

c50db0d32631.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.03%3A_What_Kind_of_Soil_Do_You_Want
c50db0d32631.sentence: Scientists usually use the term soil quality, but both refer to the same idea: how well the soil is functioning for whatever use is being considered.

d45e24e20455.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.03%3A_What_Kind_of_Soil_Do_You_Want
d45e24e20455.sentence: The concept of soil health focuses on the human factor—the anthropogenic influence—that is increasingly significant due to many years of intensive management.

786549f1e43e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.03%3A_What_Kind_of_Soil_Do_You_Want
786549f1e43e.sentence: This is different from the inherent differences in soils that are the result of the natural factors that formed the soil, such as the parent material, climate, etc. Thereby, an analogy with humans is apt: We may have some natural differences from our genetic backgrounds (taller or shorter, fairer or darker, etc.), but our health still strongly affects the way we can function and is greatly influenced by how we treat our bodies.

5a6cac70db2f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.03%3A_What_Kind_of_Soil_Do_You_Want
5a6cac70db2f.sentence: Farmers can certainly tell you which of the soils on their farms are of low, medium or high quality, and oftentimes they refer to how dark and crumbly it is.

f3ea609b4ac4.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.03%3A_What_Kind_of_Soil_Do_You_Want
f3ea609b4ac4.sentence: They know high-quality soil because it generates higher yields with less effort.

b88c987ba28f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.03%3A_What_Kind_of_Soil_Do_You_Want
b88c987ba28f.sentence: Less rainwater runs off and fewer signs of erosion are seen on the better-quality soils.

5e637163d281.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.03%3A_What_Kind_of_Soil_Do_You_Want
5e637163d281.sentence: Less power is needed to operate machinery on a healthy soil than on poor, compacted soils.

55ce77b1e56f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.03%3A_What_Kind_of_Soil_Do_You_Want
55ce77b1e56f.sentence: A soil should have a sufficient supply of nutrients throughout the growing season.

17731c7dbadd.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.03%3A_What_Kind_of_Soil_Do_You_Want
17731c7dbadd.sentence: We want a soil with good tilth so that plant roots can fully develop with the least amount of effort.

aac03a93d490.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.03%3A_What_Kind_of_Soil_Do_You_Want
aac03a93d490.sentence: A soil that has a favorable and stable soil structure also promotes rainfall infiltration and water storage for plants to use later.

6e7343293995.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.03%3A_What_Kind_of_Soil_Do_You_Want
6e7343293995.sentence: For good root growth and drainage, we want a soil with sufficient depth before a compact soil layer or bedrock is reached.

327e151b1101.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.03%3A_What_Kind_of_Soil_Do_You_Want
327e151b1101.sentence: We want a soil to be well drained so that it dries enough in the spring and during the following rains to permit timely field operations.

f1525f8abdbf.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.03%3A_What_Kind_of_Soil_Do_You_Want
f1525f8abdbf.sentence: Also, it’s essential that oxygen is able to enter the root zone and just as important that carbon dioxide leaves it (it also enriches the air near the leaves as it diffuses out of the soil, allowing plants to have higher rates of photosynthesis).

69ba57247284.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.03%3A_What_Kind_of_Soil_Do_You_Want
69ba57247284.sentence: For example, flooded soils are desirable for cranberry and paddy rice production.

4363922c6b39.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.03%3A_What_Kind_of_Soil_Do_You_Want
4363922c6b39.sentence: A soil should have low populations of plant disease and parasitic organisms.

a3e745f7d810.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.03%3A_What_Kind_of_Soil_Do_You_Want
a3e745f7d810.sentence: Certainly, there should also be low weed pressure, especially of aggressive and hard-to-control weeds.

a5f06d0c1678.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.03%3A_What_Kind_of_Soil_Do_You_Want
a5f06d0c1678.sentence: Most soil organisms are beneficial, and we certainly want high amounts of organisms that help plant growth, such as earthworms and many bacteria and fungi.

e87ffd037c0b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.03%3A_What_Kind_of_Soil_Do_You_Want
e87ffd037c0b.sentence: We want a soil that is free of chemicals that might harm the plant.

82a732a3fd6a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.03%3A_What_Kind_of_Soil_Do_You_Want
82a732a3fd6a.sentence: These can occur naturally, such as soluble aluminum in very acid soils or excess salts and sodium in arid soils.

fff97ca9db17.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.03%3A_What_Kind_of_Soil_Do_You_Want
fff97ca9db17.sentence: Potentially harmful chemicals also are introduced by human activity, such as fuel oil spills or when sewage sludge with high concentrations of toxic elements is applied.

d11edb884b10.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.03%3A_What_Kind_of_Soil_Do_You_Want
d11edb884b10.sentence: Finally, a high-quality soil should resist being degraded.

b82a0ddda965.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.03%3A_What_Kind_of_Soil_Do_You_Want
b82a0ddda965.sentence: It should also be resilient, recovering quickly after unfavorable changes like compaction.

77c01efd908c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.02%3A_How_is_Soil_Made
77c01efd908c.sentence: They facilitate the cycling of organic matter and of the nutrients, which allows soil to continue supporting life.

deb21c6b0db1.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.02%3A_How_is_Soil_Made
deb21c6b0db1.sentence: Soil consists of four parts: solid mineral particles, water, air and organic matter.

1a781ae1921e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.02%3A_How_is_Soil_Made
1a781ae1921e.sentence: But these elements are generally locked up in the crystalline particles and are not directly available to plants.

0112f555133d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.02%3A_How_is_Soil_Made
0112f555133d.sentence: This is an important process because it allows the soil water, with the help of carbon dioxide in the air, to very slowly dissolve the mineral particles and release nutrients—we call this chemical weathering.

eb3abd966711.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.02%3A_How_is_Soil_Made
eb3abd966711.sentence: The soil water and dissolved nutrients, together referred to as the soil solution, are now available for plants.

5cfabb1c29a2.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.02%3A_How_is_Soil_Made
5cfabb1c29a2.sentence: Plants’ leaves capture solar energy and atmospheric carbon from carbon dioxide (CO2) through photosynthesis.

daa0f9a8e174.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.02%3A_How_is_Soil_Made
daa0f9a8e174.sentence: At the same time, plant roots absorb both soil water and the dissolved nutrients (nitrogen is added to soils or directly to plants through associated biological processes).

cda6a6ba94cb.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.02%3A_How_is_Soil_Made
cda6a6ba94cb.sentence: Now, the mineral nutrients that were derived from the soil are stored in the plant biomass in organic form in combination with the carbon from the atmosphere.

f3dc65c7fc17.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.02%3A_How_is_Soil_Made
f3dc65c7fc17.sentence: Eventually plants die and their leaves and stems return to the soil surface.

706e6ddc0501.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.02%3A_How_is_Soil_Made
706e6ddc0501.sentence: This dead plant material and manure become a feast for a wide variety of organisms—beetles, spiders, worms, fungi, bacteria, etc.—that in turn benefit from the energy and nutrients the plants had previously stored in their biomass.

5944eaecc601.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.02%3A_How_is_Soil_Made
5944eaecc601.sentence: At the same time, the decomposition of organic material makes nutrients available again to plants, now completing the cycle.

d063fcf4d670.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.02%3A_How_is_Soil_Made
d063fcf4d670.sentence: On the other end of the cycle the soil captures some of the organic matter and puts it “in storage.” This happens because soil mineral particles, especially clays, form bonds with the organic molecules and thereby protect them from further decomposition by soil organisms.

8ce257305bdc.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.02%3A_How_is_Soil_Made
8ce257305bdc.sentence: In addition, organic matter particles inside soil aggregates are protected from decomposition.

3faca8df6e14.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.02%3A_How_is_Soil_Made
3faca8df6e14.sentence: Over a long time, the soil builds up a considerable reservoir of nutrients from slowly decomposing minerals and carbon, and of energy from plant residue in the form of organic matter—similar to putting a small amount of money into a retirement account each month.

2f194a5cb3af.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.02%3A_How_is_Soil_Made
2f194a5cb3af.sentence: This organic matter storage system is especially impressive with prairie and steppe soils in temperate regions (places like the central United States, Argentina and Ukraine) because natural grasslands have deep roots and high organic matter turnover (Figure 1.1).

fcd83c3f227b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.02%3A_How_is_Soil_Made
fcd83c3f227b.sentence: But when lands were first developed for agriculture, plowing was used to suppress weeds and to prepare the soil for planting grain crops.

0835d0550f16.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.02%3A_How_is_Soil_Made
0835d0550f16.sentence: Plowing was also beneficial because it accelerated organic matter decomposition and released more nutrients than unplowed land.

3fdda8cb074a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.02%3A_How_is_Soil_Made
3fdda8cb074a.sentence: This was a major rift in organic matter cycling, because it caused more organic matter to be lost each year than was returned to the soil.

167945317b4e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.02%3A_How_is_Soil_Made
167945317b4e.sentence: In addition, a related rift occurred in nutrient cycling as some of the nutrients were harvested as part of the crop, removed from the fields and never returned.

450525d29d5c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.02%3A_How_is_Soil_Made
450525d29d5c.sentence: Only in the past century did we find effective ways to replenish the lost nutrients by applying fertilizers that are derived from geologic deposits or the Haber-Bosch process for producing nitrogen fertilizers.

6c2f92285e2f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.02%3A_How_is_Soil_Made
6c2f92285e2f.sentence: But the need to replace the organic matter (carbon) was mostly ignored until recently.

fa19696a7f9d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.02%3A_How_is_Soil_Made
fa19696a7f9d.sentence: Not only does it store and supply nutrients and energy for organisms, it also helps form aggregates when mineral and organic particles clump together.

6ab796e3a6e4.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.02%3A_How_is_Soil_Made
6ab796e3a6e4.sentence: When it is made up of large amounts of different-sized aggregates, the soil contains more spaces for storing water and allowing gas exchange, as oxygen enters for use by plant roots and by soil organisms and the carbon dioxide produced by organisms leaves the soil.

817f1bd8f40f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.02%3A_How_is_Soil_Made
817f1bd8f40f.sentence: So in summary, the mineral particles and pore spaces form the basic structure of the soil, but the organic matter is mostly what makes it fertile.

affeca2cc781.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/23%3A_How_Good_Are_Your_Soils/23.01%3A_Introduction
affeca2cc781.sentence: The most obvious reason is that it allows you to identify specific problems, such as P deficiency or surface compaction, and to target your management practices as part of the effort to increase overall soil health.

75f08b4a3c7f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/23%3A_How_Good_Are_Your_Soils/23.01%3A_Introduction
75f08b4a3c7f.sentence: A second reason might be to monitor the health of your soils over time after you have made some management changes.

fe73ca614d8b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/23%3A_How_Good_Are_Your_Soils/23.01%3A_Introduction
fe73ca614d8b.sentence: Another reason might be to better value your soils.

c47331d2e9a0.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/23%3A_How_Good_Are_Your_Soils/23.01%3A_Introduction
c47331d2e9a0.sentence: Is your soil improving after you started planting cover crops, began a new rotation or switched to reduced tillage?

23701e40a082.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/23%3A_How_Good_Are_Your_Soils/23.01%3A_Introduction
23701e40a082.sentence: A good soil health assessment done over a number of years allows you to see whether you are going in the right direction.

bd079f2639f1.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/23%3A_How_Good_Are_Your_Soils/23.01%3A_Introduction
bd079f2639f1.sentence: If they are in excellent health due to many years of good management, your land should be worth more when sold or rented than fields that have been worn out.

09f4d88fe7da.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/23%3A_How_Good_Are_Your_Soils/23.01%3A_Introduction
09f4d88fe7da.sentence: After all, a healthy soil produces more and allows for reduced purchased inputs.

94447319c927.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/23%3A_How_Good_Are_Your_Soils/23.01%3A_Introduction
94447319c927.sentence: Being able to effectively appraise soil health may be an additional incentive for farmers to invest in good management and build equity in their land.

9ee6dd7a5346.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/23%3A_How_Good_Are_Your_Soils/23.01%3A_Introduction
9ee6dd7a5346.sentence: We can approach soil health assessment at three levels of detail:

9a2510815ed0.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/23%3A_How_Good_Are_Your_Soils/23.03%3A_Field_Indicators
9a2510815ed0.sentence: In several states, farmers and researchers have developed “soil health scorecards” that are based on observations made in the field.

073b5b3f0f1c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/23%3A_How_Good_Are_Your_Soils/23.03%3A_Field_Indicators
073b5b3f0f1c.sentence: The goal of this type of assessment is to help you understand your soil’s health and improve it over time by identifying key limitations or problems.

e85442b9b6f7.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/23%3A_How_Good_Are_Your_Soils/23.03%3A_Field_Indicators
e85442b9b6f7.sentence: The NRCS has developed a somewhat different visual evaluation system, the Cropland In-Field Soil Health Assessment Worksheet (Table 23.1 is based on this worksheet).

767c7beb6ed6.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/23%3A_How_Good_Are_Your_Soils/23.03%3A_Field_Indicators
767c7beb6ed6.sentence: Soil cover | Organic matter, organism habitat | Anytime | Greater than 75% surface cover from plants, residue or mulch

129a0603073f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/23%3A_How_Good_Are_Your_Soils/23.03%3A_Field_Indicators
129a0603073f.sentence: Residue breakdown | Organic matter, organism habitat | Anytime; mostly no-till; farmer interview | Natural decomposition of crop residues as expected; previous year residues partially decomposed and disappearing

94875f1a4743.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/23%3A_How_Good_Are_Your_Soils/23.03%3A_Field_Indicators
94875f1a4743.sentence: Surface crusts | Aggregation | Before tillage; before or early in the growing season | Crusting in no more than 5% of field

16cac9ff5654.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/23%3A_How_Good_Are_Your_Soils/23.03%3A_Field_Indicators
16cac9ff5654.sentence: Ponding | Compaction, aggregation | After rain or irrigation (not when frozen); farmer interview | No ponding within 24 hours after major rainfall or irrigation

b67de3f196a9.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/23%3A_How_Good_Are_Your_Soils/23.03%3A_Field_Indicators
b67de3f196a9.sentence: Penetration resistance | Compaction | With adequate soil moisture; before tillage; before, early in or after the growing season | Penetrometer rating <150 psi in surface layer and <300 psi in subsoil layer, OR slight or no resistance with wire flag inserted

5f05e20ea0db.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/23%3A_How_Good_Are_Your_Soils/23.03%3A_Field_Indicators
5f05e20ea0db.sentence: Water stable aggregates | Aggregation, organism habitat | Anytime | Water-submerged in glass jar: at least 80% remains intact after 5 minutes with little cloudy water

4a5c9b64ffb3.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/23%3A_How_Good_Are_Your_Soils/23.03%3A_Field_Indicators
4a5c9b64ffb3.sentence: Soil structure | Compaction, soil organic matter, aggregation, organism habitat | Anytime | Granular structure in surface horizon and no platy structure in surface or subsoil horizons

24a52f8d7992.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/23%3A_How_Good_Are_Your_Soils/23.03%3A_Field_Indicators
24a52f8d7992.sentence: Soil color | Organic matter | With adequate soil moisture | No color difference between field and fence row samples, OR value is in darker range using color chart

19220ee3708d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/23%3A_How_Good_Are_Your_Soils/23.03%3A_Field_Indicators
19220ee3708d.sentence: Plant roots | Compaction, organic matter, organism habitat | During growing season | Roots covered in a soil film or part of soil aggregates, OR living roots are healthy (no black/dry roots or lesions), fully branched and extended into subsoil

de4a191708f1.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/23%3A_How_Good_Are_Your_Soils/23.03%3A_Field_Indicators
de4a191708f1.sentence: Biological diversity | Organic matter, organism habitat | With adequate moisture; before tillage | More than three different types of organisms observed without magnification

e7427ae77e6a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/23%3A_How_Good_Are_Your_Soils/23.03%3A_Field_Indicators
e7427ae77e6a.sentence: Biopores | Organic matter, compaction, aggregation, organism habitat | Before tillage; mostly no-till | Presence of root or earthworm channels that extend vertically through the soil, with some connecting to the surface

701d5901afa1.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/23%3A_How_Good_Are_Your_Soils/23.03%3A_Field_Indicators
701d5901afa1.sentence: Whenever you try to become more quantitative, you should be aware that measurements naturally vary within a field or may change over the course of a year.

b682fef957c3.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/23%3A_How_Good_Are_Your_Soils/23.03%3A_Field_Indicators
b682fef957c3.sentence: For example, if you decide to evaluate soil hardness with a penetrometer (Figure 23.1) or metal rod, you should perform at least 10 penetrations in different parts of the field and be aware that your results also depend on the soil moisture conditions at the time of measurement.

e5361f8fd4e8.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/23%3A_How_Good_Are_Your_Soils/23.03%3A_Field_Indicators
e5361f8fd4e8.sentence: If you do this after a dry spring, you may find the soil quite hard.

85dded849e2f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/23%3A_How_Good_Are_Your_Soils/23.03%3A_Field_Indicators
85dded849e2f.sentence: If you go back the next year following a wet spring, the soil may be much softer.

288934c47f1d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/23%3A_How_Good_Are_Your_Soils/23.03%3A_Field_Indicators
288934c47f1d.sentence: Similarly, earthworms will be abundant in the surface 6–9 inch layer when it’s moist but tend to go deeper into the soil during dry periods, although you may still observe the wormholes and casts (Figure 23.2).

5d6ffb8e95e0.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/23%3A_How_Good_Are_Your_Soils/23.03%3A_Field_Indicators
5d6ffb8e95e0.sentence: Avoid unusual areas (e.g., where machinery turns) and aim to include areas with higher and lower yields.

767ba179f7ce.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/23%3A_How_Good_Are_Your_Soils/23.03%3A_Field_Indicators
767ba179f7ce.sentence: Generally, soil health is best measured in the early spring and late fall under moist (but not too wet) soil condition.

5df750833f9f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/23%3A_How_Good_Are_Your_Soils/23.03%3A_Field_Indicators
5df750833f9f.sentence: But soil health problems are better observed during wet or dry periods when you might see runoff or crop drought stress symptoms.

c52f038bbca4.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/23%3A_How_Good_Are_Your_Soils/23.03%3A_Field_Indicators
c52f038bbca4.sentence: Crusting can be recognized by a dense layer at the surface that becomes hard after it dries (Figure 15.1).

0c55d8b09a64.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/23%3A_How_Good_Are_Your_Soils/23.03%3A_Field_Indicators
0c55d8b09a64.sentence: Ponding can be recognized either directly when the water is still in a field depression, or afterward in small areas where the soil has slaked (that is, aggregates have disintegrated).

9fd3139f1500.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/23%3A_How_Good_Are_Your_Soils/23.03%3A_Field_Indicators
9fd3139f1500.sentence: Slaked areas going down the slope are an indication that runoff and early erosion have occurred.

df2b9e894344.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/23%3A_How_Good_Are_Your_Soils/23.03%3A_Field_Indicators
df2b9e894344.sentence: When rills and gullies are present, a severe erosion problem is at hand.

b9a67b7e8008.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/23%3A_How_Good_Are_Your_Soils/23.03%3A_Field_Indicators
b9a67b7e8008.sentence: These symptoms are a sign of poor soil health, but the lack of visible signs doesn’t necessarily mean that the soil is in good health: it must rain hard for these signs to occur.

4a93374e8f07.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/23%3A_How_Good_Are_Your_Soils/23.03%3A_Field_Indicators
4a93374e8f07.sentence: Soil color is the result of a combination of the soil’s mineralogy, oxidation status and organic matter content.

2eb7497b5f4f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/23%3A_How_Good_Are_Your_Soils/23.03%3A_Field_Indicators
2eb7497b5f4f.sentence: We therefore associate black soils with high quality, and within the same soil type and texture class you can reasonably conclude that the darker the soil, the better.

cc0f977e911b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/23%3A_How_Good_Are_Your_Soils/23.03%3A_Field_Indicators
cc0f977e911b.sentence: However, don’t expect a dramatic color change when you add organic matter; it may take years to notice a difference.

194092b0862e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.06%3A_How_Do_You_Build_A_Healthy_High-Quality_Soil
194092b0862e.sentence: We use the term building soils to emphasize that the nurturing process of converting a degraded or low-quality soil into a truly high-quality one requires understanding, thought and significant actions.

0a486ed3ce47.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.06%3A_How_Do_You_Build_A_Healthy_High-Quality_Soil
0a486ed3ce47.sentence: It is a process that mirrors the building of soil through natural processes where plants and organic matter are key elements.

6e09525dc527.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.06%3A_How_Do_You_Build_A_Healthy_High-Quality_Soil
6e09525dc527.sentence: For example, an application of ground limestone will make a soil less acid and will increase the availability of many nutrients to plants.

bc6fdc2b8bfc.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.06%3A_How_Do_You_Build_A_Healthy_High-Quality_Soil
bc6fdc2b8bfc.sentence: But what if the soil is only a few inches deep?

97777e43ce78.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.06%3A_How_Do_You_Build_A_Healthy_High-Quality_Soil
97777e43ce78.sentence: In that case, there is little that can be done within economic reason, except on a very small, garden-size plot.

c215c04274f2.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.06%3A_How_Do_You_Build_A_Healthy_High-Quality_Soil
c215c04274f2.sentence: If the soil is poorly drained because of a restricting subsoil layer of clay, tile drainage can be installed, but at a significant cost economically and environmentally.

1f11f987a3e8.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.06%3A_How_Do_You_Build_A_Healthy_High-Quality_Soil
1f11f987a3e8.sentence: Soil organic matter has a positive influence on almost all of the characteristics we’ve just discussed.

f34883bbdc30.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.06%3A_How_Do_You_Build_A_Healthy_High-Quality_Soil
f34883bbdc30.sentence: As we will see in Chapter 2 and Chapter 8, soil organic matter is even critical for managing pests.

19546f61c6d3.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.06%3A_How_Do_You_Build_A_Healthy_High-Quality_Soil
19546f61c6d3.sentence: Appropriate organic matter management is, therefore, the foundation for high-quality soil and for a more sustainable and thriving agriculture.

f39e812860ee.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.06%3A_How_Do_You_Build_A_Healthy_High-Quality_Soil
f39e812860ee.sentence: However, we cannot forget other critical aspects of management, such as trying to lessen soil compaction and good nutrient management.

5aa3c948ff5e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.06%3A_How_Do_You_Build_A_Healthy_High-Quality_Soil
5aa3c948ff5e.sentence: - Minimize tillage and other soil disturbances to maintain soil structure and decrease losses of native soil organic matter.

689a2411803a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.06%3A_How_Do_You_Build_A_Healthy_High-Quality_Soil
689a2411803a.sentence: - Implement a number of practices that add diverse sources of organic materials to the soil.

9bf5b8cf1079.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.06%3A_How_Do_You_Build_A_Healthy_High-Quality_Soil
9bf5b8cf1079.sentence: - Maximize live roots in the soil and use rotations and cover crops that include a diverse mix of crops with different types of root systems.

eb8ff781f45d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.06%3A_How_Do_You_Build_A_Healthy_High-Quality_Soil
eb8ff781f45d.sentence: - Provide plenty of soil cover through cover crops and/or surface residue even when economic crops aren’t present in order to protect the soil from raindrops and temperature extremes.

089fea829a0a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.06%3A_How_Do_You_Build_A_Healthy_High-Quality_Soil
089fea829a0a.sentence: - Whenever traveling on the soil with field equipment, use practices that help develop and maintain good soil structure.

8f84f3933669.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.06%3A_How_Do_You_Build_A_Healthy_High-Quality_Soil
8f84f3933669.sentence: - Manage soil fertility status to maintain optimal pH levels for your crops and a sufficient supply of nutrients for plants without contributing to water pollution.

26143b5de7c2.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.06%3A_How_Do_You_Build_A_Healthy_High-Quality_Soil
26143b5de7c2.sentence: - In arid regions, reduce the amount of sodium or salt in the soil.

b82be94a4bf1.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.05%3A_How_Do_Soils_Become_Degraded
b82be94a4bf1.sentence: Although we want to emphasize healthy, high-quality soils because of their ability to produce high yields of crops, it is also crucial to recognize that many soils in the United States and around the world have become degraded: they have become “worn out.” Degradation most commonly begins with tillage—plowing and harrowing the soil—causing soil aggregates to break apart, which then causes more rapid loss of soil organic matter as organisms have greater access to residues.
