4feadefe5444.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.05%3A_How_Do_Soils_Become_Degraded
4feadefe5444.sentence: This accelerates erosion, because soils with lower organic matter content and less aggregation are more prone to accelerated erosion.

8ce10ddf0559.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.05%3A_How_Do_Soils_Become_Degraded
8ce10ddf0559.sentence: And erosion, which takes away topsoil enriched with organic matter, initiates a downward spiral resulting in poor crop production.

6c1a5a720b23.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.05%3A_How_Do_Soils_Become_Degraded
6c1a5a720b23.sentence: Soils become compact, making it hard for water to infiltrate and for roots to develop properly.

e8fd1de0b982.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.05%3A_How_Do_Soils_Become_Degraded
e8fd1de0b982.sentence: Erosion continues and nutrients decline to levels too low for good crop growth.

7e1ecc9ec760.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.05%3A_How_Do_Soils_Become_Degraded
7e1ecc9ec760.sentence: The development of saline (too salty) soils under irrigation in arid regions is another cause of reduced soil health.

c5bd17fe605b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.05%3A_How_Do_Soils_Become_Degraded
c5bd17fe605b.sentence: (Salts added in the irrigation water need to be leached beneath the root zone to avoid the problem.)

b381aa4b8bef.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.05%3A_How_Do_Soils_Become_Degraded
b381aa4b8bef.sentence: Tropical rainforest conditions (high temperature and rainfall, with most of the organic matter near the soil surface) may lead to significant soil degradation within two or three years of conversion to cropland.

768545b02034.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.05%3A_How_Do_Soils_Become_Degraded
768545b02034.sentence: This is the reason the “slash and burn” system, with people moving to a new patch of forest every few years, developed in the tropics.

6703d9812fbf.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.05%3A_How_Do_Soils_Become_Degraded
6703d9812fbf.sentence: Under the environmental conditions of the Great Plains (moderate rainfall and temperature, with organic matter distributed deeper in the soil), it took many decades for the effects of soil degradation to become evident (Figure 1.2).

ac8732730f33.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.05%3A_How_Do_Soils_Become_Degraded
ac8732730f33.sentence: The extent of deteriorating soil on a worldwide basis is staggering: Soil degradation has progressed so far as to decrease yields on about 20% of all the world’s cropland and on 19–27% of the grasslands and rangelands.

e7c46efd7c42.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.05%3A_How_Do_Soils_Become_Degraded
e7c46efd7c42.sentence: The majority of agricultural soils are in only fair, poor or very poor condition.

3fe149c37f55.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.05%3A_How_Do_Soils_Become_Degraded
3fe149c37f55.sentence: Each year some 30–40 billion tons of topsoil are eroded from the croplands of the world.

5d37eb8e7cea.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.05%3A_How_Do_Soils_Become_Degraded
5d37eb8e7cea.sentence: This led either to colonial ventures to help feed the citizenry—like the Romans invading the Egyptian breadbasket—or to the decline of the civilization.

5095ea4bfe68.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.05%3A_How_Do_Soils_Become_Degraded
5095ea4bfe68.sentence: The only exceptions were the convergence zones in the landscapes, valleys and deltas where the nutrients and sediments flow together and fertility can be maintained for many centuries (more about this in Chapter 7).

9c7cf0e0dfcf.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.05%3A_How_Do_Soils_Become_Degraded
9c7cf0e0dfcf.sentence: The westward push of U.S. agriculture was stimulated by rapid soil degradation in the East, originally a zone of temperate forest.

f964b007effc.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.07%3A_Soil_Health_Plant_Health_and_Human_Health
f964b007effc.sentence: To answer these questions we need to understand the two main components of the food chain: how soil health affects plant health and how plant health subsequently affects human health.

5c36b3155072.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.07%3A_Soil_Health_Plant_Health_and_Human_Health
5c36b3155072.sentence: Together, this is the soil-plant-human health connection.

650831614e92.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.07%3A_Soil_Health_Plant_Health_and_Human_Health
650831614e92.sentence: For example, people in the path of dust storms, which pick up fine particles from bare soils, may have significant respiratory problems and damaged lung tissue.

dea13f6500b4.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.07%3A_Soil_Health_Plant_Health_and_Human_Health
dea13f6500b4.sentence: In fact, frequent contact with soil and farm animals early in life results in fewer allergies and stimulates the immune system, helping it to better respond to infections as one grows older.

9e6094c063fa.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.07%3A_Soil_Health_Plant_Health_and_Human_Health
9e6094c063fa.sentence: In natural ecosystems the nutrients in plant material are mostly cycled back to the soil, but agricultural systems generally remove many of these nutrients from the farm when the harvested crops are sold, with variable amounts of nutrients remaining on the farm in residues, depending on the crop.

1230e799c11b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.07%3A_Soil_Health_Plant_Health_and_Human_Health
1230e799c11b.sentence: With the use of synthetic fertilizers some nutrients, notably nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium and calcium, are being replenished, but the minerals needed in small or trace amounts generally don’t get replaced.

fb3682565b2f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.07%3A_Soil_Health_Plant_Health_and_Human_Health
fb3682565b2f.sentence: This is especially the case in developing countries where farmers often don’t analyze their soils and they apply standard fertilizer blends.

1a1e34483fc8.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.07%3A_Soil_Health_Plant_Health_and_Human_Health
1a1e34483fc8.sentence: In some cases soils are naturally deficient in essential elements that may affect plants, animals or humans.

21a8296e2971.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.07%3A_Soil_Health_Plant_Health_and_Human_Health
21a8296e2971.sentence: For example, selenium is naturally low in the northeastern and northwestern United States.

2d3736c58db3.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.07%3A_Soil_Health_Plant_Health_and_Human_Health
2d3736c58db3.sentence: It does not affect plants much but can cause problems with animals and humans.

f3b8a17280ac.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.07%3A_Soil_Health_Plant_Health_and_Human_Health
f3b8a17280ac.sentence: In other cases agricultural activities themselves cause problems, like the long-term use of fertilizers containing high levels of cadmium.

7a8089da423d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.07%3A_Soil_Health_Plant_Health_and_Human_Health
7a8089da423d.sentence: An unusual case involved the introduction of tube wells in Bangladesh to irrigate rice.

fb51ff5514e5.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.07%3A_Soil_Health_Plant_Health_and_Human_Health
fb51ff5514e5.sentence: The groundwater source contains naturally high levels of arsenic, which accumulates in the rice grains, causing serious health concerns with local populations.

978d16f4e2e3.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.07%3A_Soil_Health_Plant_Health_and_Human_Health
978d16f4e2e3.sentence: The most significant effect of soil degradation relates to the reduced ability to produce sufficient nutritious foodstuffs to meet peoples’ basic caloric and protein needs.

36cda606935a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.07%3A_Soil_Health_Plant_Health_and_Human_Health
36cda606935a.sentence: Especially in isolated rural areas in developing countries people depend on crops and animals raised on their own farms with little opportunity to buy additional food.

9465d0066207.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.07%3A_Soil_Health_Plant_Health_and_Human_Health
9465d0066207.sentence: In developed societies nutritional deficiencies are rare because people obtain food from diverse sources.

1559fb1f2412.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.07%3A_Soil_Health_Plant_Health_and_Human_Health
1559fb1f2412.sentence: For example, regional soil selenium deficiency does not impact people when they also eat nuts from other regions.

fe5f6abca6e6.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.07%3A_Soil_Health_Plant_Health_and_Human_Health
fe5f6abca6e6.sentence: It is difficult to scientifically prove effects of soil health on human health, in part due to the complexity of diets and ethical considerations around clinical trials involving humans.

9cdf2709bc34.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.02%3A_Soil_Health_and_Management
9cdf2709bc34.section: SOIL HEALTH MANAGEMENT > Farmer Profile > 6C–3: Continuous Living Plants
9cdf2709bc34.sentence: Continuous living plants protect the soil against disturbance, while tightly cycling nutrients and water and provide a steady supply of organic inputs from roots and litterfall to build soil organic matter (Table 15.3).

40eec237a5c8.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.02%3A_Soil_Health_and_Management
40eec237a5c8.section: SOIL HEALTH MANAGEMENT > Farmer Profile > 6C–3: Continuous Living Plants
40eec237a5c8.sentence: Continuous living plants, primarily by perennializing cropping systems, is the only 6C soil health management strategy that contributes to all three soil health principles (Table 15.3) protect soil, diversity + perennialization and building carbon.

2b1eef879e7c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.02%3A_Soil_Health_and_Management
2b1eef879e7c.section: SOIL HEALTH MANAGEMENT > Farmer Profile > 6C–3: Continuous Living Plants
2b1eef879e7c.sentence: Soils in these ecosystems have a continuous cover of mostly perennial plants and a layer of plant litter that remains at the soil surface.

180b31882731.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.02%3A_Soil_Health_and_Management
180b31882731.section: SOIL HEALTH MANAGEMENT > Farmer Profile > 6C–3: Continuous Living Plants
180b31882731.sentence: In contrast, agricultural systems where annual plants are typically grown, there are periods during the year in the early spring and late fall when living plants are not growing.

13b575650268.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.02%3A_Soil_Health_and_Management
13b575650268.section: SOIL HEALTH MANAGEMENT > Farmer Profile > 6C–3: Continuous Living Plants
13b575650268.sentence: Moreover, some farmland, largely on the Prairies, is intentionally left as fallow land to conserve soil moisture for subsequent grain crops.

09a17760faf1.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.02%3A_Soil_Health_and_Management
09a17760faf1.section: SOIL HEALTH MANAGEMENT > Farmer Profile > 6C–3: Continuous Living Plants
09a17760faf1.sentence: As far back as the early 20th century, however, soil scientists could measure the negative impact of frequent fallow on soil organic matter levels in prairie crop rotations (Janzen, 2001).

78e61a658394.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.02%3A_Soil_Health_and_Management
78e61a658394.section: SOIL HEALTH MANAGEMENT > Farmer Profile > 6C–3: Continuous Living Plants
78e61a658394.sentence: Plants allocate roughly 40% of their net photosynthetic carbon towards roots (Jones et al., 2009)—this is a large amount of carbon that can contribute to increasing soil carbon and soil health.

8b67edc515fb.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.02%3A_Soil_Health_and_Management
8b67edc515fb.section: SOIL HEALTH MANAGEMENT > Farmer Profile > 6C–3: Continuous Living Plants
8b67edc515fb.sentence: In general, perennial crops provide more carbon inputs than annual crops because their root systems are not only larger, but for a much longer time the plant is able to photosynthesize and release carbon to the soil from decomposition of aboveground residues, dead roots, and rhizodeposits from live root systems.

90aee5897c7b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.02%3A_Soil_Health_and_Management
90aee5897c7b.section: SOIL HEALTH MANAGEMENT > Farmer Profile > 6C–3: Continuous Living Plants
90aee5897c7b.sentence: The presence of continuous living plants results in improvements in soil structure and aggregation conferred by roots, rhizodeposits, and rhizosphere microbial communities.

f6ae1af89732.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.02%3A_Soil_Health_and_Management
f6ae1af89732.section: SOIL HEALTH MANAGEMENT > Farmer Profile > 6C–3: Continuous Living Plants
f6ae1af89732.sentence: In turn, these improvements result in greater hydraulic conductivity and therefore greater infiltration and drainage, which is important in humid regions.

104993939be8.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.02%3A_Soil_Health_and_Management
104993939be8.section: SOIL HEALTH MANAGEMENT > Farmer Profile > 6C–3: Continuous Living Plants
104993939be8.sentence: In regions with limitted rainfall, continuous living plants can improve soil hydrological properties such as soil porosity and the water retained at field capacity (Basche and DeLonge, 2017).

5f35ba2bcea1.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.02%3A_Soil_Health_and_Management
5f35ba2bcea1.section: SOIL HEALTH MANAGEMENT > Farmer Profile > 6C–3: Continuous Living Plants
5f35ba2bcea1.sentence: Increasing the duration of time that living plants grow and transpire water from deep in the soil profile can help reduce salinity (Chapter 5).

0bd61c2fe0ed.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.02%3A_Soil_Health_and_Management
0bd61c2fe0ed.section: SOIL HEALTH MANAGEMENT > Farmer Profile > 6C–3: Continuous Living Plants
0bd61c2fe0ed.sentence: Soil cover and living roots growing in the soil limits evaporation and reduces the upward movement of salts carried in water towards the soil surface.

39e63471075d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.02%3A_Soil_Health_and_Management
39e63471075d.section: SOIL HEALTH MANAGEMENT > Farmer Profile > 6C–3: Continuous Living Plants
39e63471075d.sentence: Growing winter annuals, such as winter wheat or fall rye in a crop rotation allows for living roots to be growing in the fall and early spring.

0f882fcfb505.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.02%3A_Soil_Health_and_Management
0f882fcfb505.section: SOIL HEALTH MANAGEMENT > Farmer Profile > 6C–3: Continuous Living Plants
0f882fcfb505.sentence: Cover crops grown in the fall and early spring are another option; their benefits and limitations are outlined in more detail in the next section.

cd9e380d1f15.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.02%3A_Soil_Health_and_Management
cd9e380d1f15.section: SOIL HEALTH MANAGEMENT > Farmer Profile > 6C–3: Continuous Living Plants
cd9e380d1f15.sentence: Increasing crop diversity (described in Crop and Animal Diversity section) by inter-seeding two plant species together through relay cropping or intercropping can also add duration and increase the number and type of living roots in annual crop rotations.

ad6a04e65f4f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.02%3A_Soil_Health_and_Management
ad6a04e65f4f.section: SOIL HEALTH MANAGEMENT > Farmer Profile > 6C–3: Continuous Living Plants
ad6a04e65f4f.sentence: Agroforestry is the integration of woody plants such as trees and shrubs into agricultural systems and is another option for perennializing the system.

7a56e8c851d6.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/23%3A_How_Good_Are_Your_Soils/23.04%3A_Laboratory_Soil_Health_Testing
7a56e8c851d6.sentence: Several soil health tests have been developed to provide a more comprehensive soil assessment through the inclusion of soil biological and physical indicators in addition to chemical ones.

c2de0580d154.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/23%3A_How_Good_Are_Your_Soils/23.04%3A_Laboratory_Soil_Health_Testing
c2de0580d154.sentence: Indicators were selected based on the soil processes that they represent, and thereby the tests provide insights into a soil’s ability to provide ecosystem services (like growing healthy crops).

fc82e232cf14.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/23%3A_How_Good_Are_Your_Soils/23.04%3A_Laboratory_Soil_Health_Testing
fc82e232cf14.sentence: The traditional soil test does not, however, make a comprehensive assessment of soil health, which probably led to the “chemical bias” in soil management.

2b7ffc893d21.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/23%3A_How_Good_Are_Your_Soils/23.04%3A_Laboratory_Soil_Health_Testing
2b7ffc893d21.sentence: In other words, the widespread availability of good chemical soil tests, although a very useful management tool, may also have encouraged the quick-fix use of chemical fertilizers over the longer-term holistic approach promoted in this book.

3a1e7e56d5a1.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/23%3A_How_Good_Are_Your_Soils/23.04%3A_Laboratory_Soil_Health_Testing
3a1e7e56d5a1.sentence: Currently (in the year 2020) there is no single standard soil health test, but there is universal agreement that a comprehensive soil health test should include indicators that represent all three types of soil processes: biological, physical and chemical (Figure 23.5).

9d5c64c268e6.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/23%3A_How_Good_Are_Your_Soils/23.04%3A_Laboratory_Soil_Health_Testing
9d5c64c268e6.sentence: Also, measured values need to be interpreted based on inherent variation in soils as a result of different climates, soil textures, etc.

3f1c67a2eb58.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/23%3A_How_Good_Are_Your_Soils/23.04%3A_Laboratory_Soil_Health_Testing
3f1c67a2eb58.sentence: For physical indicators, aggregate stability (Figure 23.6) relates to infiltration, crusting and shallow rooting, and represents the “tilth” of the soil.

450dc816183b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/23%3A_How_Good_Are_Your_Soils/23.04%3A_Laboratory_Soil_Health_Testing
450dc816183b.sentence: It generally shows a fast response after the introduction of new management practices like reduced tillage, cover cropping or manure or compost additions.

6e46f5aa34c0.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/23%3A_How_Good_Are_Your_Soils/23.04%3A_Laboratory_Soil_Health_Testing
6e46f5aa34c0.sentence: Available water capacity relates to plant-available water and is relevant to drought resistance.

4318f3ab51b5.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/23%3A_How_Good_Are_Your_Soils/23.04%3A_Laboratory_Soil_Health_Testing
4318f3ab51b5.sentence: It is more sensitive to inherent soil texture differences than to changes in management.

8f113f46aa4f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/23%3A_How_Good_Are_Your_Soils/23.04%3A_Laboratory_Soil_Health_Testing
8f113f46aa4f.sentence: For biological indicators, the most common indicator is total soil organic matter (SOM) content, which affects almost all important soil processes, including water and nutrient retention, and biological activities.

3a70e7fbae2d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/23%3A_How_Good_Are_Your_Soils/23.04%3A_Laboratory_Soil_Health_Testing
3a70e7fbae2d.sentence: It is often the single most important measurement of soil health, but unfortunately it is not very sensitive to management.

115462e81092.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/23%3A_How_Good_Are_Your_Soils/23.04%3A_Laboratory_Soil_Health_Testing
115462e81092.sentence: It takes many years to measure a real change in SOM, and farmers would generally want to know earlier about the benefits of a management change.

e07b95f2d6bd.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/23%3A_How_Good_Are_Your_Soils/23.04%3A_Laboratory_Soil_Health_Testing
e07b95f2d6bd.sentence: Active carbon is an inexpensive test that relates to a small fraction of the organic material that is more actively engaged with biological functions, and it has shown to be very sensitive to changes in soil management.

b2c1e28421c9.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/23%3A_How_Good_Are_Your_Soils/23.04%3A_Laboratory_Soil_Health_Testing
b2c1e28421c9.sentence: It is therefore a good early indicator of soil health improvements.

d4bffa0d9533.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/23%3A_How_Good_Are_Your_Soils/23.04%3A_Laboratory_Soil_Health_Testing
d4bffa0d9533.sentence: Active C is assessed as the portion of soil organic matter that is oxidized by potassium permanganate, and the results can be measured with an inexpensive spectrophotometer (Figure 23.7).

f04defe82869.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/23%3A_How_Good_Are_Your_Soils/23.04%3A_Laboratory_Soil_Health_Testing
f04defe82869.sentence: Similarly, soil protein content is an indicator of the soil organic nitrogen potentially available to microorganisms, and it also shows strong response to management changes, especially when more legumes are introduced.

59e68dbec217.title: Soil governance

573d26ca2c7f.title: Soil governance

f26f1e039fbf.sentence: Through various ministries the national programme aspires to implement the UNCCD by increasing capacity in soil and soil water management, improving access to micro-credit with a focus on women and marginalised groups, promoting alternative energy supplies to reduce reliance on wood increasing soil monitoring and strengthening legislation regarding land management in industrial and mining activities.

0db3f74ab09d.title: Soil governance
0db3f74ab09d.sentence: In the developing world, industrialization and urbanization are emerging as significant contributors to land and soil degradation.

93e725a1b333.title: Soil governance
93e725a1b333.sentence: In the developing and developing world governance of soils in urban areas requires bespoke policies because of the nature of urban and industrial developments in the cities.

5b197ea92bfe.title: Soil governance
5b197ea92bfe.sentence: Industrialization alters the chemical aspects of the soil through pollution of heavy metals and effluents.

92ae5d7ad3d3.title: Soil governance
92ae5d7ad3d3.sentence: Construction and landfills in urban areas affect soil through compaction and excavation, which affect natural processes such as water purification and storage.

06dbce97eb32.title: Soil governance
06dbce97eb32.sentence: Lack of sufficient knowledge in soil management and disregard for the environment has been identified as key reasons affecting urban soil degradation.

82f08a1734c5.title: Soil governance
82f08a1734c5.sentence: Often, developing countries lack resources to implement policies governing settlements and industries, thus the soil and water are often heavily polluted.

d7466f1e8eac.title: Soil governance
d7466f1e8eac.sentence: In Central Europe, governance of urban soils is facilitated by the urban soil management strategy that aims to design applicable soil management strategies in select European cities.

7192a0d326a2.title: Soil governance
7192a0d326a2.sentence: Through networks created with universities and municipal authorities the project aims to research into and develop an interdisciplinary approach to manage urban soils,.

065a80cbb64f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/08%3A_Soil_Health/8.04%3A_Activity_3_-_Soil_Nitrate
065a80cbb64f.sentence: - Collect approximately ½ cup of soil from a garden or farm.

0fc41a9c189c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/08%3A_Soil_Health/8.04%3A_Activity_3_-_Soil_Nitrate
0fc41a9c189c.sentence: This is an estimate of the nitrate-N concentration in the solution.

d674a21d7d75.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/08%3A_Soil_Health/8.04%3A_Activity_3_-_Soil_Nitrate
d674a21d7d75.sentence: - Add 30 mL of distilled water to the soil subsample, creating a 1:1 soil to water ration on a volume basis

807371fcb988.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/08%3A_Soil_Health/8.04%3A_Activity_3_-_Soil_Nitrate
807371fcb988.sentence: - Put the lid on the container and shake vigorously 25 times.

605041d2076f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/08%3A_Soil_Health/8.04%3A_Activity_3_-_Soil_Nitrate
605041d2076f.sentence: - Using the eye dropper and one nitrate/nitrite test strip, place 1 or 2 drops of the filtered solution on each of the strip’s two pads.

c4bcb2633b61.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/08%3A_Soil_Health/8.04%3A_Activity_3_-_Soil_Nitrate
c4bcb2633b61.sentence: - After 60 seconds, compare the first pad furthest from your thumb) along the nitrate scale and estimate the amount according to the degree of color change.

706c27c07ca7.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/08%3A_Soil_Health/8.04%3A_Activity_3_-_Soil_Nitrate
706c27c07ca7.sentence: Nitrite rarely occurs in measurable amounts in the soils, so nitrite readings from the test strips are not recorded.

90ad45116d8f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/08%3A_Soil_Health/8.04%3A_Activity_3_-_Soil_Nitrate
90ad45116d8f.sentence: Note: The maximum nitrate-N reading on the nitrate/nitrite test strip container is 50 ppm.

dc2d3e599afb.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/08%3A_Soil_Health/8.04%3A_Activity_3_-_Soil_Nitrate
dc2d3e599afb.sentence: If the sample reading falls into the 50 ppm category, the sample can be diluted to get a better estimate of the actual amount over 50 ppm.

a1694306b756.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/08%3A_Soil_Health/8.04%3A_Activity_3_-_Soil_Nitrate
a1694306b756.sentence: Multiply the estimated nitrate-N in ppm by 2 before using the calculations.

f7c10f96a6a4.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/08%3A_Soil_Health/8.04%3A_Activity_3_-_Soil_Nitrate
f7c10f96a6a4.sentence: If the nitrate reading falls into the category of 50 ppm again, repeat the dilution steps, and multiply the estimated nitrate-N in ppm by 4.

1b63e99d6ac8.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Introduction_to_Soil_Science_Laboratory_Manual_(Schwyter_and_Vaughan)/08%3A_Soil_Health/8.04%3A_Activity_3_-_Soil_Nitrate
1b63e99d6ac8.sentence: Note: for garden topsoil, bulk density can be assumed to be 1.1 g/cm3 and 1.5 g/cm3 for subsoil.

ff14eb889b5b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.01%3A_Introduction
ff14eb889b5b.sentence: In the real world, you need to combine a number of these approaches and use them together.

52c2fed8773f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.01%3A_Introduction
52c2fed8773f.sentence: In fact, each practice is related to, or affects, other practices that promote soil health.

2cdf10687697.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.01%3A_Introduction
2cdf10687697.sentence: Solutions can be found by matching them with the needs and opportunities of your farm.

0cc3e0c42a42.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.01%3A_Introduction
0cc3e0c42a42.sentence: Research shows that the practices that improve soil health generally also improve the economics of the farm, in some cases dramatically.

1925de2f2c87.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.01%3A_Introduction
1925de2f2c87.sentence: Higher soil health tends to provide higher yields and more yield stability, while allowing for reduced crop inputs.

1c8b24f666f4.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.01%3A_Introduction
1c8b24f666f4.sentence: After you implement new practices, soil health may improve slowly, and it may take a few years to see improved yields or changes in the soil itself.

4e66458a9663.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.01%3A_Introduction
4e66458a9663.sentence: Changing management practices may involve an investment in new equipment; for example, changing tillage systems requires new tillage tools and planters.

d14000b4207d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.01%3A_Introduction
d14000b4207d.sentence: Big changes are probably best implemented at strategic times.

91735927fb35.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.01%3A_Introduction
91735927fb35.sentence: For example, when you are ready to buy a new planter, consider a whole new approach to tillage as well.

c52a8eb58b37.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.01%3A_Introduction
c52a8eb58b37.sentence: Also, take advantage of flush times—for example, when you receive high prices for products—to invest in new management approaches.

c2c19f3db0ed.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.01%3A_Introduction
c2c19f3db0ed.sentence: If you establish a new orchard, vineyard or landscaped area, it’s best to do whatever is possible to improve the soil before you put your plants into the ground.

901be025008d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.01%3A_Introduction
901be025008d.sentence: When switching to no-till it likewise makes sense to try to add extra organic matter, take care of subsoil compaction and correct any nutrient deficiencies.

064f4a0a8167.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.01%3A_Introduction
064f4a0a8167.sentence: Remember that soil health management is a long-term commitment.

395b547ac3c4.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.01%3A_Introduction
395b547ac3c4.sentence: There are no silver bullets or snake oils that will work to build soil health; it requires integrating the concepts of physical, biological and chemical processes we have discussed in this book.

994bcc99d5ad.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.03%3A_What_Makes_Sense_for_Your_Situation
994bcc99d5ad.sentence: We strongly advocate a holistic management approach designed to prevent problems from developing, as preventive medicine approaches do.

9c51e1513c76.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.03%3A_What_Makes_Sense_for_Your_Situation
9c51e1513c76.sentence: And, as with human health, we have the ability to diagnose problems through observations and testing.

d0e82737c54b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.03%3A_What_Makes_Sense_for_Your_Situation
d0e82737c54b.sentence: Similarly for soil health, what makes sense for any individual operation depends on the soils, the climate, the nature of the enterprise, the surrounding region, potential markets and your goals.

48e9cec0c70c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.03%3A_What_Makes_Sense_for_Your_Situation
48e9cec0c70c.sentence: The tests and observations provide useful guidance to help target constraints, but there is rarely a simple recipe.

14e3da7a510e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.03%3A_What_Makes_Sense_for_Your_Situation
14e3da7a510e.sentence: Start with regularly testing your soils, preferably using comprehensive soil health analyses, and applying amendments only when they are needed.

aa211d055752.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.03%3A_What_Makes_Sense_for_Your_Situation
aa211d055752.sentence: Testing soils on each field every two to three years is one of the best investments you can make.

85c9488ab5d0.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.03%3A_What_Makes_Sense_for_Your_Situation
85c9488ab5d0.sentence: If you keep the report forms, or record the results, you will be able to follow soil health changes over the years.

462fe3ef9da7.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.03%3A_What_Makes_Sense_for_Your_Situation
462fe3ef9da7.sentence: Monitoring soil test changes will help you fine-tune your practices.

32c5836e82f3.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/08%3A_Soil_Health_Plant_Health_and_Pests/8.05%3A_Plant_Defenses_Management_Practices_and_Pests
32c5836e82f3.sentence: Plants under attack by insects also produce airborne (volatile) chemicals that signal to beneficial insects that the specific host it desires is on the plant.

4348a9bf2944.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/08%3A_Soil_Health_Plant_Health_and_Pests/8.05%3A_Plant_Defenses_Management_Practices_and_Pests
4348a9bf2944.sentence: However, when fed upon, by caterpillars for example, many plants produce a sticky, sweet substance from the wounds, called “extra-floral nectar,” which provides some attraction and food for beneficial organisms.

a74e81582d72.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/08%3A_Soil_Health_Plant_Health_and_Pests/8.05%3A_Plant_Defenses_Management_Practices_and_Pests
a74e81582d72.sentence: The beneficial insect, frequently a small wasp, then hones in on the chemical signal, finds the caterpillar and lays its eggs inside it (Figure 8.3).

83d7216b9c4d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/08%3A_Soil_Health_Plant_Health_and_Pests/8.05%3A_Plant_Defenses_Management_Practices_and_Pests
83d7216b9c4d.sentence: As the eggs develop, they kill the caterpillar.

6cf3936c7633.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/08%3A_Soil_Health_Plant_Health_and_Pests/8.05%3A_Plant_Defenses_Management_Practices_and_Pests
6cf3936c7633.sentence: When attacked by the western corn rootworm, a major pest, the roots of some varieties of corn have been shown to release a chemical that attracts a nematode that infects and kills rootworm larvae.

6c932a1579f0.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/08%3A_Soil_Health_Plant_Health_and_Pests/8.05%3A_Plant_Defenses_Management_Practices_and_Pests
6c932a1579f0.sentence: During the process of breeding corn in the United States, this ability to signal the beneficial nematode has apparently been lost.

8773908a72ab.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/08%3A_Soil_Health_Plant_Health_and_Pests/8.05%3A_Plant_Defenses_Management_Practices_and_Pests
8773908a72ab.sentence: However, it is present in wild relatives and in European corn varieties and is, therefore, available for reintroduction into U.S. corn varieties.

15b43eccd3d4.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/08%3A_Soil_Health_Plant_Health_and_Pests/8.05%3A_Plant_Defenses_Management_Practices_and_Pests
15b43eccd3d4.sentence: There is also evidence that plants near those with feeding damage sense the chemicals released by the wounded leaves and start making chemicals to defend themselves even before they are attacked.

6d3009704a5a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.02%3A_General_Approaches
6d3009704a5a.sentence: You can maintain or increase soil organic matter more easily when you use reduced-tillage systems, especially no-till and strip-till.

00b9f533fa72.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.02%3A_General_Approaches
00b9f533fa72.sentence: The decreased soil disturbance keeps biological activity and organic matter decomposition near the surface and helps maintain a soil structure that allows rainfall to infiltrate rapidly.

3e0f71f1c854.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.02%3A_General_Approaches
3e0f71f1c854.sentence: Leaving residue on the surface, or applying mulches, has a dramatic impact on soil biological activity.

74e70345f3a1.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.02%3A_General_Approaches
74e70345f3a1.sentence: It encourages the development of earthworm populations, maintains soil moisture and moderates temperature extremes.

24f045d83acf.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.02%3A_General_Approaches
24f045d83acf.sentence: Compared with conventional tillage, soil erosion is greatly reduced under minimum-tillage systems, which help keep organic matter and rich topsoil in place.

b5f4abf34525.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.02%3A_General_Approaches
b5f4abf34525.sentence: Any other practices that reduce soil erosion, such as contour tillage, strip cropping along the contours and terracing, also help maintain soil organic matter.

da11579b718e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.02%3A_General_Approaches
da11579b718e.sentence: In fact, it may be more important to rotate crops when large amounts of residue remain on the surface, as they may harbor insect and disease organisms.

daab1128c660.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.02%3A_General_Approaches
daab1128c660.sentence: These problems may be worse in monoculture with no-till practices than with conventional tillage.

684895076c97.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.02%3A_General_Approaches
684895076c97.sentence: A good analogy is to think of your soil as a bank account with credits and debits.

a0998340d171.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.02%3A_General_Approaches
a0998340d171.sentence: The credits are management practices that improve soil health, like manure additions, reduced tillage and cover crops.

d76077da620f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.02%3A_General_Approaches
d76077da620f.sentence: The debits are the ones that degrade the soil, like compaction from field traffic and intensive tillage (Table 24.1).

997c62c324f7.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.02%3A_General_Approaches
997c62c324f7.sentence: One farming system may result in a different balance sheet than another due to specific constraints.

bbcc18d980bd.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.02%3A_General_Approaches
bbcc18d980bd.sentence: For example, a daily harvest schedule means that you cannot avoid traffic on wet soils, and small-seeded crops require intensive tillage (at least in the planting row) in order to prepare a seedbed.

9c0e7ecda26b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.02%3A_General_Approaches
9c0e7ecda26b.sentence: Still, strive to optimize the system: If a “bad” practice, such as harvesting in a wet field that contains spoilable crops, is unavoidable, try to balance it with a “good” practice, thereby making your soil health account flush.

e5c962be5367.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.02%3A_General_Approaches
e5c962be5367.sentence: Also, you may have options to reduce the impacts of a bad practice, like controlling traffic to certain lanes to reduce unavoidable soil compaction.

eefd295929c4.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.04%3A_Practices_to_Help_Remedy_Specific_Constraints
eefd295929c4.sentence: They are listed in terms of two timelines: short term or intermittent, and long term.

599dfd53c3e7.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.04%3A_Practices_to_Help_Remedy_Specific_Constraints
599dfd53c3e7.sentence: The short-term recommendations provide relatively quick responses to soil health problems, and they may need to be repeated to prevent recurrence of the problem.

35d8ef524c6d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.04%3A_Practices_to_Help_Remedy_Specific_Constraints
35d8ef524c6d.sentence: The long-term approaches focus on management practices that don’t provide quick fixes but that address the concern more sustainably.

2f55b0b4729b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.04%3A_Practices_to_Help_Remedy_Specific_Constraints
2f55b0b4729b.sentence: You will probably note that the same practices are often recommended for different constraints because they address multiple concerns at the same time.

7d8fed6d214f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.04%3A_Practices_to_Help_Remedy_Specific_Constraints
7d8fed6d214f.sentence: We cannot be quite as precise for making recommendations regarding physical and biological constraints as we can be for nutrient problems because these systems are more complex and we don’t have as strong a research base.

d7b8a470fba8.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.04%3A_Practices_to_Help_Remedy_Specific_Constraints
d7b8a470fba8.sentence: Low aggregate stability | Fresh organic materials (shallow-rooted cover/rotation crops, manure, green clippings) | Reduced tillage, surface mulch, rotation with sod crops

f9a280d7c27f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.04%3A_Practices_to_Help_Remedy_Specific_Constraints
f9a280d7c27f.sentence: Low available water capacity | Stable organic materials (compost, crop residues high in lignin, biochar) | Reduced tillage, rotation with sod crops

d35d94f6d192.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.04%3A_Practices_to_Help_Remedy_Specific_Constraints
d35d94f6d192.sentence: Many fruit crops, such as brambles, citrus, grapes, apples and stone fruits, are perennials that take several years to establish and may be harvested for 20 or more years.

bfad1f42d2a8.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.04%3A_Practices_to_Help_Remedy_Specific_Constraints
bfad1f42d2a8.sentence: Similarly, landscaped areas in parks and gardens are intended to remain attractive for many years with minimal maintenance.

1dd50537c486.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.04%3A_Practices_to_Help_Remedy_Specific_Constraints
1dd50537c486.sentence: This makes it especially important to address soil health concerns up front and to avoid mistakes during the establishment years, which can have negative impacts long into the future.

2b4eadfad8e1.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.04%3A_Practices_to_Help_Remedy_Specific_Constraints
2b4eadfad8e1.sentence: For tree and vine crops, these evaluative steps should pay attention to deeper soil layers, especially the presence of hard pans, subsoil acidity and shallow water tables, because the quality of the fruits is often strongly influenced by deep roots.

972871d96687.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.04%3A_Practices_to_Help_Remedy_Specific_Constraints
972871d96687.sentence: It is often worthwhile to make one-time investments like drainage installation, in-row deep ripping and deep lime and compost incorporations, as these are difficult to perform after planting.

b2ca78dd5127.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.04%3A_Practices_to_Help_Remedy_Specific_Constraints
b2ca78dd5127.sentence: Post-establishment, the emphasis should be on managing the surface layer.

1137b834a710.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.04%3A_Practices_to_Help_Remedy_Specific_Constraints
1137b834a710.sentence: Avoiding compaction is important, and maintaining good surface mulches is generally also beneficial, depending on the crop type.

bab4bc0ce4cb.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.04%3A_Practices_to_Help_Remedy_Specific_Constraints
bab4bc0ce4cb.sentence: Most grain crop farms export a lot of nutrients and are managed with a net loss of organic matter.

a19f713b1c64.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.04%3A_Practices_to_Help_Remedy_Specific_Constraints
a19f713b1c64.sentence: Nevertheless, these farms provide a great deal of flexibility in adopting alternative soil management systems because a wide range of equipment is available for grain production systems.

c922ac7fc6b6.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.04%3A_Practices_to_Help_Remedy_Specific_Constraints
c922ac7fc6b6.sentence: You can promote soil health easily with reduced-tillage systems, especially no-till and strip-till.

f79a10156f8f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.04%3A_Practices_to_Help_Remedy_Specific_Constraints
f79a10156f8f.sentence: Well-drained, coarse-textured soils are especially well adapted to no-till systems, and finer-textured soils do well with strip-till or zone-till systems.

2b3019dabc82.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.04%3A_Practices_to_Help_Remedy_Specific_Constraints
2b3019dabc82.sentence: Regardless of the tillage system that is used, travel on soils only when they’re dry enough to resist compaction.

847315415498.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.04%3A_Practices_to_Help_Remedy_Specific_Constraints
847315415498.sentence: However, managing no-till cropping on soils that are easily compacted is quite a challenge because there are few options to relieve compaction once it occurs.

f9a47d717672.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.04%3A_Practices_to_Help_Remedy_Specific_Constraints
f9a47d717672.sentence: Controlled-traffic farming is a very promising approach, especially for such situations, although it may require adjustments of equipment and investment in a GPS guidance system.

217b7dc67e1b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.04%3A_Practices_to_Help_Remedy_Specific_Constraints
217b7dc67e1b.sentence: Even if you use minimum-tillage systems that leave significant quantities of residue on the surface and decrease the severity of erosion, you also should use sound crop rotations.

0dc28ff506b9.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.04%3A_Practices_to_Help_Remedy_Specific_Constraints
0dc28ff506b9.sentence: Consider ones that use grass or legume perennial forage crops, or a combination of the two.

7ec79071f0ed.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.04%3A_Practices_to_Help_Remedy_Specific_Constraints
7ec79071f0ed.sentence: Even bringing small grains into a row crop system (like corn and soybeans) can improve soil health and open up opportunities for cover crops.

14f996083b4c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.04%3A_Practices_to_Help_Remedy_Specific_Constraints
14f996083b4c.sentence: Soil health management is especially challenging on vegetable farms.

6784f2cffa82.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.04%3A_Practices_to_Help_Remedy_Specific_Constraints
6784f2cffa82.sentence: Many vegetable crops are sensitive to soil compaction and often pose greater challenges in pest management.

9ff5dece40ca.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.04%3A_Practices_to_Help_Remedy_Specific_Constraints
9ff5dece40ca.sentence: Vegetable lands have generally been worked hard over many years and have a long way to go toward improved soil health.

909db54efa16.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.04%3A_Practices_to_Help_Remedy_Specific_Constraints
909db54efa16.sentence: Most vegetable farms are not integrated with livestock production, and it is difficult to maintain a continuous supply of fresh organic matter.

47073a736323.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.04%3A_Practices_to_Help_Remedy_Specific_Constraints
47073a736323.sentence: Bringing manure, compost or other locally available sources of organic materials to the farm should be seriously considered.

ebb0970264e4.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.04%3A_Practices_to_Help_Remedy_Specific_Constraints
ebb0970264e4.sentence: Farms near urban areas may benefit from leaves and grass clippings, and municipal or food waste composts, which are increasingly available.

e7deacd0e0b1.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.04%3A_Practices_to_Help_Remedy_Specific_Constraints
e7deacd0e0b1.sentence: In such cases, care should be taken to ensure that the compost does not contain contaminants.

7d91ca785f99.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.04%3A_Practices_to_Help_Remedy_Specific_Constraints
7d91ca785f99.section: Vegetable Farms > More Is Not Always Better With Grapevines
7d91ca785f99.sentence: Vegetable cropping systems are often well adapted to the use of cover crops because the main cropping season is generally shorter than those for grain and forage crops.

980b5e6c5198.section: Vegetable Farms > More Is Not Always Better With Grapevines
980b5e6c5198.sentence: There is usually sufficient time for the growth of cover crops in the pre-, mid- or post-season to gain real benefits, even in colder climates, and vegetable growers often have a multitude of cover cropping options.

11d07fcdf6a7.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.04%3A_Practices_to_Help_Remedy_Specific_Constraints
11d07fcdf6a7.section: Vegetable Farms > More Is Not Always Better With Grapevines
11d07fcdf6a7.sentence: Using them as a mulch (or importing mulch materials from off the farm) appears to be a good system for certain fresh market vegetables, as it keeps the crop from direct contact with the ground, thereby reducing the potential for rot or disease.

8d5d16b489c5.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.04%3A_Practices_to_Help_Remedy_Specific_Constraints
8d5d16b489c5.section: Vegetable Farms > More Is Not Always Better With Grapevines
8d5d16b489c5.sentence: But many vegetable crops are highly susceptible to diseases, and selection of the right cover or rotation crop is critical.

215205df5622.sentence: For example, according to Cornell plant pathologist George Abawi, bean root rot is suppressed by rapeseed, crown vetch, wheat and rye but is actually enhanced by white clover.

6e7641b0069f.section: Vegetable Farms > More Is Not Always Better With Grapevines
6e7641b0069f.sentence: This complex interaction between soil, climate and vine is referred to as terroir.

9fac4cf07647.section: Vegetable Farms > More Is Not Always Better With Grapevines
9fac4cf07647.sentence: But the best wines generally come from soils that are not overly fertile and that allow for some water stress during the season.

8c99b9e0ae15.section: Vegetable Farms > More Is Not Always Better With Grapevines
8c99b9e0ae15.sentence: High organic matter and nitrogen contents in vineyard soils create overly abundant vegetative growth in grapevines, reducing fruit set and requiring repeated pruning.

6f0dc98e5780.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/24%3A_Putting_It_All_Together/24.04%3A_Practices_to_Help_Remedy_Specific_Constraints

6f0dc98e5780.sentence: Mild water stress and reduced root growth during the early summer (between bloom and the beginning of the ripening stage) increase the content of these pigments.

eaa811bb9ab9.sentence: Also, important traits of wines are enhanced by the presence of the grapes’ anthocyanin pigments, which contribute to both the taste and to the color of wine.

c678b6d798a5.sentence: Some of the world’s best wines are grown on soils that allow for deep rooting; are calcareous, sandy or gravelly; and are low in organic matter.

e47bc04e5371.sentence: Poor drainage and aeration are bad for wine quality.

8a50a3191c48.sentence: In fields, visual soil assessments generally require little time (less than an hour), minimal tools (a spade or shovel, and water), and offer immediate results.

74c941f809e7.sentence: It can be said that visual soil health assessments focus primarily on surface soil (unless pits are dug for a profile assessment) and on physical attributes, compared to biological and chemical attributes.

c18c8990a5f8.sentence: With a bit more effort and access to simple tools, visual interpretations about chemistry (soil pH) and biology (respiration, earthworm counts) can be done.

2b941bea8ffc.sentence: To help with visual soil health assessments, score cards have been developed as a simple tool to guide soil, plant, water, and animal observations on quality.

6aa63bfd24f9.sentence: As such, visual soil assessments may be more useful in inferring soil health status when combined with other analytical techniques.

95b272d639bf.sentence: As the weight of farm equipment has been increasing over recent decades so too has the force exerted on the soil.

b452bcaa7b2b.sentence: An increase in farm size plays a role, as having more ground to cover often means that in order to complete field operations in a timely manner, field activities like seeding, spraying, or harvesting may occur when conditions are too wet.

7b9752a8f0ae.sentence: Monitoring axel loads and tire inflation on field equipment as well as avoiding field activities when soils are wet can help avoid soil compaction.

1018dc33e392.sentence: Deep tillage, called subsoiling, with a chisel plow is expensive because it takes a lot of fuel and time.

38cf7df28b01.sentence: Tillage also needs to happen at a time of the year when the soil is dry enough to fracture and break up the plow pan (compaction layer), rather than smear and create a new deeper layer of soil compaction if soils are too wet.

95c4091c19d2.sentence: If the management practices that caused soil compaction in the first place do not change after the subsoiling, then action to alleviate compaction will likely be needed again after a few years.

f2e2c8e4a9b9.sentence: A soil’s various properties are frequently related to one another, and the interrelationships should be kept in mind.

4da417a85083.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/08%3A_Soil_Health_Plant_Health_and_Pests/8.02%3A_Soil_Properties_and_Their_Interrelationships
4da417a85083.sentence: Therefore, to prevent problems and develop soil habitat that is optimal for plants, we can’t just focus on one aspect of soil but must approach crop and soil management from a holistic point of view.

074702b71dc4.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/08%3A_Soil_Health_Plant_Health_and_Pests/8.02%3A_Soil_Properties_and_Their_Interrelationships
074702b71dc4.sentence: For example, when a soil is compacted, there is a loss of the large pore spaces, making it difficult or impossible for some of the larger soil organisms to move or even survive.

fc3f3236defa.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/08%3A_Soil_Health_Plant_Health_and_Pests/8.02%3A_Soil_Properties_and_Their_Interrelationships
fc3f3236defa.sentence: (You often don’t find earthworms in compacted soils.) In addition, compaction may make the soil waterlogged, causing chemical changes such as when nitrate (NO3-) is denitrified and lost to the atmosphere as nitrogen gas (N2) and the greenhouse gas N2O.

148943a63f00.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/08%3A_Soil_Health_Plant_Health_and_Pests/8.02%3A_Soil_Properties_and_Their_Interrelationships
148943a63f00.sentence: When soils contain a lot of sodium, common in arid and semiarid climates, aggregates may break apart and cause the soils to have few pore spaces for air exchange as well as water drainage into the subsoil.

4fea12c2ed13.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/08%3A_Soil_Health_Plant_Health_and_Pests/8.02%3A_Soil_Properties_and_Their_Interrelationships
4fea12c2ed13.sentence: Plants will grow poorly in a soil that has low organic matter content and degraded structure even if it contains an optimum amount of nutrients.

129b9f8ed25d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/08%3A_Soil_Health_Plant_Health_and_Pests/8.06%3A_Inoculate_With_Beneficial_Organisms
129b9f8ed25d.sentence: In this soil condition there would usually be little advantage to applying beneficial organisms to seeds or transplant roots.

08dff22031cf.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/08%3A_Soil_Health_Plant_Health_and_Pests/8.06%3A_Inoculate_With_Beneficial_Organisms
08dff22031cf.sentence: However, even with high biological diversity with active organisms, it is still recommended to inoculate legume seeds with the appropriate nitrogen-fixing rhizobia bacteria.

1e6863e11011.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/08%3A_Soil_Health_Plant_Health_and_Pests/8.06%3A_Inoculate_With_Beneficial_Organisms
1e6863e11011.sentence: But there is growing interest in the possible use of other microorganisms that might promote plant growth by producing hormone-like chemicals to increase growth, helping plants defend themselves from diseases and insects, helping plants better access water and nutrients, and helping plants through stresses such as drought and wet conditions.

7c27ab15e205.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/08%3A_Soil_Health_Plant_Health_and_Pests/8.06%3A_Inoculate_With_Beneficial_Organisms
7c27ab15e205.sentence: A variety of growth-promoting beneficial bacterial and fungal species have been explored, but there are no general recommendations for their use.

7b78030d1361.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/08%3A_Soil_Health_Plant_Health_and_Pests/8.06%3A_Inoculate_With_Beneficial_Organisms
7b78030d1361.sentence: These types of inoculants may be especially helpful in situations in which plants might be under stress: in soils that are low in organic matter, in soils that tend to be dry and/or have moderate to high salinity, and in fields or plots newly used for farming, especially urban soils.

b06b5714ab64.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/08%3A_Soil_Health_Plant_Health_and_Pests/8.06%3A_Inoculate_With_Beneficial_Organisms
b06b5714ab64.sentence: And when transplanting vegetables, it might be worthwhile to dip into solutions containing mycorrhizae if the soil is one in which cover crops weren’t grown that year and, especially, if you’re planting following a brassica (which does not form associations with mycorrhizal fungi).

0883170278a8.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/23%3A_How_Good_Are_Your_Soils/23.03%3A_Field_Indicators
0883170278a8.sentence: If the soil seals readily, the aggregates are not very stable and break down completely when wet.

2fd90316a089.sentence: If the soil doesn’t usually form a crust, you might take a sample of aggregates from the top 3–4 inches of soil from fields that seem to have different soil quality (or from a field and an adjacent fencerow area).

0044fb641c45.sentence: Gently drop a number of aggregates from each field into separate glass jars that are half filled with water (the aggregates should be completely submerged in water).

95213d02dd49.sentence: See whether they hold up or break apart (slake).

e1dad9674368.sentence: If the broken-up aggregates also disperse and stay in suspension, you may have an additional problem with high sodium content (a problem that usually occurs only in arid and semiarid regions).

31c27e4b0e79.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/23%3A_How_Good_Are_Your_Soils/23.03%3A_Field_Indicators
31c27e4b0e79.sentence: Is the plow layer fluffy, and does it mostly consist of granules of about a quarter inch in size?

a07aff3d7102.sentence: They should generally come apart easily in well-defined aggregates of several inches in size.

10f0cdc3f6fe.sentence: If the soil is compacted, it does not easily come apart in distinct units.

5ad96112847b.sentence: Score cards and laboratory tests have been developed to help farmers assess their soils, using scales to rate the health of soils.

995b663f8d02.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.06%3A_How_Do_You_Build_A_Healthy_High-Quality_Soil
995b663f8d02.sentence: In the field, you can evaluate the presence of earthworms, severity of erosion, ease of tillage, soil structure and color, extent of compaction, water infiltration rate and drainage status.

e008459124a7.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/01%3A_Healthy_Soils/1.06%3A_How_Do_You_Build_A_Healthy_High-Quality_Soil
e008459124a7.sentence: Then you rate crops growing on the soils by such characteristics as their general appearance, growth rates, root health, degree of resistance to drought and yield.

c81a7cfa6a02.sentence: It’s a good idea for all farmers to fill out such a scorecard for every major field or soil type on your farm every few years, or, alternatively, to send in soil to a lab that offers soil health analyses.

5eba26a1744e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/08%3A_Soil_Health_Plant_Health_and_Pests/8.04%3A_Ecological_Crop_and_Soil_Management
5eba26a1744e.sentence: This has been successfully practiced by planting Blue Hubbard squash on the perimeter of summer squash fields to intercept the striped cucumber beetle.
