2f4ce7987e6c.sentence: The push-pull system practiced in East Africa goes a step further by planting the low-growing legume Desmodium within corn rows as a repellent plant for stem borers (push), and grasses along the field perimeter to attract the adult insect moths (pull), while also providing nitrogen and suppressing weeds.

52c3493655b5.sentence: In this book we promote reduced tillage and retention of crop residues at the soil surface.

a0b80ae98bff.sentence: They occur usually with a spotty, circular distribution within certain parts of fields, and are more of a problem in certain geographic locations.

dee4d707ca65.sentence: Potatoes and beans appear to be less damaged by the pest, and it has been found that transplanted tomatoes do better than direct seeded ones when symphylans are present.

4ad496e0dfd4.sentence: Care is essential when importing organic amendments: You do not want to introduce this pest by accident.

d22c50f3b4fc.sentence: Some studies have shown that organically produced food can positively impact some indicators such as increased levels of antioxidants.

8da06f464e5f.sentence: But due to many other confounding factors (people who eat organic food typically have better diets, healthier lifestyles, and are wealthier), no study has been able to definitively correlate those with positive human health outcomes.

47c5822f5de7.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/08%3A_Soil_Health_Plant_Health_and_Pests/8.05%3A_Plant_Defenses_Management_Practices_and_Pests
47c5822f5de7.sentence: This phenomenon is called “induced resistance.” This causes the plant to form various hormones and proteins that enhance the plant’s defense system.

421c35deac18.sentence: The resistance is called systemic because the entire plant becomes resistant to a pathogen, even far away from the infection site.

38fdfdd9a222.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/08%3A_Soil_Health_Plant_Health_and_Pests/8.05%3A_Plant_Defenses_Management_Practices_and_Pests
38fdfdd9a222.sentence: There are two major types of induced resistance that are induced in response to signals from microorganisms: systemic acquired resistance (SAR) and induced systemic resistance (ISR) (Figure 8.4).

89d024f24c80.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/08%3A_Soil_Health_Plant_Health_and_Pests/8.05%3A_Plant_Defenses_Management_Practices_and_Pests
89d024f24c80.sentence: SAR is induced when plants are exposed to a pathogen or even to some organisms that do not produce disease.

db400c625803.sentence: Once the plant is exposed to the organism, it will produce the hormone salicylic acid and defense proteins that protect the plant from a wide range of pathogens.

8b816641c750.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/08%3A_Soil_Health_Plant_Health_and_Pests/8.05%3A_Plant_Defenses_Management_Practices_and_Pests
8b816641c750.sentence: ISR is induced when plant roots are exposed to specific plant growth, promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR) in the soil.

270438464b5e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/08%3A_Soil_Health_Plant_Health_and_Pests/8.05%3A_Plant_Defenses_Management_Practices_and_Pests
270438464b5e.sentence: Once the plants are exposed to these, hormones (jasmonate and ethylene) are produced that protect the plants from various pests.

6ddc5fd0df1f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/08%3A_Soil_Health_Plant_Health_and_Pests/8.05%3A_Plant_Defenses_Management_Practices_and_Pests
6ddc5fd0df1f.sentence: Some organic amendments have been shown to induce resistance in plants, and farmers who have very biologically active soils high in organic matter may already be taking advantage of it, as well as of other ways pests are controlled in such soils.

109fc726fea1.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/08%3A_Soil_Health_Plant_Health_and_Pests/8.05%3A_Plant_Defenses_Management_Practices_and_Pests
109fc726fea1.sentence: However, there currently are no reliable and cost-effective indicators to determine whether a soil amendment or soil is enhancing a plant’s defense mechanisms.

b68c0c37e4b2.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/08%3A_Soil_Health_Plant_Health_and_Pests/8.05%3A_Plant_Defenses_Management_Practices_and_Pests
b68c0c37e4b2.sentence: Beneficial bacteria in soil surrounding the root (the rhizosphere zone) provide a first line of defense against soil-borne diseases by competition or antagonism.

dbd053c5545d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/08%3A_Soil_Health_Plant_Health_and_Pests/8.05%3A_Plant_Defenses_Management_Practices_and_Pests
dbd053c5545d.sentence: If the disease organism (let’s say a fungus like Rhizoctonia solani that causes root diseases in seedlings of diverse crops such as wheat, rice, potatoes, tomatoes and sugarbeets) makes it through the rhizosphere and contacts the root surface, beneficial organisms living inside roots provide another line of defense by producing chemicals that attach the fungus.

fa71556d8ec1.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/08%3A_Soil_Health_Plant_Health_and_Pests/8.05%3A_Plant_Defenses_Management_Practices_and_Pests
fa71556d8ec1.sentence: Then the plant itself also can produce chemicals that help it resist the attack.

e9d99d6cab20.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/08%3A_Soil_Health_Plant_Health_and_Pests/8.05%3A_Plant_Defenses_Management_Practices_and_Pests
e9d99d6cab20.sentence: When plants are healthy and thriving, they are better able to defend themselves from attack and may also be less attractive to pests.

33c95e8d062e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/08%3A_Soil_Health_Plant_Health_and_Pests/8.05%3A_Plant_Defenses_Management_Practices_and_Pests
33c95e8d062e.sentence: When under one or more stresses, such as drought, nutrient limitations or soil compaction, plants may “unwittingly” send out signals to pests saying, in effect, “Come get me, I’m weak.” Vigorous plants, taller and with more extensive root systems, are also better competitors with weeds as they are able to shade them out or just compete well for water and nutrients.

d0b706dcc9c6.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/08%3A_Soil_Health_Plant_Health_and_Pests/8.05%3A_Plant_Defenses_Management_Practices_and_Pests
d0b706dcc9c6.sentence: Ecological soil and plant management is so critical to plant health because it helps to suppress pest populations and also influences, as we have just seen, the ability of plants to resist pests.

4c340cc83597.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/08%3A_Soil_Health_Plant_Health_and_Pests/8.05%3A_Plant_Defenses_Management_Practices_and_Pests
4c340cc83597.sentence: Developing optimal soil health is, therefore, the basis for management of crop pests on farms; it should be a central goal that underpins crop integrated pest management (IPM) programs.

538e251de0e0.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/08%3A_Soil_Health_Plant_Health_and_Pests/8.03%3A_Ecological_Principles_for_Agriculture

538e251de0e0.sentence: It is well established and known by most farmers that crop rotation can decrease many disease, insect, nematode and weed pressures.

cd81630f8a59.sentence: - Insect damage can be reduced by avoiding excess inorganic nitrogen levels in soils by using precision nitrogen management.

03094005713a.sentence: - Adequate nutrient levels reduce disease incidence.

3d32ed252450.sentence: For example, calcium applications have reduced diseases in crops such as wheat, peanuts, soybeans and peppers, while added potassium has reduced the incidence of fungal diseases in crops such as cotton, tomatoes and corn.

6f356a06b86c.sentence: - Damage from insects and diseases (such as fungal diseases of roots) can be decreased by lessening soil compaction.

2a0bea77e926.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/08%3A_Soil_Health_Plant_Health_and_Pests/8.03%3A_Ecological_Principles_for_Agriculture

2a0bea77e926.sentence: - The severity of root rots and leaf diseases can be reduced with composts that contain low levels of available nitrogen but still have some active organic matter.

c42c7d3b3966.sentence: Most cover crops, especially in reduced tillage systems, help keep mycorrhizal fungi spore counts high and promote higher rates of colonization by the beneficial fungi in the following crop.

e468af757443.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/08%3A_Soil_Health_Plant_Health_and_Pests/8.03%3A_Ecological_Principles_for_Agriculture

e468af757443.sentence: - Parasitic fungal and nematode infections can be suppressed by selected cover crops.

13db18dd2edc.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/08%3A_Soil_Health_Plant_Health_and_Pests/8.03%3A_Ecological_Principles_for_Agriculture

13db18dd2edc.sentence: - Residues of some cover crops, such as cereal rye, produce chemicals that reduce weed seed germination.

4534f3319ca9.section: Managing Soils And Crops To Minimize Pest Problems
4534f3319ca9.sentence: - Weed seed numbers are reduced in soils that have high biological activity, with both microorganisms and insects helping the process.

7e5b94d53d26.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Building_Soils_for_Better_Crops_-_Ecological_Management_for_Healthy_Soils_4e_(Magdoff_and_van_Es)/08%3A_Soil_Health_Plant_Health_and_Pests/8.03%3A_Ecological_Principles_for_Agriculture

7e5b94d53d26.sentence: - Weed seed predation by ground beetles is encouraged by reduced tillage and maintenance of surface residues.

b6b2a378282e.title: Urban agriculture

d5120f83f797.title: Urban agriculture
d5120f83f797.sentence: This contributes greatly to the functionality of the soil food web.

6e7042d11982.title: Soil contamination
6e7042d11982.sentence: Soil contamination, soil pollution, or land pollution as a part of land degradation is caused by the presence of xenobiotic (human-made) chemicals or other alteration in the natural soil environment.

abdcef5af456.title: Soil contamination
abdcef5af456.sentence: It is typically caused by industrial activity, agricultural chemicals or improper disposal of waste.

a02e9e818e50.title: Soil contamination
a02e9e818e50.sentence: The most common chemicals involved are petroleum hydrocarbons, polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons (such as naphthalene and benzo(a)pyrene), solvents, pesticides, and heavy metals.

fc838c64d33d.title: Soil contamination
fc838c64d33d.sentence: The concern over soil contamination stems primarily from health risks, from direct contact with contaminated soil or consumption of plants growing in contaminated soil, vapour inhalation from the contaminants, or from secondary contamination of water supplies within (groundwater) and underlying the soil (aquifer).

057a8f14aaeb.title: Soil
057a8f14aaeb.sentence: Soil contamination at low levels is often within a soil's capacity to treat and assimilate waste material.

6c35d6fb9a03.title: Soil
6c35d6fb9a03.sentence: Soil biota can treat waste by transforming it, mainly through microbial enzymatic activity.

eeb03b8439a3.title: Soil
eeb03b8439a3.sentence: Soil organic matter and soil clay minerals can adsorb the waste material and decrease its toxicity, although when in colloidal form they may transport the adsorbed contaminants to subsurface environments.

f0aba2a39483.title: Soil
f0aba2a39483.sentence: Exceeding treatment capacity can damage soil biota and limit soil function.

19339d76f3d1.title: Soil
19339d76f3d1.sentence: Derelict soils occur where industrial contamination or other development activity damages the soil to such a degree that the land cannot be used safely or productively, although some ecosystem services (e.g. decomposition) could still be provided by some derelict soils.

41522088b30b.title: Soil contamination
41522088b30b.sentence: Mapping of contaminated soil sites and the resulting cleanups are time-consuming and expensive tasks, and require expertise in geology, hydrology, chemistry, computer modelling, and GIS in Environmental Contamination, as well as an appreciation of the history of site pollution.

b0e43248597a.title: Soil contamination
b0e43248597a.sentence: In North America and Europe the extent of contaminated land is best known for as many of the countries in these areas have a legal framework to identify and deal with this environmental problem.

aaca898aac41.title: Soil contamination
aaca898aac41.sentence: Other countries tend to be less tightly regulated despite some of them have undergone significant industrialization and are searching for more regulation.

d63630948641.title: Soil contamination
d63630948641.sentence: According to the received data from member states in 2012, in the European Union the number of estimated potential contaminated sites was more than 2.5 million and the identified contaminated sites around 342 thousand.

e53c42eb0095.title: Soil contamination
e53c42eb0095.sentence: Mineral oil and heavy metals were the main contaminants contributing around 60% to soil contamination.

a34136293dc7.section: By country > People's Republic of China
a34136293dc7.sentence: According to a scientific sampling, 150 million mu (100,000 square kilometres) of China's cultivated land have been polluted, with contaminated water being used to irrigate a further 32.5 million mu (21,670 square kilometres) and another 2 million mu (1,300 square kilometres) covered or destroyed by solid waste.

77b6e4e85d41.title: Soil contamination
77b6e4e85d41.section: By country > People's Republic of China
77b6e4e85d41.sentence: In total, the area accounts for one-tenth of China's cultivatable land, and is mostly in economically developed areas.

09d12540c53d.title: Nonpoint source pollution
09d12540c53d.sentence: Nonpoint source (NPS) pollution refers to diffuse contamination (or pollution) of water or air that does not originate from a single discrete source.

84f39aef2f2e.title: Nonpoint source pollution
84f39aef2f2e.sentence: This type of pollution is often the cumulative effect of small amounts of contaminants gathered from a large area.

72479404fe1e.title: Nonpoint source pollution
72479404fe1e.sentence: It is in contrast to point source pollution which results from a single source.

b17e7b0babd3.title: Nonpoint source pollution
b17e7b0babd3.sentence: Nonpoint source pollution generally results from land runoff, precipitation, atmospheric deposition, drainage, seepage, or hydrological modification (rainfall and snowmelt) where tracing pollution back to a single source is difficult.

1cd8e7ca7e5c.title: Nonpoint source pollution
1cd8e7ca7e5c.sentence: Types of nonpoint source water pollution include sediment, nutrients, toxic contaminants and chemicals and pathogens.

ff5df4200df2.title: Nonpoint source pollution
ff5df4200df2.sentence: Principal sources of nonpoint source water pollution include: urban and suburban areas, agricultural operations, atmospheric inputs, highway runoff, forestry and mining operations, marinas and boating activities.

404b6d273d8e.title: Nonpoint source pollution
404b6d273d8e.sentence: Nonpoint source water pollution is difficult to control because it comes from the everyday activities of many different people, such as lawn fertilization, applying pesticides, road construction or building construction.

83d78db2b0cd.title: Nonpoint source pollution
83d78db2b0cd.sentence: Nonpoint source water pollution may derive from many different sources with no specific solutions or changes to rectify the problem, making it difficult to regulate.

064c6a03ef30.title: Nonpoint source pollution
064c6a03ef30.sentence: In agriculture, the leaching out of nitrogen compounds from fertilized agricultural lands is a nonpoint source water pollution.

bb1402b6efc2.title: Nonpoint source pollution
bb1402b6efc2.sentence: Nutrient runoff in storm water from "sheet flow" over an agricultural field or a forest are also examples of non-point source pollution.

b93c62161a16.title: Nonpoint source pollution
b93c62161a16.section: Principal sources (for water pollution) > Atmospheric inputs
b93c62161a16.sentence: Typically, industrial facilities, like factories, emit air pollution via a smokestack.

e867a88c60a3.title: Nonpoint source pollution
e867a88c60a3.section: Principal sources (for water pollution) > Atmospheric inputs
e867a88c60a3.sentence: Although this is a point source, due to the distributional nature, long-range transport, and multiple sources of the pollution, it can be considered as nonpoint source in the depositional area.

6a58d6322546.title: Nonpoint source pollution
6a58d6322546.section: Control (for water pollution) > Urban and suburban areas
6a58d6322546.sentence: Buffer strips provide a barrier of grass in between impervious paving material like parking lots and roads, and the closest body of water.

7e65d99177c7.title: Nonpoint source pollution
7e65d99177c7.section: Control (for water pollution) > Urban and suburban areas
7e65d99177c7.sentence: This allows the soil to absorb any pollution before it enters the local aquatic system.

cb8ce188a2f2.title: Nonpoint source pollution
cb8ce188a2f2.section: Control (for water pollution) > Urban and suburban areas
cb8ce188a2f2.sentence: Retention ponds can be built in drainage areas to create an aquatic buffer between runoff pollution and the aquatic environment.

5c06c704a33d.title: Nonpoint source pollution
5c06c704a33d.section: Control (for water pollution) > Urban and suburban areas
5c06c704a33d.sentence: Runoff and storm water drain into the retention pond allowing for the contaminants to settle out and become trapped in the pond.

fdbcb6cc98be.title: Nonpoint source pollution
fdbcb6cc98be.section: Control (for water pollution) > Urban and suburban areas
fdbcb6cc98be.sentence: The use of porous pavement allows for rain and storm water to drain into the ground beneath the pavement, reducing the amount of runoff that drains directly into the water body.

ff681aa80fe3.title: Nonpoint source pollution
ff681aa80fe3.section: Control (for water pollution) > Urban and suburban areas
ff681aa80fe3.sentence: Restoration methods such as constructing wetlands are also used to slow runoff as well as absorb contamination.

d7d5db77503f.title: Nonpoint source pollution
d7d5db77503f.sentence: Nonpoint source pollution is the leading cause of water pollution in the United States today, with polluted runoff from agriculture and hydromodification the primary sources.

b4fcc36d746c.title: Nutrient pollution
b4fcc36d746c.sentence: Nutrient pollution is a form of water pollution caused by too many nutrients entering the water.

83a889678e64.title: Nutrient pollution
83a889678e64.sentence: It is a primary cause of eutrophication of surface waters (lakes, rivers and coastal waters), in which excess nutrients, usually nitrogen or phosphorus, stimulate algal growth.

342b33aaa701.title: Nutrient pollution
342b33aaa701.sentence: Sources of nutrient pollution include surface runoff from farms, waste from septic tanks, feedlots, and emissions from burning fuels.

c47d61f09835.title: Nutrient pollution
c47d61f09835.sentence: Raw sewage, which is rich in nutrients, is also a contributing factor when dumped in water bodies.

733eb9b32f79.title: Nutrient pollution
733eb9b32f79.sentence: Agricultural production relies heavily on the use of natural and synthetic fertilizers.

ff3ee8911afb.title: Nutrient pollution
ff3ee8911afb.sentence: These often contain high levels of nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium.

b207e55f2391.title: Nutrient pollution
b207e55f2391.sentence: When nitrogen and phosphorus are not fully used by the growing plants, they are lost from the farm fields and negatively impact air and downstream water quality.

adf551130ecb.title: Nonpoint source pollution
adf551130ecb.sentence: Phosphorus is most often transported to water bodies via soil erosion because many forms of phosphorus tend to be adsorbed on to soil particles.

d54565a133fb.title: Nonpoint source pollution
d54565a133fb.sentence: Nitrogen is most often transported by water as nitrate (NO3).

a137583bec54.title: Nonpoint source pollution
a137583bec54.sentence: Since the nitrate is generally already incorporated into the soil, the water traveling through the soil (i.e., interflow and tile drainage) is the most likely to transport it, rather than surface runoff.

1ae168274238.title: Nutrient pollution
1ae168274238.sentence: Excess nitrogen causes environmental problems such as harmful algal blooms, hypoxia, acid rain, nitrogen saturation in forests, and climate change.

b827d097d2d9.title: Nutrient pollution
b827d097d2d9.sentence: Human health effects include excess nitrate in drinking water (blue baby syndrome) and disinfection by-products in drinking water.

ed8c46495080.title: Nutrient pollution
ed8c46495080.sentence: Swimming in water affected by a harmful algal bloom can cause skin rashes and respiratory problems.

c596bbba7adb.title: Nutrient pollution
c596bbba7adb.sentence: Nutrient pollution can have economic impacts due to increasing water treatment costs, commercial fishing, shellfish losses, recreational fishing losses, and reduced tourism income.

686cd1e21636.title: Nutrient pollution
686cd1e21636.sentence: These include installing buffer zones of vegetation around farms or artificial wetlands to absorb excess nutrients.

60a8e63d76d7.title: Nutrient pollution
60a8e63d76d7.sentence: For instance, farms can create artificial wetlands, which help remove nutrient run-off.

ef3198503619.title: Nutrient pollution
ef3198503619.sentence: Finally, by vegetating drainage ditches, there is another opportunity for excess nutrients to be captured.

21b114ed8560.title: Nutrient pollution
21b114ed8560.sentence: Additionally, better wastewater treatment and reducing sewage dumping can help limit nutrient discharge into water systems.

54372f85e54f.title: Nutrient pollution
54372f85e54f.sentence: Finally, countries can create a permit system under the polluter pays principle.

9e0da5052955.title: Nonpoint source pollution
9e0da5052955.section: Principal types (for water pollution) > Toxic contaminants and chemicals
9e0da5052955.sentence: Inorganic compounds, including heavy metals like lead, mercury, zinc, and cadmium are resistant to breakdown.

96ffc684a885.title: Nonpoint source pollution
96ffc684a885.section: Principal types (for water pollution) > Toxic contaminants and chemicals
96ffc684a885.sentence: These contaminants can come from a variety of sources including human sewage sludge, mining operations, vehicle emissions, fossil fuel combustion, urban runoff, industrial operations and landfills.

c5d5b02fd925.title: Soil contamination
c5d5b02fd925.section: By country > People's Republic of China
c5d5b02fd925.sentence: Recent survey shows that 19% of the agricultural soils are contaminated with heavy metals and metalloids, and the rate of contamination still increases dramatically.

3350622348e0.title: Soil contamination
3350622348e0.section: By country > People's Republic of China
3350622348e0.sentence: An estimated 12 million tonnes of grain are contaminated by heavy metals every year, causing direct losses of 20 billion yuan ($2.57 billion USD).

ac4bc48f2e1c.title: Soil contamination
ac4bc48f2e1c.sentence: A study investigating the heavy metal pollution in the vicinity of the smelter reveals that elevated levels of nickel and copper were found in the soil; values going as high as 5,104ppm Ni, and 2,892 ppm Cu within a 1.1 km range of the smelter location.

06bd08e2f8df.title: Soil contamination
06bd08e2f8df.sentence: Furthermore, upon examining the different vegetation surrounding the smelter it was evident that they too had been affected; the results show that the plants contained nickel, copper and aluminium as a result of soil contamination.

a758699b517b.title: Environmental remediation
a758699b517b.sentence: Migration of metal contaminants must also be considered whenever modifying subsurface oxidation-reduction potential.

9a58e6f77576.title: Environmental remediation
9a58e6f77576.sentence: Certain metals are more soluble in oxidizing environments while others are more mobile in reducing environments.

9d69945a7357.title: Colloid
9d69945a7357.sentence: Radionuclides and heavy metals easily sorb onto colloids suspended in water.

6bd41bfb9dfb.title: Bioavailability (soil)
6bd41bfb9dfb.sentence: Ionic compounds, such as heavy metals, can be precipitated into the solid phase.

1357992561d9.title: Bioremediation
1357992561d9.sentence: Unlike organic pollutants, metals (or more properly, metal ions and metal compounds) cannot be degraded.

a6e8960fdb69.title: Bioremediation
a6e8960fdb69.sentence: The mobility of the metals could be decreased, resulting in their immobilization.

564beb208e9f.title: Bioremediation
564beb208e9f.sentence: For example, reduction of the more mobile U(VI) species affords the less mobile U(IV) derivatives.

b00914b0a50e.title: Bioremediation
b00914b0a50e.sentence: Again, this approach remains more conceptual than practical.

e54ba3ef69f8.title: Heavy metals
e54ba3ef69f8.sentence: Some heavy metals are either essential nutrients (typically iron, cobalt, copper, and zinc), or relatively harmless (such as ruthenium, silver, and indium), but can be toxic in larger amounts or certain forms.

cd9876c0ff22.title: Heavy metals
cd9876c0ff22.sentence: Other heavy metals, such as arsenic, cadmium, mercury, and lead, are highly poisonous.

cae35aece5c8.title: Heavy metals
cae35aece5c8.sentence: The definitions surveyed in this article encompass up to 96 of the 118 known chemical elements; only mercury, lead, and bismuth meet all of them.

d4b620c7a6ca.title: Heavy metals
d4b620c7a6ca.sentence: A heavy metal may be defined on the basis of density, atomic number, or chemical behaviour.

2ebde8e1220c.title: Heavy metals
2ebde8e1220c.sentence: The International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry (IUPAC), which standardizes nomenclature, says "the term 'heavy metals' is both meaningless and misleading".

81d59c9da387.title: Environmental remediation
81d59c9da387.sentence: Environmental remediation is the cleanup of hazardous substances dealing with the removal, treatment and containment of pollution or contaminants from environmental media such as soil, groundwater, sediment.

8e26c726a049.title: Soil
8e26c726a049.sentence: Remediation of derelict soil uses principles of geology, physics, chemistry and biology to degrade, attenuate, isolate or remove soil contaminants to restore soil functions and values.

fac8c79b6178.title: Soil contamination
fac8c79b6178.sentence: Cleanup or environmental remediation is analyzed by environmental scientists who utilize field measurement of soil chemicals and also apply computer models (GIS in Environmental Contamination) for analyzing transport and fate of soil chemicals.

241b5f048447.title: Environmental remediation
241b5f048447.sentence: Remediation technologies are many and varied but can generally be categorized into ex-situ and in-situ methods.

47b62bfb0fab.title: Environmental remediation
47b62bfb0fab.sentence: Ex-situ methods involve excavation of affected soils and subsequent treatment at the surface as well as extraction of contaminated groundwater and treatment at the surface.

25d691dfb936.title: Environmental remediation
25d691dfb936.sentence: In-situ methods seek to treat the contamination without removing the soils or groundwater.

8004ca21e84d.title: Environmental remediation
8004ca21e84d.sentence: Traditional remediation approaches consist of soil excavation and disposal to landfill and groundwater "pump and treat".

6eb85923c030.title: Soil contamination
6eb85923c030.sentence: - Excavate soil and take it to a disposal site away from ready pathways for human or sensitive ecosystem contact.

cb1b4407f7e4.title: Soil contamination
cb1b4407f7e4.sentence: This technique also applies to dredging of bay muds or navigable canals containing toxicants.

29b88f644700.title: Soil contamination
29b88f644700.sentence: - Aeration of soils at the contaminated site, with attendant risk of creating air pollution.

cd91d88c78c2.title: Soil contamination
cd91d88c78c2.sentence: - Thermal remediation (thermal desorption) by introduction of heat to raise subsurface temperatures sufficiently high to volatilize chemical contaminants out of the soil for vapor extraction.

a956c2b648be.title: Soil contamination
a956c2b648be.sentence: - Extraction of groundwater or soil vapor with an active electromechanical system (electrokinetic soil flushing (EKSF)), with subsequent air stripping of the contaminants from the extract.

5dccce336155.title: Soil contamination
5dccce336155.sentence: - Bioremediation, involving microbial digestion of certain organic chemicals.

db43a6d1f7a3.title: Soil contamination
db43a6d1f7a3.sentence: - Phytoremediation, or using plants (such as willow) to extract heavy metals.

f91dd7d86e58.title: Soil contamination
f91dd7d86e58.sentence: - Mycoremediation, or using fungi to metabolize contaminants and accumulate heavy metals.

53b7ecc0f6f0.title: Environmental remediation
53b7ecc0f6f0.sentence: In-situ technologies include but are not limited to: solidification and stabilization, soil vapor extraction, permeable reactive barriers, monitored natural attenuation, bioremediation-phytoremediation, chemical oxidation, steam-enhanced extraction and in situ thermal desorption and have been used extensively in the USA.

1300a0b246dd.title: Environmental remediation
1300a0b246dd.sentence: Contaminants can be removed from a site or controlled.

660a446c481f.title: Environmental remediation
660a446c481f.sentence: One option for control are barrier walls, which can be temporary to prevent contamination during treatment and removal, or more permanent.

3442242ccd59.title: Environmental remediation
3442242ccd59.sentence: The waste material can also be contained by physical barriers like slurry walls.

a9dc1cf26d1a.title: Environmental remediation
a9dc1cf26d1a.sentence: Barrier walls must be constructed of impermeable materials and resistant to deterioration from contact with waste, for the lifespan of the barrier wall.

17483954f4c2.title: Environmental remediation
17483954f4c2.sentence: Remediation may be required by regulations before development of land revitalization projects.

8d3951b65cc3.title: Environmental remediation
8d3951b65cc3.sentence: Remedial action is generally subject to an array of regulatory requirements, and may also be based on assessments of human health and ecological risks where no legislative standards exist, or where standards are advisory.

b69b6491c5cc.title: Bioremediation
b69b6491c5cc.sentence: Bioremediation broadly refers to any process wherein a biological system (typically bacteria, microalgae, fungi in mycoremediation, and plants in phytoremediation), living or dead, is employed for removing environmental pollutants from air, water, soil, fuel gasses, industrial effluents etc., in natural or artificial settings.

2f7aeeef2964.title: Bioremediation
2f7aeeef2964.sentence: The natural ability of organisms to absorb, accumulate, and degrade common and emerging pollutants has attracted the use of biological resources in treatment of contaminated environment.

b74fe20a9fb5.title: Bioremediation
b74fe20a9fb5.sentence: In comparison to conventional physicochemical treatment methods bioremediation may offer advantages as it aims to be sustainable, eco-friendly, cheap, and scalable.

0822323252a7.title: Bioremediation
0822323252a7.sentence: Most bioremediation is inadvertent, involving native organisms.

21aaa4e14cb6.title: Bioremediation
21aaa4e14cb6.sentence: Research on bioremediation is heavily focused on stimulating the process by inoculation of a polluted site with organisms or supplying nutrients to promote their growth.

35d4dc3fdf18.title: Bioremediation
35d4dc3fdf18.sentence: Oxidations enhance the water-solubility of organic compounds and their susceptibility to further degradation by further oxidation and hydrolysis.

6664b696a9f4.title: Bioremediation
6664b696a9f4.sentence: Ultimately biodegradation converts hydrocarbons to carbon dioxide and water.

40fb7dbdbde2.title: Bioremediation
40fb7dbdbde2.sentence: Most bioremediation processes involve oxidation-reduction reactions where either an electron acceptor (commonly oxygen) is added to stimulate oxidation of a reduced pollutant (e.g. hydrocarbons) or an electron donor (commonly an organic substrate) is added to reduce oxidized pollutants (nitrate, perchlorate, oxidized metals, chlorinated solvents, explosives and propellants).

6c0ac7ed9e80.title: Bioremediation
6c0ac7ed9e80.sentence: While organic pollutants are susceptible to biodegradation, heavy metals cannot be degraded, but rather oxidized or reduced.

e614078f6871.title: Bioremediation
e614078f6871.sentence: For heavy metals, bioremediation offers few solutions.

ff045d5b02ca.title: Bioremediation
ff045d5b02ca.sentence: Bioremediation techniques can be classified as (i) in situ techniques, which treat polluted sites directly, vs (ii) ex situ techniques which are applied to excavated materials.

200afee6381d.title: Bioremediation
200afee6381d.sentence: The main challenge to bioremediations is rate: the processes are slow.

7c1505203b81.title: Bioremediation
7c1505203b81.sentence: In 2010 there was a massive oil spill in the Gulf of Mexico.

284ac21fed43.title: Bioremediation
284ac21fed43.sentence: Populations of bacteria and archaea were used to rejuvenate the coast after the oil spill.

70b2e877383b.title: Bioremediation
70b2e877383b.sentence: These microorganisms over time have developed metabolic networks that can utilize hydrocarbons such as oil and petroleum as a source of carbon and energy.

2b09a19c1c5e.title: Phytoremediation
2b09a19c1c5e.sentence: Phytoremediation technologies use living plants to clean up soil, air and water contaminated with pollutants.

b7b3a4840567.title: Phytoremediation
b7b3a4840567.sentence: It is a type of bioremediation.

361b25486692.title: Phytoremediation
361b25486692.sentence: Phytoremediation is proposed as a sustainable alternative to conventional remediation methods, although it has never been used at large scales.

cdf6e72d82d1.title: Phytoremediation
cdf6e72d82d1.sentence: Other forms of bioremediation, such as those employing microorganisms, have so far been more successful.

f3668c972db4.title: Phytoremediation
f3668c972db4.sentence: Major phytoremediation mechanisms include phytoextraction, phytostabilization, phytovolatilization, and phytofiltration.

6ea2c32700e4.title: Phytoremediation
6ea2c32700e4.sentence: Phytodegradation (also called phytotransformation) is the use of plants to degrade organic pollutants.

59796f89d1c1.title: Phytoremediation
59796f89d1c1.sentence: Phytostimulation (or rhizodegradation) is the enhancement of soil microbial activity for the degradation of organic contaminants, typically by organisms that associate with roots.

6c6eff2505a4.title: Phytoremediation
6c6eff2505a4.sentence: Biological hydraulic containment occurs when some plants, like poplars, draw water upwards through the soil into the roots and out through the plant, which decreases the movement of soluble contaminants downwards, deeper into the site and into the groundwater.

bb5b56db5c3e.title: Phytoremediation
bb5b56db5c3e.sentence: Phytodesalination uses halophytes (plants adapted to saline soil) to extract salt from the soil to improve its fertility.

4176308d5f00.title: Phytoremediation
4176308d5f00.sentence: Breeding programs and genetic engineering are powerful methods for enhancing natural phytoremediation capabilities, or for introducing new capabilities into plants.

a664b0148dbc.title: Phytoremediation
a664b0148dbc.sentence: For example, genes encoding a nitroreductase from a bacterium were inserted into tobacco and showed faster removal of TNT and enhanced resistance to the toxic effects of TNT.

6b48032a3994.title: Phytoremediation
6b48032a3994.sentence: PGPB have been shown to assist heavily with enhancing the transport of soil pollutants like heavy metals from the soil into the roots of hyperaccumulators via phytostimulation.

7b5abb109d62.title: Phytoremediation
7b5abb109d62.sentence: PGPB increase transport speed by improving plant metabolic processes and biomass production, and by producing chelating or solubilizing agents that mobilize heavy metals, overall improving phytoremediation efficiency.

40c3cef2412b.title: Phytoremediation
40c3cef2412b.sentence: Some natural, biodegradable compounds, such as exogenous polyamines, allow plants to tolerate higher concentrations of pollutants and increase pollutant uptake.

4e7e9946b137.title: Mycoremediation
4e7e9946b137.sentence: Mycoremediation (from ancient Greek μύκης (mukēs), meaning "fungus", and the suffix -remedium, in Latin meaning 'restoring balance') is a form of bioremediation in which fungi-based remediation methods are used to decontaminate the environment.

88304557a13b.title: Mycoremediation
88304557a13b.sentence: Fungi have been proven to be a cheap, effective and environmentally sound way for removing a wide array of contaminants from damaged environments or wastewater.

7690bc91e477.title: Mycoremediation
7690bc91e477.sentence: These contaminants include heavy metals, organic pollutants, textile dyes, leather tanning chemicals and wastewater, petroleum fuels, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, pharmaceuticals and personal care products, pesticides and herbicides in land, fresh water, and marine environments.

cd6856dfc1f7.title: Mycoremediation
cd6856dfc1f7.sentence: Fungi, thanks to their non-specific enzymes, are able to break down many kinds of substances including pharmaceuticals and fragrances that are normally recalcitrant to bacteria degradation, such as paracetamol (also known as acetaminophen).

e00362c64143.title: Mycoremediation
e00362c64143.sentence: Mycoremediation is a cheaper method of remediation, and it doesn't usually require expensive equipment.

e6a04f8f39d7.title: Mycoremediation
e6a04f8f39d7.sentence: For this reason, it is often used in small scale applications, such as mycofiltration of domestic wastewater, and industrial effluent filtration.

efc760944c98.title: Mycoremediation
efc760944c98.sentence: Soils soaked with creosote contain high concentrations of PAH and in order to stop the spread, mycoremediation has proven to be the most successful strategy.

7c5bfddf3fd7.title: Mycoremediation
7c5bfddf3fd7.sentence: The byproducts of the remediation can be valuable materials themselves, such as enzymes (like laccase), edible or medicinal mushrooms, making the remediation process even more profitable.

e6aad71fe5a7.title: Mycoremediation
e6aad71fe5a7.sentence: Antarctic fungi species such as Metschnikowia sp., Cryptococcus gilvescens, Cryptococcus victoriae, Pichia caribbica and Leucosporidium creatinivorum can withstand extreme cold and still provide efficient biodegradation of contaminants.

f46914fce803.title: Mycoremediation
f46914fce803.sentence: Due to the nature of colder, remote environments like Antarctica, usual methods of contaminant remediation, such as the physical removal of contaminated media, can prove costly.

4594db3bd66b.title: Mycoremediation
4594db3bd66b.sentence: These species of fungi are able to assimilate and degrade compounds such as phenols, n-Hexadecane, toluene, and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons in these harsh conditions.

61fe36495f87.title: Mycoremediation
61fe36495f87.sentence: These compounds are found in crude oil and refined petroleum.

8c1afb0d4752.title: Mycoremediation
8c1afb0d4752.sentence: Fungi such as Rhodotorula taiwanensis can possibly be used in the bioremediation of radioactive waste due to their low pH and radiation resistant properties.

b5d5c46b82dc.title: Mycoremediation
b5d5c46b82dc.sentence: Mycoremediation can even be used for fire management with the encapsulation method.

f72ef3014509.title: Mycoremediation
f72ef3014509.sentence: This process consists of using fungal spores coated with agarose in a pellet form, which is introduced to a substrate in the burnt forest, breaking down toxins and stimulating growth.

f4b9925d53a5.title: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon
f4b9925d53a5.sentence: A polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) is any member of a class of organic compounds that is composed of multiple fused aromatic rings.

af6c37a94589.title: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon
af6c37a94589.sentence: Most are produced by the incomplete combustion of organic matter—by engine exhaust fumes, tobacco, incinerators, in roasted meats and cereals, or when biomass burns at lower temperatures as in forest fires.

debc1259df00.title: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon
debc1259df00.sentence: Many of them are also found in fossil fuel deposits such as coal and in petroleum.

558fd8a857f9.title: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon
558fd8a857f9.section: Distribution in the environment > Environmental pollution
558fd8a857f9.sentence: Oil spills, creosote, coal mining dust, and other fossil fuel sources can also distribute PAHs in the environment.

9556365b8706.title: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon
9556365b8706.section: Distribution in the environment > Environmental pollution
9556365b8706.sentence: Soil and river sediment near industrial sites such as creosote manufacturing facilities can be highly contaminated with PAHs.

fcc9ef072850.title: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon
fcc9ef072850.section: Distribution in the environment > Environmental pollution
fcc9ef072850.sentence: Two- and three-ringed PAHs can disperse widely while dissolved in water or as gases in the atmosphere, while PAHs with higher molecular weights can disperse locally or regionally adhered to particulate matter that is suspended in air or water until the particles land or settle out of the water column.

8807fae9ca68.title: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon
8807fae9ca68.section: Distribution in the environment > Environmental pollution
8807fae9ca68.sentence: PAHs have a strong affinity for organic carbon, and thus highly organic sediments in rivers, lakes, and the ocean can be a substantial sink for PAHs.

3de81a9cf25c.title: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon
3de81a9cf25c.section: Distribution in the environment > Urban soils
3de81a9cf25c.sentence: The British Geological Survey reported the amount and distribution of PAH compounds including parent and alkylated forms in urban soils at 76 locations in Greater London.

d4650bdba4aa.title: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon
d4650bdba4aa.section: Distribution in the environment > Urban soils
d4650bdba4aa.sentence: The study showed that parent (16 PAH) content ranged from 4 to 67 mg/kg (dry soil weight) and an average PAH concentration of 18 mg/kg (dry soil weight) whereas the total PAH content (33 PAH) ranged from 6 to 88 mg/kg and fluoranthene and pyrene were generally the most abundant PAHs.

6f4b33124467.title: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon
6f4b33124467.section: Distribution in the environment > Urban soils
6f4b33124467.sentence: London soils contained more stable four- to six-ringed PAHs which were indicative of combustion and pyrolytic sources, such as coal and oil burning and traffic-sourced particulates.

fa545a4ae063.title: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon
fa545a4ae063.sentence: Biological degradation by microbes is a dominant form of PAH transformation in the environment.

0513bf662f7a.title: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon
0513bf662f7a.sentence: Soil-consuming invertebrates such as earthworms are claimed to speed PAH degradation, either through direct metabolism or by improving the conditions for microbial transformations.

0fe4964b4d71.title: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon
0fe4964b4d71.sentence: Most vertebrates metabolize and excrete PAHs relatively rapidly.

9c0c05a853b5.title: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon
9c0c05a853b5.sentence: Tissue concentrations of PAHs do not increase (biomagnify) from the lowest to highest levels of food chains.

f289e176c654.title: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon
f289e176c654.sentence: Exposure to PAHs can lead to different types of cancer, fetal development complications, and cardiovascular issues.

9cf5cc6196ef.title: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon
9cf5cc6196ef.sentence: Some governmental bodies, including the European Union as well as NIOSH and the United States Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), regulate concentrations of PAHs in air, water, and soil.

179714c03e07.title: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon
179714c03e07.section: Distribution in the environment > Urban soils
179714c03e07.sentence: Benzo[a]pyrene (BaP), the most toxic of the parent PAHs, is widely considered a key marker PAH for environmental assessments; the normal background concentration of BaP in the London urban sites was 6.9 mg/kg (dry soil weight).

d74353b96643.title: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon
d74353b96643.sentence: Managed burning of moorland vegetation in the UK has been shown to generate PAHs which become incorporated into the peat surface.

f1a3dce17444.title: Pesticide
f1a3dce17444.sentence: Pesticides are substances that are used to control pests.

bd8dd581ca1f.title: Pesticide
bd8dd581ca1f.sentence: They include herbicides, insecticides, nematicides, fungicides, and many others (see table).

1d2f9bf0aae0.title: Pesticide
1d2f9bf0aae0.sentence: In general, a pesticide is a chemical or biological agent (such as a virus, bacterium, or fungus) that deters, incapacitates, kills, or otherwise discourages pests.

0f687c283edd.title: Pesticide
0f687c283edd.sentence: The most common of these are herbicides, which account for approximately 50% of all pesticide use globally.

b39d69415811.title: Pesticide
b39d69415811.sentence: Total pesticides use in agriculture in 2023 was 3.73 million tonnes of active ingredients (Mt), a 2% decrease compared with 2022, a 14 percent increase in a decade, and a doubling since 1990.

646d5a901687.title: Pesticide
646d5a901687.sentence: Pesticides use per area of cropland in 2023 was 2.40 kg per hectare (kg/ha), a decrease of 2 percent compared with 2022; use per value of agricultural production was 0.88 g per international dollar (g/I$) (−4%); and use per person was 0.45 kg per capita (kg/cap) (−3%).

f56c4f76040f.title: Pesticide
f56c4f76040f.sentence: Over 98% of sprayed insecticides and 95% of herbicides reach a destination other than their target species, including non-target species, air, water and soil.

44dbca28e2ed.title: Pesticide
44dbca28e2ed.sentence: The Stockholm Convention on Persistent Organic Pollutants banned all persistent pesticides, in particular DDT and other organochlorine pesticides, which were stable and lipophilic, and thus able to bioaccumulate in the body and the food chain. and which spread throughout the planet.

c738aae75e75.title: Pesticide
c738aae75e75.sentence: Because the half life in soil is long (for DDT 2–15 years) residues can still be detected in humans at levels 5 to 10 times lower than found in the 1970s.

4508f47bac20.title: Pesticide
4508f47bac20.sentence: Pesticides now have to be degradable in the environment.

7cd58cc8bf08.title: Pesticide
7cd58cc8bf08.sentence: For example, the presence of halogens within a chemical structure often slows down degradation in an aerobic environment.

612b569856ad.title: Pesticide
612b569856ad.sentence: Adsorption to soil may retard pesticide movement, but also may reduce bioavailability to microbial degraders.

3e9adb9adf74.title: Pesticide
3e9adb9adf74.sentence: Pests can develop a resistance to the pesticide (pesticide resistance), necessitating a new pesticide.

274de7c64d1e.title: Pesticide
274de7c64d1e.sentence: Alternatively a greater dose of the pesticide can be used to counteract the resistance, although this will cause a worsening of the ambient pollution problem.

61595629d8fc.title: Eutrophication
61595629d8fc.sentence: Eutrophication is a general term describing a process in which nutrients accumulate in a body of water, resulting in an increased growth of organisms that may deplete the oxygen in the water; i.e. the process of too many plants growing on the surface of a river, lake, etc., often because chemicals that are used to help crops grow have been carried there by rain.

9eafca01e050.title: Eutrophication
9eafca01e050.sentence: Eutrophication may occur naturally or as a result of human actions.

ab33817f4ee9.title: Eutrophication
ab33817f4ee9.sentence: Eutrophication can be a natural process and occurs naturally through the gradual accumulation of sediment and nutrients.

4d30ca9015ea.title: Eutrophication
4d30ca9015ea.sentence: The main difference between natural and anthropogenic eutrophication is that the natural process is very slow, occurring on geological time scales.

a83f4f7ea683.title: Eutrophication
a83f4f7ea683.sentence: Manmade, or cultural, eutrophication occurs when sewage, industrial wastewater, fertilizer runoff, and other nutrient sources are released into the environment.

d911e3a098b1.title: Eutrophication
d911e3a098b1.sentence: Phosphorus is the limiting factor for plant growth in most freshwater ecosystems, and because phosphate adheres tightly to soil particles and sinks in areas such as wetlands and lakes, due to its prevalence nowadays more and more phosphorus is accumulating inside freshwater bodies.

cb7b7d484896.title: Eutrophication
cb7b7d484896.sentence: In marine ecosystems, nitrogen is the primary limiting nutrient; nitrous oxide (created by the combustion of fossil fuels) and its deposition in the water from the atmosphere has led to an increase in nitrogen levels, and also the heightened levels of eutrophication in the ocean.

134267fdc526.title: Nonpoint source pollution
134267fdc526.sentence: Excess amounts of phosphorus in aquatic systems (particularly freshwater lakes, reservoirs, and ponds) leads to proliferation of microscopic algae called phytoplankton.

a3543292db2e.title: Nonpoint source pollution
a3543292db2e.sentence: Similar to phosphorus in fresh-waters, excess amounts of bioavailable nitrogen in marine systems lead to eutrophication and algae blooms.

64c8247f8aad.title: Eutrophication
64c8247f8aad.sentence: Algal blooms can shade out benthic plants thereby altering the overall plant community.

2241619fe20d.title: Eutrophication
2241619fe20d.sentence: When algae die off, their degradation by bacteria removes oxygen, potentially, generating anoxic conditions.

1587214b970f.title: Eutrophication
1587214b970f.sentence: This anoxic environment kills off aerobic organisms (e.g. fish and invertebrates) in the water body.

e5b43c84936f.title: Nutrient pollution
e5b43c84936f.section: Impacts > Excess growth of algae (harmful algal blooms); and biodiversity loss
e5b43c84936f.sentence: Too much harmful algae blooms are referred to as 'red tide'.

0866ebbc75c4.title: Nutrient pollution
0866ebbc75c4.section: Impacts > Excess growth of algae (harmful algal blooms); and biodiversity loss
0866ebbc75c4.sentence: When they finally die they release harmful toxins into the water.

ac2bae812cd6.title: Nutrient pollution
ac2bae812cd6.section: Impacts > Excess growth of algae (harmful algal blooms); and biodiversity loss
ac2bae812cd6.sentence: This kills even more life, resulting in 'dead zones' where there is no life.

e9ed0ea53770.title: Nutrient pollution
e9ed0ea53770.section: Impacts > Excess growth of algae (harmful algal blooms); and biodiversity loss

ffa9250d2f22.title: Nonpoint source pollution
ffa9250d2f22.sentence: Each summer, hypoxic conditions form in bottom waters where the Mississippi River enters the Gulf of Mexico.

08241e911994.title: Nonpoint source pollution
08241e911994.sentence: During recent summers, the aerial extent of this "dead zone" is comparable to the area of New Jersey and has major detrimental consequences for fisheries in the region.

6e73e1e8807f.title: Eutrophication
6e73e1e8807f.sentence: The problem became more apparent following the introduction of chemical fertilizers in agriculture (green revolution of the mid-1900s).

324f65f36688.title: Eutrophication
324f65f36688.sentence: Prior to their being phasing out in the 1970's, phosphate-containing detergents contributed to eutrophication.

1e2267403055.title: Eutrophication
1e2267403055.sentence: Since then, sewage and agriculture have emerged as the dominant phosphate sources.

1e8488e7d241.title: Eutrophication
1e8488e7d241.sentence: Approaches for prevention and reversal of eutrophication include minimizing point source pollution from sewage and agriculture as well as other nonpoint pollution sources.

2e3342ab1278.title: Eutrophication
2e3342ab1278.sentence: Additionally, the introduction of bacteria and algae-inhibiting organisms such as shellfish and seaweed can also help reduce nitrogen pollution, which in turn controls the growth of cyanobacteria, the main source of harmful algae blooms.

f996ebcb55e8.title: Soil contamination
f996ebcb55e8.sentence: Not unexpectedly, soil contaminants can have significant deleterious consequences for ecosystems.

3bd045ae7889.title: Soil contamination
3bd045ae7889.sentence: There are radical soil chemistry changes which can arise from the presence of many hazardous chemicals even at low concentration of the contaminant species.

91dd0ff2c5a3.title: Soil contamination
91dd0ff2c5a3.sentence: These changes can manifest in the alteration of the metabolism of soil microorganisms and soil animals resident in a given soil environment.

60bf2666da4d.title: Soil contamination
60bf2666da4d.sentence: The result can be virtual eradication of some of the primary food chain, which in turn could have major consequences for predator or consumer species.

1f345e0c6b11.title: Soil contamination
1f345e0c6b11.sentence: In contaminated land the topsoil passes from a stage in which organic matter is decomposed and incorporated to mineral matter (mull humus, with a good granular soil structure) to a stage in which organic matter accumulates undecayed above a compact mineral soil with poor structure (mor humus).

cbdf76d41dc6.title: Soil contamination
cbdf76d41dc6.sentence: It has been suggested that the examination of humus forms, which necessitates only a cursory glance upon ground floor thickness and structure of the underlying mineral horizon, could used at low cost for the early detection and mapping of potential soil contamination.

5bfd751708bc.title: Soil contamination
5bfd751708bc.sentence: Agricultural lands display certain types of soil contamination, involving in particular heavy metals and metalloids.

b25b9818fa48.title: Soil contamination
b25b9818fa48.sentence: These contaminants typically alter plant metabolism, often causing a reduction in crop yields.

5d69b5fbd567.title: Soil contamination
5d69b5fbd567.sentence: This has a secondary effect upon soil conservation, since the languishing crops cannot shield the Earth's soil from erosion.

ddaf6d2ef974.title: Soil contamination
ddaf6d2ef974.sentence: Some of these chemical contaminants have long half-lives and in other cases derivative chemicals are formed from decay of primary soil contaminants.

814816560290.title: Soil contamination
814816560290.sentence: Most exposure to soil contamination is accidental, and can happen through:

2fc816d1bab3.title: Soil contamination
2fc816d1bab3.sentence: - Ingesting food or vegetables grown in contaminated soil or with foods in contact with contaminants

57a42c166c7f.title: Soil contamination
57a42c166c7f.sentence: - Skin contact with dust or soil

c8efeb0dc90b.title: Soil contamination
c8efeb0dc90b.sentence: - Inhaling clouds of dust while working in soils or windy environments

b61f82c9ed75.title: Soil contamination
b61f82c9ed75.sentence: However, some studies estimate that 90% of human exposure is through eating contaminated food.

f029bee17746.title: Soil contamination
f029bee17746.sentence: Potentially greater threats are posed by the infiltration of soil contaminants into groundwater aquifers used for irrigation or direct human consumption, sometimes in areas far from any apparent source of above-ground contamination (long-range diffuse soil contamination).

7cf77eca6e50.title: Soil contamination
7cf77eca6e50.sentence: Toxic metals can also make their way up the food chain through plants that reside in soils containing high concentrations of heavy metals.

d1de97c445d8.title: Soil contamination
d1de97c445d8.sentence: This tends to result in the development of pollution-related diseases.

8d4bb2b6439c.title: Contaminated land
8d4bb2b6439c.section: Classification as contaminated site and recording > Impact pathways
8d4bb2b6439c.sentence: In Germany, the test and action values according to the Bundes-Bodenschutz- und Altlastenverordnung (Federal Soil Protection and Contaminated Sites Ordinance) apply to the following impact pathways:

f0836310de74.title: Contaminated land
f0836310de74.section: Classification as contaminated site and recording > Impact pathways
f0836310de74.sentence: - Impact pathway Soil-Groundwater: Drinking water is obtained from groundwater and feeds into surface water.

55d643b0161f.title: Contaminated land
55d643b0161f.section: Classification as contaminated site and recording > Impact pathways
55d643b0161f.sentence: - Impact pathway soil-cultivated plants: Cultivated plants absorb the pollutants via their roots and store them in tubers (potatoes, beetroot) or leaves (lettuce, spinach, cabbage).

d07fe9fc04b0.title: Contaminated land
d07fe9fc04b0.section: Classification as contaminated site and recording > Impact pathways
d07fe9fc04b0.sentence: - Impact pathway soil-humans: Humans come into contact with contaminated soil or absorb the pollutants via the lungs (dust in the air), the skin (gardening) or the gastrointestinal tract (small children who eat soil).

1e48ea516150.title: Soil contamination
1e48ea516150.sentence: A pesticide is a substance used to kill a pest.

927bfef937fd.title: Soil contamination
927bfef937fd.sentence: A pesticide may be a chemical substance, biological agent (such as a virus or bacteria), antimicrobial, disinfectant or device used against any pest.

da2bf52f9c17.title: Soil contamination
da2bf52f9c17.sentence: - Agrochemicals, such as pesticides, herbicides and fertilizers

90741178cc16.title: Soil contamination
90741178cc16.sentence: Most herbicides are biodegradable by soil bacteria.

fa7eece46f1a.title: Soil contamination
fa7eece46f1a.sentence: However, one group derived from trinitrotoluene (2,4-D and 2,4,5-T) have the impurity dioxin, which is very toxic and causes fatality even in low concentrations.

6ab61a08c264.title: Soil contamination
6ab61a08c264.sentence: Another common herbicide is Paraquat, banned in the European Union but still frequently used in agricultural areas of the United States and Asia.

9be33d175158.title: Soil contamination
9be33d175158.sentence: It is highly toxic to humans and other animals and cannot rapidly degrade in the soil where it is adsorbed and thus protected in clay lattices.

a352712d1678.title: Soil contamination
a352712d1678.sentence: Glyphosate is rapidly transformed in AMPA by soil bacteria but its residues are detected in drinking water, agriculture, and food products and have major effects on the health of reproductive systems.Glyphosate is used in genetically modified crops to kill all vegetation except the target crop, more especially in developing countries where it offers yield and profit gains despite growing concerns about environment and human health.

68867d33b84b.title: Soil contamination
68867d33b84b.sentence: There are now three main groups of synthetic insecticides:

08bf6793ae97.title: Soil contamination
08bf6793ae97.sentence: Organochlorines include DDT, Aldrin, Dieldrin and benzene hexachloride (BHC).

0a869ada419c.title: Soil contamination
0a869ada419c.sentence: They are cheap to produce, potent and persistent but have harmful effects on a lot of beneficial organisms, from microbes to a wide range of plants and animals, humans included, hence their banishment in many (but not all) countries, inasmuch as resistance occurred in a lot of target insect pests.

66217c7f89c4.title: Soil contamination
66217c7f89c4.sentence: This group of insecticides works by preventing normal nerve transmission as acetylcholinesterase is prevented from breaking down the transmitter substance acetylcholine, resulting in uncontrolled muscle movements.

8fbaaf91e7a5.title: Soil contamination
8fbaaf91e7a5.sentence: They affect the central nervous system of insects, with higher selectivity for insects than organophosphates and organochlorines.

f70e726ce70e.title: Soil contamination
f70e726ce70e.sentence: Like nicotine, their molecular base, they are degraded in the soil but the environmental residues of neonicotinoids have enormously increased due to large-scale applications.

46f32bf9d9f0.title: Soil contamination
46f32bf9d9f0.sentence: However, their biocidal action includes both pests and beneficial organisms, e.g. pollinators, predatory insects, parasitoids.

354b6ce6f9c4.title: Soil contamination
354b6ce6f9c4.sentence: Soil pollution can be caused by the following (non-exhaustive list):

9ea4558d6129.title: Soil contamination
9ea4558d6129.sentence: - Mining and activities by other heavy industries

110e1fa71e82.title: Soil contamination
110e1fa71e82.sentence: - Accidental spills may happen during activities, etc.

c04dbbb02a82.title: Soil contamination
c04dbbb02a82.sentence: - Corrosion of underground storage tanks (including piping used to transmit the contents)

4e770688911c.title: Soil contamination
4e770688911c.sentence: - Contamination by Pb due to vehicle exhaust, Cd, and Zn caused by tire wear.

21c4242356c7.title: Soil contamination
21c4242356c7.sentence: - Contamination by rocks containing large amounts of toxic elements.

034999b0c6a8.title: Soil contamination
034999b0c6a8.sentence: Historical deposition of coal ash used for residential, commercial, and industrial heating, as well as for industrial processes such as ore smelting, were a common source of contamination in areas that were industrialized before about 1960.

a4820c55c26b.title: Soil contamination
a4820c55c26b.sentence: Coal naturally concentrates arsenic, cadmium lead and zinc during its formation, as well as other heavy metals to a lesser degree.

c12640218602.title: Soil contamination
c12640218602.sentence: When the coal is burned, most of these metals become concentrated in the ash (the principal exception being mercury, which evaporates).

0435cb3c7de4.title: Soil contamination
0435cb3c7de4.sentence: In addition to lead, coal ash typically contains variable but significant concentrations of polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs; e.g., benzo(a)anthracene, benzo(b)fluoranthene, benzo(k)fluoranthene, benzo(a)pyrene, indeno(1,2,3-cd)pyrene, phenanthrene, anthracene, and others).

33230a37bfaa.title: Soil contamination
33230a37bfaa.sentence: These PAHs are known human carcinogens and the acceptable concentrations of them in soil are typically from 0.1 mg/kg to 10 mg/kg, with a strong variation from a PAH to another.

c252038921fc.title: Soil contamination
c252038921fc.sentence: Treated sewage sludge, known in the industry as biosolids, has become controversial as a "fertilizer".

576d1cc896c9.title: Soil contamination
576d1cc896c9.sentence: As it is the byproduct of sewage treatment, it generally contains more contaminants such as organisms, pesticides, and heavy metals than other soil.

d5e0e93b270c.title: Soil contamination
d5e0e93b270c.sentence: This has good agricultural properties due to the high nitrogen, phosphate and potassium content.

46469e4b128c.title: Soil contamination
46469e4b128c.sentence: Composting of sewage sludge allows to decrease its content in pathogens and organic pollutants (bioremediation, to the exception of persistent organic pollutants) but not that of heavy metals, although these are in a less bioavailable form.

8dae5601713f.title: Soil
8dae5601713f.sentence: An example of diffuse pollution with contaminants is copper accumulation in vineyards and orchards to which fungicides are repeatedly applied, even in organic farming.

fd20d3924e21.title: Persistent organic pollutant
fd20d3924e21.sentence: Persistent organic pollutants (POPs) are organic compounds that are resistant to degradation through chemical, biological, and photolytic processes.

0c040799187b.title: Persistent organic pollutant
0c040799187b.sentence: They are toxic and adversely affect human health and the environment around the world.

93ddafd859d6.title: Persistent organic pollutant
93ddafd859d6.sentence: Most POPs are pesticides or insecticides, and some are also solvents, pharmaceuticals, and industrial chemicals.

d33669890e32.title: Persistent organic pollutant
d33669890e32.sentence: Although some POPs arise naturally (e.g. from volcanoes and forest fires), most are man-made.

b6adc7d85099.title: Persistent organic pollutant
b6adc7d85099.sentence: POPs typically are halogenated organic compounds (see lists below) and as such exhibit high lipid solubility.

befa93a06edf.title: Persistent organic pollutant
befa93a06edf.sentence: For this reason, they bioaccumulate in fatty tissues.

bf3b769d0ff7.title: Persistent organic pollutant
bf3b769d0ff7.sentence: Halogenated compounds also exhibit great stability reflecting the nonreactivity of C-Cl bonds toward hydrolysis and photolytic degradation.

c7fd673865c0.title: Persistent organic pollutant
c7fd673865c0.sentence: POPs enter the gas phase under certain environmental temperatures and volatilize from soils, vegetation, and bodies of water into the atmosphere, resisting breakdown reactions in the air, to travel long distances before being re-deposited.

65db29a58f82.title: Persistent organic pollutant
65db29a58f82.sentence: This results in accumulation of POPs in areas far from where they were used or emitted, specifically environments where POPs have never been introduced such as Antarctica, and the Arctic Circle.

416d2fa97e66.title: Persistent organic pollutant
416d2fa97e66.sentence: POPs have low solubility in water but are easily captured by solid particles, and are soluble in organic fluids (oils, fats, and liquid fuels).

fac30be06ef6.title: Persistent organic pollutant
fac30be06ef6.sentence: The effect of POPs on human and environmental health was discussed, with intention to eliminate or severely restrict their production, by the international community at the Stockholm Convention on Persistent Organic Pollutants in 2001.

2bb348d93568.title: Persistent organic pollutant
2bb348d93568.sentence: The "dirty dozen" POPs identified by the Stockholm Convention include aldrin, chlordane, dieldrin, endrin, heptachlor, HCB, mirex, toxaphene, PCBs, DDT, dioxins, and polychlorinated dibenzofurans.

e73e96fd2cb7.title: Persistent organic pollutant
e73e96fd2cb7.sentence: However, there have since been many new POPs added (e.g. PFOS).

6c8105c3501b.title: Persistent organic pollutant
6c8105c3501b.section: In urban areas and indoor environments
6c8105c3501b.sentence: Several studies have shown that indoor (air and dust) POP levels frequently exceed outdoor (air and soil) POP concentrations.

eb5b3a1be4f3.title: Persistent organic pollutant
eb5b3a1be4f3.section: Control and removal in the environment
eb5b3a1be4f3.sentence: Current efforts are more focused on banning the use and production of POPs worldwide rather than removal of POPs.

185a61e74cc4.title: Soil contamination
185a61e74cc4.sentence: DDT was used on a massive scale from the 1930s, with a peak of 72,000 tonnes used in 1970.

9294fdf0712c.title: Soil contamination
9294fdf0712c.sentence: Then usage fell as the harmful environmental effects were realized.

5b9095e7ad9f.title: Soil contamination
5b9095e7ad9f.sentence: It was found worldwide in fish and birds and was even discovered in the snow in the Antarctic.

b15d1b46d159.title: Soil contamination
b15d1b46d159.sentence: It is only slightly soluble in water but is very soluble in the bloodstream, and in fats.

47723d8c887c.title: Soil contamination
47723d8c887c.sentence: It affects the nervous and endocrine systems and causes the eggshells of birds to lack calcium causing them to be easily breakable.

a01d9b5ea4a3.title: Soil contamination
a01d9b5ea4a3.sentence: It is thought to be responsible for the decline of numbers of birds of prey like ospreys and peregrine falcons in the 1950s, now recovering.

9e621c90901a.title: Soil contamination
9e621c90901a.sentence: DDT was banned by the Stockholm convention in 2001 to stop its further buildup in the food chain.

0c9b2942f32b.title: Soil contamination
0c9b2942f32b.sentence: However, the World Health Organization allowed its reintroduction only for control of vector-borne diseases in some tropical countries in 2006.

c88ee905fa7c.title: DDT
c88ee905fa7c.sentence: DDT is a persistent organic pollutant that is readily adsorbed to soils and sediments, which can act both as sinks and as long-term sources of exposure affecting organisms.

3773b2a76468.title: DDT
3773b2a76468.sentence: Routes of loss and degradation include runoff, volatilization, photolysis and aerobic and anaerobic biodegradation.

554af6ab4c7d.title: DDT
554af6ab4c7d.sentence: Its breakdown products and metabolites, DDE and DDD, are also persistent and have similar chemical and physical properties.

e6df20128d7d.title: DDT
e6df20128d7d.sentence: Despite being banned for many years, in 2018 research showed that DDT residues are still present in European soils and Spanish rivers.

3c992db64d06.title: DDT
3c992db64d06.sentence: DDT and its breakdown products are transported from warmer areas to the Arctic by the phenomenon of global distillation, where they then accumulate in the region's food web.

3ee66c96eb11.title: PFAS
3ee66c96eb11.sentence: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS or PFASs) are a group of synthetic organofluorine chemical compounds that have multiple fluorine atoms attached to an alkyl chain.

4b4431eeedc6.title: PFAS
4b4431eeedc6.sentence: Because of their high chemical and thermal stability, these compounds have long environmental lifetimes, and thus are commonly called "forever chemicals".

dc0040eee0f0.title: PFAS
dc0040eee0f0.sentence: Their widespread use began in 1938 with the invention of Teflon (polytetrafluoroethylene), a fluoropolymer coating that resists heat, oil, stains, grease, and water.

5dfd7195710c.title: PFAS
5dfd7195710c.sentence: Since their inception, thousands of PFAS compounds have been created.

92ce4ac17eb4.title: PFAS
92ce4ac17eb4.sentence: They are used in a wide variety of products including waterproof fabric, yoga pants, carpets, shampoo, mobile phone screens, wall paint, furniture, adhesives, food packaging, firefighting foam, electrical insulation, and cosmetics.

4a3d0071d712.title: PFAS
4a3d0071d712.sentence: PFAS are often found in rainwater, groundwater, wastewater and soil; wastewater treatment facilities and landfills have the highest levels of pollution.

a1a66ae041c8.title: PFAS
a1a66ae041c8.sentence: In addition, areas near airports and air force bases are contaminated from the use of PFAS-containing firefighting foam.

be65a5fb52cf.title: PFAS
be65a5fb52cf.section: Environmental effects > Prevalence in rain, soil, water bodies, and air
be65a5fb52cf.sentence: Soil contamination can result in higher levels of PFAS found in foods such as white rice, coffee, and animals reared on contaminated ground.

7b11aaa4c2e5.title: PFAS
7b11aaa4c2e5.sentence: Furthermore, crop uptake of PFAS and bioaccumulation of PFAS into fish, livestock, and wildlife can act as potential routes of human exposure.

7933a25e228d.title: PFAS
7933a25e228d.section: Environmental effects > Prevalence in rain, soil, water bodies, and air
7933a25e228d.sentence: Soil is also contaminated and the chemicals have been found in remote areas such as Antarctica.

fbf92ec3dc3d.title: PFAS
fbf92ec3dc3d.section: Environmental effects > Prevalence in rain, soil, water bodies, and air
fbf92ec3dc3d.sentence: In 2024, a worldwide study of 45,000 groundwater samples found that 31% of samples contained levels of PFAS that were harmful to human health; these samples were taken from areas not near any obvious source of contamination.

ff2466f7e631.title: PFAS
ff2466f7e631.sentence: Exposure to PFAS, some of which are carcinogens or endocrine disruptors, has been linked to diseases and health conditions including cancers, ulcerative colitis, thyroid disease, suboptimal antibody response or decreased immunity, decreased fertility, hypertensive disorders in pregnancy, fetal and child developmental issues, obesity, and high cholesterol.

fa64e8470eb1.title: PFAS
fa64e8470eb1.sentence: Due to the health and environmental concerns associated with many PFAS, PFOS and PFOA were listed in the Stockholm Convention on Persistent Organic Pollutants in 2009 and 2019, respectively.

f689766529e7.title: PFAS
f689766529e7.sentence: A global meta-analysis found that PFAS concentrations increase, on average, twofold with each trophic level, with substantial variation among compounds.

b351bcd6f2ce.title: PFAS
b351bcd6f2ce.sentence: - Sorption (including granular activated carbon, biochar, and ion exchange resins)

abd7354b98d8.title: Soil vapor extraction
abd7354b98d8.sentence: Soil vapor extraction (SVE) is a physical treatment process for in situ remediation of volatile contaminants in vadose zone (unsaturated) soils (EPA, 2012).

765e4d5398b8.title: Soil vapor extraction
765e4d5398b8.sentence: SVE (also referred to as in situ soil venting or vacuum extraction) is based on mass transfer of contaminant from the solid (sorbed) and liquid (aqueous or non-aqueous) phases into the gas phase, with subsequent collection of the gas phase contamination at extraction wells.

55482d21225e.title: Soil vapor extraction
55482d21225e.sentence: The soil vapor extraction remediation technology uses vacuum blowers and extraction wells to induce gas flow through the subsurface, collecting contaminated soil vapor, which is subsequently treated aboveground.

efddd43065d0.title: Soil vapor extraction
efddd43065d0.sentence: The vacuum extraction of soil gas induces gas flow across a site, increasing the mass transfer driving force from aqueous (soil moisture), non-aqueous (pure phase), and solid (soil) phase into the gas phase.

24814d593d71.title: Soil vapor extraction
24814d593d71.sentence: Extracted contaminant mass in the gas phase (and any condensed liquid phase) is treated in aboveground systems.

800e13f977d9.title: Soil vapor extraction
800e13f977d9.sentence: In essence, SVE is the vadose zone equivalent of the pump-and-treat technology for groundwater remediation.

827b48625cb2.title: Soil vapor extraction
827b48625cb2.sentence: SVE is particularly amenable to contaminants with higher Henry's law constants, including various chlorinated solvents and hydrocarbons.

2acf8b982cb0.title: Soil vapor extraction
2acf8b982cb0.sentence: SVE is a well-demonstrated, mature remediation technology and has been identified by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) as presumptive remedy.

93fe5e69b7dc.title: Soil vapor extraction
93fe5e69b7dc.sentence: The system can be implemented with standard wells and off-the-shelf equipment (blowers, instrumentation, vapor treatment, etc.).

de3b518ca948.title: Soil vapor extraction
de3b518ca948.sentence: SVE can also be implemented with a minimum of site disturbance, primarily involving well installation and minimal aboveground equipment.

63acf3d25cc4.title: Soil vapor extraction
63acf3d25cc4.sentence: Depending on the nature of the contamination and the subsurface geology, SVE has the potential to treat large soil volumes at reasonable costs.

a4f52f8fb992.title: Soil vapor extraction
a4f52f8fb992.sentence: As an example, a residual quantity of a highly volatile contaminant (such as trichloroethene) in a homogeneous sand with high permeability and low carbon content (i.e., low/negligible adsorption) will be readily treated with SVE.

84ac412a4f08.title: Soil vapor extraction
84ac412a4f08.sentence: In contrast, a heterogeneous vadose zone with one or more clay layers containing residual naphthalene would require a longer treatment time or SVE enhancements.

4462aa92bcef.title: Soil vapor extraction
4462aa92bcef.sentence: SVE effectiveness issues include tailing and rebound, which result from contaminated zones with lower air flow (i.e., low permeability zones or zones of high moisture content) or lower volatility (or higher adsorption).

44741fbf621f.title: Soil vapor extraction
44741fbf621f.section: Design, optimization, performance assessment, and closure
44741fbf621f.sentence: As time goes on, it is typical for a SVE system to exhibit a diminishing rate of contaminant extraction due to mass transfer limitations or removal of contaminant mass.

453949f6d820.title: Soil vapor extraction
453949f6d820.sentence: Enhancements for improving the effectiveness of SVE can include directional drilling, pneumatic and hydraulic fracturing, and thermal enhancement (e.g., hot air or steam injection).

bd8d8d27f1e9.title: Soil vapor extraction
bd8d8d27f1e9.sentence: Directional drilling and fracturing enhancements are generally intended to improve the gas flow through the subsurface, especially in lower permeability zones.

29c307d3fbce.title: Soil vapor extraction
29c307d3fbce.sentence: Thermal enhancements such as hot air or steam injection increase the subsurface soil temperature, thereby improving the volatility of the contamination.

9612c1d2385b.title: Soil vapor extraction
9612c1d2385b.sentence: In addition, injection of hot (dry) air can remove soil moisture and thus improve the gas permeability of the soil.

c764e10e6fab.title: Soil vapor extraction
c764e10e6fab.sentence: In situ air sparging is a remediation technology for treating contamination in groundwater.

5ab6f1e458f9.title: Soil vapor extraction
5ab6f1e458f9.sentence: Air is injected and "sparged" through the groundwater and then collected via soil vapor extraction wells.

3672f00b95d8.title: Soil vapor extraction
3672f00b95d8.sentence: In some situations, such as enhancement of monitored natural attenuation, a passive SVE system that relies on barometric pumping may be employed.
