653e7fde6f10.title: Biomagnification
653e7fde6f10.sentence: Biomagnification, also known as bioamplification or biological magnification, is the increase in concentration of a substance in the tissues of organisms at successively higher levels in a food chain.

7c21ddabeb9e.title: Soil contamination
7c21ddabeb9e.sentence: Many of these effects are now well known, such as the concentration of persistent DDT materials for avian consumers, leading to weakening of egg shells, increased chick mortality and potential extinction of species.

a66940136f1b.title: Polychlorinated biphenyl
a66940136f1b.sentence: Like many lipophilic toxins, PCBs undergo biomagnification and bioaccumulation primarily due to the fact that they are easily retained within organisms.

de96e1bd2871.title: Polychlorinated biphenyl
de96e1bd2871.sentence: The concentration of PCBs within an organism will increase over their lifetime; this process is called bioaccumulation.

47b22811510b.title: Biomagnification
47b22811510b.sentence: - Bioaccumulation occurs within a trophic level, and is the increase in the concentration of a substance in certain tissues of organisms' bodies due to absorption from food and the environment.

7e57e3bbe642.title: Biomagnification
7e57e3bbe642.sentence: Thus, bioconcentration and bioaccumulation occur within an organism, and biomagnification occurs across trophic (food chain) levels.

3f40b5ef53ab.title: Biomagnification
3f40b5ef53ab.sentence: For example, herring contains mercury at approximately 0.01 parts per million (ppm) and shark contains mercury at greater than 1 ppm.

67f986a40ccc.title: Biomagnification
67f986a40ccc.sentence: The biomagnification factor (BMF) describes the ratio of the contaminant concentration in a predator to the concentration in its prey once a steady state is reached.

f9680a747e43.title: Biomagnification
f9680a747e43.sentence: A BMF > 1 indicates that the contaminant accumulates more strongly in the feeding organism than in its feed.

8f63fa1ed214.title: Biomagnification
8f63fa1ed214.sentence: The trophic magnification factor (TMF) offers a more comprehensive perspective by quantifying biomagnification across an entire food web.

355de3a5e807.title: Biomagnification
355de3a5e807.sentence: A TMF > 1 indicates biomagnification, while a TMF < 1 indicates trophic dilution.

2a1f166dbdc0.title: Biomagnification
2a1f166dbdc0.sentence: In a review, a large number of studies, Suedel et al. concluded that although biomagnification is probably more limited in occurrence than previously thought, there is good evidence that DDT, DDE, PCBs, toxaphene, and the organic forms of mercury and arsenic do biomagnify in nature.

29716a4236dc.title: Environmental remediation
29716a4236dc.sentence: Developers who agree to voluntary cleanup may be offered incentives under state or municipal programs like New York State's Brownfield Cleanup Program.

3c400dc5b6a3.title: Environmental remediation
3c400dc5b6a3.sentence: A set of standards used in Europe exists and is often called the Dutch standards.

49d166611fad.title: Environmental remediation
49d166611fad.sentence: Excavation processes can be as simple as hauling the contaminated soil to a regulated landfill, but can also involve aerating the excavated material in the case of volatile organic compounds (VOCs).

6ee289bcbdc1.title: Environmental remediation
6ee289bcbdc1.sentence: Techniques to construct barrier walls are deep soil mixing, jet grouting, low pressure grouting with cement and chemicals, freezing and slurry walls.

99a5e22d659a.title: Nonpoint source pollution
99a5e22d659a.section: Principal sources (for water pollution) > Agricultural operations
99a5e22d659a.sentence: Nutrients (nitrogen and phosphorus) are typically applied to farmland as commercial fertilizer, animal manure, or spraying of municipal or industrial wastewater (effluent) or sludge.

bc0c937e8ce7.title: Nonpoint source pollution
bc0c937e8ce7.section: Principal sources (for water pollution) > Agricultural operations
bc0c937e8ce7.sentence: Other agrochemicals such as pesticides and fungicides can enter environments from agricultural lands through runoff and deposition as well.

020e6cc423f9.title: Nonpoint source pollution
020e6cc423f9.section: Principal sources (for water pollution) > Agricultural operations
020e6cc423f9.sentence: Sediment (loose soil) washed off fields is a form of agricultural pollution.

a6b340f360d3.title: Nonpoint source pollution
a6b340f360d3.section: Principal sources (for water pollution) > Agricultural operations
a6b340f360d3.sentence: Nutrients may also enter runoff from crop residues, irrigation water, wildlife, and atmospheric deposition.

4e22430ea1bf.title: Nonpoint source pollution
4e22430ea1bf.section: Principal sources (for water pollution) > Agricultural operations
4e22430ea1bf.sentence: Pesticides such as DDT or atrazine can travel through waterways or stay suspended in air and carried by wind in a process known as "spray drift".

ba7ba7c231bc.title: Nonpoint source pollution
ba7ba7c231bc.section: Principal sources (for water pollution) > Agricultural operations
ba7ba7c231bc.sentence: When large tracts of land are plowed to grow crops, it exposes and loosens soil that was once buried.

53e321d5d470.title: Nonpoint source pollution
53e321d5d470.section: Principal sources (for water pollution) > Agricultural operations
53e321d5d470.sentence: This makes the exposed soil more vulnerable to erosion during rainstorms.

26aeb40c8c68.title: Nonpoint source pollution
26aeb40c8c68.section: Principal sources (for water pollution) > Agricultural operations
26aeb40c8c68.sentence: It also can increase the amount of fertilizer and pesticides carried into nearby bodies of water.

2f187637231e.title: Nonpoint source pollution
2f187637231e.sentence: Common techniques include contour plowing, crop mulching, crop rotation, planting perennial crops, or installing riparian buffers.

54a9cff8301f.title: Nonpoint source pollution
54a9cff8301f.sentence: Conservation tillage is a concept used to reduce runoff.

72ade6a20ccb.title: Nonpoint source pollution
72ade6a20ccb.sentence: Farmers can develop and implement nutrient management plans to reduce excess application of nutrients.

858c8e22a8d0.title: Microplastics
858c8e22a8d0.sentence: Microplastics are "synthetic solid particulate matter or polymeric matrices, with regular or irregular shape and with size ranging from 1 μm to 5 mm, of either primary or secondary manufacturing origin, which are insoluble in water." Microplastics cause pollution by entering natural ecosystems from a variety of sources, including cosmetics, clothing, construction, renovation, food packaging, and industrial processes.

6fe89708f6e0.title: Microplastics
6fe89708f6e0.sentence: Microplastics also accumulate in the air and terrestrial ecosystems.

a98453674cf3.title: Microplastics
a98453674cf3.sentence: Primary microplastics include any plastic fragments or particles that are already 5 mm in size or less before entering the environment.

53242e305862.title: Microplastics
53242e305862.sentence: These include microfibers from clothing, microbeads, plastic glitter and plastic pellets (also known as nurdles).

402972b91cf9.title: Microplastics
402972b91cf9.sentence: Secondary microplastics arise from the degradation (breakdown) of larger plastic products through natural weathering processes after entering the environment.

4e4252231b21.title: Soil
4e4252231b21.sentence: 100% of agricultural soil samples from southwestern China contain plastic particles, 92% of which are microfibres.

709d35b41f07.title: Soil
709d35b41f07.sentence: Sources of microfibres likely include string or twine, as well as irrigation water in which clothes have been washed.

03ab38c9c02a.title: Soil
03ab38c9c02a.sentence: The application of biosolids from sewage sludge and compost can introduce microplastics to soils.

a847082a435a.title: Soil
a847082a435a.sentence: This adds to the burden of microplastics from other sources (e.g. the atmosphere).

07129e3ab2c4.title: Soil
07129e3ab2c4.sentence: Approximately half the sewage sludge in Europe and North America is applied to agricultural land.

01a0c0245b7c.title: Soil
01a0c0245b7c.sentence: In Europe it has been estimated that for every million inhabitants 113 to 770 tonnes of microplastics are added to agricultural soils each year.

e83b276cff40.title: Microplastics
e83b276cff40.sentence: Furthermore, geophagous soil fauna, such as earthworms, mites, and collembolans could contribute to the amount of secondary microplastic present in soil by converting consumed plastic debris into microplastic via digestive processes.

3d7e85667d4d.title: Microplastics
3d7e85667d4d.section: Effects on the environment > Microbes, soil ecosystems and terrestrial plants
3d7e85667d4d.sentence: A 2024 meta-analysis of 180 studies found that microplastic exposure increased soil carbon dioxide emissions by 25.7%, while also increasing soil organic carbon content by 25.4%.

5f1b5df1ed8e.title: Microplastics
5f1b5df1ed8e.section: Effects on the environment > Microbes, soil ecosystems and terrestrial plants
5f1b5df1ed8e.sentence: The analysis also found a significant reduction in aboveground plant biomass, suggesting that microplastic pollution may affect agricultural productivity.

2634e0a32bbb.title: Microplastics
2634e0a32bbb.section: Effects on the environment > Microbes, soil ecosystems and terrestrial plants
2634e0a32bbb.sentence: In agricultural soils, residues of plastic mulch films have been shown to affect wheat growth and biomass allocation.

7f144541ce54.title: Microplastics
7f144541ce54.section: Effects on the environment > Microbes, soil ecosystems and terrestrial plants
7f144541ce54.sentence: There is also evidence that microplastics can alter root and leaf traits, total biomass, and morphophysiological characteristics of plants.

324c4e0ac1fa.title: Microplastics
324c4e0ac1fa.section: Effects on the environment > Microbes, soil ecosystems and terrestrial plants
324c4e0ac1fa.sentence: The impact of microplastics on plants can, in some aspects, be compared to their effects on microorganisms, as it strongly depends on the type of plastic.

3cf039a4a320.title: Microplastics
3cf039a4a320.sentence: A substantial portion of microplastics are expected to end up in the world's soil, yet very little research has been conducted on microplastics in soil outside of aquatic environments.

2634b945820a.title: Microplastics
2634b945820a.sentence: There is concrete data linking the use of organic waste materials to synthetic fibers being found in the soil; but most studies on plastics in soil merely report its presence and do not mention origin or quantity.

3125d3c7c38c.title: Soil contamination
3125d3c7c38c.section: Ecosystem effects > Potential effects of contaminants to soil functions
3125d3c7c38c.sentence: Heavy metals and other soil contaminants can adversely affect the activity, species composition and abundance of soil microorganisms, thereby threatening soil functions such as biochemical cycling of carbon and nitrogen.

476a05df00b1.title: Soil contamination
476a05df00b1.section: Ecosystem effects > Potential effects of contaminants to soil functions
476a05df00b1.sentence: However, soil contaminants can also become less bioavailable by time (natural attenuation), and microorganisms and ecosystems can adapt to altered conditions.

ca1241dd231f.title: Soil contamination
ca1241dd231f.section: Ecosystem effects > Potential effects of contaminants to soil functions
ca1241dd231f.sentence: Soil properties such as pH, organic matter content and texture are very important and modify mobility, bioavailability and toxicity of pollutants in contaminated soils.

7c7728fad8ad.title: Soil contamination
7c7728fad8ad.section: Ecosystem effects > Potential effects of contaminants to soil functions
7c7728fad8ad.sentence: The same amount of contaminant can be toxic in one soil but totally harmless in another soil.

fe2b58d10e07.title: Soil contamination
fe2b58d10e07.section: Ecosystem effects > Potential effects of contaminants to soil functions
fe2b58d10e07.sentence: This stresses the need for soil-specific risk assessment and remediation measures.

45f4ee1d0bb9.title: Soil contamination
45f4ee1d0bb9.sentence: Health consequences from exposure to soil contamination vary greatly depending on pollutant type, the pathway of attack, and the vulnerability of the exposed population.

b5cc0d89119d.title: Soil contamination
b5cc0d89119d.sentence: Chronic exposure to chromium, lead, and other metals, petroleum, solvents, and many pesticide and herbicide formulations can be carcinogenic (mutagenic), can cause congenital disorders, or other chronic diseases.

b54ef2c68766.title: Soil contamination
b54ef2c68766.sentence: Chronic exposure to benzene at sufficient concentrations is known to be associated with a higher incidence of leukemia.

4d64c0ece675.title: Soil contamination
4d64c0ece675.sentence: Mercury and cyclodienes are known to induce higher incidences of kidney damage and some irreversible diseases.

2e65f1050046.title: Soil contamination
2e65f1050046.sentence: PCBs and cyclodienesare linked to liver toxicity.

fd8c62eb4e07.title: Soil contamination
fd8c62eb4e07.sentence: Industrial or human-made concentrations of naturally occurring substances, such as nitrate and ammonia associated with livestock manure from agricultural operations, have also been identified as health hazards in soil and groundwater.

b5ff736f9617.title: Soil contamination
b5ff736f9617.sentence: At sufficient dosages a large number of soil contaminants can cause death by exposure via direct contact, inhalation or ingestion.

ccccdb3c7440.title: Soil contamination
ccccdb3c7440.sentence: - Ammunitions, chemical agents, and other agents of war

b7fc1cc6d61e.title: Soil contamination
b7fc1cc6d61e.sentence: The disposal of munitions, and a lack of care in manufacture of munitions caused by the urgency of production, can contaminate soil for extended periods.

c575406c5efb.title: Soil contamination
c575406c5efb.sentence: There is little published evidence on this type of contamination largely because of restrictions placed by governments of many countries on the publication of material related to war effort, in particular under ongoing conflict scenarios.

3b4f6bc7b7b6.title: Soil contamination
3b4f6bc7b7b6.sentence: However, mustard gas stored during World War II has contaminated some sites for up to 50 years and the testing of Anthrax as a potential biological weapon contaminated the whole island of Gruinard, leaving it in quarantine for 48 years.

43aea1269ae1.title: Soil contamination
43aea1269ae1.sentence: There are abandoned delaboration sites around the former World War I front in Belgium and also in France which are still contaminated by arsenic and lead.

eab01912b5fa.title: Biostimulation
eab01912b5fa.sentence: Biostimulation involves the modification of the environment to stimulate existing bacteria capable of bioremediation.

6008a0b75d17.title: Biostimulation
6008a0b75d17.sentence: This can be done by addition of various forms of rate limiting nutrients and electron acceptors, such as phosphorus, nitrogen, oxygen, or carbon (e.g. in the form of molasses).

bcd888416d00.title: Biostimulation
bcd888416d00.sentence: Alternatively, remediation of halogenated contaminants in anaerobic environments may be stimulated by adding electron donors (organic substrates), thus allowing indigenous microorganisms to use the halogenated contaminants as electron acceptors.

fa53dc8a1a85.title: Biostimulation
fa53dc8a1a85.sentence: The primary advantage of biostimulation is that bioremediation will be undertaken by already present native microorganisms that are well-suited to the subsurface environment, and are well distributed spatially within the subsurface.

126acd71c231.title: Biostimulation
126acd71c231.sentence: Biostimulation can be enhanced by bioaugmentation.

f28c3618ffbe.title: Biostimulation
f28c3618ffbe.sentence: Tight, impermeable subsurface lithology (tight clays or other fine-grained material) make it difficult to spread additives throughout the affected area.

238fd53303f7.title: Biostimulation
238fd53303f7.sentence: Fractures in the subsurface create preferential pathways in the subsurface which additives preferentially follow, preventing even distribution of additives.

dcbbbb464d12.title: Biostimulation
dcbbbb464d12.sentence: Investigations to determine subsurface characteristics (such as natural groundwater velocity during ambient conditions, hydraulic conductivity of the subsurface, and lithology of the subsurface) are important in developing a successful biostimulation system.

5da224395233.title: Biostimulation
5da224395233.sentence: In addition, a pilot-scale study of the potential biostimulation system should be undertaken prior to full-scale design and implementation.

c9e78603db34.title: Biostimulation
c9e78603db34.sentence: While biostimulation is usually associated with remediation of hydrocarbon or high production volume chemical spills, it is also potentially useful for treatment of less frequently encountered contaminant spills, such as pesticides, particularly herbicides.

4a35f0090368.title: Bioremediation
4a35f0090368.sentence: Specific to marine oil spills, nitrogen and phosphorus have been key nutrients in biodegradation.

70d119a18d7b.title: Brownfield land
70d119a18d7b.sentence: Brownfield land is previously developed land that has been abandoned or left underused, and which may carry pollution or a risk of pollution from previous industrial use.

05e7e6e496f9.title: Brownfield land
05e7e6e496f9.sentence: Examples of post industrial brownfield sites include abandoned factories, ash ponds, landfills, dry cleaning establishments, and gas stations.

e51fb5b34b73.title: Brownfield land
e51fb5b34b73.sentence: Typical contaminants found on contaminated brownfield land include hydrocarbon spillages, solvents, pesticides, heavy metals such as lead (e.g., paints), tributyl tins, and asbestos.

9414e0c9624d.title: Brownfield land
9414e0c9624d.sentence: The definition varies and is decided by policy makers and land developers within different countries.

957b263c9362.title: Brownfield land
957b263c9362.sentence: The main difference in definitions of whether a piece of land is considered a brownfield or not depends on the presence or absence of pollution.

2249474594a9.title: Brownfield land
2249474594a9.sentence: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) defined brownfield as a property where expansion, redevelopment or reuse may be complicated by the presence or potential presence of a hazardous substance, pollutant or contaminant.

ef5d6f8f1f48.title: Brownfield land
ef5d6f8f1f48.sentence: Many contaminated brownfield sites sit unused for decades because the cost of cleaning them to safe standards is more than the land would be worth after redevelopment, in the process becoming involuntary parks as they grow over.

b5638fa564fa.title: Brownfield land
b5638fa564fa.sentence: In the process of cleaning contaminated brownfield sites, previously unknown underground storage tanks, buried drums or buried railroad tank cars containing wastes are sometimes encountered.

67d2721eba6d.title: Brownfield land
67d2721eba6d.sentence: Unexpected circumstances increase the cost for study and clean-up.

468874586a22.title: Brownfield land
468874586a22.sentence: Innovative remediation techniques used at distressed brownfields in recent years include in situ thermal remediation, bioremediation and in situ oxidation.

be31132e8afa.title: Brownfield land
be31132e8afa.sentence: Often, these strategies are used in conjunction with each other or with other remedial strategies such as soil vapor extraction.

f44ebedfbd74.title: Brownfield land
f44ebedfbd74.sentence: Binders can be added to contaminated soil to prevent chemical leaching.

c3d14a37db18.title: Brownfield land
c3d14a37db18.sentence: Some brownfields with heavy metal contamination have even been cleaned up through an innovative approach called phytoremediation, which uses deep-rooted plants to soak up metals in soils into the plant structure as the plant grows.

14ea53edda6e.title: Brownfield land
14ea53edda6e.sentence: To avoid unexpected contamination and increased costs, many developers insist that a site be thoroughly investigated (via a Phase II Site Investigation or Remedial Investigation) prior to commencing remedial cleanup activities.

3c3c2828df2f.title: Brownfield land
3c3c2828df2f.sentence: The term brownfield first came into use on June 28, 1992, at a U.S. congressional field hearing hosted by the Northeast Midwest Congressional Coalition.

95fd976781a2.title: Brownfield land
95fd976781a2.sentence: As of September 2023, the EPA estimates that the EPA Brownfields program has resulted in 134,414 acres of land readied for reuse.

ac16c593ddc5.title: Groundwater pollution
ac16c593ddc5.sentence: Groundwater pollution (also called groundwater contamination) occurs when pollutants are released to the ground and make their way into groundwater.

b8278b044956.title: Groundwater pollution
b8278b044956.sentence: This type of water pollution can also occur naturally due to the presence of a minor and unwanted constituent, contaminant, or impurity in the groundwater, in which case it is more likely referred to as contamination rather than pollution.

15bd311bb9e8.title: Groundwater pollution
15bd311bb9e8.sentence: Groundwater pollution can occur from on-site sanitation systems, landfill leachate, effluent from wastewater treatment plants, leaking sewers, petrol filling stations, hydraulic fracturing (fracking), or from over application of fertilizers in agriculture.

423a2318cd51.title: Groundwater pollution
423a2318cd51.sentence: Pollution (or contamination) can also occur from naturally occurring contaminants, such as arsenic or fluoride.

6610ba6873cc.title: Groundwater pollution
6610ba6873cc.sentence: The pollutant often produces a contaminant plume within an aquifer.

a834eb236f65.title: Groundwater pollution
a834eb236f65.sentence: Movement of water and dispersion within the aquifer spreads the pollutant over a wider area.

14ea6b91095d.title: Groundwater pollution
14ea6b91095d.sentence: Its advancing boundary, often called a plume edge, can intersect with groundwater wells and surface water, such as seeps and springs, making the water supplies unsafe for humans and wildlife.

2bee3f48576b.title: Groundwater pollution
2bee3f48576b.sentence: Different mechanisms have influence on the transport of pollutants, e.g. diffusion, adsorption, precipitation, decay, in the groundwater.

3a49ac44ae56.title: Groundwater pollution
3a49ac44ae56.sentence: Analysis of groundwater pollution may focus on soil characteristics and site geology, hydrogeology, hydrology, and the nature of the contaminants.

2d8bf4e854a8.title: Groundwater pollution
2d8bf4e854a8.sentence: The passage of water through the subsurface can provide a reliable natural barrier to contamination but it only works under favorable conditions.

656f5c737e21.title: Groundwater pollution
656f5c737e21.sentence: Areas of karst topography on limestone bedrock are sometimes vulnerable to surface pollution from groundwater.

0fce9c15e056.title: Groundwater pollution
0fce9c15e056.sentence: Earthquake faults can also be entry routes for downward contaminant entry.

ce0cb3c01e97.title: Groundwater pollution
ce0cb3c01e97.sentence: A noteworthy class of such chemicals is the chlorinated hydrocarbons such as trichloroethylene (used in industrial metal degreasing and electronics manufacturing) and tetrachloroethylene used in the dry cleaning industry.

06b346cfe562.title: Groundwater pollution
06b346cfe562.sentence: Both of these chemicals, which are thought to be carcinogens themselves, undergo partial decomposition reactions, leading to new hazardous chemicals (including dichloroethylene and vinyl chloride).

d4ad15651971.title: Groundwater pollution
d4ad15651971.sentence: Nitrate is the most common chemical contaminant in the world's groundwater and aquifers.

7f03721cd5a3.title: Groundwater pollution
7f03721cd5a3.sentence: It is also stable (it does not degrade) under high oxygen conditions.

bc600a78dee7.title: Groundwater pollution
bc600a78dee7.sentence: Prevention methods include: applying the precautionary principle, groundwater quality monitoring, land zoning for groundwater protection, locating on-site sanitation systems correctly and applying legislation.

416e22cd420e.title: Groundwater pollution
416e22cd420e.sentence: When pollution has occurred, management approaches include point-of-use water treatment, groundwater remediation, or as a last resort, abandonment.

a03847ad75bc.title: Phytoremediation
a03847ad75bc.sentence: Phytoextraction (or phytoaccumulation or phytosequestration) aims to exploit the ability of some plants to absorb certain contaminants from soil or water.

110754caba12.title: Phytoremediation
110754caba12.sentence: In principle, the roots take up substances from the soil or water and concentrate them above ground in the plant biomass.

63a245e77560.title: Phytoremediation
63a245e77560.sentence: Organisms that can uptake high amounts of particular metal-containing compounds are called hyperaccumulators.

cf49ed1dfcc8.title: Phytoremediation
cf49ed1dfcc8.sentence: Since arsenic (As) is a toxic industrial by-product, As-accumulating plants -e.g. Chinese brake - have been proposed to concentrate and then remove As from contaminated soils.

51e55878e317.title: Phytoremediation
51e55878e317.sentence: Phytoextraction could also be performed by non-hyperaccumulating plants (e.g. Populus and Salix).

349a9982dd20.title: Phytoremediation
349a9982dd20.sentence: Although they take up only low levels of pollutants, owing to their high growth rate, such plants could in principle remove a considerable amount of contaminants from the soil.

ea97360f10a5.title: Phytoremediation
ea97360f10a5.sentence: One challenge to phytoremediation is that heavy metals are often insufficiently mobile to be taken up by the plants, hyperaccumulators or otherwise.

20b7af8906e7.title: Phytoremediation
20b7af8906e7.sentence: This challenge prompted the invention of assisted phytoextraction, whereby a chelator is added to soil to increase metal solubility or mobilization so that the plants can absorb them more easily.

d1df087c402e.title: Phytoremediation
d1df087c402e.sentence: Hyperaccumulating plants are often metallophytes, i.e. they hyperaccumulate metals.

5af8a88f15c6.title: Phytoremediation
5af8a88f15c6.sentence: Metallophytes are the basis of phytomining, a proposed technology for collecting valuable metals without excavating.

2f6ee0ea5c87.sentence: GIS in environmental contamination is the use of GIS software to map and analyze contaminants on Earth, including soil contamination, water pollution, and air pollution.

ffd32218f113.title: GIS in environmental contamination
ffd32218f113.sentence: Various GIS methods are used to conduct spatial analysis of pollutants to identify, monitor, and assess them.

ce87d8bdcdf7.title: GIS in environmental contamination
ce87d8bdcdf7.sentence: GIS can use other technologies to advance their process of analysis including remote sensing, LIDAR, GeoAI, and WebGIS.

d2a7cb9c69cf.title: GIS in environmental contamination
d2a7cb9c69cf.sentence: GIS is used to monitor sites for metal contaminants on Earth to identify high-risk sites where remediation and monitoring are needed.

c43fd9cb4eca.title: GIS in environmental contamination
c43fd9cb4eca.sentence: One method includes spatial interpolation, which allows for a more efficient approach to remediation and monitoring of soil and water contaminants.

35655415b80d.title: GIS in environmental contamination
35655415b80d.sentence: Soil contamination from heavy elements can be found in urban environments, which can be attributed to emissions from transportation, industrial activities, and naturally occurring processes, such as background levels (mineral-leaching heavy elements from weathering).

795673c4eb51.sentence: In Idrija, Slovenia, a mercury (Hg) mine had been operating for over 500 years, releasing a significant amount of Hg emissions into the atmosphere.

0d7a57cf9193.title: GIS in environmental contamination

0d7a57cf9193.sentence: These Hg emissions were absorbed by the surface of the soil, which resulted in the release and diffusion of Hg through the soil's pores.

a1d4113ee67d.title: Metal toxicity
a1d4113ee67d.sentence: Metal toxicity or metal poisoning is toxicity affecting plants, animals, or humans due to excessive concentration of metals.

5dec872475e3.title: Metal toxicity
5dec872475e3.sentence: At low concentrations, metals such as copper, iron, manganese, and zinc are essential nutrients obtained through the diet supporting health, but have toxicity at high exposure concentrations.

4de6de5b2e95.title: Metal toxicity
4de6de5b2e95.sentence: Other metals having no biological roles in animals, but with potential for toxicity include arsenic, cadmium, lead, mercury, and thallium.

e6fca33e65bf.title: Metal toxicity
e6fca33e65bf.sentence: Only soluble metal-containing compounds are toxic by forming coordination complexes, which consist of a metal ion surrounded by ligands.

76be669d8078.title: Metal toxicity
76be669d8078.sentence: Toxic metal complexes can be detoxified by conversion to insoluble derivatives or by binding them in rigid molecular environments using chelating agents.

e14075391594.title: Metal toxicity
e14075391594.sentence: Chromium, arsenic, cadmium, mercury, and lead have a strong affinity for sulfur; in the human body they usually bind, via thiol groups (–SH), to enzymes responsible for controlling the speed of metabolic reactions.

a4e1485dad56.title: Metal toxicity
a4e1485dad56.sentence: The resulting sulfur-metal bonds inhibit the proper functioning of the enzymes involved; human health deteriorates, sometimes fatally.

3cbf3b105403.title: Metal toxicity
3cbf3b105403.sentence: The International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry (IUPAC), which standardizes nomenclature, says the term "'heavy metals' is both meaningless and misleading".

8e1b4ebaf69a.title: Metal toxicity
8e1b4ebaf69a.sentence: Not all heavy metals are toxic and some toxic metals are not heavy.

40d8bd10eb3a.title: Metal toxicity
40d8bd10eb3a.sentence: - Arsenic poisoning (As) mainly arises from ground water naturally containing high concentrations of arsenic in the supply of drinking water.

bd1eeaea2042.title: Metal toxicity
bd1eeaea2042.sentence: - Lead poisoning (Pb), in contrast to arsenic poisoning, is caused by industrial materials, such as leaded gasoline and lead leached from plumbing.

526ff49ac86a.title: Metal toxicity
526ff49ac86a.sentence: In 1956, a factory in the city released methylmercury in the industrial wastewater resulting in thousands of deaths and many other health problems.

57d681d6ccec.title: Metal toxicity
57d681d6ccec.sentence: This incident alerted the world to the phenomenon of bioaccumulation.

360cfcbd7349.title: Agricultural pollution
360cfcbd7349.sentence: Agricultural pollution problem refers to biotic and abiotic byproducts of farming practices that result in contamination or degradation of the environment and surrounding ecosystems, and/or cause injury to humans and their economic interests.

7642aea2e1ed.title: Agricultural pollution
7642aea2e1ed.sentence: The pollution may come from a variety of sources, ranging from point source water pollution (from a single discharge point) to more diffuse, landscape-level causes, also known as non-point source pollution and air pollution.

4b62db0b3980.title: Agricultural pollution
4b62db0b3980.sentence: Pollutants from farming include sediments, nutrients, pathogens, pesticides, metals, and salts.

2f6eee44ab9d.title: Agricultural pollution
2f6eee44ab9d.sentence: Pollutants from agriculture greatly affect water quality and can be found in lakes, rivers, wetlands, estuaries, and groundwater.

47fee9568e60.title: Agricultural pollution
47fee9568e60.sentence: Bad management practices include poorly managed animal feeding operations, overgrazing, plowing, fertilizer, and improper, excessive, or badly timed use of pesticides.

77ac4f5afd56.title: Agricultural pollution
77ac4f5afd56.sentence: For example 2,4-D and atrazine have with lifetimes up to 20 years.

bf5461738ede.title: Agricultural pollution
bf5461738ede.sentence: Pesticides can also accumulate in animals that eat contaminated pests and soil organisms.

a146531afcf6.title: Agricultural pollution
a146531afcf6.section: Abiotic sources > From equipment and agricultural plastics
a146531afcf6.sentence: For example, the widespread use of plastic sheeting for greenhouses, plastic storage for applications like animal feed and seed bags and silage, and plastic mulch means that both microplastic and macroplastic are increasingly introduced into farmed landscapes.

dc2fe56838eb.title: Agricultural pollution
dc2fe56838eb.section: Abiotic sources > From equipment and agricultural plastics
dc2fe56838eb.sentence: A 2021 study by FAO of plastic waste in agriculture, found an estimated 10 million tons of plastic waste produced each year.

5962ff1d4f14.title: Agricultural pollution
5962ff1d4f14.sentence: Manures and biosolids, although having value as fertilizers, they may also contain contaminants, including pharmaceuticals and personal care products (PPCPs).

c92cbdc06eb8.title: Electrokinetic remediation
c92cbdc06eb8.sentence: Electrokinetic remediation, also termed electrokinetics, is a technique of using direct electric current to remove organic, inorganic and heavy metal particles from the soil by electric potential.

a27bc590312e.title: Electrokinetic remediation
a27bc590312e.sentence: A basic electrokinetics remediation site contains an external direct current source, a positively charged electrode (or anode) and a negatively charged electrode (or a cathode) placed into the ground.

14178d11d4a1.title: Electrokinetic remediation
14178d11d4a1.sentence: Placement of electrodes is based on the size and shape of known contaminant plumes.

db57f2cd5701.title: Electrokinetic remediation
db57f2cd5701.sentence: Each electrode is encased in a reservoir well in which an electrolytic solution can be injected.

b6869da44e53.title: Electrokinetic remediation
b6869da44e53.sentence: The electrolytic solutions serve both as a conducting media (or pore fluid) and as a means to extract contaminants and introduce chemicals or biological entities.

aff87bb73f1d.title: Electrokinetic remediation
aff87bb73f1d.sentence: Although many types of migrations occur in tandem with the current there are two driving migrations within electrokinetics; ionic migration and electrophoresis.

7951fa2e50f3.title: Electrokinetic remediation
7951fa2e50f3.sentence: The charged particles are driven by electrophoresis flow from the cathode to the anode while electrolytic solution flows from the anode to the cathode.

1f6b0684b4ab.title: Electrokinetic remediation
1f6b0684b4ab.sentence: Of the two main processes electrophoresis (or electromigration) is more dominant than electroosmosis.

11ce3c8a0733.title: Electrokinetic remediation
11ce3c8a0733.sentence: For electromigration to occur absorbed material must be dissolved to an ionic form whether they are metals, organic or inorganic particles.

2cf8ff47372b.title: Electrokinetic remediation
2cf8ff47372b.sentence: Electroosmotic flow between the electrodes promotes the development of a low-pH environment in the soil.

cc81c662cbc2.title: Electrokinetic remediation
cc81c662cbc2.sentence: This low pH environment inhibits metallic contaminants from being sorbed onto soil particle surfaces which aids in the formation of compounds making electrokinetics possible.

bba5bc73865f.title: Electrokinetic remediation
bba5bc73865f.sentence: By this thought it is possible to acidify the soil and induce the release of absorbed heavy metals.

c53fc2e7a593.title: Electrokinetic remediation
c53fc2e7a593.sentence: Heavy metals are one of the main contaminants that are removed by the electrokinetics process.

456bd6e67b28.title: Electrokinetic remediation
456bd6e67b28.sentence: Some metals like cadmium (II) can be removed with high consequences on energy expenditure.

ae765a857fb0.title: Electrokinetic remediation
ae765a857fb0.sentence: Chromium (III) can be removed but with low efficiency because of the ease of hydrolysis allowing it to sorb to other substances.

7ddcada24b14.title: Electrokinetic remediation
7ddcada24b14.sentence: Other heavy metal species that are tested and reported to be treatable include; mercury, zinc, iron, lead, copper, and magnesium.

d238dc168a6b.title: Electrokinetic remediation
d238dc168a6b.sentence: Electrokinetics can also be used to treat polar organic compounds (phenol and acetic acid) and radionucleotides (radium), toxic anions (nitrates and sulfates), dense, non-aqueous-phase liquids (DNAPLs), cyanide, petroleum hydrocarbons (diesel fuel, gasoline, kerosene and lubricating oils), halogenated pollutants, explosives, halogenated and polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons.

0b4f8b5807f6.title: Electrokinetic remediation
0b4f8b5807f6.sentence: Electrokinetic remediation is also suitable for use at sites with radioactive contamination.

85e566c15ea2.title: Electrokinetic remediation
85e566c15ea2.sentence: At tests between 20 and 30 volts, alkali metals were known to move between 50 and 60 cm per day per volts whereas heavy metal moved at velocities between 10 and 20 cm per day per volts.

9c19df2a00f4.title: Electrokinetic remediation
9c19df2a00f4.sentence: It is possible that this difference could be because of the slow desorption and dissolution of heavy metals.

49f3f5f2357e.title: Electrokinetic remediation
49f3f5f2357e.sentence: One of the advantages of electrokinetics is that the remediation can be conducted in situ (within the remediation site) to treat contaminants in low permeability zones to overcome accessibility of contaminants or delivery of treatment.

86e576f151c4.title: Electrokinetic remediation
86e576f151c4.sentence: Electrokinetics has the advantage of use in saturated or unsaturated soils because of the insertion of pore fluid.

aa1425e1927a.title: Electrokinetic remediation
aa1425e1927a.sentence: For soils that are low in permeability like kaolinite and clayey sands it is possible to remove up to 90% of heavy metal contaminants.

91c7326b34e7.title: Electrokinetic remediation
91c7326b34e7.sentence: Counterintuitively, highly permeable soils lower the efficiency of electrokinetics.

32d6e5674d32.title: Electrokinetic remediation
32d6e5674d32.sentence: If the contaminant cannot be dissolved it is not possible to extract the contaminant of interest.

7e17ac92fbff.title: Electrokinetic remediation
7e17ac92fbff.sentence: Electrolysis near the electrodes can alter the pH of the soil especially if the current is induced for an extended period of time.

4b89c6ee4035.title: Electrokinetic remediation
4b89c6ee4035.sentence: Large metal objects that are buried underground also pose as a limitation to electrodes because they offer a path to short circuit the system.

3cfbe93694f1.title: Electrokinetic remediation
3cfbe93694f1.sentence: Another major limitation of the electrokinetics process is the decrease in the electric potential of the system.

f2de0e1f67da.title: Electrokinetic remediation
f2de0e1f67da.sentence: Different polarization effects can decrease how the system runs.

64c25f41c980.title: Electrokinetic remediation
64c25f41c980.sentence: In 1995 at the Paducah site, in Kentucky, USA a new technique was developed for removing heavy metals from soils.

1165027c9898.title: Electrokinetic remediation
1165027c9898.sentence: Called the Lasagna Process, it simply is the creation of several horizontal permeable zones used to provide treatment through the contaminated soil matrix by adding different admixtures to the electrolytic solution.

6ba83542e926.title: Electrokinetic remediation
6ba83542e926.sentence: The first test of this process proved 98% effective of removing trichloroethylene from the Paducah site.

553db75f4e09.title: Bioremediation
553db75f4e09.sentence: Anaerobic bioremediation can in principle be employed to treat a range of oxidized contaminants including PCE, TCE, DCE, VC), chlorinated ethanes (TCA, DCA), chloromethanes (CT, CF), chlorinated cyclic hydrocarbons, various energetics (e.g., perchlorate, RDX, TNT), and nitrate.

3adcd009d954.title: Bioremediation
3adcd009d954.sentence: This process involves the addition of an electron donor to: 1) deplete background electron acceptors including oxygen, nitrate, oxidized iron and manganese and sulfate; and 2) stimulate the biological and/or chemical reduction of the oxidized pollutants.

27b48cfbec8a.title: Bioremediation
27b48cfbec8a.sentence: The added organic substrates are first fermented to hydrogen (H2) and volatile fatty acids (VFAs).

3734d566e20a.title: Bioremediation
3734d566e20a.sentence: The VFAs, including acetate, lactate, propionate and butyrate, provide carbon and energy for bacterial metabolism.

e9ee6abba77d.title: Bioremediation
e9ee6abba77d.sentence: Substrate can be added using conventional well installations, by direct-push technology, or by excavation and backfill such as permeable reactive barriers (PRB) or biowalls.

2a0b01af07e3.title: Bioremediation
2a0b01af07e3.sentence: Slow-release products composed of edible oils or solid substrates tend to stay in place for an extended treatment period.

1b011c8182a1.title: Bioremediation
1b011c8182a1.sentence: For example, under anaerobic conditions, the reductive dehalogenation of TCE may produce dichloroethylene (DCE) and vinyl chloride (VC), which are suspected or known carcinogens.

d8e86fe60bd5.title: Bioremediation
d8e86fe60bd5.sentence: However, the microorganism Dehalococcoides can further reduce DCE and VC to the non-toxic product ethene.

3e3e66fa102d.title: Bioremediation
3e3e66fa102d.sentence: However, the soil is excavated and piled with an aeration system.

5fe2888e705d.title: Bioremediation
5fe2888e705d.sentence: This aeration system enhances microbial activity by introducing oxygen under positive pressure or removes oxygen under negative pressure.

895d55a6ad86.title: Bioremediation
895d55a6ad86.sentence: Windrow systems are similar to compost techniques where soil is periodically turned in order to enhance aeration.

8b1be4e7fa58.title: Bioremediation
8b1be4e7fa58.sentence: Biopiles, similar to bioventing, are used to remove petroleum pollutants by increasing aerobic degradation to contaminated soils.

7be2de7ed078.title: Bioremediation
7be2de7ed078.sentence: This periodic turning also allows contaminants present in the soil to be uniformly distributed which accelerates the process of bioremediation.

fab5cf7160e1.title: Bioremediation
fab5cf7160e1.sentence: Ex situ techniques are often more expensive because of excavation and transportation costs to the treatment facility, while in situ techniques are performed at the site of contamination so they only have installation costs.

0572fca2d1e8.title: Bioremediation
0572fca2d1e8.sentence: Biosparging is the process of groundwater remediation as oxygen, and possible nutrients, is injected.

7709bc5b32ed.title: Bioremediation
7709bc5b32ed.sentence: When oxygen is injected, indigenous bacteria are stimulated to increase rate of degradation.

f3e39b04e74f.title: Bioremediation
f3e39b04e74f.sentence: However, biosparging focuses on saturated contaminated zones, specifically related to ground water remediation.

cc41ae59652b.title: Bioremediation
cc41ae59652b.sentence: Bioventing is a process that increases the oxygen or air flow into the unsaturated zone of the soil, this in turn increases the rate of natural in situ degradation of the targeted hydrocarbon contaminant.

1d6cd56bd3f0.title: Bioremediation
1d6cd56bd3f0.sentence: Air sparging involves the injection of air under pressure below the water table.

d14eb491947f.title: Bioremediation
d14eb491947f.sentence: The air injection pressure must be great enough to overcome the hydrostatic pressure of the water and resistance to air flow through the soil.

b6fc057d176b.title: Bioremediation
b6fc057d176b.sentence: Bioventing, an aerobic bioremediation, is the most common form of oxidative bioremediation process where oxygen is provided as the electron acceptor for oxidation of petroleum, polyaromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), phenols, and other reduced pollutants.

9278f86a07eb.title: Bioremediation
9278f86a07eb.sentence: Microorganisms can degrade a wide variety of hydrocarbons, including components of gasoline, kerosene, diesel, and jet fuel.

1bd637e6653e.title: Bioremediation
1bd637e6653e.sentence: Under ideal aerobic conditions, the biodegradation rates of the low- to moderate-weight aliphatic, alicyclic, and aromatic compounds can be very high.

7881fa930413.title: Bioremediation
7881fa930413.sentence: As molecular weight of the compound increases, the resistance to biodegradation increases simultaneously.

2c645d3a5379.title: Bioremediation
2c645d3a5379.sentence: Another example is bioventing, which is inexpensive to bioremediate contaminated sites, however, this process is extensive and can take a few years to decontaminate a site.

7ce4e6fa87dc.title: Bioremediation
7ce4e6fa87dc.sentence: Approaches for oxygen addition below the water table include recirculating aerated water through the treatment zone, addition of pure oxygen or peroxides, and air sparging.

a757fbdc7c4c.title: Bioremediation
a757fbdc7c4c.sentence: However, the amount of oxygen that can be provided by this method is limited by the low solubility of oxygen in water (8 to 10 mg/L for water in equilibrium with air at typical temperatures).

925453da7f53.title: Bioremediation
925453da7f53.sentence: The use of genetic engineering to create organisms specifically designed for bioremediation is under preliminary research.

40dc59c79968.title: Bioremediation
40dc59c79968.sentence: Two category of genes can be inserted in the organism: degradative genes, which encode proteins required for the degradation of pollutants, and reporter genes, which encode proteins able to monitor pollution levels.

6aed0558962d.title: Bioremediation
6aed0558962d.sentence: Numerous members of Pseudomonas have been modified with the lux gene for the detection of the polyaromatic hydrocarbon naphthalene.

955124166ce1.title: Bioremediation
955124166ce1.sentence: Genetically modified organisms have been created to treat oil spills and break down certain plastics (PET).

3e2d1fca3e63.title: Bioremediation
3e2d1fca3e63.sentence: There are concerns surrounding release and containment of genetically modified organisms into the environment due to the potential of horizontal gene transfer.

255e55624d5b.title: Bioremediation
255e55624d5b.sentence: Organisms can be modified such that they can only survive and grow under specific sets of environmental conditions.

b26ce2acbc04.title: Bioremediation
b26ce2acbc04.sentence: In addition, the tracking of modified organisms can be made easier with the insertion of bioluminescence genes for visual identification.

4949ac68e580.title: Bioremediation
4949ac68e580.sentence: Bioremediation is rarely employed to remediate pollutants.

ef7eff305eb2.title: Bioremediation
ef7eff305eb2.sentence: Heavy metals and radionuclides simply do not biodegrade, although in some cases, these metals can be immobilized.

2e2b7156e653.title: Bioremediation
2e2b7156e653.sentence: In many cases, bioremediation takes more time than other alternatives such as land filling and incineration.

b2ef5528ab6e.title: Bioremediation
b2ef5528ab6e.sentence: The biological processes used by these microbes are highly specific, therefore, many environmental factors must be taken into account and regulated as well.

670fd5e30594.title: Bioremediation
670fd5e30594.sentence: In some cases, microbes do not fully mineralize the pollutant, potentially producing a more toxic compound.

ef681de48b09.title: Bioremediation
ef681de48b09.sentence: It can be difficult to extrapolate the results from the small-scale test studies into big field operations.

4cc6db48e5da.title: Bioremediation
4cc6db48e5da.sentence: Biodegradation requires microbial population with the metabolic capacity to degrade the pollutant in a suitable timeframe.

e5dfed83817d.title: Bioremediation
e5dfed83817d.sentence: The organism must be sufficiently plentiful to clean the site.

896779f90217.title: Bioremediation
896779f90217.sentence: Another major challeng is invasive species: indigenous species are preferred.

64503f136e01.title: Bioremediation
64503f136e01.sentence: Of the many ways to deal with pesticide contamination, bioremediation promises to be more effective.

bf5f3197ba19.title: Bioremediation
bf5f3197ba19.sentence: Many sites around the world are contaminated with agrichemicals.

abf84cd5b4af.title: Bioremediation
abf84cd5b4af.sentence: These agrichemicals often resist biodegradation, by design.

eaa4b3c2ac23.title: Bioremediation
eaa4b3c2ac23.sentence: An example is Lindane which was a commonly used insecticide in the 20th century.

eff17afef262.title: Bioremediation
eff17afef262.sentence: While Lindane has been mostly limited to specific use, it is still produced and used around the world.

2df577fa1ec5.title: Bioremediation
2df577fa1ec5.sentence: Lindane reduces the potential of beneficial bacteria in the soil such as nitrogen fixation cyanobacteria.

4935e1112a18.title: Bioremediation
4935e1112a18.sentence: Actinobacteria has been a promising candidate in situ technique specifically for removing pesticides.

a5d714b1fad0.title: Bioremediation
a5d714b1fad0.sentence: When certain strains of Actinobacteria have been grouped together, their efficiency in degrading pesticides has enhanced.

ccba594d19de.title: Bioremediation
ccba594d19de.sentence: Despite encouraging results, Actinobacteria has only been used in controlled lab settings and will need further development in finding the cost effectiveness and scalability of use.

87adaacafc7f.title: Biodegradation
87adaacafc7f.sentence: Biodegradation is the breakdown of organic matter by microorganisms, such as bacteria and fungi.

bff12fb26abc.title: Biodegradation
bff12fb26abc.sentence: In practice, almost all chemical compounds and materials are subject to biodegradation, the limiting element being time.

3147948c15d0.title: Biodegradation
3147948c15d0.sentence: Biodegradation does not apply to elements; thus heavy metal pollutants do not biodegrade.

692b50fa0b13.title: Biodegradation
692b50fa0b13.sentence: The process of biodegradation can be divided into three stages: biodeterioration, biofragmentation, and assimilation.

f95a921e68cd.title: Biodegradation
f95a921e68cd.sentence: Biofragmentation of a polymer is the lytic process in which bonds within a polymer are cleaved, generating oligomers and monomers in its place.

404bb2ce40c6.title: Biodegradation
404bb2ce40c6.sentence: In the assimilation stage, the resulting products from biofragmentation are then integrated into microbial cells.

10749a54dffa.title: Biodegradation
10749a54dffa.sentence: The main difference between these processes is that anaerobic reactions produce methane, while aerobic reactions do not (however, both reactions produce carbon dioxide, water, some type of residue, and a new biomass).

623635b87ad5.title: Biodegradation
623635b87ad5.sentence: In addition, aerobic digestion typically occurs more rapidly than anaerobic digestion, while anaerobic digestion does a better job reducing the volume and mass of the material.

fb5e633b7cfa.title: Biodegradation
fb5e633b7cfa.sentence: Factors include light, water, oxygen and temperature.

5174d72d0ade.title: Biodegradation
5174d72d0ade.sentence: The degradation rate of many organic compounds is limited by their bioavailability, which is the rate at which a substance is absorbed into a system or made available at the site of physiological activity, as compounds must be released into solution before organisms can degrade them.

cd053e035c50.title: Biodegradation
cd053e035c50.sentence: First one places a solid waste sample in a container with microorganisms and soil, and then aerates the mixture.

b9967e5b9080.title: Biodegradation
b9967e5b9080.sentence: Over the course of several days, microorganisms digest the sample bit by bit and produce carbon dioxide – the resulting amount of CO2 serves as an indicator of degradation.

a5a255b91186.title: In situ thermal desorption
a5a255b91186.sentence: In situ thermal desorption (or thermal conduction heating) is an advanced soil remediation technology where heat and sometimes vacuum are applied directly to contaminated soil.

dfb4950d673a.title: In situ thermal desorption
dfb4950d673a.sentence: As the soil is heated to high (up to 900 °C) temperatures, pollutants are vaporized or broken down by steam distillation, oxidation, or pyrolysis.

85fe8bd1e65a.title: In situ thermal desorption
85fe8bd1e65a.sentence: Contaminants are then captured and extracted through a vacuum system.

1e6645bc0137.title: In situ thermal desorption
1e6645bc0137.sentence: Thermal conductive heating is the application of heat to subsurface soils through conductive heat transfer.

1033bc3f00ac.title: In situ thermal desorption
1033bc3f00ac.sentence: The source of the heat is applied via electric or gas powered thermal wells.

8d530fbaff67.title: In situ thermal desorption
8d530fbaff67.sentence: Thermal wells are inserted vertically, or horizontally, in an array within the soil.

6e5c2820261a.title: In situ thermal desorption
6e5c2820261a.sentence: Vaporized contaminants are collected from vapor extraction wells and containerized for removal or recycling.

6133dce58232.title: In situ thermal desorption
6133dce58232.sentence: This method is effective in tight soils like clay, efficiently removing pollutants.

f8f707014eae.title: In situ thermal desorption
f8f707014eae.sentence: Processes can be applied at low (<100 °C), moderate (~100 °C) and higher (>100 °C) temperature levels to accomplish the remediation of a wide variety of contaminants, both above and below the water table, achieving subsurface target treatment temperatures above the boiling point of water.

ea15c21e8202.title: In situ thermal desorption
ea15c21e8202.sentence: - Developed by Shell Oil Co. in the late 1980s, ISTD/TCH and grew out of enhanced oil recovery research and development.

293cac1262d2.title: In situ thermal desorption
293cac1262d2.sentence: - During the mid-1990s, Shell Oil Company commercialized ISTD with an investment of over $30 million.

60c8b2e1e1a4.title: Nonpoint source pollution
60c8b2e1e1a4.sentence: Pathogens are bacteria and viruses that can be found in water and cause diseases in humans.

3d4a82003c73.title: Nonpoint source pollution
3d4a82003c73.sentence: Typically, pathogens cause disease when they are present in public drinking water supplies.

4e05ce54d02d.title: Nonpoint source pollution
4e05ce54d02d.sentence: Pathogens found in contaminated runoff may include:

c53d0922c18c.title: Nonpoint source pollution
c53d0922c18c.sentence: Coliform bacteria and fecal matter may also be detected in runoff.

a308e50de143.title: Nonpoint source pollution
a308e50de143.sentence: These bacteria are a commonly used indicator of water pollution, but not an actual cause of disease.

80f1a1d25c12.title: Nonpoint source pollution
80f1a1d25c12.sentence: Pathogens may contaminate runoff due to poorly managed livestock operations, faulty septic systems, improper handling of pet waste, the over application of human sewage sludge, contaminated storm sewers, and sanitary sewer overflows.

0cfd31758cd9.title: Groundwater remediation
0cfd31758cd9.sentence: Groundwater remediation is the process that is used to treat polluted groundwater by removing the pollutants or converting them into harmless products.

96d2c56ebd0b.title: Groundwater remediation
96d2c56ebd0b.sentence: Globally, between 25 percent and 40 percent of the world's drinking water is drawn from boreholes and dug wells.

55a17f1e5ae7.title: Groundwater remediation
55a17f1e5ae7.sentence: Consequently, waste materials have often been disposed of or stored on land surfaces where they percolate into the underlying groundwater.

831165d27980.title: Groundwater remediation
831165d27980.sentence: Current practices can still impact groundwater, such as the over application of fertilizer or pesticides, spills from industrial operations, infiltration from urban runoff, and leaking from landfills.

6185cad7b1dc.title: Groundwater remediation
6185cad7b1dc.sentence: Some of the biological treatment techniques include bioaugmentation, bioventing, biosparging, bioslurping, and phytoremediation.

e714ba7cb5aa.title: Groundwater remediation
e714ba7cb5aa.sentence: Some chemical treatment techniques include ozone and oxygen gas injection, chemical precipitation, membrane separation, ion exchange, carbon absorption, aqueous chemical oxidation, and surfactant enhanced recovery.

f7f8cff5b9fd.title: Groundwater remediation
f7f8cff5b9fd.sentence: Physical treatment techniques include, but are not limited to, pump and treat, air sparging, and dual phase extraction.

99e6a962a53b.title: Groundwater remediation
99e6a962a53b.sentence: Most ground water treatment techniques utilize a combination of technologies.

72a706ee4fc9.title: Phytoremediation
72a706ee4fc9.sentence: This process has been proposed to deal with herbicides, trichloroethylene, and methyl tert-butyl ether.

b35a4fba48c3.title: Phytoremediation
b35a4fba48c3.sentence: Trinitrotoluene phytotransformation has been extensively researched and a transformation pathway has been proposed.

0d41855c7f73.title: Phytoremediation
0d41855c7f73.sentence: The term "Green Liver" has been used to describe phytotransformation, as plants can be thought to behave analogously to the human liver when dealing with these xenobiotic compounds (foreign compound/pollutant).

14d778453a78.title: Phytoremediation
14d778453a78.sentence: As plants can translocate and accumulate particular contaminants, plants can be used as biosensors of subsurface contamination, thereby allowing investigators to delineate contaminant plumes.

c3f962310f91.title: Phytoremediation
c3f962310f91.sentence: Chlorinated solvents, such as trichloroethylene, have been observed in tree trunks at concentrations related to groundwater concentrations.

7039849557ef.title: Phytoremediation
7039849557ef.sentence: To ease field implementation of phytoscreening, standard methods have been developed to extract a section of the tree trunk for later laboratory analysis, often by using an increment borer.

ee1a3047ebba.title: Phytoremediation
ee1a3047ebba.sentence: Phytoscreening could lead to more optimized site investigations and lower site cleanup costs.

74df846ba072.title: Phytoremediation
74df846ba072.sentence: This concept is yet another example of phytoremediation that has achieved no practical application.

64c6b7669dcb.title: Phytoremediation
64c6b7669dcb.sentence: Phytostabilization lowers the mobility of substances in the soil, for example, by limiting the leaching of substances from the soil.

f956f8147616.title: Phytoremediation
f956f8147616.sentence: It focuses on the long term stabilization and containment of the pollutant.

544c60abc367.title: Phytoremediation
544c60abc367.sentence: Unlike phytoextraction, phytostabilization focuses mainly on sequestering pollutants in soil near the roots but not in plant tissues.

771ac098252c.title: Phytoremediation
771ac098252c.sentence: Stabilization results in reduced erosion, runoff, leaching, in addition to reducing the bioavailability of the contaminant.

617ee2070840.title: Phytoremediation
617ee2070840.sentence: Phytostabilization involving a vegetative cap has been used to stabilize and contain mine tailings.

f5447fa54524.title: Phytoremediation
f5447fa54524.sentence: Some soil amendments decrease radiosource mobility – while at some concentrations the same amendments will increase mobility.

10f55e804550.title: Phytoremediation
10f55e804550.sentence: This process occurs within the rhizosphere, which is the layer of soil that surrounds the roots.

de2af86097ed.title: Phytoremediation
de2af86097ed.sentence: Plants release carbohydrates and acids that stimulate microorganism activity which results in the biodegradation of the organic contaminants.

1eb37f521bf5.title: Phytoremediation
1eb37f521bf5.sentence: Leaf litter and organic matter from plants can stabilize microbial soil biosiversity and minimize further loss of microogranisms from contaminants.

ec5e82fbd525.title: Phytoremediation
ec5e82fbd525.sentence: Phytostimulation has been tested with petroleum, PCBs, and PAHs.

40c275484597.title: Phytoremediation
40c275484597.sentence: Phytovolatilization is the removal of substances from soil or water with release into the air, as a result of phytotransformation to more volatile and/or less polluting substances.

f497df3e47f9.title: Phytoremediation
f497df3e47f9.sentence: Evidence has been presented that selenium (Se) and mercury (Hg) can removed from soil through phytovolatilization.

d73c7b00d05e.title: Phytoremediation
d73c7b00d05e.sentence: Selenium is volatilized as dimethyl selenide and mercury as the element.

214bf74428c0.title: Phytoremediation
214bf74428c0.sentence: Poplar trees have been touted for removing VOCs, exploiting the high rate of transpiration for this tree species.

29858226fa30.title: Point source pollution
29858226fa30.sentence: A point source of pollution is a single identifiable source of air, water, thermal, noise or light pollution.

c783dce39a22.title: Point source pollution
c783dce39a22.sentence: A point source has negligible extent, distinguishing it from other pollution source geometrics (such as nonpoint source or area source).

670a8027653b.title: Point source pollution
670a8027653b.sentence: The sources are called point sources because in mathematical modeling, they can be approximated as a mathematical point to simplify analysis.

625dc1bb5a9c.title: Point source pollution
625dc1bb5a9c.sentence: - Water pollution from factories, power plants, municipal sewage treatment plants and some farms (see concentrated animal feeding operation).

89e74d37fc5e.title: Point source pollution
89e74d37fc5e.sentence: - Man-made, natural, and groundwater reservoirs can all be contaminated by point source pollution which can threaten human health and safety.

44158b87bf5f.title: Nutrient pollution
44158b87bf5f.section: Reducing nutrient pollution > Nutrient source apportionment
44158b87bf5f.sentence: Nutrient source apportionment is used to estimate the nutrient load from various sectors entering water bodies, following attenuation or treatment.

360d4bcf0758.title: Nutrient pollution
360d4bcf0758.section: Reducing nutrient pollution > Nutrient source apportionment
360d4bcf0758.sentence: Agriculture is typically the principal source of nitrogen in water bodies in Europe, whereas in many countries households and industries tend to be the dominant contributors of phosphorus.

c4d4305c3c70.title: Nutrient pollution
c4d4305c3c70.section: Reducing nutrient pollution > Nutrient source apportionment
c4d4305c3c70.sentence: There are two broad approaches to load apportionment modelling, (i) load-orientated approaches which apportion origin based on in-stream monitoring data and (ii) source-orientated approaches where amounts of diffuse, or nonpoint source pollution, emissions are calculated using models typically based on export coefficients from catchments with similar characteristics.

783e4a9f366d.title: Nutrient pollution
783e4a9f366d.section: Reducing nutrient pollution > Nutrient source apportionment
783e4a9f366d.sentence: For example, the Source Load Apportionment Model (SLAM) takes the latter approach, estimating the relative contribution of sources of nitrogen and phosphorus to surface waters in Irish catchments without in-stream monitoring data by integrating information on point discharges (urban wastewater, industry and septic tank systems), diffuse sources (pasture, arable, forestry, etc.), and catchment data, including hydrogeological characteristics.

7514b677b648.title: Nutrient pollution
7514b677b648.sentence: Nutrient trading is a type of water quality trading, a market-based policy instrument used to improve or maintain water quality.

28cb9884d26f.title: Nutrient pollution
28cb9884d26f.sentence: Water quality trading involves the voluntary exchange of pollution reduction credits from sources with low costs of pollution control to those with high costs of pollution control, and the same principles apply to nutrient water quality trading.

7fd145d64f97.title: Nutrient pollution
7fd145d64f97.sentence: The concept of water quality trading is based on the fact that different pollution sources in a watershed can face very different costs to control the same pollutant.

53dcbc5b645d.title: Nutrient pollution
53dcbc5b645d.sentence: The underlying principle is "polluter pays", usually linked with a regulatory requirement for participating in the trading program.

b03f8acf7aeb.title: Nutrient pollution
b03f8acf7aeb.sentence: A 2013 Forest Trends report summarized water quality trading programs and found three main types of funders: beneficiaries of watershed protection, polluters compensating for their impacts and "public good payers" that may not directly benefit, but fund the pollution reduction credits on behalf of a government or NGO.

a9d7655006d9.title: Nutrient pollution
a9d7655006d9.sentence: As of 2013, payments were overwhelmingly initiated by public good payers like governments and NGOs.

e520ae59e6df.title: Landfarming
e520ae59e6df.sentence: Landfarming is an ex situ waste treatment process that is performed in the upper soil zone or in biotreatment cells.

0893efef0cd4.title: Landfarming
0893efef0cd4.sentence: Contaminated soils, sediments, or sludges are transported to the landfarming site, mixed into the soil surface and periodically turned over (tilled) to aerate the mixture.

f1b350593221.title: Landfarming
f1b350593221.sentence: These land farming activities cultivate and enhance microbial degradation of hazardous compounds.

9dedd7e0f99a.title: Landfarming
9dedd7e0f99a.sentence: This technique has been used for years in the management and disposal of drill cuttings, oily sludge and other petroleum refinery wastes.

a6afc154e1cc.title: Landfarming
a6afc154e1cc.sentence: The equipment employed in land farming is typical of that used in agricultural operations.

b97a2a7cc40e.title: Landfarming
b97a2a7cc40e.sentence: Landfarming commonly uses a clay or composite liner to intercept leaching contaminants and prevent groundwater pollution, however, a liner is not a universal requirement.

0e9e35f8ad17.title: Landfarming
0e9e35f8ad17.sentence: As a rule of thumb, the higher the molecular weight (i.e., the more rings within a polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon), the slower the degradation rate.

286e92365bc6.title: Landfarming
286e92365bc6.sentence: Also, the more chlorinated or nitrated the compound, the more difficult it is to degrade.

df1644941bf3.title: Landfarming
df1644941bf3.sentence: Hydrocarbon compounds that have been identified as being not readily degraded by land farming include creosote, pentachlorophenol (PCP), and bunker C oil.

436fd0793f71.title: Landfarming
436fd0793f71.sentence: - the conditions advantageous for biological degradation of contaminants are largely uncontrolled, which increases the required length of time until complete degradation, particularly for recalcitrant compounds

881f7a5c352d.title: Landfarming
881f7a5c352d.sentence: - high levels of hydrocarbon contamination (>7%) are toxic to the microbes and will not degrade

d7439a61b8e2.title: Landfarming
d7439a61b8e2.sentence: - the microbes convert hydrocarbons to greenhouse gases

e276419f7283.title: Radioactive contamination
e276419f7283.sentence: Radioactive contamination, also called radiological pollution, is the deposition of, or presence of radioactive substances on surfaces or within solids, liquids, or gases (including the human body), where their presence is unintended or undesirable (from the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) definition).

3ad94e393416.title: Radioactive contamination
3ad94e393416.sentence: Such contamination presents a hazard because the radioactive decay of the contaminants produces ionizing radiation (namely alpha, beta, gamma rays and free neutrons).

eb9d30127fe2.title: Radioactive contamination
eb9d30127fe2.sentence: The sources of radioactive pollution can be classified into two groups: natural and man-made.

e44c7e685ff5.title: Radioactive contamination
e44c7e685ff5.section: Sources of contamination > Naturally occurring radioactivity
e44c7e685ff5.sentence: Elements like uranium and thorium, and their decay products, are present in rock and soil.

78b768bd8a70.title: Radioactive contamination
78b768bd8a70.section: Sources of contamination > Naturally occurring radioactivity
78b768bd8a70.sentence: Naturally occurring radioactive materials (NORM) can be brought to the surface or concentrated by human activities such as mining, oil and gas extraction, and coal consumption.

69cfe7e296d8.title: Radioactive contamination
69cfe7e296d8.sentence: Following an atmospheric nuclear weapon discharge or a nuclear reactor containment breach, the air, soil, people, plants, and animals in the vicinity will become contaminated by nuclear fuel and fission products.

3099601fa9e1.title: Radioactive contamination
3099601fa9e1.sentence: Cases of widespread radioactive contamination include the Bikini Atoll, the Rocky Flats Plant in Colorado, the area near the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear disaster, the area near the Chernobyl disaster, and the area near the Mayak disaster.

f092a50d56ac.title: Radioactive contamination
f092a50d56ac.sentence: Nuclear fallout is the distribution of radioactive contamination by the 520 atmospheric nuclear explosions that took place from the 1950s to the 1980s.

9e3459369856.title: Radioactive contamination
9e3459369856.sentence: The degree of hazard is determined by the concentration of the contaminants, the energy of the radiation being emitted, the type of radiation, and the proximity of the contamination to organs of the body.

3af7e037fad4.title: Radioactive contamination
3af7e037fad4.sentence: In some cases of large areas of contamination, the contamination may be mitigated by burying and covering the contaminated substances with concrete, soil, or rock to prevent further spread of the contamination to the environment.

669e449d230a.title: Radioactive contamination
669e449d230a.sentence: Cleaning up contamination results in radioactive waste unless the radioactive material can be returned to commercial use by reprocessing.

65b6c92ce7da.title: Radioactive contamination
65b6c92ce7da.sentence: Stripping out the key radioisotope threatening health (caesium-137) from low-level waste could also dramatically decrease the volume of waste requiring special disposal.

3119dc5f88b3.title: Radioactive contamination
3119dc5f88b3.sentence: A goal is to find techniques that might be able to strip out 80 to 95% of the caesium from contaminated soil and other materials, efficiently and without destroying the organic content in the soil.

fed0e698ece3.title: Radioactive contamination
fed0e698ece3.sentence: The aim is to get annual exposure from the contaminated environment down to one millisievert (mSv) above background.

ce1ec72a5e37.title: Radioactive contamination
ce1ec72a5e37.sentence: The national government is under pressure to clean up radioactivity due to the Fukushima nuclear accident of March 2011 from as much land as possible so that some of the 110,000 displaced people can return.

39bf93526972.title: Permeable reactive barrier
39bf93526972.sentence: One definition for PRBs is an in situ treatment zone that passively captures a plume of contaminants and removes or breaks down the contaminants, releasing uncontaminated water.

f36352ebef22.title: Permeable reactive barrier
f36352ebef22.sentence: A permeable reactive barrier (PRB), also referred to as a permeable reactive treatment zone (PRTZ), is a developing technology that has been recognized as being a cost-effective technology for in situ (at the site) groundwater remediation.

06477871bf15.title: Permeable reactive barrier
06477871bf15.sentence: PRBs are typically installed by digging a long trench in the path of the flow of the contaminated groundwater.

47eda0d3a26a.title: Permeable reactive barrier
47eda0d3a26a.sentence: The trench is then filled with the reactive materials (typically iron, carbon, or limestone).

42c11f2fd56f.title: Permeable reactive barrier
42c11f2fd56f.sentence: After the trench has been filled with reactive material, soil will typically be used to cover the PRB, thus eliminating visibility from the surface.

eee2e683e69c.title: Permeable reactive barrier
eee2e683e69c.sentence: The two main processes are immobilization (AKA sequestration) and transformation.

a809b636bffb.title: Permeable reactive barrier
a809b636bffb.sentence: Immobilization of the contaminant may occur through sorption to the barrier materials or precipitation from the dissolved state.

44c3453789b2.title: Permeable reactive barrier
44c3453789b2.sentence: Sorption and precipitation are potentially reversible and may thus require removal of the reactive medium and gathered products in order to continue with remediation.

2e28324f1f93.title: Permeable reactive barrier
2e28324f1f93.sentence: Transformation most commonly takes the form of an irreversible redox reaction.

20c5985d3f3d.title: Permeable reactive barrier
20c5985d3f3d.sentence: Zerovalent Iron was the first material to be used in PRBs for groundwater remediation.

fcf7ae7a617b.title: Permeable reactive barrier
fcf7ae7a617b.sentence: It continues to be the main material used in the construction of these barriers.

e07786ed9ef5.title: Permeable reactive barrier
e07786ed9ef5.sentence: Sometimes material will be put into the ground to stimulate the growth of microbes that facilitate the groundwater remediation.

702107a89108.title: Permeable reactive barrier
702107a89108.sentence: Surfactant Modified Zeolites (SMZs) are promising for treating non-polar organic contaminants.

eed52b90c5f3.title: Permeable reactive barrier
eed52b90c5f3.sentence: Peat moss seems to be an effective ion-exchange material for removing heavy metals and some anions.

37194f1a57ef.title: Permeable reactive barrier
37194f1a57ef.sentence: The reactivity of the media, rather than a reduction in permeability is more likely the factor that limits field PRB longevity.

596a0c67333a.title: Permeable reactive barrier
596a0c67333a.sentence: Depending on assumptions of controlling factors, longevity estimates can differ by an order of magnitude (e.g. 10–100 years).

64e500ed6b3b.title: Bioremediation
64e500ed6b3b.sentence: The indigenous microbes present will determine the metabolic activity and act as a natural attenuation.

96f207efe6ae.title: Bioremediation
96f207efe6ae.sentence: While there is no anthropogenic involvement in bioattenuation, the contaminated site must still be monitored.

8fd0a6244bb1.title: Natural attenuation
8fd0a6244bb1.sentence: Natural attenuation occurs through dilution, evaporation, sorption onto soil or plant particles, and biodegradation; it works if only smaller amounts of contaminants are left and the actual source of contaminants was removed.

f349a2693e85.title: Natural attenuation
f349a2693e85.sentence: Often it is referred to as monitored natural attenuation, because environmental agencies check soil and water for the contaminant levels over time.

5d4f4116a0fe.title: In situ bioremediation
5d4f4116a0fe.sentence: Monitored natural attenuation is used in sites where the source of contamination is no longer present, often after other more active types of in situ bioremediation have been conducted.

6e826407ae4d.title: Environmental remediation
6e826407ae4d.sentence: Broad categories of bioremediation include biostimulation, bioaugmentation, and natural recovery (natural attenuation).

d1fde10cba81.title: Soil
d1fde10cba81.sentence: Techniques include leaching, air sparging, soil conditioners, phytoremediation, bioremediation and Monitored Natural Attenuation.

b59eba414c17.title: Environmental remediation
b59eba414c17.sentence: Oxygen gas or ambient air can also be injected to promote growth of aerobic bacteria which accelerate natural attenuation of organic contaminants.

b5c69b669895.title: Environmental remediation
b5c69b669895.sentence: One disadvantage of this approach is the possibility of decreasing anaerobic contaminant destruction natural attenuation where existing conditions enhance anaerobic bacteria which normally live in the soil prefer a reducing environment.

b292d373a1ac.title: Surfactant leaching (decontamination)
b292d373a1ac.sentence: Surfactant leaching is a method of water and soil decontamination, e.g., for oil recovery in petroleum industry.

d7793f6d2e81.title: Surfactant leaching (decontamination)
d7793f6d2e81.sentence: It involves mixing of contaminated water or soil with surfactants with the subsequent leaching of emulsified contaminants.

8828df6e4ac6.title: Surfactant leaching (decontamination)
8828df6e4ac6.sentence: In oil recovery, most common surfactant types are ethoxylated alcohols, ethoxylated nonylphenols, sulphates, sulphonates, and biosurfactants.

0c3f43bb3317.title: Environmental remediation
0c3f43bb3317.sentence: This is used in removing non-aqueous phase liquids (NAPLs) from aquifer.

f09c8a23ffdc.title: Environmental remediation
f09c8a23ffdc.sentence: This is done by pumping surfactant solution into contaminated aquifer using injection wells which are passed through contaminated zones to the extraction wells.

9234fcd8884a.title: Environmental remediation
9234fcd8884a.sentence: The Surfactant solution containing contaminants is then captured and pumped out by extraction wells for further treatment at the surface.

23b2a325af02.title: Bioaugmentation
23b2a325af02.sentence: Bioaugmentation is a type of bioremediation commonly used in municipal wastewater treatment to restart activated sludge bioreactors.

2d603ff7f641.title: Bioremediation
2d603ff7f641.sentence: In some cases, specialized microbial cultures are added (bioaugmentation) to further enhance biodegradation.

aa8d3e2db52b.title: Bioaugmentation
aa8d3e2db52b.sentence: Aside from waste water treatment, bioaugmentation remains more aspirational than practical on scale.

bac4b2d1398a.title: Bioaugmentation
bac4b2d1398a.sentence: Relevant to soil remediation, bioaugmentation has been proposed for decontamination of polluted soils.

7747de45a883.title: Bioaugmentation
7747de45a883.sentence: It has been proposed for treatment of chlorocarbons (e.g. from dry cleaning facilities) and hydrocarbons (e.g. from petrol stations), TX.

eace871cf064.title: Bioaugmentation
eace871cf064.sentence: Bioaugmentation is typically performed in conjunction with the addition of electron donor (biostimulation) to achieve geochemical conditions in groundwater that favor the growth of the dechlorinating microorganisms in the bioaugmentation culture.

462b2bd2eb76.title: Bioaugmentation
462b2bd2eb76.section: Case studies > Failures and potential solutions
462b2bd2eb76.sentence: There have been many instances where bioaugmentation had deficiencies in its process, including the use of the wrong organism.

24f8dcf8d1de.title: Bioaugmentation
24f8dcf8d1de.section: Case studies > Failures and potential solutions
