24f8dcf8d1de.sentence: The implementation of bioaugmentation on the environment can pose problems of predation, nutritional competition between indigenous and inoculated bacteria, insufficient inoculations, and disturbing the ecological balance due to large inoculations.

e1246951f42c.title: Bioaugmentation
e1246951f42c.section: Case studies > Failures and potential solutions
e1246951f42c.sentence: In many of the cases that have failed, only the microbes' ability to break down compounds was considered and less their fitness in existing communities and the resulting competitive stress.

3440bcfa1f5f.title: Mycoremediation
3440bcfa1f5f.sentence: Many fungi are hyperaccumulators, therefore they are able to concentrate toxins in their fruiting bodies for later removal.

a7b1cbec004b.title: Mycoremediation
a7b1cbec004b.sentence: Hyperaccumulation occurs via biosorption on the cellular surface, where the metals enter the mycelium passively with very little intracellular uptake.

aa5c6e199536.title: Mycoremediation
aa5c6e199536.sentence: A variety of fungi, such as Pleurotus, Aspergillus, and Trichoderma, have proven to be effective in the removal of lead, cadmium, nickel, chromium, mercury, arsenic, copper, boron, iron and zinc in marine environments, wastewater and on land.

5769624d7ed3.title: Mycoremediation
5769624d7ed3.sentence: This is usually true for populations that have been exposed to contaminants for a long time, and have developed a high tolerance.

6d0736f9e423.title: Mycoremediation
6d0736f9e423.sentence: A dilution of the water can drastically improve the ability of biosorption of the fungi.

c1404c9fce9c.title: Mycoremediation
c1404c9fce9c.sentence: The capacity of certain fungi to extract metals from the ground also can be useful for bioindicator purposes, and can be a problem when the mushroom is of an edible variety.

c39029b9dc16.title: Mycoremediation
c39029b9dc16.sentence: For example, the shaggy ink cap (Coprinus comatus), a common edible mushroom found in the Northern Hemisphere, can be a very good bioindicator of mercury.

b2146376d8ec.title: Mycoremediation
b2146376d8ec.sentence: However, as the shaggy ink cap accumulates mercury in its body, it can be toxic to the consumer.

de0e85efdfc0.title: Mycoremediation
de0e85efdfc0.sentence: For example, VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland reported an 80% recovery of gold from electronic waste using mycofiltration techniques.

0b42ec973169.title: Mycoremediation
0b42ec973169.sentence: In fact, cell walls of some species of dead fungi can be used as a filter that can adsorb heavy metals and radionuclides present in industrial effluents, preventing them from being released into the environment.

b62fe84a36b3.title: Mycoremediation
b62fe84a36b3.sentence: Wood-decay fungi, especially white rot, secrete extracellular enzymes and acids that break down lignin and cellulose, the two main building blocks of plant fiber.

57da7f6142a2.title: Mycoremediation
57da7f6142a2.sentence: These are long-chain organic (carbon-based) compounds, structurally similar to many organic pollutants.

c72140bbee2c.title: Mycoremediation
c72140bbee2c.sentence: The enzymes involved in this degradation are ligninolytic and include lignin peroxidase, versatile peroxidase, manganese peroxidase, general lipase, laccase and sometimes intracellular enzymes, especially the cytochrome P450.

738bef60f556.title: Mycoremediation
738bef60f556.sentence: Other toxins fungi are able to degrade into harmless compounds include petroleum fuels, phenols in wastewater, polychlorinated biphenyl (PCB) in contaminated soils using Pleurotus ostreatus, polyurethane in aerobic and anaerobic conditions, such as conditions at the bottom of landfills using two species of the Ecuadorian fungus Pestalotiopsis, and more.

000e7c8d6f35.title: Mycoremediation
000e7c8d6f35.sentence: The mechanisms of degradation are not always clear, as the mushroom may be a precursor to subsequent microbial activity rather than individually effective in the removal of pollutants.

378f3c78d954.title: Mycoremediation
378f3c78d954.sentence: The most commonly used fungi for helping in the degradation of such substances are white rot fungi, which, thanks to their extracellular ligninolytic enzymes like laccase and manganese peroxidase, are able to degrade high quantity of such components.

5416a5d22349.title: Mycoremediation
5416a5d22349.sentence: Examples includes the insecticide endosulfan, imazalil, thiophanate methyl, ortho-phenylphenol, diphenylamine, chlorpyrifos in wastewater, and atrazine in clay-loamy soils.

d4cde47cb24c.title: Mycoremediation
d4cde47cb24c.sentence: Mycoremediation has proven to be a cheap and effective remediation technology for dyes such as malachite green, nigrosin and basic fuchsin with Aspergillus niger and Phanerochaete chrysosporium and Congo red, a carcinogenic dye recalcitrant to biodegradative processes, direct blue 14 (using Pleurotus).

f4c0694b41dd.title: Mycoremediation
f4c0694b41dd.sentence: Pentachlorophenol (PCP) has been used worldwide as a wood preservative, biocides and for the bleaching of paper or tissues.

2815f95e8dfa.title: Mycoremediation
2815f95e8dfa.sentence: PCP toxicity and extensive use has placed it among the worst environmental pollutants, and therefore its microbiological degradation to develop bioremediation techniques has been intensively studied.

4d74f88b5a7f.title: Mycoremediation
4d74f88b5a7f.sentence: The removal of soil contaminants by mycorrhizal fungi is called mycorrhizoremediation.

36996223ac99.title: Mycoremediation
36996223ac99.sentence: Researchers found that phytoremediation is enhanced by mycorrhizae.

b6d5201cc51e.title: Mycoremediation
b6d5201cc51e.sentence: Mycorrhizal fungi, especially AMF, can greatly improve the phytoremediation capacity of some plants.

ac8dde179566.title: Mycoremediation
ac8dde179566.sentence: This is mostly due to the stress the plants suffer because of the pollutants is greatly reduced in the presence of AMF, so they can grow more and produce more biomass.

5bd81e4fecb8.title: Mycoremediation
5bd81e4fecb8.sentence: The fungi also provide more nutrition, especially phosphorus, and promote the overall health of the plants.

45b303917447.title: Mycoremediation
45b303917447.sentence: Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) produce proteins that bind heavy metals and thereby decrease their bioavailability.

e54f6182255c.title: Mycoremediation
e54f6182255c.sentence: The mycelium's quick expansion can also greatly extend the rhizosphere influence zone (hyphosphere), providing the plant with access to more nutrients and contaminants.

59b053645571.title: Mycoremediation
59b053645571.sentence: Increasing the rhizosphere overall health also means a rise in the bacteria population, which can also contribute to the bioremediation process.

be83781375b2.title: Mycoremediation
be83781375b2.sentence: This relationship has been proven useful with many pollutants, such as Rhizophagus intraradices and Robinia pseudoacacia in lead contaminated soil, Rhizophagus intraradices with Glomus versiforme inoculated into vetiver grass for lead removal, AMF and Calendula officinalis in cadmium and lead contaminated soil, and in general was effective in increasing the plant bioremediation capacity for metals, petroleum fuels, and PAHs.

38b8da904b40.title: Mycoremediation
38b8da904b40.sentence: In wetlands AMF greatly promote the biodegradation of organic pollutants like benzene-, methyl tert-butyl ether- and ammonia from groundwater when inoculated into Phragmites australis.

dcead1308a33.title: Ecotoxicology
dcead1308a33.sentence: Ecotoxicology is the study of how organisms, ecosystems, and populations are affected by toxic chemicals.

cdf0ca2423ba.title: Ecotoxicology
cdf0ca2423ba.sentence: This field is multidisciplinary and integrates toxicology and ecology.

806931f6077a.title: Ecotoxicology
806931f6077a.sentence: Ecotoxicology differs from environmental toxicology; it examines the effects of pollution across all biological levels, from molecular to entire ecosystems.

e5a43f6272a9.title: Ecotoxicology
e5a43f6272a9.sentence: Environmental toxicology, on the other hand, focuses specifically on how organisms are affected, specifically human health.

ab8e6c7df834.title: Ecotoxicology
ab8e6c7df834.sentence: Once these chemicals are introduced into an ecosystem, they begin to move through the food web, resulting in accumulation within the organisms over time.

2f968c245b76.title: Ecotoxicology
2f968c245b76.sentence: Due to this, the top predators are often the most affected by the toxic substances.

2966df98f9da.title: Ecotoxicology
2966df98f9da.sentence: While contaminants do result in direct toxic effects, such as mortality, they can also produce indirect effects such as the alteration of organism behavior, their interactions within their ecosystems, and their reproduction.

cc3a45e29fae.title: Ecotoxicology
cc3a45e29fae.sentence: Nonlethal exposure to these pollutants can impair movement or reduce feeding rates; all of which can influence competition and predator-prey relationships.

c9f99b308c0c.title: Ecotoxicology
c9f99b308c0c.section: Effects of ecotoxicity on a community
c9f99b308c0c.sentence: Species-rich communities are more likely to recover from contaminant disturbances than a less diverse one.

0770192c48a1.title: Ecotoxicology
0770192c48a1.sentence: Ecotoxicology is used to understand and predict how pollution will affect environmental systems.

350130770b7d.title: Ecotoxicology
350130770b7d.sentence: Where pollution has already affected an ecosystem, ecotoxicology studies can identify ways to restore ecosystem services, structures, and functions.

9d561d8b0157.title: Arsenic contamination of groundwater
9d561d8b0157.sentence: Arsenic contamination of groundwater is a form of groundwater pollution which is often due to naturally occurring high concentrations of arsenic in deeper levels of groundwater.

eeee13afb7da.title: Arsenic contamination of groundwater
eeee13afb7da.sentence: A 2007 study found that over 137 million people in more than 70 countries are probably affected by arsenic poisoning of drinking water.

040910c365e8.title: Arsenic contamination of groundwater
040910c365e8.sentence: The World Health Organization recommends limiting arsenic concentrations in water to 10 μg/L, although this is often an unattainable goal for many problem areas due to the difficult nature of removing arsenic from water sources.

9d8d9f101407.title: Groundwater pollution
9d8d9f101407.sentence: The natural arsenic pollution occurs because aquifer sediments contain organic matter that generates anaerobic conditions in the aquifer.

3d34d9ac049c.title: Groundwater pollution
3d34d9ac049c.sentence: These conditions result in the microbial dissolution of iron oxides in the sediment and, thus, the release of the arsenic, normally strongly bound to iron oxides, into the water.

2ca4714549b1.title: Groundwater pollution
2ca4714549b1.sentence: As a consequence, arsenic-rich groundwater is often iron-rich, although secondary processes often obscure the association of dissolved arsenic and dissolved iron.

a55ac75e09b8.title: Groundwater pollution
a55ac75e09b8.sentence: Arsenic is found in groundwater most commonly as the reduced species arsenite and the oxidized species arsenate, the acute toxicity of arsenite being somewhat greater than that of arsenate.

f2ca08e6ee20.title: Arsenic contamination of groundwater
f2ca08e6ee20.section: Speciation of arsenic compounds in water
f2ca08e6ee20.sentence: These compounds are extracted from the underlying rocks that surround the aquifer.

dee7ad836b34.title: Arsenic contamination of groundwater
dee7ad836b34.section: Contamination in specific nations and regions > South Asia > Bangladesh
dee7ad836b34.sentence: During the 1970s, UNICEF worked with the Department of Public Health Engineering to install tube-wells.

89fb7c025788.title: Arsenic contamination of groundwater
89fb7c025788.section: Contamination in specific nations and regions > South Asia > Bangladesh
89fb7c025788.sentence: This lack of precaution led to one of the largest mass poisonings of a population because the ground water used for drinking was contaminated with arsenic.

fbaaeca9ae02.title: Arsenic contamination of groundwater
fbaaeca9ae02.section: Contamination in specific nations and regions > South Asia > Bangladesh
fbaaeca9ae02.sentence: In 1993, it was discovered that groundwater in large parts of Bangladesh was naturally contaminated with arsenic.

2b2bbc5a820b.title: Arsenic contamination of groundwater
2b2bbc5a820b.section: Contamination in specific nations and regions > South Asia > Bangladesh
2b2bbc5a820b.sentence: In the Ganges Delta, the affected wells are typically more than 20 meters and less than 100 meters deep.

d9a74fdd8987.title: Arsenic contamination of groundwater
d9a74fdd8987.section: Contamination in specific nations and regions > South Asia > Bangladesh
d9a74fdd8987.sentence: Groundwater closer to the surface typically has spent a shorter time in the ground, therefore likely absorbing a lower concentration of arsenic; water deeper than 100 meters is exposed to much older sediments, which have already been depleted of arsenic.

38f18c26cbe6.title: Arsenic contamination of groundwater
38f18c26cbe6.sentence: Researchers from Bangladesh and the United Kingdom have claimed that dietary intake of arsenic adds significantly to total intake where contaminated water is used for irrigation.

1cd4365fec4c.title: Dense non-aqueous phase liquid
1cd4365fec4c.sentence: A dense non-aqueous phase liquid or DNAPL is a denser-than-water NAPL, i.e. a liquid that is both denser than water and is immiscible in or does not dissolve in water.

bf34795e041e.title: Dense non-aqueous phase liquid
bf34795e041e.sentence: DNAPLs tends to sink below the water table when spilled in significant quantities and only stop when they reach impermeable layers such as clay layers or low porosity bedrock.

1ae720d77f4d.title: Dense non-aqueous phase liquid
1ae720d77f4d.sentence: Their penetration into an aquifer makes them difficult to locate and remediate.

19a3fa44cc9f.title: Dense non-aqueous phase liquid
19a3fa44cc9f.sentence: - chlorinated solvents, such as trichloroethylene, tetrachloroethylene, 1,1,1-trichloroethane and carbon tetrachloride

d40bb0bd1aba.title: Dense non-aqueous phase liquid
d40bb0bd1aba.sentence: When spilled into the environment, chlorinated solvents are frequently present as DNAPL and the DNAPL can provide a long-term secondary source of the chlorinated solvent to dissolved groundwater plumes.

aab9e8118686.title: Dense non-aqueous phase liquid
aab9e8118686.sentence: Therefore, DNAPL which is a chlorinated solvent can act as an ongoing pathway for constituents to dissolve into groundwater.

8f96ac3c7350.title: Dense non-aqueous phase liquid
8f96ac3c7350.sentence: "DNAPL movement follows the slope of the impermeable strata underlying the aquifer and can move in the opposite direction to the groundwater gradient."

f00bd5b829e1.title: Dense non-aqueous phase liquid
f00bd5b829e1.sentence: Removal or in situ destruction of DNAPLs eliminates the potential exposure to the compounds in the environment and can be an effective method for remediation; however, at some DNAPL sites remediation of DNAPL may not be practicable, and containment may be the only viable remedial action.

c2676e831954.title: In situ chemical reduction
c2676e831954.sentence: In situ chemical reduction (ISCR) is a proposed environmental remediation technique used for soil and/or groundwater remediation to lower the concentrations of targeted environmental contaminants to acceptable levels.

39b3d3ec1dc8.title: In situ chemical reduction
39b3d3ec1dc8.sentence: ISCR is usually applied in the environment by injecting reductive additives into the contaminated area or placing a solid medium of chemical reductants in the path of a contaminant plume.

bb32f951b5c3.title: In situ chemical reduction
bb32f951b5c3.sentence: It is the mirror process of In Situ Chemical Oxidation (ISCO).

74d1035e708f.title: In situ chemical reduction
74d1035e708f.sentence: In mprinciple, ISCR can be used to remediate a variety of organic compounds, including some that are resistant to natural degradation.

b1bdf5e3fe61.title: In situ chemical reduction
b1bdf5e3fe61.sentence: Zero-valent metals are the main reductants used in ISCR.

a29186826d9d.title: In situ chemical reduction
a29186826d9d.sentence: The most common metal used is iron, in the form of ZVI (zero valent iron), and it is also the metal longest in use.

cc99d3b02f88.title: In situ chemical reduction
cc99d3b02f88.sentence: Some applications of ZVMs are to clean up Trichloroethylene (TCE) and Hexavalent chromium (Cr(VI)).

494e208cf29d.title: In situ chemical reduction
494e208cf29d.section: Reactions in ISCR > Surface catalyzed reactions
494e208cf29d.sentence: Pathway A represents direct electron transfer (ET) for Fe0 to the adsorbed halocarbon (RX) at the metal/water point of contact, resulting in dechlorination and production of Fe2+.

1a6f7fe26e35.title: In situ chemical reduction
1a6f7fe26e35.section: Reactions in ISCR > Surface catalyzed reactions
1a6f7fe26e35.sentence: Pathway B shows that Fe2+ (resulting from corrosion of Fe0) may also dechlorinate RX, producing Fe3+.

e306fffcfda4.title: In situ chemical reduction
e306fffcfda4.section: Reactions in ISCR > Surface catalyzed reactions
e306fffcfda4.sentence: Pathway C shows that H2 from the anaerobic corrosion of Fe2+ might react with RX if a catalyst is present.

36be885384c5.title: In situ chemical reduction
36be885384c5.sentence: A common implementation of ISCR is the installation of permeable reactive barriers (PRBs), but there are instances when the reductant can be directly injected into the subsurface to treat source areas.

584952719c26.title: In situ chemical reduction
584952719c26.sentence: Commonly a trench with ZVI, nanoscale iron, or palladium.

49b1df291fa5.title: In situ chemical reduction
49b1df291fa5.sentence: Nanoscale iron particles can also be injected directly into the subsurface to treat plumes, and they have large surface areas and, therefore, high reactivities and can be distributed more evenly in the contamination site.

095008993b9b.title: Hexavalent chromium
095008993b9b.sentence: Hexavalent chromium (chromium(VI), Cr(VI), chromium 6) is any chemical compound that contains the element chromium in the +6 oxidation state (thus hexavalent).

59c1e779f56c.title: Hexavalent chromium
59c1e779f56c.sentence: Hexavalent chromium compounds can be carcinogens (IARC Group 1), especially if airborne and inhaled where they can cause lung cancer.

0eba335b545b.title: Hexavalent chromium
0eba335b545b.sentence: Hexavalent chromium occurs only rarely in nature, an exception being crocoite (PbCrO4).

8f400bd523f2.title: Hexavalent chromium
8f400bd523f2.sentence: It is, however, produced on a large scale industrially.

4cea9df81e8a.title: Hexavalent chromium
4cea9df81e8a.sentence: Virtually all chromium ore is processed via the formation of hexavalent chromium, specifically the salt sodium dichromate.

147c93d0f515.title: Hexavalent chromium
147c93d0f515.sentence: Many hexavalent chromium compounds can be carcinogens (IARC Group 1), especially if airborne and inhaled where they can cause lung cancer.

6ee7ccbeed06.title: Hexavalent chromium
6ee7ccbeed06.sentence: Ingestion of chromium(VI) through drinking water has been found to cause cancer in the oral cavity and small intestine.

95084af20848.title: Hexavalent chromium
95084af20848.sentence: Due to its structural similarity to sulfate, chromate (a typical form of chromium(VI) at neutral pH) is transported into cells via sulfate channels.

aafe851d56f0.title: Hexavalent chromium
aafe851d56f0.sentence: Inside the cell, hexavalent chromium(VI) is reduced first to pentavalent chromium(V) then to trivalent chromium(III) without the aid of any enzymes.

5f2a51beb114.title: Hexavalent chromium
5f2a51beb114.sentence: The resultant chromium(III) forms stable complexes with nucleic acids and proteins.

c9abe97818e6.title: Hexavalent chromium
c9abe97818e6.sentence: This causes strand breaks and Cr–DNA adducts which are responsible for mutagenic damage.

bd4f3dcb75bf.title: Hexavalent chromium
bd4f3dcb75bf.section: Remediation of hexavalent chromium in water
bd4f3dcb75bf.sentence: The more practical methods focus on reduction of Cr(VI) to Cr(III).

d956849bf85e.title: Hexavalent chromium
d956849bf85e.section: Remediation of hexavalent chromium in water
d956849bf85e.sentence: Experiments with activated sludge have also shown its ability to reduce Cr(VI) to Cr(III).

c199bcb10507.title: Phytotoxicity
c199bcb10507.sentence: Phytotoxicity describes any adverse effects on plant growth, physiology, or metabolism caused by a chemical substance, such as high levels of fertilizers, herbicides, heavy metals, or nanoparticles.

027bb2ef454f.title: Phytotoxicity
027bb2ef454f.sentence: General phytotoxic effects include altered plant metabolism, growth inhibition, or plant death.

b432ea8c6288.title: Phytotoxicity
b432ea8c6288.sentence: Changes to plant metabolism and growth are the result of disrupted physiological functioning, including inhibition of photosynthesis, water and nutrient uptake, cell division, or seed germination.

7bcbcf4f51b3.title: Phytotoxicity
7bcbcf4f51b3.sentence: High concentrations of mineral salts in solution within the plant growing medium can result in phytotoxicity, commonly caused by excessive application of fertilizers.

97a4f134323f.title: Phytotoxicity
97a4f134323f.sentence: However, if too much is applied, phytotoxic effects can result from urea toxicity directly or ammonia production from hydrolysis of urea.

f1cb50166d6c.title: Phytotoxicity
f1cb50166d6c.sentence: Organic fertilizers, such as compost, also have the potential to be phytotoxic if not sufficiently humified, as intermediate products of this process are harmful to plant growth.

75532c384737.title: Phytotoxicity
75532c384737.sentence: However, the use of herbicides can cause phytotoxic effects on non-targeted plants through wind-blown spray drift or from the use of herbicide-contaminated material (such as straw or manure) being applied to the soil.

2fb426f87ff8.title: Phytotoxicity
2fb426f87ff8.sentence: Of these, Co, Cu, Fe, Ni, and Zn are trace elements required in small amounts for enzyme and redox reactions essential in plant development.

745daa2b69a7.title: Phytotoxicity
745daa2b69a7.sentence: However, past a certain threshold they become toxic.

3cf32f4d64d6.title: Phytotoxicity
3cf32f4d64d6.sentence: The other heavy metals listed are considered toxic at any concentration and can bioaccumulate, posing a health hazard to humans if consumed.

1ab5a90e9d95.title: GIS in environmental contamination
1ab5a90e9d95.section: GIS in Water Pollution > DRASTIC Summary Index Score modeled using GIS
1ab5a90e9d95.sentence: Under certain hydrological parameters, some aquifers are more prone to contamination than other aquifers.

0896351bf24d.title: GIS in environmental contamination
0896351bf24d.section: GIS in Water Pollution > DRASTIC Summary Index Score modeled using GIS
0896351bf24d.sentence: These seven parameters derive DRASTIC summary index score, which determines which are more prone to contamination than other.

f23190ae0911.title: GIS in environmental contamination
f23190ae0911.section: GIS in Water Pollution > DRASTIC Summary Index Score modeled using GIS
f23190ae0911.sentence: The parameters that are taken into consideration when calculating the vulnerability of aquifers to contamination are depth to water (factor d), net recharge (factor r), aquifer media (factor a), soil media (factor s), topography (factor t), impact of the vadose zone (factor i), and the hydraulic conductivity (factor c), which together spell out DRASTIC.

9ebe776bb410.title: GIS in environmental contamination
9ebe776bb410.section: GIS in Water Pollution > DRASTIC Summary Index Score modeled using GIS
9ebe776bb410.sentence: Furthermore, there is a weighting factor associated with each of the parameters that can range from one to five.

21e63b22e97b.title: GIS in environmental contamination
21e63b22e97b.section: GIS in Water Pollution > DRASTIC Summary Index Score modeled using GIS
21e63b22e97b.sentence: In addition, the lower the numbers for the DRASTIC index after the assessment of the aquifer, the lower the risk of aquifer contamination in that area.

0081384f03aa.title: GIS in environmental contamination
0081384f03aa.section: GIS in Water Pollution > DRASTIC Summary Index Score modeled using GIS
0081384f03aa.sentence: The significance of the DRASTIC summary index score is that it shows areas that are more prone; as a result, the state or local authorities, depending on the scale, will place necessary measures in place that would prevent or mitigate contamination of the water supply.

0de6329d158b.title: Soil guideline value
0de6329d158b.sentence: This guidance stipulates three stages in such risk assessments:

f2b169ee3b8d.title: Soil guideline value
f2b169ee3b8d.sentence: - Preliminary qualitative assessment including development of conceptual site model

62ede3152754.title: Environmental remediation
62ede3152754.sentence: Once a site is suspected of being contaminated there is a need to assess the contamination.

0d62c0befd0b.title: Environmental remediation
0d62c0befd0b.sentence: Often the assessment begins with preparation of a Phase I Environmental Site Assessment.

2b8041792daf.title: Environmental remediation
2b8041792daf.sentence: The historical use of the site and the materials used and produced on site will guide the assessment strategy and type of sampling and chemical analysis to be done.

28010d11a6a9.title: Contaminated land
28010d11a6a9.section: United Kingdom > The process > Risk assessment
28010d11a6a9.sentence: - Preliminary Risk Assessment – Also known as a Phase 1 Preliminary Risk Assessment, or Desk Study, this work involves the collection and review of many different sources of information including: local authority registers, environmental databases, geological maps, and historic records.

05fb5e6e8235.title: Contaminated land
05fb5e6e8235.section: United Kingdom > The process > Risk assessment
05fb5e6e8235.sentence: A site walkover is usually also undertaken to identify any specific sources of contamination and to collect relevant photographs.

aef752532eb9.title: Contaminated land
aef752532eb9.section: United Kingdom > The process > Risk assessment
aef752532eb9.sentence: This information is compiled to produce a Conceptual Site Model (CSM).

91636aba8008.title: Contaminated land
91636aba8008.section: United Kingdom > The process > Risk assessment
91636aba8008.sentence: In order for a contaminant linkage to be active, a source, pathway, and receptor must all be present.

327ed530ed8a.title: Contaminated land
327ed530ed8a.section: United Kingdom > The process > Risk assessment
327ed530ed8a.sentence: It can typically involve completion of boreholes or trial pits and collection of soil or groundwater samples for submission to an appropriately accredited laboratory.

c74a074e06ad.title: Contaminated land
c74a074e06ad.section: United Kingdom > The process > Risk assessment
c74a074e06ad.sentence: - Generic/Detailed Risk Assessment – This process involves assessment of contaminant concentrations in the context of the site's proposed end use.

c7b72579718a.title: Contaminated land
c7b72579718a.section: United Kingdom > The process > Risk assessment
c7b72579718a.sentence: Assessment can be either generic (using predefined assessment criteria) or detailed (taking into account a number of site and receptor-specific factors).

9de44e3a4fb8.title: Environmental remediation
9de44e3a4fb8.sentence: Often nearby sites owned by the same company or which are nearby and have been reclaimed, levelled or filled are also contaminated even where the current land use seems innocuous.

d3792c41cc1e.title: Environmental remediation
d3792c41cc1e.sentence: Off-site contamination of nearby sites often occur through decades of emissions to soil, groundwater, and air.

8683c0215a1f.title: Environmental remediation
8683c0215a1f.sentence: For example, a car park may have been levelled by using contaminated waste in the fill.

c5eaa97aaf56.title: Environmental remediation
c5eaa97aaf56.sentence: Ceiling dust, topsoil, surface and groundwater of nearby properties should also be tested, both before and after any remediation.

8259ec1adc57.title: Soil guideline value
8259ec1adc57.sentence: The SGVs are therefore conservative estimates for a given scenario.

3f5ce0998dbd.title: Soil guideline value
3f5ce0998dbd.sentence: Exceedance of a SGV does not confirm that there is a "significant possibility of significant harm", merely that the possibility exists and therefore more detailed, site-specific investigation of contaminants present, pathways and receptors is required.

f959899bce40.title: Soil contamination
f959899bce40.sentence: Various national standards for concentrations of particular contaminants include the United States EPA Region 9 Preliminary Remediation Goals (U.S. PRGs), the United States EPA Region 3 Risk Based Concentrations (U.S. EPA RBCs), and National Environment Protection Council of Australia Guideline on Investigation Levels for Soil and Groundwater.

56eb0878ec57.title: Environmental remediation
56eb0878ec57.sentence: In the United States, the most comprehensive set of Preliminary Remediation Goals (PRGs) is from the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Regional Screening Levels (RSLs).

f0b4d3ec58da.title: Environmental remediation
f0b4d3ec58da.sentence: In Canada, most standards for remediation are set by the provinces individually, but the Canadian Council of Ministers of the Environment provides guidance at a federal level in the form of the Canadian Environmental Quality Guidelines and the Canada-Wide Standards|Canada-Wide Standard for Petroleum Hydrocarbons in Soil.

44dc66dcb16b.title: Environmental remediation
44dc66dcb16b.sentence: The European Union (EU) is rapidly moving towards Europe-wide standards, although most of the industrialised nations in Europe have their own standards at present.

07fc8173d4eb.title: Environmental remediation
07fc8173d4eb.sentence: This is a controversial step as:

800d4588df68.title: Environmental remediation
800d4588df68.sentence: - No one wants to have to pay for the cleanup of the site;

bacfde4bb057.title: Environmental remediation
bacfde4bb057.sentence: - If nearby properties are found to be contaminated, it may have to be noted on their property title, potentially affecting the value;

74924ff428d5.title: Environmental remediation
74924ff428d5.sentence: - No one wants to pay for the cost of assessment.

fa350b52e97c.title: Soil vapor extraction
fa350b52e97c.sentence: The soil gas (vapor) that is extracted by the SVE system generally requires treatment prior to discharge back into the environment.

a6011d9caeed.title: Soil vapor extraction
a6011d9caeed.sentence: The most commonly applied aboveground treatment technologies are thermal oxidation and granular activated carbon adsorption.

0edc0f4ee659.title: Soil vapor extraction
0edc0f4ee659.sentence: A variety of treatment techniques are available for aboveground treatment and include thermal destruction (e.g., direct flame thermal oxidation, catalytic oxidizers), adsorption (e.g., granular activated carbon, zeolites, polymers), biofiltration, non-thermal plasma destruction, photolytic/photocatalytic destruction, membrane separation, gas absorption, and vapor condensation.

251d52d9ecd0.title: Soil vapor extraction
251d52d9ecd0.sentence: The selection of a particular aboveground treatment technology depends on the contaminant, concentrations in the offgas, throughput, and economic considerations.

3d13ca89f9da.title: Environmental remediation
3d13ca89f9da.sentence: Generally, carbon is used for low (below 500 ppmV) VOC concentration vapor streams, oxidation is used for moderate (up to 4,000 ppmV) VOC concentration streams, and vapor condensation is used for high (over 4,000 ppmV) VOC concentration vapor streams.

84d9dc76f607.title: Environmental remediation
84d9dc76f607.sentence: - Thermal oxidation which uses a system that acts as a furnace and maintains temperatures ranging from 1,350 to 1,500 °F (730 to 820 °C).

b3032e9ceed8.title: Environmental remediation
b3032e9ceed8.sentence: - Catalytic oxidation which uses a catalyst on a support to facilitate a lower temperature oxidation.

222be0136777.title: Environmental remediation
222be0136777.sentence: This system usually maintains temperatures ranging from 600 to 800 °F (316 to 427 °C).

6fcd9afa0e2b.title: Environmental remediation
6fcd9afa0e2b.sentence: The activated carbon must be replaced periodically as it may become saturated and unable to adsorb (i.e. reduced absorption efficiency with loading).

2005b5eead85.title: Environmental remediation
2005b5eead85.sentence: Activated carbon is not effective in removing heavy metals.

415596884559.title: Environmental remediation
415596884559.sentence: This approach is somewhat controversial because of the risks of dioxins released in the atmosphere through the exhaust gases or effluent off-gas.

e05aaeedbafb.title: Air sparging
e05aaeedbafb.sentence: Air sparging, also known as in situ air stripping and in situ volatilization is an in situ remediation technique, used for the treatment of saturated soils and groundwater contaminated by volatile organic compounds (VOCs) like petroleum hydrocarbons, a widespread problem for the ground water and soil health.

db114e429d44.title: Air sparging
db114e429d44.sentence: In saturated zone remediation, air sparging refers to the injection of a hydrocarbon-free gaseous medium into the ground where contamination has been found.

2b77b448735d.title: Air sparging
2b77b448735d.sentence: Air sparging is a subsurface contaminant remediation technique that involves the injection of pressurized air into contaminated ground water causing hydrocarbons to change state from dissolved to vapor state.

ae4f0a602cca.title: Air sparging
ae4f0a602cca.sentence: A blower is attached to wells, usually through a manifold, below the water table creating pressure.

7f4b67bae116.title: Air sparging
7f4b67bae116.sentence: The pressurized air forms small bubbles that travel through the contamination in and above water column.

122222c1740f.title: Air sparging
122222c1740f.sentence: The bubbles of air volatilize contaminants and carry them to the unsaturated soils above.

b6d7476d766f.title: Air sparging
b6d7476d766f.sentence: Vacuum points are installed in the unsaturated soils above the saturated zone.

d435550a9e1e.title: Air sparging
d435550a9e1e.sentence: The vacuum points extract the vapors through to a soil vapor extraction system.

74d7b1e4b493.title: Air sparging

b7c3b2db1d07.title: Hyperaccumulator

b1b1f6641042.title: Hyperaccumulator

0b5d48e90ff9.title: Hyperaccumulator

5cb3a89ceba1.title: Hyperaccumulator

0966ad51b6ca.title: Phytoremediation

6b26a1b6336e.title: Hyperaccumulator

86711071490f.title: Pesticide degradation
86711071490f.sentence: Pesticide degradation is the process by which a pesticide is transformed into a benign substance that is environmentally compatible with the site to which it was applied.

86f735d74b4b.title: Pesticide degradation
86f735d74b4b.sentence: Globally, an estimated 1 to 2.5 million tons of active pesticide ingredients are used each year, mainly in agriculture.

b0478298079c.title: Pesticide degradation
b0478298079c.sentence: Pesticide use, therefore, represents an important source of diffuse chemical environmental inputs.

2af7b0f3cc04.title: Pesticide degradation
2af7b0f3cc04.sentence: Typically, documented soil half-lives are in the range of days to weeks.

bee461bd9068.title: Pesticide degradation
bee461bd9068.sentence: However, pesticide residues are found ubiquitously in the environment in ng/liter to low μg/liter concentrations.

08cca9950cf7.title: Pesticide degradation
08cca9950cf7.sentence: Degradation involves both biotic and abiotic transformation processes.

80a2d9862527.title: Pesticide degradation
80a2d9862527.sentence: Biotic transformation is mediated by microorganisms, while abiotic transformation involves processes such as chemical and photochemical reactions.

4346f674a217.title: Pesticide degradation
4346f674a217.sentence: Biodegradation is generally recognized as the biggest contributor to degradation.

979c0567ffdf.title: Pesticide degradation
979c0567ffdf.sentence: Redox gradients in soils, sediments or aquifers often determine which transformations can occur.

ad01cede66e3.title: Pesticide degradation
ad01cede66e3.sentence: Similarly, photochemical transformations require sunlight, available only in the topmost meter(s) of lakes or rivers, plant surfaces or submillimeter soil layers.

1d40d4a06907.title: Pesticide degradation

774e403b25a1.title: Pesticide degradation
774e403b25a1.sentence: Microbes that cleave the C-P bond are widespread in the environment, and some can metabolize glyphosate.

9d77da6cfb95.title: Pesticide degradation

8625adf18bef.title: Pesticide degradation

542fcb3df942.title: Pesticide degradation

315a5c2e9b41.title: In situ bioremediation

058a6e9412e8.title: In situ bioremediation

0d3e21c87657.title: In situ bioremediation

8e3a131dafa7.title: In situ bioremediation

d2258e830088.title: In situ bioremediation

b765e501cd90.title: In situ bioremediation

b6aee04583f7.sentence: The attractiveness of a constructed wetlands solution lies in its relative low cost.

c07e745d2bea.title: Acid mine drainage
c07e745d2bea.sentence: They are limited by the metal loads they can deal with (either from high flows or metal concentrations), though current practitioners have succeeded in developing constructed wetlands that treat high volumes (see description of Campbell Mine constructed wetland) and/or highly acidic water (with adequate pre-treatment).

52ed1343bd07.title: Acid mine drainage
52ed1343bd07.section: Treatment > Methods > Precipitation of metal sulfides
52ed1343bd07.sentence: In this process, sulfate-reducing bacteria (SRB) oxidize organic matter using sulfate as terminal electron acceptor, instead of oxygen.

444360b5af4d.title: Acid mine drainage
444360b5af4d.section: Treatment > Methods > Precipitation of metal sulfides
444360b5af4d.sentence: Their metabolic products include bicarbonate produced by organic matter oxidation, which can neutralize water acidity, and hydrogen sulfide, which forms highly insoluble precipitates with many toxic metals.

c46d46c90ec7.title: Acid mine drainage
c46d46c90ec7.sentence: When the pH of acid mine drainage is raised past 3, either through contact with fresh water or neutralizing minerals, previously soluble iron(III) ions precipitate as iron(III) hydroxide, a yellow-orange solid colloquially known as yellow boy.

cf5f710ad8b0.title: Acid mine drainage
cf5f710ad8b0.sentence: Other types of iron precipitates are possible, including iron oxides and oxyhydroxides, and sulfates such as jarosite.

de1851a0e0fe.title: Acid mine drainage
de1851a0e0fe.sentence: All these precipitates can discolor water and smother plant and animal life on the streambed, disrupting stream ecosystems (a specific offense under the Fisheries Act in Canada).

5dc5b69eb1b3.title: Acid mine drainage
5dc5b69eb1b3.sentence: The process also produces additional hydrogen ions, which can further decrease pH.

7d684b138927.title: Acid mine drainage
7d684b138927.sentence: In some cases, the concentrations of iron hydroxides in yellow boy are so high the precipitate can be recovered for commercial use in pigments.

048a437b2120.title: Thermal desorption
048a437b2120.sentence: Thermal desorption is an environmental remediation technology that utilizes heat to increase the volatility of contaminants such that they can be removed (separated) from the solid matrix (typically soil, sludge or filter cake sediment).

5b6134f9d22c.title: Thermal desorption
5b6134f9d22c.sentence: The volatilized contaminants are then either collected or thermally destroyed.

c52a1562bef9.title: Thermal desorption
c52a1562bef9.sentence: A thermal desorption system therefore has two major components; the desorber itself and the offgas treatment system.

a52ee1a2ff67.title: Thermal desorption
a52ee1a2ff67.sentence: A status report from the United States Environmental Protection Agency shows that thermal desorption has been used at 69 Superfund sites through FY2000.

46520adb5f74.title: Thermal desorption
46520adb5f74.sentence: Stabilization does not provide a permanent remedy, since the contaminants are still on site.

fcf1c5a66190.title: Thermal desorption
fcf1c5a66190.sentence: Thermal desorption is a widely accepted technology that provides a permanent solution at an economically competitive cost.

e33573bb644e.title: Thermal desorption
e33573bb644e.sentence: - Heated screw (hot oil, molten salt, electric)

7ffc9c52427b.title: Thermal desorption
7ffc9c52427b.sentence: With a carbon steel shell, the maximum solids temperature is around 1,000 °F, while temperatures of 1,800 °F with special alloy cylinders are attainable.

f37ea8c7a1e7.title: Thermal desorption
f37ea8c7a1e7.sentence: A thermal desorber removing 500 mg/kg of organic contaminants from 20,000 tons of soil will produce less than 3,000 US gallons (11,000 L) of liquid organic.

0c47444e5781.title: Thermal desorption
0c47444e5781.sentence: In essence 20,000 tons of contaminated soil could be reduced to less than one tank truck of extracted liquid residue for off-site disposal.

539097a4599c.title: Thermal desorption
539097a4599c.sentence: Thermal desorption first appeared as an environmental treatment technology in 1985 when it was specified in the Record of Decision for the McKin Company Superfund site within the Royal River watershed in Maine.

af412c5103c5.title: Light non-aqueous phase liquid
af412c5103c5.sentence: A light non-aqueous phase liquid (LNAPL) is a groundwater contaminant, specifically they are "hydrocarbons that exist as a separate, immiscible phase when in contact with water and/or air." It is not soluble in water and has a lower density than water, in contrast to a DNAPL which has a higher density than water.

a00c6e99356e.title: Light non-aqueous phase liquid
a00c6e99356e.sentence: Once a LNAPL pollution infiltrates the ground, it will stop at the depth of the water table because of its positive buoyancy.

393d290f5daf.title: Light non-aqueous phase liquid
393d290f5daf.sentence: Examples of LNAPLs are benzene, toluene, xylene, and other hydrocarbons.

df7861e8975d.title: Light non-aqueous phase liquid
df7861e8975d.sentence: Efforts to locate and remove LNAPLs are relatively less expensive and easier than for DNAPLs because LNAPLs float on top of the water table.

c1797feaf3cc.title: Biosorption
c1797feaf3cc.sentence: Biosorption is a physicochemical process that occurs naturally in certain biomass which allows it to passively concentrate and bind contaminants onto its cellular structure.

d0422ee70744.title: Biosorption
d0422ee70744.sentence: Biosorption can be defined as the ability of biological materials to accumulate heavy metals from wastewater through metabolically mediated or physico-chemical pathways of uptake.

ec89e870f418.title: Biosorption
ec89e870f418.sentence: Biosorption is a metabolically passive process, meaning it does not require energy, and the amount of contaminants a sorbent can remove is dependent on kinetic equilibrium and the composition of the sorbents cellular surface.

a58f5188d60c.title: Biosorption
a58f5188d60c.sentence: Bioaccumulation is an active metabolic process driven by energy from a living organism and requires respiration.

fcc93f9e06bf.title: Biosorption
fcc93f9e06bf.sentence: Since metals are bound onto the cellular surface, biosorption is a reversible process whereas bioaccumulation is only partially reversible.

2faab78bf22f.title: Biosorption
2faab78bf22f.sentence: Both bioaccumulation and biosorption occur naturally in all living organisms however, in a controlled experiment conducted on living and dead strains of bacillus sphaericus it was found that the biosorption of chromium ions was 13–20% higher in dead cells than living cells.

d1d09e72299e.title: Biosorption
d1d09e72299e.sentence: Since biosorption is determined by equilibrium, it is largely influenced by pH, the concentration of biomass and the interaction between different metallic ions.

0b808d508177.title: Biosorption
0b808d508177.sentence: However, an extensive body of research has found that a wide variety of commonly discarded waste including eggshells, bones, peat, fungi, seaweed, crab shells, yeast, baggase and carrot peels can efficiently remove toxic heavy metal ions from contaminated water.

9d470f24fc86.title: Biosorption
9d470f24fc86.sentence: It is an alternative to using man-made ion-exchange resins, which cost ten times more than biosorbents.

2faed3d9dff5.title: Metal toxicity
2faed3d9dff5.sentence: Soils contaminated by heavy metals can be remediated by one or more of the following technologies: isolation; immobilization; toxicity reduction; physical separation; or extraction.

3bd484c6efc3.title: Metal toxicity
3bd484c6efc3.sentence: Isolation involves the use of caps, membranes or below-ground barriers in an attempt to quarantine the contaminated soil.

a204dc02d362.title: Metal toxicity
a204dc02d362.sentence: Immobilization aims to alter the properties of the soil so as to hinder the mobility of the heavy contaminants.

ccc444c0319a.title: Metal toxicity
ccc444c0319a.sentence: Toxicity reduction attempts to oxidise or reduce the toxic heavy metal ions, via chemical or biological means into less toxic or mobile forms.

8a1262672400.title: Metal toxicity
8a1262672400.sentence: Extraction is an on or off-site process that uses chemicals, high-temperature volatization, or electrolysis to extract contaminants from soils.

85ab8cc1ea9c.title: Metal toxicity
85ab8cc1ea9c.sentence: The process or processes used will vary according to contaminant and the characteristics of the site.

8c46bb5c5936.title: Agricultural pollution
8c46bb5c5936.sentence: Pesticide leaching occurs when aqueous solutions of pesticides migrate to off-target sites.

2e2826a247db.title: Agricultural pollution
2e2826a247db.sentence: Leaching is a major source of groundwater pollution.

49cccf10e38d.title: Agricultural pollution
49cccf10e38d.sentence: Leaching is affected by the soil, the pesticide, and rainfall and irrigation.

55438ccbc746.title: Agricultural pollution
55438ccbc746.sentence: Leaching is more problematic with water-soluble pesticides and when the soil tends to be sandy in texture; if excessive watering occurs just after pesticide application; if the adsorption ability of the pesticide to the soil is low.

f22c791d1635.title: Agricultural pollution
f22c791d1635.sentence: In addition to treated fields, Leaching may also originate from pesticide mixing areas, pesticide application machinery washing sites, or disposal areas.

49e17de4045c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.03%3A_Soil_Reclamation_and_Remediation_of_Disturbed_Lands
49e17de4045c.sentence: Soil reclamation is part of the overall land reclamation process and is usually addressed after removal of infrastructure, recontouring, and contaminant remediation, and before revegetation (Figure 16.1).

95a205400bb9.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.03%3A_Soil_Reclamation_and_Remediation_of_Disturbed_Lands
95a205400bb9.sentence: Land reclamation is the process of converting disturbed or damaged land to its former or other productive uses.

5df3cc15f8f3.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.03%3A_Soil_Reclamation_and_Remediation_of_Disturbed_Lands
5df3cc15f8f3.sentence: Reclamation encompasses all disturbed components of an ecosystem, including but not limited to, soils, hydrology, flora, and fauna.

12f75dbe1fea.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.03%3A_Soil_Reclamation_and_Remediation_of_Disturbed_Lands
12f75dbe1fea.sentence: Soil reclamation and soil remediation are components of the land reclamation process that take place on the landscape after disturbance of ecosystems and sites.

73a7c1af9ecb.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.03%3A_Soil_Reclamation_and_Remediation_of_Disturbed_Lands
73a7c1af9ecb.sentence: An important concept in soil reclamation is end land use.

08987e164001.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.03%3A_Soil_Reclamation_and_Remediation_of_Disturbed_Lands
08987e164001.sentence: For example, regulatory requirements are more stringent for agricultural land and land that people will occupy than land used for industrial purposes.

fcfda9f43533.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.03%3A_Soil_Reclamation_and_Remediation_of_Disturbed_Lands
fcfda9f43533.sentence: These potential end land uses can be similar to what was there prior to the disturbance or can require a complete change of ecosystem.

7c96a4b9319a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.03%3A_Soil_Reclamation_and_Remediation_of_Disturbed_Lands
7c96a4b9319a.section: SOIL RECLAMATION > Soil Replacement and Amendments
7c96a4b9319a.sentence: When soil has been stripped in horizons and stockpiled during disturbance it is normally replaced in its natural horizon sequence.

319a4fb12628.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.03%3A_Soil_Reclamation_and_Remediation_of_Disturbed_Lands
319a4fb12628.section: SOIL RECLAMATION > Soil Replacement and Amendments
319a4fb12628.sentence: Although admixing of horizons can be an issue, careful placement techniques can mitigate it.

d4261bc6d8e8.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.03%3A_Soil_Reclamation_and_Remediation_of_Disturbed_Lands
d4261bc6d8e8.section: SOIL RECLAMATION > Soil Replacement and Amendments
d4261bc6d8e8.sentence: The most likely issue is compaction when the soil is replaced and this can be mitigated through tillage operations.

1aef3de39f7e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.03%3A_Soil_Reclamation_and_Remediation_of_Disturbed_Lands
1aef3de39f7e.section: SOIL RECLAMATION > Soil Replacement and Amendments
1aef3de39f7e.sentence: Much damage to soils can be reduced by having construction activities occur under frozen, or dry conditions.

abd251d956cc.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.03%3A_Soil_Reclamation_and_Remediation_of_Disturbed_Lands
abd251d956cc.section: SOIL RECLAMATION > Soil Replacement and Amendments
abd251d956cc.sentence: Soil quality can be retained if soils are stockpiled only for short periods of time.

d2b7b638836e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.03%3A_Soil_Reclamation_and_Remediation_of_Disturbed_Lands
d2b7b638836e.sentence: Erosion is a problem at most disturbed sites prior to and during reclamation as the soil is bare and devoid of vegetation, exposing the surface to wind and water erosion.

d17388af0a96.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.03%3A_Soil_Reclamation_and_Remediation_of_Disturbed_Lands
d17388af0a96.sentence: Erosion can be reduced on reclamation sites with contouring, amendments, and various materials such as erosion control blankets, and mulch.

9c93b83fcc0d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.03%3A_Soil_Reclamation_and_Remediation_of_Disturbed_Lands
9c93b83fcc0d.sentence: Many techniques, called bioengineering, include use of plant materials with techniques such as live staking (i.e., planting individual live wood cuttings into the soil).

1f16150b4bea.title: Soil
1f16150b4bea.sentence: Soils which contain high levels of particular clays with high swelling properties, such as smectites, are often very fertile.

3c62494f2064.title: Soil
3c62494f2064.sentence: For example, productivity has declined and soil erosion has increased in the low-clay soils of northern Thailand, following the abandonment of shifting cultivation for a more permanent land use.

cadcc666c915.title: Soil
cadcc666c915.sentence: Scientists experimented with adding bentonite, one of the smectite family of clays, to the soil.

6b4d2f5a7fab.title: Soil
6b4d2f5a7fab.sentence: Supplementing the farmer's usual practice with a single application of 200 kilograms per rai (1,300 kg/ha; 1,100 lb/acre) of bentonite resulted in an average yield increase of 73%.

27b9f4b42a0a.title: Soil
27b9f4b42a0a.sentence: If the soil is too high in clay or salts (e.g. saline sodic soil), adding gypsum, washed river sand and organic matter (e.g.municipal solid waste) will balance the composition.

9b16fea82868.title: Soil
9b16fea82868.sentence: Adding organic matter, like ramial chipped wood or compost, to soil which is depleted in nutrients and too high in sand will boost its quality and improve production.

0004728af251.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.03%3A_Soil_Reclamation_and_Remediation_of_Disturbed_Lands
0004728af251.section: SOIL RECLAMATION > Soil Replacement and Amendments
0004728af251.sentence: If soil chemical properties do not meet end land use requirements, amendments can be used to bring soils to an appropriate criteria.

1f10835d6786.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.03%3A_Soil_Reclamation_and_Remediation_of_Disturbed_Lands
1f10835d6786.sentence: Amendments can be added in smaller amounts to improve physical, chemical, and/or biological properties such as nutrient content, infiltration capacity, or pH.

ed1bdf1b350d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.03%3A_Soil_Reclamation_and_Remediation_of_Disturbed_Lands
ed1bdf1b350d.section: SOIL RECLAMATION > Soil Replacement and Amendments
ed1bdf1b350d.sentence: A common issue in soil reclamation is lack of organic matter and impacts on its associated properties.

fb706a636e69.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.03%3A_Soil_Reclamation_and_Remediation_of_Disturbed_Lands
fb706a636e69.section: SOIL RECLAMATION > Soil Replacement and Amendments
fb706a636e69.sentence: This can be addressed by adding an organic amendment such as animal manure or straw from a local agricultural operation, or forest floor material (LFH) from an area that has been deforested.

b154950e2d6b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.03%3A_Soil_Reclamation_and_Remediation_of_Disturbed_Lands
b154950e2d6b.section: SOIL RECLAMATION > Soil Replacement and Amendments
b154950e2d6b.sentence: Another common issue is lack of soil nutrients necessary for revegetation.

e53a3b69f2fe.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.03%3A_Soil_Reclamation_and_Remediation_of_Disturbed_Lands
e53a3b69f2fe.section: SOIL RECLAMATION > Soil Replacement and Amendments
e53a3b69f2fe.sentence: These deficiencies can best be addressed by adding commercial fertilizers composed of the necessary nutrients such as nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium.

a857962c10f9.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.03%3A_Soil_Reclamation_and_Remediation_of_Disturbed_Lands
a857962c10f9.section: SOIL RECLAMATION > Soil Replacement and Amendments
a857962c10f9.sentence: Fertilizers can be formulated in bulk to meet specific needs of a reclamation site.

af5e1c763aaa.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.03%3A_Soil_Reclamation_and_Remediation_of_Disturbed_Lands
af5e1c763aaa.section: SOIL RECLAMATION > Soil Replacement and Amendments
af5e1c763aaa.sentence: A common and environmentally important process is to use waste materials in soil reclamation.

d368f01cb055.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.03%3A_Soil_Reclamation_and_Remediation_of_Disturbed_Lands
d368f01cb055.section: SOIL RECLAMATION > Soil Replacement and Amendments
d368f01cb055.sentence: This has the added benefit of removing many materials from the landfills where they would otherwise be placed.

db16ae23f022.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.03%3A_Soil_Reclamation_and_Remediation_of_Disturbed_Lands
db16ae23f022.section: SOIL RECLAMATION > Soil Replacement and Amendments
db16ae23f022.sentence: Sewage is available from waste treatment facilities from most mine camps and is a good source of nutrients and organic matter (Figure 16.2).

ab1df1e4736b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.03%3A_Soil_Reclamation_and_Remediation_of_Disturbed_Lands
ab1df1e4736b.section: SOIL RECLAMATION > Soil Replacement and Amendments
ab1df1e4736b.sentence: However, there are concerns with raw sewage use due to possible presence of salts, metals, and disease causing microorganisms.

7f4ba3abbf88.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.03%3A_Soil_Reclamation_and_Remediation_of_Disturbed_Lands
7f4ba3abbf88.section: SOIL RECLAMATION > Soil Replacement and Amendments
7f4ba3abbf88.sentence: Biosolids are widely used as soil amendments.

35d6c00b763a.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.03%3A_Soil_Reclamation_and_Remediation_of_Disturbed_Lands
35d6c00b763a.section: SOIL RECLAMATION > Soil Replacement and Amendments
35d6c00b763a.sentence: They are sewage sludges which have been treated to lower pathogen risk.

2cc346aef1d8.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.03%3A_Soil_Reclamation_and_Remediation_of_Disturbed_Lands
2cc346aef1d8.section: SOIL RECLAMATION > Soil Replacement and Amendments
2cc346aef1d8.sentence: Other amendments can be used in reclamation, including calcium sources, paper mill waste, industrial sludges, biochar, wood ash, and commercial products.

eaa23bbc74cc.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.03%3A_Soil_Reclamation_and_Remediation_of_Disturbed_Lands

eaa23bbc74cc.sentence: Each have specific properties than can be aligned with the soil properties that need improvement, and each often come with associated negative properties that require balancing.

19f3758380b5.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.03%3A_Soil_Reclamation_and_Remediation_of_Disturbed_Lands
19f3758380b5.section: SOIL RECLAMATION > Soil Replacement and Amendments
19f3758380b5.sentence: Many jurisdictions have regulations or guidelines for use of wastes and industrial by-products as soil amendments.

cd65b1bba4e7.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.03%3A_Soil_Reclamation_and_Remediation_of_Disturbed_Lands

cd65b1bba4e7.sentence: Thus, micro topographic variability is needed on the constructed, reclaimed landscape to provide micro sites for plants and microorganisms, to reduce erosion, and to be aesthetically pleasing.

2a5e66a58539.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.03%3A_Soil_Reclamation_and_Remediation_of_Disturbed_Lands
