2a5e66a58539.sentence: This can be provided through features such as mounds, furrows, depressions, rocks, boulders, coarse textured substrates, mulches, and cracks.

1bf52cdbddf0.title: Cadmium poisoning
1bf52cdbddf0.sentence: Cadmium is a naturally occurring toxic metal with common exposure in industrial workplaces, plant soils, and from smoking.

47e043bfc2a1.title: Cadmium poisoning
47e043bfc2a1.sentence: Some sources of phosphate in fertilizers contain cadmium in amounts of up to 100 mg/kg, which can lead to an increase in the concentration of cadmium in soil (for example in New Zealand).

036a9945c0c9.title: Cadmium poisoning
036a9945c0c9.section: Signs and symptoms > Chronic > Bone and joints
036a9945c0c9.sentence: One of the main effects of cadmium poisoning is weak and brittle bones.

f41d464a6663.title: Cadmium poisoning
f41d464a6663.section: Signs and symptoms > Chronic > Bone and joints
f41d464a6663.sentence: The bones become soft (osteomalacia), lose bone mineral density (osteoporosis), and become weaker.

7f139cfdbeb1.title: Cadmium poisoning
7f139cfdbeb1.sentence: The kidney damage inflicted by cadmium poisoning is irreversible.

9bc9d9cd5c11.title: Cadmium poisoning
9bc9d9cd5c11.sentence: The kidneys can shrink up to 30 percent.

4bc7b74536e8.title: Cadmium poisoning
4bc7b74536e8.sentence: Intake is reported to be approximately 8 to 30μg in Europe and the United States versus 59 to 113 μg in various areas of Japan.

175d82f1298e.title: Cadmium poisoning
175d82f1298e.sentence: Environmental exposure to cadmium has been particularly problematic in Japan where many people have consumed rice that was grown in cadmium-contaminated irrigation water.

a8382c8431c3.title: Biological half-life
a8382c8431c3.sentence: - Cadmium in bone has a biological half-life of about 30 years.

d411d54882e9.title: Groundwater remediation
d411d54882e9.sentence: Bioslurping combines elements of bioventing and vacuum-enhanced pumping of free-product that is lighter than water (light non-aqueous phase liquid or LNAPL) to recover free-product from the groundwater and soil, and to bioremediate soils.

d06ab9ef8a75.title: Groundwater remediation
d06ab9ef8a75.sentence: The bioslurper system uses a “slurp” tube that extends into the free-product layer.

dded2109d6d5.title: Groundwater remediation
dded2109d6d5.sentence: Much like a straw in a glass draws liquid, the pump draws liquid (including free-product) and soil gas up the tube in the same process stream.

a80dde75ff69.title: Groundwater remediation
a80dde75ff69.sentence: Pumping lifts LNAPLs, such as oil, off the top of the water table and from the capillary fringe (i.e., an area just above the saturated zone, where water is held in place by capillary forces).

2db8efc30409.title: Groundwater remediation
2db8efc30409.sentence: The biological processes in the term “bioslurping” refer to aerobic biological degradation of the hydrocarbons when air is introduced into the unsaturated zone contaminated soil.

7360a39a1bfe.title: Groundwater remediation
7360a39a1bfe.section: Techniques > Physical treatment technologies > Dual phase vacuum extraction
7360a39a1bfe.sentence: Dual-phase vacuum extraction (DPVE), also known as multi-phase extraction, is a technology that uses a high-vacuum system to remove both contaminated groundwater and soil vapor.

857c20775740.title: Groundwater remediation
857c20775740.section: Techniques > Physical treatment technologies > Dual phase vacuum extraction
857c20775740.sentence: As the water table around the well is lowered from pumping, unsaturated soil is exposed.

178bb4774469.title: Groundwater remediation
178bb4774469.section: Techniques > Physical treatment technologies > Dual phase vacuum extraction
178bb4774469.sentence: This area, called the capillary fringe, is often highly contaminated, as it holds undissolved chemicals, chemicals that are lighter than water, and vapors that have escaped from the dissolved groundwater below.

25003d18275d.title: Groundwater remediation
25003d18275d.section: Techniques > Physical treatment technologies > Dual phase vacuum extraction
25003d18275d.sentence: Contaminants in the newly exposed zone can be removed by vapor extraction.

24ff4e959fed.title: Groundwater remediation
24ff4e959fed.section: Techniques > Physical treatment technologies > Dual phase vacuum extraction
24ff4e959fed.sentence: Use of dual-phase vacuum extraction with these technologies can shorten the cleanup time at a site, because the capillary fringe is often the most contaminated area.

c46c39b94a1e.title: Rhizofiltration
c46c39b94a1e.sentence: Rhizofiltration is a form of phytoremediation that involves filtering contaminated groundwater, surface water and wastewater through a mass of roots to remove toxic substances or excess nutrients.

fd868cf11d25.title: Phytoremediation
fd868cf11d25.sentence: Rhizofiltration is a process that filters water through a mass of roots to remove toxic substances or excess nutrients.

95687fde95c1.title: Rhizofiltration
95687fde95c1.sentence: This process is very similar to phytoextraction in that it removes contaminants by trapping them into harvestable plant biomass.

d6597cae6e71.title: Rhizofiltration
d6597cae6e71.sentence: Both processes are also aimed more toward concentrating and precipitating heavy metals than organic contaminants.

06ebf6b4a4d6.title: Rhizofiltration
06ebf6b4a4d6.sentence: The major difference between rhizofiltration and phytoextraction is that rhizofiltration is used for treatment in aquatic environments, while phytoextraction deals with soil remediation.

42cf7b982e04.title: Phytoremediation
42cf7b982e04.sentence: In either case though, typically plants are first grown in a greenhouse under precise conditions.

4e5958a8eb91.title: Phytoremediation
4e5958a8eb91.sentence: This process is often used to clean up contaminated groundwater through planting directly in the contaminated site or through removing the contaminated water and providing it to these plants in an off-site location.

d2dc6c098062.title: Rhizofiltration
d2dc6c098062.sentence: One study found that roots of sunflower reduced levels of Uranium by nearly 95% in just 24 hours.

24876f1c61c5.title: Rhizofiltration
24876f1c61c5.sentence: The removal of radionuclides from water using sunflowers was estimated to cost between $2 and $6 per thousand gallons of water treated, including waste disposal and capital costs.

0e6c632900a0.title: Rhizofiltration
0e6c632900a0.sentence: Any contaminant that is below the rooting depth will not be extracted.

a9eb07d70cb5.title: Rhizofiltration
a9eb07d70cb5.sentence: Most importantly, it can take years to reach regulatory levels.

59b3735d1fa4.title: Rhizofiltration
59b3735d1fa4.sentence: Plants grown on polluted water and soils become a potential threat to human and animal health, and therefore, careful attention must be paid to the harvesting process and only non-fodder crop should be chosen for the rhizofiltration remediation method.

5f3a4e6fc872.title: Pneumatic fracturing
5f3a4e6fc872.sentence: The method consists of injecting gas into a contaminated subsurface at a pressure higher than that of the gases that are present.

5b0b413a19d6.title: Pneumatic fracturing
5b0b413a19d6.sentence: By doing this fractures "spider-web" throughout the subsurface so that pumps may be placed in the ground to suck out the contaminated water through these cracks.

387996b46710.title: Pneumatic fracturing
387996b46710.sentence: Substrates may also be injected into the soil through the cracks to further the remediation of the soil and ground water.

1a86a7442c45.title: Pneumatic fracturing
1a86a7442c45.sentence: The clean-up technique was developed and patented through the research of various professors at the New Jersey Institute of Technology in 1996 with hopes of cleaning up various United States Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Superfund sites which are some of the most heavily contaminated sites in the country.

08358b409b35.title: Total petroleum hydrocarbon
08358b409b35.sentence: Total petroleum hydrocarbons (TPH) is a term used for any mixture of hydrocarbons that are found in crude oil.

3710ac829934.title: Total petroleum hydrocarbon
3710ac829934.sentence: However, it is useful to measure the total amount of TPH at a site.

af0770ff7b8b.title: Total petroleum hydrocarbon
af0770ff7b8b.sentence: There are several hundred of these compounds, but not all occur in any one sample; because there are so many different chemicals in crude oil and in other petroleum products, it is not practical to measure each one separately when testing for contamination.

3d3c6a624168.title: Total petroleum hydrocarbon
3d3c6a624168.sentence: TPH is the sum of volatile petroleum hydrocarbons (VPH) and extractable petroleum hydrocarbons (EPH).

20ef084111f4.title: Total petroleum hydrocarbon
20ef084111f4.sentence: VPH is also known as petrol (or gasoline) range organics (PRO or GRO) and includes hydrocarbons from C6-C10.

06deab694b7a.title: Total petroleum hydrocarbon
06deab694b7a.sentence: Diesel range organics (DRO) includes hydrocarbons from C10-C28.

dd0237b4e98e.title: Total petroleum hydrocarbon
dd0237b4e98e.sentence: Chemicals that occur in TPH include hexane, benzene, toluene, xylenes, naphthalene, fluorene, and constituents of commonly used fuels among others.

bde0125f4ac8.title: Electrical resistance heating
bde0125f4ac8.sentence: Electrical resistance heating (ERH) is an intensive in situ environmental remediation method that uses the flow of alternating current electricity to heat soil and groundwater and evaporate contaminants.

032c45d9a6a3.title: Electrical resistance heating
032c45d9a6a3.sentence: Electric current is passed through a targeted soil volume between subsurface electrode elements.

516e55a8712a.title: Electrical resistance heating
516e55a8712a.sentence: The resistance to electrical flow that exists in the soil causes the formation of heat; resulting in an increase in temperature until the boiling point of water at depth is reached.

fbd5bc543037.title: Electrical resistance heating
fbd5bc543037.sentence: After reaching this temperature, further energy input causes a phase change, forming steam and removing volatile contaminants.

295dab8252a5.title: Electrical resistance heating
295dab8252a5.sentence: Volatilized contaminants are captured by a subsurface vapor recovery system and conveyed to the surface along with recovered air and steam.

47941865fc3b.title: Electrical resistance heating
47941865fc3b.sentence: ERH is typically most effective on volatile organic compounds (VOCs).

d4ee9543b34b.title: Electrical resistance heating
d4ee9543b34b.sentence: The chlorinated compounds perchloroethylene, trichloroethylene, and cis- or trans- 1,2-dichloroethylene are contaminants that are easily remediated with ERH.

a3c280308fe5.title: Electrical resistance heating
a3c280308fe5.sentence: Less volatile contaminants like xylene or diesel can also be remediated with ERH but energy requirements increase as the volatility decreases.

4d25d66abbd2.title: Electrical resistance heating
4d25d66abbd2.sentence: At an ERH site, the primary electrical current path is on the thin layer of water immediately adjacent to the soil or rock grains.

0f1b7784f498.title: Electrical resistance heating
0f1b7784f498.sentence: Because electricity can and does travel through any lithology that contains some water, ERH can be effective in any soil type.

f299604c112f.title: Electrical resistance heating
f299604c112f.sentence: ERH is not capable of desiccating the subsurface.

c88096f86ad1.title: Electrical resistance heating
c88096f86ad1.sentence: A typical remediation may consist of electrodes spaced 15 to 20 feet apart with operating times usually less than a year.

9b299589a8e3.title: Electrical resistance heating
9b299589a8e3.sentence: - Peat or high organic carbon in the subsurface will preferentially adsorb VOCs due to van der Waals forces.

bb84b0e434d7.title: Electrical resistance heating
bb84b0e434d7.sentence: This preferential adsorption will increase the amount of energy required to remove the VOCs from the subsurface.

673cb4202ece.title: Microbial biodegradation
673cb4202ece.sentence: Microbial biodegradation is the use of bioremediation and biotransformation methods to harness the naturally occurring ability of microbial xenobiotic metabolism to degrade, transform or accumulate environmental pollutants, including hydrocarbons (e.g. oil), polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs), polyaromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), heterocyclic compounds (such as pyridine or quinoline), pharmaceutical substances, radionuclides and metals.

9456d2697409.title: Microbial biodegradation
9456d2697409.sentence: In particular, hydrocarbons and halogenated compounds have long been doubted to be degradable in the absence of oxygen, but the isolation of hitherto unknown anaerobic hydrocarbon-degrading and reductively dehalogenating bacteria during the last decades provided ultimate proof for these processes in nature.

f018017d1ba3.title: Microbial biodegradation
f018017d1ba3.section: Bioavailability, chemotaxis, and transport of pollutants
f018017d1ba3.sentence: Bioavailability, or the amount of a substance that is physiochemically accessible to microorganisms is a key factor in the efficient biodegradation of pollutants.

c52db0d22c50.title: Microbial biodegradation
c52db0d22c50.section: Bioavailability, chemotaxis, and transport of pollutants
c52db0d22c50.sentence: O'Loughlin et al. (2000) showed that, with the exception of kaolinite clay, most soil clays and cation exchange resins attenuated biodegradation of 2-picoline by Arthrobacter sp. strain R1, as a result of adsorption of the substrate to the clays.

d52794569331.title: Microbial biodegradation
d52794569331.sentence: Despite its toxicity, a considerable fraction of petroleum oil entering marine systems is eliminated by the hydrocarbon-degrading activities of microbial communities, in particular by a recently discovered group of specialists, the hydrocarbonoclastic bacteria (HCB).

4aa16b10030a.title: Ecotoxicology
4aa16b10030a.sentence: - Acute and chronic toxicity tests are performed terrestrial and aquatic organisms including fish, invertebrates, avians, mammalians, non-target arthropods, earthworms and rodents.

debf5d0f1e80.title: Ecotoxicology
debf5d0f1e80.sentence: Ecotoxicological studies are generally performed in compliance with international guidelines, including EPA, OECD, EPPO, OPPTTS, SETAC, IOBC, and JMAFF.

e35cf6ab5907.title: Ecotoxicology
e35cf6ab5907.sentence: - LC50 is the acute toxicity, the lethal concentration at which 50% of the test organism dies within the test-specified time.

e77b385d4561.title: Ecotoxicology
e77b385d4561.sentence: The test may start with eggs, embryos, or juveniles and last up to 96 hours.

c3cffacfbeea.title: Ecotoxicology
c3cffacfbeea.sentence: - EC50 is the concentration that causes adverse effects in 50% of the test organisms (for a binary yes/no effect such as mortality or a specified sublethal effect) or causes a 50% (usually) reduction in a non-binary parameter such as growth.

4bd922943f4f.title: Ecotoxicology
4bd922943f4f.sentence: - No observed effect concentration (NOEC) is the highest dose of stressor at which there is no statistically significant difference of effect (p<0.05) seen in the test organism.

cd2cb6f18bd2.title: Pesticide degradation
cd2cb6f18bd2.sentence: Even though their undesirable effects are typically lowered, transformation products may remain problematic.

f1cb0a43e696.title: Pesticide degradation
f1cb0a43e696.sentence: Second, some products are more potent than their parents.

20f7e9ab6a77.title: Pesticide degradation
20f7e9ab6a77.sentence: Such products should receive particular attention because they are often smaller and more polar than their parents.

939c7bdffcc5.title: Pesticide degradation
939c7bdffcc5.sentence: This increases their potential to reach drinking water resources such as groundwater and surface waters, where polar products are found at fairly constant concentrations.

0b3ccc90f49c.title: Pesticide degradation
0b3ccc90f49c.sentence: In Europe, for instance, "nonrelevant" metabolites are distinguished from metabolites that are "relevant for groundwater resources" or even "ecotoxicologically relevant".

2ee5303a82e1.title: Pesticide degradation
2ee5303a82e1.sentence: Groundwater-relevant metabolites are those likely to reach groundwater in concentrations above 0.1 μg/liter and to display the same toxicity as the parent compound.

53f67caec42b.title: Pesticide degradation
53f67caec42b.sentence: The decision to tolerate up to 10 μg/liter of "nonrelevant" metabolites in groundwater and drinking water is politically highly contentious in Europe.

e20ac3ed990f.title: Pesticide degradation
e20ac3ed990f.sentence: Some consider the higher limit acceptable as no imminent health risk can be proven, whereas others regard it as a fundamental deviation from the precautionary principle.

04207a913973.title: In situ bioremediation
04207a913973.sentence: Naturally occurring within the soil are microbial populations that utilize hydrocarbons as a source of energy and carbon.

935816bf13ea.title: In situ bioremediation
935816bf13ea.sentence: Up to twenty percent of microbial soil populations can metabolize hydrocarbons.

9be802016fde.title: In situ bioremediation
9be802016fde.sentence: The metabolic mode of hydrocarbon remediation is primarily aerobic.

01a894786e75.title: In situ bioremediation
01a894786e75.sentence: The end products of the remediation for hydrocarbons are Carbon Dioxide and water.

1780d4da47ae.title: In situ bioremediation
1780d4da47ae.sentence: Long-chain aliphatic carbons are the most effectively degraded.

0c84c5f44175.title: In situ bioremediation
0c84c5f44175.sentence: Short-chained, branched, and quaternary aliphatic hydrocarbons are less effectively degraded.

0478297b5e38.title: In situ bioremediation
0478297b5e38.sentence: Compounds with two or three rings are degraded at an effective rate, but compounds possessing four or more rings can be more resilient to bioremediation efforts.

e7f0d578b11b.title: In situ bioremediation
e7f0d578b11b.sentence: Meanwhile, for larger-molecular-sized compounds, the only metabolic mode that is effective is cometabolism.

31810c386ecc.title: In situ bioremediation
31810c386ecc.sentence: It has a porous and absorbent structure and creates optimal conditions for microorganisms to degrade pollutants in the soil.

cbe87aad1cd8.title: In situ bioremediation
cbe87aad1cd8.sentence: Additionally, Biochar is rich in carbon, which makes the Biochar act as a trap for PAH pollutants.

d7d2ff93f990.title: In situ bioremediation
d7d2ff93f990.sentence: The Raymond Process is a type of accelerated in situ bioremediation that was developed by Richard Raymond and involves the introduction of nutrients and electron acceptors to a contaminated site.

cfb423f2950a.title: In situ bioremediation
cfb423f2950a.sentence: This process is primarily used to treat polluted groundwater.

e4254038635b.title: In situ bioremediation
e4254038635b.sentence: In the Raymond process, a loop system is created.

079c3ba04b55.title: In situ bioremediation
079c3ba04b55.sentence: Contaminated Groundwater from downstream of the groundwater flow is pumped to the surface and infused with nutrients and an electron donor, often oxygen.

59d625879b57.title: In situ bioremediation
59d625879b57.sentence: This treated water is then pumped back down below the water table upstream of where it was originally taken.

66839d42f2b3.title: In situ bioremediation
66839d42f2b3.sentence: Oxygen can be injected into the subsurface through injection wells.

c70408bffe3a.title: In situ bioremediation
c70408bffe3a.sentence: It can also be introduced through an injection gallery.

3f31581ad6d6.title: In situ bioremediation
3f31581ad6d6.section: Classification > Raymond Process > Oxygen injection > Ozone injection
3f31581ad6d6.sentence: Within twenty minutes after being injected into the subsurface, fifty percent of the ozone will have decomposed to oxygen.

3330bd0dad44.title: In situ bioremediation
3330bd0dad44.sentence: A patent was filed in 1974 by Richard Raymond, Reclamation of Hydrocarbon Contaminated Ground Waters, which provided the basis for the commercialization of in situ bioremediation.

f2a96bbaf3c8.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.03%3A_Soil_Reclamation_and_Remediation_of_Disturbed_Lands
f2a96bbaf3c8.sentence: Soil contaminants can be broadly grouped as organic and inorganic.

0ab2b0613ef9.sentence: Organic contaminants include pesticides, organic solvents, and other industrial products (Table 16.1).

9459f5a55dee.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.03%3A_Soil_Reclamation_and_Remediation_of_Disturbed_Lands
9459f5a55dee.section: SOIL REMEDIATION > Table 16.1. Common soil contaminants
9459f5a55dee.sentence: Inorganic contaminants include metals or salts, often as anions or cations.

6b27d687a68b.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.03%3A_Soil_Reclamation_and_Remediation_of_Disturbed_Lands
6b27d687a68b.sentence: The most common organic contaminants (mass or volume) at contaminated sites in Canada are petroleum hydrocarbons (PHCs), including crude oil and refined products such as fuels and lubricating oils.

29b186f9e39e.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.03%3A_Soil_Reclamation_and_Remediation_of_Disturbed_Lands
29b186f9e39e.sentence: Dioxins, furans, and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) are organic compounds.

5f135cdf984f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.03%3A_Soil_Reclamation_and_Remediation_of_Disturbed_Lands
5f135cdf984f.section: SOIL REMEDIATION > Table 16.1. Common soil contaminants
5f135cdf984f.sentence: Inorganic contaminants | Chemical, industrial, mine wastes, firing ranges, fly and bottom ash, metal recycling, battery disposal

3380562ca2c1.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.03%3A_Soil_Reclamation_and_Remediation_of_Disturbed_Lands
3380562ca2c1.section: SOIL REMEDIATION > Table 16.1. Common soil contaminants
3380562ca2c1.sentence: Heavy and trace metals, metalloids | Acid rock drainage, chemical spills

4629a757a56e.section: SOIL REMEDIATION > Table 16.1. Common soil contaminants

def5c7e26731.section: SOIL REMEDIATION > Table 16.1. Common soil contaminants

e0dceb73b980.section: SOIL REMEDIATION > Table 16.1. Common soil contaminants
e0dceb73b980.sentence: They can be beneficial to soil ecosystems at background concentrations, although at high concentrations may pose a risk to human or non-human receptors.

60e6834d7e58.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.03%3A_Soil_Reclamation_and_Remediation_of_Disturbed_Lands
60e6834d7e58.section: SOIL REMEDIATION > Table 16.1. Common soil contaminants
60e6834d7e58.sentence: For example, copper, molybdenum, cobalt, and zinc are important plant micronutrients, but are contaminants at high concentrations.

0ea20a08e320.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.03%3A_Soil_Reclamation_and_Remediation_of_Disturbed_Lands
0ea20a08e320.section: SOIL REMEDIATION > Table 16.1. Common soil contaminants
0ea20a08e320.sentence: Non-metal anions such as chloride can build up in soils from de-icing operations or chemical spills.

0adddff80afb.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.03%3A_Soil_Reclamation_and_Remediation_of_Disturbed_Lands
0adddff80afb.section: SOIL REMEDIATION > Table 16.1. Common soil contaminants
0adddff80afb.sentence: At high concentrations they can increase soil electrical conductivity or have direct impacts on plants.

b8d7afb5fcf6.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.03%3A_Soil_Reclamation_and_Remediation_of_Disturbed_Lands
b8d7afb5fcf6.section: SOIL REMEDIATION > Table 16.1. Common soil contaminants
b8d7afb5fcf6.sentence: High concentrations of nutrients such as nitrogen, phosphorus, and sulphur, can be considered contaminants.

c2cd02cc8c52.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.03%3A_Soil_Reclamation_and_Remediation_of_Disturbed_Lands
c2cd02cc8c52.section: SOIL REMEDIATION > Table 16.1. Common soil contaminants
c2cd02cc8c52.sentence: They originate from waste materials that are inappropriately stored or disposed of on land, such as livestock waste applied on agricultural land.

89c3ce6f2a5d.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.03%3A_Soil_Reclamation_and_Remediation_of_Disturbed_Lands
89c3ce6f2a5d.section: SOIL REMEDIATION > Properties of Soils and Contaminants Relevant to Remediation
89c3ce6f2a5d.sentence: Selecting an appropriate remediation strategy is dependent on contaminant and site properties, including soil properties.

ac1d4196ff34.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.03%3A_Soil_Reclamation_and_Remediation_of_Disturbed_Lands

ac1d4196ff34.sentence: For example, petroleum hydrocarbons vary in molecular weight, water solubility, volatility, and density; gasoline tends to have lower molecular weight and higher volatility than lubricating oils.

a4886db5ea8c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.03%3A_Soil_Reclamation_and_Remediation_of_Disturbed_Lands
a4886db5ea8c.section: SOIL REMEDIATION > Properties of Soils and Contaminants Relevant to Remediation
a4886db5ea8c.sentence: Larger hydrocarbon compounds tend to be less volatile and less water soluble than smaller ones.

6b05d9f1c9b6.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.03%3A_Soil_Reclamation_and_Remediation_of_Disturbed_Lands
6b05d9f1c9b6.section: SOIL REMEDIATION > Properties of Soils and Contaminants Relevant to Remediation
6b05d9f1c9b6.sentence: Large, non-soluble hydrocarbons can exhibit strong sorption (are sorbed) to native soil organic matter (high sorption coefficient) making them difficult to degrade or remove, particularly in fine textured soils due to greater sorption and potential for entrapment within soil aggregates, and reduced movement of air and water.

fb2b0d8647fe.sentence: Inorganic contaminants, such as metals, can be present in different forms in soils.

b773237b6171.sentence: Distribution among the various components will be affected by soil texture, mineralogy, pH, cation and anion exchange capacity, organic matter content, and aeration status.

ed1d17972ce4.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.03%3A_Soil_Reclamation_and_Remediation_of_Disturbed_Lands

ed1d17972ce4.sentence: Remediation strategies need to take the various forms of chemical species into consideration.

3fae1d731feb.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.03%3A_Soil_Reclamation_and_Remediation_of_Disturbed_Lands
3fae1d731feb.sentence: Remediation strategies for contaminated soil can be broadly classified as biological, chemical, or physical (Table 16.2).

2232e01e7375.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.03%3A_Soil_Reclamation_and_Remediation_of_Disturbed_Lands
2232e01e7375.sentence: Many are a combination of more than one type, and can be applied either ex situ or in situ.

91af76f8a0fc.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.03%3A_Soil_Reclamation_and_Remediation_of_Disturbed_Lands
91af76f8a0fc.sentence: Ex situ methods involve excavating the soil from the impacted zone and treating the soil either on or off site.

11f0907da100.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.03%3A_Soil_Reclamation_and_Remediation_of_Disturbed_Lands
11f0907da100.sentence: In situ methods treat the contaminated soil in place.

6cfe3abf6de5.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.03%3A_Soil_Reclamation_and_Remediation_of_Disturbed_Lands

6cfe3abf6de5.sentence: Vitrification heats soil to 1400 to 2000°C to melt silica and convert it to stable glass and crystalline solids.

f14c5b8f336f.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.03%3A_Soil_Reclamation_and_Remediation_of_Disturbed_Lands
f14c5b8f336f.section: SOIL REMEDIATION > Table 16.2. Common remediation strategies for contaminated soils
f14c5b8f336f.sentence: Heat may be generated by electrodes and electrical resistance or plasma arc technology.

2ecc91a72dc5.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.03%3A_Soil_Reclamation_and_Remediation_of_Disturbed_Lands
2ecc91a72dc5.section: SOIL REMEDIATION > Table 16.2. Common remediation strategies for contaminated soils
2ecc91a72dc5.sentence: Organic contaminants are volatilized, trapped, and treated or destroyed and inorganic contaminants, including radionuclides, are encased.

00edcb0bed58.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.03%3A_Soil_Reclamation_and_Remediation_of_Disturbed_Lands
00edcb0bed58.section: SOIL REMEDIATION > Table 16.2. Common remediation strategies for contaminated soils
00edcb0bed58.sentence: Incineration involves heating soil ex situ to 870 to 1370°C to destroy organic contaminants.

ea22a8172349.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.03%3A_Soil_Reclamation_and_Remediation_of_Disturbed_Lands
ea22a8172349.section: SOIL REMEDIATION > Table 16.2. Common remediation strategies for contaminated soils
ea22a8172349.sentence: Soil washing is done ex situ and may involve separating soil fines (silt, clay) from coarse material thereby reducing the total mass and volume that needs to be treated.

9b8be78a6180.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.03%3A_Soil_Reclamation_and_Remediation_of_Disturbed_Lands
9b8be78a6180.section: SOIL REMEDIATION > Table 16.2. Common remediation strategies for contaminated soils
9b8be78a6180.sentence: Soil flushing occurs in situ, where the contaminated zone is treated with a solution, and mobilized contaminants are brought to the surface for disposal, treatment, or re-circulation.

884303ce1c5c.title: doc>geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Soil_Science/Digging_into_Canadian_Soils%3A_An_Introduction_to_Soil_Science/03%3A_Digging_Deeper/3.03%3A_Soil_Reclamation_and_Remediation_of_Disturbed_Lands
884303ce1c5c.section: SOIL REMEDIATION > Table 16.2. Common remediation strategies for contaminated soils
884303ce1c5c.sentence: Treatment solutions can be water, basic, acidic, chelating or complexing, reducing, co-solvents, or surfactants.

5f4ee9408370.title: Bioremediation of polychlorinated biphenyls
5f4ee9408370.sentence: Bioremediation of PCBs is the use of microorganisms to degrade PCBs from contaminated sites, relying on multiple microorganisms' co-metabolism.

84f05ef06d57.title: Bioremediation of polychlorinated biphenyls
84f05ef06d57.sentence: Polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs) are various biphenyl based artificial products that are widely used as a dielectric fluid, industrial coolant, and lubricants in the 1960s and 1970s.

544387a52ab9.title: Bioremediation of polychlorinated biphenyls
544387a52ab9.sentence: They are classified as persistent organic pollutants.

56fce58fd75b.title: Bioremediation of polychlorinated biphenyls
56fce58fd75b.sentence: Hence, the degradation of PCBs in the natural environment is very slow, which can range from 3 to 37 years depending on the number of chloride substitutions and their positions.

6327c32d702c.title: Bioremediation of polychlorinated biphenyls
6327c32d702c.sentence: However, due to the chlorination, PCBs can be used as electron acceptors in anaerobic respiration to store energy, which is also the first stage of the degradation pathway, reductive dechlorination.

4d1e2ab5743d.title: Bioremediation of polychlorinated biphenyls
4d1e2ab5743d.sentence: Anaerobic microorganisms dechlorinate PCBs first, and other microorganisms that are capable of doing BH pathway can break down the dechlorinated PCBs to usable intermediates like acyl-CoA or carbon dioxide.

3400627ed3b6.title: Bioremediation of polychlorinated biphenyls
3400627ed3b6.sentence: - PCBs are dechlorinated by anaerobic bacteria, then transport the metabolites to aerobic bacteria or fungi through a biofilm.

5d5c852134a9.title: Bioremediation of polychlorinated biphenyls
5d5c852134a9.section: Limiting Factors > PCBs entering the cells
5d5c852134a9.sentence: PCBs have low water solubility, so they adhere tightly to soil and cannot be easily accessed by bacteria.

edfea5525baa.title: Bioremediation of polychlorinated biphenyls
edfea5525baa.section: Limiting Factors > Soil and sediment characteristics
edfea5525baa.sentence: The PCBs’ availability suffers from increasing organic carbon and clay content, for they promote the absorption of PCBs into soil or sediment matrices.

c9eee3f4a4b0.title: Bioremediation of polychlorinated biphenyls
c9eee3f4a4b0.sentence: PCBs are toxic to bacterial communities above 1000 mg/kg.

e25995531fb2.title: Bioremediation of polychlorinated biphenyls
e25995531fb2.sentence: However, if the concentration is too low (lower than 50 mg/kg), the degradation slows down significantly, for there is not enough material to stimulate the expression of required genes and support the growth of competent microorganisms.

38ea7dad0325.title: Bioremediation of polychlorinated biphenyls
38ea7dad0325.sentence: Generally speaking, the more chlorines in a PCB molecule, the harder for it to be degraded.

254e3d81c054.title: Medical geology
254e3d81c054.sentence: There are two priorities that have been established within the medical geology field, "(1) the study of trace elements, especially their bioavailability and (2) a need to establish baseline, or background levels of contaminants/xenobiotics/potentially harmful but naturally occurring materials in water, soil, air, food, and animal tissue." The elements and minerals in the land affect people and animals immensely, especially when there is a close relationship between the two.

e98400fec9e1.title: Environmental remediation
e98400fec9e1.sentence: These are compared against both natural background levels in the area and standards for areas zoned as nearby areas are zoned and against standards used in other recent remediations.

be92085774c6.title: Arsenic
be92085774c6.sentence: Typical background concentrations of arsenic do not exceed 3 ng/m3 in the atmosphere; 100 mg/kg in soil; 400 μg/kg in vegetation; 10 μg/L in freshwater and 1.5 μg/L in seawater.

7132041caf3c.title: Lead
7132041caf3c.sentence: Typical background concentrations of lead do not exceed 0.1 μg/m3 in the atmosphere; 100 mg/kg in soil; 4 mg/kg in vegetation, 5 μg/L in fresh water and seawater.

2c57cfa0690f.title: Nickel
2c57cfa0690f.sentence: Typical background concentrations of nickel do not exceed 20 ng/m3 in air, 100 mg/kg in soil, 10 mg/kg in vegetation, 10 μg/L in freshwater and 1 μg/L in seawater.

86b6ed1996fa.title: Cadmium
86b6ed1996fa.sentence: Typical background concentrations of cadmium do not exceed 5 ng/m3 in the atmosphere; 2 mg/kg in soil; 1 μg/L in freshwater and 50 ng/L in seawater.

b5755051d4ad.title: Copper
b5755051d4ad.sentence: Typical background concentrations of copper do not exceed 1 ng/m3 in the atmosphere; 150 mg/kg in soil; 30 mg/kg in vegetation; 2 μg/L in freshwater and 0.5 μg/L in seawater.

639db6afee21.title: Zinc
639db6afee21.sentence: Typical background concentrations of zinc do not exceed: 1 μg/m3 in atmosphere, 300 mg/kg in soil, 100 mg/kg in vegetation, 20 μg/L in freshwater, and 5 μg/L in seawater.

677f8f101bcf.title: Chromium
677f8f101bcf.sentence: Typical background concentrations of chromium in environmental media are: atmosphere <10 ng/m3; soil <500 mg/kg; vegetation <0.5 mg/kg; freshwater <10 μg/L; seawater <1 μg/L; sediment <80 mg/kg.

6a66a1f92cdd.title: Selenium
6a66a1f92cdd.sentence: Typical background concentrations of selenium do not exceed 1 ng/m3 in the atmosphere; 1 mg/kg in soil and vegetation and 0.5 μg/L in freshwater and seawater, 0.05 – 0.09 mg/kg average crustal abundance.

0a6ca4c37c6e.title: Contaminants of emerging concern
0a6ca4c37c6e.sentence: Contaminants of emerging concern (CEC) is a term used by water quality professionals to describe pollutants that have been detected in environmental monitoring samples, that may cause ecological or human health impacts, and typically are not regulated under current environmental laws.

300c0baa1da6.title: Contaminants of emerging concern
300c0baa1da6.sentence: CEC include different substances like pharmaceuticals, personal care products, industrial byproducts, and agricultural chemicals.

25d0689e9a76.title: Contaminants of emerging concern
25d0689e9a76.sentence: These substances often bypass regular detection and treatment processes, leading to their unintended persistence in the environment.

cea85d1eb632.title: Contaminants of emerging concern
cea85d1eb632.sentence: Agricultural runoff is a major pathway through which CEC enter the environment.

08ad3d655b8e.title: Contaminants of emerging concern
08ad3d655b8e.sentence: Then runoff happens after rainfall or irrigation, which causes an influx of chemicals to leak out of the soil where they were dumped and into rivers, lakes, and groundwater.

b80fd6001e13.title: Contaminants of emerging concern
b80fd6001e13.sentence: It is particularly important to ensure that water treatment approaches do not simply move contaminants from effluent to sludge given the potential for sludge to be spread to land providing an alternative route to entering the environment.

bf9f4c074670.title: Contaminants of emerging concern
bf9f4c074670.section: Environmental and health impacts > Selected compounds listed as emerging contaminants
bf9f4c074670.sentence: Trinitrotoluene (TNT) | Pure explosive, military and underwater blasting | Major contaminant of groundwater and soils | Listed as cancer-causing by Office of Environmental Health, may cause carcinoma and bladder papilloma

a6dccde87fff.title: Bioremediation of radioactive waste
a6dccde87fff.sentence: Bioremediation of radioactive waste or bioremediation of radionuclides is an application of bioremediation based on the use of biological agents bacteria, plants and fungi (natural or genetically modified) to catalyze chemical reactions that allow the decontamination of sites affected by radionuclides.

8a9904c21341.title: Bioremediation of radioactive waste
8a9904c21341.sentence: The techniques of bioremediation of environmental areas as soil, water and sediments contaminated by radionuclides are diverse and currently being set up as an ecological and economic alternative to traditional procedures.

8ee4bc083445.title: Bioremediation of radioactive waste
8ee4bc083445.sentence: Physico-chemical conventional strategies are based on the extraction of waste by excavating and drilling, with a subsequent long-range transport for their final confinement.

650cd67ea8b2.title: Bioremediation of radioactive waste
650cd67ea8b2.sentence: These works and transport have often unacceptable estimated costs of operation that could exceed a trillion dollars in the US and 50 million pounds in the UK.

3b0d48906e9b.title: Bioremediation of radioactive waste
3b0d48906e9b.sentence: The species involved in these processes have the ability to influence the properties of radionuclides such as solubility, bioavailability and mobility to accelerate its stabilization.

3a1b5191be70.title: Bioremediation of radioactive waste
3a1b5191be70.section: Areas contaminated by radioactivity > Typology of radionuclides and polluting waste
3a1b5191be70.sentence: The most frequent radionuclides in soils are naturally radium-226 (226Ra), radon-222 (222Rn), thorium-232 (232Th), uranium-238 (238U) and potassium-40 (40K).

f6f7aa8f776d.title: Bioremediation of radioactive waste
f6f7aa8f776d.sentence: Since then, it has been shown that some species of Penicillium, Cladosporium, Paecilomyces and Xerocomus are able to use ionizing radiation as energy through the electronic properties of melanins.

9a8fffb4713c.title: Bioremediation of radioactive waste
9a8fffb4713c.sentence: Other fungi like oyster mushrooms can bioremediate plutonium-239 and americium-241.

5b288ee6ad66.title: Bioremediation of radioactive waste
5b288ee6ad66.sentence: Their redox potential is exploited by some microbial species to carry out reductions that alter the solubility and hence, mobility, bioavailability and radiotoxicity.

ebc1f83cb2b2.title: Bioremediation of radioactive waste
ebc1f83cb2b2.sentence: This waste treatment technique called bioreduction or enzymatic biotransformation is very attractive because it can be done in mild conditions for the environment, does not produce hazardous secondary waste and has potential as a solution for waste of various kinds.

fe54ddd52e71.title: Bioremediation of radioactive waste
fe54ddd52e71.sentence: Direct enzymatic reduction is the change of radionuclides of a higher oxidation state to a lower one made by facultative and obligate anaerobes.

476f837af2cd.title: Bioremediation of radioactive waste
476f837af2cd.sentence: The radioisotope interact with binding sites of metabolically active cells and is used as terminal electron acceptor in the electron transport chain where compounds such as ethyl lactate act as electron donors under anaerobic respiration.

b086fe7e5adf.title: Bioremediation of radioactive waste
b086fe7e5adf.sentence: In the reduction of uranium (VI) to insoluble uranium (IV), made by Shewanella putrefaciens, Desulfovibrio vulgaris, Desulfovibrio desulfuricans and Geobacter sulfurreducens, the activity of periplasmic cytochromes is required.

6a5c764e3aee.title: Bioremediation of radioactive waste
6a5c764e3aee.sentence: The phenomenon of indirect enzymatic reduction is carried out by sulfate-reducing and dissimilatory metal-reducing bacteria on excretion reactions of metabolites and breakdown products.

a7b64d8276cf.title: Bioremediation of radioactive waste
a7b64d8276cf.sentence: There are several species of reducing microorganisms that produce indirect sequestering agents and specific chelators, such as siderophores.

7855f75ea234.title: Bioremediation of radioactive waste
7855f75ea234.sentence: These sequestering agents are crucial in the complexation of radionuclides and increasing their solubility and bioavailability.

fb4a8880e34e.title: Bioremediation of radioactive waste
fb4a8880e34e.sentence: In phytoextraction (also phytoaccumulation, phytosequesteration or phytoabsorption) plants carry radioactive waste from the root system to the vascular tissue and become concentrated in the biomass of shoots.

23c9de1eb417.title: Bioremediation of radioactive waste
23c9de1eb417.sentence: It is a technique that removes radionuclides without destroying the soil structure, with minimal impact on soil fertility and valid for large areas with a low level of radioactivity.

902599e1428a.title: Bioremediation of radioactive waste
902599e1428a.sentence: By contrast, it requires large biomass production in short periods of time.

03c223b65c1f.title: Bioremediation of radioactive waste
03c223b65c1f.sentence: Its efficiency is evaluated through bioaccumulation coefficient (BC) or total removal of radionuclides per m2, and is proven to attract cesium-137, strontium-90, technetium-99, cerium-144, plutonium-240, americium-241, neptunium-237 and various radioisotopes of thorium and radium.

0d57ed2ea04b.title: Bioremediation of radioactive waste
0d57ed2ea04b.sentence: In this region of Ukraine, mustard greens could remove up to 22% of average levels of cesium activity in a single growing season.

dac4f9a510b6.title: Sustainable remediation
dac4f9a510b6.sentence: Sustainable remediation brings together the concepts of remediation with the practice of sustainability.

39b5fe48de8f.title: Sustainable remediation
39b5fe48de8f.sentence: Sustainable remediation is the practice of considering the effects of implementing an environmental cleanup and incorporating options to minimize the footprint of the cleanup actions.

8d67381b690a.title: Sustainable remediation
8d67381b690a.sentence: Five core elements are evaluated as part of the environmental footprint analysis including 1) energy, 2) air and atmosphere, 3) materials and waste, 4) land and ecosystem, and 5) water.

ad9ace2d2cf2.title: Sustainable remediation
ad9ace2d2cf2.sentence: In the US alone, there are more than 450,000 brown field sites that require significant reinvestment due to years of toxic contamination and/or degradation.

e65b7c5dcb7d.title: Sustainable remediation
e65b7c5dcb7d.sentence: Certain treatments like pump and treat, and dig and haul can, in certain situations, have some long lasting unintended effects upon the environment that are more detrimental than helpful in some situations.

bd633a0316f9.title: Sustainable remediation
bd633a0316f9.section: Current practices in the field of sustainable remediation
bd633a0316f9.sentence: Techniques like these are much more environmentally friendly than more traditional ex-situ methods, and can greatly increase the benefits of remediation.

c138db4ce31e.title: Sustainable remediation
c138db4ce31e.section: Current practices in the field of sustainable remediation
c138db4ce31e.sentence: In fact some of these newer techniques have shown to reduce the life-cycle greenhouse gas emissions by between 50 and 80 percent.

3648b7a0f57f.title: Sustainable remediation
3648b7a0f57f.sentence: Projects like this and increased regulations in Europe led to the eventual creation of several professional groups such as the Network for Industrially Contaminated Land in Europe (NICOLE, founded in 1995 in Europe) and the Sustainable Remediation Forum (SuRF, founded in 2006 in the United States).

da283a58b736.title: Vapor intrusion
da283a58b736.sentence: Vapor intrusion (VI) is the process by which chemicals, usually volatile organic compounds (VOCs), in soil or groundwater migrate to indoor air above or around a contaminated site.

394033944c7d.title: Vapor intrusion
394033944c7d.sentence: The United States Environmental Protection Agency defines vapor intrusion as "a migration of volatile chemicals from groundwater contamination or contaminated soil into an overlying building".

eddca4569799.title: Vapor intrusion
eddca4569799.sentence: VOCs are most able to travel through porous soils because of the space it allows for the chemicals, and then diffuse in the vadose zone of soil, eventually to areas underneath manmade structures and buildings.

6ac6294fb7e2.title: Vapor intrusion
6ac6294fb7e2.sentence: Once under building foundation, the processes of advection and diffusion are responsible for the compounds traveling through cracks of the foundation until the gaseous compounds mix with the components of the indoor air.

21d0001b47a9.title: Vapor intrusion
21d0001b47a9.sentence: The ability of the compound to enter a building through advectio can be related to the pressure gradient of the soil versus the building, which is caused by the 'stack effect' of the foundation.

d5b4ae153beb.title: Vapor intrusion
d5b4ae153beb.sentence: Preferential pathways, such as elevator shafts, pipes, and storm drains, act as an easy path for VOCs to travel through via groundwater or soil gas, and enter a building through man-made entrances like vents and faucets.

f231119a901f.title: Vapor intrusion
f231119a901f.sentence: When these chemicals mix with the indoor air, they can lead to acute or chronic health problems, like headaches, mental status changes, and increased risk of certain cancers.

e0ebf0245cec.title: Vapor intrusion
e0ebf0245cec.sentence: Vapor intrusion can also pose a threat when an infiltrated building contains flammable materials, as many VA compounds can act as a catalyst to cause an explosion.

aa0e532809ef.title: Vapor intrusion
aa0e532809ef.sentence: Two methods in particular are described, sub-slab depressurization, which entails using a fan to vent chemical vapors outdoors, and the over-pressurization of buildings, in which building pressure is increased to decrease the pressure gradient between under the building and the inside of the building.

f21e7a24265e.title: Vapor intrusion
f21e7a24265e.sentence: On June 11, 2015, the EPA released its final Vapor Intrusion Technical Guide, along with a Technical Guide for Addressing Petroleum Vapor Intrusion At Leaking Underground Storage Tank Sites.

868cd69ddeaf.title: Geophagia
868cd69ddeaf.sentence: Geophagia (/ˌdʒiːəˈfeɪdʒ(i)ə/), also known as geophagy (/dʒiˈɒfədʒi/), is the intentional practice of consuming earth or soil-like substances such as clay, chalk, or termite mounds.

3a4662ada562.title: Geophagia
3a4662ada562.sentence: It is a behavioural adaptation that occurs in many animals and has been documented in more than 100 primate species.

e4c583e350f8.title: Geophagia
e4c583e350f8.sentence: Geophagy in primates is primarily used for protection from parasites, to provide mineral supplements and to help metabolize toxic compounds from leaves.

e9e60897121c.title: Geophagia
e9e60897121c.sentence: Geophagy also occurs in humans and is most commonly reported among children and pregnant women.

222f790cadc4.title: Geophagia
222f790cadc4.sentence: Human geophagia is a form of pica – the craving and purposive consumption of non-food items – and is classified as an eating disorder in the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM) if not socially or culturally appropriate.

d5c210aabe81.title: Geophagia
d5c210aabe81.sentence: > The oldest evidence of geophagy practised by humans comes from the prehistoric site at Kalambo Falls on the border between Zambia and Tanzania (Root-Bernstein & Root-Bernstein, 2000).

590d7da214b5.title: Geophagia
590d7da214b5.sentence: Here, a calcium-rich white clay was found alongside the bones of Homo habilis (a potential predecessor of Homo sapiens).

43dd2f613e7c.title: Geophagia
43dd2f613e7c.sentence: Kaolin for human consumption is sold at most markets in Cameroon and is often flavoured with spices such as black pepper and cardamom.

84ea922b7712.title: Geophagia
84ea922b7712.sentence: Consumption is greatest among women, especially to cure nausea during pregnancy, in spite of the possible dangerous levels of arsenic and lead to the unborn child.

d246bf99168d.title: Geophagia
d246bf99168d.sentence: Clay minerals have been reported to have beneficial microbiological effects, such as protecting the stomach against toxins, parasites, and pathogens.

020295553978.title: Geophagia
020295553978.sentence: Mineral content in soils may vary by region, but many contain high levels of calcium, copper, magnesium, iron, and zinc; these minerals are critical for developing fetuses, which may explain cravings by pregnant women to chew metallic objects, soil, ice cravings.

38ae21543fb5.title: Geophagia
38ae21543fb5.sentence: There are obvious health risks in the consumption of soil that is contaminated by animal or human feces; in particular, helminth eggs, such as Ascaris, which can stay viable in the soil for years, can lead to helminth infections.

8cf6c2000b20.title: Geophagia
8cf6c2000b20.sentence: Lead poisoning is also associated with soil ingestion, as well as health risks associated with zinc exposure can be problematic among people who eat soils on a regular basis.

2a38f6c4ee16.title: Geophagia
2a38f6c4ee16.sentence: Bentonite clay is available worldwide as a digestive aid; kaolin is also widely used as a digestive aid and as the base for some medicines.

17f6463a0838.title: Geophagia
17f6463a0838.sentence: Attapulgite, another type of clay, is an active ingredient in many anti-diarrheal medicines.

a76e8aab325a.title: Itai-itai disease
a76e8aab325a.sentence: Itai-itai disease (Japanese: イタイイタイ病, Hepburn: itai-itai byō; lit. '"it hurts, it hurts" disease') was the name given to the mass cadmium poisoning of Toyama Prefecture, Japan, starting around 1912.

b816533d42cb.title: Itai-itai disease
b816533d42cb.sentence: The term "itai-itai disease" was coined by locals for the severe pains (Japanese: 痛い itai) people with the condition felt in the spine and joints.

3df938424ec6.title: Itai-itai disease
3df938424ec6.sentence: Starting in 1910 and continuing through 1945, cadmium was released in significant quantities by mining operations, and the disease first appeared around 1912.

4414ce76d20f.title: Itai-itai disease
4414ce76d20f.sentence: Sphalerite, the main zinc containing ore in Komioka, is almost always coupled with greenockite, the only major cadmium-containing mineral in the world.

f84815e1c224.title: Itai-itai disease
f84815e1c224.sentence: Because of this, cadmium is a regular by-product of the zinc ore mining process.

53b27302d399.title: Itai-itai disease
53b27302d399.section: History > Cadmium pollution in Jinzū river
53b27302d399.sentence: Due to the residents being unaware of the cadmium and its dangers, they used the water from the Jinzū to irrigate their rice fields.

a1f0f01e614c.title: Itai-itai disease
a1f0f01e614c.section: History > Cadmium pollution in Jinzū river
a1f0f01e614c.sentence: Cadmium is highly water-soluble and the rice paddies' prolonged exposure led to the rice quickly becoming contaminated and toxic.

7d3951bd43d1.title: Itai-itai disease
7d3951bd43d1.section: History > Cadmium pollution in Jinzū river
7d3951bd43d1.sentence: The local residents' consumption of this rice and drinking water then resulted in elevated cadmium body burdens – leading directly to symptoms characteristic of itai-itai disease.

6021100860d0.title: Itai-itai disease
6021100860d0.section: History > Cadmium accumulation in a human body
6021100860d0.sentence: Cadmium accumulates mainly in the liver and the kidneys, but has more of an effect on the kidneys.

cc39143c1717.title: Itai-itai disease
cc39143c1717.section: History > Cadmium accumulation in a human body
cc39143c1717.sentence: Once the kidneys have experienced extensive damage, those affected begin experiencing musculoskeletal damage, due to the disruption of calcium homeostasis.

739996ce6484.title: Itai-itai disease
739996ce6484.section: History > Cadmium accumulation in a human body
739996ce6484.sentence: This musculoskeletal damage is what causes the bone pain and bone deformities that characterize itai-itai disease.

d7d05eb2bf2d.title: Itai-itai disease
d7d05eb2bf2d.sentence: Only in 1955 did Dr. Hagino and his colleagues suspect cadmium as the cause of the disease.

58de93ffb858.title: Itai-itai disease
58de93ffb858.sentence: Toyama Prefecture also started an investigation in 1961, determining that the Mitsui Mining and Smelting's Kamioka Mining Station caused the cadmium pollution and that the worst-affected areas were 30 kilometres (19 mi) downstream of the mine.

673d18ffcefe.title: Itai-itai disease
673d18ffcefe.sentence: After the first reports of Itai-Itai in 1912, it took 55 years for the epidemiological investigation to discover that the disease was due to cadmium poisoning.

b8a5a3e36b33.title: Itai-itai disease
b8a5a3e36b33.sentence: Itai-itai disease is known as one of the Four Big Pollution Diseases of Japan.

addab86db4d2.title: Itai-itai disease
addab86db4d2.sentence: The cadmium was released into rivers by mining companies in the mountains, which were successfully sued for the damage.

e74b87197487.title: Coccidioidomycosis
e74b87197487.sentence: Coccidioidomycosis (/kɒkˌsɪdiɔɪdoʊmaɪˈkoʊsɪs/, kok-SID-ee-oy-doh-my-KOH-sis) is a mammalian fungal disease caused by Coccidioides immitis or Coccidioides posadasii.

058a9e11ee97.title: Coccidioidomycosis
058a9e11ee97.sentence: It is commonly known as cocci, Valley fever, or San Joaquin Valley fever.

8e1cada14962.title: Coccidioidomycosis
8e1cada14962.sentence: Infections usually occur due to inhalation of the arthroconidial spores after soil disruption.

e775ce0a3b42.title: Coccidioidomycosis
e775ce0a3b42.sentence: C. immitis is a dimorphic saprophytic fungus that grows as a mycelium in the soil and produces a spherule form in the host organism.

729c32f1e680.title: Coccidioidomycosis
729c32f1e680.sentence: It resides in the soil in certain parts of the southwestern United States, most notably in California and Arizona.

499a26f4278d.title: Coccidioidomycosis
499a26f4278d.sentence: It is also commonly found in northern Mexico, and parts of Central and South America.

4b489f79cb63.title: Coccidioidomycosis
4b489f79cb63.sentence: Rain starts the cycle of initial growth of the fungus in the soil.

87f70135b30c.title: Coccidioidomycosis
87f70135b30c.sentence: Over a prolonged dry period, cells within hyphae degenerate to form alternating barrel-shaped cells (arthroconidia) which are light in weight and carried by air currents.

8ec563ad8b68.title: Coccidioidomycosis
8ec563ad8b68.sentence: The spores, known as arthroconidia, are swept into the air by disruption of the soil, such as during construction, farming, low-wind or singular dust events, or an earthquake.

f186028830b6.title: Coccidioidomycosis
f186028830b6.sentence: In December 1977, a windstorm in an endemic area around Arvin, California, led to several hundred cases, including deaths, in non-endemic areas hundreds of miles away.

5954541927a0.title: Coccidioidomycosis
5954541927a0.section: One Health and climate change > Climate and geographic range
5954541927a0.sentence: The growth and dispersal of Coccidioides depend on cycles of precipitation and drought: wet periods support growth of the fungus in soil, and subsequent dry, windy conditions release infectious arthroconidia into the air.

c78246153869.title: Coccidioidomycosis
c78246153869.section: One Health and climate change > Climate and geographic range
c78246153869.sentence: A 2022 analysis of two decades of case data from the western United States found that incidence rose after wet winters that followed multi-year droughts, consistent with this "grow and blow" pattern, and that drought–rain cycles are becoming more pronounced with climate change.

50247a153a8f.title: Coccidioidomycosis
50247a153a8f.section: One Health and climate change > Climate and geographic range
50247a153a8f.sentence: One widely cited model projected that under a high-warming scenario the climate-limited endemic region could more than double in area by 2100, extend from 12 to 17 states, and produce roughly 50% more cases, with expansion northward through the Great Plains and Pacific Northwest.

35195b5343d9.title: Coccidioidomycosis
35195b5343d9.sentence: Dust control measures such as planting grass and wetting the soil, and also limiting exposure to dust storms are advisable for residential areas in endemic regions.

8cf535b2a93f.title: Coccidioidomycosis
8cf535b2a93f.sentence: The National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health identifies coccidioidomycosis as an occupational concern for workers in agriculture, archaeology, construction, geology, mining, oil and gas extraction, firefighting, and the military in endemic areas.

7ae4300bc72c.title: Coccidioidomycosis
7ae4300bc72c.section: One Health and climate change > Animals as sentinels
7ae4300bc72c.sentence: Dogs are highly susceptible to coccidioidomycosis and, because they dig and sniff at the ground, are typically exposed to spores earlier and more intensely than the people they live with.

13a56cded090.title: Coccidioidomycosis
13a56cded090.section: One Health and climate change > Animals as sentinels
13a56cded090.sentence: This has led researchers to use canine infections as a sentinel for human risk.

66c57cbce09f.title: Medical geology
66c57cbce09f.sentence: Medical geology is an interdisciplinary scientific field studying the relationship between natural geological factors and their effects on human and animal health.

e4c2b0f3dc19.title: Medical geology
e4c2b0f3dc19.sentence: In its broadest sense, medical geology studies exposure to or deficiency of trace elements and minerals; inhalation of ambient and anthropogenic mineral dusts and volcanic emissions; transportation, modification and concentration of organic compounds; and exposure to radionuclides, microbes and pathogens.

188315de42f3.title: Medical geology
188315de42f3.sentence: Those who depend heavily on the land are faced with one of two problems.

63b9fe329597.title: Medical geology
63b9fe329597.sentence: First, those who live in places such as Maputaland, South Africa are exposed to heavily impoverished soils which result in a number of diseases caused by mineral imbalances.

6337eded1ca9.title: Medical geology
6337eded1ca9.sentence: Secondly, those in areas such as India and Bangladesh are often exposed to an excess of elements in the land, resulting in mineral toxicity.

a95e56dd3ca4.title: Medical geology
a95e56dd3ca4.sentence: One of the biggest geochemical diseases is iodine deficiency.

825535292888.title: Medical geology
825535292888.sentence: Another source of it is in soil; however, goitrogens such as humus and clay trap the iodine, making it hard for people to access it.

56791b7892e1.title: Medical geology
56791b7892e1.sentence: Among the problems presented there are also issues with fluoride in Africa and India, arsenic in Argentina, Chile, and Taiwan, selenium in areas of the United States, Venezuela, China and nitrate in agricultural areas.

83de102771fd.title: Medical geology
83de102771fd.sentence: Paracelsus, the "father of pharmacology" (1493–1541), stated that "all substances are poisons, there is none which is not a poison.

6944aad347a6.title: Medical geology
6944aad347a6.sentence: The right dosage differentiates a poison and a remedy." This passage sums up the idea of medical geology.

daa1d08ed88d.title: Medical geology
daa1d08ed88d.sentence: The goal of this field is to find the right balance and intake of elements/minerals in order to improve and maintain health.

882c71c6fcaf.title: Medical geology
882c71c6fcaf.sentence: Hippocrates and Aristotle first recognized the relationship between human diseases and the earth's elements.

dd4785bea7a6.title: Medical geology
dd4785bea7a6.sentence: It was established in 1990 by the International Union of Geological Sciences.

7daf5831390c.title: Iodine deficiency
7daf5831390c.sentence: Iodine deficiency is a lack of the trace element iodine, a dietary mineral that is essential in the diet.

5249a324f52c.title: Iodine deficiency
5249a324f52c.sentence: The thyroid hormones thyroxine and triiodothyronine contain iodine.

7e186dc99477.title: Iodine deficiency
7e186dc99477.sentence: In areas with little iodine in the diet, typically remote inland areas where no marine foods are eaten, deficiency is common, especially in mountainous regions where food is grown in iodine-poor soil.

71095bac2994.title: Iodine deficiency
71095bac2994.sentence: The defiency is endemic in some parts of the world and may result in metabolic problems such as goiter.

0cb31bba7cd8.title: Iodine deficiency
0cb31bba7cd8.sentence: If congenital, it may result in a syndrome that causes developmental delays and other health problems, sometimes including physical deformities.

0f34acc8b993.title: Iodine deficiency
0f34acc8b993.sentence: It is also a preventable cause of intellectual disability, as it is necessary for neurodevelopment in children.

7708213a6440.title: Iodine deficiency
7708213a6440.sentence: Certain areas of the world, due to natural deficiency and unavailability of iodine, are severely affected by iodine deficiency, which affects approximately two billion people worldwide.

0f4f0835d06c.title: Iodine deficiency
0f4f0835d06c.sentence: It is particularly common in the Western Pacific, South-East Asia and Africa.

9f399b93110b.title: Iodine deficiency
9f399b93110b.sentence: Iodine deficiency resulting in goiter occurs in 187 million people globally as of 2010^ (2.7% of the population).

49423413a9ae.title: Iodine deficiency
49423413a9ae.sentence: The problem is mainly prevented by the addition of small amounts of iodine to table salt, creating iodized salt.

407522f45dca.title: Iodine deficiency
407522f45dca.sentence: The cost of adding iodine to salt is negligible—"Only a few cents a ton."

3c72c9e57642.title: Selenium deficiency
3c72c9e57642.sentence: Selenium deficiency occurs when an organism lacks the required levels of selenium, a critical nutrient in many species.

dc6ca9d561ce.title: Selenium deficiency
dc6ca9d561ce.sentence: People dependent on food grown from selenium-deficient soil may be at risk for deficiency.

be28f78566a2.title: Selenium deficiency
be28f78566a2.sentence: Selenium deficiency is uncommon, but regions in China, Europe, Russia, and New Zealand have low selenium levels in croplands and diet.

e85816f008a4.title: Selenium deficiency
e85816f008a4.sentence: The worldwide prevalence of selenium deficiency is however predicted to rise under climate change due to the loss of selenium from croplands.

7dec5684b464.title: Selenium deficiency
7dec5684b464.sentence: Selenium deficiency in combination with Coxsackievirus infection can lead to Keshan disease, which is potentially fatal.

cb9b1e80b9bf.title: Selenium deficiency
cb9b1e80b9bf.sentence: Selenium deficiency also contributes (along with iodine deficiency) to Kashin-Beck disease.

edd321b2190e.title: Selenium deficiency
edd321b2190e.sentence: Kashin-Beck disease results in atrophy, degeneration, and necrosis of cartilage tissue.

9b255337af5c.title: Selenium deficiency
9b255337af5c.sentence: In Finland, selenium salts are added to chemical fertilizers, as a way to increase selenium in soils.

f9edcbc74025.title: Selenium deficiency
f9edcbc74025.sentence: Selenium deficiency is responsible (either alone or together with vitamin E deficiency) for many of the cases of WMD ("white muscle disease"), evidenced at slaughter or during necropsy by the whitish appearance of striated muscle tissue due to bleaching by peroxides and hydroperoxides.

e29d9106bd6f.title: Selenium deficiency
e29d9106bd6f.sentence: Although this degenerative disease can occur in foals, pigs, and other animal species, ruminants are particularly susceptible.

c7594b4f1060.title: Selenium deficiency
c7594b4f1060.sentence: In general, absorption of dietary selenium is lower in ruminants than in non-ruminants and lower from forages than from grain.

2182ce4af775.title: Selenium deficiency
2182ce4af775.sentence: In the US, the Dietary Reference Intake for adults is 55 μg/day.

94f9a5b82f56.title: Selenium deficiency
94f9a5b82f56.sentence: The European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) recommends a dietary allowance of 70 μg per day selenium intake for adults.

871e9a0c4e67.title: Prion
871e9a0c4e67.sentence: A prion (/ˈpriː.ɒn/ ⓘ, /ˈpraɪ.ɒn/) is a misfolded protein that induces folding problems in normal variants of the same protein, leading to cellular death.

21b53158fe98.title: Prion
21b53158fe98.sentence: Prions are responsible for prion diseases, which are fatal and transmissible neurodegenerative diseases affecting animals, including humans.

b97942614f7a.title: Prion
b97942614f7a.sentence: Unlike other infectious agents such as viruses, bacteria, and fungi, prions do not contain nucleic acids (DNA or RNA).

000cbf87f8e1.title: Prion
000cbf87f8e1.sentence: They are the hypothesized cause of various diseases, including scrapie in sheep, chronic wasting disease (CWD) in deer, bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE) in cattle (mad cow disease), and Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease (CJD) in humans.

5e3a9a888320.title: Prion
5e3a9a888320.sentence: It is thought that prions may be deposited in the environment through the remains of dead animals and via urine, saliva, and other body fluids.

151e232d4027.title: Prion
151e232d4027.sentence: They may then linger in the soil by binding to clay and other minerals.

1ace1115863a.title: Prion
1ace1115863a.section: Transmissible spongiform encephalopathies > Degradation resistance in nature
1ace1115863a.sentence: Experimental evidence shows that unbound prions degrade over time, while soil-bound prions remain at stable or increasing levels, suggesting that prions likely accumulate in the environment.

4b788392519e.title: Prion
4b788392519e.section: Transmissible spongiform encephalopathies > Degradation resistance in nature
4b788392519e.sentence: One 2015 study by US scientists found that repeated drying and wetting may render soil bound prions less infectious, although this was dependent on the soil type they were bound to.

970cd1d102f0.title: Prion
970cd1d102f0.section: Transmissible spongiform encephalopathies > Transmission > Prions in plants
970cd1d102f0.sentence: When researchers fed hamsters grass that grew on ground where a deer that died with chronic wasting disease was buried, the hamsters became ill with CWD.

e045b68e63ad.title: Prion
e045b68e63ad.section: Transmissible spongiform encephalopathies > Transmission > Prions in plants
e045b68e63ad.sentence: The findings suggest that prions can be taken up by plants that are eaten by herbivores, thus completing the cycle.

8cc7d3154f78.title: Melioidosis
8cc7d3154f78.sentence: Melioidosis is an infectious disease caused by a gram-negative bacterium called Burkholderia pseudomallei.

739a26df9b1f.title: Burkholderia pseudomallei
739a26df9b1f.sentence: It is a soil-dwelling bacterium endemic in tropical and subtropical regions worldwide, particularly in Thailand and northern Australia.

742dddc1512a.title: Melioidosis
742dddc1512a.sentence: Humans are infected with B. pseudomallei by contact with contaminated soil or water.

7a37b961ac32.title: Melioidosis
7a37b961ac32.sentence: B. pseudomallei is normally found in soil and surface water, and is most abundant at soil depths of 10 to 90 cm.

65ef62b90d70.title: Melioidosis
65ef62b90d70.sentence: It has been found in soils, ponds, streams, pools, stagnant water, and rice paddy fields.

c152e16a5fb8.title: Melioidosis
c152e16a5fb8.sentence: B. pseudomallei can survive in nutrient-poor conditions such as distilled water, desert soil, and nutrient-depleted soil for more than 16 years.

59f68e4d908c.title: Melioidosis
59f68e4d908c.sentence: It can also survive in antiseptic and detergent solutions, acidic environments (pH 4.5 for 70 days), and in environments at temperatures ranging from 24 °C (75.2 °F) to 32 °C (89.6 °F).

d2ef448f77a6.title: Melioidosis
d2ef448f77a6.sentence: The bacteria enter the body through wounds, inhalation, or ingestion.

8c78618bb0fc.title: Melioidosis
8c78618bb0fc.sentence: The infection is constantly present in Southeast Asia (particularly northeast Thailand) and northern Australia.

813746c154a6.title: Melioidosis
813746c154a6.sentence: Increased rainfall and severe weather events such as thunderstorms are associated with an increased number of melioidosis cases in endemic areas.

8a4aecc05b6b.title: Melioidosis
8a4aecc05b6b.sentence: Approximately 165,000 people are infected by melioidosis per year, resulting in about 89,000 deaths, based on a mathematical model published in 2016.

9c9ab55fee1f.title: Melioidosis
9c9ab55fee1f.sentence: Diabetes is a major risk factor for melioidosis; over half of melioidosis cases are in people with diabetes.

14e394077119.title: Melioidosis
14e394077119.sentence: Spotnitz coined the term "Vietnam Time Bomb" to highlight the fact that B. pseudomallei could remain dormant for years.

54ad1e7d750e.title: Melioidosis
54ad1e7d750e.sentence: Efforts to prevent melioidosis include: wearing protective gear while handling contaminated water or soil, practising hand hygiene, drinking boiled water, and avoiding direct contact with soil, water, or heavy rain.

48a066f1e051.title: Melioidosis
48a066f1e051.sentence: There is no approved vaccine for melioidosis.

641be296100a.title: Soil-transmitted helminthiasis
641be296100a.sentence: Soil-transmitted helminthiasis is a type of worm infection (helminthiasis) caused by different species of roundworms.

a0d9cd159ca6.title: Soil-transmitted helminthiasis
a0d9cd159ca6.sentence: It is caused specifically by worms transmitted through soil contaminated with fecal matter and are known as soil-transmitted helminths.

26572f87d367.title: Soil-transmitted helminthiasis
26572f87d367.sentence: Three types of soil-transmitted helminthiasis can be distinguished: ascariasis, hookworm infection and whipworm infection.

c5ed968e340e.title: Soil-transmitted helminthiasis
c5ed968e340e.sentence: It has become the most common parasitic disease of humans worldwide.

aaa0f472b84c.title: Soil-transmitted helminthiasis
aaa0f472b84c.sentence: Approximately two billion people (about a fourth of global population) are infected as of the latest estimate, and four billion at risk, surpassing even the all-time most prevalent parasitic disease, malaria.

47bc914c0b6d.title: Soil-transmitted helminthiasis
47bc914c0b6d.sentence: Soil-transmitted helminths are intestinal parasites and their eggs which are liberated into soil along with the feces of infected persons.

0943f55c7e82.title: Soil-transmitted helminthiasis
0943f55c7e82.sentence: Ascaris and hookworm eggs become infective as they develop into larvae in soil.

745063ba6664.title: Soil-transmitted helminthiasis
745063ba6664.sentence: Infection occurs when vegetables and fruits contaminated with egg-infested soil are consumed, or when contaminated hands or fingers are placed in the mouth.

fc078c97a568.title: Soil-transmitted helminthiasis
fc078c97a568.sentence: They hatch in soil, releasing mobile larvae that can penetrate the skin.

e45dec44cc8a.title: Soil-transmitted helminthiasis
e45dec44cc8a.sentence: Its main cause, like for many types of helminth infections, is lack of sanitation, such as the practice of open defecation, lack of hygiene such as hand washing and walking barefoot on contaminated soil.

2a496ad544d1.title: Soil-transmitted helminthiasis
2a496ad544d1.sentence: Therefore, the disease is most prevalent in warm and moist climates where sanitation and hygiene are poor and waters are unsafe, including the temperate zones during warmer months.

10f182d6fea1.title: Soil-transmitted helminthiasis
10f182d6fea1.sentence: It is the leading cause of anaemia and protein deficiency in developing nations, affecting an estimated 740 million people.

d2c83cf4f8a5.title: Soil-transmitted helminthiasis
d2c83cf4f8a5.sentence: Although periodic deworming reduces intestinal worm burden, reinfection can occur when people remain exposed to contaminated environments.

607f78395cb1.title: Soil-transmitted helminthiasis
607f78395cb1.sentence: A systematic review and meta-analysis found that access to improved water, sanitation and hygiene was associated with lower odds of soil-transmitted helminth infection, which support the importance of environmental and behavioural interventions alongside anthelmintic treatment.

5a29b1f32a3c.title: Keshan disease
5a29b1f32a3c.sentence: Keshan disease is a congestive cardiomyopathy caused by a combination of dietary deficiency of selenium and the presence of a mutated strain of Coxsackievirus, named after Keshan County of Heilongjiang province, Northeast China, where symptoms were first noted.

512f103bc880.title: Keshan disease
512f103bc880.sentence: These symptoms were later found prevalent in a wide belt extending from northeast to southwest China, all due to selenium-deficient soil.

a04c3c0d3fc8.title: Keshan disease
a04c3c0d3fc8.sentence: The disease peaked in 1960–1970, killing thousands of people.

ce36e8cfe93f.title: Keshan disease
ce36e8cfe93f.sentence: Current research suggests that the lack of selenium results in a more virulent strain of the coxsackievirus becoming the dominant viral species present in the population of virus, but the mechanism of this selection event is unclear.

9876d0c7ac56.title: Keshan disease
9876d0c7ac56.sentence: Over decades, supplementation with selenium reduced this condition.

5290ff44fa29.title: Keshan disease
5290ff44fa29.sentence: Individuals in China with the disease treat it with a herb called Astragalus, which accumulates selenium from the soil.

71b29ce97dac.title: Keshan disease
71b29ce97dac.sentence: Garlic, onions, mushroom, broccoli, tomatoes, radishes, and Swiss chard may be good sources of selenium if the soil in which they are grown contains it.

93a7e37d5339.title: One Health
93a7e37d5339.sentence: > "One Health is an integrated, unifying approach that aims to sustainably balance and optimize the health of humans, animals, plants and ecosystems.

ba4fe278128c.title: One Health
ba4fe278128c.sentence: It recognizes the health of humans, domestic and wild animals, plants and the wider environment (including ecosystems) are closely linked and interdependent.

f36e34aeab7c.title: One Health
f36e34aeab7c.sentence: It developed in response to evidence of the spreading of zoonotic diseases between species and increasing awareness of "the interdependence of human and animal health and ecological change".

c2456436d18c.title: One Health
c2456436d18c.sentence: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is widely recognized as a major global public health threat and is commonly addressed through a One Health framework, as resistant microorganisms and antimicrobial residues can circulate among humans, animals, plants, and the environment.

b642d491dc07.title: One Health
b642d491dc07.sentence: The use and misuse of antimicrobials in human medicine, veterinary care, and agriculture contribute to the selection of resistant organisms, while environmental pathways such as wastewater, soil, and agricultural runoff facilitate their spread.

565e5db291c3.title: One Health
565e5db291c3.sentence: - The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO),

758fc38569a0.title: One Health
758fc38569a0.sentence: - The World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH, formerly OIE),

9339b6178aa5.title: One Health
9339b6178aa5.sentence: - and the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP)), and others.

49189f3c3d9b.title: Podoconiosis
