49189f3c3d9b.sentence: Podoconiosis, also known as nonfilarial elephantiasis, is a disease of the lymphatic vessels of the lower extremities that is caused by chronic exposure to irritant soils.

26503f7bfdf4.title: Podoconiosis
26503f7bfdf4.sentence: It is the second most common cause of tropical lymphedema after lymphatic filariasis, and it is characterized by prominent swelling of the lower extremities, which leads to disfigurement and disability.

4302dd064aa8.title: Podoconiosis
4302dd064aa8.sentence: Podoconiosis has been seen to occur in patients who are genetically susceptible and come into chronic contact with red clay soil.

031e07d604c7.title: Podoconiosis
031e07d604c7.sentence: The disease is primarily seen in the rural highlands due to the formation of the irritant soil requiring 1500mm of rainfall at 1500m altitude.

303541ce5039.title: Podoconiosis
303541ce5039.sentence: The red nature of the soil is related to the alkelic volcanic bedrock the soil sits on, further explaining the geographic preference of the disease.

e115ade75c82.title: Podoconiosis
e115ade75c82.sentence: The study found that those regions with podoconiosis were highly enriched with kaolinite and gibbsite due to leeching from the volcanic bedrock.

c4d91b7edbd0.title: Podoconiosis
c4d91b7edbd0.sentence: Though no singluar component of the soil has been proven to be the inciting factor, current suspects are kaolinite, smectite, micas, quartz, iron oxides, and trace elements.

8dd017b5174f.title: Podoconiosis
8dd017b5174f.sentence: In susceptible individuals, irritant soil particles penetrate the feet, interact with macrophages, and collect in regional lymph nodes and lymphatic vessels.

539745b832ab.title: Podoconiosis
539745b832ab.sentence: Over time, chronic inflammation within the lymphatic vessels leads to fibrosis and occlusion.

60cfdb89ab67.title: Podoconiosis
60cfdb89ab67.sentence: Ernest W Price, a British surgeon living in Ethiopia, discovered the true etiology of podoconiosis in the 1970s and 1980s by studying the lymph nodes and vessels of those afflicted with the disease.

8c50c8e2655b.title: Podoconiosis
8c50c8e2655b.sentence: After examining the same tissue using electron microscopy, he could identify the presence of silicon, aluminum, and other soil metals both in the phagosomes of macrophages and adhered to the surface of lymphocytes.

835d20fc0849.title: Podoconiosis
835d20fc0849.sentence: Podoconiosis is most commonly seen in higher altitude areas with volcanic soil, and it is estimated to affect 4 million people worldwide.

5fdcbb4ad748.title: Podoconiosis
5fdcbb4ad748.sentence: The amount of people affected in Ethiopia is 1.5 million, "40 000 in Cameroon, 9000 in Kenya and 7000 in Rwanda".

963810037175.title: Podoconiosis
963810037175.sentence: Methods of prevention include wearing shoes and using floor coverings.

7d5a67e2a339.title: Podoconiosis
7d5a67e2a339.sentence: In 2011, podoconiosis was added to the World Health Organization's neglected tropical diseases list, which was an important milestone in raising global awareness of the condition.

2a8ecc421b45.title: Geophagia
2a8ecc421b45.sentence: Many species of South American parrots have been observed at clay licks, and sulphur-crested cockatoos have been observed ingesting clays in Papua New Guinea.

fe5de248d7ab.title: Geophagia
fe5de248d7ab.sentence: Analysis of soils consumed by wild birds show that they often prefer soils with high clay content, usually with the smectite clay families being well represented.

82b6f25c3b59.title: Geophagia
82b6f25c3b59.sentence: For example, Peruvian Amazon rainforest parrots congregate not just at one particular bend of the Manu River but at one specific layer of soil which runs hundreds of metres horizontally along that bend.

a0a1400d367a.title: Geophagia
a0a1400d367a.sentence: The parrots avoid eating the substrate in layers one metre above or below the preferred layer.

7e1af920f5de.title: Geophagia
7e1af920f5de.sentence: Their preferred soils have a much higher cation-exchange capacity than the adjacent, rejected layers of soils because they are rich in the minerals smectite, kaolin, and mica.

bffc2a5bc3e8.title: Geophagia
bffc2a5bc3e8.sentence: Because many of these chemicals become positively charged in the acidic stomach, they bind to clay minerals which have negatively charged cation-exchange sites, and are thereby rendered safe.

52e82cbd08d9.title: Geophagia
52e82cbd08d9.sentence: Repeated studies have shown that the soils consumed most commonly by parrots in South America have higher sodium contents than those that are not consumed.

bfa8109db39b.title: Geophagia
bfa8109db39b.sentence: Researchers Lee et al. show that parrot geophagy in South America is positively correlated to a significant degree with distance from the ocean.

dd66db77588a.title: Geophagia
dd66db77588a.sentence: This work, coupled with the recent findings of consistently high sodium levels in consumed soils, make it highly likely that sodium is the primary driver of avian geophagy among parrots (and possibly other taxa) in the western Amazon Basin.

3910ad1c95c9.title: Geophagia
3910ad1c95c9.sentence: The hooves of livestock such as cattle and sheep collect soil and press it against vegetation of pastures on which they graze, causing ingestion for soil.

720937bfbf53.title: Geophagia
720937bfbf53.sentence: It can be observed as a function of ash content in the feces.

e2a2d261b75f.title: Geophagia
e2a2d261b75f.sentence: This is common especially in weak, poorly drained soils, which easily break apart.

1fdb08e7f974.title: Geophagia
1fdb08e7f974.sentence: In autumn and winter, wetter conditions render soil muddier and hence more transferrable.

6874b897cccd.title: Geophagia
6874b897cccd.sentence: Since the soil contains various nutrients such as iron, manganese, zinc, cobalt, copper, selenium, and iodine that herbage lacks, it contributes to nutrition of grazers.

6f31fc56999f.title: Geophagia
6f31fc56999f.sentence: In sheep, soil consumption can also cause cumulative incisor tooth wear.

5cc36c7dc3d1.title: Chronic wasting disease
5cc36c7dc3d1.sentence: Chronic wasting disease (CWD), is a transmissible spongiform encephalopathy (TSE) naturally affecting members of the deer family.

d83a2c25aa67.title: Chronic wasting disease
d83a2c25aa67.sentence: TSEs are a family of diseases caused by misfolded proteins called prions and include similar diseases such as mad cow disease in cattle, Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease in humans, and scrapie in sheep.

4b0cddaacb9c.title: Chronic wasting disease
4b0cddaacb9c.sentence: How the prions that cause CWD spread is unknown, but recent research indicates that prions can be excreted by deer and elk, and are transmitted by eating grass growing in contaminated soil.

1ccef72007eb.title: Chronic wasting disease
1ccef72007eb.sentence: Once in the environment, CWD prions may remain infectious for many years.

4d26f0fa2c5c.title: Chronic wasting disease
4d26f0fa2c5c.sentence: CWD prions bind so tightly to soil surface particles that the ground becomes a source of infection and may be a major route of transmission due to frequent ground contact when animals in the deer family graze.

62f87d57b4a1.title: Chronic wasting disease
62f87d57b4a1.sentence: In 2013, researchers at the National Wildlife Research Center in Fort Collins, Colorado, successfully infected white-tailed deer with the misfolded prion via the nasal passage, when the prions were mixed with clay.

e3040e7617a2.title: Chronic wasting disease
e3040e7617a2.sentence: This was important because the prions had already been shown by 2006 to bind with sandy quartz clay minerals.

7e0b2ccd7525.title: Chronic wasting disease
7e0b2ccd7525.sentence: The Canadian Food Inspection Agency ordered the cull, as well as the decontamination of 25 centimetres (9.8 in) of soil in certain places on the 400-hectare (990-acre) operation.

a568b844b169.title: Chronic wasting disease
a568b844b169.sentence: In 1967, CWD was first identified in mule deer at a government research facility in northern Colorado, United States.

1bac4a81e55f.title: Mycobacterium vaccae
1bac4a81e55f.sentence: Mycobacterium vaccae is a nonpathogenic species of the Mycobacteriaceae family of bacteria that lives naturally in soil.

424e88ee6b16.title: Mycobacterium vaccae
424e88ee6b16.sentence: Mycobacterium vaccae was first isolated from the Ugandan Lang'o District, where locals claimed that a "muddy substance had the power to cure a number of ailments".

6ab422b2a1ce.title: Mycobacterium vaccae
6ab422b2a1ce.sentence: Its name originates from the Latin word, vacca (cow), since the first Mycobacterium strain was cultured from cow dung in Austria.

c09f6ea53567.title: Mycobacterium vaccae
c09f6ea53567.sentence: A research group at Henry Wellcome Laboratories for Integrative Neuroscience and Endocrinology, University of Bristol, Bristol, England, UK has shown that heat-killed Mycobacterium vaccae injected into mice stimulated a newly discovered group of neurons, increased levels of serotonin and decreased levels of anxiety.

bff17f4070ea.title: Mycobacterium vaccae
bff17f4070ea.sentence: "Mice that were fed live M. vaccae navigated the maze twice as fast and with less demonstrated anxiety behaviors as control mice", according to Dorothy Matthews, who conducted the research with Susan Jenks at the Sage Colleges, Troy, New York, USA.

4f4a8c1868ac.title: Mycobacterium vaccae
4f4a8c1868ac.sentence: Research areas being pursued with regard to killed Mycobacterium vaccae vaccine include immunotherapy for allergic asthma, cancer, depression, leprosy, psoriasis, dermatitis, eczema and tuberculosis.

986429ca2bf0.title: Itai-itai disease
986429ca2bf0.sentence: The cadmium pollution had also contaminated many of the agricultural areas surrounding the mine.

2681b8beb052.title: Itai-itai disease
2681b8beb052.sentence: Following the trial victory of the plaintiffs over the Mitsui Mining Co in 1972, Mitsui Mining agreed to begin the process of remediation for the mine, as well as the surrounding farmland and river region.

50c926cbaf6b.title: Itai-itai disease
50c926cbaf6b.sentence: As a response to the metal pollution, the Japanese government enacted the Prevention of Soil Contamination in Agricultural Land Law of 1970.

a2ebfedc8db3.title: Itai-itai disease
a2ebfedc8db3.sentence: It ordered planting to be stopped so that restoration of the soil could be implemented in areas with 1ppm of cadmium or more in the soil.

e9f5063c410b.title: Itai-itai disease
e9f5063c410b.sentence: Surveying in Toyama Prefecture began in 1971, and by 1977, 1,500 hectares (3,700 acres) along the Jinzū River were designated for soil restoration.

a675feed7c03.title: Itai-itai disease
a675feed7c03.sentence: On 17 March 2012, officials concluded the cleanup project of the cadmium-polluted areas in the Jinzū River basin.

79050a93f129.title: Itai-itai disease
79050a93f129.sentence: 863 hectares (2,130 acres) of topsoil had been replaced since the cleanup began in 1979 at a total cost of ¥40.7 billion.

1f10addbf870.title: Itai-itai disease
1f10addbf870.sentence: In 1996, the mean concentration of cadmium in agricultural lands had returned to the background level of 0.1 ppb, signifying trivial cadmium outflow.

7ad7f2722292.title: Biofortification
7ad7f2722292.sentence: Biofortification is the practice of breeding crops to increase their nutritional value.

3f41889efb18.title: Biofortification
3f41889efb18.sentence: This can be done either through conventional selective breeding, or through genetic engineering.

5148e01f99ff.title: Biofortification
5148e01f99ff.sentence: Biofortification differs from ordinary fortification because it focuses on making plant foods more nutritious as the plants are growing, rather than having nutrients added to the foods when they are being processed.

9ded140f9659.title: Biofortification
9ded140f9659.sentence: Biofortification is seen as an upcoming strategy for dealing with deficiencies of micronutrients in low and middle-income countries.

fa5d4473fbf6.title: Biofortification
fa5d4473fbf6.sentence: Deficiencies of various micronutrients, including vitamin A, zinc, and iron are common in low and middle-income countries and affect billions of people.

24f24385ec73.title: Biofortification
24f24385ec73.sentence: This is an important improvement on ordinary fortification when it comes to providing nutrients for the rural poor, who rarely have access to commercially fortified foods.

c1e44b2b902b.title: Biofortification
c1e44b2b902b.sentence: As such, increasing the micronutrient levels in staple crops can help prevent and reduce the micronutrient deficiencies – in one trial in Mozambique, eating sweet potatoes biofortified with beta-carotene reduced the incidence of vitamin A deficiency in children by 24%.

a2d4517768c1.title: Biofortification
a2d4517768c1.sentence: In two separate randomized clinical trials in India, eating iron- and zinc- biofortified pearl millet was found to improve iron status among school-aged children and was found to improve hemoglobin concentrations in younger male children, and in children ages 12–18 months who were iron-deficient at baseline.

99646c20575f.title: Biofortification
99646c20575f.sentence: Researchers at the University of Warwick have been looking for ways to boost the low selenium levels in British grains, and have been working to help develop a grain to be used in making bread biofortified with selenium.

ce095dc1b481.title: Biofortification
ce095dc1b481.sentence: Some have criticized biofortification programs because they may encourage "further simplification of human diets and food systems", because "[biofortification is] a strategy that aims to concentrate more nutrients in few staple foods [which] may contribute to further simplifying diets already overly dependent on a few carbohydrate staples." This may seem irresponsible, as lack of access to a diverse and balanced diet is the major cause of malnutrition.

c4016b9baeb3.title: Biofortification
c4016b9baeb3.sentence: As a result these critics urge caution, and the use of biofortification as part of a larger strategy involving diversification of foods in low and middle-income countries.

776dd195f123.title: Hygiene hypothesis
776dd195f123.sentence: In medicine, the hygiene hypothesis states that early childhood exposure to particular microorganisms (such as the gut flora and helminth parasites) protects against allergies by properly tuning the immune system.

45d2c62d574f.title: Hygiene hypothesis
45d2c62d574f.sentence: While early versions of the hypothesis referred to microorganism exposure in general, later versions apply to a specific set of microbes that have co-evolved with humans.

f392feb27b13.title: Hygiene hypothesis
f392feb27b13.sentence: In 2003, Graham Rook proposed the "old friends" hypothesis which has been described as a more rational explanation for the link between microbial exposure and inflammatory disorders.

b6698753146c.title: Hygiene hypothesis
b6698753146c.sentence: The hypothesis states that the vital microbial exposures are not colds, influenza, measles and other common childhood infections which have evolved relatively recently over the last 10,000 years, but rather the microbes already present during mammalian and human evolution, that could persist in small hunter-gatherer groups as microbiota, tolerated latent infections, or carrier states.

a70778817306.title: Hygiene hypothesis
a70778817306.sentence: - Ambient species that exist in the same environments as humans

ae2bc33ec866.title: Hygiene hypothesis
ae2bc33ec866.sentence: "Evolution turns the inevitable into a necessity." This means that the majority of mammalian evolution took place in mud and rotting vegetation and more than 90 percent of human evolution took place in isolated hunter-gatherer communities and farming communities.

c36af3d0a82c.title: Hygiene hypothesis
c36af3d0a82c.sentence: There is a significant amount of evidence supporting the idea that lack of exposure to these microbes is linked to allergies or other conditions, although it is still rejected by many scientists.

4ae4bfa8d7a6.title: Hygiene hypothesis
4ae4bfa8d7a6.sentence: The hygiene hypothesis has difficulty explaining why allergic diseases also occur in less affluent regions.

43a8ff7f5a39.title: Hygiene hypothesis
43a8ff7f5a39.sentence: The term "hygiene hypothesis" has been described as a misnomer because people incorrectly interpret it as referring to their own cleanliness.

70d2b4f96d25.title: Hygiene hypothesis
70d2b4f96d25.sentence: Having worse personal hygiene, such as not washing hands before eating, only increases the risk of infection without affecting the risk of allergies or immune disorders.

673c33681fad.title: Photosynthesis
673c33681fad.sentence: Photosynthesis is a system of biological processes by which photopigment-bearing autotrophic organisms, such as most plants, algae and cyanobacteria, convert light energy—typically from sunlight—into the chemical energy necessary to fuel their metabolism.

b9e87269b5ee.title: Photosynthesis
b9e87269b5ee.sentence: The term photosynthesis usually refers to oxygenic photosynthesis, a process that releases oxygen as a byproduct of water splitting.

632d3708a515.title: Photosynthesis
632d3708a515.sentence: Photosynthetic organisms store the converted chemical energy within the bonds of intracellular organic compounds (complex compounds containing carbon), typically carbohydrates like sugars (mainly glucose, fructose and sucrose), starches, phytoglycogen and cellulose.

1b3dc2925def.title: Photosynthesis
1b3dc2925def.sentence: When needing to use this stored energy, an organism's cells then metabolize the organic compounds through cellular respiration.

1ff4222e9622.title: Photosynthesis
1ff4222e9622.sentence: In plants, these pigments are chlorophylls (a porphyrin derivative that absorbs the red and blue spectra of light, thus reflecting green) held inside chloroplasts, abundant in leaf cells.

cd3172f4b1d3.title: Photosynthesis
cd3172f4b1d3.sentence: In these light-dependent reactions, some energy is used to strip electrons from suitable substances, such as water, producing oxygen gas.

3a18a6cf66c5.title: Photosynthesis
3a18a6cf66c5.sentence: The hydrogen freed by the splitting of water is used in the creation of two important molecules that participate in energetic processes: reduced nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NADPH) and ATP.

04e362d830ae.title: Photosynthesis
04e362d830ae.sentence: In plants, algae, and cyanobacteria, sugars are synthesized by a subsequent sequence of light-independent reactions called the Calvin cycle.

62e03bbefa8f.title: Photosynthesis
62e03bbefa8f.sentence: In this process, atmospheric carbon dioxide is incorporated into already existing organic compounds, such as ribulose bisphosphate (RuBP).

75f9dcf678d1.title: Photosynthesis
75f9dcf678d1.sentence: Photosynthesis plays a critical role in producing and maintaining the oxygen content of the Earth's atmosphere, and it supplies most of the biological energy necessary for complex life on Earth.

6d22f4ca47f9.title: Photosynthesis
6d22f4ca47f9.sentence: The average rate of energy captured by global photosynthesis is approximately 130 terawatts, which is about eight times the total power consumption of human civilization.

2c5a4f039c5b.title: Photosynthesis
2c5a4f039c5b.sentence: Photosynthetic organisms also convert around 100–115 billion tons (91–104 Pg petagrams, or billions of metric tons), of carbon into biomass per year.

70638cfad21e.title: Photosynthesis
70638cfad21e.sentence: Plants usually convert light into chemical energy with a photosynthetic efficiency of 3–6%.

7d5c580e6d65.title: Photosynthesis
7d5c580e6d65.sentence: Actual plants' photosynthetic efficiency varies with the frequency of the light being converted, light intensity, temperature, and proportion of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere, and can vary from 0.1% to 8%.

8d2391f46462.title: Photosynthesis
8d2391f46462.sentence: Photosynthesis was discovered in 1779 by Jan Ingenhousz who showed that plants need light, not just soil and water.

09995680225b.title: Geochronology
09995680225b.sentence: Geochronology is the science of determining the age of rocks, fossils, and sediments using signatures inherent in the rocks themselves.

565a34e55262.title: Geochronology
565a34e55262.sentence: Absolute geochronology can be accomplished through radioactive isotopes, whereas relative geochronology is provided by tools such as paleomagnetism and stable isotope ratios.

d22aa702a7e7.title: Geochronology
d22aa702a7e7.sentence: By combining multiple geochronological (and biostratigraphic) indicators the precision of the recovered age can be improved.

71b49f562ca6.title: Geochronology
71b49f562ca6.sentence: By measuring the amount of radioactive decay of a radioactive isotope with a known half-life, geologists can establish the absolute age of the parent material.

2390b94b2ae9.title: Geochronology
2390b94b2ae9.sentence: More slowly decaying isotopes are useful for longer periods of time, but less accurate in absolute years.

ea8c1edc64dd.title: Geochronology
ea8c1edc64dd.sentence: This technique measures the decay of carbon-14 in organic material and can be best applied to samples younger than about 60,000 years.

6737da8be9b8.title: Geochronology
6737da8be9b8.sentence: Uranium–lead dating is applied to samples older than about 1 million years.

d974d0e22c63.title: Geochronology
d974d0e22c63.sentence: This technique is used to date speleothems, corals, carbonates, and fossil bones.

03b200437ce5.title: Geochronology
03b200437ce5.sentence: Its range is from a few years to about 700,000 years.

daa9c48178c9.title: Geochronology
daa9c48178c9.section: Dating methods > Correlation of marker horizons
daa9c48178c9.sentence: Marker horizons are stratigraphic units of the same age and of such distinctive composition and appearance that, despite their presence in different geographic sites, there is certainty about their age-equivalence.

fd155eedd580.title: Geochronology
fd155eedd580.section: Dating methods > Correlation of marker horizons
fd155eedd580.sentence: Tephrochronology is a method for geochemical correlation of unknown volcanic ash (tephra) to geochemically fingerprinted, dated tephra.

3cb2a0fd1e11.title: Geochronology
3cb2a0fd1e11.sentence: Incremental dating techniques allow the construction of year-by-year annual chronologies, which can be fixed (i.e. linked to the present day and thus calendar or sidereal time) or floating.

e5df1ab23e48.title: Geochronology
e5df1ab23e48.sentence: Amino acid dating cannot produce numerical age estimates on its own, requiring site-specific calibration from other dating methods, but it is relatively cheap.

0a8d0996e29d.title: Radiocarbon dating
0a8d0996e29d.sentence: Radiocarbon dating (also referred to as carbon dating or carbon-14 dating) is a method for determining the age of an object containing organic material by using the properties of radiocarbon, a radioactive isotope of carbon.

9cd96c08ae0b.title: Radiocarbon dating
9cd96c08ae0b.sentence: It is based on the fact that radiocarbon (14 C) is constantly being created in the Earth's atmosphere by the interaction of cosmic rays with atmospheric nitrogen.

fd8fe44c4b8a.title: Radiocarbon dating
fd8fe44c4b8a.sentence: The resulting 14 C combines with atmospheric oxygen to form radioactive carbon dioxide, which is incorporated into plants by photosynthesis; animals then acquire 14 C by eating the plants.

6b7060879814.title: Radiocarbon dating
6b7060879814.sentence: When the animal or plant dies, it stops exchanging carbon with its environment, and thereafter the amount of 14 C it contains begins to decrease as the 14 C undergoes radioactive decay.

70a2e29f182e.title: Radiocarbon dating
70a2e29f182e.sentence: The older a sample is, the less 14 C there is to be detected.

663e77012302.title: Radiocarbon dating
663e77012302.sentence: The half-life of 14 C (the period of time after which half of a given sample will have decayed) is about 5,730 years, so the oldest dates that can be reliably measured by this process date to approximately 50,000 years ago, although special preparation methods occasionally make an accurate analysis of older samples possible.

2153ca905fa1.title: Radiocarbon dating
2153ca905fa1.sentence: The method was developed in the late 1940s at the University of Chicago by Willard Libby.

a4c816021c79.title: Radiocarbon dating
a4c816021c79.sentence: Libby received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for his work in 1960.

face2a4754a3.title: Radiocarbon dating
face2a4754a3.sentence: Other corrections must be made to account for the proportion of 14 C in different types of organisms (fractionation), and the varying levels of 14 C throughout the biosphere (reservoir effects).

83241ddb0c9b.title: Radiocarbon dating
83241ddb0c9b.sentence: Additional complications come from the burning of fossil fuels, such as coal and oil, and from the above-ground nuclear tests done in the 1950s and 1960s.

2ede82c1d242.title: Radiocarbon dating
2ede82c1d242.sentence: More recently, accelerator mass spectrometry has become the method of choice; it counts all the 14 C atoms in the sample and not just the few that happen to decay during the measurements; it can therefore be used with much smaller samples (as small as individual plant seeds), and gives results much more quickly.

b3d78b74c10e.title: Radiocarbon dating
b3d78b74c10e.sentence: If a sample that is 17,000 years old is contaminated so that 1% of the sample is modern carbon, it will appear to be 600 years younger; for a sample that is 34,000 years old, the same amount of contamination would cause an error of 4,000 years.

b65db7070a55.title: Radiocarbon dating
b65db7070a55.sentence: Contamination with old carbon, with no remaining 14 C, causes an error in the other direction independent of age – a sample contaminated with 1% old carbon will appear to be about 80 years older than it truly is, regardless of the date of the sample.

22b132ee8279.title: Radiocarbon dating
22b132ee8279.sentence: The development of radiocarbon dating has had a profound impact on archaeology.

a3504c965bc8.title: Radiocarbon dating
a3504c965bc8.sentence: Histories of archaeology often refer to its impact as the "radiocarbon revolution".

5b28ae321711.title: Radiocarbon dating
5b28ae321711.sentence: These results were published in Science in December 1949.

0b0d9a4a8052.title: Palynology
0b0d9a4a8052.sentence: Palynology is the study of microorganisms and microscopic fragments of macroorganisms that are composed of acid-resistant organic material and occur in sediments, sedimentary rocks, and even some metasedimentary rocks.

3c55c8342c31.title: Palynology
3c55c8342c31.sentence: Palynomorphs are broadly defined as organic remains, including microfossils, and microscopic fragments of macroorganisms that are composed of acid-resistant organic material and range in size between 5 and 500 micrometres.

5b964046d235.title: Palynology
5b964046d235.sentence: Typical palynomorphs include dinoflagellate cysts, acritarchs, spores, pollen, plant tissue, fungi, scolecodonts (scleroprotein teeth, jaws, and associated features of polychaete annelid worms), arthropod organs (such as insect mouthparts), and chitinozoans.

aee0c234c6a5.title: Palynology
aee0c234c6a5.sentence: They are extracted from soils, sedimentary rocks and sediment cores, and other materials by a combination of physical (ultrasonic treatment and wet sieving) and chemical (acid digestion) procedures to remove the non-organic fraction.

34475974ef16.title: Palynology
34475974ef16.section: Methods of studying palynomorphs > Chemical preparation
34475974ef16.sentence: Initially the only chemical treatment used by researchers was treatment with potassium hydroxide (KOH) to remove humic substances; defloculation was accomplished through surface treatment or ultra-sonic treatment, although sonification may cause the pollen exine to rupture.

bc6330ad852d.title: Palynology
bc6330ad852d.section: Methods of studying palynomorphs > Chemical preparation
bc6330ad852d.sentence: In 1924, the use of hydrofluoric acid (HF) to digest silicate minerals was introduced by Assarson and Granlund, greatly reducing the amount of time required to scan slides for palynomorphs.

fbeca74d0dfc.title: Palynology
fbeca74d0dfc.section: Methods of studying palynomorphs > Chemical preparation
fbeca74d0dfc.sentence: Palynological studies using peats presented a particular challenge because of the presence of well-preserved organic material, including fine rootlets, moss leaflets and organic litter.

00da95697811.title: Palynology
00da95697811.section: Methods of studying palynomorphs > Chemical preparation
00da95697811.sentence: Acetolysis was developed by Gunnar Erdtman and his brother to remove these fine cellulose materials by dissolving them.

e3bc3132df4b.title: Palynology
e3bc3132df4b.sentence: Quantitative analysis of pollen began with Lennart von Post's published work.

9e4607ae384f.title: Palynology
9e4607ae384f.sentence: In particular, his Kristiania lecture of 1916 was important in gaining a wider audience.

55cb81dc9018.title: Palynology
55cb81dc9018.sentence: When the slides are observed under a microscope, the researcher counts the number of grains of each pollen taxon.

d4e6ebe5c82b.title: Palynology
d4e6ebe5c82b.sentence: This record is next used to produce a pollen diagram.

9c21bf46512a.title: Palynology
9c21bf46512a.sentence: This was the introduction of pollen analysis in North America; pollen diagrams today still often remain in the same format with depth on the y-axis and abundances of species on the x-axis.

2fa632eac618.title: Palynology
2fa632eac618.sentence: Researchers will often study either modern samples from a number of unique sites within a given area, or samples from a single site with a record through time, such as samples obtained from peat or lake sediments.

5415a25f1466.title: Palynology
5415a25f1466.sentence: Palynology can be used to reconstruct past vegetation (land plants) and marine and Freshwater phytoplankton communities, and so infer past environmental (palaeoenvironmental) and palaeoclimatic conditions in an area thousands or millions of years ago, a fundamental part of research into climate change.

1dfbf529f086.title: Palynology
1dfbf529f086.sentence: These data can be used to detect anthropogenic effects, such as logging, traditional patterns of land use or long term changes in regional climate

a002b779775e.title: Palynology
a002b779775e.sentence: Palynology can be applied to problems in many scientific disciplines including geology, botany, paleontology, archaeology, pedology (soil study), and physical geography:

9e142d4ebc86.title: Palynology
9e142d4ebc86.sentence: Geologists use palynological studies in biostratigraphy to correlate strata and determine the relative age of a given bed, horizon, formation or stratigraphical sequence.

dfb7067a1567.title: Luminescence dating
dfb7067a1567.sentence: Luminescence dating refers to a group of chronological dating methods of determining how long ago mineral grains were last exposed to sunlight or sufficient heating.

5aaa97252a2a.title: Luminescence dating
5aaa97252a2a.sentence: Background ionizing radiation around the minerals—for instance quartz or potassium feldspar—buried in the ground causes charge to build up within the minerals.

c90fd4fe0fbb.title: Luminescence dating
c90fd4fe0fbb.sentence: The sources of this natural radiation are cosmic rays and trace amounts of radioactive isotopes of elements such as potassium, uranium, thorium, and rubidium.

1d4638521d17.title: Luminescence dating
1d4638521d17.sentence: Exposure to light causes the charge to quickly decay and produce light; however, if these mineral grains are stimulated using either light (blue or green for OSL; infrared for IRSL) or heat (for TL), a luminescence signal is emitted as the stored electron energy is released, the intensity of which varies depending on the duration of burial (and hence radiation absorbed) and specific properties of the mineral.

03673fbb3643.title: Luminescence dating
03673fbb3643.sentence: Most luminescence dating methods rely on the assumption that the mineral grains were sufficiently exposed to light or "bleached" at the time of the event being dated.

6901d824cfa7.title: Luminescence dating
6901d824cfa7.sentence: For example, in quartz a short daylight exposure in the range of 1–100 s before burial is sufficient to effectively "reset" the OSL dating clock.

e2cfa56d6377.title: Luminescence dating
e2cfa56d6377.sentence: This is usually, but not always, the case with aeolian deposits, such as sand dunes and loess, and some water-laid deposits.

21248a180785.title: Luminescence dating
21248a180785.sentence: Luminescence dating is one of several techniques in which an age is calculated as follows:

74abd5e8722b.title: Luminescence dating
74abd5e8722b.sentence: Where A is the age, typically given in years or thousand years (ka, ky, kyr), De the equivalent dose in Gy (Gray) and D˙ in Gy ka−1 the environmental dose rate.

01e0ec345d8e.title: Luminescence dating
01e0ec345d8e.sentence: The dose rate is usually in the range of 0.5 - 5 Gy/1000 years.

bb5b5bf272b6.title: Luminescence dating
bb5b5bf272b6.sentence: Single Quartz OSL ages can be determined typically from 100 to 350,000 years BP, and can be reliable when suitable methods are used and proper checks are done.

9350a3117aff.title: Luminescence dating
9350a3117aff.sentence: The uncertainty of an OSL date is typically 5-10% of the age of the sample.

fc592d5ff151.title: Luminescence dating
fc592d5ff151.sentence: Feldspar IRSL techniques have the potential to extend the datable range out to a million years as feldspars typically have significantly higher dose saturation levels than quartz, though issues regarding anomalous fading will need to be dealt with first.

43b5d7b0af3f.title: Luminescence dating
43b5d7b0af3f.sentence: Unlike 14C dating, luminescence dating methods do not require a contemporary organic component of the sediment to be dated; just quartz, potassium feldspar, or certain other mineral grains that have been fully bleached during the event being dated.

9adc04748f36.title: Luminescence dating
9adc04748f36.sentence: These methods also do not suffer from overestimation of dates when the sediment in question has been mixed with "old carbon", or 14 C-deficient carbon that is not the same isotopic ratio as the atmosphere.

92913c2076e9.title: Luminescence dating
92913c2076e9.sentence: In a study of the chronology of arid-zone lacustrine sediments from Lake Ulaan in southern Mongolia, Lee et al. discovered that OSL and radiocarbon dates agreed in some samples, but the radiocarbon dates were up to 5800 years older in others.

c9ac350f758a.title: Luminescence dating
c9ac350f758a.sentence: Westerly winds delivered an influx of 14 C-deficient carbon from adjacent soils and Paleozoic carbonate rocks, a process that is also active today.

feb600d133e0.title: Luminescence dating
feb600d133e0.sentence: However, the wind-blown origin of these sediments were ideal for OSL dating, as most of the grains would have been completely bleached by sunlight exposure during transport and burial.

e8459abf58c8.title: Luminescence dating
e8459abf58c8.sentence: In 1963, Aitken et al. noted that TL traps in calcite could be bleached by sunlight as well as heat, and in 1965 Shelkoplyas and Morozov were the first to use TL to date unheated sediments.

046415185944.title: Luminescence dating
046415185944.sentence: Optical dating using optically stimulated luminescence (OSL) was developed in 1984 by David J. Huntley and colleagues.

840819b6e3f0.title: Luminescence dating
840819b6e3f0.sentence: The concept of using luminescence dating in archaeological contexts was first suggested in 1953 by Farrington Daniels, Charles A. Boyd, and Donald F. Saunders, who thought the thermoluminescence response of pottery shards could date the last incidence of heating.

b461f6e35895.title: Cosmogenic nuclide
b461f6e35895.sentence: Cosmogenic nuclides (or cosmogenic isotopes) are rare nuclides (isotopes) created when a high-energy cosmic ray interacts with the nucleus of an in situ Solar System atom, causing nucleons (protons and neutrons) to be expelled from the atom (see cosmic ray spallation).

0e97f535424d.title: Cosmogenic nuclide
0e97f535424d.sentence: These nuclides are produced within Earth materials such as rocks or soil, in Earth's atmosphere, and in extraterrestrial items such as meteoroids.

87d698b614bc.title: Cosmogenic nuclide
87d698b614bc.sentence: These nuclides all share the common feature of being absent in the host material at the time of formation.

16d9feaa9706.title: Cosmogenic nuclide
16d9feaa9706.section: Cosmogenic nuclides > Applications in geology listed by isotope
16d9feaa9706.sentence: beryllium | 10 | 1,387,000 | exposure dating of rocks, soils, ice cores

4bc4ac9729b1.title: Cosmogenic nuclide
4bc4ac9729b1.section: Cosmogenic nuclides > Applications in geology listed by isotope
4bc4ac9729b1.sentence: aluminium | 26 | 720,000 | exposure dating of rocks, sediment

a7b42499ee9e.title: Cosmogenic nuclide
a7b42499ee9e.section: Cosmogenic nuclides > Applications in geology listed by isotope
a7b42499ee9e.sentence: chlorine | 36 | 308,000 | exposure dating of rocks, groundwater tracer

eddc0cdcf121.title: Surface exposure dating
eddc0cdcf121.sentence: In rock and other materials of similar density, most of the cosmic ray flux is absorbed within the first meter of exposed material in reactions that produce new isotopes called cosmogenic nuclides.

9cf1fadee534.title: Cosmogenic nuclide
9cf1fadee534.sentence: - cosmic ray spallation, which is the most common reaction on the near-surface (typically 0 to 60 cm below) the Earth and can create secondary particles which can cause additional reaction upon interaction with another nuclei called a collision cascade.

37a377ea7512.title: Cosmogenic nuclide
37a377ea7512.sentence: - muon capture, which pervades at depths a few meters below the subsurface because muons are inherently less reactive; in some cases, high-energy muons can reach greater depths

399878d42919.title: Cosmogenic nuclide
399878d42919.sentence: - neutron capture, which due to the neutron's low energy are captured into a nucleus, most commonly by water, but this process is highly dependent on snow, soil moisture and trace element concentrations.

da8d146bb4ac.title: Cosmogenic nuclide
da8d146bb4ac.section: Use in geochronology > Corrections for cosmic-ray fluxes
da8d146bb4ac.sentence: Atmospheric pressure, for example, which varies with altitude, can change the production rate of nuclides within minerals by a factor of 30 between sea level and the top of a 5 km high mountain.

54a5436a05d1.title: Photosynthesis
54a5436a05d1.sentence: The first photosynthetic organisms probably evolved early in the evolutionary history of life using reducing agents such as hydrogen or hydrogen sulfide, rather than water, as sources of electrons.

3c203a60bc0a.title: Photosynthesis
3c203a60bc0a.sentence: Early photosynthetic systems, such as those in green and purple sulfur and green and purple nonsulfur bacteria, are thought to have been anoxygenic, and used various other molecules than water as electron donors.

75b7a7fd93cf.title: Photosynthesis
75b7a7fd93cf.sentence: Fossils of what are thought to be filamentous photosynthetic organisms have been dated at 3.4 billion years old.

d5ffa0f1885e.title: Photosynthesis
d5ffa0f1885e.sentence: More recent studies also suggest that photosynthesis may have begun about 3.4 billion years ago, though the first direct evidence of photosynthesis comes from thylakoid membranes preserved in 1.75-billion-year-old cherts.

0f87ca6c6ac3.title: Photosynthesis
0f87ca6c6ac3.section: Evolution > Cyanobacteria and the evolution of photosynthesis
0f87ca6c6ac3.sentence: The biochemical capacity to use water as the source for electrons in photosynthesis evolved once, in a common ancestor of extant cyanobacteria (formerly called blue-green algae).

59581d176dd9.title: Photosynthesis
59581d176dd9.section: Evolution > Cyanobacteria and the evolution of photosynthesis
59581d176dd9.sentence: The geological record indicates that this transforming event took place early in Earth's history, at least 2450–2320 million years ago (Ma), and, it is speculated, much earlier.

da60daff5ed3.title: Photosynthesis
da60daff5ed3.sentence: Cyanobacteria appeared later; the excess oxygen they produced contributed directly to the oxygenation of the Earth, which rendered the evolution of complex life possible.

95b7538b9ec3.title: Photosynthesis
95b7538b9ec3.sentence: Oxygenic photosynthesis is the main source of oxygen in the Earth's atmosphere, and its earliest appearance is sometimes referred to as the oxygen catastrophe.

47886383e050.title: Photosynthesis
47886383e050.sentence: Total photosynthesis is limited by a range of environmental factors.

83f1a429409f.title: Photosynthesis
83f1a429409f.sentence: These include the amount of light available, the amount of leaf area a plant has to capture light (shading by other plants is a major limitation of photosynthesis), the rate at which carbon dioxide can be supplied to the chloroplasts to support photosynthesis, the availability of water, and the availability of suitable temperatures for carrying out photosynthesis.

370f64d4c203.title: Photosynthesis
370f64d4c203.section: Factors > Carbon dioxide levels and photorespiration
370f64d4c203.sentence: As carbon dioxide concentrations rise, the rate at which sugars are made by the light-independent reactions increases until limited by other factors.

ee4a72ca4e8f.title: Photosynthesis
ee4a72ca4e8f.sentence: In the light-dependent reactions, one molecule of the pigment chlorophyll absorbs one photon and loses one electron.

f9f8fdcf7499.title: Photosynthesis
f9f8fdcf7499.sentence: This electron is taken up by a modified form of chlorophyll called pheophytin, which passes the electron to a quinone molecule, starting the flow of electrons down an electron transport chain that leads to the ultimate reduction of NADP to NADPH.

74eb0e7d9d10.title: Photosynthesis
74eb0e7d9d10.sentence: In addition, this creates a proton gradient (energy gradient) across the chloroplast membrane, which is used by ATP synthase in the synthesis of ATP.

92c51841658c.title: Photosynthesis
92c51841658c.sentence: The chlorophyll molecule ultimately regains the electron it lost when a water molecule is split in a process called photolysis, which releases oxygen.

e5757f7358d6.title: Photosynthesis
e5757f7358d6.sentence: In plants, light-dependent reactions occur in the thylakoid membranes of the chloroplasts where they drive the synthesis of ATP and NADPH.

eaa5dd02a395.title: Photosynthesis
eaa5dd02a395.sentence: Not all wavelengths of light can support photosynthesis.

4b9190f22dc5.title: Photosynthesis
4b9190f22dc5.sentence: For example, in green plants, the action spectrum resembles the absorption spectrum for chlorophylls and carotenoids with absorption peaks in violet-blue and red light.

d5240f8edc4b.title: Photosynthesis
d5240f8edc4b.sentence: In red algae, the action spectrum is blue-green light, which allows these algae to use the blue end of the spectrum to grow in the deeper waters that filter out the longer wavelengths (red light) used by above-ground green plants.

c2df0b36ce6b.title: Photosynthesis
c2df0b36ce6b.sentence: In the light-independent (or "dark") reactions, the enzyme RuBisCO captures CO2 from the atmosphere and, in a process called the Calvin cycle, uses the newly formed NADPH and releases three-carbon sugars, which are later combined to form sucrose and starch.

cf84e09b1647.title: Photosynthesis
cf84e09b1647.sentence: The simple carbon sugars photosynthesis produces are then used to form other organic compounds, such as the building material cellulose, the precursors for lipid and amino acid biosynthesis, or as a fuel in cellular respiration.

c951c458a6c2.title: Photosynthesis
c951c458a6c2.section: Factors > Carbon dioxide levels and photorespiration
c951c458a6c2.sentence: However, if the carbon dioxide concentration is low, RuBisCO will bind oxygen instead of carbon dioxide.

77b9aa356357.title: Photosynthesis
77b9aa356357.section: Factors > Carbon dioxide levels and photorespiration
77b9aa356357.sentence: This process, called photorespiration, uses energy, but does not produce sugars.

f35bb95225da.title: Photosynthesis
f35bb95225da.section: Factors > Carbon dioxide levels and photorespiration
f35bb95225da.sentence: - One product of oxygenase activity is phosphoglycolate (2 carbon) instead of 3-phosphoglycerate (3 carbon).

f59c5830b991.title: Photosynthesis
f59c5830b991.section: Factors > Carbon dioxide levels and photorespiration
f59c5830b991.sentence: Phosphoglycolate cannot be metabolized by the Calvin-Benson cycle and represents carbon lost from the cycle.

658a1a2ab18f.title: Photosynthesis
658a1a2ab18f.section: Factors > Carbon dioxide levels and photorespiration
658a1a2ab18f.sentence: - Phosphoglycolate is quickly metabolized to glycolate that is toxic to a plant at a high concentration; it inhibits photosynthesis.

60760fa1d55b.title: Photosynthesis
60760fa1d55b.section: Factors > Carbon dioxide levels and photorespiration
60760fa1d55b.sentence: - Salvaging glycolate is an energetically expensive process that uses the glycolate pathway, and only 75% of the carbon is returned to the Calvin-Benson cycle as 3-phosphoglycerate.

d022be2949f5.title: Photosynthesis
d022be2949f5.section: Factors > Carbon dioxide levels and photorespiration
d022be2949f5.sentence: The reactions also produce ammonia (NH3), which is able to diffuse out of the plant, leading to a loss of nitrogen.

48cdf82b48d0.title: Photosynthesis
48cdf82b48d0.section: Light-independent reactions > Carbon concentrating mechanisms > On land
48cdf82b48d0.sentence: In hot and dry conditions, plants close their stomata to prevent water loss.

8b071773cb1f.title: Photosynthesis
8b071773cb1f.section: Light-independent reactions > Carbon concentrating mechanisms > On land
8b071773cb1f.sentence: Under these conditions, CO2 will decrease and oxygen gas, produced by the light reactions of photosynthesis, will increase, causing an increase of photorespiration by the oxygenase activity of ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate carboxylase/oxygenase (RuBisCO) and decrease in carbon fixation.

e15bb1fb7b7d.title: Photosynthesis
e15bb1fb7b7d.section: Light-independent reactions > Carbon concentrating mechanisms > On land
e15bb1fb7b7d.sentence: Plants that use the C4 carbon fixation process chemically fix carbon dioxide in the cells of the mesophyll by adding it to the three-carbon molecule phosphoenolpyruvate (PEP), a reaction catalyzed by an enzyme called PEP carboxylase, creating the four-carbon organic acid oxaloacetic acid.

11769fd574b0.title: Photosynthesis
11769fd574b0.section: Light-independent reactions > Carbon concentrating mechanisms > On land
11769fd574b0.sentence: In contrast to C4 metabolism, which spatially separates the CO2 fixation to PEP from the Calvin cycle, CAM temporally separates these two processes.

1e95ad20caeb.title: Photosynthesis
1e95ad20caeb.section: Light-independent reactions > Carbon concentrating mechanisms > On land
1e95ad20caeb.sentence: Oxaloacetic acid or malate synthesized by this process is then translocated to specialized bundle sheath cells where the enzyme RuBisCO and other Calvin cycle enzymes are located, and where CO2 released by decarboxylation of the four-carbon acids is then fixed by RuBisCO activity to the three-carbon 3-phosphoglyceric acids.

c59e0b209a40.title: Photosynthesis
c59e0b209a40.section: Light-independent reactions > Carbon concentrating mechanisms > On land
c59e0b209a40.sentence: The physical separation of RuBisCO from the oxygen-generating light reactions reduces photorespiration and increases CO2 fixation and, thus, the photosynthetic capacity of the leaf.

178c18a70f53.title: Photosynthesis
178c18a70f53.section: Light-independent reactions > Carbon concentrating mechanisms > On land
178c18a70f53.sentence: C4 plants can produce more sugar than C3 plants in conditions of high light and temperature.

92558be7802d.title: Photosynthesis
92558be7802d.section: Light-independent reactions > Carbon concentrating mechanisms > On land
92558be7802d.sentence: Many important crop plants are C4 plants, including maize, sorghum, sugarcane, and millet.

203d50ed4aae.title: Photosynthesis
203d50ed4aae.section: Light-independent reactions > Carbon concentrating mechanisms > On land
203d50ed4aae.sentence: Over 90% of plants use C3 carbon fixation, compared to 3% that use C4 carbon fixation; however, the evolution of C4 in over sixty plant lineages makes it a striking example of convergent evolution.

95e10310f2c5.title: Photosynthesis
95e10310f2c5.section: Light-independent reactions > Carbon concentrating mechanisms > On land
95e10310f2c5.sentence: Xerophytes, such as cacti and most succulents, also use PEP carboxylase to capture carbon dioxide in a process called Crassulacean acid metabolism (CAM).

c9b4e777bee0.title: Photosynthesis
c9b4e777bee0.section: Light-independent reactions > Carbon concentrating mechanisms > On land
c9b4e777bee0.sentence: CAM plants have a different leaf anatomy from C3 plants, and fix the CO2 at night, when their stomata are open.

2e745f186135.title: Photosynthesis
2e745f186135.section: Light-independent reactions > Carbon concentrating mechanisms > On land
2e745f186135.sentence: CAM plants store the CO2 mostly in the form of malic acid via carboxylation of phosphoenolpyruvate to oxaloacetate, which is then reduced to malate.

15aea5dd3daf.title: Photosynthesis
15aea5dd3daf.section: Light-independent reactions > Carbon concentrating mechanisms > On land
15aea5dd3daf.sentence: Decarboxylation of malate during the day releases CO2 inside the leaves, thus allowing carbon fixation to 3-phosphoglycerate by RuBisCO.

8ec52537073f.title: Photosynthesis
8ec52537073f.section: Light-independent reactions > Carbon concentrating mechanisms > On land
8ec52537073f.sentence: CAM is used by 16,000 species of plants.

8fa4b2d9b26d.title: Δ13C
8fa4b2d9b26d.sentence: In geochemistry, paleoclimatology, archaeology, and paleoceanography, δ13C (pronounced "delta carbon thirteen") is a normalized ratio of the two stable isotopes of carbon—13C and 12C—reported in parts per thousand (per mille, ‰).

cab042bd8447.title: Δ13C
cab042bd8447.sentence: where the standard is an established reference material.

2411e02b0bd0.title: Δ13C
2411e02b0bd0.sentence: The initial reference material used to standardize carbon isotope ratios was the "Pee Dee Belemnite" (PDB)—a Cretaceous marine fossil, Belemnitella americana, originating from the Peedee Formation in South Carolina.

833814af174e.title: Δ13C
833814af174e.sentence: Due to the high demand for the PDB standard, the supply was ultimately exhausted.

87cac569212d.title: Δ13C
87cac569212d.sentence: Other standards calibrated to the same ratio, including one known as VPDB (for "Vienna PDB"), have replaced the original.

0b837531c94f.title: Δ13C
0b837531c94f.sentence: Organisms preferentially take up light 12C, and have a δ13C signature of about −25‰, depending on their metabolic pathway.

efbf5f364431.title: Δ13C
efbf5f364431.sentence: Whereas C4 plants have a δ13C of −16 to −10‰, C3 plants have a δ13C of −33 to −24‰.

43844fdc56fa.title: Δ13C
43844fdc56fa.sentence: C3 and C4 plants have different signatures, allowing the abundance of C4 grasses to be detected through time in the δ13C record.

4cdbe2b5f268.title: Δ13C
4cdbe2b5f268.sentence: For example, carbon dioxide derived from ecosystem respiration can be differentiated from carbon dioxide formed from the combustion of fossil fuels using δ13C, as the precursor materials (modern organic matter and petroleum, respectively) have different isotopic values – the basis of the "Suess effect".

f8aa8c8fee13.title: Pliocene
f8aa8c8fee13.sentence: In the Loess Plateau, δ13C values of occluded organic matter increased by 2.5% while those of pedogenic carbonate increased by 5% over the course of the Late Miocene and Pliocene, indicating increased aridification.

1e2c49a1e6ad.title: Optically stimulated luminescence
1e2c49a1e6ad.sentence: In physics, optically stimulated luminescence (OSL) is a method for measuring doses from ionizing radiation.

b7ed518445cf.title: Optically stimulated luminescence
b7ed518445cf.sentence: - Luminescence dating of ancient materials: mainly geological sediments and sometimes fired pottery, bricks etc., although in the latter case thermoluminescence dating is used more often

c1f2d304483f.title: Optically stimulated luminescence
c1f2d304483f.sentence: The method makes use of electrons trapped between the valence and conduction bands in the crystalline structure of certain minerals (most commonly quartz and feldspar).

c1e824da700a.title: Optically stimulated luminescence
c1e824da700a.sentence: The trapping sites are imperfections of the lattice — impurities or defects.

35ce34ee6e3a.title: Optically stimulated luminescence
35ce34ee6e3a.sentence: Under the stimulation of light, the electrons may free themselves from the trap and get into the conduction band.

769b4bf7be16.title: Optically stimulated luminescence
769b4bf7be16.sentence: If the centre with the hole is a luminescence center (radiative recombination centre), emission of light will occur.

282fb564d1e0.title: Optically stimulated luminescence
282fb564d1e0.sentence: To carry out OSL dating, mineral grains have to be extracted from the sample without exposure to light.

ae864b9f4465.title: Optically stimulated luminescence
ae864b9f4465.sentence: Most commonly these are so-called coarse grains of 100-200 μm or fine grains of 4-11 μm.

a3917e08ed0b.title: Optically stimulated luminescence
a3917e08ed0b.sentence: The difference between radiocarbon dating and OSL is that the former is used to date organic materials, while the latter is used to date minerals.

8c138c7f5bb1.title: Optically stimulated luminescence
8c138c7f5bb1.sentence: It is also used for dating the deposition of geological sediments after they have been transported by air (aeolian sediments) or rivers (fluvial sediments).

e61445d927bf.title: Optically stimulated luminescence
e61445d927bf.sentence: The most widely-used OSL method is called single-aliquot regeneration (SAR).

cdd914ab3bb1.title: Tephrochronology
cdd914ab3bb1.sentence: Tephrochronology is a geochronological technique for dating archaeological, geological and palaeoenvironmental sequences and events by their location between upper and lower layers of tephra (volcanic ejecta) of known date, and for correlating such sequences and events at separate locations between the same layers.

0a51473bbaae.title: Tephrochronology
0a51473bbaae.sentence: The premise of the technique is that each volcanic event produces a "tephra horizon", a layer of ash with a unique chemical "fingerprint" that allows the deposit to be identified across the area affected by fallout.

4621c67c0277.title: Tephrochronology
4621c67c0277.sentence: Thus, once the volcanic event has been independently dated, the tephra horizon will act as time marker.

d13226d9f86d.title: Tephrochronology
d13226d9f86d.sentence: The main advantages of the technique are that the volcanic ash layers can be relatively easily identified in many sediments and that the tephra layers are deposited relatively instantaneously over a wide spatial area.

0e9b5f38745c.title: Tephrochronology
0e9b5f38745c.sentence: This means they provide accurate temporal marker layers which can be used to verify or corroborate other dating techniques, linking sequences widely separated by location into a unified chronology that correlates climatic sequences and events.

57ac3acb9afa.title: Tephrochronology
57ac3acb9afa.sentence: An important recent advance is the use of LA-ICP-MS (i.e., laser ablation ICP-MS) to measure trace-element abundances in individual tephra shards.

5cf916917671.title: Tephrochronology
5cf916917671.sentence: One problem in tephrochronology is that tephra chemistry can become altered over time, at least for basaltic tephras.

d22ff555e2e3.title: Tephrochronology
d22ff555e2e3.sentence: Since the late 1990s, techniques developed by Chris S. M. Turney and others for extracting tephra horizons invisible to the naked eye ("cryptotephra") have revolutionised the application of tephrochronology.

7a806c9a683a.title: Tephrochronology
7a806c9a683a.sentence: Since then researchers have targeted stratigraphic archives of peat, lake sediment, ice cores, marine sediments, loess, floors of caves and rock shelters or stalagmites as well as contemporary eruption deposits.

907c89ad606c.title: Thermoluminescence dating
907c89ad606c.sentence: Thermoluminescence dating (TL) is the determination, by means of measuring the accumulated radiation dose, of the time elapsed since material containing crystalline minerals was either heated (lava, ceramics) or exposed to sunlight (sediments).

97bfa6f2fb08.title: Thermoluminescence dating
97bfa6f2fb08.sentence: Thermoluminescence dating presupposes a "zeroing" event in the history of the material, either heating (in the case of pottery or lava) or exposure to sunlight (in the case of sediments), that removes the pre-existing trapped electrons.

08654be8c24e.title: Thermoluminescence dating
08654be8c24e.sentence: As time goes on, the ionizing radiation field around the material causes the trapped electrons to accumulate (Figure 2).

d6c06b85de08.title: Thermoluminescence dating
d6c06b85de08.sentence: This is commonly done by measurement of the alpha radioactivity (the uranium and thorium content) and the potassium content (K-40 is a beta and gamma emitter) of the sample material.

542cbce6aec7.title: Thermoluminescence dating
542cbce6aec7.sentence: Often the gamma radiation field at the position of the sample material is measured, or it may be calculated from the alpha radioactivity and potassium content of the sample environment, and the cosmic ray dose is added in.

153fde93f6e4.title: Thermoluminescence dating
153fde93f6e4.sentence: Once all components of the radiation field are determined, the accumulated dose from the thermoluminescence measurements is divided by the dose accumulating each year, to obtain the years since the zeroing event.

451c4708bd56.title: Thermoluminescence dating
451c4708bd56.sentence: Subsequent irradiation, for example if an x-ray is taken, can affect accuracy, as will the "annual dose" of radiation a buried object has received from the surrounding soil.

a107dcee64f1.title: Thermoluminescence dating
a107dcee64f1.sentence: Ideally this is assessed by measurements made at the precise findspot over a long period.

ee629c7ed55b.title: Thermoluminescence dating
ee629c7ed55b.sentence: Thermoluminescence dating is used for material where radiocarbon dating is not available, like sediments.

6038b038e184.title: Thermoluminescence dating
6038b038e184.sentence: The heating must have taken the object above 500 °C, which covers most ceramics, although very high-fired porcelain creates other difficulties.

f07b0770ad23.title: Radiocarbon dating
f07b0770ad23.sentence: The resulting data, in the form of a calibration curve, is now used to convert a given measurement of radiocarbon in a sample into an estimate of the sample's calendar age.

4c9057319552.title: Radiocarbon dating
4c9057319552.sentence: The calculations given above produce dates in radiocarbon years: i.e. dates that represent the age the sample would be if the 14 C/12 C ratio had been constant historically.

22e4dade6287.title: Radiocarbon dating
22e4dade6287.sentence: The above calculations make several assumptions, such as that the level of 14 C in the atmosphere has remained constant over time.

56e0a03feacd.title: Radiocarbon dating
56e0a03feacd.sentence: In fact, the level of 14 C in the atmosphere has varied significantly and as a result, the values provided by the equation above have to be corrected by using data from other sources.

e70878758d72.title: Radiocarbon dating
e70878758d72.sentence: The study of tree rings led to the first such sequence: individual pieces of wood show characteristic sequences of rings that vary in thickness because of environmental factors such as the amount of rainfall in a given year.

c128d35a4a6b.title: Radiocarbon dating
c128d35a4a6b.sentence: Hans Suess used this data to publish the first calibration curve for radiocarbon dating in 1967.

ec783220d86a.title: Radiocarbon dating
ec783220d86a.sentence: These were superseded by the IntCal series of curves, beginning with IntCal98, published in 1998, and updated in 2004, 2009, 2013, and 2020.

d94ba4966a18.title: Radiocarbon dating
d94ba4966a18.sentence: There are separate curves for the northern hemisphere (IntCal20) and southern hemisphere (SHCal20), as they differ systematically because of the hemisphere effect.

f6a8830fffb3.title: Radiocarbon dating
f6a8830fffb3.sentence: There is also a separate marine calibration curve, MARINE20.

89ff04c6e4bf.title: Radiocarbon dating
89ff04c6e4bf.sentence: For consistency with these early papers, it was agreed at the 1962 Radiocarbon Conference in Cambridge (UK) to use the "Libby half-life" of 5568 years.

5e65722717f6.title: Radiocarbon dating
5e65722717f6.sentence: Radiocarbon ages are still calculated using this half-life, and are known as "Conventional Radiocarbon Age".

841ba7b3e3ef.title: Radiocarbon dating
841ba7b3e3ef.sentence: - Soil contains organic material, but because of the likelihood of contamination by humic acid of more recent origin, it is very difficult to get satisfactory radiocarbon dates.

80e7c3dcd0e7.title: Radiocarbon dating
80e7c3dcd0e7.sentence: It is preferable to sieve the soil for fragments of organic origin, and date the fragments with methods that are tolerant of small sample sizes.

9981e50e35ba.title: Radiocarbon dating
9981e50e35ba.sentence: - The three major components of peat are humic acid, humins, and fulvic acid.

f178e415df1f.title: Radiocarbon dating
f178e415df1f.sentence: Of these, humins give the most reliable date as they are insoluble in alkali and less likely to contain contaminants from the sample's environment.

43f8167e13bd.title: Radiocarbon dating
43f8167e13bd.section: Dating considerations > Reservoir effects > Other effects
43f8167e13bd.sentence: These rocks are usually so old that they no longer contain any measurable 14 C, so this carbon lowers the 14 C/12 C ratio of the water it enters, which can lead to apparent ages of thousands of years for both the affected water and the plants and freshwater organisms that live in it.

4d285f16f527.title: Radiocarbon dating
4d285f16f527.section: Dating considerations > Reservoir effects > Other effects
4d285f16f527.sentence: This is known as the hard water effect because it is often associated with calcium ions, which are characteristic of hard water; other sources of carbon such as humus can produce similar results, and can also reduce the apparent age if they are of more recent origin than the sample.

082c7ced86b7.title: Surface exposure dating
082c7ced86b7.sentence: Surface exposure dating is a collection of geochronological techniques for estimating the length of time that a rock has been exposed at or near Earth's surface.

0508297c772d.title: Surface exposure dating
0508297c772d.sentence: Surface exposure dating is used to date glacial advances and retreats, erosion history, lava flows, meteorite impacts, rock slides, fault scarps, cave development, and other geological events.

5e301d05a42a.title: Surface exposure dating
5e301d05a42a.sentence: It is most useful for rocks which have been exposed for between 10^3 and 10^6 years.

0db5395f129e.title: Surface exposure dating
0db5395f129e.sentence: Accordingly, by measuring the concentration of these cosmogenic nuclides in a rock sample, and accounting for the flux of the cosmic rays and the half-life of the nuclide, it is possible to estimate how long the sample has been exposed to the cosmic rays.

4faba0bef546.title: Surface exposure dating
4faba0bef546.sentence: Using certain cosmogenic radionuclides, scientists can date how long a particular surface has been exposed, how long a certain piece of material has been buried, or how quickly a location or drainage basin is eroding.

b84c1d24d38e.title: Surface exposure dating
b84c1d24d38e.sentence: 10Be and 26Al are produced when a portion of a quartz crystal (SiO2) is bombarded by a spallation product: oxygen of the quartz is transformed into 10Be and the silicon is transformed into 26Al.

a3b7306fb9c9.title: Surface exposure dating
a3b7306fb9c9.sentence: Because there are two radionuclides decaying, the ratio of concentrations of these two nuclides can be used without any other knowledge to determine an age at which the sample was buried past the production depth (typically 2–10 meters).

5fa1ee1e1c4a.title: Surface exposure dating
5fa1ee1e1c4a.sentence: These rates are usually estimated empirically by comparing the concentration of nuclides produced in samples whose ages have been dated by other means, such as radiocarbon dating, thermoluminescence, or optically stimulated luminescence.

84632bd0afc5.title: Surface exposure dating
84632bd0afc5.sentence: The excess relative to natural abundance of cosmogenic nuclides in a rock sample is usually measured by means of accelerator mass spectrometry.

39f6169d7dcc.title: Isotopes of beryllium
39f6169d7dcc.sentence: Beryllium-10 (10Be) has a half-life of 1.387 million years and beta decays to stable boron-10 with a maximum energy of 556.0 keV:

ddd346266f40.title: Isotopes of beryllium
ddd346266f40.sentence: Beryllium-10 is formed in the Earth's atmosphere mainly by cosmic ray spallation of nitrogen and oxygen.

76a962fc8a34.title: Isotopes of beryllium
76a962fc8a34.sentence: Because beryllium tends to exist in solutions below about pH 5.5 (and rainwater above many industrialized areas can have a pH less than 5), it will dissolve and be transported to the Earth's surface via rainwater.

fbac10a250ba.title: Isotopes of beryllium
fbac10a250ba.sentence: As the precipitation quickly becomes more alkaline, beryllium drops out of solution.

a07bd3ef3714.title: Isotopes of beryllium
a07bd3ef3714.sentence: Cosmogenic 10Be thereby accumulates at the soil surface, where its relatively long half-life does not limit its residence time there.

27eb6d92c326.title: Isotopes of beryllium
27eb6d92c326.sentence: 10Be and its daughter product have been used in surface exposure dating to examine soil erosion, soil formation from regolith, the development of lateritic soils and the age of ice cores.

9b8b4d4c4e84.title: Isotopes of beryllium
9b8b4d4c4e84.sentence: Presence of 7 Be in sediments is often used to establish that they are fresh, i.e. less than about 3–4 months in age, or about two half-lives of 7 Be.

27b3a4f744f3.title: Bomb pulse
27b3a4f744f3.sentence: The bomb pulse is the sudden increase of carbon-14 (14C) in Earth's atmosphere due to the hundreds of above-ground nuclear tests that started in 1945 and intensified after 1950 until 1963, when the Limited Test Ban Treaty was signed by the United States, the Soviet Union and the United Kingdom.

3ac45141de27.title: Bomb pulse
3ac45141de27.sentence: These blasts were followed by an almost doubling of the relative concentration of 14C in the atmosphere.

06540434499e.title: Bomb pulse
06540434499e.sentence: Since the nuclear test ban in 1963, atmospheric 14C relative concentration has been decreasing at 4% per year.

b35057039e13.title: Bomb pulse
b35057039e13.sentence: This continuous decrease permits scientists to determine, among other things, the age of deceased people and allows them to study cell activity in tissues.

ec538e511796.title: Bomb pulse
ec538e511796.sentence: The perturbation in atmospheric 14C from the bomb testing was an opportunity to validate atmospheric transport models, and to study the movement of carbon between the atmosphere and oceanic or terrestrial sinks.

9bd3a2b3595d.title: Bomb pulse
9bd3a2b3595d.sentence: Around the year 2030 the bomb pulse will die out if no more nuclear weapons are detonated aboveground.

8874be0cc415.title: Isotopes of lead
8874be0cc415.sentence: Lead-210 (210Pb) is a radiogenic isotope of lead, found in the decay chain of uranium-238.

e449725c8727.title: Isotopes of lead
e449725c8727.sentence: It is a beta emitter with a half-life of 22.20 years.

7b7e35062a54.title: Isotopes of lead
7b7e35062a54.sentence: In addition to dating recent sediments, 210Pb is widely applied for studying soil erosion and sedimentation dynamics in agricultural and natural environments.

f1a396774e66.title: Isotopes of lead
f1a396774e66.sentence: The unsupported or excess component (210Pbex), derived from atmospheric fallout of radon-222 decay products, accumulates in surface soils and decays with a half-life of 22.3 years.

a6af788c9bc8.title: Isotopes of lead
a6af788c9bc8.sentence: Its depth-dependent activity profile enables reconstruction of soil redistribution over the past century.

337a23094d0d.title: Isotopes of lead
337a23094d0d.sentence: It has been used to quantify erosion and deposition rates, assess land degradation, and evaluate soil conservation practices, offering valuable data for geomorphic and environmental research.

9353e6c27bb7.title: Isotopes of lead
9353e6c27bb7.sentence: Because 210Pb deposition is continuous and globally widespread, the method provides a long-term perspective that complements the medium-term records obtained from anthropogenic radionuclides such as 137Cs.

15f680ec52b0.title: Isotopes of lead
15f680ec52b0.sentence: A shorter-lived naturally occurring radioisotope, 210Pb with a half-life of 22.2 years, is useful for studying the sedimentation chronology of environmental samples on time scales shorter than 100 years.

216d4f30b5be.title: Rhizolith
216d4f30b5be.sentence: Rhizoliths are organosedimentary structures formed in soils or fossil soils (paleosols) by plant roots.

93ebf8a7cc60.title: Rhizolith
93ebf8a7cc60.sentence: They include root moulds, casts, and tubules, root petrifactions, and rhizocretions.

6e350b2c0d43.title: Rhizolith
6e350b2c0d43.sentence: Rhizoliths are important for identifying paleosols in the geologic record.

d4aa20951cc2.title: Rhizolith
d4aa20951cc2.sentence: However, they are limited to post-Silurian beds, since vascular plants with extensive root systems did not flourish until this time.

c52f2d385d07.title: Rhizolith
c52f2d385d07.sentence: One possibility is that some plant roots take up more anions than cations, maintaining charge balance by secreting HCO3− ions rather than H+ ions.

413a5cd58be3.title: Rhizolith
413a5cd58be3.sentence: In so doing, the pH of the surrounding soil is raised, rather than lowered.

1bcdd902f544.title: Rhizolith
1bcdd902f544.sentence: This may trigger precipitation of calcium carbonate around roots, this leading to the formation of rhizocretions.

1ba51f91608b.title: Rhizolith
1ba51f91608b.sentence: Rhizohaloes are zones of chemical reduction around decomposed plant roots.

237c69c3e708.title: Rhizolith
237c69c3e708.sentence: These typically appear as elongated gray mottles with reddish rims.

b449d7783b89.title: Rhizolith
b449d7783b89.sentence: Conditions of water saturation in paleosols can thus be inferred from the mineralogy of rhizoliths.

c5d7166bf0c2.title: Marine isotope stages
c5d7166bf0c2.sentence: Marine isotope stages (MIS), marine oxygen-isotope stages, or oxygen isotope stages (OIS), are alternating warm and cool periods in the Earth's paleoclimate, deduced from oxygen isotope data derived from deep sea core samples.

d28155e8a37a.title: Marine isotope stages
d28155e8a37a.sentence: Working backwards from the present, which is MIS 1 in the scale, stages with even numbers have high levels of oxygen-18 and represent cold glacial periods, while the odd-numbered stages are lows in the oxygen-18 figures, representing warm interglacial intervals.

565d8bf35548.title: Marine isotope stages
565d8bf35548.sentence: The MIS timescale was developed from the pioneering work of Cesare Emiliani in the 1950s, modifying an earlier system introduced by oceanographer Gustaf Arrhenius.

81ffa30a0f33.title: Marine isotope stages
81ffa30a0f33.sentence: Emiliani's work in turn depended on Harold Urey's prediction in a paper of 1947 that the ratio between oxygen-18 and oxygen-16 isotopes in calcite, the main chemical component of the shells and other hard parts of a wide range of marine organisms, should vary depending on the prevailing water temperature in which the calcite was formed.

6743383f79dc.title: Marine isotope stages
6743383f79dc.sentence: A further important advance came in 1967, when Nicholas Shackleton suggested that the fluctuations over time in the marine isotope ratios that had become evident by then were caused not so much by changes in water temperature, as Emiliani thought, but mainly by changes in the volume of ice-sheets, which when they expanded took up the lighter oxygen-16 isotope in preference to the heavier oxygen-18.

c47487fd8ac6.title: Marine isotope stages
c47487fd8ac6.sentence: The MIS data also matches the astronomical data of Milankovitch cycles of orbital forcing or the effects of variations in insolation caused by cyclical slight changes in the tilt of the Earth's axis of rotation – the "orbital theory".

5b1efa738c88.title: Marine isotope stages
5b1efa738c88.sentence: Indeed, that the MIS data matched Milankovich's theory, which he formed during World War I, so well was a key factor in the theory gaining general acceptance, despite some remaining problems at certain points, notably the so-called 100,000-year problem.

4350691470b2.title: Marine isotope stages
4350691470b2.sentence: It is now widely used in archaeology and other fields to express dating in the Quaternary period (the last 2.6 million years), as well as providing the fullest and best data for that period for paleoclimatology or the study of the early climate of the Earth, representing "the standard to which we correlate other Quaternary climate records".

d0b20a32a634.title: Marine isotope stages
d0b20a32a634.sentence: Over 100 stages have been identified, currently going back some 6 million years, and the scale may eventually reach back as far as 15 million years.

24de87e4dbd9.title: Marine isotope stages
24de87e4dbd9.sentence: - MIS 5e – 123 (peak of Last Interglacial, also known as the Eemian among other names)

ea511e16811c.title: Marine isotope stages
ea511e16811c.sentence: - MIS 3 – 57 (MIS 5d - MIS 2 is called the Last Glacial Period, Wisconsinan glaciation in North America, Weichselian glaciation in northern Europe)

9bd62c6df15f.title: Marine isotope stages
9bd62c6df15f.sentence: The list continues to MIS 104, beginning 2.614 million years ago.

fa7f525e1640.title: Clumped isotopes
fa7f525e1640.sentence: Clumped isotopes are heavy isotopes that are bonded to other heavy isotopes.

8c076c813dc3.title: Clumped isotopes
8c076c813dc3.sentence: The relative abundance of clumped isotopes (and multiply substituted isotopologues) in molecules such as methane, nitrous oxide, and carbonate is an area of active investigation.

7c1e52908e03.title: Clumped isotopes
7c1e52908e03.sentence: The carbonate clumped-isotope thermometer, or "13C–18O order/disorder carbonate thermometer", is a new approach for paleoclimate reconstruction, based on the temperature dependence of the clumping of 13C and 18O into bonds within the carbonate mineral lattice.

790d3bae57d3.title: Clumped isotopes
790d3bae57d3.sentence: The equilibrium constants for these reactions are temperature-dependent, with a tendency for heavy isotopes to "clump" with each other (increasing the proportions of multiply substituted isotopologues) as temperature decreases.

eb6e21f73859.title: Clumped isotopes
eb6e21f73859.sentence: Results are usually expressed as Δ47 (said as "cap 47"), which is the deviation of the ratio of isotopologues of CO2 with a molecular weight of 47 to those with a weight of 44 from the ratio expected if they were randomly distributed.

e1adc1152e4d.title: Clumped isotopes
e1adc1152e4d.section: Differences from the conventional δ18O analysis
e1adc1152e4d.sentence: In conventional δ18O analysis, both the δ18O values in carbonates and water are needed to estimate paleoclimate.

b78cea297be2.title: Clumped isotopes
b78cea297be2.section: Differences from the conventional δ18O analysis
b78cea297be2.sentence: Whereas for the carbonate clumped-isotope thermometer, the equilibrium is independent of the isotope compositions of waters from which carbonates grew.

a51a02561449.title: Clumped isotopes
a51a02561449.sentence: While conventional δ18O analysis solves for temperature as a function of both carbonate and water δ18O, clumped isotope analyses can provide temperature estimates that are independent of the source water δ18O. Δ47-derived temperature can then be used in conjunction with carbonate δ18O to reconstruct δ18O of the source water, thus providing information on the water with which the carbonate was equilibrated.

df24b87b5260.title: Clumped isotopes
df24b87b5260.sentence: Clumped isotope analyses thus allow for estimates of two key environmental variables: temperature and water δ18O.

fd94c2186a48.title: Clumped isotopes
fd94c2186a48.sentence: - Extract CO2 from carbonates by reaction with anhydrous phosphoric acid.

945fd7c4241c.title: Clumped isotopes
945fd7c4241c.sentence: - Purify the CO2 that has been extracted.

bd28489453ae.title: Clumped isotopes
bd28489453ae.sentence: - Mass spectrometric analyses of purified CO2, to obtain δ13C, δ18O, and Δ47 (abundance of mass-47 CO2) values.

9e81b3cbc184.title: Clumped isotopes
9e81b3cbc184.sentence: (Precision needs to be as high as ≈10^−5, for the isotope signals of interest are often less than ≈10^−3.)

98dc4184a1a8.title: Clumped isotopes
98dc4184a1a8.sentence: Studies have used temperatures derived from clumped isotopes for varied and numerous paleoclimate applications — to constrain δ18O of past seawater, pinpoint the timing of icehouse-hothouse transitions, track changes in ice volume through an ice age, and to reconstruct temperature changes in ancient lake basins.

8e02cd328b5a.title: Clumped isotopes
8e02cd328b5a.sentence: Clumped isotope analyses have recently been used to constrain the paleoaltitude or uplift history of a region.

f568d09e1bc2.title: Clumped isotopes
f568d09e1bc2.sentence: Two recent studies derive the timing of the uplift of the Andes Mountains and the Altiplano Plateau, citing sharp decreases in Δ47-derived temperatures as evidence of rapid tectonic uplift.

ae9876ea974c.title: Clumped isotopes
ae9876ea974c.sentence: Measurements of Δ47 can be used to better understand the physiology of extinct organisms, and to place constraints on the early development of endothermy, the process by which organisms regulate their body temperature.

6bc9be98565a.title: Clumped isotopes
6bc9be98565a.sentence: The temperature dependent relationship is subtle (−0.0005%/°C).

c82cff52250e.title: Clumped isotopes
c82cff52250e.sentence: Therefore, to obtain adequate precision, this approach requires long analyses (≈2–3 hours) and very large and uncontaminated samples.

25457fd988f0.title: Silurian-Devonian Terrestrial Revolution
