25457fd988f0.sentence: The Silurian-Devonian Terrestrial Revolution (SDTR), also known as the Devonian Plant Explosion (DePE) and the Devonian explosion, was a period of rapid colonization, diversification and radiation of land plants (particularly vascular plants) and fungi (especially dikaryans) on dry lands that occurred 428 to 359 million years ago (Mya) during the Silurian and Devonian periods, with the most critical phase occurring during the Late Silurian and Early Devonian.

50039b0a88d3.title: Silurian-Devonian Terrestrial Revolution
50039b0a88d3.sentence: Early non-vascular plants that began colonizing land during the Ordovician and early Silurian had limited bioengineering effects due to the lack of deep roots that could break up solid rocks into regolith and soil.

ea1478f8deb4.title: Silurian-Devonian Terrestrial Revolution
ea1478f8deb4.sentence: Their roots also eroded into the rocks, creating a layer of water-holding and mineral/organic matter-rich soil on top of Earth's crust known as the pedosphere, and significantly altering the chemistry of Earth's lithosphere and hydrosphere.

3b9a1c24cd74.title: Silurian-Devonian Terrestrial Revolution
3b9a1c24cd74.sentence: The symbiotic relationship between vascular plant root systems and various symbiont microbiomes evolved into mutualistic communities called rhizosphere, which synergistically further enhanced the weathering of the lithosphere into the pedosphere and increased release of essential minerals such as phosphates, calcium and magnesium.

1e78b2e96316.title: Silurian-Devonian Terrestrial Revolution
1e78b2e96316.sentence: Expansion of terrestrial Devonian flora modified soil properties, increasing silicate weathering by way of rhizosphere development as evidenced by pedogenic carbonates.

06045a978c65.title: Silurian-Devonian Terrestrial Revolution
06045a978c65.section: Environmental impact > Effects on atmosphere and climate
06045a978c65.sentence: Enhanced silicate weathering caused atmospheric CO2 levels to fall from around 6300 to 2100 ppmv, although it also drastically reduced the albedo of much of Earth's land surface, retarding the cooling effects of this greenhouse gas drawdown.

1e6728018e39.title: Silurian-Devonian Terrestrial Revolution
1e6728018e39.section: Environmental impact > Effects on atmosphere and climate
1e6728018e39.sentence: However, an alternative hypothesis holds that land plant evolution actually decreased silicate weathering rates, instead causing a drop in atmospheric carbon dioxide levels through elevated organic carbon burial brought about by the formation of wetlands.

22b999ef09fc.title: Taphonomy
22b999ef09fc.sentence: Taphonomy is the study of how organisms decay and become fossilized or preserved in the paleontological record.

d998f10b2847.title: Taphonomy
d998f10b2847.sentence: The term taphonomy (from Greek táphos, τάφος 'burial' and nomos, νόμος 'law') was introduced to paleontology in 1940 by the Soviet scientist Ivan Efremov to describe the study of the transition of remains, parts, or products of organisms from the biosphere to the lithosphere.

7bd1031177f2.title: Taphonomy
7bd1031177f2.sentence: Taphonomic phenomena are grouped into two phases: biostratinomy, events that occur between the death of the organism and the burial; and diagenesis, events that occur after the burial.

f5f9de98b380.title: Taphonomy
f5f9de98b380.sentence: These can include thermal alteration, rodent disturbances, gnaw marks, and the effects of soil pH to name a few.

7949b8fa5418.title: Taphonomy
7949b8fa5418.sentence: The methodology of taphonomy involves observing transformation processes to understand their impact on archaeological material and interpret patterns at real sites.

6639fe3cf3fa.title: Geoarchaeology
6639fe3cf3fa.sentence: Geoarchaeology is a multidisciplinary field of study that applies the theories and techniques of the geosciences to archaeology.

6eb17b783541.title: Geoarchaeology
6eb17b783541.sentence: It draws on techniques and approaches from geomorphology, sedimentology, pedology, stratigraphy, and geochronology to interpret sediments, soils, and landforms in archaeological investigations to inform archaeological and chronological knowledge and thought.

f17be299da44.title: Geoarchaeology
f17be299da44.sentence: There are three main objectives in most kinds of geoarchaeological investigations:

052690f429a7.title: Geoarchaeology
052690f429a7.sentence: - To place archaeological sites and their contents into their temporal context.

3b53f2015116.title: Geoarchaeology
3b53f2015116.sentence: - To understand the natural processes that create archaeological sites.

3418d0f92ea6.title: Geoarchaeology
3418d0f92ea6.sentence: - To develop landscape reconstructions of the area where the site was located to aid in interpretations of the site.

3b94f3562ea3.title: Geoarchaeology
3b94f3562ea3.sentence: Geoarchaeologists study the natural physical processes that affect archaeological sites such as geomorphology, for example, and their effects on buried sites and artifacts post-deposition.

98f60bf2d785.title: Geoarchaeology
98f60bf2d785.sentence: The application of stratigraphic principles to archaeological sites stems from the work of Niels Stenson (aka Nicolas Steno) in 1669 and James Hutton in 1788.

a14da8ef6c64.title: Geoarchaeology
a14da8ef6c64.sentence: Geoarchaeology, as we know it today, developed as a subfield of archaeology in the 1970s-1980s through the work of multidisciplinary teams applying geoscience field techniques to their studies.

15a590b435ed.title: Geoarchaeology
15a590b435ed.sentence: Monolith sampling is a geoarchaeological sampling technique that involves collecting sample cores from a section of an archaeological site to analyze and detect the buried processes that have affected the site.

b4d9a1e64bf6.title: Geoarchaeology
b4d9a1e64bf6.sentence: Narrow metal tins are hammered into the section, either by hand or by using machinery, in a sequence to collect the complete profile of the site for study.

d4ee90debbd4.title: Geoarchaeology
d4ee90debbd4.sentence: If more than one tin is needed, they are arranged in offset and overlapping positions so the complete profile can be rebuilt, typically off-site in laboratory conditions.

970ebf51d900.title: Geoarchaeology
970ebf51d900.sentence: The particle size distribution of a soil sample may indicate the conditions under which the strata or sediment were deposited.

22c2f3a05949.title: Environmental DNA
22c2f3a05949.sentence: Environmental DNA or eDNA is DNA that is collected from a variety of environmental samples such as soil, sediment, freshwater, seawater, snow or air, rather than directly sampled from an individual organism.

1cc9a8aeb027.title: Environmental DNA
1cc9a8aeb027.sentence: Such eDNA can be sequenced by environmental omics to reveal facts about the species that are present in an ecosystem — even microscopic ones not otherwise apparent or detectable.

24409512a21b.title: Environmental DNA
24409512a21b.sentence: Although scientists work to mimic these environments, many microbial organisms can not be removed and cultured in a laboratory setting.

27917be10e3e.title: Environmental DNA
27917be10e3e.sentence: The genetic makeup of some microbes is then only accessible through eDNA analysis.

770960b380f8.title: Environmental DNA
770960b380f8.sentence: Its concentration in soil may be as high as 2 μg/L, and its concentration in natural aquatic environments may be as high at 88 μg/L.

e51f71a0f1e4.title: Environmental DNA
e51f71a0f1e4.sentence: Analytical techniques of eDNA were first applied to terrestrial sediments yielding DNA from both extinct and extant mammals, birds, insects and plants.

9520cfd8e781.title: Environmental DNA
9520cfd8e781.sentence: Samples extracted from these terrestrial sediments are commonly referenced as 'sedimentary ancient DNA' (sedaDNA or dirtDNA).

d2064b6e9cf5.title: Soil mark
d2064b6e9cf5.sentence: Soil marks are differences in soil colour as a result of underlying archaeological features.

697a72ce0498.title: Soil mark
697a72ce0498.sentence: They can be seen when a ploughed-out earthwork has left hard dry material of a former bank and damper wetter material from a former ditch.

084a31d1eadf.title: Soil mark
084a31d1eadf.sentence: They can also occur when a feature has cut through the top soil to reveal underlying chalk.

45bab09a4b16.title: Soil mark
45bab09a4b16.sentence: Soil marks typically become visible in ploughed or harrowed fields, usually where there are restricted periods before the crops grow.

8ef64f765ec0.title: Soil mark
8ef64f765ec0.sentence: The color of the soil is very important in determining whether or not organic or burnt deposits happened over the soil, producing a black or red colored soil.

1560385eccd7.title: Soil mark
1560385eccd7.sentence: This allows archaeologists to understand the purpose of the artefacts found in the vicinity of the soil mark and can indicate whether or not fire was used.

1dc1b6aba3dc.title: Soil mark
1dc1b6aba3dc.sentence: For instance, indicating a dried-up river channel (known as a palaeochannel), which may subsequently reveal rich waterlogged archaeological deposits in its lower layers, or an area of slightly higher ground above winter flood level on an alluvial floodplain, which may be very hard to detect from the ground but which has attracted settlement for thousands of years.

985cde2d1e57.title: Midden
985cde2d1e57.sentence: A midden is an old dump for domestic waste.

ff39977fe88b.title: Midden
ff39977fe88b.sentence: It may consist of animal bones, human excrement, botanical material, mollusc shells, potsherds, lithics (especially debitage), and other artifacts and biofacts associated with past human occupation.

f667f0d7e9bd.title: Midden
f667f0d7e9bd.sentence: Middens with damp, anaerobic conditions can even preserve organic remains in deposits as the debris of daily life are tossed on the pile.

db9b183bf4cf.title: Midden
db9b183bf4cf.sentence: Shells have a high calcium carbonate content, which tends to make the middens alkaline.

7e1d84c35cf9.title: Midden
7e1d84c35cf9.sentence: This slows the normal rate of decay caused by soil acidity, leaving a relatively high proportion of organic material (food remnants, organic tools, clothing, human remains) available for archaeologists to find.

e085514b1ca5.title: Midden
e085514b1ca5.sentence: During the course of deposition, sediment is deposited as well.

4b5671268224.title: Midden
4b5671268224.sentence: Different mechanisms, from wind and water to animal digs, create a matrix which can also be analysed to provide seasonal and climatic information.

6203a48a6ab7.title: Law of superposition
6203a48a6ab7.sentence: In its plainest form, it states that in undeformed stratigraphic sequences, the oldest strata will lie at the bottom of the sequence, while newer material stacks upon the surface to form new deposits over time.

1fc69a6fd5a9.title: Law of superposition
1fc69a6fd5a9.sentence: The law of superposition was first proposed in 1669 by the Danish scientist Nicolas Steno, and is present as one of his major theses in the groundbreaking seminal work Dissertationis prodromus (1669).

d438df999df8.title: Law of superposition
d438df999df8.sentence: In the English-language literature, the law was popularized by William "Strata" Smith, who used it to produce the first geologic map of Britain.

1d92184352e9.title: Law of superposition
1d92184352e9.sentence: Some archaeological strata (often termed as contexts or layers) are created by undercutting previous strata.

801128f229d0.title: Law of superposition
801128f229d0.sentence: Superposition in archaeology requires a degree of interpretation to correctly identify chronological sequences and in this sense superposition in archaeology is more dynamic and multi-dimensional.

9c99c8d046d2.title: Law of superposition
9c99c8d046d2.section: Other limitations to stratification and superposition
9c99c8d046d2.sentence: Original stratification induced by natural processes can subsequently be disrupted or permutated by a number of factors, including animal interference and vegetation, as well as limestone crystallization.

5f13bd355650.title: Stratigraphy (archaeology)
5f13bd355650.sentence: Archaeological stratification or sequence is the dynamic superimposition of single units of stratigraphy, or contexts.

bc392ddbc3ed.title: Stratigraphy (archaeology)
bc392ddbc3ed.sentence: When archaeological finds are below the surface of the ground (as is most commonly the case), the identification of the context of each find is vital in enabling the archaeologist to draw conclusions about the site and about the nature and date of its occupation.

15d6f78f16cd.title: Stratigraphy (archaeology)
15d6f78f16cd.sentence: Contexts are single events or actions that leave discrete, detectable traces in the archaeological sequence or stratigraphy.

1837d9e64b4e.title: Stratigraphy (archaeology)
1837d9e64b4e.sentence: They can be deposits (such as the back-fill of a ditch), structures (such as walls), or "zero thickness surfaces", better known as "cuts".

763aa2caa448.title: Stratigraphy (archaeology)
763aa2caa448.sentence: Cuts represent actions that remove other solid contexts such as fills, deposits, and walls.

fe41c63190cb.title: Stratigraphy (archaeology)
fe41c63190cb.sentence: Stratigraphic relationships are the relationships created between contexts in time, representing the chronological order in which they were created.

22136962a738.title: Stratigraphy (archaeology)
22136962a738.sentence: The temporal relationship of "the fill" context to the ditch "cut" context is such that "the fill" occurred later in the sequence; you have to dig a ditch before you can back-fill it.

ed3b86afdd55.title: Stratigraphy (archaeology)
ed3b86afdd55.sentence: It is more useful to think of "higher" as it relates to the context's position in a Harris matrix, a two-dimensional representation of a site's formation in space and time.

e074a3de10f9.title: Stratigraphy (archaeology)
e074a3de10f9.sentence: - The principle of superposition establishes that within a series of layers and interfacial features, as originally created, the upper units of stratification are younger and the lower are older, for each must have been deposited on, or created by the removal of, a pre-existing mass of archaeological stratification.

16d1ca2bba28.title: Stratigraphy (archaeology)
16d1ca2bba28.sentence: - The principle that layers can be no older than the age of the most recent artefact discovered within them.

bfc0435f7d24.title: Stratigraphy (archaeology)
bfc0435f7d24.sentence: He also proposed three additional principles:

cff4b2d17674.title: Stratigraphy (archaeology)
cff4b2d17674.sentence: - The principle of original horizontality states that any archaeological layer deposited in an unconsolidated form will tend towards a horizontal deposition.

3260794920a3.title: Stratigraphy (archaeology)
3260794920a3.sentence: - The principle of lateral continuity states that any archaeological deposit, as originally laid down, will be bounded by the edge of the basin of deposition, or will thin down to a feather edge.

8a06857cc19f.title: Stratigraphy (archaeology)
8a06857cc19f.sentence: - The principle of stratigraphic succession states that any given unit of archaeological stratification exists within the stratigraphic sequence from its position between the undermost of all higher units and the uppermost of all lower units and with which it has a physical contact.

35e34b0b0392.title: Stratigraphy (archaeology)
35e34b0b0392.sentence: For example, the date of formation of a context which is totally sealed between two datable layers will fall between the dates of the two layers sealing it.

1c00a9e42ef6.title: Stratigraphy (archaeology)
1c00a9e42ef6.section: Stratigraphic dating > Residual and intrusive finds
1c00a9e42ef6.sentence: These artifacts are referred to as "residual" or "residual finds".

1b2ed9fbb805.title: Stratigraphy (archaeology)
1b2ed9fbb805.section: Stratigraphic dating > Residual and intrusive finds
1b2ed9fbb805.sentence: These artifacts may be termed intrusive finds.

3d0d57db4a40.title: Stratigraphy (archaeology)
3d0d57db4a40.section: Stratigraphic dating > Residual and intrusive finds
3d0d57db4a40.sentence: It is crucial that dating a context is based on the latest dating evidence drawn from the context.

72e0d0d09509.title: Forensic geology
72e0d0d09509.sentence: Forensic geology is the study of evidence relating to materials found in the Earth used to answer questions raised by the legal system.

c45f8f95296d.title: Forensic geology
c45f8f95296d.sentence: The main use of forensic geology as it is applied today is regarding trace evidence.

30a80edfa4db.title: Forensic geology
30a80edfa4db.sentence: By examining the soil and sediment particles forensic geologists can potentially link a suspect to a particular crime or a particular crime scene.

1995a217e446.title: Trace evidence
1995a217e446.sentence: The importance of trace evidence in criminal investigations was shown by Edmond Locard in the early 20th century, with his exchange principle, that every contact leaves a trace.

13cf58fb93a6.title: Forensic geology
13cf58fb93a6.sentence: In 1891, Hans Gross used microscopic analysis of soils and other materials from a suspect's shoes to link him to the crime scene.

44db12c3a1b1.title: Forensic geology
44db12c3a1b1.sentence: According to Murray, forensic geology began with Sherlock Holmes writer, Sir Arthur Conan Doyle.

63f095431e88.title: Forensic geology
63f095431e88.sentence: The character Sherlock Holmes claimed to be able to identify where an individual had been by various methods, including his having memorized the exposed geology of London to such a degree that detecting certain clays on a person's shoe would give away a locale.

4dd6c13c6990.title: Forensic geology
4dd6c13c6990.sentence: In 1975, Ray Murray and fellow Rutgers University professor John Tedrow published Forensic Geology.

2f7ee13e367f.title: Forensic geology
2f7ee13e367f.sentence: The principle use of a ground-penetrating radar device in regards to forensic geology is to find buried bodies.

a579ea966912.title: Forensic geology
a579ea966912.sentence: As well improving the recovery of the body by giving a general area to which the body is buried this also decreases excavation time.

dfa638610f9e.title: Forensic geology
dfa638610f9e.sentence: The first being the questioned sample, samples of unknown origin.

52cc86a557b6.title: Forensic geology
52cc86a557b6.sentence: The other type of sample consists of the control sample which the forensic geologist can choose.

2b06297b9fee.title: Forensic geology
2b06297b9fee.sentence: The most common control sample would be soil taken from the crime scene.

3d97f14dbae8.title: Forensic geology
3d97f14dbae8.sentence: The questioned and control sample would then be compared to find similarities or distinction from the two.

1536cddd40db.title: Forensic geology
1536cddd40db.sentence: Colour is one of the most important physical characteristics associated with soil samples.

edd98842613f.title: Forensic geology
edd98842613f.sentence: One technique used is comparing the soil to the Munsell soil chart.

aafa891d5c7f.title: Forensic geology
aafa891d5c7f.sentence: Although colour is a very subjective topic, two people can have a complete different perception of colour and could then associate it differently with the Munsell soil chart thus effecting the accuracy of this method.

c0446d722d82.title: Forensic geology
c0446d722d82.sentence: To avoid the errors of simply using human perception, to obtain objective results computer controlled spectrophotometry can be used.

d8ed39560eca.title: Forensic geology
d8ed39560eca.sentence: One computerized method is using CIELAB which consists of using an electronic spectrophotometer and calorimeter to create 3D plotting of colour.

d8dd0e1c1f9e.title: Forensic geology
d8dd0e1c1f9e.sentence: One of the most discriminating physical characteristics consist of particle size where it is characterized as particle size frequency distributions.

5891dce79294.title: Forensic geology
5891dce79294.sentence: Depending on the sample, different methods can be used such as examination use a microscope, laser diffraction, dry/ wet sieving, computer program analysis and many more.

c09f77aeda1c.title: Forensic geology
c09f77aeda1c.sentence: It can indicate the presence of many elements such as P, Zn, B, Cu, Fe etc., as well as estimating lime requirement.

b43b8e1cd6f9.title: Forensic geology
b43b8e1cd6f9.sentence: Soil samples can differ from a very small distance and is why the questioned sample should be examined first two establish particle size/ colour or any other distinguishable factors to then carefully choose a location at the scene to sample in comparison.

773d571492d9.title: Forensic geology
773d571492d9.sentence: If the questioned sample is found to be a lump of soil, this lump needs to obtained in its entirety to essentially preserve the different layers of soil in the lump itself as well as the keeping intact the particles.

1a26345b9e59.title: Forensic geology
1a26345b9e59.sentence: When samples are being taken from the ground it is recommended to take samples from different layers of the soil such as the horizon or the bed layer.

9f15e92ea5d3.title: Forensic geology
9f15e92ea5d3.sentence: It is important to obtain samples that vary on colour, mineral composition and textures.

c8f47d110bd0.title: Forensic geology
c8f47d110bd0.sentence: Need to assure the samples are allowed to dry before collection, moist samples will still allow further biological material will be modified changing the overall composition of the sample.

a4f319891710.title: Forensic geology
a4f319891710.sentence: To avoid continuous microbial activity related to sample taken from damp area, they are refrigerated prior.

d8d5dfbeadf7.title: Celtic field
d8d5dfbeadf7.sentence: Celtic field is an old name for traces of early (prehistoric) agricultural field systems found in North-West Europe, i.e. Britain, Ireland, Belgium, Netherlands, Germany, Denmark, France, Sweden, Poland and the Baltic states.

382f1413f61b.title: Celtic field
382f1413f61b.sentence: The fields themselves are not related to the Celtic culture.

b481979da5c9.title: Celtic field
b481979da5c9.sentence: The name was given by O. G. S. Crawford.

8a0a947b1156.title: Celtic field
8a0a947b1156.sentence: They are sometimes preserved in areas where industrial farming has not been adopted and can date from any time from the Early Bronze Age (c. 1800 BC) until the early medieval period.

596512037f64.title: Celtic field
596512037f64.sentence: They can be preserved as earthworks or soil marks.

82ba9e6d59ba.title: Celtic field
82ba9e6d59ba.sentence: They are characterised by their proximity to other ancient features such as enclosures, sunken lanes and farmsteads and are divided into a patchwork quilt of square plots rarely more than 2,000 m2 (0.49 acres) in area although larger examples are known (e.g. Dorset and Wiltshire).

c157bd980be1.title: Celtic field
c157bd980be1.sentence: Their small size (35–50 m; 40–55 yd) implies that each was cultivated by a single person or household.

d76b8421768d.title: Celtic field
d76b8421768d.sentence: Lynchets, evidence of early ploughing can often be seen at the upper and lower ends.

25311145578e.title: Ridge and furrow
25311145578e.sentence: Ridge and furrow is an archaeological pattern of ridges (Medieval Latin: sliones) and troughs created by a system of ploughing used in Europe during the Middle Ages, typical of the open-field system.

c5bad3361e6f.title: Ridge and furrow
c5bad3361e6f.sentence: Ridge and furrow topography was a result of ploughing with non-reversible ploughs on the same strip of land each year.

0b58aeefc75a.title: Ridge and furrow
0b58aeefc75a.sentence: This process has the effect of moving the soil in each half of the strip one furrow's width towards the centre line each time the field is ploughed.

494256626245.title: Ridge and furrow
494256626245.sentence: The movement of soil year after year gradually built the centre of each strip up into a ridge, leaving a dip, or "furrow" between each ridge (this use of "furrow" is different from that for the small furrow left by each pass of the plough).

117cd2241726.title: Ridge and furrow
117cd2241726.sentence: The raised ridges offered better drainage in a wet climate: moisture drained into the furrows, and since the ridges were laid down a slope, in a sloping field water would collect in a ditch at the bottom.

7b4fed09d930.title: Ridge and furrow
7b4fed09d930.sentence: Only on some well-drained soils were the fields left flat.

ae6bb73145b9.title: Ridge and furrow
ae6bb73145b9.sentence: The surviving ridges are parallel, ranging from 3 to 22 yards (3 to 20 m) apart and up to 24 inches (61 cm) tall—they were much taller when in use.

1aec49e4f813.title: Ridge and furrow
1aec49e4f813.sentence: When in active use, the height difference was even more, over 6 feet (1.8 m) in places.

b0b49c9607cb.title: Ridge and furrow
b0b49c9607cb.sentence: However, in some cases the land became grassland, and where this has not been ploughed since, the pattern has often been preserved.

036c89389724.title: Ridge and furrow
036c89389724.sentence: In most places ploughing continued over the centuries, and later methods (especially the reversible plough) removed the ridge and furrow pattern.

00476c7a1821.title: Forensic palynology
00476c7a1821.sentence: Forensic palynology is a subdiscipline of palynology (the study of pollen grains, spores, and other palynomorphs), that aims to prove or disprove a relationship among objects, people, and places that may pertain to both criminal and civil cases.

2d95410758e3.title: Forensic palynology
2d95410758e3.sentence: Pollen can reveal where a person or object has been, because regions of the world, countries, and even different parts of a single garden will have a distinctive pollen assemblage.

d267ff8438ed.title: Forensic palynology
d267ff8438ed.sentence: Pollen evidence can also reveal the season in which a particular object picked up the pollen.

2b3507cdb6d2.title: Forensic palynology
2b3507cdb6d2.sentence: Pollen can also be found in soil, clothing, hair, drugs, stomach contents, ropes, and rock which are places where it would be difficult for the suspect to remove because of pollen's adhesion properties.

3485ea79b333.title: Forensic palynology
3485ea79b333.sentence: Soil samples in the suspect's car and under the soles of the suspect's shoes also contained the same palynomorph composition as the coastline area where the body was found.

55deecb15d84.title: Forensic palynology
55deecb15d84.sentence: Another recent study did research in Bolivia to study the pollen assemblage in high altitude soils, this study also created a forensic database for uses in non-seasonal soil.

71a20ab6ac0f.title: Forensic palynology
71a20ab6ac0f.sentence: This database creation is allowing forensic palynology to be used in a more broad area now, as data for both high altitude pollen assemblage and non-seasonal soil data has been collected.

51e9103ba7e8.title: Forensic anthropology
51e9103ba7e8.sentence: Forensic anthropology is the application of the anatomical science of anthropology and its various subfields, including forensic archaeology and forensic taphonomy, in a legal setting.

305e810d123f.title: Forensic anthropology
305e810d123f.sentence: Forensic archaeologists can help determine potential grave sites that might have been overlooked.

5d3ad4594827.title: Forensic anthropology
5d3ad4594827.sentence: Processing scenes of mass fatality or incidents of terrorism (i.e. homicide, mass graves and war crimes, and other violations of human rights) is a branch of work that forensic archaeologists are involved with as well.

00ca39869005.title: Forensic anthropology
00ca39869005.sentence: Differences in the soil can help forensic archaeologists locate these sites.

8519f2510962.title: Forensic anthropology
8519f2510962.sentence: During the burial of a body, a small mound of soil will form from the filling of the grave.

25649def18d4.title: Forensic anthropology
25649def18d4.sentence: The loose soil and increasing nutrients from the decomposing body encourages different kinds of plant growth than surrounding areas.

ec851a0f22ad.title: Forensic anthropology
ec851a0f22ad.sentence: Typically, grave sites will have looser, darker, more organic soil than areas around it.

5b87d66529f5.title: Forensic anthropology
5b87d66529f5.sentence: Geotaphonomy is the examination of how the decomposition of the body affects the environment.

ee394967e5c3.title: Taphonomy
ee394967e5c3.sentence: Geotaphonomy studies how the burial practices and the burial itself affect the surrounding environment.

247c72d05d42.title: Forensic anthropology
247c72d05d42.sentence: Geotaphonomy examinations can include how the soil was disturbed, pH alteration of the surrounding area, and either the acceleration or deceleration of plant growth around the body.

0571b01d5a1c.title: Taphonomy
0571b01d5a1c.sentence: This includes soil disturbances and tool marks from digging the grave, disruption of plant growth and soil pH from the decomposing body, and the alteration of the land and water drainage from introducing an unnatural mass to the area.

9d769bb25bd0.title: Forensic anthropology
9d769bb25bd0.sentence: Forensic taphonomy is the study of these postmortem changes to human remains caused by soil, water, and the interaction with plants, insects, and other animals.

c8bbae4f6816.title: Forensic anthropology
c8bbae4f6816.sentence: William M. Bass | Created the first body farm to investigate decomposition in various conditions, such as partially buried, buried during particular times of the year, left out in the open for animal scavengers, and burning. |

19137329dd55.title: Geoarchaeology
19137329dd55.sentence: The magnetic susceptibility of a material is a measure of its ability to become magnetised by an external magnetic field (Dearing, 1999).

9d590099024f.title: Geoarchaeology
9d590099024f.sentence: Just because the soil contains a lot of iron does not mean that it will have high magnetic susceptibility.

0a7d077207c5.title: Geoarchaeology
0a7d077207c5.sentence: Magnetic forms of iron can be formed by burning and microbial activity, such as in top-soils and some anaerobic deposits.

c632d6ede435.title: Geoarchaeology
c632d6ede435.sentence: - Identifying hearth areas and the presence of burning residues in deposits.

a964d6d25d8f.title: Geoarchaeology
a964d6d25d8f.sentence: - Explaining whether areas of reddening are due to burning or other natural processes such as gleying (waterlogging).

bd98ff84e381.title: Geoarchaeology
bd98ff84e381.sentence: - Identify buried soils in depositional sequences.

48ad3521f845.title: Geoarchaeology
48ad3521f845.sentence: - Identify redeposited soil materials in peat, lake sediments, etc.

86cdfcc57561.title: Geophysical survey (archaeology)
86cdfcc57561.sentence: In archaeology, geophysical survey is ground-based physical sensing techniques used for archaeological imaging or mapping.

9e31ea85f3be.title: Geophysical survey (archaeology)
9e31ea85f3be.sentence: Geophysical instruments can detect buried features when their physical properties contrast measurably with their surroundings.

88b067ce9e60.title: Geophysical survey (archaeology)
88b067ce9e60.sentence: Unlike other archaeological methods, geophysical survey is neither invasive nor destructive.

be39ba343526.title: Geophysical survey (archaeology)
be39ba343526.sentence: In contrast, most archaeological sites are relatively near the surface, often within the top meter of earth.

cd0dbab55ac6.title: Geophysical survey (archaeology)
cd0dbab55ac6.sentence: Another challenge is to detect subtle and often very small features – which may be as ephemeral as organic staining from decayed wooden posts - and distinguish them from rocks, roots, and other natural "clutter".

e0c93eb13b57.title: Geophysical survey (archaeology)
e0c93eb13b57.sentence: Most commonly applied to archaeology are magnetometers, electrical resistance meters, ground-penetrating radar (GPR) and electromagnetic (EM) conductivity meters.

2742841ef42b.title: Geophysical survey (archaeology)
2742841ef42b.sentence: A stone foundation might impede the flow of electricity, while the organic deposits within a midden might conduct electricity more easily than surrounding soils.

075bb5bbe070.title: Geophysical survey (archaeology)
075bb5bbe070.sentence: Magnetometers react very strongly to iron and steel, brick, burned soil, and many types of rock, and archaeological features composed of these materials are very detectable.

1c8d6c2a1665.title: Geophysical survey (archaeology)
1c8d6c2a1665.sentence: Where these highly magnetic materials do not occur, it is often possible to detect very subtle anomalies caused by disturbed soils or decayed organic materials.

c7ce53bb293d.title: Geophysical survey (archaeology)
c7ce53bb293d.sentence: GPR can be a powerful tool in favorable conditions (uniform sandy soils are ideal).

92f8a469b525.title: Geophysical survey (archaeology)
92f8a469b525.sentence: The high electrical conductivity of fine-grained sediments (clays and silts) causes conductive losses of signal strength; rocky or heterogeneous sediments scatter the GPR signal.

3510785af4e3.title: Magnetometer
3510785af4e3.sentence: Ploughed fields behave as sources of magnetic noise in such surveys.

c6dd2cc820aa.title: Magnetometer
c6dd2cc820aa.sentence: Walking tracks and roadways can sometimes be mapped with differential compaction in magnetic soils or with disturbances in clays, such as on the Great Hungarian Plain.

4a725a41390b.title: Geophysical survey (archaeology)
4a725a41390b.sentence: The use of geophysical surveys is well established in European archaeology, especially in Great Britain, where it was pioneered in the 1940s and 1950s.

40f4202c03ad.title: Geoarchaeology
40f4202c03ad.section: Techniques Used > Phosphate and Orthophosphate Content with Spectrophotometry
40f4202c03ad.sentence: Phosphate in man-made soils derives from people and their animals, rubbish, and bones.

dd7d56c11c6b.title: Geoarchaeology
dd7d56c11c6b.section: Techniques Used > Phosphate and Orthophosphate Content with Spectrophotometry
dd7d56c11c6b.sentence: One hundred people excrete about 62 kg of phosphate annually, with about the same amount from their rubbish.

2baee1876d55.title: Geoarchaeology
2baee1876d55.section: Techniques Used > Phosphate and Orthophosphate Content with Spectrophotometry
2baee1876d55.sentence: Most is quickly immobilised on the clay of the soil and 'fixed', where it can persist for thousands of years.

76c264999d43.title: Geoarchaeology
76c264999d43.section: Techniques Used > Phosphate and Orthophosphate Content with Spectrophotometry
76c264999d43.sentence: Therefore, it doesn't take long for human activity to make orders-of-magnitude differences in the phosphate concentration in soil.

dbb7c689509e.title: Geoarchaeology
dbb7c689509e.section: Techniques Used > Phosphate and Orthophosphate Content with Spectrophotometry
dbb7c689509e.sentence: The human body contains about 650 g of PO 4 (500g, or 80%, in the skeleton), resulting in elevated levels in burial sites.

bbf2f1f5381b.title: Cropmark
bbf2f1f5381b.sentence: Cropmarks or crop marks are a means through which sub-surface archaeological, natural and recent features may be visible from the air or a vantage point on higher ground or a temporary platform.

a999367de7af.title: Cropmark
a999367de7af.sentence: Crop marks are due to the principle of differential growth.

f25fd19c211a.title: Cropmark
f25fd19c211a.sentence: Soil conditions are a key factor influencing vegetation growth.

0c515275adc8.title: Cropmark
0c515275adc8.sentence: For instance, a buried stone wall can impact crop development above it by redirecting water away from the area and displacing the more fertile soil needed for healthy plant growth.

bffccbacf986.title: Cropmark
bffccbacf986.sentence: Conversely, a buried ditch, with a fill containing more organic matter than the natural earth, provides much more conducive conditions, and water will naturally collect there, nourishing the plants growing above.

0a881e579664.title: Cropmark
0a881e579664.sentence: By their nature, crop marks are visible only seasonally and may not be visible at all except in exceptionally wet or dry years.

f2093cb03ebd.title: Cropmark
f2093cb03ebd.sentence: Droughts can be especially useful to cropmark hunters, as the differential growth can become apparent in normally hardy species such as grass.

3dda92f1880e.title: Cropmark
3dda92f1880e.sentence: An alternative approach is thermal imaging, where differential water loss (which is dependent on the availability of water at the roots) can create temperature differences, which result in thermal crop marks that are potentially visible at any time during crop growth.

1e131181ab6d.title: Raised field
1e131181ab6d.sentence: In agriculture, a raised field is a large, cultivated elevation, typically bounded by water-filled ditches, that is used to allow cultivators to control environmental factors such as moisture levels, frost damage, and flooding.

21e198320ab3.title: Raised field
21e198320ab3.sentence: Examples of raised field agriculture can be found among some Pre-Hispanic cultures of Latin America, such as those from tropical lowlands and the Budi Lake Mapuche.

5360e9e63ca3.title: Raised field
5360e9e63ca3.sentence: Pre-Hispanic raised fields are known from the region near Santa Cruz de Mompox in northern Colombia and in the Llanos de Moxos region of lowland Bolivia.

c870bea39a3b.title: Raised field
c870bea39a3b.sentence: In highland Bolivia, where this was utilized by the Tiwanaku culture near Lake Titicaca, this technique is known as Waru Waru or camellones.

1ccf915b5e0b.title: Raised field
1ccf915b5e0b.sentence: Ancient raised-field agriculture has also been documented in Central America at Pulltrouser Swamp in Belize, where it was practiced by the Maya civilization.

14209362b9fc.title: Raised field
14209362b9fc.sentence: Toltec and Aztec people also practiced raised-field agriculture on the shore of Lake Texcoco, where these fields were known as chinampas.

16dfc40e05c7.title: World Congress of Soil Science
16dfc40e05c7.sentence: The World Congress of Soil Science (WCSS) is a conference held every four years (although interrupted by World War II) under the guidance of the International Union of Soil Sciences (IUSS).

c315049ed588.title: World Congress of Soil Science
c315049ed588.sentence: The purpose of a congress is to: (i) ensure the advancement of soil science and its application, and (ii) to handle the business of the society.

ca6760db7b55.title: World Congress of Soil Science
ca6760db7b55.sentence: The congresses are only open to society members.

0d080e082803.title: World Congress of Soil Science
0d080e082803.sentence: The number of members attending has steadily increased, with approximately 2000 members attending each congress since the 15th WCSS in Acapulco, Mexico.

e9a94ca0d5a2.title: International Union of Soil Sciences
e9a94ca0d5a2.sentence: Until 2014, the IUSS President was designated by the national soil science society that was responsible for the next World Congress of Soil Science.

dab4be696c8c.title: World Congress of Soil Science
dab4be696c8c.sentence: The 21st WCSS was held in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, in August 2018, the 22nd in 2022 in Glasgow, Scotland, and the 23rd in 2026 in Nanjing, China.

ef1ad4ad3ee1.title: World Congress of Soil Science
ef1ad4ad3ee1.sentence: The next WCSS will be 2030 in Toronto, Canada.

e38399a0bf49.title: The Formation of Vegetable Mould Through the Action of Worms

61b687593bd3.title: Long-term experiment
61b687593bd3.sentence: A long-term experiment is an experimental procedure that runs through a long period of time, in order to test a hypothesis or observe a phenomenon that takes place at an extremely slow rate.

58a250d798d6.title: Long-term experiment

064429fdb5fd.title: Long-term experiment

c832f0470c4e.title: Long-term experiment
c832f0470c4e.sentence: Examples include the Park Grass Experiment at Rothamsted Experimental Station (1843–present), the Morrow Plots (1876–present) at the University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign, Sanborn Field at the University of Missouri (1888-present), the Magruder Plots (1892–present) at Oklahoma State University, Auburn's Old Rotation (1896–present), and the Haughley Experiment (1939–1982?).

213056112f29.title: Long-term experiment

e7a8e31790a7.title: Long-term experiment

1ef820e9de4d.title: Long-term experiment

5df563cc18f4.title: Long-term experiment

5e56b0863136.title: History of soil science
5e56b0863136.sentence: A major re-evaluation of soil formation and the role of biota commenced in the 1980s, as soil-geomorphologists began to re-evaluate Charles Darwin's and Nathaniel Shaler's early ideas on the role of bioturbation in soil formation.

7c0d87a60d4a.title: Bioturbation

b658deaab504.title: History of soil science
b658deaab504.sentence: There is now ample evidence to support Darwin's conclusions, and in many areas biota that burrow in soil are major agents of pedogenesis.

c4b8efae6356.title: History of soil science
c4b8efae6356.sentence: As a consequence, the formation of soil has come to be treated as the aggregate of many interrelated physical, chemical, and biological processes.

308fd02676e2.title: History of soil science
308fd02676e2.sentence: In 1941 Hans Jenny's (1899–1992) Factors of Soil Formation: A System of Quantitative Pedology concisely summarized and illustrated many of the basic principles of modern soil science to that date.

581c4e44ffe8.title: History of soil science
581c4e44ffe8.sentence: Since 1940, time has assumed much greater significance among the factors of soil formation, and geomorphological studies have become important in determining the time that soil material at any place has been subjected to soil-forming processes.

a04df8b17e1e.title: History of soil science

7e53e124231a.title: Vasily Dokuchaev
7e53e124231a.sentence: Vasily Vasilyevich Dokuchaev (Russian: Васи́лий Васи́льевич Докуча́ев; 1 March 1846 – 8 November 1903) was a Russian geologist and geographer who is credited with laying the foundations of soil science.

0cf7fc2b9395.title: Vasily Dokuchaev
0cf7fc2b9395.sentence: Vasily Vasilevich Dokuchaev is commonly regarded as the father of soil science, the study of soils in their natural setting.

d46333cc6933.title: Vasily Dokuchaev
d46333cc6933.sentence: He developed soil science in Russia and was perhaps the first to conduct broad geographical investigations of different soil types.

436ce5e5bf84.title: Vasily Dokuchaev
436ce5e5bf84.sentence: He introduced the idea that other variables could explain the geographical variations in soil type besides geological factors (parent material), such as climatic and topographic factors, and by the duration of pedogenesis (soil formation).

41140c8faa12.title: Vasily Dokuchaev
41140c8faa12.sentence: Dokuchaev considers the soil as a natural body having its own genesis and its own history of development, a body with complex and multiform processes taking place within it.

67410d6b814b.title: Vasily Dokuchaev
67410d6b814b.sentence: The soil is considered as different from bedrock.

78249ad745af.title: Vasily Dokuchaev
78249ad745af.sentence: The latter becomes soil under the influence of a series of soil-formation factors (climate, vegetation, parent material, relief and age).

c52739919063.title: Vasily Dokuchaev
c52739919063.sentence: He developed the very first soil classification, using these ideas as a starting point.

7215dbeb62ab.title: Vasily Dokuchaev
7215dbeb62ab.sentence: Dokuchaev's work on soil science produced a system of soil classification that described five factors for soil formation.

b4aafa1ffefd.title: Vasily Dokuchaev
b4aafa1ffefd.sentence: He arrived at his theory after extensive field studies on Russian soils in 1883.

1644e8ca6e06.title: Vasily Dokuchaev

e5a6dad875e1.title: Vasily Dokuchaev

8e4f0c5a57b5.title: Vasily Dokuchaev

8382bd425056.title: Vasily Dokuchaev

47e2918125c5.title: Justus von Liebig
47e2918125c5.sentence: Justus Freiherr von Liebig (12 May 1803 – 18 April 1873) was a German scientist who made major contributions to the theory, practice, and pedagogy of chemistry, as well as to agricultural and biological chemistry; he is considered one of the principal founders of organic chemistry.

1ec4954f9739.title: Justus von Liebig
1ec4954f9739.sentence: He has been described as the "father of the fertilizer industry" for his emphasis on nitrogen and minerals as essential plant nutrients, and his popularization of the law of the minimum, which states that plant growth is limited by the scarcest nutrient resource, rather than the total amount of resources available.

3dc504423b67.title: Justus von Liebig
3dc504423b67.sentence: His book Die organische Chemie in ihrer Anwendung auf Agricultur und Physiologie (Organic Chemistry in its Application to Agriculture and Physiology) (1840) promoted the idea that chemistry could revolutionize agricultural practice, increasing yields and lowering costs.

277ff91a8c3c.title: Justus von Liebig
277ff91a8c3c.sentence: It was widely translated, vociferously critiqued, and highly influential.

d7f5bec464e8.title: Justus von Liebig
d7f5bec464e8.sentence: Liebig's awareness of both synthesis and degradation led him to become an early advocate of conservation, promoting ideas such as the recycling of sewage.

30a5384ff5e8.title: Justus von Liebig
30a5384ff5e8.sentence: Liebig's lack of experience in practical applications, and differences between editions of the book, fueled considerable criticism.

ef39864016ec.title: Justus von Liebig
ef39864016ec.sentence: Nonetheless, Liebig's writings had a profound impact on agriculture, spurring experiment and theoretical debate in Germany, England, and France.

b5133e0893b4.title: Justus von Liebig
b5133e0893b4.sentence: In 1863 he published the book "Es ist ja die Spitze meines lebens" in which he revised his early perceptions, now appreciating soil life and in particular the biological nitrogen fixation.

87a203d21f1d.title: Hans Jenny (pedologist)
87a203d21f1d.sentence: Hans Jenny (7 February 1899 – 9 January 1992) was a Swiss-born soil scientist and expert on pedology (the study of soil in its natural environment), particularly the processes of soil formation.

8fc63346611b.title: Hans Jenny (pedologist)
8fc63346611b.sentence: He earned a diploma in agriculture from the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology (ETH Zurich) in 1922, and a D. Sc. degree in 1927 for a thesis on ion exchange reactions.

e344ba4794d9.title: Hans Jenny (pedologist)
e344ba4794d9.sentence: Following an appointment at the University of Missouri, he joined the faculty of the University of California at Berkeley in 1936.

1f00da211502.title: Hans Jenny (pedologist)
1f00da211502.sentence: International recognition came to Jenny after the 1941 publication of Factors of Soil Formation: A System of Quantitative Pedology.

5d4f1709ae27.title: Hans Jenny (pedologist)
5d4f1709ae27.sentence: His synthesis of field studies with the abstract formalism of physical chemistry set down the generic mathematical relationship that connects the observed properties of soil with the independent factors that determine the process of soil formation:

e678d479343b.title: Hans Jenny (pedologist)
e678d479343b.sentence: In The Soil Resource, Origin and Behaviour (1980), Jenny redefined the soil forming factors as state variables and extended the effects to ecosystem properties.

82ebb17676e7.title: Hans Jenny (pedologist)

4034731e6cc7.title: Hans Jenny (pedologist)

0be02530fb6c.title: Hans Jenny (pedologist)

dde8b1166b4c.title: Sergei Winogradsky
dde8b1166b4c.sentence: Sergei Nikolaevich Winogradsky ForMemRS (Russian: Сергей Николаевич Виноградский; Ukrainian: Сергій Миколайович Виноградський; 13 September [O.S. 1 September] 1856 – 24 February 1953), also published under the name Sergius Winogradsky, was a Ukrainian and Russian microbiologist, ecologist and soil scientist who pioneered the cycle-of-life concept.

2307e04d895b.title: Sergei Winogradsky
2307e04d895b.sentence: Winogradsky discovered various biogeochemical cycles and parts of these cycles.

010739273200.title: Sergei Winogradsky
010739273200.sentence: Winogradsky was one of the first researchers to attempt to understand microorganisms outside of the medical context, making him among the first students of microbial ecology and environmental microbiology.

f6543df87493.title: Sergei Winogradsky
f6543df87493.sentence: He reported that Beggiatoa oxidized hydrogen sulfide (H2S) as an energy source and formed intracellular sulfur droplets.

e7be4e5e802a.title: Sergei Winogradsky
e7be4e5e802a.sentence: In 1888, after de Bary's death, he relocated to Zürich, where he began investigation into the process of nitrification, identifying the genera Nitrosomonas and Nitrosococcus, which oxidizes ammonium to nitrite, and Nitrobacter, which oxidizes nitrite to nitrate.

ddbdf2098240.title: Sergei Winogradsky

4fdda3078ffb.title: Sergei Winogradsky

cf4cdb78f4ac.title: Sergei Winogradsky

e1b652f4cde3.title: Sergei Winogradsky
e1b652f4cde3.sentence: During this period, he worked on a number of topics, among them iron bacteria, nitrifying bacteria, nitrogen fixation by Azotobacter, cellulose-decomposing bacteria, and culture methods for soil microorganisms.

a3c8742d502c.title: Martinus Beijerinck
a3c8742d502c.sentence: Nitrogen fixation, the process by which diatomic nitrogen gas is converted to ammonium ions and becomes available to plants, was also investigated by Beijerinck.

d52f775491b8.title: Martinus Beijerinck

4147f89314ba.title: Martinus Beijerinck
4147f89314ba.sentence: He named the new pathogen virus to indicate its non-bacterial nature.

d22a33978d24.title: Martinus Beijerinck

d33d5012881d.title: Martinus Beijerinck
d33d5012881d.sentence: He is often incorrectly credited with framing the microbial ecology idea that "everything is everywhere, but, the environment selects", which was stated by Lourens Baas Becking.

0fb331fe463f.title: Friedrich Albert Fallou
0fb331fe463f.sentence: Friedrich Albert Fallou (11 November 1794 – 6 September 1877) was a German lawyer who is considered one of the founders of modern soil science.

a49951186453.title: Friedrich Albert Fallou
a49951186453.sentence: While working as a lawyer and tax assessor, Fallou established himself as an independent scientist and a recognized authority in the natural history of farm and forest soil.

a6ce97569a6a.title: Friedrich Albert Fallou
a6ce97569a6a.sentence: Working in soil evaluation for most of his professional life, Fallou became concerned with the declining soil quality in his region and developed a passionate interest in soil.

0c3809fa682b.title: Soil

530f0e736530.title: Friedrich Albert Fallou
530f0e736530.sentence: In 1862, he proposed that soil was separate in nature from geology and, intent on establishing the study of soils as an independent science, Fallou introduced the term pedology (German: pedologie).

b4639c062ba0.title: Friedrich Albert Fallou

52a8ac6273e2.title: Friedrich Albert Fallou

6c5a3d496b9e.title: Friedrich Albert Fallou

f7edb83f046e.title: Friedrich Albert Fallou

aedb8eb8e002.title: Friedrich Albert Fallou

b6b23395b49d.title: Friedrich Albert Fallou

4c49d81e9691.sentence: Konstantin Dmitrievich Glinka (Russian: Константи́н Дми́триевич Гли́нка) (1867–1927) was a Russian soil scientist.

4232a372b6cb.title: Konstantin Glinka
4232a372b6cb.sentence: Glinka became very influential resulting in wide distribution of the ideas of the Russian school of soil science.

6e5ff3e94555.title: Konstantin Glinka
6e5ff3e94555.sentence: In 1889 he began to engage in geological and soil research at the University under the guidance of V. B. Dokuchaev.

eb21b92c047b.title: Konstantin Glinka
eb21b92c047b.sentence: He worked in the Poltava (1889-1890) and in the expedition of the Forest Department (1892).

eb29c08f550a.title: Konstantin Glinka
eb29c08f550a.sentence: He was Director of the Agricultural College of Leningrad and Experimental Station, and the first director of the Dokuchaev Soil Science Institute.

951e794652f3.title: Konstantin Glinka
951e794652f3.sentence: He authored over 150 works on soil, geography, mineralogy, and geology.

77b4ccc3d2ad.title: Konstantin Glinka

8e2a97c59b82.title: Konstantin Glinka
8e2a97c59b82.sentence: It included the first schematic soil map of the world.

876d5bf1a6c3.sentence: Due to language barriers, the work of this team was not communicated to Western Europe until 1914 through a publication in German by Konstantin Glinka, a member of the Russian team.

3081ef239dfa.title: Konstantin Glinka
3081ef239dfa.sentence: A shortened version was interpreted into German, and from German into English by Curtis F. Marbut.

e8dc01c94116.title: Konstantin Glinka
e8dc01c94116.sentence: He became the first soil scientist elected to the Academy of Sciences of the USSR.

aea27dd727e2.title: Konstantin Glinka

61d7a407733d.title: Eugene W. Hilgard
61d7a407733d.sentence: Eugene Woldemar Hilgard (January 5, 1833 – January 8, 1916) was a German-American expert on pedology (the study of soil resources).

c592438cd278.title: Eugene W. Hilgard
c592438cd278.sentence: An authority on climate as a soil forming factor, soil chemistry and reclamation of alkali soils, he is considered as the father of modern soil science in the United States.

50e79f57be8d.title: Soil
50e79f57be8d.section: History of studies and research > Studies of soil formation
50e79f57be8d.sentence: In 1860, while in Mississippi, Eugene W. Hilgard (1833–1916) studied the relationship between rock material, climate, vegetation, and the type of soils that were developed.

e7edddacd2a1.title: Eugene W. Hilgard
e7edddacd2a1.sentence: From 1875 to 1904 he was professor of agricultural chemistry at the University of California, Berkeley and director of the state agricultural experiment station.

7c5cf9a2241b.title: Eugene W. Hilgard
7c5cf9a2241b.sentence: He conducted the agricultural division of the Northern Transcontinental Survey, 1881–1883, and made a specialty of the study of soils of the southwestern states and of the Pacific slope in their relation to geology, to their chemical and physical composition, to their native flora, and to their agricultural qualities.

ba48a09b1895.title: Eugene W. Hilgard
ba48a09b1895.sentence: He prepared for the United States Weather Bureau in 1892 a discussion of the Relations of Climate to Soils, which was translated into several European languages and gained for the author in 1894, from the Royal Bavarian Academy of Sciences, the Liebig medal for important advances in agricultural science.

12ec7ebc5513.title: Eugene W. Hilgard
12ec7ebc5513.sentence: Together with his book Soils (1906), Climate... established the basis for understanding climate as a factor of soil formation in the United States.
