c2dba15927d7.title: Lorenzo A. Richards
c2dba15927d7.sentence: Lorenzo Adolph Richards (April 24, 1904 – March 12, 1993) or known as Ren was one of the 20th century's most influential minds in the field of soil physics.

315161c65b65.title: Lorenzo A. Richards
315161c65b65.sentence: His PhD thesis, completed at Cornell University in 1931 and entitled Capillary conduction of liquids through porous mediums, was arguably one of the best known in the field of soil physics.

ff0a16a80aa7.title: Lorenzo A. Richards
ff0a16a80aa7.sentence: His thesis represented the first decisive progress beyond the work of Edgar Buckingham in the extension of Darcy's law to describe water movement in unsaturated soils.

35b319ad0105.title: Lorenzo A. Richards
35b319ad0105.sentence: In this research, Richards described a partial differential equation, now commonly known by as the Richards equation.

e3a8e9d3b9a2.title: Lorenzo A. Richards
e3a8e9d3b9a2.sentence: Richards also proposed the tension plate apparatus for determining capillary potential in soil.

b3977d3a311f.title: Lorenzo A. Richards
b3977d3a311f.sentence: In 1941 he published a paper describing the pressure-membrane apparatus.

9909104ee30a.title: Lorenzo A. Richards
9909104ee30a.sentence: Although Richards claimed the primary purpose of the apparatus was the extraction of soil solution for salinity analysis, he also pointed out its potential for application to energy studies.

19ecb757dbd0.title: Lorenzo A. Richards
19ecb757dbd0.sentence: Following his time at Cornell, and a brief stint at Iowa State University, he spent the most part of his working life engaged in soil physics research at the United States Department of Agriculture Salinity Laboratory in Riverside, California.

f1840c3e5ddc.title: Lorenzo A. Richards
f1840c3e5ddc.sentence: He developed much of the modern apparatus and methodology used for study of soil water, hence playing a pivotal role in the transformation of knowledge on this subject from the qualitative stage to one based on measurements and mathematics.

db00427b6b02.title: Justus von Liebig
db00427b6b02.sentence: Liebig synthesized ideas about the mineral theory of plant nutrition and added his own conviction that inorganic materials could provide nutrients as effectively as organic sources.

a5cc12007c6c.title: Justus von Liebig
a5cc12007c6c.sentence: He reported that plants acquire carbon (C) and hydrogen (H) from the atmosphere and from water (H2O).

7d3602028597.title: Justus von Liebig
7d3602028597.sentence: Nicolas-Théodore de Saussure's experiments, reported in Recherches Chimiques sur la Végétation (1804), suggested that carbon was obtained from atmospheric rather than soil-based sources.

73f7de275351.title: Justus von Liebig
73f7de275351.sentence: He also studied the absorption of minerals by plants, and observed that mineral concentrations in plants tended to reflect their presence in the soil in which the plants were grown.

caf4127c84a2.title: Justus von Liebig
caf4127c84a2.sentence: Using more precise methods of measurement as a basis for estimation, he pointed out contradictions such as the inability of existing soil humus to provide enough carbon to support the plants growing in it.

92855643cf42.title: Justus von Liebig
92855643cf42.sentence: By the late 1830s, researchers such as Karl Sprengel were using Liebig's methods of combustion analysis to assess manures, concluding that their value could be attributed to their constituent minerals.

38ab2b26f428.title: Justus von Liebig
38ab2b26f428.sentence: In his theory of mineral nutrients, Liebig identified the chemical elements of nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), and potassium (K) as essential to plant growth.

0ddbda4710c4.title: Justus von Liebig
0ddbda4710c4.sentence: A plant's development is limited by the one essential mineral that is in the relatively shortest supply.

85bd20b042fa.title: John Bennet Lawes
85bd20b042fa.sentence: Sir John Bennet Lawes, 1st Baronet, FRS (28 December 1814 – 31 August 1900) was an English entrepreneur and agricultural scientist.

730f743c4a6a.title: John Bennet Lawes
730f743c4a6a.sentence: He founded an experimental farm at his home at Rothamsted Manor that eventually became Rothamsted Research, where he developed a superphosphate that would mark the beginnings of the chemical fertilizer industry.

893ad62d0899.title: John Bennet Lawes
893ad62d0899.sentence: Before leaving Oxford in 1832, Lawes had begun to interest himself in growing various medicinal plants on the Estates and started to experiment on the effects of various manures on plants growing in pots.

114d62a0f09e.title: John Bennet Lawes
114d62a0f09e.sentence: A year or two later the experiments were extended to crops in the field in order to free farmers from relying on animals to produce fertilizer.

51835b31d5a7.title: John Bennet Lawes
51835b31d5a7.sentence: In 1842, he patented a manure formed by treating phosphates with sulphuric acid, and thus initiated the artificial manure industry.

402bd44b9a9f.title: John Bennet Lawes
402bd44b9a9f.sentence: In the succeeding year he enlisted the services of Joseph Henry Gilbert, with whom he experimented for more than half a century in raising crops and feeding animals, activities which have rendered Rothamsted famous to scientific agriculturists.

37fb335cd7c4.title: John Bennet Lawes
37fb335cd7c4.sentence: In 1854, he was elected a Fellow of the Royal Society, which in 1867 bestowed a Royal Medal on Lawes and Gilbert jointly, and in 1882 he was awarded the title of baronet.

b03a48e4703d.title: John Bennet Lawes
b03a48e4703d.sentence: In 1889, Lawes took measures to ensure the continued existence of the Rothamsted experimental farm by setting aside money solely for that purpose and so established The Lawes Agricultural Trust.

fc01ae748a26.title: John Bennet Lawes
fc01ae748a26.sentence: Rothamsted Experimental Station is the oldest agricultural research facility in the world.

6a2526067602.title: Guy D. Smith
6a2526067602.sentence: Guy Donald Smith (1907–1981) was a distinguished international soil scientist, who was born in Atlantic, Iowa.

d8a596aa17d9.title: Soil classification
d8a596aa17d9.sentence: The USDA classification was originally developed by Guy Donald Smith, director of the U.S. Department of Agriculture's soil survey investigations.

db6e43f2b830.title: Guy D. Smith
db6e43f2b830.sentence: Upon returning from his service to the US military, Guy was hired to work for the U.S. Department of Agriculture.

3c67b7e3fe5d.title: Guy D. Smith
3c67b7e3fe5d.sentence: In 1946, Guy worked as a soil correlator for the Soil Conservation Service in Iowa, and in 1952 he was made Director of Soil Survey Investigations.

a74a314f0aac.title: Guy D. Smith
a74a314f0aac.sentence: While working for the USDA, Guy was tasked with developing a method for classifying soils.

1130c9f9cf92.title: Guy D. Smith
1130c9f9cf92.sentence: He produced the 1st of seven iterations of what would eventually become a soil taxonomy system used worldwide.

04460fcfecc2.title: Guy D. Smith
04460fcfecc2.sentence: Guy collaborated with European soil scientists in developing Soil Taxonomy.

e41b8b7ac4c9.title: Guy D. Smith
e41b8b7ac4c9.sentence: Guy retired from the Soil Conservation Service in 1973.

30be3f12136a.title: Guy D. Smith
30be3f12136a.sentence: After retirement, he spent time consulting with international partners on the application of Soil Taxonomy worldwide.

5a81db726c3f.title: Guy D. Smith
5a81db726c3f.sentence: Guy died in 1981 in Ghent, Belgium, where he taught at the University of Ghent.

ab70426b7846.title: Rattan Lal
ab70426b7846.sentence: Rattan Lal (born 5 September 1944) is an Indian-American soil scientist.

6fb175e8e9fc.title: Rattan Lal
6fb175e8e9fc.sentence: He is considered a pioneer in soil-centric agricultural management to improve global food security and develop climate-resilient agriculture.

34c740ca935b.title: Rattan Lal
34c740ca935b.sentence: Lal worked as a senior research fellow with the University of Sydney from 1968 to 1969, and then as a soil physicist at the International Institute of Tropical Agriculture (IITA), Ibadan, Nigeria, from 1970 to 1987.

fc07c4d63c2f.title: Rattan Lal
fc07c4d63c2f.sentence: While in Nigeria, Lal discovered that organic carbon and other nutrients disappeared after deforestation and his research centered on mulching, cover crops and no-till farming to bring back the soil components.

1561dbfbd5d9.title: Rattan Lal
1561dbfbd5d9.sentence: His research diverged from the conventional 1970s soil fertility strategy of heavy reliance on commercial fertilizers.

3a00a3598139.title: Rattan Lal
3a00a3598139.sentence: His research led to a better understanding of how no-till farming, cover crops, crop residues, mulching, and agroforestry can restore degraded soils, increasing organic matter by sequestering atmospheric carbon in the soil, and help combat rising carbon dioxide levels in the air.

d1a766f0f582.title: Rattan Lal
d1a766f0f582.sentence: The research models Lal uses indicate that restoring soil health can lead to multiple benefits by 2100.

52812afd3816.title: Rattan Lal
52812afd3816.sentence: Benefits include doubling the global annual grain yield, decreasing the land area by 30% that is used for grain cultivation, and decreasing fertilizer use.

a723a4f72dab.title: Rattan Lal
a723a4f72dab.sentence: In 1987, he returned to the Ohio State University, where as of 2024 he is a Distinguished Professor of Soil Science as well as founder and Director of the CFAES Rattan Lal Center for Carbon Management and Sequestration (Lal Carbon Center).

7d24cc5b1f36.title: Rattan Lal
7d24cc5b1f36.sentence: In 2021, he and his team launched the C-FARM research project on carbon farming to provide in-field validation of how soil captures and stores carbon dioxide.

d31ad19ca554.title: Rattan Lal
d31ad19ca554.sentence: Lal served as president of the International Union of Soil Science from 2017 to 2018.

1a76aff1afb4.title: Rattan Lal
1a76aff1afb4.sentence: He has received the Padma Shri Award (2021), World Food Prize (2020), Arrell Global Food Innovation Award (2020), the Japan Prize (2019), the GCHERA World Agriculture Prize (2018), and the Glinka World Soil Prize (2018), among others, for his work.

249c588375bf.title: Rattan Lal
249c588375bf.sentence: This research earned him the Japan Prize in 2019.

fc5439855986.title: Hugh Hammond Bennett
fc5439855986.sentence: Hugh Hammond Bennett (April 15, 1881 – July 7, 1960) was a pioneer in the field of soil conservation in the United States of America.

5bdf1e1418be.title: Hugh Hammond Bennett
5bdf1e1418be.sentence: He was the head of the Soil Erosion Service, a federal agency now referred to as the Natural Resources Conservation Service.

c9355467ddb1.title: Hugh Hammond Bennett
c9355467ddb1.sentence: Immediately upon graduation, he became a soil surveyor, and conducted soil studies, both in the United States and in other countries, that eventually convinced him that soil erosion was a serious problem facing the planet.

4d9c2a7e210e.title: Hugh Hammond Bennett
4d9c2a7e210e.sentence: In 1905 at Louisa County, Virginia employed in a soil survey for the U.S. Department of Agriculture, the subject first realized the link between soil quality and erosion.

294a49cac5b9.title: Hugh Hammond Bennett
294a49cac5b9.sentence: He co-wrote a United States Department of Agriculture publication in 1928 titled Soil Erosion: A National Menace, which was regarded as his most influential work and garnered the attention of Representative James P. Buchanan of Texas.

a5486f3db09f.title: Hugh Hammond Bennett
a5486f3db09f.sentence: He found his opinions opposed by some colleagues, a supervisor stating, "The soil is the one indestructible... asset the nation possesses...

21c9dfa9481f.title: Hugh Hammond Bennett
21c9dfa9481f.sentence: It is the one resource that cannot be exhausted."

5e0311badefc.title: Hugh Hammond Bennett
5e0311badefc.sentence: Buchanan, who was a member of the United States House Committee on Appropriations, helped obtain funding in 1929 for soil erosion studies in the United States.

4ef960e074e7.title: Hugh Hammond Bennett
4ef960e074e7.sentence: Largely in response to Bennett's campaign for soil conservation, Representative James P. Buchanan of Texas attached an amendment to the 1930 appropriations bill authorizing the USDA to establish a series of soil erosion experiment stations.

94549841308e.title: Hugh Hammond Bennett
94549841308e.sentence: The locations for these stations were selected by Bennett, and involved teams of researchers establishing plots to measure erosion conditions under various types of crops, soils, rotations, and their responses to different agricultural managements practices and structures.

de45a2cb73c0.title: Hugh Hammond Bennett
de45a2cb73c0.sentence: When the Soil Erosion Service was established as part of the United States Department of the Interior in September 1933, Bennett became the director.

14feb983923d.title: Hugh Hammond Bennett
14feb983923d.sentence: He continued to speak out on soil conservation issues, especially through the Dust Bowl years, and eventually influenced the passage of the soil conservation act of April 27, 1935, which created the Soil Conservation Service at the USDA.

c0ee9db40738.title: Hugh Hammond Bennett
c0ee9db40738.sentence: He remained at the head of that organization until he retired in 1951.

edeeedbabe44.title: Hugh Hammond Bennett
edeeedbabe44.sentence: > Hugh Hammond Bennett, the head of the Soil Conservation Service, put Finnell in charge of Region Six, the hardest-hit area of the country; code name: "Operation Dustbowl." Finnell set up shop north of Dalhart.

220bccf6ddd8.title: Hugh Hammond Bennett
220bccf6ddd8.sentence: By May of 1936, nearly 40,000 farmers had joined him, and 5.5 million acres were under new terraced and contour-listed cultivation.

ecfdd81e30a0.title: Hugh Hammond Bennett
ecfdd81e30a0.sentence: The Coon Creek Watershed Project, in southwestern Wisconsin, was the first of many watershed-based projects initiated to demonstrate soil conservation practices to farmers.

5059f48e95b8.title: Hugh Hammond Bennett
5059f48e95b8.sentence: The creation of the Soil Conservation Service and its inclusion in the United States Department of Agriculture also marked the US government's acceptance and establishment of the interpretation of soils for soil and water conservation.

ead367e1a97e.title: Franklin Hiram King
ead367e1a97e.sentence: Franklin Hiram King (8 June 1848 – 4 August 1911) was an American agricultural scientist who was born on a farm near Whitewater, Wisconsin, attended country schools, and received his professional training first at Whitewater State Normal School, graduating in 1872, and then at Cornell University.

09bf29fa03a4.title: Franklin Hiram King
09bf29fa03a4.sentence: King served as a professor of agricultural physics at the University of Wisconsin–Madison from 1888 until 1902.

4f0faf077110.title: Franklin Hiram King
4f0faf077110.sentence: Interested in a wide range of subjects throughout his career, King made major contributions during these years in research and teaching that dealt with applications of physics to agriculture.

0b260f1c92a7.title: Franklin Hiram King
0b260f1c92a7.sentence: The impact of his career was greatest in the field of soil science.

ed9e19fc9b0a.title: Franklin Hiram King
ed9e19fc9b0a.sentence: King left Wisconsin to become chief of the Division of Soil Management in the USDA Bureau of Soils in Washington, D.C. in January 1902.

c29feb15e331.title: Franklin Hiram King
c29feb15e331.sentence: His findings in the next two years, that the concentration of nutrients in soil solution was correlated with crop yields, began to undermine beliefs held strongly by the chief of the bureau, Milton Whitney, about the relations of soil chemistry to plant growth and soil fertility.

5dad88a6e7f4.title: Franklin Hiram King
5dad88a6e7f4.sentence: King was forced to resign but privately published several additional papers from his research during this period.

0a86633bd6ab.title: Franklin Hiram King
0a86633bd6ab.sentence: King is now best remembered for his first-hand account of traditional agricultural practices in Asia, now regarded as an organic farming classic text.

9cd1557fc9fc.title: Franklin Hiram King
9cd1557fc9fc.sentence: Three of his seven books were written during that period, the best known of which is Farmers of Forty Centuries, or Permanent Agriculture in China, Korea, and Japan, which recounted his investigations into what would now be called organic farming or sustainable agriculture during a nine-month tour of Asia in 1909.

db0db6833048.title: Jean-Baptiste Boussingault
db0db6833048.sentence: Jean-Baptiste Joseph Dieudonné Boussingault (2 February 1801 – 11 May 1887) was a French chemist who made significant contributions to agricultural science, petroleum science and metallurgy.

c824d3f6a46a.title: Jean-Baptiste Boussingault
c824d3f6a46a.sentence: From 1836 he devoted himself mainly to agricultural chemistry and animal and vegetable physiology, with occasional excursions into mineral chemistry.

2cd1f5c7bf09.title: Jean-Baptiste Boussingault
2cd1f5c7bf09.sentence: Boussingault established the first agricultural experiment station on his wife's property in Pechelbronn in Alsace, France some 60 km north of Strasbourg, France in 1836.

6dd25e295e12.title: Jean-Baptiste Boussingault
6dd25e295e12.sentence: Rothamsted in the UK, generally considered the longest continuous experimental station was started some seven years later in 1843, and the German equivalent in Moeckern in 1852.

b98fdd911c20.title: Jean-Baptiste Boussingault
b98fdd911c20.sentence: Boussingault re-introduced the quantitative methods first employed by de Saussure and is credited with the following discoveries related to agriculture:

627c6e1039ef.title: Jean-Baptiste Boussingault
627c6e1039ef.sentence: - the first analysis of crops grown in a rotation

43d1ed95c24f.title: Jean-Baptiste Boussingault
43d1ed95c24f.sentence: - the increase in soil nitrogen following the growth of legume crops

d4594cce77b3.title: Jean-Baptiste Boussingault
d4594cce77b3.sentence: - plant growth is proportional to the amount of available assimilatory nitrogen, which in practical terms allows greater plant growth from the simultaneous application of phosphorus and nitrogen

c8f6c6db90c3.title: Jean-Baptiste Boussingault
c8f6c6db90c3.sentence: His work included papers on the quantity of nitrogen in different foods, the amount of gluten in different wheats, investigations on the question whether plants can assimilate free nitrogen from the atmosphere (which he answered in the negative and propose the basis of what became known as the nitrogen cycle), the respiration of plants, the function of their leaves, the action and value of manures and chemical fertilizers, and other similar subjects.

4c3167e6b8ab.title: Jean-Baptiste Boussingault
4c3167e6b8ab.sentence: Later he became professor of chemistry at Lyon, and in 1839 was appointed to the chair of agricultural and analytical chemistry at the Conservatoire des Arts et Metiers in Paris.

76c2f743ab66.title: Jean-Baptiste Boussingault
76c2f743ab66.sentence: His experimental station did not survive him, or rather could not withstand the vacillations of the 1870 Franco-Prussian war despite some revealing respect for intellectual works in WWII anecdotes, but his discoveries were built on by others, including his better known contemporary, Liebig – who loudly acknowledged Boussingault as the pioneer and great discoverer of many advances in soil and plant chemistry.

75f912bdb82e.title: Jean-Baptiste Boussingault
75f912bdb82e.sentence: His works and experiments contributed to an understanding of the critical role of nitrogen in plant growth and ecological systems.

6f68fc156bbc.title: Jean-Baptiste Boussingault
6f68fc156bbc.sentence: These developments, such as the Haber–Bosch process, eventually resulted in nitrogen fertilizers and related products.

d8f5eff5a2d3.title: Edmund Ruffin
d8f5eff5a2d3.sentence: Edmund Ruffin III (January 5, 1794 – June 17, 1865) was an American planter, politician, scientist, and activist best known as an early advocate for secession of the Southern slave states from the United States.

5bf064cde6b5.title: Edmund Ruffin
5bf064cde6b5.sentence: Ruffin is also known for his pioneering work in methods to preserve and improve soil productivity.

2df2233482f9.title: Edmund Ruffin
2df2233482f9.sentence: Ruffin, like many other planters in Virginia, farmed using slaves.

db9cbee119d9.title: Edmund Ruffin
db9cbee119d9.sentence: While in his twenties, Ruffin began experimenting with marl to rejuvenate the soil on his land, which had been worn out by more than a century of monoculture of tobacco, a crop that consumes many nutrients from the soil.

eac9c7dd4616.title: Edmund Ruffin
eac9c7dd4616.sentence: He recommended crop rotation and amendments to restore soils exhausted from tobacco monoculture.

78a99a248cf3.title: Edmund Ruffin
78a99a248cf3.sentence: Early in his career, he studied bogs and swamps to learn how to correct soil acidity.

db793f48acef.title: Edmund Ruffin
db793f48acef.sentence: He experimented using lime to raise pH in peat soils.

717da828bfd9.title: Edmund Ruffin
717da828bfd9.sentence: Ruffin presented a paper, later expanded into an article for American Farmer and eventually into the highly influential book An Essay on Calcareous Manures (1852).

732fdeaa785d.title: Edmund Ruffin
732fdeaa785d.sentence: He explained how applications of calcareous earths (marl) had reduced soil acidity and improved yields of mixed crops of corn and wheat on his land, which had been worn out by two centuries of tobacco farming.

0d2772378dbe.title: Edmund Ruffin
0d2772378dbe.sentence: However, his advice to use marl was not widely followed in his own time.

b6f01a23f777.title: Edmund Ruffin
b6f01a23f777.sentence: He has since become known as "the father of soil science" in the United States.

de63d0b94244.title: Edgar Buckingham
de63d0b94244.sentence: Edgar Buckingham (July 8, 1867 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania – April 29, 1940 in Washington DC) was an American physicist.

c159fe9643f9.title: Edgar Buckingham
c159fe9643f9.sentence: He worked as a soil physicist at the USDA Bureau of Soils from 1902 to 1906.

839084b3d86b.title: Edgar Buckingham
839084b3d86b.sentence: Buckingham's first work on soil physics is on soil aeration, particularly the loss of carbon dioxide from the soil and its subsequent replacement by oxygen.

d557b1bccd50.title: Edgar Buckingham
d557b1bccd50.sentence: From his experiments he found that the rate of gas diffusion in soil was not dependent significantly on the soil structure, compactness or water content of the soil.

8820774f74ab.title: Edgar Buckingham
8820774f74ab.sentence: Using an empirical formula based on his data, Buckingham was able to give the diffusion coefficient as a function of air content.

a61194495a24.title: Edgar Buckingham
a61194495a24.sentence: This relation is still commonly cited in many modern textbooks and used in modern research.

216e08b3b4bb.title: Edgar Buckingham
216e08b3b4bb.sentence: The outcomes of his research on gas transport were to conclude that the exchange of gases in soil aeration takes place by diffusion and is sensibly independent of the variations of the outside barometric pressure.

55caca1e000c.title: Edgar Buckingham
55caca1e000c.sentence: Buckingham's work on soil water is published in Bulletin 38 USDA Bureau of Soils: Studies on the movement of soil moisture, which was released in 1907.

e904a5a08cfd.title: Edgar Buckingham
e904a5a08cfd.sentence: He found that soils of various textures could strongly inhibit evaporation, particularly where capillary flow through the uppermost layers was prevented.

e2faa9015d2c.title: Edgar Buckingham
e2faa9015d2c.sentence: Buckingham found evaporative losses were initially higher from the arid soil, then after three days the evaporation under arid conditions became less than under humid conditions, with the total loss ending up greater from the humid soil.

7cbd03de2723.title: Edgar Buckingham
7cbd03de2723.sentence: Buckingham believed this occurred due to the self-mulching behaviour (he referred to it as the soil forming a natural mulch) exhibited by the soil under arid conditions.

a8f532fc10e5.title: Edgar Buckingham
a8f532fc10e5.sentence: He firstly recognized the importance of the potential of the forces arising from interactions between soil and water.

03fb4f8f8625.title: Edgar Buckingham
03fb4f8f8625.sentence: He called this the capillary potential, this is now known as the moisture or water potential (matric potential).

a8c6e90ea438.title: Edgar Buckingham
a8c6e90ea438.sentence: He combined capillary theory and an energy potential in soil physics theory, and was the first to expound the dependence of soil hydraulic conductivity on capillary potential.

902b620effc3.title: Edgar Buckingham
902b620effc3.sentence: He also applied a formula equivalent to Darcy's law to unsaturated flow.

8c940f43b424.title: Justus von Liebig
8c940f43b424.sentence: In addition to emphasizing the importance of minerals in the soil, he argued that plants feed on nitrogen compounds derived from the air.

eb5f4b8383be.title: Justus von Liebig
eb5f4b8383be.sentence: This assertion was a source of contention for many years, and turned out to be true for legumes, but not for other plants.

7cdbbec509c6.title: Justus von Liebig
7cdbbec509c6.sentence: In the first two editions of his book (1840, 1842), Liebig reported that the atmosphere contained insufficient nitrogen, and argued that nitrogen-based fertilizer was needed to grow the healthiest possible crops.

9f54c0b2df97.title: Justus von Liebig
9f54c0b2df97.sentence: Liebig believed that nitrogen could be supplied in the form of ammonia, and recognized the possibility of substituting chemical fertilizers for natural ones (animal dung, etc.)

54891f9738de.title: Justus von Liebig
54891f9738de.sentence: He later became convinced that nitrogen was sufficiently supplied by precipitation of ammonia from the atmosphere, and argued vehemently against the use of nitrogen-based fertilizers for many years.

9cd50fd88607.title: Justus von Liebig
9cd50fd88607.sentence: An early commercial attempt to produce his own fertilizers was unsuccessful, due to lack of nitrogen in the mixtures.

1763c6a373b8.title: Justus von Liebig
1763c6a373b8.sentence: When tested in a farmer's field, Liebig's manure was found to have no appreciable effect.

c9c34fad4058.title: Justus von Liebig
c9c34fad4058.sentence: By the publication of the seventh German edition of Agricultural Chemistry he had moderated some of his views, admitting some mistakes and returning to the position that nitrogen-based fertilizers were beneficial or even necessary.He was instrumental in the use of guano for nitrogen.

8f827b0bc3e9.title: Selman Waksman
8f827b0bc3e9.sentence: Selman Abraham Waksman (22 July [O.S. 10 July] 1888 – August 16, 1973) was a Russian-born American inventor, biochemist and microbiologist, whose research into the decomposition of organisms that live in soil enabled the discovery of streptomycin and several other antibiotics.

3ada2468c60e.title: Selman Waksman
3ada2468c60e.sentence: During his graduate study, he worked under J. G. Lipman at the New Jersey Agricultural Experiment Station at Rutgers performing research in soil bacteriology.

a964c260b818.title: Selman Waksman
a964c260b818.sentence: Waksman spent some months in 1915–1916 at the United States Department of Agriculture in Washington, DC under Charles Thom, studying soil fungi.

9270730e8998.title: Selman Waksman
9270730e8998.sentence: - Humus: origin, chemical composition, and importance in nature (1936, 1938)

5aba42980213.title: Selman Waksman
5aba42980213.sentence: At Rutgers, Waksman's team discovered several antibiotics, including actinomycin, clavacin, streptothricin, streptomycin, grisein, neomycin, fradicin, candicidin, candidin.

b042090e471e.title: Selman Waksman
b042090e471e.sentence: A professor of biochemistry and microbiology at Rutgers University for four decades, he discovered several antibiotics (and introduced the modern sense of that word to name them), and he introduced procedures that have led to the development of many others.

62a96c30ef9e.title: Selman Waksman
62a96c30ef9e.sentence: Waksman had been studying the Streptomyces family of organisms since his college student days and had, for a time, been studying the organism Streptomyces griseus.

963e01365c25.title: Selman Waksman
963e01365c25.sentence: Streptomycin was isolated from S. griseus and found effective against tuberculosis by one of Waksman's graduate students, Albert Schatz.

5115637d7641.title: Selman Waksman
5115637d7641.sentence: Streptomycin was the first effective drug against gram-negative bacteria and the first antibiotic used to cure tuberculosis.

41ac30fa7b8c.title: Selman Waksman
41ac30fa7b8c.sentence: He won the Nobel Prize for "ingenious, systematic, and successful studies of the soil microbes that led to the discovery of streptomycin." During his Nobel Prize award presentation, Waksman was called "one of the greatest benefactors to mankind," as the result of his discovery of streptomycin.

ea8abb59f3cc.title: Selman Waksman
ea8abb59f3cc.sentence: The details and credit for the discovery of streptomycin and its usefulness as an antibiotic were strongly contested by Albert Schatz, leading to litigation in 1950.

2b489f0ad361.title: Selman Waksman
2b489f0ad361.sentence: Waksman and Rutgers settled out of court with Schatz, resulting in financial remuneration and entitlement to "legal and scientific credit as co-discoverer of streptomycin." Schatz was awarded $120,000 for patent rights and 3% of royalties.

4de49e4bc680.title: Carl Sprengel
4de49e4bc680.sentence: Karl or Philipp Carl Sprengel (29 March 1787 – 19 April 1859) was a German botanist from Schillerslage (now part of Burgdorf, Hanover).

1c4cab610d3c.title: Carl Sprengel
1c4cab610d3c.sentence: Influenced by (one of the students at Regenwalde Akademie der Landwirtschaft) Felicjan Sypniewski theories, Sprengel was the first to formulate the "theory of minimum" in agricultural chemistry, meaning that plant growth is limited by the essential nutrient at the lowest concentration.

e38867a6fb9a.title: Carl Sprengel
e38867a6fb9a.sentence: Sprengel worked under Albrecht Thaer (1752–1828) in Celle.

7a5df8095d5d.title: Carl Sprengel
7a5df8095d5d.sentence: He then worked from 1804 to 1808 with Heinrich Einhof (1778–1808) in Möglin on agricultural studies.

a79a55e57812.title: Carl Sprengel
a79a55e57812.sentence: Between 1821 and 1828, he studied natural sciences in Göttingen, where he eventually became professor.

822112adae98.title: Carl Sprengel
822112adae98.sentence: This rule, often incorrectly attributed to Justus von Liebig as Liebig's law of the minimum, was instead only popularised later as a scientific concept by Liebig.

7460b50d3788.title: Carl Sprengel
7460b50d3788.sentence: Having his financial needs satisfied, finally he could fulfil his dream and establish Regenwalde Akademie der Landwirtschaft (Academy of Agriculture in Resko), where he taught, studied and lived until his death in 1859.

c0a3dcfc40d2.title: Carl Sprengel
c0a3dcfc40d2.sentence: - 1839: Die Lehre vom Dünger oder Beschreibung aller bei der Landwirthschaft gebräuchlicher vegetablilischer, animalischer und mineralischer Düngermaterialien, nebst Erklärung ihrer Wirkungsart, Leipzig

fe8873dbac1a.title: Carl Sprengel
fe8873dbac1a.sentence: - 1844: Die Bodenkunde oder die Lehre von Boden, nebst einer volständigen Anleitung zur chemischen Analyse der Ackererden via Internet Archive

f1bdfdd86ba4.title: Joseph Henry Gilbert
f1bdfdd86ba4.sentence: Sir Joseph Henry Gilbert FRS (1 August 1817 – 23 December 1901) was an English chemist, noteworthy for his long career spent improving the methods of practical agriculture.

aa4299c12c38.title: Joseph Henry Gilbert
aa4299c12c38.sentence: At the age of 24 he entered university studying chemistry first at Glasgow under Thomas Thomson; then at University College, London, in the laboratory of Anthony Todd Thomson (1778-1849), the professor of medical jurisprudence, also attending Thomas Graham's lectures; he also studied German in order to pursue his doctorate at the University of Giessen under Justus von Liebig.

4e4de0cc34ba.title: Joseph Henry Gilbert
4e4de0cc34ba.sentence: On his return to England from Germany he acted for a year or so as assistant to his old master A. T. Thomson at University College, and in 1843, after spending a short time in the study of calico dyeing and printing near Manchester, accepted the directorship of the chemical laboratory at the agricultural experiment station established by John Bennet Lawes at Rothamsted, near St. Albans.

2c90847d3bf1.title: Joseph Henry Gilbert
2c90847d3bf1.sentence: Gilbert moved there in June 1843 and worked there until his death on 23 December 1901.

ab4c6390e4a6.title: Joseph Henry Gilbert
ab4c6390e4a6.sentence: Although much of the work went under both their names, the chemist who conducted most of the meticulous studies was Gilbert.

d3a50d8ceb17.title: Agricultural science
d3a50d8ceb17.sentence: In 1843, John Bennet Lawes and Joseph Henry Gilbert began a set of long-term field experiments at Rothamsted Research in England, some of which are still running as of 2018.

0a9c94fa9a64.title: Agriculture
0a9c94fa9a64.sentence: Research became more systematic when in 1843, John Lawes and Henry Gilbert began a set of long-term agronomy field experiments at Rothamsted Research Station in England; some of them, such as the Park Grass Experiment, are still running.

5149f4978692.title: Joseph Henry Gilbert
5149f4978692.sentence: One of the key findings of Lawes and Gilbert was that cereal crops took up nitrogen from the soil, contrary to the ideas of Justus von Liebig who held that it was obtained only from the air.

9c3dd797d61b.title: Joseph Henry Gilbert
9c3dd797d61b.sentence: Their work made Rothamstead a leading centre of agricultural research.

71d763c3fe3f.title: Joseph Henry Gilbert
71d763c3fe3f.sentence: Gilbert was elected a fellow of the Royal Society in 1860, and in 1867 was awarded a Royal Medal jointly with Lawes.

96c53154d49c.title: Sergei Winogradsky
96c53154d49c.sentence: Winogradsky is best known for discovering chemoautotrophy, which soon became popularly known as chemosynthesis, the process by which organisms derive energy from a number of different inorganic compounds and obtain carbon in the form of carbon dioxide.

88d0f20e97d3.title: Sergei Winogradsky
88d0f20e97d3.sentence: Previously, it was believed that autotrophs obtained their energy solely from light, not from reactions of inorganic compounds.

64bd9d697d88.title: Sergei Winogradsky
64bd9d697d88.sentence: With the discovery of organisms that oxidized inorganic compounds such as hydrogen sulfide and ammonium as energy sources, autotrophs could be divided into two groups: photoautotrophs and chemoautotrophs.

a6f49c06e351.title: Sergei Winogradsky
a6f49c06e351.sentence: This research provided the first example of lithotrophy, but not autotrophy.

4d721c98e513.title: Sergei Winogradsky
4d721c98e513.sentence: His research on nitrifying bacteria would report the first known form of chemoautotrophy, showing how a lithotroph fixes carbon dioxide (CO2) to make organic compounds.

73b67a087b8d.title: Konstantin Gedroits
73b67a087b8d.sentence: Konstantin Kaetanovich Gedroits (Russian: Константин Каэтанович Гедройц; 25 March 1872 – 5 October 1932) was a Russian soil scientist of Lithuanian origins.

15b9b38c72ea.title: Konstantin Gedroits
15b9b38c72ea.sentence: Gedroits was the founder of colloidal soil chemistry in Russia.

3a3b172e96dc.title: Konstantin Gedroits
3a3b172e96dc.sentence: He introduced the concept of "soil absorbing complex" and singled out several types of soil absorption capacity, including mechanical, physico-chemical and biological.

e841debcbcce.title: Konstantin Gedroits
e841debcbcce.sentence: He also developed a classification of soils based on the difference in the composition, which included soils unsaturated with cations, soils saturated with calcium and sodium ions, etc. He explained the evolution of saline soils from the chemical point of view, and developed a theoretical basics of liming and of the introduction of gypsum into the soil.

e3524e4acb5e.title: Konstantin Gedroits
e3524e4acb5e.sentence: After that he led the chemistry laboratory of the Dokuchaev Soil Institute in Moscow (1915–17) and the Department of Soil Science of the Forest Institute in Saint Petersburg (1917–30).

93cbd6935cf4.title: Konstantin Gedroits
93cbd6935cf4.sentence: In 1929–30 he headed the Dokuchaev Soil Institute, and in 1927 was elected as president of the International Union of Soil Sciences.

20da4075d492.title: Konstantin Gedroits
20da4075d492.sentence: He was a full member of the Academy of Sciences of the Soviet Union and a president of the International Union of Soil Sciences (1927–1930).

23489bb21696.title: Konstantin Gedroits
23489bb21696.sentence: For his achievement in soil science, Gedroits was awarded the Lenin Prize in 1927.

7acfe118ab4d.title: Peter Erasmus Müller (forester)
7acfe118ab4d.sentence: Peter Erasmus Müller (1840 – 1926) was a Danish forester and naturalist.

207de62dc7f0.title: Peter Erasmus Müller (forester)
207de62dc7f0.sentence: PE Müller had an extensive scientific writing output, published among other things in the series of articles "Studier over Skovjord" (1878—84), which appeared in the Journal of Forestry published by him.

dab2ccbfadf3.title: Peter Erasmus Müller (forester)
dab2ccbfadf3.sentence: - Studies on Forest Soil (1879 and 1884; translated into German and French),

305e19a7f5a5.title: Peter Erasmus Müller (forester)
305e19a7f5a5.sentence: In 1875, he began publishing Tidsskrift for Skovbrug as the first independent journal of Danish forestry, thereby laying the foundation for all subsequent forestry literature.

6daf284e95ff.title: Peter Erasmus Müller (forester)
6daf284e95ff.sentence: In this journal he published the results of his forestry studies, of which especially those concerning the forest soil have had a profound influence by demonstrating the influence of plant communities and the associated animals on the Earth's surface, such as the formation of heathland, the emergence of Red soil as a result of the peat that forms on top of the soil, and similar phenomena in the forest.

059819bf0b63.title: Peter Erasmus Müller (forester)
059819bf0b63.sentence: As late as 1924, Müller published through the Danish Academy of Sciences a last major literary work: Contributions to the Natural History of the Jutland Heaths, Karup Heaths and Related Formations, the main result of which was that the Danish heaths must be assumed to lie as a direct continuation of the tundra that arose after the ice age, from which it follows that they have not been forested in the same way as the hilly heaths, the heath marshes and the banks along the river valleys.

7edc5e1ec4f6.title: Charles Darwin
7edc5e1ec4f6.sentence: Charles Robert Darwin (/ˈdɑːrwɪn/ DAR-win; 12 February 1809 – 19 April 1882) was an English naturalist, geologist, and biologist, widely known for his contributions to evolutionary biology.

31ac235a9d79.title: Charles Darwin
31ac235a9d79.sentence: However, it was his five-year voyage on HMS Beagle from 1831 to 1836 that established Darwin as an eminent geologist.

487c0e778bba.title: Charles Darwin
487c0e778bba.sentence: His uncle Josiah pointed out an area of ground where cinders had disappeared under loam.

1a543d978df7.title: Charles Darwin
1a543d978df7.sentence: Darwin suggested that this might have been the work of earthworms, inspiring "a new & important theory" on their role in soil formation, which he presented at the Geological Society on 1 November 1837.

56e794e5125d.title: Charles Darwin
56e794e5125d.sentence: His final book was The Formation of Vegetable Mould, through the Actions of Worms (1881).

730f3b4c3d8a.title: Charles Darwin
730f3b4c3d8a.sentence: While On the Origin of Species dominates perceptions of his work, The Descent of Man and The Expression of the Emotions in Man and Animals had considerable impact, and his books on plants including The Power of Movement in Plants were innovative studies of great importance, as was his final work on The Formation of Vegetable Mould Through the Action of Worms.

9ea7d7738cc7.title: Nicolas Théodore de Saussure
9ea7d7738cc7.sentence: Nicolas-Théodore de Saussure (French pronunciation: [nikɔla teɔdɔʁ də sosyʁ]; 14 October 1767 – 18 April 1845) was a Swiss chemist and student of plant physiology who made seminal advances in phytochemistry.

af56c55ef8fe.title: Nicolas Théodore de Saussure
af56c55ef8fe.sentence: He is one of the major pioneers in the study of photosynthesis.

4e0cf7bbff26.title: Nicolas Théodore de Saussure
4e0cf7bbff26.sentence: He became interested in the chemistry and physiology of plants, including gas exchange and the ways that different soils affected their growth.

46f9ec091c4b.title: Nicolas Théodore de Saussure
46f9ec091c4b.sentence: His early papers on these subjects laid the groundwork for some of the chapters in his magnum opus, Recherches chimiques sur la Végétation ("Chemical Research on Plant Growth"), published in 1804.

8aaca585d02f.title: Nicolas Théodore de Saussure
8aaca585d02f.sentence: In contrast to some of his predecessors in the field of photosynthesis research, Saussure based his conclusions on extensive quantitative data that he had collected.

438335864900.title: Nicolas Théodore de Saussure
438335864900.sentence: In addition, Saussure demonstrated that plants obtain their carbon from the carbon dioxide in the atmosphere, not through uptake from humus in the soil, as his immediate predecessors in photosynthesis research had generally believed.

0ce67eae5610.title: Nicolas Théodore de Saussure

40b461e36e20.sentence: The presence of olivine, which is an easily weatherable primary mineral, has been interpreted to mean that physical rather than chemical weathering processes currently dominate on Mars.

ca324cfa9520.title: Martian regolith
ca324cfa9520.sentence: It is believed that large quantities of water and carbon dioxide ices remain frozen within the regolith in the equatorial parts of Mars and on its surface at higher latitudes.

76a6509e823c.title: Martian regolith
76a6509e823c.sentence: According to the High Energy Neutron Detector of the Mars Odyssey satellite the water content of Martian regolith is up to 5% by weight.

6db2268e43ef.title: Martian regolith
6db2268e43ef.sentence: High concentrations of ice in regolith is thought to be the cause of accelerated soil creep, which forms the rounded "softened terrain" characteristic of the Martian midlatitudes.

c00d0acdf425.title: Martian regolith
c00d0acdf425.sentence: In June 2008, the Phoenix lander returned data showing Martian regolith to be slightly alkaline and containing vital nutrients such as magnesium, sodium, potassium and chloride, all of which are ingredients for living organisms to grow on Earth.

9f34ea1d7412.title: Martian regolith
9f34ea1d7412.sentence: However, in August 2008, the Phoenix Lander conducted simple chemistry experiments, mixing water from Earth with Martian soil in an attempt to test its pH, and discovered traces of the salt perchlorate, while also confirming many scientists' hypotheses that the Martian surface was considerably basic, measuring at 8.3.

c47ea172f6c4.title: Martian regolith
c47ea172f6c4.sentence: On October 17, 2012 (Curiosity rover at "Rocknest"), the first X-ray diffraction analysis of Martian regolith was performed.

f2b9d5908121.title: Martian regolith
f2b9d5908121.sentence: The results revealed the presence of several minerals, including feldspar, pyroxenes and olivine, and suggested that the Martian regolith in the sample was similar to the "weathered basaltic soils" of Hawaiian volcanoes.

b547a0ebd0d2.title: Martian regolith
b547a0ebd0d2.sentence: Research on Earth is currently limited to using Martian regolith simulants, such as the MGS-1 simulant produced by Exolith Lab, which are based on the analysis from the various Mars spacecraft.

d3024a6c2b9b.title: Martian regolith
d3024a6c2b9b.sentence: A number of Mars sample return missions are being planned, which would allow actual Martian regolith to be returned to Earth for more advanced analysis than is possible in situ on the surface of Mars.

2e9670de779a.title: Martian regolith
2e9670de779a.sentence: This should allow even more accurate simulants.

052acbf00d15.title: Martian regolith
052acbf00d15.sentence: The first of these missions is a multi-part mission beginning with the Mars 2020 lander.

1e01f64757dd.title: Lunar regolith simulant
1e01f64757dd.sentence: A lunar regolith simulant is a terrestrial material synthesized in order to approximate the chemical, mechanical, engineering, mineralogical, or particle-size distribution properties of lunar regolith.

785460754b32.title: Lunar regolith simulant
785460754b32.sentence: Lunar regolith simulants are used by researchers who wish to research the materials handling, excavation, transportation, and uses of lunar regolith.

0f94ed374599.title: Lunar regolith simulant
0f94ed374599.sentence: Samples of actual lunar regolith are too scarce, and too small, for such research, and have been contaminated by exposure to Earth's atmosphere.

0d1012c5ef2b.title: Lunar regolith simulant
0d1012c5ef2b.sentence: In the run-up to the Apollo program, crushed terrestrial rocks were first used to simulate the anticipated soils that astronauts would encounter on the lunar surface.

56eca165c688.title: Lunar regolith simulant
56eca165c688.sentence: In some cases the properties of these early simulants were substantially different from actual lunar soil, and the issues associated with the pervasive, fine-grained, sharp dust grains on the Moon came as a surprise.

432ed4a4c72a.title: Lunar regolith simulant
432ed4a4c72a.sentence: Many of these were given three-letter acronyms to distinguish them (e.g., MLS-1, JSC-1), and numbers to designate subsequent versions.

931249968c58.title: Lunar regolith simulant
931249968c58.sentence: These simulants were broadly divided into highlands or mare soils, and were usually produced by crushing and sieving analogous terrestrial rocks (anorthosite for highlands, basalt for mare).

d31baf0fa952.title: Lunar regolith simulant
d31baf0fa952.sentence: Returned Apollo and Luna samples were used as reference materials in order to target specific properties such as elemental chemistry or particle size distribution.

d1ad93f58015.title: Lunar regolith simulant
d1ad93f58015.sentence: JSC-1 (Johnson Space Center Number One) was a lunar regolith simulant that was developed in 1994 by NASA and the Johnson Space Center.

c52e514083ba.title: Lunar regolith simulant
c52e514083ba.sentence: Its developers intended it to approximate the lunar soil of the maria.

382a12ac3e65.title: Lunar regolith simulant
382a12ac3e65.sentence: It was sourced from a basaltic ash with a high glass content.

0882f3e5bb14.title: Lunar regolith simulant
0882f3e5bb14.sentence: Many of these simulants were criticized by prominent lunar scientist Larry Taylor for a lack of quality control and wasted money on features like nanophase iron that had no documented purpose.

8be0f913ca7a.title: Lunar regolith simulant
8be0f913ca7a.sentence: JSC-1A can geopolymerize in an alkaline solutions resulting in a hard, rock-like, material.

3af31ead6774.title: Lunar regolith simulant
3af31ead6774.sentence: Tests show that the maximum compressive and flexural strength of the 'lunar' geopolymer is comparable to that of conventional cements.

bd6a77f1d1d8.title: Lunar regolith simulant
bd6a77f1d1d8.sentence: Other simulants include Lunar Highlands Simulant (LHS-1) and Lunar Mare Simulant (LMS-1) produced and distributed by the not-for-profit Exolith Lab run out of the University of Central Florida.

186911a46227.title: Lunar regolith simulant
186911a46227.sentence: Indian Space Research Organisation has developed its own lunar highland soil simulant called LSS-ISAC1 for its Chandrayaan programme.

4bc5038a7a77.title: Space weathering
4bc5038a7a77.sentence: Space weathering is the type of weathering that occurs to any object exposed to the harsh environment of outer space.

8822e13a2a5c.title: Space weathering
8822e13a2a5c.sentence: Bodies without atmospheres (including the Moon, Mercury, the asteroids, comets, and most of the moons of other planets) take on many weathering processes:

5ada78f8030c.title: Space weathering
5ada78f8030c.sentence: - collisions of galactic cosmic rays and solar cosmic rays,

b75fcd8f4414.title: Space weathering
b75fcd8f4414.sentence: - irradiation, implantation, and sputtering from solar wind particles, and

b517c6118c3a.title: Space weathering
b517c6118c3a.sentence: - bombardment by different sizes of meteorites and micrometeorites.

7bfb690af52c.title: Space weathering
7bfb690af52c.sentence: Much of our knowledge of the space weathering process comes from studies of the lunar samples returned by the Apollo program, particularly the lunar soils (or regolith).

b72bccfa5985.title: Space weathering
b72bccfa5985.sentence: The constant flux of high energy particles and micrometeorites, along with larger meteorites, act to comminute, melt, sputter and vaporize components of the lunar soil.

dc6b6289093c.title: Space weathering
dc6b6289093c.sentence: These are created when micrometeorites melt a small amount of material, which incorporates surrounding glass and mineral fragments into a glass-welded aggregate ranging in size from a few micrometers to a few millimeters.

b546c83d78f6.title: Space weathering
b546c83d78f6.sentence: Agglutinates are very common in lunar soil, accounting for as much as 60 to 70% of mature soils.

0565679b2048.title: Space weathering
0565679b2048.sentence: These very small (one to a few hundred nanometers in diameter) blebs of metallic iron are created when iron-bearing minerals (e.g. olivine and pyroxene) are vaporized and the iron is liberated and redeposited in its native form.

8f182dcfd9d6.title: Space weathering
8f182dcfd9d6.sentence: It wasn't until the 1990s that improved instruments, in particular transmission electron microscopes, and techniques allowed for the discovery of very thin (60-200 nm) patinas, or rims, which develop on individual lunar soil grains as a result of the redepositing of vapor from nearby micrometeorite impacts and the redeposition of material sputtered from nearby grains.

dfd989dd097c.title: Space weathering
dfd989dd097c.sentence: On the Moon, the spectral effects of space weathering are threefold: as the lunar surface matures it becomes darker (the albedo is reduced), redder (reflectance increases with increasing wavelength), and the depth of its diagnostic absorption bands are reduced These effects are largely due to the presence of nanophase iron in both the agglutinates and in the accreted rims on individual grains.

958773c0d180.title: Space weathering
958773c0d180.sentence: Young, fresh craters have bright ray systems, because they have exposed fresh, unweathered material, but over time those rays disappear as the weathering process darkens the material.

5ca7142f5973.title: Space weathering
5ca7142f5973.sentence: Space weathering is important because these processes affect the physical and optical properties of the surface of many planetary bodies.

ba9b5c46fbe0.title: Space weathering
ba9b5c46fbe0.sentence: Therefore, it is critical to understand the effects of space weathering in order to properly interpret remotely sensed data.

9e2c0ce7a804.title: Space weathering
9e2c0ce7a804.sentence: Therefore, space weathering should occur more slowly and to a lesser degree on the surfaces of asteroids.

75295266b7e0.title: Space weathering
75295266b7e0.sentence: In addition, definitive evidence of space weathering alteration has been identified in the grains of soil returned by the Hayabusa spacecraft.

3f98ab83691b.title: Space weathering
3f98ab83691b.sentence: Per unit area, impacts on Mercury are expected to produce 13.5x the melt and 19.5x the vapor produced on the Moon.

770d42ffb4bb.title: Astropedology
770d42ffb4bb.sentence: Astropedology is the study of very ancient paleosols and meteorites relevant to the origin of life and different planetary soil systems.

d6c0c9c461e0.title: Astropedology
d6c0c9c461e0.sentence: It is a branch of soil science (pedology) concerned with soils of the distant geologic past and of other planetary bodies to understand Earth's place in the universe.

ef2b63bf234d.title: Astropedology
ef2b63bf234d.sentence: A geologic definition of soil is "a material at the surface of a planetary body modified in place by physical, chemical or biological processes".

064a98435bd2.title: Astropedology
064a98435bd2.sentence: Soils are sometimes defined by biological activity but can also be defined as planetary surfaces altered in place by biologic, chemical, or physical processes.

f6a4fce189fe.title: Astropedology
f6a4fce189fe.sentence: By this definition, the question for Martian soils and paleosols becomes, were they alive?

7d5c0dd81039.title: Astropedology
7d5c0dd81039.sentence: Astropedology symposia are a new focus for scientific meetings on soil science.

6161bf7fed84.title: Martian regolith
6161bf7fed84.sentence: Martian regolith is toxic, due to relatively high concentrations of perchlorate compounds containing chlorine.

2114ecd89652.title: Martian regolith
2114ecd89652.sentence: Perchlorates such as calcium perchlorate were first discovered on Mars in 2008 by the NASA Phoenix lander.

329e85fa4a0f.title: Martian regolith
329e85fa4a0f.sentence: However, each new lander has confirmed their presence in the regolith locally and the Mars Odyssey orbiter confirmed they are spread globally across the entire surface of the planet.

01fa8a178d87.title: Martian regolith
01fa8a178d87.sentence: The levels detected in the Martian regolith are around 0.5%, which is a level considered toxic to humans.

9792f57eb05d.title: Astropedology
9792f57eb05d.sentence: Since even trace amounts interfere with thyroid functions in humans, the presence of perchlorates in Martian soils is a significant issue that needs to be addressed before colonization occurs.

62a55b4103a3.title: Martian regolith
62a55b4103a3.sentence: A 2013 terrestrial study found that a 0.5 g per liter concentration caused:

fb37b38fdaaf.title: Martian regolith
fb37b38fdaaf.sentence: - a significant decline in the chlorophyll content in plant leaves

fefc98c12535.title: Martian regolith
fefc98c12535.sentence: - reduction in the oxidizing power of plant roots

994c0c118710.title: Martian regolith
994c0c118710.sentence: - reduction in the size of the plant both above and below ground

f2e198ce96b7.title: Martian regolith
f2e198ce96b7.sentence: - an accumulation of concentrated perchlorates in the leaves

796dea9b8350.title: Martian regolith
796dea9b8350.sentence: The report noted that one of the types of plant studied, Eichhornia crassipes, seemed resistant to the perchlorates and could be used to help remove the toxic salts from the environment, although the plants themselves would end up containing a high concentration of perchlorates as a result.

5b100099c22b.title: Astropedology
5b100099c22b.sentence: Since there is no ozone layer on Mars, UV rays penetrate to the surface of the planet.

cda6c8ef1860.title: Martian regolith
cda6c8ef1860.sentence: However, the added effect of the high levels of UV reaching the surface of Mars breaks molecular bonds, creating even more dangerous chemicals which in lab tests on Earth were shown to be more lethal to bacteria than the perchlorates alone.

92bdceacb8f4.title: Astropedology
92bdceacb8f4.sentence: Research suggests that the iron oxides and hydrogen peroxide present in the soil on Mars increases the toxicity of perchlorates.

88619450bb2a.title: Martian regolith
88619450bb2a.sentence: There is evidence that some bacterial lifeforms are able to overcome perchlorates by physiological adaptations to increasing perchlorate concentrations, and some even live off them.

b57be0e0c18e.title: Martian regolith
b57be0e0c18e.sentence: In 2022, NASA and the U.S. National Science Foundation co-funded a multi-year grant to study the use of the bacteria Dehalococcoides mccartyi to break down perchlorates into harmless chlorides and oxygen.

786ebcd0dd58.title: Martian regolith
786ebcd0dd58.sentence: Also, perchlorates, the presence of which may make detection of life-related organic molecules difficult, were found at the Curiosity rover landing site (and earlier at the more polar site of the Phoenix lander) suggesting a "global distribution of these salts".

e73b4f9b8f98.title: Lunar regolith
e73b4f9b8f98.sentence: It is easily disturbed and poses a significant hazard to exposed equipment and human health.

1cc0e193cd00.title: Lunar regolith
1cc0e193cd00.sentence: The dust found on the lunar surface could cause harmful effects on any human outpost technology and crew members:

00ed4f77cae4.title: Lunar regolith
00ed4f77cae4.sentence: - Darkening of surfaces, leading to a considerable increase in radiative heat transfer;

212c92f7f427.title: Lunar regolith
212c92f7f427.sentence: - Abrasive nature of the dust particles may rub and abrade surfaces through friction;

bc31b9162d39.title: Lunar regolith
bc31b9162d39.sentence: - Negative effect on coatings used on gaskets to seal equipment from space, optical lenses, solar panels, and windows as well as wiring;

b0f11ddf9ab5.title: Lunar regolith
b0f11ddf9ab5.sentence: If the chemically reactive particles are deposited in the lungs, they may cause respiratory disease.

8a36197d3178.title: Lunar regolith
8a36197d3178.sentence: Long-term exposure to the dust may cause a more serious respiratory disease similar to silicosis.

d146a54c2b59.title: Lunar regolith
d146a54c2b59.section: Harmful effects of lunar dust > Toxic effects
d146a54c2b59.sentence: After each EVA, the crew modules were heavily contaminated with dust; many astronauts reported coughs, throat irritation, watery eyes, and blurred vision that likely reduced their performance.

2e73d619107e.title: Lunar regolith
2e73d619107e.section: Harmful effects of lunar dust > Toxic effects
2e73d619107e.sentence: In each case, symptoms resolved within 24 hours, and post-flight pulmonary testing found no permanent impacts in the astronauts.

cae6d5eb7c54.title: Lunar regolith
cae6d5eb7c54.sentence: A 2005 NASA study listed 20 risks that required further study before humans should commit to a human Mars expedition, and ranked "dust" as the number one challenge.

4c76744fcd2c.title: Lunar regolith
4c76744fcd2c.sentence: Although that report addressed Martian dust, the concerns are equally valid concerning lunar dust.

ca6ec0a05a86.title: Lunar regolith
ca6ec0a05a86.sentence: The Apollo astronauts brought back some 360 kilograms (790 lb) of lunar rocks from six landing sites.

dd0aa806b5f9.title: Lunar regolith
dd0aa806b5f9.sentence: On 16 December 2020, China's Chang'e 5 mission returned to Earth with about 2 kilograms of rock and dirt it picked up from the Moon.

eee0c291b70d.title: Lunar regolith
eee0c291b70d.sentence: Every sample brought back from the Moon has been contaminated by Earth's air and humidity.

c9fec1decf91.title: Lunar regolith
c9fec1decf91.sentence: The dust has acquired a patina of rust, and due to bonding with terrestrial water and oxygen molecules, its chemical reactivity is gone.

7b9d11befe98.title: Lunar regolith
7b9d11befe98.sentence: The chemical and electrostatic properties of the dirt no longer match what future astronauts will encounter on the Moon.

4e316964321d.title: Lunar regolith
4e316964321d.sentence: It is the first lunar regolith sample to return to Earth since 1972.

747116bc26d8.title: Lunar regolith
747116bc26d8.sentence: China is the third country in the world to have brought such material back to Earth.

b785583edc9a.title: Lunar regolith
b785583edc9a.sentence: Chang'e 6 collected and returned samples from the far side of the Moon in 2024.

06de4e196f2a.title: Lunar regolith
06de4e196f2a.sentence: The major processes involved in the formation of lunar regolith are:

c10b00fda3c2.title: Lunar regolith
c10b00fda3c2.sentence: These processes continue to change the physical and optical properties of the dirt over time, and it is known as space weathering.

7c9ec7bb71b2.title: Lunar regolith
7c9ec7bb71b2.sentence: - Comminution: mechanical breaking of rocks and minerals into smaller particles by meteorite and micrometeorite impacts;

763727b6a6b6.title: Lunar regolith
763727b6a6b6.sentence: - Agglutination: welding of mineral and rock fragments together by micrometeorite-impact-produced glass;

86e98d74d2f5.title: Lunar regolith
86e98d74d2f5.sentence: - Solar wind sputtering and cosmic ray spallation caused by impacts of ions and high energy particles.

4dad37f0b95e.title: Astropedology
4dad37f0b95e.sentence: The first stages consist of a coarse-grained and poorly-sorted blanket of impact ejecta.

cb5c65ad7652.title: Astropedology
cb5c65ad7652.sentence: In the next stages, micrometeoroid bombardment breaks down the material to even finer grains, which increases the ratio of agglutinates.

4de7856cedd9.title: Astropedology
4de7856cedd9.sentence: This micrometeoroid bombardment also adds meteoritic metal and reduces iron (Fe^2+) in silicates to metallic iron in the soil.

9783cd36a3c3.title: Astropedology
9783cd36a3c3.sentence: Agglutinates and metal cause the soil to darken in color over a long period.

4ab7f09cc39a.title: Astropedology
4ab7f09cc39a.sentence: These calculations demonstrate that there are comparably much slower soil formation rates on the Moon than on Earth.

e43c65598bbf.title: Astropedology
e43c65598bbf.sentence: Extrapolations for the time of soil formation have also been made based on crater production rates that suggest 81 thousand years (ka) for the time for overturning the upper 2 cm of Lunar soil.

8412a8ef455f.title: Lunar regolith
8412a8ef455f.sentence: In addition, fire fountaining, whereby volcanic lava is lofted and cools into small glass beads before falling back to the surface, can create small but important deposits in some locations, such as the orange dirt found at Shorty Crater in the Taurus-Littrow valley by Apollo 17, and the green glass found at Hadley–Apennine by Apollo 15.

a3acb3bc25b2.title: In situ resource utilization
a3acb3bc25b2.sentence: In space exploration, in situ resource utilization (ISRU) is the practice of collection, processing, storing and use of materials found or manufactured on other astronomical objects (the Moon, Mars, asteroids, etc.) that replace materials that would otherwise be brought from Earth.

d7739dfb6afa.title: In situ resource utilization
d7739dfb6afa.sentence: ISRU could provide materials for life support, propellants, construction materials, and energy to a spacecraft payloads or space exploration crews.

38ac8206705b.title: In situ resource utilization
38ac8206705b.sentence: ISRU has long been considered as a possible avenue for reducing the mass and cost of space exploration architectures, in that it may be a way to drastically reduce the amount of payload that must be launched from Earth in order to explore a given planetary body.

3db2cec13743.title: In situ resource utilization
3db2cec13743.sentence: The colonization of planets or moons will require obtaining local building materials, such as regolith.

db5a9af56775.title: In situ resource utilization
db5a9af56775.sentence: For water that is chemically bound to regolith, solid ice, or some manner of permafrost, sufficient heating can recover the water.

ee1b7dc89201.title: In situ resource utilization
ee1b7dc89201.sentence: However this is not as easy as it appears because ice and permafrost can often be harder than plain rock, necessitating laborious mining operations.

e5e760804296.title: In situ resource utilization
e5e760804296.sentence: Oxygen is often found in iron-rich lunar minerals and glasses as iron oxide.

c3f4e1439a3a.title: In situ resource utilization
c3f4e1439a3a.sentence: The oxygen can be extracted by heating the material to temperatures above 900 °C and exposing it to hydrogen gas.

55199c5e5e18.title: Martian regolith
55199c5e5e18.sentence: On Earth, the term "soil" usually includes organic content.

68d081240960.title: Martian regolith
68d081240960.sentence: Disagreement over the significance of soil's definition arises due to the lack of an integrated concept of soil in the literature.

7b28250592f1.title: Martian regolith
7b28250592f1.sentence: Rocks generally refers to 10 cm scale and larger materials (e.g., fragments, breccia, and exposed outcrops) with high thermal inertia, with areal fractions consistent with the Viking Infrared Thermal Mapper (IRTM) data, and immobile under current aeolian (wind) conditions.

89ce416c6744.title: Martian regolith
89ce416c6744.sentence: Consequently, rocks are classified as grains exceeding the size of cobbles on the Wentworth scale.

3429afa6674d.title: Martian regolith
3429afa6674d.sentence: Soil refers to all other, typically unconsolidated, material including those sufficiently fine-grained to be mobilized by wind.

edf4b86b795d.title: Martian regolith
edf4b86b795d.sentence: The pragmatic definition "medium for plant growth" has been commonly adopted in the planetary science community but a more complex definition describes soil as "(bio)geochemically/physically altered material at the surface of a planetary body that encompasses surficial extraterrestrial telluric deposits".

eda785edd00d.title: Martian regolith
eda785edd00d.sentence: This definition emphasizes that soil is a body that retains information about its environmental history and that does not need the presence of life to form.

e0d3acc747bb.title: Astropedology
e0d3acc747bb.sentence: One option is to simply use our present soil classification schemes, in which case many extraterrestrial soils would be Entisols in the United States Soil Taxonomy (ST) or Regosols in the World Reference Base for Soil Resources (WRB).

815fb9463840.title: Astropedology
815fb9463840.sentence: However, applying an Earth-based system to such dissimilar settings is debatable.

6533ef7403b6.title: Astropedology
6533ef7403b6.sentence: Another option is to distinguish the (largely) biotic Earth from the abiotic Solar System, and include all non-Earth soils in a new Order or Reference Group, which might be tentatively called Astrosols.

4bde6d19cd3b.title: Martian regolith
4bde6d19cd3b.sentence: Martian dust generally connotes even finer materials than Martian soil, the fraction which is less than 30 micrometres in diameter.

48bc661fc571.title: Martian regolith
48bc661fc571.sentence: The Martian atmospheric dust particles are generally 3 μm in diameter.

222475314dca.title: Martian regolith
222475314dca.sentence: For example, the dust suspended by the 2001 global dust storms on Mars only remained in the Martian atmosphere for 0.6 years, while the dust from Mount Pinatubo took about two years to settle.

e3963f837366.title: Martian regolith
e3963f837366.sentence: On Earth, dust that leaves atmospheric suspension usually gets aggregated into larger particles through the action of soil moisture or gets suspended in oceanic waters.

5496f5308e03.title: Martian regolith
5496f5308e03.sentence: Neither process occurs on Mars, leaving deposited dust available for suspension back into the Martian atmosphere.

e41c4b85c806.title: Martian regolith
e41c4b85c806.sentence: In fact, the composition of Martian atmospheric dust – very similar to surface dust – as observed by the Mars Global Surveyor Thermal Emission Spectrometer, may be volumetrically dominated by composites of plagioclase feldspar and zeolite which can be mechanically derived from Martian basaltic rocks without chemical alteration.

13ae9c6e62c5.title: Martian regolith
13ae9c6e62c5.sentence: It found that the dust reacted with small amounts of water to produce highly reactive molecules that are also produced during the mining of quartz and known to produce lung disease in miners on Earth, including cancer (the study also noted that lunar dust may be worse).

ba94638382dd.title: Lunarcrete
ba94638382dd.sentence: Lunarcrete, also known as "mooncrete", an idea first proposed by Larry A. Beyer of the University of Pittsburgh in 1985, is a hypothetical construction aggregate, similar to concrete, formed from lunar regolith, that would reduce the construction costs of building on the Moon.

9ff946b948fe.title: Lunarcrete
9ff946b948fe.sentence: The basic ingredients for lunarcrete would be the same as those for terrestrial concrete: aggregate, water, and cement.

effa08748923.title: Lunarcrete
effa08748923.sentence: In the case of lunarcrete, the aggregate would be lunar regolith.

89af3a398ce1.title: Lunarcrete
89af3a398ce1.sentence: The cement would be manufactured by beneficiating lunar rock that had a high calcium content.

7705c7af60a6.title: Lunarcrete
7705c7af60a6.sentence: Lin et al. used 40 g of the lunar regolith samples obtained by Apollo 16 to produce lunarcrete in 1986.

7754b4f49467.title: Lunarcrete
7754b4f49467.sentence: It was capable of withstanding compressive pressures of 75 MPa, and lost only 20% of that strength after repeated exposure to vacuum.

76d5a502869c.title: Lunarcrete
76d5a502869c.sentence: In 2008, Houssam Toutanji, of the University of Alabama in Huntsville, and Richard Grugel, of the Marshall Space Flight Center, used a lunar soil simulant to determine whether lunarcrete could be made without water, using sulfur (obtainable from lunar dust) as the binding agent.

29ceb9e2c5bb.title: Lunarcrete
29ceb9e2c5bb.sentence: The best mixture for tensile and compressive strength is 65% JSC-1 lunar regolith simulant and 35% sulfur, with an average compressive strength of 33.8 MPa and tensile strength of 3.7 MPa.

3329ce15449a.title: Lunarcrete
3329ce15449a.sentence: AstroCrete is a concrete-like material proposed to be used on Moon or Mars made from regolith and human serum albumin (HSA), a protein from human blood.

11cb15526a62.title: Martian regolith simulant
11cb15526a62.sentence: Martian regolith simulant (or Martian soil simulant) is a terrestrial material that is used to simulate the chemical and mechanical properties of Martian regolith for research, experiments and prototype testing of activities related to Martian regolith such as dust mitigation of transportation equipment, advanced life support systems and in-situ resource utilization.

8ee969b663cf.title: Martian regolith simulant
8ee969b663cf.section: Variations > JSC Mars-1 and JSC Mars-1A
8ee969b663cf.sentence: The studies of the Martian soil properties led to the development of JSC Mars-1 Martian regolith simulant at NASA's Johnson Space Center in 1998.

65d252b8bd99.title: Martian regolith simulant
65d252b8bd99.section: Variations > JSC Mars-1 and JSC Mars-1A
65d252b8bd99.sentence: The palagonitic tephra, which is glassy volcanic ash altered at low temperature, was mined from a quarry at the Pu'u Nene cinder cone.

944ed99ba7d5.title: Martian regolith simulant
944ed99ba7d5.sentence: MMS or Mojave Mars Simulant was developed in 2007 to address some issues with JSC Mars-1.

0db1d19355db.title: Martian regolith simulant
0db1d19355db.sentence: While JSC Mars-1 did simulate the color of Martian regolith, it performed poorly in many qualities, including its hygroscopic tendencies—it had undergone weathering that attracts water, making it more clay-like.

9f1ed14e8ee8.title: Martian regolith simulant
9f1ed14e8ee8.sentence: MMS, however, was hygroscopically inert due to minimal weathering and the way it was crushed, which allowed it to better simulate that feature of Martian regolith, among others.

1a43adf75f9a.title: Martian regolith simulant
1a43adf75f9a.sentence: MGS-1 or Mars Global Simulant was developed starting in 2018 as the first mineralogically accurate Martian regolith simulant.

fe0eabd1a991.title: Martian regolith simulant
fe0eabd1a991.sentence: It is based on the Rocknest soil in Gale crater on Mars that has been analyzed extensively by the NASA Curiosity rover.

1e994f86fbfd.title: Martian regolith simulant
1e994f86fbfd.sentence: MGS-1 is produced by mixing pure minerals together in accurate proportions, with a realistic particle size distribution.

b0bbcd811ecb.title: Martian regolith simulant
b0bbcd811ecb.sentence: Although perchlorates were discovered on Mars in 2008 by the Phoenix lander, none of the simulants include perchlorates.

a9aafdea9924.title: Martian regolith simulant
a9aafdea9924.sentence: However, end users can spike the material with perchlorate salts or other superoxide species.

6477022cf022.title: Martian regolith simulant
6477022cf022.sentence: Exposure to regolith simulants may pose some health risks due to the fine particles and the presence of crystalline silica.

c839213cca51.title: Impact gardening
c839213cca51.sentence: Impact gardening is the process by which impact events stir the outermost crusts of moons and other celestial objects with no atmospheres.

2e8fa1329d8f.title: Impact gardening
2e8fa1329d8f.sentence: In the particular case of the Moon, this is more often known as lunar gardening.

91fef301e4bd.title: Impact gardening
91fef301e4bd.sentence: Planetary bodies lacking an atmosphere will generally also lack any erosional processes, with the possible exception of volcanism, and as a result impact debris accumulates at the object's surface as a rough "soil," commonly referred to as regolith.

41c5a7f29810.title: Impact gardening
41c5a7f29810.sentence: Subsequent impacts, especially by micrometeorites, stir and mix this soil.

11c18d1c6437.title: Impact gardening
11c18d1c6437.sentence: It had long been estimated that the top centimeter of the lunar surface is overturned every 10 million years.

22af13a873d5.title: Impact gardening

9732b9056a07.title: Astropedology
9732b9056a07.section: Growing plants on the Moon and Mars
9732b9056a07.sentence: Lunar and Mars explorations have provided information about the mineral composition of the soils on the Moon and Mars.

34a41465b947.title: Astropedology
34a41465b947.section: Growing plants on the Moon and Mars
34a41465b947.sentence: All essential minerals for the growth of plants appear to be present in sufficient quantities in both soils probably with the exception of reactive nitrogen.

26e951550455.title: Astropedology
26e951550455.section: Growing plants on the Moon and Mars
26e951550455.sentence: However, the Mars Pathfinder was not able to detect reactive nitrogen.

daa373e1c909.title: Astropedology
daa373e1c909.section: Growing plants on the Moon and Mars
daa373e1c909.sentence: Thus the actual presence of major quantities of reactive nitrogen remains uncertain.

37ccea060c64.title: Astropedology
37ccea060c64.section: Growing plants on the Moon and Mars
37ccea060c64.sentence: The absence of sufficient reactive nitrogen may be solved by using nitrogen fixing species.

f1718ba7df3f.title: Astropedology
f1718ba7df3f.section: Growing plants on the Moon and Mars
f1718ba7df3f.sentence: In symbioses with bacteria these nitrogen fixers are able to bind nitrogen from the air and transform it into nitrates, a process which requires nitrogen in the atmosphere.

6fe68fd97b7f.title: Astropedology
6fe68fd97b7f.section: Growing plants on the Moon and Mars
6fe68fd97b7f.sentence: However, there is no atmosphere on the moon, and on Mars it is only minimally present and contains traces of nitrogen.

053eca6329ce.title: Astropedology
053eca6329ce.section: Growing plants on the Moon and Mars
053eca6329ce.sentence: The results show that plants are able to germinate and grow on both Martian and moon soil simulant for a period of 50 days without any addition of nutrients.

0dff6e46a30c.title: Astropedology
0dff6e46a30c.section: Growing plants on the Moon and Mars
0dff6e46a30c.sentence: Growth and flowering on Mars regolith simulant was much better than on Moon regolith simulant and even slightly better than on our control nutrient poor river soil.
