d81430256cb7.sentence: The differences between Earth's and lunar soil mean that plants struggle to grow.

de21d6e693cd.title: Lunar regolith
de21d6e693cd.sentence: As a result long-term space missions could require complicated and expensive efforts to provide food, such as importing Earth soil, chemically treating lunar regolith to remove heavy metals and oxidize iron atoms, and selectively breeding strains of plants that are adapted to the inhospitable lunar regolith.

94adf2b687e3.title: Astropedology
94adf2b687e3.sentence: Evidence of paleosols on Mars is derived from both in-situ and orbital remote sensing investigations of the Martian surface.

d0732ac0e42e.title: Astropedology
d0732ac0e42e.sentence: In-situ chemical / mineralogical analyses (Mars Science Laboratory) and images (Mastcam, MAHLI) from the Curiosity rover in Gale Crater on Mars have shown similarities with soil horizons and soil structures found on Earth.

3882dd81ac30.title: Astropedology
3882dd81ac30.sentence: Morphological evidence includes soil features such as gradational alteration and bedding disruption by dilational cracks and veins, consistent with soluans of desert soils, blocky angular ped structures, sand wedges, a shallow gypsic (By) horizon, and vesicular structure.

50fcd21da17d.title: Astropedology
50fcd21da17d.sentence: Mineral abundances within the paleosols show olivine weathering to smectite and a modest depletion of phosphorus.

075574696db0.title: Astropedology
075574696db0.sentence: Radiometric dating suggests the paleosols at Yellowknife Bay are 3.7 billion years old (± 0.3 billion years) and reveal a change from possible "warm and wet" conditions of the Early Noachian (~4.1-3.9 Ga) to an extreme arid and cold climate with limited soil formation.

759f0eafaf39.title: Astropedology
759f0eafaf39.sentence: Remote sensing of the Martian surface by the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO)'s CRISM instrument and the Infrared Mineralogical Mapping Spectrometer (OMEGA) has detected the presence of dioctahedral and trioctahedral phyllosilicate clays in thousands of locations across the surface of the planet.

bbe6f149cbd2.title: Astropedology
bbe6f149cbd2.sentence: These areas include Gale Crater, Mawrth Vallis, Oxia Planum, and Nili Fossae, among others, and date to 4.0-3.7 Ga.

c6b3ac58be88.title: Astropedology
c6b3ac58be88.sentence: There are two hypotheses to explain the formation and distribution of phyllosilicate clays on Mars: (1) subsurface and hydrothermal activity and/or diagenesis which yield trioctahedral phyllosilicates, and (2) surface / subaerial chemical weathering, e.g., pedogenesis which yield dioctahedral phyllosilicates.

a93e4c7c84b5.title: Astropedology
a93e4c7c84b5.sentence: Structures like those found in Earth's desert soils caused by microbial gas production after rains (vesicular structure) have been recognized on Mars, but definitive evidence of life on Mars has yet to be obtained.

2dd5303e0334.title: Astropedology
2dd5303e0334.sentence: The chemical and morphological features of the Yellowknife Bay paleosols are a new line of evidence for late Noachian (3.7 ± 0.3 Ga) paleoclimate on Mars, and are interpreted as forming under a hyperarid frigid paleoclimate.

2fc1c266f1ba.title: Astropedology
2fc1c266f1ba.sentence: The theory that life evolved in soil is appealing because soil traps water between the grains of clay, providing an array of microscopic reaction chambers.

710fa0896178.title: Astropedology
710fa0896178.sentence: These may also promote formation of organic compounds by mechanisms demonstrated in the Urey-Miller experiment, so that planetary surfaces were covered with carbonaceous chondrite.

b1b173bce813.title: Astropedology
b1b173bce813.sentence: Clayey and organic soils are protected from erosion and thus continued to produce clay and organic matter.

eb0fb8e9534f.title: Astropedology
eb0fb8e9534f.sentence: Unicellular life, when it evolved, would also have served same purpose of binding the soil.

dc55ecf04da8.title: Astropedology
dc55ecf04da8.sentence: The ingredients required for life are still provided by the weathering cycle, which promotes life.

e6f66c2a0b0f.title: Viking lander biological experiments
e6f66c2a0b0f.sentence: In 1976, two identical Viking program landers each carried four types of biological experiments to the surface of Mars.

02894ce1fe82.title: Viking lander biological experiments
02894ce1fe82.sentence: The first successful Mars landers, Viking 1 and Viking 2, then carried out experiments to look for biosignatures of microbial life on Mars.

d2cf95a1e115.title: Viking lander biological experiments
d2cf95a1e115.sentence: The landers each used a robotic arm to pick up and place soil samples into sealed test containers on the craft.

0f5d03697f20.title: Viking lander biological experiments
0f5d03697f20.sentence: The two landers carried out the same tests at two places on Mars' surface, Viking 1 near the equator and Viking 2 further north.

00b3f0f97c2e.title: Viking lander biological experiments
00b3f0f97c2e.section: The experiments > Gas chromatograph – mass spectrometer
00b3f0f97c2e.sentence: It could measure molecules present at a level of a few parts per billion.

f12c7d428737.title: Viking lander biological experiments
f12c7d428737.section: The experiments > Gas chromatograph – mass spectrometer
f12c7d428737.sentence: The GCMS measured no significant amount of organic molecules in the Martian soil.

82cd93e520dd.title: Viking lander biological experiments
82cd93e520dd.section: The experiments > Gas chromatograph – mass spectrometer
82cd93e520dd.sentence: In fact, Martian soils were found to contain less carbon than lifeless lunar soils returned by the Apollo program.

20e68b0f941b.title: Viking lander biological experiments
20e68b0f941b.sentence: The gas exchange (GEX) experiment (PI: Vance Oyama, NASA Ames) looked for gases given off by an incubated soil sample by first replacing the Martian atmosphere with the inert gas helium.

0629c7630b33.title: Viking lander biological experiments
0629c7630b33.sentence: It applied a liquid complex of organic and inorganic nutrients and supplements to a soil sample, first with just nutrients added, then with water added too.

bae529e489a1.title: Viking lander biological experiments
bae529e489a1.sentence: Again, oxygen disappeared once the nutrient solution came into contact with the soil.

c3cf0c1153fa.title: Viking lander biological experiments
c3cf0c1153fa.sentence: Again, carbon dioxide began to appear and still continues to evolve".

9466818f0070.title: Viking lander biological experiments
9466818f0070.sentence: The pyrolytic release (PR) experiment (PI: Norman Horowitz, Caltech) consisted of the use of light, water, and a carbon-containing atmosphere of carbon monoxide (CO) and carbon dioxide (CO2), simulating that on Mars.

dd6bb8682faf.title: Viking lander biological experiments
dd6bb8682faf.sentence: The carbon-bearing gases were made with carbon-14 (14C), a heavy, radioactive isotope of carbon.

f90641b31009.title: Viking lander biological experiments
f90641b31009.sentence: After several days of incubation, the experiment removed the gases, baked the remaining soil at 650 °C (1200 °F), and collected the products in a device which counted radioactivity.

5a8cf33c44b6.title: Viking lander biological experiments

744c31641fa4.title: Viking lander biological experiments

cbc2955a618f.title: Viking lander biological experiments

0e4b269ae42a.title: Viking lander biological experiments
0e4b269ae42a.sentence: Despite the positive result from the Labeled Release experiment, a general assessment is that the results seen in the four experiments are best explained by oxidative chemical reactions with the Martian soil.

ff1a083d3116.title: Viking lander biological experiments
ff1a083d3116.sentence: One of the current conclusions is that the Martian soil, being continuously exposed to UV light from the Sun (Mars has no protective ozone layer), has built up a thin layer of a very strong oxidant.

9dcfa507d7ed.title: Viking lander biological experiments
9dcfa507d7ed.sentence: The study's authors found that perchlorate can destroy organics when heated and produce chloromethane and dichloromethane as byproduct, the identical chlorine compounds discovered by both Viking landers when they performed the same tests on Mars.

e899959a70a2.title: Viking lander biological experiments

27782fc8ecfd.title: Viking lander biological experiments

de1b116e54a9.title: Viking lander biological experiments

7c72dd04be3d.title: Mars sample-return mission

59497983582e.sentence: Such a mission would allow more extensive analysis than that allowed by onboard sensors, focused on whether Mars once hosted life.

cfa9fa5614c9.title: Mars sample-return mission

a44383625c17.title: Mars sample-return mission

e68103bc36dc.sentence: The nutrients (7 molecular compounds that were Miller-Urey products) were tagged with radioactive 14C.

0c3857dd7242.title: Viking lander biological experiments
0c3857dd7242.sentence: The air above the soil was monitored for the evolution of radioactive 14CO2 (or other carbon-based) gas as evidence that microorganisms in the soil had metabolized one or more of the nutrients.

fa42fa3ae6c1.title: Viking lander biological experiments
fa42fa3ae6c1.sentence: The result was quite a surprise, considering the negative results of the first two tests, with a steady stream of radioactive gases being given off by the soil immediately following the first injection.

b2ac8cd1e2a0.title: Viking lander biological experiments
b2ac8cd1e2a0.sentence: The experiment was done by both Viking probes, the first using a sample from the surface exposed to sunlight and the second probe taking the sample from underneath a rock; both initial injections came back positive.

f233ead6b832.sentence: Samples heated for 3 hours at 160 °C gave off no radioactive gas when nutrients were injected, and samples heated for 3 hours at 50 °C exhibited a substantial reduction in radioactive gas released following nutrient injection.

The 2011 edition of the same textbook noted that "Albert Yen of the Jet Propulsion Laboratory has shown that, under extremely cold and dry conditions and in a carbon dioxide atmosphere, ultraviolet light (remember: Mars lacks an ozone layer, so the surface is bathed in ultraviolet) can cause carbon dioxide to react with soils to produce various oxidizers, including highly reactive superoxides (salts containing O2−).

afce097e606a.sentence: When mixed with small organic molecules, superoxides readily oxidize them to carbon dioxide, which may account for the LR result.

bf76f0907393.title: Viking lander biological experiments

af9c97d199fb.title: Viking lander biological experiments

f7ebd8a40581.title: Viking lander biological experiments
